# TKCode.Arc documentation

> Every page of https://docs.tkcode.si in one file, for TKCode.Arc 0.3.2-preview.1 (Avalonia 12.1.4): the guides, then every component and block. The index with one line per page is https://docs.tkcode.si/llms.txt.

---

# Introduction

TKCode.Arc brings [Arc](https://uiarc.dev) to Avalonia: the same component groups, the same visual language and the
same spring motion, built as native Avalonia controls that depend on nothing but Avalonia and MIT packages. It ports
the free Arc components (110 components in 22 groups) and adds page-level blocks, a spreadsheet-style data grid and a
streaming Markdown renderer, so a desktop product can be assembled from one consistent kit instead of a patchwork of
styles.

This gallery is the library's documentation. Every component page is written from the component's source, shows live
examples you can interact with, and lists the generated API reference.

![A billing overview built only from Arc components: metric cards, a status badge, a form field and actions](https://docs.tkcode.si/shots/Guides/Introduction/images/ProductOverview.webp)

```xml
<StackPanel Width="760" Spacing="20">
    <Grid ColumnDefinitions="*,Auto">
        <StackPanel Spacing="4">
            <TextBlock Text="Acme Analytics"
                       FontSize="22"
                       FontWeight="Medium"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
            <TextBlock Text="Workspace overview, October 2026"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
        </StackPanel>
        <StackPanel Grid.Column="1" Orientation="Horizontal" Spacing="8" VerticalAlignment="Center">
            <arc:Badge Content="Pro plan" Tone="Success" />
            <arc:Button Content="Export report" Variant="Secondary" />
            <arc:Button Content="Invite members" />
        </StackPanel>
    </Grid>
    <UniformGrid Columns="3">
        <arc:MetricCard Label="Monthly revenue" Prefix="$" Value="48210" Change="+6.4%" Context="vs last month" Margin="0,0,8,0" />
        <arc:MetricCard Label="Active accounts" Value="1284" Change="+42" Context="Across 3 regions" Margin="4,0" />
        <arc:MetricCard Label="Churn" Suffix="%" Value="1.8" Decimals="1" Change="-0.3 pts" Context="Lower is better" Margin="8,0,0,0" />
    </UniformGrid>
    <arc:Input Label="Billing email"
               Text="billing@acme.com"
               Description="Invoices and payment receipts are sent here." />
</StackPanel>
```

## What is in the library

| Part | What it gives you |
|---|---|
| Components | 110 controls in Arc's 22 groups: buttons, gestures, menus, text fields, special inputs, selects, toggles, sliders, pickers, editors, navigation, expand, overlays, messages, progress, avatars, cards, charts, tables, activity, media and text effects. |
| Blocks | Page-level compositions for application shells and settings: Sidebar, PageHeader, CommandPalette, SearchResults, NotificationCenter, EmptyStates, SettingsPage, SettingsCommand, SecuritySettings, BillingOverview, UsageBilling and CancelFlow. |
| AdvancedCharts | `DataGrid`, a spreadsheet-style grid with sorting, filtering, editing, selection statistics, undo and export. |
| Illustrations | Animated explainer scenes (DataFlow, PaymentFlow, MultiRegionFailover, VectorSearch) for landing and onboarding pages. |
| Content | A streaming `Markdown` control and a highlighted `CodeBlock`, for documentation and AI chat replies. |
| Icons and fonts | 187 Lucide glyphs built into the core, the full Lucide set (2155 icons) as a separate package, and Geist and Geist Mono. |

### Component groups

| Group | Count | Typical use |
|---|---|---|
| Buttons | 10 | Primary and secondary actions, split and grouped actions, copy, confirm, theme switching |
| Gestures | 3 | Hold to confirm, emoji reactions, swipe actions on list rows |
| Menus | 3 | Context menus, dropdown menus, the account menu |
| Text fields | 7 | Single-line and multi-line input, passwords, search, in-place editing |
| Special inputs | 7 | Numbers, money, phone numbers, tags, mentions, scrubbing, keyboard shortcuts |
| Selects | 5 | Single and multiple choice from lists, searchable choice, chips |
| Toggles | 6 | Switches, checkboxes, radio groups and cards, segmented controls, billing period toggles |

| Editors | 3 | Rich text, file drop zones, signatures |
| Navigation | 3 | Tabs, breadcrumbs, pagination |
| Expand | 5 | Accordions, expandable cards and text, resizable panels, scroll areas |
| Overlays | 6 | Dialogs, drawers, bottom sheets, popovers, hover cards, tooltips |
| Messages | 5 | Alerts, toasts and toast stacks, announcement bars, cookie consent |
| Progress | 5 | Progress bars, skeletons, steppers, countdowns, usage meters |
| Avatars | 3 | Avatars, avatar groups, badges |
| Cards | 3 | Content cards, metric cards, empty states |
| Charts | 13 | Line, bar, donut, gauge, sparkline, treemap, heatmap and more |
| Tables | 6 | Sortable tables, filter toolbars, tree views, reorderable lists, JSON and code viewers |
| Activity | 3 | Chat threads, comment threads, timelines |
| Media | 3 | Carousels, card stacks, image comparison |
| Text effects | 4 | Text reveal, morph, shimmer, in-view titles |

## Design principles

**Arc fidelity.** Sizes, radii, colors, easing curves and spring constants come from Arc's own tokens, so a screen
built with TKCode.Arc reads like Arc on the web. Where Avalonia differs from the browser (focus, keyboard, overlays,
accessibility), the behavior is mapped to the native desktop equivalent rather than imitated.

**Native Avalonia controls.** Every control derives from an Avalonia base type: `Input` is a `TextBox`, `Button` is a
`Button`, `Select` and `MultiSelect` are `SelectingItemsControl`s. Data binding, commands, styles, data validation and
the keyboard work the way an Avalonia developer expects.

**Tokens, not hard-coded values.** Colors, radii, shadows, type and motion come from the ArcDesign tokens. Switching
between light and dark, or choosing one of eight accents, restyles every control at once. See **Theming**.

**Motion with restraint.** Springs and timings follow Arc's motion system, and every animation has three levels
(Full, Reduced and Off) that you can set per window or per container. See **Motion**.

**Accessible by default.** Fields are named by their labels, errors are announced through live regions, every
interactive control has a keyboard model, and each page documents what assistive technology reads.

**Ready for AOT.** The library uses no reflection and is trimming- and NativeAOT-compatible, so desktop apps can ship
as small, fast-starting single files.

## Packages

| Package | Contents | Where |
|---|---|---|
| `TKCode.Arc` | The components (`UseArcControls()`), the streaming `Markdown` control and `CodeBlock`. Brings in `TKCode.Arc.Core`. | NuGet |
| `TKCode.Arc.Core` | ArcDesign tokens and palette, the spring motion engine, shared primitives, 187 built-in Lucide glyphs. Brings in `TKCode.Arc.Foundation`. | NuGet |
| `TKCode.Arc.Foundation` | The theme, token, language and package runtime (`UseArc(...)`, `ArcTheme`, `ArcLanguage`) and its source generator. | NuGet (0.4 and later) |
| `TKCode.Arc.Fonts` | Geist and Geist Mono (`WithArcFonts()`). | NuGet |
| `TKCode.Arc.Icons.Lucide` | The full Lucide set (2155 icons): the `LucideIcon` control and the `LucideGeometry` markup extension. | NuGet |
| `TKCode.Arc.Blocks` | Page-level blocks (`UseArcBlocks()`). | NuGet |
| `TKCode.Arc.AdvancedCharts` | The `DataGrid` (`UseArcAdvancedCharts()`). | NuGet |
| `TKCode.Arc.Special` | Animated AI explainers (`UseArcSpecial()`). | NuGet |

**Installation** walks through adding them to an application.

## Requirements and platforms

- **.NET**: the packages target `net8.0`, `net10.0` and `net11.0`.
- **Avalonia**: Avalonia `12.1.4`, pinned to the exact version. Use the same version in your application. Arc has no
  other UI framework dependency.
- **Platforms**: desktop on Windows, macOS and Linux. The gallery also runs in the browser through its WebAssembly
  host.
- **Rendering of text and code**: Markdown and syntax highlighting use StreamMark, which the `TKCode.Arc` package
  brings in.

## Using this gallery

- **Sidebar.** Docs (these guides), Components (the 22 Arc groups plus Charts' DataGrid, Content and Illustrations) and
  Blocks. `Cmd+K` or `Ctrl+K` focuses the search from anywhere; the All, Ready and Planned filter narrows the list.
- **Component pages.** The header shows the package and its install command. The preview at the top is live. The
  sections follow the same order on every page: when to use, when not to use, usage (with live examples, business
  examples and guidelines), the API reference generated from the XML documentation, accessibility, motion and related
  components.
- **Examples.** Each live example has a Preview tab and a Code tab with its `.axaml` and code-behind. Pictures of
  larger business screens show the exact XAML that produced them, and follow the light or dark appearance.
- **Copy page.** Copies the whole page as Markdown with every example's source included, ready to paste into an issue,
  a design review or an AI assistant.
- **Appearance.** The Appearance panel switches between light and dark, chooses one of the eight accents, sets the
  motion level and changes the language (English, 简体中文, 繁體中文). Everything you see, including the pictures,
  follows these settings.

## Status and versioning

TKCode.Arc is in preview. Versions follow [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/); while a version carries a
`-preview` suffix, the API may still change between releases, and each release lists breaking changes in the
**Changelog**. Pin the exact version in your project and read the changelog before upgrading.

## License

TKCode.Arc is released under the MIT license. It ports Arc (MIT) and uses Lucide (ISC), the Geist fonts (OFL),
StreamMark, TextMateSharp, Oniguruma and Markdig. Every package in the dependency chain, Avalonia included, is under a
permissive license, so closed-source applications can ship Arc in a single file or a NativeAOT build.
`THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md` in the repository lists them all.

# Installation

This guide adds TKCode.Arc to an Avalonia desktop application, from the package references to the first screen. It
takes about five minutes on a new project and does not change how the rest of your Avalonia code works.

## Requirements

| Item | Version | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| .NET | `net10.0` or `net11.0` | The packages target both. |
| Avalonia | `12.1.4` | Pinned to the exact version the library is built against. |
| TKCode.Arc.Foundation | same as Arc | MIT; the theme, token, language and package runtime. Comes with `TKCode.Arc`. |
| Fonts (optional) | `Avalonia.Fonts.Inter` | Arc's body text uses Inter; Geist comes from `TKCode.Arc.Fonts`. |

TKCode.Arc is in preview, and Avalonia is pinned to an exact version. Besides Avalonia, every Arc package depends only
on MIT packages of its own. Use the same Avalonia version in your application; mixing versions leads to restore
warnings and, at run time, to missing styles or type load errors.

## 1. Add the packages

```bash
dotnet add package TKCode.Arc --version 0.3.2-preview.1
dotnet add package TKCode.Arc.Fonts --version 0.3.2-preview.1           # optional: Geist and Geist Mono
dotnet add package TKCode.Arc.Icons.Lucide --version 0.3.2-preview.1    # optional: the full Lucide set
dotnet add package Avalonia.Fonts.Inter --version 12.1.4                 # optional: Inter for body text
```

`TKCode.Arc` brings in `TKCode.Arc.Core`, `TKCode.Arc.Foundation` and StreamMark. If your solution uses central
package management, add the versions to `Directory.Packages.props` once and keep the project files version-free:

```xml
<ItemGroup>
    <PackageVersion Include="TKCode.Arc" Version="0.3.2-preview.1" />
    <PackageVersion Include="TKCode.Arc.Fonts" Version="0.3.2-preview.1" />
    <PackageVersion Include="TKCode.Arc.Icons.Lucide" Version="0.3.2-preview.1" />
    <PackageVersion Include="Avalonia.Fonts.Inter" Version="12.1.4" />
</ItemGroup>
```

Pin the exact preview version. Floating versions such as `0.1.*` can pick up a preview with breaking changes on the next
restore.

## 2. Register Arc in the application builder

Arc is registered on the `AppBuilder` with `UseArc(...)`. A typical `Program.cs`:

```csharp
using Avalonia;
using TKCode.Arc;
using TKCode.Arc.Fonts;

internal static class Program
{
    [STAThread]
    public static void Main(string[] args) => BuildAvaloniaApp().StartWithClassicDesktopLifetime(args);

    public static AppBuilder BuildAvaloniaApp() =>
        AppBuilder.Configure<App>()
                  .UsePlatformDetect()
                  .WithInterFont()      // Inter for body text (Avalonia.Fonts.Inter)
                  .WithArcFonts()       // Geist for display text, Geist Mono for code (TKCode.Arc.Fonts)
                  .UseArc(arc => arc
                      .UseArcControls()
                      .WithTheme(t => t.Appearance(ArcAppearance.System).Accent(ArcAccentPreset.Neutral)));
}
```

What each call does:

| Call | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `UseArc(...)` | Starts Arc's theme manager, design tokens and languages once the application is initialized. The callback lists the packages and the initial theme. |
| `UseArcControls()` | Registers Arc's controls, themes and tokens. It also registers `TKCode.Arc.Core` (`UseArcCore()`), so you do not call that yourself. |
| `WithTheme(...)` | Optional: the theme the first frame is drawn with (appearance, accent, token overrides). Without it Arc starts light with the `Neutral` accent. See **Theming**. |
| `WithInterFont()`, `WithArcFonts()` | Register the fonts Arc's type scale is designed for. Without them, text falls back to the system font. |

The `Application` class needs nothing from Arc: no base class, no `partial` keyword, no styles in `App.axaml`.

```csharp
public class App : Application
{
    public override void OnFrameworkInitializationCompleted()
    {
        if (ApplicationLifetime is IClassicDesktopStyleApplicationLifetime desktop)
        {
            desktop.MainWindow = new MainWindow();
        }
        base.OnFrameworkInitializationCompleted();
    }
}
```

Arc also styles the Avalonia controls its templates use (`ScrollViewer`, `ScrollBar`, `ItemsControl`, `PathIcon`, the
text selection handles and the popup hosts). Scroll bars look like Arc's `ScrollArea`: thin, shown while the pointer is
over the view or while it scrolls, hidden at rest; set `ScrollViewer.AllowAutoHide="False"` to keep them visible. When
`App.axaml` already includes `FluentTheme` or `SimpleTheme`, Arc leaves these controls to that theme.

## 3. Use the controls in XAML

Arc's XAML namespace is `https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc`; every control, token resource and markup
extension lives there.

![A notification settings card built in the first minutes with Arc](https://docs.tkcode.si/shots/Guides/Installation/images/FirstScreen.webp)

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             Width="560">
    <arc:Card Title="Notifications" Description="Choose how Acme Analytics keeps your team informed.">
        <StackPanel Spacing="16" Margin="0,12,0,0">
            <arc:Input Label="Alert email"
                       Text="ops@acme.com"
                       Description="Incidents and failed payments are sent here." />
            <arc:Switch Content="Weekly usage digest" IsChecked="True" />
            <arc:Switch Content="Product announcements" />
            <StackPanel Orientation="Horizontal" Spacing="8" HorizontalAlignment="Right">
                <arc:Button Content="Cancel" Variant="Secondary" />
                <arc:Button Content="Save changes" />
            </StackPanel>
        </StackPanel>
    </arc:Card>
</UserControl>
```

The controls behave like the Avalonia controls they derive from: bind `Text`, `IsChecked` and `Command` to a view
model, style them with selectors, and validate with Avalonia's data validation. Each component page in this gallery
shows the bindings, events and keyboard model of that control.

### Name clashes with Avalonia controls

`Button`, `Calendar`, `Carousel`, `ContextMenu`, `DatePicker`, `Slider`, `SplitButton`, `TabItem`, `TimePicker`,
`TreeView` and `TreeViewItem` share their names with types in `Avalonia.Controls`. In XAML the `arc:` prefix keeps them
apart. In C#, alias one namespace when a file uses both:

```csharp
using Avalonia.Controls;
using ArcButton = TKCode.Arc.Button;

var save = new ArcButton { Content = "Save changes" };
```

## Optional packages

### Icons

Arc's own glyphs (`{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Check}` and 186 more) cover every icon the components use. For any other
Lucide icon, add `TKCode.Arc.Icons.Lucide` and use its namespace:

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:lucide="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc/lucide">
    <lucide:LucideIcon Kind="Sparkles" Size="20" />
</UserControl>
```

### Blocks and the data grid

`TKCode.Arc.Blocks` (page-level blocks), `TKCode.Arc.AdvancedCharts` (the `DataGrid`) and `TKCode.Arc.Special` (animated
AI explainers) are separate packages. Add the ones you need and register them inside `UseArc(...)`:

```bash
dotnet add package TKCode.Arc.Blocks --version 0.3.2-preview.1
dotnet add package TKCode.Arc.AdvancedCharts --version 0.3.2-preview.1
dotnet add package TKCode.Arc.Special --version 0.3.2-preview.1
dotnet add package TKCode.Arc.Workflow --version 0.3.2-preview.1
dotnet add package TKCode.Arc.Themes.Pixel --version 0.3.2-preview.1    # optional: pixel-art theme (UseArcPixelTheme())
dotnet add package TKCode.Arc.Themes.Corners --version 0.3.2-preview.1    # optional: global corner style (UseArcCorners())
dotnet add package TKCode.Arc.Mobile --version 0.3.2-preview.1    # optional: touch-first controls, not yet verified on devices (UseArcMobile())
```

```csharp
.UseArc(arc => arc
    .UseArcControls()
    .UseArcBlocks()            // TKCode.Arc.Blocks
    .UseArcAdvancedCharts()    // TKCode.Arc.AdvancedCharts
    .UseArcSpecial()           // TKCode.Arc.Special
    .UseArcWorkflow()          // TKCode.Arc.Workflow
    .UseArcPixelTheme()        // TKCode.Arc.Themes.Pixel
    .UseArcCorners()           // TKCode.Arc.Themes.Corners
    .UseArcMobile())           // TKCode.Arc.Mobile
```

Each package registers the packages it depends on (Blocks registers the controls, for example), and registering one
twice does nothing.

### Languages

Arc handles the application language (namespace `TKCode.Arc.Localization`). To offer more than one, declare them in
`UseArc(...)`: the first argument is the start-up language, the second the languages the application offers. The
gallery offers English, Simplified Chinese and Traditional Chinese this way:

```csharp
.UseArc(arc => arc
    .UseArcControls()
    .UseLanguages(LanguageTags.EnUS, [LanguageTags.EnUS, LanguageTags.ZhCN, LanguageTags.ZhTW]))

// Later, for example from a settings page:
ArcLanguage.Set(LanguageTags.ZhCN);
```

`ArcLanguage.Current` is the current language, `ArcLanguage.Culture` the culture to format numbers and dates with, and
`ArcLanguage.Changed` is raised after a switch. The packages with built-in text of their own (the `DataGrid`, the
workflow canvas) ship English, Simplified Chinese and Traditional Chinese. Start-up fails with a list of the missing
text when an enabled package does not cover a declared language.

Arc controls ship English defaults for their built-in text (for example "Show password" or "Clear search"). The
controls expose that text as properties or label objects, so you can translate it from your own resources.

## Publishing

- **NativeAOT and trimming.** The libraries are trimming- and AOT-compatible and use no reflection. Publish a desktop
  app as a single self-contained file with `-p:PublishAot=true`, or `-p:PublishSingleFile=true --self-contained` when
  you do not use AOT.
- **.NET SDK 11 and NativeAOT.** The .NET 11 SDK's optimized AOT publish drops the compiled XAML of every Avalonia
  12.1 application, which then fails at start with `No precompiled XAML found`. Turn it off in the application's
  project file: `<UseOptimizedPublish>false</UseOptimizedPublish>`.
- **License.** Arc, its Foundation package and its other dependencies are MIT licensed (Avalonia too), so a closed-source
  single-file or NativeAOT publish has no LGPL obligations.
- **Globalization.** Do not enable `InvariantGlobalization`. Number, currency and date formatting in the inputs,
  pickers and charts needs culture data.
- **macOS.** The repository's `tools/macos` scripts show how the gallery is wrapped into a signed and notarized `.app`;
  the same flow applies to your application.

## Building from source

Building the repository needs the .NET 11 SDK (see `global.json`) and the .NET 10 runtime (the tests and the
gallery run on `net10.0`):

```bash
dotnet build TKCode.Arc.slnx
dotnet test tests/TKCode.Arc.Core.Tests
dotnet test tests/TKCode.Arc.Foundation.Tests
dotnet test tests/TKCode.Arc.Tests
dotnet run --project gallery/TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Desktop -f net10.0
```

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Arc controls appear unstyled or empty | `UseArcControls()` is not called in `UseArc(...)` | Add it to the `UseArc(...)` callback. |
| `InvalidOperationException` at start-up listing missing text | A language in `UseLanguages` is not covered by an enabled package | Declare only languages the packages ship, or add the missing translations. |
| `No precompiled XAML found` in a NativeAOT build | The .NET 11 SDK's optimized publish | Set `<UseOptimizedPublish>false</UseOptimizedPublish>`. |
| `ThemeSwitcher` switches without its transition | The window has no overlay layer | Give the window's template a `VisualLayerManager` with `EnableOverlayLayer="True"`. |
| Headings and code use the system font | The fonts are not registered | Call `WithInterFont()` and `WithArcFonts()` on the `AppBuilder`. |
| Wrong number or date formats, or exceptions while formatting | `InvariantGlobalization` is enabled | Remove it from the project file. |
| `'Button' is an ambiguous reference` | `TKCode.Arc` and `Avalonia.Controls` are both imported | Alias one of them, as shown above. |
| Restore warnings about Avalonia versions | Another package pulls a different Avalonia | Reference Avalonia `12.1.4` explicitly in the application. |
| Blocks, `DataGrid` or Special types are not found | The package is not referenced or not registered | Add `TKCode.Arc.Blocks`, `TKCode.Arc.AdvancedCharts` or `TKCode.Arc.Special` and call `UseArcBlocks()`, `UseArcAdvancedCharts()` or `UseArcSpecial()` in `UseArc(...)`. |

# Theming

Every color, radius, shadow, font size and motion timing in TKCode.Arc comes from one set of design tokens, the
ArcDesign tokens. Controls never hard-code a value; they read tokens, so changing the appearance (light or dark), the
accent or a single token restyles the whole application at once and keeps every control consistent with the others.

This page explains how the theme is built, how to switch it at run time, which tokens exist, and how to use them in
your own views and controls.

## How the theme is built

The theme runtime is part of `TKCode.Arc.Foundation`, which `TKCode.Arc` brings in:

1. **The theme manager** (`ArcThemeManager`, one per application, created by `UseArc(...)`) owns the active theme and
   publishes its tokens to the application's resources.
2. **The theme state** (`ArcThemeState`) is everything a theme is computed from: the appearance (`Light`, `Dark` or
   `System`), the accent seed, the motion level, theme presets and token overrides. It is immutable; an
   `ArcThemeBuilder` describes a change, and what a change does not mention stays as it was.
3. **The ArcDesign identity** holds Arc's own tokens: colors, radii, type, spacing and motion.
4. **Control tokens** hold the geometry of individual controls (paddings, widths, offsets) and colors that do not
   depend on the accent.

When a theme is applied, every token is recalculated for the appearance and the accent, only the values that changed
are written, and every control that reads a token updates in place: no page reload, no restart.

## Light and dark

Set the theme the application starts with in `UseArc(...)`, and change it later with `ArcTheme.Apply`:

```csharp
using TKCode.Arc;

// Program.cs: the first frame is drawn with this theme.
.UseArc(arc => arc
    .UseArcControls()
    .WithTheme(t => t.Appearance(ArcAppearance.System).Accent(ArcAccentPreset.Violet)))

// At run time: only the appearance changes, the accent and every other setting stay.
public static void ApplyAppearance(bool dark)
    => ArcTheme.Apply(t => t.Appearance(dark ? ArcAppearance.Dark : ArcAppearance.Light));
```

`ArcAppearance.System` follows the operating system's light or dark setting and switches with it. `ArcTheme.State` is
the current state, and `ArcThemeManager.Current` the manager: its `IsDark` says which appearance is showing, and
`StateChanged` is raised after every change. `ArcThemeManager.ApplyAsync` computes the tokens on a background thread and
publishes them on the UI thread; await it, and never block on it (`.Wait()`, `.Result`) on the UI thread, which
deadlocks. A change that names an unknown token or an invalid value throws `ArcThemeException` listing every problem,
and nothing is changed.

Keep the user's choice (light, dark, or following the system) in your settings store and pass it to `WithTheme` at
start-up, so the first frame already has the right appearance. The gallery's Appearance panel works exactly this way.

### The ThemeSwitcher control

For a header or a toolbar, `ThemeSwitcher` is a ready-made light and dark switch with Arc's page transitions (`Reveal`,
`Eclipse`, `Split` and `Rise`, set with `Variant`). Pressing it raises `ThemeChangeRequested`. If no handler marks the event
handled, the switcher changes the appearance through `ArcThemeManager` itself and keeps the rest of the current theme. Handle the event
when the application owns the appearance, for example to save the choice:

```csharp
themeSwitcher.ThemeChangeRequested += async (_, e) =>
{
    e.Handled = true;
    await settings.SaveAppearanceAsync(e.Next);
    ApplyAppearance(e.Next == ThemeSwitcherAppearance.Dark);
};
```

The transition draws on the window's overlay layer. A window whose template has no `VisualLayerManager` with
`EnableOverlayLayer="True"` switches without it.

## Accents

Arc ships eight accent presets. The accent drives buttons, selection, focus rings, switches, sliders, chart series and
links; everything else stays neutral, so changing the accent changes the brand color without changing the layout or
the contrast of text.

![The eight accent presets in their light and dark tones](https://docs.tkcode.si/shots/Guides/Theming/images/AccentPresets.webp)

```xml
<StackPanel Width="720" Spacing="10">
    <Grid ColumnDefinitions="120,*,*">
        <TextBlock Grid.Column="1" Text="Light" Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
        <TextBlock Grid.Column="2" Text="Dark" Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
    </Grid>
    <Grid ColumnDefinitions="120,*,*">
        <TextBlock Text="Neutral" VerticalAlignment="Center" Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
        <Border Grid.Column="1" Height="32" CornerRadius="16" Margin="0,0,8,0" Background="#353535" />
        <Border Grid.Column="2" Height="32" CornerRadius="16" Background="#BEBEBE" />
    </Grid>
    <Grid ColumnDefinitions="120,*,*">
        <TextBlock Text="Violet" VerticalAlignment="Center" Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
        <Border Grid.Column="1" Height="32" CornerRadius="16" Margin="0,0,8,0" Background="#7747FF" />
        <Border Grid.Column="2" Height="32" CornerRadius="16" Background="#A78BFF" />
    </Grid>
    <Grid ColumnDefinitions="120,*,*">
        <TextBlock Text="Blue" VerticalAlignment="Center" Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
        <Border Grid.Column="1" Height="32" CornerRadius="16" Margin="0,0,8,0" Background="#0562EF" />
        <Border Grid.Column="2" Height="32" CornerRadius="16" Background="#6BA3FF" />
    </Grid>
    <Grid ColumnDefinitions="120,*,*">
        <TextBlock Text="Green" VerticalAlignment="Center" Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
        <Border Grid.Column="1" Height="32" CornerRadius="16" Margin="0,0,8,0" Background="#0DB879" />
        <Border Grid.Column="2" Height="32" CornerRadius="16" Background="#53DCA6" />
    </Grid>
    <Grid ColumnDefinitions="120,*,*">
        <TextBlock Text="Amber" VerticalAlignment="Center" Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
        <Border Grid.Column="1" Height="32" CornerRadius="16" Margin="0,0,8,0" Background="#F3AD20" />
        <Border Grid.Column="2" Height="32" CornerRadius="16" Background="#FFCB62" />
    </Grid>
    <Grid ColumnDefinitions="120,*,*">
        <TextBlock Text="Orange" VerticalAlignment="Center" Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
        <Border Grid.Column="1" Height="32" CornerRadius="16" Margin="0,0,8,0" Background="#F48120" />
        <Border Grid.Column="2" Height="32" CornerRadius="16" Background="#FFAD5E" />
    </Grid>
    <Grid ColumnDefinitions="120,*,*">
        <TextBlock Text="Coral" VerticalAlignment="Center" Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
        <Border Grid.Column="1" Height="32" CornerRadius="16" Margin="0,0,8,0" Background="#F15F55" />
        <Border Grid.Column="2" Height="32" CornerRadius="16" Background="#FF9386" />
    </Grid>
    <Grid ColumnDefinitions="120,*,*">
        <TextBlock Text="Rose" VerticalAlignment="Center" Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
        <Border Grid.Column="1" Height="32" CornerRadius="16" Margin="0,0,8,0" Background="#ED4E9D" />
        <Border Grid.Column="2" Height="32" CornerRadius="16" Background="#FF8BC5" />
    </Grid>
</StackPanel>
```

| Preset | Seed | Accent, light | Accent, dark | Strong, light |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Neutral` (default) | `#353535` | `#353535` | `#BEBEBE` | `#1F1F1F` |
| `Violet` | `#7747FF` | `#7747FF` | `#A78BFF` | `#5528CE` |
| `Blue` | `#0562EF` | `#0562EF` | `#6BA3FF` | `#074DB7` |
| `Green` | `#0DB879` | `#0DB879` | `#53DCA6` | `#087C54` |
| `Amber` | `#F3AD20` | `#F3AD20` | `#FFCB62` | `#9C6300` |
| `Orange` | `#F48120` | `#F48120` | `#FFAD5E` | `#AA4700` |
| `Coral` | `#F15F55` | `#F15F55` | `#FF9386` | `#B92C27` |
| `Rose` | `#ED4E9D` | `#ED4E9D` | `#FF8BC5` | `#AE2570` |

Each preset has hand-tuned values for both appearances: the accent, a stronger shade for text and pressed states, a
subtle tint for selected backgrounds, the color of text on the accent, and the colors of switches and checkboxes.

### A brand color

When none of the presets matches the brand, pass the brand color itself. Arc derives the light and dark accent family
from it in the OKLCH color space, so the steps stay perceptually even:

```csharp
ArcTheme.Apply(t => t.Accent(Color.Parse("#0E7C86")));
```

Check the result in both appearances. Very light seeds (yellow, lime) make poor text colors on white; prefer a preset
or a darker shade of the brand for those.

## Design tokens

Tokens are grouped by what they describe. The names below are the members of `ArcDesignTokenKind`, which is also how
XAML refers to them.

![Surfaces, text levels, status colors and radii, read from the tokens of the current appearance](https://docs.tkcode.si/shots/Guides/Theming/images/TokenPreview.webp)

```xml
<StackPanel Width="720" Spacing="16">
    <UniformGrid Columns="4">
        <Border Height="84" Margin="0,0,8,0" Padding="12" CornerRadius="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource RadiusControl}"
                Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Background}"
                BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Border}" BorderThickness="1">
            <TextBlock Text="Background" Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
        </Border>
        <Border Height="84" Margin="4,0" Padding="12" CornerRadius="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource RadiusControl}"
                Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Surface}"
                BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Border}" BorderThickness="1">
            <TextBlock Text="Surface" Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
        </Border>
        <Border Height="84" Margin="4,0" Padding="12" CornerRadius="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource RadiusControl}"
                Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource SurfaceMuted}"
                BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Border}" BorderThickness="1">
            <TextBlock Text="SurfaceMuted" Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
        </Border>
        <Border Height="84" Margin="8,0,0,0" Padding="12" CornerRadius="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource RadiusControl}"
                Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource SurfaceRaised}"
                BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Border}" BorderThickness="1">
            <TextBlock Text="SurfaceRaised" Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
        </Border>
    </UniformGrid>
    <StackPanel Spacing="4">
        <TextBlock Text="Foreground: titles and primary text" Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" FontSize="16" />
        <TextBlock Text="TextSecondary: descriptions and secondary values" Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
        <TextBlock Text="TextMuted: hints, captions and placeholders" Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
    </StackPanel>
    <StackPanel Orientation="Horizontal" Spacing="8">
        <arc:Badge Content="Success" Tone="Success" />
        <arc:Badge Content="Warning" Tone="Warning" />
        <arc:Badge Content="Danger" Tone="Danger" />
        <arc:Button Content="Accent" />
        <arc:Button Content="Secondary" Variant="Secondary" />
    </StackPanel>
</StackPanel>
```

| Group | Tokens | Values and use |
|---|---|---|
| Surfaces | `Background`, `Surface`, `SurfaceMuted`, `SurfaceRaised`, `Scrim` | The page, cards and fields, muted wells, raised menus and popups, the dim layer behind dialogs. |
| Text | `Foreground`, `TextSecondary`, `TextMuted` | Three levels of emphasis. Use `TextMuted` only for hints, never for information a reader must see. |
| Borders | `Border`, `BorderStrong`, `BorderSubtle` | Card outlines, field frames, dividers. |
| Accent | `Accent`, `AccentStrong`, `AccentSubtle`, `AccentForeground` | Brand color, its strong shade for text, its tint for selected backgrounds, text on the accent. |
| Controls | `ControlOn`, `ControlOnSubtle`, `ControlThumb`, `ControlThumbOn`, `ControlTrack`, `ControlTrackHover`, `ControlGlyph`, `ControlFill`, `ControlThumbShadow` | Switches, checkboxes, radios and sliders. |
| Status | `Success`, `Warning`, `Danger` and their `…Subtle` tints | Results, warnings and errors; the tints are for badge and alert backgrounds. |
| Data | `Series1` to `Series4`, `Neutral0` to `Neutral11` | Chart series that follow the accent, and a neutral ramp for charts and illustrations. |
| Focus | `FocusRing`, `FocusRingWidth` (2), `FocusRingOffset` (2) | The keyboard focus ring. |
| Shape | `RadiusControl` (18), `RadiusPanel` (26), `RadiusSurface` (34), `RadiusPill` | Fields and buttons, cards and panels, large surfaces, pills and badges. |
| Size | `ControlSizeSM` (36), `ControlSizeMD` (44), `ControlSizeLG` (50); `GlyphSizeSM` (16), `GlyphSizeMD` (20), `GlyphSizeLG` (24); `IconStrokeWidth` | Control heights for the `Small`, `Medium` and `Large` sizes, and icon sizes. |
| Spacing | `Space1` (4) to `Space24` (96) | A 4 px based spacing scale: 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 32, 40, 48, 64, 80, 96. |
| Type | `TypeXS` (12), `TypeSM` (14), `TypeBase` (16), `TypeLG` (18), `TypeXL` (22), `Type2XL` (28), `Type3XL` (36), `Type4XL` (52), `Type5XL` (72) | The type scale. |
| Type style | `BodyFontFamily`, `DisplayFontFamily`, `MonoFontFamily`, `WeightRegular`, `WeightMedium`, `LeadingBody` (1.4), `LeadingDisplay` (1.1), `TrackingBody`, `TrackingDisplay` | Families, weights, line height and letter spacing for body and display text. |
| Elevation | `ShadowResting`, `ShadowRaised`, `ShadowFloating` | Cards at rest, raised cards and menus, floating dialogs and popovers. Dark mode uses deeper shadows. |
| Effects | `BlurSubtle`, `BlurSoft`, `BlurText`, `BackdropBlurDialog`, `BackdropBlurDrawer`, `ReduceTransparency` | Motion blur steps and the frosted backdrops of dialogs and drawers. |
| Motion | `Duration…`, `Ease…`, `Spring…`, `Stagger…`, `MotionMode` | Timings, curves, spring presets and the motion level. See **Motion**. |

## Using tokens in your views

### In XAML

`ArcDesignTokenResource` reads a token and follows theme changes:

```xml
<Border Padding="16"
        Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Surface}"
        BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource BorderSubtle}"
        BorderThickness="1"
        CornerRadius="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource RadiusPanel}">
    <StackPanel Spacing="4">
        <TextBlock Text="Usage this month"
                   FontSize="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TypeLG}"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
        <TextBlock Text="182 of 250 GB"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
    </StackPanel>
</Border>
```

### In code

`ArcTokens.Bind` binds a property to a token so it updates with the theme; `ArcTokens.Get` and `ArcTokens.GetColor`
read the current value once, for example to draw in a custom `Render`:

```csharp
ArcTokens.Bind(card, Border.BackgroundProperty, ArcDesignTokenKind.Surface);
ArcTokens.Bind(title, TextBlock.ForegroundProperty, ArcDesignTokenKind.Foreground);

var accent = ArcTokens.GetColor(chart, ArcDesignTokenKind.Accent);
```

Prefer `Bind` over `Get` for anything that stays on screen: a value read once does not change when the user switches
to dark mode.

### Control tokens

Each Arc control has its own token class for its geometry, read in XAML as `{arc:<Control>TokenResource Name}`. For
example, all text fields share `{arc:FieldTextBoxTokenResource SelectionFill}` for the selection color. Control tokens
hold values that do not depend on the accent, so they rarely need to change; when you write a control that should look
like an Arc field, read these instead of copying the numbers.

## Changing tokens

`Token(name, value)` overrides the final value of an ArcDesign token, `Token(identity, name, value)` one of a control's
tokens, and `MotionLevel` sets the motion level for the whole theme:

```csharp
ArcTheme.Apply(t => t
    .Accent(ArcAccentPreset.Blue)
    .Token(nameof(ArcDesignTokenKind.Danger), "#D92D20")
    .Token("Switch", "TrackWidth", "50")
    .MotionLevel(ArcMotionLevel.Reduced));
```

Values are text, parsed for the token's type (`#RRGGBB`, `12`, `4,8`, `120ms`, an enum member). The identity of a control
token is its control name; the mobile controls use `MobileButton`, `MobileCheckbox`, `MobileDialog`, `MobileSwitch` and
`MobileToast`. `ClearTokens()` removes every override.

Change as little as possible. A token change applies everywhere: overriding `Danger` changes every error message,
destructive button and failed status in the application. Overrides of colors should be checked in both appearances,
because the override is not recalculated for dark mode.

## Corner style

Arc's corners are round: 18 for controls, 26 for panels, 34 for surfaces. If your product wants squarer corners, change
the corner style instead of overriding the four `Radius*` tokens. Those four are only the top layer: the radius steps
used inside templates, the radius tokens of about 300 control properties (a checkbox box, a combobox option, the
highlight behind a hovered menu row) and the radii that some controls compute while they animate are separate values.
Setting only the four leaves popups, hover backgrounds and checkboxes round.

The `TKCode.Arc.Themes.Corners` package sets all of them with one call and changes nothing but corners: colors, borders,
shadows and motion stay as they are. Register it with `UseArcCorners()` in `UseArc(...)`, then:

```csharp
using TKCode.Arc.Themes.Corners;

ArcTheme.Apply(t => t
    .Accent(ArcAccentPreset.Blue)
    .Corners(ArcCornerStyle.Square));
```

| Style | Result |
|---|---|
| `ArcCornerStyle.Default` | Arc as shipped. Nothing is written. |
| `ArcCornerStyle.Scale(0.5)` | Every radius is multiplied by the factor. `Scale(0)` is `Square`, `Scale(1)` is `Default`, a factor above 1 rounds more. |
| `ArcCornerStyle.Square` | Every corner is square. |

- **Pills and circles.** Radii of 999 and more (pill buttons, round avatars, dots) keep their shape under `Scale`. Only
  `Square` flattens them, so a square style turns round avatars into squares. Use `Scale` to keep them round.
- **Presets.** A corner style is a theme preset (`ArcThemePreset`): a named set of token overrides for light and dark.
  `Corners(style)` is `Preset(ArcCornerPresets.Create(style))`; `ArcCornerPresets.Square` and `ArcCornerPresets.Half`
  are ready-made. A preset covers every Arc package and skips the ones the application has not registered.
- **Replacing.** A corner style fills one slot (`ArcCornerPresets.Slot`), so the next `Corners(...)` replaces it and
  `Corners(ArcCornerStyle.Default)` removes it. Your own `Token(...)` overrides are applied after presets and win.
- **Scroll bars.** Scroll bars keep their thin pill shape under every corner style.
- **Pixel.** The `TKCode.Arc.Themes.Pixel` package (`UseArcPixelTheme()`) adds the Pixel style: square corners, hard
  shadows, a limited palette for light and dark and pixel fonts. Apply it with `ArcTheme.Apply(t => t.Pixel())` and
  go back with `t.RemovePreset(ArcPixelPresets.Slot)`. It has its own slot, so a corner style chosen after it changes
  its corners.

## Styling a single control

For local adjustments, use Avalonia's normal tools instead of tokens:

- **Properties**: `Width`, `Margin`, `HorizontalAlignment` and the documented properties of each control.
- **Styles**: a `Style` with a selector such as `arc|Button.toolbar` changes every button with that class in a scope.
- **Control themes**: a `ControlTheme` with `BasedOn` the Arc theme replaces the template of one kind of control in
  your application while keeping Arc's states.

Keep colors in these styles token-based (`{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource ...}`) so they still follow the appearance.

## Guidelines

**Do**

- Read every color from a token. A single hex value in a view is a bug in dark mode.
- Use the accent for the one action or state that matters on a screen; leave the rest neutral.
- Pair status colors with words or icons. A red border alone does not explain an error, and some readers cannot see
  the difference between red and green.
- Test each screen in light and dark, with at least two accents, before shipping.

**Avoid**

- Using `TextMuted` for information people must read: it has the lowest contrast of the three text levels and is
  meant for short hints and captions.
- Overriding many tokens to restyle the library into a different design system; the controls' spacing, radii and
  motion are tuned together.
- Hard-coding `#FFFFFF` for text on an accent background; use `AccentForeground`, which is dark on light accents such
  as Amber.

---

# Motion

Motion in TKCode.Arc follows Arc's motion system: springs for anything that moves or changes size, short eased fades
for color and opacity, and rolling digits and word-by-word rewrites for text that changes. Motion is there to explain
what changed (where a panel came from, which value moved, which word is new), not to decorate. Every animation in the
library respects a motion level, so people who are sensitive to motion, and machines that need to stay light, get a
calmer interface without losing any information.

## Motion levels

There are three levels, `ArcMotionLevel.Full`, `Reduced` and `Off`:

| Level | What moves | When to use it |
|---|---|---|
| `Full` (default) | Springs, travel, scale, morphs, blur, staggered entrances, rolling digits | The normal experience. |
| `Reduced` | Only short fades and color changes; positions and sizes jump to their end, decorative loops stop | People who asked for less motion, remote desktop sessions, presentations. |
| `Off` | Nothing; every change applies at once | Tests and screenshots, kiosk and low-power devices. |

No information is carried by motion alone: under `Reduced` and `Off`, the end state is the same as under `Full`.

### Setting the level

`ArcMotion.Level` is an inherited attached property. Set it on a window to affect everything in it, or on any
container to affect only that part of the interface:

```csharp
ArcMotion.SetLevel(mainWindow, ArcMotionLevel.Reduced);
```

```xml
<StackPanel arc:ArcMotion.Level="Off" Spacing="12">
    <arc:Progress Label="Import" Value="64" />
    <arc:Switch Content="Sync in background" IsChecked="True" />
</StackPanel>
```

The theme can set a level for the whole application too, through `ArcTheme.Apply(t => t.MotionLevel(...))` (see
**Theming**). The effective level of a control is the lower of the two: the inherited `ArcMotion.Level` and the theme's
motion mode. A window set to `Full` in a theme set to `Reduced` runs reduced motion.

The library does not read the operating system's reduce-motion preference on its own. Offer a setting in your
application (the gallery's Appearance panel has Full, Reduced and Off), store it with the user's other preferences,
and apply it to the main window at start-up.

## The motion system

### Springs

Arc's springs are defined by how long they look and how much they bounce, not by physics constants. The presets are
`ArcSpring` values and are also available as `ArcMotionPresets`:

| Spring | Shape | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| `Smooth` | 0.4 s, no bounce | Motion that reports state: switch thumbs, panels, progress, values. |
| `Snappy` | 0.26 s, bounce 0.12 | Presses, small indicators, icon swaps, pop-ins, menus. |
| `Morph` | 0.42 s, bounce 0.16 | Shared highlights, widths that follow content, shape morphs. |
| `Responsive` | stiffness 520, damping 38 | Direct manipulation that must keep up with the pointer. |
| `Gentle` | stiffness 340, damping 34 | Larger, calmer movements. |

A spring started while another is running continues from the current position and velocity, so interrupting an
animation (pressing a button twice, dragging back) never jumps.

### Durations and easing

| Token | Value | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| `DurationInstant` | 120 ms | Hover and press colors. |
| `DurationFast` | 160 ms | Small fades, the reduced-motion replacement for most movements. |
| `DurationExit` | 180 ms | Leaving elements; exits are quicker than entrances. |
| `DurationStandard` | 240 ms | Most fades and color transitions. |
| `DurationConsidered` | 480 ms | Larger, deliberate changes. |
| `DurationSpring` | 580 ms | The CSS-style spring curve. |

The easing curves are `EaseEnter`, `EaseExit`, `EaseStandard` and `EaseInOut` (`ArcEasings` in code). Staggered
entrances use `StaggerChar` (16 ms), `StaggerWord` (40 ms), `StaggerLine` (80 ms) and `StaggerItem` (35 ms) between
elements.

### Performance

Motion runs on a shared frame scheduler: running springs and loops advance together in one batch per frame, and
nothing is scheduled while nothing moves. Continuous effects (skeleton pulses, shimmers, live dots) pause
when their control is scrolled out of view, hidden or detached. Animated blurs are quantized to 0.25 px steps and
reused, so a running blur does not allocate per frame.

## Motion in your own controls

The rules the library follows apply to controls you write as well.

### Transitions in a control theme

Declare transitions in the control's `ControlTheme`, under the motion pseudo-classes, and set
`arc:ArcMotion.Tracks="True"` so the control receives them. A tracked control gets `:motion-full` or
`:motion-reduced` after it is loaded, so the first frame never animates; with level `Off` it gets neither, and nothing
animates:

```xml
<ResourceDictionary xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
                    xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
                    xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <ControlTheme x:Key="StatusPanelTheme" TargetType="Border">
        <Setter Property="arc:ArcMotion.Tracks" Value="True" />
        <Style Selector="^:motion-full">
            <Setter Property="Transitions">
                <Transitions>
                    <arc:SpringDoubleTransition Property="Opacity" Spring="Smooth" />
                    <arc:SpringThicknessTransition Property="Padding" Spring="Snappy" />
                </Transitions>
            </Setter>
        </Style>
        <Style Selector="^:motion-reduced">
            <Setter Property="Transitions">
                <Transitions>
                    <DoubleTransition Property="Opacity" Duration="0:0:0.16" />
                </Transitions>
            </Setter>
        </Style>
    </ControlTheme>
</ResourceDictionary>
```

The spring transitions (`SpringDoubleTransition`, `SpringThicknessTransition`, `SpringCornerRadiusTransition`,
`SpringSizeTransition`, `SpringPointTransition`, `SpringVectorTransition` and
`SpringTransformOperationsTransition`) take a `Spring` preset, or a custom `VisualDuration` and `Bounce`. Under reduced
motion, replace movement with a short opacity fade and let sizes and positions change at once.

### Motion that a theme cannot express

When a value must follow the pointer, keep its velocity across interruptions, or drive custom drawing, use
`MotionValue<T>`. It honors the effective motion level of its owner: under `Off`, and for springs under `Reduced`, it
jumps to the target.

```csharp
public sealed class SpendBar : Control
{
    private readonly MotionValue<double> _fill;
    private double _shown;

    public SpendBar()
    {
        _fill = new MotionValue<double>(this, 0, MotionVectors.Double);
        _fill.Changed += value =>
        {
            _shown = value;
            InvalidateVisual();
        };
    }

    public void ShowShare(double share) => _ = _fill.AnimateTo(share, MotionSpec.Spring(ArcSpring.Smooth));

    public override void Render(DrawingContext context)
    {
        var accent = ArcTokens.GetColor(this, ArcDesignTokenKind.Accent);
        context.FillRectangle(new SolidColorBrush(accent), new Rect(0, 0, Bounds.Width * _shown, Bounds.Height));
    }
}
```

`MotionVectors` covers `double`, `Point`, `Vector`, `Size`, `Rect`, `Thickness`, `CornerRadius` and `Color`; each
component runs its own spring. `MotionSpec.Tween(duration, easing)` runs a timed curve instead of a spring, and
`MotionSpec.Instant` jumps. For loops (a pulse, a sweep) use `LiveLoop`, which pauses off screen and below its minimum
motion level; for a value that runs to 1 over a fixed time (a hold-to-confirm fill, a countdown) use `MotionTimeline`.

Use code-driven motion only when a control theme cannot express it, and say why in a comment next to it. Theme
transitions are cheaper, easier to review and automatically follow the motion level.

## Guidelines

**Do**

- Animate the change, not the element: move what moved, fade what appeared, roll the digit that changed.
- Keep entrances under half a second and exits quicker than entrances.
- Give every animated change an end state that reads correctly without the animation, then check it with `Off`.
- Use `Snappy` for feedback on a press and `Smooth` for anything that reports a value.

**Avoid**

- Motion as the only signal of a state change; pair it with text, an icon or a color.
- Animating many large surfaces at once; stagger them or animate the container.
- Bounce on anything that represents money, progress or an error: it reads as playful.
- Infinite loops in the main content; reserve them for loading states and stop them when the content arrives.

## Testing

- Run tests and capture screenshots with `ArcMotionLevel.Off`, so the results show final states and do not depend on
  timing. The library's own tests and the gallery's screenshots do this.
- Review each screen once with `Reduced`: nothing should slide, scale or bounce, and nothing should be missing.
- Watch for layout jumps under `Off`: a container that only looked right because of a size animation needs a fixed
  layout.

# AI and MCP

AI coding assistants work well with TKCode.Arc, because everything they need is written down in plain text: every
component has a Markdown page written from its source, every public property and event has an XML description, and
the conventions are consistent across the library. What makes the difference between generated code that compiles and
code that invents properties is the context the assistant is given. This page shows where that context lives, how to
hand it over, and how to review what comes back. The documentation site publishes the same knowledge for assistants
that fetch it themselves: an `llms.txt` index, every page as Markdown, and an agent skill.

## What an assistant should know first

Most mistakes assistants make with this library come from a few wrong assumptions. State these up front, in a project
instruction file or at the start of a conversation:

| Fact | Why it matters |
|---|---|
| This is Avalonia 12 with TKCode.Arc, not WPF, WinUI or HTML. | Assistants otherwise mix in WPF properties (`Visibility`, `DataTemplateSelector`) or CSS ideas. |
| Arc controls live in `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`. | Without the prefix, `Button` resolves to Avalonia's own button and loses Arc's look. |
| The app calls `AppBuilder.UseArc(arc => arc.UseArcControls())`, and switches the theme with `ArcTheme.Apply(...)`. | Without `UseArcControls()` the controls are unstyled; theme APIs from other libraries do not exist here. |
| Colors, radii and fonts come from `{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource ...}` or `ArcTokens`. | Hard-coded hex values break dark mode and accents. |
| Motion is declared under `^:motion-full` and `^:motion-reduced` and respects `ArcMotion.Level`. | Hand-written animations otherwise ignore reduced motion. |
| Only documented properties exist. | The component pages and API tables list them; anything else is invented. |

## Where the knowledge lives

| Source | Location | Best for |
|---|---|---|
| `llms.txt` | https://docs.tkcode.si/llms.txt | The first thing to give an assistant: install steps, rules, and every page with a one-line summary and a link to its Markdown. |
| Pages as Markdown | A page's address plus `.md`, such as https://docs.tkcode.si/components/button.md (translations under `/zh-CN/` and `/zh-TW/`) | One component, block or guide in full, with example source and API reference, without a clone. |
| Agent skill | https://docs.tkcode.si/skills/tkcode-arc/SKILL.md | Coding agents that load skills: workflow, rules, component choices and a review checklist. |
| Component pages | `gallery/TKCode.Arc.Gallery/Docs/<Category>/<Component>/en-US.md` (also `zh-CN.md`, `zh-TW.md`) | When to use a component, usage, binding, validation, accessibility, keyboard and motion. |
| Live examples | `gallery/TKCode.Arc.Gallery/Demos/<Category>/<Component>/*.axaml` | Working XAML for each example on the pages. |
| API descriptions | The XML documentation shipped with the packages | Every public property, event and type, as IntelliSense shows it and as the API tables list it. |
| This gallery | The Docs section and every component page | Reading in context, with live examples. |
| Repository conventions | `AGENTS.md` at the repository root | Contributors and assistants working on the library itself. |

### Copy page

Every component page has **Copy page** at the top. It copies the entire page as Markdown, including the source of
every live example (the `.axaml` and its code-behind) and the generated API table. Paste it into the conversation when
you ask for help with a component: the assistant then works from the real API and real examples instead of from
memory.

For a screen that uses several components, copy each of their pages, or point the assistant at the Markdown files in
the repository when it can read files directly.

## llms.txt and Markdown pages

The gallery at https://docs.tkcode.si is an Avalonia WebAssembly app that draws to a canvas, so an assistant that
fetches a page's address gets no text. The site therefore publishes the same pages as plain text, generated from the
docs pages each time it is published:

| Address | Contents |
|---|---|
| `/llms.txt` | The index, in the llms.txt format: what the library is, how to install it, rules for agents, and every guide, component and block with a one-line summary and a link to its Markdown. |
| `/llms-full.txt` | Every English page in one file, for assistants with a large context window. |
| `/<section>/<slug>.md` | One page: its address plus `.md`, such as `/docs/theming.md`, `/components/button.md` or `/blocks/sidebar.md`. A component page is what **Copy page** copies, under a header with its package and install command. |
| `/zh-CN/…`, `/zh-TW/…` | The same pages in Simplified and Traditional Chinese, such as `/zh-CN/components/button.md`. |

For an assistant that can fetch web pages, one sentence is enough:

```text
Before writing UI code with TKCode.Arc, read https://docs.tkcode.si/llms.txt, then fetch the Markdown page of every
component you use and use only the properties and events in its API reference.
```

## Agent skill

A skill is a folder of instructions that a coding agent loads when a task needs it. The TKCode.Arc skill holds the
workflow, the rules on this page, a table of which component fits which need, and two reference files:

| File | Contents |
|---|---|
| `SKILL.md` | The workflow (find, read, install, wire, style, review), the rules, the common tokens and quick component decisions. |
| `components.md` | Every component and block by group, with its class, its purpose and a link to its page. |
| `checklist.md` | The review checklist an agent runs before it finishes a screen. |

To install it for Claude Code in a project, download the three files into `.claude/skills/tkcode-arc/`:

```bash
mkdir -p .claude/skills/tkcode-arc
for file in SKILL.md components.md checklist.md; do
  curl -fsSL "https://docs.tkcode.si/skills/tkcode-arc/$file" -o ".claude/skills/tkcode-arc/$file"
done
```

Put the folder in `~/.claude/skills/` instead to use it in every project; other agents that support skills read the
same layout from their own skills folder. The files name the TKCode.Arc version they describe, so download them again
after an upgrade.

## A project instruction file

Assistants such as Claude Code, Cursor and GitHub Copilot read an instruction file from the repository (for example
`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` or `.github/copilot-instructions.md`). A section like this one, adapted to your app, prevents
most of the mistakes above:

```text
## UI library: TKCode.Arc

- UI is Avalonia 12.1.4 + TKCode.Arc. Do not use WPF or WinUI APIs.
- Setup: AppBuilder.UseArc(arc => arc.UseArcControls()); theme changes: ArcTheme.Apply(t => t.Appearance(...)).
- Arc controls use xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc" (arc:Button, arc:Input, ...).
- Only use properties, events and enum values that the component's docs page or API table lists.
- Colors, radii, spacing and fonts: {arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Name} in XAML, ArcTokens.Bind in code.
  Never hard-code a color.
- Forms: arc:Input / arc:Select / arc:Switch with Label and Description; errors through ErrorMessage
  or data validation on the bound property.
- Motion: Arc controls animate themselves. For custom controls, declare transitions under ^:motion-full
  and ^:motion-reduced with arc:ArcMotion.Tracks="True".
- View models use CommunityToolkit.Mvvm ([ObservableProperty], [RelayCommand]).
- Component docs: https://docs.tkcode.si/llms.txt (every page as Markdown, such as
  https://docs.tkcode.si/components/button.md)
```

## Prompts that work

Give the assistant the business goal, the component pages, and the constraints. Compare:

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| "Make a settings page." | "Build a workspace settings view with arc:Input for the name and billing email, arc:Select for the currency and arc:Switch for the weekly digest. Use the attached Input, Select and Switch pages. Bind to a WorkspaceSettingsViewModel with ObservableValidator; validate the email on lost focus." |
| "Add a chart." | "Show daily active users for the last 30 days with arc:LineChart, following the attached LineChart page. Data comes from IAnalyticsService.GetDailyActiveUsersAsync(); format numbers with the current culture." |
| "Make it look nicer." | "Align this form with the Input page's content guidelines: sentence-case labels, a description for each field that has a constraint, and error messages that say how to fix the value." |

Ask for one screen or one component at a time, and ask the assistant to list the properties it used and where each is
documented. That list is quick to check against the API tables.

## Reviewing generated code

Before accepting code an assistant wrote, check:

- **Names.** Every `arc:` element, property, event and enum value exists in the component's API table. A XAML
  property that does not exist fails at build time; an event handler with the wrong argument type fails later.
- **Tokens.** No hex colors or fixed corner radii in views; tokens instead.
- **Binding modes.** Two-way properties (`Text`, `IsChecked`, `SelectedItem`, `Value`) are bound to settable view model
  properties; read-only ones (`EffectiveErrorMessage`, `SelectedValues`) are only read.
- **Accessibility.** Every field has a `Label` (visible, or hidden with `IsLabelVisible="False"` only when something
  else on screen names it); icon-only buttons have an accessible name.
- **Motion.** No hand-written animations where a control already animates, and custom transitions under the motion
  pseudo-classes.
- **Threading.** Values that come from background work are set on the UI thread (`Dispatcher.UIThread`).

The skill's `checklist.md` is a longer form of this list, written for an agent to run on its own code.

## MCP

The Model Context Protocol (MCP) lets an assistant read resources and call tools from a server, instead of relying on
what was pasted into the conversation.

TKCode.Arc does not ship its own MCP server yet. Until it does, three setups give an assistant the documentation
directly:

- **Assistants that fetch web pages**: start them at https://docs.tkcode.si/llms.txt (see above).
- **Assistants that read files** (Claude Code, Cursor and similar): clone the repository next to your project, or add
  it to the workspace, and point the assistant at `gallery/TKCode.Arc.Gallery/Docs` and `.../Demos`.
- **Clients that only use MCP**: run a file system MCP server over the docs folder. With the reference server from the
  MCP project, a client configuration looks like this:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "tkcode-arc-docs": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem", "/path/to/TKCode.Arc/gallery/TKCode.Arc.Gallery/Docs"]
    }
  }
}
```

The assistant can then list the component folders and read the page for each component it uses. Keep the clone on
the same version as the packages in your application, so the docs describe the API you compile against.

---

# Changelog

All notable changes to TKCode.Arc, newest first. Versions follow [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/). While a
version carries a `-preview` suffix, the API may still change between releases; read the notes before upgrading and
keep the version pinned in your project. The same list is kept in `CHANGELOG.md` in the repository.

NuGet packages published with each release: `TKCode.Arc`, `TKCode.Arc.Core`, `TKCode.Arc.Foundation` (from 0.3.2), `TKCode.Arc.Fonts` and
`TKCode.Arc.Icons.Lucide`, `TKCode.Arc.Blocks`, `TKCode.Arc.AdvancedCharts`, `TKCode.Arc.Special`, `TKCode.Arc.Workflow`, `TKCode.Arc.Themes.Pixel`, `TKCode.Arc.Themes.Corners`, `TKCode.Arc.Mobile`, `TKCode.Arc.Terminal`, `TKCode.Arc.Audio`, `TKCode.Arc.Audio.Native` and `TKCode.Arc.Audio.Browser`.

## 0.3.2-preview.1 (2026-10-28)

Arc no longer depends on AtomUI. Every package now depends only on Avalonia and on the new MIT package `TKCode.Arc.Foundation`, so the whole dependency chain is under permissive licenses and closed-source applications can publish Arc as a single file or with NativeAOT (issue #25). The application entry point and the theme API change; the controls, their properties and the XAML (`{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource ...}`, `{arc:XxxTokenResource ...}`) do not. See *Migrating from 0.3.1 to 0.3.2* below.

### Added

- **Foundation** (new package `TKCode.Arc.Foundation`): the theme manager (`ArcThemeManager`, `ArcTheme`, `ArcThemeState`, `ArcThemeBuilder`), theme presets (`ArcThemePreset`), local themes (`ArcThemeScope`), package registration (`AppBuilder.UseArc(...)`, `ArcBuilder`), languages (`ArcLanguage`, `ArcLanguageManager`) and a source generator for tokens, theme files and language catalogs. No reflection; trimming and NativeAOT safe. A control's theme loads the first time a control of that type is used.
- **ArcImage** and `ImageSource` (Core): background image loading (http, `avares://`, files, `data:`, bitmaps) with a shared cache, on desktop and in the browser.
- **ArcOverlayHost** (Core): a panel with its own overlay layer, so dialogs, drawers and sheets opened inside it stay within it.
- **Base theme** (Core): Arc's own themes for the Avalonia controls its templates use (`ScrollViewer`, `ScrollBar`, `ItemsControl`, `PathIcon`, `TextSelectionHandle` and the popup hosts). It steps aside when the application uses `FluentTheme` or `SimpleTheme`.
- **Scroll bars** look like `ScrollArea`: thin, shown while the pointer is over the view or while it scrolls, hidden at rest. `ScrollViewer.AllowAutoHide="False"` keeps them visible.
- **Corners theme**: `UseArcCorners()` and `t.Corners(style)`; ready-made `ArcCornerPresets.Square` and `ArcCornerPresets.Half`.
- **Menus**: long menus scroll inside `MaxDropDownHeight`.
- **Gallery**: the desktop window draws its own title bar (logo, title, pin on top; window buttons on Windows and Linux).

### Changed

- **Breaking: entry point.** `AppBuilder.UseAtomUI(b => b.UseDesktopControls().UseArc())` is now `AppBuilder.UseArc(arc => arc.UseArcControls())`. The `Application` class no longer needs to be `partial`.
- **Breaking: theme API.** `ThemeConfigBuilder`, `ThemeAlgorithm`, `IThemeManager.ApplyThemeAsync` and `WithArc(...)` are replaced by `ArcTheme.Apply(t => ...)`, `ArcThemeManager.Apply` / `ApplyAsync` and `WithTheme(...)` in `UseArc`.
- **Breaking: Pixel and Corners** are theme presets: `t.Pixel()` and `t.Corners(style)`. `ArcPixelTheme`, `ArcPixelScope`, `WithArcCorners` and `ArcCornerScope` are removed; a preset skips the packages the application has not registered.
- **Breaking: languages** move to `TKCode.Arc.Localization` (`ArcLanguage`, `ArcLanguageManager`); `UseLanguages` is on `ArcBuilder`.
- **Breaking: images and popups.** `AsyncImage` is replaced by `ArcImage` (`IsLoaded` is now `IsImageLoaded`). `ArcPopup` derives from Avalonia's `Popup`; `OpenMotion` and `CloseMotion` are `ArcPopupMotion`, `AdjustPlacementAnchor` lost its `ref flipX, ref flipY` parameters, and `IsOpen` stays true until the exit motion finishes. `ArcPopupFrame` replaces `BaseMotionActor`, and `ArcOverlayHost` replaces `ScopeAwareOverlayLayerPanel`.
- **Breaking: mobile token identities** are `MobileButton`, `MobileCheckbox`, `MobileDialog`, `MobileSwitch` and `MobileToast`, so they no longer share names with the desktop controls.
- Arc no longer shares its theme with AtomUI controls; applications that mix the two stay on 0.3.1-preview.6.
- **Performance**: `Button` builds its loading spinner the first time it loads; `Select` values and field messages shape their text only when needed.

### Fixed

- **ToastStack**: a toast dismissed while the stack resumes its timers no longer breaks the resume.
- **DataGrid**: the search box of the filter list is drawn again (it had no template).
- **PasswordField**: long strength labels no longer overlap the strength bar (#23).
- **Gallery**: the text box of the env variables event log is drawn again (it had no template).
- **Popups**: menus, selects and popovers draw their whole shadow again; the popup host clipped it, so their corners looked square.
- **Gallery**: the swipe actions inbox demo has its header, a live count and avatars, like Arc's.

### Migrating from 0.3.1 to 0.3.2

1. Remove every `AtomUI.*` package reference and `using AtomUI...;` line; Arc brings in what it needs.
2. Replace `UseAtomUI(...)` with `UseArc(...)` and rename `UseArc()` (the controls) to `UseArcControls()`. The other package calls keep their names and move into the `UseArc` callback.
3. Replace theme requests with `ArcTheme.Apply`. A change names only what changes; the rest of the state stays.
4. The `App` class may drop its `partial` keyword; nothing generates code into it any more.
5. With the .NET 11 SDK and `PublishAot`, set `<UseOptimizedPublish>false</UseOptimizedPublish>` in the application project.

```csharp
// 0.3.1
AppBuilder.Configure<App>()
          .UsePlatformDetect()
          .UseAtomUI(builder =>
          {
              builder.UseDesktopControls();
              builder.UseArc();
              builder.UseArcBlocks();
              builder.UseLanguages(LanguageTags.EnUS, [LanguageTags.EnUS, LanguageTags.ZhCN]);
          });

// 0.3.2
AppBuilder.Configure<App>()
          .UsePlatformDetect()
          .UseArc(arc => arc
              .UseArcControls()
              .UseArcBlocks()
              .UseLanguages(LanguageTags.EnUS, [LanguageTags.EnUS, LanguageTags.ZhCN])
              .WithTheme(t => t.Appearance(ArcAppearance.System)));
```

```csharp
// 0.3.1
var builder = new ThemeConfigBuilder()
    .WithAlgorithms(ThemeAlgorithm.Default, ThemeAlgorithm.Dark)
    .WithArc(arc => arc.Accent(ArcAccentPreset.Blue).MotionMode(ArcMotionLevel.Reduced));
await manager.ApplyThemeAsync(new ThemeRequest(IThemeManager.DEFAULT_THEME_ID, builder.Build(),
                                               ThemeTransitionReason.UserRequest));

// 0.3.2
ArcTheme.Apply(t => t
    .Appearance(ArcAppearance.Dark)
    .Accent(ArcAccentPreset.Blue)
    .MotionLevel(ArcMotionLevel.Reduced));
```

| 0.3.1 (AtomUI) | 0.3.2 |
|---|---|
| `AppBuilder.UseAtomUI(b => ...)`, `UseDesktopControls()` | `AppBuilder.UseArc(arc => ...)` |
| `UseArc()` (the controls) | `UseArcControls()` |
| `UseArcCore`, `UseArcBlocks`, `UseArcAdvancedCharts`, `UseArcSpecial`, `UseArcWorkflow`, `UseArcMobile`, `UseArcPixelTheme`, `UseArcGallery` on `IAtomUIBuilder` | The same names on `ArcBuilder`; new `UseArcCorners()` |
| `builder.UseLanguages(...)` | `arc.UseLanguages(...)`, same arguments |
| `partial class App`, `ApplicationStartup.Attach` | Not needed |
| `ThemeConfigBuilder`, `WithAlgorithms(ThemeAlgorithm.Dark)` | `t.Appearance(ArcAppearance.Dark)` (or `Light`, `System`) |
| `IThemeManager.ApplyThemeAsync(new ThemeRequest(...))` | `ArcTheme.Apply(t => ...)`, `ArcThemeManager.Current.Apply` / `ApplyAsync` (await it; never block on it on the UI thread) |
| `WithArc(a => a.Accent(preset or color))` | `t.Accent(preset or color)` |
| `WithArc(a => a.Token(name, value))` | `t.Token(name, value)` |
| `WithArc(a => a.ControlToken(catalog, control, name, value))` | `t.Token(identity, name, value)` |
| `WithArc(a => a.MotionMode(level))` | `t.MotionLevel(level)` |
| `WithArcCorners(style, scope)`, `arc.Corners(style, scope)`, `ArcCornerScope` | `t.Corners(style)`, `ArcCornerPresets` |
| `ArcPixelTheme.CreateRequest(...)`, `WithArcPixel(...)`, `ArcPixelScope` | `t.Pixel()`, `ArcPixelPresets`; back to Arc with `t.RemovePreset(ArcPixelPresets.Slot)` |
| `using AtomUI.Localization;` | `using TKCode.Arc.Localization;` |
| `Application.Current.GetLanguageManager()`, `ILanguageManager` | `ArcLanguageManager.Current` |
| `GetLocalizer().Get(kind)`, `Format(kind, args)` | `XxxLangResources.Get(kind)`, `XxxLangResources.Format(kind, args)` |
| `LanguageChanged`, `ChangeLanguage(tag)` | `Changed`, `Set(tag)` (or `ArcLanguage.Changed`, `ArcLanguage.Set`) |
| `FormattingCulture`, `CurrentLanguage` | `ArcLanguage.Culture`, `ArcLanguage.Current` |
| Mobile token overrides by catalog | Identities `MobileButton`, `MobileCheckbox`, `MobileDialog`, `MobileSwitch`, `MobileToast` |
| `AtomUI.Controls.ImageSource`, `AsyncImage`, `IsLoaded` | `TKCode.Arc.ImageSource`, `ArcImage`, `IsImageLoaded` |
| `ArcPopup` on AtomUI's `Popup`, `BaseMotionActor` | `ArcPopup` on Avalonia's `Popup`, `ArcPopupFrame`; `OpenMotion` / `CloseMotion` are `ArcPopupMotion` |
| `AdjustPlacementAnchor(placement, ref flipX, ref flipY)` | `AdjustPlacementAnchor(placement)` |
| `ScopeAwareOverlayLayerPanel` | `ArcOverlayHost` |
| AtomUI's themes for `ScrollViewer`, `ScrollBar`, `ItemsControl` and the popup hosts | Arc's base theme; scroll bars hide at rest (`ScrollViewer.AllowAutoHide="False"` keeps them) |

- **Windows and overlays.** Without AtomUI's window theme, a plain Avalonia `Window` has no overlay layer unless its template has a `VisualLayerManager` with `EnableOverlayLayer="True"`. `ThemeSwitcher` needs one for its transition; without it, it switches directly.
- **AtomUI controls.** An application that also uses AtomUI controls no longer gets one shared theme for both. Stay on 0.3.1-preview.6 until those screens are moved to Arc.

## 0.3.1-preview.6 (2026-10-28)

### Added

- **Cascader** (Extras): pick one node of a hierarchy level by level, such as province, city and district. The field, menu, gliding highlight and clear button match `Select`; a parent opens its children in a column to the right and the menu width springs to its new size. Data is read through delegates (`ChildrenSelector`, `TextSelector`, `ValueSelector`), so nothing is reflected. `SelectedItem`, `SelectedValue` and `SelectedPath` stay in step, and a value written before the data arrives is kept and resolved when it does. Options: `LeafOnly`, `ExpandTrigger`, `ShowFullPath`, `PathSeparator`, `IsClearable`, `IsReadOnly`; full keyboard support.

## 0.3.1-preview.5 (2026-10-28)

### Added

- **Audio** (new packages `TKCode.Arc.Audio`, `TKCode.Arc.Audio.Native` and `TKCode.Arc.Audio.Browser`): the `IAudioPlayer` abstraction behind the media blocks, silent by default, with desktop playback through miniaudio (`ArcAudioNative.Use()`) and WebAssembly playback through an HTML audio element (`ArcAudioBrowser.UseAsync()`).
- **Blocks**: `MediaPlayer` (cover art, playlist, seek bar, previous and next, volume with mute) and `FileUpload` (drop zone, file list, progress, validation).
- **Special**: a Cursor group with the `DotGrid`, `GravityWell` and `InkFluid` pointer effects.
- **Gallery**: the Northstar dashboard demo at `/demo`, a copy of uiarc.dev/demo with eleven pages and a sign-in page; open it from "Live demo" on the home page or "Demo" in the top menu.

### Fixed

- **ArcContentSwap**: showing a control again after it was swapped out no longer throws (switching the Webhooks inspector between Payload and Headers crashed the app).
- **Charts**: the axis tick next to the average line stays hidden, so the average label no longer overlaps it.
- **Webhooks**: Payload and Headers each open at their first line.

## 0.3.1-preview.4 (2026-10-27)

## 0.3.1-preview.1 (2026-10-26)

### Added

- **Mobile**: the new `TKCode.Arc.Mobile` package (`UseArcMobile()`) with the first touch-first controls: `Button` (press state, 44 x 44 touch target), `Switch`, `Page` (header, content and footer inside the safe area), `Navbar` and `Tabbar`. It depends on `TKCode.Arc.Core` only and has its own namespace. It has not been verified on Android or iOS devices yet, and it still pulls `Avalonia.Desktop` and `AtomUI.Desktop.Controls` in through `TKCode.Arc.Core`.
- **Gallery › Mobile**: a Mobile section with a phone-frame preview (iPhone 15, Pixel, small phone, tablet, portrait and landscape, status bar, simulated safe area, soft-keyboard placeholder). It is a desktop simulation, not a device.
- **Pixel theme**: the new `TKCode.Arc.Themes.Pixel` package (`UseArcPixelTheme()`): square corners, hard shadows and a limited palette in light and dark, with the Silkscreen and VT323 pixel fonts (SIL OFL) in `TKCode.Arc.Fonts` (`WithArcPixelFonts()`). The Gallery's Appearance panel has a Style switch, Arc or Pixel.
- **Tables › TreeTable**: a table with nested rows, tri-state selection, hierarchy-preserving sort, lazy-loaded children and treegrid keyboard navigation. The Gallery marks new components with a New badge for 60 days.
- **Core**: design tokens for border widths and corner radii (`EdgeThickness`, `FocusEdgeThickness`, `RadiusStep*`, `EdgeThickness*`) so a theme can change them; every default equals the value it replaces.

### Changed

- **Gallery** (web): the WebAssembly host is published without ahead-of-time compilation again, because the compiled build crashed at startup. Its icon URLs are versioned so browsers drop the old favicon.

### Fixed

- **Carousel**: a slide whose timer had already run out no longer advances the rotation again without yielding; it starts a fresh interval.

## 0.3.0-preview.5 (2026-10-24)

### Added

- **Workflow canvas**: the new `TKCode.Arc.Workflow` package (`UseArcWorkflow()`): `WorkflowCanvas` shows a graph of steps and connections and plays its runs, with pan and zoom, editing, connections, undo and redo, copy and paste, node templates, a minimap and layout of 500 steps in about 2 ms. Also `WorkflowNodeCard` and `WorkflowZoomControls`.
- **Blocks › Auth**: `SignIn`, `SignupForm`, `LoginSplit`, `LoginCentered`, `LoginImmersive`, `OtpInput`, `OnboardingIllustration` and `MultiStepForm`.
- **Core**: `PanZoomTransform`, `WheelRouter` and `LayeredGraphLayout`.

### Changed

- **Gallery** (web): the site is compiled ahead of time to WebAssembly, which smooths animations on slow CPUs; the first visit downloads more.

### Fixed

- **Memory**: many controls (`TreeView`, `ChatThread`, `Markdown`, the charts, `DataGrid`, the AI, Projects and Special blocks and more) listened to the data they show for their whole life and kept their page in memory. They now listen only while in a visual tree. `SiteFooter`, `SemanticZoom`, `AgentStatus` and the Gallery pages no longer leak either.
- **Menus**: a closed sheet no longer leaves its scrim over the window.
- **ChatThread**: the reaction picker no longer writes debug lines to the console.
- **Accordion** and **ExpandableCard**: cheaper dividers while opening, with an unchanged look.
- **Markdown** and the AI answers use StreamMark `0.1.0`.
