  `ExplodedView`) and the first AI blocks (Model picker, Agent memory, AI composer, AI chat, AI answer, plus the side
  panel and prompt studio).
- **Core**: `ArcSurface.Elevation` (dialogs, drawers, popovers and menus content knows it sits on a raised surface),
  `RollingDigitsFalloff.None`, new springs, `ArcContentSwap` modes, `ArcRing`, `WordDiff`, `WordPacer`,
  `DecoratedTextBlock` and 23 more Lucide glyphs.
- **Button**: a ghost button on a raised surface now has a visible hover and press fill.
- **Special inputs**: `TokenTextEditor`, a multi-line editor whose tokens act as single units; `MentionInput` is built
  on it.
- **Gallery**: the docs site serves `llms.txt`, `llms-full.txt`, every page as Markdown and an agent skill for AI
  assistants.

### Changed

- **Breaking, repository move**: the repository is now `AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc` and the XAML namespace follows it. Change
  `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AtomUICommunity/TKCode.Arc"` to `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
  (and the Lucide namespace likewise).
- **Sidebar**: `ResizeMode` now defaults to `Overlay`; set `ResizeMode="Push"` for the previous behavior.
- **Performance**: the motion scheduler advances each driver once per frame, hidden loops cost nothing, cached blur
  effects and text layouts, and a much cheaper ActivityTerrain and LayoutMorph.
- **Gallery**: the WebAssembly site downloads about 1.5 MB less before its first frame.

### Fixed

- **Tabs**, **PageHeader**, **Breadcrumb**, **ArcContentSwap**, **DataGrid**: templates are no longer built with a
  `null` data context.
- **Core**: a content swap that left the window mid-change no longer comes back half transparent; anchored popups draw
  their shadow with rounded corners again.
- **Sidebar**: content no longer keeps the first-frame width after the sidebar opens from the rail.
- **Motion**: fading a fill from or out to `Transparent` no longer flashes a gray (`ArcBrushTransition` mixes with
  premultiplied alpha).
- **TagInput**, **Textarea**, **TimePicker**: the heavy focus ring is gone; `FieldFrameToken` `FocusRing*` values are
  removed.

The full list is in `CHANGELOG.md` in the repository.

## 0.3.0-preview.1 (2026-10-22)

### Added

- **Core**: `ArcZoom.Scale`, an inherited attached property for apps that scale their window content. Anchored popups
  (menus, selects, tooltips, hover cards, popovers) draw in the window's overlay layer, outside the scaled container, so
  they could not follow the zoom; they now lay out at the inherited scale. `ArcPopup.Surface` returns the surface that
  was assigned to `Child` (the popup now hosts it in a scaling element, so `Child` itself is that element).
- **ExpandableContent**: the ExpandableText clamp, toggle and motion around any content, such as selectable text, a
  read-only editor or rendered Markdown. The clamp ends on a line of the content's first visible text (`TextBlock`,
  `SelectableTextBlock`, or a control that implements the new `IExpandableLineSource`); other content clamps at
  `Lines × LineHeight`. `ExpandableText` and `ExpandableContent` share the new `ExpandableClamp` base class.
- **ExpandableText**, **ExpandableContent**: `IsFadeEnabled` turns off the fade over the last line.

### Changed

- AtomUI is pinned to 6.2.8; 0.2.0-preview.1 was built on 6.2.7.
- **ExpandableText**: while collapsed, the text is laid out only to the line after the clamp, and in full when it opens.
  A 600-line text measured about 1ms collapsed instead of about 135ms. Text with inline controls is still laid out in
  full, so a link below the clamp can take focus. The clamp now ends on the text's own line boundaries instead of
  `Lines × LineHeight`.
- **ExpandableText**: `Lines`, `IsExpanded`, `MoreLabel`, `LessLabel`, `LineHeight`, `IsOverflowing` and
  `ExpandedChanged` are now declared on the new `ExpandableClamp` base class. Code that uses them through
  `ExpandableText` is unchanged.

### Fixed

- **ExpandableText**: a change of `IsExpanded` that arrives with a new data context, for example in a recycled item
  template, no longer animates or scrolls the page.
- **Switch**, **Checkbox**: a value that arrives with a new data context, for example when a detail view is reused for
  the next item, shows at once; the thumb no longer slides and stretches, and the check mark no longer draws in, as if
  the user had clicked.
- **Progress**: a `Value` change that leaves the whole percentage unchanged no longer restarts the spring or updates the
  readout and the accessibility status. A download that reports hundreds of times a second now costs one update per
  percent.
- **SegmentedControl** and the other gliding-indicator toggles: a hidden control no longer places its indicator on
  every layout pass of the window; it is placed when the control is shown again.
- **GlidingIndicator**: the outline pen is kept between frames instead of being created on every render.
- TreeView and JsonViewer: a second change to the rows before the next layout pass, while rows from the first change were
  still closing, threw `IndexOutOfRangeException` in `RowTop`. The panel now refreshes its row geometry as soon as the
  rows change.

# Button

> A clear, responsive action with quiet secondary states.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/button

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ButtonVariantsDemo">
    <WrapPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center" ItemSpacing="12" LineSpacing="12">
        <arc:Button Content="Save changes" Variant="Primary" />
        <arc:Button Content="Cancel" Variant="Secondary" />
        <arc:Button Content="Learn more" Variant="Ghost" />
        <arc:Button Content="Delete project" Variant="Danger" />
    </WrapPanel>
</UserControl>
```

## When to use

`Button` is the default control for a single action on a page, form, dialog or toolbar. It provides the four visual
weights a product needs (primary, secondary, ghost and danger), three heights, a loading state that keeps the label's
width, and a label that can change in place. Most actions in an application are this control, and the other Arc action
controls are specialised cases of the same idea.

- **Saving a customer record in a CRM**: a Save changes primary button at the foot of the contact form, with Cancel as a
  secondary button beside it. One primary action per form tells the person what the next step is.
- **Creating an invoice in a billing console**: Create invoice as the primary action of a dialog footer, with Save as
  draft as its secondary companion. Both use the same medium height so the footer stays aligned.
- **Adding a card in a checkout settings page**: Add card as a primary button, with View history as a ghost button beside
  it that does not compete with it.
- **Exporting a report in an analytics dashboard**: Export report with `IsLoading` while the file is built. The label
  keeps its width, the spinner shows where the label was, and keyboard focus stays on the button.
- **Deleting a project in a settings page**: Delete project as a danger button, so the colour warns before the press.
  Pair it with a confirmation step when the deletion cannot be undone.

## When not to use

- **A submit that must show its result on the button, such as Saved or Sent**: use `ActionButton`, which holds pending
  and success words and returns to idle by itself.
- **Two to five close alternatives for the same action**: use `SplitButton`, with the alternatives in its menu.
- **A destructive action that needs a deliberate press**: use `HoldToConfirm` from Gestures, so one accidental click
  cannot delete the data.
- **A value that stays selected, such as a view mode or a period**: use `SegmentedControl` from Toggles. A button runs an
  action once; it does not remember a choice.
- **Several related actions on the same object, such as Share, Duplicate and Archive**: use `ButtonGroup`, which joins
  them into one surface with dividers instead of a row of separate buttons.

## Usage

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:Button Content="Save changes" Variant="Primary" />
</UserControl>
```

`Button` derives from Avalonia's `Button`, so `Content`, `Click`, `Command`, `CommandParameter`, `IsEnabled`, `IsDefault`
and the Enter and Space activation all work as they do on any button. The Arc layer adds the variant, the size, the
loading state and the Arc frame, focus ring and motion. Because `Content` holds the label, a button can show any content
and not only text, but keep the label short so the width stays predictable.

### Anatomy

1. **Frame**: a 1 px border with the control radius (`RadiusControl`). The fill and the
   border colour come from the variant.
2. **Label** (`Content`): centred text in the small body size (`TypeSM`) and medium weight. A change to the content
   rises in place.
3. **Spinner** (`IsLoading`): a 16 px ring that turns in the centre of the frame while loading. The label stays in its
   slot, faded out, so the width does not change.
4. **Inline padding** by size: 12 px for `Small`, 16 px for `Medium` and 20 px for `Large`, on each side.
5. **Height** by size (`MinHeight`): 36 px for `Small`, 44 px for `Medium` and 50 px for `Large`.
6. **Focus ring**: a 2 px ring in the focus colour, drawn 2 px outside the frame with a
   22 px corner radius. It appears for keyboard focus only.

### Variants

`Variant` sets the visual weight. Use one `Primary` action per surface. The other variants answer the question "how
important is this action compared with the one next to it?"

| Variant | Fill and border | Text | Use it for |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Primary` | Foreground fill | Background colour | The one main action on a surface, such as Save changes or Create invoice |
| `Secondary` | Surface with a border | Foreground colour | The alternative beside the primary, such as Cancel or Save as draft |
| `Ghost` | Transparent, no border | Secondary text, foreground on hover | Low-emphasis actions in cards and toolbars, such as View history |
| `Danger` | Surface with a border | Danger colour | A destructive action, where the colour warns before the press |

```xml
<arc:Button Content="Save changes" Variant="Primary" />
<arc:Button Content="Cancel" Variant="Secondary" />
<arc:Button Content="Learn more" Variant="Ghost" />
<arc:Button Content="Delete project" Variant="Danger" />
```

Each variant has its own states. `Primary` lowers its opacity on hover and press. `Secondary` and `Ghost` fill with the
muted surface on hover and press. On a raised surface (a dialog, drawer, bottom sheet, popover or menu) `Ghost` uses a
stronger fill instead, because the muted surface is nearly the colour of the raised one. `Danger` turns its border to the danger colour on hover and press. Disabled buttons
keep their shape: `Primary` fades to 52 percent opacity, while the outlined variants switch to muted text on a muted
surface. The disabled danger label is tinted toward the surface, so it still reads as a danger action.

Keep a `Danger` button apart from the `Primary` action, with a secondary button or a clear gap between them, so the two
are not mistaken for each other.

### Sizes

`Size` sets the minimum height: `Small` is 36 px, `Medium` is 44 px (the default) and `Large` is 50 px. The size does
not change with the window width, so a row of buttons keeps its rhythm when the window narrows.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ButtonSizesDemo">
    <WrapPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center" ItemSpacing="12" LineSpacing="12">
        <arc:Button Content="Small" Size="Small" Variant="Secondary" />
        <arc:Button Content="Medium" Size="Medium" Variant="Secondary" />
        <arc:Button Content="Large" Size="Large" Variant="Secondary" />
    </WrapPanel>
</UserControl>
```

Use one size for each form, dialog or toolbar. `Small` suits tables, toolbars and inline actions, `Medium` is the default
for forms, dialogs and settings, and `Large` fits a single prominent action on a sign-in or empty-state page. Inline
padding follows the size, so the label's margin stays proportional to the height.

### Loading and label morph

Set `IsLoading` to `True` to show the spinner. The label stays in its slot with its width, so the footer of a dialog
does not shift while the request runs. The button keeps keyboard focus, but clicks and key presses are ignored until the
work ends. Changing `Content` swaps the label: the new text rises 4 px out of a soft blur while the old text moves up
3 px and fades, and the width springs to fit the new label.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ButtonLoadingMorphDemo">
    <arc:Button x:Name="Save"
                Content="Save"
                Variant="Primary"
                HorizontalAlignment="Center"
                Click="OnSaveClick" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class ButtonLoadingMorphDemo : UserControl
{
    public ButtonLoadingMorphDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
    }

    private async void OnSaveClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        Save.IsLoading = true;
        await Task.Delay(900);
        Save.IsLoading = false;
        Save.Content = "Saved";
        await Task.Delay(1600);
        Save.Content = "Save";
    }
}
```

```xml
<arc:Button Content="{Binding SaveLabel}"
            IsLoading="{Binding IsSaving}"
            Variant="Primary" />
```

Use `IsLoading` for work that finishes in a few seconds. For a longer job, such as an export of thousands of rows, show
progress in the page (for example a progress indicator or a status line) and keep the button for the request that starts
the job. A spinner that runs for a minute tells the person nothing about how far the work has come.

### Icon-only button

An icon-only button has no visible text, so give it an accessible name. A button that is 48 px wide or narrower is treated
as an icon button: it presses deeper, to 96 percent of its size, than a text button.

```xml
<arc:Button Size="Small" Variant="Ghost"
            AutomationProperties.Name="Close">
    <TextBlock Text="×" />
</arc:Button>
```

Give every icon-only button a name that describes its action, such as "Close" or "Remove filter", and a tooltip when the
icon is not self-explanatory. The name is what a screen reader announces, and it is the only way the action is identified
for people who cannot see the glyph.

### Disabled

Set `IsEnabled` to `False`. Outlined variants keep their shape, so an unavailable action still reads as a button. A
disabled button leaves the tab order, as any disabled control does.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ButtonDisabledDemo">
    <WrapPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center" ItemSpacing="12" LineSpacing="12">
        <arc:Button Content="Primary" IsEnabled="False" />
        <arc:Button Content="Secondary" Variant="Secondary" IsEnabled="False" />
        <arc:Button Content="Ghost" Variant="Ghost" IsEnabled="False" />
        <arc:Button Content="Danger" Variant="Danger" IsEnabled="False" />
    </WrapPanel>
</UserControl>
```

Disable an action only when it cannot apply, and say why nearby, for example "Connect a payment method to publish
invoices" under the button. A disabled button without a reason sends the person looking for the problem.

### Binding to a view model

A button has a command, a label and a busy state. The view model owns the work and the button shows its progress. The
example below uses CommunityToolkit.Mvvm and an app service that saves the draft.

```csharp
public interface IInvoiceService
{
    Task SaveDraftAsync(string invoiceId);
}

public partial class InvoiceViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    private readonly IInvoiceService _invoices;

    public InvoiceViewModel(IInvoiceService invoices)
    {
        _invoices = invoices;
    }

    [ObservableProperty]
    private string _invoiceId = "inv_2026_0412";

    [ObservableProperty]
    private bool _isSaving;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private string _saveLabel = "Save changes";

    [RelayCommand]
    private async Task SaveAsync()
    {
        IsSaving = true;
        try
        {
            await _invoices.SaveDraftAsync(InvoiceId);
            SaveLabel = "Saved";
        }
        finally
        {
            IsSaving = false;
        }
    }
}
```

```xml
<StackPanel Width="420" Spacing="16">
    <arc:Input Label="Invoice number" Text="{Binding InvoiceId}" />
    <arc:Button Content="{Binding SaveLabel}"
                Command="{Binding SaveCommand}"
                IsLoading="{Binding IsSaving}"
                Variant="Primary"
                HorizontalAlignment="Right" />
</StackPanel>
```

Every binding is one way. `Content`, `IsLoading` and `Variant` come from the view model, and the button writes nothing
back. The button raises `Click` and runs `Command`, so `Command` is the place for the work. While `IsLoading` is
`True`, the button ignores activation, so `Command` does not run a second time when the person presses again. Compiled
bindings need `x:DataType` on the view; the examples leave it out for brevity.

### Example: billing settings footer

A payment settings panel in a SaaS billing console. The primary action, Save changes, is the last control on the right,
where the eye lands after reading the form. Cancel sits to its left as the secondary alternative. Remove card is a
danger button on the left, separated from the save pair, so a destructive press is not one slip away from saving. View
history is a ghost button because it navigates rather than changes anything.

![A billing settings footer with a ghost, a danger, a secondary and a primary button](https://docs.tkcode.si/shots/Docs/Buttons/Button/images/BillingFooter.webp)

```xml
<StackPanel Width="600" Spacing="20">
    <StackPanel Spacing="6">
        <TextBlock Text="Payment method"
                   FontSize="20"
                   FontWeight="SemiBold"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
        <TextBlock Text="Visa ending 4242, used for the Growth plan. Next invoice on 1 November 2026."
                   TextWrapping="Wrap"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
    </StackPanel>
    <Grid ColumnDefinitions="Auto,*,Auto">
        <arc:Button Grid.Column="0" Content="Remove card" Variant="Danger" />
        <StackPanel Grid.Column="2" Orientation="Horizontal" Spacing="8">
            <arc:Button Content="View history" Variant="Ghost" />
            <arc:Button Content="Cancel" Variant="Secondary" />
            <arc:Button Content="Save changes" Variant="Primary" />
        </StackPanel>
    </Grid>
</StackPanel>
```

### Content guidelines

- **Label**: a verb and its object in sentence case: "Save changes", "Create invoice", "Delete project". A bare verb such
  as "Delete" is ambiguous when two items are on the screen.
- **Length**: keep labels to two or three words. A long label pushes the other buttons of a footer off the row.
- **Dismissal**: use "Cancel" for a dialog that discards changes, and "Close" only when nothing was edited.
- **No punctuation**: no trailing period and no exclamation mark. The button is an instruction, not a sentence.
- **No vague confirmations**: "OK" tells the person nothing about what will happen. Name the change.

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| OK | Save changes |
| Submit | Create invoice |
| Delete | Delete project |
| Click here | View invoice |
| Done! | Saved |

### Best practices

**Do**

- Use one `Primary` button per surface. Two filled buttons compete for the same attention, and the person has to read
  both labels to find the next step.
- Put the primary action last, at the end of the row, with the secondary action to its left. People read the row from
  left to right and expect the commit action where the reading ends.
- Use one `Size` for every button in a form, dialog or toolbar. Mixed heights make a footer look broken even when each
  button is correct.
- Give an icon-only button an accessible name, and a tooltip when the icon is not self-explanatory.
- Use `IsLoading` for a request that finishes in seconds. The width is kept, so the layout does not move when the spinner
  appears.

**Avoid**

- Using `Danger` for an action that is not destructive. A red button trains people to ignore the colour, and it no longer
  warns them when it matters.
- Disabling the primary button to hide a validation problem. Validate when the person presses it and point to the first
  problem, so the reason is visible.
- Swapping the label back and forth on a timer. The button ends up in a state the person cannot predict; use `ActionButton`
  when a result word belongs on the button.
- Using `Ghost` for the only action on a surface. Its low contrast is right for a secondary navigation link, but the one
  action a screen needs should be visible at a glance.
- Putting several long labels in one row. The row then wraps or scrolls, and the actions lose their order.

### Common questions

**Why does a loading button keep focus but ignore my clicks?** That is by design. `IsLoading` swallows clicks and key
presses so the request is not repeated, and it keeps focus so the person and assistive technology stay in place. The
button reports itself as busy and unavailable.

**Does `Command` run while the button is loading?** No. The button returns early from its click handling while
`IsLoading` is `True`, so neither `Click` nor `Command` runs.

**Why does my menu anchor button not scale when pressed?** Set `IsPressScaleEnabled` to `False` on a button that opens
a popup or menu. The popup measures the anchor's pressed size, so the anchor answers with colour only. The property
defaults to `True`.

**My button width jumps when the label changes. How do I keep it steady?** The width springs to fit each label. To keep a
fixed width, set `MinWidth` to the width of the longest label you expect, so the button never narrows below it.

**Why does a narrow icon button press deeper than a text button?** Press depth follows the width. At 48 px or narrower the
button presses to 96 percent, and above 220 px it presses to 98.5 percent, so the depth matches the size of the target.

## API reference

### Button

Arc button: a clear, responsive action with quiet secondary states. Presses scale on a snappy spring, label changes crossfade with a short blur while the width springs to fit, and `IsLoading` shows a spinner while keeping keyboard focus (clicks are swallowed instead of disabling the button).

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Variant` | `ButtonVariant` | `Primary` | Visual style: Primary (default), Secondary, Ghost or Danger. |
| `Size` | `ControlSize` | `Medium` | Button height: Small, Medium (default) or Large. |
| `IsLoading` | `bool` | `false` | Puts the button in its loading state while true. |
| `IsPressScaleEnabled` | `bool` | `true` | Anchors of popups and menus must not scale on press (the popup measures the pressed size); they answer with color only. Defaults to true. |

Pseudo-classes: `:loading`, `:narrow`, `:wide`, `:raised`

Derives from `Button`: every member of `Button` works as well.

Companion types used on this page:

| `ButtonVariant` value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `Primary` | The default. The foreground fill for the main action of a surface. |
| `Secondary` | A surface with a border, for the alternative next to the primary action. |
| `Ghost` | A transparent button for low-emphasis actions. |
| `Danger` | A surface with a danger-coloured label, for destructive actions. |

`Size` uses the `ControlSize` values `Small`, `Medium` (the default) and `Large`.

## Accessibility

- The button has the Button role. An icon-only button needs `AutomationProperties.Name`, because it has no text to name it.
- While `IsLoading` is set, the button stays focusable and reports itself as busy and unavailable.
- Enter and Space activate the button. Clicks and key presses are swallowed while loading.
- Keyboard focus shows a 2 px ring offset by 2 px. Pointer focus draws no ring, so a click does not leave a highlight behind.
- A disabled button is removed from the tab order and reports itself as unavailable. It is dimmed, not hidden, so the
  person still sees that the action exists.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` | Moves focus to the next or previous button. A disabled button is skipped. |
| `Enter` / `Space` | Activates the button, raising `Click` and running `Command`. Ignored while `IsLoading` is `True`. |
| `Enter` in a text field | Presses the window's default button, the one marked `IsDefault="True"`, when there is one. |

## Motion

- A press scales the content down slightly and a release springs it back. Narrow icon buttons scale a little more.
- Label changes rise in from a soft blur, and the width springs to the new label. The spinner turns continuously while
  loading.
- Reduced motion removes the press scale and the width spring. Labels and the spinner fade with a short crossfade,
  and the spinner stops turning. Off replaces the label and the state at once.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| Press | Content scales to 97 percent (96 for icon buttons, 98.5 for wide ones), then springs back | No press scale | No press scale |
| Label changes | The new text rises from a soft blur, the old text fades up, the width springs to fit | Instant crossfade | Immediate |
| Loading starts or ends | The label fades under the spinner, which turns every 0.7 seconds | Crossfade, and the spinner stops turning | Immediate |
| Hover, press, disabled colours | The colours crossfade on a fast curve | Instant | Immediate |

## Related

- `ActionButton` for an asynchronous submit that shows pending and success on the button.
- `SplitButton` for a primary action with a menu of nearby alternatives.
- `ButtonGroup` for several related actions joined into one surface.
- `CopyButton` for copying a value with a confirmation.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `ActionButton` | A submit should show a pending word and a result word on the button |
| `SplitButton` | One default action sits next to two to five close alternatives |
| `ButtonGroup` | Several actions act on the same object and share one surface |
| `ConfirmMorph` | A destructive action should ask for confirmation in place |
| `HoldToConfirm` | A destructive action needs a deliberate press that cannot be triggered by accident |
| `SegmentedControl` | The control shows a choice that stays selected, such as a view mode |

# Action button

> A compact button for frequent toolbar actions.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/action-button

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ActionButtonDefaultDemo">
    <arc:ActionButton x:Name="Save" HorizontalAlignment="Center" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class ActionButtonDefaultDemo : UserControl
{
    public ActionButtonDefaultDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Save.AsyncAction = () => Task.Delay(1200);
    }
}
```

## When to use

`ActionButton` is the call to action for one asynchronous submit, such as Save, Publish or Send invite. It shows the
work on the button itself: the label changes to a pending word while the task runs, a spinner turns, and a success word
with a drawn check confirms the result. The person learns the outcome where they clicked, without a toast, and the
button returns to its idle label by itself. Place it at the end of a form, in a document header or in a settings card,
wherever the submit is the one action that matters.

- **Publishing a post in a content editor**: the Publish post button in the editor header reads Publishing while the
  post is sent and Published when it is live, so the editor knows the change landed without leaving the page.
- **Saving a settings page in an admin console**: the Save settings button at the foot of a workspace settings page
  shows Settings saved after the request succeeds, and the form stays on screen for the next change.
- **Sending an invitation from a team page**: Send invite becomes Sent once the mail service accepts the request, then
  returns to Send invite after 2.4 seconds so the admin can invite the next person.
- **Sending a test event from a webhook editor**: Send test event shows Sending while the endpoint is called and
  Delivered when it answers. A failed call returns the button to idle and the editor explains the error beside it.

## When not to use

- **An ordinary form submit with a spinner and no result word**: use `Button` with `IsLoading`. It keeps its label and
  width while the work runs and needs no success state.
- **A destructive action that needs a deliberate press**: use `HoldToConfirm` from Gestures. A hold makes an accidental
  delete hard, while a success word appears only after the data is already gone.
- **A destructive action that asks for confirmation in place**: use `ConfirmMorph`, which asks the question where the
  control sits before anything runs.
- **Several alternatives for the same action**: use `SplitButton`, for example Merge pull request with Squash and merge
  and Rebase and merge in its menu.
- **A row action repeated in a dense table**: keep the result in the row with a small `Button`. An animated label per row
  is noise, and each letter of the label is an animated element.
- **Copying a value to the clipboard**: use `CopyButton`, which confirms the copy inline and is built for that job.

## Usage

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:ActionButton Label="Save" PendingLabel="Saving" SuccessLabel="Saved" />
</UserControl>
```

```csharp
var save = new ActionButton
{
    Label = "Save",
    PendingLabel = "Saving",
    SuccessLabel = "Saved",
    AsyncAction = () => documentService.SaveAsync()
};
```

`ActionButton` derives from Avalonia's `Button`, not from the Arc `Button`. It keeps everything a button does: `Click`,
`Command`, `IsEnabled`, activation with Enter and Space, the focus model and the automation peer. It does not expose
`Variant`, `Size` or `IsLoading`, because it has one look and one height, and its pending state comes from
`AsyncAction`. Set `Label` rather than `Content`: the template draws the text from `Label`, `PendingLabel` and
`SuccessLabel`.

### Anatomy

1. **Label** (`Label`): the idle text, in the small body size (`TypeSM`) and medium weight. It is drawn by a text
   morph, so the pending and success words replace it in the same place. It is also the accessible name.
2. **Icon slot**: a 17 px square 8 px after the label. It shows a right arrow at idle, a
   16 px spinner while the action is pending and a check on success.
3. **Frame**: a 1 px border with the control radius (`RadiusControl`). The fill is the Foreground token and the text is
   the Background token, so the button is the inverse of the page: dark on a light page, light on a dark page.
4. **Padding and height**: 20 px inline padding and a minimum height of the medium control size (44 px). It has one
   size and does not follow the window width.
5. **Focus ring**: a 2 px ring in the focus color, drawn 2 px outside the frame. It appears for keyboard focus only.

The button aligns to the left by default. Set `HorizontalAlignment` when it sits in a centred column. Hover adds the
resting shadow to the frame. A press scales the button to 97 percent, or to 98.5 percent when it is wider than 220 px,
on a snappy spring. A pending button does not scale. Disabled, it fades to 70 percent opacity and shows the "not
allowed" cursor.

### Labels and reset

`Label` is the idle text and the accessible name. `PendingLabel` (default "Saving") shows while `AsyncAction` runs, and
`SuccessLabel` (default "Saved") shows after it completes. Use a verb for the idle label, its present participle for the
pending word and the past tense for the success word: "Publish post", "Publishing", "Published". A label set like this
keeps the width change small when the label morphs.

`ResetAfter` sets how long the success word stays before the button returns to idle. The default is 2.4 seconds
(2400 ms). A zero value keeps the success state until `Reset()` is called. Use the default in a toolbar, where the
result is a glance. Use zero on a settings page that the person keeps editing, so the confirmation does not vanish while
they read it.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ActionButtonLabelsDemo">
    <WrapPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center" ItemSpacing="12" LineSpacing="12">
        <arc:ActionButton x:Name="Publish"
                          Label="Publish post"
                          PendingLabel="Publishing"
                          SuccessLabel="Published" />
        <arc:ActionButton x:Name="Invite"
                          Label="Send invite"
                          PendingLabel="Sending"
                          SuccessLabel="Sent" />
    </WrapPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class ActionButtonLabelsDemo : UserControl
{
    public ActionButtonLabelsDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Publish.AsyncAction = () => Task.Delay(1500);
        Invite.AsyncAction = () => Task.Delay(800);
    }
}
```

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ActionButtonKeepResultDemo">
    <WrapPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center" ItemSpacing="12" LineSpacing="12">
        <arc:ActionButton x:Name="Settings"
                          Label="Save settings"
                          SuccessLabel="Settings saved"
                          ResetAfter="00:00:00" />
        <arc:Button Content="Reset"
                    Variant="Ghost"
                    Size="Small"
                    Click="OnResetClick" />
    </WrapPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class ActionButtonKeepResultDemo : UserControl
{
    public ActionButtonKeepResultDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Settings.AsyncAction = () => Task.Delay(700);
    }

    private void OnResetClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        Settings.Reset();
    }
}
```

```xml
<arc:ActionButton Label="Publish post"
                  PendingLabel="Publishing"
                  SuccessLabel="Published"
                  ResetAfter="00:00:03" />
```

Reset the button yourself when the state it reports is no longer true. `Reset()` returns to idle at once and cancels a
pending success reset. It also invalidates a run that is still in progress: when that task completes later, its result
is ignored and the button stays idle.

### Lifecycle

| Moment | State | Visible word | What the person hears |
|---|---|---|---|
| Button is ready | `Idle` | `Label` and the arrow | Name: `Label` |
| Activation starts `AsyncAction` | `Pending` | `PendingLabel` and the spinner | The pending label, once, from the status region |
| The task completes | `Success` | `SuccessLabel` and the check | The success label, once |
| `ResetAfter` elapses or `Reset()` runs | `Idle` | `Label` and the arrow | Nothing |
| The task throws | `Idle` | `Label`; `ActionFailed` is raised | Nothing from the button; show the error nearby |
| The button leaves the visual tree during success | `Idle` | `Label` | Nothing |

The state changes only through these moments, so you can read `State` (a read-only `ActionButtonState`) to decide what
else on the screen should change.

### Failure

When `AsyncAction` throws, the button returns to idle and raises `ActionFailed`. The event is a bubbling routed event,
and its `ActionButtonFailedEventArgs.Exception` holds what the action threw. The success word never shows, and the reset
timer does not start.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ActionButtonFailureDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12">
        <arc:ActionButton x:Name="Sync"
                          Label="Sync now"
                          PendingLabel="Syncing"
                          SuccessLabel="Synced"
                          HorizontalAlignment="Center"
                          ActionFailed="OnActionFailed" />
        <TextBlock x:Name="Message"
                   FontSize="13"
                   TextWrapping="Wrap"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class ActionButtonFailureDemo : UserControl
{
    public ActionButtonFailureDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Sync.AsyncAction = async () =>
        {
            await Task.Delay(900);
            throw new InvalidOperationException("The server did not answer.");
        };
    }

    private void OnActionFailed(object? sender, ActionButtonFailedEventArgs e)
    {
        Message.Text = $"Back to idle: {e.Exception.Message}";
    }
}
```

```csharp
sync.ActionFailed += (_, e) => status.Text = $"Back to idle: {e.Exception.Message}";
```

Show the message beside the button, not on it. The button is already back to its idle label, so the person can retry at
once, and the text next to it explains what went wrong. Keep the input the person typed, so the retry does not start from
an empty form.

### Commands and clicks

`Click` and `Command` run first, before `AsyncAction`. The button raises `Click` while it is still idle, then sets the
pending state and starts the action. Without an `AsyncAction`, the command or click counts as an immediate success, and
the success word shows at once. Setting both is valid: the command runs synchronously and the async action starts after
it, so the command should be the quick part of the work.

`ICommand.Execute` returns nothing, so a command cannot hold the pending state for a task. For asynchronous work, use
`AsyncAction` (see the view model example below).

### Disabled

Set `IsEnabled` to `False` to dim the button to 70 percent opacity and remove it from the tab order. While
`AsyncAction` is pending, the button keeps keyboard focus and ignores repeated activation without becoming disabled.
Use `IsEnabled` to block an action that cannot run, for example when there is nothing to save, and say why nearby.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ActionButtonDisabledDemo">
    <arc:ActionButton Label="Save" IsEnabled="False" HorizontalAlignment="Center" />
</UserControl>
```

Do not disable the button to show that a form is invalid. Validate when the person presses it, then move focus to the
first field that needs attention.

### Binding to a view model

An `ActionButton` has a commit action and reports a state, so the view model owns the work and the button only shows its
progress. The view model below uses CommunityToolkit.Mvvm. `PublishAsync` is an ordinary public method that returns a
`Task`.

```csharp
public partial class PostEditorViewModel : ObservableValidator
{
    private readonly IPostService _posts;

    public PostEditorViewModel(IPostService posts)
    {
        _posts = posts;
    }

    [ObservableProperty]
    [NotifyDataErrorInfo]
    [Required(ErrorMessage = "Enter a post title.")]
    private string _title = string.Empty;

    [RelayCommand]
    private void Discard()
    {
        Title = string.Empty;
    }

    public async Task PublishAsync()
    {
        ValidateAllProperties();
        if (HasErrors)
        {
            return;
        }
        await _posts.PublishAsync(Title);
    }
}
```

```xml
<StackPanel Width="420" Spacing="16">
    <arc:Input Label="Post title" Text="{Binding Title}" />
    <StackPanel Orientation="Horizontal" Spacing="8" HorizontalAlignment="Right">
        <arc:Button Content="Discard" Variant="Ghost" Command="{Binding DiscardCommand}" />
        <arc:ActionButton x:Name="Publish" Label="Publish post" PendingLabel="Publishing" SuccessLabel="Published" />
    </StackPanel>
</StackPanel>
```

```csharp
public partial class PostEditorView : UserControl
{
    public PostEditorView()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Publish.AsyncAction = () => ((PostEditorViewModel)DataContext!).PublishAsync();
    }
}
```

The bindings are one way. `Label`, `PendingLabel` and `SuccessLabel` come from the view or from localized resources, and
`Title` is two-way on the input. `ActionButton` writes nothing back: `State` is read-only, and its result is reported by
the view model's own state. The `AsyncAction` assignment stays in code because a method group cannot be bound to a
`Func<Task>` in XAML. Do not bind the same work to `Command` and `AsyncAction`, or it runs twice. The `Discard` button
uses `Command`, since it completes at once.

### Example: publishing a post in a content editor

A post editor header in a content management system. The title is the heading of the editor, and the footer holds the
three actions a writer uses: discard the draft, keep it as a draft and publish it. Publish is the only primary action on
the surface, so it is the only `ActionButton`. The explanatory copy says what publishing changes for readers, which is
the consequence the writer needs before pressing it. The success word Published confirms the change where the press
happened, and the button returns to Publish post in a few seconds, so the header stays ready for the next edit.

![A post editor footer with Discard, Save draft and an idle Publish post action button](https://docs.tkcode.si/shots/Docs/Buttons/ActionButton/images/PostEditorFooter.webp)

```xml
<StackPanel Width="600" Spacing="20">
    <StackPanel Spacing="6">
        <TextBlock Text="Q2 pricing update"
                   FontSize="20"
                   FontWeight="SemiBold"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
        <TextBlock Text="Draft saved 4 minutes ago. Starter plan readers see the new prices after you publish."
                   TextWrapping="Wrap"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
    </StackPanel>
    <StackPanel Orientation="Horizontal" Spacing="8" HorizontalAlignment="Right">
        <arc:Button Content="Discard" Variant="Ghost" />
        <arc:Button Content="Save draft" Variant="Secondary" />
        <arc:ActionButton Label="Publish post" PendingLabel="Publishing" SuccessLabel="Published" />
    </StackPanel>
</StackPanel>
```

### Content guidelines

- **Idle label**: a verb and its object in sentence case: "Publish post", "Save settings", "Send invite". The object
  tells the person what will change, which a bare "Submit" does not.
- **Pending label**: the present participle with no ellipsis: "Publishing". The spinner already signals progress, and a
  trailing "..." repeats it.
- **Success label**: the past tense of the action, in one or two words: "Published", "Settings saved". Keep it short so
  the width change stays small.
- **Scope**: one result per button. A success word that describes several things at once ("Saved and sent") is hard to
  trust and hard to translate.

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| Submit | Publish post |
| Saving... | Saving |
| Done! | Published |
| Click to save | Save settings |

### Best practices

**Do**

- Use `AsyncAction` for any work that must hold the pending state. A command returns before an async task finishes, so
  the button would show success too early.
- Keep one `ActionButton` on a surface, for the one submit that matters. Two animated results compete for attention and
  the person cannot tell which one the result belongs to.
- Set `Label`, `PendingLabel` and `SuccessLabel` before the button can run. A change to `Label` shows only when the
  button is idle, so while it is pending or showing success the visible word stays as it was until the button returns
  to idle.
- Show a failure beside the button. The button has already returned to its idle label, so the message belongs next to
  the field or the form that failed.

**Avoid**

- Placing it in a dense table or a list with one button per row. Each button animates its own letters, and the motion
  becomes noise (see the table guidance above).
- Setting `ResetAfter` to a fraction of a second. A success word that disappears before it is read gives no result, and
  the polite announcement is easy to miss.
- Disabling the button to show that a request is running. Pending already keeps the button focused and ignores
  activation, and it tells assistive technology the button is unavailable.
- Using it for a destructive action. A success word appears after the data is gone; ask for a deliberate press with
  `HoldToConfirm` or confirm in place with `ConfirmMorph`.

### Common questions

**Why does my async command show Saved before the save finishes?** `ICommand.Execute` returns nothing, so the button
sees the command as complete as soon as it returns. Move the work to `AsyncAction`, which the button awaits.

**Can I use `Command` and `AsyncAction` together?** Yes, but use each for a different job. The command runs first and
synchronously, then the async action starts. Two paths that save the same data run the save twice.

**How do I keep the success word on screen until the next save?** Set `ResetAfter` to zero (`ResetAfter="00:00:00"`).
The button then holds `Success` until you call `Reset()`, for example when the person edits the form again.

**What happens when the button leaves the visual tree while it shows success?** The reset timer stops and the button
returns to idle at once. A pending action is not cancelled: it keeps running, and when it completes the button records
the success only if that run is still the current one.

**Why does the label not change when I set `Content`?** The template draws the text from `Label`, `PendingLabel` and
`SuccessLabel`. `Content` is inherited from `Button` but is not part of the visual.

## API reference

### ActionButton

A call to action for one asynchronous submit (Save, Publish): pending and success show on the button itself. The changed letters of the label rise out of a soft blur while kept letters glide (P4) and the width follows on a spring (P5); the trailing arrow leaves in the direction of the action, a spinner turns while `AsyncAction` runs, a check draws itself on success (P15), and the button returns to idle after `ResetAfter`. Pending keeps keyboard focus: activation is swallowed instead of disabling the button.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Label` | `string` | `"Save"` | The idle label and, always, the accessible name (default "Save"). |
| `PendingLabel` | `string` | `"Saving"` | Shown while `AsyncAction` runs (default "Saving"). |
| `SuccessLabel` | `string` | `"Saved"` | Shown after the action succeeds (default "Saved"). |
| `ResetAfter` | `TimeSpan` | `00:00:02.4000000` | How long success stays before returning to idle (default 2.4s); zero keeps it. |
| `AsyncAction` | `Func<Task>?` | `null` | The work to run. The button is pending until the task completes; a fault returns it to idle and raises `ActionFailed`. `Command` and `Click` run first and, without an async action, count as an immediate success. |
| `State` | `ActionButtonState` | – | *Read-only.* Current phase: Idle, Pending while AsyncAction runs, or Success after it completes. Read-only. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ActionFailed` | `ActionButtonFailedEventArgs` | Raised when `AsyncAction` throws. |

Pseudo-classes: `:pending`, `:success`, `:wide`

Derives from `Button`: every member of `Button` works as well.

Companion types used on this page:

| `ActionButtonState` value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `Idle` | Shows `Label`. Activation runs `Click`, `Command` and `AsyncAction`. |
| `Pending` | `AsyncAction` is running. Shows `PendingLabel`. Activation is ignored. |
| `Success` | The action completed. Shows `SuccessLabel` until `ResetAfter` elapses or `Reset()` is called. |

| `ActionButtonFailedEventArgs` member | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `Exception` | What the action threw. The button is back at idle when the event is raised. |

## Accessibility

- The accessible name is always `Label`, so the letters of the animated label are not read one by one.
- While pending, the button reports itself as unavailable but keeps keyboard focus.
- A hidden polite status region announces the pending label and the success label, so the change is heard without
  moving focus.
- Enter and Space run the action. Repeated activation is ignored while pending.
- The button does not announce a failure. Put the error text in a place screen readers reach, such as a live region or
  a text block next to the button, so the person hears why the button went back to idle.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Enter` / `Space` | Runs the action. Ignored while the button is pending. |
| `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` | Moves to the next or previous control. A pending button keeps its focus stop, so focus does not jump. |

## Motion

- Changed letters rise out of a soft blur and kept letters glide to their new positions. The width follows on a spring.
- The arrow leaves in the direction of the action and returns from the left. A spinner turns while the action runs, and
  a check draws itself on success.
- Reduced motion removes the press scale, the width spring and the drawn check. Label changes become an instant
  crossfade. Off replaces the label at once.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| Label changes to pending or success | Changed letters rise from a soft blur, kept letters glide, the width springs | Instant crossfade | Immediate |
| Success check | Draws itself in 240 ms | Appears without drawing | Immediate |
| Press | Scales to 97 percent (98.5 percent when wide) on a snappy spring; never while pending | No press scale | No press scale |

## Related

- `Button` for a plain action, with `IsLoading` for a spinner and no result word.
- `CopyButton` for copying a value, with the same kind of inline confirmation.
- `ConfirmMorph` for a destructive action that asks for confirmation in place.
- `HoldToConfirm` for a destructive action that needs a deliberate press.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `Button` | The action has no result word, or it shows a spinner while the request runs |
| `SplitButton` | One default submit sits next to a menu of close alternatives |
| `CopyButton` | The action copies a value and the confirmation is an inline word |
| `ConfirmMorph` | A destructive action should ask a question in place before it runs |
| `HoldToConfirm` | A destructive action needs a deliberate press that cannot be triggered by accident |
| `ButtonGroup` | Several related actions on one object share a single surface |

# Action swap

> Swap an action label while preserving its place and intent.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/action-swap

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class ActionSwapPreviewDemo : UserControl
{
    public ActionSwapPreviewDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        // "Added" and "Sent" run a request; with the switch on, it fails and the pill shows "Try again".
        Library.AsyncAction = (next, _) => next.Id == "added" ? Request(1100, "Couldn't save the article. Try again") : null;
        Invite.AsyncAction = (next, _) => next.Id == "sent" ? Request(1300, "Couldn't send the invite. Try again") : null;
    }

    private async Task Request(int milliseconds, string failure)
    {
        await Task.Delay(milliseconds);
        if (Offline.IsChecked == true)
        {
            Status.Text = failure;
            throw new InvalidOperationException("offline");
        }
    }

    private void OnFollowChanged(object? sender, ActionSwapValueChangedEventArgs e) =>
        Status.Text = e.Value == "following" ? "You're following Emma Collins" : "You unfollowed Emma Collins";

    private void OnLibraryChanged(object? sender, ActionSwapValueChangedEventArgs e) =>
        Status.Text = e.Value == "added" ? "Saved to your library" : "Removed from your library";

    private void OnInviteChanged(object? sender, ActionSwapValueChangedEventArgs e)
    {
        if (e.Value == "sent")
        {
            Status.Text = "Invite sent to Ava Mitchell";
        }
    }

    private void OnOfflineChanged(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) =>
        Status.Text = Offline.IsChecked == true ? "Connection lost: the next request will fail" : "Connection restored";
}
```

## When to use

`ActionSwap` is one control that cycles through a few related states: Follow and Following, Send invite and Sent, Add
to library and Added. A press moves it to the next state and wraps around at the end. The pill keeps its place on the
screen while its width, tone, icon and letters change together, so the person sees that it is the same action in a new
state rather than a different button.

- **Following a person or a topic**: Follow becomes Following and fills in quietly, and a second press goes back. The
  pending word keeps the pill the same width of thought while the request is sent.
- **Sending an invitation or a message**: Send invite shows Sending while the mail service answers, then Sent with a
  drawn check, and returns to Send invite by itself after two seconds so the next person can be invited.
- **Adding something to a collection** (a library, a cart, a watch list): the pill folds into a round spinner while the
  server works and opens again with the result.
- **A toggle that can fail**: a rejected action shows a short failure word in place, then returns to the state it left,
  so the person can retry at once.

## When not to use

- **One save or publish that ends in a success tick**: use `ActionButton`, which has a fixed idle, pending and success
  sequence and a reset timer.
- **An action whose label never changes**: use `Button`.
- **A light and dark switch**: use `ThemeSwitcher`.
- **A destructive action that asks first**: use `ConfirmMorph`, which asks the question in place before anything runs.
- **A dense table with one control per row**: every letter is an animated element, so keep the count of swapping labels
  on a screen small.

## Usage

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:ActionSwap>
        <arc:ActionSwap.States>
            <arc:ActionSwapState Id="idle" Label="Send invite" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Send}" />
            <arc:ActionSwapState Id="sent" Label="Sent" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Check}" Tone="Success"
                                 PendingLabel="Sending" HoldFor="0:0:2" />
        </arc:ActionSwap.States>
    </arc:ActionSwap>
</UserControl>
```

```csharp
var swap = new ActionSwap { AsyncAction = async (next, current) => await invites.SendAsync() };
swap.States.Add(new ActionSwapState { Id = "idle", Label = "Send invite", Icon = ArcIcons.Send });
swap.States.Add(new ActionSwapState
{
    Id = "sent", Label = "Sent", Icon = ArcIcons.Check, Tone = ActionSwapTone.Success,
    PendingLabel = "Sending", HoldFor = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(2)
});
```

```xml

        <arc:ActionSwap.States>
            <arc:ActionSwapState Id="idle" Label="Send invite" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Send}" />
            <arc:ActionSwapState Id="sent" Label="Sent" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Check}" Tone="Success"
                                 PendingLabel="Sending" HoldFor="0:0:2" />
        </arc:ActionSwap.States>
    </arc:ActionSwap>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class ActionSwapSendInviteDemo : UserControl
{
    public ActionSwapSendInviteDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        // The task holds the working phase ("Sending") until the invite is sent; "Sent" then holds for two seconds.
        Invite.AsyncAction = async (next, _) =>
        {
            if (next.Id == "sent")
            {
                await Task.Delay(900);
            }
        };
    }
}
```

`ActionSwap` derives from Avalonia's `Button`. It keeps `Click`, `Command`, `IsEnabled`, activation with Enter and
Space, the focus model and the automation peer. Describe the faces in `States`, in order; `Value` is the `Id` of the
face being shown (the first one when it is null). The control needs at least two states: with fewer it is inert and
dimmed.

### States

Each `ActionSwapState` is one face:

- `Id` and `Label` are required. The label is also the accessible name while the state is shown.
- `Icon` is a 16 px Lucide glyph before the label. Use `ArcIcons` or `ArcIcons.Parse(pathData)`.
- `Tone` colors the pill: `Neutral` (the default, foreground fill), `Accent`, `Success`, `Warning` and `Quiet`. Filled
  tones carry the primary action; the tinted `Success` and `Warning` tones confirm a result with most of the color on
  the icon, and `Quiet` is a bordered surface for the "already done" side of a toggle.
- `PendingLabel` is shown while `AsyncAction` runs on the way into this state, such as Sending before Sent. Without it
  the pill folds into a round spinner.
- `HoldFor` holds the state for a while and then moves on by itself, for brief confirmations such as Sent. The timer
  restarts only when the state or the duration changes, so a data refresh never resets it.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ActionSwapTonesDemo">
    <arc:ActionSwap HorizontalAlignment="Center">
        <arc:ActionSwap.States>
            <arc:ActionSwapState Id="neutral" Label="Neutral" Tone="Neutral" />
            <arc:ActionSwapState Id="accent" Label="Accent" Tone="Accent" />
            <arc:ActionSwapState Id="success" Label="Success" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Check}" Tone="Success" />
            <arc:ActionSwapState Id="warning" Label="Warning" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.CircleAlert}" Tone="Warning" />
            <arc:ActionSwapState Id="quiet" Label="Quiet" Tone="Quiet" />
        </arc:ActionSwap.States>
    </arc:ActionSwap>
</UserControl>
```

### Actions

`AsyncAction` runs on press with the next and the current state, before the control moves on. Return a task to show the
working phase, or null to move on at once.

- While the task runs the control is **working**: it ignores presses, reports itself busy and keeps keyboard focus. A
  fast answer still shows the working shape for at least 450 ms, so it reads as a step and not as a flash.
- When the task completes the new state **commits**: `Value` changes, the label is announced and `ValueChanged` is
  raised.
- When the task faults, or the action throws, the control shows `FailureLabel` (default "Try again") for 1.8 seconds
  and returns to the state it left. Nothing commits.

```csharp
follow.AsyncAction = async (next, current) =>
{
    await api.SetFollowingAsync(userId, next.Id == "following");
};
follow.ValueChanged += (_, e) => status.Text = e.State.Label;
```

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ActionSwapFollowToggleDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12" HorizontalAlignment="Center">
        <arc:ActionSwap x:Name="Follow" HorizontalAlignment="Center" ValueChanged="OnValueChanged">
            <arc:ActionSwap.States>
                <arc:ActionSwapState Id="follow" Label="Follow" Tone="Accent" />
                <arc:ActionSwapState Id="following" Label="Following" Tone="Quiet" PendingLabel="Following" />
            </arc:ActionSwap.States>
        </arc:ActionSwap>
        <TextBlock x:Name="Message"
                   Text="Not following"
                   FontSize="13"
                   HorizontalAlignment="Center"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs

public partial class ActionSwapFollowToggleDemo : UserControl
{
    public ActionSwapFollowToggleDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Follow.AsyncAction = async (_, _) => await Task.Delay(700);
    }

    {
        Message.Text = e.Value == "following" ? "Following Maya Chen" : "Not following";
    }

```

### Working without a label

A state with no `PendingLabel` folds the whole pill into a circle around a small spinner while its action runs. The
padding eases down on the same spring as the width, and the letters give way as the shape closes. When the result
arrives the pill opens again and the new letters rise in as the shape widens.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ActionSwapSpinnerDemo">
    <arc:ActionSwap x:Name="Save" HorizontalAlignment="Center">
        <arc:ActionSwap.States>
            <arc:ActionSwapState Id="idle" Label="Add to library" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Plus}" />
            <arc:ActionSwapState Id="added" Label="Added" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Check}" Tone="Success" HoldFor="0:0:2.4" />
        </arc:ActionSwap.States>
    </arc:ActionSwap>
</UserControl>
```

```cs

{

    {
        InitializeComponent();
        // "Added" has no PendingLabel, so the pill folds into a round spinner while the task runs.
        Save.AsyncAction = async (next, _) =>
        {
            if (next.Id == "added")
            {
                await Task.Delay(1100);
            }
        };
```

### Failure

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ActionSwapFailureDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12" HorizontalAlignment="Center">
        <arc:ActionSwap x:Name="Publish" FailureLabel="Try again" HorizontalAlignment="Center">
            <arc:ActionSwap.States>
                <arc:ActionSwapState Id="draft" Label="Publish" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Send}" />
                <arc:ActionSwapState Id="live" Label="Published" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Check}" Tone="Success"
                                     PendingLabel="Publishing" HoldFor="0:0:2" />
            </arc:ActionSwap.States>
        </arc:ActionSwap>
        <TextBlock x:Name="Message"
                   FontSize="13"
                   HorizontalAlignment="Center"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class ActionSwapFailureDemo : UserControl
{
    private int _attempts;

    public ActionSwapFailureDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        // The first attempt fails: the pill shows "Try again" for 1.8 seconds, then returns to "Publish".
        Publish.AsyncAction = async (next, _) =>
        {
            await Task.Delay(800);
            if (_attempts++ % 2 == 0)
            {
                Message.Text = "The first attempt fails, the second succeeds.";
                throw new InvalidOperationException("The server did not answer.");
            }
            Message.Text = string.Empty;
        };
    }
}
```

Show the reason beside the control. The failure word is short on purpose ("Try again"); the detail belongs in a message
the person can read after the pill has returned to its state.

### Sizes

`Size` is `Small` (36 px high), `Medium` (44 px, the default) or `Large` (50 px), with 16, 20 and 24 px of inline
padding. The pill hugs its label, so give related states labels of similar length to keep neighbours from shifting.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ActionSwapSizesDemo">
    <StackPanel Orientation="Horizontal" Spacing="12" HorizontalAlignment="Center" VerticalAlignment="Center">
        <arc:ActionSwap Size="Small">
            <arc:ActionSwap.States>
                <arc:ActionSwapState Id="save" Label="Save" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Bookmark}" />
                <arc:ActionSwapState Id="saved" Label="Saved" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Check}" Tone="Quiet" />
            </arc:ActionSwap.States>
        </arc:ActionSwap>
        <arc:ActionSwap Size="Medium">
            <arc:ActionSwap.States>
                <arc:ActionSwapState Id="save" Label="Save" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Bookmark}" />
                <arc:ActionSwapState Id="saved" Label="Saved" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Check}" Tone="Quiet" />
            </arc:ActionSwap.States>
        </arc:ActionSwap>
        <arc:ActionSwap Size="Large">
            <arc:ActionSwap.States>
                <arc:ActionSwapState Id="save" Label="Save" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Bookmark}" />
                <arc:ActionSwapState Id="saved" Label="Saved" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Check}" Tone="Quiet" />
            </arc:ActionSwap.States>
        </arc:ActionSwap>
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

### Disabled

Set `IsEnabled` to `False` to dim the control to 60 percent and remove it from the tab order.

```xml

             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ActionSwapDisabledDemo">
    <arc:ActionSwap IsEnabled="False" HorizontalAlignment="Center">
        <arc:ActionSwap.States>
            <arc:ActionSwapState Id="send" Label="Send invite" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Send}" />
            <arc:ActionSwapState Id="sent" Label="Sent" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Check}" Tone="Success" />
        </arc:ActionSwap.States>
    </arc:ActionSwap>
</UserControl>
```

### Content guidelines

- **Labels**: a verb and its object in sentence case, short: "Send invite", "Follow". The label is both what is shown
  and the accessible name.
- **Pending labels**: the present participle with no ellipsis: "Sending". The spinner already signals progress.
- **Result labels**: the past tense in one or two words: "Sent", "Added".
- **Count**: two or three states. More than that is a menu or a segmented control.

## API reference

### ActionSwap

A compact action that morphs through a small set of related states (idle, working, done, and back) and keeps its place and intent. Pressing it moves to the next state, wrapping around. Width, padding, tone and icon move together on springs (P5); only the changed letters of the label rise in out of a soft blur while the rest glide (P4); icons trade places through a blur and a success tick wipes in (P15). An action that returns a task shows a working phase (`PendingLabel`, or a round spinner without one) for at least 450ms; a fault shows `FailureLabel` for 1.8s. Every change can be interrupted mid-flight. Pending keeps keyboard focus: activation is swallowed instead of disabling the button.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `States` | `AvaloniaList<ActionSwapState>` | – | *Read-only.* The states, in order; at least two are needed. A press moves to the next one and wraps around. In XAML, add `ActionSwapState` children. |
| `Value` | `string?` | `null` | The id of the shown state (two-way); null shows the first state. A press sets it when the next state commits. |
| `AsyncAction` | `Func<ActionSwapState, ActionSwapState, Task?>?` | `null` | Runs on press with the next and the current state, before the control moves on. Return a task to show the working phase, null to move on at once; a faulted task, or an exception, shows `FailureLabel` and stays on the current state. |
| `FailureLabel` | `string` | `"Try again"` | Shown for 1.8s after a failed action (default "Try again"). |
| `Size` | `ControlSize` | `Medium` | Height: Small (36), Medium (44, default) or Large (50). |
| `Phase` | `ActionSwapPhase` | – | *Read-only.* Where the control is in a press: Idle, Working while the action runs, or Failed. Read-only. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ValueChanged` | `ActionSwapValueChangedEventArgs` | Raised when a new state commits, by a press, by its hold running out, or after its action succeeds. |

Pseudo-classes: `:neutral`, `:accent`, `:success`, `:warning`, `:quiet`, `:danger`, `:working`, `:folded`, `:failed`, `:inactive`, `:wide`

Derives from `Button`: every member of `Button` works as well.

### ActionSwapState

One face of an `ActionSwap`.

### ActionSwapValueChangedEventArgs

Arguments of `ValueChanged`.

Derives from `RoutedEventArgs`: every member of `RoutedEventArgs` works as well.

| `ActionSwapTone` value | Look |
|---|---|
| `Neutral` | Foreground fill with background text (default). |
| `Accent` | Accent fill with accent foreground text. |
| `Success` | A success-tinted surface, a success-colored icon. |
| `Warning` | A warning-tinted surface, a warning-colored icon. |
| `Quiet` | A bordered surface with the default text color. |

| `ActionSwapPhase` value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `Idle` | Showing the current state. A press runs the action. |
| `Working` | `AsyncAction` is running. Presses are ignored. |
| `Failed` | The action failed. `FailureLabel` shows for 1.8 seconds. |

## Accessibility

- The control is a native button: the accessible name is the visible label of the face being shown, so the animated
  letters are not read one by one.
- While working it reports itself as unavailable but keeps keyboard focus; a hidden polite status region announces new
  labels, pending labels and failures.
- With fewer than two states the control is inert.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Enter` / `Space` | Runs the action and moves to the next state. Ignored while working. |
| `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` | Moves to the next or previous control. A working pill keeps its focus stop. |

## Motion

- Only the changed letters of a label rise in out of a soft 4 px blur while the kept ones glide to their new places;
  leaving letters lift away a little faster. The width follows on a spring.
- Icons trade places through a blur: the old one shrinks away while the new one grows out of it. A success icon settles
  with a little more give while its stroke wipes in from the leading edge.
- Tone, padding and width move on one spring and every change can be interrupted mid-flight.
- A press scales the pill to 97 percent (98.5 percent when it is wider than 220 px) and springs back. Hover styles apply
  to mouse and pen only; on touch the press scale is the only feedback.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| New label or icon | Letters rise from a blur, icons grow, width springs | A 120 ms crossfade, no width or fold animation | Immediate |
| Working without a label | The pill folds into a circle around a spinner | Immediate fold, a still ring | Immediate |
| Press | Scales to 97 percent on a snappy spring | No scale | No scale |

## Related

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `ActionButton` | One save or publish ends in a success tick and a reset timer |
| `Button` | The label never changes state |
| `ThemeSwitcher` | The action switches between light and dark |
| `ConfirmMorph` | A destructive action should ask a question in place |
