# Split button

> A primary action with a menu of nearby alternatives.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/split-button

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.SplitButtonMergeStrategiesDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12">
        <arc:SplitButton Label="Merge pull request"
                         Icon="M18 15a3 3 0 1 0 0 6 3 3 0 0 0 0-6z M6 3a3 3 0 1 0 0 6 3 3 0 0 0 0-6z M6 21V9a9 9 0 0 0 9 9"
                         HorizontalAlignment="Center"
                         Click="OnMergeClick"
                         ItemClicked="OnItemClicked">
            <arc:MenuEntry Header="Squash and merge" />
            <arc:MenuEntry Header="Rebase and merge" />
            <arc:MenuEntry Header="Close pull request"
                           Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.CircleX}"
                           IsDestructive="True"
                           HasSeparatorBefore="True" />
        </arc:SplitButton>
        <TextBlock x:Name="Log"
                   Text="Run the main action, or open the chevron for the alternatives."
                   FontSize="13"
                   TextWrapping="Wrap"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class SplitButtonMergeStrategiesDemo : UserControl
{
    public SplitButtonMergeStrategiesDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
    }

    private void OnMergeClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        Log.Text = "Merged with a merge commit.";
    }

    private void OnItemClicked(object? sender, MenuEntryClickedEventArgs e)
    {
        Log.Text = $"Menu: {e.Header}";
    }
}
```

## When to use

`SplitButton` joins one default action to a chevron that opens the nearby alternatives. It answers two questions in
one control: what usually happens here, and what else can happen. The common path is one click, and the alternatives
are one more click away, so the control fits a toolbar, a page header or a footer where one action dominates.

- **Merge pull request in a code review screen**: Merge with a merge commit is the default. Squash and merge and
  Rebase and merge sit in the menu, with Close pull request as a destructive row after a separator.
- **Export on a revenue report**: Export as CSV is the format most finance teams use, so it is the default. JSON and
  PDF are one click away, and the report keeps its filters either way.
- **Send on an invoice editor**: Send invoice is the default action. Send reminder, Save as draft and Void invoice
  are the alternatives, and the menu separates the destructive action from the rest.
- **Copy with a result in place**: Copy page answers Copied on the same button for a moment, so the confirmation sits
  where the person's eyes already are and no toast is needed.
- **Deploy in a CI console**: Deploy to production is the default for a release branch. Deploy to staging is in the
  menu for the cases where a release needs a rehearsal.

## When not to use

- **Equal options with no default action**, such as Share by email, Slack or link: use `DropdownMenu`, which has a
  trigger and no primary half.
- **A single action with nothing to choose from**, such as Save changes on a settings form: use `Button`.
- **Actions on one row or card object**, such as Rename, Archive and Delete on an order: use `ContextMenu` for the
  pointer and keyboard context menu of the object.
- **Several related actions with no default**, shown side by side: use `ButtonGroup`.
- **A choice that stays selected**, such as a period or a view: use `SegmentedControl` or `Select`. A split button
  runs its action; it does not hold a value.

## Usage

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:SplitButton Label="Merge pull request">
        <arc:MenuEntry Header="Squash and merge" />
        <arc:MenuEntry Header="Rebase and merge" />
        <arc:MenuEntry Header="Close pull request" IsDestructive="True" HasSeparatorBefore="True" />
    </arc:SplitButton>
</UserControl>
```

`SplitButton` derives from Avalonia's `TemplatedControl`. Its two halves are real buttons, so each one takes focus,
shows the focus ring and responds to the keyboard on its own. The menu is the same `MenuSurface` that `DropdownMenu`
uses, so its rows, highlight and keyboard movement match the rest of the library. The rows are `MenuEntry` items,
declared inline in `Items` or supplied through `ItemsSource`.

### Anatomy

1. **Main half**: the default action. It shows the `Label` and, when set, the `Icon` in front
   of it. Its inner padding is 16 px on each side (12 px when `Secondary`), and its minimum height is the medium
   control height.
2. **Icon** (`Icon`): a 16 px Lucide glyph with a 1.75 stroke, followed by the label after an 8 px gap. A new icon
   grows in while the old one shrinks away.
3. **Divider**: a 1 px line between the halves, a faint tint of the text color on the primary variant.
4. **Chevron half**: 38 px wide (32 px when `Secondary`). Its 16 px chevron turns while the
   menu is open. It never scales when pressed.
5. **Menu** (`Menu`): a dropdown anchored to the chevron, aligned to its end and opened 4 px below it. Its rows are
   `MenuEntry` items. A row with `HasSeparatorBefore` starts a new group, and `IsDestructive` colors it as a danger
   action.
6. **Focus ring**: a 2 px ring offset 2 px from each half, shaped to match that half's corners.

The primary variant is a filled pill with the foreground color as its fill. The `Secondary` variant is an outlined
pill: 36 px tall, 12 px text, a main half at least 142 px wide, on the surface color.

### Choosing the variant and the default action

Put the most common action in the main half. Order the menu rows from the most to the least frequent, so the list
reads as a ranking. Put a destructive row last and separate it with `HasSeparatorBefore`, so a misclick on the
chevron does not reach it.

Use `Primary` in a page header, a dialog footer or a card where the action is the goal of the screen. Use `Secondary`
in a dense toolbar or a table header, where a filled button would compete with the content. Do not mix the two
variants in one toolbar: the outlined pill and the filled pill read as different levels of importance.

### Click and menu selection

The main half raises `Click` and runs `Command`. `Click` is raised before the command runs, so a handler can prepare
state the command reads. The chevron half opens the menu, and a row raises `ItemClicked` with the row that was
chosen. The menu closes when a row is chosen.

```xml
<arc:SplitButton Label="Export as CSV"
                 Variant="Secondary"
                 Command="{Binding ExportCommand}">
    <arc:MenuEntry Header="Export as JSON" />
    <arc:MenuEntry Header="Export as PDF" />
</arc:SplitButton>
```

```csharp
merge.Click += (_, _) => log.Text = "Merged with a merge commit.";
merge.ItemClicked += (_, e) => log.Text = $"Menu: {e.Header}";
```

### Rows from data

Use `ItemsSource` for rows that come from a view model, and `ItemTemplate` to draw each row. `MenuEntry` instances
are used as they are. Other items are shown as row headers, so give each row a `MenuEntry` or a template when it needs
its own look. `ItemClicked` returns the data item in `e.Item`, which keeps the handler free of string matching.

```xml
<arc:SplitButton Label="Share" ItemsSource="{Binding ShareTargets}" />
```

### Icon and result in place

`Icon` takes a 24 by 24 Lucide geometry and is set in code. Changing `Label` and `Icon` morphs the main half to the
new text, so a result can be shown on the button itself: "Copy page" becomes "Copied", and the check icon replaces the
copy icon. The shared letters stay in place and only the changed letters move, so the eye does not lose the button.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.SplitButtonResultInPlaceDemo">
    <arc:SplitButton x:Name="Copy"
                     Label="Copy page"
                     Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Copy}"
                     HorizontalAlignment="Center"
                     Click="OnCopyClick">
        <arc:MenuEntry Header="Copy as Markdown" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.FileText}" />
        <arc:MenuEntry Header="Copy link" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Link}" />
        <arc:MenuEntry Header="View as plain text" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Eye}" />
    </arc:SplitButton>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class SplitButtonResultInPlaceDemo : UserControl
{
    private int _copies;

    public SplitButtonResultInPlaceDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
    }

    // Copy page answers Copied in place: the shared "Cop" stays put while the rest of the label morphs.
    private async void OnCopyClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        var current = ++_copies;
        Copy.Label = "Copied";
        Copy.Icon = ArcIcons.Check;
        await Task.Delay(1600);
        if (current == _copies)
        {
            Copy.Label = "Copy page";
            Copy.Icon = ArcIcons.Copy;
        }
    }
}
```

Keep a result label to one word, and restore the original label after a short pause. Use the same pattern for a
confirmation such as "Sent" or "Saved", and do not use it for a process that takes a while: then show progress
instead of a label.

### Disabled

Set `IsEnabled` to `False` to disable both halves. A disabled split button also keeps its menu closed, so no
alternative can be chosen while the default action is unavailable. The control fades to about 52% opacity, which
keeps it visible in the layout.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.SplitButtonDisabledDemo">
    <WrapPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center" ItemSpacing="12" LineSpacing="12">
        <arc:SplitButton Label="Deploy" IsEnabled="False">
            <arc:MenuEntry Header="Deploy to staging" />
        </arc:SplitButton>
        <arc:SplitButton Label="Publish" Variant="Secondary" IsEnabled="False">
            <arc:MenuEntry Header="Publish later" />
        </arc:SplitButton>
    </WrapPanel>
</UserControl>
```

Disable the control only while the action cannot apply, and say why nearby. A Deploy button disabled because the
branch has failing checks is clearer with a line of text that names the failing check.

### Secondary

`Variant="Secondary"` is a compact outlined pill with 12px text and a 142px main half. In this example, picking a format makes it the default.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.SplitButtonSecondaryDemo">
    <arc:SplitButton x:Name="Export"
                     Variant="Secondary"
                     Label="Export as CSV"
                     Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Download}"
                     HorizontalAlignment="Center"
                     ItemClicked="OnItemClicked">
        <arc:MenuEntry Header="Export as JSON" />
        <arc:MenuEntry Header="Export as PDF" />
        <arc:MenuEntry Header="Schedule export…"
                       Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Clock}"
                       HasSeparatorBefore="True" />
    </arc:SplitButton>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class SplitButtonSecondaryDemo : UserControl
{
    public SplitButtonSecondaryDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
    }

    // Picking a format makes it the default.
    private void OnItemClicked(object? sender, MenuEntryClickedEventArgs e)
    {
        Export.Label = e.Header?.ToString() ?? Export.Label;
    }
}
```

The secondary variant suits toolbars and table headers. In this example, a picked alternative becomes the new label.
Keep the choice in the view model when it must survive a restart, and set `Label` from it when the view loads.

### Binding to a view model

An invoice editor exposes its send actions as commands and holds the menu state in the view model. The main action
is a command, the alternatives come from a collection, and the open state is two-way so that the view model can close
the menu after a send.

```csharp
public partial class InvoiceViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    private readonly IInvoiceService _invoices;

    public InvoiceViewModel(IInvoiceService invoices)
    {
        _invoices = invoices;
        AlternativeSends = new ObservableCollection<SendOption>
        {
            new("Send reminder", SendKind.Reminder),
            new("Save as draft", SendKind.Draft),
            new("Void invoice", SendKind.Void)
        };
    }

    [ObservableProperty]
    private bool _isMenuOpen;

    public string InvoiceId { get; } = "inv_2026_0412";

    public ObservableCollection<SendOption> AlternativeSends { get; }

    [RelayCommand]
    private async Task SendInvoiceAsync()
    {
        var result = await _invoices.SendAsync(InvoiceId, SendKind.Invoice);
        IsMenuOpen = false;
    }

    public async Task RunAsync(SendOption option) =>
        await _invoices.SendAsync(InvoiceId, option.Kind);
}

public enum SendKind { Invoice, Reminder, Draft, Void }

public sealed record SendOption(string Label, SendKind Kind);
```

```xml
<arc:SplitButton Label="Send invoice"
                 Command="{Binding SendInvoiceCommand}"
                 IsOpen="{Binding IsMenuOpen, Mode=TwoWay}"
                 ItemsSource="{Binding AlternativeSends}"
                 MenuButtonLabel="Other ways to send" />
```

```csharp
invoice.ItemClicked += (_, e) => _ = viewModel.RunAsync((SendOption)e.Item!);
```

- `IsOpen` is two-way. The view model can open or close the menu, and the chevron writes the state back when the
  person opens it.
- `Command` runs the default action.
- The alternatives are handled in `ItemClicked`, because a row's data item is the natural argument; the view model
  owns the action and the control owns the menu.

### Example: invoice footer

An invoice editor in a billing console. The footer shows the total on the left and the send actions on the right. Send
invoice is the default, the chevron offers the reminder, the draft and the void, and the void sits below a separator
because it is the only destructive row. The secondary Cancel button is a ghost button, so the split button is the only
filled control in the footer.

![An invoice footer with a Send invoice split button and its alternatives](https://docs.tkcode.si/shots/Docs/Buttons/SplitButton/images/InvoiceFooter.webp)

```xml
<StackPanel Width="620" Spacing="16">
    <Border Padding="24"
            Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Surface}"
            BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Border}"
            BorderThickness="1"
            CornerRadius="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource RadiusPanel}">

            <Grid ColumnDefinitions="*,Auto">
                <StackPanel Spacing="2">
                    <TextBlock Text="Invoice inv_2026_0412"
                               FontSize="16"
                               FontWeight="SemiBold"
                               Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
                    <TextBlock Text="Northwind Traders, due May 14, 2026"
                               FontSize="13"
                               Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
                </StackPanel>
                <TextBlock Grid.Column="1"
                           Text="Draft"
                           VerticalAlignment="Center"
                           Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
            </Grid>
            <Border Height="1" Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Border}" />

                                 Label="Send invoice"

                                 VerticalAlignment="Center">
                    <arc:MenuEntry Header="Send reminder" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Bell}" />
                    <arc:MenuEntry Header="Save as draft" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.FileText}" />
                    <arc:MenuEntry Header="Void invoice"
                                   Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.CircleX}"

            </Grid>
        </StackPanel>
    </Border>

```

### Content guidelines

- **Main label**: a verb and an object, in sentence case: "Merge pull request", "Export as CSV", "Send invoice". It
  names the action the default performs, so the person knows what a click does before reading the menu.
- **Menu rows**: the same grammar as the main label, and the same nouns. A destructive row names its consequence:
  "Void invoice", not "Delete".
- **Chevron name**: the default `{Label} more actions` is correct for most controls. Set `MenuButtonLabel` when the label
  is a generic verb such as "Send" or "Export", so the name says what the menu offers.
- **Result labels**: one word that confirms the action, such as "Copied" or "Sent", in the same tense as the default.

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| Click here to send | Send invoice |
| Export | Export as CSV |
| Delete invoice (in the menu) | Void invoice |
| Copied successfully! | Copied |
| More options (chevron name) | Other ways to send |

### Best practices

**Do**

- Put the action that most people take in the main half. A split button whose default is rarely used teaches people to
  open the menu every time.
- Put a destructive row last, below a separator, so a misclick on the chevron does not reach it.
- Bind `Command` for the default action and keep the menu rows to actions that can run in the same context.
- Keep the label short enough that the main half stays under the width of the toolbar it sits in.

**Avoid**

- Using a split button when every option is equal. Without a default, the primary half implies a choice the person
  has not made; use `DropdownMenu`.
- Disabling the control to hide an action that needs a precondition. Disabled controls teach nothing; say why
  nearby.
- Using several different split buttons in one toolbar. The menus compete, and the person has to read every
  chevron.
- Changing the label for a long process. A result label confirms a finished action; a running process needs
  progress.
- Putting the `Secondary` variant next to `Primary` controls in one row. The two weights read as different levels of
  importance.

### Common questions

**How do I change the accessible name of the chevron?** Set `MenuButtonLabel`. When it is `null` (the default), the
name is `{Label} more actions`.

**What does Enter do on the chevron?** It opens the menu with the first row highlighted. The main action runs only on
the main half.

**Can the code open or close the menu?** Yes. Call `Open()` to open it with focus on the surface, or `Open(true)` to
highlight the first row. `Close()` closes it without returning focus. `IsOpen` is two-way, so binding it is the same
as calling those methods.

**Does Click run before Command?** Yes. `Click` is raised first, then the command runs. Use `Click` for state the
command depends on, and keep the command for the work itself.

**Why does a row not look destructive?** Set `IsDestructive="True"` on the `MenuEntry`. The row takes the danger color,
and `HasSeparatorBefore="True"` adds the separator above it.

## API reference

### SplitButton

One default action joined to a chevron menu of nearby alternatives (Arc split button): Merge pull request with Squash and merge or Rebase and merge, an export with its usual format, Copy page that answers Copied in place. The whole pill presses in for the main action; the chevron half anchors the menu, so it answers in color only and turns while the menu is open. The main label morphs letter by letter (shared runs glide, changed letters rise out of a soft blur), a new `Icon` grows in while the old one shrinks away, and the main half springs to the new width. Menu rows are `MenuEntry` items declared inline or supplied with `ItemsSource`; the menu opens 4px below the chevron, aligned to the end. Keyboard: Enter or Space runs the main action on the main half and opens the menu on the first row from the chevron (ArrowDown too); arrow keys move through the rows and loop, Escape closes the menu and returns focus to the chevron. Label changes are announced politely.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Label` | `string` | `"Merge pull request"` | Main label (Arc: required). A change morphs letter by letter and is announced politely. |
| `Icon` | `Geometry?` | `null` | Leading icon of the main half (a 24×24 Lucide geometry such as `ArcIcons.Copy`); a new icon crossfades in. |
| `Variant` | `SplitButtonVariant` | `Primary` | Visual weight: Primary (default, a filled button) or Secondary (a compact outlined pill). |
| `Command` | `ICommand?` | `null` | Command of the main action. |
| `CommandParameter` | `object?` | `null` | Parameter passed to Command when the main action runs. |
| `IsOpen` | `bool` | `false` | Whether the menu is open (two-way). |
| `MenuButtonLabel` | `string?` | `null` | Accessible name of the chevron half; null uses "{Label} more actions". |
| `ItemsSource` | `IEnumerable?` | `null` | Menu rows from data (`MenuEntry` instances are used as is; other items become row headers). |
| `ItemTemplate` | `IDataTemplate?` | `null` | Template that draws each row taken from ItemsSource. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Click` | `RoutedEventArgs` | Raised when the main half is activated (before `Command` runs). |
| `ItemClicked` | `MenuEntryClickedEventArgs` | Raised when a menu row is activated. |

Pseudo-classes: `:open`, `:primary-pressed`, `:secondary`, `:has-icon`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

### MenuEntry

One row of a `MenuSurface`: a leading icon (a Lucide `Geometry` such as `{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Pencil}`, or any control), a header, an optional shortcut hint and the check or radio indicator of toggle rows. Rows never draw their own hover or focus fill: the surface's shared highlight glides to the row under the pointer and jumps to the keyboard position. Activation runs `Command`, raises `Click` and the surface's `ItemClicked`, then closes the menu unless `StaysOpenOnClick` is set.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Header` | `object?` | `null` | The row label (strings ellipsize; any content is accepted). Also the typeahead text unless `TextSearch.Text` is set. |
| `HeaderTemplate` | `IDataTemplate?` | `null` | Data template that renders the header; without one, a string header is drawn as ellipsizing text. |
| `Icon` | `object?` | `null` | Leading icon: a 24x24 Lucide `Geometry` (drawn as a 16px stroke glyph) or any control. |
| `InputGesture` | `KeyGesture?` | `null` | Shortcut shown as a quiet hint at the row end (display only; bind the key with a hot key yourself). |
| `InputGestureText` | `string?` | `null` | Free-form shortcut hint (for example "⌘ ,"); wins over `InputGesture`. |
| `Command` | `ICommand?` | `null` | Command run when the row is activated; the row is disabled while the command cannot execute. |
| `CommandParameter` | `object?` | `null` | Parameter passed to Command when the row is activated. |
| `IsDestructive` | `bool` | `false` | Danger text and icon, and a danger-tinted highlight. Put destructive rows last and name what they destroy. |
| `ToggleType` | `MenuEntryToggleType` | `None` | How the row toggles when activated: None for a command row, CheckBox, or Radio. |
| `IsChecked` | `bool` | `false` | Checked state (two-way). Rows without an icon show a check (or a dot for radio rows) when checked. |
| `GroupName` | `string?` | `null` | Radio rows with the same group name (within one surface) are mutually exclusive. |
| `HasSeparatorBefore` | `bool` | `false` | Draws a separator line above the row (Arc's `separatorBefore`). |
| `StaysOpenOnClick` | `bool` | `false` | Keeps the menu open after activation (toggles that people flip several times). |
| `Variant` | `MenuSurfaceVariant` | `Dropdown` | Inherited from the owning `MenuSurface`; selects the row geometry. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Click` | `RoutedEventArgs` | Raised when the row is activated (pointer release, Enter or Space), before the menu closes. |

Pseudo-classes: `:highlighted`, `:pressed`, `:checked`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

`SplitButtonVariant` has two values: `Primary` (the filled default) and `Secondary` (the outlined pill). The event
argument of `ItemClicked` is `MenuEntryClickedEventArgs`, which exposes `Entry` (the activated row), `Item` (the data
item behind the row, or the entry itself for inline rows) and `Header` (the row's header).

## Accessibility

- The main half and the chevron are two buttons. The main half is named by `Label`. The chevron is named
  `{Label} more actions`, unless `MenuButtonLabel` sets another name, and reports whether the menu is expanded.
- The menu uses the Menu and MenuItem roles. Arrow keys move through the rows and loop at the ends.
- A change of `Label` is announced politely, so a result such as "Copied" reaches a screen reader without moving focus.
- Set `MenuButtonLabel` when the label alone does not say what the chevron offers. "Send invoice more actions" is
  accurate but long; "Other ways to send" says what the menu contains.
- The focus ring follows each half, so keyboard users see which half will act.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` | Moves between the main half and the chevron, then to the next control. |
| `Enter` / `Space` on the main half | Raises `Click` and runs `Command`. |
| `Enter` / `Space` on the chevron | Opens the menu with its first row highlighted. |
| `ArrowDown` on the chevron | Opens the menu with its first row highlighted. |
| `ArrowDown` / `ArrowUp` in the menu | Moves to the next or previous row. Disabled rows are skipped, and the movement loops at both ends. |
| `Escape` | Closes the menu and returns focus to the chevron. |

## Motion

- The label changes letter by letter: shared letters glide, and changed letters rise out of a soft blur. The icon
  crossfades, and the main half springs to the new width.
- The main half presses in slightly. The chevron never scales, and it turns while the menu is open.
- The menu opens 4px below the chevron and its rows fade in one after another.
- Reduced motion removes the press, the width spring and the menu transform, and keeps a short fade. Off shows the
  menu and the label change at once.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| Label changes | Shared letters glide, changed letters rise out of a soft blur, removed letters lift and fade | Crossfades in 120 ms | Replaces at once |
| Icon changes | The new icon grows in from a smaller size out of a subtle blur; the old one shrinks away | A short fade | Immediate |
| Main half pressed | The whole pill presses in slightly | No press | Immediate |
| Menu opens | Opens 4 px below the chevron, and its rows fade in one after another | A short fade without the transform | Immediate |

## Related

- `DropdownMenu` for a menu of equal options with no default action.
- `Button` for a single action without alternatives.
- `ButtonGroup` for several related actions shown side by side.
- `MenuEntry` is the row type of both the split button and the menus.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `DropdownMenu` | All options are equal and none is the default |
| `Button` | There is one action and nothing to choose |
| `ButtonGroup` | Several related actions sit side by side without a default |
| `FloatingButtonGroup` | Icon actions float over a canvas or a selection |
| `SegmentedControl` | A value stays selected, such as a period or a view |

---

# Button group

> Related actions joined into one surface with hairline dividers: a hover highlight glides between segments, the pressed one answers in place, and an attached menu can close the row.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/button-group

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ButtonGroupDocumentActionsDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12">
        <arc:ButtonGroup Label="Document actions"
                         HorizontalAlignment="Center"
                         ActionInvoked="OnActionInvoked"
                         MenuItemClicked="OnMenuItemClicked">
            <arc:ButtonGroupItem x:Name="Share"
                                 Label="Share"
                                 Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Share2}"
                                 Click="OnShareClick" />
            <arc:ButtonGroupItem Label="Duplicate" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Copy}" />
            <arc:ButtonGroupItem Label="Archive" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Archive}" />
            <arc:ButtonGroup.Menu>
                <arc:MenuSurface>
                    <arc:MenuEntry Header="Pin" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Bookmark}" />
                    <arc:MenuEntry Header="Move to…" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Folder}" />
                    <arc:MenuEntry Header="Delete"
                                   Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Trash2}"
                                   IsDestructive="True"
                                   HasSeparatorBefore="True" />
                </arc:MenuSurface>
            </arc:ButtonGroup.Menu>
        </arc:ButtonGroup>
        <TextBlock x:Name="Log"
                   Text="Point at the group, or Tab into it and use the arrow keys."
                   FontSize="13"
                   TextWrapping="Wrap"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class ButtonGroupDocumentActionsDemo : UserControl
{
    private int _copies;

    public ButtonGroupDocumentActionsDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Share.ReserveLabels = ["Copied"];
    }

    private async void OnShareClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        var current = ++_copies;
        Share.Label = "Copied";
        Share.Icon = ArcIcons.Check;
        await Task.Delay(1600);
        if (current == _copies)
        {
            Share.Label = "Share";
            Share.Icon = ArcIcons.Share2;
        }
    }

    private void OnActionInvoked(object? sender, ButtonGroupActionEventArgs e)
    {
        Log.Text = $"Action: {e.Item.Label}";
    }

    private void OnMenuItemClicked(object? sender, MenuEntryClickedEventArgs e)
    {
        Log.Text = $"Menu: {e.Header}";
    }
}
```

## When to use

`ButtonGroup` joins two to five related actions on one object into a single surface with hairline dividers. Use it where
the actions belong together and act on the same thing: a document header, a zoom control, a formatting toolbar, a message
thread. One highlight glides under the pointer or the keyboard focus, so the person always sees which segment is active,
and an optional chevron segment holds the rarer actions without making the row longer.

- **Document actions in a file viewer**: Share, Duplicate and Archive on the header of a deck or a contract, with a
  chevron menu for Pin, Move to and Delete.
- **Zoom controls in a report or chart viewer**: Zoom out, a live value that shows 100% and resets the zoom, and Zoom in.
  The value sits between the two buttons, so the person reads the level where they change it.
- **Reply actions in a support inbox**: Reply, Reply all and Forward at the foot of a ticket thread. The three related
  actions stay together and read as one decision.
- **Formatting toolbar in an internal wiki or CMS editor**: Bold, Italic and Underline as icon-only segments above a text
  block. Familiar glyphs need no label, and the tooltip names each one.
- **Insert blocks in a vertical side toolbar**: Image, Table and Code block stacked in a column beside the editor, with the
  less common blocks in a menu at the end.

## When not to use

- **Options that stay selected, such as a view mode or a period**: use `SegmentedControl` from Toggles. A segment of a button
  group runs an action once and does not remember that it was chosen.
- **One primary action with a few close alternatives**: use `SplitButton`, which keeps the default action prominent and
  puts the alternatives in its menu.
- **Switching between views or panels**: use `Tabs` from Navigation, which shows which panel is open.
- **A long list of actions**: use `DropdownMenu` from Menus for the list, and keep only the few most used actions in the
  group. A row of ten segments collapses or scrolls and loses its meaning.
- **Floating, separate buttons in a tray**: use `FloatingButtonGroup`, which gives each button its own soft surface.

## Usage

Each segment is a `ButtonGroupItem`. Give the group a `Label`, which is its accessible name.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:ButtonGroup Label="Document actions">
        <arc:ButtonGroupItem Label="Share" />
        <arc:ButtonGroupItem Label="Duplicate" />
        <arc:ButtonGroupItem Label="Archive" />
    </arc:ButtonGroup>
</UserControl>
```

`ButtonGroup` is an `ItemsControl`, so segments can be declared inline or generated from `ItemsSource`. Each
`ButtonGroupItem` derives from Avalonia's `Button`: `Click`, `Command`, `CommandParameter` and `IsEnabled` work on a
segment as they do on a button. The group itself adds the surface, the highlight, the dividers, the chevron menu and
the row layout.

Plain values in `ItemsSource` become segments with their text as the label. This suits a fixed set of choices, such as
export formats:

```xml
<arc:ButtonGroup Label="Export format" ItemsSource="{Binding ExportFormats}" />
```

### Anatomy

1. **Frame**: a 1 px border with the control radius on the surface colour. The group's `Label` names it
   for assistive technology and is not drawn.
2. **Segments**: 42 px high and at least 42 px wide inside the border, with 14 px inline padding. The icon and the label
   are 8 px apart. A `Small` group uses 34 px segments, 12 px padding and a 6 px gap.
3. **Dividers**: 1 px hairlines between neighbouring segments, inset 11 px from the top and bottom (9 px when `Small`). In
   a `Solid` group they are a mix of the page colour into the foreground.
4. **Highlight**: a surface-muted rounded rectangle, 3 px inside its segment with a 14 px corner radius. It glides to the
   pointer or to keyboard focus and deepens while a segment is pressed.
5. **Chevron segment**: 38 px wide and 42 px high, with a 16 px chevron. It appears only when `Menu` is
   set, and it turns over while the menu is open. A `Small` group uses 30 by 34 px.
6. **Status region**: a hidden polite region that announces a changed label. It has no visible text.

### Icons and icon-only segments

Set `Icon` to a 24 by 24 Lucide geometry, such as `ArcIcons.Share2`. The icon draws at 16 px beside the label. `IsIconOnly`
hides the label, which then becomes the tooltip and the accessible name, so an icon-only segment still has a clear name.

```xml
<arc:ButtonGroup Label="Zoom" Size="Small">
    <arc:ButtonGroupItem Label="Zoom out" IsIconOnly="True" />
    <arc:ButtonGroupItem Label="Zoom in" IsIconOnly="True" />
</arc:ButtonGroup>
```

Use icon-only segments for glyphs that everyone recognises, such as bold, zoom in and undo. For an action whose icon is
ambiguous, keep the label visible, so the segment says what it does.

### Live value and label change

`Value` shows content in place of the label, such as a zoom level. Text values use tabular figures, so the digits do not
shift when the value changes. A control value is shown as it is. `Label` stays the accessible name.

A label can also change after a press. List the other labels in `ReserveLabels` so the segment keeps the width of the
widest one and nothing next to it moves.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ButtonGroupLiveValueDemo">
    <arc:ButtonGroup Label="Zoom" Size="Small" HorizontalAlignment="Center">
        <arc:ButtonGroupItem Label="Zoom out"
                             Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.ZoomOut}"
                             IsIconOnly="True"
                             Click="OnZoomOutClick" />
        <arc:ButtonGroupItem x:Name="ZoomValue"
                             Label="Reset zoom"
                             Value="100%"
                             Click="OnZoomResetClick" />
        <arc:ButtonGroupItem Label="Zoom in"
                             Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.ZoomIn}"
                             IsIconOnly="True"
                             Click="OnZoomInClick" />
    </arc:ButtonGroup>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class ButtonGroupLiveValueDemo : UserControl
{
    private int _zoom = 100;

    public ButtonGroupLiveValueDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
    }

    private void OnZoomOutClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        SetZoom(_zoom - 25);
    }

    private void OnZoomInClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        SetZoom(_zoom + 25);
    }

    private void OnZoomResetClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        SetZoom(100);
    }

    private void SetZoom(int value)
    {
        _zoom = Math.Clamp(value, 25, 400);
        ZoomValue.Value = $"{_zoom}%";
    }
}
```

```csharp
var zoomValue = new ButtonGroupItem { Label = "Reset zoom", Value = "100%" };
zoomValue.Click += (_, _) => zoomValue.Value = "100%";

var share = new ButtonGroupItem { Label = "Share", ReserveLabels = ["Copied"] };
share.Click += async (_, _) =>
{
    share.Label = "Copied";
    await Task.Delay(1600);
    share.Label = "Share";
};
```

A changed label is announced once when it changes within one second of the press. The quiet return to the original label
is not announced, so the person hears "Copied" once and does not hear "Share" again.

### Attached menu

`Menu` adds a chevron segment at the end of the row. It takes a `MenuSurface`, and `MenuLabel` names the chevron (default
"More actions"). The menu opens six pixels below the chevron, aligned to the group's end, with a minimum width of 208 px.
`MenuItemClicked` reports the chosen row. Menu rows do not raise `ActionInvoked`, so handle them in `MenuItemClicked`.

```xml
<arc:ButtonGroup Label="Document actions" MenuLabel="More document actions">
    <arc:ButtonGroupItem Label="Share" />
    <arc:ButtonGroupItem Label="Archive" />
    <arc:ButtonGroup.Menu>
        <arc:MenuSurface>
            <arc:MenuEntry Header="Pin" />
            <arc:MenuEntry Header="Delete" IsDestructive="True" HasSeparatorBefore="True" />
        </arc:MenuSurface>
    </arc:ButtonGroup.Menu>
</arc:ButtonGroup>
```

Put the destructive action in the menu, behind the chevron, and separate it with `HasSeparatorBefore`. A row of segments
that delete things invites a slip; the menu adds one step without hiding the action.

### Variants, orientation and events

`Variant` is `Outline` by default: a bordered surface. `Variant="Solid"` uses the primary fill for the main actions of a
screen, and it is best used at most once per screen. `Orientation="Vertical"` stacks the segments in a column; the menu
then aligns to the start edge. `Size` is `Small` (36 px group, 34 px segments) or `Medium` (44 px, the default). `Large` is
treated as `Medium`.

`ActionInvoked` runs after a segment's own click handler and reports the segment in `Item` and the source object in
`Data`. For inline segments `Data` is the segment itself; for `ItemsSource` it is the data object.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ButtonGroupSolidDemo">
    <arc:ButtonGroup Label="Message actions" Variant="Solid" HorizontalAlignment="Center">
        <arc:ButtonGroupItem Label="Reply" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Reply}" />
        <arc:ButtonGroupItem Label="Reply all"
                             Icon="M7 17l-5-5 5-5 M12 17l-5-5 5-5 M22 18v-2a4 4 0 0 0-4-4H7" />
        <arc:ButtonGroupItem Label="Forward"
                             Icon="M15 17l5-5-5-5 M4 18v-2a4 4 0 0 1 4-4h12" />
    </arc:ButtonGroup>
</UserControl>
```

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ButtonGroupVerticalDemo">
    <arc:ButtonGroup Label="Insert"
                     Orientation="Vertical"
                     MenuLabel="More blocks"
                     HorizontalAlignment="Center">
        <arc:ButtonGroupItem Label="Image" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Image}" />
        <arc:ButtonGroupItem Label="Table" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Table}" />
        <arc:ButtonGroupItem Label="Code block" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Code}" />
        <arc:ButtonGroup.Menu>
            <arc:MenuSurface>
                <arc:MenuEntry Header="Divider" />
                <arc:MenuEntry Header="Callout" />
            </arc:MenuSurface>
        </arc:ButtonGroup.Menu>
    </arc:ButtonGroup>
</UserControl>
```

```csharp
document.ActionInvoked += (_, e) => log.Text = $"Action: {e.Item.Label}";
```

### Collapsing labels

When a horizontal row does not fit the width it is given, segments that have an icon drop their label and keep the icon.
The label moves to the tooltip and the accessible name. The labels come back once the width is enough for the full row
again, and the group remembers the width that forced the collapse, so it does not flicker between the two states. Segments
without an icon keep their labels. Vertical groups do not collapse.

If the row still does not fit after collapsing, it scrolls sideways with a hidden scroll bar. Set `IsLabelCollapseEnabled`
to `False` to keep the labels and accept the scroll instead.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ButtonGroupCollapsingLabelsDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12">
        <WrapPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center" ItemSpacing="12" LineSpacing="12">
            <arc:Button Content="Narrow"
                        Variant="Secondary"
                        Size="Small"
                        Click="OnNarrowClick" />
            <arc:Button Content="Wide"
                        Variant="Secondary"
                        Size="Small"
                        Click="OnWideClick" />
        </WrapPanel>
        <Border x:Name="Frame" Width="240" HorizontalAlignment="Left">
            <arc:ButtonGroup Label="Editing">
                <arc:ButtonGroupItem Label="Undo" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Undo2}" />
                <arc:ButtonGroupItem Label="Redo" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Redo2}" />
                <arc:ButtonGroupItem Label="Download" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Download}" />
                <arc:ButtonGroupItem Label="Settings" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Settings}" />
            </arc:ButtonGroup>
        </Border>
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

{
    public ButtonGroupCollapsingLabelsDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
    }

    private void OnNarrowClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        Frame.Width = 240;
    }

    private void OnWideClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        Frame.Width = 520;
    }
}
```

### Disabled

A segment with `IsDisabled="True"` stays focusable and reports itself as unavailable, so a keyboard user can find it and
hear that it is not available. Activation is swallowed and its content dims to 40 percent. Hovering over a disabled
segment shows no highlight. Set `IsEnabled` to `False` on the group to dim it as a whole and remove all its stops.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ButtonGroupDisabledDemo">
    <WrapPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center" ItemSpacing="12" LineSpacing="12">
        <arc:ButtonGroup Label="Publishing">
            <arc:ButtonGroupItem Label="Preview" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Eye}" />
            <arc:ButtonGroupItem Label="Publish" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Upload}" IsDisabled="True" />
            <arc:ButtonGroupItem Label="Schedule" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Clock}" />
        </arc:ButtonGroup>
        <arc:ButtonGroup Label="Formatting" IsEnabled="False">
            <arc:ButtonGroupItem Label="Bold" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Bold}" IsIconOnly="True" />
            <arc:ButtonGroupItem Label="Italic" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Italic}" IsIconOnly="True" />
            <arc:ButtonGroupItem Label="Underline" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Underline}" IsIconOnly="True" />
        </arc:ButtonGroup>
    </WrapPanel>
</UserControl>
```

### Binding to a view model

A button group has commands and sometimes an item list, so the view model owns the work and the group shows it. The
example below uses CommunityToolkit.Mvvm and an app service that performs the document actions.

```csharp
public interface IDocumentService
{
    Task OpenShareDialogAsync(string documentId);
    Task DuplicateAsync(string documentId);
    Task ArchiveAsync(string documentId);
}

public partial class DocumentViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    private readonly IDocumentService _documents;

    public DocumentViewModel(IDocumentService documents)
    {
        _documents = documents;
    }

    [ObservableProperty]
    private bool _isArchived;

    [RelayCommand]
    private Task ShareAsync() => _documents.OpenShareDialogAsync("doc_2026_0931");

    [RelayCommand]
    private Task DuplicateAsync() => _documents.DuplicateAsync("doc_2026_0931");

    [RelayCommand]
    private Task ArchiveAsync() => _documents.ArchiveAsync("doc_2026_0931");
}
```

```xml
<arc:ButtonGroup Label="Document actions" MenuLabel="More document actions">
    <arc:ButtonGroupItem Label="Share"
                         Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Share2}"
                         Command="{Binding ShareCommand}" />
    <arc:ButtonGroupItem Label="Duplicate"
                         Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Copy}"
                         Command="{Binding DuplicateCommand}" />
    <arc:ButtonGroupItem Label="Archive"
                         Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Archive}"
                         Command="{Binding ArchiveCommand}"
                         IsDisabled="{Binding IsArchived}" />
</arc:ButtonGroup>
```

Every binding is one way. `Label`, `Icon`, `Command` and `IsDisabled` come from the view model, and the group writes
nothing back, because a button group has no selection to report. Bind `ItemsSource` one way too. `ActionInvoked` and
`MenuItemClicked` are the places to run code that belongs to the view, such as logging or closing a flyout. Compiled
bindings need `x:DataType` on the view; the examples leave it out for brevity.

### Example: document header in a file viewer

The header of a board deck in a document viewer. The title and the last edit line identify the document, and the group
on the right holds the three actions the owner uses most: Share, Duplicate and Archive. Pin and Delete live in the
chevron menu, so the header stays short and the destructive action is one step away from the common ones. Share has an
icon and a label because it is the most used action on the page, and the group is centred against the title block, so
the actions read as actions on this document rather than on the page.

![A document header with a title and a three-segment document actions group with a chevron menu](https://docs.tkcode.si/shots/Docs/Buttons/ButtonGroup/images/DocumentHeader.webp)

```xml
<Grid Width="680" ColumnDefinitions="*,Auto">
    <StackPanel Spacing="4" VerticalAlignment="Center">
        <TextBlock Text="Q2 board deck"
                   FontSize="20"
                   FontWeight="SemiBold"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
        <TextBlock Text="Edited by Priya Nair, 12 minutes ago"
                   FontSize="13"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
    </StackPanel>
    <arc:ButtonGroup Grid.Column="1" Label="Document actions" MenuLabel="More document actions">
        <arc:ButtonGroupItem Label="Share" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Share2}" />
        <arc:ButtonGroupItem Label="Duplicate" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Copy}" />
        <arc:ButtonGroupItem Label="Archive" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Archive}" />
        <arc:ButtonGroup.Menu>
            <arc:MenuSurface>
                <arc:MenuEntry Header="Pin" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Bookmark}" />
                <arc:MenuEntry Header="Delete"
                               Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Trash2}"
                               IsDestructive="True"
                               HasSeparatorBefore="True" />

    </arc:ButtonGroup>
</Grid>
```
