### Content guidelines

- **Segment label**: a short verb or noun for the action: "Share", "Duplicate", "Zoom in". Two words at most, in sentence
  case.
- **Group label**: a noun phrase that names the object or the set, such as "Document actions" or "Zoom". Assistive
  technology reads it first, so it should say what the group acts on.
- **Menu label**: name the scope of the menu: "More document actions", not "More".
- **Result word**: a single word for the confirmation, such as "Copied". It appears for a moment and then returns to the
  original label.
- **Live value**: the value alone, with its unit: "100%", not "Zoom is 100%".

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| Click to share | Share |
| Actions | Document actions |
| More | More document actions |
| Zoom is 100% | 100% |
| Copy link to clipboard | Copy link |

### Best practices

**Do**

- Keep two to five segments in a group. More segments collapse to icons or scroll, and the person can no longer see the
  whole set at once.
- Give every group a `Label`, because it is the accessible name and is not drawn on screen.
- Give every icon-only segment a clear `Label`, because the label becomes its tooltip and its accessible name.
- Use `ReserveLabels` for a segment whose label changes, so the group does not resize when the label does.
- Move rare and destructive actions into the chevron menu, and keep the common actions in the row.

**Avoid**

- Using a button group as a selection control. A pressed segment does not stay selected, so people cannot tell which
  view is active. Use `SegmentedControl` for that.
- Using `Solid` on more than one group per screen. The primary fill is meant for the main actions of a screen, and several
  filled groups compete with each other and with the primary buttons.
- Relying on label collapse for a layout that must show the words. The labels collapse as soon as the row is narrower
  than its full width, so size the container for the labels you need.
- Putting a destructive action in the row beside common ones. A single misdirected press then deletes data.
- Placing a vertical group in a narrow column with long labels. Vertical groups never collapse, so the labels must fit
  the column as they are.

### Common questions

**Why do my labels disappear?** The row is narrower than its full width, so segments that have an icon collapsed to their
icons. Give the container more width, shorten the labels, or set `IsLabelCollapseEnabled` to `False` to keep the labels and
let the row scroll. Segments without an icon never collapse.

**How do I show a result on a segment, such as Copied, without moving the row?** Change `Label` in the click handler and
list the result word in `ReserveLabels`. The segment keeps the width of the widest label, and the change is announced once.

**Does a menu row raise `ActionInvoked`?** No. `ActionInvoked` is raised for segments only. Handle `MenuItemClicked` for
the rows of the chevron menu, and use `MenuEntryClickedEventArgs.Header` to tell them apart.

**Can a segment open a link instead of running code?** Yes. Set `NavigateUri` and the segment opens that address with the
platform launcher. It reports itself as a hyperlink to assistive technology.

**How do I disable one action but keep the others?** Set `IsDisabled` on that segment. The disabled segment stays focusable
and dims, so the person can still find it and learn that it is unavailable. Set `IsEnabled` on the group only when every
action must stop.

## API reference

### ButtonGroup

Two to five related actions joined into one surface with hairline dividers (Arc button group): Share, Duplicate and Archive on a document, zoom controls, Reply / Reply all / Forward. One soft highlight glides between segments under the pointer or keyboard focus (the dividers beside it step aside), the pressed segment answers in place, and an optional chevron segment (`Menu`) opens rarer or destructive actions in a menu aligned to the group's edge. Segments are `ButtonGroupItem`s declared inline or generated from `ItemsSource` (plain data becomes the label). When a horizontal row does not fit, segments with an icon drop their label (it moves to the tooltip and the accessible name); if it still does not fit the row scrolls sideways without a scrollbar. Keyboard: every segment is a Tab stop; the arrow keys along the orientation (mirrored right to left), Home and End move between segments and wrap; Enter or Space activates. On the chevron, Enter, Space or ArrowDown opens the menu on the first row and Escape returns focus. A label that changes right after its segment was pressed (Share to Copied) is announced once.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Label` | `string` | `"Actions"` | Accessible name of the group (Arc: required), such as "Document actions". |
| `Variant` | `ButtonGroupVariant` | `Outline` | Outline (default) for a bordered surface, or Solid for the main action of a screen (use at most once). |
| `Size` | `ControlSize` | `Medium` | Small (36px) or Medium (44px, default). Large is treated as Medium. |
| `Orientation` | `Orientation` | `Horizontal` | Lays the segments out in a row (Horizontal, default) or a column (Vertical). |
| `IsLabelCollapseEnabled` | `bool` | `true` | When a horizontal row does not fit, segments with an icon drop their label (default true). |
| `Menu` | `MenuSurface?` | `null` | Adds a trailing chevron segment that opens this menu, aligned to the group's end (start when vertical). |
| `MenuLabel` | `string` | `"More actions"` | Accessible name and tooltip of the chevron segment. |
| `AreLabelsCollapsed` | `bool` | – | *Read-only.* True while segments show only their icons because the row did not fit. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ActionInvoked` | `ButtonGroupActionEventArgs` | Raised after a segment's own click handlers and command. |
| `MenuItemClicked` | `MenuEntryClickedEventArgs` | Raised when a row of the chevron menu is activated. |

Pseudo-classes: `:vertical`, `:small`, `:solid`, `:compact`, `:pressing`, `:menu-open`, `:has-menu`

Derives from `ItemsControl`: every member of `ItemsControl` works as well.

Companion type used on this page:

| `ButtonGroupItem` property | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `Label` | The visible text and the accessible name. Becomes the tooltip when the segment is icon-only or collapsed. |
| `Icon` | A 24 by 24 Lucide geometry, drawn at 16 px. |
| `IsIconOnly` | Hides the label; the label becomes the name and the tooltip. |
| `Value` | Visible content in place of the label, such as a zoom level. |
| `ReserveLabels` | Other labels the segment can show; it keeps the width of the widest one. |
| `NavigateUri` | Opens the address with the platform launcher, and reports the segment as a hyperlink. |
| `IsDisabled` | Unavailable but focusable: activation is swallowed and the content dims. |

## Accessibility

- The group has the Group role and is named by `Label`.
- Every segment is a Tab stop, including a disabled one. Arrow keys move between segments along the orientation and wrap
  around. Home and End move to the first and last segment.
- Enter or Space activates a segment. On the menu segment, Enter, Space or ArrowDown opens the menu.
- Icon-only and collapsed segments use their label as the name and tooltip, and their icons are hidden.
- A label that changes shortly after a press is announced once. The state is never shown by colour alone.
- A disabled segment reports itself as unavailable, so the person hears that it exists and cannot be used.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` | Moves focus into the group and out of it. Every segment and the chevron is a stop. |
| `Right` / `Left` (`Down` / `Up` in a vertical group) | Moves to the next or previous segment and wraps at the ends. Mirrored in right-to-left layouts. |
| `Home` / `End` | Moves to the first or the last segment. |
| `Enter` / `Space` | Activates the focused segment. On the chevron, opens the menu. |
| `ArrowDown` on the chevron | Opens the menu and highlights its first row. |
| `Up` / `Down` in the menu | Moves between rows, wrapping at the ends and skipping disabled rows. |
| `Escape` in the menu | Closes the menu and returns focus to the chevron. |

## Motion

- One highlight glides to the pointer or the keyboard focus. The dividers beside it fade out as it passes.
- A pressed segment dips its content slightly and springs back. The group frame and its neighbours do not move.
- A segment whose label changes resizes on a spring, or crossfades when its width is reserved.
- The menu grows out of the group's edge and the chevron turns while it is open.
- Reduced motion jumps the highlight to its target, removes the press dip and the chevron turn, and crossfades the labels
  and the menu. Off moves everything to its final state at once.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| Highlight moves to the pointer or focus | Glides on a snappy spring; fades in where it appears from outside the group | Jumps to the target | Immediate |
| Segment pressed | Content dips to 97 percent (90 for icon-only) and springs back; the highlight deepens at once | No dip; the highlight deepens | No dip |
| Label changes on a reserved segment | Crossfades in a fixed box | Crossfade | Immediate |
| Label changes on an unreserved segment | The segment width springs to the new label | Crossfade | Immediate |
| Menu opens | Grows from the group's edge with a short shift; the chevron turns | Crossfades; the chevron does not turn | Immediate |

## Related

- `SegmentedControl` for a choice that stays selected.
- `SplitButton` for one default action with a menu of alternatives.
- `FloatingButtonGroup` for separate soft buttons in a tray.
- `ExpandingButtonGroup` for compact icon buttons whose labels appear on focus.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `SegmentedControl` | The choice stays selected, such as a view mode |
| `SplitButton` | One default action is more important than its nearby alternatives |
| `Button` | A single action stands alone on the surface |
| `Tabs` | The segments switch between panels of content |
| `FloatingButtonGroup` | The actions are separate floating buttons rather than one joined surface |
| `ExpandingButtonGroup` | Compact icon buttons should reveal their labels on focus |
| `DropdownMenu` | The actions form a long list that does not fit in a row |

---

# Floating button group

> Separate soft buttons in a quiet tray, with one shared highlight that morphs from button to button as you move, and a pressed state that settles in place.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/floating-button-group

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.FloatingButtonGroupMutedTrayDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12">
        <arc:FloatingButtonGroup Label="Board actions"
                                 HorizontalAlignment="Center"
                                 ActionInvoked="OnActionInvoked">
            <arc:FloatingButtonGroupItem Label="Undo"
                                         Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Undo2}"
                                         IsIconOnly="True"
                                         Shortcut="⌘Z" />
            <arc:FloatingButtonGroupItem Label="Redo"
                                         Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Redo2}"
                                         IsIconOnly="True"
                                         Shortcut="⇧⌘Z" />
            <arc:FloatingButtonGroupSeparator />
            <arc:FloatingButtonGroupItem x:Name="Share"
                                         Label="Share"
                                         Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Share2}"
                                         Click="OnShareClick" />
            <arc:FloatingButtonGroupItem x:Name="Present"
                                         Label="Present"
                                         Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Monitor}"
                                         IsChecked="False"
                                         Click="OnPresentClick" />
        </arc:FloatingButtonGroup>
        <TextBlock x:Name="Log"
                   Text="Point at the tray, or Tab into it and use the arrow keys."
                   FontSize="13"
                   TextWrapping="Wrap"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class FloatingButtonGroupMutedTrayDemo : UserControl
{
    public FloatingButtonGroupMutedTrayDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Share.ReserveLabels = ["Copied"];
    }

    private async void OnShareClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        Share.Label = "Copied";
        await Task.Delay(1600);
        Share.Label = "Share";
    }

    private void OnPresentClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        Present.IsChecked = Present.IsChecked != true;
    }

    private void OnActionInvoked(object? sender, FloatingButtonGroupActionEventArgs e)
    {
        Log.Text = $"Action: {e.Item.Label}";
    }
}
```

## When to use

`FloatingButtonGroup` puts the actions for a surface that floats over other content in one small tray: a canvas, a
document, a chart or a map. It keeps those actions close to the content they act on, so the page header stays free
for navigation and the surface stays the focus of the screen.

- **Canvas actions in a whiteboard or design tool**: Undo, Redo, Share and Present float over the board. Icon-only
  buttons with shortcut hints keep the tray narrow, and the tooltips carry the names.
- **A selection toolbar over a document**: Bold, Italic and Link appear over the text a person selected in an incident
  postmortem or a help-center article. The tray reads as a layer above the text.
- **A vertical tool rail beside a diagram or map**: Select, Pen and Eraser stack in a column at the edge of the
  canvas. The tooltips open to the right, away from the drawing.
- **A zoom control on an analytics chart**: `ItemsSource` turns a list of zoom levels (Fit, 50%, 100%) into buttons, so
  the list lives in the view model and the tray only shows it.
- **A mode that stays on while a view is open**: Present in a dashboard editor, or Focus in a long document, toggles
  with `IsChecked` and keeps a quiet tint while it is on.

## When not to use

- **A choice that stays selected, such as a text alignment or a view mode**: use `SegmentedControl`, which shows one
  chosen segment as the answer to a question. A single on or off mode can use `IsChecked` on an item.
- **Too many actions for one row**: use `DropdownMenu` for the overflow, or move the rare actions into the menu of
  the surface. A tray that wraps or scrolls is hard to scan.
- **Related actions joined in a page header or a form footer**: use `ButtonGroup`, which joins the buttons into one
  bordered surface with dividers.
- **Compact icon actions on a card or a message, where labels should appear on focus**: use `ExpandingButtonGroup`.
- **A single action**: use `Button`. A tray with one button only adds a surface around it.

## Usage

Each button is a `FloatingButtonGroupItem`. Give the tray a `Label`, which becomes its accessible name, such as
"Board actions" or "Text formatting".

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:FloatingButtonGroup Label="Board actions">
        <arc:FloatingButtonGroupItem Label="Undo" Shortcut="⌘Z" IsIconOnly="True" />
        <arc:FloatingButtonGroupItem Label="Redo" Shortcut="⇧⌘Z" IsIconOnly="True" />
        <arc:FloatingButtonGroupSeparator />
        <arc:FloatingButtonGroupItem Label="Share" />
    </arc:FloatingButtonGroup>
</UserControl>
```

`FloatingButtonGroup` derives from Avalonia's `ItemsControl`, so `Items`, `ItemsSource`, `ItemsPanel` and the
selection-free item model work as they do for any items control. Each `FloatingButtonGroupItem` derives from
Avalonia's `Button`: `Click`, `Command`, `CommandParameter`, `IsEnabled` and the keyboard activation all behave as they
do on a button. The tray adds the highlight, the keyboard model, the layout (row or column), the sizes and the surface
variants. `FloatingButtonGroupSeparator` is a thin rule between two groups of buttons.

### Anatomy

1. **Tray** (`FloatingButtonGroup`): a rounded surface with a 1 px edge. Its corner radius is 18 px, and its padding
   is 4 px on each side. `Size="Small"` shrinks both to 15 px and 3 px.
2. **Highlight**: one rounded shape behind the buttons, drawn in the highlight color (the foreground at 7%, 9% in dark
   mode). It is the only element that moves between buttons. Its corner radius is 13 px, or 11 px when small.
3. **Item** (`FloatingButtonGroupItem`): a button 36 px high (30 px when small) with a 12 px inset on each side (10 px
   when small). An icon-only item is a square of the same height. Its corner radius is 13 px, or 11 px when small.
4. **Icon** (`Icon`): a 16 px Lucide glyph with a 1.75 px stroke, drawn 6 px before the label.
5. **Label** (`Label`): the text of the item, in the tray's secondary text color with medium weight. It is hidden when
   `IsIconOnly` is true.
6. **Separator** (`FloatingButtonGroupSeparator`): a 1 px rule, 18 px long (15 px when small), with 2 px of space on
   each side. In a column it is a horizontal rule of the same length. Its color is the foreground at 12%, set by
   `RuleBrush` in the theme.
7. **Shortcut hint** (`Shortcut`): not drawn on the button. It appears in the item's tooltip, after the label.

The surface comes in two variants. `Muted` (the default) is a translucent tint of the foreground color, at 4.5% in
light mode and 6% in dark mode, with a 3% edge. It reads on a muted background without a shadow. `Floating` uses the
raised surface color, the standard border color and the floating shadow, so it lifts above the content it covers.

### Variant and size

Choose the variant by the layer the tray sits on. A tray beside the content uses `Muted`. A tray over content, such
as a selection toolbar, can use `Floating` to show that it is a separate layer.

```xml
<arc:FloatingButtonGroup Label="Selection actions" Variant="Floating">
    <arc:FloatingButtonGroupItem Label="Comment" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.MessageSquare}" />
</arc:FloatingButtonGroup>
```

`Size` takes `Medium` (the default, 36 px buttons) or `Small` (30 px buttons); `Large` is treated as `Medium`. Use
`Small` in dense areas such as a table toolbar or a chart corner, and `Medium` for a canvas, where the buttons are the
main tool and need the larger hit area.

### Icons and icon-only items

Set `Icon` to a 24 by 24 Lucide geometry in code or with `{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Name}` in XAML. The icon is drawn
at 16 px. `IsIconOnly` on an item hides its label, and setting `IsIconOnly` on the tray makes every item icon only.
An item's own setting wins over the tray's, so a single text button can stay in an icon-only tray. Set
`IsIconOnly` on the tray only when every action has an icon that people already know, such as Bold, Undo or Link.

Icon-only items and items with a `Shortcut` show their label in a tooltip. An icon-only item still needs a `Label`,
because it is the accessible name. `IsIconOnly` has no effect on an item that has no
`Icon`: such an item keeps its text.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.FloatingButtonGroupIconOnlyDemo">
    <arc:FloatingButtonGroup Label="Text formatting"
                             Variant="Floating"
                             IsIconOnly="True"
                             HorizontalAlignment="Center">
        <arc:FloatingButtonGroupItem Label="Bold" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Bold}" Shortcut="⌘B" />
        <arc:FloatingButtonGroupItem Label="Italic" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Italic}" Shortcut="⌘I" />
        <arc:FloatingButtonGroupItem Label="Underline" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Underline}" Shortcut="⌘U" />
        <arc:FloatingButtonGroupItem Label="Strikethrough" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Strikethrough}" />
        <arc:FloatingButtonGroupSeparator />
        <arc:FloatingButtonGroupItem Label="Link" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Link}" Shortcut="⌘K" />
        <arc:FloatingButtonGroupItem Label="Quote" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Quote}" IsEnabled="False" />
    </arc:FloatingButtonGroup>
</UserControl>
```

```csharp
bold.Icon = ArcIcons.Bold;
link.Icon = ArcIcons.Link;
```

### Label change and reserved width

A label can change to confirm an action, for example from "Share" to "Copied" after the link is on the clipboard. Set
`ReserveLabels` to every other label the item can show. The button then keeps the width of the widest label, so the
buttons next to it do not move when the text changes. Without reserved labels, the highlight follows the new width.

```csharp
var share = new FloatingButtonGroupItem { Label = "Share", ReserveLabels = ["Copied"] };
share.Click += async (_, _) =>
{
    share.Label = "Copied";
    await Task.Delay(1600);
    share.Label = "Share";
};
```

Keep confirmation labels to one or two words, and restore the original after a short pause (the demo uses 1.6
seconds).

### Items from data and vertical layout

`ItemsSource` turns plain data into buttons. Each item's label is the text of the object (`ToString()`), unless the
item container has a label already. `Orientation="Vertical"` stacks the buttons in a column, and the tooltips then
open to the right by default. Set `TooltipPlacement` to change the side for every item: `Top`, `Bottom`, `Left` or
`Right`. A row uses `Top` by default.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.FloatingButtonGroupFromItemsSourceDemo">
    <arc:FloatingButtonGroup x:Name="Zoom"
                             Label="Zoom"
                             Size="Small"
                             HorizontalAlignment="Center" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class FloatingButtonGroupFromItemsSourceDemo : UserControl
{
    public FloatingButtonGroupFromItemsSourceDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Zoom.ItemsSource = new[] { "Fit", "50%", "100%", "200%" };
    }
}
```

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.FloatingButtonGroupVerticalDemo">
    <arc:FloatingButtonGroup Label="Tools"
                             Orientation="Vertical"
                             IsIconOnly="True"
                             HorizontalAlignment="Center">
        <arc:FloatingButtonGroupItem Label="Select" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Move}" Shortcut="V" />
        <arc:FloatingButtonGroupItem Label="Pen" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Pencil}" Shortcut="P" />
        <arc:FloatingButtonGroupItem Label="Highlighter" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Highlighter}" />
        <arc:FloatingButtonGroupSeparator />
        <arc:FloatingButtonGroupItem Label="Eraser" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Eraser}" Shortcut="E" />
    </arc:FloatingButtonGroup>
</UserControl>
```

```xml
<arc:FloatingButtonGroup Label="Zoom" Size="Small" ItemsSource="{Binding ZoomLevels}" />

<arc:FloatingButtonGroup Label="Tools" Orientation="Vertical" IsIconOnly="True">
    <arc:FloatingButtonGroupItem Label="Select" Shortcut="V" />
    <arc:FloatingButtonGroupItem Label="Pen" Shortcut="P" />
</arc:FloatingButtonGroup>
```

A vertical tray moves with the Up and Down arrow keys, and the separator turns into a horizontal rule.

### Checked items

`IsChecked` turns an item into a mode that stays on: Present, Focus, Show grid. A checked item keeps a quiet tint
behind the button (the control-on color at 12%, 16% in dark mode), and it reports its state to assistive technology
as On or Off. `IsChecked` set to `null` (the default) makes a plain action with no state.

```xml
<arc:FloatingButtonGroupItem Label="Present"
                             Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Monitor}"
                             IsChecked="{Binding IsPresenting, Mode=TwoWay}" />
```

Do not use `IsChecked` for a choice among several options; use `SegmentedControl` for that.

### Shortcut hints and tooltips

`Shortcut` is a hint, not a binding. The string appears in the tooltip, and `AutomationProperties.HelpText` carries
it for screen readers. The group never handles the key itself. Register the key on the window or the view, and run the
same command the button runs, so the shortcut works when the tray has no focus.

```csharp
KeyBindings.Add(new KeyBinding
{
    Gesture = new KeyGesture(Key.Z, KeyModifiers.Control),
    Command = vm.UndoCommand
});
```

Tooltips open above a row and to the right of a column, unless `TooltipPlacement` says otherwise.

### Events

`ActionInvoked` runs after the item's own `Click` handler and its `Command`. `e.Item` is the button that ran, and
`e.Data` is the source: the button itself for inline items, or the data object for an `ItemsSource`. Handle it to
route every action of a tray in one place; keep per-button behavior in `Click` or `Command`.

```csharp
board.ActionInvoked += (_, e) => log.Text = $"Action: {e.Item.Label}";
```

For an `ItemsSource` tray, read the data object from `e.Data`:

```csharp
zoom.ActionInvoked += (_, e) => viewModel.Zoom = (string)e.Data!;
```

### Binding to a view model

A board editor exposes its actions as commands and keeps the presentation state as properties. The tray binds to them
directly, and the highlight, the pressed state and the keyboard model stay in the control.

```csharp
public partial class BoardViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    private readonly IBoardHistory _history;

    public BoardViewModel(IBoardHistory history)
    {
        _history = history;
        ZoomLevels = new ObservableCollection<string> { "Fit", "50%", "100%", "200%" };
    }

    [ObservableProperty]
    private bool _isPresenting;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private string _zoom = "Fit";

    public ObservableCollection<string> ZoomLevels { get; }

    [RelayCommand(CanExecute = nameof(CanUndo))]
    private void Undo() => _history.Undo();

    [RelayCommand(CanExecute = nameof(CanRedo))]
    private void Redo() => _history.Redo();

    private bool CanUndo => _history.CanUndo;

    private bool CanRedo => _history.CanRedo;
}
```

```xml
<Grid RowDefinitions="Auto,*">
    <arc:FloatingButtonGroup Grid.Row="0" Label="Board actions" HorizontalAlignment="Center">
        <arc:FloatingButtonGroupItem Label="Undo"
                                     Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Undo2}"
                                     IsIconOnly="True"
                                     Shortcut="⌘Z"
                                     Command="{Binding UndoCommand}" />
        <arc:FloatingButtonGroupItem Label="Redo"
                                     Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Redo2}"
                                     IsIconOnly="True"
                                     Shortcut="⇧⌘Z"
                                     Command="{Binding RedoCommand}" />
        <arc:FloatingButtonGroupSeparator />
        <arc:FloatingButtonGroupItem Label="Present"
                                     Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Monitor}"
                                     IsChecked="{Binding IsPresenting, Mode=TwoWay}" />
    </arc:FloatingButtonGroup>
    <arc:FloatingButtonGroup Grid.Row="1" Label="Zoom" Size="Small"
                             HorizontalAlignment="Left"
                             ItemsSource="{Binding ZoomLevels}" />
</Grid>
```

- `IsChecked` is two-way: the item writes its state to `IsPresenting`, and the view model can change it too.
- `Command` drives the action items. When `CanExecute` is false, the item is disabled: it fades to 50% opacity and
  leaves the Tab and arrow-key path.
- The zoom tray is one-way; its choice reaches the view model through `ActionInvoked`, as shown above.

### Example: selection toolbar over a postmortem draft

A tray sits above a paragraph of an incident postmortem. The person selected the sentence about the
certificate rotation, and the tray offers the inline formatting and the comment action. The formatting items are
icon only, because people know Bold, Italic and Link by their icons, and each carries a shortcut hint in its tooltip.
Comment and Quote keep their labels, since their icons are less universal. The tray is left-aligned over the text, so
it reads as attached to the selection.

![A floating selection toolbar with formatting and comment actions above a postmortem paragraph](https://docs.tkcode.si/shots/Docs/Buttons/FloatingButtonGroup/images/SelectionToolbar.webp)

```xml
<StackPanel Width="600" Spacing="14">
    <arc:FloatingButtonGroup Label="Selection actions"
                             HorizontalAlignment="Left"
                             Margin="24,0,0,0">
        <arc:FloatingButtonGroupItem Label="Bold"
                                     Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Bold}"
                                     IsIconOnly="True"
                                     Shortcut="⌘B" />
        <arc:FloatingButtonGroupItem Label="Italic"
                                     Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Italic}"
                                     IsIconOnly="True"
                                     Shortcut="⌘I" />
        <arc:FloatingButtonGroupItem Label="Link"
                                     Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Link}"
                                     IsIconOnly="True"
                                     Shortcut="⌘K" />
        <arc:FloatingButtonGroupSeparator />
        <arc:FloatingButtonGroupItem Label="Comment"
                                     Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.MessageSquare}" />
        <arc:FloatingButtonGroupItem Label="Quote"
                                     Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Quote}" />
    </arc:FloatingButtonGroup>
    <Border Padding="24"
            Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Surface}"
            BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Border}"
            BorderThickness="1"
            CornerRadius="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource RadiusPanel}">
        <StackPanel Spacing="10">
            <TextBlock Text="Postmortem: checkout outage on March 12"
                       FontSize="18"
                       FontWeight="SemiBold"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
            <TextBlock Text="A certificate rotation on the payment gateway stopped card authorizations for 47 minutes. About 1,200 orders were retried after service returned."
                       TextWrapping="Wrap"
                       LineHeight="22"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
            <TextBlock Text="Owner: Priya Raman, Platform team. Follow-up due April 3, 2026."
                       FontSize="13"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
        </StackPanel>
    </Border>
</StackPanel>
```

### Content guidelines

- **Label**: one or two words in sentence case, a verb or a noun the person can act on: "Undo", "Share", "Present".
  The tray's `Label` is a noun for the group, such as "Board actions" or "Zoom".
- **Icon-only labels**: the label is the accessible name, so it must say the full action ("Bold", "Insert link"), not the
  icon's shape.
- **Shortcut hints**: show the key the platform uses, with the symbols as in the examples (⌘Z, ⇧⌘Z). Write the hint
  as the key combination only; the tooltip already carries the action name.
- **Confirmation labels**: a single short word ("Copied") that matches the action. Keep the reserved label short so the
  button width stays small.

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| Click here to undo the last change | Undo |
| share | Share |
| Ctrl + Z | ⌘Z (or the platform's key, as the app runs) |
| Copied to your clipboard! | Copied |

### Best practices

**Do**

- Put the tray where the content it acts on is: over the selection, beside the canvas, or at the top of the board.
  People look for actions near their work.
- Use `Floating` only over content. A tray on the page background looks like a raised panel with nothing to lift it
  from.
- Give every icon-only item a `Label` and a `Shortcut` where one exists. The label gives the accessible name, and the
  shortcut teaches people the keyboard path over time.
- Bind commands to the items so the disabled state comes from the view model. A disabled item stays visible.
- Reserve the labels of confirmations up front, so the neighbouring buttons do not move.

**Avoid**

- Using the tray for a choice that stays selected. A tray of view modes hides which one is current; use
  `SegmentedControl`.
- Putting more than six or seven actions in one tray. Past that, the tray is hard to scan and the overflow belongs in
  a `DropdownMenu`.
- Handling the shortcut only in the tooltip. The group does not bind keys, so a shortcut that is shown but not
  registered teaches people a key that does nothing.
- Mixing icon-only and labelled items in one row without a reason. Mixed widths make the row uneven; set `IsIconOnly`
  on the tray for a consistent row, and use item-level settings only for the exceptions.

### Common questions

**Why does my icon-only item show its label as text?** `IsIconOnly` takes effect only when the item has an `Icon`. An
item without an icon always shows its label, so add the icon or remove `IsIconOnly`.

**Why does the highlight stay on a button after I move the pointer out?** While the pointer is in the tray it owns the
highlight. When the pointer leaves, the highlight returns to the button with keyboard focus if there is one, and fades
out otherwise.

**Which setting wins, the item's `IsIconOnly` or the tray's?** The item's own value, when it is not `null`.

## API reference

### FloatingButtonGroup

Separate soft buttons in a quiet tray for floating editors and canvas toolbars (Undo, Redo, Share, Present). One shared highlight (P7 `GlidingIndicator`) morphs in position and size to whichever button the pointer or keyboard focus is on, holds still across gaps and separators, fades when the pointer leaves the tray, and settles darker in place while a button is pressed; the buttons themselves never scale. Icon-only buttons and shortcut hints show the Arc `Tooltip`. One Tab stop; arrow keys move and wrap, Home and End jump, Enter and Space act.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Label` | `string` | `"Actions"` | Accessible name of the toolbar, such as "Board actions". |
| `Variant` | `FloatingButtonGroupVariant` | `Muted` | Surface of the tray: Muted (default), or Floating for a raised shadow and hairline edge. |
| `Size` | `ControlSize` | `Medium` | Small (30px buttons) or Medium (36px, default). Large is treated as Medium. |
| `Orientation` | `Orientation` | `Horizontal` | Lays the buttons out in a row (Horizontal, default) or a column (Vertical). |
| `IsIconOnly` | `bool` | `false` | Shows every item as an icon with its label in a tooltip; items with their own setting win. |
| `TooltipPlacement` | `TooltipSide?` | `null` | Side of the item tooltips; null uses Top for a row and Right for a column. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ActionInvoked` | `FloatingButtonGroupActionEventArgs` | Raised after an item's own click handlers and command. |

Pseudo-classes: `:pressing`, `:vertical`, `:small`

Derives from `ItemsControl`: every member of `ItemsControl` works as well.

### Item and event arguments

`FloatingButtonGroupItem` is the button of a tray. It adds these properties to the inherited `Button` members:

| Property | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `Label` | `string` | Visible text, and the accessible name when only the icon shows. |
| `Icon` | `Geometry?` | A 16 px Lucide glyph, for example `ArcIcons.Undo2`. |
| `IsIconOnly` | `bool?` | Shows only the icon. `null` follows the tray's `IsIconOnly`. |
| `IsChecked` | `bool?` | A mode that switches on. `null` is a plain action. |
| `Shortcut` | `string?` | A shortcut hint shown in the tooltip. The tray does not bind the key. |
| `ReserveLabels` | `IReadOnlyList<string>?` | Other labels the item can show; the button keeps the widest width. |

`FloatingButtonGroupActionEventArgs` (the argument of `ActionInvoked`) exposes `Item` (the button that ran) and `Data`
(the source object). `FloatingButtonGroupVariant` has two values: `Muted` and `Floating`.

## Accessibility

- The tray has the toolbar role and takes its name from `Label`. It reports its orientation.
- The tray is a single Tab stop. Focus returns to the last button that had keyboard focus.
- Each item is named by its label, including icon-only items. The shortcut hint is exposed as help text.
- An item with `IsChecked` reports a toggle state of On or Off. Changing the value announces the new state.
- Separators are announced as separators, so the grouping is available without the visuals.
- Disabled items stay readable and are skipped by the arrow keys. They keep their label, so people still learn that the
  action exists.
- The shared highlight shows only for pointer hover or keyboard focus, so it never marks a button that a person did
  not reach.

### Keyboard

The tray is one stop in the Tab order. Arrow keys move the highlight between the buttons.

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Tab` | Enters the tray at the button that had focus last, or the first enabled button. The next `Tab` leaves the tray. |
| `Left` / `Right` (row) or `Up` / `Down` (column) | Moves to the next or previous enabled button. The movement wraps at both ends. |
| `Home` / `End` | Moves to the first or last enabled button. |
| `Enter` / `Space` | Runs the focused button: its `Click` and `Command`, then `ActionInvoked`. |

## Motion

- One highlight glides to the button under the pointer or the keyboard focus. It holds still when the pointer crosses
  a gap or a separator, so the highlight never flickers between buttons.
- When the tray first receives a target, the highlight lands in place and grows from 94% to 100%. When the pointer
  leaves the tray, the highlight fades out.
- A pressed button darkens the highlight and the highlight contracts slightly. The button itself does not scale.
- Label changes crossfade in place. A button with `ReserveLabels` keeps its width; otherwise the highlight follows the
  new width.
- Reduced motion moves the highlight to its target with a short fade and crossfades the labels without a shift. Off
  puts everything in its final place at once.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| Highlight moves to another button | The highlight glides in position and size on a morph spring | Jumps to the target with a short fade | Immediate |
| Highlight appears on the first target | Grows from 94% to 100% on a snappy spring | Immediate | Immediate |
| Button is pressed | The highlight darkens and contracts to 96.5% on a snappy spring | Immediate | Immediate |
| Label changes | Crossfades in place with a short upward move and a soft blur | Crossfades without a shift | Immediate |

## Related

- `ButtonGroup` for related actions joined into one surface with dividers.
- `ExpandingButtonGroup` for compact icon actions whose labels expand on focus.
- `SegmentedControl` for a choice that stays selected.
- `Button` for a single action.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `ButtonGroup` | Related actions belong on one bordered surface in a page header or a form footer |
| `ExpandingButtonGroup` | Compact icon actions on a card or a message should reveal their labels on focus |
| `SegmentedControl` | A choice stays selected, such as a view mode, an alignment or a period |
| `DropdownMenu` | Actions overflow the tray and can wait behind one trigger |
| `SplitButton` | One primary action has alternatives in a menu |
| `Button` | There is one action with no state |

---

# Expanding button group

> Icon buttons in a compact group: the one you point at or focus grows to reveal its label while its neighbours slide aside, and an action confirms in place.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/expanding-button-group

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ExpandingButtonGroupMessageActionsDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12">
        <arc:ExpandingButtonGroup Label="Message actions"
                                  HorizontalAlignment="Center"
                                  ActionInvoked="OnActionInvoked">
            <arc:ExpandingButtonGroupItem Label="Reply" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Reply}" />
            <arc:ExpandingButtonGroupItem Label="Send"
                                          Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Send}"
                                          DoneLabel="Sent" />
            <arc:ExpandingButtonGroupItem x:Name="Archive"
                                          Label="Archive"
                                          Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Archive}"
                                          DoneLabel="Archived" />
            <arc:ExpandingButtonGroupItem Label="Save"
                                          Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Bookmark}"
                                          DoneLabel="Saved" />
            <arc:ExpandingButtonGroupItem Label="Delete"
                                          Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Trash2}"
                                          DoneLabel="Deleted"
                                          Tone="Danger" />
        </arc:ExpandingButtonGroup>
        <TextBlock x:Name="Log"
                   Text="Point at an action, or Tab in and use the arrow keys."
                   FontSize="13"
                   TextWrapping="Wrap"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class ExpandingButtonGroupMessageActionsDemo : UserControl
{
    public ExpandingButtonGroupMessageActionsDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Archive.AsyncAction = async () =>
        {
            await Task.Delay(600);
            return true;
        };
    }

    private void OnActionInvoked(object? sender, ExpandingButtonGroupActionEventArgs e)
    {
        Log.Text = $"Action: {e.Item.Label}";
    }
}
```

## When to use

`ExpandingButtonGroup` puts three to six related actions in one compact pill. One action always shows its label, and the
one the pointer or the keyboard reaches takes that label over while its neighbours slide aside. It fits a surface where
space is tight and the actions are familiar, so people learn the icons quickly and the labels appear only when needed.

- **Message and comment actions** in a support inbox or a team chat: Reply, Archive and Delete under a message, where the
  active label names the action and the Archive confirmation reads "Archived" in place.
- **File actions** in a document list or a file browser: Download, Share and Delete for the selected file, with a
  `Small` size that matches the dense rows of a table.
- **Card actions** on a dashboard or a project board: Like, Comment and Publish on a post or a task card, where one action
  is the most likely next step and is expanded at rest.
- **Save and confirm flows** in an editor toolbar, where a Save action can confirm with "Saved" for a moment before the
  label returns to rest, so the person knows the change was stored.

## When not to use

- **A choice that stays selected**, such as a view switcher between List, Board and Calendar: use `SegmentedControl` from
  Toggles, which shows the selection and keeps it.
- **One or two actions with enough room**: use a labelled `Button`, since the labels never need to be discovered.
- **More than about six actions**: use `DropdownMenu` from Menus, which lists them with their labels.
- **Icon actions that need labels all the time**, such as a shared toolbar that new users must read: use
  `FloatingButtonGroup` or `ButtonGroup`, whose labels stay visible.

## Usage

Each action is an `ExpandingButtonGroupItem`. The group needs a `Label`, which is its accessible name.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:ExpandingButtonGroup Label="Message actions">
        <arc:ExpandingButtonGroupItem Label="Reply" />
        <arc:ExpandingButtonGroupItem Label="Send" DoneLabel="Sent" />
        <arc:ExpandingButtonGroupItem Label="Archive" DoneLabel="Archived" />
    </arc:ExpandingButtonGroup>
</UserControl>
```

`ExpandingButtonGroup` derives from `ItemsControl`, so its items are the `ExpandingButtonGroupItem` containers. Each item
derives from Avalonia's `Button`: `Command`, `Click` and `IsEnabled` behave as they do on a button, and the group adds the
expansion, the confirmation, the busy state and the keyboard model on top.

### Anatomy

1. **Pill** (`Label` names it): a 1 px border on the surface color with the pill radius and a 3 px inset. The actions sit
   2 px apart. `Label` is the toolbar's name and is not drawn.
2. **Collapsed action**: a square 36 px in the Medium size (28 px in `Small`) with a 16 px icon (14 px in `Small`). The
   icon starts 10 px in from the left edge (7 px in `Small`).
3. **Expanded label**: the label follows the icon after a 7 px gap (5 px in `Small`) and ends with a 14 px inset (11 px in
   `Small`). The expanded action fills with the muted surface color and the text uses the foreground color.
4. **Danger tone** (`Tone="Danger"`): while expanded, the text uses the danger color on a danger tint of 10% (14% in dark
   mode) over the surface.
5. **Confirmation** (`DoneLabel`): the icon becomes a check and the label becomes the done word on a success tint of 10%
   (14% in dark mode) over the surface. The done word reserves the same space as the longer of the two words.
6. **Focus ring**: a ring that appears only for keyboard focus.
7. **Disabled action** (`IsDisabled`): dimmed, with the label in the muted text color. It stays focusable and still
   expands, so people can see what it would do.

### Icons and the resting action

Set `Icon` to a 16 by 16 Lucide geometry in code or with `x:Static`. The group shows one label at rest: the first enabled
action by default. `DefaultExpandedItem` picks another one, and when that item is disabled or not in the group, the
group falls back to the first enabled action.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ExpandingButtonGroupRestingActionDemo">
    <arc:ExpandingButtonGroup Label="Card actions"
                              DefaultExpandedItem="{Binding #Comment}"
                              HorizontalAlignment="Center">
        <arc:ExpandingButtonGroupItem Label="Like"
                                      Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Heart}"
                                      DoneLabel="Liked" />
        <arc:ExpandingButtonGroupItem x:Name="Comment"
                                      Label="Comment"
                                      Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.MessageCircle}" />
        <arc:ExpandingButtonGroupItem x:Name="Publish"
                                      Label="Publish"
                                      Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Upload}"
                                      DoneLabel="Published" />
    </arc:ExpandingButtonGroup>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class ExpandingButtonGroupRestingActionDemo : UserControl
{
    public ExpandingButtonGroupRestingActionDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        // Returning false declines the result, so Publish skips the confirmation.
        Publish.AsyncAction = async () =>
        {
            await Task.Delay(500);
            return false;
        };
    }
}
```

```csharp
reply.Icon = ArcIcons.Reply;
archive.Icon = ArcIcons.Archive;

var comment = new ExpandingButtonGroupItem { Label = "Comment", Icon = ArcIcons.MessageCircle };
var card = new ExpandingButtonGroup
{
    Label = "Card actions",
    DefaultExpandedItem = comment
};
```

Choose the resting action with the most likely next step. On a card that asks for a review, the review action rests open
so the purpose of the card is visible without a pointer.

### Confirmation

`DoneLabel` is the past tense word shown after the action. Leave it out for actions that open something. The
confirmation stays for `ConfirmDuration`, which is 1.4 seconds by default, and then the item collapses unless the pointer
or the keyboard is still on it. The group announces the done word politely, and a repeated action announces it again.

```xml
<arc:ExpandingButtonGroupItem Label="Save" DoneLabel="Saved" />
```

### Async action

`AsyncAction` returns a `Task<bool>`. The item is busy until the task ends, its icon pulses in the motion levels that
allow it, and repeated activation is ignored. Returning `false`, or throwing, skips the confirmation. Without an async
action, `Click` and `Command` count as success.

```csharp
var archive = new ExpandingButtonGroupItem
{
    Label = "Archive",
    Icon = ArcIcons.Archive,
    DoneLabel = "Archived",
    AsyncAction = async () =>
    {
        await archiveService.ArchiveAsync();
        return true;
    }
};
```

### Size and tone

`Size` sets the group. `Medium` (the default) uses 36 px actions with 16 px icons. `Small` uses 28 px actions with 14 px
icons and a smaller label size, which suits a dense table row. `Large` is treated as `Medium`.

`Tone="Danger"` colors an expanded destructive action in the danger color. A disabled item stays focusable and still
reveals its label, but it does not run.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ExpandingButtonGroupSmallDemo">
    <arc:ExpandingButtonGroup Label="File actions" Size="Small" HorizontalAlignment="Center">
        <arc:ExpandingButtonGroupItem Label="Download"
                                      Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Download}"
                                      DoneLabel="Downloaded" />
        <arc:ExpandingButtonGroupItem Label="Share"
                                      Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Share2}"
                                      DoneLabel="Link copied" />
        <arc:ExpandingButtonGroupItem Label="Lock"
                                      Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Lock}"
                                      IsDisabled="True" />
        <arc:ExpandingButtonGroupItem Label="Delete"
                                      Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Trash2}"
                                      Tone="Danger"
                                      DoneLabel="Deleted" />
    </arc:ExpandingButtonGroup>
</UserControl>
```

### Events

`ActionInvoked` runs before the item's own `AsyncAction`, and it is raised for every action that runs. `e.Item` is the
action that runs. `e.Data` is the item itself for inline items, and the data object for an `ItemsSource`.

```csharp
message.ActionInvoked += (_, e) => log.Text = $"Action: {e.Item.Label}";
```

### Binding to a view model

The action set is usually fixed for a page, so define the items in XAML and bind their commands and async actions to the
view model. The view model owns the work; the group only reports the state.

```csharp
public interface ITicketService
{
    Task<bool> ArchiveAsync(string ticketId);

    Task<bool> DeleteAsync(string ticketId);
}

public partial class TicketViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    private readonly ITicketService _tickets;

    public TicketViewModel(ITicketService tickets)
    {
        _tickets = tickets;
    }

    [ObservableProperty]
    private string _ticketId = "tkt_2026_0412";

    public Func<Task<bool>> ArchiveAction => () => _tickets.ArchiveAsync(TicketId);

    public Func<Task<bool>> DeleteAction => () => _tickets.DeleteAsync(TicketId);

    [RelayCommand]
    private void Reply()
    {
        // Open the reply composer for TicketId.
    }
}
```

```xml
<arc:ExpandingButtonGroup Label="Ticket actions">
    <arc:ExpandingButtonGroupItem Label="Reply"
                                  Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Reply}"
                                  Command="{Binding ReplyCommand}" />
    <arc:ExpandingButtonGroupItem Label="Archive"
                                  Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Archive}"
                                  DoneLabel="Archived"
                                  AsyncAction="{Binding ArchiveAction}" />
    <arc:ExpandingButtonGroupItem Label="Delete"
                                  Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Trash2}"
                                  DoneLabel="Deleted"
                                  Tone="Danger"
                                  AsyncAction="{Binding DeleteAction}" />
</arc:ExpandingButtonGroup>
```

- Nothing here is two-way. The items are configured once, and `ExpandedItem`, `IsExpanded`, `IsDone` and `IsBusy` are
  read-only properties that report state for styling or tests.
- `Command` runs as the action and counts as success, so a command that cannot fail needs no `AsyncAction`.
- A command that returns a result belongs in `AsyncAction`, because only the `Task<bool>` decides whether the
  confirmation shows.

### Pointer, touch and keyboard

The group expands the action the person is working with, and it follows the input that is in use.

- **Mouse**: the label moves to the action under the pointer. The pointer must travel 4 px into a neighbour before the
  expansion moves, so an action does not take over when it slides under a still pointer. When the pointer leaves the
  group, the expansion returns to the confirmed action, the focused action or the resting action.
- **Touch**: there is no hover. The first tap expands the action, and the second tap runs it. An action that is already
  expanded runs at once. A tap outside the group collapses a label that a first tap opened.
- **Keyboard**: focus expands the focused action. The group is a single Tab stop, and the arrow keys move between
  actions, so the expansion always follows focus.

### Layout and width

Each action has a fixed height, and its collapsed width is a square. The expanded width is the icon, the gap and the
longer of `Label` and `DoneLabel`. The label slot reserves that longer word from the start, so a confirmation does not
change the width. The row grows and shrinks as the expanded action changes, and its neighbours slide to make room.

Place the group at its start edge, and leave room for the widest expansion. For five Medium actions with short labels,
reserve about 260 to 280 px. A group that is laid out in a large container that reflows often should be placed on its
own row, because the width changes as the expansion moves.

### Example: ticket actions in a support inbox

A support agent reads a message on a ticket, and the group sits under the message. Reply rests open because it is the
most likely next step. Archive confirms with "Archived" after its task completes, and Delete is in the danger tone so its
expanded state is clearly different. The group is left aligned under the text it acts on.

![A support ticket message with an expanded Reply action and two collapsed actions](https://docs.tkcode.si/shots/Docs/Buttons/ExpandingButtonGroup/images/TicketActions.webp)

```xml
<StackPanel Width="600" Spacing="14">
    <Border Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Surface}"
            BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Border}"
            BorderThickness="1"
            CornerRadius="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource RadiusPanel}"
            Padding="20">
        <StackPanel Spacing="12">
            <StackPanel Orientation="Horizontal" Spacing="8">
                <TextBlock Text="Maya Chen"
                           FontWeight="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource WeightMedium}"
                           Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
                <TextBlock Text="21 Oct 2026, 09:14"
                           FontSize="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TypeSM}"
                           Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}"
                           VerticalAlignment="Center" />
            </StackPanel>
            <TextBlock Text="The March invoice still shows the old seat count. Can you check it before the 28th?"
                       TextWrapping="Wrap"
                       FontSize="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TypeBase}"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
            <arc:ExpandingButtonGroup Label="Ticket actions" Margin="0,4,0,0">
                <arc:ExpandingButtonGroupItem Label="Reply"
                                              Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Reply}" />
                <arc:ExpandingButtonGroupItem Label="Archive"
                                              Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Archive}"
                                              DoneLabel="Archived" />
                <arc:ExpandingButtonGroupItem Label="Delete"
                                              Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Trash2}"
                                              DoneLabel="Deleted"
                                              Tone="Danger" />
            </arc:ExpandingButtonGroup>
        </StackPanel>
    </Border>
</StackPanel>
```

The message and the sender set the context, so the icons alone are enough for the three actions. The reply label is
visible because it is the resting action, which tells the agent what the group offers before any pointer moves.

### Content guidelines

- **Label**: a short verb in sentence case, such as "Reply", "Archive" or "Save". The label is the accessible name even
  when it is collapsed, so it must read clearly on its own.
- **Done label**: the past tense of the verb, one word, such as "Archived" or "Sent". It appears for about a second and
  a half, so it must be understood at a glance.
- **Icon**: choose a glyph that people already associate with the action, and keep it the same across the product.

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| Archive this message | Archive |
| Done! | Archived |
| Click to send | Send |
| Mark as saved | Saved |

### Best practices

**Do**

- Put the most likely next action first and let it rest open, so the group explains itself before any pointer moves.
- Use the `Danger` tone for destructive actions, so the expanded state signals the consequence.
- Give every item an `AsyncAction` when the work can fail. A `false` result or an exception skips the confirmation, so a
  failed archive never claims success.
- Keep three to six actions. Fewer than three is better as buttons; more than six makes the expansions hard to scan.

**Avoid**

- Putting selection controls in the group. A group that remembers a choice is a `SegmentedControl`, and mixing the two
  confuses the expansion with the selection.
- Long labels. A label that is much longer than its icon widens the group on every expansion, so the row moves more than
  the person expects.
- Disabling the item the person needs most without explanation. A disabled item stays focusable and expands, but people
  still need the reason nearby, in the surrounding text.
- Relying on the done word alone for a change that matters. The check and the word last about 1.4 seconds, so confirm
  important results in the page as well.

### Common questions

**Why does the first enabled action show its label at rest?** That is the default resting action. A disabled first item is
skipped, and `DefaultExpandedItem` overrides the choice. If the item is not in the group, the group falls back to the
first enabled action.

**Why did my action run without a confirmation?** It has no `DoneLabel`, or its `AsyncAction` returned `false`, or it
threw. Only a `true` result from a task with a `DoneLabel` shows the confirmation.

**Can I run an action from code, such as a keyboard shortcut?** Call `ActivateAsync(item)` on the group. It runs the
action as a press would, and it does nothing for a disabled, busy or confirming item.

**Does the group collapse after a confirmation?** Yes, after `ConfirmDuration`, unless the pointer or the keyboard focus
is still on the item. A repeated action on the same item shows its done word again.

## API reference

### ExpandingButtonGroup

A compact pill of icon buttons for 3 to 6 related actions (message, file and card actions). One action always shows its label; the one you point at or focus takes it over while its neighbours slide aside (width springs inside one row, P5), and an action can confirm in place: the icon draws a check and the label becomes a past tense word (P2, P15). On touch the first tap reveals the label and a second tap runs the action. One Tab stop; arrow keys move and wrap, Home and End jump, Enter and Space run.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Label` | `string` | `"Actions"` | Accessible name of the toolbar, such as "Message actions". |
| `Size` | `ControlSize` | `Medium` | Small (28px, 14px icons) or Medium (36px, 16px icons; default). Large is treated as Medium. |
| `DefaultExpandedItem` | `object?` | `null` | The action (item or its container) whose label shows at rest; null uses the first enabled action. |
| `ConfirmDuration` | `TimeSpan` | `00:00:01.4000000` | How long a confirmation stays (default 1.4s). |
| `ExpandedItem` | `ExpandingButtonGroupItem?` | – | *Read-only.* The action currently showing its label. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ActionInvoked` | `ExpandingButtonGroupActionEventArgs` | Raised whenever an action runs, before its own `AsyncAction`. |

Pseudo-classes: `:small`

Derives from `ItemsControl`: every member of `ItemsControl` works as well.

### ExpandingButtonGroupItem

One action of an `ExpandingButtonGroup`: an icon that grows to reveal its label. The width rides the morph spring between the icon and the icon plus the longer of `Label` and `DoneLabel`; the label slides out from behind the icon and tucks back faster. Code-driven because the reveal is asymmetric (240ms with a delay in, 120ms out) and blurs, which a ControlTheme transition cannot express.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Label` | `string` | `""` | A short verb, visible once expanded and the accessible name at all times. |
| `Icon` | `Geometry?` | `null` | 16px Lucide glyph shown while collapsed (sized by the group). |
| `DoneLabel` | `string?` | `null` | Past tense word shown in place after the action (such as "Archived"); omit for actions that open something. |
| `Tone` | `ExpandingButtonGroupTone` | `Neutral` | Color of the expanded action: Neutral (default), or Danger for destructive actions such as Delete. |
| `IsDisabled` | `bool` | `false` | Dimmed and inert, but still focusable and still reveals its label, so people can learn what it would do. |
| `AsyncAction` | `Func<Task<bool>>?` | `null` | Runs the action. The button is busy until the task completes; returning false, or throwing, skips the confirmation. Without it, `Click` and `Command` count as success. |
| `IsExpanded` | `bool` | – | *Read-only.* True while this action shows its label. |
| `IsDone` | `bool` | – | *Read-only.* True while the confirmation shows. |
| `IsBusy` | `bool` | – | *Read-only.* True while `AsyncAction` runs. |

Pseudo-classes: `:expanded`, `:done`, `:busy`, `:unavailable`, `:small`

Derives from `Button`: every member of `Button` works as well.

## Accessibility

- The group has the ToolBar role, named by `Label`. The full label is the name even while the label is collapsed.
- The group is a single Tab stop. Left and Right arrow keys move between actions and wrap. Home and End move to the
  first and last action.
- Enter and Space run the focused action. Repeated activation is ignored while the action is busy.
- A disabled action keeps keyboard focus and reports as unavailable.
- A confirmation word is announced politely, and a repeated confirmation is announced again.
- The collapsed label is hidden from assistive technology, so the name is read once, not twice.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` | Enters the group on its last focused action, or the resting action; a second Tab leaves the group |
| `Left` / `Right` | Moves to the previous or next action and expands it; wraps at either end |
| `Home` / `End` | Moves to the first or last action |
| `Enter` / `Space` | Runs the focused action; ignored while the action is busy |

## Motion

- The focused or hovered action grows on a spring to show its label, and its neighbours slide aside.
- The label slides out from behind the icon with a short fade and a slight blur, and tucks back faster.
- On confirmation the icon draws a check and the label changes to the done word, which rises in while the old word moves out.
- Pointer movement must travel a few pixels into a neighbour before the label moves, so the group does not jump under a
  still pointer.
- Reduced motion changes the label and the width at once with a quick fade, and the check appears without drawing. Off
  makes the same change without any transition.
- A busy action pulses its icon. Reduced motion holds the icon at 60% opacity instead of pulsing.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| Expansion | The width springs between the icon and the icon plus label; neighbours slide | The label and width change at once with a quick fade | Immediate |
| Label | Slides out from behind the icon with a blur: 240 ms with a short delay in, 120 ms out | Quick fade | Immediate |
| Confirmation | The check draws in 240 ms; the old word moves up and out as the new word rises in | The check appears without drawing; the word fades | Immediate |

## Related

- `FloatingButtonGroup` for separate soft buttons whose labels stay visible in a tray.
- `ButtonGroup` for related actions joined into one surface with dividers.
- `ActionButton` for one asynchronous submit with pending and success on the button.
- `DropdownMenu` for a longer list of commands.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `SegmentedControl` | One option stays selected, such as a view or a filter |
| `Button` | One or two actions have room for their labels |
| `ButtonGroup` | Related actions need visible labels joined into one surface |
| `FloatingButtonGroup` | Separate soft buttons with labels that stay visible in a tray |
| `ActionButton` | One submit needs its own pending and success states |
| `DropdownMenu` | There are more than about six commands, or the commands need full text |

# Copy button

> Copy a value with immediate confirmation.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/copy-button

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.CopyButtonOutlineDemo">
    <WrapPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center" ItemSpacing="12" LineSpacing="12">
        <arc:CopyButton Value="npx arc add copy-button" />
        <arc:CopyButton Value="sk_live_51H..." Label="Copy key" />
        <arc:CopyButton Value="https://uiarc.dev" IsIconOnly="True" />
    </WrapPanel>
</UserControl>
```

## When to use

`CopyButton` copies one value to the clipboard and confirms the copy in place: the icon becomes a check, the label
changes to "Copied" and the button returns to rest after a moment. It sits next to the value it copies, so the person
never has to select text, find the right characters or leave the row they are working in. It is a `Button`, so it works
with the keyboard, in a toolbar and in any layout that takes a button.

- **Secrets and keys shown once**: an API key or a webhook signing secret on a developer console page. The person copies
  the full value into a password manager or a config file, and the masked text beside it never has to be selected.
- **Install commands and snippets in onboarding pages**: a line such as `npx arc add copy-button` in a docs page or a
  setup wizard. The `Plain` variant keeps the command readable and still offers the copy action.
- **Shareable links on an invoice or a report**: a payment link or a read-only report URL on a billing page, copied
  so the person can paste it into an email to a customer.
- **Identifiers in dense tables**: order IDs, workspace IDs or tracking numbers in a list, where the icon-only form adds
  one copy action per row without widening the table.
- **Values that must be exact**: a connection string or a SKU, where typing it by hand or selecting it from wrapped text
  invites a mistake.

## When not to use

- **Copying the value in several formats**, such as Copy link, Copy as Markdown or Copy embed code: use `SplitButton`,
  so the primary copy stays one press and the alternatives sit in its menu.
- **A complete code sample** with a copy control of its own: use `CodeBlock`, which already has one in its header.
- **A read-only field the person may need to edit or read in full**: use `Input` with `IsReadOnly="True"`, which keeps
  the value selectable. Use `CopyButton` beside that field when a single press should copy the whole value.
- **Actions that send or run something** rather than copy it, such as a Send invite or a Rotate key action: use `Button`
  or `ActionButton`, whose pending and success states describe the work.
- **A list of row actions where copying is one of many**: use `DropdownMenu` from Menus, so the copy action sits with
  Edit, Rename and Delete instead of taking a button of its own on every row.

## Usage

Set `Value` to the text that goes to the clipboard. `Label` is the visible text and the accessible name.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:CopyButton Value="npx arc add copy-button" />
</UserControl>
```

`CopyButton` derives from Avalonia's `Button`. It keeps `Command`, `Click`, `IsEnabled` and the other button behavior,
and it adds the copy in its click handling: the value is read when the button is clicked, and the clipboard write is
awaited, so the window keeps running while the copy completes.

### Anatomy

1. **Frame** (`Variant`, `Background`, `BorderBrush`): a 1 px border on the surface color with the control radius and a
   minimum height of the small control size (36 px). Hover moves the frame to the muted surface and the strong border.
2. **Icon**: a 16 px copy glyph. After a copy it becomes a check in the success color; after a failure it becomes an
   alert in the danger color.
3. **Label** (`Label`, `CopiedLabel`, `FailedLabel`): the text. The label cell reserves the widest of the three words,
   so the button keeps its width while the words change. The gap between icon and label is 8 px and the inline padding
   is 12 px on each side.
4. **Focus ring**: a 2 px ring in the focus color, drawn 4 px outside the frame. It appears only for keyboard focus.

### Variants and sizes

`Variant` sets the frame. `Outline` (the default) draws the surface and the border, so the button reads as an action.
`Plain` removes the frame and uses the secondary text color, which suits a row of code, a dense table or a caption where
an outlined button would compete with the content.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.CopyButtonPlainDemo">
    <WrapPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center" ItemSpacing="12" LineSpacing="12">
        <arc:CopyButton Value="#7C5CFF" Label="Copy hex" Variant="Plain" />
        <arc:CopyButton Value="rgb(124 92 255)" Variant="Plain" IsIconOnly="True" />
    </WrapPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```xml
<arc:CopyButton Value="https://uiarc.dev" IsIconOnly="True" />
<arc:CopyButton Value="#7C5CFF" Label="Copy hex" Variant="Plain" />
```

Pick one variant per region. Use `Outline` for the copy that matters most in a panel, and `Plain` for the copy actions
that repeat in a list or sit inside a code block.

### Icon only and labels

`IsIconOnly` hides the label and leaves a square 36 px button with the icon. The `Label` still names the button for
assistive technology, so an icon-only copy needs a specific label: "Copy order ID" is announced where "Copy" would be
ambiguous in a table with many rows. The icon-only button is 36 px wide, so it fits a table column without widening it.

### Reset time and events

The button returns to idle after `ResetAfter`, which is 1.9 seconds by default. `Copied` is raised after a successful
copy, and never after a failure. `State` reports `Idle`, `Copied` or `Error` and is read-only: the control sets it, and
code reads it.

```csharp
copy.Copied += (_, _) => log.Text = "Copied to the clipboard.";
copy.ResetAfter = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(3);
```

Lengthen `ResetAfter` only when the person must read the confirmation before it changes, for example when the copy is
followed by a step on another page. Keep the default for a single copy, so the control is ready again for the next one.

### Binding to a view model

The value is usually data the view model already holds, so bind `Value` one way and let the click copy whatever it holds
at that moment. The `Failure` demo shows the case where no value exists.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.CopyButtonFailureDemo">
    <arc:CopyButton Label="Copy nothing" HorizontalAlignment="Center" />
</UserControl>
```

```csharp
public partial class DeveloperKeysViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    [ObservableProperty]
    private string? _apiKey = "ak_live_2026_7f3a9c21";

    [ObservableProperty]
    private string? _installCommand = "npx arc add copy-button";
}
```

```xml
<StackPanel Spacing="8">
    <arc:CopyButton Value="{Binding ApiKey}" Label="Copy key" />
    <arc:CopyButton Value="{Binding InstallCommand}" Label="Copy command" Variant="Plain" />
</StackPanel>
```

- `Value` is one-way. The control never writes to the view model, so a copy cannot change the data it copies.
- A `null` value makes the copy fail: the button shows its failed state and its width does not change. Bind the value
  to the data that is actually available, rather than to a placeholder that would be copied by mistake.
- Keep the `Value` in step with the data on screen. A masked display such as "ak_live_****" should not be the bound
  value, because the person would paste the mask.

### Example: developer API keys

A developer console page that shows a production key with a copy action and an install command in the same panel. The
key is the most important value, so it uses the outline variant and a full label. The command is a secondary value, so
it uses the plain variant with an icon-only copy. Both values are visible in full, so the person can check them before
copying.

![An API keys panel with a production key and a copy command row](https://docs.tkcode.si/shots/Docs/Buttons/CopyButton/images/ApiKeys.webp)

```xml
<StackPanel Width="620" Spacing="16">
    <TextBlock Text="API keys"
               FontSize="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TypeLG}"
               FontWeight="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource WeightMedium}"
               Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
    <Border Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Surface}"
            BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Border}"
            BorderThickness="1"
            CornerRadius="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource RadiusPanel}"
            Padding="20">
        <StackPanel Spacing="18">
            <StackPanel Spacing="6">
                <TextBlock Text="Production key"
                           FontWeight="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource WeightMedium}"
                           Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
                <TextBlock Text="Created 14 April 2026. Use it on the server only."
                           TextWrapping="Wrap"
                           FontSize="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TypeSM}"
                           Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
            </StackPanel>
            <Grid ColumnDefinitions="*,Auto">

                        Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource SurfaceMuted}"

                               FontFamily="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource MonoFontFamily}"

                </Border>
                <arc:CopyButton Grid.Column="1"
                                Label="Copy key"

            <Border Height="1" Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource BorderSubtle}" />
            <Grid ColumnDefinitions="Auto,*,Auto">
                <TextBlock Grid.Column="0"
                           Text="Install"
                           Margin="0,0,16,0"
                           VerticalAlignment="Center"
                           FontSize="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TypeSM}"
                           Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
                <TextBlock Grid.Column="1"
                           Text="npx arc add copy-button"
                           FontFamily="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource MonoFontFamily}"
                           FontSize="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TypeSM}"
                           VerticalAlignment="Center"
```
