The key is the one value the page exists to copy, so it has a full label, the surface frame and a monospace face that
keeps characters such as the `0` and `O` distinct. The command is secondary, so its icon-only copy lets the row stay
short while its accessible name still says what it copies.

### Content guidelines

- **Label**: a verb and its object in sentence case, such as "Copy key" or "Copy command". Name the value so the
  button makes sense out of context and to a screen reader reading a list of buttons.
- **Copied label**: a short past-tense confirmation, "Copied" or "Key copied". The copied state lasts only a moment, so
  the word must be understood at a glance.
- **Failed label**: say what did not happen, not why. "Could not copy" tells the person to try again or select the text.

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| Click to copy | Copy key |
| Success! | Copied |
| Error | Could not copy |
| Copy to clipboard (in a table of 40 rows) | Copy order ID |

### Best practices

**Do**

- Name the value in the `Label` ("Copy key", "Copy invoice link"), since the label is the accessible name even when the
  icon hides it. A generic "Copy" repeated down a list gives a screen reader nothing to tell the rows apart.
- Copy the complete value the person needs, not a masked display. A pasted mask is a support ticket the page could have
  prevented.
- Use `Plain` in dense rows and code, and `Outline` for the copy that matters most in a panel. One outlined copy per
  panel keeps the primary action clear.
- Keep the default `ResetAfter` for a single copy, so the control returns to its label before the person moves on.

**Avoid**

- Binding `Value` to data that may be missing without handling the failure. A `null` value shows the failed state, and
  the person needs a reason to try again, not a silent button.
- Combining the copy with a destructive action in one button, such as "Copy and rotate key". Copying is safe, so keep
  the rotation in its own control with a confirmation.
- Stacking several outlined copy buttons in one row. The eye reads the row as several equal actions; use `Plain` for
  the secondary copies.
- Relying on the `Copied` event to show a message. The button already confirms the copy in place; a second message
  repeats the same signal and competes with the page.

### Common questions

**Why does the button show the failed state even though `Value` is set?** The click reports failure when the clipboard
refuses the write, so the failed state is not caused by the value alone. Show the failure label and let the person copy
the text by hand from a selectable field.

**Does `Copied` fire when the copy fails?** No. The event is raised only after a successful copy. Use `State` to read the
result of the last click, including `Error`.

**Can the button copy a value that is generated when the person clicks?** Not from `Value` alone. The value is read at
the click, so keep it current with the data on screen. Generate long or remote values before the page shows the button,
and bind the result to `Value`.

**How do I make the button icon only on narrow screens?** Set `IsIconOnly` from code when the layout narrows, for example
in a `SizeChanged` handler. The label stays the accessible name, so keep it specific.

## API reference

### CopyButton

Copies a value with immediate, in-place confirmation: the icon swaps to a hand-drawn check, the label morphs to "Copied", and everything returns to idle after 1.9s. The label cell reserves its widest state so the button never changes width.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Value` | `string?` | `null` | Text copied to the clipboard when the button is clicked. |
| `Label` | `string` | `"Copy"` | Label of the button in its idle state (default "Copy"). |
| `CopiedLabel` | `string` | `"Copied"` | Label shown after a successful copy (default "Copied"). |
| `FailedLabel` | `string` | `"Failed"` | Label shown when the copy fails (default "Failed"). |
| `IsIconOnly` | `bool` | `false` | Shows only the icon, without the label. |
| `Variant` | `CopyButtonVariant` | `Outline` | Visual style: Outline (default) or Plain. |
| `ResetAfter` | `TimeSpan` | `00:00:01.9000000` | Time the button keeps the copied or error state before it returns to idle (default 1.9 seconds). |
| `State` | `CopyState` | – | *Read-only.* Current copy state: Idle, Copied or Error (read-only). |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Copied` | `EventHandler?` | Occurs after the value is copied to the clipboard. |

Pseudo-classes: `:copied`, `:error`, `:icon-only`

Derives from `Button`: every member of `Button` works as well.

## Accessibility

- The accessible name is always `Label`, including when the button is icon only.
- A hidden polite status region announces the result, such as "Copy key: Copied" or "Copy key: Could not copy".
- Enter and Space copy the value.
- The label cell keeps the width of its widest state, so the layout around the button does not move.
- Keyboard focus shows the focus ring. Pointer focus draws no ring.
- A disabled button drops to half opacity.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` | Moves focus to the next or previous focusable control, including the copy button |
| `Enter` or `Space` | Copies the value; the copied or failed state shows, then returns to rest after `ResetAfter` |

## Motion

- The icon swaps with a soft blur and scales in on a slow, nearly critically damped spring. The check draws itself.
- Only the changed letters of the label move, and they play back in reverse when the button returns to idle.
- A press scales the content down slightly and a release springs it back.
- Reduced motion uses an instant crossfade for the icon and the text, skips the stroke drawing and the press scale. Off
  replaces the icon and the label at once.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| Copied or failed | The icon swaps with a soft blur and the check draws itself | The icon and the label crossfade instantly; the check does not draw | Immediate |
| Label change | Only the changed letters move, and they return in reverse at rest | Instant crossfade | Immediate |
| Press | The content scales to 0.97 (0.96 when icon only) and springs back on release | No press scale | No press scale |
| Hover | The frame crossfades to the muted surface and the strong border | Instant | Immediate |

## Related

- `SplitButton` when copying is one of several actions, such as Copy page with Copy link and Copy as Markdown.
- `ActionButton` for an asynchronous submit with a pending and a success state.
- `Button` for a plain action with no clipboard result.
- `CodeBlock` for a code sample that already includes a copy control.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `SplitButton` | Copy is the primary action and the alternatives are formats or variants of the same value |
| `CodeBlock` | The copied text is a code sample that already shows its own copy control |
| `Input` (`IsReadOnly`) | The value must stay selectable and readable in full, with a copy action beside it |
| `ActionButton` | The action sends or saves something and needs a pending and success state |
| `DropdownMenu` | Copying is one of several row commands that belong in a menu |

```cs
using Avalonia.Automation;
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class IconMorphEightPairsDemo : UserControl
{
    public IconMorphEightPairsDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
    }

    private void OnToggleClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        if (sender is not Button { Content: IconMorph icon } button)
        {
            return;
        }

        icon.IsActive = !icon.IsActive;
        // Tag holds the name of the other state; swap it in so the button always names what the next press does.
        var name = AutomationProperties.GetName(button);
        AutomationProperties.SetName(button, button.Tag as string);
        button.Tag = name;
    }
}
```

## When to use

`IconMorph` draws the eight icon pairs that products use for a state change: a menu that becomes a close icon, a play
button that becomes pause, a copy icon that becomes a check. It sits inside a button and shows the state the way a
person would see it change, so the change reads as one action rather than two icons swapping. It belongs in the
toolbars, headers and rows of an application, where the icon is the only thing a person looks at.

- **A live-data header in an operations dashboard**: a play and pause control that freezes the metrics stream while
  someone reads a spike. The icon morphs, so the person sees that the stream stopped.
- **A notification switch on an incident or order page**: a bell that rings once when notifications are turned on and
  is struck through when they are off, for a team that follows a single incident.
- **A disclosure control in a settings or billing list**: a chevron that turns when an invoice group or a filter
  panel opens, so the row shows its state without a separate label.
- **A navigation toggle in a SaaS app shell**: a menu icon that becomes a close icon when the side navigation opens on
  a narrow window.
- **A like or favourite on a shared report**: a heart that fills with a short burst when a teammate marks a report as
  useful.

## When not to use

- **A copy action with a confirmation**: use `CopyButton`, which already morphs its icon and announces the result.
- **A light and dark switch with a label**: use `ThemeSwitcher`, which carries the text and the state together.
- **An icon that never changes state**: use a plain Lucide icon from `ArcIcons` in the button. A morph with no second
  state adds nothing.
- **The icon as the only control**: `IconMorph` is decorative and never takes focus, so put it inside a `Button` or
  another control that has a name and a state.
- **A menu of several actions behind one icon**: use `DropdownMenu` with its trigger. The morph only shows that one
  thing is open or closed.

## Usage

`IconMorph` draws one of eight icon pairs. `Kind` selects the pair and `IsActive` selects the second state. Put it
inside a button and name the button.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:Button Variant="Ghost" AutomationProperties.Name="Open menu">
        <arc:IconMorph Kind="Menu" />
    </arc:Button>
</UserControl>
```

`IconMorph` derives from Avalonia's `Control`. It draws its glyph in `Render` on a 24 by 24 grid, so it has no template
and no parts to restyle. Its `IsActive` property is two-way by default, which makes it a natural target for a view
model property. The control does not handle pointer or keyboard input: clicks and key presses go to the button that
hosts it.

### Anatomy

1. **Glyph** (`Kind`): one drawn shape, on a 24-unit grid, that morphs between its inactive and active forms.
2. **Stroke** (`StrokeThickness`): 1.75 on the grid by default. It scales with `IconSize`, so the icon keeps its weight
   at 16 px, 24 px and 32 px.
3. **Size** (`IconSize`): the rendered size in pixels, 24 by default. The theme sets the same default.
4. **Color** (`Foreground`): inherited from the parent like the text foreground, so a ghost button colors its icon with
   its own text color.
5. **Liked color** (`LikeBrush`): the color of a liked heart. The theme sets it to the danger color.
6. **Moment**: the bell's ring and the heart's ring and sparks. A moment plays once each time the icon is turned on and
   has no visible part in the other states.

### Kinds

`Menu` morphs to close, `Play` to pause, `Plus` to check, `Copy` to check, `Theme` to the moon, `Chevron` turns,
`Bell` turns notifications on and off, and `Heart` likes. The active state of each pair is the second item in its name:
a plus becomes a check, a bell turns on, a heart is liked.

```xml
<arc:IconMorph Kind="Play" />
<arc:IconMorph Kind="Theme" IsActive="True" />
<arc:IconMorph Kind="Heart" IsActive="{Binding IsLiked}" />
```

Choose the pair by the meaning of the state, not by the look of the icon. `Plus` to `Check` fits an "add to list"
action whose result is a checked item. `Copy` to `Check` fits a copy action. `Play` to `Pause` is for a stream or a
clip that the person starts and stops, not for a one-way action.

### Toggle state

Bind `IsActive` to the state of the button. Flip it in the click handler, and update the name of the button to match
the new meaning.

```csharp
var icon = new IconMorph { Kind = IconMorphKind.Play };
var button = new Button { Content = icon, Variant = ButtonVariant.Ghost };
button.Click += (_, _) =>
{
    icon.IsActive = !icon.IsActive;
    AutomationProperties.SetName(button, icon.IsActive ? "Pause" : "Play");
};
```

### Size and stroke

`IconSize` sets the rendered size in pixels; the default is 24. `StrokeThickness` is set on the 24-unit grid and scales
with `IconSize`, so the default stroke of 1.75 stays in proportion at any size.


```cs
using Avalonia.Automation;
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class IconMorphSizesDemo : UserControl
{
    public IconMorphSizesDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
    }

    private void OnToggleClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        if (sender is not Button { Content: IconMorph icon } button)
        {
            return;
        }

        icon.IsActive = !icon.IsActive;
        // Tag holds the name of the other state; swap it in so the button always names what the next press does.
        var name = AutomationProperties.GetName(button);
        AutomationProperties.SetName(button, button.Tag as string);
        button.Tag = name;
    }
}
```

```xml
<arc:IconMorph Kind="Menu" IconSize="16" />
<arc:IconMorph Kind="Menu" IconSize="32" StrokeThickness="2" />
```

Match the icon to the button. A 16 px icon fits a 36 px button, a 24 px icon fits 44 px, and a 32 px icon fits the
52 px hero buttons. A 24 px icon in a 28 px button looks cramped, and a 16 px icon in a 52 px button looks lost.

### Chevron direction

For `Chevron`, `ChevronPointing` sets the rest direction, and `ChevronTurn` sets the angle in degrees when the icon is
active. A value of 180 flips down to up. A value of 90 turns right to down.


Use `Down` with a 180 turn for a section that expands downward, and `Right` with a 90 turn for a row that opens to the
side, such as a tree node. Keep the same direction for every chevron in one list, so that a row that opens and a row
that does not are easy to tell apart.

### MorphGlyph

`MorphGlyph` is the path morph primitive: it morphs between any two pieces of path data. Menu to close keeps its vertices, and close to check resamples by arc length.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.IconMorphMorphGlyphDemo">
    <arc:Button Width="52"
                Height="52"
                Padding="0"
                Variant="Ghost"
                HorizontalAlignment="Center"
                AutomationProperties.Name="Morph to the next shape"
                Click="OnMorphClick">
        <arc:MorphGlyph x:Name="Morph" Data="M4 6h16 M4 12h16 M4 18h16" Size="32" />
    </arc:Button>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class IconMorphMorphGlyphDemo : UserControl
{
    // Menu, close and check: menu to close keeps its vertices, close to check resamples by arc length.
    private static readonly string[] Shapes =
    [
        "M4 6h16 M4 12h16 M4 18h16",
        "M6 6 L18 18 M12 12h0 M6 18 L18 6",
        "M4 12.5l5 5L20 6.5"
    ];

    private int _index;

    public IconMorphMorphGlyphDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
    }

    private void OnMorphClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        _index = (_index + 1) % Shapes.Length;
        Morph.Data = Shapes[_index];
    }
}
```

Use `MorphGlyph` for a shape the eight pairs do not cover. Give it the second shape with `MorphTo`, which animates
from the current outline. Use `Morph` in code when a custom state needs to know that the morph has finished.

```csharp
var glyph = this.FindControl<MorphGlyph>("StatusGlyph")!;
await glyph.MorphTo("M4 12.5l5 5L20 6.5");
```

### Binding to a view model

A dashboard view model owns the live state, and the header only shows it. `IsActive` binds two-way, so the icon can
both show and change the state.

```csharp
public partial class LiveMetricsViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    [ObservableProperty]
    [NotifyPropertyChangedFor(nameof(LiveToggleName))]
    private bool _isPaused;

    public string LiveToggleName => IsPaused ? "Resume live updates" : "Pause live updates";

    [RelayCommand]
    private void ToggleLive() => IsPaused = !IsPaused;
}
```

```xml
<arc:Button Variant="Ghost"
            Width="36"
            Height="36"
            Padding="0"
            AutomationProperties.Name="{Binding LiveToggleName}"
            Command="{Binding ToggleLiveCommand}">
    <arc:IconMorph Kind="Play" IsActive="{Binding IsPaused}" IconSize="18" />
</arc:Button>
```

- `IsActive` is two-way. A change in the view model moves the icon, and a change to the icon writes the new state.
  Bind it only to the property that owns the state; a second writer makes the morph flip back and forth.
- The button name comes from the view model, so a screen reader hears the action the next press performs, not the icon.
- The command performs the change. The icon follows the state, and does not run the action itself.

### Using motion with restraint

The morph is the feedback for a state change, so it helps wherever a person has to see that something changed. It
distracts where the same change repeats many times in a row, or where the icon is the whole signal of an action.

- **Helps**: a single toggle that changes what the next action does, such as pause and resume, or menu and close.
- **Distracts**: a bell in a list that fires for every item, or a heart in a feed where people like many posts in a row.
  The burst then plays on every press. Keep the moments for a single, deliberate action.
- **Reduced motion** completes every morph at once and skips the bell's ring and the heart's burst. Test the state
  change without the motion too: the icon and the button name must still tell the person what happened.

### Example: incident header controls

An incident page in an operations console shows the live status of the incident and three controls: pause the live
updates, turn notifications on or off, and expand the list of affected services. Each control is a ghost button with a
name that matches the state the button is in, and the icons morph so the state is visible without a label. The
header keeps a menu icon for less frequent actions, with its name written as the action it opens.

![An incident header with a pause control, a bell, a collapsed chevron and a menu icon](https://docs.tkcode.si/shots/Docs/Buttons/IconMorph/images/IncidentHeader.webp)

```xml
<StackPanel Width="600" Spacing="12">

            Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Surface}"
            BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Border}"
            BorderThickness="1"

                               FontSize="16"

                    <TextBlock Text="Checkout latency above 900 ms since 14:05 UTC"
```

### Content guidelines

- **Button name**: the action the press performs, as a verb and an object, in sentence case: "Pause live updates",
  "Turn notifications off", "Collapse affected services". When the state changes, the name changes with it.
- **Icon-only buttons**: the name is the only text a screen reader gets, so it must be complete. Do not name a button
  after its icon ("Play icon").
- **Pairs**: use the same pair for the same action everywhere in the app, so that a play control always means play.

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| Play | Pause live updates (while it runs) |
| Menu | Open incident actions |
| Click to expand | Expand affected services |
| Bell icon | Turn notifications on |
| Like button | Like (then Unlike while liked) |

### Best practices

**Do**

- Put the icon inside a button and give the button the name. The icon is decorative, and only the button can be reached
  and named.
- Bind `IsActive` to the state the view model owns, and let the command perform the action.
- Keep one icon size per row, and match it to the button size.
- Change the button name whenever `IsActive` changes, so the name and the icon never disagree.

**Avoid**

- Using a morph for a one-way action with no second state. A copy action that never reverts needs no morph, and
  `CopyButton` already confirms it.
- Putting a heart or a bell burst on a control that people press many times in a row. The repeated moment becomes noise.
- Setting `IsActive` on both the icon and a binding that writes it back. The state flips twice and the morph stutters.
- Relying on the color change alone. The shape changes too; keep the name, so the state is clear without the color.

### Common questions

**Why does my icon not change its color?** `IconMorph` inherits `Foreground` from its parent, as text does. Set the
color on the button or on the icon, or use the theme's ghost button colors. The liked heart uses `LikeBrush`, not
`Foreground`.

**Why does a click on the icon not toggle it?** The icon is not hit-test visible, so the click goes to the button that
hosts it. Put the click handler or the command on the button.

**Does the bell ring again when I turn it on a second time?** Yes. The ring plays once each time `IsActive` becomes
`True`, and turning it off strikes the bell through.

**How do I show a state that is not one of the eight pairs?** Use `MorphGlyph` with its own path data, or use a plain
icon from `ArcIcons` and change it in code.

## API reference

### IconMorph

Icons that morph between two states instead of swapping: lines rotate and slide into place, outlines interpolate (P16 `PathMorph`), and a few carry a moment of their own (the bell rings, the heart bursts). Every morph rides an interruptible spring, so toggling quickly reverses from wherever the icon is. Drawn in one `Render` on the 24-unit grid. The icon is decorative: put it in a button that carries the name and the pressed or expanded state.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Kind` | `IconMorphKind` | `Menu` | Which pair to draw. |
| `IsActive` | `bool` | `false` | The second state: close, pause, check, moon, turned, notifications on, liked. |
| `IconSize` | `double` | `24` | Rendered size in px (default 24). |
| `StrokeThickness` | `double` | `1.75` | Stroke width on the 24-unit grid (default 1.75); it scales with `IconSize`. |
| `ChevronTurn` | `double` | `180` | Degrees the chevron turns when active: 180 flips down to up, 90 turns right to down. |
| `ChevronPointing` | `IconMorphChevronPointing` | `Down` | Rest direction of a Chevron: Down (default) or Right. |
| `Foreground` | `IBrush?` | `Black` | Brush that paints the glyph, inherited from the parent like text foreground. |
| `LikeBrush` | `IBrush?` | `null` | Color of a liked heart (Arc `--icon-morph-like`; the theme uses Danger). |

Derives from `Control`: every member of `Control` works as well.

`IconMorphKind` lists the eight pairs, in the order of the `Kind` values: `Menu`, `Play`, `Plus`, `Copy`, `Theme`,
`Chevron`, `Bell` and `Heart`. `IconMorphChevronPointing` has two values: `Down` (the default) and `Right`.

## Accessibility

- The icon is hidden from assistive technology. The button around it provides the name.
- Show the state on the button: a toggle for a pressed state, an expanded state for a disclosure, or a changed name.
- Change the name when the meaning changes, such as Play to Pause.
- The icon does not take focus, does not hit-test and does not handle keys. The surrounding button handles them, so a
  keyboard user reaches the control through the button and its focus ring.

## Motion

- Lines rotate and slide into place, and outlines interpolate between their two shapes. Quick toggles reverse from
  wherever the icon currently is.
- A copy icon folds its back sheet away and draws a check. The sun becomes a moon with a crescent cut.
- A bell rings once when turned on, and a heart pops with a ring and sparks each time it is liked.
- Reduced motion completes every morph at once and skips the ring and the burst. Off does the same.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| Menu, Play, Plus, Theme, Chevron | Morphs on an interruptible spring from the current position | Completes at once | Immediate |
| Copy to check | The sheet folds away and the check draws in | Completes at once | Immediate |
| Bell turned on | Rings once, the clapper lagging the bell slightly | No ring | No ring |
| Heart liked | Pops with a ring and sparks | No burst | No burst |

## Related

- `CopyButton` for a copy action with its own confirmation.
- `ThemeSwitcher` for a labelled light and dark switch.
- `Button` as the control that carries the name and state of an icon morph.
- `ExpandingButtonGroup` for icon actions that reveal their labels.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `CopyButton` | The action copies a value and should confirm the copy in place |
| `ThemeSwitcher` | A light and dark choice needs a visible label |
| `Button` | The icon needs a name, a state and a pressed or focus treatment |
| `ExpandingButtonGroup` | Several icon actions should reveal their labels on focus |
| `DropdownMenu` | One trigger opens a list of actions rather than showing a state |
| `ArcIcons` glyphs | The icon never changes state |

# Confirm morph

> A destructive button that morphs into an inline confirmation, a spinner, and a result with undo.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/confirm-morph

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ConfirmMorphPressDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12">
        <arc:ConfirmMorph x:Name="Delete"
                          Label="Delete project"
                          Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Trash2}"
                          HorizontalAlignment="Center"
                          StateChanged="OnStateChanged" />
        <TextBlock x:Name="Log"
                   Text="State: Idle"
                   FontSize="13"
                   TextWrapping="Wrap"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class ConfirmMorphPressDemo : UserControl
{
    public ConfirmMorphPressDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Delete.ConfirmAction = () => Task.Delay(900);
        Delete.UndoAction = () => Task.Delay(600);
    }

    private void OnStateChanged(object? sender, ConfirmMorphStateChangedEventArgs e)
    {
        Log.Text = $"State: {e.NewState}";
    }
}
```

## When to use

`ConfirmMorph` is a button for a destructive or important action that asks first, in place. Pressing it turns the same
pill into a one-line question, then into a spinner while the work runs, then into a result with an optional Undo. It
fits an action that one question explains, so the person answers without leaving the table, card or editor.

- **Deleting the selected items in a list**: a file browser or an order list where the toolbar asks "Delete 3 files?".
  The question names the count, so the person sees exactly what will go without a modal interrupting the selection.
- **Removing a member or revoking access** on a team page: the row action "Remove member" answers in one press, and the
  result ("Removed") confirms the change in the same spot without a toast the person might miss.
- **Discarding an unsaved draft** in an editor: a short countdown gives the person a few seconds to change their mind
  before the discard runs, which suits an action that cannot be recovered.
- **Reversible actions with a grace period**: archiving a project or closing a support ticket, where the result offers
  Undo for a few seconds after the server accepts the change.
- **Calls to a server that can fail**: the pending face shows that work is running, and a failed call turns into an error
  face with Retry, so the person does not have to find the control again.

## When not to use

- **A consequence that needs several lines of explanation or a typed name**, such as deleting an account or a production
  database: use `Dialog`, which can hold the detail, a list of what will be lost and a text field.
- **A safe asynchronous submit with no question**: use `ActionButton`, which shows its pending and success states without
  asking first.
- **An action that must never fire on a tap**, such as a factory reset in a device console: use `HoldToConfirm` from
  Gestures, a dedicated hold control for that job.
- **A list of commands with no single default action**, such as Duplicate, Move, Export and Delete for one row: use
  `DropdownMenu` from Menus.
- **A decision that must block the rest of the page**, such as unsaved changes before navigation: use `Dialog`. The
  morph does not block input elsewhere; an outside press answers the question no.

## Usage

Set `Label` to the resting text. The question is `Prompt`, or the label with a question mark when `Prompt` is not set.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:ConfirmMorph Label="Delete project" Prompt="Delete this project?" />
</UserControl>
```

`ConfirmMorph` derives from Avalonia's `TemplatedControl`, not from `Button`. Its template declares every face (the
resting pill, the question, the countdown, the spinner, the result and the error) and the control switches between them
as its `State` changes. The resting pill and the answer buttons are ordinary Avalonia buttons inside the template, so
they take focus and respond to Enter and Space like any other button. The control itself is focusable but is not a tab
stop: Tab moves between the buttons of the face that is showing.

The state machine has five values, `Idle`, `Confirming`, `Pending`, `Done` and `Error`. `State` reads and writes that
value and is two-way by default, so a view model can observe the flow, start it or force a face without running any
action.

### Anatomy

1. **Resting pill** (`Label`, `Icon`): a 36 px tall pill on the raised surface color with the label in the small text
   size and medium weight. `Icon` is an optional 16 px glyph before the label. The pill has 14 px of padding on the left
   and 16 px on the right. Hover, press and keyboard focus add a tint of the foreground color at 5%, 9% and 6%.
2. **Question** (`Prompt`): the question text, up to 256 px wide, with 12 px of padding on the left and 8 px on the right.
3. **Cancel** (`CancelLabel`): a secondary answer in the secondary text color. Its hover, press and focus fills are the
   foreground color at 7%, 11% and 8%.
4. **Confirm** (`ConfirmLabel`, `Tone`): the answer that runs the action. The danger tone uses the danger color at 13%
   at rest, 18% on hover and 22% when pressed, with the danger color for the text. The neutral tone uses the accent fill
   with the accent foreground.
5. **Countdown** (`CountdownSeconds`, `CountdownLabel`): a ring that drains over the countdown, the remaining seconds
   and its own Cancel button.
6. **Pending** (`PendingLabel`, `UndoingLabel`): a spinner and a label while `ConfirmAction` runs. `UndoingLabel` shows
   while `UndoAction` runs.
7. **Result** (`DoneLabel`, `UndoLabel`): a check mark that draws itself, the done label and an Undo button when
   `UndoAction` is set.
8. **Error** (`ErrorLabel`, `RetryLabel`): the error label in the danger color and a Retry button.

The answer buttons are 28 px tall, which is the pill height less 8 px, so every face fits inside the pill. Each face
keeps its natural width; only the pill's width animates between them.

### Actions and undo

`ConfirmAction` runs when the question is answered. A task that has not completed keeps the pending face on screen. A
task that throws moves the control to the error face, and Retry runs `ConfirmAction` again. When the task completes, the
result face shows `DoneLabel`.

`UndoAction` adds Undo to the result. Pressing Undo runs it with the pending face showing `UndoingLabel`, and the control
returns to rest when it finishes. Without `UndoAction` the result has no Undo button.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ConfirmMorphErrorAndRetryDemo">
    <arc:ConfirmMorph x:Name="Delete"
                      Label="Delete 3 files"
                      Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Trash2}"
                      Prompt="Delete 3 files?"
                      HorizontalAlignment="Center" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class ConfirmMorphErrorAndRetryDemo : UserControl
{
    private int _attempts;

    public ConfirmMorphErrorAndRetryDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        // Every other attempt fails, so the error face and Retry show up.
        Delete.ConfirmAction = async () =>
        {
            await Task.Delay(800);
            if (++_attempts % 2 == 1)
            {
                throw new InvalidOperationException("Offline");
            }
        };
    }
}
```

```csharp
delete.ConfirmAction = () => documentService.DeleteAsync(selected);
delete.UndoAction = () => documentService.RestoreAsync(selected);
```

The sample above fails every other attempt, so the error face and Retry appear during the demo. In production the
task should throw only for failures the person can retry, such as a network error. A validation error that the person
must fix is better shown in the page than behind a Retry button.

### Choosing a confirm mode

`ConfirmMode` sets how the question is answered. The default is `Press`.

| Mode | How the action is answered | Choose it when |
|---|---|---|
| `Press` (default) | One press on Confirm, or Enter from anywhere in the question | The question is clear and the result can be undone or the action is cheap to repeat |
| `Hold` | Confirm is held until its fill completes; `HoldDuration` sets the time (1 second by default) | A tap is too easy to trigger by accident, such as removing a member from a shared workspace |
| `Countdown` | Confirm starts a `CountdownSeconds` countdown (3 seconds by default) that Cancel or Escape can stop | The person may need a last chance after deciding, such as discarding a draft they just closed |

### Hold mode

In `Hold` mode, a pointer press on Confirm, or Enter or Space while Confirm has focus, fills the Confirm button from its
leading edge. The action runs when the fill completes. Letting go early springs the fill back to empty and announces
that a longer hold is needed. The help text of Confirm is "Press and hold".

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ConfirmMorphHoldDemo">
    <arc:ConfirmMorph x:Name="Remove"
                      Label="Remove member"
                      ConfirmLabel="Remove"
                      PendingLabel="Removing"
                      DoneLabel="Removed"
                      ConfirmMode="Hold"
                      HorizontalAlignment="Center" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class ConfirmMorphHoldDemo : UserControl
{
    public ConfirmMorphHoldDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Remove.ConfirmAction = () => Task.Delay(700);
    }
}
```

```xml
<arc:ConfirmMorph Label="Remove member"
                  ConfirmLabel="Remove"
                  ConfirmMode="Hold"
                  HoldDuration="00:00:01" />
```

### Countdown mode

In `Countdown` mode, answering Confirm starts the countdown rather than the action. The ring drains and the seconds
count down. The action runs when the countdown reaches zero, or at once when Enter is pressed during the countdown.
Cancel, the Escape key or an outside press stops it, and the action does not run.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ConfirmMorphCountdownDemo">
    <arc:ConfirmMorph x:Name="Discard"
                      Label="Discard draft"
                      ConfirmLabel="Discard"
                      PendingLabel="Discarding"
                      DoneLabel="Discarded"
                      ConfirmMode="Countdown"
                      HorizontalAlignment="Center" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class ConfirmMorphCountdownDemo : UserControl
{
    public ConfirmMorphCountdownDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Discard.UndoAction = () => Task.Delay(500);
    }
}
```

```xml
<arc:ConfirmMorph Label="Discard draft"
                  ConfirmLabel="Discard"
                  ConfirmMode="Countdown"
                  CountdownSeconds="3" />
```

`CountdownLabel` sets the text before the seconds. When it is not set, the control uses the pending label followed by
"in".

### Labels and tone

The eight text properties (`ConfirmLabel`, `CancelLabel`, `PendingLabel`, `DoneLabel`, `ErrorLabel`, `RetryLabel`,
`UndoLabel` and `UndoingLabel`) set the words of each face. Their defaults are "Delete", "Cancel", "Deleting", "Deleted",
"Couldn’t finish", "Retry", "Undo" and "Restoring", so a control with no text properties set still reads as a delete
action. Set every one of them that the action changes, because the defaults are English and describe deletion.

`Tone="Neutral"` colors the confirm answer with the accent for an important action that can be reversed. The default
`Danger` suits destructive actions.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ConfirmMorphNeutralToneDemo">
    <arc:ConfirmMorph x:Name="Revoke"
                      Label="Revoke access"
                      Prompt="Revoke 3 keys?"
                      ConfirmLabel="Revoke"
                      PendingLabel="Revoking"
                      DoneLabel="Revoked"
                      Tone="Neutral"
                      HorizontalAlignment="Center" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class ConfirmMorphNeutralToneDemo : UserControl
{
    public ConfirmMorphNeutralToneDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Revoke.ConfirmAction = () => Task.Delay(800);
    }
}
```

### Controlled state and timeouts

`State` is two-way. Setting it from code moves the control to that face without running an action, so a view model can
restore the result of an earlier session or show the pending face while its own request is in flight. `StateChanged`
reports each move with `OldState` and `NewState`, and `Cancelled` is raised when the question or the countdown is
cancelled.

`ConfirmTimeout` returns an unanswered question to rest (6 seconds by default), and `ResultTimeout` removes a result
(5 seconds by default). A pointer resting on the control holds both timers, and so does a minimized window, so the
person is never hurried while they are looking at the control. Set either timeout to zero to turn it off.

```csharp
confirm.StateChanged += (_, e) => log.Text = $"State: {e.NewState}";
confirm.Cancelled += (_, _) => log.Text = "Cancelled";
confirm.State = ConfirmMorphState.Idle;
```

Setting `State` to `Pending` or `Done` from code shows that face without running `ConfirmAction` or `UndoAction`. Calling
`Ask()` opens the question as a press on the resting button would, and `Cancel()` closes an open question or countdown.
`Ask()` does nothing unless the control is in `Idle` and enabled.

### Focus and dismissal

The control moves focus with the morph so that the keyboard always has a sensible place. Confirm receives focus when the
question opens, the control itself receives focus while a countdown or the pending work is running, Undo or Retry
receives focus on the result or the error, and the resting pill receives focus again when the control returns to rest.

An open question is dismissed by:

- Cancel, or the Escape key;
- a press outside the control, which answers the question no (set `IsOutsidePressCancelEnabled` to `False` to keep
  the question open on an outside press);
- `ConfirmTimeout`, when the person does not answer.

`ResultTimeout` also returns a result to rest when the person does not act on it.

### Disabled

The resting pill drops its shadow when `IsEnabled` is `False`, and `Ask()` ignores the request. Say why nearby, in the
row's description.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ConfirmMorphDisabledDemo">
    <arc:ConfirmMorph Label="Delete project"
                      Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Trash2}"
                      IsEnabled="False"
                      HorizontalAlignment="Center" />
</UserControl>
```

### Example: project danger zone

A settings page that holds two actions with different weight. "Archive project" is reversible, so it uses the neutral
tone, and its question is open in the markup below so the state is visible. "Delete project" is permanent, so it keeps
the danger tone and rests as a pill until the person asks for it. Each row explains the consequence in one sentence
next to the control, so the question itself can stay short.

![A danger zone with an open archive question and a resting delete button](https://docs.tkcode.si/shots/Docs/Buttons/ConfirmMorph/images/DangerZone.webp)

```xml
<StackPanel Width="640" Spacing="16">

               FontSize="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TypeLG}"
               FontWeight="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource WeightMedium}"
               Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
    <Border Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Surface}"
            BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Border}"
            BorderThickness="1"
            CornerRadius="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource RadiusPanel}"
            Padding="20">
        <StackPanel Spacing="20">
            <Grid ColumnDefinitions="*,Auto">
                <StackPanel Grid.Column="0" Spacing="4" VerticalAlignment="Center">
                    <TextBlock Text="Archive Acme Analytics"
                               FontWeight="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource WeightMedium}"
                               Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
                    <TextBlock Text="Archived projects can be restored for 30 days."
                               TextWrapping="Wrap"

                </StackPanel>

                               TextWrapping="Wrap"
```

### Binding to a view model

With CommunityToolkit.Mvvm, the view model owns the state of the action and the work it runs. `ConfirmAction` and
`UndoAction` are `Func<Task>` properties, so the view model exposes them as properties of that type and binds them. The
`State` value is bound two-way, so the view model can also move the control.

```csharp
public interface IProjectService
{
    Task ArchiveAsync(string projectId);

    Task RestoreAsync(string projectId);

    Task DeleteAsync(string projectId);
}

public partial class ProjectDangerViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    private readonly IProjectService _projects;

    public ProjectDangerViewModel(IProjectService projects)
    {
        _projects = projects;
    }

    [ObservableProperty]
    private ConfirmMorphState _archiveState = ConfirmMorphState.Idle;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private string _projectName = "Acme Analytics";

    public Func<Task> ArchiveAction => () => _projects.ArchiveAsync(ProjectId);

    public Func<Task> UndoArchiveAction => () => _projects.RestoreAsync(ProjectId);

    public Func<Task> DeleteAction => () => _projects.DeleteAsync(ProjectId);

    public string ProjectId { get; } = "prj_2026_0412";
}
```

```xml
<StackPanel Spacing="12">
    <arc:ConfirmMorph Label="Archive project"
                      Prompt="Archive this project?"
                      ConfirmLabel="Archive"
                      Tone="Neutral"
                      State="{Binding ArchiveState, Mode=TwoWay}"
                      ConfirmAction="{Binding ArchiveAction}"
                      UndoAction="{Binding UndoArchiveAction}" />
    <arc:ConfirmMorph Label="Delete project"
                      Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Trash2}"
                      ConfirmAction="{Binding DeleteAction}" />
</StackPanel>
```

- `State` is two-way and is the only property that needs `Mode=TwoWay`, which is already its default. Read it to keep
  other controls in step, such as disabling the row's other actions while an archive runs.
- `ConfirmAction` and `UndoAction` are one-way: the view model supplies the work, and the control calls it.
- The event `StateChanged` is useful for logging, but the view model should not need it when `State` is bound.
- Compiled bindings need `x:DataType` on the view; the example leaves it out for brevity.

### Content guidelines

- **Label**: a verb and its object in sentence case, such as "Delete project" or "Archive project". The label is what the
  person sees before they decide, so it must say what the action does.
- **Prompt**: the question with the count or the name in it, ending with a question mark: "Delete 3 files?" A prompt that
  names the object tells the person what they are answering.
- **Confirm label**: the verb alone, "Delete", "Archive", "Revoke". It answers the question with the same word the label
  uses, so "Yes" never appears.
- **Done label**: the past tense of the verb, "Deleted", "Archived". Keep it short so the result fits the pill.
- **Error label**: say that the action did not finish, not what went wrong in technical terms. The Retry button handles
  the next step.

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| Yes | Delete |
| Are you sure you want to delete this item? | Delete 3 files? |
| Oops, something went wrong! | Couldn’t finish |
| Done! | Deleted |
| Undo last action | Undo |

### Best practices

**Do**

- Name the object in the label or the prompt, so the question is answered in context: "Delete 3 files?" needs no reading
  of the page around it.
- Pick `Tone="Neutral"` only for reversible actions. Keep the danger tone for anything the person cannot take back, so
  the color keeps its meaning.
- Offer `UndoAction` when the server can restore the object for a while. The result stays long enough to press Undo
  before `ResultTimeout` returns the control to rest.
- Set every text property the action needs. The defaults describe deletion, and a generic "Deleting" label on an
  archive action reads as a mistake.
- Use `Countdown` or `Hold` for the actions that are costly to repeat, and `Press` for the rest. One mode per screen
  keeps the answers consistent.

**Avoid**

- Using the control for consequences that need several lines of explanation or a typed name. The question face is one
  line; put the detail in a `Dialog` instead.
- Long prompts. The question face is sized for one short line, and the prompt has a 256 px maximum width; keep it to a
  question about the object.
- Setting `ConfirmTimeout` to a very short time for a question the person must read. Six seconds is enough for a
  glance; much less makes the question vanish before it is read.
- Turning off `IsOutsidePressCancelEnabled` by default. An outside press that does nothing feels like a stuck control;
  keep the default unless the question must stay open while the person works elsewhere.
- Running a long action in `ConfirmAction` without a pending label. The spinner and the label are the only signal that
  work is in progress.

### Common questions

**Why does the Enter key that opened the question not answer it at once?** A press in the first 280 milliseconds after
the question opens is ignored, and so is the auto-repeat of Enter. This stops a double click or a held key from
answering a question the person has not read.

**Does a failed action leave the control in a broken state?** No. A `ConfirmAction` task that throws moves the control
to `Error`, which shows `ErrorLabel` and a Retry button. Retry runs `ConfirmAction` again, and Escape returns the control
to rest without running it.

**How do I open the question from a keyboard shortcut or from code?** Call `Ask()`. It opens the question in the same way
a press on the resting pill does, and it is ignored unless the control is in `Idle` and enabled.

**How do I know when the action has finished?** Watch `State` for `Done`, or handle `StateChanged`. The control moves to
`Done` after `ConfirmAction` completes and to `Error` when it throws, so a view model can refresh its list in either
case.

## API reference

### ConfirmMorph

A button for destructive or important actions that asks in place: pressing it morphs the same pill into an inline question with Cancel and Confirm, then into a spinner, then into a result with Undo. Only the pill's width moves (growing on the morph spring, shrinking on smooth, P5 / P9); each face sits at its natural width and its parts clear a small blur in reading order (P20) while the old face fades (P2). Unanswered questions and results time out on a pausable timer (P22, held while the pointer rests on the control), Escape and an outside press return it to rest, and focus follows the morph. Answer with a press, a hold, or a press followed by a short countdown.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Label` | `string` | `"Delete project"` | The resting label, such as "Delete project". |
| `Icon` | `Geometry?` | `null` | A plain 16px glyph before the resting label. |
| `Prompt` | `string?` | `null` | The question, such as "Delete 3 files?"; null uses the label with a question mark. |
| `ConfirmLabel` | `string` | `"Delete"` | Label of the confirm button (default "Delete"). |
| `CancelLabel` | `string` | `"Cancel"` | Label of the cancel button (default "Cancel"). |
| `PendingLabel` | `string` | `"Deleting"` | Shown beside the spinner while `ConfirmAction` runs. |
| `DoneLabel` | `string` | `"Deleted"` | Label shown after the action succeeds (default "Deleted"). |
| `ErrorLabel` | `string` | `"Couldn’t finish"` | Label shown when the action fails (default "Couldn’t finish"). |
| `RetryLabel` | `string` | `"Retry"` | Label of the retry button shown after a failure (default "Retry"). |
| `UndoLabel` | `string` | `"Undo"` | Label of the undo action (default "Undo"). |
| `UndoingLabel` | `string` | `"Restoring"` | Shown beside the spinner while `UndoAction` runs. |
| `CountdownLabel` | `string?` | `null` | Text before the seconds in countdown mode; null uses the pending label followed by "in". |
| `Tone` | `ConfirmMorphTone` | `Danger` | Danger (default) colors the confirm answer for destructive actions; Neutral uses the accent. |
| `ConfirmMode` | `ConfirmMorphMode` | `Press` | How the question is answered: Press (default), Hold or Countdown. |
| `HoldDuration` | `TimeSpan` | `00:00:01` | How long Confirm must be held in `Hold` (default 1s). |
| `CountdownSeconds` | `int` | `3` | Seconds counted down in `Countdown` (default 3). |
| `ConfirmAction` | `Func<Task>?` | `null` | Runs on confirm. A task that has not completed shows the pending face; a fault shows the error face with Retry. |
| `UndoAction` | `Func<Task>?` | `null` | Offering it adds Undo to the result. |
| `State` | `ConfirmMorphState` | `Idle` | The face shown (two-way). Setting it from outside moves the control without running actions. |
| `ConfirmTimeout` | `TimeSpan` | `00:00:06` | Time before an unanswered question returns to rest; the pointer resting on the control holds it. Zero turns it off. |
| `ResultTimeout` | `TimeSpan` | `00:00:05` | Time a result stays before returning to rest; the pointer resting on the control holds it. Zero turns it off. |
| `IsOutsidePressCancelEnabled` | `bool` | `true` | A press outside the control cancels an open question (default true). |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `StateChanged` | `ConfirmMorphStateChangedEventArgs` | Raised when the state changes; the argument carries the old and new state. |
| `Cancelled` | `RoutedEventArgs` | Raised when a question or countdown is cancelled (Cancel, Escape, outside press, timeout). |

Pseudo-classes: `:counting`, `:has-undo`, `:idle`, `:confirming`, `:pending`, `:done`, `:error`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

## Accessibility

- The question is a group named by its prompt. The resting button keeps the name of its label.
- The focus follows the morph: Confirm when the question opens, the control while a countdown or the pending work is
  running, Undo or Retry on the result, and the resting pill at rest.
- Presses in the first 280 milliseconds after the question opens are ignored, so a double click or a held Enter does not
  answer it by accident.
- In `Hold` mode the help text is "Press and hold". Letting go early announces that a longer hold is needed.
- The prompt, the pending and the result words, and "Undo is available" are announced politely through a status region.
- Enter and Space press the button on the current face. Escape cancels the question or countdown, and returns a result
  or an error to rest.
- Keyboard focus shows as a tint of the button's background (6% to 20%, by tone and state), not as a ring.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Enter` / `Space` on the resting pill | Opens the question |
| `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` | Moves between the buttons of the face that is showing, such as Cancel and Confirm |
| `Enter` (`Press` mode) | Answers yes from anywhere in the question, except while Cancel has focus |
| `Enter` / `Space` on Confirm (`Hold` mode) | Fills Confirm while held; the action runs when the fill completes |
| `Enter` / `Space` on Confirm (`Countdown` mode) | Starts the countdown |
| `Enter` during a countdown | Runs the action now |
| `Enter` / `Space` on Cancel, Undo or Retry | Presses that button |
| `Escape` | Cancels the question or the countdown; returns a result or an error to rest |

## Motion

- Only the width of the pill changes. It grows on a spring and shrinks more smoothly, and the text does not scale.
- Each new face's parts clear a small blur in reading order, and the old face fades out in place.
- The result check draws itself. The countdown ring drains and its digits roll, and the pending spinner turns.
- In `Hold` mode a filled copy of the danger color reveals from the left as Confirm is held. Letting go early springs it back.
- Reduced motion removes the width spring and the blur, crossfades the faces and slows the spinner. The hold fill and the
  countdown ring still show progress. Off switches the faces at once.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| Question opens or closes | The pill width grows on a spring and shrinks smoothly | No width spring; the faces crossfade | Immediate |
| Face changes | Parts clear a small blur in reading order, 35 ms apart; the old face fades out over 120 ms | Crossfade | Immediate |
| Result | The check mark draws itself | The check appears without drawing | Immediate |
| Countdown | The ring drains and the seconds roll | The ring still drains | Immediate |
| Pending | The spinner turns | The spinner turns more slowly | Immediate |
| Hold fill | The fill reveals from the leading edge and springs back on early release | The fill still shows progress | Immediate |

## Related

- `Dialog` for a consequence that needs more explanation or a typed name.
- `ActionButton` for an asynchronous submit with no question.
- `HoldToConfirm` for an action that must never fire on a tap.
- `DropdownMenu` for a list of commands without one default action.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `Dialog` | The consequence needs several lines, a list of affected items or a typed name |
| `ActionButton` | The action is safe and asynchronous, and no question should come first |
| `HoldToConfirm` (Gestures) | A single hold is the whole interaction and the action must never fire on a tap |
| `DropdownMenu` (Menus) | The row or toolbar offers several commands and none is the default |
| `CopyButton` | The action copies a value to the clipboard and shows the result in place |
| `ButtonGroup` | Several buttons form one toolbar and none of them needs its own question |

---

# Theme switcher

> Four smooth ways to move between light and dark appearance.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/theme-switch

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"

                       FontSize="12"

            <WrapPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center" ItemSpacing="12" LineSpacing="12">

        </StackPanel>
        <StackPanel Spacing="8">

                <arc:ThemeSwitcher Variant="Rise" IsIconOnly="True" />
```
