## When to use

A theme switch is a single control in the chrome of a product: a header, a toolbar or the top bar of a desktop tool.
A person flips the whole window between light and dark in one press. `ThemeSwitcher` names the next appearance for
assistive technology, shows the icon of the current one, and plays a page transition whose shape matches the layout.
Use it when the change of appearance should feel deliberate, not abrupt.

- **Switching the console header in an admin product**: a switch sits beside the workspace menu and the notification
  bell in the header of an operations console. The icon-only form keeps the header quiet, and the control stays in the
  same corner on every page.
- **Moving between light and dark during a long analytics session**: a finance team reviews a revenue dashboard late in
  the day and flips the window to dark. The `Rise` variant is the quietest, so the chart colours settle without a
  distracting sweep across the data.
- **Previewing an appearance in a showcase or release page**: a design team demonstrating a new product release uses
  `Eclipse`, whose disc crosses the page, so the audience sees the change happen.
- **Centred top bars in a docs site or a marketing landing page**: a centred layout has no fixed corner for the change
  to start from. `Split` opens from a centre seam and does not depend on where the button sits.
- **Desktop tools that remember the appearance per workspace**: an internal CRM or a developer tool stores the choice
  in its settings and applies it to every window. The handler receives the request, so the app decides what to apply.

## When not to use

- **A theme choice among light, dark and system, or a choice that sits in an account menu**: use `UserMenu`. A menu
  keeps the three choices out of the header when they are not needed every day.
- **A choice that stays visible in a settings page**: use `SegmentedControl` for light, dark and system as named
  options that stay selected, or `RadioCards` when each option needs a description.
- **A plain action that does not change the theme**, such as Export report or Invite member: use `Button`.
- **A single on or off setting**, such as Compact sidebar or Show values on charts: use `Switch`, which reports a
  setting rather than a change of the whole window.
- **Another named choice, such as language, density or accent colour**: use `Select` or `SegmentedControl`.
  `ThemeSwitcher` only changes between light and dark.
- **Two states of an icon that is not the theme**, such as play and pause or menu and close: use `IconMorph`, the
  two-state icon button.

## Usage

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:ThemeSwitcher Variant="Reveal" />
</UserControl>
```

`ThemeSwitcher` derives from Avalonia's `TemplatedControl`, and its template contains an Arc `Button` in the secondary
variant at the small size. The press scale, the hover and the focus ring therefore come from the Arc button theme, the
same as on any other Arc button. The switcher adds the appearance logic on top: it tracks the window's theme variant,
swaps the sun and the moon, raises a request before the theme changes, and exposes the button to assistive technology as
a toggle. Without an `Appearance`, it follows the actual theme variant of the window.

### Anatomy

1. **Button frame** (the inner Arc button): a secondary button at the small size, 36 px high. In the text form, hovering
   darkens the border to the strong border color. The icon-only form is a 38 by 38 px square with a 12 px corner radius
   and no padding; its hover removes the shadow, so the square answers with the surface change only.
2. **Icon** (the icon part): the sun for the light appearance and the moon for the dark one. The glyph is 16 px with a
   1.75 px stroke, drawn in an 18 px icon area inside a 20 px square that carries the icon nudge of the variant.
3. **Gap** (`IconTextGap`): 8 px between the icon and the text.
4. **Text** (`Text`): the visible label. It defaults to "Switch theme", takes the button's text colour and
   is hidden when `IsIconOnly` is `True`.

The switcher aligns itself to the left and centres itself vertically, so it sits at the start of a toolbar without
extra layout. Put it in a `StackPanel` or a `DockPanel` and let the parent place it.

### Variants

`Variant` picks the page transition. The same value also sets the direction of the icon nudge in dark mode, so the icon
and the reveal move the same way. The transition plays when the switcher applies a change itself; the variant does not
change the appearance.

| Variant | The new appearance | Choose it when |
|---|---|---|
| `Reveal` (default) | Grows as a circle from the button to the farthest corner of the window | The switch sits in a corner, so the reveal starts where the person pressed |
| `Eclipse` | A disc as wide as the window's diagonal enters from the right and settles over the page | Showcase pages, presentations and release pages where the change itself is the point |
| `Split` | A slim seam at the centre widens to the full window | Centred layouts, where the button position gives no sense of direction |
| `Rise` | Rises from the bottom edge to the top | Dense work screens, where the quietest change suits; it is the choice for an icon-only header |

```xml
<arc:ThemeSwitcher Variant="Eclipse" />
<arc:ThemeSwitcher Variant="Split" />
<arc:ThemeSwitcher Variant="Rise" IsIconOnly="True" />
```

Pick one variant for each product and keep it on every page. A person who learns the reveal from the header should see
the same motion when the switch is used elsewhere. Use `Reveal` when the switch is in a corner and the reveal can start
from it; choose `Split` when the switch is centred, because a reveal from the middle of a centred bar would look
arbitrary.

### Icon only and text

`IsIconOnly` shows a 38 by 38 square button and hides `Text`. Use it in a dense toolbar or a header where the icon is
enough and the surrounding controls are icons too. Use the text form, with `Text="Appearance"` or the default, when the
switch sits among labelled actions or when a person may not read the sun and moon as theme controls.

```xml
<arc:ThemeSwitcher Text="Appearance" Label="Switch appearance" />
```

`Label` sets the accessible name. Without a `Label`, the switcher names the next appearance itself ("Switch to dark
mode" while light, "Switch to light mode" while dark). A fixed `Label` replaces that name in both appearances, so it no
longer says which appearance the next press switches to. Set `Label` only when the name must not change, and keep it
short and specific.

`Text` is never used as the accessible name. The switcher sets the name of its button itself, so the visible text is
for people who see the control, not for the name that assistive technology reads.

### Handling the request

`ThemeChangeRequested` is raised before the theme changes, on every press and on `Toggle()`. Its arguments give the
appearance to switch to (`Next`), the variant (`Variant`), the button that was pressed (`Trigger`) and the centre of that
button in its top level's coordinates (`Origin`), which is the start of a reveal. Set `Handled` to apply the theme
yourself. The switcher then leaves the theme alone, and it also leaves `Appearance` alone: if your handler does not set
it, the icon and the name stay as they were.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ThemeSwitcherHandledByAppDemo">
    <StackPanel Orientation="Horizontal" Spacing="12">
        <arc:ThemeSwitcher x:Name="Switcher"
                           Appearance="Light"
                           Variant="Rise"
                           ThemeChangeRequested="OnThemeChangeRequested" />
        <TextBlock x:Name="Status"
                   Text="Next: Dark"
                   FontSize="13"
                   TextWrapping="Wrap"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class ThemeSwitcherHandledByAppDemo : UserControl
{
    public ThemeSwitcherHandledByAppDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
    }

    // Controlled: the app handles the request itself; here it only flips a local appearance.
    private void OnThemeChangeRequested(object? sender, ThemeSwitcherChangeRequestedEventArgs e)
    {
        e.Handled = true;
        Switcher.Appearance = e.Next;
        Status.Text = $"Requested {e.Next} ({e.Variant}) from {e.Origin.X:0},{e.Origin.Y:0}; the app decides what to apply.";
    }
}
```

```csharp
switcher.ThemeChangeRequested += (_, e) =>
{
    e.Handled = true;
    switcher.Appearance = e.Next;
    ApplyAppearance(e.Next);
};
```

Handle the request when the app owns the appearance, for example when the choice is saved per user, applied to several
windows, or applied after a server call. Handle it on the switcher or on a parent: the event bubbles, so a single handler
on a window can serve every switcher in it. When the handler needs the same page transition as the built-in apply, pass
the trigger, the variant and your apply step to `RunTransitionAsync`:

```csharp
switcher.ThemeChangeRequested += async (_, e) =>
{
    e.Handled = true;
    await ThemeSwitcher.RunTransitionAsync(e.Trigger, e.Variant,
        () => _viewModel.ApplyAsync(e.Next));
};
```

`RunTransitionAsync` snapshots the window, runs your apply step underneath it and reveals the new appearance by the
variant. Under reduced motion, with motion off, or when the trigger has no overlay layer, it runs the apply step and
returns without the transition.

### Controlled appearance

`Appearance` is the appearance shown: the icon, the pressed state and the accessible name. It is a nullable
`ThemeSwitcherAppearance`, with `Light` and `Dark` as its values, and it is a two-way binding by default. Set it from
code to keep the switcher in step with the app. `EffectiveAppearance` returns the appearance in effect, whether it comes
from `Appearance` or from the window.

- When `Appearance` is `null` (the default), the switcher follows the window's actual theme variant and updates when
  that changes.
- When `Appearance` has a value, the switcher shows that value and stops following the window. Set it back to `null` to
  resume following.
- Setting `Appearance` changes the icon and the name, but it does not play the page transition. The transition runs only
  when the switcher applies a change itself, from a press or from `Toggle()`.

```xml
<arc:ThemeSwitcher Appearance="Light" Variant="Rise" />
```

```csharp
switcher.Toggle();
```

`Toggle()` switches to the other appearance as a press would: it raises `ThemeChangeRequested` and, unless the request is
handled, applies the change. Use it for a keyboard shortcut in the app, such as a command in a command palette.

### Binding to a view model

In an MVVM app the view model owns the appearance and the apply step; the switcher only shows the value and reports the
request. The following view model uses CommunityToolkit.Mvvm and an app-side settings store. `ApplyAsync` is the app's
own code that changes the theme of the application.

```csharp
public partial class AppearanceViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    private readonly IAppearanceStore _store;
    private readonly IThemeService _themes;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private ThemeSwitcherAppearance? _appearance;

    public AppearanceViewModel(IAppearanceStore store, IThemeService themes)
    {
        _store = store;
        _themes = themes;
        _appearance = store.Load();
    }

    public async Task ApplyAsync(ThemeSwitcherAppearance next)
    {
        await _themes.ApplyAsync(next == ThemeSwitcherAppearance.Dark);
        Appearance = next;
        await _store.SaveAsync(next);
    }
}
```

```xml
<arc:ThemeSwitcher x:Name="ThemeSwitch"
                   Appearance="{Binding Appearance}"
                   Variant="Rise" />
```

```csharp
public partial class ShellView : UserControl
{
    public ShellView()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        ThemeSwitch.ThemeChangeRequested += OnThemeChangeRequested;
    }

    private async void OnThemeChangeRequested(object? sender, ThemeSwitcherChangeRequestedEventArgs e)
    {
        e.Handled = true;
        await ThemeSwitcher.RunTransitionAsync(e.Trigger, e.Variant,
            () => _viewModel.ApplyAsync(e.Next));
    }
}
```

- `Appearance` is two-way: the switcher writes its value into the view model when the appearance changes, and the view
  model's value reaches the switcher when the app sets it, for example at startup when the stored choice loads.
- The switcher has no command. The request goes through the event, because the event carries the trigger and the origin
  that the transition needs. Wire it in code-behind, as shown, and let the handler call the view model.
- Compiled bindings need `x:DataType` on the view (the examples here leave it out for brevity).

### Persisting the choice

Load the stored value before the first frame or right after it, and assign it to the view model. The first appearance set
does not animate, and a value that lands during the first frames does not play the icon swap either, so the switcher
starts in the right state without a flash. Save the value in `ApplyAsync` after the theme has changed, so a failed apply
does not store an appearance the window never showed.

### Using motion with restraint

Use the page transition for a change the whole window makes. It shows the person that the theme changed everywhere, which
a fast recolour can miss. Do not use it for a change that happens often: a person who flips the theme several times in a
minute is served better by a quiet `Rise` than by an eclipse each time. The transition captures the whole window at its
render scale, so its cost grows with the window size and the display density. Keep the variant quiet in large windows.

Reduced motion removes the page transition and the icon nudge, and the icon fades in at once. Off switches the theme
without any of these effects.

### Example: analytics console header

A header of an operations console with the product name and the workspace, a ghost button for an export and an
icon-only switch at the end. The switch follows the window's theme because it has no `Appearance`; the header does not
decide the appearance, and the app does. The icon-only `Rise` variant keeps the header quiet, and the export button is a
ghost so it does not compete with the content below. The switch sits at the end of the row, where a person looks for
window-level controls.

![A console header with an export ghost button and an icon-only theme switch](https://docs.tkcode.si/shots/Docs/Buttons/ThemeSwitcher/images/ConsoleHeader.webp)

```xml
<Border Width="640"
        Padding="16,12"
        CornerRadius="12"
        Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Surface}"
        BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource BorderSubtle}"
        BorderThickness="1">
    <DockPanel LastChildFill="False">
        <StackPanel DockPanel.Dock="Left" Spacing="2">
            <TextBlock Text="Acme Analytics"
                       FontSize="15"
                       FontWeight="SemiBold" />
            <TextBlock Text="Workspace: Northwind EMEA"
                       FontSize="12"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
        </StackPanel>
        <StackPanel DockPanel.Dock="Right"
                    Orientation="Horizontal"
                    Spacing="8"
                    VerticalAlignment="Center">
            <arc:Button Content="Export" Variant="Ghost" />
            <arc:ThemeSwitcher Variant="Rise" IsIconOnly="True" />
        </StackPanel>
    </DockPanel>
</Border>
```

### Content guidelines

- **Default name and text**: keep the default text "Switch theme" for a header, and the default accessible name, which
  states the next appearance. Override the text with a short noun, such as "Appearance", when the switch sits in a row of
  labelled settings.
- **Label**: when you set it, name the action and the appearance it switches to: "Switch to dark mode". Leave out words
  such as "toggle" or "button" that the screen reader already announces.
- **Text**: a verb and an object or a noun phrase in sentence case, with no punctuation. Do not write the current state
  in the text, because the icon already shows it.
- **Icon only**: use the icon-only form only where the surrounding controls are icons too. A lone sun and moon among
  labelled buttons is easy to miss.

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| Dark | Switch to dark mode |
| Change look | Switch appearance |
| Theme toggle (click) | Switch theme |
| Night mode for the app | Switch to dark mode |
| Mode | Switch to light mode |

### Best practices

**Do**

- Place the switch in the same spot of the header on every page. A person who finds it once expects it in the same place,
  so the switch stays discoverable.
- Handle `ThemeChangeRequested` when the app saves the choice, applies it to several windows or applies it after a call
  to a server. The handler is the one place that sees the next appearance, the variant and the origin together.
- Keep one variant for the whole product. The motion becomes a signature of the product only when it repeats.
- Leave `Label` unset unless the name must stay fixed. The default name tells a screen reader which appearance the next
  press switches to, and a fixed name does not.

**Avoid**

- `Eclipse` or `Reveal` in a dense dashboard. A full-window sweep competes with the chart redraws the same instant; the
  quieter `Rise` keeps the attention on the data.
- Setting `Appearance` from code to fake a change of theme. Setting it moves the icon and the name only, so the window
  stays in the old appearance. Apply the theme in the handler, then set the value.
- A fixed `Label` such as "Switch appearance" in both states. The name stops telling the person which appearance the next
  press switches to.
- Putting the switch in a menu next to system choices when the header has room. A menu hides the switch, and the
  three-way choice belongs in `UserMenu`.
- Pressing the switch in a loop from code, such as an automated test that flips the theme on every step. Each press
  captures the whole window and runs a transition, so a fast series costs a snapshot each time.

### Common questions

**Why does the icon change but the window stays the same?** Setting `Appearance` moves the icon, the pressed state and
the name only. The theme changes when the switcher applies it or when your handler applies it. If you handle the request,
apply the theme in the handler, as shown in "Handling the request".

**Why does the icon stop following the window when I set `Appearance`?** A value in `Appearance` overrides the window's
theme variant. Set `Appearance` back to `null` to follow the window again.

**Does the transition play when the stored preference loads at startup?** No. Setting `Appearance` never plays the page
transition. The icon swap runs only after the switcher has loaded and settled, so a value set at startup appears without a
swap.

**Does the built-in apply keep my accent and other theme settings?** Yes. The switcher reuses the configuration of the
last theme request it observed, and it toggles only the dark algorithm. Before any request it carries the current Arc
accent preset over, so the accent does not reset when the appearance changes.

**Can I use my own transition for the built-in apply?** Handle the request and call `RunTransitionAsync` with the trigger,
the variant and your apply step, as shown in "Handling the request". The helper runs the transition the variant names and
falls back to a plain apply under reduced motion.

## API reference

### ThemeSwitcher

A single light / dark switch for a header: a secondary button that swaps sun and moon on a shared turn and names the next appearance. Pressing it raises `ThemeChangeRequested`; unless a handler marks it handled, the switcher applies the change through `ArcThemeManager` (changing the appearance and keeping the rest of the current theme) inside the page transition of its `Variant`. Arc hands that transition to the View Transitions API; here the old window is snapshotted into an overlay whose animated clip reveals the new theme beneath (`RunTransitionAsync`, also usable from a handler). Reduced motion switches without a transition.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Appearance` | `ThemeSwitcherAppearance?` | `null` | The appearance shown; null follows the control's actual theme variant (default). |
| `Variant` | `ThemeSwitcherVariant` | `Reveal` | Which page transition to play (default Reveal). |
| `Label` | `string?` | `null` | Accessible name; null says "Switch to dark mode" or "Switch to light mode". |
| `Text` | `string` | `"Switch theme"` | The visible text beside the icon (default "Switch theme"). |
| `IsIconOnly` | `bool` | `false` | Shows only the icon in a 38×38 square. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ThemeChangeRequested` | `ThemeSwitcherChangeRequestedEventArgs` | Raised before the theme changes. Set `Handled` to apply the theme yourself (optionally inside `RunTransitionAsync`); otherwise the switcher applies it through `ArcThemeManager`. |

Pseudo-classes: `:dark`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

**`ThemeSwitcherChangeRequestedEventArgs`** is the argument of `ThemeChangeRequested`.

| Member | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `Next` | `ThemeSwitcherAppearance` | The appearance to switch to |
| `Variant` | `ThemeSwitcherVariant` | The page transition the switcher asks for |
| `Trigger` | `Control` | The button that was pressed |
| `Origin` | `Point` | The centre of the trigger in its top level's coordinates, the start of a reveal |
| `Handled` | `bool` | Set to `True` to apply the theme yourself; inherited from `RoutedEventArgs` |

**`ThemeSwitcherVariant`** and **`ThemeSwitcherAppearance`** are the two enums the switcher uses.

| Enum | Members |
|---|---|
| `ThemeSwitcherVariant` | `Reveal` (default), `Eclipse`, `Split`, `Rise` |
| `ThemeSwitcherAppearance` | `Light`, `Dark` |

## Accessibility

- The switcher is a toggle button. It reports the dark appearance as On and the light appearance as Off, and each change
  of the appearance raises a toggle state change for assistive technology.
- Its accessible name names the next appearance ("Switch to dark mode" or "Switch to light mode") unless `Label` is set.
  The name updates when the appearance changes.
- The sun and moon icons are hidden from assistive technology. The name carries the meaning, not the glyph.
- The switcher takes keyboard focus like any Arc button and shows the standard focus ring. Enter and Space switch the
  appearance.
- Reduced motion switches the theme at once, without the page transition or the icon nudge.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Enter` or `Space` | Switch to the other appearance; raises `ThemeChangeRequested` first |

## Motion

- The sun and the moon turn and scale into each other on a shared path, and the old icon leaves quickly. Both icons turn
  the same way, so the swap reads as a single rotation rather than two separate icons.
- In dark mode the icon nudges in the direction of its variant: `Reveal` enlarges it to 108 percent, `Eclipse` moves it
  2 px left, `Split` moves it 1 px right and `Rise` moves it 2 px up.
- The page transition reveals the new appearance by its variant. The window is kept as a snapshot in the overlay layer,
  the new appearance is applied underneath, and the snapshot's clip opens to show it.
- The first appearance set does not animate. The icon swap starts only after the switcher has loaded and settled.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| Theme change | The page transition plays for the variant | No transition; the theme switches at once | Immediate |
| Sun and moon swap | The icons turn and scale into each other | The icon fades in at once | Immediate |
| Dark-mode icon nudge | The icon moves by its variant | No nudge | Immediate |

## Related

- `Button` for a plain action with no theme change, and the button the switcher is built on.
- `UserMenu` for a theme choice that includes system and lives in an account menu.
- `SegmentedControl` for a choice among a few named options that stays selected.
- `IconMorph` for a standalone icon that morphs between two states.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `Button` | The action does not change the theme |
| `UserMenu` | The theme choice includes system or lives in an account menu |
| `SegmentedControl` | Light, dark and system are visible named options in a settings page |
| `RadioCards` | Each appearance option needs its own description in a settings page |
| `Switch` | A single on or off setting that does not change the whole window |
| `IconMorph` | A two-state icon that is not the theme |

# Hold to confirm

> Confirm a destructive action by holding, not tapping.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/hold-to-confirm

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.HoldToConfirmDefaultDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12">
        <WrapPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center" ItemSpacing="12" LineSpacing="12">
            <arc:HoldToConfirm x:Name="Project"
                               Label="Hold to delete project"
                               ConfirmedLabel="Deleted"
                               HoldingChanged="OnHoldingChanged" />
            <arc:Button Content="Reset"
                        Variant="Ghost"
                        Size="Small"
                        Click="OnResetClick" />
        </WrapPanel>
        <TextBlock x:Name="Hint"
                   Text="Press and hold, or focus it and hold Space or Enter."
                   FontSize="13"
                   TextWrapping="Wrap"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class HoldToConfirmDefaultDemo : UserControl
{
    public HoldToConfirmDefaultDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
    }

    private void OnHoldingChanged(object? sender, HoldToConfirmHoldingChangedEventArgs e)
    {
        Hint.Text = e.IsHolding
            ? "Keep holding…"
            : Project.IsConfirmed ? "Deleted." : "Let go early and the fill rewinds.";
    }

    private void OnResetClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        Project.IsConfirmed = false;
    }
}
```

## When to use

`HoldToConfirm` is a button that runs its action only after the person has held it for a set time. It fits a
destructive or hard to undo action whose consequence is already visible on the screen, so the person does not need
to read a separate message. The fill grows across the button while it is held, and letting go early rewinds it, so
the control shows exactly how far the action has progressed before it commits.

- **Deleting a project from a settings page**: the danger zone at the bottom of a project's settings lists "Hold to
  delete project" beside the project name. The name is on screen, so a hold is enough to confirm the choice.
- **Revoking an API key or a webhook secret in a developer console**: a key row shows its prefix and last-used date,
  and the revoke button holds for two seconds. A key that is still in use by a build pipeline breaks at once, so the
  longer hold guards against a stray tap.
- **Cancelling a subscription in a compact billing row**: the plan row already shows the renewal date and the amount
  that stops. A hold keeps the decision on the row instead of a confirmation dialog that repeats the same facts.
- **Emptying a trash or resetting a sandbox in an internal tool**: a warehouse or support tool used on a shared tablet,
  where a stray tap on "Empty trash" must not remove 300 records.

## When not to use

- **Safe actions or ones that are easy to undo, such as saving a draft or muting a channel**: use `Button` or
  `ActionButton`. A hold on a reversible action makes people wait for nothing.
- **Actions that need the consequences read first, such as a refund, a plan downgrade with proration or a bulk
  change to billing details**: use `Dialog`, which can show the amount, the affected records and a clear cancel
  choice.
- **Removing one row from a touch list, such as an inbox, an order queue or a notification list**: use
  `SwipeActions`, which reveals the action on a swipe and keeps it next to the row.
- **Choosing a value or an option from a set**: use `Select`, `Combobox` or `MorphSelect`. A hold only commits one
  action.
- **Confirming a change that the person made on a form before saving**: use the form's primary `Button` and validate
  on submit. Holding a save button adds a delay to every save.

## Usage

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:HoldToConfirm Label="Hold to delete project"
                       ConfirmedLabel="Deleted"
                       Command="{Binding DeleteProject}" />
</UserControl>
```

`HoldToConfirm` derives from Avalonia's `Button`, so `Command`, `CommandParameter`, `IsEnabled` and the button's
template and style mechanics work as they do on a button. The difference is the trigger: the `Click` event and the
`Command` run only when a hold completes. A normal click, a tap that is shorter than the hold, or an automation
invoke does nothing. The control adds the fill, the done state, the `IsHolding` state and the `Confirmed` event on
top of the button.

### Anatomy

1. **Icon** (`Icon`): a 24 by 24 Lucide geometry drawn at 18 px before the label. The default is a trash icon. It is
   replaced by a drawn check mark when the hold completes.
2. **Label** (`Label`): the instruction and the action, for example "Hold to delete project". After completion the
   text shows `ConfirmedLabel` instead, "Done" by default. The icon and label are separated by 8 px and centered in
   the button.
3. **Surface**: a 1 px border in the strong border color, the control radius (`RadiusControl`) and the surface
   background. The minimum height is the medium control size, 44 px in the default theme. Horizontal padding is 20 px.
4. **Hover tint**: while the pointer is over an unconfirmed button, the tone color is mixed over the surface at 6%.
   It is a tint, not a second fill, and it never hides the label.
5. **Fill**: a layer in the tone color, revealed from the left edge as the hold progresses. The same icon and label
   are drawn again inside the fill in the tone's contrasting color, so the text changes color exactly at the edge.
6. **Focus ring** (keyboard focus only): a 2 px ring in the focus color, drawn 4 px outside the button with a 22 px
   radius. It is not shown for pointer focus.
7. **Disabled state**: the whole button drops to 50% opacity and shows the "not allowed" cursor.

### Choosing a tone

`Tone` sets the color of the fill. The label stays readable at every point of the hold because the text changes
color at the fill edge.

| Tone | Fill | Use it for |
|---|---|---|
| `Accent` (default) | The selected accent color | A deliberate action that is not destructive, such as "Hold to publish" |
| `Danger` | The danger color, with a danger-tinted border and label | An irreversible action: delete, revoke, purge, close an account |
| `Neutral` | The foreground color | A reversible action that still needs a deliberate hold, such as "Hold to archive" |

Use `Danger` for the actions people cannot take back, and keep one `Danger` control per group. A list of several red
holds in a single panel makes the real danger hard to read. Pick `Neutral` for archive-style actions so the danger
color keeps its meaning.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.HoldToConfirmTonesDemo">
    <WrapPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center" ItemSpacing="12" LineSpacing="12">
        <arc:HoldToConfirm Label="Hold to delete"
                           Tone="Danger"
                           ConfirmedLabel="Deleted" />
        <arc:HoldToConfirm Label="Hold to archive"
                           Tone="Neutral"
                           Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Archive}"
                           ConfirmedLabel="Archived" />
        <arc:HoldToConfirm Label="Hold to revoke"
                           HoldDuration="0:0:2"
                           Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Key}"
                           ConfirmedLabel="Revoked" />
    </WrapPanel>
</UserControl>
```

### Hold duration

`HoldDuration` sets how long the button must be held before it completes. The default is 1.2 seconds, which is long
enough to ignore a tap and short enough that a deliberate hold does not feel slow. Set a longer value, such as two
seconds, for an action with a wide impact, like revoking a key used by production systems. Keep the value the same for
all holds on one screen so the person learns one rhythm. The text in the help copy is generated from the duration, so
it stays correct when you change it.

The value is a `TimeSpan`. In XAML, write it as `HoldDuration="0:0:2"` for two seconds.

### Icon

`Icon` is a `Geometry`. The default is Lucide's trash icon, which suits deletion. Choose an icon that matches the
action's noun, such as an archive box for archiving or a key for revoking. Pass `null` when the label is enough on its own.

```csharp
var archive = new HoldToConfirm
{
    Label = "Hold to archive",
    Tone = HoldToConfirmTone.Neutral,
    Icon = ArcIcons.Archive,
    ConfirmedLabel = "Archived"
};
```

In XAML, use a static resource: `Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Archive}"`.

### Hint while holding

`HoldingChanged` is raised when a hold starts and when it ends. `IsHolding` tells you the current state. Use them
for a hint next to the button, such as "Keep holding" while the fill grows.

```csharp
project.HoldingChanged += (_, e) =>
{
    hint.Text = e.IsHolding
        ? "Keep holding…"
        : project.IsConfirmed ? "Deleted." : "Let go early and the fill rewinds.";
};
```

Letting go early rewinds the fill on a spring and nothing is confirmed. When the hold completes, `HoldingChanged`
reports `IsHolding` as `false` before `IsConfirmed` becomes `true`. The check in the example above therefore reads
`false` at completion. Show the done text from the `Confirmed` event instead:

```csharp
project.Confirmed += (_, _) => hint.Text = "Deleted.";
```

### Done state

`IsConfirmed` is two-way. It becomes `true` when the hold completes, before `Confirmed` is raised and before `Command`
runs. Once it is `true`, the button shows `ConfirmedLabel`, draws the check mark, reports itself as unavailable to
assistive technology, and cannot be held again. Set it back to `false` to reset the button; the fill rewinds as the
label morphs back to `Label`.

```xml
<arc:HoldToConfirm Label="Hold to delete project"
                   IsConfirmed="{Binding IsDeleted}" />
```

```csharp
reset.Click += (_, _) => project.IsConfirmed = false;
```

A confirmation set from code, for example when a project is deleted in another window, fills the button without a
hold.

### Disabled

A disabled button cannot be held, and a hold in progress is cancelled when the button becomes disabled. Use the
disabled state only while the action cannot apply, and say why in the text next to it, for example "Transfer the
ownership first".

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.HoldToConfirmDisabledDemo">
    <arc:HoldToConfirm Label="Hold to delete"
                       IsEnabled="False"
                       HorizontalAlignment="Center" />
</UserControl>
```

### Cancelling a hold

A hold cancels in these cases, and the fill rewinds without confirming:

- The person lets go of the pointer or the key before `HoldDuration` has passed.
- The pointer moves more than 24 px beyond the edge of the button while held, the same slack a native press allows.
  Moving the pointer back inside does not restart the hold.
- Focus moves away from the button, for example with Tab.
- The window loses activation, because a key-up can be lost when the window deactivates mid-hold.
- The button is disabled or removed from the visual tree during the hold.

To cancel a hold from code, for example when a dialog opens over the page, call `CancelHold()`.

### Binding to a view model

In an MVVM app the view model owns the state of the action. With CommunityToolkit.Mvvm, the view model holds the
`IsDeleted` flag and the delete command, and the button binds to both. The command runs once, after the hold
completes and after `IsDeleted` has become `true`.

```csharp
public partial class ProjectDangerZoneViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    private readonly IProjectService _projects;
    private readonly string _projectId;

    public ProjectDangerZoneViewModel(IProjectService projects, string projectId)
    {
        _projects = projects;
        _projectId = projectId;
    }

    [ObservableProperty]
    private bool _isDeleted;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private string? _error;

    [RelayCommand]
    private async Task DeleteProjectAsync()
    {
        var result = await _projects.DeleteAsync(_projectId);
        if (!result.IsSuccess)
        {
            // The button shows "Deleted" until the flag is cleared, so reset it on failure.
            IsDeleted = false;
            Error = result.Error;
        }
    }
}
```

```xml
<StackPanel Spacing="12">
    <arc:HoldToConfirm Label="Hold to delete project"
                       ConfirmedLabel="Deleted"
                       Tone="Danger"
                       IsConfirmed="{Binding IsDeleted}"
                       Command="{Binding DeleteProjectCommand}" />
    <TextBlock Text="{Binding Error}"
               Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Danger}"
               TextWrapping="Wrap" />
</StackPanel>
```

- `IsConfirmed` is two-way by default, so the view model's `IsDeleted` flag follows the completed hold. Set it to
  `true` from code and the button shows the done state without a hold.
- `Command` is one-way. Bind `Command` only to the action that runs when the hold completes; do not also handle
  `Confirmed` for the same work, or the action runs twice.
- Use `Confirmed` for a side effect that is not the action itself, such as analytics or a hint.
- A failed action must set `IsConfirmed` back to `false`. Otherwise the button still shows "Deleted" for an action that
  did not happen.
- Compiled bindings need `x:DataType` on the view (the examples here leave it out for brevity).

### Example: danger zone on a project settings page

The danger zone at the bottom of a project settings page in a SaaS admin console. Each row names the consequence in
plain words ("Deletes the project and its 42 invoices"), and the button shows the action in the same words. Both
actions use the `Danger` tone because neither can be undone. The button sits on the right so the text is read first.

![A danger zone with two hold to confirm buttons beside their consequence text](https://docs.tkcode.si/shots/Docs/Gestures/HoldToConfirm/images/DangerZone.webp)

```xml
<Border Width="640"
        Padding="24"
        CornerRadius="12"
        BorderThickness="1"
        BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Border}"
        Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Surface}">
    <StackPanel Spacing="20">
        <TextBlock Text="Danger zone"
                   FontSize="16"
                   FontWeight="SemiBold"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Danger}" />
        <Grid ColumnDefinitions="*,Auto" ColumnSpacing="24">
            <StackPanel Spacing="4">
                <TextBlock Text="Transfer project ownership"
                           FontSize="14"
                           FontWeight="Medium"
                           Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
                <TextBlock Text="The new owner receives billing contact and admin rights."
                           FontSize="13"
                           TextWrapping="Wrap"
                           Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
            </StackPanel>
            <arc:HoldToConfirm Grid.Column="1"
                               Label="Hold to transfer"
                               ConfirmedLabel="Transferred"
                               Tone="Neutral"
                               Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Users}"
                               VerticalAlignment="Center" />
        </Grid>
        <Border Height="1" Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Border}" />
        <Grid ColumnDefinitions="*,Auto" ColumnSpacing="24">
            <StackPanel Spacing="4">
                <TextBlock Text="Delete project"
                           FontSize="14"
                           FontWeight="Medium"
                           Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
                <TextBlock Text="Deletes Acme Analytics and its 42 invoices. This cannot be undone."
                           FontSize="13"
                           TextWrapping="Wrap"
                           Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
            </StackPanel>
            <arc:HoldToConfirm Grid.Column="1"
                               Label="Hold to delete"
                               ConfirmedLabel="Deleted"
                               Tone="Danger"
                               VerticalAlignment="Center" />
        </Grid>
    </StackPanel>
</Border>
```

Hold-to-confirm is the right tool for the delete row. The transfer row uses `Neutral` because a transfer can be
reversed by a second transfer, so the danger color is kept for the action that cannot be undone. Each action has
its own hold, so the person confirms the row they meant, and each row names the consequence beside the button.

### Content guidelines

- **Label**: an instruction and an object, "Hold to delete project", so the person knows both the verb and the
  target before they hold. Do not write only "Delete", which reads as a normal button.
- **Confirmed label**: the result in past tense, "Deleted", "Archived", "Revoked". It replaces the instruction once
  the action is committed, so it must describe what now stands.
- **Consequence text**: a sentence next to the button that names what is lost, with the count when it is known:
  "Deletes Acme Analytics and its 42 invoices." Keep it in the same row, not in a tooltip, because a tooltip is not
  visible to a touch user.
- **Tone**: sentence case, no exclamation marks, no "Are you sure?" The hold is the confirmation.

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| Delete | Hold to delete project |
| Click to delete | Hold to delete project |
| Deleted! | Deleted |
| Are you sure you want to delete this project? | Deletes the project and its 42 invoices. This cannot be undone. |
| Hold this button for 1.2 seconds to delete | Hold to delete project |

### Best practices

**Do**

- Put the consequence in visible text next to the button. A hold confirms a choice the person can see, so it does not
  replace the explanation.
- Use `Danger` only for actions that cannot be undone, and `Neutral` or `Accent` for the rest. A danger color on every
  control removes its meaning.
- Set `IsConfirmed` back to `false` when the action fails, so the button does not report success for an action that
  did not happen.
- Keep one hold per row and do not put several holds on one line. A stray hold on the wrong row is harder to spot
  when the rows are close together.
- Tell keyboard users the way to confirm in the visible copy when the form is dense, because the hint is hidden from
  sight.

**Avoid**

- Holds for reversible or safe actions. People wait for a delay that protects nothing and stop trusting the control.
- Bulk actions on many selected rows. A single hold that deletes 50 invoices hides the count; use `Dialog` with the
  list of affected records.
- Showing the done state for an action that has not completed on the server. Set `IsConfirmed` after the save
  succeeds, or reset it on failure.
- Long labels. The button widens with its label, and a long instruction pushes the consequence text out of view.
- Relying on `Confirmed` and `Command` together for one action. Choose one trigger for the work so it does not run
  twice.

### Common questions

**Why does a click not run the command?** A hold is the only path to completion. A click, a short press or an
automation invoke does nothing. Show the hold in the label, "Hold to delete project", so people know how to act.

**Can keyboard users confirm an action?** Yes. Hold Space or Enter. Auto-repeat from holding the key does not restart
the fill, and releasing the key before the hold completes rewinds it. Enter is handled by the button, so it does not
press the window's default button while the control has focus.

**How do I reset the button after a successful undo?** Set `IsConfirmed` to `false`, for example `project.IsConfirmed = false;`.
The fill rewinds as the label changes back to `Label`, so the change is visible without a separate message.

**How do I change the hold time for one button only?** Set `HoldDuration` on that button. The help text for
assistive technology is recalculated when `HoldDuration` changes, so it stays accurate.

**Why does `IsHolding` read false when the hold completes?** `HoldingChanged` is raised for the end of the hold before
`IsConfirmed` is set. Read `IsConfirmed` in the `Confirmed` event for the done state, not in `HoldingChanged`.

## API reference

### HoldToConfirm

A button that commits only after it is held, for destructive or hard to undo actions where a stray tap must not count. The fill tracks the hold on a linear, pausable timeline (P22) and is revealed from the leading edge with the label inverted exactly at the edge (P29); letting go early rewinds it on a smooth spring, and finishing morphs the label and icon into the done state (P2, P5, P15). Space and Enter can be held too; the hint is in the help text.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Label` | `string` | `"Hold to delete"` | The instruction and the action, such as "Hold to delete project". |
| `ConfirmedLabel` | `string` | `"Done"` | Shown once the hold completes (default "Done"). |
| `HoldDuration` | `TimeSpan` | `00:00:01.2000000` | How long the button must be held (default 1.2s). |
| `Icon` | `Geometry?` | – | Leading 24×24 glyph (default Lucide trash-2); it becomes a drawn check when done. |
| `Tone` | `HoldToConfirmTone` | `Accent` | Fill color: Accent (default), Danger for irreversible actions, or Neutral. |
| `IsConfirmed` | `bool` | `false` | The done state. Set it back to false to reset the button (the fill rewinds as the label morphs back). |
| `IsHolding` | `bool` | – | *Read-only.* True while a hold is in progress (for surrounding hints such as "Keep holding"). |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Confirmed` | `RoutedEventArgs` | Raised once when a hold completes (after which `Command` runs). |
| `HoldingChanged` | `HoldToConfirmHoldingChangedEventArgs` | Raised when a hold starts and when it ends. |

Pseudo-classes: `:holding`, `:confirmed`, `:wide`

Derives from `Button`: every member of `Button` works as well.

### Tone values

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `Accent` | Fills with the selected accent (the Arc default) |
| `Danger` | For an irreversible action: danger ink and fill |
| `Neutral` | Fills with the foreground color |

## Accessibility

- `Label` names the button. After the hold completes, the name follows `ConfirmedLabel`.
- The help text says how to confirm: press and hold for the duration, or hold Space or Enter with a keyboard. It is
  generated from `HoldDuration` and is removed once the action is done.
- The completed state is announced once through a polite status region, and the button reports that it is no longer
  available but keeps focus.
- Holding with Space or Enter uses the keyboard; key auto-repeat does not restart the hold. Moving focus away cancels
  the hold, and so does moving the pointer more than 24 px from the button.
- The text is drawn twice, once on the surface and once inside the fill. Its color changes exactly at the fill edge, so
  the contrast holds at every point of the hold.
- Assistive technology reads the hold instruction as the button's help text, so a screen reader user hears how to
  confirm before the action runs.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Space` or `Enter`, held | Starts the fill; the hold completes after `HoldDuration` |
| `Space` or `Enter`, released early | Rewinds the fill; nothing is confirmed |
| Key auto-repeat while held | Ignored; it does not restart the fill |
| `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` | Moves focus; leaving the button cancels a hold in progress |
| A quick press of `Space` or `Enter` | Does nothing; a hold must last for `HoldDuration` |

## Motion

- While held, the fill moves across the button at a steady rate for the time that is left. Letting go early rewinds
  it on a smooth spring that keeps no overshoot.
- The label and icon change with a short blur-and-slide when the hold completes, and the icon draws a check.
- Reduced motion removes the press scale and the rewind spring. The label and icon fade, and the fill still follows
  the hold because it shows progress.
- Off motion keeps only the fill progress. Everything else changes at once.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| Fill while held | Advances across the button at a steady rate | Advances with the hold | Advances with the hold |
| Early release | Rewinds on a smooth spring with no overshoot | Jumps back without the spring | Immediate |
| Press scale while held | Scales to 0.97 (0.985 when wider than 220 px) on a snappy spring | None | None |
| Label and icon at completion | Blur-and-slide; the check mark draws itself | Fade | Immediate |
| Label and icon on reset | The label morphs back as the fill rewinds | Fade | Immediate |

Use motion to show progress, not decoration. The fill is the only element that matters while the person holds the
button, so it stays on every motion level. Reduced motion removes the press scale and the spring, which move the
button itself and can cause discomfort for some people.

## Related

- `Button` and `ActionButton` for actions that do not need a hold.
- `Dialog` when the person must read the consequences before confirming.
- `SwipeActions` for deleting a row in a touch list.
- `ConfirmMorph` when the button should ask a question in place, with a Cancel path or a countdown.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `Button` / `ActionButton` | The action is safe, reversible or common, and one click is enough |
| `ConfirmMorph` | The button should ask in place, with a Cancel path or a countdown, before it acts |
| `Dialog` | The consequences must be read, or the action affects several records at once |
| `SwipeActions` | The action belongs to one row in a touch list such as an inbox or an order queue |
| `Select` / `Combobox` | The person chooses a value from a set instead of committing an action |
| `Toast` | The action already ran and the result should be reported without blocking the page |

# Swipe actions

> Reveal row actions with a swipe, or from the same actions in a menu.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/swipe-actions

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             xmlns:demos="using:TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.SwipeActionsInboxDemo">
    <UserControl.Styles>
        <Style Selector="TextBlock.sender">
            <Setter Property="FontWeight" Value="Normal" />
        </Style>
        <Style Selector="TextBlock.sender.unread">
            <Setter Property="FontWeight" Value="SemiBold" />
        </Style>
    </UserControl.Styles>
    <StackPanel Width="400" HorizontalAlignment="Center" Spacing="12">
        <Grid ColumnDefinitions="*,Auto" Margin="2,0">
            <TextBlock Text="Inbox"
                       FontSize="15"
                       FontWeight="SemiBold"
                       VerticalAlignment="Center"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
            <TextBlock x:Name="Remaining"
                       Grid.Column="1"
                       FontSize="13"
                       VerticalAlignment="Center"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
        </Grid>

                          Label="Inbox"
                          ActionInvoked="OnActionInvoked">

                <arc:SwipeAction Label="Unread"
                                 Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Mail}"
                                 Tone="Accent"
                                 KeepsRow="True" />
            </arc:SwipeActions.LeadingActions>
            <arc:SwipeActions.TrailingActions>
                <arc:SwipeAction Label="Archive" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Archive}" />
                <arc:SwipeAction Label="Delete" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Trash2}" Tone="Danger" />
            </arc:SwipeActions.TrailingActions>

                                    Size="Medium"
                                    VerticalAlignment="Center" />

                                           Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />

                                           Text="{Binding Time}"
                                           FontSize="12"
                                           Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
                            </Grid>
                            <TextBlock Text="{Binding Subject}"
                                       FontSize="13"
                                       TextTrimming="CharacterEllipsis"
                                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
                            <TextBlock Text="{Binding Preview}"
                                       FontSize="12"
                                       TextTrimming="CharacterEllipsis"
                                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
                        </StackPanel>
                    </Grid>
                </DataTemplate>
            </arc:SwipeActions.ItemTemplate>
        </arc:SwipeActions>
        <TextBlock x:Name="Status"
                   Text="Swipe a message, or use its menu."
                   Margin="2,0"
                   FontSize="13"
                   TextWrapping="Wrap"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
        <WrapPanel x:Name="Recovery" ItemSpacing="8" IsVisible="False">
            <arc:Button x:Name="Undo"
                        Content="Undo"
                        Variant="Ghost"
                        Size="Small"
                        IsVisible="False"
                        Click="OnUndoClick" />
            <arc:Button Content="Reset inbox"
                        Variant="Secondary"
                        Size="Small"
                        Click="OnResetClick" />
        </WrapPanel>
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using System.Collections.ObjectModel;
using System.ComponentModel;
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class SwipeActionsInboxDemo : UserControl
{
    private readonly ObservableCollection<Message> _messages = [];
    private Message? _lastRemoved;
    private int _lastIndex;

    public SwipeActionsInboxDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Inbox.ItemsSource = _messages;
        _messages.CollectionChanged += (_, _) => UpdateRemaining();
        Fill();
    }

    private void UpdateRemaining()
    {
        Remaining.Text = _messages.Count == 0 ? "All caught up" : $"{_messages.Count} left to triage";
    }

    private void Fill()
    {
        _messages.Clear();
        _messages.Add(new Message("Maya Chen", "Design review moved to Thursday", "The room is booked from 2pm. Bring the latest flows.", "9:41", 47));
        _messages.Add(new Message("Daniel Ortiz", "Contract draft for Fernhill", "Two clauses changed since Monday. Legal wants a reply today.", "8:15", 12));
        _messages.Add(new Message("Priya Nair", "Survey results are in", "Response rate was 38%. The summary deck is in the shared folder.", "Yesterday", 45) { IsUnread = false });
        _messages.Add(new Message("Jonas Weber", "Invoice #2041", "Attached is the invoice for October. Thanks again!", "Mon", 59) { IsUnread = false });
        UpdateRemaining();
    }

    private void OnActionInvoked(object? sender, SwipeActionInvokedEventArgs e)
    {
        if (e.Item is not Message message)
        {
            return;
        }

        if (e.Action.KeepsRow)
        {
            message.IsUnread = !message.IsUnread;
            Status.Text = $"Marked “{message.Subject}” as {(message.IsUnread ? "unread" : "read")}.";
            return;
        }

        _lastIndex = _messages.IndexOf(message);
        _lastRemoved = message;
        _messages.Remove(message);
        Undo.IsVisible = true;
        Recovery.IsVisible = true;
        Status.Text = $"{(e.Action.Tone == SwipeActionTone.Danger ? "Deleted" : "Archived")} “{message.Subject}”.";
    }

    private void OnUndoClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        if (_lastRemoved is null)
        {
            return;
        }

        _messages.Insert(Math.Clamp(_lastIndex, 0, _messages.Count), _lastRemoved);
        _lastRemoved = null;
        Undo.IsVisible = false;
        Status.Text = "Restored.";
    }

    private void OnResetClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        Fill();
        Undo.IsVisible = false;
        Recovery.IsVisible = false;
        Status.Text = "Swipe a message, or use its menu.";
    }

    public sealed class Message(string sender, string subject, string preview, string time, int portrait) : INotifyPropertyChanged
    {
        private bool _isUnread = true;

        public event PropertyChangedEventHandler? PropertyChanged;

        public string Sender { get; } = sender;

        public string Subject { get; } = subject;

        public string Preview { get; } = preview;

        public string Time { get; } = time;

        public ImageSource? Photo { get; } = ImageSource.TryParse($"https://i.pravatar.cc/160?img={portrait}", out var source) ? source : null;

        public bool IsUnread
        {
            get => _isUnread;
            set
            {
                if (_isUnread != value)
                {
                    _isUnread = value;
                    PropertyChanged?.Invoke(this, new PropertyChangedEventArgs(nameof(IsUnread)));
                }
            }
        }

        public override string ToString() => Subject;
    }
}
```

## When to use

`SwipeActions` is a list whose rows reveal actions when they are swiped sideways. It is built for touch-first triage,
where a person works through a long list of items one at a time and each item needs one or two quick decisions. The
actions sit under the row, so the decision is made where the item is read, and a full swipe removes the row and closes
the gap without a separate confirmation.

- **Mail triage on a tablet**: a support or sales inbox where a swipe left archives a thread and a swipe right marks it
  unread. Both actions are one tap from the row, and the list closes the gap after an archive.
- **Field service job list on a phone**: a technician swipes right to mark a job done and left to reschedule it. The
  job card stays readable while the actions wait under it, so the decision is made without opening the job.
- **Approvals on a phone**: a manager approves a purchase request with an accent swipe and rejects it with a danger
  swipe. Full swipe is turned off for the rejection row, so a long drag cannot reject a request by accident.
- **Notification center in a companion app**: a sign-in alert is dismissed with a danger swipe, and a long-running
  export is muted with an action that keeps the row in place.

## When not to use

- **A desktop table, or a list used mainly with a mouse**: use `ContextMenu` on the row or `DropdownMenu` on a row
  button. Swipe gestures are the wrong primary path for a pointer, and the menu is already on every row.
- **Reordering rows by dragging them up and down**: use `ReorderableList`. Swipe gestures lock to the horizontal axis
  and never change the order of the rows.
- **Long, paged or sorted datasets with many columns**: use `Table`. Swipe rows are not virtualized, so a
  list of thousands of rows should be paginated before it is shown here.
- **One destructive action outside a list**, such as deleting a project from its settings page: use `HoldToConfirm`,
  which needs a deliberate hold instead of a gesture a row can trigger by accident.
- **More than two quick actions on a side**: the revealed width grows with each action. Keep the two most common
  actions on the swipe and move the rest into the row's More actions menu, or use `ContextMenu` for a full list.

## Usage

`SwipeActions` is the list. Each item is a `SwipeActionsRow`, or a data item shown through `ItemTemplate`.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:SwipeActions Label="Inbox" ItemsSource="{Binding Messages}">
        <arc:SwipeActions.LeadingActions>
            <arc:SwipeAction Label="Unread" Tone="Accent" KeepsRow="True" />
        </arc:SwipeActions.LeadingActions>
        <arc:SwipeActions.TrailingActions>
            <arc:SwipeAction Label="Archive" />
            <arc:SwipeAction Label="Delete" Tone="Danger" />
        </arc:SwipeActions.TrailingActions>
        <arc:SwipeActions.ItemTemplate>
            <DataTemplate>
                <TextBlock Text="{Binding Subject}" />
            </DataTemplate>
        </arc:SwipeActions.ItemTemplate>
    </arc:SwipeActions>
</UserControl>
```

Leading and trailing actions are shared by every row. The outermost action of a side is the one that a full swipe
runs.

`SwipeActions` derives from Avalonia's `ItemsControl`, so `ItemsSource`, `ItemTemplate` and the item containers work as
they do on a list. Each container is a `SwipeActionsRow`, which derives from `ContentControl`, so a row can also be used
on its own. Each `SwipeAction` is a plain model object, not a control: it holds the label, the icon, the tone and the
command, and the row draws it.

Leading actions sit under the left edge and are revealed by a swipe to the right. Trailing actions sit under the right
edge and are revealed by a swipe to the left. Each side can hold any number of actions, but the revealed width grows
with each one, so two per side is the practical limit.

### Anatomy

1. **List frame** (`Label` names it): one surface around all rows, with a hairline separator between rows. The
   separator starts 16 px in from the left edge (`SeparatorInset`).
2. **Row body** (`MinRowHeight` 64 px): the content you supply, with 16 px of padding on the left, 12 px above and
   below, and 8 px on the right before the More actions button. The row grows taller when its content is taller.
3. **More actions button**: a 32 px square with a 12 px radius and an 18 px ellipsis. It is the
   keyboard and screen reader path to the same actions, so it is always present on every row.
4. **Revealed actions**: each action is 76 px wide at rest, with its icon in a 20 px glyph over its label. The icon and
   label are 3 px apart. A neutral action fills with the foreground color mixed 20% into the surface; the accent and
   danger actions use their theme colors.
5. **Full swipe stretch**: when a swipe passes the commit threshold, the outermost action stretches across the whole row.
6. **More actions menu**: a menu at least 176 px wide, placed 6 px below the More actions button. It lists the row's
   actions in the same order as the swipe, and marks a destructive action so it reads as one.

### Tones

`Tone` sets the fill of a revealed action. Choose the tone by the result, not by the position on the row.

| Tone | Fill | Use it for |
|---|---|---|
| `Neutral` (default) | A quiet neutral fill | Archive, snooze, move, and other reversible housekeeping |
| `Accent` | The accent color | Done, approve, mark unread: a positive or primary result |
| `Danger` | The danger color | Delete, reject, dismiss: a result that removes or refuses something |

Pair a `Danger` action with a label that names the result, such as "Delete" or "Reject", so the color is not the only
signal. Keep at most one `Danger` action on each side, and place it outermost, so a full swipe can only reach it
deliberately.

### Actions that run

`Command` runs when the action is chosen, by a full swipe, a tap on the revealed action or the More actions menu.
`Invoked` on the `SwipeAction` and `ActionInvoked` on the list or row tell you which row and item it was. The
`Invoked` handler of the action runs first, then its `Command`. `CommandParameter` defaults to the row's data item when
it is not set.

`KeepsRow="True"` runs the action and returns the row to its place instead of removing it. Use it for toggles such as
unread, mute and flag, where the row should stay on the list.

```csharp
inbox.ActionInvoked += (_, e) =>
{
    if (!e.Action.KeepsRow)
    {
        messages.Remove((Message)e.Item!);
    }
};
```

Remove the data item in the handler. An action that does not keep the row runs only after the row has slid away and
collapsed, so the list closes the gap without a jump. The handler can remove the item directly. If the item is still in
the list 1.4 seconds after the action ran, the row slides back into place, so an action that never removes its item
does not leave an empty band behind.

The inbox demo keeps the removed message and offers an undo, which is the pattern to follow for an archive or delete.
A removed row is inserted back at its old index when the person taps Undo.

### Rows with their own actions

A `SwipeActionsRow` can declare its own actions. A row that declares them ignores the list's leading and trailing
actions. `IsFullSwipeEnabled` on a row overrides the list's setting: `False` keeps the row from committing on a full
swipe, so the person must tap the revealed action; `True` allows it, even when the list turns it off; `null` (the
default) follows the list.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.SwipeActionsOwnActionsDemo">
    <arc:SwipeActions x:Name="Tasks"
                      Label="Tasks"
                      Width="440"
                      HorizontalAlignment="Left"
                      ActionInvoked="OnActionInvoked">
        <arc:SwipeActionsRow Label="Write the release notes">
            <arc:SwipeActionsRow.LeadingActions>
                <arc:SwipeAction Label="Done" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Check}" Tone="Accent" />
            </arc:SwipeActionsRow.LeadingActions>
            <arc:SwipeActionsRow.TrailingActions>
                <arc:SwipeAction Label="Flag" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Flag}" KeepsRow="True" />
                <arc:SwipeAction Label="Delete" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Trash2}" Tone="Danger" />
            </arc:SwipeActionsRow.TrailingActions>
            <TextBlock Text="Write the release notes"
                       VerticalAlignment="Center"
                       FontSize="14"
                       TextWrapping="Wrap"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
        </arc:SwipeActionsRow>
        <arc:SwipeActionsRow Label="Review pull request #418" IsFullSwipeEnabled="False">
            <arc:SwipeActionsRow.LeadingActions>
                <arc:SwipeAction Label="Done" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Check}" Tone="Accent" />
            </arc:SwipeActionsRow.LeadingActions>
            <arc:SwipeActionsRow.TrailingActions>
                <arc:SwipeAction Label="Flag" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Flag}" KeepsRow="True" />
                <arc:SwipeAction Label="Delete" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Trash2}" Tone="Danger" />
            </arc:SwipeActionsRow.TrailingActions>
            <StackPanel Spacing="2" VerticalAlignment="Center">
                <TextBlock Text="Review pull request #418"
                           FontSize="14"
                           TextWrapping="Wrap"
                           Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
                <TextBlock Text="Full swipe off: tap the revealed action"
                           FontSize="13"
                           TextWrapping="Wrap"
                           Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
            </StackPanel>
        </arc:SwipeActionsRow>
        <arc:SwipeActionsRow Label="Book flights for the offsite">
            <arc:SwipeActionsRow.LeadingActions>
                <arc:SwipeAction Label="Done" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Check}" Tone="Accent" />
            </arc:SwipeActionsRow.LeadingActions>
            <arc:SwipeActionsRow.TrailingActions>
                <arc:SwipeAction Label="Flag" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Flag}" KeepsRow="True" />
                <arc:SwipeAction Label="Delete" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Trash2}" Tone="Danger" />
            </arc:SwipeActionsRow.TrailingActions>
            <TextBlock Text="Book flights for the offsite"
                       VerticalAlignment="Center"
                       FontSize="14"
                       TextWrapping="Wrap"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
        </arc:SwipeActionsRow>
    </arc:SwipeActions>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class SwipeActionsOwnActionsDemo : UserControl
{
    public SwipeActionsOwnActionsDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
    }

    private void OnActionInvoked(object? sender, SwipeActionInvokedEventArgs e)
    {
        if (!e.Action.KeepsRow)
        {
            Tasks.Items.Remove(e.Row);
        }
    }
}
```

### Resting open

`Open(SwipeActionSide.Trailing)` shows a row's actions without a gesture, springing the row to its resting width. A row
with one revealed action rests at 76 px; a row with two rests at 152 px. The list holds one open row at a time: opening
a row puts the previous one away. `Close()` puts an open row away, and `SwipeActions.CloseRows()` closes the open row of
the list. `OpenRow` returns the row that is open, or `null`.

```csharp
// Show the export row's actions when the notifications screen opens.
export.Open(SwipeActionSide.Trailing);
```

Use a resting open row to show that a swipe is possible, such as the first time a person opens a notification list.
Do not leave a row open permanently, because it hides the row's content and makes the list look broken.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.SwipeActionsRestingOpenDemo">
    <arc:SwipeActions x:Name="Notifications"
                      Label="Notifications"
                      Width="440"
                      HorizontalAlignment="Left"
                      ActionInvoked="OnActionInvoked">
        <arc:SwipeActionsRow x:Name="Export" Label="Your export is ready">
            <arc:SwipeActionsRow.TrailingActions>
                <arc:SwipeAction Label="Mute" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.BellOff}" KeepsRow="True" />
                <arc:SwipeAction Label="Dismiss" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.X}" Tone="Danger" />
            </arc:SwipeActionsRow.TrailingActions>
            <StackPanel Spacing="2" VerticalAlignment="Center">
                <TextBlock Text="Your export is ready"

                <arc:SwipeAction Label="Dismiss" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.X}" Tone="Danger" />
            </arc:SwipeActionsRow.TrailingActions>
```

### Full swipe

A full swipe commits the outermost action of a side. The threshold is the larger of two values: the open width of the
side plus 48 px, or 56% of the row's width. Once the row passes the threshold, it stays armed until the drag comes back
20 px, so a small wobble does not cancel the commit. A flick faster than 900 px/s also commits when it carries the row past the
threshold in its direction.

Set `IsFullSwipeEnabled="False"` on the list, or on a row, for an action where a stray long drag would be costly, such
as a rejection or a payment. The revealed action still runs on a tap.

### Binding to a view model

In an MVVM app the view model owns the collection and the rules that remove items. The list binds to the collection,
and the actions are wired in code, because `SwipeAction` is a plain model object and not a control in the visual tree.

```csharp
public partial class InboxViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    private readonly IMailService _mail;

    public InboxViewModel(IMailService mail)
    {
        _mail = mail;
    }

    public ObservableCollection<MailThread> Threads { get; } = [];

    [RelayCommand]
    private async Task ArchiveAsync(MailThread thread)
    {
        await _mail.ArchiveAsync(thread.Id);
        Threads.Remove(thread);
    }

    [RelayCommand]
    private void ToggleUnread(MailThread thread)
    {
        thread.IsUnread = !thread.IsUnread;
    }
}
```

```xml
<arc:SwipeActions Label="Inbox"
                  ItemsSource="{Binding Threads}"
                  RowLabelBinding="{Binding Subject}">
    <arc:SwipeActions.ItemTemplate>
        <DataTemplate>
            <StackPanel Spacing="2">
                <TextBlock Text="{Binding Sender}" FontWeight="SemiBold" />
                <TextBlock Text="{Binding Subject}" />
                <TextBlock Text="{Binding Preview}" Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
            </StackPanel>
        </DataTemplate>
    </arc:SwipeActions.ItemTemplate>
</arc:SwipeActions>
```

```csharp
// In the view's code-behind, where the view model is available:
var archive = new SwipeAction { Label = "Archive", Icon = ArcIcons.Archive, Command = viewModel.ArchiveCommand };
var unread = new SwipeAction { Label = "Unread", Icon = ArcIcons.Mail, Tone = SwipeActionTone.Accent, KeepsRow = true, Command = viewModel.ToggleUnreadCommand };
inbox.TrailingActions.Add(archive);
inbox.LeadingActions.Add(unread);
```

- The list reads `ItemsSource`, and the view model changes the collection to add or remove rows. Use an `ObservableCollection<T>` so the list updates when items are removed.
- `RowLabelBinding` names each generated row for its More actions button, for example "More actions for Invoice #2041".
- The command receives the row's data item as its parameter, so one command serves every row.
- Compiled bindings need `x:DataType` on the view and on the data template (the examples here leave it out for
  brevity).

and the trailing actions archive it or delete it. The rows in this scene declare no actions of their own, so every row
uses the list's actions. The screenshot shows the resting list; the revealed actions appear only when a row is swiped
or opened.
