The three rows show the three things a triage list needs: a subject that asks for an action, a thread that is only
informational, and a personal message. The list uses one set of actions, so the same swipe means the same thing on
every row. The danger action is outermost, so only a deliberate full swipe reaches it, and the More actions menu
offers the same actions for a keyboard user.

### Content guidelines

- **Action label**: one short word, such as "Archive", "Delete", "Done" or "Unread". The label sits under a 20 px icon
  in a 76 px column, so a longer phrase is cut off. Keep the verb in the menu, where the full width is available.
- **Row label**: the subject or the item's name, for example "Invoice #2041 is overdue". It names the row for the More
  actions button, so write it as a sentence a screen reader user would recognize.
- **List label**: the collection's name, "Inbox", "Tasks", "Notifications". It is the list's accessible name.
- **Result wording**: name the result, not the gesture. "Delete" describes what happens; "Swipe to delete" describes
  how to reach it, and the swipe is not the only way.

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| Swipe to archive | Archive |
| Move this thread to the archive folder | Archive |
| Remove | Delete |
| Mark as unread | Unread |
| Trash it forever | Delete |

### Best practices

**Do**

- Put the action a full swipe should run in the outermost position of a side, since that is the one it commits. Keep
  a destructive action out of that position unless an Undo is offered.
- Use `KeepsRow="True"` for toggles that change the row's state, such as unread or flag, and remove the item only for
  actions that finish with it. A toggle that removes the row is confusing when the person wants to undo it.
- Give each row a `Label` through `RowLabelBinding`, so the More actions button names the row it belongs to.
- Provide an Undo path after a removing action, such as a button or a toast, because a full swipe is quick and easy
  to trigger by accident.
- Keep the same actions on every row of one list, unless a row has a real reason to differ, such as a locked item.

**Avoid**

- Gestures as the only way to act. The More actions button is always present, and it serves keyboard and screen reader
  users who cannot swipe.
- Danger actions on both sides of a row, which makes a stray swipe in either direction destructive.
- Long labels on revealed actions. The label is cut to the 76 px column, so the meaning must fit in one word.
- Turning off full swipe on every row. Keep it on for reversible actions and turn it off only for a rejection or a
  payment, where the extra tap is the safeguard.
- Thousands of rows in one list. Rows are not virtualized, so the list builds every container; page the data instead.

### Common questions

**Why does my handler run after the row has slid away?** An action that removes its item runs after the row slides out
and collapses, so the list closes the gap without a visible jump. If you need the action to run immediately, set
`KeepsRow="True"` and remove the item later, for example after the server confirms the change.

**What happens if the item is not removed?** If the item is still in the list 1.4 seconds after the action ran, the row
slides back into place. Remove the item in the handler, or set `KeepsRow` when the row should stay.

**How do I stop a full swipe from running a destructive action?** Set `IsFullSwipeEnabled` to `False` on the row. The
person can still reveal the action and tap it, but a long drag only opens the row.

**Why do my row's actions ignore the list's actions?** A row that declares its own leading or trailing actions uses only
those. The list's actions are the default for rows that declare none.

**Can I use a single row without a list?** Yes. `SwipeActionsRow` works on its own, with its own actions and its own
`Open`, `Close` and `Run` methods. It has no list, so the single-open rule and the list's full-swipe setting do not
apply.

## API reference

### SwipeActions

A list whose rows reveal actions on a horizontal swipe, the way a mail inbox does (Arc swipe actions): short, touch-first triage lists such as mail, notifications or tasks. Rows are `SwipeActionsRow`s declared inline or generated from `ItemsSource` (with `LeadingActions` / `TrailingActions` shared by every row that declares none, and `RowLabelBinding` naming each row). Only one row stays open at a time; pressing anywhere else or Escape puts it away. Every row also has a More actions menu with the same actions, so keyboard and screen reader users never need the gesture. Remove the item in `ActionInvoked` (or the action's own handler or command): removing actions run once their row has slid away and collapsed. The surface fades with the last row and hides when the list is empty. Rows are not virtualized; paginate long lists.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Label` | `string` | `"List"` | Accessible name of the list (Arc: required), such as "Inbox". |
| `IsFullSwipeEnabled` | `bool` | `true` | Lets a long swipe commit the outermost action of rows that do not decide for themselves (default true). |
| `MoreActionsFormat` | `string` | `"More actions for {0}"` | Accessible name of each row's More actions button; {0} is the row's label. |
| `RowLabelBinding` | `BindingBase?` | `null` | Binding that names generated rows (their `Label`), such as the message subject. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ActionInvoked` | `SwipeActionInvokedEventArgs` | Raised (bubbling from the row) after an action ran. |

Pseudo-classes: `:empty`, `:all-leaving`

Derives from `ItemsControl`: every member of `ItemsControl` works as well.

### SwipeAction

One action of a `SwipeActionsRow`: revealed under the row's edge by a swipe (icon over label), committed by a full swipe on the outermost action, a tap on the revealed action, or the row's More actions menu. An action that removes its item (the default) runs once the row has slid away and collapsed, so the handler can remove the item without a jump; set `KeepsRow` for actions such as Mark as unread, which run at once while the row springs home.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Label` | `string` | `""` | Shown under the icon and in the menu (Arc: required). |
| `Icon` | `Geometry?` | `null` | 24×24 Lucide geometry drawn at 20px (Arc: required), for example `ArcIcons.Archive`. |
| `Tone` | `SwipeActionTone` | `Neutral` | Fill of the revealed action: Neutral (default), Accent or Danger. |
| `KeepsRow` | `bool` | `false` | The row springs home after the action instead of sliding away and collapsing. |
| `Command` | `ICommand?` | `null` | Runs after `Invoked`; its parameter defaults to the row's data item. |
| `CommandParameter` | `object?` | `null` | Parameter passed to Command; when null the row's data item is used. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Invoked` | `SwipeActionInvokedEventArgs` | Raised when the action runs (full swipe, tap on the revealed action, or the menu). |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### SwipeActionsRow

One row of `SwipeActions` (Arc SwipeActionsRow): its content follows a horizontal swipe to reveal `LeadingActions` under the left edge and `TrailingActions` under the right. Past the last stop the row still follows with rubber-band resistance; a full swipe commits the outermost action (the action stretches across the row, the row slides away and collapses), and a release settles open or closed on a spring that carries the release velocity. Vertical drags pass through to the page. Every row also has a More actions button with the same actions in a menu, so the gesture is never required: Enter or Space opens it on the first row, arrows move, Escape closes the menu or puts an open row away. Pressing outside an open row closes it, and only one row of a list is open at a time. Use it on its own or inside a `SwipeActions` list (whose actions it uses when it declares none of its own).

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Label` | `string` | `""` | Names the row in its More actions button, for example the message subject (Arc: required). |
| `IsFullSwipeEnabled` | `bool?` | `null` | Lets a long swipe commit the outermost action without a tap; null follows the list (default on). |
| `SeparatorInset` | `double` | `16` | Left inset of the hairline separator under the row (Arc `--swipe-actions-inset`, default 16). |
| `OpenSide` | `SwipeActionSide` | – | *Read-only.* The side resting open (or heading there), or `None`. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ActionInvoked` | `SwipeActionInvokedEventArgs` | Raised on the row (and bubbled to its list) after an action ran. |

Pseudo-classes: `:open`, `:dragging`, `:leaving`, `:has-actions`

Derives from `ContentControl`: every member of `ContentControl` works as well.

### Tone and side values

| Type | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `SwipeActionTone` | `Neutral` | A quiet neutral fill (the default) |
| `SwipeActionTone` | `Accent` | The accent fill |
| `SwipeActionTone` | `Danger` | The danger fill, for a destructive or refusing result |
| `SwipeActionSide` | `None` | The row is closed |
| `SwipeActionSide` | `Leading` | Under the left edge, revealed by a swipe to the right |
| `SwipeActionSide` | `Trailing` | Under the right edge, revealed by a swipe to the left |

## Accessibility

- The list has a name from `Label`, and each row is a list item. Each row has a More actions button named "More actions for" the row's `Label`.
- Mouse and keyboard users never need the gesture: Tab to the More actions button, press Enter or Space to open the menu, and move with the arrow keys.
- Escape closes the menu or puts away an open row. Pressing elsewhere also puts an open row away.
- The revealed actions are hidden from assistive technology and are not in the Tab order.
- When a row is removed from its menu, focus moves to the neighbouring row's More actions button. When the last row
  leaves, focus lands on the list itself.
- The menu lists the same actions as the swipe, and a destructive entry is marked as destructive, so a screen reader
  user hears the risk before the action runs.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` | Moves between the rows' focusable content and More actions buttons; revealed actions are skipped |
| `Enter` or `Space` on a More actions button | Opens the row's menu with its first item highlighted |
| `Up` or `Down` on a More actions button | Opens the menu at its last or first item, when it is closed |
| `Up` / `Down` in the menu | Moves between the actions |
| `Enter` in the menu | Runs the highlighted action |
| `Escape` | Closes the menu, or puts an open row away |

## Motion

- The row follows the pointer. Past its last stop it resists, so the row stretches a little and then returns.
- On release the row settles on the nearest stop with a spring that keeps the release speed. A quick flick
  counts as a swipe to the stop in its direction.
- A full swipe stretches the outermost action across the row, and the row slides away. The list then closes the gap.
- Reduced motion jumps the row to its stop and fades rows in and out without a height animation. Off motion moves
  everything at once.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| Row follows the pointer | Follows the pointer, with rubber-band resistance past the last stop | No follow; the row jumps to its stop | No follow; the row jumps to its stop |
| Release | Springs to the stop with the release speed: smooth to close, snappy to open | Jumps to the stop | Immediate |
| Full swipe | The outermost action stretches across the row, and the row slides away | Fades out | Immediate |
| Row removed | The row's height collapses on a smooth spring after 120 ms, and the list closes the gap | Fades out, no height animation | Immediate |
| Row added | The row grows in on a smooth height spring with a fade | Fades in, no height animation | Immediate |
| More actions menu | Opens and closes with the menu surface's transition | The menu surface's reduced transition | The menu surface's off transition |

The swipe itself is the only motion the person controls, so keep it direct and responsive on every motion level. Use
the spring on release to show where the row will stop, and skip decorative movement on the list around it.

## Related

- `ContextMenu` and `DropdownMenu` for row actions on desktop.
- `ReorderableList` for dragging rows into a new order.
- `HoldToConfirm` for a single destructive action outside a list.
- `Table` for large, sortable datasets.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `ContextMenu` / `DropdownMenu` | The primary input is a mouse, or the row has many actions |
| `ReorderableList` | The person changes the order of the rows by dragging them |
| `Table` | The data has columns, sorting or a large number of rows |
| `HoldToConfirm` | One destructive action needs a deliberate hold, outside a list |
| `Dialog` | The consequences must be read before the action runs |
| `Toast` | An action ran and the result should be reported with an undo |

# Reactions

> Acknowledge a post in one tap, with counts that roll.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/reactions

using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class ReactionsDefaultDemo : UserControl
{
    public ReactionsDefaultDemo()

        InitializeComponent();
        Bar.Value = [new Reaction("like", 3)];

## When to use

`Reactions` is a bar of reaction pills with counts, plus an add button that opens a small picker. It lets people
acknowledge a piece of content in one tap, without writing a reply. It sits under the content it refers to, such as a
release note, a status update or a design review comment, and the counts show how many people responded with each
option.

- **Release notes and changelog entries**: a team reads "Release 2026.10 is live" and taps "Ship it" or "Celebrate".
  The counts show how many engineers saw the release, and the viewer's own reaction is highlighted when the saved list includes it.
- **Status updates in a team workspace**: a daily incident summary or a project update gets a "Like" or "Thanks" from
  the people who read it, so the author knows the update landed without a reply thread.
- **Design review comments**: a reviewer marks a comment as "Agreed" or "Question" with one tap. The counts tell the
  author which comments the team already accepts.
- **Announcement feeds in an internal portal**: a welcome post for a new hire gets "Love" and "Celebrate". The
  tooltip names the people who reacted, which turns a count into a sign of who saw it.

## When not to use

- **A response that needs words**, such as a question, a decision or a reply to a comment: use `CommentThread` or
  `ChatThread`, which keep the text and its author together. A reaction cannot carry a sentence.
- **A count the viewer cannot change**, such as the number of open tickets or unread messages: use `Badge` for a fixed
  count, or `AnimatedCounter` when the number should roll in a metric.
- **Choosing one value from a list**, such as a priority, a status or a category: use `Select`, `Combobox` or
  `MorphSelect`. A reaction bar allows several options at once and has no single result.
- **A rating on a numeric scale**, such as one to five stars or a satisfaction score: use `Slider` or a form control
  that stores a number. A reaction carries a choice, not a quantity.
- **Row actions in a touch list**, such as archive or mark as read on an inbox row: use `SwipeActions`, which keeps
  the action next to the row it applies to.

## Usage

The options are the children of `Reactions`. The counts and the viewer's own reactions are its `Value`, which is
set in code or bound from a view model.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:Reactions Label="Reactions">
        <arc:ReactionOption Id="like" Label="Like" />
        <arc:ReactionOption Id="love" Label="Love" />
        <arc:ReactionOption Id="celebrate" Label="Celebrate" />
    </arc:Reactions>
</UserControl>
```

```csharp
var reactions = new Reactions
{
    Value = [new Reaction("like", 3)]
};
reactions.Options.Add(new ReactionOption("like", "Like", ArcIcons.ThumbsUp));
reactions.Options.Add(new ReactionOption("love", "Love", ArcIcons.Heart));
reactions.Options.Add(new ReactionOption("celebrate", "Celebrate", ArcIcons.Smile));
```

`Reactions` derives from Avalonia's `TemplatedControl`, so its template, style and layout behave like other Arc
controls. The options are plain data (`ReactionOption` is not a control), and the bar builds one toggle pill for each
reaction that has a count. Use the same `Id` values in `Options` and in `Value`: the id is what your server stores
for a reaction, and the label is only what people read.

A `ReactionOption` takes a 24 by 24 Lucide geometry in `Icon`, drawn with a 1.75 stroke. Icons that are not in
`ArcIcons` can be parsed with `ArcIcons.Parse` or taken from a `StreamGeometry` resource, as the gallery does for a
party popper.

### Anatomy

1. **Bar** (`Label` names it): a group that wraps its pills in rows. Pills are 6 px apart in a row and rows are 8 px
   apart. The bar grows to fit the rows it needs.
2. **Pill**: 32 px high with a pill radius. It has 9 px of padding before the icon and 11 px after the count, with 6 px
   between the icon and the count. The icon is 16 px, and the count uses the small text size in the secondary text
   color.
3. **Count**: the number of people who reacted. When the number changes, only the digits that changed roll.
4. **Viewer's own reaction**: a pill with `Reacted` set has the subtle accent fill and the strong accent text. Its
   border takes a ring of the accent color mixed into the border at 45%, so it stays visible on any surface.
5. **Add button** (`AddLabel`, default "Add reaction"): 38 px wide and 32 px high, showing a smile-plus glyph. It shows
   a close glyph while the picker is open.
6. **Picker** (`PickerLabel`, default "Add a reaction"): a tray that opens above the add button with an 8 px gap. It
   pads its content by 5 px. Each option is a 40 px round toggle with a 20 px glyph, and a caption under the options
   names the highlighted option. The caption adds a check when the viewer has already chosen that option.
7. **Tip**: the pill's name and its tooltip, which appears after `TipDelay` (450 ms by default). It shows the option
   label and, when `ReactedBy` is known, the people who reacted.

### Value and changes

`Value` is two-way. Each `Reaction` holds an id, a count and the viewer's own flag. A reaction with a count of 0 is not
shown, so it leaves the bar. A reaction whose id matches no option is not shown either. When an id appears twice in
`Value`, the first entry wins.

| Action | Result in `Value` | Event |
|---|---|---|
| The viewer taps a pill that is not theirs | Count plus one, `Reacted` set to `true` | `ValueChanged` with `Change.Reacted` set to `true` |
| The viewer taps their own pill | Count minus one, `Reacted` set to `false`; a count of 0 removes the reaction | `ValueChanged` with `Change.Reacted` set to `false` |
| The viewer picks an option that has no pill yet | A new reaction with count 1 joins the end of the list | `ValueChanged` |
| Code sets `Value` | The bar shows the new list; no change is raised | None |

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ReactionsWhoReactedDemo">
    <UserControl.Resources>
        <!-- Lucide party-popper, which is not in the Arc glyph subset. -->
        <StreamGeometry x:Key="PartyPopper">
            M5.8 11.3 2 22l10.7-3.79 M4 3h.01 M22 8h.01 M15 2h.01 M22 20h.01
            M22 2l-2.24.75a2.9 2.9 0 0 0-1.96 3.12c.1.86-.57 1.63-1.45 1.63h-.38c-.86 0-1.6.6-1.76 1.44L14 10
            M22 13l-.82-.33c-.86-.34-1.82.2-1.98 1.11c-.11.7-.72 1.22-1.43 1.22H17
            M11 2l.33.82c.34.86-.2 1.82-1.11 1.98C9.52 4.9 9 5.52 9 6.23V7
            M11 13c1.93 1.93 2.83 4.17 2 5-.83.83-3.07-.07-5-2-1.93-1.93-2.83-4.17-2-5 .83-.83 3.07.07 5 2Z
        </StreamGeometry>
    </UserControl.Resources>
    <arc:Reactions x:Name="Bar" HorizontalAlignment="Left">
        <arc:ReactionOption Id="like" Label="Like" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.ThumbsUp}" />
        <arc:ReactionOption Id="love" Label="Love" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Heart}" />
        <arc:ReactionOption Id="celebrate" Label="Celebrate" Icon="{StaticResource PartyPopper}" />
        <arc:ReactionOption Id="smile" Label="Smile" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Smile}" />
        <arc:ReactionOption Id="star" Label="Star" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Star}" />
        <arc:ReactionOption Id="ship" Label="Ship it" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Zap}" />
    </arc:Reactions>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class ReactionsWhoReactedDemo : UserControl
{
    public ReactionsWhoReactedDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Bar.Value =
        [
            new Reaction("love", 4, true) { ReactedBy = ["Ada Okafor", "Jonas Berg", "Lin Park"] },
            new Reaction("celebrate", 2) { ReactedBy = ["Maya Chen", "Sam Ortiz"] },
            new Reaction("ship", 12) { ReactedBy = ["Priya Nair", "Tom Hale", "Eli Moss"] }
        ];
    }
}
```

`ValueChanged` is raised after `Value` has changed. Its `Next` property is the new value in bar order, without the
reactions whose count reached zero, and its `Change` property names the option and whether the viewer reacted.

```csharp
reactions.ValueChanged += (_, e) =>
{
    // Save e.Next with the post, and e.Change to show what the viewer did.
};
```

`Toggle(id)` performs the same change as a tap, so a keyboard shortcut or a menu item can add or remove the viewer's
reaction from code. `OpenPicker()` and `ClosePicker()` open and close the picker, and `IsPickerOpen` tells you whether
it is open.

### Binding to a view model

In an MVVM app the view model owns the saved reactions, and the bar updates them when the viewer taps. Each
`Reaction` is an immutable record, so the view model replaces the list instead of editing an item in place. With
CommunityToolkit.Mvvm:

```csharp
public partial class ReleaseNoteViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    private readonly IReleaseNoteService _notes;
    private readonly string _noteId;

    public ReleaseNoteViewModel(IReleaseNoteService notes, string noteId)
    {
        _notes = notes;
        _noteId = noteId;
    }

    [ObservableProperty]
    private IReadOnlyList<Reaction> _reactionValues = [];

    public async Task SaveReactionsAsync(IReadOnlyList<Reaction> next)
    {
        await _notes.SaveReactionsAsync(_noteId, next);
    }
}
```

```xml
<arc:Reactions Label="Reactions to Release 2026.10"
               Value="{Binding ReactionValues}"
               HorizontalAlignment="Left">
    <arc:ReactionOption Id="ship" Label="Ship it" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Zap}" />
    <arc:ReactionOption Id="love" Label="Love" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Heart}" />
    <arc:ReactionOption Id="celebrate" Label="Celebrate" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Smile}" />
</arc:Reactions>
```

```csharp
// In the view's code-behind, where the view model is available:
reactions.ValueChanged += async (_, e) => await viewModel.SaveReactionsAsync(e.Next);
```

- `Value` is two-way by default, so the bar writes each tap back to `ReactionValues` before `ValueChanged` is raised.
  Keep the binding two-way; a one-way binding makes the bar show a change that the view model never saved.
- The bar does not remember the viewer. Your server or view model decides which reactions belong to the signed-in
  user, and sets `Reacted` when it loads the list.
- Compiled bindings need `x:DataType` on the view (the examples here leave it out for brevity).

### Wrapping and width

The bar wraps its pills into rows when they do not fit. Give it a `Width` to see the wrap, or leave the width free so
the bar takes its parent's width. When a change adds a row, the bar's height springs to the new size, and the pills
glide into their new places.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ReactionsWrappingDemo">
    <UserControl.Resources>
        <!-- Lucide party-popper, which is not in the Arc glyph subset. -->
        <StreamGeometry x:Key="PartyPopper">
            M5.8 11.3 2 22l10.7-3.79 M4 3h.01 M22 8h.01 M15 2h.01 M22 20h.01
            M22 2l-2.24.75a2.9 2.9 0 0 0-1.96 3.12c.1.86-.57 1.63-1.45 1.63h-.38c-.86 0-1.6.6-1.76 1.44L14 10
            M22 13l-.82-.33c-.86-.34-1.82.2-1.98 1.11c-.11.7-.72 1.22-1.43 1.22H17
            M11 2l.33.82c.34.86-.2 1.82-1.11 1.98C9.52 4.9 9 5.52 9 6.23V7
            M11 13c1.93 1.93 2.83 4.17 2 5-.83.83-3.07-.07-5-2-1.93-1.93-2.83-4.17-2-5 .83-.83 3.07.07 5 2Z
        </StreamGeometry>
    </UserControl.Resources>
    <arc:Reactions x:Name="Bar" Width="220" HorizontalAlignment="Left">
        <arc:ReactionOption Id="like" Label="Like" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.ThumbsUp}" />
        <arc:ReactionOption Id="love" Label="Love" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Heart}" />
        <arc:ReactionOption Id="celebrate" Label="Celebrate" Icon="{StaticResource PartyPopper}" />
        <arc:ReactionOption Id="smile" Label="Smile" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Smile}" />
        <arc:ReactionOption Id="star" Label="Star" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Star}" />
        <arc:ReactionOption Id="ship" Label="Ship it" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Zap}" />
    </arc:Reactions>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class ReactionsWrappingDemo : UserControl
{
    public ReactionsWrappingDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Bar.Value = [new Reaction("like", 8), new Reaction("love", 3, true), new Reaction("celebrate", 1)];
    }
}
```

Keep the bar on one row in a dense list row or a card footer by giving it enough width for the expected number of
options. In a narrow column, the wrap is the right behavior: it keeps every pill visible without a scroll bar.

### Labels and tips

`Label` names the bar, `AddLabel` names the add button and its tooltip, and `PickerLabel` names the picker. Use a name
that says what the bar refers to, such as "Reactions to this release", so a screen reader user hears the context
before the pills.

`TipDelay` sets how long the pointer must rest on a pill before its tip shows. The default is 450 ms. `TipSelector`
builds the tip for each pill: it receives the option and the reaction and returns the content to show, or `null` to
use the default text.

```xml
<arc:Reactions Label="Reactions to this release"
               AddLabel="Add a reaction"
               TipDelay="0:0:0.6">
    <arc:ReactionOption Id="ship" Label="Ship it" />
    <arc:ReactionOption Id="star" Label="Star" />
</arc:Reactions>
```

The tip is the option label followed by the people who reacted, when your data has them. The default lists up to
three names, with "You" first when the viewer reacted. It then says how many others there are:

| Reaction data | Tip |
|---|---|
| No `ReactedBy` | "Love" |
| `Reacted` and two names | "Love · You, Ada and Lin" |
| Six people, four named | "Love · Ada, Lin, Sam and 3 others" |

### Who reacted

Set `ReactedBy` on a `Reaction` to name the people behind the count. The names are shown only in the tip, not in the
bar, so the pill stays compact. Pass the names in the order you want them to appear, most relevant first. The tip shows up to three names.

Names are optional. A count without names is still correct, and the tip falls back to the option label.

### Live counts

Counts that change on another person's screen arrive through `Value`. The bar rolls only the digits that changed, up
when the count grows and down when it shrinks, and it does not play the tap impulse on the icon, because the viewer
did not tap. A pill that appears in a live update enters the bar, and one that reaches zero leaves it.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ReactionsLiveCountsDemo">
    <UserControl.Resources>
        <!-- Lucide party-popper, which is not in the Arc glyph subset. -->
        <StreamGeometry x:Key="PartyPopper">
            M5.8 11.3 2 22l10.7-3.79 M4 3h.01 M22 8h.01 M15 2h.01 M22 20h.01
            M22 2l-2.24.75a2.9 2.9 0 0 0-1.96 3.12c.1.86-.57 1.63-1.45 1.63h-.38c-.86 0-1.6.6-1.76 1.44L14 10
            M22 13l-.82-.33c-.86-.34-1.82.2-1.98 1.11c-.11.7-.72 1.22-1.43 1.22H17
            M11 2l.33.82c.34.86-.2 1.82-1.11 1.98C9.52 4.9 9 5.52 9 6.23V7
            M11 13c1.93 1.93 2.83 4.17 2 5-.83.83-3.07-.07-5-2-1.93-1.93-2.83-4.17-2-5 .83-.83 3.07.07 5 2Z
        </StreamGeometry>
    </UserControl.Resources>
    <StackPanel Spacing="12">
        <arc:Reactions x:Name="Bar" HorizontalAlignment="Left">
            <arc:ReactionOption Id="like" Label="Like" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.ThumbsUp}" />
            <arc:ReactionOption Id="love" Label="Love" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Heart}" />
            <arc:ReactionOption Id="celebrate" Label="Celebrate" Icon="{StaticResource PartyPopper}" />
        </arc:Reactions>
        <WrapPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center" ItemSpacing="12" LineSpacing="12">
            <arc:Button Content="Someone reacts" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Click="OnSomeoneReactsClick" />
            <arc:Button Content="Someone leaves" Variant="Ghost" Size="Small" Click="OnSomeoneLeavesClick" />
        </WrapPanel>
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class ReactionsLiveCountsDemo : UserControl
{
    private readonly Random _random = new(7);

    public ReactionsLiveCountsDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Bar.Value = [new Reaction("like", 98), new Reaction("love", 9, true)];
    }

    private void OnSomeoneReactsClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        var current = Bar.Value ?? [];
        var id = _random.Next(3) switch { 0 => "like", 1 => "love", _ => "celebrate" };
        var existing = current.FirstOrDefault(r => r.Id == id);
        Bar.Value = existing is null
            ? [.. current, new Reaction(id, 1)]
            : current.Select(r => r.Id == id ? r with { Count = r.Count + 1 } : r).ToArray();
    }

    private void OnSomeoneLeavesClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        var current = Bar.Value ?? [];
        var target = current.Where(r => r.Count > (r.Reacted ? 1 : 0)).OrderBy(_ => _random.Next()).FirstOrDefault();
        if (target is not null)
        {
            Bar.Value = current.Select(r => r == target ? r with { Count = r.Count - 1 } : r).Where(r => r.Count > 0).ToArray();
        }
    }
}
```

Replace the `Value` list with a new list when the server sends an update. The bar matches reactions by `Id`, so a
pill that stays in the list keeps its identity and only its count changes. A new id gets a new pill, and a removed id
gets a pill that leaves the bar.

### Example: release note reactions

A release note in an internal changelog. The reactions sit under the summary so the team can acknowledge the release
without a reply. The bar names the release in its label, the counts show the team's responses, and the viewer's own
"Love" is highlighted. Each option name is a short verb or phrase that reads well in a tooltip. Put a short summary
above the bar so the reactions have something concrete to refer to. The bar is bound to `ReactionValues` from the view
model shown above, so the saved counts appear when the note opens.

```xml
<Border Padding="20"
        CornerRadius="12"
        BorderThickness="1"
        BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Border}"
        Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Surface}">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12">
        <TextBlock Text="Release 2026.10 is live"
                   FontSize="16"
                   FontWeight="SemiBold"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
        <TextBlock Text="Usage exports now finish up to four times faster, and the billing summary reads the new invoice schema."
                   FontSize="14"
                   TextWrapping="Wrap"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
        <arc:Reactions Label="Reactions to Release 2026.10"
                       Value="{Binding ReactionValues}"
                       HorizontalAlignment="Left">
            <arc:ReactionOption Id="ship" Label="Ship it" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Zap}" />
            <arc:ReactionOption Id="love" Label="Love" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Heart}" />
            <arc:ReactionOption Id="celebrate" Label="Celebrate" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Smile}" />
        </arc:Reactions>
    </StackPanel>
</Border>
```

```csharp
// The server returns the saved counts when the note loads; the viewer's own reaction has Reacted set.
viewModel.ReactionValues =
[
    new Reaction("ship", 12),
    new Reaction("love", 4, true) { ReactedBy = ["Ada Okafor", "Jonas Berg", "Lin Park"] },
    new Reaction("celebrate", 2)
];
```

The bar shows the reactions in the order of `Value`, and the viewer's own "Love" has the accent fill. Its tooltip reads
"Love · You, Ada Okafor, Jonas Berg and 1 other": the viewer first, up to three names in all, then the remaining count.

### Content guidelines

- **Option label**: one or two words that name the reaction in the same way people would say it: "Like", "Love",
  "Celebrate", "Ship it". The label is read aloud and shown in the tip, so avoid codes such as "thumbs_up" or
  "+1".
- **Bar label**: name the content the reactions refer to, "Reactions to Release 2026.10", not a generic "Reactions".
- **Add button**: "Add reaction" is the default and matches the picker's purpose. Keep it unless the product uses a
  different term for the same action.
- **Count wording**: the accessible name gives the count as a number ("Like, 4 reactions, including yours"). Do not
  repeat the count in the bar's `Label`.
- **Tip**: the label and the people who reacted, in sentence case, with no punctuation at the end.

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| Reactions | Reactions to Release 2026.10 |
| +1 | Like |
| Click to react | Add reaction |
| thumbs_up | Like |
| Smiley | Celebrate |

### Best practices

**Do**

- Give every option a stable `Id` that your data stores, and a `Label` that can change with the language. Changing an
  id creates a new reaction and orphans the old counts.
- Set `Reacted` from the signed-in user's data when the list loads. Without it the bar cannot show the viewer's own
  reaction, and a second tap adds a count instead of removing one.
- Save the change in `ValueChanged`, or bind `Value` to a view model that saves it. A tap that is not saved reverts
  on reload and the counts disagree between people.
- Keep the option set short, three to six options. The picker is compact by design, and a long list makes the choice
  slower than a tap.
- Name the bar with `Label` so a screen reader user knows what the reactions refer to.

**Avoid**

- Reactions for choices that need a reply. A bar that asks people to "Agree" on a proposal hides the reasons behind
  the vote; use a comment thread or a poll.
- Showing a count of zero as a pill. A zero count leaves the bar by design, so store zero counts as missing.
- Editing a `Reaction` in place in a list that the bar already shows. Records are immutable, so replace the entry with
  `with` and assign a new list, or the bar may not refresh.
- Relying on the tip for meaning. The tip appears after a delay on hover or focus, so the option label must already
  make sense alone.
- Two options with the same label. The tooltips and the screen reader names cannot tell them apart, and the viewer
  cannot choose the right one.

### Common questions

**Why is a reaction not shown in the bar?** The bar shows only reactions whose count is above zero and whose `Id`
matches an option. Check the option id against the reaction id, and set the count to a positive number.

**How do I remove a reaction the viewer made from code?** Call `Toggle(id)` for the reaction the viewer already has.
The viewer's own reaction is removed and its count goes down by one. Calling `Toggle` on a reaction the viewer did not
make adds one for them.

**Why does the count not change when another person reacts?** The control does not poll the server. Update `Value`
when your data changes, for example from a live feed or after a refresh; the counts then roll to the new values.

**Does the order of the options change the order of the pills?** No. The picker shows the options in the order they
were added. The bar shows the reactions in the order of `Value`, and a reaction added by the viewer joins the end of
that list.

**How does the viewer's own reaction survive a reload?** It does not, unless your data stores it. Save `Reacted` or
the reaction's `ReactedBy` names with the post, and load them into `Value` the next time the page opens.

## API reference

### Reactions

Arc reactions: a bar of reaction pills with counts plus an add button that opens a compact picker, like Slack's reactions on a comment, post or release note. One tap adds or removes the viewer's reaction: the count rolls (only the digits that change, in the direction it moved), the icon gets a velocity kick that stacks on quick taps (P27), the viewer's own reactions take the accent and a filled glyph. Pills scale in out of a blur and leave the bar when their count reaches zero while the rest glide into place (P26, P19); a new row grows the bar on a spring (P6). Hovering or focusing a pill shows its label and who reacted (`Tooltip`). Keyboard: Enter / Space toggles a pill or opens the picker; in the picker every arrow moves and wraps, Home / End jump, Enter picks, Escape closes and returns focus to the add button. Each change is announced politely.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Options` | `IList<ReactionOption>` | – | Every reaction the picker offers, in picker order (inline children or a bound list). |
| `Value` | `IReadOnlyList<Reaction>?` | `null` | The reactions shown, in bar order (two-way). A reaction whose count reaches zero leaves the bar. |
| `Label` | `string` | `"Reactions"` | Accessible name of the bar (default "Reactions"). |
| `AddLabel` | `string` | `"Add reaction"` | Name and tooltip of the add button (default "Add reaction"). |
| `PickerLabel` | `string` | `"Add a reaction"` | Accessible name of the picker tray (default "Add a reaction"). |
| `TipSelector` | `Func<ReactionOption, Reaction, object?>?` | `null` | Builds a pill's tooltip from its option and reaction; null uses the label followed by who reacted ("Love · You, Ada and 2 others"). |
| `TipDelay` | `TimeSpan` | `00:00:00.4500000` | How long a pointer rests on a pill before its tooltip shows (the theme sets Arc's 0.45s). |
| `PickerOffset` | `double` | `8` | Gap between the picker and the add button (the theme sets Arc's sideOffset 8). |
| `IsPickerOpen` | `bool` | – | *Read-only.* True while the picker is open. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ValueChanged` | `ReactionsValueChangedEventArgs` | Raised when the viewer adds or removes a reaction (Arc's onValueChange), after `Value` changed. |

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

### ReactionOption

One reaction the picker offers (Arc's `ReactionOption`): an id, a label and a 24×24 Lucide glyph.

### Reaction

The state of one reaction (Arc's `Reaction`): how many people chose it and whether the viewer did. A reaction whose count reaches zero leaves the bar.

### Change values

`ValueChanged` passes a `ReactionChange` with the reaction that was changed and the viewer's new state.

| Member | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `Id` | The option id the viewer tapped or picked |
| `Reacted` | `true` when the viewer reacted, `false` when they removed their reaction |

## Accessibility

- The bar is a group named by `Label`. Each pill is a toggle button, and its name gives the label, the count and
  whether the viewer is among them, such as "Like, 4 reactions, including yours".
- The picker is a toolbar with roving focus. The four arrow keys move between options and wrap around, Home and End
  go to the ends, and every option has a name.
- Enter or Space on a pill switches the viewer's reaction. Enter or Space on the add button opens the picker, and
  Escape closes it and returns focus to the add button.
- Every change is announced once through a polite status region, such as "Added Love. 4 reactions." The message is
  not shown on screen.
- When the focused pill leaves the bar, focus moves to a neighbouring pill or to the add button, so keyboard focus is
  never lost.
- Hover highlights an option in the picker only for a mouse. Touch picks an option directly, so a touch user never
  needs to hover first.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` | Moves between the pills and the add button |
| `Enter` or `Space` on a pill | Switches the viewer's reaction on or off |
| `Enter` or `Space` on the add button | Opens the picker and moves focus to its first option |
| `Right` / `Down`, `Left` / `Up` (in the picker) | Move to the next or previous option; the focus wraps at the ends |
| `Home` / `End` (in the picker) | Move to the first or last option |
| `Enter` or `Space` (in the picker) | Picks the option, toggles the viewer's reaction and returns focus to the add button |
| `Escape` (in the picker) | Closes the picker and returns focus to the add button |

## Motion

- A new pill grows in from a half size with a soft blur. A removed pill shrinks and fades. The other pills glide
  into their new places.
- The icon gets a small kick when the viewer reacts, and fast taps add up instead of restarting it.
- Counts roll only the digits that changed, up when they grow and down when they shrink.
- The picker grows out of the add button, and its options appear one after another.
- Reduced motion uses short fades only and no size springs. Off motion changes everything at once.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| A pill appears | Grows from half size out of a soft blur, with a snappy scale and a quick fade | Short fade | Immediate |
| A pill leaves at zero | Shrinks to 0.6 with a subtle blur and fades; the other pills glide | Short fade | Immediate |
| The viewer taps a reaction | The icon kicks, and quick taps add velocity | No kick | No kick |
| A count changes | Only the changed digits roll, up when growing and down when shrinking | Instant fade | Immediate |
| Rows change | The bar height springs and the pills glide | No size spring | Immediate |
| The picker opens | Grows from the add button; options appear 40 ms later, 35 ms apart | Short fade | Immediate |

## Related

- `Badge` for a fixed count that the viewer cannot change.
- `Popover` and `DropdownMenu` for other content or choices that open from a button.
- `SwipeActions` for row actions in a touch list.
- `HoldToConfirm` for a single destructive action that must not run on a stray tap.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `CommentThread` | The response needs words, and the comment should keep its author and time |
| `ChatThread` | The conversation is a sequence of messages between people |
| `Badge` | The number is fixed and the viewer cannot change it |
| `Select` / `MorphSelect` | The person picks one value from a list |
| `SwipeActions` | The action belongs to one row in a touch list |
| `Slider` | The person sets a quantity on a scale |

# Dropdown menu

> A focused list of actions anchored to a trigger.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/dropdown-menu

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.DropdownMenuActionsDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12">
        <WrapPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center" ItemSpacing="12" LineSpacing="12">
            <arc:DropdownMenu Label="Actions" ItemClicked="OnItemClicked">
                <arc:MenuEntry Header="Rename" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Pencil}" />
                <arc:MenuEntry Header="Duplicate" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Copy}" />
                <arc:MenuEntry Header="Delete"
                               Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Trash2}"
                               IsDestructive="True"
                               HasSeparatorBefore="True" />
            </arc:DropdownMenu>
            <arc:DropdownMenu Label="Share" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Share2}">
                <arc:MenuEntry Header="Copy link" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Link}" />
                <arc:MenuEntry Header="Email" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Mail}" />
                <arc:MenuEntry Header="Export PDF" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Download}" IsEnabled="False" />
                <arc:MenuEntry Header="Embed" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Code}" />
            </arc:DropdownMenu>
        </WrapPanel>
        <TextBlock x:Name="Status"
                   Text="Pick an action."
                   FontSize="14"
                   TextWrapping="Wrap"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class DropdownMenuActionsDemo : UserControl
{
    public DropdownMenuActionsDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
    }

    private void OnItemClicked(object? sender, MenuEntryClickedEventArgs e) => Status.Text = $"Selected: {e.Header}";
}
```

## When to use

A dropdown menu puts a short group of commands behind a labelled trigger. The trigger is a visible control with a
name, so people can find the actions without a gesture, and the menu closes after a choice so the page stays in
place. It fits the places where an object or a view has several commands, and the commands do not deserve buttons of
their own.

- **Row actions in a data table**: Rename, Duplicate, Archive and Delete behind the more button of an invoice or
  customer row in a `Table`. Each row gets one trigger, and the destructive row sits last behind a divider.
- **Page header actions in an admin console**: Export, Share and Print for a report page. The page keeps one visible
  entry point for the secondary commands, and the primary action stays a button beside it.
- **Sort and view options in a list toolbar**: Sort by Newest, Oldest or Name as radio rows, and View options as
  check rows, on the toolbar of an order list. The trigger label shows the current choice, such as "Sort: Newest".
- **Display settings that people flip in one visit**: Show sidebar, Show minimap and Wrap lines as check rows that stay
  open, so several options change without reopening the menu.
- **Export and share in a billing or reporting page**: Export CSV, Export PDF and Send to accounting in one group,
  with the destructive or irreversible action last.

## When not to use

- **A default action with a few alternatives**: use `SplitButton`. The default runs on the main button and the menu
  holds the less common choices, so the primary action is one click away.
- **Right-click actions on a piece of content**: use `ContextMenu`, which opens at the pointer on the content itself
  and has no visible trigger.
- **The account menu behind an avatar, with identity and theme**: use `UserMenu`, which carries the profile header,
  the theme switch and sign out.
- **A value chosen from a list in a form**: use `Select` or `Combobox`. They hold the value, a label and a validation
  state, which a menu does not.
- **Options that are always visible and compared side by side**: use `SegmentedControl` for a few exclusive views, or a
  `Checkbox` group for independent options. A menu hides the options until it opens.

## Usage

`DropdownMenu` derives from Avalonia's `TemplatedControl`. Its built-in trigger is an Arc `Button` (Secondary, Small),
and its rows live in a `MenuSurface` that it creates and owns. The control adds the label morph, the chevron, the
keyboard model and the motion, and the rows are the same `MenuEntry` items that the other Arc menus use. Declare the
rows inline, and set `Label` to the text on the trigger.

Declare the rows inline. Use `MenuEntry` for a command, `MenuEntrySeparator` for a divider and `MenuEntryLabel` for a
group heading.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:DropdownMenu Label="Actions">
        <arc:MenuEntry Header="Rename" />
        <arc:MenuEntry Header="Duplicate" />
        <arc:MenuEntry Header="Delete"
                       IsDestructive="True"
                       HasSeparatorBefore="True" />
    </arc:DropdownMenu>
</UserControl>
```

Set an icon from code with `ArcIcons`, a 24x24 Lucide geometry.

```csharp
var rename = (MenuEntry)menu.Items[0];
rename.Icon = ArcIcons.Pencil;
```

### Anatomy

1. **Trigger** (the built-in `arc:Button`, or the control in `Trigger`): 36 px tall, the Secondary small button. Hover
   and the open state change the border to the strong border color; the open state also uses the muted surface color.
   The trigger never scales when pressed.
2. **Leading icon** (`Icon`): a 16 px glyph in the secondary text color. It is hidden when `Icon` is null.
3. **Label** (`Label`): the trigger text, truncated with an ellipsis within its maximum width. Changing it morphs the
   trigger: the new label rises in while the trigger width springs to fit.
4. **Chevron**: 15 px with a 1.8 px stroke, in the muted text color. It turns 180 degrees while the menu is open.
5. **Menu panel**: at least 192 px wide (12 rem) and placed 6 px away from the trigger. `Alignment` sets the edge it
   lines up with; the default is `End`. `Side` sets the edge it opens from: `Bottom` by default, or `Top`, `Left`
   or `Right`. The menu flips to another side when there is no room.
6. **Rows** (`MenuEntry`): 36 px tall in the Dropdown variant. A row shows its icon, its header, an optional shortcut
   hint at the end, and a check or a dot for toggle rows.
7. **Dividers and group labels** (`HasSeparatorBefore`, `MenuEntrySeparator`, `MenuEntryLabel`): a line above a row,
   or a non-selectable heading that groups the rows below it.

Keep the built-in trigger for a standard action group. Replace it with `Trigger` when the trigger must be an icon
button, a row "more" button or a control that already exists on the page; the menu then anchors to that control.

### Choosing the trigger, side and alignment

- Use the built-in trigger with a text `Label` when the group needs a name, such as "Actions" or "Sort: Newest". The
  visible text tells a keyboard user what the menu does before it opens.
- Use `Trigger` with a ghost button and an ellipsis glyph for a row "more" menu. `Label` names only the built-in
  trigger, so set `AutomationProperties.Name` on the custom button to name the row it belongs to.
- Keep `Side` at `Bottom` for toolbars at the top of a page. Use `Top` for a control at the bottom of a window, and
  `Right` or `Left` only for a control at the edge of a sidebar.
- Keep `Alignment` at `End` for a trigger at the right of a toolbar, so the menu grows back toward the content. Use
  `Start` for a trigger at the left edge.

### Handling a selection

`ItemClicked` reports the activated row. The menu closes after the event unless the row sets `StaysOpenOnClick`.

```csharp
menu.ItemClicked += (_, e) => status.Text = $"Selected: {e.Header}";
```

Use one handler for a group that shares a purpose, and read `e.Entry` to tell the rows apart. Use the row's own `Click`
event when one row has its own behavior. The data item behind a generated row is in `e.Item`.

### Live label and radio rows

Set `Label` from code to change the trigger text. Radio rows with the same `GroupName` are mutually exclusive, and
choosing one closes the menu. Check rows (`ToggleType="CheckBox"`) with `StaysOpenOnClick="True"` stay open so
several options can be flipped in one visit.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.DropdownMenuLabelAndTogglesDemo">
    <WrapPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center" ItemSpacing="12" LineSpacing="12">
        <arc:DropdownMenu x:Name="Sort"
                          Label="Sort: Newest"
                          Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.ArrowUpDown}"
                          Alignment="Start"
                          ItemClicked="OnSortClicked">
            <arc:MenuEntryLabel Text="Sort by" />
            <arc:MenuEntry Header="Newest" ToggleType="Radio" GroupName="sort" IsChecked="True" />
            <arc:MenuEntry Header="Oldest" ToggleType="Radio" GroupName="sort" />
            <arc:MenuEntry Header="Name" ToggleType="Radio" GroupName="sort" />
            <arc:MenuEntry Header="Size" ToggleType="Radio" GroupName="sort" />
        </arc:DropdownMenu>
        <arc:DropdownMenu Label="View" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.LayoutGrid}">
            <arc:MenuEntry Header="Show sidebar"
                           ToggleType="CheckBox"
                           IsChecked="True"
                           StaysOpenOnClick="True"
                           InputGesture="Ctrl+B" />
            <arc:MenuEntry Header="Show minimap"
                           ToggleType="CheckBox"
                           StaysOpenOnClick="True"
                           InputGesture="Ctrl+M" />
            <arc:MenuEntry Header="Wrap lines"
                           ToggleType="CheckBox"
                           IsChecked="True"
                           StaysOpenOnClick="True" />
            <arc:MenuEntrySeparator />
            <arc:MenuEntryLabel Text="Density" />
            <arc:MenuEntry Header="Comfortable" ToggleType="Radio" GroupName="density" IsChecked="True" />
            <arc:MenuEntry Header="Compact" ToggleType="Radio" GroupName="density" />
        </arc:DropdownMenu>
    </WrapPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class DropdownMenuLabelAndTogglesDemo : UserControl
{
    public DropdownMenuLabelAndTogglesDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
    }

    // A new label rises in while the trigger width springs.
    private void OnSortClicked(object? sender, MenuEntryClickedEventArgs e) => Sort.Label = $"Sort: {e.Header}";
}
```

Choose a radio row when exactly one option applies, such as a sort order: the trigger label then states the current
choice. Choose a check row when each option is independent, such as which columns to show. Keep a radio group to
about five options; a longer choice belongs in a `Select`.

### Data-driven rows and a custom trigger

`ItemsSource` creates one row per item. `Trigger` replaces the built-in button with any control. The menu anchors to
that control, and a `Button` opens it on click.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             xmlns:generic="using:System.Collections.Generic"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.DropdownMenuCustomTriggerDemo">
    <WrapPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center" ItemSpacing="12" LineSpacing="12">
        <arc:DropdownMenu>
            <arc:DropdownMenu.Trigger>
                <arc:Button Variant="Ghost" Size="Small">
                    <arc:ArcGlyph Data="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Ellipsis}" />
                </arc:Button>
            </arc:DropdownMenu.Trigger>
            <arc:DropdownMenu.ItemsSource>
                <generic:List x:TypeArguments="x:String">
                    <x:String>Move to folder</x:String>
                    <x:String>Make a copy</x:String>
                    <x:String>Version history</x:String>
                </generic:List>
            </arc:DropdownMenu.ItemsSource>
        </arc:DropdownMenu>
    </WrapPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```xml
<arc:DropdownMenu ItemsSource="{Binding FileActions}" Side="Bottom">
    <arc:DropdownMenu.Trigger>
        <Button Content="..." />
    </arc:DropdownMenu.Trigger>
</arc:DropdownMenu>
```

Data-driven rows take an `ItemTemplate` for their header when the items are not `MenuEntry` objects. The item behind
each row is reported in `ItemClicked` as `e.Item`, so the handler can run the command for that item.

### Opening from code

```csharp
menu.Open(focusFirst: true);
menu.Close();
```

`Open(true)` opens the menu with its first row highlighted, as Enter or ArrowDown does on the trigger. `IsOpen` is
two-way, so a view model can open the menu by setting it. A menu that starts open with `IsOpen` set in XAML does not
take focus.

### MenuSurface

`MenuSurface` is the reusable surface behind every Arc menu. Open it from code against any anchor. Its rows, its
keyboard model and its motion are the same as the dropdown's, but it has no trigger of its own.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.DropdownMenuMenuSurfaceDemo">
    <UserControl.Resources>
        <arc:MenuSurface x:Key="DraftMenu" Alignment="Start" AnchorGap="4">
            <arc:MenuEntry Header="Save as draft"
                           Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.FileText}"
                           InputGestureText="⌘S" />
            <arc:MenuEntry Header="Schedule" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Clock}" />
            <arc:MenuEntry Header="Discard"
                           Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Trash2}"
                           IsDestructive="True"
                           HasSeparatorBefore="True" />
        </arc:MenuSurface>
    </UserControl.Resources>
    <WrapPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center" ItemSpacing="12" LineSpacing="12">
        <arc:Button x:Name="Anchor"
                    Content="Open a MenuSurface"
                    Variant="Secondary"
                    IsPressScaleEnabled="False"
                    Click="OnAnchorClick" />
    </WrapPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class DropdownMenuMenuSurfaceDemo : UserControl
{
    public DropdownMenuMenuSurfaceDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
    }

    // The surface is opened from code against any anchor, here the button.
    private void OnAnchorClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        var surface = (MenuSurface)this.FindResource("DraftMenu")!;
        if (surface.IsOpen)
        {
            surface.Close(returnFocus: false);
        }
        else
        {
            surface.Open(Anchor);
        }
    }
}
```

Use a `MenuSurface` declared as a resource when several controls share one menu, and pass the anchor in
`Open(anchor)`. A bare surface does not react to the anchor's clicks; attach it with `DropdownMenu.Menu` when the
control should toggle the menu itself.

### Binding to a view model

A dropdown usually changes the page it sits on. The view model owns the label, the choice and the commands; the
menu shows them and reports the choice back. Bind the label and the items in XAML, and set the commands in code.

```csharp
public interface IExportService
{
    Task StartCsvAsync(string filter);
}

public partial class InvoiceListViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    private readonly IExportService _exports;

    public InvoiceListViewModel(IExportService exports) => _exports = exports;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private string _sortLabel = "Sort: Newest";

    [ObservableProperty]
    private string _filter = "status:open";

    [RelayCommand]
    private async Task ExportCsvAsync()
    {
        // Start the export for the current filter.
        await _exports.StartCsvAsync(Filter);
    }
}
```

```xml
<arc:DropdownMenu Label="{Binding SortLabel}"
                  Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.ArrowUpDown}"
                  Alignment="Start">
    <arc:MenuEntryLabel Text="Sort by" />
    <arc:MenuEntry Header="Newest" ToggleType="Radio" GroupName="sort" IsChecked="True" />
    <arc:MenuEntry Header="Oldest" ToggleType="Radio" GroupName="sort" />
</arc:DropdownMenu>
```

```csharp
menu.Items.Add(new MenuEntry { Header = "Export CSV", Command = viewModel.ExportCsvCommand });
menu.ItemClicked += (_, e) => viewModel.SortLabel = $"Sort: {e.Header}";
```

- `Label` is bound one-way; the view model changes it and the trigger morphs. Use `ItemClicked` to write the choice
  back, because a radio row's `IsChecked` is changed by the menu itself.
- A row's `Command` runs when the row is activated, and the row is disabled while the command cannot execute. Use
  `[RelayCommand]` from CommunityToolkit.Mvvm and its `CanExecute` to disable a row that does not apply.
- Set `Command` in code for rows that are created in code. Rows declared inline in XAML are part of the menu, so keep
  their logic in `ItemClicked`.

### Focus and dismissal

The trigger is the menu's anchor and the place focus returns to. A keyboard opening puts the highlight on a row, and a
pointer opening leaves the highlight off. The menu closes on Escape or Tab (focus returns to the trigger), on a choice
that does not stay open, on an outside press, and when the trigger leaves the visual tree.

Rows that change state keep the menu open only when they say so. A check row that people flip several times sets
`StaysOpenOnClick="True"`. A radio row closes the menu, because a choice is final. A dropdown holds a short list: its
rows are not virtualized, so a list of several hundred items belongs in a `Combobox` or on a page with search.

### Example: invoice list page header

The invoice page header has one primary action, a visible Export menu and a Sort menu that states the current order in
its label. Export groups the file formats and puts the irreversible action last behind a divider. The Export trigger
names the action in its text, so people read what the menu does before they open it. Commands run from the view model,
and the labels follow the state.

```xml
<DockPanel>
    <TextBlock DockPanel.Dock="Left"
               Text="Invoices"
               FontSize="22"
               FontWeight="SemiBold"
               VerticalAlignment="Center"
               Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
    <StackPanel Orientation="Horizontal" Spacing="8" HorizontalAlignment="Right">
        <arc:DropdownMenu Label="Sort: Newest"
                          Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.ArrowUpDown}"
                          Alignment="End">
            <arc:MenuEntryLabel Text="Sort by" />
            <arc:MenuEntry Header="Newest" ToggleType="Radio" GroupName="sort" IsChecked="True" />
            <arc:MenuEntry Header="Oldest" ToggleType="Radio" GroupName="sort" />
            <arc:MenuEntry Header="Amount" ToggleType="Radio" GroupName="sort" />
        </arc:DropdownMenu>
        <arc:DropdownMenu Label="Export" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Download}">
            <arc:MenuEntry Header="Export CSV" />
            <arc:MenuEntry Header="Export PDF" />
            <arc:MenuEntry Header="Send to accounting" />
            <arc:MenuEntry Header="Void selected invoices"
                           Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Trash2}"
                           IsDestructive="True"
                           HasSeparatorBefore="True" />
        </arc:DropdownMenu>
    </StackPanel>
</DockPanel>
```

### Content guidelines

A trigger label is a short phrase that says what the menu does or what it currently shows. Each row is a verb and its
object, or a choice in a group that has a heading.

- Use one verb or noun for a menu that acts, such as "Export" or "Actions". Use "Name: value" when the label shows
  a state, such as "Sort: Newest".
- Write rows in sentence case, with the verb first: "Export CSV", not "CSV export".
- Name the object in a destructive row: "Void selected invoices", "Delete file".
- Keep a trigger label under about 18 characters; the trigger is a toolbar control and a long label pushes the toolbar.
- Use a `MenuEntryLabel` heading for each group of radio rows, so the group has a name.

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| Sort | Sort: Newest |
| More options | Actions |
| Export data | Export CSV |
| Delete | Delete file |
| Click to change view | View |

### Best practices

**Do**

- Keep a group to two to seven rows. A longer list needs search, which a menu does not provide.
- Put the destructive row last with `HasSeparatorBefore="True"`, and name what it removes in its header.
- Use radio rows for one choice that applies to the whole page, and check rows for independent options.
- Keep the trigger label in step with the state, so the page shows the current sort or view before the menu opens.
- Give a custom trigger the same name as its action with `AutomationProperties.Name`, because `Label` names only the
  built-in trigger.

**Avoid**

- Putting a form value in a dropdown. A value that feeds a form needs a `Select` or a `Combobox`, which hold the value,
  the label and the validation state.
- Hiding the only route to an action. A primary action belongs on a visible button, because a menu is one extra step.
- Changing the rows while the menu is open. The rows are read at open; update the list before the trigger opens it.
- Using a menu for two actions. Two actions read better as two buttons or a `ButtonGroup`.
- Relying on a color to flag the destructive row. Its header names the object, so the meaning survives without color.

### Common questions

**Why does my check row close the menu?** A row closes the menu after a choice unless it sets `StaysOpenOnClick="True"`.
Add that attribute to every check row that people might flip several times.

**How do I change the trigger text when a choice is made?** Set `Label` in the `ItemClicked` handler, or bind it to a
view model property. The new label rises in with the morph motion while the width springs to fit.

**Can I open the menu from code?** Yes. Call `Open()` to show it under the trigger, or `Open(focusFirst: true)` to start
with the first row highlighted. Both work once the trigger is part of a window.

**How do I use a custom control as the trigger?** Set `Trigger` to any control. The menu anchors to that control, and a
`Button` toggles it on click. For a control that already exists on the page, attach the menu with `DropdownMenu.Menu`
instead.

**Which side does the menu open on when there is no room?** It flips to the other side. `Side` is the preferred edge,
and the menu moves when the window does not have room for it.

**What happens when the menu has many rows?** The menu stops at 384 px and scrolls beyond that. It also never grows past
the room the window leaves beside the trigger. Set `MaxDropDownHeight` to change the limit. For long lists of values,
such as dozens of models to choose from, prefer a `Select` or a `Combobox`: they draw only the visible options and add
search.

## API reference

### DropdownMenu

A focused list of actions anchored to a labelled trigger (Arc dropdown menu). The trigger shows an optional icon, the `Label` (a new label rises in from a soft blur while the trigger width springs) and a chevron that turns on the CSS spring while open. The menu grows from the trigger edge on Arc's 580ms CSS spring with a 160ms fade, one highlight glides between rows for the pointer and jumps for the keyboard, and rows fade in with a short stagger. Rows are declared inline (`<arc:MenuEntry Header="Rename" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Pencil}"/>`) or supplied with `ItemsSource`. Replace the built-in trigger with `Trigger` (any control; buttons toggle the menu on click and never press-scale). Enter, Space or ArrowDown on the trigger open the menu on the first row; Escape closes it and returns focus to the trigger.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Menu` | `MenuSurface?` | `null` | *Attached.* Turns any control into a dropdown trigger for a `MenuSurface`: clicks (buttons) or taps toggle the menu, Enter / Space / ArrowDown open it on the first row, ArrowUp on the last, Escape returns focus to the control, and Arc buttons stop press-scaling while they anchor the menu. Used by split buttons, button groups and row "more" buttons: `<arc:Button arc:DropdownMenu.Menu="{StaticResource RowMenu}"/>`. |
| `Label` | `string?` | `"Actions"` | Trigger text (Arc: required). Changing it morphs the trigger. |
| `Icon` | `Geometry?` | `null` | Leading icon of the built-in trigger (a 24x24 Lucide geometry such as `ArcIcons.Settings`). |
| `Trigger` | `object?` | `null` | Custom trigger content that replaces the built-in button (the menu anchors to it). |
| `IsOpen` | `bool` | `false` | Whether the menu is open (two-way). |
| `Side` | `MenuSide` | `Bottom` | Edge of the trigger the menu opens from: Bottom (default), Top, Left or Right. |
| `Alignment` | `MenuAlignment` | `End` | Menu alignment against the trigger (Arc: end). |
| `MaxDropDownHeight` | `double` | `NaN` | Maximum height of the menu; longer menus scroll. NaN (default) uses the theme's 384px. The menu never grows past the room the window leaves beside the trigger, whatever this is set to. |
| `ItemsSource` | `IEnumerable?` | `null` | Data items shown as one row each; ItemTemplate renders them when set. |
| `ItemTemplate` | `IDataTemplate?` | `null` | Template that renders each ItemsSource item as a row. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ItemClicked` | `MenuEntryClickedEventArgs` | Raised when a row is activated. |
| `Opened` | `RoutedEventArgs` | Raised when the menu opens. |
| `Closed` | `RoutedEventArgs` | Raised when the menu closes. |

Pseudo-classes: `:open`, `:custom-trigger`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

### MenuEntry

One row of a `MenuSurface`: a leading icon (a Lucide `Geometry` such as `{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Pencil}`, or any control), a header, an optional shortcut hint and the check or radio indicator of toggle rows. Rows never draw their own hover or focus fill: the surface's shared highlight glides to the row under the pointer and jumps to the keyboard position. Activation runs `Command`, raises `Click` and the surface's `ItemClicked`, then closes the menu unless `StaysOpenOnClick` is set.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Header` | `object?` | `null` | The row label (strings ellipsize; any content is accepted). Also the typeahead text unless `TextSearch.Text` is set. |
| `HeaderTemplate` | `IDataTemplate?` | `null` | Data template that renders the header; without one, a string header is drawn as ellipsizing text. |
| `Icon` | `object?` | `null` | Leading icon: a 24x24 Lucide `Geometry` (drawn as a 16px stroke glyph) or any control. |
| `InputGesture` | `KeyGesture?` | `null` | Shortcut shown as a quiet hint at the row end (display only; bind the key with a hot key yourself). |
| `InputGestureText` | `string?` | `null` | Free-form shortcut hint (for example "⌘ ,"); wins over `InputGesture`. |
| `Command` | `ICommand?` | `null` | Command run when the row is activated; the row is disabled while the command cannot execute. |
| `CommandParameter` | `object?` | `null` | Parameter passed to Command when the row is activated. |
| `IsDestructive` | `bool` | `false` | Danger text and icon, and a danger-tinted highlight. Put destructive rows last and name what they destroy. |
| `ToggleType` | `MenuEntryToggleType` | `None` | How the row toggles when activated: None for a command row, CheckBox, or Radio. |
| `IsChecked` | `bool` | `false` | Checked state (two-way). Rows without an icon show a check (or a dot for radio rows) when checked. |
| `GroupName` | `string?` | `null` | Radio rows with the same group name (within one surface) are mutually exclusive. |
| `HasSeparatorBefore` | `bool` | `false` | Draws a separator line above the row (Arc's `separatorBefore`). |
| `StaysOpenOnClick` | `bool` | `false` | Keeps the menu open after activation (toggles that people flip several times). |
| `Variant` | `MenuSurfaceVariant` | `Dropdown` | Inherited from the owning `MenuSurface`; selects the row geometry. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Click` | `RoutedEventArgs` | Raised when the row is activated (pointer release, Enter or Space), before the menu closes. |

Pseudo-classes: `:highlighted`, `:pressed`, `:checked`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

## Accessibility

- The trigger is announced with its `Label` and reports whether the menu is expanded.
- Rows have the menu item role. Typeahead moves to a row by its first letters, and disabled rows are skipped.
- Enter, Space or ArrowDown on the trigger opens the menu on the first row. Escape closes it and returns focus to the
  trigger.
- A destructive row is marked by its colour only, so its `Header` should say what will be deleted.
- Icons and the highlight are hidden from assistive technology.
- Name the trigger with a `Label` that says what the menu does, such as "Sort: Newest" or "Export". A custom,
  text-free trigger needs its own `AutomationProperties.Name`, because `Label` names only the built-in trigger.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Enter`, `Space` or `ArrowDown` on the trigger | Opens the menu with the first row highlighted |
| `ArrowUp` on the trigger | Opens the menu with the last row highlighted |
| Click or tap on the trigger | Toggles the menu; the menu opens with no row highlighted |
| `ArrowDown` / `ArrowUp` | Move the highlight to the next or previous row; the list loops and skips disabled rows |
| `Home` / `End` | Move the highlight to the first or last row |
| Letters | Typeahead moves to a row whose text starts with the typed letters |
| `Enter` / `Space` in the menu | Activates the highlighted row, then closes the menu unless the row stays open |
| `Escape` / `Tab` | Closes the menu and returns focus to the trigger |

## Motion

- The menu grows from the trigger edge on a spring with a short fade. Closing is quicker and smaller.
- One highlight glides between rows for the pointer and jumps for the keyboard. Rows fade in with a short stagger.
- A new `Label` rises in with a soft blur while the trigger width adjusts to it. The chevron turns when the menu opens.
- Reduced motion removes the scale and the glide and keeps a quick fade. Off shows the menu at once.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| Menu opens | The menu grows from the trigger edge, from a 5 px offset and 0.97 scale, on a 580 ms spring with a 160 ms fade | Quick fade, no scale | Immediate |
| Menu closes | Quicker and smaller: 130 ms, half the offset, scaling to 0.985 | Quick fade | Immediate |
| Highlight moves | The pointer highlight glides on a snappy spring; the keyboard highlight jumps | The highlight jumps | Immediate |
| Rows appear | Each row fades in over 240 ms, staggered 35 ms apart | Quick fade | Immediate |
| `Label` changes | The new label rises 0.3 em with a soft blur and the trigger width springs to fit | Instant fade | Immediate |
| Chevron | Turns 180 degrees on the spring as the menu opens | Turns at once | Immediate |

## Related

- `ContextMenu` for secondary actions on a selected object, opened by right-click.
- `SplitButton` when one action is the default and the menu holds the alternatives.
- `UserMenu` for the account entry point in an app's top bar.
- `MenuSurface` is the shared menu popup, for anchoring a menu to any control.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `ContextMenu` | The actions belong to one object and should open at the pointer |
| `SplitButton` | One action is the default and the menu holds the alternatives |
| `ButtonGroup` | The commands are a row of related buttons rather than a hidden list |
| `UserMenu` | The menu is the account behind the avatar, with identity and theme |
| `Select` / `Combobox` | The menu picks a value that feeds a form |
| `MenuSurface` | You need a menu on a control that is not a dropdown trigger |

using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class ContextMenuFileTileDemo : UserControl

        InitializeComponent();

    private void OnReportItemClicked(object? sender, MenuEntryClickedEventArgs e)
        => Status.Text = $"Q3 report.pdf: {e.Header}";

        => Status.Text = $"Launch.png: {e.Header}";
