## When to use

A context menu keeps the secondary actions for one object next to that object. A file tile, a dashboard card or a
row in a table shows its content, and the actions appear at the pointer or under the target when someone asks for
them. The primary actions stay in the page's toolbar; the context menu only holds what people do to one item at a
time.

- **Files and assets in a shared folder**: Copy link, Rename, Move to folder and Move to trash on a file tile in a
  workspace library. The people who manage files learn the gesture quickly, and the toolbar stays for upload and
  new folder.
- **Cards in an analytics dashboard**: Duplicate chart, Export CSV and Remove from dashboard on a metric card such as
  Revenue by region. A card is not a button, so a menu adds actions without a visible menu button on every card.
- **Records in a billing or order console**: Copy invoice ID, Resend receipt and Void invoice on a row of an invoice
  list. The row keeps its click target for opening the record, and the menu is for the less common actions.
- **Developer and log tools**: Copy value, Copy path and Filter by this key on a node of a JSON or log viewer, where
  the object is the data and the actions are about the data.
- **Short, flat lists with one destructive row**: a few actions on one object, with the destructive row last and set
  apart by a separator.

## When not to use

- **Actions that people must find without a right-click or a tap**: use `DropdownMenu` with a visible trigger. A menu
  that opens on a gesture is easy to miss, and keyboard and screen reader users need a labelled control to start from.
- **Touch-first lists that reveal actions by a swipe**: use `SwipeActions`, which matches the swipe that phone users
  expect on a row.
- **A target that needs its own click**: use a `Button` beside it. A plain click or tap on the wrapped content also
  opens the menu, so a card that opens its record on click should not be wrapped in a `ContextMenu`.
- **A default action with a few alternatives**: use `SplitButton`. It keeps the default action one click away and
  puts the alternatives in its menu.
- **A list of choices that feeds a form**: use `Select`, `Combobox` or `RadioGroup`. They carry a value, a label and
  a validation state, and a menu does not.
- **Account settings and the sign-out action**: use `UserMenu`, which sits behind the avatar in the top bar.

## Usage

`ContextMenu` derives from Avalonia's `ContentControl`. The content is the target: any single element, which keeps its
own look and its own layout. The control adds a menu surface (a `MenuSurface` in the Context variant), the row
collection `Items`, and the wiring that opens the menu on a right-click, on the ContextMenu key, on Shift+F10 and on a
plain click or tap. Because it is a `ContentControl`, the usual content properties (`Content`, `ContentTemplate`,
`Padding`) apply to the target.

Wrap the target in `ContextMenu` and set its `Label`. The content is the target. Add the rows from code to `Items`. In
the snippet below, `file` is the `ContextMenu`.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:ContextMenu Label="Actions for Q3 report.pdf">
        <Border Width="220" Height="120" Padding="16" CornerRadius="18" BorderThickness="1">
            <TextBlock Text="Q3 report.pdf" />
        </Border>
    </arc:ContextMenu>
</UserControl>
```

```csharp
file.Items.Add(new MenuEntry { Header = "Copy link", Icon = ArcIcons.Copy });
file.Items.Add(new MenuEntry { Header = "Delete file", Icon = ArcIcons.Trash2, IsDestructive = true });
```

The same rows can be declared in XAML under `<arc:ContextMenu.Items>`, which is how the demo on this page is written.

### Anatomy

1. **Target** (`Content`): the element the menu belongs to. The theme sets its background to transparent and removes
   the focus adorner, so the menu is the only response to a press. Give the target its own visible shape (a border,
   a background and a corner radius), as the demo does, so people see what they act on.
2. **Menu panel** (`Menu`): the surface that holds the rows, announced with the `Label`. In the Context variant, rows
   are 34 px tall, the panel is at least 208 px (13 rem) wide, and it is never taller than 300 px; a longer list
   scrolls inside the panel.
3. **Icon slot** (`Icon` on a `MenuEntry`): a 24 by 24 Lucide geometry drawn as a 16 px stroke glyph. A row without an
   icon shows a check when `IsChecked` is true and a quiet ellipsis when it is not, so every row keeps the same
   left edge.
4. **Label** (`Header`): the row text. Long labels end in an ellipsis instead of wrapping. The header is also the
   text that typeahead matches.
5. **Shortcut hint** (`InputGestureText` or `InputGesture`): quiet text at the end of the row. It is display only; the
   app binds the key itself.
6. **Destructive row** (`IsDestructive`): the text and icon take the danger color, and the highlight is danger-tinted
   when the row is highlighted.
7. **Separator and group label** (`HasSeparatorBefore`, `MenuEntrySeparator`, `MenuEntryLabel`): a divider line above
   a row, or a non-selectable heading that groups the rows below it.
8. **Highlight**: one shared highlight covers the row under the pointer or the keyboard position. Rows do not draw
   their own hover fill.

### Handling a selection

Activating a row raises the row's `Click` event, runs its `Command`, raises the menu's `ItemClicked` and then closes
the menu, unless the row sets `StaysOpenOnClick`. `ItemClicked` reports the activated row in `Entry`, the data item
behind it in `Item`, and its `Header`. The menu's own `Opened` and `Closed` events fire around the open and close
motion.

```csharp
file.ItemClicked += (_, e) => status.Text = $"Q3 report.pdf: {e.Header}";
```

Use `ItemClicked` when one handler serves every row, and the row's `Click` event when one row needs its own work.
Keep the handler short. The menu closes after it returns, so long work belongs in a command or an asynchronous
method that the handler starts.

### Checked rows

A row without an icon shows a check when `IsChecked` is true. Set `ToggleType="CheckBox"` when the row is a switch:
activation flips `IsChecked` for you and the row shows a check. The row in the example below is a plain row that
the handler toggles itself.

```csharp
var pinned = new MenuEntry { Header = "Pinned", IsChecked = true };
pinned.Click += (_, _) => pinned.IsChecked = !pinned.IsChecked;
image.Items.Add(pinned);
```

Use either the handler or `ToggleType`, not both, or the value flips twice. A toggle row that should stay open while
several options are changed sets `StaysOpenOnClick="True"`.

### Data-driven rows

`ItemsSource` creates one row per item. `MenuEntry` instances are used as they are; other data needs an
`ItemTemplate`, which renders the header of each generated row. Bind the collection on the `ContextMenu` itself, which
sits in the page's tree, and read the data item in `ItemClicked`.

```xml
<arc:ContextMenu Label="File actions" ItemsSource="{Binding FileActions}">
    <arc:ContextMenu.ItemTemplate>
        <DataTemplate>
            <TextBlock Text="{Binding Name}" />
        </DataTemplate>
    </arc:ContextMenu.ItemTemplate>
    <Border Width="220" Height="96" CornerRadius="18" BorderThickness="1" />
</arc:ContextMenu>
```

### Attaching a menu to any control

`arc:ContextMenu.Menu` gives any control a right-click menu without wrapping it. The attached surface becomes a
Context menu unless its `Variant` was set, and it closes on scroll or resize unless `ClosesOnViewportChange` was set.
Use this form when the element already has a template or a parent that you do not want to change.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ContextMenuAttachedDemo">
    <WrapPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center" ItemSpacing="12" LineSpacing="12">
        <Border Width="220"
                Height="96"
                CornerRadius="18"
                BorderThickness="1"
                Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Surface}"
                BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Border}">
            <arc:ContextMenu.Menu>
                <arc:MenuSurface>
                    <arc:MenuEntry Header="New folder" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Folder}" />
                    <arc:MenuEntry Header="Paste"
                                   Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Copy}"
                                   InputGestureText="⌘V" />
                    <arc:MenuEntry Header="Refresh" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.RefreshCw}" />
                </arc:MenuSurface>
            </arc:ContextMenu.Menu>
            <TextBlock Text="Right-click anywhere here"
                       FontSize="14"
                       TextWrapping="Wrap"
                       HorizontalAlignment="Center"
                       VerticalAlignment="Center"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
        </Border>
    </WrapPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```xml
<Border Width="220" Height="96" CornerRadius="18" BorderThickness="1">
    <arc:ContextMenu.Menu>
        <arc:MenuSurface>
            <arc:MenuEntry Header="New folder" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Folder}" />
            <arc:MenuEntry Header="Paste" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Copy}" InputGestureText="⌘V" />
            <arc:MenuEntry Header="Refresh" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.RefreshCw}" />
        </arc:MenuSurface>
    </arc:ContextMenu.Menu>
    <TextBlock Text="Right-click anywhere here" HorizontalAlignment="Center" VerticalAlignment="Center" />
</Border>
```

### Opening and closing from code

`Open` shows the menu under the target. Pass a point in target coordinates to open it at a position, for example at
the place the person clicked in a canvas. `Close` closes it without moving focus. `IsOpen` is two-way, so a view model
can open the menu by setting it.

```csharp
file.Open(); // under the target
file.Open(new Point(120, 40), MenuOpenFocus.First); // at a point, with the first row highlighted
file.Close();
```

The menu opens from `IsOpen` only once the target is attached to a window. Setting it to `True` before that does
nothing visible, so set it after the page loads.

### Binding to a view model

A context menu usually acts on an item of a collection, so the view model owns the items and the commands, and the
handler routes the activated row to the command. The menu shows the items; it does not run them.

```csharp
public sealed record FileAction(string Name, bool IsDestructive);

public partial class FileListViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    public ObservableCollection<FileAction> FileActions { get; } =
    [
        new FileAction("Copy link", IsDestructive: false),
        new FileAction("Move to trash", IsDestructive: true)
    ];

    [RelayCommand]
    private void RunFileAction(FileAction action)
    {
        // Run the action for the file that this menu belongs to.
    }
}
```

```csharp
file.ItemClicked += (_, e) =>
{
    if (e.Item is FileAction action)
    {
        viewModel.RunFileActionCommand.Execute(action);
    }
};
```

Bind `ItemsSource` in XAML (see Data-driven rows) and route the activated item through `ItemClicked`, as above. For a
row declared inline that needs a command, set `Command` on the `MenuEntry` in code when you create it. The view model
uses `ObservableObject` and `[RelayCommand]` from CommunityToolkit.Mvvm and holds no UI types.

### Focus and dismissal

The menu opens where the person acted. A right-click opens it at the pointer. A click or tap on the target, and the
ContextMenu key or Shift+F10 on a focused target, open it under the target, 12 px in from its left edge and 8 px
below its bottom edge. A pointer opens the menu with focus on the surface and no highlighted row. The keyboard opens
put the highlight on the first row.

The menu closes rather than follows. It closes on an outside press, on any scroll of an ancestor scroll viewer, on a
window resize, and when the target leaves the visual tree. A primary press on the target while the menu is open
closes it, and the click that follows does not reopen it. Escape and Tab close the menu and return focus to the target.
When the menu is near a window edge, Avalonia's placement flips it to the other side.

### Example: revenue dashboard card

A dashboard card carries four actions, and the destructive one is last behind a separator. The card keeps its own
border and its title, so the menu stays on the object and the page's toolbar keeps the page-level actions. The label
names the chart, because a screen reader announces only the target's name. The Pin to home row is a toggle, so its
checked state is announced to assistive technology. The shortcut hint is display only; the app must bind the key
itself.

```xml
<arc:ContextMenu Label="Actions for Revenue by region">
    <arc:ContextMenu.Items>
        <arc:MenuEntry Header="Duplicate chart"
                       Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Copy}"
                       InputGestureText="⌘D" />
        <arc:MenuEntry Header="Export CSV" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Download}" />
        <arc:MenuEntry Header="Pin to home"
                       ToggleType="CheckBox"
                       IsChecked="True" />
        <arc:MenuEntry Header="Remove from dashboard"
                       Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Trash2}"
                       IsDestructive="True"
                       HasSeparatorBefore="True" />
    </arc:ContextMenu.Items>
    <Border Width="300"
            Padding="16"
            CornerRadius="16"
            BorderThickness="1"
            Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource SurfaceMuted}"
            BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource BorderSubtle}">
        <StackPanel Spacing="6">
            <TextBlock Text="Revenue by region"
                       FontSize="14"
                       FontWeight="Medium"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
            <TextBlock Text="$1.84M"
                       FontSize="26"
                       FontWeight="SemiBold"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
            <TextBlock Text="+12.6% against Q2 2026"
                       FontSize="12"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
        </StackPanel>
    </Border>
</arc:ContextMenu>
```

### Content guidelines

Rows are short commands, and the menu is read at a glance, so write each row as a verb and its object. Keep the
`Label` specific, because it is the only name a screen reader gives the target.

- Write row labels in sentence case, with a verb first: "Copy link", not "Link".
- Name the object in a destructive row, so the person knows what goes: "Move to trash" for a file, "Remove from
  dashboard" for a card.
- Keep a row under about 24 characters. A longer label ends in an ellipsis, so the important words go first.
- Do not end a row with a colon or a full stop, and do not put a shortcut in the label text; use `InputGestureText`.
- Use the product's own words for the action, such as "Void invoice" when the product voids invoices.

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| Link | Copy link |
| Delete | Delete file |
| Actions | Actions for Q3 report.pdf |
| Remove | Move to trash |
| Click here to export | Export CSV |
| Duplicate (Ctrl+D) | Duplicate chart, with the shortcut in `InputGestureText` |

### Best practices

**Do**

- Keep the list to three to seven rows. A longer list belongs in a `DropdownMenu` on a visible trigger or on a page.
- Give the target a visible shape, such as a border, a background or a corner radius. The target has no outline of
  its own, so the menu is the only feedback and people need to see what they act on.
- Put the destructive row last and set `HasSeparatorBefore="True"`, so it is not hit by accident.
- Offer the important actions from a visible control as well. A right-click, a tap on the target and Shift+F10 are not
  discoverable, and touch and keyboard users need a labelled way in.
- Name the target with `Label` after the object, so a screen reader announces what the actions belong to.

**Avoid**

- Wrapping a target that needs its own click. A plain click or tap also opens the menu, so the target's action and the
  menu compete for the same press. Set `OpensOnClick` to `False` when the target only needs the right-click menu.
- Long labels that rely on wrapping. Rows end long labels in an ellipsis, so the meaning can be cut off.
- Marking a destructive row by color alone. The row is marked by its danger color only, so its `Header` must say what
  will be removed.
- Expecting the menu to follow the target while the page scrolls. It closes on scroll, and the person reopens it.
- Putting the only route to an action in the menu. Keep one visible route for the actions that matter most.

### Common questions

**How do I stop a left click from opening the menu?** `OpensOnClick` controls the plain click and tap. Set it to
`False` on the `ContextMenu` to keep the right-click, the ContextMenu key and Shift+F10. The default is `True`.

**Avalonia also has a `ContextMenu` type. How do I tell them apart?** Both namespaces define a type called
`ContextMenu`. When a file uses both `Avalonia.Controls` and `TKCode.Arc`, add an alias
such as `using ArcContextMenu = TKCode.Arc.ContextMenu;` and use the alias in code. In XAML the `arc:` prefix already
selects the Arc type.

**How do I give a control a menu without wrapping it?** Set `arc:ContextMenu.Menu` to a `MenuSurface` on the control
(see Attaching a menu to any control). The surface takes the Context variant unless you set its variant yourself.

**Can I open the menu at the place the person clicked?** Yes. Call `Open` with a point in the target's coordinates, for
example `file.Open(e.GetPosition(file))` from a pointer handler. Without a point, the menu opens under the target.

**Why does the menu show a check on one row but not the others?** A row without an icon shows a check when `IsChecked`
is true, and an ellipsis when it is not, so the rows keep one left edge. A row with an icon shows the icon instead.
Set `ToggleType="CheckBox"` on a row whose state should flip on activation.

## API reference

### ContextMenu

Secondary actions kept close to the selected object (Arc context menu). Wraps its `Content` and opens a menu at the pointer on right-click, or under the target (12px in, 8px below) on a plain click, a tap, the ContextMenu key or Shift+F10. The menu grows from the pointer on a snappy spring, rows press with a tint, and it closes on any scroll, resize or outside press instead of repositioning. Avoid it on targets that need their own click. To give any control a right-click menu without wrapping it, attach a surface: `<Border><arc:ContextMenu.Menu><arc:MenuSurface>…</arc:MenuSurface></arc:ContextMenu.Menu></Border>`.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Menu` | `MenuSurface?` | `null` | *Attached.* Attaches a right-click (and ContextMenu key / Shift+F10) menu to any control. The surface becomes a `Context` menu unless its variant was set explicitly. |
| `Label` | `string?` | `"Context menu"` | Accessible name of both the target and the menu (Arc default: "Context menu"). |
| `IsOpen` | `bool` | `false` | Whether the menu is open; binds two-way by default. |
| `OpensOnClick` | `bool` | `true` | Whether a plain click or tap on the target opens the menu (Arc: true). |
| `ItemsSource` | `IEnumerable?` | `null` | Data items generated as menu rows; `ItemTemplate` defines how each row looks. |
| `ItemTemplate` | `IDataTemplate?` | `null` | Template that builds each menu row from an `ItemsSource` item. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ItemClicked` | `MenuEntryClickedEventArgs` | Raised when a menu row is clicked; the argument carries the clicked entry and item. |
| `Opened` | `RoutedEventArgs` | Raised when the menu opens. |
| `Closed` | `RoutedEventArgs` | Raised when the menu closes. |

Derives from `ContentControl`: every member of `ContentControl` works as well.

### MenuEntry

One row of a `MenuSurface`: a leading icon (a Lucide `Geometry` such as `{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Pencil}`, or any control), a header, an optional shortcut hint and the check or radio indicator of toggle rows. Rows never draw their own hover or focus fill: the surface's shared highlight glides to the row under the pointer and jumps to the keyboard position. Activation runs `Command`, raises `Click` and the surface's `ItemClicked`, then closes the menu unless `StaysOpenOnClick` is set.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Header` | `object?` | `null` | The row label (strings ellipsize; any content is accepted). Also the typeahead text unless `TextSearch.Text` is set. |
| `HeaderTemplate` | `IDataTemplate?` | `null` | Data template that renders the header; without one, a string header is drawn as ellipsizing text. |
| `Icon` | `object?` | `null` | Leading icon: a 24x24 Lucide `Geometry` (drawn as a 16px stroke glyph) or any control. |
| `InputGesture` | `KeyGesture?` | `null` | Shortcut shown as a quiet hint at the row end (display only; bind the key with a hot key yourself). |
| `InputGestureText` | `string?` | `null` | Free-form shortcut hint (for example "⌘ ,"); wins over `InputGesture`. |
| `Command` | `ICommand?` | `null` | Command run when the row is activated; the row is disabled while the command cannot execute. |
| `CommandParameter` | `object?` | `null` | Parameter passed to Command when the row is activated. |
| `IsDestructive` | `bool` | `false` | Danger text and icon, and a danger-tinted highlight. Put destructive rows last and name what they destroy. |
| `ToggleType` | `MenuEntryToggleType` | `None` | How the row toggles when activated: None for a command row, CheckBox, or Radio. |
| `IsChecked` | `bool` | `false` | Checked state (two-way). Rows without an icon show a check (or a dot for radio rows) when checked. |
| `GroupName` | `string?` | `null` | Radio rows with the same group name (within one surface) are mutually exclusive. |
| `HasSeparatorBefore` | `bool` | `false` | Draws a separator line above the row (Arc's `separatorBefore`). |
| `StaysOpenOnClick` | `bool` | `false` | Keeps the menu open after activation (toggles that people flip several times). |
| `Variant` | `MenuSurfaceVariant` | `Dropdown` | Inherited from the owning `MenuSurface`; selects the row geometry. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Click` | `RoutedEventArgs` | Raised when the row is activated (pointer release, Enter or Space), before the menu closes. |

Pseudo-classes: `:highlighted`, `:pressed`, `:checked`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

## Accessibility

- The target is focusable and the menu is announced with the `Label`, which names both the target and the menu.
- The target exposes a menu that can be expanded and collapsed, so assistive technology reports whether it is open.
- Rows have the menu item role. Enter and Space choose a row, and Escape closes the menu and returns focus to the
  target.
- Shift+F10 and the ContextMenu key open the menu under a focused target, with the first row highlighted.
- A checked row without an icon shows a check, but on its own the checked state is not announced. Rows with
  `ToggleType="CheckBox"` or `ToggleType="Radio"` expose their state to assistive technology, so use a toggle type
  for a row whose state matters, or put the state in the `Header`.
- Destructive rows are marked by color only, so name what will be removed in the `Header`.
- Keep the `Label` specific to the object, such as "Actions for Q3 report.pdf". It is the only name a screen reader
  gives the target.

### Keyboard

A focused target opens the menu from the keyboard. Once the menu is open, the rows follow the menu keyboard model.

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| ContextMenu key, `Shift+F10` | Opens the menu under the focused target, with the first row highlighted |
| `ArrowDown` / `ArrowUp` | Moves the highlight to the next or previous row; the list loops and skips disabled rows |
| `Home` / `End` | Moves the highlight to the first or last row |
| Letters | Typeahead moves to a row whose text starts with the typed letters |
| `Enter` / `Space` | Activates the highlighted row, then closes the menu unless the row stays open |
| `Escape` / `Tab` | Closes the menu and returns focus to the target |

## Motion

- Right-click makes the menu grow from the pointer on a quick spring with a short fade. Rows fade in with a short stagger.
- A click, tap or Shift+F10 opens the menu under the target with the same motion.
- Scrolling or resizing closes the menu. It does not move to follow the target.
- Reduced motion removes the scale and the glide and keeps a quick fade. Off shows and hides the menu at once.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| Right-click opens | The menu grows from the pointer, from 0.96 to full size on a snappy spring, with a 160 ms fade | Quick fade, no scale | Immediate |
| Click, tap or Shift+F10 opens | The menu grows out of the point under the target, with the same spring and fade | Quick fade | Immediate |
| Menu closes | The menu scales to 0.98 and fades in 120 ms | Quick fade | Immediate |
| Highlight moves | The pointer highlight glides on a snappy spring; the keyboard highlight jumps | The highlight jumps | Immediate |
| Rows appear | Each row fades in over 240 ms, staggered 35 ms apart up to the fifth row | Quick fade | Immediate |
| Row pressed | The row tints; it does not scale | The row tints | Immediate |

## Related

- `DropdownMenu` when the actions need a visible trigger that people can find.
- `SwipeActions` for touch-first rows that reveal actions by a swipe.
- `SplitButton` when one action is the default and the menu holds the alternatives.
- `MenuSurface` is the shared menu popup, for anchoring a menu to any control.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `DropdownMenu` | The actions need a labelled trigger that people can see and find |
| `SwipeActions` | Touch-first rows reveal their actions by a swipe |
| `SplitButton` | One action is the default and the menu holds the alternatives |
| `UserMenu` | The menu belongs to the account behind the avatar in the top bar |
| `Dialog` | A destructive row must be confirmed before anything is removed |
| `MenuSurface` | You need a menu on a control without the right-click gesture, or from code |

# User menu

> Your account, settings, theme, and sign out behind the avatar. Opens as a bottom sheet on phones.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/user-menu

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.UserMenuTopBarDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12">
        <Border Padding="16,8"
                CornerRadius="18"
                BorderThickness="1"
                Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Surface}"
                BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Border}">
            <DockPanel>
                <arc:UserMenu x:Name="Account"
                              DockPanel.Dock="Right"
                              DisplayName="Ada Lovelace"
                              Email="ada@analytical.dev"
                              Plan="Pro"
                              IsNameVisible="True"
                              SignOutGestureText="⇧⌘Q"
                              ThemePreferenceChanged="OnThemePreferenceChanged"
                              ItemClicked="OnItemClicked"
                              SignOutRequested="OnSignOutRequested">
                    <arc:MenuEntry Header="Profile" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.User}" />
                    <arc:MenuEntry Header="Settings"
                                   Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Settings}"
                                   InputGestureText="⌘ ," />
                    <arc:MenuEntry Header="Billing" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.CreditCard}" />
                </arc:UserMenu>
                <TextBlock Text="Northwind"
                           FontSize="15"
                           FontWeight="Medium"
                           TextWrapping="Wrap"
                           VerticalAlignment="Center"
                           Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
            </DockPanel>
        </Border>
        <TextBlock x:Name="Status"
                   Text="Theme: System"
                   FontSize="14"
                   TextWrapping="Wrap"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class UserMenuTopBarDemo : UserControl
{
    public UserMenuTopBarDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        // Sign out shows a spinner on its row until the task settles.
        Account.SignOutAction = () => Task.Delay(1200);
    }

    private void OnThemePreferenceChanged(object? sender, UserMenuThemePreferenceChangedEventArgs e)
        => Status.Text = $"Theme: {e.ThemePreference}";

    private void OnItemClicked(object? sender, MenuEntryClickedEventArgs e) => Status.Text = $"Opened {e.Header}";

    private void OnSignOutRequested(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) => Status.Text = "Signing out…";
}
```

## When to use

A user menu is the one account entry point in an app's top bar. It sits behind the avatar and gathers what belongs to
the signed-in person: the identity header, two to four account destinations, a theme choice, an optional presence
status and sign out. It keeps account concerns out of the page toolbar, so the page's own actions stay visible and the
account stays one click away.

- **Account destinations in a SaaS admin console**: Profile, Workspace settings and Billing behind the avatar of an
  admin who manages several workspaces. The plan badge shows Admin or Pro beside the name.
- **Presence in a team app**: an incident console where the on-call engineer sets Busy during a response, and the dot
  on the avatar tells teammates the status without a chat message.
- **Theme choice in a dashboard or design tool**: Light, Dark or System, chosen in the menu. The menu stays open after
  the choice so the page can change theme in front of the person.
- **Sign out of a session that takes time**: a sign-out that revokes tokens on the server. The row shows a spinner until
  the task finishes, and the menu then closes.
- **Narrow windows and phones**: the same menu opens as a bottom sheet below 640 px, so the account stays reachable on
  a phone without a second navigation pattern.

## When not to use

- **A general list of commands that is not about the account**: use `DropdownMenu` behind a labelled trigger, such as
  an Actions menu on a report page.
- **A theme switch on its own, outside an account menu**: use `ThemeSwitcher`, which is a light and dark control that
  is not tied to a person.
- **More than four destinations**: move the extra ones to a page and link to it from one destination. A long menu
  stops being a shortcut.
- **A menu opened from a row or a card**: use `ContextMenu` for right-click actions on the object, or `DropdownMenu` on
  a visible trigger.
- **A form value picked from a list**: use `Select` or `Combobox`. The user menu carries commands and two switches, not
  a value that feeds a form.

## Usage

Set the identity properties and declare the destinations under `UserMenu.Items`. The avatar is the trigger.

`UserMenu` derives from Avalonia's `TemplatedControl`. Its trigger is an Arc `Button` (Ghost, a 40 px pill) that holds
the avatar, the presence dot and the name. Its panel is a `MenuSurface` in the Account variant, which the control
configures and owns. Below 640 px the same surface switches to the Sheet variant. The panel holds a header built from
the identity properties, the destination rows, the theme and status switches and the sign-out row.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:UserMenu DisplayName="Ada Lovelace"
                  Email="ada@analytical.dev"
                  Plan="Pro"
                  IsNameVisible="True"
                  SignOutGestureText="⇧⌘Q">
        <arc:UserMenu.Items>
            <arc:MenuEntry Header="Profile" />
            <arc:MenuEntry Header="Settings" InputGestureText="⌘ ," />
            <arc:MenuEntry Header="Billing" />
        </arc:UserMenu.Items>
    </arc:UserMenu>
</UserControl>
```

### Anatomy

1. **Trigger** (the Ghost `arc:Button` in the template): a 40 px pill with a 4 px inset. It has a 10 px right inset when
   the name shows. It never scales when pressed; pressing and opening change only its background color.
2. **Avatar** (`DisplayName`, `AvatarSource`): a 32 px avatar. With `AvatarSource` set, the photo shows; while the photo
   loads, or when it fails, the initials show.
3. **Presence dot** (`Status`, `IsStatusVisible`): an 11 px dot at the bottom right of the avatar, ringed by 2 px of the
   trigger's background color. Available is a solid success-colored dot, Busy is a danger-colored dot with a bar and
   Away is a warning-colored dot with a hollow center, so the status reads without color.
4. **Name** (`DisplayName`, `IsNameVisible`): medium weight, up to 176 px, truncated with an ellipsis. It shows beside
   the avatar only when `IsNameVisible` is `True` and the window is at least 640 px wide.
5. **Chevron**: 16 px in the muted text color. It shows with the name and turns 180 degrees while the menu is open.
6. **Panel** (`PanelAlignment`): an Account panel 248 px wide (15.5 rem), 8 px away from the avatar. The default
   alignment is `End`, so the panel lines up with the trigger's right edge.
7. **Identity header**: a 34 px avatar with the presence dot when status shows, the name with a `Plan` badge beside
   it, and the `Email` under the name. A long name, plan or email ends in an ellipsis instead of widening the panel.
8. **Destinations** (`Items` or `ItemsSource`): rows of 32 px with 13 px text, each with an optional icon and a shortcut
   hint at the end.
9. **Theme switch** (`ThemePreference`, `IsThemeSwitchVisible`): a Theme row with three segments, Light (sun icon),
   Dark (moon icon) and System (monitor icon). It is 36 px tall in the panel and 52 px in the sheet.
10. **Status switch** (`Status`, `IsStatusVisible`): a Status row with three segments, Available, Busy and Away, at the
    same heights as the theme switch.
11. **Sign out row**: a LogOut icon, the label "Sign out" and the `SignOutGestureText` hint. While the sign-out task
    runs, the label reads "Signing out" and the icon becomes a spinner.
12. **Separators**: a line between the destinations, the switches and the sign-out row.

### Choosing the layout

- Show the name (`IsNameVisible="True"`) in a wide top bar where the person's name helps them confirm the account. Hide
  it in a narrow toolbar, where the avatar alone is enough.
- Keep `IsThemeSwitchVisible` at its default `True` in an app that supports both themes. Set it to `False` when the app
  has one theme, so the menu does not offer a choice that does nothing.
- Show the presence dot (`IsStatusVisible="True"`) only in an app where teammates use the status. A dot that nobody
  sets adds noise to every avatar.
- Use `PanelAlignment="Start"` when the avatar sits at the left edge of a window, so the panel opens toward the content.

### Theme and status

`ThemePreference` is `Light`, `Dark` or `System`. The menu reports the choice and stays open. The app applies the theme
itself. `IsThemeSwitchVisible="False"` hides the switch.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.UserMenuPresenceDemo">
    <WrapPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center" ItemSpacing="12" LineSpacing="12">
        <arc:UserMenu DisplayName="Grace Hopper"
                      Email="grace@compiler.dev"
                      Plan="Admin"
                      IsStatusVisible="True"
                      Status="Busy"
                      IsThemeSwitchVisible="False"
                      PanelAlignment="Start">
            <arc:MenuEntry Header="Profile" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.User}" />
            <arc:MenuEntry Header="Settings"
                           Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Settings}"
                           InputGestureText="⌘ ," />
            <arc:MenuEntry Header="Billing" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.CreditCard}" />
        </arc:UserMenu>
    </WrapPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```xml
<arc:UserMenu DisplayName="Grace Hopper"
              Email="grace@compiler.dev"
              ThemePreference="{Binding ThemePreference, Mode=TwoWay}"
              Status="{Binding Status, Mode=TwoWay}"
              IsStatusVisible="True" />
```

```csharp
userMenu.ThemePreferenceChanged += (_, e) => ApplyTheme(e.ThemePreference);
userMenu.StatusChanged += (_, e) => status.Text = $"Status: {e.Status}";
```

`Status` and `ThemePreference` are two-way bound, so the view model always holds the current choice. The events fire
only for a choice made in the menu. Use them to apply the theme or to send the status to the server, because the
menu does neither itself.

### Asynchronous sign out

`SignOutAction` runs when the sign-out row is chosen. While the task runs, the row shows a spinner and the menu stays
open. The menu closes when the task finishes.

```csharp
userMenu.SignOutAction = () => auth.SignOutAsync();
userMenu.SignOutRequested += (_, _) => status.Text = "Signing out…";
```

`SignOutRequested` fires before the action runs, so it is the place to show a status line or to clear a local cache.
If the action throws, the menu still stops waiting and closes; report the failure from the action itself, because the
menu does not show it. When no action is set, or the task has already finished, the menu closes at once and returns
focus to the avatar.

### Photo and destinations as data

`AvatarSource` shows a photo. Without one, or while the photo loads, the initials are shown. `ItemsSource` creates
the destinations from data when `Items` is not enough.

```xml
<arc:UserMenu DisplayName="{Binding Name}"
              Email="{Binding Email}"
              AvatarSource="{Binding Avatar}"
              ItemsSource="{Binding AccountLinks}" />
```

Each generated row shows the item, or the `ItemTemplate` result when one is set. `ItemClicked` reports the row and its
data item in `e.Item`, so a single handler can route each destination to a page.

### Binding to a view model

The view model owns the identity, the theme, the status and the sign-out logic. The menu shows them and reports back
through its two-way properties and its events. Keep the account destinations in the view model as data, so the menu
and the navigation stay in step.

```csharp
public partial class AccountViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    private readonly IAuthService _auth;

    public AccountViewModel(IAuthService auth) => _auth = auth;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private string _displayName = "Ada Lovelace";

    [ObservableProperty]
    private string _email = "ada@analytical.dev";

    [ObservableProperty]
    private UserMenuThemePreference _themePreference = UserMenuThemePreference.System;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private UserMenuStatus _status = UserMenuStatus.Available;

    [RelayCommand]
    private Task SignOutAsync() => _auth.SignOutAsync();
}
```

```xml
<arc:UserMenu DisplayName="{Binding DisplayName}"
              Email="{Binding Email}"
              IsNameVisible="True"
              ThemePreference="{Binding ThemePreference, Mode=TwoWay}"
              IsStatusVisible="True"
              Status="{Binding Status, Mode=TwoWay}" />
```

```csharp
userMenu.SignOutAction = () => viewModel.SignOutCommand.ExecuteAsync(null);
```

- `ThemePreference` and `Status` are two-way, so a theme chosen in the menu reaches the view model, and a status set in
  code reaches the dot and the switch.
- `DisplayName` and `Email` are one-way: the view model changes them after a profile update and the header follows.
- Use `ThemePreferenceChanged` to apply the theme, and `StatusChanged` to save the status. The two-way value only
  records the choice; the events are where the app acts on it.
- The sign-out command is a `Func<Task>`, so assign it in code, or wrap the command in a method that returns a `Task`.

### Focus and dismissal

A pointer opens the menu with focus on the panel and no row highlighted. A keyboard opening highlights the first row
from Enter, Space or ArrowDown, or the last row from ArrowUp. A menu that starts open, with `IsOpen` set when the page
loads, does not take focus or scroll the page.

Choosing a destination closes the menu. The theme and status switches keep it open, so a person can flip both in one
visit. The sign-out row keeps the menu open with its spinner until the task settles, then closes it. An outside press
closes the menu; on a sheet, a press on the scrim does the same.

The menu changes its form with the window. When the window crosses the 640 px breakpoint while the menu is open, the
menu closes rather than turning a panel into a sheet, so the person reopens it in the new form. Escape and Tab close the
menu and return focus to the avatar.

### Example: operations console top bar

The top bar of an incident console shows the on-call engineer's account. The name is visible because the console is a
wide window, and the presence dot shows Busy so teammates know the engineer is in a response. The plan badge reads
Admin, and the menu holds three destinations, with sign out last and its shortcut hint. The theme switch stays at its
default, because responders work in dark rooms and need the choice without a settings page.

```xml
<Border Padding="16,8"
        CornerRadius="18"
        BorderThickness="1"
        Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Surface}"
        BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Border}">
    <DockPanel>
        <TextBlock DockPanel.Dock="Left"
                   Text="Incident console"
                   FontSize="15"
                   FontWeight="Medium"
                   VerticalAlignment="Center"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
        <arc:UserMenu DockPanel.Dock="Right"
                      DisplayName="Grace Hopper"
                      Email="grace@compiler.dev"
                      Plan="Admin"
                      IsNameVisible="True"
                      IsStatusVisible="True"
                      Status="Busy"
                      SignOutGestureText="⇧⌘Q">
            <arc:MenuEntry Header="Profile" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.User}" />
            <arc:MenuEntry Header="On-call schedule" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Clock}" />
            <arc:MenuEntry Header="Billing" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.CreditCard}" />
        </arc:UserMenu>
    </DockPanel>
</Border>
```

### Content guidelines

The menu is short and read at a glance. Destinations are nouns for the page they open, and the switches and the sign-out
row use the words the app uses everywhere else.

- Name a destination after its page: "Billing", "Workspace settings". Keep it under about 24 characters.
- Use "Sign out" for the sign-out row, a verb and its particle, with no exclamation mark or confirmation text in the label.
- Keep the plan badge to a word such as "Pro" or "Admin"; it is a badge, not a sentence.
- Use the three statuses as they are. The menu offers Available, Busy and Away; an "Offline" status is not one of them.
- Write theme options as single words: Light, Dark, System.

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| Logout | Sign out |
| My account settings | Profile |
| Dark mode | Dark |
| Offline | Away |
| Sign out now! | Sign out |

### Best practices

**Do**

- Keep the destinations to two to four. A fifth destination belongs on a page, linked from one of the four.
- Keep sign out as the last row. The layout already separates it; do not add rows below it.
- Show the presence dot only in an app where teammates set and read the status. A dot that nobody sets is noise on
  every avatar.
- Apply the theme in `ThemePreferenceChanged`, so the choice takes effect while the menu is still open.
- Set `Email` and `Plan` to values that fit. Long values are truncated, so a short name and plan read better.

**Avoid**

- Long settings forms in the menu. A form belongs in a `Drawer` or on a page; the menu is for choices and navigation.
- A long list of accounts or workspaces. Use a `Select` or a page for a switcher, because the menu shows only a few rows
  comfortably.
- Designing the page around a setting in the menu. The breakpoint is fixed at 640 px, so design the page for both the
  panel and the sheet.
- Running the sign-out work without feedback. An unfinished task shows the spinner; a task that finishes at once closes
  the menu without one.
- Adding a custom switch to the menu. The API offers the theme and status switches only; other choices belong in a
  `DropdownMenu` or a page.

### Common questions

**Why does the name disappear on my narrow window?** Below 640 px the trigger shows the avatar alone, and the menu opens as a
bottom sheet. `CompactBreakpoint` is a fixed constant of 640, so plan the layout for the avatar-only trigger in narrow
windows.

**Why is the presence dot missing?** `IsStatusVisible` defaults to `False`. Set it to `True` to show the dot and the
status switch.

**How do I hide the theme choice?** Set `IsThemeSwitchVisible="False"`. The theme row then leaves the panel, and the app
can apply its own theme control elsewhere.

**How does the sign-out spinner appear?** Return an unfinished `Task` from `SignOutAction`. The row shows the spinner and
the label "Signing out" until the task completes, then the menu closes.

**Can I show the name and the chevron on a narrow window?** No. The name and the chevron show only on windows at least
640 px wide, and the sheet keeps the avatar alone. Plan the page layout around that, because the menu does not expose the
breakpoint as a setting.

## API reference

### UserMenu

The account menu behind a person's avatar in an app's top bar (Arc user menu): a compact identity header, a short group of account destinations (`Items`, keep it to three or four), an inline light / dark / system switch, an optional presence switch and sign out. Theme and status choices keep the menu open; everything else closes it and returns focus to the avatar. When `SignOutAction` returns an unfinished task the row shows a spinner and "Signing out", and the menu closes once it settles. Below a 640px wide window the menu opens as a bottom sheet that follows a downward drag. The panel scales out of the avatar on a spring that never overshoots, rows fade in 16ms apart, one highlight glides between rows and the switch thumbs slide on Arc's CSS spring.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `DisplayName` | `string?` | `null` | Name shown in the menu header; also used in the avatar's automation name. |
| `Email` | `string?` | `null` | Email address shown under the name in the menu header. |
| `Plan` | `string?` | `null` | Plan or role shown as a small badge beside the name ("Pro"). |
| `AvatarSource` | `ImageSource?` | `null` | Photo; falls back to initials while it loads or when it fails. |
| `IsNameVisible` | `bool` | `false` | Shows the name and a chevron beside the avatar (wide windows only). |
| `ThemePreference` | `UserMenuThemePreference` | `System` | Theme chosen in the inline switch (Light, Dark or System); two-way bound. Applying it is up to the app. |
| `IsThemeSwitchVisible` | `bool` | `true` | Shows the inline light / dark / system switch. |
| `Status` | `UserMenuStatus` | `Available` | Presence status (Available, Busy or Away) shown by the dot and the status switch; two-way bound. |
| `IsStatusVisible` | `bool` | `false` | Shows the presence dot on the avatar and the inline status switch. |
| `SignOutAction` | `Func<Task>?` | `null` | Sign-out handler. An unfinished task keeps the menu open with a spinner until it settles. |
| `SignOutGestureText` | `string?` | `null` | Shortcut hint for the sign-out row (for example "⇧⌘Q"). |
| `IsOpen` | `bool` | `false` | Whether the menu is open; two-way bound. |
| `PanelAlignment` | `MenuAlignment` | `End` | Panel alignment against the avatar (Arc: end). |
| `ItemsSource` | `IEnumerable?` | `null` | Account destinations as data (rows are generated; `MenuEntry` items are used as is). |
| `ItemTemplate` | `IDataTemplate?` | `null` | Data template applied to the header of each row generated from ItemsSource. |
| `IsSigningOut` | `bool` | – | *Read-only.* True while an asynchronous `SignOutAction` runs. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ItemClicked` | `MenuEntryClickedEventArgs` | Raised when an account destination row is clicked; the argument carries the entry and its item. |
| `ThemePreferenceChanged` | `UserMenuThemePreferenceChangedEventArgs` | Raised when a theme is chosen; the menu stays open and applying the theme is up to the app. |
| `StatusChanged` | `UserMenuStatusChangedEventArgs` | Raised when a status is chosen; the menu stays open. |
| `SignOutRequested` | `RoutedEventArgs` | Raised when the sign-out row is activated (before `SignOutAction` runs). |
| `Opened` | `RoutedEventArgs` | Raised when the menu opens. |
| `Closed` | `RoutedEventArgs` | Raised when the menu closes. |

Pseudo-classes: `:open`, `:compact`, `:signing-out`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

### MenuEntry

One row of a `MenuSurface`: a leading icon (a Lucide `Geometry` such as `{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Pencil}`, or any control), a header, an optional shortcut hint and the check or radio indicator of toggle rows. Rows never draw their own hover or focus fill: the surface's shared highlight glides to the row under the pointer and jumps to the keyboard position. Activation runs `Command`, raises `Click` and the surface's `ItemClicked`, then closes the menu unless `StaysOpenOnClick` is set.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Header` | `object?` | `null` | The row label (strings ellipsize; any content is accepted). Also the typeahead text unless `TextSearch.Text` is set. |
| `HeaderTemplate` | `IDataTemplate?` | `null` | Data template that renders the header; without one, a string header is drawn as ellipsizing text. |
| `Icon` | `object?` | `null` | Leading icon: a 24x24 Lucide `Geometry` (drawn as a 16px stroke glyph) or any control. |
| `InputGesture` | `KeyGesture?` | `null` | Shortcut shown as a quiet hint at the row end (display only; bind the key with a hot key yourself). |
| `InputGestureText` | `string?` | `null` | Free-form shortcut hint (for example "⌘ ,"); wins over `InputGesture`. |
| `Command` | `ICommand?` | `null` | Command run when the row is activated; the row is disabled while the command cannot execute. |
| `CommandParameter` | `object?` | `null` | Parameter passed to Command when the row is activated. |
| `IsDestructive` | `bool` | `false` | Danger text and icon, and a danger-tinted highlight. Put destructive rows last and name what they destroy. |
| `ToggleType` | `MenuEntryToggleType` | `None` | How the row toggles when activated: None for a command row, CheckBox, or Radio. |
| `IsChecked` | `bool` | `false` | Checked state (two-way). Rows without an icon show a check (or a dot for radio rows) when checked. |
| `GroupName` | `string?` | `null` | Radio rows with the same group name (within one surface) are mutually exclusive. |
| `HasSeparatorBefore` | `bool` | `false` | Draws a separator line above the row (Arc's `separatorBefore`). |
| `StaysOpenOnClick` | `bool` | `false` | Keeps the menu open after activation (toggles that people flip several times). |
| `Variant` | `MenuSurfaceVariant` | `Dropdown` | Inherited from the owning `MenuSurface`; selects the row geometry. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Click` | `RoutedEventArgs` | Raised when the row is activated (pointer release, Enter or Space), before the menu closes. |

Pseudo-classes: `:highlighted`, `:pressed`, `:checked`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

The two choice types that the menu reports:

| Type | Values | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `UserMenuThemePreference` | `Light`, `Dark`, `System` | The theme the person chose; the default is `System` |
| `UserMenuStatus` | `Available`, `Busy`, `Away` | The presence shown by the dot and the status switch; the default is `Available` |

## Accessibility

- The avatar trigger is announced as an account menu with the display name. The status is added to the name when shown.
- The rows have the menu item role. The theme and status switches are named groups, and each option is selectable.
- The arrow keys choose within a theme or status switch, and Enter or Space activates a row.
- Escape or Tab closes the menu and returns focus to the avatar.
- The presence dot changes shape as well as colour, so it does not rely on colour alone.
- While the sign-out task runs, the sign-out row reports itself as busy.
- Give the account destinations a `Header` that says where they go, such as "Billing" or "Workspace settings". The
  rows are read out by their header.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Enter`, `Space` or `ArrowDown` on the avatar | Opens the menu with the first row highlighted |
| `ArrowUp` on the avatar | Opens the menu with the last row highlighted |
| Click or tap on the avatar | Toggles the menu |
| `ArrowDown` / `ArrowUp` | Move the highlight to the next or previous row; the list loops and skips disabled rows |
| `Home` / `End` | Move the highlight to the first or last row |
| Letters | Typeahead moves to a row whose text starts with the typed letters, such as `S` for Sign out |
| `ArrowLeft` / `ArrowRight` on a switch | Choose the previous or next option, wrapping at the ends; the menu stays open |
| `Enter` / `Space` | Activates a destination or the sign-out row; on a switch row they do nothing |
| `Escape` / `Tab` | Closes the menu and returns focus to the avatar |

## Motion

- On wide windows the panel grows out of the avatar without overshoot, and its rows fade in one after another.
- A single highlight glides between rows, and the theme and status thumbs slide to the chosen option.
- Below 640px the menu opens as a bottom sheet that rises from the bottom edge. It follows a downward drag and closes
  when dragged far enough.
- Reduced motion uses a short fade for the panel and switches, jumps the highlight and disables the drag. Off shows the
  menu at once.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| Wide panel opens | Grows out of the avatar from 0.94 on a smooth spring with no overshoot, then the rows fade in 16 ms apart | Short fade | Immediate |
| Wide panel closes | Scales to 0.97 and fades out within 120 ms | Short fade | Immediate |
| Highlight moves | Glides between rows for the pointer and the keyboard | Jumps | Immediate |
| Switch thumb moves | Slides to the chosen option on the 580 ms spring | Short fade | Immediate |
| Sheet opens (below 640 px) | Rises from the bottom edge on a smooth spring; rows enter 20 ms apart after 60 ms | Short fade | Immediate |
| Sheet drag | Follows a downward drag; closes past 80 px or on a fast flick | Drag disabled | Immediate |
| Chevron | Turns 180 degrees on the spring as the menu opens | Turns at once | Immediate |

## Related

- `DropdownMenu` for a general command list behind a labelled trigger.
- `ThemeSwitcher` for a light and dark switch that is not part of an account menu.
- `Avatar` is the picture the trigger shows and can be reused in the identity header.
- `MenuSurface` is the shared menu popup that the panel and the bottom sheet are built on.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `DropdownMenu` | The commands are not about the account and need a labelled trigger |
| `ThemeSwitcher` | A light and dark switch stands alone, outside an account |
| `Avatar` | A picture or initials identify a person in a list or a header |
| `ContextMenu` | The actions belong to one object and open at the pointer |
| `Drawer` | Account settings need a full side panel with forms, not a short menu |
| `Dialog` | A sign-out or account change needs a confirmation before it runs |
