# Input

> A single line field with clear labels and useful states.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/input

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.InputBasicDemo">
    <arc:Input Label="Email"
               Placeholder="you@example.com"
               Width="360"
               HorizontalAlignment="Left" />
</UserControl>
```

## When to use

`Input` is the default control for a short, free-form value that a person types. It carries the whole field (a
visible label, the frame, helper copy and an error row), so a form is a column of inputs with no extra layout around
them.

- **Identity and contact data** in sign-up, checkout and profile forms: a full name, a work email, a job title, a
  company name. These values have no fixed shape, so a plain text field with good validation is the right tool.
- **Short identifiers in admin and developer consoles**: a project slug, a webhook URL, an API key name, a DNS record
  value. Use `Prefix` and `Suffix` for the fixed part (`https://`, `.acme.dev`) so people type only what varies.
- **Values with live feedback**: a username with length and character rules, or a workspace URL whose availability is
  checked as it is typed. The helper row rewrites only the words that change and rolls the counts, so constant
  feedback stays calm instead of flickering.
- **Read-only values people need to copy**: a workspace ID or an account number shown in a settings form, next to the
  fields that can change, with `IsReadOnly` keeping the same frame and alignment.

## When not to use

- **Several lines of text**, such as a description, a note, a support message, a postal address typed as one block: use
  `Textarea`, which wraps and can be resized.
- **Secrets**: use `PasswordField` (masked, with a reveal toggle) or `PasswordStrength` when people choose a new
  password and need its rules.
- **Values with a fixed shape**: numbers that people step or scrub (`NumberField`, `ScrubInput`), amounts of money
  (`MoneyInput`), phone numbers (`PhoneInput`), short tokens such as tags or recipients (`TagInput`) and @mentions
  (`MentionInput`). These parse and format the value; `Input` only holds a string.
- **A value from a known list**: use `Select` or `Combobox`; for dates and times use `DatePicker` and `TimePicker`.
- **Search and filtering**: use `SearchField` (clear button, Escape to clear, `SearchSubmitted`) or `ExpandingSearch`
  in a header.
- **Renaming a title in place on a page**: use `InlineEdit`, which looks like text until it is edited.

## Usage

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:Input Label="Email"
               Placeholder="you@example.com"
               Description="We never share it." />
</UserControl>
```

`Input` derives from Avalonia's `TextBox`, so everything a text box does is still there: a two-way `Text`, `MaxLength`,
`IsReadOnly`, `TextAlignment`, `CaretIndex`, `SelectAll()`, undo, IME composition and the clipboard shortcuts. The
field adds the label, the message rows and the Arc frame on top of it.

### Anatomy

1. **Label** (`Label`): 14 px, medium weight, 8 px above the frame. It is also the field's accessible name. Hide it
   with `IsLabelVisible="False"` only when another visible element already names the field.
2. **Frame**: a 1 px border with the control radius on the surface color. Hover and focus only darken the border;
   an error turns it to the danger color; nothing changes size.
3. **Prefix** (`Prefix`): optional content before the text: a scheme, a currency symbol, an icon.
4. **Text and placeholder**: the editable text; `Placeholder` shows in a muted color while the text is empty.
5. **Suffix** (`Suffix`): optional content after the text: a unit or a small action.
6. **Description row** (`Description`): 12 px helper copy in a muted color under the frame.
7. **Error row** (`ErrorMessage`): 12 px copy in the danger color. While it has text, the field is invalid.

### Helper and error copy

Derive the copy from state and change the string. Only the words that change move, and numbers roll digit by
digit, so do not swap between separate messages.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.InputHelperAndErrorDemo">
    <arc:Input x:Name="Username"
               Label="Username"
               Placeholder="ada"
               Description="3 to 20 characters. 20 left."
               Width="360"
               HorizontalAlignment="Left"
               TextChanged="OnTextChanged" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class InputHelperAndErrorDemo : UserControl
{
    public InputHelperAndErrorDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
    }

    // The helper copy is derived from state: changing the string rewrites only the words that changed,
    // and the count rolls.
    private void OnTextChanged(object? sender, TextChangedEventArgs e)
    {
        var text = Username.Text ?? string.Empty;
        var left = Math.Max(0, 20 - text.Length);
        Username.Description = $"3 to 20 characters. {left} left.";
        Username.ErrorMessage = text.Length is > 0 and < 3
            ? "Use at least 3 characters."
            : text.Contains(' ') ? "Spaces are not allowed in a username." : null;
    }
}
```

```xml
<arc:Input Label="Username"
           Text="{Binding UserName}"
           Description="{Binding UserNameHint}"
           ErrorMessage="{Binding UserNameError}" />
```

A non-empty `ErrorMessage` makes the field invalid. While it is empty, a validation error from the `Text`
binding shows instead.

The error that is actually on screen is `EffectiveErrorMessage`: `ErrorMessage` when it has text, otherwise the
message of the binding's validation error. `IsInvalid` is forced to `True` while either one exists; set it yourself
only to show the danger border without a message, for example on every field of a group that failed together.

### Binding to a view model

In an MVVM app the view model owns the value and its rules, and the input only shows them. With
CommunityToolkit.Mvvm, an `ObservableValidator` validates each property when it is set and reports the errors through
`INotifyDataErrorInfo`; Avalonia passes them to the `Text` binding, and the input shows the first one.

```csharp
public partial class ProfileViewModel : ObservableValidator
{
    [ObservableProperty]
    [NotifyDataErrorInfo]
    [Required(ErrorMessage = "Enter your full name.")]
    [StringLength(80, ErrorMessage = "Use 80 characters or fewer.")]
    private string _fullName = string.Empty;

    [ObservableProperty]
    [NotifyDataErrorInfo]
    [Required(ErrorMessage = "Enter a work email.")]
    [EmailAddress(ErrorMessage = "Enter an email address such as name@company.com.")]
    private string _email = string.Empty;

    [RelayCommand]
    private async Task SaveAsync()
    {
        ValidateAllProperties();
        if (HasErrors)
        {
            return;
        }
        await _profiles.SaveAsync(FullName, Email);
    }
}
```

```xml
<StackPanel Spacing="16">
    <arc:Input Label="Full name" Text="{Binding FullName}" />
    <arc:Input Label="Work email"
               Text="{Binding Email, UpdateSourceTrigger=LostFocus}"
               Placeholder="name@company.com" />
    <arc:Button Content="Save profile" Command="{Binding SaveCommand}" IsDefault="True" />
</StackPanel>
```

- `UpdateSourceTrigger=LostFocus` writes the email to the view model when the person leaves the field, so a format
  error appears after they finish typing, not at the first keystroke. Keep the default (`PropertyChanged`) for values
  whose helper copy reacts while typing, such as a character count.
- Use one source of validation. When the view model validates its DataAnnotations attributes and Avalonia's own
  DataAnnotations plugin checks them too, each rule runs twice; the Avalonia MVVM app template removes the plugin for
  this reason.
- Compiled bindings need `x:DataType` on the view (the examples here leave it out for brevity).

### Validation timing

Good forms check each rule at the moment the person can act on it. A rule that fires too early reads as blame; one
that fires too late wastes a submit.

| Rule | When to check | Where it shows |
|---|---|---|
| Length limits and allowed characters | While typing | `Description` counts down ("12 left"); `ErrorMessage` only once the limit is broken |
| Format (email, URL, slug) | When the field loses focus | `ErrorMessage` (binding validation with `LostFocus`) |
| Required | On submit, then while the value is still empty | `ErrorMessage`; move focus to the first invalid field |
| Availability or uniqueness (server) | After a pause in typing, or on blur | `Description` while checking ("Checking…"), then `ErrorMessage` if taken |
| Errors the server returns on save | After the request | `ErrorMessage` on the field the error is about; clear it when the value changes |

```csharp
// The server is the last word: show its message on the field it is about, and clear it once the value changes.
var result = await api.CreateWebhookAsync(endpoint.Text);
endpoint.ErrorMessage = result.IsSuccess ? null : result.Error;

endpoint.TextChanged += (_, _) => endpoint.ErrorMessage = null;
```

### Sizes

`Size` sets the frame height: `Small` is 36, `Medium` is 44 (the Arc look) and `Large` is 50.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.InputSizesDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="16">
        <arc:Input Label="Small"
                   Size="Small"
                   Placeholder="36px tall"
                   Width="360"
                   HorizontalAlignment="Left" />
        <arc:Input Label="Medium"
                   Placeholder="44px tall (default)"
                   Width="360"
                   HorizontalAlignment="Left" />
        <arc:Input Label="Large"
                   Size="Large"
                   Placeholder="50px tall"
                   Width="360"
                   HorizontalAlignment="Left" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

Keep one size per form. `Small` suits dense admin tables and toolbars, `Medium` is the default for forms and
settings, and `Large` fits a single prominent field such as the email on a sign-in page. Pickers, selects and the
special inputs take the same `Size` values, so a mixed form lines up when they all use the same one.

### Prefix and suffix

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.InputPrefixAndSuffixDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="16">
        <arc:Input Label="Site"
                   Placeholder="example.com"
                   Width="360"
                   HorizontalAlignment="Left">
            <arc:Input.Prefix>
                <TextBlock Text="https://"
                           FontSize="14"
                           Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
            </arc:Input.Prefix>
        </arc:Input>
        <arc:Input Label="Price"
                   Text="49"
                   Width="360"
                   HorizontalAlignment="Left">
            <arc:Input.Prefix>
                <TextBlock Text="$"
                           FontSize="14"
                           Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
            </arc:Input.Prefix>
            <arc:Input.Suffix>
                <TextBlock Text="USD"
                           FontSize="14"
                           Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
            </arc:Input.Suffix>
        </arc:Input>
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

Use `Prefix` and `Suffix` for text that is part of the value's context but not of the value: `https://` before a
domain, `$` before a price, `USD` or `GB` after a number, `.acme.dev` after a subdomain. Show them in the muted text
color so the typed text stays the strongest element. They are not part of `Text`, so the view model receives only
what the person typed. For a value that must be parsed as a number or an amount, use `NumberField` or `MoneyInput`
instead of a prefix on a plain input.

### States

A field can be disabled, read-only or invalid.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.InputStatesDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="16">
        <arc:Input Label="Disabled"
                   Text="Not editable right now"
                   IsEnabled="False"
                   Width="360"
                   HorizontalAlignment="Left" />
        <arc:Input Label="Read-only"
                   Text="ws_7f3a9c"
                   IsReadOnly="True"
                   Description="Copy it, but it cannot change."
                   Width="360"
                   HorizontalAlignment="Left" />
        <arc:Input Label="Website"
                   Text="example"
                   ErrorMessage="Enter a full address, like https://example.com."
                   Width="360"
                   HorizontalAlignment="Left" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

- **Read-only** keeps the value focusable, selectable and copyable, and assistive technology still reads it. Use it
  for values people need to see and copy but cannot change here, such as an ID.
- **Disabled** fades the field to 50% and removes it from the tab order. Use it only while a value cannot apply,
  and say why nearby, for example in the description of a switch that turns the feature on.
- **Invalid** shows the danger border and the error row. Keep the error until the value is fixed; do not clear it
  on focus.

### Field foundation

`Field` adds a label and message rows around a `FieldFrame`. Pickers and special inputs reuse both.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.InputFieldFoundationDemo">
    <arc:Field Label="Due date"
               Description="Pickers and special inputs reuse Field and FieldFrame."
               Width="360"
               HorizontalAlignment="Left">
        <arc:FieldFrame>
            <arc:FieldFrame.Prefix>
                <arc:ArcGlyph Data="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Calendar}" Size="18" />
            </arc:FieldFrame.Prefix>
            <TextBlock Text="Pick a date"
                       FontSize="14"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
        </arc:FieldFrame>
    </arc:Field>
</UserControl>
```

Use `Field` and `FieldFrame` when you build your own trigger or composite editor and want it to look and behave
like the other fields: the same label, frame states, message rows and size. `Field.MessageSwap` chooses how the rows
change: `Words` (the default) moves only the words that changed; `Whole` replaces the entire line.

### Example: workspace settings form

A settings form in a SaaS admin console. The labels are short nouns, the helper copy explains consequences
("Shown on invoices"), the workspace ID is read-only so it can be copied, and the URL field shows the fixed part of
the address as a prefix so the person types only the workspace's own part. The email field shows the kind of error
the form should produce: what is wrong and how to fix it.

![A workspace settings form with a read-only ID, a URL field with a prefix and an email error](https://docs.tkcode.si/shots/Docs/TextFields/Input/images/WorkspaceForm.webp)

```xml
<StackPanel Width="560" Spacing="20">
    <arc:Input Label="Workspace name"
               Text="Acme Analytics"
               Description="Shown on invoices and in emails to your team." />
    <arc:Input Label="Workspace ID"
               Text="ws_7f3a9c21"
               IsReadOnly="True"
               Description="Use it when you contact support." />
    <arc:Input Label="Workspace URL"
               Text="acme-analytics"
               Description="Lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens.">
        <arc:Input.Prefix>
            <TextBlock Text="app.acme.dev/"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}"
                       VerticalAlignment="Center" />
        </arc:Input.Prefix>
    </arc:Input>
    <arc:Input Label="Billing email"
               Text="billing@acme"
               ErrorMessage="Enter a full email address, such as billing@acme.com." />
    <StackPanel Orientation="Horizontal" Spacing="8" HorizontalAlignment="Right">
        <arc:Button Content="Cancel" Variant="Secondary" />
        <arc:Button Content="Save changes" />
    </StackPanel>
</StackPanel>
```

### Content guidelines

- **Label**: a short noun phrase in sentence case, without a colon: "Work email", not "Please enter your work email:".
  The label stays visible while typing, so it carries the meaning; a placeholder does not.
- **Placeholder**: an example of the expected format ("name@company.com", "acme-analytics"), never the only
  instruction and never a repeat of the label. It disappears as soon as typing starts.
- **Description**: one sentence about a constraint or a consequence: "3 to 20 characters", "Shown on invoices".
  Write numbers as digits so counts roll smoothly.
- **Error**: say what is wrong and how to fix it, in the same terms as the description. Avoid blame and jargon.

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| Invalid input. | Enter an email address such as name@company.com. |
| Error: field required | Enter your full name. |
| Username too short!! | Use at least 3 characters. |
| Regex mismatch | Use only lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens. |

### Best practices

**Do**

- Give every input a visible label, even in compact layouts; use `IsLabelVisible="False"` only when a visible
  heading or a column header already names it.
- Keep one long-lived string per message row and update it, so the motion explains what changed.
- Put the field the error is about in focus when a submit fails, and keep the entered value.
- Match the field width to the expected value: a postal code field should not span the page.

**Avoid**

- Placeholder text as the label, or instructions that disappear when typing starts.
- Errors that appear on the first keystroke for format rules; wait for blur or submit.
- Disabling the submit button until the form is valid; people cannot discover what is missing. Validate on submit
  instead and point to the first problem.
- Swapping between several different message strings on a timer; the row then never settles.

### Common questions

**My binding has a validation error, but the field shows another message.** `ErrorMessage` wins over the binding's
error. Clear `ErrorMessage` (set it to `null` or an empty string) and the validation message shows.

**How do I submit the form with Enter?** `Input` does not handle Enter itself. Set `IsDefault="True"` on the form's
primary `Button`; Enter in any field then presses it.

**How do I ask for the email keyboard or autofill hints?** Use Avalonia's attached
`TextInputOptions.ContentType`, for example `TextInputOptions.ContentType="Email"`. On-screen keyboards and input
methods use it.

**Why is there no right-click menu?** The Arc input has no context menu; cut, copy, paste, undo and select all work
from the keyboard.

**Does the word-by-word rewrite work for Chinese or Japanese copy?** The row splits text at spaces. Copy without
spaces changes as one piece, which still animates but rewrites the whole line.

## API reference

### Input

Arc input: a single-line field with a visible label, helper and error rows that open on a spring and rewrite only the words that change, and the Arc frame states (hover and focus darken the border, an error turns it danger, disabled fades). Everything from Avalonia's TextBox is kept: caret, selection, IME, undo, clipboard and a two-way `Text`.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Label` | `string?` | `null` | The visible label above the frame; also the accessible name. |
| `Description` | `string?` | `null` | Helper copy under the frame (rewrites changed words in place; counts roll). |
| `ErrorMessage` | `string?` | `null` | Error copy under the frame; non-empty makes the field invalid. |
| `IsInvalid` | `bool` | `false` | Invalid state; always true while an error is shown. |
| `IsLabelVisible` | `bool` | `true` | When false the label is hidden visually but still names the field. |
| `Size` | `ControlSize` | `Medium` | Frame height: Small 36, Medium 44 (default), Large 50. |
| `Prefix` | `object?` | `null` | Content before the text (icon, unit, currency). |
| `Suffix` | `object?` | `null` | Content after the text (unit, action button). |
| `Placeholder` | `string?` | `null` | Hint shown while the field is empty (same as `PlaceholderText`). |
| `EffectiveErrorMessage` | `string?` | – | *Read-only.* The error actually shown: `ErrorMessage`, else the binding's validation message. |

Pseudo-classes: `:invalid`

Derives from `TextBox`: every member of `TextBox` works as well.

## Accessibility

- `Label` names the field. With `IsLabelVisible="False"` the label is hidden but still names it.
- The description and the error are the field's help text, read after the name and the value.
- The error row is an assertive live region: a new error is announced at once, without moving focus.
- Animated words are hidden from assistive technology, which reads a plain copy instead.
- Caret, selection, IME, undo and clipboard shortcuts are the native `TextBox` behavior.
- Hover and focus change only the border color; the focused field is the one with the darker border and the caret.
  When focus is hard to see in a dense form, use `Large` or add space between the fields rather than removing the
  label.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` | Move to the next or previous field; a read-only field is still a stop, a disabled one is not |
| `Left` / `Right`, `Home` / `End` | Move the caret by character or to the start or end |
| `Ctrl+Left` / `Ctrl+Right` (`Option` on macOS) | Move the caret by word |
| `Shift` + any of the above | Extend the selection |
| `Ctrl+A`, `Ctrl+C`, `Ctrl+X`, `Ctrl+V` (`Cmd` on macOS) | Select all, copy, cut, paste |
| `Ctrl+Z` / `Ctrl+Y` (`Cmd+Z` / `Cmd+Shift+Z` on macOS) | Undo, redo |
| `Enter` | Not handled by the input; presses the window's default button when there is one |

## Motion

- Helper and error rows open their height on a smooth spring. Changed words rise in and unblur, and numbers roll
  digit by digit.
- Reduced motion shows the rows at full height and swaps words with an instant fade. Off jumps to the end state.
- Hover and focus only darken the border; nothing changes size.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| A message row appears or goes | Height opens on a smooth spring and the text fades in | Shown at full height | Immediate |
| A message changes | Only the changed words rise in from below with a soft blur | Instant fade | Immediate |
| A number in the copy changes | Only the changed digits roll, up when it grows, down when it shrinks | Instant fade | Immediate |
| Hover, focus, invalid | The border color crossfades | The border color crossfades | Immediate |

## Related

- `Textarea` for several lines, `PasswordField` for secrets and `SearchField` for search.
- `Field` and `FieldFrame` give any editor or trigger the same label, frame and message rows.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `Textarea` | The text runs over several lines or people paste paragraphs |
| `PasswordField` / `PasswordStrength` | The value is a secret, or a new password with rules |
| `SearchField` / `ExpandingSearch` | The text filters or searches instead of being saved |
| `NumberField` / `MoneyInput` / `PhoneInput` | The value is a number, an amount or a phone number that needs parsing |
| `TagInput` / `MentionInput` | The value is a list of tokens or text with @mentions |
| `InlineEdit` | A title or a name is renamed where it is shown |
| `Field` + `FieldFrame` | You build your own editor or trigger and want it to match the other fields |

---

# Textarea

> A multiline field for notes, descriptions, and longer text.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/textarea

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.TextareaLiveCountDemo">
    <arc:Textarea x:Name="Bio"
                  Label="Bio"
                  Placeholder="A sentence or two about you"
                  Description="160 characters left"
                  MaxLength="160"
                  Width="420"
                  HorizontalAlignment="Left"
                  TextChanged="OnTextChanged" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class TextareaLiveCountDemo : UserControl
{
    private const int Limit = 160;

    public TextareaLiveCountDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
    }

    // The count rolls only the digits that change.
    private void OnTextChanged(object? sender, TextChangedEventArgs e)
        => Bio.Description = $"{Limit - (Bio.Text?.Length ?? 0)} characters left";
}
```

## When to use

`Textarea` is the field for free text that runs over several lines: a reply to a customer ticket, an incident summary, a
product description, a note on an invoice. It fills its column, starts at a usable height and lets the person drag it
taller, so a long value stays readable without the form jumping around it. The helper and error rows are the same as
`Input`, so a multi-line field fits a form column without special layout.

- **Replies in a support console**: an agent writes a reply of a few sentences to a ticket. A live count against the
  reply limit tells the agent how much room is left, and the field keeps the draft while the agent checks an order.
- **Incident summaries and change notes**: an operator writes what happened, when, and what changed. Several paragraphs
  need line breaks and room to re-read, which a single-line `Input` does not give.
- **Product and catalog descriptions**: a merchandising editor enters a description that the storefront shows, with a
  count of characters against the limit the storefront enforces.
- **Feedback and survey answers**: a short free-text question such as "What would make the export faster?" with a rule
  for a minimum length that is checked when the person submits.
- **Internal notes on an account or an invoice**: a billing operator records why a refund was approved. The note is
  saved with the record, so a resizable field helps when the note is long.

## When not to use

- **A single line such as a name, an email address or a subject**: use `Input`, which has the same rows and no line
  breaks to manage.
- **A secret**: use `PasswordField`, or `PasswordStrength` when the person chooses a new password.
- **Text with headings, lists, links or emphasis**: use `RichTextEditor`. A `Textarea` holds plain text only.
- **Editing a title or a short description in place on a page**: use `InlineEdit`, which looks like text until it is
  edited.
- **A list of short values such as tags or recipients**: use `TagInput`, which turns each entry into a token.

## Usage

Enter adds a line. The field fills its column and is at least 110 px tall.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:Textarea Label="Bio"
                  Placeholder="A sentence or two about you"
                  Description="160 characters left"
                  MaxLength="160"
                  Width="420"
                  HorizontalAlignment="Left" />
</UserControl>
```

`Textarea` derives from the shared Arc field base over Avalonia's `TextBox`. It turns on `AcceptsReturn` and wraps the
text at the width of the frame, so a line break is a plain Enter. `Text` is two-way, `MaxLength` stops input at the limit,
`IsReadOnly`, the caret, selection, undo, IME and the clipboard are the native text box behavior. The field adds the
label, the Arc frame, the helper and error rows, the focus ring and the resize grip.

### Anatomy

1. **Label** (`Label`): 14 px, medium weight, 8 px above the frame, the same as `Input`. It is the field's accessible
   name. Hide it with `IsLabelVisible="False"` only when a visible heading already names the field.
2. **Frame**: a 1 px border with the control radius on the surface color, and 12 px of padding on every side. Hover and
   focus only darken the border. A focused field draws a 3 px focus ring around the border.
3. **Text and placeholder** (`Placeholder`): the text wraps at the inner width of the frame. The placeholder shows in the
   muted text color while the field is empty.
4. **Minimum height**: the frame is at least 110 px tall at every size. The frame does not grow with its content; when the
   text is longer than the frame, the text scrolls inside it.
5. **Resize grip** (`IsResizable`): a 12 px cell in the lower-right corner with two short diagonal strokes, pulled into
   the padding so it sits close to the border. It is hidden when `IsResizable` is false and when the field is disabled.
6. **Description row** (`Description`): 12 px helper copy in a muted color under the frame. A count such as "120
   characters left" lives here.
7. **Error row** (`ErrorMessage`): 12 px copy in the danger color. While it has text, the field is invalid.

### Choosing a height

The frame starts at 110 px and keeps that height until the person drags the grip or your code sets `FrameHeight`. The
grip writes the chosen height in pixels, and any value below the 110 px minimum is raised to the minimum.

- **Short notes in a form column** (a comment, a reason for a change): keep the 110 px minimum and leave the grip on, so
  the person can make room for a longer note without a separate screen.
- **Replies and summaries of several paragraphs**: start taller by setting `FrameHeight` to about 200, so the first
  view shows the whole draft.
- **A fixed layout such as a dashboard card or a side panel**: set `IsResizable="False"`, so the card keeps its
  geometry. The field then scrolls its text.
- **A field that must keep the size the person chose**: bind `FrameHeight` with `Mode=TwoWay` and store the value in the
  view model or in user settings. `FrameHeight` is one-way by default.

### Binding to a view model

The view model owns the reply and its rules. It counts the characters, reports the error from a submit, and clears the
error when the reply changes.

```csharp
public partial class ReplyViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    private const int MaxReplyLength = 500;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private string _replyText = string.Empty;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private string? _replyError;

    public string CountText => $"{MaxReplyLength - ReplyText.Length} characters left";

    partial void OnReplyTextChanged(string value)
    {
        ReplyError = null;
        OnPropertyChanged(nameof(CountText));
    }

    [RelayCommand]
    private void SendReply()
    {
        ReplyError = ReplyText.Trim().Length < 40
            ? "Add a little more detail: at least 40 characters."
            : null;
        if (ReplyError is not null)
        {
            return;
        }
        // Send the reply to the ticket service here.
    }
}
```

```xml
<StackPanel Spacing="16">
    <arc:Textarea Label="Reply to the customer"
                  Text="{Binding ReplyText}"
                  Description="{Binding CountText}"
                  ErrorMessage="{Binding ReplyError}"
                  MaxLength="500"
                  Width="520"
                  HorizontalAlignment="Left" />
    <arc:Button Content="Send reply"
                Command="{Binding SendReplyCommand}"
                HorizontalAlignment="Left" />
</StackPanel>
```

`Text` is two-way. `Description`, `ErrorMessage`, `IsResizable` and `IsEnabled` are one-way. `FrameHeight` is one-way
unless you bind it with `Mode=TwoWay`, as described above. The control has no command of its own; the send action is a
command on the view model.

### Live count and validation

Update the description as the text changes. Only the digits that change roll. Set `ErrorMessage` to mark the
field invalid; an empty value clears the error.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.TextareaValidationDemo">
    <arc:Textarea Label="Feedback"
                  Text="Loving the new dashboard, but"
                  ErrorMessage="Tell us a little more: at least 40 characters."
                  Width="420"
                  HorizontalAlignment="Left"
                  TextChanged="OnTextChanged" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class TextareaValidationDemo : UserControl
{
    public TextareaValidationDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
    }

    private void OnTextChanged(object? sender, TextChangedEventArgs e)
    {
        var feedback = (Textarea)sender!;
        feedback.ErrorMessage = (feedback.Text?.Trim().Length ?? 0) < 40
            ? "Tell us a little more: at least 40 characters."
            : null;
    }
}
```

```csharp
const int limit = 160;
bio.TextChanged += (_, _) =>
{
    var length = bio.Text?.Length ?? 0;
    bio.Description = $"{limit - length} characters left";
    bio.ErrorMessage = length < 40 ? "Tell us a little more: at least 40 characters." : null;
};
```

`MaxLength` stops the person at the limit but shows nothing, so the count must come from your code, as above. Count
the length the way the storefront or the server counts it: a `TextBox` counts UTF-16 characters, so an emoji takes two.

The validation rules follow the same pattern as `Input`: check each rule at the moment the person can act on it.

| Rule | When to check | Where it shows |
|---|---|---|
| Maximum length | While typing; `MaxLength` stops input | `Description` counts down; no error needed |
| Minimum length of a reply | On submit, then while the reply is still short | `ErrorMessage`; move focus to the field |
| Required | On submit | `ErrorMessage` |
| Content checks on the server, such as a blocked phrase | After the request returns | `ErrorMessage`, cleared when the text changes |

### Bind the text

`Text` is a two-way property. Bind it to a view model string.

```xml
<arc:Textarea Label="Feedback"
              Text="{Binding Feedback}"
              ErrorMessage="{Binding FeedbackError}" />
```

Enter stores a line break in `Text`. On Windows the break can be stored as `\r\n`, so normalize line endings before you
compare two values or save the text to a system that expects `\n`.

### Resizing

The corner grip drags the field taller. The height starts at the minimum and does not follow the content;
the field scrolls instead. Turn the grip off with `IsResizable`.

```xml
<arc:Textarea Label="Notes"
              IsResizable="False"
              Text="Fixed height." />
```

When the user drags the grip, `FrameHeight` holds the chosen height in pixels. Set it from code to start
the field at a given height.

```csharp
notes.FrameHeight = 200;
```

### Disabled

A disabled field is faded to 0.6 and has no grip.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.TextareaDisabledDemo">
    <arc:Textarea Label="Notes"
                  IsResizable="False"
                  Text="Not resizable, disabled."
                  IsEnabled="False"
                  Width="420"
                  HorizontalAlignment="Left" />
</UserControl>
```

### Example: Support reply form

A reply form in a support console. The agent has written a reply of 280 characters against a limit of 500, so the count
shows 220 characters left. The field is a little taller than the minimum because a reply is a few sentences, and the
grip in the lower-right corner shows that the field can be taller. The buttons below the field use the verbs and
objects the agent needs: save the draft, or send the reply. The screenshot is the settled state: no error, the count is
final and the text fits the frame.

![Support reply form with a live count and a resize grip](https://docs.tkcode.si/shots/Docs/TextFields/Textarea/images/SupportReply.webp)

```xml
<StackPanel Width="600" Spacing="20">
    <TextBlock Text="Reply to Northwind Logistics"
               FontSize="18"
               FontWeight="SemiBold"
               Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
    <arc:Textarea Label="Reply"
                  Text="Thanks for the detail. The export stopped at 2 million rows because the workspace reached its row limit. We raised the limit to 5 million rows on your plan, so the export should now finish. If the file is still incomplete tomorrow morning, reply here and we will rerun it for you."
                  Description="220 characters left"
                  MaxLength="500"
                  FrameHeight="180" />
    <StackPanel Orientation="Horizontal"
                HorizontalAlignment="Right"
                Spacing="12">
        <arc:Button Content="Save draft" Variant="Secondary" />
        <arc:Button Content="Send reply" />
    </StackPanel>
</StackPanel>
```

### Content guidelines

Name the content, not the control. A label says what the note is for, and an error says what to add.

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| Notes | Reason for the refund |
| Enter text here | Describe what you tried before the error |
| Invalid input | Add a little more detail: at least 40 characters. |
| Max 500 | 220 characters left |
| Submit | Send reply |
| Field is required | Add a reason for the refund. |

Use sentence case for labels and messages, digits for counts, and a full sentence for each error. Keep the count in the
description in the same words everywhere it appears, so a reply shows "characters left" in the same form in every screen.

### Best practices

**Do**

- Show the count before the limit is near, and count the way the server counts. A person who can see the room left
  shortens the text before a save is rejected.
- Use `MaxLength` as the hard stop and the description as the feedback. `MaxLength` alone gives no feedback, so the
  person only learns about the limit when the text stops changing.
- Start at the 110 px minimum for a short note and set `FrameHeight` for long content. A tall empty field makes a short
  form look unfinished.
- Keep the draft in the view model when the person leaves the screen. A multi-line draft is the costliest value to retype.
- Normalize line endings before you compare or save the text. A `\r\n` break from Windows and a `\n` break from another
  system otherwise look like different values.

**Avoid**

- Expecting the field to grow with its content. It scrolls, so the person cannot see the whole draft at once; give it a
  height that fits the task.
- Showing a minimum-length error while the person is still writing the first sentence. It reads as blame; check on
  blur or on submit.
- Using a `Textarea` for a single line such as a name or a subject. Enter adds a line, and pasted text keeps its breaks.
- Turning off `IsResizable` in a form where people read long text. The field then has only its minimum height, and the
  text scrolls in a small window.
- Relying on the grip for keyboard users. The grip responds to the pointer only, so give the field a height that works
  without resizing.

### Common questions

**Why does the field stay the same height while I type more lines?** It holds its height so the form layout does not
move. The text scrolls inside the frame. Let the person drag the grip, or set `FrameHeight` to the height the task needs.

**Why does `FrameHeight` of 60 still show a 110 px field?** Any height below the 110 px minimum is raised to the minimum.
The minimum applies at every `Size`, so `Small` does not make the field shorter.

**Does the field insert a tab character when the person presses Tab?** No. `AcceptsTab` is false, so Tab moves focus to
the next control. Set `AcceptsTab="True"` only when the field is a code or table editor and a tab character is the value.

**Can keyboard users resize the field?** No. The grip responds to the pointer only. Set `FrameHeight` in code, or
choose a fixed layout that works at the minimum height.

## API reference

### Textarea

Arc textarea: a labeled multiline field (Enter adds a line) with the same helper / error rows as `Input`; a live count in the description ("120 characters") rolls only the digits that change. It fills its column with a 110px minimum height and, like Arc's `resize: vertical`, can be made taller by dragging the corner grip (`IsResizable`). Focus draws Arc's 3px focus ring around the border. Arc's textarea does not grow with its content, so neither does this one; it scrolls instead.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `IsResizable` | `bool` | `true` | Shows the corner grip that drags the field taller (Arc: `resize: vertical`). Default true. |
| `FrameHeight` | `double` | `NaN` | Height chosen with the grip, in px; NaN follows the minimum height. |
| `Label` | `string?` | `null` | The visible label above the frame; also the accessible name. |
| `Description` | `string?` | `null` | Helper copy under the frame (rewrites changed words in place; counts roll). |
| `ErrorMessage` | `string?` | `null` | Error copy under the frame; non-empty makes the field invalid. |
| `IsInvalid` | `bool` | `false` | Invalid state; always true while an error is shown. |
| `IsLabelVisible` | `bool` | `true` | When false the label is hidden visually but still names the field. |
| `Size` | `ControlSize` | `Medium` | Frame height: Small 36, Medium 44 (default), Large 50. |
| `Prefix` | `object?` | `null` | Content before the text (icon, unit, currency). |
| `Suffix` | `object?` | `null` | Content after the text (unit, action button). |
| `Placeholder` | `string?` | `null` | Hint shown while the field is empty (same as `PlaceholderText`). |
| `EffectiveErrorMessage` | `string?` | – | *Read-only.* The error actually shown: `ErrorMessage`, else the binding's validation message. |

Pseudo-classes: `:invalid`

Derives from `TextBox`: every member of `TextBox` works as well.

## Accessibility

- `Label` names the field. `Description` and `ErrorMessage` are merged into its help text.
- An error is announced assertively when it appears. Animated copy is hidden from assistive technology, which reads
  a plain version instead.
- Enter inserts a line break. Caret, selection, IME, undo and clipboard shortcuts are the native `TextBox` behavior.
- Focus draws a 3 px focus ring around the frame.
- The resize grip responds to the pointer only. A keyboard user keeps the minimum height and scrolls the text, so the
  layout must work at 110 px. Set `FrameHeight` in code when the content needs more room for everyone.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| Text keys | Insert text; `Enter` inserts a line break |
| `Up` / `Down` | Move the caret between lines |
| `Home` / `End`, `Ctrl+Home` / `Ctrl+End` (`Cmd` on macOS) | Move to the start or end of the line, or of the text |
| `Shift` + any of the above | Extend the selection |
| `Ctrl+A`, `Ctrl+C`, `Ctrl+X`, `Ctrl+V`, `Ctrl+Z`, `Ctrl+Y` (`Cmd` on macOS) | Select all, copy, cut, paste, undo and redo |
| `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` | Move focus to the next or previous control; `AcceptsTab` stays false, so Tab does not insert a tab character |

## Motion

- The helper and error row opens its height on a smooth spring. Changed words rise in with a soft blur.
- The character count rolls only the digits that change.
- Dragging the grip sets the height directly, so the frame follows the pointer without a transition.
- Reduced motion removes the spring, the digit roll and the blur, and changes the copy at once. Off does the same.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| A message row appears or goes | Height opens on a smooth spring and the text fades in | Shown at full height | Immediate |
| A message changes | Only the changed words rise in from below with a soft blur | Instant fade | Immediate |
| A number in the count changes | Only the changed digits roll, up when it grows, down when it shrinks | Instant fade | Immediate |
| Hover, focus, invalid | The border color crossfades | The border color crossfades | Immediate |

## Related

- `Input` for a single line of text.
- `InlineEdit` to edit a value in place without a visible frame.
- `TagInput` for a list of short values rather than free text.
- `RichTextEditor` for text that needs headings or lists.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `Input` | The value is one line, such as a name, an email or a subject |
| `RichTextEditor` | The text needs headings, lists, links or emphasis |
| `InlineEdit` | A title or a short description is renamed where it is shown |
| `TagInput` | The value is a list of short tokens such as tags or recipients |
| `PasswordField` / `PasswordStrength` | The value is a secret |
| `SearchField` | The text filters a list instead of being saved |

# Password field

> Capture sensitive text with a visible reveal control.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/password-field

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.PasswordFieldSignInDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12">
        <arc:PasswordField x:Name="Password"
                           Label="Password"
                           Placeholder="Your password"
                           Description="Use the reveal toggle to check what you typed."
                           Width="360"
                           HorizontalAlignment="Left" />
        <TextBlock x:Name="State"
                   Text="Hidden"
                   FontSize="14"
                   TextWrapping="Wrap"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class PasswordFieldSignInDemo : UserControl
{
    public PasswordFieldSignInDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Password.PropertyChanged += (_, e) =>
        {
            if (e.Property == PasswordField.IsRevealedProperty)
            {
                State.Text = Password.IsRevealed ? "Shown" : "Hidden";
            }
        };
    }
}
```

## When to use

`PasswordField` holds a secret that already exists and that the person types or pastes: a password at sign-in, a
current password that confirms a sensitive change, or a secret an operator enters into an admin screen. It is an
`Input` with the value masked by default and a reveal toggle inside the frame, so the label, the helper row, the error
row and the sizes behave exactly as they do on every other field of the form.

- **Sign-in to a SaaS or billing portal**: an email field and a password field stacked in a card, with one "Sign in"
  button. The toggle lets the person check a long passphrase they typed on a phone keyboard before they submit.
- **Re-authentication for a sensitive change**: "Current password" on an Acme Billing screen that changes the payout
  account or the card on file. The field asks for the secret before the change is applied, and the toggle helps the person
  avoid a typo that would lock them out of the change.
- **Operator credentials in an admin console**: a database or SMTP password entered on a settings page. The value is
  masked on screen, but the operator can reveal it to confirm a paste went in correctly.
- **Confirming an existing secret in a multi-step flow**: a second field that repeats a password the person already
  chose, such as "Confirm password" when a settings page saves a change to it.
- **Secrets entered on a shared or recorded screen**: a masked default keeps the value off the display until the person
  reveals it, which matters for kiosks, demos and support sessions.

## When not to use

- **Choosing a new password with rules**: use `PasswordStrength`, which shows how strong the value is and which rules it
  meets. A plain `PasswordField` gives no feedback about the value's quality.
- **Text that is not secret**: use `Input`. A masked field for a username or an account number makes people type blind.
- **A secret that must be copied out**: a generated API key, a recovery code or a token that the person copies to another
  system. Use `Input` with `IsReadOnly` and a `CopyButton`, because a masked value cannot be read back for copying.
- **A search query**: use `SearchField`. It has a clear control and submits on Enter; a masked search field hides what the
  person is looking for.
- **A one-time code from an authenticator app**: use `Input`. Codes are short, shown as typed and often pasted, so the
  dots and the reveal toggle only slow the person down.

## Usage

The eye toggle inside the field shows or hides the text. Its name is read by assistive technology.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:PasswordField Label="Password"
                       Placeholder="Your password"
                       Description="Use the reveal toggle to check what you typed."
                       Width="360"
                       HorizontalAlignment="Left" />
</UserControl>
```

`PasswordField` derives from the same shared field base as `Input`, and that base derives from Avalonia's `TextBox`. The
text box provides the value, caret, selection, IME composition, undo and the clipboard shortcuts. The shared base provides
the label, the frame, the helper and error rows, the sizes and the invalid state. `PasswordField` adds the mask (a `•`
password character by default, from the text box's `PasswordChar`), the reveal toggle, and the eye glyph inside the toggle.
Read the `Input` page for the parts that both fields share, such as validation timing and the message rows.

### Anatomy

1. **Label** (`Label`): 14 px, medium weight, above the frame. It is also the field's accessible name. `IsLabelVisible`
   hides it visually while the name stays.
2. **Frame**: a 1 px border with the control radius on the surface color. Hover and focus only darken the border;
   an error turns it to the danger color.
3. **Prefix** (`Prefix`): optional content before the text. The reveal toggle takes the suffix position of the frame,
   so the inherited `Suffix` property does not show on a password field.
4. **Masked text**: the typed value shown with the `PasswordChar` (`•`). When `IsRevealed` is `True`, the same text shows
   as characters. `Placeholder` shows in the muted text color while the value is empty.
5. **Reveal toggle**: a 30 px round button in the Medium and Large sizes and 26 px in Small, with a 7 px inset from the
   top, bottom and trailing edge in Medium. It holds an 18 px eye glyph with a slash. The toggle has a hover fill in the
   muted surface color and a 2 px focus ring for keyboard focus.
6. **Description row** (`Description`): 12 px helper copy under the frame.
7. **Error row** (`ErrorMessage`): 12 px copy in the danger color. While it has text, the field is invalid.

The frame padding changes with the size: 12 px before the text and 6 px after the toggle in Medium, 10 and 4 px in Small,
and 14 and 9 px in Large. The text runs at the body size (14 px) in Medium and Small, and at the base type size in Large.

### Bind the value

`Text` is a two-way property, so bind it to a view model. Use `IsRevealed` to read or set the visible state.

```xml
<arc:PasswordField Label="Password"
                   Text="{Binding Password}"
                   ErrorMessage="{Binding PasswordError}" />
```

```csharp
signIn.PropertyChanged += (_, e) =>
{
    if (e.Property == PasswordField.IsRevealedProperty)
    {
        state.Text = signIn.IsRevealed ? "Shown" : "Hidden";
    }
};
```

`IsRevealed` is two-way too. Setting it from code reveals or masks the value, and the toggle follows. The field also keeps
the text box's own `RevealPassword` in step with `IsRevealed`, so code that reads `RevealPassword` sees the same state.

### Binding to a view model

A sign-in form keeps the password in a view model with the other fields, and submits through a command. Keep the
password out of logs, analytics events and any persisted state; the view model holds it only for the request.

```csharp
public partial class SignInViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    private readonly IAuthService _auth;

    public SignInViewModel(IAuthService auth)
    {
        _auth = auth;
    }

    [ObservableProperty]
    private string _email = string.Empty;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private string _password = string.Empty;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private string? _passwordError;

    [RelayCommand]
    private async Task SignInAsync()
    {
        PasswordError = null;
        if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(Password))
        {
            PasswordError = "Enter your password.";
            return;
        }

        var result = await _auth.SignInAsync(Email, Password);
        Password = string.Empty;
        if (!result.IsSuccess)
        {
            PasswordError = "The email or password is incorrect.";
        }
    }
}
```

```xml
<StackPanel Width="360" Spacing="16">
    <arc:Input Label="Work email" Text="{Binding Email}" />
    <arc:PasswordField Label="Password"
                       Text="{Binding Password}"
                       ErrorMessage="{Binding PasswordError}" />
    <arc:Button Content="Sign in" Command="{Binding SignInCommand}" IsDefault="True" />
</StackPanel>
```

- `Text` and `IsRevealed` are two-way. `ErrorMessage` is one-way: the view model owns the message and clears it when the
  person edits the field, or when the next submit starts.
- `IsDefault="True"` on the sign-in button lets Enter in either field submit the form. The field does not handle Enter
  itself.
- The view model clears `Password` after the request, whether or not it succeeded, so the secret is not kept in memory
  longer than the request needs.

### Validation

Sign-in validates for presence and for the outcome of the request, not for the shape of the password. A password that
was valid when it was created can be shorter than today's rules, and a format rule at sign-in would lock out people who
have an older password.

| Rule | When to check | Where it shows |
|---|---|---|
| Required | On submit | `ErrorMessage`: "Enter your password." Move focus into the field |
| Wrong email or password | After the server rejects the request | `ErrorMessage` with one generic sentence for both cases |
| Account locked or rate limited | After the server answers | `ErrorMessage` with the next step ("Try again in 15 minutes.") |
| Length or character rules | Only on sign-up or a password change (use `PasswordStrength`) | Not on sign-in |
| Match with a confirmation field | When the confirmation field loses focus, or on submit | `ErrorMessage` on the confirmation field |

Clear `ErrorMessage` when the person edits the field, so the message does not outlive the value it describes. Do not
say which of the two (email or password) was wrong: a generic message avoids telling an attacker which accounts exist.

### Confirmation

Set `ErrorMessage` from the second field while the two values differ. Clear it by setting it to `null`.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.PasswordFieldConfirmDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="16">
        <arc:PasswordField x:Name="NewPassword"
                           Label="New password"
                           Width="360"
                           HorizontalAlignment="Left"
                           TextChanged="OnTextChanged" />
        <arc:PasswordField x:Name="ConfirmPassword"
                           Label="Confirm password"
                           Width="360"
                           HorizontalAlignment="Left"
                           TextChanged="OnTextChanged" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class PasswordFieldConfirmDemo : UserControl
{
    public PasswordFieldConfirmDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
    }

    private void OnTextChanged(object? sender, TextChangedEventArgs e)
    {
        ConfirmPassword.ErrorMessage = !string.IsNullOrEmpty(ConfirmPassword.Text) && ConfirmPassword.Text != NewPassword.Text
            ? "The passwords do not match yet."
            : null;
    }
}
```

The demo checks the match on every keystroke, so the error appears while the person is still typing the second value. In
an application, check the match when the confirmation field loses focus or when the form is submitted, and clear the
message as soon as the two values are equal. The message then appears once the person has finished a value, not
character by character.

### Toggle names

The toggle names come from `ShowPasswordText` and `HidePasswordText`. Set them to translate the copy.

```xml
<arc:PasswordField Label="Mot de passe"
                   ShowPasswordText="Afficher"
                   HidePasswordText="Masquer" />
```

The toggle reports its name as "Show password" or "Hide password" by default, and changes it with `IsRevealed`. Translate
both names together with the label, so a screen reader user hears one language throughout the form.

### Sizes and states

`Size` sets the frame height: `Small` is 36 and `Medium` (the default) is 44. `Large` (50) suits a single prominent field.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.PasswordFieldSizesAndStatesDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="16">
        <arc:PasswordField Label="Small"
                           Size="Small"
                           Text="secret"
                           Width="360"
                           HorizontalAlignment="Left" />
        <arc:PasswordField Label="Disabled"
                           Text="secret"
                           IsEnabled="False"
                           Width="360"
                           HorizontalAlignment="Left" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

Use one size per form, as with `Input`. `Small` suits a dense admin screen, where the toggle also gets smaller (26 px) to
keep the row in proportion. Disabled and invalid states work as they do on `Input`: a disabled field fades and leaves the
tab order, and an invalid field shows the danger border with its error row.

### Example: sign-in card

A sign-in card for a billing portal. The card names the product, the email field is a plain `Input`, and the password
field shows the error that a failed sign-in produces: one generic sentence that does not say which part was wrong. The
value is masked, which is the default state, so the picture shows what a person sees before they reveal anything. The
button is the form's default, so Enter in the password field submits the form.

![A sign-in card with an email field and a masked password field showing a generic error](https://docs.tkcode.si/shots/Docs/TextFields/PasswordField/images/SignInCard.webp)

```xml
<Border Width="560"
        Padding="32"
        CornerRadius="16"
        BorderThickness="1"
        BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Border}"
        Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Surface}">
    <StackPanel Width="360"
                Spacing="18"
                HorizontalAlignment="Center">
        <StackPanel Spacing="4">
            <TextBlock Text="Sign in to Acme Billing"
                       FontSize="20"
                       FontWeight="SemiBold"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
            <TextBlock Text="Use your work email and password."
                       FontSize="14"
                       TextWrapping="Wrap"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
        </StackPanel>
        <arc:Input Label="Work email"
                   Text="ada@acme.com" />
        <arc:PasswordField Label="Password"
                           Text="correct-horse-battery"
                           ErrorMessage="The email or password is incorrect." />
        <arc:Button Content="Sign in"
                    IsDefault="True"
                    HorizontalAlignment="Stretch" />
        <TextBlock Text="Forgot your password?"
                   FontSize="14"
                   HorizontalAlignment="Center"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
    </StackPanel>
</Border>
```

### Content guidelines

- **Label**: the noun for the secret, in sentence case: "Password", "Current password", "Confirm password". Do not write
  "Enter your password" as the label; that is an instruction for the placeholder or the error.
- **Placeholder**: optional. Use it for a short format hint only when the field has one ("At least 12 characters" belongs
  on `PasswordStrength`, not here). Do not repeat the label.
- **Description**: one sentence that explains a consequence or helps the person check the value ("Use the reveal toggle to
  check what you typed.").
- **Error**: one sentence, in the same terms as the label. For sign-in, one generic sentence covers a wrong email or a wrong
  password.
- **Toggle names**: the default "Show password" and "Hide password" are clear. Translate them with the rest of the form.

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| Enter your password please!!! | Enter your password. |
| Invalid credentials | The email or password is incorrect. |
| Password wrong | The email or password is incorrect. |
| Re-enter password | Confirm password |
| Your password must not be weak | Use at least 12 characters, with a number and a symbol. |

### Best practices

**Do**

- Keep the value masked by default, and let the person reveal it with the toggle. A masked default protects the value on
  shared screens and in screen recordings.
- Use `PasswordStrength` for any screen that sets a new password, and `PasswordField` for any screen that uses an
  existing one, so the rules appear only where a person is choosing a value.
- Show one generic message for a failed sign-in, so the form does not reveal which accounts exist.
- Clear the password from the view model after the request, and keep it out of logs and analytics.
- Keep the label, the description and the error copy in the same language, and set `ShowPasswordText` and
  `HidePasswordText` to match.

**Avoid**

- Using `PasswordField` for a value that must be copied out, such as a generated key. A masked value cannot be read back
  reliably for copying; use `Input` with `IsReadOnly` instead.
- Validating the length or the character classes of a password at sign-in. Older passwords can break newer rules, and the
  person is locked out for a rule that did not apply when they set the password.
- Turning off the mask as a default because a person found the dots hard to read. Offer the toggle, and leave the default
  alone.
- Using a placeholder that looks like a value, such as "••••••••". A person can mistake it for a saved password.
- Placing the field in a dense toolbar or header. A password is a form value; search or filter fields belong there.

### Common questions

**How do I change the mask character?** `PasswordChar` (inherited from the text box) sets the character. It defaults to
`•`. Change it only when the platform or the brand needs a different symbol; the eye toggle works the same either way.

**How do I know whether the value is revealed?** Read `IsRevealed`, or listen for `PasswordField.IsRevealedProperty`
changes, as the demo does. Setting `IsRevealed` from code reveals or hides the value and moves the toggle.

**Can I translate the toggle names without changing the label?** Yes. Set `ShowPasswordText` and `HidePasswordText` on
each field. The label and the messages are separate properties, so translating them is independent.

**Where do the length rules for a new password belong?** On the screen that sets the password, with `PasswordStrength`,
which shows how strong the value is while the person types. Keep `PasswordField` for the screens that use a password that
already exists.

## API reference

### PasswordField

Arc password field: a labeled password input with a reveal toggle inside the frame. The toggle's eye is crossed out by a slash that draws itself (it is never swapped for a second icon), and after the first toggle every switch between dots and characters resolves in place from a light blur. Enter or Space on the toggle shows or hides the password; the toggle reports its pressed state and switches its name between `ShowPasswordText` and `HidePasswordText`. The explicit reveal selection persists across focus changes until the user or caller changes `IsRevealed`.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `IsRevealed` | `bool` | `false` | Shows the password as text (two-way). |
| `ShowPasswordText` | `string` | `"Show password"` | Name of the toggle while the password is hidden. |
| `HidePasswordText` | `string` | `"Hide password"` | Name of the toggle while the password is shown. |
| `Label` | `string?` | `null` | The visible label above the frame; also the accessible name. |
| `Description` | `string?` | `null` | Helper copy under the frame (rewrites changed words in place; counts roll). |
| `ErrorMessage` | `string?` | `null` | Error copy under the frame; non-empty makes the field invalid. |
| `IsInvalid` | `bool` | `false` | Invalid state; always true while an error is shown. |
| `IsLabelVisible` | `bool` | `true` | When false the label is hidden visually but still names the field. |
| `Size` | `ControlSize` | `Medium` | Frame height: Small 36, Medium 44 (default), Large 50. |
| `Prefix` | `object?` | `null` | Content before the text (icon, unit, currency). |
| `Suffix` | `object?` | `null` | Content after the text (unit, action button). |
| `Placeholder` | `string?` | `null` | Hint shown while the field is empty (same as `PlaceholderText`). |
| `EffectiveErrorMessage` | `string?` | – | *Read-only.* The error actually shown: `ErrorMessage`, else the binding's validation message. |

Pseudo-classes: `:invalid`

Derives from `TextBox`: every member of `TextBox` works as well.

## Accessibility

- `Label` names the field. `Description` and `ErrorMessage` are merged into its help text, so a screen reader reads the name,
  the value and then the help.
- The reveal toggle is a toggle button with a pressed state. Its name changes between "Show password" and
  "Hide password", and it reports the pressed state through `IsOn`.
- The password is masked by default. Caret, selection, IME, undo and clipboard shortcuts are the native `TextBox`
  behavior.
- The error row is announced as the field's error, and the field is marked invalid while it shows.
- The toggle keeps its full contrast while the value is revealed.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` | Move between the field, its reveal toggle and the next control |
| `Enter` or `Space` on the toggle | Shows the password, or hides it when it is already shown |
| `Left` / `Right`, `Home` / `End` | Move the caret by character or to the start or end |
| `Shift` + any of the above | Extend the selection |
| `Ctrl+A`, `Ctrl+C`, `Ctrl+X`, `Ctrl+V` (`Cmd` on macOS) | Select all, copy, cut, paste |
| `Ctrl+Z` / `Ctrl+Y` (`Cmd+Z` / `Cmd+Shift+Z` on macOS) | Undo, redo |
| `Enter` in the field | Not handled by the field; a default button in the window receives it, as with `Input` |

## Motion

- The eye's slash draws itself across the icon when the state changes. The eye is never swapped for a second icon.
- Each switch between dots and characters resolves in place: the text starts at 35% opacity with a light blur and settles
  to full opacity and sharp focus.
- The toggle scales down slightly while it is pressed. The helper and error rows behave like those of `Input`.
- Reduced motion draws the slash at once and removes the blur and the press scale. Off does the same.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| Reveal or mask | The slash draws across the eye on a standard tween; the outline under it is cut and returns as the slash leaves | The slash is drawn or removed at once | Immediate |
| Dots and characters switch | The text resolves from 35% opacity and a 2 px blur to sharp | No resolve effect | No resolve effect |
| Toggle pressed | Scales to 96% while held | No scale | No scale |
| Helper and error row | As `Input`: the row opens on a smooth spring, and changed words rise in | As `Input` | As `Input` |

## Related

- `PasswordStrength` for choosing a new password and showing its strength.
- `Input` for text that is not secret.
- `SearchField` for a query with a clear control.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `PasswordStrength` | The person sets a new password and needs to see its strength and rules |
| `Input` | The value is not secret, or a secret must be read back and copied |
| `SearchField` | The text is a query that filters content on the page |
| `CopyButton` | A generated value is shown read-only and the person copies it |
| `Textarea` | The value is a long text, not a short secret |
