### Content guidelines

Name the collection being searched, and let the placeholder show examples of what matches rather than an instruction.

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| Search | Search customers |
| Type to search | Filter by name or ID |
| No results | No customers match “acme”. |
| Clear | Clear search |
| Go | Open invoice |

Use sentence case. Put the number of matches in plain text beside the field, and write the empty result as a sentence
that repeats the query, so the person can see what did not match.

### Best practices

**Do**

- Name the collection in the label, for example "Search customers" rather than "Search". The person knows what the query
  applies to, and a screen reader announces the same name.
- Filter from the full data set, not from the rows on screen. Clearing the query then restores every row.
- Show the match count beside the field. The person sees that a query matched nothing before scanning an empty list.
- Keep the field width fixed. The reserved clear slot already keeps it steady, so do not resize the field when the button
  appears.

**Avoid**

- Sending one request per key press to a remote source. Debounce the query or wait for Enter, because responses to earlier
  queries can arrive after later ones.
- Using `SearchSubmitted` for a list that already filters on each key. Enter then adds nothing and people wonder what it
  does.
- Putting a chosen value in a search field. Use `Combobox`, which keeps the choice rather than a free query.
- Relying on Escape alone to clear the field. The clear button is the visible affordance, and Escape is not discoverable.

### Common questions

**Why does Escape do nothing in a read-only field?** Escape clears only a field that has text and is not read-only. The
clear button follows the same rule, so it is hidden when `IsReadOnly` is true.

**How do I translate the clear button?** Set `ClearText`. Its default is "Clear search", and it is the button's accessible
name.

**Does `Clear` move focus?** Yes, by default. `Clear(focus: false)` empties the field and leaves focus where it is, which is
what Escape does.

**Does Enter submit when the field is empty?** Yes. `SearchSubmitted` is raised with an empty `Query`, so ignore empty
queries in your handler if an empty submit should do nothing.

## API reference

### SearchField

Arc search field: a labeled search input with a leading glass that wakes up (full contrast) while the field is focused or filled, and a clear button that pops into a reserved slot, so the field never changes width. Every keystroke updates the two-way `Text` (debounce expensive filtering yourself); Escape clears the field, Enter raises `SearchSubmitted`, and clearing with the button returns focus to the field.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ClearText` | `string` | `"Clear search"` | Name of the clear button. |
| `Label` | `string?` | `null` | The visible label above the frame; also the accessible name. |
| `Description` | `string?` | `null` | Helper copy under the frame (rewrites changed words in place; counts roll). |
| `ErrorMessage` | `string?` | `null` | Error copy under the frame; non-empty makes the field invalid. |
| `IsInvalid` | `bool` | `false` | Invalid state; always true while an error is shown. |
| `IsLabelVisible` | `bool` | `true` | When false the label is hidden visually but still names the field. |
| `Size` | `ControlSize` | `Medium` | Frame height: Small 36, Medium 44 (default), Large 50. |
| `Prefix` | `object?` | `null` | Content before the text (icon, unit, currency). |
| `Suffix` | `object?` | `null` | Content after the text (unit, action button). |
| `Placeholder` | `string?` | `null` | Hint shown while the field is empty (same as `PlaceholderText`). |
| `EffectiveErrorMessage` | `string?` | – | *Read-only.* The error actually shown: `ErrorMessage`, else the binding's validation message. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `SearchSubmitted` | `SearchSubmittedEventArgs` | Raised when Enter is pressed in the field. |

Pseudo-classes: `:filled`, `:invalid`

Derives from `TextBox`: every member of `TextBox` works as well.

## Accessibility

- `Label` names the field. The search glass is hidden from assistive technology, so the field is announced by its label
  and its value.
- The clear button is named "Clear search" by default. Set `ClearText` to translate it.
- Enter submits the query and Escape clears the field from the keyboard.
- The clear button is reachable with the keyboard while it is shown and draws the focus ring when focused. Enter on it
  clears the field and returns focus to the field, so keyboard users do not lose their place.
- `Description` and `ErrorMessage` form the field's help text, read after the name and the value, as in `Input`.
- Show the number of matches in plain text beside the field, as in the example, so the result is visible without
  counting the rows.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| Text keys | Edit the query; `TextChanged` runs on each key |
| `Enter` | Raises `SearchSubmitted` with the query and marks the key as handled |
| `Escape` | Clears a field that has text and is not read-only; focus stays in the field |
| `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` | Move to the clear button while it is shown, then to the next control |
| `Enter` on the clear button | Clears the field and returns focus to the field |
| `Left` / `Right`, `Home` / `End`, `Shift` selection, `Ctrl+A` | Native text box editing |

## Motion

- The clear button scales in from a slightly smaller size with a light blur.
- Its slot is always reserved, so the field keeps its width whether or not the button is visible.
- Pressing the clear button scales it down slightly, with full motion only.
- Reduced motion only fades the clear button, with no scale and no blur. Off shows and hides it at once.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| Clear button appears | Scales in from 0.8 on a snappy spring with a soft blur | Fades in | Immediate |
| Clear button leaves | Animates out before it is removed | Fades out | Immediate |
| Clear button pressed | Scales to 0.96 | No scale | No scale |

## Related

- `ExpandingSearch` for a compact search in a header that shows results beneath it.
- `Combobox` for a value chosen from a list.
- `Input` for a general single-line field.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `ExpandingSearch` | The search lives in a header or toolbar and opens only when used |
| `FilterToolbar` | The search sits with other filters, sort options or view switches |
| `Combobox` | The chosen value is saved in a form, not a query |
| `Input` | The text is a name, a title or a value rather than a query |
| `Textarea` | The query needs several lines, such as a question for an assistant |
| `Select` | The person chooses one option from a fixed list instead of typing |

---

# Expanding search

> An icon that morphs into a search field with results beneath it.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/expanding-search

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ExpandingSearchHeaderSearchDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="16">
        <Border Padding="12"
                CornerRadius="18"
                BorderThickness="1"
                BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Border}">
            <DockPanel>
                <TextBlock DockPanel.Dock="Left"
                           Text="Workspace"
                           FontSize="16"
                           FontWeight="Medium"
                           TextWrapping="Wrap"
                           VerticalAlignment="Center"
                           Margin="4,0,16,0"
                           Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
                <arc:ExpandingSearch x:Name="Header"
                                     Label="Search projects and docs"
                                     ItemSelected="OnItemSelected" />
            </DockPanel>
        </Border>
        <TextBlock x:Name="Chosen"
                   Text="Nothing chosen yet."
                   FontSize="14"
                   TextWrapping="Wrap"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Media;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class ExpandingSearchHeaderSearchDemo : UserControl
{
    public ExpandingSearchHeaderSearchDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        List<ExpandingSearchItem> items =
        [
            Item("q3", "Quarterly report", "Doc · Edited 2 hours ago", "Docs", ArcIcons.FileText),
            Item("roadmap", "Roadmap 2026", "Doc · Ada Lovelace", "Docs", ArcIcons.FileText),
            Item("onboarding", "Onboarding checklist", "Doc · 14 items", "Docs", ArcIcons.FileText),
            Item("atlas", "Atlas redesign", "Project · 12 open tasks", "Projects", ArcIcons.Folder),
            Item("reports", "Report automation", "Project · 4 open tasks", "Projects", ArcIcons.Folder),
            Item("billing", "Billing migration", "Project · Paused", "Projects", ArcIcons.Folder, "invoices", "payments"),
            Item("revenue", "Revenue dashboard", "Dashboard · Updated daily", "Dashboards", ArcIcons.ChartBar),
            Item("growth", "Growth funnel", "Dashboard · Weekly", "Dashboards", ArcIcons.ChartBar)
        ];
        Header.ItemsSource = items;
        // Shown before anything is typed.
        Header.Suggestions = new[] { items[0], items[3], items[6] };
    }

    private void OnItemSelected(object? sender, ExpandingSearchItemSelectedEventArgs e)
        => Chosen.Text = $"Opened “{e.Item.Title}”";

    private static ExpandingSearchItem Item(string id, string title, string meta, string group, Geometry icon, params string[] keywords)
        => new() { Id = id, Title = title, Meta = meta, Group = group, Icon = icon, Keywords = keywords };
}
```

## When to use

`ExpandingSearch` is a search for a crowded header or toolbar. At rest it is a 44 px circle with a search glyph, so it
costs no more room than an icon button. When the person activates it, the circle grows into a text field and the
matching results open beneath it in groups. It fits where a full search field would take space the page needs for
navigation, titles and actions, and where search is an occasional way to jump somewhere rather than the main task.

- **Project and document jump in a SaaS console header**: a Northwind workspace header with a notification bell and an
  avatar. Typing "atlas" opens the Atlas redesign project, and the person is in the right place in two keystrokes.
- **Recent items before the person types**: `Suggestions` shows the three documents or dashboards the person opened
  most recently under a "Recent" heading, so the field is useful before any text is typed.
- **Dashboard and report switching in an analytics app**: a toolbar that already holds a date range and an export
  button. The search finds one of 200 dashboards by name, a keyword or its owner's team without a second row of controls.
- **Support and operations tools**: a ticket, customer or order lookup in the top bar of an internal console. Each
  result has a title and one meta line (for example "Order · Paid · 12 Mar 2026"), which tells two similar results apart.
- **Settings and admin navigation**: a compact way to reach a settings page from any screen, where the list of pages is
  short enough to match on titles and keywords.

## When not to use

- **Filtering a table, list or grid already on the page**: use `SearchField`, which filters in place with a clear button
  and `SearchSubmitted`. An expanding field hides its filter behind a click, so people do not see that the list narrowed.
- **Choosing a value that is stored in a form**: use `Combobox` or `Select`. Those keep the chosen value as a field of the
  form and support validation; this control only reports the item that was chosen.
- **A global command palette that runs actions**: use the `CommandPalette` block from the gallery, which is built for
  commands with shortcuts and categories. `ExpandingSearch` is for finding records and places.
- **A search over thousands of records with server paging**: the control ranks the items it is given in memory on every
  keystroke. Query the server with `SearchField` and show the page of results in a `Table` or `DataGrid`.
- **A search that must stay visible**: a results list that a person reads through (for example, a message search with
  snippets over several lines) needs room. Put it on a page with `SearchField` and a result list.
- **A single fixed choice in the header**, such as a workspace switcher: use `DropdownMenu` or `Select`, which keep the
  options visible and labelled.

## Usage

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:ExpandingSearch Label="Search projects and docs"
                         MaxResults="6"
                         ExpandedWidth="360" />
</UserControl>
```

`ExpandingSearch` derives from Avalonia's `TemplatedControl`. Its template is a button that covers the collapsed
circle, a shell that grows with the field, and a field built on Avalonia's `TextBox`. Caret, selection, IME composition
and the clipboard shortcuts therefore behave as they do in a text box. The results list is a popup that is anchored to
the field, so it is never clipped by the header it sits in. The control adds the state machine: opening, closing,
highlighting and choosing.

### Anatomy

1. **Trigger button**: a transparent button that covers the collapsed circle. Its name is `Label`. The circle is 44 px,
   the height of the medium control size.
2. **Search glyph**: an 18 px Lucide search icon placed 12 px from the leading edge of the circle. It uses the secondary
   text color at rest and the foreground color when the field is open or focused.
3. **Shell**: a 1 px border on the surface color. It uses the default border color at rest, the strong border color while
   the field is open, and the foreground color while the field or the button has focus. The shell's corner radius
   travels from a circle to the control radius as it widens.
4. **Focus ring**: a 3 px halo outside the shell in the focus color. It shows for keyboard focus only.
5. **Field text and placeholder**: the text runs at the body size (14 px) with a 38 px leading inset and a 40 px
   trailing inset that keeps text clear of the clear button. `PlaceholderText` shows in the muted text color while the
   field is empty; when it is not set, `Label` is the placeholder.
6. **Clear button**: a 28 px round button, 7 px from the trailing edge, with a 16 px close glyph. It appears only while
   the field has text. It is not focusable; the keyboard clears the query with `Escape`, which also folds the field.
7. **Results panel**: a floating surface on the raised surface color with the floating shadow and the panel radius. It
   sits 8 px below the field, follows the field's width and is at most 352 px tall or 60% of the window height, whichever
   is smaller. Longer lists scroll inside it.
8. **Group heading**: the group name (`Group`) in the muted color, 12 px, medium weight, above its rows.
9. **Result row**: at least 48 px tall, with 12 px horizontal and 6 px vertical padding and a 20 px corner radius. It
   holds an optional 18 px icon (`Icon`), the title at 14 px with the matched text in medium weight, and an optional
   meta line at 12 px in the muted color.
10. **Empty state**: the title "No results for" followed by the query in quotes, and the `EmptyHint` line in the muted
    color.

### Items and suggestions

Fill `ItemsSource` with `ExpandingSearchItem` objects. Each item has an `Id` (a stable key, which falls back to the
title when empty), a `Title`, and optional `Meta`, `Group`, `Icon`, `Keywords` and `Tag`. `Keywords` are extra words that
find the item without being shown. `Tag` is any object you want back when the item is chosen, such as the record or
its route. Inline `Items` added in XAML work the same way: the control observes changes to that list.

`Suggestions` is a second list that appears before anything is typed, under the heading `SuggestionsLabel` (the default
heading is "Recent"). Suggestions are not filtered by the query; they are replaced by the results as soon as the person
types.

```csharp
var items = new List<ExpandingSearchItem>
{
    new() { Id = "q3", Title = "Quarterly report", Meta = "Doc · Edited 2 hours ago", Group = "Docs" },
    new() { Id = "atlas", Title = "Atlas redesign", Meta = "Project · 12 open tasks", Group = "Projects" },
    new() { Id = "billing", Title = "Billing migration", Group = "Projects", Keywords = ["invoices", "payments"] }
};

header.ItemsSource = items;
header.Suggestions = new[] { items[0], items[1] };
header.SuggestionsLabel = "Recent";
```

#### How results are ranked

Matching is case-insensitive and uses the trimmed query. Each item gets the best of four match tiers, and lower tiers
sort first:

| Tier | The query matches | Example for "report" |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | The start of the title | "Report automation" |
| 2 | The start of a word in the title (after a space, `-` or `/`) | "Quarterly report" |
| 3 | Text inside a word in the title | "Subreport tools" |
| 4 | The meta line or a keyword, when the title does not match | "Revenue", with the meta "Monthly report" |

Items with no match are dropped. Items in the same tier keep the order in which they were supplied. `MaxResults`
(default 6) applies after ranking, so the best matches stay when the list is cut. Results are then grouped under their
`Group` headings, and the groups appear in the order their first item appears in the source list, not in the order of
the best match. Only the matching items of each group are shown.

Because the tiers come first, a short item that starts with the query beats a long item that only contains it. Give
titles the words people actually type, since the start of the title carries the most weight.

### Selection

A result is chosen in two ways: the person presses `Enter` on the highlighted result, or clicks a row with the left
mouse button. Either way the choice runs in the same order:

1. The field folds back into the icon and the query is cleared.
2. Focus returns to the trigger button.
3. `ItemSelected` is raised with the chosen item in `e.Item`. The event bubbles, so a handler higher in the tree also
   sees it.
4. `SelectCommand` runs with the chosen item as its parameter, if the command can execute.

Use `SelectCommand` in an MVVM app, and the event when the code-behind needs to act on the item directly.

```csharp
header.ItemSelected += (_, e) => Open(e.Item.Id);
```

```xml
<arc:ExpandingSearch Label="Search"
                     ItemsSource="{Binding Items}"
                     SelectCommand="{Binding OpenCommand}" />
```

### Binding to a view model

The view model owns the items, the query and the navigation. The control shows the results and reports the choice.
`Query` and `IsExpanded` are two-way; `ItemsSource`, `Suggestions` and `SelectCommand` are one-way.

```csharp
public partial class HeaderViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    private readonly INavigationService _navigation;

    public HeaderViewModel(INavigationService navigation)
    {
        _navigation = navigation;
    }

    [ObservableProperty]
    private string _searchText = string.Empty;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private bool _isSearchOpen;

    public ObservableCollection<ExpandingSearchItem> SearchItems { get; } = new();

    public ObservableCollection<ExpandingSearchItem> RecentItems { get; } = new();

    [RelayCommand]
    private void OpenResult(ExpandingSearchItem? item)
    {
        if (item is null)
        {
            return;
        }
        IsSearchOpen = false;
        _navigation.Open(item.Id);
    }
}
```

```xml
<arc:ExpandingSearch Label="Search projects and docs"
                     ItemsSource="{Binding SearchItems}"
                     Suggestions="{Binding RecentItems}"
                     SuggestionsLabel="Recent"
                     Query="{Binding SearchText, Mode=TwoWay}"
                     IsExpanded="{Binding IsSearchOpen, Mode=TwoWay}"
                     SelectCommand="{Binding OpenResultCommand}" />
```

- `Query` is two-way and follows each keystroke. Collapsing the field, by `Escape` or by a choice, clears it and the view
  model sees the empty string. Setting it from the view model updates the field.
- `IsExpanded` is two-way. Setting it to `True` opens the field and focuses it; the control sets it back to `False`
  when it folds. Use it to open search from a keyboard shortcut in the window.
- Run the search where `Query` changes (in its setter or a property-changed handler) if it must run as the person types.
- `ItemsSource` is read again on each query change. Changes to an `ObservableCollection` appear at the next keystroke,
  or at once when you assign a new collection to `ItemsSource`.
- Compiled bindings need `x:DataType` on the view (the examples here leave it out for brevity).

### Open and close from code

`Expand` opens the field and moves focus into it. `Collapse` folds it back into the icon and clears the query. By
default `Collapse` returns focus to the trigger button; pass `returnFocus: false` when the caller is moving focus
somewhere else, for example to a page that the item opened.

```csharp
search.Expand();
search.Collapse();
search.Collapse(returnFocus: false);
```

`IsExpanded` is two-way, so you can also bind it to the view model. Three read-only members report what is listed:
`IsPanelOpen` (the results are showing), `VisibleItems` (the items in order, suggestions or results) and `ActiveIndex`
(the highlighted position in `VisibleItems`, or -1). Read `Query` for the text in the field.

### Anchor and width

`Anchor` sets the edge the button sits on. The field grows away from that edge up to `ExpandedWidth` (default 360).
Put the control in a lane that can hold the full width; the control fills its lane, and the field never grows past the
lane or past `ExpandedWidth`, whichever is smaller. On a narrow header the field shrinks to the lane instead of
pushing the other header items.

Use `Anchor="Start"` when the control sits at the left edge of a header or a panel, so the circle stays where the
person expects it and the field opens toward the content. Keep the default `End` when the control is at the right edge
of a toolbar, which is the common case.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             xmlns:generic="using:System.Collections.Generic"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ExpandingSearchAnchoredAtStartDemo">
    <Border Width="420" HorizontalAlignment="Left">
        <arc:ExpandingSearch Label="Find a dashboard"
                             Anchor="Start"
                             ExpandedWidth="300">
            <arc:ExpandingSearch.ItemsSource>
                <generic:List x:TypeArguments="arc:ExpandingSearchItem">
                    <arc:ExpandingSearchItem Id="revenue"
                                             Title="Revenue dashboard"
                                             Meta="Dashboard · Updated daily"
                                             Group="Dashboards"
                                             Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.ChartBar}" />
                    <arc:ExpandingSearchItem Id="growth"
                                             Title="Growth funnel"
                                             Meta="Dashboard · Weekly"
                                             Group="Dashboards"
                                             Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.ChartBar}" />
                </generic:List>
            </arc:ExpandingSearch.ItemsSource>
        </arc:ExpandingSearch>
    </Border>
</UserControl>
```

### Focus and dismissal

Opening the field moves focus into it. The results panel opens only while the field has focus, and it stays open until
the field loses focus or the field folds. Clicks outside the panel do not close it, because light dismiss is off; the
panel closes when focus leaves the field.

- **Focus leaves an empty field**: the field folds back into the icon at once, without moving focus.
- **Focus leaves a field with text**: the results close and the field stays open with its text. Focus returns to it
  through a click or a keyboard move, and the results reopen.
- **Switching to another window**: the field keeps its state. It does not fold when the window loses activation.
- **Escape**: folds the field, clears the query and returns focus to the trigger button.

### Example: project search in a console header

A header for an analytics console. The workspace name and an avatar sit on the left and right, and the search waits in
the middle as its 44 px circle, the way it looks before anyone uses it. The header reserves the room the field needs
when it opens, so the title and the avatar do not move when the person activates it. The field's results are not in the
picture: they open in a floating panel on input, as the panel description above explains. In the application, the
header would also set `Suggestions`, so the panel offers recent items as soon as the field opens.

![A console header with the workspace name, a collapsed project search circle and an avatar](https://docs.tkcode.si/shots/Docs/TextFields/ExpandingSearch/images/ProjectSearchHeader.webp)

```xml
<Border Width="680"
        Padding="16,12"
        CornerRadius="16"
        BorderThickness="1"
        BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Border}"
        Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Surface}">
    <DockPanel>
        <Border DockPanel.Dock="Right"
                Width="32"
                Height="32"
                CornerRadius="16"
                Margin="12,0,0,0"
                Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource AccentSubtle}">
            <TextBlock Text="AL"
                       FontSize="12"
                       FontWeight="Medium"
                       HorizontalAlignment="Center"
                       VerticalAlignment="Center"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
        </Border>
        <TextBlock DockPanel.Dock="Left"
                   Text="Acme Analytics"
                   FontSize="16"
                   FontWeight="Medium"
                   VerticalAlignment="Center"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
        <arc:ExpandingSearch Label="Search projects and docs"
                             ExpandedWidth="360"
                             HorizontalAlignment="Right" />
    </DockPanel>
</Border>
```

### Content guidelines

- **Label**: a short noun phrase that names what is searched, such as "Search projects and docs" or "Search orders".
  It is the accessible name of the button and the field, so it must make sense on its own.
- **Placeholder**: set `PlaceholderText` only when the default (the label) would be unclear. Show what can be found,
  not an instruction, for example "Projects, docs, dashboards".
- **Item titles**: the name the person would recognise: a project, a document, a customer. Keep titles under about
  40 characters so the row does not truncate.
- **Meta line**: one short line of facts that separates similar items: the type, the owner or the last change, with
  numbers as digits ("12 open tasks").
- **Empty hint**: name the next step ("Try a shorter word or check the spelling." is the default). Do not blame the person.
- **Group names**: plural nouns in sentence case ("Projects", "Docs", "Dashboards").
- **Suggestions label**: a short heading that says why the items are shown ("Recent", "Pinned").

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| Search... | Search projects and docs |
| No matches found!!! | No results for "forecast" |
| Results | Projects |
| Enter the name of the item you are looking for | Projects, docs, dashboards |

### Best practices

**Do**

- Name the field for what it finds ("Search projects and docs"). `Label` is the accessible name of the button, the field
  and the results, so a generic label makes every result list ambiguous.
- Set `Suggestions` for the destinations people open most. The panel then has useful content before anything is typed,
  and the first keystroke narrows a short list rather than starting from nothing.
- Give every item a stable `Id` and a `Group`. The id keeps the chosen item traceable to its record, and groups keep a
  long result list scannable.
- Put the control in a lane that can hold `ExpandedWidth`. The field never grows past its lane, so a narrow lane gives a
  cramped search and a clipped result row.
- Bind `SelectCommand` in an MVVM app. The command runs after the field folds back, so navigation starts from a settled
  header.

**Avoid**

- Searching a list that is already on the page. Use `SearchField`, which filters in place and does not hide its filter
  behind a click.
- Filling `ItemsSource` with thousands of records. Ranking runs over every item on each keystroke, so pre-filter by
  permission and let the server answer large queries.
- Relying on a hidden result when the query is empty. Without a query and without `Suggestions`, the panel shows nothing,
  so the field looks broken to a person who has not typed yet.
- Replacing the items while the field is open without a new query. The panel reads `ItemsSource` again only when the
  query changes or the property is reassigned, so a stale list stays on screen until the next keystroke.
- Using the control for a value stored in a form. `Combobox` keeps the value and its validation; this control only
  reports the item that was chosen.

### Data shape and performance

Each keystroke runs the ranking over every item, then builds the rows for the results. That is fast for hundreds of items
in a header, and slower for thousands. For a large catalogue, keep `ItemsSource` to the items the person can open in
this workspace (filter by permission before you bind), and let the server answer the query when the list is too long
for memory. Keep `MaxResults` small (6 to 8), because the panel is short by design and a long list only scrolls.

Build the items once per session and reuse them. Create a new `ExpandingSearchItem` for each record, with a stable
`Id`, so the control and the view model can match the chosen item back to its record. Put the record itself in `Tag`
when the route needs more than the `Id`.

Format numbers and dates in the meta line with the application's culture, for example
`amount.ToString("C", CultureInfo.CurrentUICulture)` for an amount, so a Chinese or German user sees the local format.
The control does not format values for you; it shows the meta string as given.

### Common questions

**Why does the field fold when I click elsewhere?** An empty field folds when it loses focus, by design, so an idle
search does not hold header space. A field with text stays open and keeps its query, so the person can come back to it.

**How do I open search with a keyboard shortcut?** Bind a shortcut in the window to a command that sets the view model's
`IsSearchOpen` to `True`, or call `Expand` on the control from the code-behind. Focus moves into the field, so the
person can type at once.

**Can a result be selected with the mouse without the keyboard?** Yes. Pressing a row with the left button keeps focus in
the field, and releasing the button on the same row chooses it. The row also takes the highlight while the pointer moves
over it, so a keyboard user and a mouse user see the same highlight.

**Why does the first result already show a highlight when I type?** As soon as the query has text, the first result is
highlighted, so `Enter` chooses it. Suggestions are shown without a highlight; `Down` selects the first suggestion.

**Why are my items not listed under the group I set?** Groups appear in the order their first item appears in
`ItemsSource`, and items keep the rank order within a group. Put the group you want first at the top of the list, and
check that `Group` matches exactly, since groups compare the text as written.

## API reference

### ExpandingSearch

Arc expanding search: a search that waits as an icon button until it is needed (headers, toolbars). The button morphs into the field on the morph spring (its corners follow the width, from a circle to the control radius), results unfold beneath it in groups with the match in medium weight, and a highlight glides between them on the snappy spring. ArrowUp / ArrowDown move (wrapping), Enter chooses, Escape folds it back into the icon; leaving an empty field folds it too. Before anything is typed it shows `Suggestions`. Place it in the lane the field may grow into: it fills that lane's width and keeps the button on the `Anchor` edge; the field never grows past `ExpandedWidth` or the lane.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Label` | `string` | `"Search"` | Names the button, the field and the results, such as "Search projects and docs". |
| `ItemsSource` | `IEnumerable<ExpandingSearchItem>?` | `null` | Items to search (alternatively add them inline as children). |
| `Suggestions` | `IEnumerable<ExpandingSearchItem>?` | `null` | Shown before anything is typed, such as recent searches. |
| `SuggestionsLabel` | `string` | `"Recent"` | Heading of the suggestions. Default "Recent". |
| `PlaceholderText` | `string?` | `null` | Hint in the open field; null shows `Label`. |
| `ExpandedWidth` | `double` | `360` | The widest the field grows (it never grows past its lane). Default 360. |
| `MaxResults` | `int` | `6` | Most results shown. Default 6. |
| `Anchor` | `ExpandingSearchAnchor` | `End` | The edge the button sits on. Default End. |
| `EmptyHint` | `string` | `"Try a shorter word or check the spelling."` | A short tip under the empty state. |
| `IsExpanded` | `bool` | `false` | Whether the field is open (two-way). |
| `Query` | `string` | `""` | The text in the field (two-way). |
| `SelectCommand` | `ICommand?` | `null` | Executed with the chosen item. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ItemSelected` | `ExpandingSearchItemSelectedEventArgs` | Raised when a result or suggestion is chosen (after the field folds back). |

Pseudo-classes: `:expanded`, `:input-focus`, `:trigger-focus`, `:trigger-pressed`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

### ExpandingSearchItem

One searchable entry of an `ExpandingSearch`.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Id` | `string` | `""` | Stable id (defaults to the title). |
| `Title` | `string` | `""` | The line that is searched first and shown in bold where it matches. |
| `Meta` | `string?` | `null` | One short line under the title (type, owner, last edit); also searched. |
| `Group` | `string?` | `null` | Results gather under this heading, in the order groups first appear. |
| `Icon` | `object?` | `null` | An 18px leading icon: a Lucide `Geometry` or any control. |
| `Keywords` | `IList<string>?` | `null` | Extra words that also find this item. |
| `Tag` | `object?` | `null` | Any value you want back when the item is chosen. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

## Accessibility

- `Label` names the trigger button and the field. The placeholder falls back to `Label`, so the name is still visible while the field is empty.
- The highlighted result's title is the field's help text. A screen reader that announces the field also says which result is highlighted as the person moves through the list.
- Each result row is named by its title, followed by its meta line when there is one ("Billing migration, Project · Paused").
- The number of results, "No results for" with the query, or the number of suggestions is announced politely. The announcement changes only when the count or the state changes.
- The collapsed field is inert: it is not focusable, takes no pointer input and is not in the tab order, so it never blocks the content under it.
- The clear button is not in the tab order. Keyboard users clear the text by selecting it and deleting, or fold the whole
  field with `Escape`.
- The button's focus ring appears for keyboard focus only (Tab or arrow navigation), so a pointer press opens the field
  without a ring. The field shows its focused border on any focus.
- Result rows are not in the tab order. Keyboard users reach them with `Down` and `Up` while the field has focus.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` | Move between the controls of the header; the collapsed button is the stop, and the open field takes its place |
| `Enter` or `Space` on the button | Opens the field and moves focus into it |
| Typing | Updates `Query`, lists the results or the empty state and highlights the first result once there is text |
| `Down` / `Up` | Move the highlight to the next or previous result and wrap at both ends. From no highlight, `Down` selects the first and `Up` selects the last |
| `Enter` | Chooses the highlighted result, folds the field and returns focus to the button. With no highlight the control does not handle it |
| `Escape` | Folds the field into the icon, clears the query and returns focus to the button |
| `Ctrl+A`, `Ctrl+C`, `Ctrl+X`, `Ctrl+V` (`Cmd` on macOS) | Select all, copy, cut and paste in the field |

## Motion

- Opening morphs the width on a spring with a slight overshoot, and the round icon becomes a rounded field. The corner
  radius rides the same spring as the width, so the two never drift apart.
- Closing folds the width back on a smoother spring with no overshoot, so the circle never dips below its size.
- The results panel opens its height from zero on a smooth spring and fades its text in. Reduced motion only fades it.
- The highlight glides between results on a snappy spring and keeps the speed of the previous move. A new result set
  fades in on its row without travel.
- A pressed button scales to 97% until it is released, and the morph takes over on release.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| Field opens | The width morphs on a spring; the placeholder and text fade in after the shape starts to move | The width changes at once; the text fades in over 150 ms | Immediate |
| Field folds | The width folds back on a smooth spring; the text fades out first | The width changes at once; the text fades out over 100 ms | Immediate |
| Results panel opens or closes | Height opens on a smooth spring; text fades in | Fades only | Immediate |
| Highlight moves | Glides between rows on a snappy spring, keeping velocity | No glide; the highlight moves in place | Immediate |
| Trigger pressed | Scales to 97% until released | No scale | Immediate |
| Hover and focus colors | The border, background and glyph colors crossfade; the focus ring fades in | Immediate | Immediate |

## Related

- `SearchField` for a field that filters content already on the page.
- `Combobox` for choosing a value that is stored in a form.
- `Input` for a general single-line field, which the search field's text box is built on.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `SearchField` | The search filters a table, a list or a page in place |
| `Combobox` / `Select` | The chosen value is stored as a field of a form |
| `DropdownMenu` | A short fixed list of actions or options is always visible in a menu |
| `Input` | A single-line value is typed and saved, not searched |
| `CommandPalette` block | The person runs commands with keyboard shortcuts across the app |
| `Breadcrumb` | The person needs to see where they are and move up the hierarchy |

# Inline edit

> Rename in place: the text becomes a field without moving.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/inline-edit

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.InlineEditRenameDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="16">
        <arc:InlineEdit x:Name="ProjectName"
                        Label="Project name"
                        Value="Atlas redesign"
                        HeadingLevel="2"
                        TextCommitted="OnTextCommitted"
                        Saved="OnSaved"
                        SaveFailed="OnSaveFailed" />
        <arc:Switch x:Name="FailNext" Content="Fail the next save" />
        <TextBlock x:Name="Log"
                   Text="Click the title to rename it."
                   FontSize="14"
                   TextWrapping="Wrap"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class InlineEditRenameDemo : UserControl
{
    public InlineEditRenameDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        ProjectName.Validator = value => value.Length == 0 ? "A project needs a name." : null;
        ProjectName.SaveHandler = SaveAsync;
    }

    // Stands in for a request; turn on the switch to see a failed save roll back.
    private async Task SaveAsync(string next)
    {
        await Task.Delay(700);
        if (FailNext.IsChecked == true)
        {
            FailNext.IsChecked = false;
            throw new InvalidOperationException("Network unavailable");
        }
    }

    private void OnTextCommitted(object? sender, InlineEditCommittedEventArgs e)
        => Log.Text = $"Committed “{e.NewValue}” (was “{e.OldValue}”)";

    private void OnSaved(object? sender, InlineEditCommittedEventArgs e)
        => Log.Text = $"Saved “{e.NewValue}”";

    private void OnSaveFailed(object? sender, InlineEditSaveFailedEventArgs e)
        => Log.Text = $"Save failed: {e.Error.Message}";
}
```

## When to use

`InlineEdit` shows a value as plain text and turns it into a field in the same place when the person chooses to edit it.
It fits the names and titles that appear on a page many times and change rarely: a project name in a header, a
dashboard title, a customer's display name on a CRM record. Nothing around the text moves when editing starts, so the
page keeps its layout, and the value saves on its own without a form around it.

- **Project and workspace names in a page header**: "Atlas redesign" at the top of a project page. People read it
  all day and rename it occasionally, so it should look like a title and become editable on activation.
- **Report and dashboard titles in an analytics app**: "Q3 revenue by region" on a dashboard. The title is saved as the
  person commits it, and a failed save returns the last saved title with a retry link.
- **Contact and account names in a CRM or billing screen**: a customer's company name or a contact's display name, where
  an edit is a single correction rather than a form submission.
- **Descriptions and short notes under a heading**: a one-line project summary, or a multiline description with
  `IsMultiline`, where the text wraps and Enter still saves.
- **Incident and ticket titles in an operations console**: a title that the on-call engineer corrects in place while the
  timeline stays where it is.

## When not to use

- **Several fields that save together**: a profile or a billing address is a form. Use `Input` or `Textarea` for each
  field and one save button, so people can review all of it before anything is saved.
- **A field that must always look editable**: a search box, an invoice number on an order that is being entered, or any
  value that people are expected to fill in. Use `Input`, which shows its frame and label at all times.
- **A long body the person writes**: a release note, a support reply or a policy text. Use `Textarea`, which holds a
  larger text and a visible frame while the person types.
- **Numbers and amounts that need parsing**: a price, a quantity or a percentage. Use `NumberField` or `MoneyInput`,
  which parse, format and step the value.
- **A value picked from a fixed list**: a status, an owner or a currency. Use `Select` or `Combobox`, which show the
  options and their state.

## Usage

The value is shown as text. Activating it turns it into a field of the same size. The value is saved when the
edit is committed.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:InlineEdit Label="Project name"
                    Value="Atlas redesign"
                    HeadingLevel="2" />
</UserControl>
```

`InlineEdit` derives from Avalonia's `TemplatedControl`. Its resting text is a button (`Enter` and `Space` start the
edit, so the text is reachable from the keyboard), and its editor is a `TextBox`, so caret, selection, IME composition
and the clipboard shortcuts work as they do in any text box. The control adds the save cycle on top: an optimistic
display of the new text, a saving indicator, a rollback on failure and the validation message.

### Anatomy

1. **Resting text**: the value in a button. The `Title` variant uses the extra-large type size (22 px) in medium
   weight on a 28 px line, with 3 px vertical and 8 px horizontal padding. The `Body` variant uses 14 px in the
   secondary text color on a 21 px line, with 5 px vertical and 8 px horizontal padding. The box has a leading margin
   of -9 px, so the text lines up with the content around it.
2. **Frame**: a box with the control radius. It stays transparent at rest, takes the muted surface color on hover
   while the text is at rest, and becomes a surface-colored box with the foreground-colored border while editing.
3. **Focus ring**: a 2 px ring at 22 px radius around the resting text when it has keyboard focus. While editing, the
   ring is 3 px and sits inside the frame.
4. **Pencil**: a 14 px muted glyph at the end of the text. It appears on hover with a fine pointer, and on keyboard focus.
   It is the visual cue that the text can be edited; touch input goes straight into the editor.
5. **Editor**: a `TextBox` with the same font metrics as the resting text, so the text does not shift when the field
   opens. Its padding adds 24 px at the trailing edge, and its minimum width is 5 em (110 px for `Title`, 70 px for
   `Body`), so the next character never waits for the box to grow.
6. **Action slot**: a reserved area at the trailing edge. While editing it holds the save button (a 28 px round primary
   button with the check glyph) and the cancel button (a 28 px outlined round button with the close glyph). While saving
   it shows a 14 px spinner; after a save it shows a check mark that draws itself; after a failed save it shows a
   danger glyph. A single line keeps 66 px free for the actions and a multiline value keeps 38 px, so the text never
   rewraps when the actions appear.
7. **Message row**: 12 px copy under the field. A validation message uses the danger color. A failed save uses the
   secondary text color and ends with the `RetryText` link, which reopens the field with the failed text.
8. **Status**: a hidden polite region that announces saving progress and the outcome.

### Variants and multiline

`Variant` sets the visual weight. `Title` is the default for names and headings; `Body` suits descriptions.
With `IsMultiline` set, the text wraps and the field grows in height. Enter still saves, and Shift+Enter adds a
line break.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.InlineEditMultilineDemo">
    <arc:InlineEdit Label="Description"
                    Variant="Body"
                    IsMultiline="True"
                    PlaceholderText="Add a description"
                    Value="A calmer home for every project: fewer clicks, clearer status and faster search across docs."
                    Width="460"
                    HorizontalAlignment="Left" />
</UserControl>
```

```xml
<arc:InlineEdit Label="Description"
                Variant="Body"
                IsMultiline="True"
                PlaceholderText="Add a description"
                Value="{Binding Description}" />
```

Use `Title` for text that names something and is read as a heading, and use `Body` for text that describes it. Keep
one variant for each kind of text on a page, so the names line up and the descriptions read as one group. Use
`IsMultiline` only for text that people write in paragraphs; a single-line name that wraps is a sign that it is too
long for the place it sits.

### Binding

`Value` is two-way. A new value from outside replaces the text while the person is not editing it.

```xml
<arc:InlineEdit Label="Project name"
                Value="{Binding ProjectName}"
                HeadingLevel="2" />
```

### Binding to a view model

In an MVVM app, the view model owns the saved value and the rules, and the control handles the editing. `Value` is
the two-way binding. `SaveHandler` and `Validator` are delegates, so they are assigned in the view's code-behind
with the view model's methods. Setting them in XAML is not possible for delegates.

```csharp
// The application's own service; it is not part of the control library.
public interface IProjectService
{
    Task RenameAsync(ProjectId id, string name);
}

public partial class ProjectHeaderViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    private readonly IProjectService _projects;
    private readonly ProjectId _projectId;

    public ProjectHeaderViewModel(IProjectService projects, ProjectId projectId)
    {
        _projects = projects;
        _projectId = projectId;
    }

    [ObservableProperty]
    private string _projectName = string.Empty;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private string _description = string.Empty;

    public string? ValidateName(string value)
        => value.Length switch
        {
            0 => "A project needs a name.",
            > 80 => "Use 80 characters or fewer.",
            _ => null
        };

    // The control sets Value to the saved text when this task completes, so the binding updates the property.
    public Task SaveNameAsync(string name) => _projects.RenameAsync(_projectId, name);
}
```

```csharp
// In the view's code-behind, after InitializeComponent and after the DataContext is set.
ProjectTitle.Validator = viewModel.ValidateName;
ProjectTitle.SaveHandler = viewModel.SaveNameAsync;
```

```xml
<StackPanel Spacing="8">
    <arc:InlineEdit x:Name="ProjectTitle"
                    Label="Project name"
                    Value="{Binding ProjectName, Mode=TwoWay}"
                    HeadingLevel="1" />
    <arc:InlineEdit Label="Description"
                    Variant="Body"
                    IsMultiline="True"
                    PlaceholderText="Add a description"
                    Value="{Binding Description, Mode=TwoWay}" />
</StackPanel>
```

- `Value` is two-way, so the saved name reaches the view model when the save lands. The control does not write the value
  before a save succeeds, so a failed save leaves the view model's property unchanged.
- A value from outside does not replace the text while the person is editing or while a save is running, so avoid
  pushing refreshed data into the view model during an edit.
- The code-behind names (`x:Name`) belong to the view. Keep the handlers in the view or in the view model; the control
  only calls them.

### Save and validation

`SaveHandler` persists the committed value. It runs while the field shows the saving state. A faulted task rolls
the text back and shows a retry link. `Validator` returns a message when the draft cannot be saved; the message
is shown under the field.

```csharp
title.Validator = value => value.Length == 0 ? "A project needs a name." : null;

title.SaveHandler = async next =>
{
    await projects.RenameAsync(projectId, next);
};
```

Handle `TextCommitted`, `Saved` and `SaveFailed` to react to the outcome.

```csharp
title.TextCommitted += (_, e) => log.Text = $"Committed “{e.NewValue}” (was “{e.OldValue}”)";
title.Saved += (_, e) => log.Text = $"Saved “{e.NewValue}”";
title.SaveFailed += (_, e) => log.Text = $"Save failed: {e.Error.Message}";
```

The save cycle has four steps, and the control exposes each one through `Phase` (`Idle`, `Saving`, `Saved`, `Failed`):

1. **Commit**: the text is trimmed (a single line also collapses inner whitespace), validated and, if it differs from
   the shown value, sent to `SaveHandler`. `TextCommitted` is raised with the previous and the new value. A commit
   that does not change the text closes the field without a save and without an event.
2. **Saving**: the new text shows at once at half opacity with a spinner. `Value` does not change yet. The field cannot
   be opened again until the save ends.
3. **Saved**: `Value` becomes the new text, `Saved` is raised and a check mark draws. The phase returns to `Idle` after
   about 1.8 seconds. Without a `SaveHandler`, the value is saved at once and the same events follow.
4. **Failed**: the shown text returns to the last saved value, `SaveFailed` is raised with the attempted text and the
   exception, and the frame flashes danger for a moment. The message row says why, using `FailedMessageFormat`, and
   offers `RetryText`. Choosing it reopens the field with the failed text and the caret at its end.

`ErrorMessage` holds the validation message while it applies. A validation failure keeps the field open with the
person's text, sets the invalid state and keeps focus in the field when the commit came from `Enter` or the save button.
The message clears when the text changes and validates again.

```csharp
// The server is the last word: its error shows as a validation message, and the next edit clears it.
title.SaveHandler = async next =>
{
    var result = await projects.RenameAsync(projectId, next);
    if (!result.IsSuccess)
    {
        throw new InvalidOperationException(result.Error);
    }
};
```

### Empty

A placeholder keeps the line until there is a value.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.InlineEditEmptyDemo">
    <arc:InlineEdit Label="Subtitle"
                    Variant="Body"
                    PlaceholderText="Add a subtitle" />
</UserControl>
```

`PlaceholderText` appears in the muted color while `Value` is empty, and the field stays as tall as a filled one, so the
layout does not jump when a value is added. Use a placeholder that says what to add ("Add a subtitle"), not a generic
prompt.

### Saving and leaving the field

Enter saves, Escape cancels, and leaving the field saves. The rules are the same whichever way the person leaves:

- **Enter** commits. In a multiline field, Shift+Enter inserts a line break instead.
- **Escape** cancels: the field closes, the saved text returns and `EditCanceled` is raised.
- **Tab, or a click outside the field** commits, the same as Enter. Focus moving to the save or cancel button does not
  commit, because the buttons belong to the control.
- **Switching to another window** does not commit. The field stays open and commits when the person returns and leaves it.
- **A validation message** keeps the field open when the commit comes from a blur as well, so the person sees the message
  before the field closes.

The Save button and the Cancel button in the action slot give the same result as Enter and Escape. The code can do the
same with `BeginEdit`, `CommitEdit` and `CancelEdit`. `BeginEdit(caret)` opens the field with the caret at a position,
and `-1` (the default) selects all the text, ready to retype.

### Example: project page header

A project page for an analytics workspace. The project name is a `Title` heading, the description is a multiline `Body`
text, and a third line holds the subtitle, which is still empty and shows its placeholder. The text looks like the
page's own content, not like a form, so the header reads as a title until someone chooses to edit it. The metadata row
below the description uses plain text, because owner and dates are read-only here. The header keeps the same layout in
both states: the frame and the text share the same metrics, so the title does not move when it becomes a field.

![A project header with an inline title, a multiline description and an empty subtitle placeholder](https://docs.tkcode.si/shots/Docs/TextFields/InlineEdit/images/ProjectHeader.webp)

```xml
<StackPanel Width="620" Spacing="8">
    <arc:InlineEdit Label="Project name"
                    Value="Atlas redesign"
                    HeadingLevel="1" />
    <arc:InlineEdit Label="Subtitle"
                    Variant="Body"
                    PlaceholderText="Add a subtitle" />
    <arc:InlineEdit Label="Description"
                    Variant="Body"
                    IsMultiline="True"
                    PlaceholderText="Add a description"
                    Value="Rebuild the analytics home with clearer status, faster search and one place for every report." />
    <TextBlock Text="Owner Ada Lovelace · Created 3 Mar 2026 · Updated 2 hours ago"
               FontSize="12"
               Margin="0,8,0,0"
               Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
</StackPanel>
```

### Content guidelines

- **Label**: the name of the field in sentence case ("Project name", "Report title"). It is the accessible name, and it
  appears in the saving announcements ("Saving project name").
- **Placeholder**: an instruction that names the content to add ("Add a subtitle", "Add a description"). Do not use
  "Click to edit", because the text itself already signals that it can be changed.
- **Validation message**: say what is wrong and what is allowed, in the same terms as the field ("A project needs a
  name.", "Use 80 characters or fewer.").
- **Failed-save sentence**: the default format reads "Couldn’t save “{0}”, so the last saved {1} is back." Keep it when
  the default reads well; change `FailedMessageFormat` only to name the object more precisely.
- **Retry text**: a verb ("Try again" by default). Keep it short, because it sits at the end of the message row.

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| Click to edit | Add a description |
| Name is required!!! | A project needs a name. |
| Error saving | Couldn’t save “Atlas”, so the last saved project name is back. |
| Enter text here | Add a subtitle |

### Best practices

**Do**

- Use `Title` for names and headings and `Body` for descriptions, and keep one variant per kind of text on a page, so
  the page reads in a consistent order.
- Set `HeadingLevel` on the title of a page or a section, so a screen reader user can jump to it by heading. Leave it
  at `0` for text that is not a heading.
- Validate the rule on the client with `Validator`, and show a server rejection through a failed `SaveHandler` with a
  clear message. The control holds the person's text while the field shows the error.
- Give each edit its own `Label`, so the announcements name the thing that was saved.

**Avoid**

- Using it for a form. Several fields that save together need `Input` or `Textarea`, where people can review every
  value before they save, and where a cancel discards all of them.
- Saving without a `SaveHandler`. Without one the value is saved at once, with no error path; add a handler whenever the
  change goes to a server, so failures roll back and the person knows.
- Long single-line names that wrap or truncate in the header. Keep titles short, or use `IsMultiline` for text that
  people write as paragraphs.
- Opening the field from code during a save. The control refuses to open while a save runs, so the call does nothing;
  check `Phase` before you open it.

### Common questions

**Why did my new name go back to the old one?** The save failed. `SaveHandler` threw an exception, the text rolled back
to the last saved value, and the message row offers "Try again". Handle `SaveFailed` to log `e.Error` and to tell the
person what went wrong.

**Why does the field stay open after I press Enter?** `Validator` returned a message. The field keeps the person's text,
marks itself invalid and shows the message. The message clears when the text changes and passes validation. A blur with a
validation message also keeps the field open.

**How do I open the field or commit it from code?** Call `BeginEdit()` to open it with all the text selected, or
`BeginEdit(caret)` to put the caret at a position. Call `CommitEdit()` to save and `CancelEdit()` to discard. Check
`IsEditing` first, because the calls do nothing when the field is not open.

**Does a refreshed value from the server overwrite what the person is typing?** No. A value from outside does not
replace the text while the person is editing or while a save runs. Hold the refresh until the edit has ended.

**Can I use it for a value with a fixed format, such as an amount or a date?** Not directly. The control holds a
string and saves what the person typed. Use `NumberField` or `MoneyInput` for amounts, and `DatePicker` for dates, so the
value is parsed before it reaches the view model.

## API reference

### InlineEdit

Arc inline edit: click-to-edit text for names and short fields read far more often than they change. The text turns into a field in place with the same metrics, so nothing around it moves, and the frame grows with what is typed. Enter commits (`TextCommitted`) and saves optimistically through `SaveHandler`: the new text shows at once, quieter until the save lands, then a check draws. Escape cancels and the text rolls back; a failed save restores the last saved `Value`, says why, and offers to try again. Tab or a click elsewhere saves like Enter. Multiline: Shift+Enter adds a line break.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Value` | `string` | `""` | The saved value (two-way). A new value from outside replaces the text while it is not being edited. |
| `Label` | `string` | `"Text"` | Accessible name, for example "Project name". |
| `PlaceholderText` | `string` | `""` | Shown while the value is empty. |
| `IsMultiline` | `bool` | `false` | Wraps onto several lines and grows in height; Enter still saves, Shift+Enter adds a line break. |
| `Variant` | `InlineEditVariant` | `Title` | Title for names and headings (default), Body for descriptions. |
| `HeadingLevel` | `int` | `0` | Heading level reported to assistive technology (Arc's `as="h1".."h3"`); 0 for none. |
| `Validator` | `Func<string, string?>?` | `null` | Returns a message when the draft cannot be saved. |
| `SaveHandler` | `Func<string, Task>?` | `null` | Persists a committed value; a faulted task rolls the text back. Null saves at once. |
| `FailedMessageFormat` | `string` | `"Couldn’t save “{0}”, so the last saved {1} is back."` | The failed-save sentence: {0} the attempted text, {1} the label in lower case. |
| `RetryText` | `string` | `"Try again"` | The retry link after a failed save. |
| `IsEditing` | `bool` | – | *Read-only.* True while the field is open. |
| `Phase` | `InlineEditPhase` | – | *Read-only.* Where the control is in its save cycle. |
| `ErrorMessage` | `string?` | – | *Read-only.* The validation message shown under the field, if any. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `TextCommitted` | `InlineEditCommittedEventArgs` | Raised when an edit is committed (Enter, Tab / click away, or the save button), before saving. |
| `EditCanceled` | `RoutedEventArgs` | Raised when an edit is cancelled with Escape or the cancel button. |
| `Saved` | `InlineEditCommittedEventArgs` | Raised when a save lands. |
| `SaveFailed` | `InlineEditSaveFailedEventArgs` | Raised when a save fails and the text rolls back. |

Pseudo-classes: `:editing`, `:invalid`, `:saving`, `:flash`, `:flash-off`, `:empty`, `:text-hover`, `:text-focus`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

## Accessibility

- The resting text is a button named with the label and the value, for example "Project name: Atlas redesign". With an
  empty value, the name uses the placeholder. Its help text is "Activate to edit."
- `HeadingLevel` reports the text as a heading to assistive technology. Use `1` to `3` for a page or section title, and
  `0` (the default) for text that is not a heading. Support for the heading level depends on the platform.
- The editor is named by `Label`. Its help text says what the keys do ("Enter saves, Escape cancels."), and while a
  validation message applies, the message replaces that help text.
- Validation messages and save errors are in a polite message row, and saving progress and the result are announced
  through a polite status region ("Saving project name", "Project name saved").
- The save and cancel buttons are named "Save project name" and "Cancel editing"; the retry link reads "Try again".
- Enter, the save button and Escape return focus to the resting text, so a keyboard user continues from the same place.
  A blur (Tab or a click elsewhere) leaves focus where the person moved it.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Enter` or `Space` on the text | Opens the field with all of the text selected, ready to retype |
| `Enter` in the field | Commits and saves; with a validation message, the field stays open |
| `Shift+Enter` (multiline) | Adds a line break |
| `Escape` in the field | Cancels, restores the saved text and returns focus to the text |
| `Tab` in the field | Commits and saves; focus moves to the next control |
| `Left` / `Right`, `Home` / `End`, `Shift` selections | Move the caret and extend the selection, as in a text box |
| `Ctrl+A`, `Ctrl+C`, `Ctrl+X`, `Ctrl+V` (`Cmd` on macOS) | Select all, copy, cut and paste in the field |

## Motion

- The old value scrolls out and the new one rises in with a soft blur. A failed save rolls back the other way and
  briefly tints the frame.
- The width follows the draft while typing, and the box changes height smoothly when it is multiline.
- While saving, a small spinner turns. When the save lands, a check mark is drawn.
- Reduced motion cross-fades the text, draws the check at once and replaces the spinner with a static mark. Off does
  the same without the fade.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| Value replaced from outside, or a save lands | The new text rises in from below with a soft blur; the old text moves up and fades | The text cross-fades | Immediate |
| Opening or closing the field | The frame's width and border spring into place; the text and actions switch with the frame | The text switches at once | Immediate |
| Typing changes the width | A quick spring without overshoot (about 0.16 s) | Immediate | Immediate |
| Saving | The spinner turns continuously and the text is at half opacity | A static mark replaces the spinner | Same as reduced |
| Save lands | The check mark draws over about 0.32 s after a short delay | The check is drawn at once | The check is drawn at once |
| Save fails | The old text drops back in from above; the frame washes with a danger tint that fades | The text cross-fades; the tint clears without a fade | Immediate |
| Hover and keyboard focus | The pencil fades in and the frame takes the hover tint | Immediate | Immediate |

## Related

- `Input` for a field that is always visible and saved with a form.
- `Textarea` for a longer body text inside a form.
- `ExpandingSearch` for a control that opens a search field and results.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `Input` | The field is always visible, has a label, and is saved with other fields |
| `Textarea` | The text is a long body that people write and review before saving |
| `NumberField` / `MoneyInput` | The value is a number or an amount that needs parsing and formatting |
| `Select` / `Combobox` | The value is one of a known list of options |
| `ExpandingSearch` | The person searches for a record or a page from a header |
| `InlineEdit` | A title or a name is renamed where it is shown, and saved on its own |
