# Number field

> Enter a bounded number with clear increment controls.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/number-field

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.NumberFieldDefaultDemo">
    <arc:NumberField x:Name="Seats"
                     Label="Seats"
                     Minimum="1"
                     Maximum="10"
                     Value="3"
                     Description="Up to 10 per team."
                     HorizontalAlignment="Center" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class NumberFieldDefaultDemo : UserControl
{
    public NumberFieldDefaultDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        // The unit follows the value: "1 seat", "3 seats".
        Seats.SuffixFormatter = n => n == 1 ? " seat" : " seats";
    }
}
```

## When to use

`NumberField` is a bounded numeric input with a stepper on each side. It fits a value that a person sets exactly and
often changes by one step: the number of seats on a plan, the items in a cart, the days of a retention window, a unit
price. The field enforces the range while the person types and when they press a stepper, so the form never stores a
value outside the limits it shows.

- **Seat and license counts in a SaaS admin console**: an admin raises the number of seats from 3 to 4 with the plus
  stepper, and the label "Up to 10 per team" stays visible while the limit is enforced.
- **Quantities in an order or cart**: a buyer changes the number of units for a line item between 1 and 99, and a limit
  note explains why the plus stepper stops at the maximum.
- **Retention and threshold settings in developer or ops tools**: an engineer sets a retry count, a timeout in seconds or
  a percentage threshold, with a unit suffix that follows the value.
- **Prices and unit costs with a fixed step**: a catalog editor steps a price by $0.50 or a cost by $0.01, and the step
  sets the number of decimals the field shows.
- **Dense settings panels where a value is adjusted in place**: a design tool's width or opacity field, where dragging
  the label changes the value when `IsScrubEnabled` is on.

## When not to use

- **Approximate values where position matters more than the exact number**: use `Slider`, which shows the whole range
  and lets the person judge a position.
- **Digit strings such as phone numbers, postal codes or verification codes**: use `Input`. A stepper makes no sense for
  an identifier, and the field would reformat it.
- **Currency amounts with a currency code**: use `MoneyInput`, which groups the amount, shows the currency and reports
  minor units.
- **Canvas-style property panels that scrub many values**: use `ScrubInput` when the whole panel is built around dragging.
- **A number chosen from a fixed list of options**: use `Select` or `Combobox`. A stepper implies the values are
  continuous.

## Usage

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:NumberField Label="Seats"
                     Minimum="1"
                     Maximum="10"
                     Value="3"
                     Description="Up to 10 per team." />
</UserControl>
```

`NumberField` derives from `FieldTextBox`, so it is an Avalonia `TextBox` with the Arc label, description and error rows
around it. The text box is the draft editor: when the field is not being edited, its text is transparent and the value is
painted as rolling digits. Typing opens a draft; the draft applies live while it is valid, in range and on the step
grid, and commits when the person presses Enter or leaves the field. `Value` is a `decimal`, so the arithmetic on
prices and fractions is exact.

### Anatomy

1. **Label** (PART_Label): the field's label, on a head row above the shell with 8 px between the row and the shell.
2. **Limit note** (PART_LimitNote): a 12 px note beside the label, such as "Max 10 seats", in a warning tint mixed from
   the foreground and the warning color. It appears when a press meets a limit.
3. **Decrease stepper** (PART_DecreaseButton): a square of 28, 34 or 40 px by size, with a 16 px minus glyph and a
   14 px corner radius.
4. **Value** (PART_ValueGroup, PART_Digits): the value with its prefix and suffix, between the steppers with a 2 px gap
   on each side.
5. **Increase stepper** (PART_IncreaseButton): the same square as the decrease stepper, with a 16 px plus glyph.
6. **Shell**: the field frame, with a 3 px inset on every side (4 px at the large size). Its width is 164, 196 or 228 px
   for the small, medium and large sizes, unless `Width` is set; the medium shell is 44 px tall.
7. **Description and error rows**: the field's help text and `ErrorMessage` under the shell.

A stepper dims to 32% at a limit, to 60% while it refuses a press, and to 35% when the field is disabled. A stepper at a
limit stays pressable, so the press still shows the limit.

### Prefix, suffix and step

`Step` sets the increment, and its precision sets the default number of fraction digits: a step of `0.5` shows one
decimal, and a step of `0.01` shows two. `Prefix` and `Suffix` are text before and after the value. `SuffixFormatter`
is a function of the value, so the unit can follow it, such as singular and plural.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.NumberFieldPriceDemo">
    <WrapPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center" ItemSpacing="12" LineSpacing="12">
        <arc:NumberField Label="Price" Prefix="$" Step="0.5" Maximum="999" Value="24.5" />
        <arc:NumberField Label="Unit cost" Prefix="$" Step="0.01" Maximum="100" Value="4.99" />
    </WrapPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```csharp
var seats = new NumberField
{
    Label = "Seats",
    Minimum = 1,
    Maximum = 10,
    Value = 3,
    SuffixFormatter = n => n == 1 ? " seat" : " seats"
};
```

`PrefixFormatter` works the same way for a prefix. Both are functions, so they are not available in XAML; set them in code
behind, as in the example above. A `Suffix` string is the static form.

A minimum below zero accepts the minus sign while the person types, so a range such as -20 to 40 needs no special
handling.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.NumberFieldNegativeRangeDemo">
    <arc:NumberField Label="Temperature"
                     Minimum="-20"
                     Maximum="40"
                     Value="21"
                     Suffix="°C"
                     Description="Type a minus sign for values below zero."
                     HorizontalAlignment="Center" />
</UserControl>
```

### Formatting and culture

`Culture` sets the grouping and decimal separators, and it defaults to `en-US` rather than the current culture, so the
same value reads the same way on every machine. `UseGrouping` turns the group separators on or off. `MinimumFractionDigits`
and `MaximumFractionDigits` override the digits that the step gives. Use them when a value has a fixed display, such as
two decimals for a rate that is stepped by whole numbers.

### Sizes

`Size` sets the width and the stepper size: `Small` is 164 px wide with 28 px steppers, `Medium` (the default) is 196 px
with 34 px steppers, and `Large` is 228 px with 40 px steppers. An explicit `Width` stretches the shell to that width
instead of the size's width.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.NumberFieldSizesDemo">
    <WrapPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center" ItemSpacing="12" LineSpacing="12">
        <arc:NumberField Label="Small" Size="Small" Value="2" Maximum="99" />
        <arc:NumberField Label="Medium" Value="12" Maximum="99" />
        <arc:NumberField Label="Large" Size="Large" Value="48" Maximum="99" />
    </WrapPanel>
</UserControl>
```

Use one size for each form. `Small` fits a dense table or a toolbar, `Medium` is the default for settings and forms, and
`Large` suits a single prominent number on a page such as a quantity on a product page.

### Limit hint and errors

`IsLimitHintEnabled` (on by default) shows a note beside the label when a press meets a limit or a typed value passes one.
The default text is "Max 10 seats" or "Min 1 seat". `LimitHintFormatter` writes the note from the edge that was reached
and its limit.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.NumberFieldLimitHintDemo">
    <arc:NumberField x:Name="Guests"
                     Label="Guests"
                     Minimum="1"
                     Maximum="8"
                     Value="8"
                     Description="Press + to meet the custom note."
                     HorizontalAlignment="Center" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class NumberFieldLimitHintDemo : UserControl
{
    public NumberFieldLimitHintDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Guests.LimitHintFormatter = (edge, limit) => edge == NumberFieldLimitEdge.Maximum
            ? $"Room holds {limit}"
            : $"At least {limit}";
    }
}
```

An `ErrorMessage` marks the field invalid. Use it for a rule the range does not express, such as a quantity that must be
at least one when the order has items.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.NumberFieldStatesDemo">
    <WrapPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center" ItemSpacing="12" LineSpacing="12">
        <arc:NumberField Label="Disabled" Value="4" Maximum="10" IsEnabled="False" Suffix=" seats" />
        <arc:NumberField Label="Quantity" Value="0" Maximum="5" ErrorMessage="Add at least one item." />
    </WrapPanel>
</UserControl>
```

### Validation

Keep range rules in the field and business rules in the view model or the form. The table shows when each check runs.

| Rule | When it is checked | Where it shows |
|---|---|---|
| Above `Maximum` | While typing, the draft turns warning-tinted; a press at the limit strains and names the limit | Limit note and the live announcement ("10 seats, maximum") |
| Below `Minimum` | While typing, after a short wait (700 ms), so a person can type the first digit of a larger number | Warning tint on the shell, then the limit note |
| On the step grid | When the draft commits (Enter or leaving the field) | The value is snapped to the step grid and clamped to the limits |
| Business rules, such as at least one item | On submit, from the view model | `ErrorMessage`; clear it when the value changes |

Setting `Value` from code never shows the strain or the note. It updates the display quietly, so a loaded form does not
flash a warning.

### Binding and events

`Value` is two-way. `ValueChanged` reports the old value, the new value and the `ChangeSource`, which says whether the
value came from code, a stepper, a key, the wheel, a scrub or typing.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.NumberFieldBindingAndEventsDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="16">
        <WrapPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center" ItemSpacing="12" LineSpacing="12">
            <arc:NumberField x:Name="Bound"
                             Label="Bound"
                             Maximum="50"
                             Value="7"
                             ValueChanged="OnValueChanged" />
            <arc:NumberField Label="Mirror"
                             Maximum="50"
                             Value="{Binding #Bound.Value, Mode=TwoWay}" />
        </WrapPanel>
        <TextBlock x:Name="Readout"
                   Text="Value 7"
                   HorizontalAlignment="Center"
                   FontSize="13"
                   FontFamily="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource MonoFontFamily}"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class NumberFieldBindingAndEventsDemo : UserControl
{
    public NumberFieldBindingAndEventsDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
    }

    private void OnValueChanged(object? sender, NumberFieldValueChangedEventArgs e)
        => Readout.Text = $"Value {e.NewValue} (was {e.OldValue}, {e.ChangeSource})";
}
```

```xml
<arc:NumberField Label="Items" Minimum="0" Maximum="50" Value="{Binding ItemCount, Mode=TwoWay}" />
```

```csharp
field.ValueChanged += (_, e) =>
{
    Console.WriteLine($"{e.OldValue} -> {e.NewValue} ({e.ChangeSource})");
};
```

`StepUp` and `StepDown` move the value by one step from code. They commit an open draft first and make no announcement and
no strain, so a "Add one" button in the app does not flash the limit.

### Binding to a view model

Keep the value and its limits in the view model, and let the field enforce the limits it shows. Changes from the field
arrive as `Value` updates, so the view model needs no extra handler.

```csharp
public partial class SeatPlanViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    public const int MaxSeats = 10;

    [ObservableProperty]
    [NotifyPropertyChangedFor(nameof(SeatCost))]
    private decimal _seats = 3;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private decimal _pricePerSeat = 12.5m;

    public decimal SeatCost => Seats * PricePerSeat;

    [RelayCommand]
    private async Task SavePlanAsync()
    {
        await _plans.SaveAsync("plan_team_2026", (int)Seats);
    }
}
```

```xml
<StackPanel Spacing="16">
    <arc:NumberField Label="Seats"
                     Value="{Binding Seats, Mode=TwoWay}"
                     Minimum="1"
                     Maximum="10"
                     Suffix=" seats"
                     Description="Up to 10 per team." />
    <arc:Button Content="Save plan" Command="{Binding SavePlanCommand}" />
</StackPanel>
```

- Keep `Minimum` and `Maximum` in XAML so the limits are visible in the markup, and bind only `Value`.
- Convert to an integer only at the boundary, because the field stores a `decimal` and a seat count is whole.

### Scrub label

With `IsScrubEnabled` on, drag the label sideways to change the value: one step for every 6 px of movement. Past a limit,
the value follows the pointer with resistance, and it settles at the limit when the pointer is released. Enable scrubbing
only where the label is a clear handle, such as a design panel. Elsewhere a stray drag on a label changes a value.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.NumberFieldScrubLabelDemo">
    <WrapPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center" ItemSpacing="12" LineSpacing="12">
        <arc:NumberField Label="Width" IsScrubEnabled="True" Suffix=" px" Maximum="640" Value="320" Step="4" />
        <arc:NumberField Label="Opacity" IsScrubEnabled="True" Suffix="%" Maximum="100" Value="80" Step="5" />
    </WrapPanel>
</UserControl>
```

### Keyboard

Focus the field to use the keyboard. The keys are listed below the field.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.NumberFieldKeyboardDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12">
        <arc:NumberField Label="Items" Maximum="1000" Value="120" LargeStep="50" HorizontalAlignment="Center" />
        <TextBlock Text="ArrowUp / ArrowDown step (hold to repeat), Shift or PageUp / PageDown take the large step, Home / End jump to the limits, Enter commits a draft or selects the number, Escape restores it. The wheel steps while the field is focused."
                   HorizontalAlignment="Center"
                   FontSize="13"
                   TextWrapping="Wrap"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

### Example: seat plan form in an admin console

An administrator sets the seats for a team plan in an admin console. The seats field shows the limit in its description
and in the limit note once the plus stepper reaches the maximum. The price per seat uses the same step rules with a
prefix and two decimals, so the price stays readable. The support hours field holds 0, which the business rule
rejects, so it carries an `ErrorMessage` that states the rule. The primary action names what happens next.

![A seat plan form with a seat count at its maximum, a price per seat and a quantity error](https://docs.tkcode.si/shots/Docs/SpecialInputs/NumberField/images/SeatPlanForm.webp)

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <StackPanel Width="620" Spacing="20">
        <TextBlock Text="Team plan: Acme Analytics"
                   FontSize="14"
                   FontWeight="SemiBold"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
        <arc:NumberField Label="Seats"
                         Value="10"
                         Minimum="1"
                         Maximum="10"
                         Suffix=" seats"
                         Width="360"
                         HorizontalAlignment="Left"
                         Description="Up to 10 per team. Changes apply from the next invoice." />
        <arc:NumberField Label="Price per seat"
                         Value="12.5"
                         Prefix="$"
                         Step="0.5"
                         MinimumFractionDigits="2"
                         Minimum="0"
                         Maximum="999"
                         Width="360"
                         HorizontalAlignment="Left"
                         Description="Billed monthly in USD." />
        <arc:NumberField Label="Support hours"
                         Value="0"
                         Minimum="0"
                         Maximum="40"
                         Suffix=" hours"
                         Width="360"
                         HorizontalAlignment="Left"
                         ErrorMessage="Add at least 1 support hour, or turn support off." />
        <StackPanel Orientation="Horizontal" Spacing="8" HorizontalAlignment="Right">
            <arc:Button Content="Discard" Variant="Secondary" />
            <arc:Button Content="Save plan" />

```

The three fields share one width, so the values line up in a column. The limit note stays hidden until a press reaches the
limit, which keeps the screen calm until it has something to say.

### Content guidelines

- **Label**: a noun for the quantity or setting: "Seats", "Retry attempts", "Timeout". The label stays visible; the
  stepper names include it, so keep it short.
- **Suffix**: name the unit in the singular and plural with `SuffixFormatter` when the unit changes with the number:
  " seat" and " seats". Use a leading space in the suffix so the digits and the unit do not touch.
- **Description**: state the limit or the consequence: "Up to 10 per team", "Changes apply from the next invoice".
  Write numbers as digits.
- **Limit hint**: name the limit the person reached in the terms of the field: "Max 10 seats", "Min 1 seat". Keep it to
  one short phrase.
- **Errors**: say what to enter, not what is wrong: "Add at least 1 support hour, or turn support off."

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| Invalid value | Enter a number from 1 to 10. |
| Quantity | Items in this order |
| Max reached! | Max 10 seats |
| Seats: | Seats |

### Best practices

**Do**

- Set `Minimum` and `Maximum` from the business rule, so the stepper stops where the rule stops and the limit note explains
  why.
- Set `Step` to the smallest change a person should make: `0.5` for a half-hour, `0.01` for cents. The step also sets the
  decimals, so the display never shows a value the step cannot produce.
- Use `StepUp` and `StepDown` for an "add one" button, because they do not flash the limit when the button is used at it.
- Keep the value in the view model as a `decimal`, and round only at the boundary with an integer or a payment API.
- Leave `IsScrubEnabled` off in forms, so a drag on a label never changes a value by accident.

**Avoid**

- Using the field for an identifier or a code, where the stepper and the formatting change the characters.
- Storing a number the field would refuse, such as a seat count above `Maximum`. The form then saves a value the screen
  never showed as valid.
- Showing an `ErrorMessage` while the person is still typing a valid number. Set it on submit, or after the field loses
  focus.
- Using a very small `Step` on a large range. A step of 0.01 across 0 to 999 needs many presses, so a text entry with
  `MoneyInput` or `Input` is faster.
- Hiding the limit note with `IsLimitHintEnabled="False"` when the limit is not obvious from the context. Without the note,
  a stopped stepper looks broken.

### Common questions

**Why does the plus stepper look dimmed?** The value is at the maximum. The stepper dims to 32% but stays pressable, so a
press still shows the limit note and the strain.

**How do I show a unit that changes with the number?** Set `SuffixFormatter` in code: `n => n == 1 ? " seat" : " seats"`.
It is a function, so it is not a XAML attribute.

**Why does a typed number snap to the step?** The draft is committed on Enter or when the field loses focus, and the commit
snaps the value to the step grid that starts at `Minimum`, then clamps it to the limits.

**How do I know the value changed because of a step and not typing?** Read `ChangeSource` in `ValueChanged`. `Key` is an
arrow or page key, `Button` is a stepper, `Wheel` is the mouse wheel while focused, `Scrub` is the label drag, `Type` is
typing and `Programmatic` is code.

**Can I use the mouse wheel?** Yes, while the field has keyboard focus, each wheel notch steps the value. This is an
extension of the Arc design, so an application that does not want it can avoid focusing the field.

## API reference

### NumberField

Arc number field: a bounded number with clear increment controls. The value rolls like an odometer, the steppers and ArrowUp / ArrowDown repeat and speed up while held, Shift, PageUp and PageDown take large steps, Home and End jump to the limits, and `IsScrubEnabled` lets the label be dragged sideways. Typing edits a plain draft that applies live while valid and commits on Enter, blur or the next step (snapped to the step grid and clamped). A press past a limit strains the value toward it, shakes the refused stepper and names the limit beside the label (`"Max 10 seats"`).

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Value` | `decimal` | `0` | The value (two-way). Arc's `value` / `onValueChange`. |
| `Minimum` | `decimal` | `0` | Lower limit and step-grid origin (default 0). |
| `Maximum` | `decimal` | `9007199254740991` | Upper limit (default 9007199254740991, Arc's `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`). |
| `Step` | `decimal` | `1` | One step (default 1; zero or less counts as 1). Its precision sets the default fraction digits. |
| `LargeStep` | `decimal?` | `null` | PageUp, PageDown and Shift with an arrow move this far (default ten steps). |
| `Culture` | `CultureInfo` | `en-US` | Formatting and parsing culture (Arc `locale`, default en-US, never the current culture). |
| `MinimumFractionDigits` | `int?` | `null` | Fewest fraction digits shown (default: the precision of `Step` and `Minimum`). |
| `MaximumFractionDigits` | `int?` | `null` | Most fraction digits shown (default: the precision of `Step` and `Minimum`). |
| `UseGrouping` | `bool` | `true` | Group separators in the display (default true). |
| `IsScrubEnabled` | `bool` | `false` | Drag the label sideways to scrub the value, one step every 6px (Arc `scrub`). |
| `IsLimitHintEnabled` | `bool` | `true` | Shows the limit note beside the label when a press meets a limit or a typed value passes one. |
| `LimitHintFormatter` | `Func<NumberFieldLimitEdge, decimal, string>?` | `null` | Writes the limit note (default `"Max 10 seats"` / `"Min 1 seat"`). |
| `PrefixFormatter` | `Func<decimal, string>?` | `null` | Computes the prefix from the value (Arc's function prefix); wins over `Prefix`. |
| `SuffixFormatter` | `Func<decimal, string>?` | `null` | Computes the suffix from the value: `n => n == 1 ? " seat" : " seats"`. |
| `IncreaseText` | `string` | `"Increase"` | Accessible name prefix of the plus stepper (default "Increase", read as "Increase Seats"). |
| `DecreaseText` | `string` | `"Decrease"` | Accessible name prefix of the minus stepper (default "Decrease"). |
| `Label` | `string?` | `null` | The visible label above the frame; also the accessible name. |
| `Description` | `string?` | `null` | Helper copy under the frame (rewrites changed words in place; counts roll). |
| `ErrorMessage` | `string?` | `null` | Error copy under the frame; non-empty makes the field invalid. |
| `IsInvalid` | `bool` | `false` | Invalid state; always true while an error is shown. |
| `IsLabelVisible` | `bool` | `true` | When false the label is hidden visually but still names the field. |
| `Size` | `ControlSize` | `Medium` | Frame height: Small 36, Medium 44 (default), Large 50. |
| `Prefix` | `object?` | `null` | Content before the text (icon, unit, currency). |
| `Suffix` | `object?` | `null` | Content after the text (unit, action button). |
| `Placeholder` | `string?` | `null` | Hint shown while the field is empty (same as `PlaceholderText`). |
| `EffectiveErrorMessage` | `string?` | – | *Read-only.* The error actually shown: `ErrorMessage`, else the binding's validation message. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ValueChanged` | `NumberFieldValueChangedEventArgs` | Raised after every real change of `Value` (never during template application). |

Pseudo-classes: `:editing`, `:warn`, `:strain`, `:strain-max`, `:strain-min`, `:at-max`, `:at-min`, `:decrease-pressed`, `:increase-pressed`, `:scrub`, `:scrub-hover`, `:scrubbing`, `:sized`, `:invalid`

Derives from `TextBox`: every member of `TextBox` works as well.

The change source and the limit edge are public enums that the events and the limit note use.

| Type | Members |
|---|---|
| `NumberFieldValueChangedEventArgs` | `OldValue`, `NewValue` (decimal), `ChangeSource` (`NumberFieldChangeSource`) |
| `NumberFieldChangeSource` | `Programmatic`, `Button`, `Key`, `Wheel`, `Scrub`, `Type` |
| `NumberFieldLimitEdge` | `Minimum`, `Maximum` |

## Accessibility

- `Label` names the field. With `IsLabelVisible="False"` the label is hidden but still names it.
- The field is a spin button with a range: its minimum, maximum, small change (1) and large change (10) are exposed, and
  its value text is the value with its prefix and suffix, such as "3 seats".
- The steppers are named "Decrease Seats" and "Increase Seats" from `DecreaseText`, `IncreaseText` and the label. They stay
  focusable at a limit, so a screen reader reaches the limit note.
- Changes are announced politely. A clamp announces the limit it reached ("10 seats, maximum"), and a typed value that
  is out of range is added to the help text.
- The focus ring appears for keyboard focus only. A press with the pointer does not draw it.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Up` / `Down` | Steps by `Step`; holding the key repeats the step, starting after 400 ms and speeding up |
| `Shift` + `Up` / `Down`, `PageUp` / `PageDown` | Steps by `LargeStep` (ten steps by default) |
| `Home` / `End` | Moves to `Minimum` / `Maximum` when no draft is open (`End` needs a finite maximum) |
| Digits, `-` (when `Minimum` is below zero), the decimal separator | Type a draft; a valid draft applies live |
| `Enter` | Commits an open draft (snapped and clamped); with no draft, selects the whole number |
| `Escape` | Reverts an open draft to the value before editing |
| `Enter` on a focused stepper | Takes one step |
| `Tab` | Moves from the editor to the Decrease and Increase steppers, then on |

The mouse wheel steps the value while the field has keyboard focus. Keys pressed on a stepper belong to the stepper, not to
the draft.

## Motion

- The digits roll like an odometer in the direction of the change, and wrap from 9 to 0. A step that is interrupted by
  another one changes its target in the middle of the roll.
- A press at a limit stretches the value back, shakes the refused stepper and shows the limit note for about 1.5 seconds.
- Reduced motion sets the value at once and flashes the limit in the warning color. Off motion does the same.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| Step with a stepper or an arrow key | Digits roll in the change direction | Value changes at once | Value changes at once |
| Press at a limit | The value stretches back, the stepper shakes, the limit note rises | The digits flash in the warning color | The digits flash in the warning color |
| Typed draft past a limit | The shell takes the warning tint | The shell takes the warning tint | The shell takes the warning tint |

## Related

- `Slider` when the position on a range matters more than the exact number.
- `Input` for digit strings that have no stepper.
- `MoneyInput` for currency amounts, and `ScrubInput` for dense property panels.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `Slider` | The person judges a position within a range and the exact figure matters less |
| `MoneyInput` | The number is an amount with a currency code and minor units |
| `ScrubInput` | Many numeric values in a dense panel are adjusted by dragging |
| `Input` | The value is an identifier or code, not a quantity |
| `Select` / `Combobox` | The value is one of a fixed list of options |

---

# Money input

> A currency field with live grouping, stable width, rolling digits, and minor-unit output.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/money-input

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.MoneyInputDefaultDemo">
    <arc:MoneyInput Label="Amount" Width="380" HorizontalAlignment="Left" />
</UserControl>
```

## When to use

`MoneyInput` is the field for a hand-typed amount of money. It groups digits as the person types, shows the missing
cents as faded digits, keeps the width steady as the amount grows, and reports both the major value (`12.5` for
$12.50) and the minor units (`1250`) that payment and ledger APIs expect. It sits where a person states an amount that
will be charged, refunded, budgeted or transferred, and where the currency may need to change.

- **Payment and checkout forms**: a customer enters a donation, a tip or a custom amount, with quick-add chips for the
  common values and a maximum that matches the card limit or the order total.
- **Refund and credit screens in a billing console**: an agent enters the refund amount up to the amount paid, and the
  range line under the field states the allowed span ("$5.00 to $120.00") before the agent types.
- **Invoices and expense reports with a changeable currency**: the amount stays as a number while the currency menu
  switches the code, so a 1,250.00 USD invoice can be re-entered as EUR without retyping the digits.
- **Budgets and transfers in a fintech app**: a person sets a monthly limit, with a minimum checked when the field loses
  focus so a value of 0.50 is reported after the person leaves the field, not while they type.
- **Storage and payment APIs that need minor units**: the field exposes `MinorUnits`, so the application sends 1250
  for $12.50 and never handles a binary floating-point amount.

## When not to use

- **Quantities and counts that carry no currency**: use `NumberField`, which has steps and a unit without currency
  formatting.
- **Choosing an amount from a range by dragging**: use `Slider`. It shows the whole span at once.
- **Dense property panels where a value is dragged in place**: use `ScrubInput`, which changes a number by dragging its
  label.
- **Free text that only looks like a number, such as an account code or an invoice number**: use `Input`. A money field
  groups digits and drops letters, which would corrupt an identifier.
- **A price picked from a list of products**: use `Select` or `Combobox`. The person chooses a record, not an amount.

## Usage

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:MoneyInput Label="Amount"
                    Currency="USD"
                    Minimum="5"
                    Maximum="1000"
                    Description="Arrow keys step by one unit." />
</UserControl>
```

`MoneyInput` derives from `FieldTextBox`, which is an Avalonia `TextBox` with the Arc label, description and error rows
around it. The text box holds the caret and the selection only: its own text is transparent, and the amount is painted
on the same origin by the field, column by column. That is why digits can roll and grow without moving the caret. The
text box also keeps the Avalonia input behavior for the caret, selection and clipboard, but undo is turned off, because
the amount is controlled and must not drift from `Value`.

### Anatomy

1. **Shell** (PART_Frame): a 76 px tall frame on the panel radius with 18 px of padding on the left and 8 px on the
   right. The border darkens while the amount itself has focus, and not while the currency switch has focus.
2. **Symbol and amount** (PART_Amount): the amount in the display face at 36 px, medium weight, with tabular digits and
   no kerning. Letter spacing is -0.03 em. Missing decimals show as faded digits in the muted color at 55% opacity.
3. **Prefix or suffix symbol** (PART_PrefixSymbol, PART_SuffixSymbol): the currency symbol before or after the digits,
   following the culture's positive pattern. Euros in `de-DE` take the symbol after the amount.
4. **Currency button** (PART_CurrencyButton): a 36 px button with the ISO code and a 16 px chevron. It opens the currency
   menu. With one currency in `Currencies`, the code becomes static text instead (PART_StaticCode).
5. **Range line** (PART_Range): 12 px muted text under the shell, such as "$5.00 to $1,000.00". It flashes in the
   warning color when a change is refused.
6. **Quick-add chips** (PART_Chips): 30 px high chips labelled "+$10", "+$50" and "+$100" by default, 6 px apart, on the
   same row as the range line.
7. **Currency menu**: 256 px wide, with rows of at least 36 px and a list up to 288 px high, placed 8 px from the shell.
8. **Description and error rows**: the field's label, description and `ErrorMessage` rows from `Field`.

### Currency and quick-add chips

`Currencies` sets the codes in the currency menu. The default is eight codes: USD, EUR, GBP, JPY, CAD, AUD, CHF and
INR. Use a shorter list that matches the markets the screen serves, because a long menu slows the choice. With one code,
the field shows the code as static text and no menu opens.

`QuickAddAmounts` sets the chips in major units. The default is 10, 50 and 100. Each chip adds its amount to the current
value. An empty list hides the chips. Set chips that suit the amount: tips and donations use small values, a refund uses
the values of the orders in the account. At the maximum, the chips look disabled.

Japanese yen has no minor unit, so the field shows no cents and the minor-unit value equals the major value.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             xmlns:generic="clr-namespace:System.Collections.Generic;assembly=System.Collections"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.MoneyInputSingleCurrencyDemo">
    <arc:MoneyInput Label="Budget"
                    Currency="EUR"
                    Value="2400"
                    Width="380"
                    HorizontalAlignment="Left">
        <arc:MoneyInput.Currencies>
            <generic:List x:TypeArguments="x:String">
                <x:String>EUR</x:String>
            </generic:List>
        </arc:MoneyInput.Currencies>
    </arc:MoneyInput>
</UserControl>
```

```xml

             xmlns:generic="clr-namespace:System.Collections.Generic;assembly=System.Collections"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.MoneyInputNoQuickAddDemo">
```

### Culture

`Culture` sets the grouping separator, the decimal separator and the symbol placement. The default is `en-US`, and the
field does not follow the current thread culture, so a user in another locale sees the same format on every screen.
Set `Culture` to the locale of the amount's audience, such as `de-DE` for a German invoice.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.MoneyInputCultureDemo">
    <arc:MoneyInput Label="Betrag"
                    Culture="de-DE"
                    Currency="EUR"
                    Value="1234.56"
                    Maximum="10000"
                    Width="380"
                    HorizontalAlignment="Left" />
</UserControl>
```

the message. A built-in range error appears instead when no explicit message is set and the value is out of range.

```xml
                        Description="Charged when the order ships."
```

### Binding and events

`Value` is two-way and uses major units, so `12.50` is `12.5`. `Currency` is also two-way. `ValueChanged` reports the
old and new value, the currency, the minor units, the formatted string and the `ChangeSource`. `CurrencyChanged` reports
the old and new code and whether the menu or code changed it.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.MoneyInputBindingAndEventsDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="14">
        <arc:MoneyInput x:Name="Amount"
                        Label="Amount"
                        Maximum="5000"
                        Width="380"
                        HorizontalAlignment="Left"
                        ValueChanged="OnValueChanged" />
        <TextBlock x:Name="Readout"
                   FontSize="13"
                   FontFamily="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource MonoFontFamily}"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
        <TextBlock x:Name="EventLine"
                   Text="ValueChanged: (none yet)"
                   FontSize="13"
                   FontFamily="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource MonoFontFamily}"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
        <StackPanel Orientation="Horizontal" Spacing="8">
            <arc:Button Content="Set Value = 99.99" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Click="OnSetClick" />
            <arc:Button Content="Clear" Variant="Ghost" Size="Small" Click="OnClearClick" />
        </StackPanel>
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using System.Globalization;
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class MoneyInputBindingAndEventsDemo : UserControl
{
    public MoneyInputBindingAndEventsDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        ShowAmount();
        // Value and Currency are two-way; read the amount back whenever either changes.
        Amount.PropertyChanged += (_, e) =>
        {
            if (e.Property == MoneyInput.ValueProperty || e.Property == MoneyInput.CurrencyProperty)
            {
                ShowAmount();
            }
        };
    }

    private void OnValueChanged(object? sender, MoneyInputValueChangedEventArgs e)
        => EventLine.Text = $"ValueChanged ({e.ChangeSource}): {Show(e.OldValue)} → {Show(e.NewValue)}, {e.Currency}, "
                            + $"minor {e.MinorUnits?.ToString(CultureInfo.InvariantCulture) ?? "null"}, \"{e.Formatted}\"";

    private void OnSetClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) => Amount.Value = 99.99m;

    private void OnClearClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) => Amount.Value = null;

    private void ShowAmount()
        => Readout.Text = $"Value = {Show(Amount.Value)}   "
                          + $"MinorUnits = {Amount.MinorUnits?.ToString(CultureInfo.InvariantCulture) ?? "null"}   "
                          + $"Formatted = \"{Amount.FormattedValue}\"   Currency = {Amount.Currency}";

    private static string Show(decimal? value) => value?.ToString(CultureInfo.InvariantCulture) ?? "null";
}
```

```xml
<arc:MoneyInput Label="Amount" Value="{Binding Amount}" Currency="{Binding Currency}" />
```

```csharp
amount.ValueChanged += (_, e) =>
{
    Console.WriteLine($"{e.Formatted} ({e.Currency}), minor units {e.MinorUnits}, from {e.ChangeSource}");
};

amount.OpenCurrencyMenu();
```

`OpenCurrencyMenu` needs at least two codes in `Currencies`; `CloseCurrencyMenu` closes the menu and returns focus to the
button. `IsCurrencyMenuOpen` reports the state.

### Binding to a view model

The view model stores the amount in major units as a `decimal?`, and the currency as its ISO code. Store the minor units
only at the boundary with the payment service.

```csharp
public partial class RefundViewModel : ObservableValidator
{
    [ObservableProperty]
    [NotifyDataErrorInfo]
    [Required(ErrorMessage = "Enter a refund amount.")]
    [Range(typeof(decimal), "0.01", "120", ErrorMessage = "Enter an amount between $0.01 and $120.00.")]
    private decimal? _amount = 84.50m;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private string _currency = "USD";

    [RelayCommand]
    private async Task RefundAsync()
    {
        ValidateAllProperties();
        if (HasErrors || Amount is not { } major)
        {
            return;
        }
        long minorUnits = decimal.ToInt64(major * 100m);
        await _payments.RefundAsync("ch_2026_0412", minorUnits, Currency);
    }
}
```

```xml
<arc:MoneyInput Label="Refund amount"
                Value="{Binding Amount, Mode=TwoWay}"
                Currency="{Binding Currency, Mode=TwoWay}"
                Minimum="0.01"
                Maximum="120" />
```

- `Value` and `Currency` are two-way by default, so the view model receives every change, including changes made from the
  menu.
- Use `ValueChanged` for side effects that depend on the change source. Programmatic sets from the view model raise
  `ValueChanged` with `ChangeSource` set to `Programmatic`, and they make no announcement and no kick.

### Minimum and maximum

`Minimum` and `Maximum` set the range in major units. Typing past the maximum is refused: the amount kicks back toward the
press, the range line flashes and the limit is announced. The minimum is checked when the field loses focus, so a person
can type a short value on the way to a larger one.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.MoneyInputLimitsDemo">
    <arc:MoneyInput Label="Transfer"
                    Minimum="5"
                    Maximum="1000"
                    Description="Arrow keys step by $1, Shift by $10, PageUp and PageDown by ten steps."
                    Width="380"
                    HorizontalAlignment="Left" />
</UserControl>
```

### Validation

Check each rule at the time the person can act on it. The field handles the range; the rest of the form decides what
an amount means.

| Rule | When it is checked | Where it shows |
|---|---|---|
| Above `Maximum` | While typing, refused as the person types | The range line flashes and the limit is announced; the value does not change |
| Below `Minimum` | When the field loses focus | `ErrorMessage` with "The minimum is $5.00" (the `MinimumErrorFormat` text); the frame turns invalid |
| Required or business rules | On submit, from the view model | `ErrorMessage`; the explicit message replaces the built-in range error |
| Server rules, such as the card limit | After the request | `ErrorMessage` on the field; clear it when the amount changes |

Set `ErrorMessage` to `null` to remove an explicit message and let the built-in range error show again. The built-in
texts come from `MinimumErrorFormat` and `MaximumErrorFormat`, and the range texts from `RangeFormat` ("{0} to {1}"),
`MaximumOnlyFormat` ("Up to {0}") and `MinimumOnlyFormat` ("At least {0}"). Change them for a product's wording, and keep
the `{0}` placeholders.

### Hidden label

`IsLabelVisible="False"` hides the label but keeps it for screen readers. Use it only when a heading above the field
already names the amount.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             xmlns:generic="clr-namespace:System.Collections.Generic;assembly=System.Collections"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.MoneyInputHiddenLabelDemo">
    <arc:MoneyInput Label="Donation"
                    IsLabelVisible="False"
                    Width="380"
                    HorizontalAlignment="Left">
        <arc:MoneyInput.QuickAddAmounts>
            <generic:List x:TypeArguments="x:Decimal">
                <x:Decimal>5</x:Decimal>
                <x:Decimal>20</x:Decimal>
                <x:Decimal>50</x:Decimal>
            </generic:List>
        </arc:MoneyInput.QuickAddAmounts>
    </arc:MoneyInput>
</UserControl>
```

### Disabled

A disabled field keeps its amount and ignores input. Explain why the amount is locked in a description, for example
"Locked after the invoice is sent".

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.MoneyInputDisabledDemo">
    <arc:MoneyInput Label="Locked amount" Value="250" IsEnabled="False" Width="380" HorizontalAlignment="Left" />
</UserControl>
```

### Example: refund form in a billing console

An agent refunds part of a payment in a billing console. The refund field shows the range under the shell ("$5.00 to
$120.00"), so the agent sees the limit before typing. Two quick-add chips (+$10 and +$25) let the agent add common
amounts. The settlement field is empty and carries an explicit error that says what is missing and where to find it,
because the bank has not confirmed the amount yet. The description states a consequence ("Returned to the card in 3 to 5
days"), which is the reason a person needs to read the field.

![A refund form with a valid amount, a range line, quick-add chips and an error on an empty settlement amount](https://docs.tkcode.si/shots/Docs/SpecialInputs/MoneyInput/images/RefundForm.webp)

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             xmlns:generic="using:System.Collections.Generic">
    <StackPanel Width="620" Spacing="20">
        <TextBlock Text="Refund for payment ch_2026_0412"
                   FontSize="14"
                   FontWeight="SemiBold"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
        <arc:MoneyInput Label="Refund amount"
                        Value="84.5"
                        Currency="USD"
                        Minimum="5"
                        Maximum="120"
                        Description="Returned to the card in 3 to 5 business days.">
            <arc:MoneyInput.QuickAddAmounts>
                <generic:List x:TypeArguments="x:Decimal">
                    <x:Decimal>10</x:Decimal>
                    <x:Decimal>25</x:Decimal>
                </generic:List>
            </arc:MoneyInput.QuickAddAmounts>
        </arc:MoneyInput>
        <arc:MoneyInput Label="Settlement amount"
                        Currency="EUR"
                        Culture="de-DE"
                        ErrorMessage="Enter the amount the bank confirmed on the settlement report." />
        <StackPanel Orientation="Horizontal" Spacing="8" HorizontalAlignment="Right">
            <arc:Button Content="Cancel" Variant="Secondary" />
            <arc:Button Content="Issue refund" />
        </StackPanel>
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

The two fields share one column and one label style, so the eye reads them as one form. The error on the second field
uses the explicit message, which replaces the built-in range error, because the field is empty and no range error applies.

### Content guidelines

- **Label**: name the amount's role in a noun phrase: "Refund amount", "Tip", "Monthly limit". Avoid "Amount" alone on a
  screen that has more than one amount.
- **Description**: state the consequence or the limit: "Returned to the card in 3 to 5 business days", "Up to the amount
  paid". Write numbers as digits.
- **Errors**: say what is wrong and what to enter, in the terms of the description: "Enter an amount between $0.01 and
  $120.00." Avoid "Invalid amount".
- **Actions**: a button names the outcome with a verb and object, "Issue refund", "Save limit". Do not write "Submit".

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| Invalid amount | Enter an amount between $0.01 and $120.00. |
| Amount | Refund amount |
| The value is too high! | The maximum is $120.00. |
| Submit | Issue refund |

### Best practices

**Do**

- Set `Minimum` and `Maximum` from the business rule, so the field refuses impossible typing and the range line tells the
  person the span before they type.
- Store and send `MinorUnits` to payment APIs, and keep `Value` in the view model in major units for display.
- Pass `Culture` for the audience of the screen, not the operating system's culture, so the same amount reads the same
  way on every machine.
- Keep the chips to two or three values that match the screen's work, because more chips crowd the row.
- Show the currency menu only when the amount may change currency. A single code is shown as static text for a reason.

**Avoid**

- Converting `Value` to `double` or `float`. The decimal type keeps the cents exact, and a binary float does not.
- Using `MoneyInput` for a quantity, a count or a percentage. The currency symbol and the cents then mislead the person.
- Showing an error on the first keystroke for a minimum. The minimum is checked on blur, so the person can finish typing
  first.
- Keeping a stale `ErrorMessage` after the amount is fixed. Clear it (set it to `null`) so the built-in range error or the
  description returns.
- Relying on the current culture for a financial screen. A machine set to another locale changes the grouping and the
  symbol.

### Common questions

**Why does the empty field show 0.00?** Those are ghost digits that mark where the cents go. `Value` is `null` and
`FormattedValue` is an empty string, so check `Value` for `null`, not the displayed digits.

**How do I get the amount for a payment API?** Read `MinorUnits` (a `long?`). For USD it is cents, for JPY yen. The
value is `null` when the field is empty, so validate it before the request.

**Why are the currency names in English?** The field uses a built-in table of ISO 4217 codes with English names, because
.NET does not provide localized display names for every currency. The symbol and the number format still follow
`Culture`.

**Why does the amount move when I enter a value over the maximum?** The refusal is a kick: the amount slides toward the
press and springs back, so the person sees that the change was refused. With reduced motion the kick is removed and the
range line still flashes.

**What happens to the amount when the currency changes?** The major amount is kept (12.5 stays 12.5), and the minor units
are recalculated in the new currency. From the menu, `CurrencyChanged` fires with `Menu`, then `ValueChanged` fires with
`ChangeSource` set to `Currency`.

## API reference

### MoneyInput

Arc money input: a currency amount field. Digits group as they are typed without moving the caret, the missing cents wait as faint ghosts so the amount never changes width when it settles, long amounts scale down to fit instead of scrolling, and quick add chips and arrow keys roll the digits. A currency menu switches the currency and keeps the major amount. `Value` is the amount in major units (12.5 for $12.50); `MinorUnits` gives the integer minor units Arc reports.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Value` | `decimal?` | `null` | The amount in major units (12.5 for $12.50); null is empty. Two-way by default. |
| `Currency` | `string` | `"USD"` | ISO 4217 code of the amount ("USD" by default). Two-way by default. |
| `Currencies` | `IList<string>` | `System.Collections.ObjectModel.ReadOnlyCollection`1[System.String]` | Codes offered by the currency menu; a single code shows it as static text instead of the menu. |
| `Minimum` | `decimal?` | `null` | Lowest amount in major units, checked when the field loses focus. |
| `Maximum` | `decimal?` | `null` | Highest amount in major units; typing past it is refused with a kick. |
| `QuickAddAmounts` | `IList<decimal>` | `System.Collections.ObjectModel.ReadOnlyCollection`1[System.Decimal]` | Quick add chips in major units (10, 50, 100 by default); an empty list hides them. |
| `Step` | `decimal?` | `null` | What the arrow keys add, in major units; null is one major unit. Shift moves ten times as far. |
| `Culture` | `CultureInfo?` | `en-US` | Formatting culture (Arc `locale`): en-US by default, never the current culture. |
| `RangeFormat` | `string` | `"{0} to {1}"` | Range text when both limits are set; {0} is the minimum, {1} the maximum. |
| `MaximumOnlyFormat` | `string` | `"Up to {0}"` | Range text when only the maximum is set. |
| `MinimumOnlyFormat` | `string` | `"At least {0}"` | Range text when only the minimum is set. |
| `MinimumErrorFormat` | `string` | `"The minimum is {0}"` | Built-in error below the minimum (after the field loses focus). |
| `MaximumErrorFormat` | `string` | `"The maximum is {0}"` | Built-in error above the maximum (after the field loses focus). |
| `MinorUnits` | `long?` | – | *Read-only.* The amount in minor units (cents for USD, yen for JPY), or null when empty. |
| `RangeText` | `string` | – | *Read-only.* The allowed range as shown under the shell ("$5.00 to $1,000.00"); empty without limits. |
| `IsCurrencyMenuOpen` | `bool` | – | *Read-only.* True while the currency menu is open. |
| `Label` | `string?` | `null` | The visible label above the frame; also the accessible name. |
| `Description` | `string?` | `null` | Helper copy under the frame (rewrites changed words in place; counts roll). |
| `ErrorMessage` | `string?` | `null` | Error copy under the frame; non-empty makes the field invalid. |
| `IsInvalid` | `bool` | `false` | Invalid state; always true while an error is shown. |
| `IsLabelVisible` | `bool` | `true` | When false the label is hidden visually but still names the field. |
| `Size` | `ControlSize` | `Medium` | Frame height: Small 36, Medium 44 (default), Large 50. |
| `Prefix` | `object?` | `null` | Content before the text (icon, unit, currency). |
| `Suffix` | `object?` | `null` | Content after the text (unit, action button). |
| `Placeholder` | `string?` | `null` | Hint shown while the field is empty (same as `PlaceholderText`). |
| `EffectiveErrorMessage` | `string?` | – | *Read-only.* The error actually shown: `ErrorMessage`, else the binding's validation message. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ValueChanged` | `MoneyInputValueChangedEventArgs` | Raised for every real change of `Value`: typing, paste, keys, chips, a currency choice, automation and programmatic sets (`ChangeSource` tells them apart). Never raised during template application. |
| `CurrencyChanged` | `MoneyInputCurrencyChangedEventArgs` | Raised when the currency changes: a choice in the menu (Arc `onCurrencyChange`) or a programmatic set (`ChangeSource`). |

Pseudo-classes: `:invalid`

Derives from `TextBox`: every member of `TextBox` works as well.

The event arguments and the change sources are public types that the events use.

| Type | Members |
|---|---|
| `MoneyInputValueChangedEventArgs` | `OldValue`, `NewValue` (decimal?), `Currency`, `MinorUnits` (long?), `Formatted`, `ChangeSource` |
| `MoneyInputCurrencyChangedEventArgs` | `OldCurrency`, `NewCurrency`, `ChangeSource` |
| `MoneyInputChangeSource` | `Programmatic`, `Type`, `Paste`, `Key`, `Chip`, `Currency`, `Automation` |
| `MoneyInputCurrencyChangeSource` | `Programmatic`, `Menu` |

## Accessibility

- `Label` names the field. With `IsLabelVisible="False"` the label is hidden but still names it.
- The field is a spin button. Its numeric value is the major value, and its value text is the full currency string, such
  as "$12.50", or "Empty" when there is no amount. The range appears as the minimum and maximum of the spin button.
- The description, the range and the error are the field's help text, read after the name and the value.
- The currency button is named "Currency, US Dollar" and opens a list with typeahead.
- Refused changes ("Maximum is $100.00"), key and chip steps, and currency changes are announced politely. Typing does
  not announce, so a screen reader does not repeat each digit.
- Animated digits are hidden from assistive technology, which reads the real text of the field.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| Digits and the decimal separator | Type the amount; letters are dropped and the caret stays |
| `Up` / `Down` | Adds or subtracts one major unit, or the `Step` value |
| `Shift` + `Up` / `Down`, `PageUp` / `PageDown` | Steps ten times as far |
| `Enter` | Settles the decimals (12.5 becomes 12.50) and moves the caret to the end |
| `Backspace` / `Delete` on a group separator | Deletes the digit next to the separator instead of doing nothing |
| `Ctrl+V` (`Cmd+V` on macOS) | Pastes a value such as "$1,234.56", "1.234,56 €" or "1234.5"; replaces a whole-field selection, otherwise inserts at the caret |
| `Tab` | Moves focus to the next control |
| `Down` / `Up` on the currency button | Opens the currency menu |
| `Up` / `Down`, `Home` / `End` in the menu | Moves the highlight through the currencies |
| Letters in the menu | Jump to the currency whose code or name starts with the typed text (typeahead resets after 600 ms) |
| `Enter` / `Space` in the menu | Chooses the highlighted currency and keeps the major amount |
| `Escape` in the menu | Closes the menu and returns focus to the currency button |
| `Tab` in the menu | Closes the menu and moves focus on |

Enter settles the decimals but does not submit. The key still reaches the form, so a default button can submit it.

## Motion

- Digits roll in the direction of the change when a step or a chip changes the amount. In full motion, typed digits land
  at once, so the caret never lags behind the keystroke.
- A refused change pushes the amount sideways with a spring and flashes the range line.
- Changing the currency rolls the symbol to its new position, and a long amount scales down to fit the width.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| Step key or quick-add chip | Digit columns roll in the change direction | Digits fade, sizes jump | Digits fade, sizes jump |
| Refused change (over the maximum) | The amount kicks sideways with a spring; the range line flashes | No kick; the range line still flashes | No kick; the range line still flashes |
| New digit column appears | The column grows in width on a spring | Width jumps | Width jumps |
| Currency change | The symbol rolls to its new place | The symbol changes without the roll | The symbol changes without the roll |

## Related

- `NumberField` for quantities and other numbers that have no currency.
- `ScrubInput` for dragged numeric settings, and `Slider` for picking from a range.
- `Input` for free text that has no amount structure.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `NumberField` | The number is a quantity, a count or a value with a unit, not money |
| `ScrubInput` | A numeric setting is adjusted by dragging it in a dense panel |
| `Slider` | The person picks a value across a range and the exact figure matters less |
| `Input` | The value is an identifier or free text that happens to contain digits |
| `Select` / `Combobox` | The person chooses a priced item or record from a list |
