# Phone input

> A phone field with a country picker, formatting as you type, and E.164 output.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/phone-input

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.PhoneInputDefaultDemo">
    <arc:PhoneInput Label="Phone number" Width="360" HorizontalAlignment="Left" />
</UserControl>
```

## When to use

`PhoneInput` collects a telephone number together with the country it belongs to. It sits in a form beside the other
fields of the flow, and it handles the parts a plain text field gets wrong: the country code, the national format, the
trunk prefix people type at home and the E.164 value that the server stores. The person picks a country once, types
the national number, and the component keeps the stored value in one canonical form.

- **Sign-up and account creation in a SaaS product**: a mobile number that receives a sign-in code. The number must be
  complete before the request leaves the page, so the field validates on blur and shows the expected digit count.
- **Checkout and delivery details in e-commerce**: a courier needs a reachable number for the parcel. Use `Country`
  with the shipping country preselected, and `PreferredCountries` for the markets the store ships to.
- **Contact forms in CRM and support tools**: a customer record holds one `+` number per contact. Bind `Value` to the
  record and store the E.164 string unchanged, so every later dialer and SMS integration reads the same value.
- **Account settings and billing profiles in fintech**: a number that the bank or payment provider sends alerts to.
  `Countries` can limit the picker to the markets where the product is licensed.
- **Bulk import screens in internal tools**: `PhoneNumbers.Parse` reads numbers written as "+44 (0)7911 123456" or
  "0044 7911..." before they are shown in the field, so a support agent can correct one row without retyping it.

## When not to use

- **Free text that is never dialed**: use `Input`. A number stored as a label, a reference or an order note does not
  need a country picker.
- **Verification codes**: use a one-time code input in your own UI. A code is not a phone number, and this library does
  not ship an OTP input.
- **Carrier, line type or reachability checks**: use a number metadata or messaging service. `PhoneInput` checks the
  length and the shape of a number against its built-in table of 49 countries, not whether the line is live.
- **A fixed list of values with no number semantics**: use `Select` or `Combobox` when the person chooses from known
  options, such as a support queue or a plan type.
- **A number that is only displayed**: use `Text` or a `Field` with `IsReadOnly` content for a value on a detail page.
  Call `PhoneNumbers.Format` to show the E.164 string in a list or table without an editor.
- **Amounts of money or counts**: use `MoneyInput` or `NumberField`. A phone number is an identifier, so it is text
  with a format, not a quantity.

## Usage

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:PhoneInput Label="Phone number"
                    Country="US"
                    Description="We text a sign-in code to this number." />
</UserControl>
```

`PhoneInput` derives from `FieldTextBox`, which derives from Avalonia's `TextBox`, so the number is an ordinary text
editor: caret, selection, IME, undo and the clipboard work as they do in a text box. The component adds the country
button, the formatting, the E.164 `Value`, the country list and the message rows. `Label`, `Description` and
`ErrorMessage` are the same properties `Input` uses.

### Anatomy

1. **Label** (`Label`): the field's name, shown above the frame. It is also the accessible name of the number. Hide it
   with `IsLabelVisible="False"` only when a visible heading already names the field.
2. **Field frame**: the Arc frame of the field. In the default theme it is the medium control height (44 px), with
   the control radius and the surface color. Hover darkens the border, focus turns it to the foreground color, and an
   invalid field turns it to the danger color. Nothing changes size.
3. **Country button**: a 36 px high button inset 3 px in the frame. It shows the flag and the
   calling code (such as "+1") with 9 px before the flag, and reserves 33 px on the right for the chevron. The chevron
   sits 12 px from the right edge of the anchor, and a divider inset 10 px top and bottom separates the trigger from the
   number.
4. **Number** (the text editor, `PhoneInput` itself): the digits as they are typed, formatted for the selected country.
   The number has 12 px of padding on the left and 36 px on the right, which keeps room for the valid check.
5. **Typing guide**: the rest of the expected number, drawn in the muted text color at 72 percent
   opacity after the typed digits. It is a hint only; it is not part of the value.
6. **Valid check**: an 18 px slot 12 px from the right edge, shown when the number has a valid
   length for the country.
7. **Description row** (`Description`): helper copy under the frame. It shows only while there is no message.
8. **Error row** (`ErrorMessage` or the built-in validation message): copy in the danger color under the frame. A
   value in `ErrorMessage` replaces the built-in message.

### Preset value

`Value` takes an E.164 string such as `+447400123456`. The country is read from the calling code, and the field shows
the national number in that country's format. A value set in code does not announce itself.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.PhoneInputPresetValueDemo">
    <arc:PhoneInput Label="Mobile" Value="+447400123456" Width="360" HorizontalAlignment="Left" />
</UserControl>
```

### Restricted countries

`Countries` limits the picker to the listed ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes. Use it when the product or the store operates in
a fixed set of markets: a Nordic bank that onboards Norway, Sweden and Denmark, or a shipping form that accepts the
countries on its delivery map. `PreferredCountries` lists the countries that appear in the Suggested group above the
full list. A preferred country that is not in `Countries` is dropped, so a restricted list never offers a country the
product does not serve. An empty `PreferredCountries` shows one list sorted by name.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             xmlns:generic="clr-namespace:System.Collections.Generic;assembly=System.Collections"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.PhoneInputRestrictedCountriesDemo">
    <arc:PhoneInput Label="Phone number"
                    Country="GB"
                    Width="360"
                    HorizontalAlignment="Left">
        <arc:PhoneInput.Countries>
            <generic:List x:TypeArguments="x:String">
                <x:String>GB</x:String>
                <x:String>IE</x:String>
                <x:String>FR</x:String>
                <x:String>DE</x:String>
                <x:String>ES</x:String>
                <x:String>IT</x:String>
                <x:String>NL</x:String>
                <x:String>PT</x:String>
            </generic:List>
        </arc:PhoneInput.Countries>
        <arc:PhoneInput.PreferredCountries>
            <generic:List x:TypeArguments="x:String">
                <x:String>GB</x:String>
                <x:String>IE</x:String>
            </generic:List>
        </arc:PhoneInput.PreferredCountries>
    </arc:PhoneInput>
</UserControl>
```

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             xmlns:generic="clr-namespace:System.Collections.Generic;assembly=System.Collections"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.PhoneInputNoPreferredCountriesDemo">
    <arc:PhoneInput Label="Phone number" Width="360" HorizontalAlignment="Left">
        <arc:PhoneInput.PreferredCountries>
            <generic:List x:TypeArguments="x:String" />
        </arc:PhoneInput.PreferredCountries>
    </arc:PhoneInput>
</UserControl>
```

Assign a new list to change either property. An existing list that is changed in place does not refresh the picker,
so replace the list instead.

### Validation and errors

Validation runs after the number loses focus, and only when the person entered digits. A field that was never typed in
stays quiet, which lets an optional number stay empty. An incomplete or too long number then shows the built-in message
in the error row, and the frame turns to the danger color. A complete number shows the valid check.

| Situation | When it is checked | Message |
|---|---|---|
| Digits entered, count shorter than the country's valid lengths | When the number loses focus | Built-in: "Numbers in United States have 10 digits" |
| Digits entered, count longer than the longest valid length | When the number loses focus | The same built-in message, with the country's lengths |
| Complete number of a valid length | Never shown as an error; the valid check appears | None |
| `ErrorMessage` has text | Immediately | The `ErrorMessage` text replaces the built-in message |
| `IsValidationEnabled` is `False` | Never | None; only `ErrorMessage` shows |

`IsValidationEnabled="False"` turns the built-in check off, so only `ErrorMessage` shows. Use it when the server
validates the number after submit, or on a profile page where a partial number is allowed. `ValidationTextFormat` changes the built-in copy; its `{0}` is the country name and its `{1}` the valid
lengths, such as "10" or "10 or 11" for countries with two lengths.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.PhoneInputValidationOffDemo">
    <arc:PhoneInput Label="Phone number"
                    IsValidationEnabled="False"
                    Description="Validation is off: incomplete numbers show no message after blur."
                    Width="360"
                    HorizontalAlignment="Left" />
</UserControl>
```

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.PhoneInputDescriptionAndErrorDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="16">
        <arc:PhoneInput Label="Phone number"
                        Description="We text a sign-in code to this number."
                        Width="360"
                        HorizontalAlignment="Left" />
        <arc:PhoneInput Label="Phone number"
                        Value="+1201555"
                        ErrorMessage="Enter the full number to get a code."
                        Width="360"
                        HorizontalAlignment="Left" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

`ValidationMessage` reports the built-in message currently shown, or `null`. Read it when the form needs the message as
text, for example in a summary at the top of a long form. `Status` gives the same answer as a value: `Empty`,
`Incomplete`, `Valid` or `TooLong`.

### Storing and checking numbers

Store the `Value` string. It is E.164: a plus sign, the calling code and the national digits without the trunk prefix,
such as `+14155550132`. The `PhoneNumbers` helpers work on the same data as the picker, so a form, an importer and a
list can share one set of rules without a second table:

| Helper | Use it for |
|---|---|
| `PhoneNumbers.Format(e164)` | Showing a stored number in a table or a summary, such as "+44 7400 123456"; returns the input when it cannot be read |
| `PhoneNumbers.Parse(input)` | Reading a pasted or imported number into a country and national digits; returns `null` when the text does not start with "+" or "00" or the code is unknown |
| `PhoneNumbers.StatusOf(country, digits)` | Checking a national number on the server with the same lengths the field uses |
| `PhoneNumbers.ToE164(country, digits)` | Building the stored value from a country and the national digits |
| `PhoneNumbers.Find(iso)` | Getting the table entry for an ISO code, or `null` for an unknown code |

To check a stored record in code, pass `Value` to `PhoneNumbers.Parse`. It returns the `Country` and the `National`
digits for `StatusOf`:

```csharp
var parsed = PhoneNumbers.Parse(contact.Phone);
if (parsed is { } number)
{
    var status = PhoneNumbers.StatusOf(number.Country, number.National);
    // status is Valid, Incomplete or TooLong; store contact.Phone unchanged when it is Valid.
}
```

### Binding and events

`Value` and `Country` are two-way. `ValueChanged` is raised on every edit (typing, pasting, picking a country). It reports
the old and new E.164 values, the country, the formatted number, the status and `IsValid`. Use the event for live
feedback and the bindings for the stored value.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.PhoneInputValueChangedDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12">
        <arc:PhoneInput Label="Phone number"
                        Width="360"
                        HorizontalAlignment="Left"
                        ValueChanged="OnValueChanged" />
        <StackPanel Spacing="4">
            <TextBlock x:Name="E164"
                       Text="E.164: —"
                       FontSize="13"
                       FontFamily="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource MonoFontFamily}"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
            <TextBlock x:Name="Formatted"
                       Text="Formatted: —"
                       FontSize="13"
                       FontFamily="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource MonoFontFamily}"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
            <TextBlock x:Name="Status"
                       Text="Status: Empty"
                       FontSize="13"
                       FontFamily="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource MonoFontFamily}"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
        </StackPanel>
        <TextBlock Text="Try +14155550132, or pick Canada with a number typed."
                   FontSize="13"
                   TextWrapping="Wrap"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class PhoneInputValueChangedDemo : UserControl
{
    public PhoneInputValueChangedDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
    }

    private void OnValueChanged(object? sender, PhoneInputValueChangedEventArgs e)
    {
        E164.Text = $"E.164: {(e.NewValue.Length > 0 ? e.NewValue : "—")}";
        Formatted.Text = $"Formatted: {(e.Formatted.Length > 0 ? $"+{e.Country.Dial} {e.Formatted}" : "—")}";
        Status.Text = $"Status: {e.Status}{(e.IsValid ? " (valid)" : string.Empty)}";
    }
}
```

```xml
<arc:PhoneInput Label="Phone number"
                Value="{Binding Phone, Mode=TwoWay}"
                Country="{Binding Country, Mode=TwoWay}" />
```

```csharp
phone.ValueChanged += (_, e) =>
{
    Console.WriteLine($"{e.NewValue} ({e.Status}, valid: {e.IsValid})");
};

phone.OpenPicker();
```

`ValueChanged` also fires when `Value` is assigned in code. A handler that writes the value back should compare
`e.NewValue` with the stored value first, so it does not loop. `OpenPicker()` and `ClosePicker()` open and close the
country list from code; `IsPickerOpen` reports the state.

### Binding to a view model

In an MVVM application the view model owns the number, the country and the rules for saving it. The field shows the
values and writes the edits back. The example below uses CommunityToolkit.Mvvm and the `PhoneNumbers` helpers to check
the number before the save call.

```csharp
public partial class ContactViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    private readonly IContactService _contacts;

    public ContactViewModel(IContactService contacts)
    {
        _contacts = contacts;
    }

    [ObservableProperty]
    private string _phone = string.Empty;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private string _country = "US";

    [ObservableProperty]
    private string? _phoneError;

    [RelayCommand]
    private async Task SaveAsync()
    {
        PhoneError = null;
        var parsed = PhoneNumbers.Parse(Phone);
        if (parsed is not { } number ||
            PhoneNumbers.StatusOf(number.Country, number.National) != PhoneNumberStatus.Valid)
        {
            PhoneError = "Enter a complete phone number, such as +1 415 555 0132.";
            return;
        }

        await _contacts.SaveAsync(Phone);
    }
}
```

```xml
<StackPanel Spacing="16">
    <arc:PhoneInput Label="Mobile number"
                    Value="{Binding Phone, Mode=TwoWay}"
                    Country="{Binding Country, Mode=TwoWay}"
                    ErrorMessage="{Binding PhoneError}" />
    <arc:Button Content="Save contact" Command="{Binding SaveCommand}" IsDefault="True" />
</StackPanel>
```

`Value` and `Country` are the two-way properties. `SaveCommand` is the command to bind to a submit button, and
`ErrorMessage` receives the server-side rule. Clear `PhoneError` when the number changes, so a stale message does not
stay on screen. `ValidationMessage`, `Status`, `SelectedCountry` and `IsPickerOpen` are read-only properties; bind them
one way when the form needs them.

### Disabled and hidden label

`IsEnabled="False"` fades the field and keeps the country list from opening. `IsLabelVisible="False"` hides the label,
which still names the number for assistive technology. Hide it only when a column header or a heading names the field.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.PhoneInputStatesDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="16">
        <arc:PhoneInput Label="Disabled"
                        Value="+14155550132"
                        IsEnabled="False"
                        Width="360"
                        HorizontalAlignment="Left" />
        <arc:PhoneInput Label="Phone number"
                        IsLabelVisible="False"
                        Value="+33612345678"
                        Width="360"
                        HorizontalAlignment="Left" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

### Keyboard

The country button sits before the number in the tab order. On the button, ArrowDown and ArrowUp open the list, and a
printable character opens a search seeded with that character. Inside the number, typing `+` opens the list with the
calling-code search, and Backspace or Delete on a separator deletes the digit beside it. The complete map is in the
Accessibility section.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.PhoneInputKeyboardDemo">
    <arc:PhoneInput Label="Phone number" Country="DE" Width="360" HorizontalAlignment="Left" />
</UserControl>
```

### Example: checkout contact details

A contact step in a checkout flow. The mobile number is stored as E.164 and has a preselected country, because the
courier calls this number for delivery. The alternate number shows a message that replaces the built-in validation
with an instruction the person can act on. The email field and the buttons complete the step, and the primary action
names what happens next.

![Checkout contact details with a mobile number, an alternate number with an error and an email field](https://docs.tkcode.si/shots/Docs/SpecialInputs/PhoneInput/images/CheckoutContact.webp)

```xml
<StackPanel Width="560" Spacing="20">
    <arc:Input Label="Full name"
               Text="Maya Chen" />
    <arc:PhoneInput Label="Mobile number"
                    Value="+14155550132"
                    Description="The courier calls this number on delivery day." />
    <arc:PhoneInput Label="Alternate number"
                    Country="GB"
                    Value="+447911"
                    ErrorMessage="Enter the full number, such as 07911 123456." />
    <arc:Input Label="Delivery email"
               Text="maya.chen@northwind.com"
               Description="Order updates go to this address." />
    <StackPanel Orientation="Horizontal" Spacing="8" HorizontalAlignment="Right">
        <arc:Button Content="Back" Variant="Secondary" />
        <arc:Button Content="Continue to payment" />
    </StackPanel>
</StackPanel>
```

### Content guidelines

- **Label**: name the number by its purpose, in sentence case: "Mobile number", "Delivery phone", "Alternate number".
  Use "Phone number" only when the form has no other number. The label stays visible while the person types.
- **Description**: one sentence that says what the number is used for: "We text a sign-in code to this number." Keep it
  to the consequence, so the person understands why the field is asked for.
- **Error**: say what is missing and show an example in the national format: "Enter the full number, such as
  07911 123456." Do not repeat the validation text as a rule ("Invalid number").
- **Country names**: the picker uses the English names from the built-in table. Localize the picker's text with
  `SearchPlaceholder`, `SearchLabel`, `ListLabel`, `SuggestedLabel` and `AllCountriesLabel`.
- **Placeholder and examples**: the placeholder and the typing guide come from the country's example number, so set
  `Country` to the market the form serves and let the field show its national shape.

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| Phone | Mobile number |
| Invalid phone number. | Enter the full number, such as 07911 123456. |
| Phone number is required. | Enter a mobile number so the courier can reach you. |
| Wrong number | Numbers in United Kingdom have 10 digits. (the built-in message; keep it) |

### Best practices

**Do**

- Store the `Value` string unchanged. E.164 is the only form the rest of the system needs, and it is what the
  integrations for SMS, calls and CRM sync expect.
- Set `Country` from the user's shipping, billing or account country before the person types. The picker then
  starts where the person expects, and the number needs no prefix.
- Limit `Countries` to the markets the product serves. The picker then never offers a country that the order or the
  account cannot use.
- Validate the number again on the server with `PhoneNumbers.StatusOf`. The client check is a convenience; the server
  must not trust the field alone.
- Keep the built-in validation on for sign-up and checkout, where a short number fails silently later otherwise.

**Avoid**

- Storing the national format or the typed text. A number saved as "07911 123456" cannot be dialed without the country
  it belongs to, and each consumer would have to guess that country.
- Using `Input` for phone numbers because the picker looks like extra work. A plain text field cannot tell "+44" from
  a trunk zero, and it cannot hold the country the number belongs to.
- Relying on the flag emoji for meaning. On Windows the flag shows as two letters, so the country name and the calling
  code are the reliable cue.
- Showing the validation message before the person leaves the field. The component waits for blur on purpose, so a
  number that is still being typed does not flash an error.
- Mutating `Countries` or `PreferredCountries` in place. Assign a new list, because the picker rebuilds from the
  property assignment.

### Common questions

**The number I pasted picked a different country. Is that a bug?** No. A pasted or typed international number ("+44 ...",
"+33 ...") sets the country from its calling code, and the picker announces "Country set to ...". `+1` picks Canada
when the area code belongs to Canada.

**How do I know whether the number is complete?** Read `Status` for the current answer, or handle `ValueChanged` and read
`IsValid`. `Status` is `Incomplete` for fewer digits than a valid length, `TooLong` for more digits than the longest
valid length, and `Valid` for a valid length. `Empty` means there are no national digits at all.

**Why does the field show no error for a number I just typed partially?** Validation runs only after the number loses
focus, and only when digits were entered. Leave the field to see the message; a number that was set in code (through
`Value`) is not checked until the person edits it and leaves it.

**Can I show the built-in message in another language?** Yes. Set `ValidationTextFormat` with `{0}` for the country
name and `{1}` for the valid lengths, and set `NoMatchesTextFormat`, `SearchLabel`, `SearchPlaceholder` and the other
text properties to your strings. The country names themselves come from the built-in table.

## API reference

### PhoneInput

Arc phone input: a phone field with a country picker. The number formats as it is typed in the selected country's shape (separators only print while digits follow, a typed trunk prefix is kept) with a faint guide showing the rest of the expected number; the value comes out in E.164. The flag button grows into a searchable country list (one morphing surface), pasted or autofilled international numbers pick their own country (+1 picks Canada by area code), and typing "+" in the number jumps into the picker with a calling-code search. After blur an incomplete or too long number shows "Numbers in United Kingdom have 10 digits" unless `IsValidationEnabled` is off or an `ErrorMessage` replaces it; a valid number shows a check. Keyboard: on the country button ArrowDown / ArrowUp open the list and a printable key opens it seeded with that key; in the search ArrowDown / ArrowUp, PageDown / PageUp (8 rows), Home / End (with an empty search) move, Enter picks, Escape closes and returns to the button, Tab closes. In the number, Backspace / Delete on a separator delete the digit beside it.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Value` | `string` | `""` | Defines the `Value` property. |
| `Country` | `string` | `"US"` | Defines the `Country` property. |
| `Countries` | `IList<string>?` | `null` | Defines the `Countries` property. |
| `PreferredCountries` | `IList<string>` | – | Defines the `PreferredCountries` property. |
| `IsValidationEnabled` | `bool` | `true` | Defines the `IsValidationEnabled` property. |
| `IsRequired` | `bool` | `false` | Defines the `IsRequired` property. |
| `SearchPlaceholder` | `string` | `"Country or code"` | Defines the `SearchPlaceholder` property. |
| `SearchLabel` | `string` | `"Search countries or calling codes"` | Defines the `SearchLabel` property. |
| `ListLabel` | `string` | `"Countries"` | Defines the `ListLabel` property. |
| `SuggestedLabel` | `string` | `"Suggested"` | Defines the `SuggestedLabel` property. |
| `AllCountriesLabel` | `string` | `"All countries"` | Defines the `AllCountriesLabel` property. |
| `NoMatchesTextFormat` | `string` | `"No countries match “{0}”"` | Defines the `NoMatchesTextFormat` property. |
| `ValidationTextFormat` | `string` | `"Numbers in {0} have {1} digits"` | Defines the `ValidationTextFormat` property. |
| `ClearSearchLabel` | `string` | `"Clear search"` | Defines the `ClearSearchLabel` property. |
| `CloseListLabel` | `string` | `"Close country list"` | Defines the `CloseListLabel` property. |
| `Status` | `PhoneNumberStatus` | – | *Read-only.* Defines the `Status` property. |
| `SelectedCountry` | `PhoneCountry` | – | *Read-only.* Defines the `SelectedCountry` property. |
| `ValidationMessage` | `string?` | – | *Read-only.* Defines the `ValidationMessage` property. |
| `IsPickerOpen` | `bool` | – | *Read-only.* Defines the `IsPickerOpen` property. |
| `Label` | `string?` | `null` | The visible label above the frame; also the accessible name. |
| `Description` | `string?` | `null` | Helper copy under the frame (rewrites changed words in place; counts roll). |
| `ErrorMessage` | `string?` | `null` | Error copy under the frame; non-empty makes the field invalid. |
| `IsInvalid` | `bool` | `false` | Invalid state; always true while an error is shown. |
| `IsLabelVisible` | `bool` | `true` | When false the label is hidden visually but still names the field. |
| `Size` | `ControlSize` | `Medium` | Frame height: Small 36, Medium 44 (default), Large 50. |
| `Prefix` | `object?` | `null` | Content before the text (icon, unit, currency). |
| `Suffix` | `object?` | `null` | Content after the text (unit, action button). |
| `Placeholder` | `string?` | `null` | Hint shown while the field is empty (same as `PlaceholderText`). |
| `EffectiveErrorMessage` | `string?` | – | *Read-only.* The error actually shown: `ErrorMessage`, else the binding's validation message. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ValueChanged` | `PhoneInputValueChangedEventArgs` | Defines the `ValueChanged` event. |

Pseudo-classes: `:open`, `:valid`, `:invalid`

Derives from `TextBox`: every member of `TextBox` works as well.

Companion types. `PhoneNumberStatus` is the value of `Status` and the `Status` of the event arguments:

| Member | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `Empty` | No national digits (a typed trunk prefix alone is still empty) |
| `Incomplete` | Fewer digits than a valid length, or a length between two valid ones |
| `Valid` | A valid length for the country |
| `TooLong` | More digits than the longest valid length |

`PhoneInputValueChangedEventArgs` is the argument of `ValueChanged`:

| Member | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `OldValue` | The previous E.164 value, `""` when there were no digits |
| `NewValue` | The new E.164 value, such as `+14155550132`, `""` when there are no digits |
| `Country` | The selected `PhoneCountry` |
| `Formatted` | The number as shown in the field, without the calling code; a typed trunk prefix is kept |
| `Status` | The `PhoneNumberStatus` of the number |
| `IsValid` | `True` when `Status` is `Valid` |

`PhoneNumbers` is the static helper class behind the field. It is public so that forms and imports can use the same
rules:

| Member | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `Countries` | The 49 countries of the built-in table, in table order |
| `Find(iso)` | The `PhoneCountry` for an ISO code (case-insensitive), or `null` |
| `Flag(iso)` | The flag as regional indicator letters; Taiwan, Hong Kong and Macao return the flag of China |
| `FormatNational(country, digits)` | Formats national digits as typed, with separators that print only while digits follow |
| `StatusOf(country, digits)` | The `PhoneNumberStatus` of national digits (a trunk prefix is allowed) |
| `ToE164(country, digits)` | The E.164 form, or `""` without digits |
| `Parse(input, pool)` | Reads an international number into a `PhoneNumberParseResult` (`Country`, `National`), or `null` |
| `Format(e164)` | Formats an E.164 number for display, such as "+44 7400 123456" |

## Accessibility

- `Label` names the field. With `IsLabelVisible="False"` the label is hidden but still names it.
- `IsRequired="True"` marks the number as required for assistive technology and for forms.
- The country button is named "Country, <name> +<code>", for example "Country, United States +1". The search box is a
  combo box that reports the active country, and the list has Suggested and All countries groups.
- ArrowDown and ArrowUp open the picker on the country button. Inside the search, arrows, PageUp and PageDown move,
  Home and End jump to the first and last item, Enter selects and Escape returns focus to the button.
- A country change caused by a paste or a picker choice is announced politely, as "Country set to <name>" or
  "<name>, +<code>". The number of results in a search is announced as "<n> countries" or "No matches".
- A number error appears after blur as help text. A valid number is announced as "Valid <country> number".
- The description and the error are the field's help text, read after the name and the value.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Tab` | From outside, moves to the country button; from the button, moves to the number; from the number, leaves the field |
| `Shift+Tab` | Moves backward: from the number to the country button, and from the button to the previous control |
| `ArrowDown` / `ArrowUp` on the country button | Opens the country list |
| A printable character on the country button | Opens the list with that character as the search |
| `Backspace` / `Delete` on the country button | No effect on the number |
| `+` typed in the number | Opens the list with a calling-code search, such as "+44" finding United Kingdom |
| `Backspace` / `Delete` on a separator in the number | Deletes the digit beside the separator |
| `ArrowDown` / `ArrowUp` in the search | Moves the active country by one row |
| `PageDown` / `PageUp` in the search | Moves by 8 rows |
| `Home` / `End` in the search | Moves to the first or last row, while the search is empty |
| `Enter` in the search | Picks the active country, keeps the digits within the new country's lengths and returns to the number |
| `Escape` in the search | Closes the list and returns focus to the country button |
| `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` in the search | Closes the list and moves to the number, or back to the country button |
| Pointer press outside the list | Closes the list without changing the country |

## Motion

- The field's surface grows from the country button into the country list: its width, height and corner radius move
  together on a spring. The list is at most 340 px wide, and the corner radius moves from 17 px to 22 px.
- The flag and the calling code roll to the new country in the direction of the list. The highlight glides between
  rows.
- A message row opens its height smoothly, and its text rises in with a soft blur. A valid check pops in.
- Reduced motion jumps the surface to its final size and swaps the content with short fades. Off motion switches at once.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| Country list opens | The surface grows from the trigger with a spring (0.4 s, slight bounce) | Surface jumps to its final size; content fades | Immediate |
| Country list closes | The surface shrinks back on a shorter spring (0.32 s, no bounce) | Surface jumps to the closed size; content fades | Immediate |
| Country changes | The flag and calling code roll in the list direction (0.2 s fade and slide) | Short fade | Immediate swap |
| Highlight moves between rows | The highlight glides (0.28 s, slight bounce) | Short fade | Immediate |
| Message row appears or changes | Height opens smoothly; the new text rises from below with a soft blur | Full height with a short fade | Immediate |
| Valid check appears | Pops in on a snappy spring | Short fade | Immediate |
| Hover, focus, invalid | The border color crossfades | The border color crossfades | Immediate |

## Related

- `Input` for text that is not a phone number, and `Textarea` for several lines.
- `Select` for a fixed list of values, and `Field` or `FieldFrame` to build a similar labeled field around your own editor.
- `MoneyInput` and `NumberField` for numeric values with their own formatting rules.
- `PasswordField` and `SearchField` for secrets and search text.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `Input` | The value is free text, an identifier or a URL and has no country or calling code |
| `Select` / `Combobox` | The person chooses one value from a known list, and the list is not a set of countries |
| `NumberField` / `MoneyInput` | The value is a quantity or an amount that you format and round |
| `SearchField` | The text filters or searches content instead of being saved as a contact detail |
| `Field` + `FieldFrame` | You build your own editor and want the same label, frame and message rows |

# Scrub input

> A Figma-style number field: drag the label to scrub, or type values, units, and arithmetic.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/scrub-input

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ScrubInputInspectorDemo">
    <Border Width="320"
            HorizontalAlignment="Center"
            Padding="16,26,16,16"
            CornerRadius="18"
            BorderThickness="1"
            Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Surface}"
            BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource BorderSubtle}">
        <Grid ColumnDefinitions="*,*" RowDefinitions="Auto,Auto,Auto" ColumnSpacing="8" RowSpacing="8">
            <arc:ScrubInput Grid.Row="0" Grid.Column="0" Label="X" Value="120" Unit="px" />
            <arc:ScrubInput Grid.Row="0" Grid.Column="1" Label="Y" Value="48" Unit="px" />
            <arc:ScrubInput Grid.Row="1" Grid.Column="0" Label="W" Value="320" Minimum="0" Unit="px" ResetValue="320" />
            <arc:ScrubInput Grid.Row="1" Grid.Column="1" Label="H" Value="180" Minimum="0" Unit="px" ResetValue="180" />
            <arc:ScrubInput Grid.Row="2" Grid.Column="0" Label="R" Value="15" Minimum="0" Maximum="360" IsWrapping="True" IsTrackVisible="False" Unit="°" ResetValue="0" />
            <arc:ScrubInput Grid.Row="2" Grid.Column="1" Label="O" Value="80" Minimum="0" Maximum="100" Unit="%" ResetValue="100" />
        </Grid>
    </Border>
</UserControl>
```

## When to use

`ScrubInput` is a compact number field for inspector and property panels. Its label doubles as a drag handle: the person
drags it sideways to tune a value, or clicks into the field to type an exact one. A panel of these fields reads like a
design tool's inspector, so it suits any screen where a row of numbers is adjusted many times and checked by eye.

- **Widget layout in a dashboard editor**: the X, Y, W and H of a chart tile. A designer drags W to see the grid respond,
  then types `320` to snap it to the grid unit.
- **Visual settings in a report or document editor**: opacity, rotation and scale. Dragging gives quick feedback, and
  typing gives the exact figure a brand guideline asks for.
- **Settings with a unit the person can change**: a stroke width that a designer enters in `px`, `pt` or `em`. The unit
  button cycles through `Units`, and a typed unit such as `50%` switches the unit.
- **Limits in a rules or threshold panel**: an alert threshold between 0 and 100 percent, or a timeout in seconds with a
  minimum of 1. `Minimum` and `Maximum` keep the value in range while the person drags.
- **Theme and token editors in internal tools**: spacing, radius and elevation values that change the preview at once,
  where `ValueChanged` drives the preview and `ValueCommitted` writes the saved theme.

## When not to use

- **A form number that people step with buttons**: use `NumberField`, which has a stepper and a limit note for a
  checkout quantity or a seat count.
- **A position on a range where the shape matters more than the exact figure**: use `Slider`, for example a volume or a
  brightness control.
- **A currency amount**: use `MoneyInput`, which handles the currency symbol, grouping and rounding of money.
- **Many numeric values in rows**: use `DataGrid` for a table of figures. `ScrubInput` is designed for a handful of fields
  in one panel, not for every cell of a list.
- **A text value with no numeric meaning**: use `Input`. A `ScrubInput` only accepts numbers, arithmetic and units.

## Usage

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:ScrubInput Label="X" Value="120" Unit="px" />
</UserControl>
```

`ScrubInput` derives from `TemplatedControl`, not from a text box. The control paints its own shell (the background, the
1 px border, the track and the stretch) and hosts a borderless text editor for typing. That is why a drag, a stretch and
a shake all happen on the shell, while the number stays a normal editable text. The label is the drag handle, so the
visible label is also the control's only handle for the mouse.

### Anatomy

1. **Label** (`Label`): text drawn at weight 500, or a control such as a 14 px `ArcGlyph`. The label is at least 30 px wide,
   with 10 px of padding before it and 4 px after. Dragging it scrubs the value, and a double click returns the value to
   `ResetValue`.
2. **Shell**: a muted surface with a 1 px border and a 12 px corner radius at the medium size (9 px at the small size).
   Its height is 36 px at `Medium` and 30 px at `Small`.
3. **Track** (`IsTrackVisible`): a quiet wash, foreground at 6 percent, that fills the shell in proportion to the value
   between the two limits. It shows only when both limits are finite, and it brightens while the value is being scrubbed.
4. **Number** (the editor): the value as the field shows it, rounded to the effective precision. It has 4 px of padding on
   the left and selects all of its text on focus.
5. **Unit** (`Unit`, `Units`): the unit after the number, with a 2 px gap. With one unit it is plain text. With several
   units it becomes a button that cycles through them, with a 6 px corner radius and a foreground wash of 7 percent on hover.
6. **Modifier tag**: a 20 px pill about 6 px above the field that reads "×10" with Shift or "×0.1" with Alt while a drag is
   in progress. It shows only while a modifier is held.

### Scrubbing and typing

A press on the label and a horizontal move of 3 px or more start a scrub. Each `PixelsPerStep` pixels (2 by default) of
travel change the value by one `Step`. The value follows the pointer while the drag runs, and the release commits it.
A click in the number focuses the field and selects its text. Typing does not change the value until the entry is
committed with Enter, when the field loses focus, or with an arrow key.

Shift and Alt change the step during a drag, and the tag shows the multiplier. Escape cancels a drag and returns the value
to where the drag started. Touch works too: a horizontal drag scrubs, and a vertical touch scrolls the parent panel
instead, so a long inspector can still be scrolled with a finger.

### Limits and wrapping

`Minimum` and `Maximum` define the range. The defaults are negative and positive infinity, which means no limit. A
dragged value past a limit stretches the field by up to 12 px with resistance and springs back on release. A typed or
stepped value past a limit is clamped to the limit and committed; a step at the limit does not change the value and
gives a small bump.

`IsWrapping` makes the value wrap from the maximum to the minimum instead of stopping. It needs both limits, and the
maximum must be larger than the minimum. Without both finite limits the setting has no effect, so an unbounded field never
wraps.

```xml
<arc:ScrubInput Label="W" Value="320" Minimum="0" Unit="px" ResetValue="320" />
<arc:ScrubInput Label="O" Value="80" Minimum="0" Maximum="100" Unit="%" ResetValue="100" />
```

```csharp
var rotation = new ScrubInput
{
    Label = "R",
    Value = 15,
    Minimum = 0,
    Maximum = 360,
    IsWrapping = true,
    IsTrackVisible = false,
    Unit = "°",
    ResetValue = 0
};
```

`ResetValue` is where a double click on the label returns. `IsTrackVisible` defaults to showing the track when both limits
are finite; set it to `False` for an angle, where a track across 0 to 360 says little.

### Steps and precision

`Step` is the change per arrow key and per step of a drag, and it defaults to 1. `FineStep` (with Alt) defaults to a tenth
of `Step`, and `CoarseStep` (with Shift) defaults to ten times `Step`. Coarse steps land on the coarse grid, so 13 with
Shift goes to 20 at a step of 10, not to 23.

`Precision` sets the decimal places. When it is not set, the field keeps the larger number of decimals of `Step` and of
the fine step, so a `Step` of 0.1 keeps two decimals. The displayed text drops trailing zeros, so 1.5 shows as `1.5`.

```xml
<arc:ScrubInput Label="Gap" Value="1.5" Step="0.1" Minimum="0" Unit="em" />
```

### Input grammar

The editor accepts arithmetic, a unit after a number, and a comma as the decimal point. `ScrubExpression.Evaluate` runs the
same grammar, so a field and a settings import agree on what a value means.

| Entry | Result |
|---|---|
| `12*2`, `12 × 2`, `24/2`, `12+3-1` | Arithmetic; `×` and `÷` and `−` are accepted as operators |
| `(100-24)/2` | Parentheses group the operations |
| `1,5em` | `1.5` with the unit `em`; a comma is a decimal point |
| `50%` | `50` with the unit `%`, which switches the unit when `%` is in `Units` |
| `15deg`, `15°` | `15` with the degree unit, the same as `°` |
| `abc`, `12px` with no `px` in `Units`, `4/0` | Rejected: the old value stays and the field flags the entry as invalid |

A unit matches its entry in any letter case. An entry with a unit that is not in the unit list is rejected, and so is a
result that is not finite, such as division by zero.

### Multiple units

With several `Units` the unit becomes a button. A click cycles to the next unit, and the value keeps its number. A typed
unit in the entry switches the unit too: typing `50%` in a field whose unit is `px` sets the unit to `%` and the value to
50. A single unit, or a field without `Units`, shows the unit as plain text, and the unit button is not a tab stop.


### Sizes

`Size` sets the height. `Small` is 30 px with 12 px text and a 9 px corner radius. `Medium` is the default: 36 px with 14 px
text and a 12 px corner radius. `Large` has no size of its own and renders as `Medium`. Use `Small` for a dense inspector
column and `Medium` for a form or a panel that mixes these fields with other 36 px controls.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"

             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ScrubInputSizesDemo">
    <Border Width="320"
            HorizontalAlignment="Center"
            Padding="16,26,16,16"
            CornerRadius="18"
            BorderThickness="1"
            Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Surface}"
            BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource BorderSubtle}">
        <StackPanel Spacing="8">
            <arc:ScrubInput Label="Small" Size="Small" Value="12" Unit="px" />
            <arc:ScrubInput Label="Medium" Value="12" Unit="px" />
        </StackPanel>
    </Border>
</UserControl>
```

### Binding and events

`Value` and `Unit` are two-way. `ValueChanged` fires for every change, including each step of a drag and each change made
from code. `ValueCommitted` fires once a change settles: when a scrub ends, when Enter or blur commits a typed entry, when
a key step lands, or when a reset runs. Both report the old value, the new value, the unit and the `ChangeSource`.

`ChangeSource` tells you where the change came from. `Programmatic` marks a value set from code or a binding, which raises
`ValueChanged` only and gives no feedback; `Scrub`, `Type`, `Key` and `Reset` mark the four ways a person changes the
value. A handler that saves the value should use `ValueCommitted`, so it does not write during every step of a drag.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ScrubInputEventsDemo">
    <Border Width="320"
            HorizontalAlignment="Center"
            Padding="16,26,16,16"
            CornerRadius="18"
            BorderThickness="1"
            Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Surface}"
            BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource BorderSubtle}">
        <StackPanel Spacing="12">
            <arc:ScrubInput x:Name="Amount"
                            Label="Amount"
                            Value="10"
                            Minimum="0"
                            Maximum="50"
                            Step="1"
                            ResetValue="10"
                            ValueChanged="OnValueChanged"
                            ValueCommitted="OnValueCommitted" />
            <arc:Button Content="Set 25 from code"
                        Variant="Secondary"
                        HorizontalAlignment="Left"
                        Click="OnSetFromCodeClick" />
            <TextBlock x:Name="Log"
                       FontSize="12"
                       LineSpacing="2"
                       FontFamily="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource MonoFontFamily}"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
        </StackPanel>
    </Border>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using System.Globalization;
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class ScrubInputEventsDemo : UserControl
{
    private const int MaxEntries = 6;

    private readonly List<string> _entries = [];

    public ScrubInputEventsDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        AddEntry("Scrub, step or type to see the events.");
    }

    // Fires for every change, including the ones made from code.
    private void OnValueChanged(object? sender, ScrubInputValueChangedEventArgs e)
        => AddEntry($"ValueChanged    {Format(e.OldValue)} → {Format(e.NewValue)}  ({e.ChangeSource})");

    // Fires once a change made in the field settles.
    private void OnValueCommitted(object? sender, ScrubInputValueChangedEventArgs e)
        => AddEntry($"ValueCommitted  {Format(e.OldValue)} → {Format(e.NewValue)}  ({e.ChangeSource})");

    private void OnSetFromCodeClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) => Amount.Value = 25;

    private void AddEntry(string entry)
    {
        _entries.Insert(0, entry);
        if (_entries.Count > MaxEntries)
        {
            _entries.RemoveAt(_entries.Count - 1);
        }
        Log.Text = string.Join('\n', _entries);
    }

    private static string Format(double value) => value.ToString("0.###", CultureInfo.InvariantCulture);
}
```

```xml
<arc:ScrubInput Label="Opacity" Value="{Binding Opacity, Mode=TwoWay}" Minimum="0" Maximum="100" Unit="%" />
```

```csharp
amount.ValueCommitted += (_, e) =>
{
    Console.WriteLine($"{e.OldValue} -> {e.NewValue} {e.Unit} ({e.ChangeSource})");
};
```

`ValueCommitted` also fires when a commit leaves the value unchanged, such as a typed entry clamped to a limit. Compare
`e.OldValue` with `e.NewValue` before you save if the save is expensive.

### Binding to a view model

A layout inspector binds each field to a property of the selected widget. The view model owns the values and the saving,
and the fields show them. The example uses CommunityToolkit.Mvvm.

```csharp
public partial class WidgetLayoutViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    [ObservableProperty]
    private double _x = 120;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private double _width = 320;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private double _opacity = 80;

    [RelayCommand]
    private void ResetLayout()
    {
        X = 0;
        Width = 320;
        Opacity = 100;
    }
}
```

```xml
<StackPanel Spacing="12">
    <arc:ScrubInput Label="X"
                    Value="{Binding X, Mode=TwoWay}"
                    Unit="px" />
    <arc:ScrubInput Label="W"
                    Value="{Binding Width, Mode=TwoWay}"
                    Minimum="0"
                    Unit="px"
                    ResetValue="320" />
    <arc:ScrubInput Label="Opacity"
                    Value="{Binding Opacity, Mode=TwoWay}"
                    Minimum="0"
                    Maximum="100"
                    Unit="%"
                    ResetValue="100" />
</StackPanel>
```

`Value` and `Unit` are the two-way properties. `ValueChanged` and `ValueCommitted` are events, not commands, so connect
them in code-behind or a behavior, and write the saved document from `ValueCommitted`. `Minimum`, `Maximum`, `Step` and
`ResetValue` are one-way settings for the field.

A 14 px glyph can stand in for the text label, which keeps a dense panel calm. A glyph has no text for assistive technology,

### States

A disabled field dims to 50 percent and ignores input, so it cannot be scrubbed or typed into. An entry that cannot be read,
such as `abc`, is rejected: the edge turns red for 900 ms with a short shake, and the old value stays. A rejected entry is
the only way the field shows an error; it has no message row, so put a visible hint next to the panel when the valid
range matters.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ScrubInputStatesDemo">
    <Border Width="320"
            HorizontalAlignment="Center"
            Padding="16,26,16,16"
            CornerRadius="18"
            BorderThickness="1"
            Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Surface}"
            BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource BorderSubtle}">
        <StackPanel Spacing="8">
            <arc:ScrubInput Label="Locked" Value="64" Unit="px" IsEnabled="False" />
            <arc:ScrubInput x:Name="SizeInput" Label="Size" Value="24" Minimum="0" Maximum="100" Unit="%" />
            <TextBlock x:Name="Hint"
                       Text="Try: abc, 12px (unknown unit), 4/0"
                       FontSize="12"
                       TextWrapping="Wrap"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
        </StackPanel>
    </Border>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class ScrubInputStatesDemo : UserControl
{
    public ScrubInputStatesDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        var tryHint = Hint.Text;
        // An entry that cannot be read sets IsInvalid for a moment and keeps the old value.
        SizeInput.PropertyChanged += (_, e) =>
        {
            if (e.Property == ScrubInput.IsInvalidProperty)
            {
                Hint.Text = SizeInput.IsInvalid ? "Rejected: the value stays at " + SizeInput.FormattedValue : tryHint;
            }
        };
    }
}
```

### Example: dashboard tile inspector

The layout panel of a dashboard editor, shown for the selected tile "Revenue by region". The designer drags the W and H
labels to feel the grid, and types an exact size when a brand spec asks for one. Rotation has no track because a track
over 0 to 360 degrees says little. A drag past 0 or 100 percent stretches the opacity field and springs back. The tile values are
the source of truth; the panel writes them back on `ValueCommitted`.

![Layout inspector for a dashboard tile with X, Y, W, H, rotation and opacity fields](https://docs.tkcode.si/shots/Docs/SpecialInputs/ScrubInput/images/TileInspector.webp)

```xml

        <arc:ScrubInput Grid.Row="0" Grid.Column="0" Label="X" Value="120" Unit="px" />
        <arc:ScrubInput Grid.Row="0" Grid.Column="1" Label="Y" Value="48" Unit="px" />
        <arc:ScrubInput Grid.Row="1" Grid.Column="0" Label="W" Value="320" Minimum="0"
                        Unit="px" ResetValue="320" />
        <arc:ScrubInput Grid.Row="1" Grid.Column="1" Label="H" Value="180" Minimum="0"
                        Unit="px" ResetValue="180" />
        <arc:ScrubInput Grid.Row="2" Grid.Column="0" Label="Rotation" Value="15" Minimum="0"
```

### Content guidelines

- **Label**: a short axis or property name in a dense panel ("X", "W", "Rotation", "Opacity"), and a full word in a form
  ("Opacity" rather than "Op"). The unit goes in `Unit`, never in the label.
- **Unit**: the unit the value is measured in: `px`, `%`, `em`, `°`. Use the symbol, not the word, in dense rows.
- **Limits**: set `Minimum` and `Maximum` to the physical or business limit, so the drag cannot pass a value that the
  product rejects. Leave them unset only when the value has no natural bound.
- **Help text**: a `ScrubInput` has no message row. State the valid range in the nearby label, a heading or a tooltip
  of the panel, for example "Opacity 0 to 100 percent".

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| Label "Width (px)" with Unit "px" | Label "W" with Unit "px" |
| Label "Opacity %" | Label "Opacity" with Unit "%" |
| Label "Rot" | Label "Rotation" with Unit "°" |
| Unit "pixels" | Unit "px" |

### Best practices

**Do**

- Set `ResetValue` on every field that has a default. A double click that returns the design to its default is faster
  than a menu, and it matches what the person expects from a design tool.
- Save from `ValueCommitted`, not from `ValueChanged`. A drag raises `ValueChanged` on every step, and saving on each
  step writes the document dozens of times per second.
- Set `Step` to the grain the product uses, such as 1 px for a layout or 0.1 em for typography. The fine and coarse steps
  follow from it.
- Keep the field width at the column width of the panel and use `Size="Small"` for a dense inspector column.

**Avoid**

- Using it for currency. A scrubbed amount has no rounding rule, and `MoneyInput` formats the currency, the grouping and
  the decimals for the locale.
- Relying on a drag alone for a value a person must reach exactly. Typing is the exact path; keep the field editable.
- Putting many `ScrubInput` fields in a long table. Each field is a template with its own pointer tracking; use `DataGrid`
  for rows of numbers.
- Setting `IsWrapping` without finite limits. Wrapping needs both `Minimum` and `Maximum`, so without them the setting does
  nothing.
- Disabling a field to show an error. A disabled field dims and ignores input; a rejected entry is the error signal.

### Common questions

**Why did my typed value jump back to the old one?** The entry was rejected. An unknown unit, a malformed expression or a
division by zero keeps the old value, sets `IsInvalid` for 900 ms and shakes the field. A value outside the limits is not
rejected; it is clamped to the limit and committed.

**Why does a typed value like `1.5` show as `1.5` when the step is 0.1?** `Precision` is not set, so the field keeps the
larger number of decimals of `Step` and of the fine step (a tenth of `Step`). Trailing zeros are dropped. Set `Precision`
to fix the number of decimals for every value.

**How do I change the unit from code?** Set `Unit` to a string. For a unit the person can cycle or type, put that string in
`Units` too, so the unit button and the typed entry accept it. The `Unit` change is two-way, so a binding receives it.

**Does it work with touch?** Yes. A horizontal touch drag scrubs the value, and a vertical touch scrolls the parent panel,
so a long inspector remains scrollable with a finger.

**Can I use it without a label?** Yes, through a glyph label, which can be any control. `Label` is an `object`, so an
`ArcGlyph` works. Give the field an `AutomationProperties.Name`, because a glyph has no text for assistive technology.

## API reference

### ScrubInput

Arc's Scrub input: a compact, Figma-style number field for inspectors and property panels. Drag the label sideways to scrub the value (Shift ten times coarser, Alt ten times finer, switching live and shown in a tag above the field), or click in and type an exact value: entries accept arithmetic such as `12*2` or `(100-24)/2` and a unit from `Units` such as `50%` (see `ScrubExpression`). Arrow keys step, Enter commits, Escape restores the last value, and a double click on the label restores `ResetValue`. At `Minimum` and `Maximum` the field strains past the limit with rubber band resistance and springs back on release; a rejected entry shakes and turns the edge red for 900ms. The row has no label or message rows of its own (the label is the drag handle) and fills its column by default.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Label` | `object?` | `null` | The label, which is also the drag handle: text (weight 500) or a control such as a 14px `ArcGlyph`. |
| `Value` | `double` | `0` | The value (two-way, default 0). |
| `Minimum` | `double` | `-Infinity` | Lower limit (default negative infinity: none). |
| `Maximum` | `double` | `Infinity` | Upper limit (default positive infinity: none). |
| `Step` | `double` | `1` | One step for arrows and scrubbing (default 1). |
| `FineStep` | `double?` | `null` | Step with Alt held (null: a tenth of `Step`). |
| `CoarseStep` | `double?` | `null` | Step with Shift held (null: ten times `Step`). |
| `Precision` | `int?` | `null` | Decimal places kept (null: the larger of the decimals of `Step` and the fine step). |
| `PixelsPerStep` | `double` | `2` | Pointer travel in px for one step while scrubbing (default 2). |
| `IsWrapping` | `bool` | `false` | Values wrap from the maximum to the minimum instead of stopping (needs both limits, Maximum > Minimum). |
| `Unit` | `string?` | `null` | The unit after the number (two-way). Null shows the first of `Units`, or none. |
| `Units` | `IList<string>?` | `null` | Units a typed value may carry; with more than one the unit becomes a button that cycles them. |
| `ResetValue` | `double?` | `null` | A double click on the label returns here (null: no reset). |
| `IsTrackVisible` | `bool?` | `null` | Shows the value's position between the limits as a quiet wash (null: on when both limits are finite). |
| `Size` | `ControlSize` | `Medium` | Small (30px, 12px text) or Medium (36px, 14px text, default). Arc has no large size: Large renders as Medium. |
| `IsPointerLockEnabled` | `bool` | `true` | Arc's `pointerLock`, kept for API parity (default true). Avalonia has no pointer lock, so scrubbing always uses normal pointer capture, as Arc does when a browser refuses the lock: a long drag can reach the screen edge. |
| `UnitButtonNameFormat` | `string` | `"Unit: {0}. Change unit"` | Accessible name of the unit button; `{0}` is the unit (Arc: "Unit: px. Change unit"). |
| `IsInvalid` | `bool` | – | *Read-only.* True for 900ms after a rejected entry. |
| `IsScrubbing` | `bool` | – | *Read-only.* True while the label is being dragged. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ValueChanged` | `ScrubInputValueChangedEventArgs` | Raised for every real change of `Value`: each step of a scrub, typed entries, key steps and resets (Arc's `onValueChange`), and values set from code or a binding (`Programmatic`). |
| `ValueCommitted` | `ScrubInputValueChangedEventArgs` | Raised once when a change settles: a scrub ends (or is cancelled), Enter or blur commits typing, a key step lands, or a reset. Like Arc it also fires when a commit leaves the value unchanged (a clamped entry at the limit). |

Pseudo-classes: `:scrubbing`, `:invalid`, `:hover`, `:handle-hover`, `:text-label`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

Companion types. `ScrubInputChangeSource` is the `ChangeSource` of the event arguments:

| Member | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `Programmatic` | `Value` was set from code or a binding; raises `ValueChanged` only |
| `Scrub` | A drag on the label; also a drag cancelled with Escape |
| `Type` | A typed entry committed with Enter, blur, an arrow key or assistive technology |
| `Key` | An ArrowUp or ArrowDown step |
| `Reset` | A double click on the label, returning to `ResetValue` |

`ScrubInputValueChangedEventArgs` is the argument of `ValueChanged` and `ValueCommitted`:

| Member | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `OldValue` | The value before the change; after a scrub `ValueCommitted` reports the value the drag started from |
| `NewValue` | The value after the change |
| `ChangeSource` | The `ScrubInputChangeSource` that produced the change |
| `Unit` | The unit in effect after the change, `""` when the field has none |

`ScrubExpression.Evaluate(text, units)` is public and returns a `ScrubExpressionResult` (`Value`, `Unit`) or `null` for a
rejected entry. Use it to read a typed value in an import or a command line with the same rules as the field.

## Accessibility

- The number is a spin button. Its accessible name is the label, its value text reads the value with its unit (for example
  "50 percent" or "90 degrees"), and it exposes the minimum, maximum and current value as a range.
- The label is a real label: a click on it focuses the field and selects its number. A label that is a glyph needs
  `AutomationProperties.Name`.
- An invalid entry sets the invalid state for a short time and keeps the old value. The message is announced.
- The unit button is named "Unit: <unit>. Change unit", and it is a tab stop only when there are several units.
- Setting a value through the range provider clamps it to the limits, as typing does.

### Keyboard

The field itself is not a focus target: the number editor takes focus, and the label is only a pointer handle.

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` | Moves focus to the number, and to the unit button when there are several units |
| Click on the number | Focuses it and selects its text |
| `ArrowUp` / `ArrowDown` | Steps the value by `Step`, after committing an open entry |
| `Shift` + `ArrowUp` / `ArrowDown` | Steps by `CoarseStep`, landing on the coarse grid |
| `Alt` + `ArrowUp` / `ArrowDown` | Steps by `FineStep` |
| `Enter` | Commits the typed entry and selects all of the text |
| `Escape` (with an open entry) | Reverts the entry to the last value and selects all |
| `Escape` (during a drag) | Cancels the drag and returns the value to where the drag started |
| Focus leaves the number | Commits the open entry |
| `Shift` or `Alt` held during a drag | Switches the step at once and shows the multiplier tag |
| Double click on the label | Returns the value to `ResetValue` |

## Motion

- Past a limit the field stretches with resistance, and it springs back on release. The digits lean with the stretch.
- An invalid entry or a step at a limit shakes the field once.
- A unit change rises in with a small blur. The track fill follows the pointer while dragging and glides to the new value
  when the value is typed or stepped.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| Drag past a limit | The field stretches up to 12 px and springs back on release | No stretch | Immediate |
| Rejected entry or step at a limit | The field shakes once; the edge is red for 900 ms | No shake; the red edge still shows for 900 ms | Immediate; the red edge shows for 900 ms |
| Unit changes | The unit rises in with a small blur | The unit fades in place | Immediate |
| Track fill | Follows the pointer while dragging; glides to the new value when typed or stepped | Jumps to the new value | Immediate |

## Related

- `NumberField` for a form number with a stepper and a limit note.
- `Slider` when the position on a range matters more than the exact value.
- `MoneyInput` for currency values.
- `Input` for free text, and `DataGrid` for tables of numbers.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `NumberField` | The number is a form value that people step with buttons, such as a quantity |
| `Slider` | People choose a place on a range, and the exact figure matters less than the position |
| `MoneyInput` | The value is an amount of money with a currency and rounding rules |
| `DataGrid` | The numbers are rows and columns in a table rather than a few fields in a panel |
| `Input` | The value is text with no numeric meaning |
