# Tag input

> Turn short text values into removable tags.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/tag-input

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             xmlns:generic="using:System.Collections.Generic"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.TagInputDefaultDemo">
    <arc:TagInput Label="Tags" Width="420" HorizontalAlignment="Left">
        <arc:TagInput.Value>
            <generic:List x:TypeArguments="x:String">
                <x:String>design</x:String>
                <x:String>motion</x:String>
                <x:String>react</x:String>
            </generic:List>
        </arc:TagInput.Value>
    </arc:TagInput>
</UserControl>
```

## When to use

`TagInput` turns short typed values into removable tags inside one form field. It fits forms where a person builds a
list of short strings and needs to see every entry at once: the labels on a support ticket, the recipients of a
scheduled report, the domains allowed to sign in to a workspace. The field draws its own label, description and error
row, so the list reads as a single form control next to the inputs around it.

- **Labels on a support ticket or a CRM contact**: an agent types `billing`, presses Enter, then `refund`. Tags are free
  text, so the set grows with the team's vocabulary instead of waiting for an admin to edit a list.
- **Recipients of a scheduled report**: a finance lead adds `cfo@northwind.com` and the other addresses one after
  another, or pastes a column copied from a spreadsheet. Pasted commas, new lines and tabs split into tags, and each
  address is visible before the report is saved.
- **Allowed domains in a single sign-on setup**: an administrator enters `acme.com` and `acme.co.uk`. Each domain
  stays on screen as its own tag, so a missing or misspelled one is easy to spot before the form is saved.
- **Keywords on a knowledge base article or a product listing**: the author adds several search terms. A duplicate is
  refused without regard to case, so Refund and refund cannot both be saved.
- **Capped lists in a plan form**: a plan that includes five integrations sets `MaxTags="5"`. The sixth add is refused
  with a shake and an announcement, so the limit is explained where the person is working.

## When not to use

- **Values picked from an existing catalog**: roles, plans, warehouses or regions that already exist as records: use
  `MultiSelect`, which chooses from a list, or `Combobox` when the list is long and needs search.
- **Facet filters on a results page**: a few toggles that narrow a table or a feed: use `ChipGroup`, which is built for
  choosing among filter facets.
- **A single value**: one email address, one name or one URL: use `Input`. A tag field with one tag is harder to read
  and validate than a single input.
- **Amounts and quantities**: a list of prices, weights or counts needs parsing and formatting: use `MoneyInput` or
  `NumberField`. `TagInput` stores plain strings and does no parsing.
- **Mentions in running text**: @people and #channel references inside a comment or a message: use `MentionInput`,
  which keeps each mention as one token inside the sentence.
- **Several lines of text**: notes, descriptions or pasted paragraphs: use `Textarea`.

## Usage

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:TagInput Label="Tags"
                  Placeholder="Add a tag"
                  Description="Press Enter or a comma to add a tag." />
</UserControl>
```

`TagInput` derives from Avalonia's `TemplatedControl`. Its frame is the shared `Field` and `FieldFrame` that the other
Arc fields use, so the label, the message rows, the focus halo and the invalid border match `Input`. Inside the frame,
the tags and a borderless text editor sit on wrapping rows. The editor is a text box, so the caret, selection, IME and
the clipboard behave as they do in `Input`; the control adds Enter, the comma, Backspace and the arrow keys for tags.

### Anatomy

1. **Label** (`Label`): the field label, with the same style as `Input` (14 px, medium weight, 8 px above the frame).
   It is also the accessible name of the editor. Hide it with `IsLabelVisible="False"` only when a visible heading
   already names the field.
2. **Frame** (`FieldFrame`): a 1 px border in the border color on the surface. Hover darkens the border only while the
   field is not focused and not invalid. Focus shows the 3 px focus halo. An error (`ErrorMessage` or `IsInvalid`)
   turns the border to the danger color. The frame has a minimum height of 44 px for one row of tags.
3. **Content**: 7 px padding on every side and 6 px between tags, the editor and wrapped rows. Each extra row adds
   34 px to the height. The height follows the rows on a smooth spring.
4. **Tag** (an item of `Value`): at least 28 px high, with 9 px of padding before the label and 4 px after it, inside a
   1 px pill border on the muted surface color. The label uses the body font at the small type size and the foreground
   color, with a 3 px gap before the remove button. A tag wider than the field is truncated with an ellipsis.
5. **Remove button**: a 22 px circle with a 14 px X glyph drawn at a 2 px stroke, in the secondary text color. Hover
   gives it the surface background. Keyboard focus draws a 1.5 px focus ring inside the circle. A press shrinks it to
   96%.
6. **Editor** (the draft): takes the rest of the line. It is at least 80 px wide, starts from a 100 px basis, is 28 px
   high and has 5 px of horizontal padding. When fewer than 100 px are left on a line, the editor moves to the next row.
7. **Placeholder** (`Placeholder`): "Add a tag" by default, drawn in the muted text color at a 12 px inset. It is shown
   only while there are no tags and no draft text.
8. **Description** (`Description`) and **error row** (`ErrorMessage`): helper copy and error copy under the frame, the
   same rows as `Input`. Non-empty `ErrorMessage` makes the field invalid.

`TagInput` has no `Size` property. Its height follows the number of rows, so let the tags wrap rather than shrink
the text.

### Initial tags

`Value` holds the tags as an `IReadOnlyList<string>`. Setting it replaces the whole list and raises `ValueChanged`;
`null` reads back as an empty list.

```csharp
var tags = new TagInput
{
    Label = "Tags",
    Value = ["design", "motion", "react"]
};
```

### Binding to a view model

In an MVVM app the view model owns the list and its rules. The control never edits the list it was given: each add,
remove or paste assigns a new array. Hold an `IReadOnlyList<string>` property and replace it; do not expect an
`ObservableCollection<T>` to change in place. The example checks the recipients' email format.

```csharp
public partial class ReportViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    [ObservableProperty]
    private IReadOnlyList<string> _labels = Array.Empty<string>();

    [ObservableProperty]
    private IReadOnlyList<string> _recipients = Array.Empty<string>();

    [ObservableProperty]
    private string? _recipientsError;

    partial void OnRecipientsChanged(IReadOnlyList<string> value)
    {
        // The control adds a tag at once, so a rule that rejects it removes it and explains why.
        var valid = value.Where(IsEmailAddress).ToArray();
        if (valid.Length != value.Count)
        {
            Recipients = valid;
            RecipientsError = "Enter a full email address, such as ops@acme.com.";
            return;
        }
        RecipientsError = null;
    }

    [RelayCommand]
    private async Task SendAsync()
    {
        if (Recipients.Count == 0)
        {
            RecipientsError = "Add at least one recipient.";
            return;
        }
        await _reports.ScheduleAsync(Labels, Recipients);
    }

    private static bool IsEmailAddress(string tag) =>
        Regex.IsMatch(tag, @"^[^@\s]+@[^@\s]+\.[^@\s]+$");
}
```

```xml
<StackPanel Spacing="16">
    <arc:TagInput Label="Labels"
                  Value="{Binding Labels, Mode=TwoWay}"
                  Description="Press Enter or a comma to add a label." />
    <arc:TagInput Label="Recipients"
                  Value="{Binding Recipients, Mode=TwoWay}"
                  ErrorMessage="{Binding RecipientsError}"
                  Placeholder="name@company.com" />
    <arc:Button Content="Schedule report" Command="{Binding SendCommand}" />
</StackPanel>
```

- `Value` is two-way by default, so `Mode=TwoWay` documents the intent. The view model receives each change, including
  tags added by paste.
- `ErrorMessage` is one-way: the view model owns the message and clears it when the list is valid again.
- Compiled bindings need `x:DataType` on the view (the example leaves it out for brevity).

### Binding and events

`ValueChanged` reports the old and new lists, plus the tags that were `Added` and `Removed`. Use the two-way `Value`
binding for the full state, and the event when you need the difference, for example to write an audit entry or to call
a server once per added tag.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             xmlns:generic="using:System.Collections.Generic"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.TagInputTwoWayValueDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="16">
        <arc:TagInput x:Name="Labels"
                      Label="Labels"
                      Width="420"
                      HorizontalAlignment="Left">
            <arc:TagInput.Value>
                <generic:List x:TypeArguments="x:String">
                    <x:String>bug</x:String>
                    <x:String>ui</x:String>
                </generic:List>
            </arc:TagInput.Value>
        </arc:TagInput>
        <arc:TagInput Label="Bound copy"
                      Description="Bound two-way to the field above."
                      Value="{Binding #Labels.Value, Mode=TwoWay}"
                      Width="420"
                      HorizontalAlignment="Left" />
        <TextBlock x:Name="ValueText"
                   Text="Value: bug, ui"
                   FontSize="13"
                   FontFamily="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource MonoFontFamily}"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
        <TextBlock x:Name="LastEvent"
                   Text="Last event: none"
                   FontSize="13"
                   FontFamily="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource MonoFontFamily}"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
        <arc:Button Content="Reset in code"
                    Variant="Ghost"
                    Size="Small"
                    HorizontalAlignment="Left"
                    Click="OnResetClick" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class TagInputTwoWayValueDemo : UserControl
{
    public TagInputTwoWayValueDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Labels.ValueChanged += OnValueChanged;
    }

    private void OnValueChanged(object? sender, TagInputValueChangedEventArgs e)
    {
        ValueText.Text = "Value: " + (e.NewValue.Count == 0 ? "(empty)" : string.Join(", ", e.NewValue));
        var parts = new List<string>(2);
        if (e.Added.Count > 0)
        {
            parts.Add("added " + string.Join(", ", e.Added));
        }
        if (e.Removed.Count > 0)
        {
            parts.Add("removed " + string.Join(", ", e.Removed));
        }
        LastEvent.Text = "Last event: " + string.Join("; ", parts);
    }

    private void OnResetClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        Labels.Value = ["bug", "ui"];
    }
}
```

```xml
<arc:TagInput Label="Keywords" Value="{Binding Keywords, Mode=TwoWay}" />
```

```csharp
tags.ValueChanged += (_, e) =>
{
    Console.WriteLine($"Added: {string.Join(", ", e.Added)}; removed: {string.Join(", ", e.Removed)}");
};

tags.AddTag("release");
tags.FocusEditor();
```

`AddTag` and `RemoveTag` raise `ValueChanged` but announce nothing, because the person did not act on the field.

### Limit and errors

`MaxTags` refuses adds past the limit. The field shakes and the limit is announced. An `ErrorMessage` marks the
field invalid and shows the error row.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             xmlns:generic="using:System.Collections.Generic"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.TagInputLimitDemo">
    <arc:TagInput Label="Skills"
                  Description="Up to 5 skills. A sixth is refused with a shake and an announcement."
                  MaxTags="5"
                  Width="420"
                  HorizontalAlignment="Left">
        <arc:TagInput.Value>
            <generic:List x:TypeArguments="x:String">
                <x:String>Figma</x:String>
                <x:String>Avalonia</x:String>
                <x:String>C#</x:String>
                <x:String>Motion</x:String>
            </generic:List>
        </arc:TagInput.Value>
    </arc:TagInput>
</UserControl>
```

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.TagInputErrorDemo">
    <arc:TagInput Label="Labels"
                  ErrorMessage="Add at least one label."
                  Width="420"
                  HorizontalAlignment="Left" />
</UserControl>
```

`MaxTags` applies to every add: typing, Enter, comma, paste and `AddTag`. `null` (the default) means no limit. A paste
past the limit adds the pieces that fit and keeps the refused ones in the draft.

Use `ErrorMessage` for a rule the control cannot know, such as a server error. Set it to `null` or an empty string to
clear it.

### Validation

`TagInput` has no pre-commit hook: Enter adds the draft as soon as it is pressed. The control enforces the limit and
duplicates; format and server rules run in the view model after the change.

| Rule | When it runs | Where it shows |
|---|---|---|
| Maximum count (`MaxTags`) | At once, on each add | The field shakes and the limit is announced; no error row. Put a counter in `Description` if people need to see it |
| Duplicate | On Enter, comma or paste | The existing tag pulses and "<tag> is already added" is announced; the draft stays |
| Format (email, domain, slug) | After the tag appears, in the view model | `ErrorMessage` bound from the view model, until the list is valid again |
| At least one tag | On submit | `ErrorMessage`; move focus to the field with `FocusEditor()` |
| Server or uniqueness rule | After the request returns | `ErrorMessage` on the field the error is about; clear it when the list changes |

The duplicate check ignores case, so Design is refused when design is present, and the existing spelling is kept.

### Data shape and performance

A tag is a string with no id, color or display text. Keep extra data, such as a color for each label, in the view model
keyed by the tag text.

Every add or removal copies the list, which is negligible for the tens of tags a form holds. Load many tags with one
`Value` assignment: it raises one `ValueChanged` event, where a loop of `AddTag` calls raises one per tag.

### Pasted lists

Pasting text that contains commas, new lines or tabs splits it into tags. The last piece stays in the draft.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.TagInputPasteDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="16">
        <arc:TagInput Label="Colors"
                      Description="Paste a list separated by commas, new lines or tabs: every piece becomes a tag and the last piece stays in the draft."
                      Width="420"
                      HorizontalAlignment="Left" />
        <arc:Button x:Name="CopySample"
                    Content="Copy “red, green, blue, teal”"
                    Variant="Secondary"
                    Size="Small"
                    HorizontalAlignment="Left"
                    Click="OnCopyClick" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;
using TKCode.Arc.Primitives;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class TagInputPasteDemo : UserControl
{
    public TagInputPasteDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
    }

    private async void OnCopyClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        await ArcClipboard.CopyTextAsync(CopySample, "red, green, blue, teal");
    }
}
```

Pieces are trimmed; empty pieces and duplicates are skipped. Text without a separator pastes into the draft.

### Wrapping rows

Tags wrap onto new rows and the field grows with them. Remove one to watch the rest glide in.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             xmlns:generic="using:System.Collections.Generic"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.TagInputWrappingDemo">
    <arc:TagInput Label="Recipients" Width="420" HorizontalAlignment="Left">
        <arc:TagInput.Value>
            <generic:List x:TypeArguments="x:String">
                <x:String>ada@example.com</x:String>
                <x:String>grace@example.com</x:String>
                <x:String>linus@example.com</x:String>
                <x:String>margaret@example.com</x:String>
                <x:String>ken@example.com</x:String>
                <x:String>barbara@example.com</x:String>
                <x:String>dennis@example.com</x:String>
            </generic:List>
        </arc:TagInput.Value>
    </arc:TagInput>
</UserControl>
```

A long list wraps and the field grows downward; it never scrolls sideways. Tags wider than the field are truncated
with an ellipsis.

### Keyboard

Backspace at the start picks the last tag, Backspace or Delete removes the pick, the arrows move it and Escape clears
it. Clicking a tag picks it too.

### Disabled

Disabled fields fade to 0.5 opacity on `SurfaceMuted`.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"

    </arc:TagInput>
</UserControl>
```

Use `IsEnabled="False"` while the list cannot change, and say why nearby. `TagInput` has no read-only state, so a
disabled field is the only way to lock the list; Tab skips it.

### Example: support ticket form

A support console form for a ticket. The recipients field shows a rule that rejected an address: the bad tag was
removed and the message says how to fix it. Both fields share a width, so their message rows line up.

![A ticket form with a label list and a recipient field that shows an invalid address](https://docs.tkcode.si/shots/Docs/SpecialInputs/TagInput/images/TagInputForm.webp)

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             xmlns:generic="using:System.Collections.Generic"
             Width="640">
    <StackPanel Spacing="20">
        <arc:Input Label="Ticket title"
                   Text="Invoice export times out for large workspaces"
                   Description="Shown to the customer in the ticket list." />
        <arc:TagInput Label="Labels"
                      Description="Press Enter or a comma to add a label. Use lowercase words."
                      HorizontalAlignment="Stretch">
            <arc:TagInput.Value>
                <generic:List x:TypeArguments="x:String">
                    <x:String>billing</x:String>
                    <x:String>export</x:String>
                    <x:String>p2</x:String>
                </generic:List>
            </arc:TagInput.Value>
        </arc:TagInput>
        <arc:TagInput Label="Notify"
                      ErrorMessage="Enter a full email address, such as ops@acme.com."
                      HorizontalAlignment="Stretch">
            <arc:TagInput.Value>
                <generic:List x:TypeArguments="x:String">
                    <x:String>finance@northwind.com</x:String>
                    <x:String>ops@acme.com</x:String>
                    <x:String>on-call-team</x:String>
                </generic:List>
```

### Content guidelines

- **Label**: a plural noun in sentence case, without a colon: "Labels", "Recipients", "Allowed domains". Do not use
  "Please enter labels:". The label stays visible while the field has tags, so it carries the meaning.
- **Placeholder**: an example of one tag ("name@company.com", "billing"), shown only while the field is empty.
- **Description**: one sentence about the rule or the effect: "Up to 5 skills.", "Shown on the invoice header." Write
  numbers as digits.
- **Tags**: store the form the person should see, with consistent case.
- **Error**: name the rule and the fix in the same words as the description: "Enter a full email address, such as
  ops@acme.com."

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| Enter tags here | Add a tag |
| Invalid email! | Enter a full email address, such as ops@acme.com. |
| Too many tags | You can add up to 5 skills. Remove one to add another. |
| Tag already exists | Design is already added. |
| Please add something | Add at least one recipient. |

### Best practices

**Do**

- Give every tag field a visible label, and a description when the rule is not obvious. The label is the editor's
  accessible name, so an unlabeled field is an unnamed control.
- Keep the list as an `IReadOnlyList<string>` property and assign a new list for each change, as the control does.
- Use `MaxTags` for a limit the form already states, so the add is refused at once and announced.
- Keep a format error on the field until the list is valid, so the rule is visible where the person is working.
- Move focus to the field with `FocusEditor()` when a submit fails.

**Avoid**

- Using a tag field for a fixed catalog. People cannot tell which tags are allowed, and typos become new values.
  Use `MultiSelect` or `Combobox` for a list that already exists.
- Removing a rejected tag without a message. Say which rule it broke and how to fix it, on the field.
- Relying on the placeholder for the rule. It disappears when the field gets a tag or a draft.

### Common questions

**Why does Enter not submit my form?** The editor consumes Enter to add the draft, so the form's default button
(`IsDefault="True"`) does not fire on that key. People press the save button or Tab to it.

**How do I show how many tags are left?** `TagInput` has no counter. Bind `Description` to a string the view model
builds from `Value.Count` and `MaxTags`, for example "3 of 5 used". The counter then updates with every change.

**How do I clear all tags?** Set `Value` to an empty list, for example `tags.Value = [];`. The placeholder returns once the draft is empty too.


## API reference

### TagInput

Arc tag input: turns short typed values into removable tags. Enter or a comma adds the trimmed draft (a duplicate, compared case-insensitively, pulses the tag that exists instead); Backspace at the start of the field picks the last tag and the next Backspace removes it; the arrow keys move the pick and a ring glides to it; leaving the field commits the draft. New tags blur in where they were typed, removed tags leave their slot and the rest glide in, and the shell follows wrapped rows on a spring; the field never scrolls sideways.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Value` | `IReadOnlyList<string>` | – | The tags (two-way). Never null: setting null reads back as an empty list. |
| `Label` | `string?` | `null` | The visible label (Arc: required). Also the accessible name of the editor. |
| `Description` | `string?` | `null` | Helper copy under the field; it describes the editor for assistive technology. |
| `ErrorMessage` | `string?` | `null` | Error copy under the field; non-empty makes the field invalid. |
| `Placeholder` | `string?` | `"Add a tag"` | Shown while there are no tags and no draft (Arc default "Add a tag"). |
| `IsLabelVisible` | `bool` | `true` | When false the label is hidden visually but still names the editor. |
| `IsInvalid` | `bool` | `false` | Invalid state (danger border). Always true while `ErrorMessage` is not empty. |
| `MaxTags` | `int?` | `null` | The most tags a user can add (extension; null = unlimited, as Arc). Negative values read as 0. |
| `RemoveLabelFormat` | `string` | `"Remove {0}"` | Accessible name of a tag's remove button; `{0}` is the tag. |
| `AddedAnnouncementFormat` | `string` | `"Added {0}"` | Announced after an add; `{0}` is the tag (or the tags, comma separated, after a paste). |
| `RemovedAnnouncementFormat` | `string` | `"Removed {0}"` | Announced after a removal; `{0}` is the tag. |
| `DuplicateAnnouncementFormat` | `string` | `"{0} is already added"` | Announced when the draft repeats a tag; `{0}` is the existing tag. |
| `PickedAnnouncementFormat` | `string` | `"{0} selected. Press Backspace to remove it."` | Announced when a tag is picked; `{0}` is the tag. |
| `LimitAnnouncementFormat` | `string` | `"You can add up to {0} tags"` | Announced when `MaxTags` refuses an add; `{0}` is the limit. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ValueChanged` | `TagInputValueChangedEventArgs` | Raised (bubbling) whenever `Value` changes, by the user or in code. |

Pseudo-classes: `:invalid`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

### Event arguments

`ValueChanged` passes a `TagInputValueChangedEventArgs`.

| Member | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `OldValue` | `IReadOnlyList<string>` | The tags before the change |
| `NewValue` | `IReadOnlyList<string>` | The tags after the change |
| `Added` | `IReadOnlyList<string>` | Tags in `NewValue` that were not in `OldValue` |
| `Removed` | `IReadOnlyList<string>` | Tags in `OldValue` that are not in `NewValue` |

## Accessibility

- `Label` names the field. With `IsLabelVisible="False"` the label is hidden but still names it.
- The editor's help text comes from `Description` and `ErrorMessage`, so a screen reader reads the rule or the error
  after the name.
- Each tag's remove button is named "Remove <tag>" (the `RemoveLabelFormat` pattern, default `Remove {0}`). The tag
  itself reads as plain text; its remove button is the only control inside it.
- Adding, removing, picking, duplicates and refused adds are announced politely. Focus does not move for an add or a
  pick; removing a tag with its button or with Backspace returns focus to the editor. A duplicate is not added: the
  existing tag pulses so the ignored Enter still gets an answer.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Enter` or `,` | Adds the trimmed draft as a tag. A duplicate is not added: the existing tag pulses and the duplicate is announced. An empty draft does nothing |
| `Backspace` with the caret at the start of an empty draft | Picks the last tag |
| `ArrowLeft` at the start of the draft, or with a tag picked | Picks the previous tag; at the first tag the pick stays where it is |
| `ArrowRight` with a tag picked | Picks the next tag; past the last tag the pick is cleared and the caret returns to the draft |
| `Backspace` or `Delete` with a tag picked | Removes the picked tag and returns focus to the editor |
| `Escape` with a tag picked | Clears the pick |
| `Backspace` inside the draft | Edits the text as usual |
| `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` | Moves through the remove buttons in value order, then to the editor |
| `Enter` on a focused remove button | Removes that tag |
| Click a tag | Picks it; a second click clears the pick. Focus stays in the editor |
| Click the empty part of the field | Focuses the editor |

Typing any character clears the pick. Leaving the field commits the draft as a tag and clears the pick.

## Motion

- A new tag fades in with a blur and a small scale where it was typed. A removed tag leaves, and the others glide to
  their new places.
- The selection ring slides between tags, and the shell height follows when tags wrap onto a new row.
- A duplicate pulses the existing tag once. A refused add shakes the field.
- Reduced motion removes the layout movement, the scale and the blur, and keeps a short fade. Off motion jumps to the end
  state.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| A tag is added | Fades in with a blur, grows from 90% where it was typed | Fades in | Immediate |
| A tag is removed | Leaves from its slot, the others glide into place | Disappears at once | Immediate |
| Tags reflow or wrap | Glide on a morph spring; the shell height follows on a smooth spring | Jump to the new place | Immediate |
| The picked tag changes | The selection ring glides to the new tag | The ring jumps to the tag | Immediate |
| A duplicate is entered | The existing tag pulses once | No pulse | No pulse |
| A refused add (limit) | The content kicks sideways and rings home on a bouncy spring | No shake | No shake |
| The placeholder appears | Rises by 0.3 em with a soft blur | Fades in | Immediate |

## Related

- `MultiSelect` or `Combobox` when the values come from a list that already exists.
- `ChipGroup` for facet filters that narrow a result set.
- `Input` for a single value.
- `MentionInput` for @people and #channel references in running text.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `Input` | The value is one line of text, not a list |
| `MultiSelect` | The values come from a fixed list and people choose several |
| `Combobox` | The list is long, and people search it before they choose |
| `ChipGroup` | The chips are filter facets over a result set |
| `MentionInput` | @people or #channel references sit inside running text |
| `Textarea` | The text runs over several lines or people paste paragraphs |
| `MoneyInput` / `NumberField` | The value is an amount or a number that needs parsing |

## When to use

`MentionInput` is a multi-line field for writing to people and channels. A person types `@` and picks a teammate, or
types `#` and picks a channel, and the mention becomes one token that the field keeps whole. It belongs in the composer
of a comment thread, a reply box, a chat message or a task description, where the text reads as a sentence and the
mentions must still point at records the application can notify or link.

- **Comment threads on an incident, an order or a ticket**: a support lead writes "Thanks @Alex Rivera, can @Priya
  Natarajan confirm the refund ID?", and each mention stores a person's ID, so the application notifies the right
  people instead of matching names afterwards.
- **Release notes and updates posted to a channel**: an engineer links `#launch-q3` inside the sentence, so the
  message carries a channel reference that the chat service can render as a link.
- **Task and review descriptions in a project tool**: a designer assigns follow-ups with `@` mentions inside the
  description, and the saved value keeps the people as structured data for the assignment history.
- **Chat composers with a send action**: a message box submits on Enter with `IsSubmitOnEnter`, clears itself and
  passes the `MentionValue` to the send command.

## When not to use

- **Plain multi-line text with no references**: use `Textarea`, which has no suggestion list and no tokens to keep
  whole.
- **Values that stand apart from the sentence**: use `TagInput`, which keeps each value as a chip outside the text.
- **Headings, lists, links or bold text**: use a rich text editor. `MentionInput` holds plain text plus mentions and
  has no formatting model.
- **A single line such as a name, a title or a search query**: use `Input` or `SearchField`. A one-line field does
  not need an auto-growing editor or a submit-on-Enter flow.
- **Picking one record from a large directory**: use `Combobox` or `Select` with a search. The mention list shows only
  the best `MaxSuggestions` matches, so it suits a short list of people and channels, not a full directory lookup.

## Usage

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:MentionInput Label="Comment"
                      Placeholder="Leave a comment. Use @ to mention, # for a channel"
                      MinLines="1"
                      MaxLines="8" />
</UserControl>
```

The field has no visible label: `Label` only names the editor for assistive technology, and the placeholder carries
the instruction. The field is not a tab stop of its own; focus moves into the editor.

`MentionInput` derives from `TemplatedControl`. Its template holds a real multi-line `TextBox`, so the caret,
selection, input method composition, undo and the clipboard behave as they do in a text box. The editor's own text is
transparent, and a mirror layer behind it paints the same text with the same metrics and tints the mention tokens, so
colors and wrapping stay aligned with the caret. You read and write the content through `Value`, a `MentionValue`:
the plain text plus the mentions with their character offsets.

### Anatomy

1. **Frame** (PART_Shell): a 1 px border with the control radius on the surface color. It uses the border color at
   rest and the strong border color while the editor has focus. Hover does not change it.
2. **Editor** (PART_TextBox): the editable text in the body font at 16 px, with a 24 px line height, letter spacing
   of -0.01 em and 14 px of padding on each side, 11 px at the top and bottom.
3. **Placeholder** (`Placeholder`): shown in the muted text color while the value is empty and no IME text is pending.
4. **Mention token**: the text `@Label` or `#Label` on a rounded background, with 3 px of horizontal and 1 px of
   vertical padding. A person token uses the accent subtle fill with the accent strong text. A channel token uses the
   foreground color at 7% opacity with the foreground text.
5. **Suggestion panel**: a popup at the trigger character, 272 px wide (or as wide as the field when it is narrower),
   placed 6 px from the line. Each row has a 28 px avatar or icon, then the name, then the role or the description. A
   channel row shows its member count on the right.

### When suggestions open

Typing `@` opens the people list and typing `#` opens the channel list. A trigger counts only at the start of a word:
after a space, at the start of a line, or after an opening bracket or a quote. So the `@` in `billing@acme.com` does
not open the list. The query after the trigger has these limits:

- A people query may contain one space, so `@maya chen` matches. A second space closes the list.
- A channel query takes no spaces, so `#launch q3` closes the list at the space.
- A query longer than 48 characters, or one that spans a line break, closes the list.
- Typing a second trigger character inside a query closes the list.

Set `People` or `Channels` to `null` or an empty collection to turn off that trigger. The field then treats `@` or `#`
as plain text, which suits a comment thread where only people can be notified.

Results are ranked before the first `MaxSuggestions` are kept (the default is 6). A name that starts with the query
ranks highest, then a word in the name that starts with it, then a name that contains it, then a match in the role or
the description. A query with no match shows an empty state ("No people match “zz”" or "No channels match “zz”"), and
the list stays open so the person can keep typing or press Escape.

### Binding to a view model

The view model owns the stored value. `Value` is two-way by default, so every edit flows back to the view model.
With CommunityToolkit.Mvvm:

```csharp
public partial class ReplyComposerViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    private readonly ICommentService _comments;

    public ReplyComposerViewModel(ICommentService comments,
                                  IReadOnlyList<MentionPerson> people,
                                  IReadOnlyList<MentionChannel> channels)
    {
        _comments = comments;
        People = people;
        Channels = channels;
    }

    [ObservableProperty]
    private MentionValue _draft = MentionValue.Empty;

    [ObservableProperty]
    [NotifyCanExecuteChangedFor(nameof(SendCommand))]
    private bool _isSending;

    public IReadOnlyList<MentionPerson> People { get; }

    public IReadOnlyList<MentionChannel> Channels { get; }

    [RelayCommand(CanExecute = nameof(CanSend))]
    private async Task SendAsync(MentionValue value)
    {
        IsSending = true;
        try
        {
            await _comments.PostAsync("inc_2026_0412", value);
            Draft = MentionValue.Empty;
        }
        finally
        {
            IsSending = false;
        }
    }

    private bool CanSend(MentionValue? value) =>
        !IsSending && value is not null && !string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(value.Text);
}
```

```xml
<StackPanel Width="560" Spacing="12">
    <arc:MentionInput Label="Reply"
                      Value="{Binding Draft, Mode=TwoWay}"
                      People="{Binding People}"
                      Channels="{Binding Channels}"
                      IsSubmitOnEnter="True"
                      SubmitCommand="{Binding SendCommand}"
                      MinLines="2"
                      MaxLines="6" />
    <arc:Button Content="Post reply"
                Command="{Binding SendCommand}"
                CommandParameter="{Binding Draft}"
                HorizontalAlignment="Right" />
</StackPanel>
```

- Bind `Value`, not the text, because the text alone loses the mentions. `People` and `Channels` are one-way.
- Use `SubmitCommand` or the `Submitted` event for the send action. The command runs only when its `CanExecute` returns
  `true` for the submitted value.
- Use `MentionAdded` for side effects of choosing a person or a channel, and `ValueChanged` for anything that depends on
  the whole text.

### Prefilled value

Set `Value` with the text and its mentions. Each offset points at the trigger character (`Start`) and just after the
label (`End`). Editing around a mention moves it: typing before it shifts both offsets. Editing inside it removes the
mention, and its text stays in the field as plain text.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             xmlns:demos="using:TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.MentionInputPrefilledDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="14">
        <arc:MentionInput x:Name="Input"
                          Label="Review note"
                          People="{x:Static demos:MentionDemoData.People}"
                          Channels="{x:Static demos:MentionDemoData.Channels}"
                          Width="440"
                          HorizontalAlignment="Center" />
        <TextBlock x:Name="Count"
                   FontSize="13"
                   TextWrapping="Wrap"
                   HorizontalAlignment="Center"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class MentionInputPrefilledDemo : UserControl
{
    public MentionInputPrefilledDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        const string text = "Thanks @Maya Chen, the new flow reads well. Can @Jordan Lee review it in #design before Friday?";
        Input.Value = new MentionValue(text,
        [
            Find(text, MentionKind.Person, "u_maya", "Maya Chen"),
            Find(text, MentionKind.Person, "u_jordan", "Jordan Lee"),
            Find(text, MentionKind.Channel, "c_design", "design")
        ]);
        Count.Text = Summary(Input.Value);
        Input.ValueChanged += (_, e) => Count.Text = Summary(e.NewValue);
    }

    private static Mention Find(string text, MentionKind kind, string id, string label)
    {
        var token = MentionSerializer.MentionText(kind, label);
        var start = text.IndexOf(token, StringComparison.Ordinal);
        return new Mention(kind, id, label, start, start + token.Length);
    }

    private static string Summary(MentionValue value) => value.Mentions.Count switch
    {
        0 => "No mentions",
        1 => "1 mention: " + value.Mentions[0].Text,
        _ => $"{value.Mentions.Count} mentions: " + string.Join(", ", value.Mentions.Select(static m => m.Text))
    };
}
```

```csharp
var text = "Thanks @Maya Chen. Can @Jordan Lee review it in #design?";
comment.Value = new MentionValue(text,
[
    new Mention(MentionKind.Person, "u_maya", "Maya Chen", 7, 17),
    new Mention(MentionKind.Person, "u_jordan", "Jordan Lee", 24, 34),
    new Mention(MentionKind.Channel, "c_design", "design", 47, 54)
]);
```

Compute the offsets from the text when it comes from a template, because a wrong offset attaches the mention to the
wrong characters.

### Submit on Enter

With `IsSubmitOnEnter` set to `True`, Enter submits and Shift+Enter adds a line. With the default `False`, Enter adds a
line and the send action is a button. Enter never submits while an input method is composing, so a candidate can be
confirmed with Enter. A blank value does not submit. While the suggestion list has results, Enter chooses the
highlighted row instead, so a half-typed mention is never sent.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             xmlns:demos="using:TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.MentionInputSubmitOnEnterDemo">
    <UserControl.Styles>
        <Style Selector="TextBlock.sent">
            <Setter Property="FontSize" Value="13" />
            <Setter Property="TextWrapping" Value="Wrap" />
            <Setter Property="Foreground" Value="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
        </Style>
    </UserControl.Styles>
    <StackPanel Spacing="14">
        <arc:MentionInput x:Name="Input"
                          Label="Message"
                          Placeholder="Message #design"
                          IsSubmitOnEnter="True"
                          People="{x:Static demos:MentionDemoData.People}"
                          Channels="{x:Static demos:MentionDemoData.Channels}"
                          Width="440"
                          HorizontalAlignment="Center"
                          Submitted="OnSubmitted" />
        <StackPanel x:Name="Log" Spacing="6" Width="440" HorizontalAlignment="Center">
            <TextBlock x:Name="Empty"
                       Text="Sent messages show up here."
                       FontSize="13"
                       TextWrapping="Wrap"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
        </StackPanel>
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class MentionInputSubmitOnEnterDemo : UserControl
{
    public MentionInputSubmitOnEnterDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
    }

    private void OnSubmitted(object? sender, MentionSubmittedEventArgs e)
    {
        Log.Children.Remove(Empty);
        var mentions = e.Value.Mentions.Count == 1 ? "1 mention" : $"{e.Value.Mentions.Count} mentions";
        Log.Children.Add(new TextBlock { Text = $"Sent: {e.Value.Text.Trim()}  ·  {mentions}", Classes = { "sent" } });
        Input.Clear();
    }
}
```

```csharp
message.IsSubmitOnEnter = true;

{
    Console.WriteLine($"{e.Value.Text} ({e.Value.Mentions.Count} mentions)");
    message.Clear();
};
```

### Lines and growth

`MinLines` and `MaxLines` set the height range in lines. The field starts at `MinLines` and grows one 24 px line at a
time as the text wraps or new lines are typed, up to `MaxLines`. Past that height the editor scrolls inside the frame
with the scrollbar hidden, so the composer does not push the rest of the page down. The defaults are 1 and 8.

A thread composer typically uses `MinLines="2"` and `MaxLines="6"`.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             xmlns:demos="using:TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.MentionInputGrowthDemo">
    <arc:MentionInput Label="Notes"
                      Placeholder="Write a few lines. Shift+Enter is not needed here: Enter adds a line."
                      MinLines="2"
                      MaxLines="4"
                      People="{x:Static demos:MentionDemoData.People}"
                      Channels="{x:Static demos:MentionDemoData.Channels}"
                      Width="440"
                      HorizontalAlignment="Center" />
</UserControl>
```

### Size and placement

`SuggestionPlacement` sets where the list opens. `Auto` (the default) opens below the line and flips above it when
there is less than 300 px below and more room above. `Top` and `Bottom` always use the chosen side.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             xmlns:demos="using:TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.MentionInputPlacementDemo">
    <arc:MentionInput Label="Reply"
                      Placeholder="Suggestions open above. Try @ or #"
                      SuggestionPlacement="Top"
                      People="{x:Static demos:MentionDemoData.People}"
                      Channels="{x:Static demos:MentionDemoData.Channels}"
                      Width="440"
                      HorizontalAlignment="Center" />
</UserControl>
```

### Commands and events

`Insert`, `OpenSuggestions` and `Clear` act on the field from code. `Insert` types the text at the caret as if the
person typed it, so it joins the undo stack. `OpenSuggestions` types the trigger for a kind, adding a space first when
the character before the caret is not whitespace. `Clear` empties the value and resets the caret.

```csharp
button.Click += (_, _) => comment.OpenSuggestions(MentionKind.Person);

comment.MentionAdded += (_, e) => Console.WriteLine($"Added {e.Mention.Text}");
```

`ValueChanged` fires on every change to `Value` and carries the old and new values. `MentionAdded` fires only when a
suggestion becomes a mention.

### Disabled

The whole field fades to 55% and takes no input. Its text and mentions stay readable.

```xml
             xmlns:demos="using:TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos"

                      Label="Locked comment"
                      IsEnabled="False"

                      Channels="{x:Static demos:MentionDemoData.Channels}"
                      Width="440"
                      HorizontalAlignment="Center" />
```

### Focus and dismissal

The suggestion list is a popup that closes on its own:

- **Escape** closes the list for the current trigger only. Typing more characters in the same query keeps it closed,
  and a new trigger after a space opens it again.
- **A press outside the field and the list** closes the list. Presses inside the field, such as moving the caret,
  do not.
- **Tab** chooses the highlighted suggestion while the list has results. Otherwise it moves focus.
- **A click on a row** keeps focus in the editor and places the caret after the token and its trailing space, so the
  person can continue typing. Undo (Ctrl+Z, Cmd+Z on macOS) takes the choice back, but not the mention object.

### Serialized output

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class MentionInputSerializedDemo : UserControl
{
    public MentionInputSerializedDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        const string text = "Ship notes are up, @Priya Natarajan. Posting in #engineering next.";
        var priya = text.IndexOf("@Priya Natarajan", StringComparison.Ordinal);
        var engineering = text.IndexOf("#engineering", StringComparison.Ordinal);
        Input.Value = new MentionValue(text,
        [
            new Mention(MentionKind.Person, "u_priya", "Priya Natarajan", priya, priya + "@Priya Natarajan".Length),
            new Mention(MentionKind.Channel, "c_engineering", "engineering", engineering, engineering + "#engineering".Length)
        ]);
        Output.Text = MentionSerializer.Serialize(Input.Value);
        Input.ValueChanged += (_, e) => Output.Text = MentionSerializer.Serialize(e.NewValue);
    }
}
```


`MentionSerializer.Serialize` turns the value into storage text. By default each person becomes `<@id>` and each
channel becomes `<#id>`, and the rest of the text is unchanged. Pass a format function to write another form, such as
a display name in brackets. Store the default form when names can change, because the stored text keeps pointing at
the same ID.

```csharp
var stored = MentionSerializer.Serialize(comment.Value);
// "Thanks <@u_maya>. Can <@u_jordan> review it in <#c_design>?"
```

### Example: incident reply thread

A reply box in the thread of an incident (`inc_2026_0412`, a duplicate charge on a Northwind order). The message being
answered sits above it for context. The reply mentions two people and one channel, each drawn as a token in the field. The primary action sits below the field on the right.

![An incident reply box with two person mentions and a channel mention](https://docs.tkcode.si/shots/Docs/SpecialInputs/MentionInput/images/ReplyThread.webp)

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             xmlns:generic="using:System.Collections.Generic">
    <StackPanel Width="600" Spacing="14">
        <StackPanel Spacing="4">
            <TextBlock Text="Duplicate charge on order NW-48213"
                       FontSize="14"
                       FontWeight="SemiBold"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
            <TextBlock Text="Priya Natarajan, 2 hours ago"
                       FontSize="12"

            <TextBlock Text="The card was charged twice at 09:14. The second charge is pending a refund."
                       FontSize="13"
                       TextWrapping="Wrap"
                       Margin="0,6,0,0"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
        </StackPanel>

            <arc:MentionInput.Value>
                <arc:MentionValue>
                    <x:Arguments>

                                    <arc:MentionKind>Person</arc:MentionKind>

                                </x:Arguments>
                            </arc:Mention>
                            <arc:Mention>

                                    <arc:MentionKind>Person</arc:MentionKind>

                                </x:Arguments>

                        </generic:List>

</UserControl>
```

A short reply keeps the two-line height that `MinLines` sets, so the box does not jump while typing.

### Content guidelines

- **Placeholder**: tell the person what the field is for and how to mention someone: "Leave a comment. Use @ to
  mention, # for a channel". Keep it to one line at the field's width.
- **Label**: a short noun phrase for assistive technology, such as "Reply to incident". It is not shown on screen.
- **Actions**: name the send action with a verb and object, "Post reply" or "Send message", not "Submit". Keep the
  empty-state copy ("No people match “{0}”") as the default, because it names the query.

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| Enter your comment here! | Leave a comment. Use @ to mention, # for a channel |
| Mention someone | Use @ to mention a person |
| Submit | Post reply |
| Mention (Maya Chen, Product designer) | Maya Chen |
| No results | No people match “zz” |

### Best practices

**Do**

- Store the `MentionValue`, or its serialized form, rather than the plain text, so the IDs survive edits and name
  changes.
- Set `MinLines` to the height of a typical reply and `MaxLines` to the space free below the field, so the composer
  does not move the page while the person types.
- Turn off a trigger with an empty collection when that kind of mention does not apply, so `@` or `#` stays plain text.
- Use stable IDs from your directory, not display names, so a renamed person keeps the same reference.

**Avoid**

- Storing only `Text`. The mentions then cannot be notified by ID or restored on the next edit.
- Using `IsSubmitOnEnter` in a document editor, where Enter must add a line. Use a button to send there.
- Loading a whole directory into `People`. The list shows the best matches only, so a large directory needs a search
  that updates `People` for each query.

### Common questions

**Why does Enter pick a suggestion instead of submitting?** While the list is open and has results, Enter and Tab choose
the highlighted row. Once the list closes (after a choice, Escape, or a space that ends the query), Enter submits.

**Why are my mentions missing after I undo?** Undo restores the typed text of a token, but not the mention object.
Handle `ValueChanged` and rebuild your own mention list from `NewValue` when undo must keep the mentions.


## API reference

### MentionInput

Arc's Mention input: an auto-growing text field with `@` people and `#` channel mentions that act as single tokens, with suggestions at the caret. The value is plain text plus structured mentions with offsets (`MentionValue`), ready to store (`MentionSerializer`) or to notify by id.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Value` | `MentionValue` | – | Defines the `Value` property. |
| `Mentions` | `IReadOnlyList<Mention>` | – | *Read-only.* Defines the `Mentions` property. |
| `People` | `IEnumerable<MentionPerson>?` | `null` | Defines the `People` property. |
| `Channels` | `IEnumerable<MentionChannel>?` | `null` | Defines the `Channels` property. |
| `IsSubmitOnEnter` | `bool` | `false` | Defines the `IsSubmitOnEnter` property. |
| `SubmitCommand` | `ICommand?` | `null` | Defines the `SubmitCommand` property. |
| `MinLines` | `int` | `1` | Defines the `MinLines` property. |
| `MaxLines` | `int` | `8` | Defines the `MaxLines` property. |
| `SuggestionPlacement` | `MentionSuggestionPlacement` | `Auto` | Defines the `SuggestionPlacement` property. |
| `MaxSuggestions` | `int` | `6` | Defines the `MaxSuggestions` property. |
| `Placeholder` | `string?` | `null` | Defines the `Placeholder` property. |
| `Label` | `string?` | `null` | Defines the `Label` property. |
| `NoPeopleMatchFormat` | `string` | `"No people match “{0}”"` | Defines the `NoPeopleMatchFormat` property. |
| `NoChannelsMatchFormat` | `string` | `"No channels match “{0}”"` | Defines the `NoChannelsMatchFormat` property. |
| `NoMatchesText` | `string` | `"No matches"` | Defines the `NoMatchesText` property. |
| `PeopleListName` | `string` | `"People"` | Defines the `PeopleListName` property. |
| `ChannelsListName` | `string` | `"Channels"` | Defines the `ChannelsListName` property. |
| `IsSuggestionsOpen` | `bool` | – | *Read-only.* Defines the `IsSuggestionsOpen` property. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ValueChanged` | `MentionInputValueChangedEventArgs` | Raised after `Value` changed (typing, choosing, programmatic). |
| `MentionAdded` | `MentionAddedEventArgs` | Raised when a suggestion becomes a mention (Arc `onMentionAdd`). |
| `Submitted` | `MentionSubmittedEventArgs` | Raised when Enter submits (with `IsSubmitOnEnter`, Arc `onSubmit`). |

Pseudo-classes: `:suggestions-open`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.
### MentionPerson

A person offered after `@`.
### MentionChannel

A channel offered after `#`.

`Mention` is the unit of the value; `Start` and `End` are character offsets into `Text`.

| Member | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `Kind` | `MentionKind` | `Person` (`@`) or `Channel` (`#`) |
| `Id` | `string` | The ID of the person or channel, for storage and notifications |
| `Label` | `string` | The name shown after the trigger character |
| `Start` | `int` | Offset of the trigger character |
| `End` | `int` | Offset just after the label (end exclusive) |
| `Text` | `string` | The token text: `@Label` or `#Label` |

## Accessibility

- The editor is a combo box with list autocomplete. `Label` names it; when `Label` is null, the control's
  `AutomationProperties.Name` is used instead.
- The suggestion list is named by `PeopleListName` (People) or `ChannelsListName` (Channels). Each row reads its name
  and role or description, for example "Maya Chen, Product designer".
- The result count is announced politely ("3 people", "1 channel", "No matches") and clears when the list closes.
- Mention colors come from a hidden layer, so assistive technology reads the plain text.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `@` or `#` after a space, a line start, or an opening bracket or quote | Opens the people or channel suggestions |
| `Down` / `Up` | Moves the highlight through the suggestions and wraps at the ends (list open) |
| `Enter` / `Tab` | Chooses the highlighted suggestion when the list has results |
| `Escape` | Closes the list for the current trigger only |
| `Enter` | Submits when `IsSubmitOnEnter` is `True` and the text is not blank; otherwise adds a line |
| `Shift+Enter` | Adds a line |
| `Left` / `Right` | Moves the caret one character, or hops over a whole mention token |
| `Backspace` / `Delete` next to a mention | Removes the whole token in one keystroke |
| `Ctrl+Z` / `Ctrl+Y` (`Cmd+Z` / `Cmd+Shift+Z` on macOS) | Undo and redo, including a choice made from the list |

Enter never submits during IME composition.

## Motion

- The field follows its content on a smooth spring, the suggestion panel opens from the caret with a small scale, and the
  highlight glides between rows. Reduced motion jumps the height and the highlight, and the panel only fades.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| Field height follows the text | Smooth spring | Jumps to the new height | Immediate |
| Suggestion panel opens | Small scale from the caret, snappy | Fades in, no scale | Immediate |
| Highlight moves between rows | Glides in 0.3 s with a slight bounce | Jumps | Immediate |
| Panel height when results change | Spring | Jumps | Immediate |
| Border on focus | Border color crossfades | Short fade | Immediate |

## Related

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `Textarea` | The text is several lines of plain text with no people or channels to reference |
| `Input` / `SearchField` | The value is one line, such as a name or a search query |
| `TagInput` | The values are a list of chips that stand apart from the sentence |
| `Select` / `Combobox` | The person must pick one value from a full list rather than mention it in text |
| `Field` + `FieldFrame` | You build your own editor and want the same label, frame and message rows |

# Shortcut recorder

> Record key combinations into key caps, with conflict warnings, Kbd, and a searchable cheatsheet.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/shortcut-recorder

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ShortcutRecorderDefaultDemo">
    <arc:ShortcutRecorder x:Name="Recorder"
                          Label="Command palette"
                          Width="320"
                          HorizontalAlignment="Center" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class ShortcutRecorderDefaultDemo : UserControl
{
    public ShortcutRecorderDefaultDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        var palette = ShortcutFormatter.Parse("mod+k", ShortcutFormatter.CurrentPlatform);
        Recorder.Value = palette;
        Recorder.ResetValue = palette;
    }
}
```

## When to use

`ShortcutRecorder` lets a person set a keyboard shortcut by pressing it, instead of typing a key name. It sits in a
settings page beside the other preferences, and it shows the result as key caps that match the platform. Behind the
field it checks the combination against the shortcuts the app already uses and against the combinations that browsers
and operating systems keep, so a remapping cannot silently break a command.

- **Shortcut settings in a productivity app**: a person remaps "Open file" from Ctrl+O to Ctrl+Shift+O. The recorder
  records the chord, warns if Ctrl+Shift+O already runs "Export report", and stores the result as a `KeyGesture`.
- **Keyboard maps in a developer tool or an IDE**: a terminal, an editor or a query console where the user rebinds
  "Run query" or "Comment line". `Bindings` holds the app's current map, so every conflict is caught at record time.
- **Help dialogs and cheatsheets that show the live binding**: the shortcut text beside a command comes from the stored
  `Value`, so a remapped shortcut shows the new keys everywhere.
- **Admin consoles with keyboard-first operators**: a dispatch or support tool where agents use shortcuts for triage.
  The recorder lets a supervisor change them without an editor for key names.
- **Reset to defaults in a preferences screen**: `ResetValue` is the default shortcut, and the reset button returns the
  field to it when the value differs.

## When not to use

- **A fixed shortcut that is only shown**: display it with your own text or a key cap control, because no one is
  remapping it.
- **Running an action by name**: use the command palette pattern from the `Blocks` and command components, which finds
  an action by its name and does not depend on a key chord.
- **Touch-only products**: there is no physical keyboard to record, and a tap would never produce a chord.
- **A text value with no key semantics**: use `Input`, for example for a macro name, a tag or a note about a shortcut.
- **Free text that a person types into a search box**: use `SearchField`; the recorder takes the whole chord and does not
  edit text.

## Usage

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:ShortcutRecorder Label="Command palette"
                          Description="Opens the command palette from anywhere in the app." />
</UserControl>
```

Click the field or press Enter, then press the combination. The recorder stores a `KeyGesture`, and it draws the gesture
as key caps.

`ShortcutRecorder` derives from `TemplatedControl`. Its frame is the Arc field frame, the same frame as `Input`, and the
recording surface inside it is a button that draws its own key caps, recording light and placeholder. The recorder is
therefore a value editor with the label, the frame and the message row of a field, plus the recording behavior of a
toggle button.

### Anatomy

1. **Label** (`Label`): the field's name above the frame. `IsLabelVisible="False"` hides it, and assistive technology still
   reads it.
2. **Frame**: the Arc field frame at the medium control height (44 px in the default theme). Hover and focus outline it in
   the foreground color. While recording the surface takes a 4 percent accent tint, and a conflict uses a warning edge.
3. **Recording surface**: fills the row, with 6 px of padding on the right and 9 px on the left. It is the element that
   takes focus and starts recording.
4. **Key caps**: one cap per key of the shortcut, with a minimum size of 26 by 26 px, an 8 px corner radius and 4 px between
   caps. On a Mac the caps show glyphs (⌃ ⌥ ⇧ ⌘); elsewhere they show names (Ctrl, Alt, Shift).
5. **Recording light and placeholder**: a 7 px dot while recording, next to `RecordingPlaceholder` ("Press keys" by
   default). `Placeholder` ("Record shortcut") shows while there is no shortcut.
6. **Clear button** (`ClearText`, "Clear shortcut"): a 32 px square with a 16 px glyph. It shows while a shortcut is set and
   the field is not recording.
7. **Reset button**: a 32 px square with the same glyph. It shows when the value differs from `ResetValue`, and it restores
   `ResetValue`.
8. **Message row**: 12 px copy under the frame. It shows one message at a time, in this order: a conflict (with a 6 px
   warning dot and the links `UseAnywayText` and `CancelText`), the modifier nudge, the recording hint
   ("Esc to cancel, Backspace to clear") and then `Description`.

### Value and reset

`Value` is the recorded `KeyGesture`, or `null` when there is no shortcut. It is two-way. `ResetValue` is what the reset
button restores. Avalonia has no default value, so `ResetValue` is `null` unless you set it; a field whose value is set but
whose reset value is `null` shows its reset button as "Reset to none".

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ShortcutRecorderEmptyDemo">
    <arc:ShortcutRecorder Label="Start dictation"
                          Width="320"
                          HorizontalAlignment="Center" />
</UserControl>
```

```csharp
var palette = new ShortcutRecorder
{
    Label = "Command palette",
    Value = ShortcutFormatter.Parse("mod+k", ShortcutPlatform.Other),
    ResetValue = ShortcutFormatter.Parse("mod+k", ShortcutPlatform.Other)
};
```

`mod` means Command on macOS and Control on other platforms. Use `ShortcutFormatter.Parse` to create a gesture from that
text, or `ShortcutFormatter.TryParse` when the text comes from a settings file and may be invalid. `Parse` throws a
`FormatException` for text that is not a shortcut with exactly one key.

### Known shortcuts and conflicts

`Bindings` lists the shortcuts the app already uses, as `ShortcutBinding` objects with a `Gesture` and a `Label`. Recording
one of them shows a conflict with two real buttons, Use anyway and Cancel. Use anyway takes the shortcut and reports the
binding it came from in `ValueChanged`, so the app can remove that binding from its own map. Cancel keeps the previous
shortcut.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ShortcutRecorderConflictsDemo">
    <arc:ShortcutRecorder x:Name="Recorder"
                          Label="Quick search"
                          Width="320"
                          HorizontalAlignment="Center" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Input;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class ShortcutRecorderConflictsDemo : UserControl
{
    public ShortcutRecorderConflictsDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        var platform = ShortcutFormatter.CurrentPlatform;
        string Caps(KeyGesture gesture) => ShortcutFormatter.Format(gesture, platform).Text;

        var quickSearch = ShortcutFormatter.Parse("mod+p", platform);
        var save = ShortcutFormatter.Parse("mod+s", platform);
        var find = ShortcutFormatter.Parse("mod+f", platform);

        Recorder.Value = quickSearch;
        Recorder.ResetValue = quickSearch;
        Recorder.Bindings.Add(new ShortcutBinding(save, "Save"));
        Recorder.Bindings.Add(new ShortcutBinding(find, "Find"));
        Recorder.Description = $"Try {Caps(save)} or {Caps(find)}: both are already bound.";
    }
}
```

Reserved combinations, such as Ctrl+W to close a tab, Ctrl+T for a new tab, Ctrl+C and Ctrl+V for copy and paste, Ctrl+Z
for undo and Ctrl+A for select all, also warn. They are checked after `Bindings`. A reserved combination that is taken
with Use anyway reports no replaced binding, because nothing in the app owns it. Set `IsReservedWarningEnabled` to `False`
only when the app owns those combinations and the warning would be noise.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ShortcutRecorderReservedDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="24" HorizontalAlignment="Center">
        <arc:ShortcutRecorder x:Name="Sidebar"
                              Label="Toggle sidebar"
                              Width="320" />
        <arc:ShortcutRecorder x:Name="Duplicate"
                              Label="Duplicate line"
                              IsReservedWarningEnabled="False"
                              Description="IsReservedWarningEnabled = false: reserved combinations record directly."
                              Width="320" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Input;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class ShortcutRecorderReservedDemo : UserControl
{
    public ShortcutRecorderReservedDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        var platform = ShortcutFormatter.CurrentPlatform;
        string Caps(KeyGesture gesture) => ShortcutFormatter.Format(gesture, platform).Text;

        var toggleSidebar = ShortcutFormatter.Parse("mod+b", platform);
        var duplicateLine = ShortcutFormatter.Parse("mod+d", platform);
        var closeTab = ShortcutFormatter.Parse("mod+w", platform);
        var copy = ShortcutFormatter.Parse("mod+c", platform);

        Sidebar.Value = toggleSidebar;
        Sidebar.ResetValue = toggleSidebar;
        Sidebar.Description = $"Try {Caps(closeTab)} or {Caps(copy)}.";
        Duplicate.Value = duplicateLine;
        Duplicate.ResetValue = duplicateLine;
    }
}
```

### Modifiers and platform

`IsModifierRequired` is `True` by default: a bare letter is not a shortcut, so the recorder shows the nudge "Include
Ctrl or Alt" (or "Include ⌘, ⌃, or ⌥" on a Mac) and waits for a modifier. Function keys are always allowed. Set it to
`False` for a single-key shortcut, such as a "?" help key or a number key that switches a view.

`Platform` sets the cap style and the meaning of `mod`: `ShortcutPlatform.Mac` shows glyphs and uses Command for `mod`,
and `ShortcutPlatform.Other` shows names and uses Control. Leave it `null` to detect the running platform, which is what
a desktop app wants. Set it explicitly in a settings screen that must show the same caps on every machine, or in a
screenshot.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ShortcutRecorderNoModifierDemo">
    <arc:ShortcutRecorder Label="Next conversation"
                          Value="J"
                          ResetValue="J"
                          IsModifierRequired="False"
                          Description="Single keys are allowed here; Escape still cancels."
                          Width="320"
                          HorizontalAlignment="Center" />
</UserControl>
```

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ShortcutRecorderPlatformsDemo">
    <WrapPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center" ItemSpacing="12" LineSpacing="12">
        <arc:ShortcutRecorder Label="Mac"
                              Platform="Mac"
                              Value="Cmd+Shift+K"
                              ResetValue="Cmd+Shift+K"
                              Width="320" />
        <arc:ShortcutRecorder Label="Windows and Linux"
                              Platform="Other"
                              Value="Ctrl+Shift+K"
                              ResetValue="Ctrl+Shift+K"
                              Width="320" />
    </WrapPanel>
</UserControl>
```

### Events

`ValueChanged` is raised when `Value` changes: a recorded shortcut, a cleared one, a reset, or a value set from code. Its
arguments carry the old and the new `KeyGesture` and the `Replaced` binding. `Replaced` holds the binding that a Use anyway
took the shortcut from, and it is `null` for every other change.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ShortcutRecorderEventsDemo">
    <UserControl.Styles>
        <Style Selector="TextBlock.log">
            <Setter Property="FontSize" Value="13" />
            <Setter Property="FontFamily" Value="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource MonoFontFamily}" />
            <Setter Property="Foreground" Value="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
        </Style>
    </UserControl.Styles>
    <StackPanel Spacing="16" HorizontalAlignment="Center">
        <arc:ShortcutRecorder x:Name="Recorder"
                              Label="Command palette"
                              Width="320"
                              HorizontalAlignment="Left" />
        <StackPanel x:Name="Log" Spacing="4">
            <TextBlock x:Name="Hint"
                       Text="Record a shortcut to see ValueChanged."
                       FontSize="13"
                       FontFamily="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource MonoFontFamily}"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
        </StackPanel>
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Input;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class ShortcutRecorderEventsDemo : UserControl
{
    public ShortcutRecorderEventsDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        var platform = ShortcutFormatter.CurrentPlatform;
        var palette = ShortcutFormatter.Parse("mod+k", platform);
        Recorder.Value = palette;
        Recorder.ResetValue = palette;
        Recorder.Bindings.Add(new ShortcutBinding(ShortcutFormatter.Parse("mod+s", platform), "Save"));
        Recorder.ValueChanged += OnValueChanged;
    }

    private void OnValueChanged(object? sender, ShortcutRecorderValueChangedEventArgs e)
    {
        var platform = Recorder.EffectivePlatform;
        string Show(KeyGesture? gesture) => gesture is null ? "none" : ShortcutFormatter.Format(gesture, platform).Text;

        var line = $"ValueChanged {Show(e.OldValue)} → {Show(e.NewValue)}";
        if (e.Replaced is { } replaced)
        {
            line += $" (replaced {replaced.Label})";
        }
        Log.Children.Remove(Hint);
        Log.Children.Insert(0, new TextBlock { Text = line, Classes = { "log" } });
        while (Log.Children.Count > 6)
        {
            Log.Children.RemoveAt(Log.Children.Count - 1);
        }
    }
}
```

```csharp
recorder.ValueChanged += (_, e) =>
{
    var replaced = e.Replaced is { } binding ? $" (replaced {binding.Label})" : string.Empty;
    Console.WriteLine($"{e.OldValue} -> {e.NewValue}{replaced}");
};
```

### Binding to a view model

A settings view model owns the map of shortcuts. Each row binds `Value` two-way to its own gesture, and the recorder's
`Bindings` list is the other shortcuts of the map. The example uses CommunityToolkit.Mvvm.

```csharp
public partial class ShortcutSettingsViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    public ShortcutSettingsViewModel()
    {
        Shortcuts.Add(new ShortcutBinding(ShortcutFormatter.Parse("ctrl+p", ShortcutPlatform.Other), "Quick open"));
        Shortcuts.Add(new ShortcutBinding(ShortcutFormatter.Parse("ctrl+s", ShortcutPlatform.Other), "Save"));
    }

    public ObservableCollection<ShortcutBinding> Shortcuts { get; } = new();

    [ObservableProperty]
    private KeyGesture? _openFile = ShortcutFormatter.Parse("ctrl+o", ShortcutPlatform.Other);

    [RelayCommand]
    private void ResetOpenFile() => OpenFile = ShortcutFormatter.Parse("ctrl+o", ShortcutPlatform.Other);
}
```

```xml
<arc:ShortcutRecorder Label="Open file"
                      Value="{Binding OpenFile, Mode=TwoWay}"
                      Bindings="{Binding Shortcuts}"
                      ResetValue="Ctrl+O"
                      Platform="Other" />
```

`Value` is two-way. `Bindings` is a list the field reads when a person records, so bind it to the map the app uses.
`ValueChanged` is an event, so connect it in code-behind when the app must remove the replaced binding from its own map.
`IsRecording` is read-only, and `StartRecording()` and `StopRecording()` start and stop the recorder from code.
