# Combobox

> Search and select from a list without leaving the field.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/combobox

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ComboboxSearchableDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12">
        <arc:Combobox x:Name="Zone"
                      Label="Time zone"
                      HorizontalAlignment="Left"
                      Description="Search by city, zone name or offset."
                      Width="320" />
        <TextBlock FontSize="13"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}"
                   Text="{Binding #Zone.SelectedValue, StringFormat='Value: {0}', TargetNullValue='Value: none'}" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Pages;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class ComboboxSearchableDemo : UserControl
{
    public ComboboxSearchableDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        // Keywords are matched by the search but not shown.
        Zone.ItemsSource = SelectsDemoData.Cities.Select(c => new SelectOption(c.City, c.City)
        {
            Keywords = $"{c.Zone} {SelectsDemoData.Utc(c.Offset)}"
        }).ToArray();
    }
}
```

## When to use

`Combobox` is a single-value picker for a list that is too long to scan, where people already know the name of the
thing they want. It sits in a form like an input: a visible label, a 44 px field and a description, with the list
opening under the field while the person types. Use it wherever the list is long enough that scrolling costs more than
typing.

- **Time zones and countries in account settings**: a team sets its default time zone or its billing country from a
  list of IANA zones. People type "berlin", "new york" or "UTC+01" and get the match in one step.
- **Account owners and assignees in a CRM or a helpdesk**: an opportunity owner or a ticket assignee is picked from the
  team directory. `Keywords` let a person find "Priya Raman" by her email alias or her team name.
- **Product and SKU lookup in an order editor**: a line item needs one product from a catalog. Keywords hold the SKU
  and old product names, so a search for the discontinued name still lands on the current item.
- **Ledger and cost-center selection in finance tools**: an expense report needs one cost center from a few hundred.
  Disabled options remain visible so a person sees that a center exists but is closed to new spend.
- **Developer tools that pick a target**: a deployment form picks one environment or one region from a long list.
  Search narrows it, and the chosen label stays in the field as the value people read.

## When not to use

- **A short, fixed list that needs no typing**: use `Select`. Three to seven options read faster in a list than behind
  a search field.
- **Choosing several values**: use `MultiSelect`, which keeps every choice visible as a token and never closes after a
  pick.
- **Facets that people switch often**: use `ChipGroup`, where every option is visible and one click changes the
  filter.
- **A search that navigates content rather than setting a value**: use `ExpandingSearch` in a header, which opens
  results rather than filling a field.
- **Free text that is not chosen from a list**: use `Input`. A combobox only holds values from its items.

## Usage

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:Combobox Label="Framework"
                  Width="280"
                  Description="Type to search.">
        <arc:SelectItem Content="Avalonia" Keywords="xaml dotnet" />
        <arc:SelectItem Content="AtomUI" Keywords="ant design" />
        <arc:SelectItem Content="MAUI" Keywords="xamarin" IsEnabled="False" />
        <arc:SelectItem Content="WinUI" />
    </arc:Combobox>
</UserControl>
```

`Combobox` derives from Avalonia's `SelectingItemsControl`, so `ItemsSource`, `Items`, `SelectedItem`, `SelectedIndex`,
`SelectedValue`, `Selection` and `SelectionChanged` behave as they do in a list box, and the chosen item is always one
of the items. What the control adds is the field: a text input that filters the list, the label and description rows,
the popup list and the clear button. Inside a `SelectingItemsControl` each `SelectItem` is one option, and `Keywords`
on it are searched but never shown.

### Anatomy

1. **Label** (`Label`): a visible label above the field in the small type size, medium weight, 8 px above the field.
   It also names the field and its list for assistive technology.
2. **Field**: 44 px high (the medium control size), 1 px border with the control radius, the surface color and 12 px of
   horizontal padding. Hover and focus change its colors, not its size.
3. **Text input**: shows the query while the list is open. While the list is closed it shows the chosen label, never
   the value.
4. **Placeholder** (`Placeholder`): the default text is "Search or select…". While the person is searching, the chosen
   label stays in the field as muted copy, so the current choice is not lost.
5. **Clear button**: a 22 px button that appears while something is selected. It removes the selection and the query.
6. **Description** (`Description`): the muted helper line under the field, 12 px in the muted text color.
7. **List** (popup): opens 8 px under the field, with the panel radius, 5 px of inner padding and option rows 36 px high.
   The list is at most 300 px tall, and never more than 40% of the window height (`MaxDropDownHeight`).
8. **Status row** (`EmptyText`): the result count below the options, or the empty text ("No matches found" by default)
   when nothing matches. It uses the small type size in the muted color.

### Choosing the data

The field is the same whether the list has five options or five hundred. The difference is in the item data:

- Use `SelectItem` children for a short, static list defined in XAML, as in the usage example.
- Use `ItemsSource` with `SelectOption` records for a list from code or a view model. `SelectOption` takes a value and a
  label, `IsDisabled` marks a shown but unavailable option, and `Keywords` adds the terms the search matches.
- Set `TextSelector` and `ValueSelector` when the items are your own objects, so the label and the stored value come
  from properties rather than from `ToString()`.

```csharp
var zone = new Combobox
{
    Label = "Time zone",
    Width = 320,
    ItemsSource = cities.Select(c => new SelectOption(c.City, c.City)
    {
        Keywords = $"{c.Zone} {c.Offset}"
    }).ToArray()
};
zone.SelectionChanged += (_, _) => Console.WriteLine(zone.SelectedValue);
```

### Binding to a view model

With CommunityToolkit.Mvvm, the view model owns the value and the list of options, and the combobox edits both through
bindings. The value is the stored identifier, and the label is shown to people.

```csharp
public partial class TeamSettingsViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    public IReadOnlyList<SelectOption> Owners { get; }

    [ObservableProperty]
    private string? _ownerId;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private string? _timeZoneId = "europe-berlin";

    public TeamSettingsViewModel(IDirectoryService directory)
    {
        Owners = directory.ListMembers()
            .Select(m => new SelectOption(m.Id, m.DisplayName) { Keywords = m.Email })
            .ToArray();
    }

    [RelayCommand]
    private async Task SaveAsync()
    {
        if (OwnerId is null)
        {
            return;
        }
        await _settings.SaveAsync(OwnerId, TimeZoneId);
    }
}
```

```xml
<StackPanel Width="360" Spacing="16">
    <arc:Combobox Label="Account owner"
                  Placeholder="Search people"
                  ItemsSource="{Binding Owners}"
                  SelectedValue="{Binding OwnerId, Mode=TwoWay}" />
    <arc:Combobox Label="Default time zone"
                  ItemsSource="{Binding TimeZones}"
                  SelectedValue="{Binding TimeZoneId, Mode=TwoWay}" />
    <arc:Button Content="Save settings" Command="{Binding SaveCommand}" />
</StackPanel>
```

- `SelectedValue` is two-way and holds `null` while nothing is chosen. Bind it with `Mode=TwoWay` so the view model
  receives the choice and can set the field from code.
- `SelectedText` is read-only and holds the label of the selection. Show it in a summary line rather than binding it
  back.
- `IsOpen` is two-way. Set it from code only when a command needs to close the list before it navigates away.
- Do not bind `SelectedIndex` for a value that comes from a database. Indexes change when the list is reloaded, so bind
  the value instead.

### Searching and filtering

By default the search matches the label, the meta and the keywords as case-insensitive substrings, and the result list
keeps the order of the items. `SearchText` reports the current query, which is empty when the list is closed.

Set `FilterPredicate` to change the match. It receives the source item and the trimmed query, and it runs for every
item on each keystroke, so keep it cheap.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ComboboxCustomFilterDemo">
    <arc:Combobox x:Name="Prefix"
                  Label="Starts with"
                  HorizontalAlignment="Center"
                  Description="A custom FilterPredicate matches the start of the label only."
                  Width="280" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Pages;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class ComboboxCustomFilterDemo : UserControl
{
    public ComboboxCustomFilterDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Prefix.ItemsSource = SelectsDemoData.Cities.Select(c => c.City).ToArray();
        Prefix.FilterPredicate = (item, query) =>
            item is string label && label.StartsWith(query, StringComparison.CurrentCultureIgnoreCase);
    }
}
```

```csharp
combo.FilterPredicate = (item, query) =>
    item is SelectOption option && option.Label.StartsWith(query, StringComparison.CurrentCultureIgnoreCase);
```

Use a prefix match for lists people scan by their first letters, such as a list of countries. Keep the default
substring match for names and aliases, where "york" should find "New York" in the middle of the words.

### Placeholder, empty text and status

`Placeholder` is shown in the empty field. `EmptyText` is the status row when nothing matches, and it should name the
thing that was searched, such as "No time zone matches." Keep the status row short, because it is announced when it
appears.

```xml
<arc:Combobox Label="Country"
              Placeholder="Search countries"
              EmptyText="No country matches." />
```

### Clearing and focus

`Clear()` removes the selection and the query, and the clear button does the same when a person presses it. Focus goes
to the field with `FocusInput()`, which opens the list, as it does when a person tabs into the field.

```csharp
zone.Clear();
zone.FocusInput();
```

Clearing is the right answer when the empty state is valid, for example a filter that can match everything. For a
required value, do not clear the field on a save; keep the value and show the message beside the field.

### Validation

The combobox has no message row of its own. Its `Description` is the place for a constraint that is always true ("Used
for report schedules."). For a rule that can fail, place a `TextBlock` below the field, bind its text to the view model's
error, and use the text color of the danger token. Check the rule when the list closes, not on each keystroke, so the
message does not appear while the person is still searching.

| Rule | When to check | Where it shows |
|---|---|---|
| A value is required | On save, or when the list closes with no value | A message below the field, with the focus moved to it |
| The value is still available | On save, because an option can be disabled later | A message below the field that names the option |
| The owner must belong to the team | On the server response | The same message row, cleared when the value changes |

### Inline options and disabled options

Disabled options show in the list but cannot be picked. The arrow keys skip them. Use this for an option that exists but
is not available to the person, such as a closed cost center. Explain the reason in the option label or in the
description, not only by graying the row.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ComboboxInlineOptionsDemo">
    <arc:Combobox Label="Framework"
                  HorizontalAlignment="Center"
                  Width="280"
                  SelectedIndex="0">
        <arc:SelectItem Content="Avalonia" Keywords="xaml dotnet" />
        <arc:SelectItem Content="AtomUI" Keywords="ant design" />
        <arc:SelectItem Content="MAUI" Keywords="xamarin" IsEnabled="False" />
        <arc:SelectItem Content="WinUI" />
        <arc:SelectItem Content="Uno Platform" />
    </arc:Combobox>
</UserControl>
```

```xml
<arc:SelectItem Content="MAUI" Keywords="xamarin" IsEnabled="False" />
```

### Disabled

A disabled `Combobox` keeps its value and ignores input. It cannot open, so the person can still read the value but not
change it. Use it when a value is set by a policy, such as a fiscal year that cannot change after the workspace is
created, and say why in the description.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ComboboxDisabledDemo">
    <arc:Combobox Label="Country"
                  HorizontalAlignment="Center"
                  Width="280"
                  IsEnabled="False"
                  SelectedIndex="0">
        <arc:SelectItem Content="Sweden" />
    </arc:Combobox>
</UserControl>
```

### Example: team settings form

A team settings form in an admin console. The owner field is a searchable list of people with keywords for their email
addresses, so a person can type a surname or a domain. The time zone field is closed with a value chosen, and the
fiscal year field is disabled with a reason in its description. The labels are nouns, the placeholder names what to
search for, and the descriptions state the effect of each choice.

![A team settings form with a searchable owner field, a time zone and a disabled fiscal year field](https://docs.tkcode.si/shots/Docs/Selects/Combobox/images/TeamSettings.webp)

```xml
<StackPanel Width="560" Spacing="20">
    <arc:Combobox Label="Account owner"
                  Width="360"
                  Placeholder="Search people"
                  Description="Receives billing and security emails.">
        <arc:SelectItem Content="Priya Raman" Keywords="priya.raman@acme.com finance" />
        <arc:SelectItem Content="Marcus Hale" Keywords="marcus.hale@acme.com operations" />
        <arc:SelectItem Content="Elena Ruiz" Keywords="elena.ruiz@acme.com support" />
        <arc:SelectItem Content="Tomas Berg" Keywords="tomas.berg@acme.com engineering" />
    </arc:Combobox>
    <arc:Combobox Label="Default time zone"
                  Width="360"
                  SelectedIndex="1"
                  Description="Used for report schedules and invoice dates.">
        <arc:SelectItem Content="Pacific time (UTC-08:00)" Keywords="los angeles seattle" />
        <arc:SelectItem Content="Central European time (UTC+01:00)" Keywords="berlin paris rome" />
        <arc:SelectItem Content="Japan time (UTC+09:00)" Keywords="tokyo osaka" />
    </arc:Combobox>
    <arc:Combobox Label="Fiscal year starts"
                  Width="360"
                  IsEnabled="False"
                  SelectedIndex="0"
                  Description="Set when the workspace is created and cannot change.">
        <arc:SelectItem Content="January" />
        <arc:SelectItem Content="April" />
    </arc:Combobox>
    <StackPanel Orientation="Horizontal" Spacing="8" HorizontalAlignment="Right">
        <arc:Button Content="Cancel" Variant="Secondary" />
        <arc:Button Content="Save settings" />
    </StackPanel>
</StackPanel>
```

### Content guidelines

- **Label**: a noun naming the value, in sentence case, such as "Account owner" or "Default time zone". Do not add a
  colon or a question.
- **Placeholder**: the action and the object, such as "Search people" or "Search countries". It is not a restatement of
  the label.
- **Description**: one sentence on the effect of the choice, for example "Used for report schedules", or the reason an
  option cannot be chosen.
- **Empty text**: name what was searched and say that nothing matched. Keep it to one line.
- **Option labels**: the name people recognize, such as a full time zone name or a person's display name. Put aliases in
  `Keywords`, not in the label.

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| Select | Search people |
| Enter a value | Search or select |
| Nothing found | No time zone matches. |
| Owner: | Account owner |
| Click to choose the time zone | Choose a default time zone |

### Best practices

**Do**

- Use `Keywords` for the terms people actually type, such as an email alias, a city, a former product name or a region,
  so the match works without the label containing them.
- Bind the value (`SelectedValue`) rather than the index, so reloading the list does not change the selection.
- Keep the list sorted by the label people read, and filter by prefix only when the list is an ordered catalog.
- Show the chosen item in a summary when the choice changes a total or a schedule, so the effect is visible without
  reopening the list.

**Avoid**

- A combobox for three or four options. The search field adds a step where a `Select` list would show every choice.
- Hiding the reason an option is disabled. A person who cannot pick "MAUI" needs to know why.
- Replacing the items while a person is typing in the list. The list is rebuilt under the query, so the highlight can
  move to an option the person did not choose.
- Building `FilterPredicate` on expensive work such as a server request. It runs on every keystroke. Load the list from
  the server with a debounced query in the view model instead.
- Relying on the placeholder to say which field is required. Put a visible label above the field.

### Common questions

**Why does the field show the label and not the value?** `SelectedValue` is the stored identifier, and the field is the
text a person reads. While the list is closed, the field shows `SelectedText`. The value stays in the view model.

**What happens to the typed query when I press Escape?** The list closes, the query is dropped and the previous value
stays. The field shows the chosen label again.

**How do I move the highlight or pick an option with the keyboard?** Press `Down` to open the list, then `Down` and
`Up` to move the highlight, and `Enter` to pick it. The highlight wraps from the last option to the first. The disabled
options are skipped.

**Can I open the list from code?** Set `IsOpen` to `True` or call `FocusInput()`, which also moves focus into the field.
The list opens when the field gains focus or when a person types.

**Does focusing the field open the list?** Yes. Focus opens the list, and typing opens it too. `Enter` picks the
highlighted option and closes it, and `Tab` closes it and moves focus on.

## API reference

### Combobox

Arc combobox: a searchable single-choice field. Typing filters the options (label and keywords) and the list springs to its new height; arrow keys move a highlight while focus stays in the field, Enter picks, Escape closes and drops the query. The chosen label settles into the field from below; a clear button pops in while something is selected. Use it for long lists people know by name (time zones, countries).

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Label` | `string?` | `null` | Visible label above the field; also names the field and its list. |
| `Description` | `string?` | `null` | Muted hint under the field. |
| `Placeholder` | `string?` | `"Search or select…"` | Shown while the field is empty (Arc: "Search or select…"). While searching the chosen label takes its place. |
| `EmptyText` | `string?` | `"No matches found"` | Status row when nothing matches (Arc: "No matches found"). |
| `IsOpen` | `bool` | `false` | Whether the list is open (two-way). |
| `MaxDropDownHeight` | `double` | `300` | Tallest the list gets (Arc: min(300px, 40% of the window)). |
| `TextSelector` | `Func<object?, string?>?` | `null` | Label of a data item (AOT-safe alternative to `DisplayMemberBinding`). |
| `ValueSelector` | `Func<object?, object?>?` | `null` | Value of a data item (AOT-safe alternative to `SelectedValueBinding`). |
| `DisabledSelector` | `Func<object?, bool>?` | `null` | Returns true for data items that are shown but cannot be picked. |
| `FilterPredicate` | `Func<object?, string, bool>?` | `null` | Defines the `FilterPredicate` property. |
| `SearchText` | `string` | – | *Read-only.* Defines the `SearchText` property. |
| `SelectedText` | `string?` | – | *Read-only.* Label of the selected option, or null. |

Pseudo-classes: `:open`

Derives from `SelectingItemsControl`: every member of `SelectingItemsControl` works as well.

### SelectOption

A plain option record for `ItemsSource` lists that every select in this category understands without selectors: `new SelectOption("us", "United States")`.

## Accessibility

- `Label` names the field and its list. `Description` is the help text read after the name and the value.
- The field is exposed as a combo box. Its value is the chosen label, and its expanded state follows the list.
- Focus stays in the text input while the person moves the highlight with the arrow keys, so typing and navigating
  do not compete.
- The clear button is named "Clear selection". The status row under the options is a polite live region, so a change
  in the result count or the empty message is announced without moving focus.
- Caret, selection, IME composition and clipboard shortcuts are the native `TextBox` behavior.
- A focused field only strengthens its border (`BorderStrong`); there is no focus ring around it.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| Typing | Filters the options by label, meta and keywords; opens the list if it is closed |
| `Down` / `Up` | Opens the list if it is closed; otherwise moves the highlight to the next or previous enabled option, wrapping |
| `Enter` | Picks the highlighted option and closes the list; with no highlight it does nothing |
| `Escape` | Closes the list and drops the query; the chosen value stays |
| `Tab` | Closes the list and moves focus to the next control |
| Focus into the field | Opens the list |
| Pointer click on an option | Picks it and closes the list |

## Motion

- The list opens from above on a spring. Its height follows the number of matching results, so it grows and shrinks as
  the query changes.
- The chosen label rises into the field from below, 0.35em, and comes out of a soft blur.
- The clear button pops in while something is selected and scales down slightly when pressed.
- The status row under the options rises 4 px and fades in when the list has no matches.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| The list opens | Springs in from above | Fades in | Immediate |
| The result count changes | The list height follows on a smooth spring | The height changes at once | Immediate |
| A chosen label appears | Rises 0.35em from below out of a soft blur | Fades in | Immediate |
| The clear button appears | Pops in | Fades in | Immediate |
| The empty status row appears | Rises 4 px and fades in | Fades in | Immediate |

## Related

- `Select` for short fixed lists that people choose from without typing.
- `MultiSelect` when several values are chosen, and `ChipGroup` for facets that people switch often.
- `ExpandingSearch` when the search navigates content rather than setting a value.
- `Input` for free text that is not chosen from a list.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `Select` | The list is short and fixed, and people do not need to type |
| `MultiSelect` | Several values are chosen and each stays visible as a token |
| `ChipGroup` | A few facets are switched often and every option should stay visible |
| `ExpandingSearch` | The search opens results to read or navigate, not to set a field |
| `Input` | The value is free text rather than one of the items |
| `TagInput` | People create their own tags instead of picking existing options |

---

# Multi-select

> Select several values while keeping the field readable.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/multi-select

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.MultiSelectChipsDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12">
        <arc:MultiSelect x:Name="Labels"
                         Label="Labels"
                         HorizontalAlignment="Left"
                         Description="Shown on the issue card."
                         Width="320"
                         SelectionChanged="OnSelectionChanged">
            <arc:SelectItem Content="Bug" Value="bug" />
            <arc:SelectItem Content="Feature" Value="feature" />
            <arc:SelectItem Content="Documentation" Value="docs" />
            <arc:SelectItem Content="Performance" Value="perf" />
            <arc:SelectItem Content="Design" Value="design" />
            <arc:SelectItem Content="Accessibility" Value="a11y" />
            <arc:SelectItem Content="Infrastructure" Value="infra" IsEnabled="False" />
        </arc:MultiSelect>
        <TextBlock x:Name="Chosen"
                   Text="Values: none"
                   FontSize="13"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class MultiSelectChipsDemo : UserControl
{
    public MultiSelectChipsDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
    }

    private void OnSelectionChanged(object? sender, SelectionChangedEventArgs e)
    {
        Chosen.Text = Labels.SelectedValues.Count == 0
            ? "Values: none"
            : $"Values: {string.Join(", ", Labels.SelectedValues)}";
    }
}
```

## When to use

`MultiSelect` lets a person pick several values from one fixed list without the field growing. It sits in forms and
filter bars where the answer is a set: the labels on a ticket, the owners of a project, the channels that receive an
alert. The picked values show as chips inside the field, so the person sees the choice without opening the menu.

- **Labels and tags on an issue or a ticket**: a support agent sets Bug, Billing and Priority on a case in the
  ticket editor. A fixed list keeps the labels consistent across the team, and the chips show the set at a glance.
- **Owner and team filters in a support queue or an order list**: a manager filters the queue by two or three
  agents or regions. The chips inside the filter bar show the active filters, and the `+N` chip shows the rest.
- **Notification channels in an alert rule**: an SRE chooses Email, Slack and PagerDuty for one rule. Each channel is
  a fixed option, and the rule form saves the picked values in the order they were chosen.
- **Environments or regions in a deploy or report scope**: a release manager picks staging and production for a
  pipeline. Each option can be disabled when the person cannot use it, and the field stays one line.
- **Large fixed lists with a search**: a sales lead picks several cities from a long list. `IsSearchable` adds a search
  field to the menu, so the list stays usable without a separate dialog.

## When not to use

- **Every option must stay visible while people toggle them**: use `ChipGroup`. Its chips are always on screen, so
  people compare the options and their states together.
- **Values that the person types and creates**: use `TagInput`. `MultiSelect` only picks from the list you give it.
- **Exactly one value**: use `Select` for a short list, or `Combobox` for a long one that people search.
- **Independent yes or no settings**: use one `Checkbox` or `Switch` per setting, so each setting has its own label and
  description.
- **Commands, not values**: use `DropdownMenu`. Choosing an item there runs an action; choosing an option here stores a
  value in the form.

## Usage

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:MultiSelect Label="Labels"
                     Description="Shown on the issue card."
                     Width="320">
        <arc:SelectItem Content="Bug" Value="bug" />
        <arc:SelectItem Content="Feature" Value="feature" />
        <arc:SelectItem Content="Documentation" Value="docs" />
        <arc:SelectItem Content="Infrastructure" Value="infra" IsEnabled="False" />
    </arc:MultiSelect>
</UserControl>
```

`MultiSelect` derives from Avalonia's `SelectingItemsControl`, so it keeps the items model you already know:
`ItemsSource`, `SelectedItems`, `Selection`, `SelectionChanged`, keyboard focus and `IsEnabled`. Its selection mode is
`Multiple | Toggle` by default, so each pick adds or removes one value. The Arc layer adds the label, the description,
the chip row, the clear button and the menu. `SelectItem` children and `SelectOption` records both work; a
`SelectItem` without a `Value` uses its `Content` as the value.

### Anatomy

1. **Label** (`Label`): 14 px, medium weight, above the trigger. It is also the field's accessible name.
2. **Trigger**: a bordered box at least 44 px high (`ControlSizeMD`) with 12 px before the chips, 11 px after the
   chevron and 5 px above and below. It uses the control radius, the surface color and the subtle border color.
   Hover and open change only the border and background colors.
3. **Chip row** (`Placeholder` is replaced by it): chips show the picked labels in the order they were picked. Each
   chip is at most 144 px wide, has 7 px horizontal and 3 px vertical padding, uses the 12 px extra-small type size
   and sits 5 px after the previous chip. Chips use the muted surface color with a subtle border.
4. **Overflow chip**: a `+N` chip after the visible chips. It takes its count from the picks beyond
   `MaxVisibleChips` and uses the secondary text color.
5. **Placeholder** (`Placeholder`, default "Select options"): the muted text shown while nothing is selected. It
   fades out as soon as a value is picked.
6. **Chevron**: a 16 px down arrow. It rotates 180 degrees while the menu is open. Its left margin grows from 8 px to
   34 px while a value is picked, so the clear button beside it never overlaps the arrow.
7. **Clear button**: a 22 px round button with a 14 px cross, placed 36 px from the right edge of the trigger. It
   appears while at least one value is picked and the field is enabled, and it is named "Clear selections".
8. **Description** (`Description`): 12 px muted helper copy under the trigger. It is also the field's accessible help
   text.
9. **Menu**: a raised surface with a 1 px border, the panel radius and 5 px of padding. It opens 8 px below the
   trigger and is as wide as the trigger. Each option row is 38 px high with a 21 px corner radius and a check mark
   for each picked option. Disabled options are drawn at 42% opacity.

The field has no height limit for its menu by default. `MaxDropDownHeight` caps it when a long list would run off the
screen (see the data shape section).

### Chips and overflow

Picked values appear as chips in the field. `MaxVisibleChips` sets how many show before the rest fold into a `+N`
chip. The default is 2. Set it to 1 for a narrow filter bar, and to 0 to show only the count. When the row runs out
of room, the visible chips shrink with the remaining width, but the `+N` chip keeps its size, so the count never
disappears.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.MultiSelectOneVisibleChipDemo">
    <arc:MultiSelect x:Name="Owners"
                     Label="Owners"
                     HorizontalAlignment="Center"
                     MaxVisibleChips="1"
                     Width="280">
        <arc:SelectItem Content="Ada" />
        <arc:SelectItem Content="Grace" />
        <arc:SelectItem Content="Linus" />
        <arc:SelectItem Content="Margaret" />
        <arc:SelectItem Content="Ken" />
    </arc:MultiSelect>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class MultiSelectOneVisibleChipDemo : UserControl
{
    public MultiSelectOneVisibleChipDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Owners.Selection.Select(0);
        Owners.Selection.Select(1);
        Owners.Selection.Select(3);
    }
}
```

```xml
<arc:MultiSelect Label="Owners"
                 MaxVisibleChips="1"
                 Width="280"
                 ItemsSource="{Binding Owners}" />
```

Choose the count by the width of the field, not by the length of the list. Each chip takes room for its label, up to
144 px. For long labels, such as "Infrastructure review", use one visible chip so the field stays on one line, and let
the menu show the full set.

### Bound options and values

Set `ItemsSource` to `SelectOption` records. `SelectedValues` lists the values in the order they were picked. It is
read-only, so read it in a handler or from code.

```csharp
var labels = new MultiSelect
{
    Label = "Labels",
    Width = 320,
    ItemsSource = new[]
    {
        new SelectOption("bug", "Bug"),
        new SelectOption("feature", "Feature"),
        new SelectOption("docs", "Documentation"),
        new SelectOption("infra", "Infrastructure", isDisabled: true),
    }
};
labels.SelectionChanged += (_, _) => Console.WriteLine(string.Join(", ", labels.SelectedValues));
```

`SelectedValues` is the list to store. The chips and `SelectedValues` both follow the pick order, not the order of
the options: if a person picks Documentation before Bug, the chips and the saved list start with Documentation.
Sort the values in your code when the saved order matters.

### Binding to a view model

In an MVVM app the view model owns the options and the picked items, and the field shows them. Bind `ItemsSource` to
the options and `SelectedItems` to an `ObservableCollection` in the view model. `MultiSelect` derives from Avalonia's
`SelectingItemsControl`, which keeps a bound `SelectedItems` list and the selection in step both ways: each pick or
chip removal adds or removes the option in the collection, and adding or removing an option in the collection from
code updates the chips.

```csharp
public partial class AlertRuleViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    private readonly IAlertRuleService _rules;

    public AlertRuleViewModel(IAlertRuleService rules) => _rules = rules;

    public ObservableCollection<SelectOption> Channels { get; } = new()
    {
        new SelectOption("email", "Email"),
        new SelectOption("slack", "Slack"),
        new SelectOption("pagerduty", "PagerDuty"),
        new SelectOption("sms", "SMS", isDisabled: true),
    };

    public ObservableCollection<SelectOption> SelectedChannels { get; } = new();

    [RelayCommand]
    private async Task SaveAsync()
    {
        var ids = SelectedChannels.Select(c => (string)c.Value!).ToArray();
        await _rules.SaveAsync("checkout-latency", ids);
    }
}
```

```xml
<StackPanel Width="320" Spacing="16">
    <arc:MultiSelect Label="Notify"
                     ItemsSource="{Binding Channels}"
                     SelectedItems="{Binding SelectedChannels}"
                     Placeholder="Pick channels"
                     Description="Channels that receive the first alert." />
    <arc:Button Content="Save rule" Command="{Binding SaveCommand}" IsDefault="True" />
</StackPanel>
```

- Bind `SelectedItems` with the default one-way mode: the control fills the collection you give it, so the view model
  keeps one collection for the lifetime of the form. Replacing the collection object resets the selection to its
  content.
- The collection follows the order of the picks as Avalonia's selection reports them; `SelectedValues` gives the
  values in the order the person picked them. Store `SelectedValues` when that order matters.
- `IsOpen` is two-way, so a binding can open and close the menu and the menu writes its state back. `SelectedValues`
  is read-only; read it, never assign it.
- `SelectionChanged` is raised after every pick and every removal, including keyboard picks; use it for side effects
  such as a live preview, not to copy the selection.
- Compiled bindings need `x:DataType` on the view (the examples here leave it out for brevity).

### Searchable menu

`IsSearchable` adds a search field at the top of the menu. Typing filters the options; press `Down` to highlight the
first match and `Enter` to pick it. `SearchPlaceholder` sets the hint in the search field, and `EmptyText` sets the
line shown when nothing matches.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.MultiSelectSearchableDemo">
    <arc:MultiSelect x:Name="Cities"
                     Label="Cities"
                     HorizontalAlignment="Center"
                     Placeholder="Pick cities"
                     IsSearchable="True"
                     Width="320" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Pages;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class MultiSelectSearchableDemo : UserControl
{
    public MultiSelectSearchableDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Cities.ItemsSource = SelectsDemoData.Cities.Select(c => c.City).ToArray();
    }
}
```

```xml
<arc:MultiSelect Label="Cities"
                 Placeholder="Pick cities"
                 SearchPlaceholder="Type a city"
                 IsSearchable="True"
                 Width="320"
                 ItemsSource="{Binding Cities}" />
```

The default match is a case-insensitive text search on each option's label, its `Meta` text and its `Keywords`. Add
`Keywords` for synonyms that people search for: an option labelled "Infrastructure" with the keyword "devops" appears
when someone types "devops". Set `FilterPredicate` when the match must follow your own rule, for example a prefix
match on a customer code. The predicate receives the option and the trimmed search text.

Searching is an addition to Arc, whose menu has no search field, so keep it for lists long enough that scrolling is
slower than typing. Opening the menu moves focus into the search field; closing the menu returns focus to the trigger
when the search field had it.

### Selecting in code

`Selection` is the selection model. `SelectAll()` and `UnselectAll()` are offered for code only, since Arc has no
select-all control.

```csharp
labels.Selection.Select(0);
labels.Selection.Select(1);
labels.UnselectAll();
```

Use `Selection.Select` and `Selection.Deselect` with the item index to change one pick at a time. `SelectAll()` picks
every enabled option, so it skips disabled options, and `UnselectAll()` clears the selection and the chips.

### Placeholder and disabled state

`Placeholder` is shown while nothing is selected. A disabled field ignores input, closes its menu if it was open, hides
the clear button and fades to 50% opacity with the "not allowed" cursor.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.MultiSelectDisabledDemo">
    <arc:MultiSelect Label="Reviewers"
                     HorizontalAlignment="Center"
                     Width="280"
                     IsEnabled="False"
                     SelectedIndex="0">
        <arc:SelectItem Content="Ada" />
        <arc:SelectItem Content="Grace" />
    </arc:MultiSelect>
</UserControl>
```

```xml
<arc:MultiSelect Label="Reviewers" Placeholder="Select options" IsEnabled="False" />
```

Disable the field only while the value cannot change, and say why nearby, for example in the description: "Locked
after the release is approved." A disabled field still shows its chips, so people can read the current set.

### Data shape and performance

Options are `SelectItem` children or `SelectOption` records, and the control draws each visible option itself
(`SelectItem` is a data carrier, not a container), so the menu does not create a control per item. Keep the item
model small: a value, a label and the flags you need (`IsDisabled`, `Keywords`). Put the heavy data, such as
avatars or account details, in the view model and look it up when you save.

- The menu has no height limit by default and the screen bounds it. For a list of more than about a dozen options,
  set `MaxDropDownHeight` (for example 320) so the menu scrolls and stays on screen.
- Keep the labels short. A label longer than the chip width (144 px) is truncated with an ellipsis, so the full
  text is only in the menu.
- When the list changes while the menu is open, the menu refilters at once and keeps the picked values. Replace the
  whole collection when you load a new list, rather than editing it item by item.

### Example: alert rule form

An alert rule form in an observability console. The labels are short nouns, the channels are a fixed list, and the
helper text explains what the choice does ("Channels that receive the first alert"). The Notify field has one chip, so
the person sees a selected value and the clear button beside it. The Environments field is empty and shows the placeholder,
so it is clear that a choice is still needed. The chip for each picked channel shows its label, and the chevron tells
people the field opens.

![An alert rule form with one channel chip and an empty environment field](https://docs.tkcode.si/shots/Docs/Selects/MultiSelect/images/AlertRuleForm.webp)

```xml
<StackPanel Width="560" Spacing="20">
    <arc:Input Label="Rule name"
               Text="Checkout latency above 800 ms"
               Description="Shown in the incident title." />
    <arc:MultiSelect Label="Notify"
                     Description="Channels that receive the first alert."
                     Placeholder="Pick channels"
                     SelectedIndex="0">
        <arc:SelectItem Content="Email" Value="email" />
        <arc:SelectItem Content="Slack" Value="slack" />
        <arc:SelectItem Content="PagerDuty" Value="pagerduty" />
        <arc:SelectItem Content="SMS" Value="sms" IsEnabled="False" />
    </arc:MultiSelect>
    <arc:MultiSelect Label="Environments"
                     Description="Environments the rule watches."
                     Placeholder="Pick environments">
        <arc:SelectItem Content="Production" Value="prod" />
        <arc:SelectItem Content="Staging" Value="staging" />
        <arc:SelectItem Content="Sandbox" Value="sandbox" />
    </arc:MultiSelect>
    <StackPanel Orientation="Horizontal" Spacing="8" HorizontalAlignment="Right">
        <arc:Button Content="Cancel" Variant="Secondary" />
        <arc:Button Content="Save rule" />
    </StackPanel>
</StackPanel>
```

The scene uses `SelectedIndex` for the picked channel because XAML cannot list several picks without names. In an
application, load the saved picks into `SelectedItems` as shown in the view model example.

### Content guidelines

- **Label**: a short plural noun in sentence case: "Labels", "Owners", "Channels". Use the singular noun for a
  single-value field.
- **Placeholder**: the instruction for an empty field, as a verb phrase: "Pick channels", "Select options". It
  disappears when the first value is picked, so it must not hold information the chips replace.
- **Option labels**: the names people already use in the product, in sentence case, with no counts or punctuation.
  "Billing", not "Billing (3)". The count belongs to the `+N` chip.
- **Description**: one sentence about what the choice does or where it appears: "Shown on the issue card."
- **Search placeholder**: an object to search for, not a command: "Type a city", not "Search for a city here".

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| Select options... | Pick channels |
| Labels (choose as many as you want) | Labels |
| Selected: Bug, Feature, Docs, +1 more | The `+N` chip already shows the rest |
| Search | Type a city |
| Click here to add labels | Pick labels |

### Best practices

**Do**

- Give every field a visible label, because the chips alone do not say what the values mean.
- Store the values (`SelectedValues`) and show the labels, so renaming an option does not change saved data.
- Set `MaxVisibleChips` from the field width so the chips fit on one line.
- Validate the required set on submit and point to the field, because the field has no error row of its own.

**Avoid**

- Using `MultiSelect` for values people type. Free text belongs in `TagInput`, where each entry is created and checked.
- Showing the same choice in two fields. A person who sets it in one place expects it to appear in the other.
- Disabling options to hide them. A disabled option is still listed, so people learn it exists and why it is locked.
- Changing the option list under an open menu without a reason. The menu refilters as soon as the list changes, so
  the person sees a different set while still picking.
- Relying on the pick order for meaning. The chips and `SelectedValues` follow the order of the picks, which varies
  from person to person; sort the values when the order matters.

### Common questions

**Why does `SelectedValues` not match the order of my list?** The control records each value when it is picked and
keeps that order, for the chips and for `SelectedValues`. Sort the values in your code when the order must match the
list.

**How do I preselect values, and clear them later?** Bind `SelectedItems` to a list of the option objects to set the
initial picks. To change the picks from code afterwards, use `Selection.Select` and `Selection.Deselect` with the item
index, or `UnselectAll()` to clear them.

**Why is there no clear button?** It appears only while at least one value is picked and the field is enabled. A
disabled field hides it, and an empty field has nothing to clear.

**Does Enter submit the form or press the default button?** No. On the trigger, Enter opens the menu, so it never
reaches the window's default button. Inside an open menu, Enter toggles the highlighted option and keeps the menu open.
Use a button for submitting the form.

**Can a person select all options with the keyboard or the mouse?** Arc has no select-all control. `SelectAll()` is
available in code, and it picks only the enabled options.

## API reference

### MultiSelect

Arc multi-select: pick several values from a fixed list while the field stays one line. Picked values show as chips in the trigger (their slots spring open, the chips grow in out of a blur); past `MaxVisibleChips` they fold into a "+N" chip whose count rolls. Each option's check draws itself. A clear button pops in while anything is selected. Keyboard: Enter or Space opens and closes; arrows open and move the highlight (wrapping, skipping disabled options); Enter toggles the highlighted option; Escape closes. `IsSearchable` adds a search field to the menu (an addition: Arc's menu has none).

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Label` | `string?` | `null` | Visible label of the control; also its accessible name. |
| `Description` | `string?` | `null` | Helper text shown under the control. |
| `Placeholder` | `string?` | `"Select options"` | Shown while nothing is selected (Arc: "Select options"). |
| `IsOpen` | `bool` | `false` | Whether the option menu is open. Two-way. |
| `MaxVisibleChips` | `int` | `2` | Defines the `MaxVisibleChips` property. |
| `MaxDropDownHeight` | `double` | `Infinity` | Tallest the menu gets before it scrolls. Arc's menu has no limit (the screen bounds it). |
| `TextSelector` | `Func<object?, string?>?` | `null` | Returns the display text for an option. |
| `ValueSelector` | `Func<object?, object?>?` | `null` | Returns the value of an option, used to match the selection. |
| `DisabledSelector` | `Func<object?, bool>?` | `null` | Returns true for an option that cannot be chosen. |
| `IsSearchable` | `bool` | `false` | Defines the `IsSearchable` property. |
| `SearchPlaceholder` | `string?` | `"Search"` | Defines the `SearchPlaceholder` property. |
| `FilterPredicate` | `Func<object?, string, bool>?` | `null` | Returns true when an option matches the search text; filters the list while searching. |
| `EmptyText` | `string?` | `"No matches found"` | Text shown when no option matches the search (default: No matches found). |
| `SelectedItems` | `IList?` | – | Defines the `SelectedItems` property. |
| `SelectedValues` | `IReadOnlyList<object?>` | – | *Read-only.* Defines the `SelectedValues` property. |

Pseudo-classes: `:open`, `:has-selection`, `:pressed`, `:searchable`

Derives from `SelectingItemsControl`: every member of `SelectingItemsControl` works as well.

### SelectOption

A plain option record for `ItemsSource` lists that every select in this category understands without selectors: `new SelectOption("us", "United States")`.

## Accessibility

- `Label` names the field. The name also lists the picked labels, so a screen reader hears the current values.
- The field announces that it opens a multi-select list. Expanded state is exposed while the menu is open.
- Chips are hidden from assistive technology and replaced by a spoken summary. The clear button is named
  "Clear selections".
- The focus ring is drawn on the trigger, not on the menu, so focus stays on the field while the menu is open.
- Each move of the highlight and each toggle is announced in the live region with the option's position in the list
  and whether it is selected.
- `Description` is the field's help text. A disabled field is read as disabled and cannot be focused for input.

### Keyboard

The keys below work while the trigger has focus. Keys with a note also work while the search field has focus.

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Enter` or `Space` | Opens the menu when it is closed |
| `Enter` (menu open, option highlighted) | Toggles the highlighted option and keeps the menu open |
| `Enter` (menu open, no option highlighted) | Closes the menu |
| `Space` (menu open) | Closes the menu; use `Enter` to toggle an option |
| `Down` / `Up` | Opens the menu when it is closed, then moves the highlight. Wraps at both ends and skips disabled options |
| `Escape` | Closes the menu without changing the picks |
| `Tab` (search field open) | Closes the menu and moves focus to the next control |
| Letters and digits (search field open) | Filter the options; `Space` types a space into the search text |

Clicking an option toggles it and keeps the menu open, so a person can pick several values in one visit. Clicking
outside the menu closes it, and clicking the clear button removes every pick, closes the menu and returns focus to the
trigger.

## Motion

- Chip slots open to their new width with a smooth spring. Each chip grows in from a blur.
- The `+N` count rolls up or down as the number changes.
- Each check draws itself in the menu, and the menu drops in from above.
- Reduced motion replaces the size and scale changes with short cross-fades. Off switches the changes directly.
- The clear button pops in with a snappy spring when the first value is picked, and presses in to 96% when pressed.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| A value is picked | The chip slot opens and the chip grows in from a blur | Short cross-fade | Immediate |
| A value is removed | The chip shrinks out and its slot closes | Short cross-fade | Immediate |
| The `+N` count changes | The digits roll up or down | Short cross-fade | Immediate |
| Menu opens or closes | Drops in from 6 px above with a slight scale | Short cross-fade | Immediate |
| An option's check changes | The check draws in or out | Short cross-fade | Immediate |
| Hover, press, open | The border and background colors crossfade | Immediate | Immediate |

## Related

- `ChipGroup` shows every option at once; `MultiSelect` keeps the list in a menu.
- `TagInput` for values that people create; `MultiSelect` for values from a fixed list.
- `Select` for one value from a short list.
- `Combobox` for one value from a long list that people search.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `ChipGroup` | All options should stay visible and a few facets are toggled |
| `TagInput` | People create free values, such as tags or recipients |
| `Select` | One value from a short list in a form |
| `Combobox` | One value from a long list that people search |
| `Checkbox` / `Switch` | Each setting is an independent yes or no |
| `DropdownMenu` | The menu runs actions instead of storing values |

# Morph select

> A select whose trigger grows into the list, with a gliding highlight and type-ahead.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/morph-select

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.MorphSelectGroupedWithSearchDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12">
        <arc:MorphSelect x:Name="Zone" Label="Time zone" />
        <TextBlock FontSize="13"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}"
                   Text="{Binding #Zone.SelectedValue, StringFormat='Value: {0}', TargetNullValue='Value: none'}" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Pages;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class MorphSelectGroupedWithSearchDemo : UserControl
{
    public MorphSelectGroupedWithSearchDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Zone.ItemsSource = SelectsDemoData.Cities.Select(c => new SelectOption(c.City, c.City)
        {
            Meta = SelectsDemoData.Utc(c.Offset),
            Group = c.Region,
            Keywords = c.Zone,
            Icon = ArcIcons.Globe
        }).ToArray();
        Zone.SelectedValue = "London";
    }
}
```

## When to use

`MorphSelect` is a single-value picker for a known list that lives in a form or a property panel. The closed trigger is
a pill that is as wide as its label, and opening it grows the same shape into the option list, so the person sees the
list come out of the value they are changing. It fits places where the choice matters and the options are known:
settings screens, detail panels and toolbars, where a plain drop-down looks too heavy.

- **Deployment settings in a developer console**: a release picks its environment (Production, Staging, Preview) and its
  region from groups of cloud regions. Grouped headings such as "Americas" and "Europe" let people find a region without
  reading the whole list.
- **Property panels in a project tracker**: a task's status, priority and assignee are picked from short known lists.
  The compact pills sit in a row above the description, and each one opens in place.
- **Owner and team pickers in a CRM detail panel**: an account owner is chosen from the sales team. With more than eight
  options the search field appears on its own, so a long team list stays usable.
- **Compact status and priority toolbars**: a board or a table toolbar shows the current filter as a pill with an icon.
  Hiding the label keeps the toolbar short, and the trigger keeps the label as its accessible name.
- **Fintech and billing settings**: an invoice currency, a billing cycle or a tax region is a known list with a short meta
  value per option, such as a rate or an offset, shown beside the name in the list.

## When not to use

- **Free text or a long list that comes from a remote source**: use `Combobox`, which searches as the person types and
  keeps the typed text as the query.
- **Choosing several values**: use `MultiSelect`, which keeps each chosen value as a token and stays open between picks.
- **Running actions rather than choosing a value**: use `DropdownMenu`, whose items perform commands such as Rename or
  Archive.
- **Three or four options that all fit on screen**: use `SegmentedControl` or `ChipGroup`, where every option is visible
  and needs no opening step.
- **A plain labelled field in a dense form where a closed list is enough**: use `Select`, which is the classic field
  with a fixed list.

## Usage

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:MorphSelect Label="Status" SelectedIndex="1">
        <arc:SelectItem Content="Backlog" />
        <arc:SelectItem Content="In progress" />
        <arc:SelectItem Content="In review" />
        <arc:SelectItem Content="Done" />
        <arc:SelectItem Content="Canceled" IsEnabled="False" />
    </arc:MorphSelect>
</UserControl>
```

`MorphSelect` derives from Avalonia's `SelectingItemsControl`, so `ItemsSource`, `Items`, `SelectedItem`, `SelectedIndex`,
`SelectedValue`, `Selection` and `SelectionChanged` behave as they do in a list box. The control adds the trigger, the
morphing surface, the label flight, search and the grouped listbox model. `SelectItem` supplies each option, and
`SelectOption` does the same in code.

### Anatomy

1. **Label** (`Label`): the small type size at medium weight in the secondary text color, 8 px above the trigger. It is
   the accessible name of the trigger and of its list, whether or not it is drawn.
2. **Trigger**: a pill 44 px high with a 1 px border, 14 px of padding before the value and 36 px kept for the chevron.
   Its corner radius is 22 px, so the ends are fully round. The width follows the selected label, plus 50 px for the
   padding and the chevron, and it is capped at 320 px.
3. **Value or placeholder**: the selected label in the foreground color. While nothing is selected, `Placeholder` shows
   in the muted color; its default is "Select".
4. **Chevron**: 12 px from the trigger's right edge.
5. **Surface** (the open state): the trigger grows into a panel `PanelWidth` wide (272 px by default, never narrower
   than the trigger). The panel has a 6 px inset around the list, and the list is at most `MaxListHeight` tall (296 px by
   default), scrolling beyond it.
6. **Option rows**: 36 px high. A group heading (`Group`) is inserted above each run of options that share a group, and
   each heading is 28 px high.
7. **Highlight**: a soft tint of the foreground at 6.5%, which glides between options as the person moves through
   the list.
8. **Search field** (when search is on): replaces the value inside the open trigger. Its clear button uses a foreground
   tint at 8%.
9. **Focus ring**: a 2 px ring 4 px outside the trigger, drawn while the trigger has focus.

### Choosing the selection mode and width

The trigger is a single choice, and its width comes from the label, so a long label makes a wide pill. Set `PanelWidth`
when the option text is long and the list should be wider than the default 272 px. Set `PanelAlignment` to `End` when
the trigger sits at the right edge of a toolbar, so the panel opens toward the empty space and not off the window.

```xml
<arc:MorphSelect Label="Priority" PanelAlignment="End" PanelWidth="220">
    <arc:SelectItem Content="Urgent" />
    <arc:SelectItem Content="High" />
    <arc:SelectItem Content="Medium" />
    <arc:SelectItem Content="Low" />
    <arc:SelectItem Content="No priority" />
</arc:MorphSelect>
```

### Groups, icons and meta

Set `Group`, `Icon` and `Meta` on each option. A group title is inserted above each run of options that share a
group, so keep the options of one group together in the source. `Icon` takes a Lucide geometry or an image. `Meta` is a
short trailing detail, such as an offset, a rate or a count, shown in a monospaced figure style.

```csharp
var zone = new MorphSelect
{
    Label = "Time zone",
    SelectedValue = "London",
    ItemsSource = cities.Select(c => new SelectOption(c.City, c.City)
    {
        Group = c.Region,
        Meta = c.Utc,
        Keywords = c.Zone,
        Icon = ArcIcons.Globe
    }).ToArray()
};
zone.SelectionChanged += (_, _) => Console.WriteLine(zone.SelectedValue);
```

Use a group when the options fall into families a person already thinks in, such as regions, plans or teams. Do not add
a group with a single option, because the heading then costs more space than the option.

### Compact toolbar

Hide the label with `IsLabelVisible="False"`. The trigger keeps the `Label` as its accessible name, so the pill stays
compact and a screen reader still names it.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.MorphSelectCompactToolbarDemo">
    <WrapPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center" ItemSpacing="12" LineSpacing="12">
        <arc:MorphSelect Label="Status" IsLabelVisible="False" SelectedIndex="1">
            <arc:SelectItem Content="Backlog" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Clock}" />
            <arc:SelectItem Content="In progress" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Activity}" />
            <arc:SelectItem Content="In review" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Eye}" />
            <arc:SelectItem Content="Done" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.CircleCheck}" />
            <arc:SelectItem Content="Canceled" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.CircleX}" IsEnabled="False" />
        </arc:MorphSelect>
        <arc:MorphSelect Label="Priority" PanelAlignment="End" PanelWidth="220">
            <arc:SelectItem Content="Urgent" />
            <arc:SelectItem Content="High" />
            <arc:SelectItem Content="Medium" />
            <arc:SelectItem Content="Low" />
            <arc:SelectItem Content="No priority" />
        </arc:MorphSelect>
    </WrapPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```xml
<arc:MorphSelect Label="Status" IsLabelVisible="False" />
<arc:MorphSelect Label="Priority" PanelAlignment="End" PanelWidth="220"
                 ItemsSource="{Binding Priorities}" />
```

Hide the label only when the pill's value explains itself, such as a status or a priority in a toolbar row. In a form
where the value could be read several ways, keep the label visible above the trigger.

### Search

`SearchMode` decides whether the open surface has a search field. `Auto`, the default, adds one above eight options.
`On` always adds it, and `Off` never does. `SearchPlaceholder` sets its hint, and it defaults to the selected label
or "Search". Typing a letter on the closed trigger jumps to a matching option and opens the list. Once the list is open
with search on, the typed text goes to the search field, and a match is searched by label, meta and keywords.

```xml
<arc:MorphSelect Label="Owner"
                 SearchMode="On"
                 SearchPlaceholder="Find a person"
                 ItemsSource="{Binding Owners}" />
```

Turn search on for any list of more than about eight people, projects or accounts. Keep `Auto` for short lists that
should not show a field, and use `Off` when the list is ordered by a rank that a search would hide.

### Binding to a view model

With CommunityToolkit.Mvvm, the view model owns the value and the list, and the morph select edits the value through a
binding. The label of the value is read-only and shown in summaries.

```csharp
public partial class DeploymentSettingsViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    public IReadOnlyList<SelectOption> Regions { get; }

    [ObservableProperty]
    private string? _regionId = "us-east-1";

    [ObservableProperty]
    private bool _isRegionOpen;

    public DeploymentSettingsViewModel(ICloudCatalog catalog)
    {
        Regions = catalog.Regions()
            .Select(r => new SelectOption(r.Id, r.Name) { Group = r.Area, Meta = r.Code })
            .ToArray();
    }

    [RelayCommand]
    private async Task SaveAsync()
    {
        await _deployments.SetRegionAsync(RegionId);
    }
}
```

```xml
<StackPanel Spacing="16" HorizontalAlignment="Left">
    <arc:MorphSelect Label="Region"
                     ItemsSource="{Binding Regions}"
                     SelectedValue="{Binding RegionId, Mode=TwoWay}"
                     IsOpen="{Binding IsRegionOpen, Mode=TwoWay}" />
    <arc:Button Content="Save region" Command="{Binding SaveCommand}" />
</StackPanel>
```

- `SelectedValue` is two-way and holds the stored identifier, so the view model receives the choice. Use the value, not
  the index, so reloading the list does not change the selection.
- `IsOpen` is two-way. Bind it when the view model must close the list before it navigates, or when a change elsewhere
  should open it.
- `SelectedText` is read-only and holds the label of the selection. Show it in a summary line rather than binding a
  view model property back to it.
- Use `SelectionChanged` for side effects that must run on every pick, and keep the command for the save.

### Validation

The trigger has no message row of its own. Place a `TextBlock` below the field and bind it to the view model's error,
using the danger text color for the message. Validate when the list closes, not while the person is moving the
highlight, so the message does not change under the pointer.

| Rule | When to check | Where it shows |
|---|---|---|
| A value is required | On save, or when the list closes with no value | A message below the trigger, with focus moved to it |
| The region is still offered | On save, because an option can be disabled later | A message below the trigger that names the region |
| The choice is allowed for the account | On the server response | The same message row, cleared when the value changes |

### Example: deployment settings panel

A deployment settings panel in a developer console. The environment and the region are closed triggers with a visible
label, and the environment has one disabled option that explains why it cannot be used. The screenshot shows the
resting state: the trigger pills, their labels and the placeholder of the field that has no value yet.

![A deployment settings panel with environment and region pills and an owner placeholder](https://docs.tkcode.si/shots/Docs/Selects/MorphSelect/images/DeploymentSettings.webp)

```xml
<StackPanel Width="560" Spacing="20">
    <TextBlock Text="Deployment settings"
               FontSize="18"
               FontWeight="SemiBold"
               Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
    <arc:MorphSelect Label="Environment" SelectedIndex="1">
        <arc:SelectItem Content="Production" />
        <arc:SelectItem Content="Staging" />
        <arc:SelectItem Content="Preview" />

    </arc:MorphSelect>
    <arc:MorphSelect Label="Region" SelectedIndex="2">
        <arc:SelectItem Content="US East (Virginia)" Group="Americas" Meta="us-east-1" />
        <arc:SelectItem Content="US West (Oregon)" Group="Americas" Meta="us-west-2" />
        <arc:SelectItem Content="EU West (Dublin)" Group="Europe" Meta="eu-west-1" />
        <arc:SelectItem Content="EU Central (Frankfurt)" Group="Europe" Meta="eu-central-1" />
        <arc:SelectItem Content="Asia Pacific (Tokyo)" Group="Asia Pacific" Meta="ap-northeast-1" />

        <arc:SelectItem Content="Priya Raman" />
        <arc:SelectItem Content="Marcus Hale" />
```
