### Content guidelines

- **Label**: a noun naming the property, in sentence case, such as "Environment" or "Region". The label names the
  trigger for assistive technology even when it is hidden.
- **Placeholder**: an instruction that completes the label, such as "Choose an owner". The default "Select" is fine for
  a generic field.
- **Option labels**: the name people use in their work, such as "US East (Virginia)" or "Production". Put the
  identifier in `Meta` and the aliases in `Keywords`.
- **Group headings**: a plural noun for the family, such as "Americas" or "Europe".
- **Search placeholder**: name what to search for, such as "Find a person" or "Find a region".

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| Select... | Choose an owner |
| ENV | Environment |
| Region (required) | Region |
| Misc | Other regions |
| Click here to pick | Choose a region |

### Best practices

**Do**

- Keep the label visible in forms, and hide it only in toolbars where the value explains the control by itself.
- Bind `SelectedValue` and keep the stored identifier in the view model, so renaming an option does not change the saved
  choice.
- Give each group at least two options, so the headings help a person scan the list.
- Turn search on for any list of more than about eight options that people know by name.

**Avoid**

- Using the pill for actions such as Rename or Archive. Those belong in `DropdownMenu`, where the items run commands.
- Long labels in a narrow toolbar. The trigger grows with its label up to 320 px, and that pushes the other toolbar items
  aside.
- Disabling an option without a reason in its label or in the surrounding copy. A person who cannot choose "Archived"
  needs to know why.
- Re-sorting the options while the list is open. The highlight stays on its index, so the person can pick the wrong item.
- Using the chevron alone as the signal that a field is interactive. Keep the label and the pill shape visible.

### Common questions

**Why does the pill grow when I pick a longer value?** The trigger is as wide as its label plus the padding and the
chevron, up to 320 px, so the pill fits the value. Give the toolbar a fixed slot if it must not move as the value
changes.

**How do I open the list on the last option?** Press `End` on the closed trigger, which opens the list on the last
option. `Home` opens it on the first. Enter, Space, `Down` and `Up` open it on the selected option.

**Does the search field show when I set `SearchMode` to `Off`?** No. `Off` never shows it, even for a long list, and
typing on the closed trigger still jumps to a matching option.

**How do I keep the list from covering the page edge?** Set `PanelAlignment` to `End` so the surface grows to the left
of the trigger. The surface keeps its position relative to the trigger and does not flip to another side.

**Can the list show options from a server?** Load the options in the view model and assign `ItemsSource` when they
arrive. The selection is matched by value, so keep the identifiers stable across loads.

## API reference

### MorphSelect

Arc morph select: a select whose trigger is the list. Opening grows the trigger itself into the options surface (width, height and corners spring together, P9), a single highlight glides between options (P7), and the chosen label lifts out of the list and settles into the trigger (P8) while the trigger springs to its new width (P5). Supports groups (`Group`), icons and trailing meta, type-ahead, search for long lists and the full listbox keyboard model. Use it for property pickers and form fields with up to a few hundred options. Keyboard: Enter, Space and the arrows open on the selected option (Home / End open on the first or last); arrows, PageUp / PageDown (8 at a time) and Home / End move; Enter or Space picks; Alt+Up picks and closes; typing jumps (or searches when search is on); Escape closes and returns focus; Tab closes without picking.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Label` | `string?` | `null` | Visible label of the trigger; also its accessible name. |
| `IsLabelVisible` | `bool` | `true` | Defines the `IsLabelVisible` property. |
| `Placeholder` | `string?` | `"Select"` | Shown while nothing is selected (Arc: "Select"). |
| `IsOpen` | `bool` | `false` | Whether the option list is open. Two-way. |
| `SearchMode` | `MorphSelectSearchMode` | `Auto` | Defines the `SearchMode` property. |
| `SearchPlaceholder` | `string?` | `null` | Defines the `SearchPlaceholder` property. |
| `PanelWidth` | `double` | `272` | Defines the `PanelWidth` property. |
| `MaxListHeight` | `double` | `296` | Defines the `MaxListHeight` property. |
| `PanelAlignment` | `MorphSelectAlignment` | `Start` | Defines the `PanelAlignment` property. |
| `TextSelector` | `Func<object?, string?>?` | `null` | Returns the display text for an option. |
| `ValueSelector` | `Func<object?, object?>?` | `null` | Returns the value of an option, used to match the selection. |
| `DisabledSelector` | `Func<object?, bool>?` | `null` | Returns true for an option that cannot be chosen. |
| `FilterPredicate` | `Func<object?, string, bool>?` | `null` | Returns true when an option matches the search text; filters the list while searching. |
| `SelectedText` | `string?` | – | *Read-only.* Label of the selected option, or null. |

Pseudo-classes: `:open`, `:placeholder`

Derives from `SelectingItemsControl`: every member of `SelectingItemsControl` works as well.

### SelectItem

Declares one option of a `Select`, `Combobox`, `MultiSelect`, `MorphSelect` or `ChipGroup` inline in XAML: `<arc:SelectItem Content="United States" Value="us" />`. The owning control draws the option itself (virtualized and filtered without containers), so this element only carries data; set `IsEnabled` to false for an option that can be seen but not picked.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Content` | `object?` | `null` | Defines the `Content` property. |
| `Value` | `object?` | `null` | Defines the `Value` property. |
| `Icon` | `object?` | `null` | Defines the `Icon` property. |
| `Meta` | `string?` | `null` | Defines the `Meta` property. |
| `Keywords` | `string?` | `null` | Defines the `Keywords` property. |
| `Group` | `string?` | `null` | Defines the `Group` property. |

Derives from `Control`: every member of `Control` works as well.

## Accessibility

- `Label` names the trigger, even when `IsLabelVisible` is `False`. The list is named by the same label.
- The trigger is a combo box with a listbox popup. While the list is open, the expanded state is exposed and the
  highlighted option is announced.
- Arrows move the highlight and skip disabled options. `Page Up` and `Page Down` move eight options at a time, and `Home`
  and `End` go to the first and last option.
- `Enter` or `Space` picks the highlighted option. `Alt+Up` picks it and closes the list. `Escape` closes the list and
  returns focus to the trigger.
- Option groups are named by their headings. When search is on, the number of results is announced politely, and the
  search field takes over the combo box role while the list is open.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Enter`, `Space`, `Down`, `Up` on the closed trigger | Open the list on the selected option |
| `Home` / `End` on the closed trigger | Open the list on the first or last option |
| `Down` / `Up` with the list open | Move the highlight to the next or previous enabled option; no wrap at the ends |
| `Page Down` / `Page Up` | Move the highlight eight options at a time |
| `Home` / `End` with the list open | Move the highlight to the first or last option |
| `Enter` or `Space` with the list open | Pick the highlighted option and close the list |
| `Alt+Up` | Pick the highlighted option and close the list |
| Printable characters | Jump to the first matching option; with search on, type into the search field |
| `Escape` | Close the list without picking and return focus to the trigger |
| `Tab` | Close the list without picking |

## Motion

- The trigger grows into the list. Its corners reshape from the pill to the panel corner, and the panel settles with a
  small bounce when it opens and with no overshoot when it closes.
- The highlight glides between options.
- The chosen label flies from the list back into the trigger, and the trigger width settles to the new label.
- The value in the trigger rolls in the direction of the list, so the change reads as the same value moving.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| The list opens | The trigger grows into the panel with a small bounce; corners reshape | The size jumps to the open shape with a short fade | Immediate |
| The list closes | The panel shrinks back to the pill with no overshoot | The size jumps to the closed shape with a short fade | Immediate |
| The highlight moves | It glides to the next option | Jumps to the option | Immediate |
| An option is picked | The label flies into the trigger and the width settles | A short fade | Immediate |
| Search takes over the trigger | The search field fades in with a subtle blur | A short fade | Immediate |

## Related

- `Select` for a plain labelled choice field with a fixed list.
- `Combobox` for a searchable single choice that people type into.
- `MultiSelect` when several values are chosen.
- `DropdownMenu` when the menu runs actions rather than choosing a value.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `Select` | A classic labelled field with a fixed list fits the form |
| `Combobox` | People type to find a value, or the list is long and remote |
| `MultiSelect` | Several values are chosen and each stays visible as a token |
| `DropdownMenu` | The menu runs commands such as Rename or Archive |
| `SegmentedControl` | Two to four options should all be visible at once |
| `ChipGroup` | A few facets are switched often and every option stays visible |

---

# Chip group

> Filter by a few facets with chips that morph as you pick them.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/chip-group

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ChipGroupFilterChipsDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12">
        <arc:ChipGroup x:Name="Topics"
                       Label="Topics"
                       MaxWidth="560"
                       HorizontalAlignment="Left"
                       SelectionChanged="OnSelectionChanged">
            <arc:SelectItem Content="Design" />
            <arc:SelectItem Content="Engineering" />
            <arc:SelectItem Content="Research" />
            <arc:SelectItem Content="Marketing" />
            <arc:SelectItem Content="Sales" />
            <arc:SelectItem Content="Support" />
            <arc:SelectItem Content="Finance" />
            <arc:SelectItem Content="Legal" />
            <arc:SelectItem Content="Operations" />
            <arc:SelectItem Content="People" />
        </arc:ChipGroup>
        <TextBlock x:Name="Chosen"
                   Text="Values: none"
                   FontSize="13"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class ChipGroupFilterChipsDemo : UserControl
{
    public ChipGroupFilterChipsDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Topics.Selection.Select(1);
    }

    private void OnSelectionChanged(object? sender, SelectionChangedEventArgs e)
    {
        Chosen.Text = Topics.SelectedValues.Count == 0
            ? "Values: none"
            : $"Values: {string.Join(", ", Topics.SelectedValues)}";
    }
}
```

## When to use

`ChipGroup` shows a small set of options as toggle chips, all visible at once, so people can see what is available and
what is active without opening a menu. It fits filter bars and facet pickers at the top of a list, where the choices are
known, few and changed often. Every chip is a button with a pressed state, and the group keeps one tab stop, so a row
of chips costs one stop in the keyboard order.

- **Support inbox filters**: a ticket list in a help desk that filters by topic (Billing, Refunds, Login, API,
  Webhooks). Agents switch topics many times per shift, and every topic stays visible, so no one has to open a menu to
  learn what exists.
- **Order status in an e-commerce back office**: a single choice of Open, Packed, Shipped or Returned for the orders
  table. With `IsMultiple="False"` a second click clears the filter, which matches how people back out of a filter.
- **Facets on an analytics dashboard**: regions or channels above a chart, such as EMEA, North America, Paid search or
  Email. The chips sit on one line above the widgets they affect, and the selection is the state the view model
  reads when it reloads the data.
- **Onboarding steps that ask for a few interests**: a workspace setup page where a team picks the areas it will use
  (Finance, Sales, Support). Choices that are short and visible are easier to scan than a dropdown.
- **Long facet lists in a reporting page**: `MaxVisibleItems` keeps the first few chips and folds the rest behind a
  "+N more" chip, so a page with twenty product lines does not grow tall, and the lines already picked stay in view.

## When not to use

- **The selection must fit inside a compact field or a toolbar slot**: use `MultiSelect`, which shows the chosen values
  in its trigger and opens a list.
- **Each option is a yes or no answer in a form**: use `Checkbox`, which carries a label, a state and a validation
  message per option.
- **Choosing one view out of a few**, such as Table, Board or Calendar: use `SegmentedControl`, which reads as a mode
  switch rather than a filter.
- **A single value from a long or searchable list in a form**: use `Select` for a short list or `Combobox` when people
  type to find the value.
- **Values people invent**: use `TagInput`, which accepts new text as a tag. A chip group only selects options that
  already exist.

## Usage

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:ChipGroup Label="Topics" MaxWidth="560">
        <arc:SelectItem Content="Design" />
        <arc:SelectItem Content="Engineering" />
        <arc:SelectItem Content="Research" />
        <arc:SelectItem Content="Marketing" />
        <arc:SelectItem Content="Sales" />
    </arc:ChipGroup>
</UserControl>
```

`ChipGroup` derives from Avalonia's `SelectingItemsControl`, the base of `ListBox`. The item source, `Items`,
`SelectedItem`, `SelectedIndex`, `Selection` and the `SelectionChanged` event behave as they do in a list box. On top of
that base, the control lays its chips out in a wrapping panel, morphs a chip when it is picked, and folds long sets
behind a "+N more" chip. `SelectItem` supplies the content and value of each option, and any object works as an option
when you set `ItemsSource`.

### Anatomy

1. **Group label** (`Label`): the accessible name of the group, such as "Topics". The control does not draw it, so
   place a visible heading above the group.
2. **Chip**: a pill with a radius of half its height. Its height is the Arc small control size, 36 px. The label uses the
   small type size (`TypeSM`) at medium weight (500), with 14 px of padding on each side (`ChipInlinePadding`). The fill
   is the surface color, the border is 1 px in the border color and the text is the secondary text color.
3. **Selected state**: the fill mixes 11% of the accent color into the surface, and the border mixes 42% of the accent
   into the border color. Both are computed in OKLab, so the tint follows the accent. On hover the mixes rise to 16%
   and 60%. The selected state always has the check as well, so color is never the only signal.
4. **Check** (selected chips): a 14 px check in the accent-strong color. Its slot is 18 px, which the label gives up
   when the chip is selected.
5. **More chip** (`+N more`): the muted surface and muted text colors, the same height as a chip. It reads "Show less"
   while the folded chips are shown.
6. **Spacing**: 8 px between chips and between lines (`ChipGap`).
7. **Focus ring**: a 2 px ring drawn 3 px outside the focused chip in the focus-ring color. The group draws no focus
   adorner of its own.

### Choosing the selection mode

`IsMultiple` is `True` by default, so each chip toggles on its own and the selected values keep the order of the
options, not the order of the clicks. Set `IsMultiple="False"` for a single choice. A click on another chip replaces the
selection, and a click on the selected chip clears it, so the group can always end with no choice. The group has no
setting that forbids clearing; if a form needs a value, validate it on submit.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ChipGroupSingleChoiceDemo">
    <arc:ChipGroup Label="Status" IsMultiple="False">
        <arc:SelectItem Content="Open" Value="open" />
        <arc:SelectItem Content="In progress" Value="progress" />
        <arc:SelectItem Content="Closed" Value="closed" />
    </arc:ChipGroup>
</UserControl>
```

```xml
<arc:ChipGroup Label="Status" IsMultiple="False">
    <arc:SelectItem Content="Open" Value="open" />
    <arc:SelectItem Content="In progress" Value="progress" />
    <arc:SelectItem Content="Closed" Value="closed" />
</arc:ChipGroup>
```

Choose single mode when the chips are mutually exclusive states of one thing, such as a ticket status or a reporting
period. Keep multiple mode for facets that combine, such as topics or regions, where "Billing and Login" is a valid
filter.

### Folding long lists

`MaxVisibleItems` shows that many chips, and the rest fold behind a "+N more" chip. The default is no limit. Two rules
keep folding predictable:

- A selected chip stays in view even when it is past the limit, so an active filter is never hidden. A chip that is
  picked while the list is expanded also stays in view after the list folds again.
- `IsExpanded` is two-way. Clicking the more chip toggles it, and the chip reads "Show less" while the list is open.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ChipGroupFoldedDemo">
    <arc:ChipGroup Label="Topics"
                   MaxVisibleItems="5"
                   MaxWidth="560"
                   HorizontalAlignment="Left"
                   SelectedIndex="7">
        <arc:SelectItem Content="Design" />
        <arc:SelectItem Content="Engineering" />
        <arc:SelectItem Content="Research" />
        <arc:SelectItem Content="Marketing" />
        <arc:SelectItem Content="Sales" />
        <arc:SelectItem Content="Support" />
        <arc:SelectItem Content="Finance" />
        <arc:SelectItem Content="Legal" />
        <arc:SelectItem Content="Operations" />
        <arc:SelectItem Content="People" />
    </arc:ChipGroup>
</UserControl>
```

```xml
<arc:ChipGroup Label="Topics"
               MaxVisibleItems="5"
               MaxWidth="560"
               IsExpanded="{Binding ShowAllTopics, Mode=TwoWay}"
               ItemsSource="{Binding Topics}" />
```

Pick a limit that keeps the first line of chips useful at the width the group has. Five to seven chips suit a filter bar
on a desktop page, and fewer suit a narrow side panel. Put the most used options first, because the folded ones are
the ones people have to expand to reach.

### Binding to a view model

With CommunityToolkit.Mvvm, the view model owns the options and the selection, and the group displays them. Bind the
options to an `ObservableCollection<T>`, bind the chosen items to a second collection, and react to changes in the view
model rather than in the view.

```csharp
public partial class TicketFilterViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    public ObservableCollection<string> Topics { get; } = new()
    {
        "Billing", "Refunds", "Login", "API", "Webhooks", "Invoices", "SSO"
    };

    public ObservableCollection<string> ChosenTopics { get; } = new();

    [ObservableProperty]
    private bool _showAllTopics;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private string? _status = "In progress";

    [RelayCommand]
    private async Task ApplyFiltersAsync()
    {
        await _tickets.QueryAsync(ChosenTopics.ToArray(), Status);
    }
}
```

```xml
<StackPanel Spacing="16">
    <arc:ChipGroup Label="Topics"
                   MaxVisibleItems="5"
                   ItemsSource="{Binding Topics}"
                   SelectedItems="{Binding ChosenTopics}"
                   IsExpanded="{Binding ShowAllTopics, Mode=TwoWay}" />
    <arc:ChipGroup Label="Status" IsMultiple="False">
        <arc:SelectItem Content="Open" Value="open" />
        <arc:SelectItem Content="In progress" Value="progress" />
        <arc:SelectItem Content="Closed" Value="closed" />
    </arc:ChipGroup>
    <arc:Button Content="Apply filters" Command="{Binding ApplyFiltersCommand}" />
</StackPanel>
```

- `SelectedItems` is two-way. A chip click adds or removes the item in `ChosenTopics`, and an item the view model adds
  to the collection is selected. Use a collection of the same values as `ItemsSource` so that the lists match by value.
- `IsExpanded` is two-way, so the view model can open the folded chips, for example after a search matches one of them.
- `SelectedItem` is the single choice in single mode. Bind it with `Mode=TwoWay` when the view model needs to set it.
- `SelectedValues` is read-only and lists the `Value` of each chosen option in option order. Read it in a handler or
  when the command runs, not as a binding source.
- To react to every change, handle `SelectionChanged` in code or query the view model when the command runs.

For items that are objects rather than strings, set `TextSelector` to the label and `ValueSelector` to the value in
code. Both are typed as delegates, so they work without reflection and under trimming.

```csharp
topicsGroup.TextSelector = item => ((Topic)item!).Name;
topicsGroup.ValueSelector = item => ((Topic)item!).Id;
```

### Data shape and performance

Each chip is a control with its own text layout and motion, so the group is built for a short facet list, not for a
catalog. Keep the option count to what a person can scan in one glance, and use `MaxVisibleItems` to keep the first
line short when a list is longer. For a catalog of many values, use `MultiSelect` with search or `Combobox`.

The chip row reflows when the options or the width change, and each chip springs to its new position. Chips move while
they reflow, so avoid changing the option list while a person is picking from it.

### Example: support inbox filter bar

A filter bar above a support ticket list. The topics are a multiple choice with a fold after five chips, the status is
a single choice that starts on "In progress", and the footer states the result count so the filter's effect is visible
before the person applies it. The chips use short nouns that match the ticket fields, and the folded set keeps the
currently selected "Invoices" chip in view even though it sits past the limit.

![A support inbox filter bar with topic chips, a folded overflow and a single status choice](https://docs.tkcode.si/shots/Docs/Selects/ChipGroup/images/SupportFilters.webp)

```xml
<StackPanel xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
            xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
            xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
            xmlns:generic="using:System.Collections.Generic"
            Width="680"
            Spacing="20">
    <TextBlock Text="Support tickets"
               FontSize="18"
               FontWeight="SemiBold"
               Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
    <StackPanel Spacing="8">
        <TextBlock Text="Topic"
                   FontSize="13"
                   FontWeight="Medium"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
        <arc:ChipGroup Label="Topics" MaxVisibleItems="5">
            <arc:ChipGroup.ItemsSource>
                <generic:List x:TypeArguments="x:String">
                    <x:String>Billing</x:String>
                    <x:String>Refunds</x:String>
                    <x:String>Login</x:String>
                    <x:String>API</x:String>
                    <x:String>Webhooks</x:String>
                    <x:String>Invoices</x:String>
                    <x:String>SSO</x:String>
                </generic:List>
            </arc:ChipGroup.ItemsSource>
            <arc:ChipGroup.SelectedItems>
                <generic:List x:TypeArguments="x:String">
                    <x:String>Billing</x:String>
                    <x:String>Invoices</x:String>
                </generic:List>
            </arc:ChipGroup.SelectedItems>
        </arc:ChipGroup>
    </StackPanel>
    <StackPanel Spacing="8">
        <TextBlock Text="Status"
                   FontSize="13"
                   FontWeight="Medium"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
        <arc:ChipGroup Label="Status" IsMultiple="False" SelectedIndex="1">
            <arc:SelectItem Content="Open" Value="open" />
            <arc:SelectItem Content="In progress" Value="progress" />
            <arc:SelectItem Content="Closed" Value="closed" />
        </arc:ChipGroup>
    </StackPanel>
    <Grid ColumnDefinitions="*,Auto">
        <TextBlock Text="Showing 42 of 318 tickets"
                   VerticalAlignment="Center"
                   FontSize="13"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
        <StackPanel Grid.Column="1" Orientation="Horizontal" Spacing="8">
            <arc:Button Content="Clear filters" Variant="Secondary" />
            <arc:Button Content="Apply filters" />
        </StackPanel>
    </Grid>
</StackPanel>
```

### Content guidelines

- **Option labels**: a short noun or a noun phrase in sentence case, such as "Billing", "Packed" or "In progress". Use the
  words of the field the filter applies to, so the chip and the column header match.
- **Group label**: the name of the facet in a visible heading above the group, such as "Topic" or "Status". The
  `Label` value repeats it for assistive technology, so keep the two the same.
- **Counts and results**: state the effect in the footer, for example "Showing 42 of 318 tickets", and write numbers as
  digits.
- **Buttons**: use a verb and an object, such as "Apply filters" and "Clear filters", not "OK".

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| Filter options | Topic |
| Select your topic(s) | Billing, Refunds |
| Click to filter | Apply filters |
| Misc | Other |
| All of the things | All topics |

### Best practices

**Do**

- Use a visible heading above each group and keep `Label` equal to it, so a screen reader and a sighted user name the
  same facet.
- Keep `IsMultiple` true for facets that combine and use single mode only for mutually exclusive states.
- Set `MaxVisibleItems` on long facet lists, and order the options so the most used ones come first.
- Apply the filter with a command or on a clear action, and show the result count, so the chips do not feel like they
  change data by themselves.

**Avoid**

- Chips for values people type or create. The group selects existing options only; use `TagInput` for new tags.
- Relying on a second click as the only way to clear a filter. A single choice clears that way, but a visible "Clear
  filters" button is easier to find and also clears multiple choices.
- Long option lists without a fold. Each chip is a control with its own motion, so a long catalog makes the bar heavy and
  hard to scan.
- Using chips for yes or no questions in a form. `Checkbox` carries the label, state and validation that a form needs.
- Reordering the options at run time. Chips move under the pointer, so people lose their place in a list that changes
  while they read it.

### Common questions

**Why does the group not show a heading?** The control draws only the chips and the "+N more" chip. `Label` is the
accessible name, so show the heading as a separate `TextBlock` above the group, as in the example.

**Can I stop people from clearing a single choice?** No. The group clears the selection on a second click by design.
If the form needs a value, validate it on submit and show the message next to the group.

**Are selected chips hidden when the list is folded?** No. A chip that is selected when the list folds stays in view,
and so does a chip picked while the list is open. Only the unselected overflow folds.

**How do I select chips in code?** Use `Selection.Select(index)` and `Selection.Deselect(index)`, or `Toggle(index)`,
which works like a click. `Toggle` ignores indexes out of range and disabled options. To select several values at
once, add them to the `SelectedItems` list.

**How do I preselect chips in XAML?** Use `SelectedIndex` for one chip in single mode, as the folded-list example above does. For
several chips, bind or set `SelectedItems` to a list of the same values as `ItemsSource`, as the screenshot does.

## API reference

### ChipGroup

Arc chip group: toggle chips for facets people switch often (topics, statuses, tags). Picking a chip morphs it: a check grows in, the label slides over and the chip's edge follows on a spring while the neighbours glide to their new places, even across lines. Long sets fold behind a "+N more" chip (selected chips always stay in view); expanding staggers the revealed chips in and the group height springs. With `IsMultiple` false it is a single choice that can still be cleared. Keyboard: one tab stop; arrows move between chips and wrap, Home / End jump to the ends; Enter or Space toggles the focused chip or expands the folded ones.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Label` | `string?` | `null` | Accessible name of the group, such as "Topics". |
| `IsMultiple` | `bool` | `true` | Defines the `IsMultiple` property. |
| `MaxVisibleItems` | `int` | `2147483647` | Defines the `MaxVisibleItems` property. |
| `IsExpanded` | `bool` | `false` | Defines the `IsExpanded` property. |
| `TextSelector` | `Func<object?, string?>?` | `null` | Label of a data item (AOT-safe alternative to `DisplayMemberBinding`). |
| `ValueSelector` | `Func<object?, object?>?` | `null` | Value of a data item (AOT-safe alternative to `SelectedValueBinding`). |
| `SelectedItems` | `IList?` | – | Defines the `SelectedItems` property. |
| `SelectedValues` | `IReadOnlyList<object?>` | – | *Read-only.* Values of the selected options, in option order (Arc keeps `value` in option order). |

Derives from `SelectingItemsControl`: every member of `SelectingItemsControl` works as well.

### SelectItem

Declares one option of a `Select`, `Combobox`, `MultiSelect`, `MorphSelect` or `ChipGroup` inline in XAML: `<arc:SelectItem Content="United States" Value="us" />`. The owning control draws the option itself (virtualized and filtered without containers), so this element only carries data; set `IsEnabled` to false for an option that can be seen but not picked.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Content` | `object?` | `null` | Defines the `Content` property. |
| `Value` | `object?` | `null` | Defines the `Value` property. |
| `Icon` | `object?` | `null` | Defines the `Icon` property. |
| `Meta` | `string?` | `null` | Defines the `Meta` property. |
| `Keywords` | `string?` | `null` | Defines the `Keywords` property. |
| `Group` | `string?` | `null` | Defines the `Group` property. |

Derives from `Control`: every member of `Control` works as well.

## Accessibility

- `Label` is the accessible name of the group. The group is exposed as a named group, and the name comes from `Label`
  when no other name is set.
- Each chip is a button with a toggle state. Screen readers announce a chip as on or off, so the selection is not
  conveyed by color alone.
- The "+N more" chip is an expandable control. It reports whether the folded chips are expanded and can be expanded and
  collapsed through the automation expand and collapse actions.
- The group keeps one tab stop, so Tab moves into the group once and moves out of it once. The stop is the last chip
  that had focus, else the first selected chip, else the first chip.
- The focus ring is drawn on the focused chip in the focus-ring color, so it stays visible on a selected chip.

### Keyboard

The group takes one tab stop, and the arrow keys move between chips inside it.

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` | Move into the group on its tab stop chip, and out of it |
| `Right` / `Down` | Move to the next chip; from the last one, wrap to the first |
| `Left` / `Up` | Move to the previous chip; from the first one, wrap to the last |
| `Home` / `End` | Move to the first or last chip, which is the "+N more" chip when the list folds |
| `Space` or `Enter` | Toggle the focused chip; on the "+N more" chip, expand or collapse the folded chips |

## Motion

- A picked chip grows a check from its left edge, and its label slides open to the new width while the chip's edge
  follows on a spring.
- Neighbouring chips glide to their new positions, including across line breaks, so the row reflows without a jump.
- Folded chips appear with a short stagger when the list expands, and the group height changes smoothly.
- A pressed chip scales down slightly and springs back when released.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| A chip is picked or cleared | The check grows, the label slides and the edge springs to the new width | A short fade | Immediate |
| Neighbouring chips move | They glide to their new positions, across lines too | A short fade | Immediate |
| Folded chips appear | Staggered entrance, with the group height easing | A short fade | Immediate |
| Folded chips leave | They fade in place, faster than they came | A short fade | Immediate |

## Related

- `MultiSelect` for the same choice inside a compact field, and `Checkbox` for form choices that each stand on their
  own.
- `SegmentedControl` for picking one view, and `Select` or `Combobox` for one value from a list in a form.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `MultiSelect` | The selected values must fit in a compact field or toolbar slot |
| `Checkbox` | Each option is a yes or no answer in a form, with its own validation |
| `SegmentedControl` | People choose one view or mode out of two to four |
| `Select` | One value from a short list in a form |
| `Combobox` | One value from a longer list that people type to find |
| `TagInput` | People create their own tags instead of picking existing options |

# Radio cards

> Selectable option cards with a sliding selection ring, price and description slots, and radio keyboard behavior.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/radio-cards

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.RadioCardsGridDemo">
    <arc:RadioCards AutomationProperties.Name="Plan" SelectedValue="pro">
        <arc:RadioCardOption Value="starter"
                             Label="Starter"
                             Description="For individuals getting started."
                             Meta="$0"
                             Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.User}" />
        <arc:RadioCardOption Value="pro"
                             Label="Pro"
                             Description="Unlimited projects and priority support."
                             Meta="$12"
                             Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Zap}" />
        <arc:RadioCardOption Value="team"
                             Label="Team"
                             Description="Shared workspaces and roles for small teams."
                             Meta="$32"
                             Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Users}" />
        <arc:RadioCardOption Value="enterprise"
                             Label="Enterprise"
                             Description="SSO, audit logs and a dedicated contact."
                             Meta="Custom"
                             Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Shield}"
                             IsDisabled="True"
                             DisabledReason="Talk to sales to enable Enterprise." />
    </arc:RadioCards>
</UserControl>
```

## When to use

`RadioCards` is a single choice where each option needs more than a label before the person can decide: a price, a
delivery time, a description or a reason it is unavailable. It sits in a form or a step of a flow, such as plan
selection at sign-up or shipping at checkout, and the card the person picks is the one the flow continues with.

- **Plan selection at sign-up or in a billing step**: a SaaS product with Starter, Pro and Team plans. Each card shows
  the plan's price in its meta slot and one line of what it includes.
- **Shipping and delivery choices at checkout**: Standard, Express and Overnight, each with a delivery window and a cost.
  The List layout keeps the window and the price on one row, so the cost is easy to compare.
- **Region or data residency choices in an admin console**: a workspace region picked for compliance, where each card
  states the region and a short note on latency or retention.
- **Options with a reason they cannot be picked**: an Enterprise plan that needs a sales contact, or a storage tier that
  the account's current plan does not include. `DisabledReason` explains the restriction where the person is looking.
- **A required choice in a short list**: an export format or a report period in a dashboard dialog, where the person
  must pick one of three to four options before Run becomes meaningful.

## When not to use

- **Short text-only options**, such as "Yes, No, Maybe" or a status: use `RadioGroup`, which is compact and has no
  price or description slot.
- **Two to four views that switch the content at once**, such as Overview, Activity and Settings above a panel: use
  `SegmentedControl`. The choice changes the view, not a value the form saves.
- **Long lists of options**, such as a country list or a hundred projects: use `Select` or `Combobox`. Cards take a lot
  of space per option and do not filter.
- **A billing period switch with a savings note**, such as Monthly and Yearly: use `BillingToggle`, which is one row of
  short labels with badges.
- **Several options that can all be on**, such as the add-ons on a plan: use `Checkbox`. A radio card allows one choice.

## Usage

The cards are the `Items` of the control. Each `RadioCardOption` takes a value, a label, a description and a meta
text, which is shown at the end of the card.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:RadioCards SelectedValue="pro">
        <arc:RadioCardOption Value="starter" Label="Starter" Description="For individuals getting started." Meta="$0" />
        <arc:RadioCardOption Value="pro" Label="Pro" Description="Unlimited projects and priority support." Meta="$12" />
        <arc:RadioCardOption Value="team" Label="Team" Description="Shared workspaces and roles for small teams." Meta="$32" />
    </arc:RadioCards>
</UserControl>
```

`RadioCards` derives from Avalonia's `SelectingItemsControl`. It has the usual items model (`ItemsSource`, `Items`,
`SelectedIndex`, `SelectedItem`) and the selection events of that base class, and `SelectedValue` is the property an
application binds, because it carries the option's value rather than the option object. The cards add the selection
ring, the indicator dot, the description and meta slots, the disabled reason and the two layouts on top of the selecting
control, so a form gets a complete radio group with no custom template.

### Anatomy

1. **Card**: a 20 px corner radius on the surface color with a 1 px border. Hover and keyboard focus strengthen the border;
   a disabled card uses the muted surface and muted text.
2. **Selection ring**: a 1.5 px ring in the control-on color drawn over the card's border. It belongs to the group, not to
   the card, so it glides from one card to the next.
3. **Indicator**: an 18 px circle with a 1.5 px border, placed at the top end of a grid
   card and at the start of a list row. When the card is chosen, it fills with the control-on color and shows a 6 px dot
   in the glyph color.
4. **Icon** (`Icon`): an 18 px glyph beside the label, drawn with the secondary text color and the foreground color when
   the card is selected. A `Geometry` is wrapped at 18 px automatically; any other content is placed as given.
5. **Label** (`Label`): medium weight, truncated with an ellipsis when it does not fit.
6. **Description** (`Description`): extra-small text in the secondary color, meant for one or two short lines, with a 2 px
   gap under the label. A disabled card shows `DisabledReason` here instead.
7. **Meta** (`Meta`): the price or estimate. In a grid card it sits at the bottom in the large text size with 14 px above
   it. In a list row it sits at the end in the small medium-weight size with 12 px before it.
8. **Focus ring**: a 2 px ring around the card for keyboard focus. It is hidden for pointer focus.

Cards in one row share the height of the tallest card, so prices line up across the row. The grid places cards in
columns of at least `MinColumnWidth` (180 by default), with a 10 px gap. The list places one card per full-width row
with an 8 px gap.

### Binding to a view model

In an MVVM app, the view model owns the options and the selected value. Bind `ItemsSource` to an
`ObservableCollection<RadioCardOption>` and `SelectedValue` to the id of the selected option. Both are two-way for the
selection and one-way for the items. Use the value, not the option object, so the saved choice is a plain string or id.

```csharp
public partial class PlanViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    public ObservableCollection<RadioCardOption> Plans { get; } = new()
    {
        new RadioCardOption("starter", "Starter", "For individuals getting started.", "$0"),
        new RadioCardOption("pro", "Pro", "Unlimited projects and priority support.", "$12"),
        new RadioCardOption("team", "Team", "Shared workspaces and roles for small teams.", "$32"),
        new RadioCardOption("enterprise", "Enterprise", "SSO, audit logs and a dedicated contact.", "Custom")
        {
            IsDisabled = true,
            DisabledReason = "Talk to sales to enable Enterprise."
        }
    };

    [ObservableProperty]
    private string? _planId = "pro";

    [RelayCommand]
    private async Task ContinueAsync()
    {
        await _subscriptions.StartAsync(PlanId);
    }
}
```

```xml
<StackPanel Spacing="16">
    <arc:RadioCards ItemsSource="{Binding Plans}"
                    SelectedValue="{Binding PlanId}"
                    AutomationProperties.Name="Plan" />
    <arc:Button Content="Continue" Command="{Binding ContinueCommand}" IsDefault="True" />
</StackPanel>
```

- `SelectedValue` is two-way: a choice made by the person writes the id to `PlanId`, and a value set in code selects the
  matching card. A value that matches no card leaves nothing selected.
- Set `IsDisabled` on the option in the view model, not in the XAML, when availability depends on the account. The card
  then shows the reason without a separate binding.
- Compiled bindings need `x:DataType` on the view (the examples here leave it out for brevity).

### Options in code

The same options can be built in code-behind or in a service, then assigned to `ItemsSource`, or the control can take
them inline in XAML. Assigning `SelectedValue` after the options are set keeps the choice.

```csharp
var plans = new RadioCards
{
    ItemsSource = new[]
    {
        new RadioCardOption("pro", "Pro", "Unlimited projects and priority support.", "$12") { Icon = ArcIcons.Zap },
        new RadioCardOption("team", "Team", "Shared workspaces and roles for small teams.", "$32") { Icon = ArcIcons.Users }
    },
    SelectedValue = "pro"
};
plans.SelectionChanged += (_, _) => Console.WriteLine(plans.SelectedValue);
```

`Icon` takes a `Geometry`. It is drawn as an 18px icon at the start of the card.

### Choosing a layout

`Layout="List"` stacks the cards as full-width rows with the meta at the end. Long descriptions wrap. The default
`Grid` layout fills columns that are at least `MinColumnWidth` wide (180 by default).

Use the grid for plans and regions, where the person compares the cards side by side and the description is the reason
to choose. Use the list for shipping, payment or delivery options, where each choice is a sentence with a time and a
price that the person scans down. The grid drops to one column when the container is narrower than about 370 px (two
columns of 180 plus the gap), so a narrow dialog still shows every card at full width.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.RadioCardsListDemo">
    <arc:RadioCards Layout="List" AutomationProperties.Name="Shipping speed" SelectedValue="standard">
        <arc:RadioCardOption Value="standard"
                             Label="Standard"
                             Description="4 to 6 business days"
                             Meta="Free"
                             Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.CalendarDays}" />
        <arc:RadioCardOption Value="express"
                             Label="Express"
                             Description="2 to 3 business days"
                             Meta="$9.00"
                             Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Clock}" />
        <arc:RadioCardOption Value="overnight"
                             Label="Overnight"
                             Description="Next business day before noon"
                             Meta="$24.00"
                             Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Zap}" />
    </arc:RadioCards>
</UserControl>
```

### Unavailable options

Set `IsDisabled` on an option to keep it visible but unavailable. Set `DisabledReason` to say why. The reason
replaces the description while the option is disabled. Arrow keys skip disabled options.

```xml
<arc:RadioCards SelectedValue="pro">
    <arc:RadioCardOption Value="pro" Label="Pro" Description="Unlimited projects and priority support." Meta="$12" />
    <arc:RadioCardOption Value="enterprise"
                         Label="Enterprise"
                         Description="SSO, audit logs and a dedicated contact."
                         Meta="Custom"
                         IsDisabled="True"
                         DisabledReason="Talk to sales to enable Enterprise." />
</arc:RadioCards>
```

### Required and disabled

`IsRequired` marks the group as required in a form. `IsEnabled="False"` disables every card.

```xml
<arc:RadioCards IsRequired="True" IsEnabled="False" />
```

### Example: plan selection at sign-up

A sign-up step for a project management product, Northwind Cloud. The four plans compare side by side in the grid. The
selected Pro card carries the ring and the filled indicator, the Enterprise card explains why it cannot be chosen online,
and the primary button continues with the chosen plan. Every card has the same height because the row takes the tallest
card, so the prices line up across the row.

![A plan selection step with four radio cards, one selected and one disabled with a reason](https://docs.tkcode.si/shots/Docs/Toggles/RadioCards/images/PlanCards.webp)

```xml
<StackPanel Width="760" Spacing="20">
    <StackPanel Spacing="4">
        <TextBlock Text="Choose a plan for Northwind Cloud"
                   FontSize="18"
                   FontWeight="SemiBold"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
        <TextBlock Text="You can change plans at any time from billing settings."
                   FontSize="13"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
    </StackPanel>
    <arc:RadioCards SelectedValue="pro" AutomationProperties.Name="Plan">
        <arc:RadioCardOption Value="starter"
                             Label="Starter"
                             Description="For individuals getting started."
                             Meta="$0"
                             Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.User}" />
        <arc:RadioCardOption Value="pro"
                             Label="Pro"
                             Description="Unlimited projects and priority support."
                             Meta="$12"
                             Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Zap}" />
        <arc:RadioCardOption Value="team"
                             Label="Team"
                             Description="Shared workspaces and roles for small teams."
                             Meta="$32"
                             Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Users}" />
        <arc:RadioCardOption Value="enterprise"
                             Label="Enterprise"
                             Description="SSO, audit logs and a dedicated contact."
                             Meta="Custom"
                             Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Shield}"
                             IsDisabled="True"
                             DisabledReason="Talk to sales to enable Enterprise." />
    </arc:RadioCards>
    <StackPanel Orientation="Horizontal" Spacing="8" HorizontalAlignment="Right">
        <arc:Button Content="Back" Variant="Secondary" />
        <arc:Button Content="Continue with Pro" />
    </StackPanel>
</StackPanel>
```

### Content guidelines

- **Label**: the plan, speed or region name as a single word or short phrase: "Pro", "Express", "EU (Frankfurt)". Use
  sentence case for multi-word labels.
- **Description**: one line of what the choice gives the person, in plain words: "Unlimited projects and priority
  support", "2 to 3 business days". Keep it under about 60 characters so it fits two lines in a grid card.
- **Meta**: the price or time, with the currency sign and the unit in the description when it is not obvious:
  "$12", "Free", "Custom". Write numbers as digits.
- **Disabled reason**: the next step the person can take, not only the restriction: "Talk to sales to enable
  Enterprise." is better than "Not available".

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| Pro plan (recommended) | Pro |
| Ships fast | 2 to 3 business days |
| 12 USD per month for the pro tier | $12 |
| Not available | Talk to sales to enable Enterprise. |

### Best practices

**Do**

- Put the price, time or other comparison in `Meta`, and keep the description for what the choice includes. A person
  compares the meta column first.
- Name the group with `AutomationProperties.Name` when no visible heading names it, so the choice is announced as
  "Plan" and not as an unnamed list of cards.
- Pick a default with `SelectedValue` when one option is the common choice, and say so in the description.
- Use `DisabledReason` for every disabled card, so a person knows why an option cannot be chosen and what to do.

**Avoid**

- Long descriptions in a grid of three or four cards. Two lines is the design; a paragraph makes the row tall and the
  comparison slow.
- Using the grid for options with no description or price. A `RadioGroup` is quicker to read for a short list.
- Removing a disabled option from the collection when the person needs to know it exists. Keep it visible with its reason.
- Setting `IsRequired` without a visible prompt. The attribute is reported to assistive technology, and the form still
  needs a message that says a plan must be chosen.

### Common questions

**What is selected when I do not set `SelectedValue`?** Nothing. The group has no selection until the person picks a card
or your code sets `SelectedValue`, and Tab then focuses the first available card.

**How does the keyboard move between cards?** The group is one tab stop. Arrow keys select the next or previous available
card, and Enter or Space selects the focused card. The arrow keys skip disabled cards, and Home and End select the first and
last available card. The keyboard map is in Accessibility.

**Why does the ring glide instead of jumping?** The ring is one shape that glides between the selected card's position
on a spring, so the eye follows the change. When the layout changes size, the ring moves to the new position at once.

**How do I show a card that is disabled but still selected?** Set `IsDisabled` and `SelectedValue` on the same option.
The card then shows its reason in place of the description, and the ring stays on it. Usually it is better to change the
selection in the view model before disabling an option.

**Can a card hold a control, such as a custom icon or a badge?** `Icon` accepts a `Geometry` or any content, and `Meta`
accepts any object, so a badge can be the meta content. Keep the content short, because the card's height is shared with
its row.

## API reference

### RadioCards

Arc radio cards: selectable option cards for choices that need more than a label (plans, shipping speeds, regions). One selection ring springs from card to card, so the eye follows the change, and a 6px dot pops into the chosen card's indicator. Behaves as a radio group: one tab stop, arrows (mirrored in right-to-left) move and select, Home / End jump to the ends and Enter / Space select. Disabled cards are skipped and show their reason. Cards come from `ItemsSource` or inline `RadioCardOption` items; `SelectedValue` (two-way) is the selected option's value.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Layout` | `RadioCardsLayout` | `Grid` | Card placement: Grid (responsive columns, the default) or List (full-width rows with the meta at the end). |
| `MinColumnWidth` | `double` | `180` | Narrowest a grid column may get before the grid drops a column (Arc default 180). |
| `IsRequired` | `bool` | `false` | A choice is required (reported to assistive technology). |

Derives from `SelectingItemsControl`: every member of `SelectingItemsControl` works as well.
### RadioCardOption

One option of `RadioCards` (Arc `RadioCardOption`): a label with optional description, a meta value (price, estimate), a decorative icon, and a reason shown in place of the description when the option is disabled.

## Accessibility

- Each card is a radio button to assistive technology. Set `AutomationProperties.Name` on the group when no visible header names it.
- The card label is the card's name. The description is its help text. A disabled card reports its `DisabledReason` instead.
- The group is one tab stop. `IsRequired` is reported to assistive technology as required for the form.
- Right-to-left layouts mirror the arrow keys: Right moves to the previous card, and Left to the next.
- Keyboard focus draws a 2px outline offset by 2px. Pointer focus does not.
- The selection shows as a ring and a dot, so it does not depend on color alone.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` | Move focus into the group on the selected card, or on the first available card when none is selected, and out of it. |
| `Right` / `Down` | Select and focus the next available card. The move wraps from the last card to the first. In right-to-left layouts, `Right` moves back. |
| `Left` / `Up` | Select and focus the previous available card. In right-to-left layouts, `Left` moves forward. |
| `Home` / `End` | Select and focus the first or the last available card. |
| `Enter` / `Space` | Select the focused card. |

## Motion

- The selection ring glides from card to card on a spring. It fades in the first time it is placed. When the layout
  changes size, it moves to the new position at once.
- The dot grows in from nothing when a card is chosen. The card background and border change color quickly.
- Reduced motion puts the ring and the dot in their final state at once and removes the color transitions. Off does the same.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| The selection moves to another card | The ring glides to the card on a spring | The ring is at the card at once | The ring is at the card at once |
| The first selection is placed | The ring fades in quickly | The ring appears at once | The ring appears at once |
| A card is chosen | The indicator dot pops in on a snappy spring | The dot appears at once | The dot appears at once |
| The layout changes size | The ring moves to the new position at once | The ring moves at once | The ring moves at once |
| Hover, press or focus on a card | The card background and border change color quickly | Immediate | Immediate |

## Related

- `RadioGroup` for short options that are plain text, in a vertical list.
- `SegmentedControl` for two to four views that switch the content at once.
- `Checkbox` when the user may choose several options.
- `BillingToggle` for a monthly or yearly billing period.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `RadioGroup` | The options are short text, with no price or description |
| `SegmentedControl` | The choice switches a view and is not saved as a value |
| `Select` / `Combobox` | The list is long or needs filtering |
| `BillingToggle` | The choice is a billing period with a savings note |
| `Checkbox` | More than one option can be on at once |

# Billing toggle

> A monthly and yearly switch with a savings badge and prices that roll to the new amount.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/billing-toggle

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.BillingTogglePricingDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="28">
        <arc:BillingToggle x:Name="Toggle"
                           Value="yearly"
                           HorizontalAlignment="Center"
                           ValueChanged="OnValueChanged" />
        <WrapPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center" ItemSpacing="32" LineSpacing="16">
            <StackPanel Spacing="6">
                <TextBlock Text="Starter" FontSize="14" Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
                <arc:BillingPrice x:Name="StarterPrice" />
            </StackPanel>
            <StackPanel Spacing="6">
                <TextBlock Text="Pro" FontSize="14" Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
                <arc:BillingPrice x:Name="ProPrice" />
            </StackPanel>
            <StackPanel Spacing="6">
                <TextBlock Text="Team" FontSize="14" Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
                <arc:BillingPrice x:Name="TeamPrice" />
            </StackPanel>
        </WrapPanel>
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class BillingTogglePricingDemo : UserControl
{
    public BillingTogglePricingDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        ShowPrices();
    }

    private void OnValueChanged(object? sender, BillingToggleValueChangedEventArgs e) => ShowPrices();

    private void ShowPrices()
    {
        var yearly = Toggle.Value == "yearly";
        ShowPrice(StarterPrice, 12, 10, yearly);
        ShowPrice(ProPrice, 30, 24, yearly);
        ShowPrice(TeamPrice, 60, 48, yearly);
    }

    // Setting Amount rolls the price to the new number. The monthly price is shown struck through under yearly billing.
    private static void ShowPrice(BillingPrice price, decimal monthly, decimal perMonthYearly, bool yearly)
    {
        price.Amount = yearly ? perMonthYearly : monthly;
        price.WasAmount = yearly ? monthly : null;
        price.Period = yearly ? "per month, billed yearly" : "per month";
    }
}
```

## When to use

`BillingToggle` is the segmented switch that picks a billing period, usually at the top of a pricing page or in the
plan section of a billing settings screen. It pairs with `BillingPrice`, which shows the amount for the chosen period
and rolls to the new number when the period changes, so the person sees the cost of each choice without leaving the
page.

- **Billing period on a pricing page**: a SaaS product that sells monthly and yearly plans. The savings badge ("Save
  20%") on the yearly option explains the discount where the decision is made.
- **Plan changes in billing settings**: an account page where an admin moves a workspace from monthly to yearly
  billing. The toggle shows the new amount and the "billed yearly" period text before the person confirms.
- **Lifetime or one-time options next to subscriptions**: a developer tool that sells monthly, yearly and lifetime
  licenses. A three-option toggle with a "Best value" badge keeps the choice in one row.
- **Checkout summaries with a period switch**: a checkout step that shows the total for a monthly or annual term, with
  the badge on the selected option stating the saving in money ("You save $48").

## When not to use

- **Switching views that do not change a price**, such as a list and a board of the same orders: use
  `SegmentedControl`. It has no badges and no price semantics.
- **Options that need a description or a vertical layout**, such as a list of plans with a sentence about each: use
  `RadioGroup` or `RadioCards`. `BillingToggle` is a single horizontal row of short labels.
- **A single on or off setting**, such as "Renew automatically": use `Switch`, which reads as a setting that takes
  effect at once.
- **Plans that each carry a price, features and a reason when unavailable**: use `RadioCards`. Put the price in the
  card and keep the toggle for the period only.
- **Choosing from a long list of billing currencies or regions**: use `Select` or `Combobox`. The toggle is for two
  to three options that fit in one row.

## Usage

The toggle with no options shows Monthly and Yearly, and Yearly carries the badge "Save 20%". Set `Value` to the
selected option's value.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:BillingToggle Value="yearly" />
</UserControl>
```

`BillingToggle` derives from Avalonia's `SelectingItemsControl`. It therefore has the usual items model (`ItemsSource`,
`Items`, `SelectedIndex`, `SelectedItem`, `SelectedValue`) and the selection events of that base class. `Value` is the
property to use in an application: it holds the selected option's value as a string, is two-way, and stays in sync
with `SelectedValue`. The toggle adds the savings badges, the gliding thumb and the period semantics on top of the
selecting control, so a billing screen gets a complete control without a custom template.

### Anatomy

1. **Track** (`BillingToggle` itself): a pill on the muted surface color with a 1 px subtle border. It is inset by 3 px
   on every side (4 px in `Large`) and holds the options in a horizontal row.
2. **Thumb**: a raised pill on the raised surface color with a soft shadow, under the selected option. It is one
   shape for the whole track, and it moves between options instead of appearing in each one.
3. **Option** (one `BillingToggleOption` per period): 34 px tall in `Medium` and 42 px in `Large`. It has 14 px side
   padding (18 px in `Large`) and the label in medium weight.
4. **Label** (`Label`, or `Value` when no label is given): the period name, such as "Monthly" or "Yearly". The text uses
   the small type size in `Medium` and the base size in `Large`.
5. **Badge** (`Badge`): a savings note 24 px tall in `Medium` and 32 px in `Large`, 8 px of side inset, in a pill with a
   quiet background (the foreground at 6%) and secondary text. It sits 8 px after the label.
6. **Active badge** (`ActiveBadge`): the text the badge shows while its option is selected, such as "You save $48".
   When it is not set, the badge keeps `Badge`. The badge takes the accent color while selected (see Size and accent).
7. **Focus ring**: a 2 px ring around the selected option. It appears for keyboard focus only.

A `BillingPrice` is a separate control with its own parts: the currency sign, the amount in the display font, the
old price (`WasAmount`) struck through to the left of the period text, and the period text (`Period`). The currency sign
is set at about 0.55 of the amount's size and raised to sit level with the top of the figures.

### Custom options

Write the options inline or bind `ItemsSource` to a list of `BillingToggleOption` objects. Options added inline must
exist before the toggle joins the logical tree, because the toggle installs its default Monthly and Yearly options only
when it has no options at that moment. `Badge` is shown on the option. `ActiveBadge` replaces it while the option is
selected, so a note can change in place without moving the content around it. Every badge text an option can show
reserves the same width, so "Save 20%" and "You save $48" do not move the neighboring option.

Use a badge for information that helps choose the option: a saving, a "Best value" marker or a plan limit. Leave it out
when every option has the same cost, because a badge that says nothing extra adds noise to the row.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.BillingToggleThreePeriodsDemo">
    <arc:BillingToggle Size="Large" Value="monthly" HorizontalAlignment="Center">
        <arc:BillingToggleOption Value="monthly" Label="Monthly" />
        <arc:BillingToggleOption Value="yearly" Label="Yearly" Badge="Save 20%" ActiveBadge="You save $48" />
        <arc:BillingToggleOption Value="lifetime" Label="Lifetime" Badge="Best value" />
    </arc:BillingToggle>
</UserControl>
```

### Prices

`BillingPrice` shows an amount. `Currency` defaults to `$` and `Decimals` to 0; a negative `Decimals` counts as 0.
`Amount` is a `decimal`, and the value is formatted with the en-US culture, so use a `decimal` and not a formatted
string. `WasAmount` draws the old price struck through when it is higher than `Amount`; a lower or null value hides it.
`Period` is the text after the amount, and it swaps in place when it changes.

```xml
<arc:BillingPrice Amount="24" WasAmount="30" Period="per month" />
```

When the period changes, update the price in the same handler that receives the toggle's value. The amount rolls to
the new number, the old price fades out with its own last value, and the period text swaps. The example below sets the
three values together, so the card never shows a new amount with an old period.

```csharp
var toggle = new BillingToggle { Value = "yearly" };
var price = new BillingPrice { Amount = 24, WasAmount = 30, Period = "per month, billed yearly" };

toggle.ValueChanged += (_, e) =>
{
    var yearly = e.NewValue == "yearly";
    price.Amount = yearly ? 24 : 30;
    price.WasAmount = yearly ? 30 : null;
    price.Period = yearly ? "per month, billed yearly" : "per month";
};
```

The `ValueChanged` event carries `OldValue` and `NewValue`. It bubbles, so a handler on a parent panel also receives
it. Use the event for side effects such as tracking or reloading a quote; use the bound view model for the data.

### Size and accent

`Size` sets the option height: `Medium` is 34 and `Large` is 42. Use one size for the whole billing area. `Medium`
fits a settings form and a pricing row; `Large` suits the hero of a pricing page, where the toggle is the first control a
visitor touches. The track inset and the text size grow with the size, so the two sizes are not simply scaled copies.

`BadgeAccent` colors the selected badge. Its default is the Arc success color. The badge background is the accent at
13% opacity in the light theme and 18% in the dark theme, and the badge text is the accent mixed with a little
foreground in the light theme. The accent is a brush the app may set, so it is derived in code rather than read from a
token. Keep the accent to the success or information family: a red or amber badge reads as a warning, not as a saving.

```xml
<arc:BillingToggle Size="Large" Value="yearly" />
```

### Binding to a view model

`Value` is two-way and carries the selected option's value. Bind it to a string property in the view model. The prices
are one-way inputs of `BillingPrice`, so the view model owns their numbers.

```csharp
public partial class PricingViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    [ObservableProperty]
    private string? _billingPeriod = "yearly";

    [ObservableProperty]
    private decimal _proAmount = 24;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private decimal? _proWasAmount = 30;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private string _proPeriod = "per month, billed yearly";

    partial void OnBillingPeriodChanged(string? value)
    {
        var yearly = value == "yearly";
        ProAmount = yearly ? 24 : 30;
        ProWasAmount = yearly ? 30 : null;
        ProPeriod = yearly ? "per month, billed yearly" : "per month";
    }
}
```

```xml
<StackPanel Spacing="24">
    <arc:BillingToggle Value="{Binding BillingPeriod}" HorizontalAlignment="Center" />
    <arc:BillingPrice Amount="{Binding ProAmount}"
                      WasAmount="{Binding ProWasAmount}"
                      Period="{Binding ProPeriod}" />
</StackPanel>
```

- `Value` is two-way. A change made by the person writes the new value back to `BillingPeriod`, and a change made in
  code selects the matching option.
- Bind `BillingPeriod` as a `string`. Options carry string values such as "monthly" and "yearly"; map it to an enum in the
  view model.
- Set the three price properties from one method, as `OnBillingPeriodChanged` does, so the view model never exposes
  a half-updated price.
- Compiled bindings need `x:DataType` on the view (the examples here leave it out for brevity).

### Example: plan section of a pricing page

A pricing page for a project management product, Northwind Cloud. The toggle sits above three plans. Each plan shows
its monthly price under yearly billing, the old monthly price struck through and the period beside it. The yearly
option carries the saving, and the Pro plan has a call to action in a card the same height as its neighbors.

![A pricing section with a yearly billing toggle and three plan prices with struck-through monthly prices](https://docs.tkcode.si/shots/Docs/Toggles/BillingToggle/images/PricingPlans.webp)

```xml
<StackPanel Width="680" Spacing="24">
```

### Content guidelines

- **Option label**: a single word for the period: "Monthly", "Yearly", "Lifetime". Use sentence case, and avoid
  "Pay yearly" or "Annual billing" because the toggle is a choice of period, not an action.
- **Badge**: a short saving or a single fact: "Save 20%", "Best value". Write percentages with the digit and the sign,
  and money with the currency sign and no decimals when the amount is whole.
- **Active badge**: the saving in money for the selected period, such as "You save $48". Keep it the same length as
  the badge when you can; a long active text makes the option wider and the row jumps.
- **Price period**: state the basis of the price, "per month, billed yearly", so the person knows the total they
  will be charged. A price without a period is ambiguous.
- **Accessible name**: name the group for what it selects when "Billing period" is not the right name, for example
  "Subscription term" in a renewal dialog.

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| Pay annually | Yearly |
| Save 20 percent | Save 20% |
| $24/mo | $24 per month, billed yearly |
| Best deal!!! | Best value |
| Annual plan billing cycle | Billing period |

### Best practices

**Do**

- Keep the monthly price visible when the yearly price is shown, with `WasAmount` or nearby text, so the saving is
  checked against a real number.
- Set `Size="Large"` for the hero toggle of a pricing page and `Medium` for settings. Mixing sizes in one row makes the
  options look unrelated.
- Update the amount, the old price and the period together, in one handler or one view model method.
- Bind `Value` to a string property, and keep the option values stable ("monthly", "yearly") because your backend and
  analytics store them.

**Avoid**

- Using the toggle to switch a list or a dashboard view. People expect a period switch to change prices, so a view
  switch that moves the badges and numbers reads as a broken price change.
- Long badge text in a short option. The badge reserves the width of every text it can show, so a long active text
  forces the whole row wider.
- Setting `WasAmount` to a value equal to or lower than `Amount` expecting a strike-through. It hides the old price,
  so the saving disappears without an explanation.
- Coloring the badge with a warning color; the accent is for a saving or a benefit, and a warning hides the message.
- Hiding the period text, which tells the person whether the amount is monthly or a yearly total.

### Common questions

**Why does my toggle show Monthly and Yearly when I did not add options?** With no items of its own, the toggle installs
`DefaultOptions` (Monthly, and Yearly with "Save 20%") when it joins the logical tree. Add your own options, or
`ItemsSource`, before the toggle is attached to show different periods.

**What is selected when I do not set `Value`?** The first option is selected when `Value` is unset, and that choice is written back to `Value`. Set `Value` explicitly when the default period must be a
particular one, such as yearly, and not the first option.

**The old price does not appear.** `WasAmount` shows only when it is higher than `Amount`. Set it to `null` to hide the
old price, or check that the monthly price is the larger number.

**Can I use a number or an enum as the value?** The `Value` property and `BillingToggleOption.Value` are strings. Use a
string key such as "yearly" and map it to your enum in the view model. 

**How do I change the accessible name of the group?** Set `AutomationProperties.Name` on the toggle. The default name is
"Billing period". Each option is announced with its label and its current badge, such as "Yearly Save 20%".

## API reference

### BillingToggle

Arc billing toggle: a billing period switch. One thumb glides between the options on a critically damped spring, and the savings note on the cheaper period tints with `BadgeAccent` and rewrites itself in place once it is chosen. Defaults to Monthly / Yearly ("Save 20%"); supply `BillingToggleOption` items (inline or via `ItemsSource`) for other periods. `Value` is two-way. Pair it with `BillingPrice` for prices that roll to the new amount.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Value` | `string?` | `null` | The selected option's value (two-way). |
| `Size` | `BillingToggleSize` | `Medium` | Option size: Medium (34px, default) or Large (42px). |
| `BadgeAccent` | `IBrush?` | `null` | Color of a selected savings badge (Arc's `--billing-accent`, default `Success`). |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ValueChanged` | `BillingToggleValueChangedEventArgs` | Raised when `Value` changes, with the old and new values. |

Derives from `SelectingItemsControl`: every member of `SelectingItemsControl` works as well.
### BillingPrice

The price beside a `BillingToggle` (Arc `BillingPrice`): the amount rolls digit by digit to its new value (`AnimatedCounter`, P14), a struck-through previous price fades in from the left while its width springs open, and the period text swaps in place while its width eases, so nothing beside them jumps.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Amount` | `decimal` | `0` | The price shown, formatted with Currency and Decimals. |
| `Currency` | `string` | `"$"` | Sign or text placed before the amount (default "$"). |
| `Decimals` | `int` | `0` | Digits after the decimal point; negative values count as 0. |
| `WasAmount` | `decimal?` | `null` | Previous price, shown struck through when it is higher than `Amount`. |
| `Period` | `string?` | `null` | Period after the price, e.g. "per month". Swaps in place when it changes. |

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.
### BillingToggleOption

One billing period of a `BillingToggle` (Arc `BillingToggleOption`).

### BillingToggleValueChangedEventArgs

| Property | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `OldValue` | `string?` | The value before the change. |
| `NewValue` | `string?` | The value after the change. |

### BillingToggleSize

| Member | Description |
|---|---|
| `Medium` | 34 px options (the default). |
| `Large` | 42 px options with the base text size. |

## Accessibility

- The group is named "Billing period" by default. Set `AutomationProperties.Name` to name it differently.
- Each option is a radio button. Its name is the label and the current badge, such as "Yearly Save 20%". The badge text
  shown while the option is selected is the active badge, when one is set.
- The thumb is hidden from assistive technology. A `BillingPrice` reads as its amount, its old price and its period, such
  as "$24, was $30 per month".
- Tab focuses the selected option. Arrow keys select and focus the next or previous option and wrap around. Home and End
  select the first and last option.
- Keyboard focus draws a 2 px outline offset by 2 px. Pointer focus does not.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` | Move focus into the group on the selected option, and out of it. Only the selected option is a tab stop. |
| `Right` / `Down` | Select and focus the next option; from the last option it wraps to the first. |
| `Left` / `Up` | Select and focus the previous option; from the first option it wraps to the last. |
| `Home` / `End` | Select and focus the first or the last option. |

## Motion

- The thumb slides under the selected option on a critically damped spring of about 0.34 seconds, with no bounce.
- The badge of the selected option takes the accent color, and its text swaps with a blur transition.
- Prices roll to the new amount. The old price collapses away, and the period text swaps in place.
- Reduced motion places the thumb at once and removes the press scale on unselected options. Off does the same.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| The selected option changes | The thumb glides on a critically damped spring, about 0.34 s, with no bounce | The thumb moves at once | The thumb moves at once |
| An unselected option is pressed | The option scales to 97% while pressed | No press scale | No press scale |
| The option text changes color on hover or selection | Color eases over the fast tween | Immediate | Immediate |
