| The selected badge takes its accent | Background eases over the standard tween; the badge text swaps with a blur | Immediate | Immediate |

## Related

- `SegmentedControl` for views that switch content without a price.
- `RadioGroup` for options that need descriptions or a vertical layout.
- `RadioCards` for plans that need a price, a description and a reason when unavailable.
- `Switch` for a single setting that takes effect at once.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `SegmentedControl` | The options switch a view, a filter or a layout and carry no price or saving |
| `RadioGroup` | The options need a description or a vertical layout |
| `RadioCards` | Each option is a plan with its own price, features and an unavailable reason |
| `Switch` | A single setting takes effect at once |
| `Select` / `Combobox` | The list is long, or the options are not a short fixed set |
| `Checkbox` | The person chooses several independent items, not one period |

---

# Checkbox

> A binary choice with a precise, legible state.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/checkbox

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.CheckboxLabelAndDescriptionDemo">
    <arc:Checkbox Content="Accept terms and conditions"
                  Description="You agree to our Terms of Service and Privacy Policy."
                  HorizontalAlignment="Center" />
</UserControl>
```

## When to use

`Checkbox` is the control for an independent yes or no choice that a person makes inside a form, a settings panel or a
table toolbar. It carries its own label and help text, and it has an indeterminate state for a parent row whose children
are only partly selected. Use it wherever the choice is confirmed by a submit or a save, and where the result is not
applied the moment the box changes.

- **Consent and terms in sign-up and checkout**: "Accept the data processing terms" with the description that says what
  the consent covers. The checkbox is required before the Create account button continues.
- **Notification channels in an admin console**: a parent row "All channels" with the Email, Slack and SMS children
  under it. The parent shows the indeterminate state when some channels are on, so the summary matches the details.
- **Row selection in a data table**: a header checkbox that selects every visible invoice, shown as indeterminate when
  only some rows are selected. The table applies the selection when the person runs a bulk action.
- **Opt-in options in a settings form**: "Send a copy of each invoice to the billing contact". The value is saved with
  the form, and the description states the consequence in one line.
- **Filters in a list view where the change applies on save**: a set of statuses in an export dialog, where the person
  picks several and presses Export.

## When not to use

- **A setting that takes effect at once**, such as turning on two-factor sign-in or pausing invoice emails: use
  `Switch`, which reads as an immediate on or off.
- **Choosing exactly one option from a set**, such as a billing country or a plan period: use `RadioGroup`, where the
  choice of one clears the others.
- **A frequently toggled filter shown as a row of chips**, such as Open, Overdue and Paid above a table: use
  `ChipGroup`. Chips are compact and read as filters, not as form fields.
- **A period or a view that switches between two states with a price or content change**, such as Monthly and Yearly:
  use `BillingToggle` or `SegmentedControl`.
- **Several independent choices that each need a long description and a price**, such as add-ons on a plan: use
  `RadioCards` when the person picks one plan, or a stack of checkboxes with descriptions in a settings form when the
  choices are independent.

## Usage

The label is the content of the control. `Description` adds a line of help text under the label. The control derives
from Avalonia's `CheckBox`, so `IsChecked` (a `bool?`, where `null` is indeterminate) and `IsThreeState` work as they do
in Avalonia. The Arc additions are the `CheckedState` enum, the description, the invalid and required states, and the
`CheckedStateChanged` event.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:Checkbox Content="Accept terms and conditions"
                  Description="You agree to our Terms of Service and Privacy Policy." />
</UserControl>
```

### Anatomy

1. **Hit area**: a 44 px square (the Arc control size). The whole square answers a click or a tap, and it is the row's
   pointer target even though the drawn box is smaller. The hit area is at the top of the row, so the first line of the
   label lines up with the box.
2. **Box**: an 18 px square with a 5 px corner radius and a 1 px border. It is centered in the hit area. Unchecked, the
   border uses the strong border color; hover darkens it to the muted text color; invalid (and unchecked) it uses the
   danger color.
3. **Fill and mark**: a checked or indeterminate box fills with the control-on color. The check or the dash is a 1.75 px
   stroke in the control glyph color, drawn with round caps and joins.
4. **Label** (`Content`): medium weight, one or more lines with a 19.6 px line height. It starts after the hit area and
   names the control for assistive technology.
5. **Description** (`Description`): extra-small text in the muted color with a 16.8 px line height, 2 px under the label.
   It is hidden when the description is empty.
6. **Focus ring**: a 2 px ring drawn around the hit area for keyboard focus. It is hidden for pointer focus.

The Arc checkbox has no size property: the box stays 18 px. A checkbox grows taller only with its label and
description, for example when the description runs to two lines.

### Required and invalid

`IsRequired` marks the field as required in a form. It is reported to assistive technology as required and does not draw
anything. `IsInvalid` shows the error state: while the box is unchecked, its border uses the danger color. A checked box
never shows the error, so clear `IsInvalid` as soon as the person checks it, or leave it set and let the check hide the
danger border.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.CheckboxStatesDemo">
    <WrapPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center" ItemSpacing="12" LineSpacing="12">
        <arc:Checkbox Content="Disabled" IsEnabled="False" />
        <arc:Checkbox Content="Disabled checked" IsChecked="True" IsEnabled="False" />
        <arc:Checkbox Content="Required"
                      Description="Check this box to continue."
                      IsInvalid="True"
                      IsRequired="True" />
        <arc:Checkbox />
    </WrapPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```xml
<arc:Checkbox Content="Accept terms and conditions"
              Description="Check this box to continue."
              IsRequired="True"
              IsInvalid="True" />
```

### Validation

A checkbox has one rule in most forms: it must be checked before the form is saved. The control reports the requirement
and the danger border, but the application decides when to show them. Show the required state at the moment the person
can act on it, and keep the message in the description so the layout does not move.

| Rule | When to check | Where it shows |
|---|---|---|
| Required consent | On submit, then as the box changes | `IsInvalid` (danger border) and a description such as "Check this box to continue." |
| Parent and children consistent | Whenever a child changes | `CheckedState` of the parent; it is not an error |
| Server rejects the choice | After the request | Description text, cleared when the box changes |

```csharp
// On submit: mark the unchecked box and move focus to it.
acceptTerms.IsInvalid = acceptTerms.IsChecked != true;
if (acceptTerms.IsInvalid)
{
    acceptTerms.Focus();
    return;
}

// Clear the mark as soon as the person checks the box.
acceptTerms.IsCheckedChanged += (_, _) => acceptTerms.IsInvalid = false;
```

### Indeterminate parent

`CheckedState` is an enum with `Unchecked`, `Checked` and `Indeterminate`. `IsChecked` is the same value as a nullable
boolean, where `null` means indeterminate. Set the parent to indeterminate while some children are checked.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.CheckboxIndeterminateParentDemo">
    <StackPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center">
        <arc:Checkbox x:Name="All" Content="All channels" CheckedStateChanged="OnAllChanged" />
        <arc:Checkbox x:Name="Email"
                      Content="Email"
                      Margin="28,0,0,0"
                      CheckedStateChanged="OnChildChanged" />
        <arc:Checkbox x:Name="Push"
                      Content="Push notifications"
                      Margin="28,0,0,0"
                      CheckedStateChanged="OnChildChanged" />
        <arc:Checkbox x:Name="Sms"
                      Content="SMS"
                      Margin="28,0,0,0"
                      CheckedStateChanged="OnChildChanged" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class CheckboxIndeterminateParentDemo : UserControl
{
    private bool _syncing;

    public CheckboxIndeterminateParentDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Email.IsChecked = true;
    }

    private Checkbox[] Children => [Email, Push, Sms];

    // The parent reflects its children: checked, unchecked or indeterminate (the check morphs into a dash).
    private void OnChildChanged(object? sender, CheckboxStateChangedEventArgs e)
    {
        if (_syncing)
        {
            return;
        }
        _syncing = true;
        var on = Children.Count(c => c.IsChecked == true);
        All.CheckedState = on == 0
            ? CheckboxState.Unchecked
            : on == Children.Length ? CheckboxState.Checked : CheckboxState.Indeterminate;
        _syncing = false;
    }

    // A click on the parent sets every child.
    private void OnAllChanged(object? sender, CheckboxStateChangedEventArgs e)
    {
        if (_syncing || e.NewState == CheckboxState.Indeterminate)
        {
            return;
        }
        _syncing = true;
        foreach (var child in Children)
        {
            child.IsChecked = e.NewState == CheckboxState.Checked;
        }
        _syncing = false;
    }
}
```

```xml
<arc:Checkbox Content="All channels" CheckedState="Indeterminate" />
```

To make a click on the parent set every child, handle `CheckedStateChanged` on the parent and set each child's
`IsChecked` to the new state. Skip the indeterminate state in that handler, because a parent cannot set its children to
"partly checked". The demo above also updates the parent from the children, and it guards both handlers with a flag so
they do not call each other.

Clicking an indeterminate parent checks it, as Radix does, and clicking a checked parent clears it. A parent that sets
its children, as the demo does, therefore sets every child on the next click. Use this order when the parent is the
"select all" control of a table or a list.

### Three-state cycle

`IsThreeState="True"` makes a click cycle through unchecked, checked and indeterminate, as the Avalonia `CheckBox` does.
Use the cycle only when the indeterminate state is itself a choice, such as a filter that means "either" in a list. For
a parent that only summarizes its children, keep the default two-state behavior, where a click on indeterminate checks
the box.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.CheckboxTriStateDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="8" HorizontalAlignment="Center">
        <arc:Checkbox x:Name="Cycle" Content="Three-state cycle" IsThreeState="True" />
        <TextBlock FontSize="12"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}"
                   Text="{Binding #Cycle.CheckedState, StringFormat='State: {0}'}" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

### Binding to a view model

In an MVVM app, bind `IsChecked` to a `bool?` property, or bind `CheckedState` to the enum when the view model prefers
three named values. Both are two-way. The indeterminate parent is a computed value, so the view model derives it from
the children rather than storing it.

```csharp
public partial class NotificationsViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    [ObservableProperty]
    [NotifyPropertyChangedFor(nameof(AllChannels))]
    private bool _email = true;

    [ObservableProperty]
    [NotifyPropertyChangedFor(nameof(AllChannels))]
    private bool _slack = true;

    [ObservableProperty]
    [NotifyPropertyChangedFor(nameof(AllChannels))]
    private bool _sms;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private bool _acceptTerms;

    public CheckboxState AllChannels => (Email, Slack, Sms) switch
    {
        (true, true, true) => CheckboxState.Checked,
        (false, false, false) => CheckboxState.Unchecked,
        _ => CheckboxState.Indeterminate
    };

    [RelayCommand]
    private void SetAllChannels(CheckboxState state)
    {
        if (state == CheckboxState.Indeterminate)
        {
            return;
        }
        Email = Slack = Sms = state == CheckboxState.Checked;
    }
}
```

```xml
<StackPanel Spacing="8">
    <arc:Checkbox Content="All channels"
                  CheckedState="{Binding AllChannels, Mode=OneWay}" />
    <arc:Checkbox Content="Email" IsChecked="{Binding Email}" Margin="28,0,0,0" />
    <arc:Checkbox Content="Slack" IsChecked="{Binding Slack}" Margin="28,0,0,0" />
    <arc:Checkbox Content="SMS" IsChecked="{Binding Sms}" Margin="28,0,0,0" />
    <arc:Checkbox Content="Accept terms and conditions"
                  IsChecked="{Binding AcceptTerms}"
                  IsRequired="True" />
</StackPanel>
```

- The parent reads the computed `AllChannels` one way. A click on the parent changes only the control, so handle
  `CheckedStateChanged` in code-behind and pass `e.NewState` to `SetAllChannelsCommand`; the children then update the
  view model. The demo above does the same work in code-behind.
- `IsChecked` is two-way, so a child box changes the view model directly and `AllChannels` updates through the
  notifications.
- Compiled bindings need `x:DataType` on the view (the examples here leave it out for brevity).

### Events

`CheckedStateChanged` reports the old and the new state. It is raised only when the state actually changes, and it
bubbles, so a handler on a parent panel also receives it. `IsCheckedChanged` (inherited from the Avalonia checkbox) is
raised for each change of `IsChecked`, including the change from `true` to `null`.

```csharp
checkbox.CheckedStateChanged += (_, e) =>
{
    Console.WriteLine($"{e.OldState} -> {e.NewState}");
};
```

### Example: notification settings for invoice reminders

A billing settings screen in a SaaS admin console. The parent row "All channels" is indeterminate because Email and
Slack are on and SMS is off, so the summary matches the children. The terms checkbox is required and shows its danger
border because the person has not accepted yet, and the audit line is disabled because the product always records it.
Each label names the thing the box turns on, and each description states the consequence in one line.

![A notification settings form with an indeterminate parent checkbox, a required terms checkbox and a disabled checkbox](https://docs.tkcode.si/shots/Docs/Toggles/Checkbox/images/InvoiceReminders.webp)

```xml
<StackPanel Width="560" Spacing="14">
    <TextBlock Text="Invoice reminders"
               FontSize="16"
               FontWeight="SemiBold"
               Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
    <arc:Checkbox Content="All channels"
                  CheckedState="Indeterminate"
                  Description="Email and Slack are on. SMS is off." />
    <StackPanel Margin="28,0,0,0" Spacing="6">
        <arc:Checkbox Content="Email" IsChecked="True" />
        <arc:Checkbox Content="Slack" IsChecked="True" />
        <arc:Checkbox Content="SMS" />
    </StackPanel>
    <arc:Checkbox Content="Send a copy to the billing contact"
                  Description="Copies go to billing@northwind.com."
                  IsChecked="True" />
    <arc:Checkbox Content="Accept the data processing terms"
                  Description="Check this box to turn on invoice reminders."
                  IsRequired="True"
                  IsInvalid="True" />
    <arc:Checkbox Content="Keep the audit log"
                  Description="Always on for this workspace."
                  IsChecked="True"
                  IsEnabled="False" />
</StackPanel>
```

### Content guidelines

- **Label**: name the thing the box turns on or agrees to, in sentence case, as a short phrase: "Email invoice
  reminders", "Accept the data processing terms". Avoid a bare noun such as "Email" when the box does something more
  specific.
- **Description**: one sentence with the consequence or the requirement: "Copies go to billing@northwind.com", "Check
  this box to continue". Write numbers as digits.
- **Invalid message**: say what to do, not that something failed. Put it in the description, because `IsInvalid` only
  draws the danger border.
- **Parent label**: use the scope of the children, such as "All channels" or "All invoices on this page", so the parent
  reads as a summary of its children.

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| Email | Email invoice reminders |
| Terms | Accept the data processing terms |
| Required field!!! | Check this box to continue. |
| Yes / No | Send a copy to the billing contact |

### Best practices

**Do**

- Use a checkbox for an independent choice that is saved with the form, and a `Switch` for a setting that applies at
  once. The person expects a checkbox to wait for the save.
- Keep the label and the description short enough for one or two lines, so the hit area and the label line up.
- Show the indeterminate state on a parent row whenever its children are partly selected, so the summary is true.
- Mark a required box only on submit, and move focus to it, so the person is not told about a field they have not yet
  reached.

**Avoid**

- Using a checkbox for one of two mutually exclusive options. A pair of checkboxes that cannot both be on should be a
  `RadioGroup`.
- Putting the only explanation of an error in the danger color. A red border without words tells the person nothing.
- Disabling a checkbox without a reason. Say in the description why it cannot change, as the audit line does.
- Changing the parent's state from its own handler and also from its children in the same pass; the two updates then
  call each other. Guard one direction with a flag, as the demo does.

### Common questions

**Why does clicking an indeterminate box check it instead of clearing it?** That follows Radix and the WAI-ARIA pattern:
an indeterminate box becomes checked on a click. A parent that should set its children to the opposite of the summary
must handle `CheckedStateChanged` and decide the next state itself.

**Why does Enter not toggle the checkbox?** The WAI-ARIA checkbox pattern uses Space. The checkbox does not handle Enter,
so the key reaches the window, and a form's default button runs.

**What is the difference between `IsRequired` and `IsInvalid`?** `IsRequired` tells assistive technology that the field
must be checked before the form is submitted, and draws nothing. `IsInvalid` draws the danger border while the box is
unchecked. Set `IsInvalid` from your own submit logic.

**How do I show a three-state option, such as Yes, No and Any?** Set `IsThreeState="True"` so a click cycles through
unchecked, checked and indeterminate. Store the value with `CheckedState` so the view model reads the three names.

**The box has no label, what name does it report?** When `Content` is empty and no name is set, the checkbox reports
"Checkbox". Set `AutomationProperties.Name` to name a box that has no visible label, such as a row selector in a table.

## API reference

### Checkbox

Arc checkbox: a binary choice with a precise, legible state. The fill grows in on a snappy spring, the check draws itself, and the indeterminate state morphs the same three-point path into a dash and back. Only the 18px square answers a press (it dips to 0.95); the 44px hit area and the label never move. Clicking an indeterminate box checks it (Radix behavior). `IsChecked` is the tri-state value (null = indeterminate); `CheckedState` is the same value as an enum.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Description` | `string?` | `null` | Secondary text under the label; also the help text read by assistive technology. |
| `IsInvalid` | `bool` | `false` | Marks the choice as invalid (the square takes the danger border). |
| `IsRequired` | `bool` | `false` | The field must be checked before a form is submitted (reported to assistive technology). |
| `CheckedState` | `CheckboxState` | `Unchecked` | The tri-state value as an enum; kept in sync with `IsChecked`. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `CheckedStateChanged` | `CheckboxStateChangedEventArgs` | Raised when the state changes, with the old and new `CheckboxState`. |

Pseudo-classes: `:invalid`

Derives from `CheckBox`: every member of `CheckBox` works as well.

### CheckboxState

| Member | Description |
|---|---|
| `Unchecked` | The box is empty. |
| `Checked` | The box shows a check. |
| `Indeterminate` | Some but not all children are checked; the check morphs into a dash. |

### CheckboxStateChangedEventArgs

| Property | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `OldState` | `CheckboxState` | The state before the change. |
| `NewState` | `CheckboxState` | The state after the change. |

## Accessibility

- The label is the checkbox's name. Without a label, set `AutomationProperties.Name`; the name falls back to "Checkbox".
- `Description` is the help text. Assistive technology reads it after the name.
- `IsRequired` is reported to assistive technology as required for the form. The visual mark is not needed for that.
- The indeterminate state is reported as a mixed state. The drawn check and dash are not exposed separately.
- The control exposes the checkbox pattern: a null `IsChecked` is reported as indeterminate, so a screen reader reports a
  parent row as indeterminate.
- Space toggles the box. Enter does not, as in the WAI-ARIA checkbox pattern.
- Keyboard focus draws a 2px outline offset by 2px. Pointer focus does not.
- The invalid border is a visual state. Pair it with a description that says what to fix, so the message does not rely
  on the color alone.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` | Move focus to the next or previous control. A disabled checkbox is skipped. |
| `Space` | Toggles the box: unchecked becomes checked, checked becomes unchecked, and indeterminate becomes checked. With `IsThreeState`, the cycle is unchecked, checked, indeterminate. |
| `Enter` | Does nothing on the checkbox. The key is not handled, so it reaches the window, and a form's default button still runs. |

## Motion

- The fill grows in from a slightly smaller size when the box is checked, and fades out quickly when it is cleared.
- The check draws in. Switching to indeterminate morphs the check into a dash, and back again.
- Pressing the box scales it down slightly, and release springs it back.
- Reduced motion applies every state change at once and removes the press scale. Off does the same.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| The box is checked | The fill grows in on a snappy spring and the check draws in | Applied at once | Applied at once |
| The box is cleared | The fill fades out quickly | Applied at once | Applied at once |
| Checked and indeterminate switch | The check morphs into the dash, or back | Applied at once | Applied at once |
| The box is pressed | The square scales to 95% at once; release springs it back | No press scale | No press scale |
| The border changes color (hover, invalid) | The border color eases quickly | Immediate | Immediate |

## Related

- `Switch` for a setting that takes effect at once.
- `RadioGroup` for choosing exactly one option from a set.
- `ChipGroup` for a set of filters the user toggles often.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `Switch` | A single setting takes effect when the person changes it |
| `RadioGroup` | Exactly one option from a set is chosen |
| `RadioCards` | Exactly one plan is chosen, and each option needs a price and a description |
| `ChipGroup` | A row of filters is toggled often above a list or a table |
| `BillingToggle` | A billing period is chosen with a savings note |
| `SegmentedControl` | The options switch a view without a choice of value to save |

---

# Radio group

> Choose one option from a visible set.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/radio-group

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.RadioGroupPlansDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12" HorizontalAlignment="Center">
        <arc:RadioGroup x:Name="Plans" Header="Plan" Width="420" SelectedValue="pro">
            <arc:RadioOption Value="hobby" Label="Hobby" Description="For side projects and experiments." />
            <arc:RadioOption Value="pro" Label="Pro" Description="For professionals who ship every week." />
            <arc:RadioOption Value="team"
                             Label="Team"
                             Description="Shared workspaces, roles and audit logs for growing teams." />
        </arc:RadioGroup>
        <TextBlock FontSize="12"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}"
                   Text="{Binding #Plans.SelectedValue, StringFormat='Selected: {0}'}" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

## When to use

A radio group shows a small set of mutually exclusive options with every option visible at once. It belongs in forms
and settings pages where the person must compare the choices before committing, and where each choice needs a
description to be understood. The group is a single labeled control: its header names it, its rows hold the options,
and its selection is one value the form can read or save.

- **Plan selection in a billing or upgrade page**: a workspace owner picks Hobby, Pro or Team. Each row carries a
  description of what the plan includes, which is the information the decision depends on.
- **Delivery or fulfillment options at checkout**: standard shipping, express or pickup, each with its delivery window
  as the description. The chosen option is submitted with the order.
- **Export format or report scope in an analytics console**: CSV, Parquet or JSON, or "This month" against "Year to
  date". Each row explains what the file contains, so the person does not guess.
- **Access or role choice in an invitation form**: Viewer, Editor or Admin, with a description of the permissions
  that come with each role. Use `IsDisabled` on a role the person's own plan does not include.
- **Environment or region selection in a developer tool**: a deployment target chosen once for a form, where every
  option must stay visible for review.

## When not to use

- **Short inline views that switch the content on screen**, such as Day, Week and Month on a chart: use
  `SegmentedControl`, which reads as a row of tabs and changes the view at once.
- **Long lists of options**, such as countries, currencies or teams with dozens of members: use `Select`, which keeps
  the list out of the way until it is needed.
- **More than one option at a time**, such as choosing several notification channels or product areas: use
  `Checkbox` for each option, since a radio group allows exactly one selection.
- **Options that need a price, a meta line or an icon on a card**: use `RadioCards`, which lays each option out as a
  selectable card.
- **A single on or off setting**, such as "Email me invoices": use `Switch`, which takes effect at once and needs no
  group.

## Usage

`Header` is the group's label. The options are the `Items` of the control; each `RadioOption` takes a value, a label
and an optional description.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:RadioGroup Header="Plan" Width="420" SelectedValue="pro">
        <arc:RadioOption Value="hobby" Label="Hobby" Description="For side projects and experiments." />
        <arc:RadioOption Value="pro" Label="Pro" Description="For professionals who ship every week." />
        <arc:RadioOption Value="team" Label="Team" Description="Shared workspaces, roles and audit logs for growing teams." />
    </arc:RadioGroup>
</UserControl>
```

`RadioGroup` derives from Avalonia's `HeaderedSelectingItemsControl`. Selection, `SelectedIndex`, `SelectedItem`,
`SelectionChanged`, the header and `HeaderTemplate` are therefore the same as in any Avalonia selecting control, and
the group adds the Arc row design, the single moving highlight, the keyboard model and the automation names on top.
The group creates one row for each option; you never add rows yourself.

### Anatomy

1. **Header** (`Header`): the group's legend, in medium weight, with 8 px below it before the first row. A string
   header also names the group for assistive technology. `HeaderTemplate` replaces the text with richer content.
2. **Rows**: the options, stacked with an 8 px gap. Each row is a 1 px bordered box with the control radius and 12 px
   of inner padding on every side. The row stretches to the width of the group.
3. **Ring**: a 17 px circle with a 1 px border in the strong border color. A selected ring fills with the accent
   color (`ControlOn`).
4. **Dot**: a 7 px dot in the glyph color (`ControlGlyph`) inside the ring. It appears only on the selected row.
   While the pointer is down on an unselected row, a faint dot at 22% opacity previews the choice.
5. **Label** (`RadioOption.Label`): medium weight, in the small type size. It sits 12 px to the right of the ring and
   falls back to the option's `Value` when `Label` is empty. Unselected labels use the secondary text color; the
   selected label uses the foreground color.
6. **Description** (`RadioOption.Description`): the extra line under the label, in the extra-small type size and the
   muted text color, 2 px below the label. It wraps on narrow widths and collapses when the description is empty.
7. **Highlight**: one outline that covers the selected row, with a 1 px accent stroke and a fill of the same color at
   5%. It is a single element for the whole group, so it moves between rows instead of appearing on each one.
8. **Focus ring**: a 2 px ring drawn 2 px outside the focused row. It appears only for keyboard focus.

The row height follows its content: a label alone gives a compact row, and a description adds one wrapped line per
text width. Disabled rows and a disabled group fade to 50% opacity.

### Bound options

Bind `ItemsSource` to a list of options and `SelectedValue` to the selected value. Both are two-way.

```xml
<arc:RadioGroup Header="Plan"
                ItemsSource="{Binding Plans}"
                SelectedValue="{Binding PlanId}" />
```

```csharp
var plans = new RadioGroup
{
    Header = "Plan",
    ItemsSource = new[]
    {
        new RadioOption("hobby", "Hobby", "For side projects and experiments."),
        new RadioOption("pro", "Pro", "For professionals who ship every week.")
    },
    SelectedValue = "pro"
};
plans.SelectionChanged += (_, _) => status.Text = $"Selected: {plans.SelectedValue}";
```

`SelectedValue` holds the selected option's `Value`, not the option object. Use `SelectedItem` when you need the whole
`RadioOption`, for example to read its description after a save. `SelectedValue` is applied when the options arrive,
so it can be set before `ItemsSource` in code or XAML.

### Binding to a view model

With CommunityToolkit.Mvvm, the view model owns the selected plan and the list of options, and the group only shows
them. `SelectedValue` and `SelectedItem` are two-way, so a change made by the pointer or the keyboard reaches the view
model at once.

```csharp
public interface IBillingService
{
    Task ChangePlanAsync(string planId);
}

public partial class UpgradeViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    private readonly IBillingService _billing;

    public UpgradeViewModel(IBillingService billing)
    {
        _billing = billing;
        Plans.Add(new RadioOption("hobby", "Hobby", "For side projects and experiments."));
        Plans.Add(new RadioOption("pro", "Pro", "For professionals who ship every week."));
        Plans.Add(new RadioOption("team", "Team", "Shared workspaces, roles and audit logs for growing teams."));
        SelectedPlanId = "pro";
    }

    public ObservableCollection<RadioOption> Plans { get; } = new();

    [ObservableProperty]
    private string? _selectedPlanId;

    [RelayCommand(CanExecute = nameof(CanSave))]
    private async Task SaveAsync()
    {
        await _billing.ChangePlanAsync(SelectedPlanId!);
    }

    private bool CanSave() => !string.IsNullOrEmpty(SelectedPlanId);

    partial void OnSelectedPlanIdChanged(string? value) => SaveCommand.NotifyCanExecuteChanged();
}
```

```xml
<StackPanel Width="420" Spacing="16">
    <arc:RadioGroup Header="Plan"
                    ItemsSource="{Binding Plans}"
                    SelectedValue="{Binding SelectedPlanId}" />
    <arc:Button Content="Change plan" Command="{Binding SaveCommand}" />
</StackPanel>
```

- `SelectedValue` is the property to bind for the saved choice. Bind `SelectedItem` as well only when the view needs the
  option object.
- `ItemsSource` takes an `ObservableCollection<RadioOption>`, so adding or removing an option updates the group.
- Use `SelectionChanged` in code for side effects that are not data, such as a preview label. Keep the save in the
  command, so it runs once when the person presses the button and not on every arrow key.
- Set `Header` in XAML with a plain string. A string header is also the group's accessible name.

### Disabled options

`IsDisabled` keeps an option visible but unavailable. Arrow keys skip disabled options, and the row cannot be selected
by the pointer or by Space and Enter.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.RadioGroupInlineOptionsDemo">
    <arc:RadioGroup Header="Density"
                    HorizontalAlignment="Center"
                    Width="420"
                    SelectedValue="comfortable">
        <arc:RadioOption Value="comfortable" Label="Comfortable" />
        <arc:RadioOption Value="compact" Label="Compact" />
        <arc:RadioOption Value="spacious" Label="Spacious" IsDisabled="True" />
    </arc:RadioGroup>
</UserControl>
```

Show a disabled option when the person needs to know it exists and why it is not available, such as a plan the account
has not reached yet. Say the reason in the option's description, for example "Available on the Team plan". Remove the
option instead when it is never relevant to this person.

### Selection events

`SelectionChanged` is raised when the selection changes, by the pointer or by the keyboard. `SelectedItem` gives the
`RadioOption` itself.

```csharp
group.SelectionChanged += (_, _) =>
{
    if (group.SelectedItem is RadioOption option)
    {
        Console.WriteLine(option.Value);
    }
};
```

### Option count and layout

The default items panel is a plain vertical `StackPanel`, so every option is created when the group is shown. That is
the right trade-off for two to six options with descriptions. For a longer list, use `Select`, which opens a list on
demand and does not place every row on the page. For a horizontal row of short views, use `SegmentedControl`.

Give the group a width at which the longest description wraps onto two or three lines. A very narrow group wraps each
description onto many short lines, and the options become harder to compare.

### Example: plan selection in a workspace upgrade

A billing page for a workspace owner, from a SaaS admin console. The header is a sentence that states the
consequence of the choice ("Changes take effect at the next invoice"). The three plans carry the one fact that
separates them, so the person can decide from the group alone. The selected row is Team, and the primary action names
what it does.

![A billing page with a plan group that has the Team plan selected and a save action](https://docs.tkcode.si/shots/Docs/Toggles/RadioGroup/images/UpgradePlan.webp)

```xml
<StackPanel Width="620" Spacing="20">
    <StackPanel Spacing="6">
        <TextBlock Text="Billing plan"
                   FontSize="18"
                   FontWeight="SemiBold"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
        <TextBlock Text="Acme Analytics renews on 1 December 2026. Changes take effect at the next invoice."
                   FontSize="13"
                   TextWrapping="Wrap"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
    </StackPanel>
    <arc:RadioGroup Header="Plan" SelectedValue="team">
        <arc:RadioOption Value="hobby"
                         Label="Hobby"
                         Description="One workspace, up to 3 seats, 30 days of history." />
        <arc:RadioOption Value="pro"
                         Label="Pro"
                         Description="Unlimited seats, 1 year of history and scheduled exports." />
        <arc:RadioOption Value="team"
                         Label="Team"
                         Description="Roles, audit logs and single sign-on for up to 500 seats." />
        <arc:RadioOption Value="enterprise"
                         Label="Enterprise"
                         Description="Contact sales. Available on annual contracts."
                         IsDisabled="True" />
    </arc:RadioGroup>
    <StackPanel Orientation="Horizontal" Spacing="8" HorizontalAlignment="Right">
        <arc:Button Content="Cancel" Variant="Secondary" />
        <arc:Button Content="Save plan" />
    </StackPanel>
</StackPanel>
```

### Content guidelines

- **Header**: a short noun phrase that names the choice: "Plan", "Delivery method", "Export format". Do not write a
  question ("Which plan?"); the options are the answer.
- **Option label**: one or two words that name the option as the person thinks of it: "Team", "Standard shipping".
  Use sentence case, and keep labels parallel, so every row is a plan or every row is a method.
- **Description**: one sentence with the fact that separates the option from the others: seats, history, delivery
  window, what is included. Write numbers as digits, and keep the descriptions about the same length.
- **Disabled reason**: name the condition in the description: "Available on the Team plan".

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| Which plan would you like? | Plan |
| Best value!!! | Unlimited seats and 1 year of history. |
| Option 2 | Pro |
| Contact our sales team for pricing information regarding enterprise options | Contact sales. Available on annual contracts. |

### Best practices

**Do**

- Put the option the person is most likely to choose first, or the one the account already has selected, so the
  decision starts from the current state.
- Give every option a description when the labels alone do not explain the difference. A row without a description is
  faster to read, so add one only when it carries information.
- Set a `SelectedValue` that matches the saved state. An empty selection shows no mark, which reads as an unanswered
  question on a form that expects an answer.
- Use `IsDisabled` for an option that exists but cannot apply, and say why in its description.

**Avoid**

- Radio groups for a yes or no choice. A `Switch` or a `Checkbox` says what the person is setting, and two radio rows
  ask the same thing twice.
- More than six options in a group. The page grows by a row for each option, and the choice becomes a scan rather
  than a comparison; use `Select` instead.
- Replacing the options on every refresh while the person is reading them. Update the collection only when the data
  changes, so the group does not redraw under the pointer.
- Relying on color alone to show the selection. The filled ring and the dot are the second cue that a selected row
  carries, so the choice does not depend on telling two colors apart.

### Common questions

**Does the group select anything by default?** No. `SelectedIndex` is -1 until a value is set, and no row shows the
mark. Set `SelectedValue` to the default you want.

**Can I set `SelectedValue` before the options arrive?** Yes. The value is applied when the options arrive, so a
group whose options load asynchronously keeps the value that was set first.

**Why does the group not name itself?** A string `Header` names the group. A non-string header, such as a panel with
a heading and a hint, does not, so set `AutomationProperties.Name` on the group in that case.

**How do I show the description of the selected option somewhere else?** Read `SelectedItem` as a `RadioOption` in
`SelectionChanged`, and show its `Description` in a text block. The group's own rows keep their descriptions.

**Can the rows take arbitrary objects?** Use `RadioOption` for every row. The row reads `Label`, `Description` and
`IsDisabled` from that type, so other objects do not give the row its text. Map your own model to `RadioOption` in
the view model.

## API reference

### RadioGroup

Arc radio group: choose one option from a visible set. One highlight (a `ControlOn` border with a faint fill) glides to the chosen row on the morph spring while the new dot springs in and the old one shrinks away, so a change reads as a single physical move. Arrow keys take the same path; the group is one tab stop (the selected row). Options come from `ItemsSource` or inline `RadioOption` items; `SelectedValue` (two-way) is the selected option's `Value`. The `Header` is the legend and the group's accessible name.

Derives from `HeaderedSelectingItemsControl`: every member of `HeaderedSelectingItemsControl` works as well.
### RadioOption

One option of a `RadioGroup` (Arc `{ value, label, description? }`). Use it in `ItemsSource` or inline in XAML; the group reports `Value` as its `SelectedValue`.

## Accessibility

- `Header` names the group when it is a string. Each option is a radio button, and its description is the help text.
- The group is one tab stop. Tab enters it at the selected option, and the next Tab leaves it. Keyboard focus never
  stops on an unselected option.
- Arrow keys move the selection to the next or previous option and wrap around. Disabled options are skipped.
- Home and End select the first and last option. Space and Enter select the focused option.
- The highlight and the dot are hidden from assistive technology. Each option reports whether it is selected.
- Keyboard focus draws a 2px ring around the row. Pointer focus does not draw one.
- Color is not the only cue: the selected row has a filled ring, a dot and a foreground label.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Tab` | Enters the group at the selected option; the next `Tab` leaves the group |
| `Down` / `Right` | Selects and focuses the next option, wrapping from the last to the first |
| `Up` / `Left` | Selects and focuses the previous option, wrapping from the first to the last |
| `Home` / `End` | Selects and focuses the first or last option |
| `Space` / `Enter` | Selects the focused option |

Arrow keys skip disabled options, in both directions.

## Motion

- One highlight glides to the selected row on a morph spring. The new dot springs in while the old one shrinks away,
  so a change reads as one physical move.
- Pressing a ring scales it down slightly. Pressing an unselected row previews its dot.
- When the group changes size, the highlight moves to its new row at once.
- Reduced motion places the highlight and the dot at once and removes the press scale. Off does the same.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| Selection moves | The highlight glides on a morph spring; the new dot springs in from 40% and fades in | The highlight and the dot land at once | Immediate |
| Old dot leaves | Shrinks and fades out at once | Immediate | Immediate |
| Ring press | Scales to 88% while held; springs back on release | No scale | No scale |
| Unselected row pressed | The preview dot shows at 22% opacity | The preview dot shows | The preview dot shows |
| Row and label colors | Background and ring colors crossfade; the label color crossfades | Immediate | Immediate |
| Group resizes | The highlight moves to the new row at once | Immediate | Immediate |

## Related

- `RadioCards` for options that need a price, a meta text or an icon on a card.
- `SegmentedControl` for two to five short views that switch the content at once.
- `Checkbox` when the person may choose several options.
- `Select` for a long list of options.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `RadioCards` | Each option needs a price, a meta line or an icon, and the cards compare well side by side |
| `SegmentedControl` | Two to five short views of the same content switch at once |
| `Checkbox` | The person may select several options, or one option is a yes or no setting |
| `Select` | The list is long, or the options are many items such as countries or teams |
| `Switch` | A single setting takes effect at once with no group |

---

# Switch

> A tactile toggle for settings that take effect immediately.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/switch

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.SwitchSettingsListDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="4">
        <arc:Switch Content="Email notifications" IsChecked="True" />
        <arc:Switch Content="Weekly digest" />
        <arc:Switch Content="Product updates" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

## When to use

A switch turns one setting on or off, and the change takes effect as soon as the person makes it. It belongs in a
settings page, a preferences panel or an account area, where each row is a setting that can be changed alone and does
not wait for a save button. The track and thumb show the state at a glance, so the person sees the current setting
without reading a label twice.

- **Notification preferences in an admin console**: "Email me when a payment fails" or "Send a weekly revenue digest".
  Each switch applies its setting on the spot, and the page needs no confirm step.
- **Feature availability in a SaaS workspace**: "Enable beta reports" or "Show archived projects". The switch is the
  only control on its row, so the label states what changes.
- **Privacy and data sharing in an account page**: "Share usage data with the product team". A switch gives the
  person a clear on or off choice with the current state visible.
- **A settings list with one switch per row**: a notifications page where each channel, such as email, SMS or in-app,
  has its own switch and its own description.
- **Operational toggles in a developer tool**: "Pause deployments for this project" or "Mirror logs to the audit
  stream". The effect starts at once, so the switch must not be used where a review step is required.

## When not to use

- **A choice that is confirmed with a submit button**, such as accepting terms or opting in to a plan at checkout:
  use `Checkbox`, whose value is saved only when the form is submitted.
- **A choice among named options**, such as Day, Week or Month: use `SegmentedControl` for short views, or
  `RadioGroup` for options that need a description each.
- **Several options where the person picks more than one**: use one `Checkbox` for each option, so the form reads as a
  list of choices rather than a list of switches with interdependent meanings.
- **An action that runs now**, such as "Restart service" or "Send invoice": use `Button`. A switch names a state,
  and a button names an action.
- **A setting that needs a confirmation or a reason before it applies**, such as disabling single sign-on: show a
  dialog from the action that changes it, instead of a switch that applies the change at once.

## Usage

`Content` is the label of the switch. The whole label is part of the click target.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:Switch Content="Email notifications" IsChecked="True" />
</UserControl>
```

`Switch` derives from Avalonia's `ToggleButton`, so `IsChecked`, `IsCheckedChanged`, `Content` and the click and
keyboard behavior of a toggle button are all there. The control adds the track and thumb design, the press stretch
of the thumb and the Arc motion. The state is two-valued: `IsChecked` is `true` or `false`, and the switch has no
mixed state.

### Anatomy

1. **Track** (42 by 24 px, fully rounded): the surface the thumb moves on. It is the control track color when off, the
   track color on hover when off, and the accent color (`ControlOn`) when on. It fades to the accent color when the
   state changes.
2. **Thumb** (18 px, fully rounded, with the Arc thumb shadow): sits 3 px inside the track. It travels 18 px from the
   off position to the on position. Its color is the thumb color when off and the on-thumb color when on.
3. **Pressed thumb**: while the pointer or the Space key is held, the thumb widens to 23 px toward the other side, and
   its far edge stays where it is. This is the press feedback, and it shows which way the thumb will go.
4. **Label** (`Content`): 12 px to the right of the track, in the small type size and the foreground color. It is
   hidden when `Content` is empty.
5. **Focus ring**: a 2 px ring for keyboard focus only, with its inner edge 2 px outside the track.

The minimum height of the control is the Arc medium control size. A disabled switch fades to 50% opacity and shows
the not-allowed cursor.

### Settings list

Stack the switches to form a list of settings. Each switch's label names the setting, and the rows are separated by
the spacing of the list rather than by lines.

```xml
<StackPanel Spacing="4">
    <arc:Switch Content="Email notifications" IsChecked="True" />
    <arc:Switch Content="Weekly digest" />
    <arc:Switch Content="Product updates" />
</StackPanel>
```

Keep the labels as the setting's name, not as a sentence about its state. "Weekly digest" is clear in both states,
while "Send me a weekly digest" reads oddly when the switch is off. Put a short description in a text block below the
label when the effect needs explaining, and keep it under the same label in the same column.

### Binding

Bind `IsChecked` to a view model property. Bind `IsEnabled` to lock the switch.

```xml
<arc:Switch Content="Email notifications"
            IsChecked="{Binding EmailEnabled}"
            IsEnabled="{Binding CanEditSettings}" />
```

`IsChecked` is two-way, so a change made by the pointer or the keyboard updates the property at once. Bind
`IsEnabled` to a permission or to a state that blocks the change, such as a setting that is managed by an
organization, and say why nearby.

### Binding to a view model

With CommunityToolkit.Mvvm, the view model holds each setting as a property, and a change saves it. The switch does
not save anything itself; the handler saves the value the person set.

```csharp
public interface ISettingsService
{
    Task SetAsync(string key, bool enabled);
}

public partial class NotificationSettingsViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    private readonly ISettingsService _settings;

    public NotificationSettingsViewModel(ISettingsService settings)
    {
        _settings = settings;
    }

    [ObservableProperty]
    private bool _emailNotifications;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private bool _canEditSettings = true;

    partial void OnEmailNotificationsChanged(bool value)
    {
        _ = _settings.SetAsync("notifications.email", value);
    }
}
```

```xml
<arc:Switch Content="Email notifications"
            IsChecked="{Binding EmailNotifications}"
            IsEnabled="{Binding CanEditSettings}" />
```

- `IsChecked` is the value to bind. Use a plain `bool` property, since the switch never produces a null value.
- The generated `OnEmailNotificationsChanged` method runs whenever the property changes, including when the saved value
  is loaded into it. Load the saved values before the page is shown, or skip the save when the value matches the
  stored one, so loading does not write the setting back.
- Keep the save in the view model, not in the view. Then the same setting saves whether the person changes it by mouse,
  keyboard or code.

### Disabled

A disabled switch keeps its state and cannot be changed.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.SwitchDisabledDemo">
    <WrapPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center" ItemSpacing="16" LineSpacing="12">
        <arc:Switch Content="Off and disabled" IsEnabled="False" />
        <arc:Switch Content="On and disabled" IsChecked="True" IsEnabled="False" />
    </WrapPanel>
</UserControl>
```

Disable a switch when the setting cannot apply at the moment, and say why in a description next to it, such as "Turned
on by your administrator". A disabled switch in a list is still read as part of the list, so keep it in its place
instead of hiding it.

### Changes

`IsCheckedChanged` is raised whenever the state changes, from the pointer, the keyboard or code. Apply the setting
there, so every way of changing it has the same effect.

```csharp
notifications.IsCheckedChanged += (_, _) =>
{
    settings.EmailEnabled = notifications.IsChecked == true;
};
```

The event fires for code changes as well as for the person's input. When a save fails, set `IsChecked` back to the
previous value in the same handler and show the error near the switch, so the switch shows the value that is really
saved.

### Example: notification settings

A notifications page for a billing administrator in a SaaS admin console. Each row names one setting in a short
noun phrase, and a description under it states what the setting sends and when. The rows are separated by a line
and are aligned on one column. The row for invoice reminders is disabled, because the organization sets it, and the
footer says that changes save at once, so the person knows no save step is coming.

![A notification settings card with three switches on, off and one disabled](https://docs.tkcode.si/shots/Docs/Toggles/Switch/images/NotificationSettings.webp)

```xml
<Border Width="640"
        Padding="24"
        BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Border}"
        BorderThickness="1"
        CornerRadius="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource RadiusControl}">
    <StackPanel Spacing="16">
        <StackPanel Spacing="4">
            <TextBlock Text="Billing notifications"
                       FontSize="18"
                       FontWeight="SemiBold"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
            <TextBlock Text="Choose which billing events email the workspace owners."
                       FontSize="13"
                       TextWrapping="Wrap"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
        </StackPanel>
        <Grid ColumnDefinitions="*,Auto" RowDefinitions="Auto,Auto">
            <StackPanel Spacing="2" VerticalAlignment="Center">
                <TextBlock Text="Payment failures"
                           FontWeight="Medium"
                           Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
                <TextBlock Text="Sent at once when a card payment fails."
                           FontSize="12"
                           Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
            </StackPanel>
            <arc:Switch Grid.Column="1"
                        AutomationProperties.Name="Payment failures"
                        IsChecked="True" />
        </Grid>
        <Border Height="1" Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Border}" />
        <Grid ColumnDefinitions="*,Auto">
            <StackPanel Spacing="2" VerticalAlignment="Center">
                <TextBlock Text="Weekly revenue digest"
                           FontWeight="Medium"
                           Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
                <TextBlock Text="Mondays at 08:00 UTC, with the previous week's totals."
                           FontSize="12"
                           Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
            </StackPanel>
            <arc:Switch Grid.Column="1"
                        AutomationProperties.Name="Weekly revenue digest" />
        </Grid>
        <Border Height="1" Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Border}" />
        <Grid ColumnDefinitions="*,Auto">
            <StackPanel Spacing="2" VerticalAlignment="Center">
                <TextBlock Text="Invoice reminders"
                           FontWeight="Medium"
                           Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
                <TextBlock Text="Set by your organization. Ask an owner to change it."
                           FontSize="12"
                           Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
            </StackPanel>
            <arc:Switch Grid.Column="1"
                        AutomationProperties.Name="Invoice reminders"
                        IsChecked="True"
                        IsEnabled="False" />
        </Grid>
        <TextBlock Text="Changes save as soon as you switch them."
                   FontSize="12"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
    </StackPanel>
</Border>
```

### Content guidelines

- **Label**: the name of the setting, in sentence case, with no colon and no question. "Email notifications", not
  "Would you like email notifications?".
- **Description**: one sentence on what the setting does and when it applies. Write times and counts as digits.
- **Disabled reason**: name who can change the setting, such as "Set by your organization", and how to ask for a change.
- **Status text**: say that changes save at once when no save button exists. "Changes save as soon as you switch them."

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| Enable | Email notifications |
| Toggle | Turn on to receive a weekly digest. |
| Would you like to get emails? | Email notifications |
| Setting disabled | Set by your organization. Ask an owner to change it. |

### Best practices

**Do**

- Apply the change as soon as the person makes it, and show the result near the switch if the save can fail. A switch
  that shows a state the server has not accepted is worse than one that waits.
- Keep the label the same in every state, so the person reads the setting's name in both positions.
- Group related switches under one heading, and keep the order the same on every visit to the page.
- Give an icon-only switch an `AutomationProperties.Name`, since it has no label to name it.

**Avoid**

- Using a switch for a choice that needs a confirmation or a reason. A dialog or a submit button makes the step visible.
- Changing the state from several code paths without a single save in the view model. The setting then depends on how
  it was changed.
- Hiding a disabled switch to simplify the list. The person then cannot learn that the setting exists or why it is off.
- Writing a state into the label ("On: email notifications"). The switch already shows the state, and a label that
  repeats it reads twice.

### Common questions

**Does the thumb animate when code changes the state?** Yes, with full motion. A change that did not come from a press
plays a short stretch of the thumb, so a code change is visible. A change within 250 ms of a press release does not
stretch, because the press already showed the motion.

**Can a switch have no label?** Yes. With no `Content` the track and thumb show alone, and the switch has no visible
name. Set `AutomationProperties.Name` so assistive technology can read it.

**Does setting `IsChecked` in code save the setting?** No. Setting it changes the state, raises `IsCheckedChanged`
and plays the stretch. The save runs only where your handler or view model calls it.

**Does the switch show a loading state while a save runs?** No. Disable the switch with `IsEnabled` while the save
runs, if the person must not change it again until the result is known.

**Why is the switch a toggle button to a screen reader?** Avalonia has no separate switch control type, so the switch
reports as a toggle button in its checked or unchecked state.

## API reference

### Switch

Arc switch: a tactile toggle for settings that take effect immediately. While pressed the thumb widens toward the other side (far edge anchored); on release it glides on a critically damped spring. Toggles that did not come from a press (keyboard, code) play a brief stretch instead.

Derives from `ToggleButton`: every member of `ToggleButton` works as well.

## Accessibility

- `Content` is the switch's name. A switch with only an icon needs `AutomationProperties.Name`.
- Space and Enter toggle the switch. The thumb keeps its stretched shape while Space is held.
- Assistive technology reports the switch as a toggle button in the checked or unchecked state. Avalonia has no separate switch control type.
- Keyboard focus draws a 2px outline offset by 2px. Pointer focus does not.
- The thumb is hidden from assistive technology. The on and off state is also shown by the track color and the thumb position.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` | Moves focus to the switch and on to the next or previous control |
| `Space` | Toggles the switch; the thumb stays stretched while Space is held |
| `Enter` | Toggles the switch |

## Motion

- Pressing the switch widens the thumb toward the other side while the far edge stays in place. Releasing glides the thumb across on a spring with no bounce.
- A change that did not come from a press, such as a key press or code, plays a brief stretch of the thumb.
- The track fill fades in and out, and the thumb color changes with it.
- Reduced motion removes the stretch, moves the thumb at once and turns off the color transitions. Off does the same.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| Thumb moves after a press | Glides across on a 0.3 s spring with no bounce | Moves at once | Moves at once |
| Thumb widens while pressed | Springs to 23 px wide; the far edge stays in place | No widening | No widening |
| Change from a key or code | One stretch to 116% and back, about 0.34 s | No stretch | No stretch |
| Track fill and thumb color | Crossfade on the standard tween | Immediate | Immediate |

## Related

- `Checkbox` for a choice that is confirmed with a submit button.
- `SegmentedControl` for switching between a few named views.
- `RadioGroup` for choosing exactly one option from a set.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `Checkbox` | The value is saved with a form or a submit button |
| `SegmentedControl` | The choice is one of a few named views of the same content |
| `RadioGroup` | The choice is one option from a set, with descriptions |
| `Button` | The control runs an action now rather than setting a state |

---

# Segmented control

> Switch between a small set of related views.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/segmented-control

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.SegmentedControlViewSwitcherDemo">
    <arc:SegmentedControl AutomationProperties.Name="Range"
                          HorizontalAlignment="Center"
                          SelectedValue="week">
        <arc:SegmentedOption Value="day" Label="Day" />
        <arc:SegmentedOption Value="week" Label="Week" />
        <arc:SegmentedOption Value="month" Label="Month" />
    </arc:SegmentedControl>
</UserControl>
```

## When to use

A segmented control is a row of two to five short choices where exactly one is active, and choosing one changes the
view at once. It sits in the header of a page or a panel, above the content it controls, and it keeps the choice
visible: the person always sees every option and which one is showing. Use it when the options are views of the same
data rather than separate pages, so the content swaps in place and the control stays where it is.

- **Time range on an analytics dashboard**: Day, Week, Month and Quarter switch the revenue chart and its totals. The
  chart redraws for the chosen range, and the control keeps the range visible while it does.
- **Status filter on an incident or ticket list**: All, Open and Resolved narrow the same list. An accessory shows the
  count of open items, so the person sees the size of each filter before choosing it.
- **Layout or density switch in a data table**: Compact and Comfortable change the row height of the grid that is
  already on screen, which is a setting that takes effect at once.
- **View mode on a shared workspace**: Board, List and Calendar show the same tasks in three arrangements, with the
  current arrangement kept as the selected segment.
- **Environment or account switch in an admin console**: Production, Staging and Sandbox change which data the page
  reads. The selected segment states the context that every number on the page depends on.

## When not to use

- **Options that need a description, a vertical layout or a longer label**: use `RadioGroup`, which gives each option
  a row with room for a description and wraps the text.
- **Options that need a price, a meta line or an icon on a card**: use `RadioCards`, which lays each option out as a
  selectable card.
- **A single on or off setting**: use `Switch`. A segmented control with two segments reads as a choice between
  views, not as a setting.
- **A choice with many options, or options that do not fit a short row**: use `Select`, which holds a long list in one
  field.
- **Switching between whole panels of content with their own tabs**: use `Tabs`, which is made for content areas and
  their navigation rather than for a row of view modes.

## Usage

Each `SegmentedOption` takes a value and a label. The control selects the segment with the value `SelectedValue`.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:SegmentedControl AutomationProperties.Name="Range" SelectedValue="week">
        <arc:SegmentedOption Value="day" Label="Day" />
        <arc:SegmentedOption Value="week" Label="Week" />
        <arc:SegmentedOption Value="month" Label="Month" />
    </arc:SegmentedControl>
</UserControl>
```

`SegmentedControl` derives from Avalonia's `SelectingItemsControl`, so `SelectedIndex`, `SelectedItem`,
`SelectedValue` and `SelectionChanged` behave as they do in any Avalonia selecting control. The control adds the
pill that glides between segments, the arrow-key model, the overflow scrolling and the `ItemIntent` event.

### Anatomy

1. **Frame**: a 1 px border with the control radius on the muted surface color. The segments scroll inside it, so the
   frame keeps its shape when the segments overflow.
2. **Track**: a 3 px inset on every side, with 2 px between segments.
3. **Selection pill**: a single rounded shape on the surface color with a 1 px border and the resting shadow. It sits
   under the labels and moves to the selected segment.
4. **Segment**: at least the small Arc control height (36 px in the default theme), with 12 px of padding on each side
   and a 14 px corner radius. Segments never shrink and never wrap their labels.
5. **Label** (`Label`): medium weight in the small type size. It uses the muted text color; it changes to the
   foreground color while the segment is hovered, pressed or selected.
6. **Accessory** (`SegmentedOption.Accessory`): optional content after the label, separated by a 6 px gap. It is
   hidden when `Accessory` is empty.
7. **Focus ring**: a 2 px ring drawn inside the focused segment. The scroll area would clip an outline drawn outside,
   so the ring stays within the segment.

With the default metrics and no accessory, the control is 44 px tall: a 36 px segment, the 3 px track inset above and
below it, and the 1 px frame.

### Choosing the variant

Use the control's default metrics for every view switch on a page, so all switches look the same. The control has no
size property: its height comes from the segment and the track, and its font follows the Arc body type. Plan the
number of segments against the width of the header. Two to five short segments fit a header comfortably; six or more
labels can overflow a header-width row, and then a `Select` holds the choice better.

Put the control at the top of the content it controls, aligned to the start of the page. The control aligns to the
left by default, so set `HorizontalAlignment="Center"` only when it is the only element in a centered header.

### Items from code

Bind `ItemsSource` to a list of options. The control also accepts plain strings, and `SelectedIndex` selects a segment
by position.

```csharp
var sections = new SegmentedControl
{
    MaxWidth = 300,
    ItemsSource = new[] { "Overview", "Activity", "Deployments", "Analytics", "Logs", "Settings" },
    SelectedIndex = 0
};
```

A plain string is its own value, so `SelectedValue` returns the string itself. Use `SegmentedOption` when the value and
the label differ, for example when the value is an enum or an ID and the label is for people to read.

### Accessory

`Accessory` is content shown after the label, such as a count. It accepts any content, so a count can be a
`TextBlock` in a small badge.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.SegmentedControlAccessoryAndIntentDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="10">
        <arc:SegmentedControl HorizontalAlignment="Center"
                              SelectedValue="all"
                              ItemIntent="OnItemIntent">
            <arc:SegmentedOption Value="all" Label="All" />
            <arc:SegmentedOption Value="unread" Label="Unread">
                <arc:SegmentedOption.Accessory>
                    <Border Padding="6,0"
                            CornerRadius="999"
                            VerticalAlignment="Center"
                            Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Surface}">
                        <TextBlock Text="3"
                                   FontSize="11"
                                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
                    </Border>
                </arc:SegmentedOption.Accessory>
            </arc:SegmentedOption>
            <arc:SegmentedOption Value="archived" Label="Archived" />
        </arc:SegmentedControl>
        <TextBlock x:Name="Intent"
                   Text="Intent: none"
                   HorizontalAlignment="Center"
                   FontSize="12"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class SegmentedControlAccessoryAndIntentDemo : UserControl
{
    public SegmentedControlAccessoryAndIntentDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
    }

    // Raised when the pointer or focus reaches a segment, before it is chosen.
    private void OnItemIntent(object? sender, SegmentedItemIntentEventArgs e)
    {
        Intent.Text = $"Intent: {e.Value}";
    }
}
```

```xml
<arc:SegmentedControl SelectedValue="all">
    <arc:SegmentedOption Value="all" Label="All" />
    <arc:SegmentedOption Value="unread" Label="Unread">
        <arc:SegmentedOption.Accessory>
            <TextBlock Text="3" />
        </arc:SegmentedOption.Accessory>
    </arc:SegmentedOption>
    <arc:SegmentedOption Value="archived" Label="Archived" IsDisabled="True" />
</arc:SegmentedControl>
```

Keep accessories to a number or a short status mark. The accessory sits inside the segment, so a long label or a wide
badge makes the segment wider and pushes its neighbors. Update the number in the accessory when the data changes; the
segment does not need to be rebuilt.

### Binding to a view model

With CommunityToolkit.Mvvm, the view model holds the list of options and the selected value, and the control shows
them. `SelectedValue` is two-way, so the view model reads the choice made by the pointer or the keyboard.

```csharp
public partial class ActivityViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    public ObservableCollection<SegmentedOption> Ranges { get; } = new()
    {
        new SegmentedOption("day", "Day"),
        new SegmentedOption("week", "Week"),
        new SegmentedOption("month", "Month")
    };

    [ObservableProperty]
    private string? _selectedRange = "week";
}
```

```xml
<arc:SegmentedControl ItemsSource="{Binding Ranges}"
                      SelectedValue="{Binding SelectedRange}"
                      AutomationProperties.Name="Range" />
```

- `SelectedValue` is two-way. Bind it to the property that holds the current view, and let the view model decide what
  the view shows from that value.
- `ItemsSource` takes an `ObservableCollection<SegmentedOption>`, so the options can change while the page is open.
- Use `SelectionChanged` when a change must load data, and keep the loading in a command or a service, not in the
  control.
- `AutomationProperties.Name` names the group. Set it in XAML, because the control has no header of its own.

### Intent

`ItemIntent` is raised when the pointer or the focus reaches a segment, before the segment is chosen. Use it for a
preview, such as a hint. Do not use it to change the view.

```csharp
segmented.ItemIntent += (_, e) => hint.Text = $"Intent: {e.Value}";
segmented.SelectionChanged += (_, _) => ShowView(segmented.SelectedValue);
```

The event carries the segment's `Item` and its `Value`. A mouse that enters a segment raises it, and so does a keyboard
focus move. Touch and pen input do not raise it on hover, but they select the segment when tapped, which then raises
`SelectionChanged`. Preload the content for a segment in `ItemIntent` when loading takes time, so the view appears
without a wait after the choice.

### Overflow

When the options are wider than the control, the row scrolls inside itself. The scroll bar is hidden, and a 20 px fade
marks each edge that has more content. The selected segment is always scrolled fully into view with 20 px of room
beside it, so it clears the fade.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.SegmentedControlOverflowDemo">
    <arc:SegmentedControl HorizontalAlignment="Center" MaxWidth="300" SelectedIndex="0">
        <x:String>Overview</x:String>
        <x:String>Activity</x:String>
        <x:String>Deployments</x:String>
        <x:String>Analytics</x:String>
        <x:String>Logs</x:String>
        <x:String>Settings</x:String>
    </arc:SegmentedControl>
</UserControl>
```

Overflow keeps the control usable on a narrow panel, but it hides options from view. Choose the number of segments so
that the row fits the widest layout the page supports. When a segment is off screen, the person may not see that it
exists, so use `Select` for a longer set.

### Example: incident status filter

A status filter in an incident list for a payments platform. The three segments are short nouns, and the Open
segment carries a count, so the person sees how many items each choice holds before selecting it. The list below the
control shows the filtered rows, and the heading gives the scope the list covers.

![An incident list with a status filter that has Open selected and a count of two](https://docs.tkcode.si/shots/Docs/Toggles/SegmentedControl/images/IncidentFilter.webp)

```xml
<StackPanel Width="680" Spacing="16">
```
