### Content guidelines

- **Label**: one or two words that name the view or the status: "Day", "Open", "Compact". A segment never wraps, so a
  long label widens the whole control. Use sentence case.
- **Accessory**: a count in digits, or a short mark. Do not put a sentence in an accessory.
- **Group name**: `AutomationProperties.Name` names the group for assistive technology. Write it as a noun: "Range",
  "Incident status", "View".
- **Segment order**: put the shortest span or the most common view first, and keep the same order on every page that
  uses the same control.

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| Show me the data for the last day | Day |
| Open issues (12 of them) | Open with the accessory 12 |
| Click here to view resolved items | Resolved |
| VIEW MODE | View |

### Best practices

**Do**

- Keep each segment a view of the same content, so the switch changes the data and not the page structure.
- Keep the selected value in the view model and update the content from it, so the control and the content cannot
  disagree after a reload.
- Use the same order and labels for the same choice on every page, so the person learns them once.
- Name the group with `AutomationProperties.Name` whenever no visible header says what the control chooses.

**Avoid**

- Using the control for a navigation between pages. A page change belongs in the navigation, and the segmented control
  keeps its choice on the current page.
- Doing expensive work in `ItemIntent`. It is not throttled, so a pointer that sweeps across the row raises it for every
  segment it passes.
- Putting disabled segments in the middle of the row without a reason. A disabled segment is still visible, and the
  person needs to know why it cannot be chosen.
- Labels that vary in length within one control. Equal-length labels keep the pill's width even and make the row easier
  to scan.

### Common questions

**Why does the control not fill its container?** It aligns left and sizes to its segments. Set `Width` for a fixed
width, or `HorizontalAlignment="Center"` to center it in a header. When the segments do not fit the width, the row
scrolls.

**How do I select a segment in code?** Set `SelectedValue` for a value, or `SelectedIndex` for a position. When the
segments overflow, the selected segment is scrolled into view as it is selected.

**Does `ItemIntent` fire before a mouse click?** Yes. A mouse raises `ItemIntent` when it enters the segment, so the
preview happens before the click chooses the segment and raises `SelectionChanged`. Touch input does not raise it on
hover.

**Can I bind a list of plain strings?** Yes. `ItemsSource` accepts strings, and `SelectedValue` returns the string
itself. Use `SegmentedOption` when the value must differ from the text, such as an enum or an ID.

## API reference

### SegmentedControl

Arc segmented control: a row of buttons for switching between a small set of related views. One selection pill glides between them on the morph spring; segments never scale or change weight, only their label color follows. Arrows (wrapping), Home and End move the selection like a tab list and only the selected segment is a tab stop. When the options are wider than the control the row scrolls inside itself with faded edges, and the selected segment is always scrolled fully into view. `ItemIntent` fires when the pointer or focus reaches a segment before it is chosen (preload what it shows).

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ItemIntent` | `SegmentedItemIntentEventArgs` | The pointer or keyboard focus reached a segment (it may not be selected yet). |

Derives from `SelectingItemsControl`: every member of `SelectingItemsControl` works as well.
### SegmentedOption

One option of a `SegmentedControl` (Arc `Segment`): a short label and optional accessory.

## Accessibility

- `AutomationProperties.Name` names the group. Set it on every control that has no visible header.
- Each segment is a button that reports its pressed state. The sliding pill is hidden from assistive technology.
- Tab enters the control at the selected segment, or the first segment when none is selected. A second Tab leaves it.
- Arrow keys select and focus the next or previous segment and wrap around. Home and End select the first and last
  segment. Disabled segments are skipped.
- Keyboard focus draws a 2px outline inside the segment, so the scroll area does not clip it. Pointer focus does not.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Tab` | Enters the control at the selected segment, or the first segment when none is selected; the next `Tab` leaves it |
| `Right` / `Down` | Selects and focuses the next segment, wrapping from the last to the first |
| `Left` / `Up` | Selects and focuses the previous segment, wrapping from the first to the last |
| `Home` / `End` | Selects and focuses the first or last segment |
| `Space` / `Enter` | Selects the focused segment |

Focus raises `ItemIntent` for each segment it reaches. The arrow keys then select that segment, so the preview and the
change come from the same movement.

## Motion

- One pill glides under the selected segment on a morph spring. The pill sits beneath the labels and scrolls with them.
- Segments never scale or change weight. Only the pill moves, and the label color changes quickly.
- When the segments overflow, the row scrolls to keep the selected segment in view, with a short ease. The first
  placement after the control loads is immediate.
- Reduced motion moves the pill at once and removes the color transition. Off does the same.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| Selection moves | The pill glides on a morph spring | The pill moves at once | The pill moves at once |
| Label color (hover, press, selected) | Crossfades on the fast tween | Immediate | Immediate |
| Overflow scrolls to the selected segment | Eases over the standard tween after the first layout | Jumps | Jumps |
| Edge fade appears or disappears | Follows the scroll position | Follows the scroll position | Follows the scroll position |
| First placement after load | Immediate | Immediate | Immediate |

## Related

- `RadioGroup` for options that need descriptions or a vertical layout.
- `BillingToggle` for a monthly or yearly billing period with savings notes.
- `Switch` for a single setting that takes effect at once.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `RadioGroup` | Options need a description each, or a vertical list suits the form |
| `RadioCards` | Options need a price, a meta line or an icon on a card |
| `Tabs` | Each option opens a whole panel of content with its own navigation |
| `Select` | The options are many, or they do not fit a short row |
| `Switch` | One setting takes effect at once and has no alternative values |
| `BillingToggle` | The choice is a monthly or yearly billing period with savings notes |

# Slider

> Pick a value or a range on a track that follows your finger.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/slider

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.SliderSingleValueDemo">
    <arc:Slider Label="Volume"
                Value="64"
                Width="360"
                HorizontalAlignment="Center">
        <arc:Slider.StartContent>
            <arc:ArcGlyph Data="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Minus}"
                          Size="16"
                          Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}"
                          VerticalAlignment="Center" />
        </arc:Slider.StartContent>
        <arc:Slider.EndContent>
            <arc:ArcGlyph Data="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Plus}"
                          Size="16"
                          Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}"
                          VerticalAlignment="Center" />
        </arc:Slider.EndContent>
    </arc:Slider>
</UserControl>
```

## When to use

`Slider` lets a person choose a value or a range by moving a thumb along a track. It fits settings and filters where
the position on the track carries the meaning and an exact digit matters less. It sits in a form, a filter panel or a
control bar, and it shows the chosen value in a readout beside the label and in a bubble above the thumb while the
person moves it.

- **Price and amount filters on a product listing**: a range with two thumbs, `IsRange="True"`, where the lower and
  upper values become the query. The track shows the spread of the catalog at a glance, and the readout shows
  "$200 to $800" while the thumbs move.
- **Spend limits and budgets** in a billing or procurement console: a monthly cap for a team, set between $0 and
  $5,000. The person sees roughly where the cap sits, and the formatted readout gives the exact figure.
- **Playback and display settings** in a media or training app: playback speed with labeled ticks at 0.5x and 1x,
  or the volume of a call. Labeled marks name the presets, and clicking a label jumps there.
- **Alert thresholds** in an operations dashboard: a CPU or error-rate threshold between 0 and 100 percent, with marks
  at the levels the team uses in its runbooks. The track makes the scale obvious where a number alone would not.
- **Opacity, density or zoom controls** in a data tool, where the value is judged by what changes on screen while the
  thumb moves.

## When not to use

- **Exact numbers the person types**, such as a refund amount or a quantity: use `NumberField`, or `MoneyInput` for an
  amount with a currency. A track only approximates a value.
- **A value the person cannot change**, such as storage used or an upload's progress: use `Progress`.
- **A single setting that should feel physical**, with the track stretching past its ends and detents the thumb clicks
  into: use `ElasticSlider`. It has one value and no range.
- **A choice from a short fixed list**, such as a plan tier or a delivery speed: use `Select` for a dropdown, or
  `SegmentedControl` when the options fit in one row.
- **A date or a time span**: use `DatePicker`, `DateRangePicker` or `TimePicker`. A slider cannot show calendar units.
- **An on or off setting**: use `Switch`. A slider implies that intermediate values are meaningful.

## Usage

Basic usage is a single value. `Value` is the position on the track, and `Minimum` and `Maximum` set its range.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:Slider Label="Volume"
                Value="64"
                Width="360" />
</UserControl>
```

`Slider` derives from Avalonia's `RangeBase`, so `Value`, `Minimum`, `Maximum`, `LargeChange` and `ValueChanged` work as
they do on any range control. Two things differ from a native slider. `SmallChange` is the step the value snaps to, and
it defaults to 1 on this control. Setting `IsRange` switches the control to two thumbs, with `LowerValue` and
`UpperValue` in place of `Value`. The control adds the label, the readout, the value bubble, the marks and the content
slots.

### Anatomy

1. **Label** (`Label`): medium weight, on the row above the track with a 19.6 px line height. It truncates with an
   ellipsis when the width is short. It names the thumb for assistive technology.
2. **Readout**: the formatted value, right-aligned on the label row in the secondary text color, with 16 px of space
   before it. In range mode it shows the low and high values with an en dash between them in the muted color, and the
   two numbers are 4 px apart. `IsValueVisible` hides it.
3. **Start content** (`StartContent`): before the track with 12 px of space. It is hidden when the property is null.
4. **Track and fill**: a 6 px track in the control track color. The fill runs from the start to the thumb, or between
   the two thumbs in range mode, in the control fill color.
5. **Thumbs**: 22 px discs with the control thumb color and a raised shadow. Each thumb's hit area reaches 11 px beyond
   each side of the disc.
6. **Ticks**: 4 px dots, one per mark. Ticks outside the fill use the foreground at 30% opacity; ticks on the fill use
   the control glyph color at 60%.
7. **Value bubble**: a raised bubble 8 px above the active thumb (18 px on a touch or pen press), at least 28 px tall,
   with 12 px of horizontal padding and a 1 px border. Its colors are inverted: the foreground is the background and
   the background is the text. It appears while the thumb is dragged or has keyboard focus.
8. **End content** (`EndContent`): after the track with 12 px of space, in the same way as the start content.
9. **Mark labels row**: 20 px high, under the track in the extra small type size. A label is muted, and the label of a
   mark that the value has reached uses the secondary color. The row appears only when at least one mark has a `Label`.

### Start and end content

`StartContent` and `EndContent` sit before and after the track, such as icons or a mute button. A mute button suits a
volume control: the person can silence the output without moving the thumb. Keep the content to a single glyph or a
small icon button, because the track takes the remaining width.

```xml
<arc:Slider Label="Volume"
            Value="64"
            Width="360">
    <arc:Slider.StartContent>
        <TextBlock Text="-" />
    </arc:Slider.StartContent>
    <arc:Slider.EndContent>
        <TextBlock Text="+" />
    </arc:Slider.EndContent>
</arc:Slider>
```

### Range

Set `IsRange` to show two thumbs. Read and write the ends with `LowerValue` and `UpperValue`, and keep the thumbs apart
with `MinStepsBetweenThumbs`, which counts in steps. In range mode `Value` is not used. `ValueFormatter` formats the
readout, the bubble and the spoken value of each thumb.

Choose a range when the person is narrowing a set, such as a price, a date span in days or a score band. Use a single
thumb for a threshold, because a second thumb asks the person to choose two related numbers at once.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.SliderRangeDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="16">
        <arc:Slider x:Name="Price"
                    Label="Price"
                    IsRange="True"
                    Minimum="0"
                    Maximum="1000"
                    SmallChange="10"
                    LowerValue="200"
                    UpperValue="800"
                    MinStepsBetweenThumbs="5"
                    LowerThumbName="Minimum price"
                    UpperThumbName="Maximum price"
                    Width="360"
                    HorizontalAlignment="Center"
                    ValueCommitted="OnValueCommitted" />
        <TextBlock x:Name="Committed"
                   Text="Committed: $200 – $800"
                   HorizontalAlignment="Center"
                   FontSize="12"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class SliderRangeDemo : UserControl
{
    public SliderRangeDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Price.ValueFormatter = v => $"${v:N0}";
    }

    // Raised once per release or key press, not on every step of the drag.
    private void OnValueCommitted(object? sender, SliderValueCommittedEventArgs e)
        => Committed.Text = $"Committed: ${e.LowerValue:N0} – ${e.UpperValue:N0}";
}
```

```xml
<arc:Slider Label="Price"
            IsRange="True"
            Minimum="0"
            Maximum="1000"
            SmallChange="10"
            LowerValue="{Binding MinPrice, Mode=TwoWay}"
            UpperValue="{Binding MaxPrice, Mode=TwoWay}"
            MinStepsBetweenThumbs="5"
            LowerThumbName="Minimum price"
            UpperThumbName="Maximum price"
            ValueFormatter="{Binding PriceFormatter}" />
```

`MinStepsBetweenThumbs` keeps the two thumbs apart by a number of steps, so with `SmallChange="10"` and a value of `5`
the thumbs can never be closer than 50 units. A thumb pressed into the other one stops at the gap. Leave it at `0`, the
default, when the two ends may meet.

### Steps and marks

`SmallChange` is the step the value snaps to. `Marks` adds ticks on the track. A mark with a label prints the label under
the track, and clicking the label moves the nearest thumb there. A bare `SliderMark` (or a number, which converts
implicitly) is a tick with no label.

Use marks for presets the person returns to, such as 0.5x, 1x and 2x for playback, or the values a runbook names for an
alert. Label only the presets that need a name, and leave the others as ticks; a row of labels under a narrow track
collides quickly.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.SliderStepsAndMarksDemo">
    <arc:Slider x:Name="Speed"
                Label="Playback speed"
                Minimum="0.5"
                Maximum="2"
                SmallChange="0.25"
                Value="1"
                Width="360"
                HorizontalAlignment="Center">
        <arc:Slider.Marks>
            <arc:SliderMark Value="0.5" Label="0.5×" />
            <arc:SliderMark Value="0.75" />
            <arc:SliderMark Value="1" Label="1×" />
            <arc:SliderMark Value="1.25" />
            <arc:SliderMark Value="1.5" Label="1.5×" />
            <arc:SliderMark Value="1.75" />
            <arc:SliderMark Value="2" Label="2×" />
        </arc:Slider.Marks>
    </arc:Slider>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class SliderStepsAndMarksDemo : UserControl
{
    public SliderStepsAndMarksDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Speed.ValueFormatter = v => $"{v:0.##}×";
    }
}
```

Marks do not change the value by themselves. A drag, a key press or a clicked label sets the value, and the marks only
show where the presets are.

### Ranges and limits

The value always stays inside `Minimum` and `Maximum`, and a range keeps both ends inside them. The control clamps values
as it receives them, so a XAML page may set `Minimum="360"` before `Maximum="900"` without an error; the final values
are the ones to rely on.

Use `LargeChange` for the jump that `PageUp`, `PageDown` and `Shift` with an arrow make. When it is not set, the jump is
a tenth of the range, which is right for most scales. Set it explicitly for a scale where a tenth is too coarse, such as
a 0 to 5 rating where the jump should be 1.

### Events

`ValueCommitted` runs once per release, per key press that changes the value, and per clicked mark label. Put slow
work, such as a network request, on this event. Its `SliderValueCommittedEventArgs` carries `Value`, `LowerValue`,
`UpperValue` and `IsRange`. For a single value the lower and upper values repeat `Value`; in range mode `Value` is the
lower end. `RangeChanged` runs on every step of a range while it is dragged or changed by keys, and its
`SliderRangeChangedEventArgs` carries `LowerValue` and `UpperValue`.

```csharp
price.ValueCommitted += (_, e) => SavePriceFilter(e.LowerValue, e.UpperValue);
price.RangeChanged += (_, e) => committed.Text = $"${e.LowerValue:N0} – ${e.UpperValue:N0}";
```

### Binding to a view model

A filter panel is the typical case: the view model owns the two prices, the thumbs mirror them, and a command runs the
query when the person has finished. Use CommunityToolkit.Mvvm for the view model.

```csharp
public interface ICatalogQuery
{
    Task FilterByPriceAsync(double minPrice, double maxPrice);
}

public partial class PriceFilterViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    private readonly ICatalogQuery _catalog;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private double _minPrice = 200;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private double _maxPrice = 800;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private string _summary = "Showing products from $200 to $800.";

    public PriceFilterViewModel(ICatalogQuery catalog) => _catalog = catalog;

    [RelayCommand]
    private async Task ApplyAsync()
    {
        Summary = $"Showing products from ${MinPrice:N0} to ${MaxPrice:N0}.";
        await _catalog.FilterByPriceAsync(MinPrice, MaxPrice);
    }
}
```

```xml
<StackPanel Spacing="12">
    <arc:Slider Label="Price"
                IsRange="True"
                Minimum="0"
                Maximum="1000"
                SmallChange="10"
                LowerValue="{Binding MinPrice, Mode=TwoWay}"
                UpperValue="{Binding MaxPrice, Mode=TwoWay}"
                MinStepsBetweenThumbs="5"
                Width="360" />
    <TextBlock Text="{Binding Summary}" />
</StackPanel>
```

- `LowerValue` and `UpperValue` are the two-way properties to bind in range mode; `Value` is the two-way property in
  single mode. Bind the one that matches `IsRange`.
- Bind `Mode=TwoWay` explicitly. The view model's `MinPrice` changes on every step of a drag, which is right for a
  readout or a summary line and wrong for a query. Run the query from `ApplyAsync`, or from `ValueCommitted` in the
  view's code behind, so a drag sends one request.
- The command in the view is a `Button` bound to `ApplyCommand`; it stays enabled while the thumbs move, so the person
  can apply the new range at any point.

### Using motion with restraint

Motion on the slider tells the person what the thumb did: the bubble confirms the value, the digits roll to show the
direction of change, and the momentum after a flick shows how far the thumb can carry. These cues help while a person
searches a range by feel. They distract on a page where the value only needs to be set once; use a plain field there.

Reduced motion removes the momentum, the stretch and the rolling digits. The thumb goes straight to the value and the
bubble only fades, which keeps the control readable without the motion that shows the direction of change.

### Disabled

A disabled slider leaves the tab order and fades to 50% opacity. Its track shows the "no" cursor and ignores the pointer
and the keys. Use it while the value cannot apply, and say why nearby, for example "Set by your plan administrator".
A value the person can never change belongs in `Progress` or in plain text.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.SliderDisabledDemo">
    <arc:Slider x:Name="OpacitySlider"
                Label="Opacity"
                Value="40"
                IsEnabled="False"
                Width="360"
                HorizontalAlignment="Center" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class SliderDisabledDemo : UserControl
{
    public SliderDisabledDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        OpacitySlider.ValueFormatter = v => $"{v:0}%";
    }
}
```

### Example: product filter panel

A filter panel on a product listing, with a price range and a minimum rating. The price thumbs have names of their own,
so a screen reader says "Minimum price" and "Maximum price", and the labels say the unit. The rating slider uses a
labeled mark at the floor ("Any") and at the top, so the lowest and highest choices are named without a row of numbers.
The summary line under the controls reports the current choice in words, so the person can read the result without
moving a thumb.

![A product filter panel with a price range slider and a minimum rating slider](https://docs.tkcode.si/shots/Docs/Sliders/Slider/images/ProductFilters.webp)

```xml
<StackPanel Width="560" Spacing="22">
    <TextBlock Text="Filter products"
               FontSize="14"
               FontWeight="SemiBold"
               Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
    <arc:Slider Label="Price (USD)"
                IsRange="True"
                Minimum="0"
                Maximum="1000"
                SmallChange="10"
                LowerValue="200"
                UpperValue="800"
                MinStepsBetweenThumbs="5"
                LowerThumbName="Minimum price"
                UpperThumbName="Maximum price" />
    <arc:Slider Label="Minimum rating"
                Minimum="0"
                Maximum="5"
                SmallChange="1"
                Value="4">
        <arc:Slider.Marks>
            <arc:SliderMark Value="0" Label="Any" />
            <arc:SliderMark Value="1" />
            <arc:SliderMark Value="2" />
            <arc:SliderMark Value="3" />
            <arc:SliderMark Value="4" />
            <arc:SliderMark Value="5" Label="5" />
        </arc:Slider.Marks>
    </arc:Slider>
    <TextBlock Text="Showing 186 products from 200 to 800 USD, rated 4 stars or more."
               Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
    <StackPanel Orientation="Horizontal" Spacing="8" HorizontalAlignment="Right">

        <arc:Button Content="Apply filters" />
    </StackPanel>
</StackPanel>
```

In the app, the summary comes from the view model and is updated in the same command that runs the query, so the text
and the results never disagree. The XAML example writes the text literally so the scene is complete.

### Content guidelines

- **Label**: a short noun, with the unit in brackets when the readout does not carry it: "Volume", "Price (USD)". The
  label names the thumb, so it must say what the value is.
- **Thumb names**: in a range, name each thumb explicitly with `LowerThumbName` and `UpperThumbName`, such as "Minimum
  price" and "Maximum price". The default "minimum" and "maximum" suffixes read poorly next to a unit.
- **Mark labels**: a short preset name or number: "0.5x", "1x", "Any". Use a word when a number is ambiguous, such as
  "Any" for a rating floor of 0.
- **Readout**: a formatted number, not a sentence. Write the unit in the formatter so the readout, the bubble and the
  spoken value agree.
- **Summary**: say the current choice in full words under the controls, such as "Showing products from $200 to $800."

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| Price range | Price (USD) |
| Minimum | Minimum price |
| Rating 0 | Any |
| $200.00 to $800.00 | $200 to $800 |
| Set the volume level | Volume |

### Best practices

**Do**

- Name the unit in the label or in the formatter, and keep the readout and the spoken value the same. Without a unit the
  number is a guess for a person who cannot see the track.
- Use a range with `IsRange` for a span that the person narrows, and write the query from the committed values so the
  results do not update on every step of a drag.
- Set `MinStepsBetweenThumbs` when two thumbs describe one thing, so the minimum can never pass the maximum in the
  application's logic.
- Label only the presets that people choose, and leave the rest as unlabeled ticks. The ticks still show where the scale
  divides, and the labels stay short enough not to collide on a narrow track.

**Avoid**

- Using a slider for a value the person must enter exactly, such as a tax rate or a refund. People cannot aim for a
  digit on a track, and a corrected value then depends on luck.
- Running an expensive request on `ValueChanged` or `RangeChanged`. A drag raises those on every step, so the request
  runs dozens of times for one adjustment.
- Setting a `SmallChange` finer than the track can show. A step of 0.001 across 1000 units moves the thumb by a fraction of
  a pixel, so keys appear to do nothing.
- Relying on the bubble to show the value. The bubble appears only while the thumb is dragged or has keyboard focus, so
  a settled value needs the readout or a summary line.

### Common questions

**Why does the thumb ignore my `Value` when `IsRange` is on?** In range mode the control reads `LowerValue` and
`UpperValue` only, and `Value` is not used. Set the two ends and read them back from the same properties.

**How do I stop the two thumbs from meeting?** Set `MinStepsBetweenThumbs` to the number of steps the thumbs must keep
apart. Keys and drags both stop at the gap, so the lower value never passes the upper one minus the gap.

**Why does a flick sometimes move the value one step past where I released?** The release carries the momentum of the
drag, and a step can take one more move when it is at least 12 px wide on screen. A pause before the release removes the
momentum, so a slow release lands on the nearest step.

**What does a click on a mark label do in range mode?** It moves the thumb nearest to the label's value and commits the
change. The other thumb stays where it is.

**Can a tick without a label be clicked?** No. Only a labeled mark responds to a click, through its label. An unlabeled
tick is reached by dragging or with the keys, so give a preset a label when the person should be able to click it.

## API reference

### Slider

Arc slider: a value or a range on a track. The thumb follows the pointer 1:1, rubber-bands up to 9px past its limits and settles on the step grid with the velocity of the release (on a coarse grid the release may carry it one step further); pressing the track springs the nearest thumb there. A bubble with rolling digits rides the thumb while it is dragged or keyboard focused and lingers 700ms after a release. Arrows, Shift+arrows, PageUp / PageDown and Home / End work as in a native range input; a key at a limit makes the thumb strain toward the press and spring home. Unlike `Slider`, `SmallChange` is the step the value snaps to. Set `IsRange` for two thumbs (`LowerValue` / `UpperValue`).

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Label` | `string?` | `null` | Visible label; also names the thumb (or, with " minimum" / " maximum", the range thumbs). |
| `IsRange` | `bool` | `false` | Two thumbs: `LowerValue` and `UpperValue` instead of `Value`. |
| `LowerValue` | `double` | `0` | Lower end of the range when IsRange is true (two-way, default 0). |
| `UpperValue` | `double` | `100` | Upper end of the range when IsRange is true (two-way, default 100). |
| `MinStepsBetweenThumbs` | `int` | `0` | The closest the two range thumbs may sit, in steps. |
| `ValueFormatter` | `Func<double, string>?` | `null` | Formats the readout, the bubble and the spoken value (default: en-US with the step's decimals). |
| `IsValueVisible` | `bool` | `true` | Shows the value beside the label. The bubble still appears while dragging or keyboard focused. |
| `LowerThumbName` | `string?` | `null` | Accessible name of the lower range thumb; when null it is the Label with ", minimum" appended. |
| `UpperThumbName` | `string?` | `null` | Accessible name of the upper range thumb; when null it is the Label with ", maximum" appended. |
| `StartContent` | `object?` | `null` | Content before the track, such as an icon or a mute button. |
| `EndContent` | `object?` | `null` | Content after the track, such as an icon or a button. |
| `Marks` | `IList<SliderMark>` | – | Ticks on the track; labeled marks also print under it and are clickable. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ValueCommitted` | `SliderValueCommittedEventArgs` | Runs once a drag is released, a key changes the value or a mark label is clicked. |
| `RangeChanged` | `SliderRangeChangedEventArgs` | Raised on every step of a range (drag or keys), like `ValueChanged` for one thumb. |

Pseudo-classes: `:dragging`, `:range`, `:marks`

Derives from `RangeBase`: every member of `RangeBase` works as well.

### SliderMark

A mark on a `Slider` or `ElasticSlider` track. A mark without a label draws a tick; a mark with a label also prints it under the track, and clicking the label moves there. On an elastic slider marks are detents the dragged thumb clicks into.

## Accessibility

- `Label` names the slider. In a range, each thumb is named from `LowerThumbName` and `UpperThumbName`, or from `Label`
  with "minimum" and "maximum".
- Each thumb reports its value as text, so the spoken value follows the `ValueFormatter`. Each thumb also reports the
  minimum and maximum allowed for it, so the other thumb limits its range.
- The readout, the bubble and the mark labels are hidden from assistive technology. A clicked label is a pointer
  shortcut; the same values are reachable with the keyboard.
- The control itself is a group, and each thumb is a separate stop in the tab order.
- The focus ring appears after a key press, not after a pointer press.

### Keyboard

Each thumb receives focus with `Tab`. In range mode `Tab` moves from the lower thumb to the upper one, and the keys below
apply to the thumb that has focus.

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` | Move focus to the next or previous thumb, then out of the control; a disabled slider is skipped |
| `Right` / `Up` | Increase the value by `SmallChange` |
| `Left` / `Down` | Decrease the value by `SmallChange` |
| `Shift` + arrow, `PageUp` / `PageDown` | Increase or decrease by `LargeChange` |
| `Home` / `End` | Go to the lowest or highest value the thumb may take; in range mode the other thumb and `MinStepsBetweenThumbs` set the limit |
| A key at a limit | The value stays put; the thumb strains toward the key and springs back |

## Motion

- The thumb follows the pointer one to one. On release it settles on the nearest step and keeps the momentum of the
  drag, so a fast flick can move it one step further. The momentum is used only when that step is at least 12 px wide.
- Pressing the track springs the nearest thumb to the pointer. A key at a limit makes the thumb strain toward the press
  and spring back.
- The value bubble pops up above the active thumb, rolls its digits while the value changes and stays for 700 ms after
  a release. The dragged thumb grows slightly.
- Past either limit the track gives by up to 9 px and returns on release, so the person feels the end of the range
  without a message.
- Reduced motion removes momentum, stretch and digit rolling. The thumb goes straight to the value and the bubble only
  fades. Off motion jumps straight to the end state.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| Drag past a limit | The track gives up to 9 px and springs back | No stretch; the thumb stops at the limit | Immediate |
| Release | The thumb settles on a step with the drag's momentum, at most one step further | The thumb settles on the nearest step with no momentum | Immediate |
| Press on the track | The nearest thumb springs under the pointer | The thumb goes straight to the pointer | Immediate |
| Dragged thumb | Grows to 1.16 times on a snappy spring | Grows at once | Immediate |
| Value bubble | Pops up from 0.6 times with a soft blur; fades out at 0.8 times | Fades in and out | Immediate |
| Readout digits | Roll digit by digit as the value changes | Switch at once | Immediate |

## Related

- `ElasticSlider` for a single setting that stretches past its ends and clicks into detents.
- `NumberField` when the person needs to type an exact number.
- `Progress` for a value that is shown but not changed by the person.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `ElasticSlider` | One physical setting, such as volume or brightness, with detents and a stretch at the limits |
| `NumberField` | The person must type or step an exact number with bounds and a unit |
| `MoneyInput` | The value is an amount of money that needs a currency and parsing |
| `Select` / `SegmentedControl` | The choice is one of a short fixed list of options |
| `DateRangePicker` | The range is a span of dates rather than numbers |
| `Progress` | The value is shown to the person and the application sets it |

---

# Elastic slider

> A slider that stretches like rubber past its ends, with a swaying value tag and detents the thumb clicks into.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/elastic-slider

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ElasticSliderRubberBandDemo">
    <arc:ElasticSlider x:Name="Volume"
                       Label="Volume"
                       Value="40"
                       Width="360"
                       HorizontalAlignment="Center">
        <arc:ElasticSlider.StartIcon>
            <arc:ArcGlyph Data="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Minus}"
                          Size="16"
                          Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}"
                          VerticalAlignment="Center" />
        </arc:ElasticSlider.StartIcon>
        <arc:ElasticSlider.EndIcon>
            <arc:ArcGlyph Data="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Volume2}"
                          Size="16"
                          Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}"
                          VerticalAlignment="Center" />
        </arc:ElasticSlider.EndIcon>
    </arc:ElasticSlider>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class ElasticSliderRubberBandDemo : UserControl
{
    public ElasticSliderRubberBandDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Volume.ValueFormatter = v => $"{v:0}%";
    }
}
```

## When to use

`ElasticSlider` sets one value on a track that gives under the finger. It fits a single setting that people adjust by
feel and confirm by looking at the track: a control in a media player bar, a tool inspector, or a settings row where
the slider is the only control on the line. The track stretches past either end and springs back on release, so the
person feels that a limit was reached without a message appearing.

- **Playback and output levels** in a meeting or media app: the volume or microphone gain in a player bar. Exact
  decibels matter less than the feel of quiet and loud, and a detent at a useful level (`Off`, `50`, `Max`) gives a
  target to aim for.
- **Adjustments in a creative tool inspector**: brightness, contrast or blur of the selected layer. People compare a
  result by dragging back and forth, so the value tag that follows the thumb and the stretch at the limits suit the
  task.
- **Device and display controls** in an operations console or a kiosk setup: screen brightness on a device settings
  page, or a fan speed on a rack panel, where the setting changes often and a preset such as 50% is a common target.
- **Strength of a visual effect** in a theme or branding editor, such as the opacity of a banner overlay or the
  intensity of a shadow, where the person is judging how it looks rather than reading a number.

## When not to use

- **A quiet form or settings page where the value is set once**: use `Slider`. It has the same track and value bubble
  but stays still at the ends and suits forms that people read top to bottom.
- **A range with a lower and an upper end**, such as a price or date filter: use `Slider` with `IsRange`.
  `ElasticSlider` has a single `Value` and no range mode.
- **An exact number the person must type**, such as a tax rate, a discount or a quantity: use `NumberField`. A track
  only approximates a value, and the stretch does not help when the person needs a precise figure.
- **A value the person cannot change**, such as upload progress, storage used or a job's completion: use `Progress`.
- **Many sliders in one list**, such as a row per channel in a mixer or per product in an inventory table: use
  `Slider`. The stretch, sway and detent pop repeat on every row and pull attention away from the data.

## Usage

Basic usage is a single value. `Value` is the position on the track, and `Minimum` and `Maximum` set its range.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:ElasticSlider Label="Volume"
                       Value="40"
                       Width="360"
                       ValueFormatter="{Binding VolumeFormatter}" />
</UserControl>
```

`ElasticSlider` derives from Avalonia's `RangeBase`. `Value`, `Minimum`, `Maximum`, `SmallChange`, `LargeChange` and the
`ValueChanged` event therefore behave as they do on any range control. The control adds the label, the readout, the
value tag, the rubber-band track, the detents and the two icon slots. `SmallChange` is the step the value snaps to, and
it defaults to 1 on this control.

### Anatomy

1. **Label** (`Label`): medium weight, on the row above the track with a 19.6 px line height. It truncates with an
   ellipsis when the width is short. It is also the thumb's accessible name.
2. **Readout**: the formatted `Value`, right-aligned on the label row in the secondary text color, with 16 px of space
   before it. It fades out while the value tag rides the thumb, so the number is never shown twice.
3. **Start icon** (`StartIcon`): before the track with 12 px of space, in the muted text color. It is hidden when the
   property is null.
4. **Track and fill**: an 8 px track in the control track color, with the part before the thumb in the control fill
   color. The track row is the medium control height.
5. **Thumb**: a 24 px disc with the control thumb color and its raised shadow. Its hit area reaches 12 px beyond each
   side of the disc, so a near miss still grabs it.
6. **Value tag**: a raised bubble 10 px above the thumb (10 px higher again after a touch or pen press), at least
   28 px tall, with 12 px of horizontal padding. It uses the foreground color as its background and the background
   color as its text.
7. **Detent ticks**: 4 px dots, one per mark. Ticks on the track use the foreground at 32% opacity; ticks on the filled
   part use the control glyph color at 60% so they stay visible on the fill.
8. **End icon** (`EndIcon`): after the track with 12 px of space, in the muted text color.
9. **Mark labels row**: 20 px high, under the track, in the extra small type size in the muted color. The row appears
   only when at least one mark has a `Label`.

### Icons

`StartIcon` and `EndIcon` sit before and after the track. When the track is pulled past an end, the icon on that end
moves outward with it, so the stretch reads as the whole control giving under the finger. Use glyphs or small icon
buttons there, not text that needs room to grow. A pair such as a minus and a plus for volume, or a moon and a sun for
brightness, tells people which way the value goes.

```xml
<arc:ElasticSlider Label="Brightness"
                   Value="50"
                   Width="360">
    <arc:ElasticSlider.StartIcon>
        <TextBlock Text="-" />
    </arc:ElasticSlider.StartIcon>
    <arc:ElasticSlider.EndIcon>
        <TextBlock Text="+" />
    </arc:ElasticSlider.EndIcon>
</arc:ElasticSlider>
```

### Detents

Add `SliderMark` values to `Marks`. A dragged thumb clicks into each mark. A mark with a label also prints the label
under the track, and clicking the label moves the thumb there.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ElasticSliderDetentsDemo">
    <arc:ElasticSlider Label="Brightness"
                       Value="50"
                       Width="360"
                       HorizontalAlignment="Center">
        <arc:ElasticSlider.StartIcon>
            <arc:ArcGlyph Data="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Moon}"
                          Size="16"
                          Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}"
                          VerticalAlignment="Center" />
        </arc:ElasticSlider.StartIcon>
        <arc:ElasticSlider.EndIcon>
            <arc:ArcGlyph Data="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Sparkles}"
                          Size="16"
                          Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}"
                          VerticalAlignment="Center" />
        </arc:ElasticSlider.EndIcon>
        <arc:ElasticSlider.Marks>
            <arc:SliderMark Value="0" Label="Off" />
            <arc:SliderMark Value="25" Label="25" />
            <arc:SliderMark Value="50" Label="50" />
            <arc:SliderMark Value="75" Label="75" />
            <arc:SliderMark Value="100" Label="Max" />
        </arc:ElasticSlider.Marks>
    </arc:ElasticSlider>
</UserControl>
```

Detents work only while the thumb is dragged. Within 7 px of a mark on screen, the pointer holds the value on the mark,
and the thumb glides onto it; moving farther away releases the value to the pointer again. A mark outside `Minimum` and
`Maximum` is ignored. When two marks are less than about 14 px apart on screen, the nearer one always wins, so the other
cannot be reached by dragging. Keys do not snap to marks: they move by `SmallChange`, and a key press that lands exactly
on a mark still plays the tick's pop.

Use marks for the values people actually choose: `0` and `100` for the limits, one middle preset, or a level that has a
meaning such as unity gain. Label only the ones that need a name (`Off`, `Max`); a row of bare numbers under the track
adds noise.

```xml
<arc:ElasticSlider Label="Brightness" Value="50" Width="360">
    <arc:ElasticSlider.Marks>
        <arc:SliderMark Value="0" Label="Off" />
        <arc:SliderMark Value="50" Label="50" />
        <arc:SliderMark Value="100" Label="Max" />
    </arc:ElasticSlider.Marks>
</arc:ElasticSlider>
```

### Steps and format

`SmallChange` is the step the value snaps to. Arrow keys and a drag without a detent both land on it. `LargeChange`
is the step for `PageUp`, `PageDown` and `Shift` with an arrow; when it is not set, it is a tenth of the range.

`ValueFormatter` formats the value tag, the readout and the spoken value. It is a `Func<double, string>`, so set it in
code or bind it from the view model. When it is not set, the value is shown with as many decimals as the step and the
minimum need, so a step of 0.1 shows `1.0` and a whole-number step shows `40`. `IsValueVisible` hides the readout
beside the label. The tag still appears while the thumb is dragged or changed by keys, so hiding the readout does not
hide the value.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ElasticSliderFineStepsDemo">
    <arc:ElasticSlider x:Name="Zoom"
                       Label="Zoom"
                       Minimum="0.5"
                       Maximum="3"
                       SmallChange="0.1"
                       Value="1"
                       Width="360"
                       HorizontalAlignment="Center">
        <arc:ElasticSlider.StartIcon>
            <arc:ArcGlyph Data="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.ZoomOut}"
                          Size="16"
                          Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}"
                          VerticalAlignment="Center" />
        </arc:ElasticSlider.StartIcon>
        <arc:ElasticSlider.EndIcon>
            <arc:ArcGlyph Data="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.ZoomIn}"
                          Size="16"
                          Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}"
                          VerticalAlignment="Center" />
        </arc:ElasticSlider.EndIcon>
        <arc:ElasticSlider.Marks>
            <arc:SliderMark Value="1" />
            <arc:SliderMark Value="2" />
        </arc:ElasticSlider.Marks>
    </arc:ElasticSlider>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class ElasticSliderFineStepsDemo : UserControl
{
    public ElasticSliderFineStepsDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Zoom.ValueFormatter = v => $"{v:0.0}×";
    }
}
```

```xml
<arc:ElasticSlider Label="Zoom"
                   Minimum="0.5"
                   Maximum="3"
                   SmallChange="0.1"
                   Value="1"
                   Width="360"
                   ValueFormatter="{Binding ZoomFormatter}" />
```

Choose the step from the track width. A step should move the thumb by several pixels: on a track about 300 px wide, a
step of 0.1 across a range of 2.5 moves it 12 px, which is visible. A much finer step makes each key press look like
nothing happened, and a much coarser one skips the values in between.

### Events

`ValueCommitted` runs once per release, per key press that changes the value, and per clicked mark label. Its
`SliderValueCommittedEventArgs.Value` is the committed value; `LowerValue` and `UpperValue` repeat it and `IsRange` is
`False`, because the control has one value. A key press at a limit does not change the value, so it does not commit.
Put slow work, such as a network request, on `ValueCommitted`, not on `ValueChanged`, which the inherited event raises
on every step of a drag.

```csharp
volume.ValueCommitted += (_, e) => SaveVolume(e.Value);
volume.ValueChanged += (_, e) => PreviewVolume(e.NewValue);
```

### Binding to a view model

In an MVVM app the view model owns the value and the slider mirrors it. Use CommunityToolkit.Mvvm for the view model.
`Value` is two-way: a drag, a key press or a detent writes the new value back to the view model, and a change made in
code moves the thumb with a spring. `ValueCommitted` is an event, not a command, so subscribe to it in the view's code
behind and call the view model from there.

```csharp
public interface IAudioSettings
{
    Task SetVolumeAsync(double level);
}

public partial class PlaybackViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    private readonly IAudioSettings _settings;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private double _volume = 40;

    public PlaybackViewModel(IAudioSettings settings) => _settings = settings;

    public Task SaveVolumeAsync(double value) => _settings.SetVolumeAsync(value);
}
```

```xml
<arc:ElasticSlider x:Name="Volume"
                   Label="Volume"
                   Minimum="0"
                   Maximum="100"
                   Value="{Binding Volume, Mode=TwoWay}"
                   Width="360" />
```

```csharp
// In the view's code behind, after InitializeComponent().
Volume.ValueCommitted += async (_, e) => await ViewModel.SaveVolumeAsync(e.Value);
```

- `Value` is the two-way property to bind.
- Bind `Mode=TwoWay` explicitly so the intent is visible in the XAML. The view model's `Volume` then changes on every
  step of a drag, which is right for a preview and wrong for an expensive save; save from `ValueCommitted` instead.
- Bind `Value` to a `double` property. The slider works in `double`, so a whole-number property should also be a
  `double`, or the view model should convert at its boundary.
- `ValueFormatter` is set in code or with a binding to a `Func<double, string>` on the view model, as in the Usage
  example.

### Using motion with restraint

The motion on this control carries information. The stretch says that the limit was reached, the sway shows how fast
the thumb moved, and the detent pop confirms that the value landed on a mark. Use it on one or two elastic sliders in a
view, where a person spends time adjusting a value by feel. Put several of them in a list and the motion becomes a
pattern that competes with the content; use `Slider` there.

Reduced motion removes the stretch, the sway and the detent pop. The thumb goes straight to the value and the tag only
fades in, so the control still reads correctly without the physical feedback. Do not depend on the motion to show the
value: the readout and the spoken value always carry it.

### Disabled

A disabled slider leaves the tab order and fades to 50% opacity. Its track shows the "no" cursor and ignores the
pointer and the keys. Use it only while the value cannot apply, and say why nearby, for example "Available on the Pro
plan". A value the person can never change belongs in `Progress` or in plain text.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ElasticSliderDisabledDemo">
    <arc:ElasticSlider Label="Contrast"
                       Value="30"
                       IsEnabled="False"
                       Width="360"
                       HorizontalAlignment="Center" />
</UserControl>
```

### Example: photo editor adjustments

An image editor's inspector with three adjustments: exposure and contrast centered on 0, and the opacity of the selected
layer. The integers need no formatter, so the readout shows plain values. The detent on 0 is the one that matters: a
person who drags exposure off neutral and back wants to land on it exactly, and the thumb holds there.

![An adjustments panel with exposure and contrast detents at zero and a layer opacity slider](https://docs.tkcode.si/shots/Docs/Sliders/ElasticSlider/images/PhotoAdjustments.webp)

```xml
<StackPanel Width="560" Spacing="22">
    <TextBlock Text="Adjustments"
               FontSize="14"
               FontWeight="SemiBold"
               Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
    <arc:ElasticSlider Label="Exposure"
                       Minimum="-100"
                       Maximum="100"
                       Value="25"
                       SmallChange="1">
        <arc:ElasticSlider.StartIcon>
            <arc:ArcGlyph Data="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Moon}"
                          Size="16"
                          Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}"
                          VerticalAlignment="Center" />
        </arc:ElasticSlider.StartIcon>
        <arc:ElasticSlider.EndIcon>
            <arc:ArcGlyph Data="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Sun}"
                          Size="16"
                          Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}"
                          VerticalAlignment="Center" />
        </arc:ElasticSlider.EndIcon>
        <arc:ElasticSlider.Marks>
            <arc:SliderMark Value="-100" Label="-100" />
            <arc:SliderMark Value="0" Label="0" />
            <arc:SliderMark Value="100" Label="100" />
        </arc:ElasticSlider.Marks>
    </arc:ElasticSlider>
    <arc:ElasticSlider Label="Contrast"
                       Minimum="-100"
                       Maximum="100"
                       Value="-10"
                       SmallChange="1">
        <arc:ElasticSlider.Marks>
            <arc:SliderMark Value="0" />
        </arc:ElasticSlider.Marks>
    </arc:ElasticSlider>
    <arc:ElasticSlider Label="Layer opacity"
                       Minimum="0"
                       Maximum="100"
                       Value="80"
                       SmallChange="1"
                       IsValueVisible="True" />
</StackPanel>
```

The labels are nouns, and the marks print only the values people need to recognize: the two limits and the neutral
point. The contrast slider has one unlabeled tick at 0, so its detent still holds without adding a label row. The
layer opacity slider has no marks, because no preset opacity is meaningful for every layer.

### Content guidelines

- **Label**: one or two nouns in sentence case, such as "Volume", "Brightness" or "Layer opacity". The label names the
  thumb for assistive technology, so it must say what the value is.
- **Mark label**: a short word or number that names the preset: `Off`, `Max`, `50`. A mark without a label still
  holds the thumb, so leave unlabeled any preset that is obvious from the track.
- **Units**: put the unit in `ValueFormatter` output, not in the label, so the readout, the tag and the spoken value
  agree. Keep the unit short; a percent sign is clearer than the word "percent" on a track this small.
- **Hints**: a sentence beside the control, not inside it, when the value has a consequence: "Applies to the selected
  layer only."

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| Set the volume level | Volume |
| Maximum volume | Max |
| 40 percent | 40% |
| Brightness (0 to 100) | Brightness |

### Best practices

**Do**

- Keep one elastic slider per decision and place it where the person is already looking at the result, such as beside
  the preview. The stretch and tag work best when the effect is visible while the thumb moves.
- Add detents at the values people return to, such as neutral, off or a standard preset, so they can land on them
  without precision.
- Save from `ValueCommitted`, not from `ValueChanged`. A drag raises `ValueChanged` on every step; committing on
  release sends one request for the chosen value.
- Pick a `SmallChange` that matches the precision the setting needs, and let `LargeChange` cover a useful jump (a tenth
  of the range by default is a good start).

**Avoid**

- Using the control for values that need an exact entry, such as a tax rate or a quantity. The track approximates the
  value, and people then have to correct it by stepping one key at a time.
- Stacking several elastic sliders in one list or table. The repeated stretch and sway draw attention away from the data
  they belong to.
- Hiding the readout and relying on the tag alone for a value people must record. The tag appears only while the thumb
  moves or is changed by keys, so a settled value is then invisible.
- Marks closer than about 14 px. The nearer mark wins and the other becomes unreachable with the pointer.
- Putting text that needs room in `StartIcon` or `EndIcon`. Those slots move with the stretch, so long content clips
  or crowds the track.

### Common questions

**Why does the thumb not land on a mark when I press a key?** Keys step by `SmallChange` and never snap to marks. A mark
is reachable with the keyboard only when a step lands on its value. For marks at 0, 25, 50, 75 and 100, set
`SmallChange="25"`, or use a `SmallChange` that divides the spacing between the marks evenly.

**How do I hide the readout and keep the value out of the way?** Set `IsValueVisible="False"` to hide the readout beside the
label. The tag still appears while the thumb is dragged or changed by keys, so the number stays available during an
adjustment and is hidden once the person stops.

**Can one elastic slider select a range?** No. `ElasticSlider` has one `Value` and no `IsRange`. Use `Slider` with
`IsRange="True"` and read `LowerValue` and `UpperValue`.

**Why does a key press at the end not raise `ValueCommitted`?** At a limit the value cannot change, so the control only
bounces the track toward the key. No value changes, so there is nothing to commit; a listener that saves on commit
correctly does nothing.

**Why is there no stretch or sway on a machine with reduced motion?** The stretch, the sway and the detent pop run only at
the full motion level. At the reduced level the thumb goes straight to the value and the tag only fades in. Test the
feel of the control at the full level, and check that the reduced level still reads correctly.

## API reference

### ElasticSlider

Arc elastic slider: a single value slider made of something that gives. The thumb swells to 1.28× under the finger (P24), the track stretches like rubber up to 26px past either end and springs back with the release velocity (0.5s, bounce 0.42), the end icons are pushed outward with the stretch, a value tag hangs off the thumb and sways with its speed (up to 11°), and marks act as detents the thumb clicks into within 7px. Arrows, Shift+arrows, PageUp / PageDown and Home / End work as in a native range input; a key at a limit hits the wall and bounces. `SmallChange` is the step the value snaps to.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Label` | `string?` | `null` | Visible label; it also names the thumb. |
| `ValueFormatter` | `Func<double, string>?` | `null` | Formats the value in the value tag and readout; when not set, the value is shown with the slider's Decimals. |
| `IsValueVisible` | `bool` | `true` | Shows the value beside the label. The tag still appears while dragging or using keys. |
| `StartIcon` | `object?` | `null` | Icon before the track; pushed outward when the track is pulled past its start. |
| `EndIcon` | `object?` | `null` | Icon after the track; pushed outward when the track is pulled past its end. |
| `Marks` | `IList<SliderMark>` | – | Detents: a dragged thumb clicks into each one and holds for a few pixels. Labels print under the track. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ValueCommitted` | `SliderValueCommittedEventArgs` | Runs once a drag is released, a key changes the value or a mark label is clicked. |

Pseudo-classes: `:dragging`, `:tag`, `:marks`

Derives from `RangeBase`: every member of `RangeBase` works as well.

### SliderMark

A mark on a `Slider` or `ElasticSlider` track. A mark without a label draws a tick; a mark with a label also prints it under the track, and clicking the label moves there. On an elastic slider marks are detents the dragged thumb clicks into.

## Accessibility

- `Label` names the thumb. The thumb's spoken value is the formatted `Value`, so a `ValueFormatter` that returns
  `40%` is read as `40%`. Without a label the thumb has no name, so keep the label visible.
- The control itself is a group, and the thumb is the only stop in the tab order. The track row, the value tag, the
  readout and the mark labels are not separate stops.
- The mark labels are hidden from assistive technology. Clicking a label is a pointer shortcut; the keyboard reaches the
  same values by stepping with `SmallChange` or `LargeChange`.
- The value tag and the detent pop are visual only. The spoken value carries the same number, so the tag adds nothing a
  screen reader user needs.
- The focus ring appears after a key press, not after a pointer press, so a mouse user is not left with a ring on the
  thumb.

### Keyboard

The thumb receives focus with `Tab`. The control itself does not take focus.

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` | Move focus to the thumb and out of it; a disabled slider is skipped |
| `Right` / `Up` | Increase the value by `SmallChange` |
| `Left` / `Down` | Decrease the value by `SmallChange` |
| `Shift` + arrow, `PageUp` / `PageDown` | Increase or decrease by `LargeChange` |
| `Home` / `End` | Go to `Minimum` or `Maximum` |
| An arrow, `PageUp`, `PageDown`, `Home` or `End` at a limit | The value stays put; the track stretches toward the key and springs back |

## Motion

- Past either end, the track stretches like rubber, up to 26 px, and springs back with the release speed. The thumb
  swells while it is held.
- The value tag hangs above the thumb and follows it on a soft spring. Its angle follows the thumb's speed, so a fast
  drag tilts it more, up to 11 degrees.
- When the thumb clicks into a detent, the tick on the track pops once, up to twice its size, and settles in 0.34 s.
- Values that arrive from outside a drag, such as a key press, a bound value or a clicked mark label, move the thumb with
  a spring from where it currently is on screen.
- Reduced motion removes the stretch, the sway and the detent pop. The thumb goes straight to the value and the tag only
  fades in. Off motion jumps straight to the end state.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| Drag past an end | The track stretches up to 26 px and springs back with the release speed (0.5 s, bounce 0.42) | No stretch; the thumb stops at the limit | Immediate |
| Thumb while dragged | Swells to 1.28 times on a snappy spring | Swells at once | Immediate |
| Value tag | Follows the thumb on a soft spring and sways up to 11 degrees | Stays at the thumb and fades in over 0.15 s | Immediate |
| Readout | Fades out while the tag rides the thumb | Switches at once | Immediate |
| Detent pop | The tick goes from 1 to 2.1 to 1 times its size over 0.34 s | No pop | No pop |

## Related

- `Slider` for a quiet form control, a range with two thumbs, or a list of sliders where the motion would repeat.
- `NumberField` when the person needs to type an exact number.
- `Progress` for a value that is shown but not changed by the person.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `Slider` | The setting sits in a form, the value is a range, or many sliders repeat in one view |
| `NumberField` | The person must type or step an exact number, with a unit and bounds |
| `ScrubInput` | The value is a number changed by dragging on the label itself, without a track |
| `Progress` | The value is shown to the person and the application sets it |
| `Switch` | The setting has two states and no intermediate values |
