# Calendar

> Browse dates in a clear, compact month view.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/calendar

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.CalendarSingleDateDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12">
        <arc:Calendar x:Name="Month"
                      ShowToday="True"
                      DateSelected="OnDateSelected" />
        <TextBlock x:Name="Picked"
                   Text="Pick a day"
                   FontSize="14"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class CalendarSingleDateDemo : UserControl
{
    public CalendarSingleDateDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Month.SelectedDate = DateOnly.FromDateTime(DateTime.Today);
    }

    private void OnDateSelected(object? sender, CalendarDateSelectedEventArgs e)
        => Picked.Text = $"Selected {e.Date:D}";
}
```

## When to use

`Calendar` shows one month of dates on the page, with the selected day, the navigation and the limits visible at all
times. It fits screens where the calendar is the content: a booking page, an availability view or a scheduling panel
in which the person compares several days before choosing one. A date field that opens a popup is a different job,
covered by `DatePicker`.

- **Stay dates on a booking page**: a guest chooses a check-in day in a hotel or rental flow. The whole month stays on
  screen, so the guest can see weekends, sold-out nights and the edges of the booking window without opening anything.
- **Appointment slots in a clinic or service console**: an operations user picks the day first and then the time. The
  month view shows which days are open before the time list is loaded for the chosen day.
- **Availability and leave planning**: a manager in an internal tool marks a day for a shift or a leave request. The
  month stays visible while the person edits the rest of the page, which a popup would hide.
- **Report and export ranges that start from one day**: a finance user picks the statement date for an invoice run.
  Limits such as `MaxDate` keep the choice inside the closing period of the books.
- **Keyboard-first forms in admin consoles**: the grid has a single tab stop, arrow keys, and Page keys for months and
  years, so an operator who never uses the mouse can still move through a month quickly.

## When not to use

- **A date field in a form**: use `DatePicker`. It is a field that opens the calendar in a popup, so the form keeps its
  height and the label, description and error rows stay aligned with the other fields.
- **A start and end date**: use `DateRangePicker`. It holds two dates, shows presets such as "Last 7 days", and applies
  the range only when the person confirms it.
- **A time of day or a date with a time**: use `TimePicker` next to a `DatePicker`. `Calendar` only chooses a day; its
  value has no time part.
- **Dates listed as records**: use `DataGrid` for invoices, orders or shipments sorted by a date column. A calendar
  shows one month at a time and cannot list the details of many records.
- **A short pick from a few known dates**: use `Select` or `RadioGroup` when the options are named values, such as
  "This week" or "Next billing cycle", rather than days on a grid.

## Usage

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:Calendar ShowToday="True" />
</UserControl>
```

`Calendar` derives from Avalonia's `TemplatedControl`, so it takes the usual layout, `IsEnabled`, `Focusable` and
styling properties. Its month and selection motion, its keyboard model and its limits are part of this library. Every public property,
method and event is listed in the API reference.

### Anatomy

1. **Month title**: the name of the displayed month and year in the culture's year-month pattern (for example
   "October 2026" in `en-US`). It uses the base type size with medium weight and sits left in the header row, which is
   at least 34 px high with 14 px below it.
2. **Today button** (`ShowToday`, `TodayLabel`): a ghost pill with the label text, 32 px high and 11 px of side padding.
   It is visible only when `ShowToday` is `True`.
3. **Previous and next buttons**: two 32 px round ghost buttons with a 16 px chevron. They sit at the right edge of the
   header with 2 px between them. A button that would move past `MinDate` or `MaxDate` is disabled and drawn at 36%
   opacity.
4. **Weekday row**: the short weekday names in the muted text color, in the extra-small type size with medium weight.
   It starts on `FirstDayOfWeek` and has 6 px below it.
5. **Day grid**: six rows of seven days, 4 px apart. Each day is 14 px text in the small type size. The six rows are
   always present, so a month with five weeks shows days from the neighboring months in the last row.
6. **Selection disc**: a filled circle in the accent color behind the selected day, with its number in the accent
   foreground color. Hovering an unselected day fills it with the surface-muted color; hovering the selected day uses
   the stronger accent.
7. **Focus ring**: a 2 px ring in the focus color around the day that holds keyboard focus.

The width is `min(100%, 328px)`: the calendar never grows beyond 328 px and it is left aligned in its container. Because
the height is fixed by the six rows, the calendar takes the same space in every month, and nothing below it moves when
the person navigates.

### Selected date

`SelectedDate` is a `DateOnly?`, and only its date part is used. It is two-way by default, so a bound value follows
the day the person picks and a value set in code moves the selection. Use `null` for no selection; the calendar then
has no selected day and its roving tab stop moves to today, or to the first open day of the month.

`DateSelected` is raised only when the person picks a day: a click, Enter or Space on a focused day, or the Today
button. Setting `SelectedDate` from code does not raise it. Subscribe to the bound property when code changes must
also trigger a reaction, and to `DateSelected` when the reaction is for a user action only.

```xml
<arc:Calendar SelectedDate="{Binding StayDate, Mode=TwoWay}" />
```

```csharp
calendar.DateSelected += (_, e) => status.Text = $"Selected {e.Date:D}";
```

The event carries one value:

| Member | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `Date` | `DateOnly` | The day the person picked. It is never a disabled day. |

### Limits and disabled days

`MinDate` and `MaxDate` are the earliest and latest selectable days. `DisabledDates` is a `Func<DateOnly, bool>` that
returns `true` for each day that must not be picked, such as weekends, booked nights or public holidays. A day is
disabled when any of the three rules applies.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.CalendarLimitsAndDisabledDaysDemo">
    <arc:Calendar x:Name="Limited" FirstDayOfWeek="Monday" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class CalendarLimitsAndDisabledDaysDemo : UserControl
{
    public CalendarLimitsAndDisabledDaysDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        var today = DateOnly.FromDateTime(DateTime.Today);
        Limited.MinDate = today.AddDays(-3);
        Limited.MaxDate = today.AddDays(45);
        Limited.DisabledDates = d => d.DayOfWeek is DayOfWeek.Saturday or DayOfWeek.Sunday;
    }
}
```

The rules apply in three places: a disabled day cannot be clicked or activated with Enter or Space, the arrow and Page
keys never land on it, and the navigation buttons stop at the month that holds the limit. When a keyboard move would
land on a disabled day, the focus steps past it in the direction of travel: with Saturday and Sunday disabled,
pressing Right on a Friday moves the focus to Monday.

### Displayed month

`DisplayMonth` is a `DateOnly?` that names the displayed month. Any day in the month works; the calendar normalizes the
value to the first of the month. It is two-way: when the person moves to another month with the buttons or the keyboard,
`DisplayMonth` is updated, so a bound view model always knows the month on screen.

```xml
<arc:Calendar DisplayMonth="{Binding ViewMonth, Mode=TwoWay}" />
```

When no `DisplayMonth` is set, the calendar starts on the month of `SelectedDate`, and on the current month when nothing
is selected. After the control has started, changing `SelectedDate` in code does not turn the view to its month; set
`DisplayMonth` or call `GoToMonth` for that. `GoToMonth(DateOnly date, bool raise = true)` slides to the month that
contains `date`, and with `raise` left at its default it also updates `DisplayMonth`.

### Labels and culture

`Culture` sets the language of the month names, the weekday names and the long date in the accessible names. When it is
not set, the current UI culture is used, so an application that follows the operating system language needs no
setting. `FirstDayOfWeek` chooses the first column; it defaults to `Sunday`, and a European or ISO layout usually sets
`Monday`.

`TodayLabel`, `PreviousMonthLabel` and `NextMonthLabel` replace the text and the names. The Today label is visible
text; the previous and next labels are only accessible names, because those buttons show chevrons. Translate all three
together so a screen reader does not switch languages in the middle of the control.

```xml
<arc:Calendar Culture="de-DE"
              FirstDayOfWeek="Monday"
              TodayLabel="Heute"
              PreviousMonthLabel="Vorheriger Monat"
              NextMonthLabel="Nächster Monat"
              ShowToday="True" />
```

### Focus and the roving tab stop

The grid has one tab stop: the day last focused, else the selected day, else today, else the first open day of the
shown month. Tab moves into the grid on that day and out of it to the next control, so a long form does not need
forty-two stops. `FocusTabbableDay(NavigationMethod method = NavigationMethod.Directional)` moves focus to that day and
returns `false` when no day can take it, for example when the control is not shown yet or every day in the month is
disabled. Host it in a popup or a dialog, and call it after the control is attached, so the arrow keys work at once.

### Binding to a view model

A booking page owns its dates and its availability rules in the view model. The calendar binds to the dates and
receives the rule as a function, so the rule can read the view model's data.

```csharp
public partial class StayViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    private readonly HashSet<DateOnly> _bookedNights;

    public StayViewModel(IReadOnlySet<DateOnly> bookedNights)
    {
        _bookedNights = bookedNights.ToHashSet();
        MinStayDate = DateOnly.FromDateTime(DateTime.Today);
    }

    [ObservableProperty]
    private DateOnly? _stayDate;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private DateOnly? _viewMonth;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private string? _reservationNotice;

    public DateOnly MinStayDate { get; }

    public DateOnly MaxStayDate => MinStayDate.AddMonths(6);

    public Func<DateOnly, bool> IsBooked => date => _bookedNights.Contains(date);

    [RelayCommand]
    private void Continue()
    {
        if (StayDate is { } checkIn)
        {
            ReservationNotice = $"Holding check-in {checkIn:MMM d, yyyy} for 15 minutes.";
        }
    }
}
```

```xml
<StackPanel Width="328" Spacing="12">
    <arc:Calendar SelectedDate="{Binding StayDate, Mode=TwoWay}"
                  DisplayMonth="{Binding ViewMonth, Mode=TwoWay}"
                  MinDate="{Binding MinStayDate}"
                  MaxDate="{Binding MaxStayDate}"
                  DisabledDates="{Binding IsBooked}" />
    <arc:Button Content="Continue" Command="{Binding ContinueCommand}" />
    <TextBlock Text="{Binding ReservationNotice}" />
</StackPanel>
```

`SelectedDate` and `DisplayMonth` are two-way, so the view model receives every pick and every month change.
`MinDate`, `MaxDate` and `DisabledDates` are one-way inputs that the view model sets when its rules change. Setting
a property to a new value is enough: the calendar refreshes its grid and its navigation buttons when a limit changes.
The calendar has no command of its own. The `Continue` button calls the view model's command, which reads `StayDate`
and sets `ReservationNotice`, a string that a `TextBlock` below the button can bind to.

The date rules are checked on user input only. A `SelectedDate` set by binding or code is not compared with
`MinDate`, `MaxDate` or `DisabledDates`, so the view model must not set a date that is outside them. Keep the
limits and the value consistent in the view model.

### Example: hotel stay dates

A rental booking page for Northwind Lodge. The guest chooses a check-in day in November 2026. The calendar starts on
the month of the selected night, the earliest day is the first of November, so the previous month button is disabled,
and the summary row below states the decision in plain words. The calendar has no visible Today button in this scene,
because the scene is fixed to a date and should look the same on every machine.

The month view is the whole control: no separate title or legend is needed, because the header names the month and the
disc shows the choice.

![A stay dates card with a November 2026 calendar, a selected check-in day and a continue button](https://docs.tkcode.si/shots/Docs/Pickers/Calendar/images/StayDates.webp)

```xml
<Border Width="560"
        Padding="24"
        Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Surface}"
        BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource BorderSubtle}"
        BorderThickness="1"
        CornerRadius="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource RadiusPanel}">
    <StackPanel Spacing="16">
        <StackPanel Spacing="4">
            <TextBlock Text="Stay dates"
                       FontSize="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TypeLG}"
                       FontWeight="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource WeightMedium}"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
            <TextBlock Text="Harbor View Suite, room 412"
                       FontSize="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TypeSM}"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
        </StackPanel>
        <arc:Calendar SelectedDate="2026-11-12"
                      MinDate="2026-11-01"
                      MaxDate="2026-12-31" />
        <Grid ColumnDefinitions="*,Auto">
            <TextBlock Text="Check in Nov 12, 2026, 3 nights"
                       VerticalAlignment="Center"
                       FontSize="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TypeSM}"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
            <arc:Button Grid.Column="1" Content="Continue" />
        </Grid>
    </StackPanel>
</Border>
```

The decisions in this example are deliberate. The limits come from the booking window, so a guest cannot choose a past
night or one beyond the year-end. The summary repeats the choice in words, which matters for a screen reader and for a
guest who scrolls back to the page. The button is the single primary action; the calendar itself has no action buttons.

### Content guidelines

- **Month title**: the calendar writes it for you in the culture's pattern; do not add a second title with the same
  month in the same card. Name the purpose in the heading above the calendar, such as "Stay dates" or "Leave request".
- **Today label**: keep the default "Today" for an English interface, or use the word the product uses for the current
  day. It is a visible button, so keep it to one word.
- **Previous and next labels**: say the destination, "Previous month" or "Next month", because the buttons are announced
  by name only.
- **Summary text under the calendar**: write the outcome in full, with the date as digits and the month name in the
  culture's format, such as "Check in Nov 12, 2026, 3 nights". State the consequence, not the mechanism.
- **Disabled days**: explain them nearby when a whole category is blocked, for example "Weekends are not bookable".
  The reason belongs on the page, because the grid itself does not say why a day is blocked.

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| Date | Stay dates |
| Choose a date | Check-in date |
| Next | Next month |
| Selected: 12 | Check in Nov 12, 2026 |
| Sat, Sun unavailable | Weekends are not bookable for this suite. |

### Best practices

**Do**

- Set `MinDate` and `MaxDate` to the real booking or reporting window. The navigation then stops at the edge, and a
  person cannot page into a month with nothing to pick.
- Use `DisabledDates` for rules that are data, such as booked nights, and `MinDate` and `MaxDate` for the window. The
  two rules read the same way in the grid and in the keyboard model.
- Bind `SelectedDate` two-way and react to the bound value in the view model, so the summary and the save action
  always see the same day as the grid.
- Choose `FirstDayOfWeek` for the region of the product, because the first column is what people scan first.
- Keep one calendar per decision. Two calendars side by side on one page make the person compare two months at once,
  which is better served by `DateRangePicker`.

**Avoid**

- Using `DateSelected` as the only source of the value. It is raised for user actions only, so a value set in code
  would never reach a view model that waits for the event.
- Setting a `SelectedDate` that breaks `MinDate`, `MaxDate` or `DisabledDates` in code. The calendar does not
  correct it, so the grid can show a selected day that the person could never pick.
- Putting the calendar inside a form that also has a date field. Two date inputs for the same value confuse the person
  about which one is current; use `DatePicker` in forms.
- Turning `ShowToday` on for a calendar whose window does not include today. The button then leads outside the limits.
- Adding a second, duplicate month title above the calendar. The header already names the month, and the duplicate
  text does not move with it when the person navigates.

### Common questions

**Why does the grid always show six weeks?** Each month uses six rows, so the grid has 42 days, and days from the
neighboring months fill the empty cells. The height never changes when the person navigates, so the content below the
calendar does not jump from one month to the next.

**Why did my handler not run when I set `SelectedDate` in code?** `DateSelected` is raised only for a pick by the
person: a click, Enter or Space on a focused day, or the Today button. Use the bound `SelectedDate` property for code
changes, and use `DateSelected` only for the actions that the person takes.

**How do I move the view to the month of a given date?** Call `GoToMonth(new DateOnly(2027, 3, 1))` for a navigation
that animates, or set `DisplayMonth` to a day in that month. `GoToMonth` also updates `DisplayMonth` unless you pass
`raise: false`.

**Can a limit change while the calendar is open?** Yes. Setting `MinDate`, `MaxDate`, `DisabledDates`, `FirstDayOfWeek`
or `Culture` refreshes the grid, and the navigation buttons are updated to match. A selection that is now disabled stays
selected until the person picks another day, so clear it in code when the rule makes it invalid.

**What happens when the calendar stays open past midnight?** The calendar follows the local date. When the day changes,
the highlighted today and the Today button are updated, so a calendar left on screen overnight does not show the old day
as today.

## API reference

### Calendar

A single-date month calendar. Months slide on one spring-driven strip (arrows, PageUp/PageDown, Today and a bound `DisplayMonth` all travel the same way), the title slides with them, and the selected disc glides between days while each number flips color as the disc passes it. Every month shows six weeks, so the height never changes. Full keyboard model: arrows, Home/End, PageUp/PageDown (Shift = year), Enter/Space; disabled days are skipped in the direction of travel.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SelectedDate` | `DateOnly?` | `null` | The selected date, or null when nothing is selected. Two-way. |
| `DisplayMonth` | `DateOnly?` | `null` | Any date in the displayed month (normalized to its first day). Defaults to the selection's month, else today's. |
| `MinDate` | `DateOnly?` | `null` | Earliest selectable date; earlier days are disabled. Null means no lower limit. |
| `MaxDate` | `DateOnly?` | `null` | Latest selectable date; later days are disabled. Null means no upper limit. |
| `DisabledDates` | `Func<DateOnly, bool>?` | `null` | Extra disabled days (weekends, booked dates...). |
| `ShowToday` | `bool` | `false` | Adds a Today button that slides back to the current month and selects today when it is available. |
| `FirstDayOfWeek` | `DayOfWeek` | `Sunday` | The first day of each week row (default Sunday). |
| `Culture` | `CultureInfo?` | `null` | Culture for month and weekday names (null = current UI culture). |
| `TodayLabel` | `string` | `"Today"` | Text of the Today button (default "Today"). |
| `PreviousMonthLabel` | `string` | `"Previous month"` | Label of the previous-month button (default "Previous month"). |
| `NextMonthLabel` | `string` | `"Next month"` | Label of the next-month button (default "Next month"). |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `DateSelected` | `CalendarDateSelectedEventArgs` | Raised when the user picks a day (click, Enter / Space, or Today). |

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

## Accessibility

- The calendar is named by its month title, for example "October 2026", so the person hears what the grid shows when
  focus enters it.
- Each day is a button named with its full date in the culture's long format, such as "Tuesday, October 20, 2026".
  The selected day carries the help text "selected", and today carries "today".
- The previous, next and Today buttons have names: the `PreviousMonthLabel`, `NextMonthLabel`, and the Today label
  followed by today's full date. The previous and next buttons are disabled in the month that holds `MinDate` or
  `MaxDate`, so they are announced as unavailable there.
- Only one day is in the Tab order at a time. Arrow keys, Home, End and the Page keys move the focus inside the grid;
  Tab leaves the grid for the next control.
- A change of month is announced politely. The months that slide out of view are not focusable and are hidden from
  assistive technology, so the focus never lands on a day the person cannot see.
- Disabled days stay in the grid, so the person can see that the day exists but cannot be picked.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Left` / `Right` | Move the focus one day back or forward; crosses into the neighboring month |
| `Up` / `Down` | Move the focus one week back or forward |
| `Home` / `End` | Move to the first or last day of the week, using `FirstDayOfWeek` |
| `PageUp` / `PageDown` | Move the focus one month back or forward; the day is kept, clamped to the month's length |
| `Shift` + `PageUp` / `PageDown` | Move the focus one year back or forward |
| `Enter` / `Space` | Select the focused day; a disabled day is ignored |

Moves stop at `MinDate` and `MaxDate`, and they step past disabled days in the direction of travel. A move onto a new
month changes `DisplayMonth` and moves the focus in the same frame the month begins to slide. Tab and Shift+Tab leave
the grid; the arrow keys are handled by the calendar only when the focus is on a day.

## Motion

- The months slide on one strip in the direction of travel. The title slides with them, and the selected disc
  glides from day to day. The numbers change color as the disc passes them.
- A long jump, such as Today or Shift + PageDown, starts from the month next to the target and does not pass
  the months in between.
- Reduced motion jumps the months and the disc straight to the end state and replaces the title in place.
  Off does the same.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| Moving one month (buttons, PageUp, PageDown) | The month strip slides on a short spring with no bounce, in the direction of travel | The new month appears at once | Immediate |
| Month title | The old title slides out in the direction of travel while the new one fades in | The title is replaced in place | Immediate |
| Selected disc between days | Glides in a straight line across the grid | Jumps to the new day | Jumps to the new day |
| First appearance of the selection | Grows from 60% scale with a quick spring while it fades in | Shown at once | Immediate |
| Day numbers under the disc | Change color as the disc passes them | Change color at once | Immediate |
| Long jump (Today, Shift + Page keys) | Starts from the month next to the target, skipping the months between | Jumps | Immediate |

Motion never delays the keyboard. A second arrow press while the strip is still sliding retargets the same spring,
so the calendar follows the newest position without queuing the earlier moves.

## Related

- `DatePicker` for a date field that opens the calendar in a popup, typically in a form.
- `DateRangePicker` for a start and end date with presets.
- `TimePicker` for choosing a time of day.
- `DataGrid` for dated records that need columns and sorting.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `DatePicker` | A form needs one date in a field with a label, description and error row |
| `DateRangePicker` | The person picks a start and an end, often with presets such as "Last 30 days" |
| `TimePicker` | The value is a time of day, or the time is paired with a date |
| `DataGrid` | The dates belong to many records that need sorting and columns |
| `Select` | The choices are named options rather than days |

# Date picker

> Choose a date without losing context.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/date-picker

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.DatePickerDateFieldDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12">
        <arc:DatePicker x:Name="Start"
                        Label="Start date"
                        Description="Type a date or press Alt+Down to open the calendar."
                        Culture="en-US"
                        Width="280"
                        HorizontalAlignment="Left"
                        SelectedDateChanged="OnSelectedDateChanged" />
        <TextBlock x:Name="Picked"
                   FontSize="13"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class DatePickerDateFieldDemo : UserControl
{
    public DatePickerDateFieldDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Start.SelectedDate = DateOnly.FromDateTime(DateTime.Today);
        Show(Start.SelectedDate);
    }

    private void OnSelectedDateChanged(object? sender, DatePickerSelectedDateChangedEventArgs e) => Show(e.NewDate);

    private void Show(DateOnly? date)
        => Picked.Text = $"SelectedDate: {(date is { } d ? d.ToString("yyyy-MM-dd") : "none")}";
}
```

## When to use

`DatePicker` is the form field for one calendar date. It looks and behaves like a text field: the person can type a date
or open a calendar popup to pick one, and the value sits next to the other fields with the same label, description and
error rows. Use it wherever a form asks for a day and the surrounding page should keep its context while the choice is
made.

- **Start and due dates in a project or order form**: a project manager sets the start date and the due date of a
  milestone. The two fields sit in one column, and the due date is limited by the start date through `MinDate`.
- **Invoice and billing dates in a finance console**: an accountant enters the issue date of an invoice. Typing
  `Oct 21, 2026` is faster than paging through a calendar for a date in the past, and the popup covers the rest.
- **Booking and appointment forms with limits**: a clinic or a rental desk accepts only dates that the business is open.
  `MinDate`, `MaxDate` and `DisabledDates` apply to the popup and to typed values, so an impossible date never reaches
  the server.
- **Localized forms for several markets**: a multilingual HR system shows the same field in German, Chinese or ISO
  format. The culture sets the month names, the parsing and the default display, and `DisplayFormat` fixes a pattern
  when the business requires one.
- **Filters that need one date**: an operations dashboard asks for a single report date before the data loads. For a
  start and end pair, use `DateRangePicker`.

## When not to use

- **A calendar that stays visible on the page**: use `Calendar` for a booking view or an availability grid that the
  person reads while they compare days. `DatePicker` hides the grid until it is opened.
- **A start and end date with presets**: use `DateRangePicker`. It holds two dates, offers presets such as "Last 7
  days", and applies the range only when the person confirms it.
- **A time of day, or a date and a time together**: use `TimePicker` next to a `DatePicker`. A `DatePicker` value has no
  time part, so a deadline with an hour must be built from two fields.
- **A date that is one of a few named periods**: use `Select` or `SegmentedControl` for choices such as "This quarter",
  "Last quarter" or "Custom". A `DatePicker` forces the person to compute the date that the period name already implies.
- **A free-text date in a message or a note**: use `Input` when the text is prose and will be read by people rather than
  stored as a date. A date field that rejects text it cannot parse is the wrong tool for a sentence.

## Usage

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:DatePicker Label="Start date"
                    Description="Type a date or press Alt+Down to open the calendar."
                    SelectedDate="{Binding StartDate, Mode=TwoWay}" />
</UserControl>
```

`DatePicker` derives from `FieldTextBox`, which is Arc's text field base and therefore an Avalonia `TextBox`. The field
keeps the text box behavior: the caret, selection, undo, IME composition and the clipboard. The label, description, error
row, size and placeholder come from the shared field foundation, so a `DatePicker` sits in a form with the same spacing
as an `Input`. The calendar popup is added on top, and the popup's own keys and pointer events never reach the text.

### Anatomy

1. **Label** (`Label`): the field name in the same style as `Input`, above the frame. It names the field for assistive
   technology and is linked to the trigger.
2. **Frame**: a 1 px border with the control radius on the surface color. Hover and focus change the border only, and
   the frame does not change size.
3. **Value**: the shown date, rolled part by part when it changes (see Motion). With no value, the placeholder shows in
   the muted text color; the default placeholder is "Select a date".
4. **Calendar button** (the drop-down button): a 28 px button at the right edge of the frame. The chevron turns 180
   degrees when the popup is open. Clicking it opens and closes the popup.
5. **Description** (`Description`): helper copy under the frame. It fades out while the popup is open, so its text does
   not show beyond the popup's corner.
6. **Error** (`ErrorMessage`): copy in the danger color under the frame. A non-empty value marks the field invalid.
7. **Popup**: the calendar and a footer, placed 8 px below the field. Its width is `min(320px, window width minus 32px)`
   with a 16 px inset. On a window 360 px wide or narrower, the popup matches the field's width and its inset is 12 px.
8. **Footer**: a "Clear" button on the left, disabled when there is no value, and a status line at the right that reads
   "Selected Oct 20, 2026" or "Choose a day".

The popup carries the same `Calendar` as the rest of the library, so the keyboard model, the limits and the month
navigation are the ones documented on the `Calendar` page.

### Value and typed text

`SelectedDate` is a `DateOnly?` and is two-way. A `null` value shows the placeholder. The value changes in three ways:
the person picks a day in the popup, the person types a date and commits it, or code sets the property. A typed date is
committed when the person presses Enter or leaves the field. An empty field commits `null`, which clears the value.

Text that does not parse, or a date outside the limits, is not accepted. The field returns to the last valid value, and
for a date outside the limits it shakes first to show that the entry was refused.

`SelectedDateChanged` is raised after each committed change, with the previous and new dates:

| Member | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `OldDate` | `DateOnly?` | The previous date, or `null` when there was none. |
| `NewDate` | `DateOnly?` | The new date, or `null` after Clear or an emptied field. |

```csharp
picker.SelectedDateChanged += (_, e) =>
{
    status.Text = e.NewDate is { } d ? $"Start: {d:yyyy-MM-dd}" : "No start date";
};
```

Code that sets `SelectedDate` directly does not pass through the typed-text rules: a value set in code is shown as it is,
so the view model must keep it inside `MinDate` and `MaxDate`. `FormattedValue` returns the text currently shown, which is
empty when there is no value.

### Limits and disabled days

`MinDate` and `MaxDate` bound the dates that can be picked. `DisabledDates` is a `Func<DateOnly, bool>` that returns
`true` for a day to block. The limits apply to the calendar and to typed dates. `IsDateAllowed(DateOnly date)` returns
the same answer in code, so a form can check a date before it sets the value.

A typed date that is out of range or disabled is rejected: the field shakes and returns to the last valid value.
The calendar also skips those days when the arrow keys move the focus.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.DatePickerLimitsAndDisabledDaysDemo">
    <arc:DatePicker x:Name="Due"
                    Label="Due date"
                    Description="Weekdays in the next eight weeks."
                    Culture="en-US"
                    ShowToday="True"
                    Width="280"
                    HorizontalAlignment="Left" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class DatePickerLimitsAndDisabledDaysDemo : UserControl
{
    public DatePickerLimitsAndDisabledDaysDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        var today = DateOnly.FromDateTime(DateTime.Today);
        Due.MinDate = today;
        Due.MaxDate = today.AddDays(56);
        Due.DisabledDates = d => d.DayOfWeek is DayOfWeek.Saturday or DayOfWeek.Sunday;
    }
}
```

Use the limits to express the business rule, not to hide a mistake. A due date that must follow the start date is
`MinDate="{Binding StartDate}"`; a week-day-only delivery is `DisabledDates`. A rule that depends on data the picker
cannot see, such as a closed period, belongs in the view model's validation, shown in `ErrorMessage`.

### Sizes

`Size` sets the field height: `Small` is 36, `Medium` is 44 (the Arc look) and `Large` is 50. A form uses one size for all
of its fields, so a `DatePicker` lines up with an `Input` or a `Select` in the same row.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.DatePickerSizesDemo">
    <StackPanel x:Name="Fields" Spacing="16">
        <arc:DatePicker Label="Small" Size="Small" Width="260" HorizontalAlignment="Left" />
        <arc:DatePicker Label="Medium" Width="260" HorizontalAlignment="Left" />
        <arc:DatePicker Label="Large" Size="Large" Width="260" HorizontalAlignment="Left" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class DatePickerSizesDemo : UserControl
{
    public DatePickerSizesDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        var today = DateOnly.FromDateTime(DateTime.Today);
        foreach (var picker in Fields.Children.OfType<DatePicker>())
        {
            picker.SelectedDate = today;
        }
    }
}
```

### Culture and display format

`Culture` controls the parsing, the calendar's month and weekday names, and the default display. When it is not set, the
current UI culture is used. The default display is the culture's long date without the weekday, with an abbreviated
month. In `en-US` a date shows as `Oct 20, 2026`; in `zh-CN` it shows as `2026年10月20日`.

`DisplayFormat` takes a .NET date pattern and replaces that default for the shown value. Use it when the business fixes a
format for every user, such as the ISO form in an export screen. The pattern does not change the calendar's names, and
the typed text is parsed with the same pattern first.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.DatePickerCulturesAndFormatsDemo">
    <StackPanel x:Name="Fields" Spacing="16">
        <arc:DatePicker Label="Deutsch"
                        Culture="de-DE"
                        FirstDayOfWeek="Monday"
                        Width="260"
                        HorizontalAlignment="Left" />
        <arc:DatePicker Label="中文"
                        Culture="zh-CN"
                        FirstDayOfWeek="Monday"
                        Width="260"
                        HorizontalAlignment="Left" />
        <arc:DatePicker Label="ISO format"
                        DisplayFormat="yyyy-MM-dd"
                        Width="260"
                        HorizontalAlignment="Left" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class DatePickerCulturesAndFormatsDemo : UserControl
{
    public DatePickerCulturesAndFormatsDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        var today = DateOnly.FromDateTime(DateTime.Today);
        foreach (var picker in Fields.Children.OfType<DatePicker>())
        {
            picker.SelectedDate = today;
        }
    }
}
```

Parsing tries three things in order: the display pattern, the culture's own date patterns, and then a lenient parse of
the text. That is why the person can type `10/21/2026` in `en-US` and `2026-10-21` in an ISO field. Override
`TryParseDate` in a subclass to accept an extra notation; the default is the behavior described here.

`FirstDayOfWeek` sets the first column of the popup's calendar. It defaults to `Sunday`; the German and Chinese demos
above use `Monday`.

### Error and disabled state

A non-empty `ErrorMessage` marks the field invalid. A disabled field is faded to half opacity and cannot be opened or
typed into.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.DatePickerInvalidAndDisabledDemo">
    <StackPanel x:Name="Fields" Spacing="16">
        <arc:DatePicker Label="Invoice date"
                        ErrorMessage="Pick a date before the due date."
                        Width="280"
                        HorizontalAlignment="Left" />
        <arc:DatePicker Label="Locked"
                        IsEnabled="False"
                        Width="280"
                        HorizontalAlignment="Left" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class DatePickerInvalidAndDisabledDemo : UserControl
{
    public DatePickerInvalidAndDisabledDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        var today = DateOnly.FromDateTime(DateTime.Today);
        foreach (var picker in Fields.Children.OfType<DatePicker>())
        {
            picker.SelectedDate = today;
        }
    }
}
```

Keep the error until the value changes. The copy belongs to the rule that failed, so write it as the fix: "Pick a date
before the due date." A disabled field should say why it is locked in its description, because the faded frame alone
does not explain the restriction.

### Validation

A `DatePicker` checks two things by itself: that typed text parses, and that the date is inside the limits. Everything
else is a business rule, and the form decides when to show it.

| Rule | When it is checked | Where it shows |
|---|---|---|
| The text parses as a date | When the person presses Enter or leaves the field | The field returns to the last valid value; the text is not kept |
| The date is inside `MinDate` and `MaxDate` | When the person presses Enter or leaves the field | The field shakes and returns to the last valid value |
| The date is not disabled | When the person presses Enter or leaves the field | The field shakes and returns to the last valid value |
| Required, or after another date | On submit, or when the related field changes | `ErrorMessage`, on the field the rule is about |
| A rule the server checks, such as a closed period | After the request | `ErrorMessage`; clear it when the value changes |

The rules that the picker checks itself are silent when they fail, because the field simply returns to its last valid
value. Show a message for every rule that the person must act on, so a silent revert is not the only feedback.

```csharp
public partial class InvoiceViewModel : ObservableValidator
{
    [ObservableProperty]
    [NotifyDataErrorInfo]
    [Required(ErrorMessage = "Pick an issue date.")]
    private DateOnly? _issueDate;

    [ObservableProperty]
    [NotifyDataErrorInfo]
    [Required(ErrorMessage = "Pick a due date.")]
    private DateOnly? _dueDate;

    [RelayCommand]
    private async Task SaveAsync()
    {
        ValidateAllProperties();
        if (HasErrors)
        {
            return;
        }
        await _invoices.SaveAsync(IssueDate!.Value, DueDate!.Value);
    }
}
```

### Binding to a view model

The view model owns the dates and the rules, and the field reflects them. `SelectedDate` is two-way, so the view model
receives a date the moment the person commits it, and `MinDate` is one-way, so the due date follows the issue date.

```xml
<StackPanel Width="280" Spacing="16">
    <arc:DatePicker Label="Issue date"
                    SelectedDate="{Binding IssueDate, Mode=TwoWay}" />
    <arc:DatePicker Label="Due date"
                    SelectedDate="{Binding DueDate, Mode=TwoWay}"
                    MinDate="{Binding IssueDate}"
                    ErrorMessage="{Binding DueDateError}" />
    <arc:Button Content="Save invoice" Command="{Binding SaveCommand}" IsDefault="True" />
</StackPanel>
```

Bind `ErrorMessage` to a string from the view model when the error comes from a rule the picker does not know, and clear
the string when the value changes. A validation error from a binding also shows in the field, so use one source for each
rule. The picker's `IsDropDownOpen` is two-way; set it to `False` from the view model to close the popup when the page
changes.

### Example: invoice dates

A billing form in a finance console. The issue date is set, the due date is limited to days on or after the issue date,
and the due date shows a message because it is earlier than the net 30 terms the account requires. The labels are nouns,
the descriptions state the rule, and the error names the fix. The popup is closed in the screenshot, so the scene shows
the field as the person sees it before they open the calendar.

![An invoice dates form with an issue date, a due date error and a save button](https://docs.tkcode.si/shots/Docs/Pickers/DatePicker/images/InvoiceDates.webp)

```xml
<Border Width="560"
        Padding="24"
        Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Surface}"
        BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource BorderSubtle}"
        BorderThickness="1"
        CornerRadius="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource RadiusPanel}">
    <StackPanel Spacing="20">
        <StackPanel Spacing="4">
            <TextBlock Text="Invoice INV-2026-0412"
                       FontSize="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TypeLG}"
                       FontWeight="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource WeightMedium}"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
            <TextBlock Text="Northwind Logistics, net 30 terms"
                       FontSize="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TypeSM}"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
        </StackPanel>
        <StackPanel Orientation="Horizontal" Spacing="16">
            <arc:DatePicker Label="Issue date"
                            Width="256"
                            SelectedDate="2026-10-21"
                            Description="The date the invoice is sent." />
            <arc:DatePicker Label="Due date"
                            Width="256"
                            SelectedDate="2026-10-30"
                            MinDate="2026-10-21"

```

The due date states the terms in its error rather than a generic "invalid date", so the person knows which date to
change. The two fields are the same width and share a row, so their labels and descriptions align. The customer
reference is an `Input` because it is an identifier, not a date.

### Content guidelines

- **Label**: a short noun phrase, sentence case, without a colon: "Issue date", "Due date", "Start date".
- **Placeholder**: keep the default "Select a date" for a form that has no other instruction. Change it only when the
  field is part of a group and the wording is clearer in context.
- **Description**: one sentence that says what the date controls, or how to enter it when that is not obvious: "Type a
  date or press Alt+Down to open the calendar."
- **Error**: name the rule and the fix: "Net 30 terms need a due date on Nov 20, 2026." Do not repeat the label.
- **Footer copy**: the popup's footer uses `ClearText`, `EmptyStatusText` and `SelectedStatusFormat`. Keep "Clear" as a
  verb, and make the status state the outcome, for example "Selected {0}".

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| Date | Issue date |
| Invalid date | Enter a date such as Oct 21, 2026. |
| Please enter a due date: | Pick a due date. |
| Wrong format | Use a date on or after Oct 21, 2026. |
| Clear date | Clear |

### Best practices

**Do**

- Set `Culture` to the user's locale, or to the company's locale for a back-office screen, so the month names and the
  parsing agree with what the person expects.
- Keep one `Size` per form, and align the `DatePicker` with its neighbors in the same row.
- Limit a dependent date with `MinDate` bound to the earlier date, so the calendar never offers a date the form would
  refuse.
- Show a message for every rule the person must act on. A rejected typed date reverts silently after a shake; a message
  says why.
- Use `DisplayFormat` only when a format is part of the contract, such as an export or a legal document, and leave the
  culture's default in place everywhere else.

**Avoid**

- Using a `DatePicker` for a time of day or a deadline with an hour. The value has no time part, so the hour is lost.
- Setting `SelectedDate` in code to a date outside `MinDate`, `MaxDate` or `DisabledDates`. Typed values are checked, but
  values set in code are not, so the field would show a date that the rules forbid.
- Putting the calendar popup and a second, visible `Calendar` for the same value on one page. Two views of one date
  invite the person to edit the wrong one.
- Relying on the Alt+Down shortcut alone. The description should say that the calendar opens, because a person who
  does not know the key never finds the popup.
- Swapping error messages on every keystroke. Errors are checked when the value is committed, so a message that changes
  while typing reads as noise.

### Common questions

**Why does the field go back to the old date when I type an invalid one?** A typed value is committed on Enter or when
the field loses focus. If it does not parse, or it is outside the limits or disabled, the value is refused and the field
shows the last valid date. Add an `ErrorMessage` if the person needs to know why.

**How do I clear the value from code?** Set `SelectedDate` to `null`. The field shows the placeholder, and the change is
raised through `SelectedDateChanged` with a `null` new date. The popup's Clear button does the same thing for a person.

**Does the popup close after a pick?** Yes. It closes about 300 ms after the pick, so the value and the footer have time
to confirm it. With reduced or off motion, it closes at once. Clear also closes the popup at once.

**How do I open the popup from code or close it when the page changes?** Set `IsDropDownOpen` to `True` or `False`. Escape
and Alt+Up close the popup from the keyboard; Tab out of the field closes it and commits the typed text.

**How do I show the date in a different format than the one I type?** Set `DisplayFormat` for the shown value. Typing
accepts the display pattern first, then the culture's patterns, so a person can type the form they already know.

## API reference

### DatePicker

Arc date field: type a date (parsed with `Culture`) or open the calendar popup (click, Alt+Down or ArrowDown) and pick a day. The shown date rolls part by part in time's direction (a later date rises from below, an earlier one drops from above; parts after a wider or narrower part slide along), the picked day's disc glides in the calendar and the footer confirms it before the popup returns to the field. Escape closes and keeps focus in the field; `MinDate`, `MaxDate` and `DisabledDates` reach the calendar and also reject typed dates. Label, description, error and size come from the field foundation.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SelectedDate` | `DateOnly?` | `null` | The picked date (two-way). Null shows the placeholder. |
| `IsDropDownOpen` | `bool` | `false` | Whether the calendar popup is open (two-way). |
| `MinDate` | `DateOnly?` | `null` | Earliest selectable date. |
| `MaxDate` | `DateOnly?` | `null` | Latest selectable date. |
| `DisabledDates` | `Func<DateOnly, bool>?` | `null` | Extra disabled days (weekends, booked dates...), passed to the calendar. |
| `Culture` | `CultureInfo?` | `null` | Culture for formatting, parsing and the calendar (null = current UI culture). |
| `DisplayFormat` | `string?` | `null` | .NET date pattern of the shown value. Null uses the culture's long date without the weekday and with the abbreviated month (en-US "Oct 20, 2026", Arc's default `{ month: "short", day: "numeric", year: "numeric" }`). |
| `ShowToday` | `bool` | `false` | Adds a Today button to the calendar header. |
| `FirstDayOfWeek` | `DayOfWeek` | `Sunday` | First column of the calendar. |
| `ClearText` | `string` | `"Clear"` | Footer button that clears the value (Arc: "Clear"). |
| `EmptyStatusText` | `string` | `"Choose a day"` | Footer status without a value (Arc: "Choose a day"). |
| `SelectedStatusFormat` | `string` | `"Selected {0}"` | Footer status with a value; {0} is the formatted date (Arc: "Selected {0}"). |
| `Label` | `string?` | `null` | The visible label above the frame; also the accessible name. |
| `Description` | `string?` | `null` | Helper copy under the frame (rewrites changed words in place; counts roll). |
| `ErrorMessage` | `string?` | `null` | Error copy under the frame; non-empty makes the field invalid. |
| `IsInvalid` | `bool` | `false` | Invalid state; always true while an error is shown. |
| `IsLabelVisible` | `bool` | `true` | When false the label is hidden visually but still names the field. |
| `Size` | `ControlSize` | `Medium` | Frame height: Small 36, Medium 44 (default), Large 50. |
| `Prefix` | `object?` | `null` | Content before the text (icon, unit, currency). |
| `Suffix` | `object?` | `null` | Content after the text (unit, action button). |
| `Placeholder` | `string?` | `"Select a date"` | Hint shown while the field is empty (same as `PlaceholderText`). |
| `EffectiveErrorMessage` | `string?` | – | *Read-only.* The error actually shown: `ErrorMessage`, else the binding's validation message. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `SelectedDateChanged` | `DatePickerSelectedDateChangedEventArgs` | Raised when `SelectedDate` changes. |

Pseudo-classes: `:open`, `:invalid`

Derives from `TextBox`: every member of `TextBox` works as well.

## Accessibility

- `Label` names the field and is linked to the trigger. `Description` is the help text; the trigger's help text includes
  the formatted value and then the description.
- The trigger exposes its expanded state, so a screen reader announces whether the calendar is open. The popup is named
  after the label, for example "Start date calendar".
- Enter, Space and ArrowDown open the calendar and move focus to the selected day, or to today when nothing is selected.
  Inside the calendar the keys work as they do in `Calendar`.
- Escape closes the calendar and returns focus to the field. Tab out of the calendar, or a pointer press outside it,
  also closes it.
- The focus ring is shown for keyboard focus only. A pointer press that opens the calendar does not show it, and the
  caret stays in the text.
- An invalid or refused entry is not kept: the field returns to the last valid value, and the error message, if the form
  sets one, stays in the description row for the person to read.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| Type, then `Enter` | Commit the typed date; an invalid or disabled date is refused and the field returns to the last valid value |
| `Enter` with no typed change | Open the calendar, or close it when it is open |
| `Alt` + `Down`, or `Down` | Open the calendar and move focus to its tab stop day (or into it when it is already open) |
| `Tab` from the field while open | Commit the typed text and move focus into the calendar |
| `Escape` with a pending typed change | Discard the typed change and show the last valid date |
| `Escape` when the calendar is open | Close the calendar and return focus to the field |
| `Alt` + `Up` in the calendar | Close the calendar and return focus to the field |
| `Tab` out of the calendar | Close the calendar and commit any typed text |

Keys pressed inside the calendar never edit the text, so an arrow key or Backspace on a selected day does not change the
typed value. Inside the calendar, the grid keys work as documented on the `Calendar` page.

## Motion

- Changed parts of the date roll in the direction of time: a later date rises and an earlier date falls. Only the
  parts that change move.
- After a date is picked, the disc slides into place and the popup closes a moment later.
- The popup opens from the calendar icon with a short fade, and closes with a shorter fade.
- Reduced motion swaps the values with a fade and closes the popup at once after a pick. Off jumps to the end state.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| A part of the date changes | Only the changed parts roll; a later date rises and an earlier one falls | The value fades to the new text | Immediate |
| A width change in one part | Later parts slide along the same curve to make room | The value fades to the new text | Immediate |
| The popup opens | Settles 8 px into place from above and scales up from 95% on a quick spring, while it fades in | Fades in | Immediate |
| The popup closes | Lifts 6 px, scales to 97% and fades out in a short tween | Fades out | Immediate |
| The description while the popup is open | Fades out quickly and returns when the popup closes | Fades out quickly | Immediate |
| The footer status after a pick | Rises into place with a soft blur | Fades in | Immediate |
| The chevron on the calendar button | Turns 180 degrees with a spring | Turns at once | Immediate |

## Related

- `Calendar` for a month view that stays on the page.
- `DateRangePicker` for a start and end date with presets.
- `TimePicker` for the time of day, to pair with a date.
- `Field` and `FieldFrame` give any editor or trigger the same label, frame and message rows.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `Calendar` | The month is the content, and the person compares several days on the page |
| `DateRangePicker` | The person picks a start and an end, often with presets such as "Last 30 days" |
| `TimePicker` | The value is a time of day, or the date needs a time as well |
| `Select` / `SegmentedControl` | The choice is one of a few named periods rather than a date |
| `Input` | The text is an identifier or prose, not a date that must be parsed |
