# Date range picker

> A range picker that grows from its trigger into two months with presets and a stretching range highlight.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/date-range-picker

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.DateRangePickerReportDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12" HorizontalAlignment="Center">
        <arc:DateRangePicker x:Name="Picker"
                             Culture="en-US"
                             SelectedRangeChanged="OnApplied" />
        <TextBlock x:Name="Status"
                   HorizontalAlignment="Center"
                   FontSize="14"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class DateRangePickerReportDemo : UserControl
{
    public DateRangePickerReportDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        var today = DateOnly.FromDateTime(DateTime.Today);
        Picker.SelectedRange = new DateRange(today.AddDays(-6), today);
        ShowDays(Picker.SelectedRange);
    }

    // Raised on Apply only: the selection is a draft until then.
    private void OnApplied(object? sender, DateRangePickerSelectedRangeChangedEventArgs e) => ShowDays(e.NewRange);

    private void ShowDays(DateRange? range)
        => Status.Text = range is { } days ? $"{days.Days} days selected" : "No range";
}
```

## When to use

`DateRangePicker` chooses a span of whole days as one value: a start day and an end day. It sits in a filter bar, a
booking form or a toolbar. The closed trigger shows the applied range as one short line, and a click opens a panel
with a preset rail and one or two months, so people can take a common period in one click or pick an exact span.

- **Report filters in an analytics dashboard**: a revenue or conversion report with presets such as Last 7 days,
  Last 30 days and Year to date. The preset rail covers the common periods, and the calendar covers the rest.
- **Stays and leave requests**: a hotel booking or a leave request in an HR portal needs a check-in and a check-out
  day. Set `MinDate` to today so past nights cannot be chosen, and `MaxDate` to the last day that can be booked.
- **Billing periods and invoice exports**: an admin console that exports invoices for a period such as
  `Oct 1 – 31, 2026`. The value changes only on Apply, so a half-picked span never reaches the export query.
- **Compact toolbars and side panels**: a log viewer or an incident timeline whose filter bar shows the window as
  one label until it is changed. `MonthCount="One"` keeps the panel narrow when the toolbar sits in a side column.

## When not to use

- **One day, such as a due date or a birth date**: use `DatePicker`. It holds a single day and has no preset rail
  or range highlight.
- **A month that stays on the page**: use `Calendar` when people scan availability or compare days across a month.
  The range picker only opens on demand, so nothing else on the page is visible while it is open.
- **A time of day, such as a shift start or a meeting slot**: use `TimePicker` for each time. `DateRange` holds
  `DateOnly` ends, so a range picker never carries a time.
- **Only a fixed list of named periods with no custom span**: use `Select`. The preset rail is part of this control;
  a plain list is simpler when the custom calendar is never used.
- **Free typing of a date range**: the trigger has no text entry, so people cannot type `10/05 - 10/09`. If the
  product needs typed dates, give the form two `DatePicker` fields and validate that the end follows the start.

## Usage

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:DateRangePicker Label="Date range" />
</UserControl>
```

```csharp
var today = DateOnly.FromDateTime(DateTime.Today);
picker.SelectedRange = new DateRange(today.AddDays(-6), today);
```

`DateRangePicker` derives from Avalonia's `TemplatedControl`, so its look comes from a ControlTheme and its panel is
a popup that the control owns. It is not a text box and it is not Avalonia's date picker: nothing is typed into the
trigger, so there is no caret, no IME and no date parsing. The field adds the label, the description and the error
row from the same `Field` foundation as the other form controls, and the panel is drawn with the Arc month grid. A
`DateRange` is a record struct of two `DateOnly` values, both ends included, so `Days` counts the two ends too.

### Anatomy

1. **Label** (`Label`, `IsLabelVisible`): the accessible name of the trigger and the panel. The label is hidden by
   default; set `IsLabelVisible="True"` to show it above the trigger in the field label style.
2. **Trigger** (the template part named by `DateRangePicker.TriggerPart`): 44 px tall (the Medium control height), 18 px corner radius, a 1 px border on the
   raised surface with the resting shadow. Padding is 14 px before the content and 12 px after it, with 10 px
   between the parts. Hover fills the trigger with a 3% tint of the foreground and strengthens the border to the
   strong border color.
3. **Calendar icon**: 16 px, in the secondary text color.
4. **Value** (the template part named by `DateRangePicker.ValuePart`): the applied range in medium weight, for example `Oct 5 – 9, 2026`. With no range it
   shows `Placeholder` in the secondary text color. Changed words roll in place.
5. **Chevron**: 16 px, in the muted text color, at the end of the trigger.
6. **Description** (`Description`) and **error row** (`ErrorMessage`): help and error copy under the trigger, from
   the field foundation. A non-empty `ErrorMessage` is the error copy; the control has no separate invalid flag.
7. **Panel** (when open): an inset of 10 px (8 px in the compact layout). Two-month layout: a 148 px preset rail (9.25
   rem) with a 10 px gap before the months. Compact layout: the presets become a horizontal row under a rule.
8. **Month navigation**: two 32 px round buttons, previous and next. A button is disabled when the months beyond it
   would fall outside `MinDate` or `MaxDate`; the disabled state is 35% opacity.
9. **Footer**: a 1 px rule above a row with the summary on the left (the day count, such as `12 days`, or `Pick an
   end date` after the first click) and Cancel and Apply on the right. Both buttons are 36 px tall. Apply is at least
   76 px wide and is disabled while there is no draft.

### Layout: one or two months

`MonthCount` chooses the panel. `Auto` (the default) shows two months beside the preset rail when the boundary is at
least 712 px wide, and one month under a horizontally scrolling preset row otherwise. `One` always uses the compact
panel, and `Two` always shows two months beside the rail.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.DateRangePickerOneMonthDemo">
    <arc:DateRangePicker MonthCount="One" Culture="en-US" />
</UserControl>
```

Use `Auto` in pages and dialogs that stretch with the window, so the panel shows the most context it can. When the
window is resized across the 712 px boundary, the panel changes between one and two months and the surface springs
to the new shape. Use `One` in narrow side columns and mobile-width layouts where a second month would be cut off.
Use `Two` only when the page is known to be wide enough, because `Two` does not fall back to the compact panel.

The panel stays inside `Boundary`, which defaults to the window. When the trigger sits near the bottom of a
scrolling page, the page scrolls so that the panel is visible, and the panel still opens from the trigger.

### Presets

`Presets` replaces the default list of eight presets. A preset is a label and a function that returns a `DateRange`
from today's date. The function receives the viewer's local today, so a preset such as Last 7 days moves with the
calendar without any code in the page. `DateRangePresets.Default` holds the default list, so a custom list can start
from it and add its own entries.

| Preset | Range |
|---|---|
| Today | Today to today |
| Yesterday | Yesterday to yesterday |
| Last 7 days | Six days before today to today |
| Last 30 days | Twenty-nine days before today to today |
| This month | The first day of this month to today |
| Last month | The whole previous calendar month |
| This quarter | The first day of the current quarter to today |
| Year to date | January 1 to today |

```csharp
picker.Presets =
[
    new DateRangePreset("Last 7 days", t => new DateRange(t.AddDays(-6), t)),
    new DateRangePreset("Next 14 days", t => new DateRange(t, t.AddDays(13))),
    new DateRangePreset("Last quarter", t => new DateRange(t.AddMonths(-3), t.AddDays(-1))),
];
```

A preset is highlighted when the draft equals its range, so the rail shows the current choice when the person picks
a preset or the same days by hand. The highlight glides from one preset to the next. Keep the list to about six
entries: the rail is 32 px per row, and in the compact layout the row scrolls sideways.

### Limits and week start

`MinDate` and `MaxDate` disable the days outside the range and the month buttons that would lead beyond it. The
keyboard also stops at the limits: arrow keys and page keys cannot move the focus onto a disabled day. `FirstDayOfWeek`
sets the first column of the grid; it is Sunday by default and can be Monday.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.DateRangePickerBookingDemo">
    <arc:DateRangePicker x:Name="Picker"
                         Label="Stay"
                         IsLabelVisible="True"
                         Description="Check-in from today, up to six months ahead."
                         Culture="en-US"
                         FirstDayOfWeek="Monday" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class DateRangePickerBookingDemo : UserControl
{
    public DateRangePickerBookingDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        var today = DateOnly.FromDateTime(DateTime.Today);
        Picker.MinDate = today;
        Picker.MaxDate = today.AddMonths(6);
        Picker.Presets =
        [
            new DateRangePreset("This weekend", WeekendFrom),
            new DateRangePreset("Next week", t => new DateRange(t.AddDays(7 - (int)t.DayOfWeek + 1), t.AddDays(7 - (int)t.DayOfWeek + 7))),
            new DateRangePreset("Two weeks", t => new DateRange(t, t.AddDays(13)))
        ];
    }

    private static DateRange WeekendFrom(DateOnly today)
    {
        var saturday = today.AddDays(((int)DayOfWeek.Saturday - (int)today.DayOfWeek + 7) % 7);
        return new DateRange(saturday, saturday.AddDays(1));
    }
}
```

Set the limits in the view model when they come from a business rule, such as a booking window of six months, and
keep the presets to ranges that fit inside it. A preset that reaches past `MaxDate` is not clipped for you, so
compute the preset from the same limit when a range must stay inside the window.

### Culture

`Culture` sets the month titles, the weekday heads, the range label and the day count. When it is null, the
current UI culture is used. The text the control shows is in properties, so a localized page sets them with the
same translation work as the rest of the form.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.DateRangePickerCultureDemo">
    <arc:DateRangePicker Culture="zh-CN" FirstDayOfWeek="Monday" Placeholder="选择日期" />
</UserControl>
```

| Property | Default | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| `Placeholder` | `Select dates` | The trigger when no range is applied |
| `ApplyText` / `CancelText` | `Apply` / `Cancel` | The footer buttons |
| `NoDatesText` | `No dates` | The trigger and the summary when the draft is empty |
| `PickEndText` | `Pick an end date` | The summary after the first click, before the end is chosen |
| `DayCountFormat` | `{0} day` | The count for one day; the one-day form is used only for 1 |
| `DaysCountFormat` | `{0} days` | The count for two or more days; `{0}` is the number |
| `PreviousMonthLabel` / `NextMonthLabel` | `Previous month` / `Next month` | The accessible names of the navigation buttons |

Set both count formats for each language, because the control picks the one-day form only when the count is 1.
`FirstDayOfWeek` is separate from `Culture`: a Monday week start is a business choice, so the demo sets it
explicitly instead of relying on the culture.

### Driving it from code

`SelectedRange` is the value and `IsDropDownOpen` opens or closes the panel. Setting `SelectedRange` while the
panel is closed updates the trigger at once. `FormattedValue` returns the text the trigger shows, which is the
placeholder when no range is applied, so a status line or an export label can reuse it.

```csharp
picker.SelectedRangeChanged += (_, e) =>
{
    status.Text = e.NewRange is { } range ? $"{range.Days} days" : "No range";
};
```

The selection is a draft until Apply is pressed. `SelectedRangeChanged` is raised only on Apply, and its event args
carry `OldRange` and `NewRange`. Cancel, Escape and a press outside the panel do not raise it.

### Binding to a view model

In an MVVM app the view model owns the range and the page binds it two ways. With CommunityToolkit.Mvvm:

```csharp
public partial class ReportFilterViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    private readonly IReportService _reports;

    public ReportFilterViewModel(IReportService reports)
    {
        _reports = reports;
        _period = new DateRange(new DateOnly(2026, 10, 1), new DateOnly(2026, 10, 21));
    }

    [ObservableProperty]
    private DateRange? _period;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private string? _periodError;

    partial void OnPeriodChanged(DateRange? value)
    {
        PeriodError = value is { Days: > 90 } ? "Choose 90 days or fewer." : null;
    }

    [RelayCommand]
    private Task RunReportAsync()
    {
        if (Period is not { } range || PeriodError is not null)
        {
            return Task.CompletedTask;
        }
        return _reports.LoadAsync(range.Start, range.End);
    }
}
```

```xml
<StackPanel Spacing="16" Width="360">
    <arc:DateRangePicker Label="Report period"
                         SelectedRange="{Binding Period, Mode=TwoWay}"
                         ErrorMessage="{Binding PeriodError}" />
    <arc:Button Content="Run report" Command="{Binding RunReportCommand}" />
</StackPanel>
```

`SelectedRange` is two-way. It is written only when the person presses Apply, so `Period` never holds a draft. The
picker has no command of its own: the form's button runs the report, and `SelectedRangeChanged` is needed only when
the page must react to every Apply, such as updating a status line. Compiled bindings need `x:DataType` on the view;
the example leaves it out for brevity.

### Validation

The picker enforces the limits it knows: `MinDate`, `MaxDate` and the disabled days. Rules about the span belong to
the view model, and the result goes to `ErrorMessage`.

| Rule | When to check | Where it shows |
|---|---|---|
| Days outside `MinDate` or `MaxDate` | While picking (the days are disabled) | Nothing: the day cannot be chosen |
| Span longer than the report allows | On Apply, through the `Period` change | `ErrorMessage` under the trigger |
| Period required by the form | On submit | `ErrorMessage`; move focus to the picker |
| Server rejects the period | After the request | `ErrorMessage`; clear it when `Period` changes |

Apply keeps the panel's draft out of the view model, so the rule runs on the committed value. Clear the error when the
person applies a new range; the `OnPeriodChanged` handler above does that because every committed change passes
through it.

### Focus and dismissal

- **Opening**: Enter or Space on the trigger opens the panel and focuses the start of the committed range. With no
  range, focus starts on today.
- **Applying**: Apply commits the draft, closes the panel and returns focus to the trigger. Apply is enabled when a
  draft exists.
- **Cancelling**: Cancel, Escape or a press outside the panel discard the draft. Cancel and Escape return focus to the
  trigger; a press outside does not move focus, because the person has already moved it.
- **Half-picked ranges**: after the first click, Apply commits a one-day range on the start day. The summary says
  `Pick an end date` at that point, so people see the choice before they apply it.
- **Tabbing out**: moving focus out of the panel closes it and discards the draft, so the panel never stays open
  behind other controls.

### Example: hotel stay in a booking form

A booking form for a hotel group. The stay is a single field, the check-in window is limited to the next six months,
and the description tells people what the dates control. The form reads the stay only after Apply, so the price
quote always matches the committed dates.

```xml
<StackPanel Width="560" Spacing="20">
    <arc:DateRangePicker Label="Stay"
                         IsLabelVisible="True"
                         Description="Check-in from today, up to six months ahead."
                         Culture="en-US"
                         FirstDayOfWeek="Monday"
                         Placeholder="Choose check-in and check-out" />
    <arc:Input Label="Guest name" Placeholder="As shown on the passport" />
    <arc:Button Content="Continue to payment" IsDefault="True" />
</StackPanel>
```

The `MinDate` and `MaxDate` limits are set in code from the same today the view model uses, so the booking window
and the disabled days never disagree with the server's rules.

### Content guidelines

Name the field after the business value: `Report period`, Stay, `Billing period`. Keep preset labels short and in
sentence case. Write the button as a verb and an object, and keep the day counts in the formats the product uses.

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| `Date` (for a range) | `Report period`, Stay, `Billing period` |
| `Last 7 Days` | `Last 7 days` |
| `OK` | `Apply` (or `Apply filter` when the button filters a list) |
| `Pick end date` | `Pick an end date` (the default text) |
| `1 days` | Set `DayCountFormat` for one day and `DaysCountFormat` for more |
| `Select a date range from the calendar below` | `Select dates` |

Keep the placeholder short so that it fits beside the calendar icon and the chevron in a 44 px trigger.

### Best practices

**Do**

- Set `Label` to the business value and show it with `IsLabelVisible="True"` in a form. A hidden label still names the
  field for assistive technology, but people scanning a form need the visible name.
- Bind `SelectedRange` two ways and read the committed value only. A draft exists only while the panel is open, so
  the rest of the page never sees a half-picked range.
- Put the presets your reports or bookings use, and keep the list short. People take a preset faster than they
  scroll a calendar.
- Set `MinDate` and `MaxDate` from the business rule. Disabled days explain the limit without a message.
- Use `MonthCount="One"` in narrow columns, where a second month would be cut off.

**Avoid**

- Using the picker for one date. The range highlight and the presets add steps that a single date does not need.
- Expecting `SelectedRange` to follow the keyboard or the pointer while the panel is open. The value changes on
  Apply only, so code that reacts to each day picked will never run; subscribe to `SelectedRangeChanged` instead.
- Relying on the default English texts in a localized product. Set `Placeholder`, `ApplyText`, `CancelText` and both
  count formats together so that the trigger and the footer use the same language.
- Using a range picker inside a scrolling list of many rows. Each row opens its own panel, which is hard to scan;
  move the filter to the header of the list.

### Common questions

**Why does the trigger still show the old range after I picked new days?** The picks are a draft until Apply. Press
Apply to commit them; Cancel, Escape or a press outside discards them and keeps the previous `SelectedRange`.

**Can I open the panel from code?** Yes. Set `IsDropDownOpen` to `True`. The panel opens with focus on the committed
start, as it does for the keyboard. Set it back to `False` to close the panel without applying the draft.

**What happens when the second day is before the first?** The picker orders the two days, so the range runs from the
earlier day to the later day. The same is true in code: `DateRange.Ordered(a, b)` returns the range in order.

**Does a range always have an end?** A `DateRange` always has two days, and both ends are included. If the person
applies after picking only a start day, the range is that single day. To require two days, check
`range.Days > 1` in the view model.

**How do I count the nights in a stay?** `Days` counts both ends, so a stay from March 3 to March 5 has three days and
two nights. Compute the nights as `range.Days - 1` for a booking that charges per night.

## API reference

### DateRangePicker

Arc date range picker: a compact trigger whose surface grows into the panel it opens (P9) — two months beside a preset rail, or one month under a scrolling preset row when the boundary is narrower than 712px. The range highlight stretches across each week as you hover or move with the keyboard, its solid ends glide between days, months slide in the direction you travel, the preset highlight glides between presets, and on Apply the formatted label flies back into the trigger as the surface shrinks around it (P8). Picking is a draft: only Apply commits (`SelectedRangeChanged`); Cancel, Escape or a press outside discard it.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SelectedRange` | `DateRange?` | `null` | The applied range (two-way). Null shows the placeholder. |
| `IsDropDownOpen` | `bool` | `false` | Whether the panel is open (two-way). |
| `Label` | `string?` | `"Date range"` | Accessible name of the trigger and the panel (Arc: "Date range"); shown above when `IsLabelVisible`. |
| `IsLabelVisible` | `bool` | `false` | Arc names the trigger with its label but does not show it; set true for a visible field label. |
| `Description` | `string?` | `null` | Helper copy under the trigger. |
| `ErrorMessage` | `string?` | `null` | Error copy under the trigger. |
| `Placeholder` | `string` | `"Select dates"` | Shown while no range is applied (Arc: "Select dates"). |
| `Presets` | `IReadOnlyList<DateRangePreset>?` | `null` | The preset rail (null = Arc's eight defaults, `Default`). |
| `MinDate` | `DateOnly?` | `null` | Earliest selectable day. |
| `MaxDate` | `DateOnly?` | `null` | Latest selectable day. |
| `FirstDayOfWeek` | `DayOfWeek` | `Sunday` | First column of the months (Arc's weekStartsOn: Sunday or Monday). |
| `Culture` | `CultureInfo?` | `null` | Culture for month titles, weekday heads and the range label. |
| `MonthCount` | `DateRangePickerMonths` | `Auto` | One or two months; Auto picks two when the boundary is at least 712px wide. |
| `Boundary` | `Control?` | `null` | The element the panel stays inside (null = the window). |
| `ApplyText` | `string` | `"Apply"` | Label of the button that applies the picked range (default Apply). |
| `CancelText` | `string` | `"Cancel"` | Label of the cancel button in the panel (default Cancel). |
| `NoDatesText` | `string` | `"No dates"` | Trigger text when no range is selected (default No dates). |
| `PickEndText` | `string` | `"Pick an end date"` | Readout while the hovered date is the start date and the end is still to be picked (default Pick an end date). |
| `DayCountFormat` | `string` | `"{0} day"` | Day count; {0} is the number (Arc: "1 day" / "12 days"). |
| `DaysCountFormat` | `string` | `"{0} days"` | Day count for two or more days; {0} is the number (default "{0} days"). |
| `PreviousMonthLabel` | `string` | `"Previous month"` | Accessible name of the previous-month button (default Previous month). |
| `NextMonthLabel` | `string` | `"Next month"` | Accessible name of the next-month button (default Next month). |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `SelectedRangeChanged` | `DateRangePickerSelectedRangeChangedEventArgs` | Raised when a range is applied. |

Pseudo-classes: `:open`, `:empty`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

### DateRange

An inclusive range of whole days.

Derives from `ValueType`: every member of `ValueType` works as well.

| Companion type | Member | Summary |
|---|---|---|
| `DateRangePreset` | `DateRangePreset(string label, Func<DateOnly, DateRange> range)` | Creates a preset from a label and a function of today |
| `DateRangePreset` | `Label` | Button text, such as `Last 7 days` |
| `DateRangePreset` | `Range` | The range for a given today |
| `DateRangePresets` | `Default` | Arc's eight presets, from Today to Year to date |

## Accessibility

- The trigger exposes its expanded state, and its name includes the current range. `Label` is the field name.
- Each month is a grid named after its title. The days in the range are exposed as selected, and today is marked.
  Each day is named with its long date.
- Enter and Space on a day choose the start and then the end. After a start is chosen, the arrow keys extend the
  range preview.
- The preset list moves with ArrowUp and ArrowDown. In the compact layout, the preset row moves with ArrowLeft and
  ArrowRight.
- Cancel, Escape and a pointer press outside discard the draft and return the focus to the trigger. Apply commits
  it and announces the start, the range and the number of days through a polite live region.
- The navigation buttons are named by `PreviousMonthLabel` and `NextMonthLabel`, so set them in the page language.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Enter` / `Space` on the trigger | Opens the panel and focuses the start of the committed range, or today |
| `Enter` / `Space` on a day | First press chooses the start; second press chooses the end and makes the draft |
| `Left` / `Right` | Moves the focus one day; with a start chosen, the preview extends to the day |
| `Up` / `Down` | Moves the focus one week |
| `Home` / `End` | Moves to the first or last day of the focused week, which follows `FirstDayOfWeek` |
| `PageUp` / `PageDown` | Moves the focus one month; with `Shift`, one year |
| `Up` / `Down` on a preset (`Left` / `Right` in the compact layout) | Moves between presets |
| `Enter` / `Space` on a preset, Cancel or Apply | Activates the focused button |
| `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` | Moves through the panel; leaving the panel closes it and discards the draft |
| `Escape` | Closes the panel, discards the draft and returns focus to the trigger |

Keyboard focus never lands on a disabled day: the arrow and page keys stop at `MinDate` and `MaxDate`.

## Motion

- The trigger surface grows into the panel, and its corners and size change together. Apply shrinks it back to the
  trigger, and the range label flies back into place.
- The range highlight stretches from day to day, and the end caps glide to their new days. The active preset glides
  between presets.
- Months slide in the direction of travel and fade out behind them. The label words roll in the direction of time.
- Reduced motion jumps the surface size and drops the shared element and the slides. Content fades for 0.08 to
  0.12 seconds. Off jumps to the end state.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| The panel opens | The trigger grows into the panel on a spring, 0.48 s | The size jumps; content fades in over 0.08 to 0.12 s | Immediate |
| The panel closes after Apply | The panel shrinks back to the trigger in 0.38 s and the label flies home | The size jumps; the summary fades | Immediate |
| The months change | The new months slide in from the direction of travel, 0.4 s | Content cross-fades over 0.08 to 0.12 s | Immediate |
| The trigger value changes | The words roll in the direction of time | Content cross-fades over 0.08 to 0.12 s | Immediate |

## Related

- `DatePicker` for one date in a form field.
- `Calendar` for a month that stays on the page.
- `TimePicker` for a time of day, when a date range needs times.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `DatePicker` | The value is one day, such as a due date or a birth date |
| `Calendar` | The month must stay visible for scanning, such as availability |
| `TimePicker` | The value is a time of day, such as a shift start |
| `Select` | The choices are a short fixed list of named periods, with no custom span |
| `Field` + `FieldFrame` | You build your own trigger that should share the label and message rows |

# Time picker

> Choose a time with sensible keyboard behavior.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/time-picker

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.TimePickerTimeFieldDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12">
        <arc:TimePicker Label="Meeting time"
                        Description="Times every 15 minutes, shown on the clock of your locale."
                        Culture="en-US"
                        Width="240"
                        HorizontalAlignment="Left"
                        SelectedTimeChanged="OnSelectedTimeChanged" />
        <TextBlock x:Name="Status"
                   Text="SelectedTime: 09:00"
                   FontSize="13"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class TimePickerTimeFieldDemo : UserControl
{
    public TimePickerTimeFieldDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
    }

    private void OnSelectedTimeChanged(object? sender, TimePickerSelectedTimeChangedEventArgs e)
        => Status.Text = $"SelectedTime: {(e.NewTime is { } time ? time.ToString("HH:mm") : "none")}";
}
```

## When to use

`TimePicker` chooses one time of day from an evenly spaced list. The list is generated every few minutes (15 by
default), so a time is always one step away from its neighbors. It sits in forms where the time is a value of its
own: a meeting slot, a reminder, a shift start, a pickup window. The value is a `TimeOnly`, and the clock shows it in
the format of the person's culture.

- **Meeting and appointment slots**: a calendar invite or a clinic booking where the times are fixed steps, such as
  every 15 minutes between 8:00 and 18:00. The list offers only the starts the grid supports, so people choose a
  time the booking system accepts.
- **Reminders and scheduled jobs**: a "send the weekly digest at" setting in an admin console. The value is a time of
  day with no date, and the picker shows it on the clock the person reads.
- **Shift and availability editors**: a staffing tool where a shift starts at 06:30 and ends at 14:30. Pair two
  pickers with `MinuteStep="30"` and validate that the end follows the start.
- **Date and time forms**: a delivery window or an event start that combines a `DatePicker` for the day with a
  `TimePicker` for the time. The two values are stored separately and combined in code.

## When not to use

- **A short list of named times, such as Morning or Evening**: use `Select`. A list of names does not need a scrolling
  list of times, and "Morning" has no single `TimeOnly` value.
- **A date**: use `DatePicker`, or `Calendar` when the month must stay visible on the page.
- **A date range**: use `DateRangePicker`. A range of whole days has no time of day and no step list.
- **Free typing of a time that must be exact to the second**: the picker is a list of steps. Use `Input` with a
  validation rule when people must type seconds or times between steps, and parse the text in the view model.
- **A duration, such as a 90 minute meeting or a 2 hour timer**: use `NumberField` for the number of minutes. A
  duration is not a time of day, and the list would suggest a clock that does not apply.

## Usage

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:TimePicker Label="Meeting time"
                    Description="Times every 15 minutes."
                    SelectedTime="{Binding MeetingTime, Mode=TwoWay}" />
</UserControl>
```

`TimePicker` derives from Avalonia's `TemplatedControl` and implements the Arc picker automation. The trigger is a
`FieldFrame` inside a `Field`, so the label, the description and the error row come from the same foundation as the
input and the date pickers. The list is a drawn panel in a popup that the control owns. It draws only the rows that
are visible, so even a one minute step (1440 options) does not create 1440 controls. Because the control is a list, it
does not parse typed text: the value only changes when a row is chosen or when code sets `SelectedTime`.

### Anatomy

1. **Label** (`Label`): above the trigger, in the field label style. It is also the accessible name of the field.
   With `IsLabelVisible="False"` the label is hidden and still names the field.
2. **Trigger frame** (the template part named by `TimePicker.FramePart`): a 1 px border on the field surface. Its height follows `Size`: 36 px for `Small`,
   44 px for `Medium` (the default) and 50 px for `Large`. Hover, press and open change the border to the strong
   border color and the background to the muted surface; an invalid field shows the danger border.
3. **Clock icon**: 16 px, in the muted text color, with a 9 px gap before the value.
4. **Value** (the template part named by `TimePicker.ValuePart`): the time in 14 px text with a 19.6 px line height (14 px × 1.4). `Large` uses the base
   type size. With no time it shows `Placeholder` in the muted text color.
5. **Chevron**: 16 px, in the muted text color. It turns 180 degrees while the list is open.
6. **Description** (`Description`) and **error row** (`ErrorMessage`): help copy and error copy under the frame. A
   non-empty `ErrorMessage` makes the field invalid, and the frame shows the danger border.
7. **List** (the template part named by `TimePicker.PopupPart`): opens 6 px below the trigger with the trigger's width. It has a 1 px border, the panel
   radius, a 5 px inset and the raised surface. It is at most `MaxDropDownHeight` tall (250 px by default), then
   scrolls.
8. **Option rows**: 36 px tall, with a 12 px inset and rounded corners. The row under the pointer or the keyboard
   gets the muted surface. The chosen time has a 6 px dot at the right edge, so only one row is ever highlighted as
   the chosen one.

### Step and clock

`MinuteStep` sets the distance between the options. The default is 15 minutes, and Arc uses 1, 5, 10, 15 or 30. The
number of options is 1440 divided by the step, rounded up.

| `MinuteStep` | Options | Use it for |
|---|---|---|
| 5 | 288 | Call slots and short appointments |
| 15 | 96 | Meetings, reminders and most schedules (the default) |
| 30 | 48 | Shift starts and opening hours |

`ClockFormat` chooses the display. `Auto` (the default) follows the short time pattern of `Culture`: a culture that
writes the hour as "H" shows 24 hours, and any other culture shows 12 hours with AM and PM. `TwelveHour` shows
"9:15 AM" and `TwentyFourHour` shows "09:15" whatever the culture. The AM and PM words come from the culture, and
fall back to AM and PM when the culture has none. The value is always a `TimeOnly`, whatever the display.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.TimePickerStepsAndClocksDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="16">
        <arc:TimePicker Label="Every 5 minutes"
                        MinuteStep="5"
                        Width="240"
                        HorizontalAlignment="Left" />
        <arc:TimePicker Label="Every 30 minutes, 24-hour"
                        MinuteStep="30"
                        ClockFormat="TwentyFourHour"
                        SelectedTime="18:30"
                        Width="240"
                        HorizontalAlignment="Left" />
        <arc:TimePicker Label="Reminder"
                        SelectedTime="{x:Null}"
                        Width="240"
                        HorizontalAlignment="Left" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

Use `Auto` in an application that serves several regions, so that each person reads times the way they write them.
Force `TwentyFourHour` in an operations console, a timetable or a log view where the 24-hour clock is the standard.
Use `TwelveHour` only when the product's copy is 12-hour everywhere, because a mixed display confuses schedules.

### Empty value and default

`SelectedTime` is a `TimeOnly?`. Arc's default is 09:00 (the property starts at 9:00 AM), so a new picker shows a time
even when nothing was chosen. When the value is `null`, the field shows `Placeholder`, which defaults to `Select a
time`. Use `null` for a field that the person must set, and set a real default only when a time is usually right.

```xml
<arc:TimePicker Label="Reminder" Placeholder="Select a time" SelectedTime="{x:Null}" />
```

```csharp
picker.SelectedTime = new TimeOnly(18, 30);
picker.SelectedTimeChanged += (_, e) =>
{
    status.Text = e.NewTime is { } time ? $"Set to {time:HH:mm}" : "No time";
};
```

A time that is not on a step is kept as it is: with a 15 minute step, `09:07` shows `9:07 AM` on the trigger, and the
list highlights the option at or just before it (09:00). Only the choices from the list land on the step.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.TimePickerSizesAndStatesDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="16">
        <arc:TimePicker Label="Small"
                        Size="Small"
                        Width="240"
                        HorizontalAlignment="Left" />
        <arc:TimePicker Label="Check-in"
                        ErrorMessage="Check-in opens at 3:00 PM."
                        SelectedTime="11:00"
                        Width="240"
                        HorizontalAlignment="Left" />
        <arc:TimePicker Label="Locked"
                        IsEnabled="False"
                        Width="240"
                        HorizontalAlignment="Left" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

### Sizes and states

`Size` sets the height of the trigger: `Small` is 36 px, `Medium` is 44 px (the Arc look) and `Large` is 50 px. Keep one
size per form, so the time fields line up with the input and the date fields beside them. A non-empty `ErrorMessage`
marks the field invalid, and `IsEnabled="False"` disables it: the field is still visible and reads its value, but
nothing opens.

### Binding to a view model

The view model owns the time and the rule that goes with it. With CommunityToolkit.Mvvm:

```csharp
public partial class ShiftViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    private readonly IShiftService _shifts;

    public ShiftViewModel(IShiftService shifts)
    {
        _shifts = shifts;
    }

    [ObservableProperty]
    private TimeOnly? _shiftStart = new TimeOnly(6, 30);

    [ObservableProperty]
    private TimeOnly? _shiftEnd = new TimeOnly(14, 30);

    [ObservableProperty]
    private string? _shiftEndError;

    partial void OnShiftStartChanged(TimeOnly? value) => ValidateShift();

    partial void OnShiftEndChanged(TimeOnly? value) => ValidateShift();

    private void ValidateShift()
    {
        ShiftEndError = ShiftStart is { } start && ShiftEnd is { } end && end <= start
            ? $"End must be after the start, {start:HH:mm}."
            : null;
    }

    [RelayCommand]
    private Task SaveShiftAsync()
    {
        if (ShiftStart is not { } start || ShiftEnd is not { } end || ShiftEndError is not null)
        {
            return Task.CompletedTask;
        }
        return _shifts.SaveAsync(start, end);
    }
}
```

```xml
<StackPanel Width="560" Spacing="20">
    <arc:TimePicker Label="Shift start"
                    SelectedTime="{Binding ShiftStart, Mode=TwoWay}"
                    MinuteStep="30"
                    Width="240"
                    HorizontalAlignment="Left" />
    <arc:TimePicker Label="Shift end"
                    SelectedTime="{Binding ShiftEnd, Mode=TwoWay}"
                    ErrorMessage="{Binding ShiftEndError}"
                    MinuteStep="30"
                    Width="240"
                    HorizontalAlignment="Left" />
    <arc:Button Content="Save shift" Variant="Primary" Command="{Binding SaveShiftCommand}" />
</StackPanel>
```

`SelectedTime` is the only property that carries the value, and it is two-way by default, so the explicit
`Mode=TwoWay` is optional. `SelectedTimeChanged` fires with the old and new times when the value changes by a choice
or by code; use it for side effects such as updating a summary, and bind the value otherwise. The control has no
command of its own. Compiled bindings need `x:DataType` on the view; the example leaves it out for brevity.

### Validation

Times are checked against the rules of the schedule, not against the picker. Put each rule in the view model, and show
the first message in `ErrorMessage` under the field that it concerns.

| Rule | When to check | Where it shows |
|---|---|---|
| End after start | When either time changes | `ErrorMessage` on the end field |
| Within opening hours | When the time changes | `ErrorMessage` on the field the time belongs to |
| Required | On submit, then while the value is `null` | `ErrorMessage`; focus the first empty field |
| Server rejects the time | After the request | `ErrorMessage` on the field it is about; clear it when the value changes |

Clear the message when the value changes, as the `OnShiftStartChanged` and `OnShiftEndChanged` handlers do, so the
error never stays on a value that was already fixed.

### Focus and dismissal

The trigger keeps focus while the list is open. The list is a popup with light dismiss, so a press outside it closes
the list. Choosing a row or pressing Escape closes it too; in each case the focus stays on the trigger and nothing else
moves. Enter or Space on a row chooses it and closes the list, so a keyboard user never needs a separate confirm button.

### Driving it from code

The list is generated from `MinuteStep`, so changing the step or the culture regenerates it while the picker is
closed. The options can be read from code when a page needs them as text:

```csharp
var labels = new List<string>();
for (var i = 0; i < picker.OptionCount; i++)
{
    labels.Add(picker.FormatTime(picker.OptionAt(i)));
}
```

`FormatTime` returns the text the trigger and the list use for the current `ClockFormat` and `Culture`, so a
summary line matches the picker exactly. To combine the time with a `DatePicker` value, use the date's own
conversion in the app: `date.ToDateTime(time)`.

### Example: shift start and end

A staffing tool where a manager sets the start and the end of a shift in half hour steps. The two fields share a size
and a width, the end field shows the error when it is not after the start, and the description on the start field
says what the step means. The save button is the only action, so the form has one primary button.

![Shift start and end times with an error on the end time](https://docs.tkcode.si/shots/Docs/Pickers/TimePicker/images/ShiftTimes.webp)

```xml
<StackPanel Width="560" Spacing="20">
    <arc:TimePicker Label="Shift start"
                    Description="Shifts start on the hour or the half hour."
                    SelectedTime="06:30"
                    MinuteStep="30"
                    Width="240"
                    HorizontalAlignment="Left" />
    <arc:TimePicker Label="Shift end"
                    ErrorMessage="End must be after the start, 06:30."
                    SelectedTime="06:00"
                    MinuteStep="30"
                    Width="240"
                    HorizontalAlignment="Left" />
    <arc:Button Content="Save shift" Variant="Primary" HorizontalAlignment="Left" />
</StackPanel>
```

### Content guidelines

Name the field for the event or the value: `Meeting time`, `Shift start`, Reminder. Keep the placeholder as a short
verb phrase, and write the description as a fact about the step, not a restatement of the label.

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| `Time` | `Meeting time`, `Shift start`, Reminder |
| `Pick a time please` | `Select a time` (the default placeholder) |
| `Times are 15 min apart.` | `Times every 15 minutes.` |
| `Invalid time` | `End must be after the start, 06:30.` |
| `12:00 AM` in a 24-hour product | `00:00` |

Write error messages with the rule and the fix: say what the time must be, not only that it is wrong.

### Best practices

**Do**

- Use `MinuteStep` for the real granularity of the schedule. A 15 minute list suits meetings, and a 30 minute list
  stops people from picking times the business does not offer.
- Keep `Size` the same as the other fields in the form, so that a row of a date and a time lines up.
- Use `null` for a value the person must choose, and show the placeholder, so that the default 09:00 is never saved
  by accident.
- Validate ranges in the view model and show the message on the field it concerns, so the person knows which time to
  change.
- Use `Auto` when the product serves several regions, and `TwentyFourHour` when the domain uses it.

**Avoid**

- Using the picker for a list of named periods. A list of "Morning" or "Evening" entries should be a `Select`,
  because a time picker suggests a clock that the periods do not have.
- Storing a time as text. The value is a `TimeOnly`; format it only for display, so comparisons and sorting stay
  correct.
- Using a step other than the ones Arc defines (1, 5, 10, 15 and 30). Stick to them so that the list reads as a clock
  people already know.
- Showing the error only on submit when the rule can be checked as soon as a time changes. The person can fix a
  shift end at once when the message is next to the field.
- Expecting one value for the date and the time. The control holds only a `TimeOnly`, so keep the day in a
  `DatePicker` and join the two in code with `date.ToDateTime(time)`.

### Common questions

**Why does the field show 9:00 AM when I did not set a time?** The control's default is 09:00, which Arc uses so that
the field always reads as a time. Set `SelectedTime` to `null` to show the placeholder instead.

**Can people type a time?** No. The trigger opens a list, and the value changes only when a row is chosen or code sets
`SelectedTime`. Use `Input` with a rule when typed input is required.

**What happens when the time is not on the step?** The value is kept as set, so `09:07` stays `09:07` and shows as
`9:07 AM`. The list highlights the option at or before the time, which is 09:00 with a 15 minute step. Round the value
in the view model if the business needs an exact step.

**How do I store the value as "HH:mm" text?** The value is a `TimeOnly`, so the text is only a format of it:
`SelectedTime?.ToString("HH:mm")` in the app, or `picker.FormatTime(time)` for the display text.

**Does the list scroll the page?** No. The list scrolls by itself, and opening it centres the chosen time in the list,
so the page does not move.

## API reference

### TimePicker

Arc time field: a trigger over a scrolling list of times generated every `MinuteStep` minutes. The list opens centred on the chosen time, arrow keys move the highlight (the list glides to keep it in view, wrapping at both ends), Enter or a click chooses and closes, Escape closes. The shown time rolls like a clock face: a later time rises from below, an earlier one drops from above. 12- or 24-hour display follows the culture unless `ClockFormat` says otherwise; the value is always a 24-hour `TimeOnly`.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SelectedTime` | `TimeOnly?` | `09:00` | The chosen time (two-way). Arc's default is 09:00; null shows the placeholder. |
| `IsDropDownOpen` | `bool` | `false` | Whether the list is open (two-way). |
| `MinuteStep` | `int` | `15` | Minutes between options (Arc: 1, 5, 10, 15 or 30; default 15). |
| `ClockFormat` | `TimePickerClockFormat` | `Auto` | 12- or 24-hour display (Auto follows the culture). |
| `Culture` | `CultureInfo?` | `null` | Culture for the clock format and the AM / PM designators (null = current UI culture). |
| `Label` | `string?` | `null` | The visible label above the trigger (Arc: required). |
| `Description` | `string?` | `null` | Helper copy under the trigger. |
| `ErrorMessage` | `string?` | `null` | Error copy under the trigger; non-empty makes the field invalid. |
| `IsLabelVisible` | `bool` | `true` | When false the label is hidden but still names the field. |
| `Size` | `ControlSize` | `Medium` | Trigger height: Small 36, Medium 44 (default), Large 50. |
| `Placeholder` | `string` | `"Select a time"` | Shown while there is no time (Arc: "Select a time"). |
| `MaxDropDownHeight` | `double` | `250` | Tallest the list grows before it scrolls (Arc: 250px). |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `SelectedTimeChanged` | `TimePickerSelectedTimeChangedEventArgs` | Raised when `SelectedTime` changes. |

Pseudo-classes: `:open`, `:pressed`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

## Accessibility

- `Label` names the field. `Description` and `ErrorMessage` are the help text.
- Focus stays on the trigger while the list is open. The trigger reports its expanded state and its value, so a
  screen reader announces the current time as the list changes.
- The trigger is exposed as a combo box whose name is the label and whose value is the formatted time, or the
  placeholder when there is no time.
- Enter, Space or ArrowDown open the list, with the chosen time in the centre and active. ArrowUp and ArrowDown
  move between the times and wrap at both ends.
- Escape closes the list. A pointer press outside it also closes it.
- A focus ring is shown on the trigger for keyboard focus.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Enter` / `Space` (list closed) | Opens the list with the chosen time active |
| `Enter` / `Space` (list open) | Chooses the active time and closes the list |
| `ArrowDown` / `ArrowUp` (list closed) | Opens the list |
| `ArrowDown` / `ArrowUp` (list open) | Moves the active time down or up, wrapping from the last time to the first and back |
| `Home` / `End` (list open) | Moves to the first time (12:00 AM or 00:00) or the last time of the day |
| `Escape` (list open) | Closes the list and keeps focus on the trigger |

The pointer does the same as the keyboard: moving over a row makes it active, and a click chooses it.

## Motion

- The value rolls in the direction of time: a later time rises from below and an earlier one falls from above.
- The list grows from the trigger with a short spring and fades in. It closes almost at once.
- The active row changes its background quickly, and a small dot marks the selected time, so only one row is
  highlighted at a time.
- Reduced motion cross-fades the value and only fades the list in and out. Off jumps to the end state.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| The value changes | The time rolls in the direction of time, with a soft blur | Cross-fade | Immediate |
| The list opens | Grows from the trigger, 6 px up and 0.97 scale to full size, on a snappy spring with a fast fade | Fades in | Immediate |
| The list closes | Lifts 4 px and scales to 0.98, then closes almost at once | Fades out | Immediate |
| The active row moves with the keyboard | The list glides to keep the row in view on a smooth spring | Positioned at once | Immediate |

## Related

- `DatePicker` to pair a date with a time.
- `Select` for a short list of named choices.
- `DateRangePicker` for a range of dates.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `DatePicker` | The value is a day, and a time is stored separately or joined in code |
| `DateRangePicker` | The value is a span of whole days |
| `Select` | The choices are a short list of named times or periods |
| `Input` | People must type a value that the list cannot express, with a validation rule |
| `NumberField` | The value is a duration in minutes, not a time of day |
