# Color picker

> A swatch that grows into a picker with format morphing, eyedropper, saved swatches, and contrast readout.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/color-picker

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ColorPickerColorFieldDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12">
        <arc:ColorPicker Label="Accent" ColorChanged="OnColorChanged" />
        <TextBlock x:Name="Status"
                   Text="onValueChange: #2F6BFF"
                   FontSize="13"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class ColorPickerColorFieldDemo : UserControl
{
    public ColorPickerColorFieldDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
    }

    private void OnColorChanged(object? sender, ColorPickerColorChangedEventArgs e)
        => Status.Text = $"onValueChange: {e.Hex}";
}
```

## When to use

`ColorPicker` gives a person a full color editor in a compact field. The closed control is a swatch with a label and the
hex value; opening it reveals the saturation and brightness area, the hue and opacity sliders, a text field that accepts
four notations, a contrast readout and a row of saved colors. It belongs where a color is a real setting that the
person must tune, not a choice from a short list.

- **Brand settings in a multi-tenant admin console**: an administrator sets the primary color for a customer's invoices
  and sign-in page. The swatch shows the current brand color in the settings list, and the panel accepts a pasted hex
  value from the customer's style guide.
- **Theme and design token editors**: a product team edits surface and accent colors, including translucent overlays
  where the alpha channel is part of the value. The OKLCH format lets them adjust lightness and chroma by hand.
- **Text color checks in a content tool**: an editor chooses a text color and reads its WCAG contrast against the
  background of the page it will sit on. The grade (AAA, AA, AA large or Fails) shows whether the text is legible
  before it is published.
- **Series colors for charts and dashboards**: an analyst assigns a color to each chart series. The saved colors keep
  the palette the team has already agreed, so each new series is picked from the same set.
- **Saved brand swatches for marketing tools**: a campaign builder keeps up to seven colors that the team reuses across
  banners and emails, with the newest color first.

## When not to use

- **A few fixed colors**: use `SegmentedControl` or `RadioGroup` when the options are named choices such as "Light",
  "Dark" or three status colors. The person picks one; they do not tune the color.
- **A plain hex value with no picker**: use `Input` when the value is typed or pasted and the person never needs the
  area or the sliders, for example an API token color in a webhook setting that is copied from documentation.
- **Small preset color labels that filter a list**: use `ChipGroup` for tags such as "Red", "Blue" or "Unassigned" that
  filter invoices or tickets. A chip group selects among presets; it does not produce arbitrary values.
- **A color derived from a brand palette that the person should not change**: show the value in a read-only `Input`
  next to the setting it belongs to. A disabled picker still takes space and invites a question about why it is
  locked; state the rule in the description instead.
- **Dates, numbers or measures**: use `NumberField`, `DatePicker` or `Slider` for values with units. A color has three
  or four channels that the picker keeps in step; those controls hold a single number.

## Usage

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:ColorPicker Label="Accent"
                     Color="#2F6BFF"
                     Format="Hex" />
</UserControl>
```

`ColorPicker` derives from Avalonia's `TemplatedControl` and implements the Arc picker automation contract, so it
takes the usual layout, `IsEnabled`, focus and styling properties. Its value is an Avalonia `Color`, so the same
color flows into brushes, resources and view models without conversion. The label, description and error copy come
from the shared field foundation, so the picker lines up with the other fields in a form.

### Anatomy

1. **Trigger**: a 44 px pill with a 22 px corner radius. It holds a 32 px chip that shows the color (over a
   checkerboard when the color is translucent), the `Label` in 12 px text and the `HexValue` in 14 px text, with a 10 px
   gap between the chip and the text. It is left aligned and takes its own width.
2. **Description** (`Description`): helper copy under the trigger, in the muted text color.
3. **Error** (`ErrorMessage`): copy in the danger color under the trigger. A non-empty value marks the picker invalid.
4. **Panel head**: when the panel is open, it repeats the chip, the label and the hex value, with a 32 px Done button at
   the right edge. The panel is at most 304 px wide, and never wider than the window minus 32 px.
5. **Saturation and brightness area**: 164 px high with a 16 px corner radius. Saturation runs left to right and
   brightness runs bottom to top, and the thumb shows the current pair.
6. **Hue and opacity sliders**: two 14 px tracks under the area. The opacity track shows the color over the checkerboard.
7. **Value field**: a 40 px row with a 14 px corner radius. The format button at its start (HEX, RGB, HSL or OKLCH) is at
   least 56 px wide. The text field takes the rest of the row, and an invalid entry shows its message below.
8. **Contrast row**: a 36 × 28 px sample with a 9 px corner radius, showing the color on `ContrastBackground`; the ratio
   text, the grade in a 22 px pill, and the words "against background" (hidden on viewports 360 px wide or less).
9. **Saved swatches**: a row of saved colors, each a small square, followed by a dashed Save button.

The panel opens downward from the trigger and grows out of it. It moves left or up only when the window edge would clip
it, and when the page is scrolled to the bottom, the page scrolls to make room first.

### Value and format

`Color` is an Avalonia `Color` and is two-way. It is the value to bind. `Format` sets the notation shown in the text
field, and the format button cycles through the four notations in the panel. Setting `Format` in code changes the
notation without changing the color.

`HexValue` is read-only and gives the color as upper-case CSS hex: `#RRGGBB`, or `#RRGGBBAA` when the color is
translucent. Use it for display, copy and export. It is not the same order as Avalonia's own string form: Avalonia's
`Color.Parse` reads eight-digit values as `#AARRGGBB`, so pass CSS values through the picker's text field or convert
them yourself.

| Format | Example output for #2F6BFF | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `Hex` | `#2F6BFF` | The default. Translucent colors add two digits: `#2F6BFF80`. |
| `Rgb` | `rgb(47 107 255)` | Space-separated. Translucent colors add `/ 50%` in the same form. |
| `Hsl` | `hsl(223 100% 59%)` | Hue in degrees, saturation and lightness in percent. |
| `Oklch` | `oklch(56.2% 0.214 263.5)` | Perceptual lightness and chroma; useful when two colors must look equally bright. |

The text field accepts the same four notations, and it is tolerant on input: three- and four-digit hex, `rgb()` and
`rgba()`, `hsl()` and `hsla()` with or without `deg`, and `oklch()`, in both the modern space-separated and the
comma-separated forms. Anything else is rejected, as described in the validation section below.

```xml
<arc:ColorPicker Label="Brand" Color="#E5484D" Format="Oklch" />
```

```csharp
picker.ColorChanged += (_, e) => status.Text = $"Color: {e.Hex}";
```

The event arguments carry the previous color, the new color and the CSS hex:

| Member | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `OldColor` | `Color` | The color before the change. |
| `NewColor` | `Color` | The color after the change. |
| `Hex` | `string` | The new color as upper-case CSS hex, with alpha digits when translucent. |

`ColorChanged` is raised for every change of `Color`, including each pointer move while a handle is dragged. A save
to a server on every move creates a burst of requests; save on the panel's close (`IsDropDownOpen` turning `False`), or
debounce the handler.

### Saved swatches

`Swatches` is an `IReadOnlyList<ColorSwatch>?`. A `ColorSwatch` is a record with an `Id` and a `Color`; create one with
`ColorSwatch.Create(color)`, which gives it a fresh identity. The list is newest first. The Save button adds the current
color to the front, and when the list is longer than `MaxSwatches` (7 by default) the oldest swatch is dropped.
Swatches can be reordered by dragging, or with `Alt` and the arrow keys, and removed with `Delete` or `Backspace`.

Every change creates a new list, so a view model should bind `Swatches` two-way and replace the list rather than
modify it. The `SwatchesChanged` event is raised for saves, reorders and removals made in the panel. Setting `Swatches`
in code only updates the property and the row; it does not raise the event.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ColorPickerFormatsAndSavedSwatchesDemo">
    <arc:ColorPicker x:Name="Brand"
                     Label="Brand"
                     Color="#E5484D"
                     Format="Oklch" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Media;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class ColorPickerFormatsAndSavedSwatchesDemo : UserControl
{
    public ColorPickerFormatsAndSavedSwatchesDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Brand.Swatches =
        [
            ColorSwatch.Create(Color.Parse("#E5484D")),
            ColorSwatch.Create(Color.Parse("#F76B15")),
            ColorSwatch.Create(Color.Parse("#30A46C")),
            ColorSwatch.Create(Color.Parse("#0090FF")),
            ColorSwatch.Create(Color.Parse("#8E4EC6"))
        ];
    }
}
```

Each swatch keeps its `Id` when it is reordered, so a view model can follow one swatch across moves.

### Limits and the eyedropper

`ColorPicker` does not offer an eyedropper. Avalonia has no cross-platform API that reads a color from the screen, and
macOS needs screen recording permission for the attempt. A design tool that needs one must take the color from its own
canvas or from the clipboard and paste the hex value into the field.

### Contrast and accessibility

`ContrastBackground` is the color that the picked color will sit on. The readout compares the value with it using the
WCAG contrast ratio, from 1 to 21, and labels the result with a grade:

| Ratio | Grade | Use |
|---|---|---|
| 7 or more | AAA | Body text at any size |
| 4.5 or more | AA | Body text |
| 3 or more | AA large | Large text and interface graphics only |
| below 3 | Fails | Do not use for text |

The default background is white. Set it to the real surface that the color sits on, such as the card color or the dark
page color, because the ratio is only as good as the background it is measured against. `ContrastRatio` and
`ContrastGrade` expose the same values in code, so a form can warn about a failing text color without opening the panel.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ColorPickerContrastDemo">
    <arc:ColorPicker Label="Text on dark"
                     Color="#A1A1AA"
                     ContrastBackground="#111113"
                     Description="The contrast readout compares against #111113." />
</UserControl>
```

### Validation and error state

A non-empty `ErrorMessage` marks the field invalid. A typed value that is not a color is rejected when the person
presses Enter: the field shakes, the danger border appears and the text "Enter a hex, RGB, HSL, or OKLCH color" (set
`InvalidColorText` to change it) is shown in the panel. The picker keeps the last valid color until a valid value is
entered.

`ErrorMessage` belongs to the app. Use it for rules the picker cannot know, such as a color that is too close to the
background of a required element, and show the rule in plain words. `IsEnabled="False"` disables the picker; it keeps the
swatch visible, so a locked value still shows what is in force.

```xml
<arc:ColorPicker Label="Locked" IsEnabled="False" />
```

### Binding to a view model

A tenant's brand settings are a view model property with a color and a list of saved swatches. The picker binds both
two-way, and the view model decides when the change is saved.

```csharp
public interface IBrandSettingsStore
{
    Task SaveBrandAsync(Color primary, IReadOnlyList<Color> saved);
}

public partial class BrandSettingsViewModel(IBrandSettingsStore settings) : ObservableObject
{
    [ObservableProperty]
    private Color _primaryColor = Color.Parse("#2F6BFF");

    [ObservableProperty]
    private IReadOnlyList<ColorSwatch> _savedColors = [];

    [RelayCommand]
    private async Task SaveAsync()
    {
        await settings.SaveBrandAsync(PrimaryColor, SavedColors.Select(s => s.Color).ToList());
    }
}
```

```xml
<StackPanel Width="304" Spacing="16">
    <arc:ColorPicker Label="Primary"
                     Color="{Binding PrimaryColor, Mode=TwoWay}"
                     Swatches="{Binding SavedColors, Mode=TwoWay}"
                     Description="Buttons, links and focus rings." />
    <arc:Button Content="Save brand" Command="{Binding SaveAsyncCommand}" />
</StackPanel>
```

`Color`, `Swatches` and `Format` are the two-way properties. `HexValue`, `ContrastRatio` and `ContrastGrade` are one-way
reads that the view model can display. `IsDropDownOpen` is two-way too, so a view model can close the panel when the
person leaves the settings page. The view model's `SaveAsync` runs from a button, not from each color change, so a
half-finished drag never reaches the server.

### Example: tenant brand colors

A brand settings card in an admin console for a SaaS product. The card holds three pickers: the primary color, the
accent color for charts, and the body text color with its contrast readout. The labels are one word, the descriptions
say where each color appears, and the error on the text color names the rule that failed. The picker is closed in the
screenshot, so the scene shows what the person sees before they open a panel.

![A brand settings card with three color pickers, one with a contrast error](https://docs.tkcode.si/shots/Docs/Pickers/ColorPicker/images/BrandSettings.webp)

```xml
<Border Width="560"
        Padding="24"
        Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Surface}"
        BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource BorderSubtle}"
        BorderThickness="1"
        CornerRadius="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource RadiusPanel}">
    <StackPanel Spacing="20">
        <StackPanel Spacing="4">
            <TextBlock Text="Brand colors"
                       FontSize="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TypeLG}"
                       FontWeight="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource WeightMedium}"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
            <TextBlock Text="Acme Analytics customer portal"
                       FontSize="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TypeSM}"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
        </StackPanel>
        <arc:ColorPicker Label="Primary"
                         Color="#2F6BFF"
                         Description="Buttons, links and focus rings." />
        <arc:ColorPicker Label="Chart accent"
                         Color="#E5484D"
                         Format="Oklch"
                         Description="Highlights the selected series in charts." />
        <arc:ColorPicker Label="Body text"
                         Color="#9CA3AF"
                         ContrastBackground="#FFFFFF"
                         ErrorMessage="Contrast 2.5 to 1 fails. Choose a darker color." />
        <arc:Button Content="Save brand colors" HorizontalAlignment="Right" />
    </StackPanel>
</Border>
```

The example uses `Oklch` for the chart accent because the team compares lightness across series, and the body text
color is checked against the white card so the error is visible without opening the panel. The button says what
happens, and it is the only action on the card.

### Content guidelines

- **Label**: a short noun that names the role of the color: "Primary", "Chart accent", "Body text". The label is drawn
  inside the swatch, so keep it to two words.
- **Description**: say where the color is used, in one sentence: "Buttons, links and focus rings."
- **Error**: name the rule and the fix: "Contrast 2.5 to 1 fails. Choose a darker color." Do not repeat the label.
- **Save action**: use a verb and an object that describe the saved scope: "Save brand colors", not "Submit".
- **Background names**: call the background by its role, such as "Card background", so the person knows what the
  contrast readout compares against.

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| Color | Primary button color |
| Invalid color!! | Enter a hex, RGB, HSL, or OKLCH color. |
| Submit | Save brand colors |
| Contrast fail | Contrast 2.5 to 1 fails. Choose a darker color. |

### Best practices

**Do**

- Bind `Color` two-way and save on a deliberate action, because `ColorChanged` fires for every pointer move while a
  handle is dragged.
- Set `ContrastBackground` to the real surface, so the readout matches what people will see.
- Show `Format` as the team's notation: `Hex` for CSS and design handoff, `Oklch` when lightness must be compared.
- Keep `MaxSwatches` at the default of 7 unless the team has a palette that needs more; a longer row is harder to scan.
- Give every picker a `Label`, even in compact settings, because the label is the name that screen readers announce.

**Avoid**

- Using `ColorChanged` as the save trigger. Each move creates an event, so a network call per move floods the server.
- Calling `Color.Parse` on a CSS eight-digit value. Avalonia reads `#AARRGGBB`, so the alpha channel lands in the wrong
  place; use `HexValue` for CSS output and let the picker parse CSS input.
- Setting `Swatches` in code and expecting `SwatchesChanged`. The event describes changes made in the panel, so a
  view model that sets the list itself already knows the new value.
- Using the picker for a palette that must stay fixed. Offer the approved colors with `SegmentedControl` or `ChipGroup`,
  because a free picker lets people leave the palette.
- Judging contrast against the default white background when the color sits on a dark surface. The grade is accurate
  for the background it is given and misleading for any other.

### Common questions

**How do I start the picker from a stored hex string?** Keep the value as an Avalonia `Color` in the view model and set
`Color`. For a CSS-order value such as `#2F6BFF80`, reorder the digits to `#802F6BFF` before `Color.Parse`, because
Avalonia reads eight-digit values as `#AARRGGBB`. Output the value with `HexValue` so the stored form stays in CSS order.

**Why does the picker show a different notation from the one I set?** `Format` is the notation of the text field. The
person can cycle it in the panel, and the value does not change; the color stays the same in every notation.

**Can I close the panel from code?** Yes. Set `IsDropDownOpen` to `False`. Done, Escape and a press outside the panel
close it in the same way, and Done and Escape return focus to the trigger.

**Why does the Escape key not close the panel while I am typing?** The first Escape discards the typed draft, which
returns the text field to the current color. A second Escape closes the panel. This keeps a half-typed value from being
lost by accident.

**What does the readout do with a translucent color?** It composites the color over `ContrastBackground` before it
measures the ratio, so the grade describes the color as it would look on that background, not the raw color.

## API reference

### ColorPicker

Arc color field: a swatch whose box grows into the full picker (a clipped reveal on a spring, its shadow following the shape). Pick saturation and brightness on the area, hue and opacity on the sliders, or type a value in hex, RGB, HSL or OKLCH; the format button morphs its label and the value between formats. A contrast readout counts to the WCAG ratio against `ContrastBackground` with its grade, and saved swatches pop in, reorder by drag or Alt + arrows and go with Delete. Arrow keys move every thumb (Shift and Page keys by ten); Escape drops a draft, then closes and returns focus. The eyedropper is not offered: Avalonia has no cross-platform screen color API.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Color` | `Color` | `#ff2f6bff` | The color (two-way). Arc's default is #2F6BFF. |
| `HexValue` | `string` | – | *Read-only.* The color as upper-case CSS hex (#RRGGBB, or #RRGGBBAA when translucent). |
| `ContrastBackground` | `Color` | `White` | The background the color will sit on, for the contrast readout (Arc: white). |
| `Label` | `string?` | `"Color"` | Name shown on the swatch, such as "Accent" (Arc: "Color"). |
| `Description` | `string?` | `null` | Helper copy under the swatch. |
| `ErrorMessage` | `string?` | `null` | Error copy under the swatch. |
| `Format` | `ColorPickerFormat` | `Hex` | Format of the value field; the format button cycles it. |
| `Swatches` | `IReadOnlyList<ColorSwatch>?` | `null` | Saved swatches, newest first (two-way; every change produces a new list). |
| `MaxSwatches` | `int` | `7` | Most saved swatches; saving past it drops the oldest (Arc: 7). |
| `IsDropDownOpen` | `bool` | `false` | Whether the panel is open (two-way). |
| `InvalidColorText` | `string` | `"Enter a hex, RGB, HSL, or OKLCH color"` | Shown under the value field for text that is not a color. |
| `AgainstBackgroundText` | `string` | `"against background"` | Text after the contrast ratio that compares the color with the background (default "against background"). |
| `DoneText` | `string` | `"Done"` | Label of the Done button that closes the panel (default "Done"). |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ColorChanged` | `ColorPickerColorChangedEventArgs` | Raised when `Color` changes. |
| `SwatchesChanged` | `ColorPickerSwatchesChangedEventArgs` | Raised when the saved swatches change. |

Pseudo-classes: `:open`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

### ColorSwatch

A saved swatch. `Id` keeps its identity while the row is reordered.

## Accessibility

- `Label` names the trigger, and the open panel is named after it: "Primary color". The trigger exposes its expanded
  state, so a screen reader announces whether the panel is open.
- The saturation and brightness area is a two-dimensional slider. Its value reports both saturation and brightness,
  and its type is announced as "2D slider". The hue and opacity sliders report their angle and percentage.
- The text field is named after the label and the notation, for example "Primary in Hex". An invalid entry sets the help
  text to the error message and is announced politely.
- The contrast ratio and its grade are text, not only color: the readout says "Contrast 4.52 to 1, passes AA" or
  "fails", so the grade does not depend on the color of the pill.
- The saved swatches form a horizontal list with one tab stop. The current color is exposed as selected, and the swatch
  names describe how to move and remove them.
- Focus is returned to the trigger when the panel closes with Done or Escape, so the person keeps their place in the form.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Enter` / `Space` on the trigger | Open the panel and move focus to the saturation area |
| `Enter` / `Space` on the trigger while open | Close the panel and return focus to the trigger |
| `Escape` in the panel | Close the panel and return focus to the trigger |
| `Left` / `Right` / `Up` / `Down` on the area | Move saturation (left and right) and brightness (up and down) by 1 percent |
| `Shift` or `PageUp` / `PageDown` on the area | Move saturation by 10 steps |
| `Left` / `Right` (`Up` / `Down`) on a slider | Move hue by 1 degree, or opacity by 1 percent |
| `Shift`, `PageUp` / `PageDown` on a slider | Move by 10 |
| `Home` / `End` on a slider | Move to the minimum or the maximum |
| `Enter` in the text field | Apply the typed value; an invalid value shakes the field and shows the error |
| `Escape` in the text field | Discard the typed draft; a second `Escape` closes the panel |
| `Left` / `Right`, `Home` / `End` on a swatch | Move focus between saved swatches |
| `Alt` + `Left` / `Right` on a swatch | Move the swatch one place |
| `Enter` / `Space` on a swatch | Apply the saved color |
| `Delete` / `Backspace` on a swatch | Remove the swatch |

Drag works with the pointer on the area and the sliders. A press outside the panel closes it without moving focus away
from the place the person pressed.

## Motion

- The panel is revealed from the swatch: the clip grows from the trigger's corners to the full panel, with a shadow
  that follows the clip.
- The handle follows the pointer with a quick spring, and it tightens while it is dragged.
- The format button morphs the text between HEX, RGB, HSL and OKLCH. The contrast ratio counts to its new value.
- An invalid entry shakes the field. A new swatch pops in, and a moved swatch settles into place.
- Reduced motion jumps the handles, fades the panel in place of the clip, and drops the format morph and the shake.
  Off jumps to the end state.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| Panel opens | Clip grows from the trigger on a spring; the content fades in and rises 10 px behind the leading edge | The panel fades in at its full size | Immediate |
| Panel closes | The clip folds back into the trigger on a short spring with no bounce | The panel fades out | Immediate |
| Handle moves | Follows the pointer on a quick spring; tightens to a firm spring while dragged | Jumps to the new position | Immediate |
| Format changes | The text morphs from the old notation to the new one | The text changes at once | Immediate |
| Contrast ratio changes | The number counts to the new value | The number changes at once | Immediate |
| Invalid entry | The field shakes side to side once and the error appears | The error appears without the shake | The error appears at once |
| Swatch saved or reordered | The swatch pops in, or settles into its new place | Appears or moves at once | Immediate |

## Related

- `SegmentedControl` or `RadioGroup` for a few fixed colors.
- `Input` for plain text values.
- `ChipGroup` for small preset labels.
- `DatePicker` for a date value that follows the same field pattern in a form.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `SegmentedControl` / `RadioGroup` | The person chooses one of a few fixed colors or themes |
| `Input` | The color is typed or pasted and never tuned in an area |
| `ChipGroup` | The colors are presets that filter or tag a list |
| `Slider` | A single numeric channel, such as opacity, is the only thing to set |
| `DatePicker` | The value is a date rather than a color, in the same form layout |

# Rich text editor

> A lightweight editor with markdown shortcuts, a floating toolbar, a slash menu, and HTML and markdown output.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/rich-text-editor

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.RichTextEditorShortcutsDemo">
    <Border Padding="24,20"
            CornerRadius="26"
            BorderThickness="1"
            MaxWidth="680"
            Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Surface}"
            BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Border}">
        <arc:RichTextEditor x:Name="Editor" />
    </Border>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class RichTextEditorShortcutsDemo : UserControl
{
    public RichTextEditorShortcutsDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Editor.Markdown = """
            # Launch notes

            Type **Markdown** as you go: `#` and a space makes a heading, `-` a list, `>` a quote, and three backticks a code block. Select text for the _floating toolbar_, or type `/` on an empty line for blocks.

            - Shortcuts: ⌘B, ⌘I, ⌘⇧X, ⌘E and ⌘K
            - Tab nests a list item
              - Shift+Tab brings it back

            > Undo is the editor's own: ⌘Z and ⌘⇧Z.
            """;
    }
}
```

## When to use

`RichTextEditor` is the writing surface for content that needs light formatting: bold and italic text, headings,
lists, quotes and code blocks. It holds the document, the floating toolbar and the block menu, so a form needs no
extra layout around it. The content leaves the editor as clean HTML or Markdown, which the app stores and reads
back later.

- **Release notes and changelog drafts in a developer tool**: an engineer types `## ` for a heading and `- ` for a
  list, and the editor saves Markdown that the release pipeline publishes unchanged.
- **Comments and replies in a project tracker or a CRM note**: short notes with bold text, lists and quotes. The
  HTML output is safe to render because the editor keeps only its own tags.
- **Knowledge base or help center articles**: an author writes an article in the admin console and saves HTML that
  the public site renders, with headings and code blocks for steps and commands.
- **Incident write-ups and postmortems**: headings, quotes for customer-facing wording and code blocks for log lines,
  set `IsReadOnly` once the report is published so the text can be read and copied but not changed.
- **Announcements in a billing or account console**: a short message with a link to the invoice page, written by a
  finance or support user who needs formatting but not layout.

## When not to use

- **Plain multi-line text with no formatting**: use `Textarea`, which wraps and resizes without a toolbar or blocks.
- **Mentions of people or tags inside a text field**: use `MentionInput`, which suggests and stores the mentions.
- **A single line that is renamed in place on a page**: use `InlineEdit`, which looks like text until it is edited.
- **Source code or a read-only code listing**: use `CodeBlock`, which shows the code with its own copy action.
- **Layout-heavy documents**: tables hold inline text only (no nested blocks), and images sit in their own block. For page layout, columns or files that must be uploaded with progress, use a document editor or `FileDropzone`.

## Usage

Set `Markdown` for the initial content. `Markdown` and `Html` are both two-way: assigning either one reloads the
editor, and both follow every edit.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:RichTextEditor Markdown="## Notes&#10;&#10;Type **Markdown** as you go, or `/` for blocks." />
</UserControl>
```

`RichTextEditor` derives from `TemplatedControl`, not from `TextBox`. It is a block editor: the document is a list of
blocks (paragraphs, headings, list items, quotes, code blocks and dividers), and each block lays out its own text
with its marks. That gives the editor its own undo history, its own clipboard rules and its own output, so the text
is not stored as a raw string that the control edits in place. It is not a `TextBox`, so it has no caret index or
`MaxLength`; read the text with `GetText()` and use the members listed in the API reference.

### Anatomy

1. **Writing surface**: the editable document, with a minimum height of 128 px. It draws the text, the list markers,
   the quote bar, the code background and the selection, and it places the caret.
2. **Placeholder** (`Placeholder`, default "Start writing"): shown in the muted text color while the document is
   empty.
3. **Block hint** (`BlockHint`, default "Type / for blocks"): shown on the empty line that holds the caret.
4. **Floating toolbar**: appears above a selection, with 32 px square buttons on a 16 px corner radius. It has the
   inline marks (bold, italic, strikethrough, inline code), a link button and the block types. Its link field
   replaces the buttons in place when a link is edited.
5. **Link field**: a one-line field in the toolbar that takes a URL for the selection or the link at the caret.
6. **Block menu**: the list that opens at a `/` and filters as you type. Its rows are 34 px high on a 12 px radius, in
   a panel with an 18 px radius.
7. **Live region**: a hidden element that announces results such as "Formatted" or "Link added" to assistive
   technology.

### Block types and marks

The document is built from blocks of one `RichTextBlockType` and inline marks from `RichTextMark`. The toolbar and
the block menu use these values with `ToggleMark`, `SetBlockType` and the `Formats` report.

| Type | Written as | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `Paragraph` | Plain text | The default block |
| `Heading1`, `Heading2`, `Heading3` | `# `, `## `, `### ` | The `Arc` profile imports h4 to h6 as `Heading3` |
| `Heading4`, `Heading5`, `Heading6` | `#### `, `##### `, `###### ` | `Docs` profile only; `Heading6` is drawn in the secondary text color |
| `BulletedList`, `NumberedList` | `- `, `1. ` | Nest with Tab; a level holds the same list kind |
| `Quote` | `> ` | A block quote with a bar at its start |
| `CodeBlock` | Three backticks | Holds plain text only; lines do not wrap |
| `Divider` | `---` | A horizontal rule; `SetBlockType` inserts one in place of an empty block |

| Mark | Written as | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `Bold` | `**text**` | |
| `Italic` | `_text_` or `*text*` | |
| `Strikethrough` | `~~text~~` | |
| `Code` | `` `text` `` | Kept within one block |

Links are not a mark in this list: `SetLink` and the link field attach an address to the selected text.

### Markdown shortcuts and the supported subset

The editor converts Markdown as the person types. A shortcut runs as soon as the typed text completes it, so the
person sees the result without a preview. Shortcuts do not run inside a code block.

| Type | Result |
|---|---|
| `# `, `## `, `### ` at the start of a line | Heading 1, 2 or 3 |
| `- `, `* `, `+ ` | Bulleted list item |
| `1. `, `1) ` | Numbered list item |
| `> ` | Quote |
| `---` | Divider |
| Three backticks | Code block |
| `**text**`, `_text_`, `~~text~~`, `` `text` `` | Bold, italic, strikethrough, inline code |

The editor writes and reads a fixed subset: paragraphs, three heading levels, nested bulleted and numbered lists,
quotes, code blocks, dividers, and the four inline marks and links. Pasted HTML is sanitized to this subset, so
unknown tags and styles disappear while their text is kept. Use the subset as the content contract for the feature:
a document that needs anything else must be stored elsewhere.

### The Docs profile

Set `Profile="Docs"` for a document-style editor. The default profile, `Arc`, stays exactly as described above; `Docs`
adds the features a longer document needs:

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.RichTextEditorDocsProfileDemo">
    <Border Padding="24,20"
            CornerRadius="26"
            BorderThickness="1"
            MaxWidth="680"
            Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Surface}"
            BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Border}">
        <arc:RichTextEditor Profile="Docs"
                            Placeholder="Plan the launch"
                            Html="&lt;h2&gt;Launch checklist&lt;/h2&gt;&lt;p data-spacing=&quot;relaxed&quot;&gt;Select text for &lt;span data-size=&quot;large&quot;&gt;size&lt;/span&gt;, &lt;u&gt;underline&lt;/u&gt;, &lt;span data-color=&quot;red&quot;&gt;text color&lt;/span&gt; and &lt;mark data-bg=&quot;yellow&quot;&gt;highlight&lt;/mark&gt;, or for x&lt;sup&gt;2&lt;/sup&gt; and H&lt;sub&gt;2&lt;/sub&gt;O.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;h4&gt;Before the release&lt;/h4&gt;&lt;ul data-todo=&quot;true&quot;&gt;&lt;li data-checked=&quot;true&quot;&gt;Freeze the release branch&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Write the announcement&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Notify support&lt;/li&gt;&lt;/ul&gt;&lt;ul data-toggle=&quot;true&quot;&gt;&lt;li data-collapsed=&quot;true&quot;&gt;Rollback plan&lt;ul&gt;&lt;li&gt;Revert the tag&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Post in the incident channel&lt;/li&gt;&lt;/ul&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&lt;/ul&gt;&lt;p data-align=&quot;center&quot;&gt;Type [] and a space for a to-do item.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;pre data-lang=&quot;bash&quot;&gt;git tag v4.2.0&lt;/pre&gt;" />
    </Border>
</UserControl>
```

| Feature | How to use it | Written as |
|---|---|---|
| Underline | `Ctrl+U`, the toolbar button, `ToggleMark(RichTextMark.Underline)` | `<u>` in HTML |
| Superscript and subscript | `Ctrl+.` and `Ctrl+,`, the toolbar buttons, `ToggleMark(RichTextMark.Superscript)` or `ToggleMark(RichTextMark.Subscript)`; turning one on turns the other off | `<sup>`, `<sub>` |
| Text size | The toolbar's size button (small, default, large, extra large, relative to the block's text); `SetTextSize` | `<span data-size="large">` |
| Line spacing | The block menu's Line spacing entries (compact, default, relaxed, loose); `SetLineSpacing` for the selected blocks. Code blocks and table cells keep their own | `data-spacing="relaxed"` on `p`, headings, list items, quotes and callout paragraphs |
| Headings 4 to 6 | `#### `, `##### ` or `###### ` at the start of a line, the slash menu, the block menu, `SetBlockType(RichTextBlockType.Heading4)` | `<h4>` to `<h6>`, `####` to `######` in Markdown |
| Text and highlight color | The toolbar's color button opens a palette of seven colors; `SetTextColor`, `SetHighlight` | `<span data-color="red">`, `<mark data-bg="yellow">` |
| To-do list | `[] ` or `[x] ` at the start of a line, the slash menu, `SetBlockType(RichTextBlockType.TodoList)`; click the checkbox to check it | `<ul data-todo="true"><li data-checked="true">`, `- [x] ` in Markdown |
| Toggle list | The slash menu or the block menu, `SetBlockType(RichTextBlockType.Toggle)`. Click the arrow, press `Ctrl+Enter` or call `ToggleFold()` to fold away the items nested under it; Enter at the end of an open toggle starts a nested item, and `Tab` nests any list item under the toggle above it. Folded items take no room, the caret skips them, and an edit that reaches into them (indenting under the toggle, Delete at its end) opens it | `<ul data-toggle="true"><li data-collapsed="true">`; a plain `- ` item in Markdown |
| Text alignment | `Ctrl+Shift+L`, `Ctrl+Shift+E`, `Ctrl+Shift+R`; `SetAlign` | `data-align="center"` or `"end"` on `p`, headings and quotes |
| `Ctrl+Shift+Up`, `Ctrl+Shift+Down` | Move the block that holds the caret up or down (`Docs` profile) |
| `Ctrl+Enter` on a toggle item | Fold or unfold it (`Docs` profile) |
| Code language | The label above a code block opens a list of languages; `SetCodeLanguage("csharp")`. The code is highlighted in that language (Plain text, or a language without a grammar, stays plain) | `<pre data-lang="csharp">`, a fenced block with an info string in Markdown |
| Callout | The `/` menu or the block menu; the block menu sets its color and icon; `SetCalloutColor`, `SetCalloutIcon`. Enter continues the box, an empty line leaves it | `<aside data-callout="blue" data-icon="💡">`, a GitHub alert (`> [!NOTE]`) in Markdown, which keeps only the five alert kinds |

The colors come from a fixed palette (`RichTextColor`: gray, red, orange, yellow, green, blue and purple) that follows
the theme in light and dark mode, so stored content never holds a raw color value. `Formats` also reports
`IsUnderline`, `IsSuperscript`, `IsSubscript`, `TextColor`, `Highlight`, `Size`, `Align`, `LineSpacing` and `CodeLanguage` for your own toolbar.
A line is as tall as the largest text on it needs, so a large word opens up its whole block.

```xml
<arc:RichTextEditor Profile="Docs" Html="{Binding Body, Mode=TwoWay}" />
```

- **Markdown is lossy for color, size and spacing.** Markdown has none of them, so `GetMarkdown()` keeps the text and drops them. Underline,
  superscript and subscript have no Markdown syntax either; they are written as inline `<u>`, `<sup>` and `<sub>` tags,
  which the `Docs` profile reads back. Store `Html` when the content must keep its colors.
- **Assign `Profile` first or in any order.** Content assigned before the profile is read again under the Docs rules.
- **Your own languages.** The language list ends with a "Custom…" row that takes any name, and `CodeLanguages` replaces the list with your own labels and ids, such as `new RichTextCodeLanguage("Zig", "zig")`. Highlighting needs a grammar for the id; a name without one is kept and shown, and the code stays plain.
- **Task lists from elsewhere import.** Markdown `- [ ]` and `- [x]` items and HTML lists whose items begin with a
  checkbox input become to-do items; in the `Arc` profile they stay plain list items.
- **Nothing else changes.** Dividers, quotes, links, the slash menu and the undo history behave as in the `Arc`
  profile, and a document written by the `Arc` profile loads unchanged.

### Images and tables

The `Docs` profile also stores images and tables. An image is one block that holds an address and a description; a
table is a grid of cells; a new one starts with a header row. Both come in and go out through Markdown (`![alt](src)` on
its own line, pipe tables) and HTML (`img`, `table`). The `Arc` profile keeps both out of the document.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.RichTextEditorImagesAndTablesDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12" MaxWidth="680">
        <Border Padding="24,20"
                CornerRadius="26"
                BorderThickness="1"
                Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Surface}"
                BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Border}">
            <arc:RichTextEditor x:Name="Editor"
                                Profile="Docs"
                                ImageSourceRequested="OnImageSourceRequested" />
        </Border>
        <TextBlock x:Name="Log"
                   TextWrapping="Wrap"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}"
                   Text="Type / and choose Image or Table, paste a screenshot, or drop an image file." />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class RichTextEditorImagesAndTablesDemo : UserControl
{
    private const string Picture = "data:image/png;base64,";

    public RichTextEditorImagesAndTablesDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Editor.Html = $"<h2>Quarterly report</h2><p>Images and tables live in their own blocks.</p><img src=\"{Picture}\" alt=\"A gradient\"><table><colgroup><col width=\"200\"><col width=\"100\"></colgroup><tr><th>Region</th><th data-align=\"end\">Revenue</th></tr><tr><td>North</td><td data-align=\"end\">1,240</td></tr><tr><td>South</td><td data-align=\"end\">980</td></tr><tr><td colspan=\"2\" data-align=\"center\" data-bg=\"gray\">Figures in thousands of euros</td></tr></table><p>Right-click a cell to add or delete rows and columns, color cells or toggle the header row and column; drag across cells to select, copy or merge them, drag a column border to resize it, or drag the grips at the top and left of the table to move columns and rows.</p>";
    }

    // The host decides where a picked, pasted or dropped picture is kept. Here it is "uploaded" to a made-up store;
    // a real app would send the bytes (ReadAllBytesAsync or OpenReadAsync) to its server and return the final address.
    private void OnImageSourceRequested(object? sender, RichTextImageSourceRequestedEventArgs e)
    {
        Log.Text = $"{e.Origin}: {e.FileName ?? "pasted image"} ({e.ContentType}) is stored by the host.";
        e.SourceTask = StoreAsync(e);
    }

    private static async Task<string?> StoreAsync(RichTextImageSourceRequestedEventArgs e)
    {
        var bytes = await e.ReadAllBytesAsync();
        return "data:" + e.ContentType + ";base64," + Convert.ToBase64String(bytes);
    }
}
```

| Feature | How to use it |
|---|---|
| Insert an image | `/` then Image (a file picker), paste an image file or a screenshot, drop image files on the editor, paste a bare image address, type `![alt](address)`, or call `InsertImage(address, alt)` |
| Resize an image | Click it, then drag the grip at its bottom-right corner; the proportions stay, and the width is stored (`width` in HTML; Markdown writes a resized image as an `<img>` tag). |
| Select and remove an image | Click it, then press Backspace or Delete; Backspace at the start of the next paragraph removes it too |
| Insert a table | `/` then Table (3 by 3), or `InsertTable(rows, columns)` |
| Move in a table | Tab and Shift+Tab move between cells (Tab in the last cell adds a row); Enter moves down the column; Up and Down stay in the column |
| Edit rows and columns | Right-click a cell, or call `AddTableRow`, `AddTableColumn`, `DeleteTableRow`, `DeleteTableColumn`, `DeleteTable` |
| Merge and split cells | Drag across the cells, right-click and choose Merge cells, or call `MergeTableCells`; right-click a merged cell and choose Split cell, or call `SplitTableCell`. `CanMergeTableCells` and `CanSplitTableCell` tell your own toolbar whether either applies |
| Resize columns | Drag the border between two columns; double-click it, choose Distribute columns or call `DistributeTableColumns` to share the width evenly again |
| Header row and column | Right-click and toggle Header row or Header column, or call `SetTableHeaderRow` and `SetTableHeaderColumn`; `TableHasHeaderRow` and `TableHasHeaderColumn` read them |
| Color cells | Select the cells, right-click and choose a color, or call `SetTableCellColor`; `TableCellColor` reads the shared color |
| Select cells, rows and columns | Drag from one cell to another to select the rectangle between them; click a grip (top of a column, left of a row) or call `SelectTableRow` and `SelectTableColumn` |
| Move rows and columns | Drag a grip to a new place, right-click and choose Move row up, Move row down, Move column left or Move column right, or call `MoveTableRow` and `MoveTableColumn` (`CanMoveTableRow` and `CanMoveTableColumn` tell your toolbar whether they can) |
| Copy and paste cells | Copy a rectangle to get tab-separated text, which spreadsheets read; paste a table or tab-separated text into a cell to fill cells from there, adding rows and columns as needed |
| Align a column | `Ctrl+Shift+L`, `Ctrl+Shift+E`, `Ctrl+Shift+R` or `SetAlign` aligns the whole column of the caret's cell |

**You decide where pictures live.** The editor never uploads anything. When a person picks, pastes or drops a picture,
it raises `ImageSourceRequested` with the file name, the media type and the bytes (`OpenReadAsync`,
`ReadAllBytesAsync`). Answer with `Source` when you already know the address, or with `SourceTask` while an upload is
in progress; the editor inserts the image when the task finishes, and a task that fails or returns null inserts
nothing. Set `Cancel` to refuse the picture. With no handler the picture is embedded as a `data:` address, which keeps
the document self-contained but large.

```csharp
editor.ImageSourceRequested += (_, e) =>
{
    e.SourceTask = UploadAsync(e.FileName, e.ContentType, e.OpenReadAsync());   // returns the CDN address
};
```

**You can also decide how pictures are loaded.** `ImageLoading` is raised when the editor needs the pixels of an
address. Set `Bitmap` or `StreamTask` to load it yourself, for example from a store that needs a token or from your own
scheme; with no answer the editor reads `data:`, http(s), `avares:` and local file addresses. `ReloadImages()` forgets
what was loaded.

- **Addresses are checked.** Script schemes and `data:` addresses that are not raster images are refused when
  content loads and when an image is inserted; your own schemes (`app://files/1`) pass.
- **Images shrink to the editor's width** and keep their proportions. While a picture loads, or when it fails, a
  placeholder of the same width stands in.
- **Table cells hold inline text**: marks, links and line breaks (Shift+Enter), not lists or nested blocks. Imported
  cells with such content are flattened to lines. Short rows are padded.
- **Merged cells** span several rows and columns, and the texts they join become lines. HTML stores them as `colspan` and `rowspan`. Markdown has no merged cells, so it writes the covered cells empty; keep `Html` when merges must survive. Tab skips the covered cells, and Enter moves below the merged cell.
- **Column widths** are proportions: the table always fills the editor's width, and a column without a width shares what the others leave (at least 48 px). HTML stores widths as `<col width>` and cell colors as `data-bg`, and writes header cells as `th`; a `table` without `th` cells in its first row reads with no header row. Markdown keeps none of these, and its tables always have a header row.
- **A rectangle of selected cells** draws as a block. Deleting or typing empties those cells and never merges them, and pasting fills them from the first one; covered cells are skipped. A selection from the table's first character to its last, or one that runs out of the table, still deletes whole tables.
- **A merged cell holds its rows or columns together**: a row cannot move while a merged cell spans rows through it or across the place it would land, and the same goes for columns. The first row stays the header row whatever moves there.

### The block handle

In the `Docs` profile, hovering a block shows two buttons in a gutter to its left. The grip (⋮⋮) drags the block to a new
place: a line shows where it will land, and a list item takes its nested items along while a table moves whole. A click on
the grip opens the block menu, which turns the block into another type (text, headings, lists, to-do, quote, code) or
duplicates or deletes it. The plus button adds an empty paragraph below and opens the block menu there. From the keyboard,
`Ctrl+Shift+Up` and `Ctrl+Shift+Down` move the block that holds the caret. Every move is one undo step.

The handle is not shown in `IsReadOnly` mode or in the `Arc` profile, which keeps the editor's text flush with its edge.
The gutter is a left margin of 56 px on the writing surface.

### Find and replace

`Ctrl+F` opens a find bar at the top right of the editor, with the selected text (a piece of one line) already in it. Every
match is highlighted as you type and the first one at or after the selection is selected; Enter and Shift+Enter (or `F3`
and `Shift+F3`) step through the rest, and the bar shows where you are ("2 of 5"). `Ctrl+H`, or the bar's replace button,
adds the replace row: Enter in it replaces the current match and moves to the next one, and Replace all changes every match
as one undo step. Escape closes the bar and returns to the text with the last match selected.

- **Matches stay inside one block.** A paragraph, list item, table cell or code block is searched on its own, so a phrase
  broken across two blocks is not found.
- **A replacement takes the style of the text it replaces**: the marks, color and link of the match's first character.
- **Case.** The search ignores case until you turn on Match case.
- **From code**: `OpenFind(replace)`, `CloseFind()`, `IsFindOpen`, `CountMatches(text, matchCase)` and
  `ReplaceAll(text, replacement, matchCase)`, which returns how many it replaced. A read-only editor finds but never replaces.

### Placeholder and block hint

`Placeholder` shows in an empty editor and says what the field is for. `BlockHint` shows on the empty line where the
caret sits and tells the person how to add structure.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.RichTextEditorPlaceholderDemo">
    <Border Padding="24,20"
            CornerRadius="26"
            BorderThickness="1"
            MaxWidth="680"
            Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Surface}"
            BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Border}">
        <arc:RichTextEditor Placeholder="Leave a comment" BlockHint="Type / for blocks" />
    </Border>
</UserControl>
```

Set both when the field is a comment or a note, so the empty state explains the next step. Keep the placeholder
short: it disappears as soon as text is typed, and the hint disappears with it.

### Read only

With `IsReadOnly` set, editing, the toolbar and the shortcuts are off. The text can still be selected and copied,
and assistive technology reads it.

```xml

Use read-only mode for a published article, a postmortem or a signed note that people must be able to quote. Show
an edit action outside the editor that switches `IsReadOnly` back to `False`, so the change is deliberate.

### Content formats

Store the content in the format the consumer reads:

| Format | Read it with | Use it for |
|---|---|---|
| Markdown (`Markdown`, `GetMarkdown()`) | Your Markdown renderer or the editor | Editable text in a pipeline, diffs and version history |
| HTML (`Html`, `GetHtml()`) | A browser or a web view | Pages that render the content directly |
| Plain text (`GetText()`) | Search and previews | One line per block, without marks |

Both `Html` and `Markdown` are sanitized when they are loaded. `SetHtml` and `SetMarkdown` load the text as one undo
step, and assigning the `Html` or `Markdown` property reloads the document only when the value differs from the one
the editor last wrote, so a two-way binding does not reset the caret while the person types.

### Importing existing Markdown

The editor stores a fixed subset, so opening a file written elsewhere can change it. `RichTextEditorMarkdown.Analyze`
reports every construct the editor cannot store, with the line, the column and a reason, without converting anything.
`TrySetMarkdown` imports only a source that loses nothing and leaves the editor untouched when it refuses, so a host can
keep the original file, warn, or open a source editor first.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.RichTextEditorImportCheckDemo">
    <Grid ColumnDefinitions="*,*" ColumnSpacing="20">
        <StackPanel Grid.Column="0" Spacing="12">
            <TextBlock Text="Markdown to import"
                       FontSize="13"
                       FontWeight="SemiBold"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
            <arc:Textarea x:Name="Source"
                          Height="220"
                          AcceptsReturn="True"
                          TextWrapping="Wrap"
                          FontFamily="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource MonoFontFamily}"
                          TextChanged="OnSourceChanged" />
            <WrapPanel ItemSpacing="8" LineSpacing="8">
                <arc:Button Content="Import if lossless"
                            Variant="Primary"
                            Size="Small"
                            Click="OnImportClick" />
                <arc:Button Content="Keep original"
                            Variant="Secondary"
                            Size="Small"
                            Click="OnKeepClick" />
            </WrapPanel>
            <TextBlock x:Name="Status"
                       Text="No issues: this source imports as written."
                       FontSize="13"
                       TextWrapping="Wrap"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
        </StackPanel>
        <StackPanel Grid.Column="1" Spacing="12">
            <TextBlock Text="Editor"
                       FontSize="13"
                       FontWeight="SemiBold"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
            <arc:RichTextEditor x:Name="Editor" Height="220" />
        </StackPanel>
    </Grid>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

/// <summary>
/// An import gate: <c>Analyze</c> reports what the editor cannot store, and <c>TrySetMarkdown</c> refuses a lossy
/// source, so the host can keep the original file or warn before it writes anything back.
/// </summary>
public partial class RichTextEditorImportCheckDemo : UserControl
{
    private const string Lossy = """
        #### A fourth level heading

        ```csharp
        var count = 3;
        ```

        | Step | Call |
        |------|------|
        | Start | `Append` |
        """;

    public RichTextEditorImportCheckDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Source.Text = Lossy;
        Editor.Markdown = "An editor keeps its content until an import succeeds.";
        Update(Lossy);
    }

    private void OnSourceChanged(object? sender, TextChangedEventArgs e) => Update(Source.Text);

    private void OnImportClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        if (Editor.TrySetMarkdown(Source.Text, out var report))
        {
            Status.Text = report.IsEmpty
                ? "Imported as written."
                : $"Imported; {report.Issues.Count} construct(s) written back in canonical form.";
            return;
        }
        Status.Text = $"Import refused; the editor kept its content. {Describe(report)}";
    }

    private void OnKeepClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
        => Status.Text = "The source is kept as it is; nothing was imported.";

    private void Update(string? markdown)
    {
        var report = RichTextEditorMarkdown.Analyze(markdown);
        Status.Text = report.IsEmpty ? "No issues: this source imports as written." : Describe(report);
    }

    private static string Describe(RichTextImportReport report)
    {
        var losses = report.Issues.Count(i => i.Severity == RichTextImportSeverity.Lossy);
        var first = report.Issues[0];
        var summary = losses > 0 ? $"{losses} loss(es) and " : string.Empty;
        return $"{summary}{report.Issues.Count - losses} normalization(s). First: line {first.Line}, {first.Reason}";
    }
}
```

```csharp
if (!editor.TrySetMarkdown(fileText, out var report))
{
    Warn($"{report.Issues.Count} constructs would be lost; the file is unchanged.");
    foreach (var issue in report.Issues.Where(i => i.Severity == RichTextImportSeverity.Lossy))
    {
        Warn($"Line {issue.Line}, column {issue.Column}: {issue.Reason}");
    }
}
```

| Reported as a loss | Why |
|---|---|
| Heading level 4 to 6 (`Arc` profile) | The `Arc` profile has three heading levels; they become Heading 3 |
| A code fence's info string | The editor does not store a code block's language |
| A tilde fence | The editor reads only backtick fences |
| A table | Kept by the `Docs` profile; in the `Arc` profile the cells become one paragraph |
| A setext heading | The editor reads only `#` headings |
| Indented code | The editor reads only fenced code |
| A list starting above 1 | The editor numbers lists from 1 |
| A hard line break, block HTML, an image inside a line of text (or any image in the `Arc` profile), a reference link, a footnote, a backslash escape | The editor keeps the source as text |

Markers written another way are reported as `RichTextImportSeverity.Normalized` and do not block the import: `*` and
`+` bullets, `1)` numbering, `__bold__`, `*italic*` and `***` dividers are written back as `-`, `1.`, `**`, `_` and
`---`. Everything in the supported subset produces no issue at all. The permissive path is unchanged: `Markdown`,
`SetMarkdown` and a pasted Markdown-looking text still convert as before, and only callers that opt in to
`TrySetMarkdown` get the gate.

### Reading the content

`ContentChanged` runs after every edit, undo, redo and load. Its `Value` is a `RichTextValue`, and the HTML, Markdown
and text are computed when they are first read. `GetHtml()`, `GetMarkdown()` and `GetText()` read the content at any
time and are always synchronous.

| Member of `RichTextValue` | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `Html` | `string` | The content as clean HTML |
| `Markdown` | `string` | The content as Markdown |
| `Text` | `string` | Plain text, one line per block |
| `IsEmpty` | `bool` | True when the document has no text |

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.RichTextEditorMarkdownAndHtmlDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="16">
        <Border Padding="24,20"
                CornerRadius="26"
                BorderThickness="1"
                MaxWidth="680"
                Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Surface}"
                BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Border}">
            <arc:RichTextEditor x:Name="Editor" ContentChanged="OnContentChanged" />
        </Border>
        <TextBlock Text="Markdown"
                   FontSize="12"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
        <TextBlock x:Name="MarkdownText"
                   FontSize="13"
                   FontFamily="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource MonoFontFamily}"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}"
                   TextWrapping="Wrap" />
        <TextBlock Text="HTML"
                   FontSize="12"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
        <TextBlock x:Name="HtmlText"
                   FontSize="13"
                   FontFamily="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource MonoFontFamily}"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}"
                   TextWrapping="Wrap" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class RichTextEditorMarkdownAndHtmlDemo : UserControl
{
    public RichTextEditorMarkdownAndHtmlDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Editor.Html = """<h2>From HTML</h2><p>Pasted <b>bold</b>, <span style="font-style:italic">styled spans</span> and <a href="https://uiarc.dev">links</a> are cleaned up.</p><ul><li>Lists nest<ul><li>like this</li></ul></li></ul>""";
        MarkdownText.Text = Editor.GetMarkdown();
        HtmlText.Text = Editor.GetHtml();
    }

    private void OnContentChanged(object? sender, RichTextContentChangedEventArgs e)
    {
        MarkdownText.Text = e.Value.Markdown;
        HtmlText.Text = e.Value.Html;
    }
}
```

```csharp
editor.ContentChanged += (_, e) =>
{
    draft.Markdown = e.Value.Markdown;
    canPost = !e.Value.IsEmpty;
};

var html = editor.GetHtml();
```

### Your own toolbar

`Formats` (a `RichTextFormats` record) reports the marks, the link and the block type at the caret. `CanUndo` and
`CanRedo` report the history. Use them to set the state of your own buttons, and call `ToggleMark`, `SetBlockType`,
`SetLink` and `EditLink` to act on the selection.

Bind `UndoCommand` and `RedoCommand` to buttons, or call `Undo()` and `Redo()` directly. The toolbar buttons should
not take focus, so the editor keeps the caret; the demo sets `Focusable="False"` on each button for that reason.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.RichTextEditorOwnToolbarDemo">
    <Border Padding="24,20"
            CornerRadius="26"
            BorderThickness="1"
            MaxWidth="680"
            Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Surface}"
            BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Border}">
        <StackPanel Spacing="16">
            <WrapPanel x:Name="Toolbar" ItemSpacing="2" LineSpacing="4">
                <WrapPanel.Styles>
                    <Style Selector="arc|Button.tool">
                        <Setter Property="Variant" Value="Ghost" />
                        <Setter Property="Size" Value="Small" />
                        <Setter Property="Width" Value="36" />
                        <Setter Property="Padding" Value="0" />
                        <!-- The editor keeps the caret: these buttons never take focus. -->
                        <Setter Property="Focusable" Value="False" />
                    </Style>
                </WrapPanel.Styles>
                <arc:Button Classes="tool"
                            Tag="{x:Static arc:RichTextMark.Bold}"
                            arc:Tooltip.Tip="Bold"
                            AutomationProperties.Name="Bold"
                            Click="OnMarkClick">
                    <arc:ArcGlyph Data="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Bold}" />
                </arc:Button>
                <arc:Button Classes="tool"
                            Tag="{x:Static arc:RichTextMark.Italic}"
                            arc:Tooltip.Tip="Italic"
                            AutomationProperties.Name="Italic"
                            Click="OnMarkClick">
                    <arc:ArcGlyph Data="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Italic}" />
                </arc:Button>
                <arc:Button Classes="tool"
                            Tag="{x:Static arc:RichTextMark.Strikethrough}"
                            arc:Tooltip.Tip="Strikethrough"
                            AutomationProperties.Name="Strikethrough"
                            Click="OnMarkClick">
                    <arc:ArcGlyph Data="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Strikethrough}" />
                </arc:Button>
                <arc:Button Classes="tool"
                            Tag="{x:Static arc:RichTextMark.Code}"
                            arc:Tooltip.Tip="Inline code"
                            AutomationProperties.Name="Inline code"
                            Click="OnMarkClick">
                    <arc:ArcGlyph Data="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Code}" />
                </arc:Button>
                <arc:Button Classes="tool"
                            x:Name="LinkButton"
                            arc:Tooltip.Tip="Link"
                            AutomationProperties.Name="Link"
                            Click="OnLinkClick">
                    <arc:ArcGlyph Data="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Link}" />
                </arc:Button>
                <Border Width="1"
                        Height="20"
