```cs
using Avalonia;
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class RichTextEditorOwnToolbarDemo : UserControl
{
    public RichTextEditorOwnToolbarDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Editor.PropertyChanged += OnEditorPropertyChanged;
        Refresh();
    }

    private void OnMarkClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        if (sender is Button { Tag: RichTextMark mark })
        {
            Editor.ToggleMark(mark);
        }
    }

    private void OnBlockClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        if (sender is Button { Tag: RichTextBlockType type })
        {
            Editor.SetBlockType(type);
        }
    }

    private void OnLinkClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) => Editor.EditLink();

    private void OnUndoClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) => Editor.Undo();

    private void OnRedoClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) => Editor.Redo();

    private void OnEditorPropertyChanged(object? sender, AvaloniaPropertyChangedEventArgs e)
    {
        if (e.Property == RichTextEditor.FormatsProperty
            || e.Property == RichTextEditor.CanUndoProperty
            || e.Property == RichTextEditor.CanRedoProperty)
        {
            Refresh();
        }
    }

    // Shows what is active at the caret, and which history buttons have something to do.
    private void Refresh()
    {
        var formats = Editor.Formats;
        foreach (var button in Toolbar.Children.OfType<Button>())
        {
            button.Variant = IsActive(button, formats) ? ButtonVariant.Secondary : ButtonVariant.Ghost;
        }
        UndoButton.IsEnabled = Editor.CanUndo;
        RedoButton.IsEnabled = Editor.CanRedo;
    }

    private bool IsActive(Button button, RichTextFormats formats)
        => button == LinkButton
            ? formats.Link is not null
            : button.Tag switch
            {
                RichTextMark.Bold => formats.IsBold,
                RichTextMark.Italic => formats.IsItalic,
                RichTextMark.Strikethrough => formats.IsStrikethrough,
                RichTextMark.Code => formats.IsCode,
                RichTextBlockType type => formats.BlockType == type,
                _ => false
            };
}
```

### Binding to a view model

In an MVVM app the view model owns the document. Bind `Markdown` two-way, read `IsEmpty` from `ContentChanged`, and
use the undo and redo commands from the view.

```csharp
public partial class ReleaseNoteViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    private readonly IReleaseNotes _notes;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private string? _bodyMarkdown;

    [ObservableProperty]
    [NotifyCanExecuteChangedFor(nameof(PublishCommand))]
    private bool _hasContent;

    public ReleaseNoteViewModel(IReleaseNotes notes) => _notes = notes;

    [RelayCommand(CanExecute = nameof(CanPublish))]
    private async Task PublishAsync()
    {
        await _notes.PublishAsync(BodyMarkdown ?? string.Empty);
    }

    private bool CanPublish() => HasContent;
}
```

```xml
<StackPanel Spacing="16">
    <arc:RichTextEditor x:Name="Editor"
                        Markdown="{Binding BodyMarkdown, Mode=TwoWay}"
                        Placeholder="Describe the release" />
    <arc:Button Content="Publish notes"
                Command="{Binding PublishCommand}"
                IsDefault="True" />
</StackPanel>
```

```csharp
// Code behind: the editor reports emptiness through ContentChanged; vm is the view's ReleaseNoteViewModel.
Editor.ContentChanged += (_, args) => vm.HasContent = !args.Value.IsEmpty;
```

- `Markdown` (and `Html`) is two-way: the view model receives every edit, and the editor reloads when the view model
  sets a different value. For a long document the value follows the typing after a short pause (see the performance
  section), so read `GetMarkdown()` in the publish command rather than trusting a cached copy.
- `Placeholder` and `BlockHint` are one-way; `IsReadOnly` is one-way and typically follows a published state.
- `UndoCommand` and `RedoCommand` are commands for your own toolbar. `CanUndo` and `CanRedo` are read-only and raise
  change notifications.
- `ContentChanged` is the event to listen to for emptiness, counts or autosave. Use `Value` inside the handler; the
  HTML and Markdown are computed the first time they are read.

### Undo and history

The editor keeps its own history of up to 300 steps, separate from the platform's undo. Typing within one second
merges into one step; a space or a change of input type starts a new one, and each command (a mark, a block type, a
link) is one step. `SetHtml`, `SetMarkdown` and `Clear` are one step each, so a load can be undone. Setting the
`Markdown` or `Html` property while the editor starts up does not enter the history.

### Long documents and performance

The editor redraws only the blocks that changed, and it draws only the part of the document in and near the
viewport. The HTML and Markdown values are written after every edit while the document has up to 400 blocks. Longer
documents write them once the person pauses for about 250 milliseconds, or when the editor loses focus or is
removed. In a 5,000-block document the serialization waits for the pause, so typing stays cheap.

`GetHtml()`, `GetMarkdown()` and `GetText()` always serialize the current document, so call them when you save and
not on every keystroke.

### Example: release notes draft

A release manager writes the notes for a version of a developer tool. The placeholder tells the author what goes
here, the body already has a heading, a list, a bold phrase and a quote for the known issue, and the publish button
sits beneath it at the default size. The text in the editor is the same Markdown the release pipeline stores.

![A release notes draft with a heading, bold and list text, and a quoted known issue](https://docs.tkcode.si/shots/Docs/Editors/RichTextEditor/images/ReleaseNotes.webp)

```xml
<StackPanel Width="640" Spacing="16">
    <TextBlock Text="Release notes"
               FontSize="18"
               FontWeight="SemiBold"
               Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
    <Border Padding="24,20"
            CornerRadius="26"
            BorderThickness="1"
            Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Surface}"
            BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Border}">
        <arc:RichTextEditor Markdown="## Acme Analytics 4.2&#10;&#10;- Dashboards load **twice as fast**&#10;- Export charts as _PNG_ from the menu&#10;&#10;> Known issue: CSV exports above 500 MB can time out." />
    </Border>
    <StackPanel Orientation="Horizontal" Spacing="8" HorizontalAlignment="Right">
        <arc:Button Content="Discard" Variant="Secondary" />
        <arc:Button Content="Publish notes" />
    </StackPanel>
</StackPanel>
```

### Content guidelines

- **Placeholder**: name the content the field holds and what to write: "Describe the release", not "Enter text".
- **Block hint**: name the one gesture that matters, such as "Type / for blocks". Do not list every shortcut.
- **Buttons**: use a verb and an object in sentence case: "Publish notes", "Save draft". Avoid "Submit" for a note
  that is published, because the person expects the text to go live.
- **Link text**: write the words the person reads, and keep the URL in the link field, not in the sentence.
- **Headings**: keep them short and in sentence case, and use `Heading2` for a section inside a document with a
  title outside the editor.

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| Enter text here | Describe the release |
| Click here | Read the migration guide |
| Submit | Publish notes |
| Type /// for blocks | Type / for blocks |

### Best practices

**Do**

- Set `Placeholder` and `BlockHint` for every empty field, so the first line explains the editor.
- Save `Markdown` when the content is edited again, and `Html` when another page only renders it. The two are equal
  for the supported subset, so pick one as the source of truth.
- Read the content with `GetMarkdown()` or `GetHtml()` in the save command. A handler on `ContentChanged` is right for
  emptiness and counts, not for every write.
- Switch to `IsReadOnly` for a published document, and offer an explicit edit action that turns it back on.
- Keep the toolbar buttons out of the tab order when they act on the selection, as the own-toolbar demo does, so the
  caret stays in the text.

**Avoid**

- Storing HTML from another editor and expecting its styling to survive. The loader keeps only the editor's subset,
  so unknown tags and inline styles are dropped and the layout changes.
- Using images and tables in the `Arc` profile. Only the `Docs` profile stores them, so the content loses them on
  the next save.
- Reading `GetHtml()` on every keystroke in a long document. Serialization on each key costs more than the edit.
- Replacing the document you are editing by assigning `Markdown` on each change. Use `SetMarkdown()` or `Clear()`,
  which are one undo step each, so the person can undo a replacement.
- Expecting screen reader users to navigate the text by character, word or line. Assistive technology reads the
  whole document as one value, so offer `GetText()` output for review when the text is long.

### Common questions

**Why does Ctrl+U (Cmd+U on macOS) do nothing?** In the default `Arc` profile underline is not part of the editor's subset. The key is
swallowed, so the text does not change, and the Markdown output has no underline syntax either. Set
`Profile="Docs"` to make `Ctrl+U` underline the selection.

**How do I add or change a link from code?** Call `SetLink(url)` to link the selection, or the link at the caret.
Pass `null` or an empty string to remove the link. `EditLink()` opens the same link field the toolbar uses, for the
selection or the link at the caret. Ctrl+K (Cmd+K on macOS) does the same from the keyboard.

**Why did my bound `Html` not reload when I set the same HTML again?** The editor reloads only when the value differs
from the one it last wrote. A two-way binding that echoes the editor's own output therefore does not move the caret.
To force a reload with identical content, call `SetHtml` or `SetMarkdown` instead.

**Why does a shortcut not convert text inside a code block?** Code blocks hold plain text only. Shortcuts such as
`# ` and `**` are off there, and Tab inserts two spaces instead of changing the list level.

**How do I start a new line inside a list item or a quote?** Press Shift+Enter for a line break in the same block.
Press Enter on an empty list item or quote to leave the list, and press Enter twice at the end of a code block to
leave it.

## API reference

### RichTextEditor

Arc's light rich text editor: Markdown shortcuts as you type, a floating selection toolbar that morphs into a link field, a slash menu for blocks, its own undo history, and HTML plus Markdown output. Blocks are paragraphs, three heading levels, nested bulleted and numbered lists, quotes, code blocks and dividers; inline marks are bold, italic, strikethrough, inline code and links. The `Docs` profile adds images and tables: `ImageSourceRequested` lets the host decide where a picked, pasted or dropped picture is kept, and `ImageLoading` lets it load the pictures itself.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Html` | `string?` | `null` | The content as HTML (two-way). Assigning reloads the editor only when the value differs from what it last wrote. |
| `Markdown` | `string?` | `null` | The content as Markdown (two-way): Arc's `defaultMarkdown`, kept in sync after every edit. |
| `Placeholder` | `string` | `"Start writing"` | Shown while the document is empty (default "Start writing"). |
| `BlockHint` | `string` | `"Type / for blocks"` | The quiet hint on an empty line holding the caret (default "Type / for blocks"). |
| `Profile` | `RichTextEditorProfile` | `Arc` | The feature set: `Arc` (the default) keeps Arc's blocks and marks; `Docs` adds underline, text and highlight colors, to-do lists, text alignment and a language label on code blocks. |
| `IsReadOnly` | `bool` | `false` | Turns off editing, the toolbar and the shortcuts; text can still be selected and copied. |
| `IsAutoFocusEnabled` | `bool` | `false` | Focuses the editor when it loads and puts the caret at the end (Arc's `autoFocus`). |
| `CanUndo` | `bool` | – | *Read-only.* True when there is a step to undo (Arc's `onHistoryChange`). |
| `CanRedo` | `bool` | – | *Read-only.* True when there is a step to redo. |
| `IsDocumentEmpty` | `bool` | – | *Read-only.* True when there is no text and no divider. |
| `Formats` | `RichTextFormats` | – | *Read-only.* The formatting at the selection, for your own toolbar's pressed states. |
| `CodeLanguages` | `IReadOnlyList<RichTextCodeLanguage>?` | `null` | The languages offered by the code block's language list, each a label and the id that is stored and highlighted. A "Custom…" row always lets the person type any other name. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ContentChanged` | `RichTextContentChangedEventArgs` | Raised after every edit, undo, redo and load (Arc's `onChange`). |
| `ImageSourceRequested` | `RichTextImageSourceRequestedEventArgs` | Raised when the editor holds a picture the user picked, pasted or dropped and the document must point at it. Set `Source` or `SourceTask` to keep the file where you want (upload it, copy it into your store); with no answer the picture is embedded as a `data:` address. |
| `ImageLoading` | `RichTextImageLoadingEventArgs` | Raised when the editor needs the pixels of an image's address. Set `Bitmap` or `StreamTask` to load it yourself; with no answer `data:`, http(s), `avares:` and file addresses are read by the editor. |

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

## Accessibility

- The writing surface is a multi-line editable text control named "Editor" by default. Set
  `AutomationProperties.Name` to name it for your form, such as "Release notes body".
- Keyboard (Cmd on macOS): `Ctrl+B`, `Ctrl+I`, `Ctrl+Shift+X` and `Ctrl+E` apply marks, and `Ctrl+K` edits a link. `Ctrl+Z` and
  `Ctrl+Shift+Z` undo and redo. `Alt+F10` moves focus into the floating toolbar, and `Escape` returns it to the text.
- Editing results such as "Formatted", "Link added", "Link removed", "Undone", "Redone" and "Numbered list added" are
  announced politely, so they do not interrupt speech.
- The floating toolbar is a toolbar, and its format buttons are toggle buttons that report their state. Their
  tooltips show the keyboard shortcut.
- The block menu is a list. Moving through it announces the current item.
- Limitation: the editor does not expose character, word or line navigation to screen readers. They read the whole
  text as one value.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Ctrl+B`, `Ctrl+I` | Toggle bold, italic |
| `Ctrl+Shift+X` | Toggle strikethrough |
| `Ctrl+E` | Toggle inline code, within one block |
| `Ctrl+K` | Open the link field for the selection or the link at the caret; `Enter` applies it, `Escape` closes it |
| `Ctrl+F`, `Ctrl+H` | Open the find bar, or the find bar with its replace row |
| `F3`, `Shift+F3` | Next and previous match while the find bar is open (`Enter` and `Shift+Enter` in its search field) |
| `Ctrl+U` | Toggle underline (`Docs` profile) |
| `Ctrl+.`, `Ctrl+,` | Toggle superscript, subscript (`Docs` profile) |
| `Ctrl+Shift+L`, `Ctrl+Shift+E`, `Ctrl+Shift+R` | Align left, center, right (`Docs` profile) |
| `Ctrl+Z`, `Ctrl+Shift+Z` (or `Ctrl+Y`) | Undo, redo |
| `Ctrl+A` | Select all |
| `Enter` | New block; leaves an empty list item or quote; twice at the end of a code block leaves the code |
| `Shift+Enter` | Line break inside the block |
| `Tab`, `Shift+Tab` | Indent or outdent a list item; in a code block, `Tab` inserts two spaces |
| `Backspace` at the start of a block | Turns a heading, quote, code block or list item into a paragraph, or outdents it; after a divider, deletes the divider |
| `/` at the start of a line or after a space | Opens the block menu; typing filters it, `Up` and `Down` move, `Enter` or `Tab` choose, `Escape` closes |
| `Alt+F10` | Moves focus into the floating toolbar; `Left` and `Right` move between its buttons, `Escape` returns to the text |

Ctrl is Command on macOS and Control on other platforms. Word movement follows the platform's text navigation
(Option on macOS, Control elsewhere). `Ctrl+U` is swallowed in the `Arc` profile because it has no underline; the `Docs` profile underlines with it.

## Motion

- The floating toolbar glides to follow the selection with a small bounce. When it changes between the format buttons
  and the link field, its size morphs, and the two faces slide past each other in opposite directions.
- The block menu opens from the `/` position. Its highlight glides between rows, and its height changes on a smooth
  spring when the filter changes the list.
- Reduced motion moves and resizes the toolbar in one step and cross-fades its two faces. The block menu only fades
  in and out, without scaling or moving.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| The toolbar follows a new selection | Glides to the new position with a small bounce | Jumps to the position | Immediate |
| The toolbar changes to or from the link field | Size morphs, faces slide past each other | Instant position and size; faces cross-fade | Immediate |
| The block menu opens | Pops out from the `/` position | Fades in | Immediate |
| The block menu's highlight moves | Glides between rows | Moves in one step | Immediate |
| The menu's list changes while filtering | Height changes on a smooth spring | Immediate | Immediate |

## Related

- `Textarea` for plain text without formatting.
- `MentionInput` for text that mentions people or tags.
- `CodeBlock` for displaying code rather than writing it.
- `FileDropzone` for images and files that accompany the text.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `Textarea` | The text is plain and runs over several lines, with no bold, lists or blocks |
| `MentionInput` | The text mentions people, and the mention must be suggested and stored |
| `InlineEdit` | A single title or name is renamed where it is shown |
| `CodeBlock` | The code is displayed, copied or read, not written |
| `FileDropzone` | Images or files accompany the text and must be uploaded |
| `Input` | The value is one line in a form, such as a subject or a title |

# Signature pad

> Smooth ink that thins with speed, with undo, replay, and PNG or SVG export.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/signature-pad

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.SignaturePadSignDemo">
    <arc:SignaturePad Signer="Ada Lovelace" MaxWidth="560" />
</UserControl>
```

## When to use

`SignaturePad` captures a hand-drawn signature for a document that a person must sign in the app. It draws the ink
on a pad with its own toolbar (color, nib, undo, redo, replay, clear and export), keeps the strokes so the signature
can be reviewed and corrected, and exports the result as an image or a vector file that the record keeps.

- **Order forms and contracts in a sales or billing console**: a customer signs the order form on a tablet at the
  end of a call. The ink is exported as a PNG and filed with the signer's name, which the form stores separately.
- **Delivery confirmations in a logistics app**: a driver signs for a parcel on a handheld screen. The signature is
  saved as a PNG on the shipment record, and a fine nib keeps the ink legible on a small pad.
- **Consent forms in a clinic or patient intake app**: a patient signs a treatment consent. An SVG export stays sharp
  when the form is printed at any size.
- **Acknowledgments in a fintech onboarding flow**: a customer signs a disclosure, and the strokes are stored with the
  account so the same signature can be shown again with `Reset`.
- **Field service sign-off**: a technician signs the work order and corrects a stroke with undo before the record is
  closed.

## When not to use

- **A typed name is enough**: use `Input`, which holds the name as text and needs no drawing.
- **A deliberate confirmation with no signature to keep**: use `HoldToConfirm`, which requires a press and hold and
  records only the decision.
- **A signed file that already exists**: use `FileDropzone` to attach the file, such as a PDF returned by a signing
  service.
- **A yes or no acceptance of terms**: use `Checkbox` with the terms linked nearby. A drawn signature adds a step that
  the terms do not need.
- **A long note or a document body**: use `RichTextEditor`, which edits text and does not capture a signature.

## Usage

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:SignaturePad Signer="Ada Lovelace"
                      Hint="Sign here" />
</UserControl>
```

`SignaturePad` derives from `TemplatedControl` and draws its ink itself, so it is not a text box and has no caret or
text. The ink lives in pad units, a 600 by 260 coordinate space, and the pad scales that space to its width. The
strokes are plain data (`InkStroke` records with their points, color, nib and start time), which is why the same
signature can be exported, stored and replayed without a bitmap of the screen.

### Anatomy

1. **Pad**: the drawing canvas. It keeps a 600 to 260 aspect ratio at every width, so a pad 560 px wide
   is about 243 px high. It has rounded corners on the panel radius and a 1.5 px dashed baseline that runs from 7%
   to 93% of the width at 72% of the height. An X marks the signing line.
2. **Hint** (`Hint`, default "Sign here"): the large hint text on the baseline, shown until the first stroke. It fades
   out when drawing starts and returns after a clear.
3. **Signer** (`Signer`): the name printed under the baseline, in the extra-small text size. It is drawn on the pad
   only; the exports contain the ink, so store the name with the record.
4. **Ink**: the strokes. The black ink follows the foreground color, and the blue and violet inks are theme values
   that change with light and dark mode. Exports use fixed print colors, so a PNG is the same in either theme.
5. **Color group**: three 36 px options (`Black`, `Blue`, `Violet`) in a single-choice group.
6. **Nib group**: three 36 px options (`Fine`, `Medium`, `Bold`). The toolbar splits into two groups aligned at each end and wraps when it is narrow.
7. **Actions**: undo, redo and replay as 36 px pill icon buttons (replay swaps its icon to stop while it runs), then
   the export buttons (PNG and SVG) under a "Save as" label, and the clear button. After a successful export the export button shows "Saved"
   for a short time.
8. **Status**: a live region that announces each change, such as "Undone" or "Signature cleared. Undo
   brings it back."

### Ink color and nib

`InkColor` (default `Black`) and `InkWidth` (default `Medium`) set the defaults for new strokes. Each stroke keeps the
color and nib it was drawn with, so changing the choice later does not repaint earlier strokes.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.SignaturePadInkAndNibDemo">
    <arc:SignaturePad InkColor="Blue"
                      InkWidth="Bold"
                      Hint="Sign in blue"
                      MaxWidth="560" />
</UserControl>
```

Use black for a signature that will be printed or filed as a contract. A blue or violet ink helps a second signer
or a witness stand apart on the same page. Use `Fine` for a small pad on a handheld, `Medium` for most forms, and
`Bold` for a kiosk where a finger draws on a large screen. The nib sets the width in pad units (3.4, 5.6 and 8.4),
so a bold stroke stays proportional on a small pad.

Pen pressure sets the width of the ink when the device reports it. A mouse or a finger has no pressure, so the pad
simulates it from the speed of the stroke: a fast stroke is thin and a slow one is full.

### Reading the strokes

`StrokesChanged` runs after every stroke and after undo, redo, clear and reset. `Strokes` is read-only and holds the
strokes in pad units. `IsEmpty` is true before the first stroke and after a clear, and `CanUndo` and `CanRedo`
report the history.

```csharp
pad.StrokesChanged += (_, e) =>
{
    saveButton.IsEnabled = e.Strokes.Count > 0;
};
```

Each `InkStroke` has an `Id`, a list of `InkPoint` values (`X`, `Y`, `Pressure` from 0 to 1 or -1 for no pressure,
and `Time` in milliseconds from the stroke's start), a `Color`, a `Width` and `At`, the time the stroke began.

### Export

`ExportPng` and `ExportSvg` return the ink cropped to its bounds. `ExportPng` takes an optional `scale` (default 3)
that multiplies the pad's resolution, and `ExportBitmap` returns the same picture as a `RenderTargetBitmap` for a
preview. `SaveAsync` opens the system save dialog with `FileName` (default "signature") as the suggested name. It
returns `false` when the person cancels, when there are no strokes, or when the write fails.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.SignaturePadUseTheSignatureDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="16" MaxWidth="560">
        <arc:SignaturePad x:Name="Pad"
                          Signer="Signed in the gallery"
                          FileName="gallery-signature"
                          StrokesChanged="OnStrokesChanged" />
        <TextBlock x:Name="Status"
                   Text="Draw to see the exported image."
                   FontSize="13"
                   TextWrapping="Wrap"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
        <Image x:Name="Preview"
               Height="64"
               Stretch="Uniform"
               HorizontalAlignment="Left" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class SignaturePadUseTheSignatureDemo : UserControl
{
    public SignaturePadUseTheSignatureDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
    }

    private void OnStrokesChanged(object? sender, SignatureStrokesChangedEventArgs e)
    {
        var previous = Preview.Source as IDisposable;
        if (e.Strokes.Count == 0)
        {
            Preview.Source = null;
            Status.Text = "Draw to see the exported image.";
        }
        else
        {
            Preview.Source = Pad.ExportBitmap(2);
            Status.Text = $"{e.Strokes.Count} {(e.Strokes.Count == 1 ? "stroke" : "strokes")} · SVG {Pad.ExportSvg().Length / 1024.0:0.0} KB";
        }
        previous?.Dispose();
    }
}
```

```csharp
var png = pad.ExportPng();
var svg = pad.ExportSvg();

var saved = await pad.SaveAsync(SignatureFileKind.Png);
```

`ExportSvg` returns an empty string when there are no strokes, so check `IsEmpty` before you store an export. Use
`SignatureFileKind.Svg` for print and `SignatureFileKind.Png` for an email or a PDF page.

### Storing and restoring a signature

`Reset` replaces the strokes without the wipe animation and clears the undo history, so a signature loaded from
storage is not treated as an edit. Pass the strokes you stored earlier to show them again, or call it with no argument
to start over.

```csharp
// Store: the strokes are plain records, so any serializer works. Use your app's options, and a source-generated
// context when the app is trimmed or published as AOT.
var json = JsonSerializer.Serialize(pad.Strokes);

// Restore: the pad shows the saved ink with an empty history.
pad.Reset(JsonSerializer.Deserialize<List<InkStroke>>(json));
```

The stored strokes keep their pad units, so a signature saved from a 560 px pad shows correctly on a 400 px pad.

### Binding to a view model

The signature is a value that the view model stores, and the pad only captures it. Read the strokes with
`StrokesChanged`, because `Strokes` is read-only and cannot be bound back. `Signer`, `Hint`, `InkColor` and `InkWidth`
are one-way settings; the view model sets them, and the pad does not write them back.

```csharp
public partial class SignOffViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    private readonly ISignatureStore _store;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private string _signerName = string.Empty;

    [ObservableProperty]
    [NotifyCanExecuteChangedFor(nameof(SubmitCommand))]
    private bool _hasSignature;

    public IReadOnlyList<InkStroke> Strokes { get; private set; } = Array.Empty<InkStroke>();

    public SignOffViewModel(ISignatureStore store) => _store = store;

    public void OnStrokesChanged(IReadOnlyList<InkStroke> strokes)
    {
        Strokes = strokes;
        HasSignature = strokes.Count > 0;
    }

    [RelayCommand(CanExecute = nameof(HasSignature))]
    private async Task SubmitAsync()
    {
        await _store.SaveAsync(SignerName, Strokes);
    }
}
```

```xml
<StackPanel Spacing="16">
    <arc:Input Label="Printed name" Text="{Binding SignerName, Mode=TwoWay}" />
    <arc:SignaturePad x:Name="Pad"
                      Signer="{Binding SignerName}"
                      Hint="Sign to accept the order" />
    <arc:Button Content="Accept and sign"
                Command="{Binding SubmitCommand}"
                IsDefault="True" />
</StackPanel>
```

```csharp
// Code behind: the view connects the pad's events to the view model.
Pad.StrokesChanged += (_, args) => vm.OnStrokesChanged(args.Strokes);
```

- `Signer` is one-way: the printed name follows the name field as the person types. Changing the name does not clear
  the strokes.
- `StrokesChanged` is the event to listen to; `IsEmpty`, `CanUndo` and `CanRedo` are read-only and update the
  view's state.
- The pad has no command for submit. Use the view model's command and the pad's `IsEmpty` or the `HasSignature`
  flag for the enabled state.

### Validation

A signature is checked when the person submits, and the pad's hint stays visible while it is empty.

| Rule | When to check | Where it shows |
|---|---|---|
| A signature exists | On submit | The form's own message; the pad's hint stays visible while it is empty |
| The printed name is filled in | On submit, or on leaving the name field | The name field's error row, from the form's own rule |
| A stored signature is shown again | When the record opens | `Reset` with the stored strokes, which adds no undo step |

These rules belong to the form, not to the pad, so the messages use the form's own components. Keep the submit
button enabled while the form is open, and show the empty-signature message after a press. Disabling it until the
pad has ink gives the person no reason for the state.

### Example: order form acceptance

A customer signs an order form at the end of a sales call. The title and the one-sentence summary say what is being
accepted, the pad's hint repeats the action in plain words, and the signer name is printed under the line so the
customer can see whose signature the line is for. The pad has no strokes in this scene because it is shown before
the customer signs.

![An order form with a summary, an empty signature pad with a hint and a printed signer name](https://docs.tkcode.si/shots/Docs/Editors/SignaturePad/images/OrderFormSignature.webp)

```xml
<StackPanel Width="640" Spacing="16">
    <TextBlock Text="Accept order form"
               FontSize="18"
               FontWeight="SemiBold"
               Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
    <TextBlock Text="Northwind Logistics agrees to the 12-month Analytics Pro plan at 4,800 USD per month, billed quarterly."
               TextWrapping="Wrap"
               Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
    <arc:SignaturePad Signer="Maya Chen, Head of Finance"
                      Hint="Sign to accept the order" />
    <arc:Button Content="Accept and sign" />
</StackPanel>
```

### Content guidelines

- **Hint**: state the action in plain words, such as "Sign to accept the order". Avoid "Signature here" because the
  person does not know what the signature accepts.
- **Signer**: print the legal name and the role, such as "Maya Chen, Head of Finance", and store the same text with
  the record, since the exported ink does not contain it.
- **Submit button**: use a verb and an object: "Accept and sign", "Sign agreement". Avoid "Done", which does not say
  what is being committed.
- **Status messages**: say what changed and what can be done next, such as "Signature cleared. Undo brings it back."

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| Signature | Sign to accept the order |
| Sign here!! | Sign here |
| Done | Accept and sign |
| Error: no signature | Add your signature before you submit. |

### Best practices

**Do**

- Set `Signer` to the legal name for every signature, so the person sees who signs, and store that name with the
  strokes.
- Store `Strokes` with the record and reload them with `Reset`, rather than storing only a picture of the pad.
- Use `ExportSvg` for documents that are printed at several sizes, and `ExportPng` for email and screens.
- Keep the undo history for the person who is signing, and show the pad at a width where the baseline is visible.
- Check `IsEmpty` on submit, and keep the form data while the person corrects the signature.

**Avoid**

- Saving an empty export. `SaveAsync` returns false with no strokes, and an empty SVG is not a signature.
- Relying on the color for meaning. The blue and violet inks are a visual choice, and a printed record needs the name.
- Making the signature optional without a reason in the form. Say whether it is required, and why.
- Replacing the strokes with `Reset` while the person is still drawing. Reset clears the history and the ink at once.
- Showing the pad in a narrow column. The baseline and the toolbar groups wrap, and a narrow pad is hard to sign.

### Common questions

**Why does Delete clear the pad, and can the person get it back?** Delete and Backspace clear the pad with the wipe
animation. The clear is one undo step, so `Ctrl+Z` (`Cmd+Z` on macOS) brings the strokes back.

**Why is my exported PNG empty?** `ExportPng` crops to the ink, and with no strokes there is nothing to export. Check
`IsEmpty`, or use the `SaveAsync` result, which is false when the pad is empty.

**Does changing the ink color repaint the existing strokes?** No. Each stroke keeps the color and nib it was drawn
with. `InkColor` and `InkWidth` only set the choice for new strokes.

**How does pressure work with a mouse or touch?** A pen reports pressure, which sets the width directly. A mouse or
a finger reports none, and the pad derives the width from speed.

**How do I show the signature again, for example as a replay?** Call `Replay()` to redraw the strokes at their
original pace, which takes about 3.2 seconds, and `StopReplay()` (or Escape) to stop it. Use `Reset(strokes)` to show
stored strokes without replaying them.

## API reference

### SignaturePad

Arc's signature field with real ink: width follows pen pressure, or speed for a mouse or finger, and the ends taper like a nib lifting off. It keeps undo and redo, clears with a wipe across the pad, replays the signature in its original rhythm, and exports a cropped PNG or SVG. A "Sign here" hint rests on the baseline until the first stroke.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Signer` | `string?` | `null` | Printed under the baseline, such as the signer's name. |
| `Hint` | `string` | `"Sign here"` | The resting hint on the baseline before the first stroke (default "Sign here"). |
| `InkColor` | `SignatureInkColor` | `Black` | The ink for new strokes (default black). Each stroke keeps the ink it was drawn with. |
| `InkWidth` | `SignatureInkWidth` | `Medium` | The nib for new strokes (default medium). |
| `FileName` | `string` | `"signature"` | File name for exports, without extension (default "signature"). |
| `Strokes` | `IReadOnlyList<InkStroke>` | – | *Read-only.* The strokes of the signature, in pad units (600 × 260). |
| `IsEmpty` | `bool` | – | *Read-only.* True before the first stroke and after a clear. |
| `CanUndo` | `bool` | – | *Read-only.* True when a change can be undone (the last 60 are kept). |
| `CanRedo` | `bool` | – | *Read-only.* True when an undone change can be redone. |
| `IsReplaying` | `bool` | – | *Read-only.* True while the signature is being replayed. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `StrokesChanged` | `SignatureStrokesChangedEventArgs` | Raised after every change: a stroke drawn, undo, redo or clear (Arc's `onChange`). |

Pseudo-classes: `:empty`, `:replaying`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

## Accessibility

- The pad is a focusable image named "Signature pad". Its accessible name includes the number of strokes, and its
  description reads "Signature pad. Empty. Draw with a pointer, pen, or finger." when it has no ink.
- The keyboard shortcuts are in the pad's help text, so a screen reader announces them when the pad gets focus.
- Ink color and nib are single-choice groups. Only the selected option is in the tab order, and the arrow keys move
  between options.
- Toolbar buttons have a name and a tooltip. Strokes, undo, redo, clear, replay and export results are announced
  politely, so the person hears each change without losing focus.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Ctrl+Z` (`Cmd+Z` on macOS) | Undo the last change while the pad has focus |
| `Ctrl+Shift+Z` (`Cmd+Shift+Z` on macOS), or `Ctrl+Y` | Redo |
| `Delete` or `Backspace` | Clear the pad with the wipe; the clear can be undone |
| `Escape` | Stop a replay in progress |
| `Left` / `Right` (or `Up` / `Down`) in the color or nib group | Move to the previous or next option and choose it |
| `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` | Move between the pad, the groups and the toolbar buttons |

## Motion

- Clear sweeps a wiper across the pad and wipes the ink away with it, over about half a second.
- Replay redraws each stroke at its original pace, with a dot at the pen tip. The pauses between strokes are capped,
  and the whole replay fits in about 3.2 seconds.
- The hint fades in while it rises, and the color and nib highlight slides to the chosen option.
- Reduced motion removes the wipe and the blur and uses short fades.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| Clear | A wiper sweeps across and wipes the ink in about 0.56 seconds | The ink clears at once | Immediate |
| Replay | Strokes redraw at their original pace in about 3.2 seconds | Strokes redraw at their pace | Replay ends at once |
| Hint appears or leaves | Fades in and rises; blurs out when drawing starts | Short fade of about 120 ms | Immediate |
| Color or nib choice changes | The highlight glides to the chosen option | The highlight jumps to the option | Immediate |
| Replay and stop icons | Icon scales and swaps | Icon swaps | Immediate |

## Related

- `Input` for a typed name next to or instead of a drawn signature.
- `HoldToConfirm` for a deliberate confirmation that does not need a signature.
- `FileDropzone` for attaching files such as an already signed document.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `Input` | The name is typed and no drawn signature is needed |
| `HoldToConfirm` | A press-and-hold decision is the record, with no signature kept |
| `Checkbox` | The person accepts terms with a yes or no choice |
| `FileDropzone` | A signed file from another service must be attached |
| `RichTextEditor` | The content is text the person writes, not a signature |

# File dropzone

> A generous target for dropping one or more files.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/file-dropzone

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.FileDropzoneUploadDemo">
    <arc:FileDropzone x:Name="Zone" MaxFiles="6" MaxWidth="560" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class FileDropzoneUploadDemo : UserControl
{
    private int _uploads;

    public FileDropzoneUploadDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Zone.UploadHandler = SimulateUploadAsync;
    }

    // A fake upload: progress in steps over about two seconds; every third file fails halfway.
    private async Task SimulateUploadAsync(FileDropzoneItem item, IProgress<double> progress, CancellationToken token)
    {
        var fails = ++_uploads % 3 == 0;
        for (var percent = 0; percent <= 100; percent += 8)
        {
            await Task.Delay(140, token);
            progress.Report(percent);
            if (fails && percent >= 48)
            {
                throw new InvalidOperationException("The server closed the connection");
            }
        }
        progress.Report(100);
    }
}
```

## When to use

`FileDropzone` is the attachment target for a form or a page that collects files. It combines the drop target, the
system file picker, clipboard paste and a list of rows that shows each file with its upload state, so the person
sees what was accepted, what is still uploading and what failed, without leaving the page. It sits where the files
belong: under the field that owns them, inside a card or a settings section.

- **Invoice and receipt attachments on a billing or expense page**: a finance user drops a stack of PDF receipts,
  sees each one with its size, and removes the one that was scanned twice. `MaxFiles` and `MaxFileSize` state the
  limits next to the target, so nobody discovers them only after the upload fails.
- **Screenshots and logs on a support ticket**: a support agent copies a screenshot and presses Ctrl+V while the
  pointer is over the target, which adds the image as a row with a thumbnail. Pasting needs no extra button.
- **Bulk data import in a CRM or an admin console**: a single CSV file with `AllowMultiple` set to `False` and
  `Accept=".csv"`. A new file replaces the old one, so there is never a question of which file the import uses.
- **Identity documents in a fintech onboarding flow**: images and PDFs under a fixed size, with the upload handed to
  the app's own secure endpoint through `UploadHandler`. The failure reason of a rejected upload is shown on its row.
- **Release assets in a developer tool**: the app runs its own upload queue and reports progress for each row with
  `ReportProgress`, `CompleteUpload` and `FailUpload`, so the list reflects the queue the app already has.

## When not to use

- **Only the system file dialog is needed, and no list of files**: call `BrowseAsync` from your own `Button`, or use
  a plain `Button` that opens the picker in the app. A dropzone without a list adds an area the person does not need.
- **An empty page where dropping is the only action**: use `EmptyState` for a larger call to action with a
  heading and a short explanation, such as the first import on a new workspace.
- **Choosing one value from a known set**: use `Select` or `RadioGroup`. A file is a value with an upload life
  cycle, so do not use the dropzone as a picker for a fixed option.
- **Drawing a signature rather than attaching a file**: use `SignaturePad`, which produces a stroke-based image in the
  app and does not read a file from disk.
- **Writing a body that contains pictures and formatting**: use `RichTextEditor`, which keeps the text and the
  formatting in one document. The dropzone only lists files beside the document.

## Usage

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:FileDropzone Label="Add files"
                      Description="Drop files here or choose from your device"
                      Accept=".pdf,image/*"
                      MaxFiles="6" />
</UserControl>
```

`FileDropzone` derives from `TemplatedControl`, not from a `Button`. The whole target is a click area: its inner
button opens the system file picker, so a click, Enter or Space anywhere on the target opens it. The rows, the error row and the drop feedback are part of the same template, so the control keeps one
label, one description and one list in every state. Drag and drop, paste and the picker all feed the same
validation path, which means one set of rules (`Accept`, `MaxFiles`, `MaxFileSize`, `AllowMultiple`) applies to
every way a file arrives.

### Anatomy

1. **Target surface**: the drawn zone with the surface background, a dashed edge and rounded corners. It uses the
   surface radius (34 px at the default size) and folds to the panel radius (26 px) in compact mode. The background
   changes to the muted surface color on hover and while the target is pressed.
2. **Paper icon**: three stacked sheets with an arrow. On hover the sheets lift 3 px, and while files are dragged
   over the target the dashed edge closes into a solid edge tinted with the accent color.
3. **Label** (`Label`): the target's heading in the foreground color. While files hover over the target, it shows
   the drop copy instead: `DropLabel` when set, otherwise "Drop to upload" with an upload handler, "Drop to add
   files" for several files and "Drop to add the file" for a single file.
4. **Description** (`Description`): one line under the label that explains what to do.
5. **Note** (`Note`): a small line under the description. By default it lists the accepted types ("Accepted:
   .pdf,image/*") or the limit ("Up to 6 files"). It is hidden in compact mode.
6. **Error row** (`ErrorMessage`, read-only): a line with a danger-colored alert icon under the target. It appears
   when files are refused and stays until the next successful add or a removal.
7. **File list**: the rows below the target (`ListPlacement="Below"`, the default) or inside its edge
   (`Inside`), with 12 px side padding. Rows are listed in the order they were added.
8. **Row**: a thumbnail (a decoded 80 px preview with 10 px corners) or a type icon, the file name, the size, the
   status, a 4 px progress bar, a Retry button 30 px tall and a Remove button 32 px square. A row is at least 58 px
   high. Below 440 px of row width the Retry button shows only its icon, and below 300 px the type icon is hidden.

### Choose the accepted types and the limits

`Accept` takes extensions (".pdf") and MIME patterns ("image/*", "application/pdf"), separated by commas, the same
way an HTML file input does. An extension matches the end of the file name, a pattern with `/*` matches the MIME
type's prefix, and any other value must equal the MIME type exactly. The system picker builds its filter from the same
list. Leave `Accept` empty to accept every file.

Set the limits from the business rule, not from the default:

- `MaxFiles` (default 5) caps the list. A batch that goes over the cap adds the files that fit and refuses the rest.
- `MaxFileSize` (in bytes, default none) fails any larger file on its row. The file is listed with the reason, has no
  Retry button, and is never uploaded. Remove it and add a smaller file instead.
- `AllowMultiple` (default `True`) allows a list. With `False`, a new file replaces the current one and cancels the
  upload of the file it replaces.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.FileDropzoneImagesDemo">
    <arc:FileDropzone Label="Add images"
                      Description="PNG, JPG or WebP, up to 2 MB each"
                      Accept="image/*"
                      MaxFileSize="2097152"
                      MaxFiles="3"
                      MaxWidth="560" />
</UserControl>
```

The Images demo accepts images only, up to 2 MB each (`MaxFileSize="2097152"`), with three files at most. The
description states the limit in the words the person needs: the format and the size.

### Row status

Each `FileDropzoneItem` has a `Status` from the `FileDropzoneStatus` enum, which decides what the row shows.

| Status | Meaning | What the row shows |
|---|---|---|
| `None` | A plain selection; nothing is uploading | The file, its size and no progress bar |
| `Uploading` | The upload is running; `Progress` goes from 0 to 100 | The progress bar and a percentage |
| `Uploaded` | The upload finished; `Progress` is 100 | A check mark on the row |
| `Failed` | The upload or the checks failed; `Error` holds the reason | The reason, a red edge and Retry when it is allowed |

`FileDropzoneItem` raises `PropertyChanged` for every property, so an app can set `Status`, `Progress` and `Error`
directly. The methods on the dropzone do the same and also announce the change to assistive technology, so prefer
them when the app drives the row.

### Single file

With `AllowMultiple` set to `False`, the dropzone holds one file. A new file replaces the current one, cancels the
upload of the old file and raises `FilesChanged`.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.FileDropzoneSingleFileDemo">
    <arc:FileDropzone AllowMultiple="False"
                      Label="Add a contract"
                      Accept=".pdf"
                      MaxWidth="560" />
</UserControl>
```

Use it for a contract or an import, where a second file would be a mistake. The drop copy then speaks in the
singular ("Drop to add the file").

### Upload handler

Set `UploadHandler` to upload each added file. The handler receives the row, an `IProgress<double>` that reports
0 to 100, and a `CancellationToken`:

- Report progress as the bytes go out. The bar never moves back, so a retry that starts from zero does not look
  like a reset to the person; values outside 0 to 100 are clamped.
- Return normally to complete the row. Throw to fail it: the exception message becomes the reason on the row, and
  an empty message shows "Upload failed".
- Observe the token. Removing a row that is still uploading cancels its token, and a cancelled upload neither
  completes nor fails the row.

```csharp
zone.UploadHandler = async (item, progress, token) =>
{
    await UploadToServerAsync(item.File!, progress, token);
};

zone.FilesChanged += (_, e) =>
{
    // e.Files holds the files the visitor added and still has listed.
};
```

Retry is offered only when an `UploadHandler` is set and the row is `Failed` with `IsRetryable` true. Pressing it
starts the handler again for that row. `FilesChanged` is raised after files are added and after files are removed;
its `Files` list holds the visitor's files, not the rows the app created.

### Application-driven rows

Without an upload handler the app drives each row. Call `ReportProgress`, `CompleteUpload` and `FailUpload`, or set
the item's `Status` and `Progress` directly. Remove acts on any row, and `Retry` restarts an upload only through
the handler, so an application-driven failure has no Retry button. The app restarts a failed upload itself and
reports progress on the same row.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.FileDropzoneAppDrivenDemo">
    <arc:FileDropzone x:Name="Zone"
                      Label="Queue files"
                      Description="The app uploads them in its own queue"
                      MaxWidth="560"
                      FilesChanged="OnFilesChanged" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Threading;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class FileDropzoneAppDrivenDemo : UserControl
{
    private readonly DispatcherTimer _timer = new() { Interval = TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(180) };

    public FileDropzoneAppDrivenDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        _timer.Tick += OnTick;
        DetachedFromVisualTree += (_, _) => _timer.Stop();
    }

    private void OnFilesChanged(object? sender, FileDropzoneFilesChangedEventArgs e) => _timer.Start();

    // The app is the uploader: it moves every pending row forward and finishes it at 100.
    private void OnTick(object? sender, EventArgs e)
    {
        var busy = false;
        foreach (var item in Zone.Items.ToList())
        {
            if (item.Status is FileDropzoneStatus.None or FileDropzoneStatus.Uploading)
            {
                busy = true;
                var next = item.Progress + 7;
                if (next >= 100)
                {
                    Zone.CompleteUpload(item);
                }
                else
                {
                    Zone.ReportProgress(item, next);
                }
            }
        }
        if (!busy)
        {
            _timer.Stop();
        }
    }
}
```

```csharp
zone.ReportProgress(item, 40);
zone.CompleteUpload(item);
zone.FailUpload(item, "The server closed the connection", retryable: true);
```

`FailUpload` treats an empty reason as "Upload failed". Pass `retryable: false` when the failure cannot be fixed by
sending the same file again, such as a file the server rejects for its format. Such a row shows its reason and
only Remove.

### Rows inside the target

`ListPlacement="Inside"` shows the rows within the target's edge, with 12 px side padding and 12 px at the bottom.
Use it when the dropzone is the whole panel, such as an upload card with its own heading. With `CompactAt`, the
prompt folds to a slim bar once that many rows are listed: the icon and the note are hidden, the corners tighten
and the padding shrinks. A file dragged over the folded target brings the icon back, so the target still invites
a drop.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.FileDropzoneListInsideDemo">
    <arc:FileDropzone x:Name="Zone"
                      ListPlacement="Inside"
                      CompactAt="2"
                      MaxWidth="560" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class FileDropzoneListInsideDemo : UserControl
{
    private int _uploads;

    public FileDropzoneListInsideDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Zone.UploadHandler = SimulateUploadAsync;
        Zone.Items.Add(new FileDropzoneItem("brand-guidelines.pdf", 3_400_000, FileDropzoneStatus.Uploaded));
    }

    // A fake upload: progress in steps over about two seconds; every third file fails halfway.
    private async Task SimulateUploadAsync(FileDropzoneItem item, IProgress<double> progress, CancellationToken token)
    {
        var fails = ++_uploads % 3 == 0;
        for (var percent = 0; percent <= 100; percent += 8)
        {
            await Task.Delay(140, token);
            progress.Report(percent);
            if (fails && percent >= 48)
            {
                throw new InvalidOperationException("The server closed the connection");
            }
        }
        progress.Report(100);
    }
}
```

### Refusals and limits

A refused file is never listed, and the target shows the reason in its error row. The accepted files of the same
batch are still added.

| Rule | When it is checked | What the person sees |
|---|---|---|
| Type not in `Accept` | When the files are added | "<name> is not an accepted file type." for one file, or "Some files were not added because their type is not accepted." for several; the target shakes |
| Too many files for `MaxFiles` | When the files are added | "You can add up to 6 files." (or "1 file" when the limit is 1); the target shakes |
| Larger than `MaxFileSize` | When the file is added | The row fails with "File is larger than 2 MB" and no Retry button; the file is not uploaded |
| Same file twice | When the files are added | A file with the same name, size and modified time as one already listed is skipped silently |
| Failed upload | While or after the upload runs | The row shows the reason from the handler or `FailUpload`; Retry when it is allowed |

Sizes use `FileDropzoneItem.FormatSize`: bytes, whole kilobytes, or megabytes with one decimal below 10 MB.

### Binding to a view model

The dropzone is a list editor: the app owns the files and their upload, and the control shows them. The
`UploadHandler` is a delegate, not a command, so set it in code behind and keep the upload logic in the view model.
`Items` is a read-only collection property and is not bindable, so the view model keeps the state it needs and
reacts to `FilesChanged`.

```csharp
public partial class ExpenseReportViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    private readonly IReceiptStore _receipts;

    [ObservableProperty]
    [NotifyCanExecuteChangedFor(nameof(SubmitCommand))]
    private int _receiptCount;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private string? _submitError;

    public ExpenseReportViewModel(IReceiptStore receipts) => _receipts = receipts;

    public Task UploadReceiptAsync(FileDropzoneItem item, IProgress<double> progress, CancellationToken token) =>
        _receipts.UploadAsync(item.File!, progress, token);

    public void OnReceiptsChanged(int count) => ReceiptCount = count;

    private bool CanSubmit() => ReceiptCount > 0;

    [RelayCommand(CanExecute = nameof(CanSubmit))]
    private async Task SubmitAsync()
    {
        SubmitError = await _receipts.SubmitAsync() ? null : "Could not submit the report. Try again.";
    }
}
```

```csharp
// Code behind of the view that hosts the dropzone.
public partial class ExpenseReportView : UserControl
{
    public ExpenseReportView()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
    }

    protected override void OnDataContextChanged(EventArgs e)
    {
        base.OnDataContextChanged(e);
        if (DataContext is ExpenseReportViewModel vm)
        {
            Receipts.UploadHandler = vm.UploadReceiptAsync;
            Receipts.FilesChanged += (_, args) => vm.OnReceiptsChanged(args.Files.Count);
        }
    }
}
```

```xml
<StackPanel Spacing="16">
    <arc:FileDropzone x:Name="Receipts"
                      Label="Add receipts"
                      Accept=".pdf,.jpg,.jpeg"
                      MaxFiles="8" />
    <arc:Button Content="Submit expense report"
                Command="{Binding SubmitCommand}"
                IsDefault="True" />
    <TextBlock Text="{Binding SubmitError}" />
</StackPanel>
```

- `UploadHandler`, `Accept`, `MaxFiles` and `MaxFileSize` are one-way settings: the view model sets them once, and
  the control does not write them back.
- `Label`, `Description`, `Note` and `DropLabel` are one-way: bind them to a view model string when the copy depends
  on the workflow (for example, "Add the signed contract").
- `FilesChanged` and `FilesRejected` are the events to listen to; `IsDragOver` and `ErrorMessage` are read-only.
- The submit command reads `ReceiptCount` from `FilesChanged`. A failed upload stays listed, so an app that needs
  only completed receipts checks each `Status` in `Items` before submitting.

### Example: expense receipts on an approval page

A finance user attaches receipts to an expense report. The label names the object, the description carries the
rule that matters (format and size), the note shows the file types, and the list shows the three states a receipt
can be in at once: uploaded, still uploading and failed. The failed row has no Retry button because this scene
has no upload handler; in the running page the handler supplies Retry.

![A receipts dropzone with an uploaded receipt, an uploading receipt and a failed receipt](https://docs.tkcode.si/shots/Docs/Editors/FileDropzone/images/ExpenseReceipts.webp)

```xml
<StackPanel Width="640" Spacing="16">
    <TextBlock Text="Expense report"
               FontSize="18"
               FontWeight="SemiBold"
               Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
    <arc:FileDropzone Label="Add receipts"
                      Description="PDF or JPG, up to 10 MB each. Attach every receipt over 25 USD."
                      Accept=".pdf,.jpg,.jpeg"
                      MaxFiles="8"
                      MaxFileSize="10485760">
        <arc:FileDropzone.Items>
            <arc:FileDropzoneItem>
                <x:Arguments>
                    <x:String>taxi_2026-04-02.pdf</x:String>
                    <x:Int64>248000</x:Int64>
                    <arc:FileDropzoneStatus>Uploaded</arc:FileDropzoneStatus>
                </x:Arguments>
            </arc:FileDropzoneItem>
            <arc:FileDropzoneItem Progress="64">
                <x:Arguments>
                    <x:String>hotel_folio_march.pdf</x:String>
                    <x:Int64>1258291</x:Int64>
                    <arc:FileDropzoneStatus>Uploading</arc:FileDropzoneStatus>
                </x:Arguments>
            </arc:FileDropzoneItem>
            <arc:FileDropzoneItem Error="The server closed the connection">
                <x:Arguments>
                    <x:String>client_dinner_scan.jpg</x:String>
                    <x:Int64>3145728</x:Int64>
                    <arc:FileDropzoneStatus>Failed</arc:FileDropzoneStatus>
                </x:Arguments>
            </arc:FileDropzoneItem>
        </arc:FileDropzone.Items>
    </arc:FileDropzone>
</StackPanel>
```

### Content guidelines

- **Label**: name the object in the plural noun the person expects: "Add receipts", "Attach contracts", "Add images".
  Use the verb "Add" for the target, and avoid "Upload", which describes the network step the person does not see.
- **Description**: state the constraint the person must meet: the format and the size. Say the consequence where it
  matters, such as "Attach every receipt over 25 USD".
- **Note**: keep the default unless the rule needs a sentence. Write the accepted types as the person would name
  them ("PDF or JPG") in the description, and the extensions in the note.
- **Row reason**: say what happened and what to do, in words the person understands, not the raw server message.

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| Upload files | Add receipts |
| Invalid file | Use a PDF or JPG file. |
| Max 8 | Up to 8 files |
| File too big | File is larger than 10 MB |
| Something went wrong | Upload failed. Remove the file and add it again. |

### Best practices

**Do**

- Show the limits next to the target in the description and the note, before the person drops anything. A refusal
  after the drop is recoverable, but the rule should already be visible.
- Keep one upload handler per dropzone and let it report progress for each row. A row that stays at 0 looks stuck
  even when the upload is working.
- Pass the real reason to `FailUpload` or throw a message the person can act on. The reason is the only help the
  row can give.
- Set `AllowMultiple` to `False` for a document that replaces the previous one, so the list never holds two
  contracts for the same field.
- Check each row's `Status` before you submit, so a failed file is fixed before the form goes out.

**Avoid**

- Using the dropzone as the only way to attach a file. Keyboard users have the Enter and Space path, but a visible
  button beside the target helps people who expect a button, and it lets a screen reader user find the action.
- Setting `MaxFileSize` without saying it in the description. A file that fails for size with no warning reads as a
  bug.
- Showing a file's raw exception text as the reason. Stack traces and status codes do not help the person; write the
  message for them and log the detail.
- Using `CompactAt` on a review step where the person must check each file. Compact mode suits a crowded panel.
- Relying on paste alone. Paste works only while the pointer is over the target or focus is inside it, so a person
  must know where to paste.

### Common questions

**Why was my file skipped without a message?** A file with the same name, size and modified time as one already in
the list is a duplicate and is skipped without an error. A file that is refused for its type or for the limit
always produces a message on the error row and a `FilesRejected` event.

**How do I remove every file, for example when the person starts over?** Loop over a copy of `Items` and call
`Remove` for each row: `foreach (var item in zone.Items.ToList()) zone.Remove(item);`. Removing a row that is
uploading cancels its upload, and `FilesChanged` is raised once for each visitor file.

**Does the dropzone upload files on its own?** No. It uploads only when `UploadHandler` is set; without a handler it
lists the files and leaves the upload to the app, which calls `ReportProgress`, `CompleteUpload` and `FailUpload`.

**Can I change the label while files are dragged over the target?** Yes. Set `DropLabel` to the copy that should
show while files hover, such as "Drop the signed contract". When it is empty, the default drop copy depends on
whether an upload handler is set and on `AllowMultiple`.

**Why does a failed row have no Retry button?** Retry appears only when an `UploadHandler` is set, the row is
`Failed` and `IsRetryable` is `True`. A file that is too large is marked not retryable, and an app-driven failure
has no handler to call.

## API reference

### FileDropzone

Arc's generous target for dropping one or more files: drag files from the system onto it, click (or Enter / Space) to choose from the device, or paste a file while the pointer is over it. Files are checked against `Accept`, `MaxFileSize` and `MaxFiles`; refusals shake the target. The list shows each file with an upload state driven by `UploadHandler` or by the app, with Retry and Remove.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Accept` | `string?` | `null` | Accepted types like an HTML file input: extensions (".pdf") and MIME types ("image/*", "application/pdf"), comma separated. |
| `AllowMultiple` | `bool` | `true` | Allow several files (default true); a single-file dropzone replaces its file. |
| `MaxFiles` | `int` | `5` | The most files the list holds (default 5). |
| `MaxFileSize` | `long?` | `null` | Files above this many bytes fail with a size reason and never upload. |
| `Label` | `string` | `"Add files"` | The target's label (default "Add files"). |
| `Description` | `string` | `"Drop files here or choose from your device"` | The line under the label (default "Drop files here or choose from your device"). |
| `Note` | `string?` | `null` | Replaces the small line under the description (default: the accepted types, or the file limit). |
| `DropLabel` | `string?` | `null` | The label while files hover over the target (default "Drop to upload" / "Drop to add files"). |
| `ListPlacement` | `FileDropzoneListPlacement` | `Below` | List the files under the target (default) or inside its edge. |
| `CompactAt` | `int?` | `null` | Once the list holds this many files, the prompt folds to a slim bar; a file dragged over brings the icon back. |
| `UploadHandler` | `Func<FileDropzoneItem, IProgress<double>, CancellationToken, Task>?` | `null` | Uploads each added file: report 0–100 through the progress, complete the task when it lands, throw to fail it (the message becomes the reason). Removing the row cancels the token. |
| `IsDragOver` | `bool` | – | *Read-only.* True while files are dragged over the target. |
| `ErrorMessage` | `string?` | – | *Read-only.* The refusal shown under the target, or null. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `FilesChanged` | `FileDropzoneFilesChangedEventArgs` | Raised when the visitor's files change (added or removed; Arc's `onFilesChange`). |
| `FilesRejected` | `FileDropzoneRejectedEventArgs` | Raised when files are refused (type not accepted, or more than `MaxFiles`). |

Pseudo-classes: `:dragover`, `:hovered`, `:trigger-pressed`, `:compact`, `:inside`, `:has-rows`, `:error`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

### FileDropzoneItem

One row of a `FileDropzone`. Every property notifies, so an app can drive an upload itself by setting `Status` and `Progress` (or through `ReportProgress` and friends).

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `PropertyChanged` | `PropertyChangedEventHandler?` | Raised when any property of this row changes. |

## Accessibility

- The target is a button named by `Label`. Its help text combines the description and the note, so a screen reader
  reads what the target accepts and how many files it takes.
- The list is a named group ("Files"). It is hidden from assistive technology while it is empty and appears when the
  first row is added.
- Each row's progress bar exposes a range from 0 to 100. The Retry and Remove buttons include the file name in their
  accessible name, so "Remove hotel_folio_march.pdf" is distinct in a list of identical buttons.
- Adding, uploading, completing, failing and removing a file are announced politely. A refusal is announced
  assertively, because the person must act on it.
- Long file names and failure reasons are shortened to one line on screen; the full text is in the row's tooltip and
  its accessible name.
- Focus stays on the control when a row is removed: it moves to the neighboring row's Remove button, or to the target
  when there are no rows left.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` | Move through the target, then the rows' Retry and Remove buttons |
| `Enter` / `Space` on the target | Open the system file picker, filtered by `Accept` |
| `Up` / `Down` in the list | Move focus to the same action (Retry or Remove) on the neighboring row |
| `Delete` / `Backspace` on a row | Remove the focused row; focus moves to a neighboring row |
| `Ctrl+V` (`Cmd+V` on macOS) | Add the files on the clipboard, such as a screenshot, while the pointer is over the target or focus is inside it; ignored while a text box has focus |

## Motion

- Dragging a file over the target lifts the paper icon, closes the dashed edge into a solid accent-tinted edge and
  starts a slow breathing pulse (scale 1 to 1.012 every 2.2 seconds). The pulse stops as soon as the drag ends.
- Rows slide in from above with a slight blur, one after another; removed rows collapse in about 0.3 seconds.
- The progress bar follows its target on a smooth spring, a completed row draws its check mark, and a failed row or
  a refused batch shakes once, for about 0.42 seconds.
- Reduced motion swaps the height and lift changes for short fades and makes progress immediate. The pulse and the
  shake do not run.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| A file is dragged over the target | Paper lifts, dashed edge closes, the target breathes | Edge and tint change at once; no pulse | Immediate |
| A row is added | Row slides in, scales up from a slight blur, staggered | Short fade | Immediate |
| A row is removed | Height collapses in about 0.3 seconds | Short fade | Immediate |
| Upload progress changes | Bar follows the value on a smooth spring | Immediate | Immediate |
| A row fails, or a batch is refused | Target or row shakes once | No shake; color change only | Immediate |

## Related

- `EmptyState` for an empty page where dropping is the main call to action.
- `Button` for a visible action that opens the picker, or for the submit action beside the list.
- `Input` and `Textarea` for values that are not files.
- `SignaturePad` for a signature that is drawn rather than attached.
- `RichTextEditor` for a document body that holds text and pictures together.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `EmptyState` | An empty page needs a larger call to action with a heading |
| `Button` | Only the system picker is needed, with no list of files |
| `Select` / `RadioGroup` | The person picks one value from a known set |
| `SignaturePad` | A signature is drawn in the app rather than read from disk |
| `RichTextEditor` | The content is text and pictures in one document |
| `Input` / `Textarea` | The value is a string, not a file |
