# Tabs

> Switch between related content in the same context.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/tabs

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.TabsDefaultDemo">
    <arc:Tabs>
        <arc:TabItem Header="Overview">
            <TextBlock Text="Revenue is up 12% this quarter. Three new regions went live and churn held steady."
                       FontSize="14"
                       TextWrapping="Wrap"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
        </arc:TabItem>
        <arc:TabItem Header="Activity">
            <StackPanel Spacing="8">
                <TextBlock Text="Maya merged “Billing v2” · 2h ago"
                           FontSize="14"
                           TextWrapping="Wrap"
                           Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
                <TextBlock Text="Leo opened 3 issues · 5h ago"
                           FontSize="14"
                           TextWrapping="Wrap"
                           Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
                <TextBlock Text="Ana deployed to production · yesterday"
                           FontSize="14"
                           TextWrapping="Wrap"
                           Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
                <TextBlock Text="Kai rotated the API keys · 2 days ago"
                           FontSize="14"
                           TextWrapping="Wrap"
                           Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
            </StackPanel>
        </arc:TabItem>
        <arc:TabItem Header="Settings">
            <StackPanel Spacing="10">
                <TextBlock Text="Workspace name, members and billing live here."
                           FontSize="14"
                           TextWrapping="Wrap"
                           Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
                <arc:Switch Content="Email digests" IsChecked="True" />
            </StackPanel>
        </arc:TabItem>
        <arc:TabItem Header="Archived" IsEnabled="False">
            <TextBlock Text="Nothing archived." FontSize="14" TextWrapping="Wrap" />
        </arc:TabItem>
    </arc:Tabs>
</UserControl>
```

## When to use

`Tabs` splits one object's screen into peer views, such as Overview, Activity and Settings on a customer record. The
person picks one view at a time, and each view has its own panel below the tab list. The tab list stays in place while
the panel changes, so the person keeps their bearings within the same record, order or workspace.

- **A customer record in a CRM**: Overview, Orders, Invoices and Notes are views of one account. The account header
  stays above the tabs, and the selected tab decides which list fills the panel.
- **A workspace or project page**: Overview, Activity and Settings. Each view is peer to the others, so none of them is
  a step in a sequence.
- **Filtering the same data by a state**: All, Open, Overdue and Paid tabs over one invoice list, where each tab shows
  its count in the label.
- **Long lists of views in a desktop tool**: a mail client's folders (Inbox, Drafts, Sent, Scheduled) with edge scroll
  buttons when the window is narrow. The selected folder is always scrolled into view.

## When not to use

- **Choosing a compact value without a panel**, such as a day, week or month range: use `SegmentedControl`. The
  options have no content of their own, so a tab panel adds nothing.
- **Content that is read in order as stacked sections**, such as the terms of a checkout: use `Accordion`, where each
  section opens in place and the person can read several at once.
- **Moving through pages of results**: use `Pagination`. Tabs switch views, not pages of one collection.
- **Showing where a page sits in a hierarchy**: use `Breadcrumb`. Crumbs lead up a path, while tabs are peers.
- **Steps that must be completed in order**, such as Shipping, Payment and Review: use `Stepper`. A person cannot skip
  ahead in a checkout the way they can switch tabs.

## Usage

Items are `TabItem` containers. The header is the trigger and the content is the panel.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:Tabs AutomationProperties.Name="Workspace">
        <arc:TabItem Header="Overview">
            <TextBlock Text="Revenue is up 12% this quarter." />
        </arc:TabItem>
        <arc:TabItem Header="Activity">
            <TextBlock Text="Maya merged Billing v2 two hours ago." />
        </arc:TabItem>
        <arc:TabItem Header="Settings">
            <CheckBox Content="Email digests" IsChecked="True" />
        </arc:TabItem>
        <arc:TabItem Header="Archived" IsEnabled="False" />
    </arc:Tabs>
</UserControl>
```

`Tabs` derives from Avalonia's `SelectingItemsControl`, so selection works as it does for any selecting list:
`SelectedIndex`, `SelectedItem` and `SelectionChanged` are the same, and the first tab is selected when the control
loads. The tab list itself takes no focus; each `TabItem` does. A `TabItem` derives from `HeaderedContentControl`, so
`Header` is its trigger and `Content` is its panel. A disabled tab is skipped by the arrow keys and cannot be selected.

### Anatomy

1. **Tab list** (`Tabs`): a 1 px border in the border color on the muted surface, with the control radius. It clips its
   contents and has 4 px of padding inside the frame.
2. **Selection pill**: the surface color with a 1 px border and the resting shadow. It sits behind the selected trigger
   and glides between triggers.
3. **Trigger** (`TabItem.Header`): at least 88 px wide and 36 px high, with 12 px of horizontal padding and a 15 px
   radius. Its label uses the small type size in medium weight and the muted text color. Hover moves it to the main
   text color, the selected tab uses the strong accent color, and a disabled tab drops to 50% opacity.
4. **Gap**: 4 px between triggers.
5. **Edge scroll buttons** (`ScrollLeftLabel`, `ScrollRightLabel`): 33 px wide, shown only when the list is wider than
   the frame, with a 17 px chevron. The button on a side is enabled only when there are tabs hidden on that side.
6. **Edge fade**: a 35 px fade on each side that has hidden tabs.
7. **Panel**: the content of the selected tab, 16 px below the list, in the secondary text color at the small type size
   with a 19.6 px line height.
8. **Focus rings**: a 2 px ring around the focused trigger, and a ring around the panel when the panel takes focus.

### Data-bound tabs

Set `ItemsSource`. `ItemTemplate` renders the trigger and `ContentTemplate` renders the panel of the selected item.
Read the selection through `SelectedItem` or `SelectionChanged`.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             xmlns:generic="using:System.Collections.Generic"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.TabsOverflowDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12">
        <arc:Tabs x:Name="Folders"
                  MaxWidth="460"
                  HorizontalAlignment="Left">
            <arc:Tabs.ItemsSource>
                <generic:List x:TypeArguments="x:String">
                    <x:String>Inbox</x:String>
                    <x:String>Drafts</x:String>
                    <x:String>Sent</x:String>
                    <x:String>Scheduled</x:String>
                    <x:String>Spam</x:String>
                    <x:String>Trash</x:String>
                    <x:String>Archive</x:String>
                    <x:String>Templates</x:String>
                    <x:String>Snoozed</x:String>
                    <x:String>Important</x:String>
                </generic:List>
            </arc:Tabs.ItemsSource>
            <arc:Tabs.ContentTemplate>
                <DataTemplate x:DataType="x:String">
                    <TextBlock Text="{Binding StringFormat='{}{0}: nothing new since this morning.'}"
                               FontSize="14"
                               TextWrapping="Wrap"
                               Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
                </DataTemplate>
            </arc:Tabs.ContentTemplate>
        </arc:Tabs>
        <TextBlock Text="{Binding #Folders.SelectedItem, StringFormat='Selected: {0}'}"
                   FontSize="12"
                   TextWrapping="Wrap"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```xml
<arc:Tabs ItemsSource="{Binding Folders}"
          SelectedItem="{Binding CurrentFolder}"
          MaxWidth="460"
          HorizontalAlignment="Left">
    <arc:Tabs.ItemTemplate>
        <DataTemplate>
            <TextBlock Text="{Binding Name}" />
        </DataTemplate>
    </arc:Tabs.ItemTemplate>
    <arc:Tabs.ContentTemplate>
        <DataTemplate>
            <TextBlock Text="{Binding Summary}" />
        </DataTemplate>
    </arc:Tabs.ContentTemplate>
</arc:Tabs>
```

A data item that is not a `TabItem` becomes the panel content directly, and `ContentTemplate` renders it.

### Binding to a view model

A customer record keeps its sections in a view model. The tabs show the sections, the selected section is a two-way
property, and the view model loads the data for the section that the person opens. With CommunityToolkit.Mvvm, the
view model is an `ObservableObject` with an `ObservableCollection<T>` of sections and an `[ObservableProperty]`
for the selection.

```csharp
public sealed record CustomerSection(string Title, string Summary);

public partial class CustomerViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    public ObservableCollection<CustomerSection> Sections { get; } = new()
    {
        new("Overview", "Account owner Maya Chen. Business plan, renews November 30, 2026."),
        new("Orders", "12 orders in the last 90 days. The latest was placed April 8, 2026."),
        new("Invoices", "2 open invoices. One is 6 days overdue."),
        new("Notes", "Asked for a quote for 40 more seats on March 2, 2026.")
    };

    [ObservableProperty]
    private CustomerSection? _selectedSection;

    partial void OnSelectedSectionChanged(CustomerSection? value)
    {
        // Load the data for the section the person opened, not for every section up front.
    }
}
```

```xml
<arc:Tabs ItemsSource="{Binding Sections}"
          SelectedItem="{Binding SelectedSection, Mode=TwoWay}"
          AutomationProperties.Name="Customer sections">
    <arc:Tabs.ItemTemplate>
        <DataTemplate>
            <TextBlock Text="{Binding Title}" />
        </DataTemplate>
    </arc:Tabs.ItemTemplate>
    <arc:Tabs.ContentTemplate>
        <DataTemplate>
            <TextBlock Text="{Binding Summary}" TextWrapping="Wrap" />
        </DataTemplate>
    </arc:Tabs.ContentTemplate>
</arc:Tabs>
```

`SelectedItem` is the value to bind two ways: it is the section the person chose, and a change from the view model
(for example, opening the Invoices section from a notification) selects the tab. Use `SelectionChanged` in code behind
when the view must react to the change itself, such as to save the scroll position of the previous section. Do not
bind `SelectedIndex` for the same purpose: an index shifts when a section is added or removed, while the item stays
the same.

### Activation mode

`ActivationMode` controls what the arrow keys do. `Automatic` (the default) selects the tab that
receives focus. `Manual` only moves focus; Enter or Space selects the tab.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.TabsManualActivationDemo">
    <arc:Tabs ActivationMode="Manual">
        <arc:TabItem Header="Day">
            <TextBlock Text="Day view" FontSize="14" TextWrapping="Wrap" Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
        </arc:TabItem>
        <arc:TabItem Header="Week">
            <TextBlock Text="Week view" FontSize="14" TextWrapping="Wrap" Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
        </arc:TabItem>
        <arc:TabItem Header="Month">
            <TextBlock Text="Month view" FontSize="14" TextWrapping="Wrap" Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
        </arc:TabItem>
        <arc:TabItem Header="Year">
            <TextBlock Text="Year view" FontSize="14" TextWrapping="Wrap" Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
        </arc:TabItem>
    </arc:Tabs>
</UserControl>
```

Use `Automatic` when the panels are cheap to show and the person is browsing: moving through the tabs with the arrow keys
previews each panel. Use `Manual` when a panel is expensive to show, when the person would lose work by previewing a
panel they did not mean to open, or when the tabs filter a list that reloads on every selection. Manual mode also
keeps the arrow keys from changing the data while the person is still deciding.

### Selecting in code

```csharp
tabs.SelectTab(2);
tabs.SelectionChanged += (_, _) =>
{
    status.Text = $"Selected: {tabs.SelectedItem}";
};
```

`SelectTab` selects the tab at the index when it exists and is enabled, and returns `false` otherwise.
`SelectedIndex` does not check whether the tab is enabled, so use `SelectTab` when the target might be disabled, such
as a tab that a permission check turns off.

### Long tab lists

A tab list wider than its frame scrolls horizontally. The edge buttons appear only while there is something to scroll
to, and the list reveals the selected or focused tab on the smooth spring. Clicking an edge button moves the list by
about three quarters of its visible width. The list keeps the selected tab
visible when the selection changes from code, so a tab deep in a long list is found without a search.

Give tabs short labels that fit the list at the narrowest width the page supports, and move the rest of the
information into the panel. A list of ten folders is usable with edge buttons; a list of fifteen with long labels is
better as a `Select` or a sidebar, because the person then has to scroll for every choice.

### Data shape and performance

Only the selected tab's content is shown. When the selection changes, the panel host replaces the content it shows and
keeps the leaving panel for the length of its fade. Put heavy loading behind the selection, for example in the view
model's selection handler, rather than loading every section when the page opens. Keep the tab count small: a tab list
of about five to seven is easy to scan, and a longer list needs a different structure.

### Example: customer record tabs

A customer record in a CRM. The account name and its plan stay above the tabs, so the context does not change when the
person moves between Overview, Orders, Invoices and Notes. The Overview panel is a short list of facts in two columns,
with the label in the muted color and the value in the main text color. The tab labels are nouns that match the lists
they open, and the first tab is selected because it is the view people open most.

![A customer record header with four tabs and the Overview facts in the panel](https://docs.tkcode.si/shots/Docs/Navigation/Tabs/images/CustomerTabs.webp)

```xml
<StackPanel Width="680" Spacing="16">
    <StackPanel Spacing="4">
        <TextBlock Text="Northwind Trading"
                   FontSize="22"
                   FontWeight="SemiBold"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
        <TextBlock Text="Business plan, renews November 30, 2026"
                   FontSize="14"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
    </StackPanel>
    <arc:Tabs AutomationProperties.Name="Customer sections">
        <arc:TabItem Header="Overview">
            <StackPanel Spacing="12">
                <Grid ColumnDefinitions="180,*">
                    <TextBlock Text="Account owner" FontSize="14"
                               Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
                    <TextBlock Grid.Column="1" Text="Maya Chen" FontSize="14" />
                </Grid>
                <Grid ColumnDefinitions="180,*">
                    <TextBlock Text="Plan" FontSize="14"
                               Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
                    <TextBlock Grid.Column="1" Text="Business, billed annually" FontSize="14" />
                </Grid>
                <Grid ColumnDefinitions="180,*">
                    <TextBlock Text="Renewal date" FontSize="14"
                               Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
                    <TextBlock Grid.Column="1" Text="November 30, 2026" FontSize="14" />
                </Grid>
                <Grid ColumnDefinitions="180,*">
                    <TextBlock Text="Open invoices" FontSize="14"
                               Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
                    <TextBlock Grid.Column="1" Text="2, one 6 days overdue" FontSize="14" />
                </Grid>
            </StackPanel>
        </arc:TabItem>
        <arc:TabItem Header="Orders">
            <TextBlock Text="12 orders in the last 90 days." FontSize="14" />
        </arc:TabItem>
        <arc:TabItem Header="Invoices">
            <TextBlock Text="inv_2026_0412 and inv_2026_0399 are open." FontSize="14" />
        </arc:TabItem>
        <arc:TabItem Header="Notes">
            <TextBlock Text="Asked for a quote for 40 more seats on March 2, 2026." FontSize="14" />
        </arc:TabItem>
    </arc:Tabs>
</StackPanel>
```

### Content guidelines

- **Tab label**: one or two words, a noun in sentence case that names the list it opens: "Invoices", "Notes". Keep the
  labels parallel, so that the list reads as one set of views.
- **Count in a label**: add a count only when the count changes what the person does next, such as "Open (2)". A count
  that never changes adds noise to every label.
- **Panel text**: start with the state or the number ("2 open invoices", "No notes yet"), not with an instruction to
  look at a tab.
- **Disabled tab**: when a tab is disabled, say why nearby, for example in the panel of the tab next to it or in the
  page header, so that the person knows whether the view is missing or unavailable to them.

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| Tab label "Misc" | Notes |
| Tab label "Stuff about the customer" | Account |
| Panel text "Click the tab above for more" | No open invoices. |
| Tab label "INVOICES" | Invoices |

### Best practices

**Do**

- Keep the labels short and the list within the narrowest width the page supports. Labels hidden by scrolling are harder
  to find than labels that are visible at once.
- Keep the shared context (the record name, its status, the primary action) above the tabs, so it stays in view while
  the person switches views.
- Bind `SelectedItem` two ways and name the list with `AutomationProperties.Name`. The view model keeps the selection,
  and assistive technology announces the list by its name.
- Use `Manual` activation when a panel is expensive to show, so that arrow keys move focus without loading each view.

**Avoid**

- Using tabs for steps. People expect tabs to be free to visit in any order, and a step that must come first needs a
  `Stepper` or a sequence of pages.
- Nesting tabs inside tabs. Two levels of peer selection make the person lose track of which level they are on, and the
  inner list scrolls inside the outer one.
- Putting the page's primary action in one tab only. The reason the person came to the record is usually visible in
  every view, not hidden in one of them.
- Disabling a tab without a reason on the page. A disabled tab with no explanation looks broken.

### Common questions

**Why does selecting a tab not scroll my page?** The tab list reveals the selected tab inside its own viewport and does
not bring the whole control into view. A tab set below the fold stays where the person scrolled, so the page does not
jump when a tab is chosen.

**How do I open a particular tab when the page loads?** Set `SelectedIndex` or `SelectedItem` before or after the
control loads. If the tab could be disabled, call `SelectTab(index)` instead, which returns `false` for a disabled or
missing tab so that you can fall back to the first enabled one.

**Why do the arrow keys not select a tab in Manual mode?** In `Manual` mode the arrow keys only move focus. Press Enter or
Space on the focused tab to select it.

**Can I style the tab list for overflow?** Yes. `Tabs` sets the `:overflow` pseudo class when the list is wider than its
frame, and `:scrolled-start` and `:scrolled-end` when tabs are hidden on each side. Use them in a style selector to
change the edge treatment without changing the control's template.

## API reference

### Tabs

Arc tabs: switch between related views of the same object. A single selection pill glides between the triggers on a morph spring, the incoming panel slides 8px in from the side of travel while the outgoing one is pinned in place and fades, and the panel area springs from the old panel height to the new one so the content below glides. Long tab lists scroll horizontally with soft edges and edge scroll buttons, and the selected or focused tab is always scrolled into view. Items are `TabItem` containers written inline (`<arc:TabItem Header="Overview">…</arc:TabItem>`) or generated from `ItemsSource`: `ItemTemplate` renders the trigger and `ContentTemplate` the panel.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ContentTemplate` | `IDataTemplate?` | `null` | Template for the panel of data items (the trigger uses `ItemTemplate`). |
| `ActivationMode` | `TabsActivationMode` | `Automatic` | Whether arrow keys select the tab they move to (`Automatic`, Arc default). |
| `ContentMargin` | `Thickness` | `0,0,0,0` | Margin around the panel; its top edge is the space between the trigger list and the panel (Arc: 16px). |
| `ScrollLeftLabel` | `string` | `"Scroll tabs left"` | Accessible name of the left scroll button. |
| `ScrollRightLabel` | `string` | `"Scroll tabs right"` | Accessible name of the right scroll button. |
| `SelectedContent` | `object?` | – | *Read-only.* The panel content of the selected tab. |
| `SelectedContentTemplate` | `IDataTemplate?` | – | *Read-only.* The template of the selected tab's panel. |

Pseudo-classes: `:overflow`, `:scrolled-start`, `:scrolled-end`

Derives from `SelectingItemsControl`: every member of `SelectingItemsControl` works as well.

## Accessibility

- The list has the Tab role and each `TabItem` exposes its selection state. Give the list a name with
  `AutomationProperties.Name`.
- Each `TabItem` is named by its header when the header is a string. Give other headers a name explicitly.
- Only the selected tab is in the tab order. Arrow keys move between tabs, Home and End jump to the first and last.
- Tab moves from the list into the panel of the selected tab.
- Scroll buttons on an overflowing list are named by `ScrollLeftLabel` and `ScrollRightLabel`, which default to
  "Scroll tabs left" and "Scroll tabs right".
- The panel of a tab that is leaving is hidden from assistive technology and cannot take focus while it fades.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` | Move into the tab list on the selected tab, or on the last tab that had focus; out of the list into the panel |
| `Left` / `Right` | Move to the previous or next enabled tab, wrapping at the ends; in `Automatic` mode the tab is also selected |
| `Home` / `End` | Move to the first or last enabled tab; in `Automatic` mode the tab is also selected |
| `Enter` / `Space` | Select the focused tab. In `Manual` mode this is how the keyboard selects; a pointer press selects in both modes. |
| Pointer press | Select the tab on press with the left button; touch selects on release |

A disabled tab is skipped by the arrow keys, Home and End, and it cannot be selected by a press.

## Motion

- The selection pill glides between triggers on a morph spring.
- The new panel slides in 8px from the side of travel and fades in. The old panel stays in place, moves 6px back
  and fades out quickly.
- The panel area springs from the old panel height to the new one, so the content below moves with it.
- Reduced motion switches the pill at once and cross-fades the panels in place without height animation. Off
  switches everything at once.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| The selection moves | The pill glides between the triggers on the morph spring | The pill switches at once | Immediate |
| The new panel appears | Slides in 8 px from the side of travel and fades in over the standard duration | Cross-fades in place over 120 ms | Immediate |
| The old panel leaves | Stays in place, moves 6 px back and fades out over 120 ms | Fades out over 100 ms | Immediate |
| The panel area changes height | Springs from the old height to the new one, moving the content below | No height animation | Immediate |
| The list scrolls to a tab | Scrolls on the smooth spring | Jumps | Jumps |
| Hover and selected trigger | The label color crossfades | Immediate | Immediate |

## Related

- `SegmentedControl` for a compact choice of a value that has no panel.
- `Accordion` for stacked sections that are read in order.
- `Pagination` for moving through pages of one collection.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `SegmentedControl` | The choice is a value, such as a range or a view mode, with no panel of its own |
| `Accordion` | Stacked sections are read in order, and several may be open at once |
| `Breadcrumb` | The page sits in a hierarchy and the person needs the path back up |
| `Pagination` | The views are pages of one collection, not peer views |
| `Stepper` | The person completes steps in a fixed order |
| `Select` | The list of views is long, and a single choice in a form is enough |

---

# Breadcrumb

> Show where a page sits in a hierarchy.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/breadcrumb

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.BreadcrumbDefaultDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12">
        <arc:Breadcrumb ItemClick="OnItemClick">
            <arc:BreadcrumbItem Content="Workspace" />
            <arc:BreadcrumbItem Content="Settings" />
            <arc:BreadcrumbItem Content="Billing" />
        </arc:Breadcrumb>
        <TextBlock x:Name="Status"
                   Text="Choose a crumb"
                   FontSize="12"
                   TextWrapping="Wrap"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class BreadcrumbDefaultDemo : UserControl
{
    public BreadcrumbDefaultDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
    }

    private void OnItemClick(object? sender, BreadcrumbItemClickEventArgs e)
        => Status.Text = $"Navigate to {((BreadcrumbItem)e.Item!).Content} (index {e.Index})";
}
```

## When to use

`Breadcrumb` shows the path from the root of an area down to the page the person is on, such as Workspace, Settings
and Billing. It sits above the page heading, where it answers "where am I?" and gives one-click exits back up the
hierarchy. In a desktop application it can also show a client-side path, such as the folder path of a file browser,
where choosing a crumb changes the view instead of an address.

- **A billing section in an admin console**: the path Acme Analytics, Billing, Invoices, inv_2026_0412 tells an
  administrator which workspace and section they are in, and each parent crumb returns to the list above it.
- **A file browser or asset library in a desktop app**: one crumb per folder (Home, Projects, Q3 Report). Choosing a
  crumb removes the crumbs after it, and the folder list updates to match the shorter path.
- **A deep settings tree**: Organization, Security, Single sign-on. People often arrive at a settings page from a
  search result or a link, so the parents show the way back.
- **Developer tools and incident records**: Platform, Incidents, INC-2026-114 shows the team and product that own a
  record, which matters when the same ID exists in several places.
- **Long hierarchies on narrow windows**: with `MaxVisibleItems`, the root and the last few levels stay visible while
  the middle collapses into one overflow button, so a deep path fits a sidebar-width column.

## When not to use

- **Browsing a whole tree of items with expandable nodes**: use `TreeView`, which shows the siblings at each level and
  keeps the branches open.
- **Switching between sibling views of the same object**, such as Overview, Activity and Settings: use `Tabs`. The
  crumbs are places people go back to, not panels they switch between.
- **Moving through pages of one collection**: use `Pagination`, which knows the page count and the current page
  number.
- **Steps the person completes in order**, such as Cart, Shipping, Payment and Review: use `Stepper`, which shows
  progress and the state of each step.
- **Choosing one value from a list**, such as a folder or a project in a form: use `Select` or `Combobox`. A breadcrumb
  does not hold a value the form submits.

## Usage

Each crumb is a `BreadcrumbItem`. The last crumb is the current page: it is plain text and never a link.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:Breadcrumb>
        <arc:BreadcrumbItem Content="Workspace" />
        <arc:BreadcrumbItem Content="Settings" />
        <arc:BreadcrumbItem Content="Billing" />
    </arc:Breadcrumb>
</UserControl>
```

`Breadcrumb` derives from Avalonia's `ItemsControl`, so `Items`, `ItemsSource` and `ItemTemplate` behave as they do for
any list. Every item is wrapped in a `BreadcrumbItem`, a `ContentControl`, so its label is `Content`. The panel lays the
crumbs out in a row and wraps them onto a new line when the path is wider than the space. The breadcrumb itself never
takes focus; only the crumbs that can be chosen do.

### Anatomy

1. **Landmark** (`Breadcrumb`, `Label`): a navigation landmark named by `Label`, which defaults to "Breadcrumb". Its
   crumbs form a list, and each one is announced with its position in the path.
2. **Separator**: a 16 px chevron in the border-strong color, drawn with a 1.75 stroke. It sits in front of every crumb
   except the first, so the root has no chevron. A 6 px gap separates the chevron from its label.
3. **Label** (`BreadcrumbItem.Content`): the small type size in the muted text color, with 2 px horizontal and 4 px
   vertical padding inside a frame with a 7 px radius. Neighboring crumbs are 6 px apart.
4. **Hover underline**: a 1 px line under the label of an interactive crumb. It appears on hover at 45% opacity.
5. **Current crumb** (`IsCurrent`): the last crumb. It uses the accent strong color and medium weight, and it is not
   interactive. Each crumb reserves the width of its label in medium weight, so becoming the current crumb never moves
   the crumbs before it.
6. **Overflow button**: when `MaxVisibleItems` collapses the path, the first hidden position becomes an ellipsis button
   named by `OverflowLabel`.
7. **Focus ring**: a 2 px ring in the focus color, drawn 4 px outside the label frame. It appears only for keyboard
   focus.
8. **Wrapped lines**: 2 px between lines when the path wraps.

### Navigating with a click

Each crumb before the current page can be chosen with the pointer, `Enter` or `Space`. Handle `ItemClick` to react to
the chosen crumb. `Index` is its position in the path, where 0 is the root, and `Item` is the data item (or the
`BreadcrumbItem` written inline).

```csharp
breadcrumb.ItemClick += (_, e) =>
{
    status.Text = $"Navigate to {((BreadcrumbItem)e.Item!).Content} (index {e.Index})";
};
```

The `ItemClick` event runs first. Then the crumb's `Command` runs with its `CommandParameter`, and then its
`NavigateUri` is opened. Handle the event for in-app navigation, because it gets the index and the item in one place;
use the other two only when the crumb itself owns the action.

### Bound path

Set `ItemsSource` to a collection of the path. Use an `ObservableCollection<T>` so that the crumbs change as the path
grows and shrinks.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.BreadcrumbClientSidePathDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12">
        <arc:Breadcrumb x:Name="Files" ItemClick="OnItemClick" />
        <WrapPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center" ItemSpacing="12" LineSpacing="12">
            <arc:Button Content="Open next folder" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Click="OnOpenClick" />
            <arc:Button Content="Up one level" Variant="Ghost" Size="Small" Click="OnUpClick" />
        </WrapPanel>
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using System.Collections.ObjectModel;
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class BreadcrumbClientSidePathDemo : UserControl
{
    private static readonly string[] Folders = ["Arc", "src", "components", "breadcrumb"];

    // A file browser: the path lives in local state, crumbs truncate it and folders extend it.
    private readonly ObservableCollection<string> _path = new() { "Home", "Projects" };

    public BreadcrumbClientSidePathDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Files.ItemsSource = _path;
    }

    private void OnItemClick(object? sender, BreadcrumbItemClickEventArgs e)
    {
        while (_path.Count > e.Index + 1)
        {
            _path.RemoveAt(_path.Count - 1);
        }
    }

    private void OnOpenClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        // Truncating to the first crumb leaves one segment, so the offset must stay non-negative.
        _path.Add(Folders[(_path.Count + Folders.Length - 2) % Folders.Length]);
    }

    private void OnUpClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        if (_path.Count > 1)
        {
            _path.RemoveAt(_path.Count - 1);
        }
    }
}
```

Opening a folder adds a crumb with `path.Add(name)`. Choosing a crumb removes the crumbs after it, which animates the
removed crumbs out. A crumb added to the end slides in from the left, and the crumbs that stay in place glide to make
room. A crumb that keeps its label at the same index does not play its entry animation again.

### Commands and navigation URIs

A crumb with `Command` runs it with `CommandParameter`, when `CanExecute` returns true, and is presented as a button.
A crumb with `NavigateUri` is presented as a link, and the address opens through the top level's `Launcher`, which
hands it to the platform. Every crumb that can be chosen is announced as a button, and a crumb with a `NavigateUri`
is announced as a link. For a desktop application's own views, prefer `ItemClick` or a command, so that the view
changes inside the window rather than in a browser.

```xml
<arc:BreadcrumbItem Content="Billing"
                    Command="{Binding OpenBillingCommand}"
                    CommandParameter="{Binding BillingId}" />
```

A crumb with `IsClickable="False"` is plain text even when it is not the current page. Use it for a segment that is
a label only, such as a year group that has no page of its own.

### Label

`Label` names the landmark for assistive technology. Set it when the breadcrumb is not the only navigation landmark on
the page, so that a screen reader user can tell the two apart. The default is "Breadcrumb".

```xml
<arc:Breadcrumb Label="Folder path" />
```

### Collapsed path

`MaxVisibleItems` folds the middle of a long path into an overflow menu. It is off by default, as in Arc, where the
path is never collapsed. When the path is longer than `MaxVisibleItems`, the root stays visible, the first hidden
position becomes an ellipsis button, and the last `MaxVisibleItems − 1` crumbs stay visible. The button opens a menu
that lists the hidden crumbs in path order. Choosing an entry raises `ItemClick` with the entry's index in the path.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.BreadcrumbCollapsedPathDemo">
    <arc:Breadcrumb MaxVisibleItems="4">
        <arc:BreadcrumbItem Content="Acme" />
        <arc:BreadcrumbItem Content="Engineering" />
        <arc:BreadcrumbItem Content="Platform" />
        <arc:BreadcrumbItem Content="Services" />
        <arc:BreadcrumbItem Content="Billing" />
        <arc:BreadcrumbItem Content="Invoices" />
        <arc:BreadcrumbItem Content="2026" />
    </arc:Breadcrumb>
</UserControl>
```

The menu is a light-dismiss popup below the button. It is opened and closed in code with `OpenOverflow()` and
`CloseOverflow()`, and `IsOverflowOpen` reports whether it is showing. The menu moves focus with `Up`, `Down`, `Home`
and `End`, closes on `Escape` and returns focus to the button, and closes after a choice has been made.

### Data shape and performance

A breadcrumb describes a path, so keep its items to the levels that matter. Each item is one `BreadcrumbItem`
container, and the panel measures and arranges all of them; the control does not virtualize its items. A path of a
few levels is the intended use. For a deep hierarchy, shorten the labels and use `MaxVisibleItems` instead of
building a long path that the window must wrap.

Labels should be text. A crumb whose content is a control keeps its place without a reserved width for the medium
weight, and the overflow menu shows the control's automation name rather than the control itself.

### Binding to a view model

A file browser keeps the path in its view model and binds the breadcrumb to it. With CommunityToolkit.Mvvm, the path is
an `ObservableCollection<string>` that the view model changes, and the breadcrumb only displays it.

```csharp
public partial class FolderBrowserViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    public ObservableCollection<string> Path { get; } = new() { "Home", "Projects", "Acme Analytics" };

    public void OpenFolder(string name)
    {
        Path.Add(name);
        // Load the listing for the new path here.
    }

    public void NavigateTo(int index)
    {
        while (Path.Count > index + 1)
        {
            Path.RemoveAt(Path.Count - 1);
        }
    }

    [RelayCommand]
    private void GoUp()
    {
        if (Path.Count > 1)
        {
            Path.RemoveAt(Path.Count - 1);
        }
    }
}
```

```xml
<StackPanel Spacing="12">
    <arc:Breadcrumb ItemsSource="{Binding Path}" Label="Folder path" />
    <arc:Button Content="Up one level" Variant="Ghost" Command="{Binding GoUpCommand}" />
</StackPanel>
```

```csharp
breadcrumb.ItemClick += (_, e) => viewModel.NavigateTo(e.Index);
```

The breadcrumb never writes to the collection. A crumb choice is a request, so
the view model decides whether the navigation happens, truncates the path with `NavigateTo`, and loads the new
listing. The `Path` collection is the only source of truth; do not keep a second copy of the current folder name.

### Example: billing section header

A page header in an admin console for one invoice. The path says where the invoice sits, the heading names it, and the
two buttons act on it. The current crumb is the invoice ID, which is text and not a link, so the person sees the
location without a link that leads back to the same page. The label "Invoice location" distinguishes this landmark from
the navigation in the sidebar.

![A billing page header with an invoice breadcrumb, a heading and two actions](https://docs.tkcode.si/shots/Docs/Navigation/Breadcrumb/images/InvoiceHeader.webp)

```xml
<StackPanel Width="640" Spacing="12">
    <arc:Breadcrumb Label="Invoice location">
        <arc:BreadcrumbItem Content="Acme Analytics" />
        <arc:BreadcrumbItem Content="Billing" />
        <arc:BreadcrumbItem Content="Invoices" />
        <arc:BreadcrumbItem Content="inv_2026_0412" />
    </arc:Breadcrumb>
    <TextBlock Text="Invoice inv_2026_0412"
               FontSize="24"
               FontWeight="SemiBold"
               Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
    <TextBlock Text="Northwind Trading, issued April 3, 2026. Paid on April 9, 2026."
               FontSize="14"
               TextWrapping="Wrap"
               Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
    <StackPanel Orientation="Horizontal" Spacing="8">
        <arc:Button Content="Download PDF" Variant="Secondary" />
        <arc:Button Content="Send receipt" />
    </StackPanel>
</StackPanel>
```

### Content guidelines

- **Crumb label**: the name of the place as the person knows it, in title case when it is a proper name ("Acme
  Analytics") and sentence case for a generic section ("Billing"). Keep each label to one or two words so the path
  stays on one line.
- **Current crumb**: the name of the page, not a sentence. It repeats the heading, so keep the two identical.
- **Label (landmark)**: a short noun phrase that names the path, such as "Invoice location" or "Folder path". Avoid
  "Breadcrumb" in translated interfaces; name the content.
- **Overflow label**: say what the button reveals ("Show hidden path"), not what it is made of.

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| Landmark label "Breadcrumb" | Invoice location |
| Current crumb as a link to the same page | The current page name, without a link |
| Overflow label "More" | Show hidden path |
| Crumb "Go to the billing overview page" | Billing |
| Crumb "Current page: Invoices" | Invoices |

### Best practices

**Do**

- Put the breadcrumb above the page heading, and make the heading and the current crumb the same name, so the path and
  the title agree.
- Set `Label` on every breadcrumb when a page has more than one navigation landmark, so assistive technology users can
  tell them apart.
- Use `ItemClick` for in-app navigation, so the view model decides how the navigation happens and the crumb stays a
  simple request.
- Set `MaxVisibleItems` for paths that can grow past what a column holds, and test the path at the narrowest width the
  page supports.

**Avoid**

- Using a breadcrumb for sibling views or steps. People expect the crumbs to lead up the hierarchy, and sibling views
  or steps send them sideways or forward, which confuses the path.
- Linking the current page. The last crumb is the page the person is on; a link to it reloads the same view and makes
  the current state harder to read.
- Building the path from strings in code-behind and then copying it into the view. Bind the path to one collection so
  that the crumbs and the content change together.
- Putting controls or long sentences into the crumbs. A crumb does not wrap its own label, so a sentence makes one crumb
  much wider than the rest and pushes the path onto a second line.

### Common questions

**Why does the current crumb not respond to a click?** The last crumb is the current page, so it is not interactive,
has no hover underline and is not in the tab order. Its `IsCurrent` value follows the position: whichever crumb is last
in the path is current.

**How do I stop a middle crumb from being a link?** Set `IsClickable="False"` on that `BreadcrumbItem`. It stays in the
path and its label stays visible, but it is plain text and cannot be chosen.

**What do I read to know which crumb was chosen, and how do I get the data item?** Read `e.Index` and `e.Item` in the
`ItemClick` handler. For an `ItemsSource` path, `Item` is the data object; for inline crumbs it is the `BreadcrumbItem`.

**Does the overflow menu close when the path changes?** Yes. Changing the items or `MaxVisibleItems` closes the menu,
so a path update that arrives while the menu is open does not leave a stale list on screen.

**Can the path show more than one line?** Yes. The crumbs wrap onto a new line when the path is wider than the space,
with 2 px between the lines. Prefer `MaxVisibleItems` when the path can get long, because a wrapped path is harder to
scan.

## API reference

### Breadcrumb

Arc breadcrumb: where a page sits in a hierarchy, from the root to the current page. Crumbs are separated by chevrons; the last one is the current page (accent, medium weight, not a link) and every crumb reserves the width of its medium-weight label so becoming current never shifts the path. Crumbs present at first render stay still; crumbs added later slide in 8px from the path before them out of a subtle blur while their siblings make room on the smooth spring, and removed crumbs slide 4px back as they fade. Items are `BreadcrumbItem`s written inline or generated from `ItemsSource` (`ItemTemplate` renders the label). Choosing a crumb raises `ItemClick`, runs its `Command` and opens its `NavigateUri`. `MaxVisibleItems` (off by default, as in Arc) folds the middle of a long path into an overflow menu.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Label` | `string` | `"Breadcrumb"` | Accessible name of the navigation landmark. |
| `MaxVisibleItems` | `int` | `0` | When greater than 1 and the path is longer, the root and the last `MaxVisibleItems − 1` crumbs stay visible and the rest collapse into an overflow menu. 0 (Arc default) never collapses. |
| `OverflowLabel` | `string` | `"Show hidden path"` | Accessible name of the overflow button. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ItemClick` | `BreadcrumbItemClickEventArgs` | Raised when a crumb or an overflow entry is chosen. |

Derives from `ItemsControl`: every member of `ItemsControl` works as well.

## Accessibility

- The root is a navigation landmark named by `Label`, which defaults to "Breadcrumb". Its crumbs form a list, and each
  one is announced with its position and the size of the path, for example "2 of 4".
- The current crumb is announced as the current page. It is text, not a button or a link, and it cannot take focus.
- A crumb with a `NavigateUri` is announced as a link; a crumb that can be chosen otherwise is announced as a button.
- The chevron separators are hidden from assistive technology.
- The overflow button is named by `OverflowLabel`, which defaults to "Show hidden path". The hidden crumbs appear in its
  menu with their own names.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` | Move between the crumbs that can be chosen, and the overflow button; the current crumb is skipped |
| `Left` / `Right` | Move focus to the previous or next crumb that can be chosen |
| `Enter` / `Space` | Choose the focused crumb, which raises `ItemClick` and runs its command or opens its address |
| `Down` / `Up` | In the overflow menu, move to the next or previous entry, wrapping at the ends |
| `Home` / `End` | In the overflow menu, move to the first or last entry |
| `Enter` / `Space` in the overflow menu | Choose the entry; the menu closes and focus returns to the button |
| `Escape` | In the overflow menu, close it and return focus to the overflow button |

A pointer press and release on a crumb chooses it, when the release happens inside the crumb.

## Motion

- A new crumb slides in from the left and unblurs while its siblings make room with a smooth spring.
- A removed crumb moves 4px left and fades out quickly. The remaining crumbs make room.
- A path that does not change does not animate its layout.
- Reduced motion and Off apply added and removed crumbs at once. The slide and the exit run only at full motion.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| A crumb is added at the end | Slides in 8 px from the left and unblurs over the standard duration | Shown at once | Shown at once |
| A crumb is removed | Moves 4 px left, fades and blurs out over 120 ms | Removed at once | Removed at once |
| Crumbs after a change | Glide to their new positions on the smooth spring | Jump to their new positions | Jump to their new positions |
| Hover, focus, current | The label color crossfades | Immediate | Immediate |

## Related

- `Tabs` for sibling views of one object.
- `TreeView` for browsing a whole hierarchy.
- `Pagination` for moving through pages of results.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `Tabs` | The views are peers of the same object, and each has its own panel |
| `TreeView` | People browse a hierarchy by expanding and collapsing nodes |
| `Pagination` | The results are one collection split into pages |
| `Stepper` | The person completes steps in a fixed order |
| `PageHeader` (block) | A page needs a heading, a breadcrumb and actions in one standard header |
| `Select` / `Combobox` | The person picks one value from a list in a form |

---

# Pagination

> Move through a long collection with clear bounds.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/pagination

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.PaginationDefaultDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12">
        <arc:Pagination x:Name="Pager"
                        PageCount="12"
                        CurrentPage="1"
                        PageChanged="OnPageChanged" />
        <TextBlock x:Name="Status"
                   Text="Page 1 of 12"
                   FontSize="12"
                   TextWrapping="Wrap"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class PaginationDefaultDemo : UserControl
{
    public PaginationDefaultDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
    }

    private void OnPageChanged(object? sender, PaginationPageChangedEventArgs e)
        => Status.Text = $"Page {e.NewPage} of {Pager.PageCount}";
}
```

## When to use

`Pagination` moves a person through one collection that the application loads a page at a time: the invoice list in a
billing console, the orders table in a store back office, the search results of a CRM. The control holds the current
page number and the page count, draws the previous and next buttons and a window of five page buttons, and leaves the
loading to the application. It sits under the data it pages, where the person looks for the next set of rows.

- **Invoices and payments in a billing console**: a list of 248 invoices loaded 10 at a time from the server. The
  footer shows Page 12 of 25, the previous and next buttons stop at the ends, and the page number lives in the view
  model so a refresh keeps the person on the same page.
- **Orders and returns in a store back office**: the orders table pages through the server results, and the page
  number is also the value a support agent quotes ("page 4 of the returns queue").
- **Search results in an internal tool**: a result set that is too long to scroll, where the count is known and each
  page is a separate request.
- **Audit logs and event streams with a known count**: the page count comes from the server's total, so the bounds of
  the list are visible before the person clicks.

## When not to use

- **Browsing a slideshow of items**, such as product photos or onboarding cards: use `Carousel`, which steps through
  content that the person views one item at a time.
- **Reading a long feed as it scrolls**, such as an activity stream or a log that grows: use `Timeline` inside a
  scrolling container such as `ScrollArea`. Page buttons break the reading flow of a feed.
- **Moving to a location inside a hierarchy**, such as Billing, then Invoices, then the invoice: use `Breadcrumb`,
  which shows the path to the current page.
- **Switching between views of the same object**, such as Overview, Activity and Settings: use `Tabs`.
- **Choosing a range of dates or numbers**: use `DateRangePicker` or a `Slider`. A page number does not describe a
  range of values.

## Usage

Bind `CurrentPage` and `PageCount`. The control renders a window of five page buttons, which moves with the current
page.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:Pagination PageCount="{Binding PageCount}"
                    CurrentPage="{Binding CurrentPage, Mode=TwoWay}" />
</UserControl>
```

`Pagination` derives from Avalonia's `TemplatedControl`, not from a list. It has no `ItemsSource`, and it never loads or
counts anything: the application computes the page count and reacts to page changes. `CurrentPage` is two-way by
default, so `Mode=TwoWay` is optional. Both values are plain integers, so the same control works with a count from
a server response, a local list or a constant.

### Anatomy

1. **Landmark** (`Label`): a navigation landmark with the name "Pagination" by default. It is not drawn.
2. **Previous button** (`PreviousLabel` is its accessible name): a 36 px square button with a 16 px left chevron. It is
   disabled on the first page and stays in place.
3. **Page buttons**: five 36 px square buttons with 4 px between them. They show the numbers in tabular figures at the
   extra-small type size, in the secondary text color, and take the control radius.
4. **Current-page mark**: a surface-colored pill with a 1 px border and the resting shadow. It sits under the current
   number and glides to the next number when the page changes.
5. **Boundary buttons and ellipses** (`ShowBoundaryPages`): the first and last page buttons and a 24 px ellipsis on
   each side of the window. They appear only when the window does not reach the ends.
6. **Next button** (`NextLabel` is its accessible name): the mirror of the previous button, disabled on the last page.
7. **Focus ring**: a 2 px ring in the focus color, drawn 4 px outside the button. It appears only for keyboard focus.

The control lays the items out in a row and keeps them left-aligned. Disabled buttons drop to 40% opacity and show the
"not allowed" cursor.

### Reacting to a page change

Handle `PageChanged` to load the page. `NewPage` is the page the user asked for, and `OldPage` is the page before the
change. The event is raised whenever `CurrentPage` changes, so a change made by code (a binding, a reset after a
filter) raises it too.

```csharp
pagination.PageChanged += async (_, e) =>
{
    status.Text = $"Page {e.NewPage} of {pagination.PageCount}";
    await LoadPageAsync(e.NewPage);
};
```

`NewPage` is the raw value of `CurrentPage`, not the value after clamping. If code sets `CurrentPage` to 99 on a list
of 25 pages, `NewPage` is 99 while the buttons show page 25; clamp it in the handler, or keep `CurrentPage` in range
in the view model (see below).

### Boundary pages

`ShowBoundaryPages` keeps the first and last page one click away, with an ellipsis between them and the window. It is
an addition beyond Arc and is off by default. The boundary buttons appear only when `PageCount` is greater than five,
and each one appears only when the window does not already reach its end. Use it for a long list where the person may
need the first or last page quickly, such as a log that is read from the newest entry.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.PaginationBoundaryPagesDemo">
    <arc:Pagination PageCount="48" CurrentPage="20" ShowBoundaryPages="True" />
</UserControl>
```

### Few pages and no pages

With fewer than five pages, all of them are shown; the arrows disable at the ends. A `PageCount` of `0` renders an
empty navigation landmark: the page buttons and the arrows are hidden, so only the landmark remains. Use zero for an
empty result, and show an empty state in place of the control.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.PaginationFewPagesDemo">
    <arc:Pagination PageCount="3" CurrentPage="2" />
</UserControl>
```

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.PaginationNoPagesDemo">
    <WrapPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center" ItemSpacing="12" LineSpacing="12">
        <arc:Pagination PageCount="0" />
        <TextBlock Text="(nothing to page)"
                   FontSize="12"
                   TextWrapping="Wrap"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
    </WrapPanel>
</UserControl>
```

### Labels

`Label` names the navigation landmark. `PreviousLabel`, `NextLabel` and `PageLabelFormat` name the buttons for
assistive technology. Set them when the default text is not in the user's language. `PageLabelFormat` takes a `{0}`
placeholder for the page number and is formatted with the current culture.

```xml
<arc:Pagination Label="Results pages"
                PreviousLabel="Previous page"
                NextLabel="Next page" />
```

### Binding to a view model

An invoice list keeps the current page and the page count in its view model. The count is derived from the total that
the server returns, and a change of the current page loads the matching rows. With CommunityToolkit.Mvvm,
the generated partial method runs when the person changes the page, so the load does not depend on the view.

```csharp
public sealed record InvoiceRow(string Id, string Customer, string Amount, string Status);

public sealed record InvoicePage(int Total, IReadOnlyList<InvoiceRow> Rows);

public interface IInvoiceService
{
    Task<InvoicePage> GetPageAsync(int page, int pageSize);
}

public partial class InvoiceListViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    private const int PageSize = 10;
    private readonly IInvoiceService _invoices;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private int _currentPage = 1;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private int _pageCount;

    public ObservableCollection<InvoiceRow> Rows { get; } = new();

    public InvoiceListViewModel(IInvoiceService invoices)
    {
        _invoices = invoices;
    }

    partial void OnCurrentPageChanged(int value)
    {
        _ = LoadPageAsync(value);
    }

    private async Task LoadPageAsync(int page)
    {
        var result = await _invoices.GetPageAsync(page, PageSize);
        PageCount = (int)Math.Ceiling(result.Total / (double)PageSize);
        if (PageCount > 0 && page > PageCount)
        {
            // The list shrank: move to the last page, which loads it.
            CurrentPage = PageCount;
            return;
        }
        Rows.Clear();
        foreach (var row in result.Rows)
        {
            Rows.Add(row);
        }
    }
}
```

```xml
<arc:Pagination PageCount="{Binding PageCount}"
                CurrentPage="{Binding CurrentPage}"
                Label="Invoice pages" />
```

`CurrentPage` is two-way, so the control writes the page the person picks back to the view model, and the view model
reacts through its own property. `PageChanged` is not needed in this design. Use it when the view code, not the view
model, must act on the change, for example to scroll a list to its top.

### Keeping the page in range

The control clamps the page it shows, but it never changes the bound value on its own. Reducing `PageCount` below
`CurrentPage` (after a filter removes rows, for example) leaves `CurrentPage` where it was: the buttons show the last
page, and the value in the view model is out of range. Set `CurrentPage` to `PageCount` in the view model when the
count changes, as `LoadPageAsync` does in the example above.

`EffectivePage` is the page the buttons show, and it is 0 when there are no pages. `WindowStart` is the first number
in the five-page window. `GoToPage(page)` moves to a page, clamped to the valid range, and returns `false` when nothing
changed. `NextPage()` and `PreviousPage()` move one page and return `false` at the ends. Use these methods in code
behind or in a keyboard shortcut, so that the same rules apply as for the buttons.

```csharp
// A shortcut that moves to the last page without knowing the count in advance.
pagination.GoToPage(int.MaxValue);
```

### Example: invoice list footer

A table of invoices with its pagination footer. The footer states the page and the total in words, which is the first
thing a person checks after a page change, and the control sits at the right so the number and the arrows read as one
group. The current page is 12 of 25, so the window is 10 to 14 and both arrows are enabled. The label names the
landmark "Invoice pages" for a screen reader user, and the rows show the amounts with two decimals and the status as
text, not only a color.

![An invoice table with a footer showing page 12 of 25 and a pagination control](https://docs.tkcode.si/shots/Docs/Navigation/Pagination/images/InvoiceFooter.webp)

### Content guidelines

- **Summary text**: state the range in words next to the control: "Page 12 of 25, 248 invoices" or "Showing 111 to 120
  of 248". The control shows numbers only, so the words carry the meaning for a person who scans the footer.
- **Labels**: name the list, not the control: "Invoice pages", "Results pages". The landmark name is read aloud, so
  "Pagination" alone tells a screen reader user nothing about the content.
- **Button names**: keep the default "Previous page" and "Next page" unless the application language differs. Format
  page labels with a `{0}` placeholder, such as "Go to page {0}", only when the default "Page {0}" reads wrong.
- **Empty results**: do not show page controls for zero results. Show the empty state with a sentence that says what
  was searched for.

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| Label "Pagination" | Invoice pages |
| Footer "12 / 25" | Page 12 of 25, 248 invoices |
| Previous (icon only, no name) | Previous page |
| Pagination under an empty table | No invoices match these filters. |

### Best practices

**Do**

- Keep `CurrentPage` in range in the view model, and set it to `PageCount` when the count shrinks, so the bound value
  always matches what the buttons show.
- Load the page in the view model, from the page number, so a refresh and a deep link can reach the same page.
- Show the range and the total in words next to the control, so the person knows how many rows exist before they page.
- Set `Label` for each pagination on a page, so that two lists on one screen read as two landmarks.

**Avoid**

- Showing a page count that is not from the server total. A count computed from the rows already loaded hides the rest
  of the list and makes the last page look like the end.
- Clearing the rows before the next page arrives. Keep the current rows on screen while the request runs, and show the
  change in the footer text, so the person sees progress rather than an empty table.
- Using `ShowBoundaryPages` on a short list. It adds ellipses and buttons that a three-page list does not need.
- Setting `PageCount` to a value computed while the total is still loading. A zero or stale count makes the arrows
  disabled for the wrong reason.

### Common questions

**Does the control let people type a page number or change the page size?** No. Arc's pagination is controlled: it shows
the window and the arrows only. Add a page-size selector with `Select` and a jump-to-page field with `NumberField`
beside it, and call `GoToPage` from their handlers.

**Why does `PageChanged` fire when I set `CurrentPage` in code?** The event is raised from the property change, so any
change raises it, from the person or from code. Compare `e.NewPage` with the page you last loaded before you start a
request, so the same page is not loaded twice.

**What happens when `PageCount` is 0?** The page buttons and the arrows are hidden, and `EffectivePage` is 0. The
navigation landmark stays in the tree, so keep it on the page only when there is something to page through, or hide
the control in the view.

**Can I show more than five pages at once?** No. The window is always five page buttons (`WindowSize` is 5). For the
first and last page, use `ShowBoundaryPages`; for anything else, use a different component or a list with its own
scrolling.

## API reference

### Pagination

Arc pagination: previous and next buttons around a sliding window of five page buttons and one current-page mark that travels between them on a morph spring. When the window moves, the numbers travel like a belt by the number of slots it moved (smooth spring), entering numbers fade in and leaving ones fade out quickly. `CurrentPage` is 1-based, two-way and clamped to `1..PageCount`; with `ShowBoundaryPages` the first and last pages stay reachable behind an ellipsis.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `CurrentPage` | `int` | `1` | The current page, 1-based. Two-way; values outside `1..PageCount` are clamped for display. |
| `PageCount` | `int` | `0` | Number of pages; 0 renders an empty navigation landmark. |
| `ShowBoundaryPages` | `bool` | `false` | Keeps the first and last pages visible behind an ellipsis when the window does not reach them (not in Arc). |
| `Label` | `string` | `"Pagination"` | Accessible name of the navigation landmark. |
| `PreviousLabel` | `string` | `"Previous page"` | Accessible name of the previous button. |
| `NextLabel` | `string` | `"Next page"` | Accessible name of the next button. |
| `PageLabelFormat` | `string` | `"Page {0}"` | Format of a page button's accessible name; `{0}` is the page number. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `PageChanged` | `PaginationPageChangedEventArgs` | Raised after the user (or code) changes the page. |

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

## Accessibility

- The control is a navigation landmark named by `Label`, and it is announced as a group of controls.
- Each page button is named by `PageLabelFormat`, for example "Page 3". The current page has the current-page state.
- The previous and next buttons are disabled at the ends and keep their names.
- Tab moves between the previous button, the page buttons and the next button. Enter or Space goes to the focused page.
  Left and Right arrows move focus between the buttons.
- The ellipses and the hidden buttons are not focusable and are hidden from assistive technology.
- Keyboard focus follows the number: when the window moves while a page button has focus, focus moves with that number
  to its new slot.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` | Move between the previous button, the visible page buttons and the next button; disabled arrows are skipped |
| `Enter` / `Space` | Go to the focused page, or to the previous or next page on an arrow |
| `Left` / `Right` | Move focus to the previous or next enabled button; the page does not change until Enter or Space |

## Motion

- A single current-page mark glides to the selected button on a morph spring.
- When the window moves, the numbers slide like a belt by the number of slots that moved, and the new numbers
  fade in.
- Reduced motion moves the mark at once and replaces the numbers in place. Off applies the change at once.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| The current page changes | The mark glides to the new number on the morph spring | The mark moves at once | Immediate |
| The window moves by some slots | Numbers travel by the slots that moved (40 px each) on the smooth spring; new numbers fade in | Numbers replaced in place | Immediate |
| A number leaves the window | Slides on and fades out in 120 ms | Removed at once | Immediate |
| Press on an arrow | The arrow scales to 96% while held | No press scale | No press scale |
| Hover, focus | The background and text colors crossfade | Immediate | Immediate |

## Related

- `Tabs` for switching between views rather than pages of one collection.
- `Breadcrumb` for the location of a page in a hierarchy.
- `Carousel` for stepping through slides.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `Tabs` | The views are peers of one object, and each has its own panel |
| `Breadcrumb` | The page sits in a hierarchy and the person needs the path back up |
| `Carousel` | The items are viewed one at a time, such as product photos |
| `Timeline` | A feed or log is read in order and the list grows as it scrolls |
| `ScrollArea` | A long list is read by scrolling, not by changing pages |
| `Select` / `NumberField` | The footer also needs a page-size selector or a jump-to-page field |
| `DateRangePicker` / `Slider` | The person chooses a range of dates or values, not a page |

# Scroll area

> A native scroll container with thin overlay scrollbars and edge fades that appear only when content overflows.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/scroll-area

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ScrollAreaVerticalDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12">
        <Border HorizontalAlignment="Left"
                BorderThickness="1"
                CornerRadius="18"
                ClipToBounds="True"
                BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Border}">
            <arc:ScrollArea Width="360"
                            Height="260"
                            CornerRadius="18"
                            Label="Release notes"
                            EdgesChanged="OnEdgesChanged">
                <ItemsControl>
                    <ItemsControl.ItemTemplate>
                        <DataTemplate x:DataType="x:String">
                            <Border Padding="16,12"
                                    BorderThickness="0,0,0,1"
                                    BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource BorderSubtle}">
                                <TextBlock Text="{Binding}"
                                           FontSize="14"
                                           TextWrapping="Wrap"
                                           Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
                            </Border>
                        </DataTemplate>

                    <x:String>v1.7 · Webhooks</x:String>

        </Border>
```
