
```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class ScrollAreaVerticalDemo : UserControl
{
    public ScrollAreaVerticalDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
    }

    private void OnEdgesChanged(object? sender, ScrollAreaEdgesChangedEventArgs e)
        => Edges.Text = "Edges: " + string.Join(", ",
            new[] { e.Edges.Top ? "top" : null, e.Edges.Bottom ? "bottom" : null }.Where(s => s is not null).DefaultIfEmpty("none"));
}
```

## When to use

`ScrollArea` gives a fixed-size region its own scrolling, so a panel can hold more content than its space without
changing the layout of the page around it. It sits inside a shell, a side panel or a dialog, where the frame is
set and the content inside it grows with the data.

- **Side panels and inspectors**: the activity timeline of a customer record or the line items of an order, beside
  a list that must stay visible. The panel keeps its height and the timeline scrolls inside it.
- **Horizontal strips of cards or tags**: a row of plan cards on a billing page or a row of filter chips above a
  table. `Horizontal` with a mandatory snap keeps each card aligned when the person scrolls with the wheel or the trackpad.
- **Feeds that load more**: a CRM activity feed or a delivery log that fetches the next page when the bottom edge
  reports that nothing is left beyond it. `EdgesChanged` supplies that signal.
- **Payloads and logs in developer tools**: a webhook request body or a deployment log in a fixed-height panel,
  where the person reads from the top and the fade shows that more text follows.
- **Option lists in a sheet or a popover**: a long list of regions or currencies that does not fit the overlay.

## When not to use

- **Paging through items one at a time**: use `Carousel`, which moves between slides and shows position.
- **Long text that should be shortened**: use `ExpandableText`, which clamps to a few lines and offers Read more.
- **Tabular data with columns and sorting**: use `Table`, or `DataGrid` for large data sets. A `ScrollArea`
  around a plain `StackPanel` measures every row, so a table of thousands of rows is slow.
- **A tree of nested items with keyboard navigation**: use `TreeView`, which handles expansion and arrow-key
  movement between levels.
- **Choosing one value from a long list**: use `Select` or `Combobox`, which own the list, its filter and its
  keyboard model.

## Usage

Set the axes with `Orientation`. The default is `Vertical`.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:ScrollArea Width="360"
                    Height="260"
                    Label="Release notes"
                    CornerRadius="18">
        <StackPanel Spacing="0">
            <TextBlock Text="v2.4 · Overlay scrollbars" Margin="16,12" />
            <TextBlock Text="v2.3 · Faster cold starts" Margin="16,12" />
            <TextBlock Text="v2.2 · Keyboard shortcuts" Margin="16,12" />
        </StackPanel>
    </arc:ScrollArea>
</UserControl>
```

`ScrollArea` derives from Avalonia's `ScrollViewer`, so the offset, extent and viewport, the snap point properties,
touch inertia, `ScrollChanged` and the scroll automation pattern all work as they do on a scroll viewer. Arc
replaces the native bars with overlay tracks, adds the edge fades and changes the default focus and scrollbar
behavior. The area clips its content to its bounds, so the content never paints outside the frame.

`Label` names the scroll area. A named area is announced as a region. Without a label, the content around the
area must explain what it holds.

### Anatomy

1. **Content** (`Content`): the child you scroll. It keeps its natural size; the area's `Width` and `Height` set the
   visible window.
2. **Edge fades**: a 28 px gradient at each edge (`FadeLength`) that dims the content where it is cut off. A fade
   appears only where content continues past that edge, and its length equals the hidden content, up to the maximum.
3. **Vertical track**: an 11 px hit area (the `TrackThickness` token) around a 5 px pill, 3 px from the trailing
   edge. Under the pointer or while dragged the pill grows to 7 px and moves to 2 px from the edge.
4. **Thumb color**: the foreground color at 30% opacity, rising to 46% while the pointer is over the track.
   The thumb is never shorter than 28 px and its position follows the offset.
5. **Horizontal track**: the same pill along the bottom edge, 11 px tall.
6. **Corner**: with `Both`, each track stops 13 px short of the corner, so the two tracks never cross.
7. **Focus ring**: a 2 px ring in the focus color, drawn inside the area so the clipping does not cut it. It shows
   only for keyboard focus.

The tracks and fades are absent when nothing overflows. A short area has no fade, no track and no `:overflow`
pseudo-class, so a list that grows or shrinks switches the cues on and off with its content.

### Axes and overlay bars

Choose the axes first, then the bar behavior.

- `Vertical` is the default for lists, feeds, logs and side panels. The horizontal bars are hidden.
- `Horizontal` is for strips of cards, tags or chips. The vertical wheel scrolls it sideways (see below).
- `Both` is for grids and wide tables that scroll in two directions. Use it sparingly, because two tracks and two
  fades compete with the content for attention.

Changing `Orientation` at run time updates the native bar visibility and the track margins, so the axes can follow a
view mode.

`OverlayScrollbarMode` decides when the bars show. `Auto` (the default) shows them while the content scrolls or the
mouse hovers over the area, and keeps them for `HideDelay` after the scrolling stops. Hover reveals the bars only
for mouse input, so a touch screen shows them only while the person is scrolling. `Always` keeps them visible
whenever the content overflows. Use `Always` for a feed, a log or a payload where the person must see that more
content exists, and `Auto` for a decorative or secondary panel.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ScrollAreaBothAxesDemo">
    <Border HorizontalAlignment="Left"
            BorderThickness="1"
            CornerRadius="18"
            ClipToBounds="True"
            BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Border}">
        <arc:ScrollArea Orientation="Both"
                        OverlayScrollbarMode="Always"
                        Height="240"
                        CornerRadius="18">
            <ItemsControl x:Name="Cells" Width="900" Height="600">
                <ItemsControl.ItemsPanel>
                    <ItemsPanelTemplate>
                        <UniformGrid Rows="12" Columns="18" />
                    </ItemsPanelTemplate>
                </ItemsControl.ItemsPanel>
                <ItemsControl.ItemTemplate>
                    <DataTemplate x:DataType="x:String">
                        <TextBlock Text="{Binding}"
                                   HorizontalAlignment="Center"
                                   VerticalAlignment="Center"
                                   FontSize="12"
                                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
                    </DataTemplate>
                </ItemsControl.ItemTemplate>
            </ItemsControl>
        </arc:ScrollArea>
    </Border>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class ScrollAreaBothAxesDemo : UserControl
{
    public ScrollAreaBothAxesDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        // A 12 by 18 sheet of cells: A1, B1, ... R1, A2, ...
        Cells.ItemsSource = Enumerable.Range(0, 12 * 18).Select(i => $"{(char)('A' + i % 18)}{i / 18 + 1}").ToArray();
    }
}
```

### Horizontal strip

A vertical wheel scrolls a horizontal area sideways while it can, then hands the wheel back to the page. Set
`HorizontalSnapPointsType` to make the items snap.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ScrollAreaHorizontalStripDemo">
    <Border HorizontalAlignment="Left"
            BorderThickness="1"
            CornerRadius="18"
            ClipToBounds="True"
            BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Border}">
        <arc:ScrollArea Orientation="Horizontal"
                        HorizontalSnapPointsType="Mandatory"
                        CornerRadius="18"
                        Label="Cards">
            <StackPanel Orientation="Horizontal" Spacing="12" Margin="16">
                <StackPanel.Styles>
                    <Style Selector="Border.tile">
                        <Setter Property="Width" Value="160" />
                        <Setter Property="Height" Value="100" />
                        <Setter Property="Padding" Value="14" />
                        <Setter Property="CornerRadius" Value="18" />
                        <Setter Property="BorderThickness" Value="1" />
                        <Setter Property="Background" Value="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource SurfaceMuted}" />
                        <Setter Property="BorderBrush" Value="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Border}" />
                    </Style>
                    <Style Selector="Border.tile > TextBlock">
                        <Setter Property="FontSize" Value="14" />
                        <Setter Property="FontWeight" Value="Medium" />
                        <Setter Property="TextWrapping" Value="Wrap" />
                        <Setter Property="Foreground" Value="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
                    </Style>
                </StackPanel.Styles>
                <Border Classes="tile"><TextBlock Text="Card 1" /></Border>
                <Border Classes="tile"><TextBlock Text="Card 2" /></Border>
                <Border Classes="tile"><TextBlock Text="Card 3" /></Border>
                <Border Classes="tile"><TextBlock Text="Card 4" /></Border>
                <Border Classes="tile"><TextBlock Text="Card 5" /></Border>
                <Border Classes="tile"><TextBlock Text="Card 6" /></Border>
                <Border Classes="tile"><TextBlock Text="Card 7" /></Border>
                <Border Classes="tile"><TextBlock Text="Card 8" /></Border>
                <Border Classes="tile"><TextBlock Text="Card 9" /></Border>
                <Border Classes="tile"><TextBlock Text="Card 10" /></Border>
                <Border Classes="tile"><TextBlock Text="Card 11" /></Border>
                <Border Classes="tile"><TextBlock Text="Card 12" /></Border>
            </StackPanel>
        </arc:ScrollArea>
    </Border>
</UserControl>
```

The wheel conversion is controlled by `IsWheelToHorizontalEnabled` (default `True`). It applies only when the wheel
movement is mostly vertical, when `Ctrl` is not held and when the strip has room in the direction of the wheel.
Each wheel step moves the strip about 50 px. Set `HorizontalSnapPointsType="Mandatory"` for cards that must land
on an edge, and `None` (the default) for free scrolling.

### Edge fades and hide delay

`FadeLength` sets the length of each edge fade in pixels (default 28). Set it to `0` to turn the fades off.
`HideDelay` sets how long the bars stay visible after scrolling stops (default 900 ms).

```xml
<arc:ScrollArea FadeLength="0"
                HideDelay="0:0:1.5" />
```

### Driving it from code

`ScrollArea` has no value to bind, so it is driven from code. `Edges` is the current state of the four edges and
`EdgesChanged` reports each change. `ScrollBy` and `ScrollToOffset` scroll the area. Under full motion they animate
on a spring. Under Reduced or Off motion they jump to the target.

```csharp
area.EdgesChanged += (_, e) =>
{
    if (!e.Edges.Bottom)
    {
        LoadMoreItems();
    }
};
```

`EdgesChanged` is raised only when an edge changes between having and not having content beyond it, so it is the
right trigger for a load-more request. Read `Edges` when the state is needed at other times.

```csharp
area.ScrollBy(new Vector(0, 240));
area.ScrollToOffset(new Vector(0, 0));
```

`ScrollBy` and `ScrollToOffset` clamp the target to the content, so a large delta stops at the end. To bring a
specific item into view, call `BringIntoView()` on the item, which is the Avalonia method every control has.

### Example: activity feed beside a customer record

older events follow. The fade at the bottom edge confirms the same thing without a bar, and the top edge has no fade
because the feed starts at the newest event.

### Content guidelines

- **Label**: a noun phrase that names what the region holds, in sentence case: "Account activity", "Release notes".
  A screen reader announces it before the content, so "Scrollable area" tells the person nothing.
- **Headers and dates**: keep the header outside the area when it must stay visible while the content scrolls. Write
  dates as they appear everywhere else in the product, and write counts as digits.
- **Overflow cues**: do not add text such as "Scroll for more". The fade and the bar already say so, and the text
  takes space from the content.

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| Label="Scrollable area" | Label="Account activity" |
| Label="list" | Label="Release notes" |
| Scroll for more below | (no text: the fade and the bar show it) |

### Best practices

**Do**

- Give every area a `Label` when the content is worth finding by a screen reader, because a named area is announced
  as a region.
- Give the area a bounded size from its parent. Scrolling needs a viewport smaller than the content; a viewport that
  grows with its content has nothing to scroll.
- Use `OverlayScrollbarMode="Always"` for feeds, logs and payloads where the person must see that more exists.
- Use `EdgesChanged` for load-more triggers instead of watching offsets, because it fires once per change, not on
  every scroll step.

**Avoid**

- Nesting two areas that scroll in the same direction. The wheel leaves the inner area only at its edge, so the
  outer area moves in unexpected jumps. Nest only when the axes differ.
- Relying on `Auto` bars on a touch-first screen. Hover reveals the bars only for a mouse, so a touch user sees them
  only while scrolling, and an idle panel gives no sign that it scrolls.
- Setting `FadeLength="0"` on a feed. Without the fade a cut line looks like the end of the content, so the person
  stops scrolling.
- Putting thousands of rows in a plain `StackPanel` inside the area. The area measures all of them, which is slow for
  large lists; use a table or a list control that manages its own rows.
- Wrapping a whole page. The page layout should own the scrolling of the screen, so that its header and footer stay
  in place; an area around the whole screen traps the scroll.

### Common questions

**Why does the keyboard not scroll my area?** Keys reach the area only when the area itself has focus. A focused
`TextBox` or `ListBox` inside the area handles the arrow keys first. Move focus to the area with `Tab` or by
clicking its background.

**Why does the scrollbar not show on my touch screen?** In `Auto` mode, hover reveals the bars only for mouse input.
Touch shows them while scrolling and hides them after `HideDelay`. Set `OverlayScrollbarMode="Always"` when the bar
is a required cue.

**Why does the wheel leave a horizontal strip at its end?** That is intended. At either end the strip has no room
left in the wheel's direction, so the wheel goes to the page, and the page scrolls.

**How do I keep the view at the bottom of a log when new lines arrive?** Call `ScrollToOffset` with a large `Y` after
you append a line, for example `area.ScrollToOffset(new Vector(0, area.Extent.Height));`, which clamps to the end,
but only when the person was already at the bottom. Otherwise the scroll would pull them away from the line they
are reading.

## API reference

### ScrollArea

Arc scroll area: native scrolling (wheel, keyboard, touch inertia, snap points) with thin overlay scrollbars that appear while scrolling or hovering and fade away at rest, and edge fades that appear only where content continues, each exactly as long as the content hidden past that edge (up to `FadeLength`). The thumb thickens under the pointer, can be dragged, and pressing the track pages toward the pointer.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Orientation` | `ScrollAreaOrientation` | `Vertical` | Axes that scroll. Defaults to `Vertical`. |
| `FadeLength` | `double` | `28` | Length of each edge fade in px (Arc: 28). 0 turns the fades off. |
| `OverlayScrollbarMode` | `ScrollAreaScrollbarMode` | `Auto` | When the overlay scrollbars show. |
| `HideDelay` | `TimeSpan` | `00:00:00.9000000` | How long scrollbars linger after scrolling stops (Arc: 900ms). |
| `IsWheelToHorizontalEnabled` | `bool` | `true` | Turns vertical wheel movement into horizontal scrolling for horizontal areas, only while there is room. |
| `Label` | `string?` | `null` | Accessible name; a named area is announced as a region. |
| `Edges` | `ScrollAreaEdges` | – | *Read-only.* Which edges still have content beyond them. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `EdgesChanged` | `ScrollAreaEdgesChangedEventArgs` | Raised when content starts or stops extending past an edge. |

Pseudo-classes: `:overflow`, `:scrolling`

Derives from `ScrollViewer`: every member of `ScrollViewer` works as well.

| Type | Member | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `ScrollAreaOrientation` | `Vertical`, `Horizontal`, `Both` | The axes the area scrolls. |
| `ScrollAreaScrollbarMode` | `Auto`, `Always` | When the overlay bars show. `Auto` shows them while scrolling or hovering. |
| `ScrollAreaEdges` | `Top`, `Bottom`, `Left`, `Right` | `True` when content continues beyond that edge. |
| `ScrollAreaEdgesChangedEventArgs` | `Edges` | The new edge state. |

## Accessibility

- `Label` sets the accessible name of the area, and a named area is announced as a region. Without a label, the
  surrounding content must explain its purpose.
- The area is focusable and is in the tab order. Arrow keys, Page Up and Page Down, Home, End and Space scroll it
  natively.
- Scrolling keeps the `ScrollViewer` automation pattern. The overlay bars are visual only, so a screen reader user
  scrolls through the content and does not operate the bars.
- Under Reduced motion, the track page jumps instead of animating.

### Keyboard

The keys apply when the area itself has focus. `Shift` changes the direction of `Space` only.

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` | Move focus to or away from the area |
| `Up` / `Down` | Scroll a vertical area by 40 px |
| `Left` / `Right` | Scroll a horizontal area by 40 px |
| `Page Up` / `Page Down` | Scroll by 90% of the viewport along the main axis |
| `Space` / `Shift+Space` | Scroll forward or back by 90% of the viewport |
| `Home` / `End` | Scroll to the start or end of the axis. In `Both`, they move the vertical axis |

## Motion

- Bars fade in while the content scrolls or the pointer hovers over the area. They stay for `HideDelay` (900 ms)
  after scrolling stops, then fade out over 480 ms.
- The thumb gets thicker under the pointer, and it can be dragged. Dragging a thumb turns off snapping until the
  drag ends.
- Each edge fade grows with the first pixels of scrolling and is never longer than the hidden content.
- Reduced motion removes the bar fade and makes track paging instant.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| Bars appear | Fade in over the fast duration | Appear at once | Appear at once |
| Bars leave | Fade out over 480 ms, after `HideDelay` | Hide at once | Hide at once |
| Thumb under the pointer | Thickens from 5 to 7 px and darkens over the fast duration | Changes at once | Changes at once |
| Key, code or track scroll | Smooth spring toward the target | Jumps to the target | Jumps to the target |
| Edge fades | Length follows the hidden content as the person scrolls | Same | Same |

## Related

- `Carousel` pages through items one at a time, with position shown.
- `ExpandableText` clamps a single block of text to a few lines instead of scrolling it.
- `ResizablePanels` splits space between panes; put a `ScrollArea` inside a pane when that pane can overflow.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `Carousel` | People move between items one at a time and need a position indicator |
| `ExpandableText` | One block of text is long and should show a few lines with Read more |
| `ResizablePanels` | The person needs to decide how much room each pane gets |
| `Table` / `DataGrid` | The content is rows and columns that people sort or scan |
| `TreeView` | Items nest and people move between levels with the keyboard |

# Accordion

> Progressively reveal supporting information in place.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/accordion

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.AccordionDefaultDemo">
    <arc:Accordion>
        <arc:AccordionItem Header="What is included in the free plan?"
                           Content="Unlimited projects, three collaborators and a week of version history. Upgrade any time to add more people and keep history for a year." />
        <arc:AccordionItem Header="Can I change plans later?"
                           Content="Yes. Plan changes apply immediately and the difference is prorated on your next invoice." />
        <arc:AccordionItem Header="How do refunds work?"
                           Content="Annual plans can be refunded within 30 days. Monthly plans can be cancelled at any time and stay active until the end of the period." />
        <arc:AccordionItem Header="Do you offer discounts for nonprofits?"
                           Content="Registered nonprofits and schools get 50% off every paid plan. Contact support with your registration details." />
    </arc:Accordion>
</UserControl>
```

## When to use

`Accordion` is a column of question rows whose answers open in place. It suits content that a reader scans by its
heading and reads only where it matters: the page keeps its length and the reader keeps their place while one answer
opens and the others stay closed.

- **Help center and billing FAQs**: a page that answers "Can I change plans later?" or "How are refunds calculated?"
  for a SaaS product. One answer is open at a time, so the reader compares questions without leaving the page.
- **Settings pages with grouped explanations**: an admin console section such as "Data retention" or "Single sign-on"
  where each heading hides the consequences of a choice. The controls stay visible; the accordion holds the reasons.
- **Checkout and order review**: "Shipping address", "Payment method" and "Tax details" as collapsed rows, so the
  customer opens only the one they want to check before placing the order.
- **Developer documentation sidebars**: a list of "Rate limits", "Pagination" and "Webhook retries" beside an API
  reference, where each answer is a few short paragraphs and a code sample.

## When not to use

- **A single disclosure on its own**, such as a "Show plan details" panel on a pricing card: use `ExpandableCard`,
  which keeps the card's header visible and can grow sideways.
- **Sibling views of the same data**, such as "Overview", "Usage" and "Invoices" for one account: use `Tabs`, which
  shows one panel at a time and exposes the choices as a tab list.
- **One long paragraph** that only needs a "Read more" link, such as a product description or a review: use
  `ExpandableText`, which clamps the text to a number of lines.
- **Steps that must be completed in order**, such as a setup wizard: use `Stepper`, which shows progress and the
  current step.
- **Rows of records that people compare or sort**, such as invoices or usage by day: use `Table`, whose
  columns line up across rows.

## Usage

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:Accordion>
        <arc:AccordionItem Header="What is included in the free plan?">
            Unlimited projects, three collaborators and a week of version history.
        </arc:AccordionItem>
        <arc:AccordionItem Header="Can I change plans later?">
            Yes. Plan changes apply immediately and the difference is prorated on your next invoice.
        </arc:AccordionItem>
    </arc:Accordion>
</UserControl>
```

Each row is an `AccordionItem`. `Accordion` derives from Avalonia's `ItemsControl`, so the rows can also come from
`Items` or `ItemsSource`, and `AccordionItem` derives from `HeaderedContentControl`: `Header` is the question and
`Content` is the answer. The Arc additions are the open-row state (`ExpandedIndex`, `IsExpanded`), the single or
multiple mode, the size and the keyboard model between the questions. Clicking the open row closes it, and opening
another row closes the open one.

### Anatomy

1. **List rule**: a 1 px line above the first row in the border color. Each row draws its own 1 px rule below it,
   so the list has a rule above and between all of its rows.
2. **Question** (`Header`): the whole row is one button. In the Medium size it is at least 50 px tall, with 8 px of
   vertical padding and the small type size (`TypeSM`) at medium weight. In the Large size it is at least 76 px tall,
   with 20 px of vertical padding and the large type size (`TypeLG`).
3. **Chevron**: a 17 px down chevron that sits 20 px after the question in Medium and 32 px after it in Large. It
   is in the muted text color when the row is closed, changes to the foreground color when the row is open or the
   pointer is over the row, and turns 180 degrees when the row opens.
4. **Answer** (`Content`): the answer text in the secondary text color at the small size with a 1.4 line height in
   Medium. Medium answers keep 32 px of space on the right and 20 px below. Large answers use the base type size
   with a 1.65 line height, keep 48 px on the right and 24 px below, and wrap at about 62 characters (about 595 px).
5. **Row rule**: a 1 px line below each row in the border color.
6. **Focus ring**: a 2 px ring in the focus color, drawn 4 px outside the row horizontally and 2 px vertically, with a
   10 px corner radius. It appears only for keyboard focus.

Hover changes only the question text (to the secondary text color) and the chevron color. Nothing changes size.

### Sizes

`Size` sets the row size for every row of the accordion. `Medium` (the default) is the look for settings panels and
help drawers inside dense admin layouts. `Large` is for a page-level FAQ, where the questions are the headline and
the answers are read at body size.

```xml
<arc:Accordion Size="Large">
    <arc:AccordionItem Header="Can I cancel at any time?">
        Monthly plans stay active until the end of the period.
    </arc:AccordionItem>
</arc:Accordion>
```

Use one size per list. A Large list inside a narrow side panel pushes the answers into a long column, so switch to
Medium there. The size also applies to rows added later, because the accordion sets it on each row it prepares.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             xmlns:demos="using:TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.AccordionLargeDemo">
    <arc:Accordion x:Name="Questions" Size="Large" ExpandedIndex="-1">
        <arc:Accordion.ItemTemplate>
            <DataTemplate x:DataType="demos:AccordionFaq">
                <TextBlock Text="{Binding Question}" TextWrapping="Wrap" />
            </DataTemplate>
        </arc:Accordion.ItemTemplate>
        <arc:Accordion.ContentTemplate>
            <DataTemplate x:DataType="demos:AccordionFaq">
                <TextBlock Text="{Binding Answer}" TextWrapping="Wrap" />
            </DataTemplate>
        </arc:Accordion.ContentTemplate>
    </arc:Accordion>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public sealed record AccordionFaq(string Question, string Answer);

public partial class AccordionLargeDemo : UserControl
{
    public AccordionLargeDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Questions.ItemsSource = new AccordionFaq[]
        {
            new("What is included in the free plan?", "Unlimited projects, three collaborators and a week of version history. Upgrade any time to add more people and keep history for a year."),
            new("Can I change plans later?", "Yes. Plan changes apply immediately and the difference is prorated on your next invoice."),
            new("How do refunds work?", "Annual plans can be refunded within 30 days. Monthly plans can be cancelled at any time and stay active until the end of the period."),
            new("Do you offer discounts for nonprofits?", "Registered nonprofits and schools get 50% off every paid plan. Contact support with your registration details.")
        };
    }
}
```

### Data-driven rows

Set `ItemsSource`, `ItemTemplate` for the question and `ContentTemplate` for the answer. `ExpandedIndex = -1`
starts with every row closed, which is the usual choice for a FAQ, where no answer should be open before the reader
asks for one.

```xml
<arc:Accordion Size="Large"
               ExpandedIndex="-1"
               ItemsSource="{Binding Questions}">
    <arc:Accordion.ItemTemplate>
        <DataTemplate>
            <TextBlock Text="{Binding Question}" TextWrapping="Wrap" />
        </DataTemplate>
    </arc:Accordion.ItemTemplate>
    <arc:Accordion.ContentTemplate>
        <DataTemplate>
            <TextBlock Text="{Binding Answer}" TextWrapping="Wrap" />
        </DataTemplate>
    </arc:Accordion.ContentTemplate>
</arc:Accordion>
```

Give every data item the same two fields, a question and an answer. Both templates are applied to every row, open or
closed, so keep them light; the section on data shape explains how to load heavier content on demand.

### Single and multiple open rows

`ExpandMode` decides how many rows can be open. `Single` is the Arc default: one row is open at a time, opening
another closes the open one, and the open row can be closed so that no row is open. Use it when the reader is
choosing one answer to read, as in a FAQ.

`Multiple` lets rows open and close independently. Use it when the reader needs two answers side by side, such as
the limits of two plans, or when the rows are independent sections of one form-like page.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.AccordionMultipleDemo">
    <arc:Accordion ExpandMode="Multiple">
        <arc:AccordionItem Header="What is included in the free plan?"
                           Content="Unlimited projects, three collaborators and a week of version history. Upgrade any time to add more people and keep history for a year." />
        <arc:AccordionItem Header="Can I change plans later?"
                           Content="Yes. Plan changes apply immediately and the difference is prorated on your next invoice." />
        <arc:AccordionItem Header="How do refunds work?"
                           Content="Annual plans can be refunded within 30 days. Monthly plans can be cancelled at any time and stay active until the end of the period." />
    </arc:Accordion>
</UserControl>
```

In `Multiple` mode `ExpandedIndex` still exists. It holds the row that was opened last; when that row closes it moves
to the first row that is still open, or to `-1` when none is.

To start several rows open, set `IsExpanded="True"` on each `AccordionItem`. An item written open wins over the
`ExpandedIndex` default, so the two settings do not fight each other.

### Opening a row from code

`ExpandedIndex` and `IsExpanded` are two-way. Bind one to a view model property, or set them in code. `Toggle(int)`
opens or closes the row at an index, and `CollapseAll()` closes every row, which is the reset to use after a search
or a page change.

```csharp
accordion.ExpandedIndex = 2;
item.IsExpanded = false;

accordion.Toggle(0);
accordion.CollapseAll();
```

### Binding to a view model

A FAQ usually comes from the server and the open row belongs to the page's state. With CommunityToolkit.Mvvm, the view
model holds the question list and the open index, and the accordion binds to both.

```csharp
public interface IBillingApi
{
    Task<string[]> GetInvoiceRulesAsync(string question);
}

public sealed partial class FaqEntry : ObservableObject
{
    public FaqEntry(string question, string answer)
    {
        Question = question;
        Answer = answer;
    }

    public string Question { get; }

    public string Answer { get; }

    /// <summary>Detail rows, loaded the first time the row opens.</summary>
    [ObservableProperty]
    private string[]? _details;
}

public partial class BillingHelpViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    private readonly IBillingApi _billing;

    public BillingHelpViewModel(IBillingApi billing) => _billing = billing;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private int _openIndex = -1;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private ObservableCollection<FaqEntry> _entries = new()
    {
        new("Can I change plans later?", "Yes. Plan changes apply immediately and the difference is prorated on your next invoice."),
        new("How do refunds work?", "Annual plans can be refunded within 30 days. Monthly plans stay active until the end of the period.")
    };

    [RelayCommand]
    private void CollapseAll() => OpenIndex = -1;

    /// <summary>Loads the detail rows of one answer the first time its row opens.</summary>
    public async Task LoadDetailsAsync(FaqEntry entry)
    {
        if (entry.Details is null)
        {
            entry.Details = await _billing.GetInvoiceRulesAsync(entry.Question);
        }
    }
}
```

```xml
<StackPanel Width="640" Spacing="12">
    <Button Content="Collapse all" Command="{Binding CollapseAllCommand}" HorizontalAlignment="Right" />
    <arc:Accordion Size="Large"
                   ExpandedIndex="{Binding OpenIndex, Mode=TwoWay}"
                   ItemsSource="{Binding Entries}">
        <arc:Accordion.ItemTemplate>
            <DataTemplate>
                <TextBlock Text="{Binding Question}" TextWrapping="Wrap" />
            </DataTemplate>
        </arc:Accordion.ItemTemplate>
        <arc:Accordion.ContentTemplate>
            <DataTemplate>
                <TextBlock Text="{Binding Answer}" TextWrapping="Wrap" />
            </DataTemplate>
        </arc:Accordion.ContentTemplate>
    </arc:Accordion>
</StackPanel>
```

`ExpandedIndex` is the two-way property to bind: the reader's clicks write the index back to `OpenIndex`, and a
change to `OpenIndex` opens or closes the rows. Bind `ExpandMode` and `Size` one way, since they are set once per
page. Use `ExpandedChanged` on an `AccordionItem` (it bubbles, so one handler on the accordion sees every row) when
the view model needs to react to each open, for example to log which answer was read.

### Data shape and performance

Every row is an `AccordionItem` container with its own answer, and the answer stays mounted while the row is
closed. That is what lets a second click reverse an opening mid-flight, and it means the cost of a closed row is
the cost of its content. Keep answers to text and simple controls. When an answer needs data, such as the rows of a
small table, load it in the view model when the row opens instead of loading it up front for every row:

```csharp
// In the view's setup: one handler on the accordion receives every row's event.
accordion.AddHandler(AccordionItem.ExpandedChangedEvent, OnRowExpandedChanged);

private void OnRowExpandedChanged(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
{
    if (e.Source is AccordionItem { IsExpanded: true, DataContext: FaqEntry entry })
    {
        _ = _billingHelp.LoadDetailsAsync(entry);
    }
}
```

A FAQ of a few dozen rows is a normal load for this control. For long lists, group the rows under headings, or filter
them in the view model before they reach the accordion, because each row is a container that is measured and
arranged with the rest of the list.

### Example: billing help center

A help panel on a billing page of a SaaS admin console. It opens with the first answer, because the first question
is the one most people arrive with. The questions are complete sentences that a customer would type, the answers
name the dates and amounts, and the list uses the Large size because it is the page's main content. The width of
680 leaves the answers a comfortable line length.

![A billing help center with the first answer open and three closed questions](https://docs.tkcode.si/shots/Docs/Expand/Accordion/images/BillingHelp.webp)

```xml
<StackPanel Width="680" Spacing="16">
    <TextBlock Text="Billing questions"
               FontSize="20"
               FontWeight="SemiBold"
               Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
    <arc:Accordion Size="Large" ExpandedIndex="0">
        <arc:AccordionItem Header="When is the Team plan charged?">
            Acme Analytics charges the Team plan on the first day of each billing period. Annual plans are
            charged once a year on the date the subscription started.
        </arc:AccordionItem>
        <arc:AccordionItem Header="Can I change plans later?">
            Yes. Upgrades apply at once, and the unused part of your current plan is credited on the next invoice.
        </arc:AccordionItem>
        <arc:AccordionItem Header="How do refunds work for annual plans?">
            Annual plans can be refunded within 30 days of the charge. Contact billing with the invoice ID,
            such as inv_2026_0412.
        </arc:AccordionItem>
        <arc:AccordionItem Header="Who can see invoices?">
            Owners and billing admins can open and download every invoice. Members see only the plan name.
        </arc:AccordionItem>
    </arc:Accordion>
</StackPanel>
```

### Content guidelines

- **Question**: a complete question in sentence case, ending with a question mark, written the way a customer
  would ask it. A question names the topic, so the reader can scan the list without opening it.
- **Answer**: the direct answer in the first sentence, then the detail. Name dates, amounts and limits with digits
  ("30 days", "$24 per seat"). Keep an answer to one or two short paragraphs; longer material belongs on a linked
  page.
- **Headers in a settings list**: a noun phrase that names the setting, with the consequence in the answer.
- **Length**: a question should fit on one line at the chosen size. A longer question reads as a sentence to skim
  and wraps in the Large size.

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| Info | How refunds work for annual plans |
| Click to read | Can I change plans later? |
| Yes, you can do that anytime. | Yes. Plan changes apply immediately. |
| Billing | Who can see invoices? |
| Read the docs for more. | Owners and billing admins can download every invoice. |

### Best practices

**Do**

- Put the most useful question first and open it by default (`ExpandedIndex="0"`) when the page is a single topic,
  so the reader sees a real answer without a click.
- Start with `ExpandedIndex="-1"` for a long FAQ, so the page opens as a scannable list of questions.
- Keep one answer per question, so a row does not hide a second topic the reader might miss.
- Use `Multiple` only when the reader must compare answers. Two open rows are easy to compare; five start to
  compete for the screen.

**Avoid**

- Hiding a required step, such as a legal term or an error that needs action, behind a question. The reader may
  never open it, so show required text on the page.
- Mixing `Medium` and `Large` rows in one list. The two sizes differ in height and type, and the list looks
  inconsistent.
- Placing a form inside an answer. Fields inside a collapsed row are unreachable until the row opens, and a
  validation message that appears in a closed answer is missed. Put the form on the page.
- Loading heavy content for every row when the page opens. Load it when the row opens, as shown in
  "Data shape and performance".
- Using the accordion as navigation between pages. Rows toggle in place; use `Tabs` or a navigation list for
  separate views.

### Common questions

**How do I start with two rows open?** Set `IsExpanded="True"` on each `AccordionItem` that should be open. An item
written open wins over the `ExpandedIndex` default, so `ExpandedIndex` is not needed for those rows. Use `Multiple`
if the reader should be able to keep both open.

**Why does the open row close when I click it?** The open row closes on its own question, so the reader can collapse
everything. `ExpandedIndex` then becomes `-1`. To keep one row open at all times, set `OpenIndex` back to its index in
the view model when the index becomes `-1`, or accept the collapse as part of the design.

**How do I know which answer the reader opened?** Subscribe to `AccordionItem.ExpandedChangedEvent` on the
accordion, which bubbles from each row, and read `e.Source` as the `AccordionItem`. Its `DataContext` is the data
item when the rows come from `ItemsSource`.

**Can an answer contain a button or a link?** Yes. `Content` takes any control. A closed answer is inert: it cannot
be clicked or focused until its row opens.

## API reference

### Accordion

Arc accordion: a list of question rows that reveal their answers in place. The panel height follows the content on a smooth spring that never overshoots and retargets mid-flight, the answer settles down 6px out of a subtle blur as it opens, and the chevron turns on a snappy spring. Single mode (Arc) keeps one row open and lets it close; `Multiple` opens rows independently. Arrow keys move between the row triggers, Home / End jump to the ends, Enter / Space toggle. Rows are `AccordionItem`s written inline (`<arc:AccordionItem Header="Question">Answer</arc:AccordionItem>`) or generated from `ItemsSource` (`ItemTemplate` renders the question, `ContentTemplate` the answer).

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ExpandedIndex` | `int` | `0` | Index of the open row; −1 closes every row (Arc defaultOpen, default 0). Two-way. |
| `ExpandMode` | `AccordionExpandMode` | `Single` | Single (Arc) or multiple open rows. |
| `Size` | `AccordionSize` | `Medium` | Row size; `Large` suits page-level FAQs. |
| `ContentTemplate` | `IDataTemplate?` | `null` | Template for the answers of data items (the question uses `ItemTemplate`). |

Derives from `ItemsControl`: every member of `ItemsControl` works as well.

### AccordionItem

One row of an `Accordion`: `Header` is the question (the whole row is the trigger) and `Content` the answer. The answer stays mounted while closed so a second click mid-flight reverses from where it is; a closed answer takes no pointer or keyboard focus.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `IsExpanded` | `bool` | `false` | Whether the answer is open. Two-way. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ExpandedChanged` | `RoutedEventArgs` | Raised after the row opens or closes. |

Pseudo-classes: `:expanded`, `:large`

Derives from `HeaderedContentControl`: every member of `HeaderedContentControl` works as well.

### Enum values

`AccordionExpandMode` sets how many rows can be open.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `Single` | One row at a time; opening another closes it, and the open row can be closed (the Arc default) |
| `Multiple` | Rows open and close independently |

`AccordionSize` sets the row size.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `Medium` | Questions at the small type size on 50 px rows (the default) |
| `Large` | Page-level FAQ rows: questions at the large type size on 76 px rows, answers at body size |

## Accessibility

- Each row trigger is a button that exposes the expand and collapse pattern, so assistive technology announces
  whether the row is open or closed and the state changes when the row does.
- Each question is a heading at level 3, so screen reader users can move from question to question by heading.
- Each row takes its accessible name from its `Header` when the header is a string.
- Each answer is labeled by its question. A closed answer leaves the accessibility tree, is not hit-testable and
  takes no keyboard focus.
- When the open row closes while focus is inside its answer, focus moves back to the question, so focus never
  disappears into a hidden panel.
- Reduced motion shows the open and closed states at once, with no change in what is announced or focusable.

### Keyboard

The question is a button, so the standard button keys apply, and the accordion adds movement between questions.

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Enter` / `Space` | Opens or closes the focused row |
| `Down Arrow` / `Up Arrow` | Moves focus to the next or previous question; wraps from the last question to the first and back |
| `Home` / `End` | Moves focus to the first or last question |
| `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` | Moves through the questions and the controls inside open answers; closed answers take no focus |

Arrow keys and `Home` / `End` only move focus; they never open or close a row. Disabled rows are skipped by the
arrow keys.

## Motion

- The row height springs open on a smooth spring that does not overshoot. A second click during the motion turns
  the row around from its current height rather than from either end.
- The answer settles 6 px down into place out of a 2 px blur as it opens. On close, the answer fades quickly while the
  panel closes.
- The chevron turns 180 degrees on a snappy spring as the row opens.
- Reduced and Off motion show the same end states in one step.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| Row opens | Height springs open and the answer fades in on a standard tween | Shown open at once | Immediate |
| Row closes | Answer fades out quickly while the panel closes | Closed at once | Immediate |
| Answer settles | Moves 6 px into place out of a 2 px blur | Immediate | Immediate |
| Chevron turns | Turns 180 degrees on a snappy spring | Immediate | Immediate |
| Hover and focus | Question and chevron colors crossfade | Immediate | Immediate |

## Related

- `ExpandableCard` for one disclosure that grows a dense card.
- `ExpandableText` for a single long paragraph that is clamped to a few lines.
- `Tabs` for switching between views of the same content.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `ExpandableCard` | A single summary card hides details that open in place and can grow sideways |
| `ExpandableText` | One paragraph is clamped to a few lines with a "Read more" toggle |
| `Tabs` | The reader switches between sibling views of the same content |
| `Stepper` | The reader works through ordered steps with a visible position |
| `Card` | The content needs no disclosure and should stay visible |
| `Table` | The rows are records that people compare or sort |

# Expandable card

> Give a dense card more room when requested.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/expandable-card

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ExpandableCardDefaultDemo">
    <arc:ExpandableCard Header="Pro plan"
                        Description="$24 per month · billed yearly"
                        CollapsedWidth="420">
        <StackPanel Spacing="8">
            <TextBlock Text="Unlimited projects and collaborators."
                       FontSize="14"
                       TextWrapping="Wrap"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
            <TextBlock Text="Version history for a full year."
                       FontSize="14"
                       TextWrapping="Wrap"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
            <TextBlock Text="Priority support with a four-hour response time."
                       FontSize="14"
                       TextWrapping="Wrap"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
        </StackPanel>
    </arc:ExpandableCard>
</UserControl>
```

## When to use

`ExpandableCard` is a summary card whose header opens a details panel below it. The card keeps the title and a
one-line summary visible, so a list of cards stays scannable, and the details appear in place only for the people
who want them. The card can also grow sideways, which gives wide details, such as a log line or a status timeline,
room without leaving the list.

- **Deployment history in a developer console**: each release is a card with the build, the time and the outcome in
  the header. A failed deploy opens to show the failing health check; a successful one stays closed.
- **Order and shipment status in a customer account**: the header reads "Order #4821" with "Shipped, arrives
  Thursday" underneath. The details list the items, the carrier and the tracking number, and the summary rolls
  forward as the status changes.
- **Plan and subscription summaries in billing**: a plan card shows the price and the billing cycle, and opens to
  list the included seats, the limits and the invoice history.
- **Incident and alert queues**: a row of alerts where the header names the service and the time, and the details
  hold the error message and the last few log lines.

## When not to use

- **Several mutually exclusive sections of text**, such as the questions of an FAQ: use `Accordion`, which keeps
  one answer open at a time and lays the rows out as a single list.
- **A card with nothing to reveal**: use `Card`. A header that does nothing is a control with no purpose.
- **Browsing several cards in the same place**, such as a deck of product or project cards: use `CardStack`, which
  moves between cards rather than opening each one in place.
- **Editing a record**: use `Drawer` or `Dialog`. A form inside a card competes with the card's header and the
  layout around it, and it has no room for validation messages.
- **A long paragraph** that needs only a "Read more" toggle: use `ExpandableText`, which clamps the text to a set
  number of lines.

## Usage

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:ExpandableCard Header="Pro plan"
                        Description="$24 per month · billed yearly"
                        CollapsedWidth="420">
        <StackPanel Spacing="8">
            <TextBlock Text="Unlimited projects and collaborators." />
            <TextBlock Text="Version history for a full year." />
            <TextBlock Text="Priority support with a four-hour response time." />
        </StackPanel>
    </arc:ExpandableCard>
</UserControl>
```

`ExpandableCard` derives from Avalonia's `HeaderedContentControl`, so `Header` and `Content` work as they do on any
headered control. The card adds the summary line (`Description`), the trigger that covers the whole header, the
chevron, the details panel and the morph between the closed and open sizes. `Header` is the card title; `Description`
is the summary line under it; `Content` holds the details.

Without a width, the card fills its container.

### Anatomy

1. **Card surface**: the surface color with a 1 px border in the border color, the surface corner radius and the
   resting shadow. The surface clips its contents, so the header's hover fill follows the card's corners.
2. **Header trigger**: the whole header is one button, at least 64 px tall, with 20 px of padding on each side and
   16 px above and below. Hover and press change its background to the muted surface color.
3. **Title** (`Header`): the small type size at medium weight in the foreground color. A string header also becomes
   the card's accessible name.
4. **Summary line** (`Description`): the extra-small type size in the muted text color, 4 px below the title. When
   `Description` is null or empty, the line is hidden and the header shrinks to the title.
5. **Chevron**: an 18 px down chevron 20 px after the copy, in the muted text color while closed. It takes the
   foreground color while the card is open or the pointer is over the header, and it turns 180 degrees when the card
   opens.
6. **Details panel** (`Content`): the muted surface color with a 1 px divider above it. Its padding is 20 px on the
   sides, 16 px on top and 20 px below. The text uses the secondary text color at the small type size with a 1.4 line
   height. A closed panel is exactly zero pixels high, because the divider is an inset line rather than a border on
   the panel itself.
7. **Focus ring**: a 2 px ring in the focus color around the header, shown for keyboard focus only.

### Widths: CollapsedWidth and ExpandedWidth

`CollapsedWidth` caps the closed card's width in pixels, and the card is centered in its container. Leave it unset
and the closed card fills the container. `ExpandedWidth` caps the width while the card is open, so the card can grow
sideways. When `ExpandedWidth` is not set, the open card uses `CollapsedWidth`. When `CollapsedWidth` is not set and
`ExpandedWidth` is, the closed card fills the container and the open card is capped at `ExpandedWidth`.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ExpandableCardGrowingSidewaysDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12">
        <arc:ExpandableCard x:Name="Order"
                            Header="Order #4821"
                            Description="Shipped · arrives Thursday"
                            CollapsedWidth="360"
                            ExpandedWidth="520">
            <StackPanel Spacing="8">
                <TextBlock Text="2 × Linen shirt, 1 × Canvas tote"
                           FontSize="14"
                           TextWrapping="Wrap"
                           Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
                <TextBlock Text="Carrier: Northwind Express · tracking NW-22-9183"
                           FontSize="14"
                           TextWrapping="Wrap"
                           Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
                <TextBlock Text="Delivery window 9:00–13:00"
                           FontSize="14"
                           TextWrapping="Wrap"
                           Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
            </StackPanel>
        </arc:ExpandableCard>
        <WrapPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center" ItemSpacing="12" LineSpacing="12">
            <arc:Button Content="Advance status" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Click="OnAdvanceClick" />
        </WrapPanel>
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class ExpandableCardGrowingSidewaysDemo : UserControl
{
    private static readonly string[] Statuses =
    [
        "Shipped · arrives Thursday",
        "Out for delivery · arrives today",
        "Delivered · left at the front door"
    ];

    private int _step;

    public ExpandableCardGrowingSidewaysDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
    }

    private void OnAdvanceClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        _step = (_step + 1) % Statuses.Length;
        Order.Description = Statuses[_step];
    }
}
```

The width and the height change together on the same spring, so a card that grows sideways should hold details that
read well at the wider size. The details are laid out at their open width the whole time, so their text never
reflows while the card moves.

### Open by default

`IsExpanded` is two-way. Set it to `True` to start open, or bind it to a view model property. A card that starts
open is the right choice when the reason for the card is the details, such as a failed deploy that needs attention
before anything else in the list.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ExpandableCardOpenByDefaultDemo">
    <arc:ExpandableCard Header="Deploy failed"
                        Description="api-gateway · 2 minutes ago"
                        IsExpanded="True">
        <TextBlock Text="Health check on /ready timed out after 30s. The previous release is still serving traffic; no action is needed until the next deploy."
                   FontSize="14"
                   TextWrapping="Wrap"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
    </arc:ExpandableCard>
</UserControl>
```

### Updating the summary

Change `Description` in code or through a binding. Only the words that changed roll in; the rest of the line stays
still, so a status change reads as a change and not as a redraw.

```csharp
order.Description = "Out for delivery · arrives today";
```

Keep the summary in one shape, such as "status · time" or "product · amount". A summary that changes its shape from
one update to the next makes every word roll, which is harder to read than a change in one part of the line.

### Events

`ExpandedChanged` is a routed event that bubbles. It is raised after the card opens or closes, so a handler sees the
new `IsExpanded` value.

```csharp
card.ExpandedChanged += (_, _) =>
{
    logger.Info($"Plan details open: {card.IsExpanded}");
};
```

### Binding to a view model

A deployment card usually belongs to a view model that owns the summary and whether the card is open. With
CommunityToolkit.Mvvm, the view model notifies the card through its properties, and the card reports the reader's
clicks back through the two-way `IsExpanded` binding.

```csharp
public partial class DeploymentViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    [ObservableProperty]
    private bool _isDetailsOpen;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private string _summary = "api-gateway · 2 minutes ago";

    [RelayCommand]
    private void Retry() => Summary = "api-gateway · retrying now";
}
```

```xml
<arc:ExpandableCard Header="Deploy failed"
                    Description="{Binding Summary}"
                    IsExpanded="{Binding IsDetailsOpen, Mode=TwoWay}">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12">
        <TextBlock Text="Health check on /ready timed out after 30s." TextWrapping="Wrap" />
        <arc:Button Content="Retry deploy"
                    Variant="Secondary"
                    Size="Small"
                    Command="{Binding RetryCommand}"
                    HorizontalAlignment="Left" />
    </StackPanel>
</arc:ExpandableCard>
```

Bind `Description` one way, because the card only displays it. Bind `IsExpanded` two-way so that a close made with the
keyboard, with Escape, or by the reader's click updates the view model. Do not write `IsDetailsOpen` from the
view model in response to `Description` changes, because the card's open state is the reader's choice.

### Layout in lists and stacks

Inside a vertical list or a `StackPanel`, the card takes the width the panel gives it, so a column of cards lines up
without any width on the cards themselves. Inside a horizontal stack, the available width is unbounded, so the caps
decide the width: set `CollapsedWidth` and `ExpandedWidth` on those cards, or the card sizes itself to its content.
A container resize applies at once without an animation, so a window resize never starts a motion.

### Example: deployment history

A deployment history in a developer console. The list shows the latest three releases of three services. The first
card is open because its deploy failed and the health check output is the thing to read first. Each header names the
service and the time, so the list reads in the order the team works through it. The width is 560, which fits the
details text on one or two lines.

![A deployment history with an open failed deploy and two closed successful deploys](https://docs.tkcode.si/shots/Docs/Expand/ExpandableCard/images/DeployHistory.webp)

```xml
<StackPanel Width="560" Spacing="12">
    <arc:ExpandableCard Header="Deploy failed"
                        Description="api-gateway · 2 minutes ago"
                        IsExpanded="True">
        <StackPanel Spacing="12">
            <TextBlock Text="Health check on /ready timed out after 30s. Build 4821 is not serving traffic; build 4818 still is."
                       FontSize="14"
                       TextWrapping="Wrap"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
            <arc:Button Content="Retry deploy"
                        Variant="Secondary"
                        Size="Small"
                        HorizontalAlignment="Left" />
        </StackPanel>
    </arc:ExpandableCard>
    <arc:ExpandableCard Header="Deploy succeeded"
                        Description="web-app · 14 minutes ago">
        <TextBlock Text="Build 4820 deployed to 6 regions in 4 minutes."
                   FontSize="14"
                   TextWrapping="Wrap"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
    </arc:ExpandableCard>
    <arc:ExpandableCard Header="Deploy succeeded"
                        Description="billing-worker · 1 hour ago">
        <TextBlock Text="Build 4812 deployed to 2 regions in 3 minutes."
                   FontSize="14"
                   TextWrapping="Wrap"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
    </arc:ExpandableCard>
</StackPanel>
```

### Content guidelines

- **Header**: the noun or the outcome in sentence case, such as "Pro plan", "Order #4821" or "Deploy failed". Keep it
  to one line; the summary carries the rest.
- **Summary**: one line of facts in a fixed shape, separated by a middle dot: "api-gateway · 2 minutes ago", "$24
  per month · billed yearly". Put the time or the status first when the list is sorted by it.
- **Details**: the detail the reader needs to act on, in complete sentences. A details panel should hold the
  reason for the status and the next step, not a repeat of the header.
- **Action**: a verb and an object on the button inside the details, such as "Retry deploy" or "Download invoice".

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| Click to see more | Plan details |
| Status: failed!!! | Deploy failed |
| More | Retry deploy |
| Details | Health check on /ready timed out after 30s |
| Order info | Order #4821 · shipped, arrives Thursday |

### Best practices

**Do**

- Keep the header and the summary short enough that a list of cards scans at a glance. The header is what the reader
  reads when nothing is open.
- Open a card by default only when its details need attention before anything else in the list, such as a failure.
- Keep the details to one or two short paragraphs and a single action. A long details panel pushes the rest of the
  list down the page, which is what the card was meant to avoid.
- Set `Description` for every card in a list, or for none. A mix of cards with and without a summary line makes the
  headers jump in height.

**Avoid**

- Putting a form inside the details. Validation messages and tab order inside a collapsed panel are hard to reach;
  a `Drawer` or `Dialog` is the right container for a form.
- Changing the summary shape on every update. Words roll only when they change, so a new shape rolls the whole
  line and reads as noise.
- Setting `CollapsedWidth` on one card in a list and leaving it unset on the others. The cards then differ in width
  and the column looks ragged.
- Using the card as the only route to a detail that everyone needs. A reader who never opens it misses it, so keep
  required information on the page.
- Relying on the animation to explain a change. The card is correct at rest, and reduced motion shows the same end
  state at once.

### Common questions

**How do I hide the summary line?** Set `Description` to `null` or an empty string. The summary row collapses, and
the header becomes only the title.

**Why does Escape not close the card?** Escape closes the card only when it is open and no control inside it has
already handled the key. A text box or a dialog inside the details that uses Escape keeps the key for itself.

**Can I open the card in code before the page is shown?** Yes. Setting `IsExpanded` before the card is loaded shows
the end state at once, so the first frame is correct. After the card is loaded, changes to `IsExpanded` animate.

**Why does the card not animate when the window is resized?** Container resizes apply at once. The morph is for the
changes the reader makes (opening, closing and a summary update), not for layout changes, so a window resize never
starts a motion.

**How do I know the state from outside the card?** Read `IsExpanded`, or handle `ExpandedChanged`. The handler runs
after the change, so `IsExpanded` already holds the new value.

## API reference

### ExpandableCard

Arc expandable card: a summary card whose header opens a details panel below it. Opening is one morph: width and height grow on the same smooth spring (real size, never a scale, so text and corners never stretch) and the chevron turns with it; the details fade in once the box has made room, and on close they fade first and the box follows 60ms later. A second click mid-flight reverses from the current size and velocity. The summary line rolls only the words that changed. Escape closes the card from anywhere inside it and returns focus to the header.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Description` | `string?` | `null` | Summary line under the title; changed words roll in. |
| `IsExpanded` | `bool` | `false` | Whether the details are open. Two-way. |
| `CollapsedWidth` | `double` | `NaN` | Width cap while collapsed, in px; NaN fills the container (Arc width). |
| `ExpandedWidth` | `double` | `NaN` | Width cap while open, so the card can grow sideways; NaN uses `CollapsedWidth` (Arc expandedWidth). |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ExpandedChanged` | `RoutedEventArgs` | Raised after the card opens or closes. |

Pseudo-classes: `:expanded`

Derives from `HeaderedContentControl`: every member of `HeaderedContentControl` works as well.

## Accessibility

- The header is a button that exposes the expand and collapse pattern, so assistive technology announces whether
  the card is open or closed, and the state changes when the card does.
- The card's accessible name is its `Header` when the header is a string. The `Description` is exposed as the help
  text of the header button, so it is read after the name.
- The summary line is also exposed as a text element with its full content, so screen readers read the whole line
  and not only the words that rolled in.
- The details are inert while the card is closed: their controls cannot take focus or receive pointer input.
- Escape closes an open card from anywhere inside it and returns focus to the header, so focus never stays in a
  panel that has closed.

### Keyboard

The header is a button, so the standard button keys apply. The card adds the Escape close.

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` | Moves to the header; moves into the details only while the card is open |
| `Enter` / `Space` | Opens or closes the card from the header |
| `Escape` | Closes an open card when focus is inside it and no control has handled the key, then moves focus to the header |

## Motion

- Opening is one motion: the width and height grow together on a smooth spring that does not overshoot, and the
  chevron turns with them. The card changes its real size instead of scaling, so text and corners never stretch.
- The details fade in once the card has made room for them. On close, the details fade out first and the card
  shrinks after them.
- A second click during the motion reverses from the current size and speed. A close that follows another change
  within about 450 ms skips the hold before the card shrinks.
- In the summary line, changed words rise in from below with a soft blur. The words they replace lift away and fade.
  Words that did not change stay still.
- Reduced motion applies the end state at once, and the summary text is replaced without animation.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| Card opens | Width and height grow together on a smooth spring; chevron turns | Open at once | Immediate |
| Details appear | Fade in once the card has made room, after a 120 ms delay | Shown at once | Immediate |
| Card closes | Details fade out in 100 ms; the card shrinks after a 60 ms hold | Closed at once | Immediate |
| Summary changes | Changed words rise in and the old words lift away and fade | Replaced at once | Immediate |
| Header hover and press | Background crossfades to the muted surface | Immediate | Immediate |

## Related

- `Accordion` for a list of mutually exclusive sections.
- `Card` for a card without expandable details.
- `ExpandableText` for a long paragraph that expands in place.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `Accordion` | Several sections of text open one at a time as a single list |
| `Card` | The card has no details to reveal, so its content stays visible |
| `CardStack` | The reader moves between cards rather than opening each one |
| `ExpandableText` | One long paragraph should show a few lines with a "Read more" toggle |
| `MetricCard` | A single number with its trend is the whole point of the card |
