# Resizable panels

> Trade space between panes by dragging the divider between them.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/resizable-panels

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ResizablePanelsDefaultDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12">
        <Border Height="320"
                Padding="1"
                BorderThickness="1"
                CornerRadius="26"
                ClipToBounds="True"
                BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Border}">
            <arc:ResizablePanels Label="Mail layout" LayoutChanged="OnLayoutChanged">
                <arc:ResizablePanel Id="folders"
                                    Label="Folders"
                                    DefaultSize="22"
                                    MinSize="140"
                                    IsCollapsible="True">
                    <Border Padding="16" Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource SurfaceMuted}">
                        <StackPanel Spacing="6">
                            <TextBlock Text="Folders"
                                       FontSize="14"
                                       FontWeight="Medium"
                                       TextWrapping="Wrap"
                                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
                            <TextBlock Text="Inbox, Drafts, Sent, Archive"
                                       FontSize="13"
                                       TextWrapping="Wrap"
                                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
                        </StackPanel>
                    </Border>
                </arc:ResizablePanel>
                <arc:ResizablePanel Id="messages"
                                    Label="Messages"
                                    DefaultSize="33"
                                    MinSize="200">
                    <Border Padding="16" Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Surface}">
                        <StackPanel Spacing="6">
                            <TextBlock Text="Messages"
                                       FontSize="14"
                                       FontWeight="Medium"
                                       TextWrapping="Wrap"
                                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
                            <TextBlock Text="42 conversations"
                                       FontSize="13"
                                       TextWrapping="Wrap"
                                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
                        </StackPanel>
                    </Border>
                </arc:ResizablePanel>
                <arc:ResizablePanel Id="reading"
                                    Label="Reading pane"
                                    DefaultSize="45"
                                    MinSize="220"
                                    IsCollapsible="True">
                    <Border Padding="16" Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Surface}">
                        <StackPanel Spacing="6">
                            <TextBlock Text="Quarterly review"
                                       FontSize="14"
                                       FontWeight="Medium"
                                       TextWrapping="Wrap"
                                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
                            <TextBlock Text="Hi team, the numbers are in and they look good. Let's walk through them on Thursday."
                                       FontSize="13"
                                       TextWrapping="Wrap"
                                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
                        </StackPanel>
                    </Border>
                </arc:ResizablePanel>
            </arc:ResizablePanels>
        </Border>
        <TextBlock x:Name="Status"
                   Text="Drag a divider"
                   FontSize="12"
                   TextWrapping="Wrap"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class ResizablePanelsDefaultDemo : UserControl
{
    public ResizablePanelsDefaultDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
    }

    private void OnLayoutChanged(object? sender, ResizablePanelsLayoutChangedEventArgs e)
        => Status.Text = "Layout: " + string.Join(" / ", e.Sizes.Select(s => $"{s:0}%"));
}
```

## When to use

`ResizablePanels` splits one area into side-by-side panes and lets the person decide how much room each pane gets.
It fits the working area of an application: the body under a page header, where a list, a detail view and a
secondary pane must share the window. The group needs a definite height from its parent, so it belongs in the
content region of a shell, not in an auto-sized row.

- **Mail and messaging clients**: a folder list, a message list and a reading pane. People widen the reading pane for
  long threads and collapse the folders when they need the room.
- **Ticket and order triage in admin consoles**: a queue on the left and the selected ticket or order on the right.
  Support agents shrink the queue for dense reading and widen it when they sort a backlog.
- **Query and code editors in analytics tools**: a schema browser, an editor and a results pane, where the editor
  needs most of the width while a SQL or DAX query is written.
- **Dashboards with a side inspector**: a chart pane beside a filter or detail inspector. The inspector collapses
  when it is not needed, which gives the chart the full width.
- **Layouts that people shape once and keep**: the sizes are stored with `Sizes` and restored in the next session,
  so a team's preferred split survives a restart.

## When not to use

- **A panel that covers the page**: use `Drawer` for a pane that slides over the content and must be dismissed
  before the person returns to the page.
- **Stacked sections of one page**: `ResizablePanels` splits horizontally only. Use `Accordion` for sections that
  open and close one above another.
- **One pane at a time**: use `Tabs` when the person switches between views and never needs to see two at once.
- **A narrow screen or a phone layout**: the panes never stack. Use `Tabs` or let the page change its structure
  for the narrow width.
- **A fixed split that nobody adjusts**: a plain Avalonia `Grid` with star-sized columns is simpler and has no
  dividers to operate.
- **Content that is longer than its pane**: keep the split and put a `ScrollArea` inside the pane. The group does
  not scroll its panes.

## Usage

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:ResizablePanels Label="Mail layout" Height="320">
        <arc:ResizablePanel Id="folders"
                            Label="Folders"
                            DefaultSize="22"
                            MinSize="140"
                            IsCollapsible="True">
            <TextBlock Text="Inbox, Drafts, Sent, Archive" />
        </arc:ResizablePanel>
        <arc:ResizablePanel Id="messages"
                            Label="Messages"
                            DefaultSize="33"
                            MinSize="200">
            <TextBlock Text="42 conversations" />
        </arc:ResizablePanel>
        <arc:ResizablePanel Id="reading"
                            Label="Reading pane"
                            DefaultSize="45"
                            MinSize="220"
                            IsCollapsible="True">
            <TextBlock Text="Quarterly review" />
        </arc:ResizablePanel>
    </arc:ResizablePanels>
</UserControl>
```

`ResizablePanels` derives from Avalonia's `Control`, and `ResizablePanel` derives from `ContentControl`. The group
takes its `Panels` collection as its content, so the panes are written directly inside it. The group lays the
panes out itself: each pane's width comes from its share and its limits, not from a `Width` you set on it. The
dividers between panes are created by the group and are focusable, so the keyboard reaches them without extra
markup.

`Label` names the group for assistive technology. Each pane's `Label` names the divider that follows it.

### Anatomy

1. **Group** (`ResizablePanels`): clipped to its bounds and laid out left to right. It has no visual of its own
   besides the dividers and restore tabs. Text inside the group uses the body font at the `TypeSM` size in the
   foreground color unless a pane sets its own.
2. **Pane** (`ResizablePanel`): its content stretches to fill the pane. Below the pane's effective minimum the
   content keeps that minimum width and stays anchored to the moving edge, so a closing pane slides away instead of
   being squeezed.
3. **Divider line**: a 1 px line in the border color. It becomes the strong border color while the pointer is over
   it, the divider is dragged or the divider has keyboard focus.
4. **Grab area**: 6 px on each side of the line, 13 px in total. Pressing anywhere in it starts a drag.
5. **Grip**: a 4 × 32 px rounded pill centered on the line. It forms when the divider is hovered, focused or dragged,
   in the strong border color, and turns to the foreground color while it is dragged.
6. **Restore tab**: an 18 × 40 px pill 5 px from the line, on the side the hidden pane returns to. It appears when a
   neighbor pane is hidden. It has the surface fill, a border stroke that darkens on hover or focus, a secondary
   text chevron and the resting shadow. The hit area of a hidden divider reaches 30 px into the visible pane so the
   tab is easy to press.
7. **Cursor**: a horizontal resize cursor over an open divider and a hand cursor over a hidden one.

### Sizing panes

Each pane has a `DefaultSize`, which is a share, not a width. The shares are relative: `22`, `33` and `45` produce
the same layout as `2.2`, `3.3` and `4.5`, and they do not need to add up to 100. The group divides the room in
proportion to the shares, then holds every pane to its limits. A pane that would break its `MinSize` or `MaxSize`
is fixed at that limit, and the remaining room is shared again among the others.

| Property | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `DefaultSize` | `1` | Starting share. Also the size the group returns to on `Reset()`. |
| `MinSize` | `80` px | Width where the pane starts to resist. Its content never reflows below it. |
| `MaxSize` | Unlimited | Upper width limit in px. A value of zero or less means no limit. |
| `IsCollapsible` | `False` | Lets the pane be hidden by its divider, the keyboard or a flick. |
| `IsCollapsed` | `False` | Starts the pane hidden. Takes effect only with `IsCollapsible="True"`. Two-way. |
| `Id` | None | Stable key for the pane. It names the divider when `Label` is empty. |

A group narrower than the sum of every pane's minimum scales the minimums down in proportion, so all panes stay
visible.

### Collapsed by default

Set `IsCollapsed="True"` on a collapsible pane to start it hidden. Its divider then shows a restore tab that
brings the pane back, and the pane is removed from hit testing and the tab order until it returns.


```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class ResizablePanelsCollapsedAndPersistedDemo : UserControl
{
    private IReadOnlyList<double>? _saved;

    public ResizablePanelsCollapsedAndPersistedDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
    }

    private void OnSaveClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) => _saved = Editor.Sizes;

    private void OnRestoreClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        if (_saved is not null)
        {
            Editor.Sizes = _saved;
        }
    }
}
```

Collapsing from code uses the same path as a drag or the Enter key. Setting `IsCollapsed` to `True` hides the pane
through its divider, and setting it to `False` restores it. Both are ignored for a pane that is not collapsible.

### Limits

`MinSize` is the width in pixels where a pane starts to resist. `MaxSize` caps the width and is unlimited by default.
Past a limit the divider stops at the limit and gives a rubber-band resistance of up to 44 px before it refuses to
move further, so the person sees that the limit has been reached.

```xml
<arc:ResizablePanel Id="code" Label="Code" DefaultSize="50" MinSize="240" MaxSize="800" />
```

Pick a `MinSize` that is the narrowest width at which the pane's content still reads. A message list needs room for
a sender and a subject, a folder list for its longest label, and a reading pane for a line of body text. The
default of 80 px only suits panes that hold an icon or a short value.

### Binding to a view model

The group's `Sizes` property is the layout, so the view model owns it. `Sizes` and each pane's `IsCollapsed` are
two-way by default, which means the view model receives every settled resize and every collapse made by a drag or
the keyboard, and it can set them to restore a layout.

```csharp
public interface IUserSettings
{
    IReadOnlyList<double>? MailPaneSizes { get; set; }
    bool MailFoldersCollapsed { get; set; }
}

public partial class MailViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    private readonly IUserSettings _settings;

    public MailViewModel(IUserSettings settings)
    {
        _settings = settings;
        _paneSizes = settings.MailPaneSizes;
        _isFoldersCollapsed = settings.MailFoldersCollapsed;
    }

    [ObservableProperty]
    private IReadOnlyList<double>? _paneSizes;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private bool _isFoldersCollapsed;

    partial void OnPaneSizesChanged(IReadOnlyList<double>? value) => _settings.MailPaneSizes = value?.ToArray();

    partial void OnIsFoldersCollapsedChanged(bool value) => _settings.MailFoldersCollapsed = value;
}
```

```xml
<arc:ResizablePanels Label="Mail layout" Sizes="{Binding PaneSizes}" Height="480">
    <arc:ResizablePanel Id="folders"
                        Label="Folders"
                        DefaultSize="22"
                        MinSize="140"
                        IsCollapsible="True"
                        IsCollapsed="{Binding IsFoldersCollapsed}">
        <!-- Folder list -->
    </arc:ResizablePanel>
    <arc:ResizablePanel Id="messages" Label="Messages" DefaultSize="33" MinSize="200">
        <!-- Message list -->
    </arc:ResizablePanel>
    <arc:ResizablePanel Id="reading" Label="Reading pane" DefaultSize="45" MinSize="220">
        <!-- Message detail -->
    </arc:ResizablePanel>
</arc:ResizablePanels>
```

- `Sizes` holds one value per pane in order, in percent of the room, and the values add up to 100. A hidden pane
  holds 0. The view model sees a new value when a resize settles (`LayoutChanged` fires at the same moment), not on
  every pointer move, so saving in the property-changed handler writes to storage once per gesture.
- Store the layout with the pane set it came from. The group expects the same panes for its whole life, so discard
  a saved array when the pane list changes and let the defaults apply.
- `Reset()` is a method, not a property. Call it from a button's click handler in the view's code-behind,
  because it returns every pane to its default share and its default collapsed state.

### Drag, flick and double-click

Dragging a divider follows the pointer one to one, and the panes move with it. Several rules shape what the person
sees when a drag crosses a limit:

- **Limits**: past a pane's minimum or maximum the divider resists, and it stops at the limit when the pointer
  is released inside the rubber band.
- **Collapse by drag**: a collapsible pane snaps closed once its width falls below its minimum minus the larger of
  half the minimum or 40 px. That threshold is 40 px for the default 80 px minimum and 100 px for a 200 px minimum.
- **Flick**: on release the group projects the pointer's speed a short distance ahead. A flick toward an edge
  collapses the pane and a flick back out restores it. Without a flick the divider stays where it was released.
- **Release motion**: the panes settle on a spring that keeps the pointer's velocity, so a fast flick carries
  naturally into the settle.
- **Press to restore**: pressing a hidden pane's divider without moving it restores the pane.
- **Double-click**: double-clicking any divider calls `Reset()`, which returns the whole group to its defaults.

These rules are tuned for a mouse and a trackpad. A touch user can drag a divider, but the flick threshold is
measured from pointer samples, so test the collapse gestures on the devices you support.

### Narrow windows

The panes never stack. When the window narrows, the minimums scale down in proportion and a pane below its minimum
fades with its width, its content held at the minimum width as it slides away. A phone-width layout needs a different
structure: switch to `Tabs` or change the page layout at that width.

### Content guidelines

- **Pane labels**: a short noun phrase in sentence case that matches the pane's visible heading: "Folders",
  "Messages", "Reading pane". The label is the name of the divider for assistive technology, so a generic label
  such as "Pane 2" leaves a screen reader user with nothing to act on.
- **Group label**: a noun phrase that says what the layout is: "Mail workspace", "Query editor". Name the layout,
  not the mechanism, so the label does not say "resizable".
- **Restore wording**: when a pane is hidden, the divider reports "Folders hidden, press Enter to show it". Keep the
  pane label short so that this sentence still reads in full.
- **Numbers in panes**: write counts as digits, "42 conversations", so a value can be scanned at a glance.

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| Label="Pane 2" | Label="Messages" |
| Label="resizable area" | Label="Mail workspace" |
| Label="Reading" (only in a deep, dense layout) | Label="Reading pane" |
| Label="Stuff on the right" | Label="Query results" |

### Best practices

**Do**

- Give every pane a stable `Id` and a visible `Label`. The `Id` identifies the pane in your saved settings, and the
  label is what a divider announces.
- Set `MinSize` to the narrowest width at which the pane's content still reads, and `MaxSize` only when a wider pane
  would waste the room, for example a code pane that stops at 800 px.
- Keep the group's height definite and let the page's shell decide it. A group in an auto-sized row has no height
  to split and shows nothing.
- Save `Sizes` when a resize settles, not on every pointer move, and set it from the saved settings when the view
  model loads.

**Avoid**

- Collapsing the pane that holds the primary action. A person who cannot find the restore tab cannot reach the
  action again, so keep the primary action in a pane that stays open.
- Setting `IsCollapsible` on a pane whose hidden state would hide information the person needs to notice, such as
  an error list or a pending approval.
- Changing the set of panes while the group is in use. The group is built for a fixed pane set, and a saved layout
  from another set does not describe it.
- Nesting groups inside a narrow pane, where the outer and inner minimums compete for the same few pixels.
- Expecting a vertical split. The group is horizontal only, so build the stacked part of the layout outside it.

### Common questions

**Why does the group show nothing?** It needs a definite height from its parent. In a `StackPanel` or an auto-sized
row the group has no height to share, so set `Height` or place it in a `Grid` row with star height.

**Why did my pane not collapse when I dragged the divider?** Only a pane with `IsCollapsible="True"` can collapse.
A drag collapses the pane only once it passes the collapse threshold; a shorter drag stops at the pane's `MinSize`
and shows the rubber band.

**How do I hide a pane from a toolbar button?** Bind the pane's `IsCollapsed` to a view model property and change
that property. Setting it to `True` collapses the pane through its divider, and `False` restores it. The same binding
receives the change when the person collapses the pane with the mouse or the keyboard.

**What does `Sizes` contain while a pane is hidden?** The hidden pane's value is 0, and the remaining panes share
the 100 percent.

## API reference

### ResizablePanels

Arc resizable panels: a horizontal split view whose panes trade space when the dividers between them are dragged, the way a mail or code editor window works. Dividers follow the pointer 1:1, resist past a pane's limits (rubber band up to 44px) and snap collapsible panes closed when dragged well past their minimum or flicked toward the edge; on release the panes settle on the smooth spring keeping the pointer's velocity. Each divider is focusable: arrows resize by 16px (Shift 64px) on the snappy spring, Home / End jump to the limits, Enter hides or restores a collapsible neighbour, Escape during a drag puts the divider back, and a double-click resets the layout. The group needs a definite height. `Sizes` (two-way, percent) persists the layout.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Label` | `string?` | `null` | Names the group for assistive technology. |
| `Sizes` | `IReadOnlyList<double>?` | `null` | Each pane's share in percent. Updated after every resize settles; set it (for example from saved settings) to restore a layout. Two-way. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `LayoutChanged` | `ResizablePanelsLayoutChangedEventArgs` | Raised with each pane's share in percent after a resize settles. |

Pseudo-classes: `:resizing`

Derives from `Control`: every member of `Control` works as well.

### ResizablePanel

One pane of a `ResizablePanels` group. It carries the pane's configuration (label, default share, limits, collapsibility) and shows its content. Below its minimum the content keeps its minimum width, stays anchored to the moving edge and fades, so a closing pane slides away like a drawer instead of being crushed.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Id` | `string?` | `null` | Stable id (dividers reference panes by id). |
| `Label` | `string?` | `null` | Names the pane for its divider, for example "Folders". |
| `DefaultSize` | `double` | `1` | Starting share of the group; shares are relative and need not add up to 100. |
| `MinSize` | `double` | `80` | Width in px where the pane starts to resist (Arc: 80). Its content never reflows below it. |
| `MaxSize` | `double` | `Infinity` | Maximum width in px (infinite by default). |
| `IsCollapsible` | `bool` | `false` | Dragging well past the minimum, or flicking toward the edge, snaps the pane closed. |
| `IsCollapsed` | `bool` | `false` | Whether the pane is hidden. Two-way; the initial value is Arc's defaultCollapsed (needs `IsCollapsible`). |

Derives from `ContentControl`: every member of `ContentControl` works as well.

| Event arguments member | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `ResizablePanelsLayoutChangedEventArgs.Sizes` | `IReadOnlyList<double>` | Each pane's share of the group in percent, 0 for hidden panes. |

## Accessibility

- `Label` sets the accessible name of the group, which is announced as a group.
- Each divider is a focusable thumb. Its value is the pane's share in percent, and its range is the share limits the
  pane pair can reach. A hidden pane is reported with the hint to press Enter to show it.
- A divider takes the label of the pane before it, or that pane's `Id` when the label is empty.
- A collapsed pane is removed from hit testing and the tab order, and is hidden from the control view of the
  accessibility tree.
- Left and Right arrows resize the divider by a small step. Shift with an arrow resizes by a large step.
- Home and End move the divider to its smallest and largest position. Enter hides or restores a collapsible neighbor.
- Escape during a pointer drag returns the divider to where the drag started.

### Keyboard

Each divider is a tab stop. The keys below apply while the divider has focus and no pointer drag is in progress.

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` | Move to the next or previous divider or focusable control |
| `Left` / `Right` | Move the divider 16 px. At a limit, it collapses a collapsible pane on that side |
| `Shift` + `Left` / `Right` | Move the divider 64 px |
| `Left` / `Right` toward a hidden pane | Restore the hidden pane |
| `Home` / `End` | Move the divider to its smallest or largest position. Ignored while a neighbor is hidden |
| `Enter` | Restore a hidden neighbor. Otherwise collapse the pane before the divider if it is collapsible, else the pane after it |
| `Escape` (during a drag) | Return the divider to where the drag started |

## Motion

- Dragging follows the pointer directly. Past a pane's minimum, the divider resists with a short rubber band.
- On release, the panes settle on a spring that keeps the pointer's speed. Dragging a collapsible pane well past its minimum,
  or flicking it toward the edge, collapses it.
- Keyboard resizing uses a snappy spring.
- A restore tab pops in when a pane is collapsed, and its content fades out as the pane shrinks.
- Reduced motion moves the panes straight to their target, and the restore tab only fades in.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pointer drag | Divider follows the pointer, with rubber band past a limit | Same | Same |
| Release, drag collapse or restore | Smooth spring that keeps the pointer's velocity | Panes jump to the target | Panes jump to the target |
| Keyboard step | Snappy spring | Panes jump to the target | Panes jump to the target |
| Reset on double-click | Smooth spring to the default shares | Panes jump to the target | Panes jump to the target |
| Restore tab appears | Scales from 60% on the snappy spring and fades in | Fades in only | Immediate |
| Restore tab leaves | Fades out and scales to 60% | Fades out | Immediate |
| Grip forms on hover or focus | Scales from 60% on the CSS-style spring | Immediate | Immediate |

## Related

- `Drawer` for a pane that covers the page as an overlay.
- `Tabs` for one pane at a time, or for a narrow layout.
- `ScrollArea` for content that overflows a pane.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `Drawer` | The pane slides over the page and is dismissed before the person returns to it |
| `Tabs` | People switch between views and never need two at once, or the window is narrow |
| `Accordion` | Sections stack vertically and open one at a time or several at a time |
| `ScrollArea` | Content overflows a pane and needs its own scrollbars |

# Expandable text

> Long text clamped to a few lines with a soft fade that glides open with Read more and closes with Show less, shown only when the text overflows.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/expandable-text

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ExpandableTextDefaultDemo">
    <arc:ExpandableText Text="We moved our whole design team onto the new workspace in a single afternoon. The import kept every comment and version, and the shared libraries meant nobody had to rebuild components from scratch. Two weeks in, review cycles are noticeably shorter: feedback lands on the exact frame, threads resolve themselves when the change ships, and the weekly digest finally replaced our status meeting. The only thing we miss is offline editing on long flights, which the team says is coming next quarter."
                        MaxWidth="520"
                        HorizontalAlignment="Left" />
</UserControl>
```

## When to use

`ExpandableText` shows a long paragraph in a few lines and lets the reader open the rest. It keeps the layout of a
list or a column even when the text lengths differ, which matters most when each item is a card or a row with a
fixed grid behind it. The toggle appears only when the text really overflows, so short text stays plain.

- **Customer reviews and comments**: a review list on a product page or a comment thread in a support tool, where
  each entry shows two lines and the reader opens the ones they want to read in full.
- **Profile and team bios**: a directory of people in an internal tool, where the bio shows three or four lines in
  each card and the full text opens on demand.
- **Product descriptions in a catalog**: a long description under the product title, clamped so the price and the
  add-to-cart button stay above the fold, with "Show full description" as the toggle label.
- **Release notes and changelogs in a developer console**: each release shows the first lines of its notes, and the
  rest opens in place without navigating to another page.

## When not to use

- **Required text**, such as legal terms, a refund policy at checkout, or an error with the steps to fix it. Do not
  clamp it; show the whole text, or link to the page that holds it.
- **A group of titled sections or questions**: use `Accordion`, which gives each section its own question as the
  row header.
- **Structured details hidden behind a summary line**, such as an order with a status and a list of items: use
  `ExpandableCard`, which keeps a header and a summary visible.
- **Text that must keep a fixed height and scroll**, such as a log or a transcript: use `ScrollArea`.
- **Text that is short by design**, such as a label or a title: use a plain `TextBlock`. A toggle on a title is noise.

## Usage

Set `Text` for the content. The text is clamped to `Lines` lines, which defaults to 3. The toggle appears only when
the text overflows the clamp.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:ExpandableText Text="We moved our whole design team onto the new workspace in a single afternoon. The import kept every comment and version."
                        MaxWidth="520"
                        HorizontalAlignment="Left" />
</UserControl>
```

`ExpandableText` derives from Avalonia's `TemplatedControl` and owns three parts: the clamped text, the fade over
its last line and the toggle row under it. The text is an ordinary wrapping `TextBlock` inside the clamp, so the
text styling (`FontSize`, `Foreground`, `LineHeight`) is set on the control and the text inherits it. The default
text is the small type size in the secondary text color with a 1.4 line height, which is the Arc look for body copy
in cards and lists.

Set `MaxWidth` or a `Width` on the control, not on the text. The clamp is measured against the width the control
receives, so the number of visible lines follows the layout.

### Anatomy

1. **Text** (`Text` or `Inlines`): wrapped text in the secondary text color at the small type size, with a 19.6 px
   line height (14 px times 1.4).
2. **Clamp**: while collapsed, the text ends on the bottom of line `Lines`, which is `Lines` times the line height.
   Text beyond that is hidden, and it is not laid out until the text opens, so a very long text costs as much as a
   short one. The clamp is recalculated when the width or the font changes, so no code is needed for a resize.
3. **Fade**: a soft mask over the bottom 1.6 lines while the text is collapsed. It dissolves as the text opens and
   returns near the clamp when it closes.
4. **Toggle row**: a gap of 8 px below the text. The toggle is left aligned, with a minimum height of 28 px, 2 px of
   horizontal padding and a left margin of minus 2 px so the label lines up with the text edge.
5. **Toggle label** (`MoreLabel` or `LessLabel`): medium weight in the foreground color. Both labels share one cell, so
   the toggle's width does not change when the label does. Hover changes the label to the secondary text color and
   pressing it changes the label to the muted text color.
6. **Chevron**: a 16 px down chevron after the label, in the muted text color. It turns 180 degrees with the
   opening, following the same progress as the text.
7. **Focus ring**: a 2 px ring around the toggle, shown for keyboard focus only.

### Line count

`Lines` sets how many lines show while the text is collapsed. Use 2 lines for dense lists such as comments and
reviews, where many entries must fit on one screen. Use 3 or 4 lines for profiles and product descriptions, where
the first sentences carry the most information. The minimum is one line; smaller values are raised to one.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ExpandableTextTwoLinesDemo">
    <arc:ExpandableText Lines="2"
                        Text="Love the new keyboard shortcuts. Cmd+K to jump anywhere is the feature I did not know I needed, and the command bar remembers what I used last, which saves a surprising amount of time every day."
                        MaxWidth="420"
                        HorizontalAlignment="Left" />
</UserControl>
```

```xml
<arc:ExpandableText Lines="2"
                    Text="{Binding CommentText}"
                    MaxWidth="420" />
```

Count lines against the real width. The same text clamps to a different number of lines in a narrow card than in a
wide column, so check the clamp at the smallest width the text appears in.

### Labels

`MoreLabel` and `LessLabel` set the toggle text. The defaults are `Read more` and `Show less`. Change them when the
toggle should name what opens, such as "Show full bio" or "Show full description", because a specific label tells
the reader what they will get.

```xml
<arc:ExpandableText MoreLabel="Show full bio"
                    LessLabel="Show less"
                    Lines="4"
                    Text="{Binding Bio}" />
```

Both labels are announced to assistive technology as the toggle's name, so each one must read as a complete action
on its own.

### Binding the expanded state

`IsExpanded` is two-way. Bind it to a view model property, or set it from code. `ExpandedChanged` is raised when the
text opens or closes, with an `ExpandableTextExpandedChangedEventArgs` whose `IsExpanded` holds the new state.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ExpandableTextControlledDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12">
        <arc:ExpandableText x:Name="Bio"
                            Lines="4"
                            Text="Maya leads platform design at Acme, where she shaped the component library used by forty product teams. Before Acme she built accessibility tooling at a public broadcaster and taught interaction design at the city college. She writes about motion that explains rather than decorates, and she still sketches every interface on paper first. Outside work she restores old film cameras and runs a small darkroom for the neighborhood."
                            MaxWidth="520"
                            HorizontalAlignment="Left"
                            ExpandedChanged="OnExpandedChanged" />
        <WrapPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center" ItemSpacing="12" LineSpacing="12">
            <arc:Button Content="Toggle from outside" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Click="OnToggleClick" />
            <TextBlock x:Name="State"
                       Text="Collapsed"
                       FontSize="12"
                       TextWrapping="Wrap"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
        </WrapPanel>
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class ExpandableTextControlledDemo : UserControl
{
    public ExpandableTextControlledDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
    }

    private void OnExpandedChanged(object? sender, ExpandableTextExpandedChangedEventArgs e)
        => State.Text = e.IsExpanded ? "Expanded" : "Collapsed";

    private void OnToggleClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) => Bio.IsExpanded = !Bio.IsExpanded;
}
```

```xml
<arc:ExpandableText Text="{Binding Bio}"
                    IsExpanded="{Binding BioExpanded, Mode=TwoWay}" />
```

Use the event when the page needs to react to the change, such as to update a status line or to save the reader's
choice. Use the binding when another control must open or close the text, as the demo's button does.

### Text that fits

The toggle appears only when the text really overflows, and follows width and font changes. Short text has no
toggle and no fade, so a list that mixes short and long entries looks correct without any extra logic.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ExpandableTextFitsDemo">
    <arc:ExpandableText Text="Short notes fit on their lines, so no toggle appears."
                        MaxWidth="520"
                        HorizontalAlignment="Left" />
</UserControl>
```

`IsOverflowing` is read-only and reports the current state. Use it to show a count or a hint elsewhere on the page,
not to decide whether the toggle appears: the control already does that.

### Driving it from data

A review list is a collection of items, each with its own text and its own open state. Keep the open state on the
item, so that opening one review does not change the others.

```csharp
public sealed partial class ReviewItem : ObservableObject
{
    public required string Author { get; init; }

    public required string Date { get; init; }

    public required string Body { get; init; }

    [ObservableProperty]
    private bool _isExpanded;
}

public partial class ProductReviewsViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    [ObservableProperty]
    private ObservableCollection<ReviewItem> _reviews = new();
}
```

```xml
<ItemsControl ItemsSource="{Binding Reviews}">
    <ItemsControl.ItemTemplate>
        <DataTemplate>
            <StackPanel Spacing="6" Margin="0,0,0,16">
                <TextBlock Text="{Binding Author}"
                           FontWeight="Medium"
                           Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
                <arc:ExpandableText Lines="2"
                                    Text="{Binding Body}"
                                    IsExpanded="{Binding IsExpanded, Mode=TwoWay}" />
            </StackPanel>
        </DataTemplate>
    </ItemsControl.ItemTemplate>
</ItemsControl>
```

The view model owns the text and the item owns the open state, so a reader's choice survives when the list is
filtered or re-sorted, as long as the same item objects stay in the collection. Replacing the items with new objects
resets their open state to collapsed.

### Rich text and links

`Text` takes plain text, with paragraphs separated by line breaks. When the copy needs runs or links, set `Inlines`
instead; it is used in place of `Text` when it is set. Build the collection in code: the property has no
default collection, so XAML cannot add runs to it. A link inside the text is an inline control, placed in an
`InlineUIContainer`, so it takes keyboard focus like any other control.

```csharp
var notice = new ExpandableText { Lines = 3, MaxWidth = 520 };
notice.Inlines = new InlineCollection
{
    new Run("Your data is stored in the EU region. Read the "),
    new InlineUIContainer(new Button { Content = "privacy policy" }),
    new Run(" for the retention rules and the list of processors.")
};
```

A link inside the clamped part is reachable by keyboard even though the reader cannot see it. When such a link takes
focus while it sits below the clamp, the text opens so that the focus is never on hidden content. Use links that
the reader would want to reach, and place the most important link early in the copy so it is usually visible.

### Selectable or rich content

`ExpandableText` draws its text with its own `TextBlock`, so the reader cannot select it. When the content must be
selectable, or is not plain text at all, put it inside `ExpandableContent`. It has the same clamp, fade, toggle and
motion, and the same `Lines`, `IsExpanded`, `MoreLabel`, `LessLabel` and `ExpandedChanged`.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ExpandableTextSelectableDemo">
    <arc:ExpandableContent MaxWidth="520" HorizontalAlignment="Left">
        <SelectableTextBlock TextWrapping="Wrap"
                             Text="Steps to reproduce: open the billing page, switch the plan to annual, then go back to monthly before saving. The total keeps the annual discount, and the invoice preview shows the lower price. Clearing the browser cache does not help, and it happens in both the desktop app and the web app. Select any part of this message to copy it into the ticket." />
    </arc:ExpandableContent>
</UserControl>
```

```xml
<arc:ExpandableContent Lines="3" MaxWidth="520" HorizontalAlignment="Left">
    <SelectableTextBlock TextWrapping="Wrap"
                         Text="{Binding Message}" />
</arc:ExpandableContent>
```

The clamp ends on a line of the first visible text in the content: a `TextBlock` or `SelectableTextBlock`, found
through plain panels, borders and presenters, or a control that implements `IExpandableLineSource`. A read-only editor
that lays out its own lines implements that interface, so the clamp stops between two of its lines instead of cutting
through one. Content that is not text, such as rendered Markdown, has no lines to report: set `LineHeight`, and the
clamp is `Lines` times `LineHeight`.

| Content | Where the clamp ends |
|---|---|
| `TextBlock`, `SelectableTextBlock` | On the bottom of line `Lines`. The text takes the Arc body style and line height unless it sets its own |
| A control that implements `IExpandableLineSource` | On the line bottom that the control reports |
| Other content, with `LineHeight` set | At `Lines` times `LineHeight` |

While collapsed, a `TextBlock` in the content is laid out only to the line after the clamp, which is enough to tell
that it overflows. A very long message, such as a pasted log, costs as much as a short one until the reader opens it.
Set `IsFadeEnabled` to `False` to drop the fade over the last line, for example when the content already ends with a
divider of its own.

### Example: product reviews

A review list on a product page of a storefront. Two-line clamps keep the reviews compact, and the toggle appears only
on the long reviews, so the short review reads as it is. The author, the verified-purchase label and the date sit
above the text in a small muted line, so the reader can judge the review before opening it. The list is 560 wide,
the width of the product column.

![A product review list with two clamped reviews, one with a Read more toggle, and one short review](https://docs.tkcode.si/shots/Docs/Expand/ExpandableText/images/ReviewList.webp)

```xml
<StackPanel Width="560" Spacing="18">
    <TextBlock Text="Customer reviews"
               FontSize="16"
               FontWeight="SemiBold"
               Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
    <StackPanel Spacing="6">
        <TextBlock Text="Priya N. · Verified purchase · 2026-03-14"
                   FontSize="12"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
        <arc:ExpandableText Lines="2"
                            Text="We took the Trail Pack on a three-day ridge walk in wet weather. The main pocket kept the sleeping bag dry, the hip belt stayed comfortable under a loaded pack, and the zips still ran smoothly on the last morning. The only change I would make is a larger side pocket for water bottles." />
    </StackPanel>
    <StackPanel Spacing="6">
        <TextBlock Text="Daniel K. · Verified purchase · 2026-02-27"
                   FontSize="12"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
        <arc:ExpandableText Lines="2"
                            Text="Fits a laptop and a lunch box with room to spare." />
    </StackPanel>
    <StackPanel Spacing="6">
        <TextBlock Text="Mei L. · Verified purchase · 2026-02-08"
                   FontSize="12"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
        <arc:ExpandableText Lines="2"
                            Text="Bought it for the commute. The shoulder straps needed a little adjusting on the first day, and after that it carried the laptop, a change of clothes and a water bottle without any strain on my back. The reflective trim is a welcome detail in the winter months." />
    </StackPanel>
</StackPanel>
```

### Content guidelines

- **Toggle labels**: a verb phrase that names what opens, in sentence case. "Read more" is the default; "Show full bio"
  and "Show full description" say what the reader gets. "Show less" closes the text.
- **Lines of copy**: write the first sentence of a review, bio or description so it stands on its own in a clamp. The
  reader decides from those lines whether to open the text.
- **Metadata above the text**: author, date and any verification or status in a short muted line, so the reader
  judges the item before the copy.
- **Numbers**: write them as digits in dates and counts ("2026-03-14", "14 reviews") so the clamp shows the full
  date before the toggle.

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| More... | Read more |
| Expand | Show full description |
| Click here to see the rest of the text | Show full bio |
| Collapse | Show less |
| Read the rest of this review, which goes on for a while about the zip. | Read more |

### Best practices

**Do**

- Use two lines for dense lists and three or four lines for a single item that the reader is likely to read, such as a
  profile. The clamp is the first thing the reader sees, so choose it for the content, not for the layout.
- Put the most useful information in the first sentence, because the rest is hidden until the reader opens it.
- Keep `Lines` the same for every item in a list so the rows align when the toggles are not shown.
- Let the control measure the overflow. Do not split the text yourself or count characters, because the clamp follows
  the real width and font.

**Avoid**

- Clamping text the reader must read, such as terms, prices, errors or warnings. The toggle hides it until the reader
  asks, and many readers do not.
- Setting `Lines` to 1 for a review or a bio. A single line hides almost everything and the toggle becomes the main
  content.
- Putting a form or a button that matters in the hidden part of the text. The reader may never open it, and focus
  would open the text unexpectedly.
- Using `ExpandableText` for a list of titled sections. Each section should be an `Accordion` row so it has its own
  heading.
- Changing `Text` on every update of a live feed. Each change re-measures the clamp, and the toggle can appear or
  disappear as the text changes. Update the text when the reader has a reason to see it.

### Common questions

**Why is there no toggle on my text?** The toggle appears only when the full text is taller than the clamp. If the text
fits in `Lines` lines at the current width, there is nothing to reveal, so the control shows it plainly. Check
`Lines`, the width and the font size.

**Why does the toggle keep the same width when the label changes?** Both labels share one cell in the toggle, so the
toggle is as wide as the longer label. The width is constant, and the labels crossfade inside it.

**Can the reader select the text?** Not in `ExpandableText`. Use `ExpandableContent` with a `SelectableTextBlock`
inside it; the clamp, the toggle and the motion stay the same.

**How do I know when the text opens or closes?** Subscribe to `ExpandedChanged`, which receives an
`ExpandableTextExpandedChangedEventArgs`, and read `IsExpanded`. Or bind `IsExpanded` two-way and watch the view model
property.

**Can a link in the hidden part of the text open it?** Yes. When a link inside the text takes keyboard focus while it
sits below the clamp, the text opens. A link that is visible above the clamp does not change the state; only the toggle
and a keyboard focus on a hidden link do.

**What happens when the text closes far down the page?** The control brings the start of the text back into view, so
the reader is not left below the text they just collapsed. Under reduced motion this happens at once.

## API reference

### ExpandableText

Arc expandable text: long text clamped to `Lines` lines with a soft fade over the last one. Read more opens it to its full height with a calm ease out (500–600ms, growing with the distance) and Show less closes it (400–450ms); the height, the fade and the chevron follow one progress value, so they always move in step, and a click mid-flight reverses from the current height. The toggle only appears when the text really overflows, and stays correct as the width or font changes. While collapsed the text is laid out only past the clamp, so a very long text costs as much as a short one. The whole text is always available to assistive technology. For selectable or rich content, use `ExpandableContent`.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Text` | `string?` | `null` | The text (paragraphs separated by line breaks). |
| `Inlines` | `InlineCollection?` | `null` | Rich text with runs and inline links (`InlineUIContainer`); used instead of `Text` when set. |
| `Lines` | `int` | `3` | How many lines show while collapsed (Arc: 3). |
| `IsExpanded` | `bool` | `false` | Whether the full content shows. Two-way. |
| `MoreLabel` | `string` | `"Read more"` | Toggle label while collapsed. |
| `LessLabel` | `string` | `"Show less"` | Toggle label while open. |
| `IsOverflowing` | `bool` | – | *Read-only.* True when the content is longer than `Lines` lines (the toggle shows). |
| `LineHeight` | `double` | `NaN` | Line height in px. `ExpandableText` lays its text out at this height (theme: text-sm × leading-body); `ExpandableContent` clamps at `Lines × LineHeight` when it is set, which is how content that is not text (rendered Markdown, a list) is clamped. |
| `IsFadeEnabled` | `bool` | `true` | Whether the last visible line fades out while collapsed (Arc: on). |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ExpandedChanged` | `ExpandableTextExpandedChangedEventArgs` | Raised when the content opens or closes. |

Pseudo-classes: `:expanded`, `:overflow`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

### Event arguments

`ExpandableTextExpandedChangedEventArgs` is the argument of `ExpandedChanged`.

| Member | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `IsExpanded` | The new state: `True` when the text has opened, `False` when it has closed |

## Accessibility

- The whole text is always in the accessibility tree. Screen readers read all of it without using the toggle, so the
  clamp is purely visual.
- The toggle is a button that exposes the expand and collapse pattern. Its name is the current label, `MoreLabel` or
  `LessLabel`, and it changes when the state changes.
- Links inside the clamped part can take keyboard focus. Focusing a link that is hidden below the clamp opens the
  text, so focus is never left on hidden content.
- The toggle works with Enter and Space.
- The text itself does not take focus. Only the toggle and the links inside it are stops in the tab order.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` | Moves through the links inside the text, then to the toggle when it is shown |
| `Enter` / `Space` | Opens or closes the text from the toggle |
| Focus on a link below the clamp | Opens the text, so the focused link is visible |

## Motion

- The height, the fade over the last line and the chevron follow one progress value, so they always move in step. They
  ease out on a calm curve and do not overshoot.
- Opening takes about half a second and closing about 0.4 seconds. Longer distances take slightly longer, up to a
  small limit.
- The fade over the last line dissolves as the text opens. Lines that appear rise through a soft edge, so no hard line
  is uncovered.
- A click during the motion reverses from the current height, so the text never jumps to either end.
- The two toggle labels crossfade with a 4 px drift and a 2 px blur, timed to the opening, and the toggle width does
  not change.
- Reduced motion opens and closes the text at once. When the text closes far down the page, the start of the text is
  brought back into view.
- A change of `IsExpanded` that arrives with a new data context, such as an item reused by a list, applies at once,
  without motion and without scrolling the page.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| Text opens | Height grows on a calm ease-out, the fade over the last line dissolves and the chevron turns | Opens at once | Immediate |
| Text closes | Height shrinks in about 0.4 seconds, the fade returns and the chevron turns back | Closes at once, with the start of the text brought into view | Immediate |
| Toggle label | "Read more" and "Show less" crossfade with a 4 px drift and a 2 px blur | Immediate | Immediate |
| Toggle hover and press | Label color crossfades | Immediate | Immediate |

## Related

- `Accordion` for several titled sections that open in place.
- `ExpandableCard` for a summary card with hidden details.
- `ScrollArea` for content that must keep a fixed height.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `Accordion` | Several titled sections open in place, each with its own question |
| `ExpandableCard` | A summary card needs a header and a summary line above its hidden details |
| `ScrollArea` | The content must keep a fixed height and scroll |
| `Textarea` | The reader edits the text rather than reads it |
| `TextBlock` | The text is short by design, such as a label or a title |
