# Dialog

> A focused surface for decisions that need attention.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/dialog

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.DialogShortFormDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12">
        <WrapPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center" ItemSpacing="12" LineSpacing="12">
            <arc:Button Content="Rename project"
                        Variant="Secondary"
                        Command="{Binding #RenameDialog.OpenCommand}" />
            <arc:Dialog x:Name="RenameDialog"
                        Title="Rename project"
                        Description="Choose a short name your team will recognize."
                        Closed="OnClosed">
                <arc:Input x:Name="ProjectName" Text="Atlas redesign" />
                <arc:Dialog.Actions>
                    <StackPanel Orientation="Horizontal" Spacing="8">
                        <arc:Button Content="Cancel" Variant="Secondary" arc:Dialog.Result="{x:False}" />
                        <arc:Button Content="Save" arc:Dialog.Result="{x:True}" />
                    </StackPanel>
                </arc:Dialog.Actions>
            </arc:Dialog>
        </WrapPanel>
        <TextBlock x:Name="Status"
                   Text="Project: Atlas redesign"
                   FontSize="14"
                   TextWrapping="Wrap"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class DialogShortFormDemo : UserControl
{
    public DialogShortFormDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
    }

    private void OnClosed(object? sender, OverlayClosedEventArgs e)
    {
        if (e.Result is true)
        {
            Status.Text = $"Project: {ProjectName.Text}";
        }
    }
}
```

## When to use

A `Dialog` is a centred, modal panel for a decision or a short task that must be finished before the person returns to
the page. It holds the question, the explanation and the buttons in one place, dims the page behind it and keeps focus
inside until the person answers. Use it where an interruption is intended, and keep it small enough that the
person can read the whole panel without scrolling.

- **Destructive confirmations** in an admin console: delete a project, revoke an API key or cancel a subscription.
  The dialog states the consequence ("This permanently deletes Atlas redesign and its 14 files") and puts the
  destructive action in the `Danger` variant next to Cancel.
- **Short forms** that fit one panel: rename a workspace, invite a teammate by email with a role, or set a payout
  reference. The fields are few, and the save or cancel decision is immediate.
- **Multi-step flows in one panel**: an onboarding step such as "Invite your team" moves through its steps by
  changing `Title` and `Description`, so the person keeps one surface and the copy crossfades in place.
- **Acknowledgements before continuing**: a billing or policy change that the person must read, such as a new
  price for the Team plan, shown before they can open the invoice page.
- **Prompts from code**: a bulk action on a table, such as "Archive 42 invoices", asks for confirmation through
  `Dialog.ConfirmAsync` and continues only when it returns `true`.

## When not to use

- **Long forms or record details**: use `Drawer`, which scrolls its body and keeps the page visible at its edge.
- **Mobile-first tasks that rest at a peek height**: use `BottomSheet`, which opens partly and expands on a drag.
- **Lightweight content that should not block the page**: use `Popover`, anchored to its trigger without a scrim.
- **A list of commands**: use `DropdownMenu` or `ContextMenu`, which keep the options next to the control they act on.
- **A message that stays with the page** until it is resolved: use `Alert`. A short result that should disappear on
  its own belongs in `Toast`.

## Usage

A `Dialog` derives from `ModalOverlay`, which itself is a `ContentControl`. Its `Content` is the body, `Title` and
`Description` form the header, `Actions` is the footer, and `IsOpen` shows or hides it. The control takes no space
where it is declared. While `IsOpen` is true, its panel is shown on the window's overlay layer above a blurred scrim,
so the dialog works from any position in the XAML tree and does not disturb the layout around it.

Declare a `Dialog` next to its trigger. It renders nothing in place and shows its panel while `IsOpen` is true.

### Declared in XAML

Put the body in the content and the buttons in `Actions`. A button with `arc:Dialog.Result` closes the dialog with
that value.

```xml
<arc:Dialog Title="Rename project"
            Description="Choose a short name your team will recognize."
            IsOpen="{Binding IsRenaming}">
    <arc:Input Text="{Binding ProjectName}" />
    <arc:Dialog.Actions>
        <StackPanel Orientation="Horizontal" Spacing="8">
            <arc:Button Variant="Secondary" Content="Cancel" arc:Dialog.Result="{x:False}" />
            <arc:Button Content="Save" arc:Dialog.Result="{x:True}" />
        </StackPanel>
    </arc:Dialog.Actions>
</arc:Dialog>
```

### Anatomy

1. **Title** (`Title`): the large type size at medium weight in the foreground color. A change while the dialog is
   open rises in with a soft blur; the old copy leaves.
2. **Description** (`Description`): the small type size in the secondary text color, 8 px under the title. It is
   hidden when empty.
3. **Close button** (`ShowCloseButton`, `CloseButtonName`): a 32 px button with a 1 px border and the control radius,
   aligned to the first line of the title. Its fill is the muted surface color at 50% opacity. It is named
   "Close dialog" by default.
4. **Header rule**: a 1 px line in the border color under the header.
5. **Body** (`Content`): 24 px padding on every side. The whole panel scrolls when it is taller than the window.
6. **Actions** (`Actions`): right aligned, 24 px below the body. It is hidden when `Actions` is null.
7. **Panel**: the raised surface color, a 1 px border, the surface radius and the floating shadow. Its width is the
   size preset (see Sizes), never wider than the window minus a 16 px gutter on each side.
8. **Scrim**: a near-black dim layer at 46% opacity in both appearances, with a 7 px background blur. The blur is turned off
   when the reduce-transparency setting is on.

### Confirmation from code

`Dialog.ConfirmAsync` builds the dialog, waits for a choice and returns `true` only for the confirm button. Escape,
the scrim and the close button return `false`. Set `isDanger` to `true` for a destructive action, so the confirm
button uses the `Danger` variant.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.DialogConfirmationDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12">
        <WrapPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center" ItemSpacing="12" LineSpacing="12">
            <arc:Button x:Name="Delete"
                        Content="Delete project"
                        Variant="Danger"
                        Click="OnDeleteClick" />
        </WrapPanel>
        <TextBlock x:Name="Status"
                   Text="Nothing deleted"
                   FontSize="14"
                   TextWrapping="Wrap"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class DialogConfirmationDemo : UserControl
{
    public DialogConfirmationDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
    }

    private async void OnDeleteClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        var confirmed = await Dialog.ConfirmAsync(Delete, "Delete project?",
            "This permanently deletes Atlas redesign and its 14 files. This cannot be undone.", "Delete", isDanger: true);
        Status.Text = confirmed ? "Deleted" : "Kept";
    }
}
```

`Dialog.ShowAsync` takes custom content and a list of `DialogAction` values, and returns the result of the clicked
action, or `null` when the dialog is dismissed. Use it when the question needs a body that a confirmation cannot
express, such as a choice between three export formats.

```csharp
var choice = await Dialog.ShowAsync(this, "Export invoices", exportForm,
    "Choose a format. The file is generated on the server.",
    new DialogAction("Cancel", false),
    new DialogAction("Export", "csv"));
```

The companion record `DialogAction` describes one button of a code-built dialog.

| Member | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `Label` | `string` | The button text |
| `Result` | `object?` | The value `ShowAsync` returns when this button is clicked |
| `Variant` | `ButtonVariant` | `Secondary` (the default) for dismissive actions; `Primary` or `Danger` for the main one |

### Step titles

Change `Title` and `Description` while the dialog is open. The new copy crossfades in place, so a step flow needs
no second dialog. Keep the step count in the body or in a small status line rather than the title, so the title can
change its wording without changing its length by much.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.DialogStepsDemo">
    <WrapPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center" ItemSpacing="12" LineSpacing="12">
        <arc:Button Content="Invite people"
                    Variant="Secondary"
                    Command="{Binding #InviteDialog.OpenCommand}" />
        <arc:Dialog x:Name="InviteDialog"
                    Title="Invite your team"
                    Description="Add people by email."
                    Opened="OnOpened">
            <TextBlock x:Name="Step"
                       Text="Step 1 of 3"
                       FontSize="14"
                       TextWrapping="Wrap"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
            <arc:Dialog.Actions>
                <arc:Button x:Name="Next" Content="Next" Click="OnNextClick" />
            </arc:Dialog.Actions>
        </arc:Dialog>
    </WrapPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class DialogStepsDemo : UserControl
{
    private static readonly string[] Titles = ["Invite your team", "Choose a role", "Send invites"];

    private static readonly string[] Descriptions =
        ["Add people by email.", "Editors can change content; viewers only read.", "We will email everyone a link."];

    private int _step;

    public DialogStepsDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
    }

    private void OnOpened(object? sender, EventArgs e)
    {
        _step = 0;
        ShowStep();
    }

    private void OnNextClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        _step++;
        if (_step >= Titles.Length)
        {
            InviteDialog.Close(true);
            return;
        }
        ShowStep();
    }

    // The new title and description crossfade in place while the dialog stays open.
    private void ShowStep()
    {
        InviteDialog.Title = Titles[_step];
        InviteDialog.Description = Descriptions[_step];
        Step.Text = $"Step {_step + 1} of {Titles.Length}";
        Next.Content = _step == Titles.Length - 1 ? "Send" : "Next";
    }
}
```

```csharp
dialog.Title = "Choose a role";
dialog.Description = "Editors can change content; viewers only read.";
```

### Sizes

`Size` sets the panel width: `Small` is 360 px, `Medium` is 440 px (the Arc default) and `Large` is 560 px. A panel
never exceeds the window minus a 16 px gutter on each side, so a narrow window shrinks every size to fit.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.DialogSizesDemo">
    <WrapPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center" ItemSpacing="12" LineSpacing="12">
        <arc:Button Content="Small" Variant="Secondary" Click="OnSmallClick" />
        <arc:Button Content="Medium" Variant="Secondary" Click="OnMediumClick" />
        <arc:Button Content="Large" Variant="Secondary" Click="OnLargeClick" />
        <arc:Dialog x:Name="LimitsDialog"
                    Title="Workspace limits"
                    Description="Panel widths: Small 360, Medium 440 (Arc), Large 560.">
            <TextBlock Text="Every size stays within the window minus a 16px gutter and scrolls when taller than the window."
                       FontSize="14"
                       TextWrapping="Wrap"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
        </arc:Dialog>
    </WrapPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class DialogSizesDemo : UserControl
{
    public DialogSizesDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
    }

    private void OnSmallClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) => Open(ControlSize.Small);

    private void OnMediumClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) => Open(ControlSize.Medium);

    private void OnLargeClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) => Open(ControlSize.Large);

    private void Open(ControlSize size)
    {
        LimitsDialog.Size = size;
        LimitsDialog.IsOpen = true;
    }
}
```

```xml
<arc:Dialog Title="Workspace limits" Size="Large" IsOpen="{Binding ShowLimits}">
    <TextBlock Text="Limits apply per workspace." />
</arc:Dialog>
```

Use `Small` for a single question with one or two buttons, such as a delete confirmation. `Medium` is the default for
forms and settings and suits most short tasks. `Large` fits a form with several fields or a table of changes that
the person must review, such as the plan limits before a downgrade. Keep one size per kind of decision across the
application, so people learn where the buttons appear.

### Closing and results

`Closing` is raised before a user dismissal and can be cancelled. `Closed` reports the reason and the result.
A button with `arc:Dialog.Result` sets the result and closes the dialog with the reason `Action`. A button with a
`Command` and no result does not close the dialog by itself; the view model sets `IsOpen` to `false` when the work
succeeds, which keeps the dialog open while the save runs and reports the reason `Programmatic`.

```csharp
dialog.Closing += (_, e) =>
{
    if (e.Reason == DismissReason.PressOutside && isSaving)
    {
        e.Cancel = true;
    }
};
dialog.Closed += (_, e) => status.Text = e.Result is true ? "Saved" : "Closed by " + e.Reason;
```

### Binding to a view model

`IsOpen` is two-way by default, so a dismissal by Escape, the scrim or the close button writes `false` back to the
view model. `Title` and `Description` are one-way: the view model owns the copy and the dialog displays it. Use
`Command` on the action buttons for work that can fail, and a result attribute only for answers that need no work.
Compiled bindings need `x:DataType` on the view; the examples leave it out for brevity.

```csharp
using CommunityToolkit.Mvvm.ComponentModel;
using CommunityToolkit.Mvvm.Input;

public interface IProjectService
{
    Task RenameAsync(string name);
}

public partial class ProjectSettingsViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    private readonly IProjectService _projects;

    public ProjectSettingsViewModel(IProjectService projects) => _projects = projects;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private bool _isRenaming;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private string _projectName = string.Empty;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private bool _isSaving;

    [RelayCommand]
    private async Task SaveNameAsync()
    {
        IsSaving = true;
        try
        {
            await _projects.RenameAsync(ProjectName);
            IsRenaming = false;
        }
        finally
        {
            IsSaving = false;
        }
    }

    [RelayCommand]
    private void CancelRename() => IsRenaming = false;
}
```

```xml
<arc:Dialog Title="Rename project"
            Description="Choose a short name your team will recognize."
            IsOpen="{Binding IsRenaming}">
    <arc:Input Label="Project name" Text="{Binding ProjectName}" />
    <arc:Dialog.Actions>
        <StackPanel Orientation="Horizontal" Spacing="8">
            <arc:Button Variant="Secondary"
                        Content="Cancel"
                        Command="{Binding CancelRenameCommand}" />
            <arc:Button Content="Save name"
                        Command="{Binding SaveNameCommand}"
                        IsEnabled="{Binding !IsSaving}" />
        </StackPanel>
    </arc:Dialog.Actions>
</arc:Dialog>
```

The dialog closes only when the view model sets `IsRenaming` to `false`. If the rename fails, the dialog stays open
with the typed name, and the view model can show the error in the input's `ErrorMessage`.

### Example: subscription cancellation in a billing console

A billing page offers "Cancel subscription" for the Team plan. The dialog states what happens on the next billing
date in plain words, and the buttons read "Keep plan" and "Cancel subscription". The keep action is the safe default
and sits on the left in the secondary variant; the destructive action is on the right in the danger variant. Both
buttons set a result, so the caller reads one value and does not need to know which button was used. Escape and the
close button dismiss the dialog without a result, so a handler that checks for `true` treats them like Keep plan.

```xml
<arc:Dialog Title="Cancel the Team plan?"
            Description="Acme Analytics keeps access until 31 October 2026. No refund is issued for the current period."
            Size="Small"
            IsOpen="{Binding IsCancelling}">
    <arc:Dialog.Actions>
        <StackPanel Orientation="Horizontal" Spacing="8">
            <arc:Button Variant="Secondary"
                        Content="Keep plan"
                        arc:Dialog.Result="{x:False}" />
            <arc:Button Variant="Danger"
                        Content="Cancel subscription"
                        arc:Dialog.Result="{x:True}" />
        </StackPanel>
    </arc:Dialog.Actions>
</arc:Dialog>
```

### Content guidelines

A dialog asks one question, and its title is the question or the action. Write the title in sentence case. A
confirmation title ends with a question mark, and the description says what changes, with the object named and any
count as a digit. Button text is a verb and an object, so the person reads the outcome before they press it. Avoid
"OK", "Yes" and "No" on their own; they force the person to reread the title to know what they agree to.

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| Are you sure? | Delete project? |
| OK | Delete project |
| Yes / No | Cancel subscription / Keep plan |
| Something went wrong | Could not save the name. Try again. |
| Click here to continue | Continue to billing |
| Delete 42 items? | Archive 42 invoices? |

### Best practices

**Do**

- Put the destructive action on the right in the `Danger` variant and the safe action on the left in the `Secondary`
  variant. People read left to right and the primary position is where they expect the commit.
- Name the object in the title and the button ("Delete project?" and "Delete project"). A reader who skims only the
  buttons still knows what they agree to.
- Use `Dialog.ConfirmAsync` for a yes or no question that needs no custom body, so the result is one `bool` and the
  call site stays short.
- Keep the close button and Escape working. They are the keyboard and assistive technology exits, and the close
  button is the only visible way out for a pointer user who does not know Escape.

**Avoid**

- Long forms in a dialog. The body scrolls, but a scrolling panel hides the actions below the fold; a `Drawer` keeps the
  page in view and the form in a longer panel.
- Disabling Escape with `CloseOnEscape` to prevent a loss of work. Handle `Closing` for the `Escape` reason and cancel
  it while the save runs, which keeps the keyboard exit available once the work finishes.
- Stacking a dialog on another dialog for a single follow-up question. Each layer adds a scrim and a focus trap, and
  only the topmost answers Escape, so the person has to close two panels to return.
- Closing the dialog from a command before the work succeeds. A failed call then leaves the person with no dialog and no
  error; set `IsOpen` to `false` only after the work succeeds.

### Focus and dismissal

Focus moves into the dialog when it opens, and the first focusable element receives it unless `InitialFocus` on the
presence is set. While the dialog is the topmost modal, Tab and Shift+Tab stay inside it. When it closes, focus returns
to the control that had it before the dialog opened, which is the button that started the flow.

Escape closes the dialog when `CloseOnEscape` is true (the default). A press on the scrim closes it when
`CloseOnOutsidePress` is true. Both reasons pass through `Closing`, so the application can cancel them while a save
runs. Set `IsModal` to `false` only when the page must stay usable beside the dialog; the scrim and focus trap are
then removed. Stacked dialogs are allowed: only the topmost one answers Escape, so pressing it closes the inner
dialog and leaves the outer one open.

### Common questions

**Why does Escape do nothing while my dialog is saving?** The application cancels the `Closing` event for the
`Escape` reason while the save runs. Set `CloseOnEscape` to `False` only when the dialog must never close from the
keyboard, because it removes the keyboard exit entirely.

**Why is the result null when the person closed the dialog?** `ShowAsync` and `ConfirmAsync` return `null` for Escape,
the scrim and the close button; they return the `Result` of the clicked action otherwise. Check for the value you
expect instead of comparing against `null`.

**Does a button with a `Command` close the dialog?** No. Only a button with `arc:Dialog.Result` closes it. For a
command that can fail, set `IsOpen` to `false` in the view model after the work succeeds.

**How do I make Enter press the primary button?** Set `IsDefault="True"` on the primary button in `Actions`. Enter in
the dialog then presses that button, as in any Avalonia window.

**Can I open a dialog from a control that is not in a window yet?** Use `ShowAsync(owner)` with a visual that is in a
window. The dialog finds the window through that owner and joins the logical tree while it is open.

## API reference

### Dialog

A focused surface for decisions that need attention: confirmations, short forms, step flows whose title crossfades. Declare it anywhere in XAML; it renders nothing in place and shows its panel above a blurred scrim while `IsOpen` is true: The overlay fades in while the panel rises 8px from 0.96 on the smooth spring; closing is shorter and starts from wherever the entrance is. Escape and a press on the scrim close it (cancellable through `Closing`); Tab cycles inside; focus returns to the opener. Code can await a result with `ShowAsync` or `ConfirmAsync`.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Size` | `ControlSize` | `Medium` | Panel width: Small 360, Medium 440 (Arc), Large 560 — always within the viewport minus 32px. |
| `Result` | `object?` | `null` | *Attached.* Set on a button inside a dialog, drawer or bottom sheet: clicking it closes that overlay with this value as its `CloseResult` (and the result of `ShowAsync`). |
| `IsOpen` | `bool` | `false` | Shown while true; set false (or call `Close`) to play the exit. Two-way by default. |
| `Title` | `string?` | `null` | Heading. Changing it while open crossfades (the new copy rises in with a soft blur). |
| `Description` | `string?` | `null` | Secondary line under the title (also the panel's accessible help text). |
| `Actions` | `object?` | `null` | Footer content, usually buttons; give them `arc:Dialog.Result` to close with a result. |
| `ShowCloseButton` | `bool` | `true` | Shows the close button on the dialog (default true). |
| `CloseButtonName` | `string` | `"Close dialog"` | Accessible name of the close button. |
| `CloseOnEscape` | `bool` | `true` | Escape closes (default true; cancellable through `Closing`). |
| `CloseOnOutsidePress` | `bool` | `true` | A press on the scrim closes (default true; cancellable through `Closing`). |
| `IsModal` | `bool` | `true` | Modal (default): scrim, backdrop blur and a focus trap. When false the page stays interactive and focus is free (Radix `modal={false}`). |
| `ScrimBrush` | `IBrush?` | `null` | Scrim brush (the theme sets the component's own scrim color). |
| `BackdropBlur` | `double` | `0` | Backdrop blur radius in px (the theme sets Arc's value; off under ReduceTransparency). |
| `CloseResult` | `object?` | – | *Read-only.* The result of the last close (from `arc:Dialog.Result` buttons, `Close` or `CloseCommand`). |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Opened` | `EventHandler?` | Raised when the overlay opens. |
| `Closing` | `OverlayClosingEventArgs` | Raised before a close requested by the user or by `Close`; cancel to keep it open. |
| `Closed` | `OverlayClosedEventArgs` | Raised when the overlay closes (the exit may still be playing). |

Derives from `ContentControl`: every member of `ContentControl` works as well.

## Accessibility

- The panel takes its name from `Title` and its help text from `Description`.
- The close button is named "Close dialog" by default. Change it with `CloseButtonName`.
- Focus moves into the dialog when it opens and Tab and Shift+Tab stay inside it. Focus returns to the control that opened
  the dialog when it closes.
- Escape closes the dialog and returns focus to the control that opened it, when `CloseOnEscape` is true.
- The dialog is a modal surface: the page behind it is not reachable by keyboard while it is open.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` | Move to the next or previous control inside the dialog, wrapping at the ends |
| `Enter` or `Space` on a button | Press the focused button; a button with `arc:Dialog.Result` closes the dialog with that result |
| `Escape` | Close with reason `Escape`, unless `CloseOnEscape` is false or `Closing` cancels it |

## Motion

- The scrim fades in while the panel rises 8 px from a scale of 0.96 on a smooth spring. Closing is shorter: the panel
  moves 4 px and scales to 0.98, and both fade quickly. Closing starts from wherever the entrance is, so a dialog
  closed during its entrance does not jump.
- A changed title or description rises in with a soft blur.
- Reduced motion keeps only a short opacity fade. Off shows or removes the dialog at once.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| Opening | Scrim fades in; the panel rises 8 px from 0.96 on a smooth spring while it fades in | Short opacity fade | Immediate |
| Closing | Panel moves 4 px and scales to 0.98 while both fade out quickly | Short opacity fade | Immediate |
| Title or description changes | The new copy rises in with a soft blur | Instant fade | Immediate |
| Close button press | The button scales to 0.96 and springs back on release | No scale | No scale |

## Related

- `Drawer` for long forms and detail panels that keep the page in view.
- `BottomSheet` for mobile-first tasks that rest at a peek height.
- `Popover` for interactive content that does not block the page.
- `Alert` for a message that stays in the page, and `Toast` for a short result.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `Drawer` | The form or the details are too long for one panel, or the page must stay visible |
| `BottomSheet` | The task is mobile-first and reads well at a peek height |
| `Popover` | The content is small, anchored to one control and does not need a scrim |
| `DropdownMenu` / `ContextMenu` | The content is a list of commands rather than a question |
| `Alert` | A message stays in the page until it is resolved |
| `Toast` | A short result, such as "Project renamed", should disappear on its own |

# Drawer

> A temporary side surface for focused work.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/drawer

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.DrawerSidesDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12">
        <WrapPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center" ItemSpacing="12" LineSpacing="12">
            <arc:Button Content="Right" Variant="Secondary" Click="OnRightClick" />
            <arc:Button Content="Left" Variant="Secondary" Click="OnLeftClick" />
            <arc:Button Content="Top" Variant="Secondary" Click="OnTopClick" />
            <arc:Button Content="Bottom" Variant="Secondary" Click="OnBottomClick" />
            <arc:Drawer x:Name="FiltersDrawer"
                        Title="Filters"
                        Description="Narrow the list without leaving it."
                        Closed="OnClosed">
                <StackPanel Spacing="16">
                    <DockPanel>
                        <arc:Switch DockPanel.Dock="Right" IsChecked="True" />
                        <TextBlock Text="Only open invoices"
                                   FontSize="14"
                                   TextWrapping="Wrap"
                                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
                    </DockPanel>
                    <DockPanel>
                        <arc:Switch DockPanel.Dock="Right" />
                        <TextBlock Text="Include drafts"
                                   FontSize="14"
                                   TextWrapping="Wrap"
                                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
                    </DockPanel>
                    <DockPanel>
                        <arc:Switch DockPanel.Dock="Right" />
                        <TextBlock Text="Show archived"
                                   FontSize="14"
                                   TextWrapping="Wrap"
                                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
                    </DockPanel>
                    <TextBlock Text="Owner"
                               FontSize="14"
                               TextWrapping="Wrap"
                               Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
                    <arc:Input Placeholder="Anyone" />
                </StackPanel>
                <arc:Drawer.Actions>
                    <StackPanel Orientation="Horizontal" Spacing="8">
                        <arc:Button Content="Reset" Variant="Secondary" arc:Dialog.Result="{x:False}" />
                        <arc:Button Content="Apply" arc:Dialog.Result="{x:True}" />
                    </StackPanel>
                </arc:Drawer.Actions>
            </arc:Drawer>
        </WrapPanel>
        <TextBlock x:Name="Log"
                   Text="Closed"
                   FontSize="14"
                   TextWrapping="Wrap"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class DrawerSidesDemo : UserControl
{
    public DrawerSidesDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
    }

    private void OnRightClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) => Open(DrawerSide.Right);

    private void OnLeftClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) => Open(DrawerSide.Left);

    private void OnTopClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) => Open(DrawerSide.Top);

    private void OnBottomClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) => Open(DrawerSide.Bottom);

    private void OnClosed(object? sender, OverlayClosedEventArgs e) => Log.Text = $"Closed by {e.Reason}";

    private void Open(DrawerSide side)
    {
        FiltersDrawer.Side = side;
        FiltersDrawer.IsOpen = true;
    }
}
```

## When to use

A `Drawer` is a modal panel that slides in from one edge of the window and keeps the page behind it visible at its
edge. It fits focused work that depends on the current view: the person filters a list and sees the result change, or
inspects one record without losing their place in the table. It closes with a button, Escape, a press on the scrim or a
drag toward the edge, so it is easy to leave and return to the same position on the page.

- **Filters on a list in an admin console**: a receivables list keeps its rows visible while the person sets status,
  date range and owner in a right-hand drawer, then applies or resets the filters.
- **Invoice or order details**: a support agent selects an invoice and reads its line items, payment history and
  notes in a drawer, then closes it and picks the next row without a page change.
- **Settings for the selected item**: a product editor opens a left drawer with the variant and pricing settings for
  the item under edit, so the catalogue stays in view.
- **Forms too long for a dialog**: a vendor onboarding form with bank details and tax fields is more than a short
  panel can hold, but the person still needs the list of vendors behind it.
- **Mobile and narrow windows**: on a narrow window a drawer nearly fills the width and keeps its header as a
  drag handle, so the person can dismiss it with a flick.

## When not to use

- **Short decisions and confirmations** such as deleting a project: use `Dialog`, which is centred and puts the
  consequence and the buttons in one panel.
- **Mobile-first panels that rest at several heights**, such as delivery options or a share sheet: use `BottomSheet`,
  which stops at a peek height and expands in steps.
- **Small content anchored to a control without a scrim**, such as a column chooser: use `Popover`.
- **A list of commands** that act on the current selection: use `DropdownMenu` or `ContextMenu`.
- **Navigation between sections of an app**: use `Tabs` for sections of one page, or a sidebar for the application's
  main areas. A drawer that holds navigation hides the destinations behind a dismissible surface.

## Usage

A `Drawer` derives from `ModalOverlay`, which itself is a `ContentControl`. Its `Content` is the scrolling body,
`Title` and `Description` form the header, `Actions` is the footer, `Side` chooses the edge and `IsOpen` shows or
hides the panel. The control takes no space where it is declared; while `IsOpen` is true, its panel slides in on the
window's overlay layer above a lightly blurred scrim. Declare it anywhere and bind `IsOpen`.

### Edge

`Side` sets the edge the panel slides in from: `Left`, `Right`, `Top` or `Bottom`. The default is `Right`.

```xml
<arc:Drawer Title="Filters"
            Description="Narrow the list without leaving it."
            Side="Left"
            IsOpen="{Binding ShowFilters}">
    <StackPanel Spacing="16">
        <CheckBox Content="Only open invoices" />
        <CheckBox Content="Include drafts" />
    </StackPanel>
</arc:Drawer>
```

Choose `Right` for filters and details beside a list on a wide window, because the list stays in view on the left.
`Left` suits content the person browses before the list, such as a category tree. `Top` and `Bottom` span the full width; the
bottom drawer shows a grabber to signal that it can be dragged away. Use one edge per kind of task, so people learn
where the panel for filters or details will open.

### Anatomy

1. **Header** (`Title`, `Description`): the header is the drag handle. Its padding is 24 px (20 px when narrow), with a
   1 px border under it. The title uses the large type size at medium weight; the description uses the small type
   size in the secondary text color, 8 px under the title and at most 512 px wide.
2. **Close button** (`ShowCloseButton`, `CloseButtonName`): a 32 px button with the control radius and a 1 px border,
   aligned to the title's first line. Its fill is the muted surface color at 65% opacity. It is always present and
   is named "Close drawer" by default.
3. **Grabber**: shown only on a `Bottom` drawer. It is a 36 × 4 px pill in the border-strong color at 75% opacity,
   9 px below the top of the header.
4. **Body** (`Content`): 24 px padding (20 px when narrow). The body scrolls while the header stays in place.
5. **Actions** (`Actions`): right aligned, 24 px below the body. It is hidden when `Actions` is null.
6. **Panel**: on a `Left` or `Right` edge it is at most 480 px wide (30 rem) and never wider than the window minus a
   16 px gutter (12 px when narrow). On a `Top` or `Bottom` edge it spans the full width and is at most
   512 px tall, or the window height when that is smaller. The corners on the inner side have a 22 px radius
   (18 px when narrow), and the hairline border is drawn only on the inner edges.
7. **Scrim**: a near-black dim layer at 38% opacity, lighter than the one under a `Dialog`, with a 4 px background
   blur. The blur is turned off when the reduce-transparency setting is on.

A window narrower than 40 rem (640 px) makes the panel narrow: it takes almost the full width, and its corners and
padding tighten.

### Long content

The body scrolls while the header stays in place. Put the full content in the drawer; there is no need to size it.
A drawer taller than the window scrolls its body, so the title, the description and the close button stay in view
while the person reads through the list of line items.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.DrawerLongContentDemo">
    <WrapPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center" ItemSpacing="12" LineSpacing="12">
        <arc:Button Content="Open record"
                    Variant="Secondary"
                    Command="{Binding #RecordDrawer.OpenCommand}" />
        <arc:Drawer x:Name="RecordDrawer"
                    Title="INV-2041"
                    Description="Paid on 12 March by Ada Lovelace.">
            <StackPanel x:Name="Lines" Spacing="10">
                <StackPanel.Styles>
                    <Style Selector="TextBlock">
                        <Setter Property="FontSize" Value="14" />
                        <Setter Property="TextWrapping" Value="Wrap" />
                        <Setter Property="Foreground" Value="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
                    </Style>
                    <Style Selector="TextBlock.muted">
                        <Setter Property="Foreground" Value="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
                    </Style>
                </StackPanel.Styles>
            </StackPanel>
        </arc:Drawer>
    </WrapPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class DrawerLongContentDemo : UserControl
{
    public DrawerLongContentDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        // Thirty lines are more than the drawer can show, so the body scrolls under the fixed header.
        for (var i = 1; i <= 30; i++)
        {
            var line = new TextBlock { Text = $"Line item {i} · Design review · {i * 12} min" };
            if (i % 2 == 0)
            {
                line.Classes.Add("muted");
            }
            Lines.Children.Add(line);
        }
    }
}
```

```xml
<arc:Drawer Title="INV-2041" Description="Paid on 12 March by Ada Lovelace." IsOpen="{Binding ShowRecord}">
    <ItemsControl ItemsSource="{Binding LineItems}" />
</arc:Drawer>
```

For a list of several hundred rows, page the data or use a control that virtualizes its items inside the body. The
body is an ordinary scroll area, so every item placed in it is measured and arranged.

### Actions

Put buttons in `Actions`. A button with `arc:Dialog.Result` closes the drawer with that value, the same as in a
`Dialog`. A filter drawer usually offers a secondary "Reset" that returns `false` and a primary "Apply" that returns
`true`, so the caller reads one result after the drawer closes.

```xml
<arc:Drawer Title="Filters" IsOpen="{Binding ShowFilters}">
    <arc:Drawer.Actions>
        <StackPanel Orientation="Horizontal" Spacing="8">
            <arc:Button Variant="Secondary" Content="Reset" arc:Dialog.Result="{x:False}" />
            <arc:Button Content="Apply" arc:Dialog.Result="{x:True}" />
        </StackPanel>
    </arc:Drawer.Actions>
</arc:Drawer>
```

### Opening from code

Set `Side` and `IsOpen` together when the same drawer serves several edges. `OpenCommand` opens the drawer from a
button without setting `IsOpen`.

```csharp
drawer.Side = DrawerSide.Bottom;
drawer.IsOpen = true;

openDetails.Command = details.OpenCommand;
```

### Closing reason

`Closed` reports why the drawer closed through `OverlayClosedEventArgs.Reason`: `CloseButton`, `Escape`,
`PressOutside`, `Gesture`, `Action` or `Programmatic`. `Closing` is raised before a user dismissal and can be
cancelled with `e.Cancel`, for example while a form in the drawer has unsaved changes.

```csharp
bool hasUnsavedChanges = true; // set by the form when a field changes
drawer.Closing += (_, e) =>
{
    if (e.Reason is DismissReason.PressOutside or DismissReason.Gesture && hasUnsavedChanges)
    {
        e.Cancel = true;
    }
};
drawer.Closed += (_, e) => log.Text = $"Closed by {e.Reason}";
```

### Dragging to close

The header is a drag handle. A drag toward the edge follows the pointer. A drag away from the edge is resisted with a
square-root curve, so the panel moves a little and springs back. On release, the drawer closes when it has been
dragged past a third of its size, or when a flick toward the edge is faster than 500 px/s. Otherwise it springs back
with the snappy spring. A press on a button or a text box in the header is a click, not a drag, so the close button
keeps working. Dragging is disabled under reduced motion and when motion is off, so closing never depends on a gesture.

### Binding to a view model

`IsOpen` is two-way by default, so a close by Escape, the scrim or a drag writes `false` back to the view model. The
drawer's `Title` and `Description` are one-way and change while the drawer is open with a soft blur, which is useful
when the drawer shows the record that the list has just selected.

```csharp
using CommunityToolkit.Mvvm.ComponentModel;
using CommunityToolkit.Mvvm.Input;

public partial class ReceivablesViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    [ObservableProperty]
    private bool _isDetailOpen;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private Invoice? _selectedInvoice;

    [RelayCommand]
    private void OpenInvoice(Invoice invoice)
    {
        SelectedInvoice = invoice;
        IsDetailOpen = true;
    }

    [RelayCommand]
    private async Task MarkPaidAsync()
    {
        await _invoices.MarkPaidAsync(SelectedInvoice!.Id);
        IsDetailOpen = false;
    }
}
```

```xml
<arc:Drawer Title="{Binding SelectedInvoice.Number}"
            Description="{Binding SelectedInvoice.Summary}"
            Side="Right"
            IsOpen="{Binding IsDetailOpen}">
    <ItemsControl ItemsSource="{Binding SelectedInvoice.LineItems}" />
    <arc:Drawer.Actions>
        <arc:Button Content="Mark as paid" Command="{Binding MarkPaidCommand}" />
    </arc:Drawer.Actions>
</arc:Drawer>
```

### Example: invoice details from the receivables list

A finance team reviews overdue invoices in a table on a wide window. Selecting a row opens a right drawer that shows
the invoice number as its title, the customer and due date as the description, and the line items in the body. The
drawer does not cover the table: the person can compare the next invoice with the previous one by closing the drawer
and selecting another row. The actions are "Send reminder" in the secondary variant and "Mark as paid" in the primary
variant, and the view model closes the drawer after the payment is recorded, so a failed call leaves it open with
the invoice visible.

```xml
<arc:Drawer Title="INV-2041"
            Description="Northwind Traders, due 30 September 2026, 21 days overdue."
            Side="Right"
            IsOpen="{Binding IsDetailOpen}">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12">
        <TextBlock Text="Design review, 12 hours at 180 EUR" />
        <TextBlock Text="Prototype build, 20 hours at 150 EUR" />
        <TextBlock Text="Travel and accommodation, 1 item at 640 EUR" />
        <TextBlock Text="Total due: EUR 5,800.00"
                   FontWeight="SemiBold"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
    </StackPanel>
    <arc:Drawer.Actions>
        <StackPanel Orientation="Horizontal" Spacing="8">
            <arc:Button Variant="Secondary" Content="Send reminder" />
            <arc:Button Content="Mark as paid" Command="{Binding MarkPaidCommand}" />
        </StackPanel>
    </arc:Drawer.Actions>
</arc:Drawer>
```

### Content guidelines

The header names the object or the task: "Filters" for a filter drawer, the invoice number for a record. The
description explains the scope in one sentence, and its numbers are digits. Action buttons use a verb and an object,
and a filter drawer uses "Apply filters" rather than "OK".

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| Options | Filters |
| INV2041 details | INV-2041 |
| Submit | Send reminder |
| OK | Apply filters |
| Click the X | Close drawer |
| Details (13 items) | Line items (13) |

Keep the title stable while the drawer is open. A title that changes on every interaction makes the header flicker
through blurred copy, so change it only when the selected object changes.

### Best practices

**Do**

- Keep the list visible behind the drawer when the drawer is about the list. The context lets the person compare the
  rows and see the effect of a filter immediately.
- Choose the edge by the task: `Right` for details and filters on wide windows, `Bottom` for a short panel on a narrow
  window with a grabber to drag away.
- Give the drawer a `Title`. It is the panel's accessible name, and the header is the drag handle, so an empty header
  is hard to recognize.
- Keep the close button and the Escape key working; the drag is an extra way to leave, not the only one.

**Avoid**

- Putting a short yes or no decision in a drawer. A `Dialog` centres the question, and a drawer hides the consequence
  at the edge of the window.
- Nesting a drawer inside a drawer. The stack of scrims makes the page hard to read, and only the topmost panel
  answers Escape.
- Navigation in a drawer that people must reach often. The drawer closes on a press on the scrim, so frequent
  destinations belong in a persistent sidebar.
- Long text in the header. Keep titles to a few words and descriptions to one sentence; the description stops at 512 px.
- Placing a horizontal scroll inside the body. The body scrolls vertically; wide tables should be narrowed or
  restructured to fit the panel.

### Common questions

**Why did my drawer close when I released the header?** The release was past a third of the panel or a flick faster
than 500 px/s toward the edge. Handle `Closing` with the `Gesture` reason and cancel it when the form has unsaved
changes.

**How do I open the drawer from a button without code-behind?** Bind the button's command to the drawer's
`OpenCommand` through its name, for example `Command="{Binding #RecordDrawer.OpenCommand}"`, or bind `IsOpen` in the
view model.

**Why is my drawer's body not scrolling?** The body scrolls when its content is taller than the panel. Remove a nested
`ScrollViewer` inside the body: the body already scrolls its whole content, and a second scroll area splits the scroll.

**Does a drawer on the bottom edge show a grabber?** Yes. The grabber is part of the bottom panel only; top, left and right drawers do not show it, because their drag direction is clear from the edge.

**How do I keep the drawer open after a failed save?** Cancel the close in `Closing` or do not set `IsOpen` to `false`
until the save succeeds. The drawer stays open with its content, so the error can appear next to the field.

## API reference

### Drawer

A temporary side surface for focused work that keeps the page in context: filters, settings, record details, forms too long for a dialog. Declare it anywhere; while `IsOpen` its panel springs in from `Side` above a lightly blurred scrim. The header is a drag handle: it follows the pointer toward the edge and rubber-bands the other way; past a third of the panel, or on a flick toward the edge faster than 500px/s, the drawer closes and keeps the flick's velocity; otherwise it springs back. A click, Escape or the scrim closes it with a quicker tween. The close button is always there; under reduced motion dragging is off and the panel only fades.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Side` | `DrawerSide` | `Right` | Edge the panel is anchored to (default Right). |
| `IsOpen` | `bool` | `false` | Shown while true; set false (or call `Close`) to play the exit. Two-way by default. |
| `Title` | `string?` | `null` | Heading. Changing it while open crossfades (the new copy rises in with a soft blur). |
| `Description` | `string?` | `null` | Secondary line under the title (also the panel's accessible help text). |
| `Actions` | `object?` | `null` | Footer content, usually buttons; give them `arc:Dialog.Result` to close with a result. |
| `ShowCloseButton` | `bool` | `true` | Shows the close button on the dialog (default true). |
| `CloseButtonName` | `string` | `"Close drawer"` | Accessible name of the close button. |
| `CloseOnEscape` | `bool` | `true` | Escape closes (default true; cancellable through `Closing`). |
| `CloseOnOutsidePress` | `bool` | `true` | A press on the scrim closes (default true; cancellable through `Closing`). |
| `IsModal` | `bool` | `true` | Modal (default): scrim, backdrop blur and a focus trap. When false the page stays interactive and focus is free (Radix `modal={false}`). |
| `ScrimBrush` | `IBrush?` | `null` | Scrim brush (the theme sets the component's own scrim color). |
| `BackdropBlur` | `double` | `0` | Backdrop blur radius in px (the theme sets Arc's value; off under ReduceTransparency). |
| `CloseResult` | `object?` | – | *Read-only.* The result of the last close (from `arc:Dialog.Result` buttons, `Close` or `CloseCommand`). |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Opened` | `EventHandler?` | Raised when the overlay opens. |
| `Closing` | `OverlayClosingEventArgs` | Raised before a close requested by the user or by `Close`; cancel to keep it open. |
| `Closed` | `OverlayClosedEventArgs` | Raised when the overlay closes (the exit may still be playing). |

Derives from `ContentControl`: every member of `ContentControl` works as well.

The side of a drawer is the companion enum `DrawerSide`, with the members `Left`, `Top`, `Right` and `Bottom`. The
default is `Right`.

## Accessibility

- The panel takes its name from `Title` and its help text from `Description`.
- Focus moves into the drawer when it opens, Tab and Shift+Tab stay inside it, and focus returns to the opener on close.
- Escape closes the drawer when `CloseOnEscape` is true. The close button is always present and is named "Close drawer"
  by default; change it with `CloseButtonName`.
- Dragging is optional. Under reduced motion it is off, so closing never depends on a gesture.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` | Move to the next or previous control inside the drawer, wrapping at the ends |
| `Enter` or `Space` on a button | Press the focused button; a button with `arc:Dialog.Result` closes the drawer with that result |
| `Escape` | Close with reason `Escape`, unless `CloseOnEscape` is false or `Closing` cancels it |

The drawer does not move by keyboard. Dragging the header is a pointer or touch action only, so the close button and
Escape are the keyboard paths out.

## Motion

- The panel slides in from its edge on a smooth spring while the scrim fades in.
- Drag the header toward the edge to follow the pointer. Past a third of the panel, or on a flick faster than 500px/s,
  the drawer closes. Otherwise it springs back.
- A click, Escape or a press on the scrim closes the drawer with a short tween, and the shadow fades out over the last
  part of the travel. A flick closes it on a spring that keeps the release velocity.
- Reduced motion turns dragging off and replaces the slide with a short fade. Off shows or removes the drawer at once.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| Opening | Panel slides in from its edge on the smooth spring; the scrim fades in | Short fade | Immediate |
| Closing by button, Escape or scrim | Standard tween out; the shadow fades in the last part of the travel | Short fade | Immediate |
| Closing by flick | Spring that keeps the release velocity | Short fade | Immediate |
| Header drag | Follows the pointer toward the edge; resists the other way | Drag disabled | Drag disabled |
| Title or description changes | The new copy rises in with a soft blur | Instant fade | Immediate |

## Related

- `Dialog` for decisions that must interrupt the page.
- `BottomSheet` for mobile-first panels that rest at a peek height and expand.
- `Popover` for small interactive content anchored to a control.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `Dialog` | The question is short and must be answered before anything else |
| `BottomSheet` | The task is mobile-first and rests at a peek height before it expands |
| `Popover` | The content is small, anchored to one control and does not need a scrim |
| `Tabs` | Sections of one page switch in place and no panel should cover the page |
| `ResizablePanels` | The list and the detail are both permanent parts of the page and the person resizes them |
| `ExpandableCard` | A record expands inside the page and the rows around it should move |

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class BottomSheetDetentsDemo : UserControl
{
    public BottomSheetDetentsDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
    }

    // The default detents are 45% and 92%; the sheet opens on the first.
    private void OnOpened(object? sender, EventArgs e) => Detent.Text = "Resting at 45%";

    private void OnDetentChanged(object? sender, BottomSheetDetentChangedEventArgs e)
        => Detent.Text = $"Resting at {e.Fraction:P0}";

    private void OnClosed(object? sender, OverlayClosedEventArgs e) => Detent.Text = $"Closed by {e.Reason}";
```
