## When to use

A `BottomSheet` is a modal panel that rises from the bottom edge of the window and rests at one or more heights,
called detents. It suits the secondary task of a mobile-first screen: the person sees a useful peek of the content
first and expands the sheet only when they need more. It sits above the page with a scrim, so it is a focused step
inside a flow, not a second navigation layer.

- **Delivery and pickup options at checkout**: a shopper on a phone chooses a delivery slot or a pickup point for
  order 4417 from a peek that shows the cheapest option, then expands for the full list of carriers and times.
- **Filters on a product or order list**: a store app shows the active filter count in the peek and lets the person
  adjust filters at full height without leaving the list they are scrolling.
- **Share and export options**: a dashboard on a tablet offers "Copy link", "Send by email" and "Export as PDF" in a
  short sheet that the person can dismiss with a downward flick.
- **Map and media views**: a delivery-tracking map shows the courier's ETA in the peek, and the person drags the sheet
  up to read the stop list while the map stays visible behind it.
- **Trip or booking details**: an itinerary opens at a peek with the first day visible, so the person can see that
  the booking exists and expand it to read the rest.

## When not to use

- **Decisions that must interrupt the whole task**, such as deleting a project or cancelling a subscription: use
  `Dialog`, which is centred and keeps Cancel and the destructive action in one visible panel.
- **Side panels on wide layouts**, where the list should stay visible next to the details: use `Drawer` on the
  right or left edge.
- **Small content anchored to one control**, such as a column picker or a colour swatch grid: use `Popover`, which
  points at its trigger and does not dim the page.
- **A one-line hint for an icon button**: use `Tooltip`. A sheet is far too heavy for a label.
- **A list of commands**: use `DropdownMenu` or `ContextMenu`, which keep the commands next to the control that
  triggers them.

## Usage

A `BottomSheet` derives from `ModalOverlay`, which itself is a `ContentControl`. Its `Content` is the scrolling body,
`Title` and `Description` form the header, and `Actions` takes an optional footer. The control renders nothing where
it is declared; while `IsOpen` is true, its panel is shown on the window's overlay layer with a scrim, a focus trap,
Escape and outside-press dismissal and an exit that finishes before the panel is removed. The sheet adds the detents,
the drag and the scroll rules described below.

### Basic sheet

```xml
<arc:BottomSheet Title="Trip to Lisbon"
                 Description="3 nights, 12 to 15 June"
                 IsOpen="{Binding ShowTrip}">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12">
        <TextBlock Text="Fri · Arrive 14:05 at LIS, taxi to Alfama" />
        <TextBlock Text="Sat · Tram 28 and the castle" />
    </StackPanel>
</arc:BottomSheet>
```

### Anatomy

1. **Grabber**: a button with a 56 × 20 px hit area around a 36 × 5 px bar. The bar
   uses the border-strong color and turns to the muted text color on hover and while the sheet is dragged. Its
   accessible name is "Expand sheet" at a smaller detent and "Collapse sheet" at the tallest one.
2. **Header** (`Title`, `Description`): 20 px side padding, 8 px above and 16 px below (16 px sides when narrow). The
   title uses the large type size at medium weight in the foreground color. The description uses the small type size
   in the secondary text color, 2 px under the title, and is hidden when empty.
3. **Close button** (`ShowCloseButton`, `CloseButtonName`): a 32 px fully rounded button on the right of the header,
   with a 1 px border and the muted surface fill. It is shown by default.
4. **Header rule**: a 1 px line in the border color under the header. It appears only once the content has scrolled
   under the header (`:scrolled`).
5. **Body** (`Content`): a scrolling area with 20 px side padding, 4 px above and 24 px below (16 px sides when
   narrow). Its scroll bar appears only at the tallest detent. Horizontal scrolling is disabled.
6. **Actions** (`Actions`): an optional footer inside the scrolling body, aligned to the right and 20 px below the
   content. It is hidden when `Actions` is null.
7. **Surface**: the surface-raised background with a 1 px border on its top and side edges and no bottom edge, the
   surface radius on its top corners and the floating shadow. It is at most 576 px wide (36 rem), centred, and extends
   160 px below the window edge so an upward stretch never shows a gap.
8. **Scrim**: a dimming layer behind the sheet with the sheet's own scrim color (light and dark variants). The scrim is
   not blurred; its opacity follows the sheet position.

### Choosing detents

`Detents` lists the resting heights as fractions of the window height. The default is 0.45 and 0.92, which gives a
peek and a nearly full view. Values are sorted, duplicates are removed, values above 1 are clamped to 1, and zero or
negative values are ignored. A single value creates a fixed-height sheet. Use a peek height that shows the first
useful row completely, because that peek is what the person decides from. Keep the tallest detent below the full
window height when the page behind the sheet still has context to show, and use 0.92 or more only for full-screen
reading such as an itinerary or a media viewer.

`BottomSheetDetents.Parse` reads a comma or space separated string, so the list can come from configuration or a
resource. `SnapPoints` is an alias of `Detents` for code that uses that name. `EffectiveDetents` returns the sorted
values in use, which is useful for logging and tests.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.BottomSheetThreeDetentsDemo">
    <WrapPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center" ItemSpacing="12" LineSpacing="12">
        <arc:Button Content="Share options"
                    Variant="Secondary"
                    Command="{Binding #ShareSheet.OpenCommand}" />
        <arc:BottomSheet x:Name="ShareSheet"
                         Title="Share"
                         Detents="0.3, 0.6, 0.95"
                         InitialDetentIndex="1">
            <StackPanel Spacing="12">
                <TextBlock Text="Copy link"
                           FontSize="14"
                           TextWrapping="Wrap"
                           Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
                <TextBlock Text="Send by email"
                           FontSize="14"
                           TextWrapping="Wrap"
                           Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
                <TextBlock Text="Embed"
                           FontSize="14"
                           TextWrapping="Wrap"
                           Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
                <TextBlock Text="Export as PDF"
                           FontSize="14"
                           TextWrapping="Wrap"
                           Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
            </StackPanel>
        </arc:BottomSheet>
    </WrapPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```csharp
share.Detents = BottomSheetDetents.Parse("0.3, 0.6, 0.95");
share.InitialDetentIndex = 1;
```

Three detents suit a share or export sheet: a small peek for quick actions, a middle stop for a short list and a full
stop for a preview. Changing `Detents` while the sheet is open keeps the same index, clamped to the new list, so a
shorter list can move the sheet to a lower stop; the sheet stays open.

### Opening and moving between detents

`InitialDetentIndex` chooses the detent the sheet opens at. The default is 0, the smallest. The index refers to the
sorted list, and it is clamped to the list. `DetentIndex` reports the detent the sheet rests on; it is read-only, so
change it through `SnapTo`, `Expand` and `Collapse`.

`OpenCommand` opens the sheet from a button without setting `IsOpen`. `Expand` moves the sheet to its tallest detent,
`Collapse` to its smallest, and `SnapTo` to any index. `SnapTo` does nothing while the sheet is closed. `DetentChanged`
is raised each time the sheet comes to rest on another detent; it is not raised during a drag.

```csharp
openTrip.Command = trip.OpenCommand;

trip.DetentChanged += (_, e) => detent.Text = $"Resting at {e.Fraction:P0}";
trip.Expand();
```

### Long content

The content is not virtualized: every item in the body is created when the sheet opens. Keep long lists paged, or
put a control that virtualizes its own items, such as a `ListBox`, inside the sheet. Below the tallest detent the
content does not scroll. A wheel scroll down, a touch drag on the content, a Tab into content below the fold or a
scroll key opens the sheet the rest of the way first. Collapsing the sheet returns the content to its top, so the
peek always shows the start of the content.

```xml
<arc:BottomSheet Title="Itinerary" IsOpen="{Binding ShowItinerary}">
    <ItemsControl ItemsSource="{Binding Items}" />
</arc:BottomSheet>
```

### Closing

`Closed` reports why the sheet closed through `OverlayClosedEventArgs.Reason`. A fling or a drag down past the
smallest detent reports `Gesture`, Escape reports `Escape`, a press on the scrim reports `PressOutside`, the close
button reports `CloseButton`, and a button that sets a result reports `Action`. `Closing` is raised before a user
dismissal and can be cancelled with `e.Cancel`.

```csharp
trip.Closed += (_, e) => detent.Text = $"Closed by {e.Reason}";
```

### Drag, flick and rubber band

The whole header is the drag handle, so a press anywhere above the content can start a drag. A touch drag on the
content moves the sheet until it is fully open; after that the content scrolls, and a pull down from the top of the
content moves the sheet again. The sheet follows the pointer one to one. Above the tallest detent it stretches with a
rubber band of at most 120 px. On release, the sheet projects 0.2 seconds of its velocity and settles on the nearest
detent, or closes when the projection lands below the smallest one. A release faster than 320 px/s always moves the
sheet at least one detent, so a quick flick is never ignored. A click on the grabber toggles between the smallest and
the tallest detent.

Drag is disabled under reduced motion and when motion is off. Use the grabber, the keyboard or `SnapTo` in those
cases, and keep the close button available for every user.

### Focus and dismissal

Focus starts on the sheet itself, so a screen reader announces its title first. While the sheet is the topmost modal,
Tab and Shift+Tab stay inside it, and focus returns to the control that opened it when the sheet closes. Escape closes
the sheet when `CloseOnEscape` is true (the default), and a press on the scrim closes it when `CloseOnOutsidePress` is
true. Set `IsModal` to false when the page must stay interactive: the scrim and the focus trap are then removed. When
sheets are stacked, only the topmost one answers Escape.

### Binding to a view model

`IsOpen` is two-way by default, so closing the sheet from a gesture or Escape writes `false` back to the view model.
`DetentIndex` is read-only, so the view model receives detent changes through the `DetentChanged` event and stores
them in its own property. Compiled bindings need `x:DataType` on the view; the examples leave it out for brevity.

```csharp
using CommunityToolkit.Mvvm.ComponentModel;
using CommunityToolkit.Mvvm.Input;

public interface IOrderService
{
    Task SetDeliverySlotAsync(string slotId);
}

public partial class DeliveryViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    private readonly IOrderService _orders;

    public DeliveryViewModel(IOrderService orders) => _orders = orders;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private bool _showOptions;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private int _restingDetent;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private string _selectedSlotId = string.Empty;

    [RelayCommand]
    private async Task ConfirmSlotAsync()
    {
        await _orders.SetDeliverySlotAsync(SelectedSlotId);
        ShowOptions = false;
    }
}
```

```xml
<arc:BottomSheet Title="Delivery options"
                 Description="Order 4417 ships from Northwind Berlin."
                 Detents="0.5, 0.9"
                 IsOpen="{Binding ShowOptions}">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12">
        <RadioButton GroupName="slot" Content="Tomorrow, 08:00 to 12:00 (free)" />
        <RadioButton GroupName="slot" Content="Tomorrow, 17:00 to 20:00 (4.90 EUR)" />
    </StackPanel>
    <arc:BottomSheet.Actions>
        <arc:Button Content="Confirm delivery slot" Command="{Binding ConfirmSlotCommand}" />
    </arc:BottomSheet.Actions>
</arc:BottomSheet>
```

```csharp
delivery.Closed += (_, e) => log.Text = $"Options closed by {e.Reason}";
delivery.DetentChanged += (_, e) => viewModel.RestingDetent = e.Index;
```

### Example: delivery options at mobile checkout

A checkout screen on a phone shows the order total and the chosen slot in the page. Tapping "Change" opens the sheet at
a 50% peek, which lists the two cheapest slots without hiding the order total above it. The second option is a
stop at 90% for the full carrier list. The header names the order, so the person sees which order the choice changes,
and the single action at the bottom states the outcome. The sheet closes after the slot is saved; the view model sets
`ShowOptions` to `false` rather than the button setting a result, because the save may fail and the sheet must then
stay open with its message.

```xml
<arc:BottomSheet Title="Delivery options"
                 Description="Order 4417 ships from Northwind Berlin."
                 Detents="0.5, 0.9"
                 IsOpen="{Binding ShowOptions}">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12">
        <RadioButton GroupName="slot"
                     Content="Tomorrow, 08:00 to 12:00 (free)"
                     IsChecked="True" />
        <RadioButton GroupName="slot" Content="Tomorrow, 17:00 to 20:00 (4.90 EUR)" />
        <RadioButton GroupName="slot" Content="Thursday, 09:00 to 13:00 (free)" />
        <TextBlock Text="Carrier: Northwind Courier. Signature required above 500 EUR."
                   TextWrapping="Wrap"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
    </StackPanel>
    <arc:BottomSheet.Actions>
        <arc:Button Content="Save delivery slot" Command="{Binding ConfirmSlotCommand}" />
    </arc:BottomSheet.Actions>
</arc:BottomSheet>
```

### Content guidelines

Write the header so a person knows what the sheet is for before they expand it. The title is a short noun phrase in
sentence case. The description names the scope, with numbers as digits and dates in a short form. The actions are
verb and object, and the peek should not depend on a hint that is only visible after expanding.

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| Options | Delivery options |
| Click here to see more | Show all 12 stops |
| Swipe up for details | Expand the sheet, or use the grabber to expand it |
| OK | Save delivery slot |
| Stuff you can do | Share itinerary |
| 3 nights from 12th June | 3 nights, 12 to 15 June |

Do not repeat the title in the first line of the body; the body should add the information the header does not contain.

### Best practices

**Do**

- Put the decision or the most useful row in the peek, so the sheet earns the expansion. The person decides from the
  peek, and content they must scroll to find is often skipped.
- Keep the close button visible. Gestures are not discoverable on every input device, and a visible control is the
  dismissal path for keyboard and assistive technology users.
- Give every sheet a `Title`. It is the panel's accessible name; without it the sheet is announced as an unnamed
  window.
- Use `DetentChanged` to store the resting position when the sheet's layout depends on it, such as a map that pans when
  the sheet grows.

**Avoid**

- Stacking sheets on top of each other. Each one adds a scrim and a focus trap, and only the topmost answers Escape,
  so the person has to close several layers to return to the page.
- Long unpaged lists in the body. The content is not virtualized, so every row is created when the sheet opens.
- Relying on a drag as the only way to close. Drag is disabled under reduced motion, and a button or the keyboard
  must always remain.
- Horizontal scrolling inside the body. Horizontal scrolling is disabled, so wide content is clipped rather than
  scrolled.
- Using a sheet for a destructive confirmation. A `Dialog` keeps the consequence and the buttons in one centred panel
  that people read before they act.

### Common questions

**Why does the sheet open at its smallest detent?** `InitialDetentIndex` defaults to 0, which is the smallest detent
in the sorted list. Set it to the index of the detent you want, or call `Expand` after opening.

**How do I open the sheet from a button without code-behind?** Bind the button's command to the sheet's `OpenCommand`
through its name, for example `Command="{Binding #TripSheet.OpenCommand}"`, or bind `IsOpen` in the view model.

**Why does my content not scroll at the peek?** Below the tallest detent the content is fixed. A wheel scroll down, a
touch drag on the content, a Tab into content below the fold or a scroll key opens the sheet first. This keeps the peek
from scrolling away from the header.

**How do I stop a tap outside the sheet from closing it?** Set `CloseOnOutsidePress` to `False`. To allow the press only
at some times, keep it `True` and cancel the `Closing` event while `e.Reason` is `PressOutside` and work is pending.

**How do I rename the close button for another language?** Set `CloseButtonName`. The default is "Close", and the
name is read by assistive technology.

**Can I read the detent in XAML?** `DetentIndex` is read-only. Subscribe to `DetentChanged` in code or in the view
model and bind the value you store.

## API reference

### BottomSheet

A modal sheet that rises from the bottom edge and rests at one or more heights (detents): trip details, share options, filters, map and media views where a peek is useful before the full view. One motion value drives the sheet: a drag follows the pointer 1:1, rubber-bands past the tallest detent, and on release projects 0.2s of its velocity to pick the nearest detent or close; a flick faster than 320px/s always moves at least one detent. The dim is a function of the sheet position. The grabber answers ArrowUp / ArrowDown / Home / End and toggles between the lowest and highest detent; reading keys on the sheet open it fully before scrolling; touch drags on the content move the sheet until it is fully open. Under reduced motion detents jump and the sheet fades. The sheet position is a `MotionValue`, not a ControlTheme transition: a drag writes it every move, a release hands the pointer velocity to the spring, and the scrim is computed from it each frame.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Detents` | `BottomSheetDetents?` | `null` | Resting heights as fractions of the window height (default 0.45 and 0.92). A single value is a fixed height. |
| `InitialDetentIndex` | `int` | `0` | Index into the sorted detents the sheet opens at (default 0, the smallest). |
| `DetentIndex` | `int` | – | *Read-only.* The detent the sheet rests on (index into the sorted detents). |
| `IsOpen` | `bool` | `false` | Shown while true; set false (or call `Close`) to play the exit. Two-way by default. |
| `Title` | `string?` | `null` | Heading. Changing it while open crossfades (the new copy rises in with a soft blur). |
| `Description` | `string?` | `null` | Secondary line under the title (also the panel's accessible help text). |
| `Actions` | `object?` | `null` | Footer content, usually buttons; give them `arc:Dialog.Result` to close with a result. |
| `ShowCloseButton` | `bool` | `true` | Shows the close button on the dialog (default true). |
| `CloseButtonName` | `string` | `"Close"` | Accessible name of the close button. |
| `CloseOnEscape` | `bool` | `true` | Escape closes (default true; cancellable through `Closing`). |
| `CloseOnOutsidePress` | `bool` | `true` | A press on the scrim closes (default true; cancellable through `Closing`). |
| `IsModal` | `bool` | `true` | Modal (default): scrim, backdrop blur and a focus trap. When false the page stays interactive and focus is free (Radix `modal={false}`). |
| `ScrimBrush` | `IBrush?` | `null` | Scrim brush (the theme sets the component's own scrim color). |
| `BackdropBlur` | `double` | `0` | Backdrop blur radius in px (the theme sets Arc's value; off under ReduceTransparency). |
| `CloseResult` | `object?` | – | *Read-only.* The result of the last close (from `arc:Dialog.Result` buttons, `Close` or `CloseCommand`). |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `DetentChanged` | `BottomSheetDetentChangedEventArgs` | The sheet came to rest on another detent. |
| `Opened` | `EventHandler?` | Raised when the overlay opens. |
| `Closing` | `OverlayClosingEventArgs` | Raised before a close requested by the user or by `Close`; cancel to keep it open. |
| `Closed` | `OverlayClosedEventArgs` | Raised when the overlay closes (the exit may still be playing). |

Derives from `ContentControl`: every member of `ContentControl` works as well.

### BottomSheetDetents

Resting heights of a `BottomSheet` as fractions of the window height. Parses from "0.45, 0.92".

Derives from `AvaloniaList<double>`: every member of `AvaloniaList<double>` works as well.

## Accessibility

- The sheet takes its name from `Title` and its help text from `Description`. Focus starts on the sheet itself.
- The grabber is a button that exposes its expanded state. Its name is "Expand sheet" or "Collapse sheet".
- On the grabber, ArrowUp and ArrowDown move one detent, Home and End go to the highest and lowest detents, and Enter or
  Space toggles between the lowest and highest.
- Changes of detent are announced politely: "Sheet expanded", "Sheet collapsed" or the new height as a percentage.
  Escape closes the sheet. Its close button is named "Close" by default; set `CloseButtonName` to change it.
- The panel reports itself to assistive technology as a window, so it is announced as a separate surface.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` | Move through the controls in the sheet; focus stays inside while the sheet is topmost. Tab into content below the fold expands the sheet |
| `ArrowUp` / `ArrowDown` (grabber) | Move one detent up or down |
| `Home` / `End` (grabber) | Go to the tallest detent or to the smallest detent |
| `Enter` or `Space` (grabber) | Toggle between the smallest and the tallest detent |
| `ArrowDown`, `PageDown` or `Space` (sheet or its content, focused) | Expand to the tallest detent first; once expanded, scroll the content down |
| `ArrowUp`, `PageUp` or `Shift+Space` (sheet or its content, focused) | Scroll the content up |
| `Escape` | Close the sheet, unless `CloseOnEscape` is false or a `Closing` handler cancels it |

Scroll steps are 48 px for the arrow keys and 85% of the visible height for the page keys.

## Motion

- One motion value drives the sheet. A drag follows the pointer, and past the tallest detent the sheet stretches with
  a rubber band of up to 120 px.
- On release the sheet settles on the nearest detent, or closes when it is dragged down. A flick faster than 320 px/s
  always moves it at least one detent.
- The dim behind the sheet depends on its position. At the smallest detent it keeps 78% of the full dim, and it fades
  as the sheet moves down.
- Reduced motion makes detents jump and fades the sheet in and out. Off shows or removes the sheet at once.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| Opening | Slides up from below the edge on the smooth spring to its detent | Shown at its detent with a short fade | Immediate |
| Closing | Springs down with a 0.3 s visual duration and keeps the release velocity | Short fade out | Immediate |
| Moving between detents | Smooth spring to the new detent | Jumps to the new detent | Immediate |
| Dragging | Follows the pointer one to one; rubber band past the tallest detent | Drag disabled | Drag disabled |
| Scrim | Follows the sheet position | Follows the sheet position | Immediate |

## Related

- `Dialog` for a decision that must be answered before anything else.
- `Drawer` for a side panel on wide layouts.
- `Popover` for small content anchored to a control.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `Dialog` | The person must confirm, cancel or enter a short value before the task continues |
| `Drawer` | Filters, settings or record details should sit beside the page on a wide layout |
| `Popover` | The content is small, anchored to one control and does not need a scrim |
| `Tooltip` | A single line explains an icon button |
| `Alert` | A message stays in the page until it is resolved |
| `Toast` | A short result, such as "Delivery slot saved", should disappear on its own |

# Popover

> A small anchored surface for contextual information.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/popover

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.PopoverShareDemo">
    <WrapPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center" ItemSpacing="12" LineSpacing="12">
        <arc:Popover AutomationProperties.Name="Share link">
            <arc:Popover.Trigger>
                <arc:Button Content="Share" Variant="Secondary" />
            </arc:Popover.Trigger>
            <StackPanel Spacing="12">
                <TextBlock Text="Share link"
                           FontSize="14"
                           FontWeight="Medium"
                           TextWrapping="Wrap"
                           Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
                <TextBlock Text="Anyone with the link can view."
                           FontSize="14"
                           TextWrapping="Wrap"
                           Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
                <arc:CopyButton Value="https://uiarc.dev/p/atlas" />
            </StackPanel>
        </arc:Popover>
    </WrapPanel>
</UserControl>
```

## When to use

`Popover` holds a small piece of interactive content next to the control that opens it: share settings, a filter form
on a list toolbar, a picker built from your own controls. It is anchored to its trigger, so the reader keeps the
context of the page, and it is non-modal by default, so the rest of the page stays usable while it is open.

- **Share and access settings on a document or record.** A Share button in a document header opens a panel with the
  link, a copy control and a permission choice, without taking the reader to a settings page.
- **Filters on a list toolbar.** A Status and date-range filter on an order or invoice list opens from a Filter button,
  applies its values and closes, so the table stays in view while the reader adjusts the criteria.
- **Column or view options in a data table.** A Columns button that lists the optional columns as check boxes, so the
  reader can show or hide fields without leaving the table.
- **Code-driven panels on a canvas or a diagram.** An app that opens a small editor next to a selected node calls
  `ShowAt` with that node's control, so the panel follows the selection.

## When not to use

- **A one-line label on hover or focus:** use `Tooltip`. A popover is opened by a click and holds controls; a tooltip is
  read-only text that appears on hover.
- **A read-only preview of a person or a link:** use `HoverCard`, which opens on hover and never takes focus.
- **A decision that must be answered before the user continues:** use `Dialog`. A popover can be dismissed by a press
  outside it, so it cannot hold a confirmation such as deleting a workspace.
- **A list of commands only:** use `DropdownMenu`, which gives arrow-key navigation and menu semantics for actions.
- **A long form or a multi-step flow:** use a page, a `Drawer` or a `Dialog`. A popover is sized for a few fields; a
  form with many fields pushes the page underneath off screen.

## Usage

A `Popover` is a `ContentControl`. Its `Content` is the panel, and its `Trigger` is the control that opens the panel.
The panel is shown in a `PopoverSurface` that is hosted in a popup, so it is not part of the layout and it can
extend past the edge of the trigger. The trigger and the panel are linked: the panel is measured against the trigger,
so the trigger answers presses with its color only and does not scale.

### Anatomy

1. **Trigger** (`Trigger`): the control that opens the panel. It stays in the page at its own size; the popover adds
   no layout of its own around it.
2. **Panel surface**: a `PopoverSurface` with the raised surface color (`SurfaceRaised`), the foreground text color, a
   1 px border in the border color (`Border`) and the panel corner radius (`RadiusPanel`). It is 16 px inside on every
   side, is at least 192 px (12 rem) and at most 352 px (22 rem) wide, and uses the body font at the small type size
   (`TypeSM`). The floating shadow is drawn by the popup.
3. **Content** (`Content`): the panel's contents. A string is shown as wrapping text in the surface's default text
   template; any other control is shown as it is.
4. **Gap** (`Offset`): 6 px between the trigger and the panel by default, and the panel's entry motion starts from this
   distance.

### Trigger and content

Set `Trigger` to the control that opens the panel. The content of the popover is the panel.

```xml
<arc:Popover>
    <arc:Popover.Trigger>
        <arc:Button Variant="Secondary" Content="Share" />
    </arc:Popover.Trigger>
    <StackPanel Spacing="8">
        <TextBlock Text="Share link" FontWeight="Medium" />
        <TextBlock Text="Anyone with the link can view." />
    </StackPanel>
</arc:Popover>
```

Activating the trigger toggles the popover: a click, a tap or the keyboard activation of a button opens it, and the
same activation closes it again. A non-button trigger opens the popover on `Enter` or `Space`.

### Attached to a control

`arc:Popover.Attach` adds a popover to any control. A click on that control toggles the panel. Use it when the control
is already the button the reader expects, and the panel does not need a separate trigger.

```xml
<arc:Button Content="Filters">
    <arc:Popover.Attach>
        <arc:Popover Placement="Top">
            <TextBlock Text="Opens on the top side." />
        </arc:Popover>
    </arc:Popover.Attach>
</arc:Button>
```

While an attached popover is open, it joins the logical tree of its target, so styles and the `DataContext` of the
target apply inside the panel. When it closes, it leaves that tree again.

### Placement and alignment

`Placement` is the preferred side: `Top`, `Bottom` (the default), `Left` or `Right`. The panel flips to another side
when the preferred side does not fit in the window, and its opening motion follows the side it actually landed on.
`Alignment` places the panel along the trigger edge: `Start` (the default), `Center` or `End`. `Offset` is the gap to
the trigger in pixels; the default is 6. Changing `Placement`, `Alignment` or `Offset` while the popover is open moves
the panel at once.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.PopoverSidesDemo">
    <WrapPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center" ItemSpacing="12" LineSpacing="12">
        <arc:Button Content="Top" Variant="Secondary">
            <arc:Popover.Attach>
                <arc:Popover Placement="Top" Content="Opens on the top side." />
            </arc:Popover.Attach>
        </arc:Button>
        <arc:Button Content="Bottom" Variant="Secondary">
            <arc:Popover.Attach>
                <arc:Popover Placement="Bottom" Content="Opens on the bottom side." />
            </arc:Popover.Attach>
        </arc:Button>
        <arc:Button Content="Left" Variant="Secondary">
            <arc:Popover.Attach>
                <arc:Popover Placement="Left" Content="Opens on the left side." />
            </arc:Popover.Attach>
        </arc:Button>
        <arc:Button Content="Right" Variant="Secondary">
            <arc:Popover.Attach>
                <arc:Popover Placement="Right" Content="Opens on the right side." />
            </arc:Popover.Attach>
        </arc:Button>
        <arc:Button Content="Center" Variant="Secondary">
            <arc:Popover.Attach>
                <arc:Popover Placement="Bottom" Alignment="Center" Content="Opens on the center side." />
            </arc:Popover.Attach>
        </arc:Button>
    </WrapPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```xml
<arc:Popover Placement="Bottom" Alignment="Center" Offset="8">
    <arc:Popover.Trigger>
        <arc:Button Variant="Ghost" Content="Filter" />
    </arc:Popover.Trigger>
    <TextBlock Text="Status: any" />
</arc:Popover>
```

Pick `Bottom` with `Start` for a toolbar button at the left of a list, so the panel lines up with the button's left
edge. Use `Center` for a control in the middle of a row and `End` for a button at the right edge of the page, so the
panel does not run past the window. The default 6 px gap is the Arc look.

### Opening from code

`ShowAt` anchors the popover to any control in the window, so one popover can serve several triggers or a node that
the user selects. `IsOpen` is two-way, and `Opened` and `Closed` report the state changes. Calling `ShowAt` while the
popover is open with a different anchor closes it and reopens it at the new anchor. `Close` closes it from code, and
`OpenCommand` and `CloseCommand` expose the same two actions as `ICommand` for buttons and bindings.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.PopoverFromCodeDemo">
    <WrapPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center" ItemSpacing="12" LineSpacing="12">
        <arc:Button Content="Show at the box" Variant="Secondary" Click="OnShowClick" />
        <Border x:Name="Anchor"
                Width="120"
                Height="36"
                CornerRadius="18"
                BorderThickness="1"
                BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource BorderStrong}" />
    </WrapPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class PopoverFromCodeDemo : UserControl
{
    private readonly Popover _popover = new()
    {
        Content = "Opened from code with ShowAt(anchor).",
        Alignment = PopoverAlignment.Center
    };

    public PopoverFromCodeDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
    }

    private void OnShowClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) => _popover.ShowAt(Anchor);
}
```

```csharp
share.ShowAt(shareButton);
share.Closed += (_, e) => status.Text = $"Closed: {e.Reason}";
```

`Closed` carries a `Reason`: `Escape` when the reader pressed Escape, `PressOutside` when they pressed outside the
panel, and `Programmatic` when the trigger toggled it, the code called `Close` or the value was set to false.

### Modal popover

`IsModal` set to true swallows presses outside the panel, so they only close it and do not reach the control
underneath. A press outside is swallowed: it closes the popover and does not reach the control underneath. Use it for a short
choice that the reader must make or dismiss before clicking elsewhere, and use `Dialog` when the content needs a
confirmation or its own scrim.

```xml
<arc:Popover IsOpen="{Binding ShowPicker}" IsModal="True">
    <TextBlock Text="Pick one option first." />
</arc:Popover>
```

### Small form

A popover can hold a small form, such as a filter. The page stays usable while it is open.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.PopoverSmallFormDemo">
    <WrapPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center" ItemSpacing="12" LineSpacing="12">
        <arc:Popover>
            <arc:Popover.Trigger>
                <arc:Button Content="Filter" Variant="Ghost" />
            </arc:Popover.Trigger>
            <StackPanel Spacing="12">
                <TextBlock Text="Status"
                           FontSize="14"
                           TextWrapping="Wrap"
                           Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
                <arc:Input Placeholder="Any" />
                <arc:Button Content="Apply" />
            </StackPanel>
        </arc:Popover>
    </WrapPanel>
</UserControl>
```

### Binding to a view model

Bind `IsOpen` when the view model decides whether the panel is open, for example when a toolbar command should open a
filter panel. `IsOpen` is two-way, so a press outside the panel also updates the view model.

```csharp
using CommunityToolkit.Mvvm.ComponentModel;
using CommunityToolkit.Mvvm.Input;

public partial class OrdersViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    [ObservableProperty]
    private bool _isFilterOpen;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private string? _status;

    [RelayCommand]
    private void ApplyFilters()
    {
        IsFilterOpen = false;
        // Reload the orders with the selected status and dates.
    }
}
```

```xml
<arc:Button Content="Filter" Variant="Ghost">
    <arc:Popover.Attach>
        <arc:Popover IsOpen="{Binding IsFilterOpen}" Placement="Bottom" Alignment="Start">
            <StackPanel Width="240" Spacing="12">
                <TextBlock Text="Status" FontWeight="Medium" />
                <arc:Button Content="Apply filters" Command="{Binding ApplyFiltersCommand}" />
            </StackPanel>
        </arc:Popover>
    </arc:Popover.Attach>
</arc:Button>
```

The attached popover toggles on click, so the reader opens and closes the panel with the button. Keep `IsOpen` as the
one source of the state, and avoid setting it from a binding and from code at the same time.

### Focus and dismissal

Focus moves into the panel when it opens: to the first focusable control inside it, or to the panel itself when it has
none. When the popover closes, focus returns to the trigger in these cases:

- **Escape** closes the popover and always returns focus to the trigger.
- **A press outside** returns focus to the trigger only when focus was inside the panel. A press that lands on another
  control keeps focus where the reader put it.
- **Closing from code** returns focus to the trigger when focus was inside the panel.

The panel cycles `Tab` among its own controls, so the reader does not Tab out of the panel into the page underneath
without first closing it. A popover nested inside a `Dialog` works: focus can enter the popover, and a press outside the
popover closes only the popover while the dialog stays open.

### Example: filter panel on an order list

A toolbar in a back-office console, above a table of orders. The Filter button opens a small form with a status choice
and two date fields, so the reader narrows the list and sees the table update behind the panel. The panel has one
primary action and a text action, and the panel is 240 px wide, so the reader sees the table behind it.
The primary button reads "Apply filters", a verb with its object, so the action is clear before the reader clicks it.

```xml
<StackPanel Width="560" Spacing="12">
    <arc:Popover Placement="Bottom" Alignment="Start">
        <arc:Popover.Trigger>
            <arc:Button Variant="Secondary" Content="Filter orders" />
        </arc:Popover.Trigger>
        <StackPanel Width="240" Spacing="12"
                    AutomationProperties.Name="Filter orders">
            <TextBlock Text="Status"
                       FontWeight="Medium"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
            <arc:Select Placeholder="Any status" />
            <TextBlock Text="Created"
                       FontWeight="Medium"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
            <arc:Input Placeholder="From" />
            <arc:Input Placeholder="To" />
            <StackPanel Orientation="Horizontal" Spacing="8" HorizontalAlignment="Right">
                <arc:Button Content="Reset" Variant="Ghost" />
                <arc:Button Content="Apply filters" />
            </StackPanel>
        </StackPanel>
    </arc:Popover>
</StackPanel>
```

### Content guidelines

- **Trigger text**: a verb and an object when the panel changes data ("Filter orders", "Share report"), or the name of
  the setting when it opens a view ("Columns"). A plain "More" hides what the panel does.
- **Panel heading**: a short noun phrase in sentence case, such as "Share link". Give the popover an
  `AutomationProperties.Name` when the content has no heading, so the panel is announced by name.
- **Button text in the panel**: a verb and an object for the primary action ("Apply filters", "Copy link"), and a
  plain verb for the dismissing action ("Reset", "Cancel").
- **Field labels**: visible and short, as in any form; a popover is not a place for placeholder-only fields.
- **Helper copy**: one sentence that states the effect of a setting, such as "Anyone with the link can view."

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| More | Filter orders |
| Click here to share this document | Share link |
| Submit | Apply filters |
| Options for Column Display | Columns |
| Please select a status from the list below. | Status |

### Best practices

**Do**

- Keep the panel to a few controls that a reader can act on in one pass. Two fields and one primary button fit well;
  more content belongs in a `Dialog` or a page.
- Give every popover a name, either a heading inside the panel or `AutomationProperties.Name` on it, so the panel is
  announced when focus moves into it.
- Put the most important action first in the panel, and keep the dismissing action beside it, aligned to the right.
- Use `Alignment="End"` for a trigger at the right edge of the page, so the panel stays inside the window.
- Close the popover after an action that completes in it, so the reader sees the result on the page.

**Avoid**

- A confirmation or a destructive action inside a popover. A press outside closes it without a choice, so the reader can
  lose the input; use `Dialog` for anything that must be confirmed.
- Long forms or scrolling content. The panel is sized for a small amount of content, and a tall panel covers the
  table or the page it was opened from.
- Opening a popover from a `HoverCard` or a `Tooltip` trigger. Hover only shows a preview; a click should open a panel
  that holds controls.
- Setting `IsOpen` from two places at once, such as a binding and a `ShowAt` call that fight over the same state.
- Using a popover as a navigation menu. A list of commands belongs in `DropdownMenu`, which gives arrow keys and menu
  semantics.

### Common questions

**What happens when I set `IsOpen` to true before the popover is in the window?** The popover records the request and
opens once it is attached to the visual tree, so a view model can set the state before the view is shown.

**Why does the trigger not scale when I press it?** The panel is measured against the trigger, so a scale on press would
move the anchor while the panel is open. Arc buttons used as a popover trigger show the press as a color change only.

**How do I close the popover from a button inside it?** Call `Close()` in code, or bind the button to a view model
command that sets `IsOpen` to false. Either way, focus returns to the trigger when it was inside the panel.

**Does a press inside the panel close it?** No. Only Escape, a press outside the panel, the trigger toggle, `Close` and
setting `IsOpen` to false close it. A press inside the panel reaches its controls as usual.

**Can I attach the popover to something that is not a button?** Yes. Any control can take `arc:Popover.Attach`. A click
toggles the panel; for a control that is not a button, `Enter` and `Space` open it from the keyboard.

## API reference

### Popover

A small surface anchored to a trigger and opened by a click, for interactive content that should not block the page: share settings, a small filter form, a picker built from your own controls. Two ways to use it: Code can open any content anchored to any control with `ShowAt`. The panel starts 5px toward its trigger at scale 0.97, fades in fast and settles on a spring from the side it actually landed on; it leaves in about 160ms at half the travel, and an open and a close reverse each other mid-flight. Escape and a press outside close it and return focus to the trigger; focus moves into the panel on open. The trigger answers presses with color only (no press scale), since the panel is measured against it.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Trigger` | `Control?` | `null` | The control that opens the panel, shown in place of the popover (optional with `AttachProperty` or `ShowAt`). |
| `IsOpen` | `bool` | `false` | Open state (two-way). |
| `Placement` | `PopoverPlacement` | `Bottom` | Preferred side (flips when it does not fit; the motion follows the side it lands on). |
| `Alignment` | `PopoverAlignment` | `Start` | Alignment along the trigger edge (default Start). |
| `Offset` | `double` | `6` | Gap to the trigger in px (Arc: 6). |
| `IsModal` | `bool` | `false` | Modal: presses outside are swallowed (they only close the popover). Default false. |
| `Attach` | `Popover?` | `null` | *Attached.* Attaches a popover to any control: a click on the control toggles it. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Opened` | `EventHandler?` | Raised when the popover opens. |
| `Closed` | `OverlayClosedEventArgs` | Raised when the popover closes (the exit may still be playing). |

Derives from `ContentControl`: every member of `ContentControl` works as well.

## Accessibility

- Enter and Space on the trigger open the popover. Escape closes it and returns focus to the trigger.
- Focus moves into the panel when it opens. A press outside closes the popover and returns focus to the trigger when
  focus was inside it.
- Give the popover an `AutomationProperties.Name` when its content has no heading. That name labels the panel.
- Non-modal popovers do not trap focus. The panel cycles `Tab` among its own controls, which keeps the reader inside
  the panel until it closes.
- The trigger exposes whether the popover is expanded: its item status is `Expanded` while it is open and `Collapsed`
  while it is closed.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Enter` or `Space` on a non-button trigger | Opens the popover and moves focus into the panel |
| `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` inside the panel | Move between the panel's controls; focus cycles within the panel |
| `Escape` | Closes the popover and returns focus to the trigger |
| Press outside the panel | Closes the popover; focus returns to the trigger when it was inside the panel |

## Motion

- The panel starts 5px toward its trigger at a scale of 0.97, fades in quickly and settles on a spring from the side it
  landed on.
- Closing takes about 160ms at half the travel. An open and a close reverse each other in the middle of the motion.
- The trigger changes color when pressed but does not scale, because the panel is measured against it.
- Reduced motion removes the movement and scaling and keeps only a short fade. Off shows or removes the panel at once.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| Panel opens | Starts 5px toward the trigger at 0.97, fades in quickly, and settles on a spring | Short fade only | Shown at once |
| Panel closes | Fades out with half the travel in about 160ms | Short fade only | Removed at once |
| Open interrupted by a close | Reverses from the current position | Short fade | Immediate |
| Trigger pressed | Color change only; no scale | Color change only | Color change only |

## Related

- `Tooltip` for a one-line label on hover or focus.
- `HoverCard` for a read-only preview that opens on hover.
- `Dialog` for content that must be dealt with before the page can be used.
- `DropdownMenu` for a list of commands.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `Tooltip` | A one-line label on hover or focus is enough, and nothing in it is clickable |
| `HoverCard` | A read-only preview of a person or link should open on hover, without taking focus |
| `Dialog` | The reader must confirm or finish something before they continue |
| `DropdownMenu` | The content is a list of commands with arrow-key navigation |
| `Drawer` | The content is a longer panel that slides in from an edge of the window |

# Hover card

> Preview a person or link on hover or focus without leaving the page.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/hover-card

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.HoverCardMentionDemo">
    <WrapPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center" ItemSpacing="12" LineSpacing="12">
        <arc:HoverCard>
            <arc:HoverCard.Trigger>
                <arc:Button Content="@maya" Variant="Ghost" />
            </arc:HoverCard.Trigger>
            <arc:HoverCardProfile DisplayName="Maya Chen"
                                  Role="Product designer, Payments"
                                  Bio="Designs checkout and billing flows. Previously at Linear."
                                  Meta="Lisbon · 14:20 local time">
                <arc:HoverCardProfile.Stats>
                    <arc:HoverCardStat Label="Projects" Value="12" />
                    <arc:HoverCardStat Label="Reviews" Value="48" />
                </arc:HoverCardProfile.Stats>
            </arc:HoverCardProfile>
        </arc:HoverCard>
    </WrapPanel>
</UserControl>
```

## When to use

`HoverCard` shows a short, read-only preview of a person, a record or a link when someone points at or focuses a name
in running text. The subject stays in the page, next to the text that names it, so a reader can check who a mention
refers to without losing their place in a thread, a table or a list.

- **A mention in a comment or an incident thread.** An `@maya` in a post-incident review opens her role, team and
  local time, so the on-call engineer knows whom to ask before tagging anyone.
- **An owner or author name in a table.** A deployment list with an owner column can open a small profile on each
  name, instead of sending the reader to a separate user page for a quick check.
- **A link to an internal record.** A link to a pull request, an order or a support ticket can preview its title and
  one line of context on hover, while a click still navigates to the record.
- **Dense rosters of people.** A list of reviewers or assignees where the reader moves from one name to the next.
  Once one card is open, the next one opens almost at once, so scanning a roster stays fast (see Dense list).

## When not to use

- **A one-line label for an icon or a truncated word:** use `Tooltip`. A hover card is for several facts about a
  subject; a label is a phrase, and a tooltip is lighter and does not need a preview layout.
- **Buttons, inputs or any action:** use `Popover`. Focus never enters a hover card, so a button inside it cannot be
  reached with Tab and a field cannot be typed into.
- **The signed-in user's own account menu:** use `UserMenu`, which lists the account actions (profile, sign out) that
  a preview card does not offer.
- **A decision or a warning the reader must see before continuing:** use `Dialog`. A hover card closes when the pointer
  leaves and on any press outside it, so it cannot hold a message the reader has to acknowledge.
- **A full profile, an activity feed or a long bio:** link to the record's page. The card is 296 px wide by default,
  and a long preview covers the content beneath it.

## Usage

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:HoverCard Placement="Bottom">
        <arc:HoverCard.Trigger>
            <arc:Button Variant="Ghost" Content="@maya" />
        </arc:HoverCard.Trigger>
        <arc:HoverCardProfile DisplayName="Maya Chen"
                              Role="Product designer, Payments"
                              Bio="Designs checkout and billing flows."
                              Meta="Lisbon · 14:20 local time">
            <arc:HoverCardProfile.Stats>
                <arc:HoverCardStat Label="Projects" Value="12" />
                <arc:HoverCardStat Label="Reviews" Value="48" />
            </arc:HoverCardProfile.Stats>
        </arc:HoverCardProfile>
    </arc:HoverCard>
</UserControl>
```

`HoverCard` derives from Avalonia's `ContentControl`, so its `Content` is the preview and `ContentTemplate` applies to
it. The `Trigger` is the focusable control that stays in the page. In place, the card shows only the trigger; its
content opens in an anchored `PopoverSurface`, the same surface `Popover` uses, hosted in a popup. The popup is not in
the layout, so the card never pushes the text around it. `HoverCardProfile` derives from `TemplatedControl` and
provides the standard person layout (avatar, name, role, bio, stats and footer) so that every card in an application
looks the same.

### Anatomy

1. **Trigger** (`Trigger`): the focusable control in the page, such as a Ghost `Button` with the handle or a link. It
   is the only part that takes up space in the layout.
2. **Card surface**: a `PopoverSurface` whose width comes from `CardWidth` (296 by default), with 16 px of padding, the
   raised surface color, a 1 px border in the border color and the panel corner radius. It is not focusable, and the
   floating shadow is drawn by the popup.
3. **Avatar**: a large `Avatar` fed by `AvatarSource`. Without a portrait it shows the initials of `DisplayName`.
4. **Name** (`DisplayName`): the base type size in medium weight and the primary text color. It is one line and ends
   with an ellipsis when it is too long.
5. **Role** (`Role`): a small line in the secondary text color, one line with an ellipsis. It is hidden while the
   string is empty.
6. **Bio** (`Bio`): a small paragraph in the secondary text color. It wraps; it is hidden while it is empty.
7. **Stats** (`Stats`): a row under a 1 px rule in the subtle border color, with 12 px above the rule. Each entry shows
   the value in the base size and medium weight, with the label beneath it in the extra-small muted color. Columns are
   24 px apart and rows 8 px apart, and the row wraps. It is hidden while `Stats` is empty.
8. **Meta** (`Meta`): a footer in the extra-small muted color, usually a location and a local time. It is hidden while
   the value is null.

The rows of the profile are separated by 12 px, and the avatar and the text column are separated by 12 px. The card sits
8 px from its trigger (`Offset`).

### Profile card

The profile above is the usual form of the preview: the name and role identify the person, the bio says what they do,
the stats give two numbers that help a reader judge the person, and the meta line gives a location and local time for
people in other time zones. Keep to two or three stats. The card has a fixed width, so each stat takes a column
beside its neighbours and a long list of stats makes the card taller than the reader expects.

### Link preview

`arc:HoverCard.Attach` adds a card to any control, such as a plain text link, without a `Trigger`. The attached card
is anchored to the control it is attached to. While it is open it joins that control's logical tree, so styles and the
`DataContext` of the target reach the card.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.HoverCardLinkPreviewDemo">
    <TextBlock Text="uiarc.dev/components/hover-card"
               Cursor="Hand"
               Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Accent}">
        <arc:HoverCard.Attach>
            <arc:HoverCard Placement="Top"
                           Content="Hover card: preview a person or link on hover or focus without leaving the page." />
        </arc:HoverCard.Attach>
    </TextBlock>
</UserControl>
```

Here the card's `Content` is a string. A string is shown as wrapping text in the card's default text template, which
is enough for a title and a one-line summary of a link. Use a `HoverCardProfile` when the subject is a person.

### Timing and width

`OpenDelay` defaults to 500 ms and `CloseDelay` to 140 ms. The open delay stops a card from appearing each time the
pointer crosses a name on the way somewhere else. The close delay is a grace period: it gives the pointer time to
travel the 8 px gap into the card, and entering the card cancels it, so the reader can scroll the bio or select text.
`CardWidth` sets the width of the card, which defaults to 296 (18.5 rem). A card is also limited by the space available
in the window, and it flips to another side when the preferred one does not fit.

```csharp
card.OpenDelay = TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(300);
card.CardWidth = 320;
```

Widen the card only when the bios are long enough to wrap onto many lines at 296. Shorten `OpenDelay` only on a
trigger where a preview matters more than a quiet page, such as an owner name on a deployment. A page-wide warm state
also applies: while any card is open, and for 300 ms after the last one closed, the next card opens after 80 ms with
a fade only, so a reader who moves across a roster does not wait 500 ms at each name.

The card's padding is `CardPadding` (16 by default; a compact preview card can use `16,14`). It is set next to `CardWidth` so
a preview of a source or a person can use the same surface in a tighter layout.

### Showing from code

`Show` and `Hide` change `IsOpen` directly. `Show` opens the card at once, without `OpenDelay`, and `Hide` closes it at
once, without `CloseDelay`. `IsOpen` is two-way, so a binding or a code change both open the card. `Opened` and `Closed`
report the state changes. `Closed` also carries a `Reason`, which is `Escape` when the person pressed Escape,
`PressOutside` when they pressed outside the card, and `Programmatic` when the pointer left the trigger or code called
`Hide`. The exit animation can still be playing when `Closed` is raised.

```csharp
card.Show();
card.Closed += (_, e) => log.Text = $"Closed by {e.Reason}";
```

The `Anchor` property is the control the card is positioned against: the attached target when the card is attached,
otherwise the `Trigger`. `Surface` and `Popup` expose the surface and the popup after the first open; they are null
before that.

### Dense list

Once a card is open, moving to the next trigger opens it almost at once with a fade only. A roster of reviewers is the
typical case: each name shows its own card without a half-second wait, and the page does not flash between cards.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.HoverCardDenseListDemo">
    <WrapPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center" ItemSpacing="12" LineSpacing="12">
        <arc:HoverCard>
            <arc:HoverCard.Trigger>
                <arc:Button Content="@ari" Variant="Ghost" />
            </arc:HoverCard.Trigger>
            <arc:HoverCardProfile DisplayName="Ari Okafor"
                                  Role="Staff engineer, Platform"
                                  Bio="Owns the build pipeline and the design token compiler."
                                  Meta="Lagos · 13:20 local time">
                <arc:HoverCardProfile.Stats>
                    <arc:HoverCardStat Label="Projects" Value="31" />
                    <arc:HoverCardStat Label="Reviews" Value="210" />
                </arc:HoverCardProfile.Stats>
            </arc:HoverCardProfile>
        </arc:HoverCard>
        <arc:HoverCard>
            <arc:HoverCard.Trigger>
                <arc:Button Content="@lena" Variant="Ghost" />
            </arc:HoverCard.Trigger>
            <arc:HoverCardProfile DisplayName="Lena Novak"
                                  Role="Research lead"
                                  Bio="Runs the quarterly usability studies."
                                  Meta="Prague · 14:20 local time">
                <arc:HoverCardProfile.Stats>
                    <arc:HoverCardStat Label="Projects" Value="7" />
                    <arc:HoverCardStat Label="Reviews" Value="19" />
                </arc:HoverCardProfile.Stats>
            </arc:HoverCardProfile>
        </arc:HoverCard>
    </WrapPanel>
</UserControl>
```

### Binding to a view model

In an MVVM application the view model owns the people, and the hover card renders one profile per item. Only `IsOpen`
is two-way; bind `Trigger`, `Content` and the profile properties one way, from the data.

```csharp
using System.Collections.ObjectModel;
using CommunityToolkit.Mvvm.ComponentModel;

public sealed record MemberProfile(
    string Handle,
    string Name,
    string Role,
    string Bio,
    string Location,
    int Projects,
    int Reviews);

public partial class ReviewersViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    public ObservableCollection<MemberProfile> Reviewers { get; } = new();
}
```

```xml
<ItemsControl ItemsSource="{Binding Reviewers}">
    <ItemsControl.ItemTemplate>
        <DataTemplate>
            <arc:HoverCard>
                <arc:HoverCard.Trigger>
                    <arc:Button Variant="Ghost" Content="{Binding Handle}" />
                </arc:HoverCard.Trigger>
                <arc:HoverCardProfile DisplayName="{Binding Name}"
                                      Role="{Binding Role}"
                                      Bio="{Binding Bio}"
                                      Meta="{Binding Location}" />
            </arc:HoverCard>
        </DataTemplate>
    </ItemsControl.ItemTemplate>
</ItemsControl>
```

`Stats` is a read-only collection, so XAML cannot bind it. Fill it in code when the profile is created, and format the
numbers with the current culture so that a thousand separator follows the reader's settings:

```csharp
var profile = new HoverCardProfile { DisplayName = member.Name, Role = member.Role };
profile.Stats.Add(new HoverCardStat("Projects", member.Projects.ToString("N0", CultureInfo.CurrentCulture)));
profile.Stats.Add(new HoverCardStat("Reviews", member.Reviews.ToString("N0", CultureInfo.CurrentCulture)));
```

Keep the handle on the trigger and the name in the card: the trigger is what a keyboard user reaches, and it needs
text that names the person.

### Focus and dismissal

A hover card opens from three inputs: the pointer, a Tab focus and a click. The rules differ, and they are chosen so
that a keyboard user and a mouse user both get a predictable card.

- **Tab focus** opens the card at once. Focus that arrives by a pointer click does not open it; the click itself does.
- **`OpensOnFocus`** makes keyboard focus follow the same timing as the pointer: with it on, Tab or arrow-key focus opens
  the card after `OpenDelay` (zero opens it at once), and the card closes as soon as focus leaves, unless the pointer is
  on the trigger or the card. Focus moving inside the trigger does not close or reopen it. A pointer-driven focus never
  opens it. Leave it off to keep the default: Tab focus opens the card at once.
- **Losing focus** starts the close grace. The card closes after `CloseDelay` unless the pointer is over the trigger or
  the card.
- **Escape** closes an open card. The card then stays closed until the pointer or the focus leaves the trigger, so it
  does not reopen while the reader is still on the same name.
- **A press outside** the card closes it with the `PressOutside` reason.
- **Only one card is open** at a time. Opening a card closes the one that was open.
- **Removing the trigger** from the page closes the card at once, without the close animation, so a list that refreshes
  never leaves a card behind.

Focus never enters the card. The card has no focusable content of its own, so the reader cannot Tab into it and
cannot type in it. A card that needs a control must be a `Popover` instead.

### Example: deployment owners in an admin console

A deployment history in a SaaS operations console. Each owner is a ghost button with a handle, so the row reads
quickly and the owner's role and local time appear on hover or focus. The card shows two stats only, because the
reader needs the owner's current load, not a history. The meta line gives the local time, which matters when a
handoff crosses time zones at the end of an on-call shift.

```xml
<StackPanel Width="560" Spacing="12">
    <Grid ColumnDefinitions="*,Auto,Auto" ColumnSpacing="16">
        <TextBlock Text="Payments API 2026.10.14" VerticalAlignment="Center" />
        <TextBlock Grid.Column="1" Text="Succeeded" VerticalAlignment="Center"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
        <arc:HoverCard Grid.Column="2" Placement="Left">
            <arc:HoverCard.Trigger>
                <arc:Button Variant="Ghost" Content="@ari" />
            </arc:HoverCard.Trigger>
            <arc:HoverCardProfile DisplayName="Ari Okafor"
                                  Role="Staff engineer, Platform"
                                  Bio="Owns the build pipeline and the release train."
                                  Meta="Lagos · 13:20 local time">
                <arc:HoverCardProfile.Stats>
                    <arc:HoverCardStat Label="Open reviews" Value="3" />
                    <arc:HoverCardStat Label="On call" Value="Today" />
                </arc:HoverCardProfile.Stats>
            </arc:HoverCardProfile>
        </arc:HoverCard>
    </Grid>
    <Grid ColumnDefinitions="*,Auto,Auto" ColumnSpacing="16">
        <TextBlock Text="Billing webhooks 2026.10.19" VerticalAlignment="Center" />
        <TextBlock Grid.Column="1" Text="Running" VerticalAlignment="Center"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
        <arc:HoverCard Grid.Column="2" Placement="Left">
            <arc:HoverCard.Trigger>
                <arc:Button Variant="Ghost" Content="@lena" />
            </arc:HoverCard.Trigger>
            <arc:HoverCardProfile DisplayName="Lena Novak"
                                  Role="Research lead"
                                  Bio="Runs the quarterly usability studies."
                                  Meta="Prague · 14:20 local time">
                <arc:HoverCardProfile.Stats>
                    <arc:HoverCardStat Label="Open reviews" Value="1" />
                    <arc:HoverCardStat Label="On call" Value="Tomorrow" />
                </arc:HoverCardProfile.Stats>
            </arc:HoverCardProfile>
        </arc:HoverCard>
    </Grid>
</StackPanel>
```

The `Placement="Left"` keeps each card clear of the status column and the rows below.

### Content guidelines

- **Display name**: the name the organization uses, in full: "Maya Chen". The handle belongs on the trigger, so the
  card does not repeat it.
- **Role**: a function and a team, separated by a comma: "Product designer, Payments". Use sentence case, and leave the
  role out rather than writing a placeholder such as "Employee".
- **Bio**: one sentence about what the person works on, in the present tense. Keep it under a line or two at the card
  width.
- **Meta**: a place and the local time, with a middle dot as the separator: "Lisbon · 14:20 local time".
- **Stat labels**: plural nouns of one or two words ("Projects", "Reviews"). Put the numbers in `Value` as digits, so
  they are easy to compare.

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| Hi! I am a designer who loves things. | Designs checkout and billing flows. |
| Role: Employee | Product designer, Payments |
| Number of projects you have worked on | Projects |
| Time: 14:20 | Lisbon · 14:20 local time |
| Name: @maya | Maya Chen (the handle is the trigger text) |

### Best practices

**Do**

- Use a focusable control as the trigger, with text that names the person, such as a Ghost `Button` with the handle.
  Keyboard users reach the card through the trigger, and the trigger's text is what a screen reader announces first.
- Keep the card read-only. Put actions on the record's page or on the trigger, and use a `Popover` when the preview
  needs a button. Focus never enters a hover card, so a button inside it is unreachable from the keyboard.
- Keep the bio to a sentence and the stats to two or three values. The card has a fixed width, so a short card reads
  at a glance in a long list.
- Keep the default `OpenDelay` on a page with many triggers. A 500 ms wait keeps the cards quiet while the pointer
  crosses names on the way to something else.
- Give a link preview the same text as the link, so the help text announced while the card is open matches what the
  reader already read.

**Avoid**

- Buttons, fields or links inside the card. Focus never enters the card, so these controls cannot be reached from the
  keyboard, and a touch user has no way to press them.
- Setting `OpenDelay` to zero on every trigger in a list. A card then opens on every pointer crossing, and the page
  reads as noise.
- Making the card the only way to reach a person's details. The screen reader hears only the summary in the trigger's
  help text, and the card is not on the page when it is closed.
- Long paragraphs in `Bio` or `Meta`. The card grows with its text and covers the rows beneath it; link to the full
  profile instead.
- A non-focusable `Trigger`, such as a plain `TextBlock`. Keyboard users cannot focus it, so the card never opens for
  them. Use `arc:HoverCard.Attach` on the text, or a focusable control as the trigger.

### Common questions

**Why does a click open the card at once when hovering waits half a second?** A mouse click on the trigger is an
explicit request, so it opens the card without `OpenDelay`. The wait only applies to hover, which can happen by accident
while the pointer crosses the trigger.

**Can the reader move the pointer into the card?** Yes. Leaving the trigger starts the close grace of `CloseDelay`
(140 ms). Entering the card cancels that close, and the card stays open while the pointer is over it. Leaving the card
closes it after the grace.

**How does a touch screen open the card?** A tap on the trigger toggles the card: the first tap opens it at once, and
the next tap on the trigger closes it. Touch pointer enter and leave events do not open or close it.

**What does a screen reader hear while the card is open?** The trigger's help text is set to the summary while the card
is open. For a `HoverCardProfile` that is the name, followed by the role when there is one. For string content it is the
string. Otherwise it is the card's own `AutomationProperties.Name`. The previous help text is restored when the card
closes, so the reader hears the normal trigger description after that.

## API reference

### HoverCard

A read-only preview of a person or link that opens after a short hover or keyboard focus: mentions, avatars, author names, link previews — where a click must stay free for navigation. It waits 500ms; moving to another trigger while a card is open (or within 300ms of one closing) opens the next after 80ms with a fade only. The pointer can travel into the card during a 140ms grace and it stays open while the pointer is over it. Tab focus opens at once, Enter skips the wait, Escape closes (and it stays closed while the pointer rests on the trigger); on touch a tap toggles it. One card is open at a time. The card grows from the trigger edge: scale 0.96 and 4px toward the trigger on the smooth spring, with its own fade; leaving mid-exit and coming back turns it around. Focus never enters the card, so keep its content read-only.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Trigger` | `Control?` | `null` | The focusable trigger shown in place of the card (a mention, an avatar, a link). |
| `IsOpen` | `bool` | `false` | Open state (two-way): it follows the card when hover, focus, a click or Escape opens or closes it, and setting it opens or closes the card at once without the delay; any write cancels a pending open or close. |
| `OpensOnFocus` | `bool` | `false` | Opens the card when keyboard focus (Tab or the arrow keys) lands on the trigger or inside it, after `OpenDelay` (zero opens at once), and closes it as soon as focus leaves unless the pointer rests on the trigger or the card; focus from a click or from code does not open it. Off by default, where Tab focus opens the card at once and losing focus starts the `CloseDelay` grace. |
| `Placement` | `PopoverPlacement` | `Bottom` | Preferred side (default Bottom). |
| `Alignment` | `PopoverAlignment` | `Start` | Alignment along the trigger edge (default Start). |
| `OpenDelay` | `TimeSpan` | `00:00:00.5000000` | Hover time before the first card opens (default 500ms); with `OpensOnFocus` also the wait after keyboard focus. |
| `CloseDelay` | `TimeSpan` | `00:00:00.1400000` | Grace after the pointer leaves, so it can travel into the card (default 140ms). |
| `CardWidth` | `double` | `296` | Card width (Arc: 18.5rem). |
| `Offset` | `double` | `8` | Gap to the trigger (Arc: 8). |
| `CardPadding` | `Thickness` | `16,16,16,16` | Space inside the card border (Arc: 16; a chat's citation preview uses 14 16). |
| `Attach` | `HoverCard?` | `null` | *Attached.* Attaches a hover card to any control. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Opened` | `EventHandler?` | Raised when the card opens. |
| `Closed` | `OverlayClosedEventArgs` | Raised when the card closes (the exit may still be playing). |

Derives from `ContentControl`: every member of `ContentControl` works as well.

### HoverCardProfile

A person preview for `HoverCard`: portrait (or initials), name, role, a short bio, a few numbers and a quiet footer line. Each time the card opens its rows settle in from 4px below with a tiny stagger (40ms + 35ms per row, standard duration, ease enter); reduced motion shows them at rest. The stagger replays on every open, which a ControlTheme transition (first frame never animates) cannot express, so one linear `MotionValue` drives a shared timeline for all rows.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `DisplayName` | `string?` | `null` | The person's name (initials come from it when there is no portrait). |
| `Role` | `string?` | `null` | Role and team, such as "Product designer, Payments". |
| `AvatarSource` | `ImageSource?` | `null` | Portrait; a downloading portrait fades in from a soft blur. |
| `Bio` | `string?` | `null` | Short biography shown under the name; empty when not set. |
| `Meta` | `object?` | `null` | Footer line, such as a location and local time (string or content). |
| `Stats` | `AvaloniaList<HoverCardStat>` | – | *Read-only.* Label / value pairs shown as a wrapping row of numbers. |

Pseudo-classes: `:has-role`, `:has-bio`, `:has-stats`, `:has-meta`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

### HoverCardStat

A number shown in a `HoverCardProfile` (value over its label).

## Accessibility

- While the card is open, its summary is written to the trigger's help text. The card itself has no accessible name
  of its own unless one is set, so the trigger's text must name the person.
- Focus never enters the card. Keep its content read-only and put actions on the trigger or in a `Popover`.
- The card surface is exposed to assistive technology as a tooltip, not as a button or a link. When nothing else describes
  it, the trigger's help text falls back to the card's visible text.
- Tab focus opens the card at once, Enter skips the open delay, and Escape closes it. It stays closed while the pointer
  rests on the trigger.
- On touch, a tap toggles the card. Only one card is open at a time, so a screen reader user never has two previews
  competing for attention.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Tab` onto the trigger | Opens the card at once, with no open delay |
| `Tab` away from the trigger | Closes the card after `CloseDelay` (140 ms), unless the pointer is over the trigger or the card |
| `Enter` on the trigger | Opens the card at once when it is closed |
| `Escape` | Closes the card; it stays closed until the pointer or the focus leaves the trigger |

## Motion

- The card grows from its trigger edge: it scales from 0.96 to 1 and moves 4px toward the trigger on a smooth spring,
  with a separate fade.
- Profile rows settle in from 4px below one after another. The avatar fades in from a soft blur once its portrait has
  loaded.
- When another card closed less than 300ms ago, the next card opens after 80ms with a fade only.
- Each opening replays the profile rows, so a card that is opened again always settles in from the same starting point.
- Reduced motion removes the scale and the movement and keeps a short fade. Off shows or removes the card at once.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| Card opens | Scales from 0.96 and moves 4px toward the trigger on a smooth spring; the fade runs alongside | Short fade only | Shown at once |
| Card closes | Fades out; reverses if it reopens mid-exit | Short fade | Removed at once |
| Profile rows open | Each row rises 4px and fades in, 35ms after the previous one, on every opening | Rows shown at rest | Rows shown at rest |
| Next card after a recent close | Opens after 80ms with a fade only | Fade only | Shown at once |

## Related

- `Tooltip` for a short text label on hover or focus.
- `Popover` for a card with buttons or inputs, opened on click.
- `Avatar` for the picture shown in a profile.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `Tooltip` | A one-line label is enough for an icon, a shortcut or a truncated word |
| `Popover` | The content has buttons, inputs or a small form, and a click opens it |
| `Avatar` / `AvatarGroup` | You need the portrait or the initials that the card shows, or a group of people |
| `Dialog` | The reader must read or act on something before continuing |
| `UserMenu` | The menu belongs to the signed-in user's own account |
| `DropdownMenu` | A list of commands opens from a trigger |
