# Tooltip

> Short supporting text for unfamiliar controls.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/tooltip

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.TooltipSidesDemo">
    <WrapPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center" ItemSpacing="12" LineSpacing="12">
        <arc:Button Content="Top" Variant="Secondary" arc:Tooltip.Tip="Copy link" />
        <arc:Button Content="Bottom" Variant="Secondary"
                    arc:Tooltip.Tip="Share with your team"
                    arc:Tooltip.Side="Bottom" />
        <arc:Button Content="Left" Variant="Secondary"
                    arc:Tooltip.Tip="Archive"
                    arc:Tooltip.Side="Left" />
        <arc:Button Content="Right" Variant="Secondary"
                    arc:Tooltip.Tip="Delete forever"
                    arc:Tooltip.Side="Right" />
    </WrapPanel>
</UserControl>
```

## When to use

`Tooltip` gives a short label to a control that does not explain itself on screen. It is attached to the control with
`arc:Tooltip.Tip`, so the trigger keeps its own layout and no extra element is added to the page. The label appears on
hover or keyboard focus, and it disappears as soon as the reader presses the control or moves away.

- **Icon-only buttons in a toolbar.** A document or order toolbar with a printer, a link or an archive icon needs a label
  such as "Print packing slip" so the reader knows what each icon does before pressing it.
- **Truncated text in a table or a card.** An order note or a product name cut off with an ellipsis can show its full
  text on hover, so the reader does not have to open the record to read it.
- **Short help beside a setting.** A short hint on a field or a toggle, such as "Refunds open after the payment settles",
  explains a rule without taking space from the form.
- **A disabled control that needs an explanation.** A disabled Refund button can explain why it is unavailable while the
  reader points at it.

## When not to use

- **Links, buttons with actions or inputs the reader must use:** use `Popover`. Tooltip content cannot be interacted
  with, so a link or a button inside it is never reachable.
- **A rich preview of a person or a link:** use `HoverCard`, which shows a profile or a summary with a layout for
  several facts.
- **Information that touch users must see:** show it on the page, not in a tooltip. Tooltips open on pointer hover and
  keyboard focus, so a touch user may never see the text.
- **Errors and validation messages:** use the field's own error row, such as the `ErrorMessage` of `Input`. A tooltip
  disappears on the next press and cannot be found by a reader who did not point at the field.
- **Explanations longer than a sentence or two:** use inline helper text or a `Popover` with a heading. The bubble is
  limited to 240 px wide and is meant for a label, not a paragraph.

## Usage

A tooltip is an attached property. Set `arc:Tooltip.Tip` on any control; the text appears on hover or keyboard focus.
The tooltip is not a child of the control, so it is safe to add to a button, a text block, a check box or an icon in a
template.

### Anatomy

1. **Trigger**: the control that carries `arc:Tooltip.Tip`. It keeps its own size and layout; the tooltip never changes
   it.
2. **Bubble**: a rounded box with the inverse of the page's text colors, so it reads as a dark label on a light page and
   as a light label on a dark page. It has a 1 px hairline border made by mixing 14% of the background into the
   foreground, which keeps its edge visible on both themes.
3. **Text**: the tip content in the small type size, regular weight. Strings and numbers wrap inside the bubble, whose
   maximum width is 240 px with 16 px of padding on each side and 12 px above and below the text.
4. **Gap**: the bubble sits 8 px away from the trigger on the side set by `Side`, and it rises 3 px into place when it
   opens.

### Basic

```xml
<arc:Button Content="Copy" arc:Tooltip.Tip="Copy link" />
```

Use a short verb phrase for an icon-only button, because the tooltip is the only visible label. A text button that
already says what it does needs no tooltip; a tooltip that repeats the button text adds delay and noise.

### Side

`arc:Tooltip.Side` sets the side of the trigger the bubble opens on: `Top` (the default), `Bottom`, `Left` or `Right`.
Choose the side that keeps the bubble clear of the content the reader is looking at.

```xml
<arc:Button Variant="Secondary" Content="Share" arc:Tooltip.Tip="Share with your team"
            arc:Tooltip.Side="Bottom" />
```

Use `Top` for controls in the middle of a page, `Bottom` for controls in a page header that sit against the top edge of
the window, and `Left` or `Right` for controls at the edge of a vertical toolbar, where a top tooltip would cover the
toolbar above it.

### Binding the text

`Tip` accepts any object. Bind it when the text comes from the view model, so a label can change with the state of
the application.

```xml
<arc:Button Content="Save" arc:Tooltip.Tip="{Binding SaveHint}" />
```

### Changing the text and the delay

Change the text in code while the tooltip is open. Strings crossfade and the bubble resizes to fit. Set
`ShowDelay` to change the wait before the first tooltip opens; the default is 250 ms, and a tooltip opened at once
while another one is warm ignores it.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.TooltipLiveTextDemo">
    <WrapPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center" ItemSpacing="12" LineSpacing="12">
        <arc:Button x:Name="Save"
                    Content="Save"
                    Variant="Primary"
                    arc:Tooltip.Tip="Save draft"
                    Click="OnSaveClick" />
    </WrapPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class TooltipLiveTextDemo : UserControl
{
    private int _saves;

    public TooltipLiveTextDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
    }

    // Changing the tip while the tooltip is open crossfades the text and springs the bubble to the new size.
    private void OnSaveClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
        => Tooltip.SetTip(Save, ++_saves % 2 == 1 ? "Saved just now" : "Save draft");
}
```

```csharp
Tooltip.SetTip(save, "Saved just now");
Tooltip.SetShowDelay(save, TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(400));
```

Change the text only when the state the reader is looking at changes, such as a button that turns from "Save draft" into
"Saved just now" after a save. Do not change it every second; a tooltip that keeps rewriting itself is hard to read.

### Showing from code

`Tooltip.SetIsOpen` shows or hides the tooltip on an element at once, without `ShowDelay`. Use it to explain a control
that the reader has just changed, for example a refund button that becomes available after a payment settles. Call it
with `false` to hide the tooltip again. The tooltip still closes on its own when the pointer leaves, the control is
pressed or the focus moves away, so do not keep it open from code after the reader has moved on.

```csharp
Tooltip.SetIsOpen(refund, true);
```

### Binding to a view model

Bind the tip to a view model property when the explanation depends on data. A disabled control is a common case: the
tip explains why the action is unavailable, and it is shown while the pointer is over the control.

```csharp
using CommunityToolkit.Mvvm.ComponentModel;

public partial class OrderRowViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    [ObservableProperty]
    private bool _canRefund;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private string _refundHint = "Refunds open after the payment settles.";
}
```

```xml
<arc:Button Content="Refund"
            IsEnabled="{Binding CanRefund}"
            arc:Tooltip.Tip="{Binding RefundHint}" />
```

A disabled control does not open a tooltip from hover or focus by itself; a tooltip on a disabled control opens only
while the pointer is over it. Keep the reason in the tip, so the reader learns what would enable the control. When
the reason changes (for example, "Refunds open after the payment settles" becomes "Refund requested on 2026-10-18"),
update the bound property and the tooltip follows.

### Queueing and timing

The first tooltip waits `ShowDelay` (250 ms by default) after the pointer enters the control or a Tab focus lands on
it. While any tooltip is open, and for 300 ms after the last one closed, the next tooltip opens at once with a fade
only. The shared timing lets a reader move along a toolbar and read each label without waiting at every button, and
the first wait keeps tooltips off the screen while the pointer simply crosses the window.

Focus by mouse does not open a tooltip; a click on a control only closes one. A press on the trigger closes the
tooltip at once, so it does not sit over a menu the press opened.

### Example: order row actions in a fulfilment console

A row in a fulfilment console with a truncated customer note and three actions. The note shows its full text in a
tooltip, because the row is too narrow to show it in full. The buttons carry text labels, so the tooltip is used only
where the label is not enough: the refund button is disabled, and its tip explains the rule that blocks it.

```xml
<StackPanel Width="560" Spacing="12">
    <Grid ColumnDefinitions="*,Auto,Auto,Auto" ColumnSpacing="8">
        <StackPanel Spacing="2" VerticalAlignment="Center">
            <TextBlock Text="ord_2026_0412 · Acme Analytics"
                       FontWeight="Medium"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
            <TextBlock Text="Leave the parcel with the concierge at the rear entrance. Ring twice."
                       MaxWidth="320"
                       TextTrimming="CharacterEllipsis"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}"
                       arc:Tooltip.Tip="Leave the parcel with the concierge at the rear entrance. Ring twice." />
        </StackPanel>
        <arc:Button Grid.Column="1" Variant="Ghost" Content="Print label"
                    VerticalAlignment="Center"
                    arc:Tooltip.Tip="Print the shipping label" />
        <arc:Button Grid.Column="2" Variant="Ghost" Content="Copy tracking"
                    VerticalAlignment="Center"
                    arc:Tooltip.Tip="Copy the tracking number" />
        <arc:Button Grid.Column="3" Variant="Secondary" Content="Refund"
                    VerticalAlignment="Center"
                    IsEnabled="False"
                    arc:Tooltip.Tip="Refunds open after the payment settles." />
    </Grid>
</StackPanel>
```

The note is truncated because the row is fixed in width and the full text would push the actions out of the row. The
tooltip repeats the full text rather than a summary, since the reader came to see the whole note. The disabled refund
button keeps its tip, because a disabled control gives no other clue about why it cannot be used.

### Content guidelines

- **Length**: one short phrase or sentence. The bubble is 240 px wide at most, so a tip longer than about 60 characters
  wraps onto several lines and is harder to scan.
- **Form**: a verb phrase for an action ("Copy link", "Print the shipping label"), or a noun phrase for a state ("Draft
  saved 2 minutes ago"). Use sentence case and no exclamation marks.
- **Period**: a single sentence can end with a period, and a phrase needs none. Pick one style per application and keep
  it.
- **Shortcuts**: include a keyboard shortcut only when the application defines it. Do not invent one for the tip.
- **Disabled controls**: say what would enable the control, not only that it is unavailable.

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| Click this button to copy the link to your clipboard. | Copy link |
| Delete | Delete draft |
| Important!!! Read this first. | Expires in 24 hours |
| Not available | Refunds open after the payment settles. |
| Save | Save draft |

### Best practices

**Do**

- Give every icon-only control a visible tooltip and an `AutomationProperties.Name`. The tooltip is for sighted readers
  who point at the control; the name is what a screen reader announces, and it is not replaced by the tooltip.
- Keep the tip to the one thing the reader needs to decide. A label that names the action is more useful than a
  description of the whole screen.
- Use the same side for tooltips in the same toolbar, so the reader's eye learns where the label appears.
- Put the full text of a truncated label in the tip, so the reader can read it without opening the record.
- Use `Bottom` in a page header and `Left` or `Right` in a vertical toolbar, so the bubble does not cover the control the
  reader is pointing at.

**Avoid**

- Interactive content in a tip, such as a link or a button. Tooltip content cannot be reached with the keyboard, so the
  action is lost for anyone who does not use a pointer.
- A tooltip as the only explanation of a required field or an error. It disappears on the next press, so the reader may
  never see it; use the field's own helper or error row.
- Tips on every control of a page. A page covered in tooltips reads as noise; add them where the icon or the truncated
  text needs them.
- Relying on a tooltip on touch. Touch users may not see it, so put anything they must read on the page.
- Repeating the button text in the tip. "Copy" with the tip "Copy" adds a delay and no information.

### Common questions

**Why does the tooltip not show on a disabled button?** A disabled control does not open a tooltip from hover or focus
by itself. The tooltip opens only while the pointer is over the disabled control, so it can explain the reason without
the control taking focus.

**Why does the tooltip disappear when I click the button?** A press on the trigger closes the tooltip at once, so it does
not sit over the menu, dialog or panel the press opened.

**Can the tooltip be dismissed with Escape?** The tooltip does not handle Escape itself. It closes when the focus moves
away or the pointer leaves.

**Does a tooltip work on a touch screen?** Tooltips open on hover and keyboard focus, which touch screens do not
provide reliably. Keep any information that a touch user needs on the page.

**Can I show a tooltip on a control that is not focusable?** It opens on pointer hover, and `Tooltip.SetIsOpen` opens it
from code. A control that cannot take focus still needs a name for a screen reader, so set `AutomationProperties.Name`.

## API reference

### Tooltip

A short label on hover or keyboard focus. Attach it to any control with `arc:Tooltip.Tip="Copy link"` (and optionally `arc:Tooltip.Side`). The first tooltip waits 250ms and rises 3px from its trigger; while any tooltip is open, and for 300ms after the last one closes, the next opens at once with a fade only. String content that changes while open crossfades and the bubble springs to the new size. The `Tooltip` instance itself is the bubble shown in the popup.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Tip` | `object?` | `null` | *Attached.* Tooltip content: a string, or any object (bind it when the text comes from the view model). |
| `Side` | `TooltipSide` | `Top` | *Attached.* Side of the trigger the bubble opens on: Top (default), Bottom, Left or Right. |
| `ShowDelay` | `TimeSpan` | `00:00:00.2500000` | *Attached.* Wait before the first tooltip opens after hover or focus; default 250 ms. Open tooltips skip the wait. |
| `IsOpen` | `bool` | `false` | *Attached.* Shows or hides the tooltip on the element at once, without ShowDelay. |

Derives from `ContentControl`: every member of `ContentControl` works as well.

The side of the trigger is set with `TooltipSide`, which has four members.

| Member | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `Top` | The bubble opens above the trigger (the default) |
| `Bottom` | The bubble opens below the trigger |
| `Left` | The bubble opens to the left of the trigger |
| `Right` | The bubble opens to the right of the trigger |

## Accessibility

- While the tooltip is open, its text is written to the trigger's help text.
- A tooltip is not a substitute for a name. An icon-only trigger still needs its own `AutomationProperties.Name`.
- A tooltip opens on hover and on keyboard focus. A Tab focus opens it after the delay, and moving the focus away closes
  it.
- The bubble is not focusable and does not take pointer input, so it never takes focus from the control it describes.
- The bubble contains no interactive elements, so keyboard users can read it without losing focus.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Tab` onto the trigger | Opens the tooltip after `ShowDelay`, or at once while another tooltip is warm |
| `Tab` away from the trigger | Closes the tooltip |

## Motion

- The first tooltip waits 250ms, then rises 3px from its trigger while it scales in from 0.97.
- When the pointer moves to a neighbouring trigger, or the last tooltip closed less than 300ms ago, the next tooltip
  opens at once with a fade only.
- When the text changes while the tooltip is open, the new words rise in with a soft blur and the bubble springs to
  its new size.
- Closing is an instant fade with the bubble shrinking to 0.98.
- Reduced motion removes the movement and keeps a short fade. Off shows or removes the tooltip at once.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| First tooltip opens | Waits for `ShowDelay`, then rises 3px and scales in from 0.97 | Short fade only | Shown at once |
| Next tooltip while warm | Opens at once with a fade only | Short fade only | Shown at once |
| Text changes while open | New words rise in with a soft blur; the bubble springs to its new size | Short fade only | Shown at once |
| Tooltip closes | Instant fade, the bubble shrinks to 0.98 | Short fade | Removed at once |

## Related

- `Popover` for interactive content anchored to a control.
- `HoverCard` for a rich, read-only preview of a person or a link.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `Popover` | The content has a link, a button or a form, and a click opens it |
| `HoverCard` | A read-only preview of a person or a link is wanted on hover |
| `Input` | A message about a field must stay on the page until the field is fixed |
| `Dialog` | The reader must read or confirm something before continuing |

# Alert

> A persistent message that helps people recover or continue.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/alert

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.AlertTonesDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12">
        <arc:Alert Title="Your card expires next month"
                   Content="Update your payment method to keep your plan active." />
        <arc:Alert Tone="Success"
                   Title="Domain verified"
                   Content="Emails from acme.dev will now be delivered." />
        <arc:Alert Tone="Warning"
                   Title="You're close to your storage limit"
                   Content="Free up space or upgrade before uploads pause." />
        <arc:Alert Tone="Danger"
                   Title="Payment failed"
                   Content="We couldn't charge the card ending in 4242." />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

## When to use

`Alert` is a notice that stays on the page until its situation is resolved. It sits in the flow of a page or a form,
next to the content it concerns, and it can change its tone, title and text as the situation changes. It is the
right tool when a message must still be there after the person looks away.

- **Billing and plan notices**: a failed card payment on a billing page, or a plan that renews in seven days. The
  notice explains the consequence and stays until the payment method is updated.
- **Quota and limit warnings**: a workspace that uses 8 of 10 seats, or an export queue that is close to its daily
  limit. The alert sits above the Invite or Export action so the person sees the limit before they hit it.
- **Status of a long-running change**: a domain verification, a sync or a save that moves from "Saving changes" to
  "All changes saved" or "Couldn't save". Keep one `Alert` and change it, so the layout does not jump.
- **Notices that a person can close**: a maintenance window on a dashboard, or a tip in a settings form. After the
  person dismisses it, the content below closes the gap.

## When not to use

- **A confirmation of a finished action**, such as "Changes saved" after a click: use `Toast`, which disappears by
  itself.
- **Queued application results** with actions such as Undo or View, which can arrive together: use `ToastStack`.
- **A decision that must be answered before the person continues**: use `Dialog`.
- **A message about one field**, such as "Enter a full email address": use the `ErrorMessage` row of `Input`, which
  is attached to the field it describes.
- **A site-wide message above every page**: use `AnnouncementBar`, which rotates and can remember a dismissal.
- **A page or list with no content**: use `EmptyState`.

## Usage

Basic usage sets a `Title` and `Content`. The default `Tone` is `Info`.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:Alert Title="Your card expires next month"
               Content="Update your payment method to keep your plan active." />
</UserControl>
```

`Alert` derives from Avalonia's `ContentControl`, so `Content` and `ContentTemplate` work as they do on any content
control. A string `Content` becomes the description line; any other content is shown below the title as it is.
It has no `Size` property: it takes the width its container gives it, so place it in a column that matches the
content it describes.

### Anatomy

1. **Tone icon** (`Tone`): an 18 px glyph with a 2 px stroke, nudged 1 px down so it sits on the first line of the
   title, with 12 px before the text. Its color follows the tone.
2. **Title** (`Title`): 14 px, medium weight, 19.6 px line height, in the default foreground color. It wraps and
   does not truncate.
3. **Description** (`Content` as a string): 12 px in the secondary text color, 4 px below the title, with a 16.8 px
   line height. An empty description takes no space.
4. **Rich content** (`Content` as any other object): shown in the same column with the same 4 px gap. Text in it
   inherits the 12 px size and the secondary color through `TextElement`.
5. **Dismiss button** (`IsDismissible`): a 28 px round ghost button in the top right corner. It is shown only when
   `IsDismissible` is `True` and is pulled into the 16 px padding (5 px above and below, 6 px to the right) so its
   glyph lines up with the title.
6. **Surface**: 16 px padding inside a 1 px border with the control corner radius, on the surface color with the
   resting shadow.

### Tones

`Tone` sets the icon, its color and how the change is announced. Pick the tone by what the person must do next,
not by how serious the event feels.

| Tone | Icon | Use it for | Announced |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Info` (default) | Info | Neutral facts and tips: a plan renewal date, a new feature | Politely |
| `Success` | Check | A problem is fixed: a domain is verified, a payment cleared | Politely |
| `Warning` | Triangle with an exclamation mark | Action is needed soon: a limit is close, a card expires | Politely |
| `Danger` | Circle with a cross | Something failed and the person must act: a payment or a sync failed | Assertively |

```xml
<StackPanel Spacing="12">
    <arc:Alert Tone="Success" Title="Domain verified"
               Content="Emails from acme.dev will now be delivered." />
    <arc:Alert Tone="Warning" Title="You're close to your storage limit"
               Content="Free up space or upgrade before uploads pause." />
    <arc:Alert Tone="Danger" Title="Payment failed"
               Content="We couldn't charge the card ending in 4242." />
</StackPanel>
```

Use `Danger` sparingly: when it appears on every second notice, people stop reading the color. A `Danger` alert is
announced assertively, so a screen reader interrupts the current speech to read it.

### Morph in place

Keep one instance and change its properties when the state changes. The icon swaps, the new text rises in and the
height follows with a spring. Replacing the control instead skips these transitions and makes the page jump.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.AlertMorphInPlaceDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="16">
        <arc:Alert x:Name="Status"
                   Title="Ready to sync"
                   Content="Changes are saved on this device." />
        <WrapPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center" ItemSpacing="12" LineSpacing="12">
            <arc:Button Content="Save" Variant="Secondary" Click="OnSaveClick" />
            <arc:Button Content="Fail" Variant="Secondary" Click="OnFailClick" />
        </WrapPanel>
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class AlertMorphInPlaceDemo : UserControl
{
    public AlertMorphInPlaceDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
    }

    // One alert instance changes tone, title and content, so the icon swaps and the height springs.
    private async void OnSaveClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        Status.Tone = AlertTone.Info;
        Status.Title = "Saving changes";
        Status.Content = "Uploading 3 files to the workspace.";
        await Task.Delay(1400);
        Status.Tone = AlertTone.Success;
        Status.Title = "All changes saved";
        Status.Content = "Everyone in the workspace now sees the latest version, including the comments you left on the draft.";
    }

    private void OnFailClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        Status.Tone = AlertTone.Danger;
        Status.Title = "Couldn't save";
        Status.Content = "Check your connection and try again.";
    }
}
```

```csharp
// One alert instance changes tone, title and content as a save progresses.
Status.Tone = AlertTone.Info;
Status.Title = "Saving changes";
Status.Content = "Uploading 3 files to the workspace.";

await _workspace.SaveAsync(draft);

Status.Tone = AlertTone.Success;
Status.Title = "All changes saved";
Status.Content = "Everyone in the workspace now sees the latest version.";
```

When the failure path needs a message the person can act on, put the next step in `Content` ("Check your connection
and try again.") rather than in a second alert.

### Dismiss

Set `IsDismissible` to show the close button. Pressing it collapses the alert, then raises `Dismissed`. Setting
`IsOpen` back to `True` shows the alert again, and its icon settles from a smaller size to full size.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.AlertDismissDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12">
        <arc:Alert x:Name="Maintenance"
                   Tone="Warning"
                   Title="Scheduled maintenance on Sunday"
                   Content="The dashboard is read-only from 02:00 to 03:00 UTC."
                   IsDismissible="True" />
        <TextBlock Text="Content below closes the gap when the alert collapses."
                   FontSize="14"
                   TextWrapping="Wrap"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
        <WrapPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center" ItemSpacing="12" LineSpacing="12">
            <arc:Button Content="Show again" Variant="Ghost" Click="OnShowAgainClick" />
        </WrapPanel>
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class AlertDismissDemo : UserControl
{
    public AlertDismissDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
    }

    private void OnShowAgainClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) => Maintenance.IsOpen = true;
}
```

```csharp
var notice = new Alert { Tone = AlertTone.Warning, IsDismissible = true, Title = "Scheduled maintenance on Sunday" };
notice.Dismissed += (_, _) => SaveDismissedState();

// Show the alert again later.
notice.IsOpen = true;
```

`Dismiss()` does the same from code: it collapses the alert and raises `Dismissed` once the collapse finishes.
Setting `IsOpen` to `False` collapses the alert too, but it does not raise `Dismissed`, because `Dismissed` reports a
person's choice. Use `IsOpen` to hide an alert for another reason, such as a state change that makes it obsolete.

### Custom content

Any non-text `Content` is shown below the title. Text content gets the detail styling; other content is shown as
it is.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.AlertCustomContentDemo">
    <arc:Alert Title="A new version is available">
        <WrapPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center" ItemSpacing="12" LineSpacing="12">
            <arc:Button Content="Reload" Size="Small" Variant="Secondary" />
        </WrapPanel>
    </arc:Alert>
</UserControl>
```

```xml
<arc:Alert Title="A new version is available">
    <WrapPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center" ItemSpacing="12" LineSpacing="12">
        <arc:Button Content="Reload" Size="Small" Variant="Secondary" />
    </WrapPanel>
</arc:Alert>
```

Keep custom content to one action or a short list. An alert with a form inside it has become a card, and a card
belongs in the layout of its own section. Content that is a plain number or another formatted value is shown as its
text, because `Alert` converts `IFormattable` values with `ToString`.

### Driving it from data

An alert is display-only, but its tone, title and visibility often come from a view model. With
CommunityToolkit.Mvvm, the view model owns the state and the alert shows it. Bind `IsOpen` two-way only when the
dismissal must reach the view model.

```csharp
public record PaymentResult(bool IsSuccess);

public abstract class BillingService
{
    public abstract Task<PaymentResult> RetryAsync(string invoiceId);
}

public partial class BillingViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    private readonly BillingService _billing;

    public BillingViewModel(BillingService billing) => _billing = billing;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private AlertTone _paymentTone = AlertTone.Danger;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private string _paymentTitle = "Payment failed";

    [ObservableProperty]
    private bool _paymentNoticeOpen = true;

    [RelayCommand]
    private async Task RetryPaymentAsync()
    {
        var result = await _billing.RetryAsync("inv_2026_0412");
        PaymentTone = result.IsSuccess ? AlertTone.Success : AlertTone.Danger;
        PaymentTitle = result.IsSuccess ? "Payment received" : "Payment failed";
    }
}
```

```xml
<StackPanel Spacing="12">
    <arc:Alert Tone="{Binding PaymentTone}"
               Title="{Binding PaymentTitle}"
               IsOpen="{Binding PaymentNoticeOpen, Mode=TwoWay}"
               IsDismissible="True"
               Content="Invoice inv_2026_0412 for Acme Analytics is still unpaid." />
    <arc:Button Content="Retry payment" Command="{Binding RetryPaymentCommand}" />
</StackPanel>
```

Give the alert the same tone and title binding as the state it reports, and let the command decide the next state.
A dismissed alert stays hidden until the view model sets `PaymentNoticeOpen` back to `True`.

### Focus and dismissal

An alert takes no focus when it appears, because a notice should not interrupt typing. Its only focus stop is the
dismiss button, which exists only when `IsDismissible` is `True`. Dismissing does not move focus to another control,
so move it yourself in the `Dismissed` handler when the person was working in the alert.

Decide per alert whether dismissal is a choice or a fix. A dismissal the person can make without resolving the
situation (a maintenance tip) can be closable. A problem that the person still has to fix (a failed payment) should
stay open until its state changes, and it should not be closable at all.

### Example: billing page notices

A billing page in a SaaS admin console shows three notices at the top of the plan section. The failed payment is
`Danger` because the workspace loses access on March 3, 2026. The seat warning is `Warning` and explains the next
action, and the receipt is `Success` and closable, because nothing needs to happen. Each title states the situation,
and the description says what the person can do about it.

![A billing section with a failed payment, a seat warning and a receipt notice](https://docs.tkcode.si/shots/Docs/Messages/Alert/images/BillingNotices.webp)

```xml
<StackPanel Width="600" Spacing="12">
    <TextBlock Text="Billing" FontSize="20" FontWeight="Medium"
               Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
    <arc:Alert Tone="Danger"
               Title="Payment failed for Acme Analytics"
               Content="We couldn't charge the card ending in 4242. Update it by March 3, 2026 to keep Pro features."
               IsDismissible="True" />
    <arc:Alert Tone="Warning"
               Title="You're close to your seat limit"
               Content="8 of 10 seats are in use. Remove an inactive member or add seats before you invite more." />
    <arc:Alert Tone="Success"
               Title="Invoice INV-2026-0412 paid"
               Content="A receipt was sent to billing@acme.com."
               IsDismissible="True" />
</StackPanel>
```

### Content guidelines

- **Title**: a short statement of the situation in sentence case, with no final period: "Payment failed for Acme
  Analytics". A title is read first by screen readers, so it must make sense on its own.
- **Description**: one or two sentences with the consequence and the next step: "Update it by March 3, 2026 to keep
  Pro features." Write dates and counts as digits.
- **Action text**: when the alert holds a button, use a verb and an object: "Update payment method", not "Click here".
- **Tone of voice**: plain and calm. Name the problem without blame, and avoid exclamation marks.

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| Error! | Payment failed |
| Something went wrong. | Couldn't save your changes. Check your connection and try again. |
| Your account is in danger!!! | Your plan ends on March 3, 2026. |
| Click here to fix it. | Update your payment method. |

### Best practices

**Do**

- Keep one alert per situation, and change its tone and text when the situation changes. A second alert for the
  same problem doubles the noise and leaves a stale message behind.
- Place an alert next to the content it describes, such as above the invoice table or inside the seat settings.
  Its meaning depends on the context around it.
- Use `Danger` only for a failure the person must act on. A `Danger` tone on a routine event trains people to ignore
  the color.
- Keep the alert open until the situation is resolved, unless the person has a real choice to make about it.

**Avoid**

- Using an alert for a finished action. A short confirmation belongs in `Toast`, which does not stay on the page.
- Making a payment or a security notice dismissible. The person can close it without fixing the problem.
- Replacing the control on every state change. The new instance has no morph and the page jumps.
- Stacking more than three alerts in one place. The page becomes a list of warnings and the important one is lost.

### Common questions

**Does `Dismissed` fire when I set `IsOpen` to `False`?** No. `Dismissed` is raised only after `Dismiss()` or the
dismiss button collapses the alert, so it reports a choice the person made. Hiding the alert from code only collapses
it.

**Does a dismissal survive a restart?** No. `Alert` keeps no state. To remember a dismissal, save it in your own
settings when `Dismissed` is raised, then set `IsOpen` to `False` at startup. `AnnouncementBar` offers a remembered
dismissal with `DismissalKey` if the notice is site-wide.

**Why is there no gap between the title and the text?** An empty or null `Content` removes the description row
completely, including its 4 px gap. Set `Content` only when it has text.

**Does the alert hide itself after a while?** No. `Alert` has no timer and no duration. A message that should
disappear by itself belongs in `Toast`. Always set `Title`, because it is the accessible name of the whole alert.

**How do I put a button in the alert?** Set `Content` to a panel that holds the button, as in the custom content
example. The button keeps its own size and command, and the alert provides the padding and the tone.

## API reference

### Alert

Arc alert: a persistent message that helps people recover or continue. Keep one instance and change `Tone`, `Title` and the content to morph it between states: the icon pops into the new tone, new text rises out of a soft blur and the height springs to fit. Hiding it (`IsOpen`) collapses the height while it fades, so the content below closes the gap. A string `Content` is the description line; any other content is shown as is.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Title` | `string?` | `null` | The headline. A new title rises in from below while the old one lifts away. |
| `Tone` | `AlertTone` | `Info` | Tone (default `Info`). |
| `IsOpen` | `bool` | `true` | Whether the alert is shown. Hiding collapses its height and fades it out. Two-way. |
| `IsDismissible` | `bool` | `false` | Shows the dismiss button. Dismissing collapses the alert, then raises `Dismissed`. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Dismissed` | `RoutedEventArgs` | Raised after a dismissed alert finished collapsing. |

Pseudo-classes: `:dismissible`, `:rich-content`

Derives from `ContentControl`: every member of `ContentControl` works as well.

Companion type `AlertTone`:

| Member | Icon | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `Info` | Info | Neutral information (accent color). This is the default. |
| `Success` | Check | Something worked. |
| `Warning` | Triangle with an exclamation mark | Attention needed soon. |
| `Danger` | Circle with a cross | Something failed. Announced assertively. |

## Accessibility

- `Title` names the alert and `Content` is read as its help text. A changed title is announced again.
- `Danger` alerts are announced assertively; the other tones are announced politely. A rich `Content` has no help
  text, so put the key sentence in the title or in a text block in the content.
- The close button is named `Dismiss: {Title}`, so the user hears which alert it closes.
- The tone icon is not exposed to assistive technology. The tone is conveyed by the title and content, so the title
  must say what happened even without the color.
- The close button is a regular button: Tab reaches it and Enter or Space activates it.
- Showing an alert takes no focus, so it never interrupts typing.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` | Moves to or from the dismiss button, when `IsDismissible` is `True` |
| `Enter` / `Space` | Dismisses the alert when the dismiss button has focus |

## Motion

- Showing and hiding the alert opens and closes its height on a smooth spring, and the content below closes up.
- A tone change swaps the icon with a short scale and blur. Changed text rises in and unblurs.
- Reduced motion removes the height animation and the movement. Text and icon only fade, and showing or hiding is
  immediate.
- Off motion jumps straight to the end state.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| Alert shown (`IsOpen` set to `True`) | Height springs open, the text fades in and the icon settles from a smaller size | Shown at full height, the text and icon fade in | Immediate |
| Alert dismissed or hidden | Height collapses on a smooth spring while the alert fades out, and the content below moves up | Immediate | Immediate |
| Tone changes | The icon swaps with a scale and a short blur | The icon fades | Immediate |
| Title or content changes | The new text rises in from a soft blur and the height springs to fit | The text fades | Immediate |

## Related

- `Toast` for a brief confirmation of an action that has finished.
- `ToastStack` for application notifications that are queued, updated and stacked.
- `AnnouncementBar` for a rotating banner across the top of a site.
- `EmptyState` when there is no content to show at all.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `Toast` | A finished action needs a short confirmation that closes by itself |
| `ToastStack` | Several results or undo actions arrive from the app and must stack |
| `AnnouncementBar` | A site-wide message sits above every page and rotates |
| `Dialog` | The person must answer before the page continues |
| `Input` | The message belongs to one field, in its description or error row |
| `EmptyState` | A list or page has no content to show |

# Toast

> Brief confirmation for a completed background action.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/toast

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ToastLocalToastDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12">
        <Border Height="200"
                Padding="20"
                CornerRadius="18"
                BorderThickness="1"
                ClipToBounds="True"
                Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Background}"
                BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource BorderSubtle}">
            <arc:Toast x:Name="Saved"
                       Title="Changes saved"
                       Description="Synced to all your devices."
                       VerticalAlignment="Bottom"
                       Closed="OnClosed" />
        </Border>
        <WrapPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center" ItemSpacing="12" LineSpacing="12">
            <arc:Button Content="Save changes" Variant="Primary" Click="OnSaveClick" />
            <arc:Button Content="Change text" Variant="Secondary" Click="OnChangeTextClick" />
        </WrapPanel>
        <TextBlock x:Name="Log"
                   Text="Swipe the toast left or right, or wait 4.5s."
                   FontSize="12"
                   TextWrapping="Wrap"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class ToastLocalToastDemo : UserControl
{
    public ToastLocalToastDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
    }

    private void OnSaveClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        Saved.Title = "Changes saved";
        Saved.Description = "Synced to all your devices.";
        Saved.IsOpen = true;
    }

    // The text changes while the toast is open: the new text rises in and the height follows.
    private void OnChangeTextClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        Saved.IsOpen = true;
        Saved.Title = Saved.Title == "Changes saved" ? "Draft published" : "Changes saved";
        Saved.Description = Saved.Description is null ? "Readers will see it in a few seconds, and subscribers get an email." : null;
    }

    private void OnClosed(object? sender, ToastClosedEventArgs e) => Log.Text = $"Closed: {e.Reason}";
}
```

## When to use

`Toast` is a single, page-owned confirmation: a short message that rises from its edge, stays for a few seconds and
goes away. It is the right tool when the page itself knows that something finished, for example after a form saved,
and the person is still looking at the same screen. The page places the toast, sets its text and decides when it is
open, so the message always matches the view it appears on.

- **Save confirmations in settings and profile pages**: "Changes saved" under a billing address form, after the
  request succeeds. The person stays on the page, so a short, self-closing message is enough.
- **Copy and export feedback**: "API key copied" beside a key in a developer console, or "Invoice link copied" on an
  invoice detail page. The toast confirms the action without taking focus from the field the person is working in.
- **Background sync results on one screen**: "Synced to all your devices" after a draft saves in a CRM note editor.
  The page sets `IsOpen` when the save completes and nothing else needs to know about it.
- **Bulk actions on a list page**: a "3 contacts archived" message under a table that the person can swipe away when
  it covers the rows they need, with no queue of earlier messages to clear.

## When not to use

- **Several messages that can be open at once, or results from anywhere in the app**: use `ToastStack`, which queues,
  types, updates and stacks notifications and can be called from any control through `Toast.Show`.
- **A message that stays until someone acts on it**, such as a payment failure or a quota warning: use `Alert` inside
  the page, where it remains until it is resolved.
- **A message that must be answered before the person continues**: use `Dialog`, which takes focus and blocks the page
  until the person chooses an answer.
- **A rotating banner across the top of a site**, for example a maintenance notice with a countdown: use
  `AnnouncementBar`.

## Usage

A `Toast` shows its `Title` and an optional `Description`. It is visible while `IsOpen` is `True`, and it closes
after `Duration` (4.5 seconds by default).

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:Toast Title="Changes saved"
               Description="Synced to all your devices."
               VerticalAlignment="Bottom" />
</UserControl>
```

`Toast` derives from Avalonia's `TemplatedControl`, so its look lives in a `ControlTheme` and can be restyled with
the usual Avalonia mechanisms. It adds the message and motion behavior: the entrance and exit, the timer, the swipe
gesture and the `Closed` event. It does not queue. Each `Toast` in the page is independent, so place it where its
message belongs and use `ToastStack` when several messages can be open together.

### Anatomy

1. **Surface** (`PART_Root` and `PART_Surface`): the card. Its width is the available width up to `MaxToastWidth`
   (416 px, 26rem), and a narrower container shrinks it. It has a 1 px border in the border color, the panel corner
   radius, the floating shadow and a surface color that is 6% mixed toward the page background. Padding is 16 px on
   the left and 14 px on the other three sides.
2. **Icon disc** (`PART_Icon`): a 30 px circle with a 12 px gap after it. Its fill is the success color at 10% over
   the surface, with a 1 px ring in the success color at 24% over the border. The disc is the same for every toast.
3. **Check mark** (`PART_Check`): a 16 px check in the success color, stroked at 2.25. It draws itself after the
   entrance begins. The check is a decoration and is not exposed to assistive technology.
4. **Title** (`PART_Title`): `Title`, 14 px, medium weight, on one line. A long title ends with an ellipsis. Its line
   box is 19.6 px and its top padding centers the first line on the 30 px disc.
5. **Description** (`PART_Description`): `Description`, 14 px in the secondary text color, wrapped. It sits 2 px below
   the title and adds no gap when it is empty.
6. **Close button** (`PART_Close`): a 32 px round ghost button with a 2 px X glyph. It is muted at rest and takes the
   foreground color on hover. Its accessible name is "Dismiss notification".

### Showing and hiding

Set `IsOpen` to `True` to show the toast again after it closed. Closing, swiping and timing out set `IsOpen` to
`False`, so the property always reflects what is on screen. Changing `Title` or `Description` while the toast is open
rises the new text in and the height follows; the timer keeps running. Setting `IsOpen` to `True` on a toast that is
already open has no effect.

```csharp
toast.Title = "Draft published";
toast.Description = "Readers will see it in a few seconds.";
toast.IsOpen = true;
```

Keep one toast per message location. When the same message needs to appear again, update its text and open it,
rather than creating a new `Toast` each time.

### Duration

`Duration` sets the time before the toast closes itself. The default is 4.5 seconds. A value of zero or less keeps the
toast open until the person closes it or the page sets `IsOpen` to `False`. The timer starts when the toast opens and
restarts when `Duration` changes while the toast is open. It does not pause on hover, so the copy has to be read in
the time given.

```xml
<arc:Toast Title="Upload complete" Duration="0:0:8" />
<arc:Toast Title="Still syncing" Duration="0" />
```

Choose the duration from the length of the copy. A one-line confirmation suits the default. A message with a
description needs more time to read, so give it a longer `Duration`, such as 8 seconds. Use zero only when the page
closes the toast itself, and make sure the page always sets `IsOpen` to `False` when the work ends.

### Closed event

`Closed` is raised when the toast starts closing for one of three reasons. `ToastCloseReason` tells them apart:
`Dismissed` for the close button or `Close()`, `Swiped` for a swipe past the distance or speed threshold, and
`TimedOut` when `Duration` elapsed.

```csharp
toast.Closed += (_, e) =>
{
    if (e.Reason == ToastCloseReason.TimedOut)
    {
        log.Text = "The message closed on its own.";
    }
};
```

`Closed` is raised only for closes that the toast starts. Setting `IsOpen` to `False` from code closes the toast
without raising it, because the page already knows the state it set. Use `Close()` when the page wants the same
result as the close button, including the event.

### App-wide toasts

`Toast.Show` sends a toast from any control in the window to the window's `ToastStack`, which is the same service
`ToastStack` offers. Use it when the message comes from code that does not own a `Toast` control, such as a shared
export command, a clipboard helper or a background job. `ToastKind` selects the icon and color: `Success`, `Info`,
`Warning`, `Error` or `Loading`. `Toast.Show` returns an id, and `Toast.Update` and `Toast.Dismiss` accept that id.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ToastFromAnywhereDemo">
    <WrapPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center" ItemSpacing="12" LineSpacing="12">
        <arc:Button Content="Success" Variant="Secondary" Click="OnSuccessClick" />
        <arc:Button Content="Info" Variant="Secondary" Click="OnInfoClick" />
        <arc:Button Content="Error" Variant="Secondary" Click="OnErrorClick" />
    </WrapPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class ToastFromAnywhereDemo : UserControl
{
    public ToastFromAnywhereDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
    }

    // Any control in the window can send a toast to the window's ToastStack.
    private void OnSuccessClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
        => Toast.Show(this, "Invite sent", ToastKind.Success, "Maya will get an email shortly.");

    private void OnInfoClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) => Toast.Show(this, "New comment", ToastKind.Info);

    private void OnErrorClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
        => Toast.Show(this, "Upload failed", ToastKind.Error, "The file is larger than 25 MB.");
}
```

```csharp
var id = Toast.Show(this, "Export started", ToastKind.Loading, "Acme Analytics is building the CSV.");

// Later, when the export finishes:
Toast.Update(this, id, new ToastUpdate
{
    Kind = ToastKind.Success,
    Title = "Export ready",
    Description = "Download it from the Exports page."
});
```

The `owner` argument is any `Visual` attached to a window. If the window has no `ToastStack`, the first call creates
one on the window's overlay layer. An owner that is not attached yet raises an `InvalidOperationException`, so call
these methods after the view is loaded. The app-wide API is covered on the `ToastStack` page.

### Binding to a view model

`IsOpen` is two-way by default, so a binding needs no `Mode`. The title and description are one-way: the view model
owns the text and the toast displays it. The view model below is written in CommunityToolkit.Mvvm style.

```csharp
public partial class ProfileViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    private readonly IProfileService _profiles;

    public ProfileViewModel(IProfileService profiles) => _profiles = profiles;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private bool _isSavedToastOpen;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private string _savedToastTitle = "Changes saved";

    [ObservableProperty]
    private string? _savedToastDescription;

    [RelayCommand]
    private async Task SaveAsync()
    {
        await _profiles.SaveAsync(Draft);
        SavedToastTitle = "Changes saved";
        SavedToastDescription = "Synced to all your devices.";
        IsSavedToastOpen = true;
    }
}
```

```xml
<Grid RowDefinitions="*,Auto">
    <!-- Form content goes here. -->
    <arc:Toast Grid.Row="1"
               Title="{Binding SavedToastTitle}"
               Description="{Binding SavedToastDescription}"
               IsOpen="{Binding IsSavedToastOpen}"
               HorizontalAlignment="Right"
               VerticalAlignment="Bottom"
               Margin="0,0,0,8" />
</Grid>
```

`IsOpen` is the only two-way property, so the view model sees every close, whatever its reason. Subscribe to `Closed`
in code behind when the view must react to the reason. For each save, set the title and description first and then
`IsSavedToastOpen` to `True`: a closed toast opens with the new text, and an open one updates its text in place.

### Example: profile save in a CRM

A contact record in a CRM has a save button in its footer. When the save succeeds, a confirmation rises at the
bottom-left of the form, names what happened and says where it went. The toast does not block the next edit and
closes on its own after the default 4.5 seconds, so the person can keep working. A failed save uses `Alert` instead,
because a failure must stay visible until the person fixes the problem.

```xml
<Grid Width="640" Height="220">
    <Border Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource SurfaceRaised}"
            BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Border}"
            BorderThickness="1"
            CornerRadius="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource RadiusPanel}" />
    <arc:Toast Title="Changes saved"
               Description="Northwind Logistics is updated in all your views."
               HorizontalAlignment="Left"
               VerticalAlignment="Bottom"
               Margin="24" />
</Grid>
```

### Content guidelines

- **Title**: one short past-tense statement of what finished: "Changes saved", "Invoice sent". It stays on one line,
  so keep it under about 30 characters in English.
- **Description**: one sentence that says where the result is or what happens next: "Synced to all your devices.",
  "Readers will see it in a few seconds." Leave it out when the title says everything.
- **No action words**: a toast has no button but its close button, so do not ask the person to do something in the
  copy. If a next step matters, put it in the page or use `Alert`.
- **Sentence case, no exclamation marks**: a confirmation states a fact; it does not celebrate.

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| Success! Your changes have been saved successfully!!! | Changes saved |
| Saved. Click here to view. | Changes saved. Find it under Activity. |
| Error saving the form | Couldn't save. Try again. |
| The item was successfully deleted from your account | Contact deleted |

### Best practices

**Do**

- Use `Toast` for one confirmation the page controls, and keep the text in the view model so the state of the page
  and the message agree.
- Keep the title short enough to fit one line. A long title ends with an ellipsis, which hides the result.
- Place the toast where the person is looking, usually the bottom of the form or the page, so the confirmation sits
  near the action that caused it.
- Bind `IsOpen` to the view model, so the open state lives with the data the page already holds rather than only in
  the view.

**Avoid**

- Messages that must be read, such as a failed payment or a permission problem. The timer does not pause, so these
  belong in `Alert` or `Dialog`, which stay until resolved.
- Using `Toast` for several notifications in a row. Each `Toast` is independent and does not queue, so every message
  needs its own place on the page and none of them knows about the others; use `ToastStack` instead.
- A zero duration without a page-side close. A toast that never times out and is never closed by the page stays on
  screen for the rest of the session.
- Motion as the only signal. The text carries the result; the rise and the check mark only add emphasis.

### Common questions

**Why did my toast close before the person could read it?** The default duration is 4.5 seconds and the timer does
not pause while the pointer is over the toast. Set a longer `Duration` for long copy, or use `Alert` when the message
must stay until it is resolved.

**How do I know why the toast closed?** Subscribe to `Closed` and read `e.Reason`. `Dismissed` means the close button
or `Close()`, `Swiped` means a swipe, and `TimedOut` means the duration elapsed. Setting `IsOpen` to `False` from code
does not raise the event.

**How do I show the same message again?** Set `IsOpen` to `True` after the toast has closed. Set the new `Title` or
`Description` first, so the toast opens with the new text. An open toast keeps its current timer when its text
changes, and setting `IsOpen` to `True` on an open toast does nothing.

**Can a view model show a toast without a reference to the view?** Yes. Pass a `Visual` of the window, such as the
view itself, to `Toast.Show` from the code that receives it, or use `ToastHost.GetService` to get the window's
`IToastService` once and hand that to the view model.

**Does the toast take focus?** No. A toast is announced politely and does not move focus. Keyboard focus stays where
the person left it, which is usually the button that started the work.

## API reference

### Toast

Arc toast: a brief confirmation for a completed background action (one locally controlled success message such as "Changes saved"). It rises from its edge on the morph spring while its check mark draws itself, closes after `Duration` (the timer does not pause, so keep the copy short), and can be swiped away in either direction with velocity. Text changes rise in place while the height springs to fit. For app-wide notifications (types, actions, updates, stacking) call `Show` from anywhere: it goes to the window's `ToastStack` (see `ToastHost`).

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Title` | `string?` | `null` | The message. A new title rises in while the old one lifts away. |
| `Description` | `string?` | `null` | Optional second line. |
| `IsOpen` | `bool` | `true` | Whether the toast is shown (default true). Closing, swiping or timing out sets it to false. Two-way. |
| `Duration` | `TimeSpan` | `00:00:04.5000000` | Time before the toast closes itself (default 4.5s); zero or less keeps it until closed. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Closed` | `ToastClosedEventArgs` | Raised when the toast starts closing. |

Pseudo-classes: `:dragging`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

Companion type. `ToastCloseReason` is the reason in `ToastClosedEventArgs.Reason`:

| Member | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `Dismissed` | The close button or `Close()` closed the toast |
| `Swiped` | A swipe passed the distance (80 px) or speed (480 px/s) threshold |
| `TimedOut` | `Duration` elapsed |

## Accessibility

- `Title` is the accessible name of the toast and `Description` is its help text, so a screen reader reads both when
  the toast appears.
- The toast is a polite live region: it is announced after the current speech and does not interrupt it.
- The close button is named "Dismiss notification". Tab reaches it and Enter or Space closes the toast.
- The check mark is decoration and is not exposed to assistive technology.
- The toast does not take focus, so it never moves the person away from the field or button they were using.
- The timer does not pause on hover or focus. Keep the copy short, and use `Alert` for a message the person may need
  more time to read.
- A swipe is a pointer and touch gesture. The close button gives the same result from the keyboard.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` | Move focus to or from the close button; the toast has no other focusable control |
| `Enter` or `Space` | Press the close button: the toast closes with the reason `Dismissed` |

A pointer drag is the only way to swipe. A press that starts on the close button does not start a drag.

## Motion

- The toast rises 16 px from below at 96% scale on a spring, and its check mark draws itself 0.12 seconds later.
- Closing sinks the toast 8 px, shrinks it to 97% and fades it out. A closed toast takes no space.
- Changed text rises in and the height springs to fit the new copy.
- A swipe follows the pointer and, when released past the threshold, carries on with the release velocity while it
  fades. A short swipe springs back.
- Reduced motion fades the toast in and out and turns swiping off. Off motion shows and hides it at once.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| The toast opens | Rises 16 px at 96% scale on the morph spring and fades in; the check draws after 0.12 seconds | Fades in at its final position, with the check already drawn | Shown at once |
| The toast closes (button, timer or `Close()`) | Sinks 8 px, shrinks to 97% and fades out over the exit duration | Fades out with the instant preset | Removed at once |
| Swipe away | Follows the pointer, then is thrown with the release velocity and fades out | Not available: swiping is off | Not available: swiping is off |
| Title or description changes | The old text lifts away, the new text rises in and the height springs to fit | Instant fade | Immediate |

## Related

- `ToastStack` for queued, typed and updatable notifications that can be raised from anywhere in the app.
- `Alert` for a message that stays on the page until it is resolved.
- `Dialog` for a message that must be answered before the person continues.
- `AnnouncementBar` for a rotating banner with a countdown.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `ToastStack` | Several results can be open at once, or the message comes from code outside the page |
| `Alert` | The message stays on the page until the person or the data resolves it |
| `Dialog` | The person must choose an answer before the page continues |
| `AnnouncementBar` | A site-wide notice rotates through messages, or needs a countdown |
| `Toast` + `IsOpen` | The page owns one short confirmation and its text, and nothing else needs to queue |
