# Toast stack

> Stack short results at the edge until you reach for them.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/toast-stack

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ToastStackStackDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12">
        <Border Height="380"
                CornerRadius="26"
                BorderThickness="1"
                ClipToBounds="True"
                Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Background}"
                BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource BorderSubtle}">
            <Grid>
                <TextBlock Text="Hover or focus the stack to fan it out. Alt+T jumps into it; Escape closes the focused toast."
                           Margin="20"
                           TextWrapping="Wrap" />
                <arc:ToastStack x:Name="Stack" IsContained="True" />
            </Grid>
        </Border>
        <WrapPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center" ItemSpacing="12" LineSpacing="12">
            <arc:Button Content="Success" Size="Small" Variant="Secondary" Click="OnSuccessClick" />
            <arc:Button Content="Info" Size="Small" Variant="Secondary" Click="OnInfoClick" />
            <arc:Button Content="Warning" Size="Small" Variant="Secondary" Click="OnWarningClick" />
            <arc:Button Content="Error" Size="Small" Variant="Secondary" Click="OnErrorClick" />
        </WrapPanel>
        <WrapPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center" ItemSpacing="12" LineSpacing="12">
            <arc:Button Content="Loading → success" Size="Small" Variant="Secondary" Click="OnLoadingClick" />
            <arc:Button Content="Undo" Size="Small" Variant="Secondary" Click="OnUndoClick" />
            <arc:Button Content="Dismiss all" Size="Small" Variant="Secondary" Click="OnDismissAllClick" />
        </WrapPanel>
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class ToastStackStackDemo : UserControl
{
    private int _version;

    public ToastStackStackDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
    }

    private void OnSuccessClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
        => Stack.Show(new ToastOptions { Kind = ToastKind.Success, Title = "Changes saved", Description = $"Version {++_version} is live." });

    private void OnInfoClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
        => Stack.Show(new ToastOptions { Kind = ToastKind.Info, Title = "Maya joined the workspace" });

    private void OnWarningClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
        => Stack.Show(new ToastOptions { Kind = ToastKind.Warning, Title = "Storage almost full", Description = "92% of 10 GB used." });

    private void OnErrorClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
        => Stack.Show(new ToastOptions { Kind = ToastKind.Error, Title = "Couldn't send invite", Description = "Check the address and try again." });

    // A loading toast waits for an update, which morphs it into its result.
    private async void OnLoadingClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        var id = Stack.Show(new ToastOptions { Kind = ToastKind.Loading, Title = "Uploading report.pdf" });
        await Task.Delay(1800);
        Stack.Update(id, new ToastUpdate { Kind = ToastKind.Success, Title = "Report uploaded", Description = "Shared with 4 people." });
    }

    // Undo updates the toast into its result instead of closing it.
    private void OnUndoClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        Stack.Show(new ToastOptions
        {
            Title = "Project archived",
            Action = new ToastAction("Undo", id => Stack.Update(id, new ToastUpdate
            {
                Kind = ToastKind.Success,
                Title = "Project restored",
                RemoveAction = true
            }))
        });
    }

    private void OnDismissAllClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) => Stack.Dismiss();
}
```

## When to use

`ToastStack` holds the short results of work that people started and do not need to wait for: an export that
finished, an invite that was sent, a file that failed to upload. It sits at the edge of the window, over the page, and
keeps the newest result in front while older ones tuck behind it. Any control in the window can add to it, so a
background job, a save handler or a command palette can report what it did without knowing about the page layout.

- **Background job results in an admin console**: "Export ready" after a billing export finishes, or "Import failed"
  with the row count, while the operator keeps working in the table.
- **Confirmations with an undo window**: "Project archived" with an Undo button in a project list, where the action
  can be reversed for a few seconds and the toast turns into "Project restored" when it is.
- **Loading that becomes its result**: "Uploading report.pdf" in a loading state that updates in place to "Report
  uploaded" or to an error with the reason, instead of two separate messages.
- **Typed notifications from several sources**: warnings about storage or quota, success messages from a checkout
  flow and errors from a sync, all in one place with one reading order and one dismissal gesture.

## When not to use

- **One confirmation that the page controls with its own state**: use `Toast`, which has no queue and is set with
  `IsOpen`. It is simpler when only one message exists.
- **A message that stays on the page until it is resolved**, such as a plan that is past its limit or a failed
  payment: use `Alert`, because a stack hides older messages behind the front one and a timer closes the rest.
- **A site-wide banner that rotates messages**, such as a maintenance notice or a promotion: use `AnnouncementBar`.
- **A message the person must answer before continuing**, such as a delete confirmation or a permission request: use
  `Dialog`, which takes focus and blocks the page until a choice is made.

## Usage

Place a `ToastStack` over the content, for example as the last child of the window's root panel. Call
`Toast.Show` from any control in the window to add a toast. If the window has no `ToastStack`, `ToastHost` creates one
on the overlay layer.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <Grid>
        <!-- Page content goes here. -->
        <arc:ToastStack Label="Notifications" />
    </Grid>
</UserControl>
```

`ToastStack` derives from Avalonia's `TemplatedControl` and implements `IToastService`, the interface of the app-wide
API: `Show`, `Update`, `Dismiss` and `Count`. Code that holds the stack can call those members directly. Code that
only knows the window uses `Toast.Show`, `Toast.Update` and `Toast.Dismiss`, or `ToastHost.GetService`, which returns the
same interface for the window's stack. A window has one active stack: a placed `ToastStack` wins over one that
`ToastHost` created.

### Anatomy

1. **Region** (the stack itself): a region landmark named by `Label`, "Notifications" by default. When
   `IsHotkeyEnabled` is on, the name ends with "(Alt+T)" so a screen reader user learns the shortcut.
2. **List** (`PART_List`): the area that holds the cards. Only the list rectangle takes pointer input, so the
   page under the rest of the stack stays clickable. The list is 360 px wide (22.5rem) or the window width minus 32 px,
   whichever is smaller.
3. **Front card**: the newest toast, drawn with the floating shadow (and the same shadow whenever the stack is expanded).
4. **Tucked cards**: older toasts behind the front card. Each step back shows 14 px of the card in front, shrinks by
   5%, uses the muted surface color and hides its content. `VisibleToasts` (3 by default) sets how many show; the rest
   wait behind.
5. **Icon slot** (`PART_Icon`): an 18 by 20 px slot with an 18 px Lucide glyph at 1.75 stroke, followed by a 12 px gap.
   The color follows the kind: success, accent, warning or danger. A loading toast shows a 15 px spinner instead.
6. **Copy** (`PART_Title` and `PART_Description`): the title in 14 px medium weight and the description in the secondary
   text color, both wrapped at a 20 px line height. The description sits 2 px below the title.
7. **Action button** (`PART_Action`): a 28 px pill with 12 px side padding, Secondary variant at small size. It sits to
   the right of the copy, or under the copy in a card narrower than 336 px.
8. **Close button** (`PART_Close`): a 28 px round ghost button with a 16 px X glyph. Its accessible name is "Dismiss
   notification".

Card content is padded 16 px on the left and 12 px on the other sides. The stack sits 24 px from the window edge
(16 px when `IsContained` is on) and is centered at the bottom edge in windows narrower than 480 px.

### Showing a toast

`Show` takes a `ToastOptions` and returns the toast's id. `Kind` selects the icon, color and spoken prefix, and
`Title` is required. `Toast.Show` takes the same values as arguments and sends them to the stack of the window that
owns the `owner` visual.

```csharp
stack.Show(new ToastOptions
{
    Kind = ToastKind.Warning,
    Title = "Storage almost full",
    Description = "92% of 10 GB used."
});

Toast.Show(button, "Invite sent", ToastKind.Success, "Maya will get an email shortly.");
```

Each toast is announced with its kind and copy, and the stack keeps the newest toast in front. `Count` reports how
many toasts are queued, both the ones on screen and the ones waiting behind them, and `ToastsChanged` is raised
whenever a toast is shown, updated or dismissed. Use that event to update a counter or a badge in the header.

### Kinds and lifetimes

`ToastKind` sets the icon and color, and the default lifetime. The default lifetime of the stack is 5 seconds.

| Kind | Icon | Default lifetime | Spoken prefix |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Success` | Circle check in the success color | `Duration` (5 seconds) | "Success:" |
| `Info` | Info glyph in the accent color | `Duration` (5 seconds) | "Info:" |
| `Warning` | Triangle alert in the warning color | 1.6 times `Duration` (8 seconds) | "Warning:" |
| `Error` | Circle X in the danger color | 1.6 times `Duration` (8 seconds) | "Error:" (announced assertively) |
| `Loading` | A turning ring | None: it waits for an update | "In progress:" |

Warnings and errors stay longer because a person may need to read and act on them. A loading toast has no timer, so
it stays until the work updates it or the stack dismisses it. Set `ToastOptions.Duration` or `ToastUpdate.Duration` to
override the default for one toast. `Timeout.InfiniteTimeSpan` keeps a toast until it is closed, and zero or less also
keeps it open.

### Loading and update

Pass an id in `ToastOptions` and call `Update` with the same id to change the toast in place. `Show` with an id that
is already on the stack updates that toast instead of adding one. Use `Duration` set to `Timeout.InfiniteTimeSpan` to
keep a toast until it is updated or dismissed. The toast icon, text and height morph to the new state, and the timer
restarts with the new lifetime.

```csharp
var id = stack.Show(new ToastOptions
{
    Kind = ToastKind.Loading,
    Title = "Uploading report.pdf",
    Duration = Timeout.InfiniteTimeSpan
});

await UploadAsync();

stack.Update(id, new ToastUpdate
{
    Kind = ToastKind.Success,
    Title = "Report uploaded",
    Description = "Shared with 4 people."
});
```

`ToastUpdate` changes only the members it sets. A null `Kind`, `Title`, `Description` or `Action` keeps the current
value. A null `Duration` restarts the toast with the default lifetime for its kind. Use `RemoveDescription` or
`RemoveAction` to take the description or the action away.
An update to an id that is no longer on the stack does nothing, so a late result for a dismissed toast is safe to
send.

### Actions

`ToastAction` adds a button to a toast. The button takes the label and a callback that receives the toast id. After
the callback runs, the toast closes unless the callback updated it, so a plain action such as "View" needs no extra
code. An Undo can update the toast into its result and remove the button with `RemoveAction`.

```csharp
stack.Show(new ToastOptions
{
    Title = "Project archived",
    Action = new ToastAction("Undo", id => stack.Update(id, new ToastUpdate
    {
        Kind = ToastKind.Success,
        Title = "Project restored",
        RemoveAction = true
    }))
});
```

The callback decides what the toast does next. If it neither updates nor dismisses the toast, the stack dismisses it
after the callback returns. The callback runs on the UI thread, so start long work from it rather than doing it inside.
An action that updates its toast and removes its button leaves a toast with only a close button; keyboard focus moves
to that button so the person can keep going with the keyboard.

### Position and limits

`Position` moves the stack to the bottom left, center or right edge. The default is `BottomRight`. A window narrower
than 480 px always centers the stack, whatever the position. `VisibleToasts` sets how many toasts show at once, and
`Limit` drops the oldest toasts beyond a count. `Limit` never goes below one.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ToastStackPositionDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12">
        <Border Height="200"
                CornerRadius="26"
                BorderThickness="1"
                ClipToBounds="True"
                Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Background}"
                BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource BorderSubtle}">
            <arc:ToastStack x:Name="Stack" IsContained="True" />
        </Border>
        <WrapPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center" ItemSpacing="12" LineSpacing="12">
            <arc:Button Content="Bottom left" Size="Small" Variant="Secondary" Click="OnBottomLeftClick" />
            <arc:Button Content="Bottom center" Size="Small" Variant="Secondary" Click="OnBottomCenterClick" />
            <arc:Button Content="Bottom right" Size="Small" Variant="Secondary" Click="OnBottomRightClick" />
        </WrapPanel>
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class ToastStackPositionDemo : UserControl
{
    public ToastStackPositionDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
    }

    private void OnBottomLeftClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) => MoveTo(ToastStackPosition.BottomLeft, "Bottom left");

    private void OnBottomCenterClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) => MoveTo(ToastStackPosition.BottomCenter, "Bottom center");

    private void OnBottomRightClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) => MoveTo(ToastStackPosition.BottomRight, "Bottom right");

    // The stack is empty until a toast arrives, so each move also shows one to see where the stack hangs.
    private void MoveTo(ToastStackPosition position, string label)
    {
        Stack.Position = position;
        Stack.Show(new ToastOptions { Kind = ToastKind.Info, Title = label });
    }
}
```

```xml
<arc:ToastStack Position="BottomCenter" VisibleToasts="3" Limit="12" />
```

`IsContained` pins the stack 16 px inside its own bounds instead of 24 px from the window edge. Turn it on for a
preview, a panel or any stack that lives inside a smaller area of the window rather than over the whole window.

### Driving it from code

A `ToastStack` is a service rather than a control with a value to bind, so a view model receives the interface, not
the control. Get the window's service from the view once, and pass it on:

```csharp
public partial class ExportViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    private readonly IToastService _toasts;

    public ExportViewModel(IToastService toasts) => _toasts = toasts;

    [RelayCommand]
    private async Task ExportAsync()
    {
        var id = _toasts.Show(new ToastOptions
        {
            Kind = ToastKind.Loading,
            Title = "Exporting invoices",
            Duration = Timeout.InfiniteTimeSpan
        });

        var result = await _exports.CreateCsvAsync(Range);
        _toasts.Update(id, result.IsSuccess
            ? new ToastUpdate { Kind = ToastKind.Success, Title = "Export ready", Description = result.FileName }
            : new ToastUpdate { Kind = ToastKind.Error, Title = "Export failed", Description = result.Error });
    }
}
```

```csharp
// In the view's code behind, once the view is attached to its window:
var toasts = ToastHost.GetService(this);
DataContext = new ExportViewModel(toasts);
```

The view model and the export service are the application's own. The stack does not need a `ToastStack` in the view:
`ToastHost` creates one on the window's overlay layer on the first call. Place a `ToastStack` yourself when the
position, limits or `IsContained` must differ from the defaults.

### Example: invoice export in a billing console

A billing console lets a finance operator export a month of invoices as a CSV. The export takes a few seconds and
the operator should keep working, so the request starts with a loading toast that has no timer. When the file is
ready, the toast becomes "Export ready" with a Download button; when it fails, the toast becomes an error with the
reason and a Retry button. Errors stay longer than the default, and only the stack's list rectangle takes pointer
input, so the invoice table stays usable around it.

The stack is placed over the page content with a limit of eight toasts, so a long session of exports cannot grow the
stack without bound:

```xml
<Grid>
    <!-- Invoice table and filters go here. -->
    <arc:ToastStack Label="Billing notifications"
                    Position="BottomRight"
                    VisibleToasts="3"
                    Limit="8" />
</Grid>
```

```csharp
var id = _toasts.Show(new ToastOptions
{
    Kind = ToastKind.Loading,
    Title = "Exporting invoices for March",
    Duration = Timeout.InfiniteTimeSpan
});

var result = await _exports.CreateCsvAsync(March2026);

_toasts.Update(id, result.IsSuccess
    ? new ToastUpdate
    {
        Kind = ToastKind.Success,
        Title = "Export ready",
        Description = "412 invoices, 1.8 MB.",
        Action = new ToastAction("Download", () => _files.Open(result.FileName))
    }
    : new ToastUpdate
    {
        Kind = ToastKind.Error,
        Title = "Export failed",
        Description = result.Error,
        Action = new ToastAction("Retry", () => _ = ExportAgainAsync())
    });
```

### Content guidelines

- **Title**: a short result in past tense or a state for loading: "Export ready", "Invite sent", "Uploading report.pdf".
  The kind already says whether it succeeded, so do not repeat it in the title.
- **Description**: one sentence with the number, name or next step: "412 invoices, 1.8 MB.", "Check the address and try
  again." Write numbers as digits.
- **Action label**: a verb, one or two words: "Undo", "Retry", "Download", "View". Never "OK" or "Close", because the
  close button already exists.
- **Errors**: say what failed and what the person can do: the reason and the way forward. Do not blame the person.
- **Sentence case, no exclamation marks**: a notification reports a fact.

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| Success!!! File uploaded | Report uploaded |
| Error | Export failed |
| Something went wrong. Please try again later. | Couldn't send the invite. Check the address and try again. |
| Click OK to continue | Project restored |

### Best practices

**Do**

- Use one toast per job and update it, so a loading state becomes its result instead of leaving two messages.
- Give every loading toast a path to an end: an update on success, an update on failure, or a timeout that the code
  sets deliberately. A loading toast with no update stays on screen.
- Keep `Limit` at a number the operator can scan, such as eight, so old results do not pile up behind new ones.
- Use `Warning` and `Error` for things the person must act on, so their longer lifetime matches the work they need
  to do.

**Avoid**

- Using the stack for messages that must stay until they are resolved, such as a plan limit. Stacked toasts close on
  their own; use `Alert` for those.
- Long descriptions. A toast is read at a glance, and the card is at most 360 px wide.
- Actions that do the main task silently, such as "Delete all" with no undo. Give destructive work a `Dialog` before
  it runs, and an Undo afterwards.
- Showing a toast for every keystroke or every poll tick. Each `Show` and `Update` is announced to assistive
  technology, so frequent messages become noise. Batch them into one result.

### Common questions

**Why did a toast disappear before I read it?** The timer runs while the stack is collapsed and stops only while the
stack is expanded, dragged or the window is minimized. Set a longer `Duration` for the toast, or hover over the stack
to pause the timers while you read.

**How do I keep a toast until the person closes it?** Set `Duration` to `Timeout.InfiniteTimeSpan` in `ToastOptions`
or `ToastUpdate`. Loading toasts already work this way until they are updated.

**What happens when a window has no `ToastStack`?** The first `Toast.Show` or `ToastHost.GetService` call creates one
on the window's overlay layer. If the window has no overlay layer, `ToastHost` throws an `InvalidOperationException`,
so place a `ToastStack` in the window in that case. A call from a control that is not attached to a window throws too.

**How do I stop the stack from taking the Alt+T shortcut?** Set `IsHotkeyEnabled` to `False`. Alt+T can clash with a
menu access key on Windows, so an application with its own menu may turn it off. You can still move focus into the
stack yourself with `FocusInto()`, for example from a "Notifications" menu item.

**Can I count or read the queued toasts?** Read `Count` for the number of queued toasts, shown or waiting, and
`IsExpanded` to tell whether the list is fanned out. Subscribe to `ToastsChanged` to keep a badge in step with the
stack.

## API reference

### ToastStack

Arc toast stack: short, non-blocking results of what someone just did, stacked at the edge of the window until they reach for them. New toasts rise from the bottom edge, older ones tuck 14px behind and shrink by 5% per step; hovering or focusing the stack fans it out into a list (Alt+T moves focus in). Toasts pause while the stack is open, dragged or the window is minimized, swipe right to dismiss, and morph in place when updated (`Update`): a loading toast becomes its result. Place one in the window (over the content, for example as the last child of the root panel) or let `ToastHost` create one on the window's overlay layer; then call `Show` or this control's `IToastService` methods from anywhere.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Duration` | `TimeSpan` | `00:00:05` | Base lifetime (default 5s). Warnings and errors stay 1.6 times longer; loading toasts wait for an update. |
| `Limit` | `int` | `12` | Oldest toasts beyond this count are dropped (default 12). |
| `Position` | `ToastStackPosition` | `BottomRight` | Edge position (default bottom right). Windows narrower than 480px always center the stack. |
| `IsContained` | `bool` | `false` | Pins the stack 16px inside its own bounds (panels and previews) instead of 24px from the window edge. |
| `VisibleToasts` | `int` | `3` | How many toasts show at once (default 3); older ones wait behind and return as the front ones close. |
| `IsHotkeyEnabled` | `bool` | `true` | Alt+T moves keyboard focus into the stack (default true). |
| `Label` | `string` | `"Notifications"` | Accessible name of the notification region (default "Notifications"). |
| `Count` | `int` | – | *Read-only.* How many toasts are queued (shown or waiting behind). |
| `IsExpanded` | `bool` | – | *Read-only.* True while the stack is fanned out (hover, keyboard focus or a tap). |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ToastsChanged` | `EventHandler?` | Raised when a toast is shown, updated or dismissed. |

Pseudo-classes: `:expanded`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

### ToastOptions

What to show in a new toast (`Show`).

Companion types, from the source:

`ToastUpdate` changes a shown toast. Null members stay as they are.

| Member | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `Kind` | New kind; the icon morphs |
| `Title` | New message |
| `Description`, `RemoveDescription` | New second line, or remove it |
| `Action`, `RemoveAction` | A new action, or fold the action button away |
| `Duration` | New lifetime; null restarts with the default for the kind |

`ToastKind` is the type of a toast: `Success`, `Info`, `Warning`, `Error` and `Loading`. `ToastStackPosition` is the
edge of the stack: `BottomRight` (default), `BottomCenter` and `BottomLeft`.

`ToastHost` finds the stack of a window and is the entry point for the app-wide API:

| Member | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `GetService(owner)` | The window's `IToastService`; creates a stack on the overlay layer when there is none |
| `GetStack(owner)` | The window's `ToastStack`, with the same creation rule |
| `Find(topLevel)` | The registered stack of a window, or null; a placed stack wins over an auto-created one |

## Accessibility

- The notification area is a region landmark named by `Label`. With `IsHotkeyEnabled` on, the name ends with
  "(Alt+T)". Alt+T moves focus into the stack and expands it.
- Tab moves between the action and close buttons of the visible toasts. Escape closes the focused toast.
- New and updated toasts are announced as "Kind: Title. Description". Errors are announced assertively; other kinds
  are announced politely.
- Each card is named "Kind: Title", so a screen reader can tell the types apart, and its description is its help text.
  The close button is named "Dismiss notification".
- Timers pause while the stack is expanded, while a toast is dragged and while the window is minimized. They keep
  running when the stack is covered by another window.
- Toasts outside `VisibleToasts` and toasts that are leaving are inert: they cannot be reached by pointer or by Tab.
- Keyboard focus is handed on when the focused toast closes. It goes to the next toast's first button; with none left,
  it returns to the element that had focus before the stack was entered.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Alt+T` | Move focus to the front toast (its action when it has one, otherwise its close button) and expand the stack. Set `IsHotkeyEnabled` to `False` to turn it off |
| `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` | Move between the action and close buttons of the visible toasts |
| `Enter` or `Space` | Press the focused button: run the action, or close the toast |
| `Escape` | Close the focused toast, with no action run |

Keyboard focus expands the stack, and leaving the stack folds it back. A mouse click on a button does not keep the stack
expanded.

## Motion

- A new toast rises from below its own height and fades in. Older toasts tuck back, shrink and lose their content
  tone. Hovering or focusing the stack fans the toasts out into a list, and leaving it folds them back.
- Swiping a toast to the right follows the pointer. A long or fast swipe dismisses it, and the card fades as it moves
  away.
- Updates morph the icon, the copy and the card height in place, and the action button opens or closes its width. A
  loading ring turns while the work runs.
- Reduced motion jumps the positions and fades toasts in and out quickly. Off motion shows every change at once.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| A new toast arrives | Rises from below with a standard enter fade | Appears in place with a fast fade | Immediate |
| Older toasts tuck back | Step back 14 px and shrink 5% per step on the morph spring; content fades | Positions jump; a fast fade | Immediate |
| The stack expands or folds | Fans out into a list on the morph spring; other changes use the smooth spring | Positions jump | Immediate |
| A toast is dismissed | Sinks 10 px and shrinks to 96% while it fades out | Fast fade | Immediate |
| A toast is swiped away | Follows the pointer; fades to 25% over 280 px; a fast release fades out in 0.22 seconds | The swipe still dismisses; the fade is quick and nothing is thrown | Immediate |
| A toast is updated | Icon, copy and card height morph; the action slot opens or closes; the loading ring turns | The loading ring stops; the new copy and height apply without a spring | Immediate |

## Related

- `Toast` for one local confirmation that the page controls with `IsOpen`.
- `Alert` for a persistent message inside the page.
- `AnnouncementBar` for a rotating banner with a countdown.
- `Dialog` for a decision that must be made before the page continues.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `Toast` | The page owns one confirmation and sets its text and open state |
| `Alert` | The message stays on the page until the person or the data resolves it |
| `AnnouncementBar` | A site-wide notice rotates through several messages |
| `Dialog` | The person must answer before the page continues |
| `ToastStack` + `Toast.Show` | Results from background work can arrive from any control and may overlap |

# Announcement bar

> A top banner that rotates messages, counts down, and collapses smoothly when dismissed.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/announcement-bar

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.AnnouncementBarRotatingMessagesDemo">
    <Border CornerRadius="18"
            BorderThickness="1"
            ClipToBounds="True"
            Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Background}"
            BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource BorderSubtle}">
        <StackPanel>
            <arc:AnnouncementBar>
                <arc:AnnouncementBar.Messages>
                    <arc:Announcement Id="launch" Message="Arc 2.0 is here, with 40 new components.">
                        <arc:Announcement.Action>
                            <arc:AnnouncementAction Label="See what's new" />
                        </arc:Announcement.Action>
                    </arc:Announcement>
                    <arc:Announcement Id="webinar" Message="Live walkthrough on Thursday at 17:00 UTC.">
                        <arc:Announcement.Action>
                            <arc:AnnouncementAction Label="Save a seat" />
                        </arc:Announcement.Action>
                    </arc:Announcement>
                    <arc:Announcement Id="status" Message="All systems operational." />
                </arc:AnnouncementBar.Messages>
            </arc:AnnouncementBar>
            <TextBlock Text="Page content" Margin="20,24" Opacity="0.6" />
        </StackPanel>
    </Border>
</UserControl>
```

## When to use

`AnnouncementBar` is a slim banner at the top of a page that speaks to every visitor, not to one section. It holds two
to four short messages, rotates through them, and can carry one call to action and a live countdown per message. When
it is dismissed, the page below moves up. It is the right place for news that applies to the whole site or app and
that the person can read at a glance.

- **Seasonal sale on a storefront or a SaaS pricing site**: "Spring sale: 30% off annual plans" with an `Upgrade`
  action and a countdown to the end of the offer, so the deadline is visible on every page.
- **Release news in an admin console**: "Arc 2.0 is here, with 40 new components" rotating with "Live walkthrough on
  Thursday at 17:00 UTC", each with its own link, so one bar carries the news of a release.
- **Scheduled maintenance on a status or operations dashboard**: an inverted bar with a "Starts in" countdown that
  stays visible until the window opens. It is the most important notice on the page, so it gets the strongest tone.
- **A campaign a returning customer should see once**: a bar with a `DismissalKey` that stays closed on the next visit
  and returns when the key changes for a new campaign.

## When not to use

- **A message about one section or form**, such as an expiring card on a billing page: use `Alert`, which lives in the
  page flow next to the content it concerns.
- **Feedback about something the visitor just did**, such as "Changes saved": use `Toast` or `ToastStack`.
- **A consent choice for cookies or tracking**: use `CookieConsent`, which asks a question and records the answer.
- **A decision the person must make before continuing**: use `Dialog`.
- **A large countdown on a page that is about the countdown**, such as a launch page or a checkout timer: use
  `Countdown`, which shows the time as the main content rather than as a line of a banner.

## Usage

Add announcements to `Messages`. The bar shows the first one and rotates through the rest every `Interval`, which
is 6 seconds by default.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:AnnouncementBar>
        <arc:AnnouncementBar.Messages>
            <arc:Announcement Id="launch"
                              Message="Arc 2.0 is here, with 40 new components." />
            <arc:Announcement Id="webinar"
                              Message="Live walkthrough on Thursday at 17:00 UTC." />
            <arc:Announcement Id="status"
                              Message="All systems operational." />
        </arc:AnnouncementBar.Messages>
    </arc:AnnouncementBar>
</UserControl>
```

`AnnouncementBar` derives from Avalonia's `TemplatedControl`. Its messages are `Announcement` objects, which the bar
draws itself. It takes the width its container gives it, so put it in the first row of the window or page layout,
where it spans the full width. The `Id` of each `Announcement` identifies it in events and in your analytics, so keep
ids stable across releases.

### Anatomy

1. **Action** (`Announcement.Action`): the label of the call to action with an arrow after it. It inherits the bar's
   foreground color in medium weight, and the arrow moves 2 px toward the destination on hover.
2. **Message** (`Message`): the message text in the bar's font size (`TypeSM`) and foreground color, on a line height
   of 19.6 px. A message change rises into place inside a window that is at least 32 px tall.
3. **Countdown** (`Announcement.Countdown`): the remaining time in medium digits, with the optional `Label` before it
   and a 6 px gap. The colons and the day mark use the muted color, and the countdown is drawn as one control.
4. **Mirror column**: an empty column on the left that is as wide as the controls on the right (32 px per control and
   a 2 px gap between them). It keeps the message centered on the page. It is removed on narrow bars.
5. **Controls** (`IsNavigationVisible`, `IsDismissible`): previous (chevron up), the pause ring and next (chevron
   down) when navigation is visible and there is more than one message, and the dismiss button (X) when
   `IsDismissible` is `True`. Each is a 32 px round ghost button in the muted color. Hover fills it at 10% and a press
   at 12%.
6. **Bar**: a muted surface with a 1 px bottom border. The padding is 16 px on the left, 8 px on the right and 6 px
   above and below. On bars 560 px wide or narrower the left padding is 14 px, the column gap is 8 px instead of 12 px
   and the mirror column is removed, so the message starts at the left edge.

### Tones

`Tone` sets the look of the bar. `Neutral` (the default) is a muted surface with a bottom border and suits almost
every page. `Inverted` fills the bar with the foreground color and sets the text in the background color. Use it for
the one notice that must not be missed, and never on more than one bar on a page.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.AnnouncementBarInvertedDemo">
    <Border CornerRadius="18"
            BorderThickness="1"
            ClipToBounds="True"
            Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Background}"
            BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource BorderSubtle}">
        <StackPanel>
            <arc:AnnouncementBar x:Name="Bar" Tone="Inverted">
                <arc:AnnouncementBar.Messages>
                    <arc:Announcement Id="maintenance" Message="Scheduled maintenance tonight.">
                        <arc:Announcement.Countdown>
                            <arc:AnnouncementCountdown Label="Starts in" />
                        </arc:Announcement.Countdown>
                    </arc:Announcement>
                </arc:AnnouncementBar.Messages>
            </arc:AnnouncementBar>
            <TextBlock Text="Page content" Margin="20,24" Opacity="0.6" />
        </StackPanel>
    </Border>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class AnnouncementBarInvertedDemo : UserControl
{
    public AnnouncementBarInvertedDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        // The maintenance window starts five hours and twelve minutes from now.
        Bar.Messages[0].Countdown!.To = DateTimeOffset.Now.AddHours(5).AddMinutes(12);
    }
}
```

In the inverted tone the secondary text is the background color at 66% and the hover fill is the background color at
10%, so the controls stay readable on the filled bar.

### Controls and autoplay

Set `IsNavigationVisible` to show the previous and next buttons and the pause ring. `IsAutoPlayEnabled` turns the
rotation off. `Next()` and `Previous()` move through the messages in code, and both wrap around at the ends.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.AnnouncementBarControlsAndCountdownDemo">
    <Border CornerRadius="18"
            BorderThickness="1"
            ClipToBounds="True"
            Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Background}"
            BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource BorderSubtle}">
        <StackPanel>
            <arc:AnnouncementBar x:Name="Bar" IsNavigationVisible="True">
                <arc:AnnouncementBar.Messages>
                    <arc:Announcement Id="sale" Message="Spring sale: 30% off annual plans.">
                        <arc:Announcement.Countdown>
                            <arc:AnnouncementCountdown Label="Ends in" />
                        </arc:Announcement.Countdown>
                        <arc:Announcement.Action>
                            <arc:AnnouncementAction Label="Upgrade" />
                        </arc:Announcement.Action>
                    </arc:Announcement>
                    <arc:Announcement Id="docs" Message="The new docs have a search that understands questions." />
                    <arc:Announcement Id="mobile" Message="Arc for iOS is in public beta.">
                        <arc:Announcement.Action>
                            <arc:AnnouncementAction Label="Join the beta" />
                        </arc:Announcement.Action>
                    </arc:Announcement>
                </arc:AnnouncementBar.Messages>
            </arc:AnnouncementBar>
            <TextBlock Text="Page content" Margin="20,24" Opacity="0.6" />
        </StackPanel>
    </Border>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class AnnouncementBarControlsAndCountdownDemo : UserControl
{
    public AnnouncementBarControlsAndCountdownDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        // The countdown ends a day and three hours from now, whenever the demo is opened.
        Bar.Messages[0].Countdown!.To = DateTimeOffset.Now.AddDays(1).AddHours(3);
    }
}
```

```xml
<arc:AnnouncementBar IsNavigationVisible="True"
                     Interval="0:0:8"
                     IsAutoPlayEnabled="True" />
```

Rotation runs only when all three conditions hold: there is more than one message, `IsAutoPlayEnabled` is `True`, and
the motion level of the bar is full. Under reduced or off motion the bar stays on its first message, so give
people a way to read the others: `IsNavigationVisible` with the previous and next buttons, or your own buttons that call
`Next()` and `Previous()`. The pause ring fills over each `Interval`. Pressing it sets `IsPaused` and stops the clock
where it is. Pressing it again resumes and finishes the remaining part of the interval.

`SelectedIndex` is two-way and reports the visible message. Use `SelectedIndexChanged` to log which message was
shown, for example to measure which announcement people reach.

### Actions and countdown

An `Announcement` can have an `Action` button with a `Label` and an `Href`, and a `Countdown` that counts down to
`To`. Use `Command` on the action instead of `Href` when the action should run code. When the action has both, the
command runs first and then the link opens. `ActionInvoked` is raised after either, with the message and its index.

```xml
<arc:AnnouncementBar>
    <arc:AnnouncementBar.Messages>
        <arc:Announcement Id="sale"
                          Message="Spring sale: 30% off annual plans.">
            <arc:Announcement.Action>
                <arc:AnnouncementAction Label="Upgrade" Href="https://example.com/upgrade" />
            </arc:Announcement.Action>
            <arc:Announcement.Countdown>
                <arc:AnnouncementCountdown To="2026-11-01T00:00:00+00:00" Label="Ends in" />
            </arc:Announcement.Countdown>
        </arc:Announcement>
    </arc:AnnouncementBar.Messages>
</arc:AnnouncementBar>
```

```csharp
public static class Analytics
{
    public static void Track(string name, string id) { }
}

bar.ActionInvoked += (_, e) => Analytics.Track("announcement.action", e.Announcement.Id);
bar.CountdownEnded += (_, e) => bar.Messages.Remove(e.Announcement);
```

The countdown shows days while a whole day or more remains, then hours, minutes and seconds, and its digits change on
the whole second. It stops at zero and shows zeros. `CountdownEnded` is raised once, when the countdown reaches zero
or when its message is shown after the end time has passed. Remove the message in that handler, as above, so the
bar does not keep an expired offer.

### Binding to a view model

The bar is a list of data with state, so bind it to a collection the view model owns. Use `ItemsSource` for the
messages; it overrides `Messages` when it is set. Bind `IsOpen` and `SelectedIndex` two-way only when the view model
needs to know that the person closed the bar or moved through the messages.

```csharp
public partial class StorefrontViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    [ObservableProperty]
    private ObservableCollection<Announcement> _announcements = new()
    {
        new Announcement { Id = "sale", Message = "Spring sale: 30% off annual plans." },
        new Announcement { Id = "webinar", Message = "Live walkthrough on Thursday at 17:00 UTC." }
    };

    [ObservableProperty]
    private bool _isBannerOpen = true;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private int _bannerIndex;
}
```

```xml
<arc:AnnouncementBar ItemsSource="{Binding Announcements}"
                     IsOpen="{Binding IsBannerOpen, Mode=TwoWay}"
                     SelectedIndex="{Binding BannerIndex, Mode=TwoWay}"
                     IsNavigationVisible="True" />
```

When the collection changes, the bar keeps the selected index (wrapped to the new count) and restarts the rotation
timer. Replacing the whole collection is therefore safe, and adding or removing a message does not need a separate
refresh.

### Remembered dismissal

Set `DismissalKey` to remember a dismissal across runs. The key is saved in `Storage`. Clear the stored value with
`AnnouncementBar.ClearDismissal` to show the bar again. The dismissal is stored by `Storage`, which defaults to a
file in the application data folder.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.AnnouncementBarRememberedDismissalDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12">
        <Border CornerRadius="18"
                BorderThickness="1"
                ClipToBounds="True"
                Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Background}"
                BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource BorderSubtle}">
            <StackPanel>
                <arc:AnnouncementBar x:Name="Campaign"
                                     DismissalKey="demo-campaign"
                                     Closed="OnClosed">
                    <arc:AnnouncementBar.Storage>
                        <arc:InMemoryMessageStorage />
                    </arc:AnnouncementBar.Storage>
                    <arc:AnnouncementBar.Messages>
                        <arc:Announcement Id="campaign" Message="Dismiss me: the choice is remembered under a key." />
                    </arc:AnnouncementBar.Messages>
                </arc:AnnouncementBar>
                <TextBlock Text="Page content" Margin="20,24" Opacity="0.6" />
            </StackPanel>
        </Border>
        <WrapPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center" ItemSpacing="12" LineSpacing="12">
            <arc:Button Content="Forget dismissal" Size="Small" Variant="Secondary" Click="OnForgetClick" />
        </WrapPanel>
        <TextBlock x:Name="Log"
                   Text="Events appear here."
                   FontSize="12"
                   TextWrapping="Wrap"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class AnnouncementBarRememberedDismissalDemo : UserControl
{
    public AnnouncementBarRememberedDismissalDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
    }

    private void OnClosed(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) => Log.Text = "Dismissed and remembered.";

    private void OnForgetClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        if (Campaign.DismissalKey is not { } key)
        {
            return;
        }
        AnnouncementBar.ClearDismissal(key, Campaign.Storage);
        // Setting the key again makes the bar read the cleared storage, so it can open.
        Campaign.DismissalKey = null;
        Campaign.DismissalKey = key;
        Campaign.IsOpen = true;
    }
}
```

```xml
<arc:AnnouncementBar DismissalKey="spring-campaign" IsDismissible="True" />
```

```csharp
AnnouncementBar.ClearDismissal("spring-campaign");
bar.IsOpen = true;
```

Choose a key that names the campaign, not the page, and change it when a new campaign starts, so every visitor sees the
new message once. Dismissing writes the key to storage at once, and `Closed` is raised at once too, before the bar has
finished collapsing.

### Example: spring campaign on a SaaS site

A marketing page for Northwind Analytics shows the spring offer above the pricing table. The bar carries the offer and
its deadline as a countdown, a link to the upgrade page, and the previous and next controls, so a visitor can read the
other notice without waiting. Autoplay is off because the offer is the message to read, not a slideshow. The page
content below stands in for the pricing table, so the bar's collapse moves it up as it would on the live site.

![A spring sale bar with a countdown, an upgrade link and navigation above a pricing table](https://docs.tkcode.si/shots/Docs/Messages/AnnouncementBar/images/SaleBanner.webp)

```xml
<Border Width="720"

                    <arc:Announcement.Countdown>

                    <arc:Announcement.Action>
                        <arc:AnnouncementAction Label="Upgrade" />
```

### Content guidelines

- **Message**: one sentence that states the news and, if needed, the date or the number: "Spring sale: 30% off annual
  plans." Keep it under about 70 characters so it fits one line on a narrow window.
- **Action label**: a verb and an object in sentence case: "See what's new", "Save a seat". Avoid "Click here".
- **Countdown label**: a short phrase before the time: "Ends in", "Starts in". The label is spoken before the time.
- **Tone of voice**: direct and factual. Give the date or the deadline instead of urgency words, and avoid exclamation
  marks.

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| Huge sale!!! | Spring sale: 30% off annual plans. |
| Click here | Save a seat |
| New! Read more | Arc 2.0 is here, with 40 new components. |
| Maintenance soon | Scheduled maintenance tonight at 22:00 UTC. |

### Best practices

**Do**

- Keep two to four messages in one bar. Each message should be readable in one interval, which is about 6 seconds.
- Put the most important message first, because the bar shows the first one when it loads.
- Give each message a stable `Id`. Events report it, so analytics can follow one message across rotations and releases.
- Remove a message from `Messages` when its countdown ends, so the bar does not keep an expired offer.

**Avoid**

- Long messages. A message that wraps to several lines pushes the page down and the bar stops looking like a banner.
- More than one inverted bar on a page. Two strong bars compete, and neither reads as the important one.
- Using the bar for one section of the page. The bar speaks to every visitor, so a notice about one form belongs in
  `Alert`.
- Relying on rotation alone. Under reduced motion the bar stops on the current message, so offer the navigation
  controls or a link to the full list.

### Common questions

**Why is `IsOpen` still `True` after a visitor dismissed the bar?** A remembered dismissal hides the bar without
changing `IsOpen`, so the bar can tell the difference between a dismissal from this session and a remembered one.
Setting `IsOpen` to `True` does not bring it back. Call `AnnouncementBar.ClearDismissal` with the key, then set
`DismissalKey` again (for example to `null` and back) so the bar reads the storage again.

**Why does the bar not rotate in my app?** Rotation needs more than one message, `IsAutoPlayEnabled` set to `True`, and
full motion. Under reduced or off motion the bar stops on the current message by design. Add the navigation controls or
call `Next()` from a timer of your own if you need to keep rotating.

**Where is the dismissal stored?** In `Storage` when you set one on the bar. Otherwise it goes to
`MessageStorage.Default`, which writes a small file in the local application data folder. Set
`MessageStorage.Default` once at startup to keep it in your settings service, or to a memory store in tests.

**How do I read the message the person is on?** Use `Current`, which is the visible `Announcement`, or `Count` for the
number of messages. `SelectedIndex` gives the position, starting at zero.

## API reference

### AnnouncementBar

Arc announcement bar: a slim banner for the top of a page. It rotates 2–4 short messages (the next one rises from below while the bar springs to the new height), pauses on hover, focus or a minimized window, and with `IsNavigationVisible` adds previous, next and a pause ring that fills over `Interval`. Messages can carry a call to action and a live countdown. Dismissing collapses the height so the page below eases up; with a `DismissalKey` the dismissal is remembered (`IMessageStorage`).

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ItemsSource` | `IList<Announcement>?` | `null` | Messages from a binding; overrides `Messages` when set. |
| `DismissalKey` | `string?` | `null` | Remembers the dismissal under this key; change the key to show a new campaign to everyone again. |
| `DismissalDuration` | `TimeSpan?` | `null` | How long a remembered dismissal keeps the bar hidden; null (default) keeps it hidden for good. |
| `IsOpen` | `bool` | `true` | Whether the bar is shown (two-way). A remembered dismissal keeps it hidden. |
| `SelectedIndex` | `int` | `0` | Index of the visible message (two-way). |
| `Interval` | `TimeSpan` | `00:00:06` | Time each message stays before the next one (default 6s). |
| `IsAutoPlayEnabled` | `bool` | `true` | Rotate automatically (default true); off under reduced motion. |
| `IsNavigationVisible` | `bool` | `false` | Show previous, next and the pause ring when there are several messages (default false). |
| `IsDismissible` | `bool` | `true` | Show the dismiss button (default true). |
| `IsPaused` | `bool` | `false` | Paused by the pause ring (two-way). |
| `Tone` | `AnnouncementBarTone` | `Neutral` | Neutral (muted surface, default) or inverted (foreground fill). |
| `Label` | `string` | `"Announcements"` | Accessible name of the region (default "Announcements"). |
| `Storage` | `IMessageStorage?` | `null` | Where the dismissal is remembered; null uses `Default`. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Closed` | `RoutedEventArgs` | Raised when the bar was dismissed. |
| `SelectedIndexChanged` | `AnnouncementEventArgs` | Raised when another message becomes visible. |
| `ActionInvoked` | `AnnouncementEventArgs` | Raised when a message's call to action is invoked. |
| `CountdownEnded` | `AnnouncementEventArgs` | Raised once when a message's countdown reaches zero. |

Pseudo-classes: `:narrow`, `:navigable`, `:rotating`, `:dismissible`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

### Announcement

One message of an `AnnouncementBar`.

Companion types used by an `Announcement`:

| Type | Properties |
|---|---|
| `AnnouncementAction` | `Label` (the text), `Href` (`Uri`, opened with the system launcher), `Command` (`ICommand`, run on invoke), `CommandParameter` |
| `AnnouncementCountdown` | `To` (`DateTimeOffset`, when the countdown reaches zero), `Label` (text before the time, optional) |

## Accessibility

- The bar is a region named by `Label`, which is `Announcements` by default.
- Each message has a name such as `1 of 3`, so a screen reader can tell where it is in the rotation.
- The rotation does not announce each change. The bar is announced when it is paused, so the user can read it.
- Tab reaches the action, the previous button, the pause ring, the next button and the close button in order.
  Enter and Space activate the focused control.
- The pause ring is a toggle. Its name changes between `Pause announcements` and `Resume announcements`.
- The rotation pauses while the pointer is over the bar, while focus is inside it, and while the window is minimized.
  Only a mouse pointer pauses it. A touch screen does not, so provide the pause ring for touch users.
- The countdown is not announced as it ticks. Its accessible name spells out the remaining days, hours and minutes.
- The previous, next and close buttons are named `Previous announcement`, `Next announcement` and `Dismiss`.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` | Moves through the action, previous, pause ring, next and dismiss controls, in that order. Hidden controls are skipped |
| `Enter` / `Space` | Runs the focused action, presses the focused button, or toggles the pause ring |

The bar itself does not take focus, so `Tab` goes straight to its controls. Focus inside the bar pauses the rotation,
so a keyboard user can read a message without it changing under them.

## Motion

- The next message rises from below with a light blur while the bar springs to fit its height.
- The pause ring fills over each interval. It stops where it is when paused and continues when resumed.
- Countdown digits drop in when they change.
- Dismissing collapses the bar and the page below moves up with it.
- Reduced motion stops the rotation and replaces messages and digits with a fade. A dismissal only fades out.
- Off motion shows every change immediately.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| Automatic rotation | Advances every `Interval`; the next message rises from below | Stops; the bar stays on the current message | Stops |
| Manual change (`Next`, `Previous`) | The message rises or drops with a blur and the height springs to fit | The message fades | Immediate |
| Pause ring | Visible while rotating; fills over the interval and stops when paused | Hidden | Hidden |
| Countdown digit change | The new digit drops in and the old one falls away | The digit fades | Immediate |
| Dismissal | The height collapses on a smooth spring and the page below moves up | The bar fades out without collapsing | Immediate |

## Related

- `Alert` for a message inside a section or a form that stays until it is resolved.
- `ToastStack` for queued results of actions the user just took.
- `CookieConsent` for consent to cookies and tracking.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `Alert` | The notice belongs to one section or form and stays until it is resolved |
| `Toast` | A finished action needs a short confirmation that closes by itself |
| `ToastStack` | Results, errors or undo actions from the app must stack at the edge of the window |
| `CookieConsent` | The notice asks visitors for a choice about cookies or tracking |
| `Countdown` | The countdown is the main content of the page, not a line of a banner |
| `Dialog` | The person must answer before the page continues |
