# Cookie consent

> A consent bar that morphs into preferences and folds into a reopen button.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/cookie-consent

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.CookieConsentConsentBarDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12">
        <Border Height="520"
                CornerRadius="26"
                BorderThickness="1"
                ClipToBounds="True"
                Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Background}"
                BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource BorderSubtle}">
            <Grid>
                <StackPanel Margin="24" Spacing="8">
                    <TextBlock Text="Acme Store"
                               FontSize="22"
                               FontWeight="Medium"
                               TextWrapping="Wrap"
                               Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
                    <TextBlock Text="The layer lets clicks through everywhere except on the consent surface."
                               FontSize="14"
                               TextWrapping="Wrap"
                               Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
                </StackPanel>
                <arc:CookieConsent x:Name="Consent"
                                   StorageKey="demo-consent"
                                   ConsentChanged="OnConsentChanged">
                    <arc:CookieConsent.Storage>
                        <arc:InMemoryMessageStorage />
                    </arc:CookieConsent.Storage>
                    <arc:CookieConsent.Policy>
                        <arc:CookieConsentPolicy Label="Cookie policy" />
                    </arc:CookieConsent.Policy>
                </arc:CookieConsent>
            </Grid>
        </Border>
        <WrapPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center" ItemSpacing="12" LineSpacing="12">
            <arc:Button Content="Cookie settings" Size="Small" Variant="Secondary" Click="OnSettingsClick" />
            <arc:Button Content="Reset" Size="Small" Variant="Secondary" Click="OnResetClick" />
            <arc:Button Content="Bottom" Size="Small" Variant="Secondary" Click="OnBottomClick" />
            <arc:Button Content="Bottom left" Size="Small" Variant="Secondary" Click="OnBottomLeftClick" />
            <arc:Button Content="Bottom right" Size="Small" Variant="Secondary" Click="OnBottomRightClick" />
        </WrapPanel>
        <TextBlock x:Name="State"
                   Text="Not decided yet."
                   FontSize="12"
                   TextWrapping="Wrap"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class CookieConsentConsentBarDemo : UserControl
{
    public CookieConsentConsentBarDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
    }

    private void OnConsentChanged(object? sender, CookieConsentChangedEventArgs e)
        => State.Text = e.Consent is null
            ? "Reset: asking again."
            : $"{e.Action}: " + string.Join(", ", e.Consent.Select(p => $"{p.Key} {(p.Value ? "on" : "off")}"));

    private void OnSettingsClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) => Consent.OpenPreferences();

    private void OnResetClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) => Consent.Reset();

    private void OnBottomClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) => Consent.Position = CookieConsentPosition.Bottom;

    private void OnBottomLeftClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) => Consent.Position = CookieConsentPosition.BottomLeft;

    private void OnBottomRightClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) => Consent.Position = CookieConsentPosition.BottomRight;
}
```

## When to use

`CookieConsent` asks a visitor for a choice about cookies and tracking, and keeps that choice. It sits over the page as
a layer at the bottom edge, so the page stays readable behind it. The bar offers Accept all, Reject all and
Customize. Customize opens a panel of categories with switches, and a saved choice folds into a small reopen button, so
the visitor can change their mind later from any page.

- **A marketing site that loads analytics and advertising scripts**: the bar appears before any optional script runs.
  Accept all and Reject all have the same weight, so refusing is as easy as accepting.
- **A store or a SaaS web app with optional categories**: Preferences, Analytics and Marketing are separate switches
  that start off, while Strictly necessary (sign-in, security, the cart) is always on.
- **Changing the choice later**: after a choice the reopen button stays in the corner, so a visitor can open the
  preferences from any page without searching for a footer link.
- **A policy update that needs a new answer**: change `Version` when the categories or the policy change, and the saved
  choice of the previous version is ignored, so the visitor is asked again.

## When not to use

- **A site-wide notice that asks for no choice**, such as a sale or a maintenance window: use `AnnouncementBar`.
- **A short confirmation that closes by itself**: use `Toast`.
- **A decision that must block the page until it is answered**, such as an age check: use `Dialog`.
- **A plain message inside one section of the page**: use `Alert`.

## Usage

Place the control over the page, for example as the last child of the window's root `Grid`. The control is a layer:
it does not take pointer input except on its own surface. With no categories set, the four Arc defaults are used:
Strictly necessary, Preferences, Analytics and Marketing.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <Grid>
        <!-- Page content goes here. -->
        <arc:CookieConsent StorageKey="site-consent" Version="1" />
    </Grid>
</UserControl>
```

`CookieConsent` derives from Avalonia's `TemplatedControl`. Its bar, panel and reopen button are three faces of one
surface that the control moves between, so you configure one control and never place the faces yourself. Because the
control draws over the content around it, it must come after that content in the parent panel.

### Anatomy

1. **Layer**: keeps 16 px from the left, right and bottom edges of the control's parent. Only the surface takes pointer
   input, so the page under the layer stays clickable.
2. **Surface**: a raised surface with a 1 px border ring and the floating shadow. The bar has a 22 px corner radius and
   the panel a 26 px one.
3. **Bar** (`IsPreferencesOpen` is `False` and no choice is saved): a message in the secondary text color with an
   inline `Policy` link at its end. The bar is at most 660 px wide with 18 px before the message and 10 px after it.
   The three buttons are Customize (ghost), Reject all and Accept all (secondary), all small and 6 px apart. Below 560 px
   the message sits above the buttons.
4. **Panel** (`IsPreferencesOpen` is `True`): 420 px wide with 18 px padding. It holds the title, a 32 px close
   button, the description, the category list and the actions. The category list scrolls after 300 px. Each row has the
   category label and its description, and a switch, or the text `Always on` for a required category. The actions are
   Reject all and Accept all side by side, and Save choices across the full width below a subtle divider.
5. **Reopen button**: a 44 px round ghost button with the cookie icon. It appears after a choice when
   `IsReopenButtonVisible` is `True`, in the corner of the bar's side (`ReopenSide`, or the left side when the bar is
   centered).

### Categories and policy

Set `Categories` to define the categories. `IsRequired` keeps a category always on, and `IsEnabledByDefault` sets the
starting state of an optional category before a choice is saved. Optional categories start off unless you set this.
`Policy` adds a link to the full policy at the end of the bar message and the panel description.

The four default categories are:

| Id | Label | Starts as |
|---|---|---|
| `necessary` | Strictly necessary | On, always (required) |
| `preferences` | Preferences | Off |
| `analytics` | Analytics | Off |
| `marketing` | Marketing | Off |

```xml
<arc:CookieConsent StorageKey="site-consent" Version="2">
    <arc:CookieConsent.Categories>
        <arc:CookieCategory Id="necessary" Label="Strictly necessary"
                            Description="Needed for the site to work."
                            IsRequired="True" IsEnabledByDefault="True" />
        <arc:CookieCategory Id="analytics" Label="Analytics"
                            Description="Helps us see which pages are useful." />
    </arc:CookieConsent.Categories>
    <arc:CookieConsent.Policy>
        <arc:CookieConsentPolicy Label="Cookie policy" Href="https://example.com/cookies" />
    </arc:CookieConsent.Policy>
</arc:CookieConsent>
```

Change `Version` when the categories or the policy change. A saved choice with another version is ignored and the
visitor is asked again. The version is a string, so `"2"` and `"2.0"` are different versions.

### Reacting to the choice

`ConsentChanged` is raised when the visitor saves, accepts, rejects or resets the choice. `Consent` maps each category
id to `True` or `False`, and is `null` while the visitor has not decided. Start optional scripts only from this event,
or from a stored choice read at startup, never before the visitor has answered.

```csharp
public static class Analytics
{
    public static bool Enabled { get; set; }
}

consent.ConsentChanged += (_, e) =>
{
    if (e.Consent is not null && e.Consent.TryGetValue("analytics", out var allowed))
    {
        Analytics.Enabled = allowed;
    }
};
```

`Action` tells you how the choice was made: `AcceptAll`, `RejectAll`, `Save` (the panel) or `Reset`. After `Reset`
the `Consent` value is `null`, so check it to know that the visitor is being asked again.

### Reading a saved choice

Read the saved choice at startup, before the control is shown, to skip the bar for a visitor who already decided.

```csharp
var record = CookieConsent.Read("site-consent", "2");
if (record is not null)
{
    Analytics.Enabled = record.Value.TryGetValue("analytics", out var allowed) && allowed;
}
```

`Read` returns `null` when nothing is stored, when the storage is unavailable, and when the stored choice was saved for
another version. A record exposes its `Value` dictionary, its `Version` and its `UpdatedAt` time. The control reads the
same storage when it is first attached, so a visitor who decided does not see the bar flash before the chip appears.

### Binding to a view model

The control has a value (`Consent`), a list of categories (`ItemsSource`) and an open state (`IsPreferencesOpen`).
With CommunityToolkit.Mvvm the view model holds them, and the bindings keep them in step with the visitor's choices.

```csharp
public partial class ConsentViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    [ObservableProperty]
    private ObservableCollection<CookieCategory> _categories = new()
    {
        new CookieCategory { Id = "necessary", Label = "Strictly necessary", IsRequired = true, IsEnabledByDefault = true },
        new CookieCategory { Id = "analytics", Label = "Analytics", Description = "Counts visits in aggregate." }
    };

    [ObservableProperty]
    private IReadOnlyDictionary<string, bool>? _consent;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private bool _isPreferencesOpen;
}
```

```xml
<arc:CookieConsent StorageKey="site-consent"
                   Version="2"
                   ItemsSource="{Binding Categories}"
                   Consent="{Binding Consent, Mode=TwoWay}"
                   IsPreferencesOpen="{Binding IsPreferencesOpen, Mode=TwoWay}" />
```

`Consent` and `IsPreferencesOpen` are two-way. The control writes them when the visitor decides or opens and closes the
panel, so the view model can read the choice without a handler. Setting `Consent` from code does not store anything:
only a visitor's decision, or `Reset`, writes the storage when `StorageKey` is set. To save a choice that you computed
yourself, use `Read` for the stored value or your own store.

### Position and reopen button

`Position` sets the bar to the bottom, bottom left or bottom right. `IsReopenButtonVisible` keeps the 44px button
after a choice is saved. `OpenPreferences` opens the panel from another control, such as a footer link.

```xml
<arc:CookieConsent Position="BottomRight" IsReopenButtonVisible="True" />
```

```csharp
settingsLink.Click += (_, _) => consent.OpenPreferences();
```

Put the position where the page's own controls are not: a bottom right bar can cover a chat button or a back-to-top
button. Keep `IsReopenButtonVisible` at `True` unless the visitor can change the choice in another place, such as an
account settings page. Without the reopen button, a saved choice hides the control completely.

### Example: consent on a marketing site

A visitor arrives at Northwind Outdoors, a store that sells trail packs, and has not answered yet. The bar sits over the
product page with the message, the policy link and the three choices at equal reading weight. Accept all and Reject all
are side by side and the same size, which is the consent pattern the visitor can trust. Customize stays a quiet ghost
button, so it is available without competing with the two answers.

![A cookie consent bar over a store page with equal Accept all and Reject all buttons](https://docs.tkcode.si/shots/Docs/Messages/CookieConsent/images/StoreConsent.webp)

```xml
<Border Width="720"
        Height="400"
        CornerRadius="12"
        ClipToBounds="True"
        Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Background}"
        BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource BorderSubtle}">
    <Grid>
        <StackPanel Margin="32,28" Spacing="10">
            <TextBlock Text="Northwind Outdoors" FontSize="24" FontWeight="Medium"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
            <TextBlock Text="Trail packs for weekend hikes, shipped within two days."
                       FontSize="14" TextWrapping="Wrap"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
            <TextBlock Text="Free returns within 30 days." FontSize="14"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
        </StackPanel>
        <arc:CookieConsent StorageKey="northwind-consent">
            <arc:CookieConsent.Storage>
                <arc:InMemoryMessageStorage />
            </arc:CookieConsent.Storage>
            <arc:CookieConsent.Policy>
                <arc:CookieConsentPolicy Label="Cookie policy" />
            </arc:CookieConsent.Policy>
        </arc:CookieConsent>
    </Grid>
</Border>
```

### Content guidelines

- **Message**: say what the cookies are for and what the visitor gets. The default message names the essential
  cookies and the optional ones, so keep the same structure when you replace it.
- **Button labels**: keep the defaults (Accept all, Reject all, Customize, Save choices) so the visitor sees the same
  words on every site. They are sentence case and say what the button does.
- **Category descriptions**: one sentence on the purpose, in plain words: "Count visits and see which pages help, only
  in aggregate."
- **Localization**: copy comes from `Labels` (`CookieConsentLabels`). Each control has its own labels, so set them in
  the language of the page instead of editing the message in code.

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| Accept | Accept all |
| We use cookies to improve your experience!!! | We use essential cookies to run this site. With your OK, we'd also use optional ones. |
| Essential | Strictly necessary |
| Cookie setting | Customize |

### Best practices

**Do**

- Give Accept all and Reject all the same weight, size and position. A consent that makes refusing harder reads as a
  dark pattern, and visitors who notice it stop trusting the rest of the site.
- Keep optional categories off until the visitor chooses, and start optional scripts only in `ConsentChanged` or from a
  stored choice read at startup.
- Change `Version` whenever a category or the policy changes, so the visitor is asked again.
- Keep the reopen button visible, so the visitor can change the choice at any time.

**Avoid**

- Pre-ticking optional categories with `IsEnabledByDefault` set to `True`. The visitor did not choose them.
- Setting `Consent` from code to record a choice. It is not stored; decide through the control or store the value yourself.
- Covering content that the visitor needs, such as the checkout button, with the bar. Test the layer on small windows.
- Using the bar for a question that is not about cookies or tracking. A consent dialog that asks for something else
  teaches visitors to dismiss it.

### Common questions

**Why does the bar not appear for a visitor who already answered?** A stored choice for the current `Version` folds the
control into the reopen button, so the bar is hidden by design. Use `Reset` to forget the choice and ask again. Check
whether `Read` returns a record with the same `StorageKey` and version if you expected the bar to show.

**Does Escape save the choice?** No. Escape closes the preferences panel without saving, and the bar stays as it was.
The draft of the switches is discarded, so reopening the panel shows the saved values.

**How do I open the preferences from a footer link?** Call `OpenPreferences()`, as in the usage example, or bind
`IsPreferencesOpen` two-way. `ClosePreferences()` closes the panel without saving. `Reset()` forgets the saved choice,
clears the storage and shows the bar again.

**Where is the choice stored?** In `Storage` when you set one on the control, or in `MessageStorage.Default`, which is
a file in the local application data folder. The stored text is JSON with the value, the version and the time, such as
`{"value":{"analytics":true},"version":"2","updatedAt":"2026-10-21T09:30:00.0000000+00:00"}`. Use an in-memory storage in
previews and tests.

**Can I use the control outside a web site?** It is a generic consent layer. In a desktop app the wording and the
categories are your decision: `Labels` changes the bar and panel copy, and your own categories name what is asked, so
the bar can ask about telemetry or data sharing instead of cookies.

## API reference

### CookieConsent

Arc cookie consent: a consent bar that morphs into a preferences panel and, once a choice is saved, folds into a small floating button that reopens it. One surface springs between the three shapes. Optional categories start off, refusing is as easy as accepting, and the choice is reported through `ConsentChanged` and can be remembered (`StorageKey`, read back with `Read`). The control is a layer: place it over the page (for example as the last child of the window's root grid, or of a preview panel); it lets clicks through everywhere except on its surface, which hangs 16px from the bottom.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ItemsSource` | `IList<CookieCategory>?` | `null` | Categories from a binding; overrides `Categories` when set. |
| `Consent` | `IReadOnlyDictionary<string, bool>?` | `null` | The saved choice (category id → allowed); null means the visitor has not decided. Two-way. |
| `StorageKey` | `string?` | `null` | Remembers the choice under this key (see `Read`). |
| `Version` | `string` | `"1"` | Bump when categories or the policy change to ask again (default "1"). |
| `Storage` | `IMessageStorage?` | `null` | Where the choice is stored; null uses `Default`. |
| `IsPreferencesOpen` | `bool` | `false` | Whether the preferences panel is open. Two-way. |
| `Policy` | `CookieConsentPolicy?` | `null` | Link to the full policy, shown in the bar and the panel. |
| `Position` | `CookieConsentPosition` | `Bottom` | Where the bar sits (default bottom, centered). |
| `IsReopenButtonVisible` | `bool` | `true` | Keep a small button after a choice so visitors can change their mind (default true). |
| `ReopenSide` | `CookieConsentSide?` | `null` | Corner of the reopen button; null follows the bar (left when the bar is centered). |
| `Labels` | `CookieConsentLabels` | – | Copy of the bar, panel and buttons (Arc's English defaults). |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ConsentChanged` | `CookieConsentChangedEventArgs` | Raised when a choice is made or reset. |

Pseudo-classes: `:bar-stacked`, `:bar-compact`, `:panel-wide`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

### CookieCategory

One group of cookies a visitor can allow or refuse.

Companion types used by a `CookieConsent`:

| Type | Members |
|---|---|
| `CookieConsentPolicy` | `Label` (link text, default `Cookie policy`), `Href` (`Uri`, opened with the system launcher), `Command` (`ICommand`, run on invoke) |
| `CookieConsentLabels` | `Message`, `Customize`, `AcceptAll`, `RejectAll`, `Save`, `PreferencesTitle`, `PreferencesDescription`, `Reopen`, `AlwaysOn`, `Close` |
| `CookieConsentAction` | `AcceptAll`, `RejectAll`, `Save`, `Reset`: how the choice was made |
| `CookieConsentPosition` | `Bottom` (default), `BottomLeft`, `BottomRight` |
| `CookieConsentRecord` | `Value` (category id to allowed), `Version`, `UpdatedAt`: returned by `CookieConsent.Read` |

## Accessibility

- The bar and the panel are non-modal dialogs. Each is named by its title, and its message or description is the
  help text.
- Opening the panel moves focus to its title. Saving the panel moves focus to the reopen button.
- Each category switch is named by the category label, with its description as help text. Required categories show
  `Always on` text instead of a switch.
- Tab moves between the buttons and switches. Space toggles the focused switch, and clicking the category name also
  toggles it.
- Escape closes the panel without saving and returns focus to the bar.
- Reject all and Accept all have the same weight and sit side by side.
- The reopen button is named `Cookie preferences` (the `Reopen` label), so it is found by name after a choice.
- The Save button's help text counts the choices, for example "2 of 3 optional categories allowed", so a screen reader
  user hears the effect before saving.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` | Moves between the buttons and switches of the bar or the panel |
| `Space` | Toggles the focused category switch |
| `Enter` | Presses the focused button: Customize, Reject all, Accept all, Save choices, Close or the reopen button |
| `Escape` | In the panel, closes it without saving and returns focus to the bar |

## Motion

- The bar, the panel and the reopen button are one surface that changes its position, width, height and corner.
- Each face rises a few pixels out of a short blur. Leaving faces fade out and drop slightly.
- The bar enters from the bottom edge with a small scale.
- Reduced motion jumps the surface between its shapes and only fades the faces in. Off motion shows every change
  immediately.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| Bar enters | Rises from the bottom edge with a small scale and fades in | Fades in | Immediate |
| Surface changes shape (bar, panel, reopen button) | Moves, resizes and changes its corner. Growing uses a small overshoot, shrinking settles without one | Jumps to the new shape | Immediate |
| Face changes | The new face rises about 10 px out of a short blur; the leaving face fades out and drops slightly | The new face fades in; the leaving face fades out quickly | Immediate |

## Related

- `AnnouncementBar` for a site-wide notice that does not ask for a choice.
- `Dialog` for a decision that blocks the page until the user answers.
- `Toast` for a short confirmation that closes by itself.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `AnnouncementBar` | The notice is for every visitor and asks for no choice |
| `Dialog` | The person must answer before the page continues |
| `Toast` | A short confirmation should close by itself |
| `Alert` | A plain message belongs to one section of the page |
| `Switch` | A single preference is set inside a form in your own page |

# Progress

> Show how much of a known task is complete.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/progress

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ProgressCountedValueDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="16">
        <arc:Progress x:Name="Upload"
                      Label="Uploading 4 files"
                      IsValueVisible="True"
                      Value="35" />
        <WrapPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center" ItemSpacing="12" LineSpacing="12">
            <arc:Button Content="Advance" Variant="Secondary" Click="OnAdvanceClick" />
            <arc:Button Content="Complete" Variant="Secondary" Click="OnCompleteClick" />
            <arc:Button Content="Reset" Variant="Ghost" Click="OnResetClick" />
        </WrapPanel>
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class ProgressCountedValueDemo : UserControl
{
    private readonly Random _random = new(3);

    public ProgressCountedValueDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
    }

    private void OnAdvanceClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        Upload.Value = Math.Min(100, Upload.Value + _random.Next(8, 30));
    }

    private void OnCompleteClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        Upload.Value = 100;
    }

    private void OnResetClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        Upload.Value = 0;
    }
}
```

## When to use

`Progress` shows how far a task with a known total has come: a file upload, a data import, a batch job or a
month-end close. It sits in the flow of the page, above or beside the content it describes, and it gives the person a
single answer to "how much is left". The optional count and the completion check let the bar carry the number as well
as the shape, so a person can read the state without interpreting the fill.

- **File uploads and exports**: an invoice export or a document upload in a billing or CRM screen, with `Label` naming
  the job ("Uploading 4 files") and `IsValueVisible` showing the percentage. The bar fills as each chunk completes.
- **Data imports with a known row count**: a contacts import of 2,400 rows in a CRM. Set `Maximum` to the row count and
  `Value` to the rows processed, so the bar and the count read in the units the user counts in.
- **Batch jobs and reconciliations**: a month-end ledger close or a nightly reconciliation in a finance console, where
  several jobs run side by side. Each job gets its own bar, and the completed ones show the check.
- **Setup and onboarding checklists with a measurable total**: a workspace setup that has imported 3 of 5 data sources.
  The bar shows the share of the setup that is done, and the list of steps says which ones remain.
- **Long operations in developer tools**: a build, a package sync or a log archive with a measurable number of steps.

## When not to use

- **A load with no measurable progress**: use `Skeleton` to reserve the space of the content that is loading.
- **A quota measured against an allowance**: use `UsageMeter` for storage, seats or API calls against a limit. A
  bar at 100% means the job finished, while a quota at 100% means the allowance is used up and needs a warning.
- **A single metric on a dashboard**: use `Gauge` for a headline number such as availability or on-time delivery.
- **A position in a multi-step flow**: use `Stepper` to show which step is current. A bar implies a total amount of
  work that the steps do not have.
- **A deadline rather than a share of work**: use `Countdown` for the time left until a moment. A bar that counts time
  down reads as work done, which is the opposite of what a deadline shows.

## Usage

Set `Value` and, when the total is not 100, `Maximum`. The bar is read-only and cannot take focus.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:Progress Label="Uploading 4 files"
                  IsValueVisible="True"
                  Value="35" />
</UserControl>
```

`Progress` derives from Avalonia's `RangeBase`, so `Value` and `Maximum` are the range properties you already know from
sliders and scroll bars. `Minimum` is treated as 0, and a `Maximum` that is zero or negative counts as 100. The control
clamps `Value` to the range when it computes the percentage, so a value above the maximum reads as 100% and a value
below zero reads as 0%. The control never writes to `Value`: it only shows what it is given, which makes it safe to
bind from a view model that owns the job.

### Anatomy

1. **Label** (`Label`): the visible name of the job, in the small type size and the secondary text color. It sits on
   the left of the row above the track and is also the accessible name. Without a label the row is hidden.
2. **Readout** (`IsValueVisible`): the counted percentage, right-aligned, in the muted text color with tabular figures.
   It sits 12 px after the label. Its box is as wide as "100%", so the check and the digits do not shift as the number
   gains a digit. At 100% a success-colored check appears beside the count.
3. **Track**: a pill 7 px high, including its 1 px border, with the border color, the surface-muted background and
   fully rounded ends. The track clips its fill, so the round end keeps its shape at every value.
4. **Fill**: the accent color from the left edge of the track, sized to the percentage. At 100% it changes to the success
   color.

The meta row (label and readout) appears only when `Label` has text or `IsValueVisible` is on. The gap between the meta
row and the track is 8 px. A bar with neither shows only the track, 7 px high, which suits a table row or a card footer.

### Bar only

Without a label or a value the bar stands alone. Its accessible name is "Progress".

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ProgressBarOnlyDemo">
    <arc:Progress Value="62" />
</UserControl>
```

Use the bar alone when the surrounding layout already names the job, such as a row in a table whose first column is the
job name, or a card whose heading says "Export". Adding a second label in that case repeats the same words.

### Custom maximum

`Percentage` is `round(Value / Maximum × 100)`, so 1,392 of 2,400 reads as 58%.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ProgressCustomMaximumDemo">
    <arc:Progress Label="Importing contacts"
                  IsValueVisible="True"
                  Maximum="2400"
                  Value="1392" />
</UserControl>
```

Use `Maximum` when the total is a count that people think in: rows, files, bytes or steps. A count reads more
honestly than a percentage that the person must compute, and it stays correct when the total changes, because the
percentage is recomputed from both numbers. Keep `Value` and `Maximum` in the same unit, and do not mix bytes and
megabytes in one bar.

### Changing label

Changing `Label` rises the new text in from a soft blur while the old text lifts away.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ProgressChangingLabelDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="16">
        <arc:Progress x:Name="Export" Label="Preparing export" Value="20" />
        <WrapPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center" ItemSpacing="12" LineSpacing="12">
            <arc:Button Content="Next phase" Variant="Secondary" Click="OnNextPhaseClick" />
        </WrapPanel>
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class ProgressChangingLabelDemo : UserControl
{
    private static readonly string[] Phases = ["Preparing export", "Compressing archive", "Uploading archive"];

    private int _phase;

    public ProgressChangingLabelDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
    }

    private void OnNextPhaseClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        _phase = (_phase + 1) % Phases.Length;
        Export.Label = Phases[_phase];
        Export.Value = 20 + _phase * 35;
    }
}
```

Use a changing label for a job that moves through named phases, such as "Preparing export", "Compressing archive" and
"Uploading archive". Keep the same bar across the phases and reset `Value` for each phase only when the phase has its own
total. A bar that restarts from zero on every phase tells the person that the whole job has started over.

```xml
<arc:Progress Label="{Binding PhaseName}"
              Value="{Binding PhaseProgress}" />
```

### Completion

At 100% the fill turns to the success color and a check appears beside the count. Style the state with the
`:complete` pseudo-class.

```csharp
upload.Value = 100;
// upload.IsComplete is now true and the check is shown when IsValueVisible is on.
```

`IsComplete` is read-only. It becomes true when the percentage reaches 100, and the `:complete` pseudo-class follows it.
A job whose count stops at 99 of 100 is not complete, so set `Value` to the full total when the work is done. Progress does not announce completion by itself. Show a notice, for example with a toast, when the task ends.

### Binding to a view model

In an MVVM app the view model owns the job and the bar shows its state. With CommunityToolkit.Mvvm, an
`ObservableObject` holds the counts and a computed percentage; the bar binds to them one way.

```csharp
public partial class ImportViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    [ObservableProperty]
    private int _rowsImported;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private int _rowsTotal = 2400;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private string _phaseName = "Importing contacts";
}
```

```xml
<arc:Progress Label="{Binding PhaseName}"
              IsValueVisible="True"
              Maximum="{Binding RowsTotal}"
              Value="{Binding RowsImported, Mode=OneWay}" />
```

Bind `Value` and `Maximum` one way. The import service sets `RowsImported` as each batch commits, and the binding
carries the change to the bar, so the page does not poll the job. Bind `Label` to the phase
name so a change in phase rises in with the new text. Use a command, such as a `Cancel` button wired to a
`[RelayCommand]`, next to the bar rather than inside it, because the bar takes no input.

### Reporting progress

Update `Value` when a unit of work completes, such as a batch of rows or a file, not on every byte or frame. Each change
starts the fill spring, so a steady stream of tiny updates keeps the bar moving but adds no information. Batches of a few
hundred rows, or one file at a time, are a good unit. When the job has long pauses, such as a server-side step with no feedback, change the `Label` to say what the job is waiting for instead of
letting the bar sit still without an explanation.

### Example: Data import in a CRM

An import screen shows three jobs that run side by side: the export of the invoice history, the contacts import and a
ledger reconciliation. Each job has its own bar and its own label, so a person can see which one is done without
reading a log. The completed job shows the check, the running one shows its count out of the total, and the job that has
just started sits near the start of its track. The copy names the job, so the bar reads without the page heading.

![A data migration panel with one finished job, one import at 58% and one job just started](https://docs.tkcode.si/shots/Docs/Progress/Progress/images/MigrationJobs.webp)

```xml
<Border Width="640"
        Padding="28"
        CornerRadius="12"
        Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Surface}"
        BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Border}"
        BorderThickness="1">
    <StackPanel Spacing="22">
        <StackPanel Spacing="4">
            <TextBlock Text="Data migration"
                       FontSize="18"
                       FontWeight="SemiBold"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
            <TextBlock Text="Three jobs for the Northwind workspace"
                       FontSize="13"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
        </StackPanel>
        <arc:Progress Label="Invoice history export"
                      IsValueVisible="True"
                      Value="100" />
        <arc:Progress Label="Contacts import"
                      IsValueVisible="True"
                      Maximum="2400"
                      Value="1392" />
        <arc:Progress Label="Ledger reconciliation"
                      IsValueVisible="True"
                      Value="4" />
    </StackPanel>
</Border>
```

Each bar uses the same width and the same readout, so the column reads as one list. The contacts import uses `Maximum`
because the team counts rows, and the other two use the default 100 because their totals are naturally percentages. A
finished job keeps its row in the list with the check, so the person sees that it is complete rather than wondering
whether it disappeared.

### Content guidelines

The label names the job and the count, so both should read correctly on their own. Name the object of the work, use
sentence case and keep the label short enough to fit on one line beside the readout. Use the present participle while
the job runs and a plain noun when it is done, so the label tells the person what state the job is in.

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| `Progress` | `Uploading 4 files` |
| `Done` | `Invoice history export` (the check and 100% say it is done) |
| `Importing... please wait` | `Importing contacts` |
| `Step 2 of 5 (40%)` | `Ledger reconciliation`, with `Value` set to 40 |
| `Error: upload failed` | `Upload failed. Retry` in a message next to the bar, and leave the bar where it stopped |

Keep the numbers in the readout in digits, and let the bar show the percentage. Do not write the percentage into the
label too, because the person then reads the same number twice.

### Best practices

**Do**

- Show `IsValueVisible` on any job that a person waits for, because the number tells them whether the job is moving.
- Use `Maximum` when the total is a count the person thinks in, because the percentage then stays correct as the total
  changes.
- Leave the bar where it stopped when a job fails, and say why in a message next to it, because a reset bar hides the
  work that was done.
- Keep one bar per job in a list, so each job has its own state, label and check.

**Avoid**

- Showing a bar for work with no measurable total, because a bar that moves at random teaches people to ignore it.
  Use `Skeleton` for content that is loading.
- Resetting `Value` to zero between phases of one job, because the person reads it as the whole job starting over.
- Updating `Value` on every byte or frame, because each change restarts the fill spring and adds no information.
- Treating the check as the only sign of completion in a list. Add a status word or a message when the job's result
  matters, such as "Export ready".

### Common questions

**What happens when `Value` is above `Maximum`?** The percentage is clamped to 100, and `IsComplete` becomes true. The
control does not change `Value` itself, so reset the job in your view model if it should not count as finished.

**Can the bar show an unknown total?** No. The control has no indeterminate state, so a bar with no total is a wrong
answer. Use `Skeleton` while the content loads, or show the job's current phase in a label without a bar.

**How do I hide the label and keep the readout?** Keep `IsValueVisible` on and leave `Label` empty. The meta row then
shows only the readout, right-aligned above the track, and the accessible name becomes "Progress". Give the bar a
heading in the surrounding layout when the name matters.

**How do I know when a job completes?** Subscribe to the view model's job state, or check `IsComplete` after you set
`Value`. The control has no event for completion, so the page announces it: show a toast or a message when the job ends.

## API reference

### Progress

Shows how much of a known task is complete (Arc Progress). One smooth spring drives both the fill and the counted percentage, so the number always matches the bar; the fill slides in from the left (keeping its round end) and turns to the success color at 100%, where a check settles in beside the count. `Minimum` is treated as 0 like Arc; a non-positive `Maximum` counts as 100.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Label` | `string?` | `null` | Visible label above the bar; it is also the accessible name (defaults to "Progress"). |
| `IsValueVisible` | `bool` | `false` | Shows the counted percentage and, at 100%, a check (Arc `showValue`). |
| `Percentage` | `int` | – | *Read-only.* Defines the `Percentage` property. |
| `IsComplete` | `bool` | – | *Read-only.* Defines the `IsComplete` property. |

Pseudo-classes: `:complete`

Derives from `RangeBase`: every member of `RangeBase` works as well.

## Accessibility

- `Label` is the accessible name. Without a label the name is "Progress".
- The control exposes the value as a percentage, so a screen reader reads the current percentage, for example 30%.
- It is a read-only progress bar for assistive technology, and it does not ask for focus.
- It is not a live region. Announce completion separately when the task ends.
- It is not focusable and has no keyboard interaction. Keep the controls that start, pause or cancel the job in the tab
  order, next to the bar, so the person can reach them with the keyboard.
- The percentage is the value that is read aloud, so give the job a name that says what is counted, such as
  "Contacts import", and the number has a meaning on its own.

## Motion

- One smooth spring moves the fill and the counted percentage together, so the number always matches the bar.
- At 100% the fill changes to the success color after a short delay, and the check settles in with a small scale and blur.
- A changed label rises in from a soft blur while the old label fades out.
- Reduced motion jumps the fill and the count straight to the new value, and swaps the label with a short fade.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Value` changes | The fill and the count move together on one smooth spring | The fill and the count jump to the new value | Immediate |
| Reaching 100% | The fill fades to the success color after 200 ms; the check scales from 0.6 after 0.24 s | The check fades in | Immediate |
| `Label` changes | The new label rises in from 0.3 em with a soft blur; the old one fades | A short fade | Immediate |

### Using motion with restraint

The fill and the count are the only moving parts that matter in a progress bar, and they should move only when the job
moves. Do not loop a pulse or a shimmer on a running bar, because the motion then suggests activity that the job does not
have. A bar that is paused or waiting should stop changing, and the label should say why. Reduced motion needs no extra
work: the control jumps the values and fades the check.

## Related

- `Skeleton` when the amount of work is unknown and the content is still loading.
- `UsageMeter` when a value fills an allowance with a limit.
- `Gauge` for a single metric on a dashboard.
- `Stepper` when the task is a sequence of named steps.
- `Countdown` when the time left matters more than the share of work done.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `Skeleton` | The content is loading and no progress can be measured |
| `UsageMeter` | A value is measured against a limit that people manage |
| `Gauge` | One headline metric is shown on a dashboard |
| `Stepper` | The task is a sequence of named steps with a current step |
| `Countdown` | The remaining time to a fixed moment is the message |

# Skeleton

> Reserve space while content is still loading.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/skeleton

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.SkeletonProfileDemo">
    <arc:Skeleton IsAvatarVisible="True" />
</UserControl>
```

## When to use

`Skeleton` holds the place of a block of content while its data loads. Its placeholder has the shape of the content it
stands for, an avatar and a number of text lines, so the page keeps its layout when the data arrives. Use it in the
regions of a screen that load on their own: a profile header, a comment list or an activity feed. The content replaces
the placeholder in the same place, so the person does not see the page jump.

- **Profile and account headers**: a user card in a SaaS admin console while the account record loads. The avatar and
  two text lines mark where the name and the role will appear.
- **Comment and activity feeds**: a team thread or an audit log that fetches its newest entries after the page opens.
  Five placeholder entries show the shape of the feed without implying a count.
- **Invoice and order details**: the summary block of an order page in e-commerce or billing, while line items and
  totals load from a separate service. Reserving the space keeps the totals from moving under the cursor.
- **Dashboard cards whose data arrives later**: a revenue card or a customer list in an analytics dashboard, where the
  card frame is already on screen and only its body is waiting for a query.
- **Content that swaps in place**: any region whose final height is known from its design, so the change from loading to
  loaded only fills the space that was held.

## When not to use

- **Work with a measurable amount of progress**: use `Progress` when the job reports how much is done, such as an upload
  or an import with a known row count. A skeleton says that content is coming, not how far along it is.
- **A loaded page with no content to show**: use `EmptyState`, which explains why the list is empty and offers the next
  action.
- **An inline status or an AI thinking line**: use `TextShimmer` for a short line of text that says the system is
  working, such as "Thinking through the invoice". A skeleton is for a block of content, not a sentence.
- **A small action that is waiting for a server reply**: use a button in its busy state. A skeleton is for a region of
  content, and a single button or field does not need a placeholder.
- **Grids, charts and media with their own shape**: draw the shape of the chart or image in a placeholder of your own.
  `Skeleton` draws only text lines and an avatar, so it cannot match a plot or a thumbnail.

## Usage

A skeleton shows its placeholder while `Content` is null. Set `Lines` for the number of text lines and
`IsAvatarVisible` for a round avatar placeholder in front of them.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:Skeleton IsAvatarVisible="True" Lines="3" />
</UserControl>
```

`Skeleton` derives from Avalonia's `ContentControl`, so `Content`, `ContentTemplate` and the content alignment
properties work as they do on any content control. The placeholder and the content share one frame: the placeholder
fades out and the content takes its place inside that frame, so the control is the same element before and after the
load. The control stretches to the width of its slot by default, and its text lines are a share of that width, so the
placeholder follows the layout around it.

### Anatomy

1. **Avatar placeholder** (`IsAvatarVisible`): a circle 44 px in diameter, the medium control size, drawn in the block
   color. It appears only when the property is on.
2. **Text lines** (`Lines`): one to six rounded bars in the block color, 12 px tall, with a 12 px gap between them. The
   first line is 16 px tall and 48% of the width. The last line is 72% of the width, and the lines between are full
   width.
3. **Block color**: a mix of the strong border color into the surface color, so the placeholder reads as a quiet
   neutral in both themes and does not depend on the accent.
4. **Spacing above the blocks**: 4 px above the first block, so the placeholder does not touch the top edge of its
   slot.
5. **Content frame** (`Content`): the loaded content, which rises 4 px into place when `IsLoading` becomes false. The
   control then takes the height of the content.

The block corners are fully rounded. Each block's corner radius is the control radius clamped to half its height, so the
16 px first line and the 12 px lines keep round ends.

### Matching the layout

Set `Lines` and `IsAvatarVisible` to match what the content will look like, not to fill the slot. A profile header
with a name and a role is an avatar and two lines. A comment is an avatar and three lines. Match the count so the
height change on load is small, and the page does not move when the content arrives.

`Lines` is clamped to 1 to 6. A value above 6 is reduced to 6, and a value below 1 is raised to 1. Use one to three lines
for most cards and no more than six for long text blocks.

### Comment placeholder

`Lines` is clamped to 1 to 6. The first line is shorter and taller, and the last line ends at 72% of the width.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.SkeletonLinesDemo">
    <arc:Skeleton Lines="4" />
</UserControl>
```

### Loaded content

Set `Content` to the real view and bind `IsLoading` to the loading state. When `IsLoading` becomes false, the
placeholder fades out, the content rises into place and the height changes smoothly.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.SkeletonIntoContentDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="16">
        <arc:Skeleton x:Name="Post" IsAvatarVisible="True" Lines="2">
            <StackPanel Spacing="10">
                <StackPanel Orientation="Horizontal" Spacing="12">
                    <arc:Avatar DisplayName="Maya Chen" Size="Medium" />
                    <TextBlock Text="Maya Chen"
                               FontSize="16"
                               Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
                </StackPanel>
                <TextBlock Text="Shipped the new billing page. The usage meter now explains what fills the plan."
                           TextWrapping="Wrap"
                           Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
            </StackPanel>
        </arc:Skeleton>
        <WrapPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center" ItemSpacing="12" LineSpacing="12">
            <arc:Button x:Name="Toggle"
                        Content="Finish loading"
                        Variant="Secondary"
                        Click="OnToggleClick" />
        </WrapPanel>
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class SkeletonIntoContentDemo : UserControl
{
    public SkeletonIntoContentDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
    }

    private void OnToggleClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        Post.IsLoading = !Post.IsLoading;
        Toggle.Content = Post.IsLoading ? "Finish loading" : "Load again";
    }
}
```

```xml
<arc:Skeleton IsAvatarVisible="True"
              Lines="2"
              IsLoading="{Binding IsLoadingProfile}">
    <StackPanel Spacing="8">
        <TextBlock Text="{Binding UserName}" />
        <TextBlock Text="{Binding Bio}" TextWrapping="Wrap" />
    </StackPanel>
</arc:Skeleton>
```

`IsLoading` defaults to true. A skeleton with `Content` shows the content only when `IsLoading` is false, so a page that
sets `Content` and forgets `IsLoading` keeps showing the placeholder. With no content the placeholder always shows, even
when `IsLoading` is false.

### Binding to a view model

In an MVVM app the view model owns the loading state and the data. With CommunityToolkit.Mvvm, an `ObservableObject`
holds the flag and the values, and a `[RelayCommand]` starts the load.

```csharp
public interface IProfileService
{
    Task<UserProfile> GetCurrentAsync();
}

public partial class ProfileViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    private readonly IProfileService _profiles;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private bool _isLoadingProfile = true;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private string _userName = string.Empty;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private string _bio = string.Empty;

    public ProfileViewModel(IProfileService profiles) => _profiles = profiles;

    [RelayCommand]
    private async Task LoadAsync()
    {
        IsLoadingProfile = true;
        var profile = await _profiles.GetCurrentAsync();
        UserName = profile.DisplayName;
        Bio = profile.Bio;
        IsLoadingProfile = false;
    }
}
```

```xml
<arc:Skeleton IsAvatarVisible="True"
              Lines="2"
              IsLoading="{Binding IsLoadingProfile, Mode=OneWay}">
    <StackPanel Spacing="8">
        <TextBlock Text="{Binding UserName}" />
        <TextBlock Text="{Binding Bio}" TextWrapping="Wrap" />
    </StackPanel>
</arc:Skeleton>
```

Bind `IsLoading` one way. The control never changes it, so the view model stays the only owner of the state. Set the flag
to false only after the values are assigned, so the content never shows empty text. A failed load should also set the
flag to false and show an error message in the content, because a skeleton that never resolves tells the person nothing.

### Example: Activity feed while the next entry loads

An account page shows its recent activity. The first entry has loaded, and the second is still waiting for its author
and text. The placeholder keeps the second entry at the height of a real entry, so the divider and the entries below
stay where they are. The copy around the feed names the workspace, so the page reads as finished even while one entry
is still loading.

![An account activity list with one loaded entry and a skeleton entry below it](https://docs.tkcode.si/shots/Docs/Progress/Skeleton/images/ActivityFeed.webp)

```xml
<Border Width="680"
        Padding="28"
        CornerRadius="12"
        Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Surface}"
        BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Border}"
        BorderThickness="1">
    <StackPanel Spacing="20">
        <StackPanel Spacing="4">
            <TextBlock Text="Account activity"
                       FontSize="18"
                       FontWeight="SemiBold"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
            <TextBlock Text="Latest changes in the Northwind workspace"
                       FontSize="13"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
        </StackPanel>
        <StackPanel Orientation="Horizontal" Spacing="12">
            <arc:Avatar DisplayName="Maya Chen" Size="Medium" />
            <StackPanel Spacing="2">
                <TextBlock Text="Maya Chen"
                           FontWeight="Medium"
                           Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
                <TextBlock Text="Changed the billing address on inv_2026_0412"
                           FontSize="13"
                           Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
            </StackPanel>
        </StackPanel>
        <Border Height="1" Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Border}" />
        <arc:Skeleton IsAvatarVisible="True" Lines="2" />
    </StackPanel>
</Border>
```

The loaded entry uses the same avatar size as the placeholder, so the two rows line up. The placeholder has two lines
because a real activity entry is one name and one sentence. The divider sits between entries rather than inside the
skeleton, so it stays when the entry loads.

### Content guidelines

A skeleton has no text of its own on screen, so its words are the accessible name and the words around it. Name the
loading region with what it loads, in sentence case, and keep the surrounding copy specific. Do not put "Loading" in the
visible heading of the region, because the heading stays on screen after the content arrives.

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| `Loading content` (the default name for a comments list) | `Loading comments` |
| `Please wait...` as a visible line under the placeholder | Nothing visible; the name carries the state for assistive technology |
| `Loading` as the section heading | The section heading, such as `Recent activity`, with the skeleton beneath it |
| `Error loading data` as the only text | `Could not load the billing history. Try again`, with a retry button |

Keep `Label` short and specific. A label such as "Loading invoice summary" tells a screen reader which region is
busy, which "Loading" alone does not.

### Best practices

**Do**

- Match `Lines` and `IsAvatarVisible` to the loaded content, because the height change on load is then small and the
  page does not jump.
- Give each independent region its own skeleton, so a slow query does not hold back the rest of the page.
- Set `IsLoading` to false after the view model has assigned the values, so the content never shows empty text.
- Show an error in the content area when a load fails, because the placeholder otherwise stays on screen with no
  explanation.

**Avoid**

- Using a skeleton for work with a known amount of progress, because a bar that reports the share of work done is more
  useful than a placeholder. Use `Progress` for those jobs.
- Rendering hundreds of skeletons at once, because each block is drawn and animated, which costs time on a long list.
  Show a few placeholder rows and let the list fill in as the data arrives.
- Placing a skeleton over a shape it cannot draw, such as a chart or a thumbnail, because the placeholder then promises a
  layout that the content does not have.
- Leaving `IsLoading` at its default of true when the page sets `Content` for a load that has already finished, because
  the content stays hidden behind the placeholder.

### Common questions

**Why does my content not show after I set `Content`?** `IsLoading` defaults to true, and the content shows only when it
is false. Bind `IsLoading` to your loading flag, or set it to false when the data is ready.

**Does the placeholder stop after a while?** The pulse runs about 20 seconds and then rests. The placeholder itself stays
on screen until `IsLoading` becomes false or `Content` replaces it. Show a status line if the load takes longer than the
pulse.

**Can I use `Skeleton` without content at all?** Yes. With `Content` null the placeholder always shows, and so does a
control with `IsLoading` set to false, which is useful for a region that is decorative while its data is not yet
connected.

**How do I draw a skeleton for a chart or an image?** `Skeleton` draws only text lines and an avatar. Build the shape of
the chart or the image in your own control or a plain border, and show it with the same fade you use for the content.

## API reference

### Skeleton

Reserves space while content is still loading (Arc Skeleton): an optional round avatar and 1–6 text lines that pulse top to bottom in a calm, finite wave. With `Content` it crossfades into the content when `IsLoading` turns false (the content rises 4px into place) while the height springs from the placeholder to the content. Without content the placeholder always shows.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Lines` | `int` | `3` | Placeholder text lines (Arc clamps to 1–6). Defaults to 3. |
| `IsAvatarVisible` | `bool` | `false` | Adds a round avatar placeholder before the lines. |
| `IsLoading` | `bool` | `true` | Keeps the placeholder visible while true; only used when `Content` is set. |
| `Label` | `string` | `"Loading content"` | Accessible name of the placeholder (Arc `label`, "Loading content"). |

Pseudo-classes: `:loading`

Derives from `ContentControl`: every member of `ContentControl` works as well.

## Accessibility

- `Label` is the accessible name while the placeholder shows. The default is "Loading content".
- The placeholder is a live region with Polite announcements, and its status reads "Loading".
- The placeholder shapes are not read. Give the real content its own labels once it loads.
- The control is not focusable and has no keyboard interaction.
- When the content is shown, the name and the status are cleared, so the loaded content is read as the page's own text.

### Keyboard

`Skeleton` takes no focus and has no keyboard interaction. Loading completes without moving the focus, so a field or a
button that the person was using keeps its focus when the content arrives.

## Motion

- The text lines and the avatar pulse from top to bottom in a calm wave. The wave runs about 20 seconds and then stops.
- When loading ends, the placeholder fades out, the content rises 4 px into place and the height springs to the content.
- Reduced motion stops the pulse, swaps the placeholder for the content with a short fade and does not animate the height.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| Placeholder pulse | Each block pulses in turn, 90 ms after the one above, on a 1.8 s cycle, 11 times (about 20 s), then rests | Stops | Stops |
| Loading ends | The placeholder fades out quickly and the content rises 4 px into place | A short fade between the placeholder and the content | Immediate |
| Height change | The height springs from the placeholder to the content | Not animated | Immediate |

### Using motion with restraint

The pulse is a finite wave, so a long load stops moving after about 20 seconds and the placeholder stays on screen. Do
not add a second moving element beside a skeleton, such as a shimmering banner or a spinner, because the page then has
two signs of loading that compete. A load that takes longer than the wave should show a status line that says what the
page is waiting for, and the placeholder can stay as it is. Reduced motion needs no extra code: the pulse stops and the
content swaps with a fade.

## Related

- `Progress` when the amount of work is known and can be reported.
- `EmptyState` when loading is done and there is nothing to show.
- `TextShimmer` for an inline status or an AI thinking state.
- `Avatar` for the loaded avatar that the placeholder stands for.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `Progress` | The amount of work is known and can be reported as a share |
| `EmptyState` | Loading has finished and there is no content to show |
| `TextShimmer` | A short line of text says the system is working |
| `Avatar` | The loaded identity is shown in the same place as the placeholder |
