# Avatar group

> Show a team or set of contributors in a small space.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/avatar-group

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.AvatarGroupTeamDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="16">
        <Border Padding="0,28,0,0">
            <arc:AvatarGroup x:Name="Group" Label="Editors" />
        </Border>
        <WrapPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center" ItemSpacing="12" LineSpacing="12">
            <arc:Button Content="Add person" Variant="Secondary" Click="OnAddClick" />
            <arc:Button Content="Remove person" Variant="Secondary" Click="OnRemoveClick" />
        </WrapPanel>
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Collections;
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class AvatarGroupTeamDemo : UserControl
{
    private static readonly string[] Names =
    [
        "Maya Chen", "Noah Park", "Leah Fox", "Omar Haddad", "Ines Duarte", "Kenji Sato", "Ava Brooks", "Luca Romano", "Zara Ali"
    ];

    private readonly AvaloniaList<AvatarGroupMember> _team = new()
    {
        new("Maya Chen", status: AvatarStatus.Online),
        new("Noah Park"),
        new("Leah Fox", status: AvatarStatus.Offline),
        new("Omar Haddad"),
        new("Ines Duarte"),
        new("Kenji Sato")
    };

    private int _next = 6;

    public AvatarGroupTeamDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Group.ItemsSource = _team;
    }

    // Joining and leaving animate the slot; the list is changed in place.
    private void OnAddClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        _team.Insert(1, new AvatarGroupMember(Names[_next++ % Names.Length]));
    }

    private void OnRemoveClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        if (_team.Count > 0)
        {
            _team.RemoveAt(Math.Min(1, _team.Count - 1));
        }
    }
}
```

## When to use

`AvatarGroup` shows a small set of people who own, edit or review one item: a header, a card or a table cell. The
avatars overlap, the first people are drawn in full and the rest fold into a "+N" chip, so the group keeps the same
footprint whether the team has four people or forty. It is display only; the names are read through the accessible
names or the list the group summarizes.

- **Editors on a shared document or pricing experiment**: the header of a page shows who is working on the item now,
  and the stack changes as people join or leave the session.
- **Reviewers on a pull request, invoice or contract** in a card: the first reviewers are visible and "+3" marks the
  rest, without a list that would take over the card.
- **Assignees in a table column** on a support ticket or a deal: `Size="Small"` keeps the column narrow while the owner
  of each row stays visible.
- **A project team panel that an admin edits while it is open**: when members are added or removed, the stack slides
  instead of jumping, so the change is visible without a refresh.
- **Watchers on a live record**, such as the people viewing an incident timeline: the first watchers show and a count
  covers the rest.

## When not to use

- **One person**: use `Avatar`, which carries the name and the status of a single person.
- **A list where each person's name and role must be read or compared**: use `Table` or a plain list.
- **A person's account actions** such as sign out or switch workspace: use `UserMenu`.
- **Choosing several people from a directory**: use `MultiSelect`, which searches and selects. A group only shows people.
- **Each person needs an action of their own**, such as Remove or Message: use `Table`, where each row can
  hold its own controls. The group is not focusable and has no per-person actions.

## Usage

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:AvatarGroup Label="Editors">
        <arc:AvatarGroupMember DisplayName="Maya Chen" Status="Online" />
        <arc:AvatarGroupMember DisplayName="Noah Park" />
        <arc:AvatarGroupMember DisplayName="Leah Fox" Status="Offline" />
    </arc:AvatarGroup>
</UserControl>
```

`AvatarGroup` derives from Avalonia's `TemplatedControl`. Its template is one panel that lays the people out and
draws the overflow chip, so the group has no focus and no pointer behavior of its own beyond the hover fan. Its
members are `AvatarGroupMember` objects; `Avatar` instances and plain strings are accepted too. The inline members
in the `Items` content are used until `ItemsSource` is set, and then `ItemsSource` takes over completely.

### Anatomy

1. **Stack** (the group): the people are placed from left to right with a 6 px overlap. Later people are drawn over
   earlier ones, so each avatar's left edge stays visible.
2. **Person slot**: each avatar has a 1 px ring in the `Border` color around it. The avatar itself has a 2 px
   `Surface` edge, which separates it from its neighbours. The ring darkens to the strong border color on hover.
3. **Avatar** (`AvatarGroupMember`): the member's photo or initials and optional status dot, at the group's size.
   The dot and its meaning are described in `Avatar`.
4. **Overflow chip**: a circle with the `SurfaceMuted` fill and `TextSecondary` text that shows "+N". Its text is
   10 px at `Small`, the Arc XS step at `Medium` and the Arc SM step at `Large`.
5. **Name pill**: a pill above the hovered person with the foreground color as its fill, the background color as its
   text, and 8 px horizontal and 4 px vertical padding.

The group's `Label` is not drawn. It names the group for assistive technology and builds the overflow label, so put
a visible heading beside the group when people need to read what it is.

### Bound members

Bind `ItemsSource` to a collection of `AvatarGroupMember`, `Avatar` or plain names. The collection takes precedence
over the inline `Items`.

```xml
<arc:AvatarGroup ItemsSource="{Binding Team}"
                 Label="Team members" />
```

### Binding to a view model

With CommunityToolkit.Mvvm, the view model owns the collection and the commands that change it, and the group only
displays it. `ItemsSource` is one-way: the group never edits the collection. `OverflowCount` is read only and is
computed from the collection and `MaxVisibleCount`. The group has no command or click event to bind to; the actions
belong to the view model or to the list beside the group.

```csharp
public partial class ProjectViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    public ObservableCollection<AvatarGroupMember> Editors { get; } = new()
    {
        new("Maya Chen", status: AvatarStatus.Online),
        new("Noah Park"),
        new("Leah Fox", status: AvatarStatus.Offline),
    };

    [ObservableProperty]
    private int _maxVisibleCount = 4;

    [RelayCommand]
    private void AddEditor(string name) => Editors.Add(new AvatarGroupMember(name));

    [RelayCommand]
    private void RemoveEditor(AvatarGroupMember member) => Editors.Remove(member);
}
```

```xml
<arc:AvatarGroup ItemsSource="{Binding Editors}"
                 MaxVisibleCount="{Binding MaxVisibleCount}"
                 Label="Editors" />
```

Joining and leaving animate the slot, and the list is updated in place, so use `Add`, `Insert` and `Remove` on the
collection. Replacing the whole collection makes every person leave and rejoin. To change how someone is shown, set
the `Status`, `DisplayName` or `Source` of the existing `AvatarGroupMember`; the avatar follows the change without a
slot animation.

```csharp
var team = new AvaloniaList<AvatarGroupMember>
{
    new("Maya Chen", status: AvatarStatus.Online),
    new("Noah Park"),
    new("Leah Fox", status: AvatarStatus.Offline),
};
group.ItemsSource = team;

// Joining and leaving animate the slot; the list is updated in place.
team.Insert(1, new AvatarGroupMember("Omar Haddad"));
team.RemoveAt(1);
```

### Overflow

`MaxVisibleCount` (4 by default) sets how many people show before the "+N" chip. `OverflowCount` reports the number
folded into the chip. The first people in the list are shown and the rest are counted, so put the most relevant
people first. Only the visible people get controls, so long lists stay cheap.

```xml
<arc:AvatarGroup ItemsSource="{Binding Team}"
                 MaxVisibleCount="3" />
```

The chip's accessible name is the overflow count followed by the lowercased `Label`, such as "2 more team members".

### Sizes

`Size` applies to every avatar and the overflow chip: `Small` is 28 px, `Medium` (the default) is 36 px and `Large` is
48 px. `XLarge` is drawn as `Large`, the largest group size the theme defines.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             xmlns:generic="using:System.Collections.Generic"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.AvatarGroupSizesAndLimitsDemo">
    <UserControl.Resources>
        <generic:List x:Key="Team" x:TypeArguments="arc:AvatarGroupMember">
            <arc:AvatarGroupMember DisplayName="Maya Chen" Status="Online" />
            <arc:AvatarGroupMember DisplayName="Noah Park" />
            <arc:AvatarGroupMember DisplayName="Leah Fox" Status="Offline" />
            <arc:AvatarGroupMember DisplayName="Omar Haddad" />
            <arc:AvatarGroupMember DisplayName="Ines Duarte" />
            <arc:AvatarGroupMember DisplayName="Kenji Sato" />
        </generic:List>
    </UserControl.Resources>
    <StackPanel Spacing="16">
        <arc:AvatarGroup ItemsSource="{StaticResource Team}" Size="Small" MaxVisibleCount="3" />
        <arc:AvatarGroup ItemsSource="{StaticResource Team}" Size="Medium" />
        <arc:AvatarGroup ItemsSource="{StaticResource Team}" Size="Large" MaxVisibleCount="5" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```xml
<arc:AvatarGroup ItemsSource="{Binding Team}" Size="Small" MaxVisibleCount="3" />
<arc:AvatarGroup ItemsSource="{Binding Team}" Size="Large" MaxVisibleCount="5" />
```

The group's width is fixed by its members and size: 6 px of padding plus each visible slot's width minus the overlap.
With four visible people and a chip at `Medium`, the group is 156 px wide, so measure the cell it goes into before
choosing `Large`.

### Inline members

Members can be written in place of a bound list. This suits a fixed set, such as the people on a static card.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.AvatarGroupInlineMembersDemo">
    <arc:AvatarGroup>
        <arc:AvatarGroupMember DisplayName="Ada Lovelace" />
        <arc:AvatarGroupMember DisplayName="Grace Hopper" />
        <arc:AvatarGroupMember DisplayName="Alan Turing" />
    </arc:AvatarGroup>
</UserControl>
```

### Data shape and performance

- **Entries**: each item is an `AvatarGroupMember`, an `Avatar` or a plain string. Null entries are skipped, so a
  list with gaps still counts correctly.
- **Visible work**: only the first `MaxVisibleCount` entries get avatars, plus one chip. A group over 500 members
  builds the same few controls as one over 5.
- **Identity**: entries are tracked by their object and by their occurrence, not by name. Two people with the same
  name are two slots, so a duplicate name does not break the animation. Keep one object per person.
- **Updates**: a live update needs a collection that raises change notifications, such as `AvaloniaList` or
  `ObservableCollection`. The group observes the source only while it is attached to the visual tree, so a detached
  group does not keep the list alive. With a plain list, assign a new collection to `ItemsSource` to refresh.
- **Animation**: joins and leaves animate only while the group is loaded and the motion level is Full. A group that
  is not loaded yet, or a page with reduced motion, takes the change at once.

### Example: project card with a team stack

A pricing project card in a SaaS planning tool lists the people working on the experiment. The title and the
description are on the left, and the group sits on the right, where the eye reads the team after the name. Six
editors are assigned, so four are drawn and the chip reads "+2". The first editor is online and the fifth is
offline, which tells a reviewer who is around to answer a question. The group's `Label` is "Editors", so the overflow
chip is named "2 more editors" for assistive technology.

![Project card header with six editors, four avatars shown and a +2 chip](https://docs.tkcode.si/shots/Docs/Avatars/AvatarGroup/images/AvatarGroupHeader.webp)

```xml
<Border Width="640"
        Padding="20"
        Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Surface}"
        BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Border}"
        BorderThickness="1"
        CornerRadius="12">
    <StackPanel Spacing="16">
        <Grid ColumnDefinitions="*,Auto">
            <StackPanel Spacing="4" VerticalAlignment="Center">
                <TextBlock Text="Q3 pricing experiment"
                           FontSize="16"
                           FontWeight="SemiBold"
                           Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
                <TextBlock Text="Shared with the growth and finance teams"
                           FontSize="12"
                           Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
            </StackPanel>
            <arc:AvatarGroup Grid.Column="1" Label="Editors" VerticalAlignment="Center">
                <arc:AvatarGroupMember DisplayName="Maya Chen" Status="Online" />
                <arc:AvatarGroupMember DisplayName="Noah Park" />
                <arc:AvatarGroupMember DisplayName="Leah Fox" Status="Offline" />
                <arc:AvatarGroupMember DisplayName="Omar Haddad" />
                <arc:AvatarGroupMember DisplayName="Ines Duarte" />
                <arc:AvatarGroupMember DisplayName="Kenji Sato" />
            </arc:AvatarGroup>
        </Grid>
        <Border Height="1" Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Border}" />
        <Grid ColumnDefinitions="*,Auto">
            <TextBlock Text="Last edited by Maya Chen on 18 Oct 2026"
                       FontSize="12"
                       VerticalAlignment="Center"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
            <arc:Button Grid.Column="1" Content="Invite editor" Variant="Secondary" />
        </Grid>
    </StackPanel>
</Border>
```

### Content guidelines

- **Label**: a plural noun for the role, in sentence case and without a colon: "Editors", "Reviewers", "Assignees".
  The label is not drawn, and it is read aloud, so the colon would be spoken.
- **Overflow phrase**: the chip reads the count, then "more", then the lowercased label. Choose a label that reads
  well after "more": "2 more reviewers" works, "2 more people" is vague when the group is about one role.
- **Heading**: put a visible sentence-case heading or a short line of text beside the group, such as "Editing now",
  because the group shows no words of its own.

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| `Label="People"` | `Label="Reviewers"`, so the chip reads "2 more reviewers" |
| `Label="Editors:"` | `Label="Editors"`, without the colon |
| `Label="Users"` | `Label="Assignees"` when the item has owners |
| `Label="team"` | `Label="Team members"`, a full noun phrase reads well after "more" |

### Best practices

**Do**

- Order the members so that the most relevant people come first. The overflow folds the tail of the list, so the
  people at the end are the ones a reader is least likely to see.
- Set `Label` to a plural noun for the role. The label is the accessible name of the group and the source of the
  overflow phrase, so one word serves both.
- Put a visible heading next to the group. The label is not drawn, so a sighted reader needs the words somewhere.
- Change `Status` on the existing `AvatarGroupMember` when presence changes. The avatar updates in place and the
  person keeps their slot, instead of leaving and rejoining the stack.

**Avoid**

- Replacing the whole collection on every refresh. Each replacement makes every person leave and join again, so the
  stack animates all of its slots at once.
- Relying on the hover name in a touch layout. Touch does not fan the stack or show the name, so the list beside it
  must carry the names.
- Placing a group with `Large` avatars in a narrow cell. Each person adds about 42 px at `Large`, and the group does not
  wrap or shrink, so the cell overflows.
- Setting `MaxVisibleCount` high to show everyone in a narrow area. The stack grows by one slot per visible person, so
  the width is set by the count and not by the space available.

### Common questions

**Why does the hover name not show on a touch screen?** The fan, the lifted person and the name pill respond only to
mouse and pen pointers. Touch input is ignored by design, so show the names in the list or card that holds the group
when touch matters.

**How do I show everyone without a "+N" chip?** Set `MaxVisibleCount` to the number of members or more. The overflow
count is then 0 and no chip is created.

**Why does my list change not appear in the group?** The group listens only to collections that raise change
notifications, such as `AvaloniaList` and `ObservableCollection`, and only while it is attached to the visual tree. A
plain `List` never reports a change. Assign a new collection to `ItemsSource`, or use an observable collection.

**Can two members have the same name?** Yes. Each member object is its own slot, and the group tracks objects, not
names. Both people are drawn and both count toward the overflow. Give each person their own `AvatarGroupMember`.

**How do I make a person clickable?** The group has no click event and takes no focus. Place a list, a table or
buttons beside it that act on the same collection, and use the group only to display who is on the item.

## API reference

### AvatarGroup

A team or set of contributors in a small space (Arc AvatarGroup): overlapping avatars with a 2px surface ring and a 1px border ring, later people stacked over earlier ones, and a "+N" chip for everyone past `MaxVisibleCount`. People who join or leave open or close their slot on the morph spring so the stack slides (P19); the overflow count rolls the way it moved (P14). Pointing at the stack (fine pointers only) loosens it from the center (P28) and lifts the person under the pointer with a crisp ring and their name while the neighbours ease aside (P27). Only the visible people get controls, so long member lists stay cheap. Items may be `AvatarGroupMember`, `Avatar` or plain names.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ItemsSource` | `IEnumerable?` | `null` | Bound members (`AvatarGroupMember`, `Avatar` or names); takes precedence over `Items`. |
| `MaxVisibleCount` | `int` | `4` | People shown before the rest fold into the overflow count (Arc `max`, 4). |
| `Size` | `AvatarSize` | `Medium` | Avatar size: Small 28, Medium 36, Large 48 (XLarge is treated as Large). |
| `Label` | `string` | `"Team members"` | Accessible name of the group, also used for the overflow chip ("2 more team members"). |
| `OverflowCount` | `int` | – | *Read-only.* How many people are folded into the "+N" chip. |

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

### AvatarGroupMember

One person in an `AvatarGroup` (Arc `members[]` entry).

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `DisplayName` | `string?` | `null` | The person's name: initials, tooltip and accessible name. |
| `Source` | `ImageSource?` | `null` | Optional photo; initials show while it loads or when it fails. |
| `Status` | `AvatarStatus` | `None` | Optional online / offline dot. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

## Accessibility

- The group is named by `Label`. Each avatar keeps its own name and status for assistive technology.
- The overflow chip is an image named from `Label`, such as "2 more team members".
- The stack has no keyboard behavior and is not focusable. Use the list or table that the group summarizes for
  keyboard work.
- The hover name is visual only: the name of each person is also in the accessible name of the avatar.
- Touch input does not fan the stack or show a name, so the names must also be visible in the layout that holds the
  group when touch is a supported input.

### Keyboard

The group takes no focus and has no keyboard commands, so `Tab` skips it. The people are reachable through the list,
table or form that the group summarizes, where each person can be focused and acted on.

## Motion

- When someone joins or leaves, their slot grows or shrinks on a morph spring while it fades and scales slightly, so
  the stack slides instead of jumping.
- The overflow count rolls up when it grows and down when it shrinks.
- With the pointer over the stack, the people loosen from the center, the person under the pointer rises a little
  and shows a ring and their name, and the neighbours move aside.
- Reduced motion removes the hover spread and keeps the ring and name; the count fades. Off changes everything at once.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| A person joins | Their slot opens on the morph spring and the stack slides | Shown at once | Immediate |
| A person leaves | Their slot closes on the morph spring while they fade and scale | Removed at once | Immediate |
| The overflow count changes | Rolls up or down with the change | Fades | Immediate |
| The pointer moves over the stack | People fan out 4 px per step, the hovered person rises 2 px and neighbours move 3 px | No fan; ring and name stay | Immediate |
| The name above the hovered person | Shows after a 60 ms delay | Shows at once | Immediate |

## Related

- `Avatar` for one person.
- `UserMenu` when the group member's avatar opens account actions.
- `Table` when names, roles and other columns must be compared.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `Avatar` | One person is shown next to a name, a comment or a record |
| `UserMenu` | An avatar opens sign out, profile or workspace actions |
| `Table` | Names, roles and other columns must be read and compared |
| `MultiSelect` | People are searched and selected from a directory |
| `Badge` | The label is a status or category rather than a set of people |
| `ChatThread` | The people are the authors of a conversation |

---

# Badge

> A small label for status, category, or metadata.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/badge

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.BadgeTonesDemo">
    <WrapPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center" ItemSpacing="12" LineSpacing="12">
        <arc:Badge Content="Draft" />
        <arc:Badge Tone="Success" Content="Live" />
        <arc:Badge Tone="Info" Content="Beta" />
        <arc:Badge Tone="Warning" Content="Degraded" />
        <arc:Badge Tone="Danger" Content="Failed" />
    </WrapPanel>
</UserControl>
```

## When to use

`Badge` is a small pill that names a state, a category or a piece of metadata. It sits beside a title or inside a
table cell, where it can be read in a glance and compared with the badges in the rows around it. It is inline text
with a tone: it does not take focus, open anything or announce itself, and its label must say the state on its own.

- **Order and invoice status in a billing table**: a `Small` badge reads "Paid", "Pending" or "Failed" in each row, so
  an operator can scan a page of invoices without opening one.
- **Deployment and environment labels** on a release page: "Live" in the success tone beside the production version,
  "Beta" in the accent tone beside a preview build, and "Draft" for work not yet published.
- **Metadata on a card or a detail header**: a plan name, a region or a "New" marker next to a customer name, where
  the label is a fact about the item and not an action.
- **A counter that changes while the page is open**: an unread count or a number of open tickets beside a menu item.
  The badge stays mounted, so the new number rises in place and the pill widens to fit.
- **A row marker with a leading icon** in an activity or incident timeline: the icon names the kind of event, and the
  tone says whether it is good, pending or failed.

## When not to use

- **A full sentence of feedback**, such as "Your card was declined": use `Alert` for a message that stays on the page,
  or `Toast` for one that goes away on its own.
- **A value the user switches on and off**, such as a filter or a tag they choose: use `ChipGroup`, which handles
  selection and keyboard focus.
- **A large number with context around it**, such as revenue this quarter: use `MetricCard`, which gives the number
  room and a caption.
- **A person's presence**, such as online or offline: use the status dot on `Avatar`. A badge names a state; it does
  not sit on a person's photo.
- **A count or state that the user must act on from the badge**: use a `Button` or a `Tabs` item, because a badge
  takes no focus and has no click behavior.

## Usage

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:Badge Content="Draft" />
</UserControl>
```

`Badge` derives from Avalonia's `ContentControl`, so `Content` can be any object. Strings and numbers get the in-place
animation described below; other content is shown as it is, without the swap. The pill's fill, border and text come
from the tone and the theme, so set `Tone` and `Size` rather than the brushes.

### Anatomy

1. **Pill** (the control itself): a 1 px border with the pill radius. The minimum height is 26 px at `Medium` and
   22 px at `Small`; the pill grows with its label.
2. **Tone ring** (`Info` only): an accent ring laid over the border at 24% opacity.
3. **Hover wash** (`Info` only): a 10% accent wash over the surface, with the ring at 32%, while the pointer is over
   the badge.
4. **Icon** (`Icon`, leading): an optional glyph in the tone color. It is hidden from assistive technology.
5. **Label** (`Content`): the text in medium weight. Keep it to one or two words, because the pill widens with it and
   a long label pushes its neighbours in a table.

Padding is 10 px on each side at `Medium` and 8 px at `Small`. The gap between the icon and the label is 5 px at
`Medium` and 4 px at `Small`.

### Tones

`Tone` sets the color treatment. `Neutral` is the default. The label must name the state by itself, because the
tone is not the only signal, and printed or grayscale reports lose color.

| Tone | Text | Fill | Border | Use it for |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Neutral` | Secondary text color | Muted surface | Border color | Draft, archived, metadata |
| `Success` | Success color | Success tint, 10% into the surface | Success tint, 25% into the border | Live, paid, passing, healthy |
| `Info` | Strong accent | Subtle accent | Border with a 24% accent ring | Beta, syncing, accent emphasis |
| `Warning` | Warning color | Warning tint, 11% into the surface | Warning tint, 27% into the border | Pending, degraded, expiring |
| `Danger` | Danger color | Danger tint, 10% into the surface | Danger tint, 26% into the border | Failed, overdue, blocked |

The success, warning and danger fills are fixed mixes of the state color into the neutral surface, so they keep their
meaning when the accent changes. `Info` follows the accent, which is why it is the tone for accent emphasis and not
for a state that must always look the same.

### Sizes

`Size` sets the height: `Medium` (the default) is 26 px and `Small` is 22 px. Use `Small` in dense tables and
`Medium` beside headings and in cards.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.BadgeSmallDemo">
    <WrapPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center" ItemSpacing="12" LineSpacing="12">
        <arc:Badge Size="Small" Content="Draft" />
        <arc:Badge Size="Small" Tone="Success" Content="Live" />
        <arc:Badge Size="Small" Tone="Info" Content="Beta" />
        <arc:Badge Size="Small" Tone="Warning" Content="Degraded" />
        <arc:Badge Size="Small" Tone="Danger" Content="Failed" />
    </WrapPanel>
</UserControl>
```

| Size | Minimum height | Side padding | Label | Icon gap |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Medium` | 26 px | 10 px | Arc XS | 5 px |
| `Small` | 22 px | 8 px | 11 px | 4 px |

Use one size for each table column or group, so the rows keep the same height. A table cell of a fixed width fits a
`Small` badge with a one-word label and an icon.

### Icon

`Icon` takes a leading icon. It takes the tone color and is hidden from assistive technology. The example uses an
`ArcGlyph` from `ArcIcons`, the Arc icon set, at 12 px.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.BadgeIconsDemo">
    <WrapPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center" ItemSpacing="12" LineSpacing="12">
        <arc:Badge Tone="Success" Content="Passing">
            <arc:Badge.Icon>
                <arc:ArcGlyph Data="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Check}" Size="12" />
            </arc:Badge.Icon>
        </arc:Badge>
        <arc:Badge Tone="Info" Content="Synced">
            <arc:Badge.Icon>
                <arc:ArcGlyph Data="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.RefreshCw}" Size="12" />
            </arc:Badge.Icon>
        </arc:Badge>
        <arc:Badge Tone="Danger" Content="Blocked">
            <arc:Badge.Icon>
                <arc:ArcGlyph Data="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.TriangleAlert}" Size="12" />
            </arc:Badge.Icon>
        </arc:Badge>
    </WrapPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```csharp
badge.Tone = BadgeTone.Success;
badge.Content = "Passing";
badge.Icon = new ArcGlyph { Data = ArcIcons.Check, Size = 12 };
```

Add the icon when the glyph adds information, such as a warning triangle for a failed check. A decorative icon on
every badge makes a table noisy, and the same tone already carries the color.

### Changing in place

Keep the badge mounted and change `Content`. A new string or number rises in from a soft blur, the old one lifts away,
and the pill width springs to fit. Re-creating the badge loses this motion and builds a new control for every change.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.BadgeChangingInPlaceDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="16">
        <WrapPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center" ItemSpacing="12" LineSpacing="12">
            <arc:Badge x:Name="Deploy" Tone="Info" Content="Queued">
                <arc:Badge.Icon>
                    <arc:ArcGlyph Data="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Clock}" Size="12" />
                </arc:Badge.Icon>
            </arc:Badge>
            <arc:Badge x:Name="Comments" Content="3" />
        </WrapPanel>
        <WrapPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center" ItemSpacing="12" LineSpacing="12">
            <arc:Button Content="Next state" Variant="Secondary" Click="OnNextStateClick" />
            <arc:Button Content="Add comment" Variant="Secondary" Click="OnAddCommentClick" />
        </WrapPanel>
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;
using Avalonia.Media;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class BadgeChangingInPlaceDemo : UserControl
{
    private static readonly (string Text, BadgeTone Tone, Geometry Icon)[] States =
    [
        ("Queued", BadgeTone.Info, ArcIcons.Clock),
        ("Deploying", BadgeTone.Warning, ArcIcons.LoaderCircle),
        ("Live", BadgeTone.Success, ArcIcons.Check),
        ("Rolled back", BadgeTone.Danger, ArcIcons.RotateCcw)
    ];

    private int _state;
    private int _comments = 3;

    public BadgeChangingInPlaceDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
    }

    private void OnNextStateClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        var (text, tone, icon) = States[_state = (_state + 1) % States.Length];
        Deploy.Content = text;
        Deploy.Tone = tone;
        Deploy.Icon = new ArcGlyph { Data = icon, Size = 12 };
    }

    private void OnAddCommentClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        Comments.Content = ++_comments;
    }
}
```

A new icon pops in from a slightly smaller size. A change caused by a font or a theme change, rather than by new
content, takes effect at once, so the layout does not play a spring when nothing about the state changed.

### Binding to a view model

`Badge` only displays its values. Bind `Content`, `Tone`, `Size` and `Icon` from the view model; the badge never
writes a value back and raises no events or commands for the view model to handle.

```csharp
public partial class DeploymentViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    [ObservableProperty]
    private string _statusText = "Queued";

    [ObservableProperty]
    private BadgeTone _statusTone = BadgeTone.Info;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private int _commentCount;
}
```

```xml
<StackPanel Orientation="Horizontal" Spacing="8">
    <arc:Badge Tone="{Binding StatusTone}" Content="{Binding StatusText}" />
    <arc:Badge Tone="Neutral" Content="{Binding CommentCount}" />
</StackPanel>
```

Set these properties on the UI thread, because Avalonia properties must change there. When the state changes, update
the text and the tone together, so the label and its color move in the same frame.

### Data shape and performance

A badge is cheap for a few labels and costs more in a long table. Each badge measures its own width to spring to fit
its label, so a table with thousands of badges on screen does more layout work than a table of plain text. In long
tables:

- Use `Small` and a one-word label, so the width changes little when the value changes.
- Keep the rows virtualized, as the Avalonia `ListBox` and `DataGrid` do by default, so only visible rows create
  badges.
- Format numbers in the code that owns them, with `ToString("N0", culture)` or a formatted string, so the
  separators match the locale: "1,204" in English and "1.204" in German.

### Example: invoice status table

A billing operations page lists the invoices sent this week. Each row names the customer and shows the status as a
`Small` badge. Paid invoices use the success tone and need no icon. A pending invoice gets a clock icon, and a failed
one gets a warning triangle, because a failed payment needs a person to act and the icon adds a second signal. The draft
row uses the neutral tone so it reads as "not sent yet" and not as a problem.

![Invoice status table with paid, pending, failed and draft badges in a Small size](https://docs.tkcode.si/shots/Docs/Avatars/Badge/images/BadgeStatusTable.webp)

```xml
<Border Width="640"
        Padding="20"
        Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Surface}"
        BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Border}"
        BorderThickness="1"
        CornerRadius="12">
    <StackPanel Spacing="14">
        <TextBlock Text="Invoices sent this week"
                   FontSize="16"
                   FontWeight="SemiBold"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
        <Grid ColumnDefinitions="176,*,Auto">
            <TextBlock Text="Invoice" FontSize="12"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
            <TextBlock Grid.Column="1" Text="Customer" FontSize="12"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
            <TextBlock Grid.Column="2" Text="Status" FontSize="12"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />

```

### Content guidelines

- **Label**: one or two words that name the state or category, in sentence case and without punctuation: "Paid",
  "Pending", "Live". The badge is read as its own name, so it must make sense without the color.
- **Numbers**: a count is a number in digits, formatted for the locale ("1,204"), and it stays short enough that the
  pill does not grow past its neighbours.
- **Tone**: pick the tone from the meaning of the state, not from the look you want. Danger means a person must act;
  Warning means a state needs attention soon; Success means the state is good.

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| `Content="LIVE NOW!!"` | `Content="Live"` |
| `Content="Status: failed"` | `Content="Failed"`, the row gives the context |
| `Content="Your card was declined"` | Use `Alert`; a badge holds a word or a short phrase |
| `Content="1204"` | `Content="1,204"`, formatted for the locale |
| `Tone="Danger"` on a neutral count | `Tone="Neutral"`, since red means action is needed |

### Best practices

**Do**

- Name the state in the label. The tone is a color, so color-blind readers and grayscale prints lose it when the label
  is vague.
- Keep the badge mounted and change `Content` and `Tone` when the state changes. The label rises in place and the pill
  springs to its new width, which tells the reader that something changed.
- Use one size in each column or group. Equal row heights keep a table scannable.
- Reserve `Danger` for failures and actions the person must take, and `Info` for accent emphasis. Mixed meanings
  across screens make people stop trusting the colors.

**Avoid**

- Using a badge for a sentence. A sentence needs room to wrap and an action to dismiss it, which `Alert` and `Toast`
  provide.
- Re-creating the badge for each state. A new control loses the in-place motion and builds layout for every change.
- Adding a long label or a large icon in a narrow table cell. The pill widens with the label and pushes the cells
  around it.
- Expecting a click. A badge does not take focus, so a status that the person must open needs a `Button` or a row
  action beside it.
- Announcing every change from the badge. A badge does not announce its own changes, so put it in a live region of
  the surrounding content when a change must be read aloud.

### Common questions

**Why does my count not animate?** The badge was probably re-created, or its `Content` is not a string or a number.
Only strings and numeric types get the in-place swap. Keep the same badge on screen and set `Content` to a string or a
number.

**Can a badge sit on an avatar as a count or a dot?** No. The badge is a standalone pill, not an overlay on another
element. For presence on a person, use the status dot on `Avatar`.

**Why does the Info tone change with the accent but Success does not?** `Info` is derived from the accent color, so it
follows the product's accent. Success, warning and danger are fixed tints of the state colors into the neutral
surface, so they keep their meaning when the accent changes.

**How do I change the tone from code?** Set `Tone` on the instance, for example `badge.Tone = BadgeTone.Warning;`. With
full motion the colors crossfade; with reduced motion the change is instant.

**Can I make the badge clickable?** Not directly. The badge is not focusable and has no click event. Put it in a
`Button` or a row that handles the action, and keep the badge as its visual label.

## API reference

### Badge

A small pill for status, category or metadata (Arc Badge): a tone, an optional leading icon and a short label. It is a standalone inline label, not a count overlay. When a string or number label changes while the badge stays mounted, the new text rises out of a soft blur, the old one lifts away, and the pill width springs to fit (P2, P5); a new icon pops in from 0.6. Other content is shown as is. Reduced motion crossfades and the width jumps.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Tone` | `BadgeTone` | `Neutral` | Color treatment (Arc `tone`, neutral by default). |
| `Size` | `BadgeSize` | `Medium` | Medium (26px, default) or Small (22px). |
| `Icon` | `object?` | `null` | Leading icon (for example an `ArcGlyph`); it takes the tone color and is hidden from assistive technology. |

Pseudo-classes: `:text`, `:icon`

Derives from `ContentControl`: every member of `ContentControl` works as well.

## Accessibility

- The badge is inline text: its label is read with the text around it.
- The icon is hidden from assistive technology. The label must say the state, not the color.
- A string or number label is the badge's accessible name. A number is named with the current culture.
- While a label changes, the old text is hidden from assistive technology and only the current text is read.
- A badge does not announce its changes. If a change must be announced, put the badge in a live region of the
  surrounding content.
- The badge is not focusable and has no keyboard behavior: `Tab` skips it, and the row or control that holds the badge
  carries any keyboard work.

## Motion

- A new label rises from a soft blur, and the old one lifts away with a subtle blur. The pill width follows on a
  morph spring.
- A new icon pops in from a slightly smaller size. A size change caused by a font change happens at once.
- Reduced motion fades the label quickly and jumps the width. Off changes everything at once.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| The label changes | The old text lifts away with a subtle blur and the new text rises from a soft blur | Quick fade | Immediate |
| The pill width after a label change | Springs to fit the new label | Jumps to the new width | Immediate |
| The tone changes | Background, border and text crossfade on the standard curve | Instant | Immediate |
| The pointer enters or leaves (fine pointers) | Background and border crossfade; `Info` fades its accent wash | Instant | Immediate |
| A font or theme change re-sizes the badge | Happens at once | Happens at once | Immediate |

## Related

- `Alert` or `Toast` for a sentence of feedback.
- `ChipGroup` for values the user can select.
- `MetricCard` for a large value with its context.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `Alert` | A message needs a sentence and stays on the page |
| `Toast` | A short confirmation or error should appear and go away on its own |
| `ChipGroup` | The user selects or clears values |
| `MetricCard` | A large number needs its label, trend and context |
| `Avatar` | The status belongs to a person, shown as a dot on the photo |
| `Table` | The badges sit in columns that the person sorts and compares |

## When to use

`Card` is the tile for a browsable collection: a grid of projects, listings, posts or workspaces where each item has
a visual, a title, an owner and a status that changes over time. It groups those parts and the few actions that
belong to the item into one contained surface, so a grid reads as a set of equal units. A card can also open a quick
look, which grows the tile into a larger view of the same item without leaving the page.

- **Project and workspace grids** in an admin console: a card per project with its cover image, the owner's avatar
  and a status such as "Updated 2 hours ago". The footer holds one action, such as "Open project".
- **Catalog and listing tiles** in a storefront or an internal product catalog: a product photo, a name, a short line
  of copy and a trailing button. The media is the visual anchor of each tile.
- **Quick look at a record** in a CRM or a case-management grid: a card for a customer or a ticket opens to show its
  open questions and milestones. The grid keeps its place, and the person returns to the same tile when the view
  closes.
- **Live state on a tile** in a billing or deployment dashboard: a card whose `Status` changes as a job runs ("Syncing
  12 of 40 invoices", then "Synced just now"). New words rise in one after another and are announced politely.
- **Feeds of posts and release notes** in a developer portal or an editorial tool: a card per post with a byline
  (`Meta`) and a footer action, without the weight of a full table.

## When not to use

- **A single number with context** such as revenue, a conversion rate or open incidents: use `MetricCard`, which
  holds the value, its change and a sparkline.
- **Content that expands in place** without a dialog, such as a settings group that opens under its header: use
  `ExpandableCard`.
- **A modal with no tile to grow from**, such as a confirmation or a form opened from a toolbar button: use `Dialog`.
- **Triage of one item at a time** where people accept or reject each card: use `CardStack`, which handles drag,
  keys and undo for a deck of cards.
- **Many records compared by columns** such as invoices with amounts, dates and statuses: use `Table`. Cards hide the
  columns that make rows comparable.
- **A grid or list with nothing in it yet**: show `EmptyState` in the grid area. An empty card is not a message.

## Usage

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:Card Title="Harbour redesign"
              Description="New booking flow and room pages."
              Width="280" />
</UserControl>
```

`Card` derives from Avalonia's `ContentControl`. `Title` and `Description` give it the heading and the supporting line,
and `Content` takes anything else, placed between the description and the footer. Each optional part is a typed
property, so a card with an avatar, a status and an action needs no extra layout: the card arranges the footer, hides
the parts that are empty and keeps the same spacing across a grid.

### Anatomy

1. **Media** (`Media`): an image or visual at the top, with a minimum height of 112 px. It is hidden while the
   property is empty.
2. **Title** (`Title`): 18 px, medium weight, 1.3 line height, at heading level 3. With `Details` set, the title
   becomes a button that opens the quick look.
3. **Description** (`Description`): 14 px body text, 8 px under the title. Its line length is capped at about 34
   digit widths, so longer copy wraps to more lines instead of stretching the card.
4. **Content** (`Content`): any element between the description and the footer, such as a list of tags or a progress
   bar. It is hidden while `Content` is empty.
5. **Footer**: 20 px below the content. It appears when `Avatar`, `Meta`, `Status` or `Action` has a value.
6. **Avatar** (`Avatar`): a leading slot 32 px wide for the owner's `Avatar` control, with 12 px gaps to the byline and
   the action.
7. **Byline** (`Meta` and `Status`): `Meta` is the owner's line in 12 px text. `Status` sits under it on a single line
   that clips at the edge and ends in an ellipsis when it is too long.
8. **Action** (`Action`): a trailing control, usually a small button. It keeps its own focus and click target and does
   not open the quick look.
9. **Surface**: a 1 px border on the surface color, 26 px corners and 20 px of content padding. The shadow is off at
   rest and appears on hover.

### Parts and combinations

Arc has no `Variant` property for the card. Its variants are combinations of the optional parts, chosen per item.

| Combination | Parts to set | Use it for |
|---|---|---|
| Plain | `Title`, `Description` | A reference tile, a link list, a summary without a visual |
| Media and byline | `Media`, `Avatar`, `Meta` | Grids where every item has a picture and an owner |
| Live | `Status` on top of the above | Items whose state changes while the page is open |
| Interactive | `Details` on top of the above | Items that open to show more, such as a record or a project brief |

A plain card with only a title and a description is under 80 px high at a width of 240 px, so a grid of plain cards
stays dense. Do not mix plain and media cards in one row unless their heights match: the grid cell stretches the card,
and empty space below short copy looks like a layout error.

### Media, owner and footer

Give every card in a grid the same media height, so the titles line up across the row. Pass a `Small` avatar in the
`Avatar` slot, which is sized for the 32 px slot. `Meta` is the owner's name; use one line of text. The action is one
control. If a card needs a second action, place it in `Content` or in `Details`, so the footer keeps one trailing
target.

```xml
<arc:Card Title="Harbour redesign"
          Description="New booking flow and room pages."
          Meta="Maya Chen"
          Status="Updated 2 hours ago"
          Width="280">
    <arc:Card.Media>
        <Border Height="132" Background="#5B8DEF" />
    </arc:Card.Media>
    <arc:Card.Avatar>
        <arc:Avatar DisplayName="Maya Chen" Size="Small" />
    </arc:Card.Avatar>
    <arc:Card.Action>
        <arc:Button Content="Share" Variant="Ghost" Size="Small" />
    </arc:Card.Action>
</arc:Card>
```

### Status

`Status` is a short line such as "Updated 2 hours ago". When the text changes, the old line lifts away and the new
words rise in one after another, about 40 ms apart. The line is drawn with cached text and creates no controls per
word, so a card that updates often stays light.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.CardStatusUpdatesDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12">
        <arc:Card x:Name="Digest"
                  Title="Weekly digest"
                  Description="Highlights from every team, every Friday."
                  Meta="Lin Park"
                  Status="Updated 2 hours ago"
                  Width="300"
                  HorizontalAlignment="Center">
            <arc:Card.Avatar>
                <arc:Avatar DisplayName="Lin Park" Size="Small" />
            </arc:Card.Avatar>
        </arc:Card>
        <arc:Button Content="Change status"
                    Variant="Secondary"
                    Size="Small"
                    HorizontalAlignment="Center"
                    Click="OnChangeStatusClick" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class CardStatusUpdatesDemo : UserControl
{
    private static readonly string[] Steps =
    [
        "Updated just now",
        "Edited 1 minute ago",
        "Published to 4 teams",
        "Updated 2 hours ago"
    ];

    private int _step;

    public CardStatusUpdatesDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
    }

    private void OnChangeStatusClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
        => Digest.Status = Steps[_step++ % Steps.Length];
}
```

```xml
<arc:Card Title="Weekly digest"
          Description="Highlights from every team, every Friday."
          Status="{Binding LastUpdate}"
          Width="300" />
```

Write the status as a fact with a time: "Syncing 12 of 40 invoices", "Published to 4 teams", "Updated 2 hours ago".
Change the string only when the state changes; re-setting the same text on a timer replays the animation and conveys
nothing new. Setting `Status` to `null` or an empty string hides the line. The roll plays only when an existing status
is replaced, so the first value appears at once.

### Quick look

Set `Details` and the title becomes a button, and the whole card becomes a trigger: a press on the card that is not on
a nested control opens the quick look. The surface, media, title, description, byline and action fly into a larger
view on the same page, and the details rise in after them.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.CardControlledDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12">
        <arc:Card x:Name="Plan"
                  Title="Quarterly plan"
                  Description="Goals, owners and dates for the next three months."
                  Width="280"
                  HorizontalAlignment="Center"
                  DetailsOpenChanged="OnDetailsOpenChanged">
            <arc:Card.Media>
                <Border>
                    <Border.Background>
                        <LinearGradientBrush StartPoint="0%,0%" EndPoint="100%,100%">
                            <GradientStop Color="#4A5568" Offset="0" />
                            <GradientStop Color="#A0AEC0" Offset="1" />
                        </LinearGradientBrush>
                    </Border.Background>
                </Border>
            </arc:Card.Media>
            <arc:Card.Details>
                <TextBlock Text="Opened from code: IsDetailsOpen is two-way, so a binding or a button can open and close the quick look."
                           FontSize="14"
                           TextWrapping="Wrap"
                           Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
            </arc:Card.Details>
        </arc:Card>
        <WrapPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center" ItemSpacing="12" LineSpacing="12">
            <arc:Button Content="Open quick look" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Click="OnOpenClick" />
            <TextBlock x:Name="Log"
                       Text="Closed"
                       FontSize="13"
                       TextWrapping="Wrap"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
        </WrapPanel>
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class CardControlledDemo : UserControl
{
    public CardControlledDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
    }

    private void OnOpenClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) => Plan.IsDetailsOpen = true;

    private void OnDetailsOpenChanged(object? sender, CardDetailsOpenChangedEventArgs e)
        => Log.Text = e.IsOpen ? "Open" : $"Closed ({e.Reason})";
}
```

```xml
<arc:Card Title="Quarterly plan"
          Description="Goals, owners and dates for the next three months."
          IsDetailsOpen="{Binding IsPlanOpen, Mode=TwoWay}"
          Width="280">
    <arc:Card.Details>
        <TextBlock Text="Opened from code: IsDetailsOpen is two-way." TextWrapping="Wrap" />
    </arc:Card.Details>
</arc:Card>
```

`Details` holds the content of the larger view and can be any control. The quick look is 480 px wide at most, and the
window keeps a 16 px gutter around it. Keep the details to what a person needs to decide whether to open the record:
a summary, the next step and one or two links. A full editing form belongs in `Dialog` or on a page.

The quick look repeats the card's copy and footer (its title is 22 px, the media sits on top with a floating close
button), so the same text is not written twice. Put only the extra material in `Details`.

Use `OpenDetails()` and `CloseDetails()` to open and close the quick look from code, and `DetailsOpenChanged` to learn
why it changed. `IsDetailsOpen` is two-way, so a binding can open or close it, and the event reports every change.

```csharp
card.DetailsOpenChanged += (_, e) => log.Text = e.IsOpen ? "Open" : $"Closed ({e.Reason})";
card.OpenDetails();
card.CloseDetails();
```

The reason is `Programmatic` for a change made by code, `CloseButton` for the close button, `Escape` for the Escape
key and `PressOutside` for a press on the scrim behind the quick look.

### Without a quick look

Without `Details` the title is a plain heading and the card only lifts on hover. The title takes no focus and a press
on the card does nothing, so the only stops are the controls inside the card. Use this form for tiles that show
information or hold a footer action.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.CardWithoutQuickLookDemo">
    <WrapPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center" ItemSpacing="12" LineSpacing="12">
        <arc:Card Title="Plain card"
                  Description="A title and a line of copy, nothing else."
                  Width="240"
                  VerticalAlignment="Top" />
        <arc:Card Title="Design review"
                  Description="Thursday, 14:00 · Room 3"
                  Meta="Six people"
                  Width="260"
                  VerticalAlignment="Top">
            <arc:Card.Action>
                <arc:Button Content="Join" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" />
            </arc:Card.Action>
        </arc:Card>
        <arc:Card Title="Spring palette"
                  Width="240"
                  VerticalAlignment="Top">
            <arc:Card.Media>
                <Border>
                    <Border.Background>
                        <LinearGradientBrush StartPoint="0%,0%" EndPoint="100%,100%">
                            <GradientStop Color="#B07CE8" Offset="0" />
                            <GradientStop Color="#F3B6D8" Offset="1" />
                        </LinearGradientBrush>
                    </Border.Background>
                </Border>
            </arc:Card.Media>
            <TextBlock Text="Twelve swatches tuned for print and screen."
                       FontSize="14"
                       TextWrapping="Wrap"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
        </arc:Card>
    </WrapPanel>
</UserControl>
```

### Binding to a view model

A project grid binds one card per item. The view model owns each item's state and the card shows it. With
CommunityToolkit.Mvvm, an `ObservableObject` holds the properties and an `ObservableCollection<T>` feeds the grid.

```csharp
public partial class ProjectCardViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    public ProjectCardViewModel(string title, string owner)
    {
        _title = title;
        _owner = owner;
    }

    [ObservableProperty]
    private string _title;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private string _owner;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private string? _status;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private bool _isBriefOpen;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private string? _brief;

    [RelayCommand]
    private async Task ShareAsync()
    {
        await _sharing.ShareAsync(Title);
    }
}

public partial class ProjectsViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    public ObservableCollection<ProjectCardViewModel> Projects { get; } = new();
}
```

```xml
<ItemsControl ItemsSource="{Binding Projects}">
    <ItemsControl.ItemsPanel>
        <ItemsPanelTemplate>
            <WrapPanel ItemSpacing="16" LineSpacing="16" />
        </ItemsPanelTemplate>
    </ItemsControl.ItemsPanel>
    <ItemsControl.ItemTemplate>
        <DataTemplate>
            <arc:Card Title="{Binding Title}"
                      Description="{Binding Brief}"
                      Meta="{Binding Owner}"
                      Status="{Binding Status}"
                      IsDetailsOpen="{Binding IsBriefOpen, Mode=TwoWay}"
                      Width="280"
                      VerticalAlignment="Top">
                <arc:Card.Action>
                    <arc:Button Content="Share" Variant="Ghost" Size="Small"
                                Command="{Binding ShareCommand}" />
                </arc:Card.Action>
                <arc:Card.Details>
                    <TextBlock Text="{Binding Brief}" TextWrapping="Wrap" />
                </arc:Card.Details>
            </arc:Card>
        </DataTemplate>
    </ItemsControl.ItemTemplate>
</ItemsControl>
```

- `Title`, `Description`, `Meta` and `Status` are one-way: the view model owns them and the card does not write them.
- `IsDetailsOpen` is two-way: a press or the close button writes `False` back, and code can set it to open the quick
  look. Bind it with `Mode=TwoWay` only when the view model must know that the person closed the view.
- Use `DetailsOpenChanged` for a side effect that needs the reason, such as saving a draft after `Escape`. Use the
  binding for the state itself.
- The `Action` is a normal button with its own `Command`. Its press does not open the quick look.
- Compiled bindings need `x:DataType` on the template and the view. The examples leave it out of the view for brevity.

### Data shape and performance

A quick look is created the first time it opens, so a grid whose cards nobody opens pays nothing extra for
`Details`. Keep the `Details` content light: it is built on the first open. For long collections, host the cards in a virtualizing panel, so off-screen cards are not created.

Set the width on the card or on its grid column. The card fills the cell it is given (its minimum width is 0), so a
fixed width of 260 to 300 px gives a regular grid, and a `UniformGrid` keeps columns equal as the window resizes.

### Focus and dismissal

A card with `Details` is one tab stop: the title button. Enter or Space on it opens the quick look, and focus moves to
the close button inside. While the quick look is open, Tab and Shift+Tab stay inside it, so the page behind is not
reachable by keyboard. Escape, a press on the scrim and the close button all close it, and closing returns focus to
the title. The close button is named "Close quick look" by default; set `CloseButtonName` when the copy needs to say
what closes, for example "Close project brief".

A press on the `Action` button runs its command and does not open the quick look. If the card leaves the window while
the quick look is open, the quick look is removed and `IsDetailsOpen` becomes `False`.

### Example: project grid in a workspace

A project list on a workspace home page. Each card shows a cover, the owner and the last update, and the footer holds
one "Open" action. The titles are nouns, the descriptions are one sentence, and the status is a fact with a
time. Both cards share one width and align at the top, so the row reads as one set.

![Two project cards in a workspace grid, one with a live status line](https://docs.tkcode.si/shots/Docs/Cards/Card/images/ProjectGrid.webp)

```xml
<StackPanel Width="640" Orientation="Horizontal" Spacing="20">
    <arc:Card Title="Harbour redesign"
              Description="New booking flow and room pages for the 2026 release."
              Meta="Maya Chen"
              Status="Updated 2 hours ago"
              Width="300"
              VerticalAlignment="Top">
        <arc:Card.Media>
            <Border Height="132">
                <Border.Background>
                    <LinearGradientBrush StartPoint="0%,0%" EndPoint="100%,100%">
                        <GradientStop Color="#5B8DEF" Offset="0" />
                        <GradientStop Color="#9CC2FF" Offset="1" />
                    </LinearGradientBrush>
                </Border.Background>
            </Border>
        </arc:Card.Media>
        <arc:Card.Avatar>
            <arc:Avatar DisplayName="Maya Chen" Size="Small" />
        </arc:Card.Avatar>
        <arc:Card.Action>
            <arc:Button Content="Open" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" />
        </arc:Card.Action>
    </arc:Card>
    <arc:Card Title="Atlas API"
              Description="Endpoint inventory and examples for the public docs."
              Meta="Jonas Berg"
              Status="Syncing 12 of 40 pages"
              Width="300"
              VerticalAlignment="Top">
        <arc:Card.Media>
            <Border Height="132">
                <Border.Background>
                    <LinearGradientBrush StartPoint="0%,0%" EndPoint="100%,100%">
                        <GradientStop Color="#2FA88B" Offset="0" />
                        <GradientStop Color="#8EE0C6" Offset="1" />
                    </LinearGradientBrush>
                </Border.Background>
            </Border>

```

### Content guidelines

- **Title**: a short noun phrase in sentence case that names the item: "Harbour redesign", "Q3 invoices". The title is
  the card's accessible name, so it must make sense out of context.
- **Description**: one sentence about what the item is or holds. It wraps at about 34 digit widths, so keep it to two
  lines at most. Do not repeat the title.
- **Status**: a fact with a time, in sentence case: "Updated 2 hours ago", "Syncing 12 of 40 invoices". Use digits for
  counts and avoid vague words such as "Recently".
- **Action**: a verb, with the object when the card does not name it: "Open", "Share report".

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| Click here to see more | Open project |
| Lots of stuff happening | Syncing 12 of 40 invoices |
| Recently updated | Updated 2 hours ago |
| This card shows a project | Harbour redesign |

### Best practices

**Do**

- Set `Details` only when the item has more to show than the card. A quick look that repeats the page adds nothing.
- Keep every card in a grid at one width and one media height, so the titles and footers line up.
- Use `Status` for state that changes while the page is open, and keep the wording stable between changes.
- Set `CloseButtonName` when the quick look holds a draft or a decision, so the close control names its outcome.

**Avoid**

- Long forms inside `Details`. The quick look is a bounded view meant for reading and one or two actions.
- More than one action in the footer. The footer has one trailing slot, and a second action competes with the press
  that opens the card.
- Re-setting `Status` to the same text on a timer. Each change replays the roll and draws attention without news.
- Relying on the hover lift to show that a card is clickable. Touch and pen never lift the card, so the title and the
  `Details` affordance must carry the meaning on their own.

### Common questions

**Why does pressing the card not open the quick look?** Only a card with `Details` opens on a press, and only when the
press is not on a nested control. Check that `Details` has a value, then check that the press is not on the `Action`.

**How do I open the quick look from a toolbar button?** Bind `IsDetailsOpen` to a view model property, or call
`OpenDetails()` from code. `CloseDetails()` closes it with the reason `Programmatic`.

**Why is the card not in the tab order?** The card itself is not focusable. With `Details`, the title button is the
tab stop; without it, the title is a heading and only the footer action takes focus.

**Does the first status animate?** No. The roll plays only when an existing status is replaced by new text. Setting the
first value, or clearing the status, changes the line at once.

**Why does the card not lift on touch?** The lift answers only a mouse pointer. Touch and pen get the same layout and
the same press behavior without the hover state.

## API reference

### Card

Arc card: a contained group of related content and actions for browsable grid items (projects, listings, posts), with optional media, an owner byline and a status line that updates in place. A pointed-at card lifts 2px on a snappy spring while its border and shadow deepen and the media drifts to 1.04 (mouse only). Set `Details` and the title becomes a button and the whole card a trigger: the card grows into a larger quick look without leaving the page (P8): its surface, media, title, description, byline and action fly into a `DialogSurface` on the overlay layer on one critically damped spring (0.3s; 0.26s back) while the corners morph, the details rise in after 120ms and the page dims behind a 7px backdrop blur. Escape, the scrim or the close button send it back into the card and return focus to the title. Reduced motion fades the quick look instead.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Title` | `string?` | `null` | Heading (required). Becomes the quick look trigger when `Details` is set. |
| `Description` | `string?` | `null` | Supporting line under the title (at most 34 characters per line). |
| `Media` | `object?` | `null` | Image or visual at the top; it drifts in slightly while the card is pointed at. |
| `Action` | `object?` | `null` | Trailing footer control (a button); stays separately focusable and clickable over the card. |
| `Avatar` | `object?` | `null` | Small leading footer visual, such as the owner's `Avatar` (shown in a 32px circle). |
| `Meta` | `object?` | `null` | Who the card belongs to, such as the owner's name. |
| `Status` | `string?` | `null` | A short status under the meta ("Updated 2 hours ago"); new words rise in and are announced politely. |
| `Details` | `object?` | `null` | Quick look content. When set, the whole card opens and grows into a larger view. |
| `IsDetailsOpen` | `bool` | `false` | Quick look open state (Arc open / defaultOpen / onOpenChange). Two-way; ignored without `Details`. |
| `ScrimBrush` | `IBrush?` | `null` | Scrim behind the quick look (the theme sets Arc's oklch(10% 0 0 / 0.46)). |
| `BackdropBlur` | `double` | `0` | Backdrop blur behind the quick look in px (the theme sets Arc's 7; off under ReduceTransparency). |
| `CloseButtonName` | `string` | `"Close quick look"` | Accessible name of the quick look's close button. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `DetailsOpenChanged` | `CardDetailsOpenChangedEventArgs` | Raised when the quick look opens or closes (the close motion may still be playing). |

Pseudo-classes: `:hover`, `:pressed`, `:interactive`, `:trigger-focus`, `:quick-look`, `:has-media`, `:has-description`, `:has-content`, `:has-footer`, `:has-byline`, `:has-avatar`, `:has-meta`, `:has-status`, `:has-action`

Derives from `ContentControl`: every member of `ContentControl` works as well.

## Accessibility

- The card is a group named by `Title`. Without `Details`, the title is a heading at level 3.
- With `Details`, the title is a button; Enter or Space opens the quick look.
- The quick look is a dialog named by its title, with the description as its help text. Its close button is named by
  `CloseButtonName`, "Close quick look" by default.
- Changes to `Status` are read out through a polite live region.
- Nested actions keep their own focus and names. Give an icon-only action a name with `AutomationProperties.Name`, and
  set alternative text on the images in `Media`, or mark them as decorative.
- The hover lift and the media zoom are visual only; the card has the same content and actions without them.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` | Move between the title (with `Details`), the content's controls and the footer action |
| `Enter` or `Space` on the title | Open the quick look, with focus moving into it |
| `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` with the quick look open | Move among its controls only; focus stays inside the quick look |
| `Escape` | Close the quick look and return focus to the title |
| `Enter` or `Space` on the close button | Close the quick look with the reason `CloseButton` |

A card without `Details` takes no focus of its own; only its nested controls are stops.

## Motion

- On hover the card lifts 2px and its border and shadow deepen. The media slowly zooms to 1.04 (mouse only).
- With `Details`, the surface, media, title and byline fly into the quick look on one spring while the page dims behind
  a blur. Closing flies them back into the card.
- A new `Status` lifts the old line away while the new words rise in.
- Reduced motion removes the lift, zoom and morph; the quick look only fades. Off applies changes at once.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| Hover on a card | Lifts 2px, border and shadow deepen | Border and shadow change at once, no lift | Immediate |
| Media on hover | Zooms to 1.04 over 960 ms, back in 480 ms | No zoom | Immediate |
| Quick look opens or closes | Surface, media and title fly on a spring (0.3 s open, 0.26 s close) | Fades in and out | Immediate |
| Status changes | Old line lifts away, new words rise one after another | Swapped at once | Immediate |
| Scrim behind the quick look | Fades in and out over the page | Fades in and out | Immediate |

## Related

- `MetricCard` for one number with its context and change.
- `ExpandableCard` for content that expands in place, without a dialog.
- `Dialog` for a modal with no card to grow from.
- `CardStack` for triaging a deck of cards one at a time.
- `EmptyState` for a grid or list that has no cards yet.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `MetricCard` | The content is one number with its change and a trend |
| `ExpandableCard` | The content opens in place inside the page, without a dialog |
| `Dialog` | The view is modal and there is no tile to grow from |
| `CardStack` | People decide on one card at a time, with drag, keys and undo |
| `Table` | The items are rows that need comparable columns |
| `EmptyState` | The grid or list has no items yet |
