# Metric card

> A compact summary for a number that needs context.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/metric-card

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             xmlns:generic="using:System.Collections.Generic"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.MetricCardDefaultDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="16">
        <WrapPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center" ItemSpacing="12" LineSpacing="12">
            <arc:MetricCard x:Name="Uptime"
                            Label="Uptime"
                            Value="99.98"
                            Decimals="2"
                            Suffix="%"
                            Context="Last 30 days"
                            Change="+0.02%"
                            Width="280"
                            VerticalAlignment="Top" />
            <arc:MetricCard x:Name="Orders"
                            Label="Orders"
                            Value="1204"
                            Context="vs last week"
                            Change="+12%"
                            Width="280"
                            VerticalAlignment="Top">
                <arc:MetricCard.Sparkline>
                    <generic:List x:TypeArguments="x:Double">
                        <x:Double>820</x:Double>
                        <x:Double>910</x:Double>
                        <x:Double>870</x:Double>
                        <x:Double>990</x:Double>
                        <x:Double>1040</x:Double>
                        <x:Double>1010</x:Double>
                        <x:Double>1204</x:Double>
                    </generic:List>
                </arc:MetricCard.Sparkline>
            </arc:MetricCard>
            <arc:MetricCard x:Name="Latency"
                            Label="p95 latency"
                            Value="182"
                            Suffix=" ms"
                            Context="vs yesterday"
                            Change="−8%"
                            IsChangeGlyphVisible="True"
                            Width="280"
                            VerticalAlignment="Top" />
        </WrapPanel>
        <WrapPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center" ItemSpacing="12" LineSpacing="12">
            <arc:Button Content="New data" Variant="Secondary" Click="OnNewDataClick" />
            <arc:Button Content="Toggle chip" Variant="Ghost" Click="OnToggleChipClick" />
        </WrapPanel>
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class MetricCardDefaultDemo : UserControl
{
    private readonly Random _random = new(3);

    public MetricCardDefaultDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
    }

    private void OnNewDataClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        var next = Math.Max(200, Orders.Value + _random.Next(-260, 300));
        var delta = (next - Orders.Value) / Orders.Value * 100;
        Orders.Value = next;
        Orders.Change = delta >= 0 ? $"+{delta:0}%" : $"−{-delta:0}%";
        Orders.Context = delta >= 0 ? "Up on last week" : "Down on last week";
        var points = new List<double>(Orders.Sparkline!) { next };
        points.RemoveAt(0);
        Orders.Sparkline = points;

        Latency.Value = Math.Max(80, Latency.Value + _random.Next(-40, 40));
        Latency.Change = Latency.Value < 182
            ? $"−{(182 - Latency.Value) / 182 * 100:0}%"
            : $"+{(Latency.Value - 182) / 182 * 100:0}%";
    }

    private void OnToggleChipClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
        => Uptime.Change = Uptime.Change is null ? "+0.02%" : null;
}
```

## When to use

`MetricCard` is the tile that answers "how are we doing" on a dashboard. It holds one number, the label that names
it, the comparison that gives it meaning and an optional change chip, in a surface that sits in a row with other
metrics. A row of them is the top of most operational and business pages: the first thing a person reads before
they open a table or a chart.

- **KPI rows on a SaaS overview page**: monthly recurring revenue, active accounts and churn, each with "vs last
  month" as its context and a chip showing the change.
- **Uptime and service health** in an operations console: "Uptime 99.98%" with "Last 30 days", so the number is read
  against the period it covers.
- **Live counts on an order or support dashboard**: open orders or the ticket backlog, where the digits roll as new
  work arrives and the context explains the time window.
- **Latency and throughput** in a developer tool or an API portal: a p95 value in milliseconds, compared with
  yesterday, with a trend line when the direction over the last few points matters.
- **Usage and billing summaries** in a fintech or billing area: a month-to-date total or an average balance, shown
  next to the period it refers to.

## When not to use

- **The trend matters more than the latest value**, such as a week of daily sign-ups read as a shape: use `Sparkline`
  or `LineChart`, which give the whole series room.
- **A bare number inside running text or a heading**, with no frame and no context: use `AnimatedCounter`.
- **A quota or a progress toward a limit**, such as seats used out of 50: use `UsageMeter`, which draws the fraction.
- **A card with media, an owner and actions**: use `Card`. A metric card holds a number, not a tile of content.
- **Many values to compare by attributes**, such as revenue per region and per plan: use `Table` or
  `DataGrid`, where each row can carry its own columns.
- **A time to reach a deadline**, such as a renewal or a trial end: use `Countdown`, which counts down on its own.

## Usage

`Label`, `Value` and `Context` are the usual parts. `Change` is optional; without it the chip is hidden.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:MetricCard Label="Uptime"
                    Value="99.98"
                    Decimals="2"
                    Suffix="%"
                    Context="Last 30 days"
                    Change="+0.02%"
                    Width="280" />
</UserControl>
```

`MetricCard` derives from Avalonia's `TemplatedControl`. It is a display control: it is not focusable, has no
press behavior and raises no events. Its number is an `AnimatedCounter` inside its template, so the rolling digits,
the decimals and the prefix and suffix are the counter's behavior, and the card adds the label, the chip and the
trend line around it. Set the value from code or a binding and the card updates in place.

### Anatomy

1. **Label** (`Label`): 14 px in the secondary text color on the top row, on the left. It truncates with an ellipsis
   when the card is narrow, and it is the card's accessible name.
2. **Change chip** (`Change`): a pill on the top row, on the right, with 8 px side and 3 px vertical padding. It
   holds the change text and, when `IsChangeGlyphVisible` is set, a 12 px trend glyph. It is hidden while `Change` is
   empty.
3. **Value** (`Value`, with `Prefix`, `Suffix` and `Decimals`): the number in the large counter, bottom-aligned. The
   `Decimals` default is 0. `Prefix` sits before the digits, such as "$", and `Suffix` after them, such as "%" or " ms".
4. **Trend line** (`Sparkline`): a 96 by 36 px line on the same row as the value, at its bottom edge. It appears only
   with two or more points.
5. **Context** (`Context`): 14 px in the muted text color, 16 px below the value row. It says what the number is
   compared with: "vs last week", "Last 30 days".
6. **Surface**: 24 px padding, a 1 px border on the surface color, the surface radius and the resting shadow. The top
   row sits 32 px above the value row.

### Value, prefix, suffix and decimals

The number is a `double`, so one property covers integers, percentages and averages. Choose the decimals for the
meaning of the number, not for the width of the card: a 99.98% uptime needs two decimals, an order count needs none.

```xml
<arc:MetricCard Label="Revenue this month"
                Value="48210"
                Prefix="$"
                Decimals="0"
                Context="vs last month"
                Change="+6.4%"
                Width="280" />
```

- Use `Prefix` for a currency symbol and `Suffix` for a unit that follows the number. Keep the unit short; a long
  suffix pushes the digits to the left and makes the value row feel unstable.
- Use one decimal place for a percentage that moves by fractions ("1.8%") and two for an availability figure that
  people compare to a service-level target ("99.98%").
- Do not put the unit in `Label` when the value carries it. "Latency" with a suffix of " ms" reads once; "Latency (ms)"
  with a suffix of " ms" reads twice.

### Change chip

A `Change` that starts with "+" is an up change, and one that starts with "-" or "−" is a down change. Any other
text is a neutral change. The direction is read back from `ChangeDirection`, and the chip shows its color from it.

| `Change` text | `ChangeDirection` | Chip look |
|---|---|---|
| "+12%" | `Up` | Success tint behind success-colored text |
| "−8%" or "-8%" | `Down` | Danger tint behind danger-colored text |
| "flat", "0%" or empty text | `None` | Outlined neutral chip |

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.MetricCardPlainNumberDemo">
    <arc:MetricCard Label="Active projects"
                    Value="48"
                    Context="Across 6 teams"
                    Width="280"
                    HorizontalAlignment="Center" />
</UserControl>
```

```xml
<arc:MetricCard Label="p95 latency"
                Value="182"
                Suffix=" ms"
                Context="vs yesterday"
                Change="−8%"
                IsChangeGlyphVisible="True"
                Width="280" />
```

Write the sign in the text. The color is a second cue, and the sign is the first, so the direction is clear to people
who do not see color differences and to screen readers. `IsChangeGlyphVisible` adds a trend arrow to a signed chip;
it is off by default.

The chip colors the direction, not whether the direction is good. A drop in latency is an improvement, but a "−8%"
chip still uses the danger tint. Explain the meaning in `Context` ("lower is better"), or show the change as a plain
neutral value when the good direction is not the same as the sign. Set `Change` to `null` to hide the chip; it fades
out.

### Trend line

`Sparkline` takes a list of values and draws a small trend line beside the number. The line draws itself in the first
time it comes into view, and it redraws when the data changes. It needs at least two points: with one value or none,
the line is hidden. The line takes the color of the change direction: accent when there is no change, success for an
up change and danger for a down change.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             xmlns:generic="using:System.Collections.Generic">
    <arc:MetricCard Label="Orders" Value="1204" Context="vs last week" Change="+12%" Width="280">
        <arc:MetricCard.Sparkline>
            <generic:List x:TypeArguments="x:Double">
                <x:Double>820</x:Double>
                <x:Double>910</x:Double>
                <x:Double>1204</x:Double>
            </generic:List>
        </arc:MetricCard.Sparkline>
    </arc:MetricCard>
</UserControl>
```

```csharp
orders.Sparkline = new List<double> { 820, 910, 870, 990, 1040, 1010, 1204 };
```

Pass a short series, such as the last seven or thirty daily values, so the line shows the shape of the recent
movement. A series of hundreds of points makes the 96 px box a noisy scribble; use `LineChart` for that.

### Binding to a view model

A metrics row binds each card to a property on the dashboard view model. With CommunityToolkit.Mvvm, the view model
raises property changes and the cards update in place, with the digits rolling to the new value.

```csharp
public partial class OverviewViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    [ObservableProperty]
    private double _orderCount;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private string? _orderContext;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private string? _orderChange;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private IList<double>? _orderTrend;

    public void ShowOrders(int openCount, int previousCount, IList<double> dailyCounts)
    {
        OrderCount = openCount;
        OrderContext = "vs last week";
        OrderChange = openCount >= previousCount
            ? $"+{openCount - previousCount}"
            : $"−{previousCount - openCount}";
        OrderTrend = dailyCounts;
    }
}
```

```xml
<arc:MetricCard Label="Orders"
                Value="{Binding OrderCount}"
                Context="{Binding OrderContext}"
                Change="{Binding OrderChange}"
                Sparkline="{Binding OrderTrend}"
                Width="280" />
```

- Bind `Value` one way. The card never writes it back.
- Update `Context`, `Change` and `Value` together in one method (`ShowOrders` above), so the card shows one consistent state.
- Compiled bindings need `x:DataType` on the view. The examples leave it out for brevity.

Each update rolls the digits to the new value and the copy rolls in from the direction the number moved, so an update
arriving every few seconds keeps the row in constant motion. For a live feed, update the view model on a fixed
interval, such as once every 30 seconds.

### Narrow windows

In a window that is 380 px wide or less, the card uses tighter padding (16 px), the top row sits 24 px above the
value row, and the change chip moves under the label with 12 px of space. The rule reads the window width, not the card
width, so every card in the window switches to the narrow layout together. No code is needed for this.

### Example: monthly overview row

An overview page for a SaaS admin console at the start of the month. The three metrics answer the questions people
ask first: how much revenue came in, how many accounts are retained and how many are active. Each card names its
period in the context, and the change chip shows the direction in the text. The churn card shows a down change in the
danger tint. A drop in churn is good news, so its context says "lower is better", which is the rule from the chip
section: the color follows the sign, and the words carry the meaning.

![Three metric cards for October: revenue, churn and active accounts](https://docs.tkcode.si/shots/Docs/Cards/MetricCard/images/MonthlyOverview.webp)

```xml
<StackPanel Width="740" Spacing="16">
    <TextBlock Text="Overview, October 2026" FontSize="18" FontWeight="SemiBold" />
    <WrapPanel ItemSpacing="12" LineSpacing="12">
        <arc:MetricCard Label="Revenue"
                        Value="48210"
                        Prefix="$"
                        Decimals="0"
                        Context="vs last month"
                        Change="+6.4%"
                        Width="236"
                        VerticalAlignment="Top" />
        <arc:MetricCard Label="Churn"
                        Value="1.8"
                        Decimals="1"
                        Suffix="%"
                        Context="Lower is better"
                        Change="−0.3 pts"
                        Width="236"
                        VerticalAlignment="Top" />
        <arc:MetricCard Label="Active accounts"
                        Value="1284"
                        Context="Across 3 regions"
                        Change="+42"
                        Width="236"
                        VerticalAlignment="Top" />
    </WrapPanel>
</StackPanel>
```

### Content guidelines

- **Label**: a short noun phrase in sentence case that names the measure: "Revenue", "Uptime", "p95 latency". It is
  the accessible name, so it must make sense without the value.
- **Value and unit**: write the unit once, either in `Prefix` or `Suffix`, and do not repeat it in the label. Write
  numbers as digits.
- **Change**: a sign and a number with its unit: "+6.4%", "−0.3 pts", "+42". Use the minus sign "−" for a down
  change; the card reads both "−" and "-".
- **Context**: the period or the comparison, in lower case after the number: "vs last month", "Last 30 days". Say
  what good looks like when the sign alone does not tell it: "Lower is better".

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| Revenue ($) | Revenue, with a `Prefix` of "$" |
| Up 6 percent! | +6.4% |
| Churn going down (good) | −0.3 pts, lower is better |
| Data from last month | vs last month |
| Latency (ms) with suffix " ms" | Latency with suffix " ms" |

### Best practices

**Do**

- Put the period in `Context` on every card, so the number is never read without its window.
- Keep the cards in a row at one width, so the values align and the eye can compare them.
- Explain a change whose good direction differs from its sign, in `Context`.
- Update the view model at a steady interval for live data. The card settles between updates, and the eye reads the
  change instead of the motion.

**Avoid**

- Showing more than four or five cards in one row. Beyond that, the numbers stop being the first thing a person reads.
- A decimal count that changes between cards in the same row, which makes the row look unfinished.
- Writing the change into `Context` ("+6.4% vs last month") when `Change` already carries it. The text repeats and the
  chip duplicates the sentence.
- Long `Value` text, such as a formatted string with words. The counter is for numbers; a word such as "Healthy"
  belongs in a status element.

### Common questions

**The chip shows a danger color for a good change. How do I fix that?** The chip colors by the sign of `Change`, not by
whether the change is good. Put the meaning in `Context` ("Lower is better") and keep the sign honest. The color
follows the sign by design, so the card does not need a second property to flip it.

**How do I show a change without the color?** Write the text without a sign (for example "Stable" or "No change"),
which makes the direction `None` and the chip neutral. The card shows the chip with an outline and no tint.

**Why does the number start at zero?** The first time the card scrolls into view, the counter rolls from zero to the
value. After that, each update rolls from the previous value.

**Why is the chip hidden when `Change` is empty?** An empty `Change` removes the chip so the top row shows only the
label. The chip fades out.

**Can a person edit the value or open the metric?** No. The card is display-only, takes no focus and raises no events.
To open a detail view, place the card in a control that your page owns and handles the press there.

## API reference

### MetricCard

Arc metric card: a compact summary for a number that needs context (uptime, orders). The value rolls like an odometer (`AnimatedCounter`, from zero on first view); the label, context and change chip roll in from the side the number moved toward (a larger number rises from below, a smaller one drops from above), and the chip's width springs to fit. A signed change reads its direction in color as well as sign; set `IsChangeGlyphVisible` to add a direction glyph and `Sparkline` for a small trend line.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Label` | `string?` | `null` | What is measured. |
| `Value` | `double` | `0` | The number; it rolls from zero on first view, then between values. |
| `Prefix` | `string?` | `null` | Text before the number, such as "$". |
| `Suffix` | `string?` | `null` | Unit after the number, such as "%" or " ms". |
| `Decimals` | `int` | `0` | Fraction digits of the number (default 0). |
| `Context` | `string?` | `null` | The comparison line, such as "vs last week". |
| `Change` | `string?` | `null` | The change chip, such as "+12%"; empty hides the chip. Write the sign: color is not the only cue. |
| `IsChangeGlyphVisible` | `bool` | `false` | Adds a trending up / down glyph to a signed change chip (default false, like Arc). |
| `Sparkline` | `IList<double>?` | `null` | Optional values for a small trend line beside the number. |
| `ChangeDirection` | `MetricChangeDirection` | – | *Read-only.* Direction read from the sign of `Change`. |

Pseudo-classes: `:narrow`, `:up`, `:down`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

## Accessibility

- The card is a group named by `Label`. Its help text is the change and the context, such as "+12% vs last week",
  or the context alone when there is no change.
- The number is read by the counter. The change chip is plain text and states its direction with "+" or "−", so the
  direction does not depend on color.
- A value change is not announced by itself. If you need an announcement, set `AutomationProperties.LiveSetting` on
  the card or on a container around it.
- The card takes no keyboard focus. Tab skips it, so a row of metrics is not a row of stops.
- Give every card a `Label` that stands on its own. The label is what a screen reader reads first, so "Uptime" is
  better than "Metric 1" and better than the value alone.

## Motion

- The number rolls from zero the first time the card scrolls into view, then turns toward each new value.
- The label, context and chip text roll in from the side the number moved toward.
- The chip width adjusts to the new text on a spring, and the chip scales and fades in or out.
- The trend line draws in over 0.9s the first time it is shown, and cross-fades when the data changes.
- Reduced motion jumps the number to its new value and fades the text. The chip and trend line change without motion.
  Off applies every change at once.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| Number changes | Rolls digit by digit, up when it grows, down when it shrinks | Jumps to the new value | Immediate |
| Label, context or chip text changes | Rolls in from the side the number moved toward | Instant fade | Immediate |
| Chip appears or disappears | Scales from 96% and fades, on a snappy spring | No motion | Immediate |
| Chip width | Springs to fit the new text | No motion | Immediate |
| Trend line first shown | Draws in over 0.9 s | Shown at once | Immediate |
| Trend line data changes | Cross-fades | No motion | Immediate |

## Related

- `AnimatedCounter` for a bare number that needs no card frame.
- `Sparkline` when the trend matters more than the latest value.
- `Card` for a group of content and actions around a number.
- `UsageMeter` for a value measured against a limit.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `AnimatedCounter` | The number sits in running text or a heading, without a card |
| `Sparkline` | The shape of the series is the message |
| `LineChart` | The series needs axes, several lines or a longer history |
| `UsageMeter` | The value is a fraction of a limit, such as seats used |
| `Card` | The tile holds media, an owner or actions beside the number |
| `Countdown` | The number is a time left until a deadline |
| `Table` | The values are rows that need sorting and comparison by attribute |

# Empty state

> A useful next step when there is nothing to show yet.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/empty-state

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.EmptyStateFirstUseDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12">
        <Border CornerRadius="26"
                BorderThickness="1"
                Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Surface}"
                BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Border}">
            <arc:EmptyState x:Name="Empty"
                            Label="Projects"
                            Title="No projects yet"
                            Description="Projects keep your files, people and conversations in one place.">
                <arc:EmptyState.Action>
                    <arc:Button x:Name="Create"
                                Content="New project"
                                Variant="Primary"
                                Click="OnCreateClick" />
                </arc:EmptyState.Action>
            </arc:EmptyState>
        </Border>
        <WrapPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center" ItemSpacing="12" LineSpacing="12">
            <arc:Button Content="Reset" Variant="Ghost" Click="OnResetClick" />
        </WrapPanel>
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class EmptyStateFirstUseDemo : UserControl
{
    public EmptyStateFirstUseDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
    }

    private void OnCreateClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        Empty.Icon = ArcIcons.Check;
        Empty.Title = "Project created";
        Empty.Description = "Invite your team or start adding files whenever you're ready.";
        Empty.Action = null;
    }

    private void OnResetClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        Empty.Icon = null;
        Empty.Title = "No projects yet";
        Empty.Description = "Projects keep your files, people and conversations in one place.";
        Empty.Action = Create;
    }
}
```

## When to use

`EmptyState` fills the place where a list, a folder or a result set would be when it has nothing to show. It
explains why the area is empty and offers the one next step that makes sense, so the person is never left at a
blank panel. It is a centered block of an icon, a title, one or two sentences and an optional action, and it sits
inside the same surface as the content it replaces.

- **First use of a list** in an admin console or a SaaS product: "No projects yet" with a primary "New project"
  button, shown where the project table will appear once the first project exists.
- **Zero results from a search or a filter** in an orders, invoices or customers list: "No results for
  'quarterly plan'" with "Clear search" and "Browse all" actions, so the person can recover without retyping.
- **A finished step that leaves nothing to list**, such as a payouts page after every invoice is paid: "All invoices
  are paid" with the next scheduled date in the description and no action at all.
- **A state that changes in place**: a team page that shows "No members yet" until the first invitation is accepted,
  then "Invitation sent" with a "Resend invite" action, without a page change.
- **Empty inbox or activity feeds** in a developer tool or a CRM: "No deployments in the last 7 days" with a link to the
  deployment history, so the empty area explains the time window it covers.

## When not to use

- **The data is still loading**: use `Skeleton`, which keeps the shape of the content. An empty state while a request
  is in flight tells people the wrong thing.
- **A failed request or an error on a page that already has content**: use `Alert`, placed above the content, so the
  data that did load stays visible.
- **A grid item that has media, an owner and footer actions**: use `Card`. An empty state is not a tile and should not
  look like one.
- **A confirmation that something was saved or changed**: use `Toast`, which does not replace the content on the
  page.
- **A large, multi-scene illustration with tabs**: use the `EmptyStates` block, which is a ready-made set of scenes.
  Use `EmptyState` when one message belongs to one place in your page.

## Usage

`Title` and `Description` carry the message, and `Action` adds the call to action. `Label` names the region for
assistive technology. The default icon is a folder.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:EmptyState Label="Projects"
                    Title="No projects yet"
                    Description="Projects keep your files, people and conversations in one place.">
        <arc:EmptyState.Action>
            <arc:Button Content="New project" Variant="Primary" />
        </arc:EmptyState.Action>
    </arc:EmptyState>
</UserControl>
```

`EmptyState` derives from Avalonia's `TemplatedControl`. It has no value, selection or items, so it raises no events.
Its only interactive parts are the buttons you place in `Action`, which keep their own focus, press and command
behavior.

### Anatomy

1. **Icon block** (fed by `Icon`): a 48 px square with a 1 px border in the border color, the muted
   surface color and the panel radius. The glyph is 24 px, drawn with a 1.5 stroke in the secondary text color.
2. **Title** (`Title`): 16 px, medium weight, 22.4 px line height (1.4), in the foreground color, centered. It is a
   heading at level 3. It sits 20 px below the icon block.
3. **Description** (`Description`): 14 px, 19.6 px line height, in the secondary text color, centered. It sits 8 px
   below the title and is capped at 288 px wide (18 rem), so it wraps to a short measure.
4. **Action** (`Action`): a row centered 20 px below the description. It is hidden until `Action` has a value.
5. **Padding**: 20 px on each side. The vertical padding follows the window width: 8% of it, kept between 32 px and
   48 px.
6. **Region**: the whole control is a region landmark. Its accessible name is `Label`.

The title and description are balanced: when the copy wraps, the lines are narrowed to an even length instead of
leaving one short last line, so a two-line description looks centered.

### Choosing the copy and the icon

The icon and the copy say why the area is empty. Choose the state first, then write the copy and pick the action
that moves the person forward.

| State | Icon | Title | Action |
|---|---|---|---|
| First use, nothing exists yet | Default folder, or the feature's own icon | "No projects yet" | The primary creation action |
| Search or filter returned nothing | `ArcIcons.Search` | "No results for 'quarterly plan'" | Clear the filter, or browse all |
| Work is done, nothing to act on | `ArcIcons.Check` | "All invoices are paid" | None, or a link to history |
| A change succeeded in place | `ArcIcons.Check` | "Project created" | Usually none; remove the old action |

The default folder suits a list that has no items yet. A search icon tells the person the list exists and their
query filtered it out. Keep one icon per state, and do not decorate the block with a different icon on every visit.

### Icon

`Icon` takes a control, or a 24 by 24 Lucide `Geometry` such as one of the `ArcIcons` glyphs. Passing a geometry
draws it at 24 px with the 1.5 stroke, which is the Arc look. Pass a control when you need a different size or a
composed image. Set `Icon` to `null` to return to the default folder.

```xml
<arc:EmptyState Title="No results"
                Description="Check the spelling or try a broader term."
                Icon="{Binding SearchIcon}" />
```

```csharp
empty.Icon = ArcIcons.Search;
```

When the icon changes, the old one is replaced by the new one with a pop. Setting the same icon again leaves it still,
so a view model can assign the icon on every refresh without an animation on each refresh.

### Action row

`Action` takes one button, or a panel with several buttons. The row is centered below the description. Use one
primary action for the way forward. When the state needs a recovery action too, put a secondary action beside it in
a `StackPanel` and keep the primary button first, so it is the first stop in the tab order.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.EmptyStateZeroResultsDemo">
    <Border CornerRadius="26"
            BorderThickness="1"
            Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Surface}"
            BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Border}">
        <arc:EmptyState Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Search}"
                        Title="No results for “quarterly plan”"
                        Description="Check the spelling or try a broader term.">
            <arc:EmptyState.Action>
                <StackPanel Orientation="Horizontal" Spacing="12">
                    <arc:Button Content="Clear search" Variant="Secondary" />
                    <arc:Button Content="Browse all" Variant="Ghost" />
                </StackPanel>
            </arc:EmptyState.Action>
        </arc:EmptyState>
    </Border>
</UserControl>
```

```xml
<arc:EmptyState Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Search}"
                Title="No results for “quarterly plan”"
                Description="Check the spelling or try a broader term.">
    <arc:EmptyState.Action>
        <StackPanel Orientation="Horizontal" Spacing="12">
            <arc:Button Content="Clear search" Variant="Secondary" />
            <arc:Button Content="Browse all" Variant="Ghost" />
        </StackPanel>
    </arc:EmptyState.Action>
</arc:EmptyState>
```

Give each button a verb and an object, such as "Clear search" or "New project". A button that repeats the title
("Projects") tells the person nothing.

### Driving it from data

Most empty states depend on a count, a filter or a load result. Keep the decision in the view model and let the
`EmptyState` show the state that matches. The control is shown only when the list is empty, so the list and the
empty state never compete for the same space.

```csharp
public partial class ProjectsViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    public ObservableCollection<ProjectRow> Projects { get; } = new();

    [ObservableProperty]
    private string _searchText = string.Empty;

    public bool HasProjects => Projects.Count > 0;

    public string EmptyTitle => string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(SearchText)
        ? "No projects yet"
        : $"No results for “{SearchText}”";

    public string EmptyDescription => string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(SearchText)
        ? "Projects keep your files, people and conversations in one place."
        : "Check the spelling or try a broader term.";

    [RelayCommand]
    private void ClearSearch() => SearchText = string.Empty;

    [RelayCommand]
    private async Task CreateProjectAsync()
    {
        await _projects.CreateAsync();
    }
}
```

```xml
<Grid>
    <ItemsControl ItemsSource="{Binding Projects}" IsVisible="{Binding HasProjects}" />
    <arc:EmptyState IsVisible="{Binding !HasProjects}"
                    Label="Projects"
                    Title="{Binding EmptyTitle}"
                    Description="{Binding EmptyDescription}">
        <arc:EmptyState.Action>
            <StackPanel Orientation="Horizontal" Spacing="12">
                <arc:Button Content="New project" Variant="Primary"
                            Command="{Binding CreateProjectCommand}" />
                <arc:Button Content="Clear search" Variant="Ghost"
                            Command="{Binding ClearSearchCommand}" />
            </StackPanel>
        </arc:EmptyState.Action>
    </arc:EmptyState>
</Grid>
```

- `Title`, `Description` and `Icon` are one-way: the view model decides the copy and the icon, and the control never
  writes them back.
- Compute the copy in the view model so the wording for each state lives in one place and can be tested.
- Show `EmptyState` only after the load has returned zero items. While the request runs, show `Skeleton` in the list's
  place instead.
- `Action` takes an object, so bind the buttons' commands inside the action panel, as shown above.

### Changing state

Keep the control mounted and change its properties. The title and description roll to the new copy, and the height
springs to fit it. Set `Action` to `null` to remove the buttons. The `:has-action` pseudo class follows the action,
so a style can change the spacing when there is no button.

```csharp
empty.Icon = ArcIcons.Check;
empty.Title = "Project created";
empty.Description = "Invite your team or start adding files whenever you're ready.";
empty.Action = null;
```

Changing the properties of one mounted control is better than replacing the control, because the icon block and the
copy keep their place and the change reads as the same area updating.

### Layout and sizing

The control has no fixed width. It fills the space its parent gives it and centers its contents, so the same control
works in a narrow side panel and in a wide content area. Its copy is limited to 288 px, so a long description stays
in a readable measure on a wide page.

Put the control in the space the content would use. A table area, a list area and a grid area all work, provided the
surrounding surface has the same background and border as the content. The demos use a surface panel with a border
and a 26 px radius; use the same panel in your page so the empty state reads as part of it.

Keep the title short. It wraps and balances like the description, so a long title does not break the block, but a
sentence-length title belongs in the description.

### Example: empty projects list in a workspace

A projects page in an admin console for a team that has not created its first project. The surface matches the
list it stands in for, the folder icon says what the area holds, the title names the state, the description tells
the person what projects give them, and the one primary action moves them forward. Nothing on the page competes with
the button.

![An empty projects list with a folder icon, a title, a description and a primary action](https://docs.tkcode.si/shots/Docs/Cards/EmptyState/images/ProjectsEmpty.webp)

```xml
<Border Width="680"
        CornerRadius="26"
        BorderThickness="1"
        Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Surface}"
        BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Border}">
    <arc:EmptyState Label="Projects"
                    Title="No projects yet"
                    Description="Projects keep your files, people and conversations in one place.">
        <arc:EmptyState.Action>
            <arc:Button Content="New project" Variant="Primary" />
        </arc:EmptyState.Action>
    </arc:EmptyState>
</Border>
```

### Content guidelines

- **Title**: a short statement of the state in sentence case, without an exclamation mark. "No projects yet",
  "No results for 'invoice'", "All invoices are paid".
- **Description**: one or two sentences that say why the area is empty and what the person can do. Name the next step
  when there is one; say when the list will update when there is not. Write numbers as digits ("last 7 days").
- **Action**: a verb and an object, such as "New project", "Clear search" or "Browse all". Use one primary action;
  secondary actions are ghost or secondary buttons.
- **Tone**: calm and factual. Do not apologize, joke or celebrate with punctuation.

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| Oops, nothing here! | No projects yet |
| Sorry, we found zero results. | No results for 'quarterly plan' |
| Empty | No deployments in the last 7 days |
| Submit | Create project |

### Best practices

**Do**

- Say why the area is empty, in the title or the first sentence of the description, so the person does not have to
  guess whether the page is broken.
- Offer a recovery action when the empty state comes from a filter or search, such as "Clear search", because it is
  the fastest way out of a dead end.
- Keep one icon and one primary action per state, so the block reads the same way every time it appears.
- Show the empty state only after the load has returned no data. Use `Skeleton` while the request runs.

**Avoid**

- Using an empty state for an error. An error needs the cause and a retry, which the empty state has no place for;
  use `Alert` above the content.
- Placing two equal primary buttons in the action row. The person has to choose between them with no guidance.
- Decorative illustrations on every screen. A single folder or search glyph keeps the block quiet, and repeated
  illustrations make the state feel like a marketing page.
- A generic "No projects yet" after a search. When a filter caused the empty result, say so, so the person knows to
  change the filter rather than create something.

### Common questions

**Why does the default icon look like a folder?** The default is `ArcIcons.Folder`, drawn at 24 px with a 1.5 stroke.
It suits the general case of a list with no items. Set `Icon` to a specific glyph for other states.

**How do I remove the button when the state no longer needs one?** Set `Action` to `null`. The action row is hidden and
the `:has-action` class is removed, so the block shrinks back to the copy.

**Does the control take keyboard focus?** No. `EmptyState` is not focusable, so Tab skips the block and goes to the
buttons in `Action`, if there are any.

**Why does the icon not animate on every update?** The icon block settles in once, the first time the control appears,
then stays. Changing the icon later pops only the new glyph, and setting the same icon again does nothing.

**Can I change the padding or the width?** The padding is set by the theme: 20 px horizontally and a vertical padding
between 32 px and 48 px that follows the window width. Set `Width` or `MaxWidth` on the control or on its parent to
constrain the block; the description already has its own 288 px measure.

## API reference

### EmptyState

Arc empty state: a useful next step when there is nothing to show yet (an empty list, zero search results, first use). A centered icon block, a title, one or two sentences and an optional action. Keep it mounted and change its properties to morph between states: the icon pops into the new one, the copy rises in while the old copy leaves, and the text block's height springs to fit. The icon block settles in once when it first appears.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Title` | `string?` | `null` | The headline (a heading, level 3). |
| `Description` | `string?` | `null` | One or two sentences on why it is empty and what to do next. |
| `Action` | `object?` | `null` | The call to action, usually a button (or a panel of two). |
| `Icon` | `object?` | `null` | The icon: a control, or a 24×24 Lucide `Geometry`. Default: Lucide Folder at stroke 1.5. |
| `Label` | `string?` | `null` | Accessible name of the region. |

Pseudo-classes: `:has-action`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

## Accessibility

- The control is a region landmark named by `Label`. Set `Label` on each empty state on a page, so a screen reader
  can announce which list is empty.
- The title is a level 3 heading. The description follows it in the reading order, and the action buttons come last.
- The icon is not exposed to assistive technology. The text carries the meaning, so the title must say the state
  without the icon.
- Buttons in `Action` keep their own focus and keyboard behavior.
- `EmptyState` takes no keyboard focus of its own. Tab moves past the block to the buttons in `Action`, in the order
  they appear, and Enter or Space presses the focused button.

## Motion

- A new title or description rises in from below with a soft blur, and the old text lifts away.
- The text block changes height on a smooth spring to fit the new copy.
- A new `Icon` pops in, and the icon block fades and scales in the first time it appears.
- Reduced motion fades the text and changes the height at once. The icon block does not animate in. Off applies every
  change at once.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| Title or description changes | Text rises in with a soft blur, old text lifts away | Text fades | Immediate |
| Copy changes height | Springs to fit the new copy | Jumps to the new height | Immediate |
| Icon block first appears | Settles in from 92% scale and fades in over 480 ms | No entry animation | Immediate |

## Related

- `Skeleton` while the content is still loading.
- `Alert` for an error or a notice on a page that already shows content.
- `Card` for a grid item with media, an owner and actions.
- `EmptyStates` (block) for a tabbed set of ready-made empty-state scenes.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `Skeleton` | The content is loading and its shape is known |
| `Alert` | Something went wrong or needs attention on a page with content |
| `Toast` | A result is confirmed and nothing on the page needs replacing |
| `Card` | The item is a tile with media, an owner and actions |
| `EmptyStates` block | You want a tabbed illustration with several scenes |

# Line chart

> A multi-series line chart with a gliding crosshair, legend toggles, and paths that morph between ranges.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/line-chart

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.LineChartRangesDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="16">
        <WrapPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center" ItemSpacing="12" LineSpacing="12">
            <arc:Button Content="7 days" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Click="On7DaysClick" />
            <arc:Button Content="30 days" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Click="On30DaysClick" />
            <arc:Button Content="90 days" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Click="On90DaysClick" />
            <arc:Button Content="Toggle loading" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Click="OnToggleLoadingClick" />
        </WrapPanel>
        <arc:LineChart x:Name="Chart"
                       Label="Signups"
                       CategoryLabel="Date"
                       ActiveIndexChanged="OnActiveIndexChanged">
            <arc:LineChart.Series>
                <arc:ChartSeries Key="current" Name="This period" />
                <arc:ChartSeries Key="previous" Name="Previous period" IsDashed="True" />
            </arc:LineChart.Series>
        </arc:LineChart>
        <TextBlock x:Name="Readout"
                   Text="Hover or use the arrow keys to read values."
                   TextWrapping="Wrap"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;
using TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Pages;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class LineChartRangesDemo : UserControl
{
    public LineChartRangesDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        ShowDays(30);
    }

    private void On7DaysClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) => ShowDays(7);

    private void On30DaysClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) => ShowDays(30);

    private void On90DaysClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) => ShowDays(90);

    private void OnToggleLoadingClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) => Chart.IsLoading = !Chart.IsLoading;

    // Replace the x positions and the values of both series together; every line morphs from the shape on screen.
    private void ShowDays(int days)
    {
        Chart.ItemsSource = ChartsADemoData.Days(days);
        Chart.Series[0].Values = ChartsADemoData.Daily(days, 420, 160, days, 2.4);
        Chart.Series[1].Values = ChartsADemoData.Daily(days, 380, 140, days + 11, 1.1);
    }

    private void OnActiveIndexChanged(object? sender, ChartActiveIndexChangedEventArgs e)
        => Readout.Text = e.Index is null
            ? "Hover or use the arrow keys to read values."
            : $"{e.Label}: {string.Join(", ", e.Values.Select(v => $"{v.Name} {v.Value:N0}"))}";
}
```

## When to use

`LineChart` shows one to three measures over time and lets the reader compare them at any point. It is the main trend
chart of an analytics page: it sits under a row of KPI tiles and follows a range selector (7, 30 and 90 days). Each
series is a stable line, so a range change reshapes the same lines instead of replacing them with a new picture.

- **Signups or revenue over a selected range** on an analytics overview. The 7, 30 and 90 day ranges share the same
  series, so the lines morph from their current shape when the person changes the range.
- **Current period against the previous period** on a billing or growth dashboard. A dashed second series shows whether
  this month is above or below the last one without a second chart.
- **Latency or error rate over time** on an incident page. A single series with `Unit="ms"` and `Curve="Linear"` keeps
  spikes at their true height, and the tooltip reads the exact value with its unit.
- **Refunds or failed payments per day** in a fintech operations console. `EmptyLabel` explains a quiet range, and
  `IsLoading` keeps the last shape on screen while the next range is fetched.
- **Usage against a target** on a quota page. A dashed target line sits beside the actual usage, and the legend lets the
  reader hide either one.

## When not to use

- **A compact trend next to one number**, such as a KPI tile or a table cell: use `Sparkline`, which has no axes, legend
  or tooltip.
- **Discrete categories such as days of the week, regions or plans**: use `BarChart`. Bars compare separate values; a
  line implies that the space between two points means something.
- **Parts of a whole**, such as revenue share by plan: use `DonutChart`. Use `WaffleChart` when the parts are counts of
  equal units.
- **More than about four measures**: the palette has four series colors, and the rest take neutral steps that are hard
  to tell apart. Use `Streamgraph` when the layers add up to a total.
- **A long history that needs zooming**: use `BrushChart`, which pairs a detail view with an overview to brush over.
- **Daily activity across a year**, such as logins per day in a calendar grid: use `ActivityHeatmap`.

## Usage

Each `ChartSeries` has a stable `Key`, so the lines keep their identity when the data changes. Set `Label` to name the
chart for assistive technology.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:LineChart Label="Signups" CategoryLabel="Date" ItemsSource="{Binding Days}">
        <arc:LineChart.Series>
            <arc:ChartSeries Key="current" Name="This period" Values="{Binding Current}" />
            <arc:ChartSeries Key="previous" Name="Previous period" Values="{Binding Previous}" IsDashed="True" />
        </arc:LineChart.Series>
    </arc:LineChart>
</UserControl>
```

`LineChart` derives from `ChartBase`, which derives from Avalonia's `TemplatedControl`. The template holds a legend above
a plot that draws every line, area, gridline, label and tooltip itself. Transitions cannot reach the coordinates inside
that one drawing, which is why the chart's motion is driven in code.

### Anatomy

1. **Legend** (`ShowLegend`): one toggle pill per series with a color swatch, 16 px above the plot. It reaches 8 px into
   the margins, so the hover pills line up with the plot edges.
2. **Plot** (`PlotHeight`): 220 px tall by default and as wide as its container. The top tick sits 12 px below the top.
3. **Gridlines** (`ShowGrid`): horizontal lines at the value ticks, in the border color, with a 1 px baseline in the
   strong border color.
4. **Lines**: 2 px round-capped strokes in the series color. A dashed series is 0.25 px thinner, so it does not look
   heavier than a solid line beside it.
5. **Area fill**: a faint 9% tint under the line. By default only the first series has one (`HasArea` changes this).
6. **Value axis** (`ShowYAxis`): tick labels in a 48 px gutter on the right, compact by default (1.2K, 2.4K).
7. **Date axis** (`ShowXAxis`): one 26 px row under the plot. Labels are spaced so they do not collide, and
   `XAxisFormatter` can drop one by returning null.
8. **Crosshair and dots**: a vertical line at the active point and a 4 px dot on each visible line, outlined in the
   surface color.
9. **Tooltip**: the date, then one row per visible series with its value and unit. It sits 14 px to the side of the
   crosshair and flips before it would leave the plot.

### Ranges

Replace the rows and the series values together when the range changes, so every series has one value per row of the
new range. Each line then morphs from the shape on screen, and the value axis springs to the new range.

```csharp
void ShowRange(SignupDay[] rows)
{
    chart.ItemsSource = rows.Select(r => r.Date).ToArray();
    chart.Series[0].Values = rows.Select(r => (double)r.Current).ToArray();
    chart.Series[1].Values = rows.Select(r => (double)r.Previous).ToArray();
}
```

The demo at the top shows the same two series for 7, 30 and 90 days. The axis rescales to the range on screen, and the
lines keep their keys.

### Single series and units

A list of `ChartPoint` items needs no series. `Unit` is shown in the tooltip, and `Curve` switches from the default
smooth curve to straight segments. `Smooth` never swings past the data; use `Linear` when a reader might take the curve
between two days as a real value.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.LineChartSingleSeriesDemo">
    <arc:LineChart x:Name="Chart"
                   Label="p95 latency"
                   Unit="ms"
                   Curve="Linear"
                   PlotHeight="180" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Pages;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class LineChartSingleSeriesDemo : UserControl
{
    public LineChartSingleSeriesDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();

        // A list of ChartPoint needs no series.
        Chart.ItemsSource = ChartsADemoData.Days(14)
            .Select((day, i) => new ChartPoint(day, 120 + 40 * Math.Sin(i / 2.0) + i * 3))
            .ToArray();
    }
}
```

```xml
<arc:LineChart Label="p95 latency" Unit="ms" Curve="Linear" PlotHeight="180" ItemsSource="{Binding Latency}" />
```

### Legend and hidden series

With more than one series the legend shows a toggle per series. `ShowLegend` forces it on or off, and `HiddenSeries`
holds the hidden keys.

```xml
<arc:LineChart Label="Signups"
               ItemsSource="{Binding Days}"
               ShowLegend="True"
               HiddenSeries="{Binding HiddenKeys}" />
```

Hiding a series fades it out and flattens it into the baseline, and the value axis rescales to the series that remain.
`HiddenSeries` is two-way: a legend toggle writes the new list back and raises `HiddenSeriesChanged`, and a change from
code shows or hides the line. When every series is hidden, the plot says "Choose a series to show".

### Loading and empty states

`IsLoading` dims the lines and shows a skeleton when there are no points. `EmptyLabel` explains an empty range.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.LineChartEmptyDemo">
    <arc:LineChart Label="Refunds" EmptyLabel="No refunds in this range" PlotHeight="160">
        <arc:LineChart.Series>
            <arc:ChartSeries Name="Refunds" />
        </arc:LineChart.Series>
    </arc:LineChart>
</UserControl>
```

```xml
<arc:LineChart Label="Refunds" EmptyLabel="No refunds in this range" IsLoading="{Binding IsBusy}" />
```

The default empty text is "No data for this range". Write the reason, so the reader knows whether the chart is wrong or
the period is quiet. While `IsLoading` is true and there are no points, the skeleton shows instead. With points, the
current shapes stay on screen and breathe, which says that new data is coming.

### Reading values

`ActiveIndexChanged` fires while the crosshair moves and when it is released. Use it to show the values in a title.

```csharp
chart.ActiveIndexChanged += (_, e) => readout.Text = e.Index is null
    ? "Hover or use the arrow keys to read values."
    : $"{e.Label}: {string.Join(", ", e.Values.Select(v => $"{v.Name} {v.Value:N0}"))}";
```

`ActiveIndex` holds the same point and is two-way, so code can point the readout at a day, such as the day of an
incident. `Values` lists only the visible series, so a hidden series never appears in the readout.

### Binding to a view model

With CommunityToolkit.Mvvm the view model owns the rows, the range and the hidden series. It replaces the whole array
for each range, and the chart morphs from the previous rows to the new ones.

```csharp
public sealed record SignupDay(string Date, int Current, int Previous);

public interface ISignupService
{
    Task<SignupDay[]> GetDailyAsync(int days);
}

public partial class SignupsViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    private readonly ISignupService _signups;

    public SignupsViewModel(ISignupService signups) => _signups = signups;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private SignupDay[] _days = [];

    [ObservableProperty]
    private IReadOnlyList<string> _hiddenKeys = [];

    [ObservableProperty]
    private int? _activeIndex;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private bool _isBusy;

    [RelayCommand]
    private async Task LoadRangeAsync(int days)
    {
        IsBusy = true;
        try
        {
            // A new array is one data change: the chart takes the rows once and morphs the lines to them.
            Days = await _signups.GetDailyAsync(days);
        }
        finally
        {
            IsBusy = false;
        }
    }
}
```

```xml
<arc:LineChart Label="Signups"
               CategoryLabel="Date"
               Height="260"
               ItemsSource="{Binding Days}"
               XBinding="{Binding Date}"
               HiddenSeries="{Binding HiddenKeys, Mode=TwoWay}"
               ActiveIndex="{Binding ActiveIndex, Mode=TwoWay}"
               IsLoading="{Binding IsBusy}">
    <arc:LineChart.Series>
        <arc:ChartSeries Key="current" Name="This period" ValueBinding="{Binding Current}" />
        <arc:ChartSeries Key="previous"
                         Name="Previous period"
                         IsDashed="True"
                         ValueBinding="{Binding Previous}" />
    </arc:LineChart.Series>
</arc:LineChart>
```

- `XBinding` reads the category from each record. Without it the chart reads the item itself, which works for `string`
  and `DateTime` items but not for a record.
- `HiddenSeries` and `ActiveIndex` are two-way, because the legend and the crosshair write them. `ItemsSource`,
  `IsLoading` and the value bindings are one-way.
- The examples use plain `Binding` for brevity. In an app that compiles its bindings, set `x:DataType` on the view and a
  `DataType` on each binding.

### Data shape and performance

`ItemsSource` holds one item per point, oldest first. Every series reads its value from the same index, so all series
need one value per row, in the same order. A missing value counts as zero, so a day without data draws as a drop to
zero. Supply a real value for every day in the range.

Format numbers with `ValueFormat`, a .NET format string read with en-US conventions: `N0` for counts, `C0` for money,
`0.0'%'` for a percentage. The default groups thousands and shows at most one decimal, so 2400 reads as "2,400". For a
currency that depends on the reader's locale, set `ValueFormatter`. Dates default to "Tue, Sep 15" in the tooltip and
"Sep 15" on the axis; set `XLabelFormatter` or `XAxisFormatter` for another label.

### Value axis

The value axis starts at zero, or at the data minimum when the data dips below zero, and ends at the next tick above the
largest value. Change that when the business question needs it:

- `YMinimum` and `YMaximum` fix either end. Fix both for a percentage (0 to 100) so the axis does not jump between ranges.
- `TickFormatter` formats the tick labels only, for example `chart.TickFormatter = v => $"{v:0}%";` in code.
- `ShowYAxis="False"` removes the gutter when the values are shown elsewhere in the card, such as in a KPI tile above.
- A `YMinimum` away from zero makes a small change look large. Use it only where zero is not a meaningful baseline, such
  as a score, and say so in the card.

```xml
<arc:LineChart Label="Checkout conversion"
               YMinimum="0"
               YMaximum="100"
               ValueFormat="0.0'%'" />
```
