### Content guidelines

- **Label**: the measure, with its unit when the axis has none: "Signups", "p95 latency (ms)". The label names the chart
  for assistive technology and the data table, so it must make sense on its own.
- **Series name**: a short noun phrase for the period or the comparison: "This period", "Previous period", "Target".
- **Empty text**: the reason for the empty range, with the scope named: "No refunds in this range".
- **Card title and caption**: state the total or the change in words, with numbers as digits, such as "1,411 new
  workspaces".

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| Data | Signups per day |
| Previous | Previous period |
| No data | No refunds in this range |
| Series 1 | This period |
| Chart of revenue | Revenue, Sep 1 to Sep 10, 2026 |

### Best practices

**Do**

- Use one series per measure and name each for its period or meaning. The legend and the tooltip repeat the name, so it
  must read without the card title.
- Set `CategoryLabel` to the unit of the axis ("Date", "Week"). The data table uses it as the first column, so screen
  reader users hear the axis name first.
- Replace the whole `ItemsSource` and the series values together on a range change, so the lines morph between two
  consistent states.
- Use `Linear` for latency and counts, and the default `Smooth` for trends where the shape matters more than the exact
  points.

**Avoid**

- A non-zero `YMinimum` on a metric that starts at zero, such as signups or revenue. A truncated axis makes a 5% change
  look like a collapse.
- More than three or four series. Beyond that the colors are hard to tell apart and the tooltip becomes a long list.
- Refreshing the data every second. The lines, the axis and the tooltip all move at once, which hides the change you
  want to show.
- Zero as a placeholder for a day with no data. A missing value counts as zero, so the line drops and reads as a real fall.
- `Smooth` for counts that come in whole units, such as refunds. A curve between two days suggests values that never
  happened.

### Common questions

**Why does the value axis start at zero?** The default baseline is zero, or the data minimum when the data dips below
zero. Set `YMinimum` to change it, and use that deliberately, as described in the value axis section.

**Why is there no legend on my chart?** With one series the legend is hidden by default. Set `ShowLegend="True"` to show
it, or add a second series and the legend appears on its own.

**Why does only the first line have a fill?** `HasArea` is null by default, so only the first series gets an area.
Set `HasArea="True"` on another series to fill it too, or `HasArea="False"` to remove the fill.

## API reference

### LineChart

Arc's line chart: one or more measures over time with series toggles, a crosshair that glides between points and a tooltip that follows on its own spring. Lines draw in from the left the first time the chart is seen, and a new range morphs every line from the shape on screen (resampled on shared x positions) while the value axis springs to its new range and the gridlines ride it. A hidden series flattens into the baseline as it fades. Motion is code-driven (`MotionValue` and a per-point spring array) because every animated value is a coordinate inside one self-drawn geometry, which ControlTheme transitions cannot express.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ShowLegend` | `bool?` | `null` | Series toggles. Null shows the legend when there is more than one series. |
| `ShowGrid` | `bool` | `true` | Horizontal gridlines at the value ticks. |
| `ShowXAxis` | `bool` | `true` | The category (time) axis labels under the plot. |
| `ShowYAxis` | `bool` | `true` | The value axis labels in the right-hand gutter. |
| `YMinimum` | `double?` | `null` | Fixes the bottom of the value axis (default: zero, or the data minimum when it dips below). |
| `YMaximum` | `double?` | `null` | Fixes the top of the value axis (default: the next nice tick above the data). |
| `TickFormatter` | `Func<double, string>?` | `null` | Formats value-axis ticks. Defaults to a compact number, such as 1.2K. |
| `Curve` | `ChartCurve` | `Smooth` | Smooth monotone curves that never swing past the data, or straight segments. |
| `HiddenSeries` | `IReadOnlyList<string>?` | `null` | Keys of hidden series. Two-way; the legend toggles it. |
| `IsLoading` | `bool` | `false` | Keeps the current shapes on screen, dimmed and breathing, while the next range loads. |
| `Label` | `string` | `""` | What is measured, such as "Signups". Names the chart, its summary and its data table. |
| `Unit` | `string` | `""` | Unit after each value in readouts, such as "ms". |
| `EmptyLabel` | `string` | `"No data for this range"` | Shown when there is nothing to draw. |
| `CategoryLabel` | `string` | `"Date"` | Name of the category column in the data table and the explore label, such as "Date". |
| `ValueFormat` | `string?` | `null` | .NET format string for values (en-US), such as "N0", "C0" or "0.0'%'". Null uses the chart's default. |
| `ValueFormatter` | `Func<ChartValueContext, string>?` | `null` | Formats values with context (series, index); wins over `ValueFormat`. |
| `PlotHeight` | `double` | `220` | Plot height in pixels; the width follows the container. |
| `ItemsSource` | `IEnumerable?` | `null` | The data items. Values are read with `YSelector`/`YBinding` (or per series), categories with `XSelector`/`XBinding`. |
| `XBinding` | `BindingBase?` | `null` | Reads each item's category or date: the AOT-safe path form, such as `XBinding="{CompiledBinding Date, DataType=local:Day}"` (a reflection `{Binding Date}` also works). |
| `XSelector` | `Func<object, object?>?` | `null` | Reads each item's category or date (a string, DateTime, DateTimeOffset or DateOnly). |
| `YBinding` | `BindingBase?` | `null` | Reads each item's value for a single-series chart (`YBinding="{CompiledBinding Visits, DataType=local:Day}"`). |
| `YSelector` | `Func<object, double>?` | `null` | Reads each item's value for a single-series chart. |
| `XLabelFormatter` | `Func<object?, string>?` | `null` | Full label of a category (tooltip, headline, screen readers). Dates default to "Tue, Sep 15". |
| `XAxisFormatter` | `Func<object?, string?>?` | `null` | Short axis label of a category; return null to keep the axis quiet there. Dates default to "Sep 15". |
| `ActiveIndex` | `int?` | `null` | The point being read (crosshair, scrubbed bar, hovered segment), or null at rest. Two-way. |
| `Summary` | `string` | – | *Read-only.* A one-paragraph description for assistive technology, such as "Signups, Sep 1 to Sep 30. ...". |
| `DataTableText` | `string` | – | *Read-only.* The accessible data table as text: a header line, then one line per row (tab separated). |
| `Announcement` | `string` | – | *Read-only.* The latest polite announcement (what Arc's live region reads), such as "Loading". |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `HiddenSeriesChanged` | `ChartHiddenSeriesChangedEventArgs` | Raised when the legend shows or hides a series; the argument carries the hidden series keys. |
| `ActiveIndexChanged` | `ChartActiveIndexChangedEventArgs` | Raised as the readout moves between points, and with a null index when it is released. |

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

## Accessibility

- `Label` names the chart. The plot exposes the date range and the latest value of each series in a hidden summary, and
  a hidden data table lists every point.
- The plot is a focusable slider. Arrow keys move one point, PageUp and PageDown move about a sixth of the range, Home
  and End go to the first and last point, and Escape releases the crosshair.
- The readout for the active point names the date and each visible series with its value and unit, such as "Fri, Sep 4:
  This period 240 users, Previous 160 users". Keyboard focus starts the readout at the latest point.
- The legend entries are toggle buttons. Each series is identified by its name and its line style, not only by color.
- The loading state is announced politely as "Loading". The lines and the tooltip are hidden from assistive technology
  to avoid repeated reading.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` | Move between the legend toggles and the plot. Entering the plot from the keyboard selects the latest point |
| `Left` / `Down` | Move to the previous point. From rest, the first press lands on the latest point |
| `Right` / `Up` | Move to the next point. From rest, the first press lands on the latest point |
| `PageUp` / `PageDown` | Move about a sixth of the points; PageUp from rest lands on the latest point |
| `Home` / `End` | Move to the first or the last point |
| `Escape` | Release the crosshair and hide the tooltip |
| `Enter` / `Space` (on a legend toggle) | Show or hide that series |

Leaving the plot releases the crosshair. A mouse reads the nearest point while it hovers the plot. Touch reads on press
and drag, and releases when the finger lifts.

## Motion

- On first view the lines draw in from left to right, and the area fill is revealed with the line.
- A new range resamples the lines on shared x positions and morphs them from their current shape. The gridlines slide
  with the value axis.
- The crosshair glides between points, and the tooltip follows on its own spring and flips at the edges.
- Loading lines pulse until the data arrives. The pulse pauses when the chart leaves the viewport.
- Reduced motion skips the draw-in, the morph and the glide, and stops the loading pulse. Off jumps straight to the
  final state.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| First view | Lines draw in from the left over about 840 ms, and the area reveals with them | The lines fade in without the draw-in | Immediate |
| New range | Lines morph from their current shape; the value axis springs and the gridlines slide | Immediate | Immediate |
| Crosshair moves | Glides between points on a spring | Jumps to the point | Jumps to the point |
| Loading | Lines breathe, dimmed | Pulse stops | Pulse stops |

## Related

- `Sparkline` for a compact trend beside a value.
- `BarChart` for one measure compared across discrete days, weeks or months.
- `BrushChart` for a dense time series that needs zooming.
- `Streamgraph` when several series should be read as stacked layers.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `Sparkline` | The trend sits beside one number, with no axes or legend |
| `BarChart` | The categories are discrete days, weeks or months and each value stands alone |
| `DonutChart` | The data is a few parts of one whole |
| `BrushChart` | The history is long and the reader needs to zoom into a period |
| `Streamgraph` | Several layers should read as parts of one stacked total |
| `ActivityHeatmap` | The data is a grid of days, such as activity across a year |

---

# Bar chart

> Compare one measure across days and scrub any bar for its value.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/bar-chart

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.BarChartWeekAndMonthDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="16">
        <WrapPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center" ItemSpacing="12" LineSpacing="12">
            <arc:Button Content="Week" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Click="OnWeekClick" />
            <arc:Button Content="Month" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Click="OnMonthClick" />
        </WrapPanel>
        <arc:BarChart x:Name="Chart" Label="Active minutes" Unit="min" CategoryLabel="Day" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using System.Globalization;
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;
using TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Pages;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class BarChartWeekAndMonthDemo : UserControl
{
    private static readonly CultureInfo s_culture = CultureInfo.GetCultureInfo("en-US");

    public BarChartWeekAndMonthDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        ShowWeek();
    }

    private void OnWeekClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) => ShowWeek();

    private void OnMonthClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) => ShowMonth();

    // Bars with the same key morph to their new height; new bars grow in beside them.
    private void ShowWeek()
    {
        var days = ChartsADemoData.Days(7);
        var values = ChartsADemoData.Daily(7, 46, 30, 3);
        Chart.Period = "Sep 24–30, 2026";
        Chart.ItemsSource = days.Select((day, i) => new ChartPoint(day, values[i])
        {
            Label = day.ToString("dddd, MMM d", s_culture),
            AxisLabel = day.ToString("ddd", s_culture)
        }).ToArray();
    }

    private void ShowMonth()
    {
        var days = ChartsADemoData.Days(30);
        var values = ChartsADemoData.Daily(30, 40, 34, 9);
        Chart.Period = "September 2026";
        Chart.ItemsSource = days.Select((day, i) => new ChartPoint(day, values[i])).ToArray();
    }
}
```

## When to use

`BarChart` compares one measure across a run of days, weeks or months and lets the reader scrub any bar for its exact
value. The headline holds the average at rest, so the first thing a reader sees is the level of the measure, and the
bars show how each period compared with it. It fits a panel on an analytics page or an operations dashboard where the
question is "which days were unusual" rather than "how does this trend continue".

- **Daily active minutes in a product analytics page**: a product team compares active minutes per day across a week
  against the daily average, and scrubs the Thursday bar to see the exact total.
- **Deploys or releases per week in an engineering console**: each bar is a week that stands on its own, so the team
  reads which sprint shipped the most without a line implying a continuous trend.
- **Support tickets per day in a help desk dashboard**: a queue lead sees the spike on Monday and reads the count
  behind it, with the average line showing what a normal day looks like.
- **Revenue or order volume by month in a finance review**: a reference line for the monthly average makes the months
  above and below it obvious, and the value axis can be fixed so two periods are drawn to the same scale.
- **Usage per billing period in a metered-service console**: API calls or storage used per day, with the total for the
  period in the headline when the reader scrubs a bar.

## When not to use

- **A continuous trend over many points or several series**: use `LineChart`, which draws the line through the points
  and can show several series with a legend.
- **A compact trend beside a single value**: use `Sparkline`, which fits in a table cell or a KPI card.
- **A full year of daily activity as a grid**: use `ActivityHeatmap`, where each day is a square and the rhythm of weeks
  is the point.
- **Parts of one whole, such as traffic sources or spend categories**: use `DonutChart`, where the segments add up to a
  total.
- **A single value against a target or a limit**: use `Gauge` or `UsageMeter`, which show how full a measure is.

## Usage

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:BarChart Label="Active minutes"
                  Period="Sep 24–30, 2026"
                  Unit="min"
                  CategoryLabel="Day"
                  ItemsSource="{Binding Week}" />
</UserControl>
```

`BarChart` derives from `ChartBase`, the base of Arc's self-drawn charts. The base owns the data pipeline, the
palette, the first-view reveal, the readout keyboard model, the accessible summary and the hidden data table, so every
Arc chart reads and scrubs the same way. The bar chart adds the headline, the average line and the bar geometry on top.
The whole plot is drawn in one pass, which keeps a week or a month of bars cheap to update.

### Anatomy

1. **Headline kind** (`AverageLabel`, `ValueLabel`): the small label above the number. It reads "Daily average" at rest and
   "Total" while a bar is scrubbed. It sits in the secondary text color at the small type size.
2. **Headline value**: the average at rest, or the scrubbed bar's value, in the display font at the 3XL size with medium
   weight. Its digits roll to the new number. `Unit` follows the number, lifted onto its baseline, in the secondary color.
3. **Period and readout** (`Period`): under the headline, the range shown at rest ("Sep 24–30, 2026") and the scrubbed
   bar's full label ("Tuesday, Sep 22") while a bar is active. The row keeps its height so swaps never move the plot.
4. **Plot**: one bar per data point. A bar fills 58% of its slot and is at most 28 px wide. Wide containers gain spacing
   between the bars instead of thicker bars.
5. **Average line** (`ShowAverage`): a dashed reference line at the average, drawn across the plot.
6. **Value axis gutter**: 52 px on the right, holding the value ticks and a short "Avg" label for the average.
7. **Category axis row**: 26 px under the bars, holding the short axis labels (`AxisLabel`, or the date's short form).
8. **Gridlines** (`ShowGrid`): horizontal guides at the value ticks, drawn behind the bars.

The headline and the plot are separated by 20 px. The plot height defaults to 176 px and is set with `PlotHeight`; the
width follows the container.

### Ranges

Replace `ItemsSource` and `Period` together when the range changes. A bar keeps its identity across the change when
its key is the same, so a day that stays in the range morphs to its new height and position, and a new bar grows in
beside it. The key defaults to the category value, so a date keeps its key; set `ChartPoint.Key` yourself when the
category is not unique or not stable.

```csharp
void ShowWeek()
{
    var culture = CultureInfo.GetCultureInfo("en-US");
    var start = new DateOnly(2026, 9, 24);
    int[] minutes = [46, 30, 52, 61, 38, 27, 44];
    chart.Period = "Sep 24–30, 2026";
    chart.ItemsSource = Enumerable.Range(0, minutes.Length).Select(i =>
    {
        var day = start.AddDays(i);
        return new ChartPoint(day, minutes[i])
        {
            Label = day.ToString("dddd, MMM d", culture),
            AxisLabel = day.ToString("ddd", culture)
        };
    }).ToArray();
}
```

`ChartPoint` is a record with the category, the value and optional text. `ChartPoint.Label` is the full name read to
assistive technology and shown in the readout. `ChartPoint.AxisLabel` is the short text under the bar; leave it null
to keep the axis quiet at that bar. The readout and the announcement use the same full names, so a range change tells the
reader the new period and the new average at once.

Set `IsLoading` while the next range is fetched. The current shapes stay on screen, dimmed and breathing, until the new
data arrives, so the page does not flash empty between two ranges.

### Headline labels

`AverageLabel` names the resting headline and `ValueLabel` names the value of a scrubbed bar. The defaults are "Daily
average" and "Total". Change them to the measure's own vocabulary, such as "Weekly average" for weekly bars, and hide the
average line with `ShowAverage` when a reference is not useful for the reader.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.BarChartWithoutAverageDemo">
    <arc:BarChart x:Name="Chart"
                  Label="Deploys"
                  Period="Last 12 weeks"
                  AverageLabel="Weekly average"
                  ValueLabel="Deploys"
                  CategoryLabel="Week"
                  ShowAverage="False"
                  PlotHeight="140" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class BarChartWithoutAverageDemo : UserControl
{
    public BarChartWithoutAverageDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();

        // Categories as strings.
        Chart.ItemsSource = Enumerable.Range(0, 12)
            .Select(i => new ChartPoint($"W{i + 27}", 4 + (i * 7 % 9)))
            .ToArray();
    }
}
```

```xml
<arc:BarChart Label="Deploys"
              Period="Last 12 weeks"
              AverageLabel="Weekly average"
              ValueLabel="Deploys"
              CategoryLabel="Week"
              ShowAverage="False"
              PlotHeight="140"
              ItemsSource="{Binding Weeks}" />
```

`Average` is the mean of all values and is read-only, so a caption or a status line can show the same number as the
headline. The average line itself is a reference drawn from the data, not a target.

### Value formatting and axes

`ValueFormat` takes a .NET format string in en-US, such as `N0` for grouped whole numbers, `C0` for currency or
`0.0'%'` for a percent with one decimal. A `ValueFormatter` receives the value with its index and series and wins over
`ValueFormat` when both are set, which is the right choice when the label depends on the bar, such as "3 incidents, 1
critical". The `Unit` text is appended to readouts such as "50 min" and to the data table.

`ShowGrid`, `ShowXAxis` and `ShowYAxis` control the guides and the labels. `YMinimum` fixes the bottom of the value axis
and `YMaximum` fixes its top. By default the axis starts at zero, or at the lowest value when data dips below zero, and
ends at the next nice tick above the largest value. Fix `YMaximum` when two charts on one page must share a scale, and
`TickFormatter` formats the tick labels when they need a different format from the values.

```xml
<arc:BarChart Label="Tickets" YMaximum="100" ShowGrid="False" ItemsSource="{Binding Tickets}" />
```

### Reading values

`ActiveIndex` is the bar under the pointer or the keyboard, or null at rest, and it is two-way. `ActiveIndexChanged`
reports every move, with the index, the item, the label and the values at that point. Use it to show a value in a
status line outside the chart.

```csharp
chart.ActiveIndexChanged += (_, e) => status.Text = e.Index is null
    ? $"Average {chart.Average:N0}"
    : e.Label;
```

`Summary` is the one-paragraph description for assistive technology, such as "Active minutes, Sep 15–21. Daily average
40 min. Highest Thursday, 60 min. Lowest Wednesday, 20 min." `DataTableText` is the same data as a tab-separated table,
with a header line and one line per bar, for example "Day\tActive minutes" followed by "Mon\t10 min". The table is
hidden from sight and available to assistive technology, so the chart can be read without seeing the bars.

### Data shape and performance

The chart reads its data once per change of `ItemsSource`, not on every redraw. Use `ChartPoint` for data that is
already in memory: `new ChartPoint(category, value)` takes an object for the category, so a `DateOnly`, a `DateTime`, a
string or a number all work, and the default axis labels format dates as "Sep 15" and full labels as "Tue, Sep 15".
When the data arrives as rows, read it with `XSelector` and `YSelector` or with `XBinding` and `YBinding`. The compiled
binding form, such as `YBinding="{CompiledBinding Visits, DataType=local:Day}"`, is the AOT-safe path.

A week or a month of bars is well within what the chart handles smoothly. For a long series prefer a `LineChart`, or
aggregate the data into weeks, because the bars become thin and the category labels thin out. The hidden data table
grows with the number of bars, so keep the range to what a reader can scan.

### Example: weekly active minutes for a product team

A product analytics page for the week of September 24 to 30, 2026. The headline shows the daily average, the period sits
under it, and the bars use short weekday labels on the axis. The team reads that Thursday was the peak and Wednesday
the trough, which is what the summary line also says. The screenshot is not shown here because the bars and the
headline number are drawn from code-supplied data (see the Demo above for a live example); the XAML needs the same
`ItemsSource` as the code sample.

```xml
<arc:BarChart Label="Active minutes"
              Period="Sep 24–30, 2026"
              Unit="min"
              CategoryLabel="Day"
              ItemsSource="{Binding ActiveMinutesThisWeek}" />
```

### Content guidelines

- **Label**: name the measure in sentence case, such as "Active minutes" or "Support tickets". It names the chart, the
  summary and the data table, so it must make sense on its own.
- **Period**: a readable range with the year, such as "Sep 24–30, 2026" or "Last 12 weeks". The period is announced
  when the range changes, so it must be specific.
- **Unit**: a short unit after the value, such as "min", "ms" or "calls". Write the full word in the label when the unit
  is long.
- **Average and value labels**: use the measure's vocabulary: "Weekly average" for weekly bars, "Deploys" for a count.
- **Category label**: the singular noun for one bar, "Day", "Week" or "Month", used as the column name in the data table.

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| Data | Active minutes |
| Avg | Daily average |
| Sep 24 - 30 | Sep 24–30, 2026 |
| Items (count) | Support tickets |
| Value | Total |

### Best practices

**Do**

- Give every chart a `Label` and a `Period`. The label names the chart for screen readers and the period is announced
  when it changes, so a reader always knows what the bars count and over which days.
- Keep the bars in one range and one unit per chart. Mixing minutes and calls in one chart makes the average meaningless.
- Set `YMaximum` when two charts must be compared side by side, so the same height means the same value on both.
- Set `Key` on `ChartPoint` when the category is not a stable identifier, so the bars morph across a range change
  instead of being redrawn.
- Use `ActiveIndexChanged` to show the scrubbed value outside the chart when the headline is not enough.

**Avoid**

- Drawing a line through unrelated categories. A bar per category keeps the reader from reading a trend between days
  that have nothing to do with each other.
- Hiding the average line when the average is the story. Leave `ShowAverage` on when the reader asks whether a day was
  above or below normal.
- Using a bar chart for a long series of bars. The bars become too thin to scrub, and a line or an aggregated
  view reads better.
- Changing `ItemsSource` many times a second. Each change morphs the bars and the average line, so frequent changes make
  the chart move without telling the reader anything.
- Relying on the colors of the bars alone. The headline, the readout and the data table carry the values, so the
  chart works for readers who cannot see the bar heights.

### Common questions

**Why does the headline show the average and not the latest bar?** At rest the headline is the average, which is the
reference for the whole range. The headline changes to the scrubbed bar's value while the pointer or the keyboard is on a
bar, and it returns to the average when the readout is released with Escape or when the focus leaves the plot.

**How do I set the scrubbed bar from code?** `ActiveIndex` is two-way: setting it moves the headline and the readout to
that bar, and setting it to null returns the headline to the average. Use it to restore a selection or to link the chart
with a list that the reader picks from.

**Why are the bars not the same width when I resize the page?** The bar width is capped at 28 px and fills 58% of its
slot. On a wide plot the extra width becomes spacing between the bars, so bars stay the same thickness and the gaps grow.

**Why does the first view animate and later changes not?** The bars grow once, left to right, the first time the chart
is seen. Later changes morph the bars from their current heights to the new ones, so a reader sees the change, not the
initial growth again.

**How do I format the value in the readout differently from the axis?** Set `ValueFormat` or `ValueFormatter` for the
values and `TickFormatter` for the value axis. The two are separate, so a value such as "1,284 min" can read in full
while the axis uses a compact format such as "1.3K".

## API reference

### BarChart

Arc's bar chart: one measure across a run of days, weeks or months, with an average reference line and a headline that reads the average at rest and the scrubbed bar while exploring. Bars grow in a left-to-right wave the first time the chart is seen; a new range zooms the slots around the latest bar while bars that keep their key morph, new ones grow beside them and leaving ones sink into the baseline. Motion is code-driven (`MotionValue` per bar) because bar heights, slots and the scale are coordinates inside the self-drawn plot, which ControlTheme transitions cannot reach.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Period` | `string` | `""` | The range on show, such as "Sep 15–21, 2026". It rests under the headline. |
| `AverageLabel` | `string` | `"Daily average"` | Headline label at rest, above the average. |
| `ValueLabel` | `string` | `"Total"` | Headline label while a bar is scrubbed. |
| `ShowAverage` | `bool` | `true` | Draws the average as a dashed reference line that springs to each new range. |
| `ShowGrid` | `bool` | `true` | Draws the gridlines behind the plot (default true). |
| `ShowXAxis` | `bool` | `true` | Shows the category (time) axis labels under the plot (default true). |
| `ShowYAxis` | `bool` | `true` | Shows the value axis labels in the right-hand gutter (default true). |
| `YMaximum` | `double?` | `null` | Fixes the top of the value axis; by default it is the next nice tick above the data. |
| `TickFormatter` | `Func<double, string>?` | `null` | Formats value-axis ticks. Defaults to the value format (Arc formats ticks like values). |
| `Label` | `string` | `""` | What is measured, such as "Signups". Names the chart, its summary and its data table. |
| `Unit` | `string` | `""` | Unit after each value in readouts, such as "ms". |
| `EmptyLabel` | `string` | `"No data for this range"` | Shown when there is nothing to draw. |
| `CategoryLabel` | `string` | `"Day"` | Name of the category column in the data table and the explore label, such as "Date". |
| `ValueFormat` | `string?` | `null` | .NET format string for values (en-US), such as "N0", "C0" or "0.0'%'". Null uses the chart's default. |
| `ValueFormatter` | `Func<ChartValueContext, string>?` | `null` | Formats values with context (series, index); wins over `ValueFormat`. |
| `PlotHeight` | `double` | `176` | Plot height in pixels; the width follows the container. |
| `ItemsSource` | `IEnumerable?` | `null` | The data items. Values are read with `YSelector`/`YBinding` (or per series), categories with `XSelector`/`XBinding`. |
| `XBinding` | `BindingBase?` | `null` | Reads each item's category or date: the AOT-safe path form, such as `XBinding="{CompiledBinding Date, DataType=local:Day}"` (a reflection `{Binding Date}` also works). |
| `XSelector` | `Func<object, object?>?` | `null` | Reads each item's category or date (a string, DateTime, DateTimeOffset or DateOnly). |
| `YBinding` | `BindingBase?` | `null` | Reads each item's value for a single-series chart (`YBinding="{CompiledBinding Visits, DataType=local:Day}"`). |
| `YSelector` | `Func<object, double>?` | `null` | Reads each item's value for a single-series chart. |
| `XLabelFormatter` | `Func<object?, string>?` | `null` | Full label of a category (tooltip, headline, screen readers). Dates default to "Tue, Sep 15". |
| `XAxisFormatter` | `Func<object?, string?>?` | `null` | Short axis label of a category; return null to keep the axis quiet there. Dates default to "Sep 15". |
| `ActiveIndex` | `int?` | `null` | The point being read (crosshair, scrubbed bar, hovered segment), or null at rest. Two-way. |
| `Summary` | `string` | – | *Read-only.* A one-paragraph description for assistive technology, such as "Signups, Sep 1 to Sep 30. ...". |
| `DataTableText` | `string` | – | *Read-only.* The accessible data table as text: a header line, then one line per row (tab separated). |
| `Announcement` | `string` | – | *Read-only.* The latest polite announcement (what Arc's live region reads), such as "Loading". |
| `ShowLegend` | `bool?` | `null` | Series toggles. Null shows the legend when there is more than one series. |
| `YMinimum` | `double?` | `null` | Fixes the bottom of the value axis (default: zero, or the data minimum when it dips below). |
| `Curve` | `ChartCurve` | `Smooth` | Smooth monotone curves that never swing past the data, or straight segments. |
| `HiddenSeries` | `IReadOnlyList<string>?` | `null` | Keys of hidden series. Two-way; the legend toggles it. |
| `IsLoading` | `bool` | `false` | Keeps the current shapes on screen, dimmed and breathing, while the next range loads. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ActiveIndexChanged` | `ChartActiveIndexChangedEventArgs` | Raised as the readout moves between points, and with a null index when it is released. |
| `HiddenSeriesChanged` | `ChartHiddenSeriesChangedEventArgs` | Raised when the legend shows or hides a series. |

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

## Accessibility

- `Label` names the chart. The summary names the average, the highest and the lowest bar.
- The arrow keys move between bars, PageUp and PageDown move up to seven bars, Home and End go to the first and last bar,
  and Escape stops scrubbing and returns to the average.
- A hidden data table lists every value, so the chart can be read without seeing the bars.
- A change of range is announced politely.
- The bars are hidden from assistive technology. The scrub position is shown by a cursor, not by a focus ring.
- The plot is a focusable element that assistive technology reads as a slider, so each bar's full label and value are
  read as the readout moves.

### Keyboard

The plot takes focus as one tab stop. Keyboard focus starts on the latest bar, so the most recent value is read first.

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` | Move focus into the plot on the latest bar, or out of it |
| `Left` / `Right`, `Down` / `Up` | Move to the previous or next bar; the first press from rest starts from the latest bar |
| `PageUp` / `PageDown` | Move up to seven bars earlier or later |
| `Home` / `End` | Move to the first or the last bar |
| `Escape` | Stop scrubbing and return the headline to the average |

Losing focus clears the readout, so the headline returns to the average when the reader leaves the chart.

## Motion

- On first view the bars grow in one after another, from left to right.
- A change of range morphs the kept bars, the axis ticks and the average line to their new values, and the bars that
  leave sink into the baseline.
- The scrub cursor glides between bars, and the headline value rolls to the new number.
- The headline label swaps between the average and the value label with a short blur.
- Reduced motion shows the bars at their final size and replaces the numbers in place. Off jumps straight to the final
  state.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| First view | Bars grow in a left-to-right wave | Bars at their final size | Immediate |
| New range | Kept bars morph, new bars grow beside them, leaving bars sink | Bars at their final size | Immediate |
| Scrubbing a bar | The cursor glides to the bar and the headline value rolls | The headline value is replaced in place | Immediate |
| Headline label | Swaps between the average and the value label with a short blur | Replaced in place | Immediate |

Motion here follows the data. A bar that keeps its key morphs, so the reader can follow one day across two ranges. Keep
the first-view wave for the chart that is the reason for the section; on a dashboard that updates often, the morphs on
each refresh add up, so refresh the data on a schedule that matches how often the numbers change.

## Related

- `LineChart` for a continuous trend over many points.
- `Sparkline` for a compact trend in a table cell or a card.
- `ActivityHeatmap` for a year of daily activity.
- `DonutChart` when the bars should show parts of a whole.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `LineChart` | The trend over many points, or several series, matters more than single periods |
| `Sparkline` | A compact trend sits beside a number in a table or a card |
| `ActivityHeatmap` | A full year of daily activity is shown as a grid of squares |
| `DonutChart` | The values are parts of one whole that add up to a total |
| `AnimatedCounter` | A single changing number is the whole message, without a chart |

# Donut chart

> A donut whose arcs morph between datasets, with the active value rolling into the center.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/donut-chart

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.DonutChartToggleSegmentsDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="16">
        <WrapPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center" ItemSpacing="12" LineSpacing="12">
            <arc:Button Content="This month" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Click="OnMonthClick" />
            <arc:Button Content="This quarter" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Click="OnQuarterClick" />
        </WrapPanel>
        <arc:DonutChart x:Name="Chart" Label="Visits by source" Unit="visits" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class DonutChartToggleSegmentsDemo : UserControl
{
    private static readonly ChartPoint[] s_month =
    [
        new("Search", 4820) { Key = "search" },
        new("Direct", 2960) { Key = "direct" },
        new("Social", 1840) { Key = "social" },
        new("Referral", 1210) { Key = "referral" },
        new("Email", 260) { Key = "email" },
        new("Podcasts", 140) { Key = "podcasts" }
    ];

    private static readonly ChartPoint[] s_quarter =
    [
        new("Search", 13900) { Key = "search" },
        new("Direct", 9800) { Key = "direct" },
        new("Social", 7200) { Key = "social" },
        new("Referral", 2600) { Key = "referral" },
        new("Email", 1900) { Key = "email" },
        new("Podcasts", 420) { Key = "podcasts" }
    ];

    public DonutChartToggleSegmentsDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Chart.ItemsSource = s_month;
    }

    // Segments keep their key, so the arcs move from their current angles to the new ones.
    private void OnMonthClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) => Chart.ItemsSource = s_month;

    private void OnQuarterClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) => Chart.ItemsSource = s_quarter;
}
```

## When to use

`DonutChart` shows how a whole divides into a few parts. The ring gives the shape of the split at a glance, the
legend beside it gives each part's value and share, and the center reads the total or the part under the pointer.
It fits a card or a panel on a dashboard, where the question is "what makes up this number" and the answer has two to
six parts.

- **Visit sources on a marketing overview**: Acme Analytics shows where this week's 48,200 visits came from (search,
  direct, social, email). The legend keeps every source readable, and small sources fold into Other instead of
  becoming slivers.
- **Spend by category on a finance page**: a controller reviews the month's spend as salaries, cloud hosting, marketing
  and software. Pinning a category in the legend keeps its value in the center while the controller reads the table.
- **Storage use on an admin console**: a workspace owner sees which projects take the most storage. Parts below a
  few percent group into Other, and the owner can hide a project to see how the rest of the ring changes.
- **Ticket status mix in a support dashboard**: the share of open, waiting and resolved tickets, switched between this
  month and this quarter with a dataset change that moves the arcs instead of redrawing the ring.

## When not to use

- **Many parts, or an exact comparison between them**: use `BarChart`. A ring makes twelve slices hard to compare, and
  the eye reads lengths better than angles.
- **A single value against a known limit**: use `Gauge` for a reading against a range with thresholds, or `UsageMeter`
  for a quota that people watch fill up.
- **A change over time**: use `LineChart`. A ring shows one moment, so a trend drawn as a series of rings hides the
  order.
- **Shares that people count, such as seats or cells of a grid**: use `WaffleChart`, which shows one cell per percent
  and reads as a count.
- **Parts nested inside parts that need drill-down**: use `Treemap`, which keeps the hierarchy and sizes the rectangles
  by value.

## Usage

Each `ChartPoint` is one segment. Give every point a stable `Key` so the segments keep their identity when the data
changes. Values that are zero or less are ignored.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:DonutChart Label="Visits by source"
                    Unit="visits"
                    TotalLabel="Total"
                    OtherLabel="Other"
                    ItemsSource="{Binding Sources}" />
</UserControl>
```

`DonutChart` derives from `ChartBase`, the base of the Arc chart family, so `Label`, `Unit`, `ValueFormat`,
`EmptyLabel` and `ItemsSource` behave as they do on the other charts. The donut adds the ring, the synced legend, the
center readout and the grouping rules. Because the ring is self-drawn, every arc is one drawing and a dataset change
moves the existing arcs instead of re-creating controls.

### Anatomy

1. **Ring**: the arcs, drawn with a 3 px gap between neighbours and 4 px rounded corners. The ring is 208 px across by
   default (`Diameter`) and 24 px thick (`RingThickness`). In a narrower container it scales down to fit.
2. **Center readout**: three short lines in the middle of the ring. At rest the top line is the total label
   (`TotalLabel`), the middle line the total value, and the bottom line the unit. Under a pointer or a pinned segment
   the lines show the segment's label, its value and its share with the total, for example "60% of total". The label and
   unit lines have a fixed height (12 px text at a 1.4 line height), so a change never moves the number.
3. **Legend rows**: one row per visible segment, with a color swatch, the label, the value and the share. The legend
   sits beside the ring when the container is at least 460 px wide, and below it otherwise.
4. **Other segment**: the grouped small parts. Its row names the parts it holds, and its tooltip and announcement list
   them.
5. **Focus ring**: drawn only for keyboard focus, around the legend row or, without a legend, around the ring.

Segment colors come from the series palette and are assigned by key the first time a key is seen, so a category keeps
its color when the dataset changes. Share text uses whole percents, and a share above zero but under one percent reads
"<1%".

### Sizes and grouping

`Diameter` and `RingThickness` set the ring. Parts whose share is below `GroupBelow` (a fraction of the total, 0.04 by
default) and parts beyond `MaxSegments` (6 by default, counting Other) fold into the Other segment. Grouping needs at
least two parts to fold: a single small part stays on its own, because grouping one part would hide it for nothing.

```xml
<arc:DonutChart Label="Storage"
                Diameter="160"
                RingThickness="18"
                GroupBelow="0.05"
                MaxSegments="5"
                ItemsSource="{Binding Storage}" />
```

Use a larger `GroupBelow` for a dashboard tile where small slices only add noise, and a smaller one for a finance page
where every category must be visible. Raise `MaxSegments` only when the legend has room: each extra row costs one line of
height beside or below the ring.

### Datasets

Replace `ItemsSource` to switch the dataset. The arcs keep their order and move from their current angles to the new
ones, so the segments do not re-mount. A segment whose key is new appears at its place in the order; a segment that
leaves closes to nothing before it drops out.

```csharp
month.Click += (_, _) => chart.ItemsSource = s_month;
quarter.Click += (_, _) => chart.ItemsSource = s_quarter;
```

Keep the keys the same across the datasets (`"search"` in both months, not `"Search"` in one and `"search-ads"` in the
other). A changed key is a different segment: it loses its color history and its hidden state.

### Legend and hidden segments

The legend hides and shows segments by default. Set `ShowLegend="False"` for a ring alone. `HiddenKeys` lists the
hidden keys and is two-way, so the view model can keep it. A hidden segment closes and the rest of the ring
redistributes, and the total in the center counts only the visible segments. The last visible segment cannot be
hidden, so the ring never becomes empty by accident.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.DonutChartRingOnlyDemo">
    <arc:DonutChart x:Name="Chart"
                    Label="Storage"
                    ShowLegend="False"
                    Diameter="160"
                    RingThickness="18"
                    HorizontalAlignment="Left" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class DonutChartRingOnlyDemo : UserControl
{
    public DonutChartRingOnlyDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Chart.ItemsSource = new[]
        {
            new ChartPoint("Photos", 41),
            new ChartPoint("Video", 27),
            new ChartPoint("Documents", 12),
            new ChartPoint("Free", 20)
        };
    }
}
```

```xml
<arc:DonutChart Label="Visits by source"
                HiddenKeys="{Binding HiddenKeys}"
                ShowLegend="True"
                ItemsSource="{Binding Sources}" />
```

A ring without a legend is a keyboard stop of its own: the arrow keys read each segment in turn. Use it when space
is tight and the ring already carries its meaning, such as a storage gauge on a card with a caption beside it.

### Pinning a segment

Set `LegendAction="Select"` to pin a segment instead of hiding it. `ActiveKey` holds the pinned key and is two-way.
Clicking a segment on the ring also pins it, in either mode. A pinned segment stays in the center readout until it is
released or another segment is pinned. `ActiveKeyChanged` fires when the pin changes, and the view model can read
`ActiveKey` in its handler or bind it.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.DonutChartSelectDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12">
        <arc:DonutChart x:Name="Chart"
                        Label="Spend by category"
                        LegendAction="Select"
                        ValueFormat="$#,##0"
                        ActiveKeyChanged="OnActiveKeyChanged" />
        <TextBlock x:Name="Pinned"
                   Text="Click a row or a segment to pin it."
                   TextWrapping="Wrap"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class DonutChartSelectDemo : UserControl
{
    public DonutChartSelectDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Chart.ItemsSource = new[]
        {
            new ChartPoint("Payroll", 64200),
            new ChartPoint("Cloud", 18400),
            new ChartPoint("Software", 9200),
            new ChartPoint("Travel", 4100),
            new ChartPoint("Office", 2300)
        };
    }

    private void OnActiveKeyChanged(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
        => Pinned.Text = Chart.ActiveKey is { } key ? $"Pinned: {key}" : "Click a row or a segment to pin it.";
}
```

```xml
<arc:DonutChart Label="Spend by category"
                LegendAction="Select"
                ValueFormat="$#,##0"
                ActiveKey="{Binding PinnedCategory}"
                ItemsSource="{Binding Spend}" />
```

### Binding to a view model

The view model owns the data, the hidden keys and the pinned category. The chart shows them and writes the reader's
choices back. With CommunityToolkit.Mvvm:

```csharp
public partial class SpendViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    private static readonly IReadOnlyList<ChartPoint> s_october =
    [
        new ChartPoint("Salaries", 9800) { Key = "salaries" },
        new ChartPoint("Cloud hosting", 4120) { Key = "cloud" },
        new ChartPoint("Marketing", 2250) { Key = "marketing" },
        new ChartPoint("Software", 1350) { Key = "software" },
        new ChartPoint("Office", 640) { Key = "office" },
        new ChartPoint("Travel", 380) { Key = "travel" }
    ];

    [ObservableProperty]
    private IReadOnlyList<ChartPoint> _spend = s_october;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private IReadOnlyList<string> _hiddenKeys = [];

    [ObservableProperty]
    private string? _pinnedCategory;
}
```

```xml
<arc:DonutChart Label="Spend by category"
                ItemsSource="{Binding Spend}"
                HiddenKeys="{Binding HiddenKeys}"
                ActiveKey="{Binding PinnedCategory}"
                LegendAction="Select"
                ValueFormat="$#,##0" />
```

- `HiddenKeys` and `ActiveKey` are two-way. A legend toggle writes the new list back, so the view model sees every
  change, including changes made with the keyboard.
- Replace the `HiddenKeys` list instead of editing it in place, because the chart reacts to the property assignment.
- `ItemsSource` is replaced on reload. Keep the keys stable so the arcs move instead of re-creating.
- `ValueFormat` (`$#,##0`) applies to the legend, the center and the announcements. Set it once on the chart rather
  than formatting the strings in the view model.

### Example: spend by category on a billing page

A finance controller opens the month's spend and sees where the money went before reading the table below. The ring
shows the split, the legend lists each category with its value and share, and the Other row groups the two small
categories so they do not clutter the ring. Office and travel together stay under the 4 percent threshold, so they fold
into Other, and the legend names both categories on that row. The view model pins the cloud hosting segment (`PinnedCategory` set to
`"cloud"`), so the center shows its value and share instead of the total. The chart is 620 px wide, so the legend sits beside the ring rather than
below it. The view model above supplies the points, so this page has no screenshot: the chart draws nothing from
markup alone.

```xml
<StackPanel Width="620" Spacing="16">
    <TextBlock Text="Spend by category, October 2026"
               FontSize="16"
               FontWeight="Medium"
               Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
    <arc:DonutChart Label="Spend by category"
                    ValueFormat="$#,##0"
                    LegendAction="Select"
                    ActiveKey="{Binding PinnedCategory}"
                    ItemsSource="{Binding Spend}" />
</StackPanel>
```

### Content guidelines

Name each segment by what it is, and let the chart title say what the whole is. The legend and the center read the
segment label aloud, so a short noun phrase works better than a sentence.

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| Visits | Visits by source |
| Other stuff | Other (a legend row lists its members) |
| Search engines and paid ads | Search |
| 0.4% | <1% (the chart writes this for small shares) |
| 48200 visits | 48,200 visits (`ValueFormat="N0"`) |
| Click a slice to see details | Click a segment to pin it |

Keep `TotalLabel` a single word such as Total, Visits or Spend, since it is the label on the center line at rest. Use
sentence case for labels, and spell out the unit that the reader needs, such as "visits" or "USD", in `Unit` rather
than repeating it in each label.

### Best practices

**Do**

- Use two to six segments. Each additional segment shrinks the arcs the reader must tell apart, and the legend is the
  reliable way to compare them.
- Give every point a stable `Key` that does not depend on the label. A key that changes on a rename gives the segment a
  new color and drops its hidden state.
- Keep the legend on for a financial or operational page. The legend is the keyboard path and the only place that
  shows each value and share.
- Set `GroupBelow` and `MaxSegments` deliberately so that Other holds only the parts too small to read.
- Pin the segment the page is about, through `ActiveKey`, so the center answers the question the page asks.

**Avoid**

- Rings for a long list or for a precise comparison. Use `BarChart` when the reader must rank the parts.
- Data that does not sum to a meaningful whole, such as overlapping categories. A segment that is counted in two places
  makes the shares wrong and the total meaningless.
- Hiding segments in the view model as the only way to show a subset. Filter the data in the view model instead when the
  hidden parts should not be counted in the total at all.
- Long labels on a narrow legend. The label is trimmed with an ellipsis, and the full name is kept in the tooltip and the
  announcement.
- Changing the keys between datasets. The arcs then close and re-open instead of moving to their new sizes.

### Common questions

**Why is a small segment missing from the ring?** It folded into Other, because its share was below `GroupBelow` (4
percent by default) or it ranked beyond `MaxSegments`. Hover the Other row or read its name in the legend to see its
members. A single small part is never folded into Other, so a part that is missing and not in Other has a value of zero
or less.

**Can the total stay on screen while a segment is pinned?** No. The center shows the pinned segment, its value and its
share instead of the total. If the page must show both, put the total in your own text next to the chart and bind it to
the same `Total` value you read from the view model.

**Does the total include hidden segments?** No. `Total` sums the visible segments, so hiding "Search" lowers the total
and the shares recalculate. Announcements read the new total after each toggle.

**How do I tell the chart to ignore a category?** Remove it from the data, or give it a value of zero or less. Values
that are zero or negative are ignored and never draw a segment.

**Can I change the ring size on a narrow card?** Set `Diameter` to the size you want, and the ring scales down to fit a
narrower container on its own. A card that is narrower than the legend breakpoint stacks the legend below the ring.

## API reference

### DonutChart

Arc's donut chart: a few parts of one whole. The legend and the ring show and hide segments together, the center reads the active segment (or the total at rest) and rolls like a drum between readouts, small parts fold into "Other", and new data moves every arc from where it is on screen, keeping its velocity. The first time the chart is seen all segments sweep out of the top together, each trailing edge a beat behind. Arc interpolates start and end angles rather than paths; every angle is a `MotionValue` written into one self-drawn ring, which ControlTheme transitions cannot express.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `TotalLabel` | `string` | `"Total"` | Center label at rest, above the total. |
| `OtherLabel` | `string` | `"Other"` | Label of the segment that holds the grouped small parts. |
| `Diameter` | `double` | `208` | Ring diameter in pixels; the ring scales down to fit narrower containers. |
| `RingThickness` | `double` | `24` | Ring thickness in pixels. |
| `GroupBelow` | `double` | `0.04` | Segments below this share of the total join "Other" (only when at least two would). |
| `MaxSegments` | `int` | `6` | The most segments drawn, counting "Other". |
| `ActiveKey` | `string?` | `null` | The selected (pinned) segment key. Hover and focus preview other segments without changing it. Two-way. |
| `HiddenKeys` | `IReadOnlyList<string>?` | `null` | Keys of hidden segments. A hidden segment closes and the rest of the ring redistributes. Two-way. |
| `LegendAction` | `DonutLegendAction` | `Toggle` | What clicking a legend row does. |
| `ShowLegend` | `bool` | `true` | The synced legend beside (at least 460px wide) or below the ring. |
| `Label` | `string` | `""` | What is measured, such as "Signups". Names the chart, its summary and its data table. |
| `Unit` | `string` | `""` | Unit after each value in readouts, such as "ms". |
| `EmptyLabel` | `string` | `"No data yet"` | Shown when there is nothing to draw. |
| `CategoryLabel` | `string` | `"Segment"` | Name of the category column in the data table and the explore label, such as "Date". |
| `ValueFormat` | `string?` | `null` | .NET format string for values (en-US), such as "N0", "C0" or "0.0'%'". Null uses the chart's default. |
| `ValueFormatter` | `Func<ChartValueContext, string>?` | `null` | Formats values with context (series, index); wins over `ValueFormat`. |
| `PlotHeight` | `double` | `220` | Plot height in pixels; the width follows the container. |
| `ItemsSource` | `IEnumerable?` | `null` | The data items. Values are read with `YSelector`/`YBinding` (or per series), categories with `XSelector`/`XBinding`. |
| `XBinding` | `BindingBase?` | `null` | Reads each item's category or date: the AOT-safe path form, such as `XBinding="{CompiledBinding Date, DataType=local:Day}"` (a reflection `{Binding Date}` also works). |
| `XSelector` | `Func<object, object?>?` | `null` | Reads each item's category or date (a string, DateTime, DateTimeOffset or DateOnly). |
| `YBinding` | `BindingBase?` | `null` | Reads each item's value for a single-series chart (`YBinding="{CompiledBinding Visits, DataType=local:Day}"`). |
| `YSelector` | `Func<object, double>?` | `null` | Reads each item's value for a single-series chart. |
| `XLabelFormatter` | `Func<object?, string>?` | `null` | Full label of a category (tooltip, headline, screen readers). Dates default to "Tue, Sep 15". |
| `XAxisFormatter` | `Func<object?, string?>?` | `null` | Short axis label of a category; return null to keep the axis quiet there. Dates default to "Sep 15". |
| `ActiveIndex` | `int?` | `null` | The point being read (crosshair, scrubbed bar, hovered segment), or null at rest. Two-way. |
| `Summary` | `string` | – | *Read-only.* A one-paragraph description for assistive technology, such as "Signups, Sep 1 to Sep 30. ...". |
| `DataTableText` | `string` | – | *Read-only.* The accessible data table as text: a header line, then one line per row (tab separated). |
| `Announcement` | `string` | – | *Read-only.* The latest polite announcement (what Arc's live region reads), such as "Loading". |
| `ShowGrid` | `bool` | `true` | Horizontal gridlines at the value ticks. |
| `ShowXAxis` | `bool` | `true` | The category (time) axis labels under the plot. |
| `ShowYAxis` | `bool` | `true` | The value axis labels in the right-hand gutter. |
| `YMinimum` | `double?` | `null` | Fixes the bottom of the value axis (default: zero, or the data minimum when it dips below). |
| `YMaximum` | `double?` | `null` | Fixes the top of the value axis (default: the next nice tick above the data). |
| `TickFormatter` | `Func<double, string>?` | `null` | Formats value-axis ticks. Defaults to a compact number, such as 1.2K. |
| `Curve` | `ChartCurve` | `Smooth` | Smooth monotone curves that never swing past the data, or straight segments. |
| `HiddenSeries` | `IReadOnlyList<string>?` | `null` | Keys of hidden series. Two-way; the legend toggles it. |
| `IsLoading` | `bool` | `false` | Keeps the current shapes on screen, dimmed and breathing, while the next range loads. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ActiveKeyChanged` | `RoutedEventArgs` | Raised when the selected segment changes. |
| `HiddenKeysChanged` | `ChartHiddenSeriesChangedEventArgs` | Raised when the legend shows or hides a segment. |
| `ActiveIndexChanged` | `ChartActiveIndexChangedEventArgs` | Raised as the readout moves between points, and with a null index when it is released. |
| `HiddenSeriesChanged` | `ChartHiddenSeriesChangedEventArgs` | Raised when the legend shows or hides a series. |

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

### Legend action

| Member | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `DonutLegendAction.Toggle` | A legend row shows or hides its segment (the default) |
| `DonutLegendAction.Select` | A legend row pins its segment as `ActiveKey`; clicking it again releases the pin |

## Accessibility

- `Label` names the chart. Each legend row is a toggle whose name includes its value, its share and, for Other, the
  parts it holds. A hidden row reads "hidden" after its name.
- The legend is the keyboard path. Each row is a stop and a toggle for its own segment.
- Showing or hiding a segment is announced politely with the new total, for example "Search hidden. Total 50 visits."
- Without a legend the ring is focusable, and its name tells the reader to use the arrow keys to read each segment.
- The center readout is a raw element for assistive technology; the same reading reaches the reader through the
  announcement and the hidden summary.
- A hidden data table and summary list every visible part with its value and share.
- The focus ring appears only for keyboard focus.

### Keyboard

With the legend shown, each legend row is a stop. Without the legend, the ring is one stop and the arrow keys move
between its segments.

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| Legend: `Down` / `Right` | Move to the next row; the last row wraps to the first |
| Legend: `Up` / `Left` | Move to the previous row; the first row wraps to the last |
| Legend: `Home` / `End` | Move to the first or last row |
| Legend: `Enter` / `Space` | Show or hide the segment; in `Select` mode, pin or release it |
| Legend: `Escape` | Release the pinned segment (only when one is pinned) |
| Ring (no legend): `Right` / `Down`, `Left` / `Up` | Preview the next or previous visible segment, wrapping at the ends |
| Ring (no legend): `Home` / `End` | Preview the first or last visible segment |
| Ring (no legend): `Enter` / `Space` | Pin or release the previewed segment |
| Ring (no legend): `Escape` | Clear the preview and release the pin |

A segment previewed by the keyboard shows in the center, so the reader hears and sees the same value. Moving focus
away from the chart clears the preview.

## Motion

- On first view all segments sweep out from the top at once, and each trailing edge follows a beat later.
- A new dataset or a hidden segment morphs the start and end angles from where the arcs are now, so the ring keeps its
  motion and its order. Arcs carry their speed into the new position.
- The active segment moves outward along its middle and thickens slightly while the others dim. The pointer keeps the
  hover across gaps between segments.
- The center reading rolls to the active segment, and the total and the shares follow the new values.
- Reduced motion shows the arcs, the outward move and the text at their final state at once. Off behaves the same as
  Reduced.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| First view | Segments sweep out from the top, each trailing edge a beat behind | Shown at the final state | Shown at the final state |
| New dataset or hidden segment | Arcs morph from their current angles, keeping their speed | Shown at the final state | Shown at the final state |
| Active segment | Moves outward and thickens, the others dim | Shown at the final state | Shown at the final state |
| Center reading | Rolls to the new reading like a drum | Changes at once | Changes at once |

## Related

- `BarChart` when the parts are many or need exact comparison.
- `WaffleChart` for a share expressed as a count of cells, one per percent.
- `Treemap` when the parts are nested and need drill-down.
- `Gauge` for one value against a known range.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `BarChart` | There are more than six parts, or the reader must rank them |
| `WaffleChart` | The share is best read as a count of cells |
| `Treemap` | The parts nest inside groups and need drill-down |
| `Gauge` | One value is read against a range and thresholds |
| `UsageMeter` | A quota or a limit is the point of the panel |
| `LineChart` | The question is how the split changes over time |
