# Streamgraph

> Layered streams on a wiggle baseline that morph between ranges, with a layer you can isolate and read week by week.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/streamgraph

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.StreamgraphTopicsOverTimeDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="16">
        <WrapPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center" ItemSpacing="12" LineSpacing="12">
            <arc:Button Content="12 weeks" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Click="On12WeeksClick" />
            <arc:Button Content="26 weeks" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Click="On26WeeksClick" />
            <arc:Button Content="52 weeks" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Click="On52WeeksClick" />
            <arc:Button Content="Wiggle" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Click="OnWiggleClick" />
            <arc:Button Content="Silhouette" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Click="OnSilhouetteClick" />
            <arc:Button Content="Zero" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Click="OnZeroClick" />
        </WrapPanel>
        <arc:Streamgraph x:Name="Chart"
                         Label="Support tickets by topic"
                         Unit="tickets"
                         CategoryLabel="Week">
            <arc:Streamgraph.Series>
                <arc:ChartSeries Key="billing" Name="Billing" />
                <arc:ChartSeries Key="login" Name="Login" />
                <arc:ChartSeries Key="performance" Name="Performance" />
                <arc:ChartSeries Key="integrations" Name="Integrations" />
                <arc:ChartSeries Key="mobile" Name="Mobile" />
            </arc:Streamgraph.Series>
        </arc:Streamgraph>
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;
using TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Pages;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class StreamgraphTopicsOverTimeDemo : UserControl
{
    public StreamgraphTopicsOverTimeDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        ShowWeeks(26);
    }

    private void On12WeeksClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) => ShowWeeks(12);

    private void On26WeeksClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) => ShowWeeks(26);

    private void On52WeeksClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) => ShowWeeks(52);

    private void OnWiggleClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) => Chart.Offset = StreamOffset.Wiggle;

    private void OnSilhouetteClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) => Chart.Offset = StreamOffset.Silhouette;

    private void OnZeroClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) => Chart.Offset = StreamOffset.Zero;

    // Replace the week starts and every layer's values together; each layer blends from its shape on screen.
    private void ShowWeeks(int weeks)
    {
        var start = ChartsADemoData.Today.AddDays(-7 * (weeks - 1));
        Chart.ItemsSource = Enumerable.Range(0, weeks).Select(w => start.AddDays(7 * w)).ToArray();
        for (var i = 0; i < Chart.Series.Count; i++)
        {
            Chart.Series[i].Values = ChartsADemoData.Daily(weeks, 60 - i * 9, 40, weeks * 7 + i, i % 2 == 0 ? 0.8 : -0.3);
        }
    }
}
```

## When to use

`Streamgraph` shows how a total is made up of parts as it changes over time. Each part is a layer, and the layers
flow along a shared time axis as one band, so the reader sees both the size of the total and the share of each part
at a glance. It fits a screen that answers "what changed in the mix, and when?" rather than "what was the exact value
of each part?"

- **Support tickets by topic in an operations review**: weekly volume split into billing, login, performance,
  integrations and mobile. After a release, the performance layer swells and the reader sees the shift in the mix as
  well as the rise in volume.
- **Traffic by acquisition channel in a marketing dashboard**: daily visits from search, social, email, referral and
  direct, over 26 weeks. The stream shows which channel carried a campaign and how the others shrank to make room.
- **Revenue by plan tier in a SaaS finance review**: monthly recurring revenue from Starter, Growth and Enterprise. The
  reader sees mix changes, such as an upgrade wave, without comparing five separate lines.
- **Incident categories over a quarter in a reliability report**: the count of incidents per category per week, where
  seasonality and spikes read more clearly as flowing layers than as separate lines.
- **Seasonal demand by product category in an e-commerce planning view**: units sold per category per week, where the
  shape of the band shows when each category peaks.

## When not to use

- **Exact values or comparisons between layers**, such as "did Billing grow faster than Login in March?": use
  `LineChart`, which puts every series on its own baseline and an axis.
- **A few periods or discrete categories**, such as four quarters or six regions: use `BarChart`, where each value is a
  separate bar and the reader can compare their heights.
- **Data with negative values**, such as net flow or profit and loss by business line: the layers stack from a
  baseline, so the stream stops reading as parts of a total. Use `LineChart`.
- **The parts of one total at a single moment**, such as the share of revenue by region today: use `DonutChart`. A
  stream needs a time axis to earn its place.
- **Many layers that are all small**: a stream with more than eight layers becomes a stack of slivers. Fold the
  smallest into an "Other" series, or use `LineChart` when every series matters.
- **Distributions of several groups rather than their totals over time**, such as the spread of response times for
  each service: use `Ridgeline`.

## Usage

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:Streamgraph Label="Support tickets by topic"
                     Unit="tickets"
                     CategoryLabel="Week"
                     ItemsSource="{Binding Weeks}">
        <arc:Streamgraph.Series>
            <arc:ChartSeries Key="billing" Name="Billing" Values="{Binding Billing}" />
            <arc:ChartSeries Key="login" Name="Login" Values="{Binding Login}" />
            <arc:ChartSeries Key="performance" Name="Performance" Values="{Binding Performance}" />
        </arc:Streamgraph.Series>
    </arc:Streamgraph>
</UserControl>
```

Each `ChartSeries` is one layer. `ItemsSource` holds the shared x positions, such as the week starts, and every
layer's `Values` has one number per position. Hover or focus a layer to isolate it.

`Streamgraph` derives from `ChartBase`, the base of Arc's self-drawn charts, and shares its data pipeline, palette,
reveal, readout and accessible summary with `LineChart` and `BarChart`. The stream adds the stacking, the layer
isolation and the direct labels. Because the layers are stacked, a layer's height is its value, and the total height
of the stream is the total of the visible layers at each week.

### Anatomy

1. **Legend** (`ShowLegend`): one square swatch and name per layer, above the plot with a 16 unit gap. The legend
   extends 8 units into the margins so that its hover areas line up with the plot edges. It is shown by default when
   there is more than one layer.
2. **Plot** (`PlotHeight`, default 260): the stacked layers, each filled with its series color. A 2 unit gap in the
   surface color separates neighboring layers, so the boundaries stay readable without outlines.
3. **Direct labels** (`ShowDirectLabels`, on by default): the layer's name on its thickest stretch, with a halo in the
   surface color so the text reads over any layer. A label appears only when its layer is at least 19 units thick at
   that point and the text fits in the plot.
4. **Crosshair**: a 1 px vertical line in the foreground color at 50% opacity, at the active week.
5. **Tooltip**: the week's title and one row per visible layer, in stack order. The isolated layer's row is emphasized.
6. **Time axis** (`ShowXAxis`): a 26 unit row under the plot with the category labels. Long ranges show fewer labels.

### Layers and series

A layer is a `ChartSeries` with a `Key`, a `Name` and `Values`. The `Key` identifies the layer in `HiddenSeries`,
`ActiveSeriesKey` and the `HiddenSeriesChanged` and `ActiveIndexChanged` events, so keep it stable across data
refreshes. The `Name` appears in the legend, the direct label, the tooltip and the announcement.

Order the layers by what the reader should see. The stack places the first layer in the middle of the stream and
alternates the rest above and below it, so the largest or the most important layer is often the best first. Keep the
same order across screens that share a legend, so that the same topic has the same place each time.

### Offset

`Offset` chooses how the layers stack around the baseline. The default is `Wiggle`.

| Value | Stack | Choose it when |
|---|---|---|
| `Wiggle` (default) | Minimizes the slope of the layers, so the stream flows and stays level | The story is the flow: layers rise and fall together and the reader should follow the band |
| `Silhouette` | Centers the whole stack around a flat middle | The total's up and down is the story, and the layers are the detail around it |
| `Zero` | Stacks the layers in order from a flat baseline at the bottom | The reader needs a stable baseline to compare the bottom layer and the layers above it |

```xml
<arc:Streamgraph Label="Topics" Offset="Silhouette" ItemsSource="{Binding Weeks}" />
```

Changing `Offset` re-stacks the layers without new data. Keep one offset per screen, so that the same layer does not
change place when the reader moves between two charts.

### Ranges

Replace `ItemsSource` and the series values together when the range changes. Every layer blends from its shape on
screen to the new one, and ranges of different lengths also morph, because each layer is resampled to the same grid
before the blend.

```csharp
void ShowRange(Streamgraph chart, IReadOnlyList<DateOnly> weeks, double[][] valuesByLayer)
{
    chart.ItemsSource = weeks;
    for (var i = 0; i < chart.Series.Count; i++)
    {
        chart.Series[i].Values = valuesByLayer[i];
    }
}
```

A layer that is hidden thins to nothing while the others close over it, and the hidden layer comes back the same way
when the reader shows it again.

### Legend, direct labels and hidden layers

The legend and the direct labels name the layers. Direct labels are drawn on the thickest stretch of each layer when
there is room, so a thin layer may have no label; its legend entry still names it. Turn `ShowDirectLabels` off when the
legend is enough and the plot is busy.

`HiddenSeries` is two-way: the legend toggles it, and the view model can keep the hidden keys. A hidden layer is removed
from the stack, the tooltip, the announcement and the total, and the others re-stack around it.

```xml
<arc:Streamgraph Label="Topics"
                 ShowLegend="True"
                 ShowDirectLabels="True"
                 HiddenSeries="{Binding HiddenKeys}"
                 ItemsSource="{Binding Weeks}" />
```

### Reading a week

`ActiveIndexChanged` reports the week under the pointer or the keyboard. Its `Index` and `Label` identify the week,
`SeriesKey` names the isolated layer, and `Values` lists each layer's value at that week. `ActiveSeriesKey` returns the
isolated layer at any time, or `null` when no layer is isolated or the isolated layer is hidden.

```csharp
chart.ActiveIndexChanged += (_, e) => readout.Text = e.Label ?? string.Empty;
```

### Binding to a view model

In an MVVM app the view model owns the weeks, the layer values and the hidden keys. With CommunityToolkit.Mvvm, the view
model is an `ObservableObject` and each range change is one command.

```csharp
public sealed record TicketReport(
    IReadOnlyList<DateOnly> Weeks,
    double[] Billing,
    double[] Login,
    double[] Performance);

public interface ITicketApi
{
    Task<TicketReport> GetTicketsByTopicAsync(int weeks);
}

public partial class TicketTrendViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    private readonly ITicketApi _api;

    public TicketTrendViewModel(ITicketApi api) => _api = api;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private IReadOnlyList<DateOnly> _weeks = [];

    [ObservableProperty]
    private double[] _billing = [];

    [ObservableProperty]
    private double[] _login = [];

    [ObservableProperty]
    private double[] _performance = [];

    [ObservableProperty]
    private IReadOnlyList<string> _hiddenKeys = [];

    [RelayCommand]
    private async Task LoadRangeAsync(int weeks)
    {
        // The week starts and the layer values come from one report, so the chart receives them as one update.
        var report = await _api.GetTicketsByTopicAsync(weeks);
        Weeks = report.Weeks;
        Billing = report.Billing;
        Login = report.Login;
        Performance = report.Performance;
    }
}
```

```xml
<arc:Streamgraph Label="Support tickets by topic"
                 Unit="tickets"
                 CategoryLabel="Week"
                 ItemsSource="{Binding Weeks}"
                 HiddenSeries="{Binding HiddenKeys, Mode=TwoWay}">
    <arc:Streamgraph.Series>
        <arc:ChartSeries Key="billing" Name="Billing" Values="{Binding Billing}" />
        <arc:ChartSeries Key="login" Name="Login" Values="{Binding Login}" />
        <arc:ChartSeries Key="performance" Name="Performance" Values="{Binding Performance}" />
    </arc:Streamgraph.Series>
</arc:Streamgraph>
```

`HiddenSeries` is two-way, so the view model sees the layers the reader hid and can keep them hidden after a refresh.
`ItemsSource` and the layer values are one-way. The `HiddenSeriesChanged` event reports the new hidden list in its
`Hidden` property for code that prefers events. `ActiveSeriesKey` is read-only; use `ActiveIndexChanged` to react to
the reader's moves.

### Data shape and performance

Each layer is resampled to a fixed grid of 161 points when the data changes, and the stack, the edges and the labels are
recomputed from those points on each frame. The cost therefore depends on the number of layers more than on the number
of weeks. Keep the layers to three to eight, and keep the values non-negative.

- **Week count**: each week is one category. The curves are resampled to the fixed grid at any week count, and the time
  axis picks its labels so that they do not overlap.
- **Layer values**: every layer needs one value per week, in the same order as `ItemsSource`. Pass zero for a week with no
  activity, so that the layers line up on the same weeks.
- **Update frequency**: a refresh once a day or once a week reads as a change of range. A stream that updates every few
  seconds keeps the layers moving and makes the isolation hard to use.
- **Formatting**: values are formatted with `ValueFormat` (a .NET format string, en-US) and the `Unit` appears after them
  in the tooltip and the announcement, such as "4 tickets". Format the axis dates with `XAxisFormatter` when the
  default short date is not the one your product uses.

### Example: ticket mix after a release

A support lead reviews the last 26 weeks of tickets. The stream shows that the performance layer grew in the weeks after
a release, while billing stayed flat. The legend stays visible so each layer can be hidden or isolated, the direct
labels name the thick layers, and the time axis labels the weeks. The reader can hide the Mobile layer to look at
the mix of the other four without a new query.

```xml
<arc:Streamgraph Label="Support tickets by topic, 26 weeks"
                 Unit="tickets"
                 CategoryLabel="Week"
                 PlotHeight="240"
                 ShowLegend="True"
                 ShowDirectLabels="True"
                 Offset="Wiggle"
                 ItemsSource="{Binding Weeks}">
    <arc:Streamgraph.Series>
        <arc:ChartSeries Key="billing" Name="Billing" Values="{Binding Billing}" />
        <arc:ChartSeries Key="login" Name="Login" Values="{Binding Login}" />
        <arc:ChartSeries Key="performance" Name="Performance" Values="{Binding Performance}" />
        <arc:ChartSeries Key="integrations" Name="Integrations" Values="{Binding Integrations}" />
        <arc:ChartSeries Key="mobile" Name="Mobile" Values="{Binding Mobile}" />
    </arc:Streamgraph.Series>
</arc:Streamgraph>
```

The keys are fixed strings, so a hidden layer stays hidden when the data refreshes. The `Name` values are the words the
reader sees in the legend and the tooltip, so they are written for people rather than for the data model.

### Content guidelines

Name the layers by the thing they count, in sentence case, and name the unit in `Unit`. A legend that reads "Billing,
Login, Performance" lets the reader scan the stream without a key.

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| `Label="Chart 1"` | `Label="Support tickets by topic"` |
| `Name="billing_v2"` | `Name="Billing"` |
| `Unit="count"` | `Unit="tickets"` |
| `CategoryLabel="x"` | `CategoryLabel="Week"` |
| `Name="Other (misc.)"` | `Name="Other"` with the smallest categories folded in |
| `Name="ALL CAPS TOPIC"` | `Name="Login"` |

### Best practices

**Do**

- Keep the layer keys stable. The key, not the name, identifies a layer in `HiddenSeries` and in events, so a renamed key
  resets what the reader hid.
- Fold the smallest categories into "Other" before you pass the data in. A layer too thin to hold its direct label is
  hard to isolate, and the legend and the tooltip become its only identification.
- Keep one offset per screen. Changing the offset re-stacks the layers, which makes it hard to follow a layer across
  two charts.
- Replace the week starts and every layer's values together when the range changes, so that the layers morph from the
  shape on screen to the new one.
- Name the unit in `Unit`, so that the tooltip and the announcement read "4 tickets" rather than a bare number.

**Avoid**

- A stream for data with negative values. The stack has no meaning below the baseline; use `LineChart`.
- More than eight layers. The thin layers become slivers that the reader cannot isolate; combine them.
- A stream for exact comparisons between layers. The stacked layers are read by their band, and their exact values are
  only in the tooltip and the announcement.
- Direct labels on a small plot with many layers. The labels hide on thin layers, so the legend is the reliable key.
- Refreshing the data every few seconds. Each refresh moves every layer, and the stream never settles for the reader.

### Common questions

**How do I isolate a layer from code?** The chart has no setter for the isolated layer. The pointer, the keyboard and
the legend preview set it, and `ActiveSeriesKey` reads it back. Read `ActiveSeriesKey` in `ActiveIndexChanged`, or when
you need the current layer, to drive a detail panel.

**Why does a layer disappear when I hide it, and why do the others move?** A hidden layer is removed from the stack, so the
remaining layers close over its space and re-stack. Its legend entry stays, and the key is kept in `HiddenSeries` until
the reader shows it again.

**What does the announcement say?** It names the week, the isolated layer and its value, the number of visible layers
and the total of the visible layers, such as "W5. Login 4 tickets, 3 layers, 30 tickets in total". Without an isolated
layer, it names the week and the totals only. Set `Unit` and `Label` so that the announcement is meaningful.

**Why is a layer missing its direct label?** Direct labels are drawn only where the layer is at least 19 units thick and
the text fits inside the plot. A thin or narrow layer keeps its legend entry and its tooltip row, and the label returns
when the layer grows.

**Can I use dates for the x axis?** Yes. `ItemsSource` accepts `DateTime`, `DateTimeOffset` or `DateOnly`, and the
category labels follow the default date format. Set `CategoryLabel` to the word the table header should use, such as
"Week".

## API reference

### Streamgraph

Arc's streamgraph: layers stacked on a wiggle baseline, flowing over time. Hovering a layer isolates it and reads every layer at that moment; switching ranges blends every layer from the shape on screen on a shared 161-point grid, a hidden layer thins to nothing while the others close over it, and the first time the chart is seen the whole stream swells out of a hairline along its center. Motion is code-driven (a per-sample spring array and `MotionValue`) because every layer edge is recomputed from the stack each frame inside one self-drawn plot.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Offset` | `StreamOffset` | `Wiggle` | How the layers stack. |
| `ShowDirectLabels` | `bool` | `true` | Names each layer inside its widest stretch when it is thick enough to hold the text. |
| `ShowLegend` | `bool?` | `null` | Layer toggles above the plot (shown by default when there is more than one layer). |
| `ShowXAxis` | `bool` | `true` | Shows the category (time) axis labels under the plot. |
| `HiddenSeries` | `IReadOnlyList<string>?` | `null` | Keys of the series hidden from the plot; the legend toggles them (two-way). |
| `Label` | `string` | `""` | What is measured, such as "Signups". Names the chart, its summary and its data table. |
| `Unit` | `string` | `""` | Unit after each value in readouts, such as "ms". |
| `EmptyLabel` | `string` | `"No data for this range"` | Shown when there is nothing to draw. |
| `CategoryLabel` | `string` | `"Date"` | Name of the category column in the data table and the explore label, such as "Date". |
| `ValueFormat` | `string?` | `null` | .NET format string for values (en-US), such as "N0", "C0" or "0.0'%'". Null uses the chart's default. |
| `ValueFormatter` | `Func<ChartValueContext, string>?` | `null` | Formats values with context (series, index); wins over `ValueFormat`. |
| `PlotHeight` | `double` | `260` | Plot height in pixels; the width follows the container. |
| `ItemsSource` | `IEnumerable?` | `null` | The data items. Values are read with `YSelector`/`YBinding` (or per series), categories with `XSelector`/`XBinding`. |
| `XBinding` | `BindingBase?` | `null` | Reads each item's category or date: the AOT-safe path form, such as `XBinding="{CompiledBinding Date, DataType=local:Day}"` (a reflection `{Binding Date}` also works). |
| `XSelector` | `Func<object, object?>?` | `null` | Reads each item's category or date (a string, DateTime, DateTimeOffset or DateOnly). |
| `YBinding` | `BindingBase?` | `null` | Reads each item's value for a single-series chart (`YBinding="{CompiledBinding Visits, DataType=local:Day}"`). |
| `YSelector` | `Func<object, double>?` | `null` | Reads each item's value for a single-series chart. |
| `XLabelFormatter` | `Func<object?, string>?` | `null` | Full label of a category (tooltip, headline, screen readers). Dates default to "Tue, Sep 15". |
| `XAxisFormatter` | `Func<object?, string?>?` | `null` | Short axis label of a category; return null to keep the axis quiet there. Dates default to "Sep 15". |
| `ActiveIndex` | `int?` | `null` | The point being read (crosshair, scrubbed bar, hovered segment), or null at rest. Two-way. |
| `Summary` | `string` | – | *Read-only.* A one-paragraph description for assistive technology, such as "Signups, Sep 1 to Sep 30. ...". |
| `DataTableText` | `string` | – | *Read-only.* The accessible data table as text: a header line, then one line per row (tab separated). |
| `Announcement` | `string` | – | *Read-only.* The latest polite announcement (what Arc's live region reads), such as "Loading". |
| `ShowGrid` | `bool` | `true` | Horizontal gridlines at the value ticks. |
| `ShowYAxis` | `bool` | `true` | The value axis labels in the right-hand gutter. |
| `YMinimum` | `double?` | `null` | Fixes the bottom of the value axis (default: zero, or the data minimum when it dips below). |
| `YMaximum` | `double?` | `null` | Fixes the top of the value axis (default: the next nice tick above the data). |
| `TickFormatter` | `Func<double, string>?` | `null` | Formats value-axis ticks. Defaults to a compact number, such as 1.2K. |
| `Curve` | `ChartCurve` | `Smooth` | Smooth monotone curves that never swing past the data, or straight segments. |
| `IsLoading` | `bool` | `false` | Keeps the current shapes on screen, dimmed and breathing, while the next range loads. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `HiddenSeriesChanged` | `ChartHiddenSeriesChangedEventArgs` | Raised when the legend shows or hides a series. |
| `ActiveIndexChanged` | `ChartActiveIndexChangedEventArgs` | Raised as the readout moves between points, and with a null index when it is released. |

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

## Accessibility

- `Label` names the chart. The plot is a focusable group named with the label and the keyboard instructions, such as
  "Support tickets by topic. Use left and right arrows to move through time, up and down to change layer."
- Each reading updates the value text and the polite announcement with the week, the isolated layer's value and the
  total of the visible layers. A reader using a screen reader hears the same numbers the tooltip shows.
- The legend entries are toggles. Focusing an entry isolates its layer, and pressing `Enter` shows or hides it.
- A hidden data table lists every layer for every week.
- The layers are named on the plot and in the legend, so they are not told apart by shade alone. A 2 unit gap in the
  surface color separates neighboring layers.
- With a pointer, moving over a layer isolates it and leaving the plot clears the reading. With touch, the reading stays
  on the touched point until the contact is released.

### Keyboard

The plot takes focus with `Tab`. When focus arrives from the keyboard, the reading starts on the latest week.

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` | Move focus among the legend entries and the plot |
| `Left` / `Right` | Move to the previous or the next week. From rest, `Right` stays on the latest week |
| `Up` / `Down` | Isolate the next or the previous visible layer in series order, for the current week. From none, `Up` picks the last visible layer and `Down` picks the first |
| `PageUp` / `PageDown` | Move about a sixth of the weeks, forward or back |
| `Home` / `End` | Move to the first or the last week |
| `Escape` | Clear the reading and the isolated layer |
| `Enter` (on a legend entry) | Show or hide the layer |

## Motion

- On first view the stream swells out from a hairline along its centre on a long spring with no overshoot.
- A new range or a new dataset blends every layer on a shared grid, so the layers keep their order and their speed.
- A hidden layer thins to nothing while the others re-stack around it.
- The crosshair and the tooltip slide on springs, and the other layers dim while one is isolated.
- Reduced motion shows the end state at once and keeps the crosshair and the tooltip, which jump to the new week
  without a spring. Off jumps to the end state.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| First view | The stream swells out of its centre line on a long spring, without overshoot | The end shape appears at once | The end shape appears at once |
| New range or dataset | Layers blend to the new shape on a smooth spring; new layers grow out of nothing | Layers jump to the new shape | Immediate |
| Hiding a layer | The layer thins to nothing while the others re-stack around it | Jumps to the re-stacked shape | Immediate |
| Isolating a layer | The other layers fade on a short standard tween | The same short tween | Immediate |
| Crosshair and tooltip | Slide to the new week on springs | Jump to the new week without a spring | Immediate |

## Related

- `LineChart` when the exact value of each series matters, and `BarChart` for a few discrete periods.
- `Ridgeline` for the distribution of several groups rather than their totals over time.
- `DonutChart` for the share of each part in one total.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `LineChart` | The reader must compare exact values, or the data has negative values |
| `BarChart` | There are a few discrete periods or categories to compare |
| `Ridgeline` | You compare the distributions of several groups, not their totals over time |
| `DonutChart` | You show the share of each part of one total at a single moment |
| `Sparkline` | You show the trend of a single total beside its headline value |

# Brush chart

> A dense time series with an overview strip: drag a window to zoom, resize it by its handles, and read events in place.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/brush-chart

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.BrushChartOverviewAndDetailDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="16">
        <WrapPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center" ItemSpacing="12" LineSpacing="12">
            <arc:Button Content="Last 30 days" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Click="OnLast30DaysClick" />
            <arc:Button Content="Last quarter" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Click="OnLastQuarterClick" />
            <arc:Button Content="Last year" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Click="OnLastYearClick" />
            <arc:Button Content="All" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Click="OnAllClick" />
        </WrapPanel>
        <arc:BrushChart x:Name="Chart"
                        Label="Daily active users"
                        Unit="users"
                        RangeChanged="OnRangeChanged" />
        <TextBlock x:Name="RangeText"
                   TextWrapping="Wrap"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class BrushChartOverviewAndDetailDemo : UserControl
{
    private static readonly DateTimeOffset s_start = new(2025, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0, TimeSpan.Zero);

    private readonly DateTimeOffset _last;

    public BrushChartOverviewAndDetailDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();

        // 640 days with a weekend dip, a slow drift and one spike (deterministic).
        var random = new Random(42);
        var points = new ChartPoint[640];
        double level = 1200;
        for (var i = 0; i < points.Length; i++)
        {
            level = Math.Max(200, level + (random.NextDouble() - 0.46) * 60);
            var weekly = (i % 7) is 5 or 6 ? -260 : 0;
            var spike = i == 410 ? 1800 : i == 411 ? 900 : 0;
            points[i] = new ChartPoint(s_start.AddDays(i), Math.Round(level + weekly + spike + random.NextDouble() * 120));
        }
        _last = s_start.AddDays(points.Length - 1);
        Chart.ItemsSource = points;

        Chart.Annotations =
        [
            new ChartAnnotation(s_start.AddDays(120), "v2 launch", "New onboarding flow shipped to everyone."),
            new ChartAnnotation(s_start.AddDays(410), "Press mention", "Featured in a weekly newsletter."),
            new ChartAnnotation(s_start.AddDays(530), "Pricing change")
        ];
    }

    private void OnLast30DaysClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) => ShowLast(30);

    private void OnLastQuarterClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) => ShowLast(91);

    private void OnLastYearClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) => ShowLast(365);

    private void OnAllClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) => Chart.Range = new ChartTimeRange(s_start, _last);

    // The window slides to the new range on a spring.
    private void ShowLast(int days) => Chart.Range = new ChartTimeRange(_last.AddDays(-days), _last);

    private void OnRangeChanged(object? sender, ChartTimeRangeChangedEventArgs e)
        => RangeText.Text = $"Window: {e.Range.Start:MMM d, yyyy} – {e.Range.End:MMM d, yyyy}";
}
```

## When to use

`BrushChart` draws a long daily series in one plot and keeps the whole history in an overview strip under it. The
reader drags a window across the strip to choose the period they care about, and the plot follows. It belongs in the
body of an analytics or review page, where the series is the main content and exploring it is the task.

- **Daily active users on a SaaS admin console**: a product team reviews a year of daily sessions, then narrows the
  window to the weeks around a pricing change. The overview keeps the rest of the year visible, so the reader never
  loses their place.
- **Incident review timelines**: a reliability lead plots p95 latency for a quarter and marks deploys and outages with
  `Annotations`. Each event sits on the line and on the overview, so the review reads cause and effect together.
- **Revenue or order volume in a finance dashboard**: a controller opens a daily revenue series of several thousand
  points, presses a preset such as "Last 30 days" that sets `Range`, and reads the new window in a caption that
  `RangeChanged` updates.
- **Metered usage on a billing page**: a customer opens API calls per day for the current billing cycle, pans to a
  spike and reads its date and value before they open a support ticket.

## When not to use

- **A few weeks of data, or several series to compare**: use `LineChart`. It draws several series with a legend and
  shows the whole range without an overview strip.
- **A small trend in a table cell or a KPI tile**: use `Sparkline`, which has no axes and no interaction.
- **Negative values, or a value axis that must not start at zero**: use `LineChart`, which exposes `YMinimum` and
  `YMaximum`. The brush chart always starts its value axis at zero, so it cannot show a signed series.
- **Layers of a composition over time, such as traffic per channel**: use `Streamgraph`, which stacks the layers. The
  brush chart draws one series.
- **A single total that changes as a count goes up**: use `AnimatedCounter`, which animates the number itself.

## Usage

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:BrushChart Label="Daily active users"
                    Unit="users"
                    PlotHeight="240"
                    OverviewHeight="52"
                    ItemsSource="{Binding Points}" />
</UserControl>
```

`BrushChart` derives from `ChartBase`, the base of the Arc chart family. The base supplies the shared shell: `Label`,
`Unit`, `PlotHeight`, `EmptyLabel`, `ValueFormat`, `ItemsSource` with `XBinding` and `YBinding`, and the tooltip rules.
The brush chart adds what a long history needs: the overview strip, the visible window (`Range`), its minimum span and
the event markers. It is self-drawn: the plot and the strip are rendered from the data in code, not assembled from child
elements, which keeps a long series responsive.

Each item supplies a date and a value. The date can be a `DateTimeOffset`, a `DateTime` or a `DateOnly`, and the
control converts it to a time internally. The control sorts the points by date whenever the data changes, so the
order of the source collection does not matter, although an ascending source avoids the work.

### Anatomy

1. **Plot**: the raw line for the points in view, or a seven-point average with its low-to-high band
   when the view is zoomed far out. The plot is 240 px tall by default (`PlotHeight`).
2. **Value axis**: on the right, in a 44 px gutter (the token's `GutterWidth`). It starts at zero and its top springs to
   the tallest point in view, with compact tick labels such as 1.2K unless `TickFormatter` is set.
3. **Gridlines**: horizontal lines at the value ticks. They follow `ShowGrid`, which is on by default.
4. **Date axis row**: 28 px tall under the plot (the token's `AxisRowHeight`). Its tick labels change with the window
   width, from days to weeks, months and years.
5. **Event markers**: a hairline with a dot in the second series color, labelled left to right. A label that would
   collide with another is skipped, so the marker stays even when its text does not fit.
6. **Crosshair and tooltip**: the crosshair sits on the active point. The tooltip shows the date, the value with its
   `Unit` and any event; it sits above the point, below it when there is no room, and never leaves the plot.
7. **Overview strip** (the overview part of the template): the whole history, drawn once per width, with the part outside the window
   stepped back. It is `OverviewHeight` tall (52 px by default), starts 8 px under the date axis and ends at the value
   gutter, so the two charts share one horizontal scale.
8. **Window and handles**: a ring over the overview with two grips at its edges. The grips are 28 by 44 px hit areas.
   Drag the ring to pan, a grip to resize, empty track to draw a new window, a tap to recenter and a double tap to reset.

### Choosing the window and the presets

`Range` is the visible window as a `ChartTimeRange` (a start and an end, both inclusive). When it is null the window
is the whole series. `Range` is two-way: a drag or a key press writes the new window back to it, and code can move the
window by assigning a new value. A code change glides to the new window on a spring at full motion, and jumps at
reduced or off motion.

```csharp
chart.Range = new ChartTimeRange(last.AddDays(-30), last);
chart.RangeChanged += (_, e) => range.Text = $"Window: {e.Range.Start:MMM d, yyyy} – {e.Range.End:MMM d, yyyy}";
```

Use presets for the windows people ask for most: the last 30 days, the last quarter, the last year and the full
series. A preset is a plain assignment, so the same code also serves a view model. The reset gesture (Escape or 0
on the window) always returns to the full series, whatever the presets are.

### Annotations

`Annotations` marks events on the plot and on the overview strip. Each `ChartAnnotation` has a date, a short label and
an optional description. The label is printed beside the marker when there is room; the description appears in the
tooltip and in screen reader announcements, so it can carry the detail a short label cannot.

```csharp
chart.Annotations =
[
    new ChartAnnotation(start.AddDays(120), "v2 launch", "New onboarding flow shipped to everyone."),
    new ChartAnnotation(start.AddDays(410), "Press mention", "Featured in a weekly newsletter."),
    new ChartAnnotation(start.AddDays(530), "Pricing change")
];
```

Keep the list to the events that explain the shape of the series. Events are part of the data the reader interprets,
so a release that is not in the list cannot be found from the chart; add it when it ships, not when someone asks.

### Minimum span

`MinSpan` stops the window from shrinking below a span. The default is seven days (`TimeSpan.FromDays(7)`). The limit
applies to drags, handles, the keyboard and code: a range narrower than the minimum widens to it, and a range that
starts or ends outside the data is pulled back inside. The span is also capped by the series length, so a series
shorter than the minimum shows the whole series.

```xml
<arc:BrushChart Label="Requests" MinSpan="14.00:00:00" ItemsSource="{Binding Points}" />
```

Pick the smallest span a reader should be able to inspect. A weekly review wants 14 days, so the window always shows
two full weekly cycles and a weekday pattern cannot hide between the points.

### Formatting

`DateFormatter` formats the dates in the tooltip and in the screen reader announcements, and `TickFormatter` formats
the value axis. The default date text is English (en-US), such as "Tue, Sep 15, 2026". The window text uses a short
form instead, such as "Jan 1, 2026 to Apr 10, 2026", and does not change with `DateFormatter`. Replace the defaults when the page uses another culture or a unit-aware number.

```xml
<arc:BrushChart Label="Revenue"
                Unit="USD"
                TickFormatter="{Binding FormatMoney}"
                ItemsSource="{Binding Points}" />
```

`ValueFormat` (a .NET format string, such as `N0` or `C0`) applies to the values in the tooltip and announcements, and
`ShowGrid` turns the gridlines off for a quieter plot.

### Binding to a view model

The view model owns the series, the window and the events. The brush chart only draws them and writes the window back
when the reader moves it. With CommunityToolkit.Mvvm:

```csharp
public sealed record DailyUsage(DateTimeOffset Date, double Calls);

public partial class UsageViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    private readonly DateTimeOffset _lastDay = new(2026, 10, 20, 0, 0, 0, TimeSpan.Zero);

    [ObservableProperty]
    private IReadOnlyList<DailyUsage> _usage = [];

    [ObservableProperty]
    private ChartTimeRange? _window;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private ObservableCollection<ChartAnnotation> _releases = [];

    [RelayCommand]
    private void ShowLast30Days() => Window = new ChartTimeRange(_lastDay.AddDays(-30), _lastDay);

    [RelayCommand]
    private void ShowAll() => Window = null;
}
```


- `Range` is two-way, so a drag or a key press writes `Window` back and a preset moves the plot. A code change to
  `Window` glides the window on a spring, so set it on a user action rather than on a timer.
- `Annotations` takes any `IEnumerable<ChartAnnotation>`. The markers redraw when the property is assigned, so after
  the list changes, assign it again (a new list or the same collection) to redraw.
- `ItemsSource` is replaced, not appended to. Assign a new `IReadOnlyList<DailyUsage>` when the series is reloaded.
- `XBinding` and `YBinding` read the date and the value. The compiled form `{CompiledBinding Date, DataType=...}` is
  the AOT-safe path; add `x:DataType` to the view when you use it. The examples leave it out for brevity.

### Example: API usage on a billing page

A billing page shows a customer the API calls they made in the current cycle. The reader needs to see the shape of the
cycle at a glance, jump to the last 30 days, and read a spike next to the release that caused it. The two preset
buttons call the view model's commands, which write `Window`; the chart reads and writes the same property, so a
preset and a drag always agree. The release markers come from the same list the product team uses for changelogs,
so the annotations are real events, not decoration. No screenshot is shown here: the chart draws its data only once
the view model supplies the points.

```xml
<StackPanel Width="720" Spacing="12">
    <StackPanel Orientation="Horizontal" Spacing="8">
        <arc:Button Content="Last 30 days" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Command="{Binding ShowLast30DaysCommand}" />
        <arc:Button Content="All" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Command="{Binding ShowAllCommand}" />
    </StackPanel>
    <arc:BrushChart Label="API calls per day"
                    Unit="calls"
                    ValueFormat="N0"
                    ItemsSource="{Binding Usage}"
                    XBinding="{Binding Date}"
                    YBinding="{Binding Calls}"
                    Range="{Binding Window, Mode=TwoWay}"
                    Annotations="{Binding Releases}" />
</StackPanel>
```

### Data shape and performance

The control expects one value per date. It reads each item's date through `XBinding` (or `XSelector`) and its value
through `YBinding` (or `YSelector`). Items whose date cannot be converted are skipped.

When the data changes, the control sorts the points, computes the seven-point average and its band once for the whole
series, and rebuilds the overview. Each data change is a full pass over the series, so replace the collection in one
assignment rather than adding points one at a time. The plot draws only the points in the window plus one on each side. When more
than two points fall into one pixel column, the line keeps only that column's low and high, so spikes survive and the
path stays small. A series of a year of daily points, or several thousand points, is the intended range.

When the data changes, the current window is kept and clamped to the new data and to the minimum span. A bound `Range`
wins over the current window, so set `Range` to the period you want and the reload follows it. The value axis
recalculates for the points in view and springs to the new top.

### Content guidelines

Name the series by what it counts and how often, because the reader sees the label before the axis. Keep the unit
short and put the event detail in the annotation description, not in the label.

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| Chart | Daily active users |
| Users | Active users per day |
| Release | v2 launch |
| Click the chart to zoom | Drag the window to zoom |
| Long description of the release in the label | Short label, with the detail in the description |
| 12000.0 calls | 12,000 calls (`ValueFormat="N0"`) |

Keep the window text and the captions in sentence case, and write dates in the form the rest of the page uses, such as
"Oct 1, 2026". Do not put the window readout in a headline: the caption under the chart is enough.

### Best practices

**Do**

- Set `Range` to the period the page opens on. Past two points per pixel the line keeps only each pixel column's low
  and high, so a reader who needs individual points needs a shorter window; the whole series is only a fallback.
- Give the window presets next to the chart, and bind `Range` two-way so the presets and the drag stay in step.
- Set `MinSpan` to the shortest period the review needs. A weekly review wants 14 days, so the window never hides a
  weekly pattern.
- Add the annotations that explain the shape of the series. Each one is a marker the reader can find without reading
  the table.
- Give the chart a `Label` and a `Unit`, so the summary and the tooltip read correctly to a screen reader user.

**Avoid**

- Negative values or a value axis that must start at a value other than zero. The brush chart always starts at zero, so
  a signed series reads as a flat line near the bottom.
- Two-week or shorter series. Few points make the overview strip hard to read and the window adds nothing; use
  `LineChart`.
- Many overlapping annotations on one day. Labels that collide are skipped, so the reader loses the events they were
  meant to see.
- Writing `Range` from a timer or from a value that changes on every frame. Each write glides the window, so the plot
  never settles.
- Reloading the whole series for a small update. Each data change rebuilds the averages and the overview, so batch the
  changes into one assignment.

### Common questions

**Why does the window snap to seven days when I set `Range`?** `MinSpan` is seven days by default. A window narrower
than the minimum span widens to it, and the end moves so the span holds. Set `MinSpan` to the smallest span you want to
allow.

**Does setting `Range` from code animate?** At full motion it glides on a spring. At reduced or off motion it jumps.
Drags and keys always follow the pointer one to one, so only code changes use the spring.

**What does the value axis start from?** Zero, always. Its top springs to the tallest point in view, so zooming into a
quiet stretch fills the plot. Use `TickFormatter` to change the tick labels, not the scale.

**Why does the chart show "No data yet" with one point?** The brush chart needs at least two points to draw a line and
an overview. `EmptyLabel` replaces the default text, which is "No data yet" for this chart.

**How do I show the window in my own text?** Handle `RangeChanged` and read `e.Range`, which has `Start` and `End` as
`DateTimeOffset` values. Format them with your own pattern, as the example above does. The same window is also
available as `Range`.

**How do I change the date format in the tooltip?** Set `DateFormatter` to a `Func<DateTimeOffset, string>`. It
formats the tooltip and the announcements; the window text keeps its short form.

## API reference

### BrushChart

Arc's brush chart: a long, dense time series with an overview strip. Drag the window to pan, drag a handle to resize, drag across empty track to draw a new window, tap to recenter, double-click to reset. When the view is zoomed far out a seven-point average and its low-to-high band replace the raw line, crossfading by density. Events are marked on both charts and labelled where they fit. The value axis springs to the tallest point in view; the line draws in from the left the first time the chart is seen. Dragging is followed 1:1 by a local tracker (`ChartDragTracker`); presets, resets and bound `Range` changes glide the window on a smooth spring (`MotionValue`), because the window is a coordinate pair inside the self-drawn overview.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Annotations` | `IEnumerable<ChartAnnotation>?` | `null` | Events drawn as markers on both charts. |
| `Range` | `ChartTimeRange?` | `null` | The visible window. A new value glides the window there; drags and keys write it back. Two-way. |
| `MinSpan` | `TimeSpan` | `7.00:00:00` | The smallest window (Arc: seven days). |
| `OverviewHeight` | `double` | `52` | Overview strip height in pixels. |
| `DateFormatter` | `Func<DateTimeOffset, string>?` | `null` | Formats a date in the tooltip and announcements. Defaults to "Tue, Sep 15, 2026". |
| `TickFormatter` | `Func<double, string>?` | `null` | Formats value-axis ticks. Defaults to a compact number, such as 1.2K. |
| `ShowGrid` | `bool` | `true` | Draws the gridlines behind the plot (default true). |
| `Label` | `string` | `""` | What is measured, such as "Signups". Names the chart, its summary and its data table. |
| `Unit` | `string` | `""` | Unit after each value in readouts, such as "ms". |
| `EmptyLabel` | `string` | `"No data yet"` | Shown when there is nothing to draw. |
| `CategoryLabel` | `string` | `"Date"` | Name of the category column in the data table and the explore label, such as "Date". |
| `ValueFormat` | `string?` | `null` | .NET format string for values (en-US), such as "N0", "C0" or "0.0'%'". Null uses the chart's default. |
| `ValueFormatter` | `Func<ChartValueContext, string>?` | `null` | Formats values with context (series, index); wins over `ValueFormat`. |
| `PlotHeight` | `double` | `240` | Plot height in pixels; the width follows the container. |
| `ItemsSource` | `IEnumerable?` | `null` | The data items. Values are read with `YSelector`/`YBinding` (or per series), categories with `XSelector`/`XBinding`. |
| `XBinding` | `BindingBase?` | `null` | Reads each item's category or date: the AOT-safe path form, such as `XBinding="{CompiledBinding Date, DataType=local:Day}"` (a reflection `{Binding Date}` also works). |
| `XSelector` | `Func<object, object?>?` | `null` | Reads each item's category or date (a string, DateTime, DateTimeOffset or DateOnly). |
| `YBinding` | `BindingBase?` | `null` | Reads each item's value for a single-series chart (`YBinding="{CompiledBinding Visits, DataType=local:Day}"`). |
| `YSelector` | `Func<object, double>?` | `null` | Reads each item's value for a single-series chart. |
| `XLabelFormatter` | `Func<object?, string>?` | `null` | Full label of a category (tooltip, headline, screen readers). Dates default to "Tue, Sep 15". |
| `XAxisFormatter` | `Func<object?, string?>?` | `null` | Short axis label of a category; return null to keep the axis quiet there. Dates default to "Sep 15". |
| `ActiveIndex` | `int?` | `null` | The point being read (crosshair, scrubbed bar, hovered segment), or null at rest. Two-way. |
| `Summary` | `string` | – | *Read-only.* A one-paragraph description for assistive technology, such as "Signups, Sep 1 to Sep 30. ...". |
| `DataTableText` | `string` | – | *Read-only.* The accessible data table as text: a header line, then one line per row (tab separated). |
| `Announcement` | `string` | – | *Read-only.* The latest polite announcement (what Arc's live region reads), such as "Loading". |
| `ShowLegend` | `bool?` | `null` | Series toggles. Null shows the legend when there is more than one series. |
| `ShowXAxis` | `bool` | `true` | The category (time) axis labels under the plot. |
| `ShowYAxis` | `bool` | `true` | The value axis labels in the right-hand gutter. |
| `YMinimum` | `double?` | `null` | Fixes the bottom of the value axis (default: zero, or the data minimum when it dips below). |
| `YMaximum` | `double?` | `null` | Fixes the top of the value axis (default: the next nice tick above the data). |
| `Curve` | `ChartCurve` | `Smooth` | Smooth monotone curves that never swing past the data, or straight segments. |
| `HiddenSeries` | `IReadOnlyList<string>?` | `null` | Keys of hidden series. Two-way; the legend toggles it. |
| `IsLoading` | `bool` | `false` | Keeps the current shapes on screen, dimmed and breathing, while the next range loads. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `RangeChanged` | `ChartTimeRangeChangedEventArgs` | Raised while the window is dragged, resized, stepped or reset. |
| `ActiveIndexChanged` | `ChartActiveIndexChangedEventArgs` | Raised as the readout moves between points, and with a null index when it is released. |
| `HiddenSeriesChanged` | `ChartHiddenSeriesChangedEventArgs` | Raised when the legend shows or hides a series. |

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

### Companion types

| Type | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `ChartAnnotation(DateTimeOffset Date, string Label, string? Description = null)` | An event on the time axis, shown as a marker with a label and a tooltip note |
| `ChartTimeRange(DateTimeOffset Start, DateTimeOffset End)` | The visible window; `Span` returns its length |
| `ChartTimeRangeChangedEventArgs` | The `RangeChanged` payload; its `Range` property is the new window |

## Accessibility

- `Label` names the chart. The window and its two handles are sliders, and their value text is the date.
- The plot is a focusable group. Its automation name is the label, the window readout and a hint to use the left and
  right arrows to read values.
- The reading for a point announces the date, the value with its unit and any event on that day, for example "Sun, Jan
  11, 2026, 110 users. Launch".
- A hidden data table lists every point in the window and its events. Events are marked with a second series color and
  a text label or a tooltip, so they are not identified by color alone.
- The focus ring of the window and its handles is drawn only for keyboard focus.

### Keyboard

The overview has four keyboard stops in this order: the plot, the window, the start handle and the end handle. Tab and
Shift+Tab move between them.

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| Plot: `Left` / `Right` | Move the crosshair one point back or forward; the first `Right` reads the last visible point |
| Plot: `PageUp` / `PageDown` | Move the crosshair by one eighth of the visible points |
| Plot: `Home` / `End` | Move the crosshair to the first or last visible point |
| Plot: `Escape` | Clear the crosshair |
| Window: `Left` / `Down`, `Right` / `Up` | Pan one tenth of the window back or forward |
| Window: `Shift` + arrow, `PageUp` / `PageDown` | Pan half the window |
| Window: `+` / `-` | Zoom in or out around the center |
| Window: `Home` / `End` | Move the window to the start or the end of the series |
| Start or end handle: `Left` / `Right` | Move the edge one point (one day in a daily series) |
| Start or end handle: `Shift` + arrow | Move the edge ten points |
| Start handle: `Home` / `End` | Move the start to the first point, or to the minimum span before the end |
| End handle: `Home` / `End` | Move the end to the minimum span after the start, or to the last point |
| Window or handle: `Escape` / `0` | Reset the window to the whole series |

## Motion

- On first view the line draws in from the left once, on a long spring without overshoot.
- Dragging follows the pointer one to one at every motion level. Presets, resets and changes of `Range` slide the window
  on a spring at full motion and jump at reduced or off motion.
- The value axis springs to the highest point in view at full motion. The raw line and the smoothed trend cross-fade as
  the density changes.
- The crosshair glides between points at full motion.
- Reduced motion places the window at once and keeps the crosshair where it is. Off jumps to the final state.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| First view | The line draws in from the left once, on a long spring | The finished line is shown | The finished line is shown |
| Drag the window or a handle | Follows the pointer one to one | Follows the pointer one to one | Follows the pointer one to one |
| Preset, reset or new `Range` | The window glides on a spring | The window moves at once | The window moves at once |
| Value axis top | Springs to the highest point in view | Moves at once | Moves at once |
| Crosshair | Glides between points | Moves at once, keeps its place | Jumps to the point |

## Related

- `LineChart` for a few weeks of data, several series or a signed value axis.
- `Sparkline` for a small trend without interaction.
- `Streamgraph` for the composition of several layers over time.
- `AnimatedCounter` for a single total that changes.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `LineChart` | The period is short, several series must be compared or values can be negative |
| `Sparkline` | The trend sits in a table cell or a KPI tile and needs no interaction |
| `Streamgraph` | The question is how the parts of a whole change over time |
| `AnimatedCounter` | One total changes and the number itself is the point |
| `BarChart` | Values are compared by period rather than read along a continuous timeline |
