# Slope chart

> Before and after on two axes: lines draw in, rank moves sit beside each value, and switching datasets slides every line to its new slope.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/slope-chart

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.SlopeChartBeforeAndAfterDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="16">
        <arc:SlopeChart x:Name="Chart"
                        Label="Conversion rate by channel"
                        StartLabel="Q1"
                        EndLabel="Q2"
                        HighlightKey="search"
                        ActiveKeyChanged="OnActiveKeyChanged" />
        <WrapPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center" ItemSpacing="12" LineSpacing="12">
            <arc:Button Content="Conversion" Variant="Secondary" Click="OnConversionClick" />
            <arc:Button Content="Retention" Variant="Secondary" Click="OnRetentionClick" />
        </WrapPanel>
        <TextBlock x:Name="Reading"
                   Text="Hover a line or focus the chart and use the arrow keys."
                   FontSize="13"
                   TextWrapping="Wrap"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class SlopeChartBeforeAndAfterDemo : UserControl
{
    private static readonly SlopeItem[] s_conversion =
    [
        new("search", "Organic search", 3.1, 4.6), new("email", "Email", 5.8, 5.2), new("paid", "Paid social", 2.2, 3.4),
        new("referral", "Referral", 4.4, 4.1), new("direct", "Direct", 3.6, 3.7), new("display", "Display ads", 1.2, 0.9)
    ];

    private static readonly SlopeItem[] s_retention =
    [
        new("search", "Organic search", 41, 48), new("email", "Email", 62, 57), new("paid", "Paid social", 23, 31),
        new("referral", "Referral", 55, 60), new("direct", "Direct", 47, 44), new("display", "Display ads", 18, 21)
    ];

    public SlopeChartBeforeAndAfterDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Chart.ValueFormatter = v => $"{v:0.0}%";
        Chart.ChangeFormatter = (change, _) => $"{(change >= 0 ? "+" : "−")}{Math.Abs(change):0.0} pts";
        Chart.ItemsSource = s_conversion;
    }

    // Change the label in the same step as the data; every line, dot and label slides to its new slope.
    private void OnConversionClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        Chart.Label = "Conversion rate by channel";
        Chart.ItemsSource = s_conversion;
    }

    private void OnRetentionClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        Chart.Label = "90-day retention by channel";
        Chart.ItemsSource = s_retention;
    }

    private void OnActiveKeyChanged(object? sender, SlopeActiveKeyChangedEventArgs e)
        => Reading.Text = e.Item is { } item ? $"{item.Label}: {item.Start} → {item.End}" : "No item in focus";
}
```

## When to use

`SlopeChart` compares two moments for a small set of items. Each item is one line from its value in the first period to
its value in the second, on one shared value axis, so the reader sees who rose, who fell and how the order changed in a
single glance. It fits a review page where the question is "what changed between these two dates", such as a quarterly
business review or a cohort comparison.

- **Conversion by acquisition channel, Q1 against Q2** in a growth review. Organic search that moved from fourth to
  second is visible without a table, and the rank move beside each value states it in words.
- **Retention by plan for two cohorts** in a SaaS board pack. Six plans on two axes show which plans improved and which
  slipped.
- **Revenue by region, this year against last year** in a sales review. The slopes show growth, and crossing lines show
  regions that overtook one another.
- **Satisfaction score by support team before and after a process change** in an operations report. The chart shows
  whether the change moved every team or only some.
- **Market share of a few vendors in two quarters** in a competitive review, where the order matters as much as the size.

## When not to use

- **Three or more moments in time**, such as monthly values for a year: use `LineChart`, which keeps the time axis.
- **Only the latest value of each item**, with no comparison: use `BarChart`.
- **Parts of one whole** rather than a change between two moments: use `DonutChart`.
- **More than about ten items**: the labels crowd each other on the two axes. Use `BarChart` for a longer list, sorted by
  the second value.
- **A distribution of many observations per group**, such as response times by region: use `Ridgeline`.

## Usage

Each `SlopeItem` is one line with a `Key`, a `Label`, a `Start` value and an `End` value. `StartLabel` and `EndLabel`
name the two moments; they default to "Before" and "After".

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:SlopeChart Label="Conversion rate by channel"
                    StartLabel="Q1"
                    EndLabel="Q2"
                    HighlightKey="search"
                    ItemsSource="{Binding Channels}" />
</UserControl>
```

`SlopeChart` derives from Avalonia's `Control` and draws itself, so the lines, labels and rank moves are one drawing that
moves smoothly when the data changes. The whole box takes the pointer, and the chart is focusable as one group.

### Anatomy

1. **Column headings** (`StartLabel`, `EndLabel`): one heading above each value axis, centered on it.
2. **Value axes**: two 1 px vertical lines in the border color. Both columns share one value scale, so a steeper line is
   a larger change.
3. **Lines**: 2 px round-capped strokes in a neutral tone. The item named by `HighlightKey` takes the first series color,
   and when one item is in focus the others fade.
4. **Dots**: a 4 px dot at each end, outlined in the surface color so it reads over the line.
5. **Start labels**: the name and then the value, right aligned 10 px to the left of the start axis.
6. **End labels**: the value 10 px to the right of the end axis, followed by the rank move when `IsRankVisible` is on:
   an arrow with the number of places, or "=" when the rank did not change.
7. **Leader lines**: a thin line from each label to its dot. Labels pushed aside to avoid a collision stay connected by
   these lines.
8. **Tooltip**: the name, both values, the change and the rank text, such as "up 1 to rank 1". It is at least 168 px wide.

The plot height is 44 px per item and at least 200 px when `PlotHeight` is not set. Below 440 px of width the label
columns narrow and the names are shortened; the full names stay in the tooltip and the data table.

### Datasets

Replace `ItemsSource` to switch the dataset. Every line, dot and label slides to its new place. Change `Label` in the same
step so the text matches the data.

```csharp
conversion.Click += (_, _) =>
{
    chart.Label = "Conversion rate by channel";
    chart.ItemsSource = Conversion;
};
```

Items keep their line across datasets when they keep the same `Key`, so the line morphs instead of being replaced. Use
keys that name the entity, such as a channel id, not a row number that changes when the list is re-sorted.

### Value and change formats

`ValueFormatter` formats the values at each end. `ChangeFormatter` formats the change beside the rank, and it receives
the change and the item.

```csharp
chart.ValueFormatter = v => $"{v:0.0}%";
chart.ChangeFormatter = (change, _) => $"{(change >= 0 ? "+" : "−")}{Math.Abs(change):0.0} pts";
```

By default values are grouped with at most one decimal, and the change is signed with a true minus sign, such as "+2" or
"−2". Set the formatters once on the chart so that every item reads the same way.

### Highlight and rank

`HighlightKey` draws one item in the first series color, and the others stay neutral. `IsRankVisible` turns the rank
moves on or off.

```xml
<arc:SlopeChart Label="Close values"
                StartLabel="2023"
                EndLabel="2024"
                IsRankVisible="False"
                MaxWidth="420"
                ItemsSource="{Binding Values}" />
```

Turn the rank off when the order does not matter to the question, or when the rank would only repeat what the slope
already shows.

### Reading an item

`ActiveKey` is the item under the pointer or the keyboard, and it is two-way. `ActiveKeyChanged` reports each change, with
the item in `Item`.

```csharp
chart.ActiveKeyChanged += (_, e) => reading.Text = e.Item is { } item
    ? $"{item.Label}: {item.Start} → {item.End}"
    : "No item in focus";
```

### Binding to a view model

With CommunityToolkit.Mvvm the view model owns the items and the key of the item in focus. Each row is a record, and the
chart reads its fields through member bindings, so the rows do not need to be `SlopeItem` objects.

```csharp
public sealed record ChannelRate(string Key, string Name, double Q1, double Q2);

public partial class ChannelsViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    [ObservableProperty]
    private ChannelRate[] _channels = [];

    [ObservableProperty]
    private string? _activeChannel;
}
```

```xml
<arc:SlopeChart Label="Conversion rate by channel"
                StartLabel="Q1"
                EndLabel="Q2"
                ItemsSource="{Binding Channels}"
                KeyMemberBinding="{Binding Key}"
                LabelMemberBinding="{Binding Name}"
                StartMemberBinding="{Binding Q1}"
                EndMemberBinding="{Binding Q2}"
                ActiveKey="{Binding ActiveChannel, Mode=TwoWay}" />
```

- `ActiveKey` is two-way: the chart writes the key of the item in focus, and the view model can focus an item from code.
- The selectors (`KeySelector`, `LabelSelector`, `StartSelector`, `EndSelector`) win over the member bindings when both
  are set, which is useful when a value needs a calculation.
- The examples use plain `Binding` for brevity. Compiled bindings need `x:DataType` on the view.

### Data shape and label collisions

Each item needs a stable `Key`, a `Label`, and both values. Both columns use one value axis, so a line's slope compares
the two moments directly. Give every item both values, because each one is a number that is drawn at its place.

When two labels would overlap in one column, they move apart by the label gap (20 px) and stay connected to their dots by
leader lines. Touching labels form a group that settles around the place its members want to be. The demo below has four
close values in the first column; the names stay readable because the labels spread instead of stacking.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.SlopeChartLabelCollisionsDemo">
    <arc:SlopeChart Label="Close values"
                    StartLabel="2023"
                    EndLabel="2024"
                    IsRankVisible="False"
                    MaxWidth="420"
                    HorizontalAlignment="Left">
        <arc:SlopeChart.Items>
            <arc:SlopeItem Key="a" Label="Alpha" Start="10" End="12" />
            <arc:SlopeItem Key="b" Label="Beta" Start="10.2" End="12.1" />
            <arc:SlopeItem Key="c" Label="Gamma" Start="10.4" End="8" />
            <arc:SlopeItem Key="d" Label="Delta with a long name" Start="10.5" End="12.2" />
        </arc:SlopeChart.Items>
    </arc:SlopeChart>
</UserControl>
```

### Example: channel conversion in a growth review

A growth review for Acme Analytics compares the conversion rate of six acquisition channels in Q1 and Q2. The chart
highlights organic search, the channel the team invested in, so the reader's eye has one target. Email still leads in
both quarters, which the slope shows without a label. The caption states the finding, so the card reads without hovering.

![A slope chart of six channels, with organic search highlighted and moving from fourth to second](https://docs.tkcode.si/shots/Docs/Charts/SlopeChart/images/ChannelConversion.webp)

```xml
<Border xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
        xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
        xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
        Width="680"
        Padding="24"
        CornerRadius="12"
        Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Surface}"
        BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Border}"
        BorderThickness="1">
    <StackPanel Spacing="16">
        <StackPanel Spacing="4">
            <TextBlock Text="Conversion rate by channel" FontSize="16" FontWeight="SemiBold" />
            <TextBlock Text="Percent of sessions that bought, Q1 and Q2 2026. Organic search moved from fourth to second."
                       TextWrapping="Wrap"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
        </StackPanel>
        <arc:SlopeChart Label="Conversion rate by channel"
                        StartLabel="Q1"
                        EndLabel="Q2"
                        HighlightKey="search">
            <arc:SlopeChart.Items>
                <arc:SlopeItem Key="search" Label="Organic search" Start="3.1" End="4.6" />
                <arc:SlopeItem Key="email" Label="Email" Start="5.8" End="5.2" />
                <arc:SlopeItem Key="paid" Label="Paid social" Start="2.2" End="3.4" />
                <arc:SlopeItem Key="referral" Label="Referral" Start="4.4" End="4.1" />
                <arc:SlopeItem Key="direct" Label="Direct" Start="3.6" End="3.7" />
                <arc:SlopeItem Key="display" Label="Display ads" Start="1.2" End="0.9" />
            </arc:SlopeChart.Items>
        </arc:SlopeChart>
    </StackPanel>
</Border>
```

The highlighted line is the story, and the rank moves beside each value say which channels rose or fell. Email and
Referral slipped slightly, and Display ads has the lowest value in both quarters. The values are plain numbers in the
screenshot, so the caption carries the unit; in an app, set `ValueFormatter` to add the percent sign.

### Content guidelines

- **Chart label**: the measure and its scope, such as "Conversion rate by channel". The label names the chart for
  assistive technology and the summary.
- **Column headings**: the real names of the two moments, such as "Q1" and "Q2" or "2025" and "2026". Use "Before" and
  "After" only when the moments are events, such as a launch.
- **Item labels**: the entity name in sentence case, short enough to sit beside its value: "Organic search", "Paid
  social". Long names are kept in the tooltip and the data table.
- **Changes**: write the change with its sign and unit, such as "+1.5 pts", so the reader does not need the axis.

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| Before / After | Q1 / Q2 |
| Conversion | Conversion rate by channel, Q1 and Q2 |
| +1.5 | +1.5 pts |
| SEO | Organic search |

### Best practices

**Do**

- Keep the same unit on both moments. A slope between two different measures is not a comparison, and a reader cannot
  tell that from the picture.
- Keep the list to about three to ten items, so the two labels in each column stay readable.
- Highlight the one item the story is about with `HighlightKey`. The other lines stay neutral, so the highlight means
  something.
- Give each item a stable `Key` that names the entity. A dataset change then morphs the same line instead of replacing it.

**Avoid**

- Plotting more than two moments as slopes. A third point makes the line look like a trend it is not; use `LineChart`.
- Highlighting several items. The first series color stops meaning anything when every line uses it.
- Hiding the change when the reader must compare magnitudes. Keep the change or the rank visible in that case.
- Changing `Label` and the data in different steps. The title then describes the previous dataset for a moment.

### Common questions

**Why do the column headings say "Before" and "After"?** Those are the defaults for `StartLabel` and `EndLabel`. Set them
to the real moments, such as "Q1" and "Q2".

**Why do the keyboard and the summary list the items in a different order from my data?** The keyboard and the summary
follow the end value, highest first, while the drawing keeps your data order. Sort the data by the end value when the two
orders should match.

**What does a flat dataset look like?** When every value is the same, the axis spans one unit on either side, so the
lines sit in the middle of the plot.

**What happens to the reading when the item in focus is removed?** `ActiveKey` is cleared to null when its item is no
longer in `ItemsSource`, so the reading stops describing an item that is gone.

## API reference

### SlopeChart

A before / after comparison on two shared axes (Arc "Slope chart"). Lines draw in from the first column to the second on first view; labels push apart instead of overlapping and connect back to their dots with thin leaders; rank movement sits beside each end value. A new dataset slides every line, dot and label to its new place on the shared morph spring. Hover or the arrow keys (in end-value order) bring one line forward and show a tooltip.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ItemsSource` | `IEnumerable?` | `null` | Defines the `ItemsSource` property. |
| `KeySelector` | `Func<object, string>?` | `null` | Defines the `KeySelector` property. |
| `LabelSelector` | `Func<object, string>?` | `null` | Defines the `LabelSelector` property. |
| `StartSelector` | `Func<object, double>?` | `null` | Defines the `StartSelector` property. |
| `EndSelector` | `Func<object, double>?` | `null` | Defines the `EndSelector` property. |
| `Label` | `string?` | `null` | Defines the `Label` property. |
| `StartLabel` | `string` | `"Before"` | Defines the `StartLabel` property. |
| `EndLabel` | `string` | `"After"` | Defines the `EndLabel` property. |
| `ValueFormatter` | `Func<double, string>?` | `null` | Defines the `ValueFormatter` property. |
| `ChangeFormatter` | `Func<double, SlopeItem, string>?` | `null` | Defines the `ChangeFormatter` property. |
| `PlotHeight` | `double` | `NaN` | Defines the `PlotHeight` property. |
| `HighlightKey` | `string?` | `null` | Defines the `HighlightKey` property. |
| `ActiveKey` | `string?` | `null` | Defines the `ActiveKey` property. |
| `IsRankVisible` | `bool` | `true` | Defines the `IsRankVisible` property. |
| `EmptyLabel` | `string` | `"No data"` | Defines the `EmptyLabel` property. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ActiveKeyChanged` | `SlopeActiveKeyChangedEventArgs` | Raised when the item in focus changes (pointer, keyboard or `ActiveKey`). |

Derives from `Control`: every member of `Control` works as well.

### SlopeItem

One line of a `SlopeChart`: an item's value in the first and the second period.

## Accessibility

- `Label` names the chart. The chart is a focusable group with a role description and instructions for the keys.
- Tab moves focus to the chart and reads the item with the highest end value first. The down and right arrow keys move
  to the next item and the up and left arrow keys to the previous one, in order of the end value.
- Home and End go to the first and last item, Escape clears the reading, and a touch press and drag reads the nearest
  line.
- A polite live region announces both values, the change and the rank move, such as "Search, Q1 3, Q2 5, +2, up 1 to
  rank 1". A hidden data table lists the items in order of their end value.
- Rank moves use an arrow glyph with a number, so they are not shown by color alone. Lines and labels are hidden from
  assistive technology.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Tab` | Focus the chart; the item with the highest end value is read first |
| `Down` / `Right` | Move to the next item in end-value order |
| `Up` / `Left` | Move to the previous item in end-value order |
| `Home` / `End` | Move to the first (highest end value) or the last item |
| `Escape` | Clear the reading |

From rest, any arrow key moves to the first item. The mouse reads the line nearest the pointer and clears the reading when
it leaves the chart.

## Motion

- On first view each line draws from its start point to its end point, with a short stagger. The dots and labels arrive
  as the line lands.
- Switching datasets moves the lines, dots, labels and leader lines on a shared morph spring. Rank numbers roll in the
  direction they moved.
- The focused item comes to the front and the others fade. The tooltip slides to the middle of its line.
- Reduced motion draws every line at once and moves them at once on a change. Off jumps to the final state.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| First view | Lines draw from start to end with a short stagger; dots and labels land with each line | Every line is drawn at once | Final state |
| Dataset change | Lines, dots, labels and leaders move on a shared spring; rank numbers roll | Moves at once | Final state |

## Related

- `LineChart` for three or more moments in time.
- `BarChart` for one value per item at a single moment.
- `Ridgeline` for how the distribution of groups changes.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `LineChart` | There are three or more moments, and the time axis matters |
| `BarChart` | Each item has one value at a single moment, or the list is longer than about ten |
| `Ridgeline` | Each group is a distribution of many observations, not one value |
| `DonutChart` | The data is parts of one whole, not a change between two moments |
| `Sparkline` | A compact trend sits beside a single number |

---

# Sparkline

> Show a compact trend beside a value.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/sparkline

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.SparklineKpiCardsDemo">
    <WrapPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center" ItemSpacing="12" LineSpacing="12">
        <arc:Sparkline x:Name="RevenueCard"
                       Label="Revenue"
                       Value="$48.2K"
                       Change="+4.1%"
                       Tone="Success"
                       Width="220" />
        <arc:Sparkline x:Name="ChurnCard"
                       Label="Churn"
                       Value="2.4%"
                       Change="+0.3 pts"
                       Tone="Danger"
                       Width="220" />
        <arc:Sparkline x:Name="LatencyCard"
                       Label="Latency"
                       Value="182 ms"
                       Change="−6 ms"
                       Tone="Accent"
                       Width="220" />
        <arc:Sparkline x:Name="QueueCard"
                       Label="Queue depth"
                       Value="1,204"
                       Change="Rising"
                       Tone="Warning"
                       Width="220" />
    </WrapPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using System.Globalization;
using Avalonia.Controls;
using TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Pages;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class SparklineKpiCardsDemo : UserControl
{
    public SparklineKpiCardsDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();

        RevenueCard.ItemsSource = ChartsADemoData.Daily(14, 40, 14, 1, 0.9);
        ChurnCard.ItemsSource = ChartsADemoData.Daily(14, 20, 8, 2, 0.4);
        LatencyCard.ItemsSource = ChartsADemoData.Daily(14, 190, 30, 3, -0.8);
        QueueCard.ItemsSource = ChartsADemoData.Daily(14, 900, 300, 4, 25);

        // One label per point: scrubbing reads the date instead of the position.
        var labels = ChartsADemoData.Days(14).Select(day => day.ToString("MMM d", CultureInfo.GetCultureInfo("en-US"))).ToArray();
        foreach (var card in new[] { RevenueCard, ChurnCard, LatencyCard, QueueCard })
        {
            card.PointLabels = labels;
        }
    }
}
```

## When to use

`Sparkline` is a small trend line with a headline value and an aside, sized to sit inside a card, a table cell or a KPI
block. It answers "where is this number going?" in the space a number takes, so the reader sees the direction and
shape of a metric next to its current value without an axis or a legend.

- **Revenue and usage cards on an analytics overview**: a card that shows `$48.2K` and `+4.1%` with the last 14 days of
  revenue underneath. The shape shows whether the number is rising in steady steps or spiking on one day.
- **Service rows in an operations console**: a table of services where each row shows a latency or error-rate trend.
  Many rows of the same size make the table scannable: one glance finds the service whose line bends the wrong way.
- **Churn, queue and backlog tiles in a CRM or support tool**: a value with its direction and a tone, such as a
  rising queue depth shown in the warning color. The tone tells the reader whether the trend is good or bad.
- **Billing and usage summaries**: a per-customer seat count or a daily API call volume beside the current total, where
  the reader needs the recent pattern more than the exact points.
- **Scrubbing a recent history in a detail panel**: a reader moves the pointer or the arrow keys along the line to read
  the value and the date of an earlier point, without opening a full chart.

## When not to use

- **Discrete periods that people compare side by side**, such as twelve months of revenue or the orders per weekday:
  use `BarChart`, which has a value axis and one bar per period.
- **A single current value with its change and no history**: use `MetricCard`. A sparkline with one point draws a flat
  line, which says nothing about direction.
- **A trend that needs axes, several series or a legend**, such as revenue by product line over a quarter: use
  `LineChart`.
- **A very long series that people must zoom or pan**, such as a year of minute-level metrics: use `BrushChart`, which
  holds a window over the full range and lets the reader select a span.
- **A value measured against a known range**, such as disk usage out of a 500 GB quota: use `Gauge`, which shows the
  position on a scale rather than the path to it.

## Usage

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:Sparkline Label="Revenue"
                   Value="$48.2K"
                   Change="+4.1%"
                   Tone="Success"
                   Width="220"
                   ItemsSource="{Binding Revenue}" />
</UserControl>
```

`ItemsSource` holds the values from oldest to newest, one value per point. `Value` and `Change` form the headline and
the aside that are shown at rest. `Label` names the measurement.

`Sparkline` derives from `ChartBase`, the base of Arc's self-drawn charts. That base supplies the data pipeline
(`ItemsSource` with `YBinding` or `YSelector` for item objects, or plain numbers), the token palette, the first-view
reveal, the active-point readout (`ActiveIndex`), value formatting and the accessible summary. The sparkline adds the
headline and aside, the scrubbing gesture and a plot with no axes. Because it shares the base with `LineChart` and
`BarChart`, the same data and formatting rules apply everywhere in a screen.

### Anatomy

1. **Label** (`Label`): the measurement's name, 14 px, in the secondary text color, on the baseline of the headline.
   It is also the start of the accessible name.
2. **Headline** (`Value`): 18 px, medium weight, in the foreground color, right-aligned in its slot. It is hidden when
   `Value` is null.
3. **Aside** (`Change`): 12 px, medium weight. At rest it shows `Change` in the tone color (the strong accent color for
   `Accent`). While scrubbing it shows the point (see "Scrubbing" below).
4. **Caption gap**: 12 units of space between the caption row and the plot.
5. **Plot**: the line, its fill, a 1 px baseline in the border color and the scrubbing cursor. The line is
   2.5 units wide with round caps.
6. **Area** (`ShowArea`): a 9% wash of the tone text color under the line. It is drawn beneath the line and can be turned off.
7. **End dot**: a round dot of the tone color that rests on the latest point, 7 units in diameter at rest and 10 while a
   point is scrubbed. It is hidden until the first reveal has finished.
8. **Focus ring**: drawn by Arc in the focus color when the plot has keyboard focus. The window's default focus adorner
   is suppressed.

### Headline, aside and scrubbing

The caption shows one of two states. At rest it shows `Value` and `Change`. While a point is scrubbed it changes to the
scrubbed point, and the headline and aside roll to the new text.

| State | Headline | Aside |
|---|---|---|
| At rest, `Value` and `Change` set | `Value` | `Change`, in the tone color |
| Scrubbing, `Value` and `PointLabels` set | The scrubbed value, formatted with `ValueFormat` | The point label, such as `Sep 14` |
| Scrubbing, `Value` set, no `PointLabels` | The scrubbed value | The position, such as `4 of 14` |
| Scrubbing, `Value` null | Hidden | The scrubbed value and the point label, joined with a dot |
| At rest, `Value` null | Hidden | `Change`, or nothing when `Change` is empty |

While a point is scrubbed, the aside uses the secondary text color instead of the tone color. The change is not
happening at that point; the date or position is context, so it stays neutral.

### Tones

`Tone` colors the line, the fill, the end dot and, at rest, the aside. Pick it from the direction of the metric and
whether that direction is good, not from the chart's decoration.

| `Tone` | Use it for | Aside color |
|---|---|---|
| `Accent` (default) | A neutral trend such as traffic, or a metric without a good or bad direction | Strong accent |
| `Success` | A metric that improves when it rises: revenue, conversion, uptime | Success |
| `Warning` | A value that needs attention without being an error: a growing queue, a rising backlog | Warning |
| `Danger` | A metric that is getting worse: churn, error rate, latency above target | Danger |

```xml
<arc:Sparkline Label="Churn" Value="2.4%" Change="+0.3 pts" Tone="Danger" ItemsSource="{Binding Churn}" />
<arc:Sparkline Label="Queue depth" Value="1,204" Change="Rising" Tone="Warning" ItemsSource="{Binding Queue}" />
```

Keep the sign in `Change` as well as the tone. A reader who cannot tell the colors apart still reads `+0.3 pts`, and a
reader on a monochrome print still reads the direction.

### Point labels

`PointLabels` gives one label for each point, in the same order as `ItemsSource`. When a point is scrubbed, its label
replaces `Change` in the aside, and it is the text the accessible value reads. Set it for every sparkline whose points
are dates. Without it, the aside shows the position, such as `4 of 14`, which means nothing to a reader.

```csharp
var labels = days.Select(d => d.ToString("MMM d", CultureInfo.GetCultureInfo("en-US"))).ToArray();
revenue.PointLabels = labels;
```

The count of labels should match the count of values. A point without a label falls back to its position.

### Scale and size

`DrawingWidth` and `DrawingHeight` are in Arc's drawing units, with defaults of 160 and 52. They set only the aspect
ratio of the plot. The plot width follows the width of the sparkline, so the height is the width multiplied by
`DrawingHeight` divided by `DrawingWidth`. A sparkline 320 pixels wide at the default ratio is 104 pixels high.

| Place | Width | `DrawingHeight` | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| KPI card | 200 to 240 | 52 (default) | Headline and aside on one row above the line |
| Chart panel beside a table | 240 to 320 | 52 (default) | Room for `ShowArea` and scrubbing |
| Table row | 120 to 160 | 32 | Set `ShowArea="False"` and `IsInteractive="False"` |

Set `Width` on the element to fix its size, and let the height follow the ratio. Leave `Height` unset: the drawing
ratio is what keeps the line from stretching when a card resizes.

### Dense tables

In a table with many rows, turn scrubbing off. `IsInteractive="False"` removes the tab stop and the pointer handling
from each row, so the table keeps one focus order. `ShowArea="False"` keeps the line quiet when twenty rows carry a wash
each.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.SparklineDenseTableDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="8">
        <Grid ColumnDefinitions="140,*">
            <TextBlock Text="api-gateway"
                       TextWrapping="Wrap"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
            <arc:Sparkline x:Name="Gateway"
                           Grid.Column="1"
                           Label="api-gateway"
                           ShowArea="False"
                           IsInteractive="False"
                           Width="160"
                           DrawingHeight="32" />
        </Grid>
        <Grid ColumnDefinitions="140,*">
            <TextBlock Text="billing"
                       TextWrapping="Wrap"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
            <arc:Sparkline x:Name="Billing"
                           Grid.Column="1"
                           Label="billing"
                           ShowArea="False"
                           IsInteractive="False"
                           Width="160"
                           DrawingHeight="32" />
        </Grid>
        <Grid ColumnDefinitions="140,*">
            <TextBlock Text="search"
                       TextWrapping="Wrap"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
            <arc:Sparkline x:Name="Search"
                           Grid.Column="1"
                           Label="search"
                           ShowArea="False"
                           IsInteractive="False"
                           Width="160"
                           DrawingHeight="32" />
        </Grid>
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Pages;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class SparklineDenseTableDemo : UserControl
{
    public SparklineDenseTableDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Gateway.ItemsSource = ChartsADemoData.Daily(20, 50, 30, 11);
        Billing.ItemsSource = ChartsADemoData.Daily(20, 50, 30, 12);
        Search.ItemsSource = ChartsADemoData.Daily(20, 50, 30, 13);
    }
}
```

```xml
<arc:Sparkline Label="api-gateway"
               Width="160"
               DrawingHeight="32"
               ShowArea="False"
               IsInteractive="False"
               ItemsSource="{Binding Gateway}" />
```

Keep the label short in a row. The row already names the service, so the sparkline label can repeat the service name
or be left as the metric, such as `Latency`.

### Without a headline

When `Value` is not set, the headline is hidden and the scrubbed value and its point label appear in the aside. Use
this form for a detail panel where the number is shown elsewhere and the line is only there to be read.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.SparklineWithoutHeadlineDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12">
        <arc:Button Content="New data" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Click="OnNewDataClick" />
        <arc:Sparkline x:Name="Visits"
                       Label="Visits (scrub for the value)"
                       Width="300"
                       HorizontalAlignment="Left" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;
using TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Pages;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class SparklineWithoutHeadlineDemo : UserControl
{
    private int _seed = 10;

    public SparklineWithoutHeadlineDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Visits.ItemsSource = ChartsADemoData.Daily(30, 300, 120, 7, 3);
    }

    // New data morphs the line.
    private void OnNewDataClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
        => Visits.ItemsSource = ChartsADemoData.Daily(30, 300, 120, _seed++, 3);
}
```

```xml
<arc:Sparkline Label="Visits" Width="300" ItemsSource="{Binding Visits}" />
```

When the data changes, the line morphs from its current shape into the new one. The same chart keeps its place on the
screen, so a refresh of a visits panel reads as an update rather than a new chart.

### Binding to a view model

In an MVVM app the view model owns the series, the headline, the change and the labels. `Sparkline` reads them through
bindings. With CommunityToolkit.Mvvm, the view model is an `ObservableObject` with observable properties, and each
refresh assigns new collections instead of editing one in place.

```csharp
public sealed record DailyRevenue(DateOnly Day, double Amount);

public interface IRevenueApi
{
    Task<IReadOnlyList<DailyRevenue>> GetDailyRevenueAsync(int days);
}

public partial class RevenueCardViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    private readonly IRevenueApi _api;

    public RevenueCardViewModel(IRevenueApi api) => _api = api;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private string? _headline = "$48.2K";

    [ObservableProperty]
    private string? _change = "+4.1%";

    [ObservableProperty]
    private IReadOnlyList<double> _amounts = [];

    [ObservableProperty]
    private IReadOnlyList<string> _pointLabels = [];

    [RelayCommand]
    private async Task RefreshAsync()
    {
        // The API returns the days from oldest to newest. A new list is one data change, so the line
        // morphs once per refresh.
        var days = await _api.GetDailyRevenueAsync(14);
        Amounts = days.Select(d => d.Amount).ToArray();
        PointLabels = days.Select(d => d.Day.ToString("MMM d", CultureInfo.GetCultureInfo("en-US"))).ToArray();
        Headline = days[^1].Amount.ToString("C1", CultureInfo.GetCultureInfo("en-US"));
    }
}
```

```xml
<arc:Sparkline Label="Revenue, 14 days"
               Value="{Binding Headline}"
               Change="{Binding Change}"
               Tone="Success"
               Width="220"
               ItemsSource="{Binding Amounts}"
               PointLabels="{Binding PointLabels}" />
```

`Value`, `Change`, `ItemsSource` and `PointLabels` are one-way: the view model's values flow into the sparkline. The
only two-way property is `ActiveIndex`, the point being read. Bind it when the screen needs to know which point the
reader is on, for example to update a detail row beside the chart.

```xml
<arc:Sparkline Label="Revenue, 14 days"
               ItemsSource="{Binding Amounts}"
               ActiveIndex="{Binding SelectedDayIndex, Mode=TwoWay}" />
```

`ActiveIndex` is `null` at rest and the index of the scrubbed point while the reader scrubs. The `ActiveIndexChanged`
event reports the same moves for code that prefers events. It is raised with a `null` index when the reader lets go.

### Data shape and performance

`ItemsSource` takes numbers or item objects. For item objects, set `YBinding` (or `YSelector`) to read the value, and
`XBinding` (or `XSelector`) for the date, which can be a `DateTime`, `DateTimeOffset` or `DateOnly`. Use
`CompiledBinding` with `DataType` so the path is checked at compile time and works with ahead-of-time compilation.

- **Length**: use the period the card names, such as 14 daily values for "Revenue, 14 days". The drawn curve has a
  fixed number of samples, so a longer series draws at about the same cost per instance; the reader gains nothing
  from a long series in a card, so aggregate it first.
- **Flat or empty series**: one value draws a flat line. An empty series shows `EmptyLabel` in the accessible summary
  and draws nothing. Set `EmptyLabel` when an empty card should say why, such as "No data yet".
- **Update frequency**: each change morphs the line, so a refresh once a minute reads as an update. A series that
  changes every second makes the line move constantly; aggregate the data before it reaches the control.
- **Many instances**: each sparkline tracks its own size and reveal, so a table with hundreds of rows creates hundreds
  of plots. Page long tables, and turn scrubbing off in dense rows.
- **Number formatting**: values are formatted with `ValueFormat`, a .NET format string such as `"N0"` or `"0.0'%'"`.
  The default is `"#,##0.###"`. Format the `Value` headline yourself with the same rule so that the headline and the
  scrubbed values agree. For context-dependent text, `ValueFormatter` receives the value and its index.

### Example: operations overview

A platform team's overview shows three trends in one row: revenue, p95 latency and the support queue. Each card keeps
its headline at rest, so the current number is always readable, and the tone follows what is good for the business:
revenue rising is `Success`, latency rising is `Danger`, a growing queue is `Warning`. The cards stay interactive
because there are only three and the reader may want the date of a spike. Each card has its own point labels, so a
scrubbed point reads as a date.

The view model supplies the headline, the change, the values and the labels for each card. The XAML only binds them.

```xml
<WrapPanel ItemSpacing="16" LineSpacing="16">
    <arc:Sparkline Label="Revenue, 14 days"
                   Value="{Binding Revenue.Headline}"
                   Change="{Binding Revenue.Change}"
                   Tone="Success"
                   Width="240"
                   ItemsSource="{Binding Revenue.Amounts}"
                   PointLabels="{Binding Revenue.PointLabels}" />
    <arc:Sparkline Label="p95 latency, 14 days"
                   Value="{Binding Latency.Headline}"
                   Change="{Binding Latency.Change}"
                   Tone="Danger"
                   Width="240"
                   ItemsSource="{Binding Latency.Amounts}"
                   PointLabels="{Binding Latency.PointLabels}" />
    <arc:Sparkline Label="Support queue, 14 days"
                   Value="{Binding Queue.Headline}"
                   Change="{Binding Queue.Change}"
                   Tone="Warning"
                   Width="240"
                   ItemsSource="{Binding Queue.Amounts}"
                   PointLabels="{Binding Queue.PointLabels}" />
</WrapPanel>
```

### Content guidelines

`Label` names the measurement and its period, in sentence case. The accessible name starts with it, so a label such as
"Revenue, 14 days" reads better than the bare metric. Keep the headline and the change short enough to fit the card on
one row.

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| `Label="LATENCY"` | `Label="Latency"` |
| `Label="Revenue trend for the last two weeks"` | `Label="Revenue, 14 days"` |
| `Value="48200"` | `Value="$48.2K"` |
| `Value="182 milliseconds"` | `Value="182 ms"` |
| `Value="1204"` | `Value="1,204"` |
| `Change="Up"` | `Change="+4.1%"` |
| `PointLabels` with `2026-09-14` | `PointLabels` with `Sep 14` |
| `Label=""` | A name for the metric, such as `Churn` |

### Best practices

**Do**

- Name the measurement and its period in `Label`, such as "Revenue, 14 days". It is the first thing a screen reader
  reads, and the period tells the reader what the line covers.
- Choose `Tone` from whether a rise is good for the business. The same shape means different things for revenue and for
  latency, and the tone tells the reader which.
- Set `PointLabels` on every sparkline whose points are dates, so a scrubbed point reads as a date rather than a position.
- Keep the sign in `Change` and format `Value` with the same rules as `ValueFormat`, so the headline and the scrubbed
  values agree.
- Turn `IsInteractive` off in table rows, where many tab stops would make the table hard to traverse.

**Avoid**

- A sparkline for a single value or a series of one point. It draws a flat line and says nothing about direction; use
  `MetricCard` for that case.
- `ShowArea` on every row of a long table. Twenty washes compete with the text they sit beside.
- Replacing `ItemsSource` on a timer that fires every second. Each change morphs the line, so the chart never settles;
  aggregate the data to the period the card shows.
- `Tone` as decoration. A color with no direction behind it teaches the reader to ignore the color.
- Setting `Height` on the element. The drawing ratio sets the height, and a fixed height stretches the line when the card
  resizes.

### Common questions

**Why does my headline disappear while I scrub?** It is hidden only when `Value` is null. Then the scrubbed value and its
point label appear in the aside. With `Value` set, the headline shows the scrubbed value and the aside shows the point
label, and both return to `Value` and `Change` when the reader leaves the plot or presses Escape.

**How do I start the readout on a specific point from code?** Set `ActiveIndex` to the point's index, for example
`revenue.ActiveIndex = 6;`, and set it to `null` to return to the latest value. The property is two-way, so a view model
bound to it sees the reader's moves too.

**What does a sparkline show with one value, or with no values?** One value draws a flat line at the middle of the plot.
An empty series draws nothing and reads `EmptyLabel` in the accessible summary. Set `EmptyLabel` when an empty card
should explain itself, such as "No data yet".

**Why is the line shorter than I expected?** The height comes from the drawing ratio, not from a fixed value. A
`Width` of 240 with the default `DrawingWidth` of 160 and `DrawingHeight` of 52 gives a plot about 78 pixels high. Change
`DrawingHeight` to make the line taller or shorter for the same width.

## API reference

### Sparkline

Arc's sparkline: a compact trend beside a value, for cards, table rows and KPI blocks. Scrub it with the pointer or the arrow keys: the cursor springs between points, the stretch after it dims as if it has not happened yet, and the headline and aside roll to the scrubbed point. The line draws once like a pen the first time it is half visible; the fill follows the tip, then the end dot lands. New data morphs the line from the shape on screen. Motion is code-driven because the pen tip, cursor and morph are coordinates inside the self-drawn plot.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Value` | `string?` | `null` | The headline at rest, such as "$48.2K". Leave it null to show the scrubbed value beside the label instead. |
| `Change` | `string?` | `null` | The aside at rest, such as "+4.1%", in the tone color. |
| `Tone` | `ChartTone` | `Accent` | Color of the line, its fill and the change. |
| `DrawingWidth` | `double` | `160` | Drawing width in Arc's SVG units; with `DrawingHeight` it sets the aspect ratio (the width follows the container). |
| `DrawingHeight` | `double` | `52` | Drawing height in Arc's SVG units. |
| `PointLabels` | `IReadOnlyList<string>?` | `null` | One label per point, such as a date; it replaces the change while that point is scrubbed. |
| `ShowArea` | `bool` | `true` | A quiet wash of the tone under the line. |
| `IsInteractive` | `bool` | `true` | Pointer and keyboard scrubbing. Turn it off in dense tables to drop the tab stop and pointer handling. |
| `Label` | `string` | `""` | What is measured, such as "Signups". Names the chart, its summary and its data table. |
| `Unit` | `string` | `""` | Unit after each value in readouts, such as "ms". |
| `EmptyLabel` | `string` | `"No data for this range"` | Shown when there is nothing to draw. |
| `CategoryLabel` | `string` | `"Point"` | Name of the category column in the data table and the explore label, such as "Date". |
| `ValueFormat` | `string?` | `null` | .NET format string for values (en-US), such as "N0", "C0" or "0.0'%'". Null uses the chart's default. |
| `ValueFormatter` | `Func<ChartValueContext, string>?` | `null` | Formats values with context (series, index); wins over `ValueFormat`. |
| `PlotHeight` | `double` | `220` | Plot height in pixels; the width follows the container. |
| `ItemsSource` | `IEnumerable?` | `null` | The data items. Values are read with `YSelector`/`YBinding` (or per series), categories with `XSelector`/`XBinding`. |
| `XBinding` | `BindingBase?` | `null` | Reads each item's category or date: the AOT-safe path form, such as `XBinding="{CompiledBinding Date, DataType=local:Day}"` (a reflection `{Binding Date}` also works). |
| `XSelector` | `Func<object, object?>?` | `null` | Reads each item's category or date (a string, DateTime, DateTimeOffset or DateOnly). |
| `YBinding` | `BindingBase?` | `null` | Reads each item's value for a single-series chart (`YBinding="{CompiledBinding Visits, DataType=local:Day}"`). |
| `YSelector` | `Func<object, double>?` | `null` | Reads each item's value for a single-series chart. |
| `XLabelFormatter` | `Func<object?, string>?` | `null` | Full label of a category (tooltip, headline, screen readers). Dates default to "Tue, Sep 15". |
| `XAxisFormatter` | `Func<object?, string?>?` | `null` | Short axis label of a category; return null to keep the axis quiet there. Dates default to "Sep 15". |
| `ActiveIndex` | `int?` | `null` | The point being read (crosshair, scrubbed bar, hovered segment), or null at rest. Two-way. |
| `Summary` | `string` | – | *Read-only.* A one-paragraph description for assistive technology, such as "Signups, Sep 1 to Sep 30. ...". |
| `DataTableText` | `string` | – | *Read-only.* The accessible data table as text: a header line, then one line per row (tab separated). |
| `Announcement` | `string` | – | *Read-only.* The latest polite announcement (what Arc's live region reads), such as "Loading". |
| `ShowLegend` | `bool?` | `null` | Series toggles. Null shows the legend when there is more than one series. |
| `ShowGrid` | `bool` | `true` | Horizontal gridlines at the value ticks. |
| `ShowXAxis` | `bool` | `true` | The category (time) axis labels under the plot. |
| `ShowYAxis` | `bool` | `true` | The value axis labels in the right-hand gutter. |
| `YMinimum` | `double?` | `null` | Fixes the bottom of the value axis (default: zero, or the data minimum when it dips below). |
| `YMaximum` | `double?` | `null` | Fixes the top of the value axis (default: the next nice tick above the data). |
| `TickFormatter` | `Func<double, string>?` | `null` | Formats value-axis ticks. Defaults to a compact number, such as 1.2K. |
| `Curve` | `ChartCurve` | `Smooth` | Smooth monotone curves that never swing past the data, or straight segments. |
| `HiddenSeries` | `IReadOnlyList<string>?` | `null` | Keys of hidden series. Two-way; the legend toggles it. |
| `IsLoading` | `bool` | `false` | Keeps the current shapes on screen, dimmed and breathing, while the next range loads. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ActiveIndexChanged` | `ChartActiveIndexChangedEventArgs` | Raised as the readout moves between points, and with a null index when it is released. |
| `HiddenSeriesChanged` | `ChartHiddenSeriesChangedEventArgs` | Raised when the legend shows or hides a series. |

Pseudo-classes: `:scrubbing`, `:success`, `:warning`, `:danger`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.


## Accessibility

- `Label` names the chart. The accessible name combines the label, the latest value and the change, such as
  "Revenue: $48.2K. +4.1%". The drawing itself is hidden from assistive technology, so the name and the text are what
  a screen reader reads.
- The headline and the change are plain text, and they are read as they are.
- When the chart is interactive, the plot is a focusable slider named "`Label`, explore by point". Its value text reads
  the point label and the value, such as "Thu: 22", or the position and the value, such as "Point 2 of 3: 1,500",
  when there are no point labels.
- Set `PointLabels` so that a scrubbed point is read with its date, not with its position in the list.
- Arc draws the focus ring for the plot in the focus color. Keyboard focus is visible without the window's default
  adorner.
- A sparkline that is not interactive has no tab stop and does not answer the pointer. Its name and text remain
  available to a screen reader.
- Tone is never the only signal. Put the sign in `Change` (`+4.1%`, `-6 ms`) so the direction survives a color
  vision difference.

### Keyboard

A sparkline takes focus only when `IsInteractive` is `True`. The model is the same as the other Arc charts with a
single series: the arrows step through the points, and Escape leaves the readout.

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` | Move focus to or from the plot |
| `Left` or `Down` | Move to the previous point. From rest, the first press lands on the point before the latest |
| `Right` or `Up` | Move to the next point. From rest, the press stays on the latest point |
| `PageUp` / `PageDown` | Move about a sixth of the points (at least one), forward or back |
| `Home` / `End` | Move to the first or the last point |
| `Escape` | Stop scrubbing and return the caption to `Value` and `Change` |

With a mouse, a press or a move over the plot scrubs to the nearest point. Leaving the plot returns to the latest value.
With touch or pen, the readout stays on the touched point until the contact is released, then returns to the latest
value.

## Motion

- On first view the line draws in once, like a pen, and the end dot appears as the line lands. The draw starts when the
  sparkline is half visible, so a card below the fold draws when the reader scrolls to it.
- While scrubbing, the cursor moves between points on a snappy spring, the stretch after the cursor dims, and the end
  dot grows to show that a point is being read.
- The headline and the aside roll to the new text, and the headline's width eases to fit it.
- New data morphs the line from its current shape into the new one. It does not redraw from the start.
- Reduced motion shows the whole line at once and moves the cursor without a spring. Off jumps to the final state.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| First view | The line draws over about 840 ms and the end dot fades in as it lands, then settles | The whole line appears at once; the end dot appears without a spring | The final state |
| Scrubbing the cursor | The cursor moves on a snappy spring | The cursor moves without a spring | Immediate |
| The stretch after the cursor | Dims on a short standard tween | Dims on the same short tween | Immediate |
| The end dot while scrubbing | Grows to 10 units on a snappy spring | Immediate size change without a spring | Immediate |
| New data | The line morphs to the new shape on a smooth spring | Jumps to the new shape | Immediate |

## Related

- `BarChart` for discrete periods that need an axis, and `LineChart` for a trend with axes, several series or a legend.
- `MetricCard` for a single value with its change and no trend.
- `Gauge` for a value against a known range, and `BrushChart` for a long series people must zoom.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `BarChart` | Each period is a separate value and people compare the periods |
| `LineChart` | The trend needs a value axis, a time axis, several series or a legend |
| `MetricCard` | There is one current value, and its change matters more than its path |
| `Gauge` | The value is read against a fixed range or a threshold, such as a quota |
| `BrushChart` | A long series needs a zoomable window over the full range |
| `Treemap` | The question is how a total splits among parts, not how it moved over time |

---

# Gauge

> Show a value against a known range.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/gauge

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.GaugeThresholdsDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="16">
        <arc:Gauge x:Name="Disk" Value="72" Label="Disk usage" Detail="360 of 500 GB">
            <arc:Gauge.Thresholds>
                <arc:GaugeThreshold From="0" Tone="Success" Label="Healthy" />
                <arc:GaugeThreshold From="60" Tone="Warning" Label="Filling up" />
                <arc:GaugeThreshold From="85" Tone="Danger" Label="Critical" />
            </arc:Gauge.Thresholds>
        </arc:Gauge>
        <WrapPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center" ItemSpacing="12" LineSpacing="12">
            <arc:Button Content="New reading" Variant="Secondary" Click="OnNewReadingClick" />
            <arc:Button Content="Almost full" Variant="Ghost" Click="OnAlmostFullClick" />
        </WrapPanel>
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class GaugeThresholdsDemo : UserControl
{
    private readonly Random _random = new(3);

    public GaugeThresholdsDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
    }

    // Set Value and Detail together so the number and its detail stay in step.
    private void OnNewReadingClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        var used = _random.Next(40, 500);
        Disk.Value = Math.Round(used / 5.0);
        Disk.Detail = $"{used} of 500 GB";
    }

    private void OnAlmostFullClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        Disk.Value = 93;
        Disk.Detail = "465 of 500 GB";
    }
}
```

## When to use

`Gauge` answers one question: where does this reading sit inside a range the reader already knows? It draws a 270
degree ring with the percentage in its center, an optional state name from named bands, and a caption under the ring.
It belongs on an overview tile, next to the number it summarizes, so the reader sees the reading, its state and its
scale in one glance.

- **Disk usage on an admin console**: a workspace owner sees that a database volume holds 72 percent of its 500 GB and
  that the state is Filling up. The detail line "360 of 500 GB" gives the absolute amount, and the ring gives the
  proportion.
- **A health score in a risk or fraud dashboard**: a credit score of 640 on a 300 to 850 scale. `Minimum` and `Maximum`
  map the real range onto the ring, so the reader does not have to convert the score to a percentage.
- **Error budget on a reliability page**: an SRE team sees that 97 percent of the month's error budget is spent. A
  danger tone and a label make the state obvious before the reader studies the number.
- **Quota or capacity tiles on a billing page**: a workspace shows the share of its seats in use. Use it for a single
  reading; a plan with a limit the customer consumes over a period is better served by `UsageMeter`.

## When not to use

- **Progress of a task that is running or finishing**: use `Progress`, which describes steps and completion rather than
  a reading against a scale.
- **A plan or quota with a limit that the user is consuming over a period**: use `UsageMeter`, which shows the amount
  used against the plan and its renewal.
- **A value that changes over time**: use `LineChart` or `Sparkline`. A ring shows one moment, so a trend drawn as a
  series of gauges hides its direction.
- **Parts of a whole rather than one value against a range**: use `DonutChart`, which shows how several parts share one
  total.
- **A single value with its change from the last period and a trend**: use `MetricCard`, which places the change and the
  comparison next to the number.

## Usage

`Value` is the reading. `Minimum` and `Maximum` set the range, which is 0 to 100 by default. `Detail` adds a line
under the reading, such as the amount in absolute units.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:Gauge Label="Disk usage"
               Value="72"
               Detail="360 of 500 GB">
        <arc:Gauge.Thresholds>
            <arc:GaugeThreshold From="0" Tone="Success" Label="Healthy" />
            <arc:GaugeThreshold From="60" Tone="Warning" Label="Filling up" />
            <arc:GaugeThreshold From="85" Tone="Danger" Label="Critical" />
        </arc:Gauge.Thresholds>
    </arc:Gauge>
</UserControl>
```

`Gauge` derives from Avalonia's `Control` and draws itself, so it has no template parts to restyle and no child
controls to place. It is a read-only display: it takes no focus and defines no keys. Its look comes from
its theme, and its sizes follow the container.

### Anatomy

1. **Ring**: a 270 degree track with a value arc on top. The stroke is 9 px in the 100 by 90 view box, so it scales with
   the ring. The ring starts at the lower left and runs clockwise, and its radius sits around the center of the box.
2. **Dial**: the ring's box is at most 176 px wide (`DialMaxWidth`) and 0.9 times as tall as it is wide. A narrower
   container shrinks it; the gauge never grows past 176 px.
3. **Number**: the percentage in the display font at the 3XL type size, with a `%` at half that size. Its
   value is `Percent`, the reading rounded to a whole percent of the range.
4. **State line** (`Thresholds`): the name of the band the value is in, in extra-small medium text in the band's tone,
   inside the ring under the number after a 4 px gap. It is hidden when no thresholds exist. Its box is at least 100 px
   wide so the text does not shift the number.
5. **Label** (`Label`): the caption under the ring, in small medium text, 10 px below the dial (`CaptionGap`). It is also
   the accessible name.
6. **Detail** (`Detail`): extra-small regular text in the muted color, under the label. It is hidden when empty.

The ring colors follow the tone: `Accent` uses the accent color with the strong accent for the state text, and
`Success`, `Warning` and `Danger` use their own tokens. A band's tone replaces the ring's `Tone` while the value is in
that band.

### Choosing thresholds

A threshold starts at `From` and holds until the next band begins. The highest band the value reaches sets the color
and names the state. Bands are sorted by `From` when they change, so the order in the markup does not matter, though
writing them in ascending order keeps the markup readable.

Choose bands that describe what the reader should do, not a decorative scale. Three bands are usually enough: a normal
state, one warning state, and one state that needs action. Use the same `From` values and labels on every tile that
measures the same thing, so a Critical disk on one page means the same as a Critical disk on another. Keep the labels
to one or two words, because the state line sits inside the ring under the number.

```csharp
disk.Thresholds.Add(new GaugeThreshold(0, GaugeTone.Success, "Healthy"));
disk.Thresholds.Add(new GaugeThreshold(60, GaugeTone.Warning, "Filling up"));
disk.Thresholds.Add(new GaugeThreshold(85, GaugeTone.Danger, "Critical"));
```

Bands use the gauge's value units, not percentages of the range. For a score from 300 to 850, a band at `From="670"`
means a score of 670, not 670 percent. Without thresholds the ring uses `Tone` only, and the reader gets no state name, so
add the bands whenever the state matters.

### Binding to a view model

The gauge displays a value; it does not write one back. `Value`, `Minimum`, `Maximum`, `Label` and `Detail` bind one
way, so the view model owns the reading and the gauge reflects every change. With CommunityToolkit.Mvvm:

```csharp
public partial class StorageViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    [ObservableProperty]
    private double _usedGigabytes;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private double _capacityGigabytes = 500;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private double _usedPercent;

    partial void OnUsedGigabytesChanged(double value)
    {
        UsedPercent = Math.Round(value / CapacityGigabytes * 100);
        DetailText = $"{value:0} of {CapacityGigabytes:0} GB";
    }

    [ObservableProperty]
    private string _detailText = string.Empty;
}
```

```xml
<arc:Gauge Label="Disk usage"
           Value="{Binding UsedPercent}"
           Detail="{Binding DetailText}">
    <arc:Gauge.Thresholds>
        <arc:GaugeThreshold From="0" Tone="Success" Label="Healthy" />
        <arc:GaugeThreshold From="60" Tone="Warning" Label="Filling up" />
        <arc:GaugeThreshold From="85" Tone="Danger" Label="Critical" />
    </arc:Gauge.Thresholds>
</arc:Gauge>
```

- Update `Value` and `Detail` together in the view model, so the number and its detail never disagree on screen. The
  page above derives both from one change.
- The bands are a list, not a binding target. Set them once in markup or in code at startup, and change the
  `From` values only when the policy changes.
- A value outside `Minimum` and `Maximum` is clamped on screen. Validate the reading in the data layer, because the
  gauge will show the clamped value without an error.

### Custom range

`Minimum` and `Maximum` map any range onto the ring. The number reads as a percentage of that range, so a score of 575
on a 300 to 850 scale shows 50 percent. Use the real range when the reader thinks in the real unit, and state the
range in the detail line so the number has a reference.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.GaugeCustomRangeDemo">
    <arc:Gauge Label="Health score"
               Value="640"
               Minimum="300"
               Maximum="850"
               Detail="640 of 850" />
</UserControl>
```

### Tone without thresholds

Without thresholds the ring uses `Tone`: `Accent`, `Success`, `Warning` or `Danger`. Use a fixed tone for a reading whose
state is always the same kind, such as an uptime figure that is always good news, and use thresholds when the state
changes with the value.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.GaugeTonesDemo">
    <WrapPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center" ItemSpacing="12" LineSpacing="12">
        <arc:Gauge Label="Build cache" Value="38" />
        <arc:Gauge Label="Uptime" Value="91" Tone="Success" />
        <arc:Gauge Label="Memory" Value="64" Tone="Warning" />
        <arc:Gauge Label="Error budget used" Value="97" Tone="Danger" />
    </WrapPanel>
</UserControl>
```

### Example: storage and health tiles for an admin console

An Acme Analytics workspace owner opens the admin console and sees three readings in one row: disk usage for the
analytics database, the health score of the ingestion pipeline, and the share of the monthly error budget that is spent.
Each tile has a label that names the measure and a detail line with the absolute amount. The first two tiles also name
their state from their own bands. The health score maps its real range from 300 to 850, so the ring shows 62 percent of the range while the detail
line keeps the score itself, 640. The error budget has no
bands: its tone is fixed to danger because it is already past the line that the team agreed to act on.

The example is 720 px wide, so the three tiles sit side by side at the default ring size.

![Three gauges for disk usage, a health score and the error budget, each with a state name](https://docs.tkcode.si/shots/Docs/Charts/Gauge/images/StorageHealth.webp)

```xml
<StackPanel Width="720" Spacing="20">
    <TextBlock Text="Platform health, Acme Analytics"
               FontSize="16"
               FontWeight="Medium"
               Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
    <Grid ColumnDefinitions="*,*,*">
        <arc:Gauge Grid.Column="0"
                   Label="Disk usage"
                   Value="72"
                   Detail="360 of 500 GB">
            <arc:Gauge.Thresholds>
                <arc:GaugeThreshold From="0" Tone="Success" Label="Healthy" />
                <arc:GaugeThreshold From="60" Tone="Warning" Label="Filling up" />
                <arc:GaugeThreshold From="85" Tone="Danger" Label="Critical" />
            </arc:Gauge.Thresholds>
        </arc:Gauge>
        <arc:Gauge Grid.Column="1"
                   Label="Ingestion health"
                   Value="640"
                   Minimum="300"
                   Maximum="850"
                   Detail="640 of 850">
            <arc:Gauge.Thresholds>
                <arc:GaugeThreshold From="300" Tone="Danger" Label="Degraded" />
                <arc:GaugeThreshold From="600" Tone="Warning" Label="Watch" />
                <arc:GaugeThreshold From="720" Tone="Success" Label="Healthy" />
            </arc:Gauge.Thresholds>
        </arc:Gauge>
        <arc:Gauge Grid.Column="2"
                   Label="Error budget used"
                   Value="97"
                   Tone="Danger"
                   Detail="97% of the monthly budget spent" />
    </Grid>
</StackPanel>
```

### Content guidelines

The label names the measure and the detail names the amount. A reader should be able to read the tile without the
surrounding page: "Disk usage" with "360 of 500 GB" says what it is, while "Storage" says nothing about the state.

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| Storage | Disk usage |
| 360/500 | 360 of 500 GB |
| Score: 640 | Health score |
| Almost out of space | Filling up |
| Very bad, act now | Critical |

Band labels are state names of one or two words in sentence case, such as Healthy, Filling up, Watch and Critical. Do not
use exclamation marks or a sentence in a band label, because the label is announced with the number and shares a short
line with it. Put the recommended action in the surrounding page, not in the gauge.

### Best practices

**Do**

- Set `Minimum` and `Maximum` to the real range of the measure, and show the absolute amount in `Detail`, so the reader
  can judge the percentage.
- Name a state with `Thresholds` whenever the state matters to the reader. The state name is read with the number, so a
  color is never the only signal.
- Keep the same bands and labels for the same measure on every page that shows it.
- Update `Value` and `Detail` together, from one source, so the number and its explanation never disagree.
- Place gauges in a row of equal columns, so the readings compare at a glance.

**Avoid**

- A gauge for a value that changes over time or that the reader must watch as a trend. Use `LineChart` or `Sparkline`.
- A gauge as the only display of a number the reader must act on. The gauge is a summary; keep the exact figure in the
  detail or in the page's table.
- Many bands with near-identical labels. A reader cannot tell "Watch" from "Attention" at a glance, so use three or four
  bands at most.
- A custom range on a reading that people think of as a percentage. The ring then shows a number the reader does not
  use.
- Thresholds whose `From` values are in the wrong units, such as percentages on a 300 to 850 scale. The band then never
  matches the reading.

### Common questions

**Why does the state name change a moment after the value?** The ring and the number move on a spring, and the band is
chosen by the number on screen. The state switches when the count crosses the band boundary, so the name and the
number always agree. At reduced or off motion the change is immediate.

**What does the gauge show for a value outside the range?** It clamps the value to `Minimum` and `Maximum` for the ring
and the number. The `Percent` property is clamped too, so a value of 1000 on a 0 to 100 gauge reads 100 percent.

**Can I read the state in code?** Yes. `CurrentThreshold` returns the band for the value, or null when there are no
bands or the value is below the first band. `Percent` gives the whole percentage the ring shows.

**Is the gauge keyboard accessible?** The gauge takes no focus and defines no keys, so it is read as part of the page.
Its value is exposed as a read-only progress bar with a range, and its help text is the percentage with the state, such
as "72%, Filling up".

**Why is there no state when I set `Tone` alone?** `Tone` sets the ring color only. The state line and the state name
come from `Thresholds`, so add at least one band to show a name.

## API reference

### Gauge

A 270° ring gauge (Arc "Gauge"): one value against a known range, read as a percentage with an optional named state from `Thresholds`. The ring fills once when half of it scrolls into view, then springs to every new value while the percentage rolls (Core `RollingDigits`); the state color and label switch exactly when the moving count crosses a band. Reduced and Off motion land on the value at once.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Value` | `double` | `0` | Defines the `Value` property. |
| `Minimum` | `double` | `0` | Defines the `Minimum` property. |
| `Maximum` | `double` | `100` | Defines the `Maximum` property. |
| `Label` | `string?` | `null` | Defines the `Label` property. |
| `Detail` | `string?` | `null` | Defines the `Detail` property. |
| `Tone` | `GaugeTone` | `Accent` | Defines the `Tone` property. |

Derives from `Control`: every member of `Control` works as well.

### GaugeThreshold

A band that starts at `From` (in value units). The highest band the value reaches sets the ring's tone and names the state under the number, so the state never rests on color alone.

### Companion type: GaugeTone

| Member | Ring and state color |
|---|---|
| `Accent` | The accent color; the state text uses the strong accent (the default) |
| `Success` | The success color |
| `Warning` | The warning color |
| `Danger` | The danger color |

## Accessibility

- `Label` names the gauge, and the value is exposed as a read-only range with the minimum and the maximum.
- The help text is the value with the current band label, such as "72%, Filling up", so the state is read with the
  number. Without thresholds it is the percentage alone.
- The gauge is a live region set to polite: a new reading is announced without moving focus.
- States are named in text by the threshold labels. Color is never the only sign of a state.
- The ring and the animated reading are hidden from assistive technology; the screen reader gets the name, the range and
  the help text instead.

### Keyboard

The gauge takes no focus and defines no keys. Read it with the page's normal reading order, or with a screen reader's
review commands.

## Motion

- Once, when the gauge is half in view, the ring fills to its value on a smooth spring without overshoot.
- A new value moves the ring to its new length, and the percentage counts to the new number at the same time.
- When the count crosses a threshold, the color and the band label switch at that moment, following the count.
- Reduced motion puts the ring and the number at the target value at once. Off behaves the same as Reduced.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| First view (half in view) | The ring fills once to its value, smooth spring, no overshoot | The ring and number are at the value at once | The ring and number are at the value at once |
| New `Value` | The ring springs to the new length and the number counts | Changes at once | Changes at once |
| Count crosses a band | The color and the state name switch with the count | Switch at once | Switch at once |
| `Tone` changes | The ring color crossfades | Changes at once | Changes at once |

## Related

- `Progress` for the completion of a task.
- `UsageMeter` for a quota that the user consumes over a period.
- `DonutChart` for parts of a whole rather than one value against a range.
- `MetricCard` for a single value with its change and a trend.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `Progress` | A task is running or finishing and the reader waits for it |
| `UsageMeter` | A plan or quota is consumed over a billing period |
| `DonutChart` | Several parts make up one total |
| `Sparkline` / `LineChart` | The value's movement over time is the point |
| `MetricCard` | One number needs its change and a trend next to it |
