An Excel export writes the groups as outlined rows with SUBTOTAL formulas, so the reader can fold them in Excel too.

### Checked rows and bulk actions

Check rows in the gutter: Shift-click checks a run, and Shift+Space checks the rows under the selection. Once a row is
checked, the toolbar offers Copy, Export, your `BulkActions` and Delete (when `CanDeleteRows` is on). Delete records the
row positions, so Undo puts the rows back in order; the status bar offers the same undo for 6 seconds.

```xml
<arc:DataGrid Label="Accounts">
    <arc:DataGrid.BulkActions>
        <arc:DataGridBulkAction Label="Archive" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Archive}" Command="{Binding ArchiveCommand}" />
        <arc:DataGridBulkAction Label="Remove from plan" IsDanger="True" Command="{Binding RemoveCommand}" />
    </arc:DataGrid.BulkActions>
</arc:DataGrid>
```

The command receives the checked rows as an `IReadOnlyList<object>` in data order. The grid also raises
`BulkActionInvoked` with the action and the rows. Labels hide below 640 px of grid width, so give every action an icon.

### Export

`ExportFormats` lists `Csv`, `Xlsx` or both (`All`); with more than one, Export opens a menu. Export writes every row the
filters keep, in view order, and the bulk Export writes only the checked rows. `Exporting` can rename or cancel the file,
and `ExportAsync` exports from code. Export is disabled where the host cannot show a save dialog.

A CSV opened in Excel or Sheets runs text that starts with `=`, `+`, `-` or `@` as a formula, which lets a hostile cell
read data or start programs (CSV injection). The grid therefore writes such text with a leading single quote (`'=1+1`), and
the quote stays visible in the cell. Numbers and days are never prefixed, and an Excel export always stores text as text.
Set `NeutralizeCsvFormulas="False"` only when the file never reaches a spreadsheet and the text must round-trip byte for
byte.

```csharp
grid.Exporting += (_, e) => e.FileName = $"renewals-{DateTime.Today:yyyy-MM-dd}";
await grid.ExportAsync(DataGridExportFormat.Xlsx);
```

The writers, clipboard helpers and parsers are public static classes (`DataGridCsv`, `DataGridXlsx`,
`DataGridClipboardText`, `DataGridValueParser`, `DataGridFilterExpression`, `DataGridSorting`) that a server can reuse.

### Server data

For data too large to send at once, set `DataSource` to an `IDataGridDataSource`. The grid requests the blocks that cover
the rows in view, shows placeholder rows while they load, and keeps up to 40 blocks. When the sort, filters or search
change, it starts over and cancels the requests in flight. The grid is then read only, does not group, hides Select all
and exports only checked rows. Set `RowKeySelector` as well, which is required with a data source.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.DataGridServerDataDemo">
    <arc:DataGrid x:Name="OrdersGrid"
                  Label="Orders"
                  MaxViewportHeight="420"
                  ExportFormats="Csv">
        <arc:DataGridColumn Key="order" Header="Order" Width="120" />
        <arc:DataGridColumn Key="customer" Header="Customer" Width="170" />
        <arc:DataGridColumn Key="status" Header="Status" Type="Select" Width="130" />
        <arc:DataGridColumn Key="placed" Header="Placed" Type="Date" Width="130" />
        <arc:DataGridColumn Key="amount" Header="Amount" Type="Currency" Decimals="2" Width="130" />
    </arc:DataGrid>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class DataGridServerDataDemo : UserControl
{
    public DataGridServerDataDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        OrdersGrid.Columns[2].Options = OrdersSource.Statuses;
        OrdersGrid.RowKeySelector = row => ((DataGridRow)row).Key;
        OrdersGrid.DataSource = new OrdersSource(100_000);
    }

    /// <summary>
    /// A stand-in for a server: 100,000 orders filtered, sorted and searched off the UI thread with the grid's public
    /// helpers, then returned one block at a time after a short delay.
    /// </summary>
    private sealed class OrdersSource(int count) : IDataGridDataSource
    {
        public static readonly string[] Statuses = ["Pending", "Paid", "Shipped", "Refunded"];
        private static readonly string[] Customers = ["Alder", "Basalt", "Cobalt", "Delta", "Ember", "Fjord", "Garnet", "Harbor"];
        private readonly Dictionary<string, int[]> _queries = new();

        public int BlockSize => 200;

        private static object? Value(int index, string key) => key switch
        {
            "order" => $"SO-{100000 + index}",
            "customer" => $"{Customers[index % Customers.Length]} {index % 97 + 1}",
            "status" => Statuses[index * 7 % Statuses.Length],
            "placed" => new DateOnly(2026, 1, 1).AddDays(index % 300),
            "amount" => Math.Round(20m + index * 37 % 5000 + index % 100 / 100m, 2),
            _ => null
        };

        public async Task<DataGridRowsResult> GetRowsAsync(DataGridRowsRequest request, CancellationToken cancellation)
        {
            await Task.Delay(350, cancellation);
            var order = await Task.Run(() => Query(request), cancellation);
            var rows = new List<object>();
            for (var i = request.Start; i < Math.Min(request.End, order.Length); i++)
            {
                var index = order[i];
                var row = new DataGridRow($"o{index}");
                foreach (var key in new[] { "order", "customer", "status", "placed", "amount" })
                {
                    row[key] = Value(index, key);
                }
                rows.Add(row);
            }
            var total = DataGridAggregates.Compute(order.Select(i => Value(i, "amount")), DataGridAggregate.Sum);
            return new DataGridRowsResult(rows, order.Length, new Dictionary<string, decimal?> { ["amount"] = total });
        }

        private int[] Query(DataGridRowsRequest request)
        {
            var key = string.Join("|", request.Sort.Select(s => $"{s.Key}{s.Direction}")) + "#" +
                      string.Join("|", request.Filters.Select(f => $"{f.Key}={f.Value}")) + "#" + request.Search;
            lock (_queries)
            {
                if (_queries.TryGetValue(key, out var cached))
                {
                    return cached;
                }
            }
            var culture = System.Globalization.CultureInfo.InvariantCulture;
            IEnumerable<int> rows = Enumerable.Range(0, count);
            foreach (var (column, filter) in request.Filters)
            {
                if (filter.Values is { } keep)
                {
                    rows = rows.Where(i => keep.Contains(Value(i, column) as string ?? string.Empty));
                }
                else if (column == "amount" && DataGridFilterExpression.TryParseNumber(filter.Expression, culture, out var number) && number is not null)
                {
                    rows = rows.Where(i => Value(i, column) is decimal d && number(d));
                }
                else if (column == "placed" && DataGridFilterExpression.TryParseDate(filter.Expression, culture, out var date) && date is not null)
                {
                    rows = rows.Where(i => Value(i, column) is DateOnly d && date(d));
                }
                else if (DataGridFilterExpression.CreateText(filter.Expression, culture) is { } text)
                {
                    rows = rows.Where(i => text(Value(i, column)?.ToString() ?? string.Empty));
                }
            }
            if (request.Search.Length > 0)
            {
                rows = rows.Where(i => $"{Value(i, "order")} {Value(i, "customer")} {Value(i, "status")}"
                    .Contains(request.Search, StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase));
            }
            var result = DataGridSorting.Sort(rows, request.Sort, Value, culture: culture).ToArray();
            lock (_queries)
            {
                _queries[key] = result;
            }
            return result;
        }
    }
}
```

### Binding to a view model

In an MVVM app the view model owns the rows, the view state and the commands. With CommunityToolkit.Mvvm, the rows are an
`ObservableCollection<DataGridRow>`, and the view state is observable properties that the grid writes back into.

```csharp
public partial class RenewalsViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    private readonly IRenewalService _renewals;

    public RenewalsViewModel(IRenewalService renewals)
    {
        _renewals = renewals;
    }

    public ObservableCollection<DataGridRow> Renewals { get; } = new();

    [ObservableProperty]
    private IReadOnlyList<DataGridSort> _sortDescriptions = [];

    [ObservableProperty]
    private IReadOnlyDictionary<string, DataGridFilter> _filters = new Dictionary<string, DataGridFilter>();

    [ObservableProperty]
    private IReadOnlyList<object> _checkedRowKeys = [];

    [ObservableProperty]
    private DataGridDensity _density = DataGridDensity.Standard;

    [RelayCommand]
    private async Task ArchiveAsync(IReadOnlyList<object> rows)
    {
        await _renewals.ArchiveAsync(rows.Cast<DataGridRow>().Select(r => r.Key));
    }
}
```

```xml
<arc:DataGrid Label="Renewals"
              ItemsSource="{Binding Renewals}"
              SortDescriptions="{Binding SortDescriptions}"
              Filters="{Binding Filters}"
              CheckedRowKeys="{Binding CheckedRowKeys}"
              Density="{Binding Density}">
    <arc:DataGrid.BulkActions>
        <arc:DataGridBulkAction Label="Archive" Command="{Binding ArchiveCommand}" />
    </arc:DataGrid.BulkActions>
</arc:DataGrid>
```

- `SortDescriptions`, `Filters`, `CheckedRowKeys`, `Density`, `SearchText` and `GroupBy` are two-way: header clicks update
  the view model, and changes in the view model update the grid.
- `ItemsSource` is one-way. Edits write into the row objects, and the grid raises `CellsChanged` for each write. Save
  changes in a `CellsChanged` handler in code-behind, since it is an event and not a command.

### Data shape and performance

Every row needs a stable key (`DataGridRow.Key`, or a `RowKeySelector` for typed rows) that never changes, since the
key identifies checked rows and scroll targets. The design targets about 10,000 rows in client mode as smooth and about
50,000 as usable; above that, use `DataSource`. Store numbers as `decimal` and days as `DateOnly`, and set `Culture` for
figures that belong to a fixed locale.

### Example: renewal review for a customer success team

A customer success manager reviews the next two quarters of renewals. The pinned account column keeps the name in view.
Stage is a `Select` with an ordered option list, so the sort follows the pipeline. ARR and region are read only because the
billing export owns them; an edit here would be overwritten at the next import. The `Min` health total shows the weakest
account in view, and `CanDeleteRows="False"` keeps accounts until billing closes them.

```xml
<arc:DataGrid Label="Renewals Q4 2026"
              MaxViewportHeight="440"
              ExportFormats="All"
              ExportFileName="renewals-q4-2026"
              CanDeleteRows="False">
    <arc:DataGridColumn Key="account" Header="Account" Width="188" MinWidth="120" IsPinned="True" IsEditable="False" />
    <arc:DataGridColumn Key="owner" Header="Owner" Width="148" />
    <arc:DataGridColumn Key="region" Header="Region" Type="Select" Width="144" IsEditable="False" />
    <arc:DataGridColumn Key="stage" Header="Stage" Type="Select" Width="140" Options="{Binding StageOptions}" />
    <arc:DataGridColumn Key="seats" Header="Seats" Type="Number" Width="96" Aggregate="Sum" />
    <arc:DataGridColumn Key="arr" Header="ARR" Type="Currency" CurrencySymbol="$" Width="128" IsEditable="False" />
    <arc:DataGridColumn Key="health" Header="Health" Type="Percent" Width="104" Aggregate="Min" />
    <arc:DataGridColumn Key="renewal" Header="Renews" Type="Date" DateFormat="yyyy-MM-dd" Width="132" />
</arc:DataGrid>
```

### Content guidelines

- **Header**: a short noun phrase in sentence case, such as "Renews" or "ARR". Add the unit when the cells do not show it
  ("ARR (USD)"). The header is the column's accessible name and the export column title.
- **Label**: name the table for the person who opens it. It is the accessible name and the default export file name.
- **Bulk action**: a verb such as "Archive". Use `IsDanger` for destructive actions, and "Remove from plan" when the record
  stays in another system.

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| Amt | ARR (USD) |
| Save file | Export as Excel |
| Error | ARR cannot be negative |
| Delete all now | Archive checked accounts |

### Best practices

**Do**

- Store raw values (decimals, `DateOnly`, option strings) and let the column format them, so sorting, totals and export
  match what the person sees.
- Key every row with a unique, stable value. A sort or a deletion moves rows, and only a stable key keeps the checks on
  the right rows.
- Pin the column that identifies the row, usually the name, so it stays visible when the grid scrolls sideways.
- Mark imported or computed columns `IsEditable="False"` rather than relying on people to leave them alone.
- Validate in `CellEditEnding` with a specific message. A refused edit keeps the editor open, so the person can fix it
  where they are.

**Avoid**

- `DataSource` for a few hundred rows. It makes the grid read only and disables grouping, which the client mode supports
  at that size.
- Formatting numbers into strings before they reach the grid. A string sorts as text and the totals ignore it.
- Several editable grids with bulk actions on one screen. Each has its own checked set, and people lose track of which
  one a bulk action affects.

### Common questions

**Why does a row stay in place after I change a value that is sorted?** Editing never re-sorts or re-filters, so the row
keeps its position until the sort or the filters change. Click the header again, or change the filter, to reorder.

**How do I undo a bulk delete from code?** Call `Undo()`, which restores the last edit, fill, paste, clear or row delete.
`CanUndo` says whether a step exists, and `ClearHistory()` forgets all steps, for example after a successful save.
`UndoLimit` sets how many steps are kept.

## API reference

### DataGrid

A spreadsheet grid for editing tabular data in place: range selection, a fill handle, Excel and Google Sheets clipboard, undo, multi-column sort, a filter row and quick search, pinned and hidden columns, row checks with bulk actions, a totals row, grouping with subtotals, CSV and Excel export, and rows and columns that render only while in view. Every piece of view state (sort, filters, search, checked rows, hidden and pinned columns, density, grouping) is a two-way property, so it works bound or left to the grid. Rows come from `ItemsSource` (`DataGridRow` objects or any class read through column bindings or accessors), or block by block from a `DataSource`. Edits write back into the row items and raise `CellsChanged`; editing never re-sorts or re-filters, so rows never jump under the cursor.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ItemsSource` | `IEnumerable?` | `null` | Row items: `DataGridRow` objects or any objects the columns can read. `INotifyCollectionChanged` sources are followed. |
| `RowKeySelector` | `Func<object, object>?` | `null` | Stable row identity; defaults to `Key`, else the item itself. Required with `DataSource`. |
| `Label` | `string` | `""` | Accessible name of the grid; also names exported files and the xlsx worksheet. |
| `MaxViewportHeight` | `double` | `400` | Tallest the scrolling area grows before it scrolls, in px (default 400); infinity fills the available height. |
| `SortDescriptions` | `IReadOnlyList<DataGridSort>` | – | Sort keys in priority order (two-way). Header clicks, Shift-clicks and the column menu change it. |
| `Filters` | `IReadOnlyDictionary<string, DataGridFilter>` | `System.Collections.Generic.Dictionary`2[System.String,TKCode.Arc.DataGridFilter]` | Column filters by column key (two-way). The filter row opens when any filter is set at start. |
| `SearchText` | `string` | `""` | Quick search text (two-way): every word must appear in some visible column. |
| `CheckedRowKeys` | `IReadOnlyList<object>` | – | Keys of the checked rows, in data order (two-way). |
| `HiddenColumns` | `IReadOnlyList<string>?` | `null` | Keys of the hidden columns (two-way); null uses each column's `IsHidden`. |
| `PinnedColumns` | `IReadOnlyList<string>?` | `null` | Keys of the pinned columns (two-way); null uses `IsPinned`, or the first column when no column sets it. |
| `Density` | `DataGridDensity` | `Standard` | Row density (two-way): Compact 32px, Standard 40px or Comfortable 48px rows. |
| `GroupBy` | `IReadOnlyList<string>` | – | Group-by column keys, outermost first (two-way). Group rows show a toggle, the value, a count and subtotals. |
| `IsFilterRowOpen` | `bool` | `false` | Whether the filter row is open (two-way). |
| `IsRowCheckEnabled` | `bool` | `true` | Shows the row gutter with row numbers and checkboxes for checking rows. |
| `ShowRowNumbers` | `bool` | `true` | Shows the row number in the gutter. When false the gutter narrows to 40px and its checkboxes always show. |
| `ShowSelectionStats` | `bool` | `true` | Shows the selection address and the Sum, Average and Count of the selected cells in the status bar. |
| `ShowToolbar` | `bool` | `true` | Shows the toolbar with search, undo and redo, filters, columns, density and export. |
| `ShowTotals` | `bool` | `true` | Shows the sticky totals row; it covers every row the filters keep, collapsed groups included. |
| `ExportFormats` | `DataGridExportFormats` | `Csv` | Formats Export offers; with more than one, Export opens a menu. |
| `ExportFileName` | `string?` | `null` | Export file name without the extension; null derives one from `Label`. |
| `NeutralizeCsvFormulas` | `bool` | `true` | Prefixes exported CSV text that a spreadsheet would run as a formula (it starts with =, +, -, @, a tab or a carriage return) with a single quote, which blocks CSV injection (default true). Numbers and days are not touched. |
| `MaxPasteCells` | `int` | `1000000` | Most cells a paste may hold (default 1,000,000). A bigger clipboard is refused with a message instead of being read, so a huge or hostile table cannot exhaust memory. |
| `CanDeleteRows` | `bool` | `true` | Shows Delete for checked rows; deleting can be undone. |
| `DataSource` | `IDataGridDataSource?` | `null` | Loads rows from a server one block at a time as people scroll, instead of `ItemsSource`. The grid is then read only, does not group, hides Select all and exports only checked rows. |
| `IsLoading` | `bool` | `false` | Shows six placeholder rows while data loads. |
| `EmptyMessage` | `string?` | `null` | Shown when there are no rows at all; null uses the built-in "No rows yet". |
| `Culture` | `CultureInfo?` | `null` | Culture for formatting and parsing values; null follows the Arc language. |
| `UndoLimit` | `int` | `100` | Steps kept for undo (default 100; 0 turns undo off). |
| `CanUndo` | `bool` | – | *Read-only.* Whether there is a step to undo. |
| `CanRedo` | `bool` | – | *Read-only.* Whether there is a step to redo. |
| `ActiveCell` | `DataGridCellAddress?` | – | *Read-only.* The active cell (display row and visible column), or null when the grid has no cells. |
| `SelectedRange` | `DataGridCellRange?` | – | *Read-only.* The selected range, or null when the grid has no cells. |
| `VisibleRowCount` | `int` | – | *Read-only.* Number of rows the filters keep (the data source's row count with a `DataSource`). |
| `IsEditing` | `bool` | – | *Read-only.* Whether a cell editor is open. |
| `IsFindOpen` | `bool` | `false` | Shows the find bar (Ctrl+F; Ctrl+H adds the replace row). Not available with a `DataSource`, where Ctrl+F focuses the toolbar search. |
| `FindText` | `string` | `""` | The text the find bar looks for in the cells' display text; matching cells are tinted while the bar is open. |
| `FindMatchCase` | `bool` | `false` | Matches only the same letter case (default false). |
| `FindMatchWholeCell` | `bool` | `false` | Matches only cells whose whole text equals `FindText` (default false). |
| `ShowContextMenu` | `bool` | `true` | Shows the built-in right-click menu (also Shift+F10 and the menu key, and a long press on touch). Default true. |
| `ColumnOrder` | `IReadOnlyList<string>?` | `null` | Column keys in display order (people drag headers, or press Alt+Shift+arrows in one, to change it). Columns not listed follow in their defined order; null keeps the defined order. Pinned columns still come first. Two-way. |
| `ColumnWidths` | `IReadOnlyDictionary<string, double>?` | `null` | The widths people set by dragging, double clicking or pressing Alt+arrows on a header, by column key. Two-way. |
| `RowFactory` | `Func<object>?` | `null` | Creates the object for a new row, for typed rows: `() => new Account()`. Rows of `DataGridRow` need no factory. Give typed rows a key that `RowKeySelector` reads and that no other row has. |
| `CanInsertRows` | `bool` | `false` | Shows Add row in the toolbar and allows `AddRow` and `InsertRow` (Ctrl+Shift+Plus inserts above the active row). Needs an `ItemsSource` that is a writable list, and either `DataGridRow` rows or a `RowFactory`. Added rows can be undone. Default false. |
| `PasteOverflow` | `DataGridPasteOverflow` | `Truncate` | What a paste does with clipboard rows that run past the last row: drop them (default) or add rows for them. |
| `ValidationMode` | `DataGridValidationMode` | `Block` | What happens to a value that fails its column's rules: refused (default) or accepted and flagged. |
| `CanEditCell` | `Func<DataGridCellContext, bool>?` | `null` | Decides per cell whether it can be edited, on top of `IsEditable` (for example locking the rows of closed deals). Edits, pastes, fills and clears skip cells it refuses. Keep it cheap: it runs for every cell a write touches. |
| `CellStyleSelector` | `Func<DataGridCellContext, DataGridCellStyle?>?` | `null` | Picks a tone for a cell from its row and value, for looks the column's `FormatRules` cannot express. It runs for every cell in view on every frame, so keep it cheap; null from it falls through to the format rules. |
| `RowStyleSelector` | `Func<object, DataGridTone?>?` | `null` | Tints a whole row with a tone chosen from the row object (null for no tint). Runs for every row in view on every frame. |
| `ErrorCount` | `int` | – | *Read-only.* How many cells are flagged for failing their rules (see `Flag` and `ValidateAll`). |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `CellEditEnding` | `DataGridCellEditEndingEventArgs` | Raised before an edit is written; cancel it to keep the editor open with an error. |
| `CellsChanged` | `DataGridCellsChangedEventArgs` | Raised after an edit, paste, cut, clear, fill, fill down, undo or redo wrote cells. |
| `RowsDeleted` | `DataGridRowsEventArgs` | Raised after checked rows were deleted (removed from the source when it is a writable list). |
| `RowsRestored` | `DataGridRowsEventArgs` | Raised after a delete was undone (rows put back into a writable source at their old indices). |
| `BulkActionInvoked` | `DataGridBulkActionEventArgs` | Raised when a bulk action is clicked (its command runs too). |
| `CellInvoked` | `DataGridCellInvokedEventArgs` | Raised when a cell renderer reports a click on something actionable, such as a link. |
| `Exporting` | `DataGridExportingEventArgs` | Raised before the save dialog of an export opens. |
| `CellClick` | `DataGridCellEventArgs` | Raised when a body cell is pressed with the primary button, after the selection moved (or when a renderer took the press). |
| `CellDoubleClick` | `DataGridCellEventArgs` | Raised on a double click or double tap of a body cell, before the editor opens; set `Handled` to keep the editor from opening. |
| `CellContextRequested` | `DataGridCellEventArgs` | Raised when a context menu is asked for on a body cell; set `Handled` to show your own menu instead of the built-in one. |
| `RowActivated` | `DataGridCellEventArgs` | Raised when Enter is pressed on a cell that cannot be edited, and on a double click of the row number: "open this row". |
| `ContextMenuOpening` | `DataGridContextMenuOpeningEventArgs` | Raised before the built-in menu opens, so the entries can be changed or the menu cancelled. |
| `RowsInserted` | `DataGridRowsEventArgs` | Raised after rows are added, and after a redo puts them back (undoing an addition raises `RowsDeleted`). |

Pseudo-classes: `:density-compact`, `:density-comfortable`, `:filtering`, `:checked-rows`, `:editing`, `:grouped`, `:scrolled-x`, `:loading`, `:empty`, `:read-only`, `:toolbar-compact`, `:toolbar-minimal`, `:status-wrap`, `:fill`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

### DataGridColumn

One column of a `DataGrid`. The cell value comes from `ValueGetter`, else from `Binding` (a compiled binding against the row item, written back two-way), else from the `DataGridRow` field (or dictionary entry) named by `Key`. Values are normalized to a string, a `Decimal`, a `DateOnly` or null by `Type`.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Key` | `string` | `""` | Row field the column reads and writes; also the id used by sorting, filters, pinning and hiding. |
| `Header` | `string` | `""` | Header text; also used for copied header rows, exports and accessible names. |
| `Width` | `double` | `140` | Starting width in px (default 140). The last column absorbs spare width on a wide grid. |
| `MinWidth` | `double` | `72` | Narrowest a resize can reach (default 72). Resizing stops at 560px. |
| `Type` | `DataGridColumnType` | `Text` | Kind of data: Text, Number, Currency, Percent, Select or Date. |
| `Decimals` | `int` | `0` | Decimal places of Number, Currency and Percent values. |
| `CurrencySymbol` | `string` | `"$"` | Symbol of a Currency column (default "$"); it does not change with the interface language. |
| `DateFormat` | `string?` | `null` | .NET format of a Date column (such as "yyyy-MM-dd"); null uses the language's short date with the month name. |
| `IsEditable` | `bool` | `true` | False makes the column read only: edits, pastes, fills and clears skip it. |
| `Options` | `IList<string>?` | `null` | Choices of a Select column, in sort order; null uses up to 200 distinct values already in the column. |
| `IsPinned` | `bool?` | `null` | Starts pinned to the left edge. When no column sets it, the first column is pinned. |
| `IsHidden` | `bool` | `false` | Starts hidden; people can show it again from the Columns menu. |
| `Aggregate` | `DataGridAggregate?` | `null` | What the totals row and group subtotals show; null sums numbers and currency, averages percent and shows nothing otherwise. |
| `IsSortable` | `bool` | `true` | False disables the header sort button and the sort items of the column menu. |
| `IsFilterable` | `bool` | `true` | False leaves the filter cell empty and drops Filter from the column menu. |
| `IsGroupable` | `bool?` | `null` | Offers Group by in the column menu; null allows it for Text, Select and Date columns. |
| `Renderer` | `DataGridCellRenderer?` | `null` | Draws the column's cells in place of the plain text: a status badge, a progress bar, a link, an icon, or your own `DataGridCellRenderer`. Null draws the formatted value. Sorting, filtering, totals and export still use the value. |
| `EditTemplate` | `IDataTemplate?` | `null` | Replaces the text box that edits the column's cells with your own content (a slider, a rating, a picker). The template gets a `DataGridEditContext` as its data context; only the cell being edited is a real control. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### DataGridBulkAction

An extra toolbar action for checked rows, shown between Export and Delete.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Label` | `string` | `""` | Button text; also the accessible name. The label hides below 640px of grid width. |
| `Icon` | `Geometry?` | `null` | A 24x24 Lucide geometry shown before the label (such as `ArcIcons.Archive`). |
| `IsDanger` | `bool` | `false` | Draws the button in the danger color. |
| `Command` | `ICommand?` | `null` | Runs with the checked rows (an `IReadOnlyList<object>` in data order) as its parameter. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### DataGridCellRenderer

Draws the cells of a `DataGridColumn` in place of the plain text: a status badge, a progress bar, a link, an icon. The grid keeps drawing rows itself, so a renderer is a few draw calls over the cell, never a control. Sorting, filtering, totals, copy and export keep working on the column's value; `GetText` decides the text that copy and screen readers see.

### BadgeRenderer

Shows the cell as a small pill colored by its value, such as a stage or a status. Map values to tones with `Tones` (or `ToneMap` in XAML); values without a mapping use `DefaultTone`.

### ProgressRenderer

Shows a number as a horizontal bar with its text at the right edge. The value is read against `Minimum` and `Maximum` (0 to 100 by default, which suits a percent column).

### LinkRenderer

Shows the cell as an accent-colored link with an underline that strengthens on hover. A click on the text raises `CellInvoked` with `Part`; the cell is not selected by that click.

### IconTextRenderer

Shows an icon chosen by the cell's value, with the text after it. Icons are 24 x 24 stroked geometries (`ArcIcons`) drawn at 16 px; `Tones` can color them by value.

### CheckboxRenderer

Draws a yes or no value as a checkbox in the middle of the cell; a click on it flips the value (one undo step, and `CellEditEnding` can refuse it). Boolean columns use it without setting `Renderer`; set it on a column of another type to show a 0 or 1 that way. Values that are not a `Boolean` draw as text.

### DataGridCellAction

One icon button of an `ActionsRenderer`.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Label` | `string` | `""` | Names the action in `Part` and for screen readers. |
| `Icon` | `Geometry?` | `null` | A 24 x 24 stroked geometry drawn at 16 px (such as `ArcIcons.Trash2`). |
| `IsDanger` | `bool` | `false` | Draws the icon in the danger color. |
| `Command` | `ICommand?` | `null` | Runs with the row object as its parameter; the button is disabled while `CanExecute` is false. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### ActionsRenderer

Draws a row of icon buttons in the cell, such as Edit and Delete at the end of a row. A click runs the action's `Command` with the row object and raises `CellInvoked` with the action's label as the part; the cell is not selected by that click.

### DataGridEditContext

What a `EditTemplate` edits: the value of one cell. The template's content gets this object as its `DataContext`; bind your controls to `Value` and call `Commit` or `Cancel` (Enter, Tab and Escape do the same when the focused control leaves them alone).

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `PropertyChanged` | `PropertyChangedEventHandler?` | Raised when `Value` or `ErrorMessage` changes. |

### RequiredRule

Fails an empty value (null, empty text).

### RangeRule

Fails a number outside `Minimum` and `Maximum`; empty values and other types pass.

### MaxLengthRule

Fails text longer than `Length` characters.

### PatternRule

Fails text that does not match a regular expression; empty values pass (add `RequiredRule` to refuse them).

### DataGridRule

A check on the values of a column. Add rules to `Rules`; they run when a value is typed, pasted, filled or set by a renderer, and `ValidateAll` runs them over every row. The first rule that returns a message decides.

### DataGridFormatRule

Tints the cells of a column whose value passes a test, such as an ARR below 10,000 or a stage that reads "Lost". Add rules to `FormatRules`; the first rule that matches decides. Compared values are read the way the column reads typed text, so `Value` for a date column is a day such as 2026-03-01.

### DataGridCellContext

One cell as the grid hands it to a validation rule, an editability predicate or a style selector.

Derives from `ValueType`: every member of `ValueType` works as well.

### DataGridMenuItem

An entry you add to the grid's context menu through `ContextMenuItems`.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Label` | `string` | `""` | The entry's text. |
| `Icon` | `Geometry?` | `null` | A 24 x 24 stroked geometry shown before the label. |
| `Command` | `ICommand?` | `null` | Runs with the row object of the clicked cell as its parameter. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### DataGridCellEventArgs

Arguments of the cell events of a `DataGrid`: `CellClick`, `CellDoubleClick`, `CellContextRequested` and `RowActivated`.

Derives from `RoutedEventArgs`: every member of `RoutedEventArgs` works as well.

### DataGridContextMenuOpeningEventArgs

Arguments of `ContextMenuOpening`: change `Items` or set `Cancel` to stop the menu.

Derives from `RoutedEventArgs`: every member of `RoutedEventArgs` works as well.

### DataGridLayoutState

The view of a `DataGrid` that people shape: column order, widths, pinned and hidden columns, sort, filters, grouping and density. `GetLayoutState` reads it and `SetLayoutState` applies it, so a view can be saved when a window closes and restored when it opens. `ToJson` and `FromJson` use a source-generated serializer (trim and AOT safe); unknown fields are ignored and missing fields fall back to the defaults.

### DataGridFilterState

A column filter as stored in a `DataGridLayoutState`: an expression or the values a select column keeps.

### DataGridCellRenderContext

Everything a `DataGridCellRenderer` needs to draw one cell.

Derives from `ValueType`: every member of `ValueType` works as well.

### DataGridCellPointerContext

A pointer press over a cell, for `OnPointerPressed`.

Derives from `ValueType`: every member of `ValueType` works as well.

### DataGridRenderPalette

The colors and pens a `DataGridCellRenderer` draws with. They are resolved from the ArcDesign tokens and follow the theme and the accent, so a renderer never holds a color of its own.

### DataGridCellInvokedEventArgs

Arguments of `CellInvoked`.

Derives from `RoutedEventArgs`: every member of `RoutedEventArgs` works as well.

Server data comes from an `IDataGridDataSource`. The grid calls `GetRowsAsync` for each block it needs.

| Member | Description |
|---|---|
| `int BlockSize` | Rows per request. The default is 100. |
| `Task<DataGridRowsResult> GetRowsAsync(DataGridRowsRequest request, CancellationToken cancellation)` | Returns one block of the sorted, filtered and searched rows. |

`DataGridRowsRequest` carries `Start` (inclusive), `End` (exclusive), `Sort`, `Filters` and `Search`. The result carries
`Rows`, `RowCount` (the whole filtered set) and `Totals` (by column key, or null to keep the previous totals).

## Accessibility

- The grid body is one focusable element. Arrow keys, Shift with arrows, Home, End, PageUp and PageDown move and extend
  the selection; Tab leaves the grid.
- The body's accessible name follows the active cell ("column, row: value"), and its help text gives the address, so
  screen readers announce each move. Avalonia has no grid automation pattern, so rows and cells are not separate nodes.
- Edits, sorts, checks, copies, pastes, fills, undo and redo are announced in a polite live region.
- Header sort buttons name the direction and the priority; the select-all box is a three-state checkbox.
- Typing starts editing with the typed text. For an input method such as Chinese or Japanese, press Enter, F2 or
  double click first, then compose in the editor.
- Narrator, NVDA and VoiceOver are untested with this control; verify the announcements on each platform.

### Keyboard

The grid body is the focus stop. These keys apply when no editor is open; Ctrl means Cmd on macOS.

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| Arrow keys | Move the active cell and collapse the selection to it |
| `Shift` + arrow keys | Extend the selection from the anchor cell |
| `Ctrl` + arrow keys | Jump to the first or last row or column in that direction; add Shift to extend |
| `Home` / `End` | First or last column of the row; `Ctrl+Home` and `Ctrl+End` go to the first and last cell |
| `Ctrl+Space` | Extend the selection to the whole column |
| `Shift+Space` | Check the rows under the selection, or uncheck them when all are checked |
| `Enter` / `F2` | Edit the active cell and keep its value |
| Printable character | Start editing and replace the value with the typed text |
| `Alt+Down` | On a `Select` or `Date` column, open the option list or the calendar |
| `Alt+Left` / `Alt+Right` | In a grouped grid, fold or unfold the group of the active row |
| `F8` | Select the next cell flagged by validation |
| `Ctrl+Shift+Plus` | Insert a row above the active row (with `CanInsertRows`) |
| `Shift+F10` / menu key | Open the context menu on the active cell |
| `Escape` | Collapse a multi-cell selection to the active cell; otherwise clear the row checks |
| `Delete` / `Backspace` | Clear the selection; read-only cells are skipped |
| `Ctrl+D` | Fill down from the first row of the selection |
| `Ctrl+F` / `Ctrl+H` | Open find, or find and replace |
| `F3` / `Shift+F3` | Next or previous match |
| `Ctrl+C` / `Ctrl+X` / `Ctrl+V` | Copy, cut and paste |
| `Ctrl+Z` / `Ctrl+Shift+Z` or `Ctrl+Y` | Undo and redo |
| `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` | Leave the grid |

While an editor is open, Enter and Shift+Enter commit and move down or up, Tab and Shift+Tab commit and move right or
left, and Escape cancels. On a header, Alt+Left and Alt+Right narrow and widen the column by 16 px, and Alt+Shift+Left and Alt+Shift+Right move it.

## Motion

- After a sort, rows slide to their new places within 700 ms, and rows that arrive from outside the view fade in.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| Selection and active cell | Spring between ranges | Jump to the new range | Jump to the new range |
| Rows after a sort | Slide to the new place within 700 ms | Jump to the new place | Jump to the new place |
| Pasted, filled, undone or redone cells | 0.9 s wash that fades out | Short fade | Immediate |
| Toolbar bulk state and status messages | Blur and vertical swap | Fade only | Immediate |
| Totals, selection statistics and checked count | Digits roll | Digits roll by the counter rules | Immediate |
| Filter row and group chevrons | Spring open, chevron turns | Height jumps, opacity fades | Immediate |

## Related

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `Table` | The records are read-only, and people sort, select and page through them |
| `Input` / `Select` / `DatePicker` | People edit one record at a time, with validation per field |
| `Card` / `ReorderableList` | Each item has its own content, images or actions |
| `TreeView` | The data is hierarchical and people expand branches |
| `BarChart` / `MetricCard` | The point is a figure or a trend, not the individual rows |

---

# Workflow canvas

> Show a workflow on a dotted canvas and play its runs: each step lights up in turn, the data draws along the edges, and every step reports its result and time.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc.Workflow`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc.Workflow --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/workflow-canvas

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.WorkflowCanvasPreviewDemo">
    <!-- A sample automation that runs sample orders on its own; Send test event runs the next one at once.
         Like Arc's hero, it only fits: no panning or zooming, so the page scrolls over it. -->
    <StackPanel MaxWidth="640" Spacing="16">
        <Grid ColumnDefinitions="*,Auto">
            <StackPanel Orientation="Horizontal" Spacing="8" VerticalAlignment="Center">
                <Ellipse x:Name="Live" Width="7" Height="7" Fill="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Success}" />
                <TextBlock Text="on-order-placed.ts"
                           FontFamily="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource MonoFontFamily}"
                           FontSize="13"
                           Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
            </StackPanel>
            <arc:Button x:Name="SendButton" Grid.Column="1" Content="Send test event" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" />
        </Grid>
        <arc:WorkflowCanvas x:Name="Canvas"
                            IsPanZoomEnabled="False"
                            CornerRadius="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource RadiusPanel}"
                            BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource BorderSubtle}"
                            BorderThickness="1" />
        <Grid ColumnDefinitions="*,Auto">
            <StackPanel Orientation="Horizontal" Spacing="12" VerticalAlignment="Center">
                <Border BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource BorderSubtle}" BorderThickness="1" CornerRadius="6"
                        Padding="7,1" Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Surface}">
                    <TextBlock Text="order.placed"
                               FontFamily="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource MonoFontFamily}"
                               FontSize="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TypeXS}"
                               Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
                </Border>
                <TextBlock x:Name="RunCount" FontSize="13" Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
            </StackPanel>
            <TextBlock x:Name="Summary" Grid.Column="1" FontSize="13" VerticalAlignment="Center"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
        </Grid>
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;
using Avalonia.Threading;
using TKCode.Arc.Motion;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

/// <summary>
/// The demo is the automation: sample orders arrive on their own, and each one runs the workflow step by step. The demo
/// only sets each step's state when it would really change; the canvas draws the data along the edges in between.
/// </summary>
public partial class WorkflowCanvasPreviewDemo : UserControl
{
    private sealed record Order(string Customer, string Amount, string Plan, bool Routed, string Task,
        int Lookup, int Branch, int Notify, int Create, int Save, int Total);

    private static readonly Order[] s_orders =
    [
        new("Brightline Labs", "$4,800", "Enterprise, 212 seats", true, "TASK-482", 118, 2, 164, 231, 58, 412),
        new("Fernwood", "$240", "Team, 9 seats", false, "", 96, 1, 0, 0, 61, 171),
        new("Kestrel Health", "$12,600", "Enterprise, 540 seats", true, "TASK-483", 131, 2, 149, 244, 66, 436)
    ];

    private readonly WorkflowGraph _graph = new();
    private readonly WorkflowNode _trigger;
    private readonly WorkflowNode _lookup;
    private readonly WorkflowNode _branch;
    private readonly WorkflowNode _notify;
    private readonly WorkflowNode _task;
    private readonly WorkflowNode _save;
    private IDisposable? _step;
    private int _index = -1;
    private int _runs = 2417;

    public WorkflowCanvasPreviewDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        _trigger = Add(new WorkflowNode("trigger", "Order placed") { Icon = ArcIcons.Zap });
        _lookup = Add(new WorkflowNode("lookup", "Find customer account") { Description = "Plan, seats and owner", Icon = ArcIcons.Search });
        _branch = Add(new WorkflowNode("branch", "Amount over $1,000") { Description = "Condition", Icon = ArcIcons.GitBranch });
        _notify = Add(new WorkflowNode("notify", "Post to #revenue") { Description = "Team chat", Icon = ArcIcons.MessageSquare, Appearance = WorkflowNodeAppearance.Compact });
        _task = Add(new WorkflowNode("task", "Create onboarding task") { Description = "Onboarding team", Icon = ArcIcons.ListChecks, Appearance = WorkflowNodeAppearance.Compact });
        _save = Add(new WorkflowNode("save", "Save to warehouse") { Description = "Postgres", Icon = ArcIcons.Database, Appearance = WorkflowNodeAppearance.Compact });
        _graph.Connect(_trigger, _lookup);
        _graph.Connect(_lookup, _branch);
        _graph.Connect(_branch, _notify);
        _graph.Connect(_branch, _task);
        _graph.Connect(_branch, _save);
        Canvas.Graph = _graph;
        SendButton.Click += (_, _) => NextOrder(at: 0);
        Prepare(s_orders[0]);
    }

    private WorkflowNode Add(WorkflowNode node)
    {
        _graph.Nodes.Add(node);
        return node;
    }

    protected override void OnLoaded(RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        base.OnLoaded(e);
        NextOrder(at: 900);
    }

    protected override void OnUnloaded(RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        base.OnUnloaded(e);
        // The run pauses off screen.
        _step?.Dispose();
        _step = null;
    }

    /// <summary>Starts the next sample order after <paramref name="at"/> ms of waiting.</summary>
    private void NextOrder(int at)
    {
        _step?.Dispose();
        _index = (_index + 1) % s_orders.Length;
        var order = s_orders[_index];
        Prepare(order);
        RunCount.Text = $"Run {++_runs:N0}";
        Summary.Text = "Waiting for the next event";
        if (!ArcMotion.IsFull(this))
        {
            // Reduced motion: show each order as its finished run without playing it.
            Finish(order);
            return;
        }
        // Each step runs for its own time; the canvas spends about 400ms drawing the data to the next one.
        Then(at, () =>
        {
            Summary.Text = "Running";
            _trigger.State = WorkflowNodeState.Running;
            Then(420, () =>
            {
                _trigger.State = WorkflowNodeState.Done;
                _lookup.State = WorkflowNodeState.Running;
                Then(400 + 640, () =>
                {
                    _lookup.Result = order.Plan;
                    _lookup.Duration = TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(order.Lookup);
                    _lookup.State = WorkflowNodeState.Done;
                    _branch.State = WorkflowNodeState.Running;
                    Then(400 + 360, () =>
                    {
                        Branch(order);
                        Then(400 + 760, () =>
                        {
                            Finish(order);
                            Then(2800, () => NextOrder(at: 900));
                        });
                    });
                });
            });
        });
    }

    private void Then(int milliseconds, Action action)
        => _step = DispatcherTimer.RunOnce(action, TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(milliseconds));

    private void Prepare(Order order)
    {
        _graph.ResetRun();
        _trigger.Description = $"{order.Customer}, {order.Amount}";
    }

    /// <summary>The branch decides: a small order skips the chat post and the task.</summary>
    private void Branch(Order order)
    {
        _branch.Result = order.Routed ? "Yes, alert the team" : "No, record only";
        _branch.Duration = TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(order.Branch);
        _branch.State = WorkflowNodeState.Done;
        _notify.State = order.Routed ? WorkflowNodeState.Running : WorkflowNodeState.Skipped;
        _task.State = order.Routed ? WorkflowNodeState.Running : WorkflowNodeState.Skipped;
        _save.State = WorkflowNodeState.Running;
    }

    private void Finish(Order order)
    {
        _trigger.State = WorkflowNodeState.Done;
        _lookup.Result = order.Plan;
        _lookup.Duration = TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(order.Lookup);
        _lookup.State = WorkflowNodeState.Done;
        if (_branch.State != WorkflowNodeState.Done)
        {
            Branch(order);
        }
        if (order.Routed)
        {
            _notify.Result = $"Sent in {order.Notify} ms";
            _notify.Duration = TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(order.Notify);
            _notify.State = WorkflowNodeState.Done;
            _task.Result = $"{order.Task} in {order.Create} ms";
            _task.Duration = TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(order.Create);
            _task.State = WorkflowNodeState.Done;
        }
        _save.Result = $"Saved in {order.Save} ms";
        _save.Duration = TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(order.Save);
        _save.State = WorkflowNodeState.Done;
        Summary.Text = $"Completed in {order.Total} ms";
    }
}
```

## When to use

- Show how an automation, pipeline or agent workflow is put together: its steps, its branches and where they lead.
- Play a run as it happens, or replay one from history: which step is running, what each step found, how long it took, and which branch the run skipped.
- Explain a product that works for the user in the background (webhooks, data syncs, deploys), where seeing the steps run is the point.
- Let people build or change a workflow themselves: move the steps, connect them, branch on a condition.

## When not to use

- A short, straight sequence of steps a person works through: use `Stepper`.
- Events in time order without a structure: use `Timeline`, or `AgentTimeline` for agent runs.
- An agent's plan as an editable checklist: use `AgentPlan`.
- Quantities flowing between stages: use a Sankey-style chart.

## Usage

Build a `WorkflowGraph` from steps (`WorkflowNode`) and the connections between them (`WorkflowEdge`, or `Connect`), and give it to a `WorkflowCanvas`. Steps without a `Position` are arranged in ranks, top to bottom, and the places are written back to the steps.

```xml
<arc:WorkflowCanvas x:Name="Canvas" />
```

```csharp
var graph = new WorkflowGraph();
var trigger = new WorkflowNode("trigger", "Order placed") { Icon = ArcIcons.Zap };
var lookup = new WorkflowNode("lookup", "Find customer account") { Description = "Plan, seats and owner" };
graph.Nodes.Add(trigger);
graph.Nodes.Add(lookup);
graph.Connect(trigger, lookup);
Canvas.Graph = graph;
```

### Playing a run

Set each step's `State` when it really changes: `Running` when the step starts, `Done` (with `Result` and `Duration`) when it finishes, `Failed` (with `Error`) when it fails, `Skipped` for the steps a branch did not take. Call `ResetRun` before the next run. Edges follow their steps on their own: when a step is done and the next one starts, the data draws along the edge in the accent; the edges into skipped steps turn dashed.

```csharp
lookup.State = WorkflowNodeState.Done;
lookup.Result = "Enterprise, 212 seats";
lookup.Duration = TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(118);
branch.State = WorkflowNodeState.Running;
```

You can set the next step running at the same moment the previous one finishes: with `QueueRunVisuals` on (the default), the next card keeps showing as waiting until the data has drawn into it, so the run always reads step, edge, step. Only what the card shows waits; `State` is what you set.

### Step states

Each card shows its step's state at the end of the row: nothing while there is no run, an empty ring while waiting, a spinning ring while running, the time and a check when done, an alert mark when failed, a minus when skipped. A running card takes the accent, a failed one a red border, a skipped one fades. `WorkflowNodeCard` also works outside a canvas.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.WorkflowCanvasStatesDemo">
    <!-- The six states a step card shows, from no run at all to failed. Cards also work outside a canvas. -->
    <WrapPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center" ItemSpacing="16" LineSpacing="16" MaxWidth="640">
        <arc:WorkflowNodeCard>
            <arc:WorkflowNodeCard.Node>
                <arc:WorkflowNode Title="Find customer account" Description="Plan, seats and owner"
                                  Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Search}" State="Idle" />
            </arc:WorkflowNodeCard.Node>
        </arc:WorkflowNodeCard>
        <arc:WorkflowNodeCard>
            <arc:WorkflowNodeCard.Node>
                <arc:WorkflowNode Title="Find customer account" Description="Plan, seats and owner"
                                  Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Search}" State="Pending" />
            </arc:WorkflowNodeCard.Node>
        </arc:WorkflowNodeCard>
        <arc:WorkflowNodeCard>
            <arc:WorkflowNodeCard.Node>
                <arc:WorkflowNode Title="Find customer account" Description="Plan, seats and owner"
                                  Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Search}" State="Running" />
            </arc:WorkflowNodeCard.Node>
        </arc:WorkflowNodeCard>
        <arc:WorkflowNodeCard>
            <arc:WorkflowNodeCard.Node>
                <arc:WorkflowNode Title="Find customer account" Description="Plan, seats and owner"
                                  Result="Enterprise, 212 seats" Duration="0:0:0.118"

            </arc:WorkflowNodeCard.Node>
        </arc:WorkflowNodeCard>
        <arc:WorkflowNodeCard>
            <arc:WorkflowNodeCard.Node>
                <arc:WorkflowNode Title="Create onboarding task" Description="Onboarding team"
                                  Error="Task service timed out" Appearance="Compact"
                                  Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.ListChecks}" State="Failed" />
```

### Compact steps

`Appearance="Compact"` lays a card out in two rows, 200 × 84: icon and state on top, title and description below. Use it for a row of actions that fan out from one step, as in the preview.

### Left to right

`LayoutDirection="LeftToRight"` runs the workflow across the canvas: edges leave a card's right side and enter the next card's left side, and arranging places ranks side by side.

### Edge styles

`EdgeStyle` draws the edges as curves (`Bezier`, the default, as in Arc), right angles with rounded corners (`Step`), or straight lines (`Straight`). The data of a run draws along any of them.


### Panning and zooming

People pan by dragging the canvas (or with the middle button), zoom with Ctrl / ⌘ + wheel, a trackpad pinch or a touch pinch, and with the + and − keys. `WheelMode` decides what plain scrolling does: `Pan` (the default) pans the canvas, which suits a canvas that fills a panel; `ModifierZoom` leaves plain scrolling to the page, which suits a canvas inside a scrolling page. `IsPanZoomEnabled="False"` turns all of it off for a workflow that should only fit, like the preview. A double click on the empty canvas fits the workflow again.

`WorkflowZoomControls` is a small zoom bar: zoom out, the current zoom (click it for 100%), zoom in, and fit. Point its `Target` at the canvas and place it over a corner. From code, `ZoomTo`, `ZoomIn`, `ZoomOut`, `FitToContent` and `ScrollIntoView` move the view with a short ease-out unless you pass `animate: false`.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.WorkflowCanvasPanZoomDemo">
    <!-- A larger workflow in a fixed-height canvas: drag to pan, scroll to pan, Ctrl + scroll or pinch to zoom.
         The zoom bar sits over the bottom-left corner. -->
    <Panel Height="420">
        <arc:WorkflowCanvas x:Name="Canvas"
                            AutoFit="Fit"
                            CornerRadius="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource RadiusPanel}"
                            BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource BorderSubtle}"
                            BorderThickness="1" />
        <arc:WorkflowZoomControls Target="{Binding #Canvas}"
                                  Margin="12"
                                  HorizontalAlignment="Left"
                                  VerticalAlignment="Bottom" />
    </Panel>
</UserControl>
```


### Arranging

The canvas arranges steps without a `Position` and remembers that it did: when such a workflow grows or loses a step, it is arranged again and the cards glide to their new places. `ArrangeNodes()` arranges every step again with Arc's spacing (52 between ranks, 72 below a step that fans out, 20 between neighbours) and hands steps your code placed back to the canvas.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.WorkflowCanvasArrangeDemo">
    <!-- Scatter the steps, then let the canvas arrange them: the cards glide into ranks and the edges follow. -->
    <StackPanel MaxWidth="640" Spacing="16">
        <StackPanel Orientation="Horizontal" Spacing="8" HorizontalAlignment="Center">
            <arc:Button x:Name="ScatterButton" Content="Scatter steps" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" />
            <arc:Button x:Name="ArrangeButton" Content="Arrange" Size="Small" />
        </StackPanel>
        <arc:WorkflowCanvas x:Name="Canvas"
                            Height="440"
                            AutoFit="Fit"
                            MaxZoom="1"
                            WheelMode="ModifierZoom"
                            CornerRadius="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource RadiusPanel}"
                            BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource BorderSubtle}"
                            BorderThickness="1" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia;
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

/// <summary>
/// Scatter places every step by hand (so the canvas stops arranging them); Arrange hands them back to the canvas, which
/// arranges the workflow and glides the cards into place.
/// </summary>
public partial class WorkflowCanvasArrangeDemo : UserControl
{
    private readonly WorkflowGraph _graph = new();
    private readonly Random _random = new(7);

    public WorkflowCanvasArrangeDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        var issue = Add(new WorkflowNode("issue", "Issue opened") { Description = "Bug report", Icon = ArcIcons.Bug });
        var triage = Add(new WorkflowNode("triage", "Triage") { Description = "Label and priority", Icon = ArcIcons.Tag });
        var repro = Add(new WorkflowNode("repro", "Reproduce") { Description = "Test environment", Icon = ArcIcons.Terminal, Appearance = WorkflowNodeAppearance.Compact });
        var assign = Add(new WorkflowNode("assign", "Assign owner") { Description = "Team rotation", Icon = ArcIcons.User, Appearance = WorkflowNodeAppearance.Compact });
        var fix = Add(new WorkflowNode("fix", "Fix and review") { Description = "Pull request", Icon = ArcIcons.GitBranch });
        var release = Add(new WorkflowNode("release", "Ship in next release") { Description = "Release notes", Icon = ArcIcons.Package });
        _graph.Connect(issue, triage);
        _graph.Connect(triage, repro);
        _graph.Connect(triage, assign);
        _graph.Connect(repro, fix);
        _graph.Connect(assign, fix);
        _graph.Connect(fix, release);
        Canvas.Graph = _graph;
        ScatterButton.Click += (_, _) => Scatter();
        ArrangeButton.Click += (_, _) => Canvas.ArrangeNodes();
    }

    private WorkflowNode Add(WorkflowNode node)
    {
        _graph.Nodes.Add(node);
        return node;
    }

    private void Scatter()
    {
        foreach (var node in _graph.Nodes)
        {
            node.Position = new Point(_random.Next(0, 520), _random.Next(0, 520));
        }
    }
}
```

### Editing

`IsEditable="True"` lets people rearrange the workflow. Drag a step to move it (the selected steps move together and snap to the dot grid when let go; hold Alt to place them freely), Shift + drag the empty canvas to select every step the rectangle touches, and drag a step near the edge to scroll the view. With the keyboard, Space selects the focused step, Ctrl / ⌘ + A selects all, M starts moving the selection with the arrow keys (Shift for five grid steps, Enter to place, Escape to cancel), and Delete removes the selected steps and edges. A step with `IsLocked` stays where it is and cannot be deleted, but can still be selected.

Ctrl / ⌘ + C copies the selected steps and the edges among them, Ctrl / ⌘ + X cuts them, Ctrl / ⌘ + V pastes them one grid step down and right of where they were copied (in the middle of the view when that place is out of sight), and Ctrl / ⌘ + D duplicates them without the clipboard; pasted steps get new ids and become the selection. Within your app a paste keeps everything a step had except its run; between apps the clipboard carries the steps as JSON, without icons. Copying works on a read-only canvas too. From code: `CopySelectionAsync`, `CutSelectionAsync`, `PasteAsync` and `DuplicateSelection`.

Selecting works on any canvas: a click selects a step, Ctrl / ⌘ + click toggles it, Shift + click adds it, and a click on the empty canvas clears the selection. Read `SelectedNodes`, change it with `Select` and `ClearSelection`, and follow it with `SelectionChanged`. Each finished edit raises `GraphEdited` once, with what changed (`Move`, `Delete`, `Connect`, `Disconnect`, `Paste`, `Undo` or `Redo`), the steps and the edges: save the workflow there.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.WorkflowCanvasEditingDemo">
    <!-- An editable workflow: drag steps (they snap to the grid), Shift + drag the empty canvas to select several,
         press M to move the selection with the arrow keys, Delete to remove it, Ctrl / Cmd + Z to undo. The approval
         step is locked. -->
    <StackPanel MaxWidth="680" Spacing="12">
        <Grid ColumnDefinitions="*,Auto">
            <TextBlock x:Name="Status"
                       VerticalAlignment="Center"
                       FontSize="13"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
            <StackPanel Grid.Column="1" Orientation="Horizontal" Spacing="8">
                <arc:Button Content="Delete selected" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Command="{Binding #Canvas.DeleteSelectionCommand}" />
                <arc:Button x:Name="ArrangeButton" Content="Arrange" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" />
            </StackPanel>
        </Grid>
        <Panel Height="460">
            <arc:WorkflowCanvas x:Name="Canvas"
                                IsEditable="True"
                                AutoFit="Fit"
                                MaxZoom="1"
                                CornerRadius="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource RadiusPanel}"
                                BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource BorderSubtle}"
                                BorderThickness="1" />
            <arc:WorkflowZoomControls Target="{Binding #Canvas}"
                                      Margin="12"
                                      HorizontalAlignment="Left"
                                      VerticalAlignment="Bottom" />
        </Panel>
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

/// <summary>
/// A refund workflow to edit. The status line follows <see cref="WorkflowCanvas.SelectionChanged"/> and
/// <see cref="WorkflowCanvas.GraphEdited"/>, which is where an app would save.
/// </summary>
public partial class WorkflowCanvasEditingDemo : UserControl
{
    public WorkflowCanvasEditingDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        var graph = new WorkflowGraph();
        WorkflowNode Add(WorkflowNode node)
        {
            graph.Nodes.Add(node);
            return node;
        }
        var request = Add(new WorkflowNode("request", "Refund requested") { Description = "Support form", Icon = ArcIcons.Inbox });
        var order = Add(new WorkflowNode("order", "Find the order") { Description = "Payments", Icon = ArcIcons.Search });
        var check = Add(new WorkflowNode("check", "Amount over $500?") { Description = "Condition", Icon = ArcIcons.GitBranch });
        var approve = Add(new WorkflowNode("approve", "Manager approval")
        {
            Description = "Locked by policy", Icon = ArcIcons.Lock, IsLocked = true, Appearance = WorkflowNodeAppearance.Compact
        });
        var refund = Add(new WorkflowNode("refund", "Issue refund") { Description = "Payments", Icon = ArcIcons.CreditCard, Appearance = WorkflowNodeAppearance.Compact });
        var notify = Add(new WorkflowNode("notify", "Email customer") { Description = "Template", Icon = ArcIcons.Mail, Appearance = WorkflowNodeAppearance.Compact });
        graph.Connect(request, order);
        graph.Connect(order, check);
        graph.Connect(check, approve);
        graph.Connect(check, refund);
        graph.Connect(approve, refund);
        graph.Connect(refund, notify);
        Canvas.Graph = graph;

        Status.Text = "Nothing selected";
        Canvas.SelectionChanged += (_, _) => Status.Text = Canvas.SelectedNodes.Count switch
        {
            0 => "Nothing selected",
            1 => $"Selected: {Canvas.SelectedNodes[0].Title}",
            var n => $"{n} steps selected"
        };
        Canvas.GraphEdited += (_, e) => Status.Text = e.Kind switch
        {
            WorkflowEditKind.Move => $"Moved {Count(e.Nodes.Count, "step")}",
            WorkflowEditKind.Delete when e.Nodes.Count > 0 => $"Deleted {Count(e.Nodes.Count, "step")}",
            WorkflowEditKind.Delete => $"Deleted {Count(e.Edges.Count, "connection")}",
            WorkflowEditKind.Connect => $"Connected {e.Nodes[0].Title} to {e.Nodes[1].Title}",
            WorkflowEditKind.Disconnect => "Removed a connection",
            WorkflowEditKind.Undo => "Undone",
            _ => "Redone"
        };
        ArrangeButton.Click += (_, _) => Canvas.ArrangeNodes();
    }

    private static string Count(int count, string noun) => $"{count} {noun}{(count == 1 ? "" : "s")}";
}
```

```csharp
Canvas.GraphEdited += (_, e) =>
{
    // Move: the steps are at their new Position. Delete: they are already out of Canvas.Graph.
    foreach (var node in e.Nodes)
    {
        Debug.WriteLine($"{e.Kind} {node.Id} at {node.Position}");
    }
};
```

A step you move is yours from then on: the canvas no longer arranges it when the workflow changes or narrows, until `ArrangeNodes` hands it back. Edits people make on the canvas never arrange the workflow again; connections your code adds to a workflow the canvas arranged do.

### Connecting steps

On an editable canvas a card shows its ports when you point at it, select it or focus it: the input on its top side and the outputs on its bottom side (left and right when the workflow runs across). Drag from an output onto another step, or close to one of its inputs, to connect them. While you drag, the steps the connection cannot go to fade, and pointing at one tells you why. Drag the end of an edge off its input to move it to another step, or let go on the empty canvas to remove it. Click an edge to select it (Ctrl / ⌘ + click toggles it, Shift + click adds it); Delete removes it. With the keyboard, C starts a connection from the focused step: when it has several outputs, choose one with the arrow keys and press Enter; then choose a step with the arrow keys and press Enter to connect.

A step without ports has one input and one output of its own (the edge's port is then null). Give a step named ports where the workflow branches, such as the "Yes" and "No" of a condition; their labels always show beside them. Turn `HasDefaultInput` off for a trigger, which nothing leads into.

```csharp
var yes = new WorkflowPort(WorkflowPortDirection.Output, "Yes");
var no = new WorkflowPort(WorkflowPortDirection.Output, "No");
check.Outputs.Add(yes);
check.Outputs.Add(no);
graph.Connect(check, yes, approve, null);
graph.Connect(check, no, refund, null);
```

Every connection is checked before it is made. It is refused when it would connect a step to itself, end at an output, repeat a connection, go past a port's `MaxConnections`, join ports whose `DataType`s differ, or close a loop (unless `AllowCycles` is on). `CanConnect` runs the same checks from code and tells you why. Put your own rules in `ConnectionRequested`: set `Cancel`, and a `Reason` the person hears. A connection let go on the empty canvas raises `ConnectionDroppedOnCanvas` with the place, in canvas units: offer a list of steps there and add the chosen one.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.WorkflowCanvasConnectingDemo">
    <!-- Drag from an output (the circles under a card when you point at it) onto another step to connect them, or drag
         the end of an edge off its input to move or remove it. Connecting "Yes" straight to the refund is refused:
         amounts over $500 need an approval first. A connection dropped on the empty canvas adds a step there. -->
    <StackPanel MaxWidth="680" Spacing="12">
        <Grid ColumnDefinitions="*,Auto">
            <TextBlock x:Name="Status"
                       VerticalAlignment="Center"
                       TextTrimming="CharacterEllipsis"
                       FontSize="13"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
            <StackPanel Grid.Column="1" Orientation="Horizontal" Spacing="8">
                <arc:Button Content="Undo" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Command="{Binding #Canvas.UndoCommand}" />
                <arc:Button Content="Redo" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Command="{Binding #Canvas.RedoCommand}" />
            </StackPanel>
        </Grid>
        <arc:WorkflowCanvas x:Name="Canvas"
                            Height="460"
                            IsEditable="True"
                            AutoFit="Fit"
                            MaxZoom="1"
                            CornerRadius="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource RadiusPanel}"
                            BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource BorderSubtle}"
                            BorderThickness="1" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia;
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

/// <summary>
/// Connecting steps: a condition with "Yes" and "No" outputs, an app rule in
/// <see cref="WorkflowCanvas.ConnectionRequested"/>, a new step where a connection is dropped on the empty canvas
/// (<see cref="WorkflowCanvas.ConnectionDroppedOnCanvas"/>), and undo and redo buttons bound to the canvas's commands.
/// </summary>
public partial class WorkflowCanvasConnectingDemo : UserControl
{
    private int _added;

    public WorkflowCanvasConnectingDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        var graph = new WorkflowGraph();
        WorkflowNode Add(WorkflowNode node)
        {
            graph.Nodes.Add(node);
            return node;
        }
        // A trigger starts the workflow, so nothing connects into it.
        var request = Add(new WorkflowNode("request", "Refund requested")
        {
            Description = "Order #1042, $640", Icon = ArcIcons.Inbox, HasDefaultInput = false
        });
        var check = Add(new WorkflowNode("check", "Amount over $500?") { Description = "Condition", Icon = ArcIcons.GitBranch });
        var yes = new WorkflowPort(WorkflowPortDirection.Output, "Yes");
        var no = new WorkflowPort(WorkflowPortDirection.Output, "No");
        check.Outputs.Add(yes);
        check.Outputs.Add(no);
        var approve = Add(new WorkflowNode("approve", "Manager approval") { Description = "Finance team", Icon = ArcIcons.ShieldCheck });
        var refund = Add(new WorkflowNode("refund", "Issue refund") { Description = "Payments", Icon = ArcIcons.CreditCard });
        Add(new WorkflowNode("email", "Email the customer") { Description = "Template: refund sent", Icon = ArcIcons.Mail });
        graph.Connect(request, check);
        graph.Connect(check, yes, approve, null);
        graph.Connect(approve, refund);
        graph.Connect(check, no, refund, null);
        Canvas.Graph = graph;

        // The workflow's own checks run first (no loops, outputs to inputs, no duplicates); this is the app's rule.
        Canvas.ConnectionRequested += (_, e) =>
        {
            if (e.SourcePort == yes && e.TargetNode == refund)
            {
                e.Cancel = true;
                e.Reason = "Amounts over $500 need a manager's approval first";
                Status.Text = e.Reason;
            }
        };
        // Let go on the empty canvas: add a step there, its input under the pointer, and connect it; one undo takes both back.
        Canvas.ConnectionDroppedOnCanvas += (_, e) =>
        {
            var step = new WorkflowNode($"notify-{++_added}", "Notify the team")
            {
                Description = "Team chat", Icon = ArcIcons.MessageSquare, Position = new Point(e.Position.X - 150, e.Position.Y)
            };
            using (graph.History.BeginGroup())
            {
                graph.Nodes.Add(step);
                graph.Connect(e.SourceNode, e.SourcePort, step, null);
            }
            Status.Text = $"Added \"{step.Title}\" after {e.SourceNode.Title}";
        };
        Canvas.GraphEdited += (_, e) => Status.Text = e.Kind switch
        {
            WorkflowEditKind.Connect => $"Connected {e.Nodes[0].Title} to {e.Nodes[1].Title}",
            WorkflowEditKind.Disconnect => "Removed a connection",
            WorkflowEditKind.Undo => "Undone",
            WorkflowEditKind.Redo => "Redone",
            WorkflowEditKind.Delete => "Deleted",
            _ => "Moved"
        };
        Status.Text = "Point at a step to see its ports";
    }
}
```

```csharp
Canvas.ConnectionRequested += (_, e) =>
{
    if (e.SourcePort == yes && e.TargetNode == refund)
    {
        e.Cancel = true;
        e.Reason = "Amounts over $500 need a manager's approval first";
    }
};
Canvas.ConnectionDroppedOnCanvas += (_, e) =>
{
    var step = new WorkflowNode("notify", "Notify the team") { Position = new Point(e.Position.X - 150, e.Position.Y) };
    // One edit: a single undo takes the step and its connection back.
    using (graph.History.BeginGroup())
    {
        graph.Nodes.Add(step);
        graph.Connect(e.SourceNode, e.SourcePort, step, null);
    }
};
```

### Undo and redo

`WorkflowGraph.History` keeps the last 100 edits people made on the canvas: moving, deleting, connecting, moving or removing edges, and pasting. Ctrl / ⌘ + Z undoes, Ctrl / ⌘ + Shift + Z or Ctrl + Y redoes, and the canvas's `Undo()` and `Redo()` do the same for your buttons; moved cards glide back. Follow `History.Changed` to update those buttons from `CanUndo` and `CanRedo`.

Changes your code makes to the workflow are recorded only inside `History.BeginGroup()`: everything added, removed or moved until the group is disposed becomes one edit, as in the handler above. If your app keeps its own undo history, turn `History.IsEnabled` off and follow `GraphEdited` instead.

### Toolbar commands

For toolbar buttons and menu items, the canvas has commands: `UndoCommand`, `RedoCommand`, `DeleteSelectionCommand`, `CopyCommand`, `CutCommand`, `PasteCommand`, `DuplicateCommand`, `ZoomInCommand`, `ZoomOutCommand` and `FitCommand`. Each runs only when it would do something, such as undo with an edit to undo or delete with something selected, so a bound button turns itself on and off.

```xml
<arc:Button Content="Undo" Command="{Binding #Canvas.UndoCommand}" />
<arc:Button Content="Delete" Command="{Binding #Canvas.DeleteSelectionCommand}" />
```

### Custom card content

`NodeTemplates` replaces the content of the cards it matches: a `WorkflowNodeTemplate` is written in XAML for one `Kind` of step, its data is the `WorkflowNode`, and the first template that matches a step wins. The card keeps its frame, the run's colors, the selection, the focus ring and its ports; steps no template matches keep the default card. Without a `Size` the card is as tall as its content. Controls in a card, such as an input or a switch, keep their own clicks and keys, so typing in them never moves or connects the step.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.WorkflowCanvasCustomNodesDemo">
    <!-- Two kinds of step have their own card content: the webhook shows its address and an on / off switch, the email
         edits its recipient and whether the invoice goes along. The other steps keep the default card. -->
    <arc:WorkflowCanvas x:Name="Canvas"
                        MaxWidth="680"
                        Height="520"
                        AutoFit="Fit"
                        MaxZoom="1"
                        IsEditable="True"
                        CornerRadius="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource RadiusPanel}"
                        BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource BorderSubtle}"
                        BorderThickness="1">
        <arc:WorkflowCanvas.NodeTemplates>
            <arc:WorkflowNodeTemplate Kind="webhook" x:DataType="arc:WorkflowNode">
                <StackPanel Spacing="8">
                    <Grid ColumnDefinitions="Auto,*,Auto" ColumnSpacing="12">
                        <arc:ArcGlyph Data="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Zap}"
                                      Size="17"
                                      StrokeThickness="1.75"
                                      Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}"
                                      VerticalAlignment="Center" />
                        <TextBlock Grid.Column="1"
                                   Text="{Binding Title}"
                                   FontWeight="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource WeightMedium}"
                                   TextTrimming="CharacterEllipsis"
                                   VerticalAlignment="Center" />
                        <arc:Switch Grid.Column="2" IsChecked="True" VerticalAlignment="Center" />

                               FontFamily="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource MonoFontFamily}"

                               TextTrimming="CharacterEllipsis" />
                </StackPanel>
            </arc:WorkflowNodeTemplate>
            <arc:WorkflowNodeTemplate Kind="email" x:DataType="arc:WorkflowNode">
                <StackPanel Spacing="10">
                    <StackPanel Orientation="Horizontal" Spacing="12">
                        <arc:ArcGlyph Data="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Mail}"
                                      Size="17"
                                      StrokeThickness="1.75"
```
