### Large workflows

The canvas is built for hundreds of steps: cards, shadows and the dot grid stay cheap to draw however many show, so a workflow of 500 steps and 800 edges stays responsive to pan, zoom and drag on a desktop. `WorkflowMinimap` shows the whole workflow small, with the part on screen as a frame: press it to go there, drag to pan. Point its `Target` at the canvas and place it over a corner, like the zoom bar.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.WorkflowCanvasLargeGraphDemo">
    <!-- A generated workflow of 200 or 500 steps, arranged by the canvas and shown from its start at 75%: drag or scroll
         to move around, use the map in the corner, or fit the whole workflow with the bar. -->
    <StackPanel MaxWidth="680" Spacing="12">
        <Grid ColumnDefinitions="*,Auto">
            <TextBlock x:Name="Status"
                       VerticalAlignment="Center"
                       FontSize="13"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
            <arc:SegmentedControl x:Name="Count"
                                  Grid.Column="1"
                                  SelectedValue="200"
                                  SelectionChanged="OnCountChanged">
                <arc:SegmentedOption Value="200" Label="200 steps" />
                <arc:SegmentedOption Value="500" Label="500 steps" />
            </arc:SegmentedControl>
        </Grid>
        <Panel Height="480">
            <arc:WorkflowCanvas x:Name="Canvas"
                                AutoFit="None"
                                Zoom="0.75"
                                MinZoom="0.05"
                                MaxZoom="1.5"
                                IsEditable="True"
                                CornerRadius="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource RadiusPanel}"
                                BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource BorderSubtle}"
                                BorderThickness="1" />
            <arc:WorkflowZoomControls Target="{Binding #Canvas}"
                                      Margin="12"
                                      HorizontalAlignment="Left"
                                      VerticalAlignment="Bottom" />
            <arc:WorkflowMinimap Target="{Binding #Canvas}"
                                 Margin="12"
                                 HorizontalAlignment="Right"
                                 VerticalAlignment="Bottom" />
        </Panel>
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

/// <summary>
/// A large generated workflow (ranks of 8 steps, each fed by one or two steps of the rank before) with the zoom bar and the
/// minimap, shown from its start. It starts at 200 steps so the page opens quickly; 500 is the size measured on a desktop.
/// </summary>
public partial class WorkflowCanvasLargeGraphDemo : UserControl
{
    public WorkflowCanvasLargeGraphDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Show(200);
    }

    private void OnCountChanged(object? sender, SelectionChangedEventArgs e)
    {
        if (Count?.SelectedValue is string value && int.TryParse(value, out var count))
        {
            Show(count);
        }
    }

    private void Show(int count)
    {
        var graph = Generate(count);
        Canvas.Graph = graph;
        // Start at the first step, once the canvas has arranged the workflow.
        void ShowStart(object? sender, EventArgs e)
        {
            Canvas.LayoutUpdated -= ShowStart;
            Canvas.ScrollIntoView(graph.Nodes[0], animate: false);
        }
        Canvas.LayoutUpdated += ShowStart;
        Status.Text = $"{count} steps, {graph.Edges.Count} connections";
    }

    private static WorkflowGraph Generate(int count)
    {
        // Seeded: the same workflow every time.
        var random = new Random(7);
        var graph = new WorkflowGraph();
        var kinds = new[]
        {
            ("Webhook", ArcIcons.Zap), ("Postgres", ArcIcons.Database), ("Team chat", ArcIcons.MessageSquare),
            ("Payments", ArcIcons.CreditCard), ("Email", ArcIcons.Mail)
        };
        var ranks = new List<List<WorkflowNode>>();
        for (var i = 0; i < count; i++)
        {
            if (i % 8 == 0)
            {
                ranks.Add([]);
            }
            var (description, icon) = kinds[i % kinds.Length];
            var node = new WorkflowNode($"step-{i + 1}", $"Step {i + 1}") { Description = description, Icon = icon };
            graph.Nodes.Add(node);
            ranks[^1].Add(node);
        }
        for (var r = 1; r < ranks.Count; r++)
        {
            var before = ranks[r - 1];
            foreach (var node in ranks[r])
            {
                var first = before[random.Next(before.Count)];
                graph.Connect(first, node);
                var second = before[random.Next(before.Count)];
                if (random.NextDouble() < 0.6 && second != first)
                {
                    graph.Connect(second, node);
                }
            }
        }
        return graph;
    }
}
```

```xml
<Panel>
    <arc:WorkflowCanvas x:Name="Canvas" MinZoom="0.05" />
    <arc:WorkflowMinimap Target="{Binding #Canvas}" Margin="12"
                         HorizontalAlignment="Right" VerticalAlignment="Bottom" />
</Panel>
```

Lower `MinZoom` (0.25 by default) so that fitting can show all of a large workflow.

### Narrow canvases

Below `NarrowBelowWidth` (520 by default, as in Arc) the canvas switches to Arc's phone layout: one-row cards become 344 × 52, two-row cards 108 × 72, and a workflow the canvas arranged is arranged again with tighter spacing (26, 36 and 10), so it shows at actual size instead of shrinking. Steps your code placed keep their places. Keep the titles of compact steps to a word or two; they have little room on a phone.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.WorkflowCanvasNarrowDemo">
    <!-- Under 520 wide the canvas switches to Arc's phone layout: narrower cards and tighter spacing, at actual size. -->
    <arc:WorkflowCanvas x:Name="Canvas"
                        MaxWidth="392"
                        WheelMode="ModifierZoom"
                        CornerRadius="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource RadiusPanel}"
                        BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource BorderSubtle}"
                        BorderThickness="1" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

/// <summary>A short automation with three actions, finished, on a phone-sized canvas.</summary>
public partial class WorkflowCanvasNarrowDemo : UserControl
{
    public WorkflowCanvasNarrowDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        var graph = new WorkflowGraph();
        var signup = new WorkflowNode("signup", "New signup") { Description = "Web app", Icon = ArcIcons.User, State = WorkflowNodeState.Done };
        var enrich = new WorkflowNode("enrich", "Enrich profile")
        {
            Description = "Company data", Result = "Brightline Labs, 212 people", Duration = TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(240),
            Icon = ArcIcons.Search, State = WorkflowNodeState.Done
        };
        var welcome = new WorkflowNode("welcome", "Welcome")
        {
            Description = "Email", Result = "Sent", Duration = TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(90),
            Icon = ArcIcons.Mail, Appearance = WorkflowNodeAppearance.Compact, State = WorkflowNodeState.Done
        };
        var crm = new WorkflowNode("crm", "CRM")
        {
            Description = "New lead", Icon = ArcIcons.Users, Appearance = WorkflowNodeAppearance.Compact, State = WorkflowNodeState.Running
        };
        var slack = new WorkflowNode("chat", "Chat")
        {
            Description = "#signups", Icon = ArcIcons.MessageSquare, Appearance = WorkflowNodeAppearance.Compact, State = WorkflowNodeState.Pending
        };
        foreach (var node in new[] { signup, enrich, welcome, crm, slack })
        {
            graph.Nodes.Add(node);
        }
        graph.Connect(signup, enrich);
        graph.Connect(enrich, welcome);
        graph.Connect(enrich, crm);
        graph.Connect(enrich, slack);
        Canvas.Graph = graph;
    }
}
```

### Fitting and sizes

`AutoFit` decides how the workflow fits the canvas. `ShrinkToFit` (the default) shows it at actual size, centered, and shrinks the whole workflow like a screenshot when it does not fit; `Fit` makes it as large as fits up to `MaxZoom`; `None` keeps the view you set with `Zoom` and `Offset`. Panning, zooming, or setting `Zoom` or `Offset` yourself stops fitting until `FitToContent`. In a container with unlimited height, such as a scrolling page, the canvas is as tall as the fitted workflow. `Padding` (24 by default) keeps the workflow off the edges.

### Placing steps

Give a step a `Position` to place it yourself (the card's top-left corner on the canvas). New steps without a position go in ranks after the steps your code placed.

### Content guidelines

- Name a step by what it does, short, in sentence case: "Find customer account", not "HubSpot lookup step".
- Put what the step works on in `Description` and what it found in `Result`; both stay on one line.
- Keep errors specific and short: "Health check failed in eu-west", not "Error".

## API reference

### WorkflowCanvas

Shows a `WorkflowGraph` on a dotted canvas (visual rules from Arc's free hero-section block, HeroRelay): one card per step, edges between them, and a run played out step by step. Set the steps' states as your run goes; when a step finishes, the data draws along its edges in the accent before the next step shows as running, and the edges of a branch the run did not take turn dashed. Steps without a position are arranged in ranks; by default the whole workflow shows at actual size and shrinks like a screenshot when it does not fit. Pan with a drag or the wheel, zoom with Ctrl / ⌘ + wheel, a pinch or the keyboard, and move between steps with the arrow keys.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Graph` | `WorkflowGraph?` | `null` | The workflow to show. |
| `AutoFit` | `WorkflowAutoFit` | `ShrinkToFit` | How the workflow fits the canvas (default `ShrinkToFit`: actual size, centered, shrinking when it does not fit). Panning, zooming or setting `Zoom` or `Offset` stops fitting until `FitToContent`. In a container with unlimited height the canvas is as tall as the fitted workflow. |
| `Zoom` | `double` | `1` | Screen pixels per canvas unit; kept within `MinZoom` and `MaxZoom`. |
| `Offset` | `Point` | `0, 0` | The canvas point shown at the top-left corner of the view. |
| `MinZoom` | `double` | `0.25` | The smallest zoom (default 0.25). |
| `MaxZoom` | `double` | `2` | The largest zoom (default 2). |
| `IsPanZoomEnabled` | `bool` | `true` | Whether people can pan and zoom (default true): dragging pans, the wheel works per `WheelMode`, a pinch zooms, and the + / − keys zoom. Turn it off for a workflow shown inside a scrolling page that should only fit (Arc's hero). `ZoomTo`, `FitToContent` and `ScrollIntoView` work either way. |
| `WheelMode` | `WheelMode` | `Pan` | What the wheel does (default `Pan`: scrolling pans, Ctrl / ⌘ + wheel zooms; `ModifierZoom` leaves plain scrolling to the page). |
| `LayoutDirection` | `WorkflowLayoutDirection` | `TopToBottom` | Which way the workflow runs: down (default, as in Arc) or across. Edges and arranging follow it. |
| `EdgeStyle` | `WorkflowEdgeStyle` | `Bezier` | How edges are drawn: curves (default, as in Arc), right angles with rounded corners, or straight lines. |
| `NarrowBelowWidth` | `double` | `520` | Below this width (default 520, as in Arc; 0 never) the canvas is narrow: cards shrink to 344 × 52 and 108 × 72, and a workflow the canvas arranged itself is arranged again with tighter spacing, so it stays readable on a phone instead of shrinking like a screenshot. Steps placed by your code keep their places. |
| `ShowGrid` | `bool` | `true` | Whether the dot grid shows (default true). |
| `QueueRunVisuals` | `bool` | `true` | Whether a step that starts while the data is still drawing toward it keeps showing as waiting until the data arrives (default true), so a run reads step, edge, step as in Arc even when your run sets the next step running at once. Only what is shown waits; the steps' states are untouched. Full motion only. |
| `IsEditable` | `bool` | `false` | Whether people can move and delete steps (default false). Selecting works either way. |
| `SnapToGrid` | `bool` | `true` | Whether moved steps snap to the dot grid when let go (default true); holding Alt while dragging skips it. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ConnectionRequested` | `WorkflowConnectionRequestedEventArgs` | Raised when a person connects two ports, after the workflow's own checks (`CanConnect`) and before the edge is added: set `Cancel` to refuse it, with a `Reason` to tell them why. |
| `ConnectionDroppedOnCanvas` | `WorkflowConnectionDroppedEventArgs` | Raised when a person drops a new connection on the empty canvas: show a list of steps there, add the chosen one and connect it yourself. |
| `NodeActivated` | `WorkflowNodeEventArgs` | Raised when a step is opened: double-clicked, or Enter pressed on its card. Open its settings here. |
| `SelectionChanged` | `WorkflowSelectionChangedEventArgs` | Raised once each time the selection changes, also when selected steps leave the workflow. |
| `GraphEdited` | `WorkflowEditEventArgs` | Raised once after each edit a person makes (moving steps, deleting steps), when it is done: save the workflow or record the edit here. |

Pseudo-classes: `:narrow`, `:panning`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

### WorkflowNodeCard

The card of one workflow step on a `WorkflowCanvas` (visual rules from Arc's free hero-section block, HeroRelay): icon, title, the description or result under it, and the run state at the end. A running card takes the accent, a skipped one fades, a failed one shows its error. The canvas creates one card per `WorkflowNode`; style it through the semantic part `arc.workflow.node`.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Node` | `WorkflowNode?` | `null` | The step this card shows. |
| `ContentTemplate` | `IDataTemplate?` | `null` | Content for the card in place of its icon, title, subtitle and state, built from the `Node` when the template matches it (a `WorkflowNodeTemplate` matches a step's `Kind`). The frame, the run's colors, the selection and the focus ring stay. Without `Size` the card is as tall as its content. On a canvas, set `NodeTemplates` instead. |
| `DisplayState` | `WorkflowNodeState` | – | *Read-only.* The state the card shows. It is the step's `State`, except that on a canvas a step that starts while the data is still drawing toward it keeps showing `Pending` until the data arrives (`QueueRunVisuals`). |

Pseudo-classes: `:pending`, `:running`, `:done`, `:failed`, `:skipped`, `:compact`, `:narrow`, `:selected`, `:dragging`, `:locked`, `:connect-invalid`, `:custom`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

### WorkflowGraph

A workflow: its steps (`Nodes`) and the connections between them (`Edges`). Show it with a `WorkflowCanvas`; change the collections or any step and the canvas follows. Removing a step removes its edges; an edge whose steps are not in `Nodes` is refused.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `AllowCycles` | `bool` | `false` | Whether a connection may close a loop (default false: people cannot connect a step to one before it). |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### WorkflowNode

One step of a `WorkflowGraph`: what it is (title, description, icon), where it sits on the canvas, and while a run goes through the workflow its state, result and time. Every property is observed, so changing a step updates the canvas.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Title` | `string` | `""` | What the step does, on one line (it is cut with an ellipsis when it does not fit). |
| `Description` | `string?` | `null` | The line under the title while nothing has run yet: what the step works on ("Plan, seats and owner"). |
| `Result` | `string?` | `null` | The line under the title once the step is done: what it found ("Enterprise, 212 seats"); null keeps the description. |
| `Kind` | `string?` | `null` | Your own category of the step (trigger, action, condition); screen readers read it after the title. |
| `Icon` | `object?` | `null` | The 20 × 20 mark at the start of the card: a Lucide geometry from `ArcIcons` (drawn as a stroke), an image, or any control. |
| `Position` | `Point` | `NaN, NaN` | The card's top-left corner on the canvas. NaN (the default) lets the canvas place the step by arranging the whole workflow, and writes the place it chose back here. |
| `Size` | `Size?` | `null` | The card's size; null uses the size of its `Appearance` (300 × 60 or 200 × 84). |
| `Appearance` | `WorkflowNodeAppearance` | `Standard` | One row (`Standard`) or two (`Compact`). |
| `State` | `WorkflowNodeState` | `Idle` | Where the step stands in the current run (`Idle` when there is no run). |
| `Duration` | `TimeSpan?` | `null` | How long the step took; shown next to the check once it is done ("118 ms"). |
| `Error` | `string?` | `null` | Why the step failed; shown under the title in the failed state and read by screen readers. |
| `IsLocked` | `bool` | `false` | A locked step stays where it is and cannot be deleted on an editable canvas; it can still be selected and opened. |
| `HasDefaultInput` | `bool` | `true` | Whether the step has an implicit input when `Inputs` is empty (default true). Turn it off for a step nothing leads into, such as a trigger. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### WorkflowEdge

A connection from one step of a `WorkflowGraph` to the next: the data of a run flows from `Source` to `Target`. The ends are fixed; to reconnect, remove the edge and add a new one.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `State` | `WorkflowEdgeState` | `Auto` | How the edge shows the run. `Auto` (the default) follows its two steps, so a run only needs to set the steps' states. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### WorkflowPort

A named connection point of a `WorkflowNode`, such as the "Yes" and "No" outputs of a condition. A step without ports of a direction has one implicit port there (an edge's port is then null).

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Label` | `string?` | `null` | A short name shown next to the port, such as "Yes"; null shows none. |
| `DataType` | `string?` | `null` | Your name for the kind of data the port carries; two ports with a data type connect only when the types are the same (null connects to anything). |
| `MaxConnections` | `int` | `2147483647` | How many edges the port takes (default no limit). |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### WorkflowHistory

Undo and redo for the edits people make on a `WorkflowCanvas` showing the workflow: moving, deleting, connecting, disconnecting and pasting steps. Changes your code makes to the `WorkflowGraph` are recorded only inside `BeginGroup`. Keeps the last 100 edits.

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Changed` | `EventHandler?` | Raised when what can be undone or redone changes. |

### WorkflowZoomControls

A small zoom bar for a `WorkflowCanvas`: zoom out, the current zoom (click it for 100%), zoom in, and fit. Set `Target` to the canvas and place the bar where it suits, usually over a corner of the canvas. It matches the library's other zoom bars: a 34px pill with 28px buttons.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Target` | `WorkflowCanvas?` | `null` | The canvas the buttons zoom. |

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

### WorkflowMinimap

A small map of a `WorkflowCanvas`: every step as a block (running and selected steps in the accent, failed ones in red) and the part the canvas shows as a frame. Press to move the view there, drag to pan. Set `Target` to the canvas and place the map over a corner, like `WorkflowZoomControls`. It is a pointer shortcut: the canvas's own keys do the same, so the map takes no focus and screen readers skip it.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Target` | `WorkflowCanvas?` | `null` | The canvas the map shows and moves. |

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

### WorkflowNodeTemplate

Content for the cards of one kind of step, written in XAML: put it in `NodeTemplates`. It matches the steps whose `Kind` is `Kind` (every step when null), and its content replaces the card's icon, title, subtitle and state; the data is the `WorkflowNode`. Write `x:DataType="arc:WorkflowNode"` on it for compiled bindings.

### WorkflowNodeEventArgs

A step of a `WorkflowCanvas`, for `NodeActivated`.

Derives from `RoutedEventArgs`: every member of `RoutedEventArgs` works as well.

### WorkflowEditEventArgs

One edit a person made on a `WorkflowCanvas`, for `GraphEdited`.

Derives from `RoutedEventArgs`: every member of `RoutedEventArgs` works as well.

### WorkflowSelectionChangedEventArgs

A change of a `WorkflowCanvas`'s selection, for `SelectionChanged`.

Derives from `RoutedEventArgs`: every member of `RoutedEventArgs` works as well.

### WorkflowConnectionRequestedEventArgs

A connection a person is making, for `ConnectionRequested`.

Derives from `RoutedEventArgs`: every member of `RoutedEventArgs` works as well.

### WorkflowConnectionDroppedEventArgs

A connection dropped on the empty canvas, for `ConnectionDroppedOnCanvas`.

Derives from `RoutedEventArgs`: every member of `RoutedEventArgs` works as well.

## Accessibility

- The canvas is named "Workflow, 6 steps" unless you name it with `AutomationProperties.Name`.
- Each card's name gives its title, its kind, its state in words, the time and the line under the title, for example "Find customer account, Done, 118 ms, Enterprise, 212 seats". A state is never shown by color alone: every state has its own mark.
- The canvas reads as a group and each card as an item of it. Edges, ports, the dot grid and the marks are decorative and hidden from assistive technology; the keyboard's connect mode reaches every connection the pointer can make. The minimap is a pointer shortcut for what the keys already do, so it takes no focus and screen readers skip it.
- A failed step and the end of a run are announced politely: "Create onboarding task failed: Task service timed out", "Run finished: 4 done, 1 failed, 1 skipped". So are edits: "Moved 2 steps", "Deleted 1 step", "Connected Amount over $500? to Manager approval", "Can't connect: This would create a loop", "Pasted 2 steps", "Undone", and how the keyboard's move and connect modes work when they start.
- A selected card adds "selected" to its name and shows an accent border with a soft halo, not only a color change.
- The canvas's help text lists the keys below.

### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Tab | Moves into the canvas, to the step that had focus last, and out again; the cards are one Tab stop. |
| Arrow keys | Move to the nearest step in that direction. |
| Alt + arrow keys | Follow the connections: along the workflow to the next step, against it to the previous one, across it to a neighbouring step that shares a previous step. |
| Home / End | Move to the first or last step. |
| Enter | Opens the step (`NodeActivated`). |
| + / − | Zoom in or out about the focused step. |
| Shift + 1 | Fits the workflow. |
| Ctrl / ⌘ + 0 | Zooms to 100%. |
| Shift + F10, Menu key | Asks for a context menu (`ContextRequested`, its source is the card). |
| Space | Selects or unselects the focused step. |
| Ctrl / ⌘ + A | Selects every step and edge. |
| Escape | Cancels a move or a connection, or clears the selection. |
| M | On an editable canvas: moves the selection (or the focused step) with the arrow keys; Shift moves five grid steps, Enter places, Escape cancels. |
| Delete / Backspace | On an editable canvas: deletes the selected steps and edges (or the focused step); locked steps stay. |
| C | On an editable canvas: connects the focused step. With several outputs, the arrow keys choose one and Enter goes on; then the arrow keys choose a step in reading order, Enter connects, Escape cancels. |
| Ctrl / ⌘ + Z | On an editable canvas: undoes the last edit. |
| Ctrl / ⌘ + Shift + Z, Ctrl + Y | On an editable canvas: redoes it. |
| Ctrl / ⌘ + C | Copies the selected steps (or the focused one) and the edges among them. |
| Ctrl / ⌘ + X, Ctrl / ⌘ + V | On an editable canvas: cuts them, and pastes. |
| Ctrl / ⌘ + D | On an editable canvas: duplicates the selected steps (or the focused one). |

Keys typed into a control in a card (an input in custom content) belong to that control.

A step reached with the keyboard is brought into view.

## Motion

- A running card's border and fill ease to the accent over the standard duration; a skipped card fades to half opacity.
- A state change swaps the mark at the end of the card: the new one grows from 0.6 while the old one shrinks away, on the snappy spring.
- The running ring turns once every 0.7s, only while it is on screen.
- When a step is done and the next one has started, the data draws along the edge in the accent over 400ms on the in-out curve; the next card shows as running once the data arrives.
- Fitting, zooming with the buttons or keys and bringing a step into view move the view on Arc's standard ease-out over 360ms; dragging, the wheel and pinches follow the hand without easing.
- Arranging glides the cards to their new places the same way, the edges following.
- A dragged card follows the pointer without easing, rides above the others, and settles on the grid on the snappy spring when let go; a cancelled move glides back to where it started.
- A connection being drawn follows the pointer without easing and jumps to the nearest input within 24px, which grows and takes the accent; the steps it cannot go to fade to 40% over the standard duration. Undo and redo glide moved cards back.
- Reduced motion: no color easing, the marks swap with a short fade, the ring stands still, the data appears drawn at once, and the view and the cards jump to where they go. Nothing loops while a workflow is at rest.

## Related

- `Stepper`: a straight sequence of steps a person works through.
- `AgentPlan`: an agent's plan as an editable checklist.
- `AgentTimeline`: a replay of a multi-agent run on one time axis.
- `DataFlow`: an illustration of data moving from sources to destinations.

# Table

> Compare structured records with sortable columns.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/table

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.TableProjectsDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12">
        <arc:Table x:Name="Table"
                               IsSelectable="True"
                               ItemNameOne="project"
                               ItemNameOther="projects"
                               Caption="Projects"
                               SortChanged="OnSortChanged"
                               SelectionChanged="OnSelectionChanged" />
        <TextBlock x:Name="Status"
                   Text="Click a header to sort; click rows or press Space to select."
                   FontSize="14"
                   TextWrapping="Wrap"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using System.Globalization;
using Avalonia;
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Controls.Templates;
using Avalonia.Layout;
using TKCode.Arc.DesignTokens;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class TableProjectsDemo : UserControl
{
    private sealed record Project(string Name, string Owner, string Status, decimal Budget, DateOnly Due);

    private static readonly CultureInfo s_en = CultureInfo.GetCultureInfo("en-US");

    private static readonly Project[] s_projects =
    [
        new("Atlas redesign", "Mina Park", "Active", 42000, new DateOnly(2026, 11, 14)),
        new("Billing migration", "Theo Walsh", "Review", 18500, new DateOnly(2026, 10, 30)),
        new("Checkout v3", "Ana Ruiz", "Active", 126000, new DateOnly(2027, 1, 9)),
        new("Docs search", "Kai Moreno", "Paused", 9600, new DateOnly(2026, 12, 2)),
        new("Edge caching", "Lee Chen", "Done", 31250, new DateOnly(2026, 9, 18)),
        new("Field reports", "Ivy Brooks", "Active", 57800, new DateOnly(2026, 11, 28))
    ];

    public TableProjectsDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Table.ItemsSource = s_projects;
        AddProjectColumns(Table);
    }

    private void OnSortChanged(object? sender, DataTableSortChangedEventArgs e) =>
        Status.Text = e.Column is null ? "Sort cleared" : $"Sorted by {e.Column.Header}, {e.Direction}";

    private void OnSelectionChanged(object? sender, DataTableSelectionChangedEventArgs e) =>
        Status.Text = $"{e.SelectedItems.Count} selected";

    private static void AddProjectColumns(Table table)
    {
        table.Columns.Add(DataTableColumn.Create<Project>("Project", p => p.Name));
        table.Columns.Add(DataTableColumn.Create<Project>("Owner", p => p.Owner));
        table.Columns.Add(new DataTableColumn("Status", p => ((Project)p).Status) { CellTemplate = new FuncDataTemplate<Project>((_, _) => new StatusPill()) });
        table.Columns.Add(new DataTableColumn("Budget", p => ((Project)p).Budget) { Formatter = Money });
        table.Columns.Add(new DataTableColumn("Due", p => ((Project)p).Due) { Formatter = v => v is DateOnly d ? d.ToString("MMM d, yyyy", s_en) : "–" });
    }

    private static string Money(object? value) => value is decimal amount ? amount.ToString("C0", s_en) : "–";

    /// <summary>A status badge that follows its data context (cells are recycled between rows).</summary>
    private sealed class StatusPill : Border
    {
        private readonly TextBlock _text = new() { FontSize = 12, VerticalAlignment = VerticalAlignment.Center };
        private IDisposable? _fill;
        private IDisposable? _fore;

        public StatusPill()
        {
            Child = _text;
            Padding = new Thickness(8, 2);
            CornerRadius = new CornerRadius(999);
            HorizontalAlignment = HorizontalAlignment.Left;
            VerticalAlignment = VerticalAlignment.Center;
        }

        protected override void OnDataContextChanged(EventArgs e)
        {
            base.OnDataContextChanged(e);
            var status = (DataContext as Project)?.Status ?? string.Empty;
            _text.Text = status;
            var (fill, fore) = status switch
            {
                "Active" => (ArcDesignTokenKind.SuccessSubtle, ArcDesignTokenKind.Success),
                "Paused" => (ArcDesignTokenKind.WarningSubtle, ArcDesignTokenKind.Warning),
                "Review" => (ArcDesignTokenKind.AccentSubtle, ArcDesignTokenKind.AccentStrong),
                _ => (ArcDesignTokenKind.SurfaceMuted, ArcDesignTokenKind.TextSecondary)
            };
            _fill?.Dispose();
            _fore?.Dispose();
            _fill = ArcTokens.Bind(this, BackgroundProperty, fill);
            _fore = ArcTokens.Bind(_text, TextBlock.ForegroundProperty, fore);
        }
    }
}
```

## When to use

`Table` shows records that share the same fields and lets people compare them by column. It is the table
for a page where the records are the work: a billing history, a project list in an admin console, a user directory.
Each column sorts on its own, the rows can carry a checkbox for bulk actions, and a count line says how many rows
exist and how many are selected.

Arc calls it the sortable data table, and earlier previews named the class `SortableDataTable`. That name still
works for now, with an obsolete warning, and will be removed in a later preview.

- **Invoices and billing history** on a billing page: sort by issue date or amount to find the latest or largest
  charge, then select rows to download or resend them.
- **Projects and workstreams** in an admin console: sort by owner, status or budget to see which work needs attention,
  with a status badge in a `CellTemplate` column.
- **Users in an internal directory**: select several people with the checkbox column, then run one bulk action such
  as deactivating accounts. The count line shows "3 selected" while the action is prepared.
- **Orders in a back office**: sort by total to find large orders, and use Shift + click to select a run of
  consecutive rows for a batch refund or export.
- **Export and job history** in a developer tool: list past runs with their status and duration, sorted by the column
  the person cares about, without any editing.

## When not to use

- **An order that people set by hand**, such as a release queue or a pinned list of priorities: use `ReorderableList`,
  because a column sort cannot express a custom order.
- **Events in time order**, such as an audit trail or an incident log: use `Timeline`, which shows the sequence and
  the gaps between events.
- **Narrowing rows by fields and search text**: put a `FilterToolbar` above the table and pass only the matching rows.
  The table sorts the rows it receives; it does not filter them.
- **Nested records**, such as folders that contain files: use `TreeView`, which expands and collapses each level.
- **Editing cells in place like a spreadsheet**: this table is read-only. Use a form built from `Input` and `Select`.

## Usage

Columns are declared in XAML. Each column reads its cell value through `Binding`, and the table sorts on that value
unless the column has a separate sort value.

```xml
<arc:Table Caption="Projects"
                       ItemsSource="{Binding Projects}"
                       ItemNameOne="project"
                       ItemNameOther="projects"
                       SortKey="Budget"
                       SortDirection="Descending">
    <arc:Table.Columns>
        <arc:DataTableColumn Header="Project" Key="Name" Binding="{Binding Name}" />
        <arc:DataTableColumn Header="Owner" Binding="{Binding Owner}" IsSortable="False" />
        <arc:DataTableColumn Header="Budget" Key="Budget" Binding="{Binding Budget}" IsNumeric="True" />
    </arc:Table.Columns>
</arc:Table>
```

`Table` derives from Avalonia's `TemplatedControl`. It does not build on `ItemsControl` or `DataGrid`: it
draws its header, rows and count line itself. Cells are text by default, which keeps a row cheap to draw, and a
column that needs more than text sets `CellTemplate`.

### Anatomy

1. **Caption** (`Caption`): the table's accessible name. It is not drawn, so write a noun phrase such as
   "Invoices for October 2026".
2. **Header row**: 44 px tall including its 1 px rule. Header labels use the medium weight. A sortable header is a
   button; a column with `IsSortable="False"` is a plain label. The sorted column's cells carry the muted column tint.
3. **Select all checkbox** (`IsSelectable`, `SelectAllLabel`): a 44 px checkbox column at the start of the header, with
   8 px extra inset before the first column. It shows a mixed state when only some rows are selected.
4. **Body rows**: 52 px tall with a 1 px divider in the subtle border color and 16 px inline cell padding. `IsNumeric`
   columns align right. Hover fills the row, and the selection fill eases in on the standard tween at full motion.
5. **Count line** (`ItemNameOne`, `ItemNameOther`, `SelectedNoun`): a 44 px footer shown only when `IsSelectable` is
   true. It reads "6 projects" with no selection and "2 selected" with one. The text is muted until a row is selected.
6. **Clear selection** (`ClearSelectionLabel`): a 30 px ghost button in the footer, shown only while rows are selected.
7. **Empty row** (`EmptyMessage`): 120 px tall, in the muted text color.
8. **Loading veil** (`IsLoading`, `LoadingMessage`): covers the rows below the header with the surface color at 60%
   opacity, an 18 px spinner and the message in the muted color.
9. **Frame**: the surface background, a 1 px border in the border color and the control corner radius. Below 560 px
   of table width the table scrolls horizontally rather than squeezing its columns.

### Columns and sorting

The header is the default sort id, so `SortKey` and the sort events report `Header` unless you set `Key`. Choose the
property that fits the data:

| Column property | Use it when |
|---|---|
| `Binding` | The value is a property of the row item and a binding is enough. |
| `ValueSelector` or `DataTableColumn.Create<T>` | The app is published with AOT or trimming, or you prefer typed code without bindings. |
| `SortBinding` or `SortValueSelector` | The displayed text is not the value to sort by, such as a formatted amount that should sort as a number. |
| `Comparer` | The order is domain specific, such as release versions. It orders ascending; empty values still go last. |
| `IsSortable="False"` | The column is descriptive, such as a free-text note. |
| `IsNumeric="True"` | The column holds amounts or counts and should right-align. Leave it unset to detect numeric columns. |
| `Width` | A pixel width (`Width="120"`) keeps a column steady; `*` shares the space left over. |

Text sorts by natural order (digit runs compare as numbers, so "Item 2" comes before "Item 10"), numbers numerically
and dates by their own order. Empty values sort last in both directions.

### Selection

Set `IsSelectable` to show a checkbox column. Clicking a row selects it, Shift + click selects every row between the
last toggled row and the clicked one, and the header checkbox selects or clears every row. `SelectedItems` is
two-way, and the table updates a bound mutable list in place.

Set `SelectsOnRowClick="False"` when a row click should do something else, such as opening the row's details: only the
checkbox cell then selects, and clicks on the rest of the row reach your own handlers. The keyboard selects the same
way in both modes.

```xml
<arc:Table ItemsSource="{Binding Projects}"
                       IsSelectable="True"
                       SelectedItems="{Binding SelectedProjects, Mode=TwoWay}">
    <arc:Table.Columns>
        <arc:DataTableColumn Header="Project" Binding="{Binding Name}" />
    </arc:Table.Columns>
</arc:Table>
```

Selection follows the row item, or the key from `RowKeySelector` when you set it. Set `RowKeySelector` when a refresh
creates new objects for the same records, so the selection and the row motion keep following the same record.

### Cell content and formatting

Use `Formatter` for text, or `CellTemplate` for custom content such as a status badge. A `Formatter` receives the raw
value and returns the text, so pass a culture to it for amounts and dates. `StringFormat` is the simpler option for a
standard or composite format. When both are set, `Formatter` wins, and a null value shows an en dash.

```csharp
var table = new Table { ItemsSource = projects, Caption = "Projects" };
table.Columns.Add(DataTableColumn.Create<Project>("Project", p => p.Name));
table.Columns.Add(DataTableColumn.Create<Project>("Budget", p => p.Budget, key: "Budget"));
table.Columns[1].Formatter = value => value is decimal amount ? amount.ToString("C0", CultureInfo.GetCultureInfo("en-US")) : "-";
table.Columns.Add(new DataTableColumn("Status", p => ((Project)p).Status)
{
    CellTemplate = new FuncDataTemplate<Project>((_, _) => new StatusPill())
});
```

Rows are recycled as the person scrolls, so a template control must read its content from the data context whenever
it changes. The status badge in the demos does this in `OnDataContextChanged`:

```csharp
public sealed record Project(string Name, string Owner, string Status, decimal Budget, DateOnly Due);

private sealed class StatusPill : Border
{
    private readonly TextBlock _text = new() { FontSize = 12 };

    public StatusPill()
    {
        Child = _text;
        Padding = new Thickness(8, 2);
        CornerRadius = new CornerRadius(999);
        HorizontalAlignment = HorizontalAlignment.Left;
    }

    protected override void OnDataContextChanged(EventArgs e)
    {
        base.OnDataContextChanged(e);
        _text.Text = (DataContext as Project)?.Status ?? string.Empty;
    }
}
```

### Sorting and events

Click a sortable header to sort ascending, and again to sort descending; a new column always starts ascending. With
`IsSortClearable` a third click clears the sort and returns the rows to the source order. `SortChanged` reports every
user sort and every call to `Sort`, and `SelectionChanged` reports user changes to the selection. `SortColumn`,
`SortKey` and `SortDirection` are two-way, so a view model can set or read the sort.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.TableSortedFromCodeDemo">
    <arc:Table x:Name="Table" SortKey="Budget" SortDirection="Descending" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using System.Globalization;
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class TableSortedFromCodeDemo : UserControl
{
    private sealed record Project(string Name, string Owner, string Status, decimal Budget, DateOnly Due);

    private static readonly CultureInfo s_en = CultureInfo.GetCultureInfo("en-US");

    private static readonly Project[] s_projects =
    [
        new("Atlas redesign", "Mina Park", "Active", 42000, new DateOnly(2026, 11, 14)),
        new("Billing migration", "Theo Walsh", "Review", 18500, new DateOnly(2026, 10, 30)),
        new("Checkout v3", "Ana Ruiz", "Active", 126000, new DateOnly(2027, 1, 9)),
        new("Docs search", "Kai Moreno", "Paused", 9600, new DateOnly(2026, 12, 2)),
        new("Edge caching", "Lee Chen", "Done", 31250, new DateOnly(2026, 9, 18)),
        new("Field reports", "Ivy Brooks", "Active", 57800, new DateOnly(2026, 11, 28))
    ];

    public TableSortedFromCodeDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Table.ItemsSource = s_projects;
        Table.Columns.Add(DataTableColumn.Create<Project>("Project", p => p.Name));
        Table.Columns.Add(new DataTableColumn("Budget", p => ((Project)p).Budget) { Key = "Budget", Formatter = Money });
        Table.Columns.Add(new DataTableColumn("Owner", p => ((Project)p).Owner) { IsSortable = false });
    }

    private static string Money(object? value) => value is decimal amount ? amount.ToString("C0", s_en) : "–";

```

```csharp
table.SortChanged += (_, e) => status.Text = e.Column is null
    ? "Sort cleared"
    : $"Sorted by {e.Column.Header}, {e.Direction}";
table.SelectionChanged += (_, e) => status.Text = $"{e.SelectedItems.Count} selected";
table.Sort(table.Columns[1], DataTableSortDirection.Ascending);
```

### Binding to a view model

The view model owns the rows, the sort and the selection; the table reflects them. The table sorts the rows it is
given, so the view model sets `SortKey` and `SortDirection` and reacts to the selection instead of sorting its own
collection. The example uses CommunityToolkit.Mvvm.

```csharp
public sealed record Invoice(string Number, string Customer, decimal Amount, DateOnly Issued);

public interface IInvoiceService
{
    Task<IReadOnlyList<Invoice>> ListAsync();
    Task ResendAsync(IReadOnlyList<string> numbers);
}

public partial class InvoicesViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    private readonly IInvoiceService _invoices;

    public InvoicesViewModel(IInvoiceService invoices) => _invoices = invoices;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private ObservableCollection<Invoice> _rows = [];

    [ObservableProperty]
    private ObservableCollection<Invoice> _selectedRows = [];

    [ObservableProperty]
    private string? _sortKey = "Issued";

    [ObservableProperty]
    private DataTableSortDirection _sortDirection = DataTableSortDirection.Descending;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private bool _isBusy;

    [RelayCommand]
    private async Task RefreshAsync()
    {
        IsBusy = true;
        try
        {
            Rows = new ObservableCollection<Invoice>(await _invoices.ListAsync());
        }
        finally
        {
            IsBusy = false;
        }
    }

    [RelayCommand(CanExecute = nameof(HasSelection))]
    private Task ResendAsync() => _invoices.ResendAsync(SelectedRows.Select(r => r.Number).ToList());

    private bool HasSelection => SelectedRows.Count > 0;
}
```

```xml
<arc:Table Caption="Invoices for October 2026"
                       ItemsSource="{Binding Rows}"
                       IsLoading="{Binding IsBusy}"
                       IsSelectable="True"
                       ItemNameOne="invoice"
                       ItemNameOther="invoices"
                       SortKey="{Binding SortKey, Mode=TwoWay}"
                       SortDirection="{Binding SortDirection, Mode=TwoWay}"
                       SelectedItems="{Binding SelectedRows, Mode=TwoWay}">
    <arc:Table.Columns>
        <arc:DataTableColumn Header="Number" Key="Number" Binding="{Binding Number}" />
        <arc:DataTableColumn Header="Customer" Binding="{Binding Customer}" />
        <arc:DataTableColumn Header="Amount" Key="Amount" Binding="{Binding Amount}" IsNumeric="True"
                             StringFormat="C0" />
        <arc:DataTableColumn Header="Issued" Key="Issued" Binding="{Binding Issued}" StringFormat="d" />
    </arc:Table.Columns>
</arc:Table>
```

- `SortKey` and `SortDirection` are two-way: a sort the person chooses writes back, and the default "Issued"
  descending from the view model applies when the table loads.
- `SelectedItems` is two-way and needs an `ObservableCollection<Invoice>` target. `ResendAsync` reads the same list.
- Bind `IsLoading` to the busy flag so the veil covers the rows while the request runs.
- Rebuild the collection on refresh, or change an existing `ObservableCollection<T>`. The selection follows the row
  key, so it survives a refresh when the rows are the same objects or `RowKeySelector` returns the same key.
- Compiled bindings need `x:DataType` on the view (the examples here leave it out for brevity).

### Data shape and performance

Each row is one record with the same fields for every column. The table sorts the rows it is given on the client, so
it suits a result set that is already loaded. Only the rows near the viewport are realized, which keeps the
5,000-row demo below scrollable, and sorting reorders the indices rather than the row controls.

Sorting runs on every change to the source or the sort, so keep the sort value cheap: sort by a stored number or
`DateOnly`, not by a string built from several fields. For a result set in the tens of thousands, load one page at a
time and show `Pagination` under the table, so the table never holds more rows than a page needs.

### Empty and loading states

`EmptyMessage` shows when there are no rows, and `IsLoading` covers the rows with a veil named by `LoadingMessage`.
Write the empty message as a reason and a next step, especially after a filter.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.TableEmptyAndLoadingDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12">
        <arc:Switch x:Name="LoadingSwitch" Content="Loading" />
        <arc:Table EmptyMessage="No projects match these filters"
                               IsLoading="{Binding #LoadingSwitch.IsChecked}">
            <arc:DataTableColumn Header="Project" />
            <arc:DataTableColumn Header="Owner" />
            <arc:DataTableColumn Header="Status" />
            <arc:DataTableColumn Header="Budget" />
            <arc:DataTableColumn Header="Due" />
        </arc:Table>
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```xml
<arc:Table EmptyMessage="No projects match these filters"
                       IsLoading="{Binding IsBusy}" />
```

### Five thousand rows

The 5,000-row demo sets `IsSortClearable` and a 420 px maximum height, so the table scrolls inside its own frame and
the header stays in place.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.TableFiveThousandRowsDemo">
    <arc:Table x:Name="Table"
                           IsSelectable="True"
                           IsSortClearable="True"
                           MaxHeight="420"
                           ItemNameOne="workstream"
                           ItemNameOther="workstreams" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using System.Globalization;
using Avalonia;
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Controls.Templates;
using Avalonia.Layout;
using TKCode.Arc.DesignTokens;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class TableFiveThousandRowsDemo : UserControl
{
    private sealed record Project(string Name, string Owner, string Status, decimal Budget, DateOnly Due);

    private static readonly CultureInfo s_en = CultureInfo.GetCultureInfo("en-US");
    private static readonly string[] s_owners = ["Mina Park", "Theo Walsh", "Ana Ruiz", "Kai Moreno", "Lee Chen", "Ivy Brooks"];
    private static readonly string[] s_status = ["Active", "Paused", "Review", "Done"];

    public TableFiveThousandRowsDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        var random = new Random(7);
        var rows = new List<Project>();
        for (var i = 0; i < 5000; i++)
        {
            rows.Add(new Project($"Workstream {i + 1:0000}", s_owners[random.Next(s_owners.Length)], s_status[random.Next(s_status.Length)],
                random.Next(1, 400) * 250, new DateOnly(2026, 1, 1).AddDays(random.Next(0, 540))));
        }
        Table.ItemsSource = rows;
        AddProjectColumns(Table);
    }

    private static void AddProjectColumns(Table table)
    {
        table.Columns.Add(DataTableColumn.Create<Project>("Project", p => p.Name));
        table.Columns.Add(DataTableColumn.Create<Project>("Owner", p => p.Owner));
        table.Columns.Add(new DataTableColumn("Status", p => ((Project)p).Status) { CellTemplate = new FuncDataTemplate<Project>((_, _) => new StatusPill()) });
        table.Columns.Add(new DataTableColumn("Budget", p => ((Project)p).Budget) { Formatter = Money });
        table.Columns.Add(new DataTableColumn("Due", p => ((Project)p).Due) { Formatter = v => v is DateOnly d ? d.ToString("MMM d, yyyy", s_en) : "–" });
    }

    private static string Money(object? value) => value is decimal amount ? amount.ToString("C0", s_en) : "–";

    /// <summary>A status badge that follows its data context (cells are recycled between rows).</summary>
    private sealed class StatusPill : Border
    {
        private readonly TextBlock _text = new() { FontSize = 12, VerticalAlignment = VerticalAlignment.Center };
        private IDisposable? _fill;
        private IDisposable? _fore;

        public StatusPill()
        {
            Child = _text;
            Padding = new Thickness(8, 2);
            CornerRadius = new CornerRadius(999);
            HorizontalAlignment = HorizontalAlignment.Left;
            VerticalAlignment = VerticalAlignment.Center;
        }

        protected override void OnDataContextChanged(EventArgs e)
        {
            base.OnDataContextChanged(e);
            var status = (DataContext as Project)?.Status ?? string.Empty;
            _text.Text = status;
            var (fill, fore) = status switch
            {
                "Active" => (ArcDesignTokenKind.SuccessSubtle, ArcDesignTokenKind.Success),
                "Paused" => (ArcDesignTokenKind.WarningSubtle, ArcDesignTokenKind.Warning),
                "Review" => (ArcDesignTokenKind.AccentSubtle, ArcDesignTokenKind.AccentStrong),
                _ => (ArcDesignTokenKind.SurfaceMuted, ArcDesignTokenKind.TextSecondary)
            };
            _fill?.Dispose();
            _fore?.Dispose();
            _fill = ArcTokens.Bind(this, BackgroundProperty, fill);
            _fore = ArcTokens.Bind(_text, TextBlock.ForegroundProperty, fore);
        }
    }
}
```

### Narrow

Below 620 px the rows fold into two lines, the row height grows to 64 px, and the header becomes a strip of sort pills
(32 px tall) with Select all pinned at the start. Clicking a pill sorts by its column and scrolls the pill into view.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"

                           IsSelectable="True"
                           Width="360"
                           HorizontalAlignment="Left" />
</UserControl>
```
