### Example: Export history with a selection

A developer tool lists the exports a team has produced. Each export is a file name, and the operator selects the ones
to download or delete. The rows are plain strings, so the column has no `Binding` and each cell shows the row item
itself; in an app the column would bind to a property such as `FileName`. The names are sorted ascending so the
exports group by type, and two rows are selected, so the count line reads "2 selected" and Clear selection appears.

![An export history table with two rows selected and the Clear selection action](https://docs.tkcode.si/shots/Docs/Tables/Table/images/ExportHistory.webp)

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             xmlns:generic="using:System.Collections.Generic"
             Width="560">
    <arc:Table Caption="Export history"
                           ItemNameOne="export"
                           ItemNameOther="exports"
                           IsSelectable="True"
                           SortKey="Export"
                           SortDirection="Ascending">
        <arc:Table.ItemsSource>
            <generic:List x:TypeArguments="x:String">
                <x:String>invoices_2026_08.csv</x:String>
                <x:String>invoices_2026_09.csv</x:String>
                <x:String>usage_2026_09.csv</x:String>
                <x:String>payouts_2026_q3.csv</x:String>
                <x:String>audit_log_2026_10_14.csv</x:String>
            </generic:List>
        </arc:Table.ItemsSource>
        <arc:Table.SelectedItems>
            <generic:List x:TypeArguments="x:Object">
                <x:String>invoices_2026_09.csv</x:String>
                <x:String>usage_2026_09.csv</x:String>
            </generic:List>
        </arc:Table.SelectedItems>
        <arc:Table.Columns>
            <arc:DataTableColumn Header="Export" Width="*" />
        </arc:Table.Columns>
    </arc:Table>
</UserControl>
```

### Content guidelines

Table text is scanned, not read. Keep headers to one or two nouns and let the cells carry the detail.

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| Total amount in USD (incl. tax) | Total |
| Date the invoice was issued on | Issued |
| 5 items are currently selected | 5 selected |
| No data | No invoices match these filters |
| Loading... please wait | Loading invoices |
| Select all records on this page | Select all invoices |


### Best practices

**Do**

- Set `Key` on columns whose header is a display label, so the sort id that events and the view model store stays
  stable when the label is translated.
- Set `IsNumeric="True"` on amount and count columns so the digits right-align.
- Set `RowKeySelector` when a refresh creates new objects for the same records, so the selection survives it.
- Give the table at least 560 px, the width below which it scrolls sideways, and test it below 620 px, where it
  folds into the compact layout.

**Avoid**

- Sorting by a formatted string such as "$1,200" without `SortBinding` or `SortValueSelector`: the text is compared by
  its digit runs, so "$1,200" sorts before "$900".
- Loading a very large data set without `Pagination`: the rows stay in memory and a sort runs over all of them on
  each click.
- Relying on color alone for a status. Keep the badge text in the cell so the status reads without color.
- Expecting the table to edit rows. It is read-only and does not track edits; open a form instead.

### Common questions

**Why does a numeric column sort as text?** The cell value is a string, usually because the binding returns a
formatted value. Bind the number, or set `SortBinding` (or `SortValueSelector`) to the numeric property.

**How do I clear the sort from code?** Call `Sort(null, DataTableSortDirection.None)`. The rows return to the source
order and `SortChanged` reports a null column.

**How do I select the rows that match a filter?** Set `ItemsSource` to the filtered rows and call `SelectAll()`, or
bind `SelectedItems` to the matching items. `ClearSelection()` clears the selection and moves focus to Select all.

**Can the table filter rows?** No. It sorts and selects the rows it receives. Filter in the view model or with a
`FilterToolbar`, and pass the filtered collection as `ItemsSource`.

## API reference

### Table

Arc's sortable data table: compare structured records with sortable columns. Click a header (or press Enter / Space on it) to sort ascending, again for descending; rows slide to their new places on a smooth spring and the sort arrow flips on a snappy one. `IsSelectable` adds a checkbox column, row-click selection, Shift range selection, Escape to clear and a count line with Clear selection. Rows are drawn as light text cells, virtualized for thousands of records, sorted by index (never by container), and the header sticks to the top of the visible area. Below 620px rows fold into two lines and the header becomes a strip of sort pills, as in Arc.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ItemsSource` | `IEnumerable?` | `null` | Row items (any enumerable; `INotifyCollectionChanged` sources are followed). |
| `SortColumn` | `DataTableColumn?` | `null` | The sorted column (two-way). Setting a column while `SortDirection` is None sorts ascending. |
| `SortKey` | `string?` | `null` | The sorted column's `EffectiveKey` (two-way, for view models). |
| `SortDirection` | `DataTableSortDirection` | `None` | Sort direction of the sorted column (two-way): None, Ascending or Descending. |
| `IsSortClearable` | `bool` | `false` | When true a third click on a sorted header clears the sort (Arc toggles between ascending and descending). |
| `IsSelectable` | `bool` | `false` | Adds the checkbox column, row-click selection and the count line with Clear selection. |
| `SelectsOnRowClick` | `bool` | `true` | When true (the default) a click anywhere on a row toggles it; when false only the checkbox cell does, and clicks on the rest of the row are left to the app. Keyboard selection is the same either way. |
| `SelectedItems` | `IList?` | `null` | Selected row items in display order (two-way). A bound mutable list is updated in place. |
| `RowKeySelector` | `Func<object, object>?` | `null` | Row identity (Arc `rowKey`); defaults to the item itself. Selection and row motion follow keys across source changes. |
| `Caption` | `string` | `"Data table"` | Accessible name of the table. |
| `EmptyMessage` | `string` | `"No rows to show"` | Text shown when there are no rows (default "No rows to show"). |
| `IsLoading` | `bool` | `false` | Shows a spinner over the body (in place of the empty message when there are no rows). |
| `LoadingMessage` | `string` | `"Loading rows"` | Text shown with the loading spinner (default "Loading rows"). |
| `ItemNameOne` | `string` | `"row"` | Singular noun of the count line, as in "1 project". |
| `ItemNameOther` | `string` | `"rows"` | Plural noun of the count line, as in "6 projects". |
| `SelectedNoun` | `string` | `"selected"` | Word for the selected rows in the count line, as in "2 selected" (default "selected"). |
| `SelectAllLabel` | `string` | `"Select all rows"` | Accessible name of the select-all checkbox in the header (default "Select all rows"). |
| `ClearSelectionLabel` | `string` | `"Clear selection"` | Text of the Clear selection action in the count line (default "Clear selection"). |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `SortChanged` | `DataTableSortChangedEventArgs` | Raised when the user sorts (header click or keyboard) or `Sort` is called. |
| `SelectionChanged` | `DataTableSelectionChangedEventArgs` | Raised when the user changes the selection (checkboxes, row clicks, Select all, Clear, Escape). |

Pseudo-classes: `:compact`, `:selectable`, `:loading`, `:empty`, `:has-selection`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

### DataTableColumn

One column of a `Table`. The cell value comes from `ValueSelector` or `Binding` (compiled against the table's item type in XAML); sorting uses `SortValueSelector` / `SortBinding` when given, else the cell value, and `Comparer` when given, else Arc's comparison (numbers numerically, text with natural ordering, empty values last in both directions). Cells are drawn as text; `CellTemplate` hosts custom content.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Header` | `string` | `""` | Column label; also the default `EffectiveKey`. |
| `Key` | `string?` | `null` | Stable id reported by `SortKey` and sort events (defaults to `SortMemberPath`, then `Header`). |
| `SortMemberPath` | `string?` | `null` | Name of the member the column sorts by, reported as the sort key. The sorted value itself comes from `SortBinding`, `SortValueSelector` or the cell value. |
| `IsSortable` | `bool` | `true` | When false the header is a plain label (Arc `sortable: false`). |
| `IsNumeric` | `bool?` | `null` | Right-aligns the column. Null detects it: every non-empty value is a number. |
| `Width` | `GridLength` | `Auto` | Pixel widths are fixed; Auto columns are measured once and held so sorting never reflows them; star columns share the rest. |
| `StringFormat` | `string?` | `null` | Format for cell text: a composite format (`{0:N0} items`) or a format string (`C0`). |
| `CellTemplate` | `IDataTemplate?` | `null` | Custom cell content (Arc `render`); the data context is the row item. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

## Accessibility

- The table has its `Caption` as its name and exposes table, header and row roles.
- A sortable header is a button named like "Sort by Budget, currently ascending". The sort direction is part of the
  name, and the header also reports it as its item status (ascending, descending or none).
- The Select all checkbox shows a mixed state when only some rows are selected. Its name is `SelectAllLabel`, which
  defaults to "Select all rows".
- Sort and selection changes are announced in a polite live region without interrupting the current speech, such as
  "Sorted by Budget, ascending", "Sort cleared", "2 of 5 selected" and "Selection cleared".
- The table draws its own focus ring for keyboard focus only, and it suppresses the window's default focus adorner.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Left` / `Right` in a header | Move to the previous or next header control; Select all is the first one when selection is on |
| `Home` / `End` in a header | Move to the first or last header control |
| `Down` in Select all | Move to the first row's checkbox (only when `IsSelectable` is true and there are rows) |
| `Enter` / `Space` on a sortable header | Sort ascending, then descending; with `IsSortClearable` a third press clears the sort |
| `Enter` / `Space` on Select all | Select every row, or clear the selection when every row is already selected |
| `Up` / `Down` in the rows | Move to the previous or next row; `Up` from the first row returns to Select all |
| `Home` / `End` in the rows | Move to the first or last row |
| `PageUp` / `PageDown` in the rows | Move by about one screen of rows |
| `Enter` / `Space` on a row | Toggle the row's selection (only when `IsSelectable` is true) |
| `Shift` + `Enter` / `Space` on a row | Toggle the row, and give the rows from the last toggled row to this one the same new state |
| `Shift` + click on a row | Give the rows from the last toggled row to the clicked row the clicked row's new state |
| `Escape` | Clear the selection when rows are selected; with Clear selection focused, focus returns to Select all |

## Motion

- When the sort changes, surviving rows slide from where they were drawn to their new places on a smooth spring, and
  the sort arrow flips on a snappy spring.
- The selection count rolls to its new value, and Clear selection fades in with a short blur.
- Reduced motion reorders rows at once and only fades the count. Off jumps straight to the final state.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sort changes | Rows slide to their new places on a smooth spring; the sort arrow flips | Rows reorder at once | Immediate |
| Selection count changes | The count rolls to the new value | The count fades | Immediate |

## Related

- `TreeView` for records that nest, such as folders with children.
- `ReorderableList` when the user sets the order by dragging, not by a column.
- `FilterToolbar` to narrow the rows by fields and search before they reach the table.
- `Pagination` to split large record sets into pages.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `ReorderableList` | The person orders the items by dragging them, and no column describes the order |
| `Timeline` | The records are events in time order and the sequence matters more than the fields |
| `FilterToolbar` | The rows need filters or search fields above them before they are compared |
| `Pagination` | The result set is too large to load at once, and each page is a separate query |
| `TreeView` | The records nest, and people open and close each level |
| `CodeBlock` | The value is a snippet to read and copy, not a set of comparable records |

---

# Tree table

> A table with nested rows, tri-state selection, hierarchy-preserving sort, and lazy-loaded children.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/tree-table

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.TreeTableBudgetDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12" MaxWidth="720">
        <arc:TreeTable x:Name="Table"
                       Caption="Cloud spend"
                       IsSelectable="True"
                       SelectionChanged="OnSelectionChanged" />
        <TextBlock x:Name="Footer"
                   Text="Select rows to total their monthly spend."
                   FontSize="14"
                   TextWrapping="Wrap"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using System.Globalization;
using Avalonia;
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class TreeTableBudgetDemo : UserControl
{
    private sealed record Spend(string Id, string Name, string Owner, int Resources, decimal Monthly, IReadOnlyList<Spend>? Children = null);

    private static readonly CultureInfo s_en = CultureInfo.GetCultureInfo("en-US");

    private static readonly Spend[] s_spend =
    [
        new("platform", "Platform", "Mira Chen", 38, 18420,
        [
            new("compute", "Compute", "Mira Chen", 22, 11200,
            [
                new("compute-web", "Web servers", "Sam Ortiz", 12, 6300),
                new("compute-jobs", "Batch jobs", "Lee Park", 10, 4900),
            ]),
            new("storage", "Storage", "Noor Ali", 11, 4120),
            new("network", "Network", "Kay Dube", 5, 3100),
        ]),
        new("data", "Data", "Theo Walsh", 24, 12640,
        [
            new("warehouse", "Warehouse", "Theo Walsh", 9, 7800),
            new("streams", "Event streams", "Ana Ruiz", 15, 4840),
        ]),
        new("security", "Security", "Ivy Brooks", 9, 3280),
    ];

    public TreeTableBudgetDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Table.KeySelector = item => ((Spend)item).Id;
        Table.RowLabelSelector = item => ((Spend)item).Name;
        Table.ChildrenSelector = item => ((Spend)item).Children;
        Table.Columns.Add(TreeTableColumn.Create<Spend>("Name", s => s.Name));
        Table.Columns.Add(new TreeTableColumn { Header = "Owner", ValueSelector = s => ((Spend)s).Owner, HideBelow = 560 });
        Table.Columns.Add(new TreeTableColumn
        {
            Header = "Resources", ValueSelector = s => ((Spend)s).Resources, Width = new GridLength(104), IsEndAligned = true, HideBelow = 420
        });
        Table.Columns.Add(new TreeTableColumn
        {
            Header = "Monthly", ValueSelector = s => ((Spend)s).Monthly, Width = new GridLength(112), IsEndAligned = true,
            Formatter = value => value is decimal amount ? amount.ToString("C0", s_en) : string.Empty
        });
        Table.ItemsSource = s_spend;
        Table.ExpandedKeys = new object[] { "platform" };
    }

    private void OnSelectionChanged(object? sender, TreeTableSelectionChangedEventArgs e)
    {
        // Parents roll up their children, so only leaves are summed.
        var leaves = e.SelectedItems.Cast<Spend>().Where(s => s.Children is not { Count: > 0 }).ToList();
        Footer.Text = leaves.Count == 0
            ? "Select rows to total their monthly spend."
            : $"{leaves.Count} {(leaves.Count == 1 ? "line" : "lines")} selected · {leaves.Sum(s => s.Monthly).ToString("C0", s_en)} per month";
    }
}
```

## When to use

`TreeTable` shows records that nest and share columns. A row can open to reveal its children, every row keeps the
same columns, and a parent can roll up what is under it. People expand the branches they care about, sort within a
branch, and select a whole branch with one checkbox.

- **File listings with size, owner and date columns**: folders open to their files, and sorting by size orders the
  files inside each folder without pulling them out of it.
- **Budgets and cost reports** that roll up through nested rows: a department holds teams, a team holds line items,
  and a footer can total the rows a person selected.
- **Org charts and permission matrices**: teams contain people, and each row carries an owner, a role or a count.
- **Large trees that load on demand**: a row can be marked as having children that are not loaded yet, and the table
  fetches them the first time the row opens, with a retry row when the request fails.
- **Bulk actions on a hierarchy**: checking a parent checks everything under it, and a parent shows a mixed state
  when only some of its children are checked.

## When not to use

- **A navigation tree without columns**: use `TreeView`, which draws one label per node and virtualizes thousands of
  rows.
- **Flat records that people compare by column**: use `Table`. A tree table adds indent and a
  chevron to the first column for no benefit when nothing nests.
- **A spreadsheet that people edit cell by cell**: use `DataGrid`, which has range selection and inline editing.
- **Items that open into free-form content**: use `Accordion`. A tree table opens into more rows with the same
  columns.
- **A few thousand rows open at once**: every visible row exists and animates. Keep an expanded tree to a few hundred
  rows and load the deeper levels on demand.

## Usage

Set `ItemsSource` to the top-level rows and `ChildrenSelector` (a delegate, set from code) to return the children of a
row. A row whose selector returns an empty list is a leaf. Add columns to `Columns`; the first column shown holds the
tree.

```xml
<arc:TreeTable Caption="Files"
               ItemsSource="{Binding Files}"
               IsSelectable="True"
               MaxHeight="480">
    <arc:TreeTableColumn Header="Name" Binding="{Binding Name}" />
    <arc:TreeTableColumn Header="Size" Binding="{Binding SizeMb}" StringFormat="{}{0} MB"
                         Width="96" IsEndAligned="True" />
    <arc:TreeTableColumn Header="Owner" Binding="{Binding Owner}" HideBelow="520" />
</arc:TreeTable>
```

`TreeTable` derives from Avalonia's `TemplatedControl`. Like Arc, it does not virtualize: every visible row is a real
row that grows in, leaves and animates. Selectors such as `ChildrenSelector` and `KeySelector` take a delegate, so
they are set from code; the rest of the table can be written in XAML.

```csharp
var table = new TreeTable
{
    ItemsSource = files,
    ChildrenSelector = item => ((FileNode)item).Children,
    KeySelector = item => ((FileNode)item).Path,
    RowLabelSelector = item => ((FileNode)item).Name,
    IsSelectable = true
};
table.Columns.Add(TreeTableColumn.Create<FileNode>("Name", f => f.Name));
table.Columns.Add(new TreeTableColumn { Header = "Size", ValueSelector = f => ((FileNode)f).SizeMb, IsEndAligned = true });
```

### Anatomy

1. **Frame**: the surface background with a 1 px border in the border color and the panel corner radius. The table
   fills its width. `MaxHeight` caps the whole table: the header stays pinned and the body scrolls.
2. **Header**: 40 px tall, in the small type size and the muted text color, with a 1 px rule below it. A sortable
   header is a button; the first column's header also holds the expand all toggle.
3. **Row**: 44 px tall with a hairline below it. Hover and focus fill the row with the muted surface color, and a
   selected row uses the accent subtle color.
4. **Tree cell**: the first column shown. It starts 10 px in, indents 20 px for each level, and has a 24 px chevron
   slot before the content. A leaf keeps the empty slot so labels line up.
5. **Indent guides**: a 1 px line through the chevron column of every ancestor. The guide of the branch under the
   pointer or the focused row darkens.
6. **Cells**: one per other shown column, with 12 px inline padding. An end-aligned column right-aligns its text and
   sets figures in tabular width.
7. **Checkbox column** (`IsSelectable`): 44 px wide, with a select all checkbox in the header.
8. **Loading and retry rows**: under a parent that is fetching, a spinner row with skeleton bars in the other
   columns, or a "Couldn't load" row with a Retry button.

### Columns

`TreeTableColumn` defines a column. The cell value comes from `ValueSelector` (a delegate, safe for AOT) or `Binding`,
and `Formatter` or `StringFormat` turns it into text. For anything other than text, set `CellTemplate`; its data
context is the row item.

| Property | Use it to |
|---|---|
| `Header`, `Key` | Label the column, and name it for `SortKey` (the header is the key when `Key` is not set) |
| `Width` | Set a pixel width (`96`) or a share of the rest (`2*`); the default is `1*`, which shrinks and truncates |
| `IsEndAligned` | Right-align numbers and amounts |
| `HideBelow` | Hide the column while the table is narrower than this many pixels |
| `SortValueSelector`, `IsSortable` | Sort by something other than the displayed text, or turn sorting off |

Columns share one set of tracks, so they line up through every level. When the table gets narrower than a column's
`HideBelow`, the column is removed from the header and every row; the tree column always stays.

### Row identity

`KeySelector` returns the identity of a row. `ExpandedKeys` and `SelectedKeys` hold these keys, so use something
stable such as an id or a path. Without a `KeySelector` the row item itself is the key.

### Expanding and collapsing

A click on a parent row, a click on its chevron, Enter, and the arrow keys all toggle it. `ExpandedKeys` is two-way:
set it to open rows from code or bind it to a view model, and read it to save the open state. The header's toggle
opens every row whose children are loaded, or closes them all.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.TreeTableControlledDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12" MaxWidth="720">
        <WrapPanel ItemSpacing="12" LineSpacing="12">
            <arc:Button Content="Expand all" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Click="OnExpandAll" />
            <arc:Button Content="Collapse all" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Click="OnCollapseAll" />
            <arc:Button Content="Sort by cost" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Click="OnSortCost" />
            <arc:Button Content="Select Engineering" Variant="Ghost" Size="Small" Click="OnSelectEngineering" />
        </WrapPanel>
        <arc:TreeTable x:Name="Table"
                       Caption="Teams"
                       IsSelectable="True" />
        <TextBlock x:Name="State"
                   FontSize="14"
                   TextWrapping="Wrap"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia;
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class TreeTableControlledDemo : UserControl
{
    private sealed record Team(string Id, string Name, int Cost, IReadOnlyList<Team>? Children = null);

    private static readonly Team[] s_teams =
    [
        new("design", "Design", 30, [new("brand", "Brand", 10), new("product-design", "Product design", 20)]),
        new("eng", "Engineering", 90, [new("backend", "Backend", 60), new("apps", "Apps", 30)]),
        new("ops", "Operations", 15)
    ];

    public TreeTableControlledDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Table.KeySelector = item => ((Team)item).Id;
        Table.ChildrenSelector = item => ((Team)item).Children;
        Table.Columns.Add(TreeTableColumn.Create<Team>("Team", t => t.Name));
        Table.Columns.Add(new TreeTableColumn { Header = "Cost", ValueSelector = t => ((Team)t).Cost, Width = new GridLength(96), IsEndAligned = true, StringFormat = "${0}k" });
        Table.ItemsSource = s_teams;
        Table.RowExpandedChanged += (_, _) => Report();
        Table.SelectionChanged += (_, _) => Report();
        Table.SortChanged += (_, _) => Report();
        Report();
    }

    private void Report() =>
        State.Text = $"Expanded: {Format(Table.ExpandedKeys)}  ·  Selected: {Format(Table.SelectedKeys)}  ·  Sort: {Table.SortKey ?? "none"} {Table.SortDirection}";

    private static string Format(IReadOnlyList<object>? keys) => keys is { Count: > 0 } ? string.Join(", ", keys) : "none";

    private void OnExpandAll(object? sender, Avalonia.Interactivity.RoutedEventArgs e) => Table.ExpandAll();

    private void OnCollapseAll(object? sender, Avalonia.Interactivity.RoutedEventArgs e) => Table.CollapseAll();

    private void OnSortCost(object? sender, Avalonia.Interactivity.RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        Table.SortKey = "Cost";
        Table.SortDirection = Table.SortDirection == DataTableSortDirection.Ascending ? DataTableSortDirection.Descending : DataTableSortDirection.Ascending;
        Report();
    }

    private void OnSelectEngineering(object? sender, Avalonia.Interactivity.RoutedEventArgs e) =>
        Table.SelectedKeys = new object[] { "eng", "backend", "apps" };
}
```

```csharp
table.Expand(item);
table.Collapse(item);
table.ExpandAll();          // every row whose children are known
table.CollapseAll();
table.FocusItem(item);      // moves keyboard focus to a visible row
```

### Selection

With `IsSelectable`, each row gets a checkbox. Checking a parent checks everything under it, and a parent whose
children are only partly checked shows the mixed state. `SelectedKeys` always holds a normalized set: a parent is in
it exactly when all its known children are. The select all checkbox is mixed when only some rows are selected.

`SelectionChanged` reports the new keys and the loaded row items. A parent rolls up its children, so a total over
the selection should count only the leaves.

```csharp
table.SelectionChanged += (_, e) =>
{
    var leaves = e.SelectedItems.Cast<Spend>().Where(s => s.Children is not { Count: > 0 });
    footer.Text = $"{leaves.Sum(s => s.Monthly):C0} per month";
};
```

### Sorting

A header with a value cycles ascending, descending, then off. Sorting is hierarchy-safe: the siblings of each parent
are sorted inside that parent, so a child never leaves its branch. Numbers compare as numbers, text with natural
order, and empty values sort last in both directions. `SortKey` and `SortDirection` are two-way, so the sort can be
set from code or saved.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.TreeTableFilesDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12" MaxWidth="720">
        <arc:TreeTable x:Name="Table"
                       Caption="Files"
                       MaxHeight="300"
                       RowActivated="OnRowActivated" />
        <TextBlock x:Name="Status"
                   Text="Click a file, or press Enter on one. Narrow the window to hide the Modified column."
                   FontSize="14"
                   TextWrapping="Wrap"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

### Loading children on demand

Mark a row that has children which are not loaded with `HasChildrenSelector`, and give the table a `ChildrenLoader`.
The first time such a row opens, the table calls the loader and shows a loading row under it. When the task finishes,
the first child takes over the loading row's place. When the task faults, a "Couldn't load" row with a Retry button
appears, `ChildrenLoadFailed` is raised, and Enter on the parent retries. Children that arrive under a checked parent
start checked. A row loads once: opening it again does not fetch again.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.TreeTableLazyLoadingDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12" MaxWidth="720">
        <arc:TreeTable x:Name="Table"
                       Caption="Accounts"
                       ChildrenLoadFailed="OnLoadFailed" />
        <TextBlock x:Name="Status"
                   Text="Open Marketing: its children load on the first expand. Sales fails once; use Retry."
                   FontSize="14"
                   TextWrapping="Wrap"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using System.Collections;
using Avalonia;
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class TreeTableLazyLoadingDemo : UserControl
{
    private sealed record Account(string Id, string Name, int Seats, bool HasChildren = false);

    private int _salesAttempts;

    public TreeTableLazyLoadingDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Table.KeySelector = item => ((Account)item).Id;
        // No ChildrenSelector: every child is loaded on demand.
        Table.HasChildrenSelector = item => ((Account)item).HasChildren;
        Table.ChildrenLoader = LoadAsync;
        Table.Columns.Add(TreeTableColumn.Create<Account>("Account", a => a.Name));
        Table.Columns.Add(new TreeTableColumn { Header = "Seats", ValueSelector = a => ((Account)a).Seats, Width = new GridLength(96), IsEndAligned = true });
        Table.ItemsSource = new[]
        {
            new Account("marketing", "Marketing", 42, HasChildren: true),
            new Account("sales", "Sales", 65, HasChildren: true),
            new Account("legal", "Legal", 8)
        };
    }

    private async Task<IEnumerable?> LoadAsync(object item)
    {
        var account = (Account)item;
        await Task.Delay(900);
        if (account.Id == "sales" && _salesAttempts++ == 0)
        {
            throw new InvalidOperationException("The sales service is not responding.");
        }
        return account.Id switch
        {
            "marketing" => new[] { new Account("brand", "Brand", 14), new Account("growth", "Growth", 19), new Account("events", "Events", 9) },
            _ => new[] { new Account("emea", "EMEA", 28), new Account("amer", "Americas", 37) }
        };
    }

    private void OnLoadFailed(object? sender, TreeTableRowEventArgs e) => Status.Text = $"Couldn't load {((Account)e.Item).Name}: {e.Error?.Message}";
}
```

```csharp
table.HasChildrenSelector = item => ((Account)item).HasChildren;
table.ChildrenLoader = async item => await api.GetChildrenAsync(((Account)item).Id);
```

### Activating a row

A click or Enter on a row without children raises `RowActivated`, which is where you open the file or the record.
A parent row toggles instead.

### Responsive columns

A table adapts to the width it is given, not to the window. Set `HideBelow` on the columns that matter least, such as
an owner or a modified date, and they drop out as the table narrows.

### Example: Cloud spend by team

The demo at the top rolls spend up through three levels. The Owner column hides below 560 px and Resources below
420 px, the Monthly column is end-aligned and formatted as currency, and a footer totals the selected lines.

### Content guidelines

- Keep the tree column's text short. It truncates, and the first column is where people look for a row.
- Put the figure people compare in an end-aligned column with a unit in its header or format, such as `{0} MB`.
- Name rows for assistive technology with `RowLabelSelector`, such as the file or team name; it labels each checkbox.
- Write `EmptyMessage` to say what is missing, such as "No files in this folder".

### Best practices

- Give every row a stable `KeySelector`. Index-based keys break the open state when the data reorders.
- Load deep levels on demand with `ChildrenLoader` rather than preloading thousands of rows.
- Put the hierarchy's rolled-up totals on the parent rows yourself; the table does not compute them.
- Keep `HideBelow` on secondary columns only, so the table never loses the column people read first.
- Set `MaxHeight` on a table that can grow tall, so the header stays in view.

### Common questions

**Why does a parent not open?** A row opens when its selector returns at least one child, or when
`HasChildrenSelector` is true and a `ChildrenLoader` is set. An empty list means a leaf.

**Can a column sort the tree flat?** No. Sorting orders the siblings inside each parent, so the hierarchy never
breaks. Use `Table` for a flat list.

**Why are the expanded rows lost when I reload the data?** `ExpandedKeys` holds keys. If `KeySelector` returns new
values on every load, the rows no longer match. Use ids that survive a reload.

**Does the table total the selection?** No. Use `SelectionChanged` and add up the items you need.

## API reference

### TreeTable

A table whose rows nest. Rows expand and collapse on a spring with indent guides, parents carry tri-state checkboxes (`IsSelectable`), sorting reorders siblings without breaking the hierarchy, and children can load on first expand (`ChildrenLoader`). The first column shown holds the tree. Keyboard follows the treegrid pattern: ↑/↓ move, → opens or enters, ← closes or goes to the parent, Home/End, PageUp/PageDown move ten rows, `*` opens all siblings, Space selects, Enter toggles a parent or activates a leaf, Ctrl/Cmd+A selects all. Rows come from `ItemsSource` and `ChildrenSelector`; each row is identified by `KeySelector` (the item itself when not set), which is what `ExpandedKeys` and `SelectedKeys` hold. Like Arc, rows are not virtualized: every visible row exists and animates, so keep an expanded tree to a few hundred rows and load deeper levels on demand.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ItemsSource` | `IEnumerable?` | `null` | The top-level rows. |
| `ChildrenSelector` | `Func<object, IEnumerable?>?` | `null` | Children of a row item (Arc `children`). Return null when the children are not loaded; an empty list means a leaf. |
| `HasChildrenSelector` | `Func<object, bool>?` | `null` | Marks a row whose children are not loaded yet (Arc `hasChildren`); needs `ChildrenLoader`. |
| `ChildrenLoader` | `Func<object, Task<IEnumerable?>>?` | `null` | Loads the children of a row with `HasChildrenSelector` the first time it expands (Arc `loadChildren`). A faulted task shows a retry row. |
| `KeySelector` | `Func<object, object>?` | `null` | Identifies a row; the keys of `ExpandedKeys` and `SelectedKeys` (Arc `id`). The item itself when not set. |
| `RowLabelSelector` | `Func<object, string?>?` | `null` | Names a row for its checkbox and for assistive technology (Arc `rowLabel`), such as the file or team name. |
| `Caption` | `string` | `"Tree table"` | The accessible name of the table (Arc `label`). |
| `EmptyMessage` | `string` | `"Nothing to show"` | Shown when there are no rows (Arc `emptyState`). |
| `IsSelectable` | `bool` | `false` | Adds a checkbox column. Checking a parent checks everything under it (Arc `selectable`). |
| `ExpandedKeys` | `IReadOnlyList<object>?` | `null` | The keys of the expanded rows (two-way; Arc `expanded` / `defaultExpanded`). |
| `SelectedKeys` | `IReadOnlyList<object>?` | `null` | The keys of the selected rows (two-way; Arc `selected` / `defaultSelected`). Parents are added or removed to match their children. |
| `SortKey` | `string?` | `null` | The key of the column rows are sorted by, or null (two-way; Arc `sort.columnId`). |
| `SortDirection` | `DataTableSortDirection` | `None` | The sort direction (two-way; Arc `sort.direction`). A header cycles ascending, descending, none. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `RowExpandedChanged` | `TreeTableExpandedChangedEventArgs` | Raised when rows expand or collapse (Arc `onExpandedChange`). |
| `SelectionChanged` | `TreeTableSelectionChangedEventArgs` | Raised with the new selection (Arc `onSelectedChange`). |
| `SortChanged` | `TreeTableSortChangedEventArgs` | Raised when a header cycles the sort (Arc `onSortChange`). |
| `RowActivated` | `TreeTableRowEventArgs` | Raised when a row without children is clicked or gets Enter (Arc `onRowActivate`). Parent rows toggle instead. |
| `ChildrenLoadFailed` | `TreeTableRowEventArgs` | Raised when `ChildrenLoader` faults; the row shows a retry line. |

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

### TreeTableColumn

One column of a `TreeTable`. The cell value comes from `ValueSelector` or `Binding` (compiled against the row item in XAML); `CellTemplate` hosts custom content. The first column shown holds the tree: its chevron, indent and guides sit before the cell content. A column is sortable when it has a value (`SortValueSelector` or `ValueSelector`) and `IsSortable` is true.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Header` | `string` | `""` | Column label; also the default `EffectiveKey`. |
| `Key` | `string?` | `null` | Stable id reported by sort events and `SortKey`. |
| `Width` | `GridLength` | `1*` | Arc's grid track: pixels (`96`), a share of the rest (`2*`). Defaults to `1*` (`minmax(0, 1fr)`). |
| `IsEndAligned` | `bool` | `false` | Right-aligns the column and sets its figures in tabular width (Arc `align: "end"`). |
| `HideBelow` | `double` | `0` | Hides the column while the table is narrower than this many pixels (0: never; Arc `hideBelow`). |
| `IsSortable` | `bool` | `true` | When false the header is a plain label even though the column has a value. |
| `StringFormat` | `string?` | `null` | Format for cell text: a composite format (`{0:N0} MB`) or a format string (`C0`). |
| `CellTemplate` | `IDataTemplate?` | `null` | Custom cell content (Arc `cell`); the data context is the row item. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### Event arguments

| Type | Member | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `TreeTableExpandedChangedEventArgs` | `ExpandedKeys` | The keys of every expanded row |
| `TreeTableSelectionChangedEventArgs` | `SelectedKeys`, `SelectedItems` | The selected keys, and the loaded items they belong to |
| `TreeTableSortChangedEventArgs` | `Column`, `Direction` | The sorted column (null when cleared) and the direction |
| `TreeTableRowEventArgs` | `Item`, `Key`, `Error` | The row; `Error` is set when a load failed |

## Accessibility

- The table has the name "Tree table" by default. Set `Caption` to name it for your content.
- Rows expose their name, their position in the set, their size and their expanded state. A sortable header
  reports its sort direction.
- Only one row is in the Tab order, and the arrow keys move between rows.
- Each checkbox is named from `RowLabelSelector`, such as "Select Design", and the mixed state is exposed.
- Loading, load errors, sorting, expand all and selection changes are announced through a polite live region.
- If the focused row disappears because its parent collapsed, focus moves to the nearest visible ancestor.
- Hover fills apply to mouse pointers only; a touch tap toggles and activates rows directly.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Up` / `Down` | Move between visible rows |
| `Right` | Open a row; on an open row, move to its first child |
| `Left` | Close a row; otherwise move to its parent |
| `Home` / `End` | Move to the first or last visible row |
| `PageUp` / `PageDown` | Move ten rows |
| `*` | Open all siblings of the focused row |
| `Space` | Toggle the row's selection (with `IsSelectable`) |
| `Enter` | Toggle a parent, retry a failed load, or activate a leaf |
| `Ctrl` / `Cmd` + `A` | Select all rows, or clear the selection (with `IsSelectable`) |

## Motion

- Rows grow from zero height on a smooth spring while they fade in, with a short stagger of 18 ms between siblings, and
  they shrink away when a parent closes.
- A loading row hands its place to the first child that arrives, so nothing squeezes past anything else.
- Sorting moves each row to its new place on a spring.
- The chevron turns a quarter on a snappy spring, the sort arrow turns over, and the expand all glyph swaps with a
  turn.
- Hover and selection fills fade in 160 ms.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| A row opens or closes | Height spring with stagger and fade | A short fade with no height spring or stagger | Immediate |
| Sorting | Rows spring to their new places | Rows jump | Immediate |
| Chevron and sort arrow | Spring turn | Immediate | Immediate |

## Related

- `TreeView` for navigation trees without columns.
- `Table` for flat records with sortable columns.
- `DataGrid` for a spreadsheet-style grid with range selection and inline editing.
- `Checkbox`, the binary control behind each row's selection.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `TreeView` | The hierarchy is navigation with one label per node |
| `Table` | The records are flat and compared by column |
| `DataGrid` | People edit cells and select ranges |
| `Accordion` | A few sections open into free-form content |

---

# Tree view

> Navigate nested folders and structured content.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/tree-view

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.TreeViewFileTreeDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12">
        <Grid ColumnDefinitions="280,*" ColumnSpacing="16">
            <arc:TreeView MinWidth="260" ItemInvoked="OnItemInvoked">
                <arc:TreeViewItem Header="src" IsExpanded="True">
                    <arc:TreeViewItem Header="components" IsExpanded="True">
                        <arc:TreeViewItem Header="button">
                            <arc:TreeViewItem Header="button.tsx" />
                            <arc:TreeViewItem Header="button.module.css" />
                        </arc:TreeViewItem>
                        <arc:TreeViewItem Header="tree-view">
                            <arc:TreeViewItem Header="tree-view.tsx" />
                            <arc:TreeViewItem Header="tree-view.module.css" />
                        </arc:TreeViewItem>
                    </arc:TreeViewItem>
                    <arc:TreeViewItem Header="lib">
                        <arc:TreeViewItem Header="motion-tokens.ts" />
                        <arc:TreeViewItem Header="utils.ts" />
                    </arc:TreeViewItem>
                </arc:TreeViewItem>
                <arc:TreeViewItem Header="docs">
                    <arc:TreeViewItem Header="getting-started.md" />
                    <arc:TreeViewItem Header="theming.md" />
                </arc:TreeViewItem>
                <arc:TreeViewItem Header="package.json" />
                <arc:TreeViewItem Header="README.md" />
            </arc:TreeView>
            <arc:CodeBlock x:Name="Viewer"
                           Grid.Column="1"
                           VerticalAlignment="Top"
                           Code="// Select a file"
                           FileName="No file selected"
                           Language="ts" />
        </Grid>
        <TextBlock x:Name="Status"
                   Text="Click or press Enter on a file."
                   FontSize="14"
                   TextWrapping="Wrap"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class TreeViewFileTreeDemo : UserControl
{
    private static readonly Dictionary<string, (string Language, string Code)> s_sources = new()
    {
        ["button.tsx"] = ("tsx", """
            export function Button({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
              return <button className="button">{children}</button>;
            }
            """),
        ["button.module.css"] = ("css", """
            .button {
              height: 44px;
              border-radius: 18px;
              padding-inline: 16px;
            }
            """),
        ["tree-view.tsx"] = ("tsx", """
            export function TreeView({ nodes }: TreeViewProps) {
              const [expanded, setExpanded] = useState(new Set<string>());
              return <div role="tree">{nodes.map(render)}</div>;
            }
            """),
        ["README.md"] = ("md", """
            # Arc

            Components with legible hierarchy and calm motion.
            """),
        ["package.json"] = ("json", """
            {
              "name": "arc",
              "version": "1.0.0"
            }
            """),
        ["motion-tokens.ts"] = ("ts", """
            export const motionTokens = {
              duration: { fast: 0.16, standard: 0.24 },
            };
            """)
    };

    public TreeViewFileTreeDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
    }

    private void OnItemInvoked(object? sender, TreeViewItemEventArgs e)
    {
        var name = ((TreeViewItem)e.Item).Header ?? string.Empty;
        Status.Text = $"Invoked {name}";
        if (s_sources.TryGetValue(name, out var source))
        {
            Viewer.FileName = name;
            Viewer.Language = source.Language;
            Viewer.Code = source.Code;
        }
    }
}
```

## When to use

`TreeView` shows nested records that people open, close and select: folders and files, a chart of accounts, a
category hierarchy. It sits in the navigation of a page, and a selection in the tree usually drives the content beside
it, such as a preview, a form or a code viewer. Rows are drawn from a flat, virtualized list, so a large hierarchy
stays responsive.

- **Repository and file browsers** in a developer tool: folders and files open and close, and the selected file
  appears in a `CodeBlock` next to the tree.
- **Documentation and knowledge-base navigation** in an internal admin: sections nest several levels, and selecting a
  page loads it in the editor pane.
- **Chart of accounts and cost centres** in a finance app: parent accounts open to reveal their children, and the
  selected account drives the ledger view.
- **Organization and team structures** in an HR or admin console: departments contain teams, and teams contain
  people, with the selection opening the person's profile.
- **Media and asset libraries** with folders of thousands of files: the tree stays usable because only the rows near
  the viewport are created.

## When not to use

- **A few collapsible sections of content** that people read top to bottom: use `Accordion`.
- **The current location in a page hierarchy**: use `Breadcrumb`, which shows the path and links back up it.
- **The keys and values of one JSON document**: use `JsonViewer`, which shows the values beside their keys and
  supports search and copy.
- **A flat list that the user reorders**: use `ReorderableList`. A tree has no drag order between siblings.
- **Records with the same fields that people compare by column**: use `Table`. A tree shows one label per
  node and no columns.

## Usage

Nodes can be declared inline in XAML. A `TreeViewItem` with child items is a folder.

```xml
<arc:TreeView MinWidth="260" ShowIndentGuides="True">
    <arc:TreeView.Items>
        <arc:TreeViewItem Header="src" IsExpanded="True">
            <arc:TreeViewItem.Items>
                <arc:TreeViewItem Header="components">
                    <arc:TreeViewItem.Items>
                        <arc:TreeViewItem Header="button.tsx" />
                        <arc:TreeViewItem Header="tree-view.tsx" />
                    </arc:TreeViewItem.Items>
                </arc:TreeViewItem>
                <arc:TreeViewItem Header="lib" />
            </arc:TreeViewItem.Items>
        </arc:TreeViewItem>
        <arc:TreeViewItem Header="README.md" />
    </arc:TreeView.Items>
</arc:TreeView>
```

`TreeView` derives from Avalonia's `TemplatedControl`. It does not use Avalonia's nested item containers: it keeps one
flat list of pooled rows, so opening a folder costs the rows it reveals and the rest of the tree is not relayouted.
Inline `Items` suit a fixed navigation tree that you write in XAML. For data from a service or a database, bind
`ItemsSource`, which takes precedence over `Items` when both are set.

### Anatomy

1. **Frame**: the surface background with a 1 px border in the border color, a 16 px corner radius and 8, 6, 8, 8 px
   padding. The tree fills its width when you set `HorizontalAlignment` to `Stretch`, the default.
2. **Row**: 36 px tall with a 2 px gap below it, so each row takes a 38 px slot. Rows have a 10 px corner radius and
   10 px inline padding.
3. **Indent**: 18 px for each level. With `ShowIndentGuides` a short branch line in the border color joins nested rows
   to their parent.
4. **Chevron**: on a folder, the arrow that turns when the folder opens.
5. **Icon** (`ShowIcons`, `IconSelector`, `TreeViewItem.Icon`): a 16 px slot before the label. Folders show a folder
   icon that opens; files show a file icon. `Icon` and `IconSelector` take a 24 by 24 glyph, such as an `ArcIcons`
   member. With `ShowIcons` false the label starts at the indent.
6. **Label** (`Header`, `HeaderSelector`): the row text in the secondary text color. The active row uses the
   foreground color.
7. **Row fills**: a hover fill and a selection fill, both in the muted surface color. The selection fill glides from
   row to row.
8. **File tints**: `.ts` and `.tsx` files, and `.css`, `.md` and `.json` files, take a file-type tint. Other files use
   the muted text color.
9. **Focus ring**: drawn by the control for keyboard focus only.

### Choosing inline items or a data source

| Source | Use it when | Children |
|---|---|---|
| Inline `Items` | The tree is fixed navigation, small and written in XAML | Nested `TreeViewItem` elements |
| `ItemsSource` | The nodes come from data and change at run time | `ChildrenSelector` returns each node's children |

### Data with a children selector

Bind `ItemsSource` and set the selectors from code. `ChildrenSelector` returns the children of a node, and
a node with children is a folder.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.TreeViewDataWithChildrenSelectorDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12">
        <WrapPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center" ItemSpacing="12" LineSpacing="12">
            <arc:Button Content="Expand all" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Click="OnExpandAllClick" />
            <arc:Button Content="Collapse all" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Click="OnCollapseAllClick" />
            <arc:Button Content="Select globals.css" Variant="Ghost" Size="Small" Click="OnRevealClick" />
        </WrapPanel>
        <arc:TreeView x:Name="Tree"
                      HorizontalAlignment="Left"
                      Width="300"
                      SelectionChanged="OnSelectionChanged" />
        <TextBlock x:Name="Selected"
                   Text="SelectedItem: (none)"
                   FontSize="14"
                   TextWrapping="Wrap"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class TreeViewDataWithChildrenSelectorDemo : UserControl
{
    private sealed record FileNode(string Name, IReadOnlyList<FileNode>? Children = null)
    {
        public override string ToString() => Name;
    }

    private readonly List<FileNode> _nodes =
    [
        new("app", [new("layout.tsx"), new("page.tsx"), new("globals.css")]),
        new("public", [new("logo.svg"), new("favicon.ico")]),
        new("next.config.ts"),
        new("tsconfig.json")
    ];

    public TreeViewDataWithChildrenSelectorDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Tree.ItemsSource = _nodes;
        Tree.ChildrenSelector = item => ((FileNode)item).Children;
        Tree.HeaderSelector = item => ((FileNode)item).Name;
    }

    private void OnExpandAllClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) => Tree.ExpandAll();

    private void OnCollapseAllClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) => Tree.CollapseAll();

    private void OnRevealClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) => Tree.SelectedItem = _nodes[0].Children![2];

    private void OnSelectionChanged(object? sender, TreeViewSelectionChangedEventArgs e) =>
        Selected.Text = $"SelectedItem: {e.NewItem}";
}
```

```csharp
var tree = new TreeView
{
    ItemsSource = nodes,
    ChildrenSelector = item => ((FileNode)item).Children,
    HeaderSelector = item => ((FileNode)item).Name,
    Width = 300
};
tree.SelectionChanged += (_, e) => selected.Text = $"SelectedItem: {e.NewItem}";
tree.SelectedItem = nodes[0].Children![2];   // expands the ancestors of the node
```

`SelectedItem` is two-way, so it can be bound to a view model:

```xml
<arc:TreeView ItemsSource="{Binding Files}"
              SelectedItem="{Binding SelectedFile, Mode=TwoWay}" />
```

### Binding to a view model

In an MVVM app the view model owns the node data and the selection, and the tree reflects them. The example uses
CommunityToolkit.Mvvm. The node is a plain record, and the view model loads the tree and holds the selected node.

```csharp
public sealed record FileNode(string Name, IReadOnlyList<FileNode>? Children = null)
{
    public override string ToString() => Name;
}

public interface IRepositoryService
{
    Task<IReadOnlyList<FileNode>> GetTreeAsync();
}

public partial class WorkspaceViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    private readonly IRepositoryService _repository;

    public WorkspaceViewModel(IRepositoryService repository) => _repository = repository;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private ObservableCollection<FileNode> _files = [];

    [ObservableProperty]
    private FileNode? _selectedFile;

    [RelayCommand]
    private async Task LoadAsync() => Files = new ObservableCollection<FileNode>(await _repository.GetTreeAsync());
}
```

```xml
<arc:TreeView ItemsSource="{Binding Files}"
              SelectedItem="{Binding SelectedFile, Mode=TwoWay}"
              ShowIcons="True" />
```

Selectors are functions, which XAML cannot express, so set them once in the view's code-behind:

```csharp
Tree.ChildrenSelector = item => ((FileNode)item).Children;
Tree.HeaderSelector = item => ((FileNode)item).Name;
```

- `SelectedFile` is two-way. Setting it from the view model selects the node and opens its ancestors, so a deep link
  to a file shows the file.
- Use the same node instances after a refresh, or the selection and the open folders no longer match the rows. When
  the service returns new objects, map the selected node by its path and assign the new instance.
- Compiled bindings need `x:DataType` on the view (the examples here leave it out for brevity).

### Icons

`ShowIcons` turns icons on or off for the whole tree, and `IconSelector` supplies an icon for each data node. A
`TreeViewItem` takes its own `Icon` instead. Both take a 24 by 24 stroked geometry, and the `ArcIcons` members are
the usual source.

```csharp
tree.ShowIcons = true;
tree.IconSelector = item => ((FileNode)item).Children is null ? ArcIcons.File : ArcIcons.Folder;
```

### Expanding and collapsing from code

```csharp
tree.ExpandAll();
tree.CollapseAll();
tree.ToggleExpanded(folderNode);
tree.ScrollIntoView(fileNode);
tree.FocusItem(fileNode);
```

`ScrollIntoView` and `FocusItem` open the ancestors of the node first, so a node the person cannot see yet becomes
visible. `IsItemExpanded` reports whether a folder is open. For an inline `TreeViewItem`, `IsExpanded` is two-way and
the tree keeps it in sync.

### Events

`ItemInvoked` fires when a row is activated by a click, Enter or Space, including a row that is already selected.
`SelectionChanged` reports a change of the selected node. `ItemExpanded` and `ItemCollapsed` report folders that open
and close. Activating a folder selects it and toggles it, so a folder that opens from a click also raises
`ItemExpanded`.

```csharp
tree.ItemInvoked += (_, e) => OpenFile(e.Item);
tree.ItemExpanded += (_, e) => log.Text = $"Opened {e.Item}";
```

### Thousands of nodes

The tree has 40 folders with 250 files each. Rows are virtualized and pooled, and only the rows near the viewport are
realized, so opening a folder costs about one screenful of rows and the rest of the tree is not built.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.TreeViewThousandsOfNodesDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12">
        <WrapPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center" ItemSpacing="12" LineSpacing="12">
            <arc:Button Content="Open all 10,000 files" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Click="OnExpandAllClick" />
            <arc:Button Content="Collapse all" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Click="OnCollapseAllClick" />
        </WrapPanel>
        <arc:TreeView x:Name="Tree"
                      MaxHeight="380"
                      HorizontalAlignment="Left"
                      Width="340" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class TreeViewThousandsOfNodesDemo : UserControl
{
    private sealed record FileNode(string Name, IReadOnlyList<FileNode>? Children = null)
    {
        public override string ToString() => Name;
    }

    public TreeViewThousandsOfNodesDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        // 40 folders with 250 files each: rows are virtualized, so opening a folder costs one screenful.
        Tree.ItemsSource = Enumerable.Range(1, 40).Select(f => new FileNode($"package-{f:00}",
            Enumerable.Range(1, 250).Select(i => new FileNode($"module-{f:00}-{i:000}.ts")).ToList())).ToList();
        Tree.ChildrenSelector = item => ((FileNode)item).Children;
    }

    private void OnExpandAllClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) => Tree.ExpandAll();

    private void OnCollapseAllClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) => Tree.CollapseAll();
}
```

### Example: Docs repository browser

A docs team browses the repository of its component documentation. The tree sits in the left pane, and a `CodeBlock`
in the right pane shows the selected file, as in the File tree demo at the top of the page. Two folders are open by
default, so the reader sees the structure at a glance, and the folders that the team rarely edits stay closed. The
file tints show which files are code, styles, prose and configuration without any extra column.

### Content guidelines

Node labels are names that people search for, so show them exactly as the source stores them.

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| Untitled folder | The folder's real name, or "New folder" while it is being created |
| Documentation (42 files) | Documentation, with the count shown elsewhere in the page |
| Click to open file | No text; the row is the control |
| Files | Project files, or the name of the repository |
| Item 1 | The file name, such as theming.md |

- Keep labels as the stored name, including its case and extension, so people can match them to their repository.
- Keep the tree's accessible name specific: "Repository files" or "Chart of accounts" rather than "Tree".

### Best practices

**Do**

- Open the first one or two levels by default, so people see the structure without hunting for it.
- Use `ShowIndentGuides` for trees deeper than two levels, so the parent of each row is easy to see.
- Keep the same node instances across a refresh, so the selection and the open folders keep matching the rows.
- Bind `SelectedItem` two-way, so a deep link or a search result can select a node from the view model.
- Bound the tree's height with `MaxHeight` when it sits in a page with other content, so the scroll area is the tree.

**Avoid**

- Using the tree for a few sections of prose: an `Accordion` reads better and needs no keyboard model.
- Putting columns of data into the labels, such as sizes and dates. Use a `Table` for records.
- Expecting multiple selection. The tree has one `SelectedItem`, and a modifier key does not select a range.
- Nesting more than a few levels by default. Deep folders expanded at once make the structure hard to scan.
- Building the tree from a fresh copy of the data on every keystroke. Refresh it on a deliberate action.

### Common questions

**Why does a node with children not show its children?** `ItemsSource` needs a `ChildrenSelector`. Without one, each
node is a file. Return the child collection from the selector, or return null or an empty list for a file.

**How do I open the tree to a specific file?** Set `SelectedItem` to the node. The tree opens its ancestors and
scrolls the row into view. Use `ScrollIntoView` when you want to reveal a node without selecting it.

**Can the tree select several nodes?** No. `SelectedItem` holds one node, and the keyboard ignores modifier keys
such as Control, Alt and Meta. Use a `Table` with `IsSelectable` when people must pick several records.

**Does the tree sort its nodes?** No. It shows the nodes in the order you supply them, so sort the source before you
bind it.

## API reference

### TreeView

A keyboard-navigable file tree with animated folders and a selection fill that glides between rows. Folders open with their space growing on a smooth spring while the new rows stagger in; the chevron turns on a snappy spring and the folder icon pops open. Keyboard: ↑/↓ move, → opens or enters, ← closes or goes to the parent, Home/End, PageUp/PageDown, Enter/Space select and toggle, and typing jumps to a matching row. Unlike `TreeView` (nested item containers), rows are a flat, virtualized list of pooled, self-drawn rows (see `TablesTreeRowsPanel`): thousands of open nodes cost one screenful of rows, and the open / close motion never relayouts the whole tree. Nodes come from inline `Items` (`TreeViewItem`) or from `ItemsSource` with `ChildrenSelector`.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ItemsSource` | `IEnumerable?` | `null` | Root nodes from data; takes precedence over `Items`. |
| `ChildrenSelector` | `Func<object, IEnumerable?>?` | `null` | Children of a data item (null or empty: a file). Not needed for `TreeViewItem` nodes. |
| `HeaderSelector` | `Func<object, string?>?` | `null` | Row label of a data item; `ToString()` when not set. |
| `IconSelector` | `Func<object, Geometry?>?` | `null` | Optional icon of a data item (24x24 stroked glyph); folders and files get Arc's icons otherwise. |
| `SelectedItem` | `object?` | `null` | The selected node (two-way). Setting it to a hidden node opens its ancestors. |
| `ShowIndentGuides` | `bool` | `true` | Draws the short branch line beside nested rows (Arc's indent guide). |
| `ShowIcons` | `bool` | `true` | Shows each row's icon (16px slot before the label); when false the label starts at the indent. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `SelectionChanged` | `TreeViewSelectionChangedEventArgs` | Raised when the selected item changes; the argument carries the old and new item. |
| `ItemInvoked` | `TreeViewItemEventArgs` | A row was clicked or activated with Enter / Space (Arc `onSelect`), even when already selected. |
| `ItemExpanded` | `TreeViewItemEventArgs` | Raised when a branch item expands. |
| `ItemCollapsed` | `TreeViewItemEventArgs` | Raised when a branch item collapses. |

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

### TreeViewItem

A node written inline in a `TreeView` (Arc's `TreeNode`): a label, optional icon and child nodes. A node with children is a folder. Not a control: the tree draws its rows itself (virtualized), so nodes stay cheap however many there are.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Header` | `string?` | `null` | Label of the row. |
| `Icon` | `Geometry?` | `null` | Optional 24x24 stroked glyph (for example an `ArcIcons` member) replacing the folder / file icon. |
| `IsExpanded` | `bool` | `false` | Whether the folder is open (two-way; the tree keeps it in sync). |

Derives from `StyledElement`: every member of `StyledElement` works as well.

### Event arguments

| Type | Member | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `TreeViewItemEventArgs` | `Item` | The node: a `TreeViewItem` or an item of `ItemsSource` |
| `TreeViewSelectionChangedEventArgs` | `OldItem`, `NewItem` | The previously selected node and the new one |

## Accessibility

- The tree has the name "File tree" by default. Set `AutomationProperties.Name` to name it for your content.
- Rows expose tree item roles with their level, position in the set, expanded state and selected state.
- Only the focused row is in the Tab order. Arrow keys, Home and End, PageUp and PageDown move between rows.
- Right arrow opens a folder or enters its first child. Left arrow closes a folder or moves to its parent.
- Enter or Space selects the row and toggles a folder. Typing a name moves to the next row that starts with it.
- The focus ring is drawn for keyboard focus only. Icons and indent guides are not announced.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Up` / `Down` | Move to the previous or next visible row |
| `Right` | Open a closed folder; on an open folder, move to its first child |
| `Left` | Close an open folder; otherwise move to the parent row |
| `Home` / `End` | Move to the first or last visible row |
| `PageUp` / `PageDown` | Move by about one screen of rows |
| `Enter` / `Space` | Select the row, raise `ItemInvoked`, and toggle a folder |
| Letters | Move to the next row whose label starts with the typed text |

The tree ignores key presses that use Control, Alt or Meta, so shortcuts of the window still work.

## Motion

- Opening a folder grows its space on a spring, and the new rows stagger in from the left.
- The selection highlight glides from row to row, and the folder arrow turns with a snappy spring.
- Closing a folder collapses its rows smoothly.
- Reduced motion shows and hides rows at once. Off jumps straight to the final state.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| A folder opens or closes | The space grows or collapses on a spring; new rows stagger in | Rows show or hide at once | Immediate |

The selection highlight glides between rows at full motion only.

## Related

- `Accordion` for a few sections of content that open and close.
- `Breadcrumb` to show where the current page sits in a hierarchy.
- `JsonViewer` for nested data that people inspect, with search and copy.
- `CodeBlock` to show the source of the file selected in the tree.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `Accordion` | A few sections of prose open and close, and the order is fixed |
| `Breadcrumb` | The page shows its place in a hierarchy and links back up it |
| `JsonViewer` | The nested data is one document that people inspect and copy |
| `CodeBlock` | The selected file's source is shown beside the tree |
| `Table` | The records share fields that people compare by column |
| `ReorderableList` | The person orders a flat list by dragging |
