# Reorderable list

> Organize items with direct drag and drop.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/reorderable-list

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ReorderableListPrioritiesDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="14">
        <arc:ReorderableList x:Name="Priorities"
                             Width="520"
                             HorizontalAlignment="Left"
                             Reordered="OnReordered">
            <arc:ReorderableListEntry Id="pricing" Title="Ship pricing page" Detail="Marketing · due Friday" />
            <arc:ReorderableListEntry Id="onboarding" Title="Review onboarding flow" Detail="Design · 3 open comments" />
            <arc:ReorderableListEntry Id="billing" Title="Migrate billing webhooks" Detail="Platform" />
            <arc:ReorderableListEntry Id="notes" Title="Write launch notes" Detail="Docs · draft ready" />
        </arc:ReorderableList>
        <TextBlock x:Name="Status"
                   Text="Drag a grip, or focus one and press ↑ / ↓. Space picks a row up, arrows move it, Space drops, Escape cancels."
                   FontSize="14"
                   TextWrapping="Wrap"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class ReorderableListPrioritiesDemo : UserControl
{
    public ReorderableListPrioritiesDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
    }

    private void OnReordered(object? sender, ReorderableListReorderedEventArgs e)
    {
        var order = Priorities.Items.OfType<ReorderableListEntry>().Select(p => p.Id);
        Status.Text = $"Moved “{(e.Item as ReorderableListEntry)?.Title}” from {e.OldIndex + 1} to {e.NewIndex + 1}. Order: {string.Join(", ", order)}";
    }
}
```

## When to use

`ReorderableList` lets a person put a short list of items in the order they want. It is the control for a decision
the person makes by hand, where the order itself is the information: the team's launch priorities, the next tracks
in a queue, the steps of a review checklist. It sits in a card, a side panel or a settings page, and it saves the
new order through the `Reordered` event.

- **Launch priorities in a planning view**: a product lead ranks four or five workstreams before a release review.
  The order is the answer, so a drag handle beside each item is clearer than a number field.
- **Playlists and task queues** in a media or operations console: the next items to play or process, where the
  person moves an item up or down and the rest of the list stays in place.
- **Approval or review steps** in a workflow editor: a checklist whose order decides which reviewer sees a document
  first, edited by the person who owns the process.
- **Pinned shortcuts** in a dashboard or a navigation panel: the items people use most, ordered to their taste and
  saved per account.

## When not to use

- **The order comes from column values**, such as sorting invoices by due date or amount: use `Table`,
  which sorts by the column and keeps the data in a grid.
- **Quick actions on a row** such as archive, snooze or delete, with no reordering: use `SwipeActions`, which reveals
  actions from a swipe without moving the row.
- **Long lists** of hundreds of items: rows are not virtualized and each row runs a layout animation when another
  row moves, so split the list or use `Table` with a sort control.
- **Nested items** such as folders, categories or subtasks: use `TreeView`, which shows the hierarchy and lets people
  expand each level.
- **A choice from a fixed set** that people toggle and do not rank, such as filter chips or channels: use
  `ChipGroup`; the order of those options is not the person's decision.

## Usage

Each row shows a grip. Dragging the grip moves the row. The list reports the new order in `Reordered`.

```xml
<arc:ReorderableList Label="Priorities"
                     Width="520"
                     ItemsSource="{Binding Priorities}" />
```

`ReorderableList` derives from Avalonia's `ItemsControl`, so `ItemsSource`, `Items`, `ItemTemplate` and the container
methods work as they do on other items controls. `ItemsSource` takes a `ReorderableListEntry` list with an `Id`, a
`Title` and an optional `Detail`.

```csharp
var priorities = new ObservableCollection<ReorderableListEntry>
{
    new("pricing", "Ship pricing page", "Marketing - due Friday"),
    new("onboarding", "Review onboarding flow", "Design - 3 open comments"),
    new("billing", "Migrate billing webhooks", "Platform")
};
var list = new ReorderableList { ItemsSource = priorities };
```

### Anatomy

1. **Grip** (the handle): a 40 px square with a 16 px vertical grip glyph, 7 px from the top, bottom and left edges
   of the row, on the muted surface color. It is the only part that starts a drag.
2. **Row**: a surface with the Arc border and control radius, at least 56 px high. Rows are 8 px apart.
3. **Content**: the item's title at 14 px medium weight, with the detail line below it at 12 px in the muted text
   color. The default content comes from `ReorderableListEntry`; `ItemTemplate` replaces it.
4. **Position** (on the right): a two-digit number, `01`, `02` and so on, at 12 px in the muted text color. It
   updates after every move and rolls in the direction the row travelled.
5. **Announcer** (not visible): a hidden polite region that speaks each keyboard and drag step.

### Reacting to a move

`Reordered` gives the item, its old index and its new index. When `ItemsSource` is an `ObservableCollection` and
`MovesItems` is `True` (the default), the list moves the item in the collection itself. Set `MovesItems` to `False`
to keep the collection unchanged and save the order yourself. A list bound to an array or another fixed source
behaves the same way: the list raises `Reordered` and leaves the source as it is.

```csharp
list.Reordered += (_, e) => status.Text =
    $"Moved {((ReorderableListEntry)e.Item!).Title} from {e.OldIndex + 1} to {e.NewIndex + 1}";

list.MoveItem(0, 2);   // move the first row to the third place
```

`MoveItem` moves the row with the same slide animation as a drag, and it also raises `Reordered`, so code moves and
person moves reach the same handler.

### Custom item template

`ItemTemplate` replaces the default title and detail. `ItemTitleSelector` gives the title used in the grip's
accessible name and in announcements; when it is not set, the list uses the entry's `Title` or the item's text.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             xmlns:local="using:TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ReorderableListCustomItemTemplateDemo">
    <arc:ReorderableList x:Name="Colors" Width="520" HorizontalAlignment="Left">
        <arc:ReorderableList.ItemTemplate>
            <DataTemplate x:DataType="x:String">
                <StackPanel Orientation="Horizontal" Spacing="10">
                    <Border Width="14"
                            Height="14"
                            CornerRadius="7"
                            VerticalAlignment="Center"
                            Background="{Binding Converter={x:Static local:ReorderableListCustomItemTemplateDemo.SwatchBrush}}" />
                    <TextBlock Text="{Binding}" VerticalAlignment="Center" />
                </StackPanel>
            </DataTemplate>
        </arc:ReorderableList.ItemTemplate>
    </arc:ReorderableList>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using System.Collections.ObjectModel;
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Data.Converters;
using Avalonia.Media;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class ReorderableListCustomItemTemplateDemo : UserControl
{
    public static readonly FuncValueConverter<string?, IBrush?> SwatchBrush = new(name => new SolidColorBrush(name switch
    {
        "Coral" => Color.Parse("#F07167"),
        "Saffron" => Color.Parse("#F4B942"),
        "Mint" => Color.Parse("#57CC99"),
        "Azure" => Color.Parse("#4EA8DE"),
        _ => Color.Parse("#9381FF")
    }));

    public ReorderableListCustomItemTemplateDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Colors.ItemsSource = new ObservableCollection<string> { "Coral", "Saffron", "Mint", "Azure", "Iris" };
    }
}
```

```csharp
var colors = new ReorderableList
{
    ItemsSource = new ObservableCollection<string> { "Coral", "Saffron", "Mint" },
    ItemTemplate = new FuncDataTemplate<string>((name, _) => new TextBlock { Text = name }),
    ItemTitleSelector = item => item.ToString() ?? string.Empty
};
```

### Length and scrolling

Put the list in a `ScrollViewer` when it is taller than the space you give it. Dragging a row to the edge of the
scrolling area scrolls it, so a person can move a row past the visible part of the list.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ReorderableListAutoScrollDemo">
    <ScrollViewer Height="340" Width="528" HorizontalAlignment="Left">
        <Border Padding="4,8">
            <arc:ReorderableList x:Name="Tracks" />
        </Border>
    </ScrollViewer>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using System.Collections.ObjectModel;
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class ReorderableListAutoScrollDemo : UserControl
{
    public ReorderableListAutoScrollDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        var tracks = new ObservableCollection<ReorderableListEntry>();
        for (var i = 1; i <= 24; i++)
        {
            tracks.Add(new ReorderableListEntry($"t{i}", $"Track {i:00}", $"{2 + i % 4}:{(i * 7) % 60:00}"));
        }
        Tracks.ItemsSource = tracks;
    }
}
```

```xml
<ScrollViewer Height="340">
    <arc:ReorderableList ItemsSource="{Binding Tracks}" />
</ScrollViewer>
```

### Binding to a view model

In an MVVM app the view model owns the collection and the code that saves the order. With CommunityToolkit.Mvvm, an
`ObservableObject` holds the collection, and the list moves the items in that collection when `MovesItems` is
`True`. The binding is one-way: the list changes the collection, and the view model reads it.

```csharp
public partial class LaunchPlanViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    public ObservableCollection<ReorderableListEntry> Priorities { get; } =
    [
        new("pricing", "Ship pricing page", "Marketing, due Friday"),
        new("onboarding", "Review onboarding flow", "Design, 3 open comments"),
        new("billing", "Migrate billing webhooks", "Platform")
    ];

    [ObservableProperty]
    private string _status = "Drag a grip to reorder the launch priorities.";

    [RelayCommand]
    private void SaveOrder()
    {
        // Persist the order here, for example through your API client.
        Status = $"Saved order: {string.Join(", ", Priorities.Select(p => p.Id))}";
    }
}
```

```xml
<StackPanel Spacing="12">
    <arc:ReorderableList Label="Launch priorities"
                         Width="560"
                         HorizontalAlignment="Left"
                         ItemsSource="{Binding Priorities}" />
    <TextBlock Text="{Binding Status}" TextWrapping="Wrap" />
</StackPanel>
```

Forward `Reordered` to the command from code behind, so each move saves the order:

```csharp
list.Reordered += (_, _) => vm.SaveOrderCommand.Execute(null);
```

`ItemsSource` is one-way. Do not bind it back from the list, because the list does not write to the property; the
collection itself carries the new order.

### Data shape and performance

The list is for short collections, and the cost is in the row count. Every row is laid out and animated when another
row moves, and rows are not virtualized, so a list of a few dozen rows moves smoothly while a list of several
hundred does not.

- **Use `ReorderableListEntry` for the common case.** It carries an `Id` for your own code to find the item when it
  saves the order, a `Title` that names the accessible row and a `Detail` line for the second line of text.
- **Use `ItemTemplate` for other data.** Items of any type show through `ItemTemplate`; set `ItemTitleSelector` as
  well so the grip names and announcements read the right title.
- **Keep the data in one collection.** When the list moves items in place, the collection must be the one the list
  is bound to, not a copy.

### Example: Launch priorities

A product lead orders the launch workstreams before a review. The list is the whole page's decision, so it has a
title above it and a status line that confirms the saved order. Each row has a detail line with an owner or a
due date, so the position reads as a plan rather than a bare number.

![A launch priorities list with four ordered rows, each with a grip and a position number](https://docs.tkcode.si/shots/Docs/Tables/ReorderableList/images/LaunchPriorities.webp)

```xml
<StackPanel Width="600" Spacing="14">
    <TextBlock Text="Launch priorities"
               FontSize="16"
               FontWeight="SemiBold"
               Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
    <TextBlock Text="Ordered by the launch lead. Drag a grip, or focus one and press Up or Down."
               FontSize="13"
               TextWrapping="Wrap"
               Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
    <arc:ReorderableList Label="Launch priorities"
                         Width="560"
                         HorizontalAlignment="Left">
        <arc:ReorderableListEntry Id="pricing"
                                  Title="Ship pricing page"
                                  Detail="Marketing, due Friday" />
        <arc:ReorderableListEntry Id="onboarding"
                                  Title="Review onboarding flow"
                                  Detail="Design, 3 open comments" />
        <arc:ReorderableListEntry Id="billing"
                                  Title="Migrate billing webhooks"
                                  Detail="Platform" />
        <arc:ReorderableListEntry Id="notes"
                                  Title="Write launch notes"
                                  Detail="Docs, draft ready" />
    </arc:ReorderableList>
</StackPanel>
```

The design decisions are in the copy and the scale. Four rows are enough to show the grip, the title, the detail and
the position without scrolling, which is the list length the control is built for. The detail lines state an owner
and a status, so a person can judge the order without opening each item.

### Content guidelines

The control writes the grip names and the announcements from the titles, so the titles carry the wording.

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| Item 1, Item 2 | The work item's name, such as Ship pricing page |
| Drag handle | Grip; its accessible name is built from the title |
| Reorder list | `Label="Launch priorities"`, the name of what is ordered |
| Priority 1: ship pricing | Ship pricing page, with the position shown by the list |
| Moved item | The title, which the announcement already includes |

- Write titles as the work item's name in sentence case, with no number in front. The list adds the position.
- Keep titles short enough for one line at the list's width; put the owner, the date or the status in `Detail`.
- Use digits for dates and counts in the detail line, such as "due Friday" or "3 open comments".

### Best practices

**Do**

- Set `Label` to the name of what is ordered. The label is the list's accessible name, and a screen reader user hears
  it before the first row.
- Save the order in `Reordered`, not when the window closes, so a closed window does not lose the change.
- Keep the list in a `ScrollViewer` with a height when it can grow, so the drag can reach past the visible rows.
- Give each item a stable `Id`, so the order you save survives a reload and a rename.
- Show the outcome in a status line, so the person sees that the change was kept.

**Avoid**

- Using the list for an order that a column already defines. A user who wants to see items by due date needs a
  sortable table, and a manual order would conflict with the sort.
- Reordering a list with hundreds of rows. Every row animates when another row moves, so the list loses its
  smoothness long before it loses its usefulness.
- Making the whole row draggable. Only the grip starts a drag, so the text stays selectable and a click on the text
  does not start a move.
- Adding a second copy of the order in a button handler. The list already moves the items in place, so save the
  collection as it is when `Reordered` fires instead of rebuilding the order by hand.

### Common questions

**The list moves rows, but my source list does not change.** `MovesItems` is `False`, or the source is not a
mutable collection. Use an `ObservableCollection` and keep `MovesItems` at its default, or save the order from
`Reordered` yourself.

**Can I start a drag from the text of a row?** No. Only the grip starts a drag, so the row text can be selected and
copied. Users with a keyboard focus the grip and use the arrow keys.

**Why does Up do nothing on the first row?** The keyboard move stops at the ends of the list, and the focus stays on
the grip. The row does not wrap to the other end; use Home or End while a row is picked up to jump to the first or
last place.

**How do I move an item from code?** Call `MoveItem(from, to)`. It uses the same slide animation as a drag and raises
`Reordered`, so the handler that saves the order runs for code moves too.

**Does focus stay on the row after a keyboard move?** Yes. Focus stays on the moved row's grip, so the next key
press moves the same row again. Tab leaves the list as it does for any other control.

## API reference

### ReorderableList

Arc's reorderable list: organize items with direct drag and drop. Rows are dragged by their grip (pointer capture): the row lifts, follows the pointer, the rows it passes slide aside on springs and the drop settles on a quick spring with the release velocity; holding a row near the edge of a scrolling ancestor scrolls it. Keyboard: ↑/↓ on a grip moves the row one place at once (Arc), Space / Enter picks it up so arrows preview the move, Space / Enter drops it and Escape cancels; every step is announced. A mutable `ItemsSource` (or inline items) is reordered in place; `Reordered` reports each move. Drag motion is render transforms only.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Label` | `string` | `"Reorder items"` | Accessible name of the list. |
| `MovesItems` | `bool` | `true` | When true (default) a mutable source is reordered in place; otherwise only `Reordered` is raised. |
| `ItemTitleSelector` | `Func<object, string>?` | `null` | Title used in the grip's accessible name and in announcements (defaults to `Title` or the item text). |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Reordered` | `ReorderableListReorderedEventArgs` | Raised after a row was moved by dragging or from the keyboard. |

Derives from `ItemsControl`: every member of `ItemsControl` works as well.

### ReorderableListEntry

A row of a `ReorderableList` as Arc models it: an id, a title and an optional detail line.

## Accessibility

- Each grip is exposed as a button. Its name gives the item title and its position, such as "Reorder Ship pricing
  page. Position 1 of 4. Use arrow keys.", and the name updates after each move.
- The list is named by `Label`, which defaults to "Reorder items". Set it to the name of what is ordered.
- Only the grip is focusable for dragging. The row text is a normal selectable text area.
- Each step is announced in a polite region: "Picked up Ship pricing page. Position 1 of 4. Use the arrow keys to
  move, Space to drop, Escape to cancel.", then "Ship pricing page dropped at position 3 of 4."
- Focus stays on the moved row's grip after a keyboard move, so the next key press acts on the same row.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Up` / `Down` (on a grip) | Move the row one place up or down at once; focus stays on its grip |
| `Space` / `Enter` (on a grip) | Pick the row up; the arrow keys then move it while the list previews the place |
| `Up` / `Down` (row picked up) | Move the picked row one place |
| `Home` / `End` (row picked up) | Move the picked row to the first or last place |
| `Space` / `Enter` (row picked up) | Drop the row at its place |
| `Escape` (row picked up) | Cancel: the row returns to where it was |
| Pointer drag on the grip | Move the row to a new place; the rows it passes make room |

## Motion

- A row lifts slightly while its grip is pressed. It settles back with a short spring when released.
- While dragging, the row follows the pointer and the rows it passes slide aside on springs.
- The position number rolls in the direction the row travelled.
- Reduced motion keeps the pointer follow, but the row lands at once and does not lift. Off behaves like Reduced.
- Dragging to the edge of a scrolling area scrolls it.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| Press a grip | The row lifts and scales to 1.02 on a snappy spring | The row does not lift | The row does not lift |
| Drag | The row follows the pointer and the rows it passes slide aside on springs | The row follows the pointer and lands at once | The row follows the pointer and lands at once |
| Drop | The row settles on a quick spring that keeps the release velocity | The row lands at once | The row lands at once |

## Related

- `Table` when the order comes from column values, not from a person's choice.
- `SwipeActions` for quick actions on a row without reordering it.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `Table` | The order comes from the values in a column, and people sort by it |
| `SwipeActions` | A row needs quick actions such as archive or snooze, not a new place |
| `TreeView` | The items nest, and people expand folders or categories to find them |
| `ChipGroup` | People pick from a fixed set of options and the order is not theirs to set |

# Filter toolbar

> Keep collection filters close and easy to reset.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/filter-toolbar

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             xmlns:collections="using:System.Collections.ObjectModel"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.FilterToolbarFiltersDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="14">
        <arc:FilterToolbar FiltersChanged="OnFiltersChanged">
            <arc:FilterToolbar.ActiveFilters>
                <collections:ObservableCollection x:TypeArguments="arc:FilterChip">
                    <arc:FilterChip Id="status" Label="Status" Value="Open" />
                    <arc:FilterChip Id="owner" Label="Owner" Value="Mina" />
                </collections:ObservableCollection>
            </arc:FilterToolbar.ActiveFilters>
            <arc:FilterField Id="status" Label="Status" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.CircleDot}">
                <arc:FilterOption Value="Open" Hint="4" />
                <arc:FilterOption Value="In progress" Hint="2" />
                <arc:FilterOption Value="Closed" Hint="2" />
            </arc:FilterField>
            <arc:FilterField Id="owner" Label="Owner" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.User}">
                <arc:FilterOption Value="Mina" />
                <arc:FilterOption Value="Theo" />
                <arc:FilterOption Value="Ana" />
                <arc:FilterOption Value="Kai" />
            </arc:FilterField>
            <arc:FilterField Id="priority" Label="Priority" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Flag}">
                <arc:FilterOption Value="Urgent" />
                <arc:FilterOption Value="High" />
                <arc:FilterOption Value="Medium" />
                <arc:FilterOption Value="Low" />
            </arc:FilterField>
        </arc:FilterToolbar>
        <TextBlock x:Name="Log"
                   Text="Remove a chip, clear all, or add a filter: pick a field, then a value."
                   FontSize="14"
                   TextWrapping="Wrap"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

public partial class FilterToolbarFiltersDemo : UserControl

    public FilterToolbarFiltersDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();

    private void OnFiltersChanged(object? sender, FilterToolbarFiltersChangedEventArgs e) =>
        Log.Text = $"{e.Kind}: {e.Filter?.Text ?? "all"} · {e.ActiveFilters.Count} active";

```

## When to use

`FilterToolbar` is the strip above a table or a list that shows which filters narrow the rows, lets people remove them
one at a time and resets them together. It holds the applied filters as removable chips, the Add filter menu that
adds the next one, an optional search field and any actions the page needs, so the list page keeps one consistent
header instead of a set of loose dropdowns.

- **Faceted filters on an order list**: a fulfillment team filters orders by status, carrier and region, sees "Status:
  Shipped" and "Region: EU" as chips, and clears them with one action when the shift changes.
- **Incident and ticket queues**: an on-call view filters incidents by severity, service and owner. The chips make
  the current view explicit when someone shares a link or a screenshot in a review.
- **Invoice and billing lists**: a finance user filters invoices by status and customer, then exports the filtered
  rows through an action placed beside the Add filter trigger.
- **Customer and CRM tables** where a search box and two or three facets work together: the search narrows the text,
  the chips narrow the segment, and the table below shows what remains.
- **Dense admin consoles on narrow windows**: below 520 px the chips stack above the actions, so the same toolbar
  works in a side panel without a separate layout.

## When not to use

- **A fixed set of options shown as on or off toggles**, such as the three views of a list (Open, Closed, All): use
  `ChipGroup`, which shows every option at once and needs no menu.
- **Free text search on its own, with no facets**: use `SearchField`. The toolbar's search box exists to sit with the
  filters; a page without filters gets nothing from the chips.
- **A form field that takes several values**, such as the assignees of a task in an editor: use `MultiSelect`. A
  filter toolbar applies a value to a list; a form field stores it on a record.
- **Choosing one value from a long list**, such as a customer among thousands: use `Combobox` with its own search.
  The Add filter menu lists every option, so it suits short lists only.
- **Sorting the rows of a table**: use the column headers of `Table`. A filter removes rows; a sort orders
  them, and the two belong in different places.

## Usage

Each filter is a `FilterChip` with an `Id`, a `Label` and a `Value`. Fields for the Add filter menu go in
`Fields`. A field has options that people choose in the second step.

```xml
<arc:FilterToolbar Label="Active filters"
                   ActiveFilters="{Binding Filters}"
                   MenuAlignment="Start">
    <arc:FilterToolbar.Fields>
        <arc:FilterField Id="status" Label="Status">
            <arc:FilterField.Options>
                <arc:FilterOption Value="Open" />
                <arc:FilterOption Value="In progress" />
                <arc:FilterOption Value="Closed" />
            </arc:FilterField.Options>
        </arc:FilterField>
        <arc:FilterField Id="owner" Label="Owner">
            <arc:FilterField.Options>
                <arc:FilterOption Value="Mina" />
                <arc:FilterOption Value="Theo" />
            </arc:FilterField.Options>
        </arc:FilterField>
    </arc:FilterToolbar.Fields>
</arc:FilterToolbar>
```

`FilterToolbar` derives from Avalonia's `TemplatedControl` and is a group for assistive technology. Its parts are a
chip area, the search box, the Add filter trigger, the Clear all button and any actions, laid out in one row. The
toolbar keeps the applied filters in `ActiveFilters`, which is two-way, so the list you bind to is the source of truth
and the chips are a view of it.

### Anatomy

1. **Chip area** (`ActiveFilters`): one chip per applied filter, in the order of the list. A chip shows the label,
   a middle dot and the value, for example "Status · Open". A chip without a `Value` shows only its label.
2. **Chip remove button**: a 24 px target with a 14 px close glyph at the end of each chip. Its name is the chip's text,
   for example "Remove Status: Open". Chips have a 1 px border, a muted surface and a pill radius, and they sit 8 px
   apart.
3. **Empty note** (`EmptyText`): "No filters applied" in the muted text color at the leading edge of the chip area when
   no filter is set. It rises in when the last chip leaves.
4. **Search box** (`IsSearchVisible`, `SearchText`, `SearchPlaceholder`): 200 px wide and as tall as the small control
   size, with a search glyph, a 1 px border and the control radius. Its focus draws the strong border color and the
   focus ring.
5. **Add filter trigger** (`AddFilterLabel`): a plus glyph and the label in medium weight, at least as tall as the
   small control size. It appears when `Fields` has at least one field and opens the two-step menu.
6. **Actions** (`Actions`): any controls you add, placed after the Add filter trigger, 12 px apart from the other
   actions.
7. **Clear all** (`ClearAllLabel`): a ghost button in the muted text color. It appears only while a filter is set.
8. **Frame**: the surface color, a 1 px border, the panel radius and 16 px of horizontal padding with 12 px of vertical
   padding. The chip area and the actions are separated by 16 px.

Below 520 px (the stacking breakpoint) the toolbar stacks: the chips take the first row and the actions move to a
second row aligned to the end.

The Add filter menu opens a panel 256 px wide (16 rem) with 6 px of inset. Each row of the field and value lists is
36 px tall, and the header row is 32 px. A value list taller than 320 px scrolls. Set `MenuAlignment` to `Start` or
`End` to choose the trigger edge the panel lines up with; the panel flips to the other side when there is no room.

### Filters from code

Create the active filters as a list of `FilterChip`. Each field keeps one chip: adding a chip with the same
`Id` replaces the chip that is already there.

```csharp
var toolbar = new FilterToolbar
{
    ActiveFilters = new ObservableCollection<FilterChip>
    {
        new("status", "Status", "Open"),
        new("owner", "Owner", "Mina")
    }
};
toolbar.AddFilter(new FilterChip("priority", "Priority", "High"));
toolbar.RemoveFilter("owner");
toolbar.ClearFilters();
```

`AddFilter`, `RemoveFilter` and `ClearFilters` are the toolbar's own operations, and they raise `FiltersChanged`.
`RemoveFilter` does nothing when no chip has the id, and `AddFilter` with an identical chip does nothing.

### Responding to changes

`FiltersChanged` reports what changed (`Kind`), the chip involved and the full set of active filters. Use it to
reload the data the toolbar filters.

```csharp
toolbar.FiltersChanged += (_, e) => Refilter(e.ActiveFilters);
```

`FilterChangeKind` has four values: `Added`, `Changed`, `Removed` and `Cleared`. `Changed` fires when a field gets a
new value, and `Previous` holds the chip it replaced. `Field` is set when the change came from the Add filter menu.

The event fires for changes made through the toolbar: a chip's remove button, Clear all, the Add filter menu and the
three operations above. It does not fire when your code changes the `ActiveFilters` list directly. The chips still
update and the change is announced, so for direct list edits, subscribe to the list's `CollectionChanged` instead.

### Search

`IsSearchVisible` adds a search box to the toolbar. `SearchText` is two-way, so the table can react to it.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.FilterToolbarSearchAndTableDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="14">
        <arc:FilterToolbar x:Name="Toolbar"
                           IsSearchVisible="True"
                           SearchPlaceholder="Search issues"
                           FiltersChanged="OnFiltersChanged">
            <arc:FilterField Id="status" Label="Status" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.CircleDot}">
                <arc:FilterOption Value="Open" Hint="4" />
                <arc:FilterOption Value="In progress" Hint="2" />
                <arc:FilterOption Value="Closed" Hint="2" />
            </arc:FilterField>
            <arc:FilterField Id="owner" Label="Owner" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.User}">
                <arc:FilterOption Value="Mina" />
                <arc:FilterOption Value="Theo" />
                <arc:FilterOption Value="Ana" />
                <arc:FilterOption Value="Kai" />
            </arc:FilterField>
            <arc:FilterField Id="priority" Label="Priority" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Flag}">
                <arc:FilterOption Value="Urgent" />
                <arc:FilterOption Value="High" />
                <arc:FilterOption Value="Medium" />
                <arc:FilterOption Value="Low" />
            </arc:FilterField>
        </arc:FilterToolbar>
        <arc:Table x:Name="Table"
                               ItemNameOne="issue"
                               ItemNameOther="issues"
                               EmptyMessage="No issues match these filters"
                               MaxHeight="360" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using System.Collections.ObjectModel;
using Avalonia;
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class FilterToolbarSearchAndTableDemo : UserControl
{
    private sealed record Issue(string Title, string Status, string Owner, string Priority);

    private static readonly Issue[] s_issues =
    [
        new("Checkout button misaligned", "Open", "Mina", "High"),
        new("Search ignores accents", "In progress", "Theo", "Medium"),
        new("Export drops last row", "Open", "Ana", "Urgent"),
        new("Avatar flickers on hover", "Closed", "Mina", "Low"),
        new("Dark mode chart contrast", "In progress", "Kai", "High"),
        new("Timezone shown twice", "Open", "Theo", "Low"),
        new("Pagination skips page 3", "Closed", "Ana", "Medium"),
        new("Toast overlaps footer", "Open", "Kai", "Medium")
    ];

    private readonly ObservableCollection<Issue> _rows = new(s_issues);

    public FilterToolbarSearchAndTableDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Table.ItemsSource = _rows;
        Table.Columns.Add(DataTableColumn.Create<Issue>("Issue", i => i.Title));
        Table.Columns.Add(DataTableColumn.Create<Issue>("Status", i => i.Status));
        Table.Columns.Add(DataTableColumn.Create<Issue>("Owner", i => i.Owner));
        Table.Columns.Add(DataTableColumn.Create<Issue>("Priority", i => i.Priority));
        Toolbar.PropertyChanged += OnToolbarPropertyChanged;
    }

    private void OnFiltersChanged(object? sender, FilterToolbarFiltersChangedEventArgs e) => Refilter();

    private void OnToolbarPropertyChanged(object? sender, AvaloniaPropertyChangedEventArgs e)
    {
        if (e.Property == FilterToolbar.SearchTextProperty)
        {
            Refilter();
        }
    }

    // Filters and search narrow the rows the table shows.
    private void Refilter()
    {
        var active = Toolbar.ActiveFilters ?? [];
        var query = Toolbar.SearchText ?? string.Empty;
        var visible = s_issues
            .Where(issue => active.All(f => f.Id switch
            {
                "status" => issue.Status == f.Value,
                "owner" => issue.Owner == f.Value,
                "priority" => issue.Priority == f.Value,
                _ => true
            }) && issue.Title.Contains(query, StringComparison.CurrentCultureIgnoreCase))
            .ToList();
        _rows.Clear();
        foreach (var issue in visible)
        {
            _rows.Add(issue);
        }
    }
}
```

```xml
<arc:FilterToolbar IsSearchVisible="True"
                   SearchPlaceholder="Search issues"
                   SearchText="{Binding Query, Mode=TwoWay}" />
```

`SearchPlaceholder` sets the hint shown while the box is empty; the default is "Search". The search is not a filter
chip, so it does not appear in `ActiveFilters`, and it is not part of the `FiltersChanged` event. Filter the rows from
`SearchText` as well as from the chips.

### Filter menu on its own

`FilterMenu` is the Add filter trigger and its two-step panel. Down on the trigger opens it on the first field, Right
enters a field and Left goes back.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             xmlns:generic="using:System.Collections.Generic"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.FilterToolbarFilterMenuDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="14">
        <arc:FilterMenu HorizontalAlignment="Left"
                        Alignment="Start"
                        FilterSelected="OnFilterSelected">
            <arc:FilterMenu.Fields>
                <generic:List x:TypeArguments="arc:FilterField">
                    <arc:FilterField Id="status" Label="Status" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.CircleDot}">
                        <arc:FilterOption Value="Open" Hint="4" />
                        <arc:FilterOption Value="In progress" Hint="2" />
                        <arc:FilterOption Value="Closed" Hint="2" />
                    </arc:FilterField>
                    <arc:FilterField Id="owner" Label="Owner" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.User}">
                        <arc:FilterOption Value="Mina" />
                        <arc:FilterOption Value="Theo" />
                        <arc:FilterOption Value="Ana" />
                        <arc:FilterOption Value="Kai" />
                    </arc:FilterField>
                    <arc:FilterField Id="priority" Label="Priority" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Flag}">
                        <arc:FilterOption Value="Urgent" />
                        <arc:FilterOption Value="High" />
                        <arc:FilterOption Value="Medium" />
                        <arc:FilterOption Value="Low" />
                    </arc:FilterField>
                </generic:List>
            </arc:FilterMenu.Fields>
        </arc:FilterMenu>
        <TextBlock x:Name="Picked"
                   Text="Nothing picked yet"
```
