
```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class FilterToolbarFilterMenuDemo : UserControl
{
    public FilterToolbarFilterMenuDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
    }

    private void OnFilterSelected(object? sender, FilterMenuSelectedEventArgs e) =>
        Picked.Text = $"Picked {e.Filter.Text}";
}
```

`FilterMenu` also works outside a toolbar. It takes its own `Fields`, shows the value each field already has through
`ActiveFilters`, and raises `FilterSelected` when a value is picked. The chip in that event has the field's `Id`, so
your handler can apply it with the same replace-by-id rule the toolbar uses.

### Binding to a view model

In an MVVM app the view model owns the applied filters, the search text and the rows they narrow. The toolbar edits
the lists it is given, so the view model stays the single source of truth. With CommunityToolkit.Mvvm:

```csharp
public partial class InvoicesViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    public InvoicesViewModel()
    {
        ActiveFilters.CollectionChanged += (_, _) => ApplyFilters();
    }

    public ObservableCollection<FilterChip> ActiveFilters { get; } = new();

    [ObservableProperty]
    private string? _searchText;

    partial void OnSearchTextChanged(string? value) => ApplyFilters();

    [RelayCommand]
    private Task ExportAsync() =>
        File.WriteAllLinesAsync("invoices.csv", VisibleInvoices.Select(invoice => invoice.Id));

    private void ApplyFilters()
    {
        // Filter the rows from ActiveFilters and SearchText, then refresh VisibleInvoices.
    }
}
```

```xml
<StackPanel Spacing="16">
    <arc:FilterToolbar ActiveFilters="{Binding ActiveFilters}"
                       IsSearchVisible="True"
                       SearchPlaceholder="Search invoices"
                       SearchText="{Binding SearchText}">
        <arc:FilterToolbar.Fields>
            <arc:FilterField Id="status" Label="Status">
                <arc:FilterOption Value="Draft" />
                <arc:FilterOption Value="Sent" />
                <arc:FilterOption Value="Overdue" />
            </arc:FilterField>
        </arc:FilterToolbar.Fields>
        <arc:FilterToolbar.Actions>
            <arc:Button Content="Export CSV" Variant="Secondary" Command="{Binding ExportCommand}" />
        </arc:FilterToolbar.Actions>
    </arc:FilterToolbar>
    <arc:Table ItemsSource="{Binding VisibleInvoices}" />
</StackPanel>
```

- `ActiveFilters` and `SearchText` are two-way, the default for both. A chip removed in the toolbar updates the
  collection, and the view model sees it through `CollectionChanged`.
- `ActiveFilters` also accepts a read-only list such as an array. The toolbar then replaces the list with a new one
  and writes it back, so use an `ObservableCollection` when the view model needs to react to every change.
- `Fields` is a read-only collection in the toolbar, so define the fields in XAML, or add them from code once with
  `toolbar.Fields.Add(...)`. They are not bound to the view model.
- Subscribe to `FiltersChanged` in code-behind only when a change needs the event's `Kind` or `Previous`. For plain
  refiltering, the `CollectionChanged` handler above is enough, because it also covers changes the toolbar does not
  report.

### Data shape and performance

The menu lists every option of a field. Options are not virtualized, so keep each value list short, roughly a few
dozen values. A field with hundreds of values belongs in a `Combobox` with its own search, and the toolbar shows the
chosen value only.

A chip stores the option's text, which is its `Label` when the option has one and its `Value` otherwise, and the
chip's `Value` is that text. Filter on the chip's value, so keep the text equal to the data the query uses. When the
wording people read must differ from the data, map the chip's `Id` and `Value` to the query in the view model.

`FilterOption.Hint` sits at the end of the row, which suits a count such as "Open 4".

### Focus and dismissal

The Add filter menu stays open until someone chooses a value or presses Escape. The trigger gets focus back when the
panel closes, whether by Escape or after a value is chosen.

When a chip is removed, focus moves to the next chip's remove button, or to the previous one when the removed chip
was last. When the last chip goes, focus moves to the Add filter trigger if it is visible.

### Example: invoice list in a billing console

A finance team reviews overdue invoices. Two filters are applied and the Add filter trigger is ready for the next
facet. Clear all appears because at least one filter is set. The table below the toolbar shows the rows that match
both chips, and the team clears the chips in one step when it starts a new review.

![A filter toolbar with status and owner chips and the Add filter trigger](https://docs.tkcode.si/shots/Docs/Tables/FilterToolbar/images/InvoiceFilters.webp)

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             xmlns:collections="using:System.Collections.ObjectModel">
    <StackPanel Width="600">
        <arc:FilterToolbar>
            <arc:FilterToolbar.ActiveFilters>
                <collections:ObservableCollection x:TypeArguments="arc:FilterChip">
                    <arc:FilterChip Id="status" Label="Status" Value="Overdue" />
                    <arc:FilterChip Id="owner" Label="Owner" Value="Mina" />
                </collections:ObservableCollection>
            </arc:FilterToolbar.ActiveFilters>
            <arc:FilterField Id="status" Label="Status" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.CircleDot}">
                <arc:FilterOption Value="Draft" Hint="3" />
                <arc:FilterOption Value="Sent" Hint="18" />
                <arc:FilterOption Value="Overdue" Hint="6" />
            </arc:FilterField>
            <arc:FilterField Id="owner" Label="Owner" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.User}">
                <arc:FilterOption Value="Mina" />
                <arc:FilterOption Value="Theo" />
                <arc:FilterOption Value="Ana" />
            </arc:FilterField>
            <arc:FilterField Id="region" Label="Region" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Flag}">
                <arc:FilterOption Value="EU" />
                <arc:FilterOption Value="US" />
                <arc:FilterOption Value="APAC" />
            </arc:FilterField>
        </arc:FilterToolbar>
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

Each field has one chip, so choosing a different owner replaces the chip rather than adding a second one. The field
options carry a `Hint` for the status counts, so the menu shows how many invoices sit in each state before the team
picks one.

### Content guidelines

- **Label** (the field name): a short noun in sentence case that matches the column it filters: "Status", "Owner",
  "Region". Do not use a verb, and do not repeat the page title.
- **Value**: the text people recognize from the table: "Overdue", "Mina", "EU". Use the same spelling as the data.
- **Add filter**: keep the default or use a verb phrase that describes the action: "Add filter" is the default and
  works for most pages.
- **Empty note**: state the condition in plain words: "No filters applied", not "Nothing to show".
- **Search placeholder**: name what is searched: "Search invoices", "Search customers by name".

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| Filter | Status |
| Choose a value... | Search invoices |
| Clear | Clear all |
| 0 filters | No filters applied |
| STATUS = OVERDUE | Status: Overdue |

### Best practices

**Do**

- Keep the chips as the record of what filters the rows. Derive the rows from `ActiveFilters` and `SearchText`, so a
  reload, a saved view or a shared link shows the same result the chips describe.
- Give each field one `Id` that stays the same across releases. The id decides which chip a new value replaces.
- Put the search box and the chips in the same toolbar when they narrow the same rows. People then read them as one
  set of filters.
- Keep the value lists short, and put the most useful values first.

**Avoid**

- Adding filters that cannot change the result, such as a field with one option. The chip stays on screen and tells
  people nothing.
- Adding a second Clear all button beside the toolbar. The toolbar already shows its own while any filter is set,
  and two resets confuse people about which one clears the rows.
- Changing `ActiveFilters` from a background thread. Controls must change on the UI thread, so marshal the change
  with `Dispatcher.UIThread` first.
- Relying on `FiltersChanged` for direct list edits, which do not raise it. Refilter from the list's
  `CollectionChanged` instead.

### Common questions

**Why does the Add filter trigger not show?** It shows only when `Fields` has at least one field. Add the fields in
XAML, or add them in code before the toolbar is shown with `Fields.Add`.

**How do I preselect filters for a saved view?** Set `ActiveFilters` to the saved chips when the view opens, in XAML or
in the view model. No event fires for the initial value, so apply the same filter to the rows in the same step.

**Why does picking a second value replace the chip instead of adding one?** Each chip id is a field id, and the toolbar
keeps one chip per field. Picking a value for a field that already has one changes that chip, and `FiltersChanged`
reports the change with `Kind` set to `Changed` and `Previous` set to the old chip.

**How do I show a filter without a value?** Create the chip with no `Value`, for example
`new FilterChip("archived", "Archived")`. The chip shows its label alone, and the remove button is named after it.

**How do I reset every filter from code?** Call `ClearFilters()`, which raises `FiltersChanged` with `Kind` set to
`Cleared`. Clearing the list directly with `ActiveFilters.Clear()` updates the chips without the event, so pick the
call that matches what your handlers need.

## API reference

### FilterToolbar

Arc's filter toolbar: keep collection filters close and easy to reset. Applied filters are removable chips ("Status · Open") whose slots open and close on a spring so neighbors slide along, a changed value morphs in place, Clear all appears while any filter is applied, and the Add filter menu picks a field, then a value (one chip per field). An optional search field sits with the actions. `ActiveFilters` is two-way and a mutable list is updated in place; `FiltersChanged` reports every change, and changes are announced.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ActiveFilters` | `IList<FilterChip>?` | `null` | The applied filters (two-way). A mutable list is updated in place by remove, Clear all and Add filter. |
| `Label` | `string` | `"Active filters"` | Accessible name of the toolbar group. |
| `EmptyText` | `string` | `"No filters applied"` | Text shown in the toolbar when no filter is applied (default No filters applied). |
| `ClearAllLabel` | `string` | `"Clear all"` | Label of the button that removes every applied filter (default Clear all). |
| `AddFilterLabel` | `string` | `"Add filter"` | Label of the Add filter button (default Add filter). |
| `MenuAlignment` | `FilterMenuAlignment` | `End` | The trigger edge the Add filter panel lines up with. |
| `Actions` | `object?` | `null` | Extra actions shown beside Add filter (Arc `children`). |
| `IsSearchVisible` | `bool` | `false` | Shows a search field with the actions; its text is `SearchText`. |
| `SearchText` | `string?` | `null` | Text of the search field (two-way). Escape in the field clears it. |
| `SearchPlaceholder` | `string` | `"Search"` | Placeholder text of the search field (default Search). |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `FiltersChanged` | `FilterToolbarFiltersChangedEventArgs` | Raised after a filter is added, changed, removed or all are cleared from the toolbar. |

Pseudo-classes: `:empty`, `:stacked`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

### FilterChip

An applied filter shown as a chip: "Label · Value". The id is the field id, so one chip per field.

### FilterField

A filterable field of the Add filter menu: pick the field, then one of its options.

## Accessibility

- The toolbar is a group named "Active filters" by default. Set `Label` to name it for your page.
- Each chip has a remove button named like "Remove Status: Open". After removing, focus moves to a neighbor chip or to the Add filter trigger.
- Adding and removing filters is announced in the status region.
- The Add filter menu is a named dialog. Its options are checkable menu items.
- Down or Up opens the menu from the trigger. Arrow keys move in the list, Right enters a field's values, Left goes back and typing jumps to an option.
- Escape closes the menu and returns focus to the trigger.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` | Move through the chip remove buttons, the search box, the Add filter trigger, the actions and Clear all |
| `Enter` or `Space` on a chip's remove button | Remove that filter; focus moves to a neighbor chip or to the Add filter trigger |
| `Escape` in the search box | Clear the search text when it is not empty |
| `Enter`, `Space` or `Down` on the Add filter trigger | Open the menu on the first field |
| `Up` on the Add filter trigger | Open the menu on the last field |
| `Down` / `Up` in the menu | Move to the next or previous row; the list wraps around |
| `Home` / `End` in the menu | Move to the first or last row |
| `Right` on a field | Show that field's values |
| `Left` in a value list | Go back to the fields |
| `Enter` or `Space` on a value | Apply the value and close the menu |
| Letters in the menu | Jump to the next row whose label starts with the typed letters |
| `Escape` in the menu | Close the menu and return focus to the trigger |

## Motion

- A chip opens and closes its own slot, and its neighbors slide to make room.
- A changed value swaps in place with a soft blur. Clear all shows while any filter is set.
- The Add filter trigger grows into the menu surface, and the field and value steps slide in their direction.
- Reduced motion swaps the changes at once with a short fade of about 160 ms. Off jumps straight to the final state.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| A filter is added | Its chip opens a slot on a morph spring, and the chips after it slide to make room | A short fade of about 160 ms | Immediate |
| A filter is removed | Its slot closes and the chips after it slide back | A short fade of about 160 ms | Immediate |
| A value changes | The value changes in place with a soft blur | A short fade of about 160 ms | Immediate |
| Clear all shows or goes | Its slot opens or closes | A short fade of about 160 ms | Immediate |
| The menu opens | The trigger grows into the panel, with a slight overshoot on open and a smooth close | A short fade of about 160 ms | Immediate |
| Field to value list | The panel slides 8 px in the direction of travel | A short fade of about 160 ms | Immediate |

## Related

- `ChipGroup` for a small fixed set of toggles.
- `SearchField` for free text search without filters.
- `Table` for the table that the filters narrow.
- `MultiSelect` for a form field that takes several values.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `ChipGroup` | The options are a short fixed set that people switch between, and all are visible |
| `SearchField` | The page searches text and has no facets to narrow |
| `Table` | The rows the filters leave are shown and sorted in a table |
| `MultiSelect` | A form stores several values on a record |
| `Combobox` | One value must be chosen from a long list that needs its own search |

---

# Code block

> Present code with legible hierarchy and copy access.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/code-block

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.CodeBlockDefaultDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12">
        <arc:CodeBlock x:Name="Block" FileName="greeting.tsx" Copied="OnCopied" />
        <TextBlock x:Name="Status"
                   Text="Copy the code to see the event."
                   FontSize="14"
                   TextWrapping="Wrap"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class CodeBlockDefaultDemo : UserControl
{
    public CodeBlockDefaultDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Block.Code = """
            import { useState } from "react";

            /** Says hello, then counts the clicks. */
            export function Greeting({ name }: { name: string }) {
              const [count, setCount] = useState(0);
              return <button onClick={() => setCount(count + 1)}>Hello {name}, {count} clicks</button>;
            }
            """;
    }

    private void OnCopied(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) =>
        Status.Text = $"Copied {Block.LineCount} lines at {DateTime.Now:T}";
}
```

## When to use

`CodeBlock` shows a source file or a snippet in a read-only, selectable frame with a file-name header, syntax colors
and a copy action. It sits in documentation, settings and developer tools where people need to read code, copy it
and know which file it belongs to, without giving them an editor.

- **Install and setup instructions** in an onboarding or integration page: a `dotnet add package` line, a `.env`
  file or a `docker compose` file, with the file name in the header so people know where each line goes.
- **Generated or exported configuration** in an admin console: a webhook payload, a CI pipeline or a Terraform plan
  that an operator copies into another system. The copy action copies the full source, not the visible part.
- **Long files that should fold**: a 200-line deployment script or a generated SDK client shows its first lines and a
  Show all toggle, so the settings page stays scannable.
- **Snippets in a developer portal or API reference**: a request and a response in `json`, a C# client call or a
  `curl` command, each with its own file name or language label.
- **Code samples inside a support or incident view**: a failing query or a configuration diff that an engineer
  reads next to a timeline, with line numbers so the team can refer to a line in a conversation.

## When not to use

- **Copying one value such as an API key or a webhook secret**: use `CopyButton` on its own. A code frame for a
  single token adds a header and a frame that the value does not need.
- **JSON that people explore by key, search or expand**: use `JsonViewer`, which shows a tree with search and per-row
  copy. `CodeBlock` shows the JSON as text.
- **Folders and file names as a navigable hierarchy**: use `TreeView` to browse the files, and place a `CodeBlock`
  beside it so the selected file drives the code shown.
- **Editing code or text in place**: use `Textarea` for plain multi-line text. `CodeBlock` is read-only; people can
  select and copy its text but cannot change it.
- **Rich documents with headings, lists and code mixed together**: use `Markdown`, which renders fenced code with the
  same syntax colors inside the document flow.

## Usage

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:CodeBlock FileName="greeting.tsx"
                   Language="tsx"
                   Code="{Binding Source}" />
</UserControl>
```

`CodeBlock` derives from Avalonia's `TemplatedControl`, so it takes the usual layout, styling and automation
behavior of a control. It is not a `TextBox`: `Code` is the only text it accepts, the text is read-only, and the frame
has a header and an optional expand row around the code area. Highlighting uses the TextMate grammars of the StreamMark
engine, painted with Arc's syntax role colors.

### Anatomy

1. **Header** (`FileName`, `SourceCodeLabel`, `Language`): at least 52 px tall, 16 px from the left edge and 12 px
   from the right, with 8 px above and below. It shows a file icon, the file name, a middle dot and the language name.
   A long file name is cut with an ellipsis while the language keeps its width. When `FileName` is empty, the header
   shows `SourceCodeLabel` (default "Source code").
2. **Copy button** (`CopyLabel`): a `CopyButton` at the end of the header, 12 px from the file label. It copies `Code`.
3. **Line number gutter** (`ShowLineNumbers`): a right-aligned column of numbers in a muted color, mixed toward the
   surface. It is hidden from assistive technology and does not move when the code scrolls sideways.
4. **Code area**: the source in the monospace font of the Arc tokens, 14 px with a line height of 23.8 px (1.7 times
   the size) and 20 px of padding on every side. Text is selectable. Long lines scroll horizontally inside the block.
5. **Expand toggle** (`IsCollapsible`, `MaxLines`, `IsExpanded`): a full-width row at least 44 px tall with a top
   border, a 16 px chevron and the label "Show all 14 lines" (or "Show fewer lines" when expanded). It appears only when
   the source has more lines than `MaxLines`.
6. **Frame**: a 1 px border in the panel radius on the surface color. The frame clips its contents, so the header and
   the expand row keep the corners of the frame.

The narrow layout starts below 420 px of width (the `CompactWidth` of the theme): the header padding drops to 12 px
on the left, the copy button shows only its icon, the code drops to 12 px with a 20.4 px line height and 16 px of
padding, and the line numbers follow the same sizes.

### Collapsing long code

`IsCollapsible` adds the expand row. `MaxLines` sets how many lines show while the block is collapsed (default 12,
at least 1). A source with the same number of lines or fewer shows no toggle, so `IsCollapsible` can stay on for
every block in a list.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.CodeBlockCollapsibleDemo">
    <arc:CodeBlock x:Name="Block"
                   FileName="pipeline.ts"
                   Language="ts"
                   IsCollapsible="True"
                   MaxLines="6" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class CodeBlockCollapsibleDemo : UserControl
{
    public CodeBlockCollapsibleDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        var steps = Enumerable.Range(1, 40).Select(i =>
            i % 5 == 0 ? $"  // step {i}: checkpoint" : $"  const value{i} = compute({i}, \"item-{i}\");");
        Block.Code = "export function pipeline() {\n" + string.Join("\n", steps) + "\n  return value40;\n}";
    }
}
```

`IsExpanded` is two-way and tells you whether the block is open. Bind it when the page remembers the state, or set it
from code when a surrounding action should open the source (for example, a search result that points to line 40).

```csharp
block.IsCollapsible = true;
block.MaxLines = 6;
block.IsExpanded = false;
```

The collapsed height is `MaxLines` times the line height, plus the padding of the code area, so a collapsed block
always has the same height for the same settings, whatever the code is.

### Language

`Language` sets the highlighting and the language label in the header. It accepts the common names and the aliases
that code fences use, such as `cs`, `ts`, `py`, `sh`, `yaml`, `json` and `axaml`. Names are case-insensitive and a
leading dot is ignored, so `.TSX` and `tsx` are the same language. The default is `tsx`.

A language without a grammar, such as `text`, shows plain text with no colors. Use it for logs, notes and output that
is not code, so the block does not color words by accident.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.CodeBlockLanguagesDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12">
        <WrapPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center" ItemSpacing="12" LineSpacing="12">
            <WrapPanel.Styles>
                <Style Selector="arc|Button.language">
                    <Setter Property="Variant" Value="Secondary" />
                    <Setter Property="Size" Value="Small" />
                </Style>
            </WrapPanel.Styles>
            <arc:Button Classes="language" Content="cs" Click="OnLanguageClick" />
            <arc:Button Classes="language" Content="tsx" Click="OnLanguageClick" />
            <arc:Button Classes="language" Content="py" Click="OnLanguageClick" />
            <arc:Button Classes="language" Content="rust" Click="OnLanguageClick" />
            <arc:Button Classes="language" Content="go" Click="OnLanguageClick" />
            <arc:Button Classes="language" Content="bash" Click="OnLanguageClick" />
            <arc:Button Classes="language" Content="yaml" Click="OnLanguageClick" />
            <arc:Button Classes="language" Content="sql" Click="OnLanguageClick" />
            <arc:Button Classes="language" Content="json" Click="OnLanguageClick" />
            <arc:Button Classes="language" Content="axaml" Click="OnLanguageClick" />
            <arc:Button Classes="language" Content="text" Click="OnLanguageClick" />
        </WrapPanel>
        <arc:CodeBlock x:Name="Viewer" FileName="CartView.cs" Language="cs" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class CodeBlockLanguagesDemo : UserControl
{
    private const string Csharp = """
        using Avalonia.Controls;

        namespace Shop;

        public sealed class CartView : UserControl
        {
            // Totals update when an item changes.
            public decimal Total { get; private set; }

            public void Add(decimal price, int quantity = 1)
            {
                Total += price * quantity;
                Status.Text = $"Total: {Total:C}";
            }
        }
        """;

    private const string Tsx = """
        import { useState } from "react";

        /** Says hello, then counts the clicks. */
        export function Greeting({ name }: { name: string }) {
          const [count, setCount] = useState(0);
          return <button onClick={() => setCount(count + 1)}>Hello {name}, {count} clicks</button>;
        }
        """;

    private const string Python = """"
        from dataclasses import dataclass

        @dataclass
        class Stats:
            count: int = 0

            def add(self, value: float) -> "Stats":
                """Counts one more sample."""
                self.count += 1  # no averaging yet
                return self
        """";

    private const string Rust = """
        use std::collections::HashMap;

        /// Counts words.
        fn count(text: &str) -> HashMap<&str, usize> {
            let mut words = HashMap::new();
            for word in text.split_whitespace() {
                *words.entry(word).or_insert(0) += 1;
            }
            words
        }
        """;

    private const string Go = """
        package main

        import "fmt"

        // Greet prints a greeting n times.
        func Greet(name string, n int) {
        	for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
        		fmt.Printf("Hello, %s!\n", name)
        	}
        }
        """;

    private const string Bash = """
        #!/usr/bin/env bash
        set -euo pipefail
        # Build, then publish the gallery.
        for rid in osx-arm64 win-x64; do
          dotnet publish -c Release -r "$rid" -o "out/$rid"
        done
        """;

    private const string Yaml = """
        name: build
        on:
          push:
            branches: [main]
        jobs:
          test:
            runs-on: ubuntu-latest
            steps:
              - run: dotnet test # all projects
        """;

    private const string Sql = """
        -- Customers with more than five orders
        SELECT c.name, COUNT(o.id) AS orders
        FROM customers c
        JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id
        GROUP BY c.name
        HAVING COUNT(o.id) > 5;
        """;

    private const string Json = """
        {
          "name": "arc-demo",
          "version": "1.4.0",
          "private": true,
          "scripts": { "dev": "next dev", "build": "next build" },
          "dependencies": { "motion": "^12.0.0", "lucide-react": "^0.460.0" }
        }
        """;

    private const string Axaml = """
        <arc:CodeBlock FileName="greeting.tsx"
                       Language="tsx"
                       IsCollapsible="True"
                       MaxLines="6"
                       Code="{Binding Source}" />
        """;

    private static readonly Dictionary<string, (string FileName, string Code)> s_samples = new()
    {
        ["cs"] = ("CartView.cs", Csharp),
        ["tsx"] = ("greeting.tsx", Tsx),
        ["py"] = ("stats.py", Python),
        ["rust"] = ("main.rs", Rust),
        ["go"] = ("greet.go", Go),
        ["bash"] = ("deploy.sh", Bash),
        ["yaml"] = ("ci.yml", Yaml),
        ["sql"] = ("orders.sql", Sql),
        ["json"] = ("package.json", Json),
        ["axaml"] = ("Usage.axaml", Axaml),
        ["text"] = ("notes.txt", "Plain text: languages without a grammar are not highlighted.")
    };

    public CodeBlockLanguagesDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Viewer.Code = Csharp;
    }

    private void OnLanguageClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        if (sender is Button { Content: string language } && s_samples.TryGetValue(language, out var sample))
        {
            Viewer.FileName = sample.FileName;
            Viewer.Language = language;
            Viewer.Code = sample.Code;
        }
    }
}
```

```xml
<arc:CodeBlock FileName="stats.py" Language="py" Code="{Binding PythonSource}" />
<arc:CodeBlock FileName="notes.txt" Language="text" Code="Plain text." />
```

The highlighter maps the TextMate token colors to nine roles: comment, string, number, keyword, type, function,
property, tag and punctuation. Comments are italic and use the muted text color, punctuation uses the secondary text
color, and the other roles have their own color per appearance. The role colors do not follow the accent, so a
product can change its accent without changing how code reads. The mapping is an approximation of the grammar's
classes. A few tokens, such as the keys of a JavaScript object literal, may show as plain text, and built-in type
names in some languages are colored as types.

### Copy and line numbers

The copy button is in the header and copies `Code` exactly as you set it: tabs and line endings are the ones in your
source. The display differs only in two ways: a tab shows as two spaces, and a carriage return and line feed show as
one line break. `ShowLineNumbers` adds a line number column that stays in place when the code scrolls sideways.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.CodeBlockLineNumbersDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12">
        <arc:CodeBlock x:Name="CartView"
                       FileName="CartView.cs"
                       Language="cs"
                       ShowLineNumbers="True" />
        <arc:CodeBlock x:Name="Usage" FileName="Usage.axaml" Language="axaml" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class CodeBlockLineNumbersDemo : UserControl
{
    public CodeBlockLineNumbersDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        CartView.Code = """
            using Avalonia.Controls;

            namespace Shop;

            public sealed class CartView : UserControl
            {
                // Totals update when an item changes.
                public decimal Total { get; private set; }

                public void Add(decimal price, int quantity = 1)
                {
                    Total += price * quantity;
                    Status.Text = $"Total: {Total:C}";
                }
            }
            """;
        Usage.Code = """
            <arc:CodeBlock FileName="greeting.tsx"
                           Language="tsx"
                           IsCollapsible="True"
                           MaxLines="6"
                           Code="{Binding Source}" />
            """;
    }
}
```

```xml
<arc:CodeBlock FileName="deploy.sh"
               Language="bash"
               ShowLineNumbers="True"
               Code="{Binding Script}" />
```

`Copied` is a routed event raised after the copy action put the code on the clipboard. Use it to confirm the copy
in your own status area:

```csharp
block.Copied += (_, _) => status.Text = "Code copied";
```

`LineCount` gives the number of lines in `Code`, which is useful for a caption such as "42 lines".

### Labels

The copy label, the file name fallback and the collapse text are properties, so you can translate them or use the
wording of your product. `ShowAllLinesFormat` takes one `{0}` placeholder, which receives the line count, formatted for
the current culture.

```xml
<arc:CodeBlock Code="{Binding Source}"
               CopyLabel="Copy snippet"
               SourceCodeLabel="Snippet"
               ShowAllLinesFormat="Show all {0} lines"
               ShowFewerLinesLabel="Show fewer lines" />
```

### Switching files

Setting a new `FileName`, `Language` and `Code` swaps the file in place. The file name slot follows the new width, the
new source rises in and the height follows on a spring. Change the three properties together, so the header and the
highlighting never show one file's name with another file's code.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.CodeBlockSwitchingFilesDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12">
        <WrapPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center" ItemSpacing="12" LineSpacing="12">
            <arc:Button Content="greeting.tsx" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Click="OnFileClick" />
            <arc:Button Content="card.module.css" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Click="OnFileClick" />
            <arc:Button Content="package.json" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Click="OnFileClick" />
        </WrapPanel>
        <arc:CodeBlock x:Name="Viewer" FileName="greeting.tsx" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class CodeBlockSwitchingFilesDemo : UserControl
{
    private const string Greeting = """
        import { useState } from "react";

        /** Says hello, then counts the clicks. */
        export function Greeting({ name }: { name: string }) {
          const [count, setCount] = useState(0);
          return <button onClick={() => setCount(count + 1)}>Hello {name}, {count} clicks</button>;
        }
        """;

    private const string Css = """
        .card {
          display: grid;
          gap: 12px;
          border-radius: 26px;
          padding: 24px;
        }
        """;

    private const string Config = """
        {
          "name": "arc-demo",
          "version": "1.4.0",
          "private": true,
          "scripts": { "dev": "next dev", "build": "next build" },
          "dependencies": { "motion": "^12.0.0", "lucide-react": "^0.460.0" }
        }
        """;

    private static readonly Dictionary<string, (string Language, string Code)> s_files = new()
    {
        ["greeting.tsx"] = ("tsx", Greeting),
        ["card.module.css"] = ("css", Css),
        ["package.json"] = ("json", Config)
    };

    public CodeBlockSwitchingFilesDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Viewer.Code = Greeting;
    }

    private void OnFileClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        if (sender is Button { Content: string name } && s_files.TryGetValue(name, out var file))
        {
            Viewer.FileName = name;
            Viewer.Language = file.Language;
            Viewer.Code = file.Code;
        }
    }
}
```

### Narrow

Below 420 px the padding and text shrink and the copy action keeps only its icon. The block adapts to its own width,
not the window width, so a narrow side panel gets the compact layout without any code.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.CodeBlockNarrowDemo">
    <arc:CodeBlock x:Name="Block"
                   Width="360"
                   HorizontalAlignment="Left"
                   Language="css"
                   FileName="card.module.css" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class CodeBlockNarrowDemo : UserControl
{
    public CodeBlockNarrowDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Block.Code = """
            .card {
              display: grid;
              gap: 12px;
              border-radius: 26px;
              padding: 24px;
            }
            """;
    }
}
```

### Data shape and performance

A `CodeBlock` holds one string. It does not create a control per token: the whole source is one text layout with
colored runs, so the cost grows with the length of the source rather than the number of tokens.

- Highlighting runs when `Code` or `Language` changes, not on every redraw. A source of up to 32 KB whose grammar has
  already been used is highlighted on the UI thread at once. Any other source shows plain text first and receives its
  colors from a background pass, so the first long file of a session may appear uncolored for a moment.
- Collapse sources of more than a few screens. The collapsed block keeps a fixed height, and the rest of the source
  opens on demand, so a page with many long files stays scannable.
- Give each file its own block. A block is one selectable text layout, so a page of many short snippets reads well
  as separate blocks, each with its own file name and copy action.

### Binding to a view model

In an MVVM app the view model owns the source, the file name and the open state. The block only shows them. With
CommunityToolkit.Mvvm, `ObservableObject` and `[ObservableProperty]` are enough.

```csharp
public partial class PipelineViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    [ObservableProperty]
    private string _fileName = "deploy.yml";

    [ObservableProperty]
    private string _language = "yaml";

    [ObservableProperty]
    private string _source = string.Empty;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private bool _isSourceExpanded;
}
```

```xml
<StackPanel Spacing="16">
    <arc:CodeBlock FileName="{Binding FileName}"
                   Language="{Binding Language}"
                   Code="{Binding Source}"
                   IsCollapsible="True"
                   MaxLines="8"
                   IsExpanded="{Binding IsSourceExpanded}" />
</StackPanel>
```

- `Code`, `FileName` and `Language` are one-way inputs. Change them in the view model, and the block updates the
  header, the highlighting and the collapse together.
- `IsExpanded` is two-way by default. The user's toggle writes back to `IsSourceExpanded`, so a page can remember the
  state, or the view model can open the block when a search result points into it.
- `Copied` is an event, not a command. Subscribe to it in code-behind or in an attached behavior, and keep the
  feedback in the view model where the status text belongs.

### Example: deployment pipeline on a settings page

A project settings page in a deployment tool shows the pipeline file the project uses. The header names the file and
its language, the line numbers let an engineer refer to "line 4" in a review, and the source collapses to three lines
with the full length shown in the toggle label. The copy action gives the whole file to the person who needs to
paste it into another repository. The install command below it sets no `IsCollapsible`, so it shows no toggle.

![A deployment pipeline file with line numbers and a collapsed expand row on a settings page](https://docs.tkcode.si/shots/Docs/Tables/CodeBlock/images/DeployPipeline.webp)

```xml
<StackPanel Width="680" Spacing="16">
    <arc:CodeBlock FileName="deploy.yml"
                   Language="yaml"
                   ShowLineNumbers="True"
                   IsCollapsible="True"
                   MaxLines="3"
                   Code="on: push&#10;jobs:&#10;  build:&#10;    runs-on: ubuntu-latest" />
    <arc:CodeBlock FileName="install.sh"
                   Language="bash"
                   CopyLabel="Copy command"
                   Code="dotnet add package TKCode.Arc" />
</StackPanel>
```

### Content guidelines

- **File name**: the path the code belongs to, as the reader would find it: `deploy.yml`, `Program.cs`.
  Use a descriptive label only when there is no file, and then keep it short: "Webhook payload", "Sample response".
- **Copy label**: a verb and an object, in sentence case: "Copy command", "Copy snippet". Use the label your product
  uses for the action elsewhere, so people recognize it.
- **Collapse label**: keep the count in the label, so people know how long the file is before they open it. The
  default "Show all 14 lines" does this; a translated format must keep the `{0}`.
- **Source text**: copy the code as it should run. Remove secrets, real customer IDs and internal host names before the
  code reaches the page, because the copy action makes them easy to take.

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| Click to copy the code below | Copy command |
| Code | Source code, or the file name |
| Show more | Show all 14 lines |
| Output (plain text) | Use `text` as the language and name the file "output.txt" |

### Best practices

**Do**

- Set `FileName` for every block that a reader might copy into a file. The header tells people where the code goes,
  and the block gets its own name for assistive technology.
- Collapse long sources with `IsCollapsible` and a `MaxLines` that shows the part people need first, such as the
  signature or the first job of a pipeline.
- Use `ShowLineNumbers` when people discuss specific lines, such as a review, an incident or a support thread.
- Use `text` for output and logs, so the block does not color words that are not code.

**Avoid**

- Using the block for one value: a `CopyButton` is the right control for a key, a token or a URL, and a frame around
  one line draws more attention than the value deserves.
- Switching `Code` to a sample in another language without setting `Language`. The new text keeps the old language's
  highlighting, so a Python sample shows C# colors. Set `FileName`, `Language` and `Code` together.
- Driving `Code` from a text editor on every keystroke. The block is a read-only view, and each change starts a new
  highlighting pass; use `Textarea` for editing and show the result in a `CodeBlock` only when the person saves.
- Expecting line numbers in the copied text. The gutter is not part of `Code`, so the copy action never includes
  them.

### Common questions

**Why does my block show no toggle when the source is long?** The toggle appears only when `IsCollapsible` is `True`
and the source has more lines than `MaxLines`. Check both, and check that `MaxLines` is larger than the number of
lines you expect to hide.

**Does collapsing change what the copy action copies?** No. The copy action copies `Code` in full, collapsed or not,
so a person can copy a 200-line file from a block that shows eight lines.

**Why does the code show without colors for a moment?** The highlighter colors a source on a background pass when its
grammar is not loaded yet, or when the source is larger than 32 KB. The text shows plain until the colors arrive. A
language with no grammar, such as `text`, stays plain.

**How do I show the line count in my own text?** Read `LineCount`. It counts the lines of `Code` after the line
breaks are normalized, so a source with a trailing line break counts one more line than the text shows.

**Can I change the tab width?** Not with a property. Tabs always display as two spaces. Use spaces in the source when
the exact width matters, because the copy action copies the source as you set it.

## API reference

### CodeBlock

A source viewer with a file-name header, syntax highlighting (TextMate grammars painted in Arc's role palette), a copy action and optional collapsing. Long sources collapse to `MaxLines` lines with a toggle that expands the rest in place on a smooth height spring; new code fades in with a short rise. Long lines scroll horizontally inside the block.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Code` | `string?` | `null` | Source shown in the block and copied by the action. |
| `Language` | `string?` | `"tsx"` | Header label and highlighting language (Arc default "tsx"): a fence-style name or alias such as `cs`, `ts`, `json`, `xml`/`axaml`, `py`, `sh`. Languages without a TextMate grammar show plain text. |
| `FileName` | `string?` | `null` | File name in the header; `SourceCodeLabel` when null. |
| `ShowLineNumbers` | `bool` | `false` | Shows a line-number gutter (an extension; Arc has none). |
| `IsCollapsible` | `bool` | `false` | Collapses sources longer than `MaxLines` lines behind a "Show all" toggle (Arc `maxLines`). |
| `MaxLines` | `int` | `12` | Lines visible while collapsed. |
| `IsExpanded` | `bool` | `false` | Whether a collapsible source shows all of its lines. |
| `CopyLabel` | `string` | `"Copy code"` | Label of the copy button in the header (default "Copy code"). |
| `SourceCodeLabel` | `string` | `"Source code"` | Header text shown when `FileName` is empty (default "Source code"). |
| `ShowAllLinesFormat` | `string` | `"Show all {0} lines"` | Collapsed toggle label; `{0}` is the line count. |
| `ShowFewerLinesLabel` | `string` | `"Show fewer lines"` | Label of the toggle while a collapsed source is expanded (default "Show fewer lines"). |
| `LineCount` | `int` | – | *Read-only.* Number of lines in `Code`. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Copied` | `RoutedEventArgs` | Raised after the copy action put the code on the clipboard. |

Pseudo-classes: `:collapsible`, `:expanded`, `:compact`, `:line-numbers`, `:code-focus-visible`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

## Accessibility

- The block is a labeled region. Its name comes from `FileName` (for example "deploy.yml source code"), or from the
  language when the file name is empty ("yaml source code"), so each block on a page has its own name.
- The code area is named "Selectable source code". The line number gutter is marked as raw content, so a screen reader
  reads the code without the numbers.
- Tab moves to the copy button, to the code area and to the expand toggle, in that order.
- Enter or Space copies the code or toggles the expanded state, depending on the focused control.
- The code area can take focus, so keyboard users can scroll long lines with the arrow keys. A keyboard focus shows a
  2 px focus ring inside the frame; a pointer click does not.
- The expand toggle exposes its expanded state to assistive technology. The copy result is announced by `CopyButton`.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` | Move between the copy button, the code area and the expand toggle |
| `Enter` or `Space` on the copy button | Copy `Code` to the clipboard |
| `Enter` or `Space` on the expand toggle | Expand or collapse the source |
| Arrow keys in the code area | Scroll the source; long lines scroll sideways |
| `Ctrl+C` (`Cmd+C` on macOS) in the code area | Copy the selected text |

## Motion

- Expanding or collapsing changes the height of the code on a smooth spring.
- New code fades in and rises slightly, so an update is visible without a jump.
- The toggle label swaps with a short blur and its arrow turns.
- The file name swaps with a short blur, and the language after it glides to its new position.
- Reduced motion sets the height at once and swaps the label in place without movement. Off jumps straight to the final state.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| Expand or collapse | The height springs to the new size and the code area clips to it | The height is set at once | Immediate |
| New `Code` | The text rises 4 px while it fades in | The text is replaced in place | Immediate |
| Toggle label | The label blurs out and in, and the chevron turns 180 degrees on a snappy spring | The label is swapped in place and the chevron turns at once | Immediate |
| New `FileName` | The name blurs out and in, and the language glides to its new position | The name is swapped in place | Immediate |

## Related

- `CopyButton` to copy a single value, such as a token or a URL.
- `JsonViewer` for JSON that people search and explore.
- `TreeView` next to a block, so the selected file drives the code shown.
- `Markdown` for documents that mix prose with fenced code.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `CopyButton` | The thing to copy is one value, not a file or a snippet |
| `JsonViewer` | People search, expand or copy parts of a JSON document |
| `TreeView` | The files form a hierarchy, and the code shown depends on the selection |
| `Markdown` | Code sits inside prose, such as a help article or a changelog |
| `Textarea` | The text is plain and people must edit it |
