# JSON viewer

> A collapsible JSON tree with search, paging for long arrays, and copy value or path.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/json-viewer

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.JsonViewerWebhookPayloadDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12">
        <arc:JsonViewer x:Name="Viewer"
                        ExpandDepth="2"
                        Copied="OnCopied"
                        CurrentRowChanged="OnCurrentRowChanged" />
        <TextBlock x:Name="Current"
                   Text="Current: root"
                   FontSize="14"
                   TextWrapping="Wrap"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
        <TextBlock x:Name="Status"
                   Text="Hover a row and use its copy actions, or press Ctrl/Cmd+C on the current row."
                   FontSize="14"
                   TextWrapping="Wrap"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class JsonViewerWebhookPayloadDemo : UserControl
{
    public JsonViewerWebhookPayloadDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Viewer.Json = """
            {
              "id": "evt_1Q2w3E4r5T",
              "type": "invoice.paid",
              "created": 1735689600,
              "livemode": false,
              "data": {
                "customer": {
                  "id": "cus_9s8d7f6g",
                  "name": "Ada Lovelace",
                  "email": "ada@example.com",
                  "tags": ["vip", "beta", "annual"]
                },
                "lines": [
                  { "description": "Pro plan", "amount": 4800, "quantity": 1 },
                  { "description": "Additional seats", "amount": 1200, "quantity": 4 }
                ],
                "total": 9600,
                "currency": "usd",
                "discount": null,
                "metadata": {
                  "order-id": "A-1042",
                  "note": "Renewed early to keep the founding-member price for the team."
                }
              }
            }
            """;
    }

    private void OnCopied(object? sender, JsonViewerCopiedEventArgs e) =>
        Status.Text = $"Copied {(e.Kind == JsonViewerCopyKind.Path ? "path" : "value")} of {e.Path}";

    private void OnCurrentRowChanged(object? sender, JsonViewerRowEventArgs e) =>
        Current.Text = $"Current: {e.Path} ({e.ValueType})";
}
```

## When to use

`JsonViewer` shows a JSON document as a tree that people can open branch by branch. It replaces the raw text in
the places where engineers and support staff need to read a document, not edit it: a developer panel, a support
console, an integration log. The viewer owns the whole surface (a toolbar with search, the tree, a path bar),
so a page only supplies the JSON and places the control in its layout.

- **Webhook delivery inspection** in an integrations console: an `invoice.paid` or `order.updated` payload that a
  developer opens to check the fields a handler reads. With `ExpandDepth="2"` the root and `data` open, and people
  open only the branch they need, such as `data.customer`.
- **API response debugging** in an internal tool: the body of a `GET /v1/orders` call shown next to the request
  that produced it. Copying the path of a field (`root.items[2].sku`) gives the exact reference for a bug report.
- **Log and event detail** in an incident timeline or an audit view: a structured log entry whose `metadata` object
  holds fields that vary by event. Search finds the key or value across the whole entry.
- **Configuration review** in a settings or deployment page: a feature-flag document or a pipeline definition that
  an operator reads and copies a value from, without the risk of editing the source.
- **Large export previews** in a data tool: an array of several thousand records that loads in pages of 50 children,
  so the first screen appears at once and the rest is loaded on request.

## When not to use

- **The whole document as copyable source**, such as a snippet for a README or a support reply: use `CodeBlock`,
  which shows the text as one block with a single copy action.
- **Nested categories that people select**, such as folders, files or an organization chart: use `TreeView`, which
  is built for selection and does not parse JSON.
- **Tabular records of one shape**, such as a list of invoices people sort and filter by column: use
  `Table`. A JSON tree shows structure; a table compares rows.
- **Values that are not JSON**, such as arbitrary .NET objects: convert them to `JsonNode` or `JsonElement` first.
  The viewer reads only System.Text.Json data.
- **Editing a document**: the viewer is read-only. Use a `Textarea` or `RichTextEditor` when people change the text.

## Usage

Pass JSON text with `Json`. Use `Value` for a `JsonNode` or `Element` for a `JsonElement` when the data is already
parsed.

```xml
<arc:JsonViewer Json="{Binding ResponseJson}"
                ExpandDepth="2"
                MaxTreeHeight="320" />
```

`JsonViewer` derives from Avalonia's `TemplatedControl`. Its template holds a toolbar, a scrolling tree of rows, a
path bar and a parse error row, and it draws its own focus ring and row actions. The theme styles those parts; the
keyboard, search, paging and copy behavior belongs to the control itself.

### Anatomy

1. **Toolbar**: shown when `IsSearchable` is `True` or the document has more than one row. It holds the search pill,
   the match counter, the previous and next match buttons, and the expand all and collapse all buttons.
2. **Search pill** (`SearchPlaceholder`, `Query`): a 34 px high pill on the muted surface color with a search glyph
   and the placeholder "Search keys and values" by default.
3. **Match counter**: `1/3` for the current match of three, or `0/0` when nothing matches. It is a polite live
   region.
4. **Tree** (`MaxTreeHeight`): the rows scroll inside this height; the default is 420 px. Each row is 30 px high.
5. **Row**: the key (or the array index), a colon, and the value. Strings use the success color, numbers the accent
   color and booleans the warning color; keys use the foreground color. Branches show their item count in the
   muted color (`2 items`, `1 key`) and, while collapsed, a preview such as `{ name, email }`.
6. **Row actions**: two icon buttons at the right edge of a row, copy value and copy path. They appear on hover and
   on the current row. They are not in the tab order.
7. **Show more row**: at the end of a long branch, "Show 50 more" with the number of hidden children. It loads the
   next page of `PageSize` children.
8. **Parse error row** (`ParseError`): shown in place of the tree when `Json` is not valid JSON.
9. **Path bar** (`IsPathVisible`): the current row's path in the monospace font, its type label with the item count
   (`object, 5 keys`) and the copy path button (`IsCopyable`). The type label hides when the viewer is narrow.

### Loading data

Three properties load a document. Each one replaces the document of the others, so the last value set is the one
on screen.

| Property | Type | What the viewer does with it |
|---|---|---|
| `Json` | `string?` | Parses the text into a document. Invalid text sets `ParseError` and leaves the tree empty. |
| `Value` | `JsonNode?` | Serializes the node into a document when set. Later changes to the node do not show; set `Value` again. |
| `Element` | `JsonElement?` | Clones the element, so its `JsonDocument` can be disposed after the viewer receives it. |

`RootName` (default `root`) is the first segment of every path. `ExpandDepth` (default `1`) sets how many levels
open when data arrives: `1` opens the root only, `2` also opens the root's children.

If the text is not valid JSON, `ParseError` holds the message and the tree stays empty.

#### Parsed data

When the data is already a `JsonNode`, bind `Value`. Build `JsonNode` values with the `JsonNode` overloads in
code, which stay AOT safe.

```csharp
var items = new JsonArray();
items.Add((JsonNode)new JsonObject { ["id"] = 1, ["sku"] = "SKU-0001", ["inStock"] = true });

viewer.Value = new JsonObject
{
    ["count"] = 1,
    ["items"] = items
};
```

### Expansion

`ExpandDepth` sets the open levels at first. The default opens the root only. `ExpandedPaths` lists the open
branches; it is two-way, so a view model can save the open set and restore it later. `ExpandedPathsChanged` is
raised after the set changes.

```csharp
viewer.ExpandAll();
viewer.CollapseAll();
viewer.Expand("root.data.lines");
viewer.Collapse("root.data.customer");
```

Setting `Json`, `Value` or `Element` starts over: the open set is rebuilt from `ExpandDepth`, the search is run again
and the tree scrolls back to the top. To keep a person's place across a refresh, read `ExpandedPaths` before the
new document arrives and set it again afterwards.

```csharp
viewer.ExpandedPaths = ["root", "root.data", "root.data.lines"];
```


### Search

`IsSearchable` is on by default. `Query` filters the keys and primitive values, case-insensitively, opens the
branches that hold a match and reports the number of matches in `MatchCount`. The count stops at 2,000 matches.
`CurrentPath` moves to the first match when a query is entered, and `NextMatch` and `PreviousMatch` step through
the matches in document order.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.JsonViewerSearchDemo">
    <arc:JsonViewer x:Name="Viewer" Query="amount" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class JsonViewerSearchDemo : UserControl
{
    public JsonViewerSearchDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Viewer.Json = """
            {
              "id": "evt_1Q2w3E4r5T",
              "type": "invoice.paid",
              "created": 1735689600,
              "livemode": false,
              "data": {
                "customer": {
                  "id": "cus_9s8d7f6g",
                  "name": "Ada Lovelace",
                  "email": "ada@example.com",
                  "tags": ["vip", "beta", "annual"]
                },
                "lines": [
                  { "description": "Pro plan", "amount": 4800, "quantity": 1 },
                  { "description": "Additional seats", "amount": 1200, "quantity": 4 }
                ],
                "total": 9600,
                "currency": "usd",
                "discount": null,
                "metadata": {
                  "order-id": "A-1042",
                  "note": "Renewed early to keep the founding-member price for the team."
                }
              }
            }
            """;
    }
}
```

```xml
<arc:JsonViewer Json="{Binding Payload}"
                Query="{Binding SearchText, Mode=TwoWay}"
                SearchPlaceholder="Search keys and values" />
```

```csharp
viewer.NextMatch();
viewer.PreviousMatch();
```

A branch that the person closes while a search is active stays closed until the query changes. The viewer does not
reopen it on the next match step, so the person's choice wins over the search.

### Long arrays

`PageSize` sets how many children a branch shows at once; the default is 50, and the minimum is 1. A "Show more"
row loads the next page and reports how many children are still hidden. Pressing Enter or Space on the row loads
the next page, and `FocusPath` moves to any row by its path.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.JsonViewerLongArraysDemo">
    <arc:JsonViewer x:Name="Viewer" ExpandDepth="2" MaxTreeHeight="320" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using System.Text.Json.Nodes;
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class JsonViewerLongArraysDemo : UserControl
{
    public JsonViewerLongArraysDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        var items = new JsonArray();
        for (var i = 0; i < 1200; i++)
        {
            // JsonNode overload: the generic Add<T> serializes through reflection (not AOT safe).
            items.Add((JsonNode)new JsonObject
            {
                ["id"] = i + 1,
                ["sku"] = $"SKU-{i + 1:0000}",
                ["inStock"] = i % 3 != 0,
                ["price"] = Math.Round(4.5 + i * 0.25, 2)
            });
        }
        Viewer.Value = new JsonObject { ["count"] = 1200, ["items"] = items };
    }
}
```

```xml
<arc:JsonViewer Json="{Binding LargeCatalog}" PageSize="50" />
```

Paging applies to arrays and objects alike. A page size of 50 keeps the first screen fast for a catalog export of
thousands of items. Raise `PageSize` only when people need to scan a whole page at once; a page of 500 rows is
rarely easier to read than ten pages of 50.

### Paths and copy

Every row has a path that describes where its value sits in the document. The path starts with `RootName` and
uses dots for identifier keys and brackets for everything else.

| Key in the JSON | Path |
|---|---|
| `data` | `root.data` |
| `$ok_1` | `root.$ok_1` (a key of letters, digits, `_` and `$` that does not start with a digit) |
| `order-id` | `root["order-id"]` |
| The second item of `lines` | `root.lines[1]` |

`IsPathVisible` shows the current row's path in the path bar, and `IsCopyable` enables the copy actions. Copying
a value gives the value's text: a string without its quotes, a branch as two-space indented JSON, and any other
value as its literal. Copying a path gives the path text.

```csharp
viewer.RootName = "payload";
viewer.Copied += (_, e) => status.Text = $"Copied {e.Kind} of {e.Path}";
viewer.CurrentRowChanged += (_, e) => current.Text = $"{e.Path} ({e.ValueType})";
```

`CurrentRowChanged` fires when a row becomes the current one, by keyboard or by click, and reports its path, value
and `JsonViewerValueType`. `Copied` reports the copy kind (`JsonViewerCopyKind.Value` or
`JsonViewerCopyKind.Path`), the path and the copied text. Use `Copied` for a status message or an audit entry.

### Narrow containers

At 420 px and below (`CompactWidth`), indentation tightens to 12 px, keys take a limited share of the row so the
values stay visible, and the type label in the path bar hides. No code is needed; the layout follows the width.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.JsonViewerNarrowDemo">
    <arc:JsonViewer x:Name="Viewer"
                    ExpandDepth="3"
                    Width="360"
                    HorizontalAlignment="Left" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class JsonViewerNarrowDemo : UserControl
{
    public JsonViewerNarrowDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Viewer.Json = """{ "user": { "id": 7, "handle": "grace", "roles": ["admin", "editor"], "active": true } }""";
    }
}
```

### Data shape and performance

The viewer accepts JSON only: text, a `JsonNode` or a `JsonElement`. It does not read arbitrary CLR objects, which
keeps it safe for ahead-of-time compilation and trimming. Serialize your model with `System.Text.Json`, or build
the `JsonNode` tree by hand as shown above, before binding it.

- **Rows are created for the viewport.** The tree is a flat list of rows that the viewer realizes only where they
  are visible. A document with thousands of objects can be opened (`ExpandAll`) and still scroll smoothly; the
  paging limit keeps each branch small.
- **Search reads the whole document on the UI thread.** It walks every key and primitive value and stops reporting
  at 2,000 matches. For a payload of several megabytes, debounce the view model's `Query` (wait for a short pause
  in typing) before it reaches the viewer.
- **Values are shown as written.** The viewer does not format currency, dates or thousands separators; format
  them in your own label beside the viewer.

### Binding to a view model

In an MVVM app the view model holds the JSON text and the search query, and the viewer shows them. With
CommunityToolkit.Mvvm, an `ObservableObject` holds the state and the commands.

```csharp
public interface IWebhookService
{
    Task<string> GetLatestPayloadJsonAsync();
}

public partial class WebhookInspectorViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    private readonly IWebhookService _webhooks;

    public WebhookInspectorViewModel(IWebhookService webhooks)
    {
        _webhooks = webhooks;
    }

    [ObservableProperty]
    private string? _payloadJson;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private string? _query;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private string _status = "Select a value to inspect it.";

    [RelayCommand]
    private async Task LoadLatestAsync()
    {
        PayloadJson = await _webhooks.GetLatestPayloadJsonAsync();
    }
}
```

```xml
<StackPanel Spacing="12">
    <arc:Button Content="Load latest delivery"
                Command="{Binding LoadLatestCommand}" />
    <arc:JsonViewer Json="{Binding PayloadJson}"
                    Query="{Binding Query, Mode=TwoWay}"
                    ExpandDepth="2"
                    MaxTreeHeight="360" />
    <TextBlock Text="{Binding Status}" />
</StackPanel>
```

- `Json`, `Value`, `Element`, `RootName`, `ExpandDepth`, `PageSize`, `MaxTreeHeight`, `IsSearchable`, `IsCopyable`
  and `IsPathVisible` are one-way: the view model sets them and the viewer does not write them back.
- `Query` is two-way. Typing in the viewer's search box updates the view model, and the view model can clear the
  search by setting `Query` to an empty string.
- `ExpandedPaths` is two-way, as described in the expansion section. `CurrentPath` and `MatchCount` are read-only
  and update as the person moves and searches.
- `Copied` and `CurrentRowChanged` are events, not commands. Forward them from code behind to the view model:

```csharp
viewer.CurrentRowChanged += (_, e) => vm.Status = $"{e.Path} ({e.ValueType})";
viewer.Copied += (_, e) => vm.Status = $"Copied {(e.Kind == JsonViewerCopyKind.Path ? "path" : "value")} of {e.Path}";
```

### Example: Webhook delivery inspector

A developer opens a delivery from the integrations console. The panel names the event and its time above the tree.
The root and its first level are open, so the customer and the line items are visible at once, and the nested
`metadata` object stays closed until the developer opens it. The tree height is limited to 340 px so the panel fits
beside the delivery list.

![A webhook delivery payload with the root and its first level open and a search toolbar](https://docs.tkcode.si/shots/Docs/Tables/JsonViewer/images/WebhookInspector.webp)

```xml
<StackPanel Width="680" Spacing="12">
    <TextBlock Text="Delivery payload"
               FontSize="16"
               FontWeight="SemiBold"
               Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
    <TextBlock Text="invoice.paid  ·  evt_1Q2w3E4r5T  ·  delivered 2026-04-12 09:14 UTC"
               FontSize="13"
               Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
    <arc:JsonViewer ExpandDepth="2" MaxTreeHeight="340">
        <arc:JsonViewer.Json>{
  "id": "evt_1Q2w3E4r5T",
  "type": "invoice.paid",
  "created": 1775985240,
  "livemode": false,
  "data": {
    "customer": {
      "id": "cus_9s8d7f6g",
      "name": "Ada Lovelace",
      "email": "ada@example.com"
    },
    "lines": [
      { "description": "Pro plan", "amount": 4800, "quantity": 1 },
      { "description": "Additional seats", "amount": 1200, "quantity": 4 }
    ],
    "total": 9600,
    "currency": "usd",
    "discount": null,
    "metadata": {
      "order-id": "A-1042",
      "note": "Renewed early to keep the founding-member price."
    }
  }
}</arc:JsonViewer.Json>
    </arc:JsonViewer>
</StackPanel>
```

The design decisions are in the data and the depth. `ExpandDepth="2"` opens the root and its direct children, so
the `data` object is open and the fields a developer checks first are one level down. The `customer`, `lines` and
`metadata` branches stay closed, each with a preview on its row (`{ id, name, email }`, `[ … ]`), so the tree reads
as a summary until someone asks for detail. The toolbar's search covers the common case of finding `customer` or
`amount` in a longer payload.

### Content guidelines

Most of the text in a viewer comes from the control (the placeholder, the counts, the copy messages). The text
around it, the heading and the status, is yours to write.

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| JSON | Delivery payload, Response body or Event data |
| Output | Response from POST /v1/invoices |
| Search... | Search keys and values (the default placeholder) |
| Root | The name your team uses in its docs, set with `RootName`, such as `event` |
| Copied! | Copied value of root.data.customer (a status line you build from the `Copied` event) |

- Name the document by its source and event, so a support engineer knows which payload is on screen.
- Use sentence case for the heading and status text, and digits for counts in the text you write.

### Best practices

**Do**

- Set `ExpandDepth` to the level that answers the usual question, usually `2`. A deeper default makes every
  document look busy and hides the field people came for.
- Keep `PageSize` at its default of 50 for arrays from external services. Smaller pages keep each branch short
  enough to scan, and the "Show more" row says how many items remain.
- Debounce `Query` for payloads of several megabytes, because the search walks the whole document on the UI
  thread.

**Avoid**

- Binding `Value` to a `JsonNode` and then changing the node in place. The viewer copies the node when it is set,
  so the tree does not update; assign `Value` again with the new node.
- Calling `ExpandAll` on large documents by default. It opens every branch, and a payload with thousands of
  objects then shows thousands of rows to scan.
- Showing a payload with secrets or personal data in a shared screen without masking it first. The viewer shows
  every value it is given.

### Common questions

**The tree did not change after I edited the `JsonNode`.** `Value` serializes the node when you set it. Changes
to the node afterwards are not seen. Set `Value` again with the updated node, or build a new `JsonObject`.

**Which of `Json`, `Value` and `Element` should I use?** Use `Json` when your data arrives as text, such as an HTTP
response body. Use `Value` when you built or parsed a `JsonNode` in code. Use `Element` when you already hold a
`JsonElement`; the viewer clones it, so you can dispose the `JsonDocument` afterwards.

**Why does the tree collapse when I refresh the data?** Each new document starts from `ExpandDepth`, so the
branches a person opened are closed again. Save `ExpandedPaths` before the refresh and set it again after the new
document loads.

**How do I copy a value from the keyboard?** Select the row with the arrow keys, then press Ctrl+C (Cmd+C on
macOS) to copy its value, or Ctrl+Shift+C (Cmd+Shift+C) to copy its path. The row action buttons are not in the tab
order, so the keyboard shortcuts are the reliable path.

## API reference

### JsonViewer

A collapsible tree for JSON. Values are colored by type, branches unfold row by row on a smooth spring, search highlights every match and opens the branches that hold them, long arrays and objects load in pages, and each row can copy its value or path. Follows the WAI-ARIA tree pattern: arrows move and open, Home/End jump, Enter/Space toggle, Ctrl/Cmd+C copies the current value (Shift: its path) and / focuses the search. Rows are a flat, virtualized list (see `TablesTreeRowsPanel`), so very large documents stay smooth. Input: `Json` (text), `Value` (`JsonNode`) or `Element`.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Json` | `string?` | `null` | JSON text to show. |
| `Value` | `JsonNode?` | `null` | A `JsonNode` to show. |
| `Element` | `JsonElement?` | `null` | A `JsonElement` to show (cloned, so its document may be disposed afterwards). |
| `RootName` | `string` | `"root"` | Name of the root in paths, as in `root.users[0].name`. |
| `ExpandDepth` | `int` | `1` | Levels open when data arrives (1 opens the root). |
| `ExpandedPaths` | `IReadOnlyList<string>` | – | Paths of open branches (two-way). |
| `IsSearchable` | `bool` | `true` | Shows the search box that filters the tree by keys and values (default true). |
| `Query` | `string?` | `""` | Search text (two-way). Matching is case-insensitive over keys and primitive values. |
| `SearchPlaceholder` | `string` | `"Search keys and values"` | Placeholder text of the search box (default: Search keys and values). |
| `PageSize` | `int` | `50` | Children shown per page in a long array or object. |
| `IsCopyable` | `bool` | `true` | Shows the copy value and copy path actions. |
| `IsPathVisible` | `bool` | `true` | Shows the current row's path under the tree. |
| `MaxTreeHeight` | `double` | `420` | Height of the scrolling tree area. |
| `ToolbarPadding` | `Thickness` | `0,0,0,0` | Padding around the search toolbar. |
| `TreePadding` | `Thickness` | `0,0,0,0` | Padding around the rows of the tree. |
| `CurrentPath` | `string?` | – | *Read-only.* Path of the current row. |
| `MatchCount` | `int` | – | *Read-only.* Number of search matches (at most 2000). |
| `ParseError` | `string?` | – | *Read-only.* Why `Json` could not be parsed, or null. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Copied` | `JsonViewerCopiedEventArgs` | Routed event behind Copied; the argument carries the copy kind, the node path and the copied text. |
| `CurrentRowChanged` | `JsonViewerRowEventArgs` | Raised when a row becomes the current one (Arc `onSelect`). |
| `ExpandedPathsChanged` | `EventHandler?` | Raised after the set of open branches changed. |

Pseudo-classes: `:compact`, `:searching`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

## Accessibility

- The tree follows the WAI-ARIA tree pattern: the rows panel is exposed as a tree, and each row exposes its level,
  its position in the set and its expanded or selected state.
- Only one row is in the tab order: the current row. Arrow keys, Home and End move the focus between rows.
- A row is read with its key and value, such as `id: evt_1`, or with its key, type and item count, such as
  `lines, array, 2 items`. A "Show more" row reads as `Show 50 more, 70 hidden`.
- The search box is named "Search JSON". The match counter is a polite live region, so each change to the count is
  announced without moving focus.
- Copy results are announced in a polite status region: "Copied value of root.customer" or "Copy failed". The
  path bar's copy button changes its name to "Copied" or "Copy failed".
- The row action buttons are painted by the control, are not in the tab order and are reached with Ctrl+C or
  Ctrl+Shift+C. The path bar copy button and the toolbar buttons are normal tab stops with names such as
  "Expand all", "Collapse all", "Previous match", "Next match" and "Copy path".
- Hover changes the row fill only; the current row is marked by the highlight and the path bar.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Up` / `Down` | Move to the previous or next visible row |
| `Home` / `End` | Move to the first row (the root) or the last visible row |
| `Right` | Open a closed branch; on an open branch, move to its first child |
| `Left` | Close an open branch; otherwise move to the parent row |
| `Enter` / `Space` | Open or close a branch; on a "Show more" row, load the next page |
| `Ctrl+C` / `Cmd+C` | Copy the current row's value |
| `Ctrl+Shift+C` / `Cmd+Shift+C` | Copy the current row's path |
| `/` | Focus the search box and select its text |
| `Enter` / `Shift+Enter` (in the search box) | Go to the next or previous match |
| `Escape` (in the search box) | Clear the query when it is not empty |
| `Down` (in the search box) | Move focus into the tree on the current row |
| `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` | Leave the tree or return to it; the tree is one tab stop |

## Motion

- Each row opens its height on a smooth spring when a branch expands. Loading a page and expanding all use the same
  motion.
- The current-row highlight glides between rows, and the tree scrolls to the row when it settles. A mouse wheel
  movement stops a scroll that is still running.
- The copy icon turns into a check mark or a cross with a small scale and blur.
- Reduced motion applies row changes at once and moves the highlight and scroll directly to their places. Off
  jumps straight to the final state.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| A branch opens or closes, or a page loads | Each row opens its height on a smooth spring | Rows change at once | Immediate |
| The current row moves | The highlight glides between rows | The highlight moves directly | Immediate |
| The tree scrolls to the current row | Springs to where the row will sit once the rows settle | Jumps directly | Immediate |
| The tree has more than 400 visible rows | Rows change at once | Rows change at once | Immediate |

## Related

- `CodeBlock` shows the whole JSON as copyable source, with one copy action.
- `TreeView` is for nested records that people select rather than inspect.
- `Table` is for records of one shape that people sort and filter by column.
- `CopyButton` copies a single value outside the tree.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `CodeBlock` | The JSON is a snippet people copy as text, such as a sample request |
| `TreeView` | The nested items are folders, files or categories that people select |
| `Table` | The records share one shape and people compare them by column |
| `CopyButton` | A single value, such as an ID or a key, needs a copy action beside it |

# Timeline

> Follow what happened, newest first, grouped by day.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/timeline

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.TimelineLiveStreamDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="16">
        <arc:Button Content="Post an update"
                    Variant="Secondary"
                    Size="Small"
                    HorizontalAlignment="Left"
                    Click="OnPostClick" />
        <Border MaxWidth="640"
                Padding="16,12,16,4"
                CornerRadius="26"
                BorderThickness="1"
                Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Surface}"
                BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Border}">
            <arc:Timeline x:Name="Feed" Label="Deployments" />
        </Border>
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using System.Collections.ObjectModel;
using Avalonia;
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;
using Avalonia.Threading;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class TimelineLiveStreamDemo : UserControl
{
    private readonly ObservableCollection<TimelineEvent> _events;
    private readonly DispatcherTimer _clock = new() { Interval = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(20) };
    private int _count;

    public TimelineLiveStreamDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        var now = TimelineDemoData.Now();
        _events =
        [
            new("live-1", now.AddMinutes(-3), "deployed web to production", "Ana Ruiz")
            {
                Meta = "Build #418 · 4m 12s",
                Avatar = "https://i.pravatar.cc/56?img=47",
                Detail = "All 312 checks passed. Rolled out to 100% of traffic in three waves."
            },
            new("live-2", now.AddMinutes(-41), "Preview environment is ready")
            {
                Meta = "feature/search",
                Icon = ArcIcons.Check,
                Tone = TimelineTone.Success
            },
            new("live-3", now.AddHours(-3), "merged Checkout redesign into main", "Theo Walsh")
            {
                Meta = "PR #212",
                Avatar = "https://i.pravatar.cc/56?img=12"
            },
            new("live-4", now.AddHours(-26), "Build failed on main")
            {
                Meta = "Step test:e2e exited with code 1",
                Icon = ArcIcons.X,
                Tone = TimelineTone.Danger,
                Detail = "Retried twice. The failing spec was quarantined in PR #215."
            },
            new("live-5", now.AddHours(-29), "requested changes on Pricing page", "Mina Park") { Meta = "PR #207" }
        ];
        Feed.Now = now;
        Feed.ItemsSource = _events;

        // A ticking clock keeps relative times fresh (Arc suggests about once a minute; faster here to show it).
        _clock.Tick += (_, _) => Feed.Now = Feed.Now.AddMinutes(1);
    }

    protected override void OnAttachedToVisualTree(VisualTreeAttachmentEventArgs e)
    {
        base.OnAttachedToVisualTree(e);
        _clock.Start();
    }

    protected override void OnDetachedFromVisualTree(VisualTreeAttachmentEventArgs e)
    {
        _clock.Stop();
        base.OnDetachedFromVisualTree(e);
    }

    private void OnPostClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        _count++;
        var (actor, title, meta) = TimelineDemoData.Update(_count);
        _events.Add(new TimelineEvent($"post-{_count}", Feed.Now.AddSeconds(_count), title, actor) { Meta = meta });
    }
}
```

## When to use

`Timeline` is the activity feed of an application where the order and the recency of events matter more than their
comparison. It shows who did what and when, grouped by day with the newest first, and it accepts updates while it is on
screen. Each row is one update: a person's action or a system event with a short title, optional context and, when the
reader needs it, a detail that expands in place.

- **Project history on a release page**: "merged Checkout redesign into main" by Theo Walsh, with the pull request as the
  context. Readers scan the day groups to see how a release came together.
- **Deployment stream in a DevOps console**: builds, rollouts and rollbacks, with a success or danger tone on system events.
  The title states the outcome, so the tone is never the only signal.
- **Audit log in an admin console**: who changed a billing plan or a user role, and when. Each row expands to show the
  before and after values, so the list stays short.
- **Account activity in a CRM**: calls, emails and contract changes for one customer, each with a portrait of the person
  who made it.
- **Incident progress on a status page**: a live feed where each update slides in at the top as responders post it.

## When not to use

- **Records the reader sorts or compares**, such as invoices by amount or users by last login: use `Table`.
- **Fixed steps with a current position**, such as checkout or onboarding: use `Stepper`.
- **A threaded discussion on one object**: use `CommentThread`. For a live two-way conversation, use `ChatThread`.
- **One current status of one item**, such as "Payment failed" on an invoice: use `Alert` next to the item. A timeline of
  one event is a message, not a feed.

## Usage

`Timeline` derives from Avalonia's `ItemsControl`. Its items are `TimelineEvent` objects, bound with `ItemsSource` or written
inline. Events can arrive in any order, and the newest shows first. Set `Now` to the reference time: relative times such as
"9m" and "2h" and the day groups "Today" and "Yesterday" are computed from it.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:Timeline Label="Release history"
                  Now="2026-10-20T12:00:00+00:00">
        <arc:TimelineEvent Id="build-418"
                           At="2026-10-20T11:48:00+00:00"
                           Actor="Ana Ruiz"
                           Title="deployed web to production"
                           Meta="Build #418"
                           Detail="All 312 checks passed in 4m 12s." />
        <arc:TimelineEvent Id="pr-212"
                           At="2026-10-20T11:02:00+00:00"
                           Actor="Theo Walsh"
                           Title="merged Checkout redesign into main"
                           Meta="PR #212" />
    </arc:Timeline>
</UserControl>
```

`Timeline` derives from `ItemsControl` and lays out its own rows, so supply `TimelineEvent` items, not item templates. The
feed grows with its page unless you set `MaxHeight`, so place it in a page that scrolls, or give it a height and let it scroll
inside.

### Anatomy

1. **Day label** (`HeadingLevel`, 3 by default): "Today", "Yesterday", or the weekday and date for older days, with the
   number of updates in that day. It is a 19.6 px line with 8 px above and below.
2. **Marker**: a 28 px circle with a 14 px glyph, 8 px below the top of the row. It shows the `Avatar` of a person, or the
   `Icon` of a system event; a person without an avatar gets an empty marker.
3. **Connector**: a line that runs from the bottom of the marker to the next row. It draws itself as the row comes into view.
4. **Trigger**: the title on a 20 px line and the `Meta` on a 16.8 px line, with the `Actor` first in the foreground color.
   The trigger has 12 px of padding and sits 36 px from the left edge.
5. **Time**: at least 44 px wide, after the title. Today's updates show relative times ("9m", "2h"); earlier days show the
   clock time ("1:00 PM").
6. **Chevron**: a 16 px arrow after the time on rows with a `Detail`. Rows without a detail show no chevron and do not
   expand.
7. **Detail**: the `Detail` revealed under the trigger, with 12 px of side padding and 16 px at the bottom.
8. **Sticky day label**: in a scrolling feed (with `MaxHeight`), the current day label stays pinned at the top while its rows
   scroll under it.
9. **Feather**: when a scrolling feed has more rows below, its bottom edge fades over 36 px.

The timeline uses the Arc surface for its day labels, which cover the rows scrolling under them. Set `HeaderBackground` to
the surface the feed sits on, or the labels show a different color from the page.

Under 420 px the trigger padding drops to 8 px and the time and chevron move closer to the title.

### Binding to a view model

The view model owns the events, the reference time and the expanded rows. The timeline shows them, and the view model
adds events as they arrive. This example uses CommunityToolkit.Mvvm.

```csharp
public partial class DeploymentFeedViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    public ObservableCollection<TimelineEvent> Events { get; } = [];

    [ObservableProperty]
    private DateTimeOffset _now = DateTimeOffset.UtcNow;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private IReadOnlyList<string> _expandedIds = [];

    public void Add(TimelineEvent item) => Events.Add(item);

    public void Tick() => Now = DateTimeOffset.UtcNow;
}
```

```xml
<arc:Timeline Label="Deployments"
              ItemsSource="{Binding Events}"
              Now="{Binding Now}"
              ExpandedIds="{Binding ExpandedIds}"
              MaxHeight="420" />
```

- `ItemsSource` takes the events. Adding to the collection slides the new row in at the top, and the view model does not
  need to rebuild the list.
- `Now` is one-way. Set it from a timer, as the next section shows; only the time labels change when it moves.
- `ExpandedIds` is two-way. It holds the ids of the open rows, so the view model can restore them when the page reloads.

### Live feed

Advance `Now` on a timer, about once a minute, so the relative times stay current. Stop the timer when the feed leaves the
screen, so an unused page does no work. `IsScrollToNewEnabled` (default true) scrolls the feed back to the top when a new
newest update arrives while the reader is scrolled down.

```csharp
var events = new ObservableCollection<TimelineEvent>();
var timeline = new Timeline { Label = "Deployments", Now = DateTimeOffset.UtcNow, ItemsSource = events };

events.Add(new TimelineEvent("post-1", DateTimeOffset.UtcNow, "merged Checkout redesign into main", "Theo Walsh")
{
    Meta = "PR #212"
});

var clock = new DispatcherTimer { Interval = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(1) };
clock.Tick += (_, _) => timeline.Now = DateTimeOffset.UtcNow;
timeline.AttachedToVisualTree += (_, _) => clock.Start();
timeline.DetachedFromVisualTree += (_, _) => clock.Stop();
```

### Expandable rows and tones

A row with a `Detail` expands when it is activated. The `Detail` can be text or any control, and it is revealed in place.
A `Detail` that is an empty string does not make the row expandable. `Tone` colors a system event:

| Tone | Use it for | How it shows |
|---|---|---|
| `Neutral` (default) | Ordinary updates | A quiet marker |
| `Success` | A completed step: a deploy, a migration, a payment | The marker is tinted and the icon takes the success color |
| `Danger` | A failure or a rollback | The marker is tinted and the icon takes the danger color |

Put the outcome in the title as well as the tone, so the meaning is not carried by color alone.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             xmlns:generic="using:System.Collections.Generic"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.TimelineExpandableDetailsDemo">
    <Border MaxWidth="640"
            Padding="16,12,16,4"
            CornerRadius="26"
            BorderThickness="1"
            Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Surface}"
            BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Border}">
        <arc:Timeline x:Name="Feed" Label="Release history">
            <arc:Timeline.ExpandedIds>
                <generic:List x:TypeArguments="x:String">
                    <x:String>build-418</x:String>
                </generic:List>
            </arc:Timeline.ExpandedIds>
        </arc:Timeline>
    </Border>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class TimelineExpandableDetailsDemo : UserControl
{
    public TimelineExpandableDetailsDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        var now = TimelineDemoData.Now();
        Feed.Now = now;
        Feed.ItemsSource = new List<TimelineEvent>
        {
            new("build-418", now.AddMinutes(-12), "deployed web to production", "Ana Ruiz")
            {
                Meta = "Build #418",
```

`ExpandedChanged` reports each row that opened or closed, whether the user did it or the code called `Expand`, `Collapse` or
`Toggle`. A person's event shows `Avatar`. A system event shows an `Icon`, such as `ArcIcons.Check`, when it has no avatar.

### Long history

Set `MaxHeight` to scroll inside the feed. The current day label stays pinned while its rows scroll, and the list is
virtualized: only the rows in view and a small buffer exist, so a long history stays responsive.

### Example: incident progress feed

An incident page for INC-204 in a status console. The feed shows the responders' actions and the system events in
order. The failed deploy is a danger event whose title already says the outcome, and its detail explains the retry. The
rollback is a person's action with the responder's name, and the health check is a success event. The yesterday group
shows that the page keeps earlier history. The title of each row is a full sentence, so the feed reads like a log.

![An incident progress feed with a danger event, a rollback, a success event and a day group](https://docs.tkcode.si/shots/Docs/Activity/Timeline/images/IncidentFeed.webp)

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
```

The scene keeps its events inline, as a static picture must. In the application they come from `ItemsSource`, and the
time labels move with `Now`.

### Content guidelines

- **Title**: a full sentence in the past tense, with the actor first in the feed: "merged Checkout redesign into main". The
  actor is a name, never "System" when a person caused the event.
- **Outcome**: say the result in the title of every success or danger event, so a reader who cannot see the color still
  knows what happened.
- **Meta**: a short reference such as a pull request, a build or a severity: "PR #212", "Build #418".
- **Detail**: one or two sentences with the facts a reader needs when they expand the row. Put the numbers in the detail, not
  in the title, when they are long.
- **Other languages**: set `Culture` for day headings and clock times. The default is en-US.

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| Update | Ana Ruiz deployed web to production |
| Error! | Deploy failed: health check timed out |
| System: done | Database migration completed |
| Click for more | Retried twice. The failing check is tracked in INC-204. |

### Best practices

**Do**

- Set `Now` from a timer and stop the timer when the feed leaves the screen. Relative times are only as current as `Now`.
- Set `TimeZone` when the audience shares one zone, such as an operations team in one region. The default is UTC, so every
  viewer sees the same clock.
- Give every event a stable `Id`. Expansion, freshness and the announcement of new updates follow it.
- Use `MaxHeight` on a long feed, so the day labels stay pinned and the reader keeps the place.
- Put the outcome in the title of every success or danger event.

**Avoid**

- Replacing the whole collection to add one event. Add to the collection, so the new row slides in.
- Setting `Tone` on ordinary person events. A tone marks a system outcome, and a person's row already has the avatar.
- Using `Detail` for the main content of an event. The row shows the title first, and a detail that holds the whole story
  is hidden until the reader expands it.
- Leaving `HeaderBackground` at its default on a feed placed on a colored panel. The day labels then cover the rows with the
  wrong color.
- Using a timeline for records a reader compares. Sorting and filtering belong in `Table`.

### Common questions

**Why do the relative times not change?** Only the time labels change when `Now` moves. Advance `Now` about once a minute, from
a timer that runs while the feed is on screen.

**Why does my row not expand?** A row expands only when its `Detail` has content. An empty string does not count, so the row
is plain text and it is not in the Tab order.

**Can I show the oldest event first?** No. The feed shows the newest update first and groups the rows by day. Sort the
events yourself if you need another order in a different view.

**How do I open a row from code?** Call `Expand(id)`, `Collapse(id)` or `Toggle(id)`. Each call raises `ExpandedChanged`, and
`IsExpanded(id)` tells you whether a row is open.

## API reference

### Timeline

A vertical activity feed grouped by day, newest first (Arc's `Timeline`), for project history, audit logs and deploy streams. Day labels stay pinned while their updates scroll, the connecting line draws itself as rows come into view, rows with a `Detail` expand in place, and new updates slide in at the top while the rest glide down. ↑ / ↓ / Home / End move between expandable rows; Enter or Space expands one.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Now` | `DateTimeOffset` | `01/01/0001 00:00:00 +00:00` | Reference time for relative labels ("9m") and day groups ("Today"). Pass a ticking clock (about once a minute) to keep labels fresh; the default (`MinValue`) reads the system clock when labels are built. |
| `Label` | `string` | `"Activity"` | Accessible name of the feed (Arc's required `label`). |
| `TimeZone` | `TimeZoneInfo` | `(UTC) Coordinated Universal Time` | Time zone for day groups and clock times. Fixed (UTC) by default, like Arc, so every viewer agrees. |
| `Culture` | `CultureInfo?` | `null` | Culture of day headings and clock times; null uses en-US (Arc's default locale). |
| `IsScrollToNewEnabled` | `bool` | `true` | Scroll back to the top when a new newest update arrives while the feed is scrolled down. |
| `ExpandedIds` | `IReadOnlyList<string>?` | `null` | Ids of the expanded rows (Arc's `defaultExpanded`, two-way). |
| `HeadingLevel` | `int` | `3` | Heading level of the day labels (2 to 6; default 3). |
| `HeaderBackground` | `IBrush?` | `null` | Background of the day labels, which cover the updates scrolling under them (Arc's `--timeline-surface`, Surface by default). Set it to the surface the feed sits on. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ExpandedChanged` | `TimelineExpandedChangedEventArgs` | A row opened or closed by the user (click, keyboard, assistive technology or the methods). |

Pseudo-classes: `:scrolls`, `:narrow`

Derives from `ItemsControl`: every member of `ItemsControl` works as well.

### TimelineEvent

One update in a `Timeline` (Arc's `TimelineEvent`): who did what and when, with optional context and a detail revealed in place. Events are read when they are added; replace an event to change it.

## Accessibility

- The feed is a named region. `Label` is its accessible name, such as "Incident INC-204".
- Each day label is a heading at `HeadingLevel` (3 by default, from 2 to 6). Its accessible name carries the count of updates,
  such as "Friday, October 16, 1 update". Each time has its full date as hidden text.
- Expandable rows expose their expanded state. Rows without a detail are plain text and are not in the Tab order.
- New events are announced in a live region as "New update: ..." without moving focus.
- Tone is color. The title must say the outcome, as the content guidelines require.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Down` / `Up` | Moves to the next or previous row that has a detail |
| `Home` / `End` | Moves to the first or last row that has a detail |
| `Enter` or `Space` | Expands or collapses the current row |

Rows with a detail take focus in the Tab order; rows without one do not. Arrow keys skip the rows that cannot expand.

## Motion

- Rows draw their connector line as they enter the viewport, and their markers pop in.
- A new event slides in from the top while the rows below move down. Expanded details open on a spring.
- Reduced motion replaces movement with a short fade and changes heights at once. Off jumps to the final state.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| Row enters the viewport | The connector draws and the marker pops in | Short fade | Immediate |
| New event arrives | Slides in from the top; rows below move down | Short fade | Immediate |
| Detail opens or closes | The detail opens on a spring | Height changes at once | Immediate |
| Day label while scrolling | Stays pinned at the top of the feed | Stays pinned | Stays pinned |

## Related

- `CommentThread` for replies on one object, and `ChatThread` for a live two-way conversation.
- `Table` when the reader needs to sort or compare records.
- `Stepper` for fixed steps with a current position.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `CommentThread` | Replies hang off one object and can be resolved |
| `ChatThread` | People talk in turns, with typing and read receipts |
| `Table` | The reader sorts or compares the records |
| `Stepper` | The steps are fixed and one of them is current |
| `Alert` | A single current status belongs next to one item |

# Comment thread

> Threaded comments with replies, reactions, mentions, inline edit, and resolve.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/comment-thread

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             xmlns:demos="using:TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.CommentThreadDesignReviewDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12">
        <Border MaxWidth="520">
            <arc:CommentThread Title="Hero headline"
                               CurrentUser="{x:Static demos:CommentThreadDemoData.Ana}"
                               Comments="{x:Static demos:CommentThreadDemoData.Review}"
                               CommentsChanged="OnCommentsChanged"
                               ResolvedChanged="OnResolvedChanged" />
        </Border>
        <TextBlock x:Name="Status"
                   Text="Reply, react, edit or delete your own comments, then resolve the thread."
                   FontSize="14"
                   TextWrapping="Wrap"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class CommentThreadDesignReviewDemo : UserControl
{
    public CommentThreadDesignReviewDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
    }

    private void OnCommentsChanged(object? sender, CommentsChangedEventArgs e)
    {
        Status.Text = e.Change.Kind switch
        {
            CommentThreadChangeKind.Reply => e.Change.ParentId is null ? "New comment" : $"Reply to {e.Change.ParentId}",
            CommentThreadChangeKind.Edit => $"Edited {e.Change.Id}",
            CommentThreadChangeKind.Delete => $"Deleted {e.Change.Id}",
            _ => $"{(e.Change.Added ? "Added" : "Removed")} {e.Change.Emoji} on {e.Change.Id}"
        };
    }

    private void OnResolvedChanged(object? sender, CommentThreadResolvedChangedEventArgs e)
    {
        Status.Text = e.IsResolved ? "Resolved" : "Reopened";
    }
}
```

## When to use

`CommentThread` is the discussion attached to one object: a design frame, a document clause, a ticket or a pull request.
Each comment carries its replies, people react with emoji, authors edit and delete their own comments in place, and the
thread can be resolved once the question is settled. The thread stays with the object, so the reason for a decision is
found next to the decision itself.

- **Design review of a checkout screen**: a product designer and an engineer discuss the spacing of the order summary. The
  replies nest under the comment they answer, and the thread is resolved when the spacing is agreed.
- **Feedback on a legal clause**: a reviewer comments on one clause of a contract and mentions the owner with "@" so the
  person is notified. The resolved thread stays on the clause as the record of the decision.
- **Discussion on a support ticket**: an engineer and a support lead discuss the cause of an incident on ticket
  INC-2026-0931. Resolving the thread marks the question closed without deleting the discussion.
- **Questions on a metric**: a finance lead asks why the annual recurring revenue figure changed, and the analyst answers in
  a thread attached to that figure.

## When not to use

- **A live conversation between people who are online together**: use `ChatThread`, which has a message list, typing
  and read receipts.
- **A history of events across many objects**, such as deployments or status changes: use `Timeline`.
- **Only an input with mention suggestions and no discussion**: use `MentionInput`.
- **A single note that nobody replies to**: use `Textarea`. A thread with one comment and no replies is a note with extra
  controls.

## Usage

Set `CurrentUser` to the person who reads the thread. They can edit and delete their own comments, and only theirs.
`Comments` is the tree of comments, oldest first, and each comment's replies sit under its `Replies` list.

```csharp
var ana = new CommentAuthor("ana", "Ana Ruiz");
var mina = new CommentAuthor("mina", "Mina Park");

var thread = new CommentThread
{
    Title = "Hero headline",
    CurrentUser = ana,
    Comments =
    [
        new ThreadComment("c1", mina, "The new headline reads well. @Theo Walsh can we tighten the subhead?", "2h")
        {
            Replies =
            [
                new ThreadComment("c2", new CommentAuthor("theo", "Theo Walsh"), "Yes, trimming it to one line.", "1h")
            ]
        }
    ]
};
```

```xml
<arc:CommentThread Title="Pricing table spacing"
                   Placeholder="Reply to the thread"
                   CurrentUser="{Binding CurrentUser}"
                   Comments="{Binding Comments}"
                   IsResolved="{Binding IsResolved}" />
```

`CommentThread` derives from `TemplatedControl`, and it sizes to its content, so place it in a container that gives it the
width you want. The thread shows every change at once: it builds a new immutable comment tree and displays it, then reports
the change. It does not wait for the application to save anything.

### Anatomy

1. **Header**: the `Title` (a string, or a control in the header only), the subtitle "3 comments" and the Resolve button.
   The header has 18 px of left padding and 12 px of top padding.
2. **Comment**: a 16 px rounded surface with 10 px of padding and 10 px between comments. It holds the portrait (28 px, or
   initials when there is no `Avatar`), the author's name, the time and "edited" for an edited comment.
3. **Body**: 14 px text at a 1.4 line height. A known person written as "@Full Name" is set in medium weight.
4. **Actions**: Reply for every comment; Edit and Delete only on the current user's comments. The actions are 28 px high.
   They are visible while the pointer is over the comment, while a key focus is inside it, while a prompt is open and
   always on touch screens.
5. **Reactions**: one chip per emoji, with its count. The add-reaction button opens a picker of 28 px emoji buttons with 16 px emoji.
6. **Replies toggle**: "Show 2 replies" or "Hide replies". Replies sit under a rail line, indented 24 px (12 px narrow).
7. **Deleted placeholder**: a deleted comment with replies stays as "This comment was deleted", so the thread keeps its
   structure.
8. **Composer**: the current user's portrait (hidden below 420 px), a field that grows from 38 px to 160 px with a 14 px
   radius, and a Send button 38 px high (32 px while editing).
9. **Replying line**: "Replying to Theo Walsh" above the composer, with a 22 px close button.
10. **Mention suggestions**: a list under the field, rows 32 px high, at most five people.
11. **Resolved chip**: when the thread is resolved, the header folds into a 24 px icon, the title, the count of people who
    took part, and a Reopen button 32 px high. The chip has a 22 px radius.

Lines and spacing are set by the component theme. Use the theme resources to change the look of the whole thread, not
per-instance properties.

### Binding to a view model

The view model owns the comments and the resolved state. It loads them, applies each change the thread reports, and
returns the saved tree. `Comments` and `IsResolved` are two-way, so the thread writes the new values back when they change.
This example uses CommunityToolkit.Mvvm.

```csharp
public interface IReviewStore
{
    Task<ThreadComment[]> LoadCommentsAsync(string reviewId);

    Task<bool> IsResolvedAsync(string reviewId);

    Task ApplyChangeAsync(string reviewId, CommentThreadChange change);
}

public partial class DesignReviewViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    private readonly IReviewStore _store;

    public DesignReviewViewModel(IReviewStore store)
    {
        _store = store;
        CurrentUser = new CommentAuthor("ana", "Ana Ruiz", "avares://Acme.Review/Assets/ana.png");
    }

    public CommentAuthor CurrentUser { get; }

    [ObservableProperty]
    private IReadOnlyList<ThreadComment> _comments = [];

    [ObservableProperty]
    private bool _isResolved;

    public async Task LoadAsync(string reviewId)
    {
        Comments = await _store.LoadCommentsAsync(reviewId);
        IsResolved = await _store.IsResolvedAsync(reviewId);
    }

    public Task RecordAsync(string reviewId, CommentThreadChange change) =>
        _store.ApplyChangeAsync(reviewId, change);
}
```

```xml
<arc:CommentThread Title="Pricing table spacing"
                   CurrentUser="{Binding CurrentUser}"
                   Comments="{Binding Comments, Mode=TwoWay}"
                   IsResolved="{Binding IsResolved, Mode=TwoWay}"
                   People="{Binding People}" />
```

- `CommentsChanged` is the event that carries each change. The code-behind forwards it to `RecordAsync`, so the store saves
  the change itself and the view model does not compare trees.
- `People` lists the people who can be mentioned. Leave it null to offer everyone in the thread and the current user.
- To refuse a change, set `Comments` back to the previous tree in the handler. The thread then shows the old tree.

### Mentions and people

Type `@` in the composer to suggest people. `People` sets the list. Without it, the people in the thread and the current user are offered. Suggestions match the start of any word in a name, so "w" finds "Theo Walsh".

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             xmlns:demos="using:TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.CommentThreadEmptyThreadDemo">
    <Border MaxWidth="520">
        <arc:CommentThread Title="Footer links"
                           CurrentUser="{x:Static demos:CommentThreadDemoData.Ana}"
                           People="{x:Static demos:CommentThreadDemoData.People}" />
    </Border>
</UserControl>
```

### Reactions and depth

`Reactions` sets the emoji the picker offers on each comment. The default is six emoji: thumbs up, red heart, party popper,
eyes, rocket and check mark. `MaxDepth` limits nesting (default 2): a reply deeper than that attaches to the deepest allowed parent.

### Resolve and reopen

`Resolve()` folds the thread into the resolved chip, and it works only when the thread has comments. `Reopen()` opens a
resolved thread again. `IsResolved` is two-way, and `ResolvedChanged` reports each change with the new state.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             xmlns:demos="using:TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.CommentThreadResolvedDemo">
    <Border MaxWidth="520">
        <arc:CommentThread Title="Pricing table spacing"
                           IsResolved="True"
                           CurrentUser="{x:Static demos:CommentThreadDemoData.Ana}"
                           Comments="{x:Static demos:CommentThreadDemoData.Settled}" />
    </Border>
</UserControl>
```

```csharp
thread.ResolvedChanged += (_, e) => Status.Text = e.IsResolved ? "Resolved" : "Reopened";

thread.Resolve();
thread.Reopen();
```

### Changes and persistence

`CommentsChanged` reports each change as a `CommentThreadChange`. Save that change on the server rather than comparing the
whole tree. The server must also check that people edit and delete only their own comments, since it receives only what the client reports.

| Kind | Fields that are set | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `Reply` | `Comment`, `ParentId` (null for a top-level comment) | A new comment or reply was written |
| `Edit` | `Id`, `Body` | A comment's body was changed |
| `Delete` | `Id` | A comment was deleted |
| `React` | `Id`, `Emoji`, `Added` | A reaction was added (`Added` true) or removed (false) |

```csharp
thread.CommentsChanged += (_, e) =>
{
    if (e.Change.Kind == CommentThreadChangeKind.Edit)
    {
        // Save e.Change.Body for e.Change.Id.
    }
};
```

### Narrow

Under 420 px the composer drops its avatar and replies indent 12 px instead of 24 px.
