The example keeps its comments inline, as a static picture must. In the application they come from the view model, and the
thread reports each change through `CommentsChanged`.

### Content guidelines

- **Title**: names the object under review ("Pricing table spacing", "Clause 4.2 termination"), not the discussion.
- **Placeholder**: invites a reply to the thread ("Reply to the thread"). The default "Reply, or @mention someone" fits a
  team that uses mentions every day.
- **Comments**: write the point and the question in full sentences. Mention a person with "@" only when that person must act.
- **Empty state**: the default line "No comments yet. Start the conversation below." is fine for a review tool. Keep it
  short when the product is not a review tool.
- **Other languages**: set `Labels` for the actions, the counts and the announcements. Counts and names are functions, so the
  plural rules belong to them.

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| Comment thread 1 | Pricing table spacing |
| Reply here... | Reply to the thread |
| 1 comments | 1 comment |
| Delete? | Delete this comment? |
| Thread closed | Resolved |

### Best practices

**Do**

- Set `CurrentUser` to the signed-in person before you show the thread. Edit and Delete follow that identity, so a wrong
  user shows the wrong actions.
- Persist each `CommentThreadChange` on the server, and check on the server that people change only their own comments.
- Give every comment a stable `Id`. The thread reuses the view of each comment by its id when the tree changes.
- Resolve the thread when the question is answered, so the resolved chip shows the outcome and folds the discussion away.
- Set `People` to the reviewers of the object, so the suggestions show the right people first.

**Avoid**

- Comparing two trees to find out what changed. The change in `CommentsChanged` already says what happened.
- Writing a draft into `Comments` while the person types. Only sent comments belong in the tree.
- Using the thread for more than one object. Each thread belongs to one object, and a second object needs a second thread.
- Removing a comment that has replies from your store. Mark it deleted instead, so the thread keeps a placeholder and the replies stay in place.
- Leaving `Reactions` at the default for a product that uses its own emoji, such as a team that reviews with check marks only.

### Common questions

**Why is there no Edit or Delete on someone else's comment?** Edit and Delete appear only on comments whose author has the same `Id` as `CurrentUser`. The server must check it again.

**Why does Resolve do nothing on a new thread?** `Resolve()` folds the thread only when it has comments, so an empty thread stays open.

**How do I start a reply from code?** Call `ReplyTo(id)` with the id of the comment. It focuses the composer, and the
replying line shows its author. `CancelReply()` cancels the reply in progress, and `ReplyingToId` returns the id being
answered, or null.

**Can I hold a change until the server accepts it?** The thread shows a change at once. To refuse one, set `Comments` back to the previous tree in the handler, as described above.

## API reference

### CommentThread

A threaded discussion (Arc's Comment thread): replies nest under their comment and collapse, reactions toggle with a count that rolls, authors edit and delete their own comments in place, mentions autocomplete in the composer, and resolving folds the whole thread into a single chip that reopens it. Use it for review discussions on documents, designs, tickets or pull requests; use `MentionInput` when only the input is needed.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Comments` | `IReadOnlyList<ThreadComment>` | – | The comments, oldest first (two way). Each change replaces it with the next tree. |
| `CurrentUser` | `CommentAuthor` | `CommentAuthor { Id = me, Name = You, Avatar =  }` | The person writing. Their comments can be edited and deleted. |
| `People` | `IReadOnlyList<CommentAuthor>?` | `null` | People who can be mentioned. Null (default) offers everyone in the thread and the current user. |
| `IsResolved` | `bool` | `false` | Whether the thread is folded into the resolved chip (two way). |
| `Title` | `object?` | `null` | What the thread is about, shown in its header and on the resolved chip ("Hero headline"). |
| `Placeholder` | `string` | `"Reply, or @mention someone"` | Placeholder (and accessible name) of the composer. |
| `Reactions` | `IReadOnlyList<string>` | `<>z__ReadOnlyArray`1[System.String]` | Emoji offered by the reaction picker. |
| `MaxDepth` | `int` | `2` | Replies deeper than this attach to the deepest allowed parent (default 2). |
| `NowLabel` | `string` | `"Just now"` | The time label of comments written now. |
| `Labels` | `CommentThreadLabels` | `CommentThreadLabels { Thread = Comment thread, CommentCount = System.Func`2[System.Int32,System.String], PeopleCount = System.Func`2[System.Int32,System.String], Resolve = Resolve, Resolved = Resolved, Reopen = Reopen, Empty = No comments yet. Start the conversation below., Reply = Reply, Edit = Edit, Delete = Delete, Cancel = Cancel, Send = Send, Save = Save, EditComment = Edit comment, Edited = edited, DeleteConfirm = Delete this comment?, DeletedText = This comment was deleted, DeletedComment = Deleted comment, ReplyingTo = System.Func`2[System.String,System.String], CancelReply = Cancel reply, ShowReplies = System.Func`2[System.Int32,System.String], HideReplies = Hide replies, AddReaction = Add reaction, CloseReactions = Close reactions, Reactions = Reactions, ReactWith = System.Func`2[System.String,System.String], ReactionCount = System.Func`4[System.String,System.Int32,System.Boolean,System.String], Mentions = People }` | Every word the thread shows or announces; English by default. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `CommentsChanged` | `CommentsChangedEventArgs` | Raised after every change with the next tree and the change. |
| `ResolvedChanged` | `CommentThreadResolvedChangedEventArgs` | Raised when the thread is resolved or reopened. |

Pseudo-classes: `:resolved`, `:narrow`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

### ThreadComment

A comment and its replies (Arc's `ThreadComment`). Immutable: every change made in a `CommentThread` produces a new tree (unchanged comments are shared), so it can be stored as is.

## Accessibility

- The thread is a named region ("Comment thread", `Label` on `Labels.Thread`). Each comment is a named group with the
  author and the time, such as "Mina Park, 2h". A deleted comment reads "Deleted comment".
- The composer is a combobox while mention suggestions are open, and its expanded state is exposed to assistive technology.
- Reaction chips are toggle buttons, and their names include the count and whether you reacted, such as "thumbs up, 2, including you".
- The button that folds replies exposes its expanded state. Icon-only actions such as Edit, Delete and Reply have names.
- The edit field is named "Edit comment", and its Save button is named "Save".

### Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Enter` (in the composer) | Adds a new line |
| `Ctrl` + `Enter` or `Cmd` + `Enter` | Sends a new comment, or saves an edit |
| `@` | Opens the mention suggestions |
| `Up` / `Down` (suggestions) | Moves the active suggestion; wraps at both ends |
| `Enter` or `Tab` (suggestions) | Inserts the active person as "@Full Name " |
| `Escape` | Closes the suggestions first; then cancels an edit, a reply, a delete confirmation or the reaction picker |

The actions of a comment take focus with `Tab` like any other button, so keyboard users reach Reply, Edit and Delete without
a pointer.

## Motion

- Opening replies, adding a comment and folding a resolved thread change the height of the thread on a spring.
- Reaction counts roll to their new value, and chips move when others are added or removed.
- The edit form, the delete confirmation and the reaction picker slide in a short distance.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| Replies open or close | The thread height springs to the new size | The content changes in place | Immediate |
| A comment is added | The thread height springs, and the comment arrives | The content changes in place | Immediate |
| Thread resolved or reopened | The thread folds into the chip, or opens, on a spring | The content changes in place | Immediate |
| Reaction count changes | The count rolls to the new value | The count changes in place | Immediate |
| Edit form, delete prompt or picker opens | Slides in 8 px | The content changes in place | Immediate |

Reduced motion replaces the movement with an in-place change and turns transitions off. Off jumps to the final state.

## Related

- `ChatThread` for a live conversation between people who are online together.
- `Timeline` for a feed of activity across many objects.
- `MentionInput` for a single input with mention suggestions and no thread.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `ChatThread` | People talk in turns, with typing and read receipts |
| `Timeline` | The history is a list of events across many objects |
| `MentionInput` | You need one input with mentions, not a discussion |
| `Textarea` | A single note is written, and nobody replies to it |
| `Avatar` | You need the portrait or initials of a person outside the thread |

---

# Chat thread

> A chat thread with grouped messages, reactions, read receipts, typing, and a composer with attachments.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/chat-thread

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             xmlns:generic="using:System.Collections.Generic"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ChatThreadSupportConversationDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12">
        <Border Height="560"
                MaxWidth="640"
                CornerRadius="26"
                BorderThickness="1"
                ClipToBounds="True"
                Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Surface}"
                BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Border}">
            <arc:ChatThread x:Name="Chat"
                            Label="Support conversation"
                            CurrentUserId="me"
                            SendRequested="OnSendRequested"
                            ReactionToggled="OnReactionToggled"
                            RetryRequested="OnRetryRequested">
                <arc:ChatThread.Participants>
                    <generic:List x:TypeArguments="arc:ChatParticipant">
                        <arc:ChatParticipant Id="me" Name="Alex Kim" />
                        <arc:ChatParticipant Id="sam" Name="Sam Rivera" />
                        <arc:ChatParticipant Id="lee" Name="Lee Chen" />
                    </generic:List>
                </arc:ChatThread.Participants>
            </arc:ChatThread>
        </Border>
        <WrapPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center" ItemSpacing="12" LineSpacing="12">
            <arc:Button Content="Simulate a reply" Click="OnReplyClick" />
            <arc:Button Content="Toggle typing" Click="OnTypingClick" />
        </WrapPanel>
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using System.Collections.ObjectModel;
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class ChatThreadSupportConversationDemo : UserControl
{
    private readonly ObservableCollection<ChatMessage> _messages;
    private readonly ObservableCollection<string> _typing = ["sam"];

    public ChatThreadSupportConversationDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        var now = DateTimeOffset.Now;
        var yesterday = now.AddDays(-1).Date.AddHours(16);
        var today = now.Date.AddHours(Math.Min(now.Hour, 9));
        _messages =
        [
            new("m1", "sam", "Hi Alex! Thanks for reaching out about the billing export.", new DateTimeOffset(yesterday.AddMinutes(2))),
            new("m2", "sam", "Could you share the account email so I can look it up?", new DateTimeOffset(yesterday.AddMinutes(3))),
            new("m3", "me", "Sure, it's alex@northwind.dev", new DateTimeOffset(yesterday.AddMinutes(9))) { Status = ChatMessageStatus.Read },
            new("m4", "sam", "Found it. The export failed because of a malformed date in **row 214**. I've attached the cleaned file.", new DateTimeOffset(today.AddMinutes(1)))
            {
                Attachments = [new ChatAttachment("f1", "billing-export-fixed.csv", ChatAttachmentKind.File) { Size = 18_642 }],
                Reactions = [new ChatReaction("🙏", 1, true)]
            },
            new("m5", "lee", "Here's what the new export screen looks like:", new DateTimeOffset(today.AddMinutes(4)))
            {
                Attachments =
                [
                    new ChatAttachment("i1", "export-1.jpg", ChatAttachmentKind.Image, "https://picsum.photos/seed/arc-chat-1/480/480"),
                    new ChatAttachment("i2", "export-2.jpg", ChatAttachmentKind.Image, "https://picsum.photos/seed/arc-chat-2/480/480"),
                    new ChatAttachment("i3", "export-3.jpg", ChatAttachmentKind.Image, "https://picsum.photos/seed/arc-chat-3/480/480")
                ]
            },
            new("m6", "me", "That fixed it, thank you both! 🎉", new DateTimeOffset(today.AddMinutes(6)))
            {
                Status = ChatMessageStatus.Read,
                Reactions = [new ChatReaction("❤️", 2), new ChatReaction("🎉", 1)]
            },
            new("m7", "me", "One more thing: can I schedule it weekly?", new DateTimeOffset(today.AddMinutes(7))) { Status = ChatMessageStatus.Failed }
        ];
        Chat.ItemsSource = _messages;
        Chat.TypingParticipantIds = _typing;
        Chat.ReadBy = new Dictionary<string, string> { ["sam"] = "m6", ["lee"] = "m6" };
    }

    private void OnSendRequested(object? sender, ChatSendEventArgs e)
    {
        _messages.Add(new ChatMessage($"s{_messages.Count + 1}", "me", e.Draft.Text, DateTimeOffset.Now)
        {
            Attachments = e.Draft.Attachments.Count > 0 ? e.Draft.Attachments : null,
            Status = ChatMessageStatus.Sent
        });
    }

    private void OnReactionToggled(object? sender, ChatReactionToggledEventArgs e)
    {
        var reactions = new List<ChatReaction>(e.Message.Reactions ?? []);
        var at = reactions.FindIndex(r => r.Emoji == e.Emoji);
        if (at < 0)
        {
            reactions.Add(new ChatReaction(e.Emoji, 1, true));
        }
        else
        {
            reactions[at] = reactions[at] with { Count = reactions[at].Count + (reactions[at].Mine ? -1 : 1), Mine = !reactions[at].Mine };
        }
        e.Message.Reactions = reactions.Where(r => r.Count > 0).ToArray();
    }

    private void OnRetryRequested(object? sender, ChatRetryEventArgs e)
    {
        e.Message.Status = ChatMessageStatus.Sent;
    }

    private void OnReplyClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        _typing.Clear();
        _messages.Add(new ChatMessage($"r{_messages.Count + 1}", "sam", "Yes! Open Settings → Exports and pick Weekly.", DateTimeOffset.Now));
        Chat.ReadBy = new Dictionary<string, string> { ["sam"] = _messages[^2].Id, ["lee"] = "m6" };
    }

    private void OnTypingClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        if (_typing.Count == 0)
        {
            _typing.Add("sam");
        }
        else
        {
            _typing.Clear();
        }
    }
}
```

## When to use

`ChatThread` is the conversation surface of an application where people talk in turns: a support widget on a billing or
order page, a direct message panel in a CRM, or a team room in an internal tool. It owns the message list, the day
separators, the scroll behavior and the composer. The page around it supplies the messages and handles what the person
sends.

- **Customer support on a billing or order page**: an invoice question answered by a support agent. Messages group by
  person and time, and the customer's messages sit on the right with a delivery state.
- **Account conversations in a CRM**: a sales owner and a customer exchange messages about a renewal. Read receipts show
  which messages the other side has seen.
- **Team rooms in an internal tool**: an incident room where engineers post text, pictures and log files. Attachments show
  as a picture gallery or a file row that opens the file.
- **Assistant replies that arrive in pieces**: a bot streams its answer into a bubble. The thread appends each chunk to the
  Markdown body without re-parsing the reply from its start.
- **Messages that can fail**: a message in a checkout or support flow that the server does not accept. It dims, shows
  "Not delivered" and offers Retry on your last message.

## When not to use

- **A threaded discussion about one object**, such as a review comment on a contract clause: use `CommentThread`, where
  replies nest under a comment and can be resolved.
- **A history of events across many objects**, such as deployments or audit entries: use `Timeline`, which has no
  composer and no read receipts.
- **Only a multi-line field with no conversation**, such as a note on a record: use `Textarea`. For @mentions in a single
  field, use `MentionInput`.
- **A composer that sits beside your own message list**: use `ChatComposer` on its own. It has the same text box,
  attachment tray and send behavior without the list.
- **History that must be paged from a server by date**: the thread displays the messages it is given and does not load
  history. Load the page in your view model and add it to the collection.

## Usage

`Participants` lists the people in the conversation, and `CurrentUserId` marks which of them is you. Your messages sit on
the right in the accent color, and other people's messages sit on the left with their names. Messages are ordered from
oldest to newest, and the list stays pinned to the newest one.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:ChatThread Label="Support conversation"
                    Participants="{Binding Participants}"
                    CurrentUserId="me"
                    ItemsSource="{Binding Messages}"
                    Height="560" />
</UserControl>
```

```csharp
var me = new ChatParticipant("me", "Alex Kim");
var sam = new ChatParticipant("sam", "Sam Rivera");

var messages = new ObservableCollection<ChatMessage>
{
    new("m1", "sam", "Hi Alex! Thanks for reaching out.", DateTimeOffset.Now)
};

var thread = new ChatThread
{
    Participants = [me, sam],
    CurrentUserId = me.Id,
    ItemsSource = messages,
    Label = "Support conversation",
    Height = 560
};
```

`ChatThread` derives from Avalonia's `ItemsControl`, so `ItemsSource` and `Items` take the collections a list does. The control builds its own rows, so you supply data, not item templates. The thread needs a bounded height from its parent.

Without an `ItemsSource`, the thread keeps its own list: messages sent from the composer are appended, and a reaction
toggles in place. Bind `ItemsSource` to your own collection when the messages come from a server.

### Anatomy

1. **Message list** (`Label` names it): the scrolling region. It follows the newest message while the reader is within
   48 px of the end.
2. **Day separator**: a 12 px label ("Yesterday", "Today" or a date) between two 1 px lines in the subtle border color.
3. **Author portrait**: 28 px, in the gutter beside other people's messages. Initials show when there is no `Avatar`.
4. **Meta line**: the author's name in 12 px medium weight and the time in 12 px muted text.
5. **Bubble**: 18 px corners, padded 8 px 13 px 9 px. Other people's bubbles use the muted surface (raised in dark mode);
   your bubbles use the accent color. A bubble takes up to 78% of the row (84% below 420 px wide) and at most 544 px.
6. **Attachments**: pictures form a gallery 240 px wide with 3 px gaps, showing up to four tiles and a "+N" scrim on the
   fourth. Other files show as a row with the name and the size.
7. **Reactions row**: one chip per emoji with its count, and a 28 px add-reaction button that opens the picker.
8. **Receipts line**: the status text and the readers' portraits, 16 px each, overlapping by 4 px.
9. **Typing row**: a 36 px bubble with animated dots, shown while `TypingParticipantIds` is not empty.
10. **Composer** (`IsComposerVisible`): a text box that grows up to six lines, the attach button and the send button.
11. **Jump pill**: 32 px high, 12 px above the bottom edge. It reads "3 new messages" when messages arrive out of view and
    "Jump to latest" when the reader is far up with nothing new.



### Binding to a view model

The view model owns the messages, their status and the receipts, and the thread displays them. This example uses CommunityToolkit.Mvvm.

```csharp
public interface ISupportApi
{
    Task<SendResult> SendMessageAsync(string text, int fileCount);
}

public sealed record SendResult(bool IsSuccess);

public partial class SupportChatViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    private readonly ISupportApi _api;

    public SupportChatViewModel(ISupportApi api)
    {
        _api = api;
        Participants =
        [
            new ChatParticipant("me", "Alex Kim"),
            new ChatParticipant("sam", "Sam Rivera")
        ];
    }

    public IReadOnlyList<ChatParticipant> Participants { get; }

    public ObservableCollection<ChatMessage> Messages { get; } = [];

    [ObservableProperty]
    private IReadOnlyDictionary<string, string> _readBy = new Dictionary<string, string>();

    [ObservableProperty]
    private IReadOnlyList<string> _typingParticipantIds = [];

    public async Task SendAsync(ChatDraft draft)
    {
        var message = new ChatMessage(Guid.NewGuid().ToString("N"), "me", draft.Text, DateTimeOffset.Now)
        {
            Attachments = draft.Attachments.Count > 0 ? draft.Attachments : null,
            Status = ChatMessageStatus.Sending
        };
        Messages.Add(message);

        var result = await _api.SendMessageAsync(draft.Text, draft.Files.Count);
        message.Status = result.IsSuccess ? ChatMessageStatus.Sent : ChatMessageStatus.Failed;
    }

    [RelayCommand]
    private async Task RetryAsync(ChatMessage message)
    {
        message.Status = ChatMessageStatus.Sending;
        var result = await _api.SendMessageAsync(message.Text ?? string.Empty, 0);
        message.Status = result.IsSuccess ? ChatMessageStatus.Sent : ChatMessageStatus.Failed;
    }
}
```

```xml
<arc:ChatThread Label="Support conversation"
                Participants="{Binding Participants}"
                CurrentUserId="me"
                ItemsSource="{Binding Messages}"
                ReadBy="{Binding ReadBy}"
                TypingParticipantIds="{Binding TypingParticipantIds}"
                RetryCommand="{Binding RetryCommand}" />
```

- The inputs (`Participants`, `ItemsSource`, `ReadBy`, `TypingParticipantIds`, `RetryCommand`) are one-way: the thread never writes them back. `IsPinned` and `UnreadCount` are read-only outputs.
- `SendRequested` is an event, not a command. The code-behind subscribes to it and passes the draft to `SendAsync`. The
  view model adds the message itself, so the thread does not append it a second time.
- Changing `Status` or `Text` on a message updates its bubble in place. Replace the collection only to add or remove messages.

### Grouping, time and culture

Messages from one person that are closer together than `GroupWindow` share a group, so only the first shows the name. The
default window is 5 minutes. A message from another person, or after a longer gap, starts a new group. 

`Culture` formats the times and day separators (default en-US), and `TimeZone` sets the zone they show in (default is the
local zone of the machine). Set both for the product's market.

```csharp
thread.Culture = CultureInfo.GetCultureInfo("en-GB");
thread.TimeZone = TimeZoneInfo.FindSystemTimeZoneById("Europe/London");
thread.GroupWindow = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(10);
```

### Sending and attachments

`SendRequested` runs when the person presses Enter in the composer or the send button. The `ChatDraft` carries the trimmed
`Text`, the chosen `Files` (local `IStorageFile` items) and the matching `Attachments`. A draft with no text and no files
does not send. Without an `ItemsSource` the thread appends the message itself. With one, the handler adds it and decides
its status, as the view model above does.

`IsAttachmentEnabled` (default true) shows the attach button and takes pasted and dropped files. `AcceptedFileTypes` limits the picker, and the tray takes at most 10 files per add. An `Image` attachment with a `Url` or `File` joins the picture gallery; other attachments show as a file row with their size.

`AttachmentClicked` runs when a picture or file is clicked. The thread opens the `Url` or local file unless the handler
marks the event as handled, so mark it handled when your app shows its own viewer.

### Status, read receipts and typing

`ChatMessage.Status` sets the text under your own last message. The states are:

| Status | Text shown | Set it when |
|---|---|---|
| `Sending` | "Sending" | The message is in flight and has not been accepted |
| `Sent` | "Sent" | The server accepted it (the default for your own messages) |
| `Delivered` | "Delivered" | The message reached the other side |
| `Read` | "Read" | The message was read; a receipt on or after it also shows this |
| `Failed` | "Not delivered" | The send failed. The bubble dims to 60% opacity |

`ReadBy` maps each participant id to the last message that person read; their portrait glides to a newer one when the map changes. Assign a new dictionary each time. `TypingParticipantIds` lists who is typing. Retry appears only when you subscribe to `RetryRequested` or set `RetryCommand`, and only on your last message. The command receives the failed `ChatMessage`.



### Reactions and the picker

The add-reaction button opens a picker of the emoji in `Reactions`. The default set is the six emoji of the Arc picker, and
`DefaultReactions` returns the same list in code. Picking an emoji, or clicking a chip, raises `ReactionToggled`. Without an
`ItemsSource` the thread toggles the reaction itself. With one, the application sets the message's `Reactions`:

```csharp
thread.ReactionToggled += (_, e) =>
{
    var reactions = new List<ChatReaction>(e.Message.Reactions ?? []);
    var at = reactions.FindIndex(r => r.Emoji == e.Emoji);
    if (at < 0)
    {
        reactions.Add(new ChatReaction(e.Emoji, 1, true));
    }
    else
    {
        var reaction = reactions[at];
        reactions[at] = reaction with { Count = reaction.Count + (reaction.Mine ? -1 : 1), Mine = !reaction.Mine };
    }
    e.Message.Reactions = reactions.Where(r => r.Count > 0).ToArray();
};
```



### Streaming a reply

A reply that arrives in pieces is added with no text, filled by `AppendToMessage` as chunks arrive and closed by
`CompleteMessage`. Each call returns `false` when no message has the id, so a late chunk for a removed message does nothing.
`IsMessageStreaming` reports whether a reply is open.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             xmlns:generic="using:System.Collections.Generic"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ChatThreadStreamingMarkdownReplyDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12">
        <Border Height="560"
                MaxWidth="640"
                CornerRadius="26"
                BorderThickness="1"
                ClipToBounds="True"
                Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Surface}"
                BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Border}">
            <arc:ChatThread x:Name="Chat"
                            Label="Assistant"
                            CurrentUserId="me"
                            Placeholder="Ask anything"
                            IsAttachmentEnabled="False"
                            SendRequested="OnSendRequested">
                <arc:ChatThread.Participants>
                    <generic:List x:TypeArguments="arc:ChatParticipant">
                        <arc:ChatParticipant Id="me" Name="Alex Kim" />
                        <arc:ChatParticipant Id="arc" Name="Arc Assistant" />
                    </generic:List>
                </arc:ChatThread.Participants>
            </arc:ChatThread>
        </Border>
        <arc:Button Content="Stream a reply" HorizontalAlignment="Center" Click="OnStreamClick" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using System.Collections.ObjectModel;
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;
using Avalonia.Threading;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class ChatThreadStreamingMarkdownReplyDemo : UserControl
{
    private const string Reply = """
        Here's a small helper that **retries** a request with exponential backoff:

        ```cs
        async Task<T> RetryAsync<T>(Func<Task<T>> run, int attempts = 3)
        {
            for (var i = 1; ; i++)
            {
                try { return await run(); }
                catch when (i < attempts) { await Task.Delay(200 * (1 << i)); }
            }
        }
        ```

        - Keep `attempts` small for user-facing calls.
        - Log the last exception before giving up.
        """;

    private readonly ObservableCollection<ChatMessage> _messages;
    private int _count;

    public ChatThreadStreamingMarkdownReplyDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        var now = DateTimeOffset.Now;
        _messages =
        [
            new("a1", "me", "How do I retry a flaky HTTP call in C#?", now.AddMinutes(-2)) { Status = ChatMessageStatus.Read },
            new("a2", "arc", Reply, now.AddMinutes(-1))
        ];
        Chat.ItemsSource = _messages;
    }

    private void OnSendRequested(object? sender, ChatSendEventArgs e)
    {
        _messages.Add(new ChatMessage($"q{++_count}", "me", e.Draft.Text, DateTimeOffset.Now) { Status = ChatMessageStatus.Sent });
        Stream($"reply{_count}");
    }

    private void OnStreamClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        Stream($"reply{++_count}");
    }

    /// <summary>Streams <see cref="Reply"/> in small chunks, as a model would.</summary>
    private void Stream(string id)
    {
        _messages.Add(new ChatMessage(id, "arc", null, DateTimeOffset.Now));
        var offset = 0;
        var timer = new DispatcherTimer { Interval = TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(40) };
        timer.Tick += (_, _) =>
        {
            if (offset >= Reply.Length)
            {
                timer.Stop();
                Chat.CompleteMessage(id);
                return;
            }
            var length = Math.Min(Reply.Length - offset, 6);
            Chat.AppendToMessage(id, Reply.Substring(offset, length));
            offset += length;
        };
        timer.Start();
    }
}
```

```csharp
messages.Add(new ChatMessage("r1", "arc", null, DateTimeOffset.Now));
thread.AppendToMessage("r1", "Here is a small helper that retries a request.");
thread.CompleteMessage("r1");
```

The Markdown body receives only the new text, so a long reply is not parsed again from its start on each chunk.

### Data shape and performance

Each `ChatMessage` raises `PropertyChanged`, so updating its properties updates its bubble. Give every message a stable `Id`, because `ReadBy`, streaming and the reaction callbacks find messages by it.

Rows are virtualized. A list of a thousand messages realizes fewer than 60 containers, and the thread keeps at most 64
rendered message bodies, so the Markdown cache does not grow with the history.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             xmlns:generic="using:System.Collections.Generic"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ChatThreadThousandMessagesDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12">
        <Border Height="440"
                MaxWidth="640"
                CornerRadius="26"
                BorderThickness="1"
                ClipToBounds="True"
                Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Surface}"
                BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Border}">
            <arc:ChatThread x:Name="Chat"
                            Label="Team history"
                            CurrentUserId="me"
                            IsComposerVisible="False">
                <arc:ChatThread.Participants>
                    <generic:List x:TypeArguments="arc:ChatParticipant">
                        <arc:ChatParticipant Id="me" Name="Alex Kim" />
                        <arc:ChatParticipant Id="sam" Name="Sam Rivera" />
                        <arc:ChatParticipant Id="lee" Name="Lee Chen" />
                    </generic:List>
                </arc:ChatThread.Participants>
            </arc:ChatThread>
        </Border>
        <arc:Button Content="New message from Lee" HorizontalAlignment="Center" Click="OnNewMessageClick" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using System.Collections.ObjectModel;
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class ChatThreadThousandMessagesDemo : UserControl
{
    private static readonly string[] Lines =
    [
        "Morning! Did the build go green?", "Yes, all checks passed.", "Shipping the release notes now.",
        "Can you review the migration?", "Looks good, one nit on naming.", "Thanks, fixed.",
        "Lunch?", "In ten minutes.", "Pushed the hotfix.", "Deploy is rolling out."
    ];

    private readonly ObservableCollection<ChatMessage> _messages = [];

    public ChatThreadThousandMessagesDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        var start = DateTimeOffset.Now.AddDays(-12);
        for (var i = 0; i < 1000; i++)
        {
            var author = (i / 3 % 3) switch { 0 => "sam", 1 => "me", _ => "lee" };
            _messages.Add(new ChatMessage($"h{i}", author, Lines[i % Lines.Length], start.AddMinutes(i * 17))
            {
                Status = author == "me" ? ChatMessageStatus.Delivered : null
            });
        }
        Chat.ItemsSource = _messages;
    }

    private void OnNewMessageClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        _messages.Add(new ChatMessage($"n{_messages.Count}", "lee", "Heads up: standup moves to 10:30.", DateTimeOffset.Now));
    }
}
```

Messages that land while the reader is scrolled up are counted in `UnreadCount` and shown by the jump pill. Older messages added at the top are not anchored for you in this release, so test that path before you ship it.

### Composer on its own

`ChatComposer` is the thread's input, and it is public so it can stand alone. It grows to six lines and sends with Enter. `Text` is two-way. `Placeholder` (default
"Message") is also the text box's accessible name. `Sent` carries the `ChatDraft`. `Send()` sends from code, `FocusInput()`
moves focus to the text box and `BrowseAsync()` opens the file picker.

```xml

### Example: support conversation on a billing page

A support panel on the billing page of a SaaS product. The panel has a fixed height, so the conversation scrolls inside it
and the composer stays visible. The agent's reply carries the statement as a file row with its size. The receipt under the
customer's last message shows the agent has read it, and the typing row shows the agent is still writing. The placeholder
names the agent, which is clearer than the default "Message".

![A support conversation with a file attachment, a read receipt and a typing indicator](https://docs.tkcode.si/shots/Docs/Activity/ChatThread/images/SupportConversation.webp)

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             xmlns:generic="using:System.Collections.Generic"
             Width="600">
    <Border Height="600"
            CornerRadius="16"
            BorderThickness="1"
            ClipToBounds="True"
            Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Surface}"
            BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Border}">
        <arc:ChatThread Label="Support conversation"
                        CurrentUserId="me"
                        Placeholder="Reply to Sam">
            <arc:ChatThread.Participants>
                <generic:List x:TypeArguments="arc:ChatParticipant">
                    <arc:ChatParticipant Id="me" Name="Alex Kim" />
                    <arc:ChatParticipant Id="sam" Name="Sam Rivera" />
                </generic:List>
            </arc:ChatThread.Participants>
            <arc:ChatThread.ReadBy>
                <generic:Dictionary x:TypeArguments="x:String, x:String">
                    <x:String x:Key="sam">m4</x:String>
                </generic:Dictionary>
            </arc:ChatThread.ReadBy>
            <arc:ChatThread.TypingParticipantIds>
                <generic:List x:TypeArguments="x:String">
                    <x:String>sam</x:String>
                </generic:List>
            </arc:ChatThread.TypingParticipantIds>
            <arc:ChatMessage Id="m1" AuthorId="sam"

                             Text="Yes, the card was charged twice. Can you refund one of them?"

            <arc:ChatMessage Id="m3" AuthorId="sam"

The scene keeps its messages inline, as a static picture must. In the application they come from `ItemsSource`.

### Content guidelines

- **Label**: a short noun phrase that names the conversation ("Support conversation", "Project Atlas"). It is the list's
  accessible name, so describe the thread, not the product.
- **Placeholder**: names the recipient or the purpose ("Reply to Sam"). The default "Message" reads like a form label in a
  support widget.

- **Errors**: use the status words the thread shows and the Retry action. Do not add a second error text under the bubble.
- **Other languages**: set `Labels`; plural rules and names belong in its functions.

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| Message | Reply to Sam |
| Conversation | Support conversation |
| Not delivered. Please try again later. | Not delivered. Retry. |
| Sam is typing... | Sam is typing |
| 1 new messages | 1 new message |

### Best practices

**Do**

- Keep the thread in a container with a fixed height, so the list has room to scroll and the composer stays at the bottom.
- Set `Status` to `Sending` when the request starts and to `Sent` or `Failed` when the server answers.
- Update the existing `ChatMessage` when it changes, so its bubble updates in place.
- Set `Culture` and `TimeZone` for the product's market, so times match the agent's clock.

**Avoid**

- Replacing the whole `ItemsSource` to change one message. Replacing the collection rebuilds every row.
- Leaving "Sam is typing" on screen after the reply arrived. Clear `TypingParticipantIds` when the event ends, or the reader
  waits for a message that is not coming.

- Expecting Retry on an earlier failed message. Retry shows only on your last message.
- Keeping the default `Reactions` for a product with its own vocabulary. Set the emoji the team actually uses.

### Common questions

**The list no longer follows new messages. Why?** The reader is more than 48 px from the end. New messages are counted in `UnreadCount`; the jump pill or `ScrollToBottom()` pins the list again.

**Why does Retry not appear on my failed message?** Retry needs a `RetryRequested` handler or a `RetryCommand`, and it
appears only on your last message. Resend the message or show the error in your own UI.

**Why do my messages show as plain text?** `MessageFormat` defaults to `Markdown`. Set it to `PlainText` on the thread, or set `Format` on one message.



## API reference

### ChatThread

A chat or support thread (Arc `ChatThread`): messages grouped by person and time with day separators, reactions, read receipts that glide to the latest read message, a typing indicator and a composer with attachments. The list stays pinned to the newest message and offers a pill when new messages land out of view.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Participants` | `IEnumerable<ChatParticipant>?` | `null` | The people in the conversation (Arc `participants`). |
| `CurrentUserId` | `string?` | `null` | The current user (Arc `currentUserId`): their messages sit on the right in the accent color. |
| `TypingParticipantIds` | `IEnumerable<string>?` | `null` | Participant ids currently typing (Arc `typing`); an observable collection is followed live. |
| `ReadBy` | `IReadOnlyDictionary<string, string>?` | `null` | The last message each participant has read, by participant id (Arc `readBy`). Their portrait sits under that message and glides when it moves. Assign a new dictionary to update. |
| `Reactions` | `IReadOnlyList<string>` | `<>z__ReadOnlyArray`1[System.String]` | Emoji offered by the reaction picker (Arc default 👍 ❤️ 😂 🎉 👀 🙏). |
| `Placeholder` | `string?` | `"Message"` | The composer's placeholder and accessible name ("Message"). |
| `IsComposerVisible` | `bool` | `true` | Shows the composer (Arc `composer`, default true). |
| `IsAttachmentEnabled` | `bool` | `true` | Lets the composer take files by button, paste or drop (Arc `allowAttachments`, default true). |
| `AcceptedFileTypes` | `IReadOnlyList<FilePickerFileType>?` | `null` | File types the attach button offers (Arc `accept`); null offers everything. |
| `GroupWindow` | `TimeSpan` | `00:05:00` | Messages from one person closer together than this share a group (Arc `groupWindow`, 5 minutes). |
| `Culture` | `CultureInfo?` | `null` | Formatting culture of times and day separators (Arc `locale`); null uses en-US. |
| `TimeZone` | `TimeZoneInfo?` | `null` | Time zone of times and day separators; null uses the local zone (as Arc's browser does). |
| `Label` | `string` | `"Conversation"` | Accessible name of the message log (Arc `label`, "Conversation"). |
| `Labels` | `ChatThreadLabels` | – | Every word the thread shows or announces (Arc `labels`). |
| `MessageFormat` | `ChatMessageFormat` | `Markdown` | How message text renders unless a message sets `Format` (default Markdown). |
| `MarkdownServices` | `MarkdownServices?` | `null` | StreamMark services for Markdown bodies; null uses `DefaultMarkdownServices`. |
| `RetryCommand` | `ICommand?` | `null` | Invoked with the failed `ChatMessage` when Retry is clicked; Retry shows when this or a handler is set. |
| `IsPinned` | `bool` | – | *Read-only.* Whether the list follows the newest message (the reader is within 48px of the end). |
| `UnreadCount` | `int` | – | *Read-only.* Messages from other people that arrived while the reader was scrolled up. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `SendRequested` | `ChatSendEventArgs` | Your message from the composer (Arc `onSend`). Without an ItemsSource the thread also appends it. |
| `ReactionToggled` | `ChatReactionToggledEventArgs` | A reaction was picked or a chip clicked (Arc `onReact`). Without an ItemsSource the thread also toggles it. |
| `RetryRequested` | `ChatRetryEventArgs` | Retry was clicked on your last, failed message (Arc `onRetry`). |
| `AttachmentClicked` | `ChatAttachmentEventArgs` | A picture or file was clicked; mark it handled to stop the thread from opening it. |

Pseudo-classes: `:narrow`, `:pinned`

Derives from `ItemsControl`: every member of `ItemsControl` works as well.

### ChatMessage

A message (Arc `ChatMessage`). Update `Text`, `Status`, `Reactions` or `Attachments` in place and the thread follows (the message raises `PropertyChanged`).

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `PropertyChanged` | `PropertyChangedEventHandler?` | Raised when a property changes. |

## Accessibility

- The message list is a named list (`Label`, default "Conversation") with a polite live setting, so each new message is read without moving focus.
- Typing is announced in its own status region ("Sam is typing", "Sam and Lee are typing"). The dots are not announced.
- Reaction chips are toggle buttons. Read receipts name the people who read a message. The portraits are decorative.
- The attach, send and add-reaction buttons take their names from `Labels` ("Attach files", "Send", "Add reaction"). The
  text box is named by `Placeholder`, and the tray by `Labels.Attachments`.
- When the picker opens, its first emoji takes focus. Escape closes it and returns focus to the add-reaction button.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Enter` (in the composer) | Sends the draft when it has text or files; ignored while an input method is composing |
| `Shift` + `Enter` (in the composer) | Adds a new line |
| `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` | Moves through the composer, the attachments, and each message's add-reaction and Retry buttons |
| `Enter` or `Space` (on a button) | Opens the picker, picks an emoji, toggles a chip or presses Retry |
| `Left` / `Right` (in the picker) | Moves between emoji and wraps at both ends |
| `Escape` (in the picker) | Closes the picker and returns focus to the add-reaction button |

The add-reaction button is visible while the pointer is over a message or a control in it has focus, so `Tab` reaches it.

## Motion

`ScrollToBottom()` glides to the end unless you pass `smooth: false`. The table shows each change:

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| A message arrives | Rises in from its side with a small scale; the list moves up | Short fade | Immediate |
| Content grows while pinned | The list follows the newest message on a spring | Immediate | Immediate |
| Read receipt moves | The portrait glides to the newer message | Short fade | Immediate |
| Reaction added or removed | The chip pops in and the count rolls | Short fade | Immediate |

| Typing indicator | The dots loop while visible | Dots stop | Dots stop |
| Jump pill appears | Rises from below | Short fade | Immediate |



## Related

- `ChatComposer` for a composer with attachments on its own.
- `CommentThread` for threaded replies on one object, with resolve and edit.
- `Timeline` for a history of events with no composer.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `ChatComposer` | You need the text box and attachment tray without the message list |
| `CommentThread` | Replies nest under one object, such as a review comment, and can be resolved |
| `Timeline` | The history is a list of events across many objects, not a conversation |
| `Textarea` | A note or description is written in several lines, with no replies |
| `MentionInput` | A field completes @mentions while people type a single message |
