# Image compare

> Drag a divider across two images to see what changed.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/image-compare

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             xmlns:pages="using:TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Pages"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ImageCompareBeforeAndAfterDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12">
        <arc:ImageCompare PositionChanged="OnPositionChanged">
            <arc:ImageCompare.Before>
                <pages:MediaArt Scene="0" Graded="False" />
            </arc:ImageCompare.Before>
            <arc:ImageCompare.After>
                <pages:MediaArt Scene="0" />
            </arc:ImageCompare.After>
        </arc:ImageCompare>
        <TextBlock x:Name="Readout"
                   Text="Position 50%"
                   FontSize="13"
                   FontFamily="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource MonoFontFamily}"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class ImageCompareBeforeAndAfterDemo : UserControl
{
    public ImageCompareBeforeAndAfterDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
    }

    private void OnPositionChanged(object? sender, ImageComparePositionChangedEventArgs e)
    {
        Readout.Text = $"Position {e.Position:0.#}%";
    }
}
```

## When to use

`ImageCompare` puts two versions of the same picture on one frame and lets the reader drag a divider across them. The
reader decides how far to reveal the change, so the component fits any place where the change itself is the point: a
retouch, a cut-out, a redesign or a visual test. It sits inside a page, a review panel or an editor, next to the
controls that produced the change.

- **Background removal on a marketplace listing**: a seller sees the original photo and the cut-out side by side on the
  same frame before the listing goes live. The divider shows whether the product edges were kept.
- **Retouch approval in a photo studio tool**: a client drags the divider across a portrait to compare the original
  skin and the retouched skin, then approves or asks for another pass.
- **Staging in a property listing tool**: an agent shows the empty room and the staged version of the same photo, with
  the captions "Empty" and "Staged" so buyers see what the furniture changes.
- **Visual regression review in a QA or design tool**: a reviewer compares the approved screenshot with the new render
  of a page and drags across the header to see whether the spacing moved.

## When not to use

- **Browsing more than two pictures**: use `Carousel`, which moves between slides without comparing them.
- **Deciding on each picture in a queue**: use `CardStack`, which asks for a keep or pass on each item.
- **Splitting live app content into two panes**: use `ResizablePanels`. The divider there resizes real content, not a
  picture.
- **Three or more versions of one picture**: use `Tabs` to switch between versions, since a divider compares only two
  sides.
- **Comparing numbers or records**: use `Table`. A picture cannot show the difference between two values.

## Usage

Both sides should use the same crop and size, so the reveal lines up.

```xml
<arc:ImageCompare Width="600" AspectRatio="1.5">
    <arc:ImageCompare.Before>
        <Border Background="#D9D2C5" />
    </arc:ImageCompare.Before>
    <arc:ImageCompare.After>
        <Border Background="#2F4858" />
    </arc:ImageCompare.After>
</arc:ImageCompare>
```

`ImageCompare` derives from Avalonia's `TemplatedControl`, not from a selecting control, so it has no items. Its two
sides are content: `Before` and `After` take any control or drawing, and `BeforeSource` and `AfterSource` can draw a
picture over them. The frame is sized by its width and `AspectRatio`, and the divider is drawn over both sides. The
before side is clipped at the divider, so dragging moves a clip and never re-lays out the content.

### Anatomy

1. **Frame**: the picture area, sized by its width and `AspectRatio` (width divided by height, default 1.5, which is
   3:2). Its corners use the theme's panel radius.
2. **After side**: the result, which fills the whole frame. `After` is sized to cover the frame.
3. **Before side**: the original, clipped at the divider. `Position` is the divider's place as a percentage from the
   left, or from the top when `Orientation` is vertical. The default is 50.
4. **Divider line**: a 2 px line with a faint 3 px edge, so it stays visible over light and dark photographs. In light
   mode the line is the raised surface color, and in dark mode it is the foreground color.
5. **Handle** (`Label` names it): a 40 px circle on the divider with an arrow on each side. While it is dragged it
   stretches into a 56 by 36 capsule. Its hit area reaches 8 px beyond the circle, and within 42 px of a frame edge it
   slows down.
6. **Captions**: `BeforeLabel` in the start corner and `AfterLabel` in the end corner, each in a frosted pill 12 px
   from the frame edge, set in the extra-small type size. The caption fades as the divider reaches it.
7. **Pictures** (`BeforeSource`, `AfterSource`): optional pictures that cover each side. A picture that fails to load
   leaves the content underneath visible.

### Labels and frame

`BeforeLabel` and `AfterLabel` caption the two sides. The defaults are "Before" and "After". Each caption fades as the
divider reaches it, so the caption under the divider never covers the detail the reader is looking at. `ShowLabels`
hides both captions. `AspectRatio` sets the frame width divided by its height, and the default is 1.5 (3 / 2). Choose
the aspect of the photographs so that the picture is not cropped heavily on either side.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             xmlns:pages="using:TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Pages"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ImageCompareWideFrameDemo">
    <arc:ImageCompare AspectRatio="1.7777"
                      ShowLabels="False"
                      Position="30"
                      Label="Cleanup preview">
        <arc:ImageCompare.Before>
            <pages:MediaArt Scene="3" Graded="False" />
        </arc:ImageCompare.Before>
        <arc:ImageCompare.After>
            <pages:MediaArt Scene="3" />
        </arc:ImageCompare.After>
    </arc:ImageCompare>
</UserControl>
```

```xml
<arc:ImageCompare AspectRatio="1.7777" ShowLabels="False" Position="30" Label="Cleanup preview">
    <arc:ImageCompare.Before>
        <Border Background="#D9D2C5" />
    </arc:ImageCompare.Before>
    <arc:ImageCompare.After>
        <Border Background="#8AA399" />
    </arc:ImageCompare.After>
</arc:ImageCompare>
```

### Vertical comparison

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             xmlns:pages="using:TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Pages"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ImageCompareVerticalDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12">
        <arc:ImageCompare x:Name="Compare"
                          Orientation="Vertical"
                          BeforeLabel="Original"
                          AfterLabel="Graded">
            <arc:ImageCompare.Before>
                <pages:MediaArt Scene="2" Graded="False" />
            </arc:ImageCompare.Before>
            <arc:ImageCompare.After>
                <pages:MediaArt Scene="2" />
            </arc:ImageCompare.After>
        </arc:ImageCompare>
        <arc:Button x:Name="Swing"
                    Content="Swing to horizontal"
                    Variant="Secondary"
                    Size="Small"
                    HorizontalAlignment="Center"
                    Click="OnSwingClick" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;
using Avalonia.Layout;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class ImageCompareVerticalDemo : UserControl
{
    public ImageCompareVerticalDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
    }

    private void OnSwingClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        Compare.Orientation = Compare.Orientation == Orientation.Vertical ? Orientation.Horizontal : Orientation.Vertical;
        Swing.Content = Compare.Orientation == Orientation.Vertical ? "Swing to horizontal" : "Swing to vertical";
    }
}
```

```xml
<arc:ImageCompare Orientation="Vertical" BeforeLabel="Original" AfterLabel="Graded">
    <arc:ImageCompare.Before>
        <Border Background="#D9D2C5" />
    </arc:ImageCompare.Before>
    <arc:ImageCompare.After>
        <Border Background="#2F4858" />
    </arc:ImageCompare.After>
</arc:ImageCompare>
```

Use the vertical layout when the change runs from top to bottom, such as a wide banner that was regraded or a page
whose header changed. Changing `Orientation` at run time swings the divider a quarter turn while the reveal follows it.

### Pictures

`BeforeSource` and `AfterSource` draw a picture over the content of each side. The picture loads in the background and
fades in from a soft blur. If it fails, the content underneath shows instead, so a page with a missing image still
compares something sensible. Set `Before` and `After` to a placeholder of the same color and crop as the picture, so
the frame looks correct while the picture loads.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             xmlns:pages="using:TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Pages"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ImageComparePhotosDemo">
    <arc:ImageCompare BeforeSource="https://picsum.photos/id/1018/1200/800?grayscale"
                      AfterSource="https://picsum.photos/id/1018/1200/800"
                      BeforeLabel="Black and white"
                      AfterLabel="Colour">
        <arc:ImageCompare.Before>
            <pages:MediaArt Scene="1" Graded="False" />
        </arc:ImageCompare.Before>
        <arc:ImageCompare.After>
            <pages:MediaArt Scene="1" />
        </arc:ImageCompare.After>
    </arc:ImageCompare>
</UserControl>
```

```csharp
var compare = new ImageCompare
{
    Before = new Border { Background = Brushes.Gray },
    After = new Border { Background = Brushes.SteelBlue },
    BeforeSource = ImageSource.Parse("https://example.com/before.jpg"),
    AfterSource = ImageSource.Parse("https://example.com/after.jpg")
};
```

### Position

`Position` is the divider position in percent from the left, or from the top when vertical. It is two-way and defaults
to 50. `PositionChanged` reports the committed value: once per whole percent while dragging, and again on release. Keys,
taps and double-clicks commit a value too.

```csharp
compare.PositionChanged += (_, e) => readout.Text = $"Position {e.Position:0.#}%";
compare.Position = 75;
```

### Binding to a view model

In an editor or a review tool, the view model holds the two pictures and the reveal position, so a saved position
comes back when the reviewer returns to the item. The control has no command: it reports its position through
`Position`, which is two-way.

```csharp
public interface IPhotoService
{
    string OriginalUrl { get; }

    string CutoutUrl { get; }
}

public partial class ListingPhotoViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    public ListingPhotoViewModel(IPhotoService photos)
    {
        OriginalPhoto = ImageSource.Parse(photos.OriginalUrl);
        CutoutPhoto = ImageSource.Parse(photos.CutoutUrl);
    }

    public ImageSource OriginalPhoto { get; }

    public ImageSource CutoutPhoto { get; }

    [ObservableProperty]
    private double _revealPercent = 50;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private string _status = "Drag the divider to compare the two versions.";
}
```

```xml
<StackPanel Spacing="12">
    <arc:ImageCompare Label="Listing photo, original and cut-out"
                      BeforeLabel="Original"
                      AfterLabel="Background removed"
                      BeforeSource="{Binding OriginalPhoto}"
                      AfterSource="{Binding CutoutPhoto}"
                      Position="{Binding RevealPercent, Mode=TwoWay}" />
    <TextBlock Text="{Binding Status}" />
</StackPanel>
```

- `Position` is written to the view model as the divider crosses each whole percent while dragging and again on
  release, so the saved value follows the reviewer's last position without a separate save step.
- A value set from the view model moves the divider to that position with a spring. Reduced motion places it directly.
- `PositionChanged` fires many times during a drag. Write analytics or a saved value on release, or throttle the
  handler, rather than on every event.
- `AfterShare` is read-only and gives the share of the after side in whole percent. Bind it to show "40% after" next to
  the frame when the wording helps the reviewer.

### Alignment and cropping

Both sides cover the frame, so the divider compares what is at the same place in each picture. If one side is cropped
differently, the comparison measures the crop, not the change. Use the same source image size and aspect for both
sides, and set `AspectRatio` to match those photographs. A photograph that is 3:2 in a 1.78 frame loses its top and
bottom on both sides equally, which keeps the reveal aligned. Two different crops of one photograph do not align at
all, so export the second version from the same frame.

### Using motion with restraint

The divider follows the pointer one to one, and it springs when a value comes from outside a drag. Motion here helps
the reader see where the change is. It distracts when the divider moves by itself, so never animate `Position` in a
loop, and avoid the orientation swing as a decoration. Use the swing only when the reader needs to switch between a
side-by-side and a stacked view. The small kick at an edge is feedback for a key press that has nowhere to go, so keep
it for the keyboard; reduced motion removes it along with the springs.

### Example: background removal on a marketplace listing

A seller tool that removes the background from a product photo before publishing. The original and the cut-out share
the same frame and the same product position, so the divider shows whether the edges of the bottle were kept and
whether the shadow was lost. The captions name each side by the step that changed it, not by "Before" and "After", so
the reviewer knows what the second picture is. The status line tells the reviewer what to do next. The shapes stand in
for a photograph so that the screenshot is self-contained; in the app, bind the two photographs as shown above.

![A product photo with the divider over an original and a background-removed version, with captions for each side](https://docs.tkcode.si/shots/Docs/Media/ImageCompare/images/CutoutCompare.webp)

```xml
<StackPanel Width="560" Spacing="16">
    <TextBlock Text="Listing photo, background removed"
               FontSize="16"
               FontWeight="Medium"
               Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
    <arc:ImageCompare Label="Listing photo, original and cut-out"
                      BeforeLabel="Original"
                      AfterLabel="Background removed"
                      Position="50">
        <arc:ImageCompare.Before>
            <Grid Background="#CFC6B6">
                <Border Height="90"
                        VerticalAlignment="Bottom"
                        Background="#A89C88" />
                <StackPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center"
                            VerticalAlignment="Center"
                            Margin="0,0,0,40">
                    <Border Width="64"
                            Height="26"
                            CornerRadius="6"
                            Background="#1E2B33" />
                    <Border Width="150"
                            Height="200"
                            CornerRadius="24"
                            Background="#2F4858" />
                </StackPanel>
            </Grid>
        </arc:ImageCompare.Before>
        <arc:ImageCompare.After>
            <Grid Background="#F6F4F0">
                <StackPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center"
                            VerticalAlignment="Center"
                            Margin="0,0,0,40">
                    <Border Width="64"
                            Height="26"
                            CornerRadius="6"
                            Background="#1E2B33" />
                    <Border Width="150"
                            Height="200"
                            CornerRadius="24"
                            Background="#2F4858" />
                </StackPanel>
            </Grid>
        </arc:ImageCompare.After>
    </arc:ImageCompare>
    <TextBlock Text="Drag the divider to compare the two versions."
               FontSize="13"
               Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
</StackPanel>
```

### Content guidelines

- **Label** (the handle's accessible name): name the picture pair, such as "Listing photo, original and cut-out". A
  generic name such as "Compare" tells a screen reader nothing about the content.
- **Before and after captions**: name the state of each side, such as "Original" and "Background removed", or "Empty"
  and "Staged". The captions are the only text a sighted reader sees on the frame, so they must say what changed.
- **Status copy**: one sentence about what the reviewer should look for, such as "Check the bottle edges and the
  shadow".
- Keep captions to one or two words, so they fit the corner chips at every frame width.

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| Before / After | Original / Background removed |
| Compare | Original and retouched |
| Image 1 / Image 2 | Front view, original / Front view, cut-out |
| Drag me! | Drag the divider to compare. |

### Best practices

**Do**

- Name each side with the change it shows through `BeforeLabel` and `AfterLabel`. A reviewer who sees "Original" and
  "Background removed" knows the question to ask without reading the page.
- Give each picture an accessible name with `AutomationProperties.Name`. The captions are visual only, so a screen
  reader would otherwise hear two unnamed pictures.
- Export both sides from the same frame, with the same size and aspect, so the reveal lines up exactly.
- Start the divider at the place where the change is most visible, such as near an edge of the product, so the reader
  sees the difference without a drag.

**Avoid**

- Comparing pictures with different framing or cropping. The divider then measures the composition, not the change.
- Looping the divider or moving it on a timer. The reader loses control of a comparison that they need to study.
- Hiding both captions with `ShowLabels="False"` when the pictures do not say what they are. A blank frame gives the
  reader no way to tell which side is which.
- Using the component for more than two versions. A second divider is not provided, so the reader cannot compare three
  pictures on one frame.
- Writing a log entry for every `PositionChanged` event during a drag. Log on release or throttle the handler.

### Common questions

**Why does the divider start in the middle?** `Position` defaults to 50. Set it in XAML or bind it to a saved value to
start elsewhere; a value set after the control loads moves the divider with a spring.

**Which key shows the before side in full?** `Home` sets `Position` to 100, so the before side covers the whole frame.
`End` sets it to 0, which shows the after side in full. `PageUp` and `PageDown` move the divider 10%.

**Why do the captions disappear near the divider?** Each caption fades as the divider reaches it, so the caption does
not sit over the detail the reader is comparing. The caption returns when the divider moves away.

**What happens when a picture fails to load?** The content under `BeforeSource` or `AfterSource` shows instead. If you
set `Before` or `After` to a placeholder of the same color, the frame still reads as a comparison.

**How do I switch between side by side and stacked?** Set `Orientation` to `Vertical` or `Horizontal`. Changing it at
run time swings the divider a quarter turn, and the position carries over.

## API reference

### ImageCompare

Before and after, split by a divider (Arc image compare). Drag anywhere to move it: the handle follows 1:1, rubber-bands past the edges and stays where it is released. A press on the image springs the divider there; on touch the press waits for a drag along the divider's axis so the page still scrolls, and a tap moves the divider. Arrow keys step 1% (Shift 10%), PageUp / PageDown 10%, Home and End reveal one side fully, and a double-click on the handle springs it back to the middle. Changing `Orientation` swings the divider a quarter turn. `Before` / `After` take any content (an `Image` with `Stretch="UniformToFill"`, a drawing, a control). `BeforeSource` / `AfterSource` load a picture with an `ArcImage` on top of that content: it fades in from a soft blur while downloading, and when it fails the content underneath shows instead.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Before` | `object?` | `null` | The original, shown on the left (or top). Sized to cover the frame. |
| `After` | `object?` | `null` | The result, shown on the right (or bottom). |
| `BeforeSource` | `ImageSource?` | `null` | Picture drawn over `Before` (an `ArcImage`, cover fit). |
| `AfterSource` | `ImageSource?` | `null` | Picture drawn over `After`. |
| `Position` | `double` | `50` | Where the divider sits, in percent from the left (or top). Two-way; defaults to 50. |
| `Orientation` | `Orientation` | `Horizontal` | Vertical stacks the images top and bottom; changing it swings the divider a quarter turn. |
| `BeforeLabel` | `string?` | `"Before"` | Caption over the before side (default "Before"). |
| `AfterLabel` | `string?` | `"After"` | Caption over the after side (default "After"). |
| `ShowLabels` | `bool` | `true` | Shows the captions; they fade as the divider reaches them (Arc `labels={false}` hides them). |
| `Label` | `string?` | `"Before and after"` | Accessible name of the divider (default "Before and after"). |
| `AspectRatio` | `double` | `1.5` | Frame proportions, width / height (default 3 / 2). |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `PositionChanged` | `ImageComparePositionChangedEventArgs` | Raised when the divider position is committed: live once per whole percent while dragging, and on release. |

Pseudo-classes: `:dragging`, `:before-image`, `:after-image`, `:before-loading`, `:after-loading`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

`ImageComparePositionChangedEventArgs` is the event data of `PositionChanged`:

| Member | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `Position` | The committed divider position, in percent from the left (or the top). |

## Accessibility

- `Label` names the divider handle. It defaults to "Before and after".
- The handle is a focusable slider. Its value is the share of the after image, for example "40% after".
- Arrow keys move the divider 1%, Shift with an arrow moves it 10%, and PageUp and PageDown move it 10%.
- Home and End reveal the before or the after image in full, and a double-click on the handle returns it to the middle.
- The focus ring appears after a key is pressed, not when focus follows the pointer.
- The caption chips are visual only. Give each picture its own `AutomationProperties.Name`, so the two sides are named
  for a screen reader.

### Keyboard

The keys act when the handle has focus. Tab to the handle first; the frame itself does not take the arrow keys.

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Left` / `Right` | Move the divider 1% in a horizontal comparison; in a vertical comparison they move it in the opposite direction |
| `Up` / `Down` | Move the divider 1% in either orientation |
| `Shift` + arrow | Move the divider 10% |
| `PageUp` / `PageDown` | Move the divider 10% |
| `Home` / `End` | Reveal the before side in full, or the after side in full |

A key pressed at either end of the range gives the divider a small kick outward, so the reader sees that the limit has
been reached.

## Motion

- The divider follows the pointer one to one while you drag, gives resistance past the edges and stays where you
  release it. The handle stretches into a capsule while it is dragged.
- Captions fade as the divider reaches them. Keys that push past an edge give a short kick.
- Reduced motion places the divider and the handle directly, without springs or edge resistance. Off jumps to the
  end state at once.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| Drag release | Settles where it is released, carrying the release speed | Placed directly | Immediate |
| Key, tap or double-click move | Springs to the new position | Placed directly | Immediate |
| Position set from code or a binding | Springs to the new position | Placed directly | Immediate |
| Key at an edge | Small kick outward | No kick | No kick |
| Orientation change | Swings a quarter turn while the reveal follows | Jumps to the new orientation | Immediate |

## Related

- `Carousel` for browsing a set of pictures or slides rather than comparing two.
- `CardStack` for going through items one at a time and deciding on each.
- `Slider` for choosing a value on a track without any picture.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `Carousel` | The reader flips through several pictures or slides |
| `CardStack` | Each picture needs a keep or pass decision |
| `Tabs` | Three or more versions of one picture are switched between |
| `ResizablePanels` | Two panes of live app content are resized against each other |
| `Slider` | A value is chosen on a track, with no picture |
| `Table` | Two sets of numbers or records are compared |

---

# Carousel

> Browse a row of slides by dragging, flicking, or arrowing through them.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/carousel

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             xmlns:demos="using:TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.CarouselSlidesDemo">
    <arc:Carousel Label="From the Harbour suites"
                  ItemsSource="{x:Static demos:CarouselDemoData.Suites}">
        <arc:Carousel.ItemTemplate>
            <DataTemplate x:DataType="demos:CarouselSuite">
                <Border BorderThickness="1"
                        ClipToBounds="True"
                        Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Surface}"
                        BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Border}"
                        CornerRadius="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource RadiusPanel}">
                    <StackPanel>
                        <ContentControl Height="200" Content="{Binding Scene, Converter={x:Static demos:CarouselDemoData.Art}}" />
                        <StackPanel Margin="18,14,18,18" Spacing="4">
                            <TextBlock Text="{Binding Name}"
                                       FontSize="16"
                                       FontWeight="Medium"
                                       TextWrapping="Wrap"
                                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
                            <TextBlock Text="{Binding Detail}"
                                       FontSize="14"
                                       TextWrapping="Wrap"
                                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
                        </StackPanel>
                    </StackPanel>
                </Border>
            </DataTemplate>
        </arc:Carousel.ItemTemplate>
    </arc:Carousel>
</UserControl>
```

## When to use

`Carousel` shows a short, ordered row of peer items on a page where the viewer glances through them and then chooses
one. The active slide sits in the center, and the neighbors on each side show that more items exist. It belongs in a
page header, a storefront section or a content hub, where the items are the same kind of thing and none needs a
decision from the viewer.

- **Featured collections on a storefront home page**: four to six seasonal collections, each a photo with a title and
  a count of items. Dragging or the arrows reveal the rest, and the viewer opens the one that matches.
- **Room types on a hotel or rental booking page**: each slide is a room with its size and nightly rate, so the guest
  compares rooms by swiping instead of opening five pages.
- **Release highlights on a product changelog**: three or four features from the latest release, one per slide, with
  autoplay left off so the reader moves through them at their own pace.
- **Customer stories on a marketing site**: three to five case studies, each a logo, a quote and a link, in a row the
  visitor can browse without a long scroll.

## When not to use

- **Deciding on each item in turn**: use `CardStack`, which asks for a keep or pass on each card and records it.
- **Comparing two images**: use `ImageCompare`, which puts a before and after on the same frame with a divider.
- **Long lists of records that people scan or sort**: use `Table`. A carousel shows one slide at a time, so
  a reader cannot compare fields across rows.
- **Text that must be read in full, such as terms, instructions or a checklist**: use `Accordion` or `ExpandableText`.
  Slides move on and hide the text the reader has not reached.
- **Switching between panels with different content**: use `Tabs`. A carousel implies that the slides are peers of
  one kind, while tabs name separate sections.
- **Messages that the user must not miss, such as a billing warning or an outage**: use `Alert` or `AnnouncementBar`.
  Autoplay would move the message away, and a carousel is the wrong place for it.

## Usage

Each child element becomes one slide. `Label` names the carousel for assistive technology.

```xml
<arc:Carousel Label="From the Harbour suites">
    <Border Height="200" Background="#2F4858" CornerRadius="12" />
    <Border Height="200" Background="#D9D2C5" CornerRadius="12" />
    <Border Height="200" Background="#8AA399" CornerRadius="12" />
</arc:Carousel>
```

`Carousel` derives from Avalonia's `SelectingItemsControl`. It has an item list, `ItemsSource` with `ItemTemplate`, and a
`SelectedIndex` that is two-way and always selects one slide. That gives a carousel the same selection model as a list,
so binding, `SelectionChanged` and automation selection all work the same way. Only the slides near the current
position are realized, so a long list costs about as much as a short one.

### Anatomy

1. **Viewport**: the track that holds the slides. The active slide sits in the center. Slide width is
   `SlideWidthRatio` of the carousel width, capped at `MaxSlideWidth`, and `SlideGap` separates the slides.
2. **Neighbors**: the slides on either side are scaled to 90% and drop to 50% opacity as they move away from the
   center. Their edges show in the margins, which is the hint that more slides exist.
3. **Viewport focus ring**: a 2 px outline drawn 4 px outside the slides when the viewport has keyboard focus.
4. **Control row**: a row below the viewport, 16 px under it. It is hidden when the carousel has one slide or none.
5. **Play and pause** (`Interval`): a button on the left of the row. It appears only when `Interval` is positive and
   motion is full. Its name changes between "Start slide rotation" and "Pause slide rotation".
6. **Indicator**: the page dots in the middle of the row. Each dot is 6 px, and the active dot stretches
   into a 22 px pill that travels with the track. The row is 36 px tall.
7. **Previous and next**: chevron buttons on the right, 8 px apart. At the first and the last slide the matching button
   is soft-disabled, so it keeps focus but does nothing.

Below 340 px the carousel is compact: the gap between the arrow buttons drops from 8 px to 4 px, and the play button
moves closer to the arrows.

### Slide width and gap

The slide takes 80% of the carousel width (`SlideWidthRatio` 0.8) up to 340 px (`MaxSlideWidth`). The cap is reached at
a carousel width of 425 px, so on a wide page the slides keep a fixed reading size and the extra width shows more of
the neighbors. Raise the ratio to 0.9 to make the slides dominate the row, or lower it to 0.7 to show more of the
neighbors on a narrow column. Keep `SlideGap` at 16 px unless the slides have their own shadow or border that needs
more air.

The slide size follows the carousel's own width, not the window's, so a carousel placed in a narrow sidebar keeps the
same proportions as one in the main content.

### Bound items

Use `ItemsSource` with an `ItemTemplate` when the slides come from data.

```xml
<arc:Carousel Label="Harbour suites" ItemsSource="{Binding Suites}">
    <arc:Carousel.ItemTemplate>
        <DataTemplate>
            <Border Height="200" Background="#2F4858" CornerRadius="12">
                <TextBlock Text="{Binding Name}" Margin="18" />
            </Border>
        </DataTemplate>
    </arc:Carousel.ItemTemplate>
</arc:Carousel>
```

### Binding to a view model

The view model owns the slides and the position the carousel should show. Bind `SelectedIndex` two-way so the view
model can set the slide at startup, and read the position back when the viewer moves. Bind `IsAutoPlay` two-way so a
settings toggle can turn rotation on or off.

```csharp
public interface IStorefrontService
{
    IEnumerable<Collection> GetFeatured();
}

public partial class HomeViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    public HomeViewModel(IStorefrontService storefront)
    {
        Collections = new ObservableCollection<Collection>(storefront.GetFeatured());
    }

    public ObservableCollection<Collection> Collections { get; }

    [ObservableProperty]
    private int _featuredIndex;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private bool _rotateFeatured;
}
```

```xml
<StackPanel Spacing="16">
    <arc:Carousel Label="Featured collections"
                  ItemsSource="{Binding Collections}"
                  SelectedIndex="{Binding FeaturedIndex, Mode=TwoWay}"
                  Interval="0:0:6"
                  IsAutoPlay="{Binding RotateFeatured, Mode=TwoWay}">
        <arc:Carousel.ItemTemplate>
            <DataTemplate>
                <Border Height="200" Background="#2F4858" CornerRadius="12">
                    <TextBlock Text="{Binding Title}" Margin="18" />
                </Border>
            </DataTemplate>
        </arc:Carousel.ItemTemplate>
    </arc:Carousel>
</StackPanel>
```

- Prefer the bound `SelectedIndex` over calling `GoTo()` from the view model. The view model then moves the carousel
  without a reference to the control, and the same binding handles the viewer's own moves.
- `SelectionChanged` fires for viewer moves and for rotation. Use it to update a readout or to log a view, and treat
  the value as the current slide, not as a decision.
- `IsRotating` and `CanRotate` are read-only. Read them to show whether rotation is running, but change rotation only
  through `IsAutoPlay`.
- The carousel has no command interface. Next, previous and go-to are methods on the control, so a view model that
  needs them keeps the carousel's `SelectedIndex` as the single source of truth instead.

### Driving it from code

```csharp
carousel.SelectionChanged += (_, _) => readout.Text = $"Slide {carousel.SelectedIndex + 1} of {count}";

carousel.Next();
carousel.Previous();
carousel.GoTo(3);
```

`Next` and `Previous` stop at the ends; they do not wrap. `GoTo` clamps the index to the valid range, so a value past the
last slide selects the last slide.

### Slide size and labels

`SlideLabelFormatter` builds the text that is announced for each slide and used as the slide's accessible name. Without
it the carousel uses the localized "2 of 5" format. Use a formatter when the slide names carry meaning, such as the
title of the content on the slide.

```csharp
carousel.SlideLabelFormatter = (index, count) => $"Archive photo {index + 1} of {count}";
```

### Autoplay

Set `Interval` to a positive time span to add a play control. The carousel moves forward on that interval and returns to
the first slide after the last one. `IsAutoPlay` starts rotation, and the play control toggles it. Rotation is off by
default, so the viewer decides when the slides move.

The indicator drains from the right while a slide is on show, so the viewer can see how long it has before the next
slide. Rotation is available only with full motion and at least two slides.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             xmlns:demos="using:TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.CarouselRotationDemo">
    <arc:Carousel Label="Seasonal offers"
                  Interval="00:00:04"
                  SelectedIndex="2"
                  ItemsSource="{x:Static demos:CarouselDemoData.Suites}">
        <arc:Carousel.ItemTemplate>
            <DataTemplate x:DataType="demos:CarouselSuite">
                <Border BorderThickness="1"
                        ClipToBounds="True"
                        Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Surface}"
                        BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Border}"
                        CornerRadius="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource RadiusPanel}">
                    <StackPanel>
                        <ContentControl Height="200" Content="{Binding Scene, Converter={x:Static demos:CarouselDemoData.Art}}" />
                        <StackPanel Margin="18,14,18,18" Spacing="4">
                            <TextBlock Text="{Binding Name}"
                                       FontSize="16"
                                       FontWeight="Medium"
                                       TextWrapping="Wrap"
                                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
                            <TextBlock Text="{Binding Detail}"
                                       FontSize="14"
                                       TextWrapping="Wrap"
                                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
                        </StackPanel>
                    </StackPanel>
                </Border>
            </DataTemplate>
        </arc:Carousel.ItemTemplate>
    </arc:Carousel>
</UserControl>
```

```xml
<arc:Carousel Label="Seasonal offers" Interval="0:0:4" IsAutoPlay="True">
    <Border Height="200" Background="#2F4858" CornerRadius="12" />
    <Border Height="200" Background="#D9D2C5" CornerRadius="12" />
</arc:Carousel>
```

### Using motion with restraint

Rotation moves content without a request, so use it only when the slides are decoration or a teaser and the reader
does not need to finish each one. Keep it off for the content the viewer must read, such as an offer's terms, a
product's price or a warning.

Rotation pauses on its own when the viewer needs control: while the mouse is over the carousel, while keyboard focus
is inside it, while a drag is running, when the carousel scrolls out of view and when the window is minimized. It
resumes when the cause ends. The play control stays visible so the viewer can stop rotation for good. Use an interval
of at least four seconds, so a slide has time to be read before it moves.

Reduced motion turns rotation off completely, so a viewer who asked for less movement sees the first slide and can
move through the others by hand.

### Long carousels

With 120 slides, only the slides around the current position are realized. The indicator then holds 120 dots. It
scrolls so that the active pill stays in the middle and fades out at the edges, so the row does not become a wall of
dots.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             xmlns:demos="using:TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.CarouselLongCarouselsDemo">

        <arc:Carousel x:Name="Archive"
                      Label="Archive"
                      SelectionChanged="OnSelectionChanged">
            <arc:Carousel.ItemTemplate>
                <DataTemplate x:DataType="x:Int32">

        <TextBlock x:Name="Readout"
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Data.Converters;
using TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Pages;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class CarouselLongCarouselsDemo : UserControl
{
    private readonly List<int> _slides = Enumerable.Range(1, 120).ToList();

    public CarouselLongCarouselsDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Archive.SlideLabelFormatter = (index, count) => $"Archive photo {index + 1} of {count}";
        Archive.ItemsSource = _slides;
    }

    /// <summary>
    /// Draws a numbered landscape. MediaArt is the gallery's stand-in for photography and its Scene and Badge are not
    /// bindable, so the template reaches it through this converter.
    /// </summary>
    public static IValueConverter NumberedArt { get; } =
        new FuncValueConverter<int, Control?>(number => new MediaArt { Scene = number, Badge = number.ToString() });

    private void OnSelectionChanged(object? sender, SelectionChangedEventArgs e)
    {
        Readout.Text = $"Slide {Archive.SelectedIndex + 1} of {_slides.Count}";
    }
}
```

### Example: storefront featured collections

A storefront home page with four seasonal collections in a row. Each slide has a color block that stands in for the
photo, a title and one line with the item count and the starting price. Autoplay is off, so the viewer chooses when to
move on, and the neighbors on both sides show that more collections exist. The copy is short and states the facts a
shopper compares: how many items and from what price. The width of the carousel is the page's content width, so the
slide size is the 340 px cap and the neighbors fill the margins.

### Content guidelines

- **Label**: name the set of slides, such as "Featured collections" or "From the Harbour suites". The label is the
  carousel's only name for assistive technology, so avoid "Carousel" or "Slides".
- **Slide title**: a short noun phrase that names the item. Keep it to one line at the slide width.
- **Slide detail**: a count and a fact the viewer compares, such as "24 pieces · from $180". Write numbers as digits and
  keep the currency symbol with the amount.
- **Slide names**: when the position matters, use a `SlideLabelFormatter` that names the slide, such as "Archive photo
  3 of 120", instead of the bare position.

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| Carousel | Featured collections |
| Click here to see more! | Trail essentials, 38 pieces from $95 |
| Slide 1 | Spring linen |
| Auto-scrolling deals | Seasonal offers, rotating every 6 seconds |

### Best practices

**Do**

- Give every carousel a `Label` that names what the slides are. It is the first thing a screen reader announces.
- Keep the active slide's copy self-contained, so a viewer who lands on it from a link understands it at once.
- Leave `IsAutoPlay` off unless the slides are decoration. A reader who did not ask for motion should not lose the
  slide they are reading.
- Use `SelectedIndex` to start on the slide the page needs, such as the newest release, instead of always starting on
  the first.

**Avoid**

- Autoplay for content that carries a warning, a price or a deadline. Rotation moves it out of view before it is read.
- Slides that do not match in kind, such as a banner next to a product card. The neighbors then read as noise, not as
  more of the same.
- Putting the only navigation to a page in a carousel. Keyboard and screen reader users still reach it, but a link list
  is easier to scan and remember.
- Very short intervals. A slide that moves within a few seconds does not allow the copy to be read.
- Replacing `ItemsSource` on every data refresh. The position is clamped and the track can jump when the items change;
  update the collection in place when the data changes.

### Common questions

**Why does the carousel stop at the first and last slide instead of wrapping?** Manual navigation does not wrap:
`Previous` and `Next` clamp at the ends, and the matching button is soft-disabled. Only autoplay wraps, and it returns to
the first slide after the last one.

**Why does the play button not appear?** The button appears only when `Interval` is a positive time span and motion is
full. With reduced motion, rotation is unavailable, so the button stays hidden and `CanRotate` is `False`.

**Why does autoplay not start even with `IsAutoPlay` set?** Rotation needs an interval, at least two slides and full
motion. It also pauses while the mouse is over the carousel, while keyboard focus is inside it, during a drag, when the
carousel scrolls out of view and when the window is minimized. `IsRotating` tells you whether it is running.

**How do I start on a particular slide?** Set `SelectedIndex`, for example `SelectedIndex="2"` in XAML, or call
`GoTo(2)` after the carousel loads. `SelectedIndex` is two-way, so the value the viewer leaves on is available to read
back.

**Why does a trackpad swipe settle on its own?** A horizontal trackpad swipe moves the track one to one with the
fingers. After 120 ms without a wheel event the carousel settles on the nearest slide, so a half-swipe does not leave the
track between two slides.

## API reference

### Carousel

A row of slides people browse by dragging, flicking, a trackpad swipe, the arrow keys, or the controls below it (Arc carousel). Use it for a short, ordered set of peers such as products or case studies, where the neighbours stay in view as a hint that there is more. The active slide sits in the center, its neighbours shrink and dim with distance, and the page indicator stretches into a pill that travels with the slides frame by frame. Slides come from `Items` / `ItemsSource` (with `ItemTemplate`); `SelectedIndex` is the active slide (two-way). Set `Interval` to add a play control that rotates through the slides; rotation pauses on hover, keyboard focus, drag, while the carousel is scrolled out of view or the window is minimized, and is unavailable with reduced motion. Only the slides near the current position are realized.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Label` | `string?` | `null` | Names the carousel for assistive technology, for example "From the Harbour suites". |
| `SlideWidthRatio` | `double` | `0.8` | Share of the carousel width one slide takes (Arc default `min(80cqw, 340px)`: 0.8). |
| `MaxSlideWidth` | `double` | `340` | Largest slide width in px (340). |
| `SlideGap` | `double` | `16` | Gap between slides in px (16). |
| `SlideLabelFormatter` | `Func<int, int, string>?` | `null` | Names each slide and its indicator; defaults to "2 of 5". |
| `Interval` | `TimeSpan` | `00:00:00` | Time per slide. A positive value adds a play control that rotates through the slides. |
| `IsAutoPlay` | `bool` | `false` | Whether the slides rotate (two-way; the play control toggles it). Off by default, so motion begins with the viewer; set it to start rotating on load. |
| `CanRotate` | `bool` | – | *Read-only.* True when rotation is available (an interval, two or more slides, full motion). |
| `IsRotating` | `bool` | – | *Read-only.* True while the rotation timer is actually running (playing and not paused). |

Pseudo-classes: `:dragging`, `:compact`, `:viewport-focus`

Derives from `SelectingItemsControl`: every member of `SelectingItemsControl` works as well.

## Accessibility

- `Label` names the carousel. Slides are announced as "2 of 5" through `SlideLabelFormatter` when the selection changes.
- Left and right arrows move one slide. Home and End go to the first and the last slide.
- Tab moves through the slides, the play control, the indicator and the previous and next buttons.
- Slides that are not active are removed from the focus order and from the automation tree.
- Autoplay pauses while the pointer is over the carousel, while keyboard focus is inside it, while a drag runs,
  when it scrolls out of view and when the window is minimized. Autoplay does not announce each slide.
- The indicator is a tab list named "Choose a slide", and each dot is a tab named like the slide it selects, such as
  "2 of 4".
- The play control is named "Start slide rotation" or "Pause slide rotation", and the previous and next buttons are
  named "Previous slide" and "Next slide".
- Selection changes made by the viewer or by a key are announced politely. Rotation does not announce.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Left` / `Right` | Move one slide back or forward; focus moves to the new indicator tab when one has focus |
| `Home` / `End` | Go to the first or the last slide |
| `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` | Move between the viewport, the play control, the indicator and the previous and next buttons |
| `Enter` or `Space` | Press the focused button: play or pause, previous or next |

Arrow keys with `Ctrl`, `Alt` or `Cmd` are not handled by the carousel, and arrow keys typed into a text box stay in the
box.

## Motion

- Slides follow the pointer while you drag and carry momentum into a snap to the nearest slide. A keyboard or button
  move slides in the direction of travel.
- Neighbors shrink and dim with their distance from the active slide.
- The indicator stretches into a pill that follows the active slide, and the pill drains while autoplay waits.
- Reduced motion jumps straight to the target slide and stops autoplay. Off jumps to the end state at once.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| Drag release | Momentum carries the track to the nearest slide; a fast flick moves at least one slide | Jumps to the nearest slide | Immediate |
| Keyboard or button move | Glides on a smooth spring toward the new slide | Jumps to the new slide | Immediate |
| Neighbor scale and opacity | Follow the track position every frame | Jump with the track | Immediate |
| Indicator pill | Stretches and follows the active slide | Jumps to the active dot | Immediate |
| Autoplay | Advances on the interval and drains the pill | Not available | Not available |

## Related

- `CardStack` when each item needs a decision, not only a look.
- `ImageCompare` for a before and after of one picture.
- `Tabs` for switching between panels that are not a row of similar items.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `CardStack` | Each item in the row needs a keep or pass decision |
| `ImageCompare` | Two versions of one picture are compared with a draggable divider |
| `Tabs` | The row switches between sections with different content |
| `Accordion` / `ExpandableText` | The reader must read the content in full, in order |
| `Alert` / `AnnouncementBar` | A message must stay visible until the user reads it |
| `Table` | The reader scans, sorts or compares many records |

# Card stack

> Review a deck one card at a time, with a throw and an undo.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/card-stack

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             xmlns:demos="using:TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.CardStackShortlistDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="16">
        <arc:CardStack x:Name="Shortlist"
                       Label="Destinations"
                       LeftOutcome="skipped"
                       RightOutcome="shortlisted"
                       ItemsSource="{x:Static demos:CardStackDemoData.Destinations}"
                       Decided="OnDecided"
                       DecisionUndone="OnDecisionUndone"
                       StackReset="OnStackReset">
            <arc:CardStack.ItemTemplate>
                <DataTemplate x:DataType="demos:CardStackDestination">
                    <Grid RowDefinitions="*,Auto">
                        <ContentControl Content="{Binding Scene, Converter={x:Static demos:CardStackDemoData.Art}}" />
                        <StackPanel Grid.Row="1" Margin="20,16,20,20" Spacing="4">
                            <TextBlock Text="{Binding Name}"
                                       FontSize="18"
                                       FontWeight="Medium"
                                       TextWrapping="Wrap"
                                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
                            <TextBlock Text="{Binding Details}"
                                       FontSize="14"
                                       TextWrapping="Wrap"
                                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
                        </StackPanel>
                    </Grid>
                </DataTemplate>
            </arc:CardStack.ItemTemplate>
        </arc:CardStack>
        <TextBlock x:Name="Log"
                   Text="Drag a card, or focus the stack and press ← / →."
                   FontSize="13"
                   FontFamily="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource MonoFontFamily}"
                   HorizontalAlignment="Center"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class CardStackShortlistDemo : UserControl
{
    public CardStackShortlistDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Shortlist.LabelSelector = item => ((CardStackDestination)item!).Name;
    }

    private void OnDecided(object? sender, CardStackDecisionEventArgs e)
    {
        var name = ((CardStackDestination)e.Item!).Name;
        Log.Text = $"{name}: {(e.Decision == CardDecision.Right ? "shortlisted" : "skipped")}";
    }

    private void OnDecisionUndone(object? sender, CardStackDecisionEventArgs e)
    {
        Log.Text = $"{((CardStackDestination)e.Item!).Name}: restored";
    }

    private void OnStackReset(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        Log.Text = "All cards are back in the stack.";
    }
}
```

## When to use

`CardStack` turns a queue of items into a deck that a person works through one card at a time. Each card asks for one
deliberate decision, pass or keep, and the next card rises into place. It fits a triage task where every item deserves
a moment of attention and a table would hide the details that matter, such as a product photo or a candidate summary.
Place it in the main area of a focused task, and show the running result, such as a count of kept items, beside it.

- **Merchandising approval**: a catalog team clears new product listings before they publish. Each card shows the
  photo, price and supplier, and the reviewer approves or rejects it. Undo covers a listing approved by mistake.
- **Candidate screening in a recruiting tool**: a recruiter keeps or passes on applicant profiles. One card per
  candidate keeps the reviewer on one summary at a time instead of a row of ten half-read records.
- **Onboarding choices in a SaaS app**: a new workspace admin keeps or passes on each suggested integration, such as
  Slack, Jira or Google Drive. The deck ends with an "All cards reviewed" state instead of a long settings form.
- **Flagged payment review in a fintech console**: an analyst confirms or clears each flagged transaction. Each
  decision is announced as it happens, and Undo returns the last one to the top of the deck before the batch is
  submitted.

## When not to use

- **Comparing items side by side or sorting them**: use `Table`. Columns and sorting let people compare
  many records at once; a deck shows one record at a time.
- **Browsing without deciding**: use `Carousel` for a row of slides, banners or photos that people look at but do not
  need to keep or pass.
- **Quick actions on a row of a list**: use `SwipeActions` for archive, snooze or mark-as-read on each row. A row is a
  place to act, not a queue that moves forward.
- **Reordering a list the person owns**: use `ReorderableList`, which keeps every item visible while it moves.
- **A single yes or no in a form**: use `Checkbox` or `Switch`, which sit inline with the other fields and need no
  queue, stamps or undo.

## Usage

```xml
<arc:CardStack Label="Destinations"
               LeftLabel="Pass"
               RightLabel="Keep"
               LeftOutcome="skipped"
               RightOutcome="shortlisted">
    <arc:CardStack.ItemTemplate>
        <DataTemplate>
            <Border Width="300" Height="360" Padding="20" CornerRadius="12" Background="#F5F1EA">
                <TextBlock Text="{Binding}" FontSize="18" />
            </Border>
        </DataTemplate>
    </arc:CardStack.ItemTemplate>
</arc:CardStack>
```

`CardStack` derives from Avalonia's `ItemsControl`, so `ItemsSource`, `Items`, `ItemTemplate` and the item container
logic work as they do in a list. Each item becomes one card, a `ContentControl` container that holds the item's
template. The stack lays out and realizes only the top four cards, plus any card still in flight, so a queue of 500
items costs about the same as a queue of five. `Label` names the stack for assistive technology.

The example above uses a fixed card size for brevity. In the theme the card is 304 px tall and the stage around it is
328 px tall, so a face built to those dimensions fills the stack without a gap.

### Anatomy

1. **Stage** (`Label` names it): the focusable group that holds the cards. It reserves the top card and the 24 px strip
   below it that the cards behind peek into, so nothing moves as cards leave. Its width is the smaller of the available
   width and 320 px.
2. **Top card**: the card that takes input, 304 px tall and 320 px wide, with the face from `ItemTemplate`. It is the
   only card that responds to a drag, a click or a key press.
3. **Cards behind**: up to three cards, each 5% smaller than the one in front and offset 12 px down, with a black shade
   at 3.5% opacity (22% in dark mode). They rise into place as the top card leaves.
4. **Stamp**: a 32 px pill in the top corner of the card, 16 px from its edges. It shows `LeftLabel` or `RightLabel`
   while the top card is dragged, and it is transparent at rest.
5. **Focus ring**: an outline drawn around the top card, or around the empty state, when the stage has keyboard focus.
   The stage itself draws no outline.
6. **Button row**: the `LeftLabel` button, the Undo button and the `RightLabel` button, 8 px apart and 20 px below the
   stage. The Undo button carries a rotate icon and the text "Undo"; below 22.5rem (360 px) it keeps only the icon.
7. **Empty state**: shown once every card is decided. It is a panel as tall as a card, with 24 px padding, a 12 px gap,
   the title "All cards reviewed" and a "Start over" button. `EmptyContent` replaces the title and the button.

Below 26rem (416 px) the stack switches to its compact layout: the cards are 280 px tall, the stage is 304 px and the
buttons use the compact size. The switch follows the stack's own width, not the window width, so a stack placed in a
narrow column changes layout even in a wide window.

### Card face and size

The card height is fixed by the theme, so the face must fit 304 px by 320 px. Keep it to a title, one or two lines of
detail and one image or icon. A long description belongs in a detail view that the person opens from the card. Use the
theme text sizes (`TypeSM` for body copy, `TypeBase` with `WeightMedium` for a title) so the face matches the rest of
the app.

### Binding to a view model

The view model owns the queue and records each decision. The stack has no command for deciding: drag, keyboard and
the buttons all raise the same `Decided` event, so one handler covers every input method. The view model holds the
collection, and the code-behind forwards each decision to it.

```csharp
public interface IShortlistService
{
    IEnumerable<Destination> LoadCandidates();

    Task SaveDecisionAsync(int id, bool keep);
}

public partial class ShortlistViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    private readonly IShortlistService _shortlist;

    public ShortlistViewModel(IShortlistService shortlist)
    {
        _shortlist = shortlist;
        Destinations = new ObservableCollection<Destination>(shortlist.LoadCandidates());
    }

    public ObservableCollection<Destination> Destinations { get; }

    [ObservableProperty]
    private string _lastDecision = "Drag a card, or focus the stack and press the arrow keys.";

    public async Task RecordAsync(Destination item, CardDecision decision)
    {
        await _shortlist.SaveDecisionAsync(item.Id, decision == CardDecision.Right);
        LastDecision = decision == CardDecision.Right
            ? $"{item.Name} kept."
            : $"{item.Name} passed.";
    }
}
```

```xml
<StackPanel Spacing="16">
    <arc:CardStack x:Name="Shortlist"
                   Label="Destinations"
                   ItemsSource="{Binding Destinations}">
        <arc:CardStack.ItemTemplate>
            <DataTemplate>
                <StackPanel Spacing="6" Margin="20">
                    <TextBlock Text="{Binding Name}" FontSize="18" FontWeight="Medium" />
                    <TextBlock Text="{Binding Details}" FontSize="14" />
                </StackPanel>
            </DataTemplate>
        </arc:CardStack.ItemTemplate>
    </arc:CardStack>
    <TextBlock Text="{Binding LastDecision}" />
</StackPanel>
```

```csharp
// Code-behind: forward the decisions to the view model.
Shortlist.LabelSelector = item => ((Destination)item!).Name;
Shortlist.Decided += async (_, e) =>
    await ViewModel.RecordAsync((Destination)e.Item!, e.Decision);
```

- `ItemsSource` is one-way: the stack reads the collection and never writes to it. `CurrentIndex` and `CanUndo` are
  read-only, so bind them one-way to show progress, for example "3 of 12".
- Use `Decided` and `DecisionUndone` for the decision itself. The event arguments carry the item and the decision, so
  the view model does not need to read the control's state.
- `ResetCommand` is an `ICommand` that restarts the deck. It can execute only while `CanUndo` is true, so a "Review
  again" button outside the stack stays disabled until a decision exists.
- Changing the collection, by adding, removing or replacing items, starts the stack over. Changing a property of an
  item does not, so update a record in place when its details change.

### Deciding and undoing in code

`Decide` throws the top card in the given direction with a default flick. `Undo` brings the last card back, and
`CanUndo` reports whether there is one to bring back. `Reset` returns every card to the stack.

```csharp
stack.Decided += (_, e) => log.Text = $"{((Destination)e.Item!).Name}: {(e.Decision == CardDecision.Right ? "shortlisted" : "skipped")}";
stack.DecisionUndone += (_, e) => log.Text = $"{((Destination)e.Item!).Name}: restored";
stack.StackReset += (_, _) => log.Text = "All cards are back in the stack.";

stack.Decide(CardDecision.Right);
stack.Undo();
stack.Reset();
```

Use these calls to drive the deck from a toolbar, a shortcut in the host app or a test without a pointer. A decision made
in code raises the same events as a drag or a key press, so the view model logic does not change.

### Naming cards

Set `LabelSelector` to return the name of each card. The name is the card's accessible label and appears in the
announcements. When the items are not strings, the selector must return a string.

```csharp
stack.LabelSelector = item => ((Destination)item!).Name;
```

Without a selector, the stack uses the item itself when it is a string, the automation name of a control item, or the
item's `ToString()`. Set the selector for any model class so the names do not depend on `ToString()`.

### Custom button and stamp text

`LeftLabel` and `RightLabel` name the buttons and the stamps that appear while a card is dragged. The defaults are
"Pass" and "Keep". `LeftOutcome` and `RightOutcome` are the past-tense words used in announcements, such as
"skipped". Without an outcome, the announcement names the action, for example "Lisbon: Keep. 4 left."

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.CardStackCustomActionsDemo">
    <arc:CardStack x:Name="Candidates"
                   Label="Candidates"
                   LeftLabel="Not now"
                   RightLabel="Interview">
        <arc:CardStack.ItemTemplate>
            <DataTemplate x:DataType="x:String">
                <StackPanel Spacing="14" VerticalAlignment="Center">
                    <arc:Avatar DisplayName="{Binding}" Size="XLarge" HorizontalAlignment="Center" />
                    <TextBlock Text="{Binding}"
                               FontSize="18"
                               FontWeight="Medium"
                               TextWrapping="Wrap"
                               HorizontalAlignment="Center"
                               Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
                    <TextBlock Text="Senior engineer · 9 years · Remote"
                               FontSize="14"
                               TextWrapping="Wrap"
                               HorizontalAlignment="Center"
                               Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
                </StackPanel>
            </DataTemplate>
        </arc:CardStack.ItemTemplate>
        <arc:CardStack.EmptyContent>
            <StackPanel Spacing="12">

                              Size="28"

```

The labels are plain text, so write them as the verbs the person performs: "Not now" and "Interview" for a candidate
deck, "Reject" and "Approve" for a listing review. Keep each label short enough to sit beside the other button.

### Empty state

`EmptyContent` replaces the default message that shows once every card is decided. Bind a button to `ResetCommand` to
offer a new pass. `EmptyContentTemplate` builds the same content from a data template and is used only when
`EmptyContent` is not set.

```xml
<arc:CardStack Label="Candidates" ItemsSource="{Binding Candidates}">
    <arc:CardStack.EmptyContent>
        <Button Content="Review again" Command="{Binding ResetCommand, RelativeSource={RelativeSource AncestorType=arc:CardStack}}" />
    </arc:CardStack.EmptyContent>
</arc:CardStack>
```

### Data shape and performance

- **Item model**: any object works. Keep each item to what the face needs and load details on demand in a separate
  view. A large model costs no more than a small one, as long as the face template is light.
- **Item count**: the stack realizes four cards and any card still moving, so the number of items does not change the
  cost of a frame. The cost that matters is the face template, which runs for each of those four cards.
- **Updates**: adding, removing or replacing items restarts the deck from the first card. Plan updates so a person does
  not lose a queue they are working through: update a single record in place, and replace the collection only when the
  batch itself changes.
- **Undo history**: each decision is kept so `Undo` can bring it back, and undo steps run in reverse order, the most
  recent decision first.

### Example: product listing approval

A catalog team at a retailer clears new listings before they go live. Each card is one listing with a photo area, the
name, the price and the supplier. The reviewer approves or rejects the listing, and Undo recovers the last one. The
labels are the verbs of the review and the outcomes are the words in the announcement ("approved", "rejected"), so
the spoken status matches the buttons. The status line below the deck gives the reviewer the last action in plain
words. The card face uses fixed copy here so the screenshot is self-contained; in the app, bind the same elements to the
listing's data.

![A product listing card in a review deck with Reject, Undo and Approve buttons](https://docs.tkcode.si/shots/Docs/Media/CardStack/images/ProductReview.webp)

### Content guidelines

- **Stack label**: a noun phrase that names the queue, such as "Listings awaiting review". It is the only name a
  screen reader gives the stack, so "Review" alone is not enough.
- **Card name**: the item's name alone, because the stack adds the position: "Lisbon, 1 of 5".
- **Button labels**: a short verb that names the decision: "Pass" and "Keep", "Reject" and "Approve". Avoid answers
  such as "Yes" and "No", which do not say what happens to the item.
- **Outcomes**: past tense, so the announcement reads as a result: "Lisbon approved. 3 left."
- **Empty state**: say that the review is complete and offer a way to start again: "All cards reviewed" with
  "Start over".

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| Yes / No | Approve / Reject |
| Left / Right | Pass / Keep |
| Done! | All cards reviewed. |
| Approved | Approved listing, or the item name with the outcome |
| Reset | Start over |

### Best practices

**Do**

- Give the stack a `Label` that names the queue. A screen reader announces it when the deck gets focus, so it is the
  first thing the person hears.
- Use past-tense `LeftOutcome` and `RightOutcome` words, so each decision is announced as a result.
- Record every decision from `Decided` in the view model. Drag, keyboard and buttons then persist the same way.
- Offer "Start over" or "Review again" in the empty state when the queue can be reused, so the end state leads
  somewhere.

**Avoid**

- Using the deck for records that need side-by-side comparison. A reader who must compare columns loses the context of
  the other items.
- Putting horizontal drags or other gestures inside a card. They compete with the card's own drag.
- Long text on the face. The card has a fixed height, and a face that does not fit is clipped.
- Relying on the stamp alone. Stamps appear only during a drag, so keyboard and screen reader users depend on the
  buttons and the announcements.
- Replacing the whole collection to refresh one record. That restarts the deck; update the record instead.

### Common questions

**Why does Undo stay disabled?** Undo is available only after a decision, and `CanUndo` is `False` again once the last
decision is undone. The button stays focusable while disabled, so keyboard users keep their place.

**How do I show how many cards are left?** Bind the count to the stack's `CurrentIndex` one-way and subtract it from
the item count, or read the "4 left" part of the announcement. The stack does not expose a remaining count property.

**Can I restart the deck from code after it is empty?** Yes. Call `Reset()`, or execute `ResetCommand`. Both bring
every card back, and the cards return from the deepest one first.

**Does editing one item restart the deck?** No. Changing a property of an item leaves the deck where it is. Adding,
removing or replacing items in the collection restarts it, so update records in place.

**Why does the card not tilt when I use the keyboard?** The tilt and the stamp follow the drag. A key press decides the
card with a default flick, so there is no drag to tilt it.

## API reference

### CardStack

A deck of cards reviewed one at a time (Arc card stack): drag or flick the top card left or right, or use the buttons and arrow keys. Use it for quick, one-by-one triage where each item deserves a moment of attention: shortlisting destinations, candidates or design options. The top card tilts with the drag and shows a stamp; a flick or a long enough drag throws it out with the release velocity, the cards behind rise into place, Undo flies the last card back from where it left, and Start over deals the deck back. Only the top four cards (and cards still in flight) are realized, however long the stack. Keyboard on the focused stage: ← / → decide, Backspace or Ctrl / Cmd + Z undo. Decisions, undo and reset are announced politely. Items come from `Items` / `ItemsSource` with `ItemTemplate`; changing the items starts the stack over.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `LeftLabel` | `string` | `"Pass"` | Name of the left action, on its button and on the stamp while dragging left (default "Pass"). |
| `RightLabel` | `string` | `"Keep"` | Name of the right action (default "Keep"). |
| `LeftOutcome` | `string?` | `null` | Past tense of the left action for announcements, such as "skipped". Without it: "Lisbon: Pass." |
| `RightOutcome` | `string?` | `null` | Past tense of the right action for announcements, such as "shortlisted". |
| `Label` | `string` | `"Cards"` | Accessible name of the stack (default "Cards"). |
| `LabelSelector` | `Func<object?, string>?` | `null` | A short name for a card, used in its accessible label and in announcements ("Lisbon"). Defaults to the item's text (a string, a control's automation name, or `ToString()`). |
| `EmptyContent` | `object?` | `null` | Shown once every card has been decided, instead of "All cards reviewed" and Start over. |
| `EmptyContentTemplate` | `IDataTemplate?` | `null` | Data template that builds the empty-state content; used when `EmptyContent` is not set. |
| `CurrentIndex` | `int` | – | *Read-only.* Index of the top card (equals the item count once every card is decided). |
| `CanUndo` | `bool` | – | *Read-only.* True when there is a decision to undo. |
| `ResetCommand` | `ICommand` | – | *Read-only.* Brings every card back (for custom empty content: `Command="{Binding $parent[arc:CardStack].ResetCommand}"`). |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Decided` | `CardStackDecisionEventArgs` | A card was decided (by drag, key, button or `Decide`). |
| `DecisionUndone` | `CardStackDecisionEventArgs` | The last decision was undone; the card is back on top. |
| `StackReset` | `RoutedEventArgs` | All cards were brought back. |

Pseudo-classes: `:compact`, `:narrow`, `:reviewed`, `:custom-empty`, `:stage-focus`

Derives from `ItemsControl`: every member of `ItemsControl` works as well.

`CardDecision` and the event data are public types the page uses:

| Type | Member | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `CardDecision` | `Left` | The card was passed (`LeftLabel`, default "Pass"). |
| `CardDecision` | `Right` | The card was kept (`RightLabel`, default "Keep"). |
| `CardStackDecisionEventArgs` | `Item` | The decided or restored item. |
| `CardStackDecisionEventArgs` | `Index` | The item's index in the items. |
| `CardStackDecisionEventArgs` | `Decision` | The decision, `Left` or `Right`. |

## Accessibility

- The stage is a focusable group named by `Label` (default "Cards"), with the role "card stack". Its help text names
  the arrow keys and Backspace, and says the top card can be passed or kept.
- Each card is named by `LabelSelector` and its position in the stack, such as "Lisbon, 1 of 5".
- Decisions, undos and resets are announced politely, so a screen reader hears them without losing focus. Examples
  are "Lisbon skipped. 1 left.", "Kyoto restored." and "All cards are back in the stack."
- The buttons mirror every gesture, so a swipe is never the only way to decide. A disabled Undo button keeps focus and
  is announced as unavailable, so a keyboard user does not lose their place when no decision exists.
- The focus ring is drawn on the top card, or on the empty state, not on the stage.

### Keyboard

The stage takes focus with `Tab`. Arrow keys decide only while the stage itself has focus; when a button has focus,
the arrows act on the focused control as usual.

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Left` / `Right` | Pass or keep the top card when the stage has focus |
| `Backspace` | Undo the last decision |
| `Ctrl+Z` / `Cmd+Z` | Undo the last decision |
| `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` | Move between the stage and the buttons; Undo stays in the order while disabled |
| `Enter` or `Space` | Press the focused button: pass, undo, keep or start over |

Arrow keys with `Ctrl` or `Cmd` are not handled by the stack, so a shortcut such as `Cmd+Left` in the host app still
reaches the app.

## Motion

- The top card follows the drag, tilts toward the direction of travel and shows its stamp. A fast flick or a long
  drag throws the card off the stack with its release speed.
- The cards behind rise into place as the top card leaves.
- Undo flies the last card back from the point where it left. Reset brings the cards back one after another, from
  the deepest one.
- A short drag springs back to the stack.
- Reduced motion fades a card out and in on the same spot, without movement. Off jumps to the end state at once.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| Top card released past the threshold | Thrown with its release speed, then fades out | Fades out in place | Removed at once |
| Cards behind after a decision | Rise into place as the top card leaves | Fade in place | Already in place |
| Undo | Flies back from where the card left | Fades in place | Shown at once |
| Start over | Cards deal back one after another, deepest first | Fade in place | Shown at once |
| Empty state appears | Settles in with a short move as the blur clears | Fades in | Shown at once |

## Related

- `Carousel` for browsing a row of items without deciding on each.
- `SwipeActions` for quick actions on a row in a list.
- `Table` for reviewing many records side by side.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `Table` | The reader compares many records by column or sorts them |
| `Carousel` | People browse slides, banners or photos without a decision |
| `SwipeActions` | Each row of a list needs a quick action such as archive or snooze |
| `ReorderableList` | The person changes the order of a list they own |
| `Checkbox` / `Switch` | A single yes or no sits inline in a form |
| `Stepper` | The task is a fixed sequence of steps rather than a queue of items |
