# Text reveal

> Reveal a short piece of content with restrained motion.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/text-reveal

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.TextRevealHeroDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="16">
        <arc:TextReveal x:Name="Hero"
                        Text="Interfaces that feel considered from the first frame"
                        Level="H1" />
        <WrapPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center" ItemSpacing="12" LineSpacing="12">
            <arc:Button Content="Replay" Variant="Secondary" Click="OnReplayClick" />
        </WrapPanel>
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class TextRevealHeroDemo : UserControl
{
    public TextRevealHeroDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
    }

    private void OnReplayClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        Hero.Replay();
    }
}
```

## When to use

`TextReveal` is a headline or a short paragraph that plays one entrance when it appears on screen. Each word rises out
of its own clip while it sharpens and fades in, so the first thing a person sees on a screen is a settled sentence
that arrived with a deliberate rhythm. It belongs at the top of a screen, where the reader's attention is on the
headline and not yet on the controls.

- **A welcome headline on a setup screen**: "Set up billing in three steps." at the top of a billing onboarding flow.
  The headline plays once when the screen opens, and the form below it is ready to use from the first frame.
- **A hero section on a pricing or product page**: the large headline of a landing page for an invoicing product,
  with a short paragraph under it that reveals word by word.
- **A release announcement at the top of a changelog page**: a headline that says what shipped, with its lines broken
  on purpose so the wording holds at every width.
- **A workspace home page greeting**: a headline such as "Good morning, Priya" that plays when the dashboard opens and
  stays put while the person works in the tables below it.

## When not to use

- **Section titles further down a page that should reveal as the reader scrolls**: use `InViewTitle`. A `TextReveal`
  mounted below the fold waits until it is visible, but it plays only once, and it is designed for the top of a screen.
- **A status line that keeps working, such as "Generating invoice summary"**: use `TextShimmer`. It loops while the
  work continues, where `TextReveal` plays once and rests.
- **Long body text**: use a regular `TextBlock`. The per-word effect is for headlines and short paragraphs only, and
  a long paragraph would keep the reader waiting for every word.
- **A label that changes state, such as "Draft" to "Sent"**: use `TextMorph`. A change to `Text` on `TextReveal` plays
  the whole entrance again, which is too much motion for a status word.
- **A warning or an error that must be read at once**: use `Alert`. A headline that reveals word by word delays a
  message the person needs straight away.

## Usage

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:TextReveal Text="Interfaces that feel considered from the first frame"
                    Level="H1" />
</UserControl>
```

`TextReveal` derives from Avalonia's `Control` and draws the whole text itself. It does not create a child control per
word, so a headline with twenty words is one control with twenty clipped words inside it. It measures to its lines, so
it sits in a `StackPanel` or a `Grid` like any text. It names itself by its text, and a heading level sets the
heading role in the outline.

The control plays its entrance once. Text with `\n` breaks lines on purpose; lines are balanced and at most 24
characters wide.

### Anatomy

1. **Headline or paragraph** (`Text`): the words, drawn line by line. A `\n` in the text forces a line break.
2. **Level** (`Level`): `H1`, `H2`, `H3` or `Paragraph`. The level picks the font size, the font family and the line
   height: `H1` uses the 4XL display size, `H2` the 3XL size and `H3` the 2XL size, all in the display font at medium
   weight. `Paragraph` uses the large body size in the body font at regular weight.
3. **Line box** (`Leading`): 1.1 times the font size for headings and 1.4 for a paragraph, from the theme.
4. **Measure** (`MaxWidthInChars`): the text is at most 24 "0" glyph widths wide. Lines are balanced, so a long
   headline splits into lines of similar length rather than one long line and one short one.
5. **Word clip**: each word rises out of a clip with a soft bottom edge while it is still arriving. Once the entrance
   ends, the words are drawn as plain text, so nothing stays masked.

### Heading levels and paragraphs

`Level` sets the heading level (`H1`, `H2`, `H3`) or `Paragraph`. Headings use display type and tighter leading. A
paragraph uses body type, regular weight and a softer blur. The level also sets `AutomationProperties.HeadingLevel` for
headings: `H1` sets level 1, `H2` level 2 and `H3` level 3. A paragraph sets no heading level.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.TextRevealForcedLinesAndDelayDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="16">
        <arc:TextReveal x:Name="Lines"
                        Text="Ship the quiet details.&#10;Keep the motion honest."
                        Level="H2"
                        Delay="0:0:0.2" />
        <WrapPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center" ItemSpacing="12" LineSpacing="12">
            <arc:Button Content="Replay" Variant="Secondary" Click="OnReplayClick" />
        </WrapPanel>
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class TextRevealForcedLinesAndDelayDemo : UserControl
{
    public TextRevealForcedLinesAndDelayDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
    }

    private void OnReplayClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        Lines.Replay();
    }
}
```

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.TextRevealParagraphDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="16">
        <arc:TextReveal x:Name="Body"
                        Text="A paragraph reveals with a softer blur, word after word, and the whole stagger stays under half a second."
                        Level="Paragraph" />
        <WrapPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center" ItemSpacing="12" LineSpacing="12">
            <arc:Button Content="Replay" Variant="Secondary" Click="OnReplayClick" />
        </WrapPanel>
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class TextRevealParagraphDemo : UserControl
{
    public TextRevealParagraphDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
    }

    private void OnReplayClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        Body.Replay();
    }
}
```

Choose the level from the page outline, not from the size you want. A welcome screen usually has one `H1` or `H2`
headline; a short lead-in under it is a `Paragraph`.

### Line breaks and width

`\n` in `Text` forces a line break, and a forced break is kept at every width. The lines are balanced inside the
width limit, so a headline with a break reads as two lines of similar length on a wide screen and still fits a
narrow one.

`MaxWidthInChars` sets the width limit in "0" glyph widths. The theme sets 24, which keeps a headline near a comfortable
line length. Set it to `0` to disable the limit and let the headline use the full width of its parent. Keep the limit
on for a paragraph, because a paragraph that runs the full width of a 1440 px screen is hard to read.

```xml
<arc:TextReveal Text="Ship invoices on the day you close the books"
                Level="H2"
                MaxWidthInChars="30" />
```

### Delay and stagger

`Delay` waits before the first word rises. The stagger after it stays under half a second, so long text does not
extend the entrance. Each word starts after the one before it, and a forced line break adds one more step, so the
second line starts after the first has begun.

A short delay gives a related control time to settle first, for example a logo or a form that appears above the
headline. Keep the delay under half a second; a longer wait looks like a slow page.

```xml
<arc:TextReveal Text="Welcome back" Level="H2" Delay="0:0:0.4" />
```

### Replay

`Replay()` plays the entrance again. Call it from code, for example from a button click. It does nothing when the
control is not attached to a window. `IsRevealing` is `true` while the entrance runs, which helps when you want to
wait for it to finish before you show something below it.

```csharp
var hero = new TextReveal { Text = "Interfaces that feel considered from the first frame", Level = TextLevel.H1 };
var replay = new Button { Content = "Replay", Variant = ButtonVariant.Secondary };
replay.Click += (_, _) => hero.Replay();
```

Changing `Text` on a control that is on screen plays the entrance again, so the change is visible. Changing `Level`
does not replay it; the new size takes effect at once.

### Entrance before the first layout

A control that is mounted below the fold waits, hidden, until it first enters the viewport. A control that is on
screen when it mounts starts on its first frame. `IsRevealing` is `true` while the entrance runs.

### Tracking, leading and blur

`Tracking` sets letter spacing in em, `Leading` sets the line height as a multiple of the font size, and
`BlurRadius` sets the starting blur of each word. The level theme sets these values; override them only when a
headline needs a different rhythm.

```xml
<arc:TextReveal Text="Quiet by default" Level="H2" Tracking="-0.02" Leading="1.2" />
```

### Driving it from data

The text can come from a view model. Bind `Text` and keep the level in XAML. Because a text change replays the
entrance, change the property only when the screen changes, such as when the person picks a different workspace.

```csharp
public partial class WelcomeViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    [ObservableProperty]
    private string _greeting = "Good morning, Priya";
}
```

```xml
<arc:TextReveal Text="{Binding Greeting}" Level="H2" />
```

### Using motion with restraint

The entrance helps once per screen: it tells the reader where the page starts and gives a calm first impression. It
distracts when a screen holds several headlines that each play, when the headline sits next to a form the person has
to fill in quickly, or when the text changes often. For those screens, use one `TextReveal` at the top and plain text
below it.

Reduced motion keeps the words in order and removes the rise and the clip, so the words only fade in quickly. With
the motion level set to `Off`, the final text shows at once. Set the level on a window or a container with
`arc:ArcMotion.Level`, which the control inherits.

### Example: setup screen for a billing product

A setup screen for a billing product opens with a headline that names the three steps and a paragraph that says how
long they take. The headline is the only `TextReveal` on the screen, so the entrance marks the start of the flow. The
paragraph uses the `Paragraph` level, so it reads as body copy and its softer blur keeps it calm. The button is the
action, and it sits under the text where the reader's eye ends up after the paragraph.

![A billing setup screen with a headline, a short paragraph and a primary button](https://docs.tkcode.si/shots/Docs/TextEffects/TextReveal/images/TextRevealSetup.webp)

```xml
<StackPanel Width="640" Spacing="16">
    <TextBlock Text="Northwind Billing / Setup"
               FontSize="13"
               FontWeight="SemiBold"
               Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
    <arc:TextReveal Text="Set up billing in 3 steps.&#10;Then send your first invoice."
                    Level="H2" />
    <arc:TextReveal Text="Connect a bank account, confirm your tax details and choose the day invoices are issued. Setup takes about ten minutes."
                    Level="Paragraph"
                    MaxWidthInChars="44" />
    <WrapPanel ItemSpacing="12" LineSpacing="12">
        <arc:Button Content="Start setup" Variant="Primary" />
        <arc:Button Content="Read the guide" Variant="Ghost" />
    </WrapPanel>
</StackPanel>
```

### Content guidelines

A headline states the outcome in sentence case, without a final period or an exclamation mark. Keep it under about
ten words so the two-line balance holds. A paragraph under the headline says what the person does next and how long
it takes. Write numbers as digits, including a step count in a headline ("3 steps").

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| "Welcome to the amazing billing setup!" | "Set up billing in 3 steps." |
| "CLICK HERE TO GET STARTED" | "Start setup" (on the button) |
| "Our revolutionary platform makes invoicing effortless." | "Send your first invoice today." |
| "We are so excited that you are here." | "Good morning, Priya" |
| "Step 1 of 3: connecting your bank account" | "Connect a bank account" |

### Best practices

**Do**

- Use one `TextReveal` at the top of a screen. The entrance tells the reader where the screen begins, and a second one
  competes with it.
- Keep the text short, so the headline settles within a second or so and the reader can start on the content below.
- Break lines with `\n` where the wording needs it, and check the break at a 360 px wide screen.
- Keep the level tied to the outline: `H1` or `H2` for the screen headline, `Paragraph` for the lead-in under it.
- Put the controls the reader needs next below the headline, so the reveal leads into the action.

**Avoid**

- Revealing body copy or long paragraphs. The word-by-word rhythm is slow to read at length, and the reader waits for
  each word.
- Changing `Text` on every update, such as a counter or a clock. Each change replays the entrance and the headline
  never settles.
- Using the effect for a status or a warning. A message the person must act on should be visible at once.
- Long delays. A `Delay` over half a second makes the page feel stalled, not considered.
- Expecting screen readers to announce a change. The control does not announce its text, so use a live region on a
  parent when a change must be read.

### Common questions

**Why does my headline appear with no animation?** The motion level is `Off`, or the text is empty. Under `Off` the
final text shows at once. An empty `Text` has no words to reveal.

**Why does my headline stay hidden until I scroll to it?** The control was mounted below the fold. It waits until it
first enters the viewport, then plays. Move it to the top of the screen if it should play when the screen opens.

**Does a headline play again when I navigate back to the screen?** Yes, if the control is removed from the visual
tree and attached again: each attachment starts a new check for the entrance. A control that stays in the tree plays
once. Call `Replay()` to play it without removing the control.

**Can I play the entrance and wait for it before I show a button?** Check `IsRevealing`. It is `true` while the
entrance runs and `false` after it ends. Under `Reduced` and `Off` the entrance ends at once or quickly, so the
button can wait on the same check in all three levels.

**How do I break a headline into exact lines?** Use `\n` in `Text`. Each piece between breaks is balanced against the
others, and a forced break is kept at every width. Check each piece fits the narrowest width the screen supports.

## API reference

### TextReveal

A headline that reveals itself once as it appears (Arc TextReveal): each word rises out of its own feathered clip while it sharpens from a soft blur and fades in, word after word (P20, P29). A title that mounts on screen starts with the first frame like Arc; one that mounts below the fold waits until it enters the viewport (S6, once). Whenever the animation cannot run (motion off, detached), the text shows at rest. Use `\n` for a deliberate line break; lines are at most `MaxWidthInChars` wide and balanced. Drawn as one control: no per-word controls.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Text` | `string?` | `null` | The headline; use `\n` for a deliberate line break. |
| `Level` | `TextLevel` | `H2` | Heading level (Arc `as`, default h2); a paragraph uses body type and a softer blur. |
| `Delay` | `TimeSpan` | `00:00:00` | Wait before the first word rises. |
| `MaxWidthInChars` | `double` | `24` | Line length limit in "0" glyph widths (Arc: 24ch). 0 disables the limit. |
| `Tracking` | `double` | `0` | Letter spacing in em (display tracking for headings). |
| `Leading` | `double` | `1.1` | Line height as a multiple of the font size. |
| `BlurRadius` | `double` | `8` | Starting blur of each word (BlurText for headings, BlurSoft for paragraphs). |
| `FontFamily` | `FontFamily` | `$Default` | Font family of the text (from TextElement). |
| `FontSize` | `double` | `12` | Font size of the text in device-independent pixels (from TextElement). |
| `FontWeight` | `FontWeight` | `Normal` | Font weight of the text (from TextElement). |
| `Foreground` | `IBrush?` | `Black` | Brush that paints the text (from TextElement). |

Derives from `Control`: every member of `Control` works as well.

## Accessibility

- Headings expose the full text as their name and set `HeadingLevel` 1 to 3. A paragraph is plain text.
- A forced line break is read as a space.
- The control does not announce its changes. Use a live region on a parent element when the text must be announced.
- The control is not focusable and has no keyboard interaction, so it adds no tab stop to the page.
- Choose the level from the page outline, not from the size you want.

## Motion

- Each word rises out of its own clip while it sharpens from a soft blur. Words start in order.
- The whole entrance plays once when the control appears on screen. It replays only when `Replay()` is called or when
  `Text` changes while the control is on screen.
- Reduced motion keeps the word order but removes the rise and the clip; the words fade in quickly.
- Off shows the final text at once.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| Control appears on screen | Words rise 0.62em, sharpen and fade in, word after word | Words fade in quickly, in order | Final text at once |
| Control mounts below the fold | Waits hidden, then plays when it enters the viewport | Waits, then fades in quickly | Final text at once |
| `Text` changes on screen | The entrance plays again | The fast fade plays again | Final text at once |
| `Replay()` | The entrance plays again | The fast fade plays again | Final text at once |
| `Level` or `Delay` changes | No replay; the new size or delay applies to the next entrance | No replay | No replay |

## Related

- `InViewTitle` for section titles that reveal as they scroll into view.
- `TextShimmer` for a status line that shows ongoing work.
- `TextMorph` for a short label that changes state letter by letter.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `InViewTitle` | A section title reveals as the reader scrolls to it |
| `TextShimmer` | A status line shows work that is still running |
| `TextMorph` | A short label changes state and the letters should move to the new text |
| `Alert` | A warning or a message must be read at once |
| `Card` | The headline sits on a card that holds its own content |

# In-view title

> Bring a section title in as it scrolls into view.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/in-view-title

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             xmlns:generic="using:System.Collections.Generic"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.InViewTitleVariantsDemo">
    <ScrollViewer Height="360">
        <StackPanel>
            <TextBlock Text="Scroll down: each title reveals itself when 45% of it is visible."
                       TextWrapping="Wrap"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
            <Border Height="380" />
            <StackPanel Spacing="64">
                <arc:InViewTitle Text="Blur sharpens word by word" Variant="Blur" />
                <arc:InViewTitle Text="Words rise out of a clip" Variant="Word" />
                <arc:InViewTitle Text="Line by line" Variant="Line">
                    <arc:InViewTitle.Lines>
                        <generic:List x:TypeArguments="x:String">
                            <x:String>Lines rise one by one,</x:String>
                            <x:String>without reflowing</x:String>
                        </generic:List>
                    </arc:InViewTitle.Lines>
                </arc:InViewTitle>
                <arc:InViewTitle Text="Tracking opens up" Variant="Tracking" />
                <arc:InViewTitle Text="A soft wipe uncovers the title" Variant="Wipe" />
                <arc:InViewTitle Text="This one replays on every entry"
                                 Variant="Blur"
                                 Level="H3"
                                 IsReplayEnabled="True" />
            </StackPanel>
            <Border Height="320" />
        </StackPanel>
    </ScrollViewer>
</UserControl>
```

## When to use

An in-view title is a section heading on a long page. It stays hidden until 45% of it is inside the viewport, then
it reveals with one of five styles. Each section announces itself as the reader reaches it, so a long page gets a
paced entrance without a separate animation timeline for every heading. It fits pages that people read from top to
bottom: a feature overview, a product tour, an annual report, a security or compliance page.

- **A billing product overview**: "Invoices and payment terms", "Tax and VAT" and "Failed payments" as section
  headings down a long landing page. Each heading reveals when the reader reaches it, so the page feels paced
  without any motion work in the app.
- **A customer success review**: a quarterly report whose chapters open with a title. The default `Blur` style suits
  editorial headings: the reader sees a calm entrance, not a burst of motion.
- **A help center or onboarding guide**: section titles that should play again with `IsReplayEnabled` when the reader
  scrolls back up to a step, so the heading they returned to is visibly there.
- **A pricing or plan comparison with fixed breaks**: a two-line headline such as "Pay for the seats you use." and
  "Add more when your team grows." The `Line` variant with `Lines` keeps those breaks at every width.

## When not to use

- **The first headline of a page that appears on load**: use `TextReveal`. An in-view title waits for the reader to
  scroll, so a hero heading at the top of the page would start only after the reader has already seen it empty.
- **A status line that keeps working, such as "Generating invoice summary"**: use `TextShimmer`. It loops while the
  work continues; an in-view title plays once and then rests.
- **Body text, labels, table headers or long paragraphs**: use a regular `TextBlock`. The per-word reveal is built
  for headings, and a paragraph that reveals word by word is slow to read.
- **A value that changes in place, such as a status word or a plan name**: use `TextMorph`, which moves the letters
  from the old label to the new one. An in-view title does not animate changes to `Text`.
- **A heading that opens and closes content**: use `Accordion`, which gives the heading a toggle and keeps the
  content state with it.

## Usage

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:InViewTitle Text="Blur sharpens word by word"
                     Variant="Blur" />
</UserControl>
```

`InViewTitle` derives from Avalonia's `Control` and draws the whole title itself. It does not create a child control
per word or per line, so a page with forty section titles holds forty controls, not thousands. It measures to the
size of its text, so it sits in a `StackPanel` or a `Grid` like any heading. It names itself by its `Text` and sets
the heading level from `Level`, so screen readers see a real heading in the page outline.

The reveal starts when 45% of the title is visible. A title that is visible when the page opens starts at once; a
title below the fold waits until the reader scrolls to it. The default variant is `Blur`.

### Anatomy

1. **Title text** (`Text`): the whole title, drawn as one run of words, lines or letters depending on the variant.
   Its text is also the accessible name.
2. **Heading level** (`Level`): sets the font size and the heading level. `H1` uses the 4XL display size, `H2`
   (default) the 3XL size, `H3` the 2XL size, and `Paragraph` the XL size. All four levels use the display font
   family, medium weight and display tracking from the theme.
3. **Line box** (`Leading`): the line height is 1.1 times the font size, from the title token. A two-line title is
   therefore about 2.2 font sizes tall.
4. **Foreground** (`Foreground`): the title color. The theme sets it from the foreground token; when no brush is set
   the title is painted black.
5. **Explicit lines** (`Lines`): an optional list of lines for the `Line` variant. Without it, the whole `Text` is
   treated as one line.
6. **Starting blur** (`BlurRadius` and `SoftBlurRadius`): the blur each word starts from in the `Blur` variant
   (`BlurRadius`) and in the `Tracking` variant (`SoftBlurRadius`). The theme sets both from the blur tokens.

### Choosing a variant

`Variant` selects the reveal style. The opacity rises first, the blur clears next where the style has one, and the
movement settles last, so the title is readable before it fully arrives. Use one variant for most headings on a page.

| Variant | What moves | Spacing between units | Settles in | Use it for |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Blur` (default) | Each word sharpens from a blur and lifts 0.2em | 60 ms, shortened for long titles | 0.8 s | Most section headings |
| `Word` | Each word rises 0.9em out of its own clip | 60 ms, shortened for long titles | 0.8 s | Headings where a clipped rise suits the layout |
| `Line` | Each line rises out of its clip | 80 ms per line | 0.86 s | Headlines with fixed breaks (needs `Lines`) |
| `Tracking` | Tight letter spacing opens up while each word clears a soft blur | 32 ms per letter | 0.9 s | Short, large openers such as a one-line hero section |
| `Wipe` | A soft-edged mask uncovers the title from left to right | None: one unit | 0.9 s | A single short phrase used as a divider |

```xml
<arc:InViewTitle Text="Words rise out of a clip" Variant="Word" />
<arc:InViewTitle Text="A soft wipe uncovers the title" Variant="Wipe" />
```

The word stagger is 60 ms per word, but it is shortened when a title has many words, so the whole stagger stays
within 0.4 s. A ten-word heading therefore starts each word 40 ms after the last. Choose `Blur` or `Word` for long
headings: the stagger stays short and the title is complete quickly.

Use `Tracking` only for short titles. The letters open across the full width of the title, so a long title looks
stretched while it moves. Use `Wipe` sparingly: its mask reads as one gesture across the whole heading, which is
effective once per page and tiring when every section does it.

### Heading level

`Level` sets the heading level (`H1`, `H2` or `H3`) and the matching `AutomationProperties.HeadingLevel`. The default
is `H2`. Choose the level from the page outline, not from the size you want. A page usually has one `H1` for its
title, `H2` for its sections and `H3` for the subsections inside a section. `Paragraph` sets no heading level, so
use it only for a short lead-in that is not part of the outline.

### Explicit lines

`Lines` sets the lines for the `Line` variant. The lines are shown as given and do not reflow. Each line must fit on
a narrow screen, so check the longest line at the smallest width the page supports. Without `Lines`, the whole `Text`
is one line.

```csharp
title.Variant = InViewTitleVariant.Line;
title.Lines = ["Lines rise one by one,", "without reflowing"];
```

Set `Lines` when the break carries meaning, such as a headline that pairs a claim with its qualifier. For copy
that should wrap naturally, use `Word` or `Blur` with `Text` alone.

### Replay on every entry

`IsReplayEnabled` hides the title when it leaves the viewport, with a quick fade and no stagger. It replays each
time the title enters again. The default is `false`, so the title plays once and then stays visible.

```xml
<arc:InViewTitle Text="This one replays on every entry"
                 IsReplayEnabled="True"
                 Level="H3" />
```

Use replay for a heading that the reader scrolls back to, such as a step in a long setup guide that the reader
returns to from a later step. Keep it off for the other headings on the page, because a heading that fades out and
rises again on every scroll competes with the content the reader is reading.

### Driving it from data

`InViewTitle` is display-only: the text comes from the view model, and the reveal runs by itself. Bind `Text` and
keep the heading level and variant in XAML.

```csharp
public partial class BillingOverviewViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    [ObservableProperty]
    private string _invoicesTitle = "Invoices and payment terms";

    [ObservableProperty]
    private string _failuresTitle = "Failed payments";
}
```

```xml
<StackPanel Spacing="48">
    <arc:InViewTitle Text="{Binding InvoicesTitle}" Variant="Blur" />
    <arc:InViewTitle Text="{Binding FailuresTitle}" Variant="Blur" Level="H3" />
</StackPanel>
```

Changing `Text` updates the words, but it does not play the reveal again. The entrance belongs to the moment the title
enters the viewport. Set the copy once per page. A title whose words change with the selection in the page, such as
the name of the open invoice, is better served by a plain heading.

### Using motion with restraint

Section titles are where this effect earns its place: the reader is already scrolling, and the heading marks the
start of a new idea. The motion is short (under a second) and it finishes before the reader reads the paragraph
beneath it.

It distracts when a page has many differently animated titles, when a heading replays on every scroll in a long list
of settings, or when a title sits inside a dense dashboard where people scan numbers. For those pages, leave the title
at the default `Blur`, keep `IsReplayEnabled` off and let the content carry the page.

Reduced motion removes all of it. With the motion level set to `Reduced` or `Off`, the title shows its final state
at once, with no movement, blur or mask. Set the level on a window or a container with `arc:ArcMotion.Level`, which
the title inherits.

### Example: billing product feature page

A feature page for a billing product has a page title in plain text and two sections below it: how invoices are
issued, and how failed payments are retried. Both section headings use `Blur` at `H2`, so the page has one rhythm
from the first section to the last. The paragraph under each heading is ordinary text, so the reader can read it as
soon as the heading settles. Each heading is a real `H2`, which keeps the outline correct for a screen reader.

![Two section titles on a billing feature page with paragraphs beneath](https://docs.tkcode.si/shots/Docs/TextEffects/InViewTitle/images/InViewTitleFeature.webp)

```xml
<StackPanel Width="640" Spacing="16">
    <TextBlock Text="Billing automation"
               FontSize="14"
               FontWeight="SemiBold"
               Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
    <arc:InViewTitle Text="Invoices and payment terms" Variant="Blur" />
    <TextBlock Text="Acme Analytics issues invoices on the first business day of each month and sends the net 30 terms with every one."
               TextWrapping="Wrap"
               FontSize="15"
               Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
    <arc:InViewTitle Text="Failed payment retries" Variant="Blur" />
    <TextBlock Text="A declined card is retried on days 3, 7 and 14. The account owner receives a notice before the last attempt."
               TextWrapping="Wrap"
               FontSize="15"
               Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
</StackPanel>
```

### Content guidelines

Section titles name the topic and stay short. Write them as noun phrases in sentence case, without a final period,
and keep them to one line at the width of the page where possible. A title is a label for the section, so the
paragraph under it carries the explanation.

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| "INVOICES & PAYMENTS" | "Invoices and payment terms" |
| "Here is how we handle the invoices you send." | "Invoices" |
| "Ready to get started" with an exclamation mark | "Start your first invoice" |
| "Failed payment processing system overview" | "Failed payments" |
| "Learn more about VAT." | "Tax and VAT" |

### Best practices

**Do**

- Use one variant for most headings on a page. Blur is the default for a reason: it reads as calm on every section.
- Set `Level` from the page outline: one `H1`, then `H2` for sections and `H3` for subsections. Screen readers and
  the outline both depend on it.
- Use `Lines` only when the breaks are part of the message, and check every line at a 360 px wide screen before you ship.
- Keep titles short. A title that wraps to four lines delays the paragraph under it and weakens the rhythm.
- Keep the copy fixed for the life of the page. Changing it does not replay the reveal, so the change is not announced.

**Avoid**

- Mixing `Word`, `Line`, `Tracking` and `Wipe` on one page. Each variant has its own timing, and the mix reads as
  noise rather than as structure.
- `IsReplayEnabled` on every heading. Replay is for a heading the reader returns to; on every heading it competes
  with the content.
- `Tracking` on long titles. The letters open across the full width, so a long heading looks stretched while it moves.
- Titles that must be read at once, such as a warning above a form. The title is hidden until 45% of it is in view,
  so a warning should be an `Alert` or a plain text row.
- Using the title as a status line or a counter. Use `TextShimmer` or `TextMorph` for copy that changes state.

### Common questions

**Why does my title not appear when I scroll to it?** The reveal starts when 45% of the title is inside a scrolling
viewport. A title that is never shown, for example one inside a tab that is not selected, does not reveal until it is
shown and then scrolled into view.

**A title near the top of a long page is already visible when the page opens. What happens?** A title that is visible
when it is attached starts its reveal at once. A title that the reader has already scrolled past shows its final state
without motion, so a reader who opens the page halfway down does not see headings play in behind them.

**Does a title play again when the reader scrolls back up?** Only with `IsReplayEnabled="True"`. The default plays
once. With replay on, the title fades out quickly when it leaves the viewport and plays the full reveal again when
it enters.

**How do I change the font of one title?** Set `FontFamily`, `FontSize`, `FontWeight` or `Foreground` on the control.
These local values override the theme for that title only. Set `Level` instead when you want the heading size that
matches the outline.

**Can I turn off the motion for a single title?** Not on its own. The motion level is inherited, so set
`arc:ArcMotion.Level="Reduced"` (or `Off`) on a window or a container, and every title under it shows its final state
at once.

## API reference

### InViewTitle

A section title that reveals itself when 45% of it scrolls into view (Arc InViewTitle, P18 + P20): opacity leads, the blur clears next and the movement settles last, so the title is readable before it fully arrives. Titles already scrolled past show at once. With `IsReplayEnabled` it hides again (a quick fade with no stagger) when it leaves and replays on every entry. Reduced motion shows the title without movement, blur or masks. Drawn as one control: no per-word controls.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Text` | `string?` | `null` | The title (also its accessible name). |
| `Variant` | `InViewTitleVariant` | `Blur` | How the title reveals itself (Arc `variant`, blur by default). |
| `Level` | `TextLevel` | `H2` | Heading level (Arc `as`, default h2). |
| `Lines` | `IReadOnlyList<string>?` | `null` | Explicit lines for the `Line` variant (no reflow); defaults to the whole text. |
| `IsReplayEnabled` | `bool` | `false` | Replays on every entry (Arc `once={false}`). |
| `Tracking` | `double` | `0` | Letter spacing in em. |
| `Leading` | `double` | `1.1` | Line height as a multiple of the font size. |
| `BlurRadius` | `double` | `8` | Starting blur of the blur variant (BlurText). |
| `SoftBlurRadius` | `double` | `4` | Starting blur of the tracking variant (BlurSoft). |
| `FontFamily` | `FontFamily` | `$Default` | Font family of the title. |
| `FontSize` | `double` | `12` | Font size of the title, in device-independent pixels. |
| `FontWeight` | `FontWeight` | `Normal` | Font weight of the title. |
| `Foreground` | `IBrush?` | `Black` | Brush the title is painted with; black when not set. |
| `IsRevealed` | `bool` | – | *Read-only.* Defines the `IsRevealed` property. |

Derives from `Control`: every member of `Control` works as well.

## Accessibility

- The title exposes its full text as its name and sets `HeadingLevel` from `Level`. A `Paragraph` title sets no
  heading level.
- The control reports the text role. The animated parts are hidden from assistive technology, so only the text is read.
- A title that is already scrolled past when the page opens shows its final state at once.
- A change to `Text` is not announced. Use a live region on a parent element when a change must be announced.
- The control is not focusable and has no keyboard interaction, so it adds no tab stop to the page.

## Motion

- The title reveals when 45% of it is visible. Opacity leads, the blur clears next and the movement settles last.
- `Word` and `Line` rise out of a clip, `Wipe` uncovers from left to right, `Tracking` opens its spacing and `Blur`
  sharpens each word.
- With `IsReplayEnabled`, leaving the viewport is a fast fade with no stagger.
- Reduced motion shows the title at once, with no movement, blur or mask. Off behaves the same way.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| Title reaches 45% visible | Units reveal in the variant's order over 0.8 to 0.9 s | Shown at once | Shown at once |
| Title already scrolled past at mount | Shown at once | Shown at once | Shown at once |
| Title leaves the viewport with `IsReplayEnabled` | Quick fade with no stagger (about 180 ms) | Stays visible | Stays visible |
| Title re-enters with `IsReplayEnabled` | Reveals again | Shown at once | Shown at once |

## Related

- `TextReveal` for the headline that plays once when the page loads.
- `TextShimmer` for a status line that shows ongoing work.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `TextReveal` | The headline is the first thing on the page and should play when it appears |
| `TextShimmer` | A status line shows work that is still running |
| `TextMorph` | A short label changes state and the letters should move from the old text to the new |
| `Accordion` | A heading opens and closes the content beneath it |
| `Alert` | A warning or a message must be read at once, without a reveal |

# Text morph

> Morph a label into its next state, letter by letter.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/text-morph

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.TextMorphStatusDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="16">
        <arc:TextMorph x:Name="Status" Text="Deploy" FontSize="28" />
        <WrapPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center" ItemSpacing="12" LineSpacing="12">
            <arc:Button Content="Next status" Variant="Secondary" Click="OnNextClick" />
        </WrapPanel>
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class TextMorphStatusDemo : UserControl
{
    private static readonly string[] Words = ["Deploy", "Deploying", "Deployed", "Rolled back"];

    private int _index;

    public TextMorphStatusDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
    }

    private void OnNextClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        Status.Text = Words[_index = (_index + 1) % Words.Length];
    }
}
```

## When to use

`TextMorph` is a short label that changes state in place. It keeps one line, measures to its text and moves the letters
that stay the same to their new positions, so a status change reads as the same label updating, not as a new one
appearing. It fits a line of product copy that is read at a glance: a status, a plan name or a price that changes
while the person is looking at it.

- **Deployment status on a release dashboard**: the label on a pipeline card moves from "Deploy" to "Deploying", then
  to "Deployed" or "Rolled back". The shared letters stay put, so the card does not flicker while the state changes.
- **Invoice status in a billing detail header**: "Draft", "Sent" or "Paid" next to the number `inv_2026_0412`. The
  change is visible from across the room in a finance review, without a toast or a modal.
- **A price in a plan picker**: "$12 / month" changes to "$120 / year" when the person switches the billing period.
  With `PrefixSuffix` matching only the amount changes; the unit at the end stays where it was.
- **A label inside a custom control**: a badge or a segmented label that changes its text as the person acts, where
  a plain `Button` would not give the right shape or behavior.

## When not to use

- **A control that is clicked and has states of its own**: use `Button`. `TextMorph` is text only and has no click,
  hover or focus behavior of its own.
- **A confirmation after copying**: use `CopyButton`, which is built for the copy action and its feedback.
- **Text that wraps onto several lines**: `TextMorph` is always one line. Use a regular `TextBlock`, or `TextReveal`
  for a headline that plays once.
- **A status line that shows ongoing work**: use `TextShimmer`. It sweeps a light across the text while work runs;
  `TextMorph` only moves letters when the text changes.
- **A message the person must read in full**: use `Toast`, which carries a full sentence and its own timing. A
  morphing label is too short to explain what happened.
- **A number that counts up or down over time**: use `AnimatedCounter`. A figure that changes every second would
  keep its letters moving, which is distracting.

## Usage

Set `Text` to the current label. When `Text` changes after the control has loaded, the letters glide, rise or fade to
the new label. The control derives from Avalonia's `Control` and draws its text itself: it measures each letter with
the text layout and draws the letters directly, so it creates no child control per letter.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:TextMorph Text="Deploy" FontSize="28" />
</UserControl>
```

```csharp
status.Text = "Deploying";
```

The control takes its font and brush from `TextElement`, the same as a text block. A value set on the control wins over
one set on a parent, and the theme sets the body font family, so an unstyled label already matches the body copy.

### Anatomy

1. **Label** (`Text`): the one line of text. Letters are measured and drawn one at a time, so the text is not wrapped
   or truncated.
2. **Font** (`FontFamily`, `FontSize`, `FontWeight`): the body font family from the theme, with the size and weight set
   on the control or on a parent. A change to any of them redraws the label at its new size without animation.
3. **Foreground** (`Foreground`): the brush that paints the letters. It inherits from `TextElement` like the font.
4. **Width**: the control is as wide as the current text. The width follows a change on a spring, so the space around
   the label (a badge edge or a button edge) grows and shrinks with the text.
5. **Motion area**: entering letters rise 0.14em from below and leaving letters lift 0.1em. The control does not clip
   its content, so these moves stay visible outside the measured box.

### Changing state

A status word changes from one state to the next. The letters both labels share glide to their new positions. New
letters rise in with a short stagger, and removed letters fade away. Set `Text` to the next state in code, for example
when the job's status arrives from a service.

```csharp
var words = new[] { "Deploy", "Deploying", "Deployed", "Rolled back" };
var index = 0;
next.Click += (_, _) => status.Text = words[index = (index + 1) % words.Length];
```

Keep the list of states short and in the order a person reads them. A label that jumps between unrelated words, such
as "Deploy" and "Rolled back", still animates correctly, but the shared letters are few and the motion carries less
meaning. Use a plain change for such pairs.

### Binding to a view model

`TextMorph` is display-only. The view model owns the state, and the label follows its text. Bind `Text` to a string
property; each change is a morph, so set the property only when the state changes.

```csharp
public partial class DeploymentViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    [ObservableProperty]
    private string _statusLabel = "Deploy";

    public void MarkRunning() => StatusLabel = "Deploying";

    public void MarkDone(bool succeeded) => StatusLabel = succeeded ? "Deployed" : "Rolled back";
}
```

```xml
<arc:TextMorph Text="{Binding StatusLabel}" FontSize="28" FontWeight="SemiBold" />
```

Do not bind `Text` to a value that changes on every frame or every tick. The label morphs on each change, so a value
that changes ten times a second keeps the letters in motion all the time.

### Matching

`Matching` sets how letters are paired between the old and the new text. It takes a `TextMorphMatching` value.

- `Occurrence` (default) pairs each character with the same occurrence in the new text. The second "i" pairs with the
  second "i". Use it for words, where letters move to their new places within the word.
- `PrefixSuffix` keeps the shared start and end in place and replaces only the middle. Use it for prices and counters,
  where the unit or the currency sign should not move while the number changes.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.TextMorphPrefixAndSuffixDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="16">
        <arc:TextMorph x:Name="Price"
                       Text="$12 / month"
                       FontSize="20"
                       Matching="PrefixSuffix" />
        <WrapPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center" ItemSpacing="12" LineSpacing="12">
            <arc:Button Content="Change plan" Variant="Secondary" Click="OnChangePlanClick" />
        </WrapPanel>
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class TextMorphPrefixAndSuffixDemo : UserControl
{
    private static readonly string[] Prices = ["$12 / month", "$120 / year", "$10 / month"];

    private int _index;

    public TextMorphPrefixAndSuffixDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
    }

    private void OnChangePlanClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        Price.Text = Prices[_index = (_index + 1) % Prices.Length];
    }
}
```

Matching works on single characters, so a character that the font would join into one shape (a ligature, or a
combined emoji) can separate while it morphs. Check such strings in the real font before you rely on them.

### Font

`TextMorph` uses the font and foreground properties of `TextElement`. Set them on the control or on a parent.

```xml
<arc:TextMorph Text="Saved" FontSize="16" FontWeight="SemiBold" />
```

A parent that sets the style for a whole row works the same way, so the status labels in a list share one size:

```xml
<StackPanel TextElement.FontSize="14"
            TextElement.FontWeight="Medium"
            TextElement.Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}">
    <arc:TextMorph Text="Draft" />
</StackPanel>
```

### Example: invoice status in a billing header

A billing detail header shows the invoice number, the amount and a status label. The status is the only part that
changes while the person works on the invoice, so it is the one `TextMorph`. The card keeps the same width for every
state, so the header does not move when the label grows from "Sent" to "Awaiting payment". The amount and the due
date are plain text that stays put.

![An invoice header with a morphing status label and the amount due](https://docs.tkcode.si/shots/Docs/TextEffects/TextMorph/images/TextMorphInvoiceStatus.webp)

```xml
<Border Width="560"
        Padding="20"
        CornerRadius="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource RadiusPanel}"
        Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Surface}"
        BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Border}"
        BorderThickness="1">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12">
        <TextBlock Text="Invoice inv_2026_0412"
                   FontSize="13"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
        <arc:TextMorph Text="Awaiting payment"
                       FontSize="22"
                       FontWeight="SemiBold" />
        <Grid ColumnDefinitions="*,Auto">
            <TextBlock Grid.Column="0"
                       Text="Due 2026-11-05"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
            <TextBlock Grid.Column="1"
                       Text="$4,800.00"
                       FontWeight="SemiBold"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
        </Grid>
    </StackPanel>
</Border>
```

### Content guidelines

A morphing label is short by design: one word or a short phrase in sentence case, with no final period. Keep the
states the same kind of word, such as the status of an object, so the change reads as a state and not as a sentence.
Put numbers in digits and keep the unit with the number.

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| "Your invoice has now been sent to the customer." | "Sent" |
| "PAID IN FULL" | "Paid" |
| "Deploying now..." | "Deploying" |
| "Price: 120 dollars per year" | "$120 / year" |
| "Rolled back because of a failure" | "Rolled back" |

### Best practices

**Do**

- Keep each state to one or two words. A long label makes the width spring visible and pushes its neighbors.
- Place the label in a container with a fixed width, or in a `Grid` column that is wide enough for the longest state.
  The control's width follows its text, so an unbounded label moves what sits beside it.
- Use `PrefixSuffix` for prices and counters, so the stable part of the label stays in place.
- Change the label only when the state changes. Each change is a motion the person must follow, so keep them rare.
- Announce the change with a live region on a parent when the new state matters. The control does not announce it.

**Avoid**

- Binding the label to a value that changes every tick, such as a timer or a progress percentage. The letters never
  settle, and a progress value is better shown in `Progress`.
- Using `TextMorph` for a button's label that has click behavior. The control has no click or focus of its own.
- Long sentences or wrapped copy. The control is one line, and a long state pushes the layout around it.
- Relying on the motion to convey the change. Reduced and Off motion jump to the new label, so the words must
  already say what changed.
- Setting the label before the control loads and expecting it to animate. The first text appears without motion.

### Common questions

**Why does my label jump instead of morphing?** The label morphs only after it has loaded, and only while the motion
level is `Full`. Under `Reduced` or `Off`, a change replaces the label at once. A change to `FontSize`, `FontWeight`
or `FontFamily` also jumps to the new size, because the letters are re-measured rather than moved.

**Why does the row next to the label move when the state changes?** The control's width follows its text on a spring,
so a longer state pushes the controls beside it. Give the label a fixed width in a `Grid` column, or measure the
longest state and reserve that width.

**Does a label morph when I set `Text` to the same value?** No. The morph starts when the text changes; setting the
same string again leaves the letters where they are.

**Can the label wrap onto two lines?** No. The control is always one line. For text that needs two lines, use
`TextReveal` for a headline or a regular text block for body copy.

**How do I make the letters move with a different motion?** The motion is fixed by the control. Its timing and
distances are built in, and the motion level set on a window or a container (`arc:ArcMotion.Level`) decides whether it
plays. Pick the states and the matching mode, and let the control do the rest.

## API reference

### TextMorph

Morphs one short label into the next in place (P4): letters both strings share glide to their new positions, new letters sharpen in with a short stagger, removed letters blur away, and the width follows on a spring. Single line; assistive technology reads the plain text. Rendered directly: no control per letter.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Text` | `string?` | `null` | The label to show; a change morphs the letters from the old text to the new one. |
| `Matching` | `TextMorphMatching` | `Occurrence` | How letters pair between the old and the new text: Occurrence (default) or PrefixSuffix. |
| `FontFamily` | `FontFamily` | `$Default` | Font family of the text (from TextElement). |
| `FontSize` | `double` | `12` | Font size of the text in device-independent pixels (from TextElement). |
| `FontWeight` | `FontWeight` | `Normal` | Font weight of the text (from TextElement). |
| `Foreground` | `IBrush?` | `Black` | Brush that paints the text (from TextElement). |

Derives from `Control`: every member of `Control` works as well.

## Accessibility

- The current text is the control's name. Assistive technology reads the plain text.
- The letters are hidden from assistive technology, so a change is not read letter by letter.
- The control does not announce a change. Use a live region on a parent element when the new state must be announced.
- Under `Reduced` and `Off` motion the new text appears at once, so the words alone must carry the change.
- The control is not focusable and has no keyboard interaction, so it adds no tab stop to the page.

## Motion

- Shared letters glide to their new positions on a spring.
- New letters rise and grow in from 80% size while they fade in, one after another. The first starts after 50 ms, each
  following letter 32 ms later, for up to eight letters.
- Removed letters fade out while they shrink slightly and lift a little, then disappear. Their exit is a short
  standard fade.
- The container width follows the new label on a spring. A font change or a size change of the container jumps to the
  new width without animation.
- Reduced motion replaces the label and the width at once. Off behaves the same way.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| Shared letters move | Glide to their new positions on a spring | Jump | Jump |
| New letters appear | Rise 0.14em while they fade in, staggered | Jump | Jump |
| Removed letters | Fade out, lift 0.1em, then leave | Removed at once | Removed at once |
| Width of the label | Springs to the new width | Jumps | Jumps |
| Font, weight or size change | Jumps to the new size | Jumps | Jumps |
| Text set before the control loads | Shown at once, no motion | Shown at once | Shown at once |

## Related

- `Button` for a control that is clicked and has states of its own.
- `TextShimmer` for a status line that shows ongoing work.
- `TextReveal` for a headline that plays once when it appears.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `Button` | The label belongs to a control that is clicked |
| `CopyButton` | The label confirms that something was copied |
| `TextShimmer` | A status line shows work that is still running |
| `TextReveal` | A headline should play once when it appears |
| `AnimatedCounter` | A figure counts up or down over time |
| `Toast` | A full sentence must be read, such as the result of an action |
