# Text shimmer

> Show ongoing work with a calm light across the words.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/text-shimmer

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.TextShimmerStatusLineDemo">
    <arc:TextShimmer Text="Thinking" />
</UserControl>
```

## When to use

`TextShimmer` is a single line of status text with a soft light that sweeps across it while work is running. It sits
where an application reports that something is still happening and has no measurable amount to show: in a status
bar, a page header, an activity row or an assistant's reply. The light says "still working" without a spinner, and
the words say what the work is.

- **An AI assistant that is still working**: a "Thinking" line above a reply, then "Generating summary" while a
  long answer is written. The label is the only thing that moves, so the reply area stays readable.
- **A background import or sync in an admin console**: a panel that shows "Importing 2,340 orders" while a nightly
  job runs. When the job ends, the same control switches to "Import complete" and the text settles in place.
- **A multi-step job whose steps are known only by name**: a workspace export that moves through "Reading 14 files",
  "Drafting a plan" and "Writing the summary". Each step replaces the text while the sweep keeps running.
- **A developer tool header while a build runs**: "Compiling 212 modules" in the top bar of a deployment view, with
  the sweep stopped once the build passes.
- **A finished label that stays on screen**: a status line that ends as solid text, such as "Summary ready", so the
  result reads as settled rather than as a loading state.

## When not to use

- **A placeholder for content that has not arrived yet**: use `Skeleton`, which shows the shape of the content. A
  shimmer over words tells people about work, not about layout.
- **Work with a known amount done**: use `Progress`, which shows how far the job has come. A sweep cannot show a
  percentage or a remaining time.
- **A label that changes letter by letter without a sweep**: use `TextMorph`, which morphs the characters into the
  next label.
- **Paragraphs or several lines of text**: use a plain `TextBlock`. The control is built for one short line and does
  not wrap.
- **A problem that needs the person to act**: a failed import, an expired session or a payment that was declined.
  Use `Alert` with the message and the next step. A sweep on a failed job says the work is still running, which is
  false.
- **Text that never changes and no work is running**: a page title or a field label. The sweep would only add noise.

## Usage

`TextShimmer` derives from Avalonia's `Control`, not from `TextBlock`, and draws its own text. Its `FontFamily`,
`FontSize`, `FontWeight` and `Foreground` properties default to the values inherited from `TextElement`, so it takes
the typography of the surrounding style without extra markup. Because it is one control that draws directly, a
busy label is one element on the page, not one element per letter. Keep the number of animated labels on a screen
small: one or two busy lines are readable, a row of six competes for attention.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:TextShimmer Text="Thinking" />
</UserControl>
```

The sweep runs while `IsActive` is `true`, which is the default. A new control therefore starts sweeping as soon as
it is shown. Set `IsActive` to `false` when the work ends, and the text settles to a solid color.

### Anatomy

1. **Base text** (drawn in `BaseForeground`): the resting color of the line. When `BaseForeground` is not set, the
   base is 12% of the `Foreground` color mixed into the muted text color in the OKLab color space. The theme sets the
   muted color to the TextMuted token, so the resting label keeps the palette of the text around it.
2. **Band**: a bell-shaped band in the `Foreground` color, 4.4 em wide (2.2 em on each side of its center). It is
   strongest at its center and fades to nothing at both edges. Internally it is the text drawn again through a
   moving mask, so the band follows the letters exactly.
3. **Solid text**: the `Foreground` color at full strength. It replaces the base once `IsActive` is `false`, and the
   band has left the line.
4. **Line**: one line of text at `FontSize` (14 px by default, from the TypeSM token), in `BodyFontFamily` at regular
   weight. The control measures the width of the text and the height of one line. It never wraps.

### Choosing the state

Use `IsActive` to say whether the work is still running, not to decorate the page. A shimmer on a label whose work
has finished tells people to wait.

- **Busy**: `IsActive="True"`, the default. The band runs and the accessible item status is "Busy".
- **Finished**: `IsActive="False"`. The band glides off and the text becomes solid. Keep the control in place, so the
  line settles where it was.
- **Idle before the first request**: create the control with `IsActive="False"`. It then shows solid text and does
  not run the loop until you set `IsActive` to `true`.

```xml
<arc:TextShimmer Text="Ready to import" IsActive="False" />
```

### Changing the text

A new `Text` value rises in place while the line springs to its new width. Keep `IsActive` on while the steps change,
so the band keeps running across the change.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.TextShimmerChangingAndFinishingDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="16">
        <arc:TextShimmer x:Name="Summary" Text="Generating summary" FontSize="22" />
        <WrapPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center" ItemSpacing="12" LineSpacing="12">
            <arc:Button Content="Next step" Variant="Secondary" Click="OnNextClick" />
            <arc:Button Content="Finish" Variant="Secondary" Click="OnFinishClick" />
        </WrapPanel>
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class TextShimmerChangingAndFinishingDemo : UserControl
{
    private static readonly string[] Steps = ["Reading 14 files", "Drafting a plan", "Writing the summary"];

    private int _index;

    public TextShimmerChangingAndFinishingDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
    }

    private void OnNextClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        Summary.IsActive = true;
        Summary.Text = Steps[_index = (_index + 1) % Steps.Length];
    }

    private void OnFinishClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        Summary.Text = "Summary ready";
        Summary.IsActive = false;
    }
}
```

Write each step as a short present participle with its object, and keep each one on screen long enough to read. A
label that changes faster than people can read it becomes a blur of rising words.

### Finishing

Set `IsActive` to `false` instead of removing the control. The band glides off and the text becomes solid, so the
line does not jump, and the surrounding layout does not shift.

```csharp
summary.Text = "Summary ready";
summary.IsActive = false;
```

Set the final text and `IsActive` in the same step, so the finished label and its settled state appear together.

### Sweep speed

`SweepDuration` sets the time of one pass across the text. The default is 1.8 seconds. Each pass is followed by a
short rest, about a third of the duration, before the next one starts. Use a slower sweep when the page is calm and
the label is a long-running background task, such as indexing a workspace. Keep the default for an assistant reply
or a button state, where people expect a brisk signal.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.TextShimmerSlowerSweepDemo">
    <arc:TextShimmer Text="Indexing the workspace" SweepDuration="0:0:3" />
</UserControl>
```

`SweepDuration` takes a `TimeSpan`. In code, `TimeSpan.FromSeconds(3)` gives the same value as the XAML above.

### Size and color

The text uses the font properties of `TextElement`. A larger size suits a status heading; the band scales with the
font size, so the sweep looks the same at any size.

```xml
<arc:TextShimmer Text="Generating summary" FontSize="22" FontWeight="SemiBold" />
```

`Foreground` sets the color of the band and of the solid text. `BaseForeground` sets the resting color explicitly.
Set it when the default mix does not hold the contrast you need, for example on a dark header where the base must
stay readable while the band passes over it.

```xml
<arc:TextShimmer Text="Syncing orders"
                 Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Accent}"
                 BaseForeground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
```

### Driving it from code

The control is display-only, so the view model owns the words and the busy flag, and the view binds them. The sweep
and the text change are handled by the control.

```csharp
public partial class ImportViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    private readonly IOrderImportService _imports;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private string _statusText = "Importing 2,340 orders";

    [ObservableProperty]
    private bool _isBusy = true;

    public ImportViewModel(IOrderImportService imports)
    {
        _imports = imports;
    }

    [RelayCommand]
    private async Task RunImportAsync()
    {
        IsBusy = true;
        StatusText = "Importing 2,340 orders";

        var result = await _imports.RunAsync();

        StatusText = result.IsSuccess ? "Import complete" : "Import needs attention";
        IsBusy = false;
    }
}
```

```xml
<arc:TextShimmer Text="{Binding StatusText}"
                 IsActive="{Binding IsBusy}"
                 FontSize="16" />
```

When the import fails, show the reason with `Alert` next to the line rather than only changing the wording of the
shimmer. The shimmer ends with `IsBusy` set to `false`, so it never claims that work is still running.

### Using motion with restraint

Motion helps when it marks the one thing that is still alive on a page. It distracts when several lines sweep at
once, when the sweep runs on a finished label, or when the words are only a decoration around the motion.

- **Where it helps**: a status row in a header or a panel where no other element moves, so the band tells people
  the job is running without a spinner.
- **Where it distracts**: a list of busy rows that all sweep, or a sweep faster than the default on a label that
  people read while they wait.
- **Reduced motion**: the band stops and the label swaps with a plain fade. The state must still read from the
  words alone, so write "Reading 14 files", not only a shimmer, and stop the sweep when the work ends.

To lower the motion for a part of the interface, set `arc:ArcMotion.Level="Reduced"` on the container. The level is
inherited, so every shimmer below it stops sweeping.

### Example: nightly import panel

A panel in an admin console that shows a nightly order import. The busy line says what the job is doing and how
many orders it covers, so people can judge the wait from the words. Below it, the finished line of an earlier run
is the same control with `IsActive` set to `false`, so the two states read as one component. The action row uses
the secondary button for the log and the primary button for the next step.

![A nightly import panel with a busy status line and a finished one](https://docs.tkcode.si/shots/Docs/TextEffects/TextShimmer/images/ImportPanel.webp)

```xml
<Border Width="640"
        Padding="24"
        CornerRadius="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource RadiusPanel}"
        Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Surface}"
        BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource BorderSubtle}"
        BorderThickness="1">
    <StackPanel Spacing="16">
        <StackPanel Spacing="4">
            <TextBlock Text="Nightly order import"
                       FontSize="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TypeLG}"
                       FontWeight="SemiBold"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
            <TextBlock Text="Northwind Commerce, store 014"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
        </StackPanel>
        <arc:TextShimmer Text="Importing 2,340 orders" FontSize="16" />
        <StackPanel Spacing="8">
            <TextBlock Text="Last run"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
            <arc:TextShimmer Text="Import complete on 20 October 2026" FontSize="16"
                             IsActive="False" />
        </StackPanel>
        <StackPanel Orientation="Horizontal" Spacing="8" HorizontalAlignment="Right">
            <arc:Button Content="View log" Variant="Secondary" />
            <arc:Button Content="Open orders" />
        </StackPanel>
    </StackPanel>
</Border>
```

### Content guidelines

The words carry the meaning, so write them as the status of the work, not as a mood.

- **Busy label**: a present participle with its object or a count: "Reading 14 files", "Generating summary". Use
  digits for counts so the number reads at a glance: "2,340 orders", not "two thousand orders".
- **Finished label**: the result as a short noun phrase or past participle: "Summary ready", "Import complete".
- **Length**: keep the line under about 40 characters, so it fits a status bar or a header on a narrow window.
- **No vague waiting copy**: name the work, not the wait. "Please wait" tells people nothing about what is happening.

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| Loading... | Reading 14 files |
| Please wait | Syncing orders |
| Processing | Importing 2,340 orders |
| Done! | Summary ready |
| Thinking about your request | Thinking |

### Best practices

**Do**

- Put the meaning in the words. The band only shows that work is live; reduced motion and assistive technology remove
  it, and the label must still say what the work is.
- Set `IsActive` to `false` when the work ends, rather than removing the control. The text settles in place, so the
  layout around it does not shift.
- Keep one busy label per region and each label on one line. The control is built for a short status line, and a
  second line of sweep competes with the first.
- Show the failure with `Alert` and stop the sweep when the job fails. A sweep means the work is still running.

**Avoid**

- Using the shimmer as a placeholder for content that has not loaded. Use `Skeleton`, which shows the shape of the
  content, so people see what will appear.
- Leaving `IsActive` on after the work is done, or on a label that has nothing to wait for. The sweep then
  contradicts the page.
- Changing the text on a timer faster than people can read it. Each change rises in with a blur, and a stream of
  them reads as noise instead of progress.
- Setting a `BaseForeground` that is close to the background. The resting base must stay readable while the band is
  elsewhere on the line.
- Using the shimmer on a label that is also the only status message for an error. Use `Alert` for errors so the
  message does not depend on motion.

### Common questions

**Why does the sweep stop when the label scrolls out of view or its window is hidden?** The control runs its loop
only while it is visible, attached to the tree, within 64 px of the viewport and at the Full motion level. It does
not spend frames on a label that nobody can see, and it resumes from the position where it stopped.

**How do I stop the sweep without hiding the text?** Set `IsActive` to `false`. The text becomes solid and stays
visible, which is what a finished state should look like. To stop it for a whole region because the person asked for
less motion, set `arc:ArcMotion.Level="Reduced"` on the container; the sweep stops and the label swaps with a fade.

**Does the text wrap when the column is narrow?** No. The control is one line. Shorten the label or give the
control more room; do not rely on wrapping.

**How do I make the sweep slower or change its colors?** Set `SweepDuration` for the speed, `Foreground` for the
band and solid color, and `BaseForeground` for the resting color. `FontSize` and `FontWeight` change the text
itself.

**Does the control announce its changes to a screen reader?** No. Its text is the accessible name and its item status
reads "Busy" while it sweeps. To announce the finished state, put a live region on the parent, or announce the
message in the same step that sets `IsActive` to `false`.

## API reference

### TextShimmer

A calm light sweeping across a short status line (Arc TextShimmer), such as "Thinking" or "Generating summary": a bell-shaped band of the text color crosses a muted base, then pauses briefly before the next pass (P21). The sweep runs only while `IsActive`, within 64px of the viewport and visible, and resumes where it stopped. Turning `IsActive` off lets a band in flight glide off while the text settles to solid. A new label rises in place from a soft blur while the line springs to its width (P2, P5). Drawn as one control: the band is the text drawn again through a sliding opacity mask, so a frame allocates nothing.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Text` | `string?` | `null` | The status text; keep it to one short line. A new value rises in place. |
| `IsActive` | `bool` | `true` | Sweeps while work is ongoing (Arc `active`, true). |
| `SweepDuration` | `TimeSpan` | `00:00:01.8000000` | One pass across the text (Arc `duration`, 1.8s). |
| `BaseForeground` | `IBrush?` | `null` | Resting base color; when unset it is 12% of the text color mixed into muted text. |
| `FontFamily` | `FontFamily` | `$Default` | Font family of the text; inherited from TextElement unless set. |
| `FontSize` | `double` | `12` | Font size in device-independent pixels; inherited from TextElement unless set. |
| `FontWeight` | `FontWeight` | `Normal` | Font weight of the text; inherited from TextElement unless set. |
| `Foreground` | `IBrush?` | `Black` | Text color; the resting base color is derived from it unless BaseForeground is set. |

Derives from `Control`: every member of `Control` works as well.

## Accessibility

- The `Text` value is the control's accessible name, and the control reports itself as a text element.
- While `IsActive` is `true`, the item status is "Busy". It is cleared when `IsActive` is `false`. Not every
  assistive technology exposes item status, so the words must carry the meaning on their own.
- The sweep is decorative. Nothing is read letter by letter, and the band is not a separate element.
- The control does not announce changes. Put the finished state in a live region on a parent element, as described
  in the common questions above.
- The control does not switch to system colors for high contrast. Choose `Foreground` and `BaseForeground` from the
  theme so that both the band and the resting base keep the contrast the page needs.
- The control takes no focus and has no keyboard interaction, so there is no keyboard table. Nothing in it can be
  reached with `Tab`.

## Motion

- The band sweeps across the text once per `SweepDuration`, rests briefly, then sweeps again. The first pass waits a
  moment after the control starts.
- The sweep runs only while the control is active, visible, within 64 px of the viewport and at the Full motion
  level. It resumes where it stopped.
- A new label rises in from below with a soft blur while the line springs to its new width. The outgoing label
  leaves upward with a shorter blur.
- Setting `IsActive` to `false` glides a band in flight off the text, then the text becomes solid. Setting it back to
  `true` returns the line to its resting base.
- Reduced motion stops the sweep and swaps labels with an instant fade. Off swaps labels at once and settles the
  state without animation.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sweep band | Crosses the text once per `SweepDuration`, then rests | No band; the text shows its resting base | No band; the text shows its resting base |
| A new `Text` value | Rises in with a soft blur over 240 ms; the old text leaves over 160 ms | Instant fade over 120 ms | Immediate |
| Width after a text change | Springs to the new width while the labels change | Jumps to the new width | Immediate |
| `IsActive` to `true` | The text returns to the resting base over 240 ms | Instant fade over 120 ms | Immediate |
| `IsActive` to `false` | The band glides off over up to 420 ms, then the text is solid over 360 ms | Solid text over 120 ms | Immediate |

## Related

- `Skeleton` for placeholder content while a page loads, and `Progress` for work with a measurable amount done.
- `TextMorph` for a short label that changes letter by letter, and `Alert` for a message that needs action.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `Skeleton` | Content is loading and the page needs placeholder shapes that match the final layout |
| `Progress` | The amount of work done is known and can be shown as a bar or a value |
| `Stepper` | The job has fixed, named steps and people need to see where they are in them |
| `TextMorph` | A short label changes state and the letters should morph into the next label |
| `Alert` | A failure, an expired session or a result needs the person's attention and a next step |
| `TextReveal` | A heading or a short paragraph enters the page for the first time |

# Markdown

> Render Markdown documents and streamed replies in Arc's style, with fenced code highlighted in Arc's syntax palette.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/markdown

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.MarkdownDocumentDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12">
        <arc:Markdown x:Name="Document" LinkClicked="OnLinkClicked" />
        <TextBlock x:Name="Status"
                   Text="Links open in the browser; LinkClicked reports them first."
                   FontSize="14"
                   TextWrapping="Wrap"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using StreamMark.Avalonia.Rendering;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class MarkdownDocumentDemo : UserControl
{
    public MarkdownDocumentDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Document.Text = """
            # Release notes

            Arc **0.4** brings a `Markdown` control rendered by *StreamMark*. Code is highlighted with TextMate grammars and
            painted in Arc's own syntax palette, so a fenced block reads like a [CodeBlock](https://uiarc.dev/components/code-block).

            ## What changed

            - Headings, lists, tables, quotes and links follow the ArcDesign tokens.
            - Fenced code highlights **C#**, **TypeScript**, **JSON**, **XAML**, shell and many more.
              - Unknown languages stay plain text.
            - Light, dark and the accent switch live.

            1. Add the package.
            2. Call `UseArcControls()` in `UseArc(...)`.
            3. Drop `<arc:Markdown Text="..." />` into a view.

            - [x] Static documents
            - [x] Streamed replies
            - [ ] Math and diagrams (add StreamMark's RaTeX and Mermaid plugins)

            > Color supports, but never replaces, the source text.
            > — Arc's code block notes

            | Feature | Status | Notes |
            |:--------|:------:|------:|
            | Text | Ready | `Text` |
            | Streaming | Ready | `Append` / `Complete` |
            | Links | Ready | `LinkClicked` |

            ## Code

            ```cs
            public sealed class CartView : UserControl
            {
                // Totals update when an item changes.
                public decimal Total { get; private set; }

                public void Add(decimal price, int quantity = 1) => Total += price * quantity;
            }
            ```

            ```ts
            export async function loadUser(id: number): Promise<User | null> {
              const response = await fetch(`/api/users/${id}`);
              return response.ok ? ((await response.json()) as User) : null;
            }
            ```

            ```json
            { "name": "arc-demo", "version": "1.4.0", "private": true, "tags": ["ui", "motion"] }
            ```

            ```xml
            <!-- A streamed reply in a chat bubble -->
            <arc:Markdown FontSize="14" Text="{Binding Reply}" />
            ```

            ```bash
            dotnet add package TKCode.Arc --prerelease
            dotnet run --project src/App
            ```
            """;
    }

    private void OnLinkClicked(object? sender, LinkClickedEventArgs e) => Status.Text = $"LinkClicked: {e.Url}";
}
```

## When to use

`Markdown` renders text that an author wrote in Markdown: headings, lists, tables, quotes, links and fenced code. It
sits where a product shows formatted prose that it does not lay out by hand, such as release notes, help articles or a
model's answer. The control takes the Markdown source, parses it and draws it in Arc's type, color and spacing, so the
text in a panel, a chat bubble or a document view looks like the rest of the application.

- **Release notes and in-app help**: a "What's new" panel in Acme Analytics that shows the notes the content team writes
  as Markdown files. Headings, lists and links look the same in every release without a hand-built layout for each one.
- **Assistant replies in a support chat**: an answer that arrives token by token. Call `Append` for each chunk and
  `Complete` at the end, and the text fades in at the end of the reply while the earlier paragraphs stay put.
- **Developer documentation with code samples**: API guides where fenced blocks in C#, TypeScript, JSON or shell read
  with syntax colors from Arc's palette. Long blocks fold to 12 lines, so one sample does not push the rest of the page
  away.
- **Rich text from a source you do not control**: a ticket body, a CMS field or an imported note. Headings, tables and
  links stay consistent with the product, and links open in the system browser unless the app takes them over.
- **Message bubbles with a smaller type size**: a 14 px reply in a support thread, where the line height and the block
  spacing follow the font size so the bubble stays compact.

## When not to use

- **A single code sample with a copy button**: use `CodeBlock`, which is one block with its own header and actions.
  `Markdown` is for a document that mixes prose, lists and code.
- **A long document that needs its own scrolling**: wrap the control in a `ScrollViewer`. The document grows with its
  content and has no scrollbar of its own. For long conversations, use the transcript view of the StreamMark library.
- **Editing Markdown source in place**: use `Textarea`, which holds the raw text, wraps it and lets the person edit it.
  `Markdown` shows the rendered result only.
- **Structured records such as a table of invoices**: use `Table` from the Tables group, which sorts and
  keeps the columns aligned as the rows change. A Markdown table is read-only and has no sorting.
- **Math, diagrams or other embedded formats**: `Markdown` renders text, code and tables. Add StreamMark's math or
  diagram plugins to your own `MarkdownServices` when you need them, instead of pasting images into the text.

## Usage

Static text is set with `Text`. The document grows with its content and has no internal scrolling.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:Markdown Text="## Release notes&#10;&#10;Arc **0.4** adds `Markdown`." />
</UserControl>
```

`Markdown` derives from Avalonia's `TemplatedControl`. Its template is a frame around a StreamMark `MarkdownView`,
which does the parsing and the layout. Arc supplies the colors, fonts and radii through the `Md.*` resources of that
view, so the document follows the theme scope, light and dark mode and the accent. Because the document is a view and
not a text block, it selects, copies and wraps like any document, and it grows with its content.

### Anatomy

1. **Frame**: a transparent `Border`. The theme sets no border and no padding on it, and the document takes the full
   width of its container (`HorizontalAlignment` is `Stretch`).
2. **Body text**: 16 px in the body font with a line height of 26 px (the font size times 1.65). Lines wrap to the width
   the container gives them.
3. **Blocks**: paragraphs, lists, quotes, code and tables are separated by 12 px (`BlockSpacing`).
4. **Headings and list markers**: headings take the foreground color, and the document view sizes them. List markers
   take the muted text color, so the item text stays the strongest element.
5. **Links**: the strong accent color, underlined. They open in the system browser by default.
6. **Inline code**: the monospace font on the muted surface color.
7. **Fenced code**: the surface color with a border in the border color, the monospace font and the Arc syntax
   palette. A block longer than 12 lines folds, with a control to show every line. Code blocks offer copy, not download.
8. **Quotes**: a bar in the strong border color beside the quoted text.
9. **Tables**: a border in the border color, a header row on the muted surface color, and the cell text in the body
   font.
10. **Marks and selection**: marked text sits on the warning subtle color, and selected text on the accent subtle color.

### Bound document

Bind `Text` to a view model property. Setting it replaces any reply that is still shown, and a `null` or empty string
shows an empty document.

```xml
<arc:Markdown Text="{Binding ReleaseNotes}" FontSize="14" BlockSpacing="10" />
```

`FontSize`, `FontFamily`, `LineHeight` and `BlockSpacing` are the only typography knobs. Leave `LineHeight` at its
default (NaN), so the line height follows the font size. Set it only when a design needs an exact value.

### Binding to a view model

The view model owns the Markdown source and, for a reply, the stream. With CommunityToolkit.Mvvm, the text is an
`ObservableProperty` and the stream is another one.

```csharp
public sealed partial class ReleaseNotesViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    [ObservableProperty]
    private string? _releaseNotes;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private MarkdownStream? _reply;
}
```

```xml
<arc:Markdown Text="{Binding ReleaseNotes}" />
<arc:Markdown Stream="{Binding Reply}" />
```

Keep both bindings one-way. The control itself sets `Text` to `null` and replaces the stream when `Append` starts a
reply, and a two-way binding would write those values back into the view model. `IsStreaming` is read-only and reports
the state of the stream on the control.

### Streamed reply

Call `Append` for each chunk as it arrives, and `Complete` when the reply ends. The text is paced and new words fade in
at the end of the document. `IsStreaming` is `true` until the paced backlog has been shown, so a status line can say
"Writing" until the reply is fully on screen rather than until the last chunk arrives.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.MarkdownStreamedReplyDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12">
        <WrapPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center" ItemSpacing="12" LineSpacing="12">
            <arc:Button x:Name="StreamButton"
                        Content="Stream reply"
                        Variant="Primary"
                        Size="Small"
                        Click="OnStreamClick" />
            <arc:Button Content="Reset"
                        Variant="Secondary"
                        Size="Small"
                        Click="OnResetClick" />
            <TextBlock x:Name="Status"
                       Text="Idle"
                       FontSize="13"
                       VerticalAlignment="Center"
                       TextWrapping="Wrap"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
        </WrapPanel>
        <arc:Markdown x:Name="Message" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;
using Avalonia.Threading;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class MarkdownStreamedReplyDemo : UserControl
{
    private const string Reply = """
        Sure — here is the short version.

        **Streaming** keeps the document stable while text arrives: finished blocks never re-render, the last block grows,
        and new words fade in.

        ```cs
        markdown.Append(chunk);   // as tokens arrive
        markdown.Complete();      // when the reply ends
        ```

        | Step | Call |
        |------|------|
        | Start | `Append("...")` |
        | Finish | `Complete()` |

        Anything else?
        """;

    private const string Prompt = "_Press **Stream reply** to simulate a model answering._";

    private DispatcherTimer? _timer;

    public MarkdownStreamedReplyDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Message.Text = Prompt;
        Message.PropertyChanged += (_, e) =>
        {
            if (e.Property == Markdown.IsStreamingProperty)
            {
                Status.Text = Message.IsStreaming ? "Streaming…" : "Complete";
                StreamButton.IsEnabled = !Message.IsStreaming;
            }
        };
    }

    private void OnStreamClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        _timer?.Stop();
        var random = new Random(7);
        var position = 0;
        _timer = new DispatcherTimer(TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(40), DispatcherPriority.Normal, (_, _) =>
        {
            if (position >= Reply.Length)
            {
                _timer?.Stop();
                Message.Complete();
                return;
            }
            var length = Math.Min(Reply.Length - position, random.Next(2, 9));
            Message.Append(Reply.Substring(position, length));
            position += length;
        });
        _timer.Start();
    }

    private void OnResetClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        _timer?.Stop();
        Message.Text = Prompt;
        Status.Text = "Idle";
    }
}
```

```csharp
markdown.Append(chunk);   // as tokens arrive, on the UI thread
markdown.Complete();      // when the reply ends
```

Three properties tune how appended text shows. `RevealFadeDuration` sets how long each new batch fades in at full motion (Arc's
standard duration when null); `RevealFadeInReducedMotion` turns the fade off at reduced motion, which suits a reply that grows
continuously; and `IsPaced` set to false shows every appended piece at once as one batch, for a host that has already paced the
text itself, such as in whole words on a fixed clock.

`Append` starts a new reply after `Complete`, and it replaces whatever is shown: `Text` reads `null` from then on. A
stream you create yourself can be set on `Stream` instead, for example one that a worker thread feeds with
`MarkdownStream.Push` and ends with `Complete`. The control applies the snapshots on the UI thread, so the worker
pushes text and never touches the controls.

### Chat size

Use a smaller `FontSize` for message bubbles. `LineHeight` defaults to the font size times 1.65, so a 14 px reply has a
23 px line height, and code follows the font size.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.MarkdownChatSizeDemo">
    <arc:Markdown x:Name="Message" FontSize="14" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class MarkdownChatSizeDemo : UserControl
{
    public MarkdownChatSizeDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Message.Text = """
            Deployed **web-42** to `staging`. Logs: [build #1042](https://uiarc.dev).

            kubectl rollout status deploy/web

### Links

Absolute `http`, `https` and `mailto` links open with the system launcher. Handle `LinkClicked` to take over, and mark
the event handled to stop the default. Set `OpensLinks="False"` to turn the default off. Links that the link policy
marks as needing confirmation are not opened by the default handler, so confirm them in your own handler. Anchors that
point inside the document scroll to their target by themselves and do not raise `LinkClicked`.

```csharp
markdown.LinkClicked += (_, e) =>
{
    e.Handled = true;
    OpenInsideApp(e.Url);
};
```

### Host integration

A host that builds its own chrome around the document uses the public surface instead of walking the template. The
outline lists every heading with the point it scrolls to; `Find` highlights the matches and returns their count;
`FindNext` / `FindPrevious` move the current match; the selection methods copy what the reader selected.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.MarkdownOutlineDemo">
    <Grid ColumnDefinitions="180,*" ColumnSpacing="20">
        <StackPanel Grid.Column="0" Spacing="8">
            <TextBlock Text="Outline"
                       FontSize="13"
                       FontWeight="SemiBold"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
            <ListBox x:Name="Outline"
                     FontSize="13"
                     Background="Transparent"
                     SelectionChanged="OnOutlineSelectionChanged" />
        </StackPanel>
        <StackPanel Grid.Column="1" Spacing="12">
            <WrapPanel ItemSpacing="8" LineSpacing="8">
                <arc:Input x:Name="FindBox"
                           Placeholder="Find in document"
                           Width="180"
                           Size="Small"
                           TextChanged="OnFindTextChanged" />
                <arc:Button Content="Previous" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Click="OnPreviousClick" />
                <arc:Button Content="Next" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Click="OnNextClick" />
                <TextBlock x:Name="Status"
                           Text="No search"
                           FontSize="13"
                           VerticalAlignment="Center"
                           Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
            </WrapPanel>
            <ScrollViewer Height="280">
                <arc:Markdown x:Name="Article" DocumentReady="OnDocumentReady" />
            </ScrollViewer>
        </StackPanel>
    </Grid>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;
using StreamMark.Avalonia.Selection;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

/// <summary>
/// An outline sidebar and a find bar built from the public host integration API of <see cref="Markdown"/>:
/// <c>GetOutline</c>, <c>ScrollToPoint</c>, <c>Find</c>, <c>FindNext</c> and <c>FindPrevious</c>.
/// </summary>
public partial class MarkdownOutlineDemo : UserControl
{
    private const string Body = """
        # A field guide to Arc

        Arc is a component library. This page shows how a host can build its own navigation and search around the
        rendered document without reaching into the template.

        ## Navigation

        An outline lists every heading in reading order. Each item carries the level, the text and the point the
        document scrolls to, so a click is one `ScrollToPoint` call.

        ### Anchors

        Links that point inside the document, such as [the search section](#search), scroll to their heading by
        themselves. `ScrollToAnchor` does the same for your own links and returns `false` when the heading is missing.

        ## Search

        `Find` returns the number of matches and highlights all of them. `FindNext` and `FindPrevious` move the current
        match and scroll to it, wrapping around at the ends.

        ## Selection

        `SelectAll`, `GetSelectedText`, `GetSelectedMarkdown` and `CopySelectionAsync` work on the same selection the
        reader makes with the mouse or the keyboard.

        ## Timing

        Parsing happens on a worker thread. Wait for `DocumentReady` before you read the outline for the first time,
        or accept that it is empty until the first snapshot lands.
        """;

    private IReadOnlyList<OutlineItem> _outline = Array.Empty<OutlineItem>();

    public MarkdownOutlineDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Article.Text = Body;
    }

    private void OnDocumentReady(object? sender, EventArgs e)
    {
        _outline = Article.GetOutline();
        Outline.ItemsSource = _outline.Select(o => $"{new string(' ', (o.Level - 1) * 2)}{o.Text}").ToList();
        Status.Text = $"{_outline.Count} headings";
    }

    private void OnOutlineSelectionChanged(object? sender, SelectionChangedEventArgs e)
    {
        if (Outline.SelectedIndex >= 0 && Outline.SelectedIndex < _outline.Count)
        {
            Article.ScrollToPoint(_outline[Outline.SelectedIndex].Target);
        }
    }

    private void OnFindTextChanged(object? sender, TextChangedEventArgs e) => Update(FindBox.Text);

    private void OnNextClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        Article.FindNext();
        ShowCurrent();
    }

    private void OnPreviousClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        Article.FindPrevious();
        ShowCurrent();
    }

    private void Update(string? query)
    {
        var count = Article.Find(query);
        if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(query))
        {
            Status.Text = "No search";
            return;
        }
        Status.Text = count == 0 ? "No matches" : $"{Article.CurrentMatchIndex + 1} of {count}";
    }

    private void ShowCurrent()
    {
        if (Article.MatchCount > 0)
        {
            Status.Text = $"{Article.CurrentMatchIndex + 1} of {Article.MatchCount}";
        }
    }
}
```

```csharp
markdown.DocumentReady += (_, _) =>
{
    foreach (var item in markdown.GetOutline())
    {
        AddOutlineRow(item.Level, item.Text, () => markdown.ScrollToPoint(item.Target));
    }
};

var count = markdown.Find(query);      // all matches highlighted
markdown.FindNext();                   // current match moves and scrolls
```

| Member | Use it for |
|---|---|
| `GetOutline()` | The headings in reading order: level, text, id and target point |
| `ScrollToPoint`, `ScrollToBlock`, `ScrollToAnchor` | Moving to an outline item, a block or a heading anchor |
| `Find`, `FindNext`, `FindPrevious`, `FindAt`, `ClearSearch` | A find bar, with `MatchCount` and `CurrentMatchIndex` for its label |
| `SelectAll`, `GetSelectedText`, `GetSelectedMarkdown`, `CopySelectionAsync` | A copy action, with `HasSelection` for its enabled state |
| `IsDocumentReady`, `DocumentReady` | Knowing when the outline, the matches and the scroll targets are final |

Parsing happens on a worker thread, so the timing is part of the contract. Before the template is applied there is no
view: the outline is empty, the scroll methods return `false`, `Find` returns 0 and the selection is empty. A new
`Text` or `Stream` makes `IsDocumentReady` `false` until its snapshot is parsed and applied, then `DocumentReady` runs
once. A find query stays set, so a document that changes under a search runs it again. Applying a new template creates
a new view: the document is handed to it, `DocumentReady` runs again and the search is run again, but a selection does
not survive. Use the `DocumentReady` event rather than a timer when the host restores a scroll position after a load.

### Code highlighting

`MarkdownHighlightPlugin` highlights fenced code with the TextMate grammars that `CodeBlock` also uses, and paints each
role in Arc's syntax palette for light or dark mode. Comments are italic. A language without a grammar stays plain text,
so an unknown tag never fails the document. The plugin is part of the default services. Pass language names to its
constructor to load those grammars in the background before the first block asks for them.

```csharp
markdown.Services = new MarkdownServices
{
    Plugins = [new MarkdownHighlightPlugin("cs", "ts")],
};
```

Leave the plugin out of `Plugins` when a view must show code without colors, and the blocks are then plain text in the
monospace font.

### Services and precedence

The StreamMark services decide how the document is parsed and how code blocks behave. The control picks them in this
order: its own `Services` property, then the services that an ancestor sets with `MarkdownServices.SetServices`, then
`Markdown.DefaultServices`. Set services on the window or the page to give every document in a view the same plugins.
Plugins can change the Markdown dialect, so a change to the services parses the static text again.

`Markdown.DefaultServices` highlights code with `MarkdownHighlightPlugin`, copies code but does not offer a download,
and folds long blocks to 12 lines.

### Example: assistant reply in a support chat

A support assistant answers an Acme Analytics customer in a chat bubble. The reply uses a short list and a link to the
export page, and it is set at 14 px to match the rest of the thread. The bubble has a muted surface and a 16 px inner
padding. The reply is static here, so the screenshot shows the settled text, the state that a streamed reply reaches
once `IsStreaming` turns `false`.

![A support assistant reply with a short list and a link inside a chat bubble](https://docs.tkcode.si/shots/Docs/Content/Markdown/images/ChatReply.webp)

```xml
<Border Width="600"
        Padding="16"
        Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource SurfaceMuted}"
        CornerRadius="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource RadiusPanel}">
    <arc:Markdown FontSize="14"
                  Text="Your March export is ready. The file holds **1,250** invoices in `invoices_2026_03.csv`.&#10;&#10;- Paid: **1,012**, pending: **105**&#10;- Overdue: **86**, failed: **47**&#10;&#10;You can open the [export page](https://uiarc.dev) to download it." />
</Border>
```

### Content guidelines

Rendered text reads as a document, so write it as a document: short headings, complete sentences and links whose text
says where they go.

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| `Here's the thing!` as a heading | `Changes in version 0.4` |
| `Click here` as a link | `Read the migration guide` |
| `Loading...` as the placeholder reply | Leave the reply empty and show a status with `IsStreaming` |
| A table with eight columns | Two or three columns, with the rest in a list under the table |
| A 60-line code sample in the middle of a chat reply | The three lines that matter and a link to the full sample |
| Bare URLs in the middle of a sentence | A link with the page name as its text |

Use sentence case for headings and keep them short enough to scan at a glance. Write code samples so that a
reader can copy them: complete statements, and the language in the fence (`cs`, `ts`, `json`, `xml`, `sh`), so the
highlighter can color them.

### Best practices

**Do**

- Set `FontSize` to match the surrounding text rather than leaving the default, so a document in a panel and a reply in
  a bubble do not show two different type sizes side by side.
- Show `IsStreaming` as a status and disable the send button while it is `true`, so a person does not send a second
  question before the first reply has finished.
- Keep one `MarkdownServices` for the application, set on the window, so every document highlights code the same way.
- Put long documents in a `ScrollViewer`, so the scrolling and the scrollbar come from one container.
- Handle `LinkClicked` when links must open inside the app or need confirmation, so the decision stays in your code.

**Avoid**

- Setting `Text` and `Stream` on one control. The value set last wins, and the other is cleared or ignored.
- Appending one character at a time. Each chunk is parsed and paced, so push chunks of a few words, as a model's token
  stream does.
- Using a fixed `LineHeight` in a multi-size layout. A fixed value does not follow the font size, so a 14 px reply and a
  16 px document drift apart.
- Relying on `Markdown` for a table people must sort or filter. A Markdown table has no sorting and no selection.
- Showing Markdown from a source you do not trust without a `LinkClicked` handler. Absolute links open in the system
  browser by default, so check the URL in your own handler first.

### Common questions

**Why does `Text` read `null` after my streamed reply?** `Append` starts a stream and sets `Text` to `null`, because the
reply replaces the static text. Set `Text` again to show static text, which also ends the stream.

**Why does my document not scroll?** `Markdown` grows with its content and has no internal scrollbar. Wrap it in a
`ScrollViewer`, which scrolls the whole document.

**How do I know when the reply is fully shown?** Read `IsStreaming`, or listen for its change in `PropertyChanged`. It
turns `false` after `Complete` once the paced backlog has been shown, which can be a moment after the last chunk.

**Why are long code blocks folded?** The default services fold a block to 12 lines and show a control to expand it,
which keeps a long sample from pushing the rest of a chat reply out of view. Set your own `CodeBlocks` options in
`MarkdownServices` to change the limit.

**Why does a link not open when I click it?** Only absolute `http`, `https` and `mailto` links open by default. A relative
link, a custom scheme or a link that needs confirmation is left for your `LinkClicked` handler to decide.

## API reference

### Markdown

An Arc-styled Markdown document rendered by StreamMark: headings, lists, tables, quotes, links, inline code and fenced code highlighted in Arc's syntax palette. Show static text with `Text`, or stream a reply with `Append` / `Complete` (or your own `Stream`). The document grows with its content (no internal scrolling); put long documents in a `ScrollViewer`.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Text` | `string?` | `null` | The Markdown source to show. Setting it ends a stream started with `Append`. |
| `Stream` | `MarkdownStream?` | `null` | A streamed reply to show instead of `Text`. `Append` creates one when none is set; you can also supply your own (for example one fed from a worker thread with `Push`). |
| `Services` | `MarkdownServices?` | `null` | StreamMark services (plugins, code block options, link policy). Null uses services set on an ancestor with `MarkdownServices.SetServices`, else `DefaultServices`. |
| `LineHeight` | `double` | `NaN` | Body line height in pixels; NaN (default) uses the font size times Arc's prose leading (1.65). |
| `BlockSpacing` | `double` | `12` | Vertical space between blocks (paragraphs, lists, code, tables). |
| `OpensLinks` | `bool` | `true` | Opens allowed absolute links (http, https, mailto) with the system launcher when no `LinkClicked` handler marks the event handled and the link policy does not ask for confirmation. |
| `RevealFadeDuration` | `TimeSpan?` | `null` | How long each batch of text appended with `Append` fades in at full motion; null uses Arc's standard duration. A host that paces the text itself usually sets 150 ms. |
| `RevealFadeInReducedMotion` | `bool` | `true` | Whether appended text still fades in at reduced motion (a short opacity fade). False shows it at once, which suits a reply that grows continuously: there is no whole to fade. |
| `IsPaced` | `bool` | `true` | Whether `Append` paces the text (true, the default: it is released in small steps that follow the arrival rate). False shows every appended piece as one batch at once: the host has already paced it, for example in whole words on a fixed clock. |
| `IsStreaming` | `bool` | – | *Read-only.* Whether a stream is attached and has not completed yet. |
| `IsDocumentReady` | `bool` | – | *Read-only.* True when the current document has been parsed and the result is applied to the view, so the outline, the search matches and the scroll targets are final. A static `Text` becomes ready once; a stream becomes ready when it completes. False before the template is applied and while a new source is being parsed. |
| `MatchCount` | `int` | – | *Read-only.* The number of matches of the last `Find`, 0 when nothing is searched. |
| `CurrentMatchIndex` | `int` | – | *Read-only.* The 0-based index of the current match, or -1 when the search has no match. |
| `HasSelection` | `bool` | – | *Read-only.* True when the document has a selection, so a copy action can be enabled. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `LinkClicked` | `LinkClickedEventArgs` | A link was clicked (anchors inside the document scroll by themselves and do not arrive here). |
| `DocumentReady` | `EventHandler?` | The current document is parsed and applied, so `GetOutline` and the scroll methods have their final targets. Raised again when a new `Text` or `Stream` becomes ready, and after a new template is applied. Runs on the UI thread. |
| `SearchChanged` | `EventHandler?` | The matches or the current match of `Find` changed (including when the document changes under a search and the query is run again). Runs on the UI thread. |
| `SelectionChanged` | `EventHandler?` | The selection of the document view changed; `HasSelection` and the copy results follow. |

Pseudo-classes: `:streaming`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

| Member | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Name` | `string` | The plugin's name, `arc-highlight` |
| `Highlighter` | `ISyntaxHighlighter` | The highlighter the plugin registers, shared by all documents |

The `MarkdownHighlightPlugin` constructor takes the language names to prewarm, such as `"cs"` and `"ts"`.

## Accessibility

- Text can be selected and copied. Links are underlined and use the accent color, so they are not told apart by color
  alone.
- Code blocks use the same palette as `CodeBlock`. Color supports the source text and never replaces it: every token
  keeps its characters, so the code reads the same in a screen reader or in plain copy.
- Use `IsStreaming` to show a status while a streamed reply is still open. A status line that says "Writing" until
  `IsStreaming` turns `false` tells people when the reply is complete.

### Keyboard

- `Markdown` takes no keyboard focus of its own and adds no key bindings. Selection and copy come from the document
  view.

## Motion

- New text in a streamed reply fades in over 240 ms. Pacing spreads the text out so it does not arrive in bursts.
- Reduced motion shortens the fade to 160 ms and uses only opacity. Off shows new text at once without a fade.
- Pacing applies in every motion level. It controls when text appears, not an animation.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| New text in a streamed reply | Fades in over 240 ms at the end of the document | Fades in over 160 ms, opacity only | Shown at once |
| Pacing of a streamed reply | Applied | Applied | Applied |

## Related

- `CodeBlock` for a single code sample on its own.
- `Textarea` when the user edits multi-line text.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `CodeBlock` | One code sample with its own copy action |
| `Textarea` | The person edits multi-line text, and the raw source is what matters |
| `Table` | The records must be sorted, such as a table of invoices |

---

# Token text editor

> A multi-line text editor whose tokens, such as commands and mentions, behave as single units, with triggers that open a query for your own list.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/token-text-editor

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.TokenTextEditorPreviewDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="8" MaxWidth="480" Margin="0,12">
        <!-- "/" is a command only at the start of a line; "@" starts a mention at the start or after a space. -->
        <Border BorderThickness="1" CornerRadius="12" Padding="12,8" BorderBrush="#40808080">
            <arc:TokenTextEditor x:Name="Editor" Placeholder="Type / for a command or @ for a file" MinLines="2" MaxLines="5">
                <arc:TokenTextEditor.Triggers>
                    <arc:TokenTrigger Symbol="/" Kind="command" Position="LineStart" />
                    <arc:TokenTrigger Symbol="@" Kind="mention" Position="AfterWhitespaceOrLineStart" />
                </arc:TokenTextEditor.Triggers>
            </arc:TokenTextEditor>
        </Border>
        <ListBox x:Name="Suggestions" IsVisible="False" MaxHeight="160" />
        <TextBlock x:Name="Summary" FontSize="12" Opacity="0.7" TextWrapping="Wrap" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class TokenTextEditorPreviewDemo : UserControl
{
    private static readonly (string Kind, string Id, string Label)[] Entries =
    [
        ("command", "recap", "recap"), ("command", "rewrite", "rewrite"), ("command", "outline", "outline"),
        ("mention", "export-worker", "export-worker.ts"), ("mention", "usage-oct", "usage-oct.csv"), ("mention", "style-guide", "style-guide.pdf")
    ];

    public TokenTextEditorPreviewDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();

        // The editor reports what is being typed; the list is yours. Pressing a row replaces the typed text with a token.
        Editor.TriggerChanged += (_, e) =>
        {
            var state = e.State;
            if (state is null)
            {
                Suggestions.IsVisible = false;
                return;
            }

            var matches = Entries.Where(x => x.Kind == state.Kind && x.Label.StartsWith(state.Query, StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase)).ToList();
            Suggestions.ItemsSource = matches.Select(x => x.Label).ToList();
            Suggestions.IsVisible = matches.Count > 0;
        };
        Suggestions.SelectionChanged += (_, _) =>
        {
            if (Suggestions.SelectedItem is not string label)
            {
                return;
            }

            var entry = Entries.First(x => x.Label == label);
            Editor.InsertToken(entry.Kind, entry.Id, entry.Label);
            Suggestions.SelectedItem = null;
            Suggestions.IsVisible = false;
            Editor.Focus();
        };
        Editor.TextChanged += (_, e) =>
            Summary.Text = e.Tokens.Count == 0 ? "No tokens yet." : "Tokens: " + string.Join(", ", e.Tokens.Select(t => $"{t.Kind} {t.Label}"));
    }
}
```

## When to use

The token text editor is the writing surface behind a prompt box, a comment field or a template editor: plain text in which
some pieces are more than text. A `/recap` command or an `@file` mention is one unit that you move over, delete and
select as a whole, and that your code can read back with its meaning.

- **A prompt box with commands and mentions**: "/" at the start of a line picks a command, "@" picks a file or a person.
- **A template editor with variables**: a variable such as the name of a customer, written between double braces, that must not be edited letter by letter.
- **A comment field**: mentions that notify someone, with the text kept readable.
- **Your own mention control**: `MentionInput` is built on this editor; use the editor directly when the tokens are not people and channels.

## When not to use

- **Plain multi-line text**: use `Textarea`.
- **@people and #channels with a ready-made list**: use `MentionInput`, which brings its own suggestion list and serialization.
- **Rich text** (bold, links, images): the tokens are the only formatting; the text is plain.
- **A single short value**: use `Input`, or `TagInput` for a list of values.

## Usage

`TokenTextEditor` derives from Avalonia's `TemplatedControl`. It holds a real `TextBox` with transparent text and paints the
same text behind it with the tokens tinted, so the caret, selection, input methods, undo and clipboard are the platform's own.
It draws no frame: put it in your own surface.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:TokenTextEditor Placeholder="Type / for a command or @ for a file" MinLines="2" MaxLines="5">
        <arc:TokenTextEditor.Triggers>
            <arc:TokenTrigger Symbol="/" Kind="command" Position="LineStart" />
            <arc:TokenTrigger Symbol="@" Kind="mention" Position="AfterWhitespaceOrLineStart" />
        </arc:TokenTextEditor.Triggers>
    </arc:TokenTextEditor>
</UserControl>
```

### Triggers

A `TokenTrigger` is a symbol that opens a query: `Symbol`, the `Kind` of token it makes and where it may start
(`Position`): `Anywhere`, `AfterWhitespaceOrLineStart` (the start of the text, a line, or after a space) or `LineStart`
(only as the first character of a line). A query ends at a space unless `AllowSpacesInQuery` or `MaxQuerySpaces` allows
some, and another trigger's symbol ends it too. `AllowAfterOpeningBracket` lets a mention start right after a "(".

The editor shows no list. It raises `TriggerChanged` with the state of the query (the trigger, the text typed after it, and
the rectangles of the symbol and the caret to place your list); you filter your items and answer with `InsertToken(kind, id, label)`.
That replaces the typed query with the token and a space and leaves the caret after it. `CancelTrigger()` tells the editor your
list was dismissed.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.TokenTextEditorPreviewDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="8" MaxWidth="480" Margin="0,12">
        <!-- "/" is a command only at the start of a line; "@" starts a mention at the start or after a space. -->
        <Border BorderThickness="1" CornerRadius="12" Padding="12,8" BorderBrush="#40808080">
            <arc:TokenTextEditor x:Name="Editor" Placeholder="Type / for a command or @ for a file" MinLines="2" MaxLines="5">
                <arc:TokenTextEditor.Triggers>
                    <arc:TokenTrigger Symbol="/" Kind="command" Position="LineStart" />
                    <arc:TokenTrigger Symbol="@" Kind="mention" Position="AfterWhitespaceOrLineStart" />
                </arc:TokenTextEditor.Triggers>
            </arc:TokenTextEditor>
        </Border>
        <ListBox x:Name="Suggestions" IsVisible="False" MaxHeight="160" />
        <TextBlock x:Name="Summary" FontSize="12" Opacity="0.7" TextWrapping="Wrap" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class TokenTextEditorPreviewDemo : UserControl
{
    private static readonly (string Kind, string Id, string Label)[] Entries =
    [
        ("command", "recap", "recap"), ("command", "rewrite", "rewrite"), ("command", "outline", "outline"),
        ("mention", "export-worker", "export-worker.ts"), ("mention", "usage-oct", "usage-oct.csv"), ("mention", "style-guide", "style-guide.pdf")
    ];

    public TokenTextEditorPreviewDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();

        // The editor reports what is being typed; the list is yours. Pressing a row replaces the typed text with a token.
        Editor.TriggerChanged += (_, e) =>
        {
            var state = e.State;
            if (state is null)
            {
                Suggestions.IsVisible = false;
                return;
            }

            var matches = Entries.Where(x => x.Kind == state.Kind && x.Label.StartsWith(state.Query, StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase)).ToList();
            Suggestions.ItemsSource = matches.Select(x => x.Label).ToList();
            Suggestions.IsVisible = matches.Count > 0;
        };
        Suggestions.SelectionChanged += (_, _) =>
        {
            if (Suggestions.SelectedItem is not string label)
            {
                return;
            }

            var entry = Entries.First(x => x.Label == label);
            Editor.InsertToken(entry.Kind, entry.Id, entry.Label);
            Suggestions.SelectedItem = null;
            Suggestions.IsVisible = false;
            Editor.Focus();
        };
        Editor.TextChanged += (_, e) =>
            Summary.Text = e.Tokens.Count == 0 ? "No tokens yet." : "Tokens: " + string.Join(", ", e.Tokens.Select(t => $"{t.Kind} {t.Label}"));
    }
}
```

### Tokens

`Tokens` lists the `TokenSpan`s of the current text: the `Kind`, `Id` and `Label` you gave and the `Start` and `End` offsets. They
move when the text before them changes and turn into plain text when someone edits inside one. Set a whole value
with `SetTextWithTokens(text, tokens)`, add one at the caret with `InsertTokenAtCaret`, and read changes in
`TextChanged`.

Arrow keys hop over a token, Backspace right after it and Delete right before it remove all of it, a click inside lands
on the nearest edge, and Shift with the arrows selects letter by letter (set `ExpandSelectionToTokens` to select whole tokens).
Undo and redo bring a removed token back with the text.

### Styling tokens

Every kind can have its own colors: add a `TokenStyle` with the `Kind`, a `Fill` and a `Foreground` to `TokenStyles`. Without one the
editor's `TokenFill` and `TokenForeground` apply. `TokenCornerRadius`, `TokenPadding` and `TokenOutset` shape the box; a token
that wraps over a line break is sliced by default (`TokenDecorationBreak`).

### Height and submitting

The height follows the text from `MinLines` to `MaxLines` lines and then the text scrolls. Enter raises `SubmitRequested` with the
text and tokens; Shift+Enter adds a line, and nothing is submitted while an input method is composing. Set `SubmitOnEnter` to false
to make Enter add a line. Mark the event handled to keep the text; clear it yourself when you want to start over.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.TokenTextEditorGrowthDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="8" MaxWidth="480" Margin="0,12">
        <!-- One line to start, up to four lines, then it scrolls. Enter submits; Shift+Enter adds a line. -->
        <Border BorderThickness="1" CornerRadius="12" Padding="12,8" BorderBrush="#40808080">
            <arc:TokenTextEditor x:Name="Editor" Placeholder="Write a few lines, then press Enter" MinLines="1" MaxLines="4" />
        </Border>
        <TextBlock x:Name="Result" FontSize="12" Opacity="0.7" TextWrapping="Wrap" Text="Nothing submitted yet." />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class TokenTextEditorGrowthDemo : UserControl
{
    public TokenTextEditorGrowthDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Editor.SubmitRequested += (_, e) =>
        {
            Result.Text = $"Submitted {e.Text.Length} characters.";
            Editor.Clear();
            e.Handled = true;
        };
    }
}
```

### Reading the state

`TriggerState` is the current query (or null), `CaretIndex` the caret position and `IsComposing` whether an input method is
composing. `InsertText`, `Select`, `Clear`, `Undo` and `Redo` do what they say.

## API reference

### TokenTextEditor

A multi-line text editor whose tokens (commands, mentions, variables) act as single units: arrow keys hop over a token, one Backspace or Delete next to it removes all of it, and a click inside lands on its nearest edge. Typing a trigger symbol (`Triggers`, such as `/` or `@`) opens a query that the owner turns into a list (`TriggerChanged`) and answers with `InsertToken`. The value is plain `Text` plus `Tokens` with offsets.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Text` | `string` | `""` | Defines the `Text` property. |
| `Tokens` | `IReadOnlyList<TokenSpan>` | – | *Read-only.* Defines the `Tokens` property. |
| `Placeholder` | `string?` | `null` | Defines the `Placeholder` property. |
| `PlaceholderForeground` | `IBrush?` | `null` | Defines the `PlaceholderForeground` property. |
| `CaretBrush` | `IBrush?` | `null` | Defines the `CaretBrush` property. |
| `IsReadOnly` | `bool` | `false` | Defines the `IsReadOnly` property. |
| `MinLines` | `int` | `1` | Defines the `MinLines` property. |
| `MaxLines` | `int` | `8` | Defines the `MaxLines` property. |
| `LineHeight` | `double` | `NaN` | Defines the `LineHeight` property. |
| `SubmitOnEnter` | `bool` | `true` | Defines the `SubmitOnEnter` property. |
| `ExpandSelectionToTokens` | `bool` | `false` | Defines the `ExpandSelectionToTokens` property. |
| `TokenFill` | `IBrush?` | `null` | Defines the `TokenFill` property. |
| `TokenForeground` | `IBrush?` | `null` | Defines the `TokenForeground` property. |
| `TokenCornerRadius` | `double` | `6` | Defines the `TokenCornerRadius` property. |
| `TokenPadding` | `Thickness` | `0,0,0,0` | Defines the `TokenPadding` property. |
| `TokenOutset` | `double` | `2` | Defines the `TokenOutset` property. |
| `TokenDecorationBreak` | `TokenDecorationBreak` | `Slice` | Defines the `TokenDecorationBreak` property. |
| `HeightMotion` | `MotionSpec?` | `TweenMotion { Delay = 00:00:00, Duration = 00:00:00.1600000, Easing = Avalonia.Animation.Easings.SplineEasing, TweenDelay = 00:00:00 }` | Defines the `HeightMotion` property. |
| `SuggestionsExpanded` | `bool` | `false` | Defines the `SuggestionsExpanded` property. |
| `TriggerState` | `TokenTriggerState?` | – | *Read-only.* Defines the `TriggerState` property. |
| `TokenRenderer` | `TokenRenderer?` | `null` | Defines the `TokenRenderer` property. |
| `TokenParser` | `Func<string, IEnumerable<TokenSpan>>?` | `null` | Defines the `TokenParser` property. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `TextChanged` | `TokenTextChangedEventArgs` | Raised after the text or its tokens changed (typing, insertion, undo, programmatic). |
| `TriggerChanged` | `TokenTriggerChangedEventArgs` | Raised when the open query starts, changes, moves or ends. |
| `TokenInserted` | `TokenInsertedEventArgs` | Raised when `InsertToken` or `InsertTokenAtCaret` added a token. |
| `SubmitRequested` | `TokenTextSubmitRequestedEventArgs` | Raised when Enter (without Shift, outside an IME composition) asks to send the text. |
| `CollapseRequested` | `RoutedEventArgs` | Raised when assistive technology collapses the owner's list (the expand / collapse pattern). |

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

### TokenTrigger

A symbol that opens a query in a `TokenTextEditor` (for example `/` for commands or `@` for mentions). The editor reports the query through `TriggerChanged`; the owner shows its list and calls `InsertToken` with the choice.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Symbol` | `char` | `@` | Defines the `Symbol` property. |
| `Kind` | `string` | `""` | Defines the `Kind` property. |
| `Position` | `TokenTriggerPosition` | `AfterWhitespaceOrLineStart` | Defines the `Position` property. |
| `AllowSpacesInQuery` | `bool` | `false` | Defines the `AllowSpacesInQuery` property. |
| `MaxQuerySpaces` | `int` | `1` | Defines the `MaxQuerySpaces` property. |
| `AllowAfterOpeningBracket` | `bool` | `false` | Defines the `AllowAfterOpeningBracket` property. |
| `IsEnabled` | `bool` | `true` | Defines the `IsEnabled` property. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### TokenStyle

The colors of one token kind in a `TokenTextEditor`. Null brushes use the editor's defaults.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Kind` | `string` | `""` | Defines the `Kind` property. |
| `Fill` | `IBrush?` | `null` | Defines the `Fill` property. |
| `Foreground` | `IBrush?` | `null` | Defines the `Foreground` property. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### TokenSpan

| Property | Description |
|---|---|
| `Kind` | The kind you gave the token, such as `command` or `mention` |
| `Id` | Your identifier for what the token stands for |
| `Label` | The text after the symbol |
| `Start` / `End` | The range of the token in the text, symbol included |

### Events

| Event | Raised when | Arguments |
|---|---|---|
| `TextChanged` | The text or the tokens changed | `OldText`, `OldTokens`, `Text`, `Tokens` |
| `TriggerChanged` | A query opens, changes or closes | `PreviousState`, `State` (null when closed) |
| `TokenInserted` | `InsertToken` made a token | `Token` |
| `SubmitRequested` | Enter without Shift, with no input method composing | `Text`, `Tokens`; set `Handled` to keep the text |

## Accessibility

- It is a text box for assistive technology: it keeps the platform's caret, selection and input method behavior, and the text it
  reads is the plain text, tokens included.
- While your list is open, set `SuggestionsExpanded` so the editor reports itself as expanded; it raises `CollapseRequested`
  when assistive technology asks to close it. Announce the number of matches in your own live region.
- Tokens are not read as separate controls: give them a clear label ("recap", not an id).
- Token colors keep their contrast in light and dark themes; do not carry a meaning by color alone.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| Typing a trigger symbol | Opens a query where the trigger's position rule allows it |
| `ArrowLeft` / `ArrowRight` | Moves the caret, hopping over a token in one step |
| `Backspace` after a token / `Delete` before it | Removes the whole token |
| `Shift` + arrows | Selects letter by letter |
| `Enter` | Raises `SubmitRequested` |
| `Shift+Enter` | Adds a line |
| `Ctrl/Cmd+Z`, `Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+Z` | Undo and redo, tokens included |

## Motion

- The height follows the text from `MinLines` to `MaxLines` in a short ease (160 ms by default; set `HeightMotion` to change it).
- Tokens are painted, not animated: a token appears the moment it is inserted and its tint follows the theme.
- Reduced motion and Off apply height changes at once.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| Height grows or shrinks | Short ease | Immediate | Immediate |
| Token inserted or removed | Immediate | Immediate | Immediate |

## Related

- `MentionInput` for @people and #channels with a built-in list.
- `Textarea` for plain multi-line text.
- `TagInput` for a list of short values.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `MentionInput` | You need people and channels with suggestions out of the box |
| `Textarea` | The text has no tokens |
| `TagInput` | The value is a list of tags |
| `AiComposer` | You need a full prompt box: attachments, tools, model and send |
