# Cascader

> Pick one node of a hierarchy level by level, such as province, city and district, with a field and menu that match Select.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/cascader

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.CascaderBasicDemo">
    <StackPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center" Width="320" Spacing="8">
        <arc:Cascader x:Name="Region"
                      Label="Region"
                      Description="Pick a province, a city and a district."
                      Placeholder="Select a district" />
        <TextBlock x:Name="Result" FontSize="12" Opacity="0.7" TextWrapping="Wrap" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class CascaderBasicDemo : UserControl
{
    public CascaderBasicDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        CascaderDemoData.Configure(Region);
        Region.ItemsSource = CascaderDemoData.Regions();
        Region.SelectionChanged += (_, _) => Result.Text = $"SelectedValue: {Region.SelectedValue ?? "none"}";
        Result.Text = "SelectedValue: none";
    }
}
```

## When to use

`Cascader` picks one node of a hierarchy. Opening it shows the first level; choosing a parent opens its children in a
column to the right, and the last choice is a leaf. The field then shows the whole path. Use it when the levels are
fixed, there are two to five of them, and the person gains from seeing the siblings at each level.

- **Province, city and district** in an address form: the three levels are one answer, and the full path is what you store.
- **Product categories** in a catalog editor: a category such as "Electronics / Phones / Smartphones".
- **An organization chart position**: pick a department and a team in one field.

## When not to use

- **Deep trees or levels with thousands of nodes**: use a `TreeView` in a `Popover`, or a `Combobox` that searches.
- **A single level**: use `Select` or `Combobox`.
- **Several values at once**: a multi-select version is not part of `Cascader`.
- **Searching across levels or loading children on demand**: not in this version.

## Usage

`Cascader` derives from Avalonia's `TemplatedControl`. Give it the root nodes in `ItemsSource` and tell it how to read a
node with delegates: `ChildrenSelector` (the same shape as `TreeView`'s), `TextSelector` and `ValueSelector`. Nothing is
reflected, so it is safe for AOT and trimming.

```csharp
public sealed record Region(string Code, string Name, IReadOnlyList<Region>? Children = null);

cascader.ItemsSource = regions;
cascader.ChildrenSelector = node => ((Region)node).Children;
cascader.TextSelector = node => ((Region)node).Name;
cascader.ValueSelector = node => ((Region)node).Code;
```

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:Cascader Label="Region"
                  Description="Pick a province, a city and a district."
                  Placeholder="Select a district"
                  Width="320" />
</UserControl>
```

A node without children, or one that `IsLeafSelector` calls a leaf, is a leaf. The field, the menu surface, the gliding
highlight and the clear button are the ones of `Select` and `Combobox`.

### Choosing parents

By default only leaves can be picked: clicking a parent opens its children. Set `LeafOnly` to `False` to let any level
be picked. A click on a parent then selects it and keeps the menu open, so the person can still go deeper.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.CascaderParentSelectableDemo">
    <arc:Cascader x:Name="Category"
                  HorizontalAlignment="Center"
                  Width="320"
                  Label="Category"
                  Description="Any level can be picked: the menu stays open on a parent so you can go deeper."
                  LeafOnly="False"
                  Placeholder="Select a category" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class CascaderParentSelectableDemo : UserControl
{
    public CascaderParentSelectableDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        CascaderDemoData.Configure(Category);
        Category.ItemsSource = CascaderDemoData.Categories();
        Category.SelectedValue = "phones";
    }
}
```

### What the field shows

`ShowFullPath` (true by default) shows the whole path, joined by `PathSeparator` (" / "). Set it to `False` to show only the
selected node. `SelectedText` is the text the field shows.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.CascaderLeafNameDemo">
    <arc:Cascader x:Name="Region"
                  HorizontalAlignment="Center"
                  Width="320"
                  Label="District"
                  ShowFullPath="False"
                  Placeholder="Select a district" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class CascaderLeafNameDemo : UserControl
{
    public CascaderLeafNameDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        CascaderDemoData.Configure(Region);
        Region.ItemsSource = CascaderDemoData.Regions();
        Region.SelectedValue = "440305";
    }
}
```

### Opening on hover

`ExpandTrigger` decides how a parent opens its children. `Click` (the default) opens on a click or the keyboard; `Hover`
also opens while the pointer rests on the parent.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.CascaderHoverExpandDemo">
    <arc:Cascader x:Name="Region"
                  HorizontalAlignment="Center"
                  Width="320"
                  Label="Region"
                  ExpandTrigger="Hover"
                  Placeholder="Select a district" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class CascaderHoverExpandDemo : UserControl
{
    public CascaderHoverExpandDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        CascaderDemoData.Configure(Region);
        Region.ItemsSource = CascaderDemoData.Regions();
    }
}
```

### Binding to a view model

`SelectedItem`, `SelectedValue` and `SelectedPath` always agree, and the first two are two-way. Values are compared with
`Equals` on what `ValueSelector` returns, so two nodes with the same name are told apart by their values. **A value must be
unique across the whole tree**: a code that starts at 01 under every province is not unique. If two nodes share a value,
the first one wins, and a debug build writes a warning.

A value that the data does not contain yet is kept. While the data is loading the field shows the placeholder and
`SelectedValue` stays as written; when `ItemsSource` or the collection raises its change, the control finds the node and
fills in `SelectedItem` and `SelectedPath`. Replacing the data with a set that lacks the node drops the item and the
path but keeps the value, so a view model's value is never wiped by a reload.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.CascaderBindingDemo">
    <StackPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center" Width="360" Spacing="8">
        <arc:Cascader x:Name="Region"
                      Label="Region"
                      Description="The value is set at once; the data arrives a second later."
                      Placeholder="Select a district" />
        <TextBlock x:Name="Path" FontSize="12" Opacity="0.7" TextWrapping="Wrap" />
        <arc:Button x:Name="Reload" Content="Reload the data" HorizontalAlignment="Left" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class CascaderBindingDemo : UserControl
{
    public CascaderBindingDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        CascaderDemoData.Configure(Region);
        // The view model has written its value before there is any data: the field keeps it and
        // finds the path when the data shows up.
        Region.SelectedValue = "330106";
        Region.SelectionChanged += (_, _) => ShowPath();
        ShowPath();
        Load();
        Reload.Click += (_, _) =>
        {
            Region.ItemsSource = null;
            Load();
        };
    }

    private void ShowPath() =>
        Path.Text = $"SelectedValue: {Region.SelectedValue ?? "none"}\n"
                    + $"SelectedPath: {(Region.SelectedPath.Count == 0 ? "(empty)" : string.Join(" > ", Region.SelectedPath.Select(n => ((CascaderRegion)n).Name)))}";

    private async void Load()
    {
        await Task.Delay(1000);
        Region.ItemsSource = CascaderDemoData.Regions();
    }
}
```

Children are watched when the root collection raises `CollectionChanged`; changes in the collections below it show when the
menu is next opened.

### Disabled and read-only

`DisabledSelector` marks nodes that are shown but cannot be picked or opened. `IsReadOnly` lets the field be focused and
opened to look, but not changed or cleared. `IsEnabled="False"` disables the field as a whole.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.CascaderDisabledDemo">
    <WrapPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center" ItemSpacing="12" LineSpacing="12">
        <arc:Cascader x:Name="Partial" Label="Some nodes disabled" Width="260" Placeholder="Select a district" />
        <arc:Cascader x:Name="Off" Label="Disabled" Width="260" IsEnabled="False" />
        <arc:Cascader x:Name="ReadOnly" Label="Read only" Width="260" IsReadOnly="True" />
    </WrapPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class CascaderDisabledDemo : UserControl
{
    public CascaderDisabledDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        foreach (var cascader in new[] { Partial, Off, ReadOnly })
        {
            CascaderDemoData.Configure(cascader);
            cascader.ItemsSource = CascaderDemoData.Regions();
        }
        Off.SelectedValue = "3302";
        ReadOnly.SelectedValue = "3101";
    }
}
```

### Clearing

While a value is set, `IsClearable` (true by default) shows a clear button; clicking it clears the value without
opening the menu. `Clear()` does the same from code, and Delete or Backspace on the focused field too.

## API reference

### Cascader

Arc cascader: a select field that picks one node of a hierarchy, level by level (province, city, district). Opening the menu shows the first level; choosing a parent opens its children in a column to the right, and the menu grows with a spring. Look and motion follow `Select`: the same trigger, menu surface, gliding highlight and clear button. Nodes are any objects: `ChildrenSelector` gives the children, `TextSelector` the label and `ValueSelector` the value, which must be unique across the whole tree. Everything goes through delegates, so nothing is reflected. `SelectedItem`, `SelectedValue` and `SelectedPath` always agree; a value written before the data arrives is kept and resolved when it does. Keyboard: Enter, Space and the arrows open; Up and Down move in the column, Right opens the highlighted parent, Left goes back a column; Enter picks a leaf (or opens a parent); Escape closes without a change; typing jumps to the next matching node; Delete clears.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Label` | `string?` | `null` | Visible label above the trigger; also the accessible name. |
| `Description` | `string?` | `null` | Muted hint under the trigger; also the accessible help text. |
| `Placeholder` | `string?` | `"Select an option"` | Muted text shown while nothing is selected. |
| `ItemsSource` | `IEnumerable?` | `null` | The root nodes (first column). |
| `ChildrenSelector` | `Func<object, IEnumerable?>?` | `null` | Children of a node; same shape as the one of `TreeView`. Null or empty means a leaf. |
| `IsLeafSelector` | `Func<object, bool>?` | `null` | Decides whether a node is a leaf; when null, a node without children is one. |
| `TextSelector` | `Func<object, string?>?` | `null` | Label of a node; when null, `ToString()`. |
| `ValueSelector` | `Func<object, object?>?` | `null` | Value of a node; it must be unique across the tree. When null, the node itself is the value. |
| `DisabledSelector` | `Func<object, bool>?` | `null` | Returns true for nodes that are shown but cannot be picked or opened. |
| `SelectedItem` | `object?` | `null` | The selected node (two-way), or null. |
| `SelectedValue` | `object?` | `null` | Value of the selected node (two-way). A value that the data does not contain (yet) is kept: the field shows the placeholder until the data arrives, then resolves it. |
| `SelectedPath` | `IReadOnlyList<object>` | – | *Read-only.* The nodes from the root to the selected node; empty when nothing is selected. |
| `SelectedText` | `string?` | – | *Read-only.* The text of the field: the full path or the selected node alone, see `ShowFullPath`. |
| `LeafOnly` | `bool` | `true` | When true (the default) only leaves can be picked; parents just open their children. |
| `ExpandTrigger` | `CascaderExpandTrigger` | `Click` | Whether a parent opens on click only, or also while the pointer rests on it. |
| `ShowFullPath` | `bool` | `true` | Show the whole path in the field (true), or only the selected node (false). |
| `PathSeparator` | `string` | `" / "` | Text between the nodes of the full path. |
| `IsClearable` | `bool` | `true` | Whether a clear button shows while a value is selected. |
| `IsReadOnly` | `bool` | `false` | The menu opens for looking, but the value cannot be changed or cleared. |
| `IsOpen` | `bool` | `false` | Whether the menu is open (two-way). |
| `MaxDropDownHeight` | `double` | `320` | Tallest a column gets before it scrolls. |
| `ColumnWidth` | `double` | `NaN` | Width of every column; NaN sizes each column to its labels (160 to 280). |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `SelectionChanged` | `CascaderSelectionChangedEventArgs` | Raised when the selected node changes: by the user, by a binding or by clearing. |

Pseudo-classes: `:open`, `:placeholder`, `:pressed`, `:readonly`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

### CascaderSelectionChangedEventArgs

Data of `SelectionChanged`.

Derives from `EventArgs`: every member of `EventArgs` works as well.

### CascaderExpandTrigger

How a parent node of a `Cascader` opens its child column.

Derives from `Enum`: every member of `Enum` works as well.

## Accessibility

- The field is exposed as a combo box that expands and collapses, and its value is `SelectedText`. `Label` is the accessible name and `Description` the help text.
- Moving the highlight announces the node, its level and the number of nodes in the column.
- Closing the menu returns focus to the field.

### Keyboard

| Key | When | Action |
|---|---|---|
| Enter, Space, Down, Up | Menu closed | Open the menu on the selected path |
| Delete, Backspace | Menu closed, value set | Clear the value |
| Up, Down | Menu open | Move in the column, skipping disabled nodes |
| Home, End, Page Up, Page Down | Menu open | Jump in the column |
| Right | Menu open | Open the highlighted parent and move into its first child |
| Left | Menu open | Back to the previous column, with its parent highlighted |
| Enter, Space | Menu open | Pick a leaf; open a parent (or pick it when `LeafOnly` is false) |
| Escape | Menu open | Close without a change |
| Tab | Menu open | Close without a change and move on |
| A letter | Menu open | Jump to the next node in the column that starts with it |

## Motion

- The menu opens and closes like `Select`'s.
- When a column comes or goes, the menu's width springs to its new size, and a running spring is redirected instead of
  waiting. A new column fades in while it slides 8 px in from the left. When the menu opens, every column of the selected
  path is laid out at once, with no column-by-column animation.
- The highlight glides between rows, and the field's text rolls when the choice changes.
- With reduced motion the width does not animate and a new column only fades in; with motion off everything is immediate.

## Related

- `Select`: a single level of options.
- `Combobox`: a single level that you search by typing.
- `TreeView`: a whole tree on the page.

# Dot grid

> A field of dots that swells away from the pointer like a lens and sends a ripple out from every click.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc.Special`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc.Special --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/dot-grid

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.DotGridPreviewDemo">
    <!-- Move the pointer over the field and click anywhere; the switch changes the gap between dots. -->
    <arc:DotGrid x:Name="Field"
                 Height="420"
                 MaxWidth="720"
                 BorderThickness="1"
                 Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Surface}"
                 BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Border}"
                 CornerRadius="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource RadiusSurface}">
        <arc:SegmentedControl SelectedValue="22"
                              SelectionChanged="OnDensityChanged"
                              HorizontalAlignment="Center"
                              VerticalAlignment="Bottom"
                              Margin="0,0,0,20">
            <arc:SegmentedOption Value="14" Label="Dense" />
            <arc:SegmentedOption Value="22" Label="Default" />
            <arc:SegmentedOption Value="32" Label="Loose" />
        </arc:SegmentedControl>
    </arc:DotGrid>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using System.Globalization;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class DotGridPreviewDemo : UserControl
{
    public DotGridPreviewDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
    }

    private void OnDensityChanged(object? sender, SelectionChangedEventArgs e)
    {
        // The event also fires while the XAML loads, before the named field exists: read the sender.
        if (Field is not null && sender is SegmentedControl { SelectedValue: string value })
        {
            Field.Gap = double.Parse(value, CultureInfo.InvariantCulture);
        }
    }
}
```

## When to use

`DotGrid` fills an area with a quiet grid of dots that reacts to the pointer. Around the pointer the dots swell outward
like a lens and take the accent color; a click or a tap sends a ring of motion across the field. Content you put
inside sits on top of the dots and keeps working as usual.

- **Landing page heroes**: give a headline some life without a video or a heavy illustration.
- **Sign-in panels, empty states and countdowns**: a background people can play with while they wait.
- **Section breaks**: a band between two parts of a long page that invites a poke.

## When not to use

- **Behind dense text, tables or charts**: moving dots fight with reading. Keep the field behind a headline and a few
  actions.
- **When nothing should react**: a static dot pattern drawn with a brush costs less.
- **Several on one screen**: one reactive background per view is plenty.

## Usage

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:DotGrid Height="420">
        <TextBlock Text="Built to be poked at" HorizontalAlignment="Center" VerticalAlignment="Center" />
    </arc:DotGrid>
</UserControl>
```

`DotGrid` is a `ContentControl` in the Special package. Register the package with `UseArcSpecial()` next to
`UseArcControls()`. Give the control a height, or let its content size it; it is at least 240px high. The field has no
background of its own: set `Background`, `BorderBrush`, `BorderThickness` and `CornerRadius` to frame it, and the dots
are clipped to that rounded box.

### As a hero

Put the headline and the actions inside. The field listens to the pointer across the whole control, over the content
too, so the lens keeps following while people move toward a button.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.DotGridHeroDemo">
    <!-- A hero: the headline and actions are the content; the field listens to the pointer over them too. -->
    <arc:DotGrid Height="380"
                 MaxWidth="720"
                 Gap="26"
                 BorderThickness="1"
                 Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Surface}"
                 BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Border}"
                 CornerRadius="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource RadiusSurface}">
        <StackPanel Spacing="12" HorizontalAlignment="Center" VerticalAlignment="Center" MaxWidth="440">
            <TextBlock Text="Built to be poked at"
                       HorizontalAlignment="Center"
                       TextAlignment="Center"
                       TextWrapping="Wrap"
                       FontFamily="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource DisplayFontFamily}"
                       FontSize="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Type3XL}"
                       FontWeight="Medium"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
            <TextBlock Text="Move across the field to bend it, and click to send a ripple."
                       HorizontalAlignment="Center"
                       TextAlignment="Center"
                       TextWrapping="Wrap"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
            <StackPanel Orientation="Horizontal" Spacing="8" HorizontalAlignment="Center" Margin="0,8,0,0">
                <arc:Button Content="Start a project" />
                <arc:Button Content="Read the guide" Variant="Ghost" />
            </StackPanel>
        </StackPanel>
    </arc:DotGrid>
</UserControl>
```

### Density, lens and colors

`Gap` is the distance between dots (22px by default, never less than 6). Lower values give a denser field: a 720 by
420 field has about 660 dots at the default gap and about 1,600 at 14. `DotSize` is the radius of a resting dot.
`Radius` is how far the lens reaches and `Strength` how far it pushes the dots at its strongest point, a third of the
way out from the pointer. `DotBrush` and `ActiveDotBrush` set the resting and the lit color; they default to the strong
border and the accent tokens, so the field follows the theme and the accent.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.DotGridColorsDemo">
    <!-- Brand colors, a wider and stronger lens, no edge fade and no ripples. -->
    <arc:DotGrid Height="300"
                 MaxWidth="720"
                 Gap="18"
                 DotSize="1.8"
                 Radius="200"
                 Strength="24"
                 IsFadeEnabled="False"
                 IsRippleEnabled="False"
                 DotBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Border}"
                 ActiveDotBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Series2}"
                 BorderThickness="1"
                 Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource SurfaceMuted}"
                 BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Border}"
                 CornerRadius="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource RadiusPanel}" />
</UserControl>
```

```xml
<arc:DotGrid Height="300"
             Gap="18"
             Radius="200"
             Strength="24"
             IsFadeEnabled="False"
             IsRippleEnabled="False"
             ActiveDotBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Series2}" />
```

`IsFadeEnabled` fades the dots out toward the edges (on by default), which keeps the field from ending in a hard line.
`IsRippleEnabled` turns the click ripples off.

### Ripples from code

`Ripple(point)` sends a ripple from a point in the control's coordinates, as a click there would. Use it to answer
something that happened elsewhere, such as a form being sent.

```csharp
field.Ripple(new Point(field.Bounds.Width / 2, field.Bounds.Height / 2));
```

### Best practices

**Do**

- Keep the content short and centred: a headline, a sentence and one or two actions.
- Use a larger `Gap` (26 to 32) for full-width heroes and slower devices.
- Match the brand with `ActiveDotBrush` rather than the resting color; the lit dots carry the color.

**Avoid**

- Very small gaps on very large areas. Every dot is simulated, so the cost grows with the dot count.
- Strengths much above the gap: dots then cross each other and the lens loses its shape.

### Common questions

**Do buttons inside still work?** Yes. The field is drawn under the content and never takes the pointer from it; it
only watches the pointer pass.

**Why don't the dots move?** Reduced motion keeps every dot in place and only lights the dots near the pointer.
With motion off the field is still.

## API reference

### DotGrid

A field of dots that bulge away from the pointer like a lens, wobble back on their own springs and ripple outward from every click or tap (Arc Dot grid, design reference). Content placed inside sits on top and stays interactive; the field listens to the pointer across the whole control, over the content too.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Gap` | `double` | `22` | Distance between dots in px; lower is denser. At least 6. |
| `DotSize` | `double` | `1.4` | Dot radius in px at rest. |
| `Radius` | `double` | `150` | Radius of the lens around the pointer in px. |
| `Strength` | `double` | `16` | How far the lens pushes dots at its strongest point, a third of the way out, in px. |
| `IsRippleEnabled` | `bool` | `true` | Whether clicks and taps send a ripple through the field. |
| `IsFadeEnabled` | `bool` | `true` | Whether the field fades out toward its edges. |
| `DotBrush` | `IBrush?` | `null` | Color of the dots at rest. The theme uses the strong border color. |
| `ActiveDotBrush` | `IBrush?` | `null` | Color the dots take under the lens and in ripples. The theme uses the accent color. |

Derives from `ContentControl`: every member of `ContentControl` works as well.

## Accessibility

- The field is decoration. It is not focusable and does not appear in the automation tree; the content keeps its own
  names and roles and stays in the reading order.
- Give the control `AutomationProperties.Name` only when the area itself means something; it then reads as a group.
- Under reduced motion the dots never move. The lens only lights the dots near the pointer, and clicks do not ripple.

## Motion

- Every dot follows its own lightly damped spring toward the offset the lens and the ripples ask of it, so the field
  wobbles a little and settles instead of snapping.
- The lens follows the pointer with a short lag and fades in when the pointer arrives and out when it leaves. Its push
  peaks a third of the way out from the pointer and falls to nothing at its rim; the dots it lights grow and take the
  active color.
- A ripple travels outward at 620px per second and fades over 1.5 seconds. Up to six ripples can overlap; a seventh
  replaces the oldest.
- On touch screens the lens appears only while a finger is down, and every tap ripples.
- Frames run only while something moves, and pause while the field is scrolled out of view.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| Lens | Pushes and lights dots | Lights dots | None |
| Ripples | Travel across the field | None | None |

## Related

- `GravityWell` bends a grid of tiles around the pointer instead of a field of dots.
- `InkFluid` fills a hero with ink that the pointer stirs.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `DotGrid` | You want a light, geometric background with a lens |
| `GravityWell` | The grid itself is content: photos, avatars or logos |
| `InkFluid` | You want a soft, organic background |

# Gravity well

> Tiles that lean toward the pointer, shrink and dim as if pulled into a well, with a click that rolls a shockwave through the grid.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc.Special`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc.Special --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/gravity-well

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             xmlns:demos="using:TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.GravityWellPreviewDemo">
    <!-- A moodboard of 42 photos in 7 columns. Move over it, click to send a shockwave, or Tab in and use the arrows. -->
    <Border MaxWidth="600"
            Padding="20"
            BorderThickness="1"
            ClipToBounds="True"
            Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Surface}"
            BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Border}"
            CornerRadius="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource RadiusSurface}">
        <arc:GravityWell Label="Studio moodboard"
                         Columns="7"
                         Cursor="Cross"
                         ItemsSource="{x:Static demos:GravityWellDemoData.Photos}">
            <arc:GravityWell.ItemTemplate>
                <DataTemplate x:DataType="arc:ImageSource">
                    <arc:ArcImage Source="{Binding}" Stretch="UniformToFill" />
                </DataTemplate>
            </arc:GravityWell.ItemTemplate>
        </arc:GravityWell>
    </Border>
</UserControl>
```

## When to use

`GravityWell` lays its items out as a grid of square tiles and bends the grid around the pointer, as if a heavy mass
sat under it. Tiles near the pointer lean in, shrink, dim and slide under their neighbours; a click sends a shockwave
that rolls out through the grid and flashes each tile's ring as it passes.

- **Team, customer and partner walls**: many faces or logos at once, where play is the point.
- **Moodboards and galleries on landing pages**: show the breadth of a collection in one playful block.
- **Small decorative sets**: icons, stickers or swatches people can push around.

## When not to use

- **Grids people must scan or click precisely**, such as file pickers: tiles move under the pointer. Use a plain grid.
- **Large collections**: every tile is animated. Keep it to a few dozen; use a photo grid or a virtualized list for
  more.

## Usage

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:GravityWell Label="Team" Columns="6">
        <Border Background="#d9c2a5" />
        <Border Background="#b8c7a3" />
        <Border Background="#a9bcd6" />
    </arc:GravityWell>
</UserControl>
```

`GravityWell` is an `ItemsControl` in the Special package. Register the package with `UseArcSpecial()` next to
`UseArcControls()`. Each item becomes one square tile, either written inline or created from `ItemsSource` and an
`ItemTemplate`. The tile clips its content to `TileCornerRadius` (12px by default) and shows a muted surface behind it,
so photos that are still loading keep their place. Stretch images with `Stretch="UniformToFill"` to fill the square.

### Columns

`Columns` fixes the number of columns. Leave it at 0 and the grid fits as many columns as it can while keeping every
tile at least `MinTileSize` wide (56px by default); the tiles then share the remaining width. `Gap` is the space
between tiles (8px).

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             xmlns:demos="using:TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.GravityWellTeamDemo">
    <!-- Without Columns the grid fits as many 64px tiles as the width allows; resize the window to see it reflow. -->
    <arc:GravityWell Label="Team"
                     MaxWidth="560"
                     MinTileSize="64"
                     Gap="10"
                     Radius="120"
                     ItemsSource="{x:Static demos:GravityWellDemoData.People}">
        <arc:GravityWell.ItemTemplate>
            <DataTemplate x:DataType="demos:GravityWellPerson">
                <Border Background="{Binding Tint}" ToolTip.Tip="{Binding Name}">
                    <TextBlock Text="{Binding Initials}"
                               HorizontalAlignment="Center"
                               VerticalAlignment="Center"
                               FontWeight="Medium"
                               Foreground="#1f1f1f" />
                </Border>
            </DataTemplate>
        </arc:GravityWell.ItemTemplate>
    </arc:GravityWell>
</UserControl>
```

### Reach and strength

`Radius` is the reach of the well in px (150) and `Strength` how hard it pulls, from 0 to about 1.5 (1). A larger
radius bends more of the grid at once; a stronger well pulls the nearest tiles further in and shrinks them more.

### Responding to a shockwave

`Pulsed` fires for every shockwave, from a click, a tap, Space or Enter, and `GravityWellPulseEventArgs.Origin` says
where it started, in px from the top left of the grid. `Pulse(point)` sends one from code. Tie it to something that
matters, such as shuffling or picking an item, or leave it as a small delight.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             xmlns:demos="using:TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.GravityWellShuffleDemo">
    <!-- Pulsed reports every shockwave with its origin; here each one shuffles the team. -->
    <StackPanel Spacing="12" MaxWidth="560">
        <arc:GravityWell x:Name="Well"
                         Label="Shuffled team"
                         Columns="8"
                         Strength="1.4"
                         Pulsed="OnPulsed">
            <arc:GravityWell.ItemTemplate>
                <DataTemplate x:DataType="demos:GravityWellPerson">
                    <Border Background="{Binding Tint}">
                        <TextBlock Text="{Binding Initials}"
                                   HorizontalAlignment="Center"
                                   VerticalAlignment="Center"
                                   FontWeight="Medium"
                                   Foreground="#1f1f1f" />
                    </Border>
                </DataTemplate>
            </arc:GravityWell.ItemTemplate>
        </arc:GravityWell>
        <TextBlock x:Name="Status"
                   Text="Click the grid, or press Space while it has focus."
                   HorizontalAlignment="Center"
                   FontSize="12"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using System.Collections.ObjectModel;
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class GravityWellShuffleDemo : UserControl
{
    private readonly ObservableCollection<GravityWellPerson> _people = new(GravityWellDemoData.People);
    private readonly Random _random = new(7);
    private int _shuffles;

    public GravityWellShuffleDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Well.ItemsSource = _people;
    }

    private void OnPulsed(object? sender, GravityWellPulseEventArgs e)
    {
        for (var i = 0; i < 4; i++)
        {
            _people.Move(_random.Next(_people.Count), _random.Next(_people.Count));
        }
        _shuffles++;
        Status.Text = $"Shuffled {_shuffles} {(_shuffles == 1 ? "time" : "times")}, last from ({e.Origin.X:0}, {e.Origin.Y:0})";
    }
}
```

```csharp
well.Pulsed += (_, e) => Shuffle(people);
```

### Best practices

**Do**

- Use a uniform set of square pictures, around 30 to 60.
- Give the grid a `Label` that names what it shows, such as "Team" or "Customers".
- Give each image tile a tooltip or an accessible name when the people or logos matter.

**Avoid**

- Mixing portrait and landscape pictures without cropping them; the tiles are always square.
- Putting buttons or links inside the tiles. The tiles move under the pointer, so they are hard to hit.

### Common questions

**Does the reading order change when tiles slide under each other?** No. Tiles keep their slots in the grid and only
move by their render transform, opacity and stacking order.

**Why does the grid stay still?** Reduced motion keeps every tile in place; a shockwave then only flashes the rings.

## API reference

### GravityWell

A grid of square tiles that bends toward the pointer like spacetime around a mass (Arc Gravity well, design reference). Tiles near the well lean in, shrink and dim on their own springs; a click, a tap, Space or Enter sends a shockwave rolling outward through the grid. Each item becomes one tile: photos, avatars, icons or any small content.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Columns` | `int` | `0` | A fixed column count; 0 (the default) fits as many columns as `MinTileSize` allows. |
| `MinTileSize` | `double` | `56` | The smallest tile width in px when `Columns` is 0. |
| `Gap` | `double` | `8` | The gap between tiles in px. |
| `Radius` | `double` | `150` | The reach of the well in px. |
| `Strength` | `double` | `1` | The pull strength, from 0 to about 1.5. |
| `TileCornerRadius` | `CornerRadius` | `0,0,0,0` | The corner radius of every tile; the content is clipped to it and the shockwave ring follows it. |
| `Label` | `string` | `"Gravity well"` | The accessible name of the grid. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Pulsed` | `GravityWellPulseEventArgs` | Raised when a click, a tap or a key sends a shockwave, with its origin in the grid. |

Derives from `ItemsControl`: every member of `ItemsControl` works as well.

### GravityWellPulseEventArgs

The origin of a `GravityWell` shockwave.

Derives from `RoutedEventArgs`: every member of `RoutedEventArgs` works as well.

## Accessibility

- The grid is a focusable group named by `Label` ("Gravity well" by default) and described as a "gravity well". The
  tiles' content keeps its own names and roles.
- Motion is decoration. Tiles never leave their slots, so the order a screen reader follows matches the grid.
- Keyboard focus shows a 2px focus ring around the grid; pointer focus shows none. While the grid has keyboard focus
  the well itself shows which tile is current.
- Under reduced motion the tiles stay in place, and a shockwave only flashes their rings.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Tab` | Focus the grid and place the well on the current tile |
| `Left` / `Right` | Move the well to the previous or next tile |
| `Up` / `Down` | Move the well a row up or down |
| `Home` / `End` | Move the well to the first or last tile |
| `Space` / `Enter` | Send a shockwave from the current tile |

## Motion

- The well follows the pointer on a critically damped spring: it trails a fast move and arrives without overshooting.
- Each tile follows the well's pull on its own lightly damped spring, so a quick sweep leaves a wobbling wake. The
  deeper a tile sits, the more it leans toward the well, shrinks (to about 0.56 at the bottom), dims and sinks under
  its neighbours.
- A shockwave travels outward at 900px per second. As its front reaches a tile it kicks the tile away from the origin,
  dips its scale and flashes its 2px accent ring, more strongly near the origin; the ring then fades out.
- On touch screens a tap sends a shockwave and a drag pulls the well; vertical scrolling keeps working.
- Each frame writes only a transform, an opacity and a stacking order per tile, with no layout. Frames stop when every
  spring is at rest and pause while the grid is out of view.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| Well | Bends the grid | None | None |
| Shockwave | Kicks the tiles and flashes the rings | Flashes the rings | None |

## Related

- `DotGrid` bends a field of dots instead of content.
- `CardStack` and `Carousel` show a few pictures one at a time.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `GravityWell` | Many small pictures should feel playful together |
| `DotGrid` | You want a reactive background behind a headline |
| `Carousel` | Each picture deserves a closer look |

# Ink fluid

> A fluid simulation behind your content: the pointer stirs soft ink that swirls and fades, and a slow stir keeps it moving when nobody does.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc.Special`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc.Special --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/ink-fluid

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.InkFluidPreviewDemo">
    <!-- Stir the ink with the pointer; leave it alone and a slow stir takes over after a moment. -->
    <arc:InkFluid MinHeight="440"
                  MaxWidth="760"
                  BorderThickness="1"
                  Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Surface}"
                  BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Border}"
                  CornerRadius="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource RadiusSurface}">
        <StackPanel Spacing="12" MaxWidth="460" Margin="24,48" HorizontalAlignment="Center" VerticalAlignment="Center">
            <TextBlock Text="Calm until you move"
                       HorizontalAlignment="Center"
                       TextAlignment="Center"
                       TextWrapping="Wrap"
                       FontFamily="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource DisplayFontFamily}"
                       FontSize="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Type4XL}"
                       FontWeight="Medium"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
            <TextBlock Text="Every stroke leaves a trail of ink that drifts, curls and settles back to quiet."
                       HorizontalAlignment="Center"
                       TextAlignment="Center"
                       TextWrapping="Wrap"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
            <StackPanel Orientation="Horizontal" Spacing="8" HorizontalAlignment="Center" Margin="0,12,0,0">
                <arc:Button Content="Start building" />
                <arc:Button Content="See examples" Variant="Ghost" />
            </StackPanel>
        </StackPanel>
    </arc:InkFluid>
</UserControl>
```

## When to use

`InkFluid` runs a small fluid simulation behind its content. Moving the pointer stirs in soft ink tinted with the
accent color; the ink curls, spreads, turns neutral as it ages and fades after a couple of seconds. When nobody is
moving, a slow stir keeps a little ink drifting so the area never looks frozen.

- **Landing heroes and sign-in screens**: a calm, living background without a video.
- **Empty states and waiting screens**: something gentle to play with while there is nothing else to show.

## When not to use

- **Dense product surfaces** such as tables, forms and dashboards: movement behind data distracts.
- **More than one per page**: each instance runs its own simulation.
- **Where text must keep full contrast at all times**: the ink is faint, but it does pass under the content.

## Usage

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:InkFluid MinHeight="440" Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Surface}">
        <TextBlock Text="Calm until you move" HorizontalAlignment="Center" VerticalAlignment="Center" />
    </arc:InkFluid>
</UserControl>
```

`InkFluid` is a `ContentControl` in the Special package. Register the package with `UseArcSpecial()` next to
`UseArcControls()`. The ink is drawn on transparent pixels over the control's own background, so give it a `Background`, and a
`CornerRadius` and border if it should look like a card; the ink is clipped to that rounded box. The control is at
least 240px high.

The ink takes its colors from the theme: neutral ink uses the foreground token and tinted ink the accent token, so it
follows light and dark themes and the accent switcher. Set `InkBrush` or `AccentInkBrush` to override either.

### Tuning the ink

`Intensity` (0.5) sets how dark the ink gets, `Tint` (0.8) how much of the fresh ink takes the accent color, and
`Force` (0.5) how hard the pointer stirs; all three run from 0 to 1. `IsAmbient` turns the slow stir on or off; it
starts 1.2 seconds after the last pointer move. `IsInteractive` lets the pointer stir the ink at all.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.InkFluidTuningDemo">
    <!-- Intensity, tint and force from 0 to 1 (the sliders show percent), the ambient stir and the grid size. -->
    <StackPanel Spacing="16" MaxWidth="640">
        <arc:InkFluid x:Name="Ink"
                      Height="300"
                      BorderThickness="1"
                      Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Surface}"
                      BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Border}"
                      CornerRadius="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource RadiusPanel}" />
        <Grid ColumnDefinitions="*,*,*" ColumnSpacing="16">
            <arc:Slider x:Name="IntensitySlider" Label="Intensity" Value="50" ValueChanged="OnChanged" />
            <arc:Slider x:Name="TintSlider" Grid.Column="1" Label="Tint" Value="80" ValueChanged="OnChanged" />
            <arc:Slider x:Name="ForceSlider" Grid.Column="2" Label="Force" Value="50" ValueChanged="OnChanged" />
        </Grid>
        <StackPanel Orientation="Horizontal" Spacing="16" HorizontalAlignment="Center">
            <arc:Switch x:Name="AmbientSwitch" Content="Ambient stir" IsChecked="True" IsCheckedChanged="OnChanged" />
            <arc:SegmentedControl x:Name="QualityPicker" SelectedValue="Medium" SelectionChanged="OnChanged">
                <arc:SegmentedOption Value="Low" Label="Low" />
                <arc:SegmentedOption Value="Medium" Label="Medium" />
                <arc:SegmentedOption Value="High" Label="High" />
            </arc:SegmentedControl>
        </StackPanel>
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class InkFluidTuningDemo : UserControl
{
    public InkFluidTuningDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Apply();
    }

    private void OnChanged(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) => Apply();

    private void Apply()
    {
        // The events also fire while the XAML loads, before every named field exists.
        if (Ink is null || IntensitySlider is null || TintSlider is null || ForceSlider is null || AmbientSwitch is null || QualityPicker is null)
        {
            return;
        }
        Ink.Intensity = IntensitySlider.Value / 100;
        Ink.Tint = TintSlider.Value / 100;
        Ink.Force = ForceSlider.Value / 100;
        Ink.IsAmbient = AmbientSwitch.IsChecked == true;
        Ink.Quality = QualityPicker.SelectedValue switch
        {
            "Low" => InkFluidQuality.Low,
            "High" => InkFluidQuality.High,
            _ => InkFluidQuality.Medium
        };
    }
}
```

```xml
<arc:InkFluid Intensity="0.8" Tint="1" Force="0.7" IsAmbient="False" />
```

### Quality

`Quality` picks the size of the simulation. The velocity grid has 96, 128 or 192 cells on the short side for `Low`,
`Medium` (the default) and `High`, and the ink is drawn at twice that resolution and scaled up smoothly. Larger grids
show finer curls and cost more; `Low` suits small areas and slower devices.

### A waiting screen

With no tint, low intensity and the low grid, the ink becomes a quiet backdrop for an empty state.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.InkFluidEmptyStateDemo">
    <!-- A waiting screen: light ink, no tint, the low grid, and the ambient stir keeping it alive. -->
    <arc:InkFluid Height="260"
                  MaxWidth="520"
                  Intensity="0.35"
                  Tint="0"
                  Quality="Low"
                  BorderThickness="1"
                  Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource SurfaceMuted}"
                  BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Border}"
                  CornerRadius="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource RadiusPanel}">
        <StackPanel Spacing="6" HorizontalAlignment="Center" VerticalAlignment="Center">
            <TextBlock Text="Nothing here yet"
                       HorizontalAlignment="Center"
                       FontSize="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TypeLG}"
                       FontWeight="Medium"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
            <TextBlock Text="New reports show up here as soon as they finish."
                       HorizontalAlignment="Center"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
        </StackPanel>
    </arc:InkFluid>
</UserControl>
```

### Best practices

**Do**

- Keep the content in the middle and short; the ink reads best around it.
- Make buttons and links inside the content as usual: the ink never takes the pointer from them.

**Avoid**

- Raising `Intensity` near 1 behind small text.
- Placing the control where it is resized constantly: every new size rebuilds the simulation.

### Common questions

**Does it need a GPU?** No. The simulation runs on the CPU on every platform Avalonia supports and draws one picture
per frame.

**Why does it look still?** Under reduced motion the control draws one composed frame of the slow stir and stops.

## API reference

### InkFluid

A real-time fluid simulation behind your content (Arc Ink fluid, design reference). The pointer stirs soft ink tinted with the accent color, which turns neutral as it spreads and fades over a couple of seconds; left alone, a slow, calm stir keeps it alive. Content placed inside sits on top and stays interactive.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Intensity` | `double` | `0.5` | How dark the ink gets, from 0 to 1. |
| `Tint` | `double` | `0.8` | How much of the fresh ink takes the accent color, from 0 to 1; the tinted share turns neutral as it spreads. |
| `Force` | `double` | `0.5` | How hard the pointer stirs, from 0 to 1. |
| `IsAmbient` | `bool` | `true` | Whether a slow stir keeps the ink moving while nobody interacts, starting 1.2s after the last pointer move. |
| `IsInteractive` | `bool` | `true` | Whether the pointer stirs the ink. |
| `Quality` | `InkFluidQuality` | `Medium` | The simulation grid and ink resolution. |
| `InkBrush` | `IBrush?` | `null` | The color of neutral ink. The theme uses the foreground color. |
| `AccentInkBrush` | `IBrush?` | `null` | The color of tinted ink. The theme uses the accent color. |

Derives from `ContentControl`: every member of `ContentControl` works as well.

The quality values:

| Type | Values |
|---|---|
| `InkFluidQuality` | `Low`, `Medium`, `High` |

## Accessibility

- The ink is decoration. It is not focusable, takes no pointer hits and does not appear in the automation tree; the
  content stays fully readable and interactive.
- The ink's coverage is capped low, so text over it keeps its contrast in both themes.
- Under reduced motion the control shows one still frame and runs no animation.

## Motion

- The fluid is a stable-fluids simulation: the velocity field carries itself and the ink along (semi-Lagrangian
  advection), vorticity confinement keeps small swirls alive, and a 20-step pressure solve keeps the flow from
  bunching up. The picture is lit softly from the ink's slope, so wisps look rounded rather than flat.
- The pointer's speed drives the stir, and the amount of ink grows with it: slow moves leave faint trails, quick
  flicks bloom.
- Ink fades over a couple of seconds. Tinted ink hands its color to the neutral share as it spreads, so fresh strokes
  carry the accent and old wisps turn grey.
- On touch screens a finger stirs while it is down; vertical scrolling keeps working.
- The simulation pauses while the control is scrolled out of view or hidden and continues where it left off. Resizes
  wait 120ms for the size to settle before the simulation is rebuilt.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ink | Live simulation | One still frame | One still frame |

## Related

- `DotGrid` is a lighter, geometric background that reacts to the pointer.
- `GravityWell` makes a grid of pictures react instead of the background.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `InkFluid` | You want a soft, organic, always-moving background |
| `DotGrid` | You want something lighter and more precise |
| `GravityWell` | The content itself should react |
