# Agent status

> A live status pill for a running agent: its mark in a spinning ring, the current step and a timer, opening into the recent steps with pause, stop and approval controls.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc.Special`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc.Special --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/agent-status

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.AgentStatusPreviewDemo">
    <!-- The pill runs an invented sample run on its own. The scenario switch and Replay belong to this demo, not to the
         control: they only change the AgentRunSimulation that drives the pill. -->
    <Grid RowDefinitions="Auto,Auto" Height="400">
        <arc:AgentStatus x:Name="Pill" Margin="0,64,0,0" HorizontalAlignment="Center" />
        <StackPanel Grid.Row="1" Orientation="Horizontal" Spacing="12" HorizontalAlignment="Center" VerticalAlignment="Bottom">
            <arc:SegmentedControl x:Name="Scenario" SelectedValue="coding" SelectionChanged="OnScenarioChanged">
                <arc:SegmentedOption Value="coding" Label="Coding agent" />
                <arc:SegmentedOption Value="research" Label="Research agent" />
            </arc:SegmentedControl>
            <arc:Button Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Click="OnReplay" VerticalAlignment="Center">
                <StackPanel Orientation="Horizontal" Spacing="8">
                    <arc:ArcGlyph Data="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.RotateCcw}" Size="16" />
                    <TextBlock Text="Replay" />
                </StackPanel>
            </arc:Button>
        </StackPanel>
    </Grid>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class AgentStatusPreviewDemo : UserControl
{
    private readonly AgentRunSimulation _simulation = new();

    public AgentStatusPreviewDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Pill.Simulation = _simulation;
        // The demo owns the run: stop its timer when the page goes away.
        DetachedFromVisualTree += (_, _) => _simulation.Dispose();
    }

    private void OnScenarioChanged(object? sender, SelectionChangedEventArgs e)
    {
        // The event also fires while the XAML loads, before the named field exists: read the sender.
        var research = sender is SegmentedControl { SelectedValue: "research" };
        _simulation.Scenario = research ? AgentStatusSamples.Research : AgentStatusSamples.Coding;
    }

    private void OnReplay(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) => _simulation.Replay();
}
```

## When to use

`AgentStatus` is the smallest honest answer to "is the agent still working, and on what?". It is a pill that sits in a
header, a title bar or above a composer: the agent's mark inside a thin ring that turns while it works, the current
activity with its icon, and how long the run has taken. One press opens the same pill in place into a floating panel
with the latest steps, a segmented progress bar and the controls to pause, stop, approve or retry. Nothing below it
moves.

- **A header or title bar that should show a run at a glance**: what the agent is doing right now and for how long,
  without a log taking over the page.
- **Approval gates**: a command, a deploy or an email that waits for a person. The pill turns into a request with Deny
  and Approve right in it, so the answer is one press away from anywhere in the app.
- **Background runs people check on now and then**: the pill stays small; the panel shows the last few steps and the
  controls only when someone asks.
- **Runs that fail and can be retried**: the pill closes its ring around a cross, says why, and offers Retry.
- **Several agents in one app**: each header slot can hold its own pill; an idle pill costs no animation frames.

## When not to use

- **The run is the page**: a transcript with every step, tool call and output needs room. Use `ToolCall` rows in a
  chat thread, or a full run view; the pill's panel lists only the latest steps.
- **A queue of approvals across agents**: build a list of requests; one pill shows one agent's run.
- **A plan the user edits before the run**: use `AgentPlan`, which reorders and edits steps.
- **Comparing many agents on one time axis**: use `AgentTimeline`.
- **One shimmering word with no timer and no controls**: use `TextShimmer`.

## Usage

With nothing set, the pill plays a sample run on its own: an invented coding agent that works through six steps and
stops on an approval that waits for as long as it takes. The preview above adds a switch to a second sample (a research
agent whose third step fails once, so Retry can be seen) and a Replay button; those two controls belong to the demo,
not to the pill.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:AgentStatus />
</UserControl>
```

`AgentStatus` derives from Avalonia's `TemplatedControl`. It lives in the Special package: register it with
`UseArcSpecial()` next to `UseArcControls()`.

In an app, drive it from your agent's events. Set `Status`, keep `Activity` to the latest tool call in the present
tense, list `Steps`, give a `StartedAt` that stays fixed for the whole run, and handle the action events. The pill never
changes its own status when it has data: pressing Approve raises `ApproveRequested`, and your code decides what happens.

```xml
<arc:AgentStatus Status="{Binding Run.Status}"
                 Activity="{Binding Run.Activity}"
                 StartedAt="{Binding Run.StartedAt}"
                 Agent="{Binding Run.Agent}" />
```

Each action is a routed event with typed arguments (`PauseRequested`, `ResumeRequested`, `StopRequested`,
`ApproveRequested`, `DenyRequested`, `RetryRequested`, `OpenRunRequested`).

```csharp
status.PauseRequested += (_, e) => agent.Pause(run.Id);
status.ApproveRequested += (_, e) => agent.Approve(run.Id);
```

```csharp
status.Steps.Add(new AgentStatusStep("scan", "Scanned 9 modules", AgentStatusStepState.Done, ArcIcons.Search)
{
    Duration = TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(1917)
});
status.Activity = new AgentStatusActivity("Checking specs", ArcIcons.Search, progressValue: 8, progressTotal: 12);
```

### Every state

The pill has seven states. Each pairs the ring and glyph with words, so a state never relies on color. Press a pill to
open its panel.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.AgentStatusStatesDemo">
    <!-- Every state, driven by the host: nothing changes on its own. Press a pill to open its panel. -->
    <StackPanel x:Name="Stack" Spacing="14" HorizontalAlignment="Center" Margin="0,0,0,330" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Layout;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class AgentStatusStatesDemo : UserControl
{
    public AgentStatusStatesDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        var agent = AgentStatusSamples.CodingAgent;
        var started = DateTimeOffset.UtcNow - TimeSpan.FromSeconds(74);
        Add(AgentStatusRunState.Idle, null, agent, started);
        Add(AgentStatusRunState.Working, new AgentStatusActivity("Checking specs", ArcIcons.Search, 8, 12), agent, started);
        Add(AgentStatusRunState.NeedsInput, new AgentStatusActivity("Needs your approval to deploy", ArcIcons.Search), agent, started);
        Add(AgentStatusRunState.Paused, new AgentStatusActivity("Checking specs", ArcIcons.Search, 8, 12), agent, started);
        Add(AgentStatusRunState.Done, new AgentStatusActivity("5 files touched"), agent, started, DateTimeOffset.UtcNow - TimeSpan.FromSeconds(14));
        Add(AgentStatusRunState.Failed, new AgentStatusActivity("Fetch failed · 2 pages did not load"), AgentStatusSamples.ResearchAgent, started);
        Add(AgentStatusRunState.Stopped, null, AgentStatusSamples.ResearchAgent, started, DateTimeOffset.UtcNow - TimeSpan.FromSeconds(7));
    }

    private void Add(AgentStatusRunState state, AgentStatusActivity? activity, AgentModel agent, DateTimeOffset started, DateTimeOffset? ended = null)
    {
        var pill = new AgentStatus
        {
            Status = state,
            Activity = activity,
            Agent = agent,
            StartedAt = started,
            EndedAt = ended,
            SettleAfter = null,
            HorizontalAlignment = HorizontalAlignment.Center
        };
        pill.Steps.Add(new AgentStatusStep("scan", "Scanned 9 modules", AgentStatusStepState.Done, ArcIcons.Search) { Duration = TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(1917) });
        pill.Steps.Add(new AgentStatusStep("patch", "Patched lib/dates/parse-due.ts", AgentStatusStepState.Done, ArcIcons.Search) { Duration = TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(2533) });
        var third = state switch
        {
            AgentStatusRunState.Working or AgentStatusRunState.Paused => AgentStatusStepState.Active,
            AgentStatusRunState.NeedsInput => AgentStatusStepState.Waiting,
            AgentStatusRunState.Failed => AgentStatusStepState.Failed,
            AgentStatusRunState.Stopped => AgentStatusStepState.Skipped,
            AgentStatusRunState.Idle => AgentStatusStepState.Skipped,
            _ => AgentStatusStepState.Done
        };
        pill.Steps.Add(new AgentStatusStep("third", state == AgentStatusRunState.Failed ? "2 pages did not load" : "Checking specs", third, ArcIcons.Search)
        {
            StartedAt = started + TimeSpan.FromSeconds(20),
            Duration = third == AgentStatusStepState.Done ? TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(3316) : null
        });
        pill.Steps.Add(new AgentStatusStep("last", "Deploy", AgentStatusStepState.Pending));
        Stack.Children.Add(pill);
    }
}
```

| State | Ring and mark | Label | Timer | Buttons |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Idle` | The mark alone, no ring | "Ready" in the secondary color | Hidden | Open run in the panel |
| `Working` | A track and a short arc turning once every 0.9 s | The activity with its icon; the text shimmers | Counts | Pause and Stop in the panel |
| `NeedsInput` | The arc leaves; an accent dot pops in with one ping | The request in the text color | Keeps counting | Deny and Approve inline; Approve and Deny in the panel |
| `Paused` | The arc freezes and turns gray, the mark dims | "Paused" with a pause icon | Frozen | Resume and Stop in the panel |
| `Done` | The ring closes in the success color and the mark becomes a drawn check | "Done in 2m 23s · 5 files touched" | Hidden | Open run |
| `Failed` | The ring closes in the danger color around a cross | The failure | Hidden | Retry inline and in the panel |
| `Stopped` | No ring; a small square replaces the mark | "Stopped after 7s" in the secondary color | Hidden | Open run |

A finished run (`Done` or `Stopped`) settles back to "Ready" after `SettleAfter` (4 seconds by default; null keeps the
result on screen). The panel keeps the last run's steps and counter, and `Settled` is raised.

### Anatomy

1. **Orb**: a 24px disc. The agent's mark is drawn at 12px in the middle of a 1.5px ring. The ring is a track with a
   short arc while working, a closed circle when done or failed, and nothing while idle or stopped.
2. **Label**: a 16px icon and one line of 14px text. A new activity rolls in from below while the old one leaves
   upward. A count such as "8 of 12" changes its digits in place and is part of the shimmer. When the label is wider
   than its room, its right edge fades over 24px instead of wrapping.
3. **Timer**: minutes and seconds in tabular figures ("2:20"), shown while the run is live.
4. **Inline buttons**: Deny and Approve while input is needed, Retry after a failure, 30px high.
5. **Panel**: opened from the pill. A line with the agent's name and "Step 3 of 6" (or "6 of 6 steps" once the run has
   ended), a progress bar with one 3px segment per step, the latest five steps with an icon, a label that wraps and a
   time, and a footer with the buttons.

### The panel

The panel grows from the pill's own surface: width and height spring together while the header row stays where it is,
and the content fades in a beat later. It floats in the window's overlay layer, so a header that clips its children or
a scroller cannot cut it off, and nothing below it moves. It is as wide as 384px or the pill, whichever is wider, and
never wider than the container.

`PanelAlignment` chooses which edge the panel keeps: `Start` for a pill against the start of a header, `End` for one at
the end, `Center` (default) to grow evenly on both sides.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.AgentStatusHeaderBarDemo">
    <!-- A header bar that clips its content: the open panel floats over the page instead of being cut off. The left pill
         grows its panel from the start edge, the right one from the end edge. -->
    <Border x:Name="Bar"
            Height="56"
            ClipToBounds="True"
            BorderThickness="1"
            CornerRadius="16"
            Margin="0,0,0,330"
            BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Border}"
            Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Surface}">
        <Grid ColumnDefinitions="Auto,*,Auto" Margin="12,0">
            <arc:AgentStatus x:Name="Left" PanelAlignment="Start" VerticalAlignment="Center" />
            <TextBlock Grid.Column="1"
                       Text="Release notes"
                       HorizontalAlignment="Center"
                       VerticalAlignment="Center"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
            <arc:AgentStatus x:Name="Right" Grid.Column="2" PanelAlignment="End" VerticalAlignment="Center" />
        </Grid>
    </Border>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class AgentStatusHeaderBarDemo : UserControl
{
    private readonly AgentRunSimulation _coding = new(AgentStatusSamples.Coding);
    private readonly AgentRunSimulation _research = new(AgentStatusSamples.Research);

    public AgentStatusHeaderBarDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Left.Simulation = _coding;
        Right.Simulation = _research;
        // The demo owns the runs: stop their timers when the page goes away.
        DetachedFromVisualTree += (_, _) =>
        {
            _coding.Dispose();
            _research.Dispose();
        };
    }
}
```

`IsExpanded` is two way. Pressing the pill, Escape and a press outside change it; set it from code or bind it to open
the panel yourself. `ExpandedChanged` reports every change. `Expand()`, `Collapse()` and `Toggle()` do the same from
code.

```xml
<arc:AgentStatus IsExpanded="{Binding IsRunOpen, Mode=TwoWay}" PanelAlignment="End" />
```

The panel lists the latest `MaxSteps` steps (five by default) that are not pending. Pending steps still count in the
progress bar. A new step fades in at the bottom while the older ones slide up and the oldest fades out at the top.
Steps are matched by `Id`, so a step that changes from "Running tests" to "Passed 12 of 12 tests" keeps its row: the old
label fades out and the new one takes its place.

### Your own run

Write step labels in the present tense while they run and in the past tense once they are done, so the words carry the
state. A step's `StartedAt` makes its time count in whole seconds while it runs; a finished step shows its `Duration`
with one decimal ("1.9s"). Failed and skipped steps show no time.

The timer counts from `StartedAt` and leaves out the time spent paused or failed by itself. Give it the run's real start
once and keep it fixed; give `EndedAt` when your backend knows it, otherwise the moment the status turned done or stopped
is used.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.AgentStatusHostDrivenDemo">
    <!-- Your code owns the run: it sets Status, Activity and Steps, and answers the events. The pill never changes its own
         status when it has data. The log below shows each event the buttons raise. -->
    <StackPanel Spacing="16" Height="420">
        <arc:AgentStatus x:Name="Pill"
                         HorizontalAlignment="Center"
                         Margin="0,24,0,0"
                         Agent="{x:Static arc:AgentStatusSamples.ResearchAgent}"
                         PauseRequested="OnPause"
                         ResumeRequested="OnResume"
                         StopRequested="OnStop"
                         ApproveRequested="OnApprove"
                         DenyRequested="OnDeny"
                         RetryRequested="OnRetry"
                         OpenRunRequested="OnOpenRun"
                         ExpandedChanged="OnExpandedChanged" />
        <WrapPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center" ItemSpacing="8" LineSpacing="8" Margin="0,200,0,0">
            <arc:Button Content="Start a run" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Click="OnStart" />
            <arc:Button Content="Ask for approval" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Click="OnAsk" />
            <arc:Button Content="Fail" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Click="OnFail" />
            <arc:Button Content="Finish" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Click="OnFinish" />
        </WrapPanel>
        <TextBlock x:Name="Log"
                   HorizontalAlignment="Center"
                   TextAlignment="Center"
                   TextWrapping="Wrap"
                   FontSize="13"
                   Text="Start a run, then press a button in the pill."
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class AgentStatusHostDrivenDemo : UserControl
{
    private readonly List<string> _entries = new();

    public AgentStatusHostDrivenDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
    }

    private void Write(string text)
    {
        _entries.Add(text);
        if (_entries.Count > 4)
        {
            _entries.RemoveAt(0);
        }
        Log.Text = string.Join("  ·  ", _entries);
    }

    private void OnStart(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        Pill.Steps.Clear();
        Pill.Steps.Add(new AgentStatusStep("plan", "Drafted 3 sub-questions", AgentStatusStepState.Done, ArcIcons.ListChecks) { Duration = TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(1400) });
        Pill.Steps.Add(new AgentStatusStep("open", "Opening pages", AgentStatusStepState.Active, ArcIcons.BookOpen) { StartedAt = DateTimeOffset.UtcNow });
        Pill.Steps.Add(new AgentStatusStep("write", "Write the summary", AgentStatusStepState.Pending));
        Pill.StartedAt = DateTimeOffset.UtcNow - TimeSpan.FromSeconds(2);
        Pill.Activity = new AgentStatusActivity("Opening pages", ArcIcons.BookOpen, 3, 9);
        Pill.Status = AgentStatusRunState.Working;
        Write("Run started");
    }

    private void OnAsk(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        Pill.Activity = new AgentStatusActivity("Needs your approval to open 2 paywalled pages", ArcIcons.BookOpen);
        Pill.Status = AgentStatusRunState.NeedsInput;
        Write("Waiting for approval");
    }

    private void OnFail(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        Pill.Activity = new AgentStatusActivity("Fetch failed · 2 pages did not load");
        if (Pill.Steps.Count > 1)
        {
            Pill.Steps[1].State = AgentStatusStepState.Failed;
            Pill.Steps[1].Label = "2 pages did not load";
        }
        Pill.Status = AgentStatusRunState.Failed;
        Write("Run failed");
    }

    private void OnFinish(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        foreach (var step in Pill.Steps)
        {
            step.State = AgentStatusStepState.Done;
            step.Duration ??= TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(1800);
        }
        Pill.Activity = new AgentStatusActivity("8 pages cited");
        Pill.Status = AgentStatusRunState.Done;
        Write("Run finished");
    }

    private void Working(string activity)
    {
        Pill.Activity = new AgentStatusActivity(activity, ArcIcons.BookOpen, 4, 9);
        Pill.Status = AgentStatusRunState.Working;
        if (Pill.Steps.Count > 1)
        {
            Pill.Steps[1].State = AgentStatusStepState.Active;
            Pill.Steps[1].Label = "Opening pages";
        }
    }

    private void OnPause(object? sender, AgentStatusActionEventArgs e)
    {
        Pill.Status = AgentStatusRunState.Paused;
        Write("Pause requested");
    }

    private void OnResume(object? sender, AgentStatusActionEventArgs e)
    {
        Working("Opening pages");
        Write("Resume requested");
    }

    private void OnStop(object? sender, AgentStatusActionEventArgs e)
    {
        Pill.Status = AgentStatusRunState.Stopped;
        Write("Stop requested");
    }

    private void OnApprove(object? sender, AgentStatusActionEventArgs e)
    {
        Working("Opening pages");
        Write("Approved");
    }

    private void OnDeny(object? sender, AgentStatusActionEventArgs e)
    {
        Pill.Activity = new AgentStatusActivity("6 pages cited, 2 skipped");
        Pill.Status = AgentStatusRunState.Done;
        Write("Denied");
    }

    private void OnRetry(object? sender, AgentStatusActionEventArgs e)
    {
        Working("Opening pages");
        Write("Retry requested");
    }

    private void OnOpenRun(object? sender, AgentStatusActionEventArgs e) => Write("Open run requested");

    private void OnExpandedChanged(object? sender, AgentStatusExpandedChangedEventArgs e) => Write(e.IsExpanded ? "Panel opened" : "Panel closed");
}
```

```csharp
pill.ApproveRequested += (_, e) =>
{
    agent.Approve(run.Id);          // your backend
    pill.Activity = new AgentStatusActivity("Deploying build 2.4.1", ArcIcons.CloudUpload);
    pill.Status = AgentStatusRunState.Working;
};
```

`Notice` is a one-off message for screen readers, such as the result of an action; it joins the next announcement.
Every word the pill shows or announces comes from `Labels` (an `AgentStatusLabels`), including the sentences with
numbers, so the pill can be translated or reworded.

### Offering only what you can honor

A button shows only while its action is allowed by `Actions` and the run's state asks for it: Pause while working,
Resume while paused, Stop while working or paused, Approve and Deny while input is needed, Retry after a failure, and
Open run in every state. `Actions` is a flags value and defaults to all of them. It is the counterpart of showing a
control only when its handler exists; set it to what your app really handles.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.AgentStatusActionsDemo">
    <!-- Actions says which buttons this app can honor. Here the run can be approved or denied and opened, but not paused,
         stopped or retried, so those buttons never show. -->
    <StackPanel Spacing="14" HorizontalAlignment="Center" Margin="0,0,0,330">
        <arc:AgentStatus Status="NeedsInput"
                         Actions="Approve, Deny, OpenRun"
                         Agent="{x:Static arc:AgentStatusSamples.CodingAgent}"
                         Activity="{x:Static arc:AgentStatusSamples.ApprovalRequest}" />
        <arc:AgentStatus Status="Working"
                         Actions="OpenRun"
                         Agent="{x:Static arc:AgentStatusSamples.ResearchAgent}"
                         Activity="{x:Static arc:AgentStatusSamples.Reading}" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```xml
<arc:AgentStatus Actions="Approve, Deny, OpenRun" />
```

The first two footer buttons keep their place when the state changes: Pause becomes Resume, Approve becomes Pause, Stop
becomes Deny. It is the same button each time, so keyboard focus stays on it. When the focused button goes away for good
(Pause after the run finished), focus moves to the pill, never to the page. Open run confirms with a check and the word
"Opened" for about 1.6 seconds.

### The simulation

The sample run is not part of the control. `AgentRunSimulation` is a driver with no UI that plays an
`AgentRunScenario` on a timer: it lists the steps, ticks counts, waits for an approval or a failure for as long as it
takes, and applies Pause, Resume, Stop, Approve, Deny, Retry and Open run to its own state. Give one to
`AgentStatus.Simulation` and the pill shows it and routes its buttons back; read its `Status`, `Activity`, `Steps` and
`Notice` yourself to drive any other view.

```csharp
var simulation = new AgentRunSimulation(AgentStatusSamples.Research);
pill.Simulation = simulation;
simulation.Replay();                                   // clears the run and starts again after 0.5 s
simulation.Scenario = AgentStatusSamples.Coding;       // starts over after 0.9 s
```

The start delay is 0.9 seconds (`StartDelay`) and 0.5 seconds after `Replay()` (`ReplayDelay`). A finished or stopped run
stays as it is until the pill settles it. The timers run on a `TimeProvider`, so a test can step the run with a manual
clock; the pill takes its own `TimeProvider` property for the timer and the settle delay.

`AgentStatusSamples` has the two invented scenarios, their agents (`CodingAgent`, `ResearchAgent`) and two activities.
Build your own `AgentRunScenario` from `AgentRunScenarioStep`s: each has a present-tense label, a past-tense label, an
icon, a duration, an optional count, an optional approval gate and an optional failure on its first attempt.

### Narrow containers

The pill follows its container's width, not the window's, and never grows past it. Below 400px of available width the
inline Deny, Approve and Retry become 30px icon buttons with accessible names, the timer steps aside while they show, and
Open run in the panel becomes an icon button. A long label fades at its right edge, and the panel's step labels wrap
instead of being cut off.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.AgentStatusNarrowDemo">
    <!-- In a 340px column (under 400) the inline buttons become icon buttons and the timer steps aside; a long label
         fades at its right edge. Open the panel: it is as wide as the column and Open run is an icon button. -->
    <StackPanel Width="340" HorizontalAlignment="Center" Margin="0,0,0,330">
        <arc:AgentStatus x:Name="Pill" Status="NeedsInput" Actions="All" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class AgentStatusNarrowDemo : UserControl
{
    public AgentStatusNarrowDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Pill.Agent = AgentStatusSamples.CodingAgent;
        Pill.StartedAt = DateTimeOffset.UtcNow - TimeSpan.FromSeconds(42);
        Pill.Activity = new AgentStatusActivity("Waiting on you to deploy to staging", ArcIcons.Search);
        Pill.Steps.Add(new AgentStatusStep("scan", "Scanned 9 modules", AgentStatusStepState.Done, ArcIcons.Search) { Duration = TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(1917) });
        Pill.Steps.Add(new AgentStatusStep("patch", "Patched lib/dates/parse-due.ts", AgentStatusStepState.Done, ArcIcons.Search) { Duration = TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(2533) });
        Pill.Steps.Add(new AgentStatusStep("deploy", "Approval needed to deploy to staging", AgentStatusStepState.Waiting, ArcIcons.CloudUpload) { StartedAt = DateTimeOffset.UtcNow });
    }

```

### Reduced motion

Under reduced motion every state, text, focus and announcement stays. Widths and the panel change at once, a new label
fades in place without rolling, the ring does not spin, the dot does not ping, the check and the closed ring appear
drawn, and the working text does not shimmer.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.AgentStatusReducedMotionDemo">
    <!-- Under reduced motion every state, text, focus and announcement stays: widths and the panel change at once, labels
         fade in place, and the ring does not spin, ping or shimmer. -->
    <Grid Height="400">
        <arc:AgentStatus arc:ArcMotion.Level="Reduced" Margin="0,64,0,0" HorizontalAlignment="Center" />
    </Grid>
</UserControl>
```

### Content guidelines

Keep the pill's label short; the panel carries the history. Write the activity as what the agent is doing now ("Reading
12 files"), the request as a sentence that asks ("Waiting on you to deploy to staging"), the failure as what went wrong
("Fetch failed · 2 pages did not load"), and the outcome without a verb for the time ("5 files touched": the pill writes
"Done in 1m 12s · 5 files touched").

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| Processing | Checking specs |
| The agent is currently reading the files of the project | Reading 12 files |
| Waiting | Waiting on you to deploy to staging |
| Error | Fetch failed · 2 pages did not load |
| Run complete! All done successfully | 5 files touched |

### Best practices

**Do**

- Use `NeedsInput` for every approval gate (a command, a push, a payment, an email) and phrase the label as the request.
- Keep `StartedAt` fixed for the whole run and let the pill leave out paused and failed time.
- Pass only the actions your backend supports in `Actions`.
- Put the pill in a container that sets its width, such as a header slot, so it can fade long labels and size its panel.
- Give a mark its brand color through `AgentModel.MarkBrush`; a default mark is drawn in the text color.

**Avoid**

- Using it as a log. It lists the latest steps and drops the rest.
- Rewriting `Activity` for every count tick. Change only the count (`new AgentStatusActivity(label, icon, 9, 12)`): the
  digits change in place and screen readers are not interrupted.
- Putting a long sentence in the label. It fades out at the edge, and the full text is in the pill's accessible name.
- Several pills of the same run on one screen.

### Common questions

**Why does the panel not push the page down?** It floats in the window's overlay layer on top of the page, starting at
the pill's footprint. The pill keeps its place in the layout.

**Can a header with `ClipToBounds` hold the pill?** Yes. The collapsed pill is inside the header; the open panel is not.

**How do I show the timer for a run that already started?** Set `StartedAt` to the real start. The pill counts from there.

**What if I give `Status` and a `Simulation`?** The simulation drives the pill and `Status` is ignored.

**Why does a count not roll like a new activity?** Only a new label and icon roll. A count changes in place, so it can
tick several times a second.

## API reference

### AgentStatus

A compact live status pill for a running agent (Arc Agent status, design reference): the agent's mark inside a thin live ring, the current activity with a matching icon, and an elapsed timer in tabular figures. A new activity rolls in from below while the pill's width follows on a spring, and the label fades at its right edge while it is wider than its room. Pressing the pill opens it in place into a small floating panel with the latest steps (icon, text, duration), a segmented step progress bar and Pause, Stop and Open run; Escape or a press outside closes it and returns focus to the pill. It covers idle (Ready), working, needs input (an accent dot and inline Approve and Deny), paused, done (the ring closes and the mark becomes a drawn check, then it settles back to Ready), failed (with Retry) and stopped. Drive it from your agent's events: set `Status`, keep `Activity` to the latest tool call in the present tense, add `Steps`, give a fixed `StartedAt` (the timer leaves out paused and failed time itself) and handle the action events; `Actions` chooses which buttons are offered, the counterpart of showing a control only when its handler exists. With nothing set, or with a `Simulation`, it plays an invented sample run on its own.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Status` | `AgentStatusRunState` | `Idle` | Where the run is. Ignored while a `Simulation` drives the pill. |
| `Activity` | `AgentStatusActivity?` | `null` | What the agent does now, in the present tense. While input is needed it is the request ("Needs your approval to run a command"), when done it is the outcome that follows "Done in …", and after a failure it is the failure. |
| `StartedAt` | `DateTimeOffset?` | `null` | When the run started: the timer counts from here and leaves out time spent paused or failed. |
| `EndedAt` | `DateTimeOffset?` | `null` | When the run ended; by default the moment the status turned done or stopped. |
| `Agent` | `AgentModel?` | `null` | The agent and its mark (drawn at 12px inside the ring); null is a plain "Agent" with a default mark. |
| `SettleAfter` | `TimeSpan?` | `00:00:04` | How long after done or stopped the pill settles back to Ready (4 seconds); null keeps the result on screen. |
| `PanelAlignment` | `AgentStatusPanelAlignment` | `Center` | Which edge of the pill the panel grows from. |
| `IsExpanded` | `bool` | `false` | Whether the panel is open. Two-way: pressing the pill, Escape and a press outside change it. |
| `MaxSteps` | `int` | `5` | How many of the latest steps the panel lists (5); older ones slide out at the top. |
| `Notice` | `string?` | `null` | A one-off message for screen readers, such as the result of an action; it joins the status announcement. |
| `Actions` | `AgentStatusActions` | `All` | Which action buttons may show (all by default); a button also needs the right state. |
| `Labels` | `AgentStatusLabels` | – | The words and number formats; replace to translate or reword. |
| `Simulation` | `AgentRunSimulation?` | `null` | A simulated run that drives the pill (its status, activity, steps and times; its buttons are routed back to it). With no data set at all the pill plays the first sample run on its own. |
| `TimeProvider` | `TimeProvider` | – | The clock for the timer and the settle delay (the system clock by default; tests pass a manual one). |
| `Steps` | `AvaloniaList<AgentStatusStep>` | – | *Read-only.* The steps list: every step of the run, pending ones included, so the progress bar knows the total. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `PauseRequested` | `AgentStatusActionEventArgs` | Raised when Pause is pressed. |
| `ResumeRequested` | `AgentStatusActionEventArgs` | Raised when Resume is pressed. |
| `StopRequested` | `AgentStatusActionEventArgs` | Raised when Stop is pressed. |
| `ApproveRequested` | `AgentStatusActionEventArgs` | Raised when Approve is pressed. |
| `DenyRequested` | `AgentStatusActionEventArgs` | Raised when Deny is pressed. |
| `RetryRequested` | `AgentStatusActionEventArgs` | Raised when Retry is pressed. |
| `OpenRunRequested` | `AgentStatusActionEventArgs` | Raised when Open run is pressed. |
| `ExpandedChanged` | `AgentStatusExpandedChangedEventArgs` | Raised when the panel opens or closes. |
| `Settled` | `RoutedEventArgs` | Raised when a finished or stopped run settles back to Ready. |

Pseudo-classes: `:idle`, `:working`, `:needs-input`, `:paused`, `:done`, `:failed`, `:stopped`, `:expanded`, `:compact`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

### AgentStatusActivity

What an agent is doing now: a short present-tense label ("Reading 12 files"), an optional icon and an optional count that ticks in place ("8 of 12"). While input is needed the label is the request, when done it is the outcome that follows "Done in …", and after a failure it is the failure. Immutable: set a new instance to change it; a new label or icon rolls in, a changed count only changes its digits.

### AgentStatusStep

One step of an agent's run in an `AgentStatus`. List every step, pending ones included, so the progress bar knows the total; the panel lists the latest finished and running ones. Write a running step's label in the present tense and a finished one's in the past tense ("Running tests", then "Passed 12 of 12 tests"), so the words carry the state. Changes reach the screen at once (each property is observed).

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Id` | `string?` | `null` | A stable id for the step (keeps its row when the label changes). |
| `Label` | `string` | `""` | What the step does or did. |
| `Icon` | `Geometry?` | `null` | A 24 × 24 stroked glyph drawn at 16px before the label (a Lucide icon), or null. |
| `State` | `AgentStatusStepState` | `Pending` | Where the step is; pending steps only count in the progress bar. |
| `StartedAt` | `DateTimeOffset?` | `null` | When an active or waiting step started; its time counts in whole seconds from here, leaving out paused time. |
| `Duration` | `TimeSpan?` | `null` | How long a finished step took; shown with one decimal ("1.9s"). |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### AgentStatusLabels

Every word an `AgentStatus` shows or announces, in English by default. Replace the instance (or set its properties) to translate or reword; texts with numbers or names are functions so that the word order can change. The durations they receive are already formatted by `FormatTimer`, `FormatTotal` and the other format functions.

### AgentStatusActionEventArgs

Arguments of the action events of an `AgentStatus` (Pause, Resume, Stop, Approve, Deny, Retry, Open run).

Derives from `RoutedEventArgs`: every member of `RoutedEventArgs` works as well.

### AgentStatusExpandedChangedEventArgs

Arguments of `ExpandedChangedEvent`.

Derives from `RoutedEventArgs`: every member of `RoutedEventArgs` works as well.

### AgentRunSimulation

Plays an `AgentRunScenario` as a live run: after `StartDelay` of Ready it works through the steps on the scenario's timing, ticks counts in place, waits for as long as it takes on an approval or a failure, and reacts to Pause, Resume, Stop, Approve, Deny, Retry and Open run. Nothing runs for real: every action only changes this object's state and says so through `Notice`. It holds no UI: give it to `Simulation` (which copies its state into the pill and routes the pill's buttons back to it), or read its state yourself after each `Changed`. Timing uses the given `TimeProvider` (the system clock by default; tests pass a manual one), and its callbacks run on the synchronization context that created the simulation (the UI thread).

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Changed` | `EventHandler?` | Raised after every change of the state (a beat, an action, a restart). |

### AgentRunScenario

A scripted agent run for `AgentRunSimulation`: the agent, its steps with their timing, the outcome and the notices the simulation announces for each action. `AgentStatusSamples` has two invented runs. Data only.

### AgentRunScenarioStep

One step of an `AgentRunScenario`: its present- and past-tense labels, icon and active duration, an optional count that ticks in place, an optional approval gate before it runs and an optional failure on its first attempt.

### AgentStatusSamples

Two invented runs for `AgentRunSimulation` (the agents, file names and texts are made up). They keep the reference's rhythm: the coding run takes six steps of 1.9, 1.5, 2.5, 1.9 and 3.3 seconds (the fifth counting 12 specs in place) and then waits for an approval for as long as it takes; the research run takes five steps, and its third fails once after five of nine pages so Retry can be seen.

The enums:

| Type | Values |
|---|---|
| `AgentStatusRunState` | `Idle`, `Working`, `NeedsInput`, `Paused`, `Done`, `Failed`, `Stopped` |
| `AgentStatusStepState` | `Pending`, `Active`, `Waiting`, `Done`, `Failed`, `Skipped` |
| `AgentStatusActions` | `None`, `Pause`, `Resume`, `Stop`, `Approve`, `Deny`, `Retry`, `OpenRun`, `All` (flags) |
| `AgentStatusPanelAlignment` | `Start`, `Center` (default), `End` |

The agent is an `AgentModel` (name, a 24 by 24 stroked mark and its brush), shared with the other agent components.

## Accessibility

- The pill is a button with an expanded state. Its name reads the agent, the activity with its count and the elapsed
  time ("Juniper Code 3: Checking specs 8 of 12, 0:09 elapsed"); a finished run reads its result.
- A polite live region announces each new activity and each outcome ("Juniper Code 3: done in 14 seconds, 5 files
  touched"), and the result of an action through `Notice`. It does not speak counts or timer ticks.
- The open panel is a region named "{agent} run details"; the progress bar is a progress bar named "Run progress" with a
  value such as "4 of 6 steps finished".
- Status never relies on color: each state has a word (Ready, Paused, Done in, Stopped after) and a different ring or
  glyph; steps use the present tense while running and the past tense when finished.
- The icon buttons of narrow containers have accessible names. A truncated label stays complete in the pill's name and
  in the panel's step list.
- Keyboard focus shows a 2px ring, inset on the pill and outside the buttons; pointer focus draws none.
- Focus is kept: a button that changes role keeps focus, and when the focused control goes away focus moves to the pill.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` | Move to the pill, then to the inline Deny and Approve or Retry. With the panel open: Pause or Resume, Stop or Deny, Open run, then on to the next control in the page |
| `Enter` / `Space` on the pill | Open or close the panel |
| `Enter` / `Space` on a button | Press it |
| `Escape` | From anywhere inside the open panel, close it and return focus to the pill |

A press outside the open panel closes it and leaves focus where the press lands. The panel is not modal and does not trap
focus.

## Motion

- A new activity rolls in over 180ms from 12px below while the old one rolls out upward in 140ms; the pill's width
  follows on a spring without bounce and the label's right edge fades while it is wider than its room.
- The panel springs width and height together from the pill's footprint (about 0.75 s to settle); the content fades in
  after 80ms over 200ms and out in 75ms when it closes.
- The ring turns once every 0.9 s while working, freezes in place when paused and picks up from the same angle. When
  input is needed the arc leaves and the dot springs in with one 0.9 s ping. When a run ends the ring draws closed in
  0.44 s while the mark shrinks away and a check (or cross) draws itself in 0.28 s after a short beat.
- The working label carries a shimmer in a 2.4 s loop (1.7 s sweep, then a pause); the count and the active step's label
  shimmer with it.
- New steps fade in over 155ms, older ones slide up on the smooth spring, and the progress segments fill from the left
  over 480ms.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| New activity | Rolls and fades | Fades in 100ms in place | Replaced |
| Pill width and panel size | Springs | Instant | Instant |
| Ring, shimmer, ping | Animated | Still | Still |
| Done and failed | Ring and check draw | Shown drawn, short fade | Shown drawn |
| Timer and counts | Change in place | Change in place | Change in place |

## Related

- `ToolCall` for a single call in a transcript, with its input and output.
- `AgentPlan` for the steps an agent will take, editable before the run.
- `AgentTimeline` for a replay of several agents on one time axis.
- `TextShimmer` for a single shimmering word.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `AgentStatus` | One agent's run should be visible in a header and open on demand |
| `ToolCall` | You list calls in a transcript |
| `AgentPlan` | The user edits and approves the steps first |
| `AgentTimeline` | Several agents and handoffs share a time axis |
| `Alert` | You report a real job's state in text |

---

# Tool call

> A tool call row for an agent transcript: the tool, what it did and how it went, opening into the call's input and output, with approval and retry in place.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc.Special`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc.Special --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/tool-call

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ToolCallPreviewDemo">
    <!-- A small transcript around a group driven by a ToolCallSimulation: the question, the agent's opening sentence, the
         group, the streamed answer and Run again. The transcript is demo content; the group is the component. -->
    <StackPanel Spacing="20" MaxWidth="640">
        <Border HorizontalAlignment="Right"
                CornerRadius="18"
                Padding="16,8"
                Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource SurfaceMuted}">
            <TextBlock Text="What is holding up the March books close?" FontSize="16" />
        </Border>
        <StackPanel x:Name="Turn" Spacing="12">
            <TextBlock x:Name="Intro" FontSize="16" Opacity="0" />
            <arc:ToolCallGroup x:Name="Group" />
            <TextBlock x:Name="Answer" FontSize="16" TextWrapping="Wrap" IsVisible="False" />
            <arc:Button x:Name="Again"
                        Variant="Ghost"
                        Size="Small"
                        HorizontalAlignment="Left"
                        IsVisible="False"
                        Click="OnRunAgain">
                <StackPanel Orientation="Horizontal" Spacing="8">
                    <arc:ArcGlyph Data="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.RotateCcw}" Size="16" VerticalAlignment="Center" />
                    <TextBlock Text="Run again" VerticalAlignment="Center" />
                </StackPanel>
            </arc:Button>
        </StackPanel>
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;
using Avalonia.Threading;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

/// <summary>The default simulated turn: calls appear and run, one fails until Retry, one waits for Allow or Deny.</summary>
public partial class ToolCallPreviewDemo : UserControl
{
    private readonly ToolCallSimulation _simulation = new();
    private readonly DispatcherTimer _stream = new() { Interval = TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(40) };
    private string[] _chunks = [];
    private int _shown;

    public ToolCallPreviewDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Group.ItemsSource = _simulation.Items;
        _simulation.PropertyChanged += (_, e) =>
        {
            if (e.Property == ToolCallSimulation.IsWorkingProperty)
            {
                Group.IsActive = _simulation.IsWorking;
            }
        };
        _simulation.Changed += OnChanged;
        _stream.Tick += OnStream;
        AttachedToVisualTree += (_, _) => Start();
        DetachedFromVisualTree += (_, _) =>
        {
            _stream.Stop();
            _simulation.Stop();
        };
    }

    private void Start()
    {
        _stream.Stop();
        Answer.IsVisible = false;
        Answer.Text = null;
        Again.IsVisible = false;
        Group.ClearValue(ToolCallGroup.IsExpandedProperty);
        Intro.Text = "Let me look at what is holding up the close.";
        Intro.Opacity = 1;
        _simulation.Start();
    }

    private void OnChanged(object? sender, ToolCallSimulationEventArgs e)
    {
        if (e.Phase != ToolCallSimulationPhase.Finished)
        {
            return;
        }
        // The group folds 450ms after the last call; the answer starts streaming in once it has.
        _chunks = _simulation.WasDenied
            ? ["Two things hold up the March close: ", "the export bug #482 and ", "job 0112, which ", "has not finished on the replica. ", "I did not post to #finance-ops."]
            : ["Two things hold up the March close: ", "the export bug #482 and ", "job 0112, which ", "has not finished on the replica. ", "I posted a note in #finance-ops."];
        _shown = 0;
        DispatcherTimer.RunOnce(() =>
        {
            Answer.Text = string.Empty;
            Answer.IsVisible = true;
            _stream.Start();
        }, TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(950));
    }

    private void OnStream(object? sender, EventArgs e)
    {
        if (_shown < _chunks.Length)
        {
            Answer.Text += _chunks[_shown++];
            return;
        }
        _stream.Stop();
        Again.IsVisible = true;
    }

    private void OnRunAgain(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) => Start();
}
```

## When to use

`ToolCall` is one line of an agent transcript: the tool's mark, what the call did in plain words, quiet meta such as
"4 results · 1.2s" and a status icon. `ToolCallGroup` collects every call of one assistant turn under a header that
reads "Used 4 tools". A click opens a call into its input and output, so the transcript stays readable and the detail
stays one click away.

- **Showing what an agent did** inside a chat or an agent log, with the arguments and the result a click away.
- **Human in the loop**: a call that must be allowed or denied before it runs, such as posting a message or writing
  to a database, with Deny and Allow in the row.
- **Recoverable failures**: a timed out query shows its reason and a Retry button where it happened.
- **Debug and audit views** where people copy the exact input and output of a call.

## When not to use

- **A plan with steps and progress**: use `AgentPlan`; a tool call is one action, not a checklist.
- **One status for a whole run**: use `AgentStatus`; the group header only summarizes the calls it holds.
- **A queue of approvals across many runs**: build a list of your own; a row decides one call in its place.
- **The tools an agent may use**: that is configuration, not history.

## Usage

Give a row a `ToolCallItem`. Tools are data, not brands: a name for screen readers, a 24 × 24 stroked mark (a Lucide
glyph) and the phrases for each status. With no item the row shows a sample web search.

```xml
<arc:ToolCall>
    <arc:ToolCallItem Id="tickets" ToolName="Tracker"
                      ToolMark="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Inbox}" Status="Success"
                      Title="Searched tickets in finance/close" Summary="4 results" Duration="0:0:1.18" />
</arc:ToolCall>
```

On its own a row sits in a 1px Surface frame (radius 16, 4px in); inside a group it is flush with no frame.

For an agent turn, add the calls to a `ToolCallGroup` as the agent starts them and change them in place:

```csharp
var group = new ToolCallGroup();
group.Items.Add(call);                  // a new row grows in from zero height
call.Status = ToolCallStatus.Success;   // the row keeps its place and its open state
group.IsActive = agentIsWorking;        // keeps "Using" between calls
```

### Anatomy

1. **Row**: 40px high. The mark (16px), the title (one line, it truncates), the meta, the status icon and a chevron.
2. **Reason line**: under the title of a failed call (its reason) or a call waiting for approval (what allowing will
   do), 12px. A row with one is 58px high.
3. **Buttons**: Retry on a failed call, Deny and Allow on one waiting for approval, 28px high.
4. **Input and Output**: a mono key and value list, and the result as a list, a table, tinted JSON or text. Each has a
   copy button that confirms in place with a check for 1.9 seconds.
5. **Group header**: overlapping marks, one per tool, then "Using 3 tools", "Used 4 tools" or "Waiting for approval",
   and on the right "1 failed" or the total duration.

### Statuses

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"

             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ToolCallStatusesDemo">

    <StackPanel Spacing="12" MaxWidth="640">

        <arc:ToolCall>
            <arc:ToolCallItem Id="s" ToolName="Tracker" ToolMark="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Inbox}" Status="Success"

        </arc:ToolCall>
        <arc:ToolCall>
            <arc:ToolCallItem Id="e" ToolName="Warehouse" ToolMark="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Database}" Status="Error"

                              Message="Sends as Ledger bot to 36 people in #finance-ops" />
        </arc:ToolCall>

            <arc:ToolCallItem Id="d" ToolName="Chat" ToolMark="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.MessageCircle}" Status="Denied"

        </arc:ToolCall>
    </StackPanel>

```


Each status has its own icon shape, so color is never the only cue: a spinner (running), a check that draws itself
once (success), an alert (error), a shield with a question mark (approval) and a ban (denied). A running title
shimmers. An approval row sits on an accent outline over a faint accent tint. A denied row is muted and its meta reads
"Denied".

`ToolCallItem` carries a phrase per status: `Title` is the settled past tense ("Searched …"), `RunningTitle` the
present tense, `ApprovalTitle` a request ("Post a status note to …") and `ErrorTitle` the failure
("Could not read …"). A missing phrase falls back to `Title`.

### Outputs

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ToolCallOutputsDemo">
    <!-- The four output kinds, each open: a list, a table, JSON that folds after ten lines, and text. -->
    <StackPanel x:Name="Host" Spacing="12" MaxWidth="640" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class ToolCallOutputsDemo : UserControl
{
    public ToolCallOutputsDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        var list = ToolCallSamples.TicketSearch();
        var table = ToolCallSamples.JobLogQuery();
        var json = ToolCallSamples.ChecklistRead();
        var text = ToolCallSamples.StatusNote(ToolCallStatus.Success);
        foreach (var item in new[] { list, table, json, text })
        {
            Host.Children.Add(new ToolCall { Item = item, IsExpanded = true });
        }
    }
}
```

| Output | Looks like | Folds | Copy gives |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ToolCallListOutput` | A lead in mono digits, a title, a tag; 32px rows | After 5 rows | One line per entry |
| `ToolCallTableOutput` | Header and mono cells; 30px rows; scrolls sideways in its well | After 5 rows | Tab separated rows with the header |
| `ToolCallJsonOutput` | Indented JSON, keys, strings, numbers and literals tinted; 20px lines | After 10 lines | The JSON text |
| `ToolCallTextOutput` | One paragraph that keeps its line breaks | Never | The text |

JSON is built on `System.Text.Json.Nodes` and tinted by a small tokenizer of our own, so nothing uses reflection.
Folded content hides behind "Show 25 more lines", which turns into "Show less". When the summary is missing it is
derived from the output: "N results", "N rows", "N fields". `OutputTemplate` replaces the built-in view of a
successful call's result with your own.

### A group driven by your own data

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ToolCallOwnDataDemo">
    <!-- A group driven by your own data: the app handles Allow, Deny and Retry itself and moves the calls on. -->
    <StackPanel Spacing="16" MaxWidth="640">
        <arc:ToolCallGroup x:Name="Group"
                           ApproveRequested="OnApprove"
                           DenyRequested="OnDeny"
                           RetryRequested="OnRetry"
                           ExpandedChanged="OnExpanded" />
        <WrapPanel HorizontalAlignment="Left" ItemSpacing="12" LineSpacing="12">
            <arc:Button Content="Add a call" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Click="OnAdd" />
            <arc:Button Content="Start over" Variant="Ghost" Size="Small" Click="OnReset" />
        </WrapPanel>
        <TextBlock x:Name="Log"
                   FontSize="13"
                   TextWrapping="Wrap"
                   Text="Allow, Deny and Retry are logged here; the app decides what happens next."
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;
using Avalonia.Threading;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class ToolCallOwnDataDemo : UserControl
{
    private readonly List<string> _entries = new();
    private int _count;

    public ToolCallOwnDataDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Reset();
    }

    private void Reset()
    {
        Group.Items.Clear();
        _count = 0;
        Add(ToolCallStatus.Success);
        Add(ToolCallStatus.Error);
        Add(ToolCallStatus.Approval);
        Write("Started over.");
    }

    private void Add(ToolCallStatus status)
    {
        _count++;
        var item = new ToolCallItem($"call-{_count}", status == ToolCallStatus.Approval ? "Deploy" : "Build",
            status == ToolCallStatus.Approval ? "Rolled out build 42" : "Ran the unit tests", status,
            status == ToolCallStatus.Approval ? ArcIcons.Server : ArcIcons.Terminal)
        {
            RunningTitle = status == ToolCallStatus.Approval ? "Rolling out build 42" : "Running the unit tests",
            ApprovalTitle = "Roll out build 42 to production",
            ErrorTitle = "Unit tests failed",
            Message = status == ToolCallStatus.Approval ? "Replaces the running version for every customer" : "3 of 212 tests failed in checkout",
            Summary = "212 tests",
            Duration = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(8.4)
        };
        item.Input.Add(new ToolCallArgument("target", status == ToolCallStatus.Approval ? "production" : "all"));
        Group.Items.Add(item);
    }

    private void Write(string line)
    {
        _entries.Add(line);
        if (_entries.Count > 3)
        {
            _entries.RemoveAt(0);
        }
        Log.Text = string.Join("  ·  ", _entries);
    }

    private void Run(ToolCallItem item, ToolCallStatus to, int milliseconds)
    {
        item.Status = ToolCallStatus.Running;
        DispatcherTimer.RunOnce(() => item.Status = to, TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(milliseconds));
    }

    private void OnApprove(object? sender, ToolCallActionEventArgs e)
    {
        e.Handled = true;
        Write($"Allow: {e.Item.Id}");
        Run(e.Item, ToolCallStatus.Success, 1500);
    }

    private void OnDeny(object? sender, ToolCallActionEventArgs e)
    {
        e.Handled = true;
        Write($"Deny: {e.Item.Id}");
        e.Item.Status = ToolCallStatus.Denied;
    }

    private void OnRetry(object? sender, ToolCallActionEventArgs e)
    {
        e.Handled = true;
        Write($"Retry: {e.Item.Id}");
        Run(e.Item, ToolCallStatus.Success, 1200);
    }

    private void OnExpanded(object? sender, ToolCallExpandedChangedEventArgs e) =>
        Write(e.IsAutomatic ? $"Group {(e.IsExpanded ? "opened" : "folded")} by itself" : $"Group {(e.IsExpanded ? "opened" : "closed")}");

    private void OnAdd(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        Add(ToolCallStatus.Success);
        Write("Added a finished call");
    }

    private void OnReset(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) => Reset();
}
```

The group raises `ApproveRequested`, `DenyRequested` and `RetryRequested` (they bubble from the row, carrying the
item). Update the call yourself, usually to running and then to success, and set `Handled`. The control never changes
a status you drive.

When nobody handles an action, the control keeps a local behaviour so a page without wiring still works: **Deny**
marks the call denied; **Allow** and **Retry** only simulate a run, and only on the built-in sample data
(`ToolCallSamples`, `ToolCallSimulation`). On any other data nothing changes. A simulated run says so through the
row's live region ("This is sample data, so the call is only simulated.").

### Opening and folding

Opening the header staggers the rows in, 20ms apart, each settling 6px down. A call appended while the group is open
grows in from zero height instead. While the agent works the group stays open; 450ms after every call has finished
(`AutoCollapse`, `AutoCollapseDelay`) it folds itself away so the answer reads right under "Used 4 tools". Once the
person has opened or closed the group or a row, it never folds by itself. A call that needs a decision opens a folded
group. `ExpandedChanged` tells whether the change was automatic.

### The simulation

`ToolCallSimulation` plays a scripted turn into an observable list on a clock: calls are appended about 225ms apart,
run for their time and settle; a failing call waits for `Retry`; a call that needs approval waits for `Approve` or
`Deny`. Bind a group's `ItemsSource` to `Items` and `IsActive` to `IsWorking`. The default script is
`ToolCallSamples.Script()`; pass a `TimeProvider` to step it in tests. The transcript around the group in the preview
(the question, the sentence, the answer and Run again) is demo content, not part of the control.

```xml
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ToolCallNarrowDemo">

         indent. Under about 370px the meta goes. -->
```

### Reduced motion

At the Reduced and Off levels the stagger, the spinner, the shimmer travel and every spring stop: panels, rows and
statuses change at once. Labels, announcements, focus and all content stay.

### Content guidelines

- Write titles as verb phrases: past tense when settled ("Read the export job log"), present while running.
- Name the tool by what it is for ("Tracker", "Warehouse"). It is read before the title.
- A reason line says what went wrong or what allowing will do, in one sentence.
- Pick the output that reads best: a list for search hits, a table for rows, JSON for structured data, text for a
  sent message or a short log.

### Best practices

- Keep `Id` stable: a row keeps its open state while its status changes.
- Change items in place; add new calls to the end.
- Set `IsActive` while the agent works so the header does not flicker between "Using" and "Used".
- Use a Lucide glyph for each tool mark; the mark follows the text color unless you set `ToolMarkBrush`.

### Common questions

**Can I use a brand logo as the mark?** The mark is any 24 × 24 stroked geometry. Brand logos are yours to license;
the samples use Lucide glyphs only.

**Does Allow run the tool?** No. It raises `ApproveRequested`; your code runs the tool and updates the status.

**Why is the Output empty for a running call?** There is no result yet; the section says so.

## API reference

### ToolCall

One tool call of an agent transcript (Arc Tool call, design reference): the tool's mark, the call as a verb phrase, quiet meta ("4 results · 1.2s") and a status icon. The whole row is a button: it springs open into Input (the arguments as a mono key / value list) and Output (the result as a list, a table, tinted JSON or text, folding long ones behind "Show N more lines"), each with a copy button. A running call shimmers its title next to a spinner; a failed one shows its reason and Retry; one that waits for approval sits on an accent outline with Deny and Allow; a denied one is muted. Bind `Item` and change the item in place as the call moves on. Allow, Deny and Retry raise `ApproveRequested`, `DenyRequested` and `RetryRequested` (they bubble, so a `ToolCallGroup` or any parent can handle them): update the call's status yourself and set `Handled`. When nothing handles them, Deny marks the call denied here; Allow and Retry only simulate a run on the built-in sample data (`ToolCallSamples`) and change nothing otherwise. With no item the row shows a sample web search. On its own the row sits in a 1px bordered Surface frame (radius 16, 4px in); inside a group it is flush.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Item` | `ToolCallItem?` | `null` | The call shown. Change it in place; the row follows every change. Null shows a sample web search. |
| `IsExpanded` | `bool` | `false` | Whether Input and Output are open (two-way). |
| `IsFlush` | `bool` | `false` | Drops the row's own frame (a group sets it on its rows). |
| `Labels` | `ToolCallLabels` | – | Every word the row shows or says. |
| `OutputTemplate` | `IDataTemplate?` | `null` | Draws a successful call's result in the Output well (a chart, a file preview); a template that does not match the item, or builds nothing, falls back to the built-in view. It receives the `ToolCallItem`. |
| `DisplayedItem` | `ToolCallItem` | – | *Read-only.* The call on screen: `Item`, or the sample when it is null. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ApproveRequested` | `ToolCallActionEventArgs` | Raised when the person presses Allow on a call waiting for approval. Bubbles. |
| `DenyRequested` | `ToolCallActionEventArgs` | Raised when the person presses Deny on a call waiting for approval. Bubbles. |
| `RetryRequested` | `ToolCallActionEventArgs` | Raised when the person presses Retry on a failed call. Bubbles. |
| `ExpandedChanged` | `ToolCallExpandedChangedEventArgs` | Raised when Input and Output open or close. |

Pseudo-classes: `:running`, `:success`, `:error`, `:approval`, `:denied`, `:expanded`, `:compact`, `:tight`, `:flush`, `:head-hover`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

### ToolCallGroup

Every tool call of one assistant turn in one quiet card (Arc Tool call group, design reference): a header with the tools' overlapping marks, "Used 4 tools" (or "Using 3 tools" with a shimmer while the agent works, or "Waiting for approval") and, on the right, "1 failed" or the total duration; below it, one `ToolCall` row per call. Append calls to `Items` (or an observable `ItemsSource`) as the agent starts them and change them in place: a new row grows in from zero height, a new tool's mark joins the stack on a spring. Opening the header staggers the rows in. While the agent works the group stays open; 450ms after every call finished it folds itself away (`AutoCollapse`) unless the person opened or closed the group or a row. A call that needs a decision (a failure, an approval) opens a folded group. An empty group takes no space; its first call grows it in. With neither `Items` nor `ItemsSource` it shows four finished sample calls. Allow, Deny and Retry bubble up from the rows as `ApproveRequested`, `DenyRequested` and `RetryRequested`; see `ToolCall` for what happens when nothing handles them.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ItemsSource` | `IEnumerable<ToolCallItem>?` | `null` | An observable list of calls that wins over `Items`. |
| `IsActive` | `bool?` | `null` | Whether the agent is still working in this turn, so the header keeps saying "Using" between calls; null (default) means "while any call runs". |
| `IsExpanded` | `bool` | `false` | Whether the list is open (two-way). Until it is set, the group opens while any call runs, waits or failed, and a finished transcript starts folded. |
| `AutoCollapse` | `bool` | `true` | Folds the list `AutoCollapseDelay` after every call finished, so the answer reads right under "Used 4 tools"; skipped once the person opened or closed the group or any row. |
| `AutoCollapseDelay` | `TimeSpan` | `00:00:00.4500000` | The wait before the group folds itself (450ms). |
| `Labels` | `ToolCallLabels` | – | Every word the group and its rows show or say. |
| `OutputTemplate` | `IDataTemplate?` | `null` | A custom result view for every successful call (see `OutputTemplate`). |
| `TotalDuration` | `TimeSpan` | – | *Read-only.* The sum of the successful calls' durations (shown once nothing runs or waits). |
| `FailedCount` | `int` | – | *Read-only.* The number of failed calls. |
| `HeaderText` | `string` | – | *Read-only.* The header as read: the label and the meta ("Used 3 tools 1 failed"). |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ExpandedChanged` | `ToolCallExpandedChangedEventArgs` | Raised when the list opens or closes, by the person, the app or the group itself (see `IsAutomatic`). |
| `ApproveRequested` | `ToolCallActionEventArgs` | Raised when a row's Allow is pressed (it bubbles from the row). |
| `DenyRequested` | `ToolCallActionEventArgs` | Raised when a row's Deny is pressed (it bubbles from the row). |
| `RetryRequested` | `ToolCallActionEventArgs` | Raised when a row's Retry is pressed (it bubbles from the row). |

Pseudo-classes: `:expanded`, `:active`, `:waiting`, `:failed`, `:empty`, `:head-hover`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

### ToolCallItem

One tool call of an agent turn: which tool ran, what it did in plain words, how it went, its arguments and what came back. Change `Status` (and the other properties) in place as the call moves on: a row keeps its place and its open state, and every change reaches the screen. Keep `Id` stable.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Id` | `string` | `""` | A stable id. A group keys its rows by it, so a call whose status changes keeps its row. |
| `ToolName` | `string` | `""` | The tool's name, read before the title by screen readers ("Search: Searched the web …"). |
| `ToolMark` | `Geometry?` | `null` | The tool's mark: a 24 × 24 stroked glyph such as a Lucide icon, drawn at 16px in the row and 12px in a group's mark stack. Null draws a wrench. |
| `ToolMarkBrush` | `IBrush?` | `null` | The mark's color; null uses the text color, which follows the theme. |
| `Title` | `string` | `""` | The settled verb phrase in the past tense, such as "Searched tickets in finance/close". One line; it truncates. |
| `RunningTitle` | `string?` | `null` | The phrase while running, in the present tense ("Searching tickets in finance/close"); null uses `Title`. |
| `ApprovalTitle` | `string?` | `null` | The phrase while waiting for approval, as a request ("Post a status note to #finance-ops"); null uses `Title`. |
| `ErrorTitle` | `string?` | `null` | The phrase after a failure ("Could not read the export job log"); null uses `Title`. |
| `Status` | `ToolCallStatus` | `Success` | Where the call stands. Change it in place as the call runs, fails, waits or finishes. |
| `Output` | `ToolCallOutput?` | `null` | What came back: a list, a table, JSON or text. Shown under Output once the call succeeded. |
| `Summary` | `string?` | `null` | Quiet meta before the duration, such as "4 results". Null derives it from `Output` (results, rows, fields, items). |
| `Message` | `string?` | `null` | One line under the title while the call failed (the reason) or waits for approval (what allowing will do). Not shown in the other statuses. |
| `Duration` | `TimeSpan?` | `null` | How long the call took, shown as "760ms" or "1.2s"; a group adds up the successful ones. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### ToolCallArgument

One argument of a tool call, shown as a key and a value in the call's mono Input list.

### ToolCallOutput

What a tool call returned, shown under Output once the call succeeded: a `ToolCallListOutput`, a `ToolCallTableOutput`, a `ToolCallJsonOutput` or a `ToolCallTextOutput`. Assign a new output to change what a row shows; an output is read when the row opens.

### ToolCallListOutput

A list result (search hits, tickets): a lead, a title and a tag per row, 32px rows, folding after five.

### ToolCallListEntry

One entry of a `ToolCallListOutput`: a short mono lead (an id such as "#482"), a title and a tag.

### ToolCallTableOutput

A table result (database rows): column headers and mono cells, 30px rows, folding after five rows. A null cell reads "null". A wide table scrolls inside its well.

### ToolCallJsonOutput

A JSON result (an API response): indented two spaces, tinted (keys, strings, numbers, literals and punctuation in their own colors), 20px lines, folding after ten lines behind "Show N more lines". Wide lines scroll inside the well. Built on `Nodes`, so no reflection is involved.

### ToolCallTextOutput

A text result (a sent message, a short log): one paragraph that keeps its line breaks.

### ToolCallLabels

Every word `ToolCall` and `ToolCallGroup` show or say, in English by default. Replace the whole object to localize or reword; sentences with numbers or names are format functions.

### ToolCallSimulation

Plays a scripted agent turn into `Items` on a clock: calls are appended one after another, run for their time and settle; a failing call waits for `Retry` and a call that needs approval waits for `Approve` or `Deny`. Bind a `ToolCallGroup`'s `ItemsSource` to `Items` and its `IsActive` to `IsWorking`: Allow, Deny and Retry on the group's rows reach the simulation when nothing else handles them. The default script is `Script`. Time comes from a `TimeProvider`, so tests can step it; callbacks run on the UI thread.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `State` | `ToolCallSimulationState` | – | *Read-only.* Where the run stands. |
| `IsWorking` | `bool` | – | *Read-only.* Whether the agent is working (appending or running calls): bind a group's `IsActive` to it, so its header keeps saying "Using" between calls. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Changed` | `ToolCallSimulationEventArgs` | Raised on the UI thread at every beat of the run (a call appended, settled, failed, retried, allowed, denied; the start and the end). |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### ToolCallSimulationStep

One scripted call of a `ToolCallSimulation`.

### ToolCallActionEventArgs

Data of `ApproveRequested`, `DenyRequested` and `RetryRequested`: the call the person acted on. Set `Handled` when you update the call yourself.

Derives from `RoutedEventArgs`: every member of `RoutedEventArgs` works as well.

### ToolCallExpandedChangedEventArgs

Data of `ExpandedChanged` and `ExpandedChanged`.

Derives from `RoutedEventArgs`: every member of `RoutedEventArgs` works as well.

### ToolCallSimulationEventArgs

Data of `Changed`.

Derives from `EventArgs`: every member of `EventArgs` works as well.

The enums:

| Type | Values |
|---|---|
| `ToolCallStatus` | `Running`, `Success`, `Error`, `Approval`, `Denied` |
| `ToolCallSimulationOutcome` | `Succeeds`, `FailsUntilRetried`, `NeedsApproval` |
| `ToolCallSimulationState` | `Idle`, `Working`, `WaitingForRetry`, `WaitingForApproval`, `Finished` |
| `ToolCallSimulationPhase` | `Started`, `CallAppended`, `CallSucceeded`, `CallFailed`, `WaitingForApproval`, `Retried`, `Allowed`, `Denied`, `Finished` |

`ToolCallSamples` holds the invented sample calls and the default script.

## Accessibility

- The group header and every row are buttons that report whether they are expanded. A row's name reads the tool, the
  phrase and the status: "Tracker: Searched tickets in finance/close Done, 4 results, 1.2s".
- Status is never color alone: each status has its own icon, failed and waiting calls show a reason line, and the name
  spells the status out.
- Each row announces status changes through a polite live region, including that a sample call is only simulated.
- Retry, Allow and Deny are named with the call they act on: "Allow: Post a status note to #finance-ops". When a
  button goes away focus moves to its row instead of dropping to the page.
- Input and Output are named groups; the copy buttons confirm through the live region without changing width.
- Pointer focus draws no ring; keyboard focus shows a 2px ring inside the row so it is never clipped.
- Every word is in `ToolCallLabels`.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab | Moves through the group header, each row, a row's Retry, Deny or Allow, and in an open row its copy buttons and the fold button |
| Enter, Space | Opens or closes the group or a row; on a button, presses it |

## Motion

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| Opening a row or the group | Height springs, content fades over 160ms | At once | At once |
| Rows when the group opens | Stagger 20ms apart, settle 6px | None | None |
| A row appended to an open group | Grows from zero height | At once | At once |
| Status icon | Scale and fade swap; the check draws over 330ms | At once | At once |
| Running title and "Using 3 tools" | Shimmer, one pass each 1.8s | Still | Still |
| Title or header text change | Rises from a soft blur over 240ms | Fades over 130ms | At once |
| A new tool mark in the header | Widens on a spring | At once | At once |
| Chevron | Turns on a spring | At once | At once |
| Approval outline | Fades over 240ms | At once | At once |

## Related

- `AgentStatus` for the live status of a whole run.
- `AgentPlan` for the plan an agent writes before it acts.
- `AgentTimeline` for a replay of a multi-agent run on one time axis.
