# Agent plan

> An agent's plan as an editable checklist: reorder, rename and add steps while it is a draft, then follow the run step by step once it is approved.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc.Special`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc.Special --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/agent-plan

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.AgentPlanPreviewDemo">
    <!-- No steps and no status: the plan shows the invented sample draft and runs the built-in simulation. -->
    <arc:AgentPlan MaxWidth="560" />
</UserControl>
```

## When to use

`AgentPlan` is the card an agent shows between "here is what I will do" and "done". While it is a draft, a person
reads the steps and fixes them: renames a title in place, drags a step to another position, removes one, adds one, or
asks the agent for one more. Approving it locks the plan, and the same card turns into a live checklist that follows
the agent through each step, with the time it took, a place for activity lines, and a decision to make when a step
fails.

- **Plan mode for a coding or operations agent**: the agent proposes the steps, a person edits and approves them, and
  the card tracks the work. Nothing runs before the approval.
- **A side panel or a chat message that tracks a multi-step task**: one current step, finished steps that settle back
  to quiet text, and a footer that ends with the total time and a one-line summary.
- **Work that can fail halfway**: a failed step stops the run and shows its reason with Retry and Skip, instead of
  hiding the failure in a log.
- **Trying the whole journey in a page or a demo**: with no data and no status the card plays an invented plan on a
  built-in simulation, so every state can be seen without an agent.

## When not to use

- **A transcript of everything the agent did**: use `ChatThread` or a log view. The plan is a short ordered list of
  intentions, not a record of tool calls and their output.
- **Approving single risky actions one at a time**: a plan is approved once, up front. Ask for each action in its own
  prompt when the person should decide case by case.
- **Independent tasks across several agents**: this is one ordered plan. Use a task list for a queue.
- **An onboarding checklist**: the steps here are an agent's, they cannot be ticked off by the person, and they only
  move forward as the agent works.
- **Reporting the state of one job**: use `Alert`, `Badge` or a table. A plan with a single step says little.

## Usage

With no `Steps` and no `Status`, the card shows an invented draft (adding full-text search to a help center) and runs
the built-in simulation when it is approved.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:AgentPlan MaxWidth="560" />
</UserControl>
```

`AgentPlan` derives from Avalonia's `TemplatedControl` and lives in the Special package; register it with
`UseArcSpecial()` next to `UseArcControls()`. The card is as wide as its container up to 560px, reads well from about 320px,
and tightens below 420px.

### Anatomy

1. **Header**: the model's mark, "Plan · 6 steps" (the number rolls when steps are added or removed) and the goal under
   it. The model's name sits on the right while the plan is a draft; once it runs, the right side counts "3 of 6".
2. **Progress line**: a 2px line on the header's bottom rule that grows with the finished steps. It is hidden in a draft.
3. **Steps**: a numbered list. Every row has a fixed lead column (the grip, later the status mark), the title, and a
   fixed trail column (the remove button, later the time or the word Skipped). The columns do not change when the plan
   is approved, so titles wrap the same way and never move.
4. **Add step**, and while the list is empty a sentence saying so.
5. **Footer**: Keep planning and Approve plan in a draft; the status and Pause or Resume while running; the total time,
   the summary and Start over when it is done.

The six status marks each have their own shape, so state never rests on color alone: an empty ring (pending), a ring
with a quarter arc that turns once every 800ms (in progress), a ring with two bars (paused), a green disc with a check
that draws itself (done), a red disc with an exclamation mark (failed) and a dashed ring (skipped).

### Editing a draft

Every step title is a text area that grows with its text.

- **Enter** saves the rename and keeps the focus. **Escape** undoes the edits since the field got the focus (or since the
  last Enter). Leaving the field saves it.
- **Backspace** in an empty title removes the step and puts the caret at the end of the step above; in the first step the
  caret goes to the start of the next one. Leaving a field you emptied removes the step too.
- **Alt+Up** and **Alt+Down** in a title move the step one place; the caret stays where it was.
- The grip moves a step with the pointer: the row lifts, follows the pointer and swaps with a neighbour once it has
  passed half that neighbour's height; letting go settles it. Focus the grip and press **Up** or **Down** to move it
  without a pointer.
- The remove button shows while the row is hovered or holds the focus.
- **Add step** appends an empty step with its title focused. With no steps left, Approve plan is disabled; Keep planning
  still works.

Approving trims the titles and drops empty steps. Keep planning asks the agent for one more step: a spinner shows in the
button, then the suggestion is inserted before the last step and its title streams in a few words at a time. When it has
finished it is an ordinary editable step with a "Suggested" note.

### A controlled plan

Set `Status` and the plan is controlled: the control never changes the status, and never touches a step's state,
activity lines, error or time. Every action is reported through an event, and you update the data.

| Event | When | You usually |
|---|---|---|
| `Approved` | Approve plan, with the steps in order, trimmed and without empty ones | Start the agent, set `Status` to Running |
| `Changed` | A draft edit: rename, move, remove, add or a streamed suggestion (`Kind`) | Keep your copy of the draft in step |
| `KeepPlanningRequested` | Keep planning | Set `IsPlanning`, ask the agent, call `StreamSuggestion` |
| `PauseChanged` | Pause (true) or Resume (false) | Pause the agent, set `Status` to Paused or Running |
| `StepAction` | Retry or Skip on a failed step (`Kind`, `Step`) | Run the step again or move on, and update its state |
| `StartOverRequested` | Start over after Done | Reset the steps, set `Status` back to Draft |

Draft edits are made in `Steps` itself (the control renames, moves, removes and adds there) and reported through
`Changed`; only the run is yours.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.AgentPlanControlledDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="16">
        <!-- Status is set, so the plan only reports: this demo plays the agent in its code-behind. -->
        <arc:AgentPlan x:Name="Plan"
                       MaxWidth="560"
                       Status="Draft"
                       Goal="Move the changelog to its own page"
                       Approved="OnApproved"
                       Changed="OnChanged"
                       StepAction="OnStepAction"
                       KeepPlanningRequested="OnKeepPlanning"
                       PauseChanged="OnPauseChanged"
                       StartOverRequested="OnStartOver" />
        <TextBlock x:Name="Log"
                   MaxWidth="560"
                   TextWrapping="Wrap"
                   FontSize="13"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}"
                   Text="Every action of the plan is logged here." />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Threading;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

/// <summary>A plan driven by the host: the demo is the agent. It works through the approved steps, fails the second one once, and answers every event.</summary>
public partial class AgentPlanControlledDemo : UserControl
{
    private static readonly string[] s_activities =
    [
        "Read 3 files", "Edited 2 files", "Ran 4 tests"
    ];

    private readonly List<string> _entries = new();
    private readonly DispatcherTimer _timer = new() { Interval = TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(900) };
    private int _current = -1;
    private int _line;
    private bool _failedOnce;
    private bool _paused;
    private int _suggestions;

    public AgentPlanControlledDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Reset();
        _timer.Tick += (_, _) => Tick();
    }

    private void Reset()
    {
        _timer.Stop();
        _current = -1;
        _line = 0;
        _failedOnce = false;
        _paused = false;
        _suggestions = 0;
        Plan.Steps.Clear();
        foreach (var title in new[]
                 {
                     "List the pages that link to the changelog",
                     "Create a page that reads the release notes",
                     "Redirect the old changelog address",
                     "Update the sitemap and the footer links"
                 })
        {
            Plan.Steps.Add(new AgentPlanStep(null, title));
        }
        Plan.Model = new AgentModel("Ember 1", ArcIcons.Sparkles);
        Plan.CanKeepPlanning = true;
        Plan.IsPlanning = false;
    }

    private void Write(string text)
    {
        _entries.Add(text);
        if (_entries.Count > 5)
        {
            _entries.RemoveAt(0);
        }
        Log.Text = string.Join("\n", _entries);
    }

    private void OnApproved(object? sender, AgentPlanApprovedEventArgs e)
    {
        Write($"Approved {e.Steps.Count} steps");
        foreach (var step in Plan.Steps)
        {
            step.State = AgentPlanStepState.Pending;
        }
        Plan.Status = AgentPlanStatus.Running;
        _current = -1;
        _timer.Start();
    }

    private void OnChanged(object? sender, AgentPlanChangedEventArgs e) => Write($"Changed: {e.Kind} ({e.Steps.Count} steps)");

    private void OnKeepPlanning(object? sender, Avalonia.Interactivity.RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        Write("Keep planning requested");
        if (_suggestions >= 2)
        {
            Plan.CanKeepPlanning = false;
            return;
        }
        Plan.IsPlanning = true;
        DispatcherTimer.RunOnce(() =>
        {
            Plan.IsPlanning = false;
            Plan.StreamSuggestion(new AgentPlanStep(null, _suggestions++ == 0
                ? "Add a feed for the release notes"
                : "Check every link on the new page"));
            Plan.CanKeepPlanning = _suggestions < 2;
        }, TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(700));
    }

    private void OnPauseChanged(object? sender, AgentPlanPauseChangedEventArgs e)
    {
        Write(e.IsPaused ? "Paused" : "Resumed");
        _paused = e.IsPaused;
        Plan.Status = e.IsPaused ? AgentPlanStatus.Paused : AgentPlanStatus.Running;
        if (e.IsPaused)
        {
            _timer.Stop();
        }
        else if (Plan.Steps.Any(s => s.State != AgentPlanStepState.Failed))
        {
            _timer.Start();
        }
    }

    private void OnStepAction(object? sender, AgentPlanStepActionEventArgs e)
    {
        Write($"{e.Kind}: {e.Step.Title}");
        if (e.Kind == AgentPlanStepActionKind.Retry)
        {
            e.Step.Error = null;
            e.Step.State = AgentPlanStepState.Active;
            _line = e.Step.Activities.Count;
        }
        else
        {
            e.Step.State = AgentPlanStepState.Skipped;
        }
        _timer.Start();
    }

    private void OnStartOver(object? sender, Avalonia.Interactivity.RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        Write("Start over");
        Reset();
        Plan.Status = AgentPlanStatus.Draft;
    }

    private void Tick()
    {
        if (_paused)
        {
            return;
        }
        var steps = Plan.Steps;
        if (_current < 0 || steps[_current].State is AgentPlanStepState.Done or AgentPlanStepState.Skipped)
        {
            _current = steps.ToList().FindIndex(s => s.State == AgentPlanStepState.Pending);
            if (_current < 0)
            {
                _timer.Stop();
                Plan.Summary = "The changelog now has its own page, and the old address redirects to it.";
                Plan.Status = AgentPlanStatus.Done;
                return;
            }
            steps[_current].State = AgentPlanStepState.Active;
            _line = 0;
            return;
        }
        var step = steps[_current];
        if (_line < s_activities.Length)
        {
            step.Activities.Add(s_activities[_line++]);
            return;
        }
        if (_current == 1 && !_failedOnce)
        {
            _failedOnce = true;
            _timer.Stop();
            step.Error = "The page did not build: a release note has no date";
            step.State = AgentPlanStepState.Failed;
            return;
        }
        step.Duration = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(12 + _current * 7);
        step.State = AgentPlanStepState.Done;
    }
}
```

```csharp
plan.Approved += (_, e) =>
{
    foreach (var step in plan.Steps) { step.State = AgentPlanStepState.Pending; }
    plan.Status = AgentPlanStatus.Running;
    agent.Start(e.Steps);
};
plan.StepAction += (_, e) => agent.Decide(e.Step, e.Kind);
```

While the agent works, change the steps and the control follows: set one step to `Active` at a time, append to its
`Activities` as it reports them, then set `Done` with a `Duration`. For a failure set `Error` first, then `Failed`, so the
announcement can read the reason. Insert a step with `NoteKind = AddedByAgent` where it belongs and it slides in with a
faint accent wash. Set `Summary` before the status becomes Done; it streams in after "Done in …".

### A plan in the middle of its run

The same data drives a plan that is already running. This one has two finished steps, a step the agent added, and a
failed step waiting for a decision.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.AgentPlanMidRunDemo">
    <!-- A plan already running: two steps done, one added by the agent, one failed and waiting for a decision. -->
    <arc:AgentPlan x:Name="Plan"
                   MaxWidth="560"
                   Status="Running"
                   Goal="Speed up the nightly build"
                   StepAction="OnStepAction" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

/// <summary>A running plan built from plain data: Retry puts the failed step back to work, Skip leaves it.</summary>
public partial class AgentPlanMidRunDemo : UserControl
{
    public AgentPlanMidRunDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Plan.Model = new AgentModel("Ember 1", ArcIcons.Sparkles);
        Plan.Steps.Add(Finished("Find the slowest ten tasks", 18, "Ran the build with timing", "Found 4 tasks over a minute"));
        Plan.Steps.Add(Finished("Cache the generated sources", 41, "Edited build/cache.json", "Ran 12 tests"));
        var added = Finished("Skip the cache when the lockfile changes", 25, "Edited build/cache.json");
        added.NoteKind = AgentPlanNoteKind.AddedByAgent;
        Plan.Steps.Add(added);
        var failed = new AgentPlanStep(null, "Run the full build and compare the time")
        {
            State = AgentPlanStepState.Failed,
            Error = "The build ran out of disk space on the runner"
        };
        failed.Activities.Add("Ran the build");
        failed.Activities.Add("Measured 3 minutes 10 seconds");
        Plan.Steps.Add(failed);
        Plan.Steps.Add(new AgentPlanStep(null, "Write the result into the contributor guide"));
    }

    private static AgentPlanStep Finished(string title, int seconds, params string[] lines)
    {
        var step = new AgentPlanStep(null, title) { State = AgentPlanStepState.Done, Duration = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(seconds) };
        foreach (var line in lines)
        {
            step.Activities.Add(line);
        }
        return step;
    }

    private void OnStepAction(object? sender, AgentPlanStepActionEventArgs e)
    {
        if (e.Kind == AgentPlanStepActionKind.Retry)
        {
            e.Step.Error = null;
            e.Step.State = AgentPlanStepState.Active;
        }
        else
        {
            e.Step.State = AgentPlanStepState.Skipped;
            Plan.Steps[^1].State = AgentPlanStepState.Active;
        }
    }
}
```

A failed step shows the word Failed, its reason, and Retry and Skip. The footer says which step failed and the Pause
button steps aside. Keyboard focus moves to Retry (it would otherwise fall to the page when Pause disappears); after
Retry or Skip it goes back to Pause.

### The simulation

`AgentPlanSimulation` is the built-in agent that runs when `Status` is null. It is event-driven: one timer waits per
state change, nothing runs while the plan is idle, Pause keeps the time that was left and Resume continues from there.
It answers the same buttons a host would. Its beats follow the measured journey (at 1× speed):

| Beat | Time |
|---|---|
| Approve plan → the first step starts | 280ms |
| Step starts → its first activity line | 372ms |
| Between activity lines | 540ms |
| Last line → step done | 470ms |
| Step done → the next one starts | 290ms |
| Last step done → plan done | 420ms |
| Retry → first new line, then 577ms, then 465ms → done | 555ms |
| Skip → the next step starts | 277ms |

In the sample the agent inserts a step after the third step's second line (417ms later) and the test step fails once
after its last line, then waits for Retry or Skip for as long as it takes. A step that has no script (one you added) runs
`GenericScript`: three activity lines and 30 seconds. Scripts are found by step id, so a renamed step keeps its script and
a removed one is skipped. Start over returns to the draft the run started from, with every suggestion available again.

Give the simulation your own steps, suggestions and summary to demo another journey:

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.AgentPlanLabelsDemo">
    <arc:AgentPlan x:Name="Plan" MaxWidth="560" Goal="Rename the settings page" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

/// <summary>The plan's words replaced: a terser vocabulary, a different note and different state words.</summary>
public partial class AgentPlanLabelsDemo : UserControl
{
    public AgentPlanLabelsDemo()

        InitializeComponent();
```

### Times and counts

A step time shows whole seconds under a minute ("23s") and minutes with two-digit seconds from a minute on ("1m 07s").
The total is the sum of the done steps' times, so skipped and failed steps add nothing. The header counts "{n} of {count}"
where n is the first step that is not done or skipped, and the progress line is done and skipped steps over all steps.
Counts roll in a reserved width with tabular digits, so a changing number never nudges the words around it.

### Narrow containers

Below 420px the header, list and footer tighten, and the draft's two buttons share the row equally. Titles wrap to as many
lines as they need; the columns stay.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.AgentPlanNarrowDemo">
    <!-- In a 360px column the padding tightens, long titles wrap and the draft's two buttons share the row. -->
    <arc:AgentPlan Width="360" HorizontalAlignment="Center" />
</UserControl>
```

### Reduced motion

Reduced and off motion keep every state, label, focus move and announcement, and drop everything that travels: rows,
activity lines, the failure block and the footer change height at once, the arc does not turn, the check appears
complete, the shimmer rests, an inserted step gets no wash and a suggestion's words appear together. The simulation runs
the same timeline.

### Content guidelines

Write titles as instructions of about 6 to 10 words, and activity lines as short past-tense phrases that start with a
verb the plan knows (`AgentPlanActivityIcons`): Read, Searched, Found, Created, Edited, Ran or Measured. Register more
verbs with `AgentPlanActivityIcons.Set`.

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| Step 1 | Find every link to the old settings page |
| Doing the search | Searched for /settings |
| Tests | Ran 6 tests |
| Something went wrong | 3 of 14 tests failed: typo matching skips two-letter words |
| Finished! | The page now lives at /preferences, and the old address redirects. |

### Best practices

**Do**

- Keep a plan to four to eight steps. A longer plan is a project; split it.
- Show the reason of a failure in the agent's own words and offer Retry and Skip, so the person can decide.
- Pass a model with its own mark so the agent's notes read as the agent's.
- Keep `Id` stable when you rename or reorder; the simulation, announcements and your own logs rely on it.

**Avoid**

- Changing `Status` back and forth while someone is editing a draft.
- Using the plan as a log. Activity lines are a handful of short facts per step, and fold away when the step is done.
- Brand marks for the model. Use a generic glyph and name the model in text.

### Common questions

**Does the plan run anything?** No. It shows a plan and, with no `Status`, plays an invented simulation. Real work is
yours: answer `Approved` and update the steps.

**How do I show a step the agent added?** Insert an `AgentPlanStep` with `NoteKind = AgentPlanNoteKind.AddedByAgent`
while the plan runs. It slides in, gets a wash and a note, and is announced.

**Can people edit while it runs?** No. Rows are fixed once the plan is approved; the only controls are Pause or Resume,
Retry and Skip on a failure, and Start over at the end.

**What if I have no model?** Leave `Model` null (with your own steps): the header shows no mark and no name.

**Why is Approve plan disabled?** The draft has no steps. Add one, or let the agent keep planning.

## API reference

### AgentPlan

The plan an agent writes before it acts, then works through as a live checklist (Arc Agent plan, design reference). A header shows the model's mark, "Plan · 6 steps" (the number rolls) and the goal. While `CurrentStatus` is `Draft` every step can be renamed in place (Enter saves, Escape undoes, Backspace in an empty title removes the step), dragged by its grip or moved with Alt and the arrow keys, removed or added to; Keep planning asks the agent for one more step, which streams in before the last one. Approve plan locks the plan: the grips become status marks, the header counts "3 of 6" over a thin progress line, the current step shimmers beside a spinning arc with its activity lines underneath, a finished step draws its check and settles to secondary text with its time, the agent can insert a step (a faint accent wash), a failed step offers Retry and Skip, the run can be paused, and the footer ends with the total time, a streamed one-line summary and Start over.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Steps` | `AvaloniaList<AgentPlanStep>` | `null` | Defines the `Steps` property. |
| `Status` | `AgentPlanStatus?` | `null` | Defines the `Status` property. |
| `Goal` | `string?` | `null` | Defines the `Goal` property. |
| `Model` | `AgentModel?` | `null` | Defines the `Model` property. |
| `Summary` | `string?` | `null` | Defines the `Summary` property. |
| `Labels` | `AgentPlanLabels` | – | Defines the `Labels` property. |
| `Simulation` | `AgentPlanSimulation?` | `null` | Defines the `Simulation` property. |
| `IsPlanning` | `bool` | `false` | Defines the `IsPlanning` property. |
| `CanKeepPlanning` | `bool` | `true` | Defines the `CanKeepPlanning` property. |
| `CurrentStatus` | `AgentPlanStatus` | – | *Read-only.* Defines the `CurrentStatus` property. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Approved` | `AgentPlanApprovedEventArgs` | Defines the `Approved` event. |
| `Changed` | `AgentPlanChangedEventArgs` | Defines the `Changed` event. |
| `StepAction` | `AgentPlanStepActionEventArgs` | Defines the `StepAction` event. |
| `KeepPlanningRequested` | `RoutedEventArgs` | Defines the `KeepPlanningRequested` event. |
| `PauseChanged` | `AgentPlanPauseChangedEventArgs` | Defines the `PauseChanged` event. |
| `StartOverRequested` | `RoutedEventArgs` | Defines the `StartOverRequested` event. |

Pseudo-classes: `:draft`, `:running`, `:paused`, `:done`, `:failed`, `:narrow`, `:empty`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

### AgentPlanStep

One step of an `AgentPlan`: an id, an instruction-style title, and while the plan runs its state, the activity lines the agent reports, an optional note (a suggested or agent-inserted step), the reason of a failure and the time a finished step took. Every property is observed, so changing a step updates the plan on screen.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Title` | `string` | `""` | Defines the `Title` property. |
| `State` | `AgentPlanStepState` | `Pending` | Defines the `State` property. |
| `Note` | `string?` | `null` | Defines the `Note` property. |
| `NoteKind` | `AgentPlanNoteKind` | `None` | Defines the `NoteKind` property. |
| `Error` | `string?` | `null` | Defines the `Error` property. |
| `Duration` | `TimeSpan?` | `null` | Defines the `Duration` property. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### AgentPlanLabels

Every word an `AgentPlan` shows or announces, in English by default. Replace the instance to translate or reword; texts with numbers or names are functions so that word order and plurals can change. The numbers in `StepCount` and `Position` roll on screen while the words around them stay.

### AgentPlanSimulation

The built-in simulated agent of an `AgentPlan` that has no `Status`: it answers the plan's buttons (Approve plan, Keep planning, Pause, Resume, Retry, Skip, Start over) and plays a scripted run, one step after the other, with the beats measured on the reference. Scripts are found by step id; a step without one runs `GenericScript`. It is event-driven: exactly one timer waits per state change, nothing runs while the plan is idle, and Pause keeps the remaining time of that timer so Resume continues where the run stopped.

### AgentPlanStepScript

How the built-in simulation runs one step: the activity lines it reports, the time it took, and optionally a failure (after the last line) with the lines and time of the retry, and a step the agent inserts after one of the lines.

### AgentPlanScriptedStep

A step with its simulation script: what the sample draft, the suggestions and the inserted step are made of.

### AgentPlanApprovedEventArgs

Arguments of `Approved`: the steps in their final order, titles trimmed, empty steps removed.

Derives from `RoutedEventArgs`: every member of `RoutedEventArgs` works as well.

### AgentPlanChangedEventArgs

Arguments of `Changed`: the draft after an edit and what the edit was.

Derives from `RoutedEventArgs`: every member of `RoutedEventArgs` works as well.

### AgentPlanStepActionEventArgs

Arguments of `StepAction`: Retry or Skip on a failed step.

Derives from `RoutedEventArgs`: every member of `RoutedEventArgs` works as well.

### AgentPlanPauseChangedEventArgs

Arguments of `PauseChanged`: Pause (true) or Resume (false).

Derives from `RoutedEventArgs`: every member of `RoutedEventArgs` works as well.

### AgentModel

The model or agent behind a run in the AI components (`AgentStatus`, `AgentPlan`, `AgentTimeline`): a display name and an optional mark. Data only; set it once per run.

The enums:

| Type | Values |
|---|---|
| `AgentPlanStatus` | `Draft`, `Running`, `Paused`, `Done` |
| `AgentPlanStepState` | `Pending`, `Active`, `Done`, `Failed`, `Skipped` |
| `AgentPlanNoteKind` | `None`, `Suggested`, `AddedByAgent` |
| `AgentPlanChangeKind` | `Rename`, `Move`, `Remove`, `Add`, `SuggestionStreamed` |
| `AgentPlanStepActionKind` | `Retry`, `Skip` |

`AgentPlanSamples` holds the invented sample (`Steps`, `Suggestions`, `GenericScript`, `Goal`, `Summary`,
`CreateModel()`, `CreateSteps()`), so a page can start from it and change one step.

## Accessibility

- The card is a group named after the model and the goal ("Lumen 2 Pro plan: Add full-text search to the help center").
  The steps are an ordered list, so a screen reader announces the count and each position.
- While the plan runs, every step announces its state in words (Pending, In progress, Done, Failed, Skipped) before its
  title. Each state also has its own shape, so it never rests on color.
- A failed step reads the word Failed, its reason and two labelled buttons (Retry and Skip, each named with the step).
- A title is a labelled text area ("Step 3") described by a hint that explains Alt plus the arrow keys and Escape. Grips
  and remove buttons are named after their position and step ("Move step 3: …").
- The progress line is a progress bar with a text value ("2 of 6 steps finished"); it is hidden from assistive
  technology while the plan is a draft.
- One polite status region announces edits, approval (and that a run is simulated), each finished step, an inserted
  step, a failure, retry, skip, pause and resume, the final summary and a reset. Dragging with the pointer says nothing.
- Focus follows the action: a moved step keeps focus, a removed step hands it to its neighbour (the last one to Add
  step), Add step focuses the new title, Approve plan hands it to Pause, a failure moves it to Retry, Retry and Skip
  hand it back to Pause, Done moves it to Start over and Start over to Approve plan.
- Keyboard focus shows a 2px ring (inset on controls inside a row); pointer focus shows none. Titles show a quiet inset
  line instead.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` | In a draft: each step's grip, title and remove button, then Add step, Keep planning and Approve plan. While running: Retry and Skip on a failed step, and Pause or Resume. Done: Start over |
| `Alt+Up` / `Alt+Down` in a title | Move the step one place; the caret stays |
| `Up` / `Down` on a grip | Move the step one place; at the ends nothing happens |
| `Enter` in a title | Save the rename and stay in the field |
| `Escape` in a title | Undo the edits since the field got the focus or since the last save |
| `Backspace` in an empty title | Remove the step and focus the one above |
| `Space`, `Enter`, `Home`, `End` on a grip | Nothing: there is no pick-up mode |

## Motion

- **One spring for every change in size or place**: critically damped, about 260ms, no overshoot. Rows slide and grow
  when a step is inserted, removed or moved, a dragged row's neighbours step aside, an activity line or the failure
  block opens, and the footer and the progress line follow. A dropped row settles on a slightly faster spring.
- A step becoming done draws its check as a stroke (after 45ms, over 200ms) while the disc fades up, the title settles
  from primary to secondary text over 240ms and the time fades in. Its activity lines fold away at the same moment.
- The current step's title shimmers (one pass in 1.8s, then a short rest) beside the turning arc. Pausing stops both.
- A suggestion streams in chunks of three to five words every 34ms, each chunk only fading in; the step the agent inserts
  arrives with an 8% accent wash that holds for about 640ms and fades out over about 1.2s.
- Counts roll with tabular digits in a reserved width. The header's right side, the footer's rows and the status marks
  swap with one short crossfade (the old one out in 60ms, the new one in and up 3px over about 145ms).

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| Heights and positions | Spring | At once | At once |
| Status swaps | Crossfade with a 3px rise | Short crossfade | At once |
| Spinner and shimmer | Turn and sweep | Still | Still |
| Check | Draws over 200ms | Shown complete | Shown complete |
| Inserted step | Slides in with a wash | Appears | Appears |
| Streamed suggestion | Chunks fade in | All words at once | All words at once |
| Timeline of the simulation | Unchanged | Unchanged | Unchanged |

## Related

- `AgentStatus` for a compact live status of one running agent.
- `ToolCall` for a single tool call with its input, output and approval.
- `AgentTimeline` for the time axis of an orchestrated run.
- `ContextWindow` for how much of a model's context a run uses.
- `ChatThread` when you show the conversation itself.

# Agent timeline

> A replay of a multi-agent run on one time axis: each agent's thinking, tool calls and waiting, the handoffs between them, and the time, tokens and cost.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc.Special`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc.Special --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/agent-timeline

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.AgentTimelinePreviewDemo">
    <!-- With no run the timeline shows its invented sample and replays it the first time it scrolls into view. -->
    <arc:AgentTimeline Margin="0,12" />
</UserControl>
```

## When to use

`AgentTimeline` shows one orchestrated run of several AI agents as a compact Gantt chart. The orchestrator sits on the
top row and each subagent gets a row below it, with a color dot, its name and the model it runs on. Spans on a shared
time axis say what each agent did and when: thinking is a tint of the agent's color, a tool call is solid, and waiting
is hatched. Thin elbow connectors show work handed down to a subagent and results coming back up. The run replays
with a playhead while the header counts the elapsed time, the tokens and the cost, and it ends on a summary with the
parallel speedup.

- **Run history and trace viewers**: show where the time of a finished multi-agent run went, which agents worked in
  parallel and which ones only waited.
- **Debugging panels**: a failed tool call and its retry stand out with a cross and a retry arrow, and pinning a span
  traces its handoff path through the run.
- **Product demos and changelogs**: replay a real run with its own numbers for time, tokens and cost, at 1x or faster.
- **Following a run as it happens**: live mode grows open spans to the current time while your backend appends events.

## When not to use

- **One agent's steps and answer**: when people need the agent's reasoning, sources and output rather than the timing,
  show the transcript with `ToolCall` rows or an `AgentPlan`.
- **One agent's state at a glance**: use `AgentStatus` for a compact live pill.
- **Distributed request tracing**: spans of services and network calls belong in a tracing view, not here; the
  timeline's vocabulary (thinking, tool calls, waiting, handoffs) is about agents.
- **Long traces of thousands of steps**: the timeline handles a few hundred spans comfortably. For longer traces pass a
  window of the run or merge tiny spans first.
- **An explanation of how agents work in general**: use the `AgentLoop` illustration, which tells that story with
  invented steps.

## Usage

Given no data, the timeline shows an invented sample run and replays it the first time it is about a fifth in view.
Register the package with `UseArcSpecial()` next to `UseArcControls()`.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:AgentTimeline />
</UserControl>
```

`AgentTimeline` derives from Avalonia's `TemplatedControl`. It fills its container up to 744px; it reads best between
360 and 760px wide.

### Anatomy

1. **Header**: the `Title` (else the run's title, else "Agent run") and the status line under it. While the run
   replays the line reads the state (Running with a shimmer, Paused or Ready), the elapsed time, the tokens and the
   cost; at the end it turns into a check and the summary: agents, length, parallel speedup and cost.
2. **Agent labels**: one 44px row per agent, the orchestrator first: a color dot, the name, and under it the model's
   mark and name.
3. **Plot**: the spans of every agent on one time axis, with grid lines at the ticks. A span that is still running has
   a square leading edge and a short shine; a finished span has round corners.
4. **Connectors**: an elbow from the orchestrator down to a subagent's next span (a dispatch) or from a subagent's last
   span up to the orchestrator (a result), with a dot where it meets the upper row.
5. **Playhead and axis**: a thin line at the current time, and under the rows the axis with its tick labels and the
   scrubber knob.
6. **Footer**: play or pause (replay once finished), restart and the speed control on the left; the legend (Thinking,
   Tool call, Waiting, Handoff, Failed) on the right, or under them when there is no room.
7. **Span card**: hover or focus a span to see who did it on which model, what it did, its tool or kind, its length and
   tokens, and notes for a failure, a retry or its handoffs.

### The sample run

The sample is an invented incident investigation, "Signup emails bouncing since Mar 3". A coordinator plans three
checks and hands them to a status watcher, a config auditor and a log reader, which work in parallel. The log reader's
first scan fails and a narrower query succeeds on the second try. The coordinator combines the reports, has a scribe
write the incident note and files it. Five agents, 30 spans and eight handoffs take 26.8 seconds, 49,920 tokens and
$0.15, a 1.5x parallel speedup. `AgentTimelineSamples.CreateIncidentRun()` returns a fresh copy of it, and
`CreateRefundRun()` a small two-agent run.

### Your own run

Give the timeline an `AgentTimelineRun`: its agents in row order (the orchestrator first), the spans with times in
seconds from the start of the run, and the handoffs. A run of your own opens finished, ready to replay; set
`AutoPlay="True"` to replay it when it comes into view instead.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.AgentTimelineOwnRunDemo">
    <!-- A finished run of your own opens complete, ready to replay. Click a span to pin it. -->
    <StackPanel Spacing="16" Margin="0,12">
        <arc:AgentTimeline x:Name="Timeline" SpanSelected="OnSpanSelected" Completed="OnCompleted">
            <arc:AgentTimeline.Run>
                <arc:AgentTimelineRun Title="Monthly refund summary">
                    <arc:AgentTimelineRun.Agents>
                        <arc:AgentTimelineAgent Id="planner" Name="Planner" Price="8">
                            <arc:AgentTimelineAgent.Model>
                                <arc:AgentModel Name="Nimbus Pro 3" Mark="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Sparkles}" />
                            </arc:AgentTimelineAgent.Model>
                        </arc:AgentTimelineAgent>
                        <arc:AgentTimelineAgent Id="clerk" Name="Data clerk" Price="0.2">
                            <arc:AgentTimelineAgent.Model>
                                <arc:AgentModel Name="Nimbus Lite 3" Mark="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Sparkles}" />
                            </arc:AgentTimelineAgent.Model>
                        </arc:AgentTimelineAgent>
                    </arc:AgentTimelineRun.Agents>
                    <arc:AgentTimelineRun.Spans>
                        <arc:AgentTimelineSpan AgentId="planner" Kind="Thinking" Start="0" End="1.2"
                                               Label="Outlined the summary" Tokens="1100" />
                        <arc:AgentTimelineSpan AgentId="planner" Kind="Waiting" Start="1.2" End="5.8"
                                               Label="Waiting on the data clerk" />
                        <arc:AgentTimelineSpan AgentId="clerk" Kind="Tool" Start="1.5" End="3.9"
                                               Label="Exported last month's refunds" Tool="Ledger"
                                               ToolMark="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Database}" Tokens="2200" />
                        <arc:AgentTimelineSpan AgentId="clerk" Kind="Thinking" Start="3.9" End="5.5"
                                               Label="Ranked the refund reasons" Tokens="800" />
                    </arc:AgentTimelineRun.Spans>
                    <arc:AgentTimelineRun.Handoffs>
                        <arc:AgentTimelineHandoff From="planner" To="clerk" At="1.2" Label="Which refund reasons grew?" />
                        <arc:AgentTimelineHandoff From="clerk" To="planner" At="5.8" Label="Damaged items lead the refunds" />
                    </arc:AgentTimelineRun.Handoffs>
                </arc:AgentTimelineRun>
            </arc:AgentTimeline.Run>
        </arc:AgentTimeline>
        <TextBlock x:Name="Log"
                   HorizontalAlignment="Center"
                   TextAlignment="Center"
                   TextWrapping="Wrap"
                   FontSize="13"
                   Text="Click a span to pin it; the pin is logged here."
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class AgentTimelineOwnRunDemo : UserControl
{
    public AgentTimelineOwnRunDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
    }

    private void OnSpanSelected(object? sender, AgentTimelineSpanSelectedEventArgs e)
    {
        Log.Text = e.Span is { } span
            ? $"Pinned: {span.Label} ({span.AgentId}, {span.Start:0.0}s to {span.End:0.0}s)"
            : "Unpinned.";
    }

    private void OnCompleted(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        var summary = Timeline.Summary;
        Log.Text = $"Replay finished: {summary.Tokens:N0} tokens, ${summary.Cost:0.00}.";
    }
}
```

```xml

        <arc:AgentTimelineRun Title="Monthly refund summary">

                <arc:AgentTimelineAgent Id="planner" Name="Planner" Price="8" />
                <arc:AgentTimelineAgent Id="clerk" Name="Data clerk" Price="0.2" />
            </arc:AgentTimelineRun.Agents>
            <arc:AgentTimelineRun.Spans>
                <arc:AgentTimelineSpan AgentId="planner" Kind="Thinking" Start="0" End="1.2"
                                       Label="Outlined the summary" Tokens="1100" />
                <arc:AgentTimelineSpan AgentId="planner" Kind="Waiting" Start="1.2" End="5.8"
                                       Label="Waiting on the data clerk" />
                <arc:AgentTimelineSpan AgentId="clerk" Kind="Tool" Start="1.5" End="3.9"
                                       Label="Exported last month's refunds" Tool="Ledger"
                                       ToolMark="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Database}" Tokens="2200" />
            </arc:AgentTimelineRun.Spans>
            <arc:AgentTimelineRun.Handoffs>
                <arc:AgentTimelineHandoff From="planner" To="clerk" At="1.2" Label="Which refund reasons grew?" />
            </arc:AgentTimelineRun.Handoffs>
        </arc:AgentTimelineRun>
    </arc:AgentTimeline.Run>
</arc:AgentTimeline>
```

```csharp
timeline.SpanSelected += (_, e) => details.Show(e.Span);   // null when the pin is removed
```

- **Agents**: `Id` names the agent in spans and handoffs. `Model` is an `AgentModel` (a name and a 24×24 stroked mark
  such as an `ArcIcons` glyph). `Price` is a blended rate in US dollars per million tokens. `Color` overrides the row
  color; by default the orchestrator is neutral and the following agents take the chart series colors 1 to 4 in turn.
- **Spans**: `Kind` is `Thinking`, `Tool` or `Waiting`. A tool call names its `Tool` and can carry a `ToolMark`
  (a wrench when none). `Status="Failed"` with a `Detail` marks a failed call; `IsRetry` marks the call that retried
  it, with its note in `Detail`. `Tokens` count up evenly across the span, and `Cost` replaces the cost worked out from
  the agent's price.
- **Handoffs**: the shape is inferred. Work handed down a row is a dispatch: it drops at `At` and turns into the
  target's next span. Work handed up is a result: it leaves the end of the source's last span and rises to the target
  at `At`. Give a dispatch a time just before the target's first span and a result a time just after the source's last.
- `Agents`, `Spans` and `Handoffs` on the timeline override the run's lists, and every list is observed when it raises
  collection changes. Spans are `AvaloniaObject`s, so a new `End` or `Status` reaches the plot at once.

### Numbers and formats

- **Time**: one decimal, rounded half up ("26.8s"); from a minute on "1m 05.3s".
- **Tokens**: each span's tokens accrue evenly from its start to its end, summed and rounded, with thousands separators.
- **Cost**: each span's tokens times its agent's price per million (or the span's own `Cost`), with two decimals.
- **Speedup**: the time agents spent thinking and calling tools, summed over every agent, divided by the run's length.
  Waiting is idle time and does not count. Under 1.05 the summary says "no parallel speedup".
- The counters update about twenty times a second and each one keeps the width of its final value, so the header never
  shifts while it counts.

The axis is as long as the run. Its tick step is the smallest of 0.1, 0.2, 0.5, 1, 2, 5, 10, 15 and 30 seconds, then
1, 2, 5, 10, 15 and 30 minutes, that gives at most six ticks from zero, at least 40px apart: 26.8 seconds shows 0 to
25 in steps of five at any width, 6.2 seconds steps by two and a minute steps by 15.

### Playback and speed

`IsPlaying` and `Speed` are two way: the footer writes them and an app can bind them. Play continues from where the
replay stands; once it has finished, it starts over. Restart always goes back to zero and plays at the current speed.
`Speeds` lists the options of the speed control (1x and 2x by default); with one option or none the control hides.
`Play()`, `Pause()`, `Restart()` and `Seek(seconds)` do the same from code. `PlaybackChanged` reports each action a
person takes (play, pause, restart, a seek, a speed), and `Completed` fires each time a replay reaches the end.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.AgentTimelineSpeedsDemo">
    <!-- Four speeds to choose from, starting at double speed. -->
    <arc:AgentTimeline x:Name="Timeline" Speed="2" Margin="0,12" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class AgentTimelineSpeedsDemo : UserControl
{
    public AgentTimelineSpeedsDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Timeline.Speeds = [0.5, 1, 2, 4];
    }
}
```

At 1x the replay runs in real time. A single frame advances at most 0.1 seconds times the speed, so a stalled window
loses a moment instead of jumping ahead, and the clock stops while the timeline is off screen.

Pressing or dragging anywhere on the axis moves the replay there and pauses it; the knob then takes keyboard focus.
`Phase` is Ready at zero, Running while it plays, Paused part way and Finished at the end.

### Pinning a span

Click a span, or press Enter on it, to pin it. The card then stays, and everything off the span's handoff path dims:
spans to 28% and connectors to 16%. For a span of the orchestrator, the path is the span itself, the handoffs that start
or end during it and the spans at their other ends. For a subagent's span, it is that agent's whole row, every handoff
to or from the agent and the spans at their other ends. Click the span again, press Enter again or press Escape to
unpin. `PinnedSpan` is two way, and `SpanSelected` reports each change.

### Live runs

Set `IsLive` while a run is in progress. The time runs from the run's `StartedAt` (or from when live mode starts),
spans without an `End` grow to now, and the playback controls hide. Append spans and handoffs as events arrive and set
each span's `End` when it closes. The axis grows in calm steps: when the time passes 90% of it, it springs to a round
length past one and a half times the time (5, 8, 12, 20, 30, 50 seconds and so on). Set `IsLive` to false when the run
ends: the timeline settles on the summary, announces it and raises `Completed`.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.AgentTimelineLiveDemo">
    <!-- Live mode: events arrive while the run happens; open spans grow to now and the axis grows in steps. -->
    <StackPanel Spacing="16" Margin="0,12">
        <arc:AgentTimeline x:Name="Timeline" Completed="OnCompleted" />
        <StackPanel Orientation="Horizontal" HorizontalAlignment="Center" Spacing="12">
            <arc:Button Content="Start a live run" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Click="OnStartClick" />
            <TextBlock x:Name="Log"
                       VerticalAlignment="Center"
                       FontSize="13"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
        </StackPanel>
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia;
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class AgentTimelineLiveDemo : UserControl
{
    // Replays the sample run as if its events were arriving from a backend right now.
    private readonly AgentTimelineLiveDriver _driver = new(AgentTimelineSamples.CreateIncidentRun());

    public AgentTimelineLiveDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
    }

    protected override void OnAttachedToVisualTree(VisualTreeAttachmentEventArgs e)
    {
        base.OnAttachedToVisualTree(e);
        Start();
    }

    protected override void OnDetachedFromVisualTree(VisualTreeAttachmentEventArgs e)
    {
        base.OnDetachedFromVisualTree(e);
        _driver.Stop();
        Timeline.IsLive = false;
    }

    private void OnStartClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) => Start();

    private void Start()
    {
        _driver.Start(Timeline);
        Log.Text = "Live: events arrive as they happen.";
    }

    private void OnCompleted(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        Log.Text = "The run ended; the timeline settled on its summary.";
    }
}
```

```csharp
timeline.Run = liveRun;            // an AgentTimelineRun your event handler appends to
timeline.IsLive = true;
// on each event
liveRun.Spans.Add(new AgentTimelineSpan("logs", AgentTimelineSpanKind.Tool, 3.1, null, "Bounce scan"));
span.End = 5.2;
// when the run ends
timeline.IsLive = false;
```

`AgentTimelineLiveDriver` plays a finished run into a timeline as if it were happening now, which is how the demo above
works.

### Narrow containers

The layout follows the timeline's own width, not the window's. Below 520px the label column narrows from 176 to 132px
and shows only the dot and the name (the span card still names the model), and the side padding drops from 24 to 16px.
When the plot would be narrower than 300px it keeps 300px and scrolls sideways with the labels pinned; a divider appears
beside the labels once it is scrolled, and the replay keeps the playhead in view unless the reader scrolled in the last
2.5 seconds. The status line wraps after a separator, and the legend moves under the controls and wraps on its own.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.AgentTimelineNarrowDemo">
    <!-- Below 520px the label column narrows to dot and name; below a 300px plot the plot scrolls with the labels pinned. -->
    <arc:AgentTimeline Width="400" HorizontalAlignment="Center" Margin="0,12" />
</UserControl>
```

### Content guidelines

Write each span label as what the agent did, in the past tense and in a few words; the card shows it in full but the
accessible name reads it with the agent, kind and times around it. Name tools by what they are in your product, with
generic glyphs as marks. Keep handoff labels to one short sentence: they appear as "From Coordinator: …" and
"To Coordinator: …" in the cards.

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| Tool call | Searched blocklist reports for our domain |
| LLM generation step 3 | Matched the bounces to SPF failures |
| Error | Full scan of mail events ran past the time limit |
| Handoff | Mail config changes since Mar 1 |

### Best practices

**Do**

- Put the orchestrator first, and order subagents so connectors cross idle rows: the agent that returns first right
  under the orchestrator, dispatches to the deepest row first.
- Mark blocked time as `Waiting`, so parallel work and idle time read at a glance and the speedup counts only real work.
- Mark a failed call with `Status="Failed"` and a `Detail`, and the call that retried it with `IsRetry`.
- Give agents a `Price` so the cost is real, or leave it out everywhere rather than on some agents only.

**Avoid**

- Brand marks of real model vendors or services. Use generic glyphs and name the model in text.
- Replacing the run object on every event in a live run; append to its lists instead.
- Several replaying timelines on one screen. Each one draws on every frame while it plays.

### Common questions

**Why does my run open finished?** A run of your own is a record, so it opens complete; set `AutoPlay="True"` to replay
it when it comes into view. Under reduced motion every timeline opens finished.

**Why is a connector only a short stub?** A dispatch looks for the target's first span starting at or after its time.
In a live run that span has not arrived yet; the elbow completes when it does.

**Why does the card show a longer time than the span?** The card always shows a span's final length, tokens and
handoffs, even while the replay is still drawing it.

**Can I translate it?** Set `Labels` to an `AgentTimelineLabels` with your words; sentences with numbers are functions,
so the word order can change.

## API reference

### AgentTimeline

A compact timeline of one orchestrated multi-agent run: the orchestrator and its subagents share a time axis, one row each (color dot, name, model). Spans show thinking (a tint of the agent's color), tool calls (solid) and waiting (hatched); thin elbow connectors show work handed down to a subagent and results coming back up, with a dot where they meet the upper row. The run replays: a playhead sweeps, the active span grows with a square leading edge and a short shine, connectors draw in as handoffs happen, and the header counts time, tokens and cost until it settles into a summary with the parallel speedup. Hover or focus a span for a card with what it did; click it (or press Enter) to pin it and dim everything off its handoff path. Play, pause, restart, a speed control and scrubbing on the axis drive the replay; live mode follows a run in progress.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Run` | `AgentTimelineRun?` | `null` | Defines the `Run` property. |
| `Agents` | `IList<AgentTimelineAgent>?` | `null` | Defines the `Agents` property. |
| `Spans` | `IList<AgentTimelineSpan>?` | `null` | Defines the `Spans` property. |
| `Handoffs` | `IList<AgentTimelineHandoff>?` | `null` | Defines the `Handoffs` property. |
| `Title` | `string?` | `null` | Defines the `Title` property. |
| `AutoPlay` | `bool?` | `null` | Defines the `AutoPlay` property. |
| `Speed` | `double` | `1` | Defines the `Speed` property. |
| `Speeds` | `IList<double>?` | `null` | Defines the `Speeds` property. |
| `IsLive` | `bool` | `false` | Defines the `IsLive` property. |
| `IsPlaying` | `bool` | `false` | Defines the `IsPlaying` property. |
| `PinnedSpan` | `AgentTimelineSpan?` | `null` | Defines the `PinnedSpan` property. |
| `Labels` | `AgentTimelineLabels` | – | Defines the `Labels` property. |
| `CurrentTime` | `double` | – | *Read-only.* Defines the `CurrentTime` property. |
| `Duration` | `double` | – | *Read-only.* Defines the `Duration` property. |
| `Phase` | `AgentTimelinePhase` | – | *Read-only.* Defines the `Phase` property. |
| `Summary` | `AgentTimelineSummary` | – | *Read-only.* Defines the `Summary` property. |
| `ActualTitle` | `string` | – | *Read-only.* Defines the `ActualTitle` property. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `SpanSelected` | `AgentTimelineSpanSelectedEventArgs` | Defines the `SpanSelected` routed event. |
| `Completed` | `RoutedEventArgs` | Defines the `Completed` routed event. |
| `PlaybackChanged` | `AgentTimelinePlaybackChangedEventArgs` | Defines the `PlaybackChanged` routed event. |

Pseudo-classes: `:ready`, `:running`, `:paused`, `:finished`, `:live`, `:narrow`, `:scrollable`, `:scrolled`, `:pinned`, `:single-speed`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

### AgentTimelineRun

One orchestrated run for an `AgentTimeline`: its agents (rows, the orchestrator first), their spans and the handoffs between them. The three lists are observed: append spans and handoffs as events arrive in a live run, and set a span's `End` when it closes.

### AgentTimelineAgent

One agent of a run, shown as a row of an `AgentTimeline`: a color dot, its name and its model. The first agent of a run is the orchestrator. Data only; set it before handing the run to the timeline.

### AgentTimelineSpan

One stretch of an agent's work on the time axis of an `AgentTimeline`: thinking, a tool call or waiting, from `Start` to `End` in seconds from the start of the run. An open span (no `End`) grows to the current time in a live run. Changes to its properties reach the timeline at once.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Id` | `string?` | `null` | Defines the `Id` property. |
| `AgentId` | `string` | `""` | Defines the `AgentId` property. |
| `Kind` | `AgentTimelineSpanKind` | `Thinking` | Defines the `Kind` property. |
| `Start` | `double` | `0` | Defines the `Start` property. |
| `End` | `double?` | `null` | Defines the `End` property. |
| `Label` | `string` | `""` | Defines the `Label` property. |
| `Detail` | `string?` | `null` | Defines the `Detail` property. |
| `Tool` | `string?` | `null` | Defines the `Tool` property. |
| `ToolMark` | `Geometry?` | `null` | Defines the `ToolMark` property. |
| `Tokens` | `int?` | `null` | Defines the `Tokens` property. |
| `Cost` | `double?` | `null` | Defines the `Cost` property. |
| `Status` | `AgentTimelineSpanStatus` | `Ok` | Defines the `Status` property. |
| `IsRetry` | `bool` | `false` | Defines the `IsRetry` property. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### AgentTimelineHandoff

Work handed from one agent to another at a moment of the run: drawn as a thin elbow connector with a dot where it meets the upper row. Handing work down a row (orchestrator to subagent) is a dispatch: it drops at `At` and enters the target's next span. Handing it up (subagent to orchestrator) is a result: it leaves the end of the source's last span and rises to the target at `At`.

### AgentTimelineLabels

Every word an `AgentTimeline` shows or speaks, with English defaults. Sentences with numbers are format delegates; numbers reach them already rounded (times in seconds to one decimal, speeds as given). Replace the whole object to translate the timeline.

### AgentTimelineSpanSelectedEventArgs

Arguments of `SpanSelected`: the span that was pinned, or null when it was unpinned.

Derives from `RoutedEventArgs`: every member of `RoutedEventArgs` works as well.

### AgentTimelinePlaybackChangedEventArgs

Arguments of `PlaybackChanged`: what the person did, and the time and speed after it.

Derives from `RoutedEventArgs`: every member of `RoutedEventArgs` works as well.

### AgentTimelineLiveDriver

Plays a finished run into an `AgentTimeline` as if it were happening now, for demos of live mode: it hands the timeline a growing copy of the run (`LiveRun`), turns `IsLive` on, and on a wall-clock timer appends each span when it starts (without an end), sets its end when it finishes and appends each handoff at its moment, the way events would arrive from a backend. When the source run is over it turns live mode off, so the timeline settles on its summary.

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Finished` | `EventHandler?` | Raised when the whole run has arrived and live mode was turned off. |

### AgentModel

The model or agent behind a run in the AI components (`AgentStatus`, `AgentPlan`, `AgentTimeline`): a display name and an optional mark. Data only; set it once per run.

The enums and values:

| Type | Values |
|---|---|
| `AgentTimelineSpanKind` | `Thinking`, `Tool`, `Waiting` |
| `AgentTimelineSpanStatus` | `Ok` (default), `Failed` |
| `AgentTimelinePhase` | `Ready`, `Running`, `Paused`, `Finished`, `Live` |
| `AgentTimelinePlaybackAction` | `Play`, `Pause`, `Restart`, `Seek`, `Speed` |
| `AgentTimelineSummary` | `AgentCount`, `Duration`, `Speedup`, `Tokens`, `Cost` (the `Summary` property) |

`AgentTimelineSamples` holds the invented runs (`CreateIncidentRun()`, `CreateRefundRun()`).

## Accessibility

- The timeline is named by its title. Each span is a button to assistive technology, named with the agent, the kind,
  the tool, "failed" or "retry", what it did, its time range and its tokens ("Log reader, Tool call, Mail logs, failed:
  Bounce scan took too long, 3.1s to 5.2s, 430 tokens"); a pinned span reads as pressed. The spans are one tab stop and
  the arrow keys move between them.
- The plot is drawn, so the spans have no control each: a focus stand-in sits on the span the keyboard is on and
  carries its name, and each arrow key moves focus to a fresh stand-in so screen readers announce the new span.
- The scrubber is a slider named "Run time" with the time as its value and help text such as "12.4s of 26.8s".
- Status is never color alone: a failed call shows a cross and "Failed" in its card and the legend, a retry shows an
  arrow and its note, and the finished state shows a check with the summary.
- A polite live region speaks when the reader acts: "Playing at 1x" on play, restart or a speed change while playing,
  "Paused at 11.1s" on pause or a seek, and the run's summary at the end. The first replay on sight is silent, and the
  counting status line is not a live region (its accessible name holds the counts and how many agents are busy).
- The span card repeats what the span's name already says, so it is hidden from assistive technology.
- Keyboard focus shows a 2px ring on the spans, the knob and the controls; pointer focus shows none.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` | Move through the spans (one stop), the scrubber, play or pause, restart and the speed control |
| `Left` / `Right` on a span | The previous or next span in the same row |
| `Up` / `Down` on a span | The span in the row above or below whose middle is closest in time (rows with nothing yet are skipped) |
| `Home` / `End` on a span | The first or last span of its row |
| `Enter` / `Space` on a span | Pin it and highlight its handoff path; again to unpin |
| `Escape` on a span | Unpin |
| `Left` / `Down`, `Right` / `Up` on the scrubber | Half a second back or forward (and pause) |
| `Shift` + arrows, `Page Down` / `Page Up` on the scrubber | Five seconds back or forward |
| `Home` / `End` on the scrubber | The start (Ready) or the end of the run (Finished) |
| `Left` / `Right` on the speed control | The previous or next speed, wrapping around |

## Motion

- The playhead, the knob and every active span move with the replay clock on each frame; the spans grow without any
  layout pass. The counters update about twenty times a second.
- An active thinking or tool span has a square leading edge and a 28px shine that sweeps across it in 1.05 seconds
  every 1.5 seconds, also while paused. When the span ends, its right corners round off, the edge fades and a failed
  call turns to its failed look over 160ms; the cross or the retry arrow appears over 160ms.
- A connector draws in over 360ms from the side the handoff leaves: a dispatch from the top, a result from the bottom.
  Its dot pops in over 160ms, at once for a dispatch and 260ms later for a result, once the line has reached it.
- Pinning dims and undims over 160ms; hovering a thinking or tool span deepens its color over 160ms.
- The span card fades in over 160ms while rising 3px, glides between spans on a critically damped spring (about 20
  rad/s), springs to its new height and crossfades its content (100ms out, 160ms in); it leaves after an 80ms grace with
  a 120ms fade.
- When the run ends the playhead fades out over 240ms and the status line crossfades to the summary (160ms in, 100ms
  out); the play button's glyph crossfades too. The knob grows to 1.3x over 160ms while focused or dragged.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| Opening | Replays the sample when it comes into view | Opens finished | Opens finished |
| Playback | Plays on request | Plays on request | Plays on request |
| Shine on active spans | Sweeps every 1.5 s | None | None |
| Span completion, dimming, hover | 160ms | At once | At once |
| Connector draw-in and dot pop | 360ms and 160ms | Appear at once | Appear at once |
| Card position and height | Springs | Jump | Jump |
| Card fade and content crossfade | 160ms / 120ms, 100 / 160ms | Kept (short crossfade) | At once |
| Status line and playhead | Crossfade, 240ms fade | At once | At once |

## Related

- `AgentStatus` for one agent's live state in a compact pill.
- `ToolCall` for the input and output of a single tool call.
- `AgentPlan` for the plan an agent follows, step by step.
- `ContextWindow` for how full a model's context is.
- `AgentLoop` for an illustration of how a single agent loops through context, tools and checks.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `AgentStatus` | You show what one running agent is doing now |
| `ToolCall` | People need one call's input and output |
| `AgentPlan` | The story is the plan, not the timing |
| `ContextWindow` | The question is how much of the context is used |
| `AgentLoop` | You explain the agent loop with an invented story |
