# Context window

> A model's context window as a grid of 200 cells that fills part by part, with a compaction threshold, a legend and actions that show what still fits.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc.Special`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc.Special --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/context-window

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ContextWindowPreviewDemo">
    <!-- With no data the card shows its sample session: send, attach, compact, switch models or point at the legend. -->
    <arc:ContextWindow Margin="0,12" />
</UserControl>
```

## When to use

`ContextWindow` shows what fills a language model's context window and how much room is left. The window is a fixed
budget of 200 cells, so every cell is a two-hundredth of it. The cells fill in reading order: the system prompt, the
tool definitions, files and memory, the summary of earlier messages and the conversation, then free space, with the
part held back for the reply drawn as outlined cells at the end. A dashed line marks where compaction starts. Above the
grid a large number reads the tokens used; beside it a legend lists every part with its tokens and its share. Send
message, Attach file and Compact now change the window, and a status line under them says what happened.

- **Developer tools and agent consoles**: show a session's budget next to the transcript, so people see why a long run
  starts to forget things and what a big attachment costs.
- **Coding agents that compact long sessions**: make compaction visible. The older messages fold into a short summary,
  the cells come back, and the status line says how much was folded.
- **Model choice in context**: switching to a model with a smaller window rearranges the grid at once and shows whether
  the session still fits; when it does not, the card folds the conversation and says so.
- **Documentation and onboarding**: explain context windows, output reserves and compaction with a sample that people
  can poke at. With no data the card plays an invented coding session.

## When not to use

- **A simple quota or plan allowance**: use `Progress` or a usage meter. The grid is about what is inside the window,
  not about how much of a plan is spent.
- **Choosing a model**: use a model picker. The pill here only switches between the windows you pass in.
- **Billing or spend over time**: use a chart. The card shows one moment of one session.
- **Many sessions at once**: a table with a small bar per row reads better. One card per screen is the intended use.

## Usage

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:ContextWindow />
</UserControl>
```

`ContextWindow` is a `TemplatedControl` in the Special package. Register the package with `UseArcSpecial()` next to
`UseArcControls()`. The card is at most 744px wide and follows its own width, not the window's.

Given no data at all (no models, items, turns or files) the card shows the invented sample session from
`ContextWindowSamples`: three sample models with 1M, 512K and 400K windows, a coding session of 436K tokens, five turns
for Send message and three files for Attach file. The sample works on its own copy, so `Items` stays empty. As soon as
you give the card any of the four lists it uses yours.

### Anatomy

1. **Readout**: the tokens used as a large number, "of 1M tokens" on its baseline, and under them the percentage used
   (a whole number that passes 100 when the window overflows), "used", a dot and the free tokens.
2. **Model pill**: the model's mark, its name, its window in muted figures and a chevron. It opens a menu of the
   models; the selected one has a check. The pill hides when there is no model.
3. **Grid**: 20 columns by 10 rows of square cells in the order system prompt, tools, files and memory, summary,
   conversation, free space and the output reserve. Free cells after the threshold line are a shade lighter.
4. **Threshold line**: a dashed line on the row boundary nearest the threshold (after row 8 for 80%).
5. **Caption**: "Each cell is 5K tokens" on the left and a dashed sample with "Compacts at 80%" on the right.
6. **Legend**: seven rows (System prompt, Tools, Files & memory, Summary, Conversation, Free, Output reserve), each with
   a swatch, its tokens and its share of the window. An empty row shows "No summary yet" or "0" in muted text and no
   share. A stronger divider separates what is used from what is left.
7. **Actions**: Send message (primary), Attach file (secondary) and Compact now (ghost, on the right while there is
   room). Send message and Attach file hide when there is nothing to send or attach.
8. **Status line**: an icon and a sentence: an info circle for plain news, a warning triangle near or past the
   threshold, the shrink glyph while messages fold, and a check circle when a compaction landed.

### How the cells are counted

The window is divided into 200 cells, so a cell holds the window over 200 tokens: 5K on a 1M window, 2.6K on 512K
and 2K on 400K. The parts are laid out by cumulative rounding: the card adds the parts up in order and rounds each
running total to whole cells (halves round up), and a part gets the cells between two such boundaries. Rounding the
running totals keeps the grid honest: the used cells always match the total used, even when every part is small.
The reserve is rounded on its own and counted back from the last cell. When the window overflows, the parts stop at
the reserve and the parts that come later get no cells; the reserve is always drawn.

Token counts read "996" below 1,000, "4.1K" with one decimal below 10K (without a trailing ".0", so "2K"), "509K"
below a million and "1M" or "1.2M" above. Shares read "0.4%" with one decimal below 10% (keeping "1.0%") and "29%"
from 10% on. Each row rounds on its own, so the rows can add up to 99.8% or 100.1%.

### Send, attach and compact

Send message adds the next of `Turns` as a message at the end of the window; Attach file adds the next of `Files` at
the end of the files and memory, and the summary and the conversation move along. Both start over after the last one.
The status line names what was added and how many tokens it took.

From 85% of the threshold (68% of the window at the default 80%) a send or an attachment warns: the status line turns
to a warning and adds that compaction is near. When one reaches the threshold, the card says it passed it and, 540ms
later, folds on its own. Switching to a model whose window the session overfills warns at once and folds after 600ms.

Folding takes 700ms. Every action and the model pill are off while the conversation dims from the oldest message to
the newest. Then every message but the newest two becomes part of one summary (about 6% of the folded tokens, at
least 4K and at most 24K), the summary lands right after the files, and the cells it frees turn back into free space.
A later compaction adds to the same summary; the summary itself is never folded. Compact now does the same on
demand while there are more messages than the newest two.

| Moment | Status | Time |
|---|---|---|
| A send past the threshold | Added “Why does the nightly sync time out?” (+35K) · past 80% | 0 |
| Folding starts | Past 80%: folding 35 earlier messages… | 540ms |
| The summary lands | Folded 608K into a 24K summary | 1,240ms |
| A switch to a smaller model | 436K is over 80% of Cirrus M | 0 |
| Folding starts | Too full for Cirrus M: folding 22 earlier messages… | 600ms |

Files are never folded. When the window is past the threshold and only the newest messages are left, the status line
says there is nothing to fold yet; when a compaction leaves the window past the threshold, it says how much was folded
and suggests removing files. The used tokens can pass the window: the readout then shows more than 100% and no free
tokens.

### Your own session

Pass your models, items, turns and files. Each `ContextWindowModel` has a window and a reserve in tokens, a name and
an optional mark (a 24 × 24 stroked glyph such as an `ArcIcons` member) with its color. Each `ContextWindowItem` has a
category, a label and its tokens; the grid groups items by category, so their order only matters within one.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ContextWindowYourSessionDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="16" Margin="0,12">
        <!-- Your own models, items, turns and files; the card rewrites Items as it goes and raises an event for each change. -->
        <arc:ContextWindow x:Name="Card"
                           ItemsChanged="OnItemsChanged"
                           Compacted="OnCompacted"
                           ModelChanged="OnModelChanged" />
        <TextBlock x:Name="Log"
                   HorizontalAlignment="Center"
                   TextAlignment="Center"
                   TextWrapping="Wrap"
                   FontSize="13"
                   Text="Send, attach, compact or switch models: each event is logged here."
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class ContextWindowYourSessionDemo : UserControl
{
    private readonly List<string> _entries = new();

    public ContextWindowYourSessionDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Card.Models.AddRange(ContextWindowDemoData.Models());
        Card.Items.AddRange(ContextWindowDemoData.Items());
        Card.Turns.AddRange(ContextWindowDemoData.Turns());
        Card.Files.AddRange(ContextWindowDemoData.Files());
    }

    private void OnItemsChanged(object? sender, ContextWindowItemsChangedEventArgs e) =>
        Add($"{e.Change}: {e.Items.Count} items, {Card.UsedTokens:N0} tokens");

    private void OnCompacted(object? sender, ContextWindowCompactedEventArgs e) =>
        Add($"Compacted ({e.Reason}): {e.FoldedCount} messages, {e.FoldedTokens:N0} → {e.SummaryTokens:N0} tokens");

    private void OnModelChanged(object? sender, ContextWindowModelChangedEventArgs e) =>
        Add($"Model: {e.OldModel?.Name} → {e.NewModel?.Name}");

    private void Add(string entry)
    {
        _entries.Add(entry);
        if (_entries.Count > 3)
        {
            _entries.RemoveAt(0);
        }
        Log.Text = string.Join("\n", _entries);
    }
}
```

```xml
<arc:ContextWindow>
    <arc:ContextWindow.Models>
        <arc:ContextWindowModel Id="heron-2" Name="Heron 2" Window="256000" Reserve="16000" />
    </arc:ContextWindow.Models>
    <arc:ContextWindowItem Category="System" Label="Style guide and instructions" Tokens="2400" />
    <arc:ContextWindowItem Category="Files" Label="handbook/billing.md" Tokens="14600" />
    <arc:ContextWindowItem Category="Messages" Label="Outline the refunds page" Tokens="8200" />
</arc:ContextWindow>
```

```csharp
card.ItemsChanged += (_, e) => log.Add($"{e.Change}: {e.Items.Count} items");
card.Compacted += (_, e) => log.Add($"Folded {e.FoldedCount} messages into {e.SummaryTokens} tokens ({e.Reason})");
```

The card rewrites `Items` as it goes: a send or an attachment inserts an item, a compaction removes the folded
messages and adds to the summary. `ItemsChanged` follows each of these with the new items and what changed them,
`Compacted` reports what was folded, the summary it became and the tokens before and after, and `ModelChanged` follows
the pill. `SelectedModel` is two way. `UsedTokens`, `FreeTokens`, `CanCompact` and `Phase` are read only and bindable.

### Driving it from your app

In a real session the items come from your app. Leave `Turns` and `Files` empty to hide Send message and Attach file,
and add real items with `AddItem`: it inserts the item where its category belongs and runs the same wave, status and
threshold check as the built-in actions. Changes you make to `Items` or to an item's `Tokens` show at once, quietly:
no status line and no automatic compaction.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ContextWindowHostDrivenDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="16" Margin="0,12">
        <!-- No turns or files: Send message and Attach file hide, and the app adds real items with AddItem. A summarizer
             reports the summary's size, and the switch turns automatic compaction off. -->
        <arc:ContextWindow x:Name="Card" Compacted="OnCompacted" />
        <WrapPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center" ItemSpacing="12" LineSpacing="12">
            <arc:Button Content="Add a reply" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Click="OnAddReply" />
            <arc:Button Content="Add a file" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Click="OnAddFile" />
            <arc:Switch x:Name="AutoSwitch" Content="Compact on its own" IsChecked="True" IsCheckedChanged="OnAutoChanged"
                        VerticalAlignment="Center" />
        </WrapPanel>
        <TextBlock x:Name="Log"
                   HorizontalAlignment="Center"
                   TextAlignment="Center"
                   TextWrapping="Wrap"
                   FontSize="13"
                   Text="Add replies until the window passes 80%."
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class ContextWindowHostDrivenDemo : UserControl
{
    private int _reply;
    private int _file;

    public ContextWindowHostDrivenDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Card.Models.Add(ContextWindowDemoData.Models().Last());
        Card.Items.AddRange(ContextWindowDemoData.Items());
        // Your summarizer knows the real size; this one says 5% of what it folds, at least 2,000 tokens.
        Card.Summarizer = folded => Math.Max(2_000, folded.Sum(item => item.Tokens) / 20);
    }

    private void OnAddReply(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        var (label, tokens) = ContextWindowDemoData.Replies[_reply++ % ContextWindowDemoData.Replies.Length];
        Card.AddItem(new ContextWindowItem(ContextWindowCategory.Messages, label, tokens));
    }

    private void OnAddFile(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        Card.AddItem(new ContextWindowItem(ContextWindowCategory.Files, $"exports/batch-{++_file}.json", 6_500));
    }

    private void OnAutoChanged(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        Card.AutoCompact = AutoSwitch.IsChecked == true;
    }

    private void OnCompacted(object? sender, ContextWindowCompactedEventArgs e)
    {
        Log.Text = $"Folded {e.FoldedCount} messages ({e.FoldedTokens:N0} tokens) into {e.SummaryTokens:N0}; " +
                   $"{e.Before:N0} → {e.After:N0} tokens used.";
    }
}
```

```csharp
// The summary your summarizer will write: here 5% of the folded tokens, at least 2,000.
card.Summarizer = folded => Math.Max(2_000, folded.Sum(item => item.Tokens) / 20);
card.AddItem(new ContextWindowItem(ContextWindowCategory.Messages, "Summarize the open tickets", 9_400));
```

`Summarizer` returns the summary's size for the messages being folded; without one the card uses 6% of them between
4K and 24K. Use `Compacted` to run your own summarization. `AutoCompact` turns the automatic folding off: the status
line still says when the threshold was passed, and Compact now stays available. `KeepRecentMessages` sets how many of
the newest messages survive a compaction (two by default).

### A different threshold

`Threshold` is the share of the window at which compaction runs (0.8 by default). The dashed line sits on the row
boundary nearest to it, so 0.6 draws it after row 6 and 0.75 after row 8, while the check itself uses the exact value.
Warnings start at 85% of the threshold.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ContextWindowThresholdDemo">
    <!-- Compaction at 60% (the line moves up to row 6, sends warn from 51%) and the newest four messages kept. -->
    <arc:ContextWindow Threshold="0.6" KeepRecentMessages="4" Margin="0,12" />
</UserControl>
```

### Narrow containers

The layout follows the card's content width, which is its width less 24px of padding on each side. Up to 640px of
content the legend moves under the grid, the cells tighten (2px apart with a 2px radius instead of 3) and the legend
takes the full width. Up to 420px the model pill moves under the readout. The actions wrap; Compact now moves to the
start of a new line when it no longer fits beside the others, and the status line wraps.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ContextWindowNarrowDemo">
    <!-- In a 360px column the legend moves under the grid, the cells tighten, the model pill moves under the readout and
         the actions wrap. -->
    <arc:ContextWindow Width="360" HorizontalAlignment="Center" Margin="0,12" />
</UserControl>
```

### Reduced motion

Under reduced motion the cells and the numbers change at once, the status line is replaced without a fade, the
conversation does not dim, and a compaction lands right away. Every status is still announced in order.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ContextWindowReducedMotionDemo">
    <!-- Under reduced motion cells and numbers change at once, a compaction lands right away and every status is still
         announced. -->
    <arc:ContextWindow arc:ArcMotion.Level="Reduced" Margin="0,12" />
</UserControl>
```

### Content guidelines

Name the parts by what they are in your product, and keep the status sentences short: they are read aloud on every
change. Item labels show only in the status line, quoted for messages, so use a few words.

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| User message #42 | Outline the refunds page |
| /Users/me/projects/docs/handbook/billing.md | handbook/billing.md |
| Context compaction has been completed successfully | Folded 279K into a 17K summary |
| Model gpt-like-large-2025 | Heron 2 |

`Labels` takes a `ContextWindowLabels` object with every word the card shows or announces, including the legend names
and the status sentences. Sentences with numbers are functions, so the word order can change in other languages:

```csharp
card.Labels = new ContextWindowLabels
{
    Messages = "Chat",
    Folded = (folded, summary) => $"{folded} folded into a {summary} summary"
};
```

### Best practices

**Do**

- Feed the real usage of a session: the system prompt, every tool definition, attached files and memory, the summary
  and each turn with the tool results it produced.
- Set the reserve to the largest output you request, so the grid shows the room the reply needs.
- Pass a `Summarizer` that reports the real summary size once your summarizer has run.
- Keep two or three models in the menu, with marks that are generic glyphs rather than vendor logos.

**Avoid**

- Rebuilding `Items` on a timer. Each change animates; update the items that changed instead.
- Presenting the sample session as real numbers. It is made up.
- Using the grid for anything but one window. It always has 200 cells; its proportions only make sense for one budget.

### Common questions

**Why does a small part sometimes have no cells?** Cells are counted from running totals, so a part smaller than half a
cell can round to nothing while the total stays exact. The legend always shows its tokens.

**Why does the summary not shrink?** A compaction adds its summary to the existing one, and summaries are never folded.
Remove or replace the summary item in `Items` when your app rewrites it.

**What happens when I switch to a bigger model?** The grid rearranges, the status line names the new model and window,
and nothing folds.

**Why are Send message and Attach file missing?** They hide when `Turns` or `Files` is empty outside the sample.

**Can the window overflow?** Yes. The readout passes 100%, free space reads 0, and the parts that do not fit before the
reserve get no cells.

## API reference

### ContextWindow

A model's context window as a fixed budget of 200 cells (20 × 10) that fills in reading order: the system prompt, tool definitions, files and memory, the summary and the conversation, then free space, with the output reserve held as outlined cells at the end. A dashed line marks the compaction threshold. The header reads the tokens used, the window, the percentage and the free tokens, with a pill to switch models; a legend lists every part with its tokens and share; Send message, Attach file and Compact now change the window, and a status line says what happened. Crossing the threshold after a send or an attachment, or switching to a model the window overfills, folds every message but the newest two into one summary (about 6% of them, between 4K and 24K), and the space comes back. The card rewrites `Items` as it goes and raises `ItemsChanged`, `Compacted` and `ModelChanged`. Given no data at all it shows an invented sample session with three sample models (`ContextWindowSamples`).

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Models` | `AvaloniaList<ContextWindowModel>` | `null` | Defines the `Models` property. |
| `SelectedModel` | `ContextWindowModel?` | `null` | Defines the `SelectedModel` property. |
| `Items` | `AvaloniaList<ContextWindowItem>` | `null` | Defines the `Items` property. |
| `Turns` | `AvaloniaList<ContextWindowTurn>` | `null` | Defines the `Turns` property. |
| `Files` | `AvaloniaList<ContextWindowTurn>` | `null` | Defines the `Files` property. |
| `Threshold` | `double` | `0.8` | Defines the `Threshold` property. |
| `Summarizer` | `Func<IReadOnlyList<ContextWindowItem>, long>?` | `null` | Defines the `Summarizer` property. |
| `KeepRecentMessages` | `int` | `2` | Defines the `KeepRecentMessages` property. |
| `AutoCompact` | `bool` | `true` | Defines the `AutoCompact` property. |
| `Labels` | `ContextWindowLabels` | – | Defines the `Labels` property. |
| `Phase` | `ContextWindowPhase` | – | *Read-only.* Defines the `Phase` property. |
| `UsedTokens` | `long` | – | *Read-only.* Defines the `UsedTokens` property. |
| `FreeTokens` | `long` | – | *Read-only.* Defines the `FreeTokens` property. |
| `CanCompact` | `bool` | – | *Read-only.* Defines the `CanCompact` property. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ModelChanged` | `ContextWindowModelChangedEventArgs` | Defines the `ModelChanged` routed event. |
| `Compacted` | `ContextWindowCompactedEventArgs` | Defines the `Compacted` routed event. |
| `ItemsChanged` | `ContextWindowItemsChangedEventArgs` | Defines the `ItemsChanged` routed event. |

Pseudo-classes: `:summarizing`, `:warning`, `:over`, `:stacked`, `:compact-header`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

### ContextWindowModel

A model the `ContextWindow` can switch to: its window and the part of it held back for the reply, in tokens, with a name and a mark for the model menu. Data only; replace the object to change a model on screen.

### ContextWindowItem

One thing in the context window: the system prompt, a tool definition, a file, the summary or a conversation turn, with its size in tokens. Items are grouped by `Category` in the grid, so their order matters only within a category. Changing a property updates the card at once.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Id` | `string` | `""` | Defines the `Id` property. |
| `Category` | `ContextWindowCategory` | `Messages` | Defines the `Category` property. |
| `Label` | `string` | `""` | Defines the `Label` property. |
| `Tokens` | `long` | `0` | Defines the `Tokens` property. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### ContextWindowTurn

A turn that Send message adds (a message with the tool results and the reply it produced), or a file that Attach file adds. Send and Attach take them in order and start over after the last.

### ContextWindowLabels

Every word a `ContextWindow` shows or announces, in English by default: the readout, the legend, the caption under the grid, the actions, the status line and the accessible names. Replace the instance to translate or reword; sentences with numbers are functions so that word order can change. Token counts and percentages arrive already formatted ("31K", "80").

### ContextWindowCompactedEventArgs

Arguments of `Compacted`: what was folded, the summary it became and the totals around it.

Derives from `RoutedEventArgs`: every member of `RoutedEventArgs` works as well.

### ContextWindowModelChangedEventArgs

Arguments of `ModelChanged`.

Derives from `RoutedEventArgs`: every member of `RoutedEventArgs` works as well.

### ContextWindowItemsChangedEventArgs

Arguments of `ItemsChanged`: the items after a send, an attachment, an added item or a compaction.

Derives from `RoutedEventArgs`: every member of `RoutedEventArgs` works as well.

The enums:

| Type | Values |
|---|---|
| `ContextWindowCategory` | `System`, `Tools`, `Files`, `Summary`, `Messages` |
| `ContextWindowPhase` | `Idle`, `Summarizing` |
| `ContextWindowCompactReason` | `Manual`, `Threshold`, `ModelSwitch` |
| `ContextWindowChange` | `Sent`, `Attached`, `Added`, `Compacted` |

`ContextWindowSamples` holds the sample session (`CreateModels()`, `CreateItems()`, `CreateTurns()`,
`CreateFiles()`), so a page can start from it and change one part.

## Accessibility

- The card is a group named "Context window". The grid is one image whose name describes it in full: the model, the
  tokens used of the window, every part with its tokens and the threshold. It updates with every change, not with
  every frame of a roll.
- The readout is read as one line ("436K of 1M tokens, 44% used, 500K free"). The legend is a list named "Context
  breakdown" whose rows read their name, tokens and share, so nothing depends on color.
- The pill is named after the model and its window and says that it changes the model. The menu's models are radio
  items with the selected one checked.
- Every send, attachment, model switch and compaction is announced through a polite live region, and every status has
  an icon as well as words.
- While messages fold every action is off. Instead of letting keyboard focus fall to the page, the card keeps it on a
  hidden holder named after the status and hands it back when the compaction lands: to the action that had it, or to
  Send message when that one is off.
- Keyboard focus shows a 2px ring; pointer focus shows none.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` | Move through the model pill, Send message, Attach file and Compact now |
| `Enter` / `Space` on the pill | Open the model menu on the selected model |
| `Up` / `Down` on the pill | Open the model menu |
| `Up` / `Down` in the menu | Move between the models, wrapping around |
| `Enter` / `Space` in the menu | Choose the model, close the menu and return to the pill |
| `Escape` in the menu | Close the menu and return to the pill |
| `Enter` / `Space` on an action | Send, attach or compact |

## Motion

- New tokens recolor their cells in a short wave from the first changed cell: 9ms per cell for a message added at the
  end, 3ms per cell for a file inserted in the middle and for the cells a compaction frees, never more than 360ms. Each
  cell turns in 240ms on the standard curve, mixing its colors in OKLab.
- A model switch recolors every changed cell in one pass from the first cell, 1.4ms per cell.
- While messages fold, the conversation dims from the oldest message to the newest (each cell to 0.35 and back to 0.5
  over 720ms, at most 6ms apart and 420ms in all). When the summary lands the cells are fully opaque again at once and
  recolor in the 3ms wave.
- The large number, the percentage and the legend's tokens and shares roll to their new values over 400ms on an
  ease-out curve, from whatever they show at that moment, so quick repeated sends never jump backwards. The free tokens,
  the window and the captions change at once.
- The status line crossfades in place: the old line fades out in 100ms while the new one fades in over 160ms and rises
  3px.
- Pointing at a legend row lights its cells and fades the other cells to 0.28 and the other rows to 0.45 in 160ms.
- The model menu grows from the pill on the CSS spring and the chevron turns over with it.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cells | Recolor in a wave | Change at once | Change at once |
| Numbers | Roll over 400ms | Change at once | Change at once |
| Status line | Crossfades | Replaced | Replaced |
| Folding | Dims for 700ms, then lands | Lands at once | Lands at once |
| Automatic compaction | After 540ms or 600ms | At once | At once |
| Legend hover | Fades in 160ms | At once | At once |

## Related

- `Progress` for a single allowance with a label.
- `PromptCache` for how a shared prompt prefix is reused across requests.
- `AgentLoop` for how an agent gathers context step by step.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `Progress` | One number against one limit is enough |
| `PromptCache` | You explain caching rather than budgeting |
| `AgentLoop` | You explain how an agent works, not what fills its window |

# Data flow

> Events stream from their sources through a queue and a batch transform into a warehouse and live dashboards.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/data-flow

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.DataFlowEventPipelineDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12">
        <arc:DataFlow x:Name="Flow" StepChanged="OnStepChanged" />
        <WrapPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center" ItemSpacing="12" LineSpacing="12">
            <arc:Button Content="0.5×" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Click="OnHalfSpeedClick" />
            <arc:Button Content="1×" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Click="OnNormalSpeedClick" />
            <arc:Button Content="2×" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Click="OnDoubleSpeedClick" />
            <arc:Button Content="Start over" Variant="Ghost" Size="Small" Click="OnRestartClick" />
            <TextBlock x:Name="Status"
                       Text="Step 1 of 3"
                       FontSize="13"
                       TextWrapping="Wrap"
                       VerticalAlignment="Center"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
        </WrapPanel>
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class DataFlowEventPipelineDemo : UserControl
{
    public DataFlowEventPipelineDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
    }

    private void OnStepChanged(object? sender, IllustrationStepChangedEventArgs e)
    {
        Status.Text = $"Step {e.Step + 1} of {Flow.StepCount}";
    }

    private void OnHalfSpeedClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        Flow.Speed = 0.5;
    }

    private void OnNormalSpeedClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        Flow.Speed = 1;
    }

    private void OnDoubleSpeedClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        Flow.Speed = 2;
    }

    private void OnRestartClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        Flow.Restart();
    }
}
```

## When to use

`DataFlow` explains how events move through a data platform: from the products and services that emit them, through
an event stream and a batch transform, into a warehouse and the live views built on top of it. It is an illustration,
not a monitor. It sits on a documentation page, an onboarding screen or an empty state, where the reader needs to
understand the pipeline before any real data exists.

- **Onboarding for an analytics product**: a first-run screen that shows where events come from (a web app, a mobile
  app, a billing webhook) before the customer connects their first source. The diagram answers "where does my data
  go" without a setup wizard.
- **Data platform documentation**: a page that describes an ingestion architecture, such as a Kafka topic that feeds a
  validation job and a lakehouse table. The caption and the labels name the real components of the platform.
- **Empty states in an operations console**: a "no events yet" panel on a pipeline page. The animation tells the user
  that the pipeline is wired up and waiting for traffic, which a blank table does not.
- **Explaining a filter step**: a privacy or quality rule that drops part of the traffic before it is stored. The
  red packets that fade out at the transform node show what the rule removes, without a table of rules.
- **Release notes and changelog pages**: a short visual for a feature that adds a stage to the pipeline, such as a new
  enrichment step, placed next to the text that describes it.

## When not to use

- **Plotting real volumes over time**: use `LineChart` or `BarChart` from the Charts category. The counters in
  `DataFlow` tell a story; they are not measurements, and the illustration does not accept your metrics.
- **A fixed sequence of steps with a current position**: use `Stepper` for a setup wizard or an ingestion job that the
  user moves through with Next and Back. `DataFlow` loops on its own and has no way to move between steps.
- **A live status of your pipeline**: use `Alert` or `Badge` with the actual state of each job, and a table for lag
  and failures. A looping diagram cannot report that a job is failing.
- **A page with many animated illustrations**: each one redraws its canvas on every frame while it plays, so keep only
  one or two running on a screen and use the reduced-motion poster for the rest.
- **A process with branches decided by users or by data**: use `Timeline` for a history of what happened, or a flow
  diagram in the documentation. `DataFlow` shows one fixed route with one filter branch.

## Usage

Playback starts when the illustration is loaded. The caption under the diagram follows the story, and the play button
pauses it. The control needs no data to run: it ships with a default story about a web app, a mobile app and webhooks
feeding a warehouse and a dashboard.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:DataFlow Label="Event pipeline" />
</UserControl>
```

`DataFlow` derives from `Illustration`, which derives from Avalonia's `TemplatedControl`. It is therefore a normal
control: it has a `Label` that names it for assistive technology, it takes focus, it can be styled through its
theme and it can be placed in any layout. The shared illustration base supplies the scene clock, the looping
script, the caption, the play button and the reduced-motion poster, so the control itself only describes the
diagram and its numbers.

### Anatomy

1. **Sources** (left column, `Sources`): one to four cards of 150 by 52 scene units with a rounded 12 px corner, an
   icon, a title and a detail line. The defaults are Web app (page views), Mobile (taps and sessions) and Webhooks
   (partner events). Sources are spread evenly down the column; the spacing shrinks as the count grows.
2. **Event stream** (`Labels.Stream`, `Labels.StreamDetail`): the queue that receives every event. A meter under the
   card fills as events arrive and empties when the transform takes a batch. The meter is capped at 24 events.
3. **Throughput readout**: the events per second under the stream card, smoothed over half-second samples and
   formatted with `Labels.EventsPerSecond`.
4. **Transform** (`Labels.Transform`, `Labels.TransformDetail`): the batch step, with a busy ring while a batch is in
   flight. Filtered events are removed here.
5. **Warehouse** (`Labels.Warehouse`, `Labels.WarehouseDetail`): the upper branch on the right. Its readout under the
   card counts the rows stored, formatted with `Labels.Rows`.
6. **Dashboards** (`Labels.Realtime`, `Labels.RealtimeDetail`): the lower branch on the right, with a readout that
   counts updates pushed to the live views, formatted with `Labels.Updates`.
7. **Caption line** (`IsCaptionVisible`): one line of secondary text under the diagram, in the small type size and
   the secondary text color. It changes with each step.
8. **Play button** (`IsPlaybackButtonVisible`): a round button at the bottom right of the frame, hidden in the still
   poster.
9. **Frame**: a surface card with a 1 px border in the border color and the surface corner radius, on a dotted
   backdrop. The padding is 20 px on the sides and top and 14 px at the bottom. The scene scales to the width the
   control is given, so the diagram keeps its proportions in a narrow column.

Packets are drawn in the accent color. Packets on a filtered path turn to the danger color and fade out, and the
routes that carry events to the live views use the success color.

### Throughput and filtering

`EventsPerSecond` sets how fast the sources emit events. It takes values from 1 to 60 and defaults to 18; values
outside the range are clamped. `FilterRatio` sets the share of events the transform removes. It takes values from 0 to
0.5 and defaults to 0.14, so about one event in seven is filtered by default.

```xml
<arc:DataFlow EventsPerSecond="8" FilterRatio="0.3" />
```

The transform takes one batch of up to eight events each second, so a rate above eight events per second makes the
meter climb toward its capacity. The illustration explains the shape of the pipeline; it does not simulate backpressure,
lag or dropped events, and it should not be used to estimate capacity.

### Sources and labels

`Sources` takes one to four `DataFlowSource` values. Each value has a `Title` and an optional `Detail` line. A list
with no items falls back to the default sources, and a list longer than four uses its first four entries. The
`Labels` property takes a `DataFlowLabels` object with every visible word of the diagram: the node titles and details,
the readout formats and the step captions. Set only the properties you need; the others keep their English defaults.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.DataFlowOwnSourcesDemo">
    <arc:DataFlow x:Name="Flow" EventsPerSecond="8" FilterRatio="0.3">
        <arc:DataFlow.Labels>
            <arc:DataFlowLabels Warehouse="Lakehouse"
                                WarehouseDetail="parquet"
                                Realtime="Alerts"
                                RealtimeDetail="on-call" />
        </arc:DataFlow.Labels>
    </arc:DataFlow>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class DataFlowOwnSourcesDemo : UserControl
{
    public DataFlowOwnSourcesDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Flow.Sources = [new DataFlowSource("Checkout", "orders"), new DataFlowSource("CRM", "contacts")];
    }
}
```

Changing `Sources` or `Labels` rebuilds the diagram, so set both when the page loads, not on every data refresh.

### Playback and speed

`IsPlaying` plays and pauses the story. It is two way: the control writes the value when the person presses the play
button or Space, and an app can read it or bind it. `Speed` scales the scene clock and takes values from 0.25 to 4.
`Play()`, `Pause()` and `Restart()` do the same from code. `Restart()` resets the counters and returns to the first
step.

```xml
<arc:DataFlow Speed="2" IsPlaying="{Binding IsPipelineRunning}" />
```

```csharp
flow.Speed = 0.5;
flow.Restart();
```

The scene clock pauses while the control is off-screen, hidden or detached, so an illustration on a scrolled-away
tab costs nothing until it is visible again.

### Following the story

`Step` and `StepCount` describe the position in the loop. The story has three steps, and the caption changes with
each one:

| Step | Caption | What is highlighted |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | The ingest caption with the source count | The connections from the sources to the stream |
| 1 | The transform caption: validated and enriched, bad events filtered out | The connection into the transform |
| 2 | The store caption: clean events land in the warehouse and update live dashboards | The connections to the warehouse and to the dashboards |

`StepChanged` gives the new step and its caption. `RowsStored` and `EventsFiltered` count what has reached the
warehouse and what the transform removed since the story started. Both are read-only; the illustration keeps them
for its own story.

```csharp
flow.StepChanged += (_, e) => status.Text = $"Step {e.Step + 1} of {flow.StepCount}: {e.Caption}";
```

### Reduced motion

Under reduced motion (or Off) the illustration is a still poster of its steady state. Every connection is highlighted,
one packet rests halfway along each route to show the direction of travel, and the caption summarizes the whole story.
The play button is hidden because there is nothing to play. Use the poster on pages where motion is not wanted, and
in print or static exports.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.DataFlowReducedMotionDemo">
    <arc:DataFlow arc:ArcMotion.Level="Reduced" />
</UserControl>
```

### Driving it from data

`DataFlow` does not read a stream of events; it draws the story it was given. In an application, bind the sources
and the labels from a view model when they come from configuration, and keep the playback state with them. The
example below uses CommunityToolkit.Mvvm and shows the pipeline of an analytics product that is still being set up.

```csharp
public partial class PipelineSetupViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    [ObservableProperty]
    private bool _isPipelineRunning = true;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private double _speed = 1;

    public IReadOnlyList<DataFlowSource> Sources { get; } =
    [
        new("Checkout", "orders"),
        new("Mobile app", "sessions"),
        new("Billing webhooks", "invoices")
    ];

    public DataFlowLabels Labels { get; } = new()
    {
        Warehouse = "Lakehouse",
        WarehouseDetail = "parquet",
        Realtime = "Alerts",
        RealtimeDetail = "on-call"
    };
}
```

```xml
<arc:DataFlow Sources="{Binding Sources}"
              Labels="{Binding Labels}"
              IsPlaying="{Binding IsPipelineRunning}"
              Speed="{Binding Speed}" />
```

Bind `Sources` and `Labels` once for each configuration. A new list or labels object rebuilds the diagram, so do not
replace them on a timer. Use `IsPlaying` to tie the story to the page state, for example to pause it while a
settings dialog is open.

### Example: data platform overview

A settings page for an analytics product. The illustration sits above a short description of the connected sources,
so the reader sees the same three sources that the text names. The warehouse is a lakehouse table in Parquet, and
the second branch feeds an alerting view for the on-call team. The labels use the platform's own names, and the
detail lines say what each stage does rather than repeating the title.

![A data pipeline with three sources, a lakehouse store and an alerting branch](https://docs.tkcode.si/shots/Docs/Illustrations/DataFlow/images/DataPipeline.webp)

```xml
<StackPanel Width="760" Spacing="16">
    <TextBlock Text="Event pipeline"
               FontSize="16"
               FontWeight="SemiBold"
               Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
    <TextBlock Text="Web, mobile and webhook events are validated every second and stored in the lakehouse."
               TextWrapping="Wrap"
               Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
    <arc:DataFlow Label="Event pipeline for Acme Analytics">
        <arc:DataFlow.Labels>
            <arc:DataFlowLabels Stream="Event queue"
                                StreamDetail="buffered"
                                Transform="Validate"
                                TransformDetail="schema · enrich"
                                Warehouse="Lakehouse"
                                WarehouseDetail="parquet"
                                Realtime="Alerts"
                                RealtimeDetail="on-call" />
        </arc:DataFlow.Labels>
    </arc:DataFlow>
</StackPanel>
```

The example keeps the default sources, which is why the caption above names web, mobile and webhook events. To show
the platform's own sources, assign `Sources` in code as shown in the view model above. The screenshot is the still
steady-state frame, so its readouts (12,480 rows, 3,120 updates) are the illustration's own poster values, not measurements.

### Content guidelines

Write the node titles as the nouns of your architecture (Event queue, Lakehouse, Alerts), and keep the detail lines
short, lowercase and specific (schema · enrich, parquet, on-call). Name real sources, not types: "Checkout orders"
tells the reader more than "Source 1". Write the captions and the labels in the same tense as the rest of the page.

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| Data Source 1 | Checkout |
| Processing | Validate |
| Database | Lakehouse |
| Real-time | Alerts |
| Events are processed in our amazing pipeline | Events are validated every second and stored in the lakehouse |
| 18 events/s throughput achieved | 18 events/s |
| Your data is flowing | Waiting for the first events |

Keep the labels at or under about 16 characters so the node cards keep one line; a longer title wraps and the card
looks crowded. Do not write a sentence into a detail line. Use `Summary` for the description of the whole story and
keep it to one sentence.

### Best practices

**Do**

- Name the real components of your platform in `Labels`, because readers compare the diagram with the architecture
  page they came from. A generic "Processing" node teaches nothing.
- Use two or three sources. The default spacing is widest at two and three, and four cards leave little room for the
  detail lines at a narrow width.
- Keep the story at its default rate on documentation pages. A rate of 18 events per second reads as activity without
  drawing attention away from the text.
- Pause the story with `IsPlaying` when it is off the page the reader is focused on, and let the poster frame replace
  it for users who turn off motion.

**Avoid**

- Using the counters as metrics. `RowsStored` and the readouts count the story the illustration tells, so a dashboard
  that shows them as real volumes would report numbers that do not come from your system.
- Placing several playing illustrations on one screen. Each one redraws its canvas on every frame, so the cost adds up
  and the screen competes for attention.
- Changing `Sources` or `Labels` on a timer or on every data refresh. Each change throws the diagram away and builds
  it again, so the story never gets to play out.
- Writing a sentence into a label. The cards are small, and long text wraps and crowds the frame.
- Relying on the diagram for status. It shows the shape of a pipeline, not whether one job is healthy, so report
  failures with `Alert` or a table.

### Common questions

**How do I rename the three steps in the caption?** Set the `Labels` properties `TransformStep` and `StoreStep`, and
`Summary` for the whole story. The first step's caption is built from `Ingest`, which takes the number of sources, so
change that function if the wording should differ.

**Why does the story always show the same numbers?** The illustration uses a fixed seed, so every run plays the same
way. The counters start at the same values on each restart, and the sources emit at intervals that are jittered but
repeatable. This keeps documentation screenshots and tests stable.

**Can I feed the readouts with my own counts?** No. `RowsStored` and `EventsFiltered` are read-only, and the readout
values are kept by the illustration. To show real volumes, use `LineChart` or `AnimatedCounter` with the numbers from
your metrics store.

**How do I show a different number of sources without changing the code?** Bind `Sources` to a collection from
configuration, as shown in the view model above. Values past the fourth are ignored, and an empty list brings back the
three default sources.

**Does the event pool grow during a long run?** No. Packets come from a fixed pool that is reused, so a story that
runs for hours keeps the same number of packet objects.

## API reference

### DataFlow

An animated data pipeline: events leave their sources, queue up in an event stream, are validated and enriched in batches (some are filtered out) and land in a warehouse, with part of them pushed to live dashboards. Readouts show throughput and what has been stored.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `EventsPerSecond` | `double` | `18` | How many events per second the sources emit (1–60). |
| `FilterRatio` | `double` | `0.14` | Share of events the transform filters out (0–0.5). |
| `Sources` | `IReadOnlyList<DataFlowSource>?` | `null` | The event sources (1–4); defaults to a web app, a mobile app and webhooks. |
| `Labels` | `DataFlowLabels` | – | Node titles, details and caption text of the diagram; set it to rename or translate the scene. |
| `IsPlaying` | `bool` | `true` | Whether the illustration plays (two way). Paused, it holds the current frame. |
| `Speed` | `double` | `1` | Playback speed (0.25–4). |
| `Label` | `string?` | `"Data flow illustration"` | The accessible name of the illustration. |
| `IsCaptionVisible` | `bool` | `true` | Shows the caption line under the diagram. |
| `IsPlaybackButtonVisible` | `bool` | `true` | Shows the play / pause button. |
| `Caption` | `string` | – | *Read-only.* What the current step shows (also the accessible help text). |
| `Step` | `int` | – | *Read-only.* The current step (0-based); see `StepCount`. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `StepChanged` | `IllustrationStepChangedEventArgs` | Raised when the story moves to another step. |

Pseudo-classes: `:playing`, `:poster`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

### DataFlowLabels

Every visible word of a `DataFlow` (override for another language or domain).

Sources use the `DataFlowSource` record.

| Property | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `Title` | `string` | The name shown on the source card, such as "Web app" |
| `Detail` | `string?` | The optional second line on the card, such as "page views"; null shows only the title |

## Accessibility

- `Label` is the accessible name of the illustration. Name the pipeline in it, for example "Event pipeline for Acme
  Analytics", because the diagram itself has no text a reader can navigate.
- The illustration takes focus and shows a 2px focus ring around the frame when it is focused.
- The current caption is exposed as the help text, so a screen reader hears the step's description when the control
  is focused.
- Caption changes are not announced. The story loops, and announcing each step would repeat it endlessly.
- The labels and readouts are the text the diagram shows. Keep them meaningful on their own, because a reader who
  cannot see the animation still gets the node titles and the caption.
- Under reduced motion the poster frame shows the steady state with the summary caption, which gives the same
  information without any movement.

### Keyboard

The illustration takes focus with Tab. Once it has focus, these keys control the story:

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` | Move focus to or from the illustration |
| `Space` or `Enter` | Play or pause the story |
| `R` | Start the story over from its first step |

## Motion

- Events travel along the connections as small packets. The stream's meter fills as events arrive and empties as
  batches leave, and the readouts count up.
- Each step lights the connections that belong to it, and the other connections fade back.
- Filtered packets turn red and fade out shortly after they leave the transform.
- The play button and the caption change with a short transition, and the step's nodes emphasize as they become active.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| Events travel along the connections | Animated packets on every route | Still poster, one packet resting on each route | Still poster |
| The current step's connections light up | Fade in over 0.4 s | Shown as the steady state (all lit) | Shown as the steady state |
| Filtered events | Turn red and fade out near the transform | Not shown | Not shown |
| Readouts (events/s, rows, updates) | Count up during the story | Show the poster values | Show the poster values |
| Play button | Visible; toggles playback | Hidden | Hidden |

## Related

- `PaymentFlow` for a single request that is approved or declined, with the same frame and playback controls.
- `MultiRegionFailover` for traffic that moves between regions when one fails.
- `VectorSearch` for a question answered from its nearest documents.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `LineChart` / `BarChart` | You plot real measurements over time |
| `Stepper` | The user moves through a fixed sequence with Next and Back |
| `Timeline` | You show a history of events in order, with their times |
| `Alert` | You state the status of a real pipeline or job in text |
| `PaymentFlow` | The story is one request that is approved or declined |
| `VectorSearch` | The story is a question answered by its nearest documents |
