# Vector search

> A question is embedded as a vector and answered with its nearest documents by cosine similarity.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/vector-search

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.VectorSearchHelpCentreSearchDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12">
        <arc:VectorSearch x:Name="Search" />
        <WrapPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center" ItemSpacing="12" LineSpacing="12">
            <arc:Button Content="0.5×" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Click="OnHalfSpeedClick" />
            <arc:Button Content="1×" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Click="OnNormalSpeedClick" />
            <arc:Button Content="2×" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Click="OnDoubleSpeedClick" />
            <arc:Button Content="Start over" Variant="Ghost" Size="Small" Click="OnRestartClick" />
        </WrapPanel>
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class VectorSearchHelpCentreSearchDemo : UserControl
{
    public VectorSearchHelpCentreSearchDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
    }

    private void OnHalfSpeedClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        Search.Speed = 0.5;
    }

    private void OnNormalSpeedClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        Search.Speed = 1;
    }

    private void OnDoubleSpeedClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        Search.Speed = 2;
    }

    private void OnRestartClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        Search.Restart();
    }
}
```

## When to use

`VectorSearch` is an animated illustration of semantic search. It types a question, turns it into a vector, places it on
a map of document vectors and lists the documents closest to it as ranked answers. Put it beside the copy that explains
a search feature, where a reader needs to see why an answer matched a question that shares no exact words with it.

- **Help-centre landing pages for a billing product**: a visitor asks "why was I charged twice" and sees the article on
  duplicate payments rank first, although the words differ. The picture sets expectations before the visitor uses the
  real search box.
- **Onboarding for an AI-assisted support console**: a new support agent sees how the assistant chose its suggested
  articles, which builds trust in the ranking and explains why a rephrased question can change the answers.
- **Product tours for an analytics workspace**: a tour step that introduces "Ask your data" shows how a plain question
  finds the saved reports it is about.
- **Developer documentation for a search feature**: a tutorial on embeddings, cosine similarity and top-k results uses
  the live map and the ranked list as the reference picture for the text beside it.
- **Training for knowledge-base authors**: the ranked list and its similarity scores show authors which titles and
  keywords carry a match, so they can improve the articles that rank poorly.

## When not to use

- **Answering real customer questions**: the built-in index uses hashed words and character trigrams, not a trained
  model, so it is a teaching tool. Use your own search service and show its results with `SearchField`.
- **Exact or filtered lookups**: an invoice number, an order ID or a date range needs an exact index with filters. Use
  `SearchField` with a normal query, not a similarity ranking.
- **Plotting real measurements**: the map is a two-dimensional projection of text similarity, with no units or axes.
  Use `LineChart` or `BarChart` for values that people compare.
- **Long result lists people act on**: rank, score and document metadata in columns are easier to scan, sort and export
  in `Table`.
- **Explaining a pipeline rather than a search**: when the picture should show how documents are collected, validated
  and stored, use `DataFlow`, which is built for that story.
- **Dense dashboards or pages with several animated pictures**: each illustration redraws its canvas every frame while
  it plays. Use a `Card` with a short static explanation instead.

## Usage

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:VectorSearch />
</UserControl>
```

`VectorSearch` derives from `Illustration`, which derives from `TemplatedControl`. The base class runs the looping
story on a scene clock, gives the control focus, adds the play and pause button and the caption line, and raises
`StepChanged` as the story moves between its four steps. The clock pauses while the control is off-screen, hidden or
detached, so a story below the fold costs nothing until it scrolls into view. `VectorSearch` adds the search itself: it
builds an in-memory index of its documents, embeds each question, ranks the documents by cosine similarity and draws
the result. The default story cycles through three example questions, so one control shows the whole path from a
question to its answers.

### Anatomy

The diagram is drawn on one canvas that scales to the width the control is given, so the proportions below hold at any
size. The padding of the frame is 20 px on the sides and top and 14 px at the bottom.

1. **Query box** (`Query` at run time): the question at the top left, typed one character at a time with a caret.
2. **Embedding model node** (`Labels.Model`, with `Labels.ModelDetail` under it): a card with a brain icon. It shows a
   busy ring while the model works on the question.
3. **Vector strip**: 16 cells that show the question's vector as a fixed projection of the whole vector. The cells
   fill from the query's real embedding, so the same question always fills them the same way.
4. **Document map**: each document is a point, grouped by its `Topic` with the topic name drawn faintly in the group.
   The query is a point placed among its nearest documents, with a ring that reaches the farthest answer.
5. **Result list**: a header (`Labels.Header`, "Top 3 · cosine similarity" by default), then one row per answer with
   its rank, title, similarity score to two decimals and a bar. Titles that are too long for the row are cut with an
   ellipsis on a single line.
6. **Caption line** (`Caption`): one line under the diagram in the secondary text color at the small type size. It
   names the current step. Hide it with `IsCaptionVisible="False"`.
7. **Play button** (`IsPlaybackButtonVisible`): a 28 px ghost circle at the bottom right that swaps between a play and
   a pause icon. It is hidden under the still frame.
8. **Frame**: a Surface card with a 1 px Border line, the surface corner radius and a dotted backdrop. A 2 px focus ring
   in the focus color appears around the frame when the control has keyboard focus.

Node cards use a corner radius of 12 px. The colors all come from ArcDesign tokens (the surface, border, text, accent
and status colors), so the control follows the light and dark themes without any color setting.

### Number of answers

`TopK` sets how many answers the list shows. The value is clamped to the range 1 to 5, and the default is 3. The list is
always best first, and the map draws the ring to the farthest answer, capped at 110 scene units so that one outlier
does not swallow the map.

```xml
<arc:VectorSearch TopK="4" />
```

Use 3 on a help page. It fits a reading column, and the best match stands out from the rest. Use 5 only when the list
itself is the point of the explanation, because the ring grows with every answer. Changing `TopK` rebuilds the scene,
so set it once when the page is built rather than on every interaction.

### Your own documents and questions

`Documents` takes `VectorSearchDocument` values. The record has three parts: `Title` is the text the result list shows,
`Topic` groups the document on the map and labels its cluster, and `Keywords` (optional) adds words to the document's
embedding without showing them. `Queries` takes the questions the story cycles through. Both replace the defaults when
they are set and have at least one item.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:generic="using:System.Collections.Generic"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.VectorSearchYourDocumentsDemo">
    <arc:VectorSearch x:Name="Recipes" TopK="4">
        <arc:VectorSearch.Queries>
            <generic:List x:TypeArguments="x:String">
                <x:String>quick salmon dinner</x:String>
                <x:String>something sweet with chocolate</x:String>
                <x:String>eggs for breakfast</x:String>
            </generic:List>
        </arc:VectorSearch.Queries>
    </arc:VectorSearch>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class VectorSearchYourDocumentsDemo : UserControl
{
    public VectorSearchYourDocumentsDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Recipes.Documents =
        [
            new VectorSearchDocument("Overnight oats with berries", "Breakfast", "oats morning quick"),
            new VectorSearchDocument("Fluffy buttermilk pancakes", "Breakfast", "pancakes morning griddle"),
            new VectorSearchDocument("Shakshuka with feta", "Breakfast", "eggs tomato morning"),
            new VectorSearchDocument("Avocado toast three ways", "Breakfast", "toast avocado morning quick"),
            new VectorSearchDocument("Weeknight chicken curry", "Dinner", "chicken curry rice spice"),
            new VectorSearchDocument("One-pan lemon salmon", "Dinner", "fish salmon oven quick"),
            new VectorSearchDocument("Mushroom risotto", "Dinner", "rice mushroom parmesan"),
            new VectorSearchDocument("Slow-cooker beef chili", "Dinner", "beef beans spice"),
            new VectorSearchDocument("Dark chocolate mousse", "Dessert", "chocolate cream sweet"),
            new VectorSearchDocument("Lemon tart", "Dessert", "lemon pastry sweet"),
            new VectorSearchDocument("Banana bread", "Dessert", "banana baking sweet"),
            new VectorSearchDocument("No-churn vanilla ice cream", "Dessert", "vanilla cream frozen sweet")
        ];
    }
}
```

```csharp
search.Documents =
[
    new VectorSearchDocument("Cancel and refund an annual plan", "Billing", "money back refund"),
    new VectorSearchDocument("Reset two-factor authentication", "Security", "phone lost new device"),
    new VectorSearchDocument("Track a delayed parcel", "Shipping", "late package courier"),
];
search.Queries = ["get my money back", "I lost my phone"];
```

Write titles as the answer a reader would click, and put the words readers actually type in `Keywords`. Keywords
count toward the match, so a title can stay short and plain. Keep the topic names few and broad (four to six is a
good range): each topic becomes one cluster on the map, and many small clusters make the map hard to read.

### Searching for a question

`Search(query)` shows a question at once: it cancels the scheduled steps, embeds the question and starts its story. A
blank or white-space string does nothing. After the answers of that question, the story carries on with the questions
in `Queries`. `Query` is the question on screen, `Results` holds its answers, best first, and `ResultsChanged` is raised
each time the answers of a question are known, including for the questions the story plays on its own.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.VectorSearchAskYourOwnDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12">
        <WrapPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center" ItemSpacing="12" LineSpacing="12">
            <arc:SearchField x:Name="Question"
                             Placeholder="Ask the help centre"
                             Width="360"
                             SearchSubmitted="OnSearchSubmitted" />
            <arc:Button Content="Search"
                        Variant="Primary"
                        Size="Small"
                        Click="OnSearchClick" />
        </WrapPanel>
        <arc:VectorSearch x:Name="Search" ResultsChanged="OnResultsChanged" />
        <TextBlock x:Name="Answers"
                   Text="Try “change my password” or “invoice for last month”."
                   FontSize="13"
                   TextWrapping="Wrap"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class VectorSearchAskYourOwnDemo : UserControl
{
    public VectorSearchAskYourOwnDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
    }

    private void OnSearchSubmitted(object? sender, SearchSubmittedEventArgs e)
    {
        Ask();
    }

    private void OnSearchClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        Ask();
    }

    private void OnResultsChanged(object? sender, EventArgs e)
    {
        Answers.Text = string.Join("  ·  ", Search.Results.Select(r => $"{r.Rank}. {r.Document.Title} ({r.Score:0.00})"));
    }

    private void Ask()
    {
        if (!string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(Question.Text))
        {
            Search.Search(Question.Text);
        }
    }
}
```

Each `VectorSearchResult` has `Document`, `Score` (the cosine similarity, from −1 to 1) and `Rank` (1 is the best match).
`Results` is a plain property and does not notify, so read it in the `ResultsChanged` handler rather than binding to it.

### Labels

`Labels` takes a `VectorSearchLabels` object with the visible words: the model name and its detail line, the list
header, and the four step captions (`Typing`, `Embedding`, `Comparing` and `Answers`). Its `Summary` is the caption of
the still frame. Replace the whole object to change the words, because the header and the model node are read when the
scene is built.

```csharp
search.Labels = new VectorSearchLabels { Model = "Text model", Header = k => $"Best {k} matches" };
```

### Playback, speed and captions

The illustration plays by default. `IsPlaying` is two-way: bind it to a toggle that the page shows, or call `Play()` and
`Pause()`. `Restart()` starts the story from its first step. The preview at the top of this page uses speed buttons, and
the same settings are available to you in code.

| Member | Use it to |
|---|---|
| `Speed` | Scale the story clock from 0.25 to 4 (default 1). Slow it for a tour that explains each step, and speed it up for a teaser. |
| `IsCaptionVisible` | Hide the caption line when the page already explains the steps in its own text. |
| `IsPlaybackButtonVisible` | Hide the play and pause button on a page where the picture must stay still. |
| `Caption` and `Step` | Read the current caption and its step (0 to 3). The read-only values also back the accessible help text. |
| `StepChanged` | React to each step, for example to highlight the matching sentence in the text beside the picture. |
| `Label` | Name the illustration for assistive technology (default "Vector search illustration"). |

### Reduced motion

Under reduced motion the illustration is a still frame of the answers to the first question. The caption summarizes the
whole story, the play button is hidden, and no caret blinks. Set the level on the control, as the demo does, or on a
parent that holds the page's motion setting.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.VectorSearchReducedMotionDemo">
    <arc:VectorSearch arc:ArcMotion.Level="Reduced" />
</UserControl>
```

### Using motion with restraint

The story helps when a reader has to see a path: the question becomes a vector, the vector finds its neighbours, and
the neighbours become the answers. Keep it on a page where the reader has time to watch one question finish, which takes
about 6.5 seconds in Full motion at speed 1. It distracts when it sits beside a form, a checkout step or a live
dashboard, where the eye should stay on the field the reader is filling in. Place at most one or two illustrations on a
page, and let the story run only while the picture is on screen. The clock already pauses off-screen, so a long page
does not pay for an illustration that the reader has not reached yet.

### Binding to a view model

In an MVVM app the view model owns the documents and the questions, and the control only shows them. The view model
below uses CommunityToolkit.Mvvm. The control's `Documents`, `Queries`, `TopK` and `Labels` are one-way inputs: a new
value rebuilds the index and the map. `IsPlaying` is the only two-way value.

```csharp
public partial class HelpCentreViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    [ObservableProperty]
    private IReadOnlyList<VectorSearchDocument> _articles = [];

    [ObservableProperty]
    private IReadOnlyList<string> _sampleQuestions = [];

    [ObservableProperty]
    private string _topMatchTitle = string.Empty;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private bool _isStoryPlaying = true;

    public void Load()
    {
        // Assigning a new list raises PropertyChanged, so the control rebuilds its index once.
        Articles =
        [
            new VectorSearchDocument("Cancel and refund an annual plan", "Billing", "money back refund"),
            new VectorSearchDocument("Reset two-factor authentication", "Security", "phone lost new device"),
            new VectorSearchDocument("Track a delayed parcel", "Shipping", "late package courier"),
        ];
        SampleQuestions = ["get my money back", "I lost my phone"];
    }
}
```

```xml
<arc:VectorSearch Documents="{Binding Articles}"
                  Queries="{Binding SampleQuestions}"
                  IsPlaying="{Binding IsStoryPlaying, Mode=TwoWay}"
                  TopK="3"
                  Label="Help centre search illustration" />
```

`Search` is a method and `Results` is a plain property, so they stay in code-behind. Forward the top match to the view
model from the `ResultsChanged` handler, and call `Search` from the handler of the page's search field:

```csharp
// In the code-behind of the view that hosts the control.
Search.ResultsChanged += (_, _) =>
{
    ViewModel.TopMatchTitle = Search.Results.Count > 0 ? Search.Results[0].Document.Title : string.Empty;
};

private void OnAskSubmitted(object? sender, SearchSubmittedEventArgs e)
{
    Search.Search(e.Query);
}
```

### Data shape and performance

- **The item model**: a `VectorSearchDocument` is a record of `Title`, `Topic` and `Keywords`. The index embeds each
  document once, when the index is built. Each question is embedded when it is searched, so a question costs one
  embedding and one ranking pass over the documents.
- **Size**: the default index holds 32 help-centre articles in four topics. The index is in memory and has no paging or
  persistence. The map runs a fixed number of stress-minimization steps (300) over the document set. It is recomputed
  only when the documents change, not on each question. The illustration is designed for a teaching-sized index: a real
  help centre with thousands of articles belongs in your search service, and this control explains how it works.
- **Updates**: replacing `Documents`, `Queries`, `TopK` or `Labels` rebuilds the scene. Editing the items of a list in
  place does not, because the control does not observe the list. Replace the list with a new one instead.
- **Formatting**: the rank and the score text use the invariant culture with two decimals (for example "0.87"), so the
  numbers read the same in every locale. Translate the words through `Labels`, not the numbers.

### Example: help-centre search for a billing question

A help centre landing page for a subscription product. The search field asks the visitor to type a question, and the
illustration beneath it explains how the articles are ranked. The text is short and says what the picture means, the
search field has a placeholder that shows the kind of question to ask, and the illustration keeps the default story so
the reader sees three different questions match three different topics. The width of 720 px suits a reading column
on a desktop page, and the frame keeps its padding at every width.

![A help-centre search illustration beside a search field and a short explanation of the ranked articles](https://docs.tkcode.si/shots/Docs/Illustrations/VectorSearch/images/HelpCentreSearch.webp)

```xml
<StackPanel Width="720" Spacing="16">
    <TextBlock Text="Help centre"
               FontSize="20"
               FontWeight="SemiBold"
               Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
    <arc:SearchField Placeholder="Ask the help centre" />
    <arc:VectorSearch TopK="3" />
    <TextBlock Text="Articles are ranked by how closely their meaning matches your question."
               FontSize="13"
               TextWrapping="Wrap"
               Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
</StackPanel>
```

### Content guidelines

- **Label**: name what the picture shows, in sentence case: "Help centre search illustration", not "Vector search".
  Screen readers read it first, so it should make sense without the picture.
- **Captions and headers**: write for the reader, not the mathematics. The default header uses the term "cosine
  similarity", which suits developers. Customer pages usually say what the number means.
- **Document titles**: write the answer a reader would click, in sentence case, and keep the title short enough to fit
  one line of the result list. Put synonyms and misspellings readers use in `Keywords`.
- **Topics**: a short noun in sentence case, the same word the navigation uses: "Billing", "Security", "Shipping".

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| Top 3 · cosine similarity | Best 3 matches |
| Vector search illustration | Help centre search illustration |
| Embedding model | Text model |
| Query | Question |
| The vector is compared with 32 document vectors | Comparing 32 articles |

### Best practices

**Do**

- Put the illustration next to the real search field, so readers can connect the picture with their own question. The
  picture explains the ranking; it does not perform the search for the page.
- Keep `TopK` at 3 on help and marketing pages. A short list fits the column and makes the best match easy to see.
- Put the words readers type into `Keywords`. They improve the match without adding clutter to the titles the reader sees.
- Expose the same answers as text when the page needs them for accessibility, using `Results`, in a list the reader can
  navigate. The drawn list is not an accessible list.

**Avoid**

- Presenting the built-in ranking as the quality of your product's search. The embeddings are hashed words and
  trigrams, so the examples teach the method rather than measure your content.
- Several story illustrations on one screen. Each redraws its canvas every frame while it plays, so the page becomes
  heavy and the reader cannot follow more than one story at once.
- Editing items in place in a document list. The control rebuilds only when the list is replaced, so the map and the
  results keep the old documents.
- Long titles that rely on the full text. The result list cuts a long title with an ellipsis on one line, so the
  important words must come first.

### Common questions

**What happens when I call `Search` while the story is running?** The scheduled steps are cancelled and the question is
shown at once. The story then carries on with the `Queries` list from the point where it was, so a single search does
not restart the loop.

**Why does the map move when I add one document?** The map is laid out from all the documents at once, so one new
document changes the positions of the others. The ranking does not change in the same way: the order of the answers
depends only on the cosine similarity between the question and each document.

**Which words count toward a match?** Words are lowercased, common words such as "the", "my" and "how" are dropped, and
plural, `-ing` and `-ed` endings are trimmed. Each word and its character trigrams go into the vector, and trigrams
count for 0.3 of a word, so "bill" and "billing" meet part way. `Keywords` count the same way but are never shown.

**Can I stop the story and still read the answers?** Yes. Set `IsPlaying="False"` to hold the current frame, and read
`Results` at any time. Under reduced motion the control shows the answers to the first question as a still frame.

## API reference

### VectorSearch

An animated semantic search: a question is typed, embedded into a vector, dropped into a map of document vectors, and its nearest neighbours by cosine similarity become the ranked answers. The search is real (hashed bag-of-words embeddings, cosine ranking, a principal-component map), so `Search` works with any question.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Documents` | `IReadOnlyList<VectorSearchDocument>?` | `null` | The documents to search (defaults to 32 help-centre articles in four topics). |
| `Queries` | `IReadOnlyList<string>?` | `null` | The questions the story cycles through. |
| `TopK` | `int` | `3` | How many answers are shown (1–5). |
| `Labels` | `VectorSearchLabels` | – | Step titles, badges and caption text of the diagram; set it to rename or translate the scene. |
| `IsPlaying` | `bool` | `true` | Whether the illustration plays (two way). Paused, it holds the current frame. |
| `Speed` | `double` | `1` | Playback speed (0.25–4). |
| `Label` | `string?` | `"Vector search illustration"` | The accessible name of the illustration. |
| `IsCaptionVisible` | `bool` | `true` | Shows the caption line under the diagram. |
| `IsPlaybackButtonVisible` | `bool` | `true` | Shows the play / pause button. |
| `Caption` | `string` | – | *Read-only.* What the current step shows (also the accessible help text). |
| `Step` | `int` | – | *Read-only.* The current step (0-based); see `StepCount`. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ResultsChanged` | `EventHandler?` | Raised when the answers of a question are known. |
| `StepChanged` | `IllustrationStepChangedEventArgs` | Raised when the story moves to another step. |

Pseudo-classes: `:playing`, `:poster`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

### VectorSearchLabels

Every visible word of a `VectorSearch` (override for another language or domain).

The two records that the page uses are public companion types in the same namespace. Their parameters come from their
source, in the order of the primary constructor.

| Record | Parameters | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `VectorSearchDocument` | `Title`, `Topic`, `Keywords` (optional) | A document to search. `Title` is shown in the list, `Topic` names its cluster, and `Keywords` count toward its embedding but are not shown. |
| `VectorSearchResult` | `Document`, `Score`, `Rank` | One answer. `Score` is the cosine similarity from −1 to 1, and `Rank` is 1 for the best match. |

## Accessibility

- `Label` is the accessible name, and the current caption is exposed as the help text.
- The illustration takes keyboard focus and shows a 2 px focus ring around its frame.
- The caption and the drawn result list are not announced when they change. The ranked answers are also available as
  text through `Results`, so show them in a list that users can read and navigate.
- Under reduced motion the control shows its still frame, so no content depends on the motion to be understood.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` | Move focus to or from the illustration |
| `Space` or `Enter` | Play or pause the story (when the illustration itself has focus) |
| `R` | Start the story over from its first step |

## Motion

- The question is typed letter by letter with a blinking caret, then the embedding model works on it.
- The vector strip fills one cell at a time, and the query point flies into the document map.
- A radius grows until it reaches the last answer, the answers light up in rank order and their rows rise into the list.
- A question takes about 6.5 seconds in Full motion at speed 1, then the next question of the story begins.
- Reduced motion and Off show the answers to the first question as a still frame, with no caret and no typing. The
  play button is hidden.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| The question appears | Typed letter by letter with a blinking caret | Shown in full, no caret | Shown in full, no caret |
| The model works on the question | The model node shows a busy ring | No busy ring | No busy ring |
| The vector strip | Cells fill one at a time | Final values | Final values |
| The query point | Flies from the strip into the map | Placed at its final position | Placed at its final position |
| The answers | The radius grows to the last answer and the neighbours light up in rank order | Final ring and answers | Final ring and answers |
| The result rows | Rise into the list in rank order | Listed at once | Listed at once |

## Related

- `SearchField` for the question input in an app, and for showing your own results.
- `DataFlow` for how the documents that feed a search are collected and stored.
- `Table` for showing a long list of results with their scores.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `SearchField` | The reader types a question into your product and your own search service answers it |
| `ExpandingSearch` | Search sits in a page header and opens on demand |
| `Table` | The results are a long list that people sort, filter or export |
| `DataFlow` | The story is how documents are collected, validated and stored |
| `LineChart` | The values are measurements that people compare over time |
| `Card` | A static explanation is enough and an illustration would compete with the page |

# Agent loop

> An agent gathers context, calls tools and checks the result, going round the loop until the task is done.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc.Special`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc.Special --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/agent-loop

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.AgentLoopSampleRunDemo">
    <!-- No iterations: the card plays its built-in sample run (three loops, an invented model and tools). -->
    <arc:AgentLoop />
</UserControl>
```

## When to use

`AgentLoop` explains how a tool-using AI agent works: it gathers context, takes an action with a tool, checks the
result, and goes round again until the check passes. A bright head with a soft trail circles a ring past three
stations around the model. Context blocks join a stack beside the ring, tool calls drop out of the ring and resolve,
and checks either pass or send the loop round once more. The run ends with the ring drawn in and a summary. It is an
illustration of a run you write, not a log of a real agent, and nothing in it calls a service.

- **Product and documentation pages for an agent feature**: a page that tells customers how an assistant fixes a
  failing build or triages a support ticket. The card shows why the agent takes several passes instead of answering
  at once.
- **Explaining failure and retry**: a first check that fails with a retry note, or a tool call that times out and is
  narrowed down in the same step, shows that an agent recovers by looking again, not by guessing.
- **Onboarding for an internal agent platform**: a short visual for engineers who are about to write their first
  tools, next to the text that describes how the platform feeds tool results back into the model.
- **Landing pages and talks**: a self-contained, accessible animation that runs once when it scrolls into view and
  ends on a still summary that reads well as a screenshot.
- **A recap of a finished run**: under reduced motion, or with the story jumped to its end, the card is a summary of
  the context the agent built up, the last tool call and the last check.

## When not to use

- **Streaming a real agent's steps**: use `ChatThread` or a log view with the agent's actual messages and tool output.
  `AgentLoop` plays the run you describe; it does not accept events while it plays.
- **A single tool call in a transcript**: show the call as a row in your chat or log. The card is about the loop, and a
  run of one call with one passing check says little.
- **Searching over many candidate thoughts**: use `ReasoningTree`, which scores and prunes branches. The agent loop is
  one path that repeats.
- **Showing how full a context window is**: the token total here counts the blocks of the story; it is not a budget or a
  meter, and it never warns about a limit.
- **Status of a live job**: use `Alert`, `Badge` or a table with the real state. A finished illustration cannot report
  that a production run failed.

## Usage

The card plays a built-in sample run when it is given no iterations: three loops of an invented triage, with an
invented model and tools. It starts the first time it is mostly in view and stops on its done state.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:AgentLoop />
</UserControl>
```

`AgentLoop` derives from `Explainer`, the base of the animated AI explainers in the Special package, which derives
from Avalonia's `TemplatedControl`. The base supplies the story clock, `IsPlaying`, `Speed`, `AutoPlay`, `IsLooping`,
the play, step and restart buttons, the polite live region and the reduced-motion opening state. `AgentLoop` adds the
iterations, the ring and its stations, the lanes and the context stack. Register the package with `UseArcSpecial()`
next to `UseArcControls()`.

The numbers in the card (tokens, durations, results) are illustrative. Say so in the text around it when the page is
about a real product.

### Anatomy

1. **Header**: the `Title` (default "Agent loop") on the left, and the status on the right: an icon with Ready,
   Running, Paused, Done or Stopped. Under them, the caption keeps room for two lines: `Task` while the run is ready
   or running, and `Summary` once it ends.
2. **Ring**: a 1.5px track with three small chevrons that point clockwise. The radius is at most 94px; on narrow
   columns it shrinks so the lower labels fit beside their nodes.
3. **Stations**: Gather context at the top, Take action at the lower right and Verify at the lower left, each a node
   with a label and an icon. An idle station is muted, the active one is filled in the accent with a thin ring and a
   calm shimmer on its name, and a visited one keeps an accent outline.
4. **Head and trail**: a bright dot that eases from station to station, dragging a gradient trail that grows and
   shrinks with each trip and is gone when the head lands.
5. **Center**: the model's mark and name (`Model`), and a line under them: Ready, the loop counter, or the ending
   ("Done in 3 loops", or "Stopped after 2 loops").
6. **Pins and lanes**: a short line drops from each lower station to its lane. Tool calls land in the lane under Take
   action and checks in the lane under Verify, each as a chip. A dashed placeholder fills a lane until its first chip.
7. **Context stack**: the heading with the running token total, and one slot per loop. Each block shows a mark, a
   label, its tokens and a detail line. A dashed placeholder fills the stack until the first block joins.
8. **Footer**: play or pause, Next step and Restart on the left, and the 0.5×, 1× and 2× speed control on the right.
   `AreControlsVisible` hides the whole row.

### The story and its timing

The run is a timeline built once from the iterations, so pausing, stepping and replaying are exact. At 1× speed each
loop takes:

| Part | Time |
|---|---|
| At Gather context (the block joins 0.1 s in) | 0.85 s |
| Trip to Take action | 0.7 s |
| At Take action, one call | 1.35 s |
| Each further call in the same loop | + 1.15 s |
| Trip to Verify | 0.5 s |
| At Verify (the check drops 0.1 s in) | 0.95 s |
| Trip back to Gather context | 0.7 s |

A loop is therefore 3.7 s plus its time at Take action, and the run starts 0.22 s after Ready. The sample run has one,
two and two calls, so it takes 0.22 + 5.05 + 6.2 + 6.2 = 17.67 seconds. A call drops 0.1 s after the head arrives,
shows "Calling" and its tool for 0.75 s, then turns into its result; the next call takes its place in the same lane.
The run ends when the head is back at Gather context after the last loop. If the last check passed, the ring draws in
and the status reads Done; if it failed, the ring stays neutral and the status reads Stopped.

The token total is the sum of the blocks gathered so far. Counts under 1,000 show as whole numbers and larger ones
with one decimal and a K, so 1,400 + 5,800 + 8,600 reads 15.8K at the end of the sample run.

### Your own run

Give the card its loops as content. Each `AgentLoopIteration` has a `Gather` block, one to three calls as its content,
and a `Verify` check. Marks are 24 by 24 stroked glyphs such as the `ArcIcons` members.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.AgentLoopBuildFixDemo">
    <arc:AgentLoop Title="Build fix"
                   Task="Fix the failing nightly build and tell #builds."
                   Summary="The build cache key had changed. Clearing it fixed the build, and #builds has the details.">
        <arc:AgentLoop.Model>
            <arc:ExplainerModel Name="Quill 2 Mini" />
        </arc:AgentLoop.Model>
        <arc:AgentLoopIteration>
            <arc:AgentLoopIteration.Gather>
                <arc:AgentLoopContext Label="Build log" Detail="Stage 3 of 7 failed" Tokens="2900" Mark="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Terminal}" />
            </arc:AgentLoopIteration.Gather>
            <arc:AgentLoopCall Tool="CI" Action="Read pipeline run" Result="Cache key changed" Mark="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.GitBranch}" />
            <arc:AgentLoopIteration.Verify>
                <arc:AgentLoopCheck Passed="False" Note="Fix not applied yet" />
            </arc:AgentLoopIteration.Verify>
        </arc:AgentLoopIteration>
        <arc:AgentLoopIteration>
            <arc:AgentLoopIteration.Gather>
                <arc:AgentLoopContext Label="Pipeline file" Detail="build.yml, 62 lines" Tokens="1700" Mark="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.FileCode}" />
            </arc:AgentLoopIteration.Gather>
            <arc:AgentLoopCall Tool="CI" Action="Clear cache and rerun" Result="Build passed in 4m 05s" Mark="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.GitBranch}" />
            <arc:AgentLoopCall Tool="Chat" Action="Post update" Result="Posted in #builds" Mark="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.MessageCircle}" />
            <arc:AgentLoopIteration.Verify>
                <arc:AgentLoopCheck Passed="True" Note="Build green, team told" />
            </arc:AgentLoopIteration.Verify>
        </arc:AgentLoopIteration>
    </arc:AgentLoop>
</UserControl>
```

```xml
<arc:AgentLoop Task="Fix the failing nightly build and tell #builds."
               Summary="The build cache key had changed. Clearing it fixed the build.">
    <arc:AgentLoopIteration>
        <arc:AgentLoopIteration.Gather>
            <arc:AgentLoopContext Label="Build log" Detail="Stage 3 of 7 failed" Tokens="2900"
                                  Mark="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Terminal}" />
        </arc:AgentLoopIteration.Gather>
        <arc:AgentLoopCall Tool="CI" Action="Read pipeline run" Result="Cache key changed"
                           Mark="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.GitBranch}" />
        <arc:AgentLoopIteration.Verify>
            <arc:AgentLoopCheck Passed="False" Note="Fix not applied yet" />
        </arc:AgentLoopIteration.Verify>
    </arc:AgentLoopIteration>
    <!-- More loops; the last one should pass its check. -->
</arc:AgentLoop>
```

`Task` is the caption while the run plays. `Summary` is the caption at the end; leave it unset to show a count of
loops and tool calls. Every loop reserves a slot in the context stack from the start, so the card does not grow while
it plays. Two to four loops read best.

Set `Status="Error"` on a call to show a failed call: the spinner turns into a cross, the result reads as the reason
and screen readers hear "failed". Follow it with a second call in the same loop to show the agent trying again.

### A run that stops

When the last loop's check fails, the run ends stopped: the status shows Stopped, the ring stays neutral and the center
says how many loops ran. Without a `Summary`, the caption says the run stopped after so many loops and calls.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.AgentLoopStoppedRunDemo">
    <!-- The last check fails, so the run ends stopped: the ring stays neutral and the summary says why. -->
    <arc:AgentLoop Title="Flaky test"
                   Task="Find out why the checkout test fails one run in ten."
                   Summary="Two passes found no cause. The agent stopped and left the test quarantined for a person to look at.">
        <arc:AgentLoopIteration>
            <arc:AgentLoopIteration.Gather>
                <arc:AgentLoopContext Label="Test history" Detail="7 failures in 70 runs" Tokens="3100" Mark="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.ChartBar}" />
            </arc:AgentLoopIteration.Gather>
            <arc:AgentLoopCall Tool="CI" Action="Rerun with logs" Result="Passed 20 times in a row" Mark="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.GitBranch}" />
            <arc:AgentLoopIteration.Verify>
                <arc:AgentLoopCheck Passed="False" Note="Failure not reproduced" />
            </arc:AgentLoopIteration.Verify>
        </arc:AgentLoopIteration>
        <arc:AgentLoopIteration>
            <arc:AgentLoopIteration.Gather>
                <arc:AgentLoopContext Label="Test source" Detail="checkout.spec, 140 lines" Tokens="2200" Mark="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.FileCode}" />
            </arc:AgentLoopIteration.Gather>
            <arc:AgentLoopCall Tool="CI" Action="Run under load" Result="Runner ran out of time" Status="Error" Mark="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.GitBranch}" />
            <arc:AgentLoopCall Tool="Tracker" Action="Quarantine test" Result="Marked as flaky" Mark="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Flag}" />
            <arc:AgentLoopIteration.Verify>
                <arc:AgentLoopCheck Passed="False" Note="Cause still unknown" />
            </arc:AgentLoopIteration.Verify>
        </arc:AgentLoopIteration>
    </arc:AgentLoop>
</UserControl>
```

### Playback, steps and speed

`IsPlaying` and `Speed` are two way: the footer writes them and an app can bind them. `Speed` scales the story clock
(0 holds it still, at most 4); the footer offers 0.5×, 1× and 2×. Transitions such as a chip landing or the ring
drawing in keep their own pace at any speed. `Play()`, `Pause()`, `StepForward()` and `Restart()` do the same from
code.

Next step plays to the next beat and stops there: a new context block, each tool result, each check, and the end. It
plays at 2.5 times the speed (at least 2.5×), so a step is quick but still shows the trip. Restart goes back to Ready
and plays. `StationChanged` fires once each time the head reaches a station, with the station and the zero-based loop;
`Finished` fires when the run reaches its end.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.AgentLoopEventLogDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="16">
        <arc:AgentLoop x:Name="Loop"
                       AutoPlay="False"
                       AreControlsVisible="False"
                       StationChanged="OnStationChanged"
                       Finished="OnFinished" />
        <WrapPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center" ItemSpacing="12" LineSpacing="12">
            <arc:Button x:Name="PlayButton" Content="Play" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Click="OnPlayClick" />
            <arc:Button Content="Next step" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Click="OnStepClick" />
            <arc:Button Content="Start over" Variant="Ghost" Size="Small" Click="OnRestartClick" />
            <arc:Switch x:Name="Fast" Content="Double speed" IsCheckedChanged="OnFastChanged" VerticalAlignment="Center" />
        </WrapPanel>
        <TextBlock x:Name="Log"
                   HorizontalAlignment="Center"
                   TextAlignment="Center"
                   TextWrapping="Wrap"
                   FontSize="13"
                   Text="Press Play: each station the head reaches is logged here."
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class AgentLoopEventLogDemo : UserControl
{
    private readonly List<string> _entries = new();

    public AgentLoopEventLogDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Loop.PropertyChanged += (_, e) =>
        {
            if (e.Property == Explainer.IsPlayingProperty)
            {
                PlayButton.Content = Loop.IsPlaying ? "Pause" : "Play";
            }
        };
    }

    private void OnStationChanged(object? sender, AgentLoopStationChangedEventArgs e)
    {
        _entries.Add($"Loop {e.Loop + 1}: {e.Station}");
        if (_entries.Count > 4)
        {
            _entries.RemoveAt(0);
        }
        Log.Text = string.Join("  ·  ", _entries);
    }

    private void OnFinished(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        Log.Text = Loop.Phase == AgentLoopPhase.Stopped
            ? "Finished: stopped, the last check did not pass."
            : "Finished: done, the last check passed.";
    }

    private void OnPlayClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        if (Loop.IsPlaying)
        {
            Loop.Pause();
        }
        else
        {
            Loop.Play();
        }
    }

    private void OnStepClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        Loop.StepForward();
    }

    private void OnRestartClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        _entries.Clear();
        Log.Text = "Started over.";
        Loop.Restart();
    }

    private void OnFastChanged(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        Loop.Speed = Fast.IsChecked == true ? 2 : 1;
    }
}
```

```csharp
loop.StationChanged += (_, e) => log.Add($"Loop {e.Loop + 1}: {e.Station}");
loop.Finished += (_, _) => status.Text = loop.Phase == AgentLoopPhase.Done ? "Done" : "Stopped";
```

`Phase` is the state the status shows: Ready, Running, Paused, Done or Stopped. `IsLooping` plays the run again four
seconds after it ends.

### Narrow containers

The layout follows the card's own width, not the window's. From a 640px container the context stack sits in a column
beside the ring, with two lanes under it. Narrower, the stack moves under the ring, with two blocks per row from 460px
and one below. Below a 360px ring column the station labels drop their icons and shrink, and the two lanes merge into
one that shows the latest tool call or check. On the narrowest cards the two lower stations move further down the ring
so their labels fit, and the speed control wraps under the buttons.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.AgentLoopNarrowDemo">
    <!-- In a 340px column the context stack moves under the ring, the two lanes merge into one, the station labels drop
         their icons and the lower stations move further down the ring; the speed control wraps under the buttons. -->
    <arc:AgentLoop Width="340" HorizontalAlignment="Center" />
</UserControl>
```

### Reduced motion

Under reduced motion the card opens on its finished run: the ring drawn in, every block in the stack, the last chips
and the summary. Play again and Next step still work. The head jumps from station to station without a trail, and
every change applies in place without a drop or a fade. Because the run is played to its end at once when the card
opens, `StationChanged` fires for every station together at that moment, followed by `Finished`.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.AgentLoopReducedMotionDemo">
    <!-- Under reduced motion the card opens on its finished run; Play again and Next step still work, in place. -->
    <arc:AgentLoop arc:ArcMotion.Level="Reduced" />
</UserControl>
```

### Driving it from data

Bind `IterationsSource` when the loops come from a view model. A new collection, or a change to an observable one,
rebuilds the story. Before the card has been seen it rebuilds quietly, so autoplay still starts on first sight; after
that it starts over.

```csharp
public sealed class AgentDemoViewModel
{
    public ObservableCollection<AgentLoopIteration> Loops { get; } =
    [
        new(new AgentLoopContext("Support ticket", "Refund not received", 1200, ArcIcons.Inbox),
            [new AgentLoopCall("Billing", "Find the payment", "Refund issued on May 2", mark: ArcIcons.CreditCard)],
            new AgentLoopCheck(true, "Customer told"))
    ];
}
```

```xml
<arc:AgentLoop IterationsSource="{Binding Loops}"
               Task="Answer a refund question."
               Speed="{Binding Speed}" />
```

An empty `IterationsSource` shows the ring at rest with the controls off. `Labels` takes an `AgentLoopLabels` object
with every word the card shows or announces, including the station names; set only what you need.

### Content guidelines

Write the run so that every piece fits on one line: a context label of one to three words, a detail under about 30
characters, a call action of two to four words and a result under about 30 characters. Name the tools by what they
are in your product, and use generic glyphs, not brand marks.

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| Context | Build log |
| Retrieved the complete build log for analysis | Stage 3 of 7 failed |
| Tool call 1 | Read pipeline run |
| The tool returned a successful response | Cache key changed |
| Verification failed | Fix not applied yet |
| The agent has completed the task successfully | The cache key had changed. Clearing it fixed the build. |

Keep the station names to about two words; a longer name is cut beside its station. The task is one sentence; the
summary can take two lines.

### Best practices

**Do**

- Let the last loop pass its check, and let an earlier one fail with a retry note. The failed check is what explains
  why agents loop.
- Show one failed tool call followed by a narrower call in the same loop, because recovering inside a step is the
  second lesson of the diagram.
- Keep the run to two to four loops. More loops make the card taller and the story longer than readers will watch.
- Say in the copy that the run is illustrative, and match its tools to the ones your product really has.

**Avoid**

- Presenting the numbers as measurements. The tokens and timings tell a story and are not read from a model.
- Brand marks of real services in the chips. Use generic glyphs and name the tool in text.
- Replacing `IterationsSource` on a timer. Each change starts the run over.
- Several playing cards on one screen. Each one draws its ring on every frame while it plays.

### Common questions

**How long does the run take?** 0.22 s plus 3.7 s per loop plus 1.35 s at Take action, and 1.15 s more for each extra
call. Divide by the speed.

**Why does a step stop where it does?** Steps stop after each beat a reader can name: a block that joined, each result,
each check and the end. A call that starts is not a stop, because its result follows.

**Can the card show more than three calls in a loop?** No. Calls past the third are ignored, because the lane shows one
chip at a time and longer steps hide the story. Split the work across loops instead.

**What does a loop without calls do?** The head still stops at Take action for one call's time, and nothing lands in
the lane.

**How do I hide the model?** Set `Model` to null. The center then shows only the loop counter.

## API reference

### AgentLoop

An animated explainer of the agent loop: a bright head with a gradient trail circles a ring past three stations (Gather context, Take action, Verify) around the model. At Gather a context block joins the stack beside the ring and the token total counts up; at Take action one to three tool calls drop out of the ring on a pin and resolve; at Verify a check passes or sends the loop round again. The run ends done (the ring draws in, a check at the center, the summary as the caption) or stopped when the last check fails. Play, pause, step, restart and a 0.5× / 1× / 2× speed control drive it; under reduced motion it opens on its end. The run is sample data: nothing calls a real service.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `IterationsSource` | `IEnumerable<AgentLoopIteration>?` | `null` | Defines the `IterationsSource` property. |
| `Task` | `string?` | `null` | Defines the `Task` property. |
| `Summary` | `string?` | `null` | Defines the `Summary` property. |
| `Labels` | `AgentLoopLabels` | – | Defines the `Labels` property. |
| `Phase` | `AgentLoopPhase` | – | *Read-only.* Defines the `Phase` property. |
| `IsPlaying` | `bool` | `false` | Defines the `IsPlaying` property. |
| `AutoPlay` | `bool` | `true` | Defines the `AutoPlay` property. |
| `IsLooping` | `bool` | `false` | Defines the `IsLooping` property. |
| `Speed` | `double` | `1` | Defines the `Speed` property. |
| `AreControlsVisible` | `bool` | `true` | Defines the `AreControlsVisible` property. |
| `Title` | `string?` | `"Agent loop"` | Defines the `Title` property. |
| `Model` | `ExplainerModel?` | – | Defines the `Model` property. |
| `PlaybackLabels` | `ExplainerPlaybackLabels` | – | Defines the `PlaybackLabels` property. |
| `IsFinished` | `bool` | – | *Read-only.* Defines the `IsFinished` property. |
| `IsStepping` | `bool` | – | *Read-only.* Defines the `IsStepping` property. |
| `CanStep` | `bool` | – | *Read-only.* Defines the `CanStep` property. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `StationChanged` | `AgentLoopStationChangedEventArgs` | Defines the `StationChanged` routed event. |
| `Finished` | `RoutedEventArgs` | Defines the `Finished` routed event. |

Pseudo-classes: `:stopped`, `:empty`, `:playing`, `:stepping`, `:finished`, `:ready`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

### AgentLoopIteration

One pass round the loop: the context gathered, one to three tool calls made one after another, and the check. Calls are its content in XAML. Calls past the third are ignored; a loop with none still stops at Take action for the time of one call, with nothing dropping into the lane.

### AgentLoopContext

A block of context gathered at the start of a loop: a label, an optional detail and its size in tokens.

### AgentLoopCall

A tool call made at the Take action station: the tool, what it was asked to do and what came back.

### AgentLoopCheck

The check at the Verify station: passed, or a retry note that sends the loop round again.

### AgentLoopLabels

Every word an `AgentLoop` shows or announces, in English by default (the playback buttons are named by `PlaybackLabels`). Replace the instance to translate or reword; texts with numbers or names are functions so that the word order can change.

### AgentLoopStationChangedEventArgs

Arguments of `StationChanged`: the head reached a station.

Derives from `RoutedEventArgs`: every member of `RoutedEventArgs` works as well.

The enums:

| Type | Values |
|---|---|
| `AgentLoopStation` | `Gather`, `Act`, `Verify` |
| `AgentLoopCallStatus` | `Success` (default), `Error` |
| `AgentLoopPhase` | `Ready`, `Running`, `Paused`, `Done`, `Stopped` |

`AgentLoopDefaults` holds the sample run (`CreateIterations()`, `CreateModel()`, `Task`, `Summary`), so a page can
start from it and change one loop.

## Accessibility

- The card is a group named by its `Title`. The ring drawing (track, chevrons, pins, head and trail) is hidden from
  assistive technology; the station names, the center, the chips and the context blocks are real text.
- The context stack is a list named "Context blocks", read in the order the blocks were gathered. A block's token
  count is followed by the word "tokens".
- A result is read with the tool's name first ("Tracker returned: …"), and a failed call says "failed". A check shows
  an icon and the words "Check passed" or "Retry", so it never relies on color.
- The status pairs each state with an icon and a word: Ready, Running, Paused, Done and Stopped.
- A polite live region speaks each beat when you step or pause (a block that joined, a call in progress, a result, a
  check) and the summary at the end. It stays quiet while the run plays on its own.
- When stepping reaches the end, Next step turns off and keyboard focus moves to Restart instead of falling to the page.
- Keyboard focus shows a 2px ring around the buttons and the speed control; pointer focus shows none.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` | Move through play or pause, Next step, Restart and the speed control |
| `Enter` / `Space` on play | Play or pause; once the run ended, play it again |
| `Enter` / `Space` on Next step | Play to the next beat and stop there |
| `Enter` / `Space` on Restart | Start over from Ready and play |
| `Left` / `Right` (or `Up` / `Down`) on the speed control | Move between 0.5×, 1× and 2×, wrapping around |
| `Home` / `End` on the speed control | Choose 0.5× or 2× |

## Motion

- The head eases between stations (0.7 s, 0.5 s and 0.7 s at 1×) and drags a gradient trail along the ring that is
  longest halfway through a trip and gone when it lands, so it never sits still with a tail.
- The active station fills, a thin ring settles around its node, and its name carries a calm shimmer.
- A tool call drops out of the ring: the pin under Take action draws down in 180ms and the chip lands at its end with a
  6px drop and a slight scale, on a spring without bounce. Its spinner crossfades to a check or a cross. A second call
  takes the place of the first after it fades out in 80ms.
- A context block fades in with a short drop while the token total counts up over 500ms.
- The loop counter rolls its number; the status, the caption and the center line crossfade.
- At the end the ring draws in clockwise over 760ms and the head fades out. A stopped run leaves the ring neutral.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| Opening | Plays when first seen | Opens on the finished run | Opens on the finished run |
| Head between stations | Eases along the ring with a trail | Jumps at the end of each trip | Jumps at the end of each trip |
| Chips and blocks | Drop in on a spring, fade out when replaced | Appear in place | Appear in place |
| Token total | Counts up over 500ms | Jumps to the total | Jumps to the total |
| Station colors and chip borders | Change over 240ms (480ms for a new block) | Change at once | Change at once |
| Done ring | Draws in over 760ms | Shown drawn | Shown drawn |

## Related

- `ReasoningTree` for a search over candidate thoughts rather than a loop of tool calls.
- `PromptCache` for how a shared prompt prefix is reused across requests.
- `SpeculativeDecoding` and `MixtureOfExperts` for how a model produces its tokens.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `ChatThread` | You show a real conversation with an agent, message by message |
| `Timeline` | You list what a real run did, in order, with times |
| `Alert` | You report the state of a real job in text |
| `ReasoningTree` | The story is choosing between candidate thoughts |
| `DataFlow` | The story is data moving through a pipeline |

# Mixture of experts

> A router scores every expert for each token and sends it to its top choices, whose outputs blend into the result.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc.Special`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc.Special --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/mixture-of-experts

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.MixtureOfExpertsRoutingDemo">
    <!-- The default story: eight experts, fifteen tokens, top 2. Point at a token or an expert to hold the story on it. -->
    <arc:MixtureOfExperts MaxWidth="760" />
</UserControl>
```

## When to use

`MixtureOfExperts` explains how a sparse mixture-of-experts layer handles text: each token is scored by a router,
handed to its best one or two experts, and rebuilt from their outputs. It answers the question readers ask when they
first see a model described as "480B parameters, 30B active": which parameters run, and why most of them sit still
for any one token. It is an explainer, not a monitor: its scores, loads and parameter counts are illustrative, so
say so in the text around it.

- **Model documentation**: a page that introduces a sparse model and its active-parameter count. The header readout
  and the summary sentence show where the smaller number comes from.
- **Courses and onboarding**: a lesson on routing, where the reader switches between top 1 and top 2, points at a token
  to see its gate scores, and points at an expert to see which tokens it took.
- **Capacity and load balancing**: a note on why experts have a capacity and what happens to the tokens that do not
  fit. The skipped choices and the load balance bar make the trade-off visible.
- **Product pages for an inference platform**: a short visual next to the text that explains why a mixture-of-experts
  model is cheaper to serve than a dense one of the same size.
- **Talks and release notes**: a looping card that tells the whole story in under forty seconds with no narration.

## When not to use

- **Showing real routing statistics from your model**: use `BarChart` or `DataGrid` with the measured expert loads. The
  card plans its own small story from the scores it is given; it is not an instrument.
- **Choosing which model answers a request**: that is a model router in your product, a different idea at a different
  level. A model picker or a plain `Select` is the right control.
- **Explaining attention or tokenization**: the card shows tokens as given and says nothing about how text is split or
  which tokens attend to which. Use a diagram made for that.
- **Many cards on one screen**: each card animates while it plays. Keep one per page, or pause the others with
  `IsPlaying`.
- **Long sequences**: the story spends 2.2 seconds on each token. Fifteen to twenty tokens tell the story; a paragraph
  turns it into a wait.

## Usage

The card needs no data: it ships with an invented sentence of fifteen tokens and eight experts. It starts the first
time it is mostly on screen and loops: after the last token a summary rests for 3.6 seconds and the routing starts
over.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:MixtureOfExperts MaxWidth="760" />
</UserControl>
```

`MixtureOfExperts` derives from `Explainer`, the base of the animated AI explainers in the Special package, which
derives from Avalonia's `TemplatedControl`. The base supplies the story clock (`IsPlaying`, `Speed`, `IsLooping`,
`Play()`, `Pause()`, `Restart()`), the start-on-view behaviour, the play button and the polite live region; this
control describes the layer, plans the routes and draws them.

### Anatomy

1. **Header**: a switch between top 1 and top 2 (`TopK`), the active-parameters readout ("Active parameters 30B of
   480B", from `Parameters`) and the round play button.
2. **Input**: the token being routed, in a chip that slides in from the left. It dims once its packet has left for the
   router.
3. **Router**: a rounded box with one score bar and percentage per expert. Bars are proportional to the score itself,
   not to the largest score, so a 50% score fills half the track. The top choices take the first and second choice
   colors; the others stay muted.
4. **Gate lines**: one line from the router to each expert. The chosen lines light up in their choice's color; a line to
   a full expert turns into a dashed warning line.
5. **Expert tiles**: an icon, the expert's name and a counter of the tokens it has taken, with a thin capacity bar along
   the bottom. A chosen tile lights up in its choice's color; a full expert that skips the token turns dashed with a
   warning sign.
6. **Merge curves and point**: the outputs of the chosen experts curve into one point, then travel to the output.
7. **Output**: the token's output chip, with a dot for each expert that processed it. A token that passed through has a
   dashed chip and no dots.
8. **Sequence**: every token as a chip under a divider. Upcoming tokens are muted, the current one has a ring and the
   routed ones have a solid fill.
9. **Footer**: the route line (the token, an arrow, each choice with its weight) and a note that says it in words. On
   the right, the load balance readout and a bar with one segment per expert.

Under 568 pixels the stage turns to run from top to bottom: the router becomes a band of vertical bars over a row of
icon tiles. Under 640 pixels the load balance moves under the footer text, and under 480 pixels the padding tightens,
the readout takes its own line and the route line drops the token chip.

### The story

Each token takes 2.2 seconds at speed 1:

| Time | What happens |
|---|---|
| 0 s | The token becomes current and its chip slides in. The router still shows the previous scores, dimmed. The footer says the router is rating the experts. |
| 0.16 – 0.48 s | A neutral packet with a short trail travels to the router. |
| 0.48 s | The router shows the token's scores; the top choices take their colors and the footer shows the route. |
| 0.76 – 1.14 s | A packet in each choice's color travels to its expert (`Routed` is raised as they leave). A packet heading for a full expert stops just short of it. |
| 1.14 s | The chosen experts light up, their counters roll and the capacity bars and the load balance move. |
| 1.38 – 1.66 s | The outputs travel along the merge curves; curves of different lengths arrive together. |
| 1.66 – 1.84 s | The merged packet travels to the output. |
| 1.84 s | The output chip changes to the token and the token is marked as routed. |

After the last token the summary says how many tokens were routed and how few parameters each one used.

### The arithmetic

The card plans the whole sequence at once, so any token can be inspected before it plays. Every number comes from
the scores of the tokens:

- **Gate scores** are normalized to sum to 1. Percentages are rounded one by one, so a pair can add up to 101.
- **The choice** is the `TopK` experts with the highest scores. Equal scores go to the expert that comes first.
- **Weights** are the chosen scores divided by their sum: scores of 44% and 22% mix 67 to 33.
- **Capacity** is ⌈factor × tokens × k ÷ experts⌉ tokens per expert. Fifteen tokens over eight experts give 4 at top 2
  and 2 at top 1.
- **Loading** goes in order. A chosen expert that is already full skips the token; it keeps its weight, and the other
  expert is not raised to 100%. A token whose every choice is full passes through unchanged.
- **Load balance** is (E − max ÷ mean) ÷ (E − 1) over the loads: 100% when every expert has the same load, 0% when
  one expert took everything.
- **Active parameters** are shared + k × per expert: with the defaults, 6 + 12 = 18B at top 1 and 6 + 24 = 30B at top 2.

With the default data, top 2 makes 28 assignments for 15 tokens, because two second choices find their expert full,
and ends at 98% balance. Top 1 lets the final period pass through.

### Top k and capacity

`TopK` takes 1 or 2 and is two way: the header switch writes it and an app can bind it. Changing it re-plans every
route and carries on from the same point of the story, so the counters, the load balance and the footer change in
place and the readout rolls to the new count. `CapacityFactor` scales the capacity; `double.PositiveInfinity` turns
it off, and the capacity bars then fill relative to the busiest expert.

```xml
<arc:MixtureOfExperts TopK="1" CapacityFactor="1.5" />
```

### Your own experts and tokens

`Experts` takes 2 to 12 `MixtureOfExpertsExpert` items with a `Name`, an optional `Handles` sentence (shown while the
expert is inspected) and an optional 24×24 `Icon` geometry (the first letter of the name stands in without one).
`Tokens` takes `MixtureOfExpertsTokenItem` items with their `Text` and, optionally, one raw score per expert in
`Scores`. A token without scores gets stable example scores derived from its text: the same text always routes the
same way. `Parameters` takes the total, shared and per-expert counts in billions.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.MixtureOfExpertsCodeModelDemo">
    <!--
        Five experts of an invented code model. The first tokens bring their own gate scores; "return" and "total"
        have none, so the card derives stable example scores from their text. A capacity factor of 1.25 gives each
        expert room for three tokens at top 1.
    -->
    <arc:MixtureOfExperts MaxWidth="760"
                          TopK="1"
                          Parameters="96, 4, 7.5"
                          CapacityFactor="1.25"
                          Title="Routing in a code model">
        <arc:MixtureOfExperts.Experts>
            <arc:MixtureOfExpertsExpert Name="Keywords" Handles="Reserved words such as if, for and return." Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Code}" />
            <arc:MixtureOfExpertsExpert Name="Names" Handles="Variables, functions and types." Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Hash}" />
            <arc:MixtureOfExpertsExpert Name="Literals" Handles="Numbers and quoted strings." Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Quote}" />
            <arc:MixtureOfExpertsExpert Name="Operators" Handles="Arithmetic, comparison and assignment." Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Equal}" />
            <arc:MixtureOfExpertsExpert Name="Punctuation" Handles="Brackets, commas and semicolons." Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Terminal}" />
        </arc:MixtureOfExperts.Experts>
        <arc:MixtureOfExpertsTokenItem Text="for" Scores="62, 12, 3, 4, 6" />
        <arc:MixtureOfExpertsTokenItem Text="(" Scores="5, 3, 2, 9, 70" />
        <arc:MixtureOfExpertsTokenItem Text="item" Scores="8, 66, 4, 3, 2" />
        <arc:MixtureOfExpertsTokenItem Text=" in" Scores="48, 21, 2, 9, 3" />
        <arc:MixtureOfExpertsTokenItem Text=" cart" Scores="4, 71, 6, 2, 3" />
        <arc:MixtureOfExpertsTokenItem Text=")" Scores="3, 2, 2, 8, 74" />
        <arc:MixtureOfExpertsTokenItem Text=" total" />
        <arc:MixtureOfExpertsTokenItem Text=" +=" Scores="3, 5, 2, 68, 9" />
        <arc:MixtureOfExpertsTokenItem Text=" 0.5" Scores="2, 6, 59, 12, 3" />
        <arc:MixtureOfExpertsTokenItem Text=";" Scores="2, 2, 3, 6, 77" />
        <arc:MixtureOfExpertsTokenItem Text=" return" />
    </arc:MixtureOfExperts>
</UserControl>
```

```xml
<arc:MixtureOfExperts TopK="1" Parameters="96, 4, 7.5" CapacityFactor="1.25">
    <arc:MixtureOfExperts.Experts>
        <arc:MixtureOfExpertsExpert Name="Keywords" Handles="Reserved words such as if, for and return."
                                    Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Code}" />

                                    Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Hash}" />
        <!-- … -->
    </arc:MixtureOfExperts.Experts>

    <arc:MixtureOfExpertsTokenItem Text=" total" />
</arc:MixtureOfExperts>
```

Spaces in `Text` are kept, as a tokenizer keeps them. Fewer than two experts fall back to the defaults, and experts
past the twelfth are left out. Changing either list starts the story over.

### Inspecting a token or an expert

Pointing at a token, or focusing it with the keyboard, holds the story where it is and shows that token's whole route
at once: its scores, both lines, the lit tiles and the loads as they stand after it, even for a token that has not
played yet. Pointing at an expert keeps the stage as it is and highlights the tokens that expert has taken so far,
tinted by whether it was their first or second choice; the footer shows its load and its `Handles` sentence. Moving
away carries on from the same moment.

A click, a tap, Enter or Space pins the token or expert: the story pauses on it and the play button offers to resume.
Escape, a second click or `Unpin()` releases it and the story plays on. `PinToken(index)` and `PinExpert(index)` do
the same from code; `InspectedTokenIndex` and `InspectedExpertIndex` report what is shown.

### Playback, events and binding

`Routed` is raised as each token's packets leave the router, with the token's `Index`, `Token`, normalized `Scores`,
the chosen `Experts` best first, their `Weights` and the `Dropped` experts that were full. `Routes` holds the whole plan
for the current settings, and `ActiveParameters`, `Capacity`, `CurrentTokenIndex` and `LoadBalance` report the state
on show. The example below logs the routes, keeps the story from looping, turns the capacity off and uses two other
series colors for the choices.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.MixtureOfExpertsRouteLogDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="16" MaxWidth="760">
        <arc:MixtureOfExperts x:Name="Card"
                              IsLooping="False"
                              CapacityFactor="Infinity"
                              FirstChoiceBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Series3}"
                              SecondChoiceBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Series4}"
                              Routed="OnRouted" />
        <Grid ColumnDefinitions="*,Auto" RowDefinitions="Auto,Auto">
            <TextBlock Text="Routes so far"
                       FontWeight="Medium"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
            <StackPanel Grid.Column="1" Orientation="Horizontal" Spacing="12">
                <TextBlock VerticalAlignment="Center"
                           Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}"
                           Text="{Binding #Card.TopK, StringFormat='Top {0}'}" />
                <TextBlock VerticalAlignment="Center"
                           Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}"
                           Text="{Binding #Card.ActiveParameters, StringFormat='{}{0}B active'}" />
                <arc:Button Content="Route again" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Click="OnRestartClick" />
            </StackPanel>
            <TextBlock x:Name="Log"
                       Grid.Row="1"
                       Grid.ColumnSpan="2"
                       Margin="0,8,0,0"
                       FontFamily="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource MonoFontFamily}"
                       FontSize="12"
                       LineHeight="18"
                       TextWrapping="Wrap"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}"
                       Text="Waiting for the first token…" />
        </Grid>
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using System.Globalization;
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class MixtureOfExpertsRouteLogDemo : UserControl
{
    private static readonly string[] s_experts = MixtureOfExpertsSamples.CreateExperts().Select(x => x.Name).ToArray();
    private readonly Queue<string> _lines = new();

    public MixtureOfExpertsRouteLogDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
    }

    private void OnRouted(object? sender, MixtureOfExpertsRoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        // Each route names its experts best first with their share of the token.
        var experts = s_experts;
        var choices = e.Experts.Select((expert, rank) => e.Dropped.Contains(expert)
            ? $"{experts[expert]} (full)"
            : $"{experts[expert]} {Math.Round(e.Weights[rank] * 100).ToString(CultureInfo.InvariantCulture)}%");
        _lines.Enqueue($"{e.Index + 1,2}. {e.Token.Trim()} → {string.Join(", ", choices)}");
        while (_lines.Count > 5)
        {
            _lines.Dequeue();
        }
        Log.Text = string.Join(Environment.NewLine, _lines);
    }

    private void OnRestartClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        _lines.Clear();
        Log.Text = "Waiting for the first token…";
        Card.Restart();
    }
}
```

```csharp
card.Routed += (_, e) =>
{
    var first = e.Experts[0];
    log.Add($"{e.Token} → expert {first} ({e.Weights[0]:P0})");
};
```

`IsPlaying` is two way, so a view model can pause the card while a dialog is open. `Speed` scales the story clock
from 0 (hold still) to 4; the card has no speed control of its own. `FirstChoiceBrush` and `SecondChoiceBrush`
replace the choice colors, which default to chart series 1 and 2 and follow the accent.

The layout follows the card's own width, not the window's, so the same card works in a side panel.


### Reduced motion

Under reduced motion the card opens on its summary, with the final loads and balance. Pressing Route again steps
through the tokens at 1.8 seconds each without any travel: the scores and the route appear at once, the experts light
up and count 0.6 seconds later, the output changes at 1.1 seconds, and the story stops on the summary instead of
looping.
