### Content guidelines

Name the experts by what they tend to handle, in one short word (the narrow layout shows only their icons), and write
`Handles` as a plain sentence a reader can check against the tokens it took. Real experts are not this tidy; say so in
the text around the card. Pick a sentence that mixes kinds of tokens (a name, a verb, code, a number, punctuation), so
the routing visibly changes from token to token.

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| Expert 3 | Digits |
| Handles numeric tokens with high activation | Whole numbers and digits inside dates. |
| A paragraph of forty tokens | One sentence of twelve to twenty tokens |
| 671B parameters (a real model's figure) | Your own illustrative figures, and say they are illustrative |
| Experts with no theme | Experts whose names match the tokens they take |

### Best practices

**Do**

- Give scores for the tokens that carry the point of the story (the one that finds its expert full, the one that passes
  through) and let the others derive theirs.
- Keep the default capacity factor when the story is about capacity: with 15 tokens and 8 experts it produces one or
  two skips, which is enough to notice.
- Explain the summary sentence in the surrounding text; it is the part readers quote.
- Let readers inspect: the hold-on-hover is how they check a route at their own pace.

**Avoid**

- Presenting the loads, the balance or the parameter counts as measurements of a real model.
- Using vendor model names or logos in the labels or the parameters.
- More than twelve experts or very long token texts; the tiles and chips do not grow to fit.
- Rebuilding the token list on a timer: every change starts the story over.

### Common questions

**Why does a skipped expert keep its weight?** That is how a capacity limit behaves in a real layer: the token's
output is mixed from the experts that processed it with the weights the router gave them. The card shows it as is so
the loss is visible, instead of quietly raising the other expert to 100%.

**What decides the scores of a token without any?** The card hashes the token's text and draws a favourite, a
runner-up and small scores for the rest from that seed. The same text always gets the same scores, so screenshots and
tests stay stable.

**Can the story start paused?** Set `AutoPlay="False"`; the card waits at its first token until `Play()` or the play
button. Set `IsLooping="False"` to stop on the summary.

**Does hovering pause the card?** It holds the story without changing `IsPlaying`, so a bound view model does not see
a pause. Pinning does pause it, and the play button then offers to resume.

## API reference

### MixtureOfExperts

An animated explainer of a sparse mixture-of-experts layer. Tokens enter one at a time; a router scores every expert (a small bar each), the token travels to its top-k experts, which light up in a first and second choice color and count it, and their outputs merge into the token's output chip. Experts have a capacity: a full expert skips the token, and a token whose every choice is full passes through unchanged. The header switches between top 1 and top 2 and shows the parameters that run per token; a load balance bar sits under the stage. Pointing at, focusing or pinning a token or an expert freezes the story on it and shows its route or its load. The routing is computed from the tokens' scores (or stable scores derived from their text); the numbers are illustrative.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Tokens` | `AvaloniaList<MixtureOfExpertsTokenItem>` | `null` | The tokens to route, in order. Leave it empty for the default sentence (see `MixtureOfExpertsSamples`). Changing the tokens starts the story over. |
| `Experts` | `AvaloniaList<MixtureOfExpertsExpert>` | `null` | The experts, 2 to 12 (more are cut to the first 12). Leave it empty, or give fewer than two, for the eight default experts. Changing the experts starts the story over. |
| `TopK` | `int` | `2` | How many experts each token goes to: 1 or 2 (default 2). The header's switch sets it; a change re-plans every route and carries on from the same point of the story. |
| `Parameters` | `MixtureOfExpertsParameters` | `MixtureOfExpertsParameters { Total = 480, Shared = 6, PerExpert = 12 }` | The parameter counts in billions behind the active-parameters readout (default 480 in all, 6 shared, 12 per expert): shared + k × per expert run for each token. |
| `CapacityFactor` | `double` | `1` | Scales each expert's capacity, ⌈factor × tokens × k / experts⌉ tokens (default 1). A full expert skips further tokens. `PositiveInfinity` never drops a token; zero, negative and NaN values count as 1. |
| `FirstChoiceBrush` | `IBrush?` | `null` | The first choice's color (null: chart series 1, which follows the accent). |
| `SecondChoiceBrush` | `IBrush?` | `null` | The second choice's color (null: chart series 2). |
| `Labels` | `MixtureOfExpertsLabels` | – | Every word the card shows or speaks; replace it to translate or reword. |
| `Routes` | `IReadOnlyList<MixtureOfExpertsRoute>` | – | *Read-only.* The planned route of every token for the current top k and capacity. |
| `Capacity` | `int?` | – | *Read-only.* The tokens each expert takes before it is full, or null when nothing is ever dropped. |
| `ActiveParameters` | `double` | – | *Read-only.* The parameters that run for one token at the current top k, in billions. |
| `CurrentTokenIndex` | `int` | – | *Read-only.* The token being routed, or −1 while the summary shows. |
| `LoadBalance` | `double?` | – | *Read-only.* The load balance the card shows, 0 to 1; null before anything is routed. |
| `InspectedTokenIndex` | `int` | – | *Read-only.* The token being inspected (hovered, keyboard-focused or pinned), or −1. |
| `InspectedExpertIndex` | `int` | – | *Read-only.* The expert being inspected (hovered, keyboard-focused or pinned), or −1. |
| `IsPlaying` | `bool` | `false` | Defines the `IsPlaying` property. |
| `AutoPlay` | `bool` | `true` | Defines the `AutoPlay` property. |
| `IsLooping` | `bool` | `true` | Defines the `IsLooping` property. |
| `Speed` | `double` | `1` | Defines the `Speed` property. |
| `AreControlsVisible` | `bool` | `true` | Defines the `AreControlsVisible` property. |
| `Title` | `string?` | `"Mixture of experts routing"` | Defines the `Title` property. |
| `Model` | `ExplainerModel?` | `null` | Defines the `Model` property. |
| `PlaybackLabels` | `ExplainerPlaybackLabels` | – | Defines the `PlaybackLabels` property. |
| `IsFinished` | `bool` | – | *Read-only.* Defines the `IsFinished` property. |
| `IsStepping` | `bool` | – | *Read-only.* Defines the `IsStepping` property. |
| `CanStep` | `bool` | – | *Read-only.* Defines the `CanStep` property. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Routed` | `MixtureOfExpertsRoutedEventArgs` | Raised when a token leaves the router for its experts, with its route. |
| `Finished` | `RoutedEventArgs` | Defines the `Finished` routed event. |

Pseudo-classes: `:narrow`, `:compact`, `:inspecting`, `:playing`, `:stepping`, `:finished`, `:ready`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

### MixtureOfExpertsTokenItem

One token that a `MixtureOfExperts` routes: its text and, optionally, the router's raw score for every expert. (The name ends in Item because `MixtureOfExpertsToken` is the control's design token.)

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Text` | `string` | `""` | The token as the model sees it (spaces are kept, so " the" and "the" are different tokens). It is shown in the input, output and sequence chips and named in the footer. |
| `Scores` | `AvaloniaList<double>?` | `null` | The router's raw score for each expert, in the order of `Experts` ("24, 6, 3, 58" in XAML). Scores are non-negative and are normalized to sum to 1; missing entries count as 0 and extra ones are ignored. Null derives stable example scores from `Text`. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### MixtureOfExpertsExpert

One expert of a `MixtureOfExperts`: a short name, what it tends to handle and an icon.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Name` | `string` | `""` | The expert's name, best one short word (the narrow layout shows only the icon and speaks the name). |
| `Handles` | `string?` | `null` | A short sentence on what the expert tends to handle, shown while it is inspected. |
| `Icon` | `Geometry?` | `null` | A 24×24 stroked glyph drawn at 14 px (Lucide style); null shows the first letter of the name. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### MixtureOfExpertsLabels

Every word a `MixtureOfExperts` shows or speaks, in English by default. Replace the instance to translate or reword; sentences with numbers or names are functions so the word order can change. Footer notes may contain `{token}`, which is replaced by a small chip with the token's text. Numbers of parameters arrive formatted ("30", "2.5").

### MixtureOfExpertsRoute

How one token was routed: its normalized gate scores, the experts it chose (best first) with their weights within the choice, the chosen experts that were full and skipped it, and the expert loads once it has been routed. The whole sequence is planned at once, so a route can be read before its token plays.

### MixtureOfExpertsRoutedEventArgs

Arguments of `Routed`: a token leaves the router for its experts.

Derives from `RoutedEventArgs`: every member of `RoutedEventArgs` works as well.

`Parameters` takes a `MixtureOfExpertsParameters` record: `Total`, `Shared` and `PerExpert` in billions, with
`Active(k)` for the parameters one token uses. In XAML it parses from "total, shared, perExpert".
`MixtureOfExpertsSamples.CreateExperts()` and `CreateTokens()` return fresh copies of the default story.

## Accessibility

- The card is a group named by `Title` ("Mixture of experts routing" by default).
- Expert tiles and sequence tokens are real buttons. Each expert group and the sequence take one Tab stop, and the
  arrow keys move within them. A pinned tile or token reports a pressed toggle state.
- A token's name carries its whole route ("Ada: People 71%, Syntax 29%", with "full, skipped" for an expert at
  capacity). A tile's name carries its load, whether it is full and its part in the route on show ("Syntax expert, 4
  tokens, at capacity, second choice for x").
- The readout and the load balance are read as sentences ("30B of 480B parameters active per token"); their rolling
  digits are hidden from screen readers.
- The live region speaks only for the reader's own actions: pause, resume, start over, pin and unpin, and a change of
  top k. The routing that plays on its own is not announced.
- Color is never the only signal: the first choice comes first in the route line, and a skipped expert has a warning
  sign, a dashed border and the word "full".

### Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` | Move between the top-k switch, the play button, the expert tiles and the token sequence |
| `←` / `→` | In the top-k switch: choose top 1 or top 2 |
| `↓` / `→`, `↑` / `←` | In the tiles or the sequence: the next or previous one (no wrapping); focusing one inspects it |
| `Home` / `End` | The first or last tile or token |
| `Enter` / `Space` | Pin or release the focused tile or token; on the play button, pause, resume or route again |
| `Escape` | Release the pin (the focused item stays inspected until focus moves) |

## Motion

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| Packets | A dot with a soft trail moves along each path, easing in and out | Not shown | Not shown |
| Token pace | 2.2 s per token, then a 3.6 s summary and a loop | 1.8 s per token, stops on the summary | Same as reduced |
| Score bars, line colors, router border | 240 ms | Change at once | Change at once |
| Tiles lighting up / going back | 160 ms / 480 ms | Change at once | Change at once |
| Counters, readout, load balance | Digits roll on a smooth spring | Change at once | Change at once |
| Capacity bars and load segments | Slide over 480 ms | Change at once | Change at once |
| Chips | The input slides in from 14 px, the output from 10 px | Change at once | Change at once |
| Footer lines | The old line fades out, the new one rises 2 px | Short crossfade | Change at once |

Packets run on the story clock, so they pause, hold and scale with `Speed`; the fades are short transitions that
finish on their own. The clock stops while the card is off screen.

## Related

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `BarChart` | You plot the measured load of each expert |
| `Progress` | You show how full one real resource is |
| `DataFlow` | The story is events moving through a data pipeline |
| `VectorSearch` | The story is a question answered by its nearest documents |

# Speculative decoding

> A small draft model guesses a few tokens ahead and the large model checks them in one pass, keeping the ones it agrees with.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc.Special`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc.Special --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/speculative-decoding

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.SpeculativeDecodingSimulatedRunDemo">
    <!-- The built-in sample: a 22-token maintenance notice, drafted four tokens at a time. -->
    <arc:SpeculativeDecoding MaxWidth="720" />
</UserControl>
```

## When to use

`SpeculativeDecoding` explains why a language model can answer faster when a small draft model works ahead of it. A
draft lane proposes a few tokens at a time as dashed "ghost" chips, a target lane checks all of them in a single
pass, and the guesses the target agrees with travel into the answer. The card plays the run once, round by round,
and keeps a running score: how much faster the answer was written than by the target alone, the share of drafts
that were accepted, and the tokens written per target pass. It is an explainer, not a decoder: the numbers are
illustrative.

- **Model and product pages about latency**: a page that says "responses are up to 2.5 times faster" can show where
  the time goes. The reader sees that every pass of the large model can write several tokens instead of one.
- **Inference dashboards and release notes**: a recorded run from your own server, replayed with `Rounds`, shows the
  acceptance and the tokens per pass of a real request next to the metrics that summarize thousands of them.
- **Teaching the trade-off of the draft length**: the slider lets the reader try drafts of 2 to 8 tokens. Longer
  drafts write more per pass when the guesses are right, but accept a smaller share, because everything after the
  first miss is thrown away. With the built-in sample the speedup peaks at 4.
- **Comparing with plain decoding**: the compare switch races a second line in which the target writes one token per
  pass on the same clock, so the gap between the two approaches is visible, not just stated.
- **Courses and blog posts**: the run is deterministic. The same tokens, seed and draft length always give the same
  rounds, so a screenshot or a paragraph that refers to "round 3" stays true.

## When not to use

- **Streaming a real answer to a user**: use `MarkdownStream` or a chat component. This card explains the mechanism
  behind the speed; it does not show text as it arrives.
- **Token probabilities and alternatives**: a card that shows the candidates for one position and their scores is a
  different story. The draft model here only guesses right or wrong; it carries no probabilities.
- **Routing requests between models**: speculative decoding runs both models on every request. To explain which
  model answers which request, use a diagram of the router.
- **What happens inside one forward pass**: attention and expert routing are below the level of this card. Use
  `MixtureOfExperts` for routing inside the model.
- **Live performance monitoring**: the statistics are computed from the run on the card, not from your traffic. Use
  charts with your own measurements for that.

## Usage

The card needs no data. With nothing set, it plays the built-in sample: a 22-token maintenance notice drafted four
tokens at a time, which takes 6 target passes and ends 2.6 times faster than the target alone.

```xml
<arc:SpeculativeDecoding />
```

`SpeculativeDecoding` derives from `Explainer`, the base of the animated AI explainers, which derives from Avalonia's
`TemplatedControl`. The base class supplies the story clock, the play and restart buttons and their names, autoplay
and the live region; this control describes the lanes, the answer and the arithmetic.

### Your own answer

`Tokens` takes the answer the target model writes, one `DecodeToken` per token. The text keeps its leading space, as
tokenizers do (`" refund"`), and a token without one, such as punctuation, joins the word before it. `Ease` says how
likely the draft guesses the token (0 to 1; tokens without it use 0.9), and `Miss` is what the draft proposes when it
gets it wrong. Give numbers, names and rare words a low ease and a believable miss; leave short function words and
punctuation easy. The lane names can carry invented model names when the page needs them.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.SpeculativeDecodingOwnAnswerDemo">
    <!-- A support reply, token by token. Amounts and dates are hard to guess (low ease, with the draft's wrong guess);
         short words and punctuation are easy. The models are invented, and the race is on from the start. -->
    <arc:SpeculativeDecoding MaxWidth="720"
                             Title="Refund reply"
                             DraftLength="5"
                             IsComparing="True"
                             DraftLabel="Lark 1B"
                             DraftDetail="1B, fast"
                             TargetLabel="Orca 70B"
                             TargetDetail="70B">
        <arc:DecodeToken Text="Your" Ease="0.97" />
        <arc:DecodeToken Text=" refund" Ease="0.7" Miss=" order" />
        <arc:DecodeToken Text=" of" Ease="0.95" />
        <arc:DecodeToken Text=" $" Ease="0.9" />
        <arc:DecodeToken Text="48" Ease="0.1" Miss="40" />
        <arc:DecodeToken Text="." Ease="0.95" />
        <arc:DecodeToken Text="20" Ease="0.2" Miss="00" />
        <arc:DecodeToken Text=" was" Ease="0.95" />
        <arc:DecodeToken Text=" approved" Ease="0.8" Miss=" sent" />
        <arc:DecodeToken Text=" and" Ease="0.9" />
        <arc:DecodeToken Text=" should" Ease="0.75" Miss=" will" />
        <arc:DecodeToken Text=" reach" Ease="0.8" Miss=" show" />
        <arc:DecodeToken Text=" your" Ease="0.95" />
        <arc:DecodeToken Text=" card" Ease="0.6" Miss=" account" />
        <arc:DecodeToken Text=" within" Ease="0.85" Miss=" in" />
        <arc:DecodeToken Text=" 5" Ease="0.3" Miss=" 3" />
        <arc:DecodeToken Text=" business" Ease="0.9" />
        <arc:DecodeToken Text=" days" Ease="0.97" />
        <arc:DecodeToken Text="." Ease="0.99" />
    </arc:SpeculativeDecoding>
</UserControl>
```

`Seed` decides which guesses succeed. Each guess draws one number from a seeded generator and succeeds when the
number is below the token's ease; drawing stops at the first miss. Change the seed until the run tells the story you
want, then keep it: the same seed, tokens and draft length always replay the same rounds. `TokensSource` takes a
sequence of tokens instead, for binding.

### A recorded run

`Rounds` (or `RoundsSource`) replays a run recorded from your own server instead of simulating one. Each
`DecodeRound` has the tokens the draft proposed, how many of them the target accepted from the start, and the
token the target wrote itself: the correction of the first rejected guess, or a bonus token when every guess was
accepted. The answer is the accepted drafts and the target tokens in order. The draft length slider is hidden,
because the rounds already fix it.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.SpeculativeDecodingRecordedRunDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12" MaxWidth="720">
        <!-- Rounds recorded from a code completion replace the simulation; the draft length slider is hidden. -->
        <arc:SpeculativeDecoding x:Name="Decoder"
                                 Title="Code completion, recorded"
                                 Completed="OnCompleted" />
        <TextBlock x:Name="Log"
                   Text="Waiting for the run to finish."
                   FontSize="13"
                   TextWrapping="Wrap"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using System.Globalization;
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class SpeculativeDecodingRecordedRunDemo : UserControl
{
    public SpeculativeDecodingRecordedRunDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        // Each round: what the draft proposed, how many the target accepted from the start, and the target's own token.
        Decoder.RoundsSource =
        [
            new DecodeRound(["const", " total", " =", " items"], 4, "."),
            new DecodeRound(["reduce", "((", "acc", ","], 2, "sum"),
            new DecodeRound([",", " row", ")", " =>"], 1, " item"),
            new DecodeRound([")", " =>", " sum", " +"], 4, " item"),
            new DecodeRound([".", "price", " *", " item"], 4, "."),
            new DecodeRound(["qty", ",", " 0"], 3, ");")
        ];
    }

    private void OnCompleted(object? sender, SpeculativeDecodingCompletedEventArgs e)
    {
        var stats = e.Stats;
        Log.Text = string.Format(CultureInfo.InvariantCulture,
            "Completed: {0} tokens in {1} passes, {2} of {3} drafts accepted, {4:0.0}× the target alone.",
            stats.Tokens, stats.Passes, stats.Accepted, stats.Drafted, stats.Speedup);
    }
}
```

### Anatomy

1. **Header**: the title (`Title`, also the card's accessible name), a status line that names the current step, and
   the play / pause and restart buttons. The status line wraps on narrow cards and reserves two lines there, so the
   lanes never move.
2. **Draft lane** (`DraftLabel`, `DraftDetail`): a small dot for the small model. Each round its chips appear one
   by one as dashed ghost chips in the draft color, with a soft shimmer while they wait.
3. **Target lane** (`TargetLabel`, `TargetDetail`): a larger dot for the large model. Under each chip sits a cell
   that the target's sweep fills from left to right. A kept guess gets a check, the first rejected guess is struck
   through with a cross and the target's own token, and the guesses after it fade. When every guess is kept, an
   extra cell with a plus brings the target's bonus token.
4. **Answer line** ("Output", "Speculative" while comparing): the whole sentence is laid out from the start, so the
   line never reflows. Tokens land in their places, each underlined in the color of the model that wrote it: the
   draft color for accepted guesses, the target color for the target's own tokens. The pass count sits under the
   name and gets a check at the end.
5. **Target-only line** (`IsComparing`): the same sentence written one token per target pass on the same clock,
   underlined in the target color.
6. **Statistics**: the speedup, the share of drafts accepted and the tokens per pass. They show a dash until the first
   round settles, then roll to the running totals after each round.
7. **Controls**: the draft length slider (2 to 8) and the compare switch.
8. **Summary**: at the end the lanes show two lines with the totals, beside the two lanes.

### The story and its arithmetic

Every round has three steps. With the defaults (a pass of 640 ms, a draft cost of 0.1):

| Step | Duration | What happens |
|---|---|---|
| Draft | k × 64 ms | The draft proposes k chips, one every 64 ms. k is the draft length, but at most the number of tokens left minus one, so the target always writes the last token. |
| Verify | 0.72 pass (461 ms) | The sweep crosses all k cells in 0.4 pass (256 ms, however many cells there are). Each cell gets its verdict as the sweep passes its middle. |
| Settle | 0.28 pass (179 ms) | The kept guesses and the target's token fly into the answer, 20 ms apart, the columns fade and the statistics roll. |

A round therefore writes the a accepted guesses plus one token of the target's, and costs one pass plus the draft
time. The statistics follow from the totals of the rounds so far:

- **Speedup** = tokens / (passes + draft cost × drafted). The draft time counts, so drafting more is not free.
- **Drafts accepted** = accepted / drafted, as a whole percentage.
- **Tokens per pass** = tokens / passes. The target alone writes exactly one.

The built-in sample shows the shape the reader should take away. The speedup rises from short drafts to a draft of 4
and falls after it, while the share of accepted drafts keeps falling:

| Draft length | Passes | Drafted | Accepted | Accepted share | Speedup |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | 10 | 19 | 12 | 63% | 1.8× |
| 3 | 8 | 21 | 14 | 67% | 2.2× |
| 4 | 6 | 24 | 16 | 67% | 2.6× |
| 5 | 6 | 29 | 16 | 55% | 2.5× |
| 6 | 6 | 33 | 16 | 48% | 2.4× |
| 8 | 6 | 39 | 16 | 41% | 2.2× |

`PlannedStats` gives the totals of the whole run as soon as it is planned, `Stats` the totals of the rounds that have
settled so far, and `Completed` reports the totals each time the speculative line finishes. `DraftCost` sets the cost
of one draft token as a share of a pass, both on screen and in the speedup, and `PassDuration` how long one pass
takes on screen.

### Comparing with the target alone

`IsComparing` opens the target-only line. It writes token m at (m − 1) passes + 0.72 pass on the same clock as the
speculative line, so after the six passes of the sample the target alone has written 8 of 22 tokens. When the
speculative line is done the story keeps running until the target alone is done too, and the status line says so.
Turning the comparison on after the run has finished carries the clock on from there; it does not restart the run.
The statistics and `Completed` always describe the speculative line.

### Playback

The run plays once, the first time the card is mostly in view (`AutoPlay`), and stops at the end; `IsLooping` plays
it again a few seconds later. The play button pauses and resumes the run where it stopped, and after the end plays it
from the start. Restart always plays from the start. `IsPlaying` is two way, and `Play()`, `Pause()` and `Restart()`
do the same from code. `Speed` scales the clock; there is no speed control on the card, and no step button.

Changing the draft length (with the slider or `DraftLength`) plans the run again and plays it from the start. So do
new tokens, rounds, a new seed, draft cost or pass duration. An input that is equal to the old one, such as a new list
with the same tokens, does not restart the run.

```xml
<arc:SpeculativeDecoding DraftLength="{Binding DraftLength}"
                         IsComparing="{Binding ShowsBaseline}" />
```

```csharp
decoder.Completed += (_, e) => status.Text = $"{e.Stats.Speedup:0.0}× faster in {e.Stats.Passes} passes";
decoder.DraftLength = 6;
decoder.Restart();
```

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.SpeculativeDecodingBoundControlsDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12" MaxWidth="720">
        <!-- The page drives the card: draft length and comparison are two-way, and every change is logged. -->
        <WrapPanel ItemSpacing="8" LineSpacing="8">
            <arc:Button Content="Draft 2" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Click="OnShortClick" />
            <arc:Button Content="Draft 4" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Click="OnMiddleClick" />
            <arc:Button Content="Draft 8" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Click="OnLongClick" />
            <arc:Button Content="Toggle the race" Variant="Ghost" Size="Small" Click="OnCompareClick" />
        </WrapPanel>
        <arc:SpeculativeDecoding x:Name="Decoder"
                                 PropertyChanged="OnDecoderPropertyChanged"
                                 Completed="OnCompleted" />
        <TextBlock x:Name="Log"
                   FontSize="13"
                   TextWrapping="Wrap"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using System.Globalization;
using Avalonia;
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class SpeculativeDecodingBoundControlsDemo : UserControl
{
    private readonly List<string> _lines = new();

    public SpeculativeDecodingBoundControlsDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Write($"Planned: {Describe(Decoder.PlannedStats)}");
    }

    private void OnShortClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) => Decoder.DraftLength = 2;

    private void OnMiddleClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) => Decoder.DraftLength = 4;

    private void OnLongClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) => Decoder.DraftLength = 8;

    private void OnCompareClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) => Decoder.IsComparing = !Decoder.IsComparing;

    private void OnDecoderPropertyChanged(object? sender, AvaloniaPropertyChangedEventArgs e)
    {
        if (e.Property == SpeculativeDecoding.DraftLengthProperty)
        {
            Write($"Draft length {Decoder.DraftLength}, planned: {Describe(Decoder.PlannedStats)}");
        }
        else if (e.Property == SpeculativeDecoding.IsComparingProperty)
        {
            Write(Decoder.IsComparing ? "Racing the target alone" : "Race hidden");
        }
    }

    private void OnCompleted(object? sender, SpeculativeDecodingCompletedEventArgs e) => Write($"Completed: {Describe(e.Stats)}");

    private static string Describe(DecodeStats? stats) => stats is null
        ? "nothing to play"
        : string.Format(CultureInfo.InvariantCulture, "{0} passes, {1:0}% accepted, {2:0.0}× faster",
            stats.Passes, stats.Acceptance * 100, stats.Speedup);

    private void Write(string line)
    {
        _lines.Insert(0, line);
        if (_lines.Count > 4)
        {
            _lines.RemoveAt(_lines.Count - 1);
        }
        Log.Text = string.Join(Environment.NewLine, _lines);
    }
}
```

### Loading and errors

`Status` describes the data behind a recorded run. While it is `Loading` the lanes dim, the status line shows a
spinner and a shimmering label, the controls are disabled and the run waits; autoplay starts once the status turns
`Ready`. `Error` shows `ErrorText` (or the default message) with a danger icon. A retry button appears next to the
playback buttons only when someone handles `RetryRequested` or `RetryCommand` is set, because a button that does
nothing is worse than none.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.SpeculativeDecodingStatusStatesDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12" MaxWidth="720">
        <WrapPanel ItemSpacing="8" LineSpacing="8">
            <arc:Button Content="Loading" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Click="OnLoadingClick" />
            <arc:Button Content="Error" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Click="OnErrorClick" />
            <arc:Button Content="Ready" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Click="OnReadyClick" />
        </WrapPanel>
        <!-- The run comes from a server: loading dims the lanes, an error offers a retry because the page handles it. -->
        <arc:SpeculativeDecoding x:Name="Decoder"
                                 Status="Loading"
                                 ErrorText="The trace from the inference server could not be read"
                                 RetryRequested="OnRetryRequested" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;
using Avalonia.Threading;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class SpeculativeDecodingStatusStatesDemo : UserControl
{
    private readonly DispatcherTimer _load = new() { Interval = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(1.5) };

    public SpeculativeDecodingStatusStatesDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        _load.Tick += (_, _) =>
        {
            _load.Stop();
            Decoder.Status = SpeculativeDecodingStatus.Ready;
        };
    }

    private void OnLoadingClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        _load.Stop();
        Decoder.Status = SpeculativeDecodingStatus.Loading;
    }

    private void OnErrorClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        _load.Stop();
        Decoder.Status = SpeculativeDecodingStatus.Error;
    }

    private void OnReadyClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        _load.Stop();
        Decoder.Status = SpeculativeDecodingStatus.Ready;
    }

    // Retry: show the loading state again, then the run (a real page would fetch the trace here).
    private void OnRetryRequested(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        Decoder.Status = SpeculativeDecodingStatus.Loading;
        _load.Start();
    }
}
```

### Narrow cards

Below 560 px of its own width the card uses its narrow layout: tighter padding, the lane names as a legend above the
columns, each line's name above its text with the pass count on the right, the slider on its own row and the switch
under it. Draft columns that do not fit wrap onto a second row, and the lanes grow on a smooth spring.

```xml

</UserControl>
```

### Reduced motion

With reduced motion the card never starts on its own and does not jump to its end either: it waits at its first
state until the reader presses play. The run then has exactly the same beats, but the chips appear without sliding,
the sweep steps a whole cell at a time, the strike is drawn at once, there is no shimmer, and tokens appear in their
places in the answer instead of flying there.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.SpeculativeDecodingReducedMotionDemo">
    <!-- Reduced motion: the card waits for Play; tokens then appear in place and the sweep steps a cell at a time. -->
    <arc:SpeculativeDecoding MaxWidth="720" arc:ArcMotion.Level="Reduced" />
</UserControl>
```

### Content guidelines

Write an answer of 15 to 30 tokens that reads well on its own, and mix easy and hard tokens the way a real model
would meet them: function words and punctuation are easy, numbers, names and the key nouns are hard. Make each miss
a plausible wrong guess of the same kind (a different number, a nearby word), not a random word. Keep the lane names
generic, or use clearly invented names; do not name real products unless the run really came from them.

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| A sentence of 60 tokens | One or two short sentences of 15 to 30 tokens |
| Every token with ease 0.5 | Easy tokens near 0.95, hard ones near 0.1 to 0.3 |
| `Miss=" banana"` for a number | `Miss=" 30"` for `" 25"` |
| A real model name on a simulated run | "Draft model" and "Target model", or invented names |
| "3× faster" in the page text next to a simulated run | "about 2.6 times faster in this illustrative run" |

### Best practices

**Do**

- Say that the numbers are illustrative when the run is simulated, and say where a recorded run came from.
- Keep the default draft length of 4 for the sample, so the first run shows the best speedup and the slider shows the
  trade-off in both directions.
- Use `Rounds` for numbers you want to quote: a recorded run shows exactly what your server did.
- Choose a seed whose run includes a kept round, a corrected round and a round whose first guess fails, so all three
  verdicts appear.

**Avoid**

- Several playing cards on one screen. Each one draws every frame while it plays.
- Tokens without leading spaces for words. The answer would run the words together, and punctuation rules depend on
  the spaces.
- Changing the tokens or the seed on a timer. Every change plans the run again and starts it over.
- Reading `Stats` as a measurement of your system. It describes the run on the card.

### Common questions

**Why is the speedup lower than the tokens per pass?** The speedup counts the draft model's time: each drafted token
costs `DraftCost` of a pass. With 6 passes and 24 drafted tokens the run costs 6 + 2.4 = 8.4 passes for 22 tokens,
which is 2.6 times faster, while the tokens per pass are 22 / 6 = 3.7.

**Why does the last round never draft the final token?** The target always writes at least one token per round, so
the plan leaves the last token of the answer to the target. A round with one token left has no drafts at all.

**Why do the chips after a rejected guess show the right words?** Once a guess is rejected, everything after it is
discarded without being checked, so those chips show the real tokens and fade.

**How do I get the same run as in a screenshot?** Keep the tokens, the seed and the draft length. The plan depends on
nothing else.

**Can I hide the playback buttons?** Set `AreControlsVisible` to false. The run still plays on its own and can be
driven with `IsPlaying`, `Play()` and `Restart()`.

## API reference

### SpeculativeDecoding

An animated explainer of speculative decoding in one card. A small draft model proposes a few ghost tokens quickly; the large target model checks them in one sweep. Accepted guesses get a check and fly into the answer, the first miss is struck through and replaced by the target's own token, and the guesses after it fade. When every guess is kept the target adds a bonus token. Rounds repeat until the sentence is written; a switch races a line where the target writes one token per pass on the same clock, and the speedup, the share of drafts accepted and the tokens per pass roll up below. Every token of the answer is underlined in the color of the model that wrote it. With `Tokens` the run is simulated from each token's ease and the `Seed`; with `Rounds` a recorded run is replayed. The numbers are illustrative. The run plays once when the card comes into view (never on its own under reduced motion, where tokens appear in place and the sweep steps a cell at a time).

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Tokens` | `AvaloniaList<DecodeToken>` | `null` | Defines the `Tokens` property. |
| `TokensSource` | `IEnumerable<DecodeToken>?` | `null` | Defines the `TokensSource` property. |
| `Rounds` | `AvaloniaList<DecodeRound>` | `null` | Defines the `Rounds` property. |
| `RoundsSource` | `IEnumerable<DecodeRound>?` | `null` | Defines the `RoundsSource` property. |
| `DraftLength` | `int` | `4` | Defines the `DraftLength` property. |
| `IsComparing` | `bool` | `false` | Defines the `IsComparing` property. |
| `Seed` | `int` | `25` | Defines the `Seed` property. |
| `DraftCost` | `double` | `0.1` | Defines the `DraftCost` property. |
| `PassDuration` | `TimeSpan` | `00:00:00.6400000` | Defines the `PassDuration` property. |
| `DraftLabel` | `string?` | `"Draft model"` | Defines the `DraftLabel` property. |
| `DraftDetail` | `string?` | `"Small, fast"` | Defines the `DraftDetail` property. |
| `TargetLabel` | `string?` | `"Target model"` | Defines the `TargetLabel` property. |
| `TargetDetail` | `string?` | `"Large"` | Defines the `TargetDetail` property. |
| `Status` | `SpeculativeDecodingStatus` | `Ready` | Defines the `Status` property. |
| `ErrorText` | `string?` | `null` | Defines the `ErrorText` property. |
| `RetryCommand` | `ICommand?` | `null` | Defines the `RetryCommand` property. |
| `Labels` | `SpeculativeDecodingLabels` | – | Defines the `Labels` property. |
| `Stats` | `DecodeStats?` | – | *Read-only.* Defines the `Stats` property. |
| `PlannedStats` | `DecodeStats?` | – | *Read-only.* Defines the `PlannedStats` property. |
| `IsPlaying` | `bool` | `false` | Defines the `IsPlaying` property. |
| `AutoPlay` | `bool` | `true` | Defines the `AutoPlay` property. |
| `IsLooping` | `bool` | `false` | Defines the `IsLooping` property. |
| `Speed` | `double` | `1` | Defines the `Speed` property. |
| `AreControlsVisible` | `bool` | `true` | Defines the `AreControlsVisible` property. |
| `Title` | `string?` | `"Speculative decoding"` | Defines the `Title` property. |
| `Model` | `ExplainerModel?` | `null` | Defines the `Model` property. |
| `PlaybackLabels` | `ExplainerPlaybackLabels` | – | Defines the `PlaybackLabels` property. |
| `IsFinished` | `bool` | – | *Read-only.* Defines the `IsFinished` property. |
| `IsStepping` | `bool` | – | *Read-only.* Defines the `IsStepping` property. |
| `CanStep` | `bool` | – | *Read-only.* Defines the `CanStep` property. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Completed` | `SpeculativeDecodingCompletedEventArgs` | Defines the `Completed` routed event. |
| `RetryRequested` | `RoutedEventArgs` | Defines the `RetryRequested` routed event. |
| `Finished` | `RoutedEventArgs` | Defines the `Finished` routed event. |

Pseudo-classes: `:narrow`, `:comparing`, `:loading`, `:error`, `:replay`, `:retry`, `:playing`, `:stepping`, `:finished`, `:ready`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

The base class's `Model` is not shown by this card; the two lanes name the models. There is no step button, so
`IsStepping` stays false unless `StepForward()` is called from code, which plays to the end of the run.

### SpeculativeDecodingLabels

Every word `SpeculativeDecoding` shows or announces, apart from the title, the lane names (`DraftLabel` and the others) and the playback buttons (`PlaybackLabels`). English by default; replace the instance to translate or reword. Texts with numbers are functions so that word order can change.

Tokens use the `DecodeToken` class.

| Property | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `Text` | `string` | The token with its leading space, such as `" refund"`; punctuation has none |
| `Ease` | `double?` | How likely the draft guesses the token, 0 to 1; null uses 0.9 |
| `Miss` | `string?` | What the draft proposes when it misses; null shows an ellipsis |

Recorded rounds use the `DecodeRound` class.

| Property | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `Drafts` | `AvaloniaList<string>` | The tokens the draft proposed, in order |
| `Accepted` | `int` | How many drafts the target accepted from the start (clamped to the drafts) |
| `TargetToken` | `string` | The token the target wrote: the correction, or the bonus after a fully kept round |

Totals use the `DecodeStats` record, also the `Stats` property of `SpeculativeDecodingCompletedEventArgs`.

| Property | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `Passes` | `int` | Target passes, one per round |
| `Drafted` | `int` | Tokens the draft proposed |
| `Accepted` | `int` | Drafted tokens the target accepted |
| `Tokens` | `int` | Tokens written into the answer |
| `Acceptance` | `double` | Accepted / drafted, 0 to 1 |
| `TokensPerPass` | `double` | Tokens / passes |
| `Speedup` | `double` | Tokens / (passes + draft cost × drafted) |

`SpeculativeDecodingStatus` is `Ready`, `Loading` or `Error`. `SpeculativeDecodingSamples` holds the built-in sample
(`Tokens`, `Seed`) and a recorded code completion (`CodeCompletion`).

## Accessibility

- The card is a named group: its accessible name is `Title`.
- The lanes are hidden from assistive technology. Once a round has its verdicts, a hidden text summarizes it: what the
  draft proposed, how many guesses the target kept and which token it wrote instead (or added).
- Each answer line carries the text written so far as its accessible name ("Output: Tomorrow at 7, the east"), so a
  screen reader reads words rather than tokens.
- Each statistic has a spoken value ("Speedup: 2.6 times", "Drafts accepted: 67 percent", "not yet" before the first
  round); the rolling digits are decorative.
- Verdicts never rely on color alone: kept guesses get a check, the rejected guess is struck through with a cross
  beside the target's token, and discarded guesses fade.
- A polite live region announces play, pause, restart, the comparison turning on or off, a new draft length with its
  expected acceptance and speedup, and the result at the end. It never announces every round.
- Pointer focus draws no ring; keyboard focus shows the shared focus ring.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` | Move through play or pause, restart, the draft length slider and the compare switch |
| `Enter`, `Space` | On play or pause and restart, activate them; on the compare switch, toggle the race |
| `Left` / `Down`, `Right` / `Up` | On the slider, shorten or lengthen the draft by one token; the run replays |
| `Home`, `End` | On the slider, jump to a draft of 2 or 8 tokens |

## Motion

- Draft chips appear one by one, fading in from 4 px to the left, and a soft shimmer crosses their text while they
  wait for the target.
- The target's sweep fills the cells from left to right; each verdict fades in as the sweep reaches the cell's middle,
  and the strike draws from the left.
- Kept guesses and the target's token fly from their chips into their places in the answer on a critically damped
  spring, 20 ms apart, while the columns fade; their underlines take the model's color shortly after they land.
- The lanes follow wrapping columns on the smooth spring, and the target-only line opens and closes on the same
  spring. The statistics roll digit by digit.
- The status line and the line name swap with a short crossfade.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| Autoplay | When the card is mostly in view | Never; waits for play | Never; waits for play |
| Chips and columns | Slide in from 4 px, shimmer while waiting | Appear in place, no shimmer | Appear in place |
| Sweep | Fills each cell continuously | Steps a whole cell at its verdict | Steps a whole cell |
| Tokens into the answer | Fly on a spring, then fade in their underline | Fade in in place | Fade in in place |
| Lanes and the target-only line | Grow and shrink on a spring | Jump to their size | Jump to their size |
| Statistics | Roll digit by digit | Change at once | Change at once |

## Related

- `MixtureOfExperts` for what happens inside one forward pass: a router sends each token to its top experts.
- `PromptCache` for another way to save time: a shared prompt prefix is read from the cache.
- `AgentLoop` and `ReasoningTree` for the other AI explainers with the same playback controls.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `MarkdownStream` | You show an answer streaming to the reader |
| `MixtureOfExperts` | The story is how a model routes each token inside one pass |
| `PromptCache` | The story is how repeated prompts become cheaper |
| `LineChart` | You plot real latency or throughput measurements |

# Prompt cache

> Requests that share a prompt prefix read it from the cache instead of processing it again, and the savings add up.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc.Special`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc.Special --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/prompt-cache

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.PromptCachePreviewDemo">
    <!-- The built-in story: a freight support assistant whose four questions share one 45.5K-token prefix. -->
    <arc:PromptCache MaxWidth="744" />
</UserControl>
```

## When to use

`PromptCache` explains prompt caching with a short simulated story. A round of up to four requests shares one stable
prefix (tool schemas, instructions, documents, the conversation so far) and adds a new message at the end of each. The
first request processes the whole prompt and stores the prefix; the next ones read the prefix back and only process
their message. The card adds up what that does to input cost and to the time before the first output token. It is a
teaching illustration with a simulated clock and sample prices, not a monitor of a real cache.

- **API and SDK documentation**: the page that introduces cache breakpoints or cached input pricing. The rows show
  why a stable prefix matters before the reader writes any code.
- **Pricing and usage pages**: a section that explains the three prices behind cached traffic (input, cache write,
  cache read) and the time to live. Pass your own prices and the totals follow.
- **Onboarding for an AI product**: a first-run explanation of why the order of a prompt matters, with the change
  toggle showing that an edit early in the prompt costs more than one at the end.
- **Engineering posts and internal training**: a talk or a post about latency, where the first-token speedup is the
  number people remember.

## When not to use

- **Reporting a real cache hit rate**: use `LineChart` or `BarChart` with numbers from your telemetry. Every number in
  this card is computed from the sample data you give it.
- **Showing how much of a quota is used**: use `UsageMeter`. It shows a real share of a limit; this card shows a story.
- **Listing real requests and their costs**: use `DataGrid` with the rows from your logs.
- **Explaining other inference ideas**: `SpeculativeDecoding` explains draft and verify, `AgentLoop` explains an
  agent's cycle of context, action and checks.

## Usage

The card needs no data: it ships with a story of its own, a support assistant for a freight company whose four
questions share a 45.5K-token prefix. It starts playing the first time it is mostly on screen and loops.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:PromptCache MaxWidth="744" />
</UserControl>
```

`PromptCache` derives from `Explainer`, the base of the Special explainers, which supplies the story clock, the play,
step and restart buttons, the live region and reduced motion. The card lays itself out from its own width, so give it
the width of the column it sits in; 744px shows the requests and the cache side by side.

### Anatomy

1. **Header**: the title (`Title`, "Prompt cache" by default), the model line (the mark and name from `Model`, then the
   time to live, "5-minute cache") and three round buttons: play or pause, send the next request, and restart.
2. **Legend**: every prefix segment with its color and token count, then the new message.
3. **Requests**: one row per request. The row header shows "Request N", the simulated time it was sent and its status;
   under it a bar of the prompt; at the right three numbers: tokens processed, input cost and time to first token.
   Above the rows, two keys tell the solid processed fill from the light cached fill.
4. **Cache panel**: a ring that shows the time to live left, the cache status (Empty, Writing, Reading, "Expires in
   4:22" or Expired), a bar of what is cached, the cached token count and the three prices.
5. **Caption**: one or two sentences that say what just happened.
6. **Footer**: the input cost of the round against the same prompts without a cache, the first-token speedup on hits,
   and the change toggle.

Bars use a square root scale, so a 200-token message stays visible next to a 33,800-token knowledge base; the legend
and the numbers give the real counts.

### The story

At full motion one round takes about ten seconds:

1. **Request 1 writes.** Nothing is cached, so the whole prompt is processed: each segment fills in turn at one steady
   speed, then the new message. The prefix lifts out of the row and flies into the cache panel, changing from the
   solid color to the light cached tint on the way. The ring fills and the countdown starts at the time to live.
2. **Requests 2 to 4 hit.** The simulated clock moves on by the request's gap and the ring drains a little. The prefix
   turns to its cached tint while a band of light passes over it (and over the panel's bar), only the message is
   processed, and the ring refills: every hit resets the time to live.
3. **Numbers roll from the row above.** Each row's three numbers start from the previous row's values, so you see the
   cost and the first token come down on a hit.
4. **The cache idles and expires.** With no more requests the clock speeds up, the ring drains, turns to the warning
   color in the last minute and empties. A looping card then starts the next round with its first request already
   written; with `IsLooping="False"` the card stops on the expired cache.

All numbers in the card are illustrative: they follow from the prices, the token counts and the first-token estimate
you pass, not from a real model.

### The arithmetic

With `P` the prefix tokens, `m` the message tokens, and the three prices per token:

| Outcome | Read from the cache | Written to the cache | Processed | Input cost |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Write (nothing cached, or the cache expired) | 0 | `P` | `P + m` | `P × write + m × input` |
| Hit | `P` | 0 | `m` | `P × read + m × input` |
| Partial hit at segment `k` | the segments before `k` | the segments from `k` on | written + `m` | cached × read + written × write + `m` × input |

The uncached cost of a request is `(P + m) × input`. The cost statistic compares the round's totals: with the built-in
story the first write costs $0.1712 against $0.1371 without a cache (25% higher), and after the three hits the round
costs $0.2147 against $0.5491 (61% lower). The speedup averages the first token of cache hits only, with and without
the cache: 0.48s against 1.42s, 2.9x. Writes and partial hits do not count toward it.

### Your own prefix and requests

Fill `Segments` with `PromptCacheSegment` items in prompt order (an id, a label, a token count and an optional
`Color`) and `Requests` with up to four `PromptCacheRequest` items (the new message's token count, the simulated
`Gap` in seconds since the request before, and a `Message` that is read out and passed in the results). While a list is
empty the card uses its built-in story. To bind instead, set `SegmentsSource` and `RequestsSource`.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.PromptCacheCodeReviewDemo">
    <!-- Your own prefix, questions, prices and model: a code review bot with an hour-long cache. -->
    <arc:PromptCache MaxWidth="744"
                     Title="Review bot cache"
                     Ttl="3600"
                     ChangeSegmentId="style">
        <arc:PromptCache.Model>
            <arc:ExplainerModel Name="Quill 2 Mini" />
        </arc:PromptCache.Model>
        <arc:PromptCache.Pricing>
            <arc:PromptCachePricing InputPrice="1.20" CacheWritePrice="2.40" CacheReadPrice="0.12" />
        </arc:PromptCache.Pricing>
        <arc:PromptCache.Segments>
            <arc:PromptCacheSegment Id="repo" Label="Repository map" Tokens="7400" />
            <arc:PromptCacheSegment Id="style" Label="Style guide" Tokens="1800" />
            <arc:PromptCacheSegment Id="diff" Label="Open diff" Tokens="21500" />
        </arc:PromptCache.Segments>
        <arc:PromptCache.Requests>
            <arc:PromptCacheRequest Message="Flag any unchecked null returns in the parser" Tokens="140" />
            <arc:PromptCacheRequest Message="Suggest a clearer name for the retry helper" Tokens="90" Gap="64" />
            <arc:PromptCacheRequest Message="Does the new migration need a rollback step?" Tokens="210" Gap="118" />
        </arc:PromptCache.Requests>
    </arc:PromptCache>
</UserControl>
```

```xml
<arc:PromptCache Title="Review bot cache" Ttl="3600" ChangeSegmentId="style">
    <arc:PromptCache.Model>
        <arc:ExplainerModel Name="Quill 2 Mini" />
    </arc:PromptCache.Model>
    <arc:PromptCache.Pricing>
        <arc:PromptCachePricing InputPrice="1.20" CacheWritePrice="2.40" CacheReadPrice="0.12" />
    </arc:PromptCache.Pricing>
    <arc:PromptCache.Segments>
        <arc:PromptCacheSegment Id="repo" Label="Repository map" Tokens="7400" />
        <arc:PromptCacheSegment Id="style" Label="Style guide" Tokens="1800" />
        <arc:PromptCacheSegment Id="diff" Label="Open diff" Tokens="21500" />
    </arc:PromptCache.Segments>
    <arc:PromptCache.Requests>
        <arc:PromptCacheRequest Message="Flag any unchecked null returns in the parser" Tokens="140" />
        <arc:PromptCacheRequest Message="Suggest a clearer name for the retry helper" Tokens="90" Gap="64" />
        <arc:PromptCacheRequest Message="Does the new migration need a rollback step?" Tokens="210" Gap="118" />
    </arc:PromptCache.Requests>
```
