
Segments without a color take the chart series colors in the order 3, 2, 4, 1, so they follow the theme and the accent.
Changing the data rebuilds the story and starts it over, so set it once rather than on every refresh.

### Prices and the first token

`Pricing` takes a `PromptCachePricing` with dollars per million tokens. The defaults are sample prices that follow a
common pattern: $3.00 input, cache writes at 1.25 times that ($3.75) and reads at a tenth ($0.30). Set
`CacheWritePrice` equal to `InputPrice` when your provider charges nothing extra for writes. `Ttl` is the time to live
in simulated seconds (300 by default); it drives the ring, the countdown and the header note.

`FirstTokenEstimator` returns the seconds to the first output token from the processed and cached token counts. The
default is an illustrative model, `0.40 + processed / 45,000 + cached / 600,000`: a fixed overhead, prefill of new
tokens, and a much cheaper load of cached ones. Pass your own measurements when you have them.

```csharp
cache.FirstTokenEstimator = (processed, cached) => 0.25 + processed / 60_000.0 + cached / 900_000.0;
```

### The change toggle

The toggle under the statistics edits one segment, `ChangeSegmentId` ("rules", the instructions, by default). While it
is armed (`IsChangeArmed`), the next request matches the cache only up to that segment: the segments before it are
read, a warning line marks the break, and the segment and everything after it are processed and written again. The
toggle releases once that request is sent, and the next one hits the rewritten cache. An edit of the first segment
breaks the match before anything, so it is a plain write. Set `ChangeSegmentId` to null (or to an id no segment has)
to hide the toggle.

### Playback, stepping and events

`IsPlaying`, `Speed` (0 to 4; 0 holds still), `Play()`, `Pause()` and `Restart()` come from `Explainer`. The step button
("Send the next request", `StepForward()`) pauses the story and sends exactly one request: a pause before it is
skipped, a request in progress is finished, and after a finished round it starts a new one whose first request hits
the cache if it is still warm. Restart empties the cache and keeps the play state, so a paused card stays paused at
its start.

`RequestCompleted` reports each finished request as a `PromptCacheResult`: its index, simulated time, kind, break,
cached, written and processed tokens, cost with and without the cache, first token with and without the cache, whether
it was edited or cold, and its message. `Expired` fires each time the cache runs out. `Results` holds the current
round's results and `CacheState` what the cache is doing.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.PromptCacheEventLogDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="16" MaxWidth="744">
        <arc:PromptCache x:Name="Cache"
                         IsLooping="False"
                         RequestCompleted="OnRequestCompleted"
                         Expired="OnExpired" />
        <WrapPanel ItemSpacing="12" LineSpacing="12">
            <arc:Button Content="0.5×" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Click="OnHalfSpeedClick" />
            <arc:Button Content="1×" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Click="OnNormalSpeedClick" />
            <arc:Button Content="2×" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Click="OnDoubleSpeedClick" />
            <arc:Switch Content="Edit the instructions"
                        IsChecked="{Binding #Cache.IsChangeArmed, Mode=TwoWay}"
                        VerticalAlignment="Center" />
        </WrapPanel>
        <TextBlock x:Name="Log"
                   Text="Requests appear here as they finish."
                   FontSize="13"
                   TextWrapping="Wrap"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using System.Globalization;
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class PromptCacheEventLogDemo : UserControl
{
    private readonly List<string> _lines = new();

    public PromptCacheEventLogDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
    }

    private void OnRequestCompleted(object? sender, PromptCacheRequestCompletedEventArgs e)
    {
        var r = e.Result;
        var kind = r.Kind switch
        {
            PromptCacheRequestKind.Hit => "hit",
            PromptCacheRequestKind.Partial => $"partial hit at {r.BreakSegmentId}",
            _ => r.IsCold ? "cold write" : "write"
        };
        Add(string.Create(CultureInfo.InvariantCulture,
            $"#{r.Index + 1} at {r.Time:0}s: {kind}, {r.CachedTokens:N0} cached, {r.ProcessedTokens:N0} processed, ${r.Cost:0.0000} (${r.UncachedCost:0.0000} uncached)"));
    }

    private void OnExpired(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) => Add("The cache expired.");

    private void Add(string line)
    {
        _lines.Add(line);
        if (_lines.Count > 6)
        {
            _lines.RemoveAt(0);
        }
        Log.Text = string.Join(Environment.NewLine, _lines);
    }

    private void OnHalfSpeedClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) => Cache.Speed = 0.5;

    private void OnNormalSpeedClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) => Cache.Speed = 1;

    private void OnDoubleSpeedClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) => Cache.Speed = 2;
}
```

```csharp
cache.RequestCompleted += (_, e) =>
    log.Add($"{e.Result.Kind}: {e.Result.Cost:C4} instead of {e.Result.UncachedCost:C4}");
cache.Expired += (_, _) => log.Add("The cache expired.");
```

### Narrow containers

The layout follows the card's content width, not the window. From 660px the cache panel sits beside the requests;
below that it becomes a strip above them, so the flight still travels from a row into the cache. Below 480px each
request takes three lines (title and status, the bar, then the three numbers under shared headings), the statistics
stack and the toggle spans the card. Below 260px the playback buttons move under the title.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.PromptCacheNarrowDemo">
    <!-- The layout follows the card's own width: under 660px of content the cache panel sits above the requests,
         under 480px every request takes three lines and the statistics stack. -->
    <arc:PromptCache Width="420" HorizontalAlignment="Center" />
</UserControl>
```

### Reduced motion

With reduced motion the card opens on a finished round and waits. Playing and stepping still work, but every change
applies at once: no sweeps, no band, no flight, no rolling numbers and no accelerated drain. After a round the cache
expires, and a looping card starts a new round a moment later.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.PromptCacheReducedMotionDemo">
    <!-- Reduced motion opens on a finished round; play and step still work, and every change applies at once. -->
    <arc:PromptCache MaxWidth="744" arc:ArcMotion.Level="Reduced" />
</UserControl>
```

### Content guidelines

Name segments after what they hold in your prompt and keep the labels short; they appear in the legend, the toggle
and the captions ("Edit the style guide"). Keep the order realistic: what changes least comes first. Write messages
as the questions your users ask; they are read out to screen readers.

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| Segment 1 | Tool schemas |
| System | Instructions |
| Big context | Knowledge base |
| Question 3 | Compare the two freight quotes in the sheet |
| $0.1 off | (let the card compute the costs) |

### Best practices

**Do**

- Use the token counts and prices of the model you describe, so the totals tell the reader something true about it.
- Keep gaps shorter than the time to live unless you want to show a cold write in the middle of a round.
- Use the change toggle to make the point about prompt order: an edit early in the prompt rewrites almost everything.
- Say near the card that the numbers are illustrative.

**Avoid**

- Feeding the card live traffic. It simulates one round at a time; real measurements belong in a chart.
- More than four requests: the card shows the first four of a round.
- Changing the data on a timer; every change starts the story over.

### Common questions

**Why does the first request cost more than no cache?** Writing to the cache costs more than plain input (1.25 times
with the sample prices), so the first write is more expensive. The hits pay it back; the cost statistic says "higher"
until they do.

**Why does the speedup ignore the partial hit?** It compares cache hits with the same prompts without a cache. A
partial hit reprocesses most of the prompt, so counting it would hide what a hit does.

**Can the card show my real cache?** No. Use `RequestCompleted` to see what the simulation computed, and a chart for
real numbers.

## API reference

### PromptCache

An animated explainer of prompt caching. Up to four requests share a prompt prefix (tool schemas, instructions, documents, the chat so far) and add a new message each. The first processes every segment in one steady sweep and carries the prefix into the cache panel, where a time-to-live ring fills; later requests read the prefix back under one passing band and only process their message, and their processed tokens, input cost and first-token time roll down from the row above. A toggle edits one segment: the next request matches the cache only up to it, shows a break there and writes the rest again. When no request arrives the ring drains on an accelerated clock and the cache expires; then the round starts over. The totals roll into the input cost saved and the first-token speedup. Costs and times are computed from `Pricing` and `FirstTokenEstimator`; the numbers are illustrative.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Segments` | `AvaloniaList<PromptCacheSegment>` | `null` | Defines the `Segments` property. |
| `SegmentsSource` | `IEnumerable?` | `null` | Defines the `SegmentsSource` property. |
| `Requests` | `AvaloniaList<PromptCacheRequest>` | `null` | Defines the `Requests` property. |
| `RequestsSource` | `IEnumerable?` | `null` | Defines the `RequestsSource` property. |
| `Pricing` | `PromptCachePricing?` | `null` | Defines the `Pricing` property. |
| `Ttl` | `double` | `300` | Defines the `Ttl` property. |
| `ChangeSegmentId` | `string?` | `"rules"` | Defines the `ChangeSegmentId` property. |
| `IsChangeArmed` | `bool` | `false` | Defines the `IsChangeArmed` property. |
| `FirstTokenEstimator` | `PromptCacheFirstTokenEstimator?` | `null` | Defines the `FirstTokenEstimator` property. |
| `Labels` | `PromptCacheLabels` | – | Defines the `Labels` property. |
| `CacheState` | `PromptCacheState` | – | *Read-only.* Defines the `CacheState` property. |
| `IsPlaying` | `bool` | `false` | Defines the `IsPlaying` property. |
| `AutoPlay` | `bool` | `true` | Defines the `AutoPlay` property. |
| `IsLooping` | `bool` | `true` | Defines the `IsLooping` property. |
| `Speed` | `double` | `1` | Defines the `Speed` property. |
| `AreControlsVisible` | `bool` | `true` | Defines the `AreControlsVisible` property. |
| `Title` | `string?` | `"Prompt cache"` | Defines the `Title` property. |
| `Model` | `ExplainerModel?` | – | Defines the `Model` property. |
| `PlaybackLabels` | `ExplainerPlaybackLabels` | – | Defines the `PlaybackLabels` property. |
| `IsFinished` | `bool` | – | *Read-only.* Defines the `IsFinished` property. |
| `IsStepping` | `bool` | – | *Read-only.* Defines the `IsStepping` property. |
| `CanStep` | `bool` | – | *Read-only.* Defines the `CanStep` property. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `RequestCompleted` | `PromptCacheRequestCompletedEventArgs` | Defines the `RequestCompleted` routed event. |
| `Expired` | `RoutedEventArgs` | Defines the `Expired` routed event. |
| `Finished` | `RoutedEventArgs` | Defines the `Finished` routed event. |

Pseudo-classes: `:narrow`, `:compact`, `:tiny`, `:empty`, `:writing`, `:reading`, `:warm`, `:expired`, `:low`, `:armed`, `:playing`, `:stepping`, `:finished`, `:ready`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

### PromptCacheSegment

One part of the stable prompt prefix of a `PromptCache` (tool schemas, instructions, documents, the chat so far). Segments are matched against the cache from left to right, so put what changes least first.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Id` | `string` | `""` | Defines the `Id` property. |
| `Label` | `string` | `""` | Defines the `Label` property. |
| `Tokens` | `int` | `0` | Defines the `Tokens` property. |
| `Color` | `IBrush?` | `null` | Defines the `Color` property. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### PromptCacheRequest

One request of a `PromptCache` round: the prefix plus a new message at the end.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Message` | `string?` | `null` | Defines the `Message` property. |
| `Tokens` | `int` | `0` | Defines the `Tokens` property. |
| `Gap` | `double` | `0` | Defines the `Gap` property. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### PromptCachePricing

The prices behind every cost a `PromptCache` shows, in dollars per million input tokens. The defaults are sample prices that follow a common pattern: cache writes at 1.25 times the input price and cache reads at a tenth of it. Pass your provider's current prices; set `CacheWritePrice` equal to `InputPrice` when writes cost nothing extra.

### PromptCacheResult

The outcome of one simulated request of a `PromptCache`.

### PromptCacheLabels

Every word a `PromptCache` shows or speaks, in English by default. Replace the instance (or set only the members you need) to translate or reword; sentences with values are functions so their word order can change. Token counts, costs and times arrive already formatted ("48.6K", "$0.0144", "0.48s"). The playback buttons' names live in `PlaybackLabels`.

## Accessibility

- The card is named after its title and marked as a simulation ("Prompt cache, a simulation with sample prices").
- The legend, the requests and the cache panel are named groups. Each request row reads as one sentence with its time,
  message, outcome, tokens read from the cache, tokens processed, cost and first token ("Request 1: not sent yet."
  before it runs); the bars and rolling numbers are hidden from assistive technology.
- Stepping, the toggle, pausing and restarting are announced in a polite live region; the story playing on its own
  stays silent.
- Outcomes never rely on color alone: every status pairs an icon with words, and cached fills differ from processed
  ones in tint and outline.
- The toggle is a toggle button and reports whether it is armed; the icon buttons have names and tooltips.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` | Move through play or pause, send the next request, restart and the change toggle |
| `Enter` or `Space` | Activate the focused button: play or pause, send a request, restart, or arm and release the edit |

Keyboard focus shows the 2px focus ring; pointer focus shows none.

## Motion

Every story animation runs on the explainer's clock, so pausing freezes all of it (a sweep in progress included) and
`Speed` scales all of it.

| Change | Full | Reduced and Off |
|---|---|---|
| Processing | Each segment fills in turn at one steady speed (a full bar in 1.1s), then the message in 120ms | Filled at once |
| Cache hit | Cached tint fades in over 160ms; a band passes over the prefix and the panel bar in 520ms | Tint at once, no band |
| Write | The written part flies into the cache panel in 460ms on a strong ease-out, solid fading to tint | Panel fills at once |
| Partial hit | A warning line rises in the gap before the changed segment (200ms); the panel drops what changed | Line shown at once |
| Numbers | Roll from the row above in 420ms (ease-out) | Change at once |
| Ring | Follows its target with a short lag; turns to the warning color in the last minute | At its target |
| Simulated gap | Passes in 0.55s on an S curve | At once |
| Idle | The time to live drains in about 4.2s, then the cache expires | Expires after a pause |
| Status and caption | Crossfade (160ms in, 100ms out) | Short crossfade |

## Related

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `SpeculativeDecoding` | You explain how a draft model speeds up generation |
| `AgentLoop` | You explain an agent's cycle of gathering context, acting and checking |
| `DataFlow` | You explain how events move through a data platform |
| `LineChart` / `BarChart` | You plot a real cache hit rate or real costs over time |
| `UsageMeter` | You show how much of a real quota is used |

---

# Reasoning tree

> A search over candidate thoughts: each is scored, weak branches are pruned, the best expand and the winning path draws in.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc.Special`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc.Special --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/reasoning-tree

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ReasoningTreeArchiveMoveDemo">
    <!-- The built-in story: three plans for moving a photo archive, searched with a beam of two. -->
    <arc:ReasoningTree MaxWidth="744" HorizontalAlignment="Center" VerticalAlignment="Top" />
</UserControl>
```

## When to use

`ReasoningTree` explains tree search over thoughts, the idea behind "tree of thoughts" prompting and beam search at test
time. A question proposes a few candidate thoughts, each one gets a score, the weakest are pruned, and the best few are
expanded one depth further. After three depths the best thought is the answer, and the path from the question to the
answer draws in. The beam width control lets the reader change how many thoughts survive each depth and watch the
search again, which is the point of the illustration: a wider search can find an answer that a greedy one misses.

- **Documentation and course material about reasoning strategies.** A page that explains why a model that explores
  several lines of thought can beat one that commits to its first idea. The reader steps through the search one beat at a
  time and reads each depth's count ("2 of 4 kept").
- **Product pages for planning or agent features.** A visual summary of how an assistant weighed options before it chose
  a plan, written in your product's own words (a migration plan, a build fix, a launch date).
- **Talks, onboarding and empty states.** A short story that plays on its own when it scrolls into view and ends on a
  clear answer with a check, without any data from your system.

The scores are illustrative. The card does not run a model and does not read real model output; it plays the search you
give it. Say so in the copy around it, for example "Scores are made up for the example."

## When not to use

- **Showing a real agent's steps as they happen.** Use `ChatThread` or `Timeline` to stream what an agent actually did. This card replays a fixed story and has no way to report progress.
- **Explaining the plan, act and observe loop of a tool-using agent.** That is a cycle, not a tree; the Agent loop
  illustration in this group tells that story.
- **Token-level mechanics.** Use the Speculative decoding or Mixture of experts illustrations for what happens inside one
  generation step. A reasoning tree works on whole thoughts.
- **Choosing a model.** A tree of thoughts does not explain routing between models; describe that with a table or a
  diagram of your own.
- **Large trees.** The card reads three depths and is designed for about three thoughts at depth 1 and two children under
  each thought. A broad tree crowds the columns; summarize it instead.

## Usage

With no data the card plays its built-in story: a team weighs three ways to move a photo archive to new storage over a
weekend. It starts the first time it is mostly in view, finds the answer in about 6.6 seconds at a beam width of 2, and
finishes drawing the path about a second later.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:ReasoningTree MaxWidth="744" />
</UserControl>
```

`ReasoningTree` derives from `Explainer`, the base of the animated AI explainers, which derives from Avalonia's
`TemplatedControl`. The base supplies the story clock, the playback buttons, autoplay on first sight, reduced-motion
handling and the polite live region; the card adds the search, the drawn tree and the beam width control.

### Your own question and thoughts

Set `Question` to a short question for the root node (about three short lines in the wide layout) and `QuestionDetail`
to the full sentence that the tag and screen readers use. Put `ReasoningThought` elements inside the card: they are the
thoughts at depth 1, and the thoughts inside them are their children. Each thought has a `Label` (two to four words, under
about 20 characters), a full `Text` and a `Score` from 0 to 0.99.

```xml
<arc:ReasoningTree Question="How do we halve the nightly build?"
                   QuestionDetail="The nightly build takes 84 minutes. How do we get it under 40 without dropping a single test suite?">
    <arc:ReasoningThought Label="Cache dependencies" Score="0.78"
                          Text="Restore packages and toolchains from a shared cache instead of downloading them every night.">
        <arc:ReasoningThought Label="Pin lockfiles" Score="0.81"
                              Text="Pin every lockfile so the cache key only changes when a dependency really does." />
        <arc:ReasoningThought Label="Warm the cache" Score="0.52"
                              Text="Run a small job before midnight that fills the cache for the nightly run." />
    </arc:ReasoningThought>
    <arc:ReasoningThought Label="Split the tests" Score="0.71"
                          Text="Run the slow integration suites on four agents in parallel instead of one." />
</arc:ReasoningTree>
```

The demo below uses that question with a full tree whose scores are written so that each beam width finds a different
answer: 0.84 with a beam of 1, 0.89 with 2 and 0.95 with 3. It starts at a beam width of 1; try 2 and 3 in its footer.

```xml

```

To bind thoughts from a view model, set `ThoughtsSource` to a collection of `ReasoningThought`; it is used instead of the
`Thoughts` written in markup. Changing a thought, adding one or removing one starts the search over. Thoughts deeper than
depth 3 are ignored, and a thought should appear under one parent only.

### Anatomy

1. **Header**: the model's mark and name (`Model`, an `ExplainerModel` with a `Name` and an optional `Mark`), the
   `Title` ("Tree of thoughts") in muted text, and the status on the right. While the search plays the status is a
   present-tense label with a calm shimmer; when the reader pauses or steps it shows a pause icon and the past tense; at
   the end it shows a green check and "Answer found". Set `Model` to null to show only the title.
2. **Column headers** (wide layout): "Question" and "Depth 1" to "Depth 3". The column of the current beat turns to the
   foreground color. After a depth is pruned its header shows "2 of 4 kept"; the last depth shows "Best of 4".
3. **Question node**: the root, on a muted fill, 84px high in the wide layout.
4. **Thought nodes**: a card with the label, a score bar and the digits. The last depth keeps room for the answer's check.
5. **Edges**: a 1.25px curve from each parent to each child in the strong border color. A pruned thought's edge retracts
   into its parent.
6. **Winning path**: a 2px line in the accent color from the question through every kept thought on the path to the
   answer, drawn over the edges with a lighter sheen at its head.
7. **Tag**: a dark bubble beside the hovered or focused thought with its full text and a second line with the score and
   fate ("Score 0.78 · Kept"). For the question, the second line reads "Question".
8. **Footer**: play or pause, next step and restart on the left, and the beam width control on the right. Under 520px the
   label reads "Beam"; under 306px the beam control moves under the buttons. `AreControlsVisible` hides the footer.

Kept thoughts and the path use `AccentBrush` (chart series 1 by default). The answer always uses the success color with a
check, so a custom accent never hides which thought won.

### The search, step by step

The search is plain beam search over at most three depths:

1. **Propose.** Depth 1 proposes every thought given to the card; later depths propose all children of the previous
   depth's survivors, in document order.
2. **Score.** Each candidate's bar fills to its score while the digits count up to it ("0.78").
3. **Keep.** The best `BeamWidth` candidates survive; the rest are pruned. Equal scores keep the thought that comes first
   in the document.
4. Survivors expand at the next depth. The last depth does not keep a beam: its best thought is the answer.

The last depth is depth 3, or an earlier depth whose survivors have no children (the search cannot go deeper). The count
beside each header is the number kept and the number of candidates; the number pruned is the difference.

With the built-in story the three widths play out like this:

| Beam width | Depth 1 | Depth 2 | Depth 3 | Answer |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1 of 3 kept | 1 of 2 kept | Best of 2 | Done by Sunday, 0.88 |
| 2 | 2 of 3 kept | 2 of 4 kept | Best of 4 | Small region first, 0.93 |
| 3 | 3 of 3 kept | 3 of 6 kept | Best of 6 | Small region first, 0.93 |

The greedy search (beam 1) follows the best first idea, copying in batches, and settles for a weaker plan; a beam of 2
keeps "Mirror, then switch" alive long enough to find the better answer.

#### Scores you leave out

A thought without a `Score` gets a seeded one: `0.18 + 0.78 × r`, rounded to two decimals, where `r` is the first value of
a mulberry32 generator seeded with `Seed` combined (XOR) with the FNV-1a hash of the thought's path key. The path key joins
the `Key` (or the label when there is no key) of the thought and its ancestors with "/". The same tree and the same
`Seed` therefore always search the same way, and giving a thought a `Key` keeps its seeded score when you rename it.
Seeded scores stay between 0.05 and 0.99. The next demo has no scores at all; "Next seed" changes `Seed` and the search
starts over with new numbers.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ReasoningTreeAnswerLogDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="16" MaxWidth="744">
        <!-- No scores: every thought gets a seeded one, so the same seed always searches the same way. -->
        <arc:ReasoningTree x:Name="Tree"
                           VerticalAlignment="Top"
                           Question="Which week should the beta open?"
                           QuestionDetail="Which week should the public beta of the team calendar open, given the support rota and the marketing plan?"
                           Answered="OnAnswered">
            <arc:ReasoningThought Key="early" Label="Open in week 18" Text="Open the beta in week 18, right after the spring release.">
                <arc:ReasoningThought Key="invites" Label="Invite-only start" Text="Start with the 400 teams on the waitlist and open fully a week later.">
                    <arc:ReasoningThought Key="mon" Label="Monday launch" Text="Send the invitations on Monday morning, when support is fully staffed." />
                    <arc:ReasoningThought Key="thu" Label="Thursday launch" Text="Send them on Thursday so the first feedback lands before the weekend." />
                </arc:ReasoningThought>
                <arc:ReasoningThought Key="open" Label="Open to everyone" Text="Let anyone sign up from the first day." />
            </arc:ReasoningThought>
            <arc:ReasoningThought Key="mid" Label="Open in week 20" Text="Open the beta in week 20, together with the conference talk.">
                <arc:ReasoningThought Key="talk" Label="Announce on stage" Text="Announce the beta during the conference keynote." />
                <arc:ReasoningThought Key="blog" Label="Blog post first" Text="Publish a blog post a day ahead so the talk can point to it." />
            </arc:ReasoningThought>
            <arc:ReasoningThought Key="late" Label="Open in week 23" Text="Open the beta in week 23, after the support team has grown." />
        </arc:ReasoningTree>
        <WrapPanel ItemSpacing="8" LineSpacing="8" VerticalAlignment="Center">
            <arc:Button Content="Beam 1" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Click="OnBeamOneClick" />
            <arc:Button Content="Beam 2" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Click="OnBeamTwoClick" />
            <arc:Button Content="Beam 3" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Click="OnBeamThreeClick" />
            <arc:Button Content="Next seed" Variant="Ghost" Size="Small" Click="OnNextSeedClick" />
            <TextBlock x:Name="State"
                       VerticalAlignment="Center"
                       FontSize="13"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
        </WrapPanel>
        <TextBlock x:Name="Log"
                   Text="Answers appear here as the search finds them."
                   FontSize="13"
                   TextWrapping="Wrap"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using System.Collections.Generic;
using System.Globalization;
using System.Linq;
using Avalonia;
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class ReasoningTreeAnswerLogDemo : UserControl
{
    private readonly List<string> _answers = new();

    public ReasoningTreeAnswerLogDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Tree.PropertyChanged += OnTreePropertyChanged;
        ShowState();
    }

    private void OnTreePropertyChanged(object? sender, AvaloniaPropertyChangedEventArgs e)
    {
        // BeamWidth is two-way: the card's own control writes it too.
        if (e.Property == ReasoningTree.BeamWidthProperty || e.Property == ReasoningTree.SeedProperty)
        {
            ShowState();
        }
    }

    private void OnAnswered(object? sender, ReasoningTreeAnsweredEventArgs e)
    {
        var path = string.Join(" → ", e.Path.Select(t => t.Label));
        _answers.Insert(0, $"Beam {e.BeamWidth}, seed {Tree.Seed}: {e.Answer.Label} ({e.Score.ToString("0.00", CultureInfo.InvariantCulture)}) via {path}");
        if (_answers.Count > 4)
        {
            _answers.RemoveAt(_answers.Count - 1);
        }
        Log.Text = string.Join("\n", _answers);
    }

    private void ShowState() => State.Text = $"Beam width {Tree.BeamWidth} · seed {Tree.Seed}";

    private void OnBeamOneClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) => Tree.BeamWidth = 1;

    private void OnBeamTwoClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) => Tree.BeamWidth = 2;

    private void OnBeamThreeClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) => Tree.BeamWidth = 3;

    private void OnNextSeedClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) => Tree.Seed++;
}
```

### Timing

At `Speed` 1 the beats fall at fixed times after a restart: the question is read for 0.56 s, then each depth proposes
(0.62 s), scores (0.88 s) and keeps (0.76 s); the last depth goes from scoring straight to the answer at 6.58 s. The path
then draws for 0.76 s after a 0.16 s pause, and the answer settles with one short press. A beat's length does not depend
on how many thoughts it shows. `Speed` divides the beat lengths (0.5 doubles them, 0 holds the story still); the fades,
bars and path keep their own durations.

### Playback

`IsPlaying` is two-way: the play button and `Play()` / `Pause()` set it, and an app can bind it. Pausing freezes the
story clock and resuming continues the current beat from where it stopped. Changes that a beat already started (a fade,
a bar filling) still finish.

`StepForward()` (the next-step button) pauses and moves to the next beat at once: from the start, nine steps reach the
answer (three per depth, minus the last keep). At the end the step button turns off and keyboard focus moves to Restart.
`Restart()` starts the search over from the question and plays it. After the answer, the play button reads "Play again".

`BeamWidth` takes 1 to 3 (other values are clamped) and is two-way: the footer control writes it and a binding can read
or set it. A new width starts the search over and plays it. `IsLooping` plays the search again four seconds after each
answer, and `AutoPlay` set to false keeps the card at "Ready" until the reader presses play.

`Answered` is raised once each time the search reaches its answer, with the answer, the path from depth 1 and the beam
width. `Answer` holds the current answer (null until it is found).

```csharp
tree.Answered += (_, e) =>
    status.Text = $"Beam {e.BeamWidth}: {e.Answer.Label} ({e.Score:0.00}) via {string.Join(" → ", e.Path.Select(t => t.Label))}";
```

### Wide and narrow

The layout follows the card's own width, not the window's. From 620px of stage (a card of about 670px) the tree reads left
to right in four columns. The question takes 19% of the width and each depth 22.5%, with 4.5% gaps. Thoughts sit on a
62px pitch, stacked around their parent and pushed apart when they would overlap. The stage reserves the tallest column
of any beam width, so the card keeps its height when the beam changes.

Narrower, the tree becomes an outline: one row per thought, indented 16px per depth and joined by elbow lines. The stage
reserves a row for every thought the current search will show, so the card does not grow while it plays. When new
thoughts are inserted under a row, the rows below glide down on a critically damped spring before the new rows fade in.
A new beam width changes the height of a narrow card over 480ms.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ReasoningTreeNarrowColumnDemo">
    <!-- Under 620px of stage the tree becomes an outline; under 520px of card the header and footer tighten. -->
    <arc:ReasoningTree Width="360" HorizontalAlignment="Center" VerticalAlignment="Top" />
</UserControl>
```

### Reduced motion

Under reduced motion (or Off) the card opens on the finished search: the path is drawn, the answer has its check, and the
status reads "Answer found". Play, step and restart still work on the same beats, but every change applies at once, the
rows do not glide and the status has no shimmer. A new beam width shows that width's finished search immediately.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ReasoningTreeReducedMotionDemo">
    <!-- Reduced motion opens on the finished search; playing and stepping still work, with every change applied at once. -->
    <arc:ReasoningTree arc:ArcMotion.Level="Reduced"
                       BeamWidth="3"
                       MaxWidth="744"
                       HorizontalAlignment="Center"
                       VerticalAlignment="Top" />
</UserControl>
```

### Content guidelines

Write the question as the reader would ask it and keep it short; put the full version, with its constraints, in
`QuestionDetail`. Write each label as the gist of a plan, not a sentence, and keep it under about 20 characters so it stays
on one line. Put the whole thought in `Text`; it appears in the tag and in the accessible name.

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| Option A | Copy in batches |
| We could maybe copy the archive in several batches | Copy in batches |
| Score: 78% | Score 0.78 (the card formats it) |
| A label with the full sentence | A short label and the sentence in `Text` |
| Question? | How should we move the photo archive? |

Write the scores so the story teaches something: if every beam width finds the same answer, the beam control has nothing
to show. A common shape is a strong first idea that leads to a mediocre plan and a weaker first idea that leads to the
best one.

### Best practices

**Do**

- Say near the card that the scores are illustrative.
- Give depth 1 about three thoughts and each later thought about two children, so the columns stay readable at every beam
  width.
- Use `Key` on thoughts whose labels may change, so their seeded scores stay put.
- Keep one playing explainer per screen and let the others wait for the reader.

**Avoid**

- Presenting the numbers as a model's real output or as a benchmark.
- Changing `Thoughts`, `Question` or `Seed` on a timer: every change starts the search over.
- Long labels: they are cut with an ellipsis, and the reader has to hover to read them.
- Trees deeper than three levels: the extra levels are ignored.

### Common questions

**Why does a beam of 3 find the same answer as a beam of 2 in the built-in story?** Because the best plan is already
inside the beam of 2. The demo with your own data shows a tree where each width finds a different answer.

**What happens with a tie?** The thought that comes first in the document wins, both for the survivors of a depth and for
the answer.

**What if a thought has no children?** It can survive its depth, but it adds no candidates to the next one. If no survivor
of a depth has children, that depth becomes the last one and its best thought is the answer.

**What if there are no thoughts at all?** An empty `Thoughts` collection without `ThoughtsSource` plays the built-in story.
An empty `ThoughtsSource` shows the question alone, with the status "No thoughts to search".

**Can I translate the card?** Yes: set `Labels` to a `ReasoningTreeLabels` with your words (headers, status, tag lines,
accessible names and announcements; sentences with numbers are functions), and `PlaybackLabels` for the buttons.

## API reference

### ReasoningTree

An animated explainer of tree search over thoughts (tree of thoughts with beam search). Each depth proposes candidate thoughts as edges draw out of their parents, scores them with bars that fill while the digits count, keeps the best `BeamWidth` and prunes the rest (they fade and their edges retract), and the survivors expand one depth further, up to three. The last depth picks its best thought as the answer, and the winning path draws from the question to the answer with a sheen at its head while each node on it lights up. Play, pause, step and restart drive the story; the beam width control starts it over. Wide cards read left to right in four columns; narrow ones become an indented outline. The scores are illustrative values, not the output of a model.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Question` | `string` | `"How should we move the photo archive?"` | Defines the `Question` property. |
| `QuestionDetail` | `string?` | `null` | Defines the `QuestionDetail` property. |
| `ThoughtsSource` | `IEnumerable<ReasoningThought>?` | `null` | Defines the `ThoughtsSource` property. |
| `BeamWidth` | `int` | `2` | Defines the `BeamWidth` property. |
| `Seed` | `int` | `7` | Defines the `Seed` property. |
| `AccentBrush` | `IBrush?` | `null` | Defines the `AccentBrush` property. |
| `Labels` | `ReasoningTreeLabels` | – | Defines the `Labels` property. |
| `Answer` | `ReasoningThought?` | – | *Read-only.* Defines the `Answer` property. |
| `IsPlaying` | `bool` | `false` | Defines the `IsPlaying` property. |
| `AutoPlay` | `bool` | `true` | Defines the `AutoPlay` property. |
| `IsLooping` | `bool` | `false` | Defines the `IsLooping` property. |
| `Speed` | `double` | `1` | Defines the `Speed` property. |
| `AreControlsVisible` | `bool` | `true` | Defines the `AreControlsVisible` property. |
| `Title` | `string?` | `"Tree of thoughts"` | Defines the `Title` property. |
| `Model` | `ExplainerModel?` | – | Defines the `Model` property. |
| `PlaybackLabels` | `ExplainerPlaybackLabels` | – | Defines the `PlaybackLabels` property. |
| `IsFinished` | `bool` | – | *Read-only.* Defines the `IsFinished` property. |
| `IsStepping` | `bool` | – | *Read-only.* Defines the `IsStepping` property. |
| `CanStep` | `bool` | – | *Read-only.* Defines the `CanStep` property. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Answered` | `ReasoningTreeAnsweredEventArgs` | Defines the `Answered` routed event. |
| `Finished` | `RoutedEventArgs` | Defines the `Finished` routed event. |

Pseudo-classes: `:compact`, `:tiny`, `:playing`, `:stepping`, `:finished`, `:ready`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

### ReasoningThought

One thought of a `ReasoningTree`: a short label for the node, the full sentence for the tag and screen readers, an illustrative score and the thoughts it leads to. The tree reads three levels: the thoughts given to `Thoughts` are depth 1, their children depth 2 and their grandchildren depth 3; deeper thoughts are ignored. Add a thought to one parent only.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Key` | `string?` | `null` | Defines the `Key` property. |
| `Label` | `string` | `""` | Defines the `Label` property. |
| `Text` | `string?` | `null` | Defines the `Text` property. |
| `Score` | `double?` | `null` | Defines the `Score` property. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### ReasoningTreeAnsweredEventArgs

The arguments of `Answered`: the answer the search reached and how it got there.

Derives from `RoutedEventArgs`: every member of `RoutedEventArgs` works as well.

### ReasoningTreeLabels

Every word a `ReasoningTree` shows or announces, in English by default: column headers, the header status, the beam width label, the tag and accessible names of the thoughts and the polite announcements. Replace the instance to translate or reword; sentences with numbers are functions so that word order can change. The playback buttons are named by `PlaybackLabels`.

## Accessibility

- The stage is a tree named after the full question ("Search tree for …"). Each shown thought is a tree item whose name is
  its full text with its score and fate (not scored yet, scored, kept, pruned, on the winning path, answer). Its help text
  gives its depth and its place among its shown siblings ("Depth 1, 1 of 3"). The question's name is "Question: " and
  the full question.
- State never relies on color alone: a pruned thought fades and loses its edge, the answer has a check, and the header
  status pairs an icon with words.
- Hover and focus show the full thought in the tag; the same words are in the accessible name, so the tag itself is hidden
  from assistive technology.
- A polite live region speaks each beat when the reader steps or pauses ("Depth 2: kept 2 of 4, pruned 2."), the new
  beam width when it changes, and the answer when the search ends. It stays quiet while the search plays on its own.
- Pointer focus draws no ring; keyboard focus draws a 2px ring outside the node that follows its corners.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Tab` | Moves to the tree (one stop, on the current thought), then play or pause, next step, restart and the beam width control |
| `ArrowUp` / `ArrowDown` | The previous or next shown thought in the same column (wide), or the previous or next row (narrow) |
| `ArrowRight` | The child on the winning path, else the best scored shown child, else the first shown child |
| `ArrowLeft` | The parent |
| `Home` / `End` | The question; the answer once it is found (before that, the first thought of the deepest shown depth) |
| `ArrowLeft` / `ArrowRight` on the beam width | Changes the beam width, which starts the search over |

When a restart hides the focused thought, focus moves to the question.

## Motion

| Change | Full | Reduced and Off |
|---|---|---|
| Thoughts proposed | Each edge draws out of its parent (240 ms) and the card fades in (180 ms), 20 ms apart per sibling | Shown at once |
| Thoughts scored | Bars fill and digits count on one 640 ms curve | Full bars and final digits |
| Depth pruned | Pruned cards fade to 40% and their edges retract (240 ms); kept bars turn to the accent | Applied at once |
| Answer | The path draws in 760 ms with a sheen at its head; each node on it lights as the line arrives; the answer settles with one press and its check | Path and check shown at once |
| New rows (narrow) | Rows below glide down on a critically damped spring before the new rows fade in | Rows jump to their places |
| Header status | Labels swap with a quiet 160 ms rise; the working label shimmers | Swap without shimmer |
| Tag | Fades in and rises 3 px out of the node's side (160 ms) | Shown at once |

The beats follow `Speed`; fades and fills keep their durations and finish even while the story is paused.

## Related

- `DataFlow` and `VectorSearch` in this group for systems rather than reasoning.
- The Agent loop, Mixture of experts, Speculative decoding and Prompt cache explainers share this card's frame, playback
  controls and header.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `Timeline` | You show what an agent really did, in order |
| `ChatThread` | You show a conversation with an assistant |
| `DataFlow` | You explain how data moves through a pipeline |
| `VectorSearch` | You explain how a question finds its nearest documents |

# Mobile page

> A phone screen: a header, the content and a footer laid out inside the device's safe area.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc.Mobile`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc.Mobile --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/mobile-page

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             xmlns:arcm="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc.Mobile"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.MobilePageBasicDemo">
    <arcm:Page>
        <arcm:Page.Header>
            <arcm:Navbar Title="Inbox">
                <arcm:Navbar.Trailing>
                    <arcm:Button Content="Edit" />
                </arcm:Navbar.Trailing>
            </arcm:Navbar>
        </arcm:Page.Header>
        <StackPanel Margin="16" Spacing="12">
            <TextBlock Text="Today" FontWeight="SemiBold" />
            <TextBlock Text="The page keeps its header and footer in place and puts the content between them."
                       TextWrapping="Wrap"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
            <arcm:Button Content="Compose" />
        </StackPanel>
        <arcm:Page.Footer>
            <arcm:Tabbar SelectedIndex="0">
                <arcm:TabbarItem Content="Inbox" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Mail}" />
                <arcm:TabbarItem Content="Search" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Search}" />
                <arcm:TabbarItem Content="Me" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.User}" />
            </arcm:Tabbar>
        </arcm:Page.Footer>
    </arcm:Page>
</UserControl>
```

## When to use

`Page` is the root of one screen of a phone or tablet app. It gives the screen its background, keeps its content clear of the status bar, the notch and the home indicator, and puts an optional header (usually a `Navbar`) above the content and an optional footer (usually a `Tabbar`) below it.

- **A screen of a mobile app**: an inbox, a settings list or a detail view, with a navbar on top and tabs at the bottom.
- **A full-bleed screen**: a welcome or onboarding screen with only content, where the background still runs under the status bar.
- **A screen that must react to the device's safe area**: the page follows the platform's safe area padding by itself, or takes one you set.

The live demos on this page run inside a phone frame: a desktop simulation with a device switcher, portrait and landscape, a simulated status bar and safe area, and a keyboard placeholder. It is not a device, and how the controls look and behave on Android and iOS, including with the real soft keyboard, has not been verified.

## When not to use

- **A desktop window or a web-style layout**: use the desktop controls (`TKCode.Arc`) and a normal layout panel. The page's safe area is zero where the platform reports none.
- **A container inside a screen**: use `Card` or a layout panel. A screen has one `Page`.
- **A modal or a sheet over a screen**: use a dialog or a drawer; the page is the screen under them.

## Usage

Set `Header`, the content and `Footer`. The mobile controls have their own XAML namespace, `https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc.Mobile`, usually prefixed `arcm`, so they sit next to the desktop controls of the same name.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             xmlns:arcm="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc.Mobile">
    <arcm:Page>
        <arcm:Page.Header>
            <arcm:Navbar Title="Inbox" />
        </arcm:Page.Header>
        <TextBlock Margin="16" Text="Hello" />
    </arcm:Page>
</UserControl>
```

Register the controls with `UseArcMobile()` next to `UseArcCore()` or `UseArcControls()`.

### Safe area

`SafeArea` is the space the page keeps free on each edge. While `UsePlatformSafeArea` is on (the default), the page follows the safe area padding of the top level's insets manager and uses zero where there is none, such as on desktop. Turn `UsePlatformSafeArea` off and set `SafeArea` yourself to override it. The background fills the whole page, so it runs under the status bar while the header and content stay inside the safe area.

The phone frame does this for the demos: it sets `SafeArea` from the simulated device and turns `UsePlatformSafeArea` off. Use the switcher above the phone to see an iPhone-like notch and home indicator, a gesture bar, a small phone and a tablet, and the keyboard toggle to see the page lay out above the keyboard.

### Content only

A page without a header or footer lets the content use the whole safe area.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             xmlns:arcm="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc.Mobile"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.MobilePageContentOnlyDemo">
    <arcm:Page>
        <StackPanel Margin="24" Spacing="12" VerticalAlignment="Center">
            <TextBlock Text="Welcome" FontSize="28" FontWeight="SemiBold" />
            <TextBlock Text="With no header and no footer the content fills the safe area, clear of the status bar and the home indicator."
                       TextWrapping="Wrap"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
            <arcm:Button Content="Get started" />
        </StackPanel>
    </arcm:Page>
</UserControl>
```

### Scrolling content

By default the content gets the page's height as it is, so a screen that fills the page can lay itself out. Set `IsScrollable="True"` when the content can be taller than the page: it then scrolls vertically inside the page, between the header and the footer. A `Navbar` with a large title in the `Header` collapses it as the content scrolls.

```xml
<arcm:Page IsScrollable="True">
    <arcm:Page.Header>
        <arcm:Navbar Title="Photos" LargeTitle="True" />
    </arcm:Page.Header>
    <!-- long content -->
</arcm:Page>
```

### Keyboard

When the soft keyboard is up, the page lays itself out above it: the content shrinks by the keyboard's height, the footer goes behind the keyboard (the way iOS hides a tab bar) and the focused input is scrolled into view. `AvoidKeyboard` (default on) controls this; turn it off for a page the keyboard may cover. `KeyboardInset` is the height the keyboard covers, 0 when it is hidden, and it combines with `SafeArea`: the page keeps the larger of the two at the bottom. Put `IsScrollable="True"` on a form so the fields scroll above the keyboard.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             xmlns:arcm="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc.Mobile"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.MobilePageKeyboardDemo">
    <arcm:Page IsScrollable="True">
        <arcm:Page.Header>
            <arcm:Navbar Title="New contact" />
        </arcm:Page.Header>
        <StackPanel Margin="16" Spacing="12">
            <TextBlock Text="Turn on Keyboard above the phone, then tap a field."
                       TextWrapping="Wrap"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
            <arcm:TextField PlaceholderText="First name" />
            <arcm:TextField PlaceholderText="Last name" />
            <arcm:TextField PlaceholderText="Company" />
            <arcm:TextField PlaceholderText="Phone" />
            <arcm:TextField PlaceholderText="Email" />
            <arcm:TextField PlaceholderText="Address" />
            <arcm:TextField PlaceholderText="Notes" />
            <arcm:Button Content="Save" />
        </StackPanel>
        <arcm:Page.Footer>
            <arcm:Tabbar SelectedIndex="0">
                <arcm:TabbarItem Content="Contacts" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.User}" />
                <arcm:TabbarItem Content="Search" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Search}" />
            </arcm:Tabbar>
        </arcm:Page.Footer>
    </arcm:Page>
</UserControl>
```

The height comes from the platform's input pane (`TopLevel.InputPane`) when there is one. A host without it, such as the phone frame on this page, reports it with a `KeyboardInsetSource`, set on any control above the page.

```csharp
var keyboard = new KeyboardInsetSource();
Page.SetKeyboardInsetSource(host, keyboard); // inherited by every page below host
keyboard.Set(291);                            // the keyboard is up, 291 high
keyboard.Set(0);                              // and down again
```

An overlay such as a `Sheet` reads the height from anywhere inside the page with `Page.GetKeyboardInset(visual)`, to lift itself above the keyboard.

### Tokens

`PageToken` holds the geometry: `ContentInset` (the padding around the content slot, 0). The background, foreground, font and size come from the ArcDesign tokens (`Background`, `Foreground`, `BodyFontFamily`, `TypeBase`), so the page follows light and dark and the accent.

## API reference

### MobilePage

A mobile page: an optional `Header` (usually a `Navbar`), the content, and an optional `Footer` (usually a `Tabbar`), laid out inside the device's safe area. The safe area is the space the notch, rounded corners and gesture bar take; on desktop and in tests it is zero unless set by hand.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Header` | `object?` | `null` | The slot above the content, usually a `Navbar`. |
| `Footer` | `object?` | `null` | The slot below the content, usually a `Tabbar`. |
| `Overlay` | `object?` | `null` | The slot over the whole page, header and footer included, for a `Sheet`. |
| `SafeArea` | `Thickness` | `0,0,0,0` | The insets the page keeps free on each edge. With `UsePlatformSafeArea` the platform sets it (zero where there is no insets manager); otherwise set it yourself. |
| `UsePlatformSafeArea` | `bool` | `true` | Whether `SafeArea` follows the platform's safe area padding. |
| `IsScrollable` | `bool` | `false` | Whether the content scrolls vertically inside the page. Off, the content gets the page's height as it is. On, a `Navbar` in `Header` that has a large title collapses it as the content scrolls. |
| `AvoidKeyboard` | `bool` | `true` | Whether the page lays out above the soft keyboard: the content shrinks by the keyboard's height, so the focused input stays visible, and the footer (a `Tabbar`) goes behind the keyboard the way iOS does. Off, the keyboard covers the page and only `KeyboardInset` reports it. |
| `KeyboardInset` | `double` | `0` | *Attached.* *Read-only.* The height the soft keyboard covers at the bottom edge, read from the page or from any control inside it with `GetKeyboardInset` (it is inherited), so an overlay such as a `Sheet` can lift itself. It is the target height, not the animated one: it is 0 when the keyboard is hidden. |
| `KeyboardInsetSource` | `KeyboardInsetSource?` | `null` | *Attached.* Where the pages below a control get the keyboard's height when the platform has no input pane: set it on a host (inherited). Null uses `TopLevel.InputPane`. |

Derives from `ContentControl`: every member of `ContentControl` works as well.

## Accessibility

The page adds no keyboard behavior or role of its own; its header, content and footer keep theirs. Keep the content in reading order and give the navbar a `Title` so the screen has a name.

## Motion

The background follows light and dark on the standard curve. With reduced motion it switches at once.

The page follows the keyboard with a `MotionValue` on the bottom inset, because the inset is a layout input that a ControlTheme transition cannot express. It uses the platform's own keyboard duration when the platform reports one, otherwise a smooth spring on the way up and a snappy one on the way down. With reduced motion, or with motion off, the layout jumps to the keyboard. The focused input is scrolled into view when the keyboard arrives and again when it has settled.

## Related

- `MobileNavbar`: the page's top bar.
- `MobileTabbar`: the page's bottom bar.
- `MobileButton` and `MobileSwitch`: touch controls for the content.

# Mobile navbar

> The 44 px top bar of a page: a leading slot, a centered title and a trailing slot for actions.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc.Mobile`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc.Mobile --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/mobile-navbar

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             xmlns:arcm="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc.Mobile"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.MobileNavbarBasicDemo">
    <arcm:Page>
        <arcm:Page.Header>
            <arcm:Navbar Title="Settings" ShowBack="True" BackText="Home">
                <arcm:Navbar.Trailing>
                    <arcm:Button Variant="Plain" Content="Done" />
                </arcm:Navbar.Trailing>
            </arcm:Navbar>
        </arcm:Page.Header>
        <TextBlock Margin="16"
                   Text="Leading, title and trailing sit in one 44 px bar."
                   TextWrapping="Wrap"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
    </arcm:Page>
</UserControl>
```

## When to use

`Navbar` is the top bar of a mobile screen. It shows where the person is (the `Title`), and offers the way back (`Leading`) and the screen's actions (`Trailing`).

- **A pushed screen**: a back button in `Leading`, the screen's name as the title and a "Done" or "Edit" button in `Trailing`.
- **A root screen with one action**: only a title and a button at the end.
- **A plain title bar**: only a title, with empty slots that keep it centered.

The live demos run inside a phone frame, a desktop simulation. How the bar sits under a real status bar or notch on Android and iOS has not been verified; the page's safe area, set by the frame here, keeps it clear of them.

## When not to use

- **Navigation between top-level areas**: use `Tabbar`, which stays at the bottom where the thumb reaches.
- **A desktop header with menus and search**: use the desktop header blocks and controls.
- **A toolbar with many actions**: a navbar has room for one or two touch targets at each end.

## Usage

Put the navbar in a page's `Header`. Both slots take any content, usually `arcm:Button`s, and keep a minimum width of 44 so a button stays touchable.

```xml
<arcm:Page xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
           xmlns:arcm="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc.Mobile">
    <arcm:Page.Header>
        <arcm:Navbar Title="Settings">
            <arcm:Navbar.Leading>
                <arcm:Button Content="Back" />
            </arcm:Navbar.Leading>
            <arcm:Navbar.Trailing>
                <arcm:Button Content="Done" />
            </arcm:Navbar.Trailing>
        </arcm:Navbar>
    </arcm:Page.Header>
</arcm:Page>
```

### Title only

Without slot content the title stays centered.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             xmlns:arcm="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc.Mobile"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.MobileNavbarTitleOnlyDemo">
    <arcm:Page>
        <arcm:Page.Header>
            <arcm:Navbar Title="Photos" />
        </arcm:Page.Header>
        <TextBlock Margin="16"
                   Text="With empty slots the title stays centered."
                   TextWrapping="Wrap"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
    </arcm:Page>
</UserControl>
```

### Back button

Set `ShowBack` to show a plain back button (a chevron and `BackText`, usually the previous screen's title) before `Leading`, and give it a `BackCommand`. Bar actions in `Trailing` should use `Variant="Plain"` so the title stays the focus.

```xml
<arcm:Navbar Title="Settings" ShowBack="True" BackText="Home" BackCommand="{Binding GoBack}" />
```


### Large title

Set `LargeTitle` on a root screen to show the title again as a large heading under the bar. Put the navbar in the `Header` of a `Page` with `IsScrollable="True"` and it collapses by itself as the content scrolls. Outside a scrolling page, drive `CollapseProgress` (0 to 1) yourself from a scroll offset divided by `LargeTitleExtent` (52): the large row shrinks and the bar's own title fades in, so the title is never shown twice at full size.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             xmlns:arcm="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc.Mobile"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.MobileNavbarLargeTitleDemo">
    <arcm:Page IsScrollable="True">
        <arcm:Page.Header>
            <arcm:Navbar Title="Photos" LargeTitle="True" />
        </arcm:Page.Header>
        <StackPanel Margin="16" Spacing="12">
            <TextBlock Text="Scroll the page: the large title collapses into the bar."
                       TextWrapping="Wrap"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
            <Border Height="120" CornerRadius="12" Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Surface}" />
            <Border Height="120" CornerRadius="12" Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Surface}" />
            <Border Height="120" CornerRadius="12" Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Surface}" />
            <Border Height="120" CornerRadius="12" Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Surface}" />
            <Border Height="120" CornerRadius="12" Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Surface}" />
            <Border Height="120" CornerRadius="12" Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Surface}" />
        </StackPanel>
    </arcm:Page>
</UserControl>
```

```xml
<arcm:Page IsScrollable="True">
    <arcm:Page.Header>
        <arcm:Navbar Title="Photos" LargeTitle="True" />
    </arcm:Page.Header>
    <!-- long content -->
</arcm:Page>
```

### Tokens

`NavbarToken` holds the geometry: `BarHeight` (44, hairline included), `BarPadding` (8 at the sides), `SlotMinWidth` (44), `BarBorderThickness` (a 1 px hairline under the bar), `LargeTitleFontSize` (30) and `LargeTitleMargin`. Colors and type come from the ArcDesign tokens.

## API reference

### MobileNavbar

The top bar of a `Page`: a `Leading` slot (usually a back button), a centered `Title` and a `Trailing` slot for actions. It is 44 high, and the slots are at least 44 wide.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Title` | `string?` | `null` | The bar's title. |
| `Leading` | `object?` | `null` | The content at the start of the bar, usually a back button. |
| `Trailing` | `object?` | `null` | The content at the end of the bar, usually action buttons. |
| `ShowBack` | `bool` | `false` | Whether the bar shows a back button (a chevron and `BackText`) before `Leading`. |
| `BackText` | `string?` | `null` | The back button's label, usually the previous screen's title. Empty shows the chevron alone. |
| `BackCommand` | `ICommand?` | `null` | The command the back button runs. |
| `LargeTitle` | `bool` | `false` | Whether the title also shows as a large heading under the bar, like a root screen in iOS. |
| `CollapseProgress` | `double` | `0` | How far the large title has collapsed into the bar, from 0 (fully shown) to 1 (gone, the bar's own title is shown). Bind it to the page's scroll offset divided by `LargeTitleExtent`. It does nothing without `LargeTitle`. |
| `LargeTitleHeight` | `double` | – | *Read-only.* The current height of the large title row, between 0 and `LargeTitleExtent`. |
| `BarTitleOpacity` | `double` | – | *Read-only.* The opacity of the title in the bar: 1 normally, and with a large title it fades in as the large one collapses. |

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

## Accessibility

The title is plain text; give every screen one. The slot buttons are normal buttons with a 44 px touch target. Give a back button a name that says where it goes.

## Motion

A changed title rises out of a soft blur while the old one lifts away (P2, `ArcContentSwap` blur swap); the first title and reduced motion do not animate. The large title follows the scroll offset one to one and has no animation of its own. The buttons in the slots press and release as `MobileButton` does.

## Related

- `MobilePage`: puts the navbar in its `Header`.
- `MobileButton`: the usual content of the slots.
- `MobileTabbar`: the bottom bar.

# Mobile toolbar

> The 44 px bottom action bar of a page: plain actions that share the width, or leading, center and trailing slots.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc.Mobile`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc.Mobile --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/mobile-toolbar

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             xmlns:arcm="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc.Mobile"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.MobileToolbarBasicDemo">
    <arcm:Page>
        <arcm:Page.Header>
            <arcm:Navbar Title="Photo" ShowBack="True" BackText="Library" />
        </arcm:Page.Header>
        <TextBlock Margin="16"
                   Text="The toolbar's actions share the width, and a finger on one dims it."
                   TextWrapping="Wrap"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
        <arcm:Page.Footer>
            <arcm:Toolbar>
                <arcm:Button Variant="Plain" Content="Share" />
                <arcm:Button Variant="Plain" Content="Edit" />
                <arcm:Button Variant="Plain" Content="Favorite" />
                <arcm:Button Variant="Plain" Content="Delete" />
            </arcm:Toolbar>
        </arcm:Page.Footer>
    </arcm:Page>
</UserControl>
```

## When to use

`Toolbar` is the bar of actions that belong to the current screen, at the bottom where the thumb reaches. It acts on what the person is looking at, where `Tabbar` moves between areas.

- **Actions on one item**: share, edit, favorite and delete under a photo or a document.
- **A selection**: "Move", "Copy" and "Delete" once rows are selected, with the count in the middle.
- **A composer or a form**: a leading "Cancel" and a trailing "Send".

The live demos run inside a phone frame, a desktop simulation. How the bar sits above the home indicator on iOS and Android has not been verified; the page's safe area, set by the frame here, keeps it clear.

## When not to use

- **Moving between top-level areas**: use `Tabbar`.
- **Actions at the top of a screen**: use the slots of `Navbar`.
- **More than about five actions**: move the rest into a `Sheet`.

## Usage

Put the toolbar in a page's `Footer`. Items are plain `arcm:Button`s with `Variant="Plain"`, so the bar stays quiet; they share the width equally and each is at least 44 px high.

```xml
<arcm:Page xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
           xmlns:arcm="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc.Mobile">
    <arcm:Page.Footer>
        <arcm:Toolbar>
            <arcm:Button Variant="Plain" Content="Share" />
            <arcm:Button Variant="Plain" Content="Edit" />
            <arcm:Button Variant="Plain" Content="Delete" />
        </arcm:Toolbar>
    </arcm:Page.Footer>
</arcm:Page>
```

### Slots

`Leading`, `Center` and `Trailing` place content at the start, the middle and the end of the bar instead of spreading items.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             xmlns:arcm="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc.Mobile"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.MobileToolbarSlotsDemo">
    <arcm:Page>
        <arcm:Page.Header>
            <arcm:Navbar Title="Inbox" />
        </arcm:Page.Header>
        <TextBlock Margin="16"
                   Text="Leading and trailing actions sit at the edges, and the middle shows a status."
                   TextWrapping="Wrap"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
        <arcm:Page.Footer>
            <arcm:Toolbar>
                <arcm:Toolbar.Leading>
                    <arcm:Button Variant="Plain" Content="Mark all" />
                </arcm:Toolbar.Leading>
                <arcm:Toolbar.Center>
                    <TextBlock Text="3 unread"
                               FontSize="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TypeSM}"
                               Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
                </arcm:Toolbar.Center>
                <arcm:Toolbar.Trailing>
                    <arcm:Button Variant="Plain" Content="Compose" />
                </arcm:Toolbar.Trailing>
            </arcm:Toolbar>
        </arcm:Page.Footer>
    </arcm:Page>
</UserControl>
```

```xml
<arcm:Toolbar>
    <arcm:Toolbar.Leading>
        <arcm:Button Variant="Plain" Content="Cancel" />
    </arcm:Toolbar.Leading>
    <arcm:Toolbar.Trailing>
        <arcm:Button Variant="Plain" Content="Send" />
    </arcm:Toolbar.Trailing>
</arcm:Toolbar>
```

### Above a tab bar, shown and hidden

Stack the toolbar and a `Tabbar` in one `StackPanel` in `Footer`. `IsOpen` shows and hides the toolbar with a slide and a fade; bind it to the state that decides whether there is anything to act on.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             xmlns:arcm="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc.Mobile"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.MobileToolbarWithTabbarDemo">
    <arcm:Page>
        <arcm:Page.Header>
            <arcm:Navbar Title="Files" />
        </arcm:Page.Header>
        <StackPanel Margin="16" Spacing="12">
            <StackPanel Orientation="Horizontal" Spacing="12">
                <arcm:Switch Name="BarSwitch" IsChecked="True" VerticalAlignment="Center" />
                <TextBlock Text="Show the toolbar"
                           VerticalAlignment="Center"
                           Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
            </StackPanel>
            <TextBlock Text="The toolbar slides down and fades out when it closes, and comes back the same way."
                       TextWrapping="Wrap"
                       FontSize="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TypeSM}"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
        </StackPanel>
        <arcm:Page.Footer>
            <StackPanel>
                <arcm:Toolbar IsOpen="{Binding #BarSwitch.IsChecked}">
                    <arcm:Button Variant="Plain" Content="Move" />
                    <arcm:Button Variant="Plain" Content="Copy" />
                    <arcm:Button Variant="Plain" Content="Delete" />
                </arcm:Toolbar>
                <arcm:Tabbar SelectedIndex="0">
                    <arcm:TabbarItem Content="Recent" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Search}" />
                    <arcm:TabbarItem Content="Browse" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Bell}" />
                </arcm:Tabbar>
            </StackPanel>
        </arcm:Page.Footer>
    </arcm:Page>
</UserControl>
```

```xml
<arcm:Page xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
           xmlns:arcm="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc.Mobile">
    <arcm:Page.Footer>
        <StackPanel>
            <arcm:Toolbar IsOpen="{Binding HasSelection}">
                <arcm:Button Variant="Plain" Content="Delete" />
            </arcm:Toolbar>
            <arcm:Tabbar SelectedIndex="0" />
        </StackPanel>
    </arcm:Page.Footer>
</arcm:Page>
```

A closed toolbar keeps its place in the layout so the content above does not jump. Set `IsVisible` to `False` to remove it.

### Tokens

`ToolbarToken` holds the geometry: `BarHeight` (44, hairline included), `BarPadding` (8 at the sides) and `BarBorderThickness` (a 1 px hairline above the bar). Colors and type come from the ArcDesign tokens.

## API reference

### MobileToolbar

The bottom action bar of a `Page`: 44 high with a hairline above it. Put plain `Button`s in it as items and they share the width equally, or fill the `Leading`, `Center` and `Trailing` slots. It is meant for `Footer`, alone or in a stack above a `Tabbar`. `IsOpen` shows and hides the bar: it slides down and fades out (faster than it came), and slides up and fades in. The position is a `MotionValue`, not a ControlTheme transition, because a toggle that flips mid-flight must continue from where the bar is rather than restart. Under reduced motion the bar jumps. A closed bar keeps its place in the layout, so the content does not jump; set IsVisible to false to remove it.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `IsOpen` | `bool` | `true` | Whether the bar is shown. False slides it away and stops it catching touches. |
| `Leading` | `object?` | `null` | The content at the start of the bar, usually one action. |
| `Center` | `object?` | `null` | The content in the middle of the bar, next to the items. |
| `Trailing` | `object?` | `null` | The content at the end of the bar, usually one action. |

Derives from `ItemsControl`: every member of `ItemsControl` works as well.

## Accessibility

Each action is a normal button with a 44 px touch target; give icon-only actions an accessible name. A closed toolbar does not catch touches.

## Motion

Closing slides the bar down by its own height while it fades out, in a short tween; opening slides it back up on a snappy spring. Toggling `IsOpen` again while it moves turns it around from where it is. The first frame has no motion, and under reduced motion the bar jumps. The buttons press and release as `MobileButton` does.

## Related

- `MobilePage`: puts the toolbar in its `Footer`.
- `MobileButton`: the usual content, with `Variant="Plain"`.
- `MobileTabbar`: the bar for moving between areas, often just below the toolbar.
- `MobileSheet`: for the actions that do not fit.
