# Mobile tabbar

> The bottom tab bar of a page: icon-over-label tabs that share the width, with the selected one highlighted.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc.Mobile`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc.Mobile --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/mobile-tabbar

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             xmlns:arcm="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc.Mobile"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.MobileTabbarBasicDemo">
    <arcm:Page>
        <TextBlock Margin="16"
                   Text="Tap a tab to select it. A finger on a tab dims it; there is no hover state."
                   TextWrapping="Wrap"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
        <arcm:Page.Footer>
            <arcm:Tabbar SelectedIndex="0">
                <arcm:TabbarItem Content="Home" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.House}" />
                <arcm:TabbarItem Content="Search" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Search}" />
                <arcm:TabbarItem Content="Alerts" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Bell}" />
                <arcm:TabbarItem Content="Profile" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.User}" />
            </arcm:Tabbar>
        </arcm:Page.Footer>
    </arcm:Page>
</UserControl>
```

## When to use

`Tabbar` is the bottom navigation of a mobile screen: a few top-level areas the person switches between with a thumb.

- **Top-level areas of an app**: Home, Search, Alerts and Profile, always in reach.
- **Two to five destinations**: the items share the width equally, so keep the label short.

Each `TabbarItem` shows an `Icon` above its label. The live demo runs inside a phone frame, a desktop simulation; touch feedback on a real device has not been verified here.

## When not to use

- **Views of one object**: use a segmented control or tabs inside the screen.
- **More than five destinations**: move the rest into a "More" screen or a menu.
- **A desktop sidebar**: use `Sidebar` from the desktop package.

## Usage

Put `TabbarItem`s in the bar, and set `SelectedIndex` (or `SelectedItem`) to the open one. `Tabbar` derives from Avalonia's `ListBox`, so selection, `SelectionChanged` and binding to `ItemsSource` work as they do there. Use the bar as a page's `Footer`.

```xml
<arcm:Tabbar xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             xmlns:arcm="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc.Mobile"
             SelectedIndex="0">
    <arcm:TabbarItem Content="Home" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.House}" />
    <arcm:TabbarItem Content="Search" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Search}" />
    <arcm:TabbarItem Content="Profile" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.User}" />
</arcm:Tabbar>
```

The selected item uses the foreground color and the others the muted text color. A finger on an item dims it; there is no hover state.

### Tokens

`TabbarToken` holds the bar's geometry: `BarHeight` (49) and `BarBorderThickness` (a 1 px hairline above it). `TabbarItemToken` holds an item's: `TouchTarget` (44), `IconExtent` (24), `IconGap` (2), `PressedOpacity` (0.6) and `ItemPadding` (4). Colors come from the ArcDesign tokens.

## API reference

### MobileTabbar

The bottom tab bar of a `Page`. Put `TabbarItem`s in it; the selected one is highlighted and the items share the width equally. One accent pill glides behind the icon of the selected item on a spring, and jumps with reduced motion.

Derives from `ListBox`: every member of `ListBox` works as well.

### MobileTabbarItem

One tab of a `Tabbar`: an `Icon` above its label (the content). It is at least 44 high and has no hover state.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Icon` | `Geometry?` | `null` | The glyph geometry shown above the label, for example a Lucide icon. |

Derives from `ListBoxItem`: every member of `ListBoxItem` works as well.

## Accessibility

Items are selectable list items with a label, so they are named by their content. Keep the labels, so the icon is never the only name. Each item is at least 44 px tall.

## Motion

One accent pill glides between the items on a spring (P7, `GlidingIndicator`): it fades in where it lands the first time, snaps instead of gliding when the bar is resized, and jumps with reduced motion. The icon and label colors change on the fast curve. A finger dims the item and shrinks its content to 0.96 on a snappy spring (P1). With reduced motion nothing scales and everything switches at once.

## Related

- `MobilePage`: puts the tabbar in its `Footer`.
- `MobileNavbar`: the top bar.

# Mobile navigation stack

> A stack of pages: a pushed page slides in over the one below, and a swipe from the left edge or a back button slides it away.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc.Mobile`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc.Mobile --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/mobile-navigation-stack

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             xmlns:arcm="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc.Mobile"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.MobileNavigationStackBasicDemo">
    <arcm:NavigationStack Name="Stack">
        <arcm:Page IsScrollable="True">
            <arcm:Page.Header>
                <arcm:Navbar Title="Inbox" LargeTitle="True" />
            </arcm:Page.Header>
            <arcm:ListGroup Footer="Tap a row to push its page. Swipe from the left edge to go back.">
                <arcm:ListItem Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.User}" Content="Ada Lovelace" Subtitle="Notes on the engine" ShowChevron="True" Click="OnOpen" />
                <arcm:ListItem Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.User}" Content="Grace Hopper" Subtitle="The compiler is ready" ShowChevron="True" Click="OnOpen" />
                <arcm:ListItem Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.User}" Content="Alan Turing" Subtitle="About that machine" ShowChevron="True" Click="OnOpen" />
            </arcm:ListGroup>
        </arcm:Page>
    </arcm:NavigationStack>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class MobileNavigationStackBasicDemo : UserControl
{
    public MobileNavigationStackBasicDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
    }

    private void OnOpen(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        var title = (string)((Mobile.ListItem)sender!).Content!;
        Stack.Push(new Mobile.Page
        {
            Header = new Mobile.Navbar { Title = title, ShowBack = true, BackText = "Inbox", BackCommand = Stack.BackCommand },
            Content = new TextBlock { Margin = new(16), Text = $"A message from {title}.", TextWrapping = Avalonia.Media.TextWrapping.Wrap },
        });
    }
}
```

## When to use

`NavigationStack` is the way a mobile app moves deeper: from a list to a detail, from settings to a sub-screen, and back again.

- **Drill-down**: each tap on a row pushes a page that explains it.
- **A flow of screens** that has one way back, such as a few steps of a form.
- **Back by swipe**: the person expects to pull the page back from the left edge, and it follows the finger.

The live demo runs inside a phone frame, a desktop simulation; the swipe and the feel of the slide on a real device have not been verified here.

## When not to use

- **Switching between top-level areas**: use `Tabbar`; each area can hold its own stack.
- **A short task over the current screen**: use `Sheet`, which does not leave the page.
- **Two panes next to each other**: a stack shows one page at a time.

## Usage

Put the first page in the stack, then `Push` pages from code. A page is any control, usually a `Page` with a `Navbar`. Bind the navbar's `BackCommand` to the stack's `BackCommand`: it runs `Pop`, and is disabled on the first page.

```xml
<arcm:NavigationStack xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
                      xmlns:arcm="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc.Mobile"
                      Name="Stack">
    <arcm:Page>
        <arcm:Page.Header>
            <arcm:Navbar Title="Inbox" />
        </arcm:Page.Header>
        <!-- the first page -->
    </arcm:Page>
</arcm:NavigationStack>
```

```csharp
stack.Push(new Page
{
    Header = new Navbar { Title = "Ada", ShowBack = true, BackText = "Inbox", BackCommand = stack.BackCommand },
    Content = detail,
});
```

A push slides the new page in from the right while the page below shifts left by a third of the width and dims. `Pop` does the reverse, and `PopToRoot` returns to the first page, sliding only the top one away. A push or pop that arrives while another is sliding finishes the first at once.

Only the top page is in the visual tree while the stack rests. Pages below it keep their state, such as the scroll position, and come back as they were.

### Tabs with a stack each

A tabbar usually sits under a stack of its own for each tab. Keep one `NavigationStack` per tab and swap the page's `Content` when the selection changes: each tab keeps the pages it has pushed, and the tabbar stays visible under every page.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             xmlns:arcm="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc.Mobile"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.MobileNavigationStackTabsWithStacksDemo">
    <arcm:Page Name="Shell">
        <arcm:Page.Footer>
            <arcm:Tabbar Name="Tabs" SelectedIndex="0" SelectionChanged="OnTabChanged">
                <arcm:TabbarItem Content="Home" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.House}" />
                <arcm:TabbarItem Content="Search" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Search}" />
                <arcm:TabbarItem Content="Profile" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.User}" />
            </arcm:Tabbar>
        </arcm:Page.Footer>
    </arcm:Page>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class MobileNavigationStackTabsWithStacksDemo : UserControl
{
    private static readonly string[] s_titles = ["Home", "Search", "Profile"];

    // One stack per tab: switching tabs swaps the stack, so each tab keeps the pages it has pushed.
    private readonly Mobile.NavigationStack[] _stacks;

    public MobileNavigationStackTabsWithStacksDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        _stacks = s_titles.Select(CreateStack).ToArray();
        Shell.Content = _stacks[0];
    }

    private static Mobile.NavigationStack CreateStack(string title)
    {
        var stack = new Mobile.NavigationStack();
        var open = new Mobile.Button { Content = "Open a page", HorizontalAlignment = Avalonia.Layout.HorizontalAlignment.Center };
        open.Click += (_, _) => stack.Push(CreateDetail(stack, title, stack.Depth));
        stack.Root = new Mobile.Page
        {
            Header = new Mobile.Navbar { Title = title },
            Content = new StackPanel { VerticalAlignment = Avalonia.Layout.VerticalAlignment.Center, Spacing = 12, Children = { open } },
        };
        return stack;
    }

    private static Mobile.Page CreateDetail(Mobile.NavigationStack stack, string tab, int depth)
    {
        var next = new Mobile.Button { Content = "Go deeper", HorizontalAlignment = Avalonia.Layout.HorizontalAlignment.Center };
        next.Click += (_, _) => stack.Push(CreateDetail(stack, tab, stack.Depth));
        return new Mobile.Page
        {
            Header = new Mobile.Navbar { Title = $"{tab} {depth}", ShowBack = true, BackText = depth == 1 ? tab : "Back", BackCommand = stack.BackCommand },
            Content = new StackPanel { VerticalAlignment = Avalonia.Layout.VerticalAlignment.Center, Spacing = 12, Children = { next } },
        };
    }

    private void OnTabChanged(object? sender, SelectionChangedEventArgs e)
    {
        // The first selection fires while the XAML loads, before the stacks exist.
        if (sender is Mobile.Tabbar { SelectedIndex: >= 0 and var index } && _stacks is not null && index < _stacks.Length)
        {
            Shell.Content = _stacks[index];
        }
    }
}
```

### Swipe back

A horizontal drag that starts within 24 px of the left edge pulls the top page away, one to one with the finger, with the page below shifting and clearing as it goes. On release the stack looks ahead 0.2 s at the finger's speed: past the middle the page leaves, and a rightward flick faster than 500 px/s pops it from anywhere. Otherwise the page springs back. Set `IsSwipeBackEnabled` to `False` for a page that must not be left by a swipe.

The `Navigated` event reports each push and pop as soon as the stack changes, while the slide may still be running.

### Tokens

`NavigationStackToken` holds `DimColor`: the dim over the page below when the top page has not moved yet, different in light and dark. The parallax (0.3 of the width) and the edge width (24) are constants of the control, `ParallaxFraction` and `EdgeWidth`.

## API reference

### MobileNavigationStack

A stack of pages, one on top. `Push` slides a page in from the right over the one below, which shifts left and dims; `Pop` and the back swipe from the left edge slide it away again. The swipe follows the finger, and on release the finger's speed decides whether the page leaves or springs back. Pages are usually `Page`s; only the top one is in the visual tree while the stack is at rest, and a page that is not on top keeps its state. Bind a `Navbar`'s `BackCommand` to `BackCommand`. The slide is a `MotionValue`, not a ControlTheme transition: the swipe writes it on every move and a release hands the finger's velocity to the spring. Under reduced motion pages change at once.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Root` | `Control?` | `null` | The first page of the stack. Setting it resets the stack to that one page. |
| `IsSwipeBackEnabled` | `bool` | `true` | Whether a swipe from the left edge pops the top page: true. |
| `CanGoBack` | `bool` | – | *Read-only.* Whether there is a page to go back to. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Navigated` | `NavigationEventArgs` | Raised when a page is pushed or popped, as soon as the stack changes (the slide may still be running). |

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

## Accessibility

Keep the back button in the navbar visible with a name that says where it goes, so the swipe is never the only way back. Only the top page is in the tree, so screen readers and the keyboard reach nothing hidden under it.

## Motion

The slide is a code-driven motion value: the swipe writes it on every move, and on release the finger's speed goes into a smooth spring, which a transition declared in the theme cannot do. The dim and the shift of the page below follow the top page's position. With reduced motion the pages change at once.

## Related

- `MobileNavbar`: its `BackCommand` binds to the stack's `BackCommand`.
- `MobilePage`: the usual page.
- `MobileSheet`: for a short task that stays on the current page.

---

# Mobile list

> Grouped rows for settings and menus: icon, title, subtitle, a value or control at the end and a chevron.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc.Mobile`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc.Mobile --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/mobile-list

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             xmlns:arcm="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc.Mobile"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.MobileListGroupBasicDemo">
    <arcm:Page IsScrollable="True">
        <arcm:Page.Header>
            <arcm:Navbar Title="Settings" LargeTitle="True" />
        </arcm:Page.Header>
        <StackPanel>
            <arcm:ListGroup Header="Account" Footer="Your name and email are shown to people you share with.">
                <arcm:ListItem Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.User}" Content="Profile" Subtitle="Ada Lovelace" ShowChevron="True" />
                <arcm:ListItem Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Search}" Content="Search history" ShowChevron="True" />
            </arcm:ListGroup>
            <arcm:ListGroup Header="Notifications">
                <arcm:ListItem Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Bell}" Content="Push notifications">
                    <arcm:ListItem.Trailing>
                        <arcm:Switch IsChecked="True" />
                    </arcm:ListItem.Trailing>
                </arcm:ListItem>
                <arcm:ListItem Content="Weekly summary" Trailing="Sundays" ShowChevron="True" />
            </arcm:ListGroup>
        </StackPanel>
    </arcm:Page>
</UserControl>
```

## When to use

`ListGroup` and `ListItem` lay out a screen of rows: settings, menus and account screens, where each row is a title the person can tap.

- **Settings**: group related rows under a short `Header`, with a `Footer` that explains them.
- **A menu of destinations**: rows with an `Icon` and a chevron that open other screens.
- **A value or a switch at the end of a row**: put it in `Trailing`.

The live demo runs inside a phone frame, a desktop simulation; touch feedback on a real device has not been verified here.

## When not to use

- **Long or endless data**: a virtualized list is the right tool, and this one is not yet built.
- **Cards with images and several actions**: build them as their own layout.
- **A desktop menu**: use the desktop menu controls; rows here have no hover state.

## Usage

Put `ListItem`s in a `ListGroup` and the group in a scrolling `Page`. The item's content is its title. `ListItem` is a button, so give it a `Command` or handle `Click`; a finger on it shades the row.

```xml
<arcm:Page xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
           xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
           xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
           xmlns:arcm="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc.Mobile"
           IsScrollable="True">
    <arcm:ListGroup Header="Account">
        <arcm:ListItem Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.User}" Content="Profile" Subtitle="Ada Lovelace" ShowChevron="True" />
        <arcm:ListItem Content="Weekly summary" Trailing="Sundays" ShowChevron="True" />
    </arcm:ListGroup>
</arcm:Page>
```

The last row of a group has no separator under it.

### Tokens

`ListItemToken` holds a row's geometry: `RowHeight` (48), `ContentPadding` (16 by 10), `IconExtent` (22), `IconGap` (12), `TrailingMargin`, `ChevronExtent` (16) and `SeparatorInset` (16). `ListGroupToken` holds the group's: `GroupPadding` (16 by 8), `CardBorderThickness` (1), `HeaderMargin` and `FooterMargin`. Colors, radii and type come from the ArcDesign tokens.

## API reference

### MobileListGroup

A card of `ListItem` rows with an optional `Header` above it and `Footer` under it, the way settings screens group their rows. Put it in a scrolling `Page`.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Header` | `string?` | `null` | A short label above the card. |
| `Footer` | `string?` | `null` | A note under the card, for example what the settings in it do. |

Derives from `ItemsControl`: every member of `ItemsControl` works as well.

### MobileListItem

One row of a `ListGroup`: an optional `Icon`, the title (the content), an optional `Subtitle`, optional `Trailing` content and an optional chevron. It is a button: give it a `Command` or handle `Click` and a finger on it shades the row. It has no hover state.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Icon` | `Geometry?` | `null` | The glyph geometry shown before the title, for example a Lucide icon. |
| `Subtitle` | `string?` | `null` | A second, smaller line under the title. |
| `Trailing` | `object?` | `null` | The content at the end of the row: a value, a badge or a control such as a `Switch`. |
| `ShowChevron` | `bool` | `false` | Whether a chevron at the end of the row shows that it opens another screen. |

Derives from `Button`: every member of `Button` works as well.

## Accessibility

A row is a button named by its title and subtitle. Give every row a title, so an icon is never its only name. Each row is at least 48 px tall, above the 44 px touch target.

## Motion

A finger on a row shades its background on the fast curve; with reduced motion the shade appears at once.

## Related

- `MobilePage`: a scrolling page holds the groups.
- `MobileSwitch`: the usual `Trailing` control for a setting.
- `MobileNavbar`: the top bar, with a large title for a root settings screen.

# Mobile pull to refresh

> Pull scrollable content down at its top to refresh it, with rubber-band resistance, a spinner and a spring back.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc.Mobile`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc.Mobile --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/mobile-pull-to-refresh

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             xmlns:arcm="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc.Mobile"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.MobilePullToRefreshBasicDemo">
    <arcm:Page>
        <arcm:Page.Header>
            <arcm:Navbar Title="Messages" />
        </arcm:Page.Header>
        <arcm:PullToRefresh Name="Refresher">
            <ScrollViewer>
                <StackPanel>
                    <TextBlock Name="Status"
                               Margin="16,12"
                               Text="Pull down from the top to refresh."
                               TextWrapping="Wrap"
                               Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
                    <arcm:ListGroup Name="Rows" />
                </StackPanel>
            </ScrollViewer>
        </arcm:PullToRefresh>
    </arcm:Page>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Threading;
using TKCode.Arc.Mobile;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class MobilePullToRefreshBasicDemo : UserControl
{
    private int _refreshes;

    public MobilePullToRefreshBasicDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        for (var i = 1; i <= 6; i++)
        {
            Rows.Items.Add(new ListItem { Content = $"Message {i}", Subtitle = "Tap to open" });
        }
        Refresher.RefreshRequested += OnRefreshRequested;
    }

    private void OnRefreshRequested(object? sender, PullRefreshRequestedEventArgs e)
    {
        // A deferral keeps the spinner going until the (simulated) request ends, then the content springs back.
        var deferral = e.GetDeferral();
        var timer = new DispatcherTimer { Interval = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(1.5) };
        timer.Tick += (_, _) =>
        {
            timer.Stop();
            _refreshes++;
            Rows.Items.Insert(0, new ListItem { Content = $"New message {_refreshes}", Subtitle = "Just now" });
            Status.Text = $"Refreshed {_refreshes} time(s). Pull down again.";
            deferral.Dispose();
        };
        timer.Start();
    }
}
```

## When to use

`PullToRefresh` wraps a scrolling list or page so the person can ask for fresh data with the gesture they already know.

- **Feeds and inboxes**: messages, timelines and order lists that change on the server.
- **Any list with a reload action**: when a button would add clutter.

The live demo ends the refresh with a timer, as a request would, and runs inside a phone frame, a desktop simulation driven by the mouse. Touch behavior on a real device, and how it combines with the platform's own overscroll, has not been verified.

## When not to use

- **Content that is not scrollable and never reloads**: there is nothing to pull.
- **Updates that should arrive on their own**: refresh in the background and show the result.
- **A horizontal list**: the pull is vertical only.

## Usage

Put the scrolling content inside it. Pulling down while the content is at its top drags the content along with resistance, and an arrow that turns over as the pull reaches `PullThreshold` (64 px by default). Releasing past the threshold raises `RefreshRequested`; releasing early springs the content back.

```xml
<arcm:PullToRefresh Command="{Binding ReloadCommand}">
    <ScrollViewer>
        <!-- the list -->
    </ScrollViewer>
</arcm:PullToRefresh>
```

The refresh keeps going, with a spinner, until `IsRefreshing` is false again. Either bind `IsRefreshing` (it is two-way), or take a deferral from the event data and dispose it when the work is done.

```csharp
refresher.RefreshRequested += async (_, e) =>
{
    using var deferral = e.GetDeferral();
    await LoadAsync();
};
```

`IsRefreshing` can also be set from code to show the spinner without a pull. That does not raise `RefreshRequested`.

### Pass-through

A gesture that starts while the inner `ScrollViewer` is scrolled, goes up, or goes mostly sideways is left to the content, so scrolling a long list never fights the pull. Pulling is not available while a refresh is running.

### Tokens

`PullToRefreshToken` holds the geometry: `IndicatorExtent` (56, also where the content rests while refreshing), `ArrowSize` (20), `SpinnerSize` (22) and `SpinnerThickness` (2). Colors come from the ArcDesign tokens.

## API reference

### MobilePullToRefresh

Pull to refresh: wraps scrollable content. Pulling down while the content is at its top drags the content along with rubber-band resistance and shows an arrow that turns over as the pull nears `PullThreshold`. Releasing past it raises `RefreshRequested` and runs `Command`; the content rests below the indicator, which spins, until `IsRefreshing` is false again (set it, or take a deferral from the event data). Releasing early springs the content back. A pull that starts while the inner scroll viewer is scrolled, or that goes sideways or up, is left to the content. The content's position is a `MotionValue`, not a ControlTheme transition: a pull writes it on every move, and a release hands the finger's velocity to the spring, which a new pull can catch mid-flight. Under reduced motion the content does not stretch with the finger; the refresh still runs and the content jumps.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `IsRefreshing` | `bool` | `false` | Whether a refresh is in progress. Two-way: a release past the threshold sets it, and setting it false ends the refresh. |
| `PullThreshold` | `double` | `64` | How far the content has to be pulled down, in px, for a release to start a refresh: 64. |
| `Command` | `ICommand?` | `null` | The command a refresh runs, with `CommandParameter`. |
| `CommandParameter` | `object?` | `null` | The parameter passed to `Command`. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `RefreshRequested` | `PullRefreshRequestedEventArgs` | Raised when a release past the threshold starts a refresh. Take a deferral if the work is asynchronous. |

Derives from `ContentControl`: every member of `ContentControl` works as well.

## Accessibility

The refresh is a gesture, so give the person another way to reload (a menu item or a button) where it matters. `RefreshRequested` and `Command` run when the pull is released, not while it is held.

## Motion

The content follows the finger with a rubber-band curve: it keeps up at first and resists more the further it goes. On release, the finger's speed is handed to a spring, so the content settles smoothly on the indicator or back at the top. A new pull catches the content in flight. The arrow turns over as the pull reaches the threshold, and a spinner replaces it while refreshing. Under reduced motion the content does not stretch with the finger; the refresh still works, and the content jumps.

## Related

- `MobileListGroup`: the usual content.
- `MobilePage`: holds the refreshed screen.
- `MobileNavbar`: the bar above it.

---

# Mobile dialog

> A centered alert or confirmation dialog with a title, a message and up to three actions, over a scrim.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc.Mobile`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc.Mobile --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/mobile-dialog

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             xmlns:arcm="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc.Mobile"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.MobileDialogBasicDemo">
    <arcm:Page>
        <arcm:Page.Header>
            <arcm:Navbar Title="Photos" />
        </arcm:Page.Header>
        <StackPanel Margin="24" Spacing="12" VerticalAlignment="Center">
            <arcm:Button Content="Delete photo" HorizontalAlignment="Stretch" Click="OnDelete" />
            <arcm:Button Content="Share options" Variant="Tinted" HorizontalAlignment="Stretch" Click="OnShare" />
            <TextBlock Text="Two actions share a row; three stack. The scrim does not close the first dialog: choose an action."
                       TextWrapping="Wrap"
                       FontSize="13"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
        </StackPanel>
        <arcm:Page.Overlay>
            <Grid>
                <arcm:Dialog Name="DeleteDialog"
                             Title="Delete this photo?"
                             Message="It will be removed from all your devices. This cannot be undone.">
                    <arcm:Button Content="Cancel" Variant="Tinted" />
                    <arcm:Button Content="Delete" arcm:Dialog.IsDestructive="True" />
                </arcm:Dialog>
                <arcm:Dialog Name="ShareDialog"
                             Title="Share photo"
                             Message="Choose how to send it."
                             IsDismissible="True">
                    <arcm:Button Content="Send a link" />
                    <arcm:Button Content="Send a copy" Variant="Tinted" />
                    <arcm:Button Content="Cancel" Variant="Plain" />
                </arcm:Dialog>
            </Grid>
        </arcm:Page.Overlay>
    </arcm:Page>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class MobileDialogBasicDemo : UserControl
{
    public MobileDialogBasicDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
    }

    private void OnDelete(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) => DeleteDialog.IsOpen = true;

    private void OnShare(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) => ShareDialog.IsOpen = true;
}
```

## When to use

`Dialog` stops the person for one decision that cannot wait: confirm a deletion, accept or refuse a permission, pick one of a few ways to continue.

- **A confirmation** before something that cannot be undone, with the destructive action marked in the Danger color.
- **An alert** that must be read before anything else happens.
- **A short choice** of two or three actions with no extra content.

The live demo runs inside a phone frame, a desktop simulation; touch feedback on a real device has not been verified here.

## When not to use

- **A list of choices or a form**: use `Sheet`, which rises from the bottom where a thumb reaches it.
- **A message that needs no answer**: use `Toast`.
- **Anything the person may want to undo afterwards**: do the thing and offer undo in a toast instead of asking first.

## Usage

Put the dialog in the page's `Overlay` slot and open it with `IsOpen`. The action buttons are the dialog's items; use `Button`s.

```xml
<arcm:Page xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
           xmlns:arcm="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc.Mobile">
    <arcm:Page.Overlay>
        <arcm:Dialog Title="Delete this photo?"
                     Message="This cannot be undone."
                     IsOpen="{Binding ConfirmDelete}">
            <arcm:Button Content="Cancel" Variant="Tinted" />
            <arcm:Button Content="Delete" arcm:Dialog.IsDestructive="True" />
        </arcm:Dialog>
    </arcm:Page.Overlay>
</arcm:Page>
```

`IsOpen` binds two ways. Pressing an action button runs its own `Click` handler or `Command` and then closes the dialog; set `CloseOnAction="False"` to close it yourself, for example after a request finishes.

Two actions share a row when each fits its half of the panel; three actions, or labels too wide for the row, stack at the full width. The panel is at most 320 wide, with 24 kept free at each edge.

By default only an action closes the dialog. Set `IsDismissible="True"` to let a tap on the scrim and Escape close it as well, which suits a dialog with a harmless way out.

`Dialog.IsDestructive="True"` on a button draws it with the Danger color: a filled button becomes a Danger pill, a tinted one Danger text on a soft pill, a plain one Danger text.

### Several overlays on one page

`Page.Overlay` holds one element. To use a dialog together with a sheet or a toast host, put them in a `Grid` in that slot, the toast last so it shows above the others, as the demo does with two dialogs.

```xml
<arcm:Page xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
           xmlns:arcm="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc.Mobile">
    <arcm:Page.Overlay>
        <Grid>
            <arcm:Sheet Title="Share" />
            <arcm:Dialog Title="Delete?" />
            <arcm:Toast />
        </Grid>
    </arcm:Page.Overlay>
</arcm:Page>
```

Each overlay is transparent to touches while it is closed.

### Tokens

`DialogToken` holds `ScrimColor` (the scrim at full opacity, different in light and dark), `PanelMaxWidth` (320), `PanelMargin` (24) and `PanelPadding`. Colors, radii and type come from the ArcDesign tokens.

## API reference

### MobileDialog

A centered alert or confirmation dialog: a `Title`, a `Message` and up to three actions (the items, usually mobile `Button`s) over a scrim. Put it in `Overlay` and open it with `IsOpen`. Two actions share a row when each fits its half; three, or narrow widths, stack them at the full width. Pressing an action button closes the dialog (see `CloseOnAction`) after the button's own click handler or command has run. Tapping the scrim and Escape close it only when `IsDismissible` is on. Set Dialog.IsDestructive on an action button for a danger-colored action. Closed, it does not catch touches. Several overlays (a dialog, a sheet, a toast host) share the one `Overlay` slot: put them together in a `Grid`. The dialog's presence is one `MotionValue` (0 gone, 1 shown) that drives the scrim's opacity and the panel's opacity and scale, so a dialog closed while it is still appearing reverses from where it is. It is not a ControlTheme transition because the exit must finish before the dialog stops catching touches.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `IsOpen` | `bool` | `false` | Whether the dialog is open. |
| `Title` | `string?` | `null` | The title, shown in bold above the message. |
| `Message` | `string?` | `null` | The message under the title. |
| `IsDismissible` | `bool` | `false` | Whether tapping the scrim or pressing Escape closes the dialog: false, so the person has to choose an action. |
| `CloseOnAction` | `bool` | `true` | Whether pressing an action button closes the dialog: true. |
| `IsDestructive` | `bool` | `false` | *Attached.* Attached to an action `Button`: whether it is a destructive action, drawn with the Danger color (filled: a Danger pill, tinted: Danger text on a soft pill, plain: Danger text). |

Derives from `ItemsControl`: every member of `ItemsControl` works as well.

## Accessibility

Escape closes a dismissible dialog. Opening moves the focus to the dialog. Give it a `Title` that states the decision as a question and name the actions with verbs ("Delete", "Cancel"), not "Yes" and "No". The buttons are at least 44 by 44. A dialog that cannot be dismissed always has a way out: include a cancel action.

## Motion

The scrim fades in while the panel scales up from 0.94 and fades in on a snappy spring, one value driving both. Closing is faster, 0.16 s on an exit curve with no overshoot, and a dialog closed while it is still appearing reverses from where it is. It is driven from code because the dialog must keep catching touches until its exit has landed, which a theme transition cannot signal. With reduced motion the panel only fades, without scaling, in 0.12 s; with motion off it appears and disappears at once.

## Related

- `MobilePage`: the `Overlay` slot holds the dialog.
- `MobileButton`: the actions, and the usual way to open it.
- `MobileSheet`: for choices and forms.
- `MobileToast`: for messages that need no answer.

---

# Mobile toast

> A transient message that slides up near the bottom, leaves by itself and can be swiped away.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc.Mobile`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc.Mobile --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/mobile-toast

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             xmlns:arcm="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc.Mobile"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.MobileToastBasicDemo">
    <arcm:Page>
        <arcm:Page.Header>
            <arcm:Navbar Title="Inbox" />
        </arcm:Page.Header>
        <StackPanel Margin="24" Spacing="12" VerticalAlignment="Center">
            <arcm:Button Content="Archive message" HorizontalAlignment="Stretch" Click="OnArchive" />
            <arcm:Button Content="Show with an icon" Variant="Tinted" HorizontalAlignment="Stretch" Click="OnIcon" />
            <Grid ColumnDefinitions="*,Auto">
                <TextBlock Text="One at a time" VerticalAlignment="Center" />
                <arcm:Switch Name="ReplaceSwitch" Grid.Column="1" />
            </Grid>
            <TextBlock Text="Hold a toast to pause its countdown; swipe it sideways to send it away."
                       TextWrapping="Wrap"
                       FontSize="13"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
        </StackPanel>
        <arcm:Page.Footer>
            <arcm:Tabbar SelectedIndex="0">
                <arcm:TabbarItem Content="Inbox" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Mail}" />
                <arcm:TabbarItem Content="Alerts" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Bell}" />
            </arcm:Tabbar>
        </arcm:Page.Footer>
        <arcm:Page.Overlay>
            <arcm:Toast Name="Toasts" />
        </arcm:Page.Overlay>
    </arcm:Page>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;
using TKCode.Arc.Mobile;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class MobileToastBasicDemo : UserControl
{
    private int _count;

    public MobileToastBasicDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
    }

    private void OnArchive(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        Toasts.Policy = ReplaceSwitch.IsChecked == true ? ToastPolicy.Replace : ToastPolicy.Stack;
        _count++;
        Toasts.Show($"Message {_count} archived");
    }

    private void OnIcon(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        Toasts.Policy = ReplaceSwitch.IsChecked == true ? ToastPolicy.Replace : ToastPolicy.Stack;
        Toasts.Show("Reminder set for tomorrow", icon: ArcIcons.Bell);
    }
}
```

## When to use

`Toast` tells the person that something happened without asking for anything: a message was archived, a link was copied, a reminder was set.

- **Confirmation of a finished action** that needs no answer.
- **A light error or status** that the person can ignore.

The live demo runs inside a phone frame, a desktop simulation; touch feedback and the swipe on a real device have not been verified here.

## When not to use

- **A decision**: use `Dialog`.
- **A message that must not be missed** or that the person has to act on: a toast leaves by itself after a few seconds.
- **Long text**: a toast is one or two lines.

## Usage

Put one `Toast` in the page's `Overlay` slot and call `Show` whenever there is something to say.

```xml
<arcm:Page xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
           xmlns:arcm="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc.Mobile">
    <arcm:Page.Overlay>
        <arcm:Toast Name="Toasts" Policy="Stack" MaxVisible="3" />
    </arcm:Page.Overlay>
</arcm:Page>
```

```csharp
Toasts.Show("Message archived");
Toasts.Show("Reminder set", TimeSpan.FromSeconds(5), ArcIcons.Bell);
Toasts.Show("Offline", TimeSpan.Zero); // stays until swiped away or DismissAll()
```

A toast stays for `DefaultDuration` (3 s) unless `Show` is given a duration. A finger on a toast holds its countdown and releasing it carries on from where it stopped; a swipe to either side past 72 px, or a quick flick, sends it away.

`Policy` decides what happens when a toast arrives while others show. `Stack` keeps the newest `MaxVisible` toasts, newest at the bottom, and sends the oldest away. `Replace` shows one at a time: the new toast replaces the one showing.

The toasts sit `BottomOffset` (16) above the page's footer and bottom safe area: the toast finds its `Page` and adds the footer's height and `SafeArea.Bottom` itself, so it clears a `Tabbar`. The rest of the overlay does not catch touches, so the page stays usable while a toast shows.

### Several overlays on one page

`Page.Overlay` holds one element. To use a toast with a sheet or a dialog, put them in a `Grid` in that slot with the toast last, so it shows above the others.

```xml
<arcm:Page xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
           xmlns:arcm="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc.Mobile">
    <arcm:Page.Overlay>
        <Grid>
            <arcm:Sheet Title="Share" />
            <arcm:Dialog Title="Delete?" />
            <arcm:Toast Name="Toasts" />
        </Grid>
    </arcm:Page.Overlay>
</arcm:Page>
```

### Tokens

`ToastToken` holds `BodyMinHeight` (44), `BodyMaxWidth` (360), `BodyPadding`, `StackGap` (8), `SideInset` (16) and `GlyphSize` (18). The toast is an inverted pill: the Foreground color as its fill and the Background color as its text.

## API reference

### MobileToast

Transient messages near the bottom of the page. Put one `Toast` in `Overlay` and call `Show`: the message slides up and fades in above the page's footer and bottom safe area, stays for `DefaultDuration` and leaves by itself. A finger on a toast holds its countdown; a swipe to either side sends it away. `ToastPolicy` chooses between a short stack and one at a time. The host does not catch touches except on the toasts themselves, so the page under it stays usable. Several overlays (a toast, a dialog, a sheet) share the one `Overlay` slot: put them together in a `Grid` with the toast last, so it shows above the others. Each toast's presence and swipe offset are `MotionValue`s rather than ControlTheme transitions: a swipe writes the offset on every move and a release hands the finger's velocity to the spring. The countdown is a `MotionTimeline`, so it can be paused and still ends on time. Under reduced motion a toast only fades, and with motion off it appears and disappears at once.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Policy` | `ToastPolicy` | `Stack` | How toasts that are showing are treated when a new one arrives: `Stack`. |
| `MaxVisible` | `int` | `3` | The most toasts shown at once under `Stack`: 3. |
| `DefaultDuration` | `TimeSpan` | `00:00:03` | How long a toast stays when `Show` is not given a duration: 3 seconds. `Zero` keeps it until dismissed. |
| `BottomOffset` | `double` | `16` | Space between the toasts and whatever is below them: the page's footer and bottom safe area plus this value: 16. |

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

## Accessibility

The message is announced politely, without taking the focus. Because a toast leaves by itself, never put the only copy of important information in one, and keep the text short. The swipe is a shortcut: a toast also leaves on its own. The toast is at least 44 high so a finger can hold it.

## Motion

A toast rises 16 px and fades in on a snappy spring, and leaves faster, in 0.16 s with no overshoot, so the next toast never waits for the last one. Presence and the swipe offset are code-driven motion values, because a swipe writes the offset on every move and a release hands the finger's velocity to a spring that brings an unfinished swipe back. The countdown is a pausable timeline, so it ends on time even while no frames are drawn. With reduced motion a toast only fades, in 0.12 s, and a swipe decides on release instead of following the finger; with motion off it appears and disappears at once.

## Related

- `MobilePage`: the `Overlay` slot holds the toast, and its footer and safe area decide where the toast sits.
- `MobileDialog`: for a decision.
- `MobileSheet`: for choices and forms.
- `MobileTabbar`: the toast rises above it.

---

# Mobile sheet

> A bottom sheet that rises over a page with a scrim and can rest at several heights, closed by tapping the scrim, pulling the handle down or flicking it.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc.Mobile`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc.Mobile --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/mobile-sheet

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             xmlns:arcm="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc.Mobile"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.MobileSheetBasicDemo">
    <arcm:Page>
        <arcm:Page.Header>
            <arcm:Navbar Title="Photos" />
        </arcm:Page.Header>
        <StackPanel Margin="24" Spacing="12" VerticalAlignment="Center">
            <arcm:Button Content="Share" HorizontalAlignment="Stretch" Click="OnShare" />
            <TextBlock Text="Tap the scrim, press Escape or pull the handle down to close the sheet."
                       TextWrapping="Wrap"
                       FontSize="13"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
        </StackPanel>
        <arcm:Page.Overlay>
            <arcm:Sheet Name="ShareSheet" Title="Share">
                <arcm:ListGroup>
                    <arcm:ListItem Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.User}" Content="Send to a person" ShowChevron="True" />
                    <arcm:ListItem Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Bell}" Content="Copy link" />
                </arcm:ListGroup>
            </arcm:Sheet>
        </arcm:Page.Overlay>
    </arcm:Page>
</UserControl>
```

## When to use

`Sheet` is the mobile answer to a popup: a panel that rises from the bottom edge, holds a short task and goes away.

- **Choices and actions**: share options, a list of actions, a filter.
- **A short form or detail** that should not leave the screen the person is on.
- **Anything a desktop app would put in a dropdown or a menu**: on a phone a sheet is easier to reach and to hit.

The live demo runs inside a phone frame, a desktop simulation; touch feedback and the drag on a real device have not been verified here.

## When not to use

- **A step in a flow with its own back stack**: that is a screen, not a sheet.
- **A short confirmation**: use a dialog.
- **Content taller than the screen**: the sheet stops at 90 percent of the page and scrolls; a long task wants a full screen.

## Usage

Put the sheet in the page's `Overlay` slot, which covers the header and the footer, and open it with `IsOpen`. The sheet sizes to its content; the person closes it by tapping the scrim, pulling the handle down, flicking it or pressing Escape.

```xml
<arcm:Page xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
           xmlns:arcm="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc.Mobile">
    <arcm:Page.Overlay>
        <arcm:Sheet Title="Share" IsOpen="{Binding ShowShare}">
            <arcm:ListGroup>
                <arcm:ListItem Content="Send to a person" ShowChevron="True" />
                <arcm:ListItem Content="Copy link" />
            </arcm:ListGroup>
        </arcm:Sheet>
    </arcm:Page.Overlay>
</arcm:Page>
```

`IsOpen` binds two ways, so a gesture that closes the sheet writes `false` back. Set `IsDismissible="False"` for a sheet that only a button can close; it then resists a downward pull like a rubber band.

A pull follows the finger one to one. On release the sheet looks ahead 0.2 s at the finger's speed: past the middle it closes, and a downward flick faster than 500 px/s closes it from anywhere. Otherwise it springs back to its open position.

### Detents

Set `Detents` (fractions of the sheet's height, parsed from text such as `"0.4, 0.9"`) and the sheet rests at several heights: a peek, then the full view. It opens at `InitialDetentIndex` (0, the lowest). `DetentIndex` says where it rests and `DetentChanged` is raised when it comes to rest on another one. `SnapTo(index)`, `Expand()` and `Collapse()` move an open sheet from code.

```xml
<arcm:Sheet Title="Nearby" Detents="0.4, 0.9" InitialDetentIndex="0">
    ...
</arcm:Sheet>
```

```csharp
nearby.DetentChanged += (_, e) => Log($"{e.Index}: {e.Fraction}");
```

A pull follows the finger one to one and stretches like a rubber band past the tallest detent. On release the sheet looks 0.2 s ahead at the finger's speed and rests on the nearest detent, or closes when that is nearest to the bottom; a flick faster than 500 px/s always moves at least one detent. A single value is a fixed height. The content scrolls only at the tallest detent: below it a finger or the wheel raises the sheet instead, and at the top of the content a pull down moves the sheet again. Without `Detents` the sheet keeps its single content-sized height.

### Bottom safe area

The sheet does not read the platform. Give it the space under the content with `SafeAreaBottom` (a number in px), for example bound to the page's safe area:

```xml
<arcm:Page x:Name="Screen">
    <arcm:Page.Overlay>
        <arcm:Sheet SafeAreaBottom="{Binding SafeArea.Bottom, ElementName=Screen}" Title="Share">
            ...
        </arcm:Sheet>
    </arcm:Page.Overlay>
</arcm:Page>
```

### Tokens

`SheetToken` holds `ScrimColor` (the scrim at full opacity, different in light and dark), `PanelRadius` (16 on the top corners), `GrabberWidth` (36), `GrabberHeight` (5) and `HandlePadding`. Colors, radii and type come from the ArcDesign tokens.

## API reference

### MobileSheet

A bottom sheet: a panel that rises over a `Page` with a scrim behind it. The person closes it by tapping the scrim, pulling the handle down or flicking it, or with Escape. Put it in `Overlay` and open it with `IsOpen`; it sizes to its content, up to `MaxHeightFraction` of the page, and the content scrolls beyond that. Closed, it does not catch touches. With `Detents` the sheet rests at several heights instead (a peek and a full view): a pull follows the finger, stretches like a rubber band past the tallest detent, and on release looks 0.2 s ahead to pick the nearest detent or close; a flick always moves at least one detent. The content scrolls only at the tallest detent, and a pull down from its top moves the sheet. The scrim follows the position. The panel's position is a `MotionValue`, not a ControlTheme transition: a drag writes it on every move, a release hands the finger's velocity to the spring, and the scrim is computed from the position each frame. Under reduced motion the panel jumps instead of gliding.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `IsOpen` | `bool` | `false` | Whether the sheet is open. |
| `Title` | `string?` | `null` | The title shown in the handle area, under the grabber. |
| `IsDismissible` | `bool` | `true` | Whether the person can close the sheet by tapping the scrim, pulling the panel down or pressing Escape. |
| `MaxHeightFraction` | `double` | `0.9` | The tallest the panel gets, as a fraction of the sheet's height: 0.9. |
| `Detents` | `SheetDetents?` | `null` | The resting heights as fractions of the sheet's height, for example "0.4, 0.9". Null or empty: the panel sizes to its content. One value is a fixed height. |
| `InitialDetentIndex` | `int` | `0` | Index into the sorted detents the sheet opens at (default 0, the lowest). |
| `DetentIndex` | `int` | – | *Read-only.* The detent the sheet rests on (index into the sorted detents). |
| `SafeAreaBottom` | `double` | `0` | The height of the bottom safe area (the home indicator) in px, kept free under the content. The sheet does not read the platform: bind it to the page, for example `SafeAreaBottom="{Binding SafeArea.Bottom, ElementName=Page}"`. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `DetentChanged` | `SheetDetentChangedEventArgs` | The sheet came to rest on another detent. |

Derives from `ContentControl`: every member of `ContentControl` works as well.

## Accessibility

Escape closes a dismissible sheet. Give the sheet a `Title`: it is the first text in the handle area. Opening moves the focus to the panel. Tapping the scrim is a shortcut, not the only way: keep a visible way to close inside the sheet when it holds a form. The handle area drags with any pointer, and the content drags the sheet by touch only, so a mouse wheel or a scroll bar never moves it. With detents, `DetentIndex` and `DetentChanged` tell the app which height the sheet rests at.

## Motion

The panel's position is a code-driven motion value: a drag writes it on every move, and on release the finger's speed goes into a spring (0.4 s smooth to open, 0.3 s to close), which a transition declared in the theme cannot do. The scrim's opacity follows the panel's position each frame: full at the tallest detent, a little lighter at the lowest of several, clear when closed. Moving between detents is one spring from wherever the panel is, so a new tap or drag interrupts it without a seam. With reduced motion the panel jumps to the detent instead of gliding.

## Related

- `MobilePage`: the `Overlay` slot holds the sheet.
- `MobileListGroup`: the usual content of an action sheet.
- `MobileButton`: the usual way to open it.
- `MobileActionSheet`: a ready-made list of actions with a Cancel row.

# Mobile action sheet

> A bottom list of actions with an optional destructive row and a separate Cancel row, closed by choosing a row, tapping the scrim or pulling it down.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc.Mobile`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc.Mobile --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/mobile-action-sheet

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             xmlns:arcm="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc.Mobile"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.MobileActionSheetBasicDemo">
    <arcm:Page>
        <arcm:Page.Header>
            <arcm:Navbar Title="Photos" />
        </arcm:Page.Header>
        <StackPanel Margin="24" Spacing="12" VerticalAlignment="Center">
            <arcm:Button Content="Photo options" HorizontalAlignment="Stretch" Click="OnShow" />
            <TextBlock Name="Result"
                       Text="Nothing chosen yet"
                       HorizontalAlignment="Center"
                       FontSize="13"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
        </StackPanel>
        <arcm:Page.Overlay>
            <arcm:ActionSheet Name="Options"
                              Title="Photo"
                              Message="IMG_2041.jpg"
                              ActionInvoked="OnAction">
                <arcm:ActionSheetItem Content="Share" />
                <arcm:ActionSheetItem Content="Add to album" />
                <arcm:ActionSheetItem Content="Delete photo" IsDestructive="True" />
            </arcm:ActionSheet>
        </arcm:Page.Overlay>
    </arcm:Page>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class MobileActionSheetBasicDemo : UserControl
{
    public MobileActionSheetBasicDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
    }

    private void OnShow(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) => Options.IsOpen = true;

    private void OnAction(object? sender, Mobile.ActionSheetActionEventArgs e)
        => Result.Text = $"Chose: {e.Action.Content}";
}
```

## When to use

`ActionSheet` is the mobile answer to a menu: a short list of actions on one subject that rises from the bottom edge.

- **Actions on an item**: share, add to an album, delete.
- **A choice that needs a way out**: the Cancel row is always under the list, apart from it, in easy reach of the thumb.
- **A destructive action** that should be easy to find but hard to hit by accident: mark the row `IsDestructive`.

The live demo runs inside a phone frame, a desktop simulation; touch feedback and the drag on a real device have not been verified here.

## When not to use

- **More than about six actions**: use a `Sheet` with a `ListGroup`, which can scroll and group.
- **A form or a task with several steps**: use a `Sheet`.
- **A confirmation of one action**: use a dialog.

## Usage

Put the action sheet in the page's `Overlay` slot and open it with `IsOpen`. Its content is the list of `ActionSheetItem` rows. Give each row a `Command`, or handle `ActionInvoked` once for the whole sheet; choosing a row closes the sheet.

```xml
<arcm:Page xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
           xmlns:arcm="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc.Mobile">
    <arcm:Page.Overlay>
        <arcm:ActionSheet Title="Photo" Message="IMG_2041.jpg" IsOpen="{Binding ShowOptions}">
            <arcm:ActionSheetItem Content="Share" Command="{Binding ShareCommand}" />
            <arcm:ActionSheetItem Content="Add to album" />
            <arcm:ActionSheetItem Content="Delete photo" IsDestructive="True" Command="{Binding DeleteCommand}" />
        </arcm:ActionSheet>
    </arcm:Page.Overlay>
</arcm:Page>
```

```csharp
void OnAction(object? sender, ActionSheetActionEventArgs e) => Log((string)e.Action.Content!);
```

`Title` and `Message` are optional and sit above the first row. `CancelText` is the label of the Cancel row (`"Cancel"`); set it to null to hide the row. Cancel closes the sheet without raising `ActionInvoked`. An action sheet is a `Sheet`: it closes on a scrim tap, a pull down or Escape (set `IsDismissible="False"` to stop that), and `SafeAreaBottom` keeps the Cancel row clear of the home indicator (see `MobileSheet`).

### Tokens

`ActionSheetToken` holds `PanelPadding` (the space around the two cards), `CancelMargin` (the gap above the Cancel card) and `HeaderPadding`; `ActionSheetItemToken` holds `RowHeight` (56) and `ContentPadding`. Colors, radii and type come from the ArcDesign tokens: actions use the accent color, destructive ones the danger color.

## API reference

### MobileActionSheet

A bottom list of actions: an optional `Title` and `Message`, a card of `ActionSheetItem` rows and, set apart under it, a Cancel row. Choosing a row raises `ActionInvoked` (and runs the row's own `Command`) and closes the sheet; so does Cancel. It is a `Sheet`, so it opens with `IsOpen` in `Overlay`, closes on a scrim tap, a pull down or Escape, and moves by the same physics: its position is a motion value written on every drag move, not a ControlTheme transition, and it jumps instead of gliding under reduced motion. Rows shade while pressed.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Message` | `string?` | `null` | A second, smaller line under the title. |
| `CancelText` | `string?` | `"Cancel"` | The label of the Cancel row: "Cancel". Null or empty hides the row. |
| `HasHeader` | `bool` | – | *Read-only.* Whether there is a title or a message, so the header shows. |
| `IsOpen` | `bool` | `false` | Whether the sheet is open. |
| `Title` | `string?` | `null` | The title shown in the handle area, under the grabber. |
| `IsDismissible` | `bool` | `true` | Whether the person can close the sheet by tapping the scrim, pulling the panel down or pressing Escape. |
| `MaxHeightFraction` | `double` | `0.9` | The tallest the panel gets, as a fraction of the sheet's height: 0.9. |
| `Detents` | `SheetDetents?` | `null` | The resting heights as fractions of the sheet's height, for example "0.4, 0.9". Null or empty: the panel sizes to its content. One value is a fixed height. |
| `InitialDetentIndex` | `int` | `0` | Index into the sorted detents the sheet opens at (default 0, the lowest). |
| `DetentIndex` | `int` | – | *Read-only.* The detent the sheet rests on (index into the sorted detents). |
| `SafeAreaBottom` | `double` | `0` | The height of the bottom safe area (the home indicator) in px, kept free under the content. The sheet does not read the platform: bind it to the page, for example `SafeAreaBottom="{Binding SafeArea.Bottom, ElementName=Page}"`. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ActionInvoked` | `ActionSheetActionEventArgs` | The person chose an action; the sheet is closing. |
| `DetentChanged` | `SheetDetentChangedEventArgs` | The sheet came to rest on another detent. |

Derives from `ContentControl`: every member of `ContentControl` works as well.

## Accessibility

Rows are buttons, at least 56 px high, so they are easy to hit and reachable with Tab and Enter or Space. Escape closes a dismissible action sheet and opening moves the focus to the panel. A destructive row is colored but also named by its label, so do not rely on color alone: say "Delete photo", not "Delete". Tapping the scrim is a shortcut; the Cancel row is the visible way out.

## Motion

The panel rises and leaves by the same code-driven motion value as `MobileSheet`: a drag writes the position on every move, a release hands the finger's speed to a spring (0.4 s smooth to open, 0.3 s to close), and the scrim follows the position each frame; a transition declared in the theme cannot follow a finger. Rows are rows, not buttons on a surface, so they do not scale: a finger on one shades it with a short fade of the background. With reduced motion the panel jumps and the shade changes at once.

## Related

- `MobileSheet`: the panel it is built on, for content that is not a list of actions.
- `MobilePage`: the `Overlay` slot holds the action sheet.
- `MobileButton`: the usual way to open it.

# Mobile button

> A touch-first button with a press state instead of a hover state and a 44 px minimum touch target.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc.Mobile`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc.Mobile --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/mobile-button

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             xmlns:arcm="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc.Mobile"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.MobileButtonBasicDemo">
    <StackPanel Margin="24" Spacing="12" VerticalAlignment="Center">
        <arcm:Button Content="Continue" HorizontalAlignment="Stretch" />
        <arcm:Button Variant="Tinted" Content="Save draft" HorizontalAlignment="Stretch" />
        <arcm:Button Variant="Plain" Content="Skip for now" HorizontalAlignment="Center" />
        <arcm:Button Content="Not available" IsEnabled="False" HorizontalAlignment="Center" />
        <TextBlock Text="Press and hold a button: it scales down and dims while a finger is on it."
                   TextWrapping="Wrap"
                   FontSize="13"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

## When to use

`Button` of `TKCode.Arc.Mobile` is the button for touch screens. It is filled, at least 44 by 44, and shows a press state: while a finger is on it the button scales down to 0.97 and dims to 0.85. There is no hover state, because a finger does not hover.

- **The main action of a screen**: "Continue" or "Save", full width at the bottom of the content.
- **An action in a navbar slot**: "Edit" or "Done".
- **A form's submit button**.

The live demo runs inside a phone frame, a desktop simulation. With a mouse, press and hold the button to see the press state. How it feels under a finger on Android and iOS has not been verified.

## When not to use

- **A desktop interface**: use `Button` from `TKCode.Arc`, which has variants, sizes and hover states.
- **A choice that stays selected**: use `MobileSwitch` for a setting, or a list for several options.

## Usage

The mobile `Button` is in the `https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc.Mobile` XAML namespace (prefix `arcm`) and in the .NET namespace `TKCode.Arc.Mobile`, so it does not clash with the desktop `Button`; this page's API table calls it `MobileButton` for the same reason. It derives from Avalonia's `Button`, so `Content`, `Command` and `Click` work as usual.

```xml
<StackPanel xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
            xmlns:arcm="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc.Mobile"
            Spacing="12">
    <arcm:Button Content="Continue" HorizontalAlignment="Stretch" />
    <arcm:Button Content="Not available" IsEnabled="False" />
</StackPanel>
```

A disabled button is dimmed to 0.5.

### Variants

`Variant` sets how prominent the button is: `Filled` (default, a solid pill for the main action), `Tinted` (a soft accent pill for a secondary action) and `Plain` (accent text with no background, for bar actions). Use one `Filled` button per screen.

```xml
<arcm:Button Variant="Tinted" Content="More" />
<arcm:Button Variant="Plain" Content="Done" />
```

### Tokens

`ButtonToken` holds the geometry: `TouchTarget` (44), `ContentPadding` (16 by 10), `PressedScale` (0.97), `PressedOpacity` (0.85) and `DisabledOpacity` (0.5). Colors, radii and type come from the ArcDesign tokens, so the button follows light and dark, the accent and the Pixel style.

## API reference

### MobileButton

Mobile button: a touch-first button with a press state (it scales down and dims while a finger is on it) and no hover state. It is at least 44 by 44 so it is easy to hit. `Variant` picks how prominent it is.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Variant` | `ButtonVariant` | `Filled` | How prominent the button is: filled, tinted or plain text. |

Derives from `Button`: every member of `Button` works as well.

## Accessibility

It is a normal Avalonia button: it can be focused and invoked from the keyboard and exposes its content as its name. The 44 px minimum keeps the target easy to hit.

## Motion

The press scale and dim are declared in the control theme and switch at once with reduced motion.

## Related

- `MobileSwitch`: a toggle for settings.
- `MobileNavbar`: buttons go in its slots.
- `MobilePage`: the screen a button sits on.

```xml
        <Grid ColumnDefinitions="*,Auto" MinHeight="52">

            <TextBlock Text="Managed by your team"
                       VerticalAlignment="Center"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
            <arcm:Switch Grid.Column="1" IsChecked="True" IsEnabled="False" />
        </Grid>
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

## When to use

`Switch` of `TKCode.Arc.Mobile` turns one setting on or off, and the change applies at once. It is a 51 by 31 track with a 27 px thumb that glides on a spring, and its hit area is at least 44 by 44. It has no hover state.

- **A settings list**: one row per setting, with the label on the left and the switch at the end.
- **Preferences that apply immediately**: notifications, sync, dark appearance.

The live demo runs inside a phone frame, a desktop simulation. Touch behavior on real Android and iOS devices has not been verified here.

## When not to use

- **A desktop settings page**: use `Switch` from `TKCode.Arc`.
- **A choice confirmed with a button**: use a checkbox or a form.
- **An action**: use `MobileButton`; a switch names a state.

## Usage

The switch derives from Avalonia's `ToggleButton`, so `IsChecked`, `IsCheckedChanged` and `Content` work as usual. It lives in the `https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc.Mobile` XAML namespace (prefix `arcm`); the API table calls it `MobileSwitch` because the desktop package has a `Switch` too. Put the label in your own row and the switch at its end.

```xml
<Grid xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
      xmlns:arcm="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc.Mobile"
      ColumnDefinitions="*,Auto" MinHeight="52">
    <TextBlock Text="Notifications" VerticalAlignment="Center" />
    <arcm:Switch Grid.Column="1" IsChecked="True" />
</Grid>
```

The track is filled with the on color when checked. A disabled switch is dimmed to 0.5 and keeps its state.

### Tokens

`SwitchToken` holds the geometry: `TrackWidth` (51), `TrackHeight` (31), `TrackInset` (2), `ThumbSize` (27), `ThumbOnMargin`, `TouchTarget` (44) and `DisabledOpacity` (0.5). Colors come from the ArcDesign selection-control tokens.

## API reference

### MobileSwitch

Mobile switch: a 51 by 31 toggle for settings that take effect immediately. The thumb glides on a spring, the hit area is at least 44 by 44, and there is no hover state. The track fills with the on color when checked.

Derives from `ToggleButton`: every member of `ToggleButton` works as well.

## Accessibility

It is a toggle button: it can be focused and toggled with the keyboard, and exposes its state. Put the setting's name in a label next to it and keep the row at least 44 px tall.

## Motion

The thumb glides on a spring and the track fades to the on color. A finger stretches the thumb to 1.18 times its width toward where it will go on a snappy spring and releases on the same spring (P24). All of it is declared in the control theme; with reduced motion the thumb jumps, does not stretch, and the colors switch at once.

## Related

- `MobileButton`: for actions.
- `MobilePage`: the screen a settings list sits on.

# Mobile text field

> A 44 px filled text field with an optional icon and a clear button, whose border takes the accent color while focused.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc.Mobile`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc.Mobile --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/mobile-text-field

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             xmlns:arcm="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc.Mobile"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.MobileTextFieldBasicDemo">
    <arcm:Page>
        <arcm:Page.Header>
            <arcm:Navbar Title="New contact" />
        </arcm:Page.Header>
        <StackPanel Margin="16" Spacing="12">
            <arcm:TextField PlaceholderText="Name" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.User}" Text="Ada Lovelace" />
            <arcm:TextField PlaceholderText="Email" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Bell}" />
            <arcm:TextField PlaceholderText="Notes (read only)" Text="Managed by your team" IsReadOnly="True" />
            <arcm:TextField PlaceholderText="Not available" IsEnabled="False" />
            <TextBlock Text="Tap a field and type: the border takes the accent color and a clear button appears."
                       TextWrapping="Wrap"
                       FontSize="13"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
        </StackPanel>
    </arcm:Page>
</UserControl>
```

## When to use

`TextField` is a single-line text input for a mobile form: names, emails, short answers.

- **Forms on a phone**: the field is 44 px high, so it is easy to hit with a thumb.
- **Fields with a meaning**: an `Icon` before the text says what the field is for.
- **Fields that people correct often**: the clear button empties it in one tap.

The live demo runs inside a phone frame, a desktop simulation; the soft keyboard on a real device has not been verified here.

## When not to use

- **Search**: use `Searchbar`, which has the search glyph, a pill shape and a Search key.
- **Long, multi-line text**: a text area is the right control, and this one is single line.
- **A choice from a few values**: use a switch, a segmented control or a sheet with a list.

## Usage

`TextField` derives from Avalonia's `TextBox`, so `Text`, selection, `IsReadOnly` and binding work as they do there. Show a hint with `PlaceholderText`.

```xml
<arcm:TextField xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
                xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
                xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
                xmlns:arcm="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc.Mobile"
                PlaceholderText="Name"
                Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.User}"
                Text="{Binding Name}" />
```

The clear button shows only while the field has focus and text, and not when it is read only or `ShowClearButton` is false. It empties the field and keeps the focus. A field has no hover state: a finger does not hover.

### Tokens

`TextFieldToken` holds the geometry: `FieldHeight` (44), `ContentPadding` (12 at the sides), `BorderWidth` (1), `GlyphExtent` (18), `IconMargin` and `DisabledOpacity` (0.5). Colors, radii and type come from the ArcDesign tokens.

## API reference

### MobileTextField

Mobile text field: a 44px filled field with an optional `Icon` before the text and a clear button that shows while the field has focus and text. The border takes the accent color while focused; there is no hover state. It derives from Avalonia's `TextBox`, so text, selection and binding work as they do there. Show a placeholder with `PlaceholderText`.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Icon` | `Geometry?` | `null` | The glyph geometry shown before the text, for example a Lucide icon. |
| `ShowClearButton` | `bool` | `true` | Whether a clear button shows while the field has focus and text: true. |
| `IsClearVisible` | `bool` | – | *Read-only.* Whether the clear button is showing now. |

Derives from `TextBox`: every member of `TextBox` works as well.

## Accessibility

Give every field a visible name next to it or an icon plus a placeholder, so the hint is not the only label once the person starts typing. The field is at least 44 px high and the clear button is a 44 px touch target.

## Motion

The border changes color on the fast curve when the field gains or loses focus. The clear button pops in from scale 0.6 with a fade (P26 through `PresenceHost`) and leaves faster than it arrived. With reduced motion the border changes at once and the clear button appears and disappears at once.

## Related

- `MobileSearchbar`: a text field made for search.
- `MobilePage`: the screen a form sits in.
- `MobileButton`: the usual way to submit a form.
