# Mobile search bar

> A pill-shaped text field with a search glyph, a clear button and a Search key that raises Submitted.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc.Mobile`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc.Mobile --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/mobile-searchbar

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             xmlns:arcm="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc.Mobile"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.MobileSearchbarBasicDemo">
    <arcm:Page>
        <arcm:Page.Header>
            <arcm:Navbar Title="Search" />
        </arcm:Page.Header>
        <StackPanel Margin="16" Spacing="12">
            <arcm:Searchbar Name="Query" PlaceholderText="Search messages" Submitted="OnSubmitted" />
            <TextBlock Name="Result"
                       Text="Press Enter to search."
                       TextWrapping="Wrap"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
        </StackPanel>
    </arcm:Page>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class MobileSearchbarBasicDemo : UserControl
{
    public MobileSearchbarBasicDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
    }

    private void OnSubmitted(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
        => Result.Text = string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(Query.Text) ? "Type something to search for." : $"Searching for “{Query.Text}”…";
}
```

## When to use

`Searchbar` is the field a person types a query into: at the top of a list, or on a search screen.

- **Filtering or searching a list**: put it at the top of the page, under the navbar.
- **A search screen**: it is the first thing on the page, and it takes focus when the screen opens.

The live demo runs inside a phone frame, a desktop simulation; the soft keyboard's Search key on a real device has not been verified here.

## When not to use

- **Ordinary text input**: use `TextField`.
- **A desktop search box with suggestions**: use the desktop search controls.

## Usage

`Searchbar` is a `TextField`, so `Text`, `PlaceholderText` and binding work as they do there. Handle `Submitted` to run the search: it is raised when the person presses Enter or the soft keyboard's Search key.

```xml
<arcm:Searchbar xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
                xmlns:arcm="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc.Mobile"
                PlaceholderText="Search messages"
                Text="{Binding Query}" />
```

```csharp
searchbar.Submitted += (_, _) => Search(searchbar.Text);
```

The search glyph is the field's `Icon`, set by default; the clear button shows while the field has focus and text. To filter as the person types, bind `Text` and react to its changes instead.

### Tokens

`Searchbar` shares `TextFieldToken` with `TextField`: the same 44 px height, padding and glyph size. Only its radius differs: the pill radius from the ArcDesign tokens.

## API reference

### MobileSearchbar

Mobile search bar: a `TextField` with a search glyph before the text and a pill shape. Enter raises `Submitted`, and the soft keyboard offers a Search key.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Icon` | `Geometry?` | `null` | The glyph geometry shown before the text, for example a Lucide icon. |
| `ShowClearButton` | `bool` | `true` | Whether a clear button shows while the field has focus and text: true. |
| `IsClearVisible` | `bool` | – | *Read-only.* Whether the clear button is showing now. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Submitted` | `RoutedEventArgs` | Raised when the person presses Enter or the keyboard's Search key. |

Derives from `TextBox`: every member of `TextBox` works as well.

## Accessibility

Give the field a placeholder that says what is searched, such as "Search messages". The field is at least 44 px high.

## Motion

The border changes color on the fast curve when the field gains or loses focus. The clear button pops in from scale 0.6 with a fade (P26 through `PresenceHost`) and leaves faster than it arrived. With reduced motion the border changes at once and the clear button appears and disappears at once.

## Related

- `MobileTextField`: the field it is built on.
- `MobileNavbar`: the bar the search bar usually sits under.
- `MobileListGroup`: the usual list of results.

# Mobile checkbox

> A 22 px rounded checkbox in a 44 px row, with a check, an indeterminate dash and no hover state.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc.Mobile`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc.Mobile --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/mobile-checkbox

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             xmlns:arcm="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc.Mobile"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.MobileCheckboxBasicDemo">
    <StackPanel Margin="24" Spacing="4" VerticalAlignment="Center">
        <arcm:Checkbox Content="Remember this device" IsChecked="True" />
        <arcm:Checkbox Content="Send me a weekly summary" />
        <arcm:Checkbox Content="Select all" IsThreeState="True" IsChecked="{x:Null}" />
        <arcm:Checkbox Content="Managed by your team" IsChecked="True" IsEnabled="False" />
        <TextBlock Text="The whole row is the touch target. A finger on it dims it."
                   Margin="0,8,0,0"
                   TextWrapping="Wrap"
                   FontSize="13"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

## When to use

`Checkbox` lets a person pick any number of options, or agree to something, in a form or a list.

- **Several choices at once**: filters, interests, items to include.
- **A single agreement**: "Remember this device", "I accept the terms".
- **Select all**: with `IsThreeState`, a parent row shows a dash when only some of its children are selected.

The live demo runs inside a phone frame, a desktop simulation; touch feedback on a real device has not been verified here.

## When not to use

- **A setting that takes effect at once**: use `Switch`.
- **Exactly one of several options**: use `Segmented` or a list of rows with a check.
- **A command**: use `Button`.

## Usage

`Checkbox` derives from Avalonia's `ToggleButton`, so `IsChecked`, `IsThreeState`, `Click` and binding work as they do there. The label is the content, and the whole row is the touch target.

```xml
<arcm:Checkbox xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
               xmlns:arcm="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc.Mobile"
               Content="Remember this device"
               IsChecked="{Binding Remember}" />
```

Set `IsThreeState` and bind `IsChecked` to a nullable value for the indeterminate state. A finger on the row dims it; there is no hover state.

### Tokens

`CheckboxToken` holds the geometry: `TouchTarget` (44), `BoxSize` (22), `BoxRadius` (6), `BoxBorderWidth` (1.5), `CheckExtent` (16), `LabelMargin`, `PressedOpacity` (0.6) and `DisabledOpacity` (0.5). Colors come from the ArcDesign tokens.

## API reference

### MobileCheckbox

Mobile checkbox: a 22px rounded box with a check, and the label (the content) beside it, in a row at least 44 high so the whole row is the touch target. A finger on the box shrinks it on a spring (the row itself does not move); there is no hover state. The check draws itself in when it appears, and with `IsThreeState` it also has an indeterminate state, shown as a dash that morphs into the check and back. With reduced motion the marks appear at once.

Derives from `ToggleButton`: every member of `ToggleButton` works as well.

## Accessibility

The row is a toggle button named by its label, so always give it content; a box with no label has no name. The row is at least 44 px high, and the box is not the only target.

## Motion

A finger shrinks the box to 0.92 on a snappy spring and releases on the same spring (P1; the row and its label stay still). The check draws itself from start to end (P15, `StrokeDrawGlyph`, 240ms on the enter curve), and the dash morphs into the check and back on a snappy spring (P16, `MorphGlyph`). The box fill and border cross-fade on the fast curve. With reduced motion the marks and colors switch at once and the box does not shrink.

## Related

- `MobileSwitch`: for a setting that takes effect at once.
- `MobileListGroup`: rows that can hold a checkbox in their trailing content.
- `MobileButton`: the usual way to submit a form.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc.Mobile`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc.Mobile --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/mobile-radio

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             xmlns:arcm="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc.Mobile"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.MobileRadioBasicDemo">
    <StackPanel Margin="24" Spacing="4" VerticalAlignment="Center">
        <TextBlock Text="Delivery"
                   FontSize="13"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
        <arcm:Radio GroupName="delivery" Content="Standard, free" IsChecked="True" />
        <arcm:Radio GroupName="delivery" Content="Express, 2 days" />
        <arcm:Radio GroupName="delivery" Content="Pick up in store" />
        <arcm:Radio GroupName="delivery" Content="Not available here" IsEnabled="False" />
        <TextBlock Text="Choosing one clears the others. The dot springs in; the whole row is the touch target."
                   Margin="0,8,0,0"
                   TextWrapping="Wrap"
                   FontSize="13"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

## When to use

`Radio` lets a person pick exactly one option out of a short list, in a form or a settings screen.

- **One of a few options**: delivery speed, a payment method, a sort order.
- **Options that need a label each**: every row has its own text, so the choices read like a list.
- **A choice that is confirmed later**: the radio shows the pick; a button submits it.

The live demo runs inside a phone frame, a desktop simulation; touch feedback on a real device has not been verified here.

## When not to use

- **A short row of views of the same content**: use `Segmented`.
- **Any number of options**: use `Checkbox`.
- **A setting that takes effect at once**: use `Switch`.

## Usage

`Radio` derives from Avalonia's `RadioButton`, so `IsChecked`, `GroupName`, `Click` and binding work as they do there. Radios that share a `GroupName` are mutually exclusive; put the radios of one group in the same panel. The label is the content, and the whole row is the touch target. The design is a `RadioButton` with group names rather than a container with a selected value: a radio can sit in any row layout, and the choice binds with `IsChecked` on each item.

```xml
<StackPanel xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
            xmlns:arcm="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc.Mobile">
    <arcm:Radio GroupName="delivery" Content="Standard, free" IsChecked="True" />
    <arcm:Radio GroupName="delivery" Content="Express, 2 days" />
</StackPanel>
```

With the focus on a radio, the arrow keys move the choice to the previous or next enabled radio of the same group among its siblings, and wrap around. A finger on the row dims it; there is no hover state.

### Tokens

`RadioToken` holds the geometry: `TouchTarget` (44), `CircleSize` (22), `CircleBorderWidth` (1.5), `DotSize` (10), `LabelMargin`, `PressedOpacity` (0.6) and `DisabledOpacity` (0.5). Colors come from the ArcDesign tokens.

## API reference

### MobileRadio

Mobile radio: a 22px circle with an accent dot that springs in when the item is chosen, and the label (the content) beside it, in a row at least 44 high so the whole row is the touch target. Items that share a `GroupName` are mutually exclusive: choosing one clears the others. The arrow keys move the choice to the previous or next enabled item of the same group among the siblings. A finger on it dims it; there is no hover state.

Derives from `RadioButton`: every member of `RadioButton` works as well.

## Accessibility

The row is a radio button named by its label, so always give it content; a radio with no label has no name. The row is at least 44 px high, and the circle is not the only target. The arrow keys move within a group, and the checked state is exposed to assistive technology as it is for any `RadioButton`.

## Motion

The dot springs in from a small scale with a fade and goes out the same way; because it is a spring, a choice that flips half-way keeps its speed. The outline changes color on the fast curve. With reduced motion, the dot and the outline change at once.

## Related

- `MobileCheckbox`: for any number of choices.
- `MobileSegmented`: for a short row of views.
- `MobileListGroup`: rows that can hold a radio in their trailing content.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"

    </StackPanel>

```

## When to use

`IconButton` is a button that shows only an icon: in a bar, on a card, or floating over content.

- **Bar actions**: search, share, more. The default `Plain` variant is an accent icon with no background.
- **A secondary action on a card or row**: `Tinted`.
- **The main action of a view**: `Filled`, or `Fab` when it floats over scrolling content.

The live demo runs inside a phone frame, a desktop simulation; touch feedback on a real device has not been verified here.

## When not to use

- **An action that needs a word to be understood**: use `Button` with text.
- **A choice between options**: use `Segmented`, `Radio` or `Checkbox`.
- **Several equal floating actions**: a floating button is one main action; use a `Sheet` for more.

## Usage

`IconButton` derives from Avalonia's `Button`, so `Click`, `Command` and binding work as they do there. Set `Icon` to a geometry and `Variant` to pick the look. The button is 44 by 44.

```xml
<arcm:IconButton xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"

                 Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Share}"
                 Variant="Filled"
                 AutomationProperties.Name="Share" />
```

### Floating action button

`Variant="Fab"` makes a 56 px accent circle with the floating shadow of the ArcDesign tokens. Put it over the content, for example in the `Page` overlay slot or a `Panel` aligned to the bottom right.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             xmlns:arcm="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc.Mobile"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.MobileIconButtonFabDemo">
    <Panel>
        <TextBlock Text="The floating action button sits over the content, at the bottom right, and springs down when pressed."
                   Margin="24"
                   VerticalAlignment="Center"
                   TextWrapping="Wrap"
                   FontSize="13"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
        <arcm:IconButton Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Plus}"
                         Variant="Fab"
                         AutomationProperties.Name="New message"
                         HorizontalAlignment="Right"
                         VerticalAlignment="Bottom"
                         Margin="24" />
    </Panel>
</UserControl>
```

### Tokens

`IconButtonToken` holds the geometry: `TouchTarget` (44), `FabSize` (56), `IconExtent` (22), `FabIconExtent` (24), `PressedOpacity` (0.85) and `DisabledOpacity` (0.5). Colors and the shadow come from the ArcDesign tokens.

## API reference

### MobileIconButton

Mobile icon button: a 44 by 44 icon-only button with a press state (it scales down while a finger is on it) and no hover state. `Variant` picks plain, tinted, filled or floating (`Fab`). An icon-only button has no visible text, so always set `AutomationProperties.Name`.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Icon` | `Geometry?` | `null` | The glyph geometry shown in the button, for example a Lucide icon. |
| `Variant` | `IconButtonVariant` | `Plain` | How prominent the button is: plain, tinted, filled or a floating action button. |

Derives from `Button`: every member of `Button` works as well.

## Accessibility

An icon has no text, so always set `AutomationProperties.Name` to say what the button does ("Search", "New message"); without it a screen reader announces nothing useful. The button is 44 by 44 at least, and the floating one is 56.

## Motion

Pressing scales the button to 0.97 (the floating one to 0.92) on a snappy spring, with no delay on the way down, and dims it a little; letting go springs back. A press that is released half-way keeps its speed. With reduced motion the button does not scale, it only dims.

## Related

- `MobileButton`: a button with text.
- `MobileNavbar`: where plain icon buttons go in the bar.
- `MobileSheet`: for more actions than one floating button can hold.

# Mobile segmented control

> A short row of segments that share the width, one selected, for switching between views of the same content.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc.Mobile`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc.Mobile --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/components/mobile-segmented

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             xmlns:arcm="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc.Mobile"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.MobileSegmentedBasicDemo">
    <arcm:Page>
        <arcm:Page.Header>
            <arcm:Navbar Title="Activity" />
        </arcm:Page.Header>
        <StackPanel Margin="16" Spacing="12">
            <arcm:Segmented SelectedIndex="1">
                <arcm:SegmentedItem Content="Day" />
                <arcm:SegmentedItem Content="Week" />
                <arcm:SegmentedItem Content="Month" />
            </arcm:Segmented>
            <TextBlock Text="The segments share the width; the selected one is raised."
                       TextWrapping="Wrap"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
        </StackPanel>
    </arcm:Page>
</UserControl>
```

## When to use

`Segmented` switches between a few views of one thing: a time range, a sort order, a list and a map of the same places.

- **Two to four options** with short labels, all visible at once.
- **Views of the same content**: the content below changes, the screen does not.

The live demo runs inside a phone frame, a desktop simulation; touch feedback on a real device has not been verified here.

## When not to use

- **Top-level areas of an app**: use `Tabbar`.
- **More than four options**, or long labels: use a list or a sheet.
- **Several choices at once**: use checkboxes.

## Usage

Put `SegmentedItem`s in the control and set `SelectedIndex`. `Segmented` derives from Avalonia's `ListBox`, so `SelectedItem`, `SelectionChanged` and binding to `ItemsSource` work as they do there.

```xml
<arcm:Segmented xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
                xmlns:arcm="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc.Mobile"
                SelectedIndex="1">
    <arcm:SegmentedItem Content="Day" />
    <arcm:SegmentedItem Content="Week" />
    <arcm:SegmentedItem Content="Month" />
</arcm:Segmented>
```

The segments share the width equally. The selected one is raised on a Surface fill with an outline and uses the foreground color; the others use the secondary text color. A finger on an unselected segment dims it; there is no hover state.

### Tokens

`SegmentedToken` holds the track's geometry: `TrackPadding` (2) and `TrackRadius` (10). `SegmentedItemToken` holds a segment's: `ItemHeight` (36), `ItemPadding`, `ItemRadius` (8) and `PressedOpacity` (0.6). With the padding, the control is 40 high. Colors and type come from the ArcDesign tokens.

## API reference

### MobileSegmented

Mobile segmented control: a short row of `SegmentedItem`s that share the width, one selected, for switching between a few views of the same content. It derives from Avalonia's `ListBox`, so `SelectedIndex`, `SelectionChanged` and binding work as they do there. It has no hover state. The selected block slides between segments on a spring (and jumps with reduced motion) while the label colors cross-fade.

Derives from `ListBox`: every member of `ListBox` works as well.

### MobileSegmentedItem

One segment of a `Segmented`: its label is the content. The selected one is raised on a Surface fill.

Derives from `ListBoxItem`: every member of `ListBoxItem` works as well.

## Accessibility

Segments are selectable list items named by their labels. Keep the labels short and distinct. A segment is 36 px high and wide, as the width is shared, so with four options a narrow phone still gives each a usable target.

## Motion

The selected block (a Surface fill with an outline) slides behind the labels on a spring (P7, `GlidingIndicator`): it fades in place the first time, snaps when the control is resized, and jumps with reduced motion. The label colors cross-fade on the fast curve, and switch at once with reduced motion.

## Related

- `MobileTabbar`: for top-level areas.
- `MobileNavbar`: the segmented control often sits under it.
- `MobilePage`: the screen it lives on.

---

# Metrics dashboard

> A one-screen analytics overview with a range switch, metric tabs that count to their totals, an inspectable area chart that can overlay the previous period, and two ranked lists.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc.Blocks`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc.Blocks --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/blocks/metrics-dashboard

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.MetricsDashboardPreviewDemo">
    <!-- A site's last 30 days: four metrics, two ranked lists. Data: MetricsDashboardDemoData (invented). -->
    <Border BorderThickness="1" CornerRadius="12" ClipToBounds="True" Margin="0,12"
            BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Border}">
        <arc:MetricsDashboard x:Name="Dashboard"
                              Title="Insights"
                              Source="northwind.dev"
                              PrimaryListTitle="Top paths"
                              SecondaryListTitle="Referrers"
                              ListValueHeader="Sessions" />
    </Border>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class MetricsDashboardPreviewDemo : UserControl
{
    public MetricsDashboardPreviewDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Dashboard.EndDate = MetricsDashboardDemoData.EndDate;
        Dashboard.Metrics.AddRange(MetricsDashboardDemoData.SiteMetrics());
        Dashboard.PrimaryItems.AddRange(MetricsDashboardDemoData.TopPaths());
        Dashboard.SecondaryItems.AddRange(MetricsDashboardDemoData.Referrers());
    }
}
```

## When to use

`MetricsDashboard` answers "how are we doing over the last N days?" in one compact surface. The header names what the
numbers are about and offers a 7D / 30D / 90D switch and an Export button. Under it, each metric is a tab with its total
for the range and the change against the period before; the selected tab drives the chart. Two ranked lists close the
block, for the top pages and the top sources or any other pair of breakdowns.

- **Product and marketing overviews.** Sessions, sign-ups, a conversion rate and a churn or bounce rate, with the pages and
  referrers that brought the traffic.
- **Usage summaries for a team or a customer.** Active teams, new projects, seat utilization and failed jobs, with the
  busiest workspaces and the plans they are on.
- **A landing view before a deeper report.** Use `PointInspected`, `SelectedMetricChanged` and `RangeChanged` to open a
  detail page for the day, the metric or the range someone is looking at.

## When not to use

- **Many series on one chart.** The chart draws one metric and, on request, its previous period. Use a line chart for
  several series side by side, or `Small multiples` for many.
- **Live, second-by-second data.** Every point is a day or a week. Use a streaming chart for live operational data.
- **Arbitrary date ranges.** The ranges are fixed lengths ending at `EndDate`. Use a date range picker and your own chart
  when people choose any start and end.
- **More than six metrics.** Four fill the row exactly, and the medium layout shows them two by two. Split a longer set
  across dashboards or use a table.

## Usage

The block derives from Avalonia's `TemplatedControl` and holds no sample data. Each metric is a
`MetricsDashboardMetric` with one value per day in `Daily`, the last value being `EndDate` (today when it is not set).
Give at least twice the longest range, so every range has a previous period to compare with; without one the change
line is hidden. List rows are `MetricsDashboardItem`s with one value per range in `Values`, largest first.

```xml
<arc:MetricsDashboard x:Name="Dashboard"
                      Title="Insights"
                      Source="northwind.dev"
                      PrimaryListTitle="Top paths"
                      SecondaryListTitle="Referrers"
                      ListValueHeader="Sessions" />
```

```csharp
Dashboard.EndDate = new DateOnly(2026, 10, 18);
Dashboard.Metrics.Add(new MetricsDashboardMetric { Label = "Sessions", Daily = sessions });
Dashboard.Metrics.Add(new MetricsDashboardMetric
{
    Label = "Churn risk", Kind = MetricsDashboardMetricKind.Ratio, HigherIsBetter = false, Daily = churn
});
Dashboard.PrimaryItems.Add(new MetricsDashboardItem { Label = "/", Values = [2602, 10840, 29268] });
```

`MetricsSource`, `PrimaryItemsSource` and `SecondaryItemsSource` take collections you own; an
`ObservableCollection` is followed, and changing a metric's or an item's properties updates the block, counting the
numbers to their new values.

### Counts and rates

A `Count` metric adds up: the total of a range or of a week is the sum of its days, and the change is relative ("11.7%").
A `Ratio` metric is a rate in percent units: the change is the difference in points ("0.1 pts"). Give `Numerators` and
`Denominators` (conversions and sessions, seats used and seats paid) and every week and range is the exact ratio of the
sums; without them it is the mean of the daily rates. `HigherIsBetter="False"` turns a fall green, for churn, bounce or
error rates. The arrow always shows the direction, and screen readers hear it in words.

### Ranges and weeks

`Ranges` (7, 30, 90) are the switch's segments, written with `RangeLabelFormat` ("{0}D") and named for screen readers
with `RangeNameFormat` ("Last {0} days"); `SelectedRange` is two-way. Ranges longer than `WeeklyThreshold` (60) are drawn
as weeks counted from the range's first day: 90 days give 13 points, and the last week has the 6 days left over. Its
tooltip says so ("Week of Oct 13 (6 days)"), because a short week is summed as it is and reads lower than the others.

### Narrow containers

The block reads its own width, not the window's. Under 640 the tabs go two by two and the lists stack; under 460 the range
switch spans the header, values drop to 18px, the plot is 168 high and the x axis shows at most four dates. When the
titles and the actions do not fit on one line, the actions move under the titles.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.MetricsDashboardNarrowDemo">
    <!-- In a 420-wide container the block picks its small layout from its own width, whatever the window's size. -->
    <Border Width="420" HorizontalAlignment="Center" BorderThickness="1" CornerRadius="12" ClipToBounds="True" Margin="0,12"
            BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Border}">
        <arc:MetricsDashboard x:Name="Dashboard"
                              Title="Insights"
                              Source="northwind.dev"
                              SelectedRange="7"
                              PrimaryListTitle="Top paths"
                              SecondaryListTitle="Referrers"
                              ListValueHeader="Sessions" />
    </Border>
</UserControl>
```


### Other data, other words

Every text is a property with an English default: `SubtitleFormat` and `SubtitleRangeFormat`, `CompareText`,
`PreviousLegendText`, `PreviousValueFormat` ("{0} previous"), `DateFormat`, `WeekTitleFormat`, `PartialWeekTitleFormat`,
`ExportText`, `ExportedText`, the list titles and `ListValueHeader`, and the screen reader texts `RangeGroupName`,
`MetricGroupName`, `ChartNameFormat`, `ChartHelpText` and `ChangeContextText`. A metric can format its own numbers with
`ValueFormatter` (tab and tooltip), `AxisFormatter` (y axis) and `DeltaFormatter` (the change); `ListValueFormatter` does
the same for the lists. This demo uses 14, 28 and 84 day ranges, an exact seat-utilization ratio and a failed-jobs rate
with two decimals.

```xml

                              ExportedText="Saved"
```

### State and events

`SelectedMetricIndex`, `SelectedRange` and `IsCompareEnabled` are two-way, so the view can be saved and restored or
driven from elsewhere. `RangeChanged`, `SelectedMetricChanged` and `CompareChanged` report every change, and
`PointInspected` reports the day (or week), its value and, with Compare on, the previous period's value whenever the
inspection moves. `InspectPoint(index)` and `ClearInspection()` do from code what the pointer and the arrow keys do;
`ActiveIndex` tells which point is inspected.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.MetricsDashboardEventsDemo">
    <!-- The view state is bindable: the buttons below drive the block, and its events are logged. -->
    <StackPanel Spacing="12" Margin="0,12">
        <Border BorderThickness="1" CornerRadius="12" ClipToBounds="True"
                BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Border}">
            <arc:MetricsDashboard x:Name="Dashboard"
                                  Title="Insights"
                                  Source="northwind.dev"
                                  IsCompareEnabled="True"
                                  PrimaryListTitle="Top paths"
                                  SecondaryListTitle="Referrers"
                                  ListValueHeader="Sessions" />
        </Border>
        <StackPanel Orientation="Horizontal" Spacing="8" HorizontalAlignment="Center">
            <arc:Button x:Name="NextMetric" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Content="Next metric" />
            <arc:Button x:Name="LongestRange" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Content="Longest range" />
            <arc:Button x:Name="LatestPoint" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Content="Inspect latest" />
            <arc:Button x:Name="ClearPoint" Variant="Ghost" Size="Small" Content="Clear" />
        </StackPanel>
        <TextBlock x:Name="Log" HorizontalAlignment="Center" TextAlignment="Center" TextWrapping="Wrap" MaxWidth="560" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class MetricsDashboardEventsDemo : UserControl
{
    public MetricsDashboardEventsDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Dashboard.EndDate = MetricsDashboardDemoData.EndDate;
        Dashboard.Metrics.AddRange(MetricsDashboardDemoData.SiteMetrics());
        Dashboard.PrimaryItems.AddRange(MetricsDashboardDemoData.TopPaths());
        Dashboard.SecondaryItems.AddRange(MetricsDashboardDemoData.Referrers());

        NextMetric.Click += (_, _) => Dashboard.SelectedMetricIndex = (Dashboard.SelectedMetricIndex + 1) % Dashboard.EffectiveMetrics.Count;
        LongestRange.Click += (_, _) => Dashboard.SelectedRange = Dashboard.Ranges.Max();
        LatestPoint.Click += (_, _) => Dashboard.InspectPoint(int.MaxValue);
        ClearPoint.Click += (_, _) => Dashboard.ClearInspection();

        Dashboard.RangeChanged += (_, e) => Log.Text = $"Range: {e.OldRange} → {e.NewRange} days";
        Dashboard.SelectedMetricChanged += (_, e) => Log.Text = $"Metric: {e.Metric?.Label}";
        Dashboard.CompareChanged += (_, e) => Log.Text = e.IsEnabled ? "Comparing with the previous period" : "Comparison off";
        Dashboard.PointInspected += (_, e) =>
            Log.Text = $"{e.Date:MMM d} ({e.Days} day{(e.Days == 1 ? "" : "s")}): {e.Value:N1}" +
                       (e.PreviousValue is { } previous ? $", previous {previous:N1}" : "");
    }
}
```

### Export

The button does not export anything by itself. `ExportCommand` runs with a `MetricsDashboardExportRequest` (the range in
days, its first and last day, the selected metric and whether the previous period is shown); when it cannot execute,
nothing happens. Then `ExportRequested` is raised and the button confirms with a check and `ExportedText` for
`ExportConfirmDuration` (1.8 seconds). `Export()` does the same from code; `IsExportVisible` hides the button.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.MetricsDashboardExportDemo">
    <!-- Export hands the view to a command (here it builds a CSV in memory); the button confirms for 1.8 seconds. -->
    <StackPanel Spacing="12" Margin="0,12">
        <Border BorderThickness="1" CornerRadius="12" ClipToBounds="True"
                BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Border}">
            <arc:MetricsDashboard x:Name="Dashboard"
                                  Title="Insights"
                                  Source="northwind.dev"
                                  SelectedRange="90"
                                  PrimaryListTitle="Top paths"
                                  SecondaryListTitle="Referrers"
                                  ListValueHeader="Sessions" />
        </Border>
        <TextBlock x:Name="Log" HorizontalAlignment="Center" TextAlignment="Center" TextWrapping="Wrap" MaxWidth="560" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using System.Globalization;
using System.Text;
using System.Windows.Input;
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class MetricsDashboardExportDemo : UserControl
{
    public MetricsDashboardExportDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Dashboard.EndDate = MetricsDashboardDemoData.EndDate;
        Dashboard.Metrics.AddRange(MetricsDashboardDemoData.SiteMetrics());
        Dashboard.PrimaryItems.AddRange(MetricsDashboardDemoData.TopPaths());
        Dashboard.SecondaryItems.AddRange(MetricsDashboardDemoData.Referrers());
        Dashboard.ExportCommand = new ExportCsv(csv => Log.Text = csv);
    }

    /// <summary>Writes the selected metric's daily values for the range as CSV and shows the first lines.</summary>
    private sealed class ExportCsv(Action<string> show) : ICommand
    {
        public event EventHandler? CanExecuteChanged
        {
            add { }
            remove { }
        }

        public bool CanExecute(object? parameter) => parameter is MetricsDashboardExportRequest { Metric.Daily: not null };

        public void Execute(object? parameter)
        {
            if (parameter is not MetricsDashboardExportRequest { Metric: { Daily: { } daily } metric } request)
            {
                return;
            }
            var csv = new StringBuilder("date,").Append(metric.Key).Append('\n');
            var first = daily.Count - request.RangeDays;
            for (var i = Math.Max(0, first); i < daily.Count; i++)
            {
                var date = request.EndDate.AddDays(i - (daily.Count - 1));
                csv.Append(date.ToString("yyyy-MM-dd", CultureInfo.InvariantCulture)).Append(',')
                   .Append(daily[i].ToString("0.##", CultureInfo.InvariantCulture)).Append('\n');
            }
            var lines = csv.ToString().Split('\n');
            show($"{metric.Label}, {request.StartDate:MMM d} – {request.EndDate:MMM d}: {lines.Length - 2} rows\n" +
                 string.Join("  ", lines.Take(4)) + " …");
        }
    }
}
```

## API reference

### MetricsDashboard

A compact product analytics overview: a header with a range switch (7D / 30D / 90D) and an Export button, a row of metric tabs (total and change for the range; the selected one drives the chart), an inspectable area chart that can overlay the previous period, and two ranked lists. Totals and list values count to their new numbers when the range changes, the chart cross-fades, the range thumb and the tab underline glide. Long ranges are drawn as weekly points. Fill `Metrics`, `PrimaryItems` and `SecondaryItems` from code or bind the `*Source` properties.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Title` | `string?` | `"Analytics"` | The heading. |
| `Source` | `string?` | `null` | What the numbers are about (a site, a product), used by `SubtitleFormat`. |
| `Subtitle` | `string?` | `null` | A fixed line under the heading; null builds it from `SubtitleFormat` and follows the range. |
| `SubtitleFormat` | `string` | `"{0} · Last {1} days"` | The line under the heading when `Subtitle` is null; {0} is `Source`, {1} the range in days. |
| `SubtitleRangeFormat` | `string` | `"Last {0} days"` | The line under the heading when there is no `Source`; {0} is the range in days. |
| `MetricsSource` | `IEnumerable?` | `null` | The metrics, when you give them as a list to follow; it wins over `Metrics`. |
| `SelectedMetricIndex` | `int` | `0` | The selected metric's index (two-way): its tab is underlined and the chart draws it. |
| `SelectedRange` | `int` | `30` | The selected range in days (two-way); one of `Ranges`. |
| `WeeklyThreshold` | `int` | `60` | Ranges longer than this many days are drawn as weekly points (60: 90D gives 13 weeks). |
| `EndDate` | `DateOnly?` | `null` | The day of the last value of every series; null is today. |
| `RangeLabelFormat` | `string` | `"{0}D"` | The range buttons' text; {0} is the number of days. |
| `RangeNameFormat` | `string` | `"Last {0} days"` | The range buttons' screen reader names; {0} is the number of days. |
| `RangeGroupName` | `string` | `"Date range"` | The screen reader name of the range switch. |
| `MetricGroupName` | `string` | `"Metric"` | The screen reader name of the metric tabs. |
| `IsCompareEnabled` | `bool` | `false` | Whether the chart overlays the previous period as a dashed line (two-way). |
| `IsCompareVisible` | `bool` | `true` | Whether the Compare check box is shown. |
| `CompareText` | `string` | `"Compare"` | The Compare check box's text. |
| `PreviousLegendText` | `string` | `"Previous period"` | The legend's name of the previous period. |
| `PreviousValueFormat` | `string` | `"{0} previous"` | The tooltip's previous-period line; {0} is the formatted value. |
| `DateFormat` | `string` | `"MMM d"` | The tooltip's date pattern (.NET, en-US) for daily points and week starts. |
| `WeekTitleFormat` | `string` | `"Week of {0}"` | The tooltip's title for a weekly point; {0} is the week's first day. |
| `PartialWeekTitleFormat` | `string` | `"Week of {0} ({1} days)"` | The tooltip's title for the last week when it is shorter than seven days; {0} is its first day, {1} its length. |
| `ChartNameFormat` | `string` | `"{0}, last {1} days"` | The chart's screen reader name; {0} is the metric, {1} the range in days. |
| `ChartHelpText` | `string` | `"Use the arrow keys to inspect each point."` | The chart's screen reader help text. |
| `ChangeContextText` | `string` | `"versus the previous period"` | Spoken after a change, so its meaning does not rest on color ("up 11.7% versus the previous period"). |
| `PrimaryItemsSource` | `IEnumerable?` | `null` | The first list, when you give it as a list to follow; it wins over `PrimaryItems`. |
| `SecondaryItemsSource` | `IEnumerable?` | `null` | The second list, when you give it as a list to follow; it wins over `SecondaryItems`. |
| `PrimaryListTitle` | `string?` | `"Top pages"` | The first list's heading. |
| `SecondaryListTitle` | `string?` | `"Sources"` | The second list's heading. |
| `ListValueHeader` | `string?` | `"Visitors"` | The column heading over the lists' values. |
| `ListValueFormatter` | `Func<double, string>?` | `null` | Formats the lists' values; null writes grouped whole numbers ("11,373"). |
| `IsExportVisible` | `bool` | `true` | Whether the Export button is shown. |
| `ExportText` | `string` | `"Export"` | The Export button's text. |
| `ExportedText` | `string` | `"Exported"` | The Export button's text while it confirms an export. |
| `ExportCommand` | `ICommand?` | `null` | Run when Export is pressed, with a `MetricsDashboardExportRequest` as its parameter; when it cannot execute nothing happens. |
| `ExportConfirmDuration` | `TimeSpan` | `00:00:01.8000000` | How long the button says `ExportedText` before it returns to `ExportText` (1.8 s). |
| `ActiveIndex` | `int` | – | *Read-only.* The point being inspected (−1 for none). |
| `LayoutSize` | `MetricsDashboardSize` | – | *Read-only.* The layout the block picked from its own width. |
| `IsExportConfirmed` | `bool` | – | *Read-only.* True while the Export button shows its confirmation. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `RangeChanged` | `MetricsDashboardRangeChangedEventArgs` | Raised when `SelectedRange` changes, by the person or by code. |
| `SelectedMetricChanged` | `MetricsDashboardMetricChangedEventArgs` | Raised when `SelectedMetricIndex` changes. |
| `CompareChanged` | `MetricsDashboardCompareChangedEventArgs` | Raised when `IsCompareEnabled` changes. |
| `PointInspected` | `MetricsDashboardPointEventArgs` | Raised when a point starts being inspected or the inspection moves to another point. |
| `ExportRequested` | `MetricsDashboardExportEventArgs` | Raised when Export is pressed (or `Export` is called), after `ExportCommand` ran. |

Pseudo-classes: `:md`, `:sm`, `:compare`, `:exported`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

### MetricsDashboardMetric

One metric of a `MetricsDashboard`: a tab with its total and change, and the series the chart draws when the tab is selected. `Daily` holds one value per day, the last one for the dashboard's `EndDate`; give at least twice the longest range so every range has a previous period to compare with.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Key` | `string?` | `null` | A stable key for your code (not shown). |
| `Label` | `string` | `""` | The name on the tab, in the legend and in the chart's screen reader name. |
| `Kind` | `MetricsDashboardMetricKind` | `Count` | Whether the metric is a count or a rate. |
| `Daily` | `IReadOnlyList<double>?` | `null` | One value per day, oldest first; the last one is the dashboard's end date. |
| `Numerators` | `IReadOnlyList<double>?` | `null` | For a rate: the daily numerators (conversions), aligned with `Daily`; with `Denominators` they give exact weekly and range rates. |
| `Denominators` | `IReadOnlyList<double>?` | `null` | For a rate: the daily denominators (sessions), aligned with `Daily`. |
| `HigherIsBetter` | `bool` | `true` | Whether a rise is good (green). False for churn, bounce or latency: a fall is then shown in the success color. |
| `ValueFormatter` | `Func<double, string>?` | `null` | Formats the tab's value and the tooltip's values; null writes counts as "36,686" and rates as "4.8%". |
| `AxisFormatter` | `Func<double, string>?` | `null` | Formats the y axis labels; null writes counts as "0", "500", "1.5K" and rates with the decimals the tick step needs ("42.5%"). |
| `DeltaFormatter` | `Func<double, string>?` | `null` | Formats the size of the change (always positive; the arrow shows the direction); null writes "11.7%" for counts and "0.1 pts" for rates. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### MetricsDashboardItem

One row of a ranked list under the chart (a page, a referrer): a name and one value per range. The row's bar shows the value as a share of the list's first row, so give the rows largest first.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Label` | `string` | `""` | The name; long names end in an ellipsis and show in full as a tooltip. |
| `Values` | `IReadOnlyList<double>?` | `null` | The value for each range, in the order of `Ranges`; a missing entry uses `Value`. |
| `Value` | `double` | `0` | The value when `Values` has none for the selected range. |
| `Tag` | `object?` | `null` | Anything of yours that belongs to the row. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### MetricsDashboardExportRequest

What an export was asked for: passed to `ExportCommand` and `ExportRequested`.

### MetricsDashboardPointEventArgs

Arguments of `MetricsDashboard.PointInspected`: a point of the chart is being inspected (pointer or keys).

Derives from `RoutedEventArgs`: every member of `RoutedEventArgs` works as well.

## Accessibility

### Keyboard

- **Tab** moves through the range switch, Export, the metric tabs, Compare and the chart. The range switch and the
  tabs are one stop each, on the selected item.
- In the range switch, **Left** / **Right** (and **Up** / **Down**) move and select, wrapping at the ends; **Home** and
  **End** jump to the first and last range.
- In the metric tabs, **Left** / **Right** move and select, wrapping; **Home** and **End** select the first and last metric.
- **Space** toggles Compare. **Enter** or **Space** presses Export.
- On the chart, focus alone shows nothing. **Right** shows the last point and **Left** the one before it; then
  **Left** / **Right** step through the points and stop at the ends, **Home** and **End** jump to the first and last
  point, and **Escape** ends the inspection. Moving the focus away or the pointer out of the plot ends it too.

### Screen readers and focus

- The block is named by its title, which is a level 2 heading; the list titles are level 3 headings and name their
  sections.
- The range switch is a group named by `RangeGroupName`; its segments are toggle buttons named "Last 7 days" and so on.
- The metric tabs are tabs in a group named by `MetricGroupName`; each says its label, its total and its change in words,
  for example "Sessions, 36,686, up 11.7% versus the previous period", so the meaning does not rest on the color.
- The chart is an image named "Sessions, last 30 days" with `ChartHelpText` as its help text. The inspected point
  ("Sep 21, 1,370, 1,111 previous") is announced politely as it changes, from the keyboard or the pointer. The legend,
  axes, gridlines and the tooltip itself are not read separately.
- Each list row is read as "name, value"; long names are cut with an ellipsis and show in full as a tooltip.
- Export's confirmation is announced; the button's name follows its text.
- Focus rings are drawn for keyboard focus only: around the range segment and Export, inside the tab's edge (so a
  neighbour or the block's edge never hides it), around the 14px Compare box and around the plot.

## Motion

- **Range change**: the switch's thumb glides on a quick critically damped spring (about 330 ms); every tab total and list
  value counts from the old number to the new one in 480 ms (.22, 1, .36, 1), all at once; the chart cross-fades from the
  old picture to the new one in 240 ms. Axis labels, dates, the subtitle and the change lines switch at once.
- **Metric change**: the underline glides to the new tab on a smooth spring (about 530 ms), across rows in the 2 × 2
  layout; the chart cross-fades in 240 ms.
- **Compare**: the dashed previous period fades in and out on the smooth spring (about 700 ms); the box's colors change in
  160 ms.
- **Inspection**: the rule, the dot and the tooltip appear, move and disappear at once. The tooltip sits in the half of the
  plot away from the point and never covers it.
- **Export**: the texts cross-fade and the glyphs swap with a fade and a scale from .8 in 160 ms; hover tints the button
  and the tabs in 160 ms and pressing Export scales it to .97.
- Nothing animates when the block first appears. Reduced motion jumps the thumb and the underline, replaces numbers and
  the chart at once and drops the color transitions; Off applies every change at once.

## Related

- `KPI drilldown`, `Metric explorer` and `Revenue explorer`, the other Analytics blocks with metric cards and charts.
- `Small multiples` for many series at a glance.
- `SegmentedControl` for a standalone range switch.

# KPI drilldown

> KPI cards with sparklines and period changes that grow in place into a detail view with a trend chart, a prior-period comparison, a readout you can drive by keyboard and a breakdown by dimension.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc.Blocks`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc.Blocks --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/blocks/kpi-drilldown

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.KpiDrilldownPreviewDemo">
    <!-- Six metrics over 180 invented days, three breakdown dimensions. Values: KpiDrilldownDemoData. -->
    <arc:KpiDrilldown x:Name="Block" Title="Studio pulse" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class KpiDrilldownPreviewDemo : UserControl
{
    public KpiDrilldownPreviewDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Block.EndDate = KpiDrilldownDemoData.End;
        Block.Dimensions.AddRange(KpiDrilldownDemoData.Dimensions());
        Block.Metrics.AddRange(KpiDrilldownDemoData.Metrics());
    }
}
```

## When to use

`KpiDrilldown` is an overview that keeps its context. A grid of cards shows each metric's latest value, how it moved
against the previous period and the shape of the period; choosing a card grows it, in place, into the full story, and
Escape folds it back.

- **A finance or growth overview.** Revenue, accounts, retention, churn and conversion on one page, each one click from its
  chart and its split.
- **Period reviews.** One range switch (7, 30 or 90 days) moves every card and the open detail view together, and Compare
  puts the prior period behind the current one.
- **Where did the change come from?** The breakdown table splits the open metric by plan, region or channel, with each
  member's share, value and change.

## When not to use

- **Many metrics.** Six cards read at a glance; more than that belongs in a table or a metric picker.
- **Free exploration.** The detail view has one chart, one range and one split. For zooming, brushing or choosing series use
  a metric explorer.
- **Live streaming values.** The block is designed around daily series that change when a range, Compare or a dimension does.

## Usage

The block derives from Avalonia's `TemplatedControl`. It contains no data: give it `Metrics`, each a `KpiMetric` whose
`Values` are daily numbers ending on `EndDate` (at least twice the longest range, so the prior period exists), and
`Dimensions` for the breakdown with matching `KpiBreakdown`s on each metric.

```xml
<arc:KpiDrilldown Title="Overview" RangeDays="30">
    <arc:KpiDrilldown.Dimensions>
        <arc:KpiDimension Key="tier" Label="Tier" />
    </arc:KpiDrilldown.Dimensions>
    <arc:KpiMetric Key="arr" Label="Annual run rate" Format="CurrencyCompact" Description="Contracted yearly revenue." />
</arc:KpiDrilldown>
```

```csharp
var metric = new KpiMetric("refunds", "Refund rate", dailyValues)
{
    Kind = KpiKind.Rate,        // the change is a difference in points ("−0.2 pts")
    IsLowerBetter = true,       // a fall is green; the arrow still points down
    Format = KpiValueFormat.Percent,
};
metric.Breakdowns.Add(new KpiBreakdown("tier", [new KpiBreakdownRow("Team", teamValues)]));
```

All numbers are invented in the demos, from a fixed seed.

### What a card shows

The value is the series' last day and does not change with the range. The change compares the last day of the current
period with the last day of the prior one: a relative percent for `Total` metrics, a difference in points for `Rate`
metrics. It shows an arrow, a sign (a true minus) and a colour, and reads "unchanged" with a level arrow when it rounds to
zero. The sparkline is the current period resampled to 40 points, drawn straight and normalised to its own range.

### Detail view

The detail view shows the name, the value, the change and "vs … in the prior N days", the metric's `Description`, a 220px
trend chart (72 points; three gridlines carrying the highest, middle and lowest value, three dates), a legend and the
breakdown. Pointing at the chart snaps a cursor to the nearest point and shows a readout with the date, the value and, with
Compare on, the prior period's value for the same day.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.KpiDrilldownControlledDemo">
    <!-- SelectedKey, RangeDays and IsCompareEnabled are two-way: the buttons drive the block, the log reports what the person did. -->
    <StackPanel Spacing="16">
        <StackPanel Orientation="Horizontal" Spacing="8">
            <arc:Button Content="Open refund rate" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Click="OnOpenRefunds" />
            <arc:Button Content="Open run rate" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Click="OnOpenRunRate" />
            <arc:Button Content="Back to cards" Variant="Ghost" Size="Small" Click="OnClose" />
            <arc:Button Content="90 days" Variant="Ghost" Size="Small" Click="OnNinety" />
        </StackPanel>
        <arc:KpiDrilldown x:Name="Block"
                          Title="Studio pulse"
                          SelectedChanged="OnSelectedChanged"
                          RangeChanged="OnRangeChanged"
                          CompareChanged="OnCompareChanged"
                          DimensionChanged="OnDimensionChanged" />
        <StackPanel Spacing="4">
            <TextBlock FontSize="13"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}"
                       Text="{Binding #Block.SelectedKey, StringFormat='SelectedKey: {0}', TargetNullValue='SelectedKey: none'}" />
            <TextBlock x:Name="Log" FontSize="13" TextWrapping="Wrap" Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
        </StackPanel>
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class KpiDrilldownControlledDemo : UserControl
{
    private readonly List<string> _lines = new();

    public KpiDrilldownControlledDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Block.EndDate = KpiDrilldownDemoData.End;
        Block.Dimensions.AddRange(KpiDrilldownDemoData.Dimensions());
        Block.Metrics.AddRange(KpiDrilldownDemoData.Metrics());
        Write("Choose a card, a range or Compare.");
    }

    private void OnOpenRefunds(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) => Block.Open("refunds");

    private void OnOpenRunRate(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) => Block.Open("arr");

    private void OnClose(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) => Block.Close();

    private void OnNinety(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) => Block.RangeDays = 90;

    private void OnSelectedChanged(object? sender, KpiSelectionChangedEventArgs e) =>
        Write(e.NewKey is null ? "SelectedChanged: back to the cards" : $"SelectedChanged: {e.OldKey ?? "none"} → {e.NewKey}");

    private void OnRangeChanged(object? sender, KpiRangeChangedEventArgs e) => Write($"RangeChanged: {e.OldDays} → {e.NewDays} days");

    private void OnCompareChanged(object? sender, KpiCompareChangedEventArgs e) => Write($"CompareChanged: {(e.IsEnabled ? "on" : "off")}");

    private void OnDimensionChanged(object? sender, KpiSelectionChangedEventArgs e) => Write($"DimensionChanged: {e.NewKey}");

    private void Write(string line)
    {
        _lines.Insert(0, line);
        if (_lines.Count > 4)
        {
            _lines.RemoveAt(_lines.Count - 1);
        }
        Log.Text = string.Join(Environment.NewLine, _lines);
    }
}
```

### Bound state and events

`SelectedKey`, `RangeDays`, `IsCompareEnabled` and `SelectedDimensionKey` are two-way. `Open(key)` and `Close()` do what
choosing a card and Escape do. `SelectedChanged`, `RangeChanged`, `CompareChanged` and `DimensionChanged` report what the
person did, and `SelectedCommand` runs when a detail view opens (parameter: the metric) or closes (parameter: null).

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.KpiDrilldownFourMetricsDemo">
    <!-- Four metrics, no dimensions (the breakdown is left out), Compare off to begin with, a 14 / 28 day range pair. -->
    <arc:KpiDrilldown x:Name="Block" Title="Weekly check" IsCompareEnabled="False" RangeDays="14" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class KpiDrilldownFourMetricsDemo : UserControl
{
    public KpiDrilldownFourMetricsDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Block.EndDate = KpiDrilldownDemoData.End;
        Block.Ranges = [14, 28, 56];
        Block.Metrics.AddRange(KpiDrilldownDemoData.Metrics(4, withBreakdowns: false));
    }
}
```

### Fewer metrics, other ranges

`Ranges` sets the range switch's days; with no `Dimensions` the breakdown is left out, and `IsCompareEnabled` starts the
block with the prior period hidden. `MetricsSource` follows a list you own.

```xml

             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.KpiDrilldownNarrowDemo">
    <!-- The layout follows the block's own width: 3 columns from 760, 2 from 520, one column with an icon-only Compare below. -->
    <Border Width="400" HorizontalAlignment="Left">
        <arc:KpiDrilldown x:Name="Block" Title="Studio pulse" />
    </Border>
</UserControl>
```


### Narrow containers

The block reads its own width: three columns from 760, two from 520, and below 520 one column, a 22px value, an icon-only
Compare button and a breakdown without the share column.

### Words

Every word besides the data comes from `Labels` (`KpiDrilldownLabels`): the Compare text, range names, the legend, the
"vs" line, the tooltip's prior line, the cards' spoken names and the chart's summary.

## API reference

### KpiDrilldown

An overview of KPI cards that open in place: each card shows a metric's value on the last day, its change against the prior period and a sparkline; choosing a card grows it into a detail view (a trend chart with the prior period dashed behind it, a readout under the pointer or keyboard cursor, a sentence about the metric and a breakdown table by dimension) and Escape folds it back. A range switch (7 / 30 / 90 days) morphs every line and rolls every number; the Compare toggle shows or hides the prior period. The block contains no data: give it `Metrics` (each a daily series ending on `EndDate`, at least twice the longest range long) and, for the breakdown, `Dimensions` with matching `Breakdowns`. Keyboard: Tab reaches Compare, the range switch and each card; Enter or Space opens a card and moves focus to the close button; in the detail view Tab reaches the close button, the chart (← / → move the cursor by a day, Home and End jump to the ends) and the dimension switch. Escape closes the detail view from anywhere on the page and returns focus to the card.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `MetricsSource` | `IEnumerable?` | `null` | The metrics, when you give them as a list to follow (observed when it raises collection changes); it wins over `Metrics`. |
| `Title` | `string?` | `"Overview"` | The heading at the top left. |
| `EndDate` | `DateOnly?` | `null` | The date of every series' last value; null uses today. |
| `Ranges` | `IReadOnlyList<int>` | `<>z__ReadOnlyArray`1[System.Int32]` | The ranges the switch offers, in days (7, 30, 90). |
| `RangeDays` | `int` | `30` | The range shown, in days (two-way); a value that is not in `Ranges` still works but selects no segment. |
| `IsCompareEnabled` | `bool` | `true` | The prior period is drawn behind the current one and listed in the readout (two-way). |
| `SelectedKey` | `string?` | `null` | The key of the metric whose detail view is open (two-way); null shows the cards. |
| `SelectedDimensionKey` | `string?` | `null` | The key of the breakdown dimension (two-way); null or an unknown key uses the first. |
| `DateFormat` | `string` | `"MMM d"` | The date pattern of the axis and the readout ("MMM d"). |
| `Labels` | `KpiDrilldownLabels` | – | Every word the block writes or speaks besides the data. |
| `SelectedCommand` | `ICommand?` | `null` | Run when a detail view opens (parameter: the metric) or closes (parameter: null), after `SelectedChanged`. |
| `SelectedMetric` | `KpiMetric?` | – | *Read-only.* The metric whose detail view is open (resolved from `SelectedKey`). |
| `IsDetailOpen` | `bool` | – | *Read-only.* True while a detail view is open or folding back. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `SelectedChanged` | `KpiSelectionChangedEventArgs` | Raised when a detail view starts to open (new key) or to close (new key null). |
| `RangeChanged` | `KpiRangeChangedEventArgs` | Raised when the range changes (by the switch or by code). |
| `CompareChanged` | `KpiCompareChangedEventArgs` | Raised when Compare is turned on or off. |
| `DimensionChanged` | `KpiSelectionChangedEventArgs` | Raised when the breakdown dimension changes. |

Pseudo-classes: `:open`, `:compact`, `:two-column`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

### KpiMetric

One KPI of a `KpiDrilldown`: a daily series whose last value falls on `EndDate`, how to write it, whether a fall is good, a sentence for the detail view and its breakdowns per dimension. The series should hold at least twice the longest range so the prior period exists.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Key` | `string` | `""` | Stable key (`SelectedKey` refers to it). |
| `Label` | `string` | `""` | The name on the card and in the detail view. |
| `Description` | `string?` | `null` | The sentence under the detail view's value (null leaves it out). |
| `Values` | `IReadOnlyList<double>?` | `null` | Daily values, oldest first; the last one is the value on `EndDate`. |
| `Kind` | `KpiKind` | `Total` | How the change is measured: relative percent (Total, default) or a difference in points (Rate). |
| `IsLowerBetter` | `bool` | `false` | A fall is good (churn, refunds, latency): the arrow still points down, the colour turns green. |
| `Format` | `KpiValueFormat` | `Number` | The built-in value format (Number by default). |
| `Decimals` | `int` | `-1` | Fraction digits of the value; −1 (default) uses the format's own (Number and Currency 0, Compact and Percent 1). |
| `CurrencySymbol` | `string` | `"$"` | The symbol of the currency formats ("$"). |
| `ValueFormatter` | `Func<double, string>?` | `null` | Writes a value instead of `Format`; numbers it writes are replaced rather than rolled. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### KpiBreakdown

The rows of one metric split by one dimension (`Breakdowns`).

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `DimensionKey` | `string` | `""` | The `Key` these rows belong to. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### KpiBreakdownRow

One row of a breakdown: a name and either a daily series (`Values`, read per range like the metric: the value on the last day of each period) or two fixed numbers (`Value` and `PreviousValue`).

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Label` | `string` | `""` | The row's name ("Enterprise", "Europe"). |
| `Values` | `IReadOnlyList<double>?` | `null` | Daily values aligned with the metric's series (last = end date); wins over the fixed numbers. |
| `Value` | `double` | `0` | The value in the current period when there is no series. |
| `PreviousValue` | `double` | `NaN` | The value in the prior period when there is no series (NaN hides the change). |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### KpiDimension

A dimension the detail view can split a metric by (the breakdown switch).

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Key` | `string` | `""` | Stable key (matches `DimensionKey`). |
| `Label` | `string` | `""` | The switch text and the table's first column heading ("Plan"). |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### KpiDrilldownLabels

Every word a `KpiDrilldown` writes or speaks besides the data, with English defaults. Placeholders are numbered as described on each property. Assign a new instance to `Labels` to translate the block.

### KpiKind

How a `KpiMetric`'s change between two periods is measured.

Derives from `Enum`: every member of `Enum` works as well.

### KpiValueFormat

How a `KpiMetric`'s values are written (cards, detail, axis, tooltip and breakdown).

Derives from `Enum`: every member of `Enum` works as well.

### KpiSelectionChangedEventArgs

Arguments of `SelectedChanged` and `DimensionChanged`.

Derives from `RoutedEventArgs`: every member of `RoutedEventArgs` works as well.

### KpiRangeChangedEventArgs

Arguments of `RangeChanged`.

Derives from `RoutedEventArgs`: every member of `RoutedEventArgs` works as well.

### KpiCompareChangedEventArgs

Arguments of `CompareChanged`.

Derives from `RoutedEventArgs`: every member of `RoutedEventArgs` works as well.

## Accessibility

### Keyboard

- **Tab** reaches Compare, the range switch (one stop; the arrows move the selection, Home and End jump) and each card.
- **Enter** or **Space** on a card opens it and moves focus to the close button.
- In the detail view Tab reaches the close button, the chart and the dimension switch; the cards behind are skipped.
- On the chart **←** and **→** move the cursor by one day (the first press shows the last day), **Home** and **End** jump to
  the first and last day, and the cursor disappears when the chart loses focus.
- **Escape** closes the detail view from anywhere on the page and returns focus to the card.

### Screen readers

- Each card is one button named by its label, value and change in words ("Refund rate, 2.6%, down 0.2 pts against the prior
  30 days. Show details"). The cards are hidden from assistive technology while a detail view is open.
- The chart is an image named by a summary of its start and end; moving the cursor by keyboard is announced politely with the
  date and value.
- The breakdown is a labelled section with one named row per member; the change uses an arrow or sign as well as colour.
- Compare keeps its name when it shrinks to an icon. Focus rings are 2px, outside the element, and only show for the keyboard.

## Motion

- **Opening**: the card hides and the panel grows from its box to the card area (inset 8) on one spring, real width, height
  and position (about 0.5s visual duration, no bounce); the content keeps its final layout and is clipped. The veil fades in
  over 240 ms, the body fades in after 120 ms over 480 ms and the surface warms over 480 ms. The area's height follows.
- **Closing**: the body fades in 120 ms, the shadow in 480 ms, and the panel folds back into the card on the same spring
  before the card reappears; focus returns to the card.
- **Range, Compare, dimension**: every sparkline and chart line morphs point by point on a smooth spring, the axis labels
  show the interpolated numbers, every number rolls digit by digit, the prior line fades in 240 ms, texts cross-fade (out
  80 ms, then in 240 ms), and the share bars spring.
- Reduced motion shows the panel at its final size with a 160 ms fade; morphs, bars and numbers jump. Off applies everything
  at once.

## Related

- `SegmentedControl` for the switches in other blocks.
- `Metric explorer` and `Revenue explorer`, the other Analytics blocks that go deeper into one number.
- `Metrics dashboard` for a row of KPIs without drilldown.
