# Metric explorer

> A row of KPI cards that each open into a chart you can inspect by dragging: the card's surface grows into the panel, the tabs morph the line from metric to metric point by point, the range switch moves a camera window over the daily data, and this period is drawn against the one before it.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc.Blocks`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc.Blocks --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/blocks/metric-explorer

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.MetricExplorerPreviewDemo">
    <!--
        Four KPI cards over two years of daily data. Click a card (or press Enter) to open its chart, switch metric and
        range, drag across the chart to read single days. Data: MetricExplorerDemoData.
    -->
    <arc:MetricExplorer x:Name="Explorer"
                        Title="Workspace health"
                        Caption="Northwind Labs · refreshed Oct 14, 2026 at 08:30 UTC" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class MetricExplorerPreviewDemo : UserControl
{
    public MetricExplorerPreviewDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        foreach (var metric in MetricExplorerDemoData.Workspace())
        {
            metric.EndDate = MetricExplorerDemoData.Today;
            Explorer.Metrics.Add(metric);
        }
    }
}
```

## When to use

`MetricExplorer` is the top of a growth or finance page: four or so numbers that matter, each with its recent shape, and a
way to look closer without leaving the page. The cards show the latest value, the change over the selected range and a
sparkline. Opening one turns the card into a chart of the same metric, with tabs for the other metrics, a range switch and
a readout that follows the pointer.

- **KPI rows that need one more level of detail.** The chart answers "is this a blip or a trend?" with a previous-period
  line behind it, without a separate page.
- **Comparing periods.** Every day on the chart is compared with the same day one period earlier, so a scrub reads
  "Sep 6 vs Aug 7" and a change in the readout, not only a value.
- **Daily data of two or three kinds.** Money, counts and rates share one block: each metric chooses its format, its axis
  precision and whether a rise is good.

## When not to use

- **A single hero number.** Use a stat card; the opening chart is overhead for one value.
- **Dozens of metrics.** The row and the tab strip are designed for three to five metrics. Use a table or the
  `Metrics dashboard` block for more.
- **Data that is not daily.** The chart assumes one value per day and compares a range with the same number of days
  before it. Use `Revenue explorer` for brushing and zooming irregular series.
- **Exact lookups.** The readout shows one day at a time; put a grid beside the block when people need to copy numbers.

## Usage

The block derives from Avalonia's `TemplatedControl`. Its content is a list of `ExplorerMetric`s. A metric has a `Title`
(the card's label and the readout's heading), a `ShortTitle` for the tab, a `Description` for the line under the chart,
and `Values`: a daily series, oldest first, whose last value belongs to `EndDate` (today when it is not set). The series
needs at least twice the longest range plus one day, because the chart draws each range against the one before it.

```xml
<arc:MetricExplorer Title="Workspace health" Caption="Refreshed Oct 14, 2026 at 08:30 UTC">
    <arc:ExplorerMetric Title="Annual run-rate" ShortTitle="ARR" ValueFormat="CurrencyCompact"
                        Values="{Binding Arr}" EndDate="{Binding Today}"
                        Description="Yearly value of active contracts, after discounts." />
</arc:MetricExplorer>
```

```csharp
explorer.Metrics.Add(new ExplorerMetric("Weekly active teams", teams, ExplorerValueFormat.Count) { ShortTitle = "Teams" });
explorer.Open(0);          // the surface grows out of the first card
explorer.SelectedRangeIndex = 1;   // 90 days
```

`MetricsSource` takes a collection you own instead (an `ObservableCollection` is followed). Changing a metric's
properties updates the block in place.

### Anatomy

- **Heading**: `Title` on the left and `Caption` on the right; the caption wraps under the title when there is no room.
- **Cards**: label, latest value, an arrow with the change and the range ("30 days"), and a sparkline ending in a dot.
  Two columns under 760 wide, four above. Hover darkens the edge; Enter, Space or a click opens the card.
- **Open chart**: metric tabs (with their values), a close button, the readout, the range switch, the legend with the
  date span, the chart and the metric's description.

### Value formats, changes and tones

`ValueFormat` chooses how a value is written: `Count` ("5,874"), `Currency` ("$12,480"), `CurrencyCompact` ("$4.62M",
"$412.00K"), `Percent` (a value in percent units, "27.3%") or `Ratio` ("1.12×"). `ValueFormatter` replaces it, and
`AxisFormatter` receives a tick's value and the step between ticks for the y labels. The y axis always has five ticks and
chooses the finest of 1, 1.5, 2, 2.5, 3, 4 and 5 times a power of ten that holds both lines with 3% of padding;
`MaxAxisDecimals` caps how many decimals a step may have (two for compact money, one for percentages, none for counts).

`ChangeMode` is `Relative` for the usual "+1.6%" or `Points` for rates ("+1.2 pts"). The arrow shows direction and the
color shows whether that is good: with `IsHigherBetter="False"` a rise turns red and a fall green, so a falling cost reads
as good news with a downward arrow.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.MetricExplorerFinanceDemo">
    <!--
        Three finance metrics. Monthly burn sets IsHigherBetter="False": its rise is red and its fall green, whichever way
        the arrow points. Rates (gross margin) use ChangeMode="Points" and read "+0.5 pts" instead of a percentage.
    -->
    <arc:MetricExplorer x:Name="Explorer"
                        Title="Finance"
                        Caption="Quarter to date"
                        SelectedRangeIndex="1" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class MetricExplorerFinanceDemo : UserControl
{
    public MetricExplorerFinanceDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        foreach (var metric in MetricExplorerDemoData.Finance())
        {
            metric.EndDate = MetricExplorerDemoData.Today;
            Explorer.Metrics.Add(metric);
        }
    }
}
```

### Ranges

A range is a window of days: 30, 90 and 364 by default (the buttons "30D", "90D" and "12M"). Create your own with
`Ranges` or `RangesSource`; each `ExplorerRange` has a `Label`, `Days`, the `CardText` the cards show ("30 days") and the
`CompareText` the readout shows ("vs 30 days ago"). `SparklineStep` is the number of days between sparkline points: 1 for
daily, 7 for a long range, so a year stays at 53 points. `SelectedRangeIndex` is two-way and the cards follow it, so the
chart you leave open decides what the collapsed cards say.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.MetricExplorerRangesDemo">
    <!--
        Your own ranges (a week, two months, half a year) and no dashed previous period. Each range says how many days it
        shows, what the cards call it, and what the readout compares with; the chart zooms its window between them.
    -->
    <arc:MetricExplorer x:Name="Explorer"
                        Title="Custom ranges"
                        Caption="Seven days, two months, half a year"
                        ShowPreviousPeriod="False"
                        IsOpen="True" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class MetricExplorerRangesDemo : UserControl
{
    public MetricExplorerRangesDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Explorer.Ranges.Add(new ExplorerRange("7D", 7, "7 days", "vs 7 days ago"));
        Explorer.Ranges.Add(new ExplorerRange("60D", 60, "60 days", "vs 60 days ago"));
        Explorer.Ranges.Add(new ExplorerRange("6M", 182, "6 months", "vs 6 months ago", 7));
        foreach (var metric in MetricExplorerDemoData.Workspace().Take(3))
        {
            metric.EndDate = MetricExplorerDemoData.Today;
            Explorer.Metrics.Add(metric);
        }
    }
}
```

`ShowPreviousPeriod` hides the dashed line and the second dot of the inspection.

### Inspecting a day

Move over the plot, press and drag, or touch it: the nearest day gets a crosshair, a dot on each line and a date capsule
on the axis. The readout's number, change and comparison switch to that day against the matching day one period
earlier ("Sep 6 vs Aug 7"), and the change digits roll. Leaving the plot clears the inspection; a finger lifting does too.

`ScrubIndex` is the inspected day (0 is the first day of the range) and `ScrubChanged` reports the date, the value and the
previous period's value. A click focuses the chart; with the keyboard, Tab onto the chart shows the last day and the
arrow keys walk through the days.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.MetricExplorerEventsDemo">
    <!--
        IsOpen, SelectedMetricIndex and SelectedRangeIndex are two-way properties, and every user action is an event. The
        buttons drive the block from outside (the surface still grows out of the card); the log shows what it reports.
    -->
    <StackPanel Spacing="12">
        <StackPanel Orientation="Horizontal" Spacing="8">
            <arc:Button x:Name="OpenTeams" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Content="Open weekly teams" />
            <arc:Button x:Name="Longer" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Content="Show 12 months" />
            <arc:Button x:Name="CloseChart" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Content="Close" />
        </StackPanel>
        <arc:MetricExplorer x:Name="Explorer"
                            Title="Workspace health"
                            Caption="Move over the chart, then press Escape." />
        <TextBlock x:Name="Log"
                   TextWrapping="Wrap"
                   FontSize="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TypeXS}"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}"
                   Text="Events appear here." />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class MetricExplorerEventsDemo : UserControl
{
    private readonly List<string> _lines = new();

    public MetricExplorerEventsDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        foreach (var metric in MetricExplorerDemoData.Workspace())
        {
            metric.EndDate = MetricExplorerDemoData.Today;
            Explorer.Metrics.Add(metric);
        }

        OpenTeams.Click += (_, _) => Explorer.Open(1);
        Longer.Click += (_, _) => Explorer.SelectedRangeIndex = 2;
        CloseChart.Click += (_, _) => Explorer.Close();

        Explorer.MetricOpened += (_, e) => Write($"Opened: {e.Metric?.Title}");
        Explorer.MetricClosed += (_, e) => Write($"Closed: {e.Metric?.Title}");
        Explorer.SelectedMetricChanged += (_, e) => Write($"Metric: {e.Metric?.Title}");
        Explorer.SelectedRangeChanged += (_, e) => Write($"Range: {e.Range?.Label}");
        Explorer.ScrubChanged += (_, e) => Write(e.Date is { } date
            ? $"Day: {date:MMM d} = {e.Value:N2} (a period earlier {e.PreviousValue:N2})"
            : "CloseChartion cleared");
    }

    private void Write(string line)
    {
        _lines.Insert(0, line);
        if (_lines.Count > 5)
        {
            _lines.RemoveAt(_lines.Count - 1);
        }
        Log.Text = string.Join(Environment.NewLine, _lines);
    }
}
```

### Narrow containers

The block reads its own width. Under 760 the cards take two columns. Under 640 the open chart tightens its paddings to 16,
drops the values from the tabs and puts the range switch under the readout. At 440 and under the cards get a two-line
label and a smaller number, the tabs share a full row, the close button moves down beside the readout and the x axis picks a
coarser ladder.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"

             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.MetricExplorerCompactDemo">
    <!--
        In a 400-wide card the block reads its own width: the cards take two columns with smaller padding and a two-line
        label, and the open chart gives the tabs a full row, moves the close button to the readout and tightens the axis.
        The chart starts open so the compact layout is visible.
    -->
    <Border Width="400"
            HorizontalAlignment="Left"
            BorderThickness="1"
            BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Border}"
            Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Background}"
            CornerRadius="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource RadiusPanel}"
            Padding="16">
        <arc:MetricExplorer x:Name="Explorer"
                            Title="Workspace health"
                            Caption="Refreshed Oct 14"
                            IsOpen="True" />
    </Border>
</UserControl>
```

### Words and screen reader text

Every visible and spoken word is a property with an English default: the legend (`ThisPeriodText`, `PreviousPeriodText`),
the close button, the tab and range labels, the card name (`CardNameFormat`), the announcements (`AnnouncementFormat`,
`ClosedAnnouncementFormat`), the comparison while inspecting (`ScrubCompareFormat`) and the direction words (`UpText`,
`DownText`, `FlatText`).

## API reference

### MetricExplorer

Metric explorer: a row of KPI cards (label, big number, change, sparkline) where any card opens into a chart you can inspect. The card's surface grows into the chart's panel: metric tabs with their values, the readout (name, big number, change with rolling digits), the range switch, a legend with the date span, and the chart itself: this period as a line with the period before it dashed beside it. Pointing at the chart, dragging, or using the arrow keys shows the nearest day with a crosshair and a date capsule, and swaps the readout to that day against the same day one period earlier. Switching metric morphs the line point by point; switching range zooms the time window like a camera. Escape clears the inspection, then closes the chart.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Title` | `string?` | `null` | The heading above the cards; null leaves it out. |
| `Caption` | `string?` | `null` | The small text on the heading's right (workspace and refresh time); null leaves it out. |
| `MetricsSource` | `IEnumerable?` | `null` | The metrics as a list you own (followed when it raises collection changes); it wins over `Metrics`. |
| `RangesSource` | `IEnumerable?` | `null` | The ranges as a list you own; it wins over `Ranges`. Empty means 30 days, 90 days and 12 months. |
| `SelectedMetricIndex` | `int` | `0` | The metric the chart shows or opens on (two-way, index into the effective list). |
| `SelectedRangeIndex` | `int` | `0` | The range the cards and the chart use (two-way, index into the effective ranges). |
| `IsOpen` | `bool` | `false` | Whether the chart is open (two-way): the cards open into it and it shrinks back into the card. |
| `ShowPreviousPeriod` | `bool` | `true` | Whether the previous period's dashed line (and its inspection dot) is drawn. |
| `ThisPeriodText` | `string` | `"This period"` | The legend's text for the solid line. |
| `PreviousPeriodText` | `string` | `"Previous period"` | The legend's text for the dashed line. |
| `CloseText` | `string` | `"Close chart"` | The close button's screen reader name. |
| `TabsLabel` | `string` | `"Metric"` | The screen reader name of the metric tabs. |
| `RangeLabel` | `string` | `"Chart range"` | The screen reader name of the range switch. |
| `ScrubLabel` | `string` | `"Scrub"` | The start of the chart's screen reader name ("Scrub" + the metric). |
| `ScrubValueFormat` | `string` | `"{0}: {1}. {2}: {3}"` | The chart's value text for the inspected day: {0} its date, {1} its value, {2} the date a period earlier, {3} that value. |
| `SummaryFormat` | `string` | `"{0} over the last {1} days, from {2} to {3}."` | The chart's summary for screen readers: {0} metric, {1} days, {2} first value, {3} last value. |
| `ScrubCompareFormat` | `string` | `"{0} vs {1}"` | The comparison in the readout while a day is inspected: {0} that day, {1} the day a period earlier ("Sep 6 vs Aug 7"). |
| `CardNameFormat` | `string` | `"{0}: {1}, {2} {3} over {4}. Open chart"` | A card's spoken name: {0} title, {1} value, {2} up / down, {3} change, {4} the range ("30 days"). |
| `PointsUnit` | `string` | `" points"` | The unit spoken after a change in points. |
| `AnnouncementFormat` | `string` | `"{0}, last {1}: {2}, {3} {4} {5}"` | Said when the metric or the range changes in the open chart: {0} metric, {1} range, {2} value, {3} up / down, {4} change, {5} comparison. |
| `ClosedAnnouncementFormat` | `string` | `"Chart closed. {0} metrics shown."` | Said when the chart closes: {0} the number of metrics. |
| `UpText` | `string` | `"up"` | The spoken word for a rise. |
| `DownText` | `string` | `"down"` | The spoken word for a fall. |
| `FlatText` | `string` | `"unchanged"` | The spoken word for no change. |
| `OpenedCommand` | `ICommand?` | `null` | Run when a chart opens, with its `MetricExplorerMetricEventArgs` as the parameter. |
| `ClosedCommand` | `ICommand?` | `null` | Run when the chart closes, with its `MetricExplorerMetricEventArgs` as the parameter. |
| `RangeChangedCommand` | `ICommand?` | `null` | Run when the range changes, with its `MetricExplorerRangeEventArgs` as the parameter. |
| `ScrubIndex` | `int?` | – | *Read-only.* The inspected day of the chart (0 = first day of the range); null when none. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `MetricOpened` | `MetricExplorerMetricEventArgs` | Raised when the chart opens. |
| `MetricClosed` | `MetricExplorerMetricEventArgs` | Raised when the chart closes. |
| `SelectedMetricChanged` | `MetricExplorerMetricEventArgs` | Raised when `SelectedMetricIndex` changes. |
| `SelectedRangeChanged` | `MetricExplorerRangeEventArgs` | Raised when `SelectedRangeIndex` changes. |
| `ScrubChanged` | `MetricExplorerScrubEventArgs` | Raised when the inspected day changes or is cleared. |

Pseudo-classes: `:open`, `:narrow`, `:compact`, `:two-column`, `:scrubbing`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

### ExplorerMetric

One metric of a `MetricExplorer`: a card in the row, a tab in the open chart. `Values` is a daily series that ends on `EndDate`; the chart shows the last days of the selected range against the same number of days before them, so the series needs at least twice the longest range plus one day.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Key` | `string?` | `null` | A stable key (events, automation ids); optional. |
| `Title` | `string` | `""` | The card's label and the readout's heading ("Weekly active teams"). |
| `ShortTitle` | `string?` | `null` | The tab's short name ("Teams"); null uses `Title`. |
| `Description` | `string?` | `null` | One sentence under the chart saying what the metric counts; null leaves it out. |
| `Values` | `IReadOnlyList<double>?` | `null` | The daily values, oldest first; the last one belongs to `EndDate`. |
| `EndDate` | `DateTime?` | `null` | The day of the last value; null means today. |
| `ValueFormat` | `ExplorerValueFormat` | `Count` | How values are written (default `Count`). |
| `CurrencySymbol` | `string` | `"$"` | The currency symbol of the currency formats ("$", "€"). |
| `ValueFormatter` | `Func<double, string>?` | `null` | Writes a value (cards, tabs, readout, announcements); null uses `ValueFormat`. |
| `AxisFormatter` | `Func<double, double, string>?` | `null` | Writes a y axis label from the tick value and the step between ticks; null uses `ValueFormat`. |
| `ChangeMode` | `ExplorerChangeMode` | `Relative` | Whether changes are relative ("+1.6%", default) or differences in points ("+1.2 pts", for rates). |
| `IsHigherBetter` | `bool` | `true` | Whether a rise is good (green). False for costs and churn: a rise turns red, a fall green. |
| `MaxAxisDecimals` | `int` | `-1` | The most decimals a y axis step may have, in the units the labels show (millions for "$1.22M"); −1 (default) takes the format's: 2 for compact money and ratios, 1 for percentages, 0 for counts and full money. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### ExplorerRange

One window of the range switch: how many days the chart shows (against the same number of days before them), the button text, and the words the cards and the readout use for it.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Label` | `string` | `""` | The switch button's text ("30D"). |
| `Days` | `int` | `30` | The number of days shown (30, 90, 364); at least 2. |
| `CardText` | `string` | `""` | The span written on the cards ("30 days", "12 months"). |
| `CompareText` | `string` | `""` | The comparison after the readout's change ("vs 30 days ago"). |
| `AccessibleName` | `string?` | `null` | The spoken name of the button ("Last 30 days"); null uses `Label`. |
| `SparklineStep` | `int` | `1` | Days between the card sparkline's points (1 = daily; 7 = weekly, used by the 12-month range). |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### ExplorerValueFormat

How an `ExplorerMetric`'s values are written (cards, tabs, readout, y axis, announcements).

Derives from `Enum`: every member of `Enum` works as well.

### ExplorerChangeMode

How a change between two days is expressed.

Derives from `Enum`: every member of `Enum` works as well.

### MetricExplorerMetricEventArgs

Arguments of `MetricOpened`, `MetricClosed` and `SelectedMetricChanged`.

Derives from `RoutedEventArgs`: every member of `RoutedEventArgs` works as well.

### MetricExplorerRangeEventArgs

Arguments of `SelectedRangeChanged`.

Derives from `RoutedEventArgs`: every member of `RoutedEventArgs` works as well.

### MetricExplorerScrubEventArgs

Arguments of `ScrubChanged`: the inspected day, or none.

Derives from `RoutedEventArgs`: every member of `RoutedEventArgs` works as well.

## Accessibility

- Each card is a button named by its content: "Annual run-rate: $4.62M, up 1.6% over 30 days. Open chart".
- The tab strip is named "Metric" and the range switch "Chart range"; both are one tab stop that follows the selection.
- The chart is a slider named "Scrub" and the metric, whose value text is the inspected day with its previous-period
  counterpart ("Sep 6, 2026: $4.55M. Aug 7, 2026: $4.43M"). Focus draws a ring around the plot. Decorative parts (the
  sparklines, the axis, the legend) are hidden from assistive technology.
- Changing the metric or the range in the open chart is announced politely with the latest value and the change; closing
  the chart announces how many metrics are shown. Inspecting a day is not announced, because the slider already says it.
- Direction is always in words as well as color ("up", "down", "unchanged").
- Colors come from the theme tokens in light and dark; the line, dots and capsule keep their contrast on both.

### Keyboard

- **Tab** goes through the cards, then (when open) the selected tab, the close button, the selected range and the chart.
- **Enter / Space** on a card opens it and moves focus to its tab.
- **← →** on the tabs and on the range switch select the previous or next item at once and wrap; **Home / End** jump to
  the ends.
- **← ↓** and **→ ↑** on the chart step to the previous or next day and stop at the ends; **Home / End** jump to the first
  and last day.
- **Escape** clears the inspection first; pressing it again (or on any other control of the chart) closes the chart and
  returns focus to its card.

## Motion

- **Card to chart**: the card's surface travels and grows into the chart's rectangle on a smooth spring (about half a
  second) while the other cards drop away at once; the chart's content fades in with a small rise and blur, starting 120 ms
  into the flight. Closing runs it backwards: the surface shrinks into its card, the other surfaces fade back in, and the
  card contents rise in again (the opened card last). The block's height changes at once.
- **Range switch**: a camera over the daily data. One spring moves the number of days in view, and every frame the lines
  are rebuilt for that window, so the point count changes continuously while today stays pinned to the right edge; the y
  domain follows the same spring and the x labels slide with it. The label ladders (weekly, every two weeks, monthly)
  cross-fade as the old ladder leaves in 160 ms and the new one arrives in 240 ms.
- **Metric switch**: every point of the lines springs from where it is to its new place, so the curve flows from one
  metric into the next; switching again mid-way starts from the shape on screen. The y labels cross-fade one by one from
  the bottom, 35 ms apart. The readout lines rise and fade; the change digits roll like an odometer and the arrow turns.
- **Tabs and range switch**: the highlight glides on the same spring.
- **Inspection** appears, moves and disappears without animation.
- Reduced motion lands the surface, the lines and the highlights at once and keeps only 120 ms fades; Off applies
  everything at once.

## Related

- `Metrics dashboard`, `KPI drilldown` and `Revenue explorer`, the other Analytics blocks around KPIs.
- `SegmentedControl`, the range switch the block uses.
- `Cohort retention`, another block that morphs between views of one dataset.

# Revenue explorer

> Monthly recurring revenue as stacked new, expansion and churn layers with three headline numbers and an overview strip: drag its window or handles and the paths, axes and numbers slide to the new range, with range presets, series chips, a previous-period comparison and a crosshair readout for the pointer and the keyboard.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc.Blocks`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc.Blocks --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/blocks/revenue-explorer

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.RevenueExplorerPreviewDemo">
    <!-- Two years of invented subscription revenue; the newest twelve months show. Data: RevenueExplorerDemoData. -->
    <arc:RevenueExplorer x:Name="Revenue" Title="Subscription revenue" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class RevenueExplorerPreviewDemo : UserControl
{
    public RevenueExplorerPreviewDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Revenue.OpeningMrr = RevenueExplorerDemoData.Opening;
        Revenue.Months.AddRange(RevenueExplorerDemoData.Standard());
    }
}
```

## When to use

`RevenueExplorer` answers the monthly questions of a subscription business in one card: how much recurring revenue
(MRR) do we have now, how much did new customers and existing customers add each month, how much did we lose, and is
that better than the period before? The chart stacks new and expansion revenue above the zero line and draws churn below
it, so the net movement of a month is the distance between the layers. Under the chart an overview strip holds every month;
its window is the range the chart, the three headline numbers and the table show.

- **Revenue review pages.** The closing MRR, the average net new per month and the churn rate, each with its change, sit
  above the chart and follow the range.
- **Moving through time.** Drag the overview window to scrub through the history, or pull a handle to zoom in; the
  paths, the axis labels and the numbers slide there instead of redrawing.
- **Checking a trend against its past.** "Compare" draws the previous period of the same length as two dashed lines, and
  the readout adds the previous month's net new.

## When not to use

- **One metric over time.** A line chart (or the `Metric explorer` block) is lighter when there is no stack and no
  zoom.
- **A bridge from one total to another.** `MRR waterfall` shows how the opening MRR becomes the closing one.
- **Daily or hourly data.** The month is the unit here: the window has at least three months and labels are months.
- **More than a few years of months.** Thirty-six to sixty months work well; beyond that aggregate to quarters.

## Usage

The block derives from Avalonia's `TemplatedControl`. Its data is a list of `RevenueMonth`s, oldest first, one per
calendar month without gaps: `New` and `Expansion` (zero or more), `Churn` (negative; a positive number is taken as its
negative) and optionally the month's closing `Mrr`. Leave `Mrr` out and the block adds each month's net new to the
previous month, starting from `OpeningMrr`, the revenue before the first month. `OpeningMrr` is also the base of the
first month's churn rate and of the first change.

```xml
<arc:RevenueExplorer Title="Subscription revenue" OpeningMrr="1050000">
    <arc:RevenueMonth Month="2024-03-01" New="41200" Expansion="14800" Churn="-17600" />
    <arc:RevenueMonth Month="2024-04-01" New="43900" Expansion="15300" Churn="-18200" />
</arc:RevenueExplorer>
```

```csharp
revenue.OpeningMrr = 1_050_000;
revenue.Months.AddRange(months);          // or: revenue.MonthsSource = observableMonths;
revenue.SetRange(12, 23);                 // months 12 to 23, sliding there
revenue.ApplyPreset(3);                   // the newest three months, as the "3M" button does
```

`MonthsSource` takes a collection you own (an `ObservableCollection` is followed); changing a month's numbers in place
rebuilds the block. Until you choose a range the newest `DefaultRangeMonths` (12) show.

### Anatomy

- **Header.** `Title`, the range as text under it (`Mar – Aug 2026`; the first year is left out inside one year), and
  the range buttons on the right. The buttons select the newest 3, 6, 12 months and everything; when the range is
  anything else none is selected. Replace them with your own `Presets`.
- **Headline numbers.** The closing MRR with its change since the month before the range; the average net new per month
  with its change against the previous range of the same length; the churn rate (churned revenue over the opening revenue
  of the months) with its change in points. Values roll digit by digit, the arrows turn between up and down, and the
  texts rise out and in. A change whose base is missing (the first months, `All`) is left out. Churn going down is good
  and drawn green.
- **Toolbar.** Three series chips (`New`, `Expansion`, `Churn`) and the compare switch.
- **Chart.** Y labels left, month labels under the plot (January shows its year), and the layers.
- **Overview.** Every month as small layers, year ticks, the window with a handle on each side.

### The range

`RangeStart` and `RangeEnd` (month indexes, both included, two-way) are the range; `RangeChanged` reports every change
with its source: `Preset`, `Drag`, `Keyboard`, `Click` or `Api`. Dragging the window moves it one to one with the
pointer while the range is the nearest whole months, so the numbers change as it crosses a month; the chart chases the window
on a spring and, on release, the window settles on the whole month. A handle moves one edge and never comes closer than
`MinRangeMonths` (3) to the other. A click on the strip outside the window moves the window's centre there.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.RevenueExplorerLongHistoryDemo">
    <!--
        Thirty-six months and your own presets: the last quarter, half year, year, two years, and everything. The window
        opens on the newest two years; with so many months the axis shows every other label while they are close together.
    -->
    <arc:RevenueExplorer x:Name="Revenue"
                         Title="Subscription revenue, three years"
                         DefaultRangeMonths="24">
        <arc:RevenueExplorer.Presets>
            <arc:RevenueRangePreset Months="3" />
            <arc:RevenueRangePreset Months="6" />
            <arc:RevenueRangePreset Months="12" />
            <arc:RevenueRangePreset Months="24" Label="2Y" AccessibleName="Last two years" />
            <arc:RevenueRangePreset Months="0" Label="All" />
        </arc:RevenueExplorer.Presets>
    </arc:RevenueExplorer>
</UserControl>
```

### Series and comparison

`IsNewVisible`, `IsExpansionVisible` and `IsChurnVisible` (two-way) switch the layers: a hidden layer collapses to zero
and the layers above it fall, the y axis re-fits, and the chip's swatch empties. The domain follows the visible stack: its
top is 18% above the highest stack plus 8% of the deepest churn, and its bottom 20% below the deepest churn. With every series
off the axes stay and the chart says `EmptyText`.

`IsCompareEnabled` draws two dashed lines for the months of the previous period (the stacked new and expansion top, and
churn) and brings them into the y domain. In the readout a row adds that month's net new. Months with no previous period
(the first ones) have no dashes.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.RevenueExplorerCompareDemo">
    <!--
        Opened on the last six months with the comparison on: two dashed lines trace the six months before (the stacked
        new and expansion top, and churn). Point at a month to see the previous period's net new in the readout.
    -->
    <arc:RevenueExplorer x:Name="Revenue"
                         Title="Subscription revenue"
                         IsCompareEnabled="True"
                         RangeStart="18"
                         RangeEnd="23" />
</UserControl>
```

### Inspecting a month

Point at the chart: a crosshair and three dots mark the nearest month of the range and a panel shows the three series, the net
new and, when comparing, the previous period's net. The panel sits 14px right of the crosshair and flips to its left when it
would leave the chart; it glides between months and fades in and out. `ScrubIndex` (two-way) is the inspected month and
`ScrubChanged` reports it.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.RevenueExplorerEventsDemo">
    <!--
        The range, the series, the comparison and the inspected month are two-way properties and every change is an event.
        Here three buttons drive the block from outside and the log shows what it reports.
    -->
    <StackPanel Spacing="12">
        <StackPanel Orientation="Horizontal" Spacing="8">
            <arc:Button x:Name="Quarter" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Content="Show the last quarter" />
            <arc:Button x:Name="Churn" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Content="Toggle churn" />
            <arc:Button x:Name="Compare" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Content="Toggle compare" />
            <arc:Button x:Name="Inspect" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Content="Inspect the newest month" />
        </StackPanel>
        <arc:RevenueExplorer x:Name="Revenue" Title="Subscription revenue" />
        <TextBlock x:Name="Log"
                   TextWrapping="Wrap"
                   FontSize="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TypeXS}"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}"
                   Text="Events appear here." />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class RevenueExplorerEventsDemo : UserControl
{
    private readonly List<string> _lines = new();

    public RevenueExplorerEventsDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Revenue.OpeningMrr = RevenueExplorerDemoData.Opening;
        Revenue.Months.AddRange(RevenueExplorerDemoData.Standard());

        Quarter.Click += (_, _) => Revenue.ApplyPreset(3);
        Churn.Click += (_, _) => Revenue.IsChurnVisible = !Revenue.IsChurnVisible;
        Compare.Click += (_, _) => Revenue.IsCompareEnabled = !Revenue.IsCompareEnabled;
        Inspect.Click += (_, _) => Revenue.ScrubIndex = Revenue.RangeEnd;

        Revenue.RangeChanged += (_, e) => Write($"Range: months {e.Start} to {e.End} ({e.RangeSource})");
        Revenue.SeriesVisibilityChanged += (_, e) => Write($"Series: {e.Series} {(e.IsVisible ? "on" : "off")}");
        Revenue.CompareChanged += (_, e) => Write($"Compare: {(e.IsCompared ? "on" : "off")}");
        Revenue.ScrubChanged += (_, e) => Write(e.Month is { } m
            ? $"Inspecting {m.Month:MMM yyyy}: net new {m.NetNew:N0}"
            : "Readout closed");
    }

    private void Write(string line)
    {
        _lines.Insert(0, line);
        if (_lines.Count > 5)
        {
            _lines.RemoveAt(_lines.Count - 1);
        }
        Log.Text = string.Join(Environment.NewLine, _lines);
    }
}
```

### Words, formats and currency

Every visible word is a property with an English default (`NewLabel`, `MrrLabel`, `CompareText`, `SinceFormat`,
`VersusFormat`, the screen reader names, the announcement formats). Amounts are compact currency (`$63.3k`, `$2.56M`):
change the symbol with `CurrencySymbol` and the language with `CultureName`, or replace the text with `ValueFormatter`
(readout, table, announcements), `AxisFormatter`, `MonthFormatter`, `MonthYearFormatter` and `RangeFormatter`. The
headline numbers always follow `CurrencySymbol`: their digits roll, which needs the symbol and the unit as separate pieces.

## API reference

### RevenueExplorer

Revenue explorer: monthly recurring revenue as three stacked series, new and expansion above the zero line and churn below it, with three headline numbers (closing revenue, average net new, churn rate) and an overview strip of every month under the chart. Drag the overview window, or its handles, to zoom the chart: the paths, the axes and the numbers slide to the new range. The range buttons pick the newest 3, 6, 12 months or everything, the chips switch series on and off, "compare" draws the previous period of the same length as dashed lines, and a crosshair with a readout panel inspects one month for the pointer and the keyboard.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Title` | `string?` | `null` | The heading; null leaves it out. |
| `MonthsSource` | `IEnumerable?` | `null` | The months as a list you own (followed when it raises collection changes); it wins over `Months`. |
| `OpeningMrr` | `double` | `NaN` | Recurring revenue before the first month: the base of the first month's churn rate and of derived closing revenue. NaN when unknown. |
| `RangeStart` | `int` | `-1` | Index of the first month of the range (two-way). Negative until a range is chosen: the newest `DefaultRangeMonths` months. |
| `RangeEnd` | `int` | `-1` | Index of the last month of the range, included (two-way). Negative until a range is chosen. |
| `DefaultRangeMonths` | `int` | `12` | How many of the newest months show before a range is chosen (12). |
| `MinRangeMonths` | `int` | `3` | The fewest months the window can hold (3). |
| `IsNewVisible` | `bool` | `true` | Whether the new series is shown (two-way). |
| `IsExpansionVisible` | `bool` | `true` | Whether the expansion series is shown (two-way). |
| `IsChurnVisible` | `bool` | `true` | Whether the churn series is shown (two-way). |
| `IsCompareEnabled` | `bool` | `false` | Whether the previous period of the same length is drawn as dashed lines (two-way). |
| `ScrubIndex` | `int?` | `null` | The inspected month (crosshair and readout): its index, or null for none (two-way). |
| `RangeCommand` | `ICommand?` | `null` | Run when the range changes, with the `RevenueRangeChangedEventArgs` as the parameter. |
| `NewLabel` | `string` | `"New"` | The new series' name (chip, readout, table). |
| `ExpansionLabel` | `string` | `"Expansion"` | The expansion series' name. |
| `ChurnLabel` | `string` | `"Churn"` | The churn series' name. |
| `NetNewLabel` | `string` | `"Net new"` | The readout's total row and the table's net column. |
| `MrrLabel` | `string` | `"MRR"` | The first headline number's label (closing recurring revenue); also the table's last column. |
| `NetNewKpiLabel` | `string` | `"Net new per month"` | The second headline number's label. |
| `ChurnRateLabel` | `string` | `"Churn rate"` | The third headline number's label. |
| `CompareText` | `string` | `"Compare to previous period"` | The compare switch's text. |
| `EmptyText` | `string` | `"Turn on a series to see revenue"` | Shown in the chart when every series is off. |
| `SinceFormat` | `string` | `"since {0}"` | The text after the closing revenue's change; {0} is the month before the range. |
| `VersusFormat` | `string` | `"vs previous {0} months"` | The text after the other two changes; {0} is the number of months of the range. |
| `PreviousRowFormat` | `string` | `"vs {0}"` | The readout's comparison row while comparing; {0} is the previous period's month. |
| `PresetGroupLabel` | `string` | `"Range"` | The screen reader name of the range buttons. |
| `PresetNameFormat` | `string` | `"Last {0} months"` | The accessible name of a preset button; {0} is its number of months. |
| `AllPresetNameFormat` | `string` | `"All {0} months"` | The accessible name of the preset that selects everything; {0} is the number of months. |
| `SeriesGroupLabel` | `string` | `"Series"` | The screen reader name of the series chips. |
| `PlotLabel` | `string` | `"Inspect a month"` | The screen reader name of the chart (a slider over the months of the range). |
| `WindowLabel` | `string` | `"Selected range"` | The screen reader name of the overview window. |
| `StartHandleLabel` | `string` | `"Range start"` | The screen reader name of the left handle. |
| `EndHandleLabel` | `string` | `"Range end"` | The screen reader name of the right handle. |
| `TableCaptionFormat` | `string` | `"Monthly revenue movements, {0}"` | The screen reader table's caption; {0} is the range text. |
| `ChartSummaryFormat` | `string` | `"{0}. Closing {1}: {2}. Average net new per month: {3}."` | The chart's screen reader summary; {0} range, {1} closing label, {2} closing value, {3} average net new. |
| `RangeAnnouncementFormat` | `string` | `"Showing {0}"` | Said when the range changes by keyboard; {0} is the range text. |
| `ScrubFormat` | `string` | `"{0}: new {1}, expansion {2}, churn {3}, net new {4}"` | What a screen reader hears for the inspected month. |
| `CurrencySymbol` | `string` | `"$"` | The currency symbol of the default amount formats and the headline numbers. |
| `CultureName` | `string` | `"en-US"` | The culture of month names and numbers. |
| `ValueFormatter` | `Func<double, string>?` | `null` | Formats an amount in the readout, the table and the announcements; null gives compact currency ("$63.3k"). |
| `AxisFormatter` | `Func<double, string>?` | `null` | Formats the y axis labels; null gives compact currency with a true minus ("−$25k"). |
| `MonthFormatter` | `Func<DateOnly, string>?` | `null` | Formats a month on the x axis; null gives the short month name, and the year for January. |
| `MonthYearFormatter` | `Func<DateOnly, string>?` | `null` | Formats a month with its year (readout title, table rows, "since" text); null gives "Mar 2026". |
| `RangeFormatter` | `Func<DateOnly, DateOnly, string>?` | `null` | Formats the range under the title; null gives "Sep 2025 – Aug 2026" ("Mar – Aug 2026" inside one year). |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `RangeChanged` | `RevenueRangeChangedEventArgs` | Raised when the range changes (a preset, a drag, keys, a click or code). |
| `SeriesVisibilityChanged` | `RevenueSeriesChangedEventArgs` | Raised when a series is switched on or off. |
| `CompareChanged` | `RevenueCompareChangedEventArgs` | Raised when the comparison with the previous period is switched. |
| `ScrubChanged` | `RevenueScrubChangedEventArgs` | Raised when the inspected month changes or closes. |

Pseudo-classes: `:compare`, `:empty-series`, `:dragging`, `:compact`, `:tight`, `:stacked`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

### RevenueMonth

One month of revenue movement in a `RevenueExplorer`: what new customers added, what existing customers expanded by, what churned (negative), and optionally the month's closing recurring revenue.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Month` | `DateOnly` | `01/01/0001` | The month (any day of it; only the year and the month are used). |
| `New` | `double` | `0` | Recurring revenue added by new customers (0 or more). |
| `Expansion` | `double` | `0` | Recurring revenue added by existing customers (0 or more). |
| `Churn` | `double` | `0` | Recurring revenue lost (a negative number; a positive one is taken as its negative). |
| `Mrr` | `double` | `NaN` | The month's closing recurring revenue. NaN (default) derives it from the previous month plus its net new, which needs `OpeningMrr` for the first month. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Changed` | `EventHandler?` | Raised when any property changes. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### RevenueRangePreset

A range button of a `RevenueExplorer`: the last `Months` months, or everything.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Months` | `int` | `0` | How many of the newest months the button selects; 0 selects every month. |
| `Label` | `string?` | `null` | The button's text ("3M"); null derives it from `Months` ("3M", or "All"). |
| `AccessibleName` | `string?` | `null` | The button's accessible name ("Last 3 months"); null derives it from `Months`. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Changed` | `EventHandler?` | Raised when any property changes. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### RevenueRangeChangedEventArgs

Arguments of `RangeChanged`.

Derives from `RoutedEventArgs`: every member of `RoutedEventArgs` works as well.

### RevenueSeriesChangedEventArgs

Arguments of `SeriesVisibilityChanged`.

Derives from `RoutedEventArgs`: every member of `RoutedEventArgs` works as well.

### RevenueCompareChangedEventArgs

Arguments of `CompareChanged`.

Derives from `RoutedEventArgs`: every member of `RoutedEventArgs` works as well.

### RevenueScrubChangedEventArgs

Arguments of `ScrubChanged`.

Derives from `RoutedEventArgs`: every member of `RoutedEventArgs` works as well.

### RevenueSeries

The three series of a `RevenueExplorer`.

Derives from `Enum`: every member of `Enum` works as well.

### RevenueRangeSource

What changed a `RevenueExplorer`'s range.

Derives from `Enum`: every member of `Enum` works as well.

## Accessibility

- The chart is a slider named "Inspect a month" over the months of the range; its value text carries every number of the
  month ("Mar 2026: new $72.5k, expansion $31.5k, churn −$34.1k, net new $69.9k"), and its help text summarises the range,
  the closing MRR and the average net new.
- The overview window and its two handles are sliders ("Selected range", "Range start", "Range end") whose value text is
  the range or the month.
- The range buttons and the series chips are toggle buttons (pressed state); the compare switch is a switch. Each headline
  number reads as one phrase with its change in words ("MRR, $2.56M, up +42.3% since Feb 2025").
- A hidden table lists every month of the range with its movements and closing MRR, and follows the range.
- Moving the range or the readout with the keyboard is announced politely; the readout and the crosshair are hidden from
  screen readers because the same text is the slider's value.
- The focus ring is drawn 2px outside the chip, switch, plot area (radius 12), window (radius 10) or handle (square).

### Keyboard

- **Tab** visits the range buttons (one stop; **← →** change the range), the three chips, the compare switch, the chart,
  the overview window, the start handle and the end handle.
- **Chart:** focusing it opens the readout on the last month; **← ↓** and **→ ↑** step one month, **Home / End** jump to the
  ends of the range, **Escape** closes the readout and keeps the focus (the next arrow starts from the last month again).
  **Shift** does not change the step here.
- **Window:** **← ↓** and **→ ↑** move one month (**Shift** three), **Home / End** to the ends of the history; the width is
  kept. **Start handle:** moves the first month, never closer than three months to the last; **End handle** likewise.
- **Enter / Space** press the chips, the switch and the range buttons.

## Motion

- **Range changes** (a preset, a click on the strip, a key): the chart's x domain, the window, the handles and the month
  labels follow one Smooth spring and arrive together; the paths are rebuilt every frame (no path morph). The y domain
  springs too; new gridlines fade in after 50ms while sliding in, and removed ones fade out in 160ms. The range text, the
  headline texts and the deltas rise 0.45em out and in; the numbers roll; the preset pill glides on a Gentle spring.
- **Dragging**: the window follows the pointer exactly and the chart keeps chasing it; when released the window settles on
  the whole month with a Gentle spring (about half a second). The grip scales to 1.15 while pressed; the window border goes
  from the strong border to the muted text colour on hover and the accent while held.
- **Series**: each layer's thickness springs between 0 and 1 (Smooth) and its line fades with it; the empty text fades in
  after 120ms. The chip's swatch fills in 240ms and scales 1 ↔ 0.8 on a 580ms curve.
- **Compare**: one spring blends each dashed line from the current line to the previous period while it fades in (it stays
  opaque for the first 40% of the way back).
- **Readout**: the crosshair and the dots jump to each month; the panel fades in with a 0.97 scale in 160ms, glides on a
  spring and fades out again (the reference left the panel behind; this one leaves cleanly).
- **Reduced motion** lands every spring at once and keeps the short fades (readout, tick, text swaps as 120ms
  cross-fades). **Off** applies everything at once.

## Related

- `Metrics dashboard`, `KPI drilldown` and `Metric explorer`, the other Analytics blocks.
- `MRR waterfall`, the bridge from opening to closing MRR.
- `SegmentedControl`, the public range switch the presets are modelled on.

# MRR waterfall

> A recurring-revenue bridge from the start of a period to its end: floating bars for new business, expansion, reactivation, contraction and churn, a side panel that lists the accounts behind any bar, and period and unit switches that move every bar, tick and number on one spring.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc.Blocks`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc.Blocks --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/blocks/mrr-waterfall

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.MrrWaterfallPreviewDemo">
    <!-- A quarter of recurring revenue split into three months and the quarter itself. Data: MrrWaterfallDemoData. -->
    <arc:MrrWaterfall x:Name="Bridge"
                      Title="Recurring revenue bridge"
                      Scope="All tiers" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class MrrWaterfallPreviewDemo : UserControl
{
    public MrrWaterfallPreviewDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Bridge.Periods.AddRange(MrrWaterfallDemoData.Periods());
    }
}
```

## When to use

`MrrWaterfall` answers "where did our recurring revenue go this period?". The first bar is the revenue at the start, the
last bar the revenue at the end, and the bars between them float: each one starts where the previous step stopped, rising
for revenue won (new business, expansion, reactivation) and falling for revenue lost (contraction, churn). Above the chart,
the ending revenue and its change sit beside three ratios that finance teams ask for first: net revenue retention, the
quick ratio and logo churn.

- **Board and finance reports.** A month or a quarter in one picture, with the accounts behind each step one click away.
- **Revenue operations reviews.** Switch between months and the quarter to see which kind of movement changed, and use the
  percent-of-start unit to compare periods of different size.
- **Customer-success follow-up.** Select the churn bar to see who left and why, then select expansion to see who grew.

## When not to use

- **A trend over many periods.** The bridge shows one period at a time; use a line or area chart for twelve months.
- **Revenue that does not start from a known level.** Every bar depends on the starting revenue; without it use a bar chart.
- **Hundreds of accounts per step.** The panel lists the largest accounts and groups the rest in one row; it is not a table.
  Link from the row to an account list instead.

## Usage

The block derives from Avalonia's `TemplatedControl`. Its data is a list of `MrrPeriod`s. A period has the starting revenue
(`StartingMrr`), the number of paying accounts at the start and the end, its names and dates (`Label`, `LongLabel`,
`Caption`, `StartDateText`, `EndDateText`) and the `Movements` in bar order. Each `MrrMovement` has a `Kind`, a positive
`Amount` (the kind decides the sign), an `AccountCount` and the named `Accounts` behind it. The ending revenue, the net
change and every ratio are computed by the block.

```xml
<arc:MrrWaterfall Title="Recurring revenue bridge" Scope="All tiers">
    <arc:MrrPeriod Label="Q2" LongLabel="Q2 2026" Caption="Apr 1 – Jun 30, 2026"
                   StartDateText="Apr 1" EndDateText="Jun 30"
                   StartingMrr="286400" StartingAccounts="892" EndingAccounts="948">
        <arc:MrrMovement Kind="New" Label="New business" ShortLabel="New" CompactLabel="New"
                         Amount="39800" AccountCount="116" CountNoun="new customers" />
    </arc:MrrPeriod>
</arc:MrrWaterfall>
```

```csharp
bridge.Periods.AddRange(periods);
bridge.SelectedPeriod = periods[^1];
bridge.SelectedIndex = 5; // the churn bar
```

`PeriodsSource` takes a collection you own instead (an `ObservableCollection` is followed, and editing a period of the
shown list updates the block in place). With one period the period switch is hidden.

### Anatomy

- **Header**: `Title`, the subtitle (`Scope` followed by the period's `Caption`), and the period and unit switches.
- **Summary**: the ending revenue rolling digit by digit, its change since the start (arrow, amount and percentage, tinted by
  direction), and the three ratios.
- **Chart**: a value axis, seven bars with their labels, connectors that carry each step's end to the next bar, and a marker
  under the selected bar.
- **Panel**: the accounts behind the selected bar, or the previewed one.

### The axis and the bars

The value axis does not start at zero, because the steps would be invisible next to the totals. Its domain reaches 0.6 of
the bridge's span below the lowest level and 0.05 above the highest, and its step is the value from 1, 2, 2.5 and 5 times a
power of ten nearest to a sixth of that range. The first and last bars are therefore cut: a slanted break mark across each
shows it. Bars are 56 wide at most, or 56% of their band, and every edge sits on a whole pixel.

### Selecting a bar and previewing one

Click a bar, or press an arrow key, and the panel lists the accounts behind it: the largest `MaxNamedAccounts` (5) by
amount, then one row for the remainder. Each row has a bar for its share of the step. The start and end bars list the
`StartingBreakdown` and `EndingBreakdown` instead (plan tiers) without a remainder row. `SelectedIndex` is two-way, survives a
change of period and unit, and raises `SelectionChanged` and `SelectionCommand`.

With a mouse, pointing at a bar previews its list without selecting it: the bar gets a plate, the other bars and labels fade,
and the hint changes to say that a click keeps the list. `HoveredIndex` reports it. Touch only selects.

### Period and unit

`SelectedPeriod` and `ValueMode` are two-way. Changing either moves the bars, the connectors, the axis, the labels and the
panel rows together: see Motion.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.MrrWaterfallPercentDemo">
    <!--
        ValueMode starts as PercentOfStart: the start bar is 100%, steps are shares of it, the panel shows two decimals.
        The headline always stays in currency.
    -->
    <arc:MrrWaterfall x:Name="Bridge"
                      Title="Recurring revenue bridge"
                      Scope="All tiers"
                      ValueMode="PercentOfStart" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class MrrWaterfallPercentDemo : UserControl
{
    public MrrWaterfallPercentDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Bridge.Periods.AddRange(MrrWaterfallDemoData.Periods());
    }
}
```

In `PercentOfStart` every value is a share of the period's starting revenue, so the start bar is 100%. The headline stays in
currency. The ticks, labels and panel amounts follow the unit.

### Words, symbols and formats

All text comes from `Labels` (`MrrWaterfallLabels`): switch names, headline labels, panel hints, the sentences read to
screen readers. `CurrencySymbol` changes the symbol everywhere; `CurrencyFormatter`, `CompactFormatter` and
`PercentFormatter` replace the number formats of the chart and the spoken texts. Numbers that roll use the symbol and
the built-in formats.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"

             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.MrrWaterfallSinglePeriodDemo">
    <!--
        One period of a different product: the period switch disappears by itself, the unit switch is hidden too, and the
        euro symbol replaces the dollar. The quarter lost more than it won, so the headline change points down.
    -->
    <arc:MrrWaterfall x:Name="Bridge"
                      Title="Legacy plan revenue"
                      Scope="Legacy plans"
                      CurrencySymbol="€"
                      IsValueModeSwitchVisible="False"
                      MaxNamedAccounts="3" />
</UserControl>
```

### Narrow containers

The block reads its own width. Under 800 the panel moves under the chart; under 560 the headline and the statistics shrink and
the statistics share the row; when a band is narrower than 72 the bar names shorten to `CompactLabel` and the bar labels lose
the currency symbol; under 48 the names use 10px type.

```xml

        statistics shrink, bar names shorten and the labels lose the currency symbol.
```

### Events

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.MrrWaterfallEventsDemo">
    <!--
        The period, the unit and the selected bar are two-way properties and every change is an event. Buttons drive the
        block from outside; the log shows what it reports. Formatters and words are replaced to show the hooks.
    -->
    <StackPanel Spacing="12">
        <StackPanel Orientation="Horizontal" Spacing="8">
            <arc:Button x:Name="Churn" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Content="Select churn" />
            <arc:Button x:Name="Wrap" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Content="Select the next bar (wraps)" />
            <arc:Button x:Name="Percent" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Content="Toggle unit" />
        </StackPanel>
        <arc:MrrWaterfall x:Name="Bridge"
                          Title="Recurring revenue bridge"
                          Scope="All tiers" />
        <TextBlock x:Name="Log"
                   TextWrapping="Wrap"
                   FontSize="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TypeXS}"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}"
                   Text="Events appear here." />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class MrrWaterfallEventsDemo : UserControl
{
    private readonly List<string> _lines = new();

    public MrrWaterfallEventsDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Bridge.Periods.AddRange(MrrWaterfallDemoData.Periods());
        Bridge.Labels.Hint = "Click a bar, or press an arrow key, to open its accounts";

        Churn.Click += (_, _) => Bridge.Select(5);
        Wrap.Click += (_, _) => Bridge.Select((Bridge.SelectedIndex + 1) % 7);
        Percent.Click += (_, _) => Bridge.ValueMode =
            Bridge.ValueMode == MrrValueMode.Currency ? MrrValueMode.PercentOfStart : MrrValueMode.Currency;

        Bridge.SelectionChanged += (_, e) => Write($"Bar {e.OldIndex} → {e.NewIndex}: {e.Name}" +
                                                    (e.Movement is { } m ? $" ({m.Kind}, {m.Accounts.Count} named accounts)" : " (a total)"));
        Bridge.PeriodChanged += (_, e) => Write($"Period: {e.OldPeriod?.Label} → {e.NewPeriod?.Label}");
        Bridge.ValueModeChanged += (_, e) => Write($"Unit: {e.OldMode} → {e.NewMode}");
    }

    private void Write(string line)
    {
        _lines.Insert(0, line);
        if (_lines.Count > 5)
        {
            _lines.RemoveAt(_lines.Count - 1);
        }
        Log.Text = string.Join(Environment.NewLine, _lines);
    }
}
```

## API reference

### MrrWaterfall

MRR waterfall: how recurring revenue moved over a period, as a bridge. One bar stands for the revenue at the start, five floating bars add or take away (new business, expansion, reactivation, contraction, churn) and the last bar is the revenue at the end. Above the chart the ending revenue rolls to its new value with the change since the start, beside net revenue retention, the quick ratio and logo churn. Select a bar, with the pointer or the arrow keys, to list the accounts behind it in the side panel; point at a bar to preview its list. Switching the period or the unit (currency or percent of the start) moves bars, axis, labels, rows and numbers together on one spring.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Title` | `string?` | `null` | The heading; null leaves it out. |
| `Scope` | `string?` | `null` | The first part of the line under the heading (what the numbers cover, "All tiers"); the period's caption follows it. |
| `PeriodsSource` | `IEnumerable?` | `null` | The periods as a list you own (followed when it raises collection changes); it wins over `Periods`. |
| `SelectedPeriod` | `MrrPeriod?` | `null` | The period shown (two-way); null shows the last one. |
| `ValueMode` | `MrrValueMode` | `Currency` | Whether amounts are currency or percent of the starting revenue (two-way). |
| `SelectedIndex` | `int` | `1` | The selected bar (two-way): 0 is the start bar, 1 the first movement, and the last bar is the end. Default 1. |
| `HoveredIndex` | `int` | – | *Read-only.* The bar under the mouse pointer (read-only), or -1. Touch does not preview. |
| `CurrencySymbol` | `string` | `"$"` | The currency symbol of every amount ("$"). |
| `CurrencyFormatter` | `Func<double, string>?` | `null` | Formats a whole currency amount in text (screen reader names, the table); null groups thousands ("$412,380"). Rolling digits use `CurrencySymbol`. |
| `CompactFormatter` | `Func<double, string>?` | `null` | Formats a currency amount on the chart's bar labels (signed for steps); null gives one decimal in thousands ("$412.4k", "+$55.8k"). |
| `PercentFormatter` | `Func<double, string>?` | `null` | Formats a percent-of-start value in percent units on the chart and in text (signed for steps); null gives one decimal ("+13.5%"). |
| `IsValueModeSwitchVisible` | `bool` | `true` | Whether the unit switch (currency or percent of start) is shown. |
| `IsPeriodSwitchVisible` | `bool` | `true` | Whether the period switch is shown (it is hidden for a single period anyway). |
| `MaxNamedAccounts` | `int` | `5` | How many accounts the panel names before the rest are grouped in one row (default 5). |
| `Labels` | `MrrWaterfallLabels` | – | The words of the block (switch names, headline labels, panel texts, announcements). |
| `SelectionCommand` | `ICommand?` | `null` | Run when the selected bar changes, with its `MrrSelectionChangedEventArgs` as the parameter. |
| `PeriodCommand` | `ICommand?` | `null` | Run when the period changes, with its `MrrPeriodChangedEventArgs` as the parameter. |
| `EndingMrr` | `double` | – | *Read-only.* The revenue at the end of the shown period. |
| `NetChange` | `double` | – | *Read-only.* The revenue gained or lost over the period (end minus start). |
| `NetChangeRatio` | `double?` | – | *Read-only.* The net change over the starting revenue (0.129 for +12.9%); null without a starting revenue. |
| `NetRevenueRetention` | `double?` | – | *Read-only.* Net revenue retention (0.977 for 97.7%): start plus expansion minus contraction and churn, over the start; null without a starting revenue. |
| `QuickRatio` | `double?` | – | *Read-only.* The quick ratio: new, expansion and reactivation over contraction and churn; null when nothing was lost. |
| `LogoChurn` | `double?` | – | *Read-only.* Logo churn (0.095 for 9.5%): accounts lost over accounts at the start; null without any. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `SelectionChanged` | `MrrSelectionChangedEventArgs` | Raised when the selected bar changes (pointer, keys or code). |
| `PeriodChanged` | `MrrPeriodChangedEventArgs` | Raised when the shown period changes. |
| `ValueModeChanged` | `MrrValueModeChangedEventArgs` | Raised when `ValueMode` changes. |

Pseudo-classes: `:stacked`, `:compact-summary`, `:compact-axis`, `:tiny-axis`, `:empty`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

### MrrPeriod

One period of the bridge ("Q2"): the revenue it started with, the five movements in bar order, how many accounts paid at the start and the end, and the split of the starting and ending revenue by plan tier.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Key` | `string?` | `null` | A stable id for the period (switch value, events); default is the label. |
| `Label` | `string` | `""` | The text of the period switch's button ("Q2"). |
| `LongLabel` | `string?` | `null` | The period's name in sentences and in the table's caption ("Q2 2026"). |
| `Caption` | `string?` | `null` | The date range in the subtitle ("Apr 1 – Jun 30, 2026"). |
| `StartDateText` | `string?` | `null` | The date the period started, for "since {0}" ("Apr 1"). |
| `EndDateText` | `string?` | `null` | The date the period ended, for "Ending MRR on {0}" ("Jun 30"). |
| `StartingMrr` | `double` | `0` | The recurring revenue at the start. |
| `StartingAccounts` | `int` | `0` | How many accounts paid at the start. |
| `EndingAccounts` | `int` | `0` | How many accounts paid at the end. |
| `StartingCountNoun` | `string?` | `null` | The words after the count when the start bar is selected ("paying customers on Apr 1"); null uses the block's text. |
| `EndingCountNoun` | `string?` | `null` | The words after the count when the end bar is selected ("paying customers on Jun 30"); null uses the block's text. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Changed` | `EventHandler?` | Raised when anything about the period changes. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### MrrMovement

One floating bar of the bridge: new business, expansion, reactivation, contraction or churn.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Kind` | `MrrMovementKind` | `New` | What the step does; it decides the sign, the color and which headline ratios it counts toward. |
| `Label` | `string` | `""` | The step's name in the panel and in announcements ("New business"). |
| `ShortLabel` | `string?` | `null` | The name under the bar ("New"); null uses `Label`. |
| `CompactLabel` | `string?` | `null` | The name under the bar when the bars are narrow ("Exp."); null uses `ShortLabel`. |
| `Amount` | `double` | `0` | The size of the step as a positive amount (the sign comes from `Kind`). |
| `AccountCount` | `int` | `0` | How many accounts the step covers. |
| `CountNoun` | `string?` | `null` | The words after the count in the panel ("new customers"); null says "accounts". |
| `RestLabel` | `string?` | `null` | The name of the remainder row; null uses the block's label. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Changed` | `EventHandler?` | Raised when a property or an account changes. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### MrrAccount

One account (or one plan tier) behind a step of the `MrrWaterfall`: a row of the side panel with its name, its amount, a line of detail and a bar for its share of the step.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Key` | `string?` | `null` | Identifies the account across periods so the panel can slide a kept row to its new place; default is the name. |
| `Name` | `string` | `""` | The account's (or tier's) name. |
| `Detail` | `string?` | `null` | The line under the name ("May · Team, 24 seats"). |
| `Amount` | `double` | `0` | The account's contribution to the step as a positive amount (the sign comes from the step's kind). |
| `AccountCount` | `int` | `1` | How many accounts the row stands for (tiers); 1 for one account. |
| `IsRest` | `bool` | `false` | Whether the row is a remainder row (muted name); the block creates the remainder row itself. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Changed` | `EventHandler?` | Raised when a property changes. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### MrrWaterfallLabels

The words of a `MrrWaterfall`: switch names, headline labels, panel texts and the sentences screen readers hear. Every default is plain English; replace the ones you need.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `PeriodSwitch` | `string` | `"Period"` | The period switch's screen reader name. |
| `ValueSwitch` | `string` | `"Show values as"` | The value switch's screen reader name. |
| `CurrencyOption` | `string` | `"USD"` | The value switch's currency button; {0} is the currency symbol. |
| `PercentOption` | `string` | `"% of start"` | The value switch's percent button. |
| `EndingFormat` | `string` | `"Ending MRR on {0}"` | The headline's label; {0} is the end date. |
| `SinceFormat` | `string` | `"since {0}"` | The text after the headline change; {0} is the start date. |
| `RetentionLabel` | `string` | `"Net revenue retention"` | The first statistic's label. |
| `QuickRatioLabel` | `string` | `"Quick ratio"` | The second statistic's label. |
| `LogoChurnLabel` | `string` | `"Logo churn"` | The third statistic's label. |
| `StartBar` | `string` | `"Start"` | The first bar's name under the bar. |
| `EndBar` | `string` | `"End"` | The last bar's name under the bar. |
| `StartTitle` | `string` | `"Starting MRR"` | The panel heading of the start bar. |
| `EndTitle` | `string` | `"Ending MRR"` | The panel heading of the end bar. |
| `AccountsNoun` | `string` | `"accounts"` | The words after the count of a step without its own noun. |
| `StartingNoun` | `string` | `"paying accounts at the start"` | The words after the count on the start bar without a period noun. |
| `EndingNoun` | `string` | `"paying accounts at the end"` | The words after the count on the end bar without a period noun. |
| `RestLabel` | `string` | `"Remaining accounts"` | The remainder row's name. |
| `AccountCountFormat` | `string` | `"{0} accounts"` | The remainder and tier rows' second line; {0} is the count. |
| `OneAccountText` | `string` | `"1 account"` | The second line of a row that stands for one account. |
| `Hint` | `string` | `"Pick a bar, or use the arrow keys, to list its accounts"` | The hint under the panel. |
| `HoverHint` | `string` | `"Click to keep this list"` | The hint while a different bar is previewed under the pointer. |
| `PanelNameFormat` | `string` | `"Accounts behind {0}"` | The panel's screen reader name; {0} is the bar's name in lower case. |
| `BarsName` | `string` | `"Movements"` | The bar group's screen reader name. |
| `BarNameFormat` | `string` | `"{0}, {1}, {2}"` | A bar's name for screen readers; {0} name, {1} amount, {2} accounts. |
| `PeriodAnnouncementFormat` | `string` | `"{0}: MRR moved from {1} to {2}, {3} {4}"` | Said when the period changes; {0} period, {1} start, {2} end, {3} up or down, {4} change. |
| `UpWord` | `string` | `"up"` | "up" in sentences. |
| `DownWord` | `string` | `"down"` | "down" in sentences. |
| `SummaryFormat` | `string` | `"MRR bridge for {0}: starts at {1}; {2}; ends at {3}."` | The chart's summary; {0} period, {1} start, {2} steps, {3} end. |
| `ChartHint` | `string` | `"Arrow keys move between bars and wrap around. Home and End jump to the first and last bar."` | The chart's help text. |
| `TableHeaders` | `string` | `"Movement,Amount,Share of starting MRR,Accounts"` | The screen reader table's column headers, comma separated: step, amount, share, accounts. |
| `EmptyText` | `string` | `"No periods to show yet."` | Shown when there is no period. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Changed` | `EventHandler?` | Raised when a text changes. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

## Accessibility

- The chart is a focusable group named by a sentence that gives the period, the starting revenue, every step and the ending
  revenue, with the key hint as its help text. The focus ring surrounds the selected bar's column.
- Every selection is announced politely with the bar's name, its signed amount and its account count: "Churn, −$18,460, 79
  customers left". A change of period announces what moved.
- A hidden table lists the movement, the amount, its share of the starting revenue and the account count for each bar.
- The panel is named for the bar it shows ("Accounts behind churn"). The switches are named, and the headline reads as one
  phrase with its change in words, not only by color.

### Keyboard

- **Tab** moves through the period switch, the unit switch and the chart, one stop each.
- **← ↑** and **→ ↓** move the selection to the previous or next bar and wrap around from the last bar to the first. Moving
  selects, so the panel follows.
- **Home / End** select the first and last bar.
- In both switches the arrow keys change the selection and wrap.

## Motion

- **Period or unit**: the bar ends, connectors, labels and the axis domain share one critically damped spring and settle in
  about 600 ms. Labels count along ("+$21.9k" to "+$39.8k"). Ticks that stay slide with the domain; new ticks fade in
  (240 ms after 60 ms), dropped ones fade out in 160 ms while they slide. A change of unit replaces every tick.
- **Panel rows**: rows are matched by account. A kept row slides to its new place on the same spring, a new row fades and
  rises in (240 ms, 35 ms apart), a removed row fades out in 120 ms where it stood, and the share bars grow on the spring.
  Numbers in the rows roll digit by digit.
- **Selection marker**: a fast, non-bouncing spring (about 400 ms for the width of the chart); the bar name turns strong in
  160 ms.
- **Hover and focus**: other bars fade to 28% and labels to 32% in 160 ms; the plate appears at once.
- **Texts**: the subtitle, headline label, change text, panel heading and row details rise out and in (160 ms out, 240 ms in).
- Reduced motion lands everything at once except that dropped ticks still fade for 160 ms. Off applies every change at once.

## Related

- `Metrics dashboard`, `Cohort retention` and the other Analytics blocks.
- `SegmentedControl`, the switches the block uses.
