
## When to use

`CohortRetention` answers one question: of the people (accounts, workspaces, installs) who started in a given period, how
many were still active one, two, three months later, and is that getting better? Each row is a cohort, oldest first, and
each column a month since the cohort started. Newer cohorts have been measured for fewer months, so the heatmap is a
triangle; the size-weighted average row under it tells you what a typical cohort looks like.

- **Growth and customer-success dashboards.** Month 1 and month 6 retention at the top, with the change between the three
  newest and the three oldest cohorts, show at a glance whether onboarding work is paying off.
- **Comparing segments.** Plans, channels or regions as segments: switching repaints the triangle in a wave and rolls every
  number, so the difference between two groups is visible while it happens.
- **Shape and level together.** The heatmap shows the level of every cell; the curves show where cohorts flatten out and
  which ones fall faster than the average.

## When not to use

- **A single retention number.** Use a stat or a line chart when there are no cohorts to compare.
- **Funnels and conversion steps.** Steps that people pass in order belong in a funnel or the `Journey flow` block, not in
  months since start.
- **Hundreds of cohorts.** The block is designed for roughly 6 to 20 cohorts and as many periods; aggregate further (months
  instead of weeks) before showing more.
- **Daily figures that need exact lookups.** Retention tables with dozens of columns read better in a `DataGrid`.

## Usage

The block derives from Avalonia's `TemplatedControl`. Its data is a list of `RetentionSegment`s, each with its
`RetentionCohort`s, oldest first. A cohort has a `Label` ("Jun 2026"), an optional `ShortLabel` for narrow layouts
("Jun ’26"), a `Size` (how many started) and `Retained`, how many were still active in month 1, 2, 3 and so on. The number
of values in `Retained` is the number of months measured so far. Every rate, the average row and the headline numbers are
computed by the block.

```xml
<arc:CohortRetention Title="Space retention"
                     Subtitle="Team spaces still editing each month after creation."
                     FirstMetricLabel="First-month retention"
                     SecondMetricLabel="Half-year retention"
                     TotalLabel="Spaces created">
    <arc:RetentionSegment Label="All" Description="all spaces">
        <arc:RetentionCohort Label="Jun 2026" ShortLabel="Jun ’26" Size="412" Retained="{Binding June}" />
        <arc:RetentionCohort Label="Jul 2026" ShortLabel="Jul ’26" Size="398" Retained="{Binding July}" />
    </arc:RetentionSegment>
</arc:CohortRetention>
```

```csharp
retention.Segments.Add(new RetentionSegment("Starter", starterCohorts, "Starter-plan spaces") { Key = "starter" });
retention.SelectSegment("starter");
```

`SegmentsSource` takes a collection you own instead (an `ObservableCollection` is followed). With one segment the segment
switch is hidden. Changing a cohort of the shown segment (its `Retained`, for example) updates the block in place.

### Anatomy

- **Header**: `Title`, `Subtitle` and the segment switch on the right.
- **Headline numbers**: the size-weighted average retention of `FirstMetricMonth` (1) and `SecondMetricMonth` (6), each
  with the change between the newest and the oldest `CompareCohortCount` (3) cohorts that reached that month, in
  percentage points; and the total that started, with the first and last cohort's names. Values roll digit by digit.
- **Toolbar**: the legend (the six heat steps with their thresholds, or the two line styles) and the view switch.
- **Chart**: cohort names and sizes on the left, the cells, the average row and the month axis.

### Heatmap and curves

`View` is `Heatmap` (default) or `Curves`, two-way. In the heatmap each cell shows its rounded percentage and a step of the
accent mixed into the surface: 8, 18, 32, 48, 66 and 86% from the lowest to the highest step, with steps starting at 20,
35, 50, 65 and 80% retained. The step uses the exact rate, so 79.8% reads "80" but keeps the fifth step. Change the
thresholds with `Thresholds` and the mix with `RampMix` (one more value than thresholds). Steps of 50% or more mix draw
their numbers in the accent's foreground color.

In the curves view, the y axis runs from 0 to 100%; each cohort is a thin straight-segment line and the average a thick
accent line on top, with a point per month.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.CohortRetentionCurvesDemo">
    <!-- The same cohorts opened on the curves view, Business plan selected; the size column is left out. -->
    <arc:CohortRetention x:Name="Retention"
                         Title="Space retention by plan"
                         Subtitle="One line per monthly cohort; the thick line is the average weighted by cohort size."
                         View="Curves"
                         ShowSizeColumn="False"
                         FirstMetricLabel="First-month retention"
                         SecondMetricLabel="Half-year retention"
                         TotalLabel="Spaces created"
                         TotalContextFormat="Created {0} – {1}"
                         AxisTitle="Months since creation"
                         StillActiveText="Still editing" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class CohortRetentionCurvesDemo : UserControl
{
    public CohortRetentionCurvesDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Retention.Segments.AddRange(CohortRetentionDemoData.SpaceSegments());
        Retention.SelectSegment("business");
    }
}
```

### Inspecting a cell

Point at a cell (or a point in the curves view) to inspect it: a box marks the cell, the rest of the chart outside its row
and column fades, the row's name and the month number turn strong, and a card beside the cell gives the exact rate, how
many were still active out of how many started, and the difference from that month's average. On the average row the
card says how many cohorts the average covers. In the curves view the nearest month is found from x and the nearest
point of that month from y, a crosshair runs to the y axis with the exact value in a tag, and the cohort's line darkens
while the others fade.

`CursorCell` holds the inspected `CohortCell` (two-way, null for none), and `CursorChanged` reports every change with the
cohort, the rate and the counts. A click, or Enter or Space, raises `CellInvoked` and runs `CellCommand`: use it to
open the cohort's people or a detail page.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.CohortRetentionEventsDemo">
    <!--
        The view, the segment and the cursor are two-way properties and every change is an event. Here two buttons drive
        the block from outside, and the log shows what the block reports: cursor moves, clicked cells (Enter or Space on
        the keyboard), view and segment changes.
    -->
    <StackPanel Spacing="12">
        <StackPanel Orientation="Horizontal" Spacing="8">
            <arc:Button x:Name="Toggle" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Content="Switch view" />
            <arc:Button x:Name="Newest" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Content="Inspect the newest cohort" />
        </StackPanel>
        <arc:CohortRetention x:Name="Retention"
                             Title="Space retention"
                             Subtitle="Point at a cell, click it, or use the arrow keys."
                             FirstMetricLabel="First-month retention"
                             SecondMetricLabel="Half-year retention"
                             TotalLabel="Spaces created" />
        <TextBlock x:Name="Log"
                   TextWrapping="Wrap"
                   FontSize="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TypeXS}"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}"
                   Text="Events appear here." />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class CohortRetentionEventsDemo : UserControl
{
    private readonly List<string> _lines = new();

    public CohortRetentionEventsDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Retention.Segments.AddRange(CohortRetentionDemoData.SpaceSegments());

        Toggle.Click += (_, _) => Retention.View =
            Retention.View == CohortRetentionView.Heatmap ? CohortRetentionView.Curves : CohortRetentionView.Heatmap;
        Newest.Click += (_, _) => Retention.CursorCell = new CohortCell(Retention.EffectiveSegments[0].Cohorts.Count - 1, 0);

        Retention.CursorChanged += (_, e) => Write(e.Cell is { } cell
            ? $"Cursor: {CellName(e)} month {cell.Month}, {e.Rate:P1} ({e.Retained:N0} of {e.Size:N0})"
            : "Cursor cleared");
        Retention.CellInvoked += (_, e) => Write($"Invoked: {CellName(e)} month {e.Cell?.Month}");
        Retention.ViewChanged += (_, e) => Write($"View: {e.OldView} → {e.NewView}");
        Retention.SegmentChanged += (_, e) => Write($"Segment: {e.OldSegment?.Label} → {e.NewSegment?.Label}");
    }

    private static string CellName(CohortCellEventArgs e) => e.Cohort?.Label ?? $"average of {e.CoveredCohorts} cohorts";

    private void Write(string line)
    {
        _lines.Insert(0, line);
        if (_lines.Count > 5)
        {
            _lines.RemoveAt(_lines.Count - 1);
        }
        Log.Text = string.Join(Environment.NewLine, _lines);
    }
}
```

### Weeks, other periods, other thresholds

Nothing in the block is tied to months: the number of columns follows the longest cohort (or `Months`), and every text that
names the period is a property (`MonthFormat`, `MetricLabelFormat`, `AxisTitle`, `AxisTitleShort`, the announcement
formats).

```csharp
retention.Thresholds = [0.10, 0.25, 0.40, 0.55, 0.70];
retention.MonthFormat = "Week {0}";
retention.MetricLabelFormat = "Week {0} retention";
```

### Narrow containers

The block reads its own width, not the window's. Under 600 the chart switches to a compact geometry: short cohort names,
no size column, 24px rows, and the axis title "Month"; when a column is narrower than 32 the numbers leave the cells.
Under 560 the paddings tighten to 16 and the segment switch moves under the titles. Under 440 the headline numbers stack,
one per row with the value on the right, and the view switch moves above the legend. The headline values scale with the
block's width between 22 and 28.

```xml

        chart uses short cohort names and smaller rows, and the numbers leave the cells once the columns get too thin.
    -->
    <Border Width="400"
            HorizontalAlignment="Left"
            BorderThickness="1"
```

### Formats and words

`PercentFormatter` (a rate from 0 to 1), `CountFormatter` and `DeltaFormatter` (percentage points) replace the default
"48.5%", "5,199" and "+5.2 pts". Every visible word is a property with an English default: the headline labels, the
legend texts, the card's row labels (`StillActiveText`, `VsAverageText`, `WeightedOverText`), the switch buttons and
their names, the empty text and the announcements. `ShowSizeColumn` and `ShowAverageRow` hide the size column and the
average row (and the average line).

## API reference

### CohortRetention

Cohort retention: how many of each starting group (a month of sign-ups, new workspaces, new customers) were still active in each month after they started. One dataset, two views: a heatmap triangle (one row per cohort, darker where more stayed, with the size-weighted average row under it) and retention curves (one line per cohort and the average); the cells shrink into points and the rows unfold into lines when the view changes. Above the chart, three headline numbers: two months' average retention with the change between the newest and the oldest cohorts, and the total that started. A segment switch filters the whole block (all, one plan, one channel): every number rolls and every cell repaints in a wave from the top-left corner. Point at a cell, or use the arrow keys, for its exact numbers.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Title` | `string?` | `null` | The heading; null leaves it out. |
| `Subtitle` | `string?` | `null` | The line under the heading (what is counted, data through when); null leaves it out. |
| `SegmentsSource` | `IEnumerable?` | `null` | The segments as a list you own (followed when it raises collection changes); it wins over `Segments`. |
| `SelectedSegment` | `RetentionSegment?` | `null` | The segment shown (two-way); null shows the first one. |
| `View` | `CohortRetentionView` | `Heatmap` | Heatmap or curves (two-way). Default heatmap. |
| `CursorCell` | `CohortCell?` | `null` | The inspected cell (pointer or keys; two-way): cursor box or ring, dimming, card. Null for none. |
| `Months` | `int` | `0` | How many month columns to draw; 0 (default) takes the longest cohort. |
| `Thresholds` | `IReadOnlyList<double>?` | `null` | Where the heat steps begin (rates 0–1, ascending); null uses 0.20, 0.35, 0.50, 0.65 and 0.80 (six steps). |
| `RampMix` | `IReadOnlyList<double>?` | `null` | How much of the accent each step mixes into the surface (0–1, one more than `Thresholds`); null uses 8, 18, 32, 48, 66 and 86%. Steps of 50% or more take the accent's foreground for their numbers. |
| `FirstMetricMonth` | `int` | `1` | The month of the first headline number (default 1). |
| `SecondMetricMonth` | `int` | `6` | The month of the second headline number (default 6). |
| `CompareCohortCount` | `int` | `3` | How many of the newest and the oldest cohorts the headline changes compare (default 3). |
| `ShowSizeColumn` | `bool` | `true` | Whether the heatmap shows each cohort's size beside its name (wide layouts only). |
| `ShowAverageRow` | `bool` | `true` | Whether the size-weighted average row (and the average curve) is drawn. |
| `PercentFormatter` | `Func<double, string>?` | `null` | Formats a rate (0–1) for the headline numbers, the card and the y tag; null gives one decimal ("48.5%"). |
| `CountFormatter` | `Func<double, string>?` | `null` | Formats counts (sizes, the total, "a of b"); null groups thousands ("5,199"). |
| `DeltaFormatter` | `Func<double, string>?` | `null` | Formats a change in percentage points; null gives a signed one-decimal value ("+5.2 pts", "−2.2 pts"). |
| `FirstMetricLabel` | `string?` | `null` | The first headline's label; null formats `MetricLabelFormat` with `FirstMetricMonth`. |
| `SecondMetricLabel` | `string?` | `null` | The second headline's label; null formats `MetricLabelFormat` with `SecondMetricMonth`. |
| `MetricLabelFormat` | `string` | `"Month {0} retention"` | The headline label of a month; {0} is the month. |
| `TotalLabel` | `string` | `"Started"` | The third headline's label (everyone who started). |
| `CompareFormat` | `string` | `"newest {0} vs oldest {0} cohorts"` | The muted text after a headline change; {0} is `CompareCohortCount`. |
| `TotalContextFormat` | `string` | `"{0} to {1}"` | The text under the total; {0} is the first cohort's name, {1} the last one's. |
| `AverageLabel` | `string` | `"Average"` | The average row's name. |
| `AxisTitle` | `string` | `"Months since start"` | The x axis title. |
| `AxisTitleShort` | `string` | `"Month"` | The x axis title in compact charts. |
| `LegendTitle` | `string` | `"% retained"` | The heatmap legend's title. |
| `AverageLegendText` | `string` | `"Average, weighted by size"` | The curves legend's text for the average line. |
| `CohortLegendText` | `string` | `"One line per cohort"` | The curves legend's text for the cohort lines. |
| `HeatmapText` | `string` | `"Heatmap"` | The view switch's heatmap button. |
| `CurvesText` | `string` | `"Curves"` | The view switch's curves button. |
| `SegmentSwitchLabel` | `string` | `"Segment"` | The screen reader name of the segment switch. |
| `ViewSwitchLabel` | `string` | `"Chart view"` | The screen reader name of the view switch. |
| `CohortTitleFormat` | `string` | `"{0} cohort"` | The card's title for a cohort; {0} is the cohort's name. |
| `MonthFormat` | `string` | `"Month {0}"` | A month's name in the card; {0} is the month. |
| `StillActiveText` | `string` | `"Still active"` | The card's first row label. |
| `OfFormat` | `string` | `"{0} of {1}"` | "a of b" in the card; {0} retained, {1} started. |
| `VsAverageText` | `string` | `"Vs average"` | The card's second row label for a cohort (its difference from the month's average). |
| `WeightedOverText` | `string` | `"Weighted over"` | The card's second row label for the average row (how many cohorts it covers). |
| `CohortCountFormat` | `string` | `"{0} cohorts"` | A number of cohorts above one; {0} is the number. |
| `OneCohortText` | `string` | `"1 cohort"` | One cohort. |
| `NotMeasuredText` | `string` | `"not measured yet"` | The screen reader table's text for a month a cohort has not reached. |
| `EmptyText` | `string` | `"No cohorts to show yet."` | Shown in the chart when the segment has no cohorts. |
| `ChartHint` | `string` | `"Arrow keys move between cohorts and months. Home and End jump to a cohort's first and last month. Escape clears."` | The chart's screen reader help text (how to use the keys). |
| `HeatmapAnnouncement` | `string` | `"Heatmap: darker cells kept more of their cohort."` | Said when the heatmap is chosen. |
| `CurvesAnnouncement` | `string` | `"Curves: one line per cohort and the size-weighted average."` | Said when the curves are chosen. |
| `SegmentAnnouncementFormat` | `string` | `"Showing {0}. {1}: {2}. {3}: {4}."` | Said when a segment is chosen; {0} the segment, {1} and {2} the first headline, {3} and {4} the second. |
| `CellAnnouncementFormat` | `string` | `"{0}, month {1}: {2} still active, {3} of {4}."` | Said for a cohort's cell; {0} cohort, {1} month, {2} rate, {3} retained, {4} size. |
| `AverageAnnouncementFormat` | `string` | `"Average of {0}, month {1}: {2} still active."` | Said for an average cell; {0} the number of cohorts, {1} month, {2} rate. |
| `CellCommand` | `ICommand?` | `null` | Run when a cell is clicked or Enter / Space is pressed on it, with its `CohortCellEventArgs` as the parameter. |
| `FirstMetric` | `double?` | – | *Read-only.* The size-weighted average retention of `FirstMetricMonth` (0–1); null when no cohort reached it. |
| `SecondMetric` | `double?` | – | *Read-only.* The size-weighted average retention of `SecondMetricMonth` (0–1); null when no cohort reached it. |
| `TotalSize` | `long` | – | *Read-only.* Everyone who started, over the selected segment's cohorts. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `CursorChanged` | `CohortCellEventArgs` | Raised when `CursorCell` changes (pointer, keys or code). |
| `CellInvoked` | `CohortCellEventArgs` | Raised when a cell is clicked, or Enter / Space is pressed on the cursor's cell (a drill-down hook). |
| `ViewChanged` | `CohortRetentionViewChangedEventArgs` | Raised when `View` changes. |
| `SegmentChanged` | `CohortRetentionSegmentChangedEventArgs` | Raised when the shown segment changes. |

Pseudo-classes: `:heatmap`, `:curves`, `:compact`, `:narrow`, `:stacked`, `:empty`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

### RetentionSegment

One segment of a `CohortRetention` (all customers, one plan, one channel): its own cohorts. The segment switch in the header lists the segments by `Label`.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Key` | `string?` | `null` | A stable identifier; optional. |
| `Label` | `string` | `""` | The segment's name on its switch button ("All", "Starter"). |
| `Description` | `string?` | `null` | What the segment holds, said when it is selected ("Starter-plan spaces"); null uses `Label`. |
| `Tag` | `object?` | `null` | Anything you want to carry along. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Changed` | `EventHandler?` | Raised when the segment, its list of cohorts or any of its cohorts changes. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### RetentionCohort

One cohort: people (or accounts, workspaces) who started in the same period, and how many of them were still active in each month after that. The number of values in `Retained` is the number of months measured so far, so newer cohorts have shorter rows and the heatmap becomes a triangle.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Key` | `string?` | `null` | A stable identifier (events, automation ids); optional. |
| `Label` | `string` | `""` | The cohort's name in wide layouts ("Jun 2026"). |
| `ShortLabel` | `string?` | `null` | The cohort's name in compact layouts ("Jun ’26"); null uses `Label`. |
| `Size` | `int` | `0` | How many started in the cohort: the denominator of every rate in its row. |
| `Retained` | `IReadOnlyList<int>?` | `null` | How many were still active in month 1, 2, … (one value per month measured so far). |
| `Tag` | `object?` | `null` | Anything you want to carry along (it comes back in the events). |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Changed` | `EventHandler?` | Raised when any property of the cohort changes. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### CohortCell

One cell of a `CohortRetention`: a cohort (or the average row) and a month since the cohort started.

Derives from `ValueType`: every member of `ValueType` works as well.

### CohortCellEventArgs

A cell of a `CohortRetention` with its numbers (cursor changes and invoked cells).

Derives from `RoutedEventArgs`: every member of `RoutedEventArgs` works as well.

### CohortRetentionView

How `CohortRetention` draws its data.

Derives from `Enum`: every member of `Enum` works as well.

## Accessibility

- The chart is a focusable group named by a summary (the view, the segment, the cohorts' range and the two headline
  values), with the key hint as its help text. The keyboard focus ring is drawn around it.
- Every cursor move is announced politely: "Jun 2026, month 3: 56.2% still active, 236 of 420." The average row says how
  many cohorts it covers. Escape empties the announcement.
- A view change announces what the view shows; a segment change announces the segment and the two headline values.
- A hidden table lists every cohort with its size and every month's rate (or "not measured yet"), with the average row
  last, so a screen reader can read the numbers without the chart.
- Each headline number reads as one phrase with its change in words ("up 5.2 pts newest 3 vs oldest 3 cohorts"), not
  only by color. The legend is named with its thresholds.
- The colors come from the accent and the surface in both themes; numbers switch to the accent's foreground on the dark
  steps.

### Keyboard

- **Tab** moves to the segment switch, the view switch and the chart, each one stop. Tabbing into the chart puts the cursor
  on the oldest cohort's first month.
- **← →** move the cursor along the cohort and stop at its first and last measured month.
- **↑ ↓** move between cohorts and keep the month, or take the cohort's last measured month when it has not reached it.
  **↓** from the newest cohort goes to the average row.
- **Home / End** jump to the cohort's first and last measured month.
- **Escape** clears the cursor; the focus stays on the chart.
- **Enter / Space** raise `CellInvoked` for the cursor's cell.
- In both switches **← →** change the selection at once and wrap around; **Home / End** jump to the ends.

## Motion

- **Heatmap to curves**: one master spring drives the morph; each part takes a slice of it, later along the diagonal
  from the top-left corner. The numbers fade, the cells shrink into points, the points travel from their rows to their
  rates pulling the lines open, the row labels fade out, then the lines and the y grid fade in, all within about a second.
  Going back plays the same slices in reverse: the last cells move first, and each cell moves before it grows.
- **Segment switch**: every value springs to its new rate, starting 9 ms later per diagonal step; the cells repaint in
  160 ms each time a value crosses a threshold, so a cell that climbs three steps repaints three times, and its number turns
  light or dark half way through. The headline numbers roll; the change texts rise out and in.
- **Cursor**: the box, ring and crosshair jump to the new cell; other cells fade in 160 ms; the card fades in where it
  appears (120 ms) and then glides to each new cell on a quick spring, and fades out in 160 ms.
- **Legend**: the old legend rises 6px and fades while the new one rises into place, 240 ms.
- Reduced motion lands the morph, the values and the colors at once and keeps only short fades (card, legend, change
  texts). Off applies everything at once.

## Related

- `Metrics dashboard`, `KPI drilldown` and `Journey flow`, the other Analytics blocks.
- `SegmentedControl`, the switches the block uses.
- `Activity terrain`, another heat map that morphs between two views.

# Usage forecast

> A billing cycle against a budget: measured usage and a dashed forecast with its likely range, a budget line you drag or step with the keys while the headline, tiles, red overage and alert chips react, and a metric switch that morphs every path.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc.Blocks`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc.Blocks --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/blocks/usage-forecast

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.UsageForecastPreviewDemo">
    <!-- Three metrics of one cycle, read on Jun 21: drag the budget line, press the arrow keys on it, switch the metric or toggle an alert. Data: UsageForecastDemoData. -->
    <arc:UsageForecast x:Name="Forecast"
                       Title="Usage outlook"
                       Subtitle="Harborline Studio · Growth plan · Renews Jul 1" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class UsageForecastPreviewDemo : UserControl
{
    public UsageForecastPreviewDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Forecast.PeriodStart = UsageForecastDemoData.Start;
        Forecast.Metrics.AddRange(UsageForecastDemoData.Metrics());
    }
}
```

## When to use

`UsageForecast` answers "will we stay inside the budget this cycle, and when will we not?". It draws the days of a billing
cycle left to right: what was measured up to today as a solid polyline, the forecast as a dashed one, and a cone around the
forecast that widens the further it looks. A horizontal line is the budget. Where the forecast meets it, a marker names the
day, and every part of every path above the budget turns red.

- **Billing and plan pages.** Usage, forecast and projected overage in one view, with a budget the account owner can move to
  see what a different limit would mean.
- **Alerts and limits.** The 50, 80 and 100% chips say when each threshold was or will be reached and let the person choose
  which ones notify them.
- **Several meters, one story.** Calls, storage and seats share the block: the switch morphs the same chart into another
  meter with its own axis, budget range, unit and price.

## When not to use

- **Spend without a forecast.** For a plain history of one number, use a line chart; this block's value is the forecast and
  the budget.
- **Many metrics at once.** The block shows one meter at a time. Compare several meters in `Metrics dashboard` or
  `Small multiples`.
- **Cycles of hundreds of days.** One vertex is drawn per day and the date labels sit a week apart; the block is made for
  cycles of about a month.

## Usage

Give the block its cycle (`PeriodStart`, `PeriodDays`) and one `UsageMetric` per meter. A metric holds the `Readings` of
days 1 to today, a `StartValue` (0 for a running total; leave it out for a level such as storage in use), the fixed value
axis, the budget with its range and step, the unit and the price of one unit over the budget. Today is the number of
readings unless `TodayIndex` says otherwise. The forecast and its range are computed from the last two weeks when you do not
supply them.

```xml
<arc:UsageForecast Title="Usage outlook" Subtitle="Harborline Studio · Growth plan · Renews Jul 1" PeriodDays="30">
    <arc:UsageMetric Key="events" Label="Events" Readings="{Binding EventReadings}" StartValue="0"
                     AxisMaximum="40" BudgetMinimum="8" BudgetMaximum="40" BudgetStep="0.5" Budget="26"
                     Unit="M" UnitPrice="150" PriceNote="At $0.15 per 1k events" />
</arc:UsageForecast>
```

```csharp
forecast.PeriodStart = new DateOnly(2027, 6, 1);
forecast.Metrics.AddRange(metrics);
forecast.SelectedMetricKey = "database";
```

`MetricsSource` takes a collection you own instead (an `ObservableCollection` is followed). With one metric the switch is
hidden, and a `UnitPrice` of 0 hides the cost tile. `Budget` is two-way on every metric and keeps its value when you switch
away and back.

### Anatomy

- **Header**: `Title`, `Subtitle` and the metric switch on the right.
- **Headline**: one sentence in four forms (the budget was passed on a day, the forecast reaches it on a day, it reaches it on
  the last day, it stays under) and a line under it with the time left and the likely range. They are rewritten while you
  drag, and only the words that change animate.
- **Tiles**: used so far with its share of the budget, the forecast for the last day with its range, and the overage cost
  (red above zero, with the price note under it).
- **Chart**: six value ticks over a fixed axis, dates a week apart, a "Today" line, the cone, the forecast, the measured line,
  alert ticks, the crossing marker with its date pill, and the budget band.
- **Footer**: the alert chips and the legend.

### The budget line

The whole 32px band around the line takes the pointer. A drag is relative (pressing off the centre does not make the line
jump), the value snaps to `BudgetStep`, and beyond the budget range the line keeps following but is squeezed, then springs
back when you let go. Every step recalculates the headline, tiles, chips and the crossing; `BudgetChanged` is raised for every
step with `IsCommitted` false and once more with `IsCommitted` true on release or after a key, which is the moment to save:

```csharp
forecast.BudgetChanged += (_, e) => { if (e.IsCommitted) Save(e.Metric.Key, e.NewValue); };
```

`BudgetCommittedCommand` does the same from a binding, with the new budget as its parameter. `SetBudget` moves the line from
code with the same spring.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.UsageForecastEventsDemo">
    <!--
        Everything the block reports is an event and the budget, the metric and the inspected day are two-way properties.
        Two buttons drive the block from outside; the log shows the events, with the budget saved only when it is let go of.
    -->
    <StackPanel Spacing="12">
        <StackPanel Orientation="Horizontal" Spacing="8">
            <arc:Button x:Name="Raise" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Content="Set the budget to 30M" />
            <arc:Button x:Name="Today" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Content="Inspect today" />
            <arc:Button x:Name="Clear" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Content="Clear the card" />
        </StackPanel>
        <arc:UsageForecast x:Name="Forecast"
                           Title="Usage outlook"
                           Subtitle="Drag the line, toggle a chip, point at the chart." />
        <TextBlock x:Name="Log"
                   TextWrapping="Wrap"
                   FontSize="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TypeXS}"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}"
                   Text="Events appear here." />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class UsageForecastEventsDemo : UserControl
{
    private readonly List<string> _lines = new();

    public UsageForecastEventsDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Forecast.PeriodStart = UsageForecastDemoData.Start;
        Forecast.Metrics.AddRange(UsageForecastDemoData.Metrics());
        Raise.Click += (_, _) => Forecast.SetBudget(30);
        Today.Click += (_, _) => Forecast.InspectedDay = 21;
        Clear.Click += (_, _) => Forecast.InspectedDay = null;
        Forecast.BudgetChanged += (_, e) =>
        {
            if (e.IsCommitted)
            {
                Write($"Budget saved: {e.Metric.Label} {e.OldValue:0.#} → {e.NewValue:0.#}");
            }
        };
        Forecast.AlertThresholdToggled += (_, e) => Write($"Alert {e.Threshold.Percent:0}%: {(e.IsEnabled ? "on" : "off")} ({e.Threshold.Status})");
        Forecast.MetricChanged += (_, e) => Write($"Metric: {e.Metric?.Label}");
        Forecast.InspectedDayChanged += (_, e) => Write(e.Day is { } day ? $"Inspecting day {day}" : "Card hidden");
    }

    private void Write(string line)
    {
        _lines.Insert(0, line);
        if (_lines.Count > 5)
        {
            _lines.RemoveAt(_lines.Count - 1);
        }
        Log.Text = string.Join(Environment.NewLine, _lines);
    }
}
```

### Alerts

`AlertThresholds` holds the chips; when you add none the block uses 50% (off), 80% and 100% (on). A threshold's `IsEnabled` is
two-way, its read-only `Status` is `AlreadyPast`, `Reached`, `Expected` or `NotExpected` and its `Date` the day. An enabled
threshold draws a tick where the line reaches that share of the budget, with its percent beside it. `AlertThresholdToggled`
reports each switch; the block never sends anything itself.

Read-only properties give the same facts to the rest of your page: `Outcome`, `CrossingDay`, `CrossingEarly`, `CrossingLate`,
`ProjectedTotal`, `ProjectedLow`, `ProjectedHigh` and `OverageCost`.

### Inspecting a day

Point at the chart, or focus it and use the keys, to get a crosshair and a card for the nearest day: its date, whether it was
measured or projected, the value, and either the share of the budget or the likely range. The card sits to the right of the
crosshair and flips to the left near the edge. `InspectedDay` is two-way (null for none).

### Narrow containers

The block reads its own width. Under 560 the paddings tighten, the switch moves under the titles, the chart is 232 high and
the tiles tighten; under 440 the tiles stack with the value on the right and every chip fills a row. The headline size follows
the width between 18 and 22.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"

             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.UsageForecastFlatDemo">
    <!-- Without a frame, in a narrow container: the block reads its own width, so the tiles stack and the chips fill their rows. -->
    <arc:UsageForecast x:Name="Forecast"
                       Width="380"
                       HorizontalAlignment="Left"

                       Subtitle="Harborline Studio · Growth plan" />
```

### Words, formats and dates

`IsFramed` false drops the card frame. `DateFormat` writes every date. A metric's `ValueFormatter`, `Unit`, `UnitSeparator`
and `CurrencyFormatter` control how values read; the tiles roll their digits from the decimals that `ValueFormatter` gives, so
it should return a plain number. Every sentence, label and spoken text is a property of `Labels`.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"

    <arc:UsageForecast x:Name="Forecast"

                       DateFormat="d MMM"
                       IsLegendVisible="False" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
            PassedDetailFormat = "{0}% over, heading for {1} by {2}.",
```

## API reference

### UsageForecast

Usage forecast: one billing cycle against a budget. Measured usage is drawn as a straight polyline up to today, the forecast continues dashed with a cone of likely range, and a horizontal budget line can be dragged (or moved with the keys) while everything reacts: the headline says when the budget will be reached, the three tiles show usage so far, the forecast for the last day and the overage cost, the part of every path above the budget turns red, a marker follows the crossing along the line, and alert chips (50, 80, 100% of the budget) report when each threshold was or will be reached. A switch changes the metric; every path, tick, number and word morphs to the new one.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Title` | `string?` | `null` | The heading; null leaves it out. |
| `Subtitle` | `string?` | `null` | The line under the heading (workspace, plan, renewal); null leaves it out. |
| `MetricsSource` | `IEnumerable?` | `null` | The metrics as a list you own (followed when it raises collection changes); it wins over `Metrics`. |
| `SelectedMetric` | `UsageMetric?` | `null` | The metric shown (two-way); null shows the first one. |
| `SelectedMetricKey` | `string?` | `null` | The key of the metric shown (two-way). |
| `PeriodStart` | `DateOnly` | `01/01/2000` | The first day of the billing cycle. |
| `PeriodDays` | `int` | `30` | The number of days in the cycle (default 30). |
| `TodayIndex` | `int` | `0` | Which day is today (1-based); 0 (default) takes the number of readings. |
| `InspectedDay` | `int?` | `null` | The day under the crosshair (two-way, 1-based); null for none. |
| `DateFormat` | `string` | `"MMM d"` | How dates are written (default "MMM d"). |
| `IsLegendVisible` | `bool` | `true` | Whether the legend shows (default true). |
| `IsAlertsVisible` | `bool` | `true` | Whether the alert chips show (default true). |
| `IsFramed` | `bool` | `true` | Whether the block has its own frame (border, radius 16, surface): the card version (default true). |
| `Labels` | `UsageForecastLabels` | – | The words of the block; assign a new `UsageForecastLabels` to translate it. |
| `BudgetCommittedCommand` | `ICommand?` | `null` | Run when the budget is settled (let go of, or moved with a key), with the new budget as the parameter. |
| `Outcome` | `UsageOutcome` | – | *Read-only.* How the shown metric stands against its budget (read-only). |
| `CrossingDay` | `double?` | – | *Read-only.* The day, as a fraction, where the line reaches the budget; null when it does not (read-only). |
| `CrossingEarly` | `int?` | – | *Read-only.* The earliest day the budget could be reached (top of the range); null when not (read-only). |
| `CrossingLate` | `int?` | – | *Read-only.* The latest day the budget could be reached (bottom of the range); null when not (read-only). |
| `ProjectedTotal` | `double` | – | *Read-only.* The forecast for the last day (read-only). |
| `ProjectedLow` | `double` | – | *Read-only.* The low end of the range on the last day (read-only). |
| `ProjectedHigh` | `double` | – | *Read-only.* The high end of the range on the last day (read-only). |
| `OverageCost` | `double` | – | *Read-only.* The cost of the forecast above the budget (read-only). |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `BudgetChanged` | `UsageBudgetChangedEventArgs` | Raised while the budget changes (every step of a drag) and when it is settled; see `IsCommitted`. |
| `AlertThresholdToggled` | `UsageAlertToggledEventArgs` | Raised when an alert chip is switched. |
| `MetricChanged` | `UsageMetricChangedEventArgs` | Raised when another metric is shown. |
| `InspectedDayChanged` | `UsageInspectedDayChangedEventArgs` | Raised when the inspected day changes. |

Pseudo-classes: `:compact`, `:narrow`, `:over-budget`, `:dragging`, `:framed`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

### UsageMetric

One metric a `UsageForecast` can show (calls, storage, seats): the measured readings of the cycle so far, an optional forecast, the fixed axis, the budget with its range and step, and how values and cost are written. The forecast and its likely range are computed from the readings when you leave them out.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Key` | `string` | `""` | A stable identifier (the switch's value, event arguments). |
| `Label` | `string` | `""` | The name on the switch, in the data table and in spoken summaries. |
| `Readings` | `IReadOnlyList<double>?` | `null` | The readings of days 1..today (a running total from the start of the cycle, or a level such as storage in use). |
| `StartValue` | `double?` | `null` | The value at the start of the cycle (day 0): 0 for running totals; null takes the first reading. |
| `Forecast` | `IReadOnlyList<double>?` | `null` | The forecast for every day after today (null computes it from the readings). |
| `ForecastLow` | `IReadOnlyList<double>?` | `null` | The lower edge of the likely range for every day after today (null computes it). |
| `ForecastHigh` | `IReadOnlyList<double>?` | `null` | The upper edge of the likely range for every day after today (null computes it). |
| `AxisMinimum` | `double` | `0` | The bottom of the value axis (default 0). |
| `AxisMaximum` | `double` | `NaN` | The top of the value axis; NaN (default) picks a round top that holds the data and the budget range. |
| `BudgetMinimum` | `double` | `NaN` | The lowest budget the line can be dragged to (default: the axis minimum). |
| `BudgetMaximum` | `double` | `NaN` | The highest budget the line can be dragged to (default: the axis maximum). |
| `BudgetStep` | `double` | `1` | The step a drag snaps to and an arrow key moves by (default 1). |
| `Budget` | `double` | `0` | The budget (two-way): where the horizontal line sits. |
| `UnitPrice` | `double` | `0` | The price of one unit above the budget; 0 hides the cost tile. |
| `PriceNote` | `string?` | `null` | The small text under the cost ("At $0.20 per 1k calls"). |
| `ValueFormatter` | `Func<double, string>?` | `null` | Writes a value without its unit; null gives one decimal. |
| `Unit` | `string` | `""` | The unit written after values ("M", "GB"). |
| `UnitSeparator` | `string` | `""` | What sits between a value and its unit ("" for "38M", " " for "640 GB"). |
| `CurrencyFormatter` | `Func<double, string>?` | `null` | Writes the cost; null gives whole dollars ("$1,449"). |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### UsageAlertThreshold

An alert threshold: a share of the budget the person wants a notification at.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Percent` | `double` | `100` | The share of the budget in percent (50, 80, 100). |
| `IsEnabled` | `bool` | `true` | Whether the alert is on (two-way). |
| `Status` | `UsageAlertStatus` | – | *Read-only.* Where the threshold stands against the current budget (read-only, kept up to date by the block). |
| `Date` | `DateOnly?` | – | *Read-only.* The day the threshold was or will be reached (null when it is not expected). |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### UsageForecastLabels

Every word a `UsageForecast` writes or speaks besides your data, with English defaults. Placeholders are numbered as described on each property. Assign a new instance to `Labels` to translate the block.

### UsageBudgetChangedEventArgs

Arguments of `BudgetChangedEvent`.

Derives from `RoutedEventArgs`: every member of `RoutedEventArgs` works as well.

### UsageOutcome

How a billing cycle looks against the budget (what the headline says).

Derives from `Enum`: every member of `Enum` works as well.

### UsageAlertStatus

Where an alert threshold stands.

Derives from `Enum`: every member of `Enum` works as well.

## Accessibility

- The chart is a slider over the days: its name is a full sentence (the metric, used so far, the forecast, the budget and the
  headline), its value reads "Jun 21: 22.9M used, 88% of budget" or "Jun 27 projected: 29.4M, likely 28.2M to 31M", and its help
  text says how to use the keys.
- The budget band is a slider over the budget with the value as text and the hint "Drag the budget line or press the arrow
  keys."
- The headline and its line are read through a polite live region when the budget is settled, a metric is chosen or an alert is
  switched; the animated words themselves are hidden from screen readers.
- Alert chips are toggle buttons named with their percent and status ("80% of budget, hit jun 19").
- A hidden table lists every day with its reading and range, projected days marked.
- The overage turns red and also says "Overage" and the amount; the red part of the paths is repeated by the headline.

### Keyboard

- **Tab** visits the metric switch (arrow keys change the selection), the chart, the budget line and each chip.
- Chart: **← →** (or **↓ ↑**) one day, **Page Up / Page Down** one week, **Home / End** the first and last day, **Escape** hides the card.
  Focusing the chart shows today.
- Budget line: **↑ →** one step up, **↓ ←** one step down, **Page Up / Page Down** five steps, **Home / End** the lowest and highest budget.
- Chips: **Enter** or **Space** toggles.

## Motion

- **Budget line**: moves on the snappy spring after a key and follows a drag with a stiff spring; the red clip follows it. Past the range the line is squeezed and springs back.
- **Crossing marker, alert ticks**: they chase the intersection of the displayed budget and the displayed line along the polyline; the date pill fades in and out and nearby date labels fade as it passes.
- **Alert ticks** draw themselves bottom up (700 ms) and are wiped the same way; their labels fade.
- **Metric switch**: every vertex of the measured line, forecast and cone springs to the new metric at once, the budget line and ticks ride with them, value labels cross-fade, tile digits roll, the headline swaps only changed words (160 ms out, 240 ms in, 40 ms apart) and chip statuses morph letter by letter.
- **Chips**: the check opens its slot on the quick spring and the width follows.
- **Inspect card**: follows the crosshair on a stiff spring, fades in 160 ms.
- Reduced motion lands every spring at once and keeps only short fades (120 ms for words). Off applies everything at once.

## Related

- `Metrics dashboard`, `KPI drilldown`, `Cohort retention`, the other Analytics blocks.
- `SegmentedControl`, the switch the block uses.

# Journey flow

> A journey as a Sankey chart: point at a step or a flow to trace that cohort through every stage, select a step to see where its people came from and went next, and switch segments to watch every flow morph.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc.Blocks`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc.Blocks --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/blocks/journey-flow

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.JourneyFlowPreviewDemo">
    <!-- October's course trials in four segments (all learners, then three channels). Data: JourneyFlowDemoData. -->
    <arc:JourneyFlow x:Name="Journey"
                     Margin="0,12"
                     Title="Trial to paid journeys"
                     SubtitleFormat="{}{0} visits in October, from first page to plan"
                     SegmentsLabel="Channel"
                     OverviewHint="Pick a step to trace where its learners came from and where they went"
                     GoalCaption="of visitors picked a paid plan"
                     OutcomesHeader="Plan at trial end"
                     CountFormat="{}{0} learners"
                     TableCaptionFormat="Flows for {0}, October"
                     AnnouncementFormat="{}{0}: {1} visits and {2} paid plans." />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class JourneyFlowPreviewDemo : UserControl
{
    public JourneyFlowPreviewDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Journey.TableColumnHeaders = ["From", "To", "Learners", "Share of step"];
        Journey.Stages.AddRange(JourneyFlowDemoData.Stages());
        Journey.Nodes.AddRange(JourneyFlowDemoData.Nodes());
        Journey.Segments.AddRange(JourneyFlowDemoData.Segments());
    }
}
```

## When to use

`JourneyFlow` shows how a group of people moves through a sequence of stages and where they leave. Stages run left to
right; each stage holds a step on the main path and, under it, the people who stopped there; ribbons between neighbouring
stages are as thick as the number of people who took that way. The goal in the last stage is green.

- **Funnels with exits.** Visit, sign-up, onboarding, activation, plan: the drop at every step is a visible ribbon, not
  only a percentage.
- **Comparing segments.** Channels, cohorts or months that share one structure. The switch over the chart morphs every
  bar, ribbon and count to the other segment, so the change itself is what people see.
- **Asking "who are these people".** Pointing at a step traces everyone who passed through it across the whole journey:
  where they came from and how they ended up. Pointing at a single ribbon does the same for the people who took that way.

## When not to use

- **Loops, skips or many paths.** Links only join neighbouring stages, and nodes stack in the order you give them. For
  journeys where people go back or jump ahead, use a graph view.
- **More than three nodes a stage.** Each node needs 44 pixels under the one above it for its label; four or five nodes in
  a column leave little room for the bars.
- **A single conversion rate.** A KPI tile or a small bar says "6% subscribed" in less space.
- **Exact numbers first.** The chart is for shape and proportion; the "Flow table" under it carries the exact counts, and a
  plain table is better when numbers are the point.

## Usage

The block derives from Avalonia's `TemplatedControl` and draws its chart itself. Give it the stages, the nodes (each with
the key of its stage) and one or more segments, each a list of links from a node to a node in the next stage.

```xml
<arc:JourneyFlow Title="Trial to paid journeys"
                 SubtitleFormat="{}{0} visits in October, from first page to plan"
                 GoalCaption="of visitors picked a paid plan">
    <arc:JourneyFlow.Stages>
        <arc:JourneyStage Key="landing" Header="Landing" ShortHeader="Land" />
        <arc:JourneyStage Key="trial" Header="Trial" />
        <arc:JourneyStage Key="plan" Header="Plan" />
    </arc:JourneyFlow.Stages>
    <arc:JourneyFlow.Nodes>
        <arc:JourneyNode Key="arrived" StageKey="landing" Header="Arrived" Description="Opened a course page" />
        <arc:JourneyNode Key="started" StageKey="trial" Header="Started trial" />
        <arc:JourneyNode Key="left" StageKey="trial" Header="Left" Kind="Exit" DropOffLabel="Left before the trial" />
        <arc:JourneyNode Key="subscribed" StageKey="plan" Header="Subscribed" Kind="Goal" />
        <arc:JourneyNode Key="lapsed" StageKey="plan" Header="Lapsed" Kind="Exit" />
    </arc:JourneyFlow.Nodes>
    <arc:JourneySegment Key="all" Header="All learners">
        <arc:JourneyLink SourceKey="arrived" TargetKey="started" Value="5320" />
        <arc:JourneyLink SourceKey="arrived" TargetKey="left" Value="11470" />
        <arc:JourneyLink SourceKey="started" TargetKey="subscribed" Value="1025" />
        <arc:JourneyLink SourceKey="started" TargetKey="lapsed" Value="4295" />
    </arc:JourneySegment>
</arc:JourneyFlow>
```

### Anatomy

- **Header**: `Title`, the subtitle from `SubtitleFormat` with the visitors count rolling in place of `{0}`, and the
  segment switch (shown for two or more segments).
- **Chart**: one column per stage with a guide line and the stage name under it; node bars 8 wide, stacked from the top 44
  apart; two label lines over each bar (name, then "count · share" of visitors); ribbons between stages. A node's count
  is the larger of what flows in and what flows out, so the first stage's total is the visitors. The scale is the same
  for every stage, so the fullest stage fills the height.
- **Side panel**: beside the chart from 860 pixels, under it below. With no selection it is an overview: the goal count
  and its share of visitors, the biggest drop-offs (exits before the last stage that nobody moves on from, with their share
  of the step before) and the last stage's outcomes. With a selected step it shows that step: its count, share of visitors,
  where its people arrived from and where they moved on to.
- **Flow table**: a disclosure under the chart that lists every flow with its share of the step it left.

### Node kinds

`Kind` sets the colours: a `Step` is drawn in the strong accent with flows into it in Accent at 10%; an `Exit` in muted grey
with faint flows (4%); a `Goal` in the success colour with green flows (16%). Exits are what the overview lists as
drop-offs, and goals are what it counts.

### Tracing and selection

Pointing at a step or its label, or at a ribbon, traces that cohort: the rest of the chart fades, every flow the cohort
took is covered by an accent band of its size, and the part of each bar the cohort makes up turns solid; labels of steps
the cohort never reached fade too. A tooltip follows the pointer with the count and two shares. Clicking a step selects
it: it stays traced while you point elsewhere, the side panel switches to it, and the selection survives a segment change.
Click it again, click the empty chart, press Escape or use the panel's Clear button to clear it. Clicking a ribbon does
not select.

`SelectedNode` and `SelectedSegment` are two-way. `SelectedNodeChanged`, `SelectedSegmentChanged` and `TraceChanged`
report the changes (the last one for the previewed node or link, pointer or keyboard), `NodeSelectedCommand` and
`SegmentSelectedCommand` run on user actions, and `GetCohort` returns the traced counts per link for your own summaries.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.JourneyFlowSelectionDemo">
    <!-- The selected step and segment are ordinary two-way properties; the buttons set them from code and the log shows the events. -->
    <StackPanel Spacing="12" Margin="0,12">
        <StackPanel Orientation="Horizontal" Spacing="8">
            <arc:Button x:Name="SelectHooked" Content="Select Hooked" Size="Small" Variant="Secondary" />
            <arc:Button x:Name="ShowSocial" Content="Show Social" Size="Small" Variant="Secondary" />
            <arc:Button x:Name="Clear" Content="Clear selection" Size="Small" Variant="Ghost" />
        </StackPanel>
        <arc:JourneyFlow x:Name="Journey"
                         Title="Trial to paid journeys"
                         SubtitleFormat="{}{0} visits in October"
                         SegmentsLabel="Channel"
                         GoalCaption="of visitors picked a paid plan"
                         CountFormat="{}{0} learners"
                         IsTableVisible="False" />
        <TextBlock x:Name="Log" Text="Point at a step or a flow, or click a step." TextWrapping="Wrap" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class JourneyFlowSelectionDemo : UserControl
{
    public JourneyFlowSelectionDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Journey.Stages.AddRange(JourneyFlowDemoData.Stages());
        Journey.Nodes.AddRange(JourneyFlowDemoData.Nodes());
        Journey.Segments.AddRange(JourneyFlowDemoData.Segments());

        SelectHooked.Click += (_, _) => Journey.SelectNode("hooked");
        ShowSocial.Click += (_, _) => Journey.SelectedSegment = Journey.Segments.First(s => s.Key == "social");
        Clear.Click += (_, _) => Journey.ClearSelection();

        Journey.SelectedNodeChanged += (_, e) =>
            Log.Text = e.NewNode is { } node ? $"Selected {node.Header}" : $"Cleared {e.OldNode?.Header}";
        Journey.SelectedSegmentChanged += (_, e) =>
            Log.Text = $"Segment {e.NewSegment?.Header}: {Journey.Visitors:N0} visits, {Journey.GoalTotal:N0} paid";
        Journey.TraceChanged += (_, e) =>
        {
            if (e.Node is { } node)
            {
                var cohort = Journey.GetCohort(node);
                Log.Text = $"Tracing {node.Header}: {cohort.Values.Sum():N0} learner-steps across {cohort.Count(c => c.Value > 0)} flows";
            }
            else if (e.Link is { } link)
            {
                Log.Text = $"Tracing {link.SourceKey} → {link.TargetKey}: {link.Value:N0} learners";
            }
        };
    }
}
```

```csharp

journey.SelectedSegment = journey.Segments.First(s => s.Key == "social");

{

    {
```

### Narrow containers

The block reads its own width, not the window's. Under 860 the side panel moves under the chart with its two groups side
by side; at 559 or less the switch spans the whole width, paddings tighten to 16 and the groups stack; at 479 or less the
labels get smaller. The chart never scrolls or rotates: it lays itself out again at every width, 404 high from a 720
pixel chart, 372 from 480 and 340 below. Under 600 the labels drop the share, and under 440 the top node of each stage
shows only its count while the stage names switch to `ShortHeader`.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.JourneyFlowNarrowDemo">
    <!-- 380 wide: the switch takes the full width, the panel moves under the chart, top nodes show only their count and stages use short names. -->
    <arc:JourneyFlow x:Name="Journey"
                     Width="380"
                     HorizontalAlignment="Left"
                     Margin="0,12"
                     Title="Trial to paid journeys"
                     SubtitleFormat="{}{0} visits in October"
                     SegmentsLabel="Channel"
                     GoalCaption="of visitors picked a paid plan"
                     OutcomesHeader="Plan at trial end"
                     CountFormat="{}{0} learners" />
</UserControl>
```

### Numbers and words

`ValueFormatter` formats every count (labels, tooltip, panel, table, spoken names), `ShareFormatter` every share given as a
fraction, and `LabelShareFormatter` the rounded share on the chart labels. The panel's numbers roll digit by digit even
with your own formatter: the text before and after the digits stays put. Every phrase is a property with an English
default: `CountFormat` ("{0} users"), `ShareOfFormat`, `VisitorsShareText`, `VisitorsCaption`, `GoalCaption`,
`OverviewHint`, `DropOffsHeader`, `OutcomesHeader`, `InboundHeader`, `OutboundHeader`, `JourneyStartText`, `JourneyEndText`,
`ClearText`, `TableHeader`, `TableCaptionFormat`, `TableColumnHeaders` and `AnnouncementFormat`. The tooltip's
"Share of …" row names the step everyone in the stage came through; set `JourneyStage.ShareBaseLabel` or
`JourneyNode.ShareLabel` to word it yourself.

With one segment the switch is hidden; `IsTableVisible` and `IsSidePanelVisible` remove the table and the panel.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.JourneyFlowTicketsDemo">
    <!-- One segment (no switch), three stages, no table; counts written compactly ("38.4k") by ValueFormatter. -->
    <arc:JourneyFlow x:Name="Journey"
                     Margin="0,12"
                     Title="Support tickets in May"
                     SubtitleFormat="{}{0} tickets opened"
                     CountFormat="{}{0} tickets"
                     VisitorsShareText="Share of all tickets"
                     VisitorsCaption="of all tickets"
                     GoalCaption="of tickets solved after a reply"
                     OverviewHint="Pick a step to see where its tickets came from and went"
                     IsTableVisible="False" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using System.Globalization;

{
    public JourneyFlowTicketsDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Journey.ValueFormatter = value => value >= 1000
            ? (value / 1000).ToString("0.0", CultureInfo.InvariantCulture) + "k"
            : value.ToString("0", CultureInfo.InvariantCulture);
        Journey.Stages.AddRange(JourneyFlowDemoData.TicketStages());
        Journey.Nodes.AddRange(JourneyFlowDemoData.TicketNodes());
        Journey.Segments.Add(JourneyFlowDemoData.TicketSegment());
    }
}
```

### Live counts

Changing a link's `Value` in the shown segment morphs the chart in place, like a segment switch. `StagesSource`,
`NodesSource` and `SegmentsSource` take collections you own (an observable collection is followed) instead of the
`Stages`, `Nodes` and `Segments` lists.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.JourneyFlowLiveDemo">
    <!-- Changing the counts of the shown segment morphs the chart, the labels and the panel in place. -->
    <StackPanel Spacing="12" Margin="0,12">
        <arc:Button x:Name="NextWeek" Content="Next week" Size="Small" Variant="Secondary" HorizontalAlignment="Left" />
        <arc:JourneyFlow x:Name="Journey"
                         Title="Trial to paid, this week"
                         SubtitleFormat="{}{0} visits this week"
                         GoalCaption="of visitors picked a paid plan"
                         CountFormat="{}{0} learners" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class JourneyFlowLiveDemo : UserControl
{
    private uint _week = 1;

    public JourneyFlowLiveDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        var baseline = JourneyFlowDemoData.AllLearners();
        var segment = JourneyFlowDemoData.Segments()[0];
        Journey.Stages.AddRange(JourneyFlowDemoData.Stages());
        Journey.Nodes.AddRange(JourneyFlowDemoData.Nodes());
        Journey.Segments.Add(segment);

        // Each "week" draws new counts around the baseline (seeded, so the sequence repeats), keeping every node
        // balanced: what leaves a step is split from what reached it.
        NextWeek.Click += (_, _) => JourneyFlowDemoData.Apply(segment, Balance(JourneyFlowDemoData.Jitter(baseline, ++_week)));
    }

    private static double[] Balance(double[] v)
    {
        // Pairs: 0,1 from arrived; 2,3 from started (= v0); 4,5 from learned (= v2); 6,7 from hooked (= v4); 8,9 from drifting (= v5).
        Split(v, 2, 3, v[0]);
        Split(v, 4, 5, v[2]);
        Split(v, 6, 7, v[4]);
        Split(v, 8, 9, v[5]);
        return v;
    }

    private static void Split(double[] v, int a, int b, double total)
    {
        var sum = v[a] + v[b];
        v[a] = sum > 0 ? Math.Round(total * v[a] / sum) : 0;
        v[b] = total - v[a];
    }
}
```

## API reference

### JourneyFlow

A journey as a Sankey chart: stages left to right, the people at each step as bars and the flows between steps as ribbons, with the people who leave below the main path and the goal in green. Point at a step or a flow to trace that cohort through the whole journey (where they came from, where they went) with a tooltip; click a step to keep it traced and read its details in the side panel (where people came from and went next); switch segments (channels, cohorts) and every bar, ribbon and count morphs to the new numbers. Under the chart, a "Flow table" lists every flow.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Title` | `string?` | `null` | The heading over the chart; null hides it. |
| `SubtitleFormat` | `string?` | `"{0} visits"` | The line under the heading; `{0}` is the visitors count, which rolls when the segment changes. Default "{0} visits"; null hides the line. |
| `StagesSource` | `IEnumerable<JourneyStage>?` | `null` | Stages used instead of `Stages` when set (an observable collection is followed). |
| `NodesSource` | `IEnumerable<JourneyNode>?` | `null` | Nodes used instead of `Nodes` when set (an observable collection is followed). |
| `SegmentsSource` | `IEnumerable<JourneySegment>?` | `null` | Segments used instead of `Segments` when set (an observable collection is followed). |
| `SelectedSegment` | `JourneySegment?` | `null` | The segment shown (two-way); null shows the first. |
| `SelectedNode` | `JourneyNode?` | `null` | The selected node (two-way): kept traced, detailed in the side panel, kept across segments. Null for none. |
| `HoveredNode` | `JourneyNode?` | – | *Read-only.* The node previewed now (pointer over it, or keyboard focus on it); null when none. |
| `HoveredLink` | `JourneyLink?` | – | *Read-only.* The link previewed now (pointer over its ribbon); null when none. |
| `Visitors` | `double` | – | *Read-only.* Visitors of the shown segment: the first stage's total. |
| `GoalTotal` | `double` | – | *Read-only.* People who reached a goal node in the shown segment. |
| `ValueFormatter` | `Func<double, string>?` | `null` | Formats counts (labels, tooltip, side panel, table); null groups whole numbers ("12,345"). |
| `ShareFormatter` | `Func<double, string>?` | `null` | Formats shares given as fractions 0–1 (tooltip, side panel, table); null shows one decimal ("31.7%"). |
| `LabelShareFormatter` | `Func<double, string>?` | `null` | Formats the shares on the chart's node labels (fractions 0–1); null rounds to whole percents ("32%"). |
| `SegmentsLabel` | `string` | `"Segment"` | Spoken name of the segment switch. Default "Segment". |
| `ChartLabel` | `string` | `"Journey steps"` | Spoken name of the chart (its node buttons form one group). Default "Journey steps". |
| `PanelLabel` | `string` | `"Step details"` | Spoken name of the side panel. Default "Step details". |
| `CountFormat` | `string` | `"{0} users"` | A count of people in the tooltip and spoken names; `{0}` is the formatted count. Default "{0} users". |
| `ShareOfFormat` | `string` | `"Share of {0}"` | The tooltip's share row; `{0}` is what it is a share of. Default "Share of {0}". |
| `VisitorsShareText` | `string` | `"Share of visitors"` | The tooltip's row for the share of all visitors. Default "Share of visitors". |
| `VisitorsCaption` | `string` | `"of visitors"` | Words after a selected node's share of visitors in the side panel. Default "of visitors". |
| `GoalCaption` | `string` | `"of visitors reached the goal"` | Words after the goal's share of visitors in the overview. Default "of visitors reached the goal". |
| `OverviewHint` | `string?` | `"Choose a step to trace who reached it and where they went next"` | The overview's note under its title. |
| `DropOffsHeader` | `string` | `"Biggest drop-offs"` | The overview's first group: the biggest exits before the last stage. Default "Biggest drop-offs". |
| `OutcomesHeader` | `string?` | `null` | The overview's second group: the last stage's nodes. Null uses the last stage's header. |
| `InboundHeader` | `string` | `"Arrived from"` | A selected node's first group: where its people came from. Default "Arrived from". |
| `OutboundHeader` | `string` | `"Moved on to"` | A selected node's second group: where its people went. Default "Moved on to". |
| `JourneyStartText` | `string` | `"The journey begins here"` | The line when a selected node has nothing flowing in. Default "The journey begins here". |
| `JourneyEndText` | `string` | `"The journey stops here"` | The line when a selected node has nothing flowing out. Default "The journey stops here". |
| `ClearText` | `string` | `"Clear"` | The label of the button that clears the selection. Default "Clear". |
| `TableHeader` | `string` | `"Flow table"` | The label of the button that opens the flow table. Default "Flow table". |
| `TableCaptionFormat` | `string` | `"Flows for {0}"` | The table's caption; `{0}` is the segment's header. Default "Flows for {0}". |
| `TableColumnHeaders` | `IReadOnlyList<string>?` | `null` | The table's column headers: from, to, count, share of the source step. |
| `AnnouncementFormat` | `string` | `"{0}: {1} visits and {2} reached the goal."` | What is announced when the segment changes; `{0}` segment, `{1}` visitors, `{2}` goal count. Default "{0}: {1} visits and {2} reached the goal." |
| `MaxDropOffRows` | `int` | `2` | How many drop-offs the overview lists. Default 2. |
| `IsSidePanelVisible` | `bool` | `true` | Shows the side panel. Default true. |
| `IsTableVisible` | `bool` | `true` | Shows the "Flow table" button and table. Default true. |
| `IsTableExpanded` | `bool` | `false` | The flow table is open (two-way). |
| `NodeSelectedCommand` | `ICommand?` | `null` | Runs when the user selects a node or clears the selection; the parameter is the node or null. |
| `SegmentSelectedCommand` | `ICommand?` | `null` | Runs when the user switches segments; the parameter is the new segment. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `SelectedNodeChanged` | `JourneyNodeChangedEventArgs` | Raised when `SelectedNode` changes (pointer, keyboard, Clear, or code). |
| `SelectedSegmentChanged` | `JourneySegmentChangedEventArgs` | Raised when `SelectedSegment` changes. |
| `TraceChanged` | `JourneyTraceChangedEventArgs` | Raised when the previewed node or link changes (pointer over it, keyboard focus on a node, or neither). |

Pseudo-classes: `:wide`, `:compact`, `:tight`, `:tracing`, `:has-selection`, `:empty`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

### JourneyStage

One stage (column) of a `JourneyFlow`, left to right: its name under the chart and the words the tooltip uses for the share of the stage.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Key` | `string?` | `null` | Identifies the stage (`StageKey`); defaults to the header. |
| `Header` | `string?` | `null` | The stage name under the chart ("Trial"). |
| `ShortHeader` | `string?` | `null` | A short name for narrow charts ("Wk 2"); null keeps `Header`. |
| `ShareBaseLabel` | `string?` | `null` | What a node's share of this stage is a share of, in the tooltip's "Share of …" row ("trial starts"). Null uses the nearest earlier node whose count equals the stage's total (the step everyone in this stage came through). |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### JourneyNode

One node of a `JourneyFlow`: a group of people at one stage (signed up, left, subscribed). Nodes stack in their stage in the order of `Nodes`; put steps first, exits after them and the goal first in the last stage.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Key` | `string?` | `null` | Identifies the node (links, `SelectNode`); defaults to the header. |
| `StageKey` | `string?` | `null` | The `Key` of the stage the node is in. |
| `Header` | `string?` | `null` | The node's name on the chart, in the tooltip and in the side panel ("Started trial"). |
| `Description` | `string?` | `null` | One sentence on who is in the node, shown under its name in the side panel when it is selected. |
| `Kind` | `JourneyNodeKind` | `Step` | Step, exit or goal. Default `Step`. |
| `DropOffLabel` | `string?` | `null` | How the overview's drop-off list names this exit ("Left before the trial"); null uses the header. |
| `ShareLabel` | `string?` | `null` | The node as the base of a share in the tooltip ("Share of trial starts"); null uses the header with a lower-case first letter. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### JourneyLink

How many people went from one node to a node in the next stage, in one `JourneySegment`. Links between stages that are not next to each other are ignored.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SourceKey` | `string?` | `null` | The `Key` the people came from. |
| `TargetKey` | `string?` | `null` | The `Key` they went to (a node in the next stage). |
| `Value` | `double` | `0` | How many people (0 or more; other values count as 0). |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### JourneySegment

One data set of a `JourneyFlow` (a channel, a cohort, a month): the same nodes with their own link counts. With two or more segments a switch over the chart picks one, and the chart morphs to it.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Key` | `string?` | `null` | Identifies the segment; defaults to the header. |
| `Header` | `string?` | `null` | The segment's name on the switch and as the side panel's overview title ("Search"). |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### JourneyNodeKind

What a `JourneyNode` stands for, which sets its colour and the colour of the flows into it.

Derives from `Enum`: every member of `Enum` works as well.

### JourneyNodeChangedEventArgs

Arguments of `SelectedNodeChanged`.

Derives from `RoutedEventArgs`: every member of `RoutedEventArgs` works as well.

### JourneySegmentChangedEventArgs

Arguments of `SelectedSegmentChanged`.

Derives from `RoutedEventArgs`: every member of `RoutedEventArgs` works as well.

### JourneyTraceChangedEventArgs

Arguments of `TraceChanged`: the node or link whose people are traced through the journey (pointer over it, or keyboard focus on a node), or neither.

Derives from `RoutedEventArgs`: every member of `RoutedEventArgs` works as well.

## Accessibility

### Keyboard

- **Tab** stops on the segment switch, then once on the chart (the last focused step, the first one to begin with), then
  on the panel's Clear button when a step is selected, then on "Flow table".
- On the switch, **←/↑** and **→/↓** move to the previous and next segment and wrap; the chart follows at once.
  **Home** and **End** go to the first and last.
- On the chart, **↑/↓** move within a stage (stopping at the ends), **←/→** move to the step of the neighbouring stage
  whose middle is nearest, **Home** and **End** go to the first and the last step. A focused step is traced and its
  tooltip sits beside it.
- **Enter** or **Space** selects the focused step, or clears it when it is already selected. **Escape** clears the
  selection and keeps the focus where it is.
- After Clear, the focus goes back to the step that was selected.

### Screen readers

- Each step is a toggle button named "Started trial: 5,320 users, 31.7% of visitors. Began the free trial." whose pressed
  state is the selection. The steps form one group named by `ChartLabel`, and its help text reads the whole chart stage by
  stage.
- The segment switch is a group named by `SegmentsLabel`; its segments report which one is pressed.
- A segment change is announced politely ("Search: 8,050 visits and 510 paid plans."). Tracing and selecting are not
  announced; the focused step's name already says it all.
- The tooltip is drawn and hidden from screen readers. Rolling numbers read their final value, never the rolling one.
- The side panel is a region named by `PanelLabel`; empty row slots are hidden. The Flow table button reports whether it
  is expanded, and the table reads as text with a caption.
- The focus ring is 2 pixels wide, 2 pixels outside the step's hit box.

## Motion

- **Segment switch**: every count rides a spring (stiffness 70, damping 16.4, no overshoot, about 0.8 s to settle) and
  the whole chart is laid out again from the moving counts each frame, so bars, ribbons and labels move as one. The label
  counts follow the same spring 65 ms later. The visitors in the subtitle and the panel's numbers roll digit by digit on
  the smooth spring, the share bars glide, and the panel's titles fade out in 120 ms while the new ones rise 4 pixels in
  240 ms. The thumb of the switch glides on a quick spring.
- **Tracing**: the rest of the chart fades in 160 ms; the cohort's bands and bar overlays grow on a quick spring and, when
  you move to another step, change from where they are rather than starting over. The tooltip fades in over 120 ms,
  follows the pointer without lag, and cross-fades its content when the traced thing changes.
- **Selecting**: the step's ring fades in over 160 ms; the panel's texts swap as above.
- **Flow table**: the height opens on the smooth spring and the chevron turns over on the quick one.
- Reduced motion places the chart and the numbers at once and keeps only the short fades (tooltip, panel titles).
  Off applies every change at once. Nothing animates when the block first appears.

## Related

- `Cohort retention` and `Metrics dashboard`, the other Analytics blocks.
- `SegmentedControl` for a standalone switch.
- `Sortable data table` when the numbers matter more than the shape.
