# Uptime status

> A status page for a set of services: 90 days of daily bars with uptime figures and a hover card per day, a response-time chart with p50 and p95 curves against a target for the chosen service, and an incident timeline, all derived from the services' samples and the incidents, with keyboard paging by a week.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc.Blocks`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc.Blocks --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/blocks/uptime-status

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.UptimeStatusPreviewDemo">
    <!-- Four services, five past incidents and a button that walks an incident on Events through start, resolution and reset. Data: UptimeStatusDemoData. -->
    <arc:UptimeStatus x:Name="Status" PageName="Larkspur status">
        <arc:UptimeStatus.ActionContent>
            <arc:Button x:Name="Simulate" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Content="Simulate incident" />
        </arc:UptimeStatus.ActionContent>
    </arc:UptimeStatus>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class UptimeStatusPreviewDemo : UserControl
{
    public UptimeStatusPreviewDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Status.Today = UptimeStatusDemoData.Now;
        Status.UpdatedAt = UptimeStatusDemoData.UpdatedAt;
        Status.Services.AddRange(UptimeStatusDemoData.Services());
        Status.Incidents.AddRange(UptimeStatusDemoData.Incidents());
        var simulation = new UptimeIncidentSimulation(Status);
        Simulate.Click += (_, _) =>
        {
            simulation.Advance();
            Simulate.Content = simulation.ActionText;
        };
    }
}
```

## When to use

`UptimeStatus` is a public or internal status page in one block. It answers three questions in the order people ask them:
is everything working right now (the header), how reliable has each service been (one bar per day for 90 days, with an
uptime figure), and what happened and when (the incident timeline). Choosing a service charts its response time over the last
day, so a slow Tuesday in the bars can be matched with a latency curve and an incident.

- **A status page for customers or the team.** The header turns from a tick to an exclamation mark and says what is wrong
  while an incident is open; every row says which service it is.
- **A service-level review.** The bars and the uptime figures are computed from the incidents you give it, so the page
  cannot disagree with the incident list.
- **A runbook companion.** The latency chart puts the p95 against the target, so "slow" is a number with a line next to it.

## When not to use

- **Real-time monitoring.** The block shows daily history and half-hourly samples; it does not poll anything. Feed it from your
  monitoring system and let it follow the data you change.
- **One metric over time.** Use a line chart or the `Metric explorer` block when there is no service, incident or target
  to relate it to.
- **Hundreds of services.** The page is made for roughly 3 to 10 rows; group the rest before showing them.
- **Per-minute detail.** A bar is a whole UTC day. Show an incident's exact timing in its timeline.

## Usage

The block derives from Avalonia's `TemplatedControl` and contains no data. Give it `Services` and `Incidents`:

```xml
<arc:UptimeStatus PageName="Larkspur status" UpdatedAt="2027-03-14T14:32:00Z">
    <arc:UptimeService Key="edge" Name="Edge" Description="Routing and TLS" TargetP95="350" />
    <arc:UptimeService Key="console" Name="Console" Description="console.larkspur.test" TargetP95="900" />
</arc:UptimeStatus>
```

```csharp
status.Services.AddRange(services);                        // each with 48 half-hourly LatencySamples
status.Incidents.Add(new UptimeIncident
{
    Title = "Elevated 5xx on Edge",
    Severity = ServiceStatus.Outage,
    Start = DateTimeOffset.Parse("2027-02-20T07:40:00Z"),
    Duration = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(19),
    ServiceKeys = { "edge" },
    Updates = { new IncidentUpdate("Investigating", start, "Some requests fail.", IncidentTone.Warning) }
});
```

`ServicesSource` and `IncidentsSource` take collections you own instead (an `ObservableCollection` is followed). The block
also follows changes to the services' samples and to every property of an incident, and shows a burst of changes together on
the next turn of the UI thread.

### What is derived

Everything on the page follows from the data, so there is nothing to keep in step by hand:

- **A day's uptime** is 1 minus the minutes of incidents that fell on that UTC day over 1,440; an incident across midnight is
  split between the two days. The hover card writes it with two decimals ("98.40%").
- **A day's status** is the most severe incident of the day: no incident is operational, a degraded one is a 65% bar, an outage
  a 35% bar. Degraded and outage minutes both count as downtime.
- **A service's uptime** is 1 minus all its minutes over `DayCount` times 1,440 ("99.95%" for 69 minutes in 90 days).
- **A service's state** (the badge on its row, the title) comes from its unresolved incidents. A resolved incident leaves its
  day's bar degraded, because the day had an incident, but the page is operational again.
- **The count** under "Incidents" is the incidents of the window, and the list is newest first.

`Today` is the last day of the window (default: the day of the newest latency sample) and `DayCount` the number of bars.

### The bars

Each bar band is as wide as the row. The bar width is `round((W - 2 (n - 1)) / n)`, never under 3, and bar *i* starts at
`round(i (W - w) / (n - 1))`: a 1,112px band gets 10px bars with 2 or 3px gaps, a 472px band 3px bars. Pointing at the band
snaps to the nearest bar (the card follows the bar, not the pointer), dims the other bars of that service to 38% and opens the
hover card above the band: the service and date with the day's uptime, the status, and each incident of the day with its
minutes, or "No incidents recorded". The card is 256 wide, sits 8 above the band, is kept 8 from the section's edges and may
cover the row above.

### The response-time chart

Choose a service by its name, by clicking its bars, or with Enter or Space on its bars; `SelectedService` is two-way.
The chart shows the last 48 half-hour samples: the band between p95 and p50, the p95 curve (2px, accent), the p50 curve (1.5px)
and a dashed line at `TargetP95`. Both curves are monotone cubic, so they never overshoot the data. The y axis starts at 0
and ends at the nice number above `ChartHeadroom` (1.2) times the larger of the target and the highest p95: a target of 400
with a highest p95 of 266 gives 0 to 500 in steps of 100; one of 1,000 with 612 gives 0 to 1,250 in steps of 250. The three
numbers above the chart (p95, p50, target) roll to the new service's values.

Pointing at the chart (or pressing → or ← on the focused chart) snaps a crosshair with a dot per curve to the nearest sample
and replaces the numbers and the time at the top right with that sample's, without rolling; leaving restores the newest.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.UptimeStatusEventsDemo">
    <!--
        The charted service is a two-way property and every inspection is an event. Buttons drive the block from outside
        (chart a service, open every incident, clear the inspection) and the log shows what it reports: days and samples
        you point at, the service you choose and the incidents you open.
    -->
    <StackPanel Spacing="12">
        <StackPanel Orientation="Horizontal" Spacing="8">
            <arc:Button x:Name="ChartIdentity" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Content="Chart Identity" />
            <arc:Button x:Name="OpenAll" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Content="Open every incident" />
            <arc:Button x:Name="Clear" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Content="Clear inspection" />
        </StackPanel>
        <arc:UptimeStatus x:Name="Status" PageName="Larkspur status" />
        <TextBlock x:Name="Log"
                   TextWrapping="Wrap"
                   FontSize="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TypeXS}"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}"
                   Text="Events appear here." />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class UptimeStatusEventsDemo : UserControl
{
    private readonly List<string> _lines = new();

    public UptimeStatusEventsDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Status.Today = UptimeStatusDemoData.Now;
        Status.UpdatedAt = UptimeStatusDemoData.UpdatedAt;
        Status.Services.AddRange(UptimeStatusDemoData.Services());
        Status.Incidents.AddRange(UptimeStatusDemoData.Incidents());

        ChartIdentity.Click += (_, _) => Status.SelectedService = Status.Services.First(s => s.Key == "identity");
        OpenAll.Click += (_, _) =>
        {
            foreach (var incident in Status.Incidents)
            {
                incident.IsExpanded = true;
            }
        };
        Clear.Click += (_, _) => Status.ClearInspection();

        Status.SelectedServiceChanged += (_, e) => Write($"Charted: {e.Service?.Name}");
        Status.DayInspected += (_, e) => Write(e.Day is { } day
            ? $"Day: {e.Service.Name} {day.Date:MMM d}, {day.Status}, {day.Uptime:P2}, {day.Incidents.Count} incident(s)"
            : $"Day: {e.Service.Name} inspection ended");
        Status.PointInspected += (_, e) => Write(e.Sample is { } sample
            ? $"Sample: {e.Service?.Name} {sample.Time:HH:mm}, p50 {sample.P50:N0} ms, p95 {sample.P95:N0} ms"
            : "Sample: inspection ended");
        Status.IncidentExpandedChanged += (_, e) => Write($"{(e.IsExpanded ? "Opened" : "Closed")}: {e.Incident.Title}");
    }

    private void Write(string line)
    {
        _lines.Insert(0, line);
        if (_lines.Count > 6)
        {
            _lines.RemoveAt(_lines.Count - 1);
        }
        Log.Text = string.Join(Environment.NewLine, _lines);
    }
}
```

### Incidents

Each incident is a button with its severity mark, title, meta line ("Major outage · Feb 20, 07:40 UTC · 19 min · Edge"), a
status (a badge while it goes on, "Resolved" afterwards) and a chevron. Opening it shows the updates, newest first, with the
newest dot filled in its `IncidentUpdate.Tone` and older ones hollow, and the line about the person leading the response.
`IsExpanded` is two-way and several incidents can be open together.

### A status that changes

Add an incident whose `IsResolved` is false and the block changes everything the incident touches: the header icon turns into an
exclamation mark and the title swaps to `DegradedTitle` (or `OutageTitle`), the affected service's row gets a badge, today's bar
fades to degraded and shrinks, its uptime rolls, the count rolls and a new incident grows into the top of the list. Set
`IsResolved`, `Duration` and add a "Resolved" update and the page returns to operational, the badge goes, today's bar stays
degraded and the newest timeline entry grows in. Removing the incident takes it all back. `StatusSummary` is the line next to the
page name while something is wrong ("Events delayed since 13:58 UTC"); without it the line reads "Updated …" from `UpdatedAt`.

The Preview demo drives exactly this from a button; the simulation lives in the demo's code, not in the block.

### Header action

`ActionContent` is whatever you want at the right of the header (a button, a link). Under a block width of 560 it moves under
the text.

### Narrow containers

"uptime" are hidden. The bars keep a minimum of 3px, so on a phone the gaps shrink.

### Words and formats

Every word is in `Labels` (an `UptimeStatusLabels`), the three titles are properties, and `LatencyFormatter`,
`PercentFormatter` and `DateFormatter` change how numbers and days are written in the hover card, the chart's tick labels and
the announcements.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.UptimeStatusFormatsDemo">
    <!--
        Everything the block writes is a property: the three titles, the words (Labels), how a response time, an uptime and a
        day are written. Here a French-flavoured page shows response times in seconds, uptimes with three decimals and the
        longer headroom of a chart that is allowed to show more empty space above the target.
    -->
    <arc:UptimeStatus x:Name="Status"
                      PageName="Statut de Larkspur"
                      OperationalTitle="Tous les systèmes fonctionnent"
                      DegradedTitle="Performances dégradées"
                      OutageTitle="Panne majeure"
                      ChartHeadroom="1.5" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class UptimeStatusFormatsDemo : UserControl
{
    public UptimeStatusFormatsDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Status.Today = UptimeStatusDemoData.Now;
        Status.UpdatedAt = UptimeStatusDemoData.UpdatedAt;
        Status.Services.AddRange(UptimeStatusDemoData.Services());
        Status.Incidents.AddRange(UptimeStatusDemoData.Incidents());

        // The hover card, the announcements and the chart's tick labels use these.
        Status.LatencyFormatter = ms => ms >= 1000 ? $"{ms / 1000:0.0#} s" : $"{ms:0} ms";
        Status.PercentFormatter = fraction => $"{fraction * 100:0.000}%";
        Status.DateFormatter = day => day.ToString("d MMM", new System.Globalization.CultureInfo("fr-FR"));
        Status.Labels = new UptimeStatusLabels
        {
            UptimeText = "Disponibilité",
            UptimeHintFormat = "{0} derniers jours · choisissez un service pour son graphique",
            OperationalText = "Opérationnel",
            DegradedText = "Dégradé",
            OutageText = "Panne majeure",
            UptimeWordText = "dispo",
            TodayText = "Aujourd'hui",
            NoIncidentsRecordedText = "Aucun incident enregistré",
            ResponseTimeText = "Temps de réponse",
            ResponseSubtitleFormat = "{0} · dernières 24 heures",
            LatestFormat = "Dernier, {0}",
            IncidentsText = "Incidents",
            IncidentsCountFormat = "{0} sur les {1} derniers jours",
            ResolvedText = "Résolu",
            UpdatedFormat = "Mis à jour le {0:d MMM} à {0:HH:mm} UTC"
        };
    }
}
```

## API reference

### UptimeStatus

A status page: the overall state of a set of services at the top, each service's last 90 days as one bar per day with its uptime, the response time of the chosen service over the last day (p50 and p95 against a target) and the incident timeline. The page is derived from the data: give it `Services` (each with half-hourly `Latency` samples and a target) and `Incidents` (each naming the services it hit, when it began and how long it lasted); every day's bar, every uptime figure, the chart domain and the counts follow. Pointing at a day's bar (or moving the keyboard cursor over it) dims the others and opens a card with the day's uptime, status and incidents; choosing a service (its name, or Enter on its bars) glides the highlight to it and morphs the chart. Changing the data (a new incident, a resolution) fades the bars, rolls the numbers, swaps the header and grows or removes incident entries. Keyboard: Tab reaches the header action, then each service's name button and its bars, then the chart and each incident. A focused bar band inspects the newest day; ← → move by a day, PageUp and PageDown by seven, Home and End jump to the ends, Escape clears and Enter or Space charts the service. The focused chart moves a cursor by half hour with ← → (the first → shows the newest sample), Home and End, and Escape clears it.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ServicesSource` | `IEnumerable?` | `null` | The services, when you give them as a list to follow (observed when it raises collection changes); it wins over `Services`. |
| `IncidentsSource` | `IEnumerable?` | `null` | The incidents, when you give them as a list to follow; it wins over `Incidents`. |
| `Today` | `DateTimeOffset?` | `null` | The last day of the window (UTC); null uses the day of the newest latency sample. |
| `DayCount` | `int` | `90` | The number of day bars (90). |
| `PageName` | `string?` | `null` | The name of the status page, the left part of the line under the title. |
| `UpdatedAt` | `DateTimeOffset?` | `null` | When the page was last updated: the right part of the line under the title while no summary is set. |
| `StatusSummary` | `string?` | `null` | The right part of the line under the title (an incident's summary); null shows "Updated …" from `UpdatedAt`. |
| `OperationalTitle` | `string` | `"All systems operational"` | The title while every service is operational. |
| `DegradedTitle` | `string` | `"Degraded performance"` | The title while a service is degraded. |
| `OutageTitle` | `string` | `"Major outage"` | The title while a service is in outage. |
| `SelectedService` | `UptimeService?` | `null` | The service whose response time is charted (two-way); null or an unknown service uses the first. |
| `ActionContent` | `object?` | `null` | What sits at the right of the header (a button, a link); the block draws no data into it. |
| `LatencyFormatter` | `Func<double, string>?` | `null` | Formats a response time for the hover texts and announcements (default grouped integer). |
| `PercentFormatter` | `Func<double, string>?` | `null` | Formats an uptime fraction (0 to 1) for the hover card and announcements (default "99.95%"). |
| `DateFormatter` | `Func<DateOnly, string>?` | `null` | Formats a day for the hover card and the bars' first date (default "ddd, MMM d" and "MMM d"). |
| `ChartHeadroom` | `double` | `1.2` | The chart's domain is the nice number above the larger of the target and the highest p95 times this (1.2). |
| `Labels` | `UptimeStatusLabels` | – | Every word the block writes or speaks besides the data and the three titles. |
| `OverallStatus` | `ServiceStatus` | – | *Read-only.* The worst status among the services that have an unresolved incident (read-only). |
| `InspectedDay` | `int?` | – | *Read-only.* The index of the inspected day of the bars (read-only; null when none). |
| `InspectedPoint` | `int?` | – | *Read-only.* The index of the inspected sample of the chart (read-only; null when none). |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `SelectedServiceChanged` | `UptimeServiceEventArgs` | Raised when another service is charted. |
| `DayInspected` | `UptimeDayEventArgs` | Raised when a day of a service's bars is inspected or the inspection ends. |
| `PointInspected` | `UptimePointEventArgs` | Raised when a sample of the chart is inspected or the inspection ends. |
| `IncidentExpandedChanged` | `UptimeIncidentEventArgs` | Raised when an incident's timeline is opened or closed by the user. |

Pseudo-classes: `:operational`, `:degraded`, `:outage`, `:stacked`, `:compact`, `:empty`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

### UptimeService

A service: a name, a response-time target and half-hourly latency samples.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Key` | `string` | `""` | A key that tells this service from the others; incidents refer to it. |
| `Name` | `string` | `""` | The name. |
| `Description` | `string?` | `null` | A short description after the name. |
| `TargetP95` | `double` | `0` | The p95 response time the service should stay under, in milliseconds (the dashed line). |
| `Uptime` | `double` | – | *Read-only.* The 90-day uptime, 0 to 1 (set by the block). |
| `CurrentStatus` | `ServiceStatus` | – | *Read-only.* Today's status (set by the block). |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### LatencySample

One half-hour sample of a service's response time.

Derives from `ValueType`: every member of `ValueType` works as well.

### UptimeIncident

An incident: something that made one or more services slower or unavailable for a while.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Key` | `string?` | `null` | A key that tells this incident from the others. |
| `Title` | `string` | `""` | The headline. |
| `Severity` | `ServiceStatus` | `Degraded` | Degraded or Outage; counts as downtime for the whole duration either way. |
| `Start` | `DateTimeOffset` | `01/01/0001 00:00:00 +00:00` | When it began. |
| `Duration` | `TimeSpan` | `00:00:00` | How long it has lasted (so far, while it is not resolved). |
| `IsResolved` | `bool` | `true` | True once it is over. |
| `Lead` | `UptimePerson?` | `null` | The person leading the response. |
| `IsExpanded` | `bool` | `false` | The timeline is open (two-way). |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### IncidentUpdate

One update in an incident's timeline.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Phase` | `string` | `""` | The stage word ("Investigating", "Identified", "Monitoring", "Resolved"). |
| `Time` | `DateTimeOffset` | `01/01/0001 00:00:00 +00:00` | When the update was posted. |
| `Body` | `string?` | `null` | What was said. |
| `Tone` | `IncidentTone` | `Neutral` | The colour of the dot while this is the newest update. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### UptimePerson

The person leading an incident response.

### UptimeDay

One day of a service's history, derived from the incidents.

### UptimeDayIncident

An incident's share of one day.

Derives from `ValueType`: every member of `ValueType` works as well.

### UptimeStatusLabels

Every word an `UptimeStatus` writes or speaks besides the data and the three header titles, with English defaults. Placeholders are numbered as described on each property. Assign a new instance to `Labels` to translate the block.

### UptimeServiceEventArgs

Event data for a change of the selected service.

Derives from `RoutedEventArgs`: every member of `RoutedEventArgs` works as well.

### UptimeDayEventArgs

Event data for a day being inspected in a service's bars.

Derives from `RoutedEventArgs`: every member of `RoutedEventArgs` works as well.

### UptimePointEventArgs

Event data for a latency sample being inspected in the chart.

Derives from `RoutedEventArgs`: every member of `RoutedEventArgs` works as well.

### UptimeIncidentEventArgs

Event data for an incident being opened or closed.

Derives from `RoutedEventArgs`: every member of `RoutedEventArgs` works as well.

### ServiceStatus

How a service, a day or a whole page is doing; the order is the order of severity.

Derives from `Enum`: every member of `Enum` works as well.

### IncidentTone

The colour of an incident update's dot in the timeline (the newest update is filled, older ones are hollow).

Derives from `Enum`: every member of `Enum` works as well.

## Accessibility

- Each service has a button named with its uptime and state ("Edge, 99.95% uptime, Operational") that is pressed while the
  service is charted, and a focusable group for its bars, named "Edge, daily status for the last 90 days" and described with the
  uptime and the incidents of the window.
- Inspecting a day with the keyboard announces it politely: "Sat, Feb 20: Major outage, 98.68% uptime. Elevated 5xx on Edge."
  Inspecting a sample announces "Mar 14, 14:00 UTC: p50 80 ms, p95 210 ms." The hover card itself is hidden from assistive
  technology; the announcements carry its content.
- The chart is a focusable group with a text summary (the newest p50 and p95, the highest p95 and when, the target) and a hidden
  table with a row per half hour.
- Incident buttons say whether they are expanded; each timeline is a list named "Updates, newest first" that reads every update.
- A separate status region announces an incident that appears and one that is resolved, and `Announce` lets you say your own
  sentence.
- Colour is never the only signal: bars differ in height as well as colour, badges and the header icon carry text and shape.
- The focus ring is 2px, 2px outside, on the bars, the chart, the service buttons and the incident buttons, for keyboard focus only.

### Keyboard

- **Tab** moves through the header action, then each service's name button and its bars, then the chart, then each incident.
- On the **bars**, focusing from the keyboard inspects the newest day. **← →** move by a day, **PageUp / PageDown** by seven days,
  **Home / End** to the ends, stopping there. **Escape** clears (the next **←** starts from the day before the newest) and
  **Enter / Space** chart the service.
- On the **chart**, focusing does not inspect. **→** shows the newest sample and **←** the one before it; then **← →** move by a half
  hour and **Home / End** jump to the ends. Page keys do nothing. **Escape** clears.
- On an **incident**, **Enter / Space** open or close it.

## Motion

- **Bars**: pointing dims the other bars to 38% in 120ms (Standard) while a full-strength copy of the inspected one stays on top.
  A day that changes status fades its colour in 240ms and its height springs (k 170, c 27).
- **Hover card**: fades in over 160ms from 97% scale; moving between bars it follows on a stiff spring (k 925, c 58, about
  240ms), also from row to row; leaving, it fades out in 120ms to 98%.
- **Choosing a service**: the highlight glides to the row (k 150, c 24, about half a second) while the curves, the band, the
  target line and the y domain spring together (k 171, c 26); tick labels cross-fade, the subtitle rises out and in, and the
  three numbers roll. Kept ticks slide with the domain.
- **Header**: the icon's line ends spring between a tick and an exclamation mark (k 160, c 26) while its colours fade in 240ms;
  title and summary swap with a short rise (about 200ms), and the colour of badges fades in 240ms.
- **Incidents**: a new incident grows from zero height on a spring while it fades in over 200ms; a removed one fades out in 130ms
  while it collapses. A timeline entry grows in on a spring (k 180, c 27). Opening an incident springs its height (k 171) and
  fades its content in 240ms; the chevron turns half way round on a quick spring.
- Reduced motion keeps the short fades (hover card, dimming, tick labels that leave) and lands springs, rolling numbers and the
  morph at once. Off applies everything at once.

## Related

- `Metrics dashboard`, `KPI drilldown` and `Metric explorer`, the other Analytics blocks.
- `Badge` and `Avatar`, the small parts the status badges and the response lead are in the spirit of.
- `Release readiness`, a Projects block with a similar state-changing header.

# Choropleth explorer

> A map shaded by a metric in quantile steps with a linked ranked list; choose a region to fly into it and rank its counties, switch the metric to sweep new colours across the map, or change the country.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc.Blocks`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc.Blocks --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/blocks/choropleth-explorer

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ChoroplethExplorerPreviewDemo">
    <!-- Eight countries, three metrics; ten US states, every UK region, French region and Italian region have finer detail.
         Outlines: Maps/*.txt (public domain); values: ChoroplethExplorerDemoData (invented, seeded). -->
    <arc:ChoroplethExplorer x:Name="Explorer" Description="Fiscal year ending March 31, 2027" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Threading;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class ChoroplethExplorerPreviewDemo : UserControl
{
    public ChoroplethExplorerPreviewDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();

        // The United States is read now; the other seven map files are read after the first frame (the switch fills in).
        var areas = ChoroplethExplorerDemoData.Areas(eager: false);
        Explorer.Areas.AddRange(areas);
        Dispatcher.UIThread.Post(() =>
        {
            foreach (var area in areas)
            {
                ChoroplethExplorerDemoData.Load(area);
            }
        }, DispatcherPriority.Background);
    }
}
```

## When to use

`ChoroplethExplorer` answers two questions on one screen: where a number is high or low, and why a region has the value it
has. Every region of an area is shaded by the chosen metric, the same regions are ranked beside the map, and choosing one
flies the camera into it to show the next level down, re-binned and re-ranked.

- **Revenue, customers or usage by geography.** States, provinces or regions shaded by a total, with the leaders and the
  long tail in the list.
- **Change over a period.** A diverging metric splits at zero: declines in one hue, gains in another, so a growth map reads
  at a glance.
- **Coverage of a market.** A share per region (signed accounts out of target accounts) with the regions that have no data
  shown as such once you zoom in.

## When not to use

- **Exact comparisons.** Colour steps group values; for precise differences between a few regions use a bar chart or a
  table. The ranked list helps, but it is not the main reading.
- **Non-geographic categories.** Shading only makes sense when position carries meaning. Use a treemap or a ranked bar list
  for product lines or teams.
- **Point data.** Stores, offices or events belong on a map with markers, not on shaded areas.
- **A map you cannot ship.** The block draws outlines you provide; it contains no map of its own.

## Usage

The block derives from Avalonia's `TemplatedControl`. You give it one or more `ChoroplethArea`s (countries), each with its
`ChoroplethRegion`s, and the `ChoroplethMetric`s to shade by. A region brings its outline as SVG path data in the area's view
box (975 × 610 by default), its bounding box (optional: it saves parsing to place the camera), a value per metric and,
optionally, its own subregions in the same view box. The outlines are parsed once, when they are first drawn.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:ChoroplethExplorer Description="Fiscal year ending March 31, 2027">
        <arc:ChoroplethExplorer.Metrics>
            <arc:ChoroplethMetric Key="revenue" Label="Revenue"
                                  HeadlineLabel="Annual recurring revenue"
                                  LegendCaption="Shaded by annual recurring revenue" />
            <arc:ChoroplethMetric Key="growth" Label="Growth" Format="Change" Scale="Diverging"
                                  Aggregate="WeightedAverage" />
        </arc:ChoroplethExplorer.Metrics>
        <arc:ChoroplethArea Key="us" Name="United States" RegionNoun="states" RegionNounSingular="state"
                            SubregionNoun="counties" SubregionNounSingular="county" />
    </arc:ChoroplethExplorer>
</UserControl>
```

```csharp
var california = new ChoroplethRegion("CA", "California", pathData, new Rect(18.7, 160, 143.9, 247));
california.SetMetricValue("revenue", 9_400_000);
california.SetMetricValue("growth", 4.2);   // percent units: +4.2%
area.Regions.Add(california);
```

The demos on this page read public-domain outlines (US Census Bureau cartographic boundary files for the United States,
Natural Earth admin-1 for the other countries) from text files that ship with the gallery; every value is invented.

### Anatomy

- **Header**: the title (`Title`, the area's `Title`, or "Revenue by state" from `ChoroplethLabels.TitleFormat`), the
  `Description`, the country switch (only with more than one area, each option with its region count) and the metric switch.
- **Summary**: the area's or the opened region's name, the headline number (the sum, or the weighted average of the
  regions, or the opened region's own value) and the metric's `HeadlineLabel`. While zoomed, a button leads back out.
- **Map**: every region shaded in its step; pointing outlines a region and shows a card with its rank, every metric
  (the current one stands out) and what choosing it does.
- **Legend**: one step per bin with the bin edges between them, a no-data step when subregions lack values, and a caption
  that names the step under the pointer ("10 states $120K to $230K").
- **Ranked list**: rank, name, value and a bar per region; a chevron marks regions that open into subregions. Pointing at a
  row outlines its region, and pointing at the map finds the row.

### Bins and colours

A sequential metric is cut into `BinCount` (5) steps at the quantiles of the values in view; a diverging metric is split at
zero first and each side is cut at its own quantiles, with the steps shared in proportion to how many values fall on each
side. Every edge is rounded to two significant digits, and a value equal to an edge belongs to the step above it. The bins
are recomputed for each level: after zooming in, the counties have steps of their own.

The positive hue is the accent, or a blue when the accent is grey; the negative hue is an amber opposite it; regions without
a value use the border colour. Set `PositiveColor`, `NegativeColor` and `NoDataColor` to use your own.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ChoroplethExplorerCustomLookDemo">
    <!-- Own hues, title and words; values written by a formatter of your own. -->
    <arc:ChoroplethExplorer x:Name="Explorer"
                            Title="Bookings by region"
                            Description="Signed contracts, calendar year 2026"
                            PositiveColor="#0E8F7E"
                            NegativeColor="#D1495B" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using System.Globalization;
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class ChoroplethExplorerCustomLookDemo : UserControl
{
    public ChoroplethExplorerCustomLookDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        var italy = ChoroplethExplorerDemoData.Area("it");
        // Revenue in thousands of euros, written the way the finance team reports it.
        var revenue = italy.Metrics[0];
        revenue.Label = "Bookings";
        revenue.HeadlineLabel = "Signed this year";
        revenue.LegendCaption = "Shaded by bookings";
        revenue.Formatter = v => (v / 1000).ToString("N0", CultureInfo.GetCultureInfo("en-US")) + " k€";
        Explorer.Labels = new ChoroplethLabels
        {
            RankedByFormat = "Sorted by {0}",
            BackFormat = "All of Italy",
            NoDataText = "No contracts",
        };
        Explorer.Areas.Add(italy);
    }
}
```

### Zooming in

Choosing a region (on the map or in the list) sets `OpenRegionKey`, raises `RegionOpened` and flies the camera so the region
fills 80% of the map (never more than 12×). The other regions stay as faded context and can be chosen to fly straight to
them. With subregions the region gives way to them, the legend and the list re-bin and re-rank, and choosing a subregion
pins it (`PinnedSubregionKey`, `SubregionPinned`). Without subregions the list says there is no finer detail and offers the
way back. `ZoomTo(key)` and `ZoomOut()` do the same from code.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ChoroplethExplorerEventsDemo">
    <!-- The zoom, the metric and the pins are two-way properties; the events report what the person did. -->
    <StackPanel Spacing="16">
        <StackPanel Orientation="Horizontal" Spacing="8">
            <arc:Button Content="Open California" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Click="OnOpenCalifornia" />
            <arc:Button Content="Open Florida" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Click="OnOpenFlorida" />
            <arc:Button Content="Zoom out" Variant="Ghost" Size="Small" Click="OnZoomOut" />
        </StackPanel>
        <arc:ChoroplethExplorer x:Name="Explorer"
                                Description="Fiscal year ending March 31, 2027"
                                RegionOpened="OnRegionOpened"
                                MetricChanged="OnMetricChanged"
                                SubregionPinned="OnSubregionPinned" />
        <StackPanel Spacing="4">
            <TextBlock FontSize="13"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}"
                       Text="{Binding #Explorer.OpenRegionKey, StringFormat='OpenRegionKey: {0}', TargetNullValue='OpenRegionKey: none'}" />
            <TextBlock x:Name="Log" FontSize="13" TextWrapping="Wrap" Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
        </StackPanel>
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class ChoroplethExplorerEventsDemo : UserControl
{
    private readonly List<string> _lines = new();

    public ChoroplethExplorerEventsDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Explorer.Areas.Add(ChoroplethExplorerDemoData.Area("us"));
        Write("Choose a state, a metric or a county.");
    }

    private void OnOpenCalifornia(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) => Explorer.ZoomTo("CA");

    private void OnOpenFlorida(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) => Explorer.ZoomTo("FL");

    private void OnZoomOut(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) => Explorer.ZoomOut();

    private void OnRegionOpened(object? sender, ChoroplethRegionOpenedEventArgs e) =>
        Write(e.Region is { } region ? $"RegionOpened: {region.Name} ({region.Subregions.Count} counties)" : "RegionOpened: zoomed out");

    private void OnMetricChanged(object? sender, ChoroplethSelectionChangedEventArgs e) => Write($"MetricChanged: {e.OldKey} → {e.NewKey}");

    private void OnSubregionPinned(object? sender, ChoroplethSubregionPinnedEventArgs e) =>
        Write(e.Subregion is { } county ? $"SubregionPinned: {county.Name}" : "SubregionPinned: released");

    private void Write(string line)
    {
        _lines.Insert(0, line);
        if (_lines.Count > 4)
        {
            _lines.RemoveAt(_lines.Count - 1);
        }
        Log.Text = string.Join(Environment.NewLine, _lines);
    }
}
```

### Card look and narrow containers

`IsCardChrome` draws the block as a bordered card. The block reads its own width: from 820 the list stands beside the map
and is exactly as tall as the map column; below that it goes under the map (400 high, 360 below 560), the controls move under
the title, and below 560 the padding tightens, the headline shrinks and the legend fills the width.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"

             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ChoroplethExplorerCardDemo">
    <!-- The card look in a narrow column: the compact layout stacks the controls and puts the list under the map. -->
    <arc:ChoroplethExplorer x:Name="Explorer"
                            MaxWidth="520"
                            HorizontalAlignment="Center"
                            IsCardChrome="True"
                            Description="Fiscal year ending March 31, 2027" />
```

### Words

Every word besides the data comes from `Labels`, a `ChoroplethLabels` with English defaults: the counts ("51 states", with
the area's singular and plural nouns), "Ranked by revenue", the legend's step names, the hover card's hints, the back
buttons, the empty panel and every announcement. Metrics bring their own `Label`, `Noun`, `HeadlineLabel`, `LegendCaption`,
`CurrencySymbol`, and optional `Formatter` and `TickFormatter`.

## API reference

### ChoroplethExplorer

A choropleth map with a linked ranked list: every region of an area (the states of a country) is shaded by the chosen metric in quantile steps, and the same regions are ranked beside the map with a bar each. Pointing at a region outlines it, shows a card with every metric and finds its row; pointing at a legend step lights that step's regions; choosing a region flies the camera into it and shows its subregions (counties) re-binned and re-ranked, or says that there is no finer detail. Switching the metric sweeps the new colours across the map from west to east while the rows slide to their new ranks; with several areas a switch changes the country. The block contains no map data: each `ChoroplethRegion` brings its outline as SVG path data in the area's view box (975 × 610 by default). Keyboard: Tab reaches the area switch, the metric switch, the back button (while zoomed), each legend step and the list (one stop). In the list ↑ / ↓ / Home / End move, Enter or Space opens a region or pins a subregion; on a legend step they pin it. Escape releases a pinned legend step first, then zooms back out.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `AreasSource` | `IEnumerable?` | `null` | The areas, when you give them as a list to follow (observed when it raises collection changes); it wins over `Areas`. |
| `SelectedAreaKey` | `string?` | `null` | The key of the area shown (two-way); null or an unknown key shows the first. |
| `SelectedMetricKey` | `string?` | `null` | The key of the metric the map is shaded by (two-way); null or an unknown key uses the first. |
| `OpenRegionKey` | `string?` | `null` | The key of the opened region (two-way): setting it flies the camera in, null zooms back out. |
| `PinnedSubregionKey` | `string?` | `null` | The key of the pinned subregion of the opened region (two-way): its outline stays and its row stays lit. |
| `PinnedBinIndex` | `int?` | `null` | The pinned legend step (two-way): 0 is the lowest step, `NoDataBinIndex` the no-data step, null none. While a step is pinned only its regions keep their colour. |
| `Title` | `string?` | `null` | The heading; null uses the area's title, else `TitleFormat` ("Revenue by state"). |
| `Description` | `string?` | `null` | The line under the heading (the period); null or empty leaves it out. |
| `IsCardChrome` | `bool` | `false` | Draws the block as a bordered card (16 radius, surface); false (default) lays it flat on the page. |
| `PositiveColor` | `Color?` | `null` | The hue of values (and of positive values on a diverging scale); null uses the accent, or a blue when the accent is grey. |
| `NegativeColor` | `Color?` | `null` | The hue of negative values on a diverging scale; null uses an amber opposite the positive hue. |
| `NoDataColor` | `Color?` | `null` | The fill of subregions without a value; null uses the border colour. |
| `Labels` | `ChoroplethLabels` | – | Every word the block writes or speaks besides the data. |
| `RegionOpenedCommand` | `ICommand?` | `null` | Run when a region opens (parameter: the region) or the map zooms out (parameter: null), after `RegionOpened`. |
| `SubregionPinnedCommand` | `ICommand?` | `null` | Run when a subregion is pinned (parameter: the subregion) or released (parameter: null). |
| `CurrentArea` | `ChoroplethArea?` | – | *Read-only.* The area being shown (resolved from `SelectedAreaKey`). |
| `CurrentMetric` | `ChoroplethMetric?` | – | *Read-only.* The metric the map is shaded by (resolved from `SelectedMetricKey`). |
| `OpenRegion` | `ChoroplethRegion?` | – | *Read-only.* The opened region (resolved from `OpenRegionKey`); null at the area level. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `AreaChanged` | `ChoroplethSelectionChangedEventArgs` | Raised when the shown area changes (by the switch or by code). |
| `MetricChanged` | `ChoroplethSelectionChangedEventArgs` | Raised when the metric changes (by the switch or by code). |
| `RegionOpened` | `ChoroplethRegionOpenedEventArgs` | Raised when the camera starts towards a region, or back out (region null). |
| `SubregionPinned` | `ChoroplethSubregionPinnedEventArgs` | Raised when a subregion is pinned or the pin is released. |

Pseudo-classes: `:wide`, `:compact`, `:zoomed`, `:card`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

### ChoroplethArea

One map a `ChoroplethExplorer` can show (a country): its regions, the words for them, and optionally its own metrics (local currency). With more than one area the block shows a country switch.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Key` | `string` | `""` | A stable id (`SelectedAreaKey`, events). |
| `Name` | `string` | `""` | The display name ("United States"): the switch, the summary, the map's accessible name. |
| `RegionNoun` | `string` | `"regions"` | The plural word for its regions ("states"). |
| `RegionNounSingular` | `string` | `"region"` | The singular word for one region ("state"). |
| `SubregionNoun` | `string` | `"subregions"` | The plural word for subregions ("counties"). |
| `SubregionNounSingular` | `string` | `"subregion"` | The singular word for one subregion ("county"). |
| `Title` | `string?` | `null` | The block's title while this area shows; null uses the block's `Title` or the generated one. |
| `ViewBox` | `Size` | `975, 610` | The size of the coordinate system the outlines are drawn in (975 × 610). |
| `EmptyDetailText` | `string?` | `null` | The first sentence of the empty panel of a region without subregions ("County data covers ten states."). |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### ChoroplethRegion

One shape on a `ChoroplethExplorer` map: a state, province or region (or, inside one, a county or department). It carries its outline as SVG path data in the area's view box, a value per metric (null = no data), and optionally the subregions shown when it is opened. The block contains no map data of its own: every outline comes from here.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Key` | `string` | `""` | A stable id (postal code, FIPS code); used by `OpenRegionKey` and the events. |
| `Code` | `string?` | `null` | A short code to show or match by ("CA"); optional. |
| `Name` | `string` | `""` | The display name ("California"). |
| `PathData` | `string?` | `null` | The outline as SVG path data in the area's view box (for subregions, in the parent's view box transformed by its `SubregionOrigin` and `SubregionScale`). Parsed once, when it is first drawn. |
| `Geometry` | `Geometry?` | `null` | The outline as a ready geometry; wins over `PathData`. |
| `Bounds` | `Rect` | `0, 0, 0, 0` | The outline's bounding box in view-box units. It places the camera and times the west-to-east sweep without parsing the outline; an empty rect (the default) uses the parsed geometry's bounds. |
| `SubregionOrigin` | `Point` | `0, 0` | Where the subregions' local grid starts, in this region's view box (0, 0 when they share it). |
| `SubregionScale` | `double` | `1` | How many view-box units one unit of the subregions' local grid is (1 when they share the view box). |
| `EmptyDetailText` | `string?` | `null` | The sentence shown when the region is opened and has no subregions; null uses the area's. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### ChoroplethMetric

One measure a `ChoroplethExplorer` can shade the map by: a segment in the metric switch, how its values are written and binned, and the words around it ("Ranked by revenue", "Shaded by annual recurring revenue").

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Key` | `string` | `""` | The key regions store their values under (`SetMetricValue`). |
| `Label` | `string` | `""` | The segment's text in the metric switch and the row's label in the hover card ("Revenue"). |
| `Noun` | `string?` | `null` | The lower-case name used inside sentences ("Ranked by revenue"); null uses `Label` in lower case. |
| `HeadlineLabel` | `string?` | `null` | The small text next to the headline number ("Annual recurring revenue"). |
| `LegendCaption` | `string?` | `null` | The line under the legend while no step is pointed at ("Shaded by annual recurring revenue"). |
| `Format` | `ChoroplethValueFormat` | `Currency` | How values are written. |
| `CurrencySymbol` | `string` | `"$"` | The currency symbol of `Currency` ("$", "€", "C$"). |
| `Formatter` | `Func<double, string>?` | `null` | Writes a value (list, hover card, headline, announcements); null uses `Format`. |
| `TickFormatter` | `Func<double, string>?` | `null` | Writes a legend tick (a bin edge rounded to two significant digits); null uses `Format`. |
| `Scale` | `ChoroplethScale` | `Sequential` | Sequential (one hue) or diverging (split at zero). |
| `Aggregate` | `ChoroplethAggregate` | `Sum` | How the headline number of a whole area is made from its regions. |
| `BinCount` | `int` | `5` | How many colour steps a sequential scale has (5; a diverging scale has one more). 2 to 9. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### ChoroplethLabels

Every word a `ChoroplethExplorer` writes or speaks besides the data, with English defaults. Placeholders are numbered as described on each property; nouns come from the area ("states", "county"), metric words from the metric ("revenue"). Assign a new instance to `Labels` to translate the block.

### ChoroplethValueFormat

How a `ChoroplethMetric`'s values are written.

Derives from `Enum`: every member of `Enum` works as well.

### ChoroplethScale

How a `ChoroplethMetric` is binned into colour steps.

Derives from `Enum`: every member of `Enum` works as well.

### ChoroplethAggregate

How the headline number of a whole area is made from its regions.

Derives from `Enum`: every member of `Enum` works as well.

### ChoroplethRegionOpenedEventArgs

Arguments of `ChoroplethExplorer.RegionOpened`: the camera started towards a region, or back out (null).

Derives from `RoutedEventArgs`: every member of `RoutedEventArgs` works as well.

### ChoroplethSubregionPinnedEventArgs

Arguments of `ChoroplethExplorer.SubregionPinned`: a subregion was pinned, or the pin was released (null).

Derives from `RoutedEventArgs`: every member of `RoutedEventArgs` works as well.

### ChoroplethSelectionChangedEventArgs

Arguments of `ChoroplethExplorer.AreaChanged` and `MetricChanged`: the selected key changed.

Derives from `RoutedEventArgs`: every member of `RoutedEventArgs` works as well.

## Accessibility

- **Tab** reaches the country switch, the metric switch (one stop; the arrows move the selection), the back button while
  zoomed, each legend step, and the list (one stop, on the last row you were on).
- In the list, **↑** and **↓** move one row and stop at the ends, **Home** and **End** jump to the first and last row; the
  focused row is outlined on the map and scrolled into view.
- **Enter** or **Space** on a region's row zooms in and moves the focus to the first row of its subregions (or to the back
  button when there are none); on a subregion's row it pins or releases it.
- **Enter** or **Space** on a legend step pins it; again releases it.
- **Escape** releases a pinned legend step first, then zooms back out and returns the focus to the region's row.
- The map is an image named "Map of United States shaded by revenue." with help text pointing to the list; the list carries
  the same data and is the way to explore by keyboard or screen reader.
- Each row is named by its rank, name and value ("1st, California, $9.8M. Open 58 counties"); negative values are read as
  "minus 4.8%". Subregion rows are toggle buttons that report whether they are pinned.
- Each legend step is a toggle button named by its count and range ("10 states $120K to $230K").
- A polite live region announces zooming in ("California, 58 counties ranked by revenue. Press Escape to zoom out."),
  zooming out, a new metric with its leader, a new country, and a pinned subregion with its value and rank.
- Values carry their sign and a true minus; the direction never depends on colour alone.
- Focus rings are 2px, outside the element, and only show for the keyboard.

## Motion

- **Metric switch**: each region's colour moves over 480 ms after a delay that grows from west to east (its centre's x over
  the map's width × 260 ms), so the new shading sweeps across the map in under 750 ms. The rows slide to their new ranks on a
  critically damped spring and every bar grows or shrinks over 580 ms; the texts cross-fade in 240 ms; the headline jumps.
- **Zooming in or out**: the camera's scale and position share one critically damped spring (about 800 ms, and it can turn
  around mid-flight). The other regions fade to 26% in 240 ms; the subregions fade in over 480 ms from 140 ms, so they
  appear while the camera still flies; leaving, they fade out in 160 ms. The headline counts to the new value in 480 ms.
- **Pointing**: the hover card fades in 160 ms and follows the pointer; the list glides to centre the region's row. On the
  legend, the lit step grows to 1.6× its height and the other regions fade to 14% and the other rows to 32% in 240 ms.
- **Changing the country**: the old map fades out in 180 ms and the new one fades in from west to east; the list fades out
  and back in.
- Reduced motion keeps only the text cross-fades: colours, camera, rows, bars and the hover card change at once. Off applies
  every change at once.

## Related

- `SegmentedControl` and `MorphSelect`, the switches in the header.
- `Metric explorer` and `Revenue explorer`, the other Analytics blocks that break a number down.
- `Revenue globe` for a 3D view of revenue by location.

# Connected scatter

> Two measures that move together, drawn as one path: a head point you scrub or play along the months, readouts that count with it, a target line that tints the healthy side, and a switch that morphs the whole path from one series to another.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc.Blocks`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc.Blocks --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/blocks/connected-scatter

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ConnectedScatterPreviewDemo">
    <!-- Three channels over eighteen months, July 2024 to December 2025. Data: ConnectedScatterDemoData. -->
    <arc:ConnectedScatter x:Name="Scatter"
                          Title="Unit economics by channel"
                          TargetRatio="3" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class ConnectedScatterPreviewDemo : UserControl
{
    public ConnectedScatterPreviewDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Scatter.XAxis = ConnectedScatterDemoData.CostAxis();
        Scatter.YAxis = ConnectedScatterDemoData.ValueAxis();
        Scatter.Series.AddRange(ConnectedScatterDemoData.Channels());
    }
}
```

## When to use

`ConnectedScatter` shows how two measures change **together** over time. Each month is a point at (x, y), the points are
joined in time order by a smooth curve with a small arrow on every segment long enough to hold one, and a head point
marks the month you are looking at. Where a line chart would show two separate lines, the path shows the relationship:
which way the pair is travelling, where it turned and where it crossed a threshold.

- **Unit economics.** Acquisition cost against the value of a customer, with a target ratio: the path crosses the
  target line when a channel goes from paying back to losing money.
- **Trade-offs over time.** Price and conversion, latency and throughput, headcount and output: any pair where the
  direction of travel matters more than either value alone.
- **Comparing channels.** The segment switch morphs the same months from one series to the next, so the eye follows
  what changed.
- **Presenting a story.** Play walks the head through the months at a steady pace, and the first appearance draws the
  whole path once.

## When not to use

- **One measure over time.** Use a line or area chart (`Metrics dashboard`, `Revenue explorer`); a path adds nothing
  when the other axis is time.
- **Many series at once.** One path is drawn at a time. Overlapping several loops is unreadable; use the switch, or a
  small multiples layout.
- **Unordered points.** The curve implies an order. For categories without a sequence use a plain scatter plot.
- **Hundreds of points.** The block is designed for roughly 8 to 36 months per series; every point has a dot and an
  arrow, and the scrubber has one stop per month.

## Usage

The block derives from Avalonia's `TemplatedControl`. Its data is a list of `ScatterSeries`; each series has a `Name`, an
optional `Key` and its `ScatterPoint`s in time order (`Label`, `X`, `Y`). Every series should have the same number of
months, so the switch can move each point to its counterpart. The two axes are `ScatterAxis` objects.

```xml
<arc:ConnectedScatter Title="Unit economics by channel" TargetRatio="3">
    <arc:ConnectedScatter.XAxis>
        <arc:ScatterAxis Name="CAC" Title="Customer acquisition cost" Minimum="300" Maximum="1900" Step="200" />
    </arc:ConnectedScatter.XAxis>
    <arc:ConnectedScatter.YAxis>
        <arc:ScatterAxis Name="LTV" Title="12 month customer value" Minimum="1000" Maximum="6000" Step="1000" />
    </arc:ConnectedScatter.YAxis>
    <arc:ScatterSeries Name="Field sales" Key="field-sales">
        <arc:ScatterPoint Label="Jul 2024" X="1150" Y="3600" />
        <arc:ScatterPoint Label="Aug 2024" X="1175" Y="3630" />
    </arc:ScatterSeries>
</arc:ConnectedScatter>
```

```csharp
scatter.Series.Add(new ScatterSeries("Community", points, "community"));
scatter.SelectedSeriesKey = "community";   // the points morph to the new series
```

`SeriesSource` takes a collection you own instead (an `ObservableCollection` is followed). With one series the switch is
hidden.

### Anatomy

- **Header**: `Title`, the description (`Description`, or a sentence written from the axes and the first and last month)
  and the series switch.
- **Readouts**: four cells that count with the head: the month and its place ("18 of 18"), the two values with their
  change since the first month ("+$200 since Jan 2025", or "Same as Jan 2025"), and the ratio with a status dot and
  "Above 3x target" or "Below 3x target". The status is always written out, never only a color.
- **Chart**: the vertical axis title and the legend (the path, the target line, the healthy zone), the plot, and the
  horizontal axis title under it at the right.
- **Transport**: a Play, Pause or Replay button and the scrubber with the quarter labels under it.

### Axes and the target line

`ScatterAxis` ranges and steps are used exactly as written: no rounding to nice numbers and no forced zero, so a zoomed
axis starts where you say. Leave `Minimum`, `Maximum` and `Step` unset (NaN) to derive them from the data of every series, so
the axes stay still while the series changes. Ticks of a step that is a multiple of 1,000 read "$2k"; others use the block's
`ValueFormatter`; `TickFormatter` replaces both.

`TargetRatio` draws the dashed line y = k · x through the origin, labels it ("3x CAC"), tints the side above it and writes
"Healthy, above 3x" in its corner. The ratio readout and the card color follow the same test on the unrounded values. NaN
removes the line, the zone, the status and their legend items.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ConnectedScatterTargetDemo">
    <!--
        A stricter target (4x) and a zoomed horizontal axis: the ranges and the step are used exactly as given, so the plot
        can start at $600 and the target line enters through the left edge instead of the bottom.
    -->
    <arc:ConnectedScatter x:Name="Scatter"
                          Title="Channels against a 4x target"
                          TargetRatio="4"
                          SelectedSeriesKey="resellers" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class ConnectedScatterTargetDemo : UserControl
{
    public ConnectedScatterTargetDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Scatter.XAxis = new ScatterAxis("CAC", "Customer acquisition cost", 900, 1800, 100);
        Scatter.YAxis = new ScatterAxis("LTV", "12 month customer value", 3500, 6000, 500);
        Scatter.Series.AddRange(ConnectedScatterDemoData.Channels());
    }
}
```

### The head, the scrubber and playback

The head point sits on the real curve, not on a straight line between months. **Pressing** the scrubber slides the head to
the pointer on the Smooth spring; once it has caught up it follows 1:1 while you drag, and **releasing** snaps it to the
nearest month. The keys, a tap on a point and the end of playback also settle the head on a month. `MonthChanged` is raised
at that moment, never frame by frame, with the index, the series and the point; `MonthChangedCommand` runs with the same
arguments. `SelectedIndex` is two-way (−1 means the last month) and `Position` is the continuous position, including the
fractions while the head moves.

**Play** moves the head one month per `PlaybackMonthDuration` (240 ms) at a constant pace from where it is, or from the
first month when it is at the last one. **Pause** stops it between two months; the readouts name the nearest month and the
values are interpolated. At the last month the button becomes **Replay**.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ConnectedScatterEventsDemo">
    <!--
        The month and the series are two-way properties and every settled change is an event: it is raised when the head is
        released, a key moves it, a point is tapped or playback ends, never while it moves. The buttons drive the block from
        outside; the log shows what it reports.
    -->
    <StackPanel Spacing="12">
        <StackPanel Orientation="Horizontal" Spacing="8">
            <arc:Button x:Name="Play" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Content="Play" />
            <arc:Button x:Name="Pause" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Content="Pause" />
            <arc:Button x:Name="Replay" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Content="Replay the first run" />
            <arc:Button x:Name="Middle" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Content="Go to Mar 2025" />
        </StackPanel>
        <arc:ConnectedScatter x:Name="Scatter"
                              Title="Unit economics by channel"
                              TargetRatio="3" />
        <TextBlock x:Name="Log"
                   TextWrapping="Wrap"
                   FontSize="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TypeXS}"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}"
                   Text="Events appear here." />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class ConnectedScatterEventsDemo : UserControl
{
    private readonly List<string> _lines = new();

    public ConnectedScatterEventsDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Scatter.XAxis = ConnectedScatterDemoData.CostAxis();
        Scatter.YAxis = ConnectedScatterDemoData.ValueAxis();
        Scatter.Series.AddRange(ConnectedScatterDemoData.Channels());

        Play.Click += (_, _) => Scatter.Play();
        Pause.Click += (_, _) => Scatter.Pause();
        Replay.Click += (_, _) => Scatter.ReplayDrawIn();
        Middle.Click += (_, _) => Scatter.GoToMonth(8);

        Scatter.MonthChanged += (_, e) =>
        {
            var point = e.Point;
            Write(point is null
                ? $"Month {e.Index + 1}"
                : $"Month {e.Index + 1} of {e.Series?.Name}: {point.Label}, CAC ${point.X:N0}, LTV ${point.Y:N0}, {point.Y / point.X:0.0}x");
        };
        Scatter.SeriesChanged += (_, e) => Write($"Series: {e.Series?.Name}");
    }

    private void Write(string line)
    {
        _lines.Insert(0, line);
        if (_lines.Count > 5)
        {
            _lines.RemoveAt(_lines.Count - 1);
        }
        Log.Text = string.Join(Environment.NewLine, _lines);
    }
}
```

### First appearance

The first time a quarter of the block is on screen, the head runs from the first month to the last in
`DrawInDuration` (1.35 s, in-out), drawing the trail behind it; when it lands, the dashed future path, the hollow dots, the
future arrows and the labels fade in together over 240 ms. Set `PlayOnFirstAppear="False"` to start at rest on the last
month, or call `ReplayDrawIn()` to show it again. Reduced and Off motion skip it.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ConnectedScatterMinimalDemo">
    <!--
        The smallest useful block: two series without notes and no axis settings. The axes take their ranges and ticks from the
        data, the description is written from the axis names and the first and last month, and the first run is left out
        (PlayOnFirstAppear is false), so the head rests on the last month.
    -->
    <arc:ConnectedScatter x:Name="Scatter"
                          Title="Cost against value"
                          PlayOnFirstAppear="False" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

{

    {

        Scatter.Series.AddRange(ConnectedScatterDemoData.PlainChannels());
    }
}
```

### Hovering, tapping and the card

Point within 30 px of a month to see a halo and a card with the month and the two values and their ratio. The card does not
move the head; between points it glides. Tapping or clicking a point moves the head there on the spring; on a touch
screen the card shows while the finger is down.

### Labels, notes and narrow containers

The first and the last month are labeled on the outer ends of the path, the last one always in Medium. A `ScatterNote`
adds an event label ("Pricing change") to a month, on the side you choose. The block reads its own width: under 720 the
readouts form a 2 × 2 grid and the plot is 330 high; under 560 the quarter labels shrink to the first, the Januaries and
the last month; under 480 the plot is 300 high, notes, the target label and the zone label go, every second tick of the
horizontal axis is skipped, and the scrubber moves under the button; under 380 the values are 18px.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ConnectedScatterNarrowDemo">
    <!--
        The block reads its own width. In a 400-wide column the readouts are a 2 x 2 grid, the chart is 300 high without notes,
        the target label and the zone label, the horizontal ticks skip every other one, the legend wraps, the paddings are 16
        and the scrubber sits under the play button.
    -->
    <Border Width="400" HorizontalAlignment="Left">
        <arc:ConnectedScatter x:Name="Scatter"
                              Title="Unit economics by channel"
                              TargetRatio="3" />
    </Border>
</UserControl>
```


### Formats and words

`ValueFormatter` and `RatioFormatter` replace "$1,234" and "4.8x" in the readouts, the card, the table and the
announcements. Every visible word is a property with an English default: the readout names, the "since" and "of" notes,
the status words, the target and zone texts, the legend, the button's texts and names, the screen reader table and the
announcement formats. Month names that read as "Jan 2025" get quarter labels under the scrubber; others get about six
evenly spaced ones.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ConnectedScatterWeeklyDemo">
    <!--
        Nothing is tied to dollars or months: weeks, euros and a 2.5x target with its own formats and words. Month names that
        are not "Jan 2025" style get about six evenly spaced labels under the scrubber.
    -->
    <arc:ConnectedScatter x:Name="Scatter"
                          Title="Paid social: spend and revenue"
                          MonthName="Week"
                          TargetRatio="2.5"
                          PlayOnFirstAppear="False"
                          AboveTargetFormat="{}Paying back above {0}"
                          BelowTargetFormat="{}Under the {0} goal"
                          ZoneLabelFormat="{}On target, above {0}"
                          TargetLegendFormat="{}Revenue = {0} spend"
                          TargetLabelFormat="{}{0} spend"
                          ZoneLegendText="On target"
                          PlayText="Run" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using System.Globalization;
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class ConnectedScatterWeeklyDemo : UserControl
{
    private static readonly CultureInfo s_culture = CultureInfo.GetCultureInfo("de-DE");

    public ConnectedScatterWeeklyDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Scatter.ValueFormatter = value => value.ToString("N0", s_culture) + " €";
        Scatter.RatioFormatter = ratio => ratio.ToString("0.00", CultureInfo.InvariantCulture) + "×";
        Scatter.XAxis = new ScatterAxis("Spend", "Weekly ad spend", 6000, 16000, 2000);
        Scatter.YAxis = new ScatterAxis("Revenue", "Weekly revenue", 16000, 40000, 8000);
        Scatter.XAxis.TickFormatter = value => (value / 1000).ToString("0", CultureInfo.InvariantCulture) + "k €";
        Scatter.YAxis.TickFormatter = value => (value / 1000).ToString("0", CultureInfo.InvariantCulture) + "k €";
        Scatter.Series.AddRange(ConnectedScatterDemoData.Weekly());
    }
}
```
