## API reference

### ConnectedScatter

Connected scatter: two measures that move together over time, drawn as one path. Each month is a point, joined in time order by a smooth curve with a small arrow on every segment long enough to hold one; a head point marks the current month and a scrubber under the chart moves it along the real curve. A dashed target line (y = k · x) splits the plot and the healthy side is tinted. A segment switch changes the series (point by point morph), the four readouts above count with the head, and Play walks the head through the months at a steady pace. The first time the block is on screen the head runs from the first month to the last and leaves its trail behind.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Title` | `string?` | `null` | The heading; null leaves it out. |
| `Description` | `string?` | `null` | The line under the heading; null writes one from the axis names and the first and last month. |
| `SeriesSource` | `IEnumerable?` | `null` | The series as a list you own (followed when it raises collection changes); it wins over `Series`. |
| `SelectedSeriesKey` | `string?` | `null` | The key of the series shown (two-way); null shows the first one. Changing it morphs the points. |
| `XAxis` | `ScatterAxis?` | `null` | The horizontal axis; null derives everything from the data. |
| `YAxis` | `ScatterAxis?` | `null` | The vertical axis; null derives everything from the data. |
| `TargetRatio` | `double` | `3` | The target line's slope (y = ratio · x); the side above it is tinted as healthy. NaN leaves out the line, the zone and the status. Default 3. |
| `ValueFormatter` | `Func<double, string>?` | `null` | Formats a value for the readouts, the card, the table and the announcements; null gives whole dollars ("$1,234"). |
| `RatioFormatter` | `Func<double, string>?` | `null` | Formats the ratio; null gives one decimal and an x ("4.8x"). |
| `SelectedIndex` | `int` | `-1` | The month the head rests on (two-way): −1 (default) means the last month, or, until the first draw-in ends, nothing yet. Setting it moves the head there on the Smooth spring. |
| `PlayOnFirstAppear` | `bool` | `true` | Whether the first time the block is on screen the head runs from the first month to the last (default true). Reduced and Off motion show the end at once. |
| `DrawInDuration` | `TimeSpan` | `00:00:01.3500000` | How long the first run takes, with the in-out easing (default 1.35s). |
| `PlaybackMonthDuration` | `TimeSpan` | `00:00:00.2400000` | How long playback stays on one month (default 240ms, constant speed). |
| `MonthName` | `string` | `"Month"` | The name of the month readout cell. |
| `RatioName` | `string?` | `null` | The ratio's name in the readouts and the card; null writes "{Y name} to {X name}". |
| `RatioNameFormat` | `string` | `"{0} to {1}"` | The automatic ratio name; {0} the vertical axis's name, {1} the horizontal one's. |
| `MonthOfFormat` | `string` | `"{0} of {1}"` | The month readout's note; {0} the month's number, {1} how many months. |
| `SinceFormat` | `string` | `"{0} since {1}"` | A value readout's note; {0} the signed change, {1} the first month's name. |
| `SameAsFormat` | `string` | `"Same as {0}"` | A value readout's note while it equals the first month; {0} the first month's name. |
| `AboveTargetFormat` | `string` | `"Above {0} target"` | The ratio readout's note above the target; {0} the target ("3x"). |
| `BelowTargetFormat` | `string` | `"Below {0} target"` | The ratio readout's note below the target; {0} the target. |
| `TargetLabelFormat` | `string` | `"{0} {1}"` | The target line's label; {0} the target ("3x"), {1} the horizontal axis's name. |
| `TargetLegendFormat` | `string` | `"{2} = {0} {1}"` | The legend text of the target line; {0} the target, {1} the horizontal axis's name, {2} the vertical one's. |
| `ZoneLabelFormat` | `string` | `"Healthy, above {0}"` | The label in the healthy zone's corner; {0} the target. |
| `ZoneLegendText` | `string` | `"Healthy zone"` | The legend text of the healthy zone. |
| `SeriesLegendFormat` | `string` | `"{0}, in time order"` | The legend text of the path; {0} the series' name. |
| `DescriptionFormat` | `string` | `"{0} against {1}, {2} to {3}."` | The automatic description; {0} the vertical axis, {1} the horizontal axis, {2} the first month, {3} the last month. |
| `PlayText` | `string` | `"Play"` | The play button's text before the last month. |
| `PauseText` | `string` | `"Pause"` | The play button's text while playing. |
| `ReplayText` | `string` | `"Replay"` | The play button's text at the last month. |
| `PlayLabel` | `string` | `"Play month by month"` | The play button's screen reader name before the last month. |
| `PauseLabel` | `string` | `"Pause"` | The play button's screen reader name while playing. |
| `ReplayLabel` | `string` | `"Replay from the first month"` | The play button's screen reader name at the last month. |
| `ScrubberLabel` | `string` | `"Month"` | The screen reader name of the scrubber. |
| `SeriesSwitchLabel` | `string` | `"Series"` | The screen reader name of the series switch. |
| `TableCaptionFormat` | `string` | `"{0}: {1} and {2} by month"` | The screen reader table's caption; {0} the series, {1} the horizontal axis's title, {2} the vertical one's. |
| `MonthAnnouncementFormat` | `string` | `"{0}: {1} {2}, {3} {4}, {5}, {6}."` | What is said (and what the scrubber's value text is) for a month; {0} the month, {1} / {2} the horizontal axis's name and value, {3} / {4} the vertical axis's, {5} the ratio, {6} the status ("above the 3x target"). |
| `SeriesAnnouncementFormat` | `string` | `"{0}. {1}"` | Said when another series is chosen; {0} the series, {1} the month's announcement. |
| `AboveAnnouncementFormat` | `string` | `"above the {0} target"` | The status words of the announcement; {0} the target ("above the 3x target"). |
| `BelowAnnouncementFormat` | `string` | `"below the {0} target"` | The status words of the announcement; {0} the target. |
| `MonthChangedCommand` | `ICommand?` | `null` | Run when the head settles on a month, with the `ScatterMonthChangedEventArgs` as the parameter. |
| `Position` | `double` | – | *Read-only.* The head's continuous month position (0 to months − 1): fractions while it moves. |
| `IsPlaying` | `bool` | – | *Read-only.* True while playback runs. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `MonthChanged` | `ScatterMonthChangedEventArgs` | Raised when the head settles on a month (released, a key, a tap, the end of playback), never while it moves. |
| `SeriesChanged` | `ScatterSeriesChangedEventArgs` | Raised when another series is chosen. |

Pseudo-classes: `:playing`, `:narrow`, `:compact`, `:empty`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

### ScatterSeries

One channel of a `ConnectedScatter`: a name and one `ScatterPoint` per month in time order. Every series of a block should have the same number of months, so that switching between them can morph point by point; with different counts the block replaces the drawing instead.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Key` | `string?` | `null` | A stable identifier (selection, events); defaults to the name. |
| `Name` | `string` | `""` | The channel's name, on the switch and in the legend. |
| `Tag` | `object?` | `null` | Anything you want to carry along (it comes back in the events). |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Changed` | `EventHandler?` | Raised when the series, its points or its notes change. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### ScatterPoint

One month of a `ScatterSeries`: the two values that move together.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Label` | `string` | `""` | The month's name ("Mar 2025"); it is also what the scrubber, the readout and the card say. |
| `ShortLabel` | `string?` | `null` | The short name under the scrubber ("Mar"); null derives it from `Label`. |
| `X` | `double` | `0` | The value on the horizontal axis (acquisition cost in the reference). |
| `Y` | `double` | `0` | The value on the vertical axis (customer value in the reference). |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Changed` | `EventHandler?` | Raised when any property of the point changes. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### ScatterNote

A short text written next to one month of a series ("Pricing change"), shown while the viewport is wide enough.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Index` | `int` | `0` | The month's index in the series, from 0. |
| `Text` | `string` | `""` | The text. |
| `Side` | `ScatterLabelSide` | `Top` | Which side of the point the text goes on. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Changed` | `EventHandler?` | Raised when any property of the note changes. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### ScatterAxis

One axis of a `ConnectedScatter`. The range and the step are used exactly as given (no rounding to nice numbers, not forced to start at zero); leave them unset to derive them from the data of every series.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Name` | `string` | `""` | The short name in the readout and the card ("CAC"). |
| `Title` | `string?` | `null` | The title of the axis ("Customer acquisition cost"). |
| `Minimum` | `double` | `NaN` | The lowest value shown; NaN (default) takes it from the data. |
| `Maximum` | `double` | `NaN` | The highest value shown; NaN (default) takes it from the data. |
| `Step` | `double` | `NaN` | The distance between ticks; NaN (default) picks a step that gives four to six ticks. |
| `TickFormatter` | `Func<double, string>?` | `null` | Formats a tick; null gives "$2k" for steps that are multiples of 1,000 and the block's value format otherwise. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Changed` | `EventHandler?` | Raised when any property of the axis changes. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### ScatterLabelSide

Which side of its point an annotation (or a first / last month label) is written on.

Derives from `Enum`: every member of `Enum` works as well.

### ScatterMonthChangedEventArgs

Reports that the head point settled on a month (released, a key, a tap, the end of playback), never while it moves.

Derives from `RoutedEventArgs`: every member of `RoutedEventArgs` works as well.

### ScatterSeriesChangedEventArgs

Reports that another series was chosen.

Derives from `RoutedEventArgs`: every member of `RoutedEventArgs` works as well.

## Accessibility

- The scrubber is a slider named "Month" from 1 to the number of months, with a value text for the settled month: "Dec 2025:
  CAC $960, LTV $4,640, 4.8x, above the 3x target." It is updated when the head settles, not while it moves or plays.
- A polite live region says the same text for every settled month, and "Series name. …" when the series changes; playback
  is announced where it stops.
- The chart is hidden detail for screen readers, as is the card; a table lists every month with the two values and the
  ratio, with a caption naming the series and the axes.
- Every control has a name; the play button's name follows its state ("Play month by month", "Pause", "Replay from the
  first month"). The target and the status are written as words.
- Colors come from the theme in both light and dark; the dots, arrows and labels keep their contrast on the tinted zone.

### Keyboard

- **Tab** moves to the series switch (one stop, the selected series), the play button and the scrubber. The chart takes no
  focus.
- On the scrubber **← ↓** go one month back and **→ ↑** one month on; **PageUp** goes three months on and **PageDown** three
  back; **Home** and **End** go to the first and the last month. The keys stop at the ends. From a position between two
  months they go to the next whole month in the direction pressed. Each key moves the head on the Smooth spring and
  settles on a month.
- In the series switch **← →** change the selection at once and wrap around; **↑ ↓** go to the previous and the next
  series; **Home** and **End** go to the ends.
- **Enter** or **Space** on the button plays, pauses or replays.
- The focus ring is drawn only for keyboard focus; a pointer press on the scrubber does not show it.

## Motion

- **First run**: the head runs 1.35 s on the in-out curve, the readouts and the scrubber follow it; on landing the future
  layers fade in together over 240 ms.
- **Head**: a key, a tap, a release and a series switch all use the Smooth spring (no overshoot, about 0.65 s); pressing the
  scrubber chases the pointer and then follows it 1:1. While playing or dragging the head's halo grows to 1.25× on a 580 ms
  spring curve.
- **Playback**: constant speed, 240 ms a month; pausing keeps the fractional position.
- **Series switch**: every point, arrow and the curve itself spring to the new series at the same time on the Smooth
  spring; the readouts count; the old labels fade out in 180 ms and the new ones in over 240 ms after that.
- **Hover**: the halo fades in 160 ms; the card fades in place and glides on a 580 ms spring curve between points.
- **Scrubber thumb**: 1.08× on hover, 1.12× pressed; its center dot grows 1.5× on keyboard focus.
- Reduced motion skips the first run and the glides: playback jumps one month every 960 ms, keys and taps jump, a series
  switch replaces the points at once, and only short fades stay. Off applies everything at once.

## Related

- `Metrics dashboard`, `KPI drilldown` and `Revenue explorer`, the other Analytics blocks.
- `SegmentedControl`, the switch the block uses.
- `Line replay`, another block that plays a series through time.

# Horizon chart

> Many daily series compared by how far each strays from its own baseline, folded into one thin band row each: the band count folds and unfolds every row on one spring, rows re-sort by name, peak or latest value, and one crosshair reads the same day across every row for the pointer, touch and the keyboard.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc.Blocks`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc.Blocks --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/blocks/horizon-chart

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.HorizonChartPreviewDemo">
    <!-- Fourteen fulfilment hubs, 119 days, against their winter forecast. Data: HorizonChartDemoData. -->
    <arc:HorizonChart x:Name="Chart"
                      Title="Orders against forecast"
                      Description="Daily orders at each fulfilment hub compared with its winter forecast, February to May 2027"
                      BaselineLabel="winter forecast" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class HorizonChartPreviewDemo : UserControl
{
    public HorizonChartPreviewDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Chart.Days = HorizonChartDemoData.OrderDays();
        Chart.Series.AddRange(HorizonChartDemoData.OrderSeries());
    }
}
```

## When to use

`HorizonChart` answers "which of these many series is off, when, and by how much" on one screen. Every row is a daily
series measured against its own baseline (a forecast, a target, an average); the distance above the baseline fills in one
colour and the distance below in another, and the distance is folded into bands that are stacked on one thin strip, so a
row costs 36px instead of a full chart. Fourteen rows of 119 days fit in about 550px.

- **Fleets of similar things.** Stores, hubs, regions, services or campaigns against their own plan: the eye finds the rows
  with a dark band and the day it happened.
- **Spotting shared events.** The crosshair crosses every row, so an outage, a promotion or a holiday that touches several
  rows shows as one vertical line with the same day's value written at the end of each row.
- **Dense dashboards.** Where a line chart per row would be too tall, and a table of numbers too flat.

## When not to use

- **A few series.** With three or four rows, a line chart shows the same thing with a scale you can read.
- **Absolute levels.** The rows are deviations from a baseline; the baseline's own level is not drawn. Show levels in a line
  or area chart.
- **Reading exact values off the shape.** The strips are for finding; the numbers come from the crosshair and the value
  column.
- **Many hundreds of days or more than about 40 rows.** Aggregate (weeks instead of days) before showing more: the block
  does not.

## Usage

The block derives from Avalonia's `TemplatedControl`. Its data is a list of `HorizonSeries` (a name and one signed value
per day: positive above the baseline, negative below it) and the `Days` they line up with, oldest first. A `HorizonDay`
carries a `Label` ("Sep 27"), a `LongLabel` ("Sunday, September 27") and an optional `Date`; when only the date is set the
labels are formatted from it.

```xml
<arc:HorizonChart Title="Orders against forecast"
                  Description="Daily orders at each hub compared with its winter forecast"
                  BaselineLabel="winter forecast"
                  Days="{Binding Days}">
    <arc:HorizonSeries Name="Northgate" Values="{Binding NorthgateValues}" />
    <arc:HorizonSeries Name="Harbor Point" Values="{Binding HarborPointValues}" />
</arc:HorizonChart>
```

```csharp
chart.Days = Enumerable.Range(0, 119).Select(i => new HorizonDay(start.AddDays(i))).ToArray();
chart.Series.Add(new HorizonSeries("Northgate", values, key: "northgate"));
chart.Bands = 2;
chart.Sort = HorizonSort.Latest;
```

`SeriesSource` takes a collection you own instead (an `ObservableCollection` is followed). The axis shows a tick on the
first day and on every first of a month for days that carry a date; set `Ticks` (index and label) to place your own. A
value of NaN draws as zero and reads as a dash.

### How the bands work

Each row is one polygon, drawn as many times as there are bands. `Extent` is the distance that fills every band: by default
the largest absolute value rounded up to a multiple of 12 (36 when the largest swing is 35). With three bands each band
spans a third of the extent, so a value of 12 fills the first band, 24 the second and 36 the third; each layer is drawn
with alpha `1 − 0.08^(1/bands)`, which stacks to 0.92 where all bands are full. Darker colour therefore means further from
the baseline, and one band is an ordinary area chart.

The band count is a continuous value while it folds: every row's four layers and the alpha follow one spring (a
critically damped spring that settles in about 600ms), so a change in the middle of a fold carries on from where it is.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.HorizonChartPaletteDemo">
    <!--
        Your own colours for the two sides, four bands, the switches hidden so the state comes from the page: here the
        buttons drive Sort and Bands, and the chart is read by the pointer, touch or the keyboard as usual.
    -->
    <StackPanel Spacing="12">
        <StackPanel Orientation="Horizontal" Spacing="8">
            <arc:Button x:Name="ByName" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Content="By name" />
            <arc:Button x:Name="ByPeak" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Content="By peak" />
            <arc:Button x:Name="OneBand" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Content="One band" />
            <arc:Button x:Name="FourBands" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Content="Four bands" />
        </StackPanel>
        <arc:HorizonChart x:Name="Chart"
                          Title="Orders against forecast"
                          BaselineLabel="winter forecast"
                          Bands="4"
                          IsSortSwitchVisible="False"
                          IsBandSwitchVisible="False" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class HorizonChartPaletteDemo : UserControl
{
    public HorizonChartPaletteDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Chart.AboveColor = Avalonia.Media.Color.Parse("#7C3AED");
        Chart.BelowColor = Avalonia.Media.Color.Parse("#0D9488");
        Chart.Days = HorizonChartDemoData.OrderDays();
        Chart.Series.AddRange(HorizonChartDemoData.OrderSeries());
        ByName.Click += (_, _) => Chart.Sort = HorizonSort.Name;
        ByPeak.Click += (_, _) => Chart.Sort = HorizonSort.Peak;
        OneBand.Click += (_, _) => Chart.Bands = 1;
        FourBands.Click += (_, _) => Chart.Bands = 4;
    }
}
```

### Sorting

`Sort` is `Name` (A to Z), `Peak` (the row's largest absolute value first, the default) or `Latest` (the last day's value,
highest first). Ties keep the data order. On a change every row moves to its new place on one spring at the same time and
the numbers move with it; the crosshair and the band count are not affected.

### The crosshair

Move the pointer over the band column (the name and value columns do not react) to put the crosshair on a day: the date
above the chart and the value at the end of every row change to that day at once, and the status line says "Picked day".
The line appears where the pointer is, then follows it on a quick spring; when the pointer leaves it fades and the
readout returns to the most recent day. On touch, a tap or a horizontal drag sets the crosshair and it stays after you
lift; a tap beside the chart clears it. `SelectedDayIndex` is two-way, `SelectDay` and `ClearSelection` drive it from
code, and `DayChanged` and `DayCommand` report every change.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.HorizonChartEventsDemo">
    <!--
        Sort, Bands and SelectedDayIndex are two-way properties and every change is an event. Here buttons set the crosshair
        and the band count from outside, and the log shows what the block reports (pointer, touch and keys included).
    -->
    <StackPanel Spacing="12">
        <StackPanel Orientation="Horizontal" Spacing="8">
            <arc:Button x:Name="FirstDay" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Content="Go to the first day" />
            <arc:Button x:Name="LastWeek" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Content="Go to the last week" />
            <arc:Button x:Name="Clear" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Content="Clear the crosshair" />
        </StackPanel>
        <arc:HorizonChart x:Name="Chart"
                          Title="Orders against forecast"
                          BaselineLabel="winter forecast" />
        <TextBlock x:Name="Log"
                   TextWrapping="Wrap"
                   FontSize="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TypeXS}"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}"
                   Text="Events appear here." />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class HorizonChartEventsDemo : UserControl
{
    private readonly List<string> _lines = new();

    public HorizonChartEventsDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Chart.Days = HorizonChartDemoData.OrderDays();
        Chart.Series.AddRange(HorizonChartDemoData.OrderSeries());
        Chart.SortChanged += (_, e) => Write($"Sort: {e.Sort}");
        Chart.BandsChanged += (_, e) => Write($"Bands: {e.Bands}");
        Chart.DayChanged += (_, e) => Write(e.Day is { } day ? $"Day {e.Index}: {day.ShortText}" : "Crosshair cleared");
        FirstDay.Click += (_, _) => Chart.SelectDay(0);
        LastWeek.Click += (_, _) => Chart.SelectDay(Chart.Days!.Count - 7);
        Clear.Click += (_, _) => Chart.ClearSelection();
    }

    private void Write(string line)
    {
        _lines.Add(line);
        if (_lines.Count > 4)
        {
            _lines.RemoveAt(0);
        }
        Log.Text = string.Join("  ·  ", _lines);
    }
}
```

### Formatting values and other units

`ValueFormatter` formats the row values, the scale's end labels and the spoken texts; the default writes a signed whole
percent with a real minus sign. Set `Extent` when you want a round band edge that does not depend on the data.

```csharp
chart.ValueFormatter = v => v switch { > 0 => $"+{v:0} ms", < 0 => $"−{-v:0} ms", _ => "0 ms" };
chart.Extent = 60;
```

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.HorizonChartLatencyDemo">
    <!--
        Twenty services, 90 days, in milliseconds above or below each service's latency target. ValueFormatter writes the
        unit, the extent is set by hand (a 60 ms band edge), two bands are enough for this many rows and the rows start in
        order of their latest value.
    -->
    <arc:HorizonChart x:Name="Chart"
                      Title="Latency against target"
                      Description="Median response time per service, June to August 2027"
                      BaselineLabel="latency target"
                      Bands="2"
                      Sort="Latest"
                      Extent="60" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class HorizonChartLatencyDemo : UserControl
{
    public HorizonChartLatencyDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Chart.ValueFormatter = value => Milliseconds(value);
        Chart.Days = HorizonChartDemoData.LatencyDays();
        Chart.Series.AddRange(HorizonChartDemoData.LatencySeries());
    }

    private static string Milliseconds(double value)
    {
        var rounded = (int)System.Math.Round(value);
        return rounded switch
        {
            > 0 => $"+{rounded} ms",
            < 0 => $"−{-rounded} ms",
            _ => "0 ms"
        };
    }
}
```

### Narrow containers

The block reads its own width. Up to 900 wide the name and value columns narrow (116 and 52); up to 560 the paddings drop
to 16, rows are 34px with 12px text and 84 / 44px columns, the switches share one line (or one each when they do not fit)
and the colour scale takes the whole line.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"

             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.HorizonChartCompactDemo">
    <!-- The breakpoints follow the block's own width: at 360 the rows shrink and the switches and the scale take whole lines. -->
    <Border Width="360" HorizontalAlignment="Left">
        <arc:HorizonChart x:Name="Chart"
                          Title="Orders against forecast"
                          Description="Daily orders at each fulfilment hub compared with its winter forecast"
                          BaselineLabel="winter forecast" />
    </Border>
</UserControl>
```


### Words

`Labels` holds every word the block writes or speaks (the switch labels, the status lines, the caption and its formats,
the announcements and the table's column names) with English defaults; assign a new `HorizonChartLabels` to translate or
reword it. `AboveColor` and `BelowColor` replace the Series1 and Series3 colours, and `IsSortSwitchVisible`,
`IsBandSwitchVisible` and `IsLegendVisible` hide parts when the page provides its own controls.

## API reference

### HorizonChart

Horizon chart: many daily series compared by how far each one strays from its own baseline, every series folded into one 28px band strip so a screenful of rows (markets, services, stores) reads at a glance. The distance above the baseline fills in one colour and the distance below in another; the strip is cut into bands that are stacked into one row height, and a darker colour means further away. One synchronized crosshair crosses every row and writes that day's value for each of them; the rows sort by name, by their largest swing or by their latest value, and the band count (1 to 4) folds or unfolds every row on one spring.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Title` | `string?` | `null` | The heading; null leaves it out. |
| `Description` | `string?` | `null` | The line under the heading (what the rows are and what they are compared with); null or empty leaves it out. |
| `SeriesSource` | `IEnumerable?` | `null` | The rows as a list you own (followed when it raises collection changes); it wins over `Series`. |
| `Days` | `IReadOnlyList<HorizonDay>?` | `null` | The days of the axis, oldest first; each row's values line up with them. Empty takes the longest row and numbers the days. |
| `Ticks` | `IReadOnlyList<HorizonTick>?` | `null` | The labelled ticks of the axis; null puts one on the first day and on every first of a month (days that carry a date). |
| `BaselineLabel` | `string?` | `null` | What the values are measured against ("winter forecast"), in the caption and the spoken texts; null takes `BaselineText`. |
| `Sort` | `HorizonSort` | `Peak` | The order of the rows (two-way). Default `Peak`. |
| `Bands` | `int` | `3` | How many bands each row folds into, 1 to 4 (two-way; other values are coerced). One band is an ordinary area chart. Default 3. |
| `Extent` | `double` | `NaN` | The distance from the baseline that fills every band; NaN (default) takes the largest absolute value rounded up to a multiple of 12. |
| `SelectedDayIndex` | `int?` | `null` | The day the crosshair is on (two-way); null hides it and shows the latest day. |
| `ValueFormatter` | `Func<double, string>?` | `null` | Formats a value for the rows, the scale and the spoken texts; null gives a signed whole percent ("+12%", "−8%", "0%"). |
| `AboveColor` | `Color?` | `null` | The colour of the distance above the baseline; null takes the Series1 token. |
| `BelowColor` | `Color?` | `null` | The colour of the distance below the baseline; null takes the Series3 token. |
| `IsSortSwitchVisible` | `bool` | `true` | Whether the sort switch is shown. |
| `IsBandSwitchVisible` | `bool` | `true` | Whether the band switch is shown. |
| `IsLegendVisible` | `bool` | `true` | Whether the colour scale and its caption are shown. |
| `Labels` | `HorizonChartLabels` | – | The words of the block, for translation or rewording. |
| `SortCommand` | `ICommand?` | `null` | Run when the order changes, with the new `HorizonSort` as the parameter. |
| `BandsCommand` | `ICommand?` | `null` | Run when the band count changes, with the new count as the parameter. |
| `DayCommand` | `ICommand?` | `null` | Run when the crosshair moves to a day or is cleared, with the day's index (or null) as the parameter. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `SortChanged` | `HorizonSortChangedEventArgs` | Raised after the order changed. |
| `BandsChanged` | `HorizonBandsChangedEventArgs` | Raised after the band count changed. |
| `DayChanged` | `HorizonDayChangedEventArgs` | Raised when the crosshair moves to another day or is cleared. |

Pseudo-classes: `:compact`, `:medium`, `:scrubbing`, `:empty`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

### HorizonSeries

One row of a `HorizonChart`: a name and one signed deviation from the baseline for each day.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Key` | `string?` | `null` | A stable identifier for the row (events and announcements); defaults to the name. |
| `Name` | `string` | `""` | The row's name (shown in the name column, ellipsized with its full text in a tooltip). |
| `Values` | `IReadOnlyList<double>` | – | One signed value per day: positive above the baseline, negative below it. NaN draws as zero and reads as missing. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### HorizonDay

One day of the horizontal axis of a `HorizonChart`, oldest first.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Label` | `string?` | `null` | The short label ("Sep 27"): the table and announcements. |
| `LongLabel` | `string?` | `null` | The long label ("Sunday, September 27"): the readout's heading. |
| `Date` | `DateOnly?` | `null` | The date; when the labels are not set they are formatted from it ("MMM d" and "dddd, MMMM d"). |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### HorizonTick

A labelled tick on the day axis of a `HorizonChart`.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Index` | `int` | `0` | The index of the day the tick marks. |
| `Label` | `string` | `""` | The tick's text ("Mar"). |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### HorizonChartLabels

Every word a `HorizonChart` writes or speaks besides the data, with English defaults. Placeholders are numbered as described on each property. Assign a new instance to `Labels` to translate the block.

### HorizonDayChangedEventArgs

Arguments of `SortChanged`.

Derives from `RoutedEventArgs`: every member of `RoutedEventArgs` works as well.

### HorizonBandsChangedEventArgs

Arguments of `BandsChanged`.

Derives from `RoutedEventArgs`: every member of `RoutedEventArgs` works as well.

### HorizonSort

Derives from `Enum`: every member of `Enum` works as well.

## Accessibility

- The chart is a focusable group named "{title}. {n} rows" with the key hint as its help text. The focus ring is drawn
  inside the chart, where the block's rounded clip cannot cut it.
- Keyboard moves of the crosshair are announced politely with the day and the highest and lowest rows: "Tuesday, March 16.
  Top Foxhollow +8%, bottom Northgate −31%." Sorting and a changed band count are announced too; moving the pointer is not.
- A hidden table lists every row in the current order with its latest, highest and lowest value and the day of each, so a
  screen reader can read the numbers without the shapes.
- The colour scale is an image with a spoken description ("Color scale from −36% under the forecast to +36% over it, 3
  bands per side"), and its caption says what one band is. Direction is also carried by the signed numbers, not only by
  colour.
- Both switches are named groups; their buttons are toggle buttons.

### Keyboard

- **Tab** goes to the sort switch, the band switch and the chart, one stop each. Tabbing into the chart puts the crosshair
  on the latest day.
- **← →** move the crosshair one day; **Shift + ← →** one week. It stops at the first and last day.
- **Home / End** jump to the first and last day.
- **Escape** hides the crosshair; the focus stays on the chart and the next arrow starts from the latest day.
- In both switches **← ↑** and **→ ↓** change the selection at once and wrap around; **Home / End** jump to the ends.

## Motion

- **Folding**: one spring (critically damped, 600ms to rest) carries every row's band count to its new value; the layers and
  their alpha follow it on every frame, nothing is rebuilt. A new target in mid-flight keeps the velocity. The colour
  scale's cells grow or shrink and change opacity over 480ms with an in-out curve, starting with the fold; its caption
  changes at once.
- **Sorting**: each row springs from where it was to where it belongs (about 700ms, no overshoot), all rows starting
  together; the rows paint an opaque ground, so a row sliding past another covers it.
- **Crosshair**: it appears in place and fades in over 160ms, follows the pointer or key on a quick critically damped
  spring (about 250ms to rest), and fades out in 160ms where it is when you leave. The text always changes at once.
- **Switches**: the selected pill glides on a non-overshooting spring.
- Nothing plays when the block first appears. Reduced motion and Off land every fold, reorder, crosshair move and scale
  change at once.

## Related

- `Metric explorer` and `Revenue explorer`, the other Analytics blocks with a crosshair across a time axis.
- `Cohort retention`, which also compares many rows over time with a colour scale.
- `SegmentedControl`, the switches the block uses.

# Market terminal

> A trading screen with a candlestick chart you zoom and pan, a live watchlist with sparklines and flashing prices, and a market and limit order ticket with its order list.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc.Blocks`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc.Blocks --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/blocks/market-terminal

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.MarketTerminalPreviewDemo">
    <!-- Eight invented symbols with live ticks, a small portfolio and two earlier orders. Data: MarketTerminalDemoData. -->
    <arc:MarketTerminal x:Name="Terminal" Margin="0,12" Ticker="ORBT" Range="SixMonths" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class MarketTerminalPreviewDemo : UserControl
{
    public MarketTerminalPreviewDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        MarketTerminalDemoData.Fill(Terminal);
    }
}
```

## When to use

`MarketTerminal` is the main screen of a product where one symbol is charted and traded at a time. The chart, the watchlist
and the ticket all read the same live price, so a tick moves the header, the row, the candle and the estimated cost
together.

- **A brokerage or investing app.** Pick a symbol from the watchlist, study its candles, then buy or sell from the ticket
  beside it.
- **Paper trading and teaching.** Everything runs on a local simulation by default: prices move, limit orders wait and fill
  on their own, and nothing leaves the screen.
- **An internal markets dashboard.** Inspect candles one by one with the keyboard, compare the 20 and 50 candle averages,
  and switch between today and a year in one click.

## When not to use

- **Order books and depth.** The block shows one live price per symbol, not bids and asks at each level.
- **Business metrics.** Revenue, sign-ups or usage have no open, high, low and close; use `LineChart` or `BarChart`.
- **Portfolio overviews.** A list of positions with gains and allocation needs a table, not a chart of one symbol.
- **Many symbols at once.** For a grid of small charts, use a `Sparkline` per symbol in a table.

## Usage

The block derives from Avalonia's `TemplatedControl`. Give it the watchlist as `MarketSymbol`s; each one has a ticker, a
name, the price now, yesterday's close, a daily volatility and an average volume. The candles of every range are generated
from those numbers, the same way every time for the same ticker, so the chart is stable across runs. `Holdings`,
`Orders` and `BuyingPower` fill the ticket.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:MarketTerminal Ticker="ORBT" Range="SixMonths" BuyingPower="18420.50">
        <arc:MarketSymbol Ticker="ORBT" Name="Orbital Freight" Price="184.53" PreviousClose="182.97" Volatility="0.024" />
        <arc:MarketSymbol Ticker="KLVN" Name="Kelvin Grid" Exchange="NYSE" Price="64.12" PreviousClose="64.80" />
        <arc:MarketTerminal.Holdings>
            <arc:MarketHolding Ticker="ORBT" Shares="120" />
        </arc:MarketTerminal.Holdings>
    </arc:MarketTerminal>
</UserControl>
```

### Anatomy

- **Header**: the ticker, the company name and its exchange; the price, which rolls digit by digit; today's change with an
  arrow; today's open, high, low and volume; and the Live button.
- **Toolbar**: the range switch (1D, 5D, 1M, 6M, 1Y), the two moving average toggles and the zoom in, zoom out and reset
  buttons.
- **Chart**: a readout line, the candles over a price grid, volume under them, the averages, the live price line with its
  tag, and the crosshair with its price and time tags.
- **Watchlist**: one row per symbol with its name, today's sparkline over a dotted line at yesterday's close, the price and
  today's change. The charted symbol's row is filled.
- **Ticket**: buy or sell, market or limit, the share count, the limit price (limit orders only), the price, the estimated
  cost or proceeds and the buying power or the shares held, a status line, the submit button and the order list.

### Ranges and the chart

`Range` picks the candles: `OneDay` uses today's 5 minute candles, `FiveDays` 30 minute candles, and `OneMonth`,
`SixMonths` and `OneYear` daily candles. Today is the same session on every range: the 30 minute and daily candles of today
are folded from the 5 minute ones, and a tick moves the live candle of every range together. `ShowMa20` and `ShowMa50`
show the moving averages (the toolbar toggles them, two-way).

The default window shows the whole range, thinned on narrow charts so candles stay at least five pixels apart. Scroll the
wheel to zoom around the pointer, drag to pan (a flick keeps moving and slows down), pinch on a touch screen, or use the
toolbar. Moving the pointer over the chart shows the crosshair and writes that candle into the readout.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.MarketTerminalIntradayDemo">
    <!-- Today in 5 minute candles, only the 20 candle average, and ticks every 600 ms. -->
    <arc:MarketTerminal x:Name="Terminal"
                        Margin="0,12"
                        Ticker="TIDE"
                        Range="OneDay"
                        ShowMa50="False"
                        TickInterval="0:0:0.6" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class MarketTerminalIntradayDemo : UserControl
{
    public MarketTerminalIntradayDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        MarketTerminalDemoData.Fill(Terminal);
    }
}
```

### Live prices

While `IsLive` is true the simulation steps every `TickInterval` (1.2 seconds by default): each price takes a small random
step, the header price rolls, the row's price flashes green or red, and the chart glides the live candle, its tag and the
averages to the new price. The Live button pauses and resumes the stream; ticks also stop while the block is not in a
window. To show real prices, keep `IsLive` false and call `SetPrice(ticker, price)` for each quote; `Tick()` advances
the simulation once.

### Orders

The ticket checks every order before the button can submit it: at least one share, a limit price above zero, enough buying
power for a buy and enough shares for a sell. The reason is written under the button.

- A **market order** fills at once at the live price.
- A **limit order** that can trade now fills at once at the better of the limit and the market; otherwise it is
  **working** and fills by itself when the price reaches the limit. A working order has a cancel button.
- A fill updates `BuyingPower` (two-way) and `Holdings`. `OrderPlaced`, `OrderFilled` and `OrderCanceled` report each step.

To place orders with a real service, set `PlaceOrderAction`. It receives a `MarketOrderRequest` and a cancellation token;
the button shows a spinner until the task finishes, and an exception keeps the order off the list and writes its message
under the button. `CancelOrderAction` does the same for a cancel. `SubmitOrderAsync()` and `CancelOrderAsync(order)` do
what the buttons do.

```csharp
terminal.PlaceOrderAction = (request, cancellation) => broker.PlaceAsync(request.Ticker, request.Side, request.Shares,
    request.Type == MarketOrderType.Limit ? request.Price : null, cancellation);
terminal.OrderFilled += (_, e) => portfolio.Refresh();
```

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.MarketTerminalOrderApiDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12" Margin="0,12">
        <arc:MarketTerminal x:Name="Terminal" Ticker="KLVN" Range="FiveDays" />
        <TextBlock x:Name="Log"
                   HorizontalAlignment="Center"
                   TextAlignment="Center"
                   TextWrapping="Wrap"
                   MaxWidth="560"
                   Text="Orders go through a pretend broker that answers in 0.8 seconds and turns down every third order." />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class MarketTerminalOrderApiDemo : UserControl
{
    private int _orders;

    public MarketTerminalOrderApiDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        MarketTerminalDemoData.Fill(Terminal);

        // A real app would call its broker here. The button stays busy while the task runs; an exception's message is
        // written under the button and the order is not placed.
        Terminal.PlaceOrderAction = async (request, cancellation) =>
        {
            await Task.Delay(800, cancellation);
            if (++_orders % 3 == 0)
            {
                throw new InvalidOperationException($"The broker turned down {request.Shares} {request.Ticker}: try a smaller order.");
            }
        };
        Terminal.CancelOrderAction = (_, cancellation) => Task.Delay(400, cancellation);

        Terminal.OrderPlaced += (_, e) => Log.Text = $"Placed: {e.Order.Side} {e.Order.Shares} {e.Order.Ticker} ({e.Order.Status})";
        Terminal.OrderFilled += (_, e) => Log.Text = $"Filled: {e.Order.Side} {e.Order.Shares} {e.Order.Ticker} at {e.Order.Price:0.00}";
        Terminal.OrderCanceled += (_, e) => Log.Text = $"Canceled: {e.Order.Side} {e.Order.Shares} {e.Order.Ticker}";
    }
}
```

### Narrow containers

they sit side by side under it; below that every card stacks. Under 640 the stats get their own row of four equal columns,

when it does not fit.

### Text

Every word comes from `Labels`, a `MarketTerminalLabels`. Replace it to localize the block: parameterized entries are
functions that receive formatted values, such as `Submit` for the button ("Buy 10 ORBT") or `NotEnoughShares` for the
status line.

## API reference

### MarketTerminal

A trading terminal screen. A candlestick chart with volume, two moving averages, a crosshair with an open, high, low and close readout, and wheel, drag and pinch zoom sits beside a watchlist with intraday sparklines and flashing live prices, and an order ticket for market and limit orders with an order list. Everything is simulated by default: candles are generated from each symbol's price, previous close and volatility, ticks are a random walk, and orders fill against the live price locally. Set `PlaceOrderAction` and `CancelOrderAction` (and feed prices with `SetPrice`) to connect it to a real service.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Ticker` | `string?` | `null` | The symbol charted and traded (two-way); null or unknown charts the first symbol. |
| `Range` | `MarketRange` | `SixMonths` | The chart's time range (two-way). One and five days use 5 and 30 minute candles; the rest are daily. |
| `ShowMa20` | `bool` | `true` | Whether the 20 candle moving average is drawn (two-way; the toolbar toggles it). |
| `ShowMa50` | `bool` | `true` | Whether the 50 candle moving average is drawn (two-way; the toolbar toggles it). |
| `IsLive` | `bool` | `true` | Whether simulated ticks stream (two-way; the Live button pauses and resumes them). |
| `TickInterval` | `TimeSpan` | `00:00:01.2000000` | Time between simulated ticks. |
| `SessionDate` | `DateTime?` | `null` | The trading day the simulation treats as today; null uses today's date. |
| `BuyingPower` | `double` | `0` | Cash available for buys (two-way). The ticket blocks a buy that costs more, and fills update it. |
| `OrderSide` | `MarketOrderSide` | `Buy` | The ticket's side (two-way). |
| `OrderType` | `MarketOrderType` | `Market` | The ticket's order type (two-way); a limit order shows the limit price field. |
| `OrderShares` | `int` | `10` | The ticket's share count (two-way). |
| `LimitPrice` | `double` | `0` | The ticket's limit price (two-way); 0 fills in the live price when the limit field opens. |
| `PlaceOrderAction` | `Func<MarketOrderRequest, CancellationToken, Task>?` | `null` | Places an order with a real service: awaited when the ticket is submitted, while the button shows a spinner. An exception leaves the order unplaced and writes its message under the button. Null places it locally at once. |
| `CancelOrderAction` | `Func<MarketOrder, CancellationToken, Task>?` | `null` | Cancels a working order with a real service; awaited before the order shows as canceled. Null cancels at once. |
| `Labels` | `MarketTerminalLabels` | – | The block's built-in text. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `TickerChanged` | `MarketTickerChangedEventArgs` | Raised when the charted symbol changes. |
| `OrderPlaced` | `MarketOrderEventArgs` | Raised when an order is placed (it may already be filled, or working). |
| `OrderFilled` | `MarketOrderEventArgs` | Raised when an order fills: a market order right away, a limit order when the price reaches it. |
| `OrderCanceled` | `MarketOrderEventArgs` | Raised when a working order is canceled from the list. |

Pseudo-classes: `:wide`, `:medium`, `:narrow`, `:compact`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

### MarketSymbol

A symbol of the `MarketTerminal` watchlist. Its candles are generated from these numbers, the same way every time for the same ticker and range, and then move with the simulated live price.

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### MarketHolding

Shares held of one ticker; the ticket blocks selling more than this.

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### MarketOrder

An order in the `MarketTerminal` order list.

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Changed` | `EventHandler?` | Raised on the order when its status or price changes (a working order filled, an order canceled). |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### MarketOrderRequest

What the ticket submits: passed to `PlaceOrderAction` and `OrderPlaced`.

### MarketRange

The time range of the `MarketTerminal` chart.

Derives from `Enum`: every member of `Enum` works as well.

### MarketOrderSide

Which side of the market an order takes.

Derives from `Enum`: every member of `Enum` works as well.

### MarketOrderType

How an order is priced.

Derives from `Enum`: every member of `Enum` works as well.

### MarketOrderStatus

Where an order stands.

Derives from `Enum`: every member of `Enum` works as well.

### MarketTerminalLabels

The built-in text of `MarketTerminal`. Replace the whole object to localize the block; parameterized entries are functions that receive already formatted values. Times and numbers use en-US formats.

## Keyboard

- **Tab** moves through the Live button, the range switch, the average toggles, the zoom buttons, the chart, the watchlist
  rows and the ticket.
- On the chart, **Left** and **Right** move the crosshair one candle (with **Shift**, ten), and the view scrolls when the
  crosshair passes an edge. **Home** and **End** go to the first and the latest candle. **+** and **-** zoom around the
  crosshair, **0** resets the view and **Escape** clears the crosshair.
- In the watchlist, **Up** and **Down** move between symbols and **Home** and **End** jump to the first and the last.
  **Enter** or **Space** charts the focused symbol.
- The range switch and the ticket's switches follow the segmented control: the arrows change the choice.

## Accessibility

- The chart is a focusable element named after the symbol, the range and the candle size ("ORBT price chart, six months of
  daily candles"), with its keys as help text. Moving the crosshair with the keyboard reads the candle's time, open, high,
  low, close, change and volume through a polite live region.
- Each watchlist row is a button whose name carries the ticker, the name, the price and the change ("up 0.85 percent
  today").
- Changes never rely on color alone: they carry a sign and an arrow, and order status is written as text.
- Problems with an order and failures are written in the line under the button, which is a polite live region; placing,
  filling and canceling an order are announced.
- Pointer focus draws no ring; keyboard focus shows Arc's focus ring around the chart, the rows, the toggles and the
  buttons.

## Motion

- **Zoom, pan and range changes**: the visible window and the price scale approach their targets exponentially, timed from
  the smooth spring, so nothing overshoots and a new gesture can reverse the motion mid-way. A drag flick keeps its speed
  and slows down like a thrown card.
- **Live ticks**: the last candle, its price tag, the price line and the averages glide to the new price; the header price
  rolls; each changed watchlist price flashes a green or red tint that fades out in 900 ms. The selected row's fill glides
  between rows.
- **Ticket**: the limit field opens with height and opacity together and closes faster; a new order grows into the top of
  the list.
- The Live dot pulses while prices stream; it is the block's only loop, because it reports a state.
- The chart draws frames only while something moves. Reduced motion places the view, the prices and the panels at once,
  drops the momentum and the pulse, and shows the flash as a short still tint. Off applies every change at once.

## Related

- `Budget variance`, the other Finance block.
- `SegmentedControl`, `NumberField`, `AnimatedCounter` and `Button`, the controls the block is made of.
- `Sparkline` and `LineChart` for charts without candles.

# Budget variance

> Budget against actual spend by department as bullet charts on one shared scale, with signed variances, a period switch that springs every bar, budget lines that open in place and a total row.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc.Blocks`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc.Blocks --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/blocks/budget-variance

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.BudgetVariancePreviewDemo">
    <!-- September, the third quarter and the year so far; Engineering opens with its lines. Data: BudgetVarianceDemoData. -->
    <arc:BudgetVariance x:Name="Budget" Margin="0,12" SelectedPeriod="month" ExpandedDepartment="engineering" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class BudgetVariancePreviewDemo : UserControl
{
    public BudgetVariancePreviewDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Budget.Periods.AddRange(BudgetVarianceDemoData.Periods());
        Budget.Departments.AddRange(BudgetVarianceDemoData.Departments());
    }
}
```

## When to use

`BudgetVariance` answers one question at a glance: which teams spent more than planned, which spent less, and by how much.
Every row is a bullet chart on the same scale, so the budget ticks line up down the table and the longest overrun stands
out without reading a number.

- **Month end and budget reviews.** Compare planned and actual operating spend by department or cost center, then open a
  department to see which lines moved it.
- **A controller's dashboard.** Switch between the month, the quarter and the year so far; every bar and figure moves to
  the new window together.
- **Any plan against actual with a tolerance.** Headcount cost, cloud spend by team or a project's phases, where a few
  percent either way is fine and more is worth a look.

## When not to use

- **Explaining how one total changed.** A waterfall that walks from the start value to the end value reads better.
- **Trends over many periods.** The block compares one window at a time; use `LineChart` or `BarChart` for a series.
- **Income.** Every figure is read as an expense, so spending under budget is favorable. Revenue against a target reads the
  other way round.
- **Dozens of cost centers.** When sorting and filtering matter more than the picture, use `Table`.

## Usage

The block derives from Avalonia's `TemplatedControl`. `Periods` are the windows of the switch; each `BudgetPeriod` has an
id, a short label, the line shown under the title and a phrase for screen reader sentences. `Departments` hold
`BudgetLine`s, and each line has one `BudgetAmount` (budget and actual) per period id. Department figures and the total are
summed from the lines, so they always reconcile.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:BudgetVariance SelectedPeriod="month" ExpandedDepartment="eng">
        <arc:BudgetVariance.Periods>
            <arc:BudgetPeriod Id="month" Label="Month" Description="March 2026" Phrase="in March" />
            <arc:BudgetPeriod Id="quarter" Label="Quarter" Description="January to March 2026" Phrase="in the first quarter" />
        </arc:BudgetVariance.Periods>
        <arc:BudgetDepartment Id="eng" Name="Engineering" Owner="Ravi Menon">
            <arc:BudgetLine Id="cloud" Name="Cloud hosting">
                <arc:BudgetAmount Period="month" Budget="176000" Actual="213700" />
                <arc:BudgetAmount Period="quarter" Budget="528000" Actual="613400" />
            </arc:BudgetLine>
        </arc:BudgetDepartment>
    </arc:BudgetVariance>
</UserControl>
```

In code, `new BudgetLine("cloud", "Cloud hosting").With("month", 176_000, 213_700)` adds the amounts of a window and
returns the line.

### Anatomy

- **Header**: `Title`, the period's description (or `Description`) and the period switch.
- **Column header**: Department, the scale over the charts (0%, 50% and 100% of budget), Actual, Budget and Variance.
- **Total row**: every department summed, with the department count under its name.
- **Department rows**: the owner's avatar (initials unless `OwnerAvatar` is set), the name and owner, the bullet chart, the
  figures and a chevron. The open department has a muted fill and its lines under it, indented past the avatar.
- **Legend**: what the bar, the tick, the red part and the band mean.

### Reading a bullet chart

- The **bands** behind each bar mark the tolerance: up to `RangeLow` of budget, from there to `RangeHigh`, and beyond.
  They use the text color at low opacity, so the block stays neutral in any accent.
- The **bar** is the actual spend. The part past the budget **tick** is drawn in the danger color.
- The **scale** is shared by every row and every window: at least 120% of budget, rounded up to a tenth so the largest
  figure of any period fits. The tick never moves when the window changes.
- The **variance** is a signed amount and a share ending in "over", "under" or "on plan". A variance smaller than
  `OnPlanThreshold` of budget (half a percent by default) is on plan and stays neutral; over is red, under is green.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.BudgetVarianceToleranceDemo">
    <!-- The quarter first, every department closed, a tighter 95 to 105% band and a wider on-plan threshold. -->
    <arc:BudgetVariance x:Name="Budget"
                        Margin="0,12"
                        Title="Operating budget"
                        SelectedPeriod="quarter"
                        RangeLow="0.95"
                        RangeHigh="1.05"
                        OnPlanThreshold="0.01" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class BudgetVarianceToleranceDemo : UserControl
{
    public BudgetVarianceToleranceDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Budget.Periods.AddRange(BudgetVarianceDemoData.Periods());
        Budget.Departments.AddRange(BudgetVarianceDemoData.Departments());
    }
}
```

### Periods and departments

`SelectedPeriod` (two-way) names the window shown; the switch changes it. `ExpandedDepartment` (two-way) names the open
department, or null; `ToggleDepartment(id)` opens one or closes it. Opening a department closes the one that was open.
`PeriodChanged` reports a window change and `DepartmentToggled` every open and close, the closing one first.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.BudgetVarianceEventsDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12" Margin="0,12">
        <arc:BudgetVariance x:Name="Budget" SelectedPeriod="ytd" Currency="€" />
        <TextBlock x:Name="Log"
                   HorizontalAlignment="Center"
                   TextAlignment="Center"
                   TextWrapping="Wrap"
                   MaxWidth="560"
                   Text="Switch the window or open a department: the events show up here." />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class BudgetVarianceEventsDemo : UserControl
{
    private readonly List<string> _lines = new();

    public BudgetVarianceEventsDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Budget.Periods.AddRange(BudgetVarianceDemoData.Periods());
        Budget.Departments.AddRange(BudgetVarianceDemoData.Departments());

        // Opening a department closes the open one, which is reported first.
        Budget.PeriodChanged += (_, e) => Write($"PeriodChanged: {e.OldPeriod} → {e.NewPeriod}");
        Budget.DepartmentToggled += (_, e) => Write($"DepartmentToggled: {e.Department.Name} {(e.IsExpanded ? "opened" : "closed")}");
    }

    private void Write(string line)
    {
        _lines.Add(line);
        if (_lines.Count > 3)
        {
            _lines.RemoveAt(0);
        }
        Log.Text = string.Join("\n", _lines);
    }
}
```

### Narrow containers

The block reads its own width. From 760 it is a table with aligned columns. Below that each row puts the name, the actual
of budget and the variance on top, and the bullet chart across the full width under them, so the chart is never squeezed.
Long names wrap instead of being cut.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"

             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.BudgetVarianceNarrowDemo">
    <!-- Below a 760 container each row puts its figures on top and the chart across the full width under them. -->
    <Border Width="520" Margin="0,12" HorizontalAlignment="Center">
        <arc:BudgetVariance x:Name="Budget" SelectedPeriod="month" ExpandedDepartment="sales" />
    </Border>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

public partial class BudgetVarianceNarrowDemo : UserControl
{
    public BudgetVarianceNarrowDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Budget.Periods.AddRange(BudgetVarianceDemoData.Periods());
        Budget.Departments.AddRange(BudgetVarianceDemoData.Departments());
```

### Text and currency

`Currency` is put before every amount ("$" by default); amounts shorten to k and M. Every other word comes from `Labels`,
a `BudgetVarianceLabels`: replace it to localize the block, including the sentences screen readers hear.

## API reference

### BudgetVariance

Budget against actual spend by department as bullet charts on one shared scale, so every budget tick lines up down the table. Each row shows three qualitative bands, the actual bar (the overspend past the tick in the danger color) and the variance as a signed amount and share, colored by whether it is favorable; every figure is an expense, so spending under budget is favorable. A period switch springs every bar and counts every number to the new window, a total row sums the table, and a department opens in place to show its budget lines. Department figures and the total are summed from the lines, so they always reconcile.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Title` | `string?` | `"Budget vs actual"` | The heading of the block. |
| `Description` | `string?` | `null` | The line under the heading; null shows the selected period's `Description`. |
| `SelectedPeriod` | `string?` | `null` | The `Id` of the window shown (two-way); null or unknown shows the first period. |
| `ExpandedDepartment` | `string?` | `null` | The `Id` of the department whose lines are open (two-way); null closes every department. |
| `RangeLow` | `double` | `0.9` | Lower edge of the tolerance band as a share of budget (0.9 = 90%). |
| `RangeHigh` | `double` | `1.1` | Upper edge of the tolerance band as a share of budget (1.1 = 110%); past it the band steps darker. |
| `OnPlanThreshold` | `double` | `0.005` | A variance smaller than this share of budget reads as on plan and stays neutral (0.005 = half a percent). |
| `Currency` | `string` | `"$"` | The symbol before every amount; amounts shorten to k and M. |
| `Labels` | `BudgetVarianceLabels` | – | The block's built-in text (headers, legend, the words after shares and the screen reader sentences). |
| `IsLegendVisible` | `bool` | `true` | Whether the legend under the table is shown. |
| `ScaleMaximum` | `double` | – | *Read-only.* The end of the shared scale as a share of budget: at least 1.2, rounded up to a tenth to fit the largest figure of any period. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `PeriodChanged` | `BudgetPeriodChangedEventArgs` | Raised when the reporting window changes. |
| `DepartmentToggled` | `BudgetDepartmentToggledEventArgs` | Raised when a department opens or closes; opening one closes the one that was open, which is reported first. |

Pseudo-classes: `:stacked`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

### BudgetPeriod

A reporting window of `BudgetVariance`: what the period switch offers ("Month", "Quarter", "Year to date").

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### BudgetDepartment

A department of `BudgetVariance`: a name, an owner and its budget lines, whose amounts it sums.

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### BudgetLine

A budget line of a `BudgetDepartment` ("Cloud hosting"), with one `BudgetAmount` per window.

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### BudgetAmount

One line's budget and actual spend in one reporting window; `Period` is the window's id.

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### BudgetVarianceKind

How a figure compares with its budget.

Derives from `Enum`: every member of `Enum` works as well.

### BudgetVarianceLabels

The built-in text of `BudgetVariance`. Replace the whole object to localize the block; parameterized entries are functions that receive already formatted amounts.

## Keyboard

- **Tab** moves to the period switch, then into the departments, then out of the block.
- On the period switch, **Left** and **Right** change the window.
- In the departments, **Up** and **Down** move to the previous or next one, and **Home** and **End** to the first or last.
- **Enter** or **Space** opens or closes the department in focus.

## Accessibility

- Each department row is a button that reports expanded or collapsed, and its name is a full sentence: what was spent of
  which budget, in which window, the variance and whether it is favorable. The total and each budget line carry the same
  sentence; the charts and the counting numbers themselves are not read, so nothing is heard twice or mid-count.
- Changing the window announces the window and the total through a polite live region.
- Variance never relies on color: amounts carry a sign and every share ends in over, under or on plan.
- Pointer focus draws no ring; keyboard focus fills the row and shows Arc's focus ring.

## Motion

- **Changing the window**: every bar springs to its new length on one critically damped spring (smooth, no overshoot), and
  every amount and share counts to its new value on the same spring. The red overspend is the same bar clipped to the
  space past the tick, so the color appears exactly as the bar crosses it.
- **Opening a department**: its lines grow in height and fade in together without overshoot; closing is faster. The
  chevron turns on Arc's spring curve and takes the accent while open.
- Every animation can be interrupted: a new window or toggle starts from where the bars and numbers are.
- Reduced motion jumps the bars and numbers to their values and opens the lines at full height. Off applies every change
  at once.

## Related

- `Market terminal`, the other Finance block.
- `SegmentedControl` and `Avatar`, the controls the block is made of.
- `Progress` for a single bar against a goal.
