# Small multiples

> A grid of small line charts, one per group, read as a single picture: one crosshair moves through every panel, the y axes switch between each group's own range and a common one, panels re-sort by value, growth or name, and flat groups can be faded.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc.Blocks`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc.Blocks --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/blocks/small-multiples

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.SmallMultiplesPreviewDemo">
    <!-- Eight markets over 24 months; hover a panel to move the crosshair in all of them. Data: SmallMultiplesDemoData. -->
    <arc:SmallMultiples x:Name="Chart"
                        Margin="0,12"
                        GrowthLag="12"
                        SeriesLegendText="Market"
                        GhostLegendText="All markets, scaled to fit" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class SmallMultiplesPreviewDemo : UserControl
{
    public SmallMultiplesPreviewDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Chart.Title = SmallMultiplesDemoData.Title;
        Chart.Description = SmallMultiplesDemoData.Description;
        Chart.Periods.AddRange(SmallMultiplesDemoData.Months());
        Chart.Series.AddRange(SmallMultiplesDemoData.Markets());
    }
}
```

## When to use

`SmallMultiples` answers "how do these segments compare over the same stretch of time?" Every series gets its own small
panel with the same x axis and the same encoding, so a reader takes in the whole grid at once and nobody has to follow
eight crossing lines on one plot.

- **One measure, many groups.** Revenue per market, signups per plan, tickets per support channel: the same figure kept
  for several groups over the same months or weeks.
- **Finding the movers.** Every panel states how far it moved since an earlier period, the grid can be ordered by that,
  and groups that barely moved can be faded into the background.
- **Reading one period everywhere.** Pointing at any panel moves a crosshair through all of them, and the readout above the
  grid shows that period and the total.

## When not to use

- **A few series on one plot.** When two or three lines are best compared directly, `LineChart` draws them together with
  one crosshair and legend toggles.
- **One metric to explore in depth.** Use a single chart with zoom or a drill-down; small multiples trade detail for
  overview.
- **A trend inside a table.** Put a `Sparkline` in the row instead.
- **Precise figures.** If readers need the numbers more than the shapes, a table serves them better.

## Usage

The block derives from Avalonia's `TemplatedControl`. Give it periods (oldest first) and one `SmallMultiplesSeries` per
panel with one value per period. Four to twelve panels work best: the grid has four columns from a 640px container and two
below.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:SmallMultiples Title="Revenue by market"
                        Description="Monthly net revenue"
                        SeriesLegendText="Market"
                        GhostLegendText="All markets, scaled to fit" />
</UserControl>
```

```csharp
chart.Periods.AddRange(months.Select(m => new SmallMultiplesPeriod(m.ToString("MMM yyyy"), m.ToString("MMMM yyyy"))));
chart.Series.Add(new SmallMultiplesSeries("us", "United States", usRevenue));
chart.Series.Add(new SmallMultiplesSeries("ca", "Canada", caRevenue));
```

`SeriesSource` and `PeriodsSource` take collections you own instead (an `ObservableCollection` is followed). A series' `Key`
keeps its panel, and its animation, when the list is rebuilt.

### Anatomy

- **Header**: `Title`, `Description` and three controls: the sort (Latest, Growth, Name), the scale (Independent, Shared)
  and the "Dim flat trends" switch. Below 640 they wrap under the heading.
- **Readout**: the period under the crosshair (or the latest), its position ("11 of 24") or "Latest", the total of every
  series, and the legend: the solid line is a series, the dashed one the total.
- **Panels**: the name, the value at the crosshair, the growth with an arrow and "vs" the comparison period, the y ticks in a
  right gutter, the dashed ghost of the total, the area, the line and its end dot.

### Growth and flat trends

Growth compares the latest value with the value `GrowthLag` periods earlier (12 by default, the same month a year before;
with fewer periods, the first one). A growth smaller than `FlatThreshold` either way (0.05 is 5%) counts as flat: the
panel says "Flat" with its percentage and, while `IsFlatDimmed` is on, its content fades to 38% while the grid lines stay.

### Scales

`Scale` chooses how panels compare. **Independent** fits each series to its own range, so the shapes are comparable;
**Shared** starts every panel at zero on the largest range, so the sizes are. Switching springs the axes and the lines
together. The ghost always uses its own range: it shows the overall shape, not a size to compare against.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.SmallMultiplesSharedScaleDemo">
    <!-- Opens on the shared scale, fastest growth first, with flat trends at full strength. -->
    <arc:SmallMultiples x:Name="Chart"
                        Margin="0,12"
                        Scale="Shared"
                        Sort="Growth"
                        IsFlatDimmed="False"
                        SeriesLegendText="Market"
                        GhostLegendText="All markets, scaled to fit" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class SmallMultiplesSharedScaleDemo : UserControl
{
    public SmallMultiplesSharedScaleDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Chart.Title = SmallMultiplesDemoData.Title;
        Chart.Description = SmallMultiplesDemoData.Description;
        Chart.Periods.AddRange(SmallMultiplesDemoData.Months());
        Chart.Series.AddRange(SmallMultiplesDemoData.Markets());
    }
}
```

### Your own units

Values are read as thousands of US dollars by default ($412k, $1.71M). Pass `ValueFormatter` for the headings, the total
and screen readers, and `TickFormatter` for the compact axis ticks. This demo shows weekly counts with growth against four
weeks earlier, at 560 wide.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.SmallMultiplesSignupsDemo">
    <!--
        Weekly signups of four plans over 26 weeks: growth compares with four weeks earlier, values are plain counts, and
        the block is 560 wide, so it shows two columns.
    -->
    <arc:SmallMultiples x:Name="Chart"
                        Width="560"
                        Margin="0,12"
                        HorizontalAlignment="Center"
                        Title="Signups by plan"
                        Description="Weekly signups, last 26 weeks"
                        GrowthLag="4"
                        SeriesLegendText="Plan"
                        GhostLegendText="All plans, scaled to fit" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class SmallMultiplesSignupsDemo : UserControl
{
    public SmallMultiplesSignupsDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        // Counts, not dollars: the readout and headings use whole numbers, the axis a compact form.
        Chart.ValueFormatter = SmallMultiplesDemoData.Signups;
        Chart.TickFormatter = SmallMultiplesDemoData.SignupTicks;
        Chart.Periods.AddRange(SmallMultiplesDemoData.Weeks());
        Chart.Series.AddRange(SmallMultiplesDemoData.Plans());
    }
}
```

### Following the crosshair

`CrosshairIndex` is the period under the crosshair, or null when it is hidden; `CrosshairIndexChanged` reports each move.
`SetCrosshairIndex` moves it from code. `SortChanged` and `ScaleChanged` report the controls; `Sort`, `Scale` and
`IsFlatDimmed` are two-way.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.SmallMultiplesCrosshairDemo">
    <!-- CrosshairIndexChanged follows the synced crosshair; the buttons move it from code. -->
    <StackPanel Margin="0,12" Spacing="12">
        <StackPanel Orientation="Horizontal" Spacing="8" HorizontalAlignment="Center">
            <arc:Button x:Name="First" Content="First month" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" />
            <arc:Button x:Name="YearAgo" Content="A year ago" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" />
            <arc:Button x:Name="Clear" Content="Clear" Variant="Ghost" Size="Small" />
        </StackPanel>
        <TextBlock x:Name="Status" HorizontalAlignment="Center" Text="Crosshair hidden" />
        <arc:SmallMultiples x:Name="Chart"
                            SeriesLegendText="Market"
                            GhostLegendText="All markets, scaled to fit" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class SmallMultiplesCrosshairDemo : UserControl
{
    public SmallMultiplesCrosshairDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        var months = SmallMultiplesDemoData.Months();
        Chart.Title = SmallMultiplesDemoData.Title;
        Chart.Description = SmallMultiplesDemoData.Description;
        Chart.Periods.AddRange(months);
        Chart.Series.AddRange(SmallMultiplesDemoData.Markets());

        Chart.CrosshairIndexChanged += (_, e) =>
            Status.Text = e.Index is { } i ? $"Crosshair on {months[i].Long}" : "Crosshair hidden";
        First.Click += (_, _) => Chart.SetCrosshairIndex(0);
        YearAgo.Click += (_, _) => Chart.SetCrosshairIndex(months.Length - 13);
        Clear.Click += (_, _) => Chart.SetCrosshairIndex(null);
    }
}
```

### Other words

Every text is a property with an English default: the options (`LatestSortText`, `GrowthSortText`, `NameSortText`,
`IndependentScaleText`, `SharedScaleText`, `DimFlatText`), the readout (`LatestText`, `PositionFormat`, `TotalText`), the
legend (`SeriesLegendText`, `GhostLegendText`), the trend (`FlatText`, `CompareFormat`, `UpFormat`, `DownFormat`), the
screen reader names (`SortLabel`, `ScaleLabel`, `PanelsLabel`, `KeyboardHint`) and the announcements.

## API reference

### SmallMultiples

Many small line charts on one grid, one per group (a market, a plan, a product), all over the same periods, so the grid is read like a single chart. Pointing at one panel moves a crosshair through all of them and the readout shows that period's total; a toggle puts every panel on its own range (compare shapes) or on one range from zero (compare sizes), with the axes springing between them; the order follows the latest value, the growth or the name, and panels fly to their new places; each panel carries a faint dashed outline of the grand total; flat groups can be faded.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SeriesSource` | `IEnumerable?` | `null` | The series as a list to follow (observed when it raises collection changes); it wins over `Series`. |
| `PeriodsSource` | `IEnumerable?` | `null` | The periods as a list to follow; it wins over `Periods`. |
| `Title` | `string?` | `null` | The heading of the block; null hides it. |
| `Description` | `string?` | `null` | The line under the heading (what is measured, over which periods); null hides it. |
| `Sort` | `SmallMultiplesSort` | `Latest` | The panel order (two-way). Default `Latest`. |
| `Scale` | `SmallMultiplesScale` | `Independent` | How the panels' y axes are set (two-way): `Independent` (the default) gives each panel its own range, which makes shapes comparable; `Shared` gives them all one range starting at zero, which makes sizes comparable. |
| `IsFlatDimmed` | `bool` | `true` | Fades the panels whose growth counts as flat (two-way); on by default. |
| `FlatThreshold` | `double` | `0.05` | The flat band: a growth whose size (up or down) is under this fraction is flat. 0.05 means ±5%. |
| `GrowthLag` | `int` | `12` | How many periods back the growth looks: the latest value is compared with the one this many periods before it (12 by default, a year for monthly data). When the data is shorter, the first period is used. |
| `ValueFormatter` | `Func<double, string>?` | `null` | Turns a value into text for the panel headings, the total and what screen readers hear. Without one, values are taken to be thousands of US dollars and written "$412k" or "$1.71M". |
| `TickFormatter` | `Func<double, string>?` | `null` | Turns a tick value into the short label at the right of each plot; without one, `ValueFormatter` is used. |
| `LatestSortText` | `string` | `"Latest"` | The sort option for `Latest`. |
| `GrowthSortText` | `string` | `"Growth"` | The sort option for `Growth`. |
| `NameSortText` | `string` | `"Name"` | The sort option for `Name`. |
| `IndependentScaleText` | `string` | `"Independent"` | The scale option for `Independent`. |
| `SharedScaleText` | `string` | `"Shared"` | The scale option for `Shared`. |
| `SortLabel` | `string` | `"Sort panels"` | The screen reader name of the sort control. |
| `ScaleLabel` | `string` | `"Y scale"` | The screen reader name of the scale control. |
| `DimFlatText` | `string` | `"Dim flat trends"` | The dimming switch's text. |
| `LatestText` | `string` | `"Latest"` | Beside the period in the readout while no crosshair is shown. |
| `PositionFormat` | `string` | `"{0} of {1}"` | Beside the period in the readout while the crosshair is shown; {0} is its position, {1} the number of periods. |
| `TotalText` | `string` | `"Total"` | The label of the total in the readout. |
| `SeriesLegendText` | `string` | `"Series"` | The legend's name for the solid line ("Market"). |
| `GhostLegendText` | `string` | `"All series, scaled to fit"` | The legend's name for the dashed ghost of the total. |
| `FlatText` | `string` | `"Flat"` | The trend text of a flat series, before its growth ("Flat +0.6%"). |
| `CompareFormat` | `string` | `"vs {0}"` | After the growth in each panel; {0} is the comparison period's short label ("vs Sep 2025"). |
| `UpFormat` | `string` | `"Up {0} {1}"` | Screen reader trend words; {0} is the unsigned percentage and {1} the comparison text ("Up 19.9% vs Sep 2025"). |
| `DownFormat` | `string` | `"Down {0} {1}"` | Screen reader trend words for a fall; same placeholders as `UpFormat`. |
| `PanelsLabel` | `string` | `"Panels"` | The screen reader name of the panels. |
| `KeyboardHint` | `string` | `"Use the left and right arrow keys to move through the periods, Home and End to jump, and Escape to clear."` | The keyboard hint read when the panels get focus. |
| `CrosshairAnnouncementFormat` | `string` | `"{0}. Total {1}. Highest {2}, {3}."` | Announced when the crosshair moves by keyboard; {0} period, {1} total, {2} the highest series, {3} its value. |
| `SortAnnouncementFormat` | `string` | `"Sorted by {0}."` | Announced after sorting; {0} is the sort option's text. |
| `SharedAnnouncement` | `string` | `"Shared scale. Panels compare size."` | Announced after switching to the shared scale. |
| `IndependentAnnouncement` | `string` | `"Independent scale. Panels compare shape."` | Announced after switching to the independent scale. |
| `DimOnAnnouncement` | `string` | `"Flat trends dimmed."` | Announced when flat trends are dimmed. |
| `DimOffAnnouncement` | `string` | `"Flat trends shown at full strength."` | Announced when flat trends are shown at full strength again. |
| `CrosshairIndex` | `int?` | – | *Read-only.* The period under the synced crosshair; null while it is hidden. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `SortChanged` | `SmallMultiplesSortChangedEventArgs` | Occurs once the panels have been put in a new order. |
| `ScaleChanged` | `SmallMultiplesScaleChangedEventArgs` | Occurs once the y axes have switched to the other scale. |
| `CrosshairIndexChanged` | `SmallMultiplesIndexChangedEventArgs` | Occurs each time the crosshair lands on another period; the index is null when the crosshair goes away. |

Pseudo-classes: `:compact`, `:phone`, `:empty`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

### SmallMultiplesSeries

A group shown in a `SmallMultiples`, which gets a panel of its own. Give it a key, a name and its values, one for each of the block's periods in the same order.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Key` | `string?` | `null` | A stable id that keeps the panel (and its animation) when the list is rebuilt; null uses `Name`. |
| `Name` | `string?` | `null` | The panel's heading ("United States"). |
| `Values` | `IReadOnlyList<double>?` | `null` | One value per period, oldest first; a missing or non-finite value leaves a gap in the line. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### SmallMultiplesPeriod

A step of the x axis that every panel of a `SmallMultiples` shares, named twice: briefly ("Oct 2026"), where a panel says what its growth is measured against, and in full ("October 2026"), in the readout and for screen readers.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Short` | `string?` | `null` | The brief name, as in "vs Oct 2025" under a panel's value. |
| `Long` | `string?` | `null` | The full name for the readout and screen readers ("October 2026"); without it, `Short` is used. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### SmallMultiplesSort

The order of the panels of a `SmallMultiples`.

Derives from `Enum`: every member of `Enum` works as well.

### SmallMultiplesScale

How the panels of a `SmallMultiples` scale their y axis.

Derives from `Enum`: every member of `Enum` works as well.

## Accessibility

- **Tab** moves through the sort control, the scale control, the dim switch and then the panels, which are one tab stop.
- On the panels, **Left** and **Right** move the crosshair one period in every panel; **Page up** and **Page down** move it
  twelve; **Home** and **End** jump to the first or latest period; **Escape** clears it. Focusing the panels with the keyboard
  places it on the latest period.
- In the sort and scale controls the arrow keys choose the previous or next option.
- Keyboard moves are read out politely: the period, the total and the group in the lead. Changing the order, the scale or
  the fading is read out too.
- Each panel is named by its series, its value at the crosshair and its trend in words ("Up 15.3% vs Oct 2025", "Flat").
- Fading is never the only signal: every panel also shows an arrow and a signed percentage (with a real minus sign), or the
  word "Flat". Keyboard focus draws the shared focus ring around the panels.

## Motion

- **Switching the scale**: both ends of each panel's y range ride the smooth spring (about 400 ms, no overshoot). Everything
  in the plot is drawn from that range on every frame, so tick labels travel with their values while the line stretches or
  flattens; the new scale's ticks fade in over 240 ms as the old ones fade out.
- **Sorting**: each panel starts from where it was and springs into its new slot, carrying its own divider lines with it.
- **Crosshair**: its first position is shown at once; later moves glide on a short spring, and each panel's dot follows its
  line between points.
- **Fading**: a flat panel's content fades over 240 ms and the grid lines are left alone.
- With reduced motion, rescaling, reordering and crosshair moves happen at once. Off applies every change at once.

## Related

- `LineChart` for a few series on one plot with a gliding crosshair.
- `Sparkline` for a compact trend beside a value.
- `Line replay`, the other Line charts block, for playing one series back in time.

# Line replay

> Watch a day of data unfold: the line draws itself as a clock runs, events you mark pop up on the chart when it reaches them, and you can pause, drag to any moment or change the speed.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc.Blocks`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc.Blocks --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/blocks/line-replay

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.LineReplayPreviewDemo">
    <!-- A release day against a typical Wednesday; press Replay. Data: LineReplayDemoData. -->
    <arc:LineReplay x:Name="Replay"
                    Margin="0,12"
                    SeriesLabel="Release day"
                    BaselineLabel="Typical Wednesday"
                    ValueLabel="Active" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class LineReplayPreviewDemo : UserControl
{
    public LineReplayPreviewDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Replay.Title = LineReplayDemoData.Title;
        Replay.Description = LineReplayDemoData.Description;
        Replay.Points = LineReplayDemoData.ReleaseDay();
        Replay.Moments.AddRange(LineReplayDemoData.ReleaseMoments());
    }
}
```

## When to use

`LineReplay` is for data whose order is the story. Play it and one series is drawn across its day; each event you marked
appears on the line when the drawing gets there, so readers see the trigger and the reaction one after the other: the
announcement, then the climb; the outage, then the dip.

- **Looking back at a launch or a campaign.** See which announcement, email or mention moved the numbers.
- **After an incident.** Walk the team through what the metric did between the alert, the fix and the all-clear.
- **Data stories.** A day, a session or a match where the order of events is the point.

## When not to use

- **Comparisons.** When several series or periods should be read side by side, `LineChart` (or `Small multiples`) shows them
  without waiting for a replay.
- **Editable annotations.** Moments come from your data; readers cannot add their own.
- **Two related measures.** Plot one against the other instead of replaying a single line.

## Usage

The block derives from Avalonia's `TemplatedControl`. `Points` are `LineReplayPoint`s on one clock in minutes from the
start (midnight in the demos), each with a value and optionally a `Baseline`; they do not need to be evenly spaced.
`Moments` are `LineReplayMoment`s on the same clock with a title, an optional detail and a `Kind` that picks the icon.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:LineReplay Title="Release day"
                    SeriesLabel="Release day"
                    BaselineLabel="Typical Wednesday"
                    ValueLabel="Active">
        <arc:LineReplayMoment Id="notes" Time="390" Title="Release notes published" Kind="Launch" />
        <arc:LineReplayMoment Id="queue" Time="705" Title="Sign-up queue backed up" Kind="Incident" />
    </arc:LineReplay>
</UserControl>
```

```csharp
replay.Points = samples.Select(s => new LineReplayPoint(s.Minute, s.Active, s.TypicalActive)).ToArray();
```

### Anatomy

- **Header**: `Title`, `Description`, and a legend for the line (`SeriesLabel`) and the dashed comparison (`BaselineLabel`).
- **Readout**: the time, the value (`ValueLabel`), the ratio to the comparison ("Versus typical Wednesday 2.6×") and the peak
  so far with its time. Each value keeps its width while it plays, so the columns never shift.
- **Chart**: a lane for the callout above the plot, the value grid, the comparison drawn in full, the area and the line up
  to the playhead, a marker and a stem for each moment passed, the value on the tip and a clock on the time axis.
- **Transport**: the play button (Play, Pause, or Replay at the end), the scrubber with a tick per moment, and the speed
  (0.5×, 1×, 2×, 4×).
- **Key moments**: one row per moment with its time and detail; once its window has played it also shows its effect, the
  rise over the next hour or, for an incident, the dip over 20 minutes. From 1000 wide the rows sit in a column beside the
  chart; below, under it in two columns, and in one column below 560.

### Playing

`Duration` is how long a full replay takes at 1× (16 seconds by default) and `Speed` sets the pace. `DefaultPosition`
chooses where the playhead rests before the first play: `End` (the default) shows the whole line with every moment, and
Replay rewinds and plays; `Start` shows an empty chart that the first play draws. Leave `Baseline` out of every point and
the comparison, its legend entry and the ratio disappear.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.LineReplayFromStartDemo">
    <!--
        A sale morning without a comparison line: the legend entry and the ratio are gone. The playhead rests at the start,
        a full replay takes 12 seconds at 1×, and it opens at 2×.
    -->
    <arc:LineReplay x:Name="Replay"
                    Margin="0,12"
                    Title="Sale morning"
                    Description="Shoppers on site every two minutes, 5 am to noon."
                    SeriesLabel="Sale day"
                    ValueLabel="Shoppers"
                    DefaultPosition="Start"
                    Duration="0:0:12"
                    Speed="2" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class LineReplayFromStartDemo : UserControl
{
    public LineReplayFromStartDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Replay.Points = LineReplayDemoData.SaleMorning();
        Replay.Moments.AddRange(LineReplayDemoData.SaleMoments());
    }
}
```

### From code

`Play()`, `Pause()`, `Replay()` and `TogglePlay()` do what the button does. `Seek(minutes)` glides the playhead to a time,
and `SeekToMoment(moment)` to a moment; if it was playing it continues from there. `Position` and `IsPlaying` report the
state. `MomentReached` fires when playback passes a moment, not when someone scrubs or jumps, so it is safe for analytics.
`AutoPlay` plays from the start the first time the block is 40% in view (not with reduced motion).

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.LineReplayEventsDemo">
    <!-- MomentReached fires as playback passes each moment (not when scrubbing); the buttons drive the replay from code. -->
    <StackPanel Margin="0,12" Spacing="12">
        <StackPanel Orientation="Horizontal" Spacing="8" HorizontalAlignment="Center">
            <arc:Button x:Name="PlayButton" Content="Replay" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" />
            <arc:Button x:Name="NoonButton" Content="Jump to noon" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" />
        </StackPanel>
        <TextBlock x:Name="Log" HorizontalAlignment="Center" Text="No moment reached yet" />
        <arc:LineReplay x:Name="Replay"
                        SeriesLabel="Release day"
                        BaselineLabel="Typical Wednesday"
                        ValueLabel="Active" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class LineReplayEventsDemo : UserControl
{
    public LineReplayEventsDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Replay.Title = LineReplayDemoData.Title;
        Replay.Description = LineReplayDemoData.Description;
        Replay.Points = LineReplayDemoData.ReleaseDay();
        Replay.Moments.AddRange(LineReplayDemoData.ReleaseMoments());

        Replay.MomentReached += (_, e) => Log.Text = $"Reached: {e.Moment.Title}";
        PlayButton.Click += (_, _) => Replay.Replay();
        NoonButton.Click += (_, _) => Replay.Seek(12 * 60);
    }
}
```

### Formats and words

`TimeFormatter` prints times ("9:40 am" by default), `TickFormatter` the axis labels ("6 am") and `ValueFormatter` the
values ("2,316"). The button texts and names (`PlayText`, `PauseText`, `ReplayText`, `PlayLabel`, `PauseLabel`,
`ReplayLabel`), the readout labels (`TimeText`, `VersusFormat`, `PeakText`, `PeakFormat`), the effects (`RiseFormat`,
`DipFormat`), `MomentsTitle`, the screen reader names and the announcements are properties with English defaults.

## API reference

### LineReplay

A line chart you play like a recording. The line is drawn from left to right as the clock runs, with the current value next to its leading end and the time on the axis below. Events you mark on the clock show up as the line reaches them: a dot lands on the line, a small card names the event above the chart, and its row in the list beside the chart is highlighted, later adding what happened next. Around the chart sit a play button, a position slider, a speed switch, and figures for the current time, value, comparison and best value so far.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Points` | `IReadOnlyList<LineReplayPoint>?` | `null` | The data to play: one entry per sample with its clock time in minutes, its value and, if you have one, a typical value to compare with. |
| `MomentsSource` | `IEnumerable?` | `null` | The key moments as a list to follow (observed when it raises collection changes); it wins over `Moments`. |
| `Title` | `string?` | `null` | The heading of the block; null hides it. |
| `Description` | `string?` | `null` | A sentence under the heading saying what the line measures and over which day; null leaves it out. |
| `SeriesLabel` | `string` | `"Today"` | What the legend calls the line being played. |
| `BaselineLabel` | `string` | `"Typical day"` | What the legend calls the dashed comparison; the ratio's label reuses it ("Versus typical day"). |
| `ValueLabel` | `string` | `"Value"` | The name of the measured quantity ("Active"), above the current value and in the slider's spoken value. |
| `TimeFormatter` | `Func<double, string>?` | `null` | Writes a clock time (minutes) wherever one is shown or spoken; without one, times read like "9:40 am". |
| `TickFormatter` | `Func<double, string>?` | `null` | Writes the hour labels under the chart; without one, they read like "6 am". |
| `ValueFormatter` | `Func<double, string>?` | `null` | Writes a value wherever one is shown or spoken; without one, values are whole numbers like "2,316". |
| `Duration` | `TimeSpan` | `00:00:16` | The time from the first point to the last at normal speed (16 seconds by default). |
| `Speed` | `double` | `1` | The playback speed (two-way): 0.5, 1, 2 or 4. |
| `DefaultPosition` | `LineReplayPosition` | `End` | Whether the chart first appears fully drawn (`End`, the default) or empty (`Start`). |
| `AutoPlay` | `bool` | `false` | Starts a replay from the beginning once, as soon as 40% of the block has scrolled into view; nothing happens when motion is reduced. |
| `PlayText` | `string` | `"Play"` | The play button's text while paused partway. |
| `PauseText` | `string` | `"Pause"` | The play button's text while playing. |
| `ReplayText` | `string` | `"Replay"` | The play button's text at the end. |
| `PlayLabel` | `string` | `"Play replay"` | The play button's screen reader name while paused partway. |
| `PauseLabel` | `string` | `"Pause replay"` | The play button's screen reader name while playing. |
| `ReplayLabel` | `string` | `"Replay from the start"` | The play button's screen reader name at the end. |
| `TimeText` | `string` | `"Time"` | The readout's time label. |
| `VersusFormat` | `string` | `"Versus {0}"` | The readout's ratio label; {0} is `BaselineLabel` with a lower-case first letter. |
| `PeakText` | `string` | `"Peak so far"` | The readout's peak label. |
| `PeakFormat` | `string` | `"{0} at {1}"` | The peak value and when; {0} value, {1} time. |
| `MomentsTitle` | `string` | `"Key moments"` | The heading of the moments column. |
| `RiseFormat` | `string` | `"+{0} in the next hour"` | A moment's effect, the rise over the next hour; {0} is the formatted rise. |
| `DipFormat` | `string` | `"{0} in 20 minutes"` | An incident's effect, the dip over 20 minutes; {0} is the signed percentage. |
| `ScrubberLabel` | `string` | `"Replay position"` | The scrubber's screen reader name. |
| `SpeedLabel` | `string` | `"Playback speed"` | The speed control's screen reader name. |
| `MomentAnnouncementFormat` | `string` | `"{0}. {1}."` | Announced when playback passes a moment; {0} time, {1} title. |
| `PausedAnnouncementFormat` | `string` | `"Paused at {0}."` | Announced when playback is paused; {0} is the time. |
| `FinishedAnnouncementFormat` | `string` | `"Replay finished. Peak {0} at {1}."` | Announced when the replay reaches the end; {0} peak value, {1} its time. |
| `Position` | `double` | – | *Read-only.* Where the playhead is, in minutes on the replay clock. |
| `IsPlaying` | `bool` | – | *Read-only.* Whether the replay is playing. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `MomentReached` | `LineReplayMomentEventArgs` | Occurs as a playing replay crosses one of the moments; dragging the slider or jumping does not raise it. |

Pseudo-classes: `:stacked`, `:narrow`, `:playing`, `:no-baseline`, `:no-moments`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

### LineReplayMoment

An event to point out in a `LineReplay`, timed on the same clock as the data. It gets a row in the list of moments, a tick on the slider, and a dot and a card on the chart once the replay gets there.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Id` | `string?` | `null` | A stable id, reported back by `MomentReached`. |
| `Time` | `double` | `0` | The clock time of the event in minutes; it may fall between two samples. |
| `Title` | `string?` | `null` | A short name for the event ("Release notes published"). |
| `Detail` | `string?` | `null` | One optional line of detail under the title. |
| `Kind` | `LineReplayMomentKind` | `Launch` | The sort of event, which decides the icon (problems also use the warning color). |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### LineReplayPoint

A sample for a `LineReplay`: when it was taken (`Time`, minutes on the block's clock), what it measured (`Value`), and optionally what a normal day measured then (`Baseline`), which the chart shows as a dashed line.

Derives from `ValueType`: every member of `ValueType` works as well.

### LineReplayMomentKind

The sort of event a `LineReplayMoment` marks, which decides its icon.

Derives from `Enum`: every member of `Enum` works as well.

### LineReplayPosition

How a `LineReplay` looks before anyone has played it.

Derives from `Enum`: every member of `Enum` works as well.

## Accessibility

- **Tab** moves through the play button, the scrubber, the speed control and each key moment.
- On the scrubber, **Space**, **Enter** or **K** plays or pauses (at the end, replays from the start); **Left** and **Right**
  step one point, or an hour with **Shift**; **Page up** and **Page down** step an hour; **Home** and **End** jump to the
  start or the end. In the speed control the arrow keys choose the speed.
- **Enter** or **Space** on a key moment moves the playhead to it.
- The scrubber reports itself as a slider in minutes. Its spoken value ("9:40 am, 2,316 active") changes only while
  playback is stopped, to keep screen readers quiet during a replay.
- Everything the line shows is also in the readout as text, so the drawing is left out of the accessibility tree.
- A polite announcement follows each moment passed, each pause or jump, and the end of the replay ("Replay finished. Peak
  4,894 at 10:40 am.").
- The play button's name says what pressing it will do: Play replay, Pause replay, Replay from the start. The most recent
  moment passed is flagged as the current one; its effect stays silent until that stretch has been played.
- An incident is told apart by its warning icon and its own title as well as by its color.

## Motion

- **Playback** runs at every motion level: the viewer asked for it and can stop it. One position moves forward each frame,
  and the line, the playhead, the labels, the scrubber and the readout are all drawn from it.
- **Rewinding and jumping** move the playhead on the smooth spring (no overshoot); the drawn line shrinks or grows with it,
  and a second jump during the first continues from the current spot.
- **Reaching a moment**: its marker grows from 40% to full size as it fades in, a dotted stem appears under it, and its card
  lifts 8px into place above the plot; the card it replaces fades out in 120 ms.
- **Hour labels** near the moving clock fade (160 ms) rather than sit under it. The moment rows change color in 160 ms and
  show their effect in 240 ms.
- With reduced motion the replay still plays, but rewinds, jumps, markers and cards simply land, and `AutoPlay` does
  nothing.

## Related

- `LineChart` for several series on one plot.
- `Small multiples`, the other Line charts block, for many series side by side.
- `SegmentedControl` and `Button`, which the transport is made of.

# Model picker

> Choose a model and its reasoning effort from one compact pill: featured models with a note each, an effort setting, every other model by provider, and a summary of what the choice costs.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc.Blocks`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc.Blocks --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/blocks/model-picker

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ModelPickerPreviewDemo">
    <!-- The picker is at most 440 wide and centers itself; the menu opens below the pill. -->
    <arc:ModelPicker x:Name="Picker" Margin="0,12,0,160" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class ModelPickerPreviewDemo : UserControl
{
    public ModelPickerPreviewDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Picker.Providers.AddRange(ModelPickerDemoData.Providers());
        Picker.Models.AddRange(ModelPickerDemoData.Models());
        Picker.SummaryNote = ModelPickerDemoData.PriceNote;
    }
}
```

## When to use

The model picker lets people decide which model answers and how hard it thinks. It is one pill that shows the current
choice, a menu behind it, and an optional summary of what the model can hold and costs. It belongs wherever the choice
matters but should not take space until someone looks for it.

- **A settings page for an AI feature**: the default model for a support assistant or a drafting tool. The summary
  under the pill shows the context size and the price per million tokens, so the choice is informed.
- **A model catalog with a few favorites**: three or four featured models with a note each ("Quick and capable for daily
  chats"), and the long tail grouped by provider under "More models".
- **An effort control tied to the model**: some models reason longer when asked. The Effort row appears only for models
  that offer levels, and a level the next model lacks moves to the nearest one.
- **A header or toolbar chip**: set `IsSummaryVisible` to false and the picker is only the pill, for the top of a chat
  or beside a prompt field.
- **A product that bills by usage**: the summary prints input and output prices, and a small note under it says which
  currency and unit they are in.

## When not to use

- **A short fixed choice with no explanation**, such as Small, Medium and Large: use `SegmentedControl` or `Select`.
- **A comparison of several models side by side**: the picker shows one model at a time. Build a table with
  `Table` when people need to compare prices and limits.
- **A choice among hundreds of models that people search by name**: the menu has no search field. Use `Combobox` and
  filter your own list.
- **A model setting that is not about the model**, such as temperature or stop words: put those in a form with
  `NumberField` and `Switch`. The picker chooses the model and its effort only.
- **Running the model**: the picker does not call anything. It reports the choice; your code decides what to do with it.

## Usage

`ModelPicker` derives from Avalonia's `TemplatedControl`. Its template holds a `ModelPill`, a `ModelSummary` and a
hidden `ModelMenu`. The picker owns the state: you give it models and read the choice back. A model is an `AiModel`, an
`AvaloniaObject` with the name, a one-line `Blurb` for the featured list, a `Description` for the summary, the context
size and prices, and the effort levels it offers. Providers group the "More models" list and supply the mark of any
model that has none.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:ModelPicker SelectedModelId="aurora-prime-3" SummaryNote="Prices in USD per 1M tokens">
        <arc:ModelPicker.Providers>
            <arc:AiModelProvider Id="aurora" Name="Aurora Labs">
                <arc:AiModelProvider.Mark>
                    <StreamGeometry>M2 19a10 10 0 0 1 20 0h-3.2a6.8 6.8 0 0 0-13.6 0Z</StreamGeometry>
                </arc:AiModelProvider.Mark>
            </arc:AiModelProvider>
        </arc:ModelPicker.Providers>
        <arc:AiModel Id="aurora-prime-3" Name="Aurora Prime 3" ProviderId="aurora"
                     Blurb="Deep work: refactors, research, long tasks"
                     Description="A careful planner for multi-step coding and research."
                     ContextTokens="800000" InputPrice="6" OutputPrice="24" />
        <arc:AiModel Id="aurora-pocket-24" Name="Aurora Pocket 2.4" ProviderId="aurora" Tag="Fast"
                     ContextTokens="400000" InputPrice="0.4" OutputPrice="1.6" />
    </arc:ModelPicker>
</UserControl>
```

Effort levels are a list, so set them in code (XAML has no array literal):

```csharp
prime.EffortLevels = [ModelEffort.Low, ModelEffort.Medium, ModelEffort.High, ModelEffort.ExtraHigh, ModelEffort.Max];
prime.DefaultEffort = ModelEffort.Medium;
```

The first four models are featured. `FeaturedIds` picks others, in the order you give. The rest appear under "More models",
grouped in the order of `Providers`. With no selection the picker selects the first featured model once and writes it
back to `SelectedModel`.

### Anatomy

1. **Pill**: 40 px high with a full radius and a 1 px border. It shows the model's mark (16 px, no tile), the name in
   medium weight, the effort in the muted text color when the model has one, and a chevron that turns while the menu is
   open. Hover and open use the muted surface and the strong border. A keyboard focus ring appears only for keyboard use.
2. **Menu**: 304 px wide (the window width less 24 px when narrower), on the raised surface with the panel radius and the
   floating shadow. It opens 8 px below the pill.
3. **Featured rows**: 54 px high. Each has the mark (18 px), the name, the blurb in the secondary color, and a check on
   the selected model.
4. **Effort row**: 40 px high, with the current level on the right. It is hidden when the selected model offers no levels.
5. **More models row**: shows the name of the selected model on the right when that model is not featured. It is hidden
   when every model is featured.
6. **Submenus**: the effort list is 264 px wide with a name, a description and a check on each level, and "Default"
   after the model's default. The other models list is 272 px wide, at most 420 px high, scrolls, and groups its compact
   rows (38 px) under the provider names, with the model's `Tag` at the end of the row.
7. **Summary**: a description of the model, a table of Context, Input, Output and Effort, an optional note, and a
   confirmation line.

### Choosing a model, effort and more

Press the pill, or press `Enter`, `Space` or `ArrowDown` while it has focus, to open the menu. One highlight follows the
pointer and jumps with the arrow keys. Choose a model to select it, close the menu and return focus to the pill. Choose
Effort or More models to open a submenu to the right; when there is no room on the right it opens on the left, and when
there is room on neither side it opens as a page. Choosing the model that is already selected closes the menu and
changes nothing.

A model that does not offer the current effort moves it to the nearest level it does offer, and to the lower of two
equal choices. The picker says so in the confirmation: "Aurora Prime 3 → Cobalt Atlas 2 · Effort adjusted to High". A
model with no levels has no effort (`Effort` is null) and the Effort row disappears.

### Pages in a narrow window

When the window is at most `PagedMenuWidth` wide (640 by default) the Effort and More models rows open pages inside
the menu instead of flyouts. A back row heads each page, the content slides in from the side of travel, and the menu's
height follows the page. The demo sets a very wide `PagedMenuWidth`, so you can see the pages in a wide window.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ModelPickerPagesDemo">
    <!-- A window at most this wide shows the effort levels and the other models as pages inside the menu. -->
    <arc:ModelPicker x:Name="Picker" PagedMenuWidth="4000" Margin="0,12,0,160" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class ModelPickerPagesDemo : UserControl
{
    public ModelPickerPagesDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Picker.Providers.AddRange(ModelPickerDemoData.Providers());
        Picker.Models.AddRange(ModelPickerDemoData.Models());
        Picker.SummaryNote = ModelPickerDemoData.PriceNote;
    }
}
```

### The summary and the confirmation

The summary shows the selected model's `Description` and four facts: Context (`ContextTokens`, such as "800K tokens"),
Input and Output (`InputPrice` and `OutputPrice` per million tokens, with `CurrencySymbol`) and Effort. A model without
levels shows "Fixed". Facts the model leaves empty show a dash. At 400 px or narrower the facts fold into two rows of two,
and a three-line description makes the summary taller without moving the pill.

After a choice in the menu, a confirmation appears under the facts: "Aurora Prime 3 → Cobalt Atlas 2" for a model, or
"Effort: Medium → High" for an effort level. It stays for `NoticeDuration` (2.6 seconds) and fades out. Its space is
always reserved, so nothing below it moves. `SummaryNote` is the small print under the facts; use it to state the unit
and whether the prices are real.

### The pill alone

Set `IsSummaryVisible` to false and the picker is only the pill. The menu, the keyboard behavior, the events and the
announcements are the same, so the pill can sit in a header or a toolbar.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ModelPickerPillOnlyDemo">
    <!-- Without the summary the picker is just the pill, for a toolbar or a header. -->
    <Border MaxWidth="560"
            Padding="16,12"
            BorderThickness="1"
            BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Border}"
            CornerRadius="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource RadiusPanel}"
            Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Surface}"
            Margin="0,0,0,160">
        <DockPanel>
            <TextBlock DockPanel.Dock="Left"
                       VerticalAlignment="Center"
                       Text="Draft reply"
                       FontSize="14"
                       FontWeight="Medium"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
            <arc:ModelPicker x:Name="Picker"
                             IsSummaryVisible="False"
                             HorizontalAlignment="Right"
                             MaxWidth="320" />
        </DockPanel>
    </Border>
</UserControl>
```

### Reading and setting the choice

`SelectedModel`, `SelectedModelId` and `Effort` are two-way. `ModelChanged` and `EffortChanged` run after a choice in the
menu, a snap to a level the model offers, or a change made in code. `IsSnap` on the effort event is true when a new
model moved the effort. `SelectCommand` and `EffortCommand` run with the new value for view models that prefer commands.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ModelPickerBindingsDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="16" MaxWidth="440" Margin="0,0,0,160">
        <arc:ModelPicker x:Name="Picker"
                         SelectedModelId="cobalt-atlas-2"
                         ModelChanged="OnModelChanged"
                         EffortChanged="OnEffortChanged" />
        <StackPanel Orientation="Horizontal" Spacing="8" HorizontalAlignment="Center">
            <arc:Button Content="Use Aurora Swift 3" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Click="OnUseSwift" />
            <arc:Button Content="Set effort to Max" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Click="OnMaxEffort" />
        </StackPanel>
        <TextBlock x:Name="Log"
                   HorizontalAlignment="Center"
                   TextAlignment="Center"
                   TextWrapping="Wrap"
                   FontSize="14"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class ModelPickerBindingsDemo : UserControl
{
    public ModelPickerBindingsDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Picker.Providers.AddRange(ModelPickerDemoData.Providers());
        Picker.Models.AddRange(ModelPickerDemoData.Models());
        Show("Start");
    }

    private void Show(string what) =>
        Log.Text = $"{what}: {Picker.SelectedModel?.Name ?? "no model"}, effort {(Picker.Effort is { } effort ? ModelEffortNames.Name(effort) : "none")}";

    // The events fire after a choice in the menu, a snap to a level the model offers, or a change made in code.
    private void OnModelChanged(object? sender, ModelPickerModelChangedEventArgs e) => Show("Model changed");

    private void OnEffortChanged(object? sender, ModelPickerEffortChangedEventArgs e) =>
        Show(e.IsSnap ? "Effort adjusted to fit the model" : "Effort changed");

    private void OnUseSwift(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) => Picker.SelectedModelId = "aurora-swift-3";

    // The model offers Low, Medium and High: a level it does not offer moves to the nearest one.
    private void OnMaxEffort(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) => Picker.Effort = ModelEffort.Max;
}
```

```csharp
public sealed class PickerSettings
{
    public string? ModelId { get; set; }

    public ModelEffort? Effort { get; set; }
}

picker.ModelChanged += (_, e) => settings.ModelId = e.NewModel?.Id;
picker.EffortChanged += (_, e) => settings.Effort = e.NewEffort;

// An id the catalog does not have yet waits for it.
picker.SelectedModelId = "cobalt-atlas-2";
```

```xml
<arc:ModelPicker SelectedModel="{Binding Model, Mode=TwoWay}"
                 Effort="{Binding Effort, Mode=TwoWay}"
                 ModelsSource="{Binding Catalog}"
                 IsOpen="{Binding IsPickerOpen, Mode=TwoWay}" />
```

- `ModelsSource` follows a collection you can change; it replaces the inline `Models`.
- `IsOpen` is two-way. Setting it before the picker is on screen opens the menu once it is shown. `Open()` and `Close()`
  do the same from code, and `Open(ModelMenuOpenFocus.Selected)` starts the keyboard position on the selected model.
- Setting `Effort` to a level the selected model does not offer corrects it at once, and the event reports the level that
  is really in use.

### Wording

`Labels` holds every word the picker shows or says, in a `ModelPickerLabels` object with English defaults. It has a part
for the pill, the menu and the summary, plus the confirmation and the announcements. Assign a new instance to change
them. The level names appear in all four places, so give each part the same function.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ModelPickerCustomWordingDemo">
    <arc:ModelPicker x:Name="Picker" Margin="0,12,0,160" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class ModelPickerCustomWordingDemo : UserControl
{
    public ModelPickerCustomWordingDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Picker.Providers.AddRange(ModelPickerDemoData.Providers());
        Picker.Models.AddRange(ModelPickerDemoData.Models());
        Picker.SummaryNote = "Preise in USD pro 1 Mio. Tokens · Beispielwerte";
        // Replace what you want to say differently; everything else keeps its English default. The level names are
        // shown by the pill, the menu, the summary and the confirmation, so each part gets the same function.
        Picker.Labels = new ModelPickerLabels
        {
            EffortName = Level,
            ModelNotice = (previous, next) => $"{previous} → {next}",
            EffortNotice = (previous, next) => $"Aufwand: {previous} → {next}",
            ModelAdjustedNotice = (previous, next, level) => $"{previous} → {next} · Aufwand auf {level} angepasst",
            ModelAnnouncement = (model, effort) => effort is null ? $"Jetzt aktiv: {model}" : $"Jetzt aktiv: {model}, Aufwand {effort}",
            EffortAnnouncement = (model, effort) => $"{model}, Aufwand {effort}",
            Pill = new ModelPillLabels
            {
                EffortName = Level,
                AutomationName = (model, effort) => $"Modell: {model.Name}, Aufwand {Level(effort)}. Modell wechseln",
                AutomationNameWithoutEffort = model => $"Modell: {model.Name}. Modell wechseln"
            },
            Menu = new ModelMenuLabels
            {
                Menu = "Modelle",
                Featured = "Empfohlene Modelle",
                Effort = "Aufwand",
                EffortMenu = "Aufwand",
                MoreModels = "Weitere Modelle",
                MoreModelsMenu = "Weitere Modelle",
                Default = "Standard",
                EffortName = Level
            },
            Summary = new ModelSummaryLabels
            {
                Region = "Gewähltes Modell",
                Context = "Kontext",
                Input = "Eingabe",
                Output = "Ausgabe",
                Effort = "Aufwand",
                NotAdjustable = "Fest",
                ContextValue = tokens => $"{tokens} Tokens",
                EffortName = Level
            }
        };
    }

    private static string Level(ModelEffort effort) => effort switch
    {
        ModelEffort.Low => "Niedrig",
        ModelEffort.Medium => "Mittel",
        ModelEffort.High => "Hoch",
        ModelEffort.ExtraHigh => "Sehr hoch",
        _ => "Maximal"
    };
}
```

```csharp
picker.Labels = new ModelPickerLabels
{
    EffortName = effort => effort == ModelEffort.Max ? "Maximal" : ModelEffortNames.Name(effort),
    ModelNotice = (previous, next) => $"{previous} → {next}",
    Menu = new ModelMenuLabels { MoreModels = "Weitere Modelle", Effort = "Aufwand" }
};
```

### Marks

A model's `Mark` is either a `Geometry` drawn in a 24 × 24 box and filled with `MarkColor` (or the text color, which
flips with the theme), or an `IImage` such as a `DrawingImage` that keeps its own colors. With no `Mark` the model uses
its provider's. Marks are decorative; the name is always next to them. Use your own shapes: the picker never adds a tile
or a border around a mark.

### Content guidelines

- **Blurb**: one line that says what the model is good at, such as "Reads charts, screenshots and PDFs". It is cut with
  an ellipsis, so put the useful words first.
- **Description**: one or two sentences for the summary. Say what it is for and what the person trades off.
- **Tag**: one or two words, such as "Fast" or "Open weights". It is plain text, not a badge.
- **Prices**: print real values only when they are real. Set `IsSamplePrice` on a placeholder and say so in `SummaryNote`.
- **Names**: use the name people see in your product, and keep the featured list to three to five models.

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| The best model for everything | Deep work: refactors, research, long tasks |
| Cheap | Quick and capable for daily chats |
| Model with 1000000 tokens | 1M tokens of context (the summary formats it) |

### Best practices

**Do**

- Give every model a stable `Id` and store the id, not the display name.
- Keep `EffortLevels` and `DefaultEffort` together on the model; the default must be one of the levels.
- Put the picker where the choice applies, such as the header of the chat or the field it affects.
- Handle `ModelChanged` and `EffortChanged` to save the choice; the picker keeps it in memory only.
- Pass `Providers` so the "More models" list is grouped and models without marks get their provider's.

**Avoid**

- Real vendor logos inside a design that is not theirs.
- More than five featured models. The menu stops being a short list.
- Hiding an effort the model cannot change: leave `EffortLevels` empty and the row disappears by itself.
- Calling `Open()` on every update. It moves keyboard focus into the menu.

### Common questions

**Why is there no search?** The menu is a short list with a long tail grouped by provider. For a long catalog use
`Combobox` and your own filter.

**Why does a level change when I pick another model?** The new model does not offer it. The picker moves the effort to the
nearest level that model offers, and says so in the confirmation.

**Can the menu open on hover?** No. The pill opens on a press, as a menu button does, so a pointer passing over it does
not open anything.

**Why does the summary say "Fixed"?** The selected model offers no effort levels. Change the wording with
`Labels.Summary.NotAdjustable`.

## API reference

### ModelPicker

Chooses a model and its reasoning effort from one compact pill. The pill shows the current choice; its menu lists a few featured models with a one-line note each, an effort setting, and every other model grouped by provider. Under the pill a summary shows what the model can hold and costs, and confirms each change for a moment. A composition of `ModelPill`, `ModelMenu` and `ModelSummary`: the catalog, the selection and the effort are properties, so bind them or read them back from the events. The pill opens on a pointer press or on Enter, Space and ArrowDown; the menu has a featured list, an Effort row and a More models row that open submenus (or pages in a narrow window); choosing closes the menu and returns focus to the pill; the effort moves to the nearest level a new model offers. Set `IsSummaryVisible` to false for the pill alone (a toolbar, a header). Screen readers hear a polite announcement after each change ("Now using Aurora Prime 3, medium effort"); the visible confirmation under the summary stays for `NoticeDuration`.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ModelsSource` | `IEnumerable<AiModel>?` | `null` | The catalog when you give it as a collection to follow; it wins over `Models` when set. |
| `SelectedModel` | `AiModel?` | `null` | The selected model (two-way). Null at first selects the first featured model once and writes it back. |
| `SelectedModelId` | `string?` | `null` | The id of the selected model (two-way); an id the catalog does not have yet waits for the catalog. |
| `Effort` | `ModelEffort?` | `null` | The effort (two-way); a level the selected model does not offer moves to the nearest one, and a model without levels has none (null). |
| `IsOpen` | `bool` | `false` | Whether the menu is open (two-way). |
| `IsSummaryVisible` | `bool` | `true` | Shows the summary under the pill (default); false leaves the pill alone, for a toolbar or a header. |
| `SummaryNote` | `string?` | `null` | Small print under the summary's facts, such as "Prices in USD per 1M tokens · demo values"; null shows none. |
| `PagedMenuWidth` | `double` | `640` | The window width at or below which the menu's submenus become pages inside the menu (640). |
| `NoticeDuration` | `TimeSpan` | `00:00:02.6000000` | How long the confirmation under the summary stays after a change (2.6 s); zero shows none. |
| `CurrencySymbol` | `string` | `"$"` | The currency symbol in front of the summary's prices ("$"). |
| `SelectCommand` | `ICommand?` | `null` | Run with the new `AiModel` when the selection changes. |
| `EffortCommand` | `ICommand?` | `null` | Run with the new `ModelEffort` (null when the model has none) when the effort changes. |
| `Labels` | `ModelPickerLabels` | – | Every word the picker shows or reads out, with English defaults (see `ModelPickerLabels`). |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ModelChanged` | `ModelPickerModelChangedEventArgs` | Raised when the selected model changes, by a choice in the menu or by code. |
| `EffortChanged` | `ModelPickerEffortChangedEventArgs` | Raised when the effort changes: a choice in the menu, a snap to a level the new model offers, or code. |

Pseudo-classes: `:open`, `:summary-hidden`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

### AiModel

A model a person can choose in the AI blocks: the model picker, the model pill and menu in a composer, a chat header or a prompt studio. Data only: an `AvaloniaObject` so the properties bind and a change (a new description, a price update) reaches what is on screen.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Id` | `string` | `""` | Stable id reported in events and bindings (the model's API id). |
| `Name` | `string` | `""` | The full display name, such as in a menu row. |
| `ShortName` | `string?` | `null` | A shorter name for tight places (a toolbar pill); `DisplayName` falls back to `Name`. |
| `ProviderId` | `string?` | `null` | The id of the provider this model belongs to (`AiModelProvider`); groups the "More models" list and supplies a missing mark. |
| `Blurb` | `string?` | `null` | One line under the name in a featured menu row. |
| `Description` | `string?` | `null` | A longer sentence for the summary below the picker. |
| `Note` | `string?` | `null` | A short note after the name in a simple menu row, such as the vendor. |
| `Tag` | `string?` | `null` | A small label at the end of a compact row, such as "Fast" or "Open weights". |
| `Mark` | `object?` | `null` | The model's mark: a `Geometry` in a 24 × 24 box (filled with `MarkColor` or the text color) or an `IImage` such as a `DrawingImage` for a multicolor mark. Null falls back to the provider's mark. |
| `MarkColor` | `IBrush?` | `null` | The fill of a `Geometry` mark; null uses the text color (it flips with the theme). |
| `ContextTokens` | `long?` | `null` | The context window in tokens. |
| `MaxOutputTokens` | `long?` | `null` | The largest reply in tokens. |
| `InputPrice` | `decimal?` | `null` | Price of one million input tokens (in the currency you show; the format adds the symbol). |
| `OutputPrice` | `decimal?` | `null` | Price of one million output tokens. |
| `IsSamplePrice` | `bool` | `false` | True when the prices are placeholders; parts that print a price note it. |
| `EffortLevels` | `IReadOnlyList<ModelEffort>?` | `null` | The effort levels the model offers; null or empty means the model has no effort setting. |
| `DefaultEffort` | `ModelEffort?` | `null` | The level used when nothing is chosen yet; must be one of `EffortLevels`. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### AiModelProvider

A company or project that makes models: groups the "More models" list and supplies the mark of its models that have none.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Id` | `string` | `""` | Stable id that `ProviderId` refers to. |
| `Name` | `string` | `""` | The group title in the "More models" list. |
| `Mark` | `object?` | `null` | The mark of models without their own; same kinds as `Mark`. |
| `MarkColor` | `IBrush?` | `null` | The fill of a `Geometry` mark; null uses the text color. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### ModelEffort

| Value | Name | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Low` | Low | Short replies, lowest latency |
| `Medium` | Medium | Everyday balance |
| `High` | High | Works through harder problems |
| `ExtraHigh` | Extra high | Long, careful reasoning |
| `Max` | Max | Exhaustive, slowest |

`ModelEffortNames.Name(effort)` and `ModelEffortNames.Description(effort)` return these words, and `ModelEffortSnap.Snap`
picks the level a model offers.

### ModelPickerLabels

| Property | Default | Where it shows |
|---|---|---|
| `Pill` | `ModelPillLabels` | Accessible name of the pill |
| `Menu` | `ModelMenuLabels` | Rows, pages and accessible names of the menu |
| `Summary` | `ModelSummaryLabels` | Fact labels and values of the summary |
| `EffortName` (function of level) | "Medium" | Confirmation and announcements |
| `ModelNotice` (function of old and new name) | "A → B" | Confirmation after a model change |
| `EffortNotice` (function of old and new level) | "Effort: Medium → High" | Confirmation after an effort change |
| `ModelAdjustedNotice` | "A → B · Effort adjusted to High" | Confirmation when the effort moved too |
| `ModelAnnouncement` | "Now using Aurora Prime 3, medium effort" | Polite announcement after a model change |
| `EffortAnnouncement` | "Aurora Prime 3, high effort" | Polite announcement after an effort change |

### ModelMenuLabels, ModelPillLabels and ModelSummaryLabels

| Property | Default | Where it shows |
|---|---|---|
| `ModelMenuLabels.Menu` | "Models" | Accessible name of the menu |
| `ModelMenuLabels.Featured` | "Featured models" | Accessible name of the featured group |
| `ModelMenuLabels.Effort` / `MoreModels` | "Effort" / "More models" | The two rows under the featured list |
| `ModelMenuLabels.EffortMenu` / `MoreModelsMenu` | "Effort" / "More models" | Submenu names and page titles |
| `ModelMenuLabels.Default` | "Default" | After the model's default level |
| `ModelMenuLabels.BackTo` | "Back to featured models, Effort" | Accessible name of the back row |
| `ModelMenuLabels.Empty` | "No models available" | The only line of an empty menu |
| `ModelPillLabels.AutomationName` | "Model: Aurora Prime 3, medium effort. Change model" | Accessible name of the pill |
| `ModelSummaryLabels.Region` | "Selected model" | Accessible name of the summary |
| `ModelSummaryLabels.Context` / `Input` / `Output` / `Effort` | "Context" / "Input" / "Output" / "Effort" | Fact labels |
| `ModelSummaryLabels.NotAdjustable` | "Fixed" | Effort fact of a model without levels |
| `ModelSummaryLabels.ContextValue` | "800K tokens" | Context fact |

## Accessibility

- The pill is a button named by the model and the effort, such as "Model: Aurora Prime 3, medium effort. Change model",
  and reports whether the menu is open.
- The menu is a menu. Featured models and effort levels are radio items with a checked state; the Effort and More models
  rows report that they open a submenu; the provider groups are named by the provider.
- After a choice, a polite live region says "Now using Aurora Swift 3, medium effort" (or the effort sentence for an
  effort change). The visible confirmation is not what screen readers hear.
- Focus returns to the pill when the menu closes. After a keyboard close the pill shows its focus ring; after a pointer
  close it does not.
- The summary is a labeled region, and each fact reads as one phrase, such as "Context: 800K tokens".
- Marks are decorative.
- Reduced motion keeps every state and every announcement.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Enter`, `Space` or `ArrowDown` on the pill | Opens the menu with the selected model highlighted |
| `ArrowUp` / `ArrowDown` in the menu | Moves between the rows; wraps around at the ends |
| `Home` / `End` | First or last row |
| A letter | Jumps to the next row whose name starts with it; repeat to cycle |
| `Enter` or `Space` on a model or level | Chooses it, closes the menu and returns focus to the pill |
| `Enter`, `Space` or `ArrowRight` on Effort or More models | Opens the submenu with the selected entry highlighted |
| `ArrowLeft` | Closes the submenu (or goes back a page) and returns to its row |
| `Escape` | Closes the whole menu and returns focus to the pill |
| `Tab` | Does nothing inside the menu |

## Motion

- The menu grows out of the pill: it starts 6 px toward it at scale 0.97, fades in over 160 ms and settles on Arc's
  spring curve over 580 ms. It leaves in 130 ms at half the distance and scale 0.985. A close during an open, or an
  open during a close, continues from where the surface is.
- One highlight glides between the rows on a snappy spring for the pointer, jumps for the keyboard, fades in where it
  appears in 80 ms and fades out in 80 ms.
- Submenus enter and leave the same way from the side of their row. Moving to another row closes the open submenu at
  once; a diagonal move toward it does not.
- In a narrow window the new page slides in 12 px from the side of travel while it fades in over 160 ms, and the menu's
  height follows the page on the smooth spring.
- After a choice the pill's mark and text crossfade in 100 and 160 ms, and its width follows the new text on a quick
  spring. The summary crossfades its description and only the facts that changed. The confirmation fades in, stays for
  2.6 seconds and fades out.
- Reduced motion drops movement and springs and keeps 120 ms fades. Off applies every change at once.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| Menu opens or closes | Grows from the pill; 160 ms fade, 580 ms spring | 120 ms fade | Immediate |
| Highlight | Glides, fades in and out in 80 ms | Jumps, 120 ms fade | Immediate |
| Page in a narrow window | Slides 12 px and fades in; height springs | 120 ms fade | Immediate |
| Pill changes model | Mark and text crossfade; width springs | 120 ms crossfade | Immediate |
| Summary changes | Description and changed facts crossfade | 120 ms crossfade | Immediate |
| Confirmation | Fades in, stays 2.6 s, fades out | 120 ms fades | Immediate |

## Related

- `Select` and `Combobox` for choosing one item from a list that is not about models.
- `DropdownMenu` for a menu of actions.
- `SegmentedControl` for a short choice that stays visible.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `Select` / `Combobox` | The list is long, searchable or not about models |
| `DropdownMenu` | The menu lists actions, not a choice that stays selected |
| `SegmentedControl` | A few options must be visible at once |
| `Popover` | A small form or panel opens from a button |
