# AI side panel

> An assistant beside a page the person reads: it reads the whole page, answers about it or about a selection, and proposes changes as a word diff that the person applies, discards or undoes, with a sweep on the page and an Undo pill.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc.Blocks`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc.Blocks --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/blocks/ai-side-panel

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.AiSidePanelPreviewDemo">
    <!-- The page on the left, the assistant on the right. Select some text on the page, or press a suggestion. -->
    <Border Height="640" BorderThickness="1" CornerRadius="16" ClipToBounds="True" BorderBrush="#33808080" Margin="0,12">
        <arc:AiSidePanel x:Name="Panel" AssistantName="Helper" ModelName="Model X1" />
    </Border>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class AiSidePanelPreviewDemo : UserControl
{
    public AiSidePanelPreviewDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Panel.Page = AiSidePanelDemoData.Page();
        Panel.Suggestions.AddRange(AiSidePanelDemoData.Suggestions);
        Panel.Responder = new AiSidePanelDemoData.ScriptedResponder();

        // Save the page when a change is applied or undone.
        Panel.ChangeApplied += (_, e) => System.Diagnostics.Debug.WriteLine($"Applied to {e.Change.BlockId}");
    }
}
```

## When to use

The AI side panel is for a page that people read and sometimes change: a specification, a record, a knowledge base article. The assistant sits next to the page, reads all of it, and
when the page should change it does not rewrite it behind the person's back: it shows the change as a card, and the person decides.

- **A design note or specification**: "Shorten the summary" returns a card with the new text as a word diff; Apply writes it into the page.
- **A record or settings page with tables**: ask for a new column and see it as a small table with the new cells tinted before anything changes.
- **A help page where people ask about a passage**: select text, press "Ask about selection", and the question carries that passage as context.
- **A page that must stay in the person's hands**: every change can be undone, and nothing is applied without Apply.

## When not to use

- **A conversation with no page**: use `AiChat`.
- **Rewriting one piece of text in place**: an inline edit control suits it better; the panel works on a page of blocks.
- **A page that is not made of headings, paragraphs and tables**: the panel renders those three kinds of block. Show richer pages yourself and use the panel's thread beside them.
- **Running the model**: the panel asks your `IAiPanelResponder`; it does not call anything by itself.

## Usage

`AiSidePanel` derives from Avalonia's `TemplatedControl` and fills its container, so give it a height. Give it a `Page`, a `Responder` and the `Suggestions` for the empty thread.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:AiSidePanel Height="640" AssistantName="Helper" ModelName="Model X1" PanelWidth="360" />
</UserControl>
```

```csharp
var page = new AiPanelPage { Title = "Offline sync", Meta = "Design note, updated Mar 3" };
page.Blocks.Add(new AiPanelParagraph { Id = "summary", Label = "Summary", Text = "Offline sync is a planned change..." });
panel.Page = page;
panel.Responder = new MyResponder();
panel.ChangeApplied += (_, e) => Save(e.Page);
```

### The page

An `AiPanelPage` has a title, a line of meta text and `Blocks`: an `AiPanelHeading`, an `AiPanelParagraph` or an `AiPanelTable` (columns and rows). Every block has an `Id` and a `Label`
("Summary", "Storage table"); the label names the block on the selection pill, the change card and the placeholder, and to screen readers. The panel works on the page object you give it: when a change is applied the block in the
page is replaced, so the page you hold is always current. Replacing `Page` resets the thread and the undo.

### Answering

A `IAiPanelResponder` receives the question, the page as it is now (with every applied change) and the selection, and returns an `AiPanelReply`: text, and optionally a change.

```csharp
public async ValueTask<AiPanelReply> RespondAsync(AiPanelRequest request, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
{
    var summary = (AiPanelParagraph)request.Page.Find("summary")!;
    return AiPanelReply.FromText(
        "Here is a shorter summary.",
        new AiPanelChangeProposal("summary", new AiPanelParagraph { Id = "summary", Label = "Summary", Text = shorter }));
}
```

While your method runs, the panel shows "Reading the page"; the text then arrives in whole words about every 50 ms (four to seven words a step, faster to catch up on a long backlog). `AiPanelReply.FromText` takes a whole
text and the panel cuts it into words itself; pass an `IAsyncEnumerable<string>` for a real stream. Stopping cancels the token and keeps what was shown, with the note "Stopped" and no card. An exception shows an error card with
Retry, which asks the same question again.

### Changes

A reply may propose a change to **one block**: the id and the whole new block. The panel shows a card with a header (the block's label and a summary such as "21 words, was 45" or "Adds Sync column"), the change as a word diff
(deleted words struck through, inserted words tinted; a table shows the new table with its new cells tinted) and the buttons Discard and Apply.

- **Apply** writes the change into the page. The block on the page sweeps with a tint from left to right while the old text fades out and the new text fades in and the block's height springs to its new size; an Undo pill ("Summary updated, Undo")
  appears above the box and focus moves to it. `ChangeApplied` is raised with the updated page; save it there.
- **Undo** restores the block with the same sweep and the card reads "Undone"; it can be applied again. Only the **last** applied change can be undone, and the pill stays until it is.
- **Discard** dims the card and ends it; it can no longer be applied.

Several cards can wait at once and be applied in any order.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.AiSidePanelProgrammaticDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12" Margin="0,12">
        <StackPanel Orientation="Horizontal" Spacing="8" HorizontalAlignment="Center">
            <arc:Button x:Name="Shorten" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Content="Ask: shorten the summary" />
            <arc:Button x:Name="Toggle" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Content="Open / close" />
            <arc:Button x:Name="Undo" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Content="Undo" />
        </StackPanel>
        <Border Height="560" BorderThickness="1" CornerRadius="16" ClipToBounds="True" BorderBrush="#33808080">
            <arc:AiSidePanel x:Name="Panel" AssistantName="Helper" />
        </Border>
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class AiSidePanelProgrammaticDemo : UserControl
{
    public AiSidePanelProgrammaticDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Panel.Page = AiSidePanelDemoData.Page();
        Panel.Responder = new AiSidePanelDemoData.ScriptedResponder();

        // The panel can be driven from code: ask, open, close, undo.
        Shorten.Click += async (_, _) => await Panel.AskAsync("Shorten the summary");
        Toggle.Click += (_, _) => Panel.IsOpen = !Panel.IsOpen;
        Undo.Click += (_, _) => Panel.Undo();
    }
}
```

### Selection

Drag across text on the page and a button "Ask about selection" appears under the selection. Pressing it clears the selection, adds a pill "Selection: Summary" to the header and marks the block with a line on its left; the box takes
focus with a placeholder about that block. The pill stays for the next questions until its × removes it. A selection belongs to the block where it starts; a table selection is labeled with the table. `SelectionAsked` reports it, and
`ClearSelection()` removes it from code.

### Open, close and narrow containers

`IsOpen` (two-way), `Open()` and `Close()` show and hide the assistant. Docked, its width springs between `PanelWidth` (360) and zero and the page column re-centers; closed, a pill with the assistant's name sits at the top right of the page to reopen it.
Escape inside the panel closes it and returns focus to that pill; opening puts focus in the box. In a container narrower than `SheetBreakpoint` (640) the assistant is a bottom sheet over the page (`SheetHeightRatio`, 74%): the page dims and is inert
while it is open, and pressing the dimmed page or the close button closes it.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.AiSidePanelNarrowDemo">
    <!-- Below 640 the assistant is a bottom sheet over the page, and the page is inert while it is open. -->
    <Border Width="480" Height="640" BorderThickness="1" CornerRadius="16" ClipToBounds="True" BorderBrush="#33808080" Margin="0,12">
        <arc:AiSidePanel x:Name="Panel" AssistantName="Helper" IsOpen="False" />
    </Border>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class AiSidePanelNarrowDemo : UserControl
{
    public AiSidePanelNarrowDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Panel.Page = AiSidePanelDemoData.Page();
        Panel.Suggestions.AddRange(AiSidePanelDemoData.Suggestions);
        Panel.Responder = new AiSidePanelDemoData.ScriptedResponder();
    }
}
```

### Wording

Every word comes from `Labels` (`AiSidePanelLabels`): replace the instance to translate or reword; formatted texts are functions. `AssistantName` and `ModelName` fill the header; `AssistantMark` replaces the spark icon (a geometry or an image).

### Content guidelines

- **Block labels**: short nouns the person would say ("Summary", "Pricing table").
- **Suggestions**: three at most, each something the page lets the assistant do ("Shorten the summary").
- **Change summaries**: let the panel generate them; they are counts, not prose.
- **Answers**: say what changed in a sentence; the card shows how.

### Best practices

- Save the page in `ChangeApplied` and `ChangeUndone`, not on every answer.
- Give blocks stable ids; a change refers to its block by id.
- Propose one block per answer; the person can ask again for the next.
- Keep the responder fast to start: the first feedback is "Reading the page".

### Common questions

**Why did Apply not change my data?** It changes the `Page` object you gave the panel; save it in `ChangeApplied`.

**Why can I only undo the last change?** The Undo pill belongs to the latest applied change; applying another replaces it, and earlier cards still say "Applied".

**Can the assistant edit several blocks at once?** One block per card; ask again for the next.

## API reference

### AiSidePanel

An assistant beside a page the person reads: the page on the left, the assistant on the right (or a bottom sheet in a narrow container). The assistant reads the whole page, answers questions about it or about a selection, and when the page should change it answers with a card that shows the change as a word diff. The person applies it (the block on the page sweeps with a tint and an Undo pill appears), discards it, or undoes it.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Page` | `AiPanelPage?` | `null` | The page to read and change. Replacing the object resets the thread and the undo. |
| `Responder` | `IAiPanelResponder?` | `null` | Answers the questions; null lets the box send nothing. |
| `IsOpen` | `bool` | `true` | Whether the assistant is open (two-way): docked beside the page, or a bottom sheet in a narrow container. |
| `AssistantName` | `string` | `"Assistant"` | The assistant's name, used in the header, the reopen button and the status texts. |
| `ModelName` | `string?` | `null` | A second line in the header, such as the model's name. |
| `AssistantMark` | `object?` | `null` | The assistant's mark (a geometry in a 24 × 24 box or an image); null shows a spark icon. |
| `PanelWidth` | `double` | `360` | The width of the docked assistant. |
| `PageMaxWidth` | `double` | `680` | The widest the page column grows. |
| `SheetBreakpoint` | `double` | `640` | Below this container width the assistant is a bottom sheet over the page. |
| `SheetHeightRatio` | `double` | `0.74` | The height of the bottom sheet as a share of the container's height. |
| `StreamInterval` | `TimeSpan` | `00:00:00.0500000` | How often streamed text is released (50 ms): each step shows a few whole words. |
| `MinWordsPerStep` | `int` | `4` | The fewest whole words a step shows. |
| `MaxWordsPerStep` | `int` | `7` | The most whole words a step shows; a long backlog is released at this rate to catch up. |
| `IsSheetMode` | `bool` | – | *Read-only.* Whether the assistant is a bottom sheet because the container is narrow (read-only). |
| `IsBusy` | `bool` | – | *Read-only.* Whether the assistant is reading the page or writing (read-only). |
| `Selection` | `AiPanelSelection?` | – | *Read-only.* The selection the next question is about (read-only); `ClearSelection` removes it. |
| `LastApplied` | `AiPanelChange?` | – | *Read-only.* The change the Undo pill would undo (read-only). |
| `ApplyCommand` | `ICommand?` | `null` | Run when the person applies a change, with the `AiPanelChange` as the parameter. |
| `UndoCommand` | `ICommand?` | `null` | Run when the person undoes a change. |
| `DiscardCommand` | `ICommand?` | `null` | Run when the person discards a change. |
| `Labels` | `AiSidePanelLabels` | – | Every word the block shows or announces. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ChangeApplied` | `AiPanelChangeEventArgs` | Raised after a change is applied and the page data is updated; save the page here. |
| `ChangeUndone` | `AiPanelChangeEventArgs` | Raised after a change is undone. |
| `ChangeDiscarded` | `AiPanelChangeEventArgs` | Raised after a change is discarded. |
| `SelectionAsked` | `AiPanelSelectionEventArgs` | Raised when a selection is added as the context of the next question. |

Pseudo-classes: `:sheet`, `:open`, `:busy`, `:empty`, `:selection`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

### AiPanelPage

The page the assistant reads and edits: a title, a line of meta text and blocks.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Title` | `string` | `""` | The title. |
| `Meta` | `string?` | `null` | A line under the title ("Updated Mar 3 by Priya"). |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### AiPanelHeading

A heading of the page.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Text` | `string` | `""` | The heading text. |
| `Id` | `string` | `""` | Stable id; selections and changes refer to blocks by it. |
| `Label` | `string?` | `null` | The name of the block ("Introduction", "Pricing table"): shown on the selection pill, the change card, the placeholder and to screen readers. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### AiPanelParagraph

A paragraph of the page.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Text` | `string` | `""` | The paragraph text. |
| `Id` | `string` | `""` | Stable id; selections and changes refer to blocks by it. |
| `Label` | `string?` | `null` | The name of the block ("Introduction", "Pricing table"): shown on the selection pill, the change card, the placeholder and to screen readers. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### AiPanelTable

A table of the page.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Id` | `string` | `""` | Stable id; selections and changes refer to blocks by it. |
| `Label` | `string?` | `null` | The name of the block ("Introduction", "Pricing table"): shown on the selection pill, the change card, the placeholder and to screen readers. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### AiPanelTurn

One exchange of the thread: the question, the context it was asked in, the answer and an optional change.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Prompt` | `string` | `""` | What the person asked. |
| `ContextLabel` | `string?` | `null` | The label of the selection the question was asked about, if any. |
| `Answer` | `string` | `""` | The answer text; grows while it streams. |
| `State` | `AiPanelTurnState` | `Done` | Where the turn is. |
| `ErrorMessage` | `string?` | `null` | Why the turn failed. |
| `Change` | `AiPanelChange?` | `null` | The change the assistant proposes with its answer, if any. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### AiPanelChange

A change to one block that the assistant proposes: shown as a card with a word diff, applied or discarded by the person.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `BlockId` | `string` | `""` | The id of the block that changes. |
| `Before` | `AiPanelBlock?` | `null` | The block as it is on the page when the card is made; the block to restore on undo. |
| `After` | `AiPanelBlock?` | `null` | The whole new block. |
| `State` | `AiPanelChangeState` | `Proposed` | Where the change is. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### Events

| Event | Raised when | Arguments |
|---|---|---|
| `ChangeApplied` | A change was applied and the page data updated | `Change`, `Page` |
| `ChangeUndone` | A change was undone | `Change`, `Page` |
| `ChangeDiscarded` | A change was discarded | `Change`, `Page` |
| `SelectionAsked` | A selection became the context of the next question | `Selection` |

### The responder

| Type | Description |
|---|---|
| `IAiPanelResponder` | `RespondAsync(request, cancellationToken)` returns an `AiPanelReply` |
| `AiPanelRequest` | The prompt, the page as it is now and the selection, if any |
| `AiPanelReply` | The answer text (whole through `FromText`, or a stream) and an optional change |
| `AiPanelChangeProposal` | The id of the block and the whole new block |

## Accessibility

- The panel is a region named after the assistant; the page and the thread are separate regions. Each page block is named by its label.
- The header's context pill says what the assistant reads; the selection pill is a button named "Remove selection" with the selected text as its description.
- A polite live region announces that the assistant is reading the page, that an answer is ready, stopped or failed, that a change was suggested, applied, undone or discarded, that a selection was added, and that the panel opened or closed.
  Streamed words are not announced one by one.
- The change card's buttons are named and report their state; an applied card is not a button.
- Focus goes where the person would look next: to the Undo pill after Apply, back to that card's Apply after Undo, into the box after Discard or opening the panel, to the reopen pill after closing it.
- In sheet mode the page below is inert while the sheet is open.
- Reduced motion keeps every state and announcement.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Tab` | Page controls, the header, the thread (cards, Retry), the Undo pill, the box |
| `Enter` or `Space` | Presses the focused button |
| `Enter` in the box | Sends; `Escape` while an answer is written stops it |
| `Escape` elsewhere in the panel | Closes the assistant and focuses the reopen pill |

## Motion

- The docked panel's width springs between open and closed; the panel body keeps its width and slides with the edge while the page re-centers.
- Streamed words appear in steps of four to seven every 50 ms and each step fades in over 150 ms.
- Applying a change sweeps a tint across the block (about 420 ms), holds, and fades it (about 630 ms); the old text fades out in 100 ms and the new text fades in after 80 ms over 180 ms, and the height springs.
- The ask button, the Undo pill and the reopen pill fade in and out.
- The bottom sheet slides and fades in.
- Reduced motion drops springs and travel: the sweep becomes a tint fade over the whole block, the sheet fades in place and words keep their cadence without fading. Off applies every change at once.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| Open and close | Width spring | 120 ms fade | Immediate |
| Apply or Undo | Sweep, crossfade, height spring | Whole-block tint fade, no travel | Immediate |
| New words | Steps of whole words, 150 ms fade | Same steps, no fade | Same steps, no fade |
| Sheet | Slide and fade | Fade in place | Immediate |

## Related

- `AiChat` for a conversation without a page.
- `AiComposer` for the prompt box on its own.
- `PromptStudio` for editing prompts rather than pages.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `AiChat` | There is no page to read or change |
| `AiComposer` | You only need the box |
| `PromptStudio` | The thing being edited is a prompt template |

# Prompt studio

> A card to edit a prompt template with colored variable chips, try it on saved test cases, and compare and ship versions: version and model menus, variable fields, a Run button and an output panel for the reply.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc.Blocks`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc.Blocks --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/blocks/prompt-studio

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.PromptStudioPreviewDemo">
    <!-- Edit the template, type {{ to add a variable, pick a test case and press Run (Ctrl or Cmd + Enter). -->
    <arc:PromptStudio x:Name="Studio" Title="Refund reply" MaxWidth="660" Margin="0,12" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class PromptStudioPreviewDemo : UserControl
{
    public PromptStudioPreviewDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Studio.Versions.AddRange(PromptStudioDemoData.Versions());
        Studio.Variables.AddRange(PromptStudioDemoData.Variables);
        Studio.TestCases.AddRange(PromptStudioDemoData.TestCases());
        Studio.Models.AddRange(PromptStudioDemoData.Models());
        Studio.OpenVersion = Studio.Versions[0];
        Studio.ProductionVersion = Studio.Versions[0];
        Studio.SelectedTestCase = Studio.TestCases[0];
        Studio.SelectedModel = Studio.Models[1];

        // Runs go through your handler; the "Out of policy" case fails once so Retry can be tried.
        Studio.RunHandler = new PromptStudioDemoData.Runner().Run;
    }
}
```

## When to use

The prompt studio is for the people who maintain the prompt behind an AI feature, not for the feature's end users. It puts the whole loop on one card: edit the template, try it on saved test cases, look at what changed
between versions, and promote one to production.

- **An admin or settings page for an AI feature**: the support-reply prompt of a help desk, the summary prompt of a document tool.
- **A review of prompt changes**: compare the open version with another as a word diff before promoting it.
- **A place to try a prompt on real examples**: saved test cases fill the variables, Run shows the reply with its time, tokens and cost.
- **Choosing a model and an effort next to the prompt**: with prices, so the cost of a change is visible.

## When not to use

- **A chat with an assistant**: use `AiChat`.
- **A code or free-text editor**: the template editor knows one kind of token, the variable in double braces.
- **Evaluating a prompt on hundreds of cases**: the card runs one test case at a time.
- **Storing the prompts**: the card edits a draft and tells you; saving, versions and promotion are your code.

## Usage

`PromptStudio` derives from Avalonia's `TemplatedControl`. Give it the `Versions`, the `Variables`, the `TestCases` and the `Models`, and a `RunHandler`; with no handler a built-in simulator answers and the card says it is simulated.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:PromptStudio Title="Refund reply" MaxWidth="660" />
</UserControl>
```

```csharp
studio.Versions.AddRange(versions);                 // newest first
studio.Variables.AddRange(["buyer_name", "ticket_id"]);
studio.TestCases.AddRange(testCases);
studio.Models.AddRange(models);
studio.OpenVersion = studio.Versions[0];
studio.ProductionVersion = studio.Versions[0];
studio.RunHandler = async IAsyncEnumerable<string> (request, cancellationToken) => { /* yield text */ };
```

### The template

A template has a system message and a user message (the System and User tabs). A variable is written between double braces, such as `{{buyer_name}}`, and shows in the editor as a colored chip with only its name.
Each variable takes one of four series colors in the order of `Variables`; names found in the text but not listed are added after them.

- Typing two opening braces opens a list of the known variables at the caret: Up and Down move, Enter or Tab insert, Escape closes, and typing filters; the last row adds the name you typed as a new variable. Typing the name and two closing braces also makes a chip, and pasted text with spaces inside the braces is normalized.
- A chip is one unit: the caret skips over it, Backspace or Delete removes it whole, and copying it writes the braces and the name.
- Undo and redo restore chips; typing is grouped into steps by pauses of about a second and by spaces.
- Pressing a chip focuses the variable's field.

`Draft` is the template being edited (two-way) and `TemplateChanged` fires after every edit; save it there. A token estimate for the shown part sits at the top right of the editor; set `TokenEstimator` to use your tokenizer.

### Variables and test cases

Each variable has a field with a dot and a label in its color. Focusing a field highlights its chips in the editor, every keystroke flashes them, and an empty value draws its chips with a dashed outline. Choosing a test case
resets the values to its own; values you typed are discarded. `Values` holds the current values.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.PromptStudioMinimalDemo">
    <!-- No versions, models or run handler: just a template, its variables and the built-in simulator. -->
    <arc:PromptStudio x:Name="Studio" Title="Greeting" MaxWidth="660" Margin="0,12" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class PromptStudioMinimalDemo : UserControl
{
    public PromptStudioMinimalDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Studio.Draft = new PromptTemplate("You greet people warmly in one sentence.", "Greet {{name}} who just joined the {{team}} team.");
        var testCase = new PromptTestCase { Id = "one", Label = "New hire" };
        testCase.Values["name"] = "Sam";
        testCase.Values["team"] = "support";
        Studio.TestCases.Add(testCase);
        Studio.SelectedTestCase = testCase;
    }
}
```

### Running

Run (or Ctrl+Enter, Cmd+Enter on a Mac, anywhere in the card) renders the template with the values and calls `RunHandler`, which returns the reply as a stream of text. The output panel shows "Thinking", then "Writing" with the reply appearing in whole words, then
"Reply" with a footer such as "1.57 s, 245 tokens, $0.0014"; the cost comes from the model's `InputPrice` and `OutputPrice` per million tokens and is left out when it has none. The button turns into Stop while it runs; stopping keeps what was written.
A handler that throws shows an error box with Retry (`RunFailed` lets you word the message). Only one run goes at a time: a new run or Stop cancels the token of the previous one. `RunState`, `LastResult`, `RunStarted` and `RunCompleted` tell the rest.

### Versions

The version pill ("v4, Production") opens the version menu: each version with its author, commit message and age, and two actions on the selected one.

- **Compare** turns the editor into a word diff between the open version and the selected one: inserted words tinted, deleted words struck through, a count such as +17 −1 and a "Back to editing" button; a dot on the tab shows which part changed. `IsCompareMode` and `CompareVersion` are two-way, and Escape leaves.
- **Promote to production** moves the Production marker to the selected version. `ProductionVersion` changes at once and `Promoted` is raised with the version and the previous one; set `Cancel` to refuse, and the studio rolls back. An Undo in the menu swaps them back, raising `Promoted` again with `IsUndo`.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.PromptStudioCompareDemo">
    <!-- The version menu compares the open version with another as a word diff, or promotes it to production. -->
    <arc:PromptStudio x:Name="Studio" Title="Refund reply" MaxWidth="660" Margin="0,12" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class PromptStudioCompareDemo : UserControl
{
    public PromptStudioCompareDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Studio.Versions.AddRange(PromptStudioDemoData.Versions());
        Studio.Variables.AddRange(PromptStudioDemoData.Variables);
        Studio.TestCases.AddRange(PromptStudioDemoData.TestCases());
        Studio.Models.AddRange(PromptStudioDemoData.Models());
        Studio.OpenVersion = Studio.Versions[0];
        Studio.ProductionVersion = Studio.Versions[1];

        // Open straight in the compare view: v4 against the version in production.
        Studio.CompareVersion = Studio.Versions[1];
        Studio.IsCompareMode = true;
        Studio.RunHandler = new PromptStudioDemoData.Runner().Run;
    }
}
```

### Model and effort

The model pill opens a menu of `Models` with their prices per million tokens (input and output) and a row of efforts. Choosing a model resets the effort to the model's default and keeps the menu open; prices marked as examples are noted at the bottom.

### Wording

Every word comes from `Labels` (`PromptStudioLabels`): replace the instance to translate or reword; formatted texts are functions. `Now` sets the moment relative times ("last week") are measured from.

### Content guidelines

- **Variable names**: lower case with underscores that say what goes in (`buyer_name`).
- **Test cases**: short labels (three or four words at most); they share one segmented control.
- **Commit messages**: what changed, in a few words.
- **Prices**: say when they are examples.

### Best practices

- Save in `TemplateChanged`, and roll a promotion back with `Cancel` when your server refuses it.
- Pass the cancellation token on in your run handler so Stop really stops.
- Keep test cases that cover the edges of the prompt, such as a missing value.
- Compare before promoting: the diff is the review.

### Common questions

**Why does Run say simulated?** No `RunHandler` is set, so the built-in simulator answered.

**Why is a chip dashed?** Its variable has no value in the current test case.

**Can I use my own variable syntax?** The card uses double braces.

## API reference

### PromptStudio

A card to edit a prompt template, try it on saved test cases, and compare and ship versions: the version and the model on top, a system / user template editor whose `{{name}}` variables are colored chips, a field for each variable, a row of test cases, a Run button and an output panel for the reply. A version menu compares the open version with another as a word diff or promotes it to production, and a model menu picks the model and the effort. With no `RunHandler` a built-in simulator answers and the card says so.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Title` | `string` | `""` | The name of the prompt, in the header. |
| `OpenVersion` | `PromptVersion?` | `null` | The version the editor has open (two-way); null opens the first (newest). |
| `ProductionVersion` | `PromptVersion?` | `null` | The version in production (two-way); null follows `OpenVersion`. Promoting updates it at once and raises `Promoted`. |
| `Draft` | `PromptTemplate` | `PromptTemplate { System = , User =  }` | The template being edited, the draft (two-way); starts as the open version's. |
| `ActivePart` | `PromptPart` | `System` | The part of the template that is shown (two-way). |
| `SelectedTestCase` | `PromptTestCase?` | `null` | The selected test case (two-way); choosing one resets the values to its own. |
| `SelectedModel` | `AiModel?` | `null` | The selected model (two-way); choosing one sets `Effort` to its default. |
| `Effort` | `ModelEffort` | `Medium` | The effort (two-way). |
| `RunHandler` | `PromptRunHandler?` | `null` | Runs the prompt; null uses the built-in simulator. |
| `TokenEstimator` | `Func<string, int>?` | `null` | Estimates the tokens of a text; null uses about a quarter of the characters. |
| `Now` | `DateTimeOffset?` | `null` | The moment relative times ("last week") are measured from; null uses now. |
| `IsCompareMode` | `bool` | `false` | Whether the editor shows the word diff against `CompareVersion` (two-way); Escape leaves it. |
| `CompareVersion` | `PromptVersion?` | `null` | The version the open one is compared with (two-way). |
| `RunState` | `PromptRunState` | – | *Read-only.* Where the run is (read-only). |
| `LastResult` | `PromptRunResult?` | – | *Read-only.* What the last finished run produced (read-only). |
| `RunCommand` | `ICommand` | – | *Read-only.* Run the prompt (read-only command for toolbars). |
| `StopCommand` | `ICommand` | – | *Read-only.* Stop the run (read-only command for toolbars). |
| `Labels` | `PromptStudioLabels` | – | Every word the block shows or announces. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `TemplateChanged` | `PromptTemplateChangedEventArgs` | Raised after every edit of the template; save it here. |
| `RunStarted` | `PromptRunStartedEventArgs` | Raised when a run starts. |
| `RunCompleted` | `PromptRunCompletedEventArgs` | Raised when a run ends: done, stopped or failed. |
| `RunFailed` | `PromptRunFailedEventArgs` | Raised when the handler throws; change `Message` to word the error. |
| `Promoted` | `PromptPromotedEventArgs` | Raised when a version is promoted to production or a promotion is undone; set `Cancel` to roll it back. |
| `VariableAdded` | `PromptVariableAddedEventArgs` | Raised after a variable is added from the editor. |

Pseudo-classes: `:compact`, `:narrow`, `:two-col`, `:one-col`, `:compare`, `:busy`, `:thinking`, `:streaming`, `:done`, `:stopped`, `:failed`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

### PromptVersion

One saved version of the prompt.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Id` | `string` | `""` | Stable id. |
| `Label` | `string` | `""` | The short name ("v4"). |
| `Message` | `string?` | `null` | The commit message. |
| `Author` | `PromptAuthor?` | `null` | Who wrote it. |
| `CreatedAt` | `DateTimeOffset` | `01/01/0001 00:00:00 +00:00` | When it was written. |
| `System` | `string` | `""` | The system message of this version. |
| `User` | `string` | `""` | The user message of this version. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### PromptAuthor

Who wrote a version.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Name` | `string` | `""` | The name. |
| `Avatar` | `IImage?` | `null` | The picture; without one the avatar shows the initials. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### PromptTestCase

A saved test case: a label and a value for each variable.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Id` | `string` | `""` | Stable id. |
| `Label` | `string` | `""` | A short label; all cases share one segmented control. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### Events

| Event | Raised when | Arguments |
|---|---|---|
| `TemplateChanged` | The template was edited | `Template` |
| `RunStarted` | A run starts | `Request` |
| `RunCompleted` | A run ends: done, stopped or failed | `State`, `Result` |
| `RunFailed` | The handler threw; change `Message` to word the error | `Exception`, `Message` |
| `Promoted` | A version was promoted or a promotion undone; set `Cancel` to roll it back | `Version`, `Previous`, `IsUndo` |
| `VariableAdded` | A variable was added from the editor | |

### Running

| Type | Description |
|---|---|
| `PromptRunHandler` | `(request, cancellationToken)` returns the reply as `IAsyncEnumerable<string>` |
| `PromptRunRequest` | The raw and rendered templates, the values, the model, the effort, the test case id and the version id |
| `PromptRunResult` | The text, the elapsed time, the estimated tokens, the cost and whether it was simulated |
| `PromptTemplate` | The system and the user message |

## Accessibility

- The card is a region named after the prompt. The tabs are a tab list; the variable fields, test cases and output panel are named groups.
- The editor is a text box for assistive technology: a chip reads as its name with the braces, and the list of variables announces how many names match.
- The version and model pills are buttons that report they open a dialog; versions are radio items; the Production version is named as such.
- A polite live region announces that a run started, that the reply is ready, that it was stopped or failed with the reason, that a variable was added, that a version was promoted or a promotion undone, that a comparison opened, and that the reply was copied.
  The streamed words are not announced one by one.
- Status never relies on color alone: dashed chips are also in the missing list, errors have an icon and a sentence, Production has a word.
- Reduced motion keeps every state and announcement.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Ctrl+Enter` / `Cmd+Enter` | Runs the prompt, from anywhere in the card |
| `Tab` | The pills, the tabs, the editor, the variable fields, the test cases, Run, Copy |
| `ArrowLeft` / `ArrowRight` on tabs and test cases | Moves and selects |
| Two opening braces in the editor | Opens the list of variables |
| `ArrowUp` / `ArrowDown` in a list | Moves; wraps around |
| `Enter` or `Tab` in the list | Inserts the variable |
| `Backspace` / `Delete` next to a chip | Removes it whole |
| `Ctrl+Z`, `Ctrl+Shift+Z` | Undo and redo, chips included |
| `Escape` | Closes a list or menu; in the compare view, goes back to editing |

## Motion

- The version and model pills take the width they need on a spring and crossfade their labels; the tabs' highlight and the test cases' highlight glide on a quick spring.
- The Production marker slides between rows of the version menu; menus grow from their pill.
- The output panel follows its content on a spring and keeps its old height while a re-run starts; the reply appears in whole words, each step fading in over 150 ms.
- A chip flashes when its field is edited; the token count rolls its digits.
- Reduced motion drops springs and travel and keeps the cadence of the words without fading; Off applies every change at once.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pill labels and widths | Crossfade, width spring | 120 ms crossfade | Immediate |
| Reply words | Whole words, 150 ms fade | Same steps, no fade | Same steps, no fade |
| Output panel height | Spring, held on re-run | Immediate | Immediate |
| Chip flash | Short pulse | None | None |

## Related

- `AiSidePanel` for an assistant beside a page.
- `ModelPicker` for choosing a model on its own.
- `TokenTextEditor` for the editor of tokens the template editor builds on.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `AiSidePanel` | The thing being edited is a page of content |
| `ModelPicker` | Only the model choice is needed |
| `TokenTextEditor` | You need your own tokens in a text editor |

# Document extraction

> Turns a document into typed data and shows where each value came from: a quiet document viewer beside an editable form whose fields fill in as the model reads, with tinted source text, curved links, low-confidence review and a typed JSON result.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc.Blocks`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc.Blocks --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/blocks/document-extraction

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.DocumentExtractionPreviewDemo">
    <!-- Press Extract: the fields fill in as the model reads, and pointing at a field or at its text links the two. Switch to the email from the file menu. -->
    <arc:DocumentExtraction x:Name="Extraction" MaxWidth="1080" Margin="0,12" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class DocumentExtractionPreviewDemo : UserControl
{
    public DocumentExtractionPreviewDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Extraction.Samples.AddRange(DocumentExtractionDemoData.Samples());
        Extraction.SelectedSample = Extraction.Samples[0];
        Extraction.Model = DocumentExtractionDemoData.Model();

        // The model's answers come from your extractor; this one plays scripted events.
        Extraction.Extractor = DocumentExtractionDemoData.Extractor();

        // Accepting hands you the typed output; save it here (throw to refuse).
        Extraction.Accepting += (_, e) => e.Defer(Task.Delay(550));
    }
}
```

## When to use

Document extraction is for the moment a person has to trust what a model read from a document. The reviewer sees the document and the extracted data side by side, can see exactly where each value came from, and decides what to correct before the data goes on.

- **Invoices, receipts and orders into a system of record**: the fields fill in as the model reads, and the table of line items grows row by row.
- **Email and message triage**: the same viewer reads an email and pulls out the order, the carrier and the dates.
- **Reviewing the model's doubt**: values below a confidence threshold carry the model's reason and a "Looks right" button, and a Review button jumps to the next one.
- **Handing typed data to your code**: dates arrive as ISO text, amounts as numbers, IBANs without spaces, and a value that does not fit its type is null and blocks "Accept all".

## When not to use

- **A conversation about a document**: use `AiChat` or `AiAnswer`.
- **Reading very long documents**: the viewer shows one page at a time and the form is meant for a few dozen fields.
- **Training or scoring a model on many documents**: this is a person reviewing one document.
- **Showing a file**: the viewer draws the document model you give it, not a PDF file.

## Usage

`DocumentExtraction` derives from Avalonia's `TemplatedControl` and is driven by data. Give it `Samples` (a document with its schema each), a `Model` for the footer and an `Extractor` that calls your model.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:DocumentExtraction x:Name="Extraction" MaxWidth="1080" />
</UserControl>
```

```csharp
extraction.Samples.Add(new ExtractionSample { Document = invoice, Schema = invoiceSchema });
extraction.SelectedSample = extraction.Samples[0];
extraction.Model = new ExtractionModelInfo { Name = "My model", Id = "my-model", InputPricePerMillion = 0.12m, OutputPricePerMillion = 0.60m };
extraction.Extractor = new MyExtractor();
extraction.Accepting += (_, e) => e.Defer(SaveAsync(e.Output.ToJson()));

public sealed class MyExtractor : IDocumentExtractor
{
    public async IAsyncEnumerable<ExtractionEvent> ExtractAsync(
        ExtractionDocument document, ExtractionSchema schema, [EnumeratorCancellation] CancellationToken cancellationToken)
    {
        // Send document.ToPlainText() and schema.ToJsonSchema() to your model, then report what comes back.
        await foreach (var found in model.ReadAsync(document.ToPlainText(), schema.ToJsonSchema(), cancellationToken))
        {
            yield return new ExtractionValueEvent(found.Path, found.Value, found.SourceId, found.Confidence, found.Note);
        }
    }
}
```

### The document

An `ExtractionDocument` is a name and a list of blocks drawn on a sheet of white paper (an email is drawn as a mail page): a masthead, a heading, paragraphs, address lines, key and value pairs, a band of labelled cells, columns, a table, totals, a rule and a footer. Text is made of runs and `DocumentSpan`s: a span is a piece of text a value can point back to, with an id that the extractor cites as `SourceId`.

### The schema

An `ExtractionSchema` lists the fields to find: a key, a label and a type (`Text`, `Date`, `Money`, `Currency`, `Iban`, `Integer`, `Number`). A table field has columns, and its values are reported by the path `key.row.column`. Fields belong to groups; each group takes one of the four series colors in turn, and the same color tints the dot, the field rows, the cited text and the links. Without groups each field gets a color of its own.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.DocumentExtractionCustomDemo">
    <!-- Your own schema: three fields and no groups, so each field gets its own color. -->
    <arc:DocumentExtraction x:Name="Extraction" MaxWidth="1080" Margin="0,12" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class DocumentExtractionCustomDemo : UserControl
{
    public DocumentExtractionCustomDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        var schema = new ExtractionSchema { Name = "parcel", Title = "Parcel" };
        schema.Fields.Add(new ExtractionField { Key = "carrier", Label = "Carrier", Type = ExtractionFieldType.Text });
        schema.Fields.Add(new ExtractionField { Key = "trackingNumber", Label = "Tracking no.", Type = ExtractionFieldType.Text });
        schema.Fields.Add(new ExtractionField { Key = "estimatedDelivery", Label = "Estimated delivery", Type = ExtractionFieldType.Date });

        Extraction.Document = DocumentExtractionDemoData.Email();
        Extraction.Schema = schema;
        Extraction.Model = DocumentExtractionDemoData.Model();
        Extraction.Extractor = new DocumentExtractionDemoData.SampleExtractor();
    }
}
```

### A run

Extract reads the document: the status line shimmers "Reading the document", a sweep crosses the page, and then values land one by one. Each landed value fills its field, tints the text it came from, and raises a bar in the footer. The viewer follows the values until you scroll by hand. The button turns into Stop; stopping keeps the values found so far. A failed run keeps them too and offers Retry. Extract again starts over.

- **Events**: the extractor yields `ExtractionValueEvent` for each value (the text as the document writes it, such as "1,400.00"; dates as `YYYY-MM-DD`), `ExtractionUsageEvent` with token totals for the cost, and `ExtractionErrorEvent` or an exception to fail. Cancel through the token.
- **Cost and time**: the footer shows the model, the cost from the token totals and the prices, and the elapsed time.

### Reviewing

- **Linking**: hovering or focusing a field lights its text on the page and draws a curved link; pointing at text on the page lights its field, and clicking it focuses the field. In a narrow container the panes stack and no links are drawn.
- **Low confidence**: a value below `ReviewThreshold` (0.8) shows a warning, the model's reason and "Looks right". Review in the status line jumps to the first one.
- **Editing**: every field is a real input. Editing marks the value "Edited", clears its low-confidence mark and updates the JSON tab, where the edited line flashes. A value that does not fit its type shows a message, is null in the output and blocks Accept all.
- **Tabs**: Fields, JSON (the typed output, linked to the fields) and Schema (the JSON schema that is sent to the model).

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.DocumentExtractionNarrowDemo">
    <!-- In a narrow container the document sits above the form and the links are not drawn. -->
    <arc:DocumentExtraction x:Name="Extraction" Width="420" HorizontalAlignment="Left" Margin="0,12" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class DocumentExtractionNarrowDemo : UserControl
{
    public DocumentExtractionNarrowDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Extraction.Samples.AddRange(DocumentExtractionDemoData.Samples());
        Extraction.SelectedSample = Extraction.Samples[0];
        Extraction.Model = DocumentExtractionDemoData.Model();
        Extraction.Extractor = DocumentExtractionDemoData.Extractor();
    }
}
```

### Accepting

Accept all raises `Accepting` with the typed output. Take a deferral with `e.Defer(task)` to save asynchronously; set `Cancel` or fault the task to undo the accept. After a successful save every field shows as accepted. Editing a value afterwards returns only that value to unaccepted.

### Zoom

The viewer zooms from 40% to 200% in steps, with Ctrl or Cmd and the plus, minus and 0 keys. Fit keeps the page the width of the pane. Zoom, `IsFitWidth` and the tab are two-way properties.

### Wording

Every word comes from `Labels` (`DocumentExtractionLabels`): replace the instance to translate or reword; formatted texts are functions.

### Content guidelines

- **Field labels**: short nouns ("Invoice no.").
- **Descriptions**: say what to look for; they go to the model in the JSON schema.
- **Reasons**: the extractor's note should say why it is unsure, in one sentence.

### Best practices

- Cite a `SourceId` for every value that has a place in the document, so the text is tinted and linkable.
- Report real confidence; the review flow depends on it.
- Pass the cancellation token on so Stop and a new run really stop the model.
- Save in `Accepting` and throw when saving fails.

### Common questions

**Why is there no link line?** Links are drawn only in the side-by-side layout, and only when both ends are visible.

**Why is a value null in the JSON?** Its text does not fit its type, for example a date that is not `YYYY-MM-DD`.

**What does the average confidence count?** Every value the model found, table cells included.

## API reference

### DocumentExtraction

Turns a document into typed data and shows where each value came from. A quiet viewer of the document sits on the left and an editable form on the right; while a model reads, the fields fill in one by one and the text each value came from is tinted. Pointing at a field or at its text lights both and draws a curved link between them; values the model is unsure of carry its reason and a "Looks right" button; "Accept all" hands the typed result to the app.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Document` | `ExtractionDocument?` | `null` | The document to read; when null the selected sample's document is used. |
| `Schema` | `ExtractionSchema?` | `null` | What to extract; when null the selected sample's schema is used. |
| `SelectedSample` | `ExtractionSample?` | `null` | The sample chosen on the file menu (two-way); choosing one clears the values. |
| `Extractor` | `IDocumentExtractor?` | `null` | Reads the document with a model; null disables Extract. |
| `Model` | `ExtractionModelInfo?` | `null` | The model's name and prices, for the footer and the cost. |
| `ModelMark` | `object?` | `null` | The mark shown before the model's name in the footer (a geometry in a 24 × 24 box or an image). |
| `ReviewThreshold` | `double` | `0.8` | Values below this confidence are marked for a check (0.8). |
| `SelectedPath` | `string?` | `null` | The path of the field the document and the form are linked on (two-way); Escape clears it. |
| `SelectedTab` | `ExtractionTab` | `Fields` | The tab of the form pane (two-way). |
| `Zoom` | `double` | `1` | The zoom of the page, 0.4 to 2 (two-way); while `IsFitWidth` it follows the canvas width. |
| `IsFitWidth` | `bool` | `true` | Whether the page is fitted to the canvas width (two-way); zooming by hand turns it off. |
| `ZoomSteps` | `IReadOnlyList<double>` | – | The zoom steps of the buttons and the keys. |
| `ExtractCommand` | `ICommand?` | `null` | Run by Extract and Retry. |
| `Labels` | `DocumentExtractionLabels` | – | Every word the block shows or announces. |
| `State` | `ExtractionState` | – | *Read-only.* Where the extraction is (read-only). |
| `ErrorMessage` | `string?` | – | *Read-only.* What went wrong when the run failed (read-only). |
| `FoundCount` | `int` | – | *Read-only.* How many fields have a value (read-only; a table counts its cells). |
| `FieldCount` | `int` | – | *Read-only.* How many values there are to find (read-only): every scalar field and every table cell so far; an empty table counts as one. |
| `CheckCount` | `int` | – | *Read-only.* How many values need a check (read-only). |
| `AverageConfidence` | `double` | – | *Read-only.* The mean confidence of every value, table cells included (read-only). |
| `Cost` | `decimal` | – | *Read-only.* The cost of the run so far, in dollars (read-only). |
| `Elapsed` | `TimeSpan` | – | *Read-only.* The time of the run (read-only). |
| `Output` | `ExtractionOutput` | – | *Read-only.* The typed output as it is now (read-only). |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ExtractionStarted` | `RoutedEventArgs` | Raised when a run starts. |
| `ExtractionCompleted` | `ExtractionCompletedEventArgs` | Raised when a run ends: done, stopped or failed. |
| `ValueChanged` | `ExtractionValueChangedEventArgs` | Raised when a value changes, by the model or by the person. |
| `ValueChecked` | `ExtractionPathEventArgs` | Raised when the person marks a low-confidence value "Looks right". |
| `Accepting` | `ExtractionAcceptingEventArgs` | Raised by Accept all so the app can save the output; throw or set `Cancel` to undo it. |
| `Accepted` | `RoutedEventArgs` | Raised after the accept was saved. |
| `SelectedPathChanged` | `ExtractionPathEventArgs` | Raised when the linked field changes. |

Pseudo-classes: `:stacked`, `:footer-wrap`, `:narrow`, `:running`, `:accepted`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

### ExtractionDocument

A document to read: a name and the blocks to draw.

### ExtractionSchema

What to extract from a document.

### ExtractionValue

One value of the form: what the document says, how sure the model was and where the person has taken it.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Text` | `string` | – | The text. |
| `SourceId` | `string?` | – | The id of the cited span. |
| `Confidence` | `double` | – | The confidence, 0 to 1. |
| `Note` | `string?` | – | The model's note. |
| `Status` | `ExtractionValueStatus` | – | The review status. |
| `Error` | `string?` | – | Why the text does not fit the type; null when it does. |
| `TypedValue` | `object?` | – | The parsed value (date, number, text); null when invalid. |
| `NeedsCheck` | `bool` | – | Whether the value is below the review threshold and not yet checked or edited. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### Events

| Event | Raised when | Arguments |
|---|---|---|
| `ExtractionStarted` | A run starts | |
| `ExtractionCompleted` | A run ends: done, stopped or failed | `Result`, `Error` |
| `ValueChanged` | A value changes by the model or the person | `Path`, `OldText`, `NewText`, `Origin` |
| `ValueChecked` | The person marks a value "Looks right" | `Path` |
| `Accepting` | Accept all needs the output saved; set `Cancel` or fault a deferral to undo | `Output`, `Values`, `Cancel`, `Defer` |
| `Accepted` | The accept was saved | |
| `SelectedPathChanged` | The linked field changes | `Path` |

### Streaming and output

| Type | Description |
|---|---|
| `IDocumentExtractor` | `ExtractAsync(document, schema, cancellationToken)` returns the events of one run |
| `ExtractionValueEvent` | A value: the path, the text, the source span id, the confidence and a note |
| `ExtractionUsageEvent` | The token totals so far |
| `ExtractionErrorEvent` | The model could not finish |
| `ExtractionOutput` | The typed result in schema order; `ToJson()` writes it |
| `ExtractionModelInfo` | The model's name, id and prices per million tokens |

## Accessibility

- The viewer is a region named after the file and the zoom, the page is an article, and the form's inputs are real, named text boxes; a table's cells are named by column and row.
- Confidence is spoken in words ("Low confidence, 64 percent, check this value"), and status is never color alone: warnings, checks and edits have icons and words.
- Invalid values are marked invalid and described by their message; low-confidence values are described by the model's reason.
- Two polite live regions announce the run (started, how many were found and how many need a check, stopped, failed) and the review (checked, accepted, a value to fix first). A failed run is announced assertively.
- Reduced motion keeps every state and announcement.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Tab` | The file button, the zoom buttons, the page, the tabs, the action button, the fields in order (a low-confidence field is followed by its Looks right button), Accept all |
| Focusing a field | Selects it: the page scrolls to its text and the link is drawn |
| `Escape` | Stops a run; otherwise clears the selected field |
| `Ctrl` or `Cmd` with `+`, `-`, `0` on the page | Zoom in, zoom out, fit to width |
| `ArrowUp` / `ArrowDown` on the page | Scrolls it |
| `ArrowLeft` / `ArrowRight` on the tabs | Moves and selects |
| `Enter` / `Space` | Activates a button, or chooses a document in the menu |

## Motion

- Values land with a short fade of the text and the confidence column; the cited text flashes a darker tint and settles; footer bars rise on a spring, and the average and the cost roll.
- Table rows open on a spring; the model's reason opens and closes on a spring; the status line changes with a crossfade and its height follows.
- Links draw themselves in a fifth of a second with a gloss that passes once; switching links crosses over.
- The page zooms on a spring about its center, and the sweep crosses the page once at the start of a run.
- Accept all marks the fields one after the other, 35 ms apart.
- Reduced motion drops the sweep, the link drawing, springs and the staggers, and keeps the crossfades; Off applies every change at once.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| Links | Draw and gloss | Appear and disappear | Appear and disappear |
| Landing values | Fade and flash | Fade | Immediate |
| Zoom, rows, bars | Springs | Immediate | Immediate |
| Accept all | Staggered 35 ms | All at once, with crossfade | Immediate |

## Related

- `ModelArena` for judging two models by their answers.
- `PromptStudio` for editing the prompt behind an extraction.
- `AiAnswer` for an answer that cites its sources.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `ModelArena` | You compare models, not read a document |
| `PromptStudio` | You maintain the prompt |
| `AiAnswer` | The result is prose with citations |

# Model arena

> A blind test of two models: one prompt goes to two anonymous models, both answers stream in at the same pace, and the models are revealed after the vote, with time to first token, speed and cost per answer and a standings list.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc.Blocks`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc.Blocks --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/blocks/model-arena

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ModelArenaPreviewDemo">
    <!-- Two hidden models answer the same prompt at the same pace; vote to reveal them. Press Run or pick a sample prompt. -->
    <arc:ModelArena x:Name="Arena" AutoStart="True" MaxWidth="800" Margin="0,12" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class ModelArenaPreviewDemo : UserControl
{
    public ModelArenaPreviewDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Arena.Contestants.AddRange(ModelArenaDemoData.Models());
        Arena.Prompts.AddRange(ModelArenaDemoData.Prompts());
        ModelArenaDemoData.SeedStandings(Arena);

        // Answers come from your runner; this one plays scripted text.
        Arena.Runner = new ModelArenaDemoData.Runner();
    }
}
```

## When to use

The model arena answers "which of these two is better for us?" with the person's own judgment instead of a benchmark. Both answers appear side by side at the same pace, so speed cannot sway the vote, and the models stay hidden until the vote is in.

- **Choosing a provider or a model version**: run the questions your product really asks and let the team vote.
- **Reviewing a prompt or a model change**: the same prompt, two candidates, a vote and the cost of each answer next to it.
- **Showing latency and price side by side**: each answer reports its time to first token, speed and cost, measured on the real stream.
- **A shared standings list**: wins, ties and losses build up as people vote; save and restore them through `Standings`.

## When not to use

- **A conversation with one assistant**: use `AiChat`.
- **Scoring hundreds of prompts automatically**: the arena is one round at a time, judged by a person.
- **Picking a default model**: use `ModelPicker`.
- **Comparing two versions of a prompt**: use `PromptStudio`, which compares them as a word diff.

## Usage

`ModelArena` derives from Avalonia's `TemplatedControl` and is driven by data: give it the `Contestants`, the sample `Prompts` and a `Runner` that streams one model's answer.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:ModelArena x:Name="Arena" MaxWidth="800" />
</UserControl>
```

```csharp
arena.Contestants.AddRange(models);
arena.Prompts.AddRange(samplePrompts);
arena.Runner = new MyArenaRunner();

public sealed class MyArenaRunner : IArenaRunner
{
    public async IAsyncEnumerable<ArenaStreamEvent> RunAsync(
        AiModel model, string prompt, [EnumeratorCancellation] CancellationToken cancellationToken)
    {
        await foreach (var piece in provider.StreamAsync(model.Id, prompt, cancellationToken))
        {
            yield return new ArenaStreamEvent(piece.Text, piece.InputTokens, piece.OutputTokens);
        }
    }
}
```

### A round

Run (Enter in the box, or Ctrl+Enter, Cmd+Enter on a Mac) sends the prompt to a pair of models picked from `Contestants`. Each answer shows "Thinking" until its first text arrives, then "Writing"; the one that completes first says "Finished first". When both are in, the vote row opens: "A is better", "Tie", "B is better" or "Both bad". The vote reveals the models, adds to the standings and offers "Next round", which picks a new pair, moves to the next sample prompt and runs it.

- **The same pace for both**: the real streams may run at very different speeds, but the text is shown on one shared clock in whole words, so what you see does not depend on which model is faster. The speed and cost figures are measured on the raw stream.
- **Blind**: until the vote, no model name or mark is in the card, its tooltips or its accessible names. The Blind switch can be turned off to see the models at once; votes still count.
- **Stop**: Run turns into Stop while a round runs, and Escape in the prompt row stops it. A pane that had not finished says "Stopped"; one that had finished keeps its answer.
- **Failure**: when a stream fails, that pane keeps what it received and shows an error card with "Retry model A". Retrying runs only that model. Throw `ArenaRunException` with `isRetryable: false` for an error that retrying cannot fix; the card then offers a sample prompt instead.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ModelArenaProgrammaticDemo">
    <!-- Start rounds from code, make the next stream fail, and read each vote. -->
    <StackPanel Spacing="12" Margin="0,12" MaxWidth="800">
        <StackPanel Orientation="Horizontal" Spacing="8">
            <Button x:Name="RunButton" Content="Run round" />
            <Button x:Name="NextButton" Content="Next round" />
            <CheckBox x:Name="BreakBox" Content="Break the next stream" VerticalAlignment="Center" />
        </StackPanel>
        <arc:ModelArena x:Name="Arena" />
        <TextBlock x:Name="LastVote" Classes="muted" Text="No votes yet." />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class ModelArenaProgrammaticDemo : UserControl
{
    public ModelArenaProgrammaticDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        var runner = new ModelArenaDemoData.Runner();
        Arena.Contestants.AddRange(ModelArenaDemoData.Models());
        Arena.Prompts.AddRange(ModelArenaDemoData.Prompts());
        Arena.Runner = runner;

        RunButton.Click += async (_, _) => await Arena.RunAsync();
        NextButton.Click += (_, _) => Arena.NextRound();
        BreakBox.IsCheckedChanged += (_, _) => runner.BreakNext = BreakBox.IsChecked == true;

        // VoteCast comes once per vote with both models and what each answer cost.
        Arena.VoteCast += (_, e) =>
        {
            var vote = e.Vote;
            LastVote.Text = $"Round {vote.Round}: {vote.Choice}, {vote.ModelA.Name} ${vote.MetricsA.CostUsd:0.0000} vs {vote.ModelB.Name} ${vote.MetricsB.CostUsd:0.0000}";
        };
    }
}
```

### Metrics

Each pane shows the time to first token (counting up while it waits), the speed in tokens per second and the cost. If the runner reports token counts in `ArenaStreamEvent` they are used; otherwise tokens are estimated at four characters each. The cost multiplies the tokens by the model's `InputPrice` and `OutputPrice` per million tokens, and is zero for a model with no price.

### Standings

The trophy button opens the standings: the models with a record, ranked by win rate (a tie counts as half a win), the top `LeaderboardSize` of them. After a vote the button shows a dot, and the first open afterwards shows the rows moving from their old places to the new ones. `Standings` is a dictionary of `ArenaRecord` by model id: fill it before the first vote to start from saved results, and save it on `VoteCast`.

### Narrow containers

Below 560 wide the two answers become two tabs (each shows the name and the status); below 480 the trophy button keeps only its icon, the keyboard hint hides and the vote buttons form a two-by-two grid. The widths are the card's own, not the window's.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ModelArenaNarrowDemo">
    <!-- In a narrow container the two answers become tabs, and below 480 the layout is compact. -->
    <arc:ModelArena x:Name="Arena" AutoStart="True" Width="400" HorizontalAlignment="Left" Margin="0,12" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class ModelArenaNarrowDemo : UserControl
{
    public ModelArenaNarrowDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Arena.Contestants.AddRange(ModelArenaDemoData.Models());
        Arena.Prompts.AddRange(ModelArenaDemoData.Prompts());
        Arena.Runner = new ModelArenaDemoData.Runner();
    }
}
```

### Wording

Every word comes from `Labels` (`ModelArenaLabels`): replace the instance to translate or reword; formatted texts are functions.

### Content guidelines

- **Sample prompts**: a short chip label and a full prompt that makes the models differ.
- **Model names**: the name and a short name for the tabs.
- **Prices**: say when they are examples.

### Best practices

- Pass the cancellation token on in your runner, so Stop and a new round really stop the stream.
- Report token counts when your provider gives them; estimates are only a fallback.
- Keep the pair random but not repeated: the default picker avoids the last pair, or set `PairPicker`.
- Save `Standings` when `VoteCast` fires.

### Common questions

**Why do both answers appear at the same speed?** The text is released by one shared clock; the speed shown under each answer is the real one.

**Why does the card say nothing about the models before I vote?** That is the blind test; turn off Blind to see them.

**Can I run it without a runner?** No: with no `Runner` Run is disabled.

## API reference

### ModelArena

A blind test of two models: one prompt goes to two anonymous models, both answers stream in at the same pace, and only after the person votes are the models revealed. Each answer shows how fast it started, how fast it came and what it cost, and a small standings list ranks the models by win rate.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `PromptText` | `string` | `""` | The prompt in the box (two-way). The first time `Prompts` has an item the box shows its text. |
| `Runner` | `IArenaRunner?` | `null` | Streams the models' answers; null cannot run (the Gallery supplies a scripted runner). |
| `IsBlind` | `bool` | `true` | Whether the models are hidden until the vote (two-way). Turning it off shows them at once and turning it on hides them again. |
| `AutoStart` | `bool` | `false` | Whether the first round starts by itself when the arena is shown. |
| `LeaderboardSize` | `int` | `5` | The most rows the standings show. |
| `IsLeaderboardOpen` | `bool` | `false` | Whether the standings popover is open (two-way). |
| `PairPicker` | `IArenaPairPicker?` | `null` | Chooses the pair of each round; null picks two random models and avoids repeating the last pair. |
| `Pacing` | `ArenaPacing` | `ArenaPacing { Interval = 00:00:00.0340000, WordsPerSecond = 95, MaxWordsPerStep = 8 }` | How the two answers are paced when shown. |
| `VoteCommand` | `ICommand?` | `null` | Run when a vote is cast, with the `ArenaVote` as the parameter. |
| `Labels` | `ModelArenaLabels` | – | Every word the block shows or announces. |
| `Round` | `int` | – | *Read-only.* The number of the current round; it grows with every run (read-only). |
| `Phase` | `ArenaPhase` | – | *Read-only.* Where the round is (read-only). |
| `PaneA` | `ArenaPaneState` | – | *Read-only.* The first answer (read-only). |
| `PaneB` | `ArenaPaneState` | – | *Read-only.* The second answer (read-only). |
| `LastVote` | `ArenaVote?` | – | *Read-only.* The last vote of this round, or null (read-only). |
| `HasUnseenResult` | `bool` | – | *Read-only.* Whether a vote was cast that the person has not yet seen in the standings (read-only). |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `VoteCast` | `ArenaVoteEventArgs` | Raised once for each vote. |
| `RoundStarted` | `ArenaRoundEventArgs` | Raised when a round starts (every run starts a round). |
| `RunStopped` | `ArenaRoundEventArgs` | Raised when a run is stopped before both answers finish. |
| `PaneFailed` | `ArenaPaneFailedEventArgs` | Raised when one answer fails. |
| `LeaderboardReset` | `RoutedEventArgs` | Raised when the standings are reset. |

Pseudo-classes: `:narrow`, `:compact`, `:running`, `:voting`, `:voted`, `:blind`, `:unseen`, `:leaderboard-open`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

### ArenaPrompt

A sample prompt: a chip that fills the box and runs.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Id` | `string` | `""` | The prompt's id. |
| `Label` | `string` | `""` | The chip's text. |
| `Text` | `string` | `""` | The whole prompt sent to both models. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### ArenaPaneState

What one of the arena's two answers shows. The arena owns and updates it; read it to follow a round. Before the vote `Model` is set but nothing the person sees carries its name (see `IsBlind`).

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Slot` | `ArenaSlot` | – | *Read-only.* The slot. |
| `Model` | `AiModel?` | – | *Read-only.* The model that answers in this slot in the current round; null before the first round. |
| `Status` | `ArenaPaneStatus` | – | *Read-only.* Where the answer is. |
| `Metrics` | `ArenaMetrics` | – | *Read-only.* What the answer cost and how fast it came so far. |
| `ErrorTitle` | `string?` | – | *Read-only.* The error card's title; null when the answer did not fail. |
| `ErrorText` | `string?` | – | *Read-only.* The error card's text; null when the answer did not fail. |
| `IsRetryable` | `bool` | – | *Read-only.* Whether a failed answer can be retried. |
| `Text` | `string` | – | *Read-only.* The text shown so far (what the pacer has released), as Markdown. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### Events

| Event | Raised when | Arguments |
|---|---|---|
| `VoteCast` | The person votes | `Vote` |
| `RoundStarted` | A round starts | `Round`, `Prompt`, `ModelA`, `ModelB` |
| `RunStopped` | A run is stopped before both answers finish | `Round`, `Prompt`, `ModelA`, `ModelB` |
| `PaneFailed` | One answer fails | `Slot`, `Model`, `Error` |
| `LeaderboardReset` | The standings are reset | |

### Streaming

| Type | Description |
|---|---|
| `IArenaRunner` | `RunAsync(model, prompt, cancellationToken)` returns one model's answer as `IAsyncEnumerable<ArenaStreamEvent>` |
| `ArenaStreamEvent` | Some text, the input tokens, the output tokens, or all three; a string converts to one |
| `ArenaRunException` | A failure the runner can describe: the message, an optional title and whether it can be retried |
| `IArenaPairPicker` | Chooses the two models of a round |
| `ArenaVote` | The round, the prompt, both models, the choice, the winner and both answers' metrics |
| `ArenaMetrics` | Time to first token, tokens per second, total time, tokens, cost and whether the tokens were estimated |
| `ArenaRecord` | Wins, ties and losses; `WinRate` counts a tie as half |

## Accessibility

- Each answer is a region named "Model A" or "Model B" (with the model's name after the vote), with its answer area as a focusable, named, scrollable area and its metrics as a named group.
- Before the vote no model name exists anywhere in the accessible tree.
- Status is a word and an icon, never color alone. The tabs are a tab list with selection following focus.
- A polite live region announces that a round started, which answer finished first, that voting is open, the result with both models' names and that the standings changed, a stop, a failure and a reset. The streamed text is not announced word by word.
- The trophy button says "Standings, updated" when there is a result not yet seen.
- Reduced motion keeps every state and announcement.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Enter` in the prompt box | Runs the box's text |
| `Ctrl+Enter` / `Cmd+Enter` | Runs the box's text, also on Run or a chip |
| `Escape` in the prompt row | Stops the run |
| `Tab` | The trophy, Blind, the box, Run, the chips, each answer, the vote buttons |
| `Enter` / `Space` on a vote button | Votes; focus moves to Next round |
| `ArrowLeft` / `ArrowRight` on the tabs | Moves and selects, wrapping around; `Home` and `End` go to the ends |
| `ArrowUp`, `PageUp`, `Home` in an answer | Scrolls up and stops following the stream |
| `Escape` in the standings | Closes them; focus returns to the trophy |

## Motion

- Status words and names swap with a short crossfade and the slot's width follows on a quick spring; the spinner turns once a second and the status text shimmers while a model works.
- New text fades in a few words at a time and the answer follows the end of the text until the person scrolls up.
- The vote row crossfades between its states and its height follows on a spring; the models are revealed with the same crossfade.
- The speed and cost numbers roll their digits. Opening the standings after a vote replays the move: rows slide to their new places and the bars grow or shrink.
- Reduced motion drops springs and travel and keeps the cadence of the words without fading; Off applies every change at once.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| Status, names, vote row | Crossfade, width and height springs | 120 ms crossfade | Immediate |
| Answer text | Whole words, 160 ms fade | Same steps, no fade | Same steps, no fade |
| Standings replay | Rows slide, bars scale | Rows and bars change in place | Immediate |
| Following the stream | Eased each frame | Jumps to the end | Jumps to the end |

## Related

- `PromptStudio` for editing a prompt and comparing its versions.
- `ModelPicker` for choosing a model on its own.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `AiChat` | One assistant answers |
| `PromptStudio` | The thing being compared is a prompt |
| `ModelPicker` | Only the model choice is needed |
