# AI composer

> The prompt box of an AI app: a text area that grows, slash commands and @ mentions that become tokens, attachments that upload in place, tool toggles, a model and effort menu, a character counter and a send button that becomes a stop button.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc.Blocks`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc.Blocks --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/blocks/ai-composer

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.AiComposerPreviewDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12" MaxWidth="720" Margin="0,12,0,140">
        <TextBlock x:Name="Reply" MinHeight="40" TextWrapping="Wrap" Opacity="0.85" Text="Send a message to see a simulated reply." />
        <!-- Type / at the start of a line for a command, @ for a file, paste or drop files, press the plus for more. -->
        <arc:AiComposer x:Name="Composer" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class AiComposerPreviewDemo : UserControl
{
    private IDisposable? _reply;

    public AiComposerPreviewDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        AiComposerDemoData.Fill(Composer);
        Composer.Placeholder = AiComposerDemoData.Placeholder;

        // Your code starts the reply; the composer only shows that one is running and lets the person stop it.
        Composer.Sent += (_, e) => _reply = AiComposerDemoData.SimulateReply(Composer, Reply, e.Message);
        Composer.StopRequested += (_, _) => _reply?.Dispose();
    }
}
```

## When to use

The AI composer is the box people write their prompt in. It is one rounded surface with a text area on top and a toolbar under
it, and it takes care of everything between typing and sending: commands, files, tools, the model and the limit.

- **A chat or assistant app**: the box at the bottom of the conversation, with a stop button while a reply is generated.
- **A prompt field in a tool**: "/" commands for the actions of your product, "@" mentions for the files or documents it can read.
- **A form that accepts files with the prompt**: pick, paste or drop files; they upload in place and the message carries only the ones that are ready.
- **A model choice next to the prompt**: the toolbar holds a model pill with an effort setting, so the choice stays where the work happens.

## When not to use

- **A short single-line field**: use `Input`, or `SearchField` for searching.
- **A comment box with @people**: use `MentionInput`, which brings people, channels and serialization.
- **A text editor with your own tokens and your own surface**: build on `TokenTextEditor`, the editor inside the composer.
- **Choosing a model on a settings page**: use `ModelPicker`; the composer's pill is for choosing while writing.
- **Running the model**: the composer only reports the message. Your code calls the model and says when a reply is being generated.

## Usage

`AiComposer` derives from Avalonia's `TemplatedControl`. Give it what the person can use (commands, context items, tools, models)
and handle `Sent`. It clears itself after a send; the message holds the text, the tokens, the ready attachments, the model, the effort
and the state of each tool.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:AiComposer Placeholder="Ask a question, type / for actions or @ for a file">
        <arc:AiComposer.Commands>
            <arc:AiCommand Id="recap" Name="recap" Description="Boil a doc or file down to its main points" />
            <arc:AiCommand Id="rewrite" Name="rewrite" Description="Rewrite in a clearer or friendlier tone" />
        </arc:AiComposer.Commands>
        <arc:AiComposer.ContextItems>
            <arc:AiContextItem Id="style-guide" Label="style-guide.pdf" Hint="Brand, 3.1 MB" Group="Files" />
        </arc:AiComposer.ContextItems>
    </arc:AiComposer>
</UserControl>
```

```csharp
composer.Sent += (_, e) =>
{
    var message = e.Message;               // Text, Tokens, Attachments, Model, Effort, Tools
    StartReply(message);
    composer.IsGenerating = true;          // the send button becomes a stop button
};
composer.StopRequested += (_, _) => CancelReply();
```

### Commands and mentions

"/" at the start of a line opens the list of `Commands` (filtered by the start of the name); "@" at the start of a line or after a space
opens the list of `ContextItems`, grouped by their `Group` in the order of `MentionGroups` ("Files" then "Docs" by default) and
filtered by the label or the hint. A "(" before the "@" does not open it. Up and Down move (and wrap), Enter or Tab inserts, Escape
closes, and the list never takes the focus. An insertion becomes a token followed by a space; `Value.Tokens` lists them with their
offsets. With no commands or no items, the symbol is plain text.

`SetPrompt(text)` fills the box for a suggestion: the commands and mentions it knows become tokens, the caret goes to the end and the
focus to the text. `InsertToken(kind, id, label)` adds one at the caret.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.AiComposerSuggestionsDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12" MaxWidth="720" Margin="0,12,0,140">
        <StackPanel Orientation="Horizontal" Spacing="8" HorizontalAlignment="Center">
            <arc:Button x:Name="First" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Content="Compare the last two sprint reviews" />
            <arc:Button x:Name="Second" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Content="Tidy up the welcome email" />
            <arc:Button x:Name="Third" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Content="Find why big exports stall" />
        </StackPanel>
        <arc:AiComposer x:Name="Composer" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class AiComposerSuggestionsDemo : UserControl
{
    public AiComposerSuggestionsDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        AiComposerDemoData.Fill(Composer, models: false, tools: false);
        Composer.Placeholder = AiComposerDemoData.Placeholder;

        // SetPrompt fills the box, turns the commands and mentions it knows into tokens and focuses the text.
        First.Click += (_, _) => Composer.SetPrompt("/recap @Sprint 15 review and list what slipped since the previous sprint");
        Second.Click += (_, _) => Composer.SetPrompt("/rewrite our tester welcome email so it fits on one screen");
        Third.Click += (_, _) => Composer.SetPrompt("/debug @export-worker.ts large CSV exports stall at the last chunk");
    }
}
```

### Attachments

The plus button opens a menu with "Upload file", your `AttachActions` (a cloud drive, a repository, a screen capture, with a separator
if you ask) and, when there are context items, "Mention a file or doc". Files can also be pasted or dropped on the composer. A paste of
at least `LongPasteCharacters` characters or `LongPasteLines` lines becomes a "Pasted text" attachment instead of text.

Each file becomes a chip that uploads in place: a ring with the percentage while it runs, a check when it finishes, then a remove button. A file over
`MaxFileSize` (30 MB by default) or not matching `AcceptedFileTypes` (the syntax of `FileDropzone.Accept`) gets an error chip with its
reason; it can be removed and does not stop sending. `UploadHandler` does the upload: report progress, honor the token, throw to refuse.
Without a handler a file is ready at once. `IsAttachmentEnabled` turns the plus, pasting and dropping off.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.AiComposerAttachmentsDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12" MaxWidth="720" Margin="0,12,0,140">
        <TextBlock TextWrapping="Wrap" Opacity="0.7"
                   Text="Press the plus, paste or drop files. Only PDF, CSV, text and images are accepted, up to 2 MB; a file whose name contains &#8220;fail&#8221; fails its upload." />
        <arc:AiComposer x:Name="Composer" AcceptedFileTypes=".pdf,.csv,.txt,image/*" MaxFileSize="2097152" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class AiComposerAttachmentsDemo : UserControl
{
    public AiComposerAttachmentsDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Composer.Placeholder = "Attach a file, then ask about it";

        // Upload somewhere: report progress, honor the token (the person cancelled), throw to refuse the file.
        Composer.UploadHandler = async (attachment, progress, cancellation) =>
        {
            for (var step = 1; step <= 10; step++)
            {
                await Task.Delay(180, cancellation);
                progress.Report(step / 10d);
                if (step == 6 && attachment.Name.Contains("fail", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase))
                {
                    throw new InvalidOperationException("Upload refused");
                }
            }
        };
    }
}
```

### Tools, model and effort

Each `AiComposerTool` in `Tools` is a toggle in the toolbar (an icon and a label that hides in a narrow composer); its `IsChecked` is two-way
and `ToolToggled` reports a change. When `Models` is not empty, a pill shows the selected model and its effort; its menu has the models,
a separator and a row of effort levels that apply at once. `SelectedModel` and `Effort` are two-way, `ModelChanged` and `EffortChanged`
report a change, and an effort the model does not offer moves to the nearest level it does.

### The limit

`MaxLength` (4000 by default; null means none) adds a counter: from `CounterThreshold` (80%) it shows how many characters are left, from
`WarningThreshold` (95%) it turns to the warning color, and over the limit it shows how many are over and sending is blocked. The text is
never cut.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.AiComposerLimitDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12" MaxWidth="720" Margin="0,12,0,24">
        <!-- A short limit so the counter shows: it appears from 80 percent, warns from 95 and blocks sending when passed. -->
        <arc:AiComposer x:Name="Composer" MaxLength="120"
                        Text="Summarize the sprint review in three bullet points and name the owner of each open question" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

### Sending and stopping

The send button is empty (nothing to send), ready, blocked (an upload is still running, or the text is over the limit; its name says
which) or generating. Enter sends; Shift+Enter adds a line; Enter does nothing while an input method is composing, while a list is
open, or while a reply is generated (the box stays editable, nothing is queued). While `IsGenerating` is true the button is a stop
square inside a ring that follows `GenerationProgress` and never goes backwards; press it, or Escape, to raise `StopRequested`.
Your code ends a reply by setting `GenerationProgress` to 1 and then `IsGenerating` to false.

`SendCommand` and `StopCommand` do the same for MVVM. `SendState` tells which of the four states the button is in.

### A minimal composer

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.AiComposerMinimalDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12" MaxWidth="560" Margin="0,12,0,24">
        <!-- No models, tools or commands, and no attachments: a prompt box and a send button. -->
        <arc:AiComposer x:Name="Composer" Placeholder="Ask anything" IsAttachmentEnabled="False" MaxLength="{x:Null}" />
        <TextBlock x:Name="Sent" HorizontalAlignment="Center" Opacity="0.7" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class AiComposerMinimalDemo : UserControl
{
    public AiComposerMinimalDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Composer.Sent += (_, e) => Sent.Text = $"Sent: “{e.Message.Text.Trim()}”";
    }
}
```

### Wording

Every word comes from `Labels` (`AiComposerLabels`): the placeholder, the names of the buttons, the counter, the chip texts, the drop
cover and the announcements. Replace the instance to translate or reword; formatted texts are functions.

### Content guidelines

- **Placeholder**: say what the box takes, in one line: "Ask a question, type / for actions or @ for a file".
- **Commands**: a short verb ("recap", "rewrite") and one line that says what it does.
- **Context items**: a name people recognize and a hint that tells apart two with the same name (a path, a source).
- **Errors on chips**: a few words ("Over 30 MB", "Type not accepted").

### Best practices

- Put the composer at the bottom of the conversation and give it the width of the thread; it adapts to its own width (compact below 680 px,
  narrower below 560 and 400).
- Set `IsGenerating` as soon as you start a reply, and always handle `StopRequested`.
- Validate on your server too: the composer limits what it sends, it is not a security boundary.
- Do not queue messages silently while a reply runs; the composer does not.

### Common questions

**Why did the box clear after sending?** It always clears the text, the tokens and the attachments; tools, model and effort stay. Keep the
message if you need to restore it.

**Where is the voice input?** Not part of this version.

## API reference

### AiComposer

The prompt box of an AI app: a text area that grows with its text, "/" commands and "@" mentions that become tokens, attachments that upload in place (picked, pasted or dropped on the box), tool toggles, a model and effort menu, a character counter and a send button that turns into a stop button while a reply is generated. The composer reports a send through `Sent` (or `SendCommand`); your code starts the reply and sets `IsGenerating` while it runs, and the send button becomes a stop button that raises `StopRequested`. While a reply is generated the box stays editable but Enter does not send.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Text` | `string` | `""` | The prompt text, tokens included (two-way). |
| `Value` | `AiComposerValue` | – | The prompt with its tokens (two-way). Setting it replaces the text and the tokens. |
| `Placeholder` | `string?` | `null` | The hint shown while the box is empty; null shows `Placeholder`. |
| `AccessibleName` | `string?` | `null` | The accessible name of the text area. |
| `MinLines` | `int` | `1` | The box is this many lines high when it is empty. |
| `MaxLines` | `int` | `8` | The box grows to this many lines and then scrolls inside (8; in the `Inline` layout 7 unless set). |
| `MaxLength` | `int?` | `4000` | The longest prompt in characters; null means no limit and no counter. Over the limit, sending is blocked. |
| `CounterThreshold` | `double` | `0.8` | From this share of `MaxLength` the counter shows how many characters are left. |
| `WarningThreshold` | `double` | `0.95` | From this share of `MaxLength` the counter turns to the warning color. |
| `IsAttachmentEnabled` | `bool` | `true` | Whether the plus menu, pasting files and dropping files are on. |
| `AcceptedFileTypes` | `string?` | `null` | The file types that may be attached, in the syntax of `FileDropzone.Accept` (".pdf,image/*"); null accepts any. |
| `MaxFileSize` | `long?` | `31457280` | The largest file in bytes (30 MB by default); a larger one is attached in the error state with its reason. Null means no limit. |
| `LongPasteCharacters` | `int` | `1200` | A pasted text of at least this many characters becomes an attachment instead of text; 0 turns the rule off. |
| `LongPasteLines` | `int` | `12` | A pasted text of at least this many lines becomes an attachment instead of text; 0 turns the rule off. |
| `SelectedModel` | `AiModel?` | `null` | The selected model (two-way). Null at first selects the first model once and writes it back. |
| `Effort` | `ModelEffort?` | `null` | The selected effort (two-way); null follows the model's default. |
| `IsGenerating` | `bool` | `false` | Whether a reply is being generated (two-way): the send button shows a stop square and a progress ring. |
| `GenerationProgress` | `double` | `0` | How far the reply is, from 0 to 1: the target of the ring around the stop button. The ring never goes backwards while generating. |
| `SendState` | `AiSendState` | – | *Read-only.* Whether the prompt can be sent, is blocked, or a reply is being generated (read-only). |
| `SendCommand` | `ICommand?` | `null` | Run when the person sends the prompt, with the `AiComposerMessage` as the parameter. |
| `StopCommand` | `ICommand?` | `null` | Run when the person stops a reply being generated. |
| `Layout` | `AiComposerLayout` | `Full` | The full composer with its toolbar (default), or the AI chat's single row: paperclip, text and send, with compact chips above (no toolbar, tools, model pill, counter, "/" or "@" lists; the progress is not shown). Events, the sent message and the labels are the same in both. It can change at any time (the template is swapped; the text and the attachments stay). |
| `Labels` | `AiComposerLabels` | – | Every word the block shows or announces. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Sent` | `AiComposerSentEventArgs` | Raised when the person sends the prompt. |
| `StopRequested` | `RoutedEventArgs` | Raised when the person stops a reply being generated. |
| `AttachmentAdded` | `AiAttachmentEventArgs` | Raised when an attachment is added (while it may still be uploading). |
| `AttachmentRemoved` | `AiAttachmentEventArgs` | Raised when an attachment is removed or its upload is cancelled. |
| `ToolToggled` | `AiComposerToolToggledEventArgs` | Raised when the person turns a tool on or off. |
| `ModelChanged` | `ModelPickerModelChangedEventArgs` | Raised when the person picks another model. |
| `EffortChanged` | `ModelPickerEffortChangedEventArgs` | Raised when the effort changes. |

Pseudo-classes: `:dragging`, `:ready`, `:blocked`, `:generating`, `:over-limit`, `:compact`, `:narrow`, `:tiny`, `:inline`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

### AiCommand

A command the person can start a prompt with, such as "/recap".

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Id` | `string` | `""` | Stable id reported in tokens. |
| `Name` | `string` | `""` | The name without the slash; the person filters by its start, ignoring case. |
| `Description` | `string?` | `null` | One line that says what it does. |
| `Icon` | `Geometry?` | `null` | A 24 × 24 icon geometry (a Lucide path works). |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### AiContextItem

An item of context the person can mention with "@", such as a file or a document.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Id` | `string` | `""` | Stable id reported in tokens. |
| `Label` | `string` | `""` | The name the token shows; the person filters by it (and by `Hint`), ignoring case. |
| `Hint` | `string?` | `null` | A second line: a path, a source or a number. |
| `Group` | `string?` | `null` | The heading of the group the item is listed under; groups follow `AiComposer.MentionGroups`. |
| `Icon` | `Geometry?` | `null` | A 24 × 24 icon geometry. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### AiAttachment

A file, an image, a pasted text or a source attached to the prompt, with its upload state.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Id` | `string` | `""` | Stable id, unique within the composer. |
| `Name` | `string` | `""` | The name shown on the chip (a file name, "Pasted text", a source's title). |
| `Kind` | `AiAttachmentKind` | `File` | What the attachment is. |
| `Size` | `long?` | `null` | The size in bytes, when known. |
| `File` | `IStorageFile?` | `null` | The file, for attachments picked, pasted or dropped from the system. |
| `PastedText` | `string?` | `null` | The text of a `PastedText` attachment. |
| `Status` | `AiAttachmentStatus` | `Ready` | Where the attachment is in its life. |
| `Progress` | `double` | `0` | How far the upload is, from 0 to 1. |
| `Error` | `string?` | `null` | A short reason for `Error`, such as "Over 30 MB". |
| `Thumbnail` | `IImage?` | `null` | A thumbnail for images. |
| `Meta` | `string?` | `null` | The second line of the chip ("PDF, 469 KB"); null makes one from `Kind`, the name and `Size`. |
| `Icon` | `Geometry?` | `null` | A 24 × 24 icon geometry for attachments without a thumbnail; null picks one from the kind and the file extension. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### AiComposerTool

A toggle in the composer's toolbar, such as "Web search": it changes how the next reply is made.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Id` | `string` | `""` | Stable id reported in the sent message. |
| `Label` | `string` | `""` | The label next to the icon (hidden in a narrow composer) and the accessible name. |
| `Tip` | `string?` | `null` | The tooltip; null shows the label. |
| `Icon` | `Geometry?` | `null` | A 24 × 24 icon geometry. |
| `IsChecked` | `bool` | `false` | Whether the tool is on (two-way). |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### AiComposerAction

An entry of the plus menu next to the prompt, besides the built-in "Upload file".

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Label` | `string` | `""` | The text of the menu entry. |
| `Icon` | `Geometry?` | `null` | A 24 × 24 icon geometry. |
| `Command` | `ICommand?` | `null` | Run for `Custom` entries, with the composer as the parameter. |
| `Kind` | `AiComposerActionKind` | `Custom` | What the entry does. |
| `IsSeparatorBefore` | `bool` | `false` | Whether a separator is drawn above the entry. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### AiComposerMessage

| Property | Description |
|---|---|
| `Text` / `Tokens` / `Value` | The prompt, the tokens in it and both together |
| `Attachments` | The attachments that are ready; failed or still uploading ones are left out |
| `Model` / `Effort` | The selected model and effort |
| `Tools` | For each tool id, whether it was on |

### Events

| Event | Raised when | Arguments |
|---|---|---|
| `Sent` | The person sends the prompt | `Message` |
| `StopRequested` | The person stops a reply being generated | |
| `AttachmentAdded` / `AttachmentRemoved` | An attachment is added, removed or its upload cancelled | `Attachment` |
| `ToolToggled` | A tool is turned on or off | `Tool` |
| `ModelChanged` / `EffortChanged` | The person picks a model or an effort | The old and new value |

## Accessibility

- The text area has an accessible name ("Message"); the lists of commands and mentions are lists whose rows are named by their title and hint,
  and the highlighted row is reported through the text area, so the focus stays where the person types.
- The send button's name says what it does or why it cannot: "Send message", "Type a message to send", "Wait for uploads to finish",
  "Shorten the message by N characters", "Stop generating".
- The toolbar buttons are named; tool toggles report whether they are pressed; the plus button reports that it opens a menu.
- A polite live region announces the number of suggestions, tools turned on or off, model and effort changes, finished and failed uploads, removals, long
  pastes, a sent message and a stop.
- Chips have named buttons ("Cancel upload of report.pdf", "Remove report.pdf"); when the last chip is removed the focus moves to the text.
- Focus goes where the person would look next: back to the plus button after Escape in its menu, to the text after choosing an entry, back to the model pill after a choice.
- Status never relies on color alone: errors add an icon and a reason, the counter adds a number.
- Reduced motion keeps every state and announcement.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Enter` | Sends (not while composing, a list is open, or a reply is generated) |
| `Shift+Enter` | Adds a line |
| `/` at the start of a line, `@` after a space | Opens the list of commands or mentions |
| `ArrowUp` / `ArrowDown` in a list | Moves between rows; wraps around |
| `Enter` or `Tab` in a list | Inserts the row as a token |
| `Escape` | Closes a list or menu; with none open, stops a reply being generated |
| `Enter`, `Space` or `ArrowDown` on the plus or the model pill | Opens its menu |
| `ArrowLeft` / `ArrowRight` on the effort row | Changes the effort |
| `Tab` | Moves through the plus, the tools, the counter, the model, the send button and the chips |

## Motion

- The text area grows line by line from `MinLines` to `MaxLines` (1 to 8) in a 160 ms ease, then scrolls.
- The border deepens when the composer has focus (160 ms); the drop cover fades in when files are dragged over.
- Chips come in at a scale of 0.92 while fading; the ring becomes a check and then a remove button on a spring.
- The send button's arrow turns into a stop square on a spring while the ring around it fades in; the ring follows the progress and never goes back.
- Menus and the suggestion list grow from their button or caret; the list's height follows its rows on a spring.
- The counter and the model pill's text take the width they need on a spring.
- Reduced motion keeps 120 ms fades and drops movement and springs. Off applies every change at once.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| Height of the box | 160 ms ease | Immediate | Immediate |
| Border and hover colors | 160 ms | 120 ms | Immediate |
| Send to stop | Shape change on a spring, ring fades in | Swap with a 120 ms fade | Immediate |
| Chip enters or leaves | Scale and fade | 120 ms fade | Immediate |
| Menus and the suggestion list | Grow from the anchor | 120 ms fade | Immediate |

## Related

- `ModelPicker` for choosing a model on a settings page.
- `TokenTextEditor` for the text area with tokens by itself.
- `MentionInput` for comments with people and channels.
- `AgentMemory` for what the assistant remembers.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `ModelPicker` | The model choice is not tied to writing a prompt |
| `TokenTextEditor` | You need the editor, not the whole box |
| `MentionInput` | The mentions are people and channels in a comment |
| `Textarea` | The text has no commands, files or tools |

# Agent memory

> A card that shows what an assistant remembers: filter by group, search, edit a sentence in place, forget with a few seconds to undo, file a just-noted memory and add one by hand.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc.Blocks`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc.Blocks --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/blocks/agent-memory

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.AgentMemoryPreviewDemo">
    <!-- The card is at most 640 wide and centers itself; the list scrolls inside it above 380. -->
    <arc:AgentMemory x:Name="Memory" AssistantName="Orbit" Margin="0,12" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class AgentMemoryPreviewDemo : UserControl
{
    public AgentMemoryPreviewDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Memory.Groups.AddRange(AgentMemoryDemoData.Groups());
        Memory.Memories.AddRange(AgentMemoryDemoData.Memories());
        Memory.Captured.AddRange(AgentMemoryDemoData.Captured());
        Memory.Capacity = AgentMemoryDemoData.Capacity;
    }
}
```

## When to use

Agent memory is the page where people see, correct and delete what an assistant has kept about them. It is one card:
a capacity meter, two switches, filter pills, a search, the memories grouped by kind, and a field to add one.

- **A settings page for an assistant that learns**: "Reference saved memories" and "Reference chat history" are the two
  switches people look for, and the list under them is the proof of what is saved.
- **A trust surface after a chat**: the assistant noted something ("Noted: you run builds with the dotnet CLI"). The
  captured pill shows it and files it in one press.
- **A memory that must be reviewable**: every sentence can be edited in place or forgotten, and a forget keeps a few
  seconds of undo before it is real.
- **A bounded memory**: the meter shows how much of the capacity is used and warns before it is full.

## When not to use

- **A log of events or messages**: a memory is one short sentence without a final period. Use a `Timeline` or a table for history.
- **Long notes or documents**: each memory is limited to `MaxLength` characters (200 by default). Use an editor for long text.
- **Settings that are not memories**: put toggles and choices in a settings page with `Switch` and `Select`.
- **Deleting with no way back**: the undo bar is the design. If your data cannot be restored for a few seconds, say so
  in the explanation text and shorten `UndoDuration`.
- **Storing the memories**: the card changes a list and tells you. Saving, syncing and what the assistant does with the
  memories is your code.

## Usage

`AgentMemory` derives from Avalonia's `TemplatedControl`. A memory is a `MemoryItem`, an `AvaloniaObject` with an id, a
sentence, the key of its group, where it came from and a date. Groups are `MemoryGroup`s; with none, the four default
groups (About you, Preferences, Projects, People) are used.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:AgentMemory AssistantName="Orbit" Capacity="2000">
        <arc:AgentMemory.Memories>
            <arc:MemoryItem Id="1" GroupKey="preferences" SourceKind="Chat"
                            Text="Prefers tables to long bullet lists" />
            <arc:MemoryItem Id="2" GroupKey="people" PersonName="Mina Okafor"
                            Text="Mina Okafor reviews every database migration" />
        </arc:AgentMemory.Memories>
    </arc:AgentMemory>
</UserControl>
```

### Anatomy

- **Header**: the title, a subtitle that names the assistant, and the capacity meter ("62% full" over a thin bar).
- **Switches**: "Reference saved memories" and "Reference chat history", each with a line that explains its state.
- **Toolbar**: the filter pills and, at the end, the search button.
- **Captured pill**: the assistant's latest note. Press it to file the memory into its group.
- **List**: the memories, grouped under headings with counts, scrolling inside the card above `ListMaxHeight`.
- **Add field**: type a sentence and press Enter; the card sorts it into a group.

### Filtering and searching

The pills filter by group; the All view shows every group that has memories under its heading, and a single group shows
its memories without a heading (or its own sentence when it is empty). The search button opens a box over the pills.
It matches anywhere in a sentence, ignores case and highlights every hit. Results are grouped with the number of hits
per group, and the search covers all groups whatever the filter is. Escape or the close button clears the search and
brings back the filter you had.

`SelectedGroupKey`, `SearchText` and `IsSearchOpen` are two-way, so you can set them from code.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.AgentMemoryBindingsDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12" Margin="0,12">
        <StackPanel Orientation="Horizontal" Spacing="8" HorizontalAlignment="Center">
            <arc:Button x:Name="Preferences" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Content="Show Preferences" />
            <arc:Button x:Name="Everything" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Content="Show everything" />
            <arc:Button x:Name="Search" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Content="Search &#8220;ai&#8221;" />
        </StackPanel>
        <arc:AgentMemory x:Name="Memory" AssistantName="Orbit" />
        <TextBlock x:Name="State" HorizontalAlignment="Center" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using System.Collections.ObjectModel;
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class AgentMemoryBindingsDemo : UserControl
{
    public AgentMemoryBindingsDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Memory.Groups.AddRange(AgentMemoryDemoData.Groups());
        Memory.Capacity = AgentMemoryDemoData.Capacity;

        // A list of your own to follow: the card changes it, and what you change in it shows up in the card.
        var memories = new ObservableCollection<MemoryItem>(AgentMemoryDemoData.Memories());
        Memory.MemoriesSource = memories;

        Preferences.Click += (_, _) => Memory.SelectedGroupKey = "preferences";
        Everything.Click += (_, _) =>
        {
            Memory.IsSearchOpen = false;
            Memory.SelectedGroupKey = null;
        };
        Search.Click += (_, _) =>
        {
            Memory.IsSearchOpen = true;
            Memory.SearchText = "ai";
        };

        void Show() => State.Text = $"{memories.Count} memories · filter: {Memory.SelectedGroupKey ?? "all"}"
            + (Memory.IsSearchOpen ? $" · search: “{Memory.SearchText}”" : string.Empty);
        Memory.PropertyChanged += (_, e) =>
        {
            if (e.Property == AgentMemory.SelectedGroupKeyProperty || e.Property == AgentMemory.SearchTextProperty
                || e.Property == AgentMemory.IsSearchOpenProperty)
            {
                Show();
            }
        };
        memories.CollectionChanged += (_, _) => Show();
        Show();
    }
}
```

Give the card a list to follow with `MemoriesSource` (an `ObservableCollection<MemoryItem>` works): the card makes its
changes on that list, and what you change in it appears in the card.

### Editing and forgetting

The Edit button on a row (visible on hover and focus) opens a small editor: Enter saves, Shift+Enter adds a line, Escape
cancels. An empty or too long sentence is refused with a message; past `MaxLength` a counter ("212 of 200 characters") appears.
Forget turns the row into a bar, "Forgot “…”", with an **Undo** button that drains for `UndoDuration`. The count and the
meter drop at once; the change is committed and `MemoryChanged` raised only when the time runs out. Several bars can
count down together.

### Saving the change

Set `CommitAsync` to save a change before it takes effect. The editor shows a saving state while the task runs. If
it throws, its message appears in place and the change is rolled back; if it is cancelled, the change is rolled back
silently. A forget is committed once its undo window has ended.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.AgentMemoryCommitDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12" Margin="0,12">
        <arc:AgentMemory x:Name="Memory" AssistantName="Orbit" />
        <TextBlock x:Name="Log" TextWrapping="Wrap" HorizontalAlignment="Center" MaxWidth="560"
                   Text="Edit or add a memory. A save that contains the word fail is refused, as a server could." />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class AgentMemoryCommitDemo : UserControl
{
    public AgentMemoryCommitDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Memory.Groups.AddRange(AgentMemoryDemoData.Groups());
        Memory.Memories.AddRange(AgentMemoryDemoData.Memories());
        Memory.Capacity = AgentMemoryDemoData.Capacity;

        // Save somewhere first: the card shows a saving state until the task ends, and a failure rolls the change back in place.
        Memory.CommitAsync = async (change, cancellation) =>
        {
            await Task.Delay(700, cancellation);
            if (change.Kind != MemoryChangeKind.Forget && change.Memory.Text.Contains("fail", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase))
            {
                throw new InvalidOperationException("The server refused this memory. Try other words.");
            }
        };

        // Sort a typed memory yourself, here by its first letter, instead of the built-in keyword guess.
        Memory.ClassifyAsync = async (text, cancellation) =>
        {
            await Task.Delay(400, cancellation);
            return char.ToLowerInvariant(text[0]) switch
            {
                >= 'a' and <= 'h' => "about",
                >= 'i' and <= 'm' => "preferences",
                >= 'n' and <= 's' => "projects",
                _ => "people"
            };
        };

        Memory.MemoryChanged += (_, e) =>
            Log.Text = $"{e.Change.Kind}: “{e.Change.Memory.Text}” · {e.Memories.Count} memories";
    }
}
```

```csharp
memory.CommitAsync = async (change, cancellation) =>
{
    await api.SaveAsync(change.Kind, change.Memory.Id, change.Memory.Text, cancellation);
};
```

`MemoryChange` has the `Kind` (`Capture`, `Add`, `Edit` or `Forget`), the `Memory` and, for an edit, the
`PreviousText`. `MemoryChanged` reports the change and the whole list after it.

### Captured memories

Put what the assistant has just noted in `Captured`: a `CapturedMemory` with a short `Note` and the `Memory` to file. The
first one not yet filed shows as a pill. Pressing it switches the filter to the memory's group if needed, adds the memory,
tints its row for a moment and changes the pill to "Saved to Preferences" before it folds away.
`FileCaptured()` does the same from code.

### Adding by hand

The field at the bottom adds a memory. The card sorts it into a group: with no `ClassifyAsync` it makes a keyword guess
(two capitalized names mean People, "prefer" or "want" mean Preferences, "project" or "moving" mean Projects, anything
else the first group). Set `ClassifyAsync` to ask your own code or a model. When the capacity would be exceeded, adding is
refused with "Memory is full" and the text stays. Set `IsAddEnabled` to false for a read-only card.

### Capacity

`Capacity` counts characters across all memories. The meter warns from `WarningRatio` (90% by default) with a color and
an icon, not color alone. A capacity of zero hides the meter and the limit.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.AgentMemoryCapacityDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12" Margin="0,12">
        <arc:AgentMemory x:Name="Memory" AssistantName="Orbit" ListMaxHeight="260" />
        <TextBlock HorizontalAlignment="Center" MaxWidth="560" TextWrapping="Wrap"
                   Text="The meter turns to the warning color from 90 percent. Add a few memories: once the capacity is used up, adding is refused and the text stays." />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class AgentMemoryCapacityDemo : UserControl
{
    public AgentMemoryCapacityDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Memory.Groups.AddRange(AgentMemoryDemoData.Groups());
        Memory.Memories.AddRange(AgentMemoryDemoData.Memories());

        // 91 percent used: the meter already warns, and one more sentence of average length fills it.
        Memory.Capacity = (int)(Memory.Memories.Sum(m => m.Text.Length) / 0.91);
        Memory.WarningRatio = 0.9;
    }
}
```

### Paused

Turning "Reference saved memories" off dims the list and replaces the captured pill with a sentence saying memories are
paused. The list stays editable; adding and forgetting still work. `IsSavedMemoriesEnabled` and `IsChatHistoryEnabled`
are two-way, and `SettingToggled` reports a change.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.AgentMemoryPausedDemo">
    <!-- Saved memories are off: the list is dimmed (still editable) and the captured pill gives way to a notice. -->
    <arc:AgentMemory x:Name="Memory" AssistantName="Orbit" IsSavedMemoriesEnabled="False" IsChatHistoryEnabled="False" Margin="0,12" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class AgentMemoryPausedDemo : UserControl
{
    public AgentMemoryPausedDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Memory.Groups.AddRange(AgentMemoryDemoData.Groups());

        // Only two memories: the Projects and People groups are empty, which the All view hides and their own filter explains.
        Memory.Memories.AddRange(AgentMemoryDemoData.Memories().Take(5));
        Memory.Captured.AddRange(AgentMemoryDemoData.Captured());
        Memory.Capacity = AgentMemoryDemoData.Capacity;
    }
}
```

### Wording

All words come from `Labels` (`AgentMemoryLabels`): replace the instance to translate or reword. Formatted texts are
functions so the word order can change.

```csharp
memory.Labels = new AgentMemoryLabels
{
    Title = "Souvenirs",
    SavedTo = group => $"Rangé dans {group}",
    NoMatches = query => $"Aucun souvenir ne correspond à « {query} »"
};
```

`Title` and `Subtitle` on the control win over the labels when set.

### Content guidelines

- **A memory is one sentence without a final period**, in the third person or as a plain fact: "Prefers tables to long bullet lists".
- **Be specific and neutral**: "Is training for a spring half marathon", not "Loves running!".
- **People**: put the name in the sentence and in `PersonName`; the row shows a small avatar with the first letter (or `PersonImage`).
- **Source**: `Chat` shows "From a chat", `Manual` "Added by you", with a short date. Give `SourceUri` to make the source a link and
  handle `SourceRequested` or `SourceCommand` to open the conversation.

### Best practices

- Save with `CommitAsync` and show real errors; never swallow a failure, the card rolls the change back for you.
- Keep `UndoDuration` at five seconds or more; shorter windows are hard to use with a screen reader.
- Offer the same list to the assistant that the card shows: what people cannot see, they cannot correct.
- Keep four to six groups; more than that scrolls the pills.

### Common questions

**Why did my forget not call `CommitAsync` at once?** It is committed when the undo window ends; until then it can be undone.

**Can I use my own groups?** Yes. Add `MemoryGroup`s with unique keys and set each memory's `GroupKey`. A memory whose key matches no
group is shown in the first group.

**Is the card also a good fit for a narrow sidebar?** Below 440 px wide it tightens its padding, wraps the subtitle and lets the filters scroll.

## API reference

### AgentMemory

A card that shows what an assistant remembers about the person: a capacity meter, two switches (use saved memories, use chat history), filter pills by group, a search, and the memories themselves, which can be edited in place or forgotten with a few seconds to undo. A memory the assistant has just noted shows as a pill that files it into its group, and a field at the bottom adds one by hand and sorts it into a group. Changes are applied to `Memories` and reported through `MemoryChanged`; set `CommitAsync` to save them somewhere first (a failure shows in place and rolls the change back).

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `MemoriesSource` | `IList<MemoryItem>?` | `null` | The memories to show and change, when you give them as a list to follow; it wins over `Memories` when set. |
| `CapturedSource` | `IList<CapturedMemory>?` | `null` | The memories the assistant has just noted, when you give them as a list to follow; it wins over `Captured` when set. |
| `IsSavedMemoriesEnabled` | `bool` | `true` | Whether the first switch ("Reference saved memories") is on (two-way). Off dims the list and pauses the captured pill. |
| `IsChatHistoryEnabled` | `bool` | `true` | Whether the second switch ("Reference chat history") is on (two-way). |
| `Capacity` | `int` | `2000` | The capacity in characters of all the memories together; the meter shows the share used. Zero or less hides the meter and the limit. |
| `WarningRatio` | `double` | `0.9` | From this share of `Capacity` the meter turns to the warning color. |
| `MaxLength` | `int` | `200` | The longest a single memory may be, for editing and adding alike. |
| `UndoDuration` | `TimeSpan` | `00:00:05` | How long a forgotten memory can be brought back before it is really forgotten. |
| `AssistantName` | `string` | `"Assistant"` | The assistant's name, used in the subtitle and the switches' explanations. |
| `Title` | `string?` | `null` | The title; null shows `Title`. |
| `Subtitle` | `string?` | `null` | The line under the title; null shows `Subtitle` with the assistant's name. |
| `SelectedGroupKey` | `string?` | `null` | The key of the group the list is filtered to (two-way); null shows all groups. |
| `SearchText` | `string` | `""` | The text of the search (two-way). Searching covers all groups whatever the filter is. |
| `IsSearchOpen` | `bool` | `false` | Whether the search box is open (two-way). |
| `IsAddEnabled` | `bool` | `true` | Whether the field to add a memory by hand is shown. |
| `ListMaxHeight` | `double` | `380` | The list scrolls inside the card above this height. |
| `Labels` | `AgentMemoryLabels` | – | Every word the block shows or announces. |
| `SourceCommand` | `ICommand?` | `null` | Run when the person presses a source with a link, with the `MemoryItem` as the parameter. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `MemoryChanged` | `MemoryChangedEventArgs` | Raised after a change is committed. |
| `SettingToggled` | `MemorySettingToggledEventArgs` | Raised when one of the two switches changes. |
| `SourceRequested` | `MemorySourceRequestedEventArgs` | Raised when the person presses the source of a memory that has a `SourceUri`. |

Pseudo-classes: `:compact`, `:paused`, `:no-meter`, `:no-add`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

### MemoryItem

One thing the assistant remembers about the person. Data only: an `AvaloniaObject` so that the properties bind and a change (an edit from elsewhere) reaches the row on screen.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Id` | `string` | `""` | Stable id, unique within `Memories`. |
| `Text` | `string` | `""` | The memory as one sentence without a final period, such as "Prefers tables to long bullet lists". |
| `GroupKey` | `string` | `""` | The key of the `MemoryGroup` the memory is filed under. |
| `SourceKind` | `MemorySourceKind` | `Manual` | Whether the memory came from a chat or was added by the person. |
| `SourceDate` | `DateTimeOffset` | `01/01/0001 00:00:00 +00:00` | The date of the source, shown as a short date such as "Sep 8". |
| `SourceUri` | `Uri?` | `null` | When set, the source text is a link: `SourceRequested` reports it. |
| `PersonName` | `string?` | `null` | When set (the memory is about a person), the row shows a small avatar and this name is its accessible name. |
| `PersonImage` | `IImage?` | `null` | The avatar image for `PersonName`; without one the avatar shows the first letter. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### MemoryGroup

A filing group of memories (About you, Preferences, Projects, People by default).

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Key` | `string` | `""` | The key a memory's `GroupKey` refers to. |
| `Label` | `string` | `""` | The label of the filter pill and the group heading. |
| `EmptyText` | `string?` | `null` | The sentence shown in the group when it has no memories while it is the only group on screen. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### CapturedMemory

A memory the assistant has just noted: `Note` (such as "Noted: you run builds with the dotnet CLI") shows in the captured pill until the person files it, after which the pill shows "Saved to" the group.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Note` | `string` | `""` | The short sentence the pill shows, such as "Noted: you run builds with the dotnet CLI". |
| `Memory` | `MemoryItem?` | `null` | The memory to file; it is added to `Memories` when the pill is pressed. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### MemoryChange

| Property | Description |
|---|---|
| `Kind` | `Capture`, `Add`, `Edit` or `Forget` |
| `Memory` | The memory that changed (for a forget, as it was) |
| `PreviousText` | The text before an edit; null for other kinds |

### Events

| Event | Raised when | Arguments |
|---|---|---|
| `MemoryChanged` | A change was committed | `Change`, `Memories` (the whole list after it) |
| `SettingToggled` | One of the two switches changed | `Setting` (`SavedMemories` or `ChatHistory`), `IsOn` |
| `SourceRequested` | A source with a link was pressed | `Memory` |

## Accessibility

- The meter is announced as "Memory used, 62% full" and reads the real value, not the animating one.
- The switches have a name and an explanation that updates with their state. The filter pills are a group with the name
  "Filter memories", report which one is pressed, and are one tab stop; Left and Right move and select.
- Rows are list items inside groups named by their heading. The Edit and Forget buttons are named with the sentence ("Edit
  memory: …") and have tooltips; they appear on hover and keyboard focus, and take no extra space.
- A polite live region announces search results, saved edits, a forget with its undo time, the end of the window, a
  restore, filing and adding, a full memory, and each switch.
- Focus goes where the person would look next: into the editor and back to Edit after saving or canceling; to Undo after Forget
  and back to Forget after Undo; to the search box and back to the search button; to the new row's Edit button after filing a
  captured memory with the keyboard.
- Status never relies on color alone: the warning meter adds an icon, errors add an icon and a sentence, saved states a check.
- Reduced motion keeps every state, announcement and the undo time.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Tab` | Switches, the selected filter pill, the search button, the captured pill, each row's Edit and Forget, the add field |
| `ArrowLeft` / `ArrowRight` on the pills | Moves to the previous or next pill and selects it; wraps around |
| `Home` / `End` on the pills | First or last pill |
| `Enter` or `Space` | Presses the focused button, switch or pill |
| `Enter` in the editor | Saves; `Shift+Enter` adds a line |
| `Escape` in the editor | Cancels |
| `Escape` in the search | Clears it, closes it and returns to the search button |
| `Enter` in the add field | Sorts and adds the memory |

## Motion

- Filtering fades leaving groups and rows out in 100 ms, fades entering ones in over 160 ms after a short delay, and
  their heights follow on a critically damped spring. The selected pill's background glides between pills.
- The search box grows over the pills in 240 ms while the pills fade out; its field and close button fade in.
- A row, its editor and its undo bar crossfade (100 ms out, 160 ms in) while the row's height springs between them.
- The undo ring drains in a straight line over the undo window; the seconds count down once a second.
- A filed or added row opens its slot on a smooth spring, then its row tints for 1.6 seconds and fades.
- The meter's fill and number follow one spring; the warning color changes at once.
- Explanations, the captured pill's text and the add field's status crossfade, rising 2 px as they come in.
- Reduced motion drops springs, movement and the drain: heights jump, crossfades become short fades, the ring stays full and
  the seconds still count. Off applies every change at once.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| Filter or search | Fade out 100 ms, in 160 ms; heights spring | Short fades; heights jump | Immediate |
| Row to editor or undo bar | Crossfade; height springs | 120 ms crossfade | Immediate |
| Selected pill | Glides on a spring | Jumps | Immediate |
| Search opens | Width over 240 ms | Immediate | Immediate |
| Undo ring | Drains over the window | Stays full | Stays full |
| Filed or added row | Slot springs open; 1.6 s tint | No slot motion; tint stays | Immediate |

## Related

- `ModelPicker` for choosing the model that uses the memories.
- `Switch` for a setting that is not about memories.
- `Timeline` for a history of events.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `Switch` | One setting turns on or off |
| `Timeline` | The list is a history in time order |
| `Textarea` | People write a longer text |
| `Toast` | A short message confirms an action and goes away |

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class SidebarPreviewDemo : UserControl
{
    public SidebarPreviewDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
    }

    // The toggle lives in the page's top bar, outside the sidebar: IsCollapsed is a normal two-way property.
    private void OnToggleSidebar(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) => Nav.ToggleCollapsed();
}
```

## When to use

The sidebar is the main navigation of an application that has more pages than a header can hold. It sits at the left
edge of the window for the whole session, so people learn where each page lives and return to it without searching.

- **The main menu of a SaaS admin console**: Home, Inbox, Reports, Billing and Settings for a workspace. Top-level
  places go in the first section without a heading, and areas with their own pages go in headed sections below.
- **Projects and areas in a work tool**: a project list with one level of pages under each project (Atlas, Beacon),
  where a parent row opens or closes its pages instead of showing a view of its own.
- **Mailboxes and docs sites**: folders with counts and colored labels, or a tree of guides that a filter narrows as
  people type.
- **Account and billing areas**: a Billing section with Invoices and Plans, next to a Usage page with a count of new
  events. The count stays visible while the person works in another area.
- **Dense internal tools with many pages**: an operations console where the filter finds a page by its first letters,
  and the icon rail keeps the pages reachable when the window is narrow.
- **Navigation that should stay on screen but take less room on demand**: the sidebar folds into a 64 px icon rail,
  and each page keeps a tooltip and a menu, so the content keeps its width.

## When not to use

- **Two to five views of the same object**, such as Overview, Activity and Settings of one order: use `Tabs`, which
  sit above the content and keep the object in view.
- **Steps of a sequence or a path through a hierarchy**: use `Stepper` for a wizard and `Breadcrumb` for the place of
  a page in a deep structure.
- **A deep tree of folders and files**: use `TreeView`. The sidebar shows one level of nested pages; a tree of files
  needs expanding and collapsing at every depth.
- **Actions rather than places**: use `DropdownMenu` for a menu of commands, or `CommandPalette` for keyboard search
  across pages and actions. A few actions that belong to the list itself ("New project", "More") may sit in it as
  action rows, but a sidebar row should mostly open a page.
- **The signed-in person and workspace switching**: use `UserMenu` in the sidebar's header or footer for the account
  menu, and keep the sidebar itself for pages.

## Usage

Put `SidebarSection` elements inside the sidebar and `SidebarItem` elements inside the sections. A section without a
`Header` has no heading, which suits the first group (Home, Inbox). Give every page a `Key` and bind `SelectedKey` to
your route. The sidebar takes its width from the theme (240 open, 64 as a rail), so place it in a `DockPanel` or an
`Auto` grid column and do not set `Width`.

```xml
<DockPanel xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
           xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
           xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
           Height="420">
    <arc:Sidebar DockPanel.Dock="Left" SelectedKey="home" IsFilterVisible="True">
        <arc:SidebarSection>
            <arc:SidebarItem Key="home" Label="Home" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.House}" />
            <arc:SidebarItem Key="inbox" Label="Inbox" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Inbox}" Badge="4" />
        </arc:SidebarSection>
        <arc:SidebarSection Header="Workspace">
            <arc:SidebarItem Key="projects" Label="Projects" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Folder}" IsExpanded="True">
                <arc:SidebarItem Key="projects/atlas" Label="Atlas" />
                <arc:SidebarItem Key="projects/beacon" Label="Beacon" />
            </arc:SidebarItem>
        </arc:SidebarSection>
    </arc:Sidebar>
    <TextBlock Margin="24" Text="Page content" />
</DockPanel>
```

`Sidebar` derives from Avalonia's `TemplatedControl`. It is not focusable itself: the list of rows inside it takes the
focus, so the whole navigation is one tab stop. Its content is the `Sections` collection (XAML content); each
`SidebarSection` holds its pages in `Items`, and a `SidebarItem` holds its child pages in its own `Items`. The model is
deliberately small: two levels of pages, one selected page, and everything else is a count, an icon or a flag.

The selected page gets a muted block behind it and an accent-colored icon, and the block glides from row to row. The
preview at the top of the page is the app rail layout: a logo and a two-line title in the header, the page's own top
bar toggling the sidebar, and the signed-in person in the footer. The layouts below show three more.

### Anatomy

1. **Header** (`Header`): content at the top of the sidebar, typically a logo with a title or a workspace switcher. It
   has 12 px side margins and shares its row with the collapse button. On the rail it gives way to the collapse button;
   without the button it stays, clipped to the rail.
2. **Collapse button** (`IsCollapseButtonVisible`, `CollapseButtonPlacement`, `CollapseButtonText`): a 40 px wide ghost
   icon button with the PanelLeft glyph. It sits at the end of the header row, or beside the filter box. It is shown by
   default.
3. **Filter** (`IsFilterVisible`, `FilterText`, `FilterPlaceholder`): a 32 px high search field under the header with
   12 px side margins. On the rail it becomes a 40 px search button.
4. **Section heading** (`SidebarSection.Header`): a 28 px row with a small text in the muted text color, with 10 px
   above it after the first section. A collapsible heading ends in a 12 px chevron. A section without a `Header` shows
   no heading; after the first section it leaves a 16 px gap instead.
5. **Page row** (`SidebarItem`): 32 px high with a 10 px corner radius and 12 px side padding. It holds a 16 px icon
   (`Icon`) in the muted color, 10 px before the label (`Label`, 13 px, secondary text color) and an optional count at
   the end (`Badge`). Rows are 1 px apart.
6. **Selection block**: a muted wash of the foreground color behind the selected row, with the label at full contrast
   and the icon in the accent color. There is no accent bar. It is one shared element that glides between rows.
7. **Unread dot and action row**: `IsUnread` adds a 6 px accent dot at the end of the row and makes the label stronger.
   An `IsAction` row is muted and is never selected.
8. **Nested page**: a child row is 30 px high, indented 26 px under its parent and hangs from a 1 px guide line in the
   subtle border color. Children of children are not shown.
9. **Parent chevron**: a 14 px chevron at the end of a parent row. It points right when the parent is closed and
   turns down when it is open.
10. **Footer** (`Footer`): content at the bottom, typically the signed-in person, under a 1 px separator. It has 12 px
    side margins and keeps its open-width layout on the rail, clipped to the rail's width.

The pane is a hair darker than the page next to it (a mix of the surface and the muted surface color) with a 1 px
border on the right. The open sidebar is 240 px wide and the rail is 64 px; both come from the theme. `Background`,
`BorderThickness` and `CornerRadius` are ordinary properties, so a sidebar can also float as a rounded card.

### Layouts

The sidebar is one control; the layout around it comes from what you put in its header, filter and footer, from the
frame you give it and from the page next to it. Four layouts show the range, and each one collapses to the rail. The
preview at the top of the page is the first, **App rail**: a header with a logo and a two-line title, no collapse
button of its own (`IsCollapseButtonVisible="False"`) because the page's top bar has a toggle that calls
`ToggleCollapsed()`, and a user block in the footer.

**Workspace.** The sidebar floats as an inset card: `CornerRadius` and `BorderThickness` give it its own rounded
border. The header holds a workspace switcher, and the collapse button sits beside the filter box
(`CollapseButtonPlacement="Filter"`). Pages use colored dots as icons, `IsUnread` marks a project with news, and an
action row ends the list. The footer carries a storage meter (a `Progress`) and the signed-in person (an `Avatar` with a
status dot).

**Inbox.** A full-width Compose button in the header (on the rail only its icon stays), folders with counts, a
collapsible Labels section with colored dots and a muted "More" row (`IsAction` with a `TrailingIcon`). The page's own

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.SidebarInboxDemo">
    <UserControl.Styles>
        <!-- On the icon rail the footer keeps only its leading 40px (the avatar); the rest fades. -->
        <Style Selector="arc|Sidebar :is(Control).rail-fade">
            <Setter Property="Opacity" Value="1" />
        </Style>
        <Style Selector="arc|Sidebar:collapsed :is(Control).rail-fade">
            <Setter Property="Opacity" Value="0" />
        </Style>
        <Style Selector="arc|Sidebar:motion-full :is(Control).rail-fade">
            <Setter Property="Transitions">
                <Transitions>
                    <DoubleTransition Property="Opacity" Duration="0:0:0.16" />
                </Transitions>
            </Setter>
        </Style>
        <!-- Compose is as wide as the rows while the sidebar is open; on the rail only its icon stays (the pane clips the rest). -->
        <Style Selector="arc|Button.compose">
            <Setter Property="HorizontalAlignment" Value="Stretch" />
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class SidebarInboxDemo : UserControl
{
    public SidebarInboxDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
    }

    // The toggle lives in the list's top bar, outside the sidebar: IsCollapsed is a normal two-way property.
    private void OnToggleSidebar(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) => Nav.ToggleCollapsed();
}
```

**Docs.** A title with a version button in the header and the filter box with the collapse button beside it. The pages
are a tree of groups with icons and a chevron; typing in the filter narrows the tree live and opens the groups that
match. The page beside it is an article with an "On this page" outline: the demo's code-behind watches the scroll
position and glides a 2 px accent bar to the active heading with a `GlidingIndicator`.

```cs
using Avalonia;
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Input;
using Avalonia.Layout;
using Avalonia.Media;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class SidebarDocsDemo : UserControl
{
    private readonly List<(Control Heading, Border Entry)> _sections = new();
    private int _active = -1;

    public SidebarDocsDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        // "On this page": one entry per heading. The bar is a GlidingIndicator in the entries' coordinate space.
        foreach (var heading in new[] { Section1, Section2, Section3, Section4, Section5, Section6 })
        {
            var entry = new Border
            {
                Child = new TextBlock { Text = heading.Text },
                Focusable = true,
                HorizontalAlignment = HorizontalAlignment.Stretch
            };
            entry.Classes.Add("entry");
            var captured = heading;
            entry.PointerReleased += (_, e) =>
            {
                if (e.InitialPressMouseButton == MouseButton.Left)
                {
                    ScrollTo(captured);
                }
            };
            entry.KeyDown += (_, e) =>
            {
                if (e.Key is Key.Enter or Key.Space)
                {
                    ScrollTo(captured);
                    e.Handled = true;
                }
            };
            OutlineItems.Children.Add(entry);
            _sections.Add((heading, entry));
        }
        Page.ScrollChanged += (_, _) => UpdateActive(animate: true);
        // The entries wrap with the column: place the bar again whenever the outline resizes (also the first layout).
        OutlineItems.SizeChanged += (_, _) => UpdateActive(animate: false, force: true);
    }

    private void ScrollTo(Control heading)
    {
        if (heading.TranslatePoint(default, Article) is { } point)
        {
            Page.Offset = new Vector(0, Math.Max(0, point.Y - 24));
        }
    }

    /// <summary>The active section is the last heading that has reached the top of the page (the last one at the end).</summary>
    private void UpdateActive(bool animate, bool force = false)
    {
        var top = Page.Offset.Y + 40;
        var atEnd = Page.Offset.Y + Page.Viewport.Height >= Page.Extent.Height - 1;
        var index = 0;
        for (var i = 0; i < _sections.Count; i++)
        {
            if (_sections[i].Heading.TranslatePoint(default, Article) is { } point && point.Y <= top)
            {
                index = i;
            }
        }
        if (atEnd && Page.Extent.Height > Page.Viewport.Height)
        {
            index = _sections.Count - 1;
        }
        if (index == _active && !force)
        {
            return;
        }
        _active = index;
        for (var i = 0; i < _sections.Count; i++)
        {
            _sections[i].Entry.Classes.Set("active", i == index);
        }
        var entry = _sections[index].Entry;
        if (entry.Bounds.Height > 0)
        {
            OutlineBar.MoveTo(new Rect(0, entry.Bounds.Y, 2, entry.Bounds.Height), animate && !force);
        }
    }
}
```

```xml

             FilterPlaceholder="Search docs"

        <TextBlock Text="Tidewater docs" />
    </arc:Sidebar.Header>

            <arc:SidebarItem Key="start/introduction" Label="Introduction" />
```

### Sections and nested pages

A `SidebarItem` with child items is a parent. A parent is never selected: choosing it opens or closes its pages, which
hang from a thin guide line. A parent that also needs a landing page should get a child for that page (for example
"Overview" under "Reports"). The `IsExpanded` flag of a parent is two-way. Set `IsCollapsible` on a `SidebarSection`
with a `Header` to let people fold the whole section away; its title then ends in a small chevron, and its own
`IsExpanded` is two-way too. A section that is not collapsible always shows its pages. Only one level of nesting is
shown.

`IsEnabled="False"` dims a page and the arrow keys skip it. A disabled parent cannot be opened either. Each item can
also carry a `Tag` and a `Command` with a `CommandParameter`.

### Counts, unread dots, actions and icons

`Badge` puts a short count at the end of a row, such as "12" for unread messages; a `null` badge shows nothing.
`IsUnread="True"` shows a small accent dot there instead, makes the label stronger and adds "unread" to the row's
accessible name. Use a count when the number matters and the dot when "something is new" is enough. On the rail both
become a dot on the icon.

`Icon` takes a 24 by 24 Lucide geometry, such as an `ArcIcons` glyph, or any control that fits the 16 px icon slot. A
small `Ellipse` makes a colored dot icon that lines up with the glyphs of the other rows. A control icon can sit in one
row only, so create one per item. `TrailingIcon` puts an icon right after the label, in the label's muted color; it
suits a hint such as the chevron of a "More" row.

`IsAction="True"` turns a row into an action: muted and never selected. Choosing it raises `ItemInvoked` and runs its
commands, but `SelectedItem` stays where it was. Use it for "New project" or "More".

```xml
<arc:Sidebar xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:SidebarSection Header="Projects">
        <arc:SidebarItem Key="projects/spring" Label="Spring launch">
            <arc:SidebarItem.Icon>
                <Ellipse Width="8" Height="8" Fill="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Series1}" />
            </arc:SidebarItem.Icon>
        </arc:SidebarItem>
        <arc:SidebarItem Key="projects/partner" Label="Partner kit" IsUnread="True" />
        <arc:SidebarItem Key="projects/new" Label="New project" IsAction="True" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Plus}" />
        <arc:SidebarItem Key="projects/more" Label="More" IsAction="True" TrailingIcon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.ChevronRight}" />
    </arc:SidebarSection>
</arc:Sidebar>
```

### Header, filter and footer

`Header` takes any content: a logo with a two-line title, a workspace switcher, a version chip, a full-width button.
`Footer` sits under a thin separator and takes the signed-in person, a storage meter, or both. Both keep the layout they
have when the sidebar is open and are clipped to the rail, so a logo or an avatar at their leading edge stays visible.
Use the `:collapsed` pseudo-class to fade the rest, as the layouts above do.

`IsFilterVisible` shows the filter box under the header (see "Filter"). The collapse button normally sits at the end of
the header row; `CollapseButtonPlacement="Filter"` puts it beside the filter box instead, as in the Workspace and Docs
layouts. Without a visible filter the button stays in the header row. On the rail it always moves to the top.
`IsCollapseButtonVisible="False"` removes it when the page has its own toggle, as in the app rail and the inbox.

### Selection and routing

`SelectedItem` and `SelectedKey` are two-way and stay in step. `SelectedKey` matches the `Key` of a page and is the
right property to bind to a route, because a route is a string. Setting `SelectedKey` before the pages exist is fine:
the sidebar selects the page once it appears, so a view model can set the route first. A key that matches no page, or
the key of a parent or an action row, selects nothing and keeps its value.

`ItemInvoked` is a routed event that fires every time a page or an action is chosen: by click, by Enter or Space, or
from a menu on the rail. It fires even when the page was already selected, which a binding to `SelectedKey` cannot tell
you. Use it for navigation that must happen on each choice, such as scrolling a page back to the top. After the event
the item's own `Command` runs, then `SelectCommand` with the item as its parameter, each only when it can execute.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.SidebarDataBindingDemo">
    <Grid ColumnDefinitions="Auto,*" ColumnSpacing="24" HorizontalAlignment="Center">
        <Border Height="360"
                CornerRadius="20"
                BorderThickness="1"
                ClipToBounds="True"
                BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Border}">
            <arc:Sidebar x:Name="Nav"
                         BorderThickness="0"
                         IsCollapseButtonVisible="False"
                         SelectedKey="inbox">
                <arc:SidebarSection>
                    <arc:SidebarItem Key="home" Label="Home" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.House}" />
                    <arc:SidebarItem Key="inbox" Label="Inbox" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Inbox}" Badge="5" />
                    <arc:SidebarItem Key="reports" Label="Reports" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.ChartBar}" />
                </arc:SidebarSection>
                <arc:SidebarSection Header="Account">
                    <arc:SidebarItem Key="billing" Label="Billing" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.CreditCard}">
                        <arc:SidebarItem Key="billing/invoices" Label="Invoices" />
                        <arc:SidebarItem Key="billing/plans" Label="Plans" />
                    </arc:SidebarItem>
                    <arc:SidebarItem Key="settings" Label="Settings" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Settings}" />
                </arc:SidebarSection>
            </arc:Sidebar>
        </Border>
        <StackPanel Grid.Column="1" Spacing="14" VerticalAlignment="Center" Width="300">

</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class SidebarDataBindingDemo : UserControl
{
    private readonly List<string> _lines = new();

    public SidebarDataBindingDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        // ItemInvoked fires for every choice, also when the page was already selected (SelectedKey would not change).
        Nav.ItemInvoked += (_, e) =>
        {
            _lines.Insert(0, $"{DateTime.Now:HH:mm:ss}  {e.Item.Label} ({e.Item.Key})");
            if (_lines.Count > 4)
            {
                _lines.RemoveAt(_lines.Count - 1);
            }
            Log.Text = string.Join(Environment.NewLine, _lines);
        };
    }
}
```

```csharp
sidebar.ItemInvoked += (_, e) => router.Navigate(e.Item.Key!);
```

### Binding to a view model

The sidebar has no `ItemsSource`: its sections are XAML content, so the rows are written in XAML or, for data that
changes, added and removed in code. The view model holds the route and the collapsed state; the sidebar binds to them
with two-way bindings and runs a command for each choice.

```csharp
public partial class WorkspaceShellViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    private readonly INavigationService _navigation;

    public WorkspaceShellViewModel(INavigationService navigation) => _navigation = navigation;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private string? _selectedKey = "home";

    [ObservableProperty]
    private bool _isNavigationCollapsed;

    [RelayCommand]
    private void OpenPage(SidebarItem item)
    {
        // Runs on every choice, including a page that is already selected.
        _navigation.Navigate(item.Key!);
    }
}
```

```xml
<arc:Sidebar SelectedKey="{Binding SelectedKey, Mode=TwoWay}"
             IsCollapsed="{Binding IsNavigationCollapsed, Mode=TwoWay}"
             SelectCommand="{Binding OpenPageCommand}"
             Label="Main navigation"
             IsFilterVisible="True" />
```

- `SelectedKey` and `IsCollapsed` are two-way, so a route change from elsewhere in the app (a link in a page, a
  back button) selects the matching row, and the rail button writes back to the view model.
- Run navigation side effects in `SelectCommand` or `ItemInvoked`, not in a handler on `SelectedKey`. The selection
  also changes when the route is set from code, and that is not always a choice a person made.
- Set `IsNavigationCollapsed` from your own window width check when the window narrows; the sidebar does not watch the
  window for you.
- When data drives the menu, build the sections in code and keep a reference to the item whose count changes:

```csharp
var inbox = new SidebarItem { Key = "inbox", Label = "Inbox", Icon = ArcIcons.Inbox };
sidebar.Sections.Add(new SidebarSection
{
    Items = { new SidebarItem { Key = "home", Label = "Home", Icon = ArcIcons.House }, inbox }
});

// The row updates in place when the count changes: no rebuild and no lost focus.
inbox.Badge = unreadCount > 0 ? unreadCount.ToString(CultureInfo.InvariantCulture) : null;
```

### Icon rail

`IsCollapsed` folds the sidebar into a 64 px rail; it is two-way, so a button anywhere in your page can drive it with a
binding or a call to `ToggleCollapsed()`. The collapse button in the sidebar and Cmd+B (Ctrl+B on Windows and Linux)
with focus inside the sidebar do the same, even while the filter has focus.

On the rail every page shows a tooltip on its right with its label. A count or an unread mark becomes a 6 px dot on the
icon, section headings become thin separator lines, the filter becomes the search button that opens the sidebar and
puts the caret in the filter, and a parent opens its pages in a menu to its right. The menu lists the parent's label,
then its pages as radio items: the selected page is checked, disabled pages are disabled, and a count appears as the
shortcut text. A page without an icon shows its first letter.

The header and footer keep the layout they have when the sidebar is open and are clipped to the rail, so a logo or an
avatar at their leading edge stays visible. Use the `:collapsed` pseudo-class to fade the rest, as the layouts do.
While the collapse button is visible, the header gives way to it on the rail.
