### Content guidelines

- **Title**: one line that names the object and the outcome, such as "Invoice inv_2026_0412 was paid". The title is cut
  with an ellipsis, so put the decisive words first. Write the actor's name in an update from a person.
- **Description**: one sentence with the detail a person needs to decide: an amount, a version, a count. It previews
  under the title and shows in full when the row opens.
- **Time**: a short label such as "2m", "40m", "Yesterday" or "Mon". Use the same unit for every item.
- **Labels**: sentence case, with action labels as verb and object ("Mark read", "Clear read").
- **Dismiss** removes the update from this list only. Say so in the product copy when a delete also removes data.

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| New notification! | Priya Shah assigned you Fix checkout totals |
| Error | Payment failed for invoice inv_2026_0412 |
| Click here | View update details |
| Delete | Dismiss |
| Something happened | Deploy to production finished |

### Best practices

**Do**

- Give every item a stable `Id` and keep the same item objects while the list refreshes. Rows are matched by id, so
  the expanded row and the keyboard position survive the refresh.
- Save `ReadChanged` and `Dismissed` to your store. The control changes its in-memory state only, so a reload would
  show the old read state without the handlers.
- Store the record key in `Tag`, so the events give you the record without a lookup by title.
- Use `Warning` for updates that need a decision and `Success` for finished work. The tone icons carry the meaning, so
  keeping each tone for one kind of update keeps the list readable.
- Set `Label` to the product's word for the list ("Activity", "Inbox"); it names the bell and the panel.

**Avoid**

- Action buttons for work that changes data, such as approving a request. The panel offers only "Mark read",
  "Mark unread" and "Dismiss"; link to the record from your own page instead.
- Calling `Open()` on every update. It moves focus into the panel and can interrupt typing in another field.
- Dismissing unread updates on the person's behalf. Dismiss removes the update from the list, so the person loses the
  pending item.
- Using the badge as the only signal for an outage or a failed payment. Show those on the page with `Alert`, where
  people act on them.
- Long titles with several sentences. They are cut to one line, and the rest is only visible in the details.

### Common questions

**Why does Dismiss remove the item from my list?** The control removes the item from `Items`, or from `ItemsSource`
when that is a writable `IList` or `ICollection`, before it raises `Dismissed`. A read-only source keeps the item, and
the control hides it. Delete the record in the `Dismissed` handler when you want the removal to be permanent.

**Why does the badge count differ from my store?** `UnreadCount` counts the items the control shows: the items in
`ItemsSource` (or `Items`) minus any item it hides from a read-only source. Read the count from the control, not from
your own list, so the bell and the panel agree.

**Does clicking a row open the related page?** No. A row only shows or hides its details, and the panel has no link
action. Route people to the record from your own page, using the item's `Tag` value.

**How do I make an actor's photo show?** Set `ActorSource` to an `ImageSource`; in XAML a URL works. Initials show while
the image loads or when it fails.

**Can I change the panel size or position?** No public property sets them. The panel is 424 px wide (or the window
width less 24 px), at most 590 px high, and sits 12 px below the bell. Place the bell where the panel can open downward.

## API reference

### NotificationCenter

A home for updates: a bell with an unread badge that opens a panel of notifications with read state, an All / Unread switch, expandable details and bulk actions ("Mark all read", "Clear read"). Use it when updates need a persistent place instead of a brief toast, and connect the read state to your data store through `IsRead` and the `ReadChanged` and `Dismissed` events. The panel grows out of the bell (6px toward it at scale 0.97, standard 240ms) and leaves in 120ms; counts roll, the summary rises into its new wording, the view highlight glides on the morph spring, rows collapse their height on the smooth spring as they leave (cascading 35ms apart after a bulk action) and settle in with a 4px rise when the panel opens. Escape closes the panel and returns focus to the bell. Ported from Arc's free notification-center block (MIT, Copyright (c) 2026 Elia Kuratli).

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ItemsSource` | `IEnumerable<NotificationItem>?` | `null` | The notifications to show; when set it replaces `Items`. Collection changes are followed. |
| `Label` | `string` | `"Notifications"` | The panel heading and the bell's accessible name. Default "Notifications". |
| `Labels` | `NotificationCenterLabels` | – | Every other word the control shows or announces, with English defaults. |
| `IsOpen` | `bool` | `false` | Whether the panel is open (two-way). |
| `View` | `NotificationCenterView` | `All` | Which notifications the panel lists: All (default) or Unread (two-way). |
| `UnreadCount` | `int` | – | *Read-only.* How many notifications are unread. |
| `ReadCount` | `int` | – | *Read-only.* How many notifications are read. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ReadChanged` | `NotificationReadChangedEventArgs` | Raised when a notification is marked read or unread; "Mark all read" raises it once per notification. |
| `Dismissed` | `NotificationDismissedEventArgs` | Raised when a notification is dismissed; "Clear read" raises it once per notification. |

Pseudo-classes: `:open`, `:has-unread`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

### NotificationItem

One update in a `NotificationCenter`: a title, an optional description, a time label and its read state. An update from a person shows their `Avatar`; a system update shows an icon for its `Tone`.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Id` | `string` | `""` | Stable id. Rows are matched by id, so a refreshed list with new objects keeps its rows in place. |
| `Title` | `string` | `""` | The headline, one line (cut with an ellipsis). |
| `Description` | `string?` | `null` | The body: previewed on one line under the title and shown in full when the row is expanded. |
| `Time` | `string` | `""` | The time as display text, such as "2m" or "Yesterday". |
| `IsRead` | `bool` | `false` | Whether the update has been read (two-way); the notification center changes it when you mark it. |
| `Tone` | `NotificationTone` | `Info` | The icon of an update without an actor: Info (default), Success or Warning. |
| `ActorName` | `string?` | `null` | The person behind the update; when set, the row shows their avatar instead of the tone icon. |
| `ActorSource` | `ImageSource?` | `null` | The actor's photo (a URL works in XAML); initials show while it loads or when it fails. |
| `Tag` | `object?` | `null` | Any value you want back in the events, such as the record id in your store. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### NotificationCenterLabels

`NotificationCenterLabels` holds every word the control shows or announces except `Label`, each with Arc's English
default. Assign a new instance to `NotificationCenter.Labels`.

| Property | Default | Where it shows |
|---|---|---|
| `Trigger` (function of label and unread count) | "Notifications, 3 unread" | Accessible name of the bell |
| `Summary` (function of unread count) | "3 updates waiting for you", "You’re all caught up" | Line under the heading |
| `Close` | "Close notifications" | Accessible name of the close button |
| `ViewSwitch` | "Show notifications" | Accessible name of the All / Unread switch |
| `All` / `Unread` | "All" / "Unread" | View buttons |
| `AllList` / `UnreadList` | "All notifications" / "Unread notifications" | Accessible names of the lists |
| `MarkAllRead` | "Mark all read" | Bulk action in the toolbar |
| `UnreadState` | "unread" | Added to an unread row's accessible name |
| `ShowDetails` / `HideDetails` | "Show details" / "Hide details" | Ends a row's accessible name |
| `FromActor` (function of name) | "From Mia Chen" | Preview of an update from a person without a description |
| `ViewDetails` | "View update details" | Preview of a system update without a description |
| `SharedUpdate` (function of name) | "Mia Chen shared an update with you." | Details of an update from a person without a description |
| `ReadyToReview` | "This update is ready to review." | Details of a system update without a description |
| `MarkRead` / `MarkUnread` | "Mark read" / "Mark unread" | Row action for the read state |
| `Dismiss` | "Dismiss" | Row action that removes the update |
| `EmptyTitle` / `EmptyDescription` | "All clear" / "New updates will appear here." | Empty All view |
| `UnreadEmptyTitle` / `UnreadEmptyDescription` | "Nothing unread" / "You’ve seen every update." | Empty Unread view |
| `ViewAll` | "View all updates" | Link from an empty Unread view to the All view |
| `ReadCount` | "{0} read" | Footer count; `{0}` is the rolling number |
| `ClearRead` | "Clear read" | Footer action that dismisses the read updates |

## Accessibility

- The bell is a button named by `Label` and the unread count, such as "Notifications, 3 unread". It reports whether the
  panel is expanded.
- Opening the panel moves focus to its close button. Tab moves through close, All and Unread, "Mark all read", the
  rows, the open row's buttons and "Clear read", and wraps around inside the panel.
- Escape and the close button close the panel and return focus to the bell.
- All and Unread are toggle buttons. Each row is a button named by its title and state, such as "Deploy finished,
  unread. Show details", and reports whether it is expanded.
- After you mark a row read in the Unread view, or dismiss a row, focus moves to the next row, then the previous one,
  then the Unread button. After "Mark all read" focus returns to the current view button.
- The summary under the heading is a polite live region, so the new count is read out.
- `Label` names both the bell and the panel heading, so choose a word that makes sense on its own, such as "Activity"
  or "Inbox".

### Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Enter` or `Space` on the bell | Opens the panel and moves focus to its close button |
| `Enter` or `Space` on the bell while open | Closes the panel and returns focus to the bell |
| `Escape` | Closes the panel and returns focus to the bell |
| `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` | Moves through close, All, Unread, "Mark all read", the rows, the open row's buttons and "Clear read" |
| `Enter` or `Space` on All or Unread | Switches the view; the expanded row closes |
| `Enter` or `Space` on a row title | Shows or hides the row's details; only one row stays open |
| `Enter` or `Space` on "Mark read", "Mark unread" or "Dismiss" | Changes the row, then moves focus as described under Accessibility |
| `Enter` or `Space` on "Mark all read" | Marks every unread update read; focus returns to the current view button |
| `Enter` or `Space` on "Clear read" | Dismisses every read update; focus moves to the All button |

## Motion

- The panel grows out of the bell: it starts 6 pixels toward the bell at scale 0.97 and fades in over 240 ms. It
  leaves in 120 ms at half the distance and scale 0.98.
- The bell tips while the panel is open. The badge pops in and out, and its number rolls up or down.
- Rows settle in 4 pixels from below, 35 ms apart, when the panel opens or a view adds them. Leaving rows fade and
  close their height on a smooth spring. After a bulk action they leave one after another, at most 200 ms apart from
  the first.
- The counts roll, the summary rises into its new wording, and the All and Unread highlight glides between the
  buttons. Details, the footer and the empty state open and close their height on the same spring.
- Reduced motion keeps only short fades of 120 ms, with no movement, scaling or blur. The panel shows and hides at
  once. Off applies every change at once.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| Panel opens | Grows out of the bell, 6 px and scale 0.97, over 240 ms | Shown at once | Immediate |
| Panel closes | Leaves in 120 ms at half the distance | Hidden at once | Immediate |
| Rows enter | Rise 4 px and fade in, 35 ms apart | Short fade, no movement | Immediate |
| Rows leave after a bulk action | Height collapses on the smooth spring, cascading up to 200 ms | Short fade, no collapse | Immediate |
| Bell while open | Tips, then returns when the panel closes | Stays upright | Immediate |
| Unread badge | Pops in and out; the number rolls | Short fade | Immediate |
| View highlight | Glides between All and Unread | Short fade | Immediate |

## Related

- `Toast` for a short message that goes away by itself.
- `Popover` for other content anchored to a button.
- `Badge` for a count or a status on another control.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `Toast` / `ToastStack` | A short result must appear once and go away without action |
| `Alert` | A problem on the current page must stay visible until it is fixed |
| `Popover` | Other content must be anchored to a button, such as a filter form |
| `Badge` | A count or a status sits on another control, and no list of updates is needed |
| `Timeline` | The events of one record must read in order |
| `ChatThread` | People reply to each other in a conversation |

# Empty states

> Four empty states in one illustration whose shapes morph between scenes as you switch tabs.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc.Blocks`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc.Blocks --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/blocks/empty-states

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.EmptyStatesPreviewDemo">
    <!-- Arc's four scenes and copy (Items left empty). The code-behind plays the work each action stands for. -->
    <arc:EmptyStates x:Name="States" ActionInvoked="OnActionInvoked" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class EmptyStatesPreviewDemo : UserControl
{
    private int _run;

    public EmptyStatesPreviewDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
    }

    // Arc's preview simulation: filters clear and come back at once; a retry, a mail check and a page search load for a
    // moment and then finish. A finished retry or search goes back to the empty state on the next press; the inbox
    // always checks again.
    private async void OnActionInvoked(object? sender, EmptyStatesActionEventArgs e)
    {
        var scene = e.Item.Scene;
        if (scene == EmptyStatesScene.NoResults || (e.Phase == EmptyStatesPhase.Done && scene != EmptyStatesScene.CaughtUp))
        {
            States.Phase = e.Phase == EmptyStatesPhase.Idle ? EmptyStatesPhase.Done : EmptyStatesPhase.Idle;
            return;
        }
        var run = ++_run;
        States.Phase = EmptyStatesPhase.Loading;
        await Task.Delay(scene switch
        {
            EmptyStatesScene.Offline => 1400,
            EmptyStatesScene.CaughtUp => 1100,
            _ => 1200
        });
        // Switching tabs meanwhile puts the block back to Idle; only finish the run that is still loading.
        if (run == _run && States.SelectedItem == e.Item && States.Phase == EmptyStatesPhase.Loading)
        {
            States.Phase = EmptyStatesPhase.Done;
        }
    }
}
```

## When to use

An empty state tells people why a view has no content and what they can do next. `EmptyStates` covers the four
situations an application meets most often (a search with no matches, a lost connection, a cleared queue and a missing
page) in one block, with a drawing and copy for each. Place it where the empty view is a whole page or panel and the
next step may take a moment, because the block shows the work in progress and the result in the same place.

- **A filtered invoice list with no matches**: a billing console where the status and month filters hide every
  invoice. The `NoResults` scene names the cause in the title and offers one action, such as showing the paid invoices.
- **A connection that drops in an offline-capable editor**: a field app keeps edits on the device. The `Offline` scene
  says the edits are safe and offers a retry, which shows the connection attempt and then the result.
- **A ticket or approval queue that is clear**: a support inbox or a review queue with nothing left to read. The
  `CaughtUp` scene confirms the state, and its action checks again for new items.
- **A link to a page that moved**: a help centre or a CRM with saved links to projects that were archived. The
  `NotFound` scene explains the move and offers a search for the new location.
- **A design review or onboarding guide**: a page that shows the four states side by side so the team can check their
  copy and drawings in one place.

## When not to use

- **One empty list with an icon and one button**: use `EmptyState`. It is a single state with no tabs and no phases, so
  it is lighter on a dense page.
- **Content that is still loading**: use `Skeleton`. It shows the shape of the content that will arrive; an empty state
  would tell people there is nothing when something is on its way.
- **An error on a page that already shows content**: use `Alert`, which sits beside the content and leaves it readable.
- **A confirmation after a save or a send**: use `Toast`, which says what happened and goes away on its own.

## Usage

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:EmptyStates Label="Workspace" />
</UserControl>
```

`EmptyStates` derives from `TemplatedControl`. Its tabs are `EmptyStatesItem` objects, its drawing is a control that
animates between scenes, and its action is a button. The block does no work of its own. The app
handles `ActionInvoked` (or runs `ActionCommand`), does the work, and moves `Phase` to `Loading` and then `Done` or
back to `Idle`. The drawing and the copy follow `Phase` and the selected tab.

### Anatomy

1. **Tab row** (`Items`): one tab per `EmptyStatesItem`, showing its `Header`. The tabs sit in a 30 px track with a 3 px
   inset and a 12 px corner radius. The tabs share the row equally up to 460 px, and a tab never gets narrower than its
   label. With one item the row is hidden. The selected tab has the surface color, a 1 px border and a resting shadow.
2. **Drawing** (`Scene`): a 320 by 216 logical canvas scaled to at most 360 px wide. Ten shapes and the 1.5 px strokes
   do not scale with the drawing. The colors come from the theme tokens: the surface and foreground colors for the main
   shape, the muted text color for the outlines and the strong border color for the supporting shapes.
3. **Title** (`Title`, `DoneTitle`): the large text size, medium weight. At 560 px wide or more the block uses the
   extra-large size.
4. **Description** (`Description`, `DoneDescription`, `LoadingDescription`): secondary text in the small size, up to
   about 350 px wide, so long sentences wrap into more lines.
5. **Action button** (`ActionLabel`, `DoneActionLabel`): a small primary button. While `Phase` is `Loading` it shows a
   spinner and ignores presses.
6. **Card**: a 1 px border, a 20 px corner radius and the surface color. The padding grows with the block's width, from
   16 to 40 px on the sides and 16 to 48 px at the top and bottom. The gaps between the parts are 20 to 32 px.

### Scenes and copy

Each `EmptyStatesItem` is one tab. `Scene` picks the drawing, and the copy properties set the text for each phase. Text
you leave out uses Arc's copy for that scene, so a tab can set only its header and action label.

| Scene | Drawing | Default header | Default title |
|---|---|---|---|
| `NoResults` | A magnifier over empty rows | No results | No results for “Q3 roadmap” |
| `Offline` | A cloud joined to a device by a broken line | Offline | You are offline |
| `CaughtUp` | A stacked inbox with a check mark | Caught up | All caught up |
| `NotFound` | A folded map whose route ends in a cross | Not found | Page not found |

Set `Header` on every tab when there are several. The header is the only label in the tab row, and people use it to
decide which state they are looking at. Choose the scene by the cause, not by the look you like: `NoResults` after a
filter, `Offline` when the connection is lost, `NotFound` for a broken link, and `CaughtUp` when nothing is left to do.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.EmptyStatesCustomItemsDemo">
    <!-- Two scenes with their own copy. Text left out falls back to Arc's copy for the scene. -->
    <arc:EmptyStates x:Name="States" Label="Invoices" ActionInvoked="OnActionInvoked">
        <arc:EmptyStatesItem Scene="NoResults"
                             Header="Search"
                             Title="No invoices match “March”"
                             Description="The status filter hides paid invoices."
                             ActionLabel="Show paid invoices"
                             DoneTitle="8 invoices from March"
                             DoneDescription="Showing paid and unpaid invoices."
                             DoneActionLabel="Hide paid invoices" />
        <arc:EmptyStatesItem Scene="CaughtUp"
                             Header="Requests"
                             Title="No open requests"
                             Description="Every request has an owner. New ones show up here first."
                             ActionLabel="Refresh"
                             LoadingDescription="Looking for new requests…"
                             DoneTitle="Still no open requests"
                             DoneDescription="Checked a moment ago."
                             DoneActionLabel="Refresh again" />
    </arc:EmptyStates>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class EmptyStatesCustomItemsDemo : UserControl
{
    public EmptyStatesCustomItemsDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
    }

    private async void OnActionInvoked(object? sender, EmptyStatesActionEventArgs e)
    {
        if (e.Item.Scene == EmptyStatesScene.NoResults)
        {
            // Showing or hiding paid invoices is instant: toggle between the two phases.
            States.Phase = e.Phase == EmptyStatesPhase.Idle ? EmptyStatesPhase.Done : EmptyStatesPhase.Idle;
            return;
        }
        States.Phase = EmptyStatesPhase.Loading;
        await Task.Delay(900);
        if (States.SelectedItem == e.Item && States.Phase == EmptyStatesPhase.Loading)
        {
            States.Phase = EmptyStatesPhase.Done;
        }
    }
}
```

```xml
<arc:EmptyStates>
    <arc:EmptyStatesItem Scene="Offline"
                         Title="Sync is paused"
                         ActionLabel="Resume sync" />
    <arc:EmptyStatesItem Scene="NotFound" />
</arc:EmptyStates>
```

`Items` is an `AvaloniaList<EmptyStatesItem>`, not an `ItemsSource`. Add the tabs in XAML or with `Items.Add` and
`Items.Remove` in code. The block keeps the selection on an item of the list: when the selected item is removed, the
selection moves to a valid index, and a selection made before the items arrive is kept.

### Actions and phases

Pressing the action button raises `ActionInvoked` with the selected item and the phase the button was pressed in, then
runs `ActionCommand` with the same event arguments. Presses are ignored while the phase is `Loading`, so the app never
receives a second press for the same work.

| Phase | Title shown | Description shown | Button |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Idle` | `Title` (or the scene's copy) | `Description` | `ActionLabel` |
| `Loading` | The title of the phase it started from | `LoadingDescription` if set, otherwise the current description | Spinner, presses ignored |
| `Done` | `DoneTitle` | `DoneDescription` | `DoneActionLabel` |

Set `Phase` to `Loading` while the work runs. A `Loading` that started from `Done` keeps the done title, so the copy does
not jump back to the empty state in the middle of an action. Set `Done` when the work succeeded, or `Idle` when it
failed. Use `Done` to show a result the person can act on (for example, "Hide paid invoices") and `Idle` to offer the
action again.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.EmptyStatesAsyncRetryDemo">
    <!-- One item: no tab row. The command in the code-behind retries a connection that fails the first time. -->
    <arc:EmptyStates x:Name="States" Label="Connection">
        <arc:EmptyStatesItem Scene="Offline"
                             Title="Can’t reach the server"
                             Description="Your changes are saved here and upload when the connection is back."
                             ActionLabel="Retry"
                             LoadingDescription="Connecting to api.example.com…"
                             DoneTitle="Connected"
                             DoneDescription="All changes are uploaded."
                             DoneActionLabel="Disconnect" />
    </arc:EmptyStates>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using System.Windows.Input;
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class EmptyStatesAsyncRetryDemo : UserControl
{
    private const string Saved = "Your changes are saved here and upload when the connection is back.";
    private int _attempts;

    public EmptyStatesAsyncRetryDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        States.ActionCommand = new AsyncCommand(RunAsync);
    }

    private async Task RunAsync(EmptyStatesActionEventArgs e)
    {
        var connection = e.Item;
        if (e.Phase == EmptyStatesPhase.Done)
        {
            // "Disconnect": back to the empty state for another round.
            _attempts = 0;
            connection.Description = Saved;
            States.Phase = EmptyStatesPhase.Idle;
            return;
        }
        States.Phase = EmptyStatesPhase.Loading;
        await Task.Delay(1500);
        if (++_attempts == 1)
        {
            // The first attempt fails. Change the copy while it still shows the loading line, then go back to Idle.
            connection.Description = "Still no connection. Check your network and try again.";
            States.Phase = EmptyStatesPhase.Idle;
            return;
        }
        States.Phase = EmptyStatesPhase.Done;
    }

    /// <summary>A command that runs one task at a time.</summary>
    private sealed class AsyncCommand(Func<EmptyStatesActionEventArgs, Task> run) : ICommand
    {
        private bool _running;

        public event EventHandler? CanExecuteChanged;

        public bool CanExecute(object? parameter) => !_running && parameter is EmptyStatesActionEventArgs;

        public async void Execute(object? parameter)
        {
            if (!CanExecute(parameter))
            {
                return;
            }
            _running = true;
            CanExecuteChanged?.Invoke(this, EventArgs.Empty);
            try
            {
                await run((EmptyStatesActionEventArgs)parameter!);
            }
            finally
            {
                _running = false;
                CanExecuteChanged?.Invoke(this, EventArgs.Empty);
            }
        }
    }
}
```

```csharp
states.ActionInvoked += async (_, e) =>
{
    if (e.Phase == EmptyStatesPhase.Done)
    {
        states.Phase = EmptyStatesPhase.Idle;
        return;
    }
    states.Phase = EmptyStatesPhase.Loading;
    var ok = await sync.RetryAsync();
    states.Phase = ok ? EmptyStatesPhase.Done : EmptyStatesPhase.Idle;
};
```

To change the copy after a failed attempt, set the item's `Description` while the phase is still `Loading`. The new
text then appears together with the return to `Idle`. The demo does this: its first attempt fails, and the description
changes to a line that tells the person what to check.

Every scene has its own default `LoadingDescription`, such as "Reaching sync.northwind.example…" for `Offline`. The
`NoResults` scene has none, so its description stays on screen while the search runs. Set `LoadingDescription` to
an empty string to keep the description on any scene.

### Binding to a view model

`EmptyStates` has no items binding, so its tabs are fixed in XAML or code. Its state is bindable: `SelectedIndex`,
`SelectedItem` and `Phase` are two-way, and `ActionCommand` is one-way. The view model owns the phase and the work, and
the block shows it.

```csharp
using CommunityToolkit.Mvvm.ComponentModel;
using CommunityToolkit.Mvvm.Input;
using TKCode.Arc;

public partial class InvoiceEmptyStateViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    private readonly IInvoiceService _invoices;

    public InvoiceEmptyStateViewModel(IInvoiceService invoices)
    {
        _invoices = invoices;
    }

    [ObservableProperty]
    private EmptyStatesPhase _phase = EmptyStatesPhase.Idle;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private int _selectedIndex;

    [RelayCommand]
    private async Task RunActionAsync(EmptyStatesActionEventArgs? args)
    {
        if (args is null)
        {
            return;
        }
        if (args.Phase == EmptyStatesPhase.Done)
        {
            Phase = EmptyStatesPhase.Idle;
            return;
        }
        Phase = EmptyStatesPhase.Loading;
        var result = await _invoices.RefreshAsync();
        Phase = result.IsSuccess ? EmptyStatesPhase.Done : EmptyStatesPhase.Idle;
    }
}
```

```xml
<arc:EmptyStates SelectedIndex="{Binding SelectedIndex, Mode=TwoWay}"
                 Phase="{Binding Phase, Mode=TwoWay}"
                 ActionCommand="{Binding RunActionCommand}"
                 Label="Invoices" />
```

- Two-way `Phase` means the block writes it back. Choosing another tab sets `Phase` to `Idle`, so the view model sees
  that change through its own `Phase` property and can drop any result it was holding.
- Compiled bindings need `x:DataType` on the view. The examples here leave it out for brevity.

### Narrow layouts

The block follows its own width, not the window's width. At 420 px or less the tabs get smaller text and tighter
padding. From 560 px the title uses the larger size. A label that does not fit keeps its width, and the tab row slides
to keep the selected tab in view.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.EmptyStatesNarrowDemo">
    <!-- 360 wide: smaller tabs, tighter padding and the smaller title. Phase starts at Done. -->
    <arc:EmptyStates Width="360" SelectedIndex="3" Phase="Done" HorizontalAlignment="Center" />
</UserControl>
```

### Using motion with restraint

The morph between scenes is the block's signature, and it works best where the state change is the news: a filter was
cleared, a connection came back, a result arrived. Let the drawing carry that change and keep the copy short.

- Use the scene change for a state the person caused (a tab, a filter, a retry). A drawing that morphs when a
  background refresh runs every few seconds draws the eye away from the list it belongs to.
- Keep the `Loading` phase short. The drawing moves on each phase change, so a spinner that runs for minutes gives
  the person a moving picture and no information; show a progress indicator in the surrounding page for long work.
- Under reduced motion the drawing crossfades instead of morphing, so the change stays visible without travel. The
  mouse tilt is off in reduced motion and is disabled entirely when motion is off.

### Example: invoices with three empty states

A billing console's invoice page has three tabs for the states the team meets most often. The first tab is selected: a
month filter hides every invoice, so the title names the month and the action clears the paid-invoice filter. The
second tab shows the sync state, and the third shows reminders that are all scheduled. Each tab sets its own header,
so the tab row reads as three short labels. The copy names real objects (the month, the customer) because people
look for the cause in the title first.

![Three empty states on an invoice page with the no results tab selected](https://docs.tkcode.si/shots/Docs/Blocks/EmptyStates/images/InvoicesEmptyStates.webp)

```xml
<arc:EmptyStates Width="640"
                 Label="Invoices"
                 TabListLabel="Invoice empty states">
    <arc:EmptyStatesItem Scene="NoResults"
                         Header="Search"
                         Title="No invoices match “March 2026”"
                         Description="The status filter hides 14 paid invoices."
                         ActionLabel="Show paid invoices"
                         DoneTitle="26 invoices from March 2026"
                         DoneDescription="Paid and unpaid invoices are shown."
                         DoneActionLabel="Hide paid invoices" />
    <arc:EmptyStatesItem Scene="Offline"
                         Header="Sync"
                         Title="Invoices may be out of date"
                         Description="Edits are saved here and sync when you reconnect."
                         ActionLabel="Try again" />
    <arc:EmptyStatesItem Scene="CaughtUp"
                         Header="Reminders"
                         Title="No reminders due"
                         Description="Every overdue invoice has a reminder this week."
                         ActionLabel="Check again" />
</arc:EmptyStates>
```

### Content guidelines

- **Title**: say what is true and name the object or the filter: "No invoices match “March 2026”", not "No data".
  Sentence case, no exclamation mark.
- **Description**: one or two sentences about the cause and the consequence: "Edits are saved here and sync when you
  reconnect." Keep it within the block's description width of about 350 px.
- **Action label**: a verb and an object, the same as a button elsewhere in the app: "Show paid invoices", "Try again".
  Use "Try again" only when the same action can succeed next time.
- **Done copy**: say what changed, with the new count or the new state: "26 invoices from March 2026". A result that
  only says "Success" tells the person nothing about what to check.
- **Loading copy**: say what is happening now, in present tense, with an ellipsis: "Connecting to api.example.com…".

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| No data | No invoices match “March 2026” |
| Error | You are offline |
| Nothing here | All caught up |
| Click here | Show paid invoices |
| Success | 26 invoices from March 2026 |

### Best practices

**Do**

- Match the scene to the cause. People read the drawing before the title; a `NotFound` drawing on a filter that hid the
  results sends them to the wrong fix.
- Set `Header` on every tab. The header is the only label in the tab row, so a tab named "Tab 2" tells the person
  nothing.
- Resolve every `Loading` to `Done` or `Idle`. Presses are ignored while `Loading`, so a phase that never resolves
  leaves the button stuck for the person.
- Write the `Done` copy as the outcome, so the person can read what changed without opening the list.
- Use `Done` for a result that has its own next step ("Hide paid invoices") and `Idle` when the action can run again.

**Avoid**

- A single empty list. Use `EmptyState`: one state, one button, no phases, and no tab row to explain.
- A destructive action as the empty state's button. `ActionInvoked` fires on the press without a confirmation, so a
  "Delete all drafts" button here runs at once. Put destructive actions behind a dialog.
- Treating the tabs as data. The block shows scenes and copy only. It does not filter, fetch or count anything, so the
  app must set `Phase` from its own results.
- Long descriptions. The copy is limited to about 350 px, so a paragraph wraps into a tall block that moves the page
  below it. Keep each description to one or two sentences.
- Changing the drawing for decoration. A scene should match the state the person is in; a "CaughtUp" drawing on an
  error suggests the error is resolved.

### Common questions

**Why does the button ignore my press?** While `Phase` is `Loading`, the block ignores presses of the action button and
does not raise `ActionInvoked` or run `ActionCommand`. Set `Phase` to `Done` or `Idle` when the work finishes.

**Why does the description stay the same while loading?** `LoadingDescription` replaces the description only when it has
text. The `Offline`, `CaughtUp` and `NotFound` scenes have a default loading line; `NoResults` has none, so the
description stays. Set `LoadingDescription` on the item to choose the line.

**Does switching tabs keep the action state?** No. Choosing another tab puts `Phase` back to `Idle`, and the new tab shows
its own `Idle` copy. To open a tab on a result, set `SelectedIndex` and `Phase` together, as in the narrow example:
`<arc:EmptyStates SelectedIndex="1" Phase="Done" />`.

**How do I add or remove a tab at run time?** Change `Items` (`Items.Add` or `Items.Remove`). The tabs follow the list,
and the selection is kept on the same item or moved to a valid index when the selected item goes away.

## API reference

### EmptyStates

Four empty states in one illustration whose shapes morph between scenes as you switch tabs. Each `EmptyStatesItem` is a tab with a scene (no results, offline, caught up, not found) and its copy; every shape of the drawing travels to its new position, size, radius, rotation and color on a spring, outlines morph point by point and line accents draw in a beat later. The primary action raises `ActionInvoked` (and runs `ActionCommand`); the app does the work and moves `Phase` to Loading and then Done, and the drawing and copy follow. With no items the block shows Arc's four scenes and copy.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Items` | `AvaloniaList<EmptyStatesItem>` | – | *Read-only.* The tabs, in order. Empty (the default) shows Arc's four scenes with Arc's copy. |
| `SelectedIndex` | `int` | `0` | The index of the selected tab (two way). |
| `SelectedItem` | `EmptyStatesItem?` | `null` | The selected item (two way). Choosing another item puts `Phase` back to Idle. |
| `Phase` | `EmptyStatesPhase` | `Idle` | Where the selected item's action stands: Idle, Loading or Done (two way). Switching tabs resets it to Idle. |
| `Label` | `string` | `"Empty states"` | The accessible name of the region. |
| `TabListLabel` | `string` | `"Empty state"` | The accessible name of the tab list. |
| `ActionCommand` | `ICommand?` | `null` | Runs when the action is pressed, after `ActionInvoked`; its parameter is the event arguments. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ActionInvoked` | `EmptyStatesActionEventArgs` | The action of the selected item was pressed (Idle or Done). Do the work and set `Phase`. |

Pseudo-classes: `:narrow`, `:wide`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

### EmptyStatesItem

One tab of an `EmptyStates` block: the scene its illustration shows and its copy for each phase. Text left null uses Arc's copy for `Scene`.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Scene` | `EmptyStatesScene` | `NoResults` | The illustration: NoResults, Offline, CaughtUp or NotFound. |
| `Header` | `string?` | `null` | The tab label. Null uses Arc's label for the scene ("No results", "Offline", "Caught up", "Not found"). |
| `Title` | `string?` | `null` | The title in the Idle phase. Null uses Arc's copy for the scene. |
| `Description` | `string?` | `null` | The description in the Idle phase. Null uses Arc's copy for the scene. |
| `ActionLabel` | `string?` | `null` | The button label in the Idle phase. Null uses Arc's copy for the scene. |
| `DoneTitle` | `string?` | `null` | The title in the Done phase. Null uses Arc's copy for the scene. |
| `DoneDescription` | `string?` | `null` | The description in the Done phase. Null uses Arc's copy for the scene. |
| `DoneActionLabel` | `string?` | `null` | The button label in the Done phase. Null uses Arc's copy for the scene. |
| `LoadingDescription` | `string?` | `null` | The description while Loading; the title and button label stay those of the phase the action started from. Null uses Arc's copy for the scene; an empty text keeps the description of that phase. |
| `IllustrationLabel` | `string?` | `null` | The accessible description of the illustration in the Idle phase. Null uses Arc's description of the drawing. |
| `LoadingIllustrationLabel` | `string?` | `null` | The accessible description of the illustration while Loading. Null uses Arc's description of the drawing. |
| `DoneIllustrationLabel` | `string?` | `null` | The accessible description of the illustration in the Done phase. Null uses Arc's description of the drawing. |
| `Tag` | `object?` | `null` | Any value you want back in `ActionInvoked`. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

## Accessibility

- The block is a region named by `Label`. The tab row is a tab list named by `TabListLabel`, and each tab reports
  whether it is selected.
- Only the selected tab is a Tab stop. ArrowLeft and ArrowRight move between tabs and wrap around. Home and End go to
  the first and last tab. Moving selects the tab.
- Each tab is named by its header and reports its position among the tabs, so a screen reader reads "Sync, 2 of 3".
- The drawing is an image named after what it shows, such as "A cloud joined to a device by a broken line". Set
  `IllustrationLabel`, `LoadingIllustrationLabel` and `DoneIllustrationLabel` to name it in another language.
- After each phase change the new title and description, or the loading text, are announced politely. Switching tabs
  clears the last announcement, so an old result is not read again.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` | Enter or leave the tab row (the selected tab), and move to the action button after it |
| `Left` / `Right` | Select and focus the previous or next tab; wraps at the ends |
| `Home` / `End` | Select and focus the first or last tab |
| `Enter` / `Space` | Select the focused tab, as for any button |

## Motion

- Switching tabs moves every shape of the drawing to the next scene on a spring. Outlines morph point by point and
  lines draw in a little later. Colors cross over in 480 ms.
- A phase change nudges the same shapes with shorter delays.
- The old copy lifts away with a blur while the new title and description rise in. The copy height springs to fit,
  so the button does not jump. The tab highlight glides to the selected tab.
- Under a mouse the layers of the drawing tilt slightly toward the pointer.
- Reduced motion crossfades the old drawing into the new one and fades the copy. Off switches at once.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| The scene changes (another tab) | Shapes spring to the new positions, sizes and colors; outlines morph; lines draw a beat later | The old drawing crossfades into the new one | Immediate |
| The phase changes | Shapes move with shorter delays | The drawing crossfades | Immediate |
| The copy changes | The old copy lifts up and blurs out; the new copy rises from below through a blur; the height springs to fit | The copy fades | Immediate |
| The pointer moves over the drawing | The layers tilt slightly toward the pointer | No tilt | No tilt |

## Related

- `EmptyState` for a single empty list with an icon, a message and an action.
- `Skeleton` while content is loading.
- `Alert` for an error on a page that already shows content.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `EmptyState` | One list or panel is empty, and one message and one action explain it |
| `Skeleton` | The content is loading and its shape is known |
| `Alert` | An error or warning concerns content that is still on the page |
| `Toast` | A short confirmation follows a save or a send and needs no action |
| `Tabs` | The person switches between sections of the page that all have content |
| `SearchResults` | A search returns results with snippets and filters, and the empty result is one of its states |

# Search results

> A workspace search page with a suggestions popup, filters whose counts follow the query, a date range, sorting, removable filter chips, highlighted results and a detail sheet.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc.Blocks`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc.Blocks --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/blocks/search-results

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.SearchResultsPreviewDemo">
    <arc:SearchResults x:Name="Search"
                       Height="760"
                       Label="Search the workspace"
                       PlaceholderText="Search docs, people and files"
                       Query="launch"
                       SortOrder="Newest">
        <arc:SearchResults.Filters>
            <arc:SearchValueFilter Key="kind" Title="Type">
                <arc:SearchFilterValue Value="Docs" />
                <arc:SearchFilterValue Value="People" IsSelected="True" />
                <arc:SearchFilterValue Value="Files" />
            </arc:SearchValueFilter>
            <arc:SearchValueFilter Key="team" Title="Team">
                <arc:SearchFilterValue Value="Support" />
                <arc:SearchFilterValue Value="Design" />
                <arc:SearchFilterValue Value="Engineering" />
                <arc:SearchFilterValue Value="Growth" />
                <arc:SearchFilterValue Value="Operations" />
                <arc:SearchFilterValue Value="Finance" />
            </arc:SearchValueFilter>
            <arc:SearchDateFilter Key="edited" Title="Edited" AppliesTo="Docs, Files" />
        </arc:SearchResults.Filters>
    </arc:SearchResults>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Media;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class SearchResultsPreviewDemo : UserControl
{
    public SearchResultsPreviewDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Search.Recent.AddRange(["launch", "rollback", "pricing copy", "Imani"]);
        Search.Suggestions = ["release notes", "budget model", "press kit", "support rota"];
        Search.ItemsSource = Workspace();
        // The control only shows how long a search took; the app measures it. Here the time is made up.
        Search.SearchChanged += (_, _) => Search.Elapsed = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(0.06 + Math.Abs(Search.Query.GetHashCode() % 17) / 100.0);
        Search.Elapsed = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(0.12);
        Search.DetailActionInvoked += OnDetailAction;
    }

    private void OnDetailAction(object? sender, SearchResultActionEventArgs e)
    {
        // "Open" would navigate in a real app; the demo just closes the detail.
        if (e.Action == SearchResultAction.Open)
        {
            Search.CloseDetail();
        }
    }

    private static DateTimeOffset Day(int year, int month, int day) => new(year, month, day, 9, 0, 0, TimeSpan.Zero);

    private static List<SearchResultItem> Workspace() =>
    [

    private static SearchResultItem Doc(string id, string title, string location, string team, DateTimeOffset date, string author, string length,
                                        string snippet, string body)
        => WithDetails(new SearchResultItem
        {
            Id = id,
            Title = title,
            Kind = "Docs",
            KindLabel = "Doc",
            Location = location,
            Snippet = snippet,
            Body = body,
            Date = date,
            Icon = ArcIcons.FileText,
            Url = $"https://tidewater.example/docs/{id}"
        }, team, author, length, date);

    private static SearchResultItem File(string id, string title, string location, string team, DateTimeOffset date, string author, string size,
                                         Geometry icon, string snippet)
        => WithDetails(new SearchResultItem
        {
            Id = id,
            Title = title,
            Kind = "Files",
            KindLabel = "File",
            Location = location,
            Snippet = snippet,
            Body = snippet,
            Date = date,
            Icon = icon,
            Url = $"https://tidewater.example/files/{id}"
        }, team, author, size, date, "Size");

    private static SearchResultItem WithDetails(SearchResultItem item, string team, string author, string length, DateTimeOffset date, string lengthLabel = "Length")
    {
        item.Attributes["team"] = team;
        item.Details.Add(new SearchResultDetail { Label = "Team", Value = team });
        item.Details.Add(new SearchResultDetail { Label = "Author", Value = author, AvatarName = author });
        item.Details.Add(new SearchResultDetail { Label = lengthLabel, Value = length });
        item.Details.Add(new SearchResultDetail { Label = "Last edited", Value = date.ToString("MMM d, yyyy"), Note = Ago(date) });
        return item;
    }

    private static string Ago(DateTimeOffset date)
    {
        var days = (int)(new DateTimeOffset(2026, 9, 21, 9, 0, 0, TimeSpan.Zero) - date).TotalDays;
        return days switch
        {
            < 14 => $"{days} days ago",
            < 60 => $"{days / 7} weeks ago",
            _ => $"{days / 30} months ago"
        };
    }

    // A person: an avatar (initials without a photo), a role line, a passage and the email as the caption.
    private static SearchResultItem Person(string id, string name, string role, string team, string email, string snippet)
    {
        var item = new SearchResultItem
        {
            Id = id,
            Title = name,
            Kind = "People",
            KindLabel = "Person",
            Subtitle = role,
            Snippet = snippet,
            Caption = email,
            AvatarName = name
        };
        item.Attributes["team"] = team;
        item.Body = snippet;
        item.Details.Add(new SearchResultDetail { Label = "Team", Value = team });
        item.Details.Add(new SearchResultDetail { Label = "Email", Value = email });
        return item;
    }
}
```

## When to use

`SearchResults` is the search page of a workspace: a large search field with a popup of recent and suggested searches, a
column of filters whose counts follow the query, a header with the number of results and a sort switch, and one list of
results, people and documents together, with the matched words marked. It fills the main content area of an application and
answers one question for a query that can span several kinds of data: what matches, of which kind, and where it lives. Choosing
a result opens a detail without leaving the page.

- **A help center or knowledge base**, where articles, how-to guides and release notes sit side by side. A customer who
  types "refund" ticks the kind that fits the question, and the counts beside every value show where the answers are before
  they click.
- **A project workspace that indexes documents, files and people.** The Team filter narrows "onboarding" to one group, the
  date range hides what nobody has touched this year, and each result states where it lives ("Doc in Support / Onboarding") so
  the right item is easy to pick.
- **A support console that searches tickets and macros on a server.** Set `IsFilteringEnabled` to false, show the server's
  order and the server's counts, and keep the highlights, the chips and the detail the control already draws.
- **An operations tool that searches incidents, runbooks and dashboards.** An on-call engineer presses `/`, types a service
  name, presses ArrowDown and opens the runbook with Enter, without leaving the keyboard.
- **A finance back office that searches invoices, customers and exports.** A result carries a passage around the match, a
  last-edited date and, in the detail, the owner and the size, so the person can tell two similar invoices apart.

## When not to use

- **Jumping to a page or running an action from anywhere in the app.** Use `CommandPalette`, which opens over the
  whole window and lists commands next to pages.
- **A compact search in a header or toolbar.** Use `ExpandingSearch`, which stays an icon until it is opened and takes
  no room in the page.
- **Filtering a list that is already on the page.** Use `SearchField` above the list and filter the list in code. A
  list of a few dozen rows does not need filters, counts or a detail.
- **Choosing one value from a short known list**, such as a status or a country. Use `Select` or `Combobox`; a search
  page with filters is too much for a choice of five.
- **Browsing records by column with sorting and filters.** Use `Table` with `FilterToolbar`. Results in
  `SearchResults` are read and opened, not compared across columns.

## Usage

Give the control its items and, for the left column, the filters you want. Every word of the query must match the title, the
subtitle, the snippet, the caption, the location, the body or a keyword of an item. The control matches, filters, counts and
sorts the items itself, unless you turn that off and let a server do it.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:SearchResults Height="640" Query="invoice" Label="Search finance">
        <arc:SearchResults.Filters>
            <arc:SearchValueFilter Key="kind" Title="Type" />
            <arc:SearchValueFilter Key="team" Title="Team" />
            <arc:SearchDateFilter Key="edited" Title="Edited" AppliesTo="Docs, Files" />
        </arc:SearchResults.Filters>
        <arc:SearchResultItem Title="Invoice template"
                              Kind="Docs"
                              KindLabel="Doc"
                              Location="Finance / Templates"
                              Snippet="Use this template for every customer invoice."
                              Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.FileText}" />
    </arc:SearchResults>
</UserControl>
```

`SearchResults` derives from Avalonia's `TemplatedControl`, so it takes the usual styling and theme resources. It is built
from Arc parts: its own search field (a styled `TextBox`), `Checkbox` rows, a two-thumb `Slider` for the date range,
a `SegmentedControl` for the sort order, `Avatar` for people, `EmptyState` for no results, `Skeleton` for loading and a
`ScrollArea` for the list. Each result is a `SearchResultItem`, an `AvaloniaObject` whose properties can be bound like any
other. The control sets the pseudo-classes `:narrow`, `:loading`, `:empty`, `:no-filters` and `:filtered` for styling.

### Anatomy

1. **Search field** (`Label`, `PlaceholderText`, `ShortcutText`): 50 px high with an 18 px radius, a magnifier, the text,
   a 24 px clear button that appears with the first character and a 24 px keycap with the key that focuses the field
   ("/" by default; it hides while the field has focus). The fill is muted with a subtle border; hover and focus use the
   strong border.
2. **Suggestions popup** (`Recent`, `Suggestions`, `RecentLabel`, `SuggestedLabel`): opens under the focused field, as wide as the
   field and 8 px below it. Two groups, "Recent" with a clock and "Suggested" with a magnifier, in 40 px rows with a 14 px
   radius. The row that equals the query shows a return key.
3. **Filters column** (`Filters`, `FiltersTitle`, `ClearAllText`): 244 px wide with a divider. A title with a "Clear all" link
   that fades in once a filter is active, then one group per filter: 34 px checkbox rows with the count right-aligned, and
   the date range with its two thumbs and a caption. Without filters the column is absent and the results take the whole width.
4. **Results header** (`ResultsFormat`, `OneResultFormat`, `ElapsedFormat`, `SortOrder`): the count in medium weight with a
   rolling number, the time it took in the muted color, and the sort switch on the right ("Best match", "Newest", "A to Z").
5. **Active filters bar** (`RemoveFilterText`, `ClearAllText`): a rounded bar under the header that opens and closes with a
   height animation. Every ticked value and narrowed range is a 34 px pill such as "Type · People" with a cross, and
   "Clear all" sits at the end.
6. **Result row** (`SearchResultItem`): a 36 px leading column (a round `Avatar` for people, a 20 px stroked icon for
   everything else), the title in medium weight, the subtitle in muted extra-small type, a snippet of up to two lines in
   the secondary text color and a muted caption. Rows have 20 px side padding, a 24 px radius and sit 4 px apart.
7. **Cursor**: one highlight block behind the active row, moved by the keyboard or the pointer. The suggestions popup has
   its own, of the same kind.
8. **Key hints** (`IsHintsVisible`, `HintMoveText`, `HintOpenText`, `HintSearchText`): small keycaps under the results,
   "↑ ↓ to move, ↵ to open, / to search", shown while results are listed.
9. **Detail** (`OpenedItem`, `DetailTemplate`): a dialog on wide screens, a bottom sheet on narrow ones, with the kind, a
   round close button, the title, the subtitle, the body, a table of facts and two buttons.
10. **Empty state and skeleton rows**: a centered `EmptyState` with the search icon, or three skeleton rows while loading.

The frame has a 1 px border and the surface radius. The field row has 24 px padding (16 px when narrow) and a 1 px rule under it.
Below 560 px the narrow layout applies.

### Items

Add `SearchResultItem` objects inline, or set `ItemsSource` to a list. When `ItemsSource` is null the inline `Items`
collection is used. When the list is an observable collection, the results follow its changes. A result is made of these
properties:

- `Id` is the stable key of the item, such as the record's own identifier. When it is empty the title is used instead.
- `Title` is the name of the result. It is marked where it matches and it decides the ranking.
- `Subtitle` is the line under the title, such as a person's role and city. Without one the row writes "`KindLabel` in
  `Location`" (the pattern is `KindLocationFormat`), or just the location.
- `Snippet` is a passage of the content. Long passages are cut to a window around the first match.
- `Caption` is a last muted line under the snippet, such as an email address.
- `Kind` is the type of the result ("Docs", "People", "Files"): the value the filter with the key `kind` reads. `KindLabel`
  is its singular name ("Doc"), used in the subtitle and the detail; it falls back to `Kind`.
- `Location` is a path or a breadcrumb such as "Engineering / Handbook". It is searched too.
- `Icon` takes a 24 by 24 Lucide geometry or any control. Without an icon the result uses the FileText glyph. A person
  shows a round avatar instead when `AvatarName` (initials) or `Avatar` (a photo) is set.
- `Keywords` are extra words that also find the item: synonyms, ticket numbers and tags. Keywords are searched but not
  shown.
- `Date` is when the item was last edited. It sorts "Newest" and feeds the date range.
- `Attributes` holds the values the other filters read, by filter key (`["team"] = "Design"`).
- `Body`, `Url` and `Details` fill the detail: the paragraphs of text, the address "Copy link" copies and the rows of the
  table of facts.
- `IsEnabled` set to false lists the item dimmed. It is skipped by the keyboard cursor and cannot be opened.
- `Tag` is any value you want back when the item is opened.

```csharp
search.ItemsSource = new ObservableCollection<SearchResultItem>
{
    new()
    {
        Id = "q3",
        Title = "Q3 planning notes",
        Kind = "Docs",
        KindLabel = "Doc",
        Location = "Product / Planning",
        Snippet = excerpt,
        Body = fullText,
        Date = new DateTimeOffset(2026, 9, 14, 9, 0, 0, TimeSpan.Zero),
        Url = "https://example.com/docs/q3",
        Attributes = { ["team"] = "Product" },
        Details = { new SearchResultDetail { Label = "Author", Value = "Maya Lindqvist", AvatarName = "Maya Lindqvist" } }
    },
    new()
    {
        Id = "maya",
        Title = "Maya Lindqvist",
        Kind = "People",
        KindLabel = "Person",
        Subtitle = "Product lead, Stockholm",
        Caption = "maya@example.com",
        AvatarName = "Maya Lindqvist",
        Attributes = { ["team"] = "Product" }
    }
};
```

If you change an item in place, call `Refresh()` to run the search and the counts again. Adding or removing items from an
observable collection does not need it, and neither do changes to the `Filters` list, to the values of a filter or to a
filter's `Key` and date range.

### Matching, ranking and highlights

The query is split on white space into distinct words, and an item matches when every word occurs in its title, subtitle,
snippet, caption, location, body or one of its keywords. A word may be found in different fields. The comparison ignores
case, but it does not fold accents: "resume" does not find "résumé". An empty query lists every item. The rows of `Details`
are only shown and the `Attributes` only feed the filters; neither is searched.

Ranking uses only the first word of the query, and applies to "Best match". Results keep their source order inside each
rank.

| Rank | The first word is found | Example for "release" |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | At the start of the title | "Release checklist" |
| 2 | At the start of a word in the title | "Q3 release notes" |
| 3 | Inside a word of the title | "Prerelease audit" |
| 4 | Only in the subtitle, snippet, caption, location, body or keywords | "Sync design: the release queue" |

Every occurrence of every word is marked in the title, the subtitle, the caption and the snippet: accent-subtle fill,
primary text and medium weight. Overlapping marks merge.

A long snippet is cut around the first match: it starts at the beginning when the match fits in the first lines, else
about 36 characters before the match, at a word start. It is at most 220 characters and two lines, with an ellipsis at each
cut end. When only the `Body` contains the words, the row shows a passage of the body in place of the snippet, so a result
always shows why it matched.

### Filters

`Filters` holds the filters of the column, and `SearchFilter` is their base. A `SearchValueFilter` is a group of checkboxes
over one attribute. Its `Key` is `kind` to read `SearchResultItem.Kind`, otherwise the name of an entry in
`SearchResultItem.Attributes`. Leave `Values` empty and the filter lists the values it finds, in the order they first appear
(new values that later items bring are appended); list them yourself as `SearchFilterValue` objects to fix their order and
labels. Several ticked values of one filter combine with OR, and the filters combine with AND.

Every value shows how many results it would show with the current query. The count ignores that filter's own ticks, as in
faceted search, so ticking "Docs" does not make "Files" read 0. It follows the query and the other filters while you type.
A value with no results keeps its place, dimmed, and cannot be ticked (unless it is already ticked, so it can be removed).

A `SearchDateFilter` is a two-thumb range slider over `SearchResultItem.Date`. The range spans the oldest and the newest
date of the items it applies to, or `Minimum` and `Maximum` when you set them. `Start` and `End` are the chosen ends (null:
that end of the range, and moving a thumb back to its end sets null again). `AppliesTo` names the kinds it concerns as a
comma separated list; items of other kinds pass, so a range over documents does not hide people, and the caption under the
slider says so ("Applies to docs and files"). While a range is narrowed, an item of an applying kind without a date is hidden. A date filter always reads `Date`; its `Key`
only names it.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.SearchResultsFiltersDemo">
    <arc:SearchResults x:Name="Search" Height="680" Label="Search the library" Query="harbour">
        <arc:SearchResults.Filters>
            <arc:SearchValueFilter Key="kind" Title="Type" />
            <arc:SearchValueFilter Key="topic" Title="Topic">
                <arc:SearchFilterValue Value="Navigation" />
                <arc:SearchFilterValue Value="Weather" />
                <arc:SearchFilterValue Value="Safety" IsSelected="True" />
                <arc:SearchFilterValue Value="Maintenance" />
            </arc:SearchValueFilter>
            <arc:SearchDateFilter Key="updated" Title="Updated" AppliesTo="Guides, Charts" />
        </arc:SearchResults.Filters>
        <arc:SearchResultItem Title="Harbour entry checklist" Kind="Guides" KindLabel="Guide" Location="Navigation / Approach"
                              Snippet="Check the tide table, call the harbour master on channel 12 and reduce speed at the outer marker."
                              Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.FileText}" />
        <arc:SearchResultItem Title="Harbour lights and marks" Kind="Charts" KindLabel="Chart" Location="Navigation / Charts"
                              Snippet="Every light and buoy around the harbour with its colour, rhythm and range."
                              Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.File}" />
        <arc:SearchResultItem Title="Storm shelter in the harbour" Kind="Guides" KindLabel="Guide" Location="Safety / Weather"
                              Snippet="Where to tie up when the wind passes force 8 and how to double the lines."
                              Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.FileText}" />
        <arc:SearchResultItem Title="Winter lay-up and harbour fees" Kind="Guides" KindLabel="Guide" Location="Maintenance / Yard"
                              Snippet="Prices per metre for the winter months and what the harbour includes."
                              Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.FileText}" />
        <arc:SearchResultItem Title="Ines Duarte" Kind="People" Subtitle="Pilot coordinator, Lisbon"
                              Snippet="Keeps the harbour pilot rota and knows who is on call this week."
                              Caption="ines@tidewater.example" AvatarName="Ines Duarte" />
        <arc:SearchResultItem Title="Marit Haugen" Kind="People" Subtitle="Harbour master, Bergen"

```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class SearchResultsFiltersDemo : UserControl
{
    public SearchResultsFiltersDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        // Filters read Kind or an entry of Attributes; the date comes from Date.
        var topics = new Dictionary<string, string>
        {
            ["Harbour entry checklist"] = "Navigation",
            ["Harbour lights and marks"] = "Navigation",
            ["Storm shelter in the harbour"] = "Safety",
            ["Winter lay-up and harbour fees"] = "Maintenance",
            ["Ines Duarte"] = "Safety",
            ["Marit Haugen"] = "Maintenance"
        };
        var day = new DateTimeOffset(2026, 2, 3, 0, 0, 0, TimeSpan.Zero);
        foreach (var item in Search.Items)
        {
            item.Attributes["topic"] = topics[item.Title];
            if (item.Kind != "People")
            {
                item.Date = day;
                day = day.AddDays(47);
            }
        }
        Search.Refresh();
    }
}
```

Ticked values and narrowed ranges appear as chips in the bar under the results header. A chip's cross removes its filter,
and "Clear all" (in the bar and in the column) removes them all. In code you can read and set a value's `IsSelected` and a date
filter's `Start` and `End`, call `ClearFilters()`, and read `HasActiveFilters` and `ActiveFilterCount`. The control reads at
most 64 filters.

### Sorting and the results header

The header shows how many results there are, how long the search took, and a sort switch. `SortOrder` is two-way: best
match, newest (`SearchResultItem.Date`, items without a date last) or A to Z (by title, using the current culture). The control
cannot measure the time, so you set `Elapsed` when your search finishes; leave it null to show only the count. Both numbers
roll to their new value. When nothing matches, the header shows `NoResultsText` instead.

### Suggestions and recent searches

Focusing the field opens a popup under it with the recent searches and your `Suggestions` (at most six, and none that are
already in Recent). The control adds a query to `Recent`, newest first and without duplicates, whenever one is submitted
(Enter, a suggestion or a "Try" chip) or a result is opened with it. `MaxRecent` caps the list. Seed `Recent` before the page
shows and save it from its `CollectionChanged` event; it is an `AvaloniaList<string>`, not a bindable property.

Arrow keys move through the rows, Enter runs the highlighted one or the text as typed, Escape closes the popup, and a click on
a row fills the field and submits it. Once you edit the text, the popup lists only the entries that contain it, and it closes
itself when nothing is left. `QuerySubmitted` tells you about every submitted query. Set `IsSuggestionsEnabled` to false for a
field that never opens the popup.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.SearchResultsSuggestionsDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12">
        <arc:SearchResults x:Name="Search"
                           Height="560"
                           Label="Search the help center"
                           PlaceholderText="Search articles"
                           MaxRecent="4">
            <arc:SearchResultItem Title="Export your data" Kind="Articles" Location="Help center / Account"
                                  Snippet="Download every invoice, customer and payment as CSV or JSON." />
            <arc:SearchResultItem Title="Schedule a recurring export" Kind="Articles" Location="Help center / Automation"
                                  Snippet="Pick a time and a format and the export is sent to your storage bucket." />
            <arc:SearchResultItem Title="Reset your password" Kind="Articles" Location="Help center / Account"
                                  Snippet="Choose “Forgot password” on the sign-in page and follow the link in the email." />
            <arc:SearchResultItem Title="Invite a teammate" Kind="Articles" Location="Help center / Teams"
                                  Snippet="Owners and admins can invite people from the Members page." />
        </arc:SearchResults>
        <TextBlock x:Name="Status"
                   Text="The popup opens with the field. Arrow keys move through the rows, Enter or a click runs one, Escape closes it."
                   TextWrapping="Wrap"
                   FontSize="14"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

    {
        InitializeComponent();
        // Recent searches are recorded by the control when a query is submitted; seed them (or save them) yourself.
        Search.Recent.AddRange(["export", "invite", "password reset"]);
        Search.Suggestions = ["billing", "single sign-on", "audit log", "api keys"];
        Search.QuerySubmitted += (_, e) => Status.Text = $"Submitted “{e.Query}”. Recent: {string.Join(", ", Search.Recent)}.";
    }
}
```

### Binding to a view model

The view model owns the query, the sort order, the items and the open command. The control owns the cursor, the filters'
ticks and the layout.

```csharp
public partial class WorkspaceSearchViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    private readonly INavigationService _navigation;

    public WorkspaceSearchViewModel(INavigationService navigation)
    {
        _navigation = navigation;
    }

    [ObservableProperty]
    private string _query = string.Empty;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private SearchSortOrder _sort = SearchSortOrder.BestMatch;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private TimeSpan? _elapsed;

    public ObservableCollection<SearchResultItem> Results { get; } = [];

    [RelayCommand]
    private void Open(SearchResultItem? item) => _navigation.Navigate(item?.Tag);
}
```

```xml
<arc:SearchResults Label="Search the workspace"
                   ItemsSource="{Binding Results}"
                   Query="{Binding Query}"
                   SortOrder="{Binding Sort}"
                   Elapsed="{Binding Elapsed}"
                   IsDetailEnabled="False"
                   InvokeCommand="{Binding OpenCommand}" />
```

- `Query` and `SortOrder` are two-way, so typing updates the view model and a link can open the page with a query
  already filled in.
- `ItemsSource` and `Elapsed` are one-way. Keep `Results` as an `ObservableCollection` and change it in place.
- `InvokeCommand` runs with the opened item as its parameter, and the control checks `CanExecute` first. This view model
  navigates, so the sample turns the built-in detail off; keep it on and bind the two-way `OpenedItem` when the view model
  should know which detail is open.
- `Filters` and `Recent` are collections you fill and read, not properties you bind.

### Opening results

Enter or a click on a result raises `ItemInvoked` with the item, runs `InvokeCommand` with the same item, and then opens the
built-in detail. `ActiveItem` is the result under the keyboard cursor, the first enabled result until you move it, so a status
line can describe what Enter will open. Results with `IsEnabled` set to false are dimmed, skipped by the cursor and cannot be
opened. When your app navigates instead of showing the detail, set `IsDetailEnabled` to false, or set `Handled` on the event.

```csharp
search.ItemInvoked += (_, e) =>
{
    Navigate(e.Item.Id);
    e.Handled = true; // skip the built-in detail
};
```

The detail is a dialog on wide screens and a bottom sheet with a grab handle on narrow ones. It shows the kind of the result
with a round close button, the title with the matches marked, the subtitle, the paragraphs of `Body` (separated by blank lines;
the snippet when there is no body), a table made of a first "Matches" row (how often the query is marked in the title and
the body) and the item's `Details`, and two buttons. "Open" (`OpenFormat`, with the kind label in lower case) and "Copy link"
raise `DetailActionInvoked`; "Copy link" also puts `Url` on the clipboard. Escape, the close button or a press on the dimmed page
closes it, and focus returns to where it was.

`OpenedItem` is two-way: set it, or call `ShowDetail(item)`, to open a detail from code, and `CloseDetail()` closes it.
`DetailTemplate` replaces the content between the header and the buttons; its data is the `SearchResultItem`.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
```
