### Server-side search

When a server searches, set `IsFilteringEnabled` to false. The items are then shown in the order you give, the counts on the
filter values are yours to set, and the words of the query are still marked. `SearchChanged` tells you, with a `Reason` of
`Query`, `Filters` or `Sort`, that something changed and you should ask again. Set `IsLoading` while the request runs: skeleton
rows take the place of the results and keep the height of the previous results, so the page does not jump, the count line
reads "Searching…" and the cursor and the hints go away. Debounce the query before you call the server, and cancel the request
that a newer keystroke overtakes. Without a debounce, every keystroke starts a request and the results flicker.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.SearchResultsServerSearchDemo">
    <arc:SearchResults x:Name="Search"
                       Height="600"
                       IsFilteringEnabled="False"
                       Label="Search support"
                       PlaceholderText="Search tickets, articles and macros">
        <arc:SearchResults.Filters>
            <arc:SearchValueFilter Key="kind" Title="Type">
                <arc:SearchFilterValue Value="Tickets" />
                <arc:SearchFilterValue Value="Articles" />
                <arc:SearchFilterValue Value="Macros" />
            </arc:SearchValueFilter>
        </arc:SearchResults.Filters>
    </arc:SearchResults>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using System.Diagnostics;
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class SearchResultsServerSearchDemo : UserControl
{
    // What the "server" knows. A real app would call its search API instead.
    private sealed record Record(string Id, string Title, string Kind, string Location, string Snippet, DateTimeOffset Date);

    private static DateTimeOffset Day(int month, int day) => new(2026, month, day, 9, 0, 0, TimeSpan.Zero);

    private static readonly Record[] s_index =
    [
        new("t-2091", "Export to CSV drops the last row", "Tickets", "#2091 · Billing", "When an export has more than 1,000 rows the last one is missing from the file.", Day(9, 18)),
        new("t-2088", "Can't export invoices from the mobile app", "Tickets", "#2088 · Mobile", "The export button stays disabled on iOS when the invoice has a discount.", Day(9, 17)),
        new("t-2075", "Scheduled export runs twice", "Tickets", "#2075 · Platform", "Daily exports started twice after the move to the new scheduler.", Day(9, 12)),
        new("t-2063", "Password reset email never arrives", "Tickets", "#2063 · Accounts", "Customers on custom domains do not get the reset email; the bounce log shows a DNS error.", Day(9, 8)),
        new("a-export", "Export your data", "Articles", "Help center / Account", "Download every invoice, customer and payment as CSV or JSON. Large exports arrive by email.", Day(9, 1)),
        new("a-schedule", "Schedule a recurring export", "Articles", "Help center / Automation", "Pick a time and a format and the export is sent to your storage bucket every day.", Day(8, 20)),
        new("a-reset", "Reset your password", "Articles", "Help center / Account", "Open the sign-in page, choose “Forgot password” and follow the link in the email.", Day(6, 4)),
        new("m-export", "Export pipeline runbook", "Macros", "Support macros", "Steps to retry a failed export and the message to send to the customer.", Day(7, 30))
    ];

    private CancellationTokenSource? _pending;

    public SearchResultsServerSearchDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        // Any change of the query, a filter or the sort order is a new request.
        Search.SearchChanged += (_, _) => _ = SearchAsync();
        Search.Query = "export";
    }

    private async Task SearchAsync()
    {
        _pending?.Cancel();
        var pending = _pending = new CancellationTokenSource();
        try
        {
            // Wait until typing pauses, then show skeleton rows while the "server" answers.
            await Task.Delay(200, pending.Token);
            Search.IsLoading = true;
            var clock = Stopwatch.StartNew();
            await Task.Delay(600, pending.Token);

            var words = Search.Query.Split(' ', StringSplitOptions.RemoveEmptyEntries);
            var matches = s_index
                .Where(r => words.All(w => r.Title.Contains(w, StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase) ||
                                           r.Snippet.Contains(w, StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase)))
                .ToList();

            // The server also counts every type for the query, whatever is ticked (the counts of the filter's own values).
            var type = (SearchValueFilter)Search.Filters[0];
            foreach (var value in type.Values)
            {
                value.Count = matches.Count(r => r.Kind == value.Value);
            }

            var kinds = type.SelectedValues.Select(v => v.Value).ToList();
            var results = matches.Where(r => kinds.Count == 0 || kinds.Contains(r.Kind));
            // The server decides the order: the control shows the items as given.
            results = Search.SortOrder switch
            {
                SearchSortOrder.Newest => results.OrderByDescending(r => r.Date),
                SearchSortOrder.Title => results.OrderBy(r => r.Title),
                _ => results
            };
            Search.ItemsSource = results
                .Select(r => new SearchResultItem
                {
                    Id = r.Id,
                    Title = r.Title,
                    Kind = r.Kind,
                    KindLabel = r.Kind.TrimEnd('s'),
                    Location = r.Location,
                    Snippet = r.Snippet,
                    Date = r.Date,
                    Icon = r.Kind switch
                    {
                        "Tickets" => ArcIcons.Inbox,
                        "Articles" => ArcIcons.FileText,
                        _ => ArcIcons.Zap
                    }
                })
                .ToList();
            Search.Elapsed = clock.Elapsed;
            Search.IsLoading = false;
        }
        catch (TaskCanceledException)
        {
            // A newer request took over.
        }
    }
}
```

### No results

When nothing matches, an empty state shows the query in its title (`EmptyTitleFormat`, with `{0}` for the query) and the
description (`EmptyDescription`). The count line shows `NoResultsText`. With an empty query and no items the title also uses
`NoResultsText`.

If filters are active, the description becomes `EmptyFilteredDescription`, "The filters leave nothing. Remove one to see
more.", and a "Clear filters" button (`ClearFiltersText`) removes them. `Suggestions` adds queries to try, shown as buttons
after `TryText` ("Try" by default). Choosing one fills the search field and runs the search.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.SearchResultsNoResultsDemo">

        <arc:SearchResults.Filters>
            <arc:SearchValueFilter Key="kind" Title="Type">
                <arc:SearchFilterValue Value="Guides" IsSelected="True" />
                <arc:SearchFilterValue Value="Charts" />
            </arc:SearchValueFilter>
        </arc:SearchResults.Filters>
        <arc:SearchResultItem Title="Reading the tide table" Kind="Charts" Snippet="How to find high water for your harbour."
                              Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.File}" />
        <arc:SearchResultItem Title="Mooring in a strong tide" Kind="Charts" Snippet="Lines, fenders and the order to tie up."
                              Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.File}" />
        <arc:SearchResultItem Title="Passage planning" Kind="Guides" Snippet="Plan a day trip from start to finish."
```

### Narrow layouts

Below 560 pixels of width the field row tightens from 24 to 16 pixels of padding, the filters column folds into a "Filters"
button that carries the number of active filters, and the button opens the same filters in a bottom sheet (`OpenFiltersSheet()`
does the same from code). The sort switch moves under the count, and the detail becomes a bottom sheet that is at most 92 percent
of the window high. With no filters at all, the narrow layout keeps the sort switch on the right. The filters sheet closes by
itself when the control becomes wide again.

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class SearchResultsNarrowDemo : UserControl
{
    public SearchResultsNarrowDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        var rooms = new[] { "Living room", "Office", "Bedroom", "Office" };
        var search = (SearchResults)Content!;
        for (var i = 0; i < search.Items.Count; i++)
        {
            search.Items[i].Attributes["room"] = rooms[i];
        }
        search.Refresh();
```

### Long lists

Only the first `PageSize` results (15 by default) are built. More follow when the list is scrolled within 240 pixels of its
end, when "Show more" (`ShowMoreText`) is pressed, or when ArrowDown or PageDown is pressed on the last listed result. A new
query, filter or sort order starts from the top again.

Typing stays fast with thousands of items. A query that only grows searches the previous matches instead of every item; ticking
a filter does not search the text again; the counts are made in the same pass as the filtering; and rows that stay are the same
controls, so a keystroke re-lays out only what changed. Searching and filtering 5,000 items takes a millisecond or two on a
development laptop, and most of the cost of a keystroke is laying out the rows that changed.

### Texts

Every text has an English default and a property to change it. Formats use `{0}` for the count, the seconds, the query or the
kind, and `{1}` where a second value is named.

| Property | Default | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| `Label` | "Search" | The landmark and the search field name |
| `PlaceholderText` | "Search" | The hint in the empty field |
| `ShortcutText` | "/" | The key on the field's keycap and in the hints |
| `FiltersTitle` | "Filters" | The title of the filters column and the sheet |
| `ClearAllText` | "Clear all" | The link that removes every filter |
| `ClearFiltersText` | "Clear filters" | The empty state's button that removes the filters |
| `ResultsFormat` | "{0} results" | The count for several results |
| `OneResultFormat` | "{0} result" | The count for one result |
| `NoResultsText` | "No results" | The count when nothing matches, and the empty title without a query |
| `LoadingText` | "Searching…" | The count while `IsLoading` is true |
| `ElapsedFormat` | "in {0} seconds" | The time after the count; `{0}` is the seconds |
| `BestMatchText` | "Best match" | The first sort option |
| `NewestText` | "Newest" | The second sort option |
| `TitleSortText` | "A to Z" | The third sort option |
| `RecentLabel` | "Recent" | The group of recent searches in the popup |
| `SuggestedLabel` | "Suggested" | The group of suggestions in the popup |
| `TryText` | "Try" | The word before the suggestions of the empty state |
| `EmptyTitleFormat` | "No results for “{0}”" | The empty state title |
| `EmptyDescription` | "Check the spelling or try fewer words." | The empty state text |
| `EmptyFilteredDescription` | "The filters leave nothing. Remove one to see more." | The empty state text while filters are active |
| `ShowMoreText` | "Show more" | The button under the listed results when more are left |
| `KindLocationFormat` | "{0} in {1}" | A subtitle made of the kind label and the location |
| `HintMoveText` | "to move," | The hint after the arrow keys |
| `HintOpenText` | "to open," | The hint after the return key |
| `HintSearchText` | "to search" | The hint after the shortcut key |
| `MatchesLabel` | "Matches" | The first row of the detail's table |
| `OpenFormat` | "Open {0}" | The detail's primary button; `{0}` is the kind label in lower case |
| `CopyLinkText` | "Copy link" | The detail's secondary button |
| `CloseText` | "Close" | The accessible name of the close buttons |
| `ClearSearchText` | "Clear search" | The accessible name of the field's clear button |
| `FiltersButtonText` | "Filters" | The narrow layout's button |
| `AppliesToFormat` | "Applies to {0}" | The caption of a date filter without one; `{0}` lists its kinds |
| `AndText` | "and" | The word between the last two kinds of that caption |
| `RemoveFilterText` | "Remove filter" | The accessible name of a chip's cross |
| `DateFormat` | "MMM yyyy" | How the ends of a date range are written, in the current culture |

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:SearchResults Label="Search the help center"
                       PlaceholderText="Search articles"
                       ResultsFormat="{}{0} articles"
                       OneResultFormat="{}{0} article"
                       NoResultsText="No articles"
                       ElapsedFormat="{}in {0}s"
                       FiltersTitle="Refine"
                       EmptyTitleFormat="Nothing found for “{0}”" />
</UserControl>
```

### Data shape and performance

The control reads the title, subtitle, snippet, caption, kind, location, body, keywords, date, attributes and id of each item
and the rows of its details; put anything else in `Tag`.

- Local matching checks every item on a new query, and only the previous matches while the query grows, so a local index of a
  few thousand items stays responsive. Past that, search on a server and set `IsFilteringEnabled` to false.
- Format dates and sizes in `Details` with the reader's culture before you set them; the control shows the strings as given.
  The date range and the sort use the current culture, and the first A to Z sort of a process is warmed up when the first
  search page is created, so it does not stall the window.
- Leave `PageSize` small. Every listed row is built and laid out, and the next page loads as the person scrolls.

### Example: Finance search for invoices

A finance back office opens search with the query "invoice" already filled in, after a link from the invoice list. The Team
filter has Finance ticked and the Edited range starts on August 1, so two chips sit under the header and an older invoice PDF is
left out. The counts beside Sales and Support show what the other teams would add. Newest first puts the person, who has no
date, last.

![Search results for invoices with filters, chips, a person and documents with the matching words marked](https://docs.tkcode.si/shots/Docs/Blocks/SearchResults/images/SearchResults.webp)

```xml
    <arc:SearchResultItem Title="Tobias Wren"
                          Kind="People"
                          KindLabel="Person"
                          Subtitle="Finance partner, Dublin"
                          Snippet="Approves every invoice above 10,000 and keeps the payment calendar."
                          Caption="tobias@tidewater.example"
                          AvatarName="Tobias Wren">
        <arc:SearchResultItem.Attributes>
            <x:String x:Key="team">Finance</x:String>
        </arc:SearchResultItem.Attributes>
    </arc:SearchResultItem>
    <arc:SearchResultItem Title="Invoice questions macro"
                          Kind="Docs"
                          KindLabel="Doc"
                          Location="Support / Macros"
                          Date="2026-08-22"
                          Snippet="A reply for customers who ask why an invoice shows two charges.">
        <arc:SearchResultItem.Attributes>
            <x:String x:Key="team">Support</x:String>
        </arc:SearchResultItem.Attributes>
    </arc:SearchResultItem>
    <arc:SearchResultItem Title="Invoice discount rules"
                          Kind="Files"
                          KindLabel="File"
                          Location="Sales / Pricing"
                          Date="2026-08-27"
                          Snippet="Which discounts may appear on an invoice, and who has to approve them.">
        <arc:SearchResultItem.Attributes>
            <x:String x:Key="team">Sales</x:String>
        </arc:SearchResultItem.Attributes>
    </arc:SearchResultItem>
    <arc:SearchResultItem Title="INV-1042.pdf"
                          Kind="Files"
                          KindLabel="File"
                          Location="Customers / Brightline"
                          Date="2026-03-12"
                          Snippet="The signed invoice for the annual plan.">
        <arc:SearchResultItem.Attributes>
            <x:String x:Key="team">Finance</x:String>
        </arc:SearchResultItem.Attributes>
    </arc:SearchResultItem>
</arc:SearchResults>
```

### Content guidelines

Write the labels and the results so that a person can choose one without opening it. Kinds are plural nouns with an
initial capital ("Docs", "People", "Files"), because they are filter values; give each a singular `KindLabel` ("Doc",
"Person", "File") for the subtitle and the "Open doc" button. Titles name the thing, not a sentence about it. Locations are
breadcrumbs joined with " / ". A person's subtitle is a role and a city, and the caption is the one way to reach them.
Rows in `Details` are short facts: a name, a size, a relative time.

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| Results: 4 | 4 results (`ResultsFormat` with the count) |
| No matches found for your query | No results for “quarterly forecast” (`EmptyTitleFormat`) |
| Reset | Clear filters (`ClearFiltersText`) |
| Open | Open doc (`OpenFormat` with the kind label) |

### Best practices

**Do**

- Give every result a `Kind` and a `KindLabel` that a person recognizes; the Type filter and every subtitle read them.
- Put the words people search for in the title first. The title is searched and ranked; the location, the subtitle and the
  keywords are searched; the snippet is searched and marked. Put the long text in `Body`, where it is searched and shown
  in the detail.
- Offer two to four filters, in the order of how often they narrow a search, and list their values yourself when the order
  matters ("Support", "Design", "Engineering" is a better order than the first-seen one).
- Set `IsLoading` for any request that takes longer than a blink, so the page keeps its height and shows that work is
  underway.
- Measure the time yourself and set `Elapsed` only for a real search; a made-up number reads as a promise.

**Avoid**

- A filter for every attribute. A long column scrolls, and the person has to read the options before the results; filters
  pay off when they cut a long list quickly.
- A whole document in `Snippet`. The control cuts long text around the match; a long passage hides why the result matched.
  `Body` is for the full text.
- Changing an item's `Kind`, `Title` or `Attributes` in place without calling `Refresh()`. The counts and the ranking are
  computed when the search runs.
- Using `IsEnabled` to hide a result. A disabled result is still listed, dimmed and counted; remove it from the items
  when it should not appear at all.
- Navigating on `ItemInvoked` and leaving `IsDetailEnabled` on. One Enter would then do both; turn the detail off or set
  `Handled`.

### Common questions

**Can I change the order of the filter values?** Yes. List them as `SearchFilterValue` objects inside the filter. Only a
filter without values lists what it finds, in the order the values first occur.

**How do I clear the search from code?** Set `Query` to an empty string and call `ClearFilters()`. An empty query lists every
item again. Escape in the field clears the query from the keyboard, after it closes the suggestions.

**Can I hide the filters?** Leave `Filters` empty (or give no value filter any value): the column goes away and the results
take the whole width.

**Why does a value show 0 and refuse to be ticked?** With the current query and the other filters it would show nothing, so
it is dimmed and disabled, and it keeps its place so the column does not jump while the person types. A value that is already
ticked stays available, so it can be removed.

**How do I keep recent searches between sessions?** Handle `Recent.CollectionChanged` and store the list; add the stored
entries to `Recent` before the page shows.

## API reference

### SearchResults

A search results page for a workspace (an original TKCode design, after Algolia InstantSearch's search box, hits, highlight, refinement list and stats). A large search field with a suggestions popup (recent and suggested searches), a filters column (checkbox groups whose counts follow the query and the other filters, and a date range), a results header with the count, the time it took and a sort switch, the active filters as removable chips, and the results: people and documents in one list, matches marked in titles and in a snippet cut around the first match. One cursor block glides between the results; Enter or a click opens a result in a detail dialog (a bottom sheet on narrow screens). Below 560 the filters move behind a button into a sheet.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ItemsSource` | `IEnumerable<SearchResultItem>?` | `null` | Items to search; when null the inline `Items` are used. Collection changes are followed. |
| `Query` | `string` | `""` | The text in the search field (two-way). |
| `SortOrder` | `SearchSortOrder` | `BestMatch` | How the results are ordered (two-way). Default `BestMatch`. |
| `Elapsed` | `TimeSpan?` | `null` | How long the search took, shown after the count ("in 0.12 seconds"). Null shows nothing; the app measures it. |
| `IsFilteringEnabled` | `bool` | `true` | When true (default) the items are matched, filtered, counted and sorted here. Set it to false when a server searched: the items are shown as given, `Count` is yours, and the query's terms are still marked. |
| `IsLoading` | `bool` | `false` | Shows skeleton rows in place of the results (keeping the previous results' height). |
| `PageSize` | `int` | `15` | Results listed first; more follow when the list is scrolled to its end or "Show more" is pressed. Default 15. |
| `IsSuggestionsEnabled` | `bool` | `true` | Whether the suggestions popup opens under the focused field. Default true. |
| `Suggestions` | `IList<string>?` | `null` | Queries offered under "Suggested" in the popup and when nothing matches; choosing one fills the search field. |
| `MaxRecent` | `int` | `5` | How many recent searches are kept. Default 5. |
| `IsDetailEnabled` | `bool` | `true` | Whether Enter or a click opens the built-in detail. Turn it off when your app navigates on `ItemInvoked`. |
| `OpenedItem` | `SearchResultItem?` | `null` | The result whose detail is open, or null (two-way). Setting it opens that result's detail. |
| `DetailTemplate` | `IDataTemplate?` | `null` | Replaces the built-in content of the detail (everything between the header and the buttons); its data is the `SearchResultItem`. |
| `IsHintsVisible` | `bool` | `true` | Whether the keyboard hints show under the results. Default true. |
| `Label` | `string` | `"Search"` | Names the search landmark and the search field. |
| `PlaceholderText` | `string` | `"Search"` | Hint in the empty search field. |
| `ShortcutText` | `string` | `"/"` | The key hint on the field's keycap (the key that focuses it). Default "/". |
| `InvokeCommand` | `ICommand?` | `null` | Executed with the opened `SearchResultItem`. |
| `ActiveItem` | `SearchResultItem?` | – | *Read-only.* The result under the cursor, or null. |
| `ResultCount` | `int` | – | *Read-only.* The number of results for the current query and filters. |
| `FiltersTitle` | `string` | `"Filters"` | The filters column title. Default "Filters". |
| `ClearAllText` | `string` | `"Clear all"` | The link that clears every filter (in the column and in the active filters bar). Default "Clear all". |
| `ClearFiltersText` | `string` | `"Clear filters"` | The empty state's button that clears the filters. Default "Clear filters". |
| `ResultsFormat` | `string` | `"{0} results"` | Stats text for several results; {0} is the count (it rolls). Default "{0} results". |
| `OneResultFormat` | `string` | `"{0} result"` | Stats text for one result; {0} is the count. Default "{0} result". |
| `NoResultsText` | `string` | `"No results"` | Stats text (and empty title without a query) when nothing matches. Default "No results". |
| `LoadingText` | `string` | `"Searching…"` | Stats text while `IsLoading` is true. Default "Searching…". |
| `ElapsedFormat` | `string` | `"in {0} seconds"` | The time after the count; {0} is the seconds. Default "in {0} seconds". |
| `BestMatchText` | `string` | `"Best match"` | The "Best match" sort option. |
| `NewestText` | `string` | `"Newest"` | The "Newest" sort option. |
| `TitleSortText` | `string` | `"A to Z"` | The "A to Z" sort option. |
| `RecentLabel` | `string` | `"Recent"` | The group of recent searches in the popup. Default "Recent". |
| `SuggestedLabel` | `string` | `"Suggested"` | The group of suggested searches in the popup. Default "Suggested". |
| `TryText` | `string` | `"Try"` | The word before the suggestions of the empty state. Default "Try". |
| `EmptyTitleFormat` | `string` | `"No results for “{0}”"` | Empty state title; {0} is the query. Default "No results for “{0}”". |
| `EmptyDescription` | `string` | `"Check the spelling or try fewer words."` | Empty state description. Default "Check the spelling or try fewer words." |
| `EmptyFilteredDescription` | `string` | `"The filters leave nothing. Remove one to see more."` | Empty state description while filters hide results. Default "The filters leave nothing. Remove one to see more." |
| `ShowMoreText` | `string` | `"Show more"` | Button under the listed results when more are left. Default "Show more". |
| `KindLocationFormat` | `string` | `"{0} in {1}"` | The kind and the location in a result's subtitle; {0} is the kind label, {1} the location. Default "{0} in {1}". |
| `HintMoveText` | `string` | `"to move,"` | The key hint "to move". Default "to move,". |
| `HintOpenText` | `string` | `"to open,"` | The key hint "to open". Default "to open,". |
| `HintSearchText` | `string` | `"to search"` | The key hint "to search". Default "to search". |
| `MatchesLabel` | `string` | `"Matches"` | The first row of the detail table: how often the query matches. Default "Matches". |
| `OpenFormat` | `string` | `"Open {0}"` | The detail's primary button; {0} is the kind label in lower case. Default "Open {0}". |
| `CopyLinkText` | `string` | `"Copy link"` | The detail's secondary button. Default "Copy link". |
| `CloseText` | `string` | `"Close"` | Names the close buttons of the detail and the filters sheet. Default "Close". |
| `ClearSearchText` | `string` | `"Clear search"` | Names the clear button of the field. Default "Clear search". |
| `FiltersButtonText` | `string` | `"Filters"` | The narrow layout's button that opens the filters. Default "Filters". |
| `AppliesToFormat` | `string` | `"Applies to {0}"` | The caption of a date filter without one; {0} lists its kinds ("docs and files"). Default "Applies to {0}". |
| `AndText` | `string` | `"and"` | The word between the last two kinds of the default caption. Default "and". |
| `RemoveFilterText` | `string` | `"Remove filter"` | Names the remove button of a filter chip. Default "Remove filter". |
| `DateFormat` | `string` | `"MMM yyyy"` | The month and year format of a date range ("Sep 2025"). Default "MMM yyyy". |
| `HasActiveFilters` | `bool` | – | *Read-only.* True while at least one filter narrows the results (read-only). |
| `ActiveFilterCount` | `int` | – | *Read-only.* The number of filter values ticked plus date ranges narrowed (read-only). |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ItemInvoked` | `SearchResultInvokedEventArgs` | Raised when a result is opened with Enter or a click (before the detail shows; set Handled to skip the detail). |
| `DetailActionInvoked` | `SearchResultActionEventArgs` | Raised when a button of the detail is pressed. |
| `SearchChanged` | `SearchChangedEventArgs` | Raised when the query, a filter or the sort order changed (ask your server again). |
| `QuerySubmitted` | `SearchQuerySubmittedEventArgs` | Raised when a query is submitted: Enter in the field, or a suggestion chosen. |

Pseudo-classes: `:narrow`, `:loading`, `:empty`, `:no-filters`, `:filtered`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

### SearchResultItem

One searchable entry of a `SearchResults`: a document, a person, a file or anything else your workspace holds. `Kind` and `Attributes` feed the filters, the text properties are searched and shown, and the detail properties fill the sheet that opens when the result is chosen.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Id` | `string` | `""` | Stable id; the title is used when it is empty. |
| `Title` | `string` | `""` | The name of the result; searched first, marked where it matches and ranked by. |
| `Subtitle` | `string?` | `null` | The line under the title (a person's role and city). When null the row shows "`KindLabel` in `Location`" (or just the location). |
| `Snippet` | `string?` | `null` | A passage of the content; long passages are cut to a window around the first match. Searched. |
| `Caption` | `string?` | `null` | A last, muted line under the snippet, such as an email address. Not searched. |
| `Kind` | `string?` | `null` | The type of the result ("Docs", "People", "Files"): the value of the filter whose key is `KindKey`. |
| `KindLabel` | `string?` | `null` | The singular name of the kind ("Doc") used in the subtitle and the detail sheet; `Kind` when null. |
| `Location` | `string?` | `null` | Where the result lives: a path or a breadcrumb ("Engineering / Handbook"). Also searched. |
| `Icon` | `object?` | `null` | A 20px icon: a 24×24 Lucide `Geometry` or a control. Default: Lucide FileText. |
| `Avatar` | `ImageSource?` | `null` | A photo for a person: the row and the detail show a round avatar instead of the icon. |
| `AvatarName` | `string?` | `null` | A person's name: the avatar shows its initials (and the photo's fallback). Setting it switches the row to an avatar. |
| `Keywords` | `IList<string>?` | `null` | Extra words that also find the result (synonyms, ids, tags). |
| `Date` | `DateTimeOffset?` | `null` | When the result was last edited; sorts "Newest" and feeds a `SearchDateFilter`. |
| `Body` | `string?` | `null` | The paragraphs shown in the detail sheet, separated by blank lines. Searched and marked there. |
| `Url` | `string?` | `null` | The address "Copy link" puts on the clipboard. |
| `IsEnabled` | `bool` | `true` | When false the result is listed dimmed, skipped by the keyboard cursor and cannot be opened. |
| `Tag` | `object?` | `null` | Any value you want back when the result is opened. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### SearchResultDetail

One key/value row of a result's detail sheet.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Label` | `string` | `""` | The muted name on the left ("Team"). |
| `Value` | `string?` | `null` | The value on the right. |
| `Note` | `string?` | `null` | A muted remark after the value ("3 weeks ago"). |
| `AvatarName` | `string?` | `null` | A person's name: a small avatar with their initials is shown before the value. |
| `Avatar` | `ImageSource?` | `null` | A person's photo for the avatar before the value. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### SearchFilter

A way to narrow the results of a `SearchResults`: a `SearchValueFilter` (a group of checkbox values) or a `SearchDateFilter` (a date range). Filters AND together; the values of one value filter OR.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Key` | `string` | `""` | Names the attribute of `SearchResultItem` the filter reads (see `Attributes`). |
| `Title` | `string` | `""` | The heading above the filter ("Type", "Team", "Edited"). |
| `Caption` | `string?` | `null` | A muted line under the filter ("Applies to docs and files"). |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### SearchValueFilter

A group of checkbox values over one attribute. Tick several values to see results with any of them. Leave `Values` empty to list the values found in the items (in the order they first appear); list them yourself to fix their order and labels. `SearchResults` writes each value's `Count`: the results that value would show with the query and the other filters applied.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Key` | `string` | `""` | Names the attribute of `SearchResultItem` the filter reads (see `Attributes`). |
| `Title` | `string` | `""` | The heading above the filter ("Type", "Team", "Edited"). |
| `Caption` | `string?` | `null` | A muted line under the filter ("Applies to docs and files"). |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### SearchFilterValue

One value of a `SearchValueFilter`: a checkbox with a label and a count.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Value` | `string` | `""` | What an item's attribute has to equal (ignoring case). |
| `Label` | `string?` | `null` | The text beside the checkbox; `Value` when null. |
| `Count` | `int` | `0` | The results behind the value. `SearchResults` writes it while it filters; with `IsFilteringEnabled` false it is yours (a server's facet counts) and the control only reads it. A value with a count of 0 is dimmed and cannot be ticked, but keeps its place. |
| `IsSelected` | `bool` | `false` | Whether the checkbox is ticked (two-way). |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### SearchDateFilter

A date range over `Date`, edited with a two-thumb slider. The range spans `Minimum` to `Maximum` (the oldest and newest item date when null); `Start` and `End` are the chosen ends (null: that end of the range). Items of kinds outside `AppliesTo` pass the filter, so a range over documents does not hide people.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Minimum` | `DateTimeOffset?` | `null` | The oldest date the slider reaches. Null: the oldest item date. |
| `Maximum` | `DateTimeOffset?` | `null` | The newest date the slider reaches. Null: the newest item date. |
| `Start` | `DateTimeOffset?` | `null` | The chosen start of the range (two-way). Null: the minimum. |
| `End` | `DateTimeOffset?` | `null` | The chosen end of the range (two-way). Null: the maximum. |
| `AppliesTo` | `string?` | `null` | The kinds the range applies to, as a comma separated list ("Docs, Files"). Empty: every item. Also words the default caption ("Applies to docs and files"). |
| `Key` | `string` | `""` | Names the attribute of `SearchResultItem` the filter reads (see `Attributes`). |
| `Title` | `string` | `""` | The heading above the filter ("Type", "Team", "Edited"). |
| `Caption` | `string?` | `null` | A muted line under the filter ("Applies to docs and files"). |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

## Accessibility

- The control is a search landmark named by `Label`, which also names the search field. The clear button, the filters
  button and the close buttons have their own names.
- The results are a list named with the result count, and the count line is a polite live region, so the number of results is
  announced as it changes. The result under the cursor is the list's selected item, and each result is named with its title,
  kind and subtitle.
- Each filter is a group named by its title. Each value is a checkbox named with its label and count; a value without results is
  disabled but keeps its place. The date range's thumbs are named after the filter ("Edited start", "Edited end") and move one
  day with the arrow keys and 30 days with PageUp and PageDown. A chip is named with its filter and value, and its cross
  says "Remove filter" followed by that name.
- The sort switch is a segmented list: the arrow keys select the previous or next option, and only the selected one is a tab stop.
- In the search field, ArrowDown walks the suggestions while the popup is open, otherwise it moves into the results. Enter runs
  the highlighted suggestion or the typed text, and with the popup closed it opens the result under the cursor. Escape closes
  the popup, then clears the query. "/" or Ctrl+F (Cmd+F on macOS) moves focus to the field while focus is inside the control,
  and typing in the results continues the query in the field.
- In the results, ArrowUp, ArrowDown, Home, End, PageUp and PageDown move the cursor, ArrowUp on the first result returns to
  the field, Enter or Space opens a result and Escape returns to the field.
- The detail and the filters sheet are modal: focus moves in, stays inside, Escape, the close button or a press on the dimmed
  page closes them, and focus returns to where it was. Closing a modal does not reopen the suggestions popup by itself.
- Disabled results stay in the list and are dimmed, but the cursor skips them, so a keyboard user never lands on an item
  that cannot be opened.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Where | Action |
|---|---|---|
| `/`, `Ctrl+F` (`Cmd+F`) | Anywhere in the control | Move focus to the search field and select its text |
| Focus | Search field | Open the suggestions popup |
| `ArrowDown` / `ArrowUp` | Search field, popup open | Move the highlight through the suggestions; ArrowUp on the first one removes it |
| `Enter` | Search field, popup open | Run the highlighted suggestion, or the text as typed |
| `Escape` | Search field | Close the popup; with the popup closed, clear the query |
| `ArrowDown` | Search field, popup closed | Move into the results; the cursor is on the first one |
| `Enter` | Search field, popup closed | Open the result under the cursor |
| `ArrowUp` / `ArrowDown` | Results | Move the cursor by one result |
| `Home` / `End`, `PageUp` / `PageDown` | Results | Move the cursor to the first or last listed result, or by a page |
| `ArrowDown`, `PageDown` on the last listed result | Results | List the next page, then move |
| `ArrowUp` on the first result | Results | Return to the search field and clear the cursor |
| `Enter` or `Space` | Results | Open the result under the cursor |
| `Escape` | Results | Return to the search field |
| Any character | Results | Return to the field and add it to the query |
| `ArrowLeft` / `ArrowRight` | Date range thumb | Move one day |
| `PageUp` / `PageDown` | Date range thumb | Move 30 days |
| `Space` | Filter value | Tick or untick the value |
| `ArrowLeft` / `ArrowRight` | Sort switch | Select the previous or next option, wrapping around |
| `Escape` | Detail or filters sheet | Close it; focus returns to where it was |
| Pointer hover | Results | Move the cursor to the row under the pointer (touch does not) |
| Click | Results | Open the result |

## Motion

- The cursor glides between results: on a spring when it follows the pointer, and with a 70 ms tween when it follows the
  arrow keys. It fades in when it first appears and fades out when it is cleared. The suggestions popup has the same cursor.
- Results that were not shown before fade in and rise 4 pixels, 35 ms apart, for at most four rows. Results that stay do not
  move, so typing that only narrows the list animates nothing.
- The count and the time roll to their new values. The selected sort option's pill glides between the options on the morph
  spring.
- The bar of active filters opens and closes with a height spring, and its chips appear with the filters. The column's
  "Clear all" link fades in and out, and the field's clear button pops in and out.
- The suggestions popup enters with a small scale and a short rise and leaves quicker, like the other floating surfaces.
- The detail rises into place on wide screens and slides up from the bottom on narrow ones; the filters sheet slides up too.
- Reduced motion keeps the fades and drops every movement: the cursor and the sort pill jump, counts change at once and
  results only fade in. Off applies every change at once.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cursor follows the pointer | Snappy spring | Jumps to the row | Immediate |
| Cursor follows an arrow key | 70 ms tween | Jumps to the row | Immediate |
| Cursor appears or is cleared | Fades in over 80 ms, out over 100 ms | Fades | Immediate |
| New results arrive | Fade in and rise 4 px, staggered 35 ms, up to four rows | Fade in | Immediate |
| Count or time changes | Digits roll to the new value | Changes at once | Immediate |
| Sort option changes | The pill slides on the morph spring | Jumps | Immediate |
| Active filters bar opens or closes | Height spring | Fades | Immediate |
| Suggestions popup opens or closes | Scale and rise with a fade | Fade | Immediate |
| Detail opens | Rises into place (slides up when narrow) | Fade | Immediate |
| Filters sheet opens | Slides up | Fade | Immediate |
| Count line, empty state, loading rows | Crossfade | Fade | Immediate |

## Related

- `CommandPalette` for actions and navigation from anywhere in the app.
- `ExpandingSearch` for a compact search in a header.
- `SearchField` for filtering a list on the page.
- `Checkbox`, `Slider` and `SegmentedControl`, which this block's filters and sort switch are built from.
- `EmptyState` and `Skeleton`, which this block uses for no results and loading.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `CommandPalette` | People run commands or jump to a page from anywhere in the app |
| `ExpandingSearch` | Search sits in a header or a toolbar and opens on demand |
| `SearchField` | The text filters a list that is already on the page |
| `FilterToolbar` | Filters sit above a table or a list, as chips, without a search page |
| `Tabs` | The kinds are views of one page rather than filters of a query |
| `Table` | The results are records to compare by column |

# Login

> Sign in and sign up pages, from a compact code card to full screen split and immersive layouts.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc.Blocks`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc.Blocks --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/blocks/login

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.LoginSignInPreviewDemo">
    <!-- Arc's preview: the card centred, everything simulated. Try emma@gmial.com, a wrong code, then 123456. -->
    <arc:SignIn x:Name="Card" HorizontalAlignment="Center" Margin="0,24" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class LoginSignInPreviewDemo : UserControl
{
    public LoginSignInPreviewDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        // Arc's teammates keep their photo when their address is typed (emma@…, marcus@…); these portraits are drawn.
        foreach (var teammate in SignInDemoData.Teammates())
        {
            Card.Accounts.Add(teammate);
        }
    }
}
```

Login is one block with five layouts, each a control of its own with the same flow vocabulary: a passwordless card that morphs from an email address to a six digit code to the signed in account (`SignIn`), a centered passkey first layout over a ring backdrop (`LoginCentered`), a full screen layout with the form beside a picture (`LoginSplit`), a full screen picture with a glass card (`LoginImmersive`) and a create account form with a password strength meter (`SignupForm`). Every layout runs a simulated flow out of the box, so nothing is sent anywhere until a host wires an async handler; `Login` hosts any of them behind a `Variant` property.

## When to use

### Email code

- The entry screen of an app that signs people in with a code sent by email.
- A sign in card that also offers passkeys and single sign-on.
- Passwordless flows that should confirm the account before continuing.

### Centered

- A full-window sign in or sign up page where passkeys are the main method.
- Auth flows that fall back to a six digit email code.
- Products that want one card for signing in and creating an account.

### Split

- The sign-in page of a product with a brand picture or illustration to show beside the form.
- Email-first sign-in, where the account (name, avatar) is known before the password is typed.
- Password sign-in with single sign-on as an alternative, and a self-service password reset.

### Immersive

- **A product without passwords**: the person types an address, follows the link in their inbox and is in. The
  page explains each beat and keeps the address visible so a typo is easy to catch.
- **A branded entry point**: the picture fills the page, so the sign-in screen carries the product's mood (a
  landscape, the team's office, the product itself). Use `Photo`; without one the page draws a dusk landscape.
- **Sign in and sign up on one page**: the header switch flips the heading and the account-creation copy; the flow
  (send a link, confirm it) is the same for both.

### Sign up

`SignupForm` is the client side of an email and password sign-up: provider buttons, a full name, a work email, a password
with a strength meter, a product updates opt-in, and an in-place completion panel once the account exists.

- Sign-up screens that should show password strength and a product updates opt-in.
- Flows that want the success panel in place instead of a redirect.
- Sign-ups that offer Google, Apple and GitHub beside the form.

## When not to use

### Email code

- **Password sign in**: use `LoginCentered`, `LoginSplit` or `LoginImmersive`.
- **Creating an account**: use `SignupForm`.
- **Only the code step inside your own form**: use `OtpInput` on its own.

### Centered

- Password sign in beside a brand photo: use `LoginSplit`.
- Magic link sign in over a full-bleed photo: use `LoginImmersive`.
- A sign in form inside an existing page: use `SignIn`.

### Split

- Passkey-first sign-in, or a six-digit code by email: use `LoginCentered` or `SignIn`.
- Sign-in by magic link over a full-bleed photo: use `LoginImmersive`.
- Creating an account: use `SignupForm`.
- A sign-in form inside an existing page or dialog: use `SignIn`; this block is a whole page.

### Immersive

- **Password sign-in**: use `LoginSplit`, which asks for a password after the email and handles the reset link.
- **One-time codes typed back into the app**: use `SignIn` or `LoginCentered`, which pair the email step with an
  `OtpInput`.
- **Inside a busy screen**: the block expects to be the page (or a large panel). For a small sign-in box inside an
  app, use a dialog with `Input` and `Button`.
- **Pictures with detail in the middle**: the card covers the centre. Choose a picture whose subject sits around the
  card, and move the crop with `PhotoAlignment`.

### Sign up

- **Returning users**: use the Email code (`SignIn`) or Centered (`LoginCentered`) variants.
- **A password inside a form you already have**: use `PasswordField`, or `PasswordStrength` for a field with a rule list.
- **Passwordless or code-based sign-up**: use `OtpInput`.

## Usage

### Email code

##### Email code (SignIn)

`SignIn` is a sign in card that moves from an email address to a six digit code to the signed in account, with a passkey
button and single sign-on buttons under the form. Each step slides in from the side it is heading to while the card's
height follows on a spring; the account's avatar grows from the code step into the signed in state, where a ring draws
around it and a check pops in. Everything in the preview is simulated: type any address, a wrong code, then `123456`.


```xml
<arc:SignIn x:Name="SignIn" HorizontalAlignment="Center" />
```

```csharp
SignIn.SendCodeAsync = SendCodeAsync;
SignIn.VerifyCodeAsync = CheckCodeAsync;
SignIn.SignInWithAsync = SignInWithAsync;
SignIn.SignedIn += (_, e) => OpenDashboard(e.Account);

// Stand-ins for your auth provider: no account from the send (the card derives one), 123456 is right, and a passkey
// or a provider signs in as Robin.
static Task<SignInAccount?> SendCodeAsync(string email, CancellationToken token) => Task.FromResult<SignInAccount?>(null);
static Task<bool> CheckCodeAsync(SignInAccount account, string code, CancellationToken token) => Task.FromResult(code == "123456");
static Task<SignInAccount?> SignInWithAsync(SignInMethod method, CancellationToken token) =>
    Task.FromResult<SignInAccount?>(new SignInAccount("Robin Park", "robin@park.dev"));
static void OpenDashboard(SignInAccount account) { }
```

The card does no authentication itself. Connect three handlers to your auth provider:

- `SendCodeAsync` runs on Continue (and on Resend) with the trimmed address. Return the account to show on the code
  step, or null to derive it from the address (see Accounts below). Throw to stay on the email step with
  `SendFailedMessage` under the field.
- `VerifyCodeAsync` runs with a complete code. Return true to sign in, false for a wrong code. Throwing shows
  `VerifyFailedMessage`.
- `SignInWithAsync` runs for the passkey button and every provider with a `SignInMethod` (`Kind` is `Passkey` or
  `Provider`, `Provider` names it). Return the account, or null for the first known account. Throwing keeps the email
  step and says so in the status line.

Every token is cancelled when `Reset()` is called or the card leaves the visual tree; a result that arrives after that is
ignored. Without handlers the card simulates Arc's preview: a send takes 800 ms, a check 700 ms and accepts `DemoCode`
(`"123456"`), a passkey 1100 ms and a provider 900 ms.

`SignedIn` reports the account and the method (`SignInSignedInEventArgs.Account`, `.Method`) and `SignedInCommand` runs
with the account. `SignedOut` follows the signed in step's Sign out button. `Step`, `Account`, `Method`, `IsBusy` and
`Status` are read-only properties you can bind to; `Email` is two-way, so you can prefill the field.

###### Connecting your auth provider

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.LoginSignInHandlersDemo">
    <!-- Wired to a (fake) auth service: the code is 424242, a passkey signs in as you, and every event is logged. -->
    <StackPanel Spacing="16" HorizontalAlignment="Center" Margin="0,24">
        <arc:SignIn x:Name="Card"
                    CodeHint="This demo's service sends 424242."
                    SignedIn="OnSignedIn"
                    SignedOut="OnSignedOut"
                    SignUpRequested="OnSignUpRequested" />
        <TextBlock x:Name="Log"
                   MaxWidth="432"
                   TextWrapping="Wrap"
                   FontSize="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TypeXS}"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class LoginSignInHandlersDemo : UserControl
{
    private readonly List<string> _log = new();

    public LoginSignInHandlersDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        // Send and check codes through your auth provider; here a fake service answers after a short wait.
        Card.SendCodeAsync = async (email, token) =>
        {
            Write($"send code to {email}");
            await Task.Delay(600, token);
            return null; // derive the name from the address
        };
        Card.VerifyCodeAsync = async (account, code, token) =>
        {
            Write($"check {code} for {account.Email}");
            await Task.Delay(500, token);
            return code == "424242";
        };
        Card.SignInWithAsync = async (method, token) =>
        {
            Write($"sign in with {method}");
            await Task.Delay(700, token);
            return new SignInAccount("Robin Park", "robin@park.dev");
        };
    }

    private void OnSignedIn(object? sender, SignInSignedInEventArgs e) => Write($"SignedIn: {e.Account.Name} with {e.Method}");

    private void OnSignedOut(object? sender, SignInSignedOutEventArgs e) => Write($"SignedOut: {e.Account.Email}");

    // Handled: the app opens its sign up flow, so the card does not say "Sign up opens in your app".
    private void OnSignUpRequested(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        e.Handled = true;
        Write("SignUpRequested: open the sign up page");
    }

    private void Write(string line)
    {
        _log.Insert(0, line);
        if (_log.Count > 4)
        {
            _log.RemoveAt(_log.Count - 1);
        }
        Log.Text = string.Join("\n", _log);
    }
}
```

The demo answers from a fake service: the code is `424242`, the passkey and the providers sign in as Robin Park, and the
log lists the calls and events. `CodeHint` replaces the demo's "For this demo, the code is 123456." helper copy (with a
`VerifyCodeAsync` handler and no `CodeHint` the code field has no helper copy). The demo handles `SignUpRequested`, so
the card does not show its own "Sign up opens in your app" status.

###### The steps

- **Email.** The address is checked as Arc does: once the field loses focus with text in it, or from the first Continue
  on; after that the message follows every keystroke ("Enter your email address." for an empty field, "Enter a full
  address, like name@example.com." otherwise). A common domain typo (`gmial.com`, `hotmial.com`, `outlok.com`, …) opens
  a "Did you mean …?" line under the field; its button puts the fixed address in the field. While a code is being sent,
  Continue shows a spinner and the field is read-only.
- **Code.** The account row shows the avatar, the address and Change (back to the email, with the address selected). The
  code field is an `OtpInput` that takes focus; filling the last slot checks the code, and so do Verify and Enter. A short
  code asks for all six digits; a wrong one clears the slots, shakes them and says so, and typing again clears the error.
  "Resend code in 0:30" counts down (the seconds roll); once it reaches zero, Resend clears the code, sends a new one and
  restarts the timer (`ResendSeconds`).
- **Signed in.** The avatar with a success ring and a check, "Welcome back, Emma", the address, how the person signed in
  and "Remembered for 30 days", and Sign out (back to the email step with the address filled in and selected).

###### Accounts and providers

```xml
<arc:SignIn>
    <arc:SignInAccount Name="Robin Park" Email="robin@park.dev" />
    <arc:SignIn.Providers>
        <arc:SignInProvider Name="Google" Mark="Google" />
        <arc:SignInProvider Name="Okta" />
    </arc:SignIn.Providers>
</arc:SignIn>
```

`Accounts` are the known people (Arc's teammates). When `SendCodeAsync` returns no account, the card follows Arc's
`accountFor`: the part before the @ is split at dots, underscores, plus and minus signs; a known account whose first name
matches the first piece keeps its name and photo, anyone else gets a name from the first two pieces ("jane.doe@acme.io"
is Jane Doe) and initials. `SignInAccount.ForEmail` exposes the same rule. Empty `Accounts` use Arc's five sample
teammates without photos (Arc's portraits are not part of its MIT registry); the preview draws its own.
`SignInAccount.Photo` takes any `IImage`.

`Providers` are the single sign-on buttons, in equal columns. Empty uses Arc's three: Google (its four colour mark),
Apple and GitHub (their marks in the text color). `Mark` picks a built-in mark; `Icon` takes a mark of your own on a 24 by
24 grid, filled in the text color; with neither the button shows the name alone. `AccountsSource` and `ProvidersSource`
take any collection and win over the lists. `IsPasskeyVisible`, `IsProvidersVisible` and `IsSignUpVisible` hide those
parts; with neither a passkey nor providers the "or" divider goes too.

###### Custom copy and providers

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.LoginSignInCustomDemo">
    <!-- Your own copy and providers: a mark of your own is a 24 by 24 path filled in the text colour. -->
    <arc:SignIn HorizontalAlignment="Center"
                Margin="0,24"
                Title="Sign in to Northwind"
                Description="We'll email you a 6 digit code. No password needed."
                PasskeyLabel="Use a passkey"
                IsSignUpVisible="False">
        <arc:SignIn.Providers>
            <arc:SignInProvider Name="Google" Mark="Google" />
            <arc:SignInProvider Name="Microsoft" Icon="M3 3h8.5v8.5H3z M12.5 3H21v8.5h-8.5z M3 12.5h8.5V21H3z M12.5 12.5H21V21h-8.5z" />
        </arc:SignIn.Providers>
    </arc:SignIn>
</UserControl>
```

Every visible string, accessible name and status line is a property with Arc's English text as its default: `Title`,
`Description`, `ContinueLabel`, `CodeTitle`, `WelcomeFormat` ("Welcome back, {0}"), `SignedInStatusFormat` and so on (see
the API table). Format properties take `{0}`.

###### Narrow containers

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.LoginSignInNarrowDemo">
    <!-- At 380 or less the card tightens its padding, heading and provider buttons; the footer wraps. -->
    <Border Width="328" HorizontalAlignment="Center" Margin="0,24">
        <arc:SignIn />
    </Border>
</UserControl>
```

The card follows the width it is given, not the window. It is at most 432 wide. At 380 or less (Arc's container query)
the steps' padding drops to 24 by 20, the heading to 28 px, the account row tightens and the provider buttons use 12 px
text; the footer puts the status line above "No account? Sign up" when they do not fit side by side. Offered 448 or less
(Arc's 480 px phone breakpoint less two 16 px gutters) the card's corners soften to the panel radius.

### Centered

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.LoginLoginCenteredPreviewDemo">
    <!-- Arc's preview: the screen full size in a frame, everything simulated. Try a passkey, or email with a wrong code, then 482913. -->
    <Border Height="720"
            BorderThickness="1"
            CornerRadius="20"
            ClipToBounds="True"
            BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Border}">
        <arc:LoginCentered IsFullScreen="True" />
    </Border>
</UserControl>
```

`LoginCentered` is a passkey-first sign in and sign up screen: a card on a quiet backdrop of concentric rings, with the
product mark and a sign in / sign up switch in the top bar and a status line with Terms and Privacy in the footer. The card
starts on the passkey view (a passkey button, "Use email instead" and Google, Apple and GitHub), falls back to a six digit
code sent by email, and ends on the signed-in account. One control covers both sign in and sign up.

```xml
<arc:LoginCentered x:Name="Login"
                   IsFullScreen="True"
                   TermsHref="https://example.com/terms"
                   PrivacyHref="https://example.com/privacy" />
```

```csharp
Login.SignedIn += (_, e) =>
{
    // e.Email, e.Method (Passkey, EmailCode, Google, Apple, GitHub) and e.Mode (SignIn or SignUp)
    NavigateTo(e.Mode == LoginCenteredMode.SignUp ? "/welcome" : "/app");
};

static void NavigateTo(string route) => Console.WriteLine(route); // your router
```

Set `IsFullScreen` when the block is the whole window: it then fills its host with no border and square corners. Without
it the block draws its own frame (a 1px border, the panel radius) and is at least 640px high.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.LoginLoginCenteredFramedDemo">
    <!-- Without IsFullScreen the block draws its own frame: a 1px border, the panel radius and at least 640px of height. -->
    <arc:LoginCentered />
</UserControl>
```

With no handlers the flow is simulated exactly like Arc's preview: the passkey resolves to `DemoEmail`
("maya@northwind.studio") after 1.7 s, a provider after 0.9 s, a code is "sent" in 0.8 s and checked in 0.7 s, and
`DemoCode` ("482913") is the right one (the code field shows it as helper copy). `SignedIn` (and `SignedInCommand`)
reports the address, the method and the mode once the card reaches the signed-in view. Sign out returns to the passkey
view in sign-in mode and raises `SignedOut`.

#### Route sign ups to onboarding

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.LoginLoginCenteredSignUpDemo">
    <!-- Opens on the sign up form (Mode="SignUp") and routes by mode once the simulated flow succeeds. Code: 482913. -->
    <StackPanel Spacing="12">
        <Border Height="680"
                BorderThickness="1"
                CornerRadius="20"
                ClipToBounds="True"
                BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Border}">
            <arc:LoginCentered x:Name="Login"
                               IsFullScreen="True"
                               Mode="SignUp"
                               SignedIn="OnSignedIn"
                               SignedOut="OnSignedOut" />
        </Border>
        <TextBlock x:Name="Route"
                   Text="Sign up or sign in to see where the app would go."
                   HorizontalAlignment="Center"
                   FontSize="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TypeSM}"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class LoginLoginCenteredSignUpDemo : UserControl
{
    public LoginLoginCenteredSignUpDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
    }

    // New accounts go to onboarding, returning people to the app (Arc's "Route sign ups to onboarding" example).
    private void OnSignedIn(object? sender, LoginCenteredSignedInEventArgs e)
    {
        var route = e.Mode == LoginCenteredMode.SignUp ? "/welcome" : "/app";
        Route.Text = $"{e.Email} ({e.Method}) would open {route}";
    }

    private void OnSignedOut(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) => Route.Text = "Signed out.";
}
```

`Mode` is two-way. Set `Mode="SignUp"` to open the block on the "Create your account" form (for a `/sign-up` route);
setting it later moves the card the way the top bar's switch does. The sign-up flow asks for a work email, verifies the
code ("Verify and create account") and ends on "Welcome to Arc"; `SignedIn` then has `Mode == SignUp`.

#### Connecting your auth service

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.LoginLoginCenteredConnectedDemo">
    <!-- The flow connected to a (fake) auth service: every call is logged; the right code is 424242. -->
    <StackPanel Spacing="12">
        <arc:Switch x:Name="Fail" Content="Fail the next send" HorizontalAlignment="Center" />
        <Border Height="680"
                BorderThickness="1"
                CornerRadius="20"
                ClipToBounds="True"
                BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Border}">
            <arc:LoginCentered x:Name="Login"
                               IsFullScreen="True"
                               TermsHref="https://example.com/terms"
                               PrivacyHref="https://example.com/privacy"
                               Navigate="OnNavigate" />
        </Border>
        <TextBlock x:Name="Log"
                   HorizontalAlignment="Center"
                   TextAlignment="Center"
                   FontFamily="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource MonoFontFamily}"
                   FontSize="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TypeXS}"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class LoginLoginCenteredConnectedDemo : UserControl
{
    private readonly List<string> _log = new();

    public LoginLoginCenteredConnectedDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        // Ask the platform for a passkey (WebAuthn); here a fake device answers after a second.
        Login.PasskeyAsync = async token =>
        {
            Write("passkey requested");
            await Task.Delay(1000, token);
            return "robin@park.dev";
        };
        // Send the code with your mailer; the switch makes the next send fail.
        Login.SendCodeAsync = async (email, mode, token) =>
        {
            Write($"send code to {email} ({mode})");
            await Task.Delay(600, token);
            if (Fail.IsChecked == true)
            {
                Fail.IsChecked = false;
                throw new InvalidOperationException("Mailer unavailable");
            }
        };
        // Check the code on your server.
        Login.VerifyCodeAsync = async (email, code, token) =>
        {
            Write($"check {code} for {email}");
            await Task.Delay(500, token);
            return code == "424242";
        };
        // Start the provider's OAuth flow and return the account it resolves to.
        Login.SignInWithProviderAsync = async (provider, token) =>
        {
            Write($"OAuth with {provider}");
            await Task.Delay(800, token);
            return "robin@park.dev";
        };
        Login.SignedIn += (_, e) => Write($"signed in: {e.Email}, {e.Method}, {e.Mode}");
    }

    // A real app opens its own terms page; the demo only logs the request.
    private void OnNavigate(object? sender, LoginCenteredNavigateEventArgs e)
    {
        e.Handled = true;
        Write($"open {e.Href}");
    }

    private void Write(string line)
    {
        _log.Add(line);
        if (_log.Count > 4)
        {
            _log.RemoveAt(0);
        }
        Log.Text = string.Join("\n", _log);
    }
}
```

Replace the simulation with four asynchronous handlers. Each one receives a `CancellationToken` that is cancelled when the
person moves on (Cancel, Change, the mode switch, Sign out).

```csharp
Login.PasskeyAsync = RequestPasskeyAsync;               // WebAuthn: returns the account's address
Login.SignInWithProviderAsync = SignInWithOAuthAsync;   // OAuth: returns the account's address
Login.SendCodeAsync = SendCodeAsync;                    // your mailer
Login.VerifyCodeAsync = CheckCodeAsync;                 // true accepts the code

// Stand-ins for your auth service.
static Task<string> RequestPasskeyAsync(CancellationToken token) => Task.FromResult("robin@park.dev");
static Task<string> SignInWithOAuthAsync(LoginCenteredProvider provider, CancellationToken token) => Task.FromResult("robin@park.dev");
static Task SendCodeAsync(string email, LoginCenteredMode mode, CancellationToken token) => Task.Delay(600, token);
static Task<bool> CheckCodeAsync(string email, string code, CancellationToken token) => Task.FromResult(code == "424242");
```

| Handler | Without it (Arc's preview) | When it throws |
|---|---|---|
| `PasskeyAsync` | 1.7 s, then `DemoEmail` | `OperationCanceledException`: "Passkey request canceled"; anything else: "Your passkey could not be used" |
| `SignInWithProviderAsync` | 0.9 s, then `DemoEmail` | The provider's button stops spinning; the status says the sign in did not finish |
| `SendCodeAsync` | 0.8 s | The email field shows "We couldn't send a code. Try again." (also used by Resend code) |
| `VerifyCodeAsync` | 0.7 s, accepts `DemoCode` | The code field shows "We couldn't check the code. Try again." |

While a request runs (`IsBusy`), the button that started it shows a spinner and keeps focus, and the other actions are
ignored rather than disabled, as Arc's `aria-disabled` buttons are. After a passkey or a code is accepted the card pauses
(0.64 s and 0.6 s) on "Passkey verified" or "Verified" before it moves on.

The footer links raise `Navigate` with the link and its address. Handle it to open your own page; otherwise an absolute
`http`, `https` or `mailto` address opens with the platform launcher, and an in-page address such as Arc's default
`#terms` only says in the status line where it would go.

#### The flow

| View | Content | Moves to |
|---|---|---|
| Passkey | "Sign in to Arc", the passkey button, "Use email instead", "or", Google / Apple / GitHub | Done (passkey, provider) or Email |
| Email | "Sign in with email" or "Create your account", the email field, Send code / Create account, "Use a passkey instead" (sign in only) | Code |
| Code | "Check your email" with the address and Change, the six digit code, Verify, Resend code (counts down from `ResendSeconds`) | Done, or Email (Change) |
| Done | The drawn check, "Welcome back" or "Welcome to Arc", the account, the method and "Remembered for 30 days", Sign out | Passkey |

The email is checked with Arc's pattern (something, `@`, something, a dot and two more characters). An empty field says
"Enter your email address."; an incomplete one "Enter a full address, like name@example.com.". The error appears once the
person submits, or leaves a field that has text in it, and then follows each keystroke. The code is checked when the last
digit is typed (or on Verify / Enter); a short code says "Enter all 6 digits.", a wrong one clears the field and shakes it.
`Step`, `PasskeyPhase`, `IsBusy`, `Account`, `Method` and `Status` are read-only properties you can bind to; `StartPasskey`,
`CancelPasskey`, `SignInWith`, `SwitchMode` and `SignOut` do what the matching controls do.

#### Narrow screens

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.LoginLoginCenteredNarrowDemo">
    <!-- A phone-sized screen: the block's own width (here 380) selects the tighter bars, card and provider buttons. -->
    <Border Width="380"
            Height="720"
            HorizontalAlignment="Center"
            BorderThickness="1"
            CornerRadius="20"
            ClipToBounds="True"
            BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Border}">
        <arc:LoginCentered IsFullScreen="True" />
    </Border>
</UserControl>
```

The block follows its own width, not the window's. At 520px or less the bars and the stage tighten to 16px, the card's
corners soften to the panel radius and its padding drops to 24px. At 400px or less the title drops from 36px to 28px, the
card's sides to 20px and the provider buttons tighten to 12px text so all three stay on one row.

#### Text and localization

Every string is in `LoginCenteredLabels` (Arc's English copy by default). Replace the whole object to localize or reword
it; sentences that carry a value are functions:

```csharp
Login.Labels = new LoginCenteredLabels
{
    PasskeyTitle = "Sign in to Northwind",
    WelcomeNew = "Welcome to Northwind",
    ResendInName = seconds => $"Resend available in {seconds} s"
};
```

### Split

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.LoginLoginSplitPreviewDemo">
    <!--
        The framed block as a page shows it: below 760 wide the picture column hides and the form stands alone.
        Try fieldnote-demo as the password, rowan@fieldnote.app for a known teammate, or any other address.
    -->
    <arc:LoginSplit Height="640" Margin="0,12">
        <arc:LoginSplit.Accounts>
            <arc:LoginSplitAccount Name="Rowan Hale" Email="rowan@fieldnote.app" />
            <arc:LoginSplitAccount Name="Iris Vance" Email="iris@fieldnote.app" />
            <arc:LoginSplitAccount Name="Teo Marsh" Email="teo@fieldnote.app" />
            <arc:LoginSplitAccount Name="Juno Park" Email="juno@fieldnote.app" />
        </arc:LoginSplit.Accounts>
    </arc:LoginSplit>
</UserControl>
```

`LoginSplit` is a two-column sign-in page. The left column holds the product's brand and a "Sign up" link at the top, the
sign-in steps in the middle and a status line with Terms and Privacy at the bottom; the right column is a full-height
picture. The flow asks for the email first, looks the account up, shows it as a chip above the password field and, once
the password is accepted, opens the account with a progress line before greeting the person by name. Google, Apple and
GitHub buttons skip the password. "Forgot password?" sends a reset link and starts a resend countdown.

```xml
<arc:LoginSplit x:Name="Login"
                IsFullScreen="True"
                BrandName="Fieldnote"
                SignUpHref="https://example.com/signup"
                TermsHref="https://example.com/terms"
                PrivacyHref="https://example.com/privacy" />
```

```csharp
Login.SignedIn += (_, e) =>
{
    // e.Account (Name, Email, Picture), e.Method (Password or Provider) and e.Provider for single sign-on.
    OpenWorkspace(e.Account.Email);
};

static void OpenWorkspace(string email) => Console.WriteLine(email); // your navigation
```

Set `IsFullScreen` when the block is the whole window: it fills its host with square corners and no border. Without it
the block draws its own frame (a 1 px border and 26 px corners) and is at least 640 px high; the preview above is the
framed block at the width of the page, where the picture column is hidden.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.LoginLoginSplitFullScreenDemo">
    <!-- A whole 1280 × 800 screen, scaled to fit the page: the form column beside the picture (columns 5:6 from 1100 wide). -->
    <Border Margin="0,12"
            CornerRadius="20"
            ClipToBounds="True"
            BorderThickness="1"
            BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Border}">
        <Viewbox Stretch="Uniform">
            <arc:LoginSplit IsFullScreen="True" Width="1280" Height="800">
                <arc:LoginSplit.Accounts>
                    <arc:LoginSplitAccount Name="Rowan Hale" Email="rowan@fieldnote.app" />
                    <arc:LoginSplitAccount Name="Iris Vance" Email="iris@fieldnote.app" />
                </arc:LoginSplit.Accounts>
            </arc:LoginSplit>
        </Viewbox>
    </Border>
</UserControl>
```

##### The flow

With no handlers the block simulates a back end with fixed pauses, so it can be tried as it is:

| Step | What happens | Simulated pause |
|---|---|---|
| Email | Continue checks the address (required, then a complete address), then looks the account up: the button shows a spinner, the field turns read-only, the status line says "Finding your account" | 650 ms |
| Password | The chip shows the account; the field's hint shows the demo password (`DemoPassword`, "fieldnote-demo"). A wrong password shows an error and selects what was typed, so the next key replaces it | 800 ms check |
| Accepted | Sign in turns into a check and narrows to a 44 px circle | 775 ms |
| Signing | The account row, "Opening Fieldnote…" and a progress line that fills over 1.4 s | 1.7 s (400 ms with reduced motion) |
| Done | The heading and sentence change in place to the greeting ("All set, Rowan") and how the person signed in; Sign out appears. `SignedIn` is raised | — |

Single sign-on skips the password: the provider's button shows a spinner for 1 s, then the account opens. It signs in the
account of the address in the email field when that address is valid, otherwise `DefaultAccount` (or the first of
`Accounts`). The account chip and Sign out both go back to the email step with the address filled in; `SignOut()` and
`Reset()` do the same from code (`Reset` also clears the address and cancels whatever runs).

`Step` (`Email`, `Password`, `Signing`, `Done`), `Account`, `IsBusy` and `StatusText` are read-only properties, and
`StepChanged` reports every change of step.

##### Accounts

Known accounts are matched on the email without regard to case and show their own name and picture:

```xml
<arc:LoginSplit>
    <arc:LoginSplit.Accounts>
        <arc:LoginSplitAccount Name="Rowan Hale" Email="rowan@fieldnote.app" />
        <arc:LoginSplitAccount Name="Iris Vance" Email="iris@fieldnote.app" />
    </arc:LoginSplit.Accounts>
</arc:LoginSplit>
```

Any other address becomes an account named after the part before the @, split at dots, underscores, plus signs and
hyphens ("ada.lovelace@example.com" signs in as "Ada Lovelace", initials "AL", greeted as "Ada").
`LoginSplitAccount.FromEmail` gives you the same account in code. Bind `AccountsSource` instead of filling `Accounts` when
a view model owns the list.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.LoginLoginSplitEventsDemo">
    <!-- Every event the block raises, newest first. Sign up, Terms and Privacy are handled here instead of opening a page. -->
    <StackPanel Spacing="16" Margin="0,12">
        <arc:LoginSplit x:Name="Split" Height="640" />
        <Border MinHeight="150"
                Padding="16,12"
                CornerRadius="12"
                Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource SurfaceMuted}">

                       FontFamily="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource MonoFontFamily}"
                       FontSize="12"
                       LineHeight="18"
                       TextWrapping="Wrap"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}"
                       Text="Sign in with fieldnote-demo, try Forgot password?, or use a link." />
        </Border>

</UserControl>
```
