# Onboarding illustration

> A compact first-run card whose line drawing morphs from an empty box to files, a team and a badge as people step through it.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc.Blocks`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc.Blocks --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/blocks/onboarding-illustration

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.OnboardingIllustrationPreviewDemo">
    <!-- The four sample steps (Steps left empty). Get started completes the card; Replay intro starts over. -->
    <arc:OnboardingIllustration Label="Northdesk onboarding" Margin="0,24" />
</UserControl>
```

## When to use

`OnboardingIllustration` is the first thing a person sees after creating an account or a workspace: a short card that
explains three or four ideas, one per step, each with a simple picture. The pictures are one line drawing whose shapes
travel from scene to scene, so the steps read as one story (an empty space, content arriving, people joining, done)
rather than four separate slides. Put it in a dialog or a first-run page and send Get started to the flow that sets
the workspace up.

- **A document or workspace product on first launch**: a notes app, a wiki or a file space that starts empty. The
  steps say where content lives, how to bring files in and how to invite people, and Get started opens the new space.
- **A new project, board or channel**: a project tool that walks a person through the first board, or a team chat app
  that creates a channel and invites members. Three steps are often enough.
- **A feature that changes how people work**: shared review, comments on a line, or a new import. A short tour of three
  or four steps before the person uses it for the first time.
- **A tour people come back to**: the completed state offers Replay intro, so the same card can live behind a Help menu
  entry such as "Show the tour again".

## When not to use

- **Tasks people complete over days**: use a checklist that tracks each task's progress and stays visible until the
  last task is done. This card does not remember which steps a person has read.
- **A form that collects information in several steps**: use `Stepper` or a multi-step form. This card shows
  information only; it has no fields and no validation.
- **A feature section on a marketing page**: use a feature block with a larger picture and a call to action. The card
  is sized for a dialog (at most 440 px wide).
- **Long explanations**: a step holds a title and a sentence or two. Material that needs headings, lists or code
  belongs in the documentation, with a link from the last step.

## Usage

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:OnboardingIllustration Label="Northdesk onboarding"
                                GetStartedCommand="{Binding CreateWorkspaceCommand}" />
</UserControl>
```

`OnboardingIllustration` derives from `TemplatedControl`. With no steps it shows four sample steps, one for each
scene, so it looks complete before you write any text. The block does no work of its own: it moves between steps,
raises events and leaves the rest to the app. Handle `GetStarted` (or bind `GetStartedCommand`) to create the
workspace, close the dialog or open the next page.

### Anatomy

1. **Card**: at most 440 px wide (narrower when its container is), a 1 px border, a 20 px corner radius, the raised
   surface color and the raised shadow. `IsFramed="False"` removes the border, the radius and the shadow.
2. **Stage**: the muted surface with a 1 px line below it. Padding 40 px above, 20 px at the sides and 16 px below.
3. **Drawing**: a 320 by 200 canvas scaled to fit, at most 352 by 220 px. Seven rounded shapes, a dotted trail, three
   short lines and a check mark. The 1.5 px strokes scale with the drawing.
4. **Skip**: a 28 px pill 10 px from the stage's top right corner, on every step but the last.
5. **Copy**: the step's title (the display face, 18 px, medium) over its sentence (14 px, secondary text). The copy
   area is at least 72 px high, so a one-line sentence and a two-line sentence leave the buttons in the same place.
6. **Step dots**: one 6 px dot per step; the current step's dot is 20 px wide. Done steps use the muted text color,
   the current step the accent and later steps the strong border color. Each dot is a button with a 32 px hit area.
7. **Back**: an outlined 36 px button with an arrow. On the first step and in the completed state it looks disabled
   but keeps its place in the Tab order.
8. **Main button**: 136 px wide and filled with the foreground color. It says Next, then Get started on the last step,
   then Replay intro once the onboarding is complete. Its width never changes with the label.

### Scenes

Each step names a scene. The scenes share the same shapes, and each shape plays a role in every scene, so moving from
one step to the next looks like one picture changing rather than a slide changing.

| Scene | What it shows | Use it for |
|---|---|---|
| `Folder` | An empty open box with a plus sign | A new, empty space; the first step |
| `Files` | Three pages dropping into the box while a note flies in along a dotted trail | Bringing content in: imports, uploads, connected sources |
| `Team` | Three people under a shared board; a dotted comment points at a highlighted line | Inviting people, sharing, reviewing together |
| `Badge` | A round badge with two ribbons, three rays and a check mark that draws in | Done: the last step |

A scene may appear on several steps; two steps with the same scene change only their text. Steps do not need to follow
the order above, but the story reads best when they do, because each shape moves to its next role.

### Your own steps

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.OnboardingIllustrationCustomStepsDemo">
    <!-- Own steps, completion text and button words (OnboardingIllustrationDemoData). -->
    <arc:OnboardingIllustration x:Name="Card"
                                Margin="0,24"
                                Label="Fieldnote onboarding"
                                CompletedTitle="Study created"
                                CompletedDescription="Open the tour again from Help whenever you like." />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class OnboardingIllustrationCustomStepsDemo : UserControl
{
    public OnboardingIllustrationCustomStepsDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Card.Steps.AddRange(OnboardingIllustrationDemoData.ResearchSteps());
        // The labels hold functions for sentences with numbers, so they are set in code.
        Card.Labels = OnboardingIllustrationDemoData.ResearchLabels();
    }
}
```

```xml
<arc:OnboardingIllustration Label="Fieldnote onboarding"
                            CompletedTitle="Study created"
                            CompletedDescription="Open the tour again from Help whenever you like.">
    <arc:OnboardingStep Scene="Folder"
                        Title="Name your research space"
                        Description="A space holds one study. Start with the April interviews and add more studies later."
                        SceneDescription="An empty open box with a plus sign beside it" />
    <arc:OnboardingStep Scene="Files"
                        Title="Import your recordings"
                        Description="Drop audio, transcripts and notes. Fieldnote tags each file by speaker and date."
                        SceneDescription="Recordings dropping into the open box while a note flies in" />
</arc:OnboardingIllustration>
```

`Steps` is an `AvaloniaList<OnboardingStep>` and the control's content, so steps can be written inside the element.
A view model can supply them through `StepsSource` instead; it wins over `Steps`, and changes to an observable
collection show at once. Editing a step's `Title`, `Description` or `Scene` while it is shown updates the card in place.

`SceneDescription` is the drawing's accessible name for that step. Describe what the picture shows, in a short
phrase: "Three people gathered around one shared board".

The button words, the dots' accessible names and the announced status texts come from `Labels`, an
`OnboardingIllustrationLabels` object with English defaults. Texts with numbers are functions, so word order can change
in other languages:

```csharp
card.Labels = new OnboardingIllustrationLabels
{
    Skip = "Skip tour",
    GetStarted = "Open study",
    ReplayIntro = "Show tour",
    StepStatus = (step, count) => $"Tour step {step} of {count}",
    DotName = (step, title) => $"Tour step {step}: {title}"
};
```

### Steps, completion and events

| Action | Result | Event |
|---|---|---|
| Next (main button, steps before the last) | The next step | `StepChanged` (`Next`) |
| Back | The previous step; nothing on the first step | `StepChanged` (`Back`) |
| A step dot | That step, even several steps away; leaves the completed state | `StepChanged` (`Dot`) |
| Left / Right arrow | The previous or next step; nothing at either end or once complete | `StepChanged` (`Keyboard`) |
| Skip | The last step (not the completed state) | `StepChanged` (`Skip`), then `Skipped` |
| Get started (last step) | The completed state, if `IsCompletionVisible` | `GetStarted` |
| Replay intro | The first step | `StepChanged` (`Replay`), then `Replayed` |

`CurrentIndex` (0-based) and `IsCompleted` are two-way, so a view model can follow the card and move it. Setting
`IsCompleted` to true moves to the last step; setting `CurrentIndex` while complete leaves the completed state. The
methods `Next`, `Back`, `GoTo`, `Skip`, `Complete` and `Replay` do the same from code and return false when there was
nothing to do.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.OnboardingIllustrationControlledDemo">
    <!-- The page owns the step: the segmented control sets CurrentIndex, the switch sets IsCompleted, and both follow the card. -->
    <StackPanel Spacing="20" Margin="0,12">
        <StackPanel Orientation="Horizontal" Spacing="16" HorizontalAlignment="Center">
            <arc:SegmentedControl x:Name="Step" SelectionChanged="OnStepSelected">
                <arc:SegmentedOption Value="0" Label="Step 1" />
                <arc:SegmentedOption Value="1" Label="Step 2" />
                <arc:SegmentedOption Value="2" Label="Step 3" />
                <arc:SegmentedOption Value="3" Label="Step 4" />
            </arc:SegmentedControl>
            <arc:Switch x:Name="Done" Content="Completed" VerticalAlignment="Center" IsCheckedChanged="OnDoneChanged" />
        </StackPanel>
        <arc:OnboardingIllustration x:Name="Card" Label="Northdesk onboarding" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class OnboardingIllustrationControlledDemo : UserControl
{
    private bool _syncing;

    public OnboardingIllustrationControlledDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Step.SelectedValue = "0";
        // The card writes CurrentIndex and IsCompleted back (Next, Back, the dots, the arrows, Get started).
        Card.PropertyChanged += (_, e) =>
        {
            if (e.Property == OnboardingIllustration.CurrentIndexProperty || e.Property == OnboardingIllustration.IsCompletedProperty)
            {
                Sync();
            }
        };
    }

    private void Sync()
    {
        _syncing = true;
        Step.SelectedValue = Card.CurrentIndex.ToString();
        Done.IsChecked = Card.IsCompleted;
        _syncing = false;
    }

    private void OnStepSelected(object? sender, SelectionChangedEventArgs e)
    {
        if (!_syncing && Card is not null && Step.SelectedValue is string value && int.TryParse(value, out var index))
        {
            Card.CurrentIndex = index;
        }
    }

    private void OnDoneChanged(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        if (!_syncing && Card is not null)
        {
            Card.IsCompleted = Done.IsChecked == true;
        }
    }
}
```

`StepChanged` carries the old index, the new index and the reason, including `Programmatic` for changes made from code.
`GetStartedCommand` and `SkipCommand` run after their events, with the event arguments as the parameter.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.OnboardingIllustrationEventsLogDemo">
    <!-- Three steps of an invite flow; every event the card raises is listed under it, newest first. -->
    <StackPanel Spacing="16" Margin="0,12">
        <arc:OnboardingIllustration x:Name="Card" Label="Channel setup" CompletedTitle="Invites sent" CompletedDescription="Replay the steps to add another channel." />
        <Border MaxWidth="440"
                MinHeight="132"
                Padding="16,12"
                CornerRadius="12"
                Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource SurfaceMuted}">
            <TextBlock x:Name="Log"
                       FontFamily="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource MonoFontFamily}"
                       FontSize="12"
                       LineHeight="18"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}"
                       Text="Use the buttons, the dots or the arrow keys." />
        </Border>
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class OnboardingIllustrationEventsLogDemo : UserControl
{
    private readonly List<string> _lines = new();

    public OnboardingIllustrationEventsLogDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Card.Steps.AddRange(OnboardingIllustrationDemoData.InviteSteps());
        Card.StepChanged += (_, e) => Add($"StepChanged  {e.OldIndex} → {e.NewIndex}  ({e.Reason})");
        Card.Skipped += (_, _) => Add("Skipped");
        Card.GetStarted += (_, _) => Add("GetStarted   (send the invites here)");
        Card.Replayed += (_, _) => Add("Replayed");
    }

    private void Add(string line)
    {
        _lines.Insert(0, line);
        if (_lines.Count > 6)
        {
            _lines.RemoveAt(_lines.Count - 1);
        }
        Log.Text = string.Join(Environment.NewLine, _lines);
    }
}
```

```csharp
card.GetStarted += async (_, _) =>
{
    await workspaces.CreateAsync(name);
    dialog.Close();
};
```

When the app closes the dialog itself, set `IsCompletionVisible="False"`: Get started then raises `GetStarted` and the
card stays on the last step instead of showing its completed state. Leave it on when the card stays on screen (a Help
page or a side panel), so the person sees that the tour is done and can replay it.

### Narrow layouts

The card follows its own width, not the window's. Narrower than 410 px it switches to a compact layout: 42 px above
the drawing and 12 px around it, 16 px around the copy, a smaller title, a copy area of at least 88 px (room for three
lines), Back as a 36 px arrow button (still named "Back" for screen readers) and a 128 px main button. The drawing
shrinks with the card and keeps its proportions.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.OnboardingIllustrationNarrowDemo">
    <!-- A 358 wide phone screen: the card fills it edge to edge (IsFramed off) and switches to its compact layout. -->
    <Border Width="358"
            Margin="0,12"
            HorizontalAlignment="Center"
            BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Border}"
            BorderThickness="1"
            CornerRadius="28"
            ClipToBounds="True"
            Padding="0,24,0,32"
            Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource SurfaceRaised}">
        <arc:OnboardingIllustration IsFramed="False" Label="Northdesk onboarding" />
    </Border>
</UserControl>
```

On a phone, where the card fills the screen from edge to edge, set `IsFramed="False"`.

### Using motion with restraint

The morph is the card's signature: the box becomes the papers' destination, the papers become people and the people
become a badge. It works because each step is short and the person controls the pace.

- Keep each step to a title and a sentence or two. The drawing carries the change; long copy pulls attention away from
  it and makes the person wait for the text instead.
- Let people drive the steps. Do not advance the card on a timer: the morph takes about a second, and a step that
  moves on its own while someone reads is lost.
- Reduced motion replaces the morph with a 240 ms crossfade of the whole picture, and the copy fades without moving.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.OnboardingIllustrationReducedMotionDemo">
    <!-- Reduced motion for this card only: scenes crossfade, the copy fades, the dots jump; no parallax. -->
    <arc:OnboardingIllustration Margin="0,24"
                                Label="Northdesk onboarding"
                                arc:ArcMotion.Level="Reduced" />
</UserControl>
```

### Content guidelines

- **Title**: what the person does or gets in this step, in four to seven words, sentence case: "Bring the files you
  already use". No ending punctuation.
- **Sentence**: one or two sentences with a concrete example from their space: "Drag in slides, sheets, and PDFs."
  Mention real names (a project, a teammate) when the app knows them.
- **Last step**: confirm what is ready, with counts if they are known: "Spring launch notes now has 5 files and 2
  teammates."
- **Completed state**: say what happened and how to see the tour again, in one short sentence each.
- **Scene description**: describe the picture, not the step: "Pages dropping into the open box", not "Import step".

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| Welcome to our amazing platform! | Set up your first space |
| Step 2 | Bring the files you already use |
| You can do lots of things with teams. | Invite Ana and Ruben to the same draft. |
| Success! | You are all set |
| Finish | Get started |

### Best practices

**Do**

- Keep the tour to three or four steps; with more, put the rest in the product where people meet it.
- Use the scenes in story order (`Folder`, `Files`, `Team`, `Badge`) so every shape moves to its next role.
- Send Get started somewhere useful: the new workspace, the import dialog, the first project.
- Keep Skip on. People who know the product already should reach the end in one press.
- Offer the tour again from a Help menu, and show the completed state there so Replay intro is one press away.

**Avoid**

- Collecting input in the card. It has no fields; use a form for settings and names.
- Advancing on a timer or on scroll. The person decides when to move on.
- Hiding the dots. They show how long the tour is and let people jump back to a step they want to read again.
- Using the badge scene before the last step: it says "done", which confuses people in the middle of a tour.

### Common questions

**How do I show the card only once?** The card does not remember anything. Store a flag when `GetStarted` (or
`Skipped`) is raised and do not open the dialog next time.

**Why does Back stay focusable on the first step?** Back is marked unavailable but stays in the Tab order (Arc's
`aria-disabled`), so the focus does not jump when a step makes it unavailable. Screen readers announce it as disabled,
and pressing it does nothing.

**What happens to focus after Skip?** Skip disappears on the last step. If it had focus, focus moves to the main
button (Get started), so keyboard users can carry on with Enter.

**Can a step reuse a scene?** Yes. Two steps with the same scene change only their text when you move between them.

**Can the card have more than four steps?** Yes, and as few as one (then the only button is Get started). The dots
grow with the steps; past five or six the tour usually needs shortening rather than more dots.

## API reference

### OnboardingIllustration

A compact first-run card: a line drawing on top whose shapes morph from scene to scene (an empty box, files dropping in, a team around a board, a badge), and below it the step's title and sentence, a row of step dots, Back and a main button. The main button says Next, then Get started on the last step, then Replay intro once the onboarding is complete; Skip in the drawing's corner jumps to the last step. The Left and Right arrow keys step back and forth anywhere in the card. With no `Steps` the card shows four sample steps, one per scene.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Steps` | `AvaloniaList<OnboardingStep>` | – | *Read-only.* The steps, in order (each with its scene and text). Empty (the default) shows four sample steps. |
| `StepsSource` | `IEnumerable<OnboardingStep>?` | `null` | Steps from a view model; when set it wins over `Steps`, and changes to an observable collection show at once. |
| `CurrentIndex` | `int` | `0` | The step shown, 0-based (two way). Values outside the steps are clamped. |
| `IsCompleted` | `bool` | `false` | True once Get started was pressed (two way): the card shows `CompletedTitle` and `CompletedDescription`, Back is unavailable and the main button replays the steps. Setting it moves to the last step; a step dot or a new `CurrentIndex` leaves it. |
| `IsSkipVisible` | `bool` | `true` | Shows Skip in the drawing's corner on every step but the last (default true). |
| `IsCompletionVisible` | `bool` | `true` | Get started enters the completed state (default true). False: Get started only raises `GetStarted` and the app moves on (closes the dialog, opens the workspace). |
| `IsFramed` | `bool` | `true` | Draws the card's border, rounded corners and shadow (default true). False for a card that fills a sheet or a phone screen edge to edge. |
| `CompletedTitle` | `string` | `"Your space is open"` | The title of the completed state. |
| `CompletedDescription` | `string` | `"Replay the tour to walk through each step again."` | The sentence of the completed state. |
| `Label` | `string` | `"Onboarding"` | The accessible name of the card's region, such as "Northdesk onboarding". |
| `Labels` | `OnboardingIllustrationLabels` | – | The button labels, the dots' names and the announced status texts. |
| `GetStartedCommand` | `ICommand?` | `null` | Runs when Get started is pressed, after `GetStarted`; its parameter is the event arguments. |
| `SkipCommand` | `ICommand?` | `null` | Runs when Skip is pressed, after `Skipped`; its parameter is the event arguments. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `StepChanged` | `OnboardingStepChangedEventArgs` | The step changed (Next, Back, a dot, an arrow key, Skip, Replay or code), with the old and new index and the reason. |
| `GetStarted` | `RoutedEventArgs` | Get started was pressed on the last step: start the app's own flow here. |
| `Skipped` | `RoutedEventArgs` | Skip was pressed (or `Skip` called); the card is now on the last step. |
| `Replayed` | `RoutedEventArgs` | Replay intro was pressed (or `Replay` called); the card is back on the first step. |

Pseudo-classes: `:first`, `:last`, `:completed`, `:compact`, `:unframed`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

### OnboardingStep

One step of `OnboardingIllustration`: its drawing, its title and sentence, and the accessible description of the drawing. A change to any of them shows at once in the block.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Scene` | `OnboardingScene` | `Folder` | The drawing shown for this step. |
| `Title` | `string` | `""` | The step's title (one short line). |
| `Description` | `string` | `""` | The sentence under the title (two lines at most fit without moving the buttons). |
| `SceneDescription` | `string` | `""` | What the drawing shows, read by screen readers as the image's name. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### OnboardingIllustrationLabels

Every word `OnboardingIllustration` shows or announces besides the steps themselves, in English by default. Replace the instance to translate or reword; texts with numbers are functions so the word order can change.

### OnboardingStepChangedEventArgs

Arguments of `StepChanged`.

Derives from `RoutedEventArgs`: every member of `RoutedEventArgs` works as well.

## Accessibility

- The card is a region named by `Label` ("Northdesk onboarding"). Put it in a dialog with its own name when it opens
  on first run.
- The drawing is an image named by the current step's `SceneDescription`; the name changes with the step.
- Every change of step reads the new title, sentence and position ("Step 2 of 4") through a polite live region. The
  completed state reads its title and sentence followed by "Onboarding complete".
- The dots are a group named "Onboarding steps". Each dot is a button named "Step 2: Bring the files you already use",
  and the current one reports "Current step".
- Back is reported as disabled on the first step and in the completed state, but stays focusable. In the compact layout
  it shows only its arrow and keeps the name "Back".
- Focus stays where it was after every action: on the main button after Next, Get started and Replay intro, on Back
  after Back, on the dot after a dot. When Skip disappears while it has focus, focus moves to the main button.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` | Move through Skip, each step dot, Back and the main button |
| `Left` / `Right` | Previous or next step, from anywhere in the card; focus does not move. Nothing at either end, and nothing once complete (`Right` never presses Get started) |
| `Enter` / `Space` | Press the focused button or dot |

## Motion

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| The step changes | Every shape springs to the next scene (centers in about half a second, sizes, corners and turns a little slower), one after another 30 ms apart; going back, the last shape moves first. The trail curves in at 100 ms and its dots appear at 160 ms; the lines follow at 120, 160 and 200 ms; colors cross over in 480 ms | The old picture fades out as the new one fades in, 240 ms | Immediate |
| The badge appears | The check mark draws in from 320 ms over 480 ms | Shown complete | Shown complete |
| A second change within about 0.7 s | Every shape turns toward the new scene at once, keeping its speed | Crossfade | Immediate |
| The copy changes | The old text lifts 4 px and blurs out in 180 ms; the new text rises 6 px out of a blur from 80 ms, over 480 ms | The texts fade (180 ms out, 480 ms in) | Immediate |
| The main button's label changes | The old label lifts out in 180 ms; the new one rises in over 240 ms | The labels fade | Immediate |
| A step dot | The current dot widens to 20 px and the old one narrows to 6 px on a spring; the color crosses over in 240 ms | Width at once; the color still crosses over | Immediate |
| Skip appears or goes | Fades in 160 ms | Fades in 160 ms | Immediate |
| A mouse moves over the stage | The shapes drift toward the pointer by up to 6 px across and 4 px down, more for shapes in front | No drift | No drift |

The card has no entrance animation and no motion at rest: the drawing only moves after an action or under the mouse.

## Related

- `EmptyStates` for an empty view whose drawing morphs between four situations.
- `Stepper` for a multi-step task that collects input and validates each step.
- `Dialog` to host the card on first run.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `OnboardingIllustration` | A short first-run tour of three or four ideas, each with a picture |
| `EmptyStates` | A view is empty and the drawing explains why |
| `Stepper` | People fill in a form in several steps |
| `Dialog` | The card opens on top of the app on first run |

# OTP input

> A six digit verification flow with paste support and keyboard navigation.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc.Blocks`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc.Blocks --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/blocks/otp-input

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.OtpInputPreviewDemo">
    <!-- Arc's preview: six digits, three of them typed, centred on the page. Type, paste or use the arrow keys. -->
    <arc:OtpInput Value="482"
                  Description="Use the six digit code from your email."
                  HorizontalAlignment="Center" />
</UserControl>
```

## When to use

Use `OtpInput` for the step after you have sent someone a one-time code: a row of single-character slots, one per
character, with a visible label and helper copy underneath. Typing fills a slot and moves to the next, a pasted code
spreads over the slots, and the arrow keys and Backspace move through the row the way people expect. Check the code on
your server; the control only collects it.

- **Verification codes** sent by email or text message.
- **Two-factor authentication** codes from an authenticator app.
- **Short PINs and recovery codes**, with another `Length` or `InputMode="Text"`.

## When not to use

- **Secrets people type from memory** (passwords, passphrases): use `PasswordField`.
- **Any other text**: use `Input`.

## Usage

```xml
<arc:OtpInput x:Name="Code"
              Description="We sent a 6-digit code to your email."
              AutoFocus="True" />
```

```csharp
Code.Completed += async (_, e) =>
{
    Code.IsReadOnly = true;                       // keep focus, ignore typing while the code is checked
    var ok = await CheckCodeAsync(e.Code);       // your server call
    Code.IsReadOnly = false;
    if (!ok)
    {
        Code.Value = "";
        Code.ErrorMessage = "That code didn't match. Check the latest email and try again.";
        Code.FocusSlot(0);
    }
};

static Task<bool> CheckCodeAsync(string code) => Task.FromResult(code == "123456");
```

`Value` holds the code and binds two-way. `Completed` is raised after every edit that leaves all slots filled (typing the
last character, or a paste), with the code in `OtpInputCompletedEventArgs.Code`; `CompletedCommand` runs with the same
code. Setting `Value` from code never raises `Completed`, so resetting the slots cannot start another check.
`ValueChanged` reports every change with its `ChangeSource`: `Typing`, `Paste` and `Deletion` for the person's edits,
`Programmatic` for yours.

With no configuration the field has six digit slots labelled "Verification code". `Label` is also the name of the group
of slots for screen readers, so give it even when the surrounding page already says what the code is for.

### Verifying a code

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.OtpInputVerifyDemo">
    <!-- A verification step: the last digit checks the code (simulated, 700 ms). A wrong code clears the slots and shakes. -->
    <StackPanel Spacing="16" HorizontalAlignment="Center" Width="360">
        <arc:OtpInput x:Name="Code"
                      Description="For this demo, the code is 123456."
                      Completed="OnCompleted"
                      ValueChanged="OnValueChanged" />
        <arc:Button x:Name="Restart" Content="Start over" Variant="Secondary" HorizontalAlignment="Left" Click="OnRestart" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Interactivity;
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class OtpInputVerifyDemo : UserControl
{
    private const string DemoCode = "123456";

    public OtpInputVerifyDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
    }

    // The code is checked when the last slot is filled; the slots stay focused but ignore typing meanwhile.
    private async void OnCompleted(object? sender, OtpInputCompletedEventArgs e)
    {
        Code.IsReadOnly = true;
        await Task.Delay(700);
        Code.IsReadOnly = false;
        if (e.Code == DemoCode)
        {
            Code.IsSuccess = true;
            Code.Description = "Code verified.";
            return;
        }
        Code.Value = string.Empty;
        Code.ErrorMessage = "That code didn't match. Check the latest email and try again.";
        Code.FocusSlot(0);
    }

    // Typing again clears the error, as Arc's sign-in does.
    private void OnValueChanged(object? sender, OtpInputValueChangedEventArgs e)
    {
        if (e.IsUserEdit && e.NewValue.Length > 0)
        {
            Code.ErrorMessage = null;
        }
    }

    private void OnRestart(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        Code.IsSuccess = false;
        Code.ErrorMessage = null;
        Code.Description = "For this demo, the code is 123456.";
        Code.Value = string.Empty;
        Code.FocusSlot(0);
    }
}
```

The demo checks the code when the last slot is filled (700 ms, simulated). A wrong code clears the slots, shows the error
and shakes the row; typing again clears the error, the way the code step of Arc's sign-in does it:

```csharp
Code.ValueChanged += (_, e) =>
{
    if (e.IsUserEdit && e.NewValue.Length > 0)
    {
        Code.ErrorMessage = null;
    }
};
```

### Errors

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.OtpInputErrorDemo">
    <!-- An error under the helper copy: danger slots and ring. Setting a new error shakes the row once. -->
    <arc:OtpInput Description="For this demo, the code is 123456."
                  ErrorMessage="That code didn't match. Check the latest email and try again."
                  HorizontalAlignment="Center" />
</UserControl>
```

A non-empty `ErrorMessage` shows under the helper copy, turns every slot and the focus ring to the danger color and makes
`IsInvalid` true. Each new error shakes the row once, so a rejected code reads as an answer to the attempt; clearing the
error and setting the same text again shakes it again. Set `IsInvalid` alone for the danger look without a message, or
call `Shake()` to nudge the row yourself.

### Success

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.OtpInputSuccessDemo">
    <!-- A checked code: success slots, read-only until the next step takes over. -->
    <arc:OtpInput Value="482913"
                  Description="Code verified."
                  IsSuccess="True"
                  IsReadOnly="True"
                  HorizontalAlignment="Center" />
</UserControl>
```

`IsSuccess` gives the slots and the ring the success color. Arc's field has no success look (its flows move on to the next
step instead); use it when the field stays on screen after a correct code. An error wins over success.

### Disabled

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.OtpInputDisabledDemo">
    <!-- Every slot disabled: dimmed to .48 on the muted surface, skipped by Tab. -->
    <arc:OtpInput Value="482"
                  Description="Request a new code to try again."
                  IsEnabled="False"
                  HorizontalAlignment="Center" />
</UserControl>
```

`IsEnabled="False"` disables every slot: dimmed to 48 % on the muted surface, skipped by `Tab`, no focus ring.
`IsReadOnly` is the busy state instead: the slots keep focus and the arrow keys, but typing, pasting and deleting are
ignored.

### Length and characters

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.OtpInputLengthDemo">
    <!-- Four digits for a PIN, and eight characters of any kind for a recovery code. -->
    <StackPanel Spacing="32" HorizontalAlignment="Center">
        <arc:OtpInput Label="PIN" Length="4" Description="The four digits you chose for this device." />
        <arc:OtpInput Label="Recovery code"
                      Length="8"
                      InputMode="Text"
                      Description="Letters and digits, from your saved recovery codes." />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```xml
<arc:OtpInput Label="PIN" Length="4" />
<arc:OtpInput Label="Recovery code" Length="8" InputMode="Text" />
```

`Length` sets the number of slots (1 to 32). `InputMode="Numeric"` (the default) drops anything that is not a digit,
from typing and from a paste, and asks touch keyboards for the number pad. `InputMode="Text"` accepts any character.

### How the code fills the slots

The code is one string, as in Arc: slot `i` shows `Value[i]`. Clearing a slot in the middle (Delete) moves the characters
after it one slot to the left, and a character typed into a slot past the end of the code becomes the next character of
the code. A filled slot takes no more typing until its character is selected (double-click it, or reach it with `Tab`) or
deleted. A paste fills the slots from the focused one and ignores what does not fit; the focus moves to the slot after the
last character pasted. An input method or a platform's SMS autofill that inserts several characters at once spreads them
over the slots the same way.

### Narrow containers

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.OtpInputNarrowDemo">
    <!-- 300 wide, as on a small phone: slots 6 apart and 44 high. Narrower still, the slots shrink to fit. -->
    <Border Width="300"
            Padding="16"
            HorizontalAlignment="Center"
            BorderThickness="1"
            CornerRadius="20"
            BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Border}"
            Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Background}">
        <arc:OtpInput Value="482" Description="Use the six digit code from your email." />
    </Border>
</UserControl>
```

The field follows the width it is given, not the window. At 328 px or less (Arc's 360 px phone breakpoint less two 16 px
gutters) the slots move 6 px apart and drop to 44 px high. When even that does not fit, every slot shrinks by the same
amount; the gaps stay. A field that is not stretched (`HorizontalAlignment` other than `Stretch`) is as wide as its widest
part, like Arc's centered preview.

### Text and localization

`Label`, `Description` and `ErrorMessage` are plain text. Each slot's accessible name comes from `SlotLabelFormat`
(default `"{0}, digit {1} of {2}"`: the label, the slot's position and the number of slots).

## API reference

### OtpInput

A row of single-character slots for one-time codes (Arc's OTP input block): a visible label, one slot per character, helper and error copy under the row. Typing fills a slot and moves on; a paste fills the slots from the focused one; arrow keys move between slots and Backspace on an empty slot clears the one before it. Characters rise into their slot, a paste lands as a short left to right wave, one focus ring glides between the slots, and a new error nudges the row side to side once. `Value` is two-way; `Completed` fires when an edit fills the last slot, which is where a host checks the code.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Length` | `int` | `6` | Number of slots (Arc's `length`), 1 to 32. |
| `Value` | `string` | `""` | The code, one character per slot (Arc's `value` and `onChange`); two-way. |
| `Label` | `string?` | `"Verification code"` | The visible label and the name of the group of slots (Arc's required `label`). |
| `Description` | `string?` | `null` | Helper copy under the slots (Arc's `description`). |
| `ErrorMessage` | `string?` | `null` | Error copy under the slots (Arc's `error`); non-empty makes the field invalid, and a new error shakes the row once. |
| `IsInvalid` | `bool` | `false` | Invalid state: danger slots and ring. Always true while `ErrorMessage` is not empty. |
| `IsSuccess` | `bool` | `false` | Success state: success slots and ring (an addition to Arc, which has no success look). |
| `InputMode` | `OtpInputMode` | `Numeric` | Which characters the slots accept (Arc's `inputMode`): digits only (default) or any text. |
| `AutoFocus` | `bool` | `false` | Focuses the first slot when the field is loaded (Arc's `autoFocus`). |
| `IsReadOnly` | `bool` | `false` | When true the slots keep focus and arrow keys but ignore typing, paste and deletion (while a host checks a code). |
| `SlotLabelFormat` | `string` | `"{0}, digit {1} of {2}"` | The accessible name of each slot: `{0}` is `Label`, `{1}` the slot's position from 1 and `{2}``Length` ("Verification code, digit 1 of 6"). |
| `CompletedCommand` | `ICommand?` | `null` | Executed with the code when an edit fills every slot (after `Completed`). |
| `IsComplete` | `bool` | – | *Read-only.* True while every slot holds a character. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ValueChanged` | `OtpInputValueChangedEventArgs` | Raised whenever `Value` changes; `ChangeSource` tells edits from code. |
| `Completed` | `OtpInputCompletedEventArgs` | Raised after every edit by the person that leaves all slots filled (Arc: `if (next.length === length) verify(next)`). |

Pseudo-classes: `:invalid`, `:success`, `:complete`, `:readonly`, `:narrow`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

### OtpInputValueChangedEventArgs

Arguments of `ValueChanged`.

Derives from `RoutedEventArgs`: every member of `RoutedEventArgs` works as well.

### OtpInputCompletedEventArgs

Arguments of `Completed`.

Derives from `RoutedEventArgs`: every member of `RoutedEventArgs` works as well.

## Accessibility

- The slots form a group named by `Label`; each slot is named like "Verification code, digit 1 of 6".
- The helper copy and the error are the help text of every slot. The error is announced assertively when it appears.
- The focus ring is the one gliding ring of the row, for the keyboard and the pointer alike. Hover styles apply to a mouse
  or a pen only.
- With `InputMode="Numeric"` touch keyboards show the number pad.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `0`-`9` / characters | Fill the slot and move to the next one. A filled slot ignores typing until its character is selected. |
| `ArrowLeft` / `ArrowRight` | Move to the previous or next slot. |
| `Backspace` | On an empty slot, clear the previous one and move back; on a filled slot, delete the character before the caret. |
| `Delete` | Clear the current slot. |
| `Ctrl+V` / `Cmd+V` | Paste a code across the slots from the focused one. |
| `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` | Move through the slots one at a time; a slot reached with `Tab` has its character selected. |

## Motion

- A typed character rises into its slot out of a soft blur; a paste lands as a short left to right wave.
- One focus ring glides between the slots while focus stays in the row, and fades in where focus lands from elsewhere.
- A new error nudges the row side to side once. The helper and error rows open their height and rewrite only the words that
  change.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| A character arrives | Rises 0.35 em and unblurs, 240 ms; a paste waits 35 ms per slot | Fades in, 120 ms | Immediate |
| A character leaves | Fades, shrinks to 90 % and blurs, 120 ms | Immediate | Immediate |
| The ring moves | Spring (visual duration 0.26 s, no bounce) | Immediate | Immediate |
| The ring appears or leaves | Fades over 160 ms and scales from 94 % | Immediate | Immediate |
| Slot border and fill | 160 ms | Immediate | Immediate |
| Shake | 360 ms | None | None |

### Responsive behavior

One breakpoint, on the width the field is given: 328 px. Slots are 42 px wide and shrink when the row does not fit.

## Related

- `Input` for a single line of text with a label and messages.
- `PasswordField` for secrets people type from memory.
- The Login block, whose email code step uses this field.

# Multi-step form

> A short form asked one step at a time in a card, with a progress list, Back and Continue, checks before each step, and a success state at the end.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc.Blocks`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc.Blocks --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/blocks/multi-step-form

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.MultiStepFormPreviewDemo">
    <!-- Two short steps: a name, then a lead. The line under the card answers the Completed event (part of this demo). -->
    <StackPanel Spacing="16" Margin="0,24">
        <arc:MultiStepForm x:Name="Form"
                           CompleteLabel="Create workspace"
                           SuccessTitle="You're in"
                           SuccessDescription="Your workspace is ready.">
            <arc:MultiStepFormStep Id="workspace"
                                   Title="Workspace basics"
                                   Description="Give it a short, memorable name.">
                <arc:Input Label="Workspace name" Text="Northwind studio" />
            </arc:MultiStepFormStep>
            <arc:MultiStepFormStep Id="lead" Title="Pick a lead">
                <arc:Combobox Label="Lead" SelectedIndex="0">
                    <arc:SelectItem Content="Priya Raman" />
                    <arc:SelectItem Content="Tomás Ortega" />
                    <arc:SelectItem Content="June Whitfield" />
                </arc:Combobox>
            </arc:MultiStepFormStep>
        </arc:MultiStepForm>
        <StackPanel x:Name="Status"
                    IsVisible="False"
                    Orientation="Horizontal"
                    Spacing="8"
                    HorizontalAlignment="Center">
            <TextBlock Text="Workspace created"
                       FontSize="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TypeXS}"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}"
                       VerticalAlignment="Center" />
            <arc:Button x:Name="StartOver" Variant="Ghost" Size="Small" Content="Start over" />
        </StackPanel>
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class MultiStepFormPreviewDemo : UserControl
{
    public MultiStepFormPreviewDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        // The host's own line after the last step; Start over is this demo's, the form itself ends on its success block.
        Form.Completed += (_, _) => Status.IsVisible = true;
        StartOver.Click += (_, _) =>
        {
            Status.IsVisible = false;
            Form.Restart();
        };
    }
}
```

## When to use

`MultiStepForm` breaks a short form into a few focused steps and walks people through them in one card. The header lists
every step with a round marker and counts where they are ("Step 1 of 2"); one step of fields fills the middle; Back and
Continue sit at the bottom, and Continue becomes the finishing action on the last step. Submitting the last step replaces
the fields with a short success message and folds the buttons away.

- **Onboarding and sign-up.** Name a workspace, pick a lead, choose a plan: two to four small decisions that would feel
  heavy as one long form.
- **Intake and requests.** A support request, a booking or an application where each step asks one kind of question and
  the last step sends everything.
- **Settings that come in a fixed order.** Profile, address, delivery: steps a person may step back through to change an
  answer without losing the others.

## When not to use

- **Only the progress indicator.** Use `Stepper` when you need the list of steps without the card, the buttons and the
  fields.
- **Long flows or full pages.** Five or more steps, steps with their own navigation, or a flow that spans pages (a
  checkout) deserve a page layout of their own. The progress list scrolls when steps do not fit, but a long list is a sign
  the flow should be shorter.
- **A single short form.** Three fields do not need steps; put them in one form with one submit button.
- **Tasks done elsewhere.** A checklist of things a person completes in other places (connect a calendar, invite the team)
  is a checklist, not a form.

## Usage

The block derives from Avalonia's `TemplatedControl`. Each step is a `MultiStepFormStep`, an `AvaloniaObject` with a
`Title` (the heading above the fields and the label in the progress list), an optional `Description` line and the step's
fields as `Content`. Write the steps as children; the fields are ordinary controls.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:MultiStepForm CompleteLabel="Create workspace"
                       SuccessTitle="You're in"
                       SuccessDescription="Your workspace is ready.">
        <arc:MultiStepFormStep Id="workspace"
                               Title="Workspace basics"
                               Description="Give it a short, memorable name.">
            <arc:Input Label="Workspace name" Text="Northwind studio" />
        </arc:MultiStepFormStep>
        <arc:MultiStepFormStep Id="lead" Title="Pick a lead">
            <arc:Combobox Label="Lead" SelectedIndex="0">
                <arc:SelectItem Content="Priya Raman" />
                <arc:SelectItem Content="Tomás Ortega" />
                <arc:SelectItem Content="June Whitfield" />
            </arc:Combobox>
        </arc:MultiStepFormStep>
    </arc:MultiStepForm>
</UserControl>
```

`Completed` is raised when the last step was submitted and the success block is shown (`CompleteCommand` runs right
after it with the same arguments). The arguments carry the steps, whose content still holds what was entered.

```csharp
form.Completed += (_, e) => workspaces.Create(nameBox.Text, (string?)leadPicker.SelectedValue);
```

### Anatomy

- **Progress header**: one entry per step, a 20 px marker and the step's title. Upcoming steps are muted, the current
  one uses the accent, done ones show a green check. The count on the right reads `CountFormat` ("Step {0} of {1}").
- **Step**: the step's title as a heading, the optional description, then the fields. The card is 540 wide (or as wide
  as its container when that is narrower) and the step area is at least 224 high, so short steps do not make the card jump.
- **Buttons**: Back (disabled on the first step) and the submit button, which reads `NextLabel` ("Continue") and
  `CompleteLabel` ("Finish") on the last step.
- **Success block**: a check, `SuccessTitle` and `SuccessDescription`, centered where the fields were.

### Values are kept

Every step keeps its fields alive while another step is shown: a step that is not current is hidden but stays in the
form, so text typed into it, a selection, bindings and the data context all survive Back and Continue. You can read the
values when `Completed` fires, bind them to your view model, or both. `Restart()` shows the first step again; it does not
clear fields, so reset your model (or the controls) if a fresh start should be empty.

### Checking a step before moving on

A step is submitted by Continue, by the finishing button, or by Enter in a single-line text field of the step. Before the
form moves on it checks, in order:

1. **Data validation errors.** A field in the step that shows a validation error (from a binding, `INotifyDataErrorInfo`,
   or `DataValidationErrors.SetError`) stops the form and takes the focus.
2. **`StepValidating`.** Set `Cancel` on the arguments to stay; good for quick checks that need no waiting.
3. **`MultiStepFormStep.ValidateAsync`.** Your own check, awaited. Return false to stay (usually after setting
   `ErrorMessage` on a field). While it runs `IsBusy` is true, the submit button shows a spinner and keeps the focus, and
   Back is disabled. Back, any other step change, `Restart()` or leaving the window cancels its token. A check that throws counts as a no.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.MultiStepFormValidationDemo">
    <!-- Three steps; the first checks its fields before it lets the form move on (code-behind). -->
    <StackPanel Spacing="12" Margin="0,24">
        <arc:MultiStepForm x:Name="Form"
                           SuccessTitle="Welcome aboard"
                           SuccessDescription="Check your inbox for the invite.">
            <arc:MultiStepFormStep Id="account"
                                   Title="Account"
                                   Description="Where should we send the invite?">
                <StackPanel Spacing="12">
                    <arc:Input x:Name="Email" Label="Work email" Placeholder="you@company.com" />
                    <arc:Input x:Name="FullName" Label="Your name" />
                </StackPanel>
            </arc:MultiStepFormStep>
            <arc:MultiStepFormStep Id="team" Title="Team" Description="Who joins you first?">
                <arc:Combobox Label="Teammate" Placeholder="Search people">
                    <arc:SelectItem Content="Ines Duarte" />
                    <arc:SelectItem Content="Kofi Mensah" />
                    <arc:SelectItem Content="Mira Lindqvist" />
                    <arc:SelectItem Content="Wen Hao" />
                </arc:Combobox>
            </arc:MultiStepFormStep>
            <arc:MultiStepFormStep Id="plan" Title="Plan">
                <arc:RadioCards x:Name="Plan" AutomationProperties.Name="Plan" Layout="List">
                    <arc:RadioCardOption Value="free" Label="Free" Description="Up to three projects." Meta="$0" />
                    <arc:RadioCardOption Value="team" Label="Team" Description="Unlimited projects and shared views." Meta="$10" />
                    <arc:RadioCardOption Value="scale" Label="Scale" Description="Roles, audit trail and priority help." Meta="$24" />
                </arc:RadioCards>
            </arc:MultiStepFormStep>
        </arc:MultiStepForm>
        <TextBlock x:Name="Log"
                   HorizontalAlignment="Center"
                   TextAlignment="Center"
                   TextWrapping="Wrap"
                   MaxWidth="520"
                   FontSize="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TypeXS}"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}"
                   Text="Leave the email empty or mistype it, then press Continue or Enter. The plan step needs a choice." />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using System.Text.RegularExpressions;
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class MultiStepFormValidationDemo : UserControl
{
    public MultiStepFormValidationDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        // The account step checks its own fields: an error message on the field, and false keeps the form on the step.
        Form.Steps.First(s => s.Id == "account").ValidateAsync = _ =>
        {
            var email = Email.Text?.Trim() ?? string.Empty;
            var name = FullName.Text?.Trim() ?? string.Empty;
            Email.ErrorMessage = email.Length == 0 ? "Enter your work email."
                : Regex.IsMatch(email, @"^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]{2,}$") ? null
                : "That does not look like an email address.";
            FullName.ErrorMessage = name.Length == 0 ? "Tell us what to call you." : null;
            if (Email.ErrorMessage is not null)
            {
                Email.Focus();
            }
            else if (FullName.ErrorMessage is not null)
            {
                FullName.Focus();
            }
            return Task.FromResult(Email.ErrorMessage is null && FullName.ErrorMessage is null);
        };

        // A synchronous check through the event: the plan step needs a choice.
        Form.StepValidating += (_, e) =>
        {
            if (e.Step.Id == "plan" && Plan.SelectedValue is null)
            {
                e.Cancel = true;
                Log.Text = "Pick a plan to finish.";
            }
        };
        Form.StepChanged += (_, e) => Log.Text = $"Step {e.OldIndex + 1} → {e.NewIndex + 1}";
        Form.Completed += (_, _) => Log.Text = $"Invite for {Email.Text} on the {Plan.SelectedValue} plan.";
    }
}
```

```csharp
// isEmailTaken is your own check, for example a call to your API.
form.Steps[0].ValidateAsync = async cancellation =>
{
    var taken = await isEmailTaken(emailBox.Text, cancellation);
    emailBox.ErrorMessage = taken ? "That email already has an account." : null;
    return !taken;
};
```

### Sending the last step

`CompleteAsync` runs when the last step is submitted, after its checks. The submit button shows a spinner until the task
finishes; then the success block appears and `Completed` is raised. If the task throws, the form stays on the last step,
`CompleteFailed` reports the exception, and the button is ready for another try. Without `CompleteAsync` the form
completes at once.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.MultiStepFormAsyncSubmitDemo">
    <!-- The last step is sent to a pretend server (1.2 s); the switch makes the next send fail. -->
    <StackPanel Spacing="12" Margin="0,24">
        <arc:Switch x:Name="FailNext" Content="Fail the next send" HorizontalAlignment="Center" />
        <arc:MultiStepForm x:Name="Form"
                           CompleteLabel="Send request"
                           SuccessTitle="Request sent"
                           SuccessDescription="We usually reply within a day.">
            <arc:MultiStepFormStep Title="Topic" Description="What do you need help with?">
                <arc:Input Label="Subject" Text="Moving our data to a new region" />
            </arc:MultiStepFormStep>
            <arc:MultiStepFormStep Title="Details">
                <arc:Textarea Label="Message" Text="We would like to move our workspace to the EU region before the end of the month." />
            </arc:MultiStepFormStep>
        </arc:MultiStepForm>
        <TextBlock x:Name="Log"
                   HorizontalAlignment="Center"
                   TextAlignment="Center"
                   TextWrapping="Wrap"
                   MaxWidth="520"
                   FontSize="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TypeXS}"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
        <arc:Button x:Name="StartOver"
                    IsVisible="False"
                    Variant="Ghost"
                    Size="Small"
                    Content="Start over"
                    HorizontalAlignment="Center" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class MultiStepFormAsyncSubmitDemo : UserControl
{
    public MultiStepFormAsyncSubmitDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        // The final submission: the button spins and Back is disabled while it runs; a throw keeps the form on the step.
        Form.CompleteAsync = async cancellation =>
        {
            Log.Text = "Sending…";
            await Task.Delay(1200, cancellation);
            if (FailNext.IsChecked == true)
            {
                FailNext.IsChecked = false;
                throw new InvalidOperationException("The server did not answer. Try again.");
            }
        };
        Form.CompleteFailed += (_, e) => Log.Text = e.Exception.Message;
        Form.Completed += (_, _) =>
        {
            Log.Text = "Sent.";
            StartOver.IsVisible = true;
        };
        StartOver.Click += (_, _) =>
        {
            StartOver.IsVisible = false;
            Log.Text = string.Empty;
            Form.Restart();
        };
    }
}
```

```csharp
// sendRequest is your own call that stores or sends the answers.
form.CompleteAsync = cancellation => sendRequest(request, cancellation);
form.CompleteFailed += (_, e) => status.Text = e.Exception.Message;
```

### Driving the step yourself

`CurrentIndex` (zero-based, two-way) is the step on screen. Set it to start somewhere else or to jump; the form moves with
the motion of the direction of travel and raises `StepChanged` with the old and new index. A value outside the steps is
clamped once the steps are known, so `CurrentIndex="1"` in XAML works before the steps are written. `NextAsync()` does
what Continue does (checks included) and returns whether the form moved; `Back()` does what Back does. `IsComplete` is
two-way too: set it to show the success block without raising `Completed`, or back to false to show the steps again.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.MultiStepFormControlledDemo">
    <!-- CurrentIndex is two-way: the switch above follows the form and moves it. The form starts on the second step. -->
    <StackPanel Spacing="16" Margin="0,24">
        <arc:SegmentedControl x:Name="Steps"
                              AutomationProperties.Name="Step"
                              HorizontalAlignment="Center"
                              SelectedIndex="1">
            <arc:SegmentedOption Value="0" Label="Profile" />
            <arc:SegmentedOption Value="1" Label="Address" />
            <arc:SegmentedOption Value="2" Label="Delivery" />
        </arc:SegmentedControl>
        <arc:MultiStepForm x:Name="Form"
                           CurrentIndex="{Binding #Steps.SelectedIndex, Mode=TwoWay}"
                           CompleteLabel="Save"
                           SuccessTitle="Saved"
                           SuccessDescription="Your details are up to date.">
            <arc:MultiStepFormStep Title="Profile">
                <arc:Input Label="Display name" Text="Lena Okafor" />
            </arc:MultiStepFormStep>
            <arc:MultiStepFormStep Title="Address" Description="Where parcels should go.">
                <arc:Input Label="Street and number" Text="14 Harbour Lane" />
            </arc:MultiStepFormStep>
            <arc:MultiStepFormStep Title="Delivery">
                <arc:Input Label="Instructions" Text="Leave it with the neighbour at 16." />
            </arc:MultiStepFormStep>
        </arc:MultiStepForm>
        <TextBlock x:Name="Log"
                   HorizontalAlignment="Center"
                   FontSize="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TypeXS}"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}"
                   Text="CurrentIndex = 1" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class MultiStepFormControlledDemo : UserControl
{
    public MultiStepFormControlledDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Form.StepChanged += (_, e) =>
            Log.Text = $"CurrentIndex = {e.NewIndex} ({(e.Direction > 0 ? "forward" : "back")} from {e.OldIndex})";
        Form.Completed += (_, _) => Log.Text = "Completed";
    }
}
```

### Narrow containers

Up to 540 wide the card follows its container; in a wider container it stays 540 wide and centers. The block reads its
own width, not the window's: at 388 or less the count moves above the progress list, the paddings tighten from 20 to 16
and the step area grows to at least 240. When the steps do not fit on one line, at any width, the list scrolls sideways
(without a scroll bar) and keeps the current step in view.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.MultiStepFormNarrowDemo">
    <!-- A 340 wide container: the count moves above the list, paddings tighten and the four steps scroll sideways. -->
    <Border Width="340" HorizontalAlignment="Center" Margin="0,24">
        <arc:MultiStepForm CompleteLabel="Book"
                           SuccessTitle="Booked"
                           SuccessDescription="See you on Thursday.">
            <arc:MultiStepFormStep Title="Service">
                <arc:Input Label="What needs doing?" Text="Bike tune-up" />
            </arc:MultiStepFormStep>
            <arc:MultiStepFormStep Title="Date and time">
                <arc:Input Label="Preferred slot" Text="Thursday, 9:30" />
            </arc:MultiStepFormStep>
            <arc:MultiStepFormStep Title="Contact">
                <arc:Input Label="Phone" Text="+44 20 7946 0958" />
            </arc:MultiStepFormStep>
            <arc:MultiStepFormStep Title="Review" Description="Nothing is charged until the visit.">
                <TextBlock Text="Bike tune-up, Thursday 9:30." TextWrapping="Wrap" />
            </arc:MultiStepFormStep>
        </arc:MultiStepForm>
    </Border>
</UserControl>
```

### Other words

Every text is a property with an English default: `NextLabel`, `CompleteLabel`, `BackLabel`, `SuccessTitle`,
`SuccessDescription` and `CountFormat` on screen; `FormName`, `ProgressNameFormat`, `AnnouncementFormat`,
`CurrentStepText` and `CompletedStepText` for screen readers. In the formats `{0}` is the one-based step and `{1}` the
number of steps; only the `{0}` part of the count rolls when the step changes.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.MultiStepFormLabelsDemo">
    <!-- Every visible and spoken text is a property: buttons, the count, the success block and the screen reader lines. -->
    <arc:MultiStepForm Margin="0,24"
                       NextLabel="Next"
                       BackLabel="Previous"
                       CompleteLabel="Submit answers"
                       CountFormat="{}{0} / {1}"
                       AnnouncementFormat="Question {0} of {1}"
                       ProgressNameFormat="Survey progress, question {0} of {1}"
                       FormName="Feedback survey"
                       SuccessTitle="Thanks for the feedback"
                       SuccessDescription="It goes straight to the team.">
        <arc:MultiStepFormStep Title="Rating" Description="How was your last order?">
            <arc:RadioCards AutomationProperties.Name="Rating" Layout="List" SelectedValue="good">
                <arc:RadioCardOption Value="great" Label="Great" />
                <arc:RadioCardOption Value="good" Label="Good" />
                <arc:RadioCardOption Value="poor" Label="Could be better" />
            </arc:RadioCards>
        </arc:MultiStepFormStep>
        <arc:MultiStepFormStep Title="Comment">
            <arc:Input Label="Anything to add?" Placeholder="Optional" />
        </arc:MultiStepFormStep>
    </arc:MultiStepForm>
</UserControl>
```

## API reference

### MultiStepForm

A guided form that asks for one thing at a time: a card with a progress list and a step count, one step of fields, and Back and Continue buttons (Continue reads `CompleteLabel` on the last step). Submitting the last step shows a success block in place of the fields and folds the buttons away. Steps slide 20 px in the direction of travel while the card springs to the new step's height (both ways); done steps draw a check and the count rolls. Every step keeps its fields alive while other steps are shown, so values survive Back and Continue. Enter in a single-line text field submits the step. A step can block its submission with `ValidateAsync`, with `StepValidating`, or by a field with a data validation error; `CompleteAsync` runs the final submission with a spinner on the button.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Steps` | `AvaloniaList<MultiStepFormStep>` | – | *Read-only.* Defines the `Steps` property. |
| `StepsSource` | `IEnumerable<MultiStepFormStep>?` | `null` | Defines the `StepsSource` property. |
| `CurrentIndex` | `int` | `0` | Defines the `CurrentIndex` property. |
| `IsComplete` | `bool` | `false` | Defines the `IsComplete` property. |
| `IsBusy` | `bool` | – | *Read-only.* Defines the `IsBusy` property. |
| `StepCount` | `int` | – | *Read-only.* Defines the `StepCount` property. |
| `NextLabel` | `string` | `"Continue"` | Defines the `NextLabel` property. |
| `CompleteLabel` | `string` | `"Finish"` | Defines the `CompleteLabel` property. |
| `BackLabel` | `string` | `"Back"` | Defines the `BackLabel` property. |
| `SuccessTitle` | `string` | `"Thank you"` | Defines the `SuccessTitle` property. |
| `SuccessDescription` | `string` | `"We received everything we need."` | Defines the `SuccessDescription` property. |
| `CountFormat` | `string` | `"Step {0} of {1}"` | Defines the `CountFormat` property. |
| `ProgressNameFormat` | `string` | `"Progress, step {0} of {1}"` | Defines the `ProgressNameFormat` property. |
| `AnnouncementFormat` | `string` | `"Step {0} of {1}"` | Defines the `AnnouncementFormat` property. |
| `FormName` | `string` | `"Multi-step form"` | Defines the `FormName` property. |
| `CurrentStepText` | `string` | `"Current step"` | Defines the `CurrentStepText` property. |
| `CompletedStepText` | `string` | `"Completed"` | Defines the `CompletedStepText` property. |
| `CompleteCommand` | `ICommand?` | `null` | Defines the `CompleteCommand` property. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `StepChanged` | `MultiStepFormStepChangedEventArgs` | Defines the `StepChanged` event. |
| `StepValidating` | `MultiStepFormStepValidatingEventArgs` | Defines the `StepValidating` event. |
| `Completed` | `MultiStepFormCompletedEventArgs` | Defines the `Completed` event. |
| `CompleteFailed` | `MultiStepFormCompleteFailedEventArgs` | Defines the `CompleteFailed` event. |

Pseudo-classes: `:first`, `:last`, `:complete`, `:narrow`, `:busy`, `:empty`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

### MultiStepFormStep

One step of a `MultiStepForm`: a title (the step's heading and its label in the progress list), an optional line of description and the step's fields as `Content`. The content stays alive while other steps are shown, so whatever a person typed is still there when they come back.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Id` | `string?` | `null` | Defines the `Id` property. |
| `Title` | `string` | `""` | Defines the `Title` property. |
| `Description` | `string?` | `null` | Defines the `Description` property. |
| `Content` | `object?` | `null` | Defines the `Content` property. |
| `ContentTemplate` | `IDataTemplate?` | `null` | Defines the `ContentTemplate` property. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### MultiStepFormStepChangedEventArgs

Arguments of `StepChanged`: the step that was shown, the one shown now and the way it went.

Derives from `RoutedEventArgs`: every member of `RoutedEventArgs` works as well.

### MultiStepFormStepValidatingEventArgs

Arguments of `StepValidating`, raised when a step is submitted and before its `ValidateAsync` runs. Set `Cancel` to stay on the step.

Derives from `RoutedEventArgs`: every member of `RoutedEventArgs` works as well.

### MultiStepFormCompletedEventArgs

Arguments of `Completed`, raised once the last step was submitted and the success state is shown.

Derives from `RoutedEventArgs`: every member of `RoutedEventArgs` works as well.

### MultiStepFormCompleteFailedEventArgs

Arguments of `CompleteFailed`: `CompleteAsync` threw, so the form stayed on the last step.

Derives from `RoutedEventArgs`: every member of `RoutedEventArgs` works as well.

## Accessibility

- After every step change the focus moves to the new step's heading, and after the last step to the success title. Both
  take the focus from code only (they are not tab stops and draw no ring), so a screen reader starts reading at the right
  place and the next Tab goes to the first field. The focus only moves when it was inside the form, so a step change made
  from elsewhere (a `CurrentIndex` binding) never takes it.
- Back turns disabled on the first step only after the focus has moved, so the focus is never dropped.
- The card is a form landmark named by `FormName`. The progress header is a navigation landmark and the list a list, both
  named by `ProgressNameFormat` ("Progress, step 1 of 2"); each entry is named by its step's title and reports
  `CurrentStepText` or `CompletedStepText` as its status. The visible count is hidden from screen readers.
- Each step is a group named by its title. A step change is announced politely with `AnnouncementFormat` ("Step 2 of 2");
  finishing announces the success title and line.
- The submit button is named by its current label; while a check or the final submission runs it keeps the focus and
  ignores presses.
- Keyboard focus rings are 2 px, 2 px outside the buttons; a pointer press draws none.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Enter | In a single-line text field of the step: submits the step (continues, or finishes on the last step). A field that uses Enter itself (an open combobox list with a highlighted option, a multi-line text area) keeps it. |
| Enter / Space | On Back or the submit button: presses it. |
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Moves through the step's fields, then Back (skipped while disabled) and the submit button. |

## Motion

- **Changing step**: the new step slides 20 px in from the direction of travel (from the right going forward, from the
  left going back) on a critically damped spring of about 0.4 s while it fades in over 240 ms; the old step slides 20 px
  the other way and fades out in 120 ms. Both start together. Going back in the middle of a change turns the old step
  around from where it is, keeping its speed.
- **Height**: the step area springs to the new step's height on the same spring, growing for a taller step and shrinking
  for a shorter one (never below its minimum). Content is clipped top and bottom only while the height moves.
- **Progress**: a step that is done swaps its number for a check that grows from 0.6 on a short critically damped spring
  and then draws itself in 320 ms; going back pops the number in again out of a slight blur. Marker and label colors move
  over 240 ms.
- **Count and label**: the step number rolls 0.3em upward going forward and downward going back, rising out of a soft
  blur over 240 ms while the old number leaves in 120 ms. The submit label swaps the same way (always upward) while the
  button's width springs to the new label.
- **Finishing**: the last step slides out, the buttons fade out in 120 ms while their row folds away on the spring, and
  the success block rises 8 px as it fades in; its check draws from 80 ms, the title rises out of a blur from 100 ms and
  the line from 140 ms.
- **Buttons**: hover colors move over 160 ms; a press scales the button to 0.98 in 100 ms and a release springs it back.
- Reduced motion and Off change steps, heights, labels, markers and the success block at once and do not scale presses;
  the focus and the announcements are the same.

## Related

- `Stepper` for a progress indicator on its own.
- `Input`, `Combobox`, `Textarea` and `RadioCards`, the fields used in the examples.
- The other Auth blocks: Login, OTP input and Onboarding illustration.

# Settings page

> A full settings page: section navigation with an account card, the chosen section beside it, and a save bar for unsaved changes.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc.Blocks`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc.Blocks --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/blocks/settings-page

