```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using TKCode.Arc;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class SettingsPageOverviewDemo : UserControl
{
    private (string Name, string Email, string Bio) _saved;

    public SettingsPageOverviewDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        _saved = (FullName.Text ?? string.Empty, Email.Text ?? string.Empty, Bio.Text ?? string.Empty);

        // Editing the profile marks its section dirty; the page then offers Save and Discard.
        FullName.TextChanged += (_, _) => UpdateDirty();
        Email.TextChanged += (_, _) => UpdateDirty();
        Bio.TextChanged += (_, _) => UpdateDirty();
        Page.SaveRequested += (_, _) =>
        {
            _saved = (FullName.Text ?? string.Empty, Email.Text ?? string.Empty, Bio.Text ?? string.Empty);
            UpdateDirty();
            Toast.Show(this, "Profile saved", ToastKind.Success);
        };
        Page.DiscardRequested += (_, _) =>
        {
            FullName.Text = _saved.Name;
            Email.Text = _saved.Email;
            Bio.Text = _saved.Bio;
        };

        // Yearly billing is $12 a seat a month instead of $15.
        Period.ValueChanged += (_, e) =>
        {
            var yearly = e.NewValue == "yearly";
            Price.Amount = yearly ? 72 : 90;
            Price.Period = yearly ? "per month, billed yearly" : "per month";
            PeriodRow.Description = yearly ? "You save $216 a year." : "Save $216 a year with yearly billing.";
        };
    }

    private void UpdateDirty()
        => Profile.IsDirty = FullName.Text != _saved.Name || Email.Text != _saved.Email || Bio.Text != _saved.Bio;
}
```

## When to use

`SettingsPage` is the settings area of an application or workspace. A column on the left lists the sections, such as
Profile, Notifications, Security and Billing, under the page title and above an account card. The chosen section fills
the rest of the page. Because the page knows which section has unsaved edits, it can show one save bar for that section,
so people always see whether their changes are pending.

- **Workspace settings in an admin console**: a Larkspur workspace with General, Members and Billing sections. An owner
  moves between them without losing the page, and each section holds the forms for its own job.
- **Account settings in a SaaS product**: Profile, Notifications, Security and Billing for one signed-in person. The
  sections match how people look for a setting, so they find "Two-step verification" under Security without searching.
- **A billing area with a save step**: the company name, billing email and VAT number are edited together and saved
  with one action. Discard restores the saved values, which a plain list of rows cannot offer.
- **Settings in a narrow window or a side panel**: below 720 px the page becomes one column, with the sections as a row
  of pills that scrolls sideways. The same page works in a split view or on a phone-width window.
- **Settings with more sections than a single form can hold**: the navigation keeps every section one click away, and
  it stays in place while a long section scrolls, because only the content column scrolls.

## When not to use

- **One short list of options**: use `SettingsGroup` with `SettingsRow` on its own, in a card or a dialog.
- **Finding and changing a setting by name from anywhere in the app**: use `SettingsCommand`, the search palette that
  changes values in place.
- **Navigation between the areas of an application**: use `Sidebar`. A settings page is one area with its own sections,
  not the shell of the app.
- **Views of the same record, such as Overview, Activity and Files**: use `Tabs`. Tabs switch views without a save step.
- **Ordered steps that must finish in sequence**, such as an onboarding or a plan change: use `Stepper`, which shows
  where the person is in the process.

## Usage

Write one `SettingsSection` per section. `Header`, `Icon` and `Badge` appear in the navigation, and the selected section
shows its header, `Description` and content on the right. The first enabled section is selected; set `SelectedIndex`
or call `Select(section)` to show another. `Title` sits above the navigation and `Footer` below it, for example an
account card.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:SettingsPage Height="480">
        <arc:SettingsSection Header="Profile" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.User}" Description="How you appear to others.">
            <arc:Input Label="Full name" Text="Noor Haddad" />
        </arc:SettingsSection>
        <arc:SettingsSection Header="Notifications" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Bell}" Badge="2">
            <arc:SettingsGroup Appearance="Plain">
                <arc:SettingsRow Header="Mentions" Description="When someone mentions you.">
                    <arc:Switch IsChecked="True" />
                </arc:SettingsRow>
            </arc:SettingsGroup>
        </arc:SettingsSection>
    </arc:SettingsPage>
</UserControl>
```

`SettingsPage` derives from Avalonia's `SelectingItemsControl`, and its items are the sections. Selection therefore works
as in any selector: `SelectedIndex`, `SelectedItem` and `SelectionChanged` behave as usual, and `SelectedSection` returns
the shown section as a `SettingsSection`. The page builds the navigation for you, one item per section, and manages the
selection pill, the content area and the save bar, so the sections only describe their content.

### Anatomy

1. **Title** (`Title`, "Settings" by default): medium-weight large text at the top of the navigation column, with 24 px
   of space on the sides.
2. **Navigation column**: 248 px wide, with a background that is the surface color mixed with 2.5% of the foreground
   color, and a 1 px divider on its right edge.
3. **Navigation item** (`Header`, `Icon`, `Badge` of each section): 40 px high with a 2 px gap between items. The icon is
   18 px and the header is small text. An unselected item uses the secondary text color; the selected item uses the
   foreground color with medium weight.
4. **Badge** (`Badge`): a small `Badge` at the end of the item, such as a count of new messages.
5. **Unsaved dot**: a 6 px accent dot in the item when `IsDirty` is set on its section.
6. **Selection pill**: a raised surface with a 1 px subtle border and a resting shadow, with a 12 px corner radius. It
   glides between items.
7. **Footer** (`Footer`): under a divider at the bottom of the column, with 16 px and 14 px of padding. Hidden in the
   compact layout.
8. **Content area**: scrolls on its own, with 36 px of space at the sides and 30 px above. The section's header is
   extra large medium-weight text, its `Description` sits 4 px below in small secondary text, and the content starts
   24 px further down.
9. **Save bar**: a raised pill, centered at the bottom of the content area, with a floating shadow and 18, 5, 5, 5 px of
   padding. It holds the note "Unsaved changes", a ghost Discard button and a primary Save changes button. The content
   keeps 72 px of room at its bottom, so the last row is never hidden behind the bar.

### Unsaved changes

Set `IsDirty` on a section while it has unsaved changes. Its navigation item shows a dot, and while it is selected the save
bar rises at the bottom of the page with Discard and Save. Save (or Ctrl+S, ⌘S on macOS) raises `SaveRequested`, and
Discard raises `DiscardRequested`. Both carry the `Section`. Set `IsDirty` back to `false` once the changes are saved or
reverted.

Set `IsDirty` from the form, not from the act of opening the section: compare the current values with the saved ones, so
the dot disappears when a person types a value back to the original. The page does not stop people from switching
sections. A section that is still dirty keeps its dot in the navigation, and its save bar appears again when it is
selected.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.SettingsPageUnsavedChangesDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12">
        <arc:SettingsPage x:Name="Page" Title="Workspace" Height="420">
            <arc:SettingsSection x:Name="General" Header="General" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Settings}"
                                 Description="Name and address of the workspace.">
                <StackPanel Spacing="16">
                    <arc:Input x:Name="WorkspaceName" Label="Workspace name" Text="Larkspur Studio" />
                    <arc:Input Label="Workspace URL" Text="larkspur" Prefix="arc.app/" IsReadOnly="True"
                               Description="Contact support to change the address." />
                </StackPanel>
            </arc:SettingsSection>
            <arc:SettingsSection Header="Members" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Users}" Badge="6"
                                 Description="People with access to this workspace.">
                <arc:SettingsGroup Appearance="Plain">
                    <arc:SettingsRow Header="Allow invites from members" Description="Otherwise only owners can invite.">
                        <arc:Switch IsChecked="True" />
                    </arc:SettingsRow>
                </arc:SettingsGroup>
            </arc:SettingsSection>
        </arc:SettingsPage>
        <TextBlock x:Name="Log" Text="Rename the workspace to see the save bar." HorizontalAlignment="Center"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using TKCode.Arc;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class SettingsPageUnsavedChangesDemo : UserControl
{
    private string _savedName;

    public SettingsPageUnsavedChangesDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        _savedName = WorkspaceName.Text ?? string.Empty;
        WorkspaceName.TextChanged += (_, _) => General.IsDirty = WorkspaceName.Text != _savedName;
        Page.SaveRequested += (_, e) =>
        {
            _savedName = WorkspaceName.Text ?? string.Empty;
            e.Section.IsDirty = false;
            Log.Text = $"Saved \"{_savedName}\" (Save button or Ctrl/⌘+S).";
        };
        Page.DiscardRequested += (_, _) =>
        {
            WorkspaceName.Text = _savedName;
            Log.Text = "Discarded the change.";
        };
    }
}
```

```csharp
page.SaveRequested += async (_, e) =>
{
    await SaveProfileAsync();
    e.Section.IsDirty = false;
};
```

### Layout and width

The page is two columns while it is at least `CompactWidth` wide (720 px by default). Below that width it becomes one
column: the title sits above a horizontal row of section pills that scrolls sideways, the footer is hidden, and the
content gets smaller padding (20 px at the sides, 22 px above and 24 px below). `IsCompact` reports the current layout,
and the page carries the `:compact` pseudo class, so a style can adjust the page for it. Choose the width by the room
the page has, not by the screen: a settings page in a 400 px side panel is compact even on a wide monitor.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.SettingsPageCompactDemo">
    <arc:SettingsPage Width="400" Height="560" HorizontalAlignment="Center">
        <arc:SettingsSection Header="Profile" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.User}" Description="How you appear to others.">
            <StackPanel Spacing="16">
                <arc:Input Label="Full name" Text="Noor Haddad" />
                <arc:Input Label="Email" Text="noor@larkspur.co" />
            </StackPanel>
        </arc:SettingsSection>
        <arc:SettingsSection Header="Notifications" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Bell}" Badge="2">
            <arc:SettingsGroup Appearance="Plain">
                <arc:SettingsRow Header="Mentions" Description="When someone mentions you.">
                    <arc:Switch IsChecked="True" />
                </arc:SettingsRow>
                <arc:SettingsRow Header="Weekly digest" Description="A Monday summary of your projects.">
                    <arc:Switch />
                </arc:SettingsRow>
            </arc:SettingsGroup>
        </arc:SettingsSection>
        <arc:SettingsSection Header="Security" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Shield}">
            <arc:SettingsGroup Appearance="Plain">
                <arc:SettingsRow Header="Two-step verification" Description="Ask for a code on new devices.">
                    <arc:Switch IsChecked="True" />
                </arc:SettingsRow>
            </arc:SettingsGroup>
        </arc:SettingsSection>
        <arc:SettingsSection Header="Billing" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.CreditCard}">
            <arc:SettingsGroup Appearance="Plain">
                <arc:SettingsRow Header="Studio plan" Description="6 seats at $15 each, renews Nov 1.">
                    <arc:Button Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Content="Change plan" />
                </arc:SettingsRow>
            </arc:SettingsGroup>
        </arc:SettingsSection>
    </arc:SettingsPage>
</UserControl>
```

### Binding to a view model

The page is a selector, so `SelectedSection` is the value to read, and `Select(section)` is the method to call. The
dirty state and the save step belong to the view model. In CommunityToolkit.Mvvm style, the view model compares the
workspace name with the saved value, exposes the result as `HasChanges`, and runs Save and Discard as commands:

```csharp
public partial class WorkspaceSettingsViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    private readonly Func<string, Task> _saveName;
    private string _savedName = "Larkspur Studio";

    [ObservableProperty]
    [NotifyPropertyChangedFor(nameof(HasChanges))]
    private string _workspaceName = "Larkspur Studio";

    public bool HasChanges => WorkspaceName != _savedName;

    [RelayCommand]
    private async Task SaveAsync()
    {
        await _saveName(WorkspaceName);
        _savedName = WorkspaceName;
        OnPropertyChanged(nameof(HasChanges));
    }

    public WorkspaceSettingsViewModel(Func<string, Task> saveName) => _saveName = saveName;

    [RelayCommand]
    private void Discard() => WorkspaceName = _savedName;
}
```

```xml
<arc:SettingsPage Title="Workspace">
    <arc:SettingsSection Header="General" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Settings}"
                         Description="Name and address of the workspace."
                         IsDirty="{Binding HasChanges}">
        <arc:Input Label="Workspace name" Text="{Binding WorkspaceName, Mode=TwoWay}" />
    </arc:SettingsSection>
</arc:SettingsPage>
```

The events connect the page's save bar to the commands in code-behind:

```csharp
Page.SaveRequested += (_, _) => ViewModel.SaveCommand.Execute(null);
Page.DiscardRequested += (_, _) => ViewModel.DiscardCommand.Execute(null);
```

Use two-way bindings for the values the sections edit, and one-way bindings for `IsDirty`, `Title` and `Footer`, which the
app sets. Read `SelectedSection` when the app needs the shown section, for example to pick the save action.

### Settings groups and rows

`SettingsGroup` and `SettingsRow` build the content of a section, and work on their own anywhere. A row shows an
optional `Icon`, a `Header` and a `Description`, and the control that changes the setting as its content. Below
`StackWidth` (440 by default) the control moves under the text. When the control is a `Switch` or `Checkbox`, clicking
the text toggles it, and the control takes the header and description as its accessible name and help text.

A group draws a card by default, with an optional `Header`, `Description`, `HeaderActions` and a tinted `Footer` strip.
`Appearance="Plain"` drops the frame for sections that are separated by hairlines inside a page. Inside a section, which
already has a title, prefer `Plain` so the page does not show cards inside a card.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.SettingsPageRowsDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="16" MaxWidth="640">
        <arc:SettingsGroup Header="Notifications" Description="Choose what reaches you and where.">
            <arc:SettingsRow Header="Mentions" Description="When someone @mentions you in a comment or a doc." Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.AtSign}">
                <arc:Switch IsChecked="True" />
            </arc:SettingsRow>
            <arc:SettingsRow Header="Weekly digest" Description="A Monday summary of activity in your projects." Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Mail}">
                <arc:Switch />
            </arc:SettingsRow>
            <arc:SettingsRow Header="Product updates" Description="Occasional news about new features." Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Sparkles}">
                <arc:Switch IsChecked="True" />
            </arc:SettingsRow>
            <arc:SettingsGroup.Footer>
                <TextBlock Text="Security alerts are always sent." VerticalAlignment="Center" />
            </arc:SettingsGroup.Footer>
        </arc:SettingsGroup>
        <arc:SettingsGroup Header="Workspace" Description="Shown to everyone in Larkspur Studio." Appearance="Plain">
            <arc:SettingsRow Header="Workspace name" Description="Larkspur Studio">
                <arc:Button Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Content="Rename" />
            </arc:SettingsRow>
            <arc:SettingsRow Header="Default language" Description="Used for new members and emails.">
                <arc:Select Width="180" SelectedIndex="0">
                    <arc:SelectItem Content="English" Value="en" />
                    <arc:SelectItem Content="Nederlands" Value="nl" />
                </arc:Select>
            </arc:SettingsRow>
        </arc:SettingsGroup>
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

### Text

`Labels` holds the save bar text and the accessible names. Replace the whole object to translate it.

```csharp
page.Labels = new SettingsPageLabels
{
    UnsavedChanges = "Nicht gespeicherte Änderungen",
    Save = "Speichern",
    Discard = "Verwerfen",
};
```

### Example: Workspace settings in an admin console

An admin console for Larkspur Studio opens on Members, while General holds an unsaved workspace name. The dot on
General tells the owner that a change is pending, and the save bar stays hidden until General is selected, so the
Members section never offers to save someone else's edit. The page is 720 px wide, so it uses two columns, and the
footer shows the avatar of the person who is signed in. The Members badge shows the size of the workspace from the navigation.

![Workspace settings page on Members, with a dot on the General section that has unsaved changes](https://docs.tkcode.si/shots/Docs/Blocks/SettingsPage/images/SettingsPage.webp)

```xml

                         Description="Name and address of the workspace." IsDirty="True">

            <arc:Input Label="Workspace name" Text="Larkspur Studio Labs" />
```

### Content guidelines

Name each section by the job it does, in sentence case, and keep the title short enough for the 248 px navigation column.
Write each section's `Description` as one sentence that says what the section changes. Use "Save changes" and "Discard"
on the save bar, so the actions read as the operation they perform.

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| Misc | Advanced |
| Your account settings | Profile |
| You have unsaved changes!!! | Unsaved changes |
| Submit | Save changes |
| Revert | Discard |
| Change your billing info | Billing |

Keep the badge short: a count such as "2" or a word such as "New". Do not put a sentence in the badge; the navigation
item has no room for one.

### Best practices

**Do**

- Group the sections by the job a person has, such as Profile, Notifications, Security and Billing, so people know where
  to look before they read the navigation.
- Set `IsDirty` as soon as a value differs from the saved one, and clear it on save or discard, so the dot and the save
  bar always match the form.
- Use `Appearance="Plain"` for groups inside a section, because the section already draws the title and the page.
- Show a `Footer` with the account the settings belong to, so people can see whose workspace or profile they change.
- Keep one save model per page. Save each section with the bar, or save everything at once, so people can tell which
  changes are pending.

**Avoid**

- Saving some sections automatically and others with the save bar. People cannot tell which changes will be kept.
- Setting `IsDirty` on a section without editable fields. The save bar then appears with nothing to save.
- Putting destructive actions, such as deleting a workspace, behind the save bar. Open a `Dialog` from the action, so
  the save flow stays for edits.
- Long sections without a `Description`. The description tells people what the section changes before they read the
  forms.
- Using the page for a single list of options. A `SettingsGroup` in a card is lighter and needs no navigation.

### Common questions

**Why does the save bar not appear when I edit a field in another section?** The bar belongs to the selected section. A
section with unsaved changes keeps its dot in the navigation, and the bar appears when that section is selected.

**Does Ctrl+S save everything?** It raises `SaveRequested` for the selected section only, and only when that section is
dirty. Handle the event for each section you save, or check `e.Section` to choose the save action.

**Which section is shown first?** The first enabled section, unless `SelectedIndex` or `Select(section)` chooses another.
A disabled section is skipped in both the initial selection and the keyboard movement.

**How do I change the Save button text?** Replace the `Labels` object with a `SettingsPageLabels` whose `Save` property
holds the text you need. The other texts keep their defaults unless you set them too.

## API reference

### SettingsPage

A full settings page. The left column holds the page `Title`, one navigation item per `SettingsSection` (icon, header, badge) under a raised selection pill that glides between them, and a `Footer` such as an account card; the chosen section fills the rest of the page. While the chosen section is `IsDirty`, a save bar rises at the bottom with Discard and Save. Narrower than `CompactWidth`, the page becomes one column with the sections as a scrolling row of pills. Write the sections inline (`<arc:SettingsSection Header="Billing" Icon="...">…</arc:SettingsSection>`) or bind them through `ItemsSource`; the first enabled section is selected by default.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Title` | `string?` | `"Settings"` | The page title above the navigation (default "Settings"). |
| `Footer` | `object?` | `null` | Content at the bottom of the navigation column, such as an account card. Hidden on compact pages. |
| `CompactWidth` | `double` | `720` | Below this width the page becomes one column with the sections as a row of pills (default 720). |
| `Labels` | `SettingsPageLabels` | – | The built-in text (save bar, accessible names). Replace the whole object to translate it. |
| `IsCompact` | `bool` | – | *Read-only.* Whether the page is narrower than `CompactWidth` and shows one column. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `SaveRequested` | `SettingsSectionEventArgs` | Raised when Save is pressed (or Ctrl/⌘+S) while the selected section has unsaved changes. |
| `DiscardRequested` | `SettingsSectionEventArgs` | Raised when Discard is pressed in the save bar. |

Pseudo-classes: `:compact`, `:dirty`

Derives from `SelectingItemsControl`: every member of `SelectingItemsControl` works as well.
### SettingsSection

One section of a `SettingsPage`: its `Header`, `Icon` and `Badge` appear in the page's navigation, and while it is selected the section itself (header, `Description` and content) fills the page's content area. Set `IsDirty` while it has unsaved changes to show the page's save bar.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Icon` | `Geometry?` | `null` | A 24×24 stroke icon shown before the header in the navigation. |
| `Description` | `string?` | `null` | A sentence under the section title in the content area. |
| `Badge` | `string?` | `null` | A short marker at the end of the navigation item, such as "New" or a count. |
| `IsDirty` | `bool` | `false` | Whether the section has unsaved changes: the page shows its save bar while this section is selected. |

Pseudo-classes: `:dirty`

Derives from `HeaderedContentControl`: every member of `HeaderedContentControl` works as well.
### SettingsGroup

A group of related settings: an optional header with a description and actions, a stack of rows (usually `SettingsRow`, written inline or bound through `ItemsSource`), and an optional footer strip for a note or a save button. Drawn as a card by default, or plain inside a page.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Description` | `string?` | `null` | A sentence under the header. |
| `HeaderActions` | `object?` | `null` | Content at the right of the header, such as a button. |
| `Footer` | `object?` | `null` | Content of the strip under the rows, such as a note and a save button. |
| `Appearance` | `SettingsGroupAppearance` | `Card` | Card (default) or Plain. |

Pseudo-classes: `:plain`

Derives from `HeaderedItemsControl`: every member of `HeaderedItemsControl` works as well.
### SettingsRow

One setting: an optional icon, a header and description on the left, and the control that changes it (`Content`) on the right. Below `StackWidth` the control moves under the text. Rows in a `SettingsGroup` (or any panel) are separated by a hairline; the first row has none. When the control is a toggle (Switch, Checkbox), clicking the header or description toggles it too, and the control takes the header as its accessible name and the description as its help text unless it has its own.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Header` | `string?` | `null` | The setting's name, shown in medium weight; also the control's accessible name. |
| `Description` | `string?` | `null` | A sentence under the header that explains the setting; also the control's help text. |
| `Icon` | `Geometry?` | `null` | A 24×24 stroke icon (for example an `ArcIcons` member) shown in a tile before the header. |
| `StackWidth` | `double` | `440` | Below this width the control moves under the header and description (default 440). |
| `IsStacked` | `bool` | – | *Read-only.* Whether the control currently sits under the text (the row is narrower than `StackWidth`). |

Pseudo-classes: `:stacked`, `:icon`

Derives from `ContentControl`: every member of `ContentControl` works as well.

### SettingsPageLabels

| Property | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `UnsavedChanges` | `string` | The note in the save bar: "Unsaved changes". |
| `Save` | `string` | The save bar's primary button: "Save changes". |
| `Discard` | `string` | The save bar's secondary button: "Discard". |
| `NavigationName` | `string` | The accessible name of the section navigation: "Settings sections". |
| `UnsavedSection` | `string` | The accessible text of the dot on a section with unsaved changes: "has unsaved changes". |

### Event arguments

| Type | Property | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `SettingsSectionEventArgs` | `Section` | The section whose changes are to be saved or discarded. |

## Accessibility

- Each navigation item is a tab item named after its section, followed by its badge and "has unsaved changes" when the
  section has them. The navigation is named "Settings sections".
- The navigation is one tab stop. Up and Down (Left and Right on a compact page) move to the previous or next enabled
  section and show it; Home and End go to the first and last. They do not wrap.
- Ctrl+S (⌘S) saves when the shown section has unsaved changes.
- Keyboard focus draws a 2px ring around the navigation item. Pointer focus does not.
- The note in the save bar is a polite live region.
- The selected item is announced as selected, so a screen reader user hears which section is shown after each move.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Up` / `Down` (`Left` / `Right` when compact) | Move focus to the previous or next enabled section and show it; does not wrap |
| `Home` / `End` | Move to the first or the last section |
| `Enter` / `Space` | Select the focused section |
| `Tab` | Leaves the navigation, which is a single stop on its focused or selected item, and moves into the content |
| `Ctrl+S` (`⌘S` on macOS) | Raise `SaveRequested` when the selected section is dirty |

## Motion

- The selection pill glides between navigation items on the snappy spring.
- The incoming section rises 6px and fades in (standard duration, enter easing) while the outgoing one fades out in place.
- The save bar rises into view and drops away.
- Reduced motion keeps the fades and drops the movement. With motion off, everything changes at once.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| The selection moves to another section | The pill glides on a snappy spring | The pill moves at once | The pill moves at once |
| The shown section changes | The new section rises 6px and fades in; the old one fades out in place | The sections crossfade in place | The new section shows at once |
| The save bar appears or goes | Rises into view and drops away | Fades in and out | Shows or hides at once |

## Related

- `SettingsCommand`, `SecuritySettings`, `BillingOverview`, `UsageBilling` and `CancelFlow`: the other settings blocks,
  which fit inside a section.
- `Tabs`: switch between views of the same object.
- `Switch`, `Input`, `Select`, `BillingToggle`: the controls the sections in the examples are built from.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `SettingsGroup` / `SettingsRow` | One list of options is enough, or a section needs its content |
| `SettingsCommand` | People search for a setting by name and change it in place |
| `Sidebar` | The navigation moves between the areas of the application |
| `Tabs` | Views of one object switch without a save step |
| `Stepper` | Ordered steps must finish in sequence |
| `SecuritySettings` / `BillingOverview` | A section needs a complete security or billing layout |

---

# Settings command

> Find any setting from one search field and change it in place: toggles flip, choices cycle and links open, all from the keyboard.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc.Blocks`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc.Blocks --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/blocks/settings-command

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class SettingsCommandInlineDemo : UserControl
{
    public SettingsCommandInlineDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
    }

    // Toggles and choices change in place; actions are the app's to run, here with a toast.
    private void OnItemInvoked(object? sender, SettingsCommandItemEventArgs e)
        => Toast.Show(this, $"Opening {e.Item.Header}", ToastKind.Info);
```

## When to use

`SettingsCommand` puts the settings of an application behind one search field. People type a few letters, such as
"email" or "dark", and change the setting on the spot: no settings page to open, no section to find and no row to scroll
to. It sits beside the full settings page as a quick path to the same values, or on its own in a dialog that opens with
a shortcut. The palette holds the values and calls the app when one of them changes, so it fits settings that take
effect at once.

- **A settings palette opened with Ctrl+, (⌘, on a Mac)** in an analytics or project tool, where people change "Theme",
  "Compact tables" or "Default chart range" many times a day. A dialog with the palette removes the trip through the
  settings navigation.
- **Notification preferences in a team inbox**: "Mentions", "Product updates" and "Email digests" are switches or three
  named values. Each change applies at once, and the footer confirms it ("Mentions off"), so there is no save step to
  forget.
- **Privacy and presence switches in a collaboration tool**: "Show online status" and "Read receipts" take effect for the
  whole workspace. A notice in the footer confirms each change, so people see the result without opening a dialog.
- **Account actions next to the settings they relate to**: "Change email" and "Two-step verification" open other pages,
  and "Sign out everywhere" runs a command. Each action can show its shortcut in key caps, so one search finds all of
  them.
- **Admin consoles with many small switches**: a tenant console where a search for "single sign-on" finds the
  enforcement switch among rows grouped under Security, Users and Billing. Keep the list short enough to scan (see
  Size and performance).

## When not to use

- **Settings that need a form, validation or a save step**: use `SettingsPage` with `SettingsGroup` and `SettingsRow`,
  or a form built from `Input` and `Select`. The palette applies each value at once and has no place for a validation
  message or a Save button.
- **Choices with many values or free text**, such as a time zone, a country or a display name: use `Combobox` or
  `Select` for a long list, and `Input` for free text. A palette row shows its options in a short pill, so it only fits
  a handful of values.
- **Dates and times**, such as quiet hours or a report start date: use `TimePicker` or `DatePicker`. A palette row
  cannot show a calendar or a clock.
- **App commands that are not settings**, such as "New project" or "Export this view": use `CommandPalette`. It searches
  commands, while this palette searches the values people configure.
- **Searching records**, such as customers, invoices or messages: use `SearchField` or `ExpandingSearch`, with results
  from the data. The palette only searches the settings it was given.

## Usage

Write the settings inside the palette. A `SettingsCommandToggle` is on or off, a `SettingsCommandChoice` steps
through its `Options`, and a `SettingsCommandAction` runs a command. `Group` lists a setting under a title, and
`Keywords` adds other words that find it. Focus stays in the search field: the up and down keys move the highlight,
Enter acts on the highlighted row, and the left and right keys step a choice. The footer confirms each change.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:SettingsCommand MaxWidth="560">
        <arc:SettingsCommandChoice Group="Appearance" Header="Theme" Options="Light, Dark, System" Keywords="dark light" />
        <arc:SettingsCommandToggle Group="Appearance" Header="Compact mode" Description="Tighter rows and smaller gaps." />
        <arc:SettingsCommandAction Group="Account" Header="Change email" IsNavigation="True" />
    </arc:SettingsCommand>
</UserControl>
```

`SettingsCommand` derives from Avalonia's `TemplatedControl`, so it takes the usual layout properties (`Width`,
`MaxWidth`, `Margin`) and styling. Its settings are an ordinary collection: `SettingsCommandItem` is the base class of
the three kinds, and the items are the content of the palette, so they can be written in XAML or added in code. The
palette is a framed panel by default, with its own surface, border, corner radius and floating shadow. Set `IsFramed`
to `False` when a surrounding surface already provides them.

### Anatomy

1. **Search row** (`Query`): 56 px high, with an 18 px search glyph in the muted text color, a borderless text box
   and the Esc key cap on the right. A divider sits under the row.
2. **Result list** (`ResultsMaxHeight`): 360 px by default, with an 8 px inset. Past that height the list scrolls, and
   its top and bottom edges fade over 20 px to show more content.
3. **Group title** (`Group`): extra small text in the muted text color, with 12, 10, 12 and 4 px of padding. Settings
   without a group appear under `Labels.Ungrouped`, and only when another setting has a group.
4. **Row** (`Header`, `Description`): 48 px high with a 12 px corner radius. The header is small body text with medium
   weight; the description is one line of extra small text in the secondary text color, cut with an ellipsis.
5. **Icon tile** (`Icon`): a 30 px tile with a 9 px corner radius and a 16 px glyph. Use an `ArcIcons` member for
   the glyph.
6. **Row control**: a switch for `SettingsCommandToggle`, a 28 px pill with two 24 px arrows and the current value for
   `SettingsCommandChoice`, and key caps or a right arrow for `SettingsCommandAction`.
7. **Active row highlight**: a muted surface with a 12 px corner radius that glides between rows.
8. **Footer**: 40 px high, with a divider above. Key hints sit on the left (up and down for Navigate, Enter for Toggle,
   Change or Open depending on the active row, and Esc for Close). The change notice sits on the right.

### Searching

The query splits on spaces. Each word must appear in the header, description, group or keywords, ignoring case, and it
may match part of a word. The results are ranked by how the header matches:

1. The header starts with the whole query.
2. A word in the header starts with the query.
3. The header contains the query.
4. Only the description, group or keywords match.

Settings with the same rank keep their declared order, and a group sorts by the rank of its best row. The matching part
of a header stays in the foreground while the rest of the header turns secondary, so people can see why a row matched.
When nothing matches, the palette shows `Labels.NoResults` with `Labels.NoResultsHint`, which suggests another word. An
empty query lists every setting in declared order, so write the settings in the order people expect to see them.

`Query` is two-way, so the app can prefill the search (for example from a deep link) or keep the last query. `Clear()`
empties it, which lists every setting again, and `FocusSearch()` moves the keyboard focus to the search field.

### Toggles, choices and actions

Pick the kind by what the setting does when it is changed:

- **`SettingsCommandToggle`** for a yes or no setting that applies at once, such as "Compact mode" or "Mentions".
  Enter or a click flips it, and the notice reads "Compact mode on" or "Compact mode off". A switch that needs a second
  step to confirm does not belong here.
- **`SettingsCommandChoice`** for three to five named values, such as "Light, Dark, System" or "Off, Daily, Weekly".
  Enter moves to the next option and wraps from the last to the first, while the arrows beside the value step without
  wrapping. Order the options so the usual next choice follows the default, because Enter moves one step at a time.
- **`SettingsCommandAction`** for a command or a link: "Change email", "Download your data", "Sign out everywhere".
  Enter or a click runs the `Command` and then raises `ItemInvoked`. Set `IsNavigation` to `True` for an action that
  opens another page, so the row shows an arrow and people expect a new screen.

Set `IsEnabled` to `False` for a setting that cannot be changed now, for example one that an admin has locked. The row
is dimmed and the keyboard skips it, but the row stays in the list, so people learn that the setting exists and why it
is unavailable. Use the `Description` to say why ("Turned off by your admin.").

### Binding to a view model

The values of a palette are styled properties. `IsChecked` and `SelectedOption` bind two-way: a change made in the
palette updates the view model, and a change made elsewhere in the app moves the row. The example below uses
CommunityToolkit.Mvvm (the `ObservableObject` base class, `[ObservableProperty]` and `[RelayCommand]` generators). The
app owns the state; the palette only edits it.

```csharp
public partial class WorkspaceSettingsViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    private readonly Action<string> _openPage;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private string? _theme = "System";

    [ObservableProperty]
    private bool _compactMode;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private bool _reduceMotion = true;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private string? _emailDigests = "Weekly";

    public WorkspaceSettingsViewModel(Action<string> openPage) => _openPage = openPage;

    [RelayCommand]
    private void ChangeEmail() => _openPage("account/email");
}
```

```xml
<arc:SettingsCommand>
    <arc:SettingsCommandChoice Group="Appearance" Header="Theme"
                               Options="Light, Dark, System"
                               SelectedOption="{Binding Theme}" />
    <arc:SettingsCommandToggle Group="Appearance" Header="Compact mode"
                               IsChecked="{Binding CompactMode}" />
    <arc:SettingsCommandToggle Group="Appearance" Header="Reduce motion"
                               IsChecked="{Binding ReduceMotion}" />
    <arc:SettingsCommandChoice Group="Notifications" Header="Email digests"
                               Options="Off, Daily, Weekly"
                               SelectedOption="{Binding EmailDigests}" />
    <arc:SettingsCommandAction Group="Account" Header="Change email" IsNavigation="True"
                               Command="{Binding ChangeEmailCommand}" />
</arc:SettingsCommand>
```

Two-way: `IsChecked`, `SelectedOption` and `Query`. One-way: `Items`, `Labels` and `ResultsMaxHeight`, which the app sets
and the palette reads. Read-only: `ActiveItem`, which is the highlighted setting, or `null` when nothing is on show.
Use the events for side effects that a binding cannot express, such as saving to a server or logging an audit entry.
`SettingChanged` runs only for changes made in the palette, so a save in the handler does not run again when the app
changes a value itself. `ItemInvoked` runs after an action's `Command` has run. Both events are routed, so a handler can
sit on a parent element as well as on the palette.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             xmlns:demos="using:TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.SettingsCommandBoundDemo"
             x:DataType="demos:SettingsCommandBoundState">
    <StackPanel Spacing="24" MaxWidth="560">
        <arc:SettingsCommand ResultsMaxHeight="320">
            <arc:SettingsCommandChoice Header="Theme" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Palette}"
                                       Description="Match your system, or always use light or dark."
                                       Options="Light, Dark, System"
                                       SelectedOption="{Binding Theme}" />
            <arc:SettingsCommandToggle Header="Compact mode" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Rows2}"
                                       Description="Tighter rows and smaller gaps in lists."
                                       IsChecked="{Binding CompactMode}" />
            <arc:SettingsCommandToggle Header="Reduce motion" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Sparkles}"
                                       Description="Fewer animations across the app."
                                       IsChecked="{Binding ReduceMotion}" />
            <arc:SettingsCommandChoice Header="Email digests" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Inbox}"
                                       Description="A summary of activity in your projects."
                                       Options="Off, Daily, Weekly"
                                       SelectedOption="{Binding EmailDigests}" />
        </arc:SettingsCommand>
        <!-- The same state, bound to ordinary controls: change either side and the other follows. -->
        <arc:SettingsGroup Header="App state" Description="Bound to the same properties as the palette.">
            <arc:SettingsRow Header="Theme">
                <arc:SegmentedControl SelectedValue="{Binding Theme}">
                    <arc:SegmentedOption Value="Light" Label="Light" />
                    <arc:SegmentedOption Value="Dark" Label="Dark" />
                    <arc:SegmentedOption Value="System" Label="System" />
                </arc:SegmentedControl>
            </arc:SettingsRow>
            <arc:SettingsRow Header="Compact mode">
                <arc:Switch IsChecked="{Binding CompactMode}" />
            </arc:SettingsRow>
            <arc:SettingsRow Header="Reduce motion">
                <arc:Switch IsChecked="{Binding ReduceMotion}" />
            </arc:SettingsRow>
            <arc:SettingsRow Header="Email digests">
                <arc:SegmentedControl SelectedValue="{Binding EmailDigests}">
                    <arc:SegmentedOption Value="Off" Label="Off" />
                    <arc:SegmentedOption Value="Daily" Label="Daily" />
                    <arc:SegmentedOption Value="Weekly" Label="Weekly" />
                </arc:SegmentedControl>
            </arc:SettingsRow>
        </arc:SettingsGroup>
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using System.ComponentModel;
using System.Runtime.CompilerServices;
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class SettingsCommandBoundDemo : UserControl
{
    public SettingsCommandBoundDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        DataContext = new SettingsCommandBoundState();
    }
}

/// <summary>The app's settings: what the palette and the controls under it both bind to.</summary>
public sealed class SettingsCommandBoundState : INotifyPropertyChanged
{
    private string? _theme = "System";
    private bool _compactMode;
    private bool _reduceMotion = true;
    private string? _emailDigests = "Weekly";

    public event PropertyChangedEventHandler? PropertyChanged;

    public string? Theme
    {
        get => _theme;
        set => Set(ref _theme, value);
    }

    public bool CompactMode
    {
        get => _compactMode;
        set => Set(ref _compactMode, value);
    }

    public bool ReduceMotion
    {
        get => _reduceMotion;
        set => Set(ref _reduceMotion, value);
    }

    public string? EmailDigests
    {
        get => _emailDigests;
        set => Set(ref _emailDigests, value);
    }

    private void Set<T>(ref T field, T value, [CallerMemberName] string? name = null)
    {
        if (!EqualityComparer<T>.Default.Equals(field, value))
        {
            field = value;
            PropertyChanged?.Invoke(this, new PropertyChangedEventArgs(name));
        }
    }
}
```

```csharp
palette.SettingChanged += (_, e) => _settings.SaveAsync(e.Item.Header, e.Value);
palette.ItemInvoked += (_, e) => _telemetry.Track("settings.action", e.Item.Header);
```

### Focus and dismissal

A palette in a `Dialog` needs three things: `IsFramed` set to `False`, so the palette does not draw a second panel;
a negative margin as large as the dialog's padding, so the search row and the footer reach the dialog's edges; and a
rule for closing. The demo gives the palette a margin of -24 for the dialog's 24 px body padding. The code below closes the `Dialog` that hosts the palette.

Escape with an empty query raises `CloseRequested`, and Escape with a query clears the query first. Close the dialog in
the `CloseRequested` handler and set `Handled` to `True`, so the dialog does not handle the same key press again.

The dialog moves focus to its first control when it opens, which would take the keyboard away from the search field.
Post `FocusSearch()` on the UI thread once the dialog is open, and clear the query when the dialog opens so each
session starts from the full list.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.SettingsCommandInDialogDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12" HorizontalAlignment="Center">
        <arc:Button Content="Open settings"
                    Variant="Secondary"
                    HorizontalAlignment="Center"
                    Click="OnOpenClick" />
        <TextBlock x:Name="ShortcutHint"
                   HorizontalAlignment="Center"
                   FontSize="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TypeSM}"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
        <arc:Dialog x:Name="SettingsDialog"
                    Title="Settings"
                    Size="Large"
                    Opened="OnOpened">
            <!-- Without its own frame, and over the dialog's 24px body padding, so the search row and the footer run edge to edge. -->
            <arc:SettingsCommand x:Name="Palette"
                                 IsFramed="False"
                                 Margin="-24"
                                 ResultsMaxHeight="300"
                                 CloseRequested="OnCloseRequested">
                <arc:SettingsCommandChoice Group="Appearance" Header="Theme" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Palette}"
                                           Description="Match your system, or always use light or dark."
                                           Keywords="dark light mode color scheme"
                                           Options="Light, Dark, System" SelectedOption="System" />
                <arc:SettingsCommandToggle Group="Appearance" Header="Compact mode" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Rows2}"
                                           Description="Tighter rows and smaller gaps in lists."
                                           Keywords="density dense spacing" />
                <arc:SettingsCommandToggle Group="Appearance" Header="Reduce motion" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Sparkles}"
                                           Description="Fewer animations across the app."
                                           Keywords="animation accessibility" />
                <arc:SettingsCommandChoice Group="Notifications" Header="Email digests" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Inbox}"
                                           Description="A summary of activity in your projects."
                                           Keywords="email summary newsletter"
                                           Options="Off, Daily, Weekly" SelectedOption="Weekly" />
                <arc:SettingsCommandToggle Group="Notifications" Header="Mentions" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.AtSign}"
                                           Description="When someone @mentions you in a comment."
                                           IsChecked="True" />
                <arc:SettingsCommandAction Group="Account" Header="Change email" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Mail}"
                                           Description="noor@larkspur.co"
                                           Keywords="address login" IsNavigation="True" />
                <arc:SettingsCommandAction Group="Account" Header="Sign out everywhere" Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.LogOut}"
                                           Description="Every device except this one."
                                           Keywords="sessions logout devices" Shortcut="mod+shift+q" />
            </arc:SettingsCommand>
        </arc:Dialog>
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia;
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Input;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;
using Avalonia.Threading;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class SettingsCommandInDialogDemo : UserControl
{
    // Command+comma on a Mac, Ctrl+comma elsewhere: the usual shortcut for settings (the gallery keeps Ctrl/⌘+K for its search).
    private static readonly KeyGesture OpenGesture = ShortcutFormatter.Parse("mod+,", ShortcutFormatter.CurrentPlatform);

    private TopLevel? _topLevel;

    public SettingsCommandInDialogDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        ShortcutHint.Text = $"or press {ShortcutFormatter.Format(OpenGesture, ShortcutFormatter.CurrentPlatform).Text}";
    }

    // The shortcut works anywhere in the window while the demo is on screen, like an app-wide command.
    protected override void OnAttachedToVisualTree(VisualTreeAttachmentEventArgs e)
    {
        base.OnAttachedToVisualTree(e);
        _topLevel = TopLevel.GetTopLevel(this);
        _topLevel?.AddHandler(KeyDownEvent, OnWindowKeyDown, RoutingStrategies.Tunnel);
    }

    protected override void OnDetachedFromVisualTree(VisualTreeAttachmentEventArgs e)
    {
        _topLevel?.RemoveHandler(KeyDownEvent, OnWindowKeyDown);
        _topLevel = null;
        base.OnDetachedFromVisualTree(e);
    }

    private void OnWindowKeyDown(object? sender, KeyEventArgs e)
    {
        if (!SettingsDialog.IsOpen && ShortcutFormatter.Matches(e, OpenGesture, ShortcutFormatter.CurrentPlatform))
        {
            e.Handled = true;
            Open();
        }
    }

    private void OnOpenClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) => Open();

    private void Open()
    {
        Palette.Clear();
        SettingsDialog.Open();
    }

    // The dialog focuses its first control when it opens; the palette wants the keyboard in its search field.
    private void OnOpened(object? sender, EventArgs e)
        => Dispatcher.UIThread.Post(Palette.FocusSearch, DispatcherPriority.Input);

    // Escape with an empty query: close the dialog (handled, so the dialog does not close a second time).
    private void OnCloseRequested(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        e.Handled = true;
        SettingsDialog.Close();
    }
}
```

```csharp
private Dialog SettingsDialog = null!; // the Dialog with x:Name="SettingsDialog" in the demo

private void OnCloseRequested(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
{
    e.Handled = true;
    SettingsDialog.Close();
}
```

The demo also opens the dialog with Ctrl+, (⌘, on a Mac), the usual shortcut for settings. The palette only shows
shortcuts, so the app registers the key gesture itself; see the next subsection.

### Shortcuts and actions

`Shortcut` shows an action's key combination in key caps. Write `mod` for the command key, which is ⌘ on a Mac and
Ctrl elsewhere, and combine it with `shift`, such as `mod+shift+e`. The palette only shows the shortcut, and the app
handles the key press, for example in a window-level key handler, so the shortcut works while the palette is closed as
well. `IsNavigation` adds an arrow for actions that open another page.

```xml
<arc:SettingsCommand>
    <arc:SettingsCommandAction Header="Download your data" Shortcut="mod+shift+e" />
    <arc:SettingsCommandAction Header="Two-step verification" IsNavigation="True" />
    <arc:SettingsCommandToggle Header="Read receipts" Description="Turned off by your admin." IsEnabled="False" />
</arc:SettingsCommand>
```

### Text

The built-in text comes from `Labels`: strings for fixed text and functions for text with a value, such as the
no-results message. Replace the whole object to translate it, and keep each function's parameters in order.

```csharp
palette.Labels = new SettingsCommandLabels
{
    Placeholder = "Instellingen zoeken",
    NoResults = query => $"Geen instellingen voor “{query}”",
    TurnedOn = header => $"{header} aan",
    TurnedOff = header => $"{header} uit",
};
```

### Size and performance

The palette creates one row per setting and keeps it for the life of the item. Filtering changes only which rows show and
their order. Settings in the low hundreds are fine without virtualization; move a longer catalogue to a settings page.

Add or remove items in code with the `Items` collection, and the list updates at once.

### Example: Notification settings in a team inbox

A team inbox keeps its notification preferences in the same palette as its other settings. The query here is "email",
which shows how the ranking works: "Email digests" starts with the query, so it ranks first; "Change email" has a
header word that starts with it; "Product updates" matches only through its keywords, so it ranks last. Each group
sorts by its best row, which puts Notifications above Account. The matching text in the header stays in the foreground,
and the footer shows the keys that apply to the highlighted choice. The palette sits at 560 px, which fits a dialog or a
settings column without stretching the rows.

![A settings palette searching for email, ranked across two groups](https://docs.tkcode.si/shots/Docs/Blocks/SettingsCommand/images/EmailSettings.webp)

```xml
<StackPanel Width="560">

                                   Header="Email digests"
                                   Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Inbox}"
                                   Description="A summary of activity in your projects."
                                   Keywords="summary newsletter"
                                   Options="Off, Daily, Weekly"
                                   SelectedOption="Weekly" />
        <arc:SettingsCommandToggle Group="Notifications"
                                   Header="Mentions"
                                   Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.AtSign}"
                                   Description="When someone @mentions you in a comment."
                                   IsChecked="True" />
        <arc:SettingsCommandToggle Group="Notifications"
```

### Content guidelines

Write each header as the name of the setting, in sentence case, so it reads the same in the row, the search and the
notice. Keep the description to one short line, because the row trims it with an ellipsis. Name the choices with the
words people use on the settings page, and keep the same names in the notice that follows a change.

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| Enable notifications for mentions | Mentions |
| Show a summary email every day | Email digests (option: Daily) |
| Toggle the compact view mode | Compact mode |
| Change your email address | Change email |
| Sign out of all devices | Sign out everywhere |
| Setting disabled by the organization administrator | Turned off by your admin. |

Use keywords for synonyms and the words people search for, such as "dark light" for Theme or "2fa security" for
Two-step verification. Do not repeat the header in the keywords, and do not add a keyword that names another setting.

### Best practices

**Do**

- Apply a change at once and confirm it in the footer. The notice is the only feedback in the palette, so it has to
  name the setting and its new value.
- Bind the values to the app's state and keep saving in the event handlers, so the palette and the rest of the app
  always show the same value.
- Keep choices to a few named values, and move anything longer to a page with a proper control.
- Register the open shortcut for each platform (`mod+,` in the demo) and show it next to the button that opens the
  palette, so people learn the shortcut from the screen they already use.
- Use `IsEnabled="False"` with a reason in the description for a locked setting, so people know it is not missing.

**Avoid**

- Settings that need a save step or validation. A palette change applies at once, so a rejected value would already be
  in effect; send those settings to `SettingsPage`.
- Actions that delete data or sign people out without a confirmation. Open a `Dialog` from the action's command, so the
  search does not skip the safeguard.
- Long lists of settings with the same description. The search cannot tell them apart, and the rows look alike.
- Changing the header of a setting for each state, such as "Turn on compact mode" and "Turn off compact mode". The row
  states the value; the header stays the same.
- Storing a value only in the palette. `SettingChanged` is raised for user changes only, so the app must keep the state
  itself.

### Common questions

**Why does the first Escape clear the query instead of closing?** Escape clears a non-empty query first, so a person can
dismiss a search without losing the palette. With an empty query, Escape raises `CloseRequested`. A dialog that hosts the
palette should close only in that handler.

**Why does the highlight stop when I press Down on the last row?** The highlight does not wrap: it stops at the first and
last enabled row. Disabled rows are skipped in both directions, so the highlight always lands on a setting that can be
changed.

**How do I react to a value that the app changes itself?** Bind the property, such as `IsChecked`, and the row follows
the change. `SettingChanged` is not raised for it, so use a `PropertyChanged` handler on the view model for changes that
must trigger a side effect.

## API reference

### SettingsCommand

A settings command palette: one search field that finds any setting and changes it in place. Toggles flip, choices cycle through their options and actions run, all without leaving the keyboard; focus stays in the search field while the arrow keys move a highlight that glides between rows. A notice in the footer confirms each change. Write the settings inline (`SettingsCommandToggle`, `SettingsCommandChoice`, `SettingsCommandAction`) or bind `Items`. Their values are styled properties, so `IsChecked` and `SelectedOption` bind two-way and the rows follow changes made elsewhere.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Items` | `IList<SettingsCommandItem>` | – | The settings to search, in the order they are listed when the query is empty. |
| `Query` | `string` | `""` | The text in the search field (two-way). |
| `ActiveItem` | `SettingsCommandItem?` | – | *Read-only.* The highlighted setting that Enter acts on, or null when nothing is on show. |
| `ResultsMaxHeight` | `double` | `360` | The tallest the result list gets before it scrolls. |
| `IsFramed` | `bool` | `true` | Whether the palette draws its own panel (surface, border, radius and floating shadow). Turn it off inside a Dialog or another surface. |
| `Labels` | `SettingsCommandLabels` | – | The built-in text; replace the whole object to localize the palette. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `SettingChanged` | `SettingsCommandChangedEventArgs` | Raised when the user changes a toggle or a choice (not when the app sets the value). |
| `ItemInvoked` | `SettingsCommandItemEventArgs` | Raised when an action is invoked with Enter or a click, after its command ran. |
| `CloseRequested` | `RoutedEventArgs` | Raised when Escape is pressed with an empty query: close the palette. Mark it handled so a surrounding Dialog does not handle the same Escape again. |

Pseudo-classes: `:empty`, `:no-results`, `:toggle-active`, `:choice-active`, `:action-active`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.
### SettingsCommandToggle

An on / off setting. Enter or a click flips `IsChecked`; the row shows a switch.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `IsChecked` | `bool` | `false` | Whether the setting is on (two-way). |
| `Header` | `string?` | `null` | The setting's name, shown in the row and searched first. |
| `Description` | `string?` | `null` | One line under the header (trimmed to a single line); also searched. |
| `Icon` | `Geometry?` | `null` | A 24×24 stroke icon (for example an `ArcIcons` member) shown in a tile before the header. |
| `Group` | `string?` | `null` | The group the row is listed under, such as "Appearance"; also searched. Without one it is listed under "Settings" when other settings have a group. |
| `Keywords` | `string?` | `null` | Other words that find the setting (synonyms separated by spaces or commas), such as "dark light appearance". |
| `IsEnabled` | `bool` | `true` | Whether the setting can be changed. Disabled rows are dimmed and skipped by the keyboard. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.
### SettingsCommandChoice

A setting with a few named values. Enter or a click moves to the next option (after the last comes the first); the left and right arrow keys, and the arrows beside the value, step without wrapping.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Options` | `AvaloniaList<string>` | – | The values in order. In XAML a comma-separated string works: `Options="Light, Dark, System"`. |
| `SelectedOption` | `string?` | `null` | The current value (two-way). When null it becomes the first option. |
| `Header` | `string?` | `null` | The setting's name, shown in the row and searched first. |
| `Description` | `string?` | `null` | One line under the header (trimmed to a single line); also searched. |
| `Icon` | `Geometry?` | `null` | A 24×24 stroke icon (for example an `ArcIcons` member) shown in a tile before the header. |
| `Group` | `string?` | `null` | The group the row is listed under, such as "Appearance"; also searched. Without one it is listed under "Settings" when other settings have a group. |
| `Keywords` | `string?` | `null` | Other words that find the setting (synonyms separated by spaces or commas), such as "dark light appearance". |
| `IsEnabled` | `bool` | `true` | Whether the setting can be changed. Disabled rows are dimmed and skipped by the keyboard. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.
### SettingsCommandAction

A command such as "Change email" or "Sign out everywhere". Enter or a click runs `Command`, then the palette raises `ItemInvoked`. The row shows the `Shortcut` in key caps and, for links to another page, an arrow.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Command` | `ICommand?` | `null` | The command to run. |
| `CommandParameter` | `object?` | `null` | The parameter passed to `Command`. |
| `Shortcut` | `string?` | `null` | The app's shortcut for the action, shown in key caps, such as "mod+shift+d" (Command on a Mac, Ctrl elsewhere) or "Ctrl+,". The palette only shows it; the app handles the shortcut itself. |
| `IsNavigation` | `bool` | `false` | Whether the action opens another page; the row shows an arrow. |
| `Header` | `string?` | `null` | The setting's name, shown in the row and searched first. |
| `Description` | `string?` | `null` | One line under the header (trimmed to a single line); also searched. |
| `Icon` | `Geometry?` | `null` | A 24×24 stroke icon (for example an `ArcIcons` member) shown in a tile before the header. |
| `Group` | `string?` | `null` | The group the row is listed under, such as "Appearance"; also searched. Without one it is listed under "Settings" when other settings have a group. |
| `Keywords` | `string?` | `null` | Other words that find the setting (synonyms separated by spaces or commas), such as "dark light appearance". |
| `IsEnabled` | `bool` | `true` | Whether the setting can be changed. Disabled rows are dimmed and skipped by the keyboard. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### SettingsCommandItem

The base class of the three kinds of setting. Each property is a styled property, so the palette follows changes.

| Property | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Header` | `string?` | The setting's name, shown in the row and searched first. |
| `Description` | `string?` | One line under the header, trimmed to a single line; also searched. |
| `Icon` | `Geometry?` | A 24 by 24 stroke icon, such as an `ArcIcons` member, shown in a tile before the header. |
| `Group` | `string?` | The group the row is listed under, such as "Appearance"; also searched. |
| `Keywords` | `string?` | Other words that find the setting, separated by spaces or commas. |
| `IsEnabled` | `bool` | Whether the setting can be changed. Disabled rows are dimmed and skipped by the keyboard. |

### SettingsCommandLabels

| Property | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Placeholder` | `string` | The search field's placeholder: "Search settings". |
| `SearchName` | `string` | The search field's accessible name: "Search settings". |
| `ResultsName` | `string` | The accessible name of the result list: "Settings". |
| `NoResults` | `Func<string, string>` | The message when nothing matches: "No settings match “theme”". |
| `NoResultsHint` | `string` | The hint under it: "Try another word, such as theme or email." |
| `Navigate`, `Toggle`, `Change`, `Open`, `Close` | `string` | The footer hints beside the keys. |
| `EscapeKey` | `string` | The Escape key cap: "Esc". |
| `TurnedOn`, `TurnedOff` | `Func<string, string>` | The notice after a toggle changes: "Compact mode on". |
| `ChangedTo` | `Func<string, string, string>` | The notice after a choice changes: "Theme: Dark". |
| `Ungrouped` | `string` | The group title of settings without a group, shown when other settings have one: "Settings". |
| `On`, `Off` | `string` | A toggle's state as assistive technology reads it. |
| `RowState` | `Func<string, string, string>` | A row's header and state: "Dark mode, on". |
| `PreviousOption`, `NextOption` | `string` | The names of the arrows beside a choice's value. |

### Event arguments

| Type | Property | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `SettingsCommandChangedEventArgs` | `Item` | The setting that changed. |
| `SettingsCommandChangedEventArgs` | `Value` | Its new value: a `bool` for a toggle, the option for a choice. |
| `SettingsCommandItemEventArgs` | `Item` | The action that was invoked. |

## Accessibility

- The search field is named "Search settings". Its help text follows the highlighted row, such as "Compact mode, off" or "Theme, Dark".
- The results are a list named "Settings", and each row is a list item named by its header.
- The keyboard stays in the search field. Up and down move the highlight and skip disabled rows, and Page Up and Page Down move five rows. The list does not wrap.
- Enter flips a toggle, moves a choice to its next option, or runs an action. Left and right step a choice without wrapping. Otherwise they move the caret.
- Escape clears the query. With an empty query it raises `CloseRequested`.
- The change notice is a polite live region, so screen readers announce "Compact mode on".
- The switches, the arrows beside a choice and the key caps cannot take focus. A click on any row acts like Enter, and the keyboard stays in the search field.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Down` / `Up` | Move the highlight to the next or previous enabled setting; it does not wrap |
| `PageDown` / `PageUp` | Move the highlight five settings |
| `Enter` | Flip a toggle, move a choice to its next option (after the last comes the first), or run an action |
| `Right` / `Left` | Step a choice to its next or previous option without wrapping; on other rows, move the caret |
| `Escape` | Clear a non-empty query; with an empty query, raise `CloseRequested` |
| Typing | Changes the query, and the list filters as you type |

A click on a row acts like Enter. Clicking a switch or a choice arrow changes that setting directly.

## Motion

- The highlight glides between rows on a snappy spring. When the results change it moves at once.
- The list scrolls smoothly to keep the highlighted row and its group title in view.
- A choice's value rolls up or down in the direction of the change, and switches slide their thumb.
- The change notice rises in with a soft blur and fades out after 2.5 seconds.
- Reduced motion fades the notice and the values and moves the highlight at once. Off shows every change at once.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| The highlight moves between rows | Glides on a snappy spring | Moves at once | Moves at once |
| A choice's value changes | Rolls up or down in the direction of the change | Fades | Shows at once |
| The change notice appears | Rises in with a soft blur, then fades out after 2.5 seconds | Fades in and out | Shows at once |

## Related

- `SettingsPage` for a full settings page with section navigation and a save bar.
- `SecuritySettings`, `BillingOverview`, `UsageBilling` and `CancelFlow`, the other Settings blocks.
- `Switch`, the control in toggle rows, and `Dialog`, which hosts the palette behind a shortcut.
- `SearchField` and `Select` for a single search or choice inside a form.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `SettingsPage` | The settings are split into sections and saved together with a save bar |
| `CommandPalette` | People run app commands, not change configured values |
| `SearchField` | The text searches records or content, not settings |
| `Switch` | A single setting sits in a form or a row that needs no search |
| `Select` / `Combobox` | A form needs one value from a long list |
