# Security settings

> A security checkup, password change, two-step verification and signed-in sessions, each handled in place.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc.Blocks`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc.Blocks --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/blocks/security-settings

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.SecuritySettingsOverviewDemo">
    <arc:SecuritySettings x:Name="Security"
                          IsAuthenticatorEnabled="True"
                          PhoneNumber="+31 6 2045 4821"
                          PasskeyCount="2"
                          AddPasskeyRequested="OnAddPasskeyRequested"
                          RecoveryCodesRequested="OnRecoveryCodesRequested" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Interactivity;
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class SecuritySettingsOverviewDemo : UserControl
{
    public SecuritySettingsOverviewDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        var now = DateTimeOffset.Now;
        Security.PasswordChangedAt = now.AddMonths(-3);
        Security.RecoveryCodesCreatedAt = now.AddDays(-140);
        Security.Sessions.Add(new SecuritySession
        {
            Device = "MacBook Air", Client = "Firefox", Location = "Rotterdam, NL", Kind = SecurityDeviceKind.Laptop,
            LastActive = now, IsCurrent = true
        });
        Security.Sessions.Add(new SecuritySession
        {
            Device = "Pixel 9", Client = "Larkspur app", Location = "Rotterdam, NL", Kind = SecurityDeviceKind.Phone,
            LastActive = now.AddHours(-2)
        });
        Security.Sessions.Add(new SecuritySession
        {
            Device = "ThinkPad X1", Client = "Edge", Location = "Utrecht, NL", Kind = SecurityDeviceKind.Laptop,
            LastActive = now.AddDays(-4)
        });
        Security.Sessions.Add(new SecuritySession
        {
            Device = "iPad mini", Client = "Safari", Location = "Ghent, BE", Kind = SecurityDeviceKind.Tablet,
            LastActive = now.AddDays(-21)
        });
    }

    // A real app runs the passkey ceremony here; the demo just counts one more.
    private void OnAddPasskeyRequested(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) => Security.PasskeyCount++;

    // A real app shows the codes (or creates them first) in a dialog.
    private void OnRecoveryCodesRequested(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) =>
        Security.RecoveryCodesCreatedAt ??= DateTimeOffset.Now;
}
```

## When to use

`SecuritySettings` is the security page of an account. It sits in the settings area of a product and gathers the four
things a person checks about their account: how well it is protected, the password, the two-step methods and the
devices that are signed in. Each action (changing the password, turning a method on, signing out a device) happens on
the page, so the person does not have to move between screens to fix what the checkup flags.

- **A customer account page in a SaaS product or a bank portal.** The checkup tells the person how many of four
  safeguards are on and what to add next, and the password row shows when the password was last changed.
- **An admin's own security settings in an internal tool**, where the admin manages the passkeys and recovery codes of
  their account before they manage anyone else's.
- **A developer platform's account page** that lists the devices holding an API session, so a developer can sign out a
  laptop they no longer have.
- **A fintech app that asks for a second step** by authenticator app or text message, where the switches and the masked
  phone number show exactly which method signs the person in.
- **A recovery flow after a lost phone**, where the person signs out every other session with one confirmed action.

## When not to use

- **Signing in or creating an account.** Use a sign-in form built from `Input` and `PasswordField`; this block assumes
  that the person is already signed in.
- **Workspace-wide security policies**, such as enforced two-step verification or the allowed sign-in methods. Those are
  admin settings: write them as `SettingsGroup` and `SettingsRow` rows on a settings page.
- **A single password field in any other form**, such as a change request inside a checkout. Use `PasswordField` with
  `PasswordStrength` directly.
- **Reviewing an audit trail of events** (who signed in, from where, when, and what changed). Use `Timeline` for the
  history, and keep this block for the current state and the actions on it.
- **Choosing one security setting from a list**, such as a session timeout. Use `Select` in a settings form.

## Usage

Set the account's state and the block shows it in four cards: a checkup, the password, two-step verification and the
signed-in sessions. Every action happens in place. The two switches write `IsAuthenticatorEnabled` and
`IsTextMessageEnabled` back (two-way), and the password form writes `PasswordChangedAt` and `HasPassword` back when it
succeeds. "Add passkey", "View codes" or "Create codes", and signing out, are raised as routed events for the host to
handle.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:SecuritySettings IsAuthenticatorEnabled="True"
                          PhoneNumber="+31 6 2045 4821"
                          PasskeyCount="2">
        <arc:SecuritySettings.Sessions>
            <arc:SecuritySession Device="MacBook Air" Client="Firefox" Location="Rotterdam, NL"
                                 Kind="Laptop" IsCurrent="True" />
            <arc:SecuritySession Device="Pixel 9" Client="Larkspur app" Location="Rotterdam, NL"
                                 Kind="Phone" LastActive="2026-10-20T08:00:00+02:00" />
        </arc:SecuritySettings.Sessions>
    </arc:SecuritySettings>
</UserControl>
```

`SecuritySettings` derives from Avalonia's `TemplatedControl`. Its cards are `SettingsGroup` and `SettingsRow` from the
Settings blocks, the switches are the Arc `Switch`, the password fields are `PasswordField` with `PasswordStrength`, and
the sign-out confirmation is `ConfirmMorph`.

Times are shown relative to `Clock`, a `TimeProvider` that defaults to the system clock. The block reads it again every
30 seconds while it is shown, so "2 hours ago" stays current. Pass a fixed clock in tests:

```csharp
sealed class FixedClock(DateTimeOffset now) : TimeProvider
{
    public override DateTimeOffset GetUtcNow() => now.ToUniversalTime();
}

security.Clock = new FixedClock(new DateTimeOffset(2026, 10, 20, 12, 0, 0, TimeSpan.FromHours(2)));
```

### Anatomy

1. **Checkup card** (`IsSummaryVisible`): a 44 px shield tile with a 22 px glyph, the title, the count line and a
   four-segment meter on the right. Each segment is 28 by 6 px with a 4 px gap, one per safeguard.
2. **Password row** (`HasPassword`, `PasswordChangedAt`): the header "Password", the description ("Last changed 3
   months ago", "Never changed" or "Updated just now") and a button: "Change password", or "Set password" without a
   password.
3. **Password form**: an inline form that opens under the row, at most 400 px wide and aligned with the row text. It holds
   the current password, the new password with its strength meter and requirement list, Cancel and "Update password".
4. **Two-step rows** (`IsAuthenticatorEnabled`, `IsTextMessageEnabled`, `PhoneNumber`, `PasskeyCount`,
   `RecoveryCodesCreatedAt`): an authenticator app switch, a text message switch with the masked number, a passkeys row
   with "Add passkey" and a recovery codes row with "View codes" or "Create codes".
5. **Sessions card** (`Sessions`): a header with the "Sign out other sessions" confirmation, and one row per session: the
   device glyph, "Device · Client", "Location · relative time" and either a "This device" badge or a "Sign out" button.

### Security checkup

The checkup counts four safeguards: a password (`HasPassword`), two-step verification by either method, at least one
passkey (`PasskeyCount`) and recovery codes (`RecoveryCodesCreatedAt`). `ProtectionScore` is that count, from 0 to 4,
and it is read-only. Each safeguard fills its own meter segment. The shield takes the score's tone: success at 4, accent
at 2 or 3, and warning at 0 or 1. The title changes at 4 to "Your account is well protected" and otherwise reads "Add
another safeguard".

Use the checkup to show what is missing, not to pressure the person. Turning a method on or adding a passkey fills the
meter, so the page explains its own result as the person acts.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.SecuritySettingsCheckupDemo">
    <!-- A new account: only a password. Each safeguard you turn on fills a segment of the meter. -->
    <arc:SecuritySettings x:Name="Security"
                          Sections="Summary, TwoStep"
                          PhoneNumber="+31 6 2045 4821"
                          AddPasskeyRequested="OnAddPasskeyRequested"
                          RecoveryCodesRequested="OnRecoveryCodesRequested" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class SecuritySettingsCheckupDemo : UserControl
{
    public SecuritySettingsCheckupDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
    }

    private void OnAddPasskeyRequested(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) => Security.PasskeyCount++;

    private void OnRecoveryCodesRequested(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) =>
        Security.RecoveryCodesCreatedAt ??= DateTimeOffset.Now;
}
```

`Sections` chooses the cards to show, and it combines flags such as `Password, Sessions`. `IsSummaryVisible` hides the
checkup alone; use it when the page already has its own summary, as the demo below does.

### Changing the password

"Change password" opens the form under the row. The form asks for the current password and a new one. "Update password"
needs both: the current password is not empty, and the new password reaches at least fair strength (the
`MinimumPasswordLevel` constant, level 2). Enter submits the form when the button is enabled, and Escape cancels.

Submitting raises `PasswordChangeRequested` with `CurrentPassword` and `NewPassword`. The host checks the password and
then decides:

- **Accept** by leaving `ErrorMessage` empty. The form closes, `PasswordChangedAt` becomes the clock's time and the row
  reads "Updated just now".
- **Reject** by setting `ErrorMessage`. The message appears under the current password field, the form stays open and
  focus returns to that field. Without a password the message appears under the new password field.

Without a password (`HasPassword="False"`) the row offers "Set password" and the form asks only for the new one. A
successful change sets `HasPassword` to true. `OpenPasswordForm()`, `ClosePasswordForm()` and `SubmitPasswordChange()`
do the same from code.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.SecuritySettingsChangePasswordDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="16">
        <arc:SecuritySettings x:Name="Security"
                              Sections="Password"
                              PasswordChangeRequested="OnPasswordChangeRequested" />
        <StackPanel Spacing="4">
            <TextBlock Text="The current password is &quot;correct horse&quot;. Anything else is rejected."
                       TextWrapping="Wrap"
                       FontSize="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TypeSM}"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
            <TextBlock x:Name="Log"
                       Text="No requests yet."
                       TextWrapping="Wrap"
                       FontSize="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TypeXS}"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
        </StackPanel>
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class SecuritySettingsChangePasswordDemo : UserControl
{
    private int _requests;

    public SecuritySettingsChangePasswordDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Security.PasswordChangedAt = DateTimeOffset.Now.AddMonths(-3);
    }

    // Check the current password; an error message keeps the form open and shows the message under that field.
    private void OnPasswordChangeRequested(object? sender, SecurityPasswordChangeEventArgs e)
    {
        _requests++;
        if (e.CurrentPassword != "correct horse")
        {
            e.ErrorMessage = "That isn't your current password.";
            Log.Text = $"Request {_requests}: rejected, the current password did not match.";
            return;
        }
        Log.Text = $"Request {_requests}: accepted, the new password is {e.NewPassword.Length} characters long.";
    }
}
```

### Signed-in sessions

Sessions are listed with the current device first, then by most recent activity. The current device has a "This device"
badge and cannot be signed out here. Every other session has a "Sign out" button. Choosing it fades and collapses the
row, removes the session from `Sessions` when that list can be changed, and raises `SessionSignedOut`.

"Sign out other sessions" is a `ConfirmMorph`. It is enabled only when another session exists, and it asks first: the
question names the count ("Sign out 3 sessions?"), and Escape or Cancel keeps every session. When the person confirms,
the rows leave one after another, 35 ms apart, and `OtherSessionsSignedOut` carries the sessions that were removed. When
the list is read-only (for example an array), the rows are hidden instead of removed.

`SignOut(session)` and `SignOutOtherSessions()` do the same from code.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.SecuritySettingsSessionsDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="16">
        <arc:SecuritySettings x:Name="Security"
                              Sections="Sessions"
                              SessionSignedOut="OnSessionSignedOut"
                              OtherSessionsSignedOut="OnOtherSessionsSignedOut" />
        <DockPanel>
            <arc:Button DockPanel.Dock="Right"
                        Variant="Secondary"
                        Size="Small"
                        Content="Reset"
                        Click="OnResetClick" />
            <TextBlock x:Name="Log"
                       Text="Sign out one session, or all the others at once."
                       VerticalAlignment="Center"
                       TextWrapping="Wrap"
                       Margin="0,0,16,0"
                       FontSize="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TypeSM}"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
        </DockPanel>
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Collections;
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class SecuritySettingsSessionsDemo : UserControl
{
    public SecuritySettingsSessionsDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Reset();
    }

    private void OnSessionSignedOut(object? sender, SecuritySessionEventArgs e) =>
        Log.Text = $"Signed out {e.Session.Device}. {Security.Sessions.Count} sessions left.";

    private void OnOtherSessionsSignedOut(object? sender, SecuritySessionsEventArgs e) =>
        Log.Text = $"Signed out {e.Sessions.Count} other sessions. Only this device is left.";

    private void OnResetClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        Reset();
        Log.Text = "Sessions restored.";
    }

    // A new list replaces the old one; the block lists it current first, then by most recent activity.
    private void Reset()
    {
        var now = DateTimeOffset.Now;
        Security.Sessions = new AvaloniaList<SecuritySession>
        {
            new() { Device = "ThinkPad X1", Client = "Edge", Location = "Utrecht, NL", Kind = SecurityDeviceKind.Laptop, LastActive = now.AddDays(-4) },
            new() { Device = "MacBook Air", Client = "Firefox", Location = "Rotterdam, NL", Kind = SecurityDeviceKind.Laptop, LastActive = now, IsCurrent = true },
            new() { Device = "iPad mini", Client = "Safari", Location = "Ghent, BE", Kind = SecurityDeviceKind.Tablet, LastActive = now.AddDays(-21) },
            new() { Device = "Pixel 9", Client = "Larkspur app", Location = "Rotterdam, NL", Kind = SecurityDeviceKind.Phone, LastActive = now.AddHours(-2) },
            new() { Device = "Studio iMac", Client = "Chrome", Location = "Rotterdam, NL", Kind = SecurityDeviceKind.Desktop, LastActive = now.AddDays(-1) }
        };
    }
}
```

On a narrow page the meter moves under the checkup text and "Sign out other sessions" moves under the list. Rows with a
small control, such as a badge or "Sign out", keep it beside the text; rows with a wider button stack it under the text.

### Binding to a view model

The view model owns the security state and the rules for it. The block shows the state, raises requests, and applies the
result that the view model sets.

```csharp
public partial class AccountSecurityViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    private readonly IAccountSecurity _security;

    public AccountSecurityViewModel(IAccountSecurity security)
    {
        _security = security;
    }

    [ObservableProperty]
    private bool _isAuthenticatorEnabled;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private DateTimeOffset? _passwordChangedAt;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private int _passkeyCount;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private DateTimeOffset? _recoveryCodesCreatedAt;

    public ObservableCollection<SecuritySession> Sessions { get; } = [];

    public async Task<string?> ChangePasswordAsync(string current, string next)
    {
        var result = await _security.ChangePasswordAsync(current, next);
        return result.IsSuccess ? null : result.Error;
    }
}
```

```xml
<arc:SecuritySettings IsAuthenticatorEnabled="{Binding IsAuthenticatorEnabled, Mode=TwoWay}"
                      PasswordChangedAt="{Binding PasswordChangedAt, Mode=TwoWay}"
                      Sessions="{Binding Sessions}"
                      PasskeyCount="{Binding PasskeyCount}"
                      RecoveryCodesCreatedAt="{Binding RecoveryCodesCreatedAt}" />
```

- `IsAuthenticatorEnabled`, `IsTextMessageEnabled`, `HasPassword` and `PasswordChangedAt` are two-way, so the view model
  receives the change from the switch or the form.
- The password change has no command. Handle `PasswordChangeRequested`, call `ChangePasswordAsync` and set the
  returned message as `ErrorMessage` on the event arguments.
- `Sessions` is an `IList<SecuritySession>` that the block updates when a session is signed out. Bind it to an
  `ObservableCollection<SecuritySession>` so the list stays in step with the server.
- `PasskeyCount` and `RecoveryCodesCreatedAt` are one-way. Update them after the host finishes "Add passkey" or "Create
  codes".

### Example: Account security for a bank customer

A bank's portal shows a customer their account security, without the sessions card (the Sessions demo covers that
card). The customer has an authenticator app and two passkeys but no recovery codes yet, so the checkup reads three of
four and the recovery codes row offers "Create codes". The scene has no open form, so the screenshot shows the resting
state.

![Account security with a three of four checkup, two-step methods and two signed-in devices](https://docs.tkcode.si/shots/Docs/Blocks/SecuritySettings/images/SecuritySettings.webp)

```xml
<arc:SecuritySettings Width="640"
                      Sections="Summary, Password, TwoStep"
                      PasswordChangedAt="2026-07-14T09:00:00+02:00"
                      IsAuthenticatorEnabled="True"
                      IsTextMessageEnabled="False"
                      PhoneNumber="+31 6 2045 4821"
                      PasskeyCount="2" />
```

### Content guidelines

The block's labels are short and written for the person who owns the account. Use the sentence case and the verbs the
defaults use, and describe a state in the row rather than in an alert. Describe a method by what it does for the person
("Codes go to •••• 4821"), not by its protocol name.

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| Two factor authentication | Two-step verification |
| Password was changed 3 months ago | Last changed 3 months ago |
| Remove session | Sign out (on each row) and Sign out other sessions (for the list) |
| Are you sure? | Sign out 3 sessions? (the count is in the question) |
| 2FA: Off | Text message switch with its row description |
| Error: wrong password | That isn't your current password. (the reason, under the field) |

Keep the labels in `SecuritySettingsLabels` when you localize. Use the `Culture` property for dates, because relative
times and dates follow it.

### Best practices

**Do**

- Turn on the checkup for every account page, so the meter and the next step are always visible. Hide it only when the
  page already has its own summary.
- Set `RecoveryCodesCreatedAt` and `PasskeyCount` from the server before showing the page. Their rows and the score
  depend on them, so a stale value gives a false checkup.
- Set `ErrorMessage` for any password the server rejects, with the server's reason in words the person can act on. The
  form stays open, so they can correct the value without retyping everything.
- Bind `Sessions` to the server's list. Signing out a session in the block removes it from the list only when the list is
  writable, so the server call belongs in the `SessionSignedOut` handler.

**Avoid**

- Showing the phone number in full. The block shows only its last four digits, and the app should not show more elsewhere
  on the page.
- Using the sessions card for the sign-in history. It lists the sessions that are open now, not past events.
- Replacing the whole `Labels` object for a single word. Build a new `SecuritySettingsLabels` with the properties you need
  changed, so the other texts keep their defaults.

### Common questions

**Why is "Update password" disabled when the new password looks fine?** The button needs both a non-empty current
password and a new password that reaches at least fair strength (level 2).

**How do I handle a sign-out the server refuses?** The row leaves before `SessionSignedOut` is raised, so the host cannot
stop it. When the server refuses, add the session back to `Sessions` and show your own message.

**Why does the text message switch stay off?** It is disabled until `PhoneNumber` has a value, and its row says "Add a
phone number first". Set the number to enable it.

**Can I show only the sessions on a page of my own?** Yes. Set `Sections="Sessions"`, or combine flags such as
`Password, Sessions`. The cards that are not chosen are not shown at all.

## API reference

### SecuritySettings

The account security page: a checkup of four safeguards (password, two-step verification, passkeys, recovery codes), the password with a change form that opens in place, the two-step methods, and every signed-in session with a way to sign it out. Each action happens on the page; the host hears about it through routed events.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `PasswordChangedAt` | `DateTimeOffset?` | `null` | When the password was last changed; null reads "Never changed". Set to the clock's time after a successful change (two-way). |
| `HasPassword` | `bool` | `true` | Whether the account has a password (default true). Without one the row offers "Set password" and the form asks only for the new password; a successful change sets it to true (two-way). |
| `IsAuthenticatorEnabled` | `bool` | `false` | Whether sign-ins ask for a code from an authenticator app (two-way, follows its switch). |
| `IsTextMessageEnabled` | `bool` | `false` | Whether sign-ins send a code by text message (two-way, follows its switch). |
| `PhoneNumber` | `string?` | `null` | The phone number for text messages; only its last four digits are shown ("•••• 4821"). Without one the text message switch is disabled. |
| `PasskeyCount` | `int` | `0` | How many passkeys the account has. |
| `RecoveryCodesCreatedAt` | `DateTimeOffset?` | `null` | When the recovery codes were created; null means there are none. |
| `Sessions` | `IList<SecuritySession>` | – | The signed-in sessions, listed current first, then by most recent activity. A signed-out session leaves its row and is removed from this list when the list can be changed. Defaults to an empty observable list. |
| `IsSummaryVisible` | `bool` | `true` | Whether the security checkup card is shown at the top (default true). |
| `Sections` | `SecuritySettingsSections` | `All` | Which cards are shown (default all): show only the sessions, or only the password, on a page of your own. |
| `ProtectionScore` | `int` | – | *Read-only.* How many of the four safeguards are on (0–4): a password, two-step verification by either method, at least one passkey, and recovery codes. |
| `IsPasswordFormOpen` | `bool` | – | *Read-only.* Whether the password form is open. |
| `Labels` | `SecuritySettingsLabels` | – | Every built-in text and the culture for dates; replace the whole object to localize. |
| `CompactWidth` | `double` | `560` | Below this width the meter moves under the summary text and "Sign out other sessions" moves under the list (default 560). |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `PasswordChangeRequested` | `SecurityPasswordChangeEventArgs` | Raised when the password form is submitted. Set `ErrorMessage` to reject it. |
| `AddPasskeyRequested` | `RoutedEventArgs` | Raised when "Add passkey" is pressed; the host runs the passkey ceremony and updates `PasskeyCount`. |
| `RecoveryCodesRequested` | `RoutedEventArgs` | Raised when "View codes" or "Create codes" is pressed; the host shows or creates the codes and updates `RecoveryCodesCreatedAt`. |
| `SessionSignedOut` | `SecuritySessionEventArgs` | Raised after a session's "Sign out" row has left and the session was taken off `Sessions`. |
| `OtherSessionsSignedOut` | `SecuritySessionsEventArgs` | Raised after "Sign out other sessions" was confirmed and every other session's row has left. |

Pseudo-classes: `:compact`, `:rows-stacked`, `:password-open`, `:tone-success`, `:tone-accent`, `:tone-warning`, `:password-on`, `:two-step-on`, `:passkey-on`, `:recovery-on`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

**SecuritySession** (a plain object, can be written in XAML)

| Property | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Device` | `string` | The device's name, such as "MacBook Air". |
| `Client` | `string?` | The browser or app, shown after the device name. |
| `Location` | `string?` | Where the device signed in from, such as "Rotterdam, NL". |
| `LastActive` | `DateTimeOffset` | When the session was last used; shown relative to `Clock`. |
| `Kind` | `SecurityDeviceKind` | `Desktop`, `Laptop`, `Phone`, `Tablet` or `Other`; picks the glyph. |
| `IsCurrent` | `bool` | The device in use: listed first, marked "This device", cannot be signed out here. |

**Event arguments**

| Type | Property | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `SecurityPasswordChangeEventArgs` | `CurrentPassword` | What was typed as the current password (empty without a password). |
| | `NewPassword` | The new password. |
| | `ErrorMessage` | Set to reject the change; the form stays open and shows it. |
| `SecuritySessionEventArgs` | `Session` | The session that was signed out. |
| `SecuritySessionsEventArgs` | `Sessions` | The sessions signed out by "Sign out other sessions", in list order. |

**SecuritySettingsSections** (flags): `Summary`, `Password`, `TwoStep`, `Sessions`, `All` (default), `None`.

**SecuritySettingsLabels**: `Culture` and one property per built-in text, such as `SummaryProtected`,
`SummaryCount`, `PasswordChanged`, `ChangePassword`, `UpdatePassword`, `TextMessageDescription`, `PasskeyCount`,
`SessionsHeader`, `SignOut`, `SignOutSession`, `SignOutOthers` and `SignOutOthersPrompt`.

## Accessibility

- Every switch and button has a name. Switches take their row's header ("Authenticator app") and description. A
  session's button is named after its device, such as "Sign out ThinkPad X1", and the badge reads "This device".
- The checkup meter is named "{n} of 4 safeguards on". The checkup title and the password row's description are polite
  live regions, so "Your account is well protected" and "Updated just now" are announced when they change.
- Opening the form moves focus to its first field. Enter submits when "Update password" is enabled and Escape cancels.
  After closing, focus returns to "Change password". A rejected change focuses the field with the error.
- When a focused "Sign out" row leaves, focus moves to the next session's button, or the previous one.
- "Sign out other sessions" follows `ConfirmMorph`: it asks first, and Escape or Cancel keeps the sessions. It is
  disabled when no other session is left.
- Tab order follows the cards from top to bottom. The text message switch is disabled without a phone number, and the
  row says why.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Where | Action |
|---|---|---|
| `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` | Anywhere | Move through the cards and rows from top to bottom |
| `Enter` | "Change password" or "Set password" | Open the password form; focus moves to the current password field |
| `Enter` | Password form | Submit when "Update password" is enabled |
| `Escape` | Password form | Cancel: close the form without saving and return focus to "Change password" |
| `Escape` or Cancel | "Sign out other sessions" question | Keep every session |

## Motion

- Session rows leave with a fade and a height collapse on a smooth spring, before the session is removed. "Sign out other
  sessions" starts each row 35 ms after the one above it.
- The password form springs open and closed under its row. The password row's description changes with a blur swap.
  "Sign out other sessions" morphs into its question and result in place.
- The checkup title blurs to its new text. The count rolls up or down with the score. Meter segments and the shield
  fade to their new color.
- Reduced motion keeps short fades and drops the springs, the blur and the roll. Off places everything at once, and a
  signed-out row leaves the list at once.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| Session row leaves | Fades and collapses on a smooth spring | Fades | Leaves at once |
| Password form opens or closes | Springs open or closed | Shown or hidden with a short fade | Immediate |
| Password description changes | Blur swap to the new text | Short fade | Immediate |
| Checkup count and meter | Count rolls; segments fade to their color | Color fades | Immediate |

## Related

- `SettingsGroup` and `SettingsRow` build the cards and rows. The other Settings blocks use them too: Settings page,
  Settings command, Billing overview, Usage billing and Cancel flow.
- `PasswordField` and `PasswordStrength` for the password form, `Switch` for the two-step methods, `Badge` for the
  current device, `Button` for the row actions and `ConfirmMorph` for signing out every other session.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `SettingsPage` | The security card sits inside a page of settings with a navigation list |
| `PasswordField` / `PasswordStrength` | You need only a password field, or a password with its rules, outside this page |
| `Switch` | A single on or off setting with a label and description |
| `ConfirmMorph` | A single destructive action needs a confirmation in place |
| `Timeline` | The person needs the history of account events, not the current state |

# Billing overview

> The current plan, next charge, payment method and invoice history on one page, with the actions next to each.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc.Blocks`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc.Blocks --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/blocks/billing-overview

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.BillingOverviewOverviewDemo">
    <arc:BillingOverview BillingEmail="accounts@larkspur.co" MaxWidth="720">
        <arc:BillingOverview.Plan>
            <arc:BillingPlan Name="Studio" Price="90" Seats="6" Interval="Month" Status="Active" RenewsOn="2026-11-01" />
        </arc:BillingOverview.Plan>
        <arc:BillingOverview.PaymentMethod>
            <arc:BillingPaymentMethod Brand="Mastercard" Last4="5108" ExpiryMonth="4" ExpiryYear="2029" />
        </arc:BillingOverview.PaymentMethod>
        <arc:BillingOverview.Invoices>
            <arc:BillingInvoice Number="LS-2026-010" Date="2026-10-01" Amount="90" Status="Paid" />
            <arc:BillingInvoice Number="LS-2026-009" Date="2026-09-01" Amount="90" Status="Paid" />
            <arc:BillingInvoice Number="LS-2026-008" Date="2026-08-01" Amount="90" Status="Paid" />
            <arc:BillingInvoice Number="LS-2026-007" Date="2026-07-01" Amount="75" Status="Refunded" />
            <arc:BillingInvoice Number="LS-2026-006" Date="2026-06-01" Amount="75" Status="Paid" />
            <arc:BillingInvoice Number="LS-2026-005" Date="2026-05-01" Amount="75" Status="Paid" />
        </arc:BillingOverview.Invoices>
    </arc:BillingOverview>
</UserControl>
```

## When to use

`BillingOverview` is the billing page of an account or workspace settings area. It answers the three questions people
bring to billing (what am I paying, when is the next charge, what did I pay before) and places the actions that change
those answers next to the facts they change: changing the plan, updating the card, editing the billing email and
downloading an invoice.

- **Workspace billing in a SaaS admin console**: an owner opens Settings, then Billing, and sees that the Team plan
  renews on Nov 1 for 12 seats, which card will be charged and when the next invoice is due. The block answers that
  without a separate report.
- **Handing invoices to finance**: a finance lead needs last quarter's invoices for an expense report. The invoice table
  lists them newest first with a download button on each row, so nobody has to ask the vendor for a PDF.
- **A per-seat plan with a fixed price**: a team plan billed monthly or yearly, where the next charge is the plan price
  for the current seat count. The plan card shows the price per period, the seats and the amount of the next charge.
- **Trials and failed payments**: a trial shows when it ends and what the first charge will be; a plan whose last charge
  failed shows a danger badge, so the owner fixes the card before access is affected.
- **Billing actions that open your own flows**: plan changes, card updates and cancellations usually need confirmation,
  proration or a payment provider's form. The block only raises events, so each flow stays in your code.

## When not to use

- **Usage-based billing where this period's total depends on metered units**: use `UsageBilling`, which shows the spend
  so far, the projected total, the usage per meter and the spending limit.
- **Choosing or comparing plans on a pricing page**: use `BillingToggle` and `BillingPrice`. `BillingOverview` shows the
  plan a customer already has, not the options they can pick from.
- **Collecting card details**: the block shows the card on file and never takes card numbers. Open your payment
  provider's form in a `Dialog` from `UpdatePaymentMethodRequested`.
- **A long, searchable payment history**: use `Table`, which sorts, filters and pages rows. The invoice
  table here shows a short, newest-first list with "Show all invoices" for the rest.
- **A cancellation with questions or a retention offer**: use `CancelFlow`, a multi-step flow that you can start from
  `CancelPlanRequested`. `BillingOverview` only raises the request.

## Usage

```xml
<arc:BillingOverview Plan="{Binding Plan}"
                     PaymentMethod="{Binding Card}"
                     BillingEmail="{Binding BillingEmail}"
                     Invoices="{Binding Invoices}"
                     VisibleInvoiceCount="6" />
```

`BillingOverview` derives from Avalonia's `TemplatedControl` and is composed of `SettingsGroup`, `SettingsRow`, `Badge`
and `Button`. It inherits their spacing, focus ring, hover states and motion, so a billing page built from it matches
the other settings blocks without extra styling. Set four data properties: `Plan`, `PaymentMethod`, `BillingEmail` and
`Invoices`. The three model classes (`BillingPlan`, `BillingPaymentMethod` and `BillingInvoice`) are plain objects.
They can be written in XAML, as in the previews, or created in code. They raise `PropertyChanged`, so a change to a
plan, card or invoice after it is shown updates the view without replacing the object.

`Invoices` starts as an empty list you can add to. Replace it or bind it to your own collection; changes to an
observable collection update the table. Invoices are always shown newest first, by `Date`.

### Anatomy

The page has three cards, separated by the 16 px `GroupGap`. From top to bottom:

1. **Plan card** (`Plan`): the eyebrow "Current plan", the plan name (`PlanNamePart`, `TypeXL`) and a status badge
   (`PlanStatusPart`). Below the name, a detail line with the seat count and the renewal date. On the right, the price
   (`PricePart`) in `TypeXL` with "per month" or "per year" in the secondary text color. The footer (`NextInvoicePart`)
   shows the next charge with the amount emphasized, then the "Cancel plan" and "Change plan" buttons.
2. **Payment card** (`PaymentMethod`, `BillingEmail`): the brand mark (`CardBrandPart`), a 36 by 24 px rounded box with
   the brand text in `TypeXS`, followed by "{Brand} ending in {Last4}" (`CardTitlePart`) and the expiry line
   (`CardExpiryPart`). The "Update" button (`UpdateCardPart`) sits on the right. Below a divider, the "Billing email" row
   (`EmailRowPart`) shows the address and the "Edit" button (`EditEmailPart`).
3. **Invoices card** (`Invoices`): the "Invoices" title and a column header with Date, Invoice, Amount and Status
   (`InvoiceHeaderPart`, 32 px high). Each row (`InvoiceRowsPart`) is 48 px high, with a hairline above it, the date,
   the invoice number, the amount right-aligned in tabular figures, a status badge and a 36 px download icon button.
4. **Folded rows and "Show all invoices"** (`MoreInvoicesPart`, `ShowAllPart`): the invoices beyond
   `VisibleInvoiceCount` sit in a folding part, and the footer button toggles it.
5. **Empty state** (`InvoicesEmptyPart`): with no invoices, a 40 px tile, "No invoices yet" and a hint line replace the
   table.

Below 560 px (`NarrowWidth`), the price moves under the plan name, the footers stack and the Invoice column hides. Card
rows under 440 px move their button under the text. The Status column keeps a 14 px gap instead of 28 px.

### Plan states

The plan's `Status` sets the badge, the detail line and the footer, so every state reads the same way.

| `Status` | Badge | Detail line | Footer |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Active` | Success | "6 seats · Renews on Nov 1, 2026" | Next charge, "Cancel plan", "Change plan" |
| `Trialing` | Accent | "Trial ends on Nov 1, 2026" | Next charge, "Cancel plan", "Change plan" |
| `PastDue` | Danger | "Payment overdue since Oct 1, 2026" | Next charge, "Cancel plan", "Change plan" |
| `Canceled` | Neutral | "Ends on Nov 1, 2026" | "Change plan" only; no "Cancel plan" |

With no plan (`Plan` is null), the card shows "No plan", "Choose a plan to get started." and a "Choose a plan" button
that raises `ChangePlanRequested`. A canceled plan keeps its object, so the owner still sees when access ends.
The payment card follows the same rule: with no `PaymentMethod`, "Add card" raises `UpdatePaymentMethodRequested`.

### Invoice states

| `Status` | Badge | Row treatment |
|---|---|---|
| `Paid` | Success | Normal |
| `Open` | Neutral | Normal; issued and not yet paid |
| `PastDue` | Danger | Normal; due and unpaid |
| `Refunded` | Neutral | Muted: badge and amount at 70 percent opacity |
| `Void` | Neutral | Muted: badge and amount at 70 percent opacity |

Muted rows stay in the table and keep their download button, because the customer still needs the document. Do not
remove a refunded invoice from `Invoices` to hide it; the history then no longer matches the bank statement.

### Trial and an expiring card

A trialing plan shows when the trial ends and what the first charge will be: set `Status` to `Trialing` and `RenewsOn`
to the trial end date.

The card expiry is checked against `Clock`. When the expiry month starts within 60 days, the expiry line turns to the
warning color and reads "Expires soon" with the date, and a card past its expiry month reads "Expired" in the danger
color. `IsPaymentMethodExpiringSoon` and `IsPaymentMethodExpired` report the same two states, so you can show a banner
in your own page or send a reminder email. The brand is shown as short text in a small frame (VISA, MC, AMEX), never
as a logo. Without invoices, the table is replaced by "No invoices yet".

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.BillingOverviewTrialDemo">
    <arc:BillingOverview x:Name="Billing" BillingEmail="noor@larkspur.co" MaxWidth="720">
        <arc:BillingOverview.Plan>
            <arc:BillingPlan Name="Studio" Price="90" Seats="6" Interval="Month" Status="Trialing" />
        </arc:BillingOverview.Plan>
        <arc:BillingOverview.PaymentMethod>
            <arc:BillingPaymentMethod Brand="Visa" Last4="0417" />
        </arc:BillingOverview.PaymentMethod>
    </arc:BillingOverview>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class BillingOverviewTrialDemo : UserControl
{
    public BillingOverviewTrialDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        // Relative to today: the trial ends in 12 days and the card expires next month, so it shows "Expires soon".
        var today = DateTime.Today;
        Billing.Plan!.RenewsOn = today.AddDays(12);
        var expiry = today.AddMonths(1);
        Billing.PaymentMethod!.ExpiryMonth = expiry.Month;
        Billing.PaymentMethod.ExpiryYear = expiry.Year;
    }
}
```

"Today" comes from the CLR property `Clock`, a `TimeProvider` (the system clock by default). Set a fixed clock in tests:

```csharp
billing.Clock = TimeProvider.System; // or any TimeProvider that your test supplies
```

### Handling the actions

Every button raises a routed event and changes nothing by itself. The events are `ChangePlanRequested`,
`CancelPlanRequested`, `UpdatePaymentMethodRequested` and `EditBillingEmailRequested`, and
`InvoiceDownloadRequested`, whose `BillingInvoiceEventArgs.Invoice` is the invoice on that row. Open your own dialog or
flow from the event, call your API, and then update `Plan`, `PaymentMethod`, `BillingEmail` or `Invoices` so the block
shows the result. The block does not confirm, prorate or call a payment service.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.BillingOverviewEventsDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="16" MaxWidth="720">
        <arc:BillingOverview x:Name="Billing" BillingEmail="accounts@larkspur.co" VisibleInvoiceCount="3">
            <arc:BillingOverview.Plan>
                <arc:BillingPlan Name="Studio" Price="90" Seats="6" Interval="Month" Status="Active" RenewsOn="2026-11-01" />
            </arc:BillingOverview.Plan>
            <arc:BillingOverview.PaymentMethod>
                <arc:BillingPaymentMethod Brand="Mastercard" Last4="5108" ExpiryMonth="4" ExpiryYear="2029" />
            </arc:BillingOverview.PaymentMethod>
            <arc:BillingOverview.Invoices>
                <arc:BillingInvoice Number="LS-2026-010" Date="2026-10-01" Amount="90" Status="Paid" />
                <arc:BillingInvoice Number="LS-2026-009" Date="2026-09-01" Amount="90" Status="Paid" />
                <arc:BillingInvoice Number="LS-2026-008" Date="2026-08-01" Amount="90" Status="Paid" />
                <arc:BillingInvoice Number="LS-2026-007" Date="2026-07-01" Amount="75" Status="Refunded" />
            </arc:BillingOverview.Invoices>
        </arc:BillingOverview>
        <Border Padding="24,16"
                TextElement.FontFamily="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource BodyFontFamily}"
                CornerRadius="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource RadiusPanel}"
                Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Surface}"
                BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Border}"
                BorderThickness="1">
            <StackPanel Spacing="6">
                <TextBlock Text="Event log"
                           FontSize="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TypeXS}"
                           FontWeight="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource WeightMedium}"
                           Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
                <TextBlock x:Name="Log"
                           Text="Press any button above."
                           TextWrapping="Wrap"
                           FontSize="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TypeSM}"
                           Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
            </StackPanel>
        </Border>
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class BillingOverviewEventsDemo : UserControl
{
    private readonly List<string> _entries = new();

    public BillingOverviewEventsDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Billing.ChangePlanRequested += (_, _) => Write("ChangePlanRequested");
        Billing.CancelPlanRequested += (_, _) => Write("CancelPlanRequested");
        Billing.UpdatePaymentMethodRequested += (_, _) => Write("UpdatePaymentMethodRequested");
        Billing.EditBillingEmailRequested += (_, _) => Write("EditBillingEmailRequested");
        Billing.InvoiceDownloadRequested += (_, e) => Write($"InvoiceDownloadRequested: {e.Invoice.Number}");
    }

    private void Write(string entry)
    {
        // Newest first, the last five events.
        _entries.Insert(0, $"{DateTime.Now:HH:mm:ss}  {entry}");
        if (_entries.Count > 5)
        {
            _entries.RemoveAt(_entries.Count - 1);
        }
        Log.Text = string.Join(Environment.NewLine, _entries);
    }
}
```

The Events demo writes each event to a log. The download handler is asynchronous, so the view model can save the file
in the background:

```csharp
billing.InvoiceDownloadRequested += async (_, e) =>
{
    var pdf = await invoices.DownloadAsync(e.Invoice.Number);
    await SaveAsync(pdf, $"{e.Invoice.Number}.pdf");
};

billing.CancelPlanRequested += (_, _) => cancelDialog.Open(); // for example a CancelFlow in a Dialog
```

`VisibleInvoiceCount` (default 4) sets how many invoices show before "Show all invoices (n)". The button unfolds the
rest and changes to "Show fewer". `IsInvoiceListExpanded` is the same state; bind it two-way to keep it in your view model.

### Data shape and performance

The block does not page, sort or search. Pass the invoices the page should show: the most recent ones for the overview,
and a link to the complete history. The table reuses its rows when the collection changes, so adding an invoice does
not rebuild the table. Give each invoice a unique `Number`, because it names the download button.

Money and dates use `Labels.Culture` (en-US by default), and each amount uses its invoice's `Currency` or the plan's.
Format amounts once, in the block.

### Binding to a view model

In an MVVM app, the view model owns the billing data and the flows, and the block displays them. The example below uses
CommunityToolkit.Mvvm. The app's own service (`IBillingService`) and its methods are placeholders for your API.

```csharp
public partial class BillingViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    private readonly IBillingService _billing;

    public BillingViewModel(IBillingService billing)
    {
        _billing = billing;
    }

    [ObservableProperty]
    private BillingPlan? _plan;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private BillingPaymentMethod? _paymentMethod;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private string? _billingEmail;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private decimal? _nextInvoiceAmount;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private bool _isInvoiceListExpanded;

    public ObservableCollection<BillingInvoice> Invoices { get; } = new();

    [RelayCommand]
    private async Task CancelPlanAsync()
    {
        await _billing.CancelAtPeriodEndAsync();
        Plan!.Status = BillingPlanStatus.Canceled;
    }

    [RelayCommand]
    private async Task DownloadInvoiceAsync(BillingInvoice invoice)
    {
        var pdf = await _billing.DownloadAsync(invoice.Number);
        await _files.SaveAsync(pdf, $"{invoice.Number}.pdf");
    }
}
```

```xml
<arc:BillingOverview Plan="{Binding Plan}"
                     PaymentMethod="{Binding PaymentMethod}"
                     BillingEmail="{Binding BillingEmail}"
                     NextInvoiceAmount="{Binding NextInvoiceAmount}"
                     Invoices="{Binding Invoices}"
                     IsInvoiceListExpanded="{Binding IsInvoiceListExpanded, Mode=TwoWay}"
                     VisibleInvoiceCount="6" />
```

The block does not expose commands, so connect its events to the view model in code-behind, calling the
`CancelPlanCommand` and `DownloadInvoiceCommand` the toolkit generates.

Two-way bindings: `IsInvoiceListExpanded` is the only property to bind `Mode=TwoWay`, because "Show all invoices"
writes it. The other inputs are one-way: change the model objects (for example `Plan.Status`) or replace the property,
and the view follows.

### Text and language

All built-in text lives in `BillingOverviewLabels`. Replace the whole object to reword or localize the block; the
texts that contain values are functions that receive the values already formatted with `Culture`. The defaults are
English, for example "Renews on Nov 1, 2026", "Show all invoices (6)" and "Download LS-2026-010".

```csharp
billing.Labels = new BillingOverviewLabels
{
    Culture = CultureInfo.GetCultureInfo("nl-NL"),
    CurrentPlan = "Huidig abonnement",
    ChangePlan = "Abonnement wijzigen",
    RenewsOn = date => $"Wordt verlengd op {date}",
    ShowAll = count => $"Alle facturen tonen ({count})",
};
```

Replace the whole object rather than one field, because its properties are init-only. Keep the functions that take values,
since they set the word order. One object covers the whole block, from the plan card to the empty state.

### Example: Team plan billing page

A workspace owner opens billing on a Team plan. Two seats were added in October, so the plan now costs $288 per month
for 14 seats, and the footer shows the next invoice on Nov 1 at the same amount. The card is a Mastercard that expires
in 2029, so no warning shows. The invoice table shows three rows and a "Show all invoices (4)" button; one earlier
invoice was refunded and is muted. The owner can download any invoice, change the plan or update the card from here.

The footer's next charge follows `Price` unless `NextInvoiceAmount` is set, so this example leaves it null. Set it only
when the next charge differs from the plan price. The invoice descriptions are not visible; they become part of each
download button's accessible name.

![A team plan billing page with a plan card, a card on file, a billing email and three recent invoices](https://docs.tkcode.si/shots/Docs/Blocks/BillingOverview/images/BillingOverview.webp)

```xml
<StackPanel Width="680" Spacing="16">
    <arc:BillingOverview BillingEmail="accounts@northwind.dev"
                         VisibleInvoiceCount="3">
        <arc:BillingOverview.Plan>
            <arc:BillingPlan Name="Team" Price="288" Currency="USD" Seats="14"
                             Interval="Month" Status="Active" RenewsOn="2026-11-01" />
        </arc:BillingOverview.Plan>
        <arc:BillingOverview.PaymentMethod>
            <arc:BillingPaymentMethod Brand="Mastercard" Last4="5108"
                                      ExpiryMonth="4" ExpiryYear="2029" />
        </arc:BillingOverview.PaymentMethod>
        <arc:BillingOverview.Invoices>
            <arc:BillingInvoice Number="LS-2026-010" Date="2026-10-01" Amount="288"
                                Status="Paid" Description="Team plan, 14 seats" />
            <arc:BillingInvoice Number="LS-2026-009" Date="2026-09-01" Amount="240"
                                Status="Paid" Description="Team plan, 12 seats" />
            <arc:BillingInvoice Number="LS-2026-008" Date="2026-08-01" Amount="200"
                                Status="Paid" Description="Team plan, 10 seats" />
            <arc:BillingInvoice Number="LS-2026-007" Date="2026-07-01" Amount="200"
                                Status="Refunded" Description="Team plan, 10 seats" />
        </arc:BillingOverview.Invoices>
    </arc:BillingOverview>
</StackPanel>
```

### Content guidelines

Write amounts with the currency and dates with the month name, as in "$240.00" and "Nov 1, 2026". Name the plan as the
customer bought it, and use the same word as the rest of the product: "Plan", not "Subscription" if the app says "Plan".

- Button text is a verb and an object in sentence case: "Change plan", "Cancel plan", "Update payment method".
- Keep the status words short. One or two words fit a badge: "Active", "Trial", "Past due", "Canceled".
- Say what happens to access, not only the plan: "Ends on Nov 1, 2026" tells the owner when service stops.

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| Subscription tier | Plan |
| Cancel subscription | Cancel plan |
| Payment failed | Past due |
| 12 Seats | 12 seats |
| Click here | Download LS-2026-010 (the row's download button) |
| Card expires soon, please update | Expires soon · Apr 2029 (the default line) |

### Best practices

**Do**

- Set `Status` and `RenewsOn` from your billing provider on every change, because the footer, the badge and the detail
  line all read them. A stale status tells the owner the wrong thing about their access.
- Set `NextInvoiceAmount` when the next charge differs from the plan price, such as after seats are added or a discount
  applies, so the footer does not show a price the owner will not pay.
- Open a confirmation dialog or a `CancelFlow` from `CancelPlanRequested`, and update `Plan` only after the server
  confirms the change. The block cannot undo a change that the server rejected.
- Keep the newest invoices in `Invoices` and link to the full history. A long list in the overview makes the most recent
  invoice harder to find.

**Avoid**

- Hiding refunded or void invoices. The owner and the accounting team compare this list with their statements, and a
  missing row looks like a missing payment.
- Formatting amounts in your view model and passing text. The block formats money with `Labels.Culture` and the
  invoice's currency; a second format leads to two different values on the same page.
- Setting `Plan` to null for a canceled subscription. The owner then sees "Choose a plan" and loses the end date.
- Collecting card numbers in a field next to the card on file. Card data belongs in the payment provider's hosted form,
  which keeps it out of your application.

### Common questions

**Why does the card say "Choose a plan" and not "Cancel plan"?** The block shows "No plan" when `Plan` is null, and then
the only action is "Choose a plan", which raises `ChangePlanRequested`. A canceled plan keeps its object with
`Status="Canceled"`, so "Cancel plan" is hidden for it and the card shows its end date.

**Why does "Show all invoices" not appear?** The button appears only when `Invoices` has more items than
`VisibleInvoiceCount`. Set `VisibleInvoiceCount` to a smaller number, or add more invoices, to see it.

**Does the block cancel the subscription or download the file?** No. It raises `CancelPlanRequested` and
`InvoiceDownloadRequested`, and your code calls the billing API, shows a confirmation and saves the file.

**Why does the expiry line show "Expires soon" in one environment but not another?** The check uses `Clock`, which
defaults to the system clock. Set `Clock` to a fixed `TimeProvider` in tests, and make sure the card's expiry month is
set the same way in every environment.

**How do I show a different currency for one invoice?** Set `BillingInvoice.Currency` on that invoice; the others keep the
plan's `Currency`.

## API reference

### BillingOverview

A billing page in one view: the current plan with its status, price and next charge; the card on file and the billing email; and the invoice history with a download button per invoice. Every action raises a routed event for the host to handle (change or cancel the plan, update the card, edit the email, download an invoice). Older invoices beyond `VisibleInvoiceCount` fold behind "Show all invoices". Composed of `SettingsGroup`, `SettingsRow`, `Badge` and `Button`.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Plan` | `BillingPlan?` | `null` | The current subscription; null shows "No plan" with a "Choose a plan" button. |
| `PaymentMethod` | `BillingPaymentMethod?` | `null` | The card on file; null shows "No payment method" with an "Add card" button. |
| `BillingEmail` | `string?` | `null` | Where invoices are emailed, shown in the payment card. |
| `NextInvoiceAmount` | `decimal?` | `null` | The amount of the next charge; null uses the plan's `Price`. |
| `Invoices` | `IList<BillingInvoice>` | – | The invoice history, shown newest first. Defaults to an empty list you can add to; replace or bind it to show another collection. Changes to an observable collection and to the invoices themselves update the table. |
| `VisibleInvoiceCount` | `int` | `4` | How many invoices show before "Show all invoices"; the rest fold behind it. |
| `IsInvoiceListExpanded` | `bool` | `false` | Whether the invoices beyond `VisibleInvoiceCount` are shown ("Show all invoices" toggles it). |
| `NarrowWidth` | `double` | `560` | Below this width the price moves under the plan name, footers stack and the Invoice column hides. |
| `Labels` | `BillingOverviewLabels` | – | The built-in text; replace the object to reword or localize the block. |
| `IsNarrow` | `bool` | – | *Read-only.* Whether the block is narrower than `NarrowWidth`. |
| `IsPaymentMethodExpiringSoon` | `bool` | – | *Read-only.* Whether the card's expiry month starts within 60 days of `Clock`'s today (and has not ended yet). |
| `IsPaymentMethodExpired` | `bool` | – | *Read-only.* Whether the card's expiry month has passed. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ChangePlanRequested` | `RoutedEventArgs` | "Change plan" (or "Choose a plan" without a plan) was pressed. |
| `CancelPlanRequested` | `RoutedEventArgs` | "Cancel plan" was pressed. The block does not change the plan; the host confirms and updates `Plan`. |
| `UpdatePaymentMethodRequested` | `RoutedEventArgs` | "Update" (or "Add card" without a payment method) was pressed. |
| `EditBillingEmailRequested` | `RoutedEventArgs` | The billing email's "Edit" (or "Add") button was pressed. |
| `InvoiceDownloadRequested` | `BillingInvoiceEventArgs` | An invoice's download button was pressed; `Invoice` is the invoice. |

Pseudo-classes: `:narrow`, `:card-expiring`, `:card-expired`, `:invoices-expanded`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

`Clock` (`TimeProvider`, default `TimeProvider.System`) is a CLR property: the source of "today" for the expiry warning.

### BillingPlan

| Property | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Name` | `string` | The plan's name, such as "Studio". |
| `Price` | `decimal` | The total charged each interval, all seats included. |
| `Currency` | `string` | ISO 4217 code of the price (default "USD"). |
| `Interval` | `BillingInterval` | `Month` or `Year`: how often the price is charged. |
| `Seats` | `int?` | Number of paid seats, or null for plans not priced per seat. |
| `Status` | `BillingPlanStatus` | `Active`, `Trialing`, `PastDue` or `Canceled`. |
| `RenewsOn` | `DateTime?` | The next renewal; the end of the trial while trialing, the end of access once canceled. |

### BillingPaymentMethod

| Property | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Brand` | `string` | The card network as text, such as "Visa" or "Mastercard". |
| `Last4` | `string` | The last four digits of the card number. |
| `ExpiryMonth` | `int` | The expiry month, 1 to 12. |
| `ExpiryYear` | `int` | The four-digit expiry year. |

### BillingInvoice

| Property | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Number` | `string` | The invoice number, such as "LS-2026-010". |
| `Date` | `DateTime` | The date the invoice was issued; the table sorts by it, newest first. |
| `Amount` | `decimal` | The invoice total. |
| `Currency` | `string?` | ISO 4217 code of the amount; null uses the plan's currency. |
| `Status` | `BillingInvoiceStatus` | `Paid`, `Open`, `PastDue`, `Refunded` or `Void`. |
| `Description` | `string?` | What the invoice was for; added to the row's accessible name. |

### BillingInvoiceEventArgs

| Property | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Invoice` | `BillingInvoice` | The invoice whose download button was pressed. |

### Enumerations

| Type | Members |
|---|---|
| `BillingInterval` | `Month`, `Year` |
| `BillingPlanStatus` | `Active` (success badge), `Trialing` (accent badge), `PastDue` (danger badge), `Canceled` (neutral badge) |
| `BillingInvoiceStatus` | `Paid` (success badge), `Open`, `PastDue` (danger badge), `Refunded` and `Void` (muted neutral badges) |

## Accessibility

- Every button has a name. The download buttons are icon-only and are named "Download LS-2026-010", which is also their
  tooltip; "Update" is named "Update payment method" and "Edit" is named "Edit billing email".
- Each invoice row reads as one line, such as "Oct 1, 2026, LS-2026-010, $90.00, Paid". The column header is hidden from
  assistive technology.
- Status badges read their text. The expiry warning is text and a glyph as well as color.
- The "Show all invoices" button's name follows its text. Folded invoices leave the tab order, so Tab never lands on a
  hidden download button.
- The block takes no focus of its own; Tab moves through its buttons in reading order.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` | Move to the next or previous button in reading order |
| `Enter` / `Space` | Press the focused button, such as "Change plan" or a download button |

## Motion

- Older invoices unfold and fold with a height spring without bounce, and the chevron of "Show all invoices" turns on a
  snappy spring while its label swaps with a short blur.
- Badge and button labels that change in place swap with a blur, as in `Badge` and `Button`. The expiry line eases to the
  warning color.
- Reduced motion keeps the crossfades and makes the height and the chevron jump. Off places everything at once.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| Older invoices fold or unfold | Height opens on a smooth spring without bounce | Height jumps to the end state | Immediate |
| "Show all invoices" toggles | The chevron turns on a snappy spring; the label swaps with a blur | The chevron jumps; the label crossfades | Immediate |
| A badge or button label changes | The text swaps with a short blur | Crossfade | Immediate |
| Expiry line becomes a warning | The text eases to the warning color | The color crossfades | Immediate |

## Related

- The other Settings blocks: `SettingsPage`, `SettingsCommand`, `SecuritySettings`, `UsageBilling` and `CancelFlow` (a
  natural answer to `CancelPlanRequested`).
- `SettingsGroup` and `SettingsRow`, the cards and rows the block is built from.
- `Badge` for the plan and invoice status, `Button` for the actions.
- `BillingToggle` and `BillingPrice` for choosing a plan, and `Dialog` for confirming changes.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `UsageBilling` | The charge depends on metered usage this period, with a spending limit |
| `CancelFlow` | The cancellation needs steps, reasons or a retention offer |
| `Table` | The payment history is long and must be sorted, filtered or paged |
| `SettingsGroup` / `SettingsRow` | You build a settings card that is not a billing summary |
| `BillingToggle` / `BillingPrice` | The customer chooses between plans or billing periods |
| `Dialog` | A plan change, card update or download needs a confirmation or a form |

# Usage billing

> A metered billing period: spend so far, a projected total, daily spend, overage per meter and a spending limit.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc.Blocks`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc.Blocks --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/blocks/usage-billing

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.UsageBillingPeriodDemo">
    <arc:UsageBilling x:Name="Billing"
                      BaseFee="90"
                      SpendLimit="250"
                      IsSpendLimitEnabled="True">
        <arc:UsageBillingMeter Name="API calls"
                               Unit="calls"
                               Used="1240000"
                               Included="1000000"
                               UnitPrice="0.40"
                               PriceUnit="10000"
                               Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Activity}" />
        <arc:UsageBillingMeter Name="Storage"
                               Unit="GB"
                               Used="182"
                               Included="250"
                               UnitPrice="0.10"
                               Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Database}" />
        <arc:UsageBillingMeter Name="Build minutes"
                               Unit="min"
```

```cs
using System;
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class UsageBillingPeriodDemo : UserControl
{
    public UsageBillingPeriodDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        // The October period of Larkspur Studio, seen on Oct 20: twenty days of spend so far.
        Billing.Clock = new FixedClock(new DateTimeOffset(2026, 10, 20, 12, 0, 0, TimeSpan.Zero));
        Billing.PeriodStart = new DateTime(2026, 10, 1);
        Billing.PeriodEnd = new DateTime(2026, 10, 31);
        Billing.DailySpend =
        [
            4.97, 4.82, 2.79, 2.41, 5.74, 5.58, 5.18, 6.04, 5.35, 3.02,
            2.76, 5.75, 6.47, 7.34, 6.12, 6.41, 3.60, 3.97, 7.45, 7.19
        ];
    }

    /// <summary>A clock stopped at one moment, so the projection and the days left stay the same.</summary>
    private sealed class FixedClock(DateTimeOffset now) : TimeProvider
    {
        public override DateTimeOffset GetUtcNow() => now;

        public override TimeZoneInfo LocalTimeZone => TimeZoneInfo.Utc;
    }
}
```

## When to use

Usage billing is the billing page of a plan that charges for consumption on top of a base fee. It answers the two
questions people ask before an invoice arrives: what has this period cost so far, and where is it heading? It sits
on an account or billing page, above the invoice history, and it is the place where an owner sets a spending cap.

- **Usage-based API plans**: a developer platform that charges $0.40 per 10,000 calls above an included million. The
  overage of each meter shows as it accrues, so an owner sees a surprise coming before the invoice.
- **Storage and build minutes**: a cloud product that bills storage in GB and CI minutes beyond the plan's allowance.
  Each meter keeps its own unit, so "3,420 min" and "182 GB" read correctly side by side.
- **Spending caps for a team**: an owner limits the period to $250. The summary turns to "Near limit" at 80% and to
  "Limit reached" at the limit, and the amount can be edited where it is shown.
- **Daily spend review**: a finance page that draws the amount spent each day, so a spike on one day is visible
  against the average.
- **Live usage**: an account page where usage events arrive while it is open. The totals, the projection and the bars
  follow each change without a reload.

## When not to use

- **Plans without metered usage**: use `BillingOverview` for the plan, the payment method and the invoices.
- **A quota without prices**, such as storage used against a plan's space or seats left: use `UsageMeter` or
  `Progress`, which show a share of a limit and do not price the overage.
- **Usage across many periods**: use `BarChart` or `LineChart` on their own for a trend. This block shows one period.
- **A list of past invoices**: use `Table`, which sorts and filters rows, and keep this block for the
  period in progress.

## Usage

Set the period, the base fee and the meters. Each `UsageBillingMeter` says how much was used, how much the plan
includes and what the rest costs: `UnitPrice` pays for `PriceUnit` units, so `$0.40` per 10,000 calls is
`UnitPrice="0.40" PriceUnit="10000"`. The block adds the meters' costs into `MeteredTotal`, adds `BaseFee` for
`CurrentTotal` and projects `ProjectedTotal` from the share of the period that has begun. Meters written inline land in
`Meters`, the content property.

```xml
<arc:UsageBilling PeriodStart="2026-10-01"
                  PeriodEnd="2026-10-31"
                  BaseFee="90"
                  SpendLimit="250"
                  IsSpendLimitEnabled="True">
    <arc:UsageBillingMeter Name="API calls"
                           Unit="calls"
                           Used="1240000"
                           Included="1000000"
                           UnitPrice="0.40"
                           PriceUnit="10000"
                           Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Activity}" />
    <arc:UsageBillingMeter Name="Storage" Unit="GB" Used="182" Included="250" UnitPrice="0.10" />
</arc:UsageBilling>
```

`UsageBilling` derives from `TemplatedControl`. Its cards are the shared parts of the Settings block: a `SettingsGroup`
for each card and a `SettingsRow` for the limit switch and each meter row. That keeps it in line with the settings
pages around it, and the same theme and motion apply.

`DailySpend` lists the amount spent on each day, starting with the first day of the period. Days after today are not
drawn, and without values the daily spend card is hidden. Pass a list that raises collection changes, such as an
`AvaloniaList<double>`, and the chart follows it.

```csharp
billing.DailySpend = new AvaloniaList<double> { 4.97, 4.82, 2.79, 2.41, 5.74 };
```

### Anatomy

1. **Summary card**: the title from `Labels.PeriodTitle`, the period's dates and the days left
   in the card's description, and the status badge in the header actions when the limit is near or reached.
2. **Spent so far**: the amount spent, in the largest type size of the card, with the label
   `SpentSoFar` above it. It rolls to each new total.
3. **Projection**: `Projected` in the small type size, under the amount, in the secondary text color.
4. **Limit column**: the label
   `SpendingLimit`, the share of the limit in medium weight, a 16 px bar with an 8 px track and a tick at
   `AlertThreshold`, and the caption `LimitProgress`. With no limit it shows `NoLimit` and a "Set a limit" button.
5. **Daily spend card**: a `BarChart` with a 160 px plot, hidden when `DailySpend` is null or empty.
6. **Usage card**: one row per meter with its icon tile, name, usage line (`MeterUsage`) and a
   charge on the right: the overage amount with its rate, or "Included". Under each row sits a 6 px bar, filled to the
   included part in the accent color and to the overage in the warning color. The footer shows `UsageTotal` and
   the metered total.
7. **Spending limit card**: a `SettingsRow` with the switch and its description, then a 320 px
   wide `MoneyInput` (Small) indented 50 px to line up with the row text. The note from `LimitNote` sits under it.

In the summary, the spend and the limit sit side by side with a 40 px gap. Below `NarrowWidth` (600 px by default),
the limit column moves under the spend and starts 24 px lower.

### Near and over the limit

The limit progress compares `CurrentTotal` with `SpendLimit`. It turns to the warning color once the spend passes
`AlertThreshold` (80% by default, where the tick sits) and to the danger color once it reaches the limit. A badge beside
the title says "Near limit" or "Limit reached", and `LimitStatus` reports the same state. Use the status for your own
logic, such as showing an alert in the navigation. This example has no `DailySpend`, so the daily spend card is hidden.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.UsageBillingNearLimitDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="20">
        <arc:SegmentedControl x:Name="Scenario"
                              HorizontalAlignment="Center"
                              SelectedValue="near"
                              SelectionChanged="OnScenarioChanged">
            <arc:SegmentedOption Value="near" Label="Near the limit" />
            <arc:SegmentedOption Value="over" Label="Over the limit" />
        </arc:SegmentedControl>
        <!-- No DailySpend: the daily spend card stays hidden. -->
        <arc:UsageBilling x:Name="Billing"
                          BaseFee="90"
                          SpendLimit="120"
                          IsSpendLimitEnabled="True">
            <arc:UsageBillingMeter Name="API calls"
                                   Unit="calls"
                                   Used="1240000"
                                   Included="1000000"
                                   UnitPrice="0.40"
                                   PriceUnit="10000"
                                   Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Activity}" />
            <arc:UsageBillingMeter Name="Storage"
                                   Unit="GB"
                                   Used="182"
                                   Included="250"
                                   UnitPrice="0.10"
                                   Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Database}" />
            <arc:UsageBillingMeter Name="Build minutes"
                                   Unit="min"
                                   Used="3420"
                                   Included="3000"
                                   UnitPrice="0.008"
                                   Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Timer}" />
        </arc:UsageBilling>

</UserControl>
```

```cs
using System;
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class UsageBillingNearLimitDemo : UserControl
{
    public UsageBillingNearLimitDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Billing.Clock = new FixedClock(new DateTimeOffset(2026, 10, 20, 12, 0, 0, TimeSpan.Zero));
        Billing.PeriodStart = new DateTime(2026, 10, 1);
        Billing.PeriodEnd = new DateTime(2026, 10, 31);
    }

    // $102.96 spent: 86% of a $120 limit is past the 80% alert; a $100 limit has been passed.
    private void OnScenarioChanged(object? sender, SelectionChangedEventArgs e)
    {
        if (Billing is not null)
        {
            Billing.SpendLimit = Scenario.SelectedValue as string == "over" ? 100 : 120;
        }
    }

        public override TimeZoneInfo LocalTimeZone => TimeZoneInfo.Utc;
    }
}
```
