### Live usage

A meter announces its changes, so the block updates as usage comes in: the amount spent rolls to the new total, and the
projection, the meter's bar, its charge and the limit progress follow. Here each click adds 50,000 API calls, which cost
$2.00 past the included million, and adds the same amount to today's bar.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.UsageBillingLiveDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="20">
        <StackPanel Orientation="Horizontal" Spacing="8" HorizontalAlignment="Center">
            <arc:Button Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Click="OnAddUsage">
                <StackPanel Orientation="Horizontal" Spacing="6">
                    <arc:ArcGlyph Data="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Plus}" Size="14" VerticalAlignment="Center" />
                    <TextBlock Text="Add usage" VerticalAlignment="Center" />
                </StackPanel>
            </arc:Button>
            <arc:Button Content="Reset" Variant="Ghost" Size="Small" Click="OnReset" />
        </StackPanel>
        <arc:UsageBilling x:Name="Billing"
                          BaseFee="90"
                          SpendLimit="130"
                          IsSpendLimitEnabled="True">
            <arc:UsageBillingMeter Name="API calls"
                                   Unit="calls"
                                   Used="1240000"
                                   Included="1000000"
                                   UnitPrice="0.40"
                                   PriceUnit="10000"
                                   Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Activity}" />
            <arc:UsageBillingMeter Name="Storage"
                                   Unit="GB"
                                   Used="182"
                                   Included="250"
                                   UnitPrice="0.10"
                                   Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Database}" />
            <arc:UsageBillingMeter Name="Build minutes"
                                   Unit="min"
                                   Used="3420"
                                   Included="3000"
                                   UnitPrice="0.008"
                                   Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Timer}" />
        </arc:UsageBilling>
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using System;
using System.Linq;
using Avalonia.Collections;
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class UsageBillingLiveDemo : UserControl
{
    private static readonly double[] s_days =
    [
        4.97, 4.82, 2.79, 2.41, 5.74, 5.58, 5.18, 6.04, 5.35, 3.02,
        2.76, 5.75, 6.47, 7.34, 6.12, 6.41, 3.60, 3.97, 7.45, 7.19
    ];

    // An observable list: changing today's amount redraws its bar.
    private readonly AvaloniaList<double> _days = new(s_days);

    public UsageBillingLiveDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Billing.Clock = new FixedClock(new DateTimeOffset(2026, 10, 20, 12, 0, 0, TimeSpan.Zero));
        Billing.PeriodStart = new DateTime(2026, 10, 1);
        Billing.PeriodEnd = new DateTime(2026, 10, 31);
        Billing.DailySpend = _days;
    }

    private UsageBillingMeter ApiCalls => Billing.Meters.First(m => m.Name == "API calls");

    // 50K more calls past the included million cost 5 × $0.40 = $2.00. The meter notifies the block, which updates
    // the spend, the projection, the bar and the limit; today's bar takes the same $2.00.
    private void OnAddUsage(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        ApiCalls.Used += 50_000;
        _days[^1] = Math.Round(_days[^1] + 2.00, 2);
    }

    private void OnReset(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        ApiCalls.Used = 1_240_000;
        _days[^1] = s_days[^1];
    }

    /// <summary>A clock stopped at one moment, so the projection and the days left stay the same.</summary>
    private sealed class FixedClock(DateTimeOffset now) : TimeProvider
    {
        public override DateTimeOffset GetUtcNow() => now;

        public override TimeZoneInfo LocalTimeZone => TimeZoneInfo.Utc;
    }
}
```

### Data shape and performance

Keep the usage counts as `double` and the money as `decimal`: `Used` and `Included` count units, while `BaseFee`,
`UnitPrice` and `SpendLimit` are amounts. The block does its arithmetic in `decimal`, so the totals are exact to the cent.
A unit price keeps as many decimals as it needs, up to four, so `$0.008` per minute shows as written.

Each meter is an `INotifyPropertyChanged` model. Changing `Used` raises the computed `Overage` and `Cost` and updates the
totals, that meter's charge and its bar; the other rows keep their values. Adding or removing a meter from `Meters` builds
or removes only that row and then recalculates the totals. Update the meters from your usage feed at a rate a person can read;
a value that changes many times a second cannot be followed.

The chart takes the days from the first of the period through today, so a period that has just started draws a few
bars.

### Spending limit

`IsSpendLimitEnabled` and `SpendLimit` are two-way: the switch and the amount field in the last card edit them.
`SpendLimitChanged` reports each change with the old and new amount and whether the limit is on. While someone types
in the field, the change is reported once, when the field loses focus or Enter is pressed. Without a limit, the summary
offers "Set a limit", which turns the limit on and moves focus to the amount.

Turning the limit off keeps the amount. The editor collapses, and the amount stays in `SpendLimit` for the next time the
switch is turned on, so a person does not retype a cap they set last month.

```csharp
billing.SpendLimitChanged += async (_, e) =>
{
    await api.SaveSpendingLimitAsync(e.IsEnabled ? e.NewLimit : null);
};
```

### Binding to a view model

The block is a display and editing surface for a period. The view model owns the period's values, the meters and the
save, and the block binds to them. `Meters` and `DailySpend` are settable, so a view model can supply them directly.

```csharp
public partial class UsageBillingViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    private readonly IBillingApi _api;

    public UsageBillingViewModel(IBillingApi api) => _api = api;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private string _currency = "USD";

    [ObservableProperty]
    private decimal _baseFee = 90m;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private decimal? _spendLimit = 250m;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private bool _isSpendLimitEnabled = true;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private IList<double>? _dailySpend;

    public ObservableCollection<UsageBillingMeter> Meters { get; } = new();

    public async Task SaveSpendingLimitAsync(decimal? limit) => await _api.SaveSpendingLimitAsync(limit);
}
```

```xml
<arc:UsageBilling Currency="{Binding Currency}"
                  BaseFee="{Binding BaseFee}"
                  Meters="{Binding Meters}"
                  DailySpend="{Binding DailySpend}"
                  SpendLimit="{Binding SpendLimit, Mode=TwoWay}"
                  IsSpendLimitEnabled="{Binding IsSpendLimitEnabled, Mode=TwoWay}" />
```

- `SpendLimit` and `IsSpendLimitEnabled` are the two-way properties. Bind them so the view model always holds the
  value the person sees.
- Save from `SpendLimitChanged`, not from the binding alone. The event reports the old and new amount and whether the
  limit is on, and it reports a typed amount once, when the field lets go.
- `BaseFee`, `Currency`, `PeriodStart` and `PeriodEnd` are one-way inputs. The block recalculates when they change.
- `Clock` is not a styled property, so set it in code, not in the binding. See "Today and the projection".

### Today and the projection

"Today" comes from `Clock`, a `TimeProvider` (the system clock by default). It sets the days left, the days drawn and
the projection: `BaseFee + MeteredTotal × days in the period ÷ days begun`. On Oct 20 of a 31-day period the
$12.96 of usage so far projects to $20.09, for $110.09 with the base fee. The projection assumes usage keeps its pace,
and the share of days is kept between one day's share and 1. Tests and previews pass a fixed clock.

```csharp
sealed class FixedClock(DateTimeOffset now) : TimeProvider
{
    public override DateTimeOffset GetUtcNow() => now;
}

billing.Clock = new FixedClock(new DateTimeOffset(2026, 10, 20, 12, 0, 0, TimeSpan.Zero));
```

### Currency and text

`Currency` is an ISO 4217 code. Amounts show `$`, `€`, `£` or `¥` before the number, and other codes after it, such as
`12.96 CHF`. All built-in text is in `Labels`; replace the object to translate it. `Labels.Culture` formats the dates,
amounts and counts.

```csharp
billing.Currency = "EUR";
billing.Labels = new UsageBillingLabels
{
    Culture = CultureInfo.GetCultureInfo("nl-NL"),
    PeriodTitle = "Deze factuurperiode",
    SpentSoFar = "Tot nu toe besteed",
    Projected = amount => $"Verwacht {amount}",
};
```

### Example: October usage for a developer platform

The billing page of a developer platform in the middle of its October period. The $90 base fee is fixed. API calls are
past the included million, so they cost money; storage is inside its allowance, so it costs nothing; build minutes are
a little past theirs. The owners cap the bill at $250, and the limit stays open because it is on. Every amount, bar and
the projection come from the three meters, so the figures agree with each other.

![October usage for a developer platform: spend, projection, meters and the spending limit](https://docs.tkcode.si/shots/Docs/Blocks/UsageBilling/images/OctoberUsage.webp)

```xml
<arc:UsageBilling Width="640"
                  PeriodStart="2026-10-01"
                  PeriodEnd="2026-10-31"
                  BaseFee="90"
                  SpendLimit="250"
                  IsSpendLimitEnabled="True">
    <arc:UsageBillingMeter Name="API calls"
                           Unit="calls"
                           Used="1240000"
                           Included="1000000"
                           UnitPrice="0.40"
                           PriceUnit="10000"
                           Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Activity}" />

                           Unit="GB"
```

### Content guidelines

- **Meter name**: a noun in sentence case that names what is measured, such as "API calls", "Storage" or "Build
  minutes". The unit comes from `Unit` and follows the plan's own term: "calls", "GB", "min".
- **Period title**: keep "This billing period" and let the description carry the dates. A month name in the title
  goes stale when the period changes.
- **Limit copy**: "Spending limit" names the setting, and the description states the effect ("Cap the total bill for
  one billing period."). Say what happens at each threshold in `LimitNote`, with the same percentages as
  `AlertThreshold`.
- **Amounts and counts**: let the block format them through `Culture` and `Currency`. Do not pre-format amounts as
  text, because a text value cannot follow a culture change.

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| Bill total | Spent so far |
| Limit | Spending limit |
| Click here to set a limit | Set a limit |
| 240000 over | 240K over (the block formats it) |
| Estimated bill | Projected $110.09 |

### Best practices

**Do**

- Set `Clock` in previews and tests. The days left, the drawn days and the projection all depend on today, so a fixed
  clock keeps screenshots and tests stable.
- Turn the limit off with `IsSpendLimitEnabled` rather than clearing the amount. The amount stays for the next time the
  switch is turned on.
- Keep `Currency` and `Labels.Culture` together. The currency sets the symbol and the culture sets the separators, so
  set both for one locale.
- Use `LimitStatus` for alerts elsewhere in the app. It is the same state the badge shows, so an alert and the card
  never disagree.

**Avoid**

- Presenting the projection as a bill. It assumes usage keeps its pace, so label it "Projected", as the default does.
- Enforcing the limit in the UI alone. The block shows the state and raises `SpendLimitChanged`; it does not stop usage.
  Your service must enforce the cap and read the same amount.
- Mixing periods in one block. It shows one period from `PeriodStart` to `PeriodEnd`; a second period needs its own
  block or a trend chart.
- Rounding the usage counts before they reach the meter. The overage and the charge come from the exact counts, and
  rounding can move a count across the included amount.

### Common questions

**Why does the projection differ from my own estimate?** The projection is `BaseFee` plus the metered total scaled by
the share of the period's days that have begun by `Clock`. On Oct 20 of a 31-day period, $12.96 of usage projects to
$20.09 of usage, or $110.09 with the base fee. Check `Clock` first.

**Why is the daily spend card missing?** A null or empty `DailySpend` hides the card. The card also draws only the days
through today, so a period that has just started shows a short chart.

**Which amount does the limit compare against?** `CurrentTotal`, which is the base fee plus the metered total, not the
usage alone. A $250 limit on a $90 base fee leaves $160 of usage before it is reached.

**Does the block stop usage at the limit?** No. The block displays `LimitStatus` and raises `SpendLimitChanged`. Your
billing service enforces the cap, and the note under the field describes the behavior you implement.

## API reference

### UsageBilling

A metered billing period on one page: what has been spent so far and the projected total, the spend per day, each meter's usage against what the plan includes (with the overage priced), and a spending limit that can be turned on and set in place. The totals follow the meters: change `Used` and the amounts, bars and projection update. "Today" comes from `Clock`.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `PeriodStart` | `DateTime` | `01/01/0001 00:00:00` | The first day of the billing period; by default the first day of the `Clock`'s month. |
| `PeriodEnd` | `DateTime` | `01/01/0001 00:00:00` | The last day of the billing period (inclusive); by default the last day of the start's month. |
| `Currency` | `string` | `"USD"` | ISO 4217 code of every amount ("USD" by default). |
| `BaseFee` | `decimal` | `0` | The fixed charge of the period (the plan price), added to the metered charges. |
| `Meters` | `IList<UsageBillingMeter>` | – | The meters of the period, in display order. Meters written inline in XAML land here. |
| `DailySpend` | `IList<double>?` | `null` | The amount spent on each day of the period, starting with the first day. Days after today are not drawn; a null or empty list hides the daily spend card. A list that raises collection changes redraws as it changes. |
| `SpendLimit` | `decimal?` | `null` | The spending limit for the period, in `Currency`. Two-way: the limit field edits it. |
| `IsSpendLimitEnabled` | `bool` | `false` | Whether the spending limit applies. Two-way: the limit switch edits it. |
| `AlertThreshold` | `double` | `0.8` | The share of the limit (0–1, default 0.8) at which the progress turns to the warning color and the tick sits. |
| `Labels` | `UsageBillingLabels` | – | The built-in text and its culture; replace the object to localize the block. |
| `MeteredTotal` | `decimal` | – | *Read-only.* The sum of every meter's `Cost`. |
| `CurrentTotal` | `decimal` | – | *Read-only.* What the period has cost so far: `BaseFee` + `MeteredTotal`. |
| `ProjectedTotal` | `decimal` | – | *Read-only.* The period's expected total if usage keeps its pace: `BaseFee` + `MeteredTotal` ÷ the share of the period's days that have begun by `Clock`'s today (kept between one day's share and 1). |
| `LimitStatus` | `UsageBillingLimitStatus` | – | *Read-only.* Where `CurrentTotal` stands against the spending limit and its alert threshold. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `SpendLimitChanged` | `UsageBillingLimitChangedEventArgs` | Raised when the spending limit changes or is turned on or off. While someone types in the limit field the change is reported once, when the field loses focus or Enter is pressed. |

Pseudo-classes: `:narrow`, `:no-limit`, `:limit-near`, `:limit-reached`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

### UsageBillingMeter

A plain model (`INotifyPropertyChanged`) that can be written in XAML. Changing any value raises `PropertyChanged`, and the
block recalculates.

| Property | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Name` | `string` | What is measured, such as "API calls"; the row's header. |
| `Unit` | `string` | The unit after the amounts, such as "calls", "GB" or "min". |
| `Used` | `double` | The amount used so far this period. |
| `Included` | `double` | The amount the plan includes at no extra cost. With 0 the row shows the usage without a bar. |
| `UnitPrice` | `decimal` | The price of `PriceUnit` units beyond the included amount. |
| `PriceUnit` | `double` | How many units `UnitPrice` pays for (default 1). |
| `Icon` | `Geometry?` | A 24×24 stroke icon shown in the row's tile. |
| `Overage` | `double` | *Read-only.* `max(0, Used − Included)`. |
| `Cost` | `decimal` | *Read-only.* `Overage ÷ PriceUnit × UnitPrice`. |

### UsageBillingLimitChangedEventArgs

| Property | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `OldLimit` | `decimal?` | The limit amount before the change. |
| `NewLimit` | `decimal?` | The limit amount after the change. |
| `IsEnabled` | `bool` | Whether the limit is on after the change. |

### UsageBillingLimitStatus

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `None` | No limit applies: it is off or has no positive amount. |
| `Ok` | The spend is below the alert threshold. |
| `Near` | The spend has passed the alert threshold but not the limit. |
| `Reached` | The spend has reached or passed the limit. |

### UsageBillingLabels

Every entry has an English default. Entries with parameters receive formatted text.

| Property | Default |
|---|---|
| `Culture` | en-US |
| `PeriodTitle` | "This billing period" |
| `DaysLeft` | days ⇒ "11 days left", "1 day left", "Last day" |
| `PeriodEnded` | "Period ended" |
| `SpentSoFar` | "Spent so far" |
| `Projected` | amount ⇒ "Projected $110.09" |
| `SpendingLimit` | "Spending limit" |
| `LimitProgress` | (current, limit) ⇒ "$102.96 of $250.00 limit" |
| `NoLimit` | "No spending limit" |
| `SetLimit` | "Set a limit" |
| `NearLimit` / `LimitReached` | "Near limit" / "Limit reached" |
| `DailySpend` | "Daily spend" (the chart's accessible name) |
| `DailyAverage` / `DaySpend` | "Average daily spend" / "Spent" (the chart headline at rest and while a day is read) |
| `Day` | "Date" (the chart's data table) |
| `Usage` | "Usage" |
| `MeterUsage` | (used, included, unit) ⇒ "1.2M of 1M calls included" |
| `MeterUsageOnly` | (used, unit) ⇒ "3.4K min" (a meter without an included amount) |
| `Overage` | amount ⇒ "240K over" (in a meter bar's accessible name) |
| `Included` | "Included" |
| `Rate` | (price, per) ⇒ "$0.40 / 10K calls" |
| `UsageTotal` | "Usage charges so far" |
| `SpendingLimitDescription` | "Cap the total bill for one billing period." |
| `LimitAmount` | "Limit amount" |
| `LimitNote` | percent ⇒ "We email the owners at 80% and pause usage-based features at 100%." |


## Accessibility

- Each card is a `SettingsGroup`. The amount spent reads with its label, such as "Spent so far: $102.96".
- The limit progress is a progress bar named like "Spending limit: $102.96 of $250.00 limit". The "Near limit" and
  "Limit reached" badge is a polite live region, so the change is announced.
- Each meter bar is a progress bar named with the meter, its usage and the overage, such as "API calls: 1.2M of 1M
  calls included, 240K over". The charge reads with its rate, such as "$9.60, $0.40 / 10K calls".
- The switch takes the setting's header as its name and the description as its help text. The amount field is labeled
  "Limit amount" and described by the note under it.
- The block takes no focus of its own; its controls do. Tab order follows the cards from top to bottom.
- While the limit is off, the editor is collapsed. Its field stays in the tree, so the block removes it from the tab
  order until the limit is on.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` | Move through the limit switch, the amount field (only while the limit is on), the "Set a limit" button and the daily spend chart, in card order |
| `Enter` in the amount field | Ends the edit and reports the new limit |
| `Enter` on "Set a limit" | Turns the limit on and moves focus to the amount field |
| Arrow keys on the chart | Move between days; Home and End go to the first and last day |
| `Page Up` / `Page Down` on the chart | Move a week |
| `Escape` on the chart | Returns the headline to the average |

The chart takes focus. Its accessible summary names the highest and lowest day, so a person hears the range before
they move through the days.

## Motion

- The amount spent rolls digit by digit to a new total.
- Meter bars and the limit progress spring to their new lengths, and the limit's color crossfades when it passes the alert threshold or the limit.
- The status badge pops in and out beside the title.
- The limit editor opens and closes in height on a spring when the switch changes.
- The chart's bars grow in a wave the first time the chart is seen and morph when the values change.
- Reduced motion keeps only the color fades: bars and the editor take their new size at once. Off changes everything at once.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| The amount spent changes | Digits roll to the new total | Changes at once | Immediate |
| A meter bar or the limit progress changes length | Springs to the new length | Takes the new length at once | Immediate |
| The limit crosses the alert threshold or the limit | Color crossfades (standard) | Color crossfades (fast) | Immediate |
| The limit editor opens or closes | Height springs | Takes its new height at once | Immediate |
| The daily spend chart appears or changes | Bars grow in a wave, then morph | Changes at once | Immediate |

## Related

- The other Settings blocks: `SettingsPage`, `SettingsCommand`, `SecuritySettings`, `BillingOverview` and `CancelFlow`.
- `SettingsGroup` and `SettingsRow`, the shared parts every card here is built from (described on the `SettingsPage` page).
- `BarChart` for the daily spend, `AnimatedCounter` for the amount spent, `MoneyInput` and `Switch` for the limit, and `Badge` for its status.
- `UsageMeter` and `Progress` for quotas without prices.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `BillingOverview` | The page shows the plan, the payment method and the invoices, with or without usage |
| `UsageMeter` / `Progress` | A quota has a limit but no price, such as seats or storage space |
| `BarChart` / `LineChart` | The trend over several periods matters more than one period's total |
| `MoneyInput` | A single amount is entered on its own, outside the spending limit card |
| `Table` | Past invoices or usage lines need sorting and filtering |
| `CancelFlow` | An owner wants to end the plan, with its reasons and offer step |

# Cancel flow

> A considerate cancellation: ask why, offer a fitting alternative, show what ends, hold to confirm, and allow a quick return.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc.Blocks`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc.Blocks --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/blocks/cancel-flow

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.CancelFlowFlowDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12" MaxWidth="520">
        <arc:Button HorizontalAlignment="Right"
                    Variant="Ghost"
                    Size="Small"
                    Click="OnResetClick">
            <StackPanel Orientation="Horizontal" Spacing="6">
                <arc:ArcGlyph Data="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.RotateCcw}" Size="14" VerticalAlignment="Center" />
                <TextBlock Text="Reset" VerticalAlignment="Center" />
            </StackPanel>
        </arc:Button>
        <arc:CancelFlow x:Name="Flow"
                        PlanName="Studio"
                        KeepPlanRequested="OnKeepPlanRequested">
            <arc:CancelFlow.Reasons>
                <arc:CancelFlowReason Title="Too expensive"
                                      Description="The price is more than it's worth to us right now.">
                    <arc:CancelFlowReason.Offer>
                        <arc:CancelFlowOffer Title="Take 40% off for 3 months"
                                             Description="Keep everything your team uses today for $54 a month instead of $90. The discount applies to your next three invoices."
                                             AcceptLabel="Claim 40% off"
                                             Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Percent}"
                                             AcceptedTitle="40% off is on"
                                             AcceptedDescription="Your next three invoices are $54 instead of $90. Thanks for staying with us." />
                    </arc:CancelFlowReason.Offer>
                </arc:CancelFlowReason>
                <arc:CancelFlowReason Title="Not using it enough"
                                      Description="We don't open it often enough to keep paying for it.">
                    <arc:CancelFlowReason.Offer>
                        <arc:CancelFlowOffer Title="Pause instead"
                                             Description="Stop billing for up to two months. Projects, members and settings stay exactly as they are, ready when you come back."
                                             AcceptLabel="Pause for 2 months"
                                             Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.Pause}"
                                             AcceptedTitle="Your plan is paused"
                                             AcceptedDescription="Billing pauses until Jan 1, 2027, and your projects stay just as they are." />
                    </arc:CancelFlowReason.Offer>
                </arc:CancelFlowReason>
                <arc:CancelFlowReason Title="Missing a feature I need"
                                      Description="Something we rely on isn't there yet."
                                      AsksForDetails="True"
                                      DetailsPrompt="What were you missing?" />
                <arc:CancelFlowReason Title="Switching to another tool"
                                      Description="We're moving our work to a different product."
                                      AsksForDetails="True"
                                      DetailsPrompt="Which tool are you moving to?" />
                <arc:CancelFlowReason Title="Something else"
                                      Description="Our reason isn't listed here."
                                      AsksForDetails="True"
                                      DetailsPrompt="What made you decide to cancel?" />
            </arc:CancelFlow.Reasons>
            <arc:CancelFlow.DefaultOffer>
                <arc:CancelFlowOffer Title="Talk to us first"
                                     Description="Fifteen minutes with our team is often enough to fix what isn't working. If it isn't, canceling stays one step away."
                                     AcceptLabel="Book a 15-minute call"
                                     Icon="{x:Static arc:ArcIcons.MessageCircle}"
                                     AcceptedTitle="We'll be in touch"
                                     AcceptedDescription="Someone from our team will email noor@larkspur.co within a day to find a time. Your plan stays as it is." />
            </arc:CancelFlow.DefaultOffer>
            <arc:CancelFlow.Losses>
                <x:String>Shared projects become read-only for all 6 members</x:String>
                <x:String>Version history older than 30 days is deleted</x:String>
                <x:String>Custom domains and single sign-on stop working</x:String>
            </arc:CancelFlow.Losses>
        </arc:CancelFlow>
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class CancelFlowFlowDemo : UserControl
{
    public CancelFlowFlowDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        // Access runs to the end of the paid month: the renewal date of the Studio plan.
        Flow.AccessEndsOn = new DateTime(2026, 11, 1);
    }

    private void OnResetClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) => Flow.Reset();

    // On a real page this closes the flow and returns to billing; here it confirms and starts over.
    private void OnKeepPlanRequested(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        Toast.Show(this, "Your Studio plan stays active", ToastKind.Success);
        Flow.Reset();
    }
}
```

## When to use

`CancelFlow` is the card that opens when a person presses "Cancel plan". It sits on a billing or plan page, or in a
dialog launched from one, and turns a cancellation into four short steps: the reason, an offer that fits that reason,
what ends and when, and a confirmation the person must hold. The host decides what each step does; the flow only
collects the answers and reports them.

- **The cancel action on a team plan page**: an admin presses "Cancel plan" on the Team plan and the flow asks why,
  so the team can learn whether price, usage or a missing feature drove the decision.
- **Subscriptions where an offer often fits better than leaving**: a discount for a price complaint or a pause for
  low usage. The offer appears only after the reason that it answers, so it does not distract people who have already
  decided.
- **Irreversible plan changes that need a clear summary**: the confirmation lists what stops working (read-only
  projects, deleted history, lost custom domains) and the date when access ends, before the person can confirm.
- **Account settings that must offer a way back**: after a confirmed cancellation the canceled step offers
  "Reactivate plan", so the change is easy to undo without contacting support.
- **Flows that must be recorded**: the events carry the chosen reason and the free-text feedback, so the answers can
  go to your analytics or your support queue.

## When not to use

- **Removing one item or one seat in place**: use `ConfirmMorph` or `HoldToConfirm` next to the item. A full flow is
  too heavy for a small change that the person can reverse.
- **Moving to another paid plan**: show the options side by side with `RadioCards` or a pricing table. The flow is for
  leaving, and a downgrade should not be framed as a cancellation.
- **Cases where the law or your terms require one-click cancellation**: keep the offer out of the way by leaving
  `DefaultOffer` null and not giving reasons an `Offer`, or link straight to the confirmation your terms describe.
- **A lighter confirmation of a small destructive action**: use `ConfirmMorph`, which asks once in place and needs no
  reasons or offers.
- **Collecting a long free-form survey**: use `Textarea` inside your own form. The flow asks one optional question
  after the reason and does not paginate a survey.

## Usage

```csharp
flow.AccessEndsOn = new DateTime(2026, 11, 1);

flow.CancellationConfirmed += (_, e) => billing.Cancel(e.Reason.Title, e.Feedback);
flow.OfferAccepted += (_, e) => billing.Apply(e.Offer.Title);
flow.KeepPlanRequested += (_, _) => page.CloseCancelFlow();
```

`CancelFlow` derives from Avalonia's `TemplatedControl`. It is one card that holds the step bar, the step content and the
buttons, and it swaps the content between steps. Each step's controls are built once and reused. The flow is built from
`RadioGroup`, `Textarea`, `HoldToConfirm` and `Button`, so it inherits their focus rules and keyboard behavior. The preview gives two reasons their own offer ("Take 40% off for 3 months" and "Pause instead"), and the
other reasons fall back to the default offer. `PlanName` and `AccessEndsOn` fill in the sentences.

### Anatomy

The card has 28 px of inner padding (20 by 22 px below 440 px wide, `NarrowWidth`) and a preferred width of 520 px. From top to bottom:

1. **Step bar** (`StepStorePart`): three segments for the path Reason, Offer and Confirm, or two segments when the
   path has no offer. The segments are 4 px high with a 6 px gap. The current segment uses the accent color, finished
   segments use the foreground color at 30 percent, and the rest use the subtle border color. The step counter
   "Step {n} of {total}" sits to the right of the back button.
2. **Back button** (`BackButtonPart`): a 32 px round button named "Back". It appears on the offer and confirmation steps.
   Alt+Left does the same.
3. **Step title and description**: 28 px title line
   height, with the description 6 px below it. The title takes focus after each step change, but it is not a tab stop.
4. **Reason list**: a `RadioGroup` in which each row has a title and an optional description. Below it, the feedback
   `Textarea` opens with a height spring after a reason is chosen. It is optional and out of the tab
   order while it is collapsed.
5. **Offer tile**: a 52 px rounded tile (16 px radius) with a 24 px icon, the offer title and its description. The
   accept button and "Continue canceling" follow.
6. **Losses box**: a panel with 16 by 14 px padding and a 16 px radius, listing each loss with a
   10 px gap between lines. It is hidden when `Losses` is empty.
7. **Hold button**: a `HoldToConfirm` in the danger color labeled "Hold to cancel plan", with "Keep my
   plan" next to it.
8. **Result mark**: a 56 px mark with a 28 px check glyph, the result title and its sentence, shown on the
   canceled and retained steps. The text is limited to 380 px wide.

The action row starts 28 px below the content. Below 440 px, the buttons stack and the secondary button moves under the
primary one.

### Choosing reasons and offers

Write a reason as the person would say it, and give each one an offer only when a concrete alternative exists. A
reason without an offer goes straight to the confirmation, so an offer that does not match the reason makes the flow
look like a sales step. Use `DefaultOffer` for a general alternative such as a call with your team, and keep it for
reasons that have no specific answer.

Set `AsksForDetails` on a reason when a follow-up question makes the feedback useful, such as "What were you missing?"
for a missing feature. The answer is still optional, and the question replaces the general prompt only after that
reason is chosen.

### Without an offer

When neither the chosen reason nor `DefaultOffer` has an offer, the flow goes from the reason straight to the
confirmation, and the step bar has two segments instead of three. With `Reasons` left empty, the flow uses the five
reasons in `Labels.DefaultReasons`. The demo below starts with a reason that asks a follow-up question, so the field
reads "What were you missing?".

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.CancelFlowNoOfferDemo">
    <arc:CancelFlow x:Name="Flow" PlanName="Studio">
        <arc:CancelFlow.Losses>
            <x:String>Shared projects become read-only for all 6 members</x:String>
            <x:String>Version history older than 30 days is deleted</x:String>
        </arc:CancelFlow.Losses>
    </arc:CancelFlow>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class CancelFlowNoOfferDemo : UserControl
{
    public CancelFlowNoOfferDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Flow.AccessEndsOn = new DateTime(2026, 11, 1);
        // No Reasons, so the flow offers the five default reasons from its labels; start with one chosen and answered.
        Flow.SelectedReason = Flow.Labels.DefaultReasons[2];
        Flow.Feedback = "Two-way sync with our shared calendar.";
    }
}
```

### In a dialog

Set `Appearance` to `Plain` to drop the card's frame, shadow and padding when the flow sits inside a `Dialog`. The
dialog closes on `KeepPlanRequested`, which both "Keep my plan" and "Done" raise. "Reactivate plan" raises
`ReactivateRequested` and then starts the flow over; mark the event handled to keep the canceled step on screen. An
offer without an `Icon` shows a gift.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.CancelFlowInDialogDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12" HorizontalAlignment="Center">
        <arc:Button HorizontalAlignment="Center"
                    Variant="Secondary"
                    Content="Cancel subscription"
                    Command="{Binding #CancelDialog.OpenCommand}" />
        <TextBlock x:Name="Status"
                   HorizontalAlignment="Center"
                   Text="Studio plan · renews on Nov 1, 2026"
                   FontSize="14"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
        <arc:Dialog x:Name="CancelDialog"
                    Title="Cancel subscription"
                    Description="Larkspur Studio · Studio plan, 6 seats"
                    Size="Large"
                    Opened="OnOpened">
            <arc:CancelFlow x:Name="Flow"
                            Appearance="Plain"
                            PlanName="Studio"
                            KeepPlanRequested="OnKeepPlanRequested"
                            OfferAccepted="OnOfferAccepted"
                            CancellationConfirmed="OnCancellationConfirmed"
                            ReactivateRequested="OnReactivateRequested">
                <arc:CancelFlow.DefaultOffer>
                    <arc:CancelFlowOffer Title="Have a month on us"
                                         Description="Stay on Studio for another month at no charge, then decide. Nothing changes for your team in the meantime."
                                         AcceptLabel="Claim a free month"
                                         AcceptedTitle="Your free month is on"
                                         AcceptedDescription="November is on us. Your next invoice is on Dec 1, 2026." />
                </arc:CancelFlow.DefaultOffer>
                <arc:CancelFlow.Losses>
                    <x:String>Shared projects become read-only for all 6 members</x:String>
                    <x:String>Custom domains and single sign-on stop working</x:String>
                </arc:CancelFlow.Losses>
            </arc:CancelFlow>
        </arc:Dialog>
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class CancelFlowInDialogDemo : UserControl
{
    private const string Active = "Studio plan · renews on Nov 1, 2026";

    public CancelFlowInDialogDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Flow.AccessEndsOn = new DateTime(2026, 11, 1);
    }

    // Every opening starts from the first step, unless the plan was just canceled.
    private void OnOpened(object? sender, EventArgs e)
    {
        if (Flow.Step != CancelFlowStep.Canceled)
        {
            Flow.Reset();
        }
    }

    private void OnKeepPlanRequested(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) => CancelDialog.Close();

    private void OnOfferAccepted(object? sender, CancelFlowOfferEventArgs e) =>
        Status.Text = "Studio plan · free month added, renews on Dec 1, 2026";

    private void OnCancellationConfirmed(object? sender, CancelFlowCancelEventArgs e) =>
        Status.Text = $"Studio plan · canceled ({e.Reason.Title.ToLowerInvariant()}), ends on Nov 1, 2026";

    // The flow resets itself after this event; the page only puts the plan back.
    private void OnReactivateRequested(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        Status.Text = Active;
        CancelDialog.Close();
    }
}
```

### Binding to a view model

The flow keeps the answers, and the view model keeps the business rules. In an MVVM app with CommunityToolkit.Mvvm,
bind the reasons, the losses and the plan facts, and handle the outcomes in the view model. The billing service is
the app's own placeholder.

```csharp
public partial class CancelPlanViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    private readonly IBillingService _billing;

    public CancelPlanViewModel(IBillingService billing)
    {
        _billing = billing;
    }

    [ObservableProperty]
    private string? _planName = "Team";

    [ObservableProperty]
    private DateTime? _accessEndsOn = new DateTime(2026, 11, 1);

    [ObservableProperty]
    private CancelFlowReason? _selectedReason;

    [ObservableProperty]
    private string? _feedback;

    public ObservableCollection<CancelFlowReason> Reasons { get; } = new();

    public ObservableCollection<string> Losses { get; } = new();

    [RelayCommand]
    private async Task CancelConfirmedAsync(CancelFlowCancelEventArgs e)
    {
        await _billing.CancelAtPeriodEndAsync(e.Reason.Title, e.Feedback);
    }
}
```

```xml
<arc:CancelFlow PlanName="{Binding PlanName}"
                AccessEndsOn="{Binding AccessEndsOn}"
                Reasons="{Binding Reasons}"
                Losses="{Binding Losses}"
                SelectedReason="{Binding SelectedReason, Mode=TwoWay}"
                Feedback="{Binding Feedback, Mode=TwoWay}" />
```

`SelectedReason` and `Feedback` are two-way, so the view model sees the answers as the person gives them. `PlanName`,
`AccessEndsOn`, `Reasons`, `Losses`, `DefaultOffer` and `Labels` are read when they change. The flow has no commands:
connect `CancellationConfirmed`, `OfferAccepted` and `KeepPlanRequested` in code-behind and forward them to the view
model. Read `Step` (read-only) when you need to know where the person is.

### Focus and dismissal

After every step change, focus moves to the new step's title, and the title is announced politely. Keep the flow in
its dialog or card until the person leaves it. Close the dialog on `KeepPlanRequested` only; `OfferAccepted` moves the flow to the retained step, and the person still needs "Done" to
leave it. Call `Reset()` to start over from the first step, which clears the reason and the feedback. `GoBack()`
returns `false` on the reason and retained steps, where nothing precedes them.

### Text and other languages

Every built-in string is in `CancelFlowLabels`. Replace the whole object to reword or translate the flow; dates follow
`Labels.Culture`. The defaults are English, such as "Why are you canceling?" and "Hold to cancel plan". The table in
the API reference lists every default.

```csharp
flow.Labels = new CancelFlowLabels
{
    Culture = CultureInfo.GetCultureInfo("nl-NL"),
    ReasonTitle = "Waarom zeg je op?",
    Continue = "Doorgaan",
    KeepPlan = "Abonnement houden",
    HoldToCancel = "Houd vast om op te zeggen",
};
```

Sentences that contain the plan name or a date are built by the labels from the plan name and the formatted date, so
translate the whole sentence, not its pieces. Offer titles and reasons are your content, so translate them in your own
data.

### Example: Team plan cancellation

An admin cancels the Team plan from account settings. The flow shows three reasons; the first two have no matching offer
yet, so the default offer is "Talk to us first". The plan name and the access end date come from the plan data, and the
step bar shows three segments because the path can include an offer. The first step is shown with "Continue" disabled, which
is the state the person sees before choosing a reason.

The design decision here is to ask before offering. A reason with an offer appears only after it is chosen, so the
offer answers the reason rather than interrupting it. The Continue button stays disabled until a reason is chosen, so
the flow never records an empty answer.

![The first step of a Team plan cancellation, before a reason is chosen](https://docs.tkcode.si/shots/Docs/Blocks/CancelFlow/images/TeamCancellation.webp)

```xml
<StackPanel Width="560">
    <arc:CancelFlow PlanName="Team" AccessEndsOn="2026-11-01">
    <arc:CancelFlow.Reasons>
        <arc:CancelFlowReason Title="Too expensive"
                              Description="The price is more than it is worth to us right now." />
        <arc:CancelFlowReason Title="Not using it enough"
                              Description="We do not open it often enough to keep paying for it." />
        <arc:CancelFlowReason Title="Missing a feature I need"
                              Description="Something we rely on is not there yet."
                              AsksForDetails="True" />
    </arc:CancelFlow.Reasons>
    <arc:CancelFlow.DefaultOffer>
        <arc:CancelFlowOffer Title="Talk to us first"
                             Description="Fifteen minutes with our team is often enough to fix what is not working."
                             AcceptLabel="Book a 15-minute call" />
    </arc:CancelFlow.DefaultOffer>
</arc:CancelFlow>
</StackPanel>
```

### Content guidelines

Write the flow as a conversation with the person who is leaving. Be direct about what ends, and do not guilt or
pressure them. The defaults already follow these rules.

- Use the plan's name in every sentence that refers to it, such as "Cancel your Team plan?", so the person knows
  which subscription is affected.
- Give the access end date with the month name, as in "You keep access until Nov 1, 2026." Do not write "end of the
  month" when the date is known.
- Write reasons in the person's own words, short enough for one line: "Too expensive", not "Price sensitivity".
- Write offer titles as the benefit with its size, such as "Take 40% off for 3 months", and the accept button as the
  action, such as "Claim 40% off".
- Write the hold button as a verb phrase with the object: "Hold to cancel plan". Do not write "Confirm" alone, because
  the person must hold the control, and the label should say what happens.
- Keep the losses in plain terms that name the consequence: "Shared projects become read-only for all 6 members".

| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| Are you sure? | Cancel your Team plan? |
| Click to confirm cancellation | Hold to cancel plan |
| We are sorry to see you go | Your plan is canceled |
| Reason: other | Something else |
| Offer expires soon | Take 40% off for 3 months |

### Best practices

**Do**

- Set `AccessEndsOn` from the billing period, so the confirmation and the result show the real end date. An empty date
  makes the flow promise access that the server may not give.
- Show the offer only when it is real and can be applied. The flow moves to the retained step as soon as the person
  accepts, without waiting for your code, so apply the offer reliably in `OfferAccepted`.
- Record the reason and the feedback with `CancellationConfirmed`, even if the cancellation later fails, so the
  support team sees what the person said.
- Keep `Losses` to the consequences that apply to this account, and leave it empty when nothing is lost, rather than
  listing generic warnings.
- Use `Appearance="Plain"` inside a `Dialog`, so the dialog does not draw a second frame around the flow.

**Avoid**

- Hiding the way out. Keep "Keep my plan" visible on the reason and confirmation steps; a flow that traps the person
  leads to chargebacks and complaints.
- Offers for reasons they do not match. A discount after "Missing a feature I need" reads as a sales attempt and
  lowers the trust in the rest of the flow.
- Changing the plan in `CancellationConfirmed` before your server has confirmed it. Mark the plan as canceled only
  after the server accepts the request.
- Removing the hold. The hold is what separates a deliberate cancellation from an accidental click, so replacing it
  with a single button defeats the purpose of the step.
- Translating the labels but leaving the reason titles and offers in English. The flow then mixes two languages on one
  card, so translate your content with the labels.

### Common questions

**Why is Continue disabled on the first step?** The flow needs a reason before it can move on, so `SelectedReason` must
be set. Choose a row with the arrow keys, or set `SelectedReason` in code.

**Why does the step bar show two segments?** The path has no offer: the chosen reason has none, and `DefaultOffer` is
null. Set `DefaultOffer` or give the reason an `Offer` to add the third segment. Before a reason is chosen, the bar
counts the path as having an offer when any reason has one.

**Why did my "Reactivate plan" button restart the flow?** The flow calls `Reset()` after `ReactivateRequested` unless a
handler marks the event handled. Set `e.Handled = true` in the handler to keep the canceled step on screen while you
restore the plan.

**How do I start the flow again from the first step?** Call `Reset()`. It clears the reason and the feedback and returns
to the first step. `GoBack()` goes back one step from the offer or confirmation, and returns `false` on the other steps.

**Does the flow cancel the subscription?** No. It reports `CancellationConfirmed` with the reason and feedback, and your
code calls the billing API. Update `Losses`, `AccessEndsOn` or the page's plan state when the server answers.

## API reference

### CancelFlow

A considerate cancellation flow in one card: it asks why, offers an alternative that fits the reason, shows what ends and when, and asks the person to hold a button to confirm; the last step thanks them or lets them reactivate. A step bar on top shows where they are. Steps slide in the direction of travel while the card's height follows on a spring; each step's controls are built once and reused. Enter runs the step's main action, Alt+Left goes back, and focus moves to the new step's title after every change.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `PlanName` | `string?` | `null` | The plan's name as people know it, such as "Studio"; used in the titles and sentences. |
| `AccessEndsOn` | `DateTime?` | `null` | The last day of paid access after canceling (usually the renewal date); null when access ends at once. |
| `Reasons` | `ICollection<CancelFlowReason>` | – | The reasons to choose from, written inline or bound. Empty (the default) uses the five reasons in `DefaultReasons`. |
| `DefaultOffer` | `CancelFlowOffer?` | `null` | The offer for reasons without one of their own; null skips the offer step for them. |
| `Losses` | `ICollection<string>` | – | What ends with the plan, listed on the confirmation step (for example "Shared projects become read-only"). |
| `Step` | `CancelFlowStep` | – | *Read-only.* The step on screen: Reason, Offer, Confirm, Canceled or Retained. Changes through the flow's buttons, `GoBack` and `Reset`. |
| `SelectedReason` | `CancelFlowReason?` | `null` | The chosen reason (two-way); Continue is disabled while it is null. |
| `Feedback` | `string?` | `null` | What the person wrote in the optional feedback field (two-way); null when empty. |
| `Labels` | `CancelFlowLabels` | – | The built-in text and date culture; replace the whole object to localize the flow. |
| `Appearance` | `CancelFlowAppearance` | `Card` | Card (default) draws the flow's own frame; Plain drops it for a flow inside a dialog or another card. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `StepChanged` | `CancelFlowStepChangedEventArgs` | Raised after the step changes, with the old and the new step. |
| `OfferAccepted` | `CancelFlowOfferEventArgs` | Raised when the person accepts the offer (the flow moves to Retained), with the reason and the offer. |
| `CancellationConfirmed` | `CancelFlowCancelEventArgs` | Raised when the hold to cancel completes (the flow moves to Canceled), with the reason and the feedback. |
| `KeepPlanRequested` | `RoutedEventArgs` | Raised by "Keep my plan" and by "Done" after an accepted offer: the person is staying, so close the flow. |
| `ReactivateRequested` | `RoutedEventArgs` | Raised by "Reactivate plan" on the canceled step. Unless a handler marks it handled, the flow then calls `Reset`. |

Pseudo-classes: `:narrow`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

`CancelFlowReason`

| Property | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Title` | `string` | The reason as the person would say it, such as "Too expensive". |
| `Description` | `string?` | A short line under the title. |
| `Offer` | `CancelFlowOffer?` | The offer shown after this reason; null falls back to `DefaultOffer`. |
| `AsksForDetails` | `bool` | When true, the feedback field asks `DetailsPrompt` instead of the general question. The answer stays optional. |
| `DetailsPrompt` | `string?` | The follow-up question, such as "What were you missing?"; null uses `Labels.DetailsPrompt`. |

`CancelFlowOffer`

| Property | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Title` | `string` | What is offered, such as "Take 40% off for 3 months". |
| `Description` | `string?` | What the offer means for the plan and the bill. |
| `AcceptLabel` | `string?` | The accept button, such as "Claim 40% off"; null uses `Labels.AcceptOffer`. |
| `Icon` | `Geometry?` | A 24×24 stroke icon for the tile above the title; null shows a gift. |
| `AcceptedTitle` | `string?` | The title of the retained step, such as "40% off is on"; null uses `Labels.RetainedTitle`. |
| `AcceptedDescription` | `string?` | The sentence under it; null uses `Labels.RetainedDescription`. |

`CancelFlowLabels` (all `init`; functions build sentences from the plan name and the formatted date)

| Property | Default |
|---|---|
| `Culture` | en-US |
| `StepCounter` | "Step {n} of {total}" |
| `Back` | "Back" |
| `ReasonTitle` / `ReasonDescription` | "Why are you canceling?" / "Your answer helps us improve {plan}." |
| `FeedbackLabel` / `DetailsPrompt` / `FeedbackPlaceholder` | "Anything else we should know?" / "Tell us a little more" / "Optional" |
| `KeepPlan` / `Continue` | "Keep my plan" / "Continue" |
| `AcceptOffer` / `ContinueCanceling` | "Accept offer" / "Continue canceling" |
| `ConfirmTitle` / `AccessUntil` / `AfterThat` | "Cancel your {plan} plan?" / "You keep access until {date}." / "After that:" |
| `LossesName` / `HoldToCancel` / `HoldConfirmed` | "What ends" / "Hold to cancel plan" / "Canceled" |
| `CanceledTitle` / `CanceledDescription` | "Your plan is canceled" / "You can keep using {plan} until {date}. We sent a confirmation to your email." |
| `Reactivate` | "Reactivate plan" |
| `RetainedTitle` / `RetainedDescription` / `Done` | "{offer} is on" / "Thanks for staying. You'll see the change on your next invoice." / "Done" |
| `DefaultReasons` | Too expensive; Not using it enough; Missing a feature I need; Switching to another tool; Something else |

`CancelFlowStep`

| Member | Shown when |
|---|---|
| `Reason` | The first step: the reason and the optional feedback |
| `Offer` | The offer for the chosen reason or `DefaultOffer` |
| `Confirm` | What ends, with the hold button |
| `Canceled` | The end of a confirmed cancellation, with "Reactivate plan" |
| `Retained` | The end of a flow where the offer was accepted and the plan stays |

## Accessibility

- After every step change, focus moves to the new step's title, which is announced politely. Titles take focus but are
  not tab stops, so Tab goes on to the step's first control.
- The reasons are a radio group named after the step title ("Why are you canceling?"). The arrow keys move between
  reasons, and the group is a single tab stop.
- The cancellation needs a deliberate hold: press and hold the button, or focus it and hold Space or Enter. Its help text
  says so.
- The round back button is named "Back" and has a tooltip. The collapsed feedback field is out of the tab order until a
  reason is chosen.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` | Move through the step's controls in order |
| `Up` / `Down` | Move between reasons in the radio group |
| `Enter` | Press the step's main action: Continue, the offer's accept button or Done. On an unchosen reason, Enter chooses it first |
| `Enter` in the feedback field | Adds a line |
| `Ctrl+Enter` / `Cmd+Enter` in the feedback field | Continue |
| `Alt+Left` | Go back from the offer and the confirmation |
| Hold `Space` or `Enter` on the hold button | Confirms the cancellation (`HoldToConfirm` behavior) |

An Enter key still held from the previous step does not press the next step's button.

## Motion

- Steps slide 12 px in the direction of travel (forward from the right, back from the left) with a short fade, and the
  card's height follows the new step on a spring.
- The feedback field opens and closes on a height spring. The step bar's segments cross-fade to their new colors, and
  the back button fades in and out as its space collapses.
- On the last step the check draws itself in about half a second.
- Reduced motion keeps only the fades: steps cross-fade in place, segment colors change quickly and the check is drawn
  at once. Off changes everything in place.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| Step changes | Slides 12 px with a fade; the card height springs to the new step | Steps cross-fade in place | Immediate |
| Feedback field opens or closes | Height opens on a spring | Shown or hidden without the height spring | Immediate |
| Step bar segment changes | Colors cross-fade | Colors change quickly | Immediate |
| Back button appears or leaves | Fades while its space collapses | Fades in place | Immediate |
| Result check on the last step | Draws in over about half a second | Drawn at once | Drawn at once |

## Related

- The other Settings blocks: `SettingsPage`, `SettingsCommand`, `SecuritySettings`, `BillingOverview` (its "Cancel plan"
  button is a natural way in) and `UsageBilling`.
- `RadioGroup`, `Textarea`, `HoldToConfirm`, `Button` and `Dialog`, which the flow is built from.
- `ConfirmMorph` for a lighter in-place confirmation of smaller destructive actions.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `BillingOverview` | The cancel button lives on the billing page, and the flow opens from `CancelPlanRequested` |
| `ConfirmMorph` | A small destructive action needs one confirmation in place |
| `HoldToConfirm` | A single irreversible action needs a deliberate hold, without reasons or offers |
| `RadioCards` | The person chooses between plans or options rather than leaving |
| `Dialog` | The flow runs in a modal window, with `Appearance="Plain"` |
| `Textarea` | A free-form answer is needed outside a cancellation flow |

# Team members

> The members page of a workspace: invite by typing or pasting addresses that fly into pending invites as the seat count rolls, change roles, search, and remove people with an inline confirm.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc.Blocks`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc.Blocks --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/blocks/team-members

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.TeamMembersPreviewDemo">
    <!-- Five members and two invites on ten seats; sending waits 700 ms and resending 600 ms. Data: TeamMembersDemoData. -->
    <arc:TeamMembers x:Name="Block" Margin="0,12" Title="Members" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class TeamMembersPreviewDemo : UserControl
{
    public TeamMembersPreviewDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        TeamMembersDemoData.Fill(Block);
        // Connect these to your API; here they only wait, so the busy buttons and the flight are visible.
        TeamMembersDemoData.Simulate(Block);
    }
}
```

## When to use

`TeamMembers` is the people page of a workspace or team settings screen. It answers three questions in one place: who
has access and with which role, who has been invited but has not joined yet, and how many seats are left. Inviting is
fast: type or paste addresses, pick a role, send. The sent addresses fly from the field into the pending list and the seat
count rolls up, so the person sees exactly where their invites went.

- **Workspace or organization settings.** Members with their role, last activity and presence, the owner marked, the
  current user marked "You".
- **Inviting several people at once.** Addresses become chips on Enter, a comma, a semicolon or a space, and a pasted
  list is split in one go. Typos stay in the field with an error; addresses that already belong to someone are refused
  with the reason.
- **Plans with a seat limit.** Members and pending invites each take a seat. The send button refuses to go over the free
  seats and says how many addresses to take out; a full workspace turns the seat bar to the warning color.

## When not to use

- **A people directory to browse.** For profiles, departments and contact details use the Team directory block; this
  block manages access.
- **Defining what each role may do.** Use the Roles and permissions block. Here a role is a name with a short line of
  text, picked from a menu.
- **A general chip input.** For tags or recipients outside an invite flow use `TagInput`.
- **Large organizations.** Rows are not virtualized. Show a page of members at a time (and search on the server) when
  there are hundreds.

## Usage

The block derives from Avalonia's `TemplatedControl`. Members are `TeamMembersPerson` objects and pending invites
`TeamMembersInvite` objects, both `AvaloniaObject`s you can bind to. Roles are keys (`"admin"`, `"member"`, `"viewer"` by
default) described by `TeamMembersRoleOption`s; the owner has no role menu.

```xml
<arc:TeamMembers Title="Members"
                 Description="Choose who can work in the Northwind Lab workspace."
                 WorkspaceName="Northwind Lab"
                 SeatLimit="10">
    <arc:TeamMembersPerson Name="Lena Hart" Email="lena@northwind.example" IsOwner="True" IsCurrentUser="True"
                           IsOnline="True" LastActive="Active now" />
    <arc:TeamMembersPerson Name="Theo Brandt" Email="theo@northwind.example" Role="admin" LastActive="Active now" />
    <arc:TeamMembersPerson Name="Ines Kowal" Email="ines@northwind.example" Role="member" LastActive="Active 3 hours ago" />
</arc:TeamMembers>
```

Without handlers every action takes effect at once. Connect each one to your server with an async handler; the block shows
a busy state while it runs and keeps the old state when it throws:

```csharp
public interface IMembersApi
{
    Task InviteAsync(string workspace, IReadOnlyList<string> emails, string? role, CancellationToken cancel);
    Task ResendAsync(string inviteId, CancellationToken cancel);
    Task RevokeAsync(string inviteId, CancellationToken cancel);
    Task RemoveAsync(string memberId, CancellationToken cancel);
    Task SetRoleAsync(string memberId, string? role, CancellationToken cancel);
}

members.SendInvitesAction = async (request, cancel) =>
    await api.InviteAsync(workspaceId, request.Emails, request.Role, cancel);
members.ResendInviteAction = (invite, cancel) => api.ResendAsync(invite.Id!, cancel);
members.RevokeInviteAction = (invite, cancel) => api.RevokeAsync(invite.Id!, cancel);
members.RemoveMemberAction = (person, cancel) => api.RemoveAsync(person.Id!, cancel);
members.ChangeRoleAction = (change, cancel) => api.SetRoleAsync(change.Member.Id!, change.NewRole, cancel);
```

### Anatomy

- **Header**: `Title`, `Description` and the seat meter ("7 of 10 seats" over a 4px bar). Hide the meter with
  `IsSeatMeterVisible`.
- **Invite form**: the address field with its chips, the "Invite as" role picker (`InviteRole`, two-way) and the send
  button, which reads "Send invite" or "Send 3 invites". The line under the field shows a hint, a seat warning or an
  error. `IsInviteVisible` hides the whole form.
- **Members**: a heading with the count, the search field (`IsSearchVisible`), and one row per member: avatar with
  presence dot, name and email, last active, the role menu (or "Owner") and a remove button.
- **Pending invites**: a heading with the count and one row per invite: a dashed avatar with initials from the address,
  the address, "role · detail" and the Resend and Revoke buttons.
- **Footer**: the result of the last action ("2 invites sent as Member"). It stays until the next action; `StatusText`
  holds it. `IsFooterVisible` hides the footer but the results are still announced.

### Inviting

Each committed piece of text is judged on its own, ignoring case:

1. Not a complete address (one @, a dotted domain, a last part of at least two letters): it stays in the field, the field
   turns red and the line under it says so. Typing again clears the error.
2. Already a chip: dropped without a word.
3. A member's address: dropped, and the line names the member.
4. A pending invite's address: dropped, with an error.
5. Anything else becomes a chip at the end.

`EmailValidator` replaces the address check. Backspace on an empty field removes the last chip and Enter on an empty field
sends. A valid address still being typed counts in the button's label and becomes a chip when the invites are sent.
`AddEmails`, `RemovePendingEmail`, `ClearPendingEmails` and `SendInvitesAsync` do the same from code; `PendingEmails` lists
the chips.

`SendInvitesAction` receives a `TeamMembersSendRequest` with the addresses, the role key and the `TeamMembersInvite`
objects the block is about to add (fill in their `Id` if your server returns one). When it finishes, the invites join the
pending list and `InvitesSent` is raised.

### Seats

`SeatsUsed` is the members plus the pending invites, `SeatsRemaining` what is left of `SeatLimit`. Only the chips count
against the free seats: with more chips than free seats the send button is disabled and the line asks to take some out;
with every seat taken the bar turns to the warning color and the line says so. Revoking an invite or removing a member
frees a seat at once.

### Bound collections and events

`MembersSource` and `InvitesSource` take your own collections and follow their changes. When they are writable lists the
block adds sent invites and removes revoked invites and removed members itself; for a read-only collection add the invites
in an `InvitesSent` handler. Every action raises an event with what changed (`InvitesSent`, `InviteResent`,
`InviteRevoked`, `MemberRemoved`, `MemberRoleChanged`) and runs the matching command. `SearchText` and `InviteRole` are
two-way.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.TeamMembersBoundDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12" Margin="0,12">
        <arc:TeamMembers x:Name="Block" Title="Members" />
        <Grid ColumnDefinitions="*,*" ColumnSpacing="12">
            <StackPanel Grid.Column="0" Spacing="8">
                <TextBlock x:Name="Seats" FontWeight="Medium" />
                <StackPanel Orientation="Horizontal" Spacing="8">
                    <arc:Button x:Name="AddSeat" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Content="Add a seat" />
                    <arc:Button x:Name="Join" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Content="Owen accepts" />
                    <arc:Button x:Name="Find" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Content="Search “coastal”" />
                </StackPanel>
            </StackPanel>
            <TextBlock Grid.Column="1" x:Name="Log" TextWrapping="Wrap" MaxHeight="120" />
        </Grid>
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using System.Collections.ObjectModel;
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class TeamMembersBoundDemo : UserControl
{
    private readonly ObservableCollection<TeamMembersPerson> _members = new(TeamMembersDemoData.Members());
    private readonly ObservableCollection<TeamMembersInvite> _invites = new(TeamMembersDemoData.Invites());
    private readonly List<string> _log = new();

    public TeamMembersBoundDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Block.Description = TeamMembersDemoData.Description;
        Block.WorkspaceName = TeamMembersDemoData.Workspace;
        Block.SeatLimit = 8;
        // Your own collections: the block adds sent invites to them and removes revoked invites and removed members.
        Block.MembersSource = _members;
        Block.InvitesSource = _invites;
        TeamMembersDemoData.Simulate(Block);

        Block.InvitesSent += (_, e) => Write($"InvitesSent: {string.Join(", ", e.Invites.Select(i => i.Email))} as {e.Role}");
        Block.InviteResent += (_, e) => Write($"InviteResent: {e.Invite.Email}");
        Block.InviteRevoked += (_, e) => Write($"InviteRevoked: {e.Invite.Email}");
        Block.MemberRemoved += (_, e) => Write($"MemberRemoved: {e.Member.Name}");
        Block.MemberRoleChanged += (_, e) => Write($"MemberRoleChanged: {e.Member.Name} {e.OldRole} → {e.NewRole}");
        Block.PropertyChanged += (_, e) =>
        {
            if (e.Property == TeamMembers.SeatsUsedProperty || e.Property == TeamMembers.SeatLimitProperty)
            {
                UpdateSeats();
            }
            else if (e.Property == TeamMembers.SearchTextProperty)
            {
                Write($"SearchText: “{Block.SearchText}”");
            }
        };

        AddSeat.Click += (_, _) => Block.SeatLimit++;
        // An invite accepted elsewhere: the invite leaves the list and a member joins.
        Join.Click += (_, _) =>
        {
            if (_invites.FirstOrDefault(i => i.Email?.StartsWith("owen", StringComparison.Ordinal) == true) is not { } invite)
            {
                return;
            }
            _invites.Remove(invite);
            _members.Add(new TeamMembersPerson { Name = "Owen Park", Email = invite.Email, Role = invite.Role, LastActive = "Joined just now", IsOnline = true });
        };
        Find.Click += (_, _) => Block.SearchText = Block.SearchText == "coastal" ? string.Empty : "coastal";
        UpdateSeats();
    }

    private void UpdateSeats() => Seats.Text = $"{Block.SeatsUsed} of {Block.SeatLimit} seats used, {Block.SeatsRemaining} free";

    private void Write(string line)
    {
        _log.Insert(0, line);
        if (_log.Count > 6)
        {
            _log.RemoveAt(_log.Count - 1);
        }
        Log.Text = string.Join(Environment.NewLine, _log);
    }
}
```

### When the server says no

A handler that throws keeps the previous state and raises `ActionFailed` with the action, its subject and the message:

- **Send**: the chips stay, the button comes back and the line under the field shows the error (as does the footer).
- **Resend**: the button goes back to Resend and the footer shows the error.
- **Revoke** and **remove**: the row stays (the confirmation stays open) and the footer shows the error.
- **Role change**: the new role shows at once and goes back if the handler throws.

The text is the exception's message, `ErrorFormatter`'s text, or a built-in sentence when there is no message. A
cancellation (the block leaving the window) is not reported.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.TeamMembersFailuresDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12" Margin="0,12">
        <arc:TeamMembers x:Name="Block" Title="Members" />
        <TextBlock x:Name="Log"
                   HorizontalAlignment="Center"
                   TextAlignment="Center"
                   TextWrapping="Wrap"
                   MaxWidth="560"
                   Text="Addresses at bounce.example fail to send, every second resend fails, Sara's invite cannot be revoked and nobody can be made an admin." />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class TeamMembersFailuresDemo : UserControl
{
    private int _resends;

    public TeamMembersFailuresDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        TeamMembersDemoData.Fill(Block);

        // Each handler waits like a server, then refuses some requests by throwing; the block keeps the old state and shows
        // the message (in the line under the field for a send, in the footer for everything else).
        Block.SendInvitesAction = async (request, cancellation) =>
        {
            await Task.Delay(700, cancellation);
            if (request.Emails.FirstOrDefault(e => e.EndsWith("@bounce.example", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase)) is { } bad)
            {
                throw new InvalidOperationException($"The mail server refused {bad}. Remove it and send again.");
            }
        };
        Block.ResendInviteAction = async (_, cancellation) =>
        {
            await Task.Delay(600, cancellation);
            if (++_resends % 2 == 0)
            {
                throw new TimeoutException();
            }
        };
        Block.RevokeInviteAction = async (invite, cancellation) =>
        {
            await Task.Delay(400, cancellation);
            if (invite.Email?.StartsWith("sara", StringComparison.Ordinal) == true)
            {
                throw new InvalidOperationException("This invite was already accepted.");
            }
        };
        Block.RemoveMemberAction = (_, cancellation) => Task.Delay(500, cancellation);
        Block.ChangeRoleAction = async (change, cancellation) =>
        {
            await Task.Delay(300, cancellation);
            if (change.NewRole == "admin")
            {
                throw new UnauthorizedAccessException();
            }
        };
        Block.ErrorFormatter = exception => exception switch
        {
            UnauthorizedAccessException => "Only the owner can make someone an admin.",
            TimeoutException => "The mail server did not answer. Try the resend again.",
            _ => exception.Message
        };
        Block.ActionFailed += (_, e) => Log.Text = $"{e.Action} failed: {e.Message}";
        Block.InvitesSent += (_, e) => Log.Text = $"Sent {e.Invites.Count} invite(s)";
        Block.InviteResent += (_, e) => Log.Text = $"Resent to {e.Invite.Email}";
    }
}
```

### Removing people

The remove button turns the row into a confirmation in place: the row tints, "Remove Ines Kowal?" and a line about losing
access replace the name, and Cancel and Remove replace the columns. Only one row asks at a time. Escape or Cancel go back
and return the focus to the remove button; after a removal the focus moves to the next row's remove button.
`RequestRemove`, `CancelRemove` and `RemoveMemberAsync` (no confirmation) do the same from code.

### Narrow containers

The block reads its own width. At 640 or less the last-active text moves under the email; at 600 the header and the
invite row stack, the search takes its own line and the paddings tighten from 20 to 16; at 480 the pending invites' buttons
move under the address; at 420 each member row splits into the person on top and last active, role and remove below.

```xml
         the pending invites' buttons go under the address. The block reads its own width, not the window's. -->
```
