### Words

Every text the block shows or announces is in `Labels`, a `TeamMembersLabels` with English defaults; texts with values are
functions so the word order can change in another language. Role names and descriptions come from `Roles`.

## API reference

### TeamMembers

The members page of a workspace's settings. A header (title, a line of text and a seat meter: "7 of 10 seats" over a thin bar that turns to the warning color when every seat is taken); an invite form where typed or pasted addresses become chips (Enter, comma, semicolon or space commits; Backspace on an empty field removes the last chip; invalid text stays with an error, duplicates drop silently, members and pending invites drop with an error), a role picker and a send button that counts the invites and refuses to go over the free seats; the members (avatar, name, email, last active, role menu, remove with an inline confirmation) and the pending invites (resend, revoke), both filtered by one search; and a footer that reports the last action. Sending flies each address from its chip into a new pending row while the seat count rolls. Every server call is an async handler you supply; a handler that throws keeps the old state and shows the error.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Title` | `string?` | `"Members"` | The heading; null leaves it out. |
| `Description` | `string?` | `null` | The line under the heading; null leaves it out. |
| `WorkspaceName` | `string?` | `null` | The workspace's name, used in the removal confirmation and its status line; null leaves it out of them. |
| `MembersSource` | `IEnumerable?` | `null` | The members, when you give them as a list to follow; it wins over `Members`. When it is a writable list the block removes members from it. |
| `InvitesSource` | `IEnumerable?` | `null` | The pending invites, when you give them as a list to follow; it wins over `Invites`. When it is a writable list the block adds and removes invites in it. |
| `SeatLimit` | `int` | `10` | How many seats the workspace has; members and pending invites each take one. |
| `InviteRole` | `string?` | `"member"` | The role key new invites get (two-way; the picker next to the invite field writes it). |
| `SearchText` | `string` | `""` | The search text (two-way); it filters members and invites by name or email. |
| `Labels` | `TeamMembersLabels` | – | Every word the block shows or announces; replace it to translate or reword. |
| `IsFramed` | `bool` | `true` | Draws the block as a bordered card with rounded corners (true); false lays it flat at the container's width. |
| `IsInviteVisible` | `bool` | `true` | Whether the invite form shows. |
| `IsSearchVisible` | `bool` | `true` | Whether the search field shows in the members section's head. |
| `IsSeatMeterVisible` | `bool` | `true` | Whether the seat meter shows in the header. |
| `IsFooterVisible` | `bool` | `true` | Whether the footer with the status line shows (the status is announced either way). |
| `IsReadOnly` | `bool` | `false` | A view for people who cannot manage the team: no invite form, roles as plain text, no remove, resend or revoke buttons. The search still works. |
| `SendInvitesAction` | `Func<TeamMembersSendRequest, CancellationToken, Task>?` | `null` | Sends the invites: awaited when Send is pressed (or `SendInvitesAsync` is called) while the button spins. An exception keeps the chips and shows its message; a cancellation keeps the chips silently. Null sends at once. |
| `ResendInviteAction` | `Func<TeamMembersInvite, CancellationToken, Task>?` | `null` | Sends a pending invite again while its Resend button spins; an exception shows an error in the footer. Null resends at once. |
| `RevokeInviteAction` | `Func<TeamMembersInvite, CancellationToken, Task>?` | `null` | Withdraws a pending invite while its Revoke button spins; an exception keeps the row. Null withdraws at once. |
| `RemoveMemberAction` | `Func<TeamMembersPerson, CancellationToken, Task>?` | `null` | Removes a member after the inline confirmation, while Remove spins; an exception keeps the row. Null removes at once. |
| `ChangeRoleAction` | `Func<TeamMembersRoleChange, CancellationToken, Task>?` | `null` | Saves a role change; the new role shows at once and goes back if it throws. Null keeps the change at once. |
| `ErrorFormatter` | `Func<Exception, string>?` | `null` | Turns a handler's exception into the error text; null uses the exception's message (or a built-in text when it has none). |
| `EmailValidator` | `Func<string, bool>?` | `null` | Replaces the built-in address check (one @, a dotted domain, a last part of at least two letters). |
| `InvitesSentCommand` | `ICommand?` | `null` | Run after invites went out, with the `TeamMembersInvitesSentEventArgs` as the parameter. |
| `InviteResentCommand` | `ICommand?` | `null` | Run after an invite was sent again, with the `TeamMembersInviteEventArgs` as the parameter. |
| `InviteRevokedCommand` | `ICommand?` | `null` | Run after an invite was withdrawn, with the `TeamMembersInviteEventArgs` as the parameter. |
| `MemberRemovedCommand` | `ICommand?` | `null` | Run after a member was removed, with the `TeamMembersMemberEventArgs` as the parameter. |
| `MemberRoleChangedCommand` | `ICommand?` | `null` | Run after a role change was saved, with the `TeamMembersRoleChangedEventArgs` as the parameter. |
| `SeatsUsed` | `int` | – | *Read-only.* Seats taken: members plus pending invites. |
| `SeatsRemaining` | `int` | – | *Read-only.* Seats free: `SeatLimit` minus `SeatsUsed` (never below zero). |
| `SendCount` | `int` | – | *Read-only.* How many invites Send would send now: the chips plus a valid address being typed. |
| `IsSending` | `bool` | – | *Read-only.* True while the send handler runs. |
| `StatusText` | `string` | – | *Read-only.* The footer's text: the result of the last action (it stays until the next one). |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `InvitesSent` | `TeamMembersInvitesSentEventArgs` | Raised when invites went out (they are in the list already). |
| `InviteResent` | `TeamMembersInviteEventArgs` | Raised when an invite was sent again. |
| `InviteRevoked` | `TeamMembersInviteEventArgs` | Raised when an invite was withdrawn. |
| `MemberRemoved` | `TeamMembersMemberEventArgs` | Raised when a member was removed. |
| `MemberRoleChanged` | `TeamMembersRoleChangedEventArgs` | Raised when a role change was saved. |
| `ActionFailed` | `TeamMembersActionFailedEventArgs` | Raised when a handler threw (the block keeps the old state and shows the error). |

Pseudo-classes: `:framed`, `:narrow`, `:stacked`, `:actions-below`, `:two-tier`, `:full`, `:sending`, `:readonly`, `:status-error`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

### TeamMembersPerson

One member of the workspace shown by `TeamMembers`: an avatar (photo or initials, with a presence dot), the name and email, when the person was last active, and the role, which can be changed from the row's menu (the owner's cannot).

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Id` | `string?` | `null` | A stable key (rows keep their state across list changes); null uses the email. |
| `Name` | `string?` | `null` | The display name; the avatar's initials come from it when there is no photo. |
| `Email` | `string?` | `null` | The email address, shown under the name and matched by the search and the invite field. |
| `Avatar` | `ImageSource?` | `null` | The photo; null (or a photo that fails to load) shows the initials. |
| `IsOnline` | `bool` | `false` | Whether the presence dot shows on the avatar. |
| `LastActive` | `string?` | `null` | When the person was last active, already formatted ("Active now", "Active 3 hours ago"). |
| `Role` | `string?` | `null` | The key of the person's role among `Roles` (two-way: the row's menu writes it). |
| `IsOwner` | `bool` | `false` | The owner: the row shows the owner label instead of a role menu and has no remove button. |
| `IsCurrentUser` | `bool` | `false` | The person looking at the page: a muted "You" follows the name. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### TeamMembersInvite

An invite that was sent and not accepted yet: shown by `TeamMembers` under the members with a dashed avatar (initials from the address), the address, "role · detail" and the Resend and Revoke buttons. It takes a seat.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Id` | `string?` | `null` | A stable key; null uses the email. |
| `Email` | `string?` | `null` | The invited address. |
| `Role` | `string?` | `null` | The key of the role the person will get. |
| `Detail` | `string?` | `null` | The text after the role ("Invited Oct 7"); the block writes its own after a send or a resend. |
| `Initials` | `string?` | `null` | The avatar's letters; null takes the first letters of the address's name part (split at . _ -), at most two. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### TeamMembersRoleOption

A role people can be given: its key, the name shown on triggers and a line describing it in the menu.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Key` | `string?` | `null` | The key stored in `Role` and `Role`. |
| `Label` | `string?` | `null` | The name shown on the triggers, in the menu and in "role · detail". |
| `Description` | `string?` | `null` | The line under the name in the menu; null leaves it out. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### TeamMembersLabels

Every word `TeamMembers` shows or announces, in English by default. Replace the instance to translate or reword; texts with values are functions so that word order can change. Role names come from `Label`.

### TeamMembersSendRequest

What `SendInvitesAction` is asked to send.

### TeamMembersRoleChange

What `ChangeRoleAction` is asked to change.

## Accessibility

### Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Enter | In the field: turns the text into a chip, or sends when the field is empty. |
| , ; Space | In the field: turns the text into a chip. |
| Backspace | In an empty field: removes the last chip. |
| Enter, Space, Up, Down | On a role picker: opens the menu with the current role focused. |
| Up, Down, Home, End | In the role menu: moves; Enter or Space chooses, Escape closes. |
| Escape | In a row asking to confirm a removal: cancels it. In the search: clears it. |

### Screen readers and focus

- The block is a group named by its title, which is a level 2 heading; the two section headings are level 3 and name
  their lists.
- The seat bar is a read-only progress bar named "Seats" whose description reads "7 of 10 seats used".
- The field is named by `Labels.EmailFieldName`. Each chip is a list item named by its address, with a remove button
  named "Remove … from the invite list".
- The line under the field is announced politely when it warns or errs; every action's result is announced politely, and
  failures assertively.
- Role pickers are combo boxes named "Role for <name>" (or "Invite as") whose value is the role; menu items report which
  one is chosen.
- Remove, Resend and Revoke are named after the person or the address; after a resend the button says the invite went
  out again.
- Focus moves to Cancel when a confirmation opens, back to the remove button when it closes, and on to the next row after
  a removal or a revoke.

## Motion

- **Chips** pop in (scale 0.9 → 1 on a quick spring with a 100 ms fade and blur); the input and the other chips slide to
  their new places on a smooth spring. A removed chip shrinks and fades in 130 ms.
- **Sending**: the button spins while the handler runs. Then each address flies from its chip to its new pending row on a
  spring (visual duration 0.5 s, no bounce) on a pill whose tint fades out; the new rows grow on the smooth spring, the
  dashed avatars pop in 170 ms later and 100 ms apart, and the seat count and the counts roll.
- **Rows** enter and leave by growing and shrinking on the smooth spring (leaving rows fade in 120 ms). Search collapses
  the rows that do not match and brings them back with a 200 ms fade.
- **Text** that changes in place (the line under the field, a pending row's detail, the footer) lifts away with a blur and
  the new text rises in; the line under the field also springs its height. A changed role morphs letter by letter.
- **Seats**: the bar's fill follows the smooth spring and turns to the warning color in 240 ms.
- **Role menu**: opens from its trigger with a short scale and fade and closes faster; the chevron turns over.
- Reduced motion keeps the send button's spinner and short cross-fades; chips, rows, flights, counts and the bar jump.
  Off applies every change at once.

## Related

- Invite people, Team directory and Roles and permissions, the other People blocks.
- `Avatar`, `SearchField`, `TextMorph` and `Button`, the controls the block is made of.
- `TagInput` for chips outside an invite flow.

# Invite people

> Invite people by name or email into a workspace, with a role for each, a seat meter against the plan, and avatars that fly from the suggestions into chips and on into a pending list.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc.Blocks`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc.Blocks --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/blocks/invite-people

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.InvitePeoplePreviewDemo">
    <!--
        The Lumen Labs workspace (InvitePeopleDemoData): five on the team, Theo invited three days ago, ten people who can
        be invited and the Basic plan with ten seats. Sending is simulated (InvitePeopleSimulation): invites are delivered
        after 680 ms, 160 ms apart, and the first person of the first send accepts after 3.5 s. The reset button starts over.
    -->
    <arc:InvitePeople x:Name="Block" Margin="0,12" IsResetVisible="True" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class InvitePeoplePreviewDemo : UserControl
{
    public InvitePeoplePreviewDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        InvitePeopleDemoData.Fill(Block);
        _ = new InvitePeopleSimulation(Block);
    }
}
```

## When to use

`InvitePeople` is the form behind an "Invite people" button: one field that takes names and addresses, a check on seats,
and the invites that are still waiting. People found in the directory become chips with their portrait and a role;
anything that cannot be invited becomes a red chip that says why. Send moves the chips into the pending list, where each
invite can be sent again or revoked, and an accepted invite leaves the list and joins the team avatars at the top.

- **Inviting several people at once.** Type a few letters to pick people from the directory, type an address, or paste
  a whole list from a spreadsheet or an email: commas, semicolons and line breaks separate the entries.
- **Seats that cost money.** The meter counts members, pending invites and the new chips against the plan. When the
  count runs over, Send is held back and the next plan is offered right there.
- **A dialog or a settings page.** Framed, the block is a card at most 600 wide; flat, it sits inside a surface of your
  own.

## When not to use

- **Managing the people who already joined.** Use `Team members` for roles, removal and seat changes of members.
- **Editing what a role can do.** Use `Roles and permissions`.
- **Plain tags.** When the entries are not people (labels, keywords, recipients without a directory), use `TagInput`.

## Usage

The block derives from Avalonia's `TemplatedControl`. People are `InvitePeoplePerson` objects (name, email, job title and
an optional portrait; without one the avatar shows initials). `Directory` holds everyone who can be found, `Members` the
team and `PendingInvites` the invites that are waiting; a directory person who is in the team or has an invite shows as
unavailable in the suggestions. `Roles` and `Plans` fill the role menu and the seat meter.

```xml
<arc:InvitePeople Title="Invite people"
                  Description="Bring people into Lumen Labs by name or email"
                  WorkspaceName="Lumen Labs">
    <arc:InvitePeople.Roles>
        <arc:InvitePeopleRole Name="Admin" Description="People, billing and settings" />
        <arc:InvitePeopleRole Name="Member" Description="Works on every project" IsDefault="True" />
        <arc:InvitePeopleRole Name="Guest" Description="Sees only shared projects" />
    </arc:InvitePeople.Roles>
    <arc:InvitePeople.Plans>
        <arc:InvitePeoplePlan Name="Basic" SeatLimit="10" />
        <arc:InvitePeoplePlan Name="Growth" SeatLimit="25" />
    </arc:InvitePeople.Plans>
    <arc:InvitePeoplePerson Name="Clara Weiss" Email="clara.weiss@lumen.example" Title="Brand designer" />
    <arc:InvitePeoplePerson Name="Mateus Rocha" Email="mateus.rocha@lumen.example" Title="Backend engineer" />
</arc:InvitePeople>
```

### Anatomy

- **Header**: `Title`, `Description` and the team's avatars (five at most, then a "+N" pill). In a narrow block the
  avatars move under the title.
- **Field**: the chips and a text box that wrap onto as many lines as they need; the field's height follows on a spring.
  Under it a hint, and a button that pastes `SampleText` when you set one.
- **Error panel**: opens when chips cannot be invited, with one line per chip and a button that removes them all.
- **Seats**: "8 of 10 seats", the plan's name, a meter with three segments (members, pending, new) and a legend. Over the
  limit the count and the new segment turn red and a line offers the next plan.
- **Footer**: the reset button (when `IsResetVisible`) and Send, whose label counts the chips.
- **Pending**: the invites, newest first, each with its status, a resend button and a revoke button.

### Adding people

Typing filters the directory by name or email (the job title is not searched); people who can be invited come first and
unavailable ones after them, five at most (`MaxSuggestions`). An empty field shows four people to start with
(`SuggestedCount`). A complete address that is not in the directory offers "Invite by email". Enter or a click picks the
highlighted person; Enter without one, a comma or a semicolon turns the text into chips.

Pasting a list (or calling `AddText`) recognizes directory names and addresses, new addresses and `Name <address>`; it
skips duplicates and adds entries that cannot be invited as red chips. The hint under the field shows a summary for a few
seconds. Selecting a red chip puts its text back into the field to fix it.

### Sending

Set `SendAction` to the work Send starts. It receives the new pending rows (status `Sending`) and a cancellation token.
Call `MarkDelivered` for each invite as it goes out; the rows that are still sending when the task completes are marked
sent. When someone accepts, call `MarkJoined`: the row says "Joined", leaves a moment later, and the person joins
`Members` with their avatar flying into the header. An exception takes the rows back and returns the chips to the field.

```csharp
// Your mail call; here it only waits.
static Task SendInviteAsync(string email, string? role, CancellationToken token) => Task.Delay(300, token);

invite.SendAction = async (request, token) =>
{
    foreach (var pending in request.Invites)
    {
        await SendInviteAsync(pending.Person!.Email!, pending.Role?.Name, token);
        invite.MarkDelivered(pending);
    }
};
invite.InviteJoined += (_, e) => log.Info($"{e.Invite.Person?.DisplayName} joined");
```

Send is held back (it stays focusable and says why) while chips need fixing or the seats run over; pressing it shakes the
red chips or the over-limit line instead. `ResendAction`, `RevokeAction` and `UpgradeAction` work the same way for the
row buttons and the upgrade button. The demo below fails every second send, and revoking Theo's invite fails, so the row
comes back.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.InvitePeopleFailureDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12" Margin="0,12">
        <arc:InvitePeople x:Name="Block" />
        <TextBlock x:Name="Log"
                   HorizontalAlignment="Center"
                   TextAlignment="Center"
                   TextWrapping="Wrap"
                   MaxWidth="560"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}"
                   Text="Every second send fails after a second, as a busy mail service could; so does revoking Theo's invite." />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class InvitePeopleFailureDemo : UserControl
{
    private int _sends;

    public InvitePeopleFailureDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        var people = InvitePeopleDemoData.Fill(Block);
        Block.SampleText = null;

        // The second, fourth, ... send is refused: the rows are taken back and the chips return to the field.
        Block.SendAction = async (request, token) =>
        {
            await Task.Delay(1000, token);
            if (++_sends % 2 == 0)
            {
                throw new InvalidOperationException("The mail service is busy. Try again in a minute.");
            }
            foreach (var invite in request.Invites)
            {
                Block.MarkDelivered(invite);
            }
        };
        // Revoking Theo's invite fails, so his row comes back.
        Block.RevokeAction = async (invite, token) =>
        {
            await Task.Delay(600, token);
            if (ReferenceEquals(invite.Person, people.Theo))
            {
                throw new InvalidOperationException("Theo's invite was already accepted on another device.");
            }
        };
        Block.UpgradeAction = (_, token) => Task.Delay(500, token);

        Block.SendFailed += (_, e) => Log.Text = $"Send {e.Request.Attempt} failed: {e.Exception.Message}";
        Block.InvitesSent += (_, e) => Log.Text = $"Send {e.Request.Attempt} went through";
        Block.InviteRevoked += (_, e) => Log.Text = $"Revoking {e.Invite.Person?.DisplayName}…";
    }
}
```

### State and events

`Entries` lists the chips, `SeatsUsed` and `IsOverLimit` can be bound, and `CurrentPlan` is two-way. `EntriesChanged`,
`RoleChanged`, `InvitesSent`, `SendFailed`, `InviteJoined`, `InviteResent`, `InviteRevoked` and `PlanUpgraded` report what
happened. `Reset()` puts the block back as it first appeared and raises `ResetPerformed`.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.InvitePeopleEventLogDemo">
    <!-- The seat count and the over-limit flag are bound; every event the block raises is written to the log. -->
    <StackPanel Spacing="12" Margin="0,12">
        <arc:InvitePeople x:Name="Block" />
        <TextBlock HorizontalAlignment="Center"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}"
                   Text="{Binding #Block.SeatsUsed, StringFormat='Seats used: {0}'}" />
        <TextBlock HorizontalAlignment="Center"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}"
                   Text="{Binding #Block.IsOverLimit, StringFormat='Over the limit: {0}'}" />
        <TextBlock x:Name="Log"
                   HorizontalAlignment="Center"
                   TextAlignment="Center"
                   TextWrapping="Wrap"
                   MaxWidth="560"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}"
                   Text="Add people, change a role, send, resend or revoke: the latest events show here." />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class InvitePeopleEventLogDemo : UserControl
{
    private readonly List<string> _lines = new();

    public InvitePeopleEventLogDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        InvitePeopleDemoData.Fill(Block);
        Block.SampleText = null;
        _ = new InvitePeopleSimulation(Block) { AcceptsOnce = false };

        Block.EntriesChanged += (_, e) => Write($"Chips: {e.Entries.Count} ({e.ValidCount} can be invited)");
        Block.RoleChanged += (_, e) => Write($"{e.Entry.Text}: {e.OldRole?.Name} → {e.NewRole?.Name}");
        Block.InvitesSent += (_, e) => Write($"Sent {e.Request.Invites.Count} (attempt {e.Request.Attempt})");
        Block.InviteResent += (_, e) => Write($"Resent to {e.Invite.Person?.DisplayName}");
        Block.InviteRevoked += (_, e) => Write($"Revoked {e.Invite.Person?.DisplayName}");
        Block.PlanUpgraded += (_, e) => Write($"Plan: {e.OldPlan?.Name} → {e.NewPlan.Name}");
    }

    private void Write(string line)
    {
        _lines.Insert(0, line);
        if (_lines.Count > 4)
        {
            _lines.RemoveAt(_lines.Count - 1);
        }
        Log.Text = string.Join("\n", _lines);
    }
}
```

### Other words

Every text is in `Labels` (`InvitePeopleLabels`), in English by default: placeholders, the hint, the error reasons, the
seat line, the button names and every announcement. Texts with values are functions, so word order can change.

## API reference

### InvitePeople

A form for inviting people to a workspace. Type a name or an address and pick from the directory, or paste a whole list: every person becomes a chip with a role, and entries that cannot be invited become red chips that say why (select one to fix it). A seat meter counts members, pending invites and the new chips against the plan, and offers the next plan when they run over. Send moves the chips into the pending list below, where each invite can be sent again or revoked; when an invite is accepted its row leaves and the person joins the team avatars in the header. Server work goes through `SendAction`, `ResendAction`, `RevokeAction` and `UpgradeAction`; `MarkDelivered` and `MarkJoined` report what happened later.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Title` | `string?` | `"Invite people"` | The heading; null leaves it out. |
| `Description` | `string?` | `null` | The line under the heading; null leaves it out. |
| `WorkspaceName` | `string?` | `null` | The workspace people join (used in the announcement when someone accepts). |
| `DirectorySource` | `IEnumerable?` | `null` | The people who can be found by name or email, when you give them as a list to follow; it wins over `Directory`. |
| `Roles` | `AvaloniaList<InvitePeopleRole>` | `null` | The roles a chip can get, in menu order; empty leaves the role buttons out. |
| `Plans` | `AvaloniaList<InvitePeoplePlan>` | `null` | The plans, smallest first: the next one after `CurrentPlan` is offered when the seats run over. |
| `CurrentPlan` | `InvitePeoplePlan?` | `null` | The plan in use; its seat limit is the meter's maximum. Null uses the first of `Plans`. |
| `MaxSuggestions` | `int` | `5` | How many people a query lists at most (5). |
| `SuggestedCount` | `int` | `4` | How many people the "Suggested" list of an empty field shows (4). |
| `SampleText` | `string?` | `null` | A list the "Paste a sample list" button pastes; null hides the button. |
| `ExampleDomain` | `string?` | `null` | The example domain of the "incomplete domain" message; null takes the domain of the first directory address. |
| `SendAction` | `Func<InvitePeopleSendRequest, CancellationToken, Task>?` | `null` | Sends the invites (called after the rows were added as "Sending"). Report deliveries with `MarkDelivered`; rows still sending when the task completes are marked sent. An exception takes the rows back and returns the chips to the field. Null sends nothing and marks the rows sent at once. |
| `ResendAction` | `Func<InvitePeoplePendingInvite, CancellationToken, Task>?` | `null` | Sends one invite again; an exception keeps the button as it was and announces the failure. |
| `RevokeAction` | `Func<InvitePeoplePendingInvite, CancellationToken, Task>?` | `null` | Revokes one invite (the row leaves first); an exception puts the row back. |
| `UpgradeAction` | `Func<InvitePeoplePlan, CancellationToken, Task>?` | `null` | Moves the workspace to the given plan; the block switches when the task completes. An exception keeps the plan. |
| `SendCommand` | `ICommand?` | `null` | Runs with the `InvitePeopleSendRequest` as its parameter when invites are sent, before `SendAction`. |
| `IsFramed` | `bool` | `true` | True (default) draws a card at most 600 wide with a border; false lays the block flat at the container's width. |
| `IsResetVisible` | `bool` | `false` | Shows the reset button beside Send (it calls `Reset`). |
| `Labels` | `InvitePeopleLabels` | – | Every word the block shows or announces. |
| `Entries` | `IReadOnlyList<InvitePeopleEntry>` | – | *Read-only.* The chips in the field, in order. |
| `SeatsUsed` | `int` | – | *Read-only.* Seats in use: members, pending invites and the chips that can be invited. |
| `IsOverLimit` | `bool` | – | *Read-only.* True when `SeatsUsed` is more than the plan's limit (Send is held back). |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `EntriesChanged` | `InvitePeopleEntriesChangedEventArgs` | The chips changed (added, removed, a role changed). |
| `RoleChanged` | `InvitePeopleRoleChangedEventArgs` | A chip's role was picked from its menu. |
| `InvitesSent` | `InvitePeopleInvitesSentEventArgs` | Invites went out (`SendAction` completed). |
| `SendFailed` | `InvitePeopleSendFailedEventArgs` | `SendAction` threw; the rows were taken back and the chips are in the field again. |
| `InviteJoined` | `InvitePeopleInviteEventArgs` | An accepted invite left the list and its person joined the team (`Members`). |
| `InviteResent` | `InvitePeopleInviteEventArgs` | An invite was sent again. |
| `InviteRevoked` | `InvitePeopleInviteEventArgs` | An invite was revoked. |
| `PlanUpgraded` | `InvitePeoplePlanUpgradedEventArgs` | The plan changed after an upgrade. |
| `ResetPerformed` | `RoutedEventArgs` | `Reset` ran (the reset button or code); simulations that drive the block should stop. |

Pseudo-classes: `:framed`, `:compact`, `:narrow`, `:over`, `:field-focused`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

### InvitePeoplePerson

A person `InvitePeople` knows: someone in the workspace directory, a member of the team, or the person an invite went to. People are matched by `Email` (case-insensitive), so the same address in `Directory` and `Members` is the same person.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Name` | `string?` | `null` | The full name ("Clara Weiss"); suggestions match it as a substring, a pasted full name finds the person. |
| `Email` | `string?` | `null` | The email address; the person's identity and what an invite is sent to. |
| `Title` | `string?` | `null` | The job title shown at the end of a suggestion ("Brand designer"); it is not searched. |
| `Avatar` | `ImageSource?` | `null` | The portrait; null shows the initials on the muted surface. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### InvitePeopleRole

A role an invited person can get (a line of the role menu).

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Name` | `string?` | `null` | The role's name, shown on the chip's role button and in the pending row ("Member"). |
| `Description` | `string?` | `null` | The second line of the role menu (what the role can do). |
| `IsDefault` | `bool` | `false` | True for the role new chips start with (the first role marked default wins; none marked = the first role). |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### InvitePeoplePlan

A plan with a seat limit. `Plans` lists them smallest first: the upgrade path.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Name` | `string?` | `null` | The plan's name ("Basic"); the seat line says "{name} plan". |
| `SeatLimit` | `int` | `10` | How many seats the plan has: members, pending invites and new invites together. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### InvitePeoplePendingInvite

An invite waiting to be accepted: a row of the pending list. It takes a seat until it is revoked or accepted.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Person` | `InvitePeoplePerson?` | `null` | The invited person (a directory person, or one made from a typed address). |
| `Role` | `InvitePeopleRole?` | `null` | The role the person will join with. |
| `Status` | `InvitePeopleInviteStatus` | `Sent` | Sending, sent or joined. |
| `SentText` | `string?` | `null` | When it was sent, in words ("2 days ago"); null says "just now". The row shows "Sent {SentText}". |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### InvitePeopleEntry

A chip in the field: a person to invite with a role, or an entry that cannot be invited (with the text as typed and the reason). Selecting an invalid chip puts its text back into the field for editing.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Role` | `InvitePeopleRole?` | `null` | The role the person will be invited with (valid entries only). |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### InvitePeopleSendRequest

What `SendAction` receives: the invites that were just added to the pending list.

## Accessibility

- The text box is named "Email or name" and described by the hint. The suggestion list is not focusable: the text box
  keeps the focus while the highlight moves, and unavailable people say why.
- A red chip's button is named "Edit {entry}. {reason}"; the remove buttons say which chip they remove; a role button says
  whose role it is and what it is now.
- The seat meter is named "Seats used" and its value reads "8 of 10 seats" (with how many are over the limit).
- Send is named by its count ("Send 3 invites"). When it is held back it describes the reason: the error panel's title or
  the seat count over the limit.
- After a revoke the focus moves to the Pending heading. The team avatars are one group ("Team, 6 people"); the "+N" pill
  reads "and N more".
- A polite live region announces each step: added and removed people, the paste summary, a marked chip, role changes,
  why Send is held back, sending and sent, an accepted invite, a resend, a revoke, an upgrade and a reset.

### Keyboard

- **Arrow Down** in the field opens the suggestions (the starting list when it is empty); **Arrow Up** and **Arrow Down**
  move the highlight and skip unavailable people. **Enter** adds the highlighted person, or turns the text into chips when
  nothing is highlighted. **Comma** and **semicolon** turn the text into chips. **Escape** closes the list, then clears
  the text.
- **Backspace** in an empty field marks the last chip; a second **Backspace** removes it. Typing anything clears the mark.
- **Tab** goes through each chip's role and remove buttons, then the field, the paste button, the error panel's button,
  the upgrade button, reset, Send and each pending row's resend and revoke buttons.
- On a role button, **Enter**, **Space** or **Arrow Down** opens the role menu with the focus on the current role.
  **Arrow Up** and **Arrow Down** wrap, **Home** and **End** jump, **Enter** or **Space** picks, and **Escape** closes;
  the focus returns to the role button.

## Motion

- **Avatars fly**: from the suggestion into the new chip, from the chip into its pending row when you send, and from an
  accepted row into the team in the header, each on one spring (about 600 ms) while the source is already gone.
- **Layout**: chips and the text box spring to new places as chips come and go, the field's height and everything under
  it follow on a smooth spring, and pending rows open and close the same way (a closing row also fades in 130 ms).
- **Suggestions**: the list rises 4 px and grows from 0.98; the highlight glides between rows. The role menu enters the
  same way from its button.
- **Numbers and words**: seat counts, the pending count and Send's count roll; words that change (a role, the plan, Send's
  noun, a row's status, "Sent again") cross-fade with a short blur while their width springs.
- **Refusals**: a red chip shakes once when it appears, and the red chips (or the over-limit line) shake when Send is
  pressed while it is held back: 6, 6, 4, 4, 2 px over 420 ms.
- Reduced motion places everything at once and keeps only the short fades and color changes; there are no flights, no
  shakes and no springs. Off applies every change at once.

## Related

- `Team members`, `Roles and permissions`, `Team directory` and `Profile page`, the other People blocks.
- `TagInput` for plain tags, `Avatar` and `AvatarGroup` for portraits, `UsageMeter` for a standalone meter.

# Team directory

> A company directory with search, team filters and the picked person's profile beside the list, from bio and status to an email address to copy.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc.Blocks`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc.Blocks --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/blocks/team-directory

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.TeamDirectoryPreviewDemo">
    <!-- Six people in three teams; copying an address uses the system clipboard. Data: TeamDirectoryDemoData. -->
    <arc:TeamDirectory x:Name="Directory" Margin="0,12" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class TeamDirectoryPreviewDemo : UserControl
{
    public TeamDirectoryPreviewDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Directory.People.AddRange(TeamDirectoryDemoData.People());
    }
}
```

## When to use

`TeamDirectory` is the page where colleagues look each other up. The list on the left narrows as you type and as you pick a
team; the right side shows one person in full: a short bio, whether they are around, their team, what they work on, where
they are and an email address with a copy button.

- **An internal people page.** Everyone in the company or a department, searchable by name, role, team or city.
- **A team page with departments.** The team buttons give a one-click view of each department with fixed head counts.
- **A contact picker that shows context.** Pick someone, read who they are, and copy their address, or react to
  `PersonSelected` to open their full profile elsewhere.

## When not to use

- **Managing members.** Changing roles, inviting people or removing them belongs in Team members or Roles and
  permissions; this block only reads.
- **A public team section.** A marketing page with large portraits and short quotes wants an image-led layout, not a
  searchable list.
- **Large tables of people.** Hundreds of rows with sorting and columns are a `DataGrid` job. The directory filters in
  memory and lays out every row; for big organizations, filter on the server and give the block one page of people.

## Usage

The block derives from Avalonia's `TemplatedControl`. Each person is a `TeamDirectoryPerson`, an `AvaloniaObject` with a
name, a role, a team, an availability, the current work, a city with a time zone, an email address, a bio and an optional
portrait (initials show without one). Changing a field updates the row, the profile and the matches.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:TeamDirectory x:Name="Directory">
        <arc:TeamDirectoryPerson Id="lena" Name="Lena Hartmann" Role="Interaction designer" Team="Design"
                                 Focus="Checkout redesign" City="Vienna" TimeZone="CET"
                                 Email="lena@northwind.test"
                                 Bio="Turns rough ideas into flows people can follow." />
        <arc:TeamDirectoryPerson Id="theo" Name="Theo Brandt" Role="Mobile engineer" Team="Engineering"
                                 Availability="Away" City="Manchester" TimeZone="GMT"
                                 Email="theo@northwind.test" />
    </arc:TeamDirectory>
</UserControl>
```

### Anatomy

- **Header**: the title with the number of people (always the total) and a search box with a clear button.
- **Team buttons**: All first, then each team with its total. A soft pill sits behind the pressed button and glides to the
  next one.
- **List**: one row per match: avatar with an availability dot, name and role. The row whose profile shows sits on a
  highlight that glides from row to row.
- **Profile**: a large avatar, name and role, the bio, and the fields Status, Team, Working on, Location (city and time
  zone) and Email (a mail link and a copy button). Empty fields are left out.

### Search and teams

Search runs on every keystroke. The text is trimmed and compared without regard to case, as one piece, with the name, the
role, the team and the city: "lena hart" finds Lena Hartmann, "hartmann lena" does not, and "operations" also finds people
whose role does not say it but whose team does. Accents are not folded, so "malmo" does not find Malmö. Set `SearchFilter`
to search differently; it receives each person and the text as typed.

The team buttons come from `Teams` when you fill it, otherwise from the people in order of first appearance. Their numbers
are totals and do not follow the search. `SelectedTeam` (null for All) and `SearchText` are two-way and independent:
changing one keeps the other. `MatchCount` and `VisiblePeople` tell what is listed.

### The person shown

`SelectedPersonId` holds the key of the person picked (their `Id`, or their name without one); only a pick, Enter or Space
on a row, or your code changes it. `DisplayedPerson` is the person whose profile shows: the picked one while they match,
otherwise the first match. Filter the picked person out and the first match shows; bring them back and they show again.
`PersonSelected` and `PersonSelectedCommand` report picks only, never the fallback, and not a second pick of the same
person. `SelectPerson` shows someone from code without raising the event.

```csharp
directory.PersonSelected += (_, e) => navigator.Open($"/people/{e.Person.Id}");
directory.SelectedTeam = "Engineering";
directory.SelectPerson("jonas");
```

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.TeamDirectoryBoundStateDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12" Margin="0,12">
        <arc:TeamDirectory x:Name="Directory" />
        <WrapPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center">
            <arc:Button x:Name="ShowFiona" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Content="Show Fiona" Margin="4" />
            <arc:Button x:Name="ShowEngineering" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Content="Engineering only" Margin="4" />
            <arc:Button x:Name="SearchMunich" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Content="Search &quot;munich&quot;" Margin="4" />
            <arc:Button x:Name="Reset" Variant="Ghost" Size="Small" Content="Clear filters" Margin="4" />
        </WrapPanel>
        <TextBlock x:Name="State" HorizontalAlignment="Center" TextAlignment="Center" TextWrapping="Wrap" />
        <ItemsControl x:Name="Log" HorizontalAlignment="Center" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using System.Collections.ObjectModel;
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class TeamDirectoryBoundStateDemo : UserControl
{
    private readonly ObservableCollection<string> _log = new();

    public TeamDirectoryBoundStateDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Directory.People.AddRange(TeamDirectoryDemoData.People());
        Log.ItemsSource = _log;

        // Picks from the list arrive as PersonSelected; the buttons below drive the same state from code without it.
        Directory.PersonSelected += (_, e) => Add($"Picked {e.Person.Name} (was {e.PreviousPerson?.Name ?? "nobody"})");
        Directory.EmailCopied += (_, e) => Add(e.Succeeded ? $"Copied {e.Email}" : $"Could not copy {e.Email}");
        Directory.PropertyChanged += (_, e) =>
        {
            if (e.Property == TeamDirectory.SelectedTeamProperty || e.Property == TeamDirectory.SearchTextProperty
                || e.Property == TeamDirectory.DisplayedPersonProperty || e.Property == TeamDirectory.SelectedPersonIdProperty)
            {
                ShowState();
            }
        };

        ShowFiona.Click += (_, _) => Directory.SelectPerson("fiona");
        ShowEngineering.Click += (_, _) => Directory.SelectedTeam = "Engineering";
        SearchMunich.Click += (_, _) => Directory.SearchText = "munich";
        Reset.Click += (_, _) => Directory.ClearFilters();
        ShowState();
    }

    private void ShowState()
    {
        var team = Directory.SelectedTeam ?? "all teams";
        var search = string.IsNullOrEmpty(Directory.SearchText) ? "no search" : $"search “{Directory.SearchText}”";
        var shown = Directory.DisplayedPerson?.Name ?? "nobody";
        var picked = Directory.SelectedPersonId ?? "none yet";
        State.Text = $"{team} · {search} · {Directory.MatchCount} shown · profile: {shown} · picked id: {picked}";
    }

    private void Add(string line)
    {
        _log.Insert(0, line);
        while (_log.Count > 5)
        {
            _log.RemoveAt(_log.Count - 1);
        }
    }
}
```

### Nobody matches

When nobody matches, the list says so with the search text and offers Clear filters, which empties the search and shows
every team again (the pick is kept); the profile area shows a short hint instead of a person. `ClearFilters()` does the
same from code.

### Copying an email address

The copy button copies the shown person's address and then reads Copied (with a check) or Retry for `CopyResetDelay`
(1.8 seconds) before it rests again; a status message tells screen readers how it went. By default it writes to the
system clipboard. Set `CopyAsync` to copy another way (a remote session, an audit call): an exception shows Retry, and
`EmailCopied` reports every attempt with the person, the address and the error. The address itself is a mail link;
`EmailLinkClicked` fires first, and setting `Handled` stops the mailto: link from opening.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.TeamDirectoryCopyFailureDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12" Margin="0,12">
        <arc:TeamDirectory x:Name="Directory" />
        <TextBlock x:Name="Log"
                   HorizontalAlignment="Center"
                   TextAlignment="Center"
                   TextWrapping="Wrap"
                   MaxWidth="560"
                   Text="Copying goes through a slow service here, and every second attempt fails. Press Copy a few times." />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class TeamDirectoryCopyFailureDemo : UserControl
{
    private int _attempts;

    public TeamDirectoryCopyFailureDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Directory.People.AddRange(TeamDirectoryDemoData.People());

        // Stand-in for a remote clipboard or an audit call: it takes half a second and refuses every second request.
        // The button stays as it is while the call runs, then shows Copied or Retry for 1.8 seconds.
        Directory.CopyAsync = async (email, cancellation) =>
        {
            await Task.Delay(500, cancellation);
            _attempts++;
            if (_attempts % 2 == 0)
            {
                throw new InvalidOperationException("The clipboard service is busy.");
            }
        };
        Directory.EmailCopied += (_, e) => Log.Text = e.Succeeded
            ? $"Attempt {_attempts}: copied {e.Email}."
            : $"Attempt {_attempts}: {e.Error?.Message ?? "failed"} The button offers a retry.";
    }
}
```

### Narrow containers

The block reads its own width, not the window's. At 640 or less the profile tightens and the copy button shows only its
glyph; at 500 or less the profile moves under the list and the button shows its label again; at 400 or less the search box
takes its own line under the title and the team counts are hidden.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.TeamDirectoryNarrowDemo">
    <!-- 380 wide: the profile stacks under the list, the search box moves under the title and the team counts hide. -->
    <arc:TeamDirectory x:Name="Directory" Width="380" HorizontalAlignment="Center" Margin="0,12" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs

    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Directory.People.AddRange(TeamDirectoryDemoData.People());

```

### Framed or flat

`IsFramed` (the default) draws a card with a 1px border and a 16 radius. Set it to false to place the directory flat on a
page or in a pane. `IsSearchVisible` and `IsFilterVisible` hide the search box and the team buttons; `Labels` takes a
`TeamDirectoryLabels` with every word and screen reader text, to translate or reword them.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.TeamDirectoryFlatDemo">
    <!-- No frame, a fixed team order and a search that also looks at email addresses. -->
    <Border BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Border}" BorderThickness="0,1" Margin="0,12">
        <arc:TeamDirectory x:Name="Directory" IsFramed="False">
            <arc:TeamDirectory.Teams>
                <x:String>Engineering</x:String>
                <x:String>Support</x:String>
                <x:String>Design</x:String>
                <x:String>Operations</x:String>
            </arc:TeamDirectory.Teams>
        </arc:TeamDirectory>
    </Border>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class TeamDirectoryFlatDemo : UserControl
{
    public TeamDirectoryFlatDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Directory.People.AddRange(TeamDirectoryDemoData.LargerDirectory());

        // The default search covers name, role, team and city; this one adds the email address.
        Directory.SearchFilter = (person, text) =>
        {
            var query = text.Trim();
            return query.Length == 0
                   || (person.Name + " " + person.Role + " " + person.Team + " " + person.City + " " + person.Email)
                      .Contains(query, StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase);
        };
    }
}
```

## API reference

### TeamDirectory

A company directory: a searchable list of people with team filters on one side and the profile of the person picked on the other (bio, status, team, current work, location and an email address to copy). Search matches the name, role, team and city as you type; the team buttons show fixed totals; the selection is kept by `Id`, so when the picked person is filtered out the first match shows and the picked person comes back when they match again. Rows that stay glide to their new places, rows that leave fade where they were, and the profile cross-fades. Narrow blocks stack the profile under the list.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `PeopleSource` | `IEnumerable?` | `null` | The people, when you give them as a list to follow (observed when it raises collection changes); it wins over `People`. |
| `SelectedTeam` | `string?` | `null` | The team shown (two-way); null shows every team. The search is kept when it changes. |
| `SearchText` | `string` | `""` | The search text (two-way), applied on every keystroke; the team filter is kept when it changes. |
| `SelectedPersonId` | `string?` | `null` | The `Key` of the person picked (two-way); only a pick or code changes it. Null, or a person not among the matches, shows the first match (see `DisplayedPerson`) without changing it. |
| `SearchFilter` | `Func<TeamDirectoryPerson, string, bool>?` | `null` | Decides whether a person matches the search text (the untrimmed text as typed); null matches the trimmed text, ignoring case, as one piece of the name, role, team or city. |
| `CopyAsync` | `Func<string, CancellationToken, Task>?` | `null` | Copies an email address: awaited when the copy button is pressed, with the address and a token that is cancelled when the block leaves the window. An exception shows Retry; null copies to the system clipboard. |
| `CopyResetDelay` | `TimeSpan` | `00:00:01.8000000` | How long the copy button shows Copied or Retry before it rests again. |
| `Labels` | `TeamDirectoryLabels` | – | Every word the block shows or announces. |
| `IsSearchVisible` | `bool` | `true` | Whether the header shows the search box. |
| `IsFilterVisible` | `bool` | `true` | Whether the team buttons show under the header. |
| `IsFramed` | `bool` | `true` | Draws a bordered card with rounded corners (true); false lays the block flat at the container's width. |
| `PersonSelectedCommand` | `ICommand?` | `null` | Run when the person picks someone from the list, with the `TeamDirectoryPerson` as the parameter. |
| `DisplayedPerson` | `TeamDirectoryPerson?` | – | *Read-only.* The person whose profile shows: the picked person while they match, otherwise the first match, otherwise null. |
| `MatchCount` | `int` | – | *Read-only.* How many people match the team filter and the search. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `PersonSelected` | `TeamDirectoryPersonSelectedEventArgs` | Raised when the person picks someone from the list (click, Enter or Space) and the pick changes. Not raised when the shown person changes because of the filter or the search, nor for `SelectPerson`. |
| `EmailCopied` | `TeamDirectoryEmailCopiedEventArgs` | Raised after the copy button tried to copy an email address, whether it worked or not. |
| `EmailLinkClicked` | `TeamDirectoryPersonEventArgs` | Raised when the profile's email address is pressed; unless a handler sets Handled, a mailto: link opens. |

Pseudo-classes: `:framed`, `:narrow`, `:stacked`, `:compact`, `:empty-results`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

### TeamDirectoryPerson

One person in a `TeamDirectory`: who they are, which team they belong to and how to reach them. The name, role, team and city are searched; the other fields only show in the profile. Changing a field updates the block.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Id` | `string?` | `null` | The stable key the selection is kept by; null or empty uses `Name`. |
| `Name` | `string` | `""` | The full name (searched; the first line of the row and the profile heading). |
| `Role` | `string` | `""` | The job title (searched; the second line of the row and the line under the profile heading). |
| `Team` | `string` | `""` | The team (searched; the key of the team filter and the profile's Team field). |
| `Availability` | `TeamDirectoryAvailability` | `Available` | Whether the person is available (the avatar's dot and the profile's Status field). |
| `Focus` | `string?` | `null` | What the person works on now, a few words (the profile's Working on field; not searched). |
| `City` | `string?` | `null` | Where the person works (searched; the profile's Location field). |
| `TimeZone` | `string?` | `null` | A short time zone name shown after the city ("CET"); plain text, not a clock, not searched. |
| `Email` | `string?` | `null` | The email address: a mail link in the profile and what the copy button copies (not searched). |
| `Bio` | `string?` | `null` | A sentence or two about the person, under the profile heading (not searched). |
| `Avatar` | `ImageSource?` | `null` | The portrait; null shows the initials of `Name`. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### TeamDirectoryLabels

Every word `TeamDirectory` shows or announces, in English by default. Replace the instance to translate or reword; texts with values in them are functions so that word order can change.

### TeamDirectoryPersonSelectedEventArgs

Arguments of `PersonSelected`: the person picked and the one shown before.

Derives from `RoutedEventArgs`: every member of `RoutedEventArgs` works as well.

### TeamDirectoryEmailCopiedEventArgs

Arguments of `EmailCopied`: whose address was copied and whether it worked.

Derives from `RoutedEventArgs`: every member of `RoutedEventArgs` works as well.

### TeamDirectoryPersonEventArgs

Arguments of an event about one person (`EmailLinkClicked`).

Derives from `RoutedEventArgs`: every member of `RoutedEventArgs` works as well.

## Accessibility

- **Tab** goes from the search box (and its clear button while there is text) to each team button, each row, the email
  link and the copy button. Every row and every team button is its own stop.
- **Enter** or **Space** presses a team button, picks a row, or presses the copy button.
- **Escape** in the search box empties it and keeps the focus there; with an empty box it is left to the page.
- The clear button empties the search and puts the focus back in the box. Clear filters moves the focus to the search box
  when it had it, instead of dropping it with the message.
- The team buttons and rows are toggle buttons: screen readers hear the pressed team and the row whose profile shows as
  pressed. The team buttons form a named group ("Team filter") and each reads its team and total ("Design, 2"); the list
  is named ("Directory").
- A row reads the name and the role; its avatar reads the name and whether the person is online or away.
- The profile area is a polite live region, so the new person is read when it changes; the profile is named with the
  name and role.
- The copy button is named "Copy email address" and becomes "Email address copied" after a copy; the outcome is also
  announced, and the announcement is cleared when the button rests.
- Every word and name is in `Labels`.

## Motion

| What | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| Team pill moving to the pressed button | Spring (visual duration .42, no bounce), position and width | Jumps | Jumps |
| Row highlight moving to the shown row | Same spring | Jumps | Jumps |
| Rows that stay when the matches change | Glide to their new place on the same spring | Jump | Jump |
| Rows that leave | Fade out where they were in 170ms, taking no space | Removed at once | Removed at once |
| Rows that arrive | Fade in in place in 150ms | Appear | Appear |
| Profile change | Old fades out in 180ms; new fades in over 220ms and rises 4px | Swaps | Swaps |
| Copy confirmation | Glyphs cross-fade in 160ms and scale on a 580ms spring; colors change at once | Colors and glyph at once | At once |
| Hover and focus colors | 160ms | At once | At once |

An interrupted glide continues from where it is drawn with its speed; an interrupted profile fades out from where it
reached, so a quick run of picks never jumps.

## Related

- `Avatar`: the portraits with initials and the availability dot.
- `SearchField` and `CopyButton`: the standalone search input and copy button.
- `GlidingIndicator`: the highlight that glides between items.

---

# Roles and permissions

> A matrix of roles and permissions with group checkboxes that ripple, locked owner access, role copies and a review bar that saves every change at once.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc.Blocks`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc.Blocks --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/blocks/roles-permissions

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.RolesPermissionsPreviewDemo">
    <!-- Five roles, four groups; Save waits 900 ms like a server call. Data: RolesPermissionsDemoData. -->
    <arc:RolesPermissions x:Name="Matrix" Margin="0,12">
        <arc:RolesPermissions.Members>
            <arc:AvatarGroupMember DisplayName="Lena Hart" Source="https://i.pravatar.cc/160?img=47" />
            <arc:AvatarGroupMember DisplayName="Omar Diaz" Source="https://i.pravatar.cc/160?img=12" />
            <arc:AvatarGroupMember DisplayName="Priya Rao" Source="https://i.pravatar.cc/160?img=32" />
            <arc:AvatarGroupMember DisplayName="Kai Moreno" Source="https://i.pravatar.cc/160?img=68" />
        </arc:RolesPermissions.Members>
    </arc:RolesPermissions>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class RolesPermissionsPreviewDemo : UserControl
{
    public RolesPermissionsPreviewDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        RolesPermissionsDemoData.Fill(Matrix);

        // Store the changes somewhere; here the save only waits, so the spinner and the "saved" state are visible.
        Matrix.SaveHandler = RolesPermissionsDemoData.SimulatedSave;
    }
}
```

## When to use

`RolesPermissions` is the access page of a workspace's settings: roles across the top, permissions down the side in
groups, and one switch where they meet. Nothing is applied while the person edits. Each changed cell gets a small dot,
the role's header gets one too, and a review bar slides up with the count, the roles the changes touch and how many
people they reach. The person saves everything at once, or throws it away.

- **Role-based access in a product's settings.** Owner, admin, member and guest style roles over a few groups of
  permissions (documents, team, billing, security).
- **Reviewing a change before it lands.** The bar says "Lead and Member · reaches 13 people" before anything is saved,
  so the person sees the reach of a change while making it.
- **Shaping a new role from an existing one.** Copy a role from its header menu, adjust the copy's column, and save the
  new role with the rest.

## When not to use

- **Assigning people to roles.** The matrix decides what a role may do, not who holds it. Use `Team members` for the
  people and their roles.
- **A handful of independent settings.** A few on/off options read better as switch rows on a `Settings page`.
- **Hundreds of permissions.** Every cell is drawn, none are virtualized. Group long lists and start most groups folded
  (`IsExpanded="False"`), or split the page.
- **A person's own security.** Passwords, two-step sign-in and sessions belong in `Security settings`.

## Usage

The block derives from Avalonia's `TemplatedControl`. Roles are `RolesPermissionsRole` objects (a key, a name, the member
count and a line for its menu; `IsLocked` for the owner), groups are `RolesPermissionsGroup` objects holding
`RolesPermissionsItem` permissions, and the grants are a set of `RolesPermissionsGrant` pairs of role key and permission key.
`SavedGrants` is the saved state; `Grants` is the current one and is written back on every change.

```xml
<arc:RolesPermissions Title="Roles &amp; access" WorkspaceName="Northwind Studio" MemberCount="31"
                      RolesSource="{Binding Roles}" GroupsSource="{Binding Groups}"
                      SavedGrants="{Binding SavedGrants}" Grants="{Binding Grants, Mode=TwoWay}" />
```

```csharp
matrix.Roles.Add(new RolesPermissionsRole("founder", "Founder", 1, "Lena Hart", isLocked: true));
matrix.Roles.Add(new RolesPermissionsRole("lead", "Lead", 4, "Omar Diaz, Priya Rao and 2 others"));
matrix.Groups.Add(new RolesPermissionsGroup("team", "Team",
    new("team.invite", "Send invitations"), new("team.roles", "Assign roles"), new("team.remove", "Remove people")));
matrix.SavedGrants = new HashSet<RolesPermissionsGrant> { new("lead", "team.invite") };
```

### Anatomy

- **Header**: `Title`, a subtitle with the workspace and two counts that roll when they change (members from
  `MemberCount`, or the number of `Members`; roles from the columns), and the members' avatars on the right. When the
  avatars do not fit beside the titles they move under them.
- **Header row**: the "Permission" caption over the label column and one button per role: its name (a lock leads a locked
  role), its member count, and a chevron that turns while its menu is open.
- **Group rows**: a disclosure button with the group's name and permission count, and one checkbox per role that is on
  when every permission of the group is on and mixed when only some are.
- **Permission rows**: the permission's name (it wraps when the column is narrow) and one switch per role.
- **Footer**: two legends, the lock and the unsaved dot.
- **Review bar**: the count, the roles and the people they reach, the Discard and Save buttons. It opens under the
  footer when there is something to save.

### Cells, groups and locked roles

A cell switches with a click, **Space** or **Enter**. A group checkbox turns every permission of the group on when it is
off or mixed, and off when it is on; the cells that change follow one another 60 ms apart, in group order. A locked role's
cells are always on: pressing one shakes the box and announces why. A cell switched back to its saved value is no longer
a change.

`GrantChanged` reports every cell that changes, with the role, the permission, the new value, whether it is now unsaved
and what changed it (a cell, a group, an undo, Discard or code). `GroupToggled` follows a group checkbox. `SetGrant`,
`ToggleGroup`, `IsGranted` and `IsUnsaved` do the same from code.

### Copying and removing roles

Each header opens a menu with the role's name and description. **Copy role** inserts "Guest (copy)" right of the source
("Guest (copy 2)" when that name is taken) with the source's permissions; its column springs open and the focus moves to
its header. A copy is new until it is saved: it reads "New role", counts as one change, and its own edits count and show
dots as well. **Undo edits** puts the role's cells back; **Remove role** (new roles only) closes the column again. Copies
are inserted into `Roles`, or into `RolesSource` when that is a list you can add to. `RoleDuplicated`, `RoleDeleted` and
`ChangesReverted` report each step; `DuplicateRole`, `DeleteRole` and `RevertRole` do it from code.

### Saving

Save awaits `SaveHandler` with a `RolesPermissionsSaveRequest`: every grant after the save, the cells that changed, the
roles and the new roles, and the count the bar showed. While it runs the button spins and the matrix takes no changes (a
person who tries hears "Saving, one moment"). Then the dots leave together, the bar reads "Access updated" with a check for
`SavedHoldDuration` (1.6 s) and closes, and `SavedGrants` holds the new baseline. Discard throws every change away at once,
the cells rippling back row by row.

```csharp
matrix.SaveHandler = async (request, cancellation) =>
{
    // Send request.Grants (and request.AddedRoles) to your server; throw to report a failure.
    await Task.Delay(900, cancellation);
};
matrix.Saved += (_, e) => Debug.WriteLine($"{e.Request.ChangeCount} access changes saved");
```

An exception keeps every change: the bar reads "Couldn't save" with the message (or `ErrorFormatter`'s text), Save becomes
"Try again", and the next edit clears the failure. `CancelSave` cancels the handler's token and returns to the review.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.RolesPermissionsFailureDemo">
    <!-- Every other save is refused: the changes stay, the bar shows the error and Try again saves them. -->
    <StackPanel Spacing="12" Margin="0,12">
        <arc:RolesPermissions x:Name="Matrix" Title="Roles &amp; access" />
        <TextBlock x:Name="Log" Opacity="0.7" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class RolesPermissionsFailureDemo : UserControl
{
    private int _attempts;

    public RolesPermissionsFailureDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        RolesPermissionsDemoData.Fill(Matrix);

        // The first attempt fails after the usual wait; the retry goes through.
        Matrix.SaveHandler = async (_, cancellation) =>
        {
            await Task.Delay(900, cancellation);
            _attempts++;
            if (_attempts % 2 == 1)
            {
                throw new InvalidOperationException("The server did not answer. Your changes are still here.");
            }
        };
        Matrix.SaveFailed += (_, e) => Log.Text = $"Attempt {_attempts} failed: {e.Exception.Message}";
        Matrix.Saved += (_, e) => Log.Text = $"Attempt {_attempts} saved {e.Request.ChangeCount} changes";
    }
}
```

### Bound state and events

`Grants` is two-way: bind it to keep a model in step, or write a new set to change the cells from outside.
`PendingChangeCount`, `HasUnsavedChanges` and `SaveState` follow the review bar. Folding a group writes its `IsExpanded`
back, so a page can fold or unfold every group.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.RolesPermissionsBoundDemo">
    <!-- The grants live in the page: buttons change them from outside and the log lists every event. -->
    <StackPanel Spacing="12" Margin="0,12">
        <StackPanel Orientation="Horizontal" Spacing="8">
            <arc:Button x:Name="GrantAll" Content="Give Guest everything" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" />
            <arc:Button x:Name="FoldAll" Content="Fold all groups" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" />
            <arc:Button x:Name="Copy" Content="Copy Member" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" />
        </StackPanel>
        <arc:RolesPermissions x:Name="Matrix" Title="Roles &amp; access" />
        <TextBlock x:Name="Status" Opacity="0.7" />
        <TextBlock x:Name="Log" TextWrapping="Wrap" Opacity="0.7" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class RolesPermissionsBoundDemo : UserControl
{
    private readonly List<string> _log = new();

    public RolesPermissionsBoundDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        RolesPermissionsDemoData.Fill(Matrix);
        Matrix.SaveHandler = RolesPermissionsDemoData.SimulatedSave;

        // Grants is two-way: the block writes a new set on every change, and a set written here shows at once.
        GrantAll.Click += (_, _) =>
        {
            var grants = new HashSet<RolesPermissionsGrant>(Matrix.Grants ?? Matrix.SavedGrants ?? new HashSet<RolesPermissionsGrant>());
            foreach (var group in Matrix.Groups)
            {
                foreach (var permission in group.Permissions)
                {
                    grants.Add(new RolesPermissionsGrant("guest", permission.Key));
                }
            }
            Matrix.Grants = grants;
        };
        FoldAll.Click += (_, _) =>
        {
            var fold = Matrix.Groups.Any(g => g.IsExpanded);
            foreach (var group in Matrix.Groups)
            {
                group.IsExpanded = !fold;
            }
            FoldAll.Content = fold ? "Unfold all groups" : "Fold all groups";
        };
        Copy.Click += (_, _) => Matrix.DuplicateRole("member");

        Matrix.GrantChanged += (_, e) => Add($"{e.Role.Name}: {e.Permission.Name} {(e.IsGranted ? "on" : "off")} ({e.ChangeSource})");
        Matrix.GroupToggled += (_, e) => Add($"{e.Role.Name}: {e.Group.Name} {(e.IsGranted ? "all on" : "all off")}, {e.ChangedCount} cells");
        Matrix.RoleDuplicated += (_, e) => Add($"Copied {e.SourceRole.Name} as {e.Role.Name}");
        Matrix.RoleDeleted += (_, e) => Add($"Removed {e.Role.Name}");
        Matrix.ChangesReverted += (_, e) => Add(e.Role is null ? $"Discarded {e.Count}" : $"Undid {e.Count} for {e.Role.Name}");
        Matrix.Saved += (_, e) => Add($"Saved {e.Request.ChangeCount}: {e.Request.Changes.Count} cells, {e.Request.AddedRoles.Count} new roles");
        Matrix.PropertyChanged += (_, e) =>
        {
            if (e.Property == RolesPermissions.PendingChangeCountProperty || e.Property == RolesPermissions.SaveStateProperty)
            {
                Status.Text = $"Pending: {Matrix.PendingChangeCount} · Save: {Matrix.SaveState}";
            }
        };
        Status.Text = "Pending: 0 · Save: Idle";
    }

    private void Add(string line)
    {
        _log.Insert(0, line);
        if (_log.Count > 6)
        {
            _log.RemoveAt(_log.Count - 1);
        }
        Log.Text = string.Join(Environment.NewLine, _log);
    }
}
```

### Framed or flat

`IsFramed` (the default) draws a card with a 1px border and a 16 radius, as on this page. Set it to false for a full
settings page: no frame, and a page margin of 32 (16 below 540).

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.RolesPermissionsFlatDemo">
    <!-- No card: the block lies on the page with a page margin, as a full settings page would show it. -->
    <arc:RolesPermissions x:Name="Matrix" IsFramed="False" Title="Workspace roles" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
```

### Narrow containers

The block reads its own content width. From 760 down, the label column needs 200 and the roles 92 each; below 540, 148 and
80, the group counts and header chevrons go, the permission names shrink to 12 and wrap, and the bar drops the word
"pending". When the roles do not fit, they scroll sideways under a sticky label column that shows its edge while scrolled;
a copied role scrolls itself into view.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.RolesPermissionsNarrowDemo">
    <!-- A 400-wide container: compact columns, wrapped names, a sticky label column while the roles scroll sideways. -->
    <arc:RolesPermissions x:Name="Matrix" Width="400" HorizontalAlignment="Center" Margin="0,12" />
</UserControl>
```
