# Webhooks

> A webhooks console where you check each endpoint's health and traffic, inspect what was sent and what came back, retry failed deliveries in place and add endpoints with a one-time signing secret.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc.Blocks`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc.Blocks --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/blocks/webhooks

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.WebhooksPreviewDemo">
    <!-- Three endpoints, one with three failed deliveries; retries, new endpoints and test events are simulated. Data: WebhooksDemoData. -->
    <Border Margin="0,12"
            Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Surface}"
            BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Border}"
            BorderThickness="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource EdgeThickness}"
            CornerRadius="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource RadiusStep16}"
            ClipToBounds="True">
        <arc:Webhooks x:Name="Hooks" />
    </Border>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class WebhooksPreviewDemo : UserControl
{
    public WebhooksPreviewDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Hooks.Description = WebhooksDemoData.Description;
        Hooks.CurrentUser = WebhooksDemoData.CurrentUser;
        Hooks.EventTypes.AddRange(WebhooksDemoData.EventTypes());
        Hooks.Endpoints.AddRange(WebhooksDemoData.Endpoints(DateTimeOffset.Now));
        // No RetryAction, CreateEndpointAction or SendTestAction: the block simulates a server that always answers 200.
    }
}
```

## When to use

`Webhooks` is the page of a developer settings area where people manage the URLs your product posts events to. From top
to bottom it shows the endpoints (each with the events it subscribes to, the share of events that went through and a
health badge), the selected endpoint's details with a chart of the last day's traffic, its recent deliveries, and an
inspector for the delivery picked in the list: the response, the request body and the request headers. A failed delivery
is sent again in place with Retry, and "Add endpoint" unfolds into a form that shows the new endpoint's signing secret
once.

- **A product with outgoing webhooks.** Payments, shipping, ticketing or scheduling services that notify their
  customers' servers, where support and developers need to see why an endpoint stopped answering.
- **An integration's diagnostics page.** One endpoint and its traffic, with a test event to check the round trip
  before going live.
- **An internal event bus console.** Teams that route events to internal services can watch the failing ones and resend
  them after a fix.

## When not to use

- **Thousands of deliveries.** The list shows the recent ones without virtualization; use a `DataGrid` with paging and
  filters for a full delivery history.
- **Editing endpoints.** The block adds endpoints and shows them; renaming, pausing, deleting and rotating secrets belong
  in a settings page of your own (the signing secret is only ever shown at creation).
- **A plain list of URLs.** When there is no traffic to show, a table or a list of cards is simpler.

## Usage

### Endpoints and deliveries

Each `WebhookEndpoint` has a `Name` (the host is shown when it is empty), the `Url`, the `Events` it subscribes to, who
added it and when (`AddedBy`, `AddedOn`; the person gets a generated avatar), a masked `SecretHint`, an `ApiVersion`, its
traffic as `Volume` buckets (oldest first; 48 half hours make a 24-hour chart) and its recent `Deliveries` (newest
first). `DeliveredRate`, `FailingCount` and `Health` follow the deliveries and the chart as they change: the rate counts
the chart's events that did not fail, rounded down to a tenth of a percent, and an endpoint is failing while one of its
deliveries failed and was not retried yet.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:Webhooks Description="Corvid signs each event and sends it to your endpoints.">
        <arc:WebhookEndpoint Name="Shipping sync"
                             Url="https://relay.tallowfield.dev/hooks/corvid/v2"
                             AddedBy="Lena Okafor"
                             SecretHint="sig_••••c41e"
                             ApiVersion="Version 2026.09" />
    </arc:Webhooks>
</UserControl>
```

A `WebhookDelivery` holds the `EventType` and `EventId`, the `Attempt`, the `StatusCode` (0 means the endpoint did not
answer) and `StatusText`, the `Duration`, `SentAt`, the `ResponseBody`, the request `Payload` (JSON is indented and
colored, other text is shown as it is) and its `Headers`. Use `EndpointsSource` for a collection you own: an
`ObservableCollection` is observed and new endpoints are inserted at its top.

`SelectedEndpoint`, `SelectedDelivery` and `InspectorTab` are two-way. Selecting an endpoint picks its first failing
delivery, or its newest one; the inspector's tab stays when the delivery changes.

### Retries, new endpoints and test events

The three server actions are asynchronous delegates. Without them the block simulates a server that always succeeds, with
fixed delays (1.1 s, 0.76 s and 0.9 s), which is what the preview does.

- `RetryAction` sends a failed delivery again and returns the new attempt. It is added at the top of the list with a
  short flash; when it went through, the original is marked resolved, the endpoint's rate and badge update, and the
  selection moves to the new attempt. When the delegate throws (or returns a failed attempt), a failed attempt with its
  own Retry button is added instead, the original shows "Retried", and the failure is announced.
- `CreateEndpointAction` receives the form as a `WebhookEndpointDraft` and returns the endpoint with its signing secret
  (`WebhookEndpointCreated`). The endpoint is added at the top of the list, flashing until the panel closes, and the
  secret is shown once with a Copy button; it is dropped when the panel closes and never stored on the endpoint. When the
  delegate throws, the form stays open with the message above its buttons. Escape while it waits cancels the request.
- `SendTestAction` is called by the "Send test event" button that an endpoint without deliveries shows. A failed test is
  added as a failed delivery.

`AppendDelivery` adds a delivery your server reported, for a live feed, and counts it in the last slice of the chart.

```csharp
var client = new HttpClient();
hooks.RetryAction = async (delivery, cancellation) =>
{
    var started = DateTimeOffset.Now;
    using var response = await client.PostAsync(
        $"https://api.example.dev/deliveries/{delivery.EventId}/resend", null, cancellation);
    return new WebhookDelivery
    {
        EventType = delivery.EventType,
        EventId = delivery.EventId,
        Attempt = delivery.Attempt + 1,
        StatusCode = (int)response.StatusCode,
        Duration = DateTimeOffset.Now - started,
        SentAt = started,
        ResponseBody = await response.Content.ReadAsStringAsync(cancellation),
        Payload = delivery.Payload,
    };
};
```

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.WebhooksFailingDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12" Margin="0,12">
        <Border Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Surface}"
                BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Border}"
                BorderThickness="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource EdgeThickness}"
                CornerRadius="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource RadiusStep16}"
                ClipToBounds="True">
            <arc:Webhooks x:Name="Hooks" />
        </Border>
        <TextBlock x:Name="Log"
                   HorizontalAlignment="Center"
                   TextAlignment="Center"
                   TextWrapping="Wrap"
                   MaxWidth="560"
                   Text="The first retry times out and the next one goes through. Adding an endpoint fails once, then works." />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class WebhooksFailingDemo : UserControl
{
    private int _retries;
    private int _creates;

    public WebhooksFailingDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Hooks.Description = WebhooksDemoData.Description;
        Hooks.EventTypes.AddRange(WebhooksDemoData.EventTypes());
        Hooks.Endpoints.AddRange(WebhooksDemoData.Endpoints(DateTimeOffset.Now));

        // Odd retries time out (the block adds a failed attempt with its own Retry); even ones are answered with 200.
        Hooks.RetryAction = async (delivery, cancellation) =>
        {
            await Task.Delay(1100, cancellation);
            if (++_retries % 2 == 1)
            {
                throw new TimeoutException("The endpoint did not answer within 30 seconds.");
            }
            var attempt = new WebhookDelivery
            {
                EventType = delivery.EventType,
                EventId = delivery.EventId,
                Attempt = delivery.Attempt + 1,
                StatusCode = 200,
                Duration = TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(143),
                SentAt = DateTimeOffset.Now,
                ResponseBody = "{\"ok\":true}",
                Payload = delivery.Payload,
            };
            attempt.Headers.AddRange(delivery.Headers.Select(h => new WebhookHeader(h.Name, h.Value)));
            return attempt;
        };

        // The first new endpoint is refused (the URL did not answer the check); the next one is added.
        Hooks.CreateEndpointAction = async (draft, cancellation) =>
        {
            await Task.Delay(760, cancellation);
            if (++_creates == 1)
            {
                throw new InvalidOperationException("The URL answered 404 to the verification request.");
            }
            var endpoint = new WebhookEndpoint
            {
                Name = draft.Description,
                Url = draft.Url,
                AddedBy = WebhooksDemoData.CurrentUser,
                AddedOn = DateTimeOffset.Now,
                SecretHint = "sig_••••51fb",
                ApiVersion = "Version 2026.09",
            };
            endpoint.Events.AddRange(draft.Events);
            return new WebhookEndpointCreated(endpoint, "sig_Hq4Vn8Lc2Tx6Rb9Zd3Wk7Mp5Ys1Fj0Ae");
        };

        Hooks.ActionFailed += (_, e) => Log.Text = $"{e.Action} failed: {e.Exception?.Message ?? "the endpoint refused it"}";
        Hooks.RetryCompleted += (_, e) => Log.Text = $"{e.Original.EventType} went through on try {e.Result.Attempt}.";
        Hooks.EndpointCreated += (_, e) => Log.Text = $"Added {e.Endpoint.DisplayName}.";
    }
}
```

### A new endpoint

An endpoint without deliveries shows a dash for its rate, "No traffic" as its badge, an empty chart and the test button.
`EventTypes` lists the checkboxes of the form; `IsDefaultSelected` ticks one when the form opens (the first one otherwise).
`UrlValidator` replaces the built-in URL check (required, https, not localhost). `CurrentUser` names who adds endpoints
when the block simulates the server.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.WebhooksNewEndpointDemo">
    <!-- One endpoint added a moment ago: no traffic yet. Send a test event, or add another endpoint. -->
    <Border Margin="0,12"
            Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Surface}"
            BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Border}"
            BorderThickness="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource EdgeThickness}"
            CornerRadius="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource RadiusStep16}"
            ClipToBounds="True">
        <arc:Webhooks x:Name="Hooks" Description="Point Corvid at a URL, pick the events, then send a test to see the round trip." />
    </Border>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class WebhooksNewEndpointDemo : UserControl
{
    public WebhooksNewEndpointDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Hooks.CurrentUser = WebhooksDemoData.CurrentUser;
        Hooks.EventTypes.AddRange(WebhooksDemoData.EventTypes());
        Hooks.Endpoints.Add(WebhooksDemoData.NewEndpoint(DateTimeOffset.Now));
    }
}
```

### Narrow containers

The layout follows the block's own width. At 880 and below the inspector moves under the deliveries; at 760 and below the
endpoint rows keep the name, the rate and the badge; at 540 and below the paddings tighten and the toolbar note hides. The
form takes two columns of events at 800, and one column for everything at 560. A delivery list 460 wide or less puts the
duration and the time under the event, and narrow headers put each name above its value.

```xml
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.WebhooksCompactDemo">
    <!-- A 420 wide container: rows keep the name, the rate and the badge; deliveries take two lines; the inspector sits below. -->
    <Border Margin="0,12"
            Width="420"
            HorizontalAlignment="Center"
            Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Surface}"
            BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Border}"
            BorderThickness="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource EdgeThickness}"
            CornerRadius="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource RadiusStep16}"
            ClipToBounds="True">
        <arc:Webhooks x:Name="Hooks" />
    </Border>
</UserControl>
```

### Events and bound state

Every change is a bubbling routed event with what changed: `EndpointSelectionChanged` and `DeliverySelectionChanged`
(with the old and new item and whether the pointer, the keyboard or the block changed it), `RetryStarted`,
`RetryCompleted` (with the old and new rate), `ActionFailed`, `EndpointCreated`, `TestEventSent`, `ContentCopied`,
`AddPanelOpened` and `AddPanelClosed` (with the reason). `RetryCommand`, `SendTestCommand` and `EndpointCreatedCommand`
run alongside. `OpenAddPanel`, `CloseAddPanel`, `RetryAsync` and `SendTestAsync` do from code what the buttons do; every
text is in `Labels`.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.WebhooksEventLogDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12" Margin="0,12">
        <Border Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Surface}"
                BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Border}"
                BorderThickness="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource EdgeThickness}"
                CornerRadius="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource RadiusStep16}"
                ClipToBounds="True">
            <arc:Webhooks x:Name="Hooks" />
        </Border>
        <StackPanel Orientation="Horizontal" Spacing="12" HorizontalAlignment="Center">
            <arc:Button x:Name="Push" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Content="Push a delivery" />
            <arc:SegmentedControl x:Name="Tab" />
        </StackPanel>
        <TextBlock x:Name="Selection" HorizontalAlignment="Center" TextAlignment="Center" />
        <TextBlock x:Name="Log" HorizontalAlignment="Center" TextAlignment="Center" TextWrapping="Wrap" MaxWidth="560" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class WebhooksEventLogDemo : UserControl
{
    private readonly List<string> _lines = new();
    private int _pushed;

    public WebhooksEventLogDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Hooks.Description = WebhooksDemoData.Description;
        Hooks.CurrentUser = WebhooksDemoData.CurrentUser;
        Hooks.EventTypes.AddRange(WebhooksDemoData.EventTypes());
        Hooks.Endpoints.AddRange(WebhooksDemoData.Endpoints(DateTimeOffset.Now));

        // The inspector's tab is a two-way property: this switch and the block's own tabs follow each other.
        Tab.ItemsSource = new[]
        {
            new SegmentedOption(WebhookInspectorTab.Payload, "Payload"),
            new SegmentedOption(WebhookInspectorTab.Headers, "Headers"),
        };
        Tab.SelectedIndex = 0;
        Tab.SelectionChanged += (_, _) => Hooks.InspectorTab = Tab.SelectedIndex == 1 ? WebhookInspectorTab.Headers : WebhookInspectorTab.Payload;
        Hooks.PropertyChanged += (_, e) =>
        {
            if (e.Property == Webhooks.InspectorTabProperty)
            {
                Tab.SelectedIndex = Hooks.InspectorTab == WebhookInspectorTab.Headers ? 1 : 0;
            }
            else if (e.Property == Webhooks.SelectedEndpointProperty || e.Property == Webhooks.SelectedDeliveryProperty)
            {
                ShowSelection();
            }
        };

        // A live feed: the host pushes what its server reports; every fourth delivery fails.
        Push.Click += (_, _) =>
        {
            if (Hooks.SelectedEndpoint is { } endpoint)
            {
                var type = endpoint.Events.Count > 0 ? endpoint.Events[_pushed % endpoint.Events.Count] : "test.ping";
                Hooks.AppendDelivery(endpoint, WebhooksDemoData.LiveDelivery(DateTimeOffset.Now, _pushed++, type));
            }
        };

        Hooks.EndpointSelectionChanged += (_, e) => Add($"Endpoint: {e.NewEndpoint?.DisplayName} ({e.ChangeSource})");
        Hooks.DeliverySelectionChanged += (_, e) => Add($"Delivery: {e.NewDelivery?.EventType} ({e.ChangeSource})");
        Hooks.RetryStarted += (_, e) => Add($"Retrying {e.Delivery.EventType}");
        Hooks.RetryCompleted += (_, e) => Add($"Retried: {Rate(e.OldRate)} → {Rate(e.NewRate)}");
        Hooks.ActionFailed += (_, e) => Add($"{e.Action} failed");
        Hooks.EndpointCreated += (_, e) => Add($"Added {e.Endpoint.DisplayName}");
        Hooks.TestEventSent += (_, e) => Add($"Test sent to {e.Endpoint.Host}");
        Hooks.ContentCopied += (_, e) => Add($"Copied the {e.Content.ToString().ToLowerInvariant()} ({e.Text.Length} characters)");
        Hooks.AddPanelOpened += (_, _) => Add("Add panel opened");
        Hooks.AddPanelClosed += (_, e) => Add($"Add panel closed ({e.Reason})");
        ShowSelection();
    }

    private static string Rate(double? rate) => rate is { } value ? $"{value * 100:0.0}%" : "–";

    private void ShowSelection() =>
        Selection.Text = $"{Hooks.SelectedEndpoint?.DisplayName ?? "No endpoint"} · {Hooks.SelectedDelivery?.EventType ?? "no delivery"}";

    private void Add(string line)
    {
        _lines.Insert(0, line);
        if (_lines.Count > 4)
        {
            _lines.RemoveAt(_lines.Count - 1);
        }
        Log.Text = string.Join("\n", _lines);
    }
}
```

## API reference

### Webhooks

A webhooks console for a developer settings page: the endpoints with their subscribed events, delivered rate and health; the selected endpoint's details and a 24-hour traffic chart you can hover; its recent deliveries with an inspector for the response, the payload and the headers; failed deliveries retried in place; and an "Add endpoint" pill that unfolds into a form and shows the new endpoint's signing secret once. Retries, new endpoints and test events call `RetryAction`, `CreateEndpointAction` and `SendTestAction`; without them the block simulates a server that always succeeds. Failures show in place: a failed attempt row, an error in the form, a failed test delivery.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Title` | `string?` | `null` | The title; null shows `Title`. |
| `Description` | `string?` | `null` | The line under the title (at most 540 wide); empty hides it. |
| `EndpointsSource` | `IEnumerable?` | `null` | The endpoints, when you give them as a list to follow; it wins over `Endpoints` when set. |
| `SelectedEndpoint` | `WebhookEndpoint?` | `null` | The selected endpoint (two-way). Null selects the first one. |
| `SelectedDelivery` | `WebhookDelivery?` | `null` | The delivery shown in the inspector (two-way). Selecting an endpoint picks its first failing delivery, else its newest one. |
| `InspectorTab` | `WebhookInspectorTab` | `Payload` | The inspector's tab (two-way); it stays when the delivery or the endpoint changes. |
| `IsAddPanelOpen` | `bool` | `false` | Whether the "Add endpoint" panel is open (two-way). |
| `AddPanelState` | `WebhookAddState` | – | *Read-only.* The state of the "Add endpoint" panel. |
| `RetryAction` | `Func<WebhookDelivery, CancellationToken, Task<WebhookDelivery>>?` | `null` | Sends a failed delivery again and returns the new attempt (a failed attempt is shown as one). Null simulates a server that answers 200 after about 1.1s. |
| `CreateEndpointAction` | `Func<WebhookEndpointDraft, CancellationToken, Task<WebhookEndpointCreated>>?` | `null` | Adds an endpoint from the form and returns it with its signing secret; throwing shows the message in the form. Null simulates it after about 0.76s with a random secret. |
| `SendTestAction` | `Func<WebhookEndpoint, CancellationToken, Task<WebhookDelivery>>?` | `null` | Sends a test event to an endpoint that has no deliveries yet and returns the delivery. Null simulates a 200 after about 0.9s. |
| `UrlValidator` | `Func<string, string?>?` | `null` | Checks the form's URL and returns the error to show, or null. Null uses the built-in check: required, https, not localhost. |
| `CurrentUser` | `string?` | `null` | Who adds endpoints in the simulated create (shown as "Added … by" with a generated avatar). |
| `ShowsRetry` | `bool` | `true` | Whether failed deliveries have a Retry button. |
| `Labels` | `WebhooksLabels` | – | Every word the block shows or announces. |
| `RetryCommand` | `ICommand?` | `null` | Run when a retry starts, with the `WebhookDelivery` as the parameter. |
| `SendTestCommand` | `ICommand?` | `null` | Run when a test event is sent, with the `WebhookEndpoint` as the parameter. |
| `EndpointCreatedCommand` | `ICommand?` | `null` | Run after an endpoint was added, with the `WebhookEndpoint` as the parameter. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `EndpointSelectionChanged` | `WebhookEndpointSelectionChangedEventArgs` | Raised when the selected endpoint changes. |
| `DeliverySelectionChanged` | `WebhookDeliverySelectionChangedEventArgs` | Raised when the inspected delivery changes. |
| `RetryStarted` | `WebhookDeliveryEventArgs` | Raised when a retry starts. |
| `RetryCompleted` | `WebhookRetryCompletedEventArgs` | Raised when a retry went through. |
| `ActionFailed` | `WebhookActionFailedEventArgs` | Raised when a retry, a new endpoint or a test event failed. |
| `EndpointCreated` | `WebhookEndpointEventArgs` | Raised after an endpoint was added. |
| `TestEventSent` | `WebhookDeliveryEventArgs` | Raised after a test event went through. |
| `ContentCopied` | `WebhookContentCopiedEventArgs` | Raised after the inspector copied the payload or the headers. |
| `AddPanelOpened` | `RoutedEventArgs` | Raised when the "Add endpoint" panel opens. |
| `AddPanelClosed` | `WebhookAddPanelClosedEventArgs` | Raised when the "Add endpoint" panel closes. |

Pseudo-classes: `:stacked`, `:narrow`, `:compact`, `:adding`, `:revealing`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

### WebhookEndpoint

An endpoint of `Webhooks`: where events are sent, which ones, who added it, its traffic chart and its recent deliveries. `DeliveredRate`, `FailingCount` and `Health` follow the deliveries and the chart as they change.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Key` | `string?` | `null` | A key of your own for the endpoint (the block never reads it). |
| `Name` | `string?` | `null` | The name; empty shows the URL's host. |
| `Url` | `string` | `""` | The URL events are posted to. |
| `AddedBy` | `string?` | `null` | Who added the endpoint (shown with a generated avatar). |
| `AddedOn` | `DateTimeOffset?` | `null` | When the endpoint was added. |
| `SecretHint` | `string?` | `null` | A masked hint of the signing secret ("sig_••••c41e"); the secret itself never reaches the block. |
| `ApiVersion` | `string?` | `null` | The payload version the endpoint receives ("Version 2026.09"). |
| `DeliveredRate` | `double?` | – | *Read-only.* The share of events that went through, from 0 to 1 (rounded down to a tenth of a percent); null when nothing was sent. |
| `FailingCount` | `int` | – | *Read-only.* How many deliveries still fail (failed, not delivered by a retry, not taken over by a later attempt). |
| `Health` | `WebhookHealth` | – | *Read-only.* How the endpoint is doing. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### WebhookDelivery

One attempt to deliver an event to an endpoint, with what was sent and what came back.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Key` | `string?` | `null` | A key of your own for the delivery (the block never reads it). |
| `EventType` | `string` | `""` | The event type ("shipment.created"). |
| `EventId` | `string?` | `null` | The event id shown under the inspector title ("evt_7Qm2Lx9Rd"). |
| `Attempt` | `int` | `1` | Which attempt this is (1 for the first send; a retry adds one). |
| `IsTest` | `bool` | `false` | Whether this is a test event (marked "Test" in the list). |
| `StatusCode` | `int` | `200` | The HTTP status the endpoint answered with; 0 means it did not answer. |
| `StatusText` | `string?` | `null` | The status text ("OK", "Internal Server Error"); empty shows a standard one for the code. |
| `Duration` | `TimeSpan` | `00:00:00` | How long the endpoint took to answer. |
| `SentAt` | `DateTimeOffset` | `01/01/0001 00:00:00 +00:00` | When the request was sent. |
| `ResponseBody` | `string?` | `null` | The body the endpoint answered with, shown in one line under the response. |
| `Payload` | `string?` | `null` | The request body; JSON is indented and colored, other text is shown as it is. |
| `IsResolved` | `bool` | `false` | Whether a later retry of this failed delivery went through. |
| `RetriedBy` | `WebhookDelivery?` | `null` | The later attempt that took over from this failed one (set by a retry, whatever its result). |
| `IsFailure` | `bool` | – | *Read-only.* Whether the endpoint did not accept the event (status 400 and up, or no answer). |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### WebhookVolumeBucket

One slice of an endpoint's traffic chart (Arc shows 48 half hours): how many events were sent in it and how many of those still fail.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Start` | `DateTimeOffset` | `01/01/0001 00:00:00 +00:00` | Where the slice starts. |
| `End` | `DateTimeOffset` | `01/01/0001 00:00:00 +00:00` | Where the slice ends. |
| `Total` | `int` | `0` | Events sent in the slice, failed ones included. |
| `Failed` | `int` | `0` | Events of the slice that failed and were not delivered by a retry yet. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### WebhookEventType

An event type the "Add endpoint" form offers as a checkbox.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Name` | `string` | `""` | The event name, shown in a monospaced font ("shipment.created"). |
| `Description` | `string?` | `null` | A short line under the name saying when the event is sent. |
| `IsDefaultSelected` | `bool` | `false` | Whether the box is ticked when the form opens. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### WebhookHeader

A request header of a `WebhookDelivery`.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Name` | `string` | `""` | The header name ("Content-Type"). |
| `Value` | `string` | `""` | The header value. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### WebhooksLabels

Every word `Webhooks` shows or announces, in English by default. Replace the instance to translate or reword; texts with values are functions so that word order and plural forms can change.

## Accessibility

- **Tab** goes through the "Add endpoint" pill, each endpoint row, each delivery row and its Retry button, the Copy
  button, the selected tab and the payload panel.
- **Up** and **Down** on an endpoint or a delivery row move to the previous or next row and select it; **Home** and **End**
  go to the first and the last. They do not wrap, and they skip the Retry buttons.
- **Left** and **Right** on the tabs switch between Payload and Headers; the payload panel scrolls with the arrow keys.
- **Enter** or **Space** selects a row or presses a button. In the form, **Enter** in a field submits it.
- **Escape** inside the panel closes it and returns the focus to the pill; while the form waits for the server, it cancels
  the request instead.
- The endpoints and the deliveries are lists with names ("Endpoints", "Recent deliveries to Shipping sync"). An endpoint
  row reads its name, host, rate, badge and events; a delivery row reads its status, event, duration and time, and
  whether a retry resolved it. A Retry button names the event and the time it was sent, and says "Resending" while it
  waits.
- The chart is a picture described in one sentence: the events, how many still fail and the busiest half hour.
- Results are announced politely: a retry that went through or failed, a new endpoint, a test event, a copy, a form
  error.
- The focus never drops: after a retry it moves from the Retry button to the new attempt, after a test event to the
  test delivery, after the panel closes to the pill, and when the endpoint changes while a delivery row has the focus, to
  the selected delivery of the new endpoint. A failed create keeps it on the submit button.
- Rings show only for keyboard focus; on rows they take the shape of the selection plate.

## Motion

- **Selecting**: the selection plate glides to the new row on a critically damped spring (about 550 ms) and follows rows
  that move under it. The endpoint's name, its details and the chart's title swap with a short blur; the bars spring to
  their new heights one after the other (4.2 ms apart, about 200 ms from the first to the last). The lower half
  crossfades, the new one rising 6 px; the old one leaves the layout at once, so nothing under it jumps.
- **Inspecting**: the title, the response and the panel swap with a short blur. The old response is lifted out of the
  layout while it fades, so the tabs never move during the swap.
- **Retrying**: the button shows a spinner and "Resending" while its width springs to the new label. The new attempt's
  row grows in (Smooth spring, opacity after 80 ms) with a flash that holds 1.4 s and fades over 1.2 s; "Resolved" blurs in
  where Retry was; the changed digits of the rate swap one slot at a time, right to left, 30 ms apart; about 500 ms later
  the selection follows.
- **Adding an endpoint**: the pill grows into the full-width panel on the same spring while the plus turns into a close
  cross, and the form fades in once the panel is half open. The secret develops out of a soft blur. The new row grows in
  at the top and keeps its flash until the panel closes.
- **Hovering the chart**: the bar under the pointer brightens and the others dim to 45% in 160 ms; the title shows that
  half hour at once.
- Reduced motion keeps only short fades: the plates, the bars, the rows and the panel move at once and the digits change
  in place. Off applies every change at once.

## Related

- API keys, Integrations and Env variables, the other Developer blocks.
- `Badge`, `Button`, `CopyButton`, `Input`, `Checkbox` and `SegmentedControl`, the controls the block is made of.
- `JsonViewer` for exploring a large JSON document as a tree.

# Integrations

> A directory of apps to connect, with search, counted category filters, a connect pill that spins, connects or offers a retry, and a drawer for permissions, sync frequency and hold to disconnect.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc.Blocks`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc.Blocks --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/blocks/integrations

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.IntegrationsPreviewDemo">
    <!-- Nine invented apps in three categories, two connected; connecting takes 1.4 seconds. Data: IntegrationsDemoData. -->
    <arc:Integrations x:Name="Directory"
                      Margin="0,12"
                      Title="Connected apps"
                      Subtitle="Link the services your workspace relies on." />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class IntegrationsPreviewDemo : UserControl
{
    public IntegrationsPreviewDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        // No ConnectAction: each connect waits SimulatedConnectDuration (1.4 s) and succeeds.
        IntegrationsDemoData.Fill(Directory);
    }
}
```

## When to use

`Integrations` is the settings page where a workspace links the services it relies on. Each app is one row with its mark,
name, category and a one-line description, and a pill at the right that says where it stands. Pressing **Connect** runs
your authorization flow while the pill spins; when it succeeds the pill turns into a green **Connected** and a **Settings**
button slides in beside it. The name or the settings button opens a drawer with what the app may do, how often it syncs and
a button you hold to disconnect it.

- **An app marketplace or an add-ons page.** Search narrows the list as you type, the filters show how many apps each
  category has, and the order never changes when an app is connected, so people can find it where they left it.
- **Workspace or project settings.** The Connected filter shows what is linked today, and the drawer answers "what can
  this app see" before and after it is linked.
- **Onboarding.** A short list of recommended services with one press each to link them.

## When not to use

- **Hundreds of apps.** Rows are live elements that glide when the list changes; the block is designed for a few dozen.
  Use a paged or virtualized catalog for a large marketplace.
- **One service.** A single connect button with its own status line is clearer than a directory of one.
- **Settings that need a full page.** The drawer holds permissions, one frequency menu and the disconnect button. Link to
  a settings page when an app needs mappings, field choices or several steps.

## Usage

### Apps, categories and frequencies

Each `IntegrationItem` is a row. `Name` is its title everywhere, `Category` is the key of an `IntegrationCategory` (its
filter and the word after the name), `Description` is the line under it and the drawer's description. `Scopes` lists
what the app may do, each with a `Kind` that picks its icon (read, write, sync, admin). `SyncOptions` fill the drawer's
menu; leave it empty and the menu is gone.

```xml
<arc:Integrations Title="Connected apps" Subtitle="Link the services your workspace relies on.">
    <arc:Integrations.Categories>
        <arc:IntegrationCategory Key="files" Label="Files" />
        <arc:IntegrationCategory Key="insights" Label="Insights" />
    </arc:Integrations.Categories>
    <arc:Integrations.SyncOptions>
        <arc:IntegrationSyncOption Key="realtime" Label="Real-time" Hint="Updates land within seconds." Phrase="in real time" />
        <arc:IntegrationSyncOption Key="nightly" Label="Nightly" Hint="Runs every night at 03:00." Phrase="nightly" />
    </arc:Integrations.SyncOptions>
    <arc:IntegrationItem Key="vaultline" Name="Vaultline" Category="files"
                         Description="Mirror design files into the matching workspace board.">
        <arc:IntegrationScope Kind="Read" Text="Browse folders you share with the workspace" />
        <arc:IntegrationScope Kind="Write" Text="Add file links to boards and tasks" />
    </arc:IntegrationItem>
</arc:Integrations>
```

Bind `ItemsSource` instead of filling `Items` when the apps come from your own list; the block follows its changes.
`SelectedFilter` (`all`, `connected` or a category key) and `SearchText` are two-way, so a page can open on a filter or
keep the search in its address.

### Marks

`Logo` takes an image, a `Geometry` (filled with `MarkBrush`) or any control, drawn 20 by 20 without a plate. Without a
logo the block draws a generated mark: the first letter of the name, or `Monogram`, on a rounded tile in one of the chart
series colors, picked from the key so it stays the same between runs. The block ships no third-party logos.

### Connecting

`ConnectAction` is your authorization flow. It receives the app and the attempt number, and a token that is cancelled
when `CancelConnect` is called or the block leaves the window. Return `IntegrationConnectResult.Connected` with who
connected it (null means the person using the block: "Linked by you just now") or `IntegrationConnectResult.Failed` with
the reason; throwing fails too, and `ErrorFormatter` turns the exception into the drawer's line. A failed app shows
**Retry** on a red tint; pressing it runs the action again with the next attempt number.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.IntegrationsFailingDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12" Margin="0,12">
        <arc:Integrations x:Name="Directory"
                          Title="Connected apps"
                          Subtitle="Ledgerline refuses the first attempt; Retry goes through." />
        <TextBlock x:Name="Log"
                   HorizontalAlignment="Center"
                   TextAlignment="Center"
                   TextWrapping="Wrap"
                   MaxWidth="520"
                   Text="Connect Ledgerline, then open it to read why it failed." />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class IntegrationsFailingDemo : UserControl
{
    public IntegrationsFailingDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        IntegrationsDemoData.Fill(Directory);

        // A stand-in for the real authorization: Ledgerline refuses its first attempt, everything else goes through.
        Directory.ConnectAction = async (request, cancellation) =>
        {
            await Task.Delay(1400, cancellation);
            if (request.Item.Key == "ledgerline" && request.Attempt == 1)
            {
                return IntegrationConnectResult.Failed("Ledgerline did not grant access. Try again.");
            }
            return IntegrationConnectResult.Connected();
        };

        Directory.StatusChanged += (_, e) =>
            Log.Text = $"{e.Item.Name}: {e.OldStatus} → {e.NewStatus}" + (e.NewStatus == IntegrationStatus.Error ? $" ({e.Item.ErrorText})" : "");
    }
}
```

```csharp
// authorize and revoke are your own calls to the service (here: delegates you provide).
Func<string, CancellationToken, Task<bool>> authorize = (key, token) => Task.FromResult(true);
Func<string, CancellationToken, Task> revoke = (key, token) => Task.CompletedTask;

directory.ConnectAction = async (request, cancellation) =>
{
    var approved = await authorize(request.Item.Key, cancellation);
    return approved
        ? IntegrationConnectResult.Connected()
        : IntegrationConnectResult.Failed($"{request.Item.Name} did not grant access. Try again.");
};
directory.DisconnectAction = (item, cancellation) => revoke(item.Key, cancellation);
```

Without a `ConnectAction` the block waits `SimulatedConnectDuration` (1.4 seconds) and succeeds, which is what the demos
on this page do. `ConnectRequested` can cancel a connect before it starts, `StatusChanged` reports every move between
idle, connecting, connected and failed, and `ConnectCommand` / `DisconnectCommand` run with the app as parameter.

### Narrow containers

The layout follows the block's own width, not the window's. Below 720 the search drops under the heading; at 520 the
side paddings tighten; at 480 and below the filters scroll sideways, rows put the pill beside a two-line description,
the category and the settings button are hidden, and the name opens the drawer.

```xml
    <arc:Integrations x:Name="Directory"
                      Width="390"

</UserControl>
```

### Events and bound state

`FilterChanged` and `SearchChanged` report the new visible count, `SyncFrequencyChanged` the old and new option keys,
and `ConfigurationOpened` / `ConfigurationClosed` the app of the drawer. `ConnectedCount`, `VisibleCount` and
`OpenItem` can be bound. `IsFramed="False"` lays the block flat on the page. Every word is in `Labels`
(`IntegrationLabels`), including the screen reader announcements.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.IntegrationsEventLogDemo">
    <!-- Flat on the page, with the filter and search bound to the controls beside it and every event written below. -->
    <StackPanel Spacing="16" Margin="0,12">
        <WrapPanel ItemSpacing="12" LineSpacing="8" HorizontalAlignment="Center">
            <TextBlock VerticalAlignment="Center" Text="{Binding #Directory.ConnectedCount, StringFormat='{}{0} connected'}" />
            <TextBlock VerticalAlignment="Center" Text="{Binding #Directory.VisibleCount, StringFormat='{}{0} shown'}" />
            <arc:Button Content="Show connected" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Click="OnShowConnected" />
            <arc:Button Content="Connect all" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Click="OnConnectAll" />
        </WrapPanel>
        <arc:Integrations x:Name="Directory"
                          IsFramed="False"
                          Title="Connected apps"
                          Subtitle="Every event of the block is written below." />
        <TextBlock x:Name="Log"
                   HorizontalAlignment="Center"
                   TextAlignment="Center"
                   TextWrapping="Wrap"
                   MaxWidth="560"
                   Text="Search, filter, connect or change a sync frequency." />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class IntegrationsEventLogDemo : UserControl
{
    private readonly List<string> _lines = new();

    public IntegrationsEventLogDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        IntegrationsDemoData.Fill(Directory);
        Directory.SimulatedConnectDuration = TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(900);

        Directory.FilterChanged += (_, e) => Write($"Filter {e.OldFilter} → {e.NewFilter}, {e.VisibleCount} shown");
        Directory.SearchChanged += (_, e) => Write($"Search “{e.Text}”, {e.VisibleCount} shown");
        Directory.ConnectRequested += (_, e) => Write($"Connect {e.Item.Name} (attempt {e.Attempt})");
        Directory.StatusChanged += (_, e) => Write($"{e.Item.Name}: {e.OldStatus} → {e.NewStatus}");
        Directory.SyncFrequencyChanged += (_, e) => Write($"{e.Item.Name} syncs {e.NewKey} (was {e.OldKey ?? "unset"})");
        Directory.ConfigurationOpened += (_, e) => Write($"Opened {e.Item.Name}");
        Directory.ConfigurationClosed += (_, e) => Write($"Closed {e.Item.Name}");
    }

    private void Write(string line)
    {
        _lines.Insert(0, line);
        if (_lines.Count > 4)
        {
            _lines.RemoveAt(_lines.Count - 1);
        }
        Log.Text = string.Join(Environment.NewLine, _lines);
    }

    private void OnShowConnected(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) => Directory.SelectedFilter = Integrations.ConnectedFilter;

    private void OnConnectAll(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        foreach (var item in Directory.Items)
        {
            _ = Directory.ConnectAsync(item);
        }
    }
}
```

## API reference

### Integrations

A directory of the apps a workspace can connect (Arc Integrations, design reference): a heading and a search field, a row of filters (All, Connected and one per category, each with its count), and one row per app with its mark, name, category, description and a status pill. Connect runs `ConnectAction` (the pill spins, then turns into a green "Connected" and a settings button slides in; a failure shows Retry). The name or the settings button opens a drawer with the permissions, the sync frequency and a hold-to-disconnect button. Search and filters reflow the list: leaving rows fade where they were, the others glide to their place and the list's height follows.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Title` | `string?` | `null` | The heading; null shows `Title`. |
| `Subtitle` | `string?` | `null` | The line under the heading; null shows `Subtitle`, an empty string hides it. |
| `ItemsSource` | `IEnumerable?` | `null` | The apps, when you give them as a list to follow (observed when it raises collection changes); it wins over `Items`. |
| `SelectedFilter` | `string` | `"all"` | The checked filter (two-way): `AllFilter`, `ConnectedFilter` or a category key. |
| `SearchText` | `string` | `""` | The search text (two-way); it matches names, category labels and descriptions, ignoring case. |
| `ShowConnectedFilter` | `bool` | `true` | Whether the Connected filter is offered (between All and the categories). |
| `ShowSearch` | `bool` | `true` | Whether the search field is shown. |
| `ConnectAction` | `Func<IntegrationConnectRequest, CancellationToken, Task<IntegrationConnectResult>>?` | `null` | Connects an app: awaited while its pill spins, with the request and a token that `CancelConnect` (or the block leaving the window) cancels. Return `Connected` or `Failed`; throwing fails too, a cancellation returns the app to idle. Null waits `SimulatedConnectDuration` and succeeds (a demo). |
| `DisconnectAction` | `Func<IntegrationItem, CancellationToken, Task>?` | `null` | Disconnects an app after the hold completed (or `DisconnectAsync`); throwing keeps it connected. Null disconnects at once. |
| `ConnectCommand` | `ICommand?` | `null` | Run when a connect starts, with the `IntegrationItem` as the parameter; when it cannot execute the connect does not start. |
| `DisconnectCommand` | `ICommand?` | `null` | Run when an app was disconnected, with the `IntegrationItem` as the parameter. |
| `SimulatedConnectDuration` | `TimeSpan` | `00:00:01.4000000` | How long a connect takes when `ConnectAction` is null (1.4 s, as measured). |
| `DisconnectSettleDelay` | `TimeSpan` | `00:00:00.6600000` | How long the disconnect button reads "Unlinked" before the app returns to idle (660 ms, as measured). |
| `ErrorFormatter` | `Func<Exception, string>?` | `null` | Turns a failed connect's exception into the drawer's line; null uses the exception's message. |
| `Labels` | `IntegrationLabels` | – | Every word it shows or announces (English by default). |
| `IsFramed` | `bool` | `true` | Draws a bordered card with rounded corners (true); false lays the block flat on the page. |
| `ConnectedCount` | `int` | – | *Read-only.* How many apps are connected. |
| `VisibleCount` | `int` | – | *Read-only.* How many apps the list shows (filter and search applied). |
| `OpenItem` | `IntegrationItem?` | – | *Read-only.* The app whose drawer is open; null while it is closed. |
| `IsCompact` | `bool` | – | *Read-only.* True at 480 wide or less: rows stack their text, filters scroll, the settings button hides. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ConnectRequested` | `IntegrationConnectRequestedEventArgs` | Raised before a connect starts; setting `Cancel` keeps it from starting. |
| `StatusChanged` | `IntegrationStatusChangedEventArgs` | Raised when an app's status changes, by the block or by code. |
| `FilterChanged` | `IntegrationFilterChangedEventArgs` | Raised when the checked filter changes. |
| `SearchChanged` | `IntegrationSearchChangedEventArgs` | Raised when the search text changes. |
| `SyncFrequencyChanged` | `IntegrationSyncFrequencyChangedEventArgs` | Raised when the person picks another sync frequency in the drawer. |
| `ConfigurationOpened` | `IntegrationEventArgs` | Raised when an app's drawer opens. |
| `ConfigurationClosed` | `IntegrationEventArgs` | Raised when the drawer closes. |

Pseudo-classes: `:narrow`, `:tight`, `:compact`, `:framed`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

### IntegrationItem

One app in `Integrations`: its name, category, one-line description, mark, permissions and connection. `Status`, `SyncFrequency` and the connection details are written by the block as the person connects, configures and disconnects it; write them yourself to reflect changes made elsewhere.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Key` | `string` | `""` | A stable key (events, automation ids); defaults to the name when empty. |
| `Name` | `string` | `""` | The app's name: the row's title, the drawer's title and part of every accessible name. |
| `Category` | `string?` | `null` | The key of its `IntegrationCategory` (the filter it belongs to); null puts it in none. |
| `Description` | `string?` | `null` | One sentence on what it does: one line in the row (two when narrow) and the drawer's description. |
| `Logo` | `object?` | `null` | The app's mark, drawn 20×20 with no plate: an `IImage`, a `Geometry` (filled with `MarkBrush`) or any control. Null draws a generated mark: `Monogram` on a rounded tile. |
| `Monogram` | `string?` | `null` | The letters of the generated mark (one or two); null uses the first letter of the name. |
| `MarkBrush` | `IBrush?` | `null` | The generated tile's fill and a geometry logo's fill; null picks a chart series color from the key. |
| `Status` | `IntegrationStatus` | `Idle` | Where it stands (two-way); the block moves it through Connecting to Connected or Error. |
| `ConnectedBy` | `string?` | `null` | Who connected it (a display name; the drawer shows a generated avatar); null when unknown. |
| `ConnectedAt` | `DateTimeOffset?` | `null` | When it was connected; null leaves the date out. |
| `IsConnectedByCurrentUser` | `bool` | `false` | True when the person using the block connected it in this session ("you, just now"). |
| `SyncFrequency` | `string?` | `null` | The key of the chosen `IntegrationSyncOption` (two-way); null uses the first option. |
| `ErrorText` | `string?` | `null` | Why the last connect attempt failed (shown in the drawer while `Status` is Error). |
| `Tag` | `object?` | `null` | Anything you want to keep with the item. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### IntegrationCategory

A filter of `Integrations`: the items whose `Category` is its key.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Key` | `string` | `""` | The key items use in `Category` (and `SelectedFilter`). |
| `Label` | `string` | `""` | The filter's text and the category shown next to an app's name. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### IntegrationScope

One permission of an `IntegrationItem`: a short phrase and the kind that picks its icon.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Kind` | `IntegrationScopeKind` | `Read` | What it lets the app do; picks the icon unless `Icon` is set. |
| `Text` | `string` | `""` | The phrase ("View rooms and their members"); it completes the drawer's lead ("Chirp can"). |
| `Icon` | `Geometry?` | `null` | A 24×24 stroke icon replacing the one `Kind` picks. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### IntegrationSyncOption

A choice of the drawer's sync frequency menu.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Key` | `string` | `""` | The key stored in `SyncFrequency`. |
| `Label` | `string` | `""` | The menu text ("Every 30 minutes"). |
| `Hint` | `string?` | `null` | The line under the menu while it is chosen ("Updates arrive in half-hour batches."). |
| `Phrase` | `string?` | `null` | The phrase screen readers hear after a change ("every 30 minutes"); null uses the label. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### IntegrationStatusChangedEventArgs

Arguments of `Integrations.StatusChanged`: an app moved from `OldStatus` to `NewStatus`.

Derives from `RoutedEventArgs`: every member of `RoutedEventArgs` works as well.

### IntegrationConnectRequestedEventArgs

Arguments of `Integrations.ConnectRequested`: a connect is about to start; set `Cancel` to stop it.

Derives from `RoutedEventArgs`: every member of `RoutedEventArgs` works as well.

### IntegrationFilterChangedEventArgs

Arguments of `Integrations.FilterChanged`: the selected filter changed.

Derives from `RoutedEventArgs`: every member of `RoutedEventArgs` works as well.

### IntegrationSearchChangedEventArgs

Arguments of `Integrations.SearchChanged`: the search text changed.

Derives from `RoutedEventArgs`: every member of `RoutedEventArgs` works as well.

### IntegrationSyncFrequencyChangedEventArgs

Arguments of `Integrations.SyncFrequencyChanged`: the person chose another sync frequency for an app.

Derives from `RoutedEventArgs`: every member of `RoutedEventArgs` works as well.

## Accessibility

- The filters are radio buttons named "{filter}, {count}"; the list, the search field and every pill, name and button
  have accessible names ("Connect Pulsegrid", "Connecting Pulsegrid", "Settings for Chirp"), and the name's help text is
  the description.
- A connected pill is a status label: it is not focusable and is named "{app} connected".
- One polite live region announces connecting, connected, failed and disconnected apps, frequency changes and the
  number of apps after a filter or search change.
- States never rely on color alone: each pill has its own icon and word.

### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Tab | Moves through the search, the checked filter, then each row: its name, then its pill (idle, connecting or failed) or its settings button (connected). One stop per action. |
| Left / Up, Right / Down | In the filters: checks the previous or next filter, wrapping at the ends. |
| Home / End | In the filters: checks the first or last filter. |
| Enter / Space | Presses the focused pill, name or button. |
| Escape | Closes the drawer. |

After a connect the focus moves from the pill to the new settings button (or to the name when it is hidden); after a
connect in the drawer it moves to the sync frequency menu; after a disconnect it lands on the drawer's Connect pill. When
the drawer closes and the row that opened it has left the list, the focus goes to the heading. A row that leaves while
it holds the focus hands it to the next row.

## Motion

- Search and filters reflow the list: rows that leave fade into a 4px blur where they were (160ms), the others glide to
  their new place on one spring, new rows fade in out of a blur (240ms) and the list's height follows.
- The filter highlight glides between pills on the same spring; a changed count rolls up or down.
- The pill's label blur-swaps and its width follows on a spring; the check draws itself; the settings button slides in
  140ms after a connect and fades out after a disconnect. The drawer's settings open and close on a height spring.
- Reduced motion keeps 120ms fades and drops travel, blur and springs (leaving rows are removed at once); Off jumps.

## Related

- `Drawer` for the panel the settings open in.
- `HoldToConfirm` for the disconnect button.
- `SearchField` and `Select` for the search and the frequency menu.
- `EmptyState` for a list that is empty for other reasons.

---

# Env variables

> A project's environment variables as a matrix of switches per environment, with masked values, inline editing, .env import, a fingerprint comparison and a redeploy banner.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc.Blocks`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc.Blocks --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/blocks/env-variables

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.EnvVariablesPreviewDemo">
    <!-- Ten keys on seventeen rows across three environments; Redeploy is simulated (about 1.7 s). Data: EnvVariablesDemoData. -->
    <arc:EnvVariables x:Name="Block" Margin="0,12" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class EnvVariablesPreviewDemo : UserControl
{
    public EnvVariablesPreviewDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        // No RedeployAction: the block simulates a deployment, so the banner can be tried here.
        EnvVariablesDemoData.Fill(Block);
    }
}
```

## When to use

`EnvVariables` is the settings page where a team keeps a project's configuration and secrets. Each row is one value and
the environments it applies to, so a key can have one value for development and staging and another for production. The
environments are columns of switches: turning a switch moves the row into or out of that environment, and a switch that
would give a key two values in the same environment is refused with a short note. Values stay hidden until someone
reveals one, and a value marked sensitive can be replaced but never shown again.

Every change marks its row and opens a banner that counts the changes and names the environments that still run the old
values. Pressing Redeploy calls your deployment; the banner confirms it, or turns red, keeps the changes and offers to try
again.

- **Project or service settings.** Keep the variables of an app, a worker or a site, with a column per environment.
- **Onboarding a project.** Paste an existing `.env` file and see, line by line, what will be added, replaced or skipped
  before anything changes.
- **Release checks.** Compare staging with production by fingerprint to find keys one side lacks or holds a different
  value for, and copy a missing value across.

## When not to use

- **Editing a single config file.** Use `CodeBlock` or a text editor when people work on the file itself, with comments
  and ordering that matter.
- **Thousands of keys.** The rows are not virtualized and every row animates; the block suits tens of keys, not a whole
  secrets store.
- **Secrets you must never send to the client.** The block only shows what you give it. Leave `Value` empty for
  sensitive rows, give a `Fingerprint` instead, and load a readable value only in `ValueRevealed`.
- **A list of unrelated settings.** For toggles and options that are not per environment, use a settings form with
  `Switch` and `Select`.

## Usage

### Environments and rows

`Environments` lists the columns in order; each `EnvEnvironment` has a `Key` that rows refer to and a `Name` people read.
Without any, the block uses Development, Preview and Production. Each `EnvVariable` has a `Key`, a `Value` and the keys of
the `Environments` it applies to; add `UpdatedAt` and `UpdatedBy` for the second line of the row. Give rows in any order:
the block sorts them by key (ordinal: upper-case letters before lower-case ones, and an underscore after the letters) and, for the same key, by
their first environment.

```xml
<arc:EnvVariables ProjectName="lumen-console" SampleDotenv="FEATURE_FLAGS_URL=https://flags.lumen.example">
    <arc:EnvVariables.Environments>
        <arc:EnvEnvironment Key="development" Name="Development" />
        <arc:EnvEnvironment Key="staging" Name="Staging" />
        <arc:EnvEnvironment Key="production" Name="Production" />
    </arc:EnvVariables.Environments>
</arc:EnvVariables>
```

```csharp
block.Variables.Add(new EnvVariable("CACHE_TTL_SECONDS", "30", "development", "staging"));
block.Variables.Add(new EnvVariable("CACHE_TTL_SECONDS", "300", "production"));
block.Variables.Add(new EnvVariable("PRIMARY_DB_DSN", null, "production") { IsSensitive = true, Fingerprint = "5e0c2a" });
```

Use `VariablesSource` for a collection you own; an `ObservableCollection` is followed, and so are changes to the rows'
properties and environment lists. The block edits that collection in place when people add, import or remove rows.

### Values, sensitive values and fingerprints

A value stays out of the screen and the accessibility tree until someone presses the eye; it is read at that moment and
dropped again when it hides. `ValueRevealed` is raised just before (fill `Value` there to load it on demand) and after it
hides. A sensitive row shows a lock and "Sensitive" instead of the eye and the copy button, and its editor starts empty:
a new value replaces the old one, and only removing the row and adding it again makes it readable.

The compare view shows a six-digit fingerprint instead of each value: by default the first six hex digits of the value's
SHA-256, computed outside the visual tree. Equal values give equal fingerprints. Set `Fingerprint` yourself for values you
do not load.

### Adding and importing

Add variable opens the single form: a key, a value, the environments (all but the last are chosen first; set
`DefaultAddEnvironments` to choose others) and the sensitive option. Errors appear after the first try and update as
people type: an empty key, a key that starts with a digit or has other characters than letters, digits and underscores,
a key already set in a chosen environment, an empty value, or no environment.

Import .env opens the paste form with `SampleDotenv`. Pasting several lines into the Key field switches to it too. The
preview under the text box shows each key line as new, replacing an existing value, or skipped (set again on a later line,
a bad key, no equals sign); comments, blank lines, `export` and quotes are handled. Importing turns the chosen
environments off on the rows they replace, removes a row left with none, and adds one row per line.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.EnvVariablesImportDotenvDemo">
    <!-- Opens on the .env form with a sample that shows every line status: new keys, a repeated key, a bad key and a replacement. -->
    <arc:EnvVariables x:Name="Block" Margin="0,12" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class EnvVariablesImportDotenvDemo : UserControl
{
    public EnvVariablesImportDotenvDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        EnvVariablesDemoData.Fill(Block);
        // Import .env opens with this text; paste your own over it, or paste several lines into the Key field.
        Block.SampleDotenv = EnvVariablesDemoData.SampleDotenv;
        Block.Loaded += (_, _) => Block.OpenAddPanel(EnvAddMode.Dotenv);
    }
}
```

### Comparing environments

The compare view puts two environments side by side (`CompareLeft` and `CompareRight`, two-way; staging and production
here). Keys one side lacks get a Copy to button that adds that environment to the row holding the value, sensitive flag
included. `ShowMatching` (the Show identical switch) lists equal keys too. The search filters both views.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.EnvVariablesCompareDemo">
    <!-- The compare view of Staging and Production: fingerprints instead of values, and Copy to for keys one side lacks. -->
    <arc:EnvVariables x:Name="Block"
                      Margin="0,12"
                      ViewMode="Compare"
                      CompareLeft="staging"
                      CompareRight="production" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

{
    public EnvVariablesCompareDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        EnvVariablesDemoData.Fill(Block);
    }

```

### Redeploying

`RedeployAction` receives an `EnvRedeployRequest` (the environments and the number of changes) and a cancellation token.
While it runs the button spins; changes made meanwhile wait for the next deployment. Throw to fail: the banner shows the
message, keeps every change and offers Retry. Without an action the block waits about 1.7 seconds, as a demo. Set
`Cancel` in `RedeployRequested` to stop it first, or call `RedeployAsync` and `CancelRedeploy` from code.

```csharp
// Your own call to the hosting service; here it only waits.
static Task StartDeployment(IReadOnlyList<string> environments, CancellationToken cancellation) =>
    Task.Delay(1500, cancellation);

block.RedeployAction = (request, cancellation) => StartDeployment(request.Environments, cancellation);
```

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.EnvVariablesFailingRedeployDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12" Margin="0,12">
        <arc:EnvVariables x:Name="Block" />
        <TextBlock x:Name="Log"
                   HorizontalAlignment="Center"
                   TextAlignment="Center"
                   TextWrapping="Wrap"
                   MaxWidth="560"
                   Text="Every first deployment fails, as a busy build queue could. Turn a switch, then press Redeploy." />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class EnvVariablesFailingRedeployDemo : UserControl
{
    private int _attempts;

    public EnvVariablesFailingRedeployDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        EnvVariablesDemoData.Fill(Block);

        // Odd attempts fail after a second; the retry goes through. The changes stay pending until one succeeds.
        Block.RedeployAction = async (request, cancellation) =>
        {
            await Task.Delay(1000, cancellation);
            _attempts++;
            if (_attempts % 2 == 1)
            {
                throw new InvalidOperationException("The build queue is full. Your changes are kept; try again.");
            }
        };
        Block.RedeployFailed += (_, e) => Log.Text = $"Attempt {_attempts} failed: {e.Exception?.Message}";
        Block.Redeployed += (_, e) =>
            Log.Text = $"Attempt {_attempts} deployed {e.Request.ChangeCount} change(s) to {string.Join(", ", e.Request.Environments)}.";
    }
}
```

### Narrow containers

The block reads its own width. Below 760 each row stacks: the key and the edit button, then the value, then one labelled
pill per environment, as many per line as fit at 120 or more; the compare table becomes one card per key. Below 560 the
side insets tighten, the header buttons share the width and the search and the view switch take a line each.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.EnvVariablesCompactDemo">
    <!-- In a 420 wide container: stacked rows with labelled environment pills, buttons across the width. -->
    <arc:EnvVariables x:Name="Block" Width="420" HorizontalAlignment="Center" Margin="0,12" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

{

    {
        InitializeComponent();
        EnvVariablesDemoData.Fill(Block);
```
