```cs
}
```

### Events and bound state

`ViewMode`, `SearchText`, `CompareLeft`, `CompareRight` and `ShowMatching` are two-way. `VariablesChanged` follows every
change with its reason and all rows; the specific events (`VariableAdded`, `VariableSaved`, `VariableRemoved`,
`VariablesImported`, `ScopeToggled`, `ScopeConflict`, `ValueCopied`) carry what changed. `PendingChangeCount`,
`PendingEnvironments` and `RedeployState` describe the banner. `IsReadOnly` keeps the block to reading and comparing, and
`IsFramed="False"` lays it flat on the page.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.EnvVariablesEventLogDemo">
    <!-- A flat block bound to its search and view, with every event it raises written below. -->
    <StackPanel Spacing="12" Margin="0,12">
        <StackPanel Orientation="Horizontal" Spacing="12">
            <TextBlock VerticalAlignment="Center" Text="Search (two-way):" />
            <arc:Input x:Name="Search" Width="180" Text="{Binding #Block.SearchText}" />
            <TextBlock VerticalAlignment="Center" x:Name="View" />
        </StackPanel>
        <arc:EnvVariables x:Name="Block" IsFramed="False" />
        <TextBlock x:Name="Log"
                   TextWrapping="Wrap"
                   FontFamily="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource MonoFontFamily}"
                   FontSize="12"
                   Text="Events appear here." />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class EnvVariablesEventLogDemo : UserControl
{
    private readonly List<string> _lines = new();

    public EnvVariablesEventLogDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        EnvVariablesDemoData.Fill(Block);
        Block.RedeployAction = (_, cancellation) => Task.Delay(800, cancellation);

        Block.VariablesChanged += (_, e) => Write($"VariablesChanged {e.Reason}: {string.Join(", ", e.Affected.Select(v => v.Key))} ({e.Snapshot.Count} rows)");
        Block.ScopeToggled += (_, e) => Write($"ScopeToggled {e.Variable.Key} {e.Environment} → {(e.IsOn ? "on" : "off")}");
        Block.ScopeConflict += (_, e) => Write($"ScopeConflict {e.Variable.Key} {e.Environment}");
        Block.VariableSaved += (_, e) => Write($"VariableSaved {e.Variable.Key} changed={e.ValueChanged} sensitive={e.BecameSensitive}");
        Block.VariableAdded += (_, e) => Write($"VariableAdded {e.Variable.Key}");
        Block.VariableRemoved += (_, e) => Write($"VariableRemoved {e.Variable.Key} at {e.Index}");
        Block.VariablesImported += (_, e) => Write($"VariablesImported {e.Added.Count} added, lines skipped: {string.Join(", ", e.SkippedLines)}");
        Block.ValueCopied += (_, e) => Write($"ValueCopied {e.Variable.Key} {e.From} → {e.To}");
        Block.ValueRevealed += (_, e) => Write($"ValueRevealed {e.Variable.Key} {(e.IsRevealed ? "shown" : "hidden")}");
        Block.RedeployRequested += (_, e) => Write($"RedeployRequested {e.Request.ChangeCount} change(s)");
        Block.Redeployed += (_, e) => Write($"Redeployed {string.Join(", ", e.Request.Environments)}");
        Block.PropertyChanged += (_, e) =>
        {
            if (e.Property == EnvVariables.ViewModeProperty || e.Property == EnvVariables.RedeployStateProperty)
            {
                View.Text = $"View: {Block.ViewMode} · Banner: {Block.RedeployState}";
            }
        };
        View.Text = $"View: {Block.ViewMode} · Banner: {Block.RedeployState}";
    }

    private void Write(string line)
    {
        _lines.Insert(0, line);
        if (_lines.Count > 8)
        {
            _lines.RemoveAt(_lines.Count - 1);
        }
        Log.Text = string.Join(Environment.NewLine, _lines);
    }
}
```

### Texts

Every word is in `Labels` (`EnvVariablesLabels`), with formats as functions so the word order can change.

```csharp
block.Labels = new EnvVariablesLabels
{
    Title = "Variables d’environnement",
    AddButton = "Ajouter",
    ScopeName = (env, key) => $"{key} en {env}",
};
```

## API reference

### EnvVariables

A project's environment variables and secrets (Arc Env variables, design reference): every row is a value and the environments it applies to, shown as a matrix of switches. Values stay masked until revealed and sensitive values are write-only. People search keys, add one variable or paste a whole .env file, edit or remove a value inline, compare two environments by fingerprint and copy a missing value across. Every change marks its row and opens a banner that redeploys the affected environments through `RedeployAction`; a failed deployment keeps the changes and offers to retry. Below `CompactWidth` the rows stack with labelled environment pills.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Title` | `string?` | `null` | The heading; null shows `Title`. |
| `ProjectName` | `string?` | `null` | The project's name, set in monospace before the key count; null shows the count alone. |
| `VariablesSource` | `IEnumerable?` | `null` | The rows, when you give them as a list to follow (observed when it raises collection changes); it wins over `Variables`. |
| `SampleDotenv` | `string` | `""` | The text the .env form starts with when it is opened by the import button (empty starts blank). |
| `DefaultAddEnvironments` | `IList<string>?` | `null` | The environment keys chosen when the add panel opens; null chooses all but the last (all of a single one). |
| `ViewMode` | `EnvVariablesView` | `Variables` | Which table shows (two-way). |
| `SearchText` | `string` | `""` | The search text (two-way): a case-insensitive part of a key name; values are never searched. |
| `CompareLeft` | `string?` | `null` | The compare view's left environment key (two-way); null uses the second environment (or the first). |
| `CompareRight` | `string?` | `null` | The compare view's right environment key (two-way); null uses the last environment. |
| `ShowMatching` | `bool` | `false` | Whether the compare view lists keys with the same value too (two-way). |
| `RedeployAction` | `Func<EnvRedeployRequest, CancellationToken, Task>?` | `null` | Deploys the changes: awaited when Redeploy is pressed (or `RedeployAsync` is called) with what the banner counted and a token that `CancelRedeploy` (or the block leaving the window) cancels. An exception fails the deployment: the banner turns red with the message and offers to retry, and the changes stay. Null simulates a deployment of about 1.7 seconds. |
| `RedeployCommand` | `ICommand?` | `null` | Run when a deployment starts, with the `EnvRedeployRequest` as the parameter, before `RedeployAction`; when it cannot execute the deployment does not start. |
| `IsReadOnly` | `bool` | `false` | Hides adding, importing, editing and the environment switches' input: the block only shows and compares. |
| `IsFramed` | `bool` | `true` | Draws the block as a bordered, rounded card (the default); false sits it flat on the page. |
| `Labels` | `EnvVariablesLabels` | – | Every text the block shows or announces. |
| `CompactWidth` | `double` | `760` | Below this width of the block the rows stack (760, from the theme). |
| `NarrowWidth` | `double` | `560` | Below this width the side insets tighten and buttons fill the width (560, from the theme). |
| `PendingChangeCount` | `int` | – | *Read-only.* The number of changes waiting for a deployment. |
| `PendingEnvironments` | `IReadOnlyList<string>` | – | *Read-only.* The keys of the environments that keep old values until the next deployment, in column order. |
| `RedeployState` | `EnvRedeployState` | – | *Read-only.* Where the redeploy banner stands. |
| `Variables` | `AvaloniaList<EnvVariable>` | `null` | The rows, in any order (the block shows them by key); `VariablesSource` wins when set. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `VariablesChanged` | `EnvVariablesChangedEventArgs` | Raised after every change of the rows (add, import, save, removal, switch, copy across) with all rows. |
| `VariableAdded` | `EnvVariableEventArgs` | Raised when a variable was added from the add panel. |
| `VariableSaved` | `EnvVariableEventArgs` | Raised when a value was saved in the inline editor. |
| `VariableRemoved` | `EnvVariableEventArgs` | Raised when a variable was removed. |
| `VariablesImported` | `EnvVariablesImportedEventArgs` | Raised when variables were imported from a .env file. |
| `ScopeToggled` | `EnvScopeEventArgs` | Raised when a row was turned on or off for an environment. |
| `ScopeConflict` | `EnvScopeEventArgs` | Raised when a switch was refused because another row of the key covers the environment; set Handled to show your own message instead of the note. |
| `ValueRevealed` | `EnvValueRevealedEventArgs` | Raised just before a value shows (fill `Value` here to load it lazily) and after it hid. |
| `ValueCopied` | `EnvValueCopiedEventArgs` | Raised when a value was copied to another environment from the compare view. |
| `RedeployRequested` | `EnvRedeployEventArgs` | Raised when a deployment is about to start; set Cancel to stop it. |
| `Redeployed` | `EnvRedeployEventArgs` | Raised when a deployment finished. |
| `RedeployFailed` | `EnvRedeployEventArgs` | Raised when a deployment failed (the changes are kept). |

Pseudo-classes: `:compact`, `:narrow`, `:framed`, `:readonly`, `:redeploy-pending`, `:redeploy-running`, `:redeploy-done`, `:redeploy-failed`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

### EnvVariable

One row of `EnvVariables`: a value and the environments it applies to. A key can have several rows (one value for development and staging, another for production), but each environment is covered by at most one row of a key. The value stays out of the visual tree until someone reveals it; a sensitive value is never shown.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Id` | `string` | `""` | A stable identifier (a new GUID by default). |
| `Key` | `string` | `""` | The variable's name (letters, digits and underscores, not starting with a digit). |
| `Value` | `string?` | `null` | The value. Shown only while revealed and copied only from there; a sensitive row may leave it null and give a `Fingerprint` instead. Fill it lazily in `ValueRevealed` if you prefer. |
| `IsSensitive` | `bool` | `false` | Whether the value is write-only: it can be replaced but never revealed, copied or made readable again. |
| `UpdatedAt` | `DateTimeOffset?` | `null` | When the value last changed (the second line reads "Updated Mar 4 by …"). |
| `UpdatedBy` | `string?` | `null` | Who changed it last. |
| `Fingerprint` | `string?` | `null` | The short fingerprint the compare view shows instead of the value (equal values, equal fingerprints). Null computes it from `Value` (the first 6 hex digits of its SHA-256); give your own for values you do not load. |
| `IsPendingDeploy` | `bool` | `false` | Whether the row changed since the last deployment (a dot after the key and "not deployed yet"). |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### EnvEnvironment

An environment of `EnvVariables`: a column of the matrix and a choice in the pills and selects.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Key` | `string` | `""` | The stable identifier that `Environments` refers to ("production"). |
| `Name` | `string` | `""` | The name people read ("Production"). |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### EnvRedeployRequest

What a redeploy covers, handed to `RedeployAction` and the redeploy events.

### EnvVariablesChangedEventArgs

Arguments of `VariablesChanged`: one change and every row after it.

Derives from `RoutedEventArgs`: every member of `RoutedEventArgs` works as well.

## Accessibility

Keyboard:

- Tab moves through Import .env, Add variable, the banner's button, the search, the view switch, then each row: the eye
  (not on sensitive rows; the copy button comes before it while a value shows), one switch per environment and the edit
  button.
- Space or Enter turns a switch, reveals or hides a value, and opens or closes the editor.
- The view switch and the add panel's form switch move and choose with the arrow keys.
- In the editor and the add panel, Enter saves and Escape closes; the focus goes back to the button that opened them.
- Escape in the search clears it.

Screen readers:

- Each switch is a toggle named "<Environment> for <KEY>", in a group named "Environments for <KEY>"; the column header is
  not read. The eye is "Reveal <KEY>", the copy button "Copy <KEY>", the edit button "Edit <KEY>".
- A hidden value reads "Hidden value" and a sensitive one "Write-only value"; the bullets are not read. A compare cell
  reads the environment, "Fingerprint" and the digits.
- The refused-switch note is an assertive live region; changes are announced politely: "KEY now on in Staging",
  "KEY updated", "KEY created in Development and Staging", "KEY deleted from Production", "Imported 3 variables into …",
  "KEY now set in Staging", "Deployed Production", and a failed deployment with its message. Revealing a value and search
  results are not announced.
- The focus never falls back to the window: after saving it returns to the edit button, after adding or importing to the
  button that opened the panel, after removing to the next row's edit button, after Copy to the next Copy to button (or Show
  identical), after Clear search to the search box, and after the banner closes to the search box.

## Motion

- **Opening and closing**: the banner, the add panel, the editor, the conflict note and new rows grow on a smooth
  critically damped spring (about 700 ms) with the opacity on the same curve; they close, and removed or filtered rows
  collapse, in 180 ms on an accelerating curve. Switching between the single and the .env form is instant.
- **Saving, adding and importing**: the row glows in the accent tint for 1.6 seconds (held, then fading).
- **Switches**: the box fills in 120 ms and grows from 60% on a quick spring while the check mark draws.
- **Values**: the bullets fade up and out while the value rises in; the copy button pops in.
- **Banner**: the count and the lines swap with a short exit and a rising entry; on success the icon pops to a check and
  the tint eases to green, and the banner closes 2.8 seconds later. The conflict note closes after 3.8 seconds.
- **Views**: the old view fades out in 120 ms, then the new one rises 6 px and fades in over 240 ms while the height
  springs to fit.
- Reduced motion and Off apply every change at once, without the glow.

## Related

- API keys, Webhooks and Integrations, the other Developer blocks.
- `SearchField`, `SegmentedControl` and `Switch`, used for the toolbar and the compare controls.
- `CopyButton` for copying a single value elsewhere.
- `Alert` for a banner that is not tied to a list of changes.

# File upload

> A complete file selection flow with constraints, progress, and error feedback.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc.Blocks`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc.Blocks --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/blocks/file-upload

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.FileUploadPreviewDemo">
    <!-- Images and PDFs up to 10 MB, uploaded as they are added. A name containing "fail" fails once; Retry succeeds. -->
    <StackPanel MaxWidth="520" Spacing="16">
        <arc:FileUpload x:Name="Upload" Accept="image/*,.pdf" MaxSize="10485760" />
        <arc:Button Content="Add sample files" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" HorizontalAlignment="Left" Click="OnAddSamples" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class FileUploadPreviewDemo : UserControl
{
    public FileUploadPreviewDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Upload.Uploader = FileUploadDemoData.CreateUploader();
    }

    private void OnAddSamples(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) => Upload.AddFiles(FileUploadDemoData.Samples());
}
```

## When to use

Use `FileUpload` for documents or media when people need to see upload progress and recover from invalid files.

- **Uploads with per-file progress**, retry and remove.
- **Attachments that must be validated** by type and size before they upload.
- **Uploads that stop when a file is removed**: removing a file cancels its upload's token.

## When not to use

- **Picking files without upload state**: use `FileDropzone`.
- **Data that needs column mapping** after it is uploaded: use an import flow built for it.

## Usage

```xml
<arc:FileUpload x:Name="Attachments" Accept="image/*,.pdf" MaxSize="10485760" />
```

```csharp
Attachments.Uploader = async (item, progress, token) =>
{
    await using var stream = await item.File!.OpenReadAsync();
    await UploadWithProgressAsync(item.Name, stream, progress, token);   // report 0-100; throw to mark the file failed
};
```

Each accepted file is uploaded through `Uploader` as soon as it is added: report 0 to 100 through the progress, return
when the upload is done, throw to mark the file as failed. The token is cancelled when the file is removed, when a new
file replaces it (`Multiple="False"`) and when the control leaves the visual tree. Without an uploader, files are only
validated and listed, and an accepted file shows a check mark.

### Type and size

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.FileUploadValidationDemo">
    <!-- No uploader: files are only checked and listed. The CSV is accepted, the archive has the wrong type, the PDF is too large. -->
    <StackPanel MaxWidth="520" Spacing="16">
        <arc:FileUpload x:Name="Upload"
                        Accept=".csv,text/plain"
                        MaxSize="1048576"
                        Label="Import contacts"
                        Description="CSV or plain text, up to 1 MB." />
        <arc:Button Content="Add sample files" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" HorizontalAlignment="Left" Click="OnAddSamples" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class FileUploadValidationDemo : UserControl
{
    public FileUploadValidationDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
    }

    private void OnAddSamples(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) =>
        Upload.AddFiles(
        [
            new FileUploadItem(null, "contacts.csv", 38_912),
            new FileUploadItem(null, "contacts-backup.zip", 204_800),
            new FileUploadItem(null, "contacts.pdf", 3_145_728),
        ]);
}
```

`Accept` takes comma-separated extensions (`.pdf`), MIME types (`application/zip`) and wildcards (`image/*`).
Avalonia's files carry no MIME type, so the control looks it up from the file's extension in a built-in table of common
types; an unknown extension matches only by extension. `MaxSize` is the largest size in bytes. A rejected file stays in
the list with its error, "This file type is not accepted." or "File is larger than 1 MB.", and is not uploaded. The
file picker is filtered by `Accept` too.

```xml
<arc:FileUpload Accept=".csv,text/plain" MaxSize="1048576"
                Label="Import contacts" Description="CSV or plain text, up to 1 MB." />
```

### One file

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.FileUploadSingleFileDemo">
    <!-- One file at a time: a new file replaces the old one and cancels its upload. -->
    <arc:FileUpload x:Name="Upload"
                    MaxWidth="520"
                    Multiple="False"
                    Accept="image/*"
                    Label="Upload a cover image"
                    Description="PNG, JPEG or WebP. A new image replaces the current one." />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class FileUploadSingleFileDemo : UserControl
{
    public FileUploadSingleFileDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Upload.Uploader = FileUploadDemoData.CreateUploader();
    }
}
```

With `Multiple="False"` the picker takes one file and a new file replaces the list, cancelling the running upload.

```xml
<arc:FileUpload Multiple="False" Accept="image/*" Label="Upload a cover image" />
```

### Disabled

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.FileUploadDisabledDemo">
    <arc:FileUpload MaxWidth="520"
                    IsEnabled="False"
                    Description="Uploads are paused while the workspace is read-only." />
</UserControl>
```

`IsEnabled="False"` dims the dropzone and stops it from opening the picker or taking drops.

### The file list

`Files` is the list, newest last, as `FileUploadItem` objects. It binds two-way: the control replaces it when files are
added or removed and raises `FilesChanged` with the new list. Each item has its `File` (an `IStorageFile`), `Name`,
`Size`, `Error`, and the upload's `Status` (`None`, `Uploading`, `Done`, `Failed`) and `Progress`.

```csharp
upload.FilesChanged += (_, e) => SaveButton.IsEnabled = e.Files.All(f => f.Status == FileUploadStatus.Done);
```

`BrowseAsync()` opens the picker, `AddFilesAsync(storageItems)` adds files from your own source (a paste, another
drop target), and `AddFiles(items)` adds items you create with a name and a size. `Retry(item)` and `Remove(item)` do
what the row buttons do.

### Text

`Label` ("Upload files"), `Description` ("Drop files here or browse from your device.") and `BrowseLabel` ("Browse")
are properties. While files are over the dropzone the label reads "Drop to add files" (or "Drop to add a file"). The
status line reads, for example, "2 files added. 1 file needs attention.", "report.pdf uploaded.",
"report.pdf could not be uploaded." and "report.pdf removed."; `Status` holds the last one.

## API reference

### FileUpload

A complete file selection flow: a dropzone that takes dropped files or opens the file picker, validation of type (`Accept`) and size (`MaxSize`), one upload per accepted file through `Uploader` with a progress bar and a counted percentage, and Retry and Remove on every row. Rejected files stay listed with their error; removing a file cancels its upload. A polite status line says what was added, rejected, uploaded, failed or removed.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Accept` | `string?` | `null` | Accepted types, comma separated: extensions (".pdf"), MIME types ("application/zip") and wildcards ("image/*"). Rejected files stay listed with an error. Empty accepts everything. |
| `MaxSize` | `long?` | `null` | The largest accepted file in bytes; larger files are listed with an error. Null or 0 sets no limit. |
| `Multiple` | `bool` | `true` | Whether several files can be added; when false a new file replaces the list (and cancels running uploads). |
| `Label` | `string` | `"Upload files"` | The dropzone's heading. |
| `Description` | `string` | `"Drop files here or browse from your device."` | The dropzone's help text; it also describes the dropzone to screen readers. |
| `BrowseLabel` | `string` | `"Browse"` | The text at the dropzone's end. |
| `Files` | `IReadOnlyList<FileUploadItem>` | – | The file list, newest last. Two-way: the control replaces it when files are added or removed. |
| `Uploader` | `Func<FileUploadItem, IProgress<double>, CancellationToken, Task>?` | `null` | Uploads one accepted file: report 0 to 100 through the progress, return when done, throw to mark the file failed. The token is cancelled when the file is removed or replaced, or the control leaves the tree. Null only lists files. |
| `IsDragging` | `bool` | – | *Read-only.* True while files are dragged over the dropzone. |
| `Status` | `string` | – | *Read-only.* The last status message ("2 files added.", "report.pdf uploaded."); empty until the first one. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `FilesChanged` | `FileUploadFilesChangedEventArgs` | Raised after files were added or removed, with the new list. |

Pseudo-classes: `:dragging`, `:zonehover`, `:zonepressed`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

### FileUploadItem

A file in a `FileUpload` list: the picked or dropped file, its name and size, the validation error when it was rejected, and the state of its upload.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Error` | `string?` | – | Why the file was rejected (wrong type or too large); null for an accepted file. |
| `Status` | `FileUploadStatus` | – | *Read-only.* Where the upload stands. |
| `Progress` | `double` | – | *Read-only.* How far the upload got, 0 to 100; it never goes back while the upload runs. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### FileUploadStatus

Where a `FileUploadItem`'s upload stands.

Derives from `Enum`: every member of `Enum` works as well.

### FileUploadFilesChangedEventArgs

Carries the file list after files were added or removed.

Derives from `RoutedEventArgs`: every member of `RoutedEventArgs` works as well.

## Accessibility

- The dropzone is a button named by `Label` and described by `Description`.
- A polite live region announces added, rejected, uploaded, failed and removed files.
- Retry and Remove are named with the file name ("Retry report.pdf", "Remove report.pdf"); the check is named "Ready" or "Uploaded".
- After a file is removed, focus moves to the next row's Remove button, else the previous row's, else the dropzone.
- Keyboard focus rings are 2 px outside the dropzone and the buttons. Hover colors apply to a mouse or a pen only.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Enter` / `Space` on the dropzone | Open the file picker. |
| `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` | Move through the dropzone and each row's Retry and Remove buttons. |

## Motion

- While files are over the dropzone its edge and fill turn to the accent, the cloud lifts 3 px and the label swaps to "Drop to add files".
- Rows open and close their height on a spring, so the list closes the gap when a file is removed. The status line opens the same way and each new message rises in.
- One spring drives the progress bar and the counted percentage. When the count reads 100% the phase turns to "Uploaded", the bar folds away and a check pops in and draws.
- A failed upload swaps its phase to "Upload failed" and pops in Retry.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| Row and status line height | Smooth spring, opacity in 240 ms | Appears at once, fades out in 120 ms | Immediate |
| Label, phase and status swaps | Rise and blur, 240 ms in, 160 ms out | Fade out in 120 ms | Immediate |
| Progress | Smooth spring | Jumps | Jumps |
| Check and Retry | Pop on a snappy spring, the check draws in 240 ms | Appear at once | Immediate |
| Dropzone colors and cloud | 240 ms; the cloud on the CSS spring | Immediate | Immediate |

### Responsive behavior

The dropzone and the list fill their container and file names are cut with an ellipsis on one line. On touch, tapping
the dropzone opens the platform's picker. Dropping files from the operating system works in the desktop hosts and in
the browser host (Avalonia 12.1 turns a browser drop into files).

### Performance

Uploads run through your `Uploader`, one call per accepted file, with no limit on how many run at once: queue large
batches yourself. The list is not virtualized, so keep it to a reasonable number of files.

## Related

- `FileDropzone` for picking files without upload state.
- `Progress` for showing how much of a single known task is complete.

# Media player

> An audio player with cover art, a playlist, a seek bar, previous and next, and volume with mute; skipping wraps around and keeps playing or paused, and the playing row shows moving bars.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc.Blocks`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc.Blocks --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/blocks/media-player

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.MediaPlayerPreviewDemo">
    <!-- Three synthesized loops with drawn covers (MediaPlayerDemoData). The gallery plays them through the host's audio backend. -->
    <arc:MediaPlayer x:Name="Player" Margin="0,12" HorizontalAlignment="Center" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class MediaPlayerPreviewDemo : UserControl
{
    public MediaPlayerPreviewDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Player.Tracks.AddRange(MediaPlayerDemoData.Tracks());
    }
}
```

## When to use

`MediaPlayer` plays a short list of audio tracks in one card. The current track's cover and title sit on top, with
previous, play and next buttons beside the title, a seek bar with the elapsed and total time under it, then the
playlist with a mute button and a volume slider in its heading. Pressing a row plays that track; pressing the current
row pauses or resumes it.

- **Episodes, lessons and samples.** A podcast's latest episodes, the audio of a course module or a set of sound
  previews next to the product they belong to.
- **Mixes and soundtracks.** A band's page, a game's soundtrack or a few ambient loops for a focus app.
- **Recorded calls and notes.** A short list of voice notes or call recordings to review in place.

## When not to use

- **A large library.** The playlist shows every track as a row, without search, sorting or virtualization; build a
  library with a `DataGrid` or a list and use the player for what is queued.
- **Video.** The block plays audio only; the cover is a still picture.
- **A single sound.** For one clip, a play button with the time is enough.

## Usage

### Tracks and audio

Each `MediaTrack` has a `Title`, an `Artist` and an `Album` (shown as "artist · album" under the title), a `Cover` image
with its `CoverDescription` for screen readers, the audio as an `AudioSource` and a `Duration` that the playlist shows
until the track is loaded (the length the audio reports then replaces it). `AudioSource.FromUri`, `FromFile` and
`FromBytes` cover addresses, local files and audio held in memory; `WavFile.Encode` writes generated samples as a WAV
file, which is how the gallery makes its three loops.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:MediaPlayer>
        <arc:MediaTrack Title="Harbor lights" Artist="Low Static" Album="Night ferry" Duration="0:0:24" />
        <arc:MediaTrack Title="Paper kites" Artist="Low Static" Album="Night ferry" Duration="0:0:24" />
    </arc:MediaPlayer>
</UserControl>
```

```csharp
player.Tracks.Add(new MediaTrack
{
    Title = "Harbor lights",
    Artist = "Low Static",
    Album = "Night ferry",
    Source = AudioSource.FromUri(new Uri("https://cdn.example.dev/audio/harbor-lights.mp3")),
});
```

### Making sound

The player plays through `ArcAudio.Backend`, or through its own `AudioBackend` when you set one. The default backend
keeps time without making sound, so the player works the same everywhere (and in tests); `IsAudible` tells which one is
in use. For sound, add a platform package and select it when the app starts:

- **Desktop** (Windows, macOS, Linux): `TKCode.Arc.Audio.Native`, built on miniaudio, plays WAV, MP3 and FLAC.
- **WebAssembly**: `TKCode.Arc.Audio.Browser` plays through the browser's audio element, so it plays what the browser
  plays. Browsers only start audio after the person has pressed something on the page.

The gallery's desktop and browser hosts both select their backend, so the demos on this page play.

### Playing, skipping and the end of a track

`IsPlaying`, `SelectedIndex` and `Volume` are two-way. `Play`, `Pause`, `TogglePlay`, `NextTrack`, `PreviousTrack`,
`PlayTrack` and `Seek` do from code what the buttons do. Skipping wraps around (after the last track comes the first)
and keeps the player playing or paused as it was; a new track always starts from the beginning. Previous always moves to
the previous track, wherever the current one is. A track that plays to its end stops and returns to 0:00 without moving
on, and raises `TrackEnded`; handle it to continue with the next track.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.MediaPlayerEventsDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12" Margin="0,12" HorizontalAlignment="Center">
        <arc:MediaPlayer x:Name="Player" />
        <StackPanel Orientation="Horizontal" Spacing="8" HorizontalAlignment="Center">
            <arc:Button x:Name="Previous" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Content="PreviousTrack()" />
            <arc:Button x:Name="Toggle" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Content="TogglePlay()" />
            <arc:Button x:Name="Skip" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Content="Seek(0:20)" />
            <arc:Button x:Name="Mute" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" Content="ToggleMute()" />
        </StackPanel>
        <TextBlock x:Name="State" HorizontalAlignment="Center" TextAlignment="Center" />
        <TextBlock x:Name="Log" HorizontalAlignment="Center" TextAlignment="Center" TextWrapping="Wrap" MaxWidth="520" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class MediaPlayerEventsDemo : UserControl
{
    private readonly List<string> _log = [];

    public MediaPlayerEventsDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Player.Tracks.AddRange(MediaPlayerDemoData.Tracks());
        Previous.Click += (_, _) => Player.PreviousTrack();
        Toggle.Click += (_, _) => Player.TogglePlay();
        Skip.Click += (_, _) => Player.Seek(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(20));
        Mute.Click += (_, _) => Player.ToggleMute();
        Player.SelectedTrackChanged += (_, e) => Add($"{e.ChangeSource}: {e.OldTrack?.Title} → {e.NewTrack?.Title}");
        Player.TrackEnded += (_, e) => Add($"Ended: {e.Track.Title}");
        Player.PlaybackFailed += (_, e) => Add($"Failed: {e.Track.Title} ({e.Message})");
        Player.PropertyChanged += (_, e) =>
        {
            if (e.Property == MediaPlayer.IsPlayingProperty || e.Property == MediaPlayer.VolumeProperty
                || e.Property == MediaPlayer.PositionProperty || e.Property == MediaPlayer.IsAudibleProperty)
            {
                ShowState();
            }
        };
        ShowState();
    }

    private void ShowState()
    {
        var sound = Player.IsAudible ? "audible backend" : "silent backend";
        State.Text = $"{(Player.IsPlaying ? "Playing" : "Paused")} at {MediaPlayerTime.Format(Player.Position)} · volume {Player.Volume:P0} · {sound}";
    }

    private void Add(string line)
    {
        _log.Insert(0, line);
        if (_log.Count > 4)
        {
            _log.RemoveAt(_log.Count - 1);
        }
        Log.Text = string.Join("\n", _log);
    }
}
```

### Volume and mute

The volume runs from 0 to 1 and starts at 0.7. The mute button sets it to zero and remembers it; pressing it again
restores that volume, or `DefaultVolume` when the slider was dragged to zero. `IsMuted` is true whenever the volume is
zero.

### Without the card

`IsFramed="False"` drops the border, the background and the rounded corners, for a player that sits on a page or a
panel of its own.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.MediaPlayerFlatDemo">
    <!-- IsFramed="False": no card, square cover corners; the player sits on the page's own surface. -->
    <arc:MediaPlayer x:Name="Player" IsFramed="False" Margin="0,12" HorizontalAlignment="Center" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class MediaPlayerFlatDemo : UserControl
{
    public MediaPlayerFlatDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Player.Tracks.AddRange(MediaPlayerDemoData.Tracks());
    }
}
```

### Narrow containers

The layout follows the player's own width. Below `CompactWidth` (420) the padding tightens from 20 to 14, the cover
becomes taller (1.7:1 instead of 2.2:1), the title shrinks from 28 to 22, the buttons and the gaps between them get
smaller and the volume slider shortens from 88 to 64. The player grows to at most 520 wide.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.MediaPlayerCompactDemo">
    <!-- 360 wide, below CompactWidth (420): tighter padding, a taller cover, smaller buttons and title, a shorter volume slider. -->
    <arc:MediaPlayer x:Name="Player" Width="360" Margin="0,12" HorizontalAlignment="Center" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class MediaPlayerCompactDemo : UserControl
{
    public MediaPlayerCompactDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Player.Tracks.AddRange(MediaPlayerDemoData.Tracks());
        Player.SelectedIndex = 2;
    }
}
```

### Events and texts

`SelectedTrackChanged` carries the old and new track and what moved the player (`Code`, `Skip` or `Playlist`);
`PlaybackFailed` carries the backend's message, and the player pauses. Every word the player shows or reads to screen
readers is in `Labels`, a `MediaPlayerLabels` you can replace to translate it; texts with values are functions, and
`FormatTime` decides how times are written.

## API reference

### MediaPlayer

An audio player with a playlist: the current track's cover, title and artist, previous / play / next buttons, a seek bar with the elapsed and total time, a mute button with a volume slider, and the tracks as rows that play when pressed. Playback goes through `Backend` (or `AudioBackend`): add `TKCode.Arc.Audio.Native` on desktop or `TKCode.Arc.Audio.Browser` in WebAssembly for sound; the default backend keeps time silently. Skipping wraps around and keeps playing or paused as it was; a track that reaches its end stops and returns to 0:00.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SelectedIndex` | `int` | `0` | The index of the current track in `Tracks` (two-way); −1 when the playlist is empty. |
| `IsPlaying` | `bool` | `false` | Whether the current track is playing (two-way): set it to play or pause. |
| `Volume` | `double` | `0.7` | The output volume from 0 to 1 (two-way, 0.7); 0 is muted. |
| `DefaultVolume` | `double` | `0.7` | The volume the mute button restores when nothing louder was muted before (0.7). |
| `IsFramed` | `bool` | `true` | Draws a bordered card with rounded corners (true); false lays the player flat on the page. |
| `AudioBackend` | `IAudioBackend?` | `null` | The backend that plays the audio; null uses `Backend`. Set it before the player is shown. |
| `CompactWidth` | `double` | `420` | Below this width the player tightens (smaller paddings, buttons and title; a taller cover). 420. |
| `Labels` | `MediaPlayerLabels` | – | Every word the player shows or reads to screen readers. |
| `SelectedTrack` | `MediaTrack?` | – | *Read-only.* The current track; null when the playlist is empty. |
| `Position` | `TimeSpan` | – | *Read-only.* How far into the current track playback is, as last reported by the backend. |
| `Duration` | `TimeSpan` | – | *Read-only.* The current track's length: what the backend reports once it is loaded, the track's own `Duration` before. |
| `IsMuted` | `bool` | – | *Read-only.* Whether the volume is zero (the mute button then offers to unmute). |
| `IsCompact` | `bool` | – | *Read-only.* Whether the compact layout applies (the player is narrower than `CompactWidth`). |
| `IsAudible` | `bool` | – | *Read-only.* Whether the backend makes sound (false for the silent default backend). |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `SelectedTrackChanged` | `MediaTrackChangedEventArgs` | Raised when the current track changes. |
| `TrackEnded` | `MediaTrackEventArgs` | Raised when the current track played to its end (the player has stopped and returned to the start). |
| `PlaybackFailed` | `MediaTrackEventArgs` | Raised when the backend could not load or play the current track. |

Pseudo-classes: `:playing`, `:muted`, `:compact`, `:framed`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

### MediaTrack

One entry of a `MediaPlayer`'s playlist: what it is called, who made it, its cover and the audio to play.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Title` | `string` | `""` | The track's name: the player's heading while it is current, and its row in the playlist. |
| `Artist` | `string?` | `null` | Who made it; shown under the heading before the album. |
| `Album` | `string?` | `null` | The album or collection; shown under the heading after the artist. |
| `Cover` | `IImage?` | `null` | The cover art, drawn to fill the cover frame (cropped, not stretched). |
| `CoverDescription` | `string?` | `null` | What the cover shows, for screen readers. |
| `Source` | `AudioSource?` | `null` | The audio to play; a track without one can be selected but stays silent. |
| `Duration` | `TimeSpan` | `00:00:00` | The track's length, shown in the playlist before it has been loaded; the player replaces it with the length the audio reports once the track is loaded. |
| `Tag` | `object?` | `null` | Anything you want to keep with the track. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### MediaPlayerLabels

Every word `MediaPlayer` shows or reads to screen readers, in English by default. Replace the instance to translate or reword; texts that take values are functions so that word order can change.

## Accessibility

- **Tab** goes through previous, play and next, the seek bar, the mute button, the volume slider and each playlist
  row.
- **Enter** or **Space** presses the focused button or row.
- On the seek bar, **Left** and **Right** (or **Down** and **Up**) move by a tenth of a second, **Page Up** and
  **Page Down** by a tenth of the track, **Home** and **End** to the start and the end. On the volume slider the arrows
  move by 1%, the page keys by 10%.
- The player is named "Audio player". The buttons are named "Previous track", "Play" or "Pause", "Next track" and
  "Mute audio" or "Unmute audio"; the sliders are "Seek" plus the title (its value reads "0:12 of 0:24") and "Volume"
  (its value reads "70%").
- The title is a level-2 heading and "Playlist" a level-3 heading. A row is named "Play" plus its title, or "Pause" plus
  its title while that track plays; the moving bars are named "Playing".
- The cover is read with its `CoverDescription`; a track without a cover shows an empty plate that screen readers skip.
- Focus rings show only for the keyboard.

## Motion

- **Changing track**: the covers crossfade over 240 ms. The old title block lifts 10 px and fades while the new one rises
  10 px into place on the Smooth spring, always upward whichever way you skipped. The rail beside the current row
  springs to the new row (Smooth, about 550 ms).
- **Play and pause**: the old glyph shrinks to 60% and blurs out while the new one grows from 60% out of a 2 px blur, in
  120 ms. Pressed buttons shrink to 94% in 120 ms; hover plates fade in 160 ms.
- **Playing**: three bars in the current row rise and fall between 30% and full height, 900 ms each way, a third of a
  cycle apart. They run only while the row is on screen.
- **Seeking**: the backend reports the position about four times a second; in between, the seek bar moves on with the
  clock, so it glides instead of stepping. The slider's dot grows by 20% while it is dragged.
- Reduced motion changes covers, titles, the rail and the play glyph at once, keeps the bars still at 60% and the seek
  bar moves with each report. Off applies every change at once.

## Related

- File upload, the other Media block.
- `Slider` for a general-purpose range input.
- `Carousel` and `ImageCompare` for browsing pictures.

# Week calendar

> A week planner where you drag to add, move and resize events and undo the last change, with a month and calendar toggles beside the grid, an all-day row, and three-day or agenda views when narrow.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc.Blocks`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc.Blocks --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/blocks/week-calendar

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.WeekCalendarPreviewDemo">
    <!-- A designer's week around today: six calendars (Health hidden), the sidebar from 1100 wide. Drag across empty
         time to add an event, drag events to move them or their bottom edge to resize, click one to edit it. -->
    <arc:WeekCalendar x:Name="Calendar" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class WeekCalendarPreviewDemo : UserControl
{
    public WeekCalendarPreviewDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Calendar.Calendars.AddRange(WeekCalendarDemoData.CreateCalendars());
        // Built around this week, so the current time line has past events behind it and coming ones ahead.
        Calendar.Events.AddRange(WeekCalendarDemoData.CreateEvents(WeekCalendarDemoData.ThisMonday()));
    }
}
```

## When to use

`WeekCalendar` is a full planning surface for a week at a time, the way a desktop calendar app shows it. A toolbar moves
between weeks and switches the view; a sidebar holds a month to jump around in and the calendars to show or hide; the grid
has a header of days, an all-day row and the hours, with each day's events laid out side by side where they overlap, the
current time drawn across today, and the past dimmed. People edit in place: drag across empty time to add an event and name
it, drag events between days and times, drag their bottom edge to change their length, click one to edit its title, day,
times and calendar, and undo the last change from a toast or with Ctrl+Z.

- **Scheduling and time blocking.** People see their meetings, focus blocks and trips in one week, how the days fill up, and
  rearrange them by dragging.
- **Team and resource calendars.** Each calendar (a team, a room, a person) has its own color and toggle, so readers can
  compare or narrow down without leaving the page.
- **Bookings seen in another place's time.** Events are instants; `TimeZone` shows them on any clock, and the corner of
  the header says which one.

## When not to use

- **Picking one date.** Use `Calendar` or `DatePicker`; this block is about what happens on the days, not choosing one.
- **Months and years.** The block shows one to seven days. A month grid of events or a year overview is a different design.
- **A short list of upcoming events.** A plain list or `Timeline` reads better than a grid with mostly empty hours.
- **Thousands of events at once.** Pass the weeks around the one shown; the block indexes every event it is given.

## Usage

### Events and calendars

Each `WeekCalendarEvent` has an `Id`, a `Title`, a `Start` and an `End` (exclusive) as `DateTimeOffset` instants, a
`CalendarId`, an optional `Location` and `Attendees` (`ProjectPerson`s; without a picture they get a generated avatar). An
event with `IsAllDay` covers whole dates instead: the dates of `Start` and `End` as written, `End` exclusive, so a three-day
hotel stay starting on Wednesday ends at midnight after Friday. Each `WeekCalendarSource` has an `Id`, a `Name`, a `Color`
(`Blue`, `Green`, `Violet`, `Amber`, `Rose`, `Teal`, `Neutral`, or `Custom` with `CustomColor`) and `IsVisible`, which its
toggle in the sidebar changes. Events of an unknown calendar are gray.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:WeekCalendar x:Name="Planner">
        <arc:WeekCalendar.Calendars>
            <arc:WeekCalendarSource Id="studio" Name="Studio" Color="Blue" />
            <arc:WeekCalendarSource Id="home" Name="Home" Color="Green" />
            <arc:WeekCalendarSource Id="health" Name="Health" Color="Rose" IsVisible="False" />
        </arc:WeekCalendar.Calendars>
    </arc:WeekCalendar>
</UserControl>
```

```csharp
var zone = TimeZoneInfo.FindSystemTimeZoneById("Europe/Berlin");
DateTimeOffset At(int day, int hour, int minute = 0) =>
    new(new DateTime(2026, 10, day, hour, minute, 0), zone.GetUtcOffset(new DateTime(2026, 10, day, hour, minute, 0)));

Planner.TimeZone = zone;
Planner.Events.Add(new WeekCalendarEvent("brief", "Write launch brief", At(19, 9, 30), At(19, 11, 30), "studio"));
Planner.Events.Add(new WeekCalendarEvent("lunch", "Lunch with Noor", At(19, 12), At(19, 13), "home") { Location = "Corner Bistro" });
Planner.Events.Add(new WeekCalendarEvent("hotel", "Hotel: Casa Azul",
    new DateTimeOffset(2026, 10, 21, 0, 0, 0, TimeSpan.Zero), new DateTimeOffset(2026, 10, 24, 0, 0, 0, TimeSpan.Zero), "home")
    { IsAllDay = true });
```

Use `EventsSource` and `CalendarsSource` for collections you own; an `ObservableCollection` is observed, and so is every
property of every event and calendar. Changes made in the same moment are applied together, and the grid updates in place.

```csharp
var events = new ObservableCollection<WeekCalendarEvent>();
calendar.EventsSource = events;

// Later, when a booking comes in, it appears at once and the day's events make room for it.
var start = new DateTimeOffset(DateTime.Today.AddHours(15));
events.Add(new WeekCalendarEvent("call-42", "Client call", start, start.AddMinutes(45), "studio") { Location = "Video room" });
```

### Editing

Editing is on unless `IsReadOnly` is set. Everything snaps to 15 minutes and lasts 15 minutes at least.

- **Draw an event.** Press on empty time and drag (4 pixels start a drag). The 15-minute slot you pressed is the anchor and the
  moving end rounds to the nearest quarter hour, so drawing works upwards too; the draft stays on the day you pressed. When
  you let go, the quick create popover opens beside the draft: type a title and press Enter (an empty title saves as
  "Untitled event"), or pick a calendar first. A click on empty time drafts an hour from the half hour under the pointer.
  New events start in `DefaultCalendarId`, or the first calendar shown.
- **Move an event.** Drag it: it hops a slot at a time and keeps the point you grabbed under the pointer, across days too.
  The other events of the day make room when you drop it. A drag that ends in the slot it started in changes nothing.
- **Resize an event.** Drag its bottom edge (the grip shows on hover); the end rounds to the quarter hour.
- **Edit an event.** Click it (or press Enter on it) for its details: the title, the date, the start and end in 15-minute
  steps, the place, the people and the calendar. Times, the date and the calendar apply as you pick them; the title and the
  place when the popover closes. All-day events show their dates as text and can change title and calendar.
- **Delete and undo.** Delete or Backspace on the focused or selected event, or Delete in its details, removes it. A toast
  rises from the bottom of the calendar for six seconds (`UndoDuration`) with Undo; Ctrl+Z (Cmd+Z on a Mac) does the same.
  Undo has one level and covers the last create, move, resize, time, date or calendar change, or delete; a run of keyboard
  moves of one event, or the changes made in one details popover, undo together. `CanUndo` says whether there is one.
- **The grid scrolls** when you drag near its top or bottom, faster the closer you get, and keeps scrolling while the pointer
  stands still.
- A press outside an open popover only closes it. Escape closes a popover, cancels a drag (the event springs back), and then
  clears the selection. `SelectedEvent` is the selected event, two-way.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.WeekCalendarEditingDemo">
    <!-- Draw, drag, resize, edit and delete: every change is logged with what it was before. -->
    <StackPanel Spacing="16">
        <arc:WeekCalendar x:Name="Calendar" GridHeight="560" InitialScrollTime="08:00" />
        <Border Padding="24,16"
                TextElement.FontFamily="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource BodyFontFamily}"
                CornerRadius="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource RadiusPanel}"
                Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Surface}"
                BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Border}"
                BorderThickness="1">
            <StackPanel Spacing="10">
                <DockPanel>
                    <arc:Checkbox x:Name="ReadOnly" DockPanel.Dock="Right" Content="Read only" />
                    <TextBlock Text="Event log"
                               VerticalAlignment="Center"
                               FontSize="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TypeXS}"
                               FontWeight="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource WeightMedium}"
                               Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
                </DockPanel>
                <TextBlock x:Name="Log"
                           Text="Drag across empty time, move or stretch an event, or press N."
                           TextWrapping="Wrap"
                           FontSize="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TypeSM}"
                           Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
            </StackPanel>
        </Border>
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using System.Globalization;
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class WeekCalendarEditingDemo : UserControl
{
    private static readonly CultureInfo English = CultureInfo.GetCultureInfo("en-US");
    private readonly List<string> _entries = new();

    public WeekCalendarEditingDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Calendar.Calendars.AddRange(WeekCalendarDemoData.CreateEditingCalendars());
        Calendar.Events.AddRange(WeekCalendarDemoData.CreateEditingWeek(WeekCalendarDemoData.ThisMonday()));
        // The calendar has already changed the events (and Events) when these run; persist from here.
        Calendar.EventCreated += (_, e) => Write($"Created \"{e.Event.Title}\", {When(e.Event)}");
        Calendar.EventUpdated += (_, e) => Write(Describe(e.Previous, e.Event));
        Calendar.EventDeleted += (_, e) => Write($"Deleted \"{e.Event.Title}\"");
        ReadOnly.IsCheckedChanged += (_, _) => Calendar.IsReadOnly = ReadOnly.IsChecked == true;
    }

    private static string When(WeekCalendarEvent e) =>
        e.Start.ToLocalTime().ToString("ddd h:mm tt", English) + " – " + e.End.ToLocalTime().ToString("h:mm tt", English);

    private string Describe(WeekCalendarEvent before, WeekCalendarEvent now)
    {
        if (before.Title != now.Title)
        {
            return $"Renamed \"{before.Title}\" to \"{now.Title}\"";
        }
        if (before.CalendarId != now.CalendarId)
        {
            return $"Moved \"{now.Title}\" from {NameOf(before.CalendarId)} to {NameOf(now.CalendarId)}";
        }
        if (before.Location != now.Location)
        {
            return $"\"{now.Title}\" is now at {now.Location ?? "no place"}";
        }
        return $"Moved \"{now.Title}\" from {When(before)} to {When(now)}";
    }

    private string NameOf(string? id) => Calendar.Calendars.FirstOrDefault(c => c.Id == id)?.Name ?? "no calendar";

    private void Write(string entry)
    {
        // Newest first, the last six changes.
        _entries.Insert(0, entry);
        if (_entries.Count > 6)
        {
            _entries.RemoveAt(_entries.Count - 1);
        }
        Log.Text = string.Join(Environment.NewLine, _entries);
    }
}
```

### Saving changes

The calendar edits your data directly: it writes `Start`, `End`, `CalendarId`, `Title` and `Location` on the
`WeekCalendarEvent` objects and adds or removes events in `Events`, or in `EventsSource` when that is a writable list (an
`ObservableCollection` is observed; a plain `List` is re-read). Then it raises `EventCreated` (also when undo brings back a
deleted event), `EventUpdated` with a `Previous` copy of the event from before the change (undo raises it again with the
values swapped), or `EventDeleted` (also when undo removes a new event). Persist from those handlers.

```csharp
calendar.EventCreated += async (_, e) => await api.CreateAsync(e.Event);
calendar.EventUpdated += async (_, e) => await api.UpdateAsync(e.Event, e.Previous);
calendar.EventDeleted += async (_, e) => await api.DeleteAsync(e.Event.Id);
```

A read-only `EventsSource` (an array, a `ReadOnlyObservableCollection`) cannot gain or lose events: the calendar still moves
and edits the event objects, but for a new or deleted event it only raises the event, and your handler changes the collection
it exposes. Set `IsReadOnly` to turn editing off altogether: no drawing, dragging, quick create, deleting or undo, and the
details show as text. New event (and its `NewEventRequested` event) drafts at the next free hour of the focused day from 9 AM;
set `Handled` to open your own form instead. `BeginCreate`, `OpenDetails`, `CloseEditor`, `DeleteEvent`, `Undo` and
`CancelDrag` do the same from code.

```xml
<arc:WeekCalendar IsReadOnly="{Binding IsArchived}" DefaultCalendarId="studio" UndoDuration="0:0:8" />
```

### Touch

On touch screens a long press (about 380 ms without moving) starts drawing on empty time or lifts an event to move it;
otherwise a vertical swipe scrolls the hours. Below 640 wide a sideways swipe changes the days: the neighbouring days come
along under your finger, and letting go past a fifth of the width (or with a flick) carries on to them without a jump; a
shorter swipe springs back. Popovers open under the event there (or over it near the bottom), kept 8 pixels inside the sides.

### Views and navigation

`View` is `Week` (seven days from `FirstDayOfWeek`, Monday by default), `WorkWeek` (Monday to Friday) or `Day`; it is two-way.
`Date` is the focused day, also two-way: the range shown always holds it, and setting a day outside it moves the calendar
there. Today, previous and next move by a week (a day in the day view, three days in the three-day view) and keep the
focused weekday; the month in the sidebar jumps to the range around any day. `GoToToday`, `Next`, `Previous`, `GoTo`,
`FocusDay` and `ScrollToTime` do the same from code. `RangeStart`, `RangeEnd`, `RangeTitle` and `EffectiveView` report what is
shown; `RangeChanged` says what moved it, in which direction.

The grid opens at the hour of the first event in view (8 AM without one), or at `InitialScrollTime`. Today also scrolls the
current time to a third of the way down. `StartHour` and `EndHour` limit the hours shown; events outside them are cut at the
edge.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.WeekCalendarWorkHoursDemo">
    <!-- Office hours only: Monday to Friday, 7 AM to 8 PM, without the sidebar. -->
    <arc:WeekCalendar x:Name="Calendar"
                      View="WorkWeek"
                      StartHour="7"
                      EndHour="20"
                      GridHeight="560"
                      IsSidebarVisible="False"
                      ShowWeekendShading="False" />
</UserControl>
```


### Narrow containers

The calendar reads its own width. From 1100 it shows the sidebar (`IsSidebarVisible` forces it on or off); below that the
calendars move into a Calendars popover in the toolbar. Below 900 the title and the header dates get smaller and New event
shows only its plus; below 760 the Calendars button shows only its colors; below 680 the toolbar takes two rows. Below 640 the
views become 3 days, Day and Agenda: the week views show three days from the focused day, and the agenda lists the week by
day, with all-day events first and "Nothing planned" on free days, each day's heading held at the top while its events
scroll. Event blocks drop their place, avatars and time as they get smaller, and titles wrap to three lines when there is
height.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.WeekCalendarPhoneDemo">
    <!-- Below 640 the calendar shows three days, a day or the agenda, and the toolbar takes two rows. -->
    <arc:WeekCalendar x:Name="Calendar"
                      Width="390"
                      GridHeight="620"
                      HorizontalAlignment="Center" />
</UserControl>
```

### Time zones

Events are absolute times; `TimeZone` (null: the computer's) decides the clock they are drawn on, the current time line and
"today". The corner of the header shows the zone's offset ("GMT+8", "GMT+5:30", "GMT"). `Culture` sets the language of dates
and times: English merges what both ends of a range share ("Sep 28 to Oct 4, 2026", "9:30 – 11:30 AM"); Chinese uses
year-month-day titles and a 24-hour clock. `Now` fixes the current time for screenshots and tests.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.WeekCalendarTimeZonesDemo">
    <!-- The same events, stored as instants, read in New York and in Kolkata (the corner says GMT−4 and GMT+5:30). -->
    <StackPanel Spacing="24">
        <StackPanel Spacing="10">
            <TextBlock Text="New York" FontWeight="Medium" />
            <arc:WeekCalendar x:Name="NewYork"
                              View="WorkWeek"
                              GridHeight="420"
                              IsSidebarVisible="False" />
        </StackPanel>
        <StackPanel Spacing="10">
            <TextBlock Text="Kolkata" FontWeight="Medium" />
            <arc:WeekCalendar x:Name="Kolkata"
                              View="WorkWeek"
                              GridHeight="420"
                              IsSidebarVisible="False" />
        </StackPanel>
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class WeekCalendarTimeZonesDemo : UserControl
{
    public WeekCalendarTimeZonesDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        var newYork = WeekCalendarDemoData.Zone("America/New_York", TimeSpan.FromHours(-4), "New York");
        var kolkata = WeekCalendarDemoData.Zone("Asia/Kolkata", new TimeSpan(5, 30, 0), "Kolkata");
        // One list of events, planned in New York; each calendar shows them on its own clock.
        var events = WeekCalendarDemoData.CreateEvents(WeekCalendarDemoData.ThisMonday(newYork), newYork);
        NewYork.TimeZone = newYork;
        Kolkata.TimeZone = kolkata;
        NewYork.Calendars.AddRange(WeekCalendarDemoData.CreateCalendars());
        Kolkata.Calendars.AddRange(WeekCalendarDemoData.CreateCalendars());
        NewYork.EventsSource = events;
        Kolkata.EventsSource = events;
        // Both open at 8 AM New York time: 5:30 PM in Kolkata.
        NewYork.InitialScrollTime = new TimeOnly(8, 0);
        Kolkata.InitialScrollTime = new TimeOnly(17, 30);
    }
}
```

### The all-day row

All-day events are bars across their days, packed into lanes. When more than `AllDayLaneLimit` lanes (3) are needed, the last
lane shows "+N more" for each day with hidden events, and a chevron under "All day" expands the row; `IsAllDayExpanded` is the
two-way state.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.WeekCalendarBusyAllDayDemo">
    <!-- Five all-day events on Wednesday: the row shows three lanes and "+3 more" until the chevron opens it. -->
    <StackPanel Spacing="12">
        <arc:WeekCalendar x:Name="Calendar"
                          GridHeight="520"
                          IsSidebarVisible="False" />
        <TextBlock x:Name="Log" Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" FontSize="12" TextWrapping="Wrap" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs

        Log.Text = "Press the chevron under All day, or a +3 more chip, to see every lane.";

        {
```
