### Texts

Every word has an English default in `WeekCalendarLabels`: the toolbar, the view names, the screen reader names of days,
events and all-day bars (functions, so the order of their parts can change), and the announcements. Replace `Labels` to
translate; dates and times inside come from `Culture`.

```csharp
calendar.Culture = CultureInfo.GetCultureInfo("de-DE");
calendar.Labels = new WeekCalendarLabels
{
    Today = "Heute",
    WeekView = "Woche",
    WorkWeekView = "Arbeitswoche",
    DayView = "Tag",
    AllDay = "Ganztägig",
    NewEvent = "Neuer Termin",
    TimedEvent = (title, day, start, end, calendar, place) => $"{title}, {day}, {start} bis {end}, {calendar}",
};
```

### Performance

- Every event block, cell and header day is self-drawn and cached; nothing is laid out while ranges slide, only moved.
- A drag moves only the dragged block; the day's other events are laid out again once, when it is dropped, and settle with
  transforms.
- Ranges are drawn into at most three pooled panes; a pane that slid out is reused for the next range with its blocks, so
  paging through weeks builds nothing new.
- The current time moves once a minute, on a timer that stops when the calendar leaves the window or `Now` is set.

## API reference

### WeekCalendar

A desktop-class week planner: a toolbar with Today, previous / next and a view switch; a sidebar with a month and the calendars to show (it folds into a Calendars popover on narrower calendars); a header of days, an all-day row and a scrolling time grid with the events of each day side by side, the current time and the past dimmed. Week, work week and day views; narrow calendars show three days, a day or an agenda. Changing the range slides the header, the all-day row and the grid together on one spring; changing the view crossfades. Events are data (`Events` or `EventsSource`) in absolute time, shown in `TimeZone`. Drag across empty time to draw an event and name it in a quick create popover, drag events between days and times, drag their bottom edge to resize, click one to edit its title, day, times and calendar; everything snaps to 15 minutes, and the last change can be undone.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Events` | `AvaloniaList<WeekCalendarEvent>` | `null` | The events. Use it in XAML; `EventsSource` takes precedence when set. |
| `EventsSource` | `IEnumerable?` | `null` | A collection of `WeekCalendarEvent`s (observed when it raises collection changes); replaces `Events`. |
| `Calendars` | `AvaloniaList<WeekCalendarSource>` | `null` | The calendars listed in the sidebar and the Calendars popover; empty hides both. |
| `CalendarsSource` | `IEnumerable?` | `null` | A collection of `WeekCalendarSource`s (observed); replaces `Calendars`. |
| `Date` | `DateOnly` | `01/01/0001` | The focused day (two-way; today by default). The days shown always hold it: setting a day outside them moves the calendar to the range around it. |
| `View` | `WeekCalendarView` | `Week` | The chosen view (two-way). Narrow calendars show `EffectiveView` instead. |
| `EffectiveView` | `WeekCalendarView` | – | *Read-only.* The view shown: below 640 the week and work week show three days; from 640 the three-day and agenda views show the week. |
| `RangeStart` | `DateOnly` | – | *Read-only.* The first day shown. |
| `RangeEnd` | `DateOnly` | – | *Read-only.* The last day shown. |
| `RangeTitle` | `string` | – | *Read-only.* The title of the days shown ("Sep 21 to 27, 2026", "Thursday, November 5"). |
| `FirstDayOfWeek` | `DayOfWeek` | `Monday` | The first day of the week (Monday). |
| `StartHour` | `int` | `0` | The first hour of the grid (0–23); the gutter labels start one hour later. |
| `EndHour` | `int` | `24` | The hour the grid ends at (1–24, after `StartHour`). |
| `HourHeight` | `double` | `52` | Pixels per hour (52, the same at every width). |
| `GridHeight` | `double` | `NaN` | The height of the grid (header, all-day row and scrolling hours); NaN takes 72% of the window, 480 to 760. |
| `TimeZone` | `TimeZoneInfo?` | `null` | The zone the grid shows times in; null uses the computer's. The header's corner shows its offset ("GMT+8"). |
| `Culture` | `CultureInfo?` | `null` | The culture of dates, times and weekday names; null uses the current culture. |
| `Now` | `DateTimeOffset?` | `null` | A fixed "now" for demos and tests; null follows the clock, moving the current time line every minute. |
| `IsSidebarVisible` | `bool?` | `null` | Shows the sidebar (true), hides it (false) or shows it from 1100 wide (null). |
| `ShowNowIndicator` | `bool` | `true` | Draws the current time line on today's range. |
| `ShowWeekendShading` | `bool` | `true` | Shades Saturday and Sunday. |
| `InitialScrollTime` | `TimeOnly?` | `null` | The hour the grid opens at; null opens at the first event's hour (8 AM without events). |
| `AllDayLaneLimit` | `int` | `3` | The all-day lanes shown before the row collapses into "+N more" chips (3); 0 never collapses. |
| `IsAllDayExpanded` | `bool` | `false` | Shows every all-day lane of a collapsed row (two-way; the chevron under "All day" toggles it). |
| `Labels` | `WeekCalendarLabels` | – | Every text the calendar shows or reads to screen readers. |
| `NewEventCommand` | `ICommand?` | `null` | Runs when New event is pressed (parameter: the focused `DateOnly`), after `NewEventRequested`. |
| `EventInvokedCommand` | `ICommand?` | `null` | Runs when an event is clicked or activated with Enter (parameter: the `WeekCalendarEvent`). |
| `IsReadOnly` | `bool` | `false` | Turns every edit off: no drawing, dragging, quick create, deleting or undo; the details show as text. |
| `SelectedEvent` | `WeekCalendarEvent?` | `null` | The selected event (two-way): clicking, dragging or a keyboard move selects one; Escape clears it. |
| `DefaultCalendarId` | `string?` | `null` | The calendar new events start in; null (or an unknown id) takes the first calendar shown. |
| `UndoDuration` | `TimeSpan` | `00:00:06` | How long the undo toast stays (6 s); zero turns undo off. |
| `CanUndo` | `bool` | – | *Read-only.* True while the last change can be undone (its toast shows). |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ViewChanged` | `WeekCalendarViewChangedEventArgs` | Raised when `View` changes. |
| `RangeChanged` | `WeekCalendarRangeChangedEventArgs` | Raised when the days shown change (previous / next, Today, a day in the month, the keys, a view change). |
| `CalendarVisibilityChanged` | `WeekCalendarVisibilityChangedEventArgs` | Raised when a calendar's toggle shows or hides its events. |
| `EventInvoked` | `WeekCalendarEventEventArgs` | Raised when an event is clicked or activated with Enter or Space; set Handled to keep its details closed. |
| `NewEventRequested` | `WeekCalendarNewEventRequestedEventArgs` | Raised when New event is pressed, with the focused day; set Handled to keep the calendar from drafting one at the day's next free hour. |
| `EventCreated` | `WeekCalendarEventEventArgs` | Raised when an event is created in the calendar (quick create), a deleted one is restored, or a delete is undone. |
| `EventUpdated` | `WeekCalendarEventUpdatedEventArgs` | Raised when an event is moved, resized or edited in the calendar (or a change is undone), with a copy of it from before. |
| `EventDeleted` | `WeekCalendarEventEventArgs` | Raised when an event is deleted in the calendar (or its creation is undone). |

Pseudo-classes: `:wide`, `:regular`, `:compact`, `:tight`, `:swatch-only`, `:stacked`, `:sidebar`, `:sliding`, `:no-calendars`, `:readonly`, `:dragging`, `:editing`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

### WeekCalendarEvent

One event of a `WeekCalendar`. `Start` and `End` are instants (store them in UTC or with their offset); the calendar shows them in its `TimeZone`. An all-day event covers whole dates: the dates of `Start` and `End` as written, with `End` exclusive (midnight after the last day); its time zone is ignored. Changing any property moves or redraws the event at once.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Id` | `string` | `""` | A stable id: focus, selection and callbacks follow it across rebuilds. |
| `Title` | `string` | `""` | The title shown on the event. |
| `Start` | `DateTimeOffset` | `01/01/0001 00:00:00 +00:00` | When the event starts. |
| `End` | `DateTimeOffset` | `01/01/0001 00:00:00 +00:00` | When the event ends (exclusive); an end at or before the start shows a 15 minute event. |
| `CalendarId` | `string?` | `null` | The `Id` of its calendar; an unknown id draws the event in gray. |
| `IsAllDay` | `bool` | `false` | True shows the event in the all-day row, spanning its dates. |
| `Location` | `string?` | `null` | Where it takes place: a line with a pin on tall events, the second line in the agenda. |
| `Attendees` | `AvaloniaList<ProjectPerson>` | `null` | The people invited; tall events show up to four avatars, the agenda three and a count. |
| `AutomationName` | `string?` | `null` | The screen reader name; null composes "title, day, start to end, calendar, location". |
| `Tag` | `object?` | `null` | Any object the app wants to keep with the event. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### WeekCalendarSource

A calendar of a `WeekCalendar` ("Work", "Home"): its events take its color, and its toggle in the sidebar (or the Calendars popover) shows or hides them.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Id` | `string` | `""` | The id events refer to through `CalendarId`. |
| `Name` | `string` | `""` | The name in the calendars list and in event names read by screen readers. |
| `Color` | `WeekCalendarColor` | `Blue` | The palette color; `Custom` uses `CustomColor`. |
| `CustomColor` | `Color?` | `null` | Any color for `Custom`; fills and text are mixed from it like the presets. |
| `IsVisible` | `bool` | `true` | False hides the calendar's events (two-way; the toggle in the calendars list sets it). |
| `Tag` | `object?` | `null` | Any object the app wants to keep with the calendar. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### WeekCalendarLabels

Every word `WeekCalendar` shows or reads to screen readers, in English by default. Replace the instance (`Labels`) to translate or reword. Dates and times inside the formatted texts come from `Culture`; the functions only arrange them, so the word order can change.

### WeekCalendarEventUpdatedEventArgs

Arguments of `EventUpdated`: the event as it is now and a copy of it before the change.

Derives from `RoutedEventArgs`: every member of `RoutedEventArgs` works as well.

### Events

| Event | Raised when | Arguments |
|---|---|---|
| `RangeChanged` | The days shown changed | `OldStart`, `OldEnd`, `NewStart`, `NewEnd`, `Direction`, `Reason` |
| `ViewChanged` | `View` changed | `OldView`, `NewView`, `EffectiveView` |
| `CalendarVisibilityChanged` | A calendar's toggle was used | `Calendar`, `IsVisible` |
| `EventInvoked` | An event was clicked or activated with Enter or Space | `Event` |
| `NewEventRequested` | New event was pressed; `Handled` keeps the calendar from drafting | `Date` (the focused day) |
| `EventCreated` | A new event was saved, or undo brought a deleted one back | `Event` |
| `EventUpdated` | An event was moved, resized or edited, or a change was undone | `Event`, `Previous` |
| `EventDeleted` | An event was deleted, or undo removed a new one | `Event` |

## Accessibility

- **Keyboard.** Tab reaches the toolbar (Today, previous, next, the view switch, Calendars, New event), the month (one tab
  stop; arrows move between days, Page Up and Page Down between months, Enter picks a day), the calendar toggles, the
  all-day bars, the grid (one tab stop: the focused day) and then each event in time order.
- **In the grid**, Left and Right move to the previous or next day; past the first or last day the next range slides in and
  the focus lands on its first or last day. On an event, Up and Down go to the previous or next event and Left and Right to the
  day before or after. T goes to today, D opens the focused day and W its week. The focus stays on the focused day after T, D
  and W and after a range slide.
- **Editing keys.** N drafts an event at the next free hour of the focused day and opens the quick create popover; Enter on a
  day does the same, Enter on an event opens its details, and Enter in the quick create title saves. Delete or Backspace
  deletes the focused or selected event. Alt with Up or Down moves the focused event by 15 minutes, Alt with Left or Right by a
  day; add Shift to Up or Down to change its length. The focus stays on the event. Ctrl+Z (Cmd+Z) undoes the last change.
  Escape closes a popover, cancels a drag, and then clears the selection.
- **Popovers** are dialogs named "New event" and "Event details". The focus moves into the title and Tab stays inside until
  Escape, Done or Cancel; then it comes back to the event (or to the day of a cancelled draft). The calendar choice is a
  radio group with one tab stop; the arrow keys pick a calendar. After a delete the focus goes to the event's day; after Undo
  on the toast it comes back to the calendar.
- The grid is a table named by its range ("Oct 19 to 25, 2026") with a help text about the keys; each day is a cell named
  "Thursday, October 22, today, 6 events". Events are buttons named "title, day, start to end, calendar, place"; all-day bars
  "title, all day, first day to last day, calendar"; agenda rows leave out the day their heading already says. The header days
  are buttons named "Show Monday, October 19"; the month's days carry "Today" as their status.
- The calendar toggles are check boxes named by the calendar; the sidebar is named "Calendar navigation".
- A polite live region announces range changes ("Oct 26 to Nov 1, 2026") and view changes ("Work week, Oct 19 to 23, 2026",
  "Day view, Thursday, October 22"), and every edit: an event added, moved, resized or rescheduled, a new calendar or title,
  a delete, a restore, an undo, a cancelled drag and a cleared selection. The toast shows the same words. All of them are in
  `WeekCalendarLabels`.
- Calendar colors are never the only cue: every event says its calendar's name.

## Motion

- **Ranges**: the header row, the all-day row and the grid slide one width together on one spring (critically damped, about
  10% left after 340 ms, at rest after about a second). Pressing next again mid-slide keeps every pane going from where it is,
  with its speed; up to three ranges are on screen at once. Jumps of several weeks also slide one width.
- **Views**: the old view fades out in 160 ms while the new one fades in over 240 ms, in place.
- **The all-day row** grows or folds in 240 ms when expanded or collapsed.
- **Hover and focus**: event fills, the half-hour slot under the pointer, header and month days fade in 160 ms. The view
  switch's highlight glides between options.
- **Dragging**: a dragged event hops between 15-minute slots and days on a fast critically damped spring (at rest in about a
  third of a second), restarting from where it is drawn at every slot; resizing changes its length a slot at a time with no
  motion. After a drop, an edit in the details, a keyboard move, an undo or a delete, the events that moved settle on the
  Smooth spring; a cancelled drag springs back on it.
- **Popovers** fade in over 160 ms while scaling from 0.96 on the Smooth spring, growing from the edge that faces their event;
  they leave in 120 ms. **The undo toast** rises 12 pixels on the Smooth spring and leaves in 160 ms, dropping 8; a newer change
  replaces it with both moving at once. Swipes on touch screens continue on the range spring from where the finger let go.
- Reduced motion turns range slides into the same crossfade, moves the view switch's highlight at once, drops the hops and
  springs of events (they move at once), and keeps only the fades of the popovers and the toast; Off applies every change at
  once.

## Related

- `Calendar` and `DatePicker` for choosing a date.
- `SegmentedControl` for the view switch on its own.
- `Popover` for the Calendars list of narrower calendars.
- `Select`, `DatePicker` and `Input` for the fields of the details popover on their own.
- `Timeline` for a feed of events in time order.

---

# Availability picker

> Find a meeting time across several people's calendars, see who is free at each time, and book the one that works.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc.Blocks`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc.Blocks --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/blocks/availability-picker

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.AvailabilityPickerPreviewDemo">
    <!-- A 30-minute check-in for three people over one week; the days and times come from AvailabilityPickerDemoData. -->
    <arc:AvailabilityPicker x:Name="Picker"
                            MaxWidth="680"
                            Title="Roadmap check-in"
                            Duration="0:30:00"
                            TimeZoneName="Lisbon time" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class AvailabilityPickerPreviewDemo : UserControl
{
    public AvailabilityPickerPreviewDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        var week = AvailabilityPickerDemoData.Create();
        Picker.Attendees.AddRange(week.People);
        Picker.Days.AddRange(week.Days);
        // Start on Monday's second free time, so the check sits in the right-hand column.
        Picker.SelectedSlot = week.Days[0].Slots[1];
    }
}
```

## When to use

`AvailabilityPicker` helps one person choose a meeting time for a group. A strip of days says how many proposed times
suit everyone on each day; the selected day lists its times with one mark per attendee, green when they are free and grey
when they are busy; the footer sums up the choice and books it. Choosing another day glides the highlight there, slides
the times in from that side and selects the first time that works for everyone.

- **Scheduling a meeting from an app's own data.** An interview loop, a design review or a client call where your service
  already knows the attendees' calendars and proposes a handful of times.
- **Booking flows with a confirmation step.** The reader compares a few days, picks a time and confirms; a new choice undoes
  the confirmation, so changing one's mind needs no extra button.
- **Times that may cost somebody a meeting.** A time with busy attendees can still be booked. The row says who is busy and
  the footer says who will need to move a meeting.

## When not to use

- **Choosing one date.** Use `Calendar` or `DatePicker`.
- **Typing any time.** Use `TimePicker`; the picker only offers the times you give it.
- **Answering an invitation.** The picker books a time for a group; showing and answering one invitation is a different
  surface.
- **Long ranges.** The day strip shows every day in equal columns, which suits a working week (five to seven days). For a
  month, let the reader choose the week elsewhere and give the picker that week.

## Usage

### Days, times and attendees

`Attendees` are the people invited, as `ProjectPerson`s: the header shows their avatars, and every time gets one mark per
attendee in this order. `Days` are `AvailabilityDay`s with a `Date` and their `Slots`. Each `AvailabilitySlot` has a
`Start` (a time of day), an optional `End` (otherwise `Duration` after the start) and the `BusyAttendees` for that time.
Times are shown sorted by start. A day's `OpenCount`, shown on its card, counts the bookable times that suit everyone.

```csharp
var noor = new ProjectPerson("Noor Haddad", "noor");
var tomas = new ProjectPerson("Tomás Ferreira", "tomas");
var ingrid = new ProjectPerson("Ingrid Solberg", "ingrid");
picker.Attendees.AddRange([noor, tomas, ingrid]);

var monday = new DateOnly(2026, 3, 9);
picker.Days.Add(new AvailabilityDay(monday,
    new AvailabilitySlot(new TimeSpan(9, 0, 0)),
    new AvailabilitySlot(new TimeSpan(11, 0, 0)),
    new AvailabilitySlot(new TimeSpan(13, 30, 0), tomas),
    new AvailabilitySlot(new TimeSpan(15, 30, 0))));
```

```xml
<arc:AvailabilityPicker x:Name="Picker"
                        Title="Roadmap check-in"
                        Duration="0:30:00"
                        TimeZoneName="Lisbon time" />
```

`Title` is the heading; the line under it is the duration and `TimeZoneName` ("30 min · Lisbon time"), or your own
`Subtitle`. Use `DaysSource` and `AttendeesSource` for collections you own: an `ObservableCollection` is observed, and
changes to a day, a time or a person show at once. A time's `Note` replaces its generated line; `IsEnabled="False"` dims a
time that cannot be booked (already taken, in the past) and keeps it from being chosen.

### Selection

`SelectedDay` and `SelectedSlot` are two-way. At first the picker selects the first day (or the day of a `SelectedSlot` you
set) and, unless you set a time, picks one. When the day changes and the selected time is not on it, `AutoSelectSlot`
decides: `FirstEveryoneFree` (the default) takes the first time that suits everyone, or the first bookable time when there
is none; `First` takes the first bookable time; `None` leaves the choice to the reader. Choices are not remembered per day.

Setting `SelectedSlot` to a time of another day selects that day too. `SelectDay` and `SelectSlot` do the same from code;
`SelectDay(day, animate: false)` moves without motion.

`SelectedDayChanged` reports the old and new day, the `Direction` (1 later, −1 earlier) and the time picked with it;
`SelectedSlotChanged` reports the old and new time. Both say whether the reader made the change (`IsUserInitiated`).

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.AvailabilityPickerBoundDemo">
    <!-- The selection is plain two-way state: the panel reads it, moves it and books it, and logs every event. -->
    <Grid ColumnDefinitions="*,260" ColumnSpacing="24">
        <arc:AvailabilityPicker x:Name="Picker"
                                Title="Roadmap check-in"
                                TimeZoneName="Lisbon time" />
        <StackPanel Grid.Column="1" Spacing="12" VerticalAlignment="Top">
            <TextBlock Text="State"
                       FontSize="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TypeXS}"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
            <TextBlock Text="{Binding #Picker.SelectedDay, StringFormat='SelectedDay: {0}'}"
                       FontFamily="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource MonoFontFamily}"
                       FontSize="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TypeXS}" />
            <TextBlock Text="{Binding #Picker.SelectedSlot, StringFormat='SelectedSlot: {0}'}"
                       FontFamily="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource MonoFontFamily}"
                       FontSize="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TypeXS}" />
            <arc:Checkbox Content="IsConfirmed" IsChecked="{Binding #Picker.IsConfirmed, Mode=TwoWay}" />
            <StackPanel Orientation="Horizontal" Spacing="8">
                <arc:Button x:Name="Previous" Content="Previous day" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" />
                <arc:Button x:Name="Next" Content="Next day" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" />
            </StackPanel>
            <TextBlock Text="Events"
                       Margin="0,8,0,0"
                       FontSize="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TypeXS}"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
            <TextBlock x:Name="Log"
                       Text="Choose a day or a time, then book it."
                       TextWrapping="Wrap"
                       LineHeight="18"
                       FontSize="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TypeXS}"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
        </StackPanel>
    </Grid>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class AvailabilityPickerBoundDemo : UserControl
{
    private readonly List<string> _lines = new();

    public AvailabilityPickerBoundDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        var week = AvailabilityPickerDemoData.Create();
        Picker.Attendees.AddRange(week.People);
        Picker.Days.AddRange(week.Days);

        Previous.Click += (_, _) => Step(-1);
        Next.Click += (_, _) => Step(1);

        Picker.SelectedDayChanged += (_, e) =>
            Write($"Day {e.OldDay?.Date:ddd d} → {e.NewDay?.Date:ddd d} ({(e.Direction < 0 ? "back" : "forward")}){(e.IsUserInitiated ? "" : ", from code")}");
        Picker.SelectedSlotChanged += (_, e) =>
            Write($"Time {e.OldSlot?.ToString() ?? "none"} → {e.NewSlot?.ToString() ?? "none"}");
        Picker.ConfirmRequested += (_, e) => Write($"Booking {e.DisplayDate}, {e.DisplayTime}…");
        Picker.Confirmed += (_, e) =>
            Write(e.Conflicts.Count == 0
                ? $"Booked {e.Start:ddd HH:mm}–{e.End:HH:mm}"
                : $"Booked {e.Start:ddd HH:mm}; {string.Join(", ", e.Conflicts.Select(p => p.DisplayShortName))} must move a meeting");
        Picker.ConfirmationReset += (_, e) => Write($"Booking of {e.Start:ddd HH:mm} undone");
    }

    private void Step(int direction)
    {
        var days = Picker.Days;
        var index = Picker.SelectedDay is { } day ? days.IndexOf(day) : 0;
        var next = Math.Clamp(index + direction, 0, days.Count - 1);
        Picker.SelectDay(days[next]);
    }

    private void Write(string line)
    {
        _lines.Insert(0, line);
        if (_lines.Count > 6)
        {
            _lines.RemoveAt(_lines.Count - 1);
        }
        Log.Text = string.Join(Environment.NewLine, _lines);
    }
}
```

### Booking

The button books the selection: `ConfirmRequested` comes first and can `Cancel` (a failed availability check, a missing
permission); then `IsConfirmed` turns true, `Confirmed` is raised and `ConfirmCommand` runs. Their arguments carry the
day and the time, the real `Start` and `End`, the `Conflicts` (busy attendees) and the texts the footer shows. Once booked
the button reads "Booked" with a check, stays focusable and does nothing; choosing another day or time undoes the booking
and raises `ConfirmationReset`. `Confirm` and `ResetConfirmation` do the same from code.

```csharp
picker.ConfirmRequested += (_, e) =>
{
    // Someone took the room in the meantime: keep the selection unbooked.
    e.Cancel = !IsRoomFree(e.Start, e.End);
};
picker.Confirmed += (_, e) => SendInvites(e.Start, e.End, e.Conflicts);

static bool IsRoomFree(DateTime start, DateTime end) => true;
static void SendInvites(DateTime start, DateTime end, IReadOnlyList<ProjectPerson> conflicts) { }
```

Setting `IsConfirmed` from code shows the booked state without announcing it, which suits restoring a booking made
earlier.

### Framed or flat

`IsFramed` (the default) draws a bordered, rounded surface with a line above the times and a muted footer, for a picker
that sits among other content. Set it to false when it fills a page or a panel of its own.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.AvailabilityPickerFlatDemo">
    <!-- Laid flat on the page: no border, no dividers, no muted footer. Starts on Wednesday's first free time. -->
    <arc:AvailabilityPicker x:Name="Picker"
                            IsFramed="False"
                            Title="Design review"
                            Duration="0:45:00"
                            TimeZoneName="Lisbon time" />
</UserControl>
```


### Narrow containers

The picker reads its own width, not the window's. Below 520 the paddings tighten, the day cards get smaller, the times take
one column and the footer stacks over a full-width button; at 360 and below the legend and the cards' counts are hidden.
`IsLegendVisible` hides the legend at any width.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"

             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.AvailabilityPickerNarrowDemo">

    <arc:AvailabilityPicker x:Name="Picker"
                            Width="340"
                            HorizontalAlignment="Center"
                            Title="Roadmap check-in"
                            TimeZoneName="Lisbon time" />
</UserControl>
```

### Harder data

A day where every time clashes for somebody selects its first bookable time, and the footer says who will need to move a
meeting. Several busy attendees are listed by their short names ("Noor and Ingrid are busy"). A day with fewer rows makes
the list's height spring to its new size; a day without times says so in place of the list.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.AvailabilityPickerTrickyDataDemo">
    <!--
        Monday has no time that suits everyone (the first time is picked and the footer names who has to move), Tuesday
        has times two and three people are busy for, Wednesday has only two times (the list changes height), Thursday has
        none and Friday has a time that is already taken.
    -->
    <arc:AvailabilityPicker x:Name="Picker"
                            MaxWidth="680"
                            Title="Quarterly planning"
                            Duration="1:00:00"
                            TimeZoneName="Lisbon time" />
</UserControl>
```

### Texts

Every text has an English default and a property: the button (`ConfirmText`, `ConfirmedText`), the lines
(`EveryoneFreeText`, `BusyFormat`, `BusyManyFormat`, `ConflictFormat`, `ConfirmedLabelText`, `NoSlotText`,
`NoSlotsText`), the counts and the legend (`OpenCountFormat`, `FreeLegendText`, `BusyLegendText`, `AndWord`), the date and
time formats (`DayNameFormat`, `DayNumberFormat`, `DayLabelFormat`, `TimeFormat`, `RangeFormat`, `SelectionFormat`,
`DurationFormat`, `SubtitleFormat`) and what screen readers hear (`AttendeesAutomationFormat`, `WeekAutomationFormat`,
`DayAutomationFormat`, `TimesAutomationFormat`, `SlotAutomationFormat`, `ConfirmedAnnouncementFormat`). Dates and times are
formatted with the current culture.

```xml
<arc:AvailabilityPicker Title="Point d’équipe"
                        ConfirmText="Réserver ce créneau"
                        ConfirmedText="Réservé"
                        EveryoneFreeText="Tout le monde est libre"
                        BusyFormat="{}{0} est occupé"
                        DayLabelFormat="{}{0:dddd d MMMM}"
                        RangeFormat="{}{0} à {1}" />
```

## API reference

### AvailabilityPicker

Find a meeting time that suits several people: a strip of days, the proposed times of the selected day with one mark per attendee (green when free, grey when busy), and a footer that sums up the choice with a button to book it. Choosing another day glides the day highlight there, slides the times in from that side and selects the first time that suits everyone; a time with busy attendees can still be booked, and the footer says who has to move a meeting. Booking turns the button into a quiet "Booked"; any new choice undoes it. The days, times and attendees are data you provide.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Days` | `AvaloniaList<AvailabilityDay>` | `null` | The days, in the order of the strip. Use it in XAML; `DaysSource` takes precedence when set. |
| `DaysSource` | `IEnumerable?` | `null` | A collection of `AvailabilityDay`s (observed when it raises collection changes); replaces `Days`. |
| `Attendees` | `AvaloniaList<ProjectPerson>` | `null` | The attendees, in the order of the avatars and of each time's marks. |
| `AttendeesSource` | `IEnumerable?` | `null` | A collection of `ProjectPerson`s (observed when it raises collection changes); replaces `Attendees`. |
| `SelectedDay` | `AvailabilityDay?` | `null` | The selected day; null (or a day that is not in `Days`) selects the first day. |
| `SelectedSlot` | `AvailabilitySlot?` | `null` | The selected time. A time of another day selects that day as well. When the day changes and this time is not on it, the picker selects one by `AutoSelectSlot`. |
| `AutoSelectSlot` | `AvailabilitySlotAutoSelect` | `FirstEveryoneFree` | Which time is selected by itself after the day changes, and at first when `SelectedSlot` is not set. |
| `IsConfirmed` | `bool` | `false` | True once the selection is booked; choosing another day or time sets it back to false. |
| `Title` | `string?` | `null` | The meeting's name, the picker's heading (and its screen reader name). |
| `Subtitle` | `string?` | `null` | The line under the title; null builds it from `Duration` and `TimeZoneName`. |
| `Duration` | `TimeSpan` | `00:30:00` | The meeting's length: shown under the title, and the end of every time without its own `End`. |
| `TimeZoneName` | `string?` | `null` | The time zone the times are in, as shown after the duration ("Lisbon time"); null shows the duration only. |
| `IsFramed` | `bool` | `true` | Draws the picker as a bordered, rounded surface with divided sections (true); false lays it flat on the page. |
| `IsLegendVisible` | `bool` | `true` | Shows the Free / Busy legend beside the day heading (always hidden at 360 wide and below). |
| `ConfirmCommand` | `ICommand?` | `null` | Runs when a selection is booked (parameter: the `AvailabilitySelectionEventArgs` of `Confirmed`). |
| `ConfirmText` | `string` | `"Book this time"` | The button's label before booking. |
| `ConfirmedText` | `string` | `"Booked"` | The button's label once booked (shown after a check). |
| `EveryoneFreeText` | `string` | `"Everyone's free"` | The line of a time that suits every attendee, and the footer's line for it. |
| `BusyFormat` | `string` | `"{0} is busy"` | The line of a time with one busy attendee; {0} is their short name. |
| `BusyManyFormat` | `string` | `"{0} are busy"` | The line of a time with several busy attendees; {0} is their short names ("Noor and Ingrid"). |
| `ConflictFormat` | `string` | `"{0} will need to move a meeting"` | The footer's line for a time with busy attendees; {0} is their short names. |
| `ConfirmedLabelText` | `string` | `"Invites on the way"` | The footer's line once booked. |
| `NoSlotText` | `string` | `"Pick a time"` | The footer's line while no time is selected. |
| `NoSlotsText` | `string` | `"No times on this day"` | Shown in place of the times on a day without any. |
| `OpenCountFormat` | `string` | `"{0} open"` | A day card's count line; {0} is `OpenCount`. |
| `FreeLegendText` | `string` | `"Free"` | The legend's word for a free attendee. |
| `BusyLegendText` | `string` | `"Busy"` | The legend's word for a busy attendee. |
| `AndWord` | `string` | `"and"` | The word joining the last two names in lists ("Noor and Ingrid"). |
| `DurationFormat` | `string` | `"{0} min"` | The duration under the title; {0} is the number of minutes. |
| `SubtitleFormat` | `string` | `"{0} · {1}"` | The line under the title when a time zone is set; {0} is the duration, {1} `TimeZoneName`. |
| `DayNameFormat` | `string` | `"{0:ddd}"` | A day card's weekday; {0} is the date (a DateTime) in the current culture. |
| `DayNumberFormat` | `string` | `"{0:%d}"` | A day card's number; {0} is the date. |
| `DayLabelFormat` | `string` | `"{0:dddd, d MMMM}"` | The long date of the heading and the footer; {0} is the date. |
| `TimeFormat` | `string` | `"{0:HH:mm}"` | A time of day; {0} is the date and time (a DateTime). |
| `RangeFormat` | `string` | `"{0} – {1}"` | A time range as shown; {0} is the start, {1} the end (both formatted). |
| `SelectionFormat` | `string` | `"{0}, {1}"` | The footer's summary; {0} is the long date, {1} the range. |
| `AttendeesAutomationFormat` | `string` | `"Invited: {0}"` | The avatars' screen reader name; {0} is the attendees' names ("A, B and C"). |
| `WeekAutomationFormat` | `string` | `"Days from {0:d MMMM}"` | The day strip's screen reader name; {0} is the first day's date. |
| `DayAutomationFormat` | `string` | `"{0:dddd, d MMMM}, open for everyone: {1}"` | A day card's screen reader name; {0} is the date, {1} `OpenCount`. |
| `TimesAutomationFormat` | `string` | `"Times for {0:dddd, d MMMM}"` | The time list's screen reader name; {0} is the date. |
| `SlotAutomationFormat` | `string` | `"{0} to {1}, {2}"` | A time's screen reader name; {0} is the start, {1} the end, {2} its line ("Everyone's free"). |
| `ConfirmedAnnouncementFormat` | `string` | `"Booked {0}, {1} to {2}."` | Announced politely when a time is booked; {0} is the long date, {1} the start, {2} the end. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `SelectedDayChanged` | `AvailabilityDayChangedEventArgs` | Raised after the selected day changed (the picker may have selected a time with it). |
| `SelectedSlotChanged` | `AvailabilitySlotChangedEventArgs` | Raised after the selected time changed. |
| `ConfirmRequested` | `AvailabilityConfirmRequestedEventArgs` | Raised when the book button is pressed or `Confirm` is called; set Cancel to keep it unbooked. |
| `Confirmed` | `AvailabilitySelectionEventArgs` | Raised when `IsConfirmed` turns true, with the booked selection. |
| `ConfirmationReset` | `AvailabilitySelectionEventArgs` | Raised when `IsConfirmed` turns false (a new choice or `ResetConfirmation`), with the selection that was booked. |

Pseudo-classes: `:framed`, `:compact`, `:narrow`, `:confirmed`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

### AvailabilityDay

One day of an `AvailabilityPicker`: a day card in the strip, and the times shown when it is selected (sorted by start).

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Date` | `DateOnly` | `01/01/0001` | The date: the card shows its short weekday and day number, the heading and the footer its long form. |
| `Slots` | `AvaloniaList<AvailabilitySlot>` | `null` | The proposed times of the day, in any order (they are shown sorted by start). |
| `Tag` | `object?` | `null` | Any object the app keeps with the day. |
| `OpenCount` | `int` | – | *Read-only.* How many selectable times suit every attendee (the card's "3 open"). |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### AvailabilitySlot

One proposed meeting time on an `AvailabilityDay`: when it starts and ends, and which attendees are busy then. A time with busy attendees can still be chosen (the footer says who has to move a meeting); set `IsEnabled` to false for a time that cannot be booked at all.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Start` | `TimeSpan` | `00:00:00` | The start, as a time of day. |
| `End` | `TimeSpan?` | `null` | The end, as a time of day; null ends `Duration` after the start. |
| `BusyAttendees` | `AvaloniaList<ProjectPerson>` | `null` | The attendees who are busy at this time; the picker draws a grey mark for each of them. |
| `Note` | `string?` | `null` | A line shown under the time instead of the generated one ("Everyone's free", "Noor is busy"). |
| `IsEnabled` | `bool` | `true` | False shows the time dimmed and keeps it from being chosen (already taken, in the past). |
| `Tag` | `object?` | `null` | Any object the app keeps with the time (a booking id, the calendar's own slot). |
| `IsEveryoneFree` | `bool` | – | *Read-only.* True while nobody in `BusyAttendees` is busy. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### AvailabilityDayChangedEventArgs

Arguments of `SelectedDayChanged`.

Derives from `RoutedEventArgs`: every member of `RoutedEventArgs` works as well.

### AvailabilitySlotChangedEventArgs

Arguments of `SelectedSlotChanged`.

Derives from `RoutedEventArgs`: every member of `RoutedEventArgs` works as well.

### AvailabilitySelectionEventArgs

A selection of an `AvailabilityPicker` as it is confirmed or undone: the day and time, their real start and end, who has to move a meeting, and the texts the footer shows.

Derives from `RoutedEventArgs`: every member of `RoutedEventArgs` works as well.

### AvailabilityConfirmRequestedEventArgs

Arguments of `ConfirmRequested`: set `Cancel` to keep the selection unconfirmed.

Derives from `RoutedEventArgs`: every member of `RoutedEventArgs` works as well.

## Accessibility

- **Keyboard.** Every day card, every time and the button is a tab stop, in reading order: the days from left to right,
  the times row by row, then the button. Enter or Space chooses the focused day or time, or books the selection; choosing
  keeps the focus where it is, and after booking the focus stays on the button, which then does nothing. The arrow keys are
  not used.
- The picker is a group named by its title, which is a level 2 heading; the date above the times is a level 3 heading.
- The avatars are one image named "Invited: Noor Haddad, Tomás Ferreira and Ingrid Solberg".
- The day strip is a group named "Days from 9 March". Each card is a toggle button whose pressed state is the selection,
  named with the date and how many times suit everyone.
- The times are a list named "Times for Monday, 9 March". Each time is a toggle button named with its range and its line
  ("13:30 to 14:00, Tomás is busy"); a time that cannot be booked is disabled. The marks and the check are not read.
- Booking is announced politely ("Booked Monday, 9 March, 13:30 to 14:00."); the announcement is cleared when a new
  choice undoes it. Day and time changes are not announced: the focused control already says them.

## Motion

- **Day highlight**: one fill under all the cards glides to the chosen day on a gentle spring (stiffness 340, damping 34,
  no overshoot). The cards' text and borders change color over 240 ms; a pressed card shrinks to 97% (the highlight with it).
- **Times**: the new list comes in 16 px from the side of travel on a smooth spring while it fades in over 160 ms, and the old
  list leaves 16 px the other way and fades out over 160 ms at the same time. Quick changes stack: an entering list turns
  around from where it is. When the new day has a different number of rows, the height springs.
- **Selection**: the chosen time's fill and border change over 160 ms; its check slides in from the right on a critically
  damped spring and pushes the marks aside, fading in over 160 ms. A pressed time shrinks to 98%.
- **Texts**: the heading and the footer's two lines swap only when they change: the old text rises 4 px into a 2 px blur and
  fades while the new one rises from 4 px below out of the blur, both in 160 ms.
- **Button**: its label and width change with the button's own blur swap and width spring.
- Reduced motion moves the highlight at once, drops the old list immediately and fades the new one in over 120 ms, and
  crossfades the texts in 120 ms; colors and the check change at once. Off applies every change at once.

## Related

- `Calendar` and `DatePicker` for choosing a single date.
- `TimePicker` for typing a time.
- `Button`, which the picker uses to book.
- `GlidingIndicator`, the primitive behind the day highlight.

# Project board

> A compact sprint board: arrow buttons step each card to the next or previous stage and it flies to its new column, under a sprint line, the team and an All work / My work switch.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc.Blocks`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc.Blocks --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/blocks/project-board

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ProjectBoardPreviewDemo">
    <!-- The "Launch prep" sprint from ProjectBoardDemoData: four stages, six tasks, a team of three; Rhea is "me". -->
    <arc:ProjectBoard x:Name="Board" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class ProjectBoardPreviewDemo : UserControl
{
    public ProjectBoardPreviewDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        ProjectBoardDemoData.Fill(Board);
    }
}
```

## When to use

`ProjectBoard` is a small board for one sprint or one project: a handful of stages as columns and a few dozen tasks as
cards. Each card has two arrow buttons that send its task one stage left or right; the card flies in a straight line to
the end of its new column while the column it left closes up. The header counts the finished tasks, a thin sprint line
fills as tasks reach the last stage, the team sits beside an All work / My work switch, and Add task drops a new card into
the first stage.

- **A team or project page.** The board answers "where is everything" at a glance and lets people move their own work
  without leaving the page.
- **A dashboard tile.** Framed, it sits among other cards; flat, it fills a page of its own.
- **Touch and keyboard first.** Moving a card is a button press, not a drag: it works the same with a mouse, a finger,
  Tab and Enter, or a screen reader, and every move is announced.

## When not to use

- **Large boards.** Every card is a live element and there is no virtualization; keep it to a few dozen tasks. For
  hundreds of tasks, drag and drop between columns, swimlanes or work-in-progress limits, use a full kanban board.
- **Free reordering.** A move always lands at the end of the next or previous column; cards cannot be dragged into a
  position or skip a stage from the card. Call `MoveTask` with an index from your own controls when you need that.
- **Editing.** Cards show a task, they do not edit it. Open your own form from `AddRequested` or from a selection
  elsewhere on the page.
- **Reporting.** For burn-down charts or comparisons across sprints use a chart; the sprint line only shows one ratio.

## Usage

### Stages, tasks and people

`Stages` are the columns, left to right; two to six read well. Each `ProjectBoardStage` has a `Key` that tasks refer to
and a `Header`. The stage marked `IsDone` counts as finished (without one, the last stage does): its tasks fill the sprint
line, their titles turn quiet and their due labels stop warning.

Each `ProjectBoardTask` is a card: `Area` and `DueText` at the top (`IsDueSoon` shows the due label in the warning color),
`Title` in the middle, then the `Owner`'s avatar, the `CommentCount` (hidden at zero) and the two arrows. `StageKey`
names the stage; a key that matches no stage shows the card in the first column. Each column shows its stage's tasks in
the order of the collection.

People are `ProjectPerson` objects: a name and a key, with an optional picture. Without a picture the board draws the
initials on a soft color picked from the key, so the same person keeps the same color. `Team` is the row of avatars in the
header and `CurrentUser` is "me": the person My work filters for and the owner of new drafts.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:ProjectBoard Title="Launch prep">
        <arc:ProjectBoard.Stages>
            <arc:ProjectBoardStage Key="planned" Header="Planned" />
            <arc:ProjectBoardStage Key="progress" Header="In progress" />
            <arc:ProjectBoardStage Key="review" Header="Review" />
            <arc:ProjectBoardStage Key="done" Header="Done" IsDone="True" />
        </arc:ProjectBoard.Stages>
        <arc:ProjectBoardTask Title="Split the settings API" StageKey="progress" Area="Platform" DueText="Wed" CommentCount="6" />
        <arc:ProjectBoardTask Title="Contrast audit for receipts" StageKey="review" Area="Checkout" DueText="Today" IsDueSoon="True" />
    </arc:ProjectBoard>
</UserControl>
```

```csharp
var rhea = new ProjectPerson("Rhea Calloway", "rhea");
board.Team.AddRange([rhea, new ProjectPerson("Tomas Vierra", "tomas")]);
board.CurrentUser = rhea;
board.TasksSource = sprint.Tasks; // an ObservableCollection<ProjectBoardTask>
```

`Tasks` is for tasks written in XAML or added in code; `TasksSource` takes your own collection and wins when set. A
collection that raises change notifications is observed, and a writable one is reordered by moves and receives new tasks,
so it always matches what the board shows. Changing a task's `StageKey` from outside moves its card too.

### Moving tasks

The right arrow sends a task to the next stage and the left arrow to the previous one; the arrow that would leave the board
is disabled. A moved task goes to the end of its new column, in both directions. `TaskMoving` comes first and can keep the
task where it is (`Cancel`); `TaskMoved` follows as the card starts to fly, with the stages and the positions before and
after, so it is the place to save the change. `MoveCommand` runs after a move made with the arrows, with a
`ProjectBoardMoveRequest`.

`MoveNext`, `MovePrevious` and `MoveTask` do the same from code; `MoveTask` can go to any stage and, with an index, to a
position in it. `FocusTask` puts the keyboard on a card and `ScrollToStage` brings a column into view.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ProjectBoardPersistedDemo">
    <!-- Every move and add is "saved" as it happens: TaskMoved fires as the card starts to fly. Review needs a reason:
         TaskMoving cancels moves into Review for tasks without comments. -->
    <StackPanel Spacing="16">
        <arc:ProjectBoard x:Name="Board" IsFramed="True" />
        <Border Padding="16,12"
                CornerRadius="16"
                Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource SurfaceMuted}">
            <StackPanel Spacing="6">
                <TextBlock Text="Saved changes"
                           FontWeight="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource WeightMedium}"
                           Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Foreground}" />
                <TextBlock x:Name="Log"
                           Text="Move a card or add a task."
                           FontSize="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TypeXS}"
                           LineHeight="18"
                           TextWrapping="Wrap"
                           Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
            </StackPanel>
        </Border>
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class ProjectBoardPersistedDemo : UserControl
{
    private readonly List<string> _lines = new();

    public ProjectBoardPersistedDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        ProjectBoardDemoData.Fill(Board);
        Board.TaskMoving += (_, e) =>
        {
            // A rule from the app: a task goes to review only once someone has commented on it.
            if (e.ToStage.Key == "review" && e.Task.CommentCount == 0)
            {
                e.Cancel = true;
                Write($"Kept “{e.Task.Title}” in {e.FromStage.Header}: review needs a comment first");
            }
        };
        Board.TaskMoved += (_, e) =>
            Write($"PATCH /tasks/{Short(e.Task.Key)}  stage: {e.FromStage.Key} → {e.ToStage.Key} (position {e.ToIndex + 1})");
        Board.TaskAdded += (_, e) =>
            Write($"POST /tasks  “{e.Task.Title}” in {e.Stage.Key}");
    }

    private static string Short(string key) => key.Length > 6 ? key[..6] : key;

    private void Write(string line)
    {
        _lines.Insert(0, line);
        if (_lines.Count > 5)
        {
            _lines.RemoveAt(_lines.Count - 1);
        }
        Log.Text = string.Join(Environment.NewLine, _lines);
    }
}
```

```csharp
board.TaskMoving += (_, e) =>
{
    if (e.ToStage.Key == "review" && e.Task.CommentCount == 0)
    {
        e.Cancel = true; // the app's rule: review needs a comment first
    }
};
board.TaskMoved += (_, e) => SaveStage(e.Task.Key, e.ToStage.Key, e.ToIndex);

void SaveStage(string taskKey, string stageKey, int position)
{
    // Send the change to your store; the board has already moved the card.
}
```

### All work and My work

With a `CurrentUser`, the header shows the switch. My work keeps the cards the current user owns (`Filter` is
`ProjectBoardFilter.Mine`); the others fade out where they are while the rest close up, and they fade back in when the
switch returns to All work. Columns count what they show and say "Nothing assigned to you" when they are empty; the header
and the sprint line always count every task. `Filter` is two-way and raises `FilterChanged`. Without a `CurrentUser` the
switch is hidden.

### Adding tasks

Add task raises `AddRequested`. Put a task in the event's `Task` to add it, or set `Handled` and add nothing, for
example to open your own form first and call `AddTask(task, stageKey)` when it is filled in. Without a handler the board
adds a draft: the next title of `DraftTitles`, with `DraftArea`, `NoDateText` as its due label and the current user as its
owner. New tasks go to the end of `AddStageKey` (the first stage by default), fade in, raise `TaskAdded`, run `AddCommand`
and are announced; focus stays on the Add button for the next one. `IsAddVisible` hides the button.

### Your own stages

Stages are data, so a board can follow any workflow. A stage's `EmptyText` replaces the board's empty texts for that
column.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ProjectBoardCustomStagesDemo">
    <!-- Five stages written in XAML, with their own empty texts; new tasks go to "Inbox", "Shipped" finishes them. -->
    <arc:ProjectBoard x:Name="Board"
                      Title="Mobile release 4.2"
                      IsFramed="True"
                      AddStageKey="inbox"
                      ProgressFormat="{}{0} of {1} live in the store build">
        <arc:ProjectBoard.Stages>
            <arc:ProjectBoardStage Key="inbox" Header="Inbox" EmptyText="Inbox zero" />
            <arc:ProjectBoardStage Key="scoped" Header="Scoped" />
            <arc:ProjectBoardStage Key="building" Header="Building" />
            <arc:ProjectBoardStage Key="testing" Header="Testing" EmptyText="Nothing waiting for QA" />
            <arc:ProjectBoardStage Key="shipped" Header="Shipped" IsDone="True" />
        </arc:ProjectBoard.Stages>
    </arc:ProjectBoard>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class ProjectBoardCustomStagesDemo : UserControl
{
    public ProjectBoardCustomStagesDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        var (rhea, tomas, ines) = ProjectBoardDemoData.CreateTeam();
        Board.Team.AddRange([rhea, tomas, ines]);
        Board.CurrentUser = tomas;
        Board.DraftTitles.AddRange(["Triage crash reports", "Check the tablet layout"]);
        Board.DraftArea = "QA";
        Board.Tasks.AddRange(
        [
            new ProjectBoardTask("Offline banner for the cart", "inbox") { Area = "Shop", DueText = "No date", Owner = ines },
            new ProjectBoardTask("Haptics on add to cart", "scoped") { Area = "Shop", DueText = "Mon", Owner = tomas, CommentCount = 2 },
            new ProjectBoardTask("Dark mode for the order history screen", "building") { Area = "Account", DueText = "Today", IsDueSoon = true, Owner = rhea, CommentCount = 5 },
            new ProjectBoardTask("Retry failed photo uploads", "building") { Area = "Reviews", DueText = "Thu", Owner = tomas, CommentCount = 1 },
            new ProjectBoardTask("Faster first launch", "shipped") { Area = "Platform", DueText = "Sep 30", Owner = rhea, CommentCount = 9 },
        ]);
    }
}
```

### Framed or flat

`IsFramed` draws the board as a card with a 1px border and a 24px radius, for a board that sits among other content. The
default is flat: the board fills its space with the surface color, like a page of its own. `Title` and the progress
sentence are optional (`IsProgressVisible` hides the sentence and the line).

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ProjectBoardFramedDemo">
    <!-- Framed: a bordered card with a 24px radius, for a board that sits among other content on a page. -->
    <arc:ProjectBoard x:Name="Board" IsFramed="True" MaxWidth="760" HorizontalAlignment="Center" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class ProjectBoardFramedDemo : UserControl
{
    public ProjectBoardFramedDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        ProjectBoardDemoData.Fill(Board);
    }
}
```

### Narrow containers

The board reads its own width, not the window's. Columns share the width down to 200 each (`MinColumnWidth`); below that
they scroll sideways. At 700 and below (`NarrowWidth`) each column is the width less 76, so the next one peeks in, the
team row is hidden, and the filter, Add and arrow buttons grow to 40px touch targets without making the cards taller. At
400 and below (`CompactWidth`) the actions take a row of their own and Add shows only its icon, keeping its name as a
tooltip. After scrolling stops, an offset within a third of a column of a column's start settles on it; a moved card's
column scrolls into view so the card can be followed.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ProjectBoardNarrowDemo">
    <!-- A 380-wide container: one column at a time with the next peeking in, swipe or scroll and it settles on a column;
         touch-sized arrows; Add shows only its icon. A moved card's column scrolls into view. -->
    <arc:ProjectBoard x:Name="Board" Width="380" IsFramed="True" HorizontalAlignment="Center" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs

    {
        InitializeComponent();
```

### Texts

Every text has an English default and a property: the progress sentence (`ProgressFormat`, "{0} of {1} shipped this
sprint"), the switch (`AllWorkText`, `MyWorkText`, `FilterLabel`), `TeamLabel`, `AddText`, the empty texts (`EmptyText`,
`EmptyMineText`), the drafts (`DraftTitles`, `NewTaskTitle`, `DraftArea`, `NoDateText`), and what screen readers hear
(`ColumnLabelFormat`, `ColumnLabelSingularFormat`, `MoveToFormat`, `MovePreviousText`, `MoveNextText`, `MovedFormat`,
`AddedFormat`, `DueLabelFormat`, `OwnerLabelFormat`, `CommentsFormat`, `CommentsSingularFormat`). In XAML a format that
starts with a brace needs `{}` in front.

```xml
<arc:ProjectBoard Title="Lancement"
                  ProgressFormat="{}{0} sur {1} livrées ce sprint"
                  AllWorkText="Tout"
                  MyWorkText="Mes tâches"
                  AddText="Ajouter"
                  MoveToFormat="Déplacer {0} vers {1}"
                  MovedFormat="{}{0} est maintenant dans {1}." />
```

## API reference

### ProjectBoard

A compact sprint board: a few stages as columns, each task a card that the arrow buttons send one stage left or right, a sprint line that fills as tasks reach the finished stage, a team row, an All work / My work switch and an Add button. A moved card flies in a straight line to the end of its new column while the old column closes up; filtered cards fade out in place as the others close the gap. Everything works with Tab, Enter and Space, and screen readers hear each move. Sized for tens of tasks; for hundreds, drag and drop and virtualization, use a full kanban board.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Stages` | `AvaloniaList<ProjectBoardStage>` | `null` | The stages, left to right (2 to 6 read well). |
| `Tasks` | `AvaloniaList<ProjectBoardTask>` | `null` | The tasks; each column shows its stage's tasks in this order. `TasksSource` takes precedence when set. |
| `TasksSource` | `IEnumerable?` | `null` | A collection of `ProjectBoardTask`s (observed when it raises collection changes) that replaces `Tasks`. A writable list is reordered by moves (a moved task goes to the end of its new column) and receives added tasks; a read-only one only has its tasks' stages changed. |
| `Team` | `AvaloniaList<ProjectPerson>` | `null` | The people shown as overlapping avatars in the header (hidden when empty and on narrow boards). |
| `CurrentUser` | `ProjectPerson?` | `null` | The person using the board: "My work" shows the tasks they own, drafts are theirs. Null hides the switch. |
| `Filter` | `ProjectBoardFilter` | `All` | Which cards are shown: every task or the current user's. |
| `Title` | `string?` | `null` | The heading in the header; null leaves the heading out (the progress sentence stays). |
| `IsProgressVisible` | `bool` | `true` | Shows the progress sentence and the sprint line (the line also divides the header from the columns). |
| `ProgressFormat` | `string` | `"{0} of {1} shipped this sprint"` | The progress sentence under the heading: {0} finished tasks, {1} all tasks (the filter never changes them). |
| `AllWorkText` | `string` | `"All work"` | The label of the button that shows every task. |
| `MyWorkText` | `string` | `"My work"` | The label of the button that shows the current user's tasks. |
| `FilterLabel` | `string` | `"Show"` | The screen reader name of the filter switch. |
| `TeamLabel` | `string` | `"Team"` | The screen reader name of the team avatars. |
| `AddText` | `string` | `"Add task"` | The Add button's label (its name and tooltip when only the icon shows). |
| `IsAddVisible` | `bool` | `true` | Shows the Add button. |
| `AddStageKey` | `string?` | `null` | The stage new tasks go to; null or unknown uses the first stage. |
| `DraftTitles` | `AvaloniaList<string>` | `null` | Titles the Add button cycles through for drafts when no `AddRequested` handler supplies a task. |
| `NewTaskTitle` | `string` | `"Untitled task"` | The title of a draft when `DraftTitles` is empty. |
| `DraftArea` | `string?` | `null` | The area label of drafts; null shows none. |
| `NoDateText` | `string?` | `"No date"` | The due label of drafts; null shows none. |
| `EmptyText` | `string` | `"No tasks yet"` | Shown in an empty column while every task is shown (a stage's own `EmptyText` wins). |
| `EmptyMineText` | `string` | `"Nothing assigned to you"` | Shown in an empty column while only the current user's tasks are shown. |
| `ColumnLabelFormat` | `string` | `"{0}, {1} tasks"` | A column's screen reader name: {0} the stage, {1} the number of cards shown. |
| `ColumnLabelSingularFormat` | `string` | `"{0}, 1 task"` | A column's screen reader name when it shows one card: {0} the stage. |
| `MoveToFormat` | `string` | `"Move {0} to {1}"` | An arrow button's name: {0} the task, {1} the stage it sends the task to. |
| `MovePreviousText` | `string` | `"the previous stage"` | Put in `MoveToFormat` for the left arrow of a task in the first stage (the button is disabled). |
| `MoveNextText` | `string` | `"the next stage"` | Put in `MoveToFormat` for the right arrow of a task in the last stage (the button is disabled). |
| `MovedFormat` | `string` | `"Moved {0} to {1}."` | Announced after a move: {0} the task, {1} its new stage. |
| `AddedFormat` | `string` | `"Added {0} to {1}."` | Announced after an add: {0} the task, {1} its stage. |
| `DueLabelFormat` | `string` | `"due {0}"` | The due part of a card's screen reader name: {0} the due label. |
| `OwnerLabelFormat` | `string` | `"assigned to {0}"` | The owner part of a card's screen reader name: {0} the owner's name. |
| `CommentsFormat` | `string` | `"{0} comments"` | The comments part of a card's screen reader name: {0} the count. |
| `CommentsSingularFormat` | `string` | `"1 comment"` | The comments part of a card's screen reader name for one comment. |
| `IsFramed` | `bool` | `false` | Draws the board as a bordered, rounded card (true); false fills its space flat (a page of its own). |
| `MinColumnWidth` | `double` | `200` | The narrowest column of the wide layout (200); narrower boards scroll sideways. |
| `NarrowWidth` | `double` | `700` | At this width and below the board turns narrow: touch-sized buttons, no team row, one column and a peek. |
| `CompactWidth` | `double` | `400` | At this width and below the actions take a row of their own and Add shows only its icon. |
| `AnimatesMoves` | `bool` | `true` | False makes moves, adds and filters change in place at once, as with reduced motion. |
| `MoveCommand` | `ICommand?` | `null` | Runs after a card's arrow button moved its task (parameter: a `ProjectBoardMoveRequest`). |
| `AddCommand` | `ICommand?` | `null` | Runs after the board added a task (parameter: the new `ProjectBoardTask`). |
| `DoneCount` | `int` | – | *Read-only.* The number of tasks in the finished stage (every task, whatever the filter). |
| `TaskCount` | `int` | – | *Read-only.* The number of tasks on the board (every task, whatever the filter). |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `TaskMoving` | `ProjectBoardTaskMovingEventArgs` | Raised before a task changes stage; set `Cancel` to keep it. |
| `TaskMoved` | `ProjectBoardTaskMovedEventArgs` | Raised when a task changed stage, as its card starts to fly (save the move here). |
| `AddRequested` | `ProjectBoardAddRequestedEventArgs` | Raised when the Add button is pressed: supply the task, add nothing, or let the board add a draft. |
| `TaskAdded` | `ProjectBoardTaskEventArgs` | Raised after the board added a task (the Add button or `AddTask`). |
| `FilterChanged` | `ProjectBoardFilterChangedEventArgs` | Raised when `Filter` changes. |

Pseudo-classes: `:narrow`, `:compact`, `:scrolling`, `:filtered`, `:framed`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

### ProjectBoardStage

One column of a `ProjectBoard`: a stage of the work, such as Planned, In progress, Review or Done. Tasks name their stage by `Key`.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Key` | `string` | `""` | A stable id that tasks refer to with `StageKey`. |
| `Header` | `string` | `""` | The column heading; empty uses `Key`. |
| `IsDone` | `bool` | `false` | Marks the stage that counts as finished: its tasks fill the sprint line, their titles turn quiet and their due labels stop warning. When no stage is marked, the last stage counts as finished. |
| `EmptyText` | `string?` | `null` | The text shown in the column while it has no cards; null uses the board's empty texts. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### ProjectBoardTask

One card of a `ProjectBoard`: a task with an area, a due label, a title, an owner and a comment count, in the stage named by `StageKey`. Changing `StageKey` moves the card to that column.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Key` | `string` | `""` | A stable id for events and persistence (a new GUID by default). |
| `Title` | `string` | `""` | The card title; long titles wrap. |
| `Area` | `string?` | `null` | The small label at the top left (a product area or team); null shows none. |
| `DueText` | `string?` | `null` | The due label at the top right ("Today", "Fri", "Oct 3"); null shows none. |
| `IsDueSoon` | `bool` | `false` | Shows the due label in the warning color; ignored once the task is in the finished stage. |
| `Owner` | `ProjectPerson?` | `null` | The person responsible (a 22px avatar; the "My work" filter compares it with the current user). |
| `CommentCount` | `int` | `0` | The number of comments; zero hides the comment count. |
| `StageKey` | `string?` | `null` | The `Key` of the task's stage; an unknown key shows it in the first stage. |
| `Tag` | `object?` | `null` | Any object the app wants to keep with the task. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### ProjectPerson

A person on a project block: a board card's owner, a calendar attendee, a meeting guest or a release owner. Without a picture the blocks draw a generated avatar: the initials on a soft color picked from the person's key or name, so the same person keeps the same color everywhere.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Key` | `string` | `""` | A stable id (cards and events refer to it); empty uses `Name`. |
| `Name` | `string` | `""` | The full name, read by screen readers and shown in lists. |
| `ShortName` | `string?` | `null` | The name used in short sentences ("Noor is busy"); null takes the first word of `Name`. |
| `Initials` | `string?` | `null` | The initials of the generated avatar; null takes the first letters of the first two words of the name. |
| `Avatar` | `IImage?` | `null` | A picture drawn in the avatar circle; null draws the generated avatar. |
| `Hue` | `double?` | `null` | The hue (0–360 degrees) of the generated avatar; null derives one from the key or name. |
| `Tag` | `object?` | `null` | Any object the app wants to keep with the person. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### ProjectBoardMoveRequest

A move made with a card's arrow buttons (the parameter of `MoveCommand`).

### Events

| Event | Raised when | Arguments |
|---|---|---|
| `TaskMoving` | A task is about to change stage | `Task`, `FromStage`, `ToStage`, `Cancel` |
| `TaskMoved` | A task changed stage, as its card starts to fly | `Task`, `FromStage`, `ToStage`, `FromIndex`, `ToIndex` |
| `AddRequested` | Add task was pressed | `Stage`, `Task` (set it to add your own), `Handled` |
| `TaskAdded` | The board added a task | `Task`, `Stage` |
| `FilterChanged` | `Filter` changed | `OldFilter`, `NewFilter` |

## Accessibility

- Keyboard: `Tab` and `Shift+Tab` go through All work, My work, Add task, then every enabled arrow, column by column
  and top to bottom; `Enter` or `Space` presses the focused button (chooses a filter, adds a task or moves the card).
- The board is a group named "Project board". Each column is a group named after its stage and the number of cards it
  shows ("Review, 1 task"); its cards are list items named after the task, its area, due label, owner and comments
  ("Split the settings API, Platform, due Wed, assigned to Rhea Calloway, 6 comments").
- The arrows are named after where they send the task ("Move Split the settings API to Review"); a disabled arrow says
  "the previous stage" or "the next stage". The switch is a group named "Show" with two toggle buttons that report which one
  is pressed. The team avatars are named "Team", the Add button "Add task" even when only its icon shows.
- Moves and adds are announced politely ("Moved Split the settings API to Review.", "Added Draft the pricing FAQ to
  Planned."); filtering is not, the column names already change.
- After a move, focus stays on the same arrow of the same card in its new column, or moves to the other arrow when that one
  turned off at the edge, so pressing Enter again keeps going; on narrow boards the column scrolls into view.
- Hover styles follow a mouse or a pen only; a finger never leaves a button looking hovered. Status never relies on color
  alone: the due label keeps its text, finished cards stay in the finished column.

## Motion

- **Moves**: the card flies from where it is drawn to the end of its new column in a straight line, on a Gentle spring
  (stiffness 340, damping 34, about 600 ms), above every other card. The cards under it in the old column slide up on the
  same spring, and both slots follow them: a closing slot never leaves a card hanging below it. A second press mid-flight
  starts again from where the card is drawn.
- **Filtering**: the highlight glides to the chosen button on a critically damped spring (stiffness 400, damping 40). Cards
  that leave fade out and shrink to 98% where they are while the others close up; cards that come back fade in and grow
  from 98%, all on the Gentle spring.
- **Adding**: the new card fades in and grows from 98%; the sprint line springs to its new ratio (also when tasks reach or
  leave the finished stage).
- **Hover and press**: colors change over 160 ms; the arrows press to 92%, Add to 97%, and Add dims to 88% under a mouse.
- Reduced motion and `AnimatesMoves="False"` apply moves, adds and filters in place at once and keep the color changes.
  Off applies everything at once. Nothing runs while the board is still.

## Related

- Release readiness, Kanban board, Week calendar and Availability picker, the other Projects blocks, share its people,
  avatars and progress line.
- `SegmentedControl` for a view switch outside the block.
- `AvatarGroup` for a stack of avatars elsewhere on the page.
- `LayoutMorph` for one set of cards in several layouts.
