# Release readiness

> A release gate where a short list of checks unlocks one action, with a progress bar, the owners, a notify switch and the result in place.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc.Blocks`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc.Blocks --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/blocks/release-readiness

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ReleaseReadinessPreviewDemo">
    <!-- Four checks, the first done; the rollout takes 1.2 seconds so the busy button shows. Data: ReleaseReadinessDemoData. -->
    <arc:ReleaseReadiness x:Name="Gate"
                          Margin="0,12"
                          Title="Version 5.3"
                          Subtitle="Lumen mobile · goes live Tuesday"
                          ChannelName="#launches" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class ReleaseReadinessPreviewDemo : UserControl
{
    public ReleaseReadinessPreviewDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Gate.Checks.AddRange(ReleaseReadinessDemoData.RolloutChecks());
        Gate.Owners.AddRange(ReleaseReadinessDemoData.RolloutOwners());

        // Start the rollout somewhere; here it only waits, so the button's busy state is visible for a moment.
        Gate.ReleaseAction = (_, cancellation) => Task.Delay(1200, cancellation);
    }
}
```

## When to use

`ReleaseReadiness` is the last step before something goes out: a short list of things that must be true, and one button
that stays locked until they are. As checks are ticked the bar fills and the text counts down ("2 to go", "All clear");
when every required check is done the bar turns green and the button unlocks. Pressing it runs your code, shows a spinner
while it works, and then says what happened right under the footer.

- **A release or rollout.** Sign-off, tests, release notes and support briefed, then "Start rollout". The notify switch
  decides whether a channel hears about it, and the success line says so.
- **A handover between teams.** Runbook, dashboards, alerts and open incidents must be done; a couple of nice-to-have
  checks can be marked optional so they are shown without holding the handover back.
- **Any irreversible action with a checklist.** A migration, a price change, a campaign send: anything where a person
  should confirm a few facts first and see the result in the same place.

## When not to use

- **Long or nested checklists.** The block is designed for three to eight checks in one list. Use a task list, a
  `Timeline` or a project board for dozens of items or for items with owners and dates of their own.
- **Checks the system can verify itself.** If a build server already knows whether tests passed, show that status
  instead of asking a person to tick it; a tick here is a person's word.
- **Forms.** Checks are booleans with a title and a description. Use `Checkbox`, `Input` and a submit button when people
  enter values.
- **Several actions.** The gate unlocks exactly one action. Offer other actions elsewhere on the page.

## Usage

The block derives from Avalonia's `TemplatedControl`. Each check is a `ReleaseCheck`, an `AvaloniaObject` with a title, an
optional description and `IsDone` (two-way). Owners are `ProjectPerson`s drawn as generated avatars: initials on a soft
tint picked from the person's key, never a photo unless you give one.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:ReleaseReadiness Title="Version 5.3"
                          Subtitle="Lumen mobile · goes live Tuesday"
                          ChannelName="#launches">
        <arc:ReleaseReadiness.Owners>
            <arc:ProjectPerson Name="Rina Kato" />
            <arc:ProjectPerson Name="Samir Aziz" />
        </arc:ReleaseReadiness.Owners>
        <arc:ReleaseCheck Title="Design signed off" Description="Final screens approved by product" IsDone="True" />
        <arc:ReleaseCheck Title="Smoke tests green" Description="Build 5.3.0-beta.2 passed on preview" />
        <arc:ReleaseCheck Title="Release notes written" Description="Customer summary drafted and reviewed" />
        <arc:ReleaseCheck Title="Support briefed" Description="Help desk knows what is changing" />
    </arc:ReleaseReadiness>
</UserControl>
```

### Anatomy

- **Header**: `Title`, `Subtitle` and the owners' avatars on the right (hidden when there are none).
- **Progress**: what is left on the left, the count ("1 of 4") on the right in tabular figures, and a 4px bar under them.
- **Checks**: one row per check. The whole label is part of the checkbox, so pressing the title or the description ticks
  it, and pointing anywhere on the row tints it.
- **Footer**: the notify switch at the start and the button at the end. When the two do not fit on one line the buttons
  move to a second line, still at the end.
- **Status line**: opens under the footer with the success or the error text.

### Checks and the gate

`TotalCount` counts the required checks and `DoneCount` the required ones that are done; `IsReady` is true when there is at
least one check and every required one is done. A check with `IsRequired="False"` is shown and can be ticked, but is left
out of the counts, the bar and the gate. Use `ChecksSource` for a collection you own (an `ObservableCollection` is
followed), or fill `Checks`. Ticking a box writes `IsDone` back, so a two-way binding on it keeps your model in step.

`CheckChanged` reports every tick with the old and new value and the counts after it; `ReadyChanged` fires when the gate
opens or closes again.

### Starting the release

Set `ReleaseAction` to the work the button starts. It receives a `ReleaseRequest` (whether to notify, every check, the
optional checks that were skipped, and the attempt number) and a cancellation token. While the task runs `State` is
`Releasing`: the button shows a spinner and keeps the keyboard focus, and the checks and the switch are locked. When it
finishes, the button reads `ReleasedText` with a check mark, the status line says the release is on its way (and that the
channel was told, when the switch was on) and a reset button appears.

```csharp
gate.ReleaseAction = async (request, cancellation) =>
{
    await deployments.StartAsync("lumen-mobile", "5.3.0", notify: request.Notify, cancellation);
};
gate.Released += (_, e) => log.Info($"Rollout started on attempt {e.Request.Attempt}");
```

`ReleaseCommand` runs first with the request as its parameter; when it cannot execute, the release does not start.
`ReleaseStarting` fires before either and can cancel. `ReleaseAsync()` does what the button does, `CancelRelease()` cancels
the token and puts the gate back at once (a late result of the task is ignored), and `Reset()` puts every check back:
to `IsInitiallyDone` when it is set, otherwise to the value the check had when the block first showed it. The notify switch
keeps its value across a reset.

### Failure and retry

An exception from the action (or the command) sets `State` to `Failed`. The error shows in the status line in the danger
color, the checks and the switch unlock, and the button is ready for another try with the focus still on it. The line
shows the exception's message, `ErrorFormatter`'s text when you set one, or `FailureText` when the message is empty.
Changing a check after a failure clears the error. A cancellation (`CancelRelease`, or the block leaving the window while
the task runs) is not a failure: the gate simply goes back to ready.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ReleaseReadinessFailingDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12" Margin="0,12">
        <arc:ReleaseReadiness x:Name="Gate"
                              Title="Version 5.3"
                              Subtitle="Lumen mobile · goes live Tuesday"
                              ChannelName="#launches" />
        <TextBlock x:Name="Log"
                   HorizontalAlignment="Center"
                   TextAlignment="Center"
                   TextWrapping="Wrap"
                   MaxWidth="520"
                   Text="Every second attempt fails, as a busy build server could. Tick the checks and start the rollout." />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class ReleaseReadinessFailingDemo : UserControl
{
    private int _runs;

    public ReleaseReadinessFailingDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Gate.Checks.AddRange(ReleaseReadinessDemoData.RolloutChecks());
        Gate.Owners.AddRange(ReleaseReadinessDemoData.RolloutOwners());

        // The first rollout goes through; the next one is refused, and the one after that (the retry) goes through again.
        Gate.ReleaseAction = async (_, cancellation) =>
        {
            await Task.Delay(900, cancellation);
            _runs++;
            if (_runs % 2 == 0)
            {
                throw new InvalidOperationException(
                    "The rollout could not start: the build is still uploading. Try again in a minute.");
            }
        };

        Gate.StateChanged += (_, e) => Log.Text = $"{e.OldState} → {e.NewState}";
        Gate.ReleaseFailed += (_, e) => Log.Text = $"Attempt {e.Request.Attempt} failed: {e.Exception.GetType().Name}";
        Gate.Released += (_, e) => Log.Text = $"Started on attempt {e.Request.Attempt}, notify: {(e.Notify ? "yes" : "no")}";
    }
}
```

### Framed or flat

`IsFramed` (the default) draws a card at most 560 wide with a 1px border, a 16 radius, the surface color and lines above
the checks and the footer. Set it to false to lay the block flat on the page at the container's width, for a full page
or a side panel; the rows keep their light dividers.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ReleaseReadinessFlatDemo">
    <!-- Laid flat on the page at the container's width: no card, no lines above the checks and the footer. -->
    <arc:ReleaseReadiness x:Name="Gate"
                          IsFramed="False"
                          MaxWidth="720"
                          Title="Version 5.3"
                          Subtitle="Lumen mobile · goes live Tuesday"
                          ChannelName="#launches" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class ReleaseReadinessFlatDemo : UserControl
{
    public ReleaseReadinessFlatDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Gate.Checks.AddRange(ReleaseReadinessDemoData.RolloutChecks());
        Gate.Owners.AddRange(ReleaseReadinessDemoData.RolloutOwners());
        Gate.ReleaseAction = (_, cancellation) => Task.Delay(800, cancellation);
    }
}
```

### Narrow containers

The block reads its own width, not the window's. At 388 or less every side padding tightens from 20 to 16. The header stays
on one line and shortens the subtitle with an ellipsis; the footer moves the buttons under the switch when they do not fit
beside it.

### Other words, optional checks

Every text is a property with an English default: `ReleaseText`, `ReleasedText`, `ResetText`; the progress texts
`RemainingFormat` ("{0} to go"), `RemainingOneText`, `ReadyText`, `ReleasingText` and `CountFormat` ("{0} of {1}"); the
notify switch's `NotifyText` or `NotifyFormat` ("Notify {0}") with `ChannelName`; the success lines `SuccessFormat` and
`SuccessNotifiedFormat` (with `ReleaseName`, or the title, and the channel); and the screen reader names `ChecksLabel`,
`ProgressLabel`, `OwnersLabel` or `OwnersLabelPrefix` with `AndWord`. `IsNotifyVisible` hides the switch and
`IsResetVisible` the reset button.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ReleaseReadinessHandoffDemo">
    <!-- Six checks, two optional (they do not hold the button back); no notify switch, other words throughout. -->
    <StackPanel Spacing="12" Margin="0,12">
        <arc:ReleaseReadiness x:Name="Gate"
                              Title="Hand over: billing service"
                              Subtitle="Platform team · Friday 16:00"
                              ReleaseName="The billing service"
                              IsNotifyVisible="False"
                              ChecksLabel="Handover checks"
                              ProgressLabel="Handover progress"
                              RemainingFormat="{}{0} required left"
                              RemainingOneText="1 required left"
                              ReadyText="Ready to hand over"
                              ReleasingText="Handing over"
                              ReleaseText="Hand over"
                              ReleasedText="Handed over"
                              ResetText="Undo"
                              SuccessFormat="{}{0} now belongs to the platform team." />
        <TextBlock x:Name="Log" HorizontalAlignment="Center" TextAlignment="Center" TextWrapping="Wrap" MaxWidth="520" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class ReleaseReadinessHandoffDemo : UserControl
{
    public ReleaseReadinessHandoffDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Gate.Checks.AddRange(ReleaseReadinessDemoData.HandoffChecks());
        Gate.Owners.AddRange(ReleaseReadinessDemoData.HandoffOwners());
        Gate.ReleaseAction = (_, cancellation) => Task.Delay(700, cancellation);

        Gate.CheckChanged += (_, e) =>
            Log.Text = $"{e.Check.Title}: {(e.NewValue ? "done" : "open")} · {e.DoneCount} of {e.TotalCount} required";
        Gate.Released += (_, e) =>
            Log.Text = e.Request.SkippedChecks.Count == 0
                ? "Handed over with every check done"
                : $"Handed over; skipped: {string.Join(", ", e.Request.SkippedChecks.Select(c => c.Title))}";
    }
}
```

## API reference

### ReleaseReadiness

A release gate: a few checks that must all be done before the one action unlocks. A header names the release and its owners, a bar fills as checks are ticked (and turns green when every required one is done), a switch chooses whether to notify a channel, and the button runs `ReleaseAction`. While it runs the button shows a spinner and the checks lock; on success the button reads `ReleasedText`, a status line opens under the footer and a reset button appears; on failure the error shows in the same line and the release can be tried again.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Title` | `string?` | `null` | The heading (the release's name, a version); null leaves it out. |
| `Subtitle` | `string?` | `null` | The line under the heading (where and when it ships); null leaves it out. |
| `OwnersSource` | `IEnumerable?` | `null` | The owners shown as overlapping avatars, when you give them as a list to follow; it wins over `Owners`. |
| `OwnersLabel` | `string?` | `null` | The screen reader name of the owners' avatars; null reads `OwnersLabelPrefix` and the names ("Owners: A and B"). |
| `OwnersLabelPrefix` | `string` | `"Owners: "` | Put before the owners' names in their generated screen reader name. |
| `AndWord` | `string` | `"and"` | The word joining the last two owners' names ("and"). |
| `ChecksSource` | `IEnumerable?` | `null` | The checks, when you give them as a list to follow (observed when it raises collection changes); it wins over `Checks`. |
| `ChecksLabel` | `string` | `"Release checks"` | The screen reader name of the list of checks. |
| `ProgressLabel` | `string` | `"Readiness"` | The screen reader name of the progress bar. |
| `IsNotifyEnabled` | `bool` | `true` | Whether the notify switch is on (two-way). A reset leaves it as it is. |
| `IsNotifyVisible` | `bool` | `true` | Whether the footer shows the notify switch. |
| `NotifyText` | `string?` | `null` | The notify switch's text; null formats `NotifyFormat` with `ChannelName`. |
| `NotifyFormat` | `string` | `"Notify {0}"` | The notify switch's text when `NotifyText` is null; {0} is `ChannelName`. |
| `ChannelName` | `string?` | `null` | The channel told about the release ("#launches"), used by the switch and the success line. |
| `ReleaseName` | `string?` | `null` | The release's name in the success line; null uses `Title`. |
| `ReleaseAction` | `Func<ReleaseRequest, CancellationToken, Task>?` | `null` | Starts the release: awaited when the button is pressed (or `ReleaseAsync` is called) with what the person chose and a token that `CancelRelease` (or the block leaving the window) cancels. An exception fails the attempt and shows its message; a cancellation returns the gate to ready without an error. Null releases at once. |
| `ReleaseCommand` | `ICommand?` | `null` | Run when a release starts, with the `ReleaseRequest` as the parameter, before `ReleaseAction`; when it cannot execute the release does not start. |
| `ReleaseText` | `string` | `"Start rollout"` | The release button's text before the release (an arrow follows it). |
| `ReleasedText` | `string` | `"Rollout started"` | The release button's text once the release started (a check mark leads it). |
| `ResetText` | `string` | `"Start over"` | The text of the button that appears after a release and puts the checks back. |
| `IsResetVisible` | `bool` | `true` | Whether the reset button appears after a release. |
| `RemainingFormat` | `string` | `"{0} to go"` | The progress text while more than one required check is open; {0} is how many. |
| `RemainingOneText` | `string` | `"1 to go"` | The progress text while one required check is open. |
| `ReadyText` | `string` | `"All clear"` | The progress text when every required check is done. |
| `ReleasingText` | `string` | `"Rolling out"` | The progress text from the moment the release starts until a reset. |
| `CountFormat` | `string` | `"{0} of {1}"` | The count on the right of the progress text; {0} is the required checks done, {1} all required checks. |
| `SuccessFormat` | `string` | `"{0} is on its way."` | The success line when nobody was notified; {0} is the release's name. |
| `SuccessNotifiedFormat` | `string` | `"{0} is on its way. We posted in {1}."` | The success line when the channel was notified; {0} is the release's name, {1} the channel. |
| `FailureText` | `string` | `"The rollout did not start. Try again."` | The error line when the exception has no message and no `ErrorFormatter` is set. |
| `ErrorFormatter` | `Func<Exception, string>?` | `null` | Turns a failed attempt's exception into the error line; null shows the exception's message. |
| `IsFramed` | `bool` | `true` | Draws a 560-wide bordered card (true); false lays the block flat on the page at the container's width. |
| `State` | `ReleaseReadinessState` | – | *Read-only.* Where the gate stands. |
| `DoneCount` | `int` | – | *Read-only.* How many required checks are done. |
| `TotalCount` | `int` | – | *Read-only.* How many checks are required (optional ones are not counted). |
| `IsReady` | `bool` | – | *Read-only.* True when there is at least one check and every required one is done. |
| `ErrorText` | `string?` | – | *Read-only.* The error line of the last failed attempt; null unless `State` is Failed. |
| `StatusText` | `string?` | – | *Read-only.* The line shown under the footer (the success or the error line); null while it is closed. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `CheckChanged` | `ReleaseCheckChangedEventArgs` | Raised when a check is ticked or cleared, by the person or by code. |
| `ReadyChanged` | `ReleaseReadyChangedEventArgs` | Raised when `IsReady` changes. |
| `StateChanged` | `ReleaseStateChangedEventArgs` | Raised when `State` changes. |
| `ReleaseStarting` | `ReleaseStartingEventArgs` | Raised before a release runs; setting `Cancel` keeps it from starting. |
| `Released` | `ReleasedEventArgs` | Raised when the release action finished without an error. |
| `ReleaseFailed` | `ReleaseFailedEventArgs` | Raised when the release action or command threw. |
| `ResetPerformed` | `ReleaseResetEventArgs` | Raised after `Reset` put the checks back. |

Pseudo-classes: `:framed`, `:compact`, `:ready`, `:releasing`, `:released`, `:failed`, `:status`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

### ReleaseCheck

One check of a `ReleaseReadiness` gate: a title, an optional line under it and whether it is done. Every required check must be done before the release can start; optional checks (`IsRequired` false) are shown and can be ticked, but do not hold the release back.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Key` | `string?` | `null` | A stable id the app can match the check by (events, saved state); null when the check has none. |
| `Title` | `string` | `""` | The check's title; also the checkbox's name for screen readers. |
| `Description` | `string?` | `null` | The line under the title; also read as the checkbox's help text. Null shows the title alone. |
| `IsDone` | `bool` | `false` | Whether the check is done (two-way: ticking the checkbox writes it back). |
| `IsInitiallyDone` | `bool` | `false` | The value `Reset` puts back. When it is not set, Reset puts back the value `IsDone` had when the block first showed the check. |
| `IsRequired` | `bool` | `true` | Whether the release waits for this check (true); an optional check is counted out of the gate and the progress. |
| `Tag` | `object?` | `null` | Any object the app wants to keep with the check. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### ReleaseRequest

What a release attempt was started with: passed to the release action, the command and the events.

### ReleaseReadinessState

Where a `ReleaseReadiness` gate stands.

Derives from `Enum`: every member of `Enum` works as well.

## Accessibility

- **Tab** moves through the checks, the notify switch and the button. The button is not a tab stop until the gate is
  ready; after a release only the reset button is.
- **Space** ticks or clears the focused check. **Enter** does not, so a check is never ticked by accident.
- **Space** or **Enter** flips the notify switch and presses the buttons.
- After a release the focus moves to the reset button (or to the status line when the reset button is hidden). After a
  reset it moves to the first check that is not done. After a failure it stays on the button for a retry. The focus only
  moves when it was inside the block, so a release started from code never takes it.
- The block is named by its title, and the title is a level 2 heading.
- The owners are one group named "Owners: Rina Kato and Samir Aziz" (`OwnersLabel` or `OwnersLabelPrefix`); the avatars are
  not read one by one.
- The bar is a read-only progress bar named by `ProgressLabel` with the required checks done as its value and all of them
  as its maximum. The list of checks is named by `ChecksLabel`.
- Each checkbox is named by its check's title and described by its description; required checks say so.
- What is left ("2 to go", "All clear", "Rolling out") is announced politely as it changes; the count beside it is not.
  The success line is announced politely and the error assertively, and an error repeated on a retry is announced again.
- While the action runs the button keeps its name and reports the releasing text as its status.

## Motion

- **Ticking a check**: the bar's fill slides on a critically damped spring (no overshoot, about 580 ms) and turns green in
  240 ms when every required check is done. The checkbox draws its mark on its own spring; the title fades to the
  secondary color in 160 ms. The texts change in place without animation.
- **Hover**: the row tints in 160 ms.
- **Releasing**: the button shows its spinner, then cross-fades its label with a short blur while its width springs to
  the new text. The status line opens on a smooth spring with a separate 160 ms fade; a reset closes it the same way.
- Reduced motion places the bar, the colors and the status line at once and keeps only the button's short cross-fade.
  Off applies every change at once.

## Related

- `Checkbox`, `Switch` and `Button`, the controls the block is made of.
- `Progress` for a standalone progress bar with a label.
- `ActionButton` for a single action with pending and success states but no checks.
- `Project board` and `Kanban board`, the other Projects blocks.

---

# Kanban board

> A team board whose cards lift, tilt with the pointer and spring into the slot that opens for them, with swimlanes by person, live work-in-progress limits, quick add and a details drawer.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc.Blocks`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc.Blocks --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/blocks/kanban-board

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.KanbanBoardPreviewDemo">
    <!-- One release of a field-inspection app (invented, KanbanBoardDemoData); Testing holds one card past its limit of two. -->
    <arc:KanbanBoard x:Name="Board" Title="Field app 4.2" Height="760" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs

public partial class KanbanBoardPreviewDemo : UserControl
{

        Board.Cards.Insert(9, new KanbanCard("FLD-215", "Compress photos before they leave the device", "testing")
```

## When to use

`KanbanBoard` is a complete board for work that moves through a fixed set of stages and whose order inside a stage
matters. Cards are picked up with the mouse, a pen, a finger (after a short hold) or the keyboard; while a card is lifted
a slot opens where it will land, the cards around it make room, and the column counts already show where the card would
end up. Columns can carry a limit that turns the column amber when it is exceeded.

- **A team's issue or task board.** Load the columns, the people and the cards from your tracker, and save the ordered
  list that `CardsChanged` hands over after every move or edit.
- **Pipelines with a manual order.** A sales pipeline, a hiring funnel or a content calendar where the card at the top of
  a stage is the next one to handle.
- **Boards that need a view per person.** `GroupBy="Assignee"` gives every person a swimlane with the same columns;
  dropping a card in another lane hands it over.

## When not to use

- **Work planned on dates.** Use a week calendar or a timeline when the question is *when*, not *in which stage*.
- **Read-only status summaries.** A table or a list with a status column is easier to scan and to sort; set
  `IsReadOnly` only for a shared view of a board people also edit.
- **Hundreds of cards in one column.** Every card is a live element so that it can glide; the board is comfortable up to a
  few hundred cards in total. Page or filter large backlogs, or use `DataGrid`.
- **Free-form arrangements.** Cards always snap into ordered columns; use a canvas for sticky-note style layouts.

## Usage

### Columns, people, labels and cards

The board takes four lists. `Columns` are the stages in order; give a column a `Limit` to warn when it holds more cards.
`People` are `ProjectPerson` objects: they draw the avatars, the swimlanes and the owner menu (without a picture they get
generated initials). `Labels` give cards a colored dot and a name. `Cards` is one flat list: the order of the list is the
order inside every column, which is also how you persist it.

A card refers to its column, owner and label by key (`ColumnKey`, `AssigneeKey`, `LabelKey`), so it can come straight
from a tracker's JSON. A card whose column is not on the board is not shown; in swimlanes, cards whose owner is not among
the people get a trailing "Unassigned" lane.

```xml
<arc:KanbanBoard Title="Sprint 18" Height="640">
    <arc:KanbanBoard.Columns>
        <arc:KanbanColumn Key="todo" Name="To do" />
        <arc:KanbanColumn Key="doing" Name="Doing" Limit="3" />
        <arc:KanbanColumn Key="done" Name="Done" />
    </arc:KanbanBoard.Columns>
    <arc:KanbanBoard.People>
        <arc:ProjectPerson Key="ines" Name="Ines Duarte" />
        <arc:ProjectPerson Key="tom" Name="Tomasz Bielski" />
    </arc:KanbanBoard.People>
    <arc:KanbanCard Key="SP-41" Title="Export the audit log as CSV" ColumnKey="todo" AssigneeKey="ines" Points="3" />
    <arc:KanbanCard Key="SP-42" Title="Rate limit the sign-in form" ColumnKey="doing" AssigneeKey="tom" Points="2" />
</arc:KanbanBoard>
```

Bind `CardsSource` to a collection your view model owns. A writable list (an `ObservableCollection` or an
`AvaloniaList`) is reordered in place on every drop and every new card, so it always matches the board; a read-only
collection is left alone and the board keeps its own order. Changes made from outside, such as a new list or a card whose
`ColumnKey` changed, are applied together and the cards glide to their new places.

### Saving changes

`CardsChanged` fires after every move, edit, checklist change and new card. Its `Reason` says what happened and `Cards` is
a snapshot of the whole list in board order: store it as it is. `CardMoved` adds the details of a move: the columns and
owners before and after, the card's position in the list before and after, and `ChangeSource` (pointer, touch, keyboard,
the drawer, or a method call).

```csharp
var saved = new List<(string Key, string Column, string? Owner)>();
board.CardsChanged += (_, e) =>
{
    // Store the snapshot as it is: its order is the order inside every column.
    saved = e.Cards.Select(c => (c.Key, c.ColumnKey, c.AssigneeKey)).ToList();
};
board.CardMoved += (_, e) => Debug.WriteLine($"{e.Card.Key}: {e.FromColumn?.Name} → {e.ToColumn?.Name}");
```

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.KanbanBoardControlledDemo">
    <!-- The board edits a list the page owns; every change is logged with its reason and the order that results. -->
    <Grid RowDefinitions="560,Auto" RowSpacing="16">
        <arc:KanbanBoard x:Name="Board" Title="Field app 4.2" />
        <Border Grid.Row="1"
                Padding="16"
                CornerRadius="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource RadiusPanel}"
                BorderThickness="1"
                BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Border}">
            <Grid ColumnDefinitions="*,*" ColumnSpacing="24">
                <StackPanel Spacing="6">
                    <TextBlock Text="Changes" FontWeight="SemiBold" />
                    <TextBlock x:Name="Log"
                               Text="Move, edit or add a card."
                               TextWrapping="Wrap"
                               Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
                </StackPanel>
                <StackPanel Grid.Column="1" Spacing="6">
                    <TextBlock Text="Saved order" FontWeight="SemiBold" />
                    <TextBlock x:Name="Order"
                               TextWrapping="Wrap"
                               FontFamily="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource MonoFontFamily}"
                               FontSize="12"
                               Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
                </StackPanel>
            </Grid>
        </Border>
    </Grid>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using System.Collections.ObjectModel;
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class KanbanBoardControlledDemo : UserControl
{
    private readonly ObservableCollection<KanbanCard> _cards = new(KanbanBoardDemoData.CreateCards());
    private readonly List<string> _log = new();

    public KanbanBoardControlledDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Board.Columns = KanbanBoardDemoData.CreateColumns();
        Board.People = KanbanBoardDemoData.CreatePeople();
        Board.Labels = KanbanBoardDemoData.CreateLabels();
        // The page owns the list: the board reorders it in place, and CardsChanged hands over the order to persist.
        Board.CardsSource = _cards;
        Board.CardsChanged += (_, e) =>
        {
            _log.Insert(0, $"{e.Reason}: {e.Card?.Key} {e.Card?.Title}");
            if (_log.Count > 6)
            {
                _log.RemoveAt(_log.Count - 1);
            }
            Log.Text = string.Join(Environment.NewLine, _log);
            ShowOrder(e.Cards);
        };
        Board.CardMoved += (_, e) =>
        {
            _log.Insert(0, $"Moved by {e.ChangeSource}: {e.FromColumn?.Name} → {e.ToColumn?.Name}, list position {e.FromIndex} → {e.ToIndex}");
        };
        ShowOrder(_cards);
    }

    private void ShowOrder(IReadOnlyList<KanbanCard> cards)
    {
        var lines = Board.Columns.Select(column =>
            $"{column.Name,-9} {string.Join(" ", cards.Where(c => c.ColumnKey == column.Identity).Select(c => c.Key))}");
        Order.Text = string.Join(Environment.NewLine, lines);
    }
}
```

### Swimlanes

`GroupBy` switches between one row of columns and one swimlane per person; the switch in the toolbar does the same, and
every card flies to its new place. Lane heads stay at the left edge while the board scrolls sideways; the column heads stay
at the top while it scrolls down. Column counts and limits always count every lane; each lane head counts its own cards.
Dropping a card in another person's lane changes its `AssigneeKey`.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.KanbanBoardSwimlanesDemo">
    <!-- One lane per person; drag a card into another lane to hand it over, or use Shift and the arrows after Space. -->
    <arc:KanbanBoard x:Name="Board" Title="Field app 4.2" GroupBy="Assignee" Height="860" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class KanbanBoardSwimlanesDemo : UserControl
{
    public KanbanBoardSwimlanesDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        KanbanBoardDemoData.Fill(Board);
        Board.CurrentUser = Board.People[2];
    }
}
```

### Work-in-progress limits

A column is over its limit only when it holds more cards than `Limit` (a full column is fine). Its count turns amber, an
"Above limit" chip appears and its cells take a warm tint; the slot of a card about to be dropped there says so too. The
counts follow a dragged card live, so the warning shows before the drop. The board only warns: handle `CardMoving` and
set `Cancel` to send the card back when the limit must hold. `ColumnLimitStateChanged` reports a column going over or
coming back.

```csharp
board.CardMoving += (_, e) => e.Cancel = e.IsTargetOverLimit && e.From.ColumnKey != e.To.ColumnKey;
```

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.KanbanBoardWipLimitsDemo">
    <!-- Building allows 3 cards and Testing 2. Limits warn by default; turn on strict limits to refuse such drops. -->
    <StackPanel Spacing="12">
        <StackPanel Orientation="Horizontal" Spacing="16">
            <arc:Switch x:Name="Strict" Content="Strict limits" />
            <TextBlock x:Name="Status"
                       VerticalAlignment="Center"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}"
                       Text="Drag a card into Building or Testing." />
        </StackPanel>
        <arc:KanbanBoard x:Name="Board" Title="Field app 4.2" Height="620" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class KanbanBoardWipLimitsDemo : UserControl
{
    public KanbanBoardWipLimitsDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        KanbanBoardDemoData.Fill(Board);
        Board.CardMoving += (_, e) =>
        {
            // The board only warns; a handler makes the limits strict by sending the card back.
            if (Strict.IsChecked == true && e.IsTargetOverLimit && e.From.ColumnKey != e.To.ColumnKey)
            {
                e.Cancel = true;
                Status.Text = $"{e.Card.Key} went back: {Board.Columns.First(c => c.Identity == e.To.ColumnKey).Name} is full.";
            }
        };
        Board.ColumnLimitStateChanged += (_, e) =>
        {
            Status.Text = e.IsOverLimit
                ? $"{e.Column.Name} is over its limit: {e.Count} of {e.Limit}."
                : $"{e.Column.Name} is back within its limit: {e.Count} of {e.Limit}.";
        };
    }
}
```

### Quick add and the details drawer

The "+" in every column head and the Add card row under every column open a composer at the end of the column (in
swimlanes, in the lane of `CurrentUser`, by default the first person). Enter adds the card and keeps the composer open for
the next one, Shift+Enter breaks the line and Escape closes it. New cards get the next number after the highest id on the
board ("FLD-244" → "FLD-245"); set `CardKeyFactory` to make your own ids, and handle `CardCreating` to change or refuse a
card before it is added.

Clicking a card, or Enter on a focused card, raises `CardInvoked` and opens the details drawer: the title, the status, the
owner, the label, the due date, the estimate, notes and a checklist. Edits apply to the card as they are typed. Changing
the status keeps the card's place in the list, so it lands on top of a later column or at the bottom of an earlier one. Set
`OpenedCard` (or call `OpenCard`) to open the drawer from code, and set `Handled` in `CardInvoked` or turn off
`IsDetailsEnabled` to show your own view instead.

### Narrow containers and read-only boards

The board reads its own width. Columns share the width down to `MinColumnWidth` (251) and the board then scrolls sideways.
At `CompactWidth` (560) and below, columns are `CompactColumnWidth` (235) wide, the paddings tighten, and the board snaps
to the nearest column after a sideways scroll, with the first column flush against the left edge. The drawer is never wider
than the board minus 16, so it covers a narrow board, and its status options wrap two by two.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.KanbanBoardNarrowDemo">
    <!-- At 560 and below the columns are 235 wide and the board snaps sideways from column to column. -->
    <arc:KanbanBoard x:Name="Board"
                     Title="Field app 4.2"
                     Width="380"
                     Height="720"
                     HorizontalAlignment="Center" />
</UserControl>
```


card. `IsDragEnabled` and `IsQuickAddEnabled` turn the two features off one at a time.


### Texts

Every word the board shows or announces is in `Strings`, a `KanbanBoardLabels` object with English defaults. Texts with
values are functions, so the word order can change in a translation.

```csharp
board.Strings = new KanbanBoardLabels
{
    StatusView = "Statut",
    LanesView = "Par personne",
    AddCard = "Ajouter une carte",
    CardsWord = n => n == 1 ? "carte" : "cartes",
    Dropped = (title, column) => $"{title} déposée dans {column}."
};
```

## API reference

### KanbanBoard

A team board of status columns where cards lift, tilt with the pointer's speed and spring into the slot that opens for them. Group it by person for swimlanes; columns can carry work-in-progress limits that update live while a card is dragged; every column has quick add, and a card opens into a details drawer for its title, status, owner, notes and checklist. Cards move with the mouse, pen, touch (after a short hold) or the keyboard (Space, arrows, Space), and every pick up, move and drop is announced. The card list's order is the order inside every column: persist `CardsChanged`'s snapshot to keep the board as the user left it.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Title` | `string?` | `null` | The heading over the board; null shows only the card count. |
| `Columns` | `AvaloniaList<KanbanColumn>` | `null` | The status columns, left to right. |
| `People` | `AvaloniaList<ProjectPerson>` | `null` | The people cards can belong to: avatars on cards, one swimlane each, and the owner menu. |
| `Labels` | `AvaloniaList<KanbanLabel>` | `null` | The labels cards can carry (the dot color and the name). |
| `Cards` | `AvaloniaList<KanbanCard>` | `null` | The cards in board order (the order inside every column). Use it in XAML; `CardsSource` wins when set. |
| `CardsSource` | `IEnumerable?` | `null` | A collection of `KanbanCard`s that replaces `Cards` (observed when it raises collection changes). A writable list is reordered in place on every drop and quick add; a read-only one is left alone and the board keeps its own order (persist `CardsChanged`). |
| `GroupBy` | `KanbanGroupBy` | `Status` | Status columns only, or one swimlane per person; switching flies every card to its new place. |
| `CurrentUser` | `ProjectPerson?` | `null` | The person new cards belong to (and whose swimlane quick add opens in); null uses the first person. |
| `OpenedCard` | `KanbanCard?` | `null` | The card shown in the details drawer; set it to open the drawer, null to close it. |
| `IsQuickAddEnabled` | `bool` | `true` | Shows the "+" buttons and the Add card rows. |
| `IsDetailsEnabled` | `bool` | `true` | Opens the details drawer when a card is clicked or Enter is pressed on it (false only raises `CardInvoked`). |
| `IsDragEnabled` | `bool` | `true` | Lets cards be dragged (pointer, touch and keyboard). |
| `IsReadOnly` | `bool` | `false` | No dragging, no quick add and no edits; the drawer still opens and shows the card. |
| `AllowUnassigned` | `bool` | `false` | Adds an "Unassigned" entry to the owner menu (cards without an owner always get their own swimlane). |
| `CardKeyFactory` | `Func<KanbanColumn, string>?` | `null` | Makes the id of a card created with quick add; null continues the highest number ("FLD-244" → "FLD-245"). |
| `DragThreshold` | `double` | `5` | How far a mouse or pen must move before a pressed card lifts (Arc: 5). |
| `TouchHoldDelay` | `TimeSpan` | `00:00:00.2500000` | How long a touch must rest on a card before it lifts; moving earlier scrolls the board (Arc: 250ms). |
| `MinColumnWidth` | `double` | `251` | The narrowest a column gets on a wide board; narrower boards scroll sideways (Arc: 251). |
| `CompactColumnWidth` | `double` | `235` | The column width of a compact board (Arc: 235). |
| `CompactWidth` | `double` | `560` | At this width and below the board is compact: narrow columns, tighter paddings, sideways snapping (Arc: 560). |
| `DrawerMaxWidth` | `double` | `400` | The widest the details drawer gets; it is never wider than the board minus 16 (Arc: 400). |
| `Strings` | `KanbanBoardLabels` | `null` | Every word the board shows or announces. |
| `CardInvokedCommand` | `ICommand?` | `null` | Runs when a card is clicked or Enter is pressed on it (parameter: the `KanbanCard`). |
| `CardCreatedCommand` | `ICommand?` | `null` | Runs after quick add created a card (parameter: the new `KanbanCard`). |
| `CardMovedCommand` | `ICommand?` | `null` | Runs after a card was moved (parameter: the `KanbanCardMovedEventArgs`). |
| `IsDragging` | `bool` | – | *Read-only.* True while a card is lifted (pointer, touch or keyboard). |
| `DraggedCard` | `KanbanCard?` | – | *Read-only.* The lifted card, or null. |
| `IsCompact` | `bool` | – | *Read-only.* True while the board is at or below `CompactWidth`. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `CardsChanged` | `KanbanCardsChangedEventArgs` | Raised after every move, edit, checklist change or new card, with the full card list in board order. |
| `CardMoved` | `KanbanCardMovedEventArgs` | Raised after a card moved (dropped, or its status or owner changed in the drawer). |
| `CardCreating` | `KanbanCardCreatingEventArgs` | Raised before quick add creates a card; change its key or title, or cancel it. |
| `CardCreated` | `KanbanCardCreatedEventArgs` | Raised after quick add created a card. |
| `CardInvoked` | `KanbanCardEventArgs` | Raised when a card is clicked or Enter is pressed on it; set Handled to keep the drawer closed. |
| `DetailsOpened` | `KanbanCardEventArgs` | Raised when the details drawer opened for a card. |
| `DetailsClosed` | `KanbanCardEventArgs` | Raised when the details drawer closed. |
| `CardEdited` | `KanbanCardEditedEventArgs` | Raised when the title or the notes of a card were edited in the drawer. |
| `ChecklistItemToggled` | `KanbanChecklistItemToggledEventArgs` | Raised when a checklist step was ticked or unticked in the drawer. |
| `GroupByChanged` | `KanbanGroupByChangedEventArgs` | Raised when the grouping changed. |
| `ColumnLimitStateChanged` | `KanbanColumnLimitEventArgs` | Raised when a column went over its limit or came back under it (committed changes, not drag previews). |
| `CardDragStarting` | `KanbanCardDragStartingEventArgs` | Raised before a card lifts; set Cancel to keep it in place. |
| `CardDragStarted` | `KanbanCardDragEventArgs` | Raised after a card lifted. |
| `CardDragTargetChanged` | `KanbanCardDragEventArgs` | Raised when the place a lifted card would land in changed. |
| `CardMoving` | `KanbanCardMovingEventArgs` | Raised before a lifted card is dropped; set Cancel to send it back. |
| `CardDragCancelled` | `KanbanCardDragCancelledEventArgs` | Raised when a drag ended without a drop and the card is going back. |

Pseudo-classes: `:compact`, `:wrap`, `:lanes`, `:details-open`, `:dragging`, `:read-only`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

### KanbanColumn

A status column of a `KanbanBoard`, with an optional work-in-progress limit.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Key` | `string` | `""` | A stable id that cards refer to in `ColumnKey`; empty uses `Name`. |
| `Name` | `string` | `""` | The column's heading. |
| `Limit` | `int?` | `null` | The most cards the column should hold; more shows a warning (null: no limit). Equal to the limit is fine. |
| `Count` | `int` | – | *Read-only.* How many cards the column holds (set by the board, across every swimlane). |
| `IsOverLimit` | `bool` | – | *Read-only.* True while the column holds more cards than its `Limit`. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### KanbanCard

A card on a `KanbanBoard`. Cards refer to their column, owner and label by key, so they can come straight from a tracker's JSON; the order of the board's card list is the order inside every column.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Key` | `string` | `""` | The card's id, shown in its top left corner (for example "FLD-214"). |
| `Title` | `string` | `""` | The card's title (it wraps; it is never cut short). |
| `ColumnKey` | `string` | `""` | The `Identity` of the card's column. |
| `AssigneeKey` | `string?` | `null` | The `Identity` of the card's owner; null for none. |
| `LabelKey` | `string?` | `null` | The `Identity` of the card's label; null for none. |
| `Due` | `DateOnly?` | `null` | The due date; null shows none. |
| `Points` | `int?` | `null` | The estimate in points; null shows none. |
| `Description` | `string?` | `null` | Free notes, edited in the details drawer. |
| `Checklist` | `AvaloniaList<KanbanChecklistItem>` | `null` | The card's checklist steps. |
| `Tag` | `object?` | `null` | Any object the app wants to keep with the card. |
| `ChecklistDone` | `int` | – | *Read-only.* How many checklist steps are done. |
| `ChecklistTotal` | `int` | – | *Read-only.* How many checklist steps there are. |
| `IsChecklistComplete` | `bool` | – | *Read-only.* True when the card has steps and every one is done. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### KanbanLabel

A label that cards can carry (a colored dot and a name).

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Key` | `string` | `""` | A stable id that cards refer to in `LabelKey`; empty uses `Name`. |
| `Name` | `string` | `""` | The label's text. |
| `Tone` | `KanbanLabelTone` | `Accent` | The dot's color family. |
| `Color` | `Color?` | `null` | An exact dot color; wins over `Tone` when set. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### KanbanChecklistItem

One step of a card's checklist.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Text` | `string` | `""` | The step's text. |
| `IsDone` | `bool` | `false` | True once the step is done. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### KanbanBoardLabels

Every word `KanbanBoard` shows or announces, in English by default. Replace the instance (or create one with `with`-style initializers) to translate or reword; texts with values are functions so word order can change.

### KanbanCardsChangedEventArgs

Data of `CardsChanged`: why the board changed and the full card list afterwards, in board order (the order inside each column). Persist `Cards` to keep the board as it is.

Derives from `RoutedEventArgs`: every member of `RoutedEventArgs` works as well.

### KanbanCardMovedEventArgs

Data of `CardMoved`: where a card was and where it is now.

Derives from `RoutedEventArgs`: every member of `RoutedEventArgs` works as well.

## Accessibility

- **Keyboard.** Tab reaches the view switch, then every "+", then each column's cards from top to bottom followed by its
  Add card row. Enter on a card opens its details. Space lifts it: Up and Down move it inside its column, Left and Right to
  the neighbouring column at the same position, Shift with Up or Down to the neighbouring swimlane; Space or Enter places
  it and Escape puts it back. Moving the focus away from a lifted card also puts it back.
- Every pick up, move and drop is announced at once ("Signature pad on the handover form lifted. Building, place 1."),
  including the person when a card changes lanes. New cards, status changes from the drawer and columns going over their
  limit are announced politely.
- Cards are buttons named "title, id, owner", described by their label, due date, checklist progress and estimate.
- Limits are shown in words as well as color: the count reads "4 of 3 allowed" and the chip and the slot say the limit is
  exceeded.
- The drawer is modal inside the board: focus moves to its close button, Tab stays inside it, and Escape, the close
  button or a click on the dimmed board closes it and returns the focus to the card. Escape in the owner menu closes only
  the menu. The text fields show a focus ring. Closing the composer returns the focus to the button that opened it.
- The view switch and the drawer's status are radio groups with one tab stop; the arrow keys change the choice.

## Motion

- **Lifting**: a card lifts after the pointer has moved more than `DragThreshold` (5px), or after a touch has rested for
  `TouchHoldDelay` (250ms); a quicker swipe scrolls the board. The card follows the pointer from the spot it was grabbed,
  grows to 1.035 and tilts with the horizontal speed (0.0064° per px/s, at most 7°) on a quick spring; when the pointer
  rests the tilt settles back to level. It is drawn above the whole board, so it can ride over the column heads and the
  title without being cut off.
- **Making room**: the slot appears where the card was and fades in; the cards around it, and the slot itself, glide on
  the layout spring (critically damped, about 0.6s) and keep their speed when the target changes again.
- **Dropping**: the card rides a small spring (stiffness 690, damping 51) into its slot, starting with the speed it was
  thrown at, and follows the slot if it is still gliding; its shadow and border ease back over 240 and 160ms. Escape flies it
  home the same way.
- **Edges**: near an edge of the board (64px) it scrolls on both axes, faster the closer the pointer, up to 1200px/s, and
  the slot keeps up with the content moving under a resting pointer.
- **Switching views, keyboard moves and drawer changes** move every affected card on the layout spring. The drawer slides
  in on the same spring while the board dims over 240ms; the composer grows and shrinks with it. Counts roll.
- Reduced motion keeps the slot, the counts and short fades but drops the tilt and every flight: cards land at once. Off
  applies every change at once.

## Related

- `ReorderableList` for reordering a single list.
- `ProjectPerson` and the other Projects blocks for the people on the board.
- `SegmentedControl`, `DropdownMenu` and `RollingDigits`, the pieces the board's toolbar, owner menu and counts follow.

# Site header

> A sticky website header that turns solid on scroll, with a gliding active link, mega menu panels, and a mobile sheet.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc.Blocks`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc.Blocks --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/blocks/site-header

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.SiteHeaderPreviewDemo">
    <!-- Arc's preview: the header inside a small scrolling page, with a switch between its three layouts. -->
    <StackPanel x:Name="Host" Spacing="16">
        <arc:SegmentedControl HorizontalAlignment="Center"
                              SelectedValue="mega"
                              SelectionChanged="OnLayoutChanged"
                              AutomationProperties.Name="Header layout">
            <arc:SegmentedOption Value="mega" Label="Mega menu" />
            <arc:SegmentedOption Value="simple" Label="Simple" />
            <arc:SegmentedOption Value="centered" Label="Centered" />
        </arc:SegmentedControl>
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Automation;
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class SiteHeaderPreviewDemo : UserControl
{
    private readonly SiteHeader _header = new() { Current = "product" };
    private readonly TextBlock _title;
    private readonly TextBlock _status = new() { Opacity = 0, Height = 0 };

    public SiteHeaderPreviewDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        // Arc's example items, with a drawn picture on the Product card.
        _header.ItemsSource = SiteHeaderDemoData.ExampleItems();
        _header.Navigate += (_, e) => _status.Text = $"Opened {e.Label}";
        AutomationProperties.SetLiveSetting(_status, AutomationLiveSetting.Polite);
        _header.PropertyChanged += (_, e) =>
        {
            if (e.Property == SiteHeader.CurrentProperty)
            {
                OnCurrentChanged(_header.Current);
            }
        };
        var frame = SiteHeaderDemoData.CreateFrame(_header, 520, out _title);
        Host.Children.Add(frame);
        Host.Children.Add(_status);
    }

    private void OnCurrentChanged(string? current)
    {
        _title.Text = current switch
        {
            "product" => "Product",
            "resources" => "Resources",
            "pricing" => "Pricing",
            "customers" => "Customers",
            _ => "Arc"
        };
    }

    private void OnLayoutChanged(object? sender, SelectionChangedEventArgs e)
    {
        if (sender is SegmentedControl { SelectedValue: string value })
        {
            _header.Variant = value switch
            {
                "simple" => SiteHeaderVariant.Simple,
                "centered" => SiteHeaderVariant.Centered,
                _ => SiteHeaderVariant.Mega
            };
        }
    }
}
```

## When to use

`SiteHeader` is the top bar of a marketing or documentation site. It holds the brand, the main links and one or two
actions, stays at the top of the page while people scroll, and opens a panel of grouped links when a menu is too big
for one row.

- **A product site with several sections**: Product and Resources open panels with described links and a feature card;
  Pricing and Customers are plain links.
- **A documentation site**: the `Simple` layout puts three or four links beside the brand, with the current section
  marked by a line under it.
- **A site with few links and a calm look**: the `Centered` layout puts the links in a quiet capsule in the middle, with
  the current link as a raised pill.
- **A narrow host**: below `CollapseWidth` (760 by default) the links fold into a menu sheet. The block follows its own
  width, so a header in a narrow pane folds even when the window is wide.

## When not to use

- **Navigation inside an application**: use `Sidebar` or `Tabs`. The header is for pages people arrive at, not for
  switching between tools they already use.
- **A page title with breadcrumbs and actions**: use `PageHeader`.
- **A single menu of commands**: use `DropdownMenu`.

## Usage

```xml
<ScrollViewer>
    <StackPanel>
        <arc:SiteHeader Current="product" />
        <!-- the page -->
    </StackPanel>
</ScrollViewer>
```

Without items the header shows Arc's example set (Product, Resources, Pricing, Customers), so a bare `SiteHeader` looks
like the Arc preview. Put the header inside the `ScrollViewer` it should stick to, or set `ScrollSource` when it
overlays one. Avalonia has no `position: sticky`: the header follows the scroll offset and stays at the top of the
viewport. The page content can start under the header (a negative top margin of the header's height) so a hero slides
beneath it.

### Items, links and the feature card

```xml
<arc:SiteHeader>
    <arc:SiteHeaderItem Value="guides" Label="Guides">
        <arc:SiteHeaderLink Label="Quick start" Description="Install and run in five minutes" Href="https://example.com/start" />
        <arc:SiteHeaderLink Label="Theming" Description="Tune color, radius and motion" />
        <arc:SiteHeaderItem.Feature>
            <arc:SiteHeaderFeature Title="What's new" Description="The spring release." Href="https://example.com/new" />
        </arc:SiteHeaderItem.Feature>
    </arc:SiteHeaderItem>
    <arc:SiteHeaderItem Value="pricing" Label="Pricing" Href="https://example.com/pricing" />
</arc:SiteHeader>
```

`Items` is an `AvaloniaList<SiteHeaderItem>`; `ItemsSource` wins when it is set and is observed when it raises collection
changes. An item with `Links` opens a panel in the `Mega` variant and is a plain link in the others. `Value` is the
item's stable name: `Current` and `SiteHeaderNavigateEventArgs.Section` use it. `SiteHeader.CreateExampleItems()` returns
Arc's items as a starting point. The feature card's `Image` is any `IImage`; it is shown 16:10 and cropped to fill, and
`ImageDescription` is what it shows. Without an image the card shows only its text.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.SiteHeaderSimpleDemo">
    <!-- Your own brand name and three plain links; the links have addresses, so a click opens them when nothing handles Navigate. -->
    <Border x:Name="FrameHost">
        <arc:SiteHeader x:Name="Header"
                        Variant="Simple"
                        BrandName="Northwind Docs"
                        BrandHref="https://example.com"
                        Current="guides"
                        PrimaryActionLabel="Open the app"
                        PrimaryActionHref="https://example.com/app"
                        IsSecondaryActionVisible="False" />
    </Border>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class SiteHeaderSimpleDemo : UserControl
{
    public SiteHeaderSimpleDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Header.ItemsSource = SiteHeaderDemoData.DocsItems();
        // The header goes into the same small scrolling page as the preview.
        FrameHost.Child = null;
        FrameHost.Child = SiteHeaderDemoData.CreateFrame(Header, 360, out _);
    }
}
```

### Choosing a destination

Every destination (an item, a panel link, the feature card, the brand, an action) raises the bubbling `Navigate` event
and runs `NavigateCommand` with the same `SiteHeaderNavigateEventArgs`. `Kind` says what was chosen, `Section` names the
item it belongs to and `Link`, `Feature` or `Item` carry the data objects. Choosing something inside an item also sets
`Current` to that item and closes the panel and the sheet. When nobody sets `Handled` and the destination has an
absolute http, https or mailto `Href`, the header opens it with the platform launcher.

```csharp
header.Navigate += (_, e) =>
{
    router.GoTo(e.Href ?? e.Label);
    e.Handled = true; // do not launch the address
};
```

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.SiteHeaderEventsDemo">
    <!-- Navigate reports every destination; Current is two way; IsMenuOpen and OpenItemValue show the header's state. -->
    <StackPanel Spacing="12">
        <Border x:Name="FrameHost" />
        <TextBlock x:Name="State"
                   FontSize="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TypeSM}"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
        <ItemsControl x:Name="Log">
            <ItemsControl.ItemTemplate>
                <DataTemplate x:DataType="x:String">
                    <TextBlock Text="{Binding}"
                               FontFamily="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource MonoFontFamily}"
                               FontSize="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TypeXS}"
                               Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
                </DataTemplate>
            </ItemsControl.ItemTemplate>
        </ItemsControl>
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using System.Collections.ObjectModel;
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class SiteHeaderEventsDemo : UserControl
{
    private readonly ObservableCollection<string> _lines = new();
    private readonly SiteHeader _header = new() { Current = "product" };

    public SiteHeaderEventsDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        _header.ItemsSource = SiteHeaderDemoData.StudioItems();
        Log.ItemsSource = _lines;
        // Handled marks the destination as dealt with: nothing is launched.
        _header.Navigate += (_, e) =>
        {
            _lines.Insert(0, $"{e.Kind}: {e.Label}{(e.Section is null ? "" : $" (in {e.Section})")}");
            while (_lines.Count > 5)
            {
                _lines.RemoveAt(_lines.Count - 1);
            }
            e.Handled = true;
        };
        _header.PropertyChanged += (_, e) =>
        {
            if (e.Property == SiteHeader.CurrentProperty || e.Property == SiteHeader.OpenItemValueProperty
                || e.Property == SiteHeader.IsMenuOpenProperty || e.Property == SiteHeader.IsScrolledProperty)
            {
                ShowState();
            }
        };
        FrameHost.Child = SiteHeaderDemoData.CreateFrame(_header, 420, out _);
        ShowState();
    }

    private void ShowState()
    {
        State.Text = $"Current: {_header.Current ?? "none"}   Panel: {_header.OpenItemValue ?? "closed"}   " +
                     $"Menu: {(_header.IsMenuOpen ? "open" : "closed")}   Scrolled: {_header.IsScrolled}";
    }
}
```

### Scrolling and solid state

The bar is transparent at the top of the page. Once the scroll offset passes `ScrollThreshold` (8) it turns solid: a
background, a bottom border and a resting shadow. It turns transparent again only below half the threshold, so it never
flickers at the edge. `IsScrolled` reports the state. The bar is also solid while a panel or the menu sheet is open.
Set `IsSticky` to false to let the header scroll away.

### Mega menu panels

Hovering a trigger with a mouse opens its panel after 70 ms; moving to another trigger switches at once. The panel
closes 180 ms after the pointer leaves the bar and the panel. Clicking a trigger toggles its panel. Touch and pen taps
never open a panel by hovering. The panel's height springs to the height of the current face, growing and shrinking on
different springs. When you move to a neighbouring item the new content slides in from the side you moved toward and
the old content slides away. Use `OpenPanel(value)` and `ClosePanel()` from code; `OpenItemValue` reports the open item.

### Narrow layouts and the menu sheet

Below `CollapseWidth` the links, the secondary action and the panels give way to a menu button. The sheet drops from the
bar: groups expand one at a time, plain links sit in rows, and the actions come last in two equal columns. A scrim
covers the page and closes the sheet when pressed, and the page does not scroll while the sheet is open. Use
`OpenMenu()`, `CloseMenu()` and the two-way `IsMenuOpen` from code.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.SiteHeaderNarrowDemo">
    <!-- The header follows its own width: in a 360 wide frame the links fold into the menu sheet. -->
    <Border x:Name="FrameHost" Width="360" HorizontalAlignment="Center">
        <arc:SiteHeader x:Name="Header" />
    </Border>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class SiteHeaderNarrowDemo : UserControl
{
    public SiteHeaderNarrowDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Header.ItemsSource = SiteHeaderDemoData.ExampleItems();
        Header.Current = "resources";
        FrameHost.Child = null;
        FrameHost.Child = SiteHeaderDemoData.CreateFrame(Header, 520, out _);
    }
}
```

### Content guidelines

- Keep the bar to four or five links. Move the rest into a panel.
- Describe a panel link in one short line that says what is there, not that it is a link.
- One primary action. The secondary action is for people who already have an account.

## API reference

### SiteHeader

A website header in three layouts (Arc's site header block): it sticks to the top of its scroll view and turns solid once the page scrolls, marks the current section with an indicator that glides between links, opens springy mega menu panels whose content slides in from the side you moved toward, and folds into a menu sheet when it is narrower than `CollapseWidth` (the block's own width, not the window's). Data driven: the links are `SiteHeaderItem`s (or `ItemsSource`); without items the header shows Arc's example set. Choosing any destination raises `Navigate` (and runs `NavigateCommand`); when nobody handles the event and the destination has an absolute http, https or mailto address, it is opened.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Variant` | `SiteHeaderVariant` | `Mega` | Identifies `Variant`. |
| `BrandName` | `string` | `"Arc"` | Identifies `BrandName`. |
| `BrandHref` | `string?` | `null` | Identifies `BrandHref`. |
| `BrandMark` | `object?` | `null` | Identifies `BrandMark`. |
| `Items` | `AvaloniaList<SiteHeaderItem>` | – | *Read-only.* Identifies `Items`. |
| `ItemsSource` | `IEnumerable<SiteHeaderItem>?` | `null` | Identifies `ItemsSource`. |
| `Current` | `string?` | `null` | Identifies `Current`. |
| `PrimaryActionLabel` | `string` | `"Get Arc"` | Identifies `PrimaryActionLabel`. |
| `PrimaryActionHref` | `string?` | `null` | Identifies `PrimaryActionHref`. |
| `IsPrimaryActionVisible` | `bool` | `true` | Identifies `IsPrimaryActionVisible`. |
| `SecondaryActionLabel` | `string` | `"Sign in"` | Identifies `SecondaryActionLabel`. |
| `SecondaryActionHref` | `string?` | `null` | Identifies `SecondaryActionHref`. |
| `IsSecondaryActionVisible` | `bool` | `true` | Identifies `IsSecondaryActionVisible`. |
| `TrailingContent` | `object?` | `null` | Identifies `TrailingContent`. |
| `IsSticky` | `bool` | `true` | Identifies `IsSticky`. |
| `ScrollSource` | `ScrollViewer?` | `null` | Identifies `ScrollSource`. |
| `ScrollThreshold` | `double` | `8` | Identifies `ScrollThreshold`. |
| `IsScrolled` | `bool` | – | *Read-only.* Identifies `IsScrolled`. |
| `IsMenuOpen` | `bool` | `false` | Identifies `IsMenuOpen`. |
| `OpenItemValue` | `string?` | – | *Read-only.* Identifies `OpenItemValue`. |
| `CollapseWidth` | `double` | `760` | Identifies `CollapseWidth`. |
| `IsCollapsed` | `bool` | – | *Read-only.* Identifies `IsCollapsed`. |
| `Label` | `string` | `"Main"` | Identifies `Label`. |
| `OpenMenuLabel` | `string` | `"Open menu"` | Identifies `OpenMenuLabel`. |
| `CloseMenuLabel` | `string` | `"Close menu"` | Identifies `CloseMenuLabel`. |
| `NavigateCommand` | `ICommand?` | `null` | Identifies `NavigateCommand`. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Navigate` | `SiteHeaderNavigateEventArgs` | Identifies `Navigate`. |

Pseudo-classes: `:solid`, `:narrow`, `:centered`, `:panel-open`, `:menu-open`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

### SiteHeaderItem

A top level destination of the `SiteHeader` (Arc's `SiteHeaderItem`). With `Links` and the `Mega` variant it opens a panel; otherwise it is a plain link.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Value` | `string` | `""` | Identifies `Value`. |
| `Label` | `string` | `""` | Identifies `Label`. |
| `Href` | `string?` | `null` | Identifies `Href`. |
| `Feature` | `SiteHeaderFeature?` | `null` | Identifies `Feature`. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### SiteHeaderLink

One destination inside a mega menu panel (Arc's `SiteHeaderLink`).

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Label` | `string` | `""` | Identifies `Label`. |
| `Description` | `string?` | `null` | Identifies `Description`. |
| `Icon` | `Geometry?` | `null` | Identifies `Icon`. |
| `Href` | `string?` | `null` | Identifies `Href`. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### SiteHeaderFeature

The card beside the links of a mega menu panel (Arc's `SiteHeaderFeature`).

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Title` | `string` | `""` | Identifies `Title`. |
| `Description` | `string?` | `null` | Identifies `Description`. |
| `Href` | `string?` | `null` | Identifies `Href`. |
| `Image` | `IImage?` | `null` | Identifies `Image`. |
| `ImageDescription` | `string?` | `null` | Identifies `ImageDescription`. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### SiteHeaderNavigateEventArgs

Arguments of `Navigate`.

Derives from `RoutedEventArgs`: every member of `RoutedEventArgs` works as well.

## Accessibility

- The links are a navigation landmark named by `Label`. The sheet is a second navigation landmark with the same name.
- A trigger reports whether its panel is expanded; the current link reports that it is selected. The panel is a region
  named by its item. The menu button's name changes between `OpenMenuLabel` and `CloseMenuLabel` and it reports
  whether the sheet is open; a group row reports whether it is expanded.
- Keyboard focus shows a 2 px ring; pointer focus shows none. Hover effects apply only to a mouse or pen.
- Every text is a property, so a localized site can replace "Get Arc", "Sign in", the menu labels and the landmark name.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` | Move through the brand, the links, the actions and the menu button in order |
| `Left` / `Right` | In the links: move focus to the previous or next link, wrapping at the ends; while a panel is open the panel follows to the new link (or closes on a plain link) |
| `Down` on a trigger | Open its panel and focus the first link |
| `Up` / `Down` / `Home` / `End` in a panel | Move between the panel's links and the feature card; `Up` on the first one closes the panel and returns to the trigger |
| `Enter` / `Space` | Choose the focused link, or toggle a trigger or a menu group |
| `Escape` | Close the panel and return to its trigger; otherwise close the sheet and return to the menu button |

## Motion

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| The bar turns solid | Background, border and shadow fade in 240 ms | At once | At once |
| The hover block | Appears on the first link, glides between links, vanishes when the pointer leaves | At once | At once |
| The current marker | Glides between links on a spring | At once | At once |
| A panel opens | Fades in 160 ms while it settles from 6 px above and a slight scale | Appears | Appears |
| A panel closes | Fades out in 180 ms, moving up 4 px | 120 ms fade | At once |
| The panel height | Springs to the face's height; growing and shrinking use different springs | At once | At once |
| Panel content changes | New content slides 36 px in through a short blur; old content slides out and fades in 120 ms | Fade | At once |
| The menu icon | Menu and close swap with a quarter turn and a small scale | Fade | At once |
| The sheet | Drops from the bar on a spring; rows rise in one after another; groups open on a spring | At once | At once |

## Related

- `PageHeader` for the title block of an application page.
- `Sidebar` for navigation inside an application.
- The site footer for the matching bottom of a marketing page.
