# Site footer

> A website footer with link columns and newsletter, a minimal layout, and a large fading Arc mark.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc.Blocks`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc.Blocks --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/blocks/site-footer

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.SiteFooterPreviewDemo">
    <!-- Arc's preview: a layout switch above a rounded frame. The frame springs between the layouts' heights while the new layout fades in. -->
    <StackPanel Spacing="16">
        <arc:SegmentedControl x:Name="Layouts"
                              HorizontalAlignment="Center"
                              AutomationProperties.Name="Footer layout"
                              SelectedValue="columns"
                              SelectionChanged="OnLayoutChanged">
            <arc:SegmentedOption Value="columns" Label="Columns" />
            <arc:SegmentedOption Value="minimal" Label="Minimal" />
            <arc:SegmentedOption Value="logo" Label="Logo" />
        </arc:SegmentedControl>
        <Border BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Border}"
                BorderThickness="1"
                CornerRadius="20"
                Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Background}"
                ClipToBounds="True">
            <arc:SpringSizeDecorator Axis="Height" Spring="Smooth">
                <arc:ArcContentSwap x:Name="Frame"
                                    Mode="Fade"
                                    EnterDuration="0:0:0.24"
                                    ExitDuration="0:0:0" />
            </arc:SpringSizeDecorator>
        </Border>
        <!-- Says which link was pressed, for screen readers (Arc's visually hidden live paragraph). -->
        <TextBlock x:Name="Note"
                   Height="0"
                   AutomationProperties.LiveSetting="Polite" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Automation;
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class SiteFooterPreviewDemo : UserControl
{
    public SiteFooterPreviewDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Show(SiteFooterVariant.Columns);
    }

    private void OnLayoutChanged(object? sender, SelectionChangedEventArgs e)
    {
        // SelectedValue is applied while the XAML loads, before the named fields are assigned; the constructor shows the first layout.
        if (Frame is null || sender is not SegmentedControl layouts)
        {
            return;
        }

        Show((layouts.SelectedValue as string) switch
        {
            "minimal" => SiteFooterVariant.Minimal,
            "logo" => SiteFooterVariant.Logo,
            _ => SiteFooterVariant.Columns
        });
    }

    // The frame draws the border, so the footer drops its own top border (Arc: ".frame .footer { border-top: 0 }").
    private void Show(SiteFooterVariant variant)
    {
        var footer = new SiteFooter { Variant = variant, BorderThickness = new Avalonia.Thickness(0) };
        footer.Navigate += (_, args) =>
        {
            Note.Text = $"Opened {args.Link.Label}";
            AutomationProperties.SetName(Note, Note.Text);
        };
        Frame.Content = footer;
    }
}
```

## When to use

`SiteFooter` closes a marketing or documentation site. It carries the links people look for at the bottom of a page
(product, resources, company), the legal lines, a system status and an email signup, in one of three layouts.

- **A product site with a newsletter**: the Columns layout puts the brand, a tagline and a release-notes signup beside
  three link columns.
- **A docs site or an app's help pages**: the Minimal layout is one quiet row of links and one line of copyright, status
  and social links.
- **A landing page that ends with the brand**: the Logo layout drops the newsletter and ends in a large arch that fades
  into the page and rises in when it scrolls into view.

## When not to use

- **A dense app screen**: an in-app status bar or a sidebar footer is smaller; this block is a page-level footer.
- **A signup that is the point of the page**: use the Newsletter signup block, which gives the form the whole section.
- **A closing call to action**: use the CTA section block above the footer and keep the footer for navigation.

## Usage

With nothing set the footer shows Arc's sample: the Arc brand, three columns, legal and social links and an "All systems
normal" status.

```xml
<arc:SiteFooter />
```

Everything is data: name the brand, give your own columns and links, and handle what is pressed.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.SiteFooterCustomDemo">
    <!-- Own brand, two columns, real addresses, a degraded status, and a log of what was pressed. -->
    <StackPanel Spacing="12">
        <Border BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Border}"
                BorderThickness="1"
                CornerRadius="20"
                Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Background}"
                ClipToBounds="True">
            <arc:SiteFooter x:Name="Footer"
                            BorderThickness="0"
                            BrandName="Northwind"
                            BrandHref="https://northwind.example"
                            Tagline="Freight tracking for small fleets."
                            IsNewsletterVisible="False"

                <arc:SiteFooterColumn Title="Platform">
                    <arc:SiteFooterLink Label="Tracking" Href="https://northwind.example/tracking" />
                    <arc:SiteFooterLink Label="Routes" Href="https://northwind.example/routes" />
                    <arc:SiteFooterLink Label="API" Href="https://developers.northwind.example" IsExternal="True" />

            </arc:SiteFooter>

        <TextBlock x:Name="Log"
                   Text="Press a link to see the event."
                   FontSize="12"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class SiteFooterCustomDemo : UserControl
{
    public SiteFooterCustomDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        // Handled here, so the footer does not open the address: the log shows what the event carries.
        Footer.Navigate += (_, e) =>
        {
            e.Handled = true;
            Log.Text = $"Navigate: {e.Kind} \"{e.Link.Label}\" {e.Link.Href ?? "(no address)"}";
        };
    }
}
```

```xml
<arc:SiteFooter BrandName="Northwind"
                BrandHref="https://northwind.example"
                Tagline="Freight tracking for small fleets."
                IsNewsletterVisible="False"
                StatusLabel="Delays in EU routing"
                StatusTone="Warning">

    </arc:SiteFooterColumn>
</arc:SiteFooter>
```

### Layouts

`Variant` picks `Columns`, `Minimal` or `Logo`. Columns and Logo share the intro, the three link columns and the legal row;
only Columns shows the newsletter, and only Logo shows the arch. Minimal shows the brand with one row of links, then
the copyright and tagline with the status and social links. Its links are `Links`; when that is null it uses the first
link of each column and the first two legal links.

### Links

A `SiteFooterLink` has a `Label`, an optional `Href` and `IsExternal` (an outward arrow). Pressing a link, the brand or
the status raises `Navigate` with the link and where it sits (`Brand`, `Column`, `Legal`, `Social`, `Status`) and runs
`NavigateCommand`. When the event is not marked handled and `Href` is an absolute http, https or mailto address, the
footer opens it with the platform launcher. A link without `Href` only raises the event.

`Columns` holds the link columns (or bind `ColumnsSource`, which wins and is observed). `LegalLinks` and `SocialLinks`
replace the sample links beside the copyright and at the end of the legal row.

### Newsletter

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.SiteFooterSubscribeDemo">
    <!-- SubscribeAsync fails on the first send and succeeds on the second, so both endings show; the log lists the Subscribed event. -->
    <StackPanel Spacing="12">
        <Border BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Border}"
                BorderThickness="1"
                CornerRadius="20"
                Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Background}"
                ClipToBounds="True">
            <arc:SiteFooter x:Name="Footer" BorderThickness="0" />
        </Border>
        <TextBlock x:Name="Log"
                   Text="Enter an address and press Subscribe. The first send fails, so press it again to see the confirmation."
                   FontSize="12"
                   TextWrapping="Wrap"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class SiteFooterSubscribeDemo : UserControl
{
    private int _sends;

    public SiteFooterSubscribeDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Footer.SubscribeAsync = SendAsync;
        Footer.Subscribed += (_, e) => Log.Text = $"Subscribed: {e.Email}";
    }

    // A real app would call its mailing list here; throwing is how a send fails.
    private async Task SendAsync(string email, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
    {
        await Task.Delay(1200, cancellationToken);
        if (++_sends % 2 == 1)
        {
            Log.Text = $"Send {_sends} failed for {email}";
            throw new InvalidOperationException("The list is unavailable.");
        }
    }
}
```

The signup validates in place. An empty field says "Enter your email address" and a malformed one "That email doesn't
look right". Validation starts when the field is left with text in it, and then runs on every keystroke. Submitting
loads (the button spins and the field is read only), awaits `SubscribeAsync`, and ends in the done state: the button
reads "Subscribed" with a check mark and the line under it says "Check {address} to confirm". Throwing from
`SubscribeAsync` returns to idle with the failure message. `Subscribed` is raised on success.

```csharp
footer.SubscribeAsync = async (email, cancellationToken) =>
{
    await Task.Delay(500, cancellationToken); // call your list here; throw to show the failure message
};
footer.Subscribed += (_, e) => Console.WriteLine($"Subscribed {e.Email}");
```

Every text of the form is a property (`NewsletterTitle`, `NewsletterDescription`, `NewsletterPlaceholder`,
`NewsletterSubscribeLabel`, `NewsletterSubscribedLabel`, `NewsletterEmptyEmailMessage`, `NewsletterInvalidEmailMessage`,
`NewsletterFailedMessage`, `NewsletterConfirmFormat`) with Arc's English as the default.

### Status

`StatusLabel`, `StatusTone` (`Success`, `Warning`, `Danger`) and `StatusHref` describe the status link; hide it with
`IsStatusVisible="False"`.

### Responsive behavior

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.SiteFooterNarrowDemo">
    <!-- 420 wide, inside the 520 breakpoint: two link columns, a full-width newsletter and a stacked legal row. -->
    <Border Width="420"
            HorizontalAlignment="Center"
            BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Border}"
            BorderThickness="1"
            CornerRadius="20"
            Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Background}"
            ClipToBounds="True">
        <arc:SiteFooter BorderThickness="0" />
    </Border>
</UserControl>
```

The breakpoints follow the footer's own width, not the window's. At 760 or less the intro sits above the link columns
with a 40 px gap. At 520 or less the columns take two across with 32 / 16 gaps, the newsletter loses its 400 px limit
and the legal row becomes a column, left aligned.

## API reference

### SiteFooter

A website footer in three layouts: link columns with a newsletter signup (`Columns`), a single quiet row (`Minimal`), and a closing layout where the Arc arch rises in, oversized and cropped by the bottom edge, fading into the page (`Logo`). The newsletter validates in place, keeps its width while the button morphs, and confirms without a toast. Every text, link, column and the status line can be replaced; with nothing set the footer shows Arc's sample footer.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Variant` | `SiteFooterVariant` | `Columns` | The layout: Columns (default), Minimal or Logo. |
| `BrandName` | `string` | `"Arc"` | The brand name, next to the mark and in the copyright line. |
| `BrandHref` | `string?` | `null` | Where the brand name leads; without it the name only raises the navigate event. |
| `BrandMark` | `object?` | `null` | The brand mark; null draws Arc's arch. |
| `Tagline` | `string?` | `"Interface components that move with intent."` | One short line under the brand (and in the copyright line of Minimal); empty hides it. |
| `Columns` | `AvaloniaList<SiteFooterColumn>` | – | *Read-only.* The link columns; empty (and without `ColumnsSource`) shows Arc's three sample columns. |
| `ColumnsSource` | `IEnumerable<SiteFooterColumn>?` | `null` | The link columns from a collection; when set it wins over `Columns` and is observed. |
| `Links` | `AvaloniaList<SiteFooterLink>?` | `null` | The one-row links of the Minimal layout; null shows the first link of each column and the first two legal links. |
| `LegalLinks` | `AvaloniaList<SiteFooterLink>` | – | *Read-only.* Small links beside the copyright; empty shows Privacy, Terms and Licenses. |
| `SocialLinks` | `AvaloniaList<SiteFooterLink>` | – | *Read-only.* Social links at the end of the legal row; empty shows X, GitHub and LinkedIn. |
| `IsNewsletterVisible` | `bool` | `true` | Whether the newsletter signup shows (Columns layout only). |
| `NewsletterTitle` | `string?` | `"Get the monthly release notes"` | The newsletter's title. |
| `NewsletterDescription` | `string?` | `"One email a month. Unsubscribe anytime."` | The hint under the newsletter input. |
| `NewsletterPlaceholder` | `string?` | `"you@example.com"` | The placeholder of the newsletter input. |
| `NewsletterEmailLabel` | `string` | `"Email address"` | The accessible name of the newsletter input. |
| `NewsletterSubscribeLabel` | `string` | `"Subscribe"` | The text of the subscribe button. |
| `NewsletterSubscribedLabel` | `string` | `"Subscribed"` | The text of the button after subscribing. |
| `NewsletterEmptyEmailMessage` | `string` | `"Enter your email address"` | The error for an empty address. |
| `NewsletterInvalidEmailMessage` | `string` | `"That email doesn't look right"` | The error for an address that does not look like `name@domain.tld`. |
| `NewsletterFailedMessage` | `string` | `"We couldn't subscribe you. Try again in a moment"` | The error shown when `SubscribeAsync` throws. |
| `NewsletterConfirmFormat` | `string` | `"Check {0} to confirm"` | The confirmation after subscribing; `{0}` is the address. |
| `SubscribeAsync` | `Func<string, CancellationToken, Task>?` | `null` | Called with a valid address; throw to show the failure message, return to show the subscribed state. Null simulates a 900 ms success. |
| `IsStatusVisible` | `bool` | `true` | Whether the status link shows. |
| `StatusLabel` | `string` | `"All systems normal"` | The text of the status link. |
| `StatusTone` | `SiteStatusTone` | `Success` | The color of the status dot. |
| `StatusHref` | `string?` | `null` | Where the status leads; without it the status only raises the navigate event. |
| `Year` | `int?` | `null` | The year of the copyright line; null uses this year. |
| `NavigationLabel` | `string` | `"Footer"` | The accessible name of the link navigation. |
| `LegalLabel` | `string` | `"Legal"` | The accessible name of the legal links. |
| `SocialLabel` | `string` | `"Social"` | The accessible name of the social links. |
| `NavigateCommand` | `ICommand?` | `null` | Runs when a link is pressed, after `Navigate`; its parameter is the event arguments. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Navigate` | `SiteFooterNavigateEventArgs` | A link, the brand or the status was pressed. Mark it handled to keep the footer from opening the address. |
| `Subscribed` | `SiteFooterSubscribedEventArgs` | The newsletter signup succeeded. |

Pseudo-classes: `:narrow`, `:stacked`, `:columns`, `:minimal`, `:logo`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

### SiteFooterLink

One link of a `SiteFooter`. A link without `Href` only raises the footer's navigate event.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Label` | `string` | `""` | The text of the link. |
| `Href` | `string?` | `null` | The destination. An absolute http, https or mailto address is opened when the navigate event is not handled. |
| `IsExternal` | `bool` | `false` | Whether the link leaves the site: it shows an outward arrow. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### SiteFooterColumn

A titled column of links in a `SiteFooter`.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Title` | `string` | `""` | The heading of the column. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### SiteFooterNavigateEventArgs

Arguments of `NavigateEvent`: a link or the status was pressed.

Derives from `RoutedEventArgs`: every member of `RoutedEventArgs` works as well.

### SiteFooterSubscribedEventArgs

Arguments of `SubscribedEvent`: the newsletter signup succeeded.

Derives from `RoutedEventArgs`: every member of `RoutedEventArgs` works as well.

## Accessibility

- The footer is a content-info landmark. The link columns are a navigation named by `NavigationLabel`; the legal and
  social links are lists named by `LegalLabel` and `SocialLabel`.
- Links with an address are exposed as links; those without are buttons.
- The email field is named by `NewsletterEmailLabel`. The hint, the confirmation and the failure are announced
  politely, and an error is announced as an alert.
- The mark, the arrows and the status dot are decorative.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` | Move through the brand, the newsletter, the links and the status |
| `Enter` | In the email field: subscribe. On a link or the button: activate it |
| `Space` | Activate the focused link or button |

Keyboard focus draws a 2 px ring around a link; a pointer press focuses without a ring.

## Motion

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| Link and status color | 160 ms | Immediate | Immediate |
| Outward arrow on hover | Moves 1 px right and up in 160 ms | Still | Still |
| Input border (focus, invalid) | 160 ms | Immediate | Immediate |
| Newsletter line | Rises from 4 px below through a blur in 240 ms; the old line lifts away in 120 ms | Fades only | Immediate |
| Subscribe button | The label cross-fades with a blur, the width springs and a spinner shows while loading | The button's reduced rules | Immediate |
| Logo arch | Once, when 30% is on screen: fades in and rises 40 px over 900 ms | Shown at once | Shown at once |

## Related

- The Newsletter signup block for a full-width signup section.
- The CTA section block for a closing call to action above the footer.
- The Site header block for the matching top bar.

# CTA section

> A call to action as a centered closing section, a split beside a setup card that completes itself, or a dismissible banner.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc.Blocks`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc.Blocks --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/blocks/cta-section

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.CtaSectionPreviewDemo">
    <!-- Arc's preview: a layout switch above a framed section. The frame springs to its content's height after a switch. -->
    <StackPanel Spacing="16">
        <arc:SegmentedControl x:Name="Layouts"
                              AutomationProperties.Name="Call to action layout"
                              HorizontalAlignment="Center"
                              SelectedValue="centered">
            <arc:SegmentedOption Value="centered" Label="Centered" />
            <arc:SegmentedOption Value="split" Label="Split" />
            <arc:SegmentedOption Value="banner" Label="Banner" />
        </arc:SegmentedControl>
        <Border x:Name="Frame"
                BorderThickness="1"
                BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Border}"
                Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Background}"
                CornerRadius="20"
                ClipToBounds="True">
            <Panel x:Name="Body" VerticalAlignment="Top">
                <arc:CtaSection x:Name="Section" IsDismissible="True" />
                <!-- After the banner is dismissed: one way back. -->
                <Border x:Name="Restore" IsVisible="False" MinHeight="104" Padding="24">
                    <arc:Button x:Name="RestoreButton"
                                Variant="Secondary"
                                Size="Small"
                                Content="Show the banner again"
                                HorizontalAlignment="Center"
                                VerticalAlignment="Center" />
                </Border>
            </Panel>
        </Border>
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using TKCode.Arc.Motion;
using Avalonia;
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;
using Avalonia.Threading;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class CtaSectionPreviewDemo : UserControl
{
    private static readonly SpringSpec s_smooth = SpringSpec.FromVisual(0.4, 0);

    private readonly MotionValue<double> _height;
    private readonly MotionValue<double> _fade;
    private DateTime _armedUntil = DateTime.MinValue;
    private bool _measured;
    private bool _changed;

    public CtaSectionPreviewDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        // Centered's faces and the setup card's teammates are drawn in code (CtaSectionDemoData), never photographs.
        foreach (var face in CtaSectionDemoData.CreateFaces())
        {
            Section.Faces.Add(face);
        }
        foreach (var face in CtaSectionDemoData.CreateSetupFaces())
        {
            Section.SetupFaces.Add(face);
        }
        // The frame's height is a measured value that springs after a layout switch, so it is driven here (Arc's useFrameHeight).
        _height = new MotionValue<double>(this, 0, MotionVectors.Double);
        _height.Changed += value => Frame.Height = value;
        _fade = new MotionValue<double>(this, 1, MotionVectors.Double);
        _fade.Changed += value => Body.Opacity = Math.Clamp(value, 0, 1);
        Layouts.SelectionChanged += OnLayoutChanged;
        Section.Dismissed += OnDismissed;
        RestoreButton.Click += OnRestore;
        Body.GetObservable(BoundsProperty).Subscribe(new BoundsObserver(this));
    }

    private sealed class BoundsObserver(CtaSectionPreviewDemo owner) : IObserver<Rect>
    {
        public void OnCompleted()
        {
        }

        public void OnError(Exception error)
        {
        }

        public void OnNext(Rect value) => owner.OnContentResized(value.Height);
    }

    private bool IsFull => ArcMotion.IsFull(this);

    /// <summary>A discrete change (a new layout, the restore button) arms the spring for 700 ms; every other resize follows at once.</summary>
    private void Arm() => _armedUntil = DateTime.UtcNow.AddMilliseconds(700);

    private void OnContentResized(double next)
    {
        if (next <= 0)
        {
            return;
        }
        if (!_measured || !IsFull || DateTime.UtcNow > _armedUntil)
        {
            _measured = true;
            _height.Jump(next + 2);
            Frame.Height = next + 2;
            return;
        }
        _ = _height.AnimateTo(next + 2, MotionSpec.Spring(s_smooth));
    }

    private void SwapView(Action change)
    {
        Arm();
        change();
        // The first layout appears as it is; later ones fade in while the frame springs to their height.
        if (_changed && IsFull)
        {
            _fade.Jump(0);
            _ = _fade.AnimateTo(1, MotionSpec.Tween(ArcMotionPresets.Standard, ArcEasings.Standard));
        }
        _changed = true;
    }

    private void OnLayoutChanged(object? sender, SelectionChangedEventArgs e)
    {
        SwapView(() =>
        {
            Section.Variant = Layouts.SelectedValue switch
            {
                "split" => CtaVariant.Split,
                "banner" => CtaVariant.Banner,
                _ => CtaVariant.Centered
            };
            Section.Show();
            Section.IsVisible = true;
            Restore.IsVisible = false;
        });
    }

    private void OnDismissed(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        SwapView(() =>
        {
            Section.IsVisible = false;
            Restore.IsVisible = true;
        });
    }

    private void OnRestore(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        SwapView(() =>
        {
            Restore.IsVisible = false;
            Section.Show();
            Section.IsVisible = true;
        });
    }
}
```

## When to use

A call to action asks one thing of the reader: start a trial, book a demo, sign up. `CtaSection` gives that request
three shapes, so the same control can close a landing page, sit beside a product visual in the middle of one, or run
across the top of an app. With nothing set it shows Arc's copy for the shape you choose.

- **The last section of a landing page**: the `Centered` shape, a quiet card with a headline, one sentence, two
  actions and a line of small print with the faces of people who already joined.
- **An in-page prompt beside a product visual**: the `Split` shape puts the copy and short benefit lines on the left
  and a setup card on the right. The card ticks through its steps once it is in view, so the reader sees the outcome the
  button leads to.
- **A slim promotional banner above content**: the `Banner` shape is one line with one action and an optional dismiss
  button. Dismissing closes its gap, so the page below moves up smoothly.

## When not to use

- **The first screen of a page**: use a hero. A call to action closes or interrupts a story; it does not open one.
- **Collecting an email address**: use a newsletter signup block, which validates, sends and confirms in place.
- **A persistent site-wide notice**: use an announcement bar. The banner here is one message with one action, closed by
  the reader, not a rotating or counting notice.
- **A decision with consequences**: use a dialog or an alert dialog. A call to action invites; it does not interrupt.

## Usage

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:CtaSection />
</UserControl>
```

`CtaSection` derives from `TemplatedControl`. `Variant` picks the shape; every text, action, list and picture is a
property, and every one has Arc's English text as its default except the pictures, which are empty until you add
images. The block is a layout, so the action rules, the data and the destinations stay in your app.

### Shapes

| `Variant` | What it shows | Actions |
|---|---|---|
| `Centered` | Headline, text, actions, and a note with up to four faces on a quiet card | Primary, secondary |
| `Split` | Copy, benefit lines and actions beside a stage; the stage holds the setup card or your own `Visual` | Primary, secondary |
| `Banner` | One line of text, an action and an optional dismiss button | Primary only |

Set `Title`, `Description`, `PrimaryAction` and `SecondaryAction` to replace the text of any shape. Leave a value unset
and the shape shows its own Arc copy, so switching `Variant` from `Centered` to `Split` changes the words too.

### Actions

Each action is a `CtaAction` with a `Label`, an optional `Href`, a `ConfirmedLabel`, a `Command` and a
`CommandParameter`. What happens on a press depends on what you gave it.

| The action has | A press does |
|---|---|
| An `Href` | Raises `ActionInvoked`, runs the command if there is one, then opens the address unless a handler marked the event handled. Only absolute http, https and mailto addresses are opened |
| A `Command`, or a handler marks `ActionInvoked` handled | Only runs. Nothing else changes on screen |
| None of these | Confirms in place: a check and `ConfirmedLabel` (or `Label`) replace the text, a second press restores it, and the change is announced politely |

The in-place confirmation is what makes a preview answer every press. In an app, give each action a command, a
destination or a handler.

```xml
<arc:CtaSection Variant="Split">
    <arc:CtaSection.PrimaryAction>
        <arc:CtaAction Label="Create a workspace" Command="{Binding CreateWorkspace}" />
    </arc:CtaSection.PrimaryAction>
    <arc:CtaSection.SecondaryAction>
        <arc:CtaAction Label="Book a demo" Href="https://example.com/demo" />
    </arc:CtaSection.SecondaryAction>
</arc:CtaSection>
```

```csharp
section.ActionInvoked += (_, e) =>
{
    if (e.IsPrimary)
    {
        analytics.Track("cta_primary", e.Action.Label);
    }
};
```

`CtaActionEventArgs` carries the `Action` that was pressed, `IsPrimary`, and `IsConfirmed`: true when the press puts a
plain action into its confirmed state. Mark the event `Handled` to take over a plain action completely.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.CtaSectionLinksDemo">
    <!-- Actions with an Href are link-style: the press raises ActionInvoked, then opens the address unless a handler marks it handled. -->
    <StackPanel Spacing="12">
        <arc:CtaSection x:Name="Section"
                        Title="Read the guide, then start"
                        Description="The guide opens in your browser; the second action is handled in code and only writes to the log."
                        Note="Opens uiarc.dev in your browser"
                        ActionInvoked="OnActionInvoked">
            <arc:CtaSection.PrimaryAction>
                <arc:CtaAction Label="Open the guide" Href="https://uiarc.dev/docs" />
            </arc:CtaSection.PrimaryAction>
            <arc:CtaSection.SecondaryAction>
                <arc:CtaAction Label="Email us" Href="mailto:hello@example.com" />
            </arc:CtaSection.SecondaryAction>
        </arc:CtaSection>
        <TextBlock x:Name="Log"
                   Text="No action pressed yet."
                   HorizontalAlignment="Center"
                   FontSize="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TypeSM}"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class CtaSectionLinksDemo : UserControl
{
    public CtaSectionLinksDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
    }

    // The mail link is handled here, so the block does not open it; the web link is not, so the launcher opens it.
    private void OnActionInvoked(object? sender, CtaActionEventArgs e)
    {
        var kind = e.IsPrimary ? "Primary" : "Secondary";
        var handled = false;
        if (!e.IsPrimary)
        {
            e.Handled = true;
            handled = true;
        }
        Log.Text = $"{kind} “{e.Action.Label}” pressed" + (handled ? " (handled in code, nothing opened)." : " (the launcher opens the page).");
    }
}
```

Primary actions end in an arrow that leans 3 px forward under a mouse or a pen. Touch does not trigger the lean.
Actions are large buttons in the centered and split shapes and small buttons in the banner.

### Centered

The `Centered` shape sets its note under the actions. `Note` defaults to "No credit card required"; set it to an empty
string to hide the text. Add images to `Faces` and up to four overlapping faces appear beside the note; the row hides
when it has neither.

```csharp
section.Note = "Join 4,000 teams";
section.Faces.Add(new Bitmap("avatar-1.png"));
section.Faces.Add(new Bitmap("avatar-2.png"));
```

The faces are decoration for screen readers, so describe what the section offers in `Title` and `Description`.

### Split and the setup card

The `Split` shape lists benefit lines in `Points` (null shows Arc's three; an empty list hides the list) and puts a
stage on the right. By default the stage holds a setup card that completes itself:

1. The stage rises into view once, when 35% of it is visible.
2. When half of the card is visible, three timers start. Step *i* finishes 520 + 620 × *i* ms later (about 0.5, 1.1 and
   1.8 seconds in).
3. As each step finishes its mark fills with a check that springs in, the progress line grows, and the next step takes
   the muted fill. The status at the top changes from "Setting up" to "Ready".
4. The last row shows `SetupFaces`, which slide in one after another once that step is current.

Configure the card with `SetupWorkspace` (its first letter is the mark), `SetupSteps` (null shows Arc's three) and
`SetupFaces`. The card is purely a picture of the outcome. It is hidden from screen readers, and the copy beside it
carries the message.

To show your own screenshot or control, set `Visual`. The stage keeps its size, border and entrance; the setup card and its
timers are not used.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             xmlns:collections="using:Avalonia.Collections"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.CtaSectionCustomVisualDemo">
    <!-- Visual replaces the setup card; Points and the actions are set as well. Any control or content works. -->
    <arc:CtaSection Variant="Split"
                    Title="See every release at a glance"
                    Description="Replace the setup card with your own product visual, and keep the copy, points and actions.">
        <arc:CtaSection.PrimaryAction>
            <arc:CtaAction Label="Open the dashboard" ConfirmedLabel="Dashboard opened" />
        </arc:CtaSection.PrimaryAction>
        <arc:CtaSection.SecondaryAction>
            <arc:CtaAction Label="Read the changelog" ConfirmedLabel="Opened" />
        </arc:CtaSection.SecondaryAction>
        <arc:CtaSection.Visual>
            <Border Width="320"
                    Padding="20"
                    CornerRadius="26"
                    BorderThickness="1"
                    BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Border}"
                    Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource SurfaceRaised}"
                    BoxShadow="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource ShadowRaised}">
                <StackPanel Spacing="12">
                    <TextBlock Text="Release 4.2"
                               FontSize="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TypeLG}"
                               FontWeight="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource WeightMedium}" />
                    <TextBlock Text="12 changes shipped this week"
                               FontSize="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TypeSM}"
                               Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
                    <Border Height="6" CornerRadius="3" Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Border}">
                        <Border Width="210" HorizontalAlignment="Left" CornerRadius="3" Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Success}" />
                    </Border>
                    <TextBlock Text="70% of checks passed"
                               FontSize="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TypeXS}"
                               Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
                </StackPanel>
            </Border>
        </arc:CtaSection.Visual>
        <arc:CtaSection.Points>
            <collections:AvaloniaList x:TypeArguments="x:String">
                <x:String>Release notes written as you merge</x:String>
                <x:String>One view for every environment</x:String>
            </collections:AvaloniaList>
        </arc:CtaSection.Points>
    </arc:CtaSection>
</UserControl>
```

```xml
<arc:CtaSection Variant="Split">
    <arc:CtaSection.Visual>
        <Border Width="320" Height="200" CornerRadius="26" Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource SurfaceRaised}" />
    </arc:CtaSection.Visual>
</arc:CtaSection>
```

### Banner

The `Banner` shape is one rounded line. Set `IsDismissible` to show the dismiss button. Pressing it, or calling
`Dismiss()`, closes the banner: it fades out in 160 ms while its height springs to zero, and then `IsOpen` becomes false
and `Dismissed` is raised. `Show()` brings it back at once.

```xml
<arc:CtaSection Variant="Banner"
                IsDismissible="True"
                IsOpen="{Binding ShowPromo, Mode=TwoWay}" />
```

`IsOpen` is two way. Setting it to false from your own code plays the same exit and does not raise `Dismissed`. Remember
the choice yourself (a setting, a cookie equivalent) if the banner should stay closed after the next launch. Set
`DismissLabel` to name the button in another language.

### Responsive layout

The block follows its own width, not the window's. At 860 px or less the split becomes one column with the stage
below the copy. At 560 px or less the paddings tighten, the cards round to 28 px, the actions stack at full width and
the banner puts its text above its actions, with the dismiss button at the right edge. The headline grows with the
block, from 30 px up to 52 px.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.CtaSectionNarrowDemo">
    <!-- 360 wide: the block follows its own width, so the paddings tighten, the actions stack at full width and the split is one column. -->
    <StackPanel Spacing="16" HorizontalAlignment="Center">
        <arc:CtaSection Width="360" Variant="Centered" />
        <arc:CtaSection Width="360" Variant="Split" />
        <arc:CtaSection Width="360" Variant="Banner" IsDismissible="True" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

### Content guidelines

- **Headline**: a promise in a few words, such as "Start building in minutes". Centered headlines wrap at about 18
  characters and balance their lines.
- **Action labels**: a verb and at most two other words ("Create a workspace", "Book a demo"). The primary action is
  the one thing you want the reader to do next.
- **Confirmed labels**: say what happened ("Workspace created"), not "Done".
- **Benefit lines**: three or fewer, each one short enough to fit in one line of the left column.

### Best practices

**Do**

- Give the primary action a real destination or command, and keep a single primary action per section.
- Use `Centered` at the end of a page, `Split` in the middle beside a relevant state, and `Banner` at the top of an app
  or documentation page.
- Keep `IsDismissible` on for banners that are not essential, and keep the choice of a reader who dismissed one.

**Avoid**

- Two primary actions. The secondary action is quieter on purpose.
- Long headlines. The title is limited by width and balanced, so a long sentence becomes a tall block.
- Relying on the in-place confirmation in production. It exists to answer presses in previews.

## API reference

### CtaSection

A call to action in three shapes: a centered closing section, a split layout beside a setup card that completes itself once it is in view, and a compact banner that closes its gap when dismissed. With no properties set it shows Arc's copy for the chosen `Variant`. Actions (`PrimaryAction`, `SecondaryAction`) are links, run a command, raise `ActionInvoked`, or, with none of these, confirm in place so a preview always answers a press. The banner closes with `Dismiss` or its dismiss button and then raises `Dismissed`.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Variant` | `CtaVariant` | `Centered` | The shape: Centered (default), Split or Banner. |
| `Title` | `string?` | `null` | The headline; null shows the variant's Arc headline. |
| `Description` | `string?` | `null` | The supporting text; null shows the variant's Arc text. |
| `PrimaryAction` | `CtaAction?` | `null` | The main action; null shows the variant's Arc action. |
| `SecondaryAction` | `CtaAction?` | `null` | The second action (Centered and Split); null shows the variant's Arc action. The banner never shows one. |
| `IsSecondaryActionVisible` | `bool` | `true` | False hides the second action (Arc: `secondaryAction = null`). |
| `Note` | `string?` | `null` | Small print under the actions of the Centered shape; null shows "No credit card required", empty hides it. |
| `Faces` | `AvaloniaList<IImage>` | – | *Read-only.* The faces beside the note in the Centered shape (at most four are shown). |
| `Points` | `AvaloniaList<string>?` | `null` | The short benefit lines of the Split shape; null shows Arc's three, an empty list hides them. |
| `Visual` | `object?` | `null` | Replaces the Split shape's setup card (any control or content); null shows the setup card. |
| `SetupWorkspace` | `string` | `"Northwind"` | The workspace shown on the setup card; its first letter is the mark. |
| `SetupSteps` | `AvaloniaList<string>?` | `null` | The setup card's steps; null shows Arc's three. |
| `SetupFaces` | `AvaloniaList<IImage>` | – | *Read-only.* The teammates' faces that slide in on the setup card's last step. |
| `IsDismissible` | `bool` | `false` | Shows the banner's dismiss button (Arc: passing `onDismiss`). |
| `IsOpen` | `bool` | `true` | Whether the banner is shown (two way). Dismissing plays the exit motion first and then sets this to false. Setting it to false from outside plays the same exit; setting it to true brings the banner back at once. |
| `DismissLabel` | `string` | `"Dismiss"` | The dismiss button's accessible name. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ActionInvoked` | `CtaActionEventArgs` | An action was pressed (before it opens its link, runs its command or confirms in place). |
| `Dismissed` | `RoutedEventArgs` | The banner was dismissed and its exit motion finished. |

Pseudo-classes: `:centered`, `:split`, `:banner`, `:stacked`, `:narrow`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

### CtaAction

One action of a `CtaSection` (Arc's `CtaAction`). With `Href` it is a link-style action: pressing it raises `ActionInvoked` and, when nobody handles the event, opens an absolute http, https or mailto address. With a `Command`, or when a handler marks the event handled, it only runs. With none of these it confirms in place (a check and `ConfirmedLabel`; pressing again restores it), so a preview always answers a press.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Label` | `string?` | `null` | The button text. |
| `Href` | `string?` | `null` | The destination: makes the action a link. |
| `ConfirmedLabel` | `string?` | `null` | The text shown after an in-place confirmation (default: `Label`). |
| `Command` | `ICommand?` | `null` | Runs when the action is pressed, after `ActionInvoked`. |
| `CommandParameter` | `object?` | `null` | The parameter passed to `Command`. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### CtaActionEventArgs

Event data of `ActionInvoked`.

Derives from `RoutedEventArgs`: every member of `RoutedEventArgs` works as well.

## Accessibility

- The section is a region named by its headline.
- Every action and the dismiss button have an accessible name. Confirmations are announced politely through a hidden
  live region, and pressing a confirmed action again announces its plain label.
- The faces and the setup card are decoration and are hidden from screen readers.
- The banner closes its gap when dismissed, so the focus order stays clean after it goes.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` | Move through the actions, then the dismiss button in the banner |
| `Enter` / `Space` | Run an action or dismiss the banner |

Keyboard focus shows a 2 px ring around the focused action or dismiss button; pointer focus does not.

## Motion

- Primary actions lean their arrow 3 px forward on hover (160 ms), and a label change crossfades.
- The split's stage rises into view once (opacity and 24 px of travel, 480 ms). In the setup card, the status words
  swap with a short blur, the progress line grows in 480 ms, step marks fill in 240 ms with the check springing in over
  580 ms, and the teammates' faces slide in 60 ms apart.
- Dismissing fades the banner in 160 ms while its height springs closed. Nothing scales.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| The stage appears | Rises in once, 480 ms | Shown at once | Shown at once |
| The setup card runs | Steps tick, the line grows, faces slide in | Every step is finished at once | The timeline runs; each change jumps |
| The banner is dismissed | Fades in 160 ms, height springs to zero | Fades in 120 ms, then is removed | Removed at once |
| The arrow leans | 160 ms | Jumps | Jumps |

## Related

- `Button` for a single action, `SegmentedControl` for the layout switch in the preview.
- A newsletter signup when the action collects an email address.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `CtaSection` | You ask for a trial, a demo or a signup at the end of a page, beside a visual, or in a banner |
| A newsletter signup | The action is an email address |
| `Button` | You need one action and no section around it |

# Newsletter signup

> An email signup framed by a stack of past issues; subscribing drops the next issue, addressed to you, onto the front.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc.Blocks`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc.Blocks --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/blocks/newsletter-signup

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.NewsletterSignupPreviewDemo">
    <!-- Arc's preview: a layout switch, a switch that makes the next send fail, and the block in a rounded frame. -->
    <StackPanel Spacing="16">
        <StackPanel Orientation="Horizontal" HorizontalAlignment="Center" Spacing="24">
            <arc:SegmentedControl x:Name="Layout"
                                  SelectedValue="inline"
                                  SelectionChanged="OnLayoutChanged"
                                  AutomationProperties.Name="Newsletter layout">
                <arc:SegmentedOption Value="inline" Label="Inline" />
                <arc:SegmentedOption Value="card" Label="Card" />
            </arc:SegmentedControl>
            <arc:Switch x:Name="Fail" Content="Fail the next send" VerticalAlignment="Center" />
        </StackPanel>
        <Border BorderThickness="1"
                CornerRadius="20"
                ClipToBounds="True"
                BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Border}"
                Background="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Background}">
            <arc:SpringSizeDecorator Axis="Height" Spring="Smooth" ClipOverflow="0">
                <arc:ArcContentSwap x:Name="Host" Mode="Fade" />
            </arc:SpringSizeDecorator>
        </Border>
        <TextBlock Text="Subscribing is simulated in this preview. Nothing is sent."
                   HorizontalAlignment="Center"
                   FontSize="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TypeXS}"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class NewsletterSignupPreviewDemo : UserControl
{
    public NewsletterSignupPreviewDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Rebuild();
    }

    private void OnLayoutChanged(object? sender, SelectionChangedEventArgs e) => Rebuild();

    // Arc keys the block by its variant, so a switch starts a fresh signup with the other layout.
    private void Rebuild()
    {
        if (Host is null)
        {
            return;
        }
        var card = Layout.SelectedValue as string == "card";
        var signup = new NewsletterSignup
        {
            Variant = card ? NewsletterVariant.Card : NewsletterVariant.Inline,
            Publication = NewsletterSignupDemoData.CreatePublication(),
            SubscribeAsync = SimulateAsync
        };
        signup.ReaderFaces.AddRange(NewsletterSignupDemoData.CreateFaces());
        Host.Content = signup;
    }

    // Fails once after 1100 ms while the switch is on, otherwise succeeds after the same time.
    private async Task SimulateAsync(string email, CancellationToken token)
    {
        await Task.Delay(1100, token);
        if (Fail.IsChecked == true)
        {
            throw new InvalidOperationException("Simulated failure");
        }
    }
}
```

## When to use

Use `NewsletterSignup` to collect newsletter or waitlist addresses where the newsletter itself is the best argument for
signing up. Beside the form it shows a stack of recent issues, so a visitor sees what arrives before giving an address.
When the address is accepted, the next issue, addressed to that visitor, lands on the front of the stack and the reader
count goes up by one.

- **A landing page section** for a design, engineering or product newsletter, with the copy and form on one side and the stack on the other.
- **A self-contained card** in a footer, a settings page or a modal, with the stack in a tray above the form.
- **A waitlist** where the form alone is enough (turn the stack and the readers off).

## When not to use

- **Account creation or login**: use a form with passwords and validation rules of its own.
- **A newsletter without issues to show**: use the footer signup of the site footer block, which is a single line.
- **Several fields** (name, topics, frequency): this block collects one email address.

## Usage

```xml
<arc:NewsletterSignup x:Name="Signup" />
```

```csharp
Signup.SubscribeAsync = async (email, token) =>
{
    await http.PostAsJsonAsync("/subscribe", new { email }, token);   // throw to show the error and keep the address
};
Signup.Subscribed += (_, e) => analytics.Track("newsletter", e.Email);
```

With no configuration the block shows Arc's copy, the publication "Margins" and 12,480 readers, and simulates the send
(1100 ms, always succeeding). Replace `SubscribeAsync` with a call to your mail provider: return to show the success
state, throw to show the failure state. The token is cancelled when the block is reset or removed.

### The subscription

| Phase | What shows |
|---|---|
| `Idle` | The empty field, "Subscribe →" and the privacy note. After a failed send the button reads "Try again →" and the address is kept. |
| `Sending` | The field is read-only and the button shows a ring and "Subscribing". Further presses are ignored. |
| `Done` | The button turns green with a check mark and "Subscribed", the confirmation replaces the note, and the next issue sits on the front of the stack. |

`Phase` and `SubscribedEmail` are read-only properties. `Reset()` (the "Use a different email" button calls it) clears the
address and returns to `Idle`.

### Validation

An empty field and a malformed address each have their own message (`EmptyMessage`, `FormatMessage`). Validation starts
when the field loses focus with text in it; once a submit was tried it follows every keystroke. Before that, typing clears
the error. A failed validation shakes the pill and keeps the focus in the field.

### Variants

`Variant` is `Inline` (the default) or `Card`.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.NewsletterSignupCardDemo">
    <!-- The card variant on its own: the stack in a tray above the copy, the form and the readers. -->
    <arc:NewsletterSignup x:Name="Signup" Variant="Card" Subscribed="OnSubscribed" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class NewsletterSignupCardDemo : UserControl
{
    public NewsletterSignupCardDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Signup.Publication = NewsletterSignupDemoData.CreatePublication();
        Signup.ReaderFaces.AddRange(NewsletterSignupDemoData.CreateFaces());
    }

    private void OnSubscribed(object? sender, NewsletterSubscribedEventArgs e)
    {
        // A real app would store the address here; the demo only simulates the send.
    }
}
```

```xml
<arc:NewsletterSignup Variant="Card" />
```

### The publication

`Publication` holds the name, the `Upcoming` issue and the `Recent` issues (newest first). The first three recent issues
make the stack. Each `NewsletterIssue` has a number (its identity), a date line, a subject and up to three
`NewsletterStory` items with a title, a thumbnail `IImage` and the reading time. Reader faces come from `ReaderFaces`.

```csharp
var publication = new NewsletterPublication { Name = "Margins", Upcoming = next };
publication.Recent.Add(issue148);
publication.Recent.Add(issue147);
signup.Publication = publication;
signup.ReaderFaces.Add(faceBitmap);
```

Without a publication the block uses Arc's sample "Margins", whose stories have no thumbnails. Set
`IsPublicationVisible` or `IsReadersVisible` to false to hide the stack or the readers.

### Form only

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.NewsletterSignupFormOnlyDemo">
    <!-- No stack and no readers: the copy and the form alone, in one column. -->
    <arc:NewsletterSignup IsPublicationVisible="False"
                          IsReadersVisible="False"
                          Title="Product notes, once a month"
                          Description="What shipped, what changed and what is next. No marketing." />
</UserControl>
```

With neither the stack nor the readers the section becomes one centered column of at most 720 px.

### Narrow containers

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.NewsletterSignupNarrowDemo">
    <!-- A 320 wide block: the form is narrower than 300, so the field and the button stack, both full width. -->
    <Border Width="320" HorizontalAlignment="Center">
        <arc:NewsletterSignup x:Name="Signup" IsPublicationVisible="False" />
    </Border>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class NewsletterSignupNarrowDemo : UserControl
{
    public NewsletterSignupNarrowDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Signup.ReaderFaces.AddRange(NewsletterSignupDemoData.CreateFaces());
    }
}
```

The block follows its own width, not the window's. At 860 px or less the layout is one column. At 520 it tightens its
spacing and type, at 400 it drops the reading times and shows only the recipient on an addressed issue, and at 360 the
readers line may wrap. A form narrower than 300 px stacks the field and the button, both full width.

### Text and localization

Every string is a property with Arc's English default: `Placeholder`, `ButtonLabel`, `PrivacyNote`, `PrivacyLinkLabel`,
`EmailLabel`, `RetryLabel`, `SendingLabel`, `DoneLabel`, `EmptyMessage`, `FormatMessage`, `FailedMessage`, `DoneMessage`,
`DifferentEmailLabel`, `RecipientFormat`, `IssueFormat`, `MinutesFormat`, `ReadersWord`, `IncludingYou` and
`SentToFormat`.

### The privacy link

Pressing it raises `Navigate` (and runs `NavigateCommand`). When the event is not handled and `PrivacyLinkHref` is an
absolute `http`, `https` or `mailto` address, it is opened with the platform launcher. Set `IsPrivacyLinkVisible` to false
to hide it.

## API reference

### NewsletterSignup

A newsletter signup framed by the newsletter itself: a stack of recent issues. Subscribing drops the next issue, addressed to the new reader, onto the front of the stack, drops the oldest one away and ticks the reader count up by one. It comes as an `Inline` page section (copy and form beside the stack) or a self-contained `Card` (the stack in a tray on top).

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Variant` | `NewsletterVariant` | `Inline` | `Inline` (the default) or `Card`. |
| `Title` | `string?` | `null` | The heading. Null uses Arc's copy for the variant. |
| `Description` | `string?` | `null` | The line under the heading. Null uses Arc's copy for the variant. |
| `Placeholder` | `string` | `"you@company.com"` | The placeholder of the email field ("you@company.com"). |
| `ButtonLabel` | `string` | `"Subscribe"` | The label of the button in its idle state ("Subscribe"). |
| `PrivacyNote` | `string` | `"No tracking pixels. Unsubscribe with one click."` | The short line under the form about frequency and privacy. |
| `PrivacyLinkLabel` | `string` | `"Privacy policy"` | The label of the link after the privacy note ("Privacy policy"). |
| `PrivacyLinkHref` | `string?` | `"#privacy"` | Where the privacy link goes ("#privacy"). Pressing it raises `Navigate`; when nobody handles the event and the value is an absolute http, https or mailto address, it is opened with the platform launcher. |
| `IsPrivacyLinkVisible` | `bool` | `true` | Whether the privacy link shows after the note (true). |
| `NavigateCommand` | `ICommand?` | `null` | Runs when the privacy link is pressed, after `Navigate`; its parameter is the destination. |
| `ReaderCount` | `int` | `12480` | The number of readers (12480). Subscribing shows one more. |
| `IsReadersVisible` | `bool` | `true` | Whether the readers row (faces and count) shows (true). |
| `Publication` | `NewsletterPublication?` | `null` | The publication behind the stack. Null shows Arc's sample publication "Margins" (without thumbnails). |
| `IsPublicationVisible` | `bool` | `true` | Whether the stack of issues shows (true). Set false for the form alone. |
| `ReaderFaces` | `AvaloniaList<IImage>` | – | *Read-only.* The faces next to the reader count (the first three are shown). |
| `Phase` | `NewsletterPhase` | – | *Read-only.* Where the subscription stands: Idle, Sending or Done (read only). |
| `SubscribedEmail` | `string?` | – | *Read-only.* The address that was subscribed, or null before that (read only). |
| `SubscribedCommand` | `ICommand?` | `null` | Runs when a subscription succeeds; its parameter is the address. |
| `EmailLabel` | `string` | `"Email address"` | The hidden label of the email field ("Email address"). |
| `RetryLabel` | `string` | `"Try again"` | The button label after a failed send ("Try again"). |
| `SendingLabel` | `string` | `"Subscribing"` | The button label while sending ("Subscribing"). |
| `DoneLabel` | `string` | `"Subscribed"` | The button label once subscribed ("Subscribed"). |
| `EmptyMessage` | `string` | `"Enter your email address"` | The message for an empty field ("Enter your email address"). |
| `FormatMessage` | `string` | `"Enter an email like name@company.com"` | The message for a malformed address ("Enter an email like name@company.com"). |
| `FailedMessage` | `string` | `"That didn't go through. Your email is kept, so try again."` | The message after a failed send. |
| `DoneMessage` | `string` | `"Check your inbox to confirm."` | The confirmation after a successful send ("Check your inbox to confirm."). |
| `DifferentEmailLabel` | `string` | `"Use a different email"` | The label of the button that starts over ("Use a different email"). |
| `RecipientFormat` | `string` | `"To {0}"` | The recipient line of an addressed issue; {0} is the address ("To {0}"). |
| `IssueFormat` | `string` | `"Issue {0}"` | The issue number at the top of an issue; {0} is the number ("Issue {0}"). |
| `MinutesFormat` | `string` | `"{0} min"` | The reading time of a story; {0} is the minutes ("{0} min"). |
| `IssueNameFormat` | `string` | `"{0}, issue {1}"` | The screen reader name of the front issue; {0} is the publication, {1} the number ("{0}, issue {1}"). |
| `ReadersWord` | `string` | `"readers"` | The word after the reader count ("readers"). |
| `IncludingYou` | `string` | `", including you"` | The phrase that opens after the count once subscribed (", including you"). |
| `SentToFormat` | `string` | `" The link went to {0}."` | What the screen reader adds to the confirmation; {0} is the address (" The link went to {0}."). |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Subscribed` | `NewsletterSubscribedEventArgs` | A subscription succeeded: the next issue now sits on the front of the stack. |
| `Navigate` | `NewsletterNavigateEventArgs` | The privacy link was pressed. Mark the event handled to stop the default (opening an absolute address). |

Pseudo-classes: `:card`, `:compact`, `:narrow`, `:tiny`, `:micro`, `:no-aside`, `:no-publication`, `:no-readers`, `:sending`, `:done`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

### NewsletterPublication

The publication shown beside the form: its name, the next issue and the recent ones. When someone subscribes the `Upcoming` issue, addressed to the new reader, lands on the front of the stack and the oldest issue drops away.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Name` | `string?` | `null` | The publication name, the masthead of every issue. |
| `Upcoming` | `NewsletterIssue?` | `null` | The next issue. It joins the front of the stack once a reader has subscribed. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### NewsletterIssue

One issue of the newsletter as it appears on the stack. The first three `Stories` are shown.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Number` | `int` | `0` | The issue number. It is the identity of the issue on the stack, so give every issue its own. |
| `Date` | `string?` | `null` | The send date as it should read, such as "Friday, September 25". |
| `Subject` | `string?` | `null` | The subject line, shown large under the masthead. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### NewsletterStory

One story teased in an issue: a title, a small square thumbnail and a reading time.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Title` | `string?` | `null` | The story title (at most two lines are shown). |
| `Image` | `IImage?` | `null` | The thumbnail, drawn as a 44 px rounded square (the longer side is cropped). Null leaves the muted tile. |
| `Minutes` | `int` | `0` | The reading time in minutes, shown as "5 min" (see `MinutesFormat`). |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### NewsletterSubscribedEventArgs

Arguments of `Subscribed`.

Derives from `RoutedEventArgs`: every member of `RoutedEventArgs` works as well.

### NewsletterNavigateEventArgs

Arguments of `Navigate`.

Derives from `RoutedEventArgs`: every member of `RoutedEventArgs` works as well.

## Accessibility

- The block is a region named by its title. The field has the hidden label `EmailLabel` and the email input hint.
- Errors are announced assertively; the confirmation is announced politely and includes where the link went.
- Only the front issue is exposed to screen readers ("Margins, issue 148"). The issues behind it, the thumbnails and the faces are decorative.
- Keyboard focus rings are 2 px outside the button and the links. Hover styles apply to a mouse or a pen only.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` | Move between the field, the button and the link. A subscribed button leaves the tab order. |
| `Enter` in the field | Check and send the address (ignored while an input method is composing). |
| `Enter` / `Space` on a button | Press it. |

After a successful send the focus moves to "Use a different email"; after `Reset()` it returns to the field.

## Motion

- Subscribing places the next issue on the front: it rises from below onto the stack while the others step back and shrink (a no-overshoot spring), and the oldest issue drops away behind.
- The label of the button and the message line swap in place with a short blur; the check mark draws itself.
- A rejected address or a failed send shakes the pill. The reader count rolls up by one and ", including you" opens its width.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| Issues trade places | Spring on position and scale, opacity in 120 ms | Placed at once, opacity in 160 ms | Immediate |
| Label and message swap | Lift and blur, 240 ms in, 160 ms out | Fade, 120 ms | Immediate |
| Shake | 360 ms | None | None |
| Check mark | Draws in 340 ms | Drawn | Drawn |

### Responsive behavior

Breakpoints use the width of the block: 860, 520, 400 and 360 px, plus 300 px for the form itself.

## Related

- The site footer block for a one-line newsletter field inside a footer.
- The CTA section block for a call to action that leads to a signup page.
- `EmptyStates` for an empty view with a retryable action.

# Activity terrain

> A week of hourly activity as a 3D terrain: orbit and zoom it, hover an hour for its numbers, fly to a bar, press it flat into a heat map, and read the total, the peak hours and the busiest day beside it.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc.Blocks`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc.Blocks --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/blocks/activity-terrain

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ActivityTerrainPreviewDemo">
    <!-- Three metrics of an invented week; the data is generated in the code-behind. -->
    <arc:ActivityTerrain x:Name="Terrain"
                         Title="Weekly rhythm"
                         Subtitle="Hourly visits, builds and incidents for Mar 2 to 8, 2026, server time." />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class ActivityTerrainPreviewDemo : UserControl
{
    public ActivityTerrainPreviewDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Terrain.Metrics.AddRange(ActivityTerrainDemoData.Metrics());
    }
}
```

## When to use

`ActivityTerrain` shows one week of hourly numbers, Monday 00:00 to Sunday 23:59, as 168 bars standing on a floor: seven
rows of days, twenty-four columns of hours. A bar is as tall and as dark as its hour was busy, so the rhythm of the week reads
at a glance: the morning ramp, the lunch dip, the quiet weekend. Hovering a bar lifts it and shows its value, the same hour a
week earlier and the shape of that day; clicking it flies the camera there. Beside the plot, a summary gives the week's total
and its change, the busiest hours and the busiest day.

- **Product analytics.** Visits, sign-ups or searches per hour, to see when people actually use the product and when a
  release or a maintenance window would hurt least.
- **Engineering activity.** Builds, deploys or merged changes per hour, to show when the team ships and whether Friday
  afternoons stay quiet.
- **Operations and on-call.** Alerts or incidents per hour in the danger tone, where one bad afternoon stands out as a single
  red spike and a rise on last week reads as bad news.
- **Support and sales desks.** Chats, tickets or calls per hour, to plan staffing around the peaks the summary lists.
- **A showcase on a dashboard's front page**, where the motion (the intro, the wave on a metric switch, the fly-in) invites
  people to explore a week they would otherwise skim in a table.

## When not to use

- **For more or fewer than seven days by twenty-four hours.** The shape is fixed; use `ActivityHeatmap` for a year of days,
  or a line or bar chart for other periods.
- **When exact comparison matters more than the overall shape.** Perspective makes far bars look smaller; the heat map view
  helps, but a table or a bar chart compares values more precisely.
- **On a page with many charts.** The terrain is large and animated; one per page is plenty. Use a sparkline or a
  `MetricCard` for small multiples.
- **For data that is not a count or an amount per hour** (ratios, averages that can be negative): bar heights start at zero
  and grow with the value.

## Usage

### Anatomy

From top to bottom: an optional title and subtitle; a toolbar with the metric switch (shown when there are two metrics or
more) and the view switch (terrain or heat map); the plot, with the hover card and a "Reset view" button that appears once the
camera has moved; a legend from less to more with a hint about the gestures; and the summary with three blocks, the week's
total and its change, the peak hours and the busiest day. The plot's height is 44% of the block's width, between 280 and 460.

### Metrics

Each `ActivityTerrainMetric` is one measure: 168 values in `Values`, Monday 00:00 first, then hour by hour and day by day
(`day × 24 + hour`). `PreviousValues` holds the week before in the same order; without it the change and the "Previous week"
row are hidden. `Label` names the metric on the switch, `Unit` follows values in the card and the summary, and `Key` lets you
select it with `SelectedMetricKey`.

```csharp
var visits = new ActivityTerrainMetric
{
    Key = "visits",
    Label = "Visits",
    Unit = "visits",
    Values = thisWeek,            // 168 numbers: Monday 00:00, Monday 01:00, … Sunday 23:00
    PreviousValues = lastWeek     // optional
};
terrain.Metrics.Add(visits);
```

Data held as a 7 × 24 grid converts with `ActivityTerrainMetric.Flatten(grid)` (rows are days from Monday, columns hours).
Missing entries count as zero. The terrain works out everything else: the total, the change on the previous week, the peak
hours (largest first, ties by day and hour), the day totals, the busiest day and the share of the week that fell in working
hours.

### Tone and good news

`Tone` colors the bars, the legend and the current hour in the card: `Accent` (the default), `Neutral`, `Success`, `Warning`
or `Danger`. `HigherIsBetter` decides whether a rise shows green or red; set it to false for errors, incidents or wait times.
A metric in the danger tone with one bad afternoon:

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ActivityTerrainIncidentsDemo">
    <!--
        One metric (no metric switch) in the danger tone: a rise is bad news, so the change turns red. Working hours are
        08:00 to 18:59 here, and the summary lists the five worst hours.
    -->
    <arc:ActivityTerrain x:Name="Terrain"
                         PeakCount="5"
                         Title="Incident load"
                         Subtitle="Alerts that paged someone, per hour.">
        <arc:ActivityTerrain.WorkingHours>
            <arc:ActivityTerrainWorkingHours FirstHour="8" LastHour="18" />
        </arc:ActivityTerrain.WorkingHours>
    </arc:ActivityTerrain>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class ActivityTerrainIncidentsDemo : UserControl
{
    public ActivityTerrainIncidentsDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        var incidents = ActivityTerrainDemoData.Metrics()[2];
        incidents.SummaryTitle = "Pages this week";
        incidents.Unit = "pages";
        Terrain.Metrics.Add(incidents);
    }
}
```

```xml
<arc:ActivityTerrain PeakCount="5"
                     Title="Incident load"
                     Subtitle="Alerts that paged someone, per hour.">
    <arc:ActivityTerrainMetric Key="incidents" Label="Incidents" Unit="incidents" Tone="Danger" HigherIsBetter="False" />
</arc:ActivityTerrain>
```

### Terrain and heat map

`ViewMode` switches between the terrain (`Perspective`) and a flat heat map seen from above (`Top`). In the heat map the bars
press flat into squares, every day is labeled, and dragging no longer turns the view; hovering, clicking and zooming still
work. The view switch in the toolbar sets the same property, and `ViewModeChanged` reports the change.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ActivityTerrainHeatMapDemo">
    <!-- Starts flat, seen from above: every hour a square, darker when busier. The switch brings the bars back up. -->
    <arc:ActivityTerrain x:Name="Terrain"
                         ViewMode="Top"
                         SelectedMetricKey="builds"
                         Title="Build activity"
                         Subtitle="When the team ships, Mar 2 to 8, 2026." />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class ActivityTerrainHeatMapDemo : UserControl
{
    public ActivityTerrainHeatMapDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Terrain.Metrics.AddRange(ActivityTerrainDemoData.Metrics());
    }
}
```

### Hovering and flying in

Hovering a bar, or moving to it with the arrow keys, highlights its hour: the bar lifts, a band runs along its row and column
to the axis labels, the rest of the week fades back, and the card shows the day, the hour, the value, the previous week, the
change and the hour's share of its day, with the day's 24 hours as small bars. `HighlightedCell` holds that hour and
`CellHovered` reports it.

Clicking a bar flies the camera to it (zoom 1.5 at least) and keeps it lifted; clicking empty floor or pressing Escape
returns to the whole week. `FocusedCell` holds the hour, `CellFocused` reports it, and `FlyTo`, `ShowWeek`, `FlyToCommand`
do the same from code. The peak hour buttons in the summary fly to their hour and back.

```csharp
terrain.CellFocused += (_, e) =>
{
    if (e.Cell is { } cell)
    {
        ShowDetails(cell.Day, cell.Hour, e.Value);
    }
};
terrain.FlyTo(new ActivityTerrainCell(Day: 2, Hour: 14));   // Wednesday 14:00
```

### Orbiting and zooming

Drag to turn the view (yaw has no limit, tilt stays between 10° and 84° and springs back after an overdrag), release to let
it glide. Ctrl or ⌘ with the wheel, or a pinch, zooms between 0.7 and 2.8; the plain wheel scrolls the page. `Yaw`, `Pitch`
and `Zoom` report the camera, `IsViewDefault` turns false once it moved, and the "Reset view" button (or `ResetView`,
`ResetViewCommand`) brings it back and raises `ViewReset`.

### Narrow layouts

The layout follows the block's own width. Below 560 the switches stack, the plot is 280 high and turned a little further
(50°), the hour labels shorten to "09", and the summary takes two columns. From 880 the summary moves into a column beside the
plot.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ActivityTerrainNarrowDemo">
    <!--
        Below 560 the switches stack, the plot is 280 high and turned to 50°, hours read "09" instead of "09:00", and the
        summary takes two columns.
    -->
    <arc:ActivityTerrain x:Name="Terrain"
                         Width="380"
                         HorizontalAlignment="Center"
                         Title="Weekly rhythm"
                         Subtitle="Hourly visits, builds and incidents for Mar 2 to 8, 2026." />
</UserControl>
```

