### Your own data and live updates

Replace `Values` (and `PreviousValues`) whenever new numbers arrive: the bars rise to them in the same wave as a metric switch,
and the summary's numbers roll. Day names come from `DayNames` and `DayAbbreviations`, and `WorkingHours` defines the hours
counted as working time.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ActivityTerrainLiveDataDemo">
    <!--
        Your own numbers: a support desk's chats and tickets with German day names. "Next week" replaces the values and
        the bars rise to them in a wave; the line under the block follows the highlighted and focused hours.
    -->
    <StackPanel Spacing="12">
        <StackPanel Orientation="Horizontal" Spacing="8">
            <arc:Button x:Name="NextWeek" Content="Next week" Variant="Secondary" Size="Small" />
            <arc:Button x:Name="FlyBusiest" Content="Busiest hour" Variant="Ghost" Size="Small" />
        </StackPanel>
        <arc:ActivityTerrain x:Name="Terrain"
                             Title="Support desk"
                             Subtitle="Chats and tickets opened per hour, Berlin time." />
        <TextBlock x:Name="Status" Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class ActivityTerrainLiveDataDemo : UserControl
{
    private uint _week = 1;

    public ActivityTerrainLiveDataDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Terrain.DayNames = ["Montag", "Dienstag", "Mittwoch", "Donnerstag", "Freitag", "Samstag", "Sonntag"];
        Terrain.DayAbbreviations = ["Mo", "Di", "Mi", "Do", "Fr", "Sa", "So"];
        var chats = new ActivityTerrainMetric { Key = "chats", Label = "Chats", Unit = "chats", Tone = ActivityTerrainTone.Accent };
        var tickets = new ActivityTerrainMetric { Key = "tickets", Label = "Tickets", Unit = "tickets", Tone = ActivityTerrainTone.Neutral };
        Terrain.Metrics.Add(chats);
        Terrain.Metrics.Add(tickets);
        LoadWeek(chats, tickets);
        NextWeek.Click += (_, _) =>
        {
            _week++;
            LoadWeek(chats, tickets);
        };
        FlyBusiest.Click += (_, _) =>
        {
            if (Terrain.FocusedCell is null)
            {
                Terrain.FlyTo(BusiestHour(Terrain.SelectedMetric));
            }
            else
            {
                Terrain.ShowWeek();
            }
        };
        Terrain.CellHovered += (_, e) => Status.Text = e.Cell is { } cell
            ? $"Highlighted: {Terrain.DayNames![cell.Day]} {cell.Hour:00}:00, {e.Value:N0}"
            : "Hover a bar or use the arrow keys.";
        Terrain.CellFocused += (_, e) =>
        {
            if (e.Cell is null)
            {
                Status.Text = "Whole week.";
            }
        };
        Status.Text = "Hover a bar or use the arrow keys.";
    }

    private void LoadWeek(ActivityTerrainMetric chats, ActivityTerrainMetric tickets)
    {
        // Your data source goes here: 168 values per metric, Monday 00:00 first.
        var thisWeek = ActivityTerrainDemoData.Visits(1000 + _week);
        var lastWeek = ActivityTerrainDemoData.Visits(1000 + _week - 1);
        chats.Values = thisWeek.Select(v => Math.Round(v / 40)).ToArray();
        chats.PreviousValues = lastWeek.Select(v => Math.Round(v / 40)).ToArray();
        tickets.Values = thisWeek.Select((v, i) => Math.Round(v / 90 + (i % 24 == 9 ? 12 : 0))).ToArray();
        tickets.PreviousValues = lastWeek.Select(v => Math.Round(v / 90)).ToArray();
    }

    private static ActivityTerrainCell BusiestHour(ActivityTerrainMetric? metric)
    {
        var values = metric?.Values ?? [];
        var best = 0;
        for (var i = 1; i < values.Count; i++)
        {
            if (values[i] > values[best])
            {
                best = i;
            }
        }
        return ActivityTerrainCell.FromIndex(best);
    }
}
```

```xml
<arc:ActivityTerrain Title="Support desk"
                     SelectedMetricKey="tickets">
    <arc:ActivityTerrain.WorkingHours>
        <arc:ActivityTerrainWorkingHours FirstDay="0" LastDay="4" FirstHour="8" LastHour="18" />
    </arc:ActivityTerrain.WorkingHours>
    <arc:ActivityTerrainMetric Key="chats" Label="Chats" Unit="chats" />
    <arc:ActivityTerrainMetric Key="tickets" Label="Tickets" Unit="tickets" Tone="Neutral" />
</arc:ActivityTerrain>
```

### Texts

Every visible and announced text is a property with an English default: the legend (`LessText`, `MoreText`), the switches
(`PerspectiveText`, `TopViewText`), `ResetViewText`, the hints (`HintText`, `TouchHintText`, `KeyboardHintText`), the card
(`PreviousWeekText`, `ChangeText`, `ShareFormat`, `HourRangeFormat`), the summary (`SummaryTitleFormat`, `ChangeSuffixText`,
`PeakHoursTitle`, `BusiestDayTitle`, `BusiestDayFormat`) and the announcements. Formats take numbered placeholders; a
metric's own `SummaryTitle` replaces `SummaryTitleFormat` for that metric, and `ValueFormat` (a .NET number format such as
`"N1"`) changes how its values print.

## API reference

### ActivityTerrain

A week of hourly activity as a terrain: 7 × 24 bars standing on a floor in perspective, as tall and as dark as each hour was busy. Drag to orbit, Ctrl/⌘ + wheel or pinch to zoom, hover a bar for its numbers and the day's shape, click it to fly the camera there; switch the metric and the bars rise to the new values in a diagonal wave; switch to the heat map and they press flat. Under the plot, a legend and a summary: the week's total and its change, the peak hours (each flies to its hour) and the busiest day.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SelectedMetric` | `ActivityTerrainMetric?` | `null` | The selected metric (two-way); null shows the first of `Metrics`. |
| `SelectedMetricKey` | `string?` | `null` | The `Key` of the selected metric (two-way). |
| `ViewMode` | `ActivityTerrainViewMode` | `Perspective` | Terrain or heat map (two-way). Default `Perspective`. |
| `Title` | `string?` | `null` | The heading over the block; null hides it. |
| `Subtitle` | `string?` | `null` | The line under the heading (what the data is, which week, which time zone); null hides it. |
| `DayNames` | `IReadOnlyList<string>?` | `null` | Full day names from Monday (card, announcements, table); null uses English. |
| `DayAbbreviations` | `IReadOnlyList<string>?` | `null` | Short day names from Monday (axis labels, peak hours); null uses English ("Mon"). |
| `WorkingHours` | `ActivityTerrainWorkingHours?` | `null` | The hours counted as working hours for the busiest day's share; null means Monday to Friday, 09:00 to 17:59. |
| `PeakCount` | `int` | `3` | How many peak hours the summary lists. Default 3. |
| `HighlightedCell` | `ActivityTerrainCell?` | `null` | The highlighted hour (hover or keyboard; two-way): crosshair, lifted bar, card. Null for none. |
| `FocusedCell` | `ActivityTerrainCell?` | `null` | The hour the camera flew to (two-way); null shows the whole week. Setting it flies the camera. |
| `Yaw` | `double` | – | *Read-only.* The camera's current turn around the week in degrees (32 at rest; 50 in narrow blocks). |
| `Pitch` | `double` | – | *Read-only.* The camera's current angle above the floor in degrees (30 at rest, 10 to 84 when orbiting, 90 in the heat map). |
| `Zoom` | `double` | – | *Read-only.* The camera's current zoom (1 at rest, 0.7 to 2.8). |
| `IsViewDefault` | `bool` | – | *Read-only.* True while the camera is (heading to) its starting view; otherwise "Reset view" shows. |
| `LessText` | `string` | `"Less"` | The low end of the legend. Default "Less". |
| `MoreText` | `string` | `"More"` | The high end of the legend. Default "More". |
| `PerspectiveText` | `string` | `"Terrain"` | The view switch's 3D option. Default "Terrain". |
| `TopViewText` | `string` | `"Heat map"` | The view switch's flat option. Default "Heat map". |
| `MetricSwitchLabel` | `string` | `"Metric"` | Names the metric switch for screen readers. Default "Metric". |
| `ViewSwitchLabel` | `string` | `"View"` | Names the view switch for screen readers. Default "View". |
| `ResetViewText` | `string` | `"Reset view"` | The button that brings the camera back. Default "Reset view". |
| `HintText` | `string` | `"Drag to turn, pinch to zoom, click a bar to look closer."` | The hint under the plot for a mouse or a pen. Default "Drag to turn, pinch to zoom, click a bar to look closer." |
| `TouchHintText` | `string` | `"Swipe sideways to turn, tap a bar to look closer."` | The hint once the plot was touched. Default "Swipe sideways to turn, tap a bar to look closer." |
| `KeyboardHintText` | `string` | `"Arrow keys move between hours and days, Home and End jump to the start and end of the day. Enter looks closer, Escape steps back. Shift with the arrow keys turns the view; plus and minus zoom."` | The keys of the plot, read by screen readers with it. |
| `PreviousWeekText` | `string` | `"Previous week"` | The card's row for the same hour a week earlier. Default "Previous week". |
| `ChangeText` | `string` | `"Change"` | The card's row for the change on the previous week. Default "Change". |
| `ShareFormat` | `string` | `"{0} share"` | The card's row for the hour's share of its day; {0} is the day's short name. Default "{0} share". |
| `HourRangeFormat` | `string` | `"{0}–{1}"` | An hour range; {0} and {1} are the start and the end ("09:00–10:00"). Default "{0}–{1}". |
| `SummaryTitleFormat` | `string` | `"{0} this week"` | The summary's title when the metric has no `SummaryTitle`; {0} is the label. Default "{0} this week". |
| `ChangeSuffixText` | `string` | `"from last week"` | The words after the week's change. Default "from last week". |
| `PeakHoursTitle` | `string` | `"Peak hours"` | The title of the peak hours. Default "Peak hours". |
| `BusiestDayTitle` | `string` | `"Busiest day"` | The title of the busiest day. Default "Busiest day". |
| `BusiestDayFormat` | `string` | `"{0} {1}, {2} during working hours"` | The busiest day's line: {0} is its total, {1} the unit, {2} the week's working-hours share (both numbers roll). Default "{0} {1}, {2} during working hours". |
| `SummaryLabel` | `string` | `"Summary of the week"` | Names the summary for screen readers. Default "Summary of the week". |
| `NoDataText` | `string` | `"No data"` | Shown on the plot when every value is zero. Default "No data". |
| `PeakButtonFormat` | `string` | `"{0} {1}, {2} {3}. Show this hour up close"` | A peak hour button's name for screen readers: {0} the day, {1} the hour, {2} the value, {3} the unit. Default "{0} {1}, {2} {3}. Show this hour up close". |
| `HoverAnnouncementFormat` | `string` | `"{0}, {1}: {2} {3}."` | Announced for a highlighted hour: {0} the day, {1} the hours, {2} the value, {3} the unit. Default "{0}, {1}: {2} {3}.". |
| `ChangeAnnouncementFormat` | `string` | `"{0}, {1}: {2} {3}, {4} on the previous week."` | Announced for a highlighted hour with a previous week: as `HoverAnnouncementFormat` plus {4}, the change. Default "{0}, {1}: {2} {3}, {4} on the previous week.". |
| `FocusAnnouncementFormat` | `string` | `"Looking closer at {0}, {1}."` | Announced when the camera flies to an hour: {0} the day, {1} the hours. Default "Looking closer at {0}, {1}.". |
| `WeekAnnouncementText` | `string` | `"Back to the whole week."` | Announced when the camera returns to the whole week. Default "Back to the whole week.". |
| `ResetAnnouncementText` | `string` | `"View reset."` | Announced after Reset view. Default "View reset.". |
| `TopViewAnnouncementText` | `string` | `"Heat map: color shows how busy each hour was."` | Announced when the heat map shows. Default "Heat map: color shows how busy each hour was.". |
| `PerspectiveAnnouncementText` | `string` | `"Terrain: bar height shows how busy each hour was."` | Announced when the terrain shows again. Default "Terrain: bar height shows how busy each hour was.". |
| `MetricAnnouncementFormat` | `string` | `"Showing {0}: {1} this week, busiest at {2} with {3}."` | Announced on a metric switch: {0} the label, {1} the week's total, {2} the busiest hour, {3} its value. Default "Showing {0}: {1} this week, busiest at {2} with {3}.". |
| `ChartSummaryFormat` | `string` | `"{0} by hour for the week: {1} in total{2}. Busiest hour {3}, busiest day {4}. Every hour is in the table that follows."` | The plot's name for screen readers: {0} the label, {1} the total, {2} the change (or nothing), {3} the busiest hour, {4} the busiest day. Default "{0} by hour for the week: {1} in total{2}. Busiest hour {3}, busiest day {4}. Every hour is in the table that follows.". |
| `TableCaptionFormat` | `string` | `"{0} per hour, Monday to Sunday"` | The caption of the table read by screen readers; {0} is the label. Default "{0} per hour, Monday to Sunday". |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `CellHovered` | `ActivityTerrainCellEventArgs` | Raised when the highlighted hour changes (hover, arrow keys, or null when it clears). |
| `CellFocused` | `ActivityTerrainCellEventArgs` | Raised when the camera flies to an hour, or returns to the whole week (cell null). |
| `ViewModeChanged` | `ActivityTerrainViewModeChangedEventArgs` | Raised when the view switches between the terrain and the heat map. |
| `ViewReset` | `RoutedEventArgs` | Raised when the camera is reset (the "Reset view" button or `ResetView`). |

Pseudo-classes: `:narrow`, `:wide`, `:top-view`, `:change-good`, `:change-bad`, `:no-comparison`, `:empty`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

### ActivityTerrainMetric

One measure an `ActivityTerrain` can show (visits, builds, incidents …): a week of hourly values, the week before for comparison, and how to name, color and judge it. Values run Monday 00:00 first, hour by hour, day by day: 168 numbers (7 × 24); missing entries count as zero.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Key` | `string?` | `null` | Identifies the metric (`SelectedMetricKey`); defaults to the label. |
| `Label` | `string?` | `null` | The name on the metric switch and in the summary ("Visits"). |
| `Unit` | `string?` | `null` | The unit after a value in the card, the busiest day and announcements ("visits"). |
| `Values` | `IReadOnlyList<double>?` | `null` | This week's 168 hourly values, Monday 00:00 first (day × 24 + hour). |
| `PreviousValues` | `IReadOnlyList<double>?` | `null` | The previous week's values in the same order; without them the change and "Last week" rows are hidden. |
| `Tone` | `ActivityTerrainTone` | `Accent` | The color of the bars, the legend and the card's current hour. Default `Accent`. |
| `HigherIsBetter` | `bool` | `true` | Whether a rise is good news (green) or bad news (red, as for errors). Default true. |
| `SummaryTitle` | `string?` | `null` | The title over the week's total; null uses `SummaryTitleFormat` ("Visits this week"). |
| `ValueFormat` | `string?` | `null` | A .NET number format for values ("N0", "N1", "C0" …); null groups whole numbers (12,345). |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

## Accessibility

- The plot is one focusable element. Screen readers hear a one-sentence summary of the week (metric, total, change, busiest
  hour and day) and the keyboard help as its description.
- The week is also available as a table for screen readers: a row per day, named by the day, with a cell per hour ("14:00:
  1,000 visits"), captioned with the metric.
- A polite live region announces the highlighted hour with its value and change, flying in and returning to the week, view
  switches, metric switches and resets.
- The metric and view switches are segmented controls with one tab stop each. The peak hour rows are toggle buttons, named
  with the day, hour and value, pressed while the camera is on their hour. "Reset view" is only in the tab order while shown.
- Keyboard focus shows a 2px ring 2px outside the plot; pointer focus does not.
- Colors are never the only signal: values are in the card, the table and the announcements, and the change carries a sign
  and an arrow.

### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| ← → ↑ ↓ | The first press highlights the busiest hour; then move by hour (← →) or day (↑ ↓), stopping at the edges |
| Home / End | The first / last hour of the highlighted day |
| Enter / Space | Fly to the highlighted hour |
| Escape | Back to the whole week; pressed again, clear the highlight |
| Shift + ← → | Turn the view by 15° |
| Shift + ↑ ↓ | Tilt the view by 8° (10° to 84°) |
| + / − | Zoom in / out by 1.25 (0.7 to 2.8) |

## Motion

- **Intro.** The first time the plot is on screen the camera swings down from far above (about 3 seconds) while the bars grow
  from the floor, back row and left column first.
- **Metric switch.** Every bar's height and color spring to the new values, each starting a little later from Monday 00:00
  toward Sunday 23:00 (a diagonal wave of about a third of a second); the summary's numbers roll digit by digit and its texts
  cross-fade; the legend changes color over 480ms.
- **Camera.** Fly-in, return, reset and view switches are springs of 1 to 1.4 seconds that keep their speed when interrupted;
  zoom is quicker; a released drag glides and an overdrag springs back inside the tilt limits. While the tilt changes, the fit
  of the terrain to the plot follows on its own spring.
- **Hover.** The bar lifts in about a quarter of a second and the rest of the week fades back; the card fades in (120ms) and
  then follows the bar on a spring as the camera moves.
- **Reduced motion.** No intro and no wave; camera moves, view switches and zooms land at once; drags follow the pointer but do
  not glide; the card only fades. With motion off nothing animates.
- An idle plot draws nothing; frames run only while something moves and only while the plot is on screen.

## Related

- `ActivityHeatmap`: a year of days as a calendar heat map.
- `BarChart`: values per category with exact comparison.
- `MetricCard`: one number with its change, for dashboards with many measures.

# Revenue globe

> A live payments map: arcs fly from every city to headquarters on a dotted globe, with a day timeline to replay or scrub and the revenue, regions and top cities beside it.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc.Blocks`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc.Blocks --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/blocks/revenue-globe

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.RevenueGlobePreviewDemo">
    <!-- An invented SaaS day: 40 cities paying into Denver. The code-behind generates the payments (seeded) and starts
         the clock at 14:30 UTC; the globe then plays the day out in real time. -->
    <arc:RevenueGlobe x:Name="Globe"
                      Title="Today's payments"
                      Description="40 cities paying into Denver. Drag the globe, or pick a city to fly there."
                      DateText="Thursday, 22 October" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class RevenueGlobePreviewDemo : UserControl
{
    public RevenueGlobePreviewDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        RevenueGlobeSampleDay.Apply(Globe);
    }
}

/// <summary>
/// The invented day every RevenueGlobe demo shows: a mid-sized SaaS with its headquarters in Denver, 40 cities in three
/// regions, and a whole day of payments drawn from a seeded model (the same day on every run). The clock starts at
/// 14:30 UTC.
/// </summary>
public static class RevenueGlobeSampleDay
{
    /// <summary>The day shown: 22 October 2026, 00:00 UTC.</summary>
    public static readonly DateTimeOffset Day = new(2026, 10, 22, 0, 0, 0, TimeSpan.Zero);

    /// <summary>Where the demo clock starts.</summary>
    public static readonly DateTimeOffset Start = Day.AddHours(14.5);

    private static (City[] Cities, RevenuePayment[] Payments, double[] Forecasts)? s_day;

    private sealed record City(string Name, string Country, string Region, double Latitude, double Longitude, double Utc, double Weight);

    private static readonly string[] s_regions = ["Americas", "EMEA", "APAC"];

    private static readonly City[] s_cities =
    [
        new("Denver", "US", "Americas", 39.74, -104.99, -7, 4.8),
        new("Boston", "US", "Americas", 42.36, -71.06, -5, 8.0),
        new("Atlanta", "US", "Americas", 33.75, -84.39, -5, 5.5),
        new("Houston", "US", "Americas", 29.76, -95.37, -6, 4.2),
        new("Phoenix", "US", "Americas", 33.45, -112.07, -7, 2.4),
        new("Minneapolis", "US", "Americas", 44.98, -93.27, -6, 2.6),
        new("Vancouver", "CA", "Americas", 49.28, -123.12, -8, 3.0),
        new("Montreal", "CA", "Americas", 45.50, -73.57, -5, 3.2),
        new("Guadalajara", "MX", "Americas", 20.67, -103.35, -6, 2.0),
        new("Panama City", "PA", "Americas", 8.98, -79.52, -5, 1.0),
        new("Medellín", "CO", "Americas", 6.24, -75.58, -5, 1.2),
        new("Quito", "EC", "Americas", -0.18, -78.47, -5, 0.7),
        new("Rio de Janeiro", "BR", "Americas", -22.91, -43.17, -3, 3.6),
        new("Montevideo", "UY", "Americas", -34.90, -56.16, -3, 0.8),
        new("Lisbon", "PT", "EMEA", 38.72, -9.14, 0, 2.2),
        new("Copenhagen", "DK", "EMEA", 55.68, 12.57, 1, 3.6),
        new("Warsaw", "PL", "EMEA", 52.23, 21.01, 1, 2.4),
        new("Vienna", "AT", "EMEA", 48.21, 16.37, 1, 3.0),
        new("Zurich", "CH", "EMEA", 47.38, 8.54, 1, 4.4),
        new("Athens", "GR", "EMEA", 37.98, 23.73, 2, 1.6),
        new("Helsinki", "FI", "EMEA", 60.17, 24.94, 2, 2.0),
        new("Brussels", "BE", "EMEA", 50.85, 4.35, 1, 3.0),
        new("Cairo", "EG", "EMEA", 30.04, 31.24, 2, 2.2),
        new("Riyadh", "SA", "EMEA", 24.71, 46.68, 3, 2.8),
        new("Casablanca", "MA", "EMEA", 33.57, -7.59, 1, 1.0),
        new("Accra", "GH", "EMEA", 5.60, -0.19, 0, 0.9),
        new("Johannesburg", "ZA", "EMEA", -26.20, 28.05, 2, 2.6),
        new("Doha", "QA", "EMEA", 25.29, 51.53, 3, 1.8),
        new("Osaka", "JP", "APAC", 34.69, 135.50, 9, 4.0),
        new("Busan", "KR", "APAC", 35.18, 129.08, 9, 3.0),
        new("Taipei", "TW", "APAC", 25.03, 121.57, 8, 2.6),
        new("Bangkok", "TH", "APAC", 13.76, 100.50, 7, 2.4),
        new("Hanoi", "VN", "APAC", 21.03, 105.85, 7, 1.6),
        new("Kuala Lumpur", "MY", "APAC", 3.14, 101.69, 8, 2.0),
        new("Delhi", "IN", "APAC", 28.61, 77.21, 5.5, 4.6),
        new("Chennai", "IN", "APAC", 13.08, 80.27, 5.5, 2.2),
        new("Colombo", "LK", "APAC", 6.93, 79.86, 5.5, 0.9),
        new("Perth", "AU", "APAC", -31.95, 115.86, 8, 2.4),
        new("Brisbane", "AU", "APAC", -27.47, 153.03, 10, 2.2),
        new("Wellington", "NZ", "APAC", -41.29, 174.78, 12, 1.4),
    ];

    /// <summary>Fills a globe with the sample day: cities, regions, HQ, payments, the day and the 14:30 clock.</summary>
    public static void Apply(RevenueGlobe globe)
    {
        var (cities, payments, forecasts) = s_day ??= Generate();
        var regions = new RevenueRegion[s_regions.Length];
        for (var i = 0; i < regions.Length; i++)
        {
            regions[i] = new RevenueRegion { Key = s_regions[i], Name = s_regions[i], Forecast = forecasts[i] };
        }
        var models = cities.Select(c => new RevenueCity
        {
            Key = c.Name,
            Name = c.Name,
            CountryCode = c.Country,
            RegionKey = c.Region,
            Latitude = c.Latitude,
            Longitude = c.Longitude,
            UtcOffsetHours = c.Utc,
            Weight = c.Weight
        }).ToArray();
        globe.Regions.AddRange(regions);
        globe.Cities.AddRange(models);
        globe.Headquarters = models[0];
        globe.DayStart = Day;
        globe.Now = Start;
        globe.Payments = payments;
    }

    // The model: payments per minute λ(h) = k·(62 + 50·g(h, 13, 6.5) + 14·g(h, 8.5, 2.4) + 10·g(h, 18.5, 3)) with
    // g(x, μ, w) = exp(−((x − μ)/w)²); ±8% jitter per 15 minutes, a 4% chance of a 1.3–1.9× burst and a 2.3× spike at
    // 11:15. Each payment picks a city by weight × daylight (0.35 at night, 1 by day in the city's own time zone);
    // amounts are log-normal around $17 with a 1.2% chance of a 15–45× order. mulberry32, seed 20261022: the same day
    // every time.
    private const double Scale = 1.6;

    private static (City[], RevenuePayment[], double[]) Generate()
    {
        var random = new Mulberry32(20261022);
        var cities = s_cities;
        var weights = new double[cities.Length];
        for (var c = 0; c < cities.Length; c++)
        {
            weights[c] = cities[c].Weight * (0.85 + 0.3 * random.Next());
        }
        var payments = new List<RevenuePayment>(220_000);
        var expected = new double[s_regions.Length];
        var share = new double[cities.Length];
        var seconds = new List<(double Second, int City, double Amount)>(512);
        var burst = 1.0;
        for (var minute = 0; minute < 1440; minute++)
        {
            var h = minute / 60.0;
            if (minute % 15 == 0)
            {
                // Each quarter hour jitters a little, now and then one bursts, and at 11:15 a newsletter goes out.
                burst = (1 + 0.08 * Gaussian(random)) * (random.Next() < 0.04 ? 1.3 + 0.6 * random.Next() : 1);
                if (minute == 11 * 60 + 15)
                {
                    burst *= 2.3;
                }
            }
            var lambda = Scale * (62 + 50 * G(h, 13, 6.5) + 14 * G(h, 8.5, 2.4) + 10 * G(h, 18.5, 3)) * burst;
            var total = 0.0;
            for (var c = 0; c < cities.Length; c++)
            {
                share[c] = weights[c] * Daylight(h, cities[c].Utc);
                total += share[c];
            }
            for (var c = 0; c < cities.Length; c++)
            {
                // Expected revenue (mean amount ≈ $31) by region, for the forecasts.
                expected[Array.IndexOf(s_regions, cities[c].Region)] += lambda / burst * share[c] / total * 31;
            }
            var count = Poisson(random, lambda);
            seconds.Clear();
            for (var i = 0; i < count; i++)
            {
                var pick = random.Next() * total;
                var city = 0;
                while (city < cities.Length - 1 && pick >= share[city])
                {
                    pick -= share[city];
                    city++;
                }
                var amount = Math.Exp(Math.Log(17) + 0.8 * Gaussian(random));
                if (random.Next() < 0.012)
                {
                    amount *= 15 + 30 * random.Next();
                }
                seconds.Add((random.Next() * 60, city, Math.Max(1, Math.Round(amount))));
            }
            seconds.Sort((a, b) => a.Second.CompareTo(b.Second));
            foreach (var (second, city, amount) in seconds)
            {
                payments.Add(new RevenuePayment(Day.AddSeconds(minute * 60 + second), cities[city].Name, amount));
            }
        }
        // Forecast: the region's expected day × 1.08, rounded to 10,000.
        var forecasts = expected.Select(e => Math.Round(e * 1.08 / 10_000) * 10_000).ToArray();
        return (cities, payments.ToArray(), forecasts);
    }

    private static double G(double x, double mu, double width) => Math.Exp(-Math.Pow((x - mu) / width, 2));

    /// <summary>0.35 at night, rising 06–09 and falling 21–24 local time.</summary>
    private static double Daylight(double utcHour, double offset)
    {
        var local = ((utcHour + offset) % 24 + 24) % 24;
        return 0.35 + 0.65 * Smoothstep(6, 9, local) * (1 - Smoothstep(21, 24, local));
    }

    private static double Smoothstep(double a, double b, double x)
    {
        var t = Math.Clamp((x - a) / (b - a), 0, 1);
        return t * t * (3 - 2 * t);
    }

    private static int Poisson(Mulberry32 random, double lambda)
    {
        // Inversion by sequential search (λ stays under 300 here).
        var u = random.Next();
        var p = Math.Exp(-lambda);
        var cumulative = p;
        var k = 0;
        while (u > cumulative && k < 2000)
        {
            k++;
            p *= lambda / k;
            cumulative += p;
            if (p < 1e-300)
            {
                break;
            }
        }
        return k;
    }

    private static double Gaussian(Mulberry32 random)
    {
        var u = Math.Max(1e-12, random.Next());
        var v = random.Next();
        return Math.Sqrt(-2 * Math.Log(u)) * Math.Cos(2 * Math.PI * v);
    }

    /// <summary>mulberry32: a tiny seeded generator, the same numbers on every platform.</summary>
    private sealed class Mulberry32(uint seed)
    {
        private uint _state = seed;

        public double Next()
        {
            unchecked
            {
                _state += 0x6D2B79F5;
                var t = _state;
                t = (t ^ (t >> 15)) * (t | 1);
                t ^= t + (t ^ (t >> 7)) * (t | 61);
                return (t ^ (t >> 14)) / 4294967296.0;
            }
        }
    }
}
```

## When to use

`RevenueGlobe` turns a day of payments into something people can watch. Every payment flies as an arc from the city it
came from to your headquarters, the figures beside the globe count up as the arcs land, and a timeline under it shows the
whole day: how busy each quarter hour was, where the present is, and a playhead you can drag back to any moment. It fits
the top of an operations or revenue overview, a screen on the office wall, or the home page of a small business tool.

- **A revenue overview for a team that sells worldwide.** Regions show today's revenue against their forecast, so the
  question "are we on track?" is answered per region at a glance, and the top cities say where the day is happening.
- **A wall display for launches and campaigns.** The globe drifts on its own, the arcs keep flying, and Replay today
  plays the whole day in under a minute, which makes the morning's spike easy to show in a stand-up.
- **A live feed from your payment provider.** Set `ClockMode` to `External`, append payments as webhooks arrive and move
  `Now`; each new payment flies its arc as soon as it is due.
- **A post-mortem of an incident.** Drag the playhead to the minute the errors started and read the totals as they were
  then: every figure, list and bar follows the playhead, not only the clock.

## When not to use

- **Precise analysis.** The globe is a picture of activity. Totals by hour, by product or by customer belong in a chart or a
  table (`DataGrid`, a line chart) where the numbers can be compared directly.
- **Many thousands of places.** The block draws each city as a dot with its own arc. A few dozen cities read well; for
  hundreds, group them into the cities people know.
- **Payments that do not happen in a day.** The timeline always spans 24 hours. Weekly or monthly totals need another view.
- **A page full of other animation.** The drifting globe and the arcs draw the eye. Put it where it can be the one moving
  thing, or turn the drift off with `DriftSpeed="0"`.

## Usage

### Anatomy

From top to bottom (wider than 880 pixels, the panel moves to the right of the globe):

1. **Header**: `Title`, `Description` and `DateText` (you format the date).
2. **Globe**: land and sea as dots shaded by depth, city dots sized by today's revenue, the headquarters with its name, and
   the payment arcs. Hovering a city shows a card with its revenue, payments, share of the total and local time.
3. **Timeline controls**: Replay today, Pause / Play, the clock at the playhead (UTC by default) and the Live pill.
4. **Timeline**: payments per 15 minutes as bars, darker up to the playhead and lighter up to the present, with dashes for
   the rest of the day, and the playhead you can drag.
5. **Panel**: revenue today, payments and the last hour; the regions against their forecast; the five top cities.

### Data

Give the cities, the regions they count toward, the headquarters and the payments. Cities and regions are plain objects,
so they can be written in XAML; payments are usually loaded in code.

```xml
<arc:RevenueGlobe x:Name="Globe"
                  Title="Ebook orders"
                  Description="Cities buying from Dublin today."
                  DateText="Thursday, 22 October"
                  CurrencySymbol="€">
    <arc:RevenueGlobe.Regions>
        <arc:RevenueRegion Key="eu" Name="Europe" Forecast="61000" />
        <arc:RevenueRegion Key="am" Name="Americas" Forecast="38000" />
    </arc:RevenueGlobe.Regions>
    <arc:RevenueCity Key="dub" Name="Dublin" CountryCode="IE" RegionKey="eu" Latitude="53.35" Longitude="-6.26" />
    <arc:RevenueCity Key="ams" Name="Amsterdam" CountryCode="NL" RegionKey="eu" Latitude="52.37" Longitude="4.90" UtcOffsetHours="1" />
    <arc:RevenueCity Key="tor" Name="Toronto" CountryCode="CA" RegionKey="am" Latitude="43.65" Longitude="-79.38" UtcOffsetHours="-4" />
</arc:RevenueGlobe>
```

```csharp
Globe.Headquarters = Globe.Cities[0];
Globe.DayStart = new DateTimeOffset(2026, 10, 22, 0, 0, 0, TimeSpan.Zero);
Globe.Payments = orders.Select(o => new RevenuePayment(o.PaidAt, o.CityKey, o.Total)).ToList();
```

- A payment names its city by `RevenueCity.Key`. Payments of the headquarters count in every total but draw no arc.
  Payments whose city is unknown count in the totals only.
- Payments should come in time order; anything else is sorted once. Totals at any moment are prefix sums, so a whole day of
  a few hundred thousand payments replays without walking them again.
- `RevenueRegion.Forecast` is the revenue expected from the region for the whole day; its row shows today's revenue as a
  share of it. A region flies the camera to `CenterLatitude` / `CenterLongitude`, or to the revenue-weighted middle of its
  cities when those are not set.
- The globe's land comes from Natural Earth 1:110m (public domain), sampled once on a lattice of 12,800 points (dots
  1.7° apart). `Land` takes a coarser or finer sampling (`RevenueGlobeLand.Sample(7000, 1200)`) or your own dots
  (`RevenueGlobeLand.FromPoints(...)`).

### The clock

`Now` is the present: payments after it wait, and the light bars of the timeline end there. With the default
`ClockMode="Internal"` the globe moves `Now` on in real time from the value you set, so a day prepared in advance plays out
live, which is what the preview above does from 14:30. When the block is scrolled out of view it stops drawing, and catches
up with the real time when it comes back.

With `ClockMode="External"` your app moves `Now`. Append payments with `AddPayment` (or add them to a collection that raises
change events) and then move `Now` to the time your server reported:

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.RevenueGlobeLiveFeedDemo">
    <!-- Your own data, streamed: an ebook shop in Dublin. ClockMode External means the app moves Now; the code-behind
         plays a server here, appending orders and moving Now every 400 ms. -->
    <arc:RevenueGlobe x:Name="Globe"
                      ClockMode="External"
                      CurrencySymbol="€"
                      DriftCenterOffset="20"
                      Title="Ebook orders"
                      Description="14 cities buying from Dublin, as the orders come in."
                      DateText="Thursday, 22 October">
        <arc:RevenueGlobe.Regions>
            <arc:RevenueRegion Key="eu" Name="Europe" Forecast="61000" />
            <arc:RevenueRegion Key="am" Name="Americas" Forecast="38000" />
            <arc:RevenueRegion Key="ap" Name="Asia Pacific" Forecast="21000" />
        </arc:RevenueGlobe.Regions>
        <arc:RevenueCity Key="dub" Name="Dublin" CountryCode="IE" RegionKey="eu" Latitude="53.35" Longitude="-6.26" Weight="3" />
        <arc:RevenueCity Key="edi" Name="Edinburgh" CountryCode="GB" RegionKey="eu" Latitude="55.95" Longitude="-3.19" Weight="2" />
        <arc:RevenueCity Key="ams" Name="Amsterdam" CountryCode="NL" RegionKey="eu" Latitude="52.37" Longitude="4.90" UtcOffsetHours="1" Weight="3" />
        <arc:RevenueCity Key="ham" Name="Hamburg" CountryCode="DE" RegionKey="eu" Latitude="53.55" Longitude="9.99" UtcOffsetHours="1" Weight="3" />
        <arc:RevenueCity Key="sto" Name="Stockholm" CountryCode="SE" RegionKey="eu" Latitude="59.33" Longitude="18.07" UtcOffsetHours="1" Weight="2" />
        <arc:RevenueCity Key="por" Name="Porto" CountryCode="PT" RegionKey="eu" Latitude="41.15" Longitude="-8.61" Weight="1" />
        <arc:RevenueCity Key="mil" Name="Milan" CountryCode="IT" RegionKey="eu" Latitude="45.46" Longitude="9.19" UtcOffsetHours="1" Weight="2" />
        <arc:RevenueCity Key="tor" Name="Toronto" CountryCode="CA" RegionKey="am" Latitude="43.65" Longitude="-79.38" UtcOffsetHours="-4" Weight="3" />
        <arc:RevenueCity Key="chi" Name="Chicago" CountryCode="US" RegionKey="am" Latitude="41.88" Longitude="-87.63" UtcOffsetHours="-5" Weight="3" />
        <arc:RevenueCity Key="sea" Name="Seattle" CountryCode="US" RegionKey="am" Latitude="47.61" Longitude="-122.33" UtcOffsetHours="-7" Weight="2" />
        <arc:RevenueCity Key="bue" Name="Buenos Aires" CountryCode="AR" RegionKey="am" Latitude="-34.60" Longitude="-58.38" UtcOffsetHours="-3" Weight="1" />
        <arc:RevenueCity Key="mel" Name="Melbourne" CountryCode="AU" RegionKey="ap" Latitude="-37.81" Longitude="144.96" UtcOffsetHours="11" Weight="2" />
        <arc:RevenueCity Key="sin" Name="Singapore" CountryCode="SG" RegionKey="ap" Latitude="1.35" Longitude="103.82" UtcOffsetHours="8" Weight="2" />
        <arc:RevenueCity Key="tok" Name="Sapporo" CountryCode="JP" RegionKey="ap" Latitude="43.06" Longitude="141.35" UtcOffsetHours="9" Weight="1" />
    </arc:RevenueGlobe>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia;
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Threading;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class RevenueGlobeLiveFeedDemo : UserControl
{
    private static readonly DateTimeOffset Day = new(2026, 10, 22, 0, 0, 0, TimeSpan.Zero);
    private readonly DispatcherTimer _timer = new() { Interval = TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(400) };
    private readonly Random _random = new(1022);
    private DateTimeOffset _now = Day.AddHours(16);

    public RevenueGlobeLiveFeedDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Globe.Headquarters = Globe.Cities[0];
        Globe.DayStart = Day;
        Globe.Now = _now;
        // The history so far, as a server would send it once: about one order every 3 seconds since midnight.
        var history = new List<RevenuePayment>();
        for (var t = Day.AddSeconds(_random.NextDouble() * 6); t < _now; t = t.AddSeconds(_random.NextDouble() * 6))
        {
            history.Add(Order(t));
        }
        Globe.Payments = history;
        _timer.Tick += OnTick;
    }

    protected override void OnAttachedToVisualTree(VisualTreeAttachmentEventArgs e)
    {
        base.OnAttachedToVisualTree(e);
        _timer.Start();
    }

    protected override void OnDetachedFromVisualTree(VisualTreeAttachmentEventArgs e)
    {
        base.OnDetachedFromVisualTree(e);
        _timer.Stop();
    }

    private void OnTick(object? sender, EventArgs e)
    {
        // A server pushes what happened in the last 400 ms: zero to three orders, then the new present.
        var next = _now.AddMilliseconds(400);
        var offsets = Enumerable.Range(0, _random.Next(0, 4)).Select(_ => _random.Next(0, 400)).Order().ToArray();
        foreach (var offset in offsets)
        {
            // In time order: appending at the end is cheap.
            Globe.AddPayment(Order(_now.AddMilliseconds(offset)));
        }
        _now = next;
        Globe.Now = next;
    }

    private RevenuePayment Order(DateTimeOffset time)
    {
        // Weighted pick of a city, and a book or two (€4–€30).
        var cities = Globe.Cities;
        var total = cities.Sum(c => c.Weight);
        var pick = _random.NextDouble() * total;
        var city = cities[^1];
        foreach (var c in cities)
        {
            pick -= c.Weight;
            if (pick < 0)
            {
                city = c;
                break;
            }
        }
        return new RevenuePayment(time, city.Key, Math.Round(4 + _random.NextDouble() * _random.NextDouble() * 26));
    }
}
```

### Replay, pause and the playhead

Replay today goes back to 00:00 and plays the day at `ReplaySpeed` (1500×: an hour in 2.4 seconds), easing in and braking
so it lands exactly on the present, where it goes live again. Pause holds the playhead (the arcs in flight still land);
Play replays on from there. Go live, or End on the timeline, fast-forwards to the present in at most two seconds.
Dragging the timeline jumps to the pointer and follows it; letting go replays on with the speed of the drag.

All of this is also available to your own controls: `ReplayCommand`, `TogglePauseCommand` and `GoLiveCommand`, the
methods `Replay()`, `Pause()`, `Play()`, `GoLive()` and `SeekTo(time)`, the two-way `Time` and `IsPaused`, and
`TimeChanged`, which fires every frame while the playhead moves:

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.RevenueGlobePlaybackDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12">
        <!-- Your own buttons can drive the timeline through the commands, and TimeChanged reports the playhead. -->
        <StackPanel Orientation="Horizontal" Spacing="8">
            <arc:Button Content="Replay at 3000×" Size="Small" Click="OnFastReplay" />
            <arc:Button Content="Pause or play" Size="Small" Command="{Binding #Globe.TogglePauseCommand}" />
            <arc:Button Content="Jump to 09:00" Size="Small" Click="OnNine" />
            <arc:Button Content="Go live" Size="Small" Variant="Ghost" Command="{Binding #Globe.GoLiveCommand}" />
        </StackPanel>
        <arc:RevenueGlobe x:Name="Globe"
                          Title="Today's payments"
                          Description="Replay the day, pause it, or drag the playhead anywhere."
                          DateText="Thursday, 22 October"
                          TimeChanged="OnTimeChanged" />
        <TextBlock x:Name="Status" Opacity="0.7" FontFeatures="tnum" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class RevenueGlobePlaybackDemo : UserControl
{
    private int _lastSecond = -1;

    public RevenueGlobePlaybackDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        RevenueGlobeSampleDay.Apply(Globe);
        ShowState(Globe.Time, Globe.PlaybackState);
    }

    private void OnFastReplay(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        Globe.ReplaySpeed = 3000;
        Globe.Replay();
    }

    private void OnNine(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) => Globe.SeekTo(RevenueGlobeSampleDay.Day.AddHours(9));

    private void OnTimeChanged(object? sender, RevenueGlobeTimeChangedEventArgs e)
    {
        // TimeChanged fires every frame while replaying: update the text once per simulated second at most.
        var second = (int)e.Time.TimeOfDay.TotalSeconds;
        if (second != _lastSecond)
        {
            _lastSecond = second;
            ShowState(e.Time, e.PlaybackState);
        }
    }

    private void ShowState(DateTimeOffset time, RevenueGlobePlaybackState state) =>
        Status.Text = $"{state} · {time:HH:mm:ss} UTC";
}
```

### Cities and regions

Click a city on the globe or in the top-cities list and the camera flies there along the great circle, zooms in to
`CityZoom` and holds the view; the card stays on the city. Click a region and the camera flies to the region at
`RegionZoom`, the other cities fade and the region's three biggest cities get their names. A city and a region are never
selected together. Click the selected row again, click empty space on the globe or press Escape to let go: the zoom springs
back, the tilt returns home and the drift resumes.

`SelectedCity` and `SelectedRegion` are two-way, `FlyTo(city)` and `FlyTo(region)` select from code, `ResetView()` clears
the selection and turns the globe back home, and `SelectionChanged` reports every change:

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.RevenueGlobeSelectionDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12">
        <!-- The selection is a two-way property: the app can point the camera at a city or a region, and hear about
             every change the user makes. -->
        <StackPanel Orientation="Horizontal" Spacing="8">
            <arc:Button Content="Zurich" Size="Small" Click="OnZurich" />
            <arc:Button Content="APAC" Size="Small" Click="OnApac" />
            <arc:Button Content="Reset view" Size="Small" Variant="Ghost" Click="OnReset" />
        </StackPanel>
        <arc:RevenueGlobe x:Name="Globe"
                          Title="Today's payments"
                          Description="Pick a city or a region; the card stays on the selected city."
                          DateText="Thursday, 22 October"
                          SelectionChanged="OnSelectionChanged" />
        <TextBlock x:Name="Status" Text="Nothing selected" Opacity="0.7" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;
using Avalonia.Interactivity;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class RevenueGlobeSelectionDemo : UserControl
{
    public RevenueGlobeSelectionDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        RevenueGlobeSampleDay.Apply(Globe);
        Globe.SelectedCity = Globe.Cities.First(c => c.Key == "Zurich");
    }

    private void OnZurich(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) => Globe.FlyTo(Globe.Cities.First(c => c.Key == "Zurich"));

    private void OnApac(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) => Globe.FlyTo(Globe.Regions.First(r => r.Key == "APAC"));

    private void OnReset(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) => Globe.ResetView();

    private void OnSelectionChanged(object? sender, RevenueGlobeSelectionChangedEventArgs e) =>
        Status.Text = e.NewCity is { } city ? $"Selected city: {city.Name}"
            : e.NewRegion is { } region ? $"Selected region: {region.Name}"
            : "Nothing selected";
}
```

### Narrow layouts

The block follows its own width, not the window's. From 880 pixels the panel sits beside the globe; between 600 and 880 it
sits under it in two columns; below 600 it is one column with a smaller revenue figure, and below 400 the clock takes a row
of its own. The globe's height follows the width (at most 580 pixels), and its radius is always 41% of the smaller side.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.RevenueGlobeNarrowDemo">
    <!-- Below 600 the panel is one column and the revenue figure is smaller; below 400 the clock takes its own row. -->
    <arc:RevenueGlobe x:Name="Globe"
                      Width="380"
                      HorizontalAlignment="Center"
                      Title="Today's payments"
                      Description="40 cities paying into Denver. Drag the globe, or pick a city to fly there."
                      DateText="Thursday, 22 October" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class RevenueGlobeNarrowDemo : UserControl
{
    public RevenueGlobeNarrowDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        RevenueGlobeSampleDay.Apply(Globe);
    }

```

### Reduced motion

When motion is turned down the globe holds still: it shows the latest arcs drawn whole, there is no drift, no Replay or
Pause button, and the pill reads "Now". Dragging, selecting and the timeline keys still work; every change lands at once.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.RevenueGlobeReducedMotionDemo">
    <!-- Under reduced motion the globe holds still: the latest arcs drawn whole, no replay or pause, the pill reads
         "Now". Dragging, selecting and the timeline keys still work, without animation. -->
    <arc:RevenueGlobe x:Name="Globe"
                      arc:ArcMotion.Level="Reduced"
                      Title="Today's payments"
                      Description="A still picture for people who turn motion down."
                      DateText="Thursday, 22 October" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

{
    public RevenueGlobeReducedMotionDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();

    }

```

### Texts

Every word the block shows or announces is in `Labels`, a `RevenueGlobeLabels` with English defaults. Replace it as a whole
to translate the block or change its wording; the formats that take numbers or names are functions.

```csharp
Globe.Labels = new RevenueGlobeLabels
{
    Replay = "Tag wiederholen",
    Live = "Live",
    GoLive = "Zur Gegenwart",
    OfForecast = percent => $"{percent:0} % der Prognose",
};
Globe.Culture = CultureInfo.GetCultureInfo("de-DE");
```

### Performance

- A frame draws 2,500 to 3,300 dots (land, sea and cities), the arcs in flight and their rings: about 3 ms in software
  rendering on a desktop, a little more while replaying (around 30 arcs), and a few kilobytes of memory per arc.
  Browsers are slower; on a phone, a coarser `Land` (`RevenueGlobeLand.Sample(7000, 1200)`) halves the dots.
- The globe asks for frames only while something moves: the drift, an arc, a glide or a flight. Under reduced motion an idle
  globe draws nothing.
- While replaying, at most 14 arcs start per second; the totals still count every payment.

## API reference

### RevenueGlobe

A live payments map: a dotted globe on which every payment flies as an arc from its city to the headquarters, a day timeline under it (payments per 15 minutes, the playhead, replay and live controls), and a panel with today's revenue, the regions against their forecast and the top cities. Drag the globe to spin it (it glides and drifts back and forth when idle), hover a city for its figures, pick a city or a region to fly there, replay the day at 1500× or drag the playhead to any moment; every figure follows the playhead.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Title` | `object?` | `null` | The block's title (text or any content). |
| `Description` | `object?` | `null` | The line under the title (text or any content). |
| `DateText` | `string?` | `null` | The date at the top right, formatted by the app ("Thursday, 22 October"). |
| `Headquarters` | `RevenueCity?` | `null` | Where the arcs land: drawn as a haloed dot with its name. Its own payments count but draw no arc. |
| `Regions` | `AvaloniaList<RevenueRegion>` | – | Regions the cities count toward; each gets a row with its revenue against its forecast. |
| `Payments` | `IEnumerable<RevenuePayment>?` | `null` | Payments in time order. Collections that raise change events are followed (appending at the end is cheap); payments after `Now` wait for it. |
| `DayStart` | `DateTimeOffset` | `01/01/0001 00:00:00 +00:00` | Midnight of the day shown; the timeline spans 24 hours from it. Default: 00:00 UTC of `Now`. |
| `Now` | `DateTimeOffset` | `01/01/0001 00:00:00 +00:00` | The present: payments up to here have happened. With `ClockMode` Internal the globe moves it on in real time from the value you set (default: the current time). |
| `Time` | `DateTimeOffset` | `01/01/0001 00:00:00 +00:00` | The playhead (two-way). Setting it jumps there; it follows `Now` while live. |
| `IsPaused` | `bool` | `false` | Time stands still and no new arcs start (two-way); the globe keeps drifting and arcs in flight land. |
| `ReplaySpeed` | `double` | `1500` | Simulated seconds per second while replaying. Default 1500 (an hour in 2.4 s). |
| `SelectedCity` | `RevenueCity?` | `null` | The selected city (two-way): the camera flies there and holds; clears `SelectedRegion`. |
| `SelectedRegion` | `RevenueRegion?` | `null` | The selected region (two-way): the camera flies to its center and other cities fade; clears `SelectedCity`. |
| `ClockMode` | `RevenueGlobeClockMode` | `Internal` | Whether the globe moves `Now` on by itself (Internal, default) or the app does (External). |
| `HomeTilt` | `double` | `22` | The tilt the camera returns to, in degrees of latitude it looks from. Default 22. |
| `DriftSpeed` | `double` | `4` | Idle drift speed in degrees per second (0 turns the drift off). Default 4. |
| `DriftCenterOffset` | `double` | `40` | Center of the drift range: degrees east of the headquarters' longitude. Default 40. |
| `DriftHalfRange` | `double` | `43` | Half width of the drift range in degrees. Default 43. |
| `CityZoom` | `double` | `1.3` | Zoom the camera flies in to for a selected city. Default 1.30. |
| `RegionZoom` | `double` | `1.08` | Zoom the camera flies in to for a selected region. Default 1.08. |
| `Land` | `RevenueGlobeLand?` | `null` | The land and sea dots; null uses `Default` (Natural Earth 1:110m). |
| `CurrencySymbol` | `string` | `"$"` | Symbol in front of amounts. Default "$"; amounts show as whole numbers with group separators. |
| `Culture` | `CultureInfo?` | `null` | Culture for numbers (separators); null uses en-US. |
| `TimeFormat` | `string` | `"HH:mm:ss"` | Format of the clock. Default "HH:mm:ss". |
| `Labels` | `RevenueGlobeLabels` | – | Every word the block shows or announces (English by default). |
| `IsLive` | `bool` | – | *Read-only.* The playhead follows the present. |
| `PlaybackState` | `RevenueGlobePlaybackState` | – | *Read-only.* What the timeline is doing: live, paused, replaying or scrubbing. |
| `CenterLongitude` | `double` | – | *Read-only.* Longitude at the center of the view, in degrees (follows the camera). |
| `CenterLatitude` | `double` | – | *Read-only.* Latitude the camera looks from, in degrees (follows the camera). |
| `Zoom` | `double` | – | *Read-only.* The camera zoom (1 = the globe fills 82% of the smaller side). |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `SelectionChanged` | `RevenueGlobeSelectionChangedEventArgs` | Raised when the user or the app changes the selected city or region. |
| `TimeChanged` | `RevenueGlobeTimeChangedEventArgs` | Raised whenever the playhead moves (every frame while replaying: throttle what you do with it). |
| `CityInvoked` | `RevenueGlobeCityEventArgs` | Raised when a city dot or a top-city row is clicked (also when it was already selected). |

Pseudo-classes: `:live`, `:paused`, `:replaying`, `:scrubbing`, `:city-selected`, `:region-selected`, `:wide`, `:stacked`, `:narrow`, `:compact`, `:reduced`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

### RevenueCity

A city on a `RevenueGlobe`: where payments come from (and, for `Headquarters`, where they go). Coordinates are in degrees; the city's local time uses `UtcOffsetHours`.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Key` | `string` | `""` | Identifies the city; `CityKey` refers to it. |
| `Name` | `string` | `""` | The name shown on the globe, in the hover card and in the list of top cities. |
| `CountryCode` | `string?` | `null` | A short country code shown after the name in the list of top cities ("US"). |
| `RegionKey` | `string?` | `null` | The `Key` of the region the city counts toward. |
| `Latitude` | `double` | `0` | Latitude in degrees, north positive. |
| `Longitude` | `double` | `0` | Longitude in degrees, east positive. |
| `UtcOffsetHours` | `double` | `0` | Offset of the city's local time from UTC in hours (5.5 for India); the hover card shows the local time. |
| `Weight` | `double` | `1` | A relative size for sample data generators; the control itself does not read it. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### RevenueRegion

A region that groups cities on a `RevenueGlobe`, with the revenue expected from it for the whole day.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Key` | `string` | `""` | Identifies the region; `RegionKey` refers to it. |
| `Name` | `string` | `""` | The name shown in the list of regions and announced when the camera flies there. |
| `Forecast` | `double` | `0` | Revenue expected from the region for the whole day; its bar shows today's revenue as a share of it. |
| `CenterLatitude` | `double?` | `null` | Latitude the camera flies to; null uses the revenue-weighted center of the region's cities. |
| `CenterLongitude` | `double?` | `null` | Longitude the camera flies to; null uses the revenue-weighted center of the region's cities. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

## Accessibility

- The globe is a focusable region named "Revenue globe" with how to use it ("Arrow keys turn the globe, Escape clears the
  selection."). Its description is a summary of the moment: revenue, payments, the time, each region and the leading city.
  It is refreshed when the minute changes, not every frame.
- Screen readers also find a hidden table of every city with its region, revenue and payments, updated with the playhead.
- The city dots themselves are not focusable. Keyboard users choose cities from the top-cities list and regions from the
  regions list; both are toggle buttons whose pressed state is the selection. A region row describes its share of today's
  revenue and its forecast.
- The figures count toward their value on screen, but screen readers read the final value at once.
- The timeline is a slider over the day so far (in seconds since midnight), named "Time of day, UTC".
- A polite live region announces "Paused", "Replaying today", "Back to live", "Camera on …" and "Selection cleared".
- Replay, Pause / Play and the Live pill are buttons; the pause button's name says what it will do.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Where | Action |
|---|---|---|
| `ArrowLeft` / `ArrowRight` | Globe | Give the globe a push west or east; it glides out |
| `ArrowUp` / `ArrowDown` | Globe | Tilt it briefly; it springs back to its home tilt |
| `Escape` | Globe | Clear the selected city or region |
| `ArrowLeft` / `ArrowRight` | Timeline | Move the playhead 5 minutes (`Shift`: an hour); in the past it replays on from there |
| `PageUp` / `PageDown` | Timeline | Move the playhead an hour |
| `Home` | Timeline | Go to 00:00 |
| `End` | Timeline | Go live |
| `Enter` or `Space` | Buttons and rows | Press the button; select or clear the region or city |
| Drag | Globe | Spin the globe; a fast release glides on, the tilt springs back home |
| Drag | Timeline | Move the playhead under the pointer; release to replay on |

## Motion

- Idle, the globe drifts back and forth at 4° a second over 86° of longitude around the headquarters, turning smoothly at
  the ends; the tilt always returns to 22° on a slow spring.
- A drag moves the surface under the pointer. Releasing glides on (the speed falls by 1.3% a frame) until the drift takes
  over; pulling the tilt past 65° stretches like a rubber band and springs back.
- Flights to a city or region follow the great circle on a critically damped spring and zoom out a little on the way when
  the flight is long.
- An arc's head travels in about a second (longer for far cities), the arc stays whole a third of a second, then its tail
  follows it into the headquarters while it fades. A small ring opens at the city when a payment starts and a larger one at
  the headquarters when it lands; the figures count up at that moment.
- The figures ease to every new value in about a quarter of a second. The hover card fades and grows in, follows its city
  on a spring and fades out.
- Under reduced motion none of this moves; see [Reduced motion](#reduced-motion).

## Related

- **Metric card** and **Animated counter**: one figure that counts toward its value, without the map.
- **Data grid** and the **line charts**: the precise numbers behind the picture, by hour, city or product.
- **Activity terrain** and **Customer galaxy**: the other showpieces that turn a dataset into a scene to explore.

# Customer galaxy

> Every customer as a dot sized by revenue and colored by health, turning as a galaxy; group them into clusters, fly in, and read the totals.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc.Blocks`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc.Blocks --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`

## When to use

`CustomerGalaxy` draws every customer account as one dot: the dot's area grows with the account's monthly recurring
revenue (MRR) and its color shows the account's health. In the overview the dots form a tilted, slowly turning spiral, with
the largest accounts packed in the core and the long tail of small ones trailing in two arms. Pick a grouping and every
dot springs into one packed cluster per value, labelled with its MRR and its number of accounts. A totals panel beside the
stage (under it in narrow containers) adds up everything, or the cluster you fly into, and lists the clusters with a bar
that splits each one by health. Use it when the question is where revenue and risk sit across thousands of accounts.

- **A customer success home page**, where the team opens the week by grouping by health and flying into the at-risk
  cluster. The big red dots are the renewals to call first; hovering one shows its owner and a one-line note.
- **A revenue review**, where finance groups by plan and reads how much of the MRR the largest tier carries, then switches
  the list to accounts to see how many customers each tier has.
- **A regional sales dashboard**, grouped by region, where each manager flies into their own cluster and steps through
  its accounts from the largest down with the arrow keys.
- **A product analytics page** that groups customers by industry to see which markets bring large accounts and which
  bring many small ones, and where the growing ones are.
- **A board deck screen** that stays on the overview: the turning galaxy with its totals reads at a glance and invites
  someone to click in.

## When not to use

- **Comparing a handful of numbers.** Use `BarChart` or `DonutChart`; a galaxy pays off with hundreds or thousands of
  accounts, not with five.
- **Reading exact values of many accounts side by side.** Use `Table` or `DataGrid`; the galaxy shows one
  account at a time in its card.
- **Trends over time.** Use `LineChart` or `Streamgraph`. The galaxy is a snapshot: its clusters do not move with dates.
- **A small widget in a sidebar or a card.** The block needs at least 360 px of stage height to be read; use
  `MetricCard` with a `Sparkline` instead.
- **Showing parts of a whole by one dimension only.** Use `Treemap` or `WaffleChart`, which keep exact areas without
  packing gaps.

## Usage

Give the control its accounts and the groupings you want as tabs. Each `GalaxyAccount` carries a name, its MRR, its
health key and, in `Groups`, its value for every grouping. The control lays out the spiral and the clusters, adds up the
totals and builds the list itself.

```xml
<arc:CustomerGalaxy Title="Where the revenue sits"
                    ItemsSource="{Binding Accounts}">
    <arc:GalaxyGrouping Key="plan" Header="Plan">
        <arc:GalaxyGroupDefinition Key="solo" Label="Solo" />
        <arc:GalaxyGroupDefinition Key="team" Label="Team" />
        <arc:GalaxyGroupDefinition Key="business" Label="Business" />
        <arc:GalaxyGroupDefinition Key="corporate" Label="Corporate" />
    </arc:GalaxyGrouping>
    <arc:GalaxyGrouping Key="region" Header="Region" />
    <arc:GalaxyGrouping Key="health" Header="Health" />
</arc:CustomerGalaxy>
```

`CustomerGalaxy` derives from Avalonia's `TemplatedControl`. The stage is drawn by the control itself (one dot per
account, batched by color and dimming level), so it stays fast with thousands of accounts; the labels, the card, the
buttons and the panel are ordinary controls. The control sets the pseudo-classes `:grouped`, `:cluster-focused`,
`:row-hover`, `:side` and `:empty` for styling.

### Anatomy

1. **Title and subtitle** (`Title`, `Subtitle`, `SubtitleFormat`): a 16 px medium title and a 14 px muted line. Without a
   `Subtitle` the line reads "2,400 accounts. Dot size shows MRR, color shows health."; an empty string hides it.
2. **Grouping tabs** (`Groupings`, `AllText`): "All" and one tab per grouping on a muted 34 px track; a surface pill glides
   to the chosen tab. The row scrolls sideways when the container is narrower than its tabs.
3. **Legend** (`ShowLegend`, `SizeLegendText`): one colored dot per health state, a divider, and a small and a large muted
   dot for size. It sits right of the tabs when both fit and moves under them otherwise.
4. **Stage**: the dots on the surface color. In the overview the disc is squashed to 68% of its height and front dots are
   drawn up to 12% larger, so it reads as a disc tilted toward you.
5. **Cluster labels**: the cluster's name over its MRR (rolling) and number of accounts, 10 px above each cluster.
6. **Card** (`AccountTooltipTemplate`): the account's name, its grouping values, MRR, owner, health and note, beside the
   pointer or pinned next to the selected dot.
7. **Gesture hint** (`ShowHint`, `HintText`): a muted line in the stage's lower left corner. It fades out while a cluster
   is focused or a list row is hovered.
8. **Zoom bar** (`ShowZoomControls`): zoom out, zoom in and fit, 12 px from the lower right corner. Fit is dimmed while
   the view already shows everything.
9. **"Show all"** (`ShowAllText`): a pill in the upper left corner while a cluster is focused.
10. **Totals panel** (`ShowTotals`, `TotalsPlacement`): the scope's name, the large MRR, the accounts, growing and at-risk
    subtotals, and the list of clusters with its MRR / Accounts switch.

### Accounts

Add `GalaxyAccount` objects inline in `Items`, or set `ItemsSource` to a list; when the list is an observable collection,
the galaxy follows its changes. The selection and the focused cluster survive a change when their account and cluster
still exist. When you change an account in place, call `Refresh()`.

- `Id` is the account's stable key; the selection matches by it. `Name` is shown on the card and announced.
- `Mrr` sets the dot's area: its radius is `0.30 + 0.028 × √MRR` px at the fitted zoom, at least 0.74 px.
- `Health` is the key of one of the `HealthStates`; accounts with an unknown key draw with the neutral state.
- `Groups` holds the account's value for each grouping, by the grouping's key (`["plan"] = "business"`).
- `Owner` and `Note` fill the card; `Tag` is yours.

```csharp
var account = new GalaxyAccount
{
    Id = "acct-0042",
    Name = "Juniper Labs",
    Mrr = 18_400,
    Health = "growing",
    Owner = "Rhea Ingram",
    Note = "Upgrade call booked"
};
account.Groups["plan"] = "business";
account.Groups["region"] = "harbor";
accounts.Add(account);
```

### Groupings

Each `GalaxyGrouping` adds a tab. Its `Key` names the `Groups` entry it reads; the key `health` groups by `Health` and
takes its clusters, labels and colors from `HealthStates`. List `GalaxyGroupDefinition`s to give the values labels and a
fixed order for ties; values the accounts carry that are not listed are added after them, and accounts without a value
form an "Other" cluster (`OtherText`). `Header` is the tab text and `ListTitle` the list's title ("By plan" is built from
`ListTitleFormat` when it is not set).

`SelectedGroupingKey` is two-way: null shows the overview. When it changes, every dot springs from where it is to its slot
in the new layout and the camera fits the new layout; the labels fade in 120 ms later. Clusters are packed largest
account first, the largest cluster in the middle and the others around it by MRR (left, right, lower left, upper right,
upper left …), with room for their labels. The overview's list is by health; choosing one of its rows switches to the
health grouping and flies into that cluster.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.CustomerGalaxyClustersDemo">
    <!-- Opens grouped by industry, the list ordered by number of accounts. -->
    <arc:CustomerGalaxy x:Name="Galaxy"
                        Title="Accounts by industry"
                        SelectedGroupingKey="industry"
                        GroupSort="Accounts" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class CustomerGalaxyClustersDemo : UserControl
{
    public CustomerGalaxyClustersDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        foreach (var grouping in CustomerGalaxyDemoData.Groupings())
        {
            Galaxy.Groupings.Add(grouping);
        }
        Galaxy.ItemsSource = CustomerGalaxyDemoData.Accounts;
    }
}
```

### Health states

`HealthStates` holds four states by default, in legend order: Growing (`Success`), Steady (`TextMuted` at 72%), Cooling
(`Warning`) and At risk (`Danger`). Each state names the ArcDesign color it draws with in `Tone` (or a fixed `Color`),
how strongly its dots and bar segments are drawn (`DotOpacity`, `BarOpacity`), and its paint order (`Layer`: steady dots
first, at-risk dots on top). The state with `IsGrowth` gives the "growing" subtotal and the one with `IsRisk` the "at risk"
subtotal and every cluster's risk share. The colors are read from the theme again on every theme or accent change.

```csharp
galaxy.HealthStates.Clear();
galaxy.HealthStates.Add(new GalaxyHealthState { Key = "expanding", Label = "Expanding", Tone = GalaxyTone.Success, Layer = 1, IsGrowth = true });
galaxy.HealthStates.Add(new GalaxyHealthState { Key = "stable", Label = "Stable", Tone = GalaxyTone.Neutral, DotOpacity = 0.72, BarOpacity = 0.5 });
galaxy.HealthStates.Add(new GalaxyHealthState { Key = "churning", Label = "Churning", Tone = GalaxyTone.Danger, Layer = 2, IsRisk = true });
```

### Focusing a cluster and selecting an account

Double-click a cluster (or its label), choose its row in the list, press ← or →, or set `FocusedGroupKey` to fly into it:
the cluster, its 10 px gap and its label fill three quarters of the stage height, every other cluster fades to a seventh of
its opacity and its label to 30%, "Show all" appears, and the panel switches to the cluster's numbers. `FlyToGroup(key)`,
`FocusNextGroup()` and `FocusPreviousGroup()` do the same from code, and `GroupFocused` reports every change.
`ResetView()`, "Show all", Fit, 0 and Home return to every cluster.

Hover a dot to see its card beside the pointer; click it to select it (`SelectedAccount`, two-way, and `AccountSelected`).
The selected dot keeps a ring and its card stays open: beside the pointer while the pointer is on the stage, pinned 12 px
right of the dot when the pointer leaves. A click on empty space or Escape clears the selection. ↓ and ↑ (or
`SelectNextAccount()` and `SelectPreviousAccount()`) step through the focused cluster's accounts from the largest down;
`FlyToAccount(account)` selects an account and zooms to it.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.CustomerGalaxyFocusedClusterDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12">
        <!-- The Corporate cluster is focused and its largest account selected; Escape steps back. -->
        <arc:CustomerGalaxy x:Name="Galaxy"
                            SelectedGroupingKey="plan"
                            FocusedGroupKey="corporate" />
        <TextBlock x:Name="Status" Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class CustomerGalaxyFocusedClusterDemo : UserControl
{
    public CustomerGalaxyFocusedClusterDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        foreach (var grouping in CustomerGalaxyDemoData.Groupings())
        {
            Galaxy.Groupings.Add(grouping);
        }
        var accounts = CustomerGalaxyDemoData.Accounts;
        Galaxy.ItemsSource = accounts;
        // The largest Corporate account (the accounts are sorted by MRR).
        Galaxy.SelectedAccount = accounts.First(a => a.Groups["plan"] == "corporate");
        Galaxy.GroupFocused += (_, e) => Show(e.Group is { } group ? $"Focused: {group.Label}" : "Showing every cluster");
        Galaxy.AccountSelected += (_, e) => Show(e.Account is { } account ? $"Selected: {account.Name}" : "No account selected");
        Show($"Focused: Corporate · Selected: {Galaxy.SelectedAccount?.Name}");
    }

    private void Show(string text) => Status.Text = text;
}
```

```csharp
galaxy.GroupFocused += (_, e) =>
{
    // e.Group is null when the view returned to every cluster.
    status.Text = e.Group is { } group ? $"{group.Label}: {group.AccountCount} accounts" : "All clusters";
};
```

### Camera

Drag to pan: the stage follows the pointer 1:1 and stretches with a rubber band past the content's edge, then springs
back; there is no glide. The mouse wheel zooms by 1.246 per notch about the pointer; trackpad scrolling still scrolls the
page, and Ctrl or ⌘ with the wheel or a pinch zooms too. The zoom buttons and the + and − keys zoom by `ZoomStep` (1.6)
about the center. The view never zooms out past the fitted view and never in past `MaxZoom` (9) times it. After a wheel
zoom the view waits 1.1 s before it slides back inside the content. `ZoomBy(factor, anchor)` zooms from code and `Zoom`
reports the current zoom (1 = fitted).

### Totals and the list

The panel names its scope ("All accounts", or the focused cluster), shows the MRR in large rolling digits and three
subtotals: accounts, growing MRR and at-risk MRR. The list has one row per cluster (per health state in the overview):
the name, the value, a 4 px bar and a caption. With `GroupSort` set to `Mrr` the rows are ordered and their bars measured
by MRR, and the caption counts the accounts; with `Accounts` they are ordered and measured by the number of accounts and
the caption shows the MRR. Outside the health grouping the caption adds the share of the cluster's MRR at risk, and the
bar is split into one segment per health state. Hovering a row dims every other cluster without moving the camera;
choosing it flies into the cluster. `Summary` exposes the same numbers for your own text.

### Layout and container width

The layout follows the control's own width, not the window's:

| Control width | Totals | Stage height |
|---|---|---|
| 880 px and wider | Beside the stage, 288 px wide | 16:9 of the stage's width, at most 560, at least the panel's height |
| 620 to 880 px | Under the stage, in two columns | `max(360, width × 0.52)` |
| Under 620 px | Under the stage, in one column | 380 |

`TotalsPlacement` set to `End` keeps the panel beside the stage at any width, and `Bottom` keeps it under the stage.
The fitted zoom follows the stage size, so a wide stage draws a larger galaxy; labels keep their size.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.CustomerGalaxySidePanelDemo">
    <!-- From 880 px the totals sit beside the stage on their own; End keeps them there in any width. -->
    <arc:CustomerGalaxy x:Name="Galaxy"
                        Title="Customer health"
                        TotalsPlacement="End"
                        SelectedGroupingKey="health" />
</UserControl>
```
