### Your own data

Any customer list works: workspaces, stores, practices. Bring your own groupings, health states and wording, and format
amounts with `CurrencySymbol` and `CultureName`, or with your own `MrrFormatter`.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.CustomerGalaxyYourDataDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="12">
        <!-- Your own accounts, groupings, health states and wording; amounts in euros. -->
        <arc:CustomerGalaxy x:Name="Galaxy"
                            Title="Workspace subscriptions"
                            Subtitle="Every workspace on a paid tier, sized by monthly revenue."
                            CurrencySymbol="€"
                            AllText="Everything"
                            AllAccountsText="All workspaces"
                            AccountCountFormat="{}{0} workspaces"
                            OneAccountFormat="{}{0} workspace"
                            SizeLegendText="Size is revenue"
                            ShowHint="False">
            <arc:GalaxyGrouping Key="tier" Header="Tier">
                <arc:GalaxyGroupDefinition Key="hobby" Label="Hobby" />
                <arc:GalaxyGroupDefinition Key="pro" Label="Pro" />
                <arc:GalaxyGroupDefinition Key="scale" Label="Scale" />
            </arc:GalaxyGrouping>
            <arc:GalaxyGrouping Key="cloud" Header="Hosting" ListTitle="By hosting" />
            <arc:GalaxyGrouping Key="health" Header="Status" />
        </arc:CustomerGalaxy>
        <TextBlock x:Name="Log" Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" Text="Click a dot to select a workspace." />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class CustomerGalaxyYourDataDemo : UserControl
{
    private static readonly string[] Clouds = ["Fjord Cloud", "Basalt Hosting", "Own servers"];
    private static readonly string[] Teams = ["Atlas", "Beacon", "Cinder", "Delta", "Ember", "Flint", "Grove", "Harbor"];

    public CustomerGalaxyYourDataDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        // Three states of your own instead of the four defaults.
        Galaxy.HealthStates.Clear();
        Galaxy.HealthStates.Add(new GalaxyHealthState { Key = "expanding", Label = "Expanding", Tone = GalaxyTone.Success, Layer = 1, IsGrowth = true });
        Galaxy.HealthStates.Add(new GalaxyHealthState { Key = "stable", Label = "Stable", Tone = GalaxyTone.Neutral, DotOpacity = 0.72, BarOpacity = 0.5 });
        Galaxy.HealthStates.Add(new GalaxyHealthState { Key = "churning", Label = "Churning", Tone = GalaxyTone.Danger, Layer = 2, IsRisk = true });
        Galaxy.ItemsSource = CreateWorkspaces();
        Galaxy.AccountSelected += (_, e) => Log.Text = e.Account is { } account
            ? $"{account.Name}: {account.Mrr:N0} € a month, {account.Owner}"
            : "Click a dot to select a workspace.";
    }

    /// <summary>420 invented workspaces from a fixed seed.</summary>
    private static List<GalaxyAccount> CreateWorkspaces()
    {
        var random = new Random(42);
        var list = new List<GalaxyAccount>();
        for (var i = 0; i < 420; i++)
        {
            var roll = random.NextDouble();
            var (tier, mrr) = roll < 0.6 ? ("hobby", 9 + random.Next(0, 40))
                : roll < 0.92 ? ("pro", 120 + random.Next(0, 900))
                : ("scale", 2_000 + random.Next(0, 14_000));
            var health = random.NextDouble() switch { < 0.12 => "expanding", < 0.9 => "stable", _ => "churning" };
            var team = Teams[random.Next(Teams.Length)];
            var account = new GalaxyAccount
            {
                Id = $"ws-{i:D3}",
                Name = $"{team} workspace {i + 1}",
                Mrr = mrr,
                Health = health,
                Owner = tier == "scale" ? "Account team" : "Self-serve",
                Note = health == "churning" ? "Seats removed last week" : null
            };
            account.Groups["tier"] = tier;
            account.Groups["cloud"] = Clouds[random.Next(Clouds.Length)];
            list.Add(account);
        }
        return list;
    }
}
```

```xml
<arc:CustomerGalaxy CurrencySymbol="€"
                    AllAccountsText="All workspaces"
                    AccountCountFormat="{}{0} workspaces"
                    OneAccountFormat="{}{0} workspace"
                    SizeLegendText="Size is revenue"
                    ShowHint="False" />
```

### Texts

Every text has an English default and a property to change it. Formats use `{0}` for the value they name.

| Property | Default | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| `SubtitleFormat` | "{0} accounts. Dot size shows MRR, color shows health." | The subtitle when `Subtitle` is null |
| `AllText` | "All" | The overview tab |
| `AllAccountsText` | "All accounts" | The panel's scope when no cluster is focused |
| `MrrCaptionText` | "Monthly recurring revenue" | The caption over the large number |
| `MrrText` | "MRR" | The sort button and the card's first row |
| `AccountsText` | "Accounts" | The subtotal and the sort button |
| `OwnerText` | "Owner" | The card's owner row |
| `HealthText` | "Health" | The card's health row |
| `ListTitleFormat` | "By {0}" | The list title; `{0}` is the grouping in lower case |
| `HealthGroupingText` | "Health" | The health grouping's name (overview list, announcements) |
| `AccountCountFormat` | "{0} accounts" | Account counts |
| `OneAccountFormat` | "{0} account" | One account |
| `AtRiskShareFormat` | "{0} at risk" | The risk share in a row's caption |
| `HintText` | "Drag to move · scroll to zoom · double-click a cluster to open it" | The gesture hint |
| `ShowAllText` | "Show all" | The pill that returns from a cluster |
| `ZoomInText`, `ZoomOutText`, `FitText` | "Zoom in", "Zoom out", "Show every account" | The zoom buttons' names |
| `SizeLegendText` | "Size shows MRR" | The legend's size entry |
| `GroupByText` | "Group accounts by" | The tabs' name |
| `SortByText` | "Order the list by" | The MRR / Accounts switch's name |
| `OtherText` | "Other" | The cluster of accounts without a value |
| `EmptyText` | "No accounts to show" | The stage without accounts |
| `FlyToClusterText`, `GroupAndFlyFormat` | "Fly to this cluster", "Group by {0} and fly to this cluster" | A row's action for screen readers |
| `KeyboardHelpText`, `StageSummaryFormat`, `OverviewLayoutText`, `GroupedLayoutFormat` | (sentences) | The stage's screen-reader name and help |
| `GroupAnnouncementFormat`, `AccountAnnouncementFormat`, `GroupingAnnouncementFormat`, `OverviewAnnouncementText` | (sentences) | Live announcements |

### Data shape and performance

- The control reads `Id`, `Name`, `Mrr`, `Health`, `Owner`, `Note` and the `Groups` of each account when the data
  changes, and works on its own copy in flat arrays; a frame of the turning galaxy allocates nothing.
- 2,400 dots draw in about 3 ms per frame in the headless Skia test host on a development laptop, and moving a grouping
  or the camera costs a fraction of a millisecond more. Expect several times that in a browser (WebAssembly); keep the
  data to a few thousand accounts there.
- Only dots inside the stage are drawn, so a zoomed-in view draws few.
- The stage asks for frames only while something moves. It stops when the pointer rests on it, when it leaves the screen,
  and at reduced motion, where the galaxy is one still picture.

## API reference

### CustomerGalaxy

A customer galaxy: every account a dot, its area by monthly recurring revenue and its color by health, slowly turning as a tilted two-armed spiral. Group the accounts by any dimension and the dots spring into one packed cluster per value, labelled with its MRR and size; pan, zoom about the pointer, double-click a cluster to fly into it, hover a dot for its card and click it to select it. A totals panel beside the stage (under it in narrow containers) shows the MRR, accounts, growing and at-risk MRR of everything or of the focused cluster, and a list of the clusters by MRR or by accounts whose rows fly to their cluster.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ItemsSource` | `IEnumerable<GalaxyAccount>?` | `null` | The accounts to draw; when null the inline `Items` are used. Collection changes are followed. |
| `SelectedGroupingKey` | `string?` | `null` | The key of the shown grouping, or null for the overview of all accounts (two-way). Changing it regroups the dots. |
| `FocusedGroupKey` | `string?` | `null` | The key of the focused cluster, or null (two-way): the camera flies into it and the other clusters dim. |
| `SelectedAccount` | `GalaxyAccount?` | `null` | The selected account, or null (two-way): it keeps a ring and its card stays open. Setting it does not move the camera. |
| `GroupSort` | `GalaxyGroupSort` | `Mrr` | How the totals list is ordered and measured (two-way). Default `Mrr`. |
| `Title` | `string?` | `null` | The title above the grouping tabs; hidden when null. |
| `Subtitle` | `string?` | `null` | The line under the title; when null it is built from `SubtitleFormat`; an empty string hides it. |
| `SubtitleFormat` | `string` | `"{0} accounts. Dot size shows MRR, color shows health."` | The automatic subtitle; `{0}` is the number of accounts. |
| `IsAutoRotate` | `bool` | `true` | Whether the overview and the clusters turn slowly (1.6°/s). Off at reduced motion. |
| `RotationSpeed` | `double` | `1.6` | The turning speed in degrees per second (default 1.6, one turn in about 224 s). |
| `ZoomStep` | `double` | `1.6` | The zoom factor of the zoom buttons and the + / − keys (default 1.6). |
| `WheelZoomSensitivity` | `double` | `0.0022` | Wheel zoom per web pixel of scroll: one notch zooms by `exp(100 × value)` (default 0.0022, ×1.246). |
| `MaxZoom` | `double` | `9` | The largest zoom relative to the fitted view (default 9); the smallest is always the fitted view. |
| `TotalsPlacement` | `GalaxyTotalsPlacement` | `Auto` | Where the totals panel goes (default `Auto`: beside the stage from 880 px). |
| `ShowLegend` | `bool` | `true` | Shows the legend of health colors and dot size. Default true. |
| `ShowTotals` | `bool` | `true` | Shows the totals panel. Default true. |
| `ShowHint` | `bool` | `true` | Shows the gesture hint in the stage's corner. Default true. |
| `ShowZoomControls` | `bool` | `true` | Shows the zoom buttons. Default true. |
| `CurrencySymbol` | `string` | `"$"` | Currency symbol of the amounts (default "$"). |
| `CultureName` | `string` | `"en-US"` | Culture of the numbers (default "en-US"). |
| `MrrFormatter` | `Func<double, string>?` | `null` | Formats every amount in place of the compact currency ($6.05M, $870K, $990). |
| `AccountTooltipTemplate` | `IDataTemplate?` | `null` | Replaces the built-in account card; its data is the `GalaxyAccount`. |
| `AllText` | `string` | `"All"` | The overview tab (default "All"). |
| `AllAccountsText` | `string` | `"All accounts"` | The totals' scope name when no cluster is focused (default "All accounts"). |
| `MrrCaptionText` | `string` | `"Monthly recurring revenue"` | The caption over the large MRR number (default "Monthly recurring revenue"). |
| `MrrText` | `string` | `"MRR"` | "MRR": the sort button and the card's first row. |
| `AccountsText` | `string` | `"Accounts"` | "Accounts": the subtotal and the sort button. |
| `OwnerText` | `string` | `"Owner"` | The card's owner row (default "Owner"). |
| `HealthText` | `string` | `"Health"` | The card's health row (default "Health"). |
| `ListTitleFormat` | `string` | `"By {0}"` | The list title of a grouping without its own `ListTitle`; `{0}` is the header in lower case ("By {0}"). |
| `HealthGroupingText` | `string` | `"Health"` | The name of health as a grouping when no health grouping is listed: the overview's list title (default "Health"). |
| `AccountCountFormat` | `string` | `"{0} accounts"` | A number of accounts ("{0} accounts"). |
| `OneAccountFormat` | `string` | `"{0} account"` | One account ("{0} account"). |
| `AtRiskShareFormat` | `string` | `"{0} at risk"` | The risk share after a row's count; `{0}` is the percentage ("{0} at risk"). |
| `HintText` | `string` | `"Drag to move · scroll to zoom · double-click a cluster to open it"` | The gesture hint in the stage's corner. |
| `ShowAllText` | `string` | `"Show all"` | The pill that returns from a focused cluster (default "Show all"). |
| `ZoomInText` | `string` | `"Zoom in"` | Screen-reader name of the + button (default "Zoom in"). |
| `ZoomOutText` | `string` | `"Zoom out"` | Screen-reader name of the − button (default "Zoom out"). |
| `FitText` | `string` | `"Show every account"` | Screen-reader name of the fit button (default "Show every account"). |
| `SizeLegendText` | `string` | `"Size shows MRR"` | The legend's size entry (default "Size shows MRR"). |
| `GroupByText` | `string` | `"Group accounts by"` | Screen-reader name of the grouping tabs (default "Group accounts by"). |
| `SortByText` | `string` | `"Order the list by"` | Screen-reader name of the MRR / Accounts switch (default "Order the list by"). |
| `OtherText` | `string` | `"Other"` | The cluster of accounts without a value for the grouping (default "Other"). |
| `EmptyText` | `string` | `"No accounts to show"` | Shown in the stage when there are no accounts (default "No accounts to show"). |
| `KeyboardHelpText` | `string` | `"Left and right arrows fly between clusters, up and down arrows step through the accounts of a cluster, plus and minus zoom, Escape goes back."` | The stage's keyboard help for screen readers. |
| `StageSummaryFormat` | `string` | `"Customer galaxy of {0} accounts and {1} in monthly recurring revenue, {2}. Dot size shows MRR, color shows health."` | The stage's screen-reader summary: `{0}` accounts, `{1}` total MRR, `{2}` the layout (`OverviewLayoutText` or `GroupedLayoutFormat`). |
| `OverviewLayoutText` | `string` | `"in one spiral"` | The overview's layout in the summary (default "in one spiral"). |
| `GroupedLayoutFormat` | `string` | `"grouped by {0}"` | A grouping's layout in the summary; `{0}` is the grouping in lower case ("grouped by {0}"). |
| `GroupAnnouncementFormat` | `string` | `"{0}, {1}, {2} MRR, {3} at risk."` | Announced when a cluster is focused: `{0}` name, `{1}` accounts, `{2}` MRR, `{3}` MRR at risk. |
| `AccountAnnouncementFormat` | `string` | `"{0}, {1} MRR, {2}, owned by {3}. {4}"` | Announced when an account is selected with the keyboard: `{0}` name, `{1}` MRR, `{2}` health, `{3}` owner, `{4}` note. |
| `GroupingAnnouncementFormat` | `string` | `"{0} clusters by {1}. {2} is the largest with {3} MRR."` | Announced when a grouping is shown or the view resets: `{0}` clusters, `{1}` grouping in lower case, `{2}` largest cluster, `{3}` its MRR. |
| `OverviewAnnouncementText` | `string` | `"All accounts in one spiral."` | Announced when the overview is shown (default "All accounts in one spiral."). |
| `HoveredAccount` | `GalaxyAccount?` | – | *Read-only.* The account under the pointer, or null. |
| `Summary` | `GalaxySummary` | – | *Read-only.* The totals of all accounts, of every health state and of every cluster of the shown grouping. |
| `Zoom` | `double` | – | *Read-only.* The camera's zoom relative to the fitted view (1 = everything visible). |
| `FlyToClusterText` | `string` | `"Fly to this cluster"` | A list row's action for screen readers (default "Fly to this cluster"). |
| `GroupAndFlyFormat` | `string` | `"Group by {0} and fly to this cluster"` | A list row's action in the overview; `{0}` is the health grouping in lower case ("Group by {0} and fly to this cluster"). |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `AccountSelected` | `GalaxyAccountEventArgs` | An account was selected or the selection cleared. |
| `GroupFocused` | `GalaxyGroupEventArgs` | A cluster was focused, or the focus returned to every cluster. |
| `GroupingChanged` | `GalaxyGroupingChangedEventArgs` | The shown grouping changed. |

Pseudo-classes: `:grouped`, `:cluster-focused`, `:row-hover`, `:side`, `:empty`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

### GalaxyAccount

One customer account of a `CustomerGalaxy`: a dot whose area follows `Mrr` and whose color follows `Health`. The values the groupings read (plan, region, industry …) go into `Groups` under the grouping's `Key`.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Id` | `string?` | `null` | Stable id (selection and incremental updates match accounts by it); the name is used when it is empty. |
| `Name` | `string?` | `null` | The account's name, shown at the top of its card and announced when it is selected. |
| `Mrr` | `double` | `0` | Monthly recurring revenue; the dot's area grows with it and every total adds it up. |
| `Health` | `string?` | `null` | The `Key` of the account's health; it picks the dot color. |
| `Owner` | `string?` | `null` | Who owns the account ("Self-serve" for accounts without one); shown on the card. |
| `Note` | `string?` | `null` | One short line about the account, shown at the bottom of its card ("Renewal call booked"). |
| `Tag` | `object?` | `null` | Any value you want back from `AccountSelected`. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### GalaxyGrouping

One way to group the accounts of a `CustomerGalaxy` into clusters (a tab of its grouping switch): the accounts' `Groups` value under `Key` picks their cluster. The key `HealthKey` groups by `Health` and takes its clusters from `HealthStates`.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Key` | `string` | `""` | The `Groups` key this grouping reads ("plan", "region"), or `HealthKey`. |
| `Header` | `string?` | `null` | The tab text ("Plan"); `Key` when null. |
| `ListTitle` | `string?` | `null` | The title of the totals list while this grouping is shown ("By plan"); built from `ListTitleFormat` when null. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### GalaxyGroupDefinition

One cluster of a `GalaxyGrouping`: the account value it collects and the label it shows.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Key` | `string` | `""` | The `Groups` value of the accounts in this cluster ("business"). |
| `Label` | `string?` | `null` | The label above the cluster and in the totals list ("Business"); `Key` when null. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### GalaxyHealthState

A health state of a `CustomerGalaxy`: its key, legend label and color, how strongly its dots are drawn, and whether it counts as growth or risk in the totals.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Key` | `string` | `""` | The value of `Health` that selects this state ("at-risk"). |
| `Label` | `string?` | `null` | The legend, card and list label ("At risk"); `Key` when null. |
| `Tone` | `GalaxyTone` | `Neutral` | The ArcDesign color of its dots, legend dot and bar segments (default `Neutral`). |
| `Color` | `Color?` | `null` | A fixed color instead of `Tone` (it does not follow the theme). |
| `DotOpacity` | `double` | `0.95` | Opacity of its dots and legend dot (default 0.95; the neutral state 0.72). |
| `BarOpacity` | `double` | `1` | Opacity of its bar segments in the totals list (default 1; the neutral state 0.5). |
| `Layer` | `int` | `0` | Paint order: lower layers are drawn first, so higher ones sit on top (neutral 0, risk last). |
| `IsGrowth` | `bool` | `false` | Its MRR is the "growing" subtotal of the totals panel. |
| `IsRisk` | `bool` | `false` | Its MRR is the "at risk" subtotal and the risk share of every cluster. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

## Accessibility

- The stage is a focusable custom control described as an "interactive chart". Its name summarizes the view ("Customer
  galaxy of 2,400 accounts and $6.05M in monthly recurring revenue, grouped by plan …") and its help text lists the keys
  (`KeyboardHelpText`). The focus ring is 2 px outside the stage and shows only for keyboard focus.
- A hidden table stands in for the canvas: one row per cluster of the current grouping with its accounts, MRR and accounts
  per health state.
- A polite live region announces the focused cluster ("Corporate, 70 accounts, $2.80M MRR, $60K at risk.", with your
  numbers), an account chosen with the arrow keys, and a new grouping or reset ("4 clusters by plan. Corporate is the
  largest …").
- The grouping tabs are a tab list: only the chosen tab is a tab stop, and the arrow keys, Home and End move the choice.
  The MRR / Accounts buttons report whether they are pressed, and each list row is a button that reports whether its
  cluster is focused, with its name, MRR, accounts and risk share as its name and its action as help text.
- The zoom buttons are named; Fit is disabled and skipped by Tab while the view already shows everything.
- Rolling numbers are read once, with their final value.
- Colors are never the only signal: the card and the list name every health state, and the legend labels the colors.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Where | Action |
|---|---|---|
| `Tab` | Anywhere | Tabs, stage, "Show all", zoom buttons, MRR / Accounts, list rows |
| `ArrowLeft` / `ArrowRight` | Tabs | Choose the previous or next grouping (wrapping); `Home` / `End` the first or last |
| `ArrowRight` / `ArrowLeft` | Stage, grouped | Fly to the next or previous cluster by MRR (wrapping; the largest or smallest first) |
| `ArrowDown` / `ArrowUp` | Stage | Select the next or previous account by MRR in the focused cluster (in all accounts otherwise); the card pins beside it |
| `+`, `=` / `−` | Stage | Zoom in or out by 1.6 about the center |
| `0`, `Home` | Stage | Return to every cluster |
| `Escape` | Stage | Clear the selection; pressed again, return to every cluster |
| `Enter`, `Space` | Rows, buttons | Choose the row (fly to its cluster) or press the button |

## Motion

- The overview and every cluster turn clockwise at 1.6° per second (one turn in about 224 s), and every dot of the overview
  drifts a few pixels over a few minutes. While the pointer rests on the stage the turning eases to a stop (about 0.4 s)
  and the stage stops drawing; it picks up again when the pointer leaves.
- A grouping change springs every dot to its new slot: about 70% set off at once, the rest up to a third of a second later;
  each first wanders slowly, then spirals in, swelling slightly while it flies. Most dots arrive within a second. The
  camera fits the new layout on the same timing and the new labels rise into place 120 ms later.
- Flights into a cluster, "Show all" and Fit move the camera on a slow critical spring (about 1 s); wheel, button and key
  zooms on a quicker one (about 0.55 s), keeping the point under the pointer still. Drags follow the pointer exactly.
- Dimming fades the other clusters to a seventh in about a quarter of a second; a hovered dot grows to 1.84 times its size
  with a ring 3 px around it.
- The card fades in and grows from 96%; the numbers roll digit by digit, 26 ms apart from the left; the bars and their
  segments ease to their new widths; reordered rows slide to their places; the tab pill glides.
- Reduced motion draws one still galaxy: no turning, no drift, and every grouping change, flight, zoom, dimming and hover
  lands at once; the card and the labels only fade. Off applies every change at once.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| Overview and clusters turn, dots drift | 1.6°/s, eases out under a resting pointer | Still | Still |
| Grouping change | Each dot springs to its slot with a staggered start | Lands at once | Immediate |
| Flight into a cluster, "Show all", Fit | Critical spring, about 1 s | Lands at once | Immediate |
| Wheel, button or key zoom | Critical spring, about 0.55 s, anchored | Lands at once | Immediate |
| Drag past the edge, then release | Rubber band, springs back | Rubber band, lands inside | Rubber band, lands inside |
| Dimming other clusters | Fades in about 0.26 s, 7 steps | At once | Immediate |
| Hovered dot | Grows to 1.84× in about 0.4 s | At once | Immediate |
| Cluster labels | Rise 4 px and fade in after 120 ms; dim to 30% over 240 ms | Fade | Immediate |
| Card | Fades in and grows from 96% | Fades | Immediate |
| Numbers | Digits roll, 26 ms apart | Change at once | Immediate |
| Bars and segments | Ease to their widths (580 ms) | Change at once | Immediate |
| Rows reordered by the sort switch | Slide to their places (about 0.55 s) | Jump | Immediate |
| Tab pill | Glides on a snappy spring | Jumps | Immediate |
| Gesture hint | Fades out over 480 ms | Fades quickly | Immediate |

## Related

- `BarChart`, `DonutChart` and `Treemap` for a few exact values or parts of a whole.
- `DataGrid` and `Table` for reading and comparing accounts row by row.
- `MetricCard` and `AnimatedCounter` for one headline number.
- `SegmentedControl`, which the grouping tabs resemble.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `Treemap` | You want exact areas for parts of a whole, without the packing gaps |
| `BarChart` | A handful of categories are compared by one value |
| `DataGrid` | People need to read, sort and edit the accounts themselves |
| `MetricCard` | A dashboard tile shows one number and its change |
| `ActivityHeatmap` | Activity over days and hours matters more than who the customers are |

# Semantic zoom

> An organization map you zoom through from teams to projects to a single task, each level showing new detail, with breadcrumbs, a minimap, a guided tour and the numbers of whatever is in view.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc.Blocks`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc.Blocks --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/blocks/semantic-zoom

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.SemanticZoomPreviewDemo">
    <!-- An invented transit operator (SemanticZoomDemoData): 5 teams, 22 projects, about 150 tasks. -->
    <arc:SemanticZoom x:Name="Map" Header="Network map" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class SemanticZoomPreviewDemo : UserControl
{
    public SemanticZoomPreviewDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        // Seeded sample data, shared by the demos on this page: the same map on every run.
        Map.Organization = SemanticZoomDemoData.Shared;
    }
}
```

## When to use

`SemanticZoom` draws a whole organization as one map you can zoom into without losing your place. Teams are panels,
projects are cards inside them, tasks are blocks on the cards, and a task opens into its details and checklist. Each zoom
level shows different information rather than the same picture larger: at the overview you see the teams with their
progress and a gray chip per task (red when blocked); closer in, the team leads and counts, then project titles, health
and due dates, then task titles and due dates, and finally the task's summary, assignee and checklist. The breadcrumbs, the
details panel and the screen-reader text always describe whatever is under the center of the view, so the map tells you
where you are while you fly.

- **A portfolio overview** for a leadership meeting: start at the whole company, fly into the team that is behind, then
  into its off-track project, and read which tasks are blocked.
- **A workspace home page** where everyone sees the same map: the overview answers "how are we doing", the zoom answers
  "what is next for my project" without changing pages.
- **A status walk-through** with the guided tour: the map flies through a team, a project and two tasks on its own while
  someone presents.
- **An onboarding view** that shows a newcomer how the organization is built: who leads which team, which projects each
  team runs, who works on what.
- **A planning check-in** where people tick checklist items right on the map and watch the task, the project and the
  team's numbers update.

## When not to use

- **Browsing a deep hierarchy item by item.** Use `TreeView`; it shows any depth as rows and is faster to scan than a map.
- **Working through tasks.** Use a board or a task list; the map is for orientation, not for moving work.
- **Flat data clustered by an attribute.** Use `CustomerGalaxy`; semantic zoom needs a hierarchy of containers.
- **Exact comparisons across many projects.** Use `DataGrid` or `Table`; the map shows one node's numbers at a
  time.
- **A small card or a sidebar.** The map needs at least 400 px of height and room around it for the page to scroll (the
  wheel always zooms the map).

## Usage

Give the control an `Organization`: a tree of `SemanticZoomTeam`s, `SemanticZoomProject`s and `SemanticZoomTask`s. The
layout, the totals (open and blocked tasks, next due date, progress, people) and every label are derived from it, so you
only describe the work itself.

```xml
<arc:SemanticZoom Header="Network map">
    <arc:SemanticZoom.Resources>
        <arc:SemanticZoomPerson x:Key="Rustam" Name="Rustam Aliyev" Role="Fleet lead" />
        <arc:SemanticZoomPerson x:Key="Hana" Name="Hana Sato" Role="Charging specialist" />
    </arc:SemanticZoom.Resources>
    <arc:SemanticZoomOrganization Title="Harbor Line Transit">
        <arc:SemanticZoomTeam Title="Fleet" Description="Vehicles, charging and everything that wears out." Lead="{StaticResource Rustam}">
            <arc:SemanticZoomProject Title="Depot charging bays" Lead="{StaticResource Hana}" Health="AtRisk">
                <arc:SemanticZoomTask Title="Order chargers" Status="InProgress" Assignee="{StaticResource Hana}" Points="3">
                    <arc:SemanticZoomChecklistItem Text="Get three quotes" IsDone="True" />
                    <arc:SemanticZoomChecklistItem Text="Check the grid connection" />
                </arc:SemanticZoomTask>
            </arc:SemanticZoomProject>
        </arc:SemanticZoomTeam>
    </arc:SemanticZoomOrganization>
</arc:SemanticZoom>
```

`SemanticZoom` derives from Avalonia's `TemplatedControl`. The map is drawn by the control itself (one pass per frame, with
cached text and brushes, and nothing drawn while it rests); the breadcrumbs, the buttons, the hover card and the details
panel are ordinary controls. The control sets the pseudo-classes `:fit`, `:touring`, `:side-panel`, `:compact` and
`:interacted` for styling.

### Anatomy

1. **Heading** (`Header`, `Subtitle`, `SubtitleFormat`): a 16 px medium heading and a 13 px muted line. Without a
   `Subtitle` the line reads "5 teams, 22 projects, 151 tasks. Zoom in to see more."; an empty string hides it.
2. **Map**: team panels on a dot grid whose spacing repeats every fourfold zoom, so the background reads as depth.
3. **Breadcrumbs** (`IsBreadcrumbVisible`): every level above the current one is a button that flies back to it.
4. **Tour button** (`IsTourButtonVisible`): starts and stops the guided tour; only its icon in narrow containers.
5. **Hover card**: the name, a status or description line and four numbers of the team, project or task under the
   pointer (or the keyboard cursor).
6. **Minimap** (`IsMinimapVisible`): appears once you leave the overview; press or drag it to move the view.
7. **Hint** (`IsHintVisible`): a muted gesture hint that fades away after the first interaction.
8. **Zoom bar** (`IsZoomControlsVisible`): zoom out, the zoom readout, zoom in, and show everything (disabled while
   everything is in view).
9. **Details panel** (`DetailPanelPlacement`, also usable on its own as `SemanticZoomPanel`): the kind and name of the
   node in view, its open and blocked tasks and next due date, its progress, and its people.

### The data

| Type | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `SemanticZoomOrganization` | The root: `Title` and its `Teams` |
| `SemanticZoomTeam` | `Title`, `Description` (shown in its hover card), `Lead` and its `Projects` |
| `SemanticZoomProject` | `Title`, `Description` (used in generated task summaries), `Lead`, `Health`, `Due` and its `Tasks` |
| `SemanticZoomTask` | `Title`, `Status`, `Assignee`, `Reviewer`, `Due`, `Points`, `CommentCount`, `Summary` and its `Checklist` |
| `SemanticZoomChecklistItem` | `Text` and `IsDone` |
| `SemanticZoomPerson` | `Name`, `Role`, an optional `Avatar` picture and optional `Initials` |

Every node exposes its totals as read-only properties: `OpenTasks`, `BlockedTasks`, `DoneTasks`, `TaskCount`, `NextDue`
(the earliest due date of an open task), `Progress` (a task's share of ticked checklist items, 1 when done; projects, teams
and the organization average every task below them), `People` (leads first, then assignees, without repeats),
`ProjectCount` and `NeedAttention` (projects not on track). They update as soon as anything below them changes.

A task without a `Summary` gets one generated from its status, assignee, due date and project. People without an
`Avatar` show their initials on a muted circle.

### Moving around

Scroll or pinch to zoom about the pointer (1× shows everything, up to 53× by default, `MaxZoom`), drag to pan (the view
glides on after a flick and springs back from the edges), and click a team, project or task to fly into it. A click on the
node you are already in, or one of its ancestors, does nothing; the next click goes one level deeper or sideways. Flights
first ease out a little and then in, and take longer the farther they go.

The current node (`Scope`, two-way) is not a separate selection: it is always the deepest node under the center of the
view that the zoom allows (teams from 1.1×, projects from 2.4×, tasks from 18×). Set `Scope` or call `FlyTo` to fly
somewhere; `FlyOut`, `ResetView` and `ZoomBy` cover the rest. `ScopeChanged` fires during flights and pans too, with
`IsUserInitiated` telling a person's input apart from code and the tour.

### Ticking checklist items

Zoomed far into a task, its checklist appears; click an item, or move the keyboard cursor onto it and press Enter, to tick
or untick it. Ticking the last open item marks the task done; unticking an item of a done task puts it back in review.
The task's block, its project's card, the team and the details panel all update at once, with the numbers rolling to their
new values. `ChecklistItemToggled` reports every change.

### The guided tour

The tour button (or `ToggleTourCommand`, `StartTour`, `IsTourPlaying`) flies through a sequence of stops and waits
`TourDwell` (1.5 s) at each. By default it visits the first team, one of its projects, two tasks of its next project, a
second team and one of its projects, and returns to the whole map. Set `TourStops` for your own route; the organization as
a stop means everything. Any manual input stops the tour where it is.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.SemanticZoomGuidedTourDemo">
    <!-- Your own tour stops and buttons outside the map: commands, the scope and the zoom readout are bindable. -->
    <StackPanel Spacing="12">
        <StackPanel Orientation="Horizontal" Spacing="8">
            <arc:Button Content="Play the tour" Command="{Binding #Map.ToggleTourCommand}" />
            <arc:Button x:Name="FleetButton" Variant="Secondary" Content="Go to Fleet" />
            <arc:Button Variant="Ghost" Content="Show everything" Command="{Binding #Map.ResetViewCommand}" />
            <TextBlock VerticalAlignment="Center" Text="{Binding #Map.ZoomText}" />
        </StackPanel>
        <arc:SemanticZoom x:Name="Map"
                          Header="Network map"
                          TourDwell="0:0:2"
                          IsTourButtonVisible="False"
                          DetailPanelPlacement="None" />
        <TextBlock x:Name="Status" Text="Showing the whole organization." />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Collections;
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class SemanticZoomGuidedTourDemo : UserControl
{
    public SemanticZoomGuidedTourDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        var org = SemanticZoomDemoData.Shared;
        Map.Organization = org;
        // Every team in turn, then the whole map.
        var stops = new AvaloniaList<SemanticZoomNode>();
        stops.AddRange(org.Teams);
        stops.Add(org);
        Map.TourStops = stops;
        FleetButton.CommandParameter = org.Teams[1];
        FleetButton.Command = Map.FlyToCommand;
        Map.ScopeChanged += (_, e) => Status.Text = e.NewScope is { } node ? $"Showing {node.Title}." : string.Empty;
    }
}
```

### Layout and container width

The map is 48% of the control's width high, between 400 and 580 px (or `StageHeight`). Above 900 px inside, the details
panel moves beside the map (264 px); under it otherwise, in two columns. In containers narrower than 600 px the map is 420
px high, the tour button shows only its icon, the minimap shrinks, the hint moves above the zoom bar and the panel uses one
column. The layout of the map itself never changes with the width: narrow containers show it smaller.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.SemanticZoomSidePanelDemo">
    <!-- The details panel beside the map (Auto does this by itself above 900 px inside); a fixed 460 px map. -->
    <arc:SemanticZoom x:Name="Map"
                      Header="Network map"
                      DetailPanelPlacement="Side"
                      StageHeight="460"
                      MinWidth="760" />
</UserControl>
```

### Your own data

The whole tree can be written in XAML, as here, or built in code and assigned to `Organization`. Teams are packed into
rows that share one card height, and each row is stretched to the widest one, so any mix of team sizes stays tidy.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.SemanticZoomYourDataDemo">
    <UserControl.Resources>
        <arc:SemanticZoomPerson x:Key="Ada" Name="Ada Moreno" Role="Head chef" />
        <arc:SemanticZoomPerson x:Key="Bo" Name="Bo Lindgren" Role="Pastry chef" />
        <arc:SemanticZoomPerson x:Key="Cyd" Name="Cyd Okonkwo" Role="Front of house" />
    </UserControl.Resources>
    <!-- The whole map written in XAML: teams hold projects, projects hold tasks, tasks hold checklist items. -->
    <arc:SemanticZoom Header="Spring menu launch" StageHeight="400">
        <arc:SemanticZoomOrganization Title="Little Fig Bistro">
            <arc:SemanticZoomTeam Title="Kitchen" Description="Recipes, suppliers and the line." Lead="{StaticResource Ada}">
                <arc:SemanticZoomProject Title="New menu" Lead="{StaticResource Ada}" Health="AtRisk" Due="2026-10-30">
                    <arc:SemanticZoomTask Title="Test the soups" Status="Done" Assignee="{StaticResource Ada}" Due="2026-09-12" Points="3">
                        <arc:SemanticZoomChecklistItem Text="Leek and potato" IsDone="True" />

                    </arc:SemanticZoomTask>
                    <arc:SemanticZoomTask Title="Price the mains" Status="InProgress" Assignee="{StaticResource Ada}" Due="2026-10-08" Points="2">
                        <arc:SemanticZoomChecklistItem Text="Supplier quotes" IsDone="True" />
                        <arc:SemanticZoomChecklistItem Text="Portion sizes" />

                    <arc:SemanticZoomTask Title="Find a cheese supplier" Status="Blocked" Assignee="{StaticResource Bo}" Due="2026-10-02" Points="1"
                                          Summary="Blocked: the dairy has stopped deliveries for a month. Bo is asking two others." />

                <arc:SemanticZoomProject Title="Desserts" Lead="{StaticResource Bo}" Due="2026-10-20">
```

### Texts and formats

Every label, button name and announcement is in `Texts` (`SemanticZoomTexts`, English defaults): kinds and panel labels,
status and health names, the lines drawn on the map, the generated summaries, the hover card rows, the tour and zoom
button names, the hint, and the screen-reader announcements. Assign a new instance to change them. Dates ("Sep 23") and
percentages ("59%") come from `Formatter` (`ISemanticZoomFormatter`; `SemanticZoomFormatter` has a `Culture`).

## API reference

### SemanticZoom

An organization map you can zoom into without losing your place: teams hold project cards, projects hold task blocks, tasks open into their details and checklist. Each zoom level shows different information (team leads and counts, then project titles and health, then task titles and due dates, then the task's summary, assignee and checklist), not the same picture larger. Scroll or pinch to zoom about the pointer, drag to pan, click anything to fly into it; the breadcrumbs, the details panel and the screen-reader text follow whatever is under the center of the view. A minimap, zoom buttons and a guided tour sit on the map; ticking a checklist item updates the task and every total above it.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Organization` | `SemanticZoomOrganization?` | `null` | The organization to map: its teams, their projects and tasks. |
| `Header` | `object?` | `null` | The heading above the map; hidden when null. |
| `Subtitle` | `string?` | `null` | The line under the heading; when null it is built from `SubtitleFormat`; an empty string hides it. |
| `SubtitleFormat` | `string` | `"{0} teams, {1} projects, {2} tasks. Zoom in to see more."` | The automatic subtitle: `{0}` teams, `{1}` projects, `{2}` tasks. |
| `Scope` | `SemanticZoomNode?` | `null` | The node in view (two-way): the organization, a team, a project or a task. It follows the camera (whatever is under the center at the current zoom); setting it flies there. |
| `ScopePath` | `IReadOnlyList<SemanticZoomNode>` | – | *Read-only.* The chain from the organization down to `Scope` (what the breadcrumbs show). |
| `Zoom` | `double` | – | *Read-only.* The zoom relative to the whole organization in view (1 = fit). |
| `ZoomText` | `string` | – | *Read-only.* The zoom as the readout shows it: one decimal under 10 ("1.6×"), whole numbers above ("31×"). |
| `MaxZoom` | `double` | `53.04` | The largest zoom (default 53, deep enough to read a task's checklist); the smallest is always 1. |
| `CursorNode` | `SemanticZoomNode?` | – | *Read-only.* The node under the keyboard cursor (null when there is none, or when the cursor is on a checklist item). |
| `IsTourPlaying` | `bool` | `false` | Whether the tour is playing (two-way). Any manual interaction with the map stops it. |
| `TourStops` | `AvaloniaList<SemanticZoomNode>?` | `null` | The tour's stops in order; the organization as a stop means the whole map. When null the tour visits a team, one of its projects, two tasks, a second team and one of its projects, then returns to the whole map. |
| `TourDwell` | `TimeSpan` | `00:00:01.5000000` | How long the tour waits at each stop after arriving (default 1.5 s; 2.4 s at reduced motion). |
| `DetailPanelPlacement` | `SemanticZoomPanelPlacement` | `Auto` | Where the details panel goes (default `Auto`). |
| `StageHeight` | `double?` | `null` | The map's height in px; when null it is 48% of the control's width between 400 and 580 (420 in containers narrower than 600 px). |
| `IsBreadcrumbVisible` | `bool` | `true` | Shows the breadcrumbs in the map's top-left corner. Default true. |
| `IsTourButtonVisible` | `bool` | `true` | Shows the tour button in the map's top-right corner. Default true. |
| `IsMinimapVisible` | `bool` | `true` | Shows the minimap (bottom left) once the view leaves the whole organization. Default true. |
| `IsZoomControlsVisible` | `bool` | `true` | Shows the zoom buttons and readout (bottom right). Default true. |
| `IsHintVisible` | `bool` | `true` | Shows the gesture hint until the first interaction. Default true. |
| `Texts` | `SemanticZoomTexts` | – | Every label, button name and announcement (English defaults); assign a new instance to change wording. |
| `Formatter` | `ISemanticZoomFormatter?` | `null` | Formats dates and percentages; null uses `Default` ("Sep 23", "59%"). |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ScopeChanged` | `SemanticZoomScopeChangedEventArgs` | Raised when the node in view changes (camera flights, pans and zooms included). |
| `NodeInvoked` | `SemanticZoomNodeEventArgs` | Raised when a node is clicked or chosen with Enter (the camera then flies into it). |
| `ChecklistItemToggled` | `SemanticZoomChecklistEventArgs` | Raised when a checklist item is ticked or unticked on the map. |
| `TourStarted` | `RoutedEventArgs` | Raised when the tour starts. |
| `TourStopped` | `SemanticZoomTourStoppedEventArgs` | Raised when the tour stops, at its end or interrupted. |

Pseudo-classes: `:fit`, `:touring`, `:side-panel`, `:compact`, `:interacted`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

### SemanticZoomPanel

The key numbers of one node of a `SemanticZoom` map: its kind and name, open and blocked tasks and the next due date, progress as a large percentage with a bar, and the people involved as an avatar stack with a closing note. Numbers roll digit by digit when `Scope` or its totals change. `SemanticZoom` shows one beside or under its map; use it on its own by binding `Scope`.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Scope` | `SemanticZoomNode?` | `null` | The node whose numbers are shown (the organization, a team, a project or a task). |
| `Layout` | `SemanticZoomPanelLayout` | `Grid` | Two columns (under a wide map) or one (beside a map, or in narrow containers). Default two. |
| `Texts` | `SemanticZoomTexts?` | `null` | Labels and notes (English defaults). |
| `Formatter` | `ISemanticZoomFormatter?` | `null` | Formats the next due date and the percentage; null uses `Default`. |

Pseudo-classes: `:stack`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

### SemanticZoomOrganization

The root of a `SemanticZoom` map: the organization and its teams.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Key` | `string?` | `null` | An optional identifier for your own bookkeeping. |
| `Title` | `string` | `""` | The name shown on the map, in breadcrumbs and in the panel. |
| `Description` | `string?` | `null` | A one-line description (teams: shown in the hover card; projects: used in generated task summaries). |
| `Parent` | `SemanticZoomNode?` | – | *Read-only.* The node above this one (null for the organization or a node not added anywhere yet). |
| `TaskCount` | `int` | – | *Read-only.* Tasks below this node (a task counts itself). |
| `OpenTasks` | `int` | – | *Read-only.* Tasks below this node whose status is not done. |
| `DoneTasks` | `int` | – | *Read-only.* Tasks below this node that are done. |
| `BlockedTasks` | `int` | – | *Read-only.* Tasks below this node that are blocked. |
| `NextDue` | `DateOnly?` | – | *Read-only.* The earliest due date among the open tasks below this node (null when none is due). |
| `Progress` | `double` | – | *Read-only.* Completion from 0 to 1: a task's share of ticked checklist items (1 when done); a project, team or the organization averages every task below it. |
| `People` | `IReadOnlyList<SemanticZoomPerson>` | – | *Read-only.* Everyone involved, without repeats: leads first, then the assignees of the tasks below. |
| `NeedAttention` | `int` | – | *Read-only.* Projects below this node that are not on track (teams and the organization). |
| `ProjectCount` | `int` | – | *Read-only.* Projects below this node (a project counts itself). |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### SemanticZoomTask

A task: a block on its project's card, and when zoomed in, a card with its status, summary, assignee and checklist. Ticking the last open checklist item marks the task `Done`; unticking an item of a done task puts it back `InReview`. Set `Status` yourself at any time.

| `People` | `IReadOnlyList<SemanticZoomPerson>` | – | *Read-only.* Everyone involved, without repeats: leads first, then the assignees of the tasks below. |
| `NeedAttention` | `int` | – | *Read-only.* Projects below this node that are not on track (teams and the organization). |
| `ProjectCount` | `int` | – | *Read-only.* Projects below this node (a project counts itself). |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### SemanticZoomChecklistItem

One line of a task's checklist. Ticking every item marks the task done; unticking one of a done task puts it back in review (`SemanticZoomTask`).

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Text` | `string` | `""` | What has to be done. |
| `IsDone` | `bool` | `false` | The item is ticked (two-way). |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### SemanticZoomPerson

A person on a `SemanticZoom` map: a team or project lead, or a task's assignee or reviewer. Without an `Avatar` the map draws a muted circle with the person's initials.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Name` | `string` | `""` | The person's full name. |
| `Role` | `string?` | `null` | Job title, shown under the name in a task's details. |
| `Avatar` | `IImage?` | `null` | A picture drawn in a circle; null draws the initials instead. |
| `Initials` | `string?` | `null` | Initials for the fallback circle; null takes the first letters of the first two words of `Name`. |

## Accessibility

- The map is one focusable element with the role "zoomable map". Its name sums up the organization and the node in view
  ("Map of Harbor Line Transit: 5 teams, 22 projects, 151 tasks. Showing Fleet. …"), and its help text lists the keys.
- A polite live region announces the node in view once the camera settles ("Now showing Fleet team: 5 projects, 31 open
  tasks, 52% done."), the item under the keyboard cursor, ticked and unticked checklist items with the task's new count
  and status, and the tour starting and stopping.
- A hidden table lists every project with its team, health, progress, open and blocked tasks and due date, so a screen
  reader can read the whole portfolio without zooming.
- The breadcrumbs are a named group of buttons; the tour button reports whether it is pressed; the zoom buttons are named
  and the fit button is disabled and skipped by Tab while everything is in view; the panel is a named group and its
  avatar stack is named with everyone's names.
- Rolling numbers are read once, with their final value. Health and status never rely on color alone: the hover card and
  the map name them in text.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Where | Action |
|---|---|---|
| `Tab` | Anywhere | Map, breadcrumbs, tour button, zoom buttons |
| `ArrowLeft` / `ArrowRight` / `ArrowUp` / `ArrowDown` | Map | Move the cursor to the nearest item that way among the current node's children and siblings (in a task, its checklist items); the first press picks the first child |
| `Enter`, `Space` | Map | Fly into the cursor's item, or tick the checklist item under it |
| `Escape` | Map | Stop the tour; clear the cursor; pressed again, zoom out one level |
| `Backspace` | Map | Zoom out one level |
| `+`, `=` / `−` | Map | Zoom in or out by 1.5 about the center |
| `0`, `Home` | Map | Show the whole organization |

## Motion

- Flights follow a smooth zoom-and-pan path (zoom out a little, travel, zoom in) on an ease-in-out curve, in
  460 ms plus 380 ms per unit of path length: about 0.6 s into a team, 1.1 s from a project into a task.
- Wheel, pinch, button and key zooms follow a critically damped spring (about 0.2 s to settle) and keep the point under
  the pointer still. Zooming past the limits stretches a little and springs back; dragging past the edges stretches and
  springs back on release; a flick glides on and slows down over about a second.
- Every level of detail fades in over a window of on-screen size, and eases over about 140 ms when the zoom jumps. Nodes
  outside the one in view dim (teams to 42%, neighbouring projects and tasks to 50%); hover outlines fade in about 0.1 s.
- The hover card fades in and grows from 96%; the minimap rises in when you leave the overview; the hint fades out after
  the first interaction; breadcrumbs fade in (240 ms) and out (120 ms); the panel's name cross-fades and its numbers roll
  digit by digit; the progress bar eases to its new width; new avatars fade in.
- The tour waits 1.5 s at each stop. At reduced motion the camera jumps to every stop instead and each stop lasts 2.4 s.
- Reduced motion lands every flight, zoom, glide, dimming and fade at once and drops the interface transitions; Off does
  the same. Checklist ticks and the totals update at every level.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| Flight to a node, back, fit | Zoom-and-pan path, 460 + 380·S ms | Lands at once | Immediate |
| Wheel, pinch, button or key zoom | Spring, about 0.2 s, anchored | Lands at once | Immediate |
| Drag past the edge, then release | Rubber band, springs back | Rubber band, lands inside | Rubber band, lands inside |
| Flick | Glides on (τ ≈ 0.27 s) | Stops | Stops |
| Level of detail | Fades by on-screen size, eased over 140 ms | By on-screen size | By on-screen size |
| Dimming and hover outline | Eased (140 ms / 90 ms) | At once | Immediate |
| Hover card | Fades in, grows from 96% | Fades | Immediate |
| Minimap | Fades in, rises 6 px | Appears | Immediate |
| Breadcrumbs | Fade in 240 ms, out 120 ms | Change at once | Immediate |
| Panel numbers and bar | Digits roll, bar eases (580 ms) | Change at once | Immediate |
| Tour | Flies, 1.5 s at each stop | Jumps, 2.4 s at each stop | Jumps, 2.4 s at each stop |

## Related

- `TreeView` for browsing any hierarchy as rows.
- `CustomerGalaxy` for flat data grouped into clusters by an attribute.
- `DataGrid` and `Table` for comparing projects side by side.
- `Breadcrumb` for a path outside a map.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `TreeView` | People expand and collapse a deep hierarchy to find one item |
| `CustomerGalaxy` | Thousands of items are grouped by an attribute, not nested |
| `DataGrid` | People need to read, sort and edit the projects themselves |
| `MetricCard` | A dashboard tile shows one number and its change |

# Layout morph

> One set of cards in six views, from a grid and a list to a fanned stack, a 3D ring and a helix, with every card flying to its new place.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc.Blocks`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc.Blocks --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/blocks/layout-morph

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.LayoutMorphPreviewDemo">
    <!-- 14 desk pieces and 10 designers; the cards and their pictures come from LayoutMorphDemoData. -->
    <arc:LayoutMorph x:Name="Morph"
                     Title="One shelf, six ways to look"
                     Lede="The Harbor Lane spring edit: 14 desk pieces from 10 designers. Choose a view and every card glides to its new spot."
                     DefaultPanelTitle="Spring edit" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class LayoutMorphPreviewDemo : UserControl
{
    public LayoutMorphPreviewDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        var items = LayoutMorphDemoData.CreateItems();
        Morph.Items.AddRange(items);
        Morph.DefaultStats.AddRange(LayoutMorphDemoData.CreateTotals(items));
    }
}
```

## When to use

`LayoutMorph` shows one collection of cards, such as products, people or projects, and lets the reader choose how to look
at it. The same cards can be a grid, a masonry wall, a list, a fanned stack, a 3D carousel or a helix. When the view
changes, every card flies from where it is to its new place on its own spring, starting near the option that was chosen
and spreading outward, so the reader can follow a card through the change. Pointing at a card lifts it and shows its
figures in the panel under the stage; selecting a card turns it into a detail with a picture, a description, facts and one
action.

- **A shop's collection page or a lookbook.** A grid scans quickly, the list puts the maker and the price beside each
  name, and the carousel shows the pictures large. The detail's button ("Add to bag") keeps its state while the reader
  keeps browsing.
- **A team or speaker page.** The carousel and the helix turn through the portraits one at a time, and the panel shows the
  person in front without any pointing.
- **A portfolio or a case-study index.** The masonry view keeps each picture's own proportions, and the stack makes a
  small set feel like a hand of cards.

## When not to use

- **Long or growing collections.** Every card is a live element that moves on every view change; the block is designed for
  about 10 to 40 cards. Use a virtualized list, `DataGrid` or a paged grid for hundreds of items.
- **Data people compare.** Use a table when readers sort, filter or compare values across many rows; the list view here
  shows one value per row and cannot be sorted.
- **A single fixed view.** If only one view makes sense for your content, use a plain grid or `Carousel` and skip the
  view switch.
- **Navigation.** Cards open an in-place detail, not a page. Use links or a list of cards when choosing an item should
  take the reader somewhere else.

## Usage

### Items

Each `LayoutMorphItem` is a card. `Title` is the name everywhere; `Subtitle` is the line under it in the grid, the
carousel, the floating tag and the panel; `Meta` is the second line of a list row and of the detail; `Value` sits on the
right of a list row and of the carousel caption. An item with an `Image` shows it cropped to fill; an item without one shows
a cover with its title at the top and its value at the bottom, set in a size that follows the card. `AspectRatio` (height
over width) shapes the masonry view.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:LayoutMorph Title="Studio shelf" DefaultPanelTitle="Shelf">
        <arc:LayoutMorphItem Key="ink-tray"
                             Title="Ink pen tray"
                             Subtitle="By Yuki Aoyama"
                             Meta="Yuki Aoyama · Blackened steel"
                             Value="$36"
                             AspectRatio="0.9"
                             Description="A shallow tray for pens and a clip or two, folded from one sheet.">
            <arc:LayoutMorphItem.Facts>
                <arc:LayoutMorphFact Label="Price" Value="$36" />
                <arc:LayoutMorphFact Label="Size" Value="24 × 8 cm" />
            </arc:LayoutMorphItem.Facts>
            <arc:LayoutMorphItem.Stats>
                <arc:LayoutMorphFact Label="Price" Value="$36" />
                <arc:LayoutMorphFact Label="In stock" Value="31" />
                <arc:LayoutMorphFact Label="Rating" Value="4.8" />
            </arc:LayoutMorphItem.Stats>
        </arc:LayoutMorphItem>
        <arc:LayoutMorphItem Key="yuki-aoyama"
                             Title="Yuki Aoyama"
                             Subtitle="Metalsmith, Osaka"
                             Meta="Metalsmith in Osaka"
                             Value="2 pieces"
                             ActionText="Follow"
                             ActiveActionText="Following" />
    </arc:LayoutMorph>
</UserControl>
```

Give every item a `Key`: when you rebuild the collection, cards whose key stays keep their place, their focus and their state.
Use `ItemsSource` for a collection you own; an `ObservableCollection` is observed, and added or removed cards move the
others to their new places.

### Views

`Layout` is the current view and is two-way, so a control outside the block can drive it. `Layouts` chooses which views the
switch offers and in which order; the arrow keys on a card step through the same list. `SetLayout` changes the view from
code and can name the point the stagger starts from.

- **Grid**: wide containers show eight captioned cards per row; narrower ones show square cards in six, five or four
  columns, whichever gives the largest cards.
- **Masonry**: columns of cards in their own proportions; when the tallest column does not fit, every card shrinks by the
  same amount, so the masonry view never scrolls.
- **List**: one to three columns of rows with a thumbnail, two lines and the value. A list taller than the stage scrolls
  with the wheel or a vertical drag.
- **Stack**: a fan of cards; the card under the pointer slides up out of the fan.
- **Carousel**: large cards round a ring, from the first card to the last. Drag or swipe and it settles on the nearest card;
  a flick turns several cards. It does not wrap round: a drag past the first or last card stretches and springs back. A
  horizontal wheel (or Shift and the wheel) nudges it. Selecting a card beside the front turns it to the front; selecting
  the front card opens it.
- **Helix**: a spiral of ten cards per turn, tilted toward the reader. Dragging spins it and moves along the spiral, so the
  card in front stays in the middle.

The carousel and the helix remember where they were when you come back to them. `FrontItem` is the card in front.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.LayoutMorphCatalogueDemo">
    <!-- Your own items through ItemsSource; Layout bound to a switch outside the block; the bag counts saved pieces. -->
    <StackPanel Spacing="16">
        <StackPanel Orientation="Horizontal" Spacing="16">
            <arc:SegmentedControl SelectedValue="{Binding #Morph.Layout, Mode=TwoWay}">
                <arc:SegmentedOption Value="{x:Static arc:LayoutMorphMode.Grid}" Label="Grid" />
                <arc:SegmentedOption Value="{x:Static arc:LayoutMorphMode.List}" Label="List" />
                <arc:SegmentedOption Value="{x:Static arc:LayoutMorphMode.Carousel}" Label="Carousel" />
            </arc:SegmentedControl>
            <TextBlock x:Name="Bag"
                       Text="Your bag is empty"
                       VerticalAlignment="Center"
                       FontSize="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TypeSM}"
                       Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}" />
        </StackPanel>
        <arc:LayoutMorph x:Name="Morph"
                         StageHeight="520"
                         DefaultPanelTitle="Desk pieces"
                         DefaultPanelSubtitle="Point at a piece for its price and stock" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using System.Collections.ObjectModel;
using System.Globalization;
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class LayoutMorphCatalogueDemo : UserControl
{
    public LayoutMorphCatalogueDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        var pieces = new ObservableCollection<LayoutMorphItem>(LayoutMorphDemoData.CreatePieces());
        Morph.Layouts = [LayoutMorphMode.Grid, LayoutMorphMode.List, LayoutMorphMode.Carousel];
        Morph.ItemsSource = pieces;
        Morph.DefaultStats.Add(new LayoutMorphFact("Pieces", pieces.Count.ToString(CultureInfo.InvariantCulture)));
        Morph.DefaultStats.Add(new LayoutMorphFact("From", "$26"));
        Morph.DefaultStats.Add(new LayoutMorphFact("Ships in", "1–14 days"));
        // IsActive flips before ItemActionInvoked: count what is in the bag now.
        Morph.ItemActionInvoked += (_, _) =>
        {
            var saved = pieces.Count(p => p.IsActive);
            Bag.Text = saved == 0 ? "Your bag is empty" : saved == 1 ? "1 piece in your bag" : saved + " pieces in your bag";
        };
    }
}
```

### The panel and the detail

The panel under the stage names the card the reader points at, focuses, has in front or has opened, with its three `Stats`;
otherwise it shows `DefaultPanelTitle`, `DefaultPanelSubtitle` and `DefaultStats`. Values such as "$1,240", "4.8" or
"2 days" roll digit by digit; set `NumericValue` when a value's text is not a plain number.

Selecting a card raises `ItemInvoked` (set `Handled` to stop it), runs `OpenCommand` and opens the detail: the card itself
grows into a dialog while the others fade back. `OpenVariant="Hero"` gives a wide card with a large picture for products
with a photo; `Profile` gives a small picture beside the text. The detail's button flips `IsActive` and shows
`ActiveActionText`; it raises `ItemActionInvoked` and runs `ActionCommand`. Set `OpenedItem` to open a card from code and
null to close it, or call `Open` and `Close`.

```csharp
morph.ItemActionInvoked += (_, e) =>
{
    if (e.Item.IsActive)
    {
        bag.Add(e.Item.Key);
    }
    else
    {
        bag.Remove(e.Item.Key);
    }
};
```

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.LayoutMorphTeamDemo">
    <!-- A team page: only people, three views, the carousel first, with its own words. -->
    <arc:LayoutMorph x:Name="Morph"
                     Layout="Carousel"
                     Title="The people behind the shelf"
                     Lede="Ten designers, from Pune to Bergen. Turn the ring to meet each of them."
                     DefaultPanelTitle="Designers"
                     DefaultPanelSubtitle="Turn the ring or point at a portrait"
                     ViewLabel="Team view"
                     CarouselLabel="Ring"
                     CarouselHint="Drag the ring; it stops on a face"
                     HelixHint="Flick the spiral to browse the team"
                     GridHint="Select a portrait to read more" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using System.Globalization;
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class LayoutMorphTeamDemo : UserControl
{
    public LayoutMorphTeamDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        Morph.Layouts = [LayoutMorphMode.Carousel, LayoutMorphMode.Helix, LayoutMorphMode.Grid];
        var people = LayoutMorphDemoData.CreateDesigners();
        Morph.Items.AddRange(people);
        var orders = people.Sum(p => int.Parse(p.Stats[1].Value, NumberStyles.AllowThousands, CultureInfo.InvariantCulture));
        Morph.DefaultStats.Add(new LayoutMorphFact("Designers", people.Count.ToString(CultureInfo.InvariantCulture)));
        Morph.DefaultStats.Add(new LayoutMorphFact("Orders", orders.ToString("#,0", CultureInfo.InvariantCulture)));
        Morph.DefaultStats.Add(new LayoutMorphFact("Cities", people.Count.ToString(CultureInfo.InvariantCulture)));
    }
}
```

### Framed or flat

`IsFramed` (the default) draws the stage and the panel as bordered, rounded surfaces, for a block that sits among other
content. Set it to false when the block fills a page or a full-screen view; the cards then float on the page. `Title` and
`Lede` are optional: leave them out to place your own heading. `IsPanelVisible` and `IsHintVisible` hide the panel and
the hint.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.LayoutMorphFlatDemo">
    <!-- Laid flat on the page: no frame around the stage or the panel, no heading, starting in the masonry view. -->
    <arc:LayoutMorph x:Name="Morph"
                     IsFramed="False"
                     Layout="Masonry"
                     DefaultPanelTitle="Spring edit" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class LayoutMorphFlatDemo : UserControl
{
    public LayoutMorphFlatDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        var items = LayoutMorphDemoData.CreateItems();
        Morph.Items.AddRange(items);
        Morph.DefaultStats.AddRange(LayoutMorphDemoData.CreateTotals(items));
    }
}
```

### Narrow containers

The block reads its own width, not the window's. Below 720 the view switch shows icons only, stretched across the width,
with the names as tooltips; the hint moves under the switch, the panel puts the name above the statistics and the detail
stacks its picture over the text. Below 520 the cards use tighter spacing and the masonry view uses four columns. The
stage is 600 high, 540 at 720 and below, 500 below 480 and 460 below 360; `StageHeight` sets your own.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.LayoutMorphNarrowDemo">
    <!-- Below 720 the switch shows icons only and the hint moves under it; below 520 the cards tighten up. -->
    <arc:LayoutMorph x:Name="Morph"
                     Width="380"
                     HorizontalAlignment="Center"
                     Title="One shelf, six ways"
                     Lede="Fourteen desk pieces and the ten designers behind them."
                     DefaultPanelTitle="Spring edit" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

{

    {
        InitializeComponent();
        var items = LayoutMorphDemoData.CreateItems();
        Morph.Items.AddRange(items);
        Morph.DefaultStats.AddRange(LayoutMorphDemoData.CreateTotals(items));
    }
```
