
### Texts

Every text has an English default and a property: the view names (`GridLabel` … `HelixLabel`), the hints (`GridHint` …
`HelixHint`), the switch's name (`ViewLabel`), the panel's default lines, and the formats read to screen readers
(`StageLabelFormat`, `LayoutChangedFormat`, `OpenedFormat`, `CloseTextFormat`, `ActionOnFormat`, `ActionOffFormat`).

```xml
<arc:LayoutMorph Title="Ateliers"
                 ViewLabel="Vue de la galerie"
                 GridLabel="Grille"
                 GridHint="Choisissez une carte pour l’ouvrir"
                 DefaultPanelSubtitle="Survolez une carte"
                 CloseTextFormat="Fermer {0}"
                 OpenedFormat="{}{0} ouvert" />
```

### Data shape and performance

- Cards draw each bitmap picture from a copy made at the size it is shown on screen (rounded up in steps of 1.25), so a
  large picture costs the GPU little and does not shimmer when shown small; the open detail draws the picture itself. A
  copy is made once: to change a picture, set `Image` to a new image (a bitmap drawn into again keeps its old copy). Use
  pictures about twice the largest size they are shown at (the hero detail is about 600 by 550) and decode them once; the
  demos draw theirs in code from a seed.
- Cards are self-drawn and move by their transform only, so a view change runs no layout. Each card has its own springs, and
  the stage stops asking for frames as soon as everything is at rest; an idle block costs nothing.
- Keep the collection to a few dozen cards. The carousel shows about five cards at a time; the cards farther along wait out
  of sight on the back of the ring.

## API reference

### LayoutMorph

One collection of cards and six ways to look at it: a grid, a masonry wall, a list, a fanned stack, a 3D carousel and a helix. Switching the view flies every card to its new place on its own spring, starting from the option you chose and spreading outward; pointing at a card lifts it and shows it in the bottom panel, and selecting a card turns it into a detail with a picture, a description, facts and an action. The carousel and helix turn by dragging, flicking, the wheel or the keys and always settle on a card.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Items` | `AvaloniaList<LayoutMorphItem>` | `null` | The cards, in order. Use it in XAML; `ItemsSource` takes precedence when set. |
| `ItemsSource` | `IEnumerable?` | `null` | A collection of `LayoutMorphItem`s (observed when it raises collection changes); replaces `Items`. |
| `Layout` | `LayoutMorphMode` | `Grid` | The current layout; changing it flies the cards to the new one. |
| `Layouts` | `IList<LayoutMorphMode>?` | `null` | The layouts offered in the view switch, in this order; null offers all six. |
| `OpenedItem` | `LayoutMorphItem?` | `null` | The item shown as an open detail; set it to open one, null to close. |
| `FrontItem` | `LayoutMorphItem?` | – | *Read-only.* The card in front of the carousel or the helix (null in the flat layouts). |
| `Title` | `string?` | `null` | The large heading above the view switch; null leaves the heading out. |
| `Lede` | `string?` | `null` | The sentence under the heading; null leaves it out. |
| `ViewLabel` | `string` | `"Gallery view"` | The screen reader name of the view switch. |
| `GridLabel` | `string` | `"Grid"` | The name of the grid view. |
| `MasonryLabel` | `string` | `"Masonry"` | The name of the masonry view. |
| `ListLabel` | `string` | `"List"` | The name of the list view. |
| `StackLabel` | `string` | `"Stack"` | The name of the stack view. |
| `CarouselLabel` | `string` | `"Carousel"` | The name of the carousel view. |
| `HelixLabel` | `string` | `"Helix"` | The name of the helix view. |
| `GridHint` | `string` | `"Select a card to open it"` | The hint beside the view switch in the grid. |
| `MasonryHint` | `string` | `"Every card keeps its own shape"` | The hint in the masonry view. |
| `ListHint` | `string` | `"Maker and price on every row"` | The hint in the list view. |
| `StackHint` | `string` | `"Hover the fan to lift one card"` | The hint in the stack view. |
| `CarouselHint` | `string` | `"Drag or swipe, it lands on the closest card"` | The hint in the carousel view. |
| `HelixHint` | `string` | `"Drag to spin, flick to keep it turning"` | The hint in the helix view. |
| `DefaultPanelTitle` | `string?` | `null` | The panel's name while no card is pointed at, focused, in front or open; `Title` when null. |
| `DefaultPanelSubtitle` | `string?` | `"Point at a card for details"` | The line under the panel's default name. |
| `DefaultStats` | `AvaloniaList<LayoutMorphFact>` | `null` | The panel's three statistics while no card is described (the collection's totals). |
| `IsFramed` | `bool` | `true` | Draws the stage and the panel as bordered, rounded surfaces (true); false lays them flat on the page. |
| `IsPanelVisible` | `bool` | `true` | Shows the bottom panel with the described card and its statistics. |
| `IsHintVisible` | `bool` | `true` | Shows the hint beside (narrow: under) the view switch. |
| `StaggerDuration` | `TimeSpan` | `00:00:00.3300000` | How long after a view change the farthest card starts (the nearest starts almost at once); zero starts all together. |
| `StageHeight` | `double` | `NaN` | The stage height; NaN follows the width (600, 540 at 720 and below, 500 below 480, 460 below 360). |
| `CloseTextFormat` | `string` | `"Close {0}"` | The close button's name; {0} is the open item's title. |
| `OpenedFormat` | `string` | `"{0} opened"` | Announced when a card opens; {0} is its title. |
| `LayoutChangedFormat` | `string` | `"{0} view"` | Announced when the view changes; {0} is the view's name. |
| `ActionOnFormat` | `string` | `"{0}: {1}"` | Announced when the detail's button turns on; {0} is the title, {1} the button's new text. |
| `ActionOffFormat` | `string` | `"{0}: {1}"` | Announced when the detail's button turns off; {0} is the title, {1} the button's new text. |
| `StageLabelFormat` | `string` | `"{0} in {1} view: {2} cards. Left and right arrows change the view, up and down move between cards, Enter opens one."` | The stage's screen reader name: {0} the title, {1} the view, {2} the number of cards. |
| `OpenCommand` | `ICommand?` | `null` | Runs when a card is selected (parameter: its `LayoutMorphItem`), before it opens. |
| `ActionCommand` | `ICommand?` | `null` | Runs when the detail's button is pressed (parameter: the item, whose `IsActive` has just flipped). |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `LayoutChanged` | `LayoutMorphLayoutChangedEventArgs` | Raised when the view changes. |
| `ItemInvoked` | `LayoutMorphItemEventArgs` | Raised when a card is selected (click, Enter, Space); set Handled to keep it from opening. |
| `ItemOpened` | `LayoutMorphItemEventArgs` | Raised when a card has opened into its detail. |
| `ItemClosed` | `LayoutMorphItemEventArgs` | Raised when the open detail closes. |
| `ItemActionInvoked` | `LayoutMorphItemEventArgs` | Raised when the detail's button is pressed, after `IsActive` flipped. |

Pseudo-classes: `:narrow`, `:dense`, `:open`, `:dragging`, `:scroll`, `:framed`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

### LayoutMorphItem

One card of a `LayoutMorph`: a product, a person or any item with a title. Items with an `Image` show it; items without one show a cover with the title and the value. Every layout, caption, detail and panel statistic is derived from these properties.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Key` | `string?` | `null` | A stable identifier: the card, its focus and its state are kept when the collection is rebuilt. |
| `Title` | `string` | `""` | The name on the card, the floating tag, the detail and the bottom panel. |
| `Subtitle` | `string?` | `null` | The second line under the title in the grid, the tag, the carousel and the panel; `Meta` when null. |
| `Meta` | `string?` | `null` | The second line of a list row and of the detail ("Maker · material"). |
| `Value` | `string?` | `null` | The value on the right of a list row and a carousel caption, and on a cover ("$96", "2 pieces"). |
| `Image` | `IImage?` | `null` | The picture, drawn to fill (cropped to) every frame; null shows a cover with the title and the value. |
| `AspectRatio` | `double` | `1` | Height over width in the masonry layout (0.75 to 1.5 reads well); the other layouts ignore it. |
| `Description` | `string?` | `null` | One to three sentences in the opened detail (left out on narrow screens). |
| `Facts` | `AvaloniaList<LayoutMorphFact>` | `null` | Up to four facts at the foot of the detail (two on narrow screens). |
| `Stats` | `AvaloniaList<LayoutMorphFact>` | `null` | The three statistics the bottom panel shows while this card is pointed at, focused, in front or open. |
| `OpenVariant` | `LayoutMorphOpenVariant` | `Profile` | The shape of the opened detail: `Hero` for photos, `Profile` otherwise. |
| `ActionText` | `string` | `"Save"` | The detail's main button while `IsActive` is false ("Add to bag", "Follow"). |
| `ActiveActionText` | `string` | `"Saved"` | The detail's main button while `IsActive` is true ("Added to bag", "Following"). |
| `IsActive` | `bool` | `false` | The main button's pressed state (saved, followed); kept while the detail is closed and reopened. |
| `AutomationName` | `string?` | `null` | The card's screen reader name; "Title, Subtitle, Value" when null. |
| `Tag` | `object?` | `null` | Any object of yours (the record behind the card). |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### LayoutMorphFact

A label and a value: a fact in the detail or a statistic in the bottom panel.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Label` | `string` | `""` | The short label above the value ("Price", "In stock"). |
| `Value` | `string` | `""` | The value as shown ("$96", "1,386", "2 days"). Numbers with an optional prefix or suffix roll in the panel. |
| `NumericValue` | `double?` | `null` | The number behind `Value`, when it should roll digit by digit in the panel. When null, a `Value` such as "$1,240" or "4.8" is read as a number with its prefix and suffix kept. |
| `Decimals` | `int` | `0` | Decimals shown for `NumericValue` (ignored when the value is read from `Value`). |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

## Accessibility

- The view switch is a radio group named by `ViewLabel`. Only the chosen option is a tab stop; the arrow keys (wrapping), Home
  and End choose as they move. On narrow containers each icon keeps its name.
- The stage is a group named from `StageLabelFormat`: the title, the view, the number of cards and how to use the keys. Every
  card is a button named "Title, Subtitle, Value" (or `AutomationName`) and described by its meta, description and facts, so
  the same information as the hidden table of a web page is available card by card.
- Only one card is a tab stop. Up and Down move to the previous or next card in data order, Home and End to the first and the
  last, Enter or Space opens it, Left and Right switch to the previous or next view and keep the focus on the same card. In the
  carousel and the helix the focused card turns to the front, and the card in front is the tab stop; in a scrolling list the
  focused row scrolls into view.
- The open detail is a dialog named by the item's title and described by its description. Focus moves to the close button,
  named "Close" and the title, and Tab stays inside the dialog until it closes. Escape, the close button or a press on the stage
  outside the card closes it, and focus returns to the card.
- View changes, opened cards and the detail's button are announced politely ("Carousel view", "Halo floor lamp opened").
- The floating tag only repeats what the card's name says and is not read. The panel is plain text.

## Motion

- **View changes**: each card moves on its own spring (stiffness 100, damping 20, critically damped, about 1.15 seconds) from
  where it is to where it goes, size, corners and picture included. The card nearest the chosen option starts first, the
  farthest 330 ms later (`StaggerDuration`). While it flies a card lifts toward the reader (0.1 × the distance at its fastest)
  and leans into the motion. A card seen from behind (in the helix, or turning on its way out of the ring) shows only its
  base at 72%. Interrupting a change starts every card again from where it is, without a jump.
- **Captions**: the old caption fades out at once; the new one fades in once the card has nearly arrived, so two layouts never
  overlap. The hint and the panel's lines rise in over 240 ms; the panel's numbers roll.
- **Pointing**: the card lifts with a shadow on a quick spring (stiffness 500, damping 49); in the stack it slides out of the
  fan, in the helix it moves forward. In the masonry, stack and helix views a tag with the name floats above the card.
- **Carousel and helix**: the ring follows the pointer one to one and, on release, settles on the card the flick points at
  (stiffness 110, damping 19.5), keeping the release speed. Past the first or last card the drag meets rubber-band
  resistance and springs back. The helix tilts toward the reader and travels along the spiral as it turns.
- **Opening**: the card grows into the detail (stiffness 130, damping 26) while the stage recedes and the other cards fade to
  12%. The text fades in near the end, and the buttons 260 ms after the start.
- Reduced motion places every card at once and keeps only short fades (the detail's buttons, the tag). Off applies every
  change at once.

## Related

- `Carousel` for a single row of slides with pagination.
- `CardStack` for a swipeable pile of cards.
- `SegmentedControl` for a view switch outside the block.
- `RollingDigits` for the panel's rolling numbers.
- `ExplodedView` and `CustomerGalaxy`, the other 3D showpieces.

# Exploded view

> A screen that comes apart as you scroll: its layers tip back, separate with labels, take turns in focus with a caption each, and close into one screen again.

- Package: `TKCode.Arc.Blocks`, `dotnet add package TKCode.Arc.Blocks --version 0.3.2-preview.1`
- XAML namespace: `xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"`
- Live page: https://docs.tkcode.si/blocks/exploded-view

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ExplodedViewPreviewDemo">
    <arc:ExplodedView x:Name="View" Height="860" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class ExplodedViewPreviewDemo : UserControl
{
    public ExplodedViewPreviewDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        // Five layers of an invented running app, drawn with Arc parts (see ExplodedViewDemoData.cs).
        ExplodedViewDemoData.Fill(View);
    }
}
```

## When to use

`ExplodedView` is a section for a launch or marketing page that shows how a screen is built. A stack of equally sized
layers, one picture each, starts as one flat screen. As the reader scrolls, the stack tips back and turns, the layers
separate in depth and a label draws in beside each one. Then the layers take turns in focus: the others dim, the focused
one takes the accent and the caption under the stage explains it. At the end the layers close up and the screen stands up
again. A row of stop buttons jumps straight to the whole screen, to any layer, or to the screen put back together.

- **A design system or UI kit page**, where the layers are the tokens, the grid, the components and the overlays of one
  sample screen, and each caption says what that layer is responsible for.
- **A product launch**, walking through a redesigned screen from its background to its floating alerts, one claim per layer.
- **Hardware with a screen**, such as a watch or a car display, where the layers are the glass, the interface and the
  sensors behind them.
- **A case study**, showing how a team split a busy screen into calm layers with one job each.

## When not to use

- **Content people need to read or act on.** The stage is a picture: it takes no input and screen readers skip it (the
  layers are listed in text instead). Put real controls on the page itself.
- **A sequence of steps someone has to complete.** Use `Stepper` for progress through a task.
- **A set of slides or images to browse.** Use `Carousel`, which keeps one item in view and pages with buttons and swipes.
- **A long article with a few illustrations.** Scroll-driven sections ask for attention; one per page reads best.
- **More than eight layers.** The labels stack up on the right and the stops get crowded; split the story in two sections.

## Usage

Add one `ExplodedLayer` per layer, from the bottom up. Each layer's `Content` is any control, laid out at `LayerSize`
(280 × 620 by default, a phone screen). `Name` is the label's first line, the caption title and the stop button's name;
`Note` is the label's second line; `Body` is the caption shown while the layer is in focus. `StartCaption` and
`EndCaption` are the captions before the stack opens and after it closes.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc">
    <arc:ExplodedView Height="760"
                      Title="Made of layers"
                      Description="Every layer does one job, and together they stay quiet.">
        <arc:ExplodedView.StartCaption>
            <arc:ExplodedCaption Title="A single screen" Body="Scroll to lift it apart, layer by layer." />
        </arc:ExplodedView.StartCaption>
        <arc:ExplodedLayer Name="Base" Note="Two neutral tokens" Kind="Plate"
                           Body="One quiet base layer under everything else.">
            <Panel />
        </arc:ExplodedLayer>
        <arc:ExplodedLayer Name="Content" Note="Fixed-width numbers"
                           Body="The numbers, the chart and the list.">
            <TextBlock Margin="16,52" Text="38.6 km" FontSize="34" />
        </arc:ExplodedLayer>
    </arc:ExplodedView>
</UserControl>
```

`ExplodedView` derives from Avalonia's `TemplatedControl`. The scene is a function of `Progress`, from 0 (the whole
screen) to 1 (put back together), which follows the scroll position; `SmoothedProgress` is that value after a soft,
overdamped spring and is what the stage draws. `CurrentStop` is 0 for the whole screen, 1 to N for the layers and N + 1 for
the screen put back together, and `StopChanged` is raised whenever it changes. The control sets the pseudo-classes
`:exploded`, `:wide`, `:compact`, `:tall-stage`, `:framed` and `:region-focus` for styling.

### Anatomy

1. **Intro** (`Title`, `Description`): the title in the display face, from 28 to 52 px as the control widens, and one or two
   sentences under it.
2. **Stage**: the layers, drawn in perspective. A `Plate` layer is opaque with a 1 px border; a `Sheet` layer shows only
   its content and, while the stack is apart, a dashed outline; a `Grid` layer is a sheet whose content fades in with the
   separation, for guides that exist only in the exploded view. All layers share `LayerCornerRadius`.
3. **Labels**: one per layer on the right, a dot on the layer's right edge (`AnchorFromBottom` above its bottom), a 24 px
   leader, the name and the note. They draw in from the bottom layer up as the stack opens.
4. **Caption**: the current stop's title and body. Its area is as tall as the tallest caption, so the page never jumps.
5. **Stop buttons**: one 36 × 44 button per stop with a tick; the current tick is thicker and takes the accent.
6. **Frame** (`IsFramed`): a 1 px border, the surface radius and a muted fill. It is the scroll region in container mode.

### Scroll modes

`ScrollMode` decides where the progress comes from:

- `Container` (default): the control scrolls inside its own frame. The frame holds an empty track `Length` frames tall
  (4 by default) and the stage stays pinned while the track passes. Touch and the scroll keys scroll it natively and a
  wheel notch moves 100 px, as in a browser; at either end the frame keeps the wheel instead of scrolling the page. The
  frame's height comes from `Height`, or 88% of the window between 620 and 860 px.
- `Page`: the control is a track `Length` viewports tall inside the page's own `ScrollViewer`, and its stage stays pinned to
  the viewport while the track passes. Turn the frame off for this mode.
- `External`: nothing scrolls. Set `Progress` yourself, from a slider, a timeline or your own scroll position.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ExplodedViewPageScrollDemo">
    <!-- Page mode: the section is a tall track in the page's scroll viewer and its stage stays pinned while it passes. -->
    <Border Height="560"
            CornerRadius="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource RadiusSurface}"
            BorderThickness="1"
            BorderBrush="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Border}"
            ClipToBounds="True">
        <ScrollViewer x:Name="Page">
            <StackPanel>
                <TextBlock Margin="32,48,32,24"
                           TextWrapping="Wrap"
                           FontSize="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TypeLG}"
                           Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}"
                           Text="Stride Ledger keeps a calm record of every run. Scroll on: the next section takes its week page apart." />
                <arc:ExplodedView x:Name="View"
                                  ScrollMode="Page"
                                  IsFramed="False"
                                  Length="3" />
                <TextBlock Margin="32,24,32,64"
                           TextWrapping="Wrap"
                           FontSize="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TypeLG}"
                           Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextSecondary}"
                           Text="After the section the page simply scrolls on." />
            </StackPanel>
        </ScrollViewer>
    </Border>
</UserControl>
```

```cs

{
    public ExplodedViewPageScrollDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        ExplodedViewDemoData.Fill(View);
        View.Description = null;
    }
}
```

### Driving the progress

In external mode `Progress` is the only input; bind it or set it, and the stage follows on its spring. `GoToStop(n)`
glides to a stop in any mode, and `Reset()` returns to the whole screen. `GetStopName(n)` and `GetStopCaption(n)` give
the texts of a stop, for example to show them elsewhere on the page.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ExplodedViewSliderProgressDemo">
    <StackPanel Spacing="16">
        <arc:ExplodedView x:Name="View"
                          Height="640"
                          ScrollMode="External"
                          IsFramed="False" />
        <arc:Slider x:Name="Scrub"
                    Label="Progress"
                    Minimum="0"
                    Maximum="100"
                    Width="360"
                    HorizontalAlignment="Center" />
        <TextBlock x:Name="Status"
                   HorizontalAlignment="Center"
                   FontSize="12"
                   Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource TextMuted}" />
    </StackPanel>
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class ExplodedViewSliderProgressDemo : UserControl
{
    public ExplodedViewSliderProgressDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        ExplodedViewDemoData.Fill(View);
        View.Title = null;
        View.Description = null;
        // External mode: nothing scrolls; the slider drives Progress and the scene follows on its spring.
        Scrub.ValueChanged += (_, _) => View.Progress = Scrub.Value / 100;
        View.StopChanged += (_, e) => Show(e.Stop);
        Show(View.CurrentStop);
    }

    private void Show(int stop) =>
        Status.Text = $"Stop {stop} of {View.StopCount - 1}: {View.GetStopName(stop)}";
}
```

```csharp
view.StopChanged += (_, e) =>
{
    // e.Stop: 0 whole screen, 1..N a layer, N + 1 put back together. e.Layer is null at the ends.
    analytics.Track("exploded-stop", e.Stop);
};
```

### Your own layers

Layers are plain controls, so any picture works: a card, a dashboard, a device. Change `LayerSize` to their design size
and `LayerCornerRadius` to their corner. The fit keeps the exploded stack and its labels inside the stage at any size.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ExplodedViewCustomLayersDemo">

    <arc:ExplodedView Height="720"

                           Body="The plate the rest sits on: the page background and a quiet border."

        <arc:ExplodedLayer Name="Copy"

                                      Foreground="{arc:ArcDesignTokenResource Success}" />

                </StackPanel>

        <arc:ExplodedLayer Name="Action"
                           Note="One primary button"
                           Body="A single button at the bottom and the badge that marks the plan most teams pick."
```

### Narrow containers

The layout follows the control's own width, not the window's. From 880 px the intro and the caption sit in a 380 px column
beside a full-height stage. From 560 to 879 px the intro is on top and the caption sits beside the stop buttons. Below
560 px the stop buttons share one row above the caption, the labels show names only, and when the stage is taller than wide
the stack turns less and spreads further (`TallMaxTilt`, `TallMaxTurn`, `TallLayerGap`) so the labels still fit.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ExplodedViewNarrowDemo">
    <!-- Below 560 px: one column, stop buttons above the caption, labels without notes, and a tall stage turns less. -->
    <arc:ExplodedView x:Name="View"
                      Width="390"
                      Height="760"
                      HorizontalAlignment="Center" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class ExplodedViewNarrowDemo : UserControl
{
    public ExplodedViewNarrowDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        ExplodedViewDemoData.Fill(View);
    }
}
```

### Reduced motion

With reduced motion the stack does not tip or separate gradually: the two ends show the flat screen and every layer stop
shows the stack fully apart. Stops follow the scroll position at once, captions and colors switch without fading, and stop
buttons jump instead of gliding.

```xml
<UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
             xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
             xmlns:arc="https://github.com/AIDotNet/TKCode.Arc"
             x:Class="TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos.ExplodedViewReducedMotionDemo">
    <!-- Reduced motion: the flat screen at the two ends, the whole stack apart at every layer, nothing in between. -->
    <arc:ExplodedView x:Name="View"
                      Height="720"
                      arc:ArcMotion.Level="Reduced" />
</UserControl>
```

```cs
using Avalonia.Controls;

namespace TKCode.Arc.Gallery.Demos;

public partial class ExplodedViewReducedMotionDemo : UserControl
{
    public ExplodedViewReducedMotionDemo()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        ExplodedViewDemoData.Fill(View);
        View.Description = null;
    }
}
```

### Tuning the scene

`MaxTilt` (60°), `MaxTurn` (−40°) and `LayerGap` (136 px) set the fully exploded pose; `Perspective` (2400) sets how
strong the perspective is; `DimmedLayerOpacity` (0.5) sets how far the other layers fade while one is in focus. The
progress timeline is fixed: the stack tips over 0.04 to 0.22, separates over 0.08 to 0.28, the layer stops share 0.28 to
0.80 evenly, and the closing mirrors the opening.

## API reference

### ExplodedView

A scroll-driven teardown of a screen: a stack of equally sized layers, one picture per layer, that tips back and turns as you scroll, separates in depth while a label draws in beside each layer, focuses the layers one at a time (the others dim, the focused one takes the accent and the caption below changes), then closes and stands up again as one screen. A row of stop buttons jumps to the whole screen, each layer and the screen put back together. Use it on a launch or marketing page to show how an interface, a design system or a device is built.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Title` | `string?` | `null` | The section title above the stage; null shows none. |
| `Description` | `string?` | `null` | One or two sentences under the title; null shows none. |
| `StartCaption` | `ExplodedCaption?` | `null` | The caption of the first stop (the whole screen); null shows `AssembledText` alone. |
| `EndCaption` | `ExplodedCaption?` | `null` | The caption of the last stop (the screen put back together); null shows `ReassembledText` alone. |
| `LayerSize` | `Size` | `280, 620` | Design size of every layer (default 280 × 620); the layers' content is laid out at it. |
| `LayerCornerRadius` | `double` | `40` | Corner radius shared by the plate's border, the dashed outlines and the grid's clip (default 40). |
| `ScrollMode` | `ExplodedScrollMode` | `Container` | Where the progress comes from: its own frame (default), the page, or the host. |
| `Length` | `double` | `4` | Scroll distance in frames (container) or viewports (page): the track is this many times the visible height (default 4). |
| `Progress` | `double` | `0` | The raw progress, 0 (whole screen) to 1 (put back together), two-way. It follows the scroll position in container and page modes; setting it scrolls there. In external mode it is the only input. |
| `SmoothedProgress` | `double` | – | *Read-only.* The progress after the follow spring: what the scene shows (read-only). |
| `CurrentStop` | `int` | – | *Read-only.* The current stop: 0 the whole screen, 1..N the layers from the bottom up, N + 1 put back together (read-only). |
| `StopCount` | `int` | – | *Read-only.* The number of stops: the layers plus the two ends (read-only). |
| `MaxTilt` | `double` | `60` | How far the stack tips back when apart, in degrees (rotateX, default 60). |
| `MaxTurn` | `double` | `-40` | How far the stack turns when apart, in degrees (rotateZ, default −40). |
| `LayerGap` | `double` | `136` | Depth between neighbouring layers when fully apart, in layer pixels (default 136). |
| `TallMaxTilt` | `double` | `62` | `MaxTilt` while `:tall-stage` (compact, stage taller than wide; default 62). |
| `TallMaxTurn` | `double` | `-20` | `MaxTurn` while `:tall-stage` (default −20). |
| `TallLayerGap` | `double` | `150` | `LayerGap` while `:tall-stage` (default 150). |
| `Perspective` | `double` | `2400` | Perspective distance in layer pixels (default 2400; smaller is a stronger perspective). |
| `DimmedLayerOpacity` | `double` | `0.5` | Opacity of the layers that are not focused while one is (default 0.5). |
| `IsFramed` | `bool` | `true` | Draws the rounded frame (1px border, surface radius, muted fill). Turn it off for a full-page or page-scroll section. |
| `StopsLabel` | `string` | `"Go to a layer"` | Accessible name of the stop button row. |
| `AssembledText` | `string` | `"Whole screen"` | Name of the first stop (and its caption title when `StartCaption` is null). |
| `ReassembledText` | `string` | `"Back together"` | Name of the last stop (and its caption title when `EndCaption` is null). |
| `RegionLabelFormat` | `string` | `"{0}. Scroll to take it apart, one layer at a time."` | Accessible name of the scroll frame; {0} is the title. |
| `LayerListLabel` | `string` | `"Layers, from the bottom up"` | Accessible name of the hidden list of layers ("name: body", bottom to top). |
| `CurrentStopText` | `string` | `"Current step"` | Status read out on the current stop button. |

| Event | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `StopChanged` | `ExplodedStopChangedEventArgs` | Raised when the shown stop changes (the smoothed progress crosses a stop boundary; the raw one under reduced motion). |

Pseudo-classes: `:exploded`, `:wide`, `:compact`, `:tall-stage`, `:framed`, `:region-focus`

Derives from `TemplatedControl`: every member of `TemplatedControl` works as well.

### ExplodedLayer

One layer of an `ExplodedView`, from the bottom up: its picture (`Content`, drawn at `LayerSize`), the label beside it (`Name` and `Note`) and the caption shown while it is focused (`Name` and `Body`).

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Name` | `string?` | `null` | The layer's name: the first line of its label, the caption title and the name of its stop button. |
| `Note` | `string?` | `null` | A short note under the name in the label ("4 columns, 8pt steps"); hidden below 560 px. |
| `Body` | `string?` | `null` | One or two sentences shown in the caption while the layer is focused. |
| `Content` | `object?` | `null` | The layer's picture: any control, laid out at the view's `LayerSize`. |
| `ContentTemplate` | `IDataTemplate?` | `null` | Template for a `Content` that is data rather than a control. |
| `Kind` | `ExplodedLayerKind` | `Sheet` | How the layer is drawn: a transparent sheet (default), an opaque plate, or a grid that fades in as the stack opens. |
| `AnchorFromBottom` | `double` | `44` | Height of the label's anchor above the layer's bottom edge, on its right edge (default 44). |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

### ExplodedCaption

The caption of an end of an `ExplodedView`: before the stack opens or after it closes.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Title` | `string?` | `null` | The caption's title. |
| `Body` | `string?` | `null` | One or two sentences under the title. |

Derives from `AvaloniaObject`: every member of `AvaloniaObject` works as well.

## Accessibility

- In container mode the frame is a focusable scroll region named from `Title` with `RegionLabelFormat` ("… Scroll to take it
  apart, one layer at a time."). A keyboard focus ring shows 2 px outside the frame; pointer focus shows none.
- The stage and its labels are hidden from assistive technology. A hidden list named `LayerListLabel` reads every layer as
  "name: body", from the bottom up.
- The stop buttons are a group named `StopsLabel`. Each button is named after its stop (`AssembledText`, a layer's name,
  `ReassembledText`), and the current one reports `CurrentStopText` as its status. The current tick is thicker as well as
  colored, so it does not rely on color alone.
- The caption is announced politely whenever the stop changes.

### Keyboard

| Keys | Where | Action |
|---|---|---|
| `ArrowUp` / `ArrowDown` | Frame | Scroll 40 px |
| `PageUp` / `PageDown`, `Shift+Space` / `Space` | Frame | Scroll the frame's height less 40 px |
| `Home` / `End` | Frame | Scroll to the start or the end |
| `ArrowLeft` / `ArrowRight` | Frame | Nothing |
| `Tab` | Frame, stop buttons | Move from the frame to each stop button in turn |
| `Enter` or `Space` | Stop button | Scroll to that stop; focus stays on the button |

## Motion

- The stage follows the progress on an overdamped spring (stiffness 330, damping 60): it starts within a frame of the
  scroll, reaches half way in about 130 ms and settles in about 750 ms, with no overshoot. Reversing mid-way keeps the
  speed, so scrolling back and forth stays smooth.
- Opening, the stack tips back and turns first, then the layers separate and the labels draw in from the bottom up; closing,
  the layers join first and the labels disappear from the top down, then the screen stands up.
- When the stop changes, the old caption leaves upwards in 180 ms while the new one rises 10 px into place in 480 ms. The
  layers' dimming eases over 480 ms; outlines, label colors and ticks change color over 240 ms; the new tick thickens on
  a springy 580 ms curve. A plate's border and an outline's dash switch at once.
- A stop button glides the scroll position there, longer for longer distances (at most 700 ms).
- Nothing animates at rest.

| Change | Full | Reduced | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| Scroll | The stage follows on its spring | Flat at the ends, fully apart at every layer | Same as reduced |
| Stop changes | Caption crossfade, dimming and colors ease | Everything switches at once | Immediate |
| Stop button | Glides to the stop | Jumps | Jumps |

## Related

- `Stepper` for progress through the steps of a task.
- `Carousel` for browsing slides with buttons and swipes.
- `ScrollArea` for a plain scrolling region with Arc's scroll bars.
- `SegmentedControl` and `Avatar`, which the sample screen is built from.

| Component | Choose it when |
|---|---|
| `Stepper` | People complete a task step by step |
| `Carousel` | Several pictures or slides are browsed one at a time |
| `Tabs` | Each part of the story is a view of its own, chosen by name |
| `ScrollArea` | The content just needs to scroll |
